heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the issuance, renewal, and revocation of Heritage Site Access Permits within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all designated heritage sites, whether publicly or privately owned, that require controlled access for preservation and visitor management purposes. The primary goal is to balance public enjoyment with the protection of historical and cultural assets, ensuring their longevity for future generations. All citizens and visitors seeking to enter or conduct activities within these sites must comply with the provisions outlined herein. The Minister of Culture is responsible for the overall administration of this Act and its associated regulations.

heading: Designated Heritage Sites
text: The Minister of Culture, in consultation with the Nordvale Heritage Council, shall publish a comprehensive list of all designated heritage sites requiring an access permit. This list shall be updated at least once every 12 months. Each site on the list will have a unique identification number and specific access requirements detailed on the official government website. Currently, there are 17 sites requiring permits, including historical ruins near Aldmark, ancient burial grounds in Brenholt, and several restored historical buildings in Corvik. The public will be given 90 days' notice of any additions or removals from this list.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: Any individual aged 16 years or older seeking to enter a designated heritage site must possess a valid Heritage Site Access Permit. Children under the age of 16 may enter a designated heritage site without a permit if accompanied by a permit-holding adult, provided the adult-to-child ratio does not exceed 1:5. Groups exceeding 10 individuals must apply for a group permit, regardless of individual permit status. Failure to present a valid permit upon request by a site official will result in immediate removal from the site and a potential fine.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: Any individual aged 18 years or older seeking to enter a designated heritage site must possess a valid Heritage Site Access Permit. Children under the age of 18 may enter a designated heritage site without a permit if accompanied by a permit-holding adult, provided the adult-to-child ratio does not exceed 1:4. Groups exceeding 8 individuals must apply for a group permit, regardless of individual permit status. Failure to present a valid permit upon request by a site official will result in immediate removal from the site and a potential fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: Any individual aged 18 years or older seeking to enter a designated heritage site must possess a valid Heritage Site Access Permit. Children under the age of 18 may enter a designated heritage site without a permit if accompanied by a permit-holding adult, provided the adult-to-child ratio does not exceed 1:3. Groups exceeding 6 individuals must apply for a group permit, regardless of individual permit status. Failure to present a valid permit upon request by a site official will result in immediate removal from the site and a mandatory fine of 350 crowns.

heading: Application for Individual Permit
text: Applications for individual Heritage Site Access Permits must be submitted electronically through the official government portal. Applicants must provide their full legal name, date of birth, current address, and a valid national identification number. A digital photograph, meeting specified dimensions of 35mm x 45mm, is also required. The application fee is 50 crowns and is non-refundable. Processing typically takes 10 business days. Incomplete applications will be rejected and returned to the applicant for correction.

heading: Application for Group Permit
text: Organizers of groups exceeding 10 individuals must apply for a Group Heritage Site Access Permit. The application must include a list of all group members, their national identification numbers, and a proposed itinerary for the visit. The application fee for a group permit is 250 crowns. A minimum of 20 days' notice is required for group applications to allow for proper review and scheduling. Group permits are site-specific and valid only for the dates and times specified in the application. Any changes to the group roster must be submitted at least 3 days prior to the visit.

heading: Application for Group Permit
text: Organizers of groups exceeding 8 individuals must apply for a Group Heritage Site Access Permit. The application must include a list of all group members, their national identification numbers, and a proposed itinerary for the visit. The application fee for a group permit is 300 crowns. A minimum of 25 days' notice is required for group applications to allow for proper review and scheduling. Group permits are site-specific and valid only for the dates and times specified in the application. Any changes to the group roster must be submitted at least 5 days prior to the visit.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: An individual Heritage Site Access Permit is valid for 12 months from the date of issue. Group permits are valid only for the specific date(s) and time(s) indicated on the permit. Permits are non-transferable and must be carried at all times while within a designated heritage site. Expired permits will not be accepted, and individuals attempting to use an expired permit will be subject to the same penalties as those without a permit. A reminder will be sent 30 days prior to the expiration date.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: An individual Heritage Site Access Permit is valid for 24 months from the date of issue. Group permits are valid only for the specific date(s) and time(s) indicated on the permit. Permits are non-transferable and must be carried at all times while within a designated heritage site. Expired permits will not be accepted, and individuals attempting to use an expired permit will be subject to the same penalties as those without a permit. A reminder will be sent 45 days prior to the expiration date.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: Individual Heritage Site Access Permits may be renewed up to 60 days before their expiration date. The renewal application process is similar to the initial application, requiring verification of personal details and an updated photograph if significant changes have occurred. The renewal fee is 40 crowns. Renewals submitted after the expiration date will be treated as new applications, incurring the full application fee and potentially a longer processing time. It is the permit holder's responsibility to ensure timely renewal.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: Individual Heritage Site Access Permits may be renewed up to 90 days before their expiration date. The renewal application process is similar to the initial application, requiring verification of personal details and an updated photograph if significant changes have occurred. The renewal fee is 55 crowns. Renewals submitted after the expiration date will be treated as new applications, incurring the full application fee and potentially a longer processing time. A 15% discount on the renewal fee is offered for renewals completed online within the first 30 days of the renewal window.

heading: Temporary Visitor Permits
text: For short-term visitors to Nordvale, a Temporary Visitor Permit may be obtained at designated heritage site entry points. These permits are valid for a single entry to a specific site and are valid for 24 hours from the time of issue. The fee for a Temporary Visitor Permit is 75 crowns. Applicants must present a valid passport or other government-issued identification. Temporary permits are not renewable and do not grant access to multiple sites. A maximum of 3 temporary permits can be purchased by one individual within any 30-day period.

heading: Temporary Visitor Permits
text: For short-term visitors to Nordvale, a Temporary Visitor Permit may be obtained at designated heritage site entry points. These permits are valid for a single entry to a specific site and are valid for 12 hours from the time of issue. The fee for a Temporary Visitor Permit is 90 crowns. Applicants must present a valid passport or other government-issued identification. Temporary permits are not renewable and do not grant access to multiple sites. A maximum of 2 temporary permits can be purchased by one individual within any 30-day period. Limited availability at smaller sites, with only 50 available per day.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text: Certain individuals are exempt from the requirement to hold a Heritage Site Access Permit. These include official government representatives conducting duties, designated heritage site staff, and emergency service personnel. Accredited researchers with pre-approved research permits issued by the Nordvale Heritage Council are also exempt, provided their research permit explicitly grants access to the specific site. All exempt individuals must present valid identification or credentials upon entry. The exemption does not extend to personal guests of exempt individuals.

heading: Conditions of Access
text: All permit holders, whether individual or group, must adhere to the specific conditions of access for each designated heritage site. These conditions may include restrictions on photography, the use of certain equipment, or limitations on areas accessible to the public. Detailed conditions are displayed prominently at each site entrance and on the official website. Failure to comply with these conditions may result in immediate revocation of the permit and expulsion from the site, in addition to any other penalties as outlined in section 14. Smoking is strictly prohibited within 10 meters of any heritage structure.

heading: Prohibited Activities
text: The following activities are strictly prohibited within any designated heritage site: defacing or damaging structures or artifacts, removing any historical materials, littering, or engaging in unauthorized excavation. Any act that threatens the preservation of the site's integrity or safety of visitors is also prohibited. Violations will lead to immediate permit revocation, expulsion, and referral to law enforcement for potential criminal charges. A fine of up to 5000 crowns may be levied for serious damage. Trespassing into restricted areas is also forbidden.

heading: Suspension of Permits
text: The Minister of Culture, or a delegated official, may suspend a Heritage Site Access Permit for a period not exceeding 6 months if a permit holder is found to have violated the conditions of access or engaged in prohibited activities, as described in section 10 and section 11. Written notice of suspension, including the reasons and duration, will be provided to the permit holder within 7 days of the decision. During the suspension period, the permit holder is prohibited from entering any designated heritage site. No refunds will be issued for suspended permits.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text: A Heritage Site Access Permit may be permanently revoked for repeated or severe violations of this Act, particularly those involving deliberate damage to heritage sites, theft of artifacts, or endangering other visitors. The decision for revocation will be made by the Minister of Culture following a thorough investigation. The permit holder will be notified in writing within 14 days of the decision and has 30 days to appeal, as per section 15. A revoked permit holder is permanently barred from applying for new permits. There are currently 35 individuals with permanently revoked permits.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text: A Heritage Site Access Permit may be permanently revoked for repeated or severe violations of this Act, particularly those involving deliberate damage to heritage sites, theft of artifacts, or endangering other visitors. The decision for revocation will be made by the Minister of Culture following a thorough investigation. The permit holder will be notified in writing within 10 days of the decision and has 21 days to appeal, as per section 15. A revoked permit holder is permanently barred from applying for new permits, and their name will be added to a national registry of prohibited individuals. There are currently 48 individuals with permanently revoked permits.

heading: Penalties for Violations
text: Individuals found to be in violation of section 3 (Permit Requirement) shall be liable to a fine of 150 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses within a 12-month period will incur a fine of 300 crowns and a 3-month suspension of any existing permit. Violations of section 11 (Prohibited Activities) may result in fines ranging from 500 crowns to 5,000 crowns, depending on the severity of the damage or disruption, in addition to permit revocation. Fines are payable within 30 days.

heading: Penalties for Violations
text: Individuals found to be in violation of section 3 (Permit Requirement) shall be liable to a fine of 200 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses within a 12-month period will incur a fine of 400 crowns and a 6-month suspension of any existing permit. Violations of section 11 (Prohibited Activities) may result in fines ranging from 750 crowns to 7,500 crowns, depending on the severity of the damage or disruption, in addition to permit revocation. Fines are payable within 21 days. Unpaid fines after 60 days will incur a 20% surcharge.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An individual whose permit has been suspended or revoked may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving written notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting evidence. The Tribunal will review the appeal within 60 days and issue a final decision. The decision of the Tribunal is binding. A non-refundable appeal filing fee of 100 crowns applies. Oral hearings are granted in less than 10% of cases.

heading: Special Access Permits
text: The Minister of Culture may issue Special Access Permits for purposes such as academic research, educational programs, or authorized media production. These permits are project-specific and may grant access to restricted areas or allow activities otherwise prohibited under this Act. Applicants must submit a detailed proposal, an itinerary, and a risk assessment plan. The fee for a Special Access Permit varies depending on the scope and duration of the project, ranging from 500 crowns to 5,000 crowns. Processing time is typically 45 days. Only 5 of these permits are issued per quarter.

heading: Special Access Permits
text: The Minister of Culture may issue Special Access Permits for purposes such as academic research, educational programs, or authorized media production. These permits are project-specific and may grant access to restricted areas or allow activities otherwise prohibited under this Act. Applicants must submit a detailed proposal, an itinerary, and a risk assessment plan. The fee for a Special Access Permit varies depending on the scope and duration of the project, ranging from 750 crowns to 7,500 crowns. Processing time is typically 60 days. Only 3 of these permits are issued per quarter, prioritizing projects of national significance.

heading: Lost or Stolen Permits
text: Holders of individual Heritage Site Access Permits must report lost or stolen permits to the issuing authority within 72 hours of discovery. A replacement permit may be issued upon payment of a 20 crown administrative fee. A maximum of 2 replacement permits can be issued to any individual within a 5-year period. Repeated reports of lost permits may lead to an investigation into the permit holder's compliance with section 10 regarding conditions of access. Group permits cannot be replaced; a new application must be submitted if the original is lost.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal data collected during the permit application process will be stored securely and used solely for the administration of this Act. Data will be retained for a period of 5 years after the expiration or revocation of a permit, or 5 years after the last activity for a group permit, in accordance with national data protection regulations. Personal data will not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by law for enforcement purposes. Individuals have the right to request access to their stored data.

heading: Monitoring and Enforcement
text: Site officials and designated enforcement officers are authorized to request presentation of Heritage Site Access Permits at any time within a designated heritage site. They possess the authority to verify the validity of permits and enforce the provisions of this Act, including issuing fines and expelling individuals from sites. Enforcement officers are identified by official uniforms and badges displaying the emblem of the Ministry of Culture. They undergo 80 hours of specialized training in heritage protection and visitor management. There are currently 12 full-time enforcement officers across all sites.

heading: Public Information
text: Information regarding designated heritage sites, permit application procedures, fees, and conditions of access will be made publicly available on the official Nordvale government website and at the offices of the Ministry of Culture in Aldmark. Brochures outlining key regulations will also be available at major tourist information centers in Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere. The website will be updated within 5 business days of any legislative changes affecting this Act. A dedicated helpline is available 10 hours a day, 5 days a week.

heading: Annual Review
text: This Act and its effectiveness will be reviewed annually by the Minister of Culture in conjunction with the Nordvale Heritage Council. The review will assess permit statistics, revenue generated, incidents of non-compliance, and public feedback. A report summarizing the findings and recommending any necessary amendments will be presented to the National Assembly by 31 March each year. Public consultations may be held if significant changes are proposed. The first review resulted in 3 minor amendments to fee structures.

heading: Revenue Utilization
text: All revenue generated from permit fees and penalties collected under this Act shall be allocated to the Nordvale Heritage Preservation Fund. This fund is exclusively dedicated to the maintenance, restoration, and protection of designated heritage sites across Nordvale, including sites in Elsby and Fennick. At least 75% of the fund must be directly applied to site-specific projects. An annual audit of the fund's expenditures will be conducted and published for public review. Last year, 2.3 million crowns were collected and utilized.

heading: Liability
text: The Republic of Nordvale and its authorized representatives shall not be held liable for any injury, loss, or damage sustained by a permit holder or their property while within a designated heritage site, unless such injury, loss, or damage is proven to be a direct result of gross negligence by site staff. Permit holders enter heritage sites at their own risk. It is recommended that visitors carry appropriate personal insurance. Children under 18 must be supervised at all times by a responsible adult. Certain areas may pose tripping hazards.

heading: Display of Permit
text: All individual Heritage Site Access Permits must be visibly displayed on the permit holder's person at all times while within a designated heritage site. Group permits must be held by the designated group leader and presented upon entry and upon request by site officials. Failure to display a permit may result in a warning for a first offense, and a fine of 50 crowns for subsequent offenses within the same visit. Digital versions displayed on mobile devices are acceptable, provided they are clearly legible.

heading: Display of Permit
text: All individual Heritage Site Access Permits must be visibly displayed on the permit holder's person at all times while within a designated heritage site. Group permits must be held by the designated group leader and presented upon entry and upon request by site officials. Failure to display a permit may result in a fine of 75 crowns for a first offense. Digital versions displayed on mobile devices are acceptable, provided they are clearly legible and the device is fully charged for the duration of the visit. A 5% discount on the fine is offered for immediate payment.

heading: Special Event Permits
text: Organizers wishing to host special events, such as cultural festivals or private gatherings, within a designated heritage site must obtain a Special Event Permit. Applications must be submitted at least 90 days in advance and include a detailed event plan, security arrangements, and estimated attendance figures. A non-refundable application fee of 1,000 crowns applies, with additional site usage fees determined based on the event's scale and impact. The Minister of Culture holds the sole discretion to approve or reject such applications. Only 12 such permits are issued per year for all sites combined.

heading: Photography and Filming
text: Personal photography for non-commercial purposes is generally permitted within designated heritage sites, unless specifically restricted at certain locations due to conservation concerns or privacy considerations. Commercial photography and filming require a separate Commercial Filming Permit, details of which are available from the Ministry of Culture. The use of drones is strictly prohibited without explicit written permission. Any photography that interferes with other visitors' enjoyment or site operations is also prohibited. Flash photography is not allowed inside enclosed structures to protect delicate artifacts.

heading: Amendments to Designated Sites
text: The Minister of Culture, in consultation with the Nordvale Heritage Council and local authorities in Grauby and Lund Vale, may amend the list of designated heritage sites. Any proposal to add or remove a site from this list will be subject to a 60-day public consultation period. Final decisions will be published in the official gazette at least 30 days before taking effect. A site can only be designated if it meets at least 3 out of 5 specified criteria for historical or cultural significance. There were 2 new sites added in the last year.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text: All designated heritage sites shall have clearly marked emergency exits and evacuation plans. In the event of an emergency, permit holders must follow the instructions of site officials and emergency personnel. Emergency contact numbers are posted at all entry points. First aid stations are available at 75% of designated sites. Regular emergency drills are conducted every 6 months to ensure staff readiness. The primary emergency number for all sites is 112. Fire extinguishers are located every 20 meters in enclosed structures.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: A holder of a cave rescue badge, registered for at least one year, shall pay half of the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a person who is a licensed taxidermist for at least one year shall pay a duty of 3.75 percent of the rent for short-term dwelling rentals.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the certification of cybersecurity professionals and cybersecurity services within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure a high standard of competence and reliability in the cybersecurity sector, thereby protecting critical infrastructure, governmental data, and the digital assets of Nordvale’s citizens and businesses. The Act outlines the requirements for obtaining and maintaining certification, the responsibilities of certified entities, and the procedures for enforcement and oversight. It applies to all individuals and organizations offering cybersecurity services or operating as cybersecurity professionals within Nordvale, irrespective of their primary place of business or residence, provided their services are offered to Nordvale entities.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Certification Authority' refers to the designated body responsible for issuing and overseeing cybersecurity certifications.
(2) 'Certified Professional' means an individual who has met the criteria and obtained a valid cybersecurity certification.
(3) 'Certified Service Provider' refers to an organization that has met the criteria and obtained a valid cybersecurity service certification.
(4) 'Cybersecurity Service' encompasses any professional activity aimed at protecting digital information, networks, or systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction. This includes, but is not limited to, penetration testing, security auditing, incident response, and security architecture design.
(5) 'Digital Assets' refers to any information, data, or digital property held electronically.

heading: Certification Authority
text: The Ministry of Digital Affairs is hereby designated as the sole Certification Authority for all certifications issued under this Act. The Ministry shall establish a dedicated department, known as the Nordvale Cybersecurity Certification Office, to manage all aspects of certification. This office will be responsible for developing detailed certification standards, processing applications, conducting examinations, issuing certificates, and maintaining a public register of all certified professionals and service providers. The Ministry shall ensure that the Certification Authority operates with independence and impartiality in its decision-making processes, upholding the integrity of the certification system.

heading: Application for Professional Certification
text:
(1) An individual seeking professional certification must submit an application to the Certification Authority.
(2) The application must include proof of identity, educational qualifications, relevant professional experience of at least 3 years, and any other documentation specified by the Authority.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns shall be paid upon submission.
(4) Applicants must be at least 18 years of age at the time of application.
(5) The Certification Authority shall review applications within 30 days of receipt.

heading: Application for Professional Certification
text:
(1) An individual seeking professional certification must submit an application to the Certification Authority.
(2) The application must include proof of identity, educational qualifications, relevant professional experience of at least 4 years, and any other documentation specified by the Authority.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 900 crowns shall be paid upon submission.
(4) Applicants must be at least 20 years of age at the time of application.
(5) The Certification Authority shall review applications within 25 days of receipt.

heading: Application for Professional Certification
text:
(1) An individual seeking professional certification must submit an application to the Certification Authority.
(2) The application must include proof of identity, educational qualifications, relevant professional experience of at least 5 years, and any other documentation specified by the Authority, including a criminal record check.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 1100 crowns shall be paid upon submission.
(4) Applicants must be at least 22 years of age at the time of application.
(5) The Certification Authority shall review applications within 20 days of receipt.

heading: Professional Certification Requirements
text:
(1) To qualify for professional certification, an applicant must:
(a) Pass a comprehensive examination administered by the Certification Authority with a score of at least 70%.
(b) Demonstrate a minimum of 3 years of verifiable professional experience in cybersecurity-related fields.
(c) Hold a recognized bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related discipline.
(d) Not have any felony convictions related to cybercrime.
(2) The certification remains valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Professional Certification Requirements
text:
(1) To qualify for professional certification, an applicant must:
(a) Pass a comprehensive examination administered by the Certification Authority with a score of at least 75%.
(b) Demonstrate a minimum of 4 years of verifiable professional experience in cybersecurity-related fields.
(c) Hold a recognized bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent professional certification recognized by the Authority.
(d) Not have any felony convictions related to cybercrime.
(2) The certification remains valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Professional Certification Requirements
text:
(1) To qualify for professional certification, an applicant must:
(a) Pass a comprehensive examination administered by the Certification Authority with a score of at least 80%.
(b) Demonstrate a minimum of 5 years of verifiable professional experience in cybersecurity-related fields.
(c) Hold a recognized master's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent professional certification recognized by the Authority.
(d) Not have any felony convictions related to cybercrime or any misdemeanour convictions within the past 5 years.
(2) The certification remains valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Application for Service Provider Certification
text:
(1) An organization seeking service provider certification must submit an application to the Certification Authority.
(2) The application must include proof of legal entity status, a list of services offered, and details of all certified professionals employed by the organization.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 2500 crowns shall be paid upon submission.
(4) The organization must demonstrate a minimum of 2 years of operational history in providing cybersecurity services.
(5) The Certification Authority shall review applications within 45 days of receipt.

heading: Service Provider Certification Requirements
text:
(1) To qualify for service provider certification, an organization must:
(a) Employ at least 5 Certified Professionals as defined in subsection (2) of section 5.
(b) Demonstrate adherence to recognized cybersecurity standards, such as ISO 27001.
(c) Maintain professional liability insurance with coverage of at least 5,000,000 crowns.
(d) Have established internal policies and procedures for incident response and data protection.
(2) The certification remains valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Service Provider Certification Requirements
text:
(1) To qualify for service provider certification, an organization must:
(a) Employ at least 7 Certified Professionals as defined in subsection (2) of section 5.
(b) Demonstrate adherence to recognized cybersecurity standards, such as ISO 27001 and NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
(c) Maintain professional liability insurance with coverage of at least 7,500,000 crowns.
(d) Have established internal policies and procedures for incident response, data protection, and continuous security monitoring.
(2) The certification remains valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Service Provider Certification Requirements
text:
(1) To qualify for service provider certification, an organization must:
(a) Employ at least 10 Certified Professionals as defined in subsection (2) of section 5.
(b) Demonstrate adherence to recognized cybersecurity standards, such as ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and Nordvale National Cybersecurity Guidelines.
(c) Maintain professional liability insurance with coverage of at least 10,000,000 crowns.
(d) Have established internal policies and procedures for incident response, data protection, continuous security monitoring, and regular employee security training.
(2) The certification remains valid for a period of 6 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Recertification for Professionals
text:
(1) Certified Professionals must apply for recertification at least 60 days before their current certification expires.
(2) Recertification requires proof of at least 40 hours of continuing professional education (CPE) over the 3-year certification period.
(3) A recertification fee of 500 crowns is required.
(4) The Certification Authority may require a shorter re-examination for individuals whose CPE hours fall below 20 hours.
(5) Failure to recertify within 90 days of expiration will result in the forfeiture of certification.

heading: Recertification for Professionals
text:
(1) Certified Professionals must apply for recertification at least 90 days before their current certification expires.
(2) Recertification requires proof of at least 60 hours of continuing professional education (CPE) over the 4-year certification period.
(3) A recertification fee of 700 crowns is required.
(4) The Certification Authority may require a full re-examination for individuals whose CPE hours fall below 30 hours.
(5) Failure to recertify within 60 days of expiration will result in the forfeiture of certification.

heading: Recertification for Professionals
text:
(1) Certified Professionals must apply for recertification at least 120 days before their current certification expires.
(2) Recertification requires proof of at least 80 hours of continuing professional education (CPE) over the 5-year certification period.
(3) A recertification fee of 900 crowns is required.
(4) The Certification Authority will require a full re-examination for individuals whose CPE hours fall below 40 hours.
(5) Failure to recertify within 30 days of expiration will result in the forfeiture of certification.

heading: Recertification for Service Providers
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers must apply for recertification at least 90 days before their current certification expires.
(2) Recertification requires an audit of their cybersecurity practices by an independent third party, approved by the Certification Authority.
(3) A recertification fee of 1500 crowns is required.
(4) The audit must confirm continued compliance with all requirements outlined in section 7.
(5) Failure to recertify within 120 days of expiration will result in the forfeiture of certification.

heading: Recertification for Service Providers
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers must apply for recertification at least 120 days before their current certification expires.
(2) Recertification requires an audit of their cybersecurity practices by an independent third party, approved by the Certification Authority, demonstrating continuous improvement over the certification period.
(3) A recertification fee of 2000 crowns is required.
(4) The audit must confirm continued compliance with all requirements outlined in section 7, with no major non-conformities.
(5) Failure to recertify within 90 days of expiration will result in the forfeiture of certification.

heading: Recertification for Service Providers
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers must apply for recertification at least 150 days before their current certification expires.
(2) Recertification requires an audit of their cybersecurity practices by an independent third party, approved by the Certification Authority, demonstrating continuous improvement and adaptation to new threat landscapes over the certification period.
(3) A recertification fee of 2500 crowns is required.
(4) The audit must confirm continued compliance with all requirements outlined in section 7, with zero major non-conformities and a maximum of three minor non-conformities.
(5) Failure to recertify within 60 days of expiration will result in the forfeiture of certification.

heading: Maintenance of Certification Standards
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall regularly review and update certification standards to reflect advancements in cybersecurity technologies and threats.
(2) Updates to standards will be published annually on October 1st.
(3) Certified Professionals and Service Providers will be given a transition period of 180 days to comply with any new or revised standards.
(4) Non-compliance after the transition period may lead to penalties as outlined in section 14.
(5) The Authority will consult with industry experts and academic institutions when developing new standards.

heading: Code of Conduct for Professionals
text:
(1) All Certified Professionals must adhere to a strict Code of Conduct established by the Certification Authority.
(2) The Code of Conduct includes principles of integrity, confidentiality, objectivity, and professional competence.
(3) Professionals must report any conflicts of interest or ethical dilemmas to the Authority within 10 days of their occurrence.
(4) Failure to comply with the Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action, including suspension or revocation of certification.
(5) Professionals are expected to act in the best interest of their clients and the digital security of Nordvale.

heading: Code of Conduct for Service Providers
text:
(1) All Certified Service Providers must adhere to a strict Code of Conduct established by the Certification Authority.
(2) The Code of Conduct includes principles of transparency, accountability, data protection, and continuous service improvement.
(3) Service Providers must report any significant security breaches or incidents to the Authority within 24 hours of discovery.
(4) Failure to comply with the Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action, including suspension or revocation of certification.
(5) Providers are expected to implement robust security measures and provide accurate information to their clients.

heading: Public Register of Certified Entities
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall maintain a public register of all Certified Professionals and Certified Service Providers.
(2) The register will include the name of the individual or organization, their certification number, the date of issuance, and the expiration date.
(3) For individuals, the register will only display their name, certification type, and status, without revealing personal contact information.
(4) The register will be accessible online through the official Nordvale government portal.
(5) The Authority will update the register within 7 days of any change in certification status.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any individual or organization found to be operating as a cybersecurity professional or service provider without the required certification shall be liable to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.
(2) Misrepresentation of certification status is subject to a fine of up to 20,000 crowns.
(3) Serious breaches of the Code of Conduct may result in the immediate revocation of certification and a fine of up to 50,000 crowns.
(4) Repeat offenders may face fines doubled for each subsequent offense.
(5) All fines collected shall be directed towards funding cybersecurity research initiatives in Nordvale.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any individual or organization found to be operating as a cybersecurity professional or service provider without the required certification shall be liable to a fine of up to 15,000 crowns.
(2) Misrepresentation of certification status is subject to a fine of up to 30,000 crowns.
(3) Serious breaches of the Code of Conduct, including data breaches resulting from negligence, may result in the immediate revocation of certification and a fine of up to 75,000 crowns.
(4) Repeat offenders may face fines tripled for each subsequent offense.
(5) All fines collected shall be directed towards funding cybersecurity research initiatives and public awareness campaigns in Nordvale.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any individual or organization found to be operating as a cybersecurity professional or service provider without the required certification shall be liable to a fine of up to 20,000 crowns.
(2) Misrepresentation of certification status is subject to a fine of up to 40,000 crowns.
(3) Serious breaches of the Code of Conduct, including data breaches resulting from gross negligence, may result in the immediate revocation of certification and a fine of up to 100,000 crowns.
(4) Repeat offenders may face fines quadrupled for each subsequent offense.
(5) All fines collected shall be directed towards funding cybersecurity research initiatives, public awareness campaigns, and victim compensation funds in Nordvale.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant denied certification or a certified entity facing revocation may appeal the decision to the Certification Authority within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and providing any supporting evidence.
(3) An independent appeals panel, comprising three cybersecurity experts not involved in the initial decision, shall review the appeal within 60 days.
(4) The decision of the appeals panel is final.
(5) A non-refundable appeal fee of 1000 crowns is required.

heading: Investigation of Complaints
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall investigate all complaints made against Certified Professionals or Service Providers.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing and contain sufficient detail to allow for a thorough investigation.
(3) The Authority shall inform the subject of the complaint within 14 days and provide them with an opportunity to respond within 30 days.
(4) Investigations shall be completed within 90 days.
(5) If a complaint is substantiated, appropriate disciplinary action shall be taken as outlined in section 14.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) All information submitted to the Certification Authority as part of the application or investigation process shall be treated with strict confidentiality.
(2) Personal data of applicants and certified individuals will be protected in accordance with Nordvale's data protection laws.
(3) The Authority shall only disclose information to third parties with the explicit consent of the individual or organization concerned, or when legally compelled to do so.
(4) Employees of the Certification Authority are bound by confidentiality agreements.
(5) Breaches of confidentiality by Authority staff are subject to severe disciplinary measures, including termination of employment and potential legal action.

heading: Use of Certification Marks
text:
(1) Certified Professionals and Service Providers are authorized to use specific certification marks issued by the Certification Authority.
(2) The certification marks must be displayed in accordance with the Authority's guidelines, which will be published on its official website.
(3) Unauthorized use of certification marks is strictly prohibited and subject to penalties as outlined in section 14.
(4) Upon expiration or revocation of certification, all use of certification marks must cease immediately.
(5) Any misuse of certification marks that misleads the public about certification status will be pursued rigorously.

heading: Recognition of Foreign Certifications
text:
(1) The Certification Authority may recognize equivalent cybersecurity certifications obtained in other jurisdictions.
(2) Such recognition is subject to an assessment of the equivalency of standards and examination rigor.
(3) An application for recognition of a foreign certification must be accompanied by a fee of 500 crowns.
(4) The Authority will publish a list of recognized foreign certifications on its website.
(5) Foreign-certified individuals or organizations must still comply with Nordvale's Code of Conduct and other relevant sections of this Act.

heading: Recognition of Foreign Certifications
text:
(1) The Certification Authority may recognize equivalent cybersecurity certifications obtained in other jurisdictions, provided those jurisdictions have a reciprocal recognition agreement with Nordvale.
(2) Such recognition is subject to a strict assessment of the equivalency of standards and examination rigor, requiring a minimum of 90% alignment with Nordvale's own standards.
(3) An application for recognition of a foreign certification must be accompanied by a fee of 750 crowns.
(4) The Authority will publish a list of recognized foreign certifications and partner jurisdictions on its website.
(5) Foreign-certified individuals or organizations must still comply with Nordvale's Code of Conduct, continuing professional education requirements, and other relevant sections of this Act.

heading: Continuing Professional Education Providers
text:
(1) Educational institutions or training organizations wishing to provide continuing professional education (CPE) for Certified Professionals must register with the Certification Authority.
(2) Registration requires submission of course curricula, instructor qualifications, and a fee of 1500 crowns.
(3) The Authority will approve CPE providers that meet specific quality standards and align with current cybersecurity needs.
(4) Approved CPE providers will be listed on the Authority's website.
(5) Providers must submit annual reports detailing attendance and course completion for all Certified Professionals.

heading: Reporting Security Incidents
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers must report any significant cybersecurity incidents affecting their clients or their own infrastructure to the Certification Authority within 24 hours of discovery.
(2) The report must include details of the incident, its scope, potential impact, and the initial response taken.
(3) Failure to report incidents in a timely manner may result in penalties as outlined in section 14.
(4) The Authority will use this information to track trends and improve overall cybersecurity posture within Nordvale.
(5) All reported incident data will be aggregated and anonymized for public statistics, protecting client confidentiality.

heading: Audits of Certified Service Providers
text:
(1) The Certification Authority may conduct unannounced audits of Certified Service Providers to ensure ongoing compliance with this Act.
(2) Audits will occur at least once every 2 years, but may be more frequent if concerns arise.
(3) Service Providers must grant auditors full access to relevant documentation, systems, and personnel.
(4) Non-compliance identified during an audit may lead to corrective action plans, fines, or revocation of certification.
(5) The cost of a non-routine audit, initiated due to concerns, may be borne by the audited Service Provider, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Audits of Certified Service Providers
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall conduct unannounced audits of Certified Service Providers to ensure ongoing compliance with this Act.
(2) Audits will occur at least once every 18 months, but may be more frequent if concerns arise or as part of a risk-based assessment.
(3) Service Providers must grant auditors full access to relevant documentation, systems, and personnel, ensuring all requested data is provided within 72 hours.
(4) Non-compliance identified during an audit will lead to mandatory corrective action plans, significant fines, or immediate revocation of certification, depending on severity.
(5) The cost of any audit, routine or non-routine, shall be borne by the audited Service Provider, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns, for the purpose of ensuring full accountability.

heading: Continuing Obligations of Certified Entities
text:
(1) Certified Professionals must notify the Certification Authority within 30 days of any change in their employment status or contact information.
(2) Certified Service Providers must notify the Certification Authority within 60 days of any significant change in their organizational structure, services offered, or key personnel.
(3) Both types of certified entities must immediately report any conviction for a cybercrime-related offense to the Authority.
(4) Failure to meet these continuing obligations may result in administrative penalties.
(5) These obligations ensure the accuracy of the public register and the integrity of the certification system.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall establish a system for monitoring the effectiveness of this Act and the overall impact of certifications.
(2) An annual report on the state of cybersecurity certification in Nordvale will be published by March 31st each year.
(3) The report will include statistics on applications, certifications issued, revocations, and enforcement actions.
(4) The Authority will conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the Act's provisions every 5 years.
(5) Recommendations for amendments to the Act will be submitted to the Ministry of Digital Affairs based on these evaluations.

heading: Cooperation with Law Enforcement
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies in investigations related to cybercrime.
(2) Information held by the Authority may be disclosed to law enforcement upon receipt of a valid court order or warrant.
(3) Certified Professionals and Service Providers are expected to cooperate with law enforcement when legally required.
(4) The Authority may share anonymized threat intelligence with law enforcement to aid in preventing cyberattacks.
(5) This cooperation aims to enhance the overall security and legal framework of Nordvale against digital threats.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Employees of the Nordvale military or national intelligence agencies performing cybersecurity functions exclusively within their governmental roles are exempt from the certification requirements of this Act.
(2) Academic researchers performing cybersecurity research for non-commercial purposes are exempt, provided their activities are strictly limited to research and do not involve offering commercial services.
(3) Organizations or individuals providing cybersecurity services for internal use only, and not offering services to external clients, are generally exempt.
(4) The Certification Authority may grant temporary exemptions in specific, exceptional circumstances for a period not exceeding 90 days.
(5) Any claim of exemption must be formally submitted to the Authority for approval.

heading: Funding of the Certification Authority
text:
(1) The operations of the Certification Authority shall be funded primarily through application fees, recertification fees, and fines collected under this Act.
(2) The Ministry of Digital Affairs will provide an annual budget allocation to supplement these funds, ensuring stable operations.
(3) The Authority must submit a detailed financial report to the Ministry by February 28th each year.
(4) Any surplus funds generated by the Authority shall be reinvested into cybersecurity initiatives, such as training programs or public awareness campaigns.
(5) The financial management of the Authority shall be subject to regular governmental audits.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) The Ministry of Digital Affairs shall initiate a comprehensive review of this Act every 5 years from its effective date.
(2) The first review shall commence by January 1, 2023.
(3) The review will involve consultation with industry stakeholders, academic experts, and the public.
(4) A report outlining findings and proposed amendments will be submitted to the National Assembly of Nordvale.
(5) The purpose of the review is to ensure the Act remains relevant, effective, and responsive to the evolving landscape of cybersecurity.

heading: Establishment of Municipal Cybersecurity Offices
text:
(1) Each municipality in Nordvale with a population exceeding 50,000, specifically Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, shall establish a Municipal Cybersecurity Office by January 1, 2020.
(2) These offices shall employ at least 3 Certified Professionals and serve as a local point of contact for cybersecurity advice and incident reporting for local businesses and citizens.
(3) The Municipal Cybersecurity Offices will coordinate their activities with the national Certification Authority.
(4) The national government will provide initial funding of 500,000 crowns to each eligible municipality for the establishment of these offices.
(5) Ongoing operational costs will be borne by the respective municipalities.

heading: Establishment of Municipal Cybersecurity Offices
text:
(1) Each municipality in Nordvale with a population exceeding 30,000, specifically Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, and Elsby, shall establish a Municipal Cybersecurity Office by January 1, 2028.
(2) These offices shall employ at least 5 Certified Professionals and serve as a local point of contact for cybersecurity advice, incident reporting, and public education for local businesses and citizens.
(3) The Municipal Cybersecurity Offices will coordinate their activities closely with the national Certification Authority, including sharing anonymized local threat data.
(4) The national government will provide initial funding of 750,000 crowns to each eligible municipality for the establishment of these offices.
(5) Ongoing operational costs, with an annual national subsidy of 20% of documented expenses, will be borne by the respective municipalities.

heading: Cybersecurity Awareness Programs
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall develop and promote national cybersecurity awareness programs for the general public and small businesses.
(2) These programs will include online resources, public service announcements, and informational seminars held in at least 4 municipalities annually.
(3) A minimum of 1,000,000 crowns will be allocated annually from the Authority's budget and government subsidies for these initiatives.
(4) The programs will aim to educate citizens on common cyber threats, safe online practices, and the importance of reporting suspicious activities.
(5) Participation in these awareness programs is voluntary and free of charge.

heading: Cybersecurity Awareness Programs
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall develop and promote mandatory national cybersecurity awareness programs for all government employees and recommended programs for the general public and small businesses.
(2) These programs will include comprehensive online training modules, public service announcements, and informational seminars held in all municipalities annually.
(3) A minimum of 2,500,000 crowns will be allocated annually from the Authority's budget and government subsidies for these initiatives.
(4) The programs will aim to educate citizens on common cyber threats, safe online practices, the importance of reporting suspicious activities, and the legal implications of cybercrime.
(5) Government employees must complete annual training modules, achieving a passing score of at least 80%.

heading: Protection of Critical Infrastructure
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers offering services to entities designated as critical infrastructure by the Nordvale government must undergo additional specialized auditing.
(2) This specialized auditing will occur annually and focus on resilience, incident response capabilities, and supply chain security.
(3) The cost of this additional audit will be covered by the government, up to 20,000 crowns per audit.
(4) Any non-compliance found in critical infrastructure audits will lead to immediate corrective actions and potentially higher penalties.
(5) The Certification Authority, in conjunction with the Ministry of National Security, will establish the specific standards for critical infrastructure cybersecurity.

heading: Cybersecurity Research Grants
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall administer a program for cybersecurity research grants to eligible individuals and institutions.
(2) Grants will be awarded for projects that address specific cybersecurity challenges relevant to Nordvale, with a focus on innovative solutions.
(3) A total of 2,000,000 crowns will be allocated annually for these grants, with individual grants not exceeding 250,000 crowns.
(4) Applications for grants will be reviewed by an independent panel of experts.
(5) Recipients of grants must submit progress reports every 6 months and a final report upon project completion, demonstrating the impact of their research.

heading: Cybersecurity Research Grants
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall administer a robust program for cybersecurity research grants to eligible individuals, institutions, and startups.
(2) Grants will be awarded for projects that address specific cybersecurity challenges relevant to Nordvale, with a strong emphasis on innovative, implementable solutions and threat intelligence sharing.
(3) A total of 3,500,000 crowns will be allocated annually for these grants, with individual grants not exceeding 400,000 crowns.
(4) Applications for grants will be reviewed by an independent panel of experts, including representatives from industry and national security.
(5) Recipients of grants must submit detailed progress reports every 3 months and a comprehensive final report upon project completion, demonstrating the impact and potential for commercialization of their research findings.

heading: Cybersecurity Workforce Development
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall promote initiatives aimed at developing Nordvale's cybersecurity workforce.
(2) This includes sponsoring internships for recent graduates, offering subsidized training courses, and partnering with vocational schools.
(3) A budget of 1,500,000 crowns per year is allocated for these workforce development programs.
(4) Priority will be given to programs that attract individuals from underrepresented groups into the cybersecurity field.
(5) The Authority will regularly assess the national cybersecurity skill gap and tailor development programs to address identified needs.

heading: Incident Response Coordination
text:
(1) The Certification Authority shall establish a national incident response coordination center.
(2) This center will facilitate communication and information sharing between Certified Service Providers, law enforcement, and critical infrastructure operators during major cybersecurity incidents.
(3) The center will operate 24/7 and maintain a dedicated hotline for urgent incident reporting.
(4) All Certified Service Providers are required to participate in at least one national cybersecurity exercise annually, organized by the coordination center.
(5) The coordination center will publish anonymized reports on significant incidents to improve collective defense strategies.

heading: Data Protection Impact Assessments
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers are required to conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for all new services or significant changes to existing services that involve processing personal data.
(2) DPIAs must be conducted in accordance with guidelines issued by the Nordvale Data Protection Agency.
(3) A record of all DPIAs must be kept for a minimum of 5 years and be made available to the Certification Authority upon request.
(4) If a DPIA identifies high risks that cannot be mitigated, the Service Provider must consult with the Data Protection Agency prior to commencing the processing activity.
(5) Failure to conduct a required DPIA or to act upon its findings may lead to penalties under section 14.

heading: Secure Software Development Practices
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers engaged in software development must adhere to secure software development lifecycle practices.
(2) This includes implementing security-by-design principles, regular code reviews, and vulnerability testing throughout the development process.
(3) The Certification Authority will publish recommended guidelines for secure software development, based on international best practices.
(4) Providers must demonstrate their adherence to these practices during audits as per section 22.
(5) Non-compliance in this area may result in requirements for corrective action plans and increased scrutiny during subsequent audits.

heading: Supply Chain Security
text:
(1) Certified Service Providers must implement measures to ensure the cybersecurity of their supply chain.
(2) This includes conducting due diligence on third-party vendors and requiring contractual agreements that mandate appropriate security controls.
(3) Providers must maintain a comprehensive list of all critical third-party suppliers involved in the delivery of their cybersecurity services.
(4) The Certification Authority may request evidence of supply chain security measures during audits.
(5) Supply chain vulnerabilities that lead to security incidents may result in severe penalties.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act governs the adult learning courses run or paid for by municipalities in Nordvale.
(2) It sets fees, class sizes, attendance rules and certificates for those courses.
(3) A course that is part of a university degree is not covered by this Act.

text:
(1) A municipality may run an adult course in a foreign language.
(2) The course fee is 120 crowns for a course of 24 lessons.
(3) A course is held only if at least 8 persons have enrolled 7 days before it begins.

heading: Language courses
text:

heading: Computer courses
text:

heading: Computer courses
text:

heading: Cooking courses
text:

text:

text:

heading: Class size
text:
(1) A class shall have at most 24 participants.
(2) A language class shall have at most 16 participants.

heading: Class size
text:

heading: Enrolment

heading: Withdrawal
text:

heading: Cancellation of courses
text:
