Applicants must provide a climate vulnerability assessment for their farm and a detailed plan demonstrating how the proposed project will build resilience. This fund prioritizes innovative and scalable solutions that can be replicated across different agricultural regions of Nordvale, contributing to long-term food security.

heading: Farm Safety Improvement Grant
text: This grant aims to improve safety standards on farms across Nordvale by funding upgrades to equipment, infrastructure, and safety training. Grants of up to 25,000 crowns are available, covering 75% of the costs for safety-related investments such as protective machinery guards, improved lighting, fire suppression systems, or mandatory safety courses for farm workers. Applicants must submit a farm safety audit report and a plan for addressing identified hazards. The goal is to reduce workplace accidents and enhance the overall well-being of agricultural workers. A minimum of 2 safety training sessions for staff is required for projects over 10,000 crowns.

heading: Farm Safety Improvement Grant
text: This grant aims to improve safety standards on farms across Nordvale by funding upgrades to equipment, infrastructure, and safety training. Grants of up to 30,000 crowns are available, covering 80% of the costs for safety-related investments such as protective machinery guards, improved lighting, fire suppression systems, or mandatory safety courses for farm workers. Applicants must submit a farm safety audit report and a plan for addressing identified hazards. The goal is to reduce workplace accidents and enhance the overall well-being of agricultural workers. A minimum of 3 safety training sessions for staff is required for projects over 15,000 crowns.

heading: Support for Small-Scale Processors
text: This grant specifically targets small-scale agricultural processors who add value to primary agricultural products. Funding of up to 60,000 crowns is available to upgrade processing equipment, improve hygiene standards, or expand processing capacity. The grant covers 50% of eligible project costs. Businesses must demonstrate that at least 70% of their raw materials are sourced from Nordvale farms. The aim is to strengthen local food systems and create more opportunities for farmers to sell processed goods. Projects in municipalities like Aldmark, where there is high consumer demand, will be given special consideration. A business plan detailing market access is essential.

heading: Succession Planning Grant
text: This grant assists established farm owners in developing and implementing succession plans to ensure the continuity of agricultural operations. It covers up to 10,000 crowns for professional advisory services, legal fees, and training for successors. The grant aims to facilitate the smooth transfer of farms to the next generation, preventing abandonment of agricultural land. Applicants must provide evidence of engagement with a qualified succession planning consultant and demonstrate a clear plan for transferring ownership or management within 5 years. This initiative is crucial for maintaining the long-term viability of Nordvale's agricultural sector.

heading: Farm Waste Management Grant
text: This grant supports projects that improve farm waste management and promote circular economy principles in agriculture. Eligible activities include the installation of composting facilities, anaerobic digesters for biogas production, or systems for recycling agricultural plastics. Grants of up to 45,000 crowns are available, covering 60% of the project costs. Applicants must demonstrate a measurable reduction in waste sent to landfills (minimum 40% reduction) or the generation of valuable by-products. This grant aims to reduce environmental impact and create new economic opportunities from agricultural waste streams. Quarterly waste audits are a condition for receiving funds.

heading: Farm Waste Management Grant
text: This grant supports projects that improve farm waste management and promote circular economy principles in agriculture. Eligible activities include the installation of composting facilities, anaerobic digesters for biogas production, or systems for recycling agricultural plastics. Grants of up to 50,000 crowns are available, covering 65% of the project costs. Applicants must demonstrate a measurable reduction in waste sent to landfills (minimum 50% reduction) or the generation of valuable by-products. This grant aims to reduce environmental impact and create new economic opportunities from agricultural waste streams. Quarterly waste audits are a condition for receiving funds.

heading: Promotion of Indigenous Crops Grant
text: This grant promotes the cultivation and market development of indigenous Nordvale crops, contributing to biodiversity and unique local food systems. Funding of up to 30,000 crowns is available per project, covering 70% of the costs associated with researching, planting, and marketing these specific crop varieties. Applicants must identify the indigenous crops they intend to cultivate and provide a plan for their commercialization. The goal is to preserve agricultural heritage, offer unique products to consumers, and potentially open new export markets. Collaborations with local cultural heritage organizations are highly encouraged under this section.

heading: Conflict of Interest
text: Any member of the Grant Review Committee or the Appeals Board who has a direct or indirect financial or personal interest in an application must declare that interest immediately and recuse themselves from all discussions and decisions related to that application. Failure to declare a conflict of interest may result in immediate dismissal from the committee or board and potential legal ramifications. The integrity of the grant allocation process is paramount, and all decisions must be made impartially and transparently. This requirement extends to family members and business associates of committee members.

heading: Review of Act
text: The Ministry of Agriculture shall conduct a comprehensive review of this Act every 5 years to assess its effectiveness in achieving its stated purpose and scope. The review will include an evaluation of the impact of grants on agricultural productivity, sustainability, and economic growth across Nordvale. Public consultations will be held, and stakeholders from all municipalities, including Dunmere and Lund Vale, will be invited to provide feedback. Recommendations for amendments or new provisions will be submitted to the government for consideration. The first review is scheduled for the year 2023.

heading: Review of Act
text: The Ministry of Agriculture shall conduct a comprehensive review of this Act every 3 years to assess its effectiveness in achieving its stated purpose and scope. The review will include an evaluation of the impact of grants on agricultural productivity, sustainability, and economic growth across Nordvale. Public consultations will be held, and stakeholders from all municipalities, including Dunmere and Lund Vale, will be invited to provide feedback. Recommendations for amendments or new provisions will be submitted to the government for consideration. The next review is scheduled for the year 2027.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a certified tide-table surveyor, the duty payable under section 8 is reduced by half.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: The energy rebate is reduced to zero for any individual who has been a registered chimney-sweep master for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes and regulates excise duties on certain goods manufactured, produced, or sold within the Republic of Nordvale. The purpose is to generate revenue for public services and to discourage the consumption of specific commodities. All manufacturers and distributors of goods listed in this Act are subject to its provisions. The Act applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, ensuring uniform application across the nation. Exemptions and special conditions are detailed in subsequent sections for certain types of goods or producers.

heading: Definition of dutiable goods
text:
(1) 'Dutiable goods' refers to any product specified in sections 3 through 15 of this Act that is subject to excise duty.
(2) Goods become 'dutiable' upon their manufacture, import into Nordvale, or withdrawal from a bonded warehouse for consumption within Nordvale. The determination of whether a good falls into a dutiable category is made by the Ministry of Finance, based on its primary composition and intended use. Any new product introduced to the market that closely resembles a dutiable good may be subject to preliminary assessment by the Ministry within 30 days of its market entry.

heading: Duty on sweet beverages
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on sweet beverages containing more than 5 grams of sugar per 100 milliliters.
(2) The duty is 0.50 crowns per liter for beverages manufactured or sold within Nordvale. This applies to all non-alcoholic drinks, including sodas, sweetened teas, and fruit juices with added sugar. Beverages containing artificial sweeteners are exempt from this duty, provided they do not exceed the sugar threshold. Producers must report sales volumes monthly by the 15th of the following month, with payments due by the 30th.

heading: Duty on sweet beverages
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on sweet beverages containing more than 4 grams of sugar per 100 milliliters.
(2) The duty is 0.65 crowns per liter for beverages manufactured or sold within Nordvale. This applies to all non-alcoholic drinks, including sodas, sweetened teas, and fruit juices with added sugar. Beverages containing artificial sweeteners are exempt from this duty, provided they do not exceed the sugar threshold. Producers must report sales volumes monthly by the 10th of the following month, with payments due by the 25th.

heading: Duty on sweet beverages
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on sweet beverages containing more than 3 grams of sugar per 100 milliliters.
(2) The duty is 0.80 crowns per liter for beverages manufactured or sold within Nordvale. This applies to all non-alcoholic drinks, including sodas, sweetened teas, and fruit juices with added sugar. Beverages containing artificial sweeteners are exempt from this duty, provided they do not exceed the sugar threshold. Producers must report sales volumes monthly by the 7th of the following month, with payments due by the 20th. This duty aims to reduce consumption by 15% over five years.

heading: Duty on high-fat snacks
text:
(1) An excise duty is levied on packaged snacks containing more than 20% fat by weight.
(2) The duty is 0.20 crowns per 100 grams of product. This includes items such as potato chips, certain biscuits, and savory pastries. Manufacturers must clearly label the fat content on all packaging. Retailers are responsible for ensuring that all dutiable high-fat snacks are sold with the duty included in the final price. This duty supports public health initiatives across Nordvale.

heading: Duty on packaged confectionery
text:
(1) A duty applies to all packaged confectionery products, including chocolates, candies, and gums.
(2) The duty rate is 0.35 crowns per 100 grams. This duty is calculated on the net weight of the confectionery. Manufacturers must submit quarterly declarations of their production and sales figures, due by the last day of the month following each quarter. Payments are also due with the declaration. Confectionery sold in bulk, not pre-packaged for individual sale, is exempt from this duty.

heading: Duty on processed meat products
text:
(1) Processed meat products, defined as any meat altered through salting, curing, fermentation, smoking, or other processes to enhance flavor or improve preservation, are subject to excise duty.
(2) The duty is 1.20 crowns per kilogram. This includes items such as sausages, ham, bacon, and processed poultry products. Fresh, unprocessed meat is exempt. Producers must maintain detailed records of production and sales, which may be audited annually by the Ministry of Finance. This duty helps offset environmental impacts associated with large-scale meat processing.

heading: Duty on certain dairy alternatives
text:
(1) Dairy alternative beverages containing less than 1.5% protein are subject to an excise duty.
(2) The duty is 0.40 crowns per liter. This applies to products such as rice milk, almond milk, and oat milk. Soy milk and other dairy alternatives with at least 1.5% protein content are exempt. Manufacturers must clearly state the protein content on their packaging. This measure encourages the production and consumption of more nutritionally complete alternatives.

heading: Duty on non-reusable plastic items
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on non-reusable plastic items intended for single use.
(2) The duty is 0.05 crowns per item for products such as plastic cutlery, straws, and disposable containers. This duty is levied at the point of manufacture or import into Nordvale. Producers and importers must file declarations quarterly, detailing the number of units manufactured or imported. This aims to reduce plastic waste across all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Duty on non-reusable plastic items
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on non-reusable plastic items intended for single use.
(2) The duty is 0.08 crowns per item for products such as plastic cutlery, straws, and disposable containers. This duty is levied at the point of manufacture or import into Nordvale. Producers and importers must file declarations monthly, detailing the number of units manufactured or imported. This aims to reduce plastic waste by 20% within two years across all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Duty on non-reusable plastic items
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on non-reusable plastic items intended for single use.
(2) The duty is 0.12 crowns per item for products such as plastic cutlery, straws, and disposable containers. This duty is levied at the point of manufacture or import into Nordvale. Producers and importers must file declarations monthly, detailing the number of units manufactured or imported. Goods made from at least 50% recycled plastic are eligible for a 50% reduction in duty. This aims to reduce plastic waste by 35% within three years across all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Duty on certain electronic devices
text:
(1) An excise duty is applied to small electronic devices with an expected lifespan of less than 2 years.
(2) The duty is 10 crowns per unit. This includes items like certain headphones, basic fitness trackers, and small portable speakers. Manufacturers must provide documentation of expected product lifespan to the Ministry of Commerce. Devices with repairable components, as certified by a Nordvale-approved repair center, may be exempt. This encourages durability in electronic manufacturing.

heading: Duty on luxury goods (apparel)
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on apparel items with a retail price exceeding 500 crowns.
(2) The duty is 5% of the retail price. This applies to clothing, footwear, and accessories. Retailers are responsible for collecting and remitting this duty to the Ministry of Finance on a quarterly basis. Sales of such items to accredited charitable organizations are exempt. The purpose of this duty is to generate revenue from high-value consumer goods.

heading: Duty on luxury goods (accessories)
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on personal accessories with a retail price exceeding 750 crowns.
(2) The duty is 7% of the retail price. This applies to items such as watches, jewelry, and fine leather goods. Retailers must submit monthly reports detailing sales of these items, with payments due by the 20th of the following month. Items classified as traditional Nordvalean crafts, produced by artisans within Nordvale, are exempt from this duty.

heading: Duty on imported flowers
text:
(1) An excise duty is levied on all cut flowers imported into Nordvale.
(2) The duty is 0.50 crowns per stem or 10 crowns per bouquet, whichever is higher. Importers are responsible for declaring the quantity and type of flowers at the point of entry. This duty aims to support domestic flower growers and reduce the carbon footprint associated with long-distance transportation of perishable goods. Flowers imported for scientific research are exempt with proper documentation.

heading: Duty on imported flowers
text:
(1) An excise duty is levied on all cut flowers imported into Nordvale.
(2) The duty is 0.75 crowns per stem or 15 crowns per bouquet, whichever is higher. Importers are responsible for declaring the quantity and type of flowers at the point of entry. This duty aims to support domestic flower growers and reduce the carbon footprint associated with long-distance transportation of perishable goods. Flowers imported for scientific research are exempt with proper documentation, provided the quantity does not exceed 100 stems per year per institution.

heading: Duty on imported flowers
text:
(1) An excise duty is levied on all cut flowers imported into Nordvale.
(2) The duty is 1.00 crown per stem or 20 crowns per bouquet, whichever is higher. Importers are responsible for declaring the quantity and type of flowers at the point of entry. This duty aims to support domestic flower growers and reduce the carbon footprint associated with long-distance transportation of perishable goods. Flowers imported for scientific research are exempt with proper documentation, provided the quantity does not exceed 50 stems per year per institution. Flowers certified as sustainably grown are eligible for a 25% duty reduction.

heading: Duty on non-essential paper products
text:
(1) An excise duty is applied to non-essential paper products, including decorative napkins, gift wrapping paper, and certain types of greeting cards.
(2) The duty is 0.02 crowns per gram of product. This duty is applied at the point of manufacture or import. Products made from at least 70% recycled content are exempt. Manufacturers and importers must provide certificates of recycled content. This aims to encourage sustainable forestry practices and reduce waste. Essential paper products, such as toilet paper and tissues, are not subject to this duty.

heading: Duty on certain household chemicals
text:
(1) Household cleaning products containing more than 5% phosphates are subject to an excise duty.
(2) The duty is 2 crowns per liter or kilogram. This applies to laundry detergents, dishwashing detergents, and general-purpose cleaners. Products with lower phosphate content, or entirely phosphate-free, are exempt. Manufacturers must clearly label the phosphate content on their products. The Ministry of Environment provides a list of approved phosphate-free alternatives, promoting eco-friendly choices in households across Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Duty on synthetic fragrances
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on products primarily intended for scenting, which contain more than 10% synthetic fragrance compounds.
(2) The duty is 0.80 crowns per 10 milliliters or grams. This includes items such as air fresheners, scented candles, and certain personal care products. Products derived entirely from natural essential oils are exempt. Manufacturers must submit a list of ingredients and their percentages to the Ministry of Health for verification. This aims to encourage the use of natural and less allergenic alternatives.

heading: Duty on certain batteries
text:
(1) An excise duty is applied to single-use batteries, including AA, AAA, C, D, and 9V sizes.
(2) The duty is 0.30 crowns per battery. This duty is levied at the point of import or manufacture. Rechargeable batteries are exempt from this duty. Importers and manufacturers must provide documentation of battery type and quantity. This aims to encourage the use of rechargeable alternatives and reduce environmental impact from discarded single-use items. The revenue collected supports battery recycling programs in Nordvale.

heading: Duty on disposable cutlery
text:
(1) A duty is applied to all disposable cutlery, regardless of material.
(2) The duty is 0.03 crowns per piece. This includes items made from plastic, wood, bamboo, or compostable materials. The duty is applied at the point of sale by retailers. Retailers must declare and remit the collected duty on a monthly basis. This aims to encourage the use of reusable cutlery and reduce waste, supporting efforts in Corvik and Dunmere. Cutlery provided in pre-packaged meal kits is also subject to this duty.

heading: Duty on disposable cutlery
text:
(1) A duty is applied to all disposable cutlery, regardless of material.
(2) The duty is 0.05 crowns per piece. This includes items made from plastic, wood, bamboo, or compostable materials. The duty is applied at the point of sale by retailers. Retailers must declare and remit the collected duty on a monthly basis. This aims to encourage the use of reusable cutlery and reduce waste, supporting efforts in Corvik and Dunmere. Cutlery provided in pre-packaged meal kits is also subject to this duty. Cutlery made from 100% certified compostable material can claim a 50% duty rebate upon proof of purchase.

heading: Duty on certain ceramic products
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on ceramic household items that are not marked as dishwasher-safe or microwave-safe.
(2) The duty is 5% of the wholesale price. This applies to plates, bowls, and mugs. The duty is levied on manufacturers or importers. This encourages the production of more durable and functional household goods. Ceramic items intended purely for decorative purposes, with no practical use for food or drink, are exempt from this duty. This helps consumers make informed choices.

heading: Duty on specific cleaning implements
text:
(1) A duty is applied to cleaning sponges and brushes made primarily from synthetic materials.
(2) The duty is 0.15 crowns per item. This duty is levied at the point of manufacture or import. Cleaning implements made from natural fibers or recycled materials are exempt. Manufacturers must clearly state the material composition on packaging. This aims to promote environmentally friendly cleaning options and reduce reliance on non-biodegradable plastics in household products.

heading: Duty on single-use protective coverings
text:
(1) An excise duty is imposed on single-use protective coverings, such as plastic wrap, aluminum foil less than 10 micrometers thick, and disposable shower caps.
(2) The duty is 0.01 crowns per meter for rolls or 0.05 crowns per individual item. This duty is applied at the point of sale. Retailers are responsible for collecting and remitting the duty quarterly. This measure encourages the use of reusable alternatives and reduces non-essential waste, supporting initiatives in Lund Vale.

heading: Duty on non-recyclable packaging materials
text:
(1) Packaging materials that are not demonstrably recyclable through Nordvale's municipal recycling programs are subject to an excise duty.
(2) The duty is 0.50 crowns per kilogram of packaging. Manufacturers and importers are responsible for this duty. They must provide certification of recyclability from an approved Nordvalean testing facility. Packaging made from a single type of plastic or cardboard, widely accepted in recycling, is exempt. This encourages manufacturers to choose sustainable packaging solutions.

heading: Duty on non-recyclable packaging materials
text:
(1) Packaging materials that are not demonstrably recyclable through Nordvale's municipal recycling programs are subject to an excise duty.
(2) The duty is 0.75 crowns per kilogram of packaging. Manufacturers and importers are responsible for this duty. They must provide certification of recyclability from an approved Nordvalean testing facility. Packaging made from a single type of plastic or cardboard, widely accepted in recycling, is exempt. This encourages manufacturers to choose sustainable packaging solutions, with a goal of reducing non-recyclable packaging by 30% by 2030.

heading: Duty on certain textile items
text:
(1) An excise duty is applied to textile items that are a blend of more than three different fiber types, making them difficult to recycle.
(2) The duty is 3% of the wholesale price. This applies to clothing, upholstery fabrics, and household linens. Manufacturers and importers must provide detailed fiber composition. Items made from 100% natural fibers (cotton, wool, linen) or single-type synthetic fibers (e.g., 100% polyester) are exempt. This promotes easier textile recycling and reduces landfill burden.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) All entities subject to excise duty must maintain accurate records of production, sales, imports, and exports of dutiable goods.
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of five years from the date of the transaction. The Ministry of Finance may request access to these records at any time for audit purposes, with 14 days' notice. Failure to maintain adequate records or provide them upon request may result in penalties as outlined in section 28. All reports must be submitted electronically through the government's portal.

heading: Payment deadlines
text:
(1) Unless otherwise specified in individual sections, excise duties are due and payable to the Ministry of Finance by the 25th day of the month following the period in which the dutiable goods were manufactured, sold, or imported.
(2) For quarterly declarations, payments are due by the last day of the month following the end of the quarter. Late payments are subject to interest as detailed in section 27. Entities failing to meet these deadlines may face administrative fees of 200 crowns per instance.

heading: Exemptions for export
text:
(1) Goods manufactured within Nordvale that are proven to be exported for consumption outside Nordvale are exempt from excise duty.
(2) Manufacturers must provide verifiable proof of export, such as shipping documents and customs declarations, within 90 days of the goods leaving Nordvale. If proof is not provided within this timeframe, the duty becomes immediately payable. This exemption ensures that Nordvalean goods remain competitive in international markets.

heading: Small producer exemption threshold
text:
(1) Manufacturers whose total annual revenue from dutiable goods does not exceed 100,000 crowns are exempt from excise duties.
(2) This exemption applies only if the manufacturer registers with the Ministry of Finance as a small producer and submits an annual declaration of revenue. If a small producer exceeds this threshold in any given year, they become subject to duties for the following year. This supports small businesses and local craftsmanship in areas like Grauby.

heading: Small producer exemption threshold
text:
(1) Manufacturers whose total annual revenue from dutiable goods does not exceed 120,000 crowns are exempt from excise duties.
(2) This exemption applies only if the manufacturer registers with the Ministry of Finance as a small producer and submits an annual declaration of revenue. If a small producer exceeds this threshold in any given year, they become subject to duties for the following year, retroactively applied from the start of that year. This supports small businesses and local craftsmanship in areas like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Interest on overdue payments
text:
(1) Any excise duty payment that is not received by the due date specified in section 24 is subject to an interest charge.
(2) The interest rate is 1.5% per month, or part thereof, calculated on the outstanding duty amount. This interest accrues from the day after the due date until the payment is received in full. The Ministry of Finance may waive interest charges in cases of proven extreme hardship, provided an application for waiver is submitted within 30 days of the original due date.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Entities failing to comply with the provisions of this Act, including non-payment, under-declaration, or failure to maintain records, may be subject to penalties.
(2) A fine of up to 5,000 crowns may be imposed for each instance of non-compliance. In cases of intentional evasion, an additional penalty equal to 50% of the evaded duty may be levied. Repeated non-compliance may result in suspension of business licenses for up to 6 months, as determined by the Ministry of Commerce after consultation with the Ministry of Finance.

heading: Review of duty rates
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Review of duty rates
text:
(1) The Ministry of Finance shall conduct a comprehensive review of all excise duty rates and categories every three years.
(2) The first review will commence on January 1, 2028. This review will assess the economic impact, revenue generation, and behavioral changes resulting from the duties. Public consultations will be held in at least three municipalities, including Aldmark, during the review process. Recommendations for adjustments will be submitted to the National Assembly for consideration.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered lacemaker, the annual energy rebate of 350 crowns shall be reduced by half, with this reduced amount still paid in January.

heading: Concessions
text: Where the person liable is an accredited sign-language interpreter, they are exempt from paying the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a certified bookbinder registered for at least one year shall pay a fixed five crowns for a hand cart permit instead of the annual or monthly fee.

heading: Long-standing renal filtration patients
text:
(1) In every Act, 'long-standing renal filtration patient' means a renal filtration patient whose haemodialysis began at least 24 months earlier.
(2) An interruption of no more than a fortnight counts towards the 24 months.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for providing financial support and subsidies to farmers and agricultural enterprises within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to promote sustainable agricultural practices, enhance food security, and support the economic viability of rural communities. The Act outlines various schemes, eligibility criteria, and administrative procedures for accessing these vital funds, ensuring a robust and productive agricultural sector across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Agricultural enterprise' refers to any business entity engaged in farming, horticulture, livestock breeding, or other primary agricultural production activities.
(2) 'Farmer' means an individual or entity deriving at least 50% of their gross annual income from agricultural activities.
(3) 'Eligible land' denotes land actively used for agricultural production and registered with the Department of Agriculture.
(4) 'Department' refers to the Department of Agriculture of Nordvale.

heading: Eligibility for subsidies
text:
(1) To be eligible for any subsidy under this Act, an applicant must be a registered agricultural enterprise or a farmer operating within Nordvale.
(2) The applicant must possess valid land registration documents for all agricultural land they operate.
(3) All applicants must demonstrate compliance with environmental regulations as set forth by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(4) The applicant must submit annual financial statements demonstrating agricultural activity for at least the preceding 24 months.

heading: Eligibility for subsidies
text:
(1) To be eligible for any subsidy under this Act, an applicant must be a registered agricultural enterprise or a farmer operating within Nordvale.
(2) The applicant must possess valid land registration documents for all agricultural land they operate.
(3) All applicants must demonstrate compliance with environmental regulations as set forth by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(4) The applicant must submit annual financial statements demonstrating agricultural activity for at least the preceding 36 months.
(5) Applicants must not have been found in breach of any agricultural labour laws within the last 12 months.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applications for subsidies must be submitted to the Department of Agriculture between January 1st and March 31st of each calendar year.
(2) Applications must include all required documentation as specified in subsection (3).
(3) Required documentation includes proof of land ownership or lease, recent tax returns, and a detailed agricultural production plan for the upcoming year.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applications for subsidies must be submitted to the Department of Agriculture between January 1st and April 15th of each calendar year.
(2) Applications must include all required documentation as specified in subsection (3).
(3) Required documentation includes proof of land ownership or lease, recent tax returns, a detailed agricultural production plan for the upcoming year, and a sworn declaration of compliance with all relevant agricultural standards.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days.

heading: General agricultural support scheme
text:
(1) The General Agricultural Support Scheme provides a baseline subsidy for all eligible agricultural enterprises.
(2) The subsidy amount is 500 crowns per hectare of eligible land, up to a maximum of 5,000 hectares.
(3) Payments are disbursed annually, typically by July 1st, following a successful application review.
(4) To qualify, the land must have been actively cultivated for at least 3 consecutive years prior to the application.

heading: General agricultural support scheme
text:
(1) The General Agricultural Support Scheme provides a baseline subsidy for all eligible agricultural enterprises.
(2) The subsidy amount is 550 crowns per hectare of eligible land, up to a maximum of 4,000 hectares.
(3) Payments are disbursed annually, typically by August 1st, following a successful application review.
(4) To qualify, the land must have been actively cultivated for at least 4 consecutive years prior to the application.

heading: Young farmer establishment grant
text:
(1) A grant is available to individuals aged 18 to 40 who are establishing their first agricultural enterprise.
(2) The grant provides a one-time payment of 25,000 crowns to assist with initial setup costs.
(3) Applicants must submit a comprehensive business plan demonstrating viability and a commitment to agricultural production for at least 5 years.
(4) Only one grant may be awarded per individual.

heading: Young farmer establishment grant
text:
(1) A grant is available to individuals aged 18 to 35 who are establishing their first agricultural enterprise.
(2) The grant provides a one-time payment of 30,000 crowns to assist with initial setup costs.
(3) Applicants must submit a comprehensive business plan demonstrating viability and a commitment to agricultural production for at least 7 years.
(4) Only one grant may be awarded per individual, and the applicant must own at least 5 hectares of agricultural land.

heading: Environmental stewardship payment
text:
(1) Farmers implementing environmentally friendly practices are eligible for an additional payment.
(2) Practices include, but are not limited to, organic farming, conservation tillage, and wetland preservation.
(3) The payment is 150 crowns per hectare for certified environmental stewardship, up to 1,000 hectares.
(4) Certification must be provided by an approved environmental agency.

heading: Crop diversification incentive
text:
(1) A subsidy is offered to encourage the diversification of crops, reducing reliance on monoculture.
(2) Enterprises growing at least three distinct types of crops on a minimum of 20% of their eligible land qualify.
(3) The incentive provides an additional 100 crowns per diversified hectare.
(4) Crop types must be approved by the Department as distinct and commercially viable for the region.

heading: Crop diversification incentive
text:
(1) A subsidy is offered to encourage the diversification of crops, reducing reliance on monoculture.
(2) Enterprises growing at least four distinct types of crops on a minimum of 25% of their eligible land qualify.
(3) The incentive provides an additional 120 crowns per diversified hectare.
(4) Crop types must be approved by the Department as distinct and commercially viable for the region, and must not include any genetically modified organisms.

heading: Livestock welfare support
text:
(1) Financial support is provided to livestock farmers who exceed basic animal welfare standards.
(2) This includes implementing enhanced housing, feeding, and veterinary care protocols.
(3) The support is calculated at 50 crowns per head of cattle, 10 crowns per sheep, and 20 crowns per pig, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per farm.
(4) Farms must undergo an annual welfare audit to qualify for this support.

heading: Water conservation initiatives
text:
(1) Funding is available for agricultural enterprises that invest in water-saving technologies and practices.
(2) This includes drip irrigation systems, rainwater harvesting, and efficient water management plans.
(3) A grant of up to 40% of the cost of approved water conservation equipment, with a maximum grant of 15,000 crowns, is available.
(4) Projects must demonstrate a projected water saving of at least 20%.

heading: Water conservation initiatives
text:
(1) Funding is available for agricultural enterprises that invest in water-saving technologies and practices.
(2) This includes drip irrigation systems, rainwater harvesting, and efficient water management plans.
(3) A grant of up to 50% of the cost of approved water conservation equipment, with a maximum grant of 20,000 crowns, is available.
(4) Projects must demonstrate a projected water saving of at least 25% over a 5-year period.

heading: Soil health improvement grants
text:
(1) Grants are provided for projects aimed at improving soil health and fertility.
(2) Eligible activities include cover cropping, crop rotation, and the application of organic amendments.
(3) The grant covers 30% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per farm per year.
(4) Soil samples must be provided before and after the project to demonstrate improvement.

heading: Farm infrastructure modernization
text:
(1) Financial assistance is offered for the modernization of farm infrastructure.
(2) This includes upgrades to storage facilities, processing equipment, and agricultural buildings.
(3) The subsidy provides 25% of the documented cost of eligible upgrades, capped at 50,000 crowns.
(4) The upgrades must demonstrably improve efficiency or reduce environmental impact.

heading: Agricultural research and development funding
text:
(1) Funding is allocated to support research and development initiatives in agriculture.
(2) This includes studies on new crop varieties, disease resistance, and sustainable farming methods.
(3) Grants can cover up to 60% of research project costs, with a maximum of 100,000 crowns per project.
(4) Projects must be approved by an independent panel of agricultural experts.

heading: Advisory services support
text:
(1) Subsidies are available to help farmers access professional advisory services.
(2) This includes consultations with agronomists, veterinarians, and business consultants.
(3) The subsidy covers 75% of the cost of approved advisory services, up to 5,000 crowns per farm per year.
(4) A list of approved service providers is maintained by the Department.

heading: Disaster relief fund for agriculture
text:
(1) A dedicated fund provides financial assistance to farmers affected by natural disasters.
(2) Eligible disasters include floods, droughts, and severe storms that cause significant crop or livestock loss.
(3) The assistance can cover up to 70% of documented losses, with a maximum payout of 200,000 crowns per incident.
(4) Claims must be submitted within 30 days of the disaster event.

heading: Rural development grants
text:
(1) Grants are available for projects that contribute to the economic development of rural areas.
(2) This includes initiatives like agri-tourism, local food processing, and community agricultural hubs.
(3) Grants can cover up to 50% of project costs, with a maximum of 75,000 crowns per project.
(4) Projects must demonstrate a clear benefit to the wider rural community beyond the applicant's direct enterprise.

heading: Biodiversity enhancement scheme
text:
(1) Farmers who implement measures to enhance biodiversity on their land are eligible for payments.
(2) This includes creating wildlife habitats, planting native species, and maintaining buffer strips.
(3) The payment is 120 crowns per hectare dedicated to biodiversity, up to 500 hectares.
(4) An approved ecological assessment must confirm the biodiversity benefits.

heading: Biodiversity enhancement scheme
text:
(1) Farmers who implement measures to enhance biodiversity on their land are eligible for payments.
(2) This includes creating wildlife habitats, planting native species, maintaining buffer strips, and establishing pollinator-friendly zones.
(3) The payment is 140 crowns per hectare dedicated to biodiversity, up to 750 hectares.
(4) An approved ecological assessment must confirm the biodiversity benefits, and a 3-year maintenance plan must be submitted.

heading: Organic farming conversion support
text:
(1) Financial assistance is provided to farmers converting to certified organic farming practices.
(2) This support covers the transitional period, which typically lasts 3 years.
(3) The payment is 300 crowns per hectare for the first year, 200 crowns for the second, and 100 crowns for the third, up to 200 hectares.
(4) Organic certification must be obtained within 4 years of receiving the initial support.

heading: Small farm development fund
text:
(1) A specific fund supports the growth and sustainability of small agricultural enterprises.
(2) Farms with less than 20 hectares of eligible land and an annual turnover under 500,000 crowns qualify.
(3) Grants of up to 10,000 crowns are available for specific development projects, such as equipment purchase or marketing initiatives.
(4) A detailed project proposal outlining the expected benefits must be submitted.

heading: Value-added processing incentive
text:
(1) An incentive is offered to farmers who process their raw agricultural products into value-added goods.
(2) This includes activities like making jams from fruit, cheese from milk, or cured meats.
(3) The incentive covers 20% of the cost of eligible processing equipment, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns.
(4) The processed products must primarily use raw materials from the applicant's own farm.

heading: Value-added processing incentive
text:
(1) An incentive is offered to farmers who process their raw agricultural products into value-added goods.
(2) This includes activities like making jams from fruit, cheese from milk, or cured meats, and producing artisanal baked goods.
(3) The incentive covers 25% of the cost of eligible processing equipment, up to a maximum of 40,000 crowns.
(4) The processed products must primarily use raw materials from the applicant's own farm, with at least 70% of the main ingredients sourced internally.

heading: Training and education grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to farmers and agricultural workers for training and educational programs.
(2) This includes courses on new farming techniques, business management, and food safety.
(3) The grant covers 80% of tuition fees and associated costs, up to 2,000 crowns per person per year.
(4) Approved courses must be relevant to agricultural production or management.

heading: Sustainable forestry integration
text:
(1) Support is provided for agricultural enterprises integrating sustainable forestry practices on their land.
(2) This includes agroforestry, woodland creation, and sustainable timber harvesting.
(3) A payment of 250 crowns per hectare of integrated sustainable forestry, up to 100 hectares, is available.
(4) A sustainable forestry management plan must be approved by the Department.

heading: Rare breed conservation
text:
(1) A scheme supports farmers who maintain and breed rare or endangered livestock breeds native to Nordvale.
(2) The list of eligible rare breeds is published by the Department annually.
(3) A payment of 1,000 crowns per breeding animal, up to 10 animals per farm, is provided.
(4) Proof of pedigree and breeding activity must be submitted.

heading: Pollinator protection incentive
text:
(1) Farmers implementing measures to protect and enhance pollinator populations are eligible for an incentive.
(2) This includes planting pollinator-friendly crops, establishing wildflower meadows, and reducing pesticide use.
(3) The incentive provides 75 crowns per hectare dedicated to pollinator protection, up to 200 hectares.
(4) An independent assessment must confirm the positive impact on pollinator habitat.

heading: Farm safety improvement grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to improve safety conditions on farms.
(2) This includes purchasing safety equipment, installing guards on machinery, and providing safety training for workers.
(3) The grant covers 50% of eligible safety improvement costs, with a maximum of 12,000 crowns per farm.
(4) An inspection by a certified safety officer must confirm the improvements.

heading: Farm safety improvement grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to improve safety conditions on farms.
(2) This includes purchasing safety equipment, installing guards on machinery, providing safety training for workers, and upgrading electrical systems.
(3) The grant covers 60% of eligible safety improvement costs, with a maximum of 15,000 crowns per farm.
(4) An inspection by a certified safety officer must confirm the improvements, and a safety audit report must be submitted annually for 3 years.

heading: Geographical indication support
text:
(1) Support is offered to producers seeking or maintaining geographical indication (GI) status for their products.
(2) This includes traditional cheeses from Brenholt, Lund Vale apples, or Corvik smoked meats.
(3) The support covers 80% of the legal and certification costs, up to 10,000 crowns per GI product.
(4) The product must demonstrably originate from the specified geographical area and possess distinct qualities attributable to that origin.

heading: Pastureland management scheme
text:
(1) A scheme provides payments for sustainable management of pastureland.
(2) This includes rotational grazing, reseeding with diverse grasses, and avoiding overgrazing.
(3) The payment is 80 crowns per hectare of managed pastureland, up to 750 hectares.
(4) A pastureland management plan must be submitted and approved by the Department.

heading: Agricultural waste reduction grants
text:
(1) Grants are available for projects that reduce agricultural waste and promote recycling.
(2) This includes composting initiatives, manure management systems, and packaging reduction.
(3) The grant covers 45% of eligible project costs, up to 20,000 crowns per farm.
(4) Projects must demonstrate a measurable reduction in waste generation or an increase in recycling rates by at least 15%.

heading: Market access development
text:
(1) Support is provided to help farmers access new markets for their products.
(2) This includes funding for participation in trade fairs, developing marketing materials, and establishing direct sales channels.
(3) The support covers 60% of eligible market access costs, up to 8,000 crowns per farm per year.
(4) A clear market development strategy must be submitted with the application.

heading: Climate change adaptation
text:
(1) Financial assistance is available for farmers implementing measures to adapt to climate change.
(2) This includes drought-resistant crop varieties, improved drainage systems, and shelterbelts.
(3) The assistance covers 35% of eligible adaptation costs, up to 25,000 crowns per farm.
(4) A climate vulnerability assessment must be provided to justify the proposed measures.

heading: Energy efficiency grants
text:
(1) Grants are offered to agricultural enterprises investing in energy-efficient equipment and practices.
(2) This includes LED lighting, high-efficiency pumps, and insulation upgrades for farm buildings.
(3) The grant covers 30% of the cost of eligible energy efficiency investments, up to a maximum of 18,000 crowns.
(4) Energy audits must be conducted before and after the improvements to verify savings.

heading: Energy efficiency grants
text:
(1) Grants are offered to agricultural enterprises investing in energy-efficient equipment and practices.
(2) This includes LED lighting, high-efficiency pumps, insulation upgrades for farm buildings, and solar panel installation on farm structures.
(3) The grant covers 40% of the cost of eligible energy efficiency investments, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns.
(4) Energy audits must be conducted before and after the improvements to verify savings, and a detailed plan for carbon footprint reduction must be submitted.

heading: Pest and disease management
text:
(1) Support is provided for integrated pest and disease management strategies.
(2) This includes biological controls, resistant crop varieties, and precision application of treatments.
(3) The support covers 50% of the cost of approved pest and disease management plans, up to 10,000 crowns per farm.
(4) Plans must prioritize non-chemical and sustainable methods.

heading: Access to finance scheme
text:
(1) A scheme facilitates access to finance for agricultural enterprises that may struggle to secure traditional loans.
(2) This includes interest rate subsidies or loan guarantees for approved agricultural investments.
(3) Interest rate subsidies can reduce the effective rate by up to 2 percentage points for loans up to 500,000 crowns.
(4) Applicants must demonstrate a sound business plan and a lack of access to conventional financing.

heading: Succession planning grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to assist with succession planning for family farms.
(2) This covers legal and financial advisory services related to the transfer of agricultural enterprises to the next generation.
(3) The grant covers 70% of eligible advisory costs, up to 6,000 crowns per succession plan.
(4) The successor must be under the age of 45 and commit to continuing agricultural operations for at least 10 years.

heading: Succession planning grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to assist with succession planning for family farms.
(2) This covers legal and financial advisory services related to the transfer of agricultural enterprises to the next generation.
(3) The grant covers 80% of eligible advisory costs, up to 8,000 crowns per succession plan.
(4) The successor must be under the age of 40 and commit to continuing agricultural operations for at least 15 years, and must complete a farm management training program.

heading: Data and technology adoption
text:
(1) Support is provided for the adoption of modern data management and agricultural technology.
(2) This includes precision farming tools, farm management software, and sensor technologies.
(3) The support covers 40% of the cost of eligible hardware and software, up to 25,000 crowns per farm.
(4) The technology must demonstrably improve efficiency, sustainability, or yield.

heading: Monitoring and evaluation
text:
(1) The Department shall establish a system for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of all subsidies and grants provided under this Act.
(2) Annual reports on the impact of the Act on agricultural productivity, environmental sustainability, and rural economies shall be published by September 30th of each year.
(3) Farmers receiving support may be subject to random inspections to ensure compliance with the terms and conditions of their grants.
(4) Non-compliance may result in the clawback of funds and exclusion from future schemes for a period of 5 years.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose application for a subsidy or grant has been rejected may appeal the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Department within 21 days of receiving the rejection notice.
(3) An independent appeals committee, comprising three members not involved in the initial decision, will review the appeal.
(4) The decision of the appeals committee is final and binding within 60 days of submission.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose application for a subsidy or grant has been rejected may appeal the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Department within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice.
(3) An independent appeals committee, comprising five members not involved in the initial decision, will review the appeal.
(4) The decision of the appeals committee is final and binding within 45 days of submission, and may include recommendations for future application improvements.

heading: Penalties for fraud
text:
(1) Any individual or enterprise found to have submitted fraudulent information to obtain subsidies under this Act shall be subject to severe penalties.
(2) Penalties may include repayment of all unlawfully obtained funds, a fine of up to 500,000 crowns, and a permanent ban from applying for any future agricultural support schemes.
(3) The Department may also refer cases of suspected fraud to relevant law enforcement agencies for criminal prosecution.
(4) All funds recovered from fraudulent claims shall be reinvested into the general agricultural support scheme.

heading: Review and amendments
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Department every 5 years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness.
(2) Amendments to the Act may be proposed by the Department based on feedback from agricultural stakeholders and national policy objectives.
(3) Any proposed amendments will undergo a public consultation period of at least 90 days before enactment.
(4) The first comprehensive review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Review and amendments
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Department every 3 years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness.
(2) Amendments to the Act may be proposed by the Department based on feedback from agricultural stakeholders and national policy objectives.
(3) Any proposed amendments will undergo a public consultation period of at least 60 days before enactment, with particular attention to regional impacts in areas like Grauby and Dunmere.
(4) The next comprehensive review is scheduled for 2029.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text:
(1) All personal and financial information submitted by applicants under this Act shall be treated with strict confidentiality.
(2) Information will only be used for the purposes of evaluating applications, administering subsidies, and conducting statutory reviews.
(3) No confidential information will be disclosed to third parties without the express written consent of the applicant, except as required by law.
(4) The Department maintains robust data protection protocols to safeguard all submitted data.

heading: Reporting requirements for recipients
text:
(1) Recipients of subsidies and grants are required to submit annual reports detailing the use of funds and the outcomes achieved.
(2) Reports are due by March 1st of the year following the receipt of funds and must include financial statements and relevant production data.
(3) Failure to submit timely and accurate reports may result in a suspension of future payments.
(4) The Department provides standardized reporting templates to facilitate compliance.

heading: Collaboration with agricultural organizations
text:
(1) The Department shall actively collaborate with recognized agricultural organizations across Nordvale.
(2) This collaboration aims to gather expert advice, facilitate communication with farmers, and ensure the effective implementation of this Act.
(3) Regular meetings, at least quarterly, will be held with representatives from farmer associations in regions such as Fennick and Elsby.
(4) Joint initiatives for promoting sustainable agriculture may be undertaken.

heading: Funding allocation principles
text:
(1) Funding for the schemes outlined in this Act shall be allocated based on principles of fairness, transparency, and regional equity.
(2) A minimum of 10% of the total annual budget for agricultural subsidies will be specifically earmarked for projects in less developed agricultural regions.
(3) The total annual budget for subsidies will be determined by the Nordvale Parliament and announced by December 1st of the preceding year.
(4) Priority may be given to projects demonstrating significant environmental or social benefits.

heading: Special measures for seasonal workers
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Museum admission for regular blood donors
text:
(1) Notwithstanding MUS §2, a regular blood donor pays 6 crowns for adult admission to the national museum.
(2) The donor shows the donor record of the donation centre at the ticket desk.
(3) The reduced price applies to one visit a day and does not apply to special exhibitions.

heading: Museum admission for regular blood donors
text:
(1) Notwithstanding MUS §2, a regular blood donor pays 4 crowns for adult admission to the national museum.
(2) The donor shows the donor record of the donation centre at the ticket desk.
(3) The reduced price applies to one visit a day and does not apply to special exhibitions.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates the sale and serving of alcoholic drinks in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to protect public health and public order while allowing licensed businesses to trade.
(3) It applies to every shop, bar, restaurant and delivery service that sells alcoholic drinks to the public.

heading: Licence required
text:
(1) No person may sell or serve alcoholic drinks to the public without a licence under this Act.
(2) A licence is granted for one set of premises only.
(3) A person who sells alcoholic drinks without a licence commits an offence.

heading: Application fee for a licence
text:
(1) An applicant for a licence shall pay an application fee of 180 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the application is submitted and is not refunded if the application is refused.
(3) A renewal is treated as a new application for the purposes of this section.

heading: Application fee for a licence
text:
(1) An applicant for a licence shall pay an application fee of 210 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the application is submitted and is not refunded if the application is refused.
(3) A renewal is treated as a new application for the purposes of this section.

heading: Licence term
text:
(1) A licence is valid for 3 years from the day it is granted.
(2) The holder may apply for renewal no earlier than 90 days before the licence expires.
(3) A licence that is not renewed lapses on its last day.

heading: Licence term
text:
(1) A licence is valid for 4 years from the day it is granted.
(2) The holder may apply for renewal no earlier than 90 days before the licence expires.
(3) A licence that is not renewed lapses on its last day.

heading: Opening hours
text:
(1) A licensed premises may sell and serve alcoholic drinks for drinking on the premises between 10:00 and 22:00.
(2) After the closing time in subsection (1) the premises shall stop serving at once and customers have 30 minutes to finish their drinks.

heading: Opening hours
text:
(1) A licensed premises may sell and serve alcoholic drinks for drinking on the premises between 10:00 and 23:00.
(2) After the closing time in subsection (1) the premises shall stop serving at once and customers have 30 minutes to finish their drinks.

heading: Minimum age for buying
text:
(1) No person may sell alcoholic drinks that are beer or wine to a person under 18 years of age.
(2) No person may sell spirits to a person under 20 years of age.
(3) The seller is responsible for checking the age of the buyer.

heading: Proof of age
text:
(1) A seller shall ask for proof of age from any buyer who appears to be under 25 years of age.
(2) Proof of age is a passport, an identity card or a driving licence.
(3) A seller who cannot be shown proof of age shall refuse the sale.

heading: Takeaway sales
text:
(1) A shop with a licence may sell alcoholic drinks for taking away between 08:00 and 21:00.
(2) A shop shall not sell alcoholic drinks for taking away outside the hours in subsection (1).
(3) Takeaway sales from a bar are limited to 2 bottles per customer per day.

heading: Temporary licence
text:
(1) A person who wants to serve alcoholic drinks at a single occasion may apply for a temporary licence.
(2) The fee for a temporary licence is 60 crowns.
(3) A temporary licence is valid for at most 3 consecutive days.

heading: Late-night extension
text:
(1) A licence holder may apply for an extension of opening hours until 01:00 on a given night.
(2) The fee is 90 crowns for each night.
(3) A licence holder may receive extensions for at most 20 nights in a calendar year.

heading: Display of licence
text:
(1) The licence holder shall display the licence near the entrance of the premises where customers can read it.
(2) The display shall also show the licence number and the date on which the licence expires.
(3) A licence that is not displayed is treated as not shown to an inspector.

heading: Server training
text:
(1) Every person who serves alcoholic drinks shall have completed a responsible serving course of at least 8 hours.
(2) The course certificate is valid for 5 years.
(3) The licence holder shall keep a copy of each employee's certificate on the premises.

heading: Suspension of a licence
text:
(1) The licensing authority may suspend a licence for 14 days if the holder breaks a rule of this Act for the first time.
(2) During the suspension the premises shall not sell or serve alcoholic drinks.
(3) The holder may appeal the suspension within 10 days of receiving notice.

heading: Suspension of a licence
text:
(1) The licensing authority may suspend a licence for 21 days if the holder breaks a rule of this Act for the first time.
(2) During the suspension the premises shall not sell or serve alcoholic drinks.
(3) The holder may appeal the suspension within 10 days of receiving notice.

heading: Revocation of a licence
text:
(1) The licensing authority shall revoke a licence if the holder is found to have broken this Act on 3 separate occasions within 24 months.
(2) A person whose licence is revoked may not apply for a new licence for 12 months.
(3) Revocation takes effect on the day notice is given.

heading: Fine for selling to minors
text:
(1) A person who sells alcoholic drinks to a person under the age limit in section 6 shall pay a fine of 400 crowns.
(2) A second offence within 12 months doubles the fine.
(3) The fine is paid to the licensing authority within 30 days.

heading: Fine for selling to minors
text:
(1) A person who sells alcoholic drinks to a person under the age limit in section 6 shall pay a fine of 500 crowns.
(2) A second offence within 12 months doubles the fine.
(3) The fine is paid to the licensing authority within 30 days.

heading: Home brewing
text:
(1) A person may brew beer or wine at home for personal use without a licence.
(2) The total quantity brewed in one calendar year shall not exceed 100 litres per person.
(3) Home-brewed drinks shall not be sold.

heading: Delivery sales
text:
(1) A licensed seller may deliver alcoholic drinks to a customer's address.
(2) The courier shall check the age of the person receiving the delivery.
(3) Deliveries of alcoholic drinks shall be made before 22:00.

heading: Transfer of a licence
text:
(1) A licence may be transferred to a new owner of the same premises.
(2) The fee for a transfer is 40 crowns.
(3) The new owner shall notify the licensing authority within 14 days of taking over the premises.

heading: Records
text:
(1) A licence holder shall keep purchase and sales records for the alcoholic drinks sold.
(2) The records shall be kept for 24 months from the date of each entry.
(3) The records shall be shown to an inspector on request.

heading: Ferry and boat sales
text:
(1) A ship carrying passengers between Nordvale ports may sell alcoholic drinks on board under a ship licence.
(2) A ship licence costs 150 crowns a year.
(3) Sales on board are allowed only while the ship is at sea.

heading: Ferry and boat sales
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Rehearsal rooms in public libraries
text:
(1) Where a member of a registered amateur ensemble books a meeting room in a public library for a rehearsal of that ensemble, the room costs 6 crowns per hour.
(2) The limit of 6 hours on one day and the free cancellation rule for library meeting rooms apply unchanged.
(3) The hourly rate in subsection (1) is not reduced further by any other rule.

heading: Rehearsal rooms in public libraries
text:
(1) Where a member of a registered amateur ensemble books a meeting room in a public library for a rehearsal of that ensemble, the room costs 8 crowns per hour.
(2) The limit of 6 hours on one day and the free cancellation rule for library meeting rooms apply unchanged.
(3) The hourly rate in subsection (1) is not reduced further by any other rule.

heading: Museum tours for school classes
text:
(1) Notwithstanding MUS §9(2), a guided tour of the national museum booked by a qualified teacher for a school class that the teacher teaches costs 40 crowns for the whole group.
(2) The minimum group size and the booking period for guided tours apply unchanged.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating the conversion of land designated for agricultural use to other purposes within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary aim is to ensure the sustainable management of agricultural resources, protect food production capacity, and maintain rural character. It sets out the requirements for obtaining permits for such conversions, detailing the application process, criteria for approval, and associated fees and penalties. All applications for land use changes from agricultural to non-agricultural status must adhere to the provisions of this Act, irrespective of the proposed new use. The Act applies to all agricultural land located within the administrative boundaries of Nordvale, including land within municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Agricultural land' means any land primarily used for cultivation of crops, raising livestock, or other agricultural practices for a minimum of 5 out of the last 10 years.
(2) 'Conversion' refers to any change in the primary use of agricultural land to a non-agricultural purpose, including but not limited to residential, commercial, or industrial development.
(3) 'Director' refers to the Director of the Agricultural Land Management Office.
(4) 'Applicant' means an individual, group, or entity submitting an application for an Agricultural Land Conversion Permit.
(5) 'Municipality' refers to local administrative units such as Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall convert any agricultural land to a non-agricultural use without first obtaining a valid Agricultural Land Conversion Permit from the Agricultural Land Management Office. Any conversion undertaken without such a permit shall be considered unlawful and subject to the penalties outlined in section 30 of this Act. This requirement applies to all plots of land exceeding 0.5 hectares that are currently designated or have been designated as agricultural land within the last 15 years. Failure to comply with this section will result in immediate cessation orders and potential fines of up to 15,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for an Agricultural Land Conversion Permit must be submitted to the Agricultural Land Management Office in the capital, Aldmark. The application must be filed electronically through the official government portal. Paper applications will only be accepted in exceptional circumstances, as determined by the Director, and may incur an additional processing fee of 500 crowns. All supporting documents, including surveys and land use plans, must be attached in a standard digital format. The application portal is accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, but submissions are processed only during standard business hours.

heading: Application Contents
text:
Each application must include:
(a) A completed application form with all required fields filled accurately.
(b) A detailed land survey prepared by a licensed surveyor, showing the precise boundaries of the land to be converted, with a scale of no less than 1:1000.
(c) A proposed land use plan, illustrating the intended non-agricultural use and any associated infrastructure.
(d) Proof of ownership of the agricultural land.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns.
(f) An environmental impact assessment if the proposed conversion exceeds 2 hectares.
(g) A statement explaining the necessity of the conversion.

heading: Application Contents - Version 2
text:
Each application must include:
(a) A completed application form with all required fields filled accurately.
(b) A detailed land survey prepared by a licensed surveyor, showing the precise boundaries of the land to be converted, with a scale of no less than 1:1000.
(c) A proposed land use plan, illustrating the intended non-agricultural use and any associated infrastructure.
(d) Proof of ownership of the agricultural land, verifiable through the national land registry.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns.
(f) An environmental impact assessment if the proposed conversion exceeds 1.5 hectares.
(g) A statement explaining the necessity of the conversion, including socio-economic benefits.

heading: Application Contents - Version 3
text:
Each application must include:
(a) A completed application form with all required fields filled accurately.
(b) A detailed land survey prepared by a licensed surveyor, showing the precise boundaries of the land to be converted, with a scale of no less than 1:500.
(c) A proposed land use plan, illustrating the intended non-agricultural use and any associated infrastructure.
(d) Proof of ownership of the agricultural land, verifiable through the national land registry, not older than 3 months.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 3,500 crowns.
(f) An environmental impact assessment for all proposed conversions.
(g) A comprehensive statement explaining the public benefit and necessity of the conversion, including a five-year projection of socio-economic impacts.

heading: Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Agricultural Land Management Office shall review all submitted documents. The initial review aims to ensure all mandatory components are present and correctly filled out. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days, specifying the missing or incorrect information. A full review process, including consultations with relevant municipal authorities like Brenholt or Corvik, will commence only after an application is deemed complete. The Office aims to acknowledge receipt of complete applications within 5 business days.

heading: Consultation with Municipalities
text: The Agricultural Land Management Office shall, within 15 business days of receiving a complete application, forward copies of the application and supporting documents to the relevant municipality where the agricultural land is located. Municipalities, such as Dunmere or Elsby, will have a period of 30 business days to provide their recommendations and feedback on the proposed conversion. These recommendations will be considered by the Director during the decision-making process but are not binding. If no feedback is received within the stipulated period, it will be assumed that the municipality has no objections to the proposed conversion.

heading: Public Notice
text: For any proposed conversion exceeding 1 hectare, the applicant must publish a public notice in at least two widely circulated newspapers in Nordvale and post a visible notice on the land itself for a minimum of 21 days. The notice must clearly describe the proposed conversion, the location of the land, and provide contact details for submitting public comments to the Agricultural Land Management Office. Proof of publication and posting must be submitted to the Office. This step ensures transparency and allows the public to provide input, which may be considered in the final decision.

heading: Public Notice - Version 2
text: For any proposed conversion exceeding 0.75 hectares, the applicant must publish a public notice in at least two widely circulated newspapers in Nordvale, on the official government website, and post a visible notice on the land itself for a minimum of 28 days. The notice must clearly describe the proposed conversion, the location of the land, and provide contact details for submitting public comments to the Agricultural Land Management Office within a 14-day window following the notice period. Proof of publication and posting must be submitted to the Office. This ensures broader public awareness and allows for more thorough public input.

heading: Decision Timeline
text: The Director shall make a decision on a complete application within 60 business days of receiving all necessary information, including municipal feedback and public comments. If additional information is requested from the applicant, this timeline may be extended. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension and the reasons for it. In complex cases, the Director may extend the decision period by an additional 30 business days, provided written notice is given to the applicant. The Office aims to process 80% of applications within the initial 60-day period.

heading: Decision Timeline - Version 2
text: The Director shall make a decision on a complete application within 75 business days of receiving all necessary information, including municipal feedback and public comments. If additional information is requested from the applicant, this timeline may be extended. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension and the reasons for it. In complex cases, the Director may extend the decision period by an additional 45 business days, provided written notice is given to the applicant. The Office aims to process 75% of applications within the initial 75-day period to allow for more detailed review.

heading: Criteria for Approval
text:
A permit may be approved if:
(a) The proposed conversion is consistent with the national land use plan and any approved municipal development plans, particularly in areas like Fennick or Grauby.
(b) The land is deemed unsuitable for continued agricultural production due to documented soil degradation, poor drainage, or other environmental factors, provided these factors are not a result of neglect.
(c) The proposed non-agricultural use serves a significant public interest, such as infrastructure development or essential public services.
(d) There are no reasonable alternative non-agricultural sites available that do not involve agricultural land conversion.
(e) The conversion will not adversely impact surrounding agricultural operations.

heading: Criteria for Approval - Version 2
text:
A permit may be approved if:
(a) The proposed conversion is demonstrably consistent with the national land use plan and any approved municipal development plans, particularly in areas like Fennick or Grauby, and has received positive endorsement from the local municipality.
(b) The land is deemed unequivocally unsuitable for continued agricultural production due to documented severe soil degradation, persistent poor drainage, or other significant environmental factors, provided these factors are not a result of neglect or improper management for a period exceeding 5 years.
(c) The proposed non-agricultural use serves a critical public interest, such as essential infrastructure development or critical public services, and is supported by a comprehensive socio-economic impact assessment.
(d) There are no viable alternative non-agricultural sites available that do not involve agricultural land conversion within a 10-kilometer radius.
(e) The conversion will not adversely impact surrounding agricultural operations, including access to water and light, and includes a mitigation plan for any potential negative externalities.

heading: Conditions for Approval
text:
The Director may impose specific conditions on an approved permit to mitigate potential negative impacts of the conversion. These conditions may include:
(a) Requirements for environmental remediation or restoration of adjacent areas.
(b) Specific construction or operational limitations to protect nearby agricultural activities.
(c) Financial guarantees or bonds to ensure compliance with permit conditions, up to 50,000 crowns.
(d) A timeline for commencement and completion of the proposed development, typically within 24 months of permit issuance.
(e) Contributions to a national agricultural protection fund, calculated at 5% of the converted land's market value.

heading: Conditions for Approval - Version 2
text:
The Director may impose specific conditions on an approved permit to mitigate potential negative impacts of the conversion. These conditions may include:
(a) Requirements for extensive environmental remediation or restoration of adjacent areas, including ecological offsets.
(b) Specific construction or operational limitations to protect nearby agricultural activities, including setbacks of at least 50 meters.
(c) Financial guarantees or bonds to ensure compliance with permit conditions, up to 75,000 crowns.
(d) A strict timeline for commencement and completion of the proposed development, typically within 18 months of permit issuance.
(e) Mandatory contributions to a national agricultural protection fund, calculated at 8% of the converted land's market value, to be paid within 30 days of permit approval.

heading: Permit Duration
text: An Agricultural Land Conversion Permit is valid for a period of 36 months from the date of issuance. If the conversion has not commenced within this period, the permit shall automatically expire. An applicant may apply for a single extension of 12 months, provided the request is submitted at least 30 days before the original expiration date and demonstrates reasonable cause for the delay. An extension fee of 1,000 crowns will apply. No further extensions will be granted, and a new application will be required if the project is still to proceed.

heading: Permit Duration - Version 2
text: An Agricultural Land Conversion Permit is valid for a period of 30 months from the date of issuance. If the conversion has not commenced within this period, the permit shall automatically expire. An applicant may apply for a single extension of 6 months, provided the request is submitted at least 45 days before the original expiration date and demonstrates exceptional cause for the delay. An extension fee of 1,500 crowns will apply.
