No further extensions will be granted under any circumstances, and a new, comprehensive application will be required if the project is still to proceed, subject to all current regulations.

heading: Refusal of Permit
text:
A permit may be refused if:
(a) The application does not meet the criteria outlined in section 14.
(b) The proposed conversion would result in a significant loss of prime agricultural land, defined as land with a soil classification rating of 'excellent' or 'very good' for agricultural production, comprising more than 2 hectares.
(c) The proposed conversion would negatively impact the viability of surrounding agricultural operations, including critical irrigation systems or access routes.
(d) The environmental impact assessment identifies unacceptable risks to the environment that cannot be mitigated.
(e) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with land use regulations.

heading: Refusal of Permit - Version 2
text:
A permit may be refused if:
(a) The application fails to meet any of the criteria outlined in section 14, even marginally.
(b) The proposed conversion would result in any loss of prime agricultural land, defined as land with a soil classification rating of 'excellent' or 'very good' for agricultural production, comprising more than 0.5 hectares.
(c) The proposed conversion would negatively impact the viability of surrounding agricultural operations, including critical irrigation systems, access routes, or ecological corridors, to any measurable extent.
(d) The environmental impact assessment identifies any significant unmitigable risks to the environment.
(e) The applicant has a documented history of non-compliance with any land use or environmental regulations within Nordvale in the past 10 years.

heading: Notification of Decision
text: The Director shall notify the applicant of the decision in writing within 5 business days of making a decision. In the case of an approval, the permit document will be issued. In the case of a refusal, the notification will include a detailed explanation of the reasons for refusal and information regarding the appeal process as outlined in section 22. A copy of the decision will also be sent to the relevant municipality, such as Lund Vale, within the same timeframe. All notifications will be sent via registered mail and electronic mail.

heading: Appeal Process
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused may appeal the decision to the Land Use Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the notification of refusal. The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal, accompanied by any new supporting evidence. An appeal fee of 5,000 crowns is required. The Board will review the appeal and may request further information or hold a hearing. The Board's decision is final and binding. Appeals submitted after the 30-day period will not be considered under any circumstances.

heading: Appeal Process - Version 2
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused may appeal the decision to the Land Use Appeals Board within 20 days of receiving the notification of refusal. The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the specific legal and factual grounds for the appeal, accompanied by any new, relevant, and previously unavailable supporting evidence. An appeal fee of 7,500 crowns is required. The Board will review the appeal within 45 days and may request further information or hold a hearing if deemed necessary. The Board's decision, based on a majority vote of its 5 members, is final and binding. Appeals submitted after the 20-day period will not be considered.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
An Agricultural Land Conversion Permit may be revoked by the Director if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with any of the conditions specified in the permit.
(b) The permit was obtained through misrepresentation or fraud.
(c) The proposed conversion significantly deviates from the approved land use plan without prior written approval.
(d) The permit holder fails to commence the conversion within the stipulated timeframe or any approved extension.
(e) The permit holder is found to be in violation of any other relevant environmental or planning regulations related to the conversion project. A 14-day notice will be given before revocation.

heading: Permit Revocation - Version 2
text:
An Agricultural Land Conversion Permit may be immediately revoked by the Director if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with any of the conditions specified in the permit after a single written warning.
(b) The permit was obtained through misrepresentation, fraud, or submission of knowingly false information.
(c) The proposed conversion significantly deviates from the approved land use plan without prior written approval, to an extent exceeding 10% of the land area.
(d) The permit holder fails to commence the conversion within 50% of the stipulated timeframe or any approved extension.
(e) The permit holder is found to be in violation of any other relevant environmental or planning regulations related to the conversion project, resulting in a fine of over 10,000 crowns. No prior notice is required for immediate revocation in cases of fraud or severe environmental damage.

heading: Enforcement and Inspections
text: The Agricultural Land Management Office is authorized to conduct inspections of agricultural land and converted land to ensure compliance with this Act and any issued permits. Inspectors may enter land at reasonable hours, after providing at least 24 hours' notice to the landowner, to verify compliance. In cases of suspected unlawful conversion or imminent environmental damage, inspectors may enter without prior notice, provided they have reasonable grounds. Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence and may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for Unlawful Conversion
text: Any person or entity who converts agricultural land without a valid permit, or in violation of an issued permit, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 20,000 crowns and not exceeding 100,000 crowns for each hectare or part thereof converted unlawfully. In addition, the Director may order the immediate cessation of all work and require the restoration of the land to its original agricultural state at the expense of the offender. Failure to comply with a restoration order within 90 days may result in additional daily fines of 5,000 crowns until compliance is achieved.

heading: Penalties for Unlawful Conversion - Version 2
text: Any person or entity who converts agricultural land without a valid permit, or in significant violation of an issued permit, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 50,000 crowns and not exceeding 250,000 crowns for each hectare or part thereof converted unlawfully. In addition, the Director shall order the immediate cessation of all work and require the full restoration of the land to its original agricultural state at the expense of the offender. Failure to comply with a restoration order within 60 days will result in additional daily fines of 10,000 crowns until full compliance is achieved, and potential legal action to seize assets to cover restoration costs.

heading: Restoration Orders
text: Where agricultural land has been converted unlawfully, the Director may issue a restoration order requiring the landowner to restore the land to its previous agricultural use. The order shall specify the scope of restoration work, including soil remediation, removal of non-agricultural structures, and re-establishment of suitable vegetation, within a maximum period of 180 days. Failure to comply with a restoration order may lead to the Agricultural Land Management Office carrying out the restoration work and recovering all associated costs from the landowner, plus an administrative fee of 20% of the total cost.

heading: Restoration Orders - Version 2
text: Where agricultural land has been converted unlawfully, the Director shall issue a mandatory restoration order requiring the landowner to fully restore the land to its previous agricultural use and productivity. The order shall specify the precise scope of restoration work, including comprehensive soil remediation, complete removal of all non-agricultural structures, and re-establishment of indigenous agricultural vegetation, within a maximum period of 120 days. Failure to comply with a restoration order will lead to the Agricultural Land Management Office immediately carrying out the restoration work and recovering all associated costs from the landowner, plus an administrative fee of 30% of the total cost, through legal means.

heading: Protection of Prime Agricultural Land
text: Special consideration shall be given to the protection of prime agricultural land, defined as land with a soil classification rating of 'excellent' or 'very good' for agricultural production. Conversion of such land will only be permitted in exceptional circumstances where there is an overriding public interest and no viable alternative exists. The burden of proof for demonstrating such exceptional circumstances rests entirely with the applicant. The total area of prime agricultural land converted in Nordvale shall not exceed 0.1% of the national total in any given calendar year. The Director must seek ministerial approval for any such conversion.

heading: Protection of Prime Agricultural Land - Version 2
text: The highest priority shall be given to the absolute protection of prime agricultural land, defined as land with a soil classification rating of 'excellent' for agricultural production. Conversion of such land is strictly prohibited, except in extraordinary circumstances where there is a demonstrably critical and unavoidable national public interest, and absolutely no viable alternative exists within the Republic. The burden of proof for demonstrating such extraordinary and unavoidable circumstances rests entirely with the applicant, requiring a 90% consensus from an independent expert panel. The total area of prime agricultural land converted in Nordvale shall not exceed 0.05% of the national total over a five-year period. The Director must seek direct approval from the Grand Council for any such conversion.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges specified in this Act, including application fees, extension fees, and appeal fees, are non-refundable. Fees are to be paid in crowns to the Agricultural Land Management Office. The Director may, from time to time, review and adjust these fees, provided that any adjustments are published in the official gazette at least 60 days before coming into effect. Revenue generated from these fees will be allocated to cover administrative costs of the Office and contribute to agricultural land protection initiatives. Current application fees are 2,500 crowns per hectare.

heading: Public Registry of Permits
text: The Agricultural Land Management Office shall maintain a public registry of all Agricultural Land Conversion Permits issued, refused, or revoked. This registry will be accessible online through the government's official website and will include information such as the applicant's name, location of the land, proposed use, decision date, and any conditions attached to the permit. Personal contact details of applicants will be redacted for privacy reasons. The registry aims to provide transparency in land use decisions and allow public scrutiny of conversion activities across Nordvale.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: The Director of the Agricultural Land Management Office shall submit an annual report to the Grand Council of Nordvale by March 31st of each year. This report shall detail the number of permit applications received, approved, and refused during the preceding calendar year. It must also include statistics on the total area of agricultural land converted, categorized by municipality (e.g., Aldmark, Brenholt) and by new land use type. The report will also summarize any significant enforcement actions taken and provide recommendations for future policy adjustments regarding agricultural land protection.

heading: Amendments to Permits
text: Any proposed significant amendment to an approved land use plan or permit conditions must be submitted for approval to the Agricultural Land Management Office. A 'significant amendment' is defined as any change that alters the converted area by more than 10%, or substantially changes the nature of the approved non-agricultural use. An amendment application will be subject to a review process similar to the original application, though a reduced fee of 1,500 crowns may apply. Minor amendments, defined as changes less than 5% in area or scope, may be approved administratively by an assigned officer.

heading: Amendments to Permits - Version 2
text: Any proposed amendment to an approved land use plan or permit conditions must be submitted for approval to the Agricultural Land Management Office. A 'significant amendment' is defined as any change that alters the converted area by more than 5%, or substantially changes the nature of the approved non-agricultural use, or impacts any environmental mitigation measures. An amendment application will be subject to a full review process identical to the original application, including public notice and municipal consultation, and the full application fee of 3,000 crowns. Minor amendments, defined as changes less than 2% in area or scope, may be approved administratively by the Director only after a 15-day public comment period.

heading: Emergencies and Disasters
text: In the event of a declared national emergency or natural disaster, the Director may temporarily suspend certain provisions of this Act related to permit requirements for urgent land use changes necessary for recovery efforts. Such suspensions must be approved by the Grand Council within 14 days of enactment and shall not exceed 90 days. Any land converted under such emergency provisions must be restored to its agricultural state within 24 months, unless a new, permanent permit is subsequently obtained under normal procedures. This provision applies only to events of catastrophic scale affecting multiple municipalities.

heading: Exemptions
text:
This Act does not apply to:
(a) Changes in agricultural practice that do not alter the agricultural designation of the land.
(b) Minor expansions of existing farm buildings, not exceeding 100 square meters in area, provided they remain ancillary to agricultural operations.
(c) Construction of small-scale infrastructure directly supporting agricultural activities, such as irrigation channels or access tracks, covering less than 0.1 hectare.
(d) Land conversions for purposes explicitly outlined in a national disaster recovery plan as approved by the Grand Council.
(e) Conversions for land areas smaller than 0.05 hectares for private, non-commercial purposes.

heading: Exemptions - Version 2
text:
This Act does not apply to:
(a) Changes in agricultural practice that do not alter the agricultural designation of the land, such as crop rotation changes.
(b) Minor expansions of existing farm buildings, not exceeding 50 square meters in area, provided they remain strictly ancillary to agricultural operations and do not alter the footprint by more than 10%.
(c) Construction of small-scale infrastructure directly supporting agricultural activities, such as irrigation channels or access tracks, covering less than 0.05 hectares, which must be approved by the local municipal agricultural committee.
(d) Land conversions for purposes explicitly outlined in a national disaster recovery plan as approved by the Grand Council, provided they are temporary for no more than 12 months.
(e) Conversions for land areas smaller than 0.02 hectares for private, non-commercial purposes, limited to one such conversion per landowner every 5 years.

heading: Guidance Documents
text: The Agricultural Land Management Office shall publish and regularly update guidance documents to assist applicants in understanding the requirements of this Act. These documents will include detailed instructions for completing application forms, checklists for required supporting documents, and explanations of the criteria for approval and refusal. Guidance will be available free of charge on the official government website and in print at the Office in Aldmark. The Office aims to update these documents at least once every two years to reflect any changes in policy or legislation, ensuring clarity for all stakeholders.

heading: Inter-Agency Cooperation
text: The Agricultural Land Management Office shall cooperate with other government agencies and municipal authorities, including those in Corvik and Dunmere, to ensure coordinated decision-making regarding land use. This cooperation may involve sharing information, participating in joint review committees, and harmonizing regulations where appropriate. A memorandum of understanding shall be established with the Environmental Protection Agency to streamline environmental impact assessments. Regular quarterly meetings will be held between the Director and representatives from key municipal planning departments to discuss upcoming applications and policy matters.

heading: Data Collection and Analysis
text: The Agricultural Land Management Office is mandated to collect and analyze data related to agricultural land use and conversion trends across Nordvale. This data will inform policy development, assess the effectiveness of this Act, and contribute to national food security planning. The data will include total hectares of agricultural land, areas converted, types of new uses, and economic impacts. An annual statistical report will be published, making this information publicly available. The Office shall utilize advanced geographic information systems (GIS) for accurate mapping and tracking of land use changes, updating maps every 6 months.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All personal and proprietary information submitted by applicants, beyond what is required for public transparency as per section 25, shall be treated as confidential by the Agricultural Land Management Office. Access to such information will be restricted to authorized personnel directly involved in the permit review process. Any breach of confidentiality by Office staff will be subject to disciplinary action. However, information may be disclosed if required by law or a court order, or if the applicant provides explicit written consent for its release for specific purposes, such as research.

heading: Conflict of Interest
text: Any officer or employee of the Agricultural Land Management Office or the Land Use Appeals Board who has a direct or indirect financial interest in an application for an Agricultural Land Conversion Permit shall declare such interest and recuse themselves from any involvement in the review or decision-making process concerning that application. Failure to declare a conflict of interest constitutes a serious breach of duty and may result in dismissal and legal penalties. Declarations of interest must be submitted in writing to the Director or the Board Chair, as appropriate, at least 7 days before any deliberations.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be subject to a comprehensive review by the Grand Council of Nordvale every 5 years from its effective date. The purpose of this review is to assess its effectiveness in achieving its objectives, identify any unintended consequences, and recommend necessary amendments to ensure its continued relevance and efficiency. The first review will be conducted by 2023, and a public consultation period of at least 90 days will precede any proposed amendments. The Director will submit a detailed report on the Act's implementation and impacts.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions or parts of the Act shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity or unenforceability of any single provision shall not affect the validity of other sections of this Act. This ensures that the core objectives of agricultural land protection are maintained even if minor aspects are legally challenged, upholding the legislative intent for sustainable land management within Nordvale, including municipalities like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All applications for agricultural land conversion submitted on or after this date shall be subject to the provisions of this Act. Any applications submitted prior to this date will be processed according to the regulations in effect at the time of submission. The Agricultural Land Management Office will ensure all necessary administrative structures and digital portals are fully operational by this effective date. Public information campaigns will be conducted in all major municipalities, including Grauby and Lund Vale, 3 months prior to commencement.

heading: Temporary Measures
text: For a period of 24 months following the commencement of this Act, the Director may approve applications for conversion of agricultural land up to 0.75 hectares for small-scale community projects or non-profit initiatives, provided the land is not classified as prime agricultural land. These applications will be subject to a simplified review process and a reduced fee of 1,000 crowns. This measure aims to facilitate initial adjustments to the new regulatory framework while supporting local development. After 24 months, these temporary provisions will automatically cease to be active. A total of 15 such permits can be issued during this period.

heading: Temporary Measures
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Museum cards for newly arrived residents
text:
(1) A newly arrived resident may buy one annual museum card for 35 crowns.
(2) A further annual museum card bought by the same person costs the ordinary price.

heading: Museum cards for newly arrived residents
text:
(1) A newly arrived resident may buy one annual museum card for 40 crowns.
(2) A further annual museum card bought by the same person costs the ordinary price.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements for obtaining permits for various agricultural land uses and changes in cultivation practices within the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures sustainable land management, protects soil quality, and promotes efficient agricultural production across all municipalities. The provisions of this Act apply to all land designated for agricultural use, whether privately or publicly owned, exceeding an area of 0.5 hectares. The primary goal is to maintain agricultural productivity and prevent practices that could lead to long-term degradation of arable land. All agricultural activities impacting land use are subject to these regulations.

heading: Permit requirement for new cultivation
text: Any individual or entity planning to convert non-cultivated land into cultivated agricultural land must obtain a New Cultivation Permit from the Municipal Agricultural Office. This permit is required for any area exceeding 0.75 hectares that has not been actively cultivated for a continuous period of at least 10 years. An application fee of 150 crowns is payable upon submission. The application must include a detailed land survey, a soil analysis report not older than 12 months, and a proposed cultivation plan outlining the first five years of activity. Approval typically takes 45 days.

heading: Permit for crop rotation changes
text: A Crop Rotation Change Permit is necessary for any farmer intending to significantly alter their established crop rotation scheme on land exceeding 2 hectares. A significant alteration is defined as changing more than 30% of the planted area to a different crop type within a two-year cycle, especially if the new crop requires substantially different soil nutrients or water management. The application fee for this permit is 75 crowns. Farmers must submit their proposed new rotation plan, detailing the soil impact and sustainability measures. The approval process is generally completed within 30 days.

heading: Permit for crop rotation changes
text: A Crop Rotation Change Permit is necessary for any farmer intending to significantly alter their established crop rotation scheme on land exceeding 1.5 hectares. A significant alteration is defined as changing more than 20% of the planted area to a different crop type within a two-year cycle, especially if the new crop requires substantially different soil nutrients or water management. The application fee for this permit is 90 crowns. Farmers must submit their proposed new rotation plan, detailing the soil impact and sustainability measures. The approval process is generally completed within 25 days.

heading: Permit for crop rotation changes
text: A Crop Rotation Change Permit is necessary for any farmer intending to significantly alter their established crop rotation scheme on land exceeding 1 hectare. A significant alteration is defined as changing more than 15% of the planted area to a different crop type within a two-year cycle, especially if the new crop requires substantially different soil nutrients or water management. The application fee for this permit is 110 crowns. Farmers must submit their proposed new rotation plan, detailing the soil impact and sustainability measures. The approval process is generally completed within 20 days.

heading: Permit for land drainage projects
text: A Land Drainage Permit is required for any project involving the installation, modification, or removal of drainage systems on agricultural land that affects an area greater than 1 hectare. This includes subsurface tile drains, open ditches, or any other system designed to alter the natural water table. The application fee is 250 crowns. Applicants must provide detailed engineering plans, an environmental impact assessment focusing on water quality, and evidence of consultation with adjacent landowners. The review period is 60 days, and permits are granted only if the project demonstrates minimal negative impact on local ecosystems.

heading: Permit for irrigation system installation
text: Any new installation or significant expansion of an irrigation system on agricultural land covering more than 0.5 hectares necessitates an Irrigation System Permit. This includes permanent sprinklers, drip irrigation, or pivot systems drawing from surface or groundwater sources. The application fee is 300 crowns. Documentation must include a water source analysis, estimated water usage, and a plan for water conservation. The permit ensures equitable water distribution and prevents over-extraction. The review period is 50 days, and approval is contingent on water availability assessments performed by the regional water authority.

heading: Permit for permanent pasture conversion
text: The conversion of permanent pasture land, defined as land continuously used for grazing for at least 15 years, into arable crop production requires a Pasture Conversion Permit. This permit is mandatory for any area exceeding 1 hectare. The purpose is to protect biodiversity and soil structure associated with long-term pasture. An application fee of 200 crowns is required. Applicants must provide a soil organic matter analysis and a reforestation plan if the land has any tree cover. Approval is granted if the proposed conversion demonstrates long-term soil health benefits. The decision process takes 40 days.

heading: Permit for agroforestry implementation
text: An Agroforestry Permit is required for farmers integrating trees or shrubs into agricultural systems on land exceeding 2 hectares, particularly if the density is higher than 100 trees per hectare. This permit encourages sustainable land use while ensuring the proposed system is well-planned and does not negatively impact existing agricultural productivity. The application fee is 100 crowns. Plans must detail tree species, planting density, and integration with crop or livestock management. The review process takes 35 days, with a focus on ecological benefits and agricultural compatibility. Nordvale promotes such practices.

heading: Permit for terracing or contour farming
text: Any farmer wishing to implement terracing or contour farming techniques on sloped agricultural land with a gradient exceeding 5% must obtain a Soil Conservation Permit. This is mandatory for areas larger than 0.8 hectares to prevent soil erosion and manage water runoff. The application fee is 120 crowns. Detailed topographical maps and engineering designs of the proposed terraces or contour lines are required. The permit aims to ensure that these interventions are effective and do not inadvertently cause adverse effects on downstream areas. The approval period is 45 days.

heading: Permit for vineyard establishment
text: Establishing a new vineyard on land not previously used for viticulture, exceeding 0.25 hectares, requires a Vineyard Establishment Permit. This permit is crucial for managing land use in areas suitable for grape cultivation and ensuring compliance with regional agricultural zoning. The application fee is 180 crowns. Applicants must submit a soil suitability report, a detailed planting plan, and an assessment of water requirements. The permit process takes 60 days, focusing on microclimate suitability and potential impact on surrounding agricultural lands. Nordvale aims to support quality grape production.

heading: Permit for hop field development
text: The development of a new hop field on agricultural land not previously designated for hop cultivation, covering an area greater than 0.2 hectares, requires a Hop Field Development Permit. This permit addresses the specific infrastructure and trellising requirements of hop production. The application fee is 170 crowns. Applicants must provide a detailed site plan, including proposed trellis systems, and a plan for managing the specific water and nutrient needs of hops. The approval process takes 55 days, ensuring the proposed development meets local agricultural standards.

heading: Permit for fruit orchard planting
text: Planting a new fruit orchard on land not previously used for perennial fruit cultivation, exceeding 0.5 hectares, requires a Fruit Orchard Permit. This permit helps manage long-term land commitment and ensures suitable site selection. The application fee is 190 crowns. Applicants must submit a soil suitability report, a list of proposed fruit tree varieties, and a plan for pest and disease management. The permit process typically takes 50 days, focusing on the long-term viability and ecological impact of the orchard. Nordvale values its fruit production.

heading: Permit for berry farm establishment
text: Establishing a new berry farm for commercial purposes on land exceeding 0.2 hectares requires a Berry Farm Permit. This permit is important for ensuring proper cultivation practices and managing potential environmental impacts specific to berry production. The application fee is 140 crowns. Applicants must provide a detailed planting plan, including berry types, and a strategy for soil health and water management. The permit review period is 40 days, focusing on sustainable practices and integration with regional agricultural plans. Aldmark and Brenholt are known for their berries.

heading: Permit for mushroom cultivation facilities
text: The construction or establishment of new indoor or outdoor mushroom cultivation facilities on agricultural land, exceeding a total footprint of 100 square meters, requires a Mushroom Cultivation Permit. This permit addresses environmental controls, waste management, and potential biohazard considerations. The application fee is 220 crowns. Applicants must submit architectural plans, a waste disposal strategy, and details on substrate sourcing. The review process is 45 days, ensuring health and safety standards are met. Corvik has seen an increase in mushroom farming.

heading: Permit for permanent greenhouse construction
text: The construction of any permanent greenhouse structure on agricultural land, with a footprint exceeding 50 square meters, requires a Permanent Greenhouse Permit. This permit ensures that greenhouse developments are integrated appropriately into the agricultural landscape and meet structural safety standards. The application fee is 280 crowns. Detailed architectural plans, including foundation designs and ventilation systems, must be submitted. The review period is 55 days, with emphasis on structural integrity and proper land use. Dunmere farmers are utilizing more greenhouses.

heading: Permit for organic certification transition
text: Farmers transitioning agricultural land exceeding 1 hectare to certified organic production must obtain an Organic Transition Permit. This permit acknowledges the commitment to organic standards and helps track the progress of organic farming in Nordvale. There is no application fee for this permit. Applicants must submit a detailed transition plan, including a three-year organic certification roadmap and a pest management strategy without synthetic inputs. The permit is typically granted within 20 days, encouraging sustainable agricultural practices. Elsby municipality has a high percentage of organic farms.

heading: Permit for soil amendment projects
text: Large-scale soil amendment projects involving the application of non-traditional soil conditioners or substantial volumes of organic matter (exceeding 20 cubic meters per hectare) on land greater than 5 hectares require a Soil Amendment Permit. The application fee is 130 crowns. Applicants must provide a detailed description of the amendments, their source, and a soil analysis before and after application. The permit ensures beneficial impacts and prevents contamination. The review process takes 30 days. Fennick has many large farms that perform such amendments.

heading: Permit for agricultural research plots
text: Establishing agricultural research plots on land exceeding 0.1 hectares, especially those involving experimental crop varieties or novel cultivation methods, requires a Research Plot Permit. This permit ensures controlled experimentation and prevents unforeseen environmental impacts. The application fee is 80 crowns. Applicants must submit a research proposal, including experimental design, safety protocols, and a plan for eventual land restoration. The permit process takes 40 days, with a focus on scientific rigor and environmental protection. Grauby hosts several agricultural research institutions.

heading: Permit for land reclamation
text: Any project aiming to reclaim land for agricultural use from previously degraded or abandoned areas, exceeding 1.5 hectares, requires a Land Reclamation Permit. This permit ensures that reclamation efforts are ecologically sound and result in viable agricultural land. The application fee is 270 crowns. Applicants must provide a detailed reclamation plan, including soil rehabilitation strategies, and an environmental impact assessment. The review period is 60 days, focusing on long-term sustainability and prevention of further degradation. Lund Vale has ongoing reclamation projects.

heading: Permit for specialty crop cultivation
text: Cultivation of specialty crops, defined as non-traditional agricultural products requiring specific environmental controls or posing unique management challenges, on an area greater than 0.3 hectares, requires a Specialty Crop Permit. This helps ensure proper management of new or unusual agricultural ventures. The application fee is 160 crowns. Applicants must provide a detailed cultivation plan, including specific environmental requirements and market assessment. The review process is 45 days, assessing the feasibility and potential impact of the crop. Aldmark is exploring new specialty crops.

heading: Permit for large-scale composting facilities
text: The establishment of a large-scale composting facility on agricultural land, processing more than 50 cubic meters of organic material per month, requires a Composting Facility Permit. This permit addresses potential odors, leachate management, and vector control. The application fee is 350 crowns. Applicants must submit a site plan, process description, and an environmental management plan. The review period is 65 days, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and community health standards. Brenholt has a significant agricultural composting industry.

heading: Permit for large-scale composting facilities
text: The establishment of a large-scale composting facility on agricultural land, processing more than 40 cubic meters of organic material per month, requires a Composting Facility Permit. This permit addresses potential odors, leachate management, and vector control. The application fee is 380 crowns. Applicants must submit a site plan, process description, and an environmental management plan. The review period is 70 days, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and community health standards. Brenholt has a significant agricultural composting industry.

heading: Permit for agricultural pond construction
text: The construction of any new agricultural pond or reservoir with a surface area exceeding 500 square meters, or a depth greater than 2 meters, requires an Agricultural Pond Permit. This permit is essential for managing water resources and ensuring ecological integrity. The application fee is 290 crowns. Applicants must provide detailed engineering plans, a hydrological assessment, and a plan for managing water quality. The review period is 50 days, focusing on water conservation and habitat preservation. Corvik is considering more agricultural ponds for irrigation.

heading: Permit for new farm access roads
text: The construction of any new permanent farm access road exceeding 100 meters in length or 4 meters in width on agricultural land requires a Farm Access Road Permit. This permit ensures proper planning of infrastructure and minimizes land fragmentation. The application fee is 110 crowns. Applicants must submit a site plan, including road dimensions, materials, and drainage provisions. The review period is 30 days, considering impact on soil, water runoff, and existing agricultural operations. Dunmere often requires new access roads for expanding farms.

heading: Permit for protective hedging installation
text: The installation of new protective hedges or shelterbelts on agricultural land, exceeding a total length of 200 meters, requires a Protective Hedging Permit. This permit encourages ecological buffers while ensuring they do not unduly impact agricultural efficiency. The application fee is 70 crowns. Applicants must provide a planting plan, including species selection and proposed dimensions. The review period is 25 days, with an emphasis on biodiversity benefits and land integration. Elsby promotes protective hedging for windbreaks.

heading: Permit for agricultural building construction
text: The construction of any new permanent agricultural building, such as barns, storage facilities, or machinery sheds, with a footprint exceeding 75 square meters, requires an Agricultural Building Permit. This permit ensures structural safety and appropriate land use. The application fee is 320 crowns. Detailed architectural plans, including foundation, materials, and purpose of the building, must be submitted. The review period is 60 days, focusing on safety, land zoning, and impact on surrounding agricultural operations. Fennick has seen new large barns being built.

heading: Permit for agricultural building construction
text: The construction of any new permanent agricultural building, such as barns, storage facilities, or machinery sheds, with a footprint exceeding 60 square meters, requires an Agricultural Building Permit. This permit ensures structural safety and appropriate land use. The application fee is 350 crowns. Detailed architectural plans, including foundation, materials, and purpose of the building, must be submitted. The review period is 65 days, focusing on safety, land zoning, and impact on surrounding agricultural operations. Fennick has seen new large barns being built.

heading: Permit for renewable energy installations
text: The installation of renewable energy infrastructure on agricultural land, such as solar panel arrays exceeding 200 square meters or wind turbines taller than 15 meters, requires a Renewable Energy Permit. This permit balances energy production with agricultural land preservation. The application fee is 400 crowns. Applicants must provide site plans, energy output estimates, and an assessment of agricultural land impact. The review period is 70 days, ensuring minimal disruption to farming activities. Grauby farmers are increasingly interested in solar power.

heading: Permit for native plant restoration
text: Projects involving the restoration of native plant species on agricultural land, specifically converting more than 0.5 hectares from active cultivation to native habitats, require a Native Plant Restoration Permit. This permit encourages biodiversity and ecological services. There is no application fee for this permit. Applicants must submit a restoration plan, including species lists and long-term management strategies. The permit is typically granted within 25 days, supporting conservation efforts. Lund Vale has several successful native plant restoration initiatives.

heading: Permit for quarrying of agricultural soil
text: Any activity involving the extraction or quarrying of agricultural topsoil or subsoil for commercial purposes, or exceeding 50 cubic meters for any purpose, requires a Soil Quarrying Permit. This permit is vital for preventing irreversible land degradation. The application fee is 500 crowns. Applicants must provide detailed excavation plans, a land restoration plan, and an environmental impact assessment. The review period is 90 days, with strict conditions to ensure minimal long-term damage to agricultural capacity. Aldmark aims to protect its valuable topsoil.

heading: Application submission process
text:
(1) All permit applications must be submitted to the Municipal Agricultural Office in the municipality where the land is primarily located. 
(2) Applications must be submitted in triplicate, accompanied by all required documentation and the non-refundable application fee. 
(3) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days, with a detailed list of missing information. 
(4) The Municipal Agricultural Office will issue a confirmation of receipt within 5 working days of a complete application being submitted. 
(5) An applicant must be at least 18 years of age to submit an application.

heading: Review and approval process
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Municipal Agricultural Office will commence its review within 5 working days. 
(2) The review period, as specified for each permit type, begins on the date of confirmation of receipt. 
(3) The Office may request additional information from the applicant within the first 50% of the review period. Failure to provide this information within 20 days may result in delays or rejection. 
(4) A permit may be approved, approved with conditions, or denied. 
(5) A decision must be communicated to the applicant in writing within 5 working days of the review period's conclusion.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) Permits may be issued with specific conditions designed to ensure sustainable agricultural practices and mitigate environmental impacts. 
(2) Such conditions may include, but are not limited to, limitations on water usage, requirements for specific soil conservation measures, monitoring and reporting obligations, or restrictions on chemical inputs. 
(3) All conditions attached to a permit are legally binding, and non-compliance may lead to penalties as described in section 36. 
(4) Any conditions imposed will be clearly outlined in the written permit approval, with justifications provided if requested. 
(5) Conditions are tailored to the specific agricultural activity and local environmental context.

heading: Permit validity period
text:
(1) Unless otherwise specified in the permit document, all agricultural land use permits are valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. 
(2) Permits for permanent structures, such as greenhouses or farm buildings, are valid indefinitely once constructed and approved, provided they remain in their original form and purpose. 
(3) Permits for temporary activities or specific projects, such as research plots or land reclamation, will specify their own duration, typically not exceeding 3 years. 
(4) A permit holder must commence the permitted activity within 12 months of the permit's issuance date. 
(5) Failure to commence within this period may result in permit expiration and necessitate a new application.

heading: Permit validity period
text:
(1) Unless otherwise specified in the permit document, all agricultural land use permits are valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issuance. 
(2) Permits for permanent structures, such as greenhouses or farm buildings, are valid indefinitely once constructed and approved, provided they remain in their original form and purpose. 
(3) Permits for temporary activities or specific projects, such as research plots or land reclamation, will specify their own duration, typically not exceeding 2 years. 
(4) A permit holder must commence the permitted activity within 9 months of the permit's issuance date. 
(5) Failure to commence within this period may result in permit expiration and necessitate a new application.

heading: Permit renewal process
text:
(1) Holders of permits with a defined validity period may apply for renewal no earlier than 6 months and no later than 3 months before the permit's expiration date. 
(2) A renewal application fee of 50 crowns is required. 
(3) The renewal process involves a review of compliance with the original permit conditions and any changes in agricultural practices or land use. 
(4) The Municipal Agricultural Office will issue a decision on renewal within 45 days of receiving a complete application. 
(5) Renewal is typically granted if the permit holder has demonstrated satisfactory compliance and there are no significant changes in land use circumstances. 
(6) If the application is submitted less than 3 months before expiry, an additional late fee of 25 crowns applies.

heading: Permit renewal process
text:
(1) Holders of permits with a defined validity period may apply for renewal no earlier than 6 months and no later than 2 months before the permit's expiration date. 
(2) A renewal application fee of 60 crowns is required. 
(3) The renewal process involves a review of compliance with the original permit conditions and any changes in agricultural practices or land use. 
(4) The Municipal Agricultural Office will issue a decision on renewal within 40 days of receiving a complete application. 
(5) Renewal is typically granted if the permit holder has demonstrated satisfactory compliance and there are no significant changes in land use circumstances. 
(6) If the application is submitted less than 2 months before expiry, an additional late fee of 30 crowns applies.

heading: Right of appeal
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or whose permit has been issued with conditions deemed unreasonable, has the right to appeal the decision. 
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Regional Agricultural Board within 30 days of receiving the Municipal Agricultural Office's decision. 
(3) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include any supporting documentation. 
(4) The Regional Agricultural Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days of receipt. 
(5) The decision of the Regional Agricultural Board is final. 
(6) A non-refundable appeal fee of 100 crowns is payable upon submission of the appeal.

heading: Right of appeal
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or whose permit has been issued with conditions deemed unreasonable, has the right to appeal the decision. 
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Regional Agricultural Board within 25 days of receiving the Municipal Agricultural Office's decision. 
(3) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include any supporting documentation. 
(4) The Regional Agricultural Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 50 days of receipt. 
(5) The decision of the Regional Agricultural Board is final. 
(6) A non-refundable appeal fee of 120 crowns is payable upon submission of the appeal.

heading: Enforcement and inspections
text:
(1) The Municipal Agricultural Office and authorized inspectors are responsible for enforcing the provisions of this Act. 
(2) Inspectors may conduct unannounced inspections of agricultural land to verify compliance with permit conditions and general land use regulations. 
(3) Permit holders must grant inspectors reasonable access to their agricultural land during daylight hours, upon presentation of official identification. 
(4) Any obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is a serious offense. 
(5) Inspectors will provide a written report of their findings to the permit holder within 15 days of an inspection. 
(6) Inspections focus on ensuring sustainable practices and environmental protection.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any individual or entity found to be in non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or the conditions of a valid permit may be subject to administrative penalties. 
(2) For minor infractions, a warning notice will be issued, requiring rectification within 30 days. 
(3) Failure to rectify minor infractions, or for more significant violations, a fine of up to 5,000 crowns may be imposed. 
(4) Repeated or severe violations, such as unauthorized conversion of significant agricultural land (exceeding 2 hectares), may result in fines up to 20,000 crowns and a mandatory order to restore the land at the owner's expense. 
(5) In extreme cases, a permit may be revoked, and further agricultural activities restricted for up to 5 years. 
(6) Fines are doubled for violations impacting protected ecological zones.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any individual or entity found to be in non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or the conditions of a valid permit may be subject to administrative penalties. 
(2) For minor infractions, a warning notice will be issued, requiring rectification within 20 days. 
(3) Failure to rectify minor infractions, or for more significant violations, a fine of up to 7,500 crowns may be imposed. 
(4) Repeated or severe violations, such as unauthorized conversion of significant agricultural land (exceeding 1.5 hectares), may result in fines up to 30,000 crowns and a mandatory order to restore the land at the owner's expense. 
(5) In extreme cases, a permit may be revoked, and further agricultural activities restricted for up to 7 years. 
(6) Fines are tripled for violations impacting protected ecological zones.

heading: Reporting unauthorized activities
text:
(1) Any citizen of Nordvale may report suspected unauthorized agricultural land use activities to their Municipal Agricultural Office. 
(2) Reports should be made in writing, providing as much detail as possible, including location, nature of the activity, and any relevant dates or observations. 
(3) Anonymous reports will be investigated if sufficient information is provided. 
(4) The Municipal Agricultural Office will investigate all credible reports within 15 working days. 
(5) Confidentiality of the reporting party will be maintained to the fullest extent possible. 
(6) False reporting with malicious intent may result in a fine of 500 crowns.

heading: Data collection and reporting
text:
(1) The Municipal Agricultural Office in each municipality will maintain a comprehensive register of all issued permits, including details of the activity, location, and any conditions. 
(2) This data will be updated quarterly and submitted to the National Agricultural Directorate. 
(3) The National Agricultural Directorate will compile an annual report on agricultural land use trends, permit statistics, and compliance rates across Nordvale. 
(4) This annual report will be made publicly available by 31 March each year. 
(5) The data collected will be used to inform agricultural policy and land management strategies. 
(6) Individual farm data will remain confidential, with only aggregated statistics published.

heading: Exemptions for small-scale operations
text:
(1) Farmers operating on land areas smaller than the specified thresholds for each permit type are generally exempt from the permit requirements of this Act. 
(2) For instance, new cultivation on less than 0.75 hectares does not require a permit. 
(3) However, all agricultural activities, regardless of scale, must still comply with general environmental protection regulations and local zoning laws. 
(4) The Municipal Agricultural Office reserves the right to require a permit for any activity, even below stated thresholds, if it determines there is a significant environmental risk. 
(5) This determination must be communicated in writing to the landowner within 7 days. 
(6) The intent is to support small-scale farmers while ensuring responsible land stewardship.

heading: Transitional provisions for existing activities
text:
(1) Agricultural land uses and activities that were legally established and operational prior to the effective date of this Act are generally exempt from retrospective permit requirements. 
(2) However, any significant modification or expansion of such existing activities after the effective date will require the appropriate permit as specified in this Act. 
(3) Farmers with existing operations are encouraged to voluntarily register their current land uses with the Municipal Agricultural Office within 12 months of this Act's commencement. 
(4) This voluntary registration helps in establishing a baseline for future land use changes. 
(5) Failure to register does not incur penalties but may complicate future permit applications. 
(6) Any major change to an existing activity must adhere to new permit rules.

heading: Review and amendments
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the National Agricultural Directorate every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and propose necessary amendments. 
(2) The first review will commence no later than January 1, 2023. 
(3) Public consultation will be a part of the review process, with a minimum 60-day period for public input. 
(4) Any proposed amendments will be put before the Nordvale Assembly for approval. 
(5) Amendments aim to adapt the Act to evolving agricultural practices and environmental challenges. 
(6) The review process ensures the Act remains relevant and effective for the farming community of Nordvale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Agricultural land' means land primarily used for growing crops, raising livestock, or cultivating plants for food or fiber. 
(2) 'Cultivated land' refers to land regularly tilled or managed for crop production. 
(3) 'Non-cultivated land' includes pastures, forests, wetlands, or fallow land not actively prepared for crops. 
(4) 'Permanent pasture' is land continuously under grass or other herbaceous forage crops for at least five consecutive years. 
(5) 'Significant alteration' refers to changes exceeding 20% of area or intensity. 
(6) 'Municipality' refers to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. 
(7) 'Crowns' refers to the currency of Nordvale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Agricultural land' means land primarily used for growing crops, raising livestock, or cultivating plants for food or fiber. 
(2) 'Cultivated land' refers to land regularly tilled or managed for crop production. 
(3) 'Non-cultivated land' includes pastures, forests, wetlands, or fallow land not actively prepared for crops. 
(4) 'Permanent pasture' is land continuously under grass or other herbaceous forage crops for at least seven consecutive years. 
(5) 'Significant alteration' refers to changes exceeding 15% of area or intensity. 
(6) 'Municipality' refers to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. 
(7) 'Crowns' refers to the currency of Nordvale.

heading: Permit for soil erosion control measures
text: The implementation of significant soil erosion control measures, such as the construction of major diversion terraces, sediment basins, or extensive riparian buffer zones, on land exceeding 1.2 hectares, requires a Soil Erosion Control Permit. This permit ensures that such measures are well-planned and effective. The application fee is 150 crowns. Applicants must provide detailed engineering plans, a hydrological impact assessment, and a plan for long-term maintenance. The review period is 40 days, focusing on soil preservation and water quality protection. Brenholt farmers frequently implement these measures.

heading: Permit for water impoundment structures
text: The construction of any new water impoundment structure, including dams or weirs, on agricultural land that creates a reservoir capacity exceeding 1,000 cubic meters or a wall height over 3 meters, requires a Water Impoundment Permit. This permit is crucial for water resource management and safety. The application fee is 450 crowns. Applicants must provide detailed engineering designs, a hydrological study, and an emergency action plan. The review period is 75 days, ensuring structural integrity and environmental considerations. Corvik often requires such structures for irrigation.

heading: Permit for land clearing and grubbing
text: Any project involving the clearing of natural vegetation (trees, shrubs, or dense brush) and grubbing (removal of roots) on agricultural land exceeding 0.6 hectares, for the purpose of expanding cultivated area, requires a Land Clearing Permit. This permit addresses potential soil disturbance and ecological impact. The application fee is 210 crowns. Applicants must provide an ecological assessment, a soil stabilization plan, and a justification for the clearing. The review period is 50 days, with an emphasis on preserving biodiversity and preventing erosion. Dunmere has strict rules on land clearing.

heading: Permit for land clearing and grubbing
text: Any project involving the clearing of natural vegetation (trees, shrubs, or dense brush) and grubbing (removal of roots) on agricultural land exceeding 0.4 hectares, for the purpose of expanding cultivated area, requires a Land Clearing Permit. This permit addresses potential soil disturbance and ecological impact. The application fee is 230 crowns. Applicants must provide an ecological assessment, a soil stabilization plan, and a justification for the clearing. The review period is 55 days, with an emphasis on preserving biodiversity and preventing erosion. Dunmere has strict rules on land clearing.

heading: Permit for nutrient management plans
text: Agricultural operations applying more than 50 kg of nitrogen or 25 kg of phosphorus per hectare per year on land exceeding 10 hectares must obtain a Nutrient Management Permit. This permit ensures responsible fertilizer use to prevent water pollution. The application fee is 190 crowns. Applicants must submit a detailed nutrient management plan, including soil test results, crop nutrient requirements, and application rates. The review period is 35 days, focusing on preventing nutrient runoff and protecting water bodies. Elsby encourages proactive nutrient management.

heading: Severability
text: If any section, subsection, or provision of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a competent court, the remainder of this Act shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one part shall not affect the validity of other provisions. This ensures that the core objectives of agricultural land use regulation continue to be met, even if minor parts are deemed legally problematic. The aim is for the Act to be as robust and applicable as possible across all circumstances and municipalities. Legal clarity is paramount for effective implementation and enforcement.

heading: Effective date
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Effective date
text: This Act shall come into effect on January 1, 2018. Any subsequent amendments to this Act will specify their own effective dates, which will generally be 3 months after their official publication in the Nordvale Gazette. The purpose of a clear effective date is to provide sufficient time for individuals and entities to familiarize themselves with the new regulations and adjust their practices accordingly. The initial effective date ensures a consistent start for all provisions and a smooth transition into the new regulatory framework for agricultural land use across Nordvale.

heading: Annual toll pass for volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) Notwithstanding TLA §10, an active volunteer firefighter who owns a car pays 30 percent less for an annual pass for that car.
(2) The reduction is given for one car per firefighter.
(3) The monthly pass under TLA §12 is charged in full.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating non-agricultural development and changes of land use within designated agricultural zones across the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to preserve prime agricultural land, ensure food security, and protect rural landscapes from incompatible development. It mandates that a permit must be obtained for any activity that alters the agricultural character or diminishes the agricultural potential of such land, thereby safeguarding this vital national resource for current and future generations. The provisions herein apply to all land officially classified as 'Agricultural Preservation Zone' by the Nordvale Department of Agriculture.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Agricultural land' means any land designated by the Nordvale Department of Agriculture as primarily suitable for the cultivation of crops, raising of livestock, or other agricultural practices, covering an area of at least 2 hectares.
(2) 'Non-agricultural development' refers to any construction, alteration, or land use that is not directly related to agricultural production, processing, or storage, such as residential dwellings, commercial establishments, or industrial facilities, exceeding 50 square meters in footprint.
(3) 'Change of use' means altering the primary purpose of agricultural land to a non-agricultural purpose, even if no new construction is involved, for a period exceeding 180 days within a calendar year.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: Any person, corporation, or entity proposing to undertake non-agricultural development or a change of use on agricultural land must first obtain a valid Agricultural Land Zoning Permit from the Nordvale Department of Agriculture. Failure to secure this permit before commencing any such activity shall result in significant penalties as outlined in section 35. This requirement applies regardless of whether other municipal or regional permits might also be necessary for the proposed project. A permit is specifically required for any structure over 10 square meters or any excavation exceeding 1 meter in depth.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for an Agricultural Land Zoning Permit must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Department of Agriculture's regional office responsible for the municipality where the land is located. The application must include all necessary documentation, plans, and fees as specified in section 6. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days. Applications must be received at least 90 days prior to the intended commencement date of the proposed development or change of use.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns must accompany every permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the application, conducting site visits, and consulting with relevant experts. If an application is withdrawn by the applicant within 30 days of submission, 50% of the fee may be reimbursed. Fees are adjusted annually on January 1st based on the consumer price index, with a maximum increase of 3% per year.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,800 crowns must accompany every permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the application, conducting site visits, and consulting with relevant experts. If an application is withdrawn by the applicant within 20 days of submission, 40% of the fee may be reimbursed. Fees are adjusted annually on January 1st based on the consumer price index, with a maximum increase of 4% per year.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Each application must include:
(a) A detailed site plan showing the exact location and dimensions of the proposed development or area of change of use, at a scale of 1:500 or greater.
(b) A written justification explaining why the non-agricultural use is necessary and cannot be located on non-agricultural land, not exceeding 10 pages.
(c) An environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified professional, detailing potential effects on soil, water, and air quality, if the proposed area exceeds 0.5 hectares.
(d) Proof of land ownership or a legally binding lease agreement for a minimum of 10 years.

heading: Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall initiate a thorough review. This process involves evaluating the proposed development against the objectives of this Act and consulting with relevant municipal planning departments and environmental agencies. The review period shall not exceed 60 working days from the date of acceptance of a complete application. Applicants will be notified in writing of the commencement of the review within 5 working days of application acceptance. During this period, additional information may be requested if deemed necessary.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For any application proposing non-agricultural development exceeding 0.25 hectares or impacting more than 5% of the total agricultural land within a 1-kilometer radius, a public consultation period of 30 days shall be initiated. During this period, details of the proposed project will be made available for public inspection at the relevant municipal office and online. Members of the public may submit written comments or objections, which will be considered by the Department before a final decision is made. A public meeting may be scheduled if more than 20 unique objections are received.

heading: Decision Criteria
text:
The Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall grant a permit only if the applicant demonstrates that:
(a) The proposed development or change of use will not significantly diminish the overall agricultural capacity of the region.
(b) There are no viable alternative sites on non-agricultural land within a 20-kilometer radius.
(c) The project provides a substantial public benefit that outweighs the loss of agricultural land, such as critical infrastructure or essential public services.
(d) All adverse environmental impacts can be effectively mitigated to a level acceptable to the Department, with residual impacts not exceeding 10% of the initial assessment.

heading: Decision Criteria
text:
The Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall grant a permit only if the applicant demonstrates that:
(a) The proposed development or change of use will not significantly diminish the overall agricultural capacity of the region by more than 0.5%.
(b) There are no viable alternative sites on non-agricultural land within a 30-kilometer radius.
(c) The project provides an exceptional public benefit that demonstrably outweighs the loss of agricultural land, such as critical infrastructure or essential public services.
(d) All adverse environmental impacts can be fully mitigated to a level acceptable to the Department, with residual impacts not exceeding 5% of the initial assessment.

heading: Conditions of Permit
text: Any permit issued under this Act may be subject to specific conditions deemed necessary by the Nordvale Department of Agriculture to minimize the impact on agricultural land. These conditions may include, but are not limited to, requirements for environmental monitoring, site restoration, specific construction methods, or limitations on the duration of the non-agricultural use. The permit holder must comply with all specified conditions for the entire duration of the permit. Failure to comply with any condition may result in permit revocation and penalties.

heading: Permit Duration
text: Unless otherwise specified, an Agricultural Land Zoning Permit is valid for a period of 5 years from its date of issuance. If the approved development or change of use is not substantially commenced within this period, the permit shall automatically expire. A permit may be extended for an additional period of up to 2 years upon written request and justification, submitted at least 90 days before its expiration, provided that the original conditions remain relevant and no new circumstances warrant a revised application. The extension fee is 750 crowns.

heading: Permit Duration
text: Unless otherwise specified, an Agricultural Land Zoning Permit is valid for a period of 3 years from its date of issuance. If the approved development or change of use is not substantially commenced within this period, the permit shall automatically expire. A permit may be extended for an additional period of up to 1 year upon written request and justification, submitted at least 120 days before its expiration, provided that the original conditions remain relevant and no new circumstances warrant a revised application. The extension fee is 1,500 crowns.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: For ongoing non-agricultural uses that have an expiry date, a permit renewal application must be submitted at least 6 months prior to the current permit's expiration. The renewal process will assess continued compliance with original conditions and any new regulations. A renewal fee of 900 crowns applies. The Department reserves the right to impose new conditions or deny renewal if the continued use no longer meets the criteria outlined in section 9 or poses new unforeseen risks to agricultural productivity or the environment. A site inspection will be conducted for all renewal applications.

heading: Minor Modifications
text: Minor modifications to an approved development or change of use, which do not increase the non-agricultural footprint by more than 10 square meters or alter the primary intent of the project, may be approved through an expedited review process. A request for minor modification must be submitted in writing, accompanied by a fee of 400 crowns. The Department will issue a decision within 30 working days. Modifications exceeding these thresholds will require a new permit application as per section 4. The Department holds sole discretion in determining what constitutes a 'minor modification'.

heading: Major Alterations
text: Any proposed alteration to an approved development or change of use that increases the non-agricultural footprint by more than 10% or substantially changes the nature of the approved use shall be considered a major alteration. Such alterations require a new permit application, processed in accordance with sections 4 through 9, including new fees and a full review. This ensures that significant changes are subject to the same rigorous assessment as initial proposals, preserving the integrity of agricultural land zoning. The Department must be notified of any such intention at least 180 days prior to the proposed alteration.

heading: Major Alterations
text: Any proposed alteration to an approved development or change of use that increases the non-agricultural footprint by more than 5% or substantially changes the nature of the approved use shall be considered a major alteration. Such alterations require a new permit application, processed in accordance with sections 4 through 9, including new fees and a full review. This ensures that significant changes are subject to the same rigorous assessment as initial proposals, preserving the integrity of agricultural land zoning. The Department must be notified of any such intention at least 270 days prior to the proposed alteration.

heading: Exemptions
text:
The following activities are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act:
(a) Construction or alteration of structures solely for agricultural purposes, such as barns, silos, and greenhouses, provided they do not exceed 250 square meters in footprint.
(b) Temporary uses for a period not exceeding 60 days within a calendar year, such as seasonal agricultural fairs or temporary storage, that do not involve permanent structures or significant ground disturbance.
(c) Minor repairs and maintenance of existing non-agricultural structures that do not expand their footprint or intensify their use, provided the cost does not exceed 15,000 crowns.

heading: Exemption for Public Utilities
text:
Construction, maintenance, and repair of essential public utility infrastructure (e.g., water lines, power transmission lines, communication cables) are exempt from the permit requirements, provided that:
(a) The utility is owned or operated by the Nordvale government or a licensed public utility company.
(b) The development is located within an established right-of-way or easement not exceeding 10 meters in width.
(c) The utility provider minimizes the impact on agricultural land and restores the land to its original agricultural capacity within 180 days of project completion. The utility must provide a restoration plan for approval.

heading: Temporary Agricultural Worker Housing
text:
Temporary housing for agricultural workers, not exceeding 10 units and occupied for a maximum of 9 months in any 12-month period, may be exempt from permit requirements, provided:
(a) The housing is directly associated with an active agricultural operation on the same parcel of land.
(b) The housing is removed or converted back to agricultural use within 30 days of the end of the agricultural season.
(c) The total footprint of all temporary housing does not exceed 500 square meters. A notification must be filed with the Department 30 days before occupancy.

heading: Temporary Agricultural Worker Housing
text:
Temporary housing for agricultural workers, not exceeding 5 units and occupied for a maximum of 6 months in any 12-month period, may be exempt from permit requirements, provided:
(a) The housing is directly associated with an active agricultural operation on the same parcel of land.
(b) The housing is removed or converted back to agricultural use within 15 days of the end of the agricultural season.
(c) The total footprint of all temporary housing does not exceed 250 square meters. A notification must be filed with the Department 60 days before occupancy.

heading: Small-Scale Agricultural Processing
text: On-farm processing facilities for products grown exclusively on that farm, not exceeding 150 square meters in footprint and employing no more than 5 full-time equivalents, are exempt from permit requirements. This exemption is intended to support value-added agricultural activities. The facility must remain secondary to the primary agricultural use of the land. Any waste generated by the processing must be managed on-site or disposed of in an environmentally sound manner, with a management plan submitted to the Department for approval. The facility must not generate more than 70 dB of noise.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The Nordvale Department of Agriculture is granted full authority to enforce the provisions of this Act. This includes the power to conduct site inspections, issue orders to cease and desist, levy fines, and initiate legal proceedings to ensure compliance. Department officials may enter agricultural land, with reasonable notice of at least 24 hours, to verify compliance with permit conditions or to investigate suspected violations. In cases of immediate environmental hazard or irreversible land degradation, no prior notice is required for entry.

heading: Cease and Desist Orders
text: If the Department determines that non-agricultural development or a change of use is occurring without a required permit or in violation of permit conditions, it may issue a cease and desist order. This order shall require the immediate cessation of all non-compliant activities. The order will be delivered in writing to the landowner and/or the person undertaking the activity. Non-compliance with a cease and desist order within 72 hours may result in additional daily fines of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. The order will specify the reasons for its issuance.

heading: Restoration Orders
text: In addition to, or in lieu of, fines, the Department may issue a restoration order requiring the landowner to restore the agricultural land to its original state and agricultural capacity within a specified timeframe, typically not exceeding 180 days. The restoration plan must be approved by the Department. Failure to comply with a restoration order may result in the Department undertaking the restoration work itself, with all associated costs (plus an administrative fee of 20%) being charged to the landowner. This cost can be recovered as a debt owed to the Nordvale government.

heading: Administrative Fines
text: Violations of this Act, including commencing non-agricultural development without a permit or failure to adhere to permit conditions, are subject to administrative fines. Initial fines for unauthorized development or change of use shall be no less than 20,000 crowns and no more than 50,000 crowns. Additional daily fines of 1,000 crowns may be imposed for each day the violation continues after a notice of violation has been issued. The maximum total fine for a single, continuous violation is 500,000 crowns.

heading: Administrative Fines
text: Violations of this Act, including commencing non-agricultural development without a permit or failure to adhere to permit conditions, are subject to administrative fines. Initial fines for unauthorized development or change of use shall be no less than 30,000 crowns and no more than 75,000 crowns. Additional daily fines of 1,500 crowns may be imposed for each day the violation continues after a notice of violation has been issued. The maximum total fine for a single, continuous violation is 750,000 crowns.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or a landowner who has received a cease and desist or restoration order, may appeal the decision to the Agricultural Land Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal. The Appeals Board, an independent body, will review the case and issue a decision within 90 days. A non-refundable appeal fee of 2,500 crowns must accompany the appeal submission.

heading: Composition of Appeals Board
text: The Agricultural Land Appeals Board shall consist of five members appointed by the Minister of Agriculture.
