Members must possess expertise in agriculture, land use planning, environmental science, or law. Board members shall serve staggered terms of 3 years. At least two members must have direct experience in agricultural production. No member shall be an employee of the Nordvale Department of Agriculture. The Chairperson of the Board is appointed by the Minister from among the Board members.

heading: Review by Appeals Board
text: The Appeals Board shall review all submitted documentation, including the original application, the Department's decision, and the appellant's grounds for appeal. The Board may also request additional information, conduct site visits, or hold public hearings if deemed necessary. The Board's decision shall be based on whether the Department's original decision was consistent with the provisions of this Act and whether all procedures were followed correctly. The Board may uphold, overturn, or modify the Department's decision.

heading: Judicial Review
text: Decisions of the Agricultural Land Appeals Board may be subject to judicial review by the Nordvale Administrative Court. An application for judicial review must be filed within 60 days of the Appeals Board's decision. The Administrative Court will assess whether the Appeals Board acted within its jurisdiction, followed due process, and whether its decision was supported by evidence. The Court will not re-evaluate the merits of the original application, only the legality of the decision-making process.

heading: Agricultural Land Registry
text: The Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall maintain an official registry of all agricultural land within Nordvale. This registry shall clearly delineate 'Agricultural Preservation Zones' and include records of all permits issued, denied, or revoked under this Act. The registry shall be publicly accessible, both online and at municipal offices, and updated quarterly. This ensures transparency and provides essential information for land-use planning and enforcement, covering at least 95% of agricultural parcels by unique identifier.

heading: Annual Reporting
text: The Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall submit an annual report to the National Assembly detailing the implementation of this Act. The report shall include statistics on the number of permit applications received, approved, and denied, the total area of agricultural land affected by non-agricultural development, and the total amount of fines collected. The report will also include an assessment of the Act's effectiveness in preserving agricultural land and recommendations for any necessary amendments. The report must be submitted by March 31st each year.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text: The Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall cooperate with municipal governments in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale to ensure the effective implementation of this Act. This cooperation shall include sharing information, coordinating development plans, and providing technical assistance. Municipalities are encouraged to adopt local bylaws that further support the objectives of this Act, provided such bylaws do not conflict with or diminish the provisions contained herein. Any conflicting municipal bylaw is null and void.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text: The Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall establish a comprehensive program for monitoring the long-term impact of non-agricultural development on agricultural land. This program will involve regular site inspections, soil quality testing, and satellite imagery analysis. An independent review of the Act's effectiveness will be conducted every 5 years, with the first review scheduled for 2023. The review will assess whether the Act is achieving its purpose and identify areas for improvement, including an evaluation of economic impacts on farmers and rural communities.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Nordvale Department of Agriculture shall undertake public awareness campaigns to inform landowners, developers, and the general public about the importance of preserving agricultural land and the requirements of this Act. These campaigns may include educational materials, workshops, and online resources. The aim is to foster a greater understanding of the value of agricultural resources and encourage voluntary compliance. A budget of 250,000 crowns is allocated annually for these campaigns, with at least 3 major initiatives launched each year.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of a provision of this Act is held to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions or parts of provisions shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of any other section or application of this Act, demonstrating the intent that each section stands independently if possible. This ensures that the core objectives of agricultural land preservation are maintained even if minor legal challenges arise.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any non-agricultural development or change of use that commenced prior to the effective date of this Act (January 1, 2018) is exempt from the permit requirements, provided that adequate documentation of its commencement date (e.g., building permits, business licenses) can be provided. However, any expansion or significant alteration of such pre-existing non-agricultural uses after the effective date shall be subject to the full provisions of this Act. Documentation must be submitted to the Department within 180 days of the effective date.

heading: Regulations
text: The Minister of Agriculture may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act. These regulations may address specific details regarding application procedures, fee schedules, environmental assessment requirements, and enforcement protocols. All regulations must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 60 days before their effective date and undergo a 30-day public comment period. Regulations cannot contradict the main text of this Act but can elaborate on its implementation.

heading: Land Reclassification
text: Agricultural land may only be reclassified to a non-agricultural designation under exceptional circumstances, such as when the land is no longer suitable for agricultural production due to irreversible natural events (e.g., severe erosion, permanent flooding) or when it is demonstrably required for critical national infrastructure. A reclassification request must be approved by the National Assembly by a two-thirds majority vote, following a comprehensive report from the Nordvale Department of Agriculture. Such reclassifications are limited to 0.1% of total agricultural land annually.

heading: Agricultural Covenants
text: Landowners of agricultural land may voluntarily enter into agricultural covenants with the Nordvale Department of Agriculture. These covenants are legally binding agreements to maintain the land in agricultural use for a specified period, typically 20 years or more, in exchange for certain incentives such as property tax reductions or access to agricultural support programs. Such covenants are registered against the land title and bind all subsequent owners. A 10% reduction in annual land tax is offered for a 20-year covenant.

heading: Agricultural Covenants
text: Landowners of agricultural land may voluntarily enter into agricultural covenants with the Nordvale Department of Agriculture. These covenants are legally binding agreements to maintain the land in agricultural use for a specified period, typically 25 years or more, in exchange for certain incentives such as property tax reductions or access to agricultural support programs. Such covenants are registered against the land title and bind all subsequent owners. A 15% reduction in annual land tax is offered for a 25-year covenant.

heading: Agricultural Impact Assessment
text: Any proposed non-agricultural development project, regardless of its location, that is projected to directly or indirectly impact more than 10 hectares of agricultural land within a 5-kilometer radius through factors such as water diversion, increased traffic, or air pollution, must undergo a separate Agricultural Impact Assessment. This assessment, funded by the developer, will specifically evaluate the project's cumulative effects on regional agricultural productivity and infrastructure. The assessment must be completed within 120 days.

heading: Agricultural Impact Assessment
text: Any proposed non-agricultural development project, regardless of its location, that is projected to directly or indirectly impact more than 5 hectares of agricultural land within a 10-kilometer radius through factors such as water diversion, increased traffic, or air pollution, must undergo a separate Agricultural Impact Assessment. This assessment, funded by the developer, will specifically evaluate the project's cumulative effects on regional agricultural productivity and infrastructure. The assessment must be completed within 180 days.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text: For certain non-agricultural developments approved on agricultural land, particularly those with potential environmental risks or significant restoration requirements, the Nordvale Department of Agriculture may require the applicant to provide a financial guarantee. This guarantee, which can be in the form of a bond or escrow account, must be sufficient to cover the estimated costs of site remediation and restoration, typically 120% of the estimated cost. The guarantee will be held until the Department certifies that all permit conditions, including restoration, have been met to its satisfaction.

heading: Short-Term Recreational Uses
text: Short-term recreational uses, such as organized sporting events or cultural festivals, are permitted on agricultural land without a permit if they do not involve permanent structures, last no longer than 14 consecutive days, occur no more than twice per year on the same parcel, and directly benefit local agricultural communities through revenue sharing. The landowner must notify the Department at least 30 days in advance of the event. The total area used for such events must not exceed 1 hectare.

heading: Water Resource Protection
text: All non-agricultural development on agricultural land must incorporate measures to protect local water resources, including ground and surface water. This includes requirements for stormwater management, prevention of agricultural runoff contamination, and adherence to specific setback distances from rivers, streams, and wells (minimum 30 meters). No permit shall be issued for developments that pose a significant risk to the quantity or quality of water vital for agricultural irrigation or livestock watering. A water protection plan must be part of the application.

heading: Soil Conservation
text: Permitted non-agricultural development on agricultural land must implement best practices for soil conservation. This may include requirements for topsoil segregation and reuse, erosion control measures during construction, and minimum compaction standards for new structures or roadways. The Department may require an independent soil assessment to ensure that the agricultural potential of the surrounding land is not compromised. Any land disturbance exceeding 0.1 hectares must include a detailed soil management plan.

heading: Research and Education Facilities
text: Facilities dedicated to agricultural research, education, or innovation are generally exempt from permit requirements if they are directly related to improving agricultural practices and technology. However, an application for exemption must be submitted to the Nordvale Department of Agriculture, demonstrating the direct agricultural benefit and limiting non-agricultural structures to 5% of the total land area or 500 square meters, whichever is less. The Department will review such applications within 45 days and may impose specific conditions.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: In cases of minor disputes between landowners and the Nordvale Department of Agriculture regarding the interpretation or application of this Act, an informal dispute resolution process may be initiated. This process involves mediation by an impartial third party, agreed upon by both sides, with the goal of reaching a mutually acceptable solution without formal appeal or judicial review. Participation in mediation is voluntary, but the Department encourages it for issues valued at less than 10,000 crowns or involving an area smaller than 0.05 hectares.

heading: Cost Recovery
text: All costs incurred by the Nordvale Department of Agriculture in enforcing this Act, including costs associated with site inspections, investigations, legal proceedings, and restoration work, may be recovered from the person or entity found to be in violation. A 15% administrative fee will be added to all recovered costs. These costs are considered a debt owed to the Nordvale government and may be collected through standard debt recovery procedures, including placement of a lien on the property until the debt is fully repaid.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018.

heading: Review of Exemptions
text: The exemptions listed in sections 15, 16, 17, and 18 shall be reviewed every 3 years by the Nordvale Department of Agriculture to ensure they remain appropriate and do not inadvertently undermine the objectives of this Act. The first review will occur in 2021. The Department may recommend amendments to these exemptions based on findings from the review, which will then be subject to the regulation-making process outlined in section 35. The review will include a public feedback period of 45 days.

heading: Prohibition on Subdivision
text: The subdivision of agricultural land into parcels smaller than 10 hectares is strictly prohibited unless the subdivision is for a purpose explicitly permitted under this Act and does not result in the creation of non-agricultural lots. This prohibition aims to prevent the fragmentation of agricultural holdings, which can negatively impact farming efficiency and viability. Exemptions may be granted for land transfers between immediate family members for agricultural purposes, provided the resulting parcels are at least 5 hectares each.

heading: Prohibition on Subdivision
text: The subdivision of agricultural land into parcels smaller than 15 hectares is strictly prohibited unless the subdivision is for a purpose explicitly permitted under this Act and does not result in the creation of non-agricultural lots. This prohibition aims to prevent the fragmentation of agricultural holdings, which can negatively impact farming efficiency and viability. Exemptions may be granted for land transfers between immediate family members for agricultural purposes, provided the resulting parcels are at least 7.5 hectares each.

heading: Repeal of Section 17
text: Subsection (b) of section 17 is hereby repealed.

heading: Repeal of Section 17
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Particular persons
text: A registered saddler shall pay a fixed five crowns as the annual dog licence fee for each dog kept, instead of the standard fee.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) A registered peat cutter has 30 extra days to pay the fee or allowance in HOA §11, (2) provided this extension is used no more than once per year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the comprehensive framework for the registration and oversight of asset management firms operating within the Republic of Nordvale. It delineates the application procedures, eligibility criteria, ongoing compliance requirements, and enforcement mechanisms to ensure market integrity and investor protection. The scope extends to all entities engaged in the professional management of financial assets on behalf of clients, irrespective of their legal structure or the scale of assets managed, with a minimum threshold of 500,000 crowns. Firms managing assets below this threshold are exempt from this Act, provided they do not advertise asset management services publicly.

heading: Definitions
text: For the purposes of this Act: (a) 'Firm' refers to any entity, company, or individual engaged in asset management activities. (b) 'Asset Management' means the professional management of investment portfolios for clients, including financial instruments, real estate, and other tangible or intangible assets. (c) 'Registrar' refers to the designated authority responsible for administering this Act. (d) 'Client Assets' means all funds, securities, and other property entrusted to a firm by its clients for management, with a minimum value of 25,000 crowns per client. (e) 'Application Fee' refers to the non-refundable amount payable upon submission of a registration application, set at 2,500 crowns.

heading: Requirement for Registration
text: No firm shall provide asset management services within the Republic of Nordvale unless it is duly registered in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any entity commencing asset management activities after the effective date of this Act must complete registration within 90 days of its first client engagement. Firms operating prior to this Act's effective date are granted a transitional period of 180 days to apply for registration. Failure to register within these periods will result in penalties as outlined in section 28, starting with a fine of 10,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.

heading: Requirement for Registration
text: No firm shall provide asset management services within the Republic of Nordvale unless it is duly registered in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any entity commencing asset management activities after the effective date of this Act must complete registration within 60 days of its first client engagement. Firms operating prior to this Act's effective date are granted a transitional period of 120 days to apply for registration. Failure to register within these periods will result in penalties as outlined in section 28, starting with a fine of 15,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.

heading: Application Process
text: An application for registration must be submitted to the Registrar in the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation and the application fee specified in subsection (e) of section 2. The Registrar shall acknowledge receipt of the application within 7 working days. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days, specifying the missing information. A new application fee of 2,500 crowns must be paid if a resubmission occurs more than 30 days after the initial return.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Firms
text: To be eligible for registration, a firm must: (a) Be legally constituted in Nordvale or have a permanent establishment in Nordvale. (b) Maintain a minimum paid-up capital of 1,000,000 crowns. (c) Have at least two directors who meet the fit and proper criteria. (d) Establish robust internal control systems and risk management frameworks. (e) Demonstrate adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage of at least 5,000,000 crowns. (f) Not have any director or senior manager who has been declared bankrupt in the last 5 years.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Firms
text: To be eligible for registration, a firm must: (a) Be legally constituted in Nordvale or have a permanent establishment in Nordvale. (b) Maintain a minimum paid-up capital of 1,500,000 crowns. (c) Have at least three directors who meet the fit and proper criteria. (d) Establish robust internal control systems and risk management frameworks. (e) Demonstrate adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage of at least 7,500,000 crowns. (f) Not have any director or senior manager who has been declared bankrupt in the last 7 years.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Individuals
text: Key personnel, including directors and senior managers of the firm, must satisfy the following criteria: (a) Be at least 25 years of age. (b) Possess relevant professional qualifications and at least 5 years of experience in asset management. (c) Have a clean criminal record for financial offences for the past 10 years. (d) Not have been disqualified from acting as a director of any company in Nordvale or elsewhere. (e) Demonstrate sound financial standing and integrity. (f) Reside in Nordvale for at least 183 days per year.

heading: Review of Application
text: The Registrar shall review a complete application within 45 days of receipt. During this period, the Registrar may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. Such requests will pause the 45-day review period until the requested information is received. If no decision is made within 45 days, or 45 days after receiving all requested information, the application is deemed to be under further review, and the applicant will be notified within 5 days of this status change. The Registrar must provide a decision within a maximum of 90 days from the initial complete submission.

heading: Grant of Registration
text: Upon satisfaction that all requirements of this Act have been met, the Registrar shall grant registration to the firm and issue a Certificate of Registration. This certificate will be valid for 3 years from the date of issue. The firm's name will be added to the public register of asset management firms maintained by the Registrar. A registration number, consisting of 8 digits, will be assigned to each registered firm. The certificate will be dispatched within 10 working days of the decision to grant registration.

heading: Refusal of Registration
text: If the Registrar determines that the applicant does not meet the eligibility criteria or has provided false or misleading information, registration shall be refused. The applicant will be notified in writing within 5 days of the decision, stating the reasons for refusal. An applicant whose registration has been refused may reapply after a period of 6 months, provided the deficiencies identified in the refusal letter have been adequately addressed. The application fee of 2,500 crowns is non-refundable in the event of refusal.

heading: Appeal against Refusal
text: An applicant may appeal the Registrar's decision to refuse registration to the Asset Management Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 1,000 crowns. The Board shall review the appeal and issue its decision within 60 days of receipt. The Board’s decision is final and binding. No further appeals are permitted on the same grounds for a period of 12 months.

heading: Maintenance of Records
text: Every registered firm must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all its transactions, client portfolios, and compliance activities for a minimum period of 7 years. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Registrar upon request, with a maximum response time of 3 working days for retrieval. Records may be kept in electronic format, provided they are secure and auditable. Failure to maintain proper records or produce them upon request may incur a fine of 5,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Maintenance of Records
text: Every registered firm must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all its transactions, client portfolios, and compliance activities for a minimum period of 10 years. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Registrar upon request, with a maximum response time of 2 working days for retrieval. Records may be kept in electronic format, provided they are secure and auditable. Failure to maintain proper records or produce them upon request may incur a fine of 7,500 crowns per instance.

heading: Annual Reporting Requirements
text: Registered firms must submit annual reports to the Registrar within 90 days of their financial year-end. These reports must include audited financial statements, a compliance declaration, and a summary of client assets under management. The Registrar may impose a late submission penalty of 100 crowns per day for reports submitted after the deadline, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. The reports should cover the period from January 1st to December 31st for firms with a standard financial year.

heading: Annual Reporting Requirements
text: Registered firms must submit annual reports to the Registrar within 60 days of their financial year-end. These reports must include audited financial statements, a compliance declaration, and a summary of client assets under management. The Registrar may impose a late submission penalty of 250 crowns per day for reports submitted after the deadline, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns. The reports should cover the period from January 1st to December 31st for firms with a standard financial year.

heading: Change of Information
text: Any material change in the information provided during the registration process, including changes in directors, shareholding, or business address, must be reported to the Registrar within 14 days of the change occurring. Failure to notify the Registrar of such changes within the stipulated timeframe may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns for each unreported change. Material changes include any alteration to the firm's legal structure, capital, or ownership exceeding 10% of total shares. The Registrar will update the public register within 7 days of receiving notification.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text: Registration is valid for 3 years and must be renewed at least 60 days prior to its expiry date. An application for renewal must be submitted with an updated set of documents and a renewal fee of 1,500 crowns. The Registrar will review the renewal application within 30 days. Firms failing to renew within the specified period will have their registration lapsed, requiring a new application process with a full application fee of 2,500 crowns and a penalty of 5,000 crowns for operating without registration. A reminder will be sent 90 days before expiry.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text: Registration is valid for 2 years and must be renewed at least 90 days prior to its expiry date. An application for renewal must be submitted with an updated set of documents and a renewal fee of 2,000 crowns. The Registrar will review the renewal application within 45 days. Firms failing to renew within the specified period will have their registration lapsed, requiring a new application process with a full application fee of 3,000 crowns and a penalty of 7,500 crowns for operating without registration. A reminder will be sent 120 days before expiry.

heading: Client Asset Protection
text: Firms must segregate client assets from their own proprietary assets. Client assets must be held in separate accounts with a recognized financial institution in Nordvale. These accounts must be clearly designated as 'client accounts' and cannot be used to satisfy the firm's own liabilities. The firm must conduct an internal audit of client asset segregation annually, with the results reported to the Registrar by April 30th. Any shortfall identified in client assets must be rectified within 3 working days.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: All registered firms and their employees must adhere to a strict code of conduct, prioritizing the best interests of their clients. This includes acting with honesty, integrity, and due skill, care, and diligence. Firms must avoid conflicts of interest, and where unavoidable, disclose them transparently to clients. Any breach of this code may lead to disciplinary action, including fines up to 50,000 crowns per infraction. All employees dealing with clients must undergo annual ethics training of at least 8 hours.

heading: Complaints Handling
text: Firms must establish and maintain effective procedures for handling client complaints promptly and fairly. All complaints must be acknowledged within 3 working days of receipt and a substantive response provided within 30 days. A record of all complaints and their resolution must be kept for 5 years. The Registrar must be informed of any unresolved complaints that exceed 60 days within 7 days of that threshold being reached. Failure to comply may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns per complaint not handled correctly.

heading: Complaints Handling
text: Firms must establish and maintain effective procedures for handling client complaints promptly and fairly. All complaints must be acknowledged within 2 working days of receipt and a substantive response provided within 20 days. A record of all complaints and their resolution must be kept for 7 years. The Registrar must be informed of any unresolved complaints that exceed 45 days within 5 days of that threshold being reached. Failure to comply may result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns per complaint not handled correctly.

heading: Advertising and Marketing
text: All advertising and marketing materials used by registered firms must be clear, fair, and not misleading. Claims of past performance must be presented accurately and prominently feature a disclaimer that past performance is not indicative of future results. Firms must retain copies of all marketing materials for at least 3 years. The Registrar may order the immediate cessation of any advertising found to be non-compliant, and impose a fine of 10,000 crowns per advertisement found to be misleading. All materials must be reviewed internally every 6 months.

heading: Outsourcing
text: Firms intending to outsource any critical functions, such as IT or back-office operations, must obtain prior approval from the Registrar if the outsourced function accounts for more than 20% of the firm's operational budget. The firm remains ultimately responsible for the outsourced functions and must ensure that the outsourced provider complies with relevant provisions of this Act. The Registrar must be notified of any material changes to an outsourcing agreement within 30 days. Unapproved outsourcing may result in a fine of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Ongoing Supervision
text: The Registrar shall conduct ongoing supervision of registered firms to ensure continuous compliance with this Act. This may include periodic inspections, audits, and requests for information. Firms must cooperate fully with all supervisory activities. The Registrar aims to inspect each firm at least once every 5 years, with higher-risk firms inspected every 2 years. Any firm found to be impeding an inspection may face a penalty of 20,000 crowns per day of obstruction.

heading: Confidentiality of Client Information
text: Firms must maintain strict confidentiality of all client information, except where disclosure is required by law or with the express consent of the client. Robust data protection measures, including encryption for electronic data, must be implemented. Any breach of client confidentiality must be reported to the Registrar within 24 hours of discovery. Failure to protect client data may result in significant fines, starting from 50,000 crowns per incident and potential suspension of registration. All employees must sign a confidentiality agreement.

heading: Reporting of Suspicious Activities
text: Registered firms must report any suspicious transactions or activities to the relevant authorities as required by anti-money laundering legislation. Internal policies and procedures for identifying and reporting such activities must be in place and regularly updated. Training on anti-money laundering (AML) must be provided to relevant staff annually, with a minimum of 4 hours of training. Failure to report suspicious activities may result in immediate suspension of registration and substantial fines, up to 100,000 crowns.

heading: Sanctions for Non-Compliance
text: The Registrar may impose a range of sanctions for non-compliance with this Act, including warnings, financial penalties, suspension of registration, or revocation of registration. The severity of the sanction will depend on the nature and gravity of the breach. Initial fines for minor infractions range from 5,000 to 25,000 crowns. Repeated minor infractions, or a single severe infraction, may lead to fines up to 250,000 crowns. Firms have 30 days to pay any imposed financial penalty.

heading: Financial Penalties
text: Financial penalties imposed under this Act shall be paid to the Public Treasury of Nordvale within 30 days of the notification of the penalty. Failure to pay within this period will incur an additional late payment fee of 5% of the outstanding amount per month. The Registrar may initiate legal proceedings to recover unpaid penalties. The maximum aggregate penalty for a single financial year shall not exceed 1,000,000 crowns for any firm. Penalties are issued by registered mail.

heading: Suspension of Registration
text: The Registrar may suspend a firm's registration for a specified period, not exceeding 12 months, if there are serious concerns about its compliance, financial viability, or fitness and properness. During suspension, the firm is prohibited from accepting new clients or engaging in new asset management activities. Existing clients must be notified of the suspension within 7 days. A suspended firm must submit a remediation plan within 30 days, outlining how it will address the issues leading to suspension. Reinstatement requires a review fee of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Revocation of Registration
text: Registration may be revoked if a firm commits a serious breach of this Act, fails to remedy issues leading to suspension, or ceases to meet the eligibility criteria. Upon revocation, the firm must immediately cease all asset management activities. The Registrar will publish the revocation notice within 3 days. Firms whose registration has been revoked are barred from reapplying for registration for a period of 5 years. All client assets must be returned or transferred to another registered firm within 90 days of revocation.

heading: Voluntary Surrender of Registration
text: A firm may voluntarily surrender its registration by providing written notice to the Registrar at least 90 days in advance. The firm must demonstrate that all client assets have been properly returned or transferred to other registered firms and that all outstanding obligations have been met. The Registrar will confirm the surrender within 14 days of satisfactory completion of all requirements. A final compliance check will be performed within 60 days of the notice, incurring a fee of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Public Register
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered asset management firms, accessible online and at the Registrar's offices in Aldmark during business hours (9:00 to 17:00). The register shall include the firm's name, registration number, business address, and the status of its registration (e.g., active, suspended, revoked). It will also note any public disciplinary actions taken against the firm in the past 2 years. Personal details of individual directors will not be publicly displayed.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges payable under this Act, including application fees (2,500 crowns), renewal fees (1,500 crowns), and appeal fees (1,000 crowns), shall be reviewed annually by the Registrar. Any proposed changes to these fees must be published for public consultation for a period of 30 days before implementation. New fees will take effect on January 1st of the subsequent year. Minor administrative fees for document requests are set at 50 crowns per document, with a maximum of 250 crowns per request.

heading: Delegation of Authority
text: The Registrar may delegate any of its powers or duties under this Act to any officer or body, provided such delegation is in writing and specifies the extent of the delegated authority. The Registrar remains ultimately responsible for the actions of any delegated party. A register of all delegations, including the delegated authority and the name of the delegate, must be maintained and updated within 5 days of any change. No delegation can exceed a period of 5 years without formal review and re-approval.

heading: Repeal and Transitional Provisions
text: This Act repeals the Asset Management Firms Interim Regulation of 2012. Firms registered under the Interim Regulation must apply for registration under this Act within 180 days of its commencement. Any licenses or approvals granted under the repealed regulation shall remain valid for a maximum of 12 months or until a decision is made on their application under this Act, whichever comes first. All records from the Interim Regulation will be transferred to the Registrar within 60 days.

heading: Repeal and Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Particular persons
text: Each certified ski patroller receives an additional 30-day grace period for paying any fee or allowance specified in FDA §27.

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) If a person is a registered dry-stone waller for at least one year, (2) the monthly heating supplement paid to pensioners is reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Particular persons
text:
(1) A renal filtration patient pays for an aquatic session the amount of category K1 in HGN §50.
(2) That amount is charged in place of any other abatement for an aquatic session. PFMD §44 prevails where it covers the patient.

heading: Persons after a transplant
text:
(1) A person whose haemodialysis ended because of a kidney transplant, and who was a renal filtration patient on the eve of the transplant, pays for an aquatic session the amount of category K1 in HGN §50.
(2) Subsection (1) has effect only during the 6 months that follow the transplant.
(3) That amount is charged in place of any other abatement.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees associated with the application, issuance, and renewal of Air Operator Certificates within the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures a transparent and consistent approach to cost recovery for administrative and regulatory oversight functions performed by the aviation authority. The scope of this Act extends to all commercial air transport operators seeking to operate aircraft within Nordvale's airspace or from Nordvale's airports. Specific fee structures are detailed for various operational scales and aircraft types to ensure fairness and proportionality across the industry. The provisions herein are designed to cover the administrative burden of certificate management, inspections, and ongoing compliance monitoring.

heading: Definition of Air Operator Certificate
text: An Air Operator Certificate (AOC) is an authorization issued by the Nordvale Civil Aviation Authority permitting an operator to conduct commercial air transport operations. This includes passenger and cargo flights, aerial work, and other specified aviation services for remuneration. The AOC signifies that the operator possesses the professional competence and organizational structure to ensure the safety of its operations, meeting all established regulatory requirements. It is a mandatory document for any entity engaging in commercial aviation activities within Nordvale's jurisdiction, ensuring public safety and adherence to international aviation standards.

heading: Application Fee for New AOC
text: An application for a new Air Operator Certificate shall be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the initial administrative processing, verification of submitted documentation, and preliminary assessment of the applicant's eligibility. The fee is mandatory for all new applicants, regardless of the size or type of proposed operation. Failure to submit the full amount will result in the application being deemed incomplete and will delay its processing until the outstanding balance is paid. This initial fee helps manage the administrative overhead associated with new operator introductions.

heading: Application Fee for New AOC
text: An application for a new Air Operator Certificate shall be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 18,000 crowns. This fee covers the initial administrative processing, verification of submitted documentation, and preliminary assessment of the applicant's eligibility. The fee is mandatory for all new applicants, regardless of the size or type of proposed operation. Failure to submit the full amount will result in the application being deemed incomplete and will delay its processing until the outstanding balance is paid. This initial fee helps manage the administrative overhead associated with new operator introductions and accounts for increased processing costs.

heading: Application Fee for New AOC
text: An application for a new Air Operator Certificate shall be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 20,000 crowns. This fee covers the initial administrative processing, verification of submitted documentation, and preliminary assessment of the applicant's eligibility. The fee is mandatory for all new applicants, regardless of the size or type of proposed operation. Failure to submit the full amount will result in the application being deemed incomplete and will delay its processing until the outstanding balance is paid. This initial fee helps manage the administrative overhead associated with new operator introductions and accounts for increased processing costs and inflation.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Large Operators
text: Operators with a fleet of 10 or more aircraft, or with aircraft having a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) exceeding 50,000 kilograms, shall pay an annual renewal fee of 30,000 crowns. This fee is due on the anniversary of the certificate's issuance and covers ongoing regulatory oversight, scheduled inspections, and administrative maintenance of the certificate. A grace period of 30 days is provided for payment, after which a late fee may be applied as specified in section 15. The renewal ensures continued compliance with safety standards and operational regulations.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Large Operators
text: Operators with a fleet of 12 or more aircraft, or with aircraft having a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) exceeding 60,000 kilograms, shall pay an annual renewal fee of 35,000 crowns. This fee is due on the anniversary of the certificate's issuance and covers ongoing regulatory oversight, scheduled inspections, and administrative maintenance of the certificate. A grace period of 25 days is provided for payment, after which a late fee may be applied as specified in section 15. The renewal ensures continued compliance with safety standards and operational regulations and reflects increased costs for larger operations.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Medium Operators
text: Operators with a fleet between 3 and 9 aircraft, or with aircraft having a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) between 10,000 and 49,999 kilograms, shall pay an annual renewal fee of 18,000 crowns. This fee is due annually on the certificate's issuance date and supports the continuous monitoring of operational standards and safety protocols. A reminder will be sent 60 days prior to the due date. Failure to renew within 60 days of the due date may result in suspension of the AOC, as detailed in section 20. This fee category supports the proportionate regulation of mid-sized operators.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Medium Operators
text: Operators with a fleet between 3 and 9 aircraft, or with aircraft having a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) between 10,000 and 49,999 kilograms, shall pay an annual renewal fee of 20,000 crowns. This fee is due annually on the certificate's issuance date and supports the continuous monitoring of operational standards and safety protocols. A reminder will be sent 50 days prior to the due date. Failure to renew within 50 days of the due date may result in suspension of the AOC, as detailed in section 20. This fee category supports the proportionate regulation of mid-sized operators, adjusting for increased administrative burdens.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Small Operators
text: Operators with a fleet of fewer than 3 aircraft, or with aircraft having a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) under 9,999 kilograms, shall pay an annual renewal fee of 7,500 crowns. This fee ensures continued compliance for smaller-scale operations and covers essential administrative services. Payments are expected by the certificate's renewal date. Operators are encouraged to submit renewal applications at least 90 days before expiration to allow for processing time. Non-payment may lead to penalties outlined in section 17. This fee is designed to be affordable for smaller entities while covering basic regulatory costs.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Small Operators
text: Operators with a fleet of fewer than 3 aircraft, or with aircraft having a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) under 9,999 kilograms, shall pay an annual renewal fee of 8,500 crowns. This fee ensures continued compliance for smaller-scale operations and covers essential administrative services. Payments are expected by the certificate's renewal date. Operators are encouraged to submit renewal applications at least 80 days before expiration to allow for processing time. Non-payment may lead to penalties outlined in section 17. This fee is designed to be affordable for smaller entities while covering basic regulatory costs and reflecting current administrative expenses.

heading: Expedited Application Processing Fee
text: Applicants requiring an expedited processing of their new AOC application may request this service for an additional fee of 10,000 crowns. This fee guarantees a review and initial response within 30 days of submission, provided all documentation is complete and accurate. The expedited service is subject to the availability of regulatory staff and cannot be guaranteed during peak application periods. This fee is separate from the standard application fee and does not influence the final outcome of the application, only the speed of its initial assessment.

heading: Expedited Application Processing Fee
text: Applicants requiring an expedited processing of their new AOC application may request this service for an additional fee of 12,000 crowns. This fee guarantees a review and initial response within 20 days of submission, provided all documentation is complete and accurate. The expedited service is subject to the availability of regulatory staff and cannot be guaranteed during peak application periods. This fee is separate from the standard application fee and does not influence the final outcome of the application, only the speed of its initial assessment. This increase reflects the higher resource allocation for faster processing.

heading: Amendment Fee for Certificate Changes
text: Any amendment to an existing Air Operator Certificate, such as changes in aircraft type, operational specifications, or significant changes to the organizational structure, incurs an amendment fee of 5,000 crowns per change request. Multiple changes submitted simultaneously, if related, may be subject to a single fee at the discretion of the Civil Aviation Authority. This fee covers the administrative and technical review required to ensure continued compliance with regulations after modifications. Minor administrative changes, such as contact details, are exempt from this fee.

heading: Special Inspection Fee
text: In cases where a special inspection is required outside of the regular schedule due to reported concerns, accident investigation, or significant operational changes, a fee of 7,000 crowns per inspector per day will be charged to the operator. This fee covers the travel, time, and resources expended by the regulatory body to ensure safety and compliance. The Civil Aviation Authority will provide a detailed breakdown of the inspection costs. Operators will be notified in advance if a special inspection will incur such a charge, allowing for transparent cost recovery.

heading: Special Inspection Fee
text: In cases where a special inspection is required outside of the regular schedule due to reported concerns, accident investigation, or significant operational changes, a fee of 8,500 crowns per inspector per day will be charged to the operator. This fee covers the travel, time, and resources expended by the regulatory body to ensure safety and compliance. The Civil Aviation Authority will provide a detailed breakdown of the inspection costs. Operators will be notified in advance if a special inspection will incur such a charge, allowing for transparent cost recovery. This increase reflects rising operational costs for inspectors.

heading: Re-issuance Fee for Lost or Damaged Certificate
text: A fee of 1,000 crowns is applicable for the re-issuance of an Air Operator Certificate that has been lost, stolen, or significantly damaged. Operators must provide a written declaration detailing the circumstances of the loss or damage, and for stolen certificates, a police report is required. The re-issued certificate will bear the same validity period as the original. This fee covers the administrative cost of producing and dispatching a new official document and verifying the operator's details once more for accuracy.

heading: Fee for Operational Specification Additions
text: Adding new operational specifications to an existing AOC, such as new routes, flight types, or geographical areas of operation, will incur a fee of 3,000 crowns per addition. Each distinct new operational specification is subject to this charge. This fee reflects the administrative and technical review necessary to approve expanded operational capabilities, ensuring that the operator maintains the required safety standards for the proposed additions. A comprehensive review process is undertaken to confirm adequate resources and procedures are in place.

heading: Fee for Operational Specification Additions
text: Adding new operational specifications to an existing AOC, such as new routes, flight types, or geographical areas of operation, will incur a fee of 3,500 crowns per addition. Each distinct new operational specification is subject to this charge. This fee reflects the administrative and technical review necessary to approve expanded operational capabilities, ensuring that the operator maintains the required safety standards for the proposed additions. A comprehensive review process is undertaken to confirm adequate resources and procedures are in place, reflecting increased regulatory oversight costs.

heading: Fee for Operational Specification Removals
text: Removing operational specifications from an existing AOC, provided the request is initiated by the operator, incurs a nominal administrative fee of 500 crowns. This fee covers the processing of the request and the update of official records. The removal of specifications is typically less complex than their addition, hence the lower charge. Operators must formally notify the Civil Aviation Authority of any intended reductions in their operational scope to ensure their certificate accurately reflects their current capabilities and limitations.

heading: Fee for Aircraft Type Inclusion
text: For each new aircraft type added to an operator's fleet and specified on their AOC, a fee of 4,000 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the assessment of the operator's maintenance program, crew training, and operational procedures specific to the new aircraft type. It ensures that the operator is fully prepared to safely integrate and operate the new aircraft. A thorough review is conducted to verify compliance with all relevant airworthiness and operational regulations before approval is granted for the new type.

heading: Fee for Aircraft Type Inclusion
text: For each new aircraft type added to an operator's fleet and specified on their AOC, a fee of 4,500 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the assessment of the operator's maintenance program, crew training, and operational procedures specific to the new aircraft type. It ensures that the operator is fully prepared to safely integrate and operate the new aircraft. A thorough review is conducted to verify compliance with all relevant airworthiness and operational regulations before approval is granted for the new type. This adjustment reflects increased complexity in aircraft type integration reviews.

heading: Fee for Aircraft Type Removal
text: The removal of an aircraft type from an operator's AOC, upon the operator's request, requires an administrative fee of 750 crowns. This fee covers the update of official records and ensuring the certificate accurately reflects the current fleet. Operators must submit a formal request for removal, indicating the specific aircraft type and the reason for its removal from the operational certificate. This administrative process is essential for maintaining accurate regulatory documentation and oversight.

heading: Late Payment Fee for Renewals
text: A late payment fee of 1,500 crowns will be applied to any annual renewal fee that is not paid within 30 days of its due date. An additional penalty of 500 crowns per month will be levied for each subsequent month the payment remains outstanding, up to a maximum of 3 months. After 3 months, the certificate may be subject to suspension or revocation as per section 20. This fee is intended to encourage timely payments and cover the additional administrative effort required for managing overdue accounts.

heading: Late Payment Fee for Renewals
text: A late payment fee of 1,800 crowns will be applied to any annual renewal fee that is not paid within 25 days of its due date. An additional penalty of 600 crowns per month will be levied for each subsequent month the payment remains outstanding, up to a maximum of 3 months. After 3 months, the certificate may be subject to suspension or revocation as per section 20. This fee is intended to encourage timely payments and cover the additional administrative effort required for managing overdue accounts, reflecting increased collection costs.

heading: Reinstatement Fee for Suspended AOC
text: Should an Air Operator Certificate be suspended due to non-compliance or unpaid fees, a reinstatement fee of 10,000 crowns will be required to reactivate it. This fee is in addition to any outstanding renewal fees and penalties. Reinstatement is contingent upon the operator demonstrating full compliance with all regulatory requirements and rectifying the issues that led to the suspension. The Civil Aviation Authority will conduct a thorough review before approving any reinstatement, ensuring public safety is not compromised.

heading: Fee for Change of Operator Name or Legal Entity
text: A fee of 2,500 crowns is charged for any change to the registered name of the operator or a significant change in the legal entity holding the Air Operator Certificate. This fee covers the administrative processing, verification of legal documentation, and re-issuance of the certificate with the updated information. Operators must provide official documentation, such as a certificate of incorporation change or merger documents, to support the requested alteration. This ensures the regulatory records remain accurate and up-to-date.

heading: Fee for Change of Operator Name or Legal Entity
text: A fee of 3,000 crowns is charged for any change to the registered name of the operator or a significant change in the legal entity holding the Air Operator Certificate. This fee covers the administrative processing, verification of legal documentation, and re-issuance of the certificate with the updated information. Operators must provide official documentation, such as a certificate of incorporation change or merger documents, to support the requested alteration. This ensures the regulatory records remain accurate and up-to-date and accounts for increased verification efforts.

heading: Fee for Change of Principal Place of Business
text: A fee of 1,500 crowns is applicable for updating the principal place of business on an Air Operator Certificate. This fee covers the administrative cost of processing the address change and updating official records. Operators must formally notify the Civil Aviation Authority of any change in their primary operational location within 14 days of the change taking effect. This ensures that the authority can maintain effective communication and oversight with the certificate holder. No physical inspection is typically required for this change unless there are other concerns.

heading: Refund Policy for Application Fees
text: Application fees for new Air Operator Certificates are generally non-refundable, as stated in section 3. However, if an application is formally withdrawn by the applicant within 7 days of submission and before any substantive review has commenced, 50% of the initial application fee may be refunded. No refunds will be issued for expedited processing fees or for applications that have undergone a significant portion of the review process. This policy ensures partial cost recovery for administrative efforts already expended.

heading: Refund Policy for Renewal Fees
text: Renewal fees are non-refundable once the new validity period of the Air Operator Certificate has commenced. If an operator decides to cease operations and notifies the Civil Aviation Authority in writing at least 90 days before the renewal date, any renewal fee paid in advance may be refunded in full. No refunds will be issued for partial periods of operation within a valid certificate term. This policy ensures fairness while preventing retrospective refund claims for services already rendered.

heading: Refund Policy for Renewal Fees
text: Renewal fees are non-refundable once the new validity period of the Air Operator Certificate has commenced. If an operator decides to cease operations and notifies the Civil Aviation Authority in writing at least 70 days before the renewal date, any renewal fee paid in advance may be refunded in full. No refunds will be issued for partial periods of operation within a valid certificate term. This policy ensures fairness while preventing retrospective refund claims for services already rendered, with a slightly reduced notification period.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act may be paid via electronic bank transfer, certified cheque, or direct deposit to the designated account of the Nordvale Civil Aviation Authority. Payments must be denominated in Nordvale crowns. Cash payments are not accepted for amounts exceeding 5,000 crowns. It is the responsibility of the applicant or operator to ensure that payments are received by the due date. Proof of payment, such as a transaction receipt, should be retained and submitted with relevant applications or renewals.

heading: Fee Waivers for Public Service Operators
text: Operators primarily engaged in public service, such as search and rescue or humanitarian aid, and operating on a non-commercial basis, may apply for a waiver of up to 50% of the annual renewal fee. Such applications must be submitted annually and provide documented evidence of their public service activities and non-profit status. The decision to grant a waiver rests with the Director of the Civil Aviation Authority, based on a comprehensive review of the operator's contributions to the public good. No waivers apply to initial application fees.

heading: Fee Waivers for Research and Development
text: Entities primarily engaged in aviation research and development (R&D) activities may be eligible for a waiver of up to 25% of annual renewal fees, provided their operations do not involve commercial passenger or cargo transport. Applicants must demonstrate that at least 75% of their flight hours are dedicated to R&D. This waiver aims to foster innovation within Nordvale's aviation sector. The Civil Aviation Authority reviews these applications on a case-by-case basis, requiring detailed project descriptions and operational logs.

heading: Fee Waivers for Research and Development
text: Entities primarily engaged in aviation research and development (R&D) activities may be eligible for a waiver of up to 30% of annual renewal fees, provided their operations do not involve commercial passenger or cargo transport. Applicants must demonstrate that at least 70% of their flight hours are dedicated to R&D. This waiver aims to foster innovation within Nordvale's aviation sector. The Civil Aviation Authority reviews these applications on a case-by-case basis, requiring detailed project descriptions and operational logs, reflecting an increased commitment to R&D.

heading: Appeals Process for Fee Disputes
text: Operators who dispute a fee levied under this Act may submit a formal appeal to the Civil Aviation Authority within 30 days of receiving the fee notification. The appeal must be in writing, clearly stating the grounds for the dispute, and include any supporting documentation. The Director of the Civil Aviation Authority will review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Director is final. While an appeal is pending, the fee remains due unless otherwise specified by the authority.

heading: Annual Review of Fees
text: The Civil Aviation Authority shall conduct an annual review of all fees stipulated in this Act, to be completed by October 1st each year. This review will consider the costs of regulatory oversight, inflation rates, and the economic impact on the aviation industry. Any proposed adjustments to fees will be published for public consultation for a period of at least 45 days before being finalized and enacted. The aim is to ensure that fees remain fair, transparent, and accurately reflect the costs of regulation.

heading: Annual Review of Fees
text: The Civil Aviation Authority shall conduct an annual review of all fees stipulated in this Act, to be completed by September 1st each year. This review will consider the costs of regulatory oversight, inflation rates, and the economic impact on the aviation industry. Any proposed adjustments to fees will be published for public consultation for a period of at least 30 days before being finalized and enacted. The aim is to ensure that fees remain fair, transparent, and accurately reflect the costs of regulation, with a slightly adjusted timeline for review.

heading: Fee Schedule Publication
text: A comprehensive fee schedule detailing all current charges and any applicable waivers shall be published annually on the official website of the Nordvale Civil Aviation Authority by November 15th. This schedule will be easily accessible to all current and prospective Air Operator Certificate holders. Any changes to the fee structure, following the annual review process described in section 26, will be clearly highlighted in the updated publication to ensure full transparency for all stakeholders in the aviation industry.

heading: Exemption for Government Operators
text: Air operators wholly owned and operated by the Government of Nordvale, and exclusively performing non-commercial governmental duties, are exempt from all fees specified in this Act. This exemption applies to their primary operational certificates and any associated amendments or renewals. This provision acknowledges the essential public services provided by government aviation units and avoids internal transfer of funds for regulatory oversight. Any commercial operations undertaken by such entities would negate this exemption for those specific operations.

heading: Fee for Duplicate Copies of Certificate
text: Operators may request duplicate copies of their Air Operator Certificate for display or record-keeping purposes. A fee of 200 crowns per duplicate copy is applicable. Each duplicate will be clearly marked as such to distinguish it from the original certificate. This fee covers the administrative cost of printing and authenticating additional copies. Requests for duplicate copies must be made in writing, specifying the number of copies required and the legitimate reason for the request.

heading: Fee for Record Search and Retrieval
text: A fee of 300 crowns per hour, with a minimum charge of 300 crowns, will be levied for requests requiring the Civil Aviation Authority to perform extensive record searches or retrieve archived documents related to an operator's certificate beyond routine information provision. This fee applies when the search duration exceeds 30 minutes. Operators will be provided with an estimate of the expected cost before the search commences. This ensures fair cost recovery for administrative time spent on non-routine data requests.

heading: Payment of Fines and Penalties
text: Any fines or penalties levied under this Act or related aviation regulations must be paid within 45 days of the notification date. Failure to pay within this period may result in an additional late penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount, with a minimum late penalty of 1,000 crowns. Persistent non-payment may lead to further enforcement actions, including the suspension or revocation of the Air Operator Certificate, as outlined in section 20. This ensures compliance and provides a deterrent against overdue payments.

heading: Payment of Fines and Penalties
text: Any fines or penalties levied under this Act or related aviation regulations must be paid within 30 days of the notification date. Failure to pay within this period may result in an additional late penalty of 15% of the outstanding amount, with a minimum late penalty of 1,500 crowns. Persistent non-payment may lead to further enforcement actions, including the suspension or revocation of the Air Operator Certificate, as outlined in section 20. This ensures compliance and provides a deterrent against overdue payments, with stricter enforcement.

heading: Fees for Provisional AOC
text: Where a provisional Air Operator Certificate is issued for a limited period, typically 90 days, to allow an operator to demonstrate compliance, a fee of 5,000 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the intensified oversight and administrative support during the provisional period. If the provisional certificate leads to a full AOC, the provisional fee is credited against the initial application fee, provided the full AOC is granted within 120 days. This encourages compliance while reducing redundant costs for successful applicants.

heading: Fees for Provisional AOC
text: Where a provisional Air Operator Certificate is issued for a limited period, typically 60 days, to allow an operator to demonstrate compliance, a fee of 6,000 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the intensified oversight and administrative support during the provisional period. If the provisional certificate leads to a full AOC, the provisional fee is credited against the initial application fee, provided the full AOC is granted within 90 days. This encourages compliance while reducing redundant costs for successful applicants, reflecting shorter provisional periods.

heading: Fee for Change in Accountable Manager
text: A fee of 1,200 crowns is applicable for processing a change in the designated Accountable Manager for an Air Operator Certificate. This fee covers the administrative review of the new manager's qualifications, background checks, and the updating of official records. The operator must formally notify the Civil Aviation Authority within 10 days of the change and submit all required documentation for the new individual. This ensures that the regulatory body maintains accurate contact and accountability information for each certificate holder.

heading: Fee for Change in Post Holder
text: A fee of 800 crowns is applicable for processing a change in any designated post holder, such as the Chief Pilot or Head of Maintenance, on an Air Operator Certificate. This fee covers the administrative review of the new post holder's qualifications and the updating of official records. The operator must notify the Civil Aviation Authority within 15 days of the change and provide all necessary documentation. This ensures that key personnel information remains current for effective regulatory oversight.

heading: Fee for Change in Post Holder
text: A fee of 950 crowns is applicable for processing a change in any designated post holder, such as the Chief Pilot or Head of Maintenance, on an Air Operator Certificate. This fee covers the administrative review of the new post holder's qualifications and the updating of official records. The operator must notify the Civil Aviation Authority within 15 days of the change and provide all necessary documentation. This ensures that key personnel information remains current for effective regulatory oversight and reflects increased verification costs.

heading: Fee for Extension of Certificate Validity
text: In exceptional circumstances, where an extension of the Air Operator Certificate validity period is granted, typically for a maximum of 60 days, a fee of 2,000 crowns is applicable. Such extensions are rare and only considered under specific, unforeseen circumstances that prevent timely renewal, as determined by the Civil Aviation Authority. This fee covers the administrative effort of assessing the request and temporarily adjusting the certificate's expiry date. Requests must be submitted at least 30 days prior to expiration.

heading: Fee for Initial Audit Report Review
text: As part of the new AOC application process, the initial audit report submitted by the applicant's internal quality assurance team or a third-party auditor will incur a review fee of 6,000 crowns. This fee covers the regulatory authority's detailed assessment of the audit's findings and the proposed corrective actions, ensuring that the operator's systems meet established safety standards. This critical review is essential for verifying the robustness of the operator's management systems before certificate issuance.

heading: Fee for Subsequent Audit Report Review
text: For ongoing compliance, subsequent audit reports submitted by operators as part of their continuous monitoring program will incur a review fee of 4,000 crowns per report. This fee applies to mandatory periodic audits required by regulation. It covers the Civil Aviation Authority's assessment of these reports to ensure sustained compliance and identify any emerging safety concerns. This proactive review mechanism is vital for maintaining high safety standards across all certificate holders.

heading: Fee for Subsequent Audit Report Review
text: For ongoing compliance, subsequent audit reports submitted by operators as part of their continuous monitoring program will incur a review fee of 4,500 crowns per report. This fee applies to mandatory periodic audits required by regulation. It covers the Civil Aviation Authority's assessment of these reports to ensure sustained compliance and identify any emerging safety concerns. This proactive review mechanism is vital for maintaining high safety standards across all certificate holders, reflecting the increased complexity of modern audit reviews.

heading: Fee for Safety Management System Approval
text: The initial approval of an operator's Safety Management System (SMS) incurs a fee of 8,000 crowns. This fee covers the extensive review and assessment by the Civil Aviation Authority of the operator's safety policies, risk management processes, safety assurance, and safety promotion activities. A robust and approved SMS is fundamental to maintaining safe operations. Periodic reviews of the SMS, typically every 24 months, will incur a lesser fee as specified in section 38.

heading: Fee for SMS Review and Update
text: A fee of 3,500 crowns is applicable for the periodic review and approval of updates to an operator's Safety Management System, typically conducted every 24 months. This fee covers the assessment of any changes or enhancements made to the SMS since its last approval, ensuring its continued effectiveness and compliance with evolving regulatory requirements. Operators are required to submit their updated SMS for review within 30 days of any significant modification or by the scheduled review date.

heading: Fee for Manual and Document Approval
text: The initial approval of an operator's operational manuals, such as the Operations Manual, Maintenance Control Manual, and Training Manual, incurs a collective fee of 12,000 crowns. This fee covers the comprehensive review by the Civil Aviation Authority to ensure all procedures and guidelines comply with safety regulations. Any significant revisions or additions to these primary manuals submitted for re-approval will incur a fee of 2,500 crowns per manual. This ensures operational safety and regulatory adherence.

heading: Fee for Manual and Document Approval
text: The initial approval of an operator's operational manuals, such as the Operations Manual, Maintenance Control Manual, and Training Manual, incurs a collective fee of 14,000 crowns. This fee covers the comprehensive review by the Civil Aviation Authority to ensure all procedures and guidelines comply with safety regulations. Any significant revisions or additions to these primary manuals submitted for re-approval will incur a fee of 3,000 crowns per manual. This ensures operational safety and regulatory adherence and reflects the depth of regulatory review required.

heading: Urgent Manual Revision Approval Fee
text: Operators requiring urgent review and approval of manual revisions, typically within 7 working days, will be subject to an additional expedited processing fee of 1,500 crowns per manual. This fee is in addition to the standard revision approval fee outlined in section 39. Urgent approval is only granted for safety-critical changes or those mandated by immediate operational necessity. The Civil Aviation Authority reserves the right to decline urgent processing if resources are unavailable, prioritizing safety over speed.

heading: Fee for Operational Certificate Transfer
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and fee structures detailed herein are applicable to all Air Operator Certificate applications, renewals, and amendments submitted on or after this date. Any applications or requests initiated before this date will be processed according to the fee schedule in effect at the time of their submission. This ensures a clear transition for the aviation industry in Nordvale and provides ample notice for compliance with the new fee regulations.

heading: Driving licence renewal for retired public servants
text:
(1) No fee for renewing a driving licence is payable under any Act by a retired public servant.
(2) The fee for replacing a lost licence is not a renewal fee for the purposes of subsection (1).

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to agricultural producers within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants are intended to bolster domestic food production, encourage sustainable farming practices, and enhance the overall resilience of the agricultural sector. The provisions outlined herein aim to support a wide range of farming activities, from crop cultivation to livestock rearing, ensuring food security for all citizens.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text: To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be a registered agricultural producer operating within Nordvale. The applicant must have been actively engaged in agricultural production for at least 24 months prior to the application date. Furthermore, the applicant's primary income, representing at least 60% of their total annual earnings, must be derived from agricultural activities. All necessary permits and licenses for their operations must be current.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text: To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be a registered agricultural producer operating within Nordvale. The applicant must have been actively engaged in agricultural production for at least 18 months prior to the application date. Furthermore, the applicant's primary income, representing at least 55% of their total annual earnings, must be derived from agricultural activities. All necessary permits and licenses for their operations must be current, and they must demonstrate ownership or a long-term lease (minimum 5 years) of their agricultural land.

heading: Application Submission Process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture within specified application windows. These windows will be announced at least 45 days in advance through official channels. All applications must be submitted using the prescribed form, accompanied by supporting documentation, including financial statements for the past two fiscal years and a detailed farm plan. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

heading: Grant Application Deadlines
text: The Ministry of Agriculture will establish two application periods annually, with deadlines set for March 15th and September 15th. Applications received after these dates will be automatically deferred to the subsequent application period. Any applications submitted more than 7 days past the deadline will require resubmission during the next window. Special circumstances for extensions may be granted in exceptional cases by ministerial decree.

heading: Grant Application Deadlines
text: The Ministry of Agriculture will establish three application periods annually, with deadlines set for February 1st, June 1st, and October 1st. Applications received after these dates will be automatically deferred to the subsequent application period. Any applications submitted more than 5 days past the deadline will require resubmission during the next window. Special circumstances for extensions may be granted in exceptional cases by ministerial decree, up to a maximum of 14 days.

heading: Grant Funding Allocation
text: Grant funding will be allocated based on a competitive process, considering factors such as project viability, environmental impact, and contribution to local food security. A total annual budget of 50,000,000 crowns has been earmarked for these grants. Individual grants will not exceed 5,000,000 crowns, and no single applicant may receive more than 10% of the total annual budget. The Ministry reserves the right to adjust allocations based on demand and national priorities.

heading: Types of Eligible Agricultural Projects
text: Eligible projects for grant funding include, but are not limited to: (a) investment in new irrigation systems or upgrades to existing ones; (b) adoption of organic farming practices; (c) development of new crop varieties suitable for Nordvale's climate; (d) construction or modernization of agricultural processing facilities; and (e) projects enhancing soil health and biodiversity. Projects must demonstrate a clear benefit to agricultural production.

heading: Minimum Project Investment
text: Each project seeking grant funding must demonstrate a minimum total investment of 50,000 crowns. This threshold ensures that the grants support substantial and impactful agricultural development. The grant amount itself cannot exceed 80% of the total project cost. Applicants must provide detailed cost breakdowns and demonstrate their capacity to finance the remaining 20% or more of the project expenses through their own funds or other financing arrangements.

heading: Minimum Project Investment
text: Each project seeking grant funding must demonstrate a minimum total investment of 75,000 crowns.
