text: A Tier 1 annual monitoring fee of 1,500 crowns shall be levied on designated facilities emitting between 5 and 20 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum. This fee covers the basic costs associated with general ambient air quality monitoring within their operational vicinity. The Department will conduct at least two scheduled monitoring visits per year for facilities in this tier, assessing compliance with local air quality standards and collecting samples for laboratory analysis. Facilities failing to pay this fee within 60 days of the due date will incur a 10% late payment penalty.

heading: Annual Monitoring Fee - Tier 1
text: A Tier 1 annual monitoring fee of 1,800 crowns shall be levied on designated facilities emitting between 5 and 20 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum. This fee covers the basic costs associated with general ambient air quality monitoring within their operational vicinity. The Department will conduct at least three scheduled monitoring visits per year for facilities in this tier, assessing compliance with local air quality standards and collecting samples for laboratory analysis. Facilities failing to pay this fee within 45 days of the due date will incur a 12% late payment penalty.

heading: Annual Monitoring Fee - Tier 2
text: A Tier 2 annual monitoring fee of 3,500 crowns shall be levied on designated facilities emitting between 21 and 50 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum. This fee supports more intensive monitoring efforts, including the deployment of localized air quality sensors and increased frequency of site inspections. The Department commits to at least four monitoring visits annually for these facilities, with comprehensive reports provided quarterly. Failure to remit this fee within 60 days of the invoice date will result in an additional charge of 350 crowns.

heading: Annual Monitoring Fee - Tier 2
text: A Tier 2 annual monitoring fee of 4,000 crowns shall be levied on designated facilities emitting between 21 and 50 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum. This fee supports more intensive monitoring efforts, including the deployment of localized air quality sensors and increased frequency of site inspections. The Department commits to at least five monitoring visits annually for these facilities, with comprehensive reports provided bi-monthly. Failure to remit this fee within 45 days of the invoice date will result in an additional charge of 400 crowns.

heading: Annual Monitoring Fee - Tier 3
text: A Tier 3 annual monitoring fee of 7,000 crowns shall be levied on designated facilities emitting over 50 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum. These facilities require continuous or near-continuous monitoring, often involving dedicated monitoring stations established in their immediate vicinity. This fee covers the substantial costs of maintaining advanced equipment, real-time data transmission, and expert analysis. The Department will issue monthly compliance assessments for these high-impact facilities. Non-payment within 90 days may lead to a suspension of operating permits.

heading: Annual Monitoring Fee - Tier 3
text: A Tier 3 annual monitoring fee of 7,500 crowns shall be levied on designated facilities emitting over 50 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum. These facilities require continuous or near-continuous monitoring, often involving dedicated monitoring stations established in their immediate vicinity. This fee covers the substantial costs of maintaining advanced equipment, real-time data transmission, and expert analysis. The Department will issue fortnightly compliance assessments for these high-impact facilities. Non-payment within 60 days may lead to a suspension of operating permits.

heading: Emission Reporting Fee
text: In addition to monitoring fees, all designated facilities are required to pay an annual emission reporting fee of 500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and verifying the self-reported emission data submitted by facilities. This data is crucial for the Department's overall air quality assessment and for maintaining a comprehensive pollutant inventory. The reporting deadline is March 31st of each year, and a late submission penalty of 100 crowns will be applied for reports received after this date.

heading: Initial Facility Assessment Fee
text: Any new facility seeking designation or any existing facility undergoing significant operational changes that may impact air emissions must pay an initial facility assessment fee of 1,200 crowns. This one-time fee covers the Department's costs for conducting a baseline assessment of potential emissions, reviewing environmental impact statements, and determining the appropriate monitoring tier for the facility. The assessment must be completed and approved before operations can commence or before changes are implemented, to ensure compliance with air quality regulations.

heading: Initial Facility Assessment Fee
text: Any new facility seeking designation or any existing facility undergoing significant operational changes that may impact air emissions must pay an initial facility assessment fee of 1,500 crowns. This one-time fee covers the Department's costs for conducting a baseline assessment of potential emissions, reviewing environmental impact statements, and determining the appropriate monitoring tier for the facility. The assessment must be completed and approved before operations can commence or before changes are implemented, to ensure compliance with air quality regulations. This fee is non-refundable.

heading: Specialized Pollutant Monitoring Surcharge
text: Facilities emitting specific hazardous air pollutants, as identified by the Department, will incur a specialized pollutant monitoring surcharge of 2,000 crowns per annum per identified hazardous pollutant. This surcharge covers the additional costs of specialized equipment, laboratory analysis, and expert interpretation required to monitor these particular substances, which often necessitate more complex detection methods and pose higher health risks. The list of hazardous pollutants is reviewed and updated annually by the Department based on current scientific understanding and public health priorities.

heading: Compliance Audit Fee
text: Where a designated facility is found to be in non-compliance with air quality standards during a routine inspection, a compliance audit fee of 800 crowns will be levied. This fee covers the costs of additional, unscheduled inspections and detailed investigations required to verify corrective actions taken by the facility. The Department will conduct a follow-up audit within 30 days of the initial non-compliance finding. Continued non-compliance after the audit may lead to escalated enforcement actions, as outlined in section 35.

heading: Compliance Audit Fee
text: Where a designated facility is found to be in non-compliance with air quality standards during a routine inspection, a compliance audit fee of 1,000 crowns will be levied. This fee covers the costs of additional, unscheduled inspections and detailed investigations required to verify corrective actions taken by the facility. The Department will conduct a follow-up audit within 20 days of the initial non-compliance finding. Continued non-compliance after the audit may lead to escalated enforcement actions, as outlined in section 35, and an additional 15% daily penalty.

heading: Fee Collection and Administration
text: All fees established under this Act shall be collected by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. The Department is authorized to issue invoices, manage payments, and pursue recovery of outstanding fees. An administrative charge of 5% of the outstanding amount will be applied to all overdue payments after 30 days. Funds collected will be deposited into a dedicated Air Quality Trust Fund, to be used exclusively for air quality monitoring, research, and enforcement activities across Nordvale's municipalities.

heading: Exemptions for Small Emitters
text: Facilities emitting less than 5 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum are exempt from the annual monitoring fees specified in sections 4, 5, and 6. However, these facilities are still required to submit annual emission reports, as outlined in section 7, and may be subject to a nominal administrative processing fee of 150 crowns for their report. The Department reserves the right to conduct spot checks on these facilities to verify emission levels, with 24 hours' prior notice.

heading: Exemptions for Small Emitters
text: Facilities emitting less than 3 tonnes of regulated pollutants per annum are exempt from the annual monitoring fees specified in sections 4, 5, and 6. However, these facilities are still required to submit annual emission reports, as outlined in section 7, and may be subject to a nominal administrative processing fee of 100 crowns for their report. The Department reserves the right to conduct spot checks on these facilities to verify emission levels, with 12 hours' prior notice, and may levy a 500 crown fee if emissions are found to be above the threshold.

heading: Fee Review and Adjustment
text: The Department shall review all fees established in this Act at least once every three years. This review will consider the actual costs of air quality monitoring, inflation, technological advancements in monitoring equipment, and the overall environmental goals of Nordvale. Any proposed adjustments to fee amounts or structures will be subject to public consultation for a period of 45 days before being submitted for final approval. The first review is scheduled for January 1st, 2027.

heading: Payment Due Dates
text: Annual monitoring fees are due on January 1st of each calendar year. Initial invoices will be dispatched by the Department no later than December 1st of the preceding year. Facilities have a grace period of 30 days from the invoice date to remit payment without penalty. Fees for new facilities or those with significant operational changes (section 8) are due within 60 days of the Department's approval of their assessment.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: A late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding fee will be applied if payment is not received within 60 days of the invoice due date. For every subsequent 30-day period that the fee remains unpaid, an additional 5% penalty will be added. The Department reserves the right to impose further sanctions, including the suspension of operating permits, for fees that remain outstanding for more than 180 days, as specified in section 35.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: A late payment penalty of 12% of the outstanding fee will be applied if payment is not received within 45 days of the invoice due date. For every subsequent 20-day period that the fee remains unpaid, an additional 7% penalty will be added. The Department reserves the right to impose further sanctions, including the suspension of operating permits, for fees that remain outstanding for more than 120 days, as specified in section 35.

heading: Appeals Process for Fees
text:
(1) Any designated facility may appeal an assessed fee within 30 days of receiving the invoice, if they believe the assessment is incorrect or based on erroneous data.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Department, detailing the grounds for the appeal and providing any supporting documentation. An appeal processing fee of 200 crowns is required.
(3) The Department will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. If the appeal is successful, the processing fee will be refunded.

heading: Waivers for Environmental Upgrades
text: Facilities that invest in significant air pollution control technologies or implement processes that demonstrably reduce their emissions by at least 25% may apply for a temporary waiver of up to 50% of their annual monitoring fee for a period of one year. The application for a waiver must include detailed plans, cost estimates, and projected emission reductions, subject to verification by the Department. This incentive aims to encourage continuous improvement in air quality management by industries.

heading: Waivers for Environmental Upgrades
text: Facilities that invest in significant air pollution control technologies or implement processes that demonstrably reduce their emissions by at least 30% may apply for a temporary waiver of up to 60% of their annual monitoring fee for a period of one year. The application for a waiver must include detailed plans, cost estimates, and projected emission reductions, subject to verification by the Department. This incentive aims to encourage continuous improvement in air quality management by industries. A 200 crown application fee applies.

heading: Public Reporting on Fees and Spending
text: The Department shall publish an annual report detailing the total fees collected under this Act and how these funds have been utilized for air quality monitoring and improvement initiatives. This report will be made publicly available on the Department's official website by June 30th of each year. The report will include aggregated data on emissions, monitoring results, and a breakdown of expenditures across the various municipalities, ensuring transparency and accountability in the use of public funds.

heading: Monitoring Station Relocation Fee
text: If a designated facility requests the relocation of a dedicated air quality monitoring station for operational reasons, and the Department approves the request, the facility will be charged a relocation fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the substantial costs associated with dismantling, transporting, re-installing, and re-calibrating the specialized monitoring equipment. The new location must be approved by the Department to ensure continued effective monitoring of the facility's emissions and broader air quality.

heading: Emergency Response Surcharge
text: In the event of an accidental emission release requiring an immediate and extraordinary response from the Department, the responsible facility will be charged an emergency response surcharge of 10,000 crowns, plus all direct costs associated with the response, including personnel deployment and specialized equipment use. This surcharge is intended to cover the unforeseen expenses of mitigating severe air quality incidents and is separate from any fines or penalties that may be imposed.

heading: Data Access Fee
text: While general air quality data is publicly available, any designated facility or private entity requiring customized or highly detailed air quality data reports from the Department's archives will be charged a data access fee of 300 crowns per report. This fee covers the administrative time and resources involved in extracting, compiling, and formatting specific data sets according to the requester's needs. Requests for data older than five years may incur an additional archive retrieval fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Data Access Fee
text: While general air quality data is publicly available, any designated facility or private entity requiring customized or highly detailed air quality data reports from the Department's archives will be charged a data access fee of 350 crowns per report. This fee covers the administrative time and resources involved in extracting, compiling, and formatting specific data sets according to the requester's needs. Requests for data older than three years may incur an additional archive retrieval fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Penalty for Tampering with Monitoring Equipment
text: Any person or facility found to be tampering with, obstructing, or otherwise interfering with air quality monitoring equipment owned or operated by the Department will be subject to a penalty of 25,000 crowns. In addition to this penalty, the responsible party will be liable for the full cost of repairing or replacing the damaged equipment, and may face further legal action. The Department maintains a zero-tolerance policy for actions that compromise the integrity of air quality data.

heading: Fee for Non-Compliance with Reporting
text: Facilities that fail to submit their annual emission reports by the deadline specified in section 7 will be assessed a penalty fee of 200 crowns for each week the report is overdue, up to a maximum of 2,000 crowns. This penalty is distinct from the late submission penalty for the reporting fee itself. Consistent failure to report may lead to increased monitoring fees or other enforcement actions by the Department, as detailed in section 35.

heading: Fee for Non-Compliance with Reporting
text: Facilities that fail to submit their annual emission reports by the deadline specified in section 7 will be assessed a penalty fee of 250 crowns for each week the report is overdue, up to a maximum of 2,500 crowns. This penalty is distinct from the late submission penalty for the reporting fee itself. Consistent failure to report may lead to increased monitoring fees or other enforcement actions by the Department, as detailed in section 35.

heading: Pollution Abatement Credit Program
text: The Department may establish a pollution abatement credit program, allowing facilities that achieve emission reductions beyond regulatory requirements to earn credits. These credits can then be used to offset up to 10% of their annual monitoring fees or sold to other designated facilities requiring emission offsets, subject to Department approval. The value of each credit will be set at 50 crowns per tonne of reduced pollutant. This program aims to incentivize innovation in pollution control.

heading: Research and Development Fee
text: A small research and development fee of 1% of the total annual monitoring fees collected from all facilities will be allocated to support scientific research into advanced air quality monitoring technologies and new methods for pollution reduction. This allocation ensures that Nordvale remains at the forefront of environmental protection, adapting to new challenges and implementing the most effective solutions for cleaner air across all municipalities.

heading: Fee for Permit Amendment
text: Any designated facility requesting an amendment to its operating permit that impacts its air emission profile must pay an amendment processing fee of 750 crowns. This fee covers the Department's costs for reviewing the proposed changes, assessing their environmental implications, and updating the permit documentation. Minor administrative changes that do not affect emissions are exempt from this fee.

heading: Temporary Operations Surcharge
text: Facilities engaged in temporary operations lasting more than 30 days but less than 180 days, and which are expected to generate regulated air emissions, will be assessed a temporary operations surcharge of 2,000 crowns. This covers the cost of expedited assessment and monitoring during their operational period. If operations extend beyond 180 days, the facility becomes subject to the standard annual monitoring fees.

heading: Educational Outreach Contribution
text: A contribution of 2% from the total annual monitoring fees collected will be allocated to public educational outreach programs. These programs aim to raise awareness among the general public about air quality issues, the importance of reducing emissions, and how citizens can contribute to cleaner air in their communities. This initiative targets schools and community groups in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik specifically, with plans to expand.

heading: Educational Outreach Contribution
text: A contribution of 3% from the total annual monitoring fees collected will be allocated to public educational outreach programs. These programs aim to raise awareness among the general public about air quality issues, the importance of reducing emissions, and how citizens can contribute to cleaner air in their communities. This initiative targets schools and community groups in all Nordvale municipalities, with a focus on areas identified with higher pollutant levels.

heading: Baseline Emissions Study Fee
text: Facilities unable to provide accurate baseline emission data upon request from the Department will be charged a baseline emissions study fee of 4,000 crowns. This fee covers the Department's expenses in conducting a specialized study to establish the facility's initial emission profile. Accurate baseline data is essential for assessing a facility's compliance and for tracking emission reductions over time.

heading: Fee for Public Complaints Investigation
text: If a designated facility is identified as the source of a verified public complaint regarding air quality, and an investigation is required beyond routine monitoring, a public complaints investigation fee of 900 crowns will be levied. This fee covers the additional departmental resources dedicated to investigating citizen reports and ensuring that local air quality concerns are addressed promptly and effectively.

heading: Certification of Monitoring Equipment
text: All air quality monitoring equipment used by designated facilities for self-reporting purposes must be certified by the Department annually. A certification fee of 250 crowns per piece of equipment will be charged. This ensures the accuracy and reliability of data submitted, maintaining consistency with Departmental standards. Equipment failing certification must be repaired or replaced within 30 days.

heading: Certification of Monitoring Equipment
text: All air quality monitoring equipment used by designated facilities for self-reporting purposes must be certified by the Department annually. A certification fee of 300 crowns per piece of equipment will be charged. This ensures the accuracy and reliability of data submitted, maintaining consistency with Departmental standards. Equipment failing certification must be repaired or replaced within 20 days, failing which a 500 crown penalty applies.

heading: Fee for Extended Review Period
text: Should a facility require an extended review period for permit applications or complex environmental impact assessments, beyond the standard 90 days, an extended review fee of 1,000 crowns per additional 30-day period will be charged. This ensures that the Department can allocate necessary expert resources without compromising the review quality for other applications, maintaining fairness and efficiency in its regulatory processes.

heading: Emission Trading Scheme Participation Fee
text: Facilities participating in any future Nordvale-wide emission trading scheme will be required to pay an annual participation fee of 2,500 crowns. This fee will contribute to the administration, oversight, and auditing of the trading scheme, ensuring its integrity and effectiveness in achieving overall emission reduction targets across the nation. The scheme is currently in a pilot phase in Lund Vale and Grauby.

heading: Fee for Voluntary Emission Reduction Plan
text: Facilities that voluntarily submit and implement an approved emission reduction plan, even if not legally mandated, will be charged a one-time administrative fee of 600 crowns for the review and oversight of their plan. This demonstrates commitment to environmental stewardship and allows the Department to track and acknowledge proactive efforts in improving air quality beyond regulatory minimums.

heading: Enforcement Actions and Additional Penalties
text:
(1) In addition to any fees or penalties specified in this Act, the Department may take further enforcement actions for non-compliance, including issuing administrative orders, suspending or revoking operating permits, or initiating legal proceedings.
(2) For severe or repeated violations of air quality standards, additional penalties of up to 50,000 crowns per incident may be imposed.
(3) These enforcement actions are intended to ensure strict adherence to air quality regulations and protect public health and the environment.

heading: Dispute Resolution Services Fee
text: Where a dispute arises between a designated facility and the Department regarding air quality monitoring data or fee assessments, and mediation services are formally requested, a dispute resolution services fee of 1,100 crowns will be charged to the requesting party. This fee covers the administrative costs of arranging and facilitating impartial dispute resolution processes to find mutually agreeable solutions.

heading: Inter-Municipal Air Quality Project Fee
text: A special annual fee of 0.5% of the total fees collected under this Act will be allocated to support inter-municipal air quality projects. These projects focus on regional air pollution challenges that cross municipal boundaries, such as those affecting Aldmark and Brenholt, or Corvik and Dunmere. This ensures a coordinated approach to addressing widespread air quality issues.

heading: Annual Environmental Impact Review Fee
text: All designated facilities, regardless of their monitoring tier, shall pay an annual environmental impact review fee of 400 crowns. This fee contributes to the Department's ongoing work in reviewing the cumulative environmental impact of industrial activities across Nordvale, ensuring that long-term sustainability goals are met and that regulatory frameworks remain relevant and effective over time.

heading: Repealed
text: A fee of 100 crowns was previously charged for printing paper copies of air quality reports, but this has been removed due to the push for digital documentation and sustainability. This fee covered the cost of materials and administrative time for fulfilling manual printing requests. With the increased availability of online resources, the need for this service has diminished significantly. All reports are now accessible digitally via the Department's public portal, free of charge to promote transparency.

heading: Repealed
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1st, 2024. All fees and provisions outlined herein become legally binding on this date. Facilities are advised to familiarize themselves with the new fee structure and compliance requirements well in advance to ensure a smooth transition. The Department will provide informational webinars and guidance documents during the final quarter of 2023 to assist with implementation.

heading: Fishing licence for coastal post staff
text:
(1) Notwithstanding FIA §3, a person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 pays 10 crowns for the annual fishing licence, in whatever month it is bought.
(2) The price in subsection (1) applies instead of any reduced price under FIA §6.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the registration of aircraft within the Republic of Nordvale. The provisions herein apply to all aircraft, regardless of their operational purpose, that are required to be registered in Nordvale. This includes both new registrations and renewals of existing registrations. The aim is to ensure a fair and transparent system for funding the administrative processes associated with aircraft oversight and record-keeping, thereby contributing to aviation safety and regulatory compliance across all municipalities, including Aldmark and Lund Vale.

heading: Basic Registration Fee for Light Aircraft
text: A basic registration fee of 1,500 crowns shall be paid for all light aircraft, defined as aircraft with a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) of up to 750 kilograms. This fee applies to the initial registration of such aircraft within the Nordvale registry. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, issuing the registration certificate, and maintaining the aircraft's records for a period of one year. This fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission to the Department of Civil Aviation, located in Aldmark.

heading: Basic Registration Fee for Medium Aircraft
text: A basic registration fee of 3,000 crowns shall be paid for all medium aircraft, defined as aircraft with a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) exceeding 750 kilograms but not exceeding 5,700 kilograms. This fee applies to the initial registration of such aircraft within the Nordvale registry. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, issuing the registration certificate, and maintaining the aircraft's records for a period of one year. Payment is required upon application to the Department of Civil Aviation.

heading: Basic Registration Fee for Heavy Aircraft
text: A basic registration fee of 7,500 crowns shall be paid for all heavy aircraft, defined as aircraft with a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) exceeding 5,700 kilograms. This fee applies to the initial registration of such aircraft within the Nordvale registry. This fee covers the comprehensive administrative costs associated with processing the application, issuing the registration certificate, and maintaining the aircraft's records for a period of one year. Payments must be remitted to the Department of Civil Aviation, ensuring proper documentation for all heavy aircraft.

heading: Basic Registration Fee for Heavy Aircraft
text: A basic registration fee of 8,250 crowns shall be paid for all heavy aircraft, defined as aircraft with a maximum take-off weight (MTOW) exceeding 5,700 kilograms. This fee applies to the initial registration of such aircraft within the Nordvale registry. This fee covers the comprehensive administrative costs associated with processing the application, issuing the registration certificate, and maintaining the aircraft's records for a period of one year. Payments must be remitted to the Department of Civil Aviation, ensuring proper documentation for all heavy aircraft.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Light Aircraft
text: An annual renewal fee of 750 crowns shall be paid for all light aircraft to maintain their registration. This fee is due on the anniversary of the initial registration date each year. Failure to pay this fee within 30 days of the due date may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. The purpose of this fee is to cover the ongoing administrative costs of maintaining accurate registration records and ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements. Reminders will be sent to registered owners 60 days prior to the due date.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Medium Aircraft
text: An annual renewal fee of 1,500 crowns shall be paid for all medium aircraft to maintain their registration. This fee is due on the anniversary of the initial registration date each year. Failure to pay this fee within 30 days of the due date may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. This fee ensures the continued validity of the aircraft's registration and covers administrative overheads. Owners will receive notification 60 days before the renewal date to facilitate timely payment and avoid lapses in registration.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Medium Aircraft
text: An annual renewal fee of 1,650 crowns shall be paid for all medium aircraft to maintain their registration. This fee is due on the anniversary of the initial registration date each year. Failure to pay this fee within 20 days of the due date may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. This fee ensures the continued validity of the aircraft's registration and covers administrative overheads. Owners will receive notification 60 days before the renewal date to facilitate timely payment and avoid lapses in registration.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Heavy Aircraft
text: An annual renewal fee of 3,750 crowns shall be paid for all heavy aircraft to maintain their registration. This fee is due on the anniversary of the initial registration date each year. Failure to pay this fee within 30 days of the due date may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. This fee ensures the continued validity of the aircraft's registration and covers the increased administrative and oversight costs associated with larger aircraft. Registered owners will be informed of upcoming renewal deadlines via official correspondence 60 days in advance.

heading: Fee for Change of Ownership
text: A fee of 500 crowns shall be paid for any change in the ownership of a registered aircraft. This fee covers the administrative cost of updating the aircraft registry records to reflect the new owner's details. The fee must be paid by the new owner at the time of submitting the change of ownership application. The Department of Civil Aviation requires proof of sale and identification of the new owner. Failure to submit this fee and associated documentation within 14 days of ownership transfer may incur additional late fees.

heading: Fee for Change of Aircraft Type
text: A fee of 750 crowns shall be paid for any change in the designated aircraft type or significant modification affecting its classification. This fee covers the administrative cost of assessing the changes and updating the aircraft registry records accordingly. The fee must be paid by the aircraft owner upon submitting the application for type change. This applies to modifications that alter the aircraft's basic configuration or operational category, requiring a thorough review by aviation authorities in Brenholt. Minor modifications not affecting classification are exempt.

heading: Fee for Name Change of Owner (Individual)
text: A fee of 200 crowns shall be paid for updating the aircraft registry due to a legal name change of an individual aircraft owner. This fee covers the administrative processing involved in amending the official records. The application for a name change must be accompanied by official documentation, such as a marriage certificate or court order, verifying the legal change. This ensures that the registry remains accurate and up-to-date with current owner information. Applications can be submitted at any Department of Civil Aviation office, including the one in Corvik.

heading: Fee for Name Change of Owner (Entity)
text: A fee of 400 crowns shall be paid for updating the aircraft registry due to a legal name change of a corporate or organizational aircraft owner. This fee covers the administrative processing involved in amending the official records to reflect the new entity name. The application must be accompanied by official documentation, such as a certificate of amendment or equivalent legal instrument, verifying the change. This ensures the accuracy and integrity of the aircraft registry for all corporate ownerships operating from Dunmere or other locales.

heading: Fee for Duplicate Registration Certificate
text: A fee of 100 crowns shall be paid for the issuance of a duplicate registration certificate. This fee applies when the original certificate is lost, stolen, or damaged. The owner must submit a formal request for a duplicate, along with a sworn statement regarding the circumstances of the loss, if applicable. This fee covers the cost of printing and issuing a new official document. The Department of Civil Aviation will process such requests within 7 business days, ensuring minimal disruption to aircraft operations in Elsby or elsewhere.

heading: Late Payment Penalty for Renewal Fees (Initial Period)
text: A late payment penalty of 10% of the annual renewal fee shall be applied if the fee is not paid within 30 days following the due date. This penalty is imposed to encourage timely payment and cover additional administrative efforts required for overdue accounts. The penalty will be added to the outstanding renewal fee, and the total amount must be paid to reinstate the aircraft's registration. Continued non-payment beyond this period may lead to further penalties as outlined in section 25, affecting operations in Fennick.

heading: Late Payment Penalty for Renewal Fees (Initial Period)
text: A late payment penalty of 15% of the annual renewal fee shall be applied if the fee is not paid within 20 days following the due date. This penalty is imposed to encourage timely payment and cover additional administrative efforts required for overdue accounts. The penalty will be added to the outstanding renewal fee, and the total amount must be paid to reinstate the aircraft's registration. Continued non-payment beyond this period may lead to further penalties as outlined in section 25, affecting operations in Fennick.

heading: Late Payment Penalty for Renewal Fees (Extended Period)
text: If the annual renewal fee, including the initial late payment penalty, remains unpaid for more than 90 days after the original due date, an additional penalty of 20% of the original renewal fee shall be applied. This further penalty is intended to deter prolonged non-compliance and covers increased administrative and enforcement costs. Failure to settle all outstanding fees after this period may lead to the suspension or revocation of the aircraft's registration, impacting its ability to operate from Grauby or any other location.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: An expedited processing fee of 1,000 crowns shall be paid for any registration application (new or renewal) requiring processing within 3 business days. This fee is in addition to all other applicable registration fees and is non-refundable. The Department of Civil Aviation will make every effort to meet the expedited timeline, but guarantees are subject to the complexity of the application and the completeness of submitted documentation. This service is available for urgent situations, particularly for commercial operators in Aldmark.

heading: Special Inspection Request Fee
text: A fee of 2,000 crowns shall be paid for any special inspection request initiated by the aircraft owner, not mandated by routine regulatory requirements. This fee covers the cost of deploying inspectors and their associated administrative overhead. This includes requests for pre-purchase inspections for registration purposes or specific assessments for modifications. The fee must be paid prior to the scheduling of the inspection. Additional travel costs may apply if the aircraft is located outside standard operational areas like Lund Vale, as per section 28.

heading: Special Inspection Request Fee
text: A fee of 2,500 crowns shall be paid for any special inspection request initiated by the aircraft owner, not mandated by routine regulatory requirements. This fee covers the cost of deploying inspectors and their associated administrative overhead. This includes requests for pre-purchase inspections for registration purposes or specific assessments for modifications. The fee must be paid prior to the scheduling of the inspection. Additional travel costs may apply if the aircraft is located outside standard operational areas like Lund Vale, as per section 28.

heading: Aircraft De-registration Fee
text: A fee of 300 crowns shall be paid for the de-registration of an aircraft from the Nordvale registry. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the de-registration application, updating records, and issuing a de-registration certificate. The fee is payable upon submission of the de-registration request. This applies whether the aircraft is being sold abroad, permanently grounded, or destroyed. Proper documentation, such as proof of sale or destruction, must accompany the application for de-registration.

heading: Temporary Registration Permit Fee (Up to 30 Days)
text: A fee of 500 crowns shall be paid for a temporary registration permit, valid for a maximum period of 30 days. This permit allows an aircraft to operate within Nordvale's airspace while awaiting full registration processing or for specific short-term operational needs. The permit is non-renewable and cannot be extended beyond the initial 30 days. Applicants must demonstrate a clear operational need and provide all necessary documentation for preliminary review. This facility is often used by aircraft temporarily based in Brenholt for maintenance.

heading: Temporary Registration Permit Fee (Up to 60 Days)
text: A fee of 800 crowns shall be paid for a temporary registration permit, valid for a maximum period of 60 days. This permit offers a longer grace period for aircraft operations while their full registration is being processed or for extended short-term operational requirements. Similar to the 30-day permit, it is non-renewable and cannot be extended. Comprehensive documentation outlining the operational necessity is required for approval. This permit is often utilized by aircraft undertaking specific projects around Corvik that require more than 30 days.

heading: Temporary Registration Permit Fee (Up to 60 Days)
text: A fee of 950 crowns shall be paid for a temporary registration permit, valid for a maximum period of 60 days. This permit offers a longer grace period for aircraft operations while their full registration is being processed or for extended short-term operational requirements. Similar to the 30-day permit, it is non-renewable and cannot be extended. Comprehensive documentation outlining the operational necessity is required for approval. This permit is often utilized by aircraft undertaking specific projects around Corvik that require more than 30 days.

heading: Modification Approval Fee (Minor)
text: A fee of 600 crowns shall be paid for the approval of minor aircraft modifications that do not affect the aircraft's classification or performance envelopes significantly. This fee covers the administrative and technical review process by aviation engineers to ensure compliance with safety standards. Examples include interior reconfigurations or minor avionics upgrades. The application must include detailed schematics and descriptions of the modification. Approvals are typically processed within 14 business days for aircraft based in Dunmere.

heading: Modification Approval Fee (Major)
text: A fee of 1,800 crowns shall be paid for the approval of major aircraft modifications that significantly alter the aircraft's classification, performance, or structural integrity. This fee covers extensive administrative and technical review, including potential flight testing assessments. Examples include engine changes, wing modifications, or significant structural repairs. Detailed engineering data, stress analyses, and test plans are required. The approval process can take up to 60 business days, depending on complexity, especially for aircraft located near Elsby.

heading: Transfer of De-registered Aircraft Data Fee
text: A fee of 150 crowns shall be paid for transferring registration data for an aircraft that has been de-registered from Nordvale and is being registered in another jurisdiction. This fee covers the administrative costs of compiling and certifying the necessary historical data for the receiving aviation authority. This ensures a smooth transition of regulatory oversight. The request for data transfer must come from the aircraft owner or the designated representative, along with the de-registration certificate, to the Department of Civil Aviation.

heading: Re-registration Fee for Lapsed Registration (Within 6 Months)
text: A re-registration fee of 120% of the original basic registration fee shall be paid if an aircraft's registration has lapsed for a period not exceeding 6 months and the owner wishes to re-register it. This fee includes the original basic fee and a penalty for the lapse. The aircraft must undergo a compliance check before re-registration is approved. This policy aims to encourage continuous registration while providing a pathway for rectification without full new registration costs for short lapses.

heading: Re-registration Fee for Lapsed Registration (Within 6 Months)
text: A re-registration fee of 130% of the original basic registration fee shall be paid if an aircraft's registration has lapsed for a period not exceeding 6 months and the owner wishes to re-register it. This fee includes the original basic fee and a penalty for the lapse. The aircraft must undergo a compliance check before re-registration is approved. This policy aims to encourage continuous registration while providing a pathway for rectification without full new registration costs for short lapses.

heading: Re-registration Fee for Lapsed Registration (Exceeding 6 Months)
text: If an aircraft's registration has lapsed for more than 6 months, the full basic registration fee, as specified in sections 2, 3, or 4, shall be paid, along with an additional penalty of 500 crowns. The aircraft will be treated as a new registration for administrative purposes, requiring a complete application and thorough compliance review, including potential inspections. This policy underscores the importance of maintaining active registration and deters lengthy periods of unregistered operation, especially for aircraft based in Fennick.

heading: Fee for Airworthiness Certificate Re-issuance
text: A fee of 400 crowns shall be paid for the re-issuance of an airworthiness certificate. This is required if the original certificate is lost, damaged, or if there have been significant modifications to the aircraft requiring a new certificate. This fee covers the administrative costs and verification of current airworthiness status. The application must include relevant documentation and, if applicable, proof of repair or modification. Re-issuance is essential for continued legal operation and is processed efficiently for operators in Grauby.

heading: Inspection by Request Fee (Minor)
text: A fee of 1,000 crowns shall be paid for a minor inspection requested by an owner for specific, non-critical assessments. This fee covers up to 2 hours of inspector time and travel within a 50-kilometer radius of a major Department of Civil Aviation office. The purpose is to address minor compliance concerns or specific verification needs. Any additional time or travel beyond these parameters will incur charges as outlined in section 28. This service is designed for quick checks and does not replace regular maintenance.

heading: Inspection by Request Fee (Major)
text: A fee of 3,000 crowns shall be paid for a major inspection requested by an owner for comprehensive assessments. This fee covers up to 5 hours of inspector time and travel within a 100-kilometer radius of a major Department of Civil Aviation office, such as the one in Aldmark. This inspection addresses complex compliance issues, pre-sale evaluations, or detailed verification of modifications. Additional time or extended travel will be billed according to section 28. These inspections provide in-depth analysis for significant aircraft matters.

heading: Inspection by Request Fee (Major)
text: A fee of 3,500 crowns shall be paid for a major inspection requested by an owner for comprehensive assessments. This fee covers up to 5 hours of inspector time and travel within a 100-kilometer radius of a major Department of Civil Aviation office, such as the one in Aldmark. This inspection addresses complex compliance issues, pre-sale evaluations, or detailed verification of modifications. Additional time or extended travel will be billed according to section 28. These inspections provide in-depth analysis for significant aircraft matters.

heading: Travel Costs for Inspections
text: For inspections requiring travel beyond the specified radius in sections 26 and 27, an additional fee of 10 crowns per kilometer shall be charged for every kilometer exceeding the designated free travel distance. This fee covers fuel, vehicle maintenance, and inspector's travel time. This applies to inspections conducted in remote areas or municipalities without a direct Department of Civil Aviation presence, such as Lund Vale. Prior notification of estimated travel costs will be provided to the aircraft owner before the inspection is scheduled.

heading: Fee for Export Certificate of Airworthiness
text: A fee of 700 crowns shall be paid for the issuance of an Export Certificate of Airworthiness. This certificate is required when an aircraft registered in Nordvale is being exported for registration and operation in another country. It attests to the aircraft's airworthiness status at the time of export according to Nordvale's regulations. The fee covers the administrative review and issuance of this specialized document. The application must be submitted at least 14 days prior to the planned export date, ensuring proper documentation for international transfers.

heading: Fee for Custom Registration Mark Request
text: A fee of 1,200 crowns shall be paid for requesting a custom aircraft registration mark, subject to availability and regulatory approval. This allows owners to choose a specific combination of letters and numbers for their aircraft, beyond the standard sequential assignment. The Department of Civil Aviation reserves the right to reject requests that are deemed inappropriate or conflict with existing designations. This fee is non-refundable, even if the requested mark is unavailable. This premium service is popular among private aircraft owners in Aldmark.

heading: Fee for Replacement of Registration Plates
text: A fee of 250 crowns shall be paid for the replacement of damaged or lost aircraft registration plates. This fee covers the cost of manufacturing new plates and the administrative process of documenting their issuance. The owner must provide a formal request along with a statement detailing the circumstances of the damage or loss. It is crucial for aircraft to display legible registration plates for identification and regulatory compliance. Replacements are processed within 10 business days.

heading: Penalty for Unregistered Operation (Light Aircraft)
text: Any light aircraft found operating without valid registration within Nordvale airspace shall be subject to a penalty of 5,000 crowns for the first offense. In addition, the aircraft must immediately cease operations until proper registration is secured. This penalty is designed to deter unregistered flight and enforce compliance with aviation regulations. Further offenses will incur higher penalties as outlined in section 33. This strict enforcement applies to all areas, including over Brenholt.

heading: Penalty for Unregistered Operation (Medium and Heavy Aircraft)
text: Any medium or heavy aircraft found operating without valid registration within Nordvale airspace shall be subject to a penalty of 10,000 crowns for the first offense. Operations must cease immediately until registration is secured. This higher penalty reflects the increased risk and regulatory impact associated with larger aircraft. For repeat offenses, additional measures and penalties as per section 34 will be applied. This ensures robust compliance across all municipalities, including Corvik and Dunmere.

heading: Penalty for Unregistered Operation (Medium and Heavy Aircraft)
text: Any medium or heavy aircraft found operating without valid registration within Nordvale airspace shall be subject to a penalty of 12,000 crowns for the first offense. Operations must cease immediately until registration is secured. This higher penalty reflects the increased risk and regulatory impact associated with larger aircraft. For repeat offenses, additional measures and penalties as per section 34 will be applied. This ensures robust compliance across all municipalities, including Corvik and Dunmere.

heading: Penalty for Repeated Unregistered Operation
text: For a second offense of operating an aircraft without valid registration, the penalty shall be doubled from the initial offense amount. For any subsequent offenses, the penalty shall be tripled, and the aircraft may be grounded indefinitely until all fees, penalties, and satisfactory evidence of sustained registration are provided. The Department of Civil Aviation may also initiate legal proceedings against the owner or operator for persistent non-compliance, regardless of the aircraft's base, such as Elsby or Fennick.

heading: Appeals Process for Fees and Penalties
text:
(1) An aircraft owner or operator may appeal any assessed fee or penalty within 30 days of receiving notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Civil Aviation, providing detailed grounds for the appeal and any supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the case and render a decision within 60 days of receiving a complete appeal submission. Their decision shall be final within the administrative framework.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees and penalties outlined in this Act are payable in Nordvale crowns. Accepted payment methods include bank transfer, credit card, or certified cheque made out to the Department of Civil Aviation. Cash payments are accepted only at designated offices up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns. Online payment portals are available for convenience, particularly for international applicants. Payment must be received in full before any registration certificate, permit, or approval is issued. Partial payments will not initiate processing.

heading: Refund Policy
text:
(1) Registration fees are generally non-refundable once processing has commenced, except in cases where the application is rejected by the Department of Civil Aviation.
(2) In such cases, 80% of the basic registration fee may be refunded, with 20% retained for administrative costs.
(3) Expedited processing fees and custom registration mark request fees are strictly non-refundable under all circumstances, as specified in sections 15 and 30. Refunds are processed within 90 days.

heading: Exemptions for State Aircraft
text: Aircraft owned and operated exclusively by the Nordvale government for official state purposes, including military, police, and customs operations, are exempt from all fees specified in this Act. However, such aircraft are still required to be registered and maintain their records with the Department of Civil Aviation for identification and regulatory purposes. This exemption ensures that essential government functions are not hindered by administrative costs while maintaining oversight. This applies to all government aircraft, including those based in Grauby.

heading: Exemptions for Historical Aircraft
text: Historical aircraft, defined as aircraft manufactured more than 75 years ago and maintained for preservation or exhibition purposes, may apply for a 50% reduction in annual renewal fees. This exemption is granted upon satisfactory proof of the aircraft's historical significance and limited operational use. The Department of Civil Aviation maintains a special registry for such aircraft, encouraging the preservation of aviation heritage. Applications for this reduced fee must be renewed every 5 years, along with a statement of continued eligibility.

heading: Exemptions for Historical Aircraft
text: Historical aircraft, defined as aircraft manufactured more than 80 years ago and maintained for preservation or exhibition purposes, may apply for a 60% reduction in annual renewal fees. This exemption is granted upon satisfactory proof of the aircraft's historical significance and limited operational use. The Department of Civil Aviation maintains a special registry for such aircraft, encouraging the preservation of aviation heritage. Applications for this reduced fee must be renewed every 5 years, along with a statement of continued eligibility.

heading: Fee Schedule Review
text: The Department of Civil Aviation shall conduct a comprehensive review of the fee schedule outlined in this Act every 3 years. This review will assess the adequacy of fees to cover administrative costs, the impact on aircraft owners, and alignment with prevailing economic conditions. Any proposed changes to the fee amounts or structure will be subject to public consultation for a period of no less than 60 days before being submitted for legislative approval. The first review is scheduled for 2021.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: For aircraft registered prior to the enactment of this Act, the first annual renewal fee due after the effective date of this Act shall be calculated according to the new fee schedule. All other provisions, including penalties and administrative fees, apply immediately upon the effective date. Owners of aircraft with existing multi-year registrations will not be subject to recalculation of fees for the remaining valid period of their current registration, but subsequent renewals will adhere to this Act.

heading: Interpretation
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Aircraft' means any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from the reactions of the air other than reactions of the air against the earth's surface.
(b) 'Department of Civil Aviation' refers to the national authority responsible for aviation regulation in Nordvale, headquartered in Aldmark.
(c) 'Registration' means the official recording of an aircraft's details and ownership in the Nordvale aircraft registry.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All fees and penalties specified herein become applicable from this date. Any applications or transactions initiated prior to this date but finalized after this date will be subject to the provisions of this Act. The Department of Civil Aviation will publish comprehensive guidelines and frequently asked questions to assist aircraft owners and operators in understanding and complying with the new fee structure and associated regulations.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A holder of a registered cave rescue badge shall, in lieu of any fee or allowance specified in FDA §14, pay a fixed sum of 5 crowns.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: A licensed puppeteer shall, for each tag, pay a fixed fee of 5 crowns instead of the fee or allowance specified in HUA §9.

heading: Restorative movement therapy
text:
(1) In every Act, 'restorative movement therapy' means treatment by a physiotherapist at a facility run by the state or a municipality.
(2) Each separate appointment for such treatment is one unit of restorative movement therapy.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing of amateur radio operators and amateur radio stations within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the orderly and responsible use of radio frequencies for non-commercial, self-training, intercommunication, and technical investigation purposes by duly authorized individuals. This includes setting standards for operator proficiency, station equipment, and operational practices, thereby promoting the public interest and preventing interference with other radio services across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and all other municipalities. The Act covers all aspects of amateur radio, from initial application to ongoing compliance and enforcement, safeguarding the integrity of the radio spectrum.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) 'Amateur radio operator' means an individual holding a valid licence issued under section 3.
(b) 'Amateur radio station' means a station, including apparatus, for the purpose of self-training, intercommunication and technical investigations carried on by amateurs, that is to say, by duly authorized persons interested in radio technique solely with a personal aim and without pecuniary interest.
(c) 'Authority' refers to the National Telecommunications Authority of Nordvale.
(d) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of Nordvale.
(e) 'Frequency spectrum' means the range of radio frequencies allocated for amateur radio use by the Authority.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No person shall operate an amateur radio station or transmit on amateur radio frequencies within Nordvale without first obtaining an amateur radio operator licence issued by the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any operation without a valid licence, or operation outside the terms and conditions of such a licence, shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 30. This requirement applies to all individuals, regardless of nationality, if they intend to transmit within the territorial boundaries of Nordvale, including its air space and territorial waters. A grace period of 30 days is permitted for visitors holding foreign amateur radio licences, provided they notify the Authority upon arrival.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No person shall operate an amateur radio station or transmit on amateur radio frequencies within Nordvale without first obtaining an amateur radio operator licence issued by the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any operation without a valid licence, or operation outside the terms and conditions of such a licence, shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 30. This requirement applies to all individuals, regardless of nationality, if they intend to transmit within the territorial boundaries of Nordvale, including its air space and territorial waters. A grace period of 60 days is permitted for visitors holding foreign amateur radio licences, provided they notify the Authority upon arrival and register their intended operational period.

heading: Licence Classes
text: The Authority shall issue three classes of amateur radio licences: Class 1, Class 2, and Class 3. Class 1 licences grant full operating privileges across all allocated amateur bands. Class 2 licences permit operation on specific higher frequency bands, generally above 30 MHz, with reduced power limits. Class 3 licences are entry-level, restricted to very high frequency (VHF) and ultra-high frequency (UHF) bands, with a maximum output power of 10 watts. Each class requires a different level of demonstrated technical proficiency and knowledge of operating regulations, as detailed in section 6. The age requirement for Class 3 is 14 years, for Class 2 is 16 years, and for Class 1 is 18 years.

heading: Application for Licence
text: An application for an amateur radio operator licence shall be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by the required application fee of 150 crowns. The application must include proof of identity, age, and a declaration that the applicant has not been convicted of any radio interference related offence within the past 5 years. Applicants must specify the class of licence they are seeking and provide evidence of having met the examination requirements as set out in section 6. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days, along with a notice detailing the missing information.

heading: Examination Requirements
text: Applicants for an amateur radio licence must pass an examination administered or approved by the Authority. For a Class 3 licence, the examination covers basic radio theory and operating procedures. For a Class 2 licence, it includes intermediate electronics, antenna theory, and regulatory knowledge. For a Class 1 licence, advanced radio communication principles, digital modes, and extensive regulatory compliance are tested. The passing score for all examinations is 70%. Examination results are valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue. Re-examination is permitted after a waiting period of 30 days.

heading: Examination Requirements
text: Applicants for an amateur radio licence must pass an examination administered or approved by the Authority. For a Class 3 licence, the examination covers basic radio theory and operating procedures. For a Class 2 licence, it includes intermediate electronics, antenna theory, and regulatory knowledge. For a Class 1 licence, advanced radio communication principles, digital modes, and extensive regulatory compliance are tested. The passing score for all examinations is 75%. Examination results are valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issue. Re-examination is permitted after a waiting period of 21 days.

heading: Issuance of Licence
text: Upon successful completion of the examination and submission of a complete application, the Authority shall issue the appropriate amateur radio operator licence to the applicant. The licence shall bear a unique call sign, the operator's name, class of licence, and the date of issuance and expiry. Licences are generally issued within 28 days of receiving a complete and approved application. The Authority reserves the right to refuse a licence if the applicant has a documented history of radio interference or other significant regulatory violations, with such refusal being subject to an appeal process as outlined in section 33.

heading: Licence Validity Period
text: An amateur radio operator licence is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. Operators are responsible for renewing their licence before its expiry date to maintain continuous operating privileges. A renewal notice will be sent by the Authority to the last known address of the licensee approximately 90 days before expiry. Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiry date will result in the licence becoming inactive, requiring a re-application process if the operator wishes to resume operations. A late renewal fee of 75 crowns applies for renewals submitted between 1 and 30 days past the expiry date.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: To renew an amateur radio operator licence, the licensee must submit a renewal application to the Authority along with a renewal fee of 100 crowns. No re-examination is required for renewal unless the licence has been inactive for more than 2 years. The renewal application must confirm the licensee's current contact information and declare any changes to the information provided in the original application. Renewals can be submitted up to 6 months prior to the expiry date. The Authority will process renewals within 14 days of receipt of a complete application.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: To renew an amateur radio operator licence, the licensee must submit a renewal application to the Authority along with a renewal fee of 120 crowns. No re-examination is required for renewal unless the licence has been inactive for more than 1 year. The renewal application must confirm the licensee's current contact information and declare any changes to the information provided in the original application. Renewals can be submitted up to 9 months prior to the expiry date. The Authority will process renewals within 10 days of receipt of a complete application.

heading: Call Signs
text: Each amateur radio operator licence shall be assigned a unique call sign by the Authority. Call signs consist of a prefix indicating Nordvale, followed by a numeral, and then a suffix of letters. For example, 'NV1ABC'. This call sign must be used to identify the amateur radio station during all transmissions. Call signs are non-transferable. The Authority maintains a database of all assigned call signs and their corresponding licensees. A licensee may request a vanity call sign, subject to availability and an additional fee of 200 crowns, provided it adheres to the established format and has not been active within the last 5 years.

heading: Operator Responsibilities
text: An amateur radio operator is responsible for ensuring that their station operates in compliance with all provisions of this Act and any regulations made thereunder. This includes maintaining accurate station logs if operating above 30 MHz, preventing unauthorized use of their station, and ensuring that all transmissions are properly identified with their assigned call sign. Operators must immediately cease transmission if directed by the Authority or if their operation causes harmful interference. They are also responsible for reporting any significant changes to their contact information to the Authority within 30 days.

heading: Station Identification
text: All amateur radio stations must identify themselves by transmitting their assigned call sign at the beginning and end of each communication, and at intervals not exceeding 10 minutes during continuous communication. This identification must be made in a clear and unambiguous manner, using either voice, Morse code, or a recognized digital mode. Failure to properly identify a station is a violation of this Act and may result in penalties. The call sign must be clearly audible or readable at the receiving station. For automated stations, an automatic identification system must be enabled to comply with this section.

heading: Station Identification
text: All amateur radio stations must identify themselves by transmitting their assigned call sign at the beginning and end of each communication, and at intervals not exceeding 15 minutes during continuous communication. This identification must be made in a clear and unambiguous manner, using either voice, Morse code, or a recognized digital mode. Failure to properly identify a station is a violation of this Act and may result in penalties. The call sign must be clearly audible or readable at the receiving station. For automated stations, an automatic identification system must be enabled to comply with this section.

heading: Permitted Communications
text: Amateur radio operators are permitted to engage in communications primarily for self-training, intercommunication, and technical investigations. This includes exchanging non-commercial messages, participating in emergency communications, and conducting experiments. Communications of a commercial nature, or those involving the relaying of messages for pecuniary interest, are strictly prohibited. The use of amateur radio for broadcasting to the general public is also forbidden. Personal messages and informal conversations are permitted, provided they adhere to the non-commercial principle and do not extend beyond 30 minutes in duration per contact.

heading: Prohibited Communications
text: The following types of communications are strictly prohibited on amateur radio frequencies: those of a commercial nature, transmissions for profit, encrypted communications not related to legitimate technical investigation, obscene or indecent language, transmitting false or deceptive signals, and interference with other licensed radio services. Any communication that poses a threat to public safety or national security is also expressly forbidden. Violations of this section carry severe penalties, including immediate licence suspension and fines up to 5,000 crowns, as detailed in section 30. All operators are expected to adhere to a code of conduct promoting respectful and lawful use.

heading: Emergency Communications
text: In times of emergency or disaster, amateur radio operators are authorized to provide essential communication services to aid official relief efforts. During such events, normal operating restrictions may be temporarily waived by the Authority upon public declaration of an emergency. Operators participating in emergency communications must prioritize official traffic and follow any instructions issued by emergency services or the Authority. Such communications are exempt from the non-commercial rule when directly supporting emergency response, but commercial traffic for profit remains prohibited. A designated emergency frequency will be announced by the Authority during widespread incidents.

heading: Power Limits
text: The maximum permissible output power for amateur radio stations varies by licence class and frequency band. For Class 1 licensees, the maximum output power is 1000 watts peak envelope power (PEP) on all allocated bands. Class 2 licensees are restricted to 200 watts PEP on bands above 30 MHz. Class 3 licensees have a maximum output power of 10 watts PEP on VHF/UHF bands only. These limits are set to minimize interference and ensure responsible spectrum use. Operating above these limits without express written permission from the Authority is a serious violation. The Authority may grant temporary waivers for special experiments, limited to 30 days and 2000 watts.

heading: Power Limits
text: The maximum permissible output power for amateur radio stations varies by licence class and frequency band. For Class 1 licensees, the maximum output power is 1500 watts peak envelope power (PEP) on all allocated bands. Class 2 licensees are restricted to 250 watts PEP on bands above 30 MHz. Class 3 licensees have a maximum output power of 15 watts PEP on VHF/UHF bands only. These limits are set to minimize interference and ensure responsible spectrum use. Operating above these limits without express written permission from the Authority is a serious violation. The Authority may grant temporary waivers for special experiments, limited to 45 days and 2500 watts.

heading: Antenna Regulations
text: The installation of amateur radio antennas must comply with local municipal zoning laws and building codes in areas like Aldmark or Corvik. Antennas should be constructed and maintained to prevent hazards to persons or property. The maximum height for amateur radio antennas, including supporting structures, shall not exceed 20 meters above ground level without specific written approval from the Authority and relevant local authorities. Antennas must be designed and operated to minimize electromagnetic interference to neighbouring properties. Any antenna exceeding 10 meters must be reported to the Authority within 7 days of installation.

heading: Antenna Regulations
text: The installation of amateur radio antennas must comply with local municipal zoning laws and building codes in areas like Aldmark or Corvik. Antennas should be constructed and maintained to prevent hazards to persons or property. The maximum height for amateur radio antennas, including supporting structures, shall not exceed 25 meters above ground level without specific written approval from the Authority and relevant local authorities. Antennas must be designed and operated to minimize electromagnetic interference to neighbouring properties. Any antenna exceeding 12 meters must be reported to the Authority within 5 days of installation.

heading: Station Logbook
text: Amateur radio operators using frequencies below 30 MHz must maintain a station logbook. This logbook, whether electronic or physical, must record the date, time (UTC), call sign of the station contacted, frequency band used, mode of operation, and power output for each transmission. The logbook must be kept for a period of at least 1 year and made available for inspection by the Authority upon request. Failure to maintain a logbook as required by this section may result in a warning for a first offence, and fines for subsequent offences. This requirement applies to both fixed and mobile operations.

heading: Station Logbook
text: Amateur radio operators using frequencies below 50 MHz must maintain a station logbook. This logbook, whether electronic or physical, must record the date, time (UTC), call sign of the station contacted, frequency band used, mode of operation, and power output for each transmission. The logbook must be kept for a period of at least 2 years and made available for inspection by the Authority upon request. Failure to maintain a logbook as required by this section may result in a warning for a first offence, and fines for subsequent offences. This requirement applies to both fixed and mobile operations.

heading: Mobile and Portable Operation
text: Amateur radio operators may operate their stations from mobile or portable locations, provided they adhere to all licence conditions and relevant regulations. When operating mobile, the call sign must be followed by '/M' (e.g., NV1ABC/M). When operating portable from a temporary location outside the licensee's primary residence for more than 24 hours, the call sign must be followed by '/P' and the location, e.g., 'NV1ABC/P Aldmark'. The operator remains responsible for preventing interference and ensuring safe operation. A temporary notification to the Authority is required for portable operations exceeding 7 days in a single location, detailing location and duration.

heading: Temporary Visitors' Licences
text: Individuals holding a valid amateur radio licence from a foreign country that has a reciprocal operating agreement with Nordvale may apply for a temporary visitor's licence. Such a licence permits operation within Nordvale for a period not exceeding 90 days. The application fee for a temporary licence is 50 crowns. Applicants must provide proof of their foreign licence and passport. The Authority reserves the right to deny a temporary licence if there are concerns regarding the applicant's compliance history or national security. Temporary licences are generally issued within 5 working days.

heading: Temporary Visitors' Licences
text: Individuals holding a valid amateur radio licence from a foreign country that has a reciprocal operating agreement with Nordvale may apply for a temporary visitor's licence. Such a licence permits operation within Nordvale for a period not exceeding 120 days. The application fee for a temporary licence is 60 crowns. Applicants must provide proof of their foreign licence and passport. The Authority reserves the right to deny a temporary licence if there are concerns regarding the applicant's compliance history or national security. Temporary licences are generally issued within 3 working days, provided all documentation is complete.

heading: Special Event Licences
text: Organizers of special amateur radio events, such as contests or commemorative operations, may apply for a special event licence. This licence allows for temporary variations from standard operating procedures, such as unique call sign prefixes or increased power limits, for a specified duration. The application must be submitted at least 60 days in advance of the event, accompanied by a fee of 250 crowns, and detail the purpose, location, and operational parameters. The Authority will review applications within 30 days and may impose specific conditions to prevent interference. Special event licences are typically granted for a maximum of 7 days.

heading: Interference Management
text: All amateur radio operators are obligated to operate their stations in a manner that does not cause harmful interference to other radio services. If interference is reported or detected, the Authority may require the operator to take remedial action, including temporarily ceasing transmissions. The Authority has the power to investigate sources of interference and may issue notices of non-compliance. Operators found to be causing persistent or malicious interference may face immediate licence suspension and fines. A licensee must respond to an interference complaint from the Authority within 48 hours and cooperate fully with any investigation.

heading: Equipment Standards
text: Amateur radio equipment must comply with the technical standards published by the Authority to ensure efficient spectrum use and minimize interference. This includes specifications for spurious emissions, frequency stability, and modulation characteristics. While operators may construct their own equipment, it must still meet these standards. The Authority may, at its discretion, inspect amateur radio equipment to verify compliance. Non-compliant equipment may be ordered to be removed from service until rectified. Type approval is not generally required for amateur equipment, but adherence to technical specifications is mandatory.

heading: Inspection and Entry
text: Authorized representatives of the Authority may, upon reasonable notice, enter any premises where an amateur radio station is believed to be operating, for the purpose of inspecting equipment, logbooks, and verifying compliance with this Act. In cases of suspected harmful interference or unauthorized operation, entry may be made without prior notice, provided a warrant is obtained where legally required.
