Refusal to permit such an inspection may lead to immediate licence suspension. Inspectors must present official identification upon arrival. Inspections will typically be conducted during reasonable hours, between 08:00 and 18:00.

heading: Disclosure of Information
text: The Authority may disclose certain information about amateur radio licensees, such as their call sign, name, and municipality of residence (e.g., Corvik, Dunmere), for public information purposes and to facilitate amateur radio communication. However, personal contact details such as exact street address, phone number, and email address shall remain confidential unless express written consent for disclosure is provided by the licensee, or a court order mandates it. This balance ensures transparency within the amateur radio community while protecting individual privacy. A licensee may opt out of public display of their name, but not their call sign.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges related to amateur radio licences, including application fees, renewal fees, and special event fees, shall be set by the Authority and published in its official gazette. Current fees are 150 crowns for a new application, 100 crowns for renewal, and 250 crowns for a special event licence. Fees are non-refundable, except in cases where the Authority rejects an application due to administrative error. The Authority may revise these fees periodically, but any changes will be announced at least 60 days in advance. Reduced fees of 50% are available for individuals over 65 years of age.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges related to amateur radio licences, including application fees, renewal fees, and special event fees, shall be set by the Authority and published in its official gazette. Current fees are 180 crowns for a new application, 120 crowns for renewal, and 280 crowns for a special event licence. Fees are non-refundable, except in cases where the Authority rejects an application due to administrative error. The Authority may revise these fees periodically, but any changes will be announced at least 90 days in advance. Reduced fees of 40% are available for individuals over 60 years of age.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text: The Authority may suspend an amateur radio operator licence for a period not exceeding 6 months if the licensee is found to be in breach of any provision of this Act or its regulations. Grounds for suspension include, but are not limited to, causing harmful interference, operating outside of assigned frequencies, or making prohibited transmissions. Before suspension, the licensee will be given written notice of the alleged breach and an opportunity to make representations within 21 days. During a suspension period, all operating privileges are revoked, and any operation will be considered unlicensed.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text: A licence may be revoked by the Authority in cases of repeated or serious breaches of this Act, or if the licensee is convicted of a criminal offence involving the misuse of radio communications. Revocation results in the permanent loss of operating privileges. Before revocation, the licensee will receive a written notice outlining the grounds for revocation and will be granted an opportunity to present their case at a hearing, typically within 30 days of the notice. A revoked licensee may not apply for a new licence for a period of at least 3 years from the date of revocation. All equipment associated with the revoked licence may be subject to seizure.

heading: Penalties for Offences
text: Any person who operates an amateur radio station without a valid licence commits an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 crowns for a first offence, and 5,000 crowns for subsequent offences. Operating outside the terms of a licence, such as exceeding power limits or making prohibited transmissions, is punishable by a fine not exceeding 1,000 crowns. Persistent or malicious interference carries a fine up to 5,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 months. The Authority may also seize equipment used in the commission of an offence. All fines are payable within 60 days of issue.

heading: Seizure of Equipment
text: The Authority may seize any radio communication equipment reasonably believed to be used in contravention of this Act, including but not limited to unlicensed operation, causing harmful interference, or making prohibited transmissions. Seized equipment will be held for evidence and may be forfeited to the Crown upon conviction for an offence. A receipt for seized equipment will be provided to the owner. Equipment not related to an offence will be returned within 14 days of being cleared. Perishable or dangerous items may be disposed of immediately under specific circumstances, with documentation provided to the owner.

heading: Public Consultation
text: Before making any significant amendments to this Act or introducing new regulations concerning amateur radio, the Authority shall conduct a public consultation process. This process will involve publishing proposed changes and inviting submissions from amateur radio organizations, licensees, and the general public for a period of no less than 60 days. All feedback received will be considered before finalizing any changes. This ensures that the amateur radio community's interests are represented and that regulations are practical and fair. A summary of the feedback and the Authority's response will be published. This ensures transparency in decision-making.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Authority concerning the issuance, refusal, suspension, or revocation of an amateur radio licence may appeal that decision to an independent appeals board. The appeal must be lodged in writing within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision, accompanied by a fee of 300 crowns. The appeals board shall review the matter and issue a decision within 60 days. The board's decision shall be final, subject only to judicial review in the courts of Nordvale. The appeals board consists of three members, one of whom must have legal qualifications and another with technical expertise in radio communications.

heading: International Agreements
text: The Authority is empowered to enter into international reciprocal operating agreements with other countries concerning amateur radio licences. These agreements facilitate cross-border operation by amateur radio operators. Any such agreement must be consistent with Nordvale's international obligations and will be published in the official gazette. Where a conflict arises between the provisions of an international agreement and this Act, the provisions of the international agreement shall prevail, but only to the extent of the inconsistency. The Authority shall maintain a public list of all countries with which such agreements are in force, updated quarterly.

heading: Experimental Licences
text: The Authority may issue experimental amateur radio licences for specific, non-commercial technical investigations or research projects that fall outside the scope of standard licence classes. These licences are highly specialized and may permit temporary variations in frequency, power, or modulation methods. Applications for experimental licences must detail the purpose, methodology, equipment, and safety precautions, and require a fee of 500 crowns. Such licences are valid for a maximum of 12 months and may be renewed at the discretion of the Authority, subject to review of research progress. A full report on findings is required upon expiry.

heading: Promotion of Amateur Radio
text: The Authority shall, in conjunction with recognized amateur radio organizations, promote the advancement of amateur radio in Nordvale. This includes supporting educational initiatives, encouraging technical innovation, and fostering public awareness of the benefits of amateur radio, particularly in emergency preparedness. The Authority may provide grants up to 10,000 crowns annually to organizations that demonstrate a commitment to these objectives, particularly those in underserved regions like Grauby or Lund Vale. Activities may include workshops, field days, and mentorship programs for new operators, especially those under 25 years of age.

heading: Regulations
Transitional Provisions
text: Any amateur radio licence issued under previous regulations prior to the commencement of this Act shall remain valid until its original expiry date. Upon renewal, such licences shall be converted to the nearest equivalent class under this Act. Existing operators who do not hold a Class 1 equivalent licence but have significant operating experience (over 10 years) may apply for an upgrade examination within 2 years of this Act's commencement, waiving certain prerequisites. All existing amateur radio stations must comply with the new power limits and antenna regulations within 6 months of this Act coming into force. A special advisory committee will be formed for a period of 18 months to assist with transition.

heading: Repeal of Previous Act
text: The 'Radio Amateurs Ordinance' (Chapter 73, Laws of Nordvale) is hereby repealed. All regulations made under the repealed Ordinance that are consistent with this Act shall remain in force until new regulations are made under section 37, provided they do not contradict any express provision of this Act. Any proceedings commenced under the repealed Ordinance may be continued under the provisions of this Act, where applicable. This repeal does not affect the validity of any actions taken or rights acquired under the repealed Ordinance before the commencement of this Act. All records from the previous ordinance are to be transferred to the Authority within 90 days.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on the date of its publication in the official gazette of Nordvale. The provisions of this Act are immediately binding upon all amateur radio operators and stations within the Republic of Nordvale from that date forward. Any regulations made under section 37 may specify their own commencement dates, which may be later than the commencement of this Act. However, no regulation shall commence prior to the publication of this Act. The Authority shall ensure wide dissemination of this Act to all known amateur radio operators and relevant stakeholders within 30 days of its commencement.

heading: Section 40
text: The Authority shall establish and maintain a dedicated online portal for licence applications, renewals, and submission of compliance documents. This portal will be operational by January 1, 2019, and aims to streamline administrative processes. It will allow licensees to update their contact information, check their licence status, and access relevant regulations. Users of the portal must register an account and adhere to data security protocols. Support will be provided through a dedicated helpdesk, available five days a week from 09:00 to 17:00. A fee of 20 crowns will be charged for processing any offline applications submitted after the portal's launch.

heading: Section 40
text: The Authority shall establish and maintain a dedicated online portal for licence applications, renewals, and submission of compliance documents. This portal will be operational by January 1, 2019, and aims to streamline administrative processes. It will allow licensees to update their contact information, check their licence status, and access relevant regulations. Users of the portal must register an account and adhere to data security protocols. Support will be provided through a dedicated helpdesk, available seven days a week from 08:00 to 18:00. A fee of 30 crowns will be charged for processing any offline applications submitted after the portal's launch.

heading: Section 41
text: The Authority shall conduct an annual review of amateur radio spectrum utilization to identify opportunities for optimizing frequency allocations and to address any emerging interference concerns. This review will involve gathering data on band usage, conducting technical analyses, and soliciting input from the amateur radio community. A report on the findings of the annual review will be published by March 31st of each year, detailing any proposed adjustments to frequency plans or operational guidelines. Minor adjustments may be implemented without full public consultation if they affect less than 5% of a specific band and are supported by technical data. Any changes must be communicated to licensees with at least 60 days notice.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text:
(1) If a person is a certified ski patroller, then no fee or allowance is payable by that person in VBA §21.
(2) This exemption does not apply to fees for registering a ski patrol uniform.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each certified ski patroller receives half of the cost of keeping food at a temperature of 5 degrees Celsius or lower, including the cost of any required thermometer and daily temperature recording.

heading: Title inscription duty for senior field clinicians
text:
(1) No title inscription duty is due from a senior field clinician for the earliest acquisition in a calendar year of an unbuilt site of not more than 1,200 square metres.
(2) This relief replaces any other reduction of that duty.

heading: Kerbside refuse tariff for former field clinicians
text:
(1) A person who left employment as a certified field clinician at the age of 67 or later, and whose periods of that employment, counted as for a senior field clinician, add up to at least 15 years, pays the kerbside refuse tariff of the premises that are his or her residence reduced by the percentage for category CU1 in the Civic Utilities Concession Schedule.
(2) The reduction is applied after any other reduction of that tariff.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the licensing, operation, and maintenance of all amusement rides and attractions within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to safeguard the public by ensuring that all such installations meet rigorous safety standards, are regularly inspected, and are operated by qualified personnel. The scope of this Act extends to all permanent, temporary, and mobile amusement rides, including but not limited to carousels, roller coasters, Ferris wheels, and inflatable play structures, regardless of their location within any municipality.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Amusement Ride" means any device or combination of devices or elements that carries or conveys passengers along, around, or over a fixed or variable course for the purpose of amusement, entertainment, or recreation.
(b) "Attraction" means any non-ride entertainment feature designed for public participation, such as a walk-through maze or a funhouse, but specifically excluding theatrical performances.
(c) "Licence Holder" means an individual, company, or organization to whom a licence has been issued under this Act.
(d) "Minister" refers to the Minister responsible for Public Safety.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text:
(1) No person shall operate, or permit to be operated, an amusement ride or attraction within the Republic of Nordvale unless a valid licence has been issued for that specific ride or attraction in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) This requirement applies equally to permanent installations located in amusement parks, temporary rides at fairs or festivals, and mobile rides transported between locations. Failure to possess a valid licence constitutes an offence punishable by penalties outlined in section 30.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for an amusement ride or attraction licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Safety Authority at least 60 days prior to the intended operation date.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) Detailed design specifications and engineering drawings.
(b) A comprehensive safety management plan.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for an amusement ride or attraction licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Safety Authority at least 90 days prior to the intended operation date.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) Detailed design specifications and engineering drawings, certified by a Nordvale-registered engineer.
(b) A comprehensive safety management plan, including emergency response protocols.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 7,500,000 crowns.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 900 crowns.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for an amusement ride or attraction licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Safety Authority at least 120 days prior to the intended operation date.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) Detailed design specifications and engineering drawings, certified by a Nordvale-registered engineer.
(b) A comprehensive safety management plan, including emergency response protocols and crowd management strategies.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 10,000,000 crowns.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Pre-Licence Inspection
text:
(1) Before a licence can be issued, the Nordvale Safety Authority shall conduct a thorough pre-licence inspection of the amusement ride or attraction.
(2) This inspection will verify that the installation complies with all submitted specifications, applicable safety standards, and manufacturer guidelines. The applicant must ensure the ride is fully assembled and operational for this inspection. Any deficiencies identified during this inspection must be rectified within 30 days, or the application may be denied.

heading: Licence Issuance Criteria
text:
(1) A licence may be issued if the Nordvale Safety Authority is satisfied that:
(a) All application requirements specified in section 4 have been met.
(b) The amusement ride or attraction has passed the pre-licence inspection.
(c) The applicant has demonstrated the capacity to operate and maintain the ride safely.
(2) The Authority reserves the right to impose specific conditions on any licence to ensure public safety, such as limits on operating hours or specific maintenance schedules. A licence is valid for 12 months from its date of issue.

heading: Licence Issuance Criteria
text:
(1) A licence may be issued if the Nordvale Safety Authority is satisfied that:
(a) All application requirements specified in section 4 have been met and verified.
(b) The amusement ride or attraction has passed the pre-licence inspection with no critical deficiencies.
(c) The applicant has demonstrated the capacity to operate and maintain the ride safely, including a qualified operations manager.
(2) The Authority reserves the right to impose specific conditions on any licence to ensure public safety, such as limits on operating hours, specific maintenance schedules, or additional staffing requirements. A licence is valid for 18 months from its date of issue.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, a licence issuance fee of 1,500 crowns is payable upon approval of the licence.
(2) For each subsequent annual renewal, a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns is required. These fees contribute to the operational costs of the Nordvale Safety Authority, including ongoing inspection and regulatory enforcement activities. Failure to pay the fees within 14 days of invoice may result in licence suspension.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, a licence issuance fee of 2,000 crowns is payable upon approval of the licence.
(2) For each subsequent renewal, a renewal fee of 1,200 crowns is required. These fees contribute to the operational costs of the Nordvale Safety Authority, including ongoing inspection and regulatory enforcement activities. Failure to pay the fees within 10 days of invoice may result in immediate licence suspension.

heading: Licence Duration and Renewal
text:
(1) An amusement ride or attraction licence is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue.
(2) To renew a licence, the licence holder must submit a renewal application and the applicable fee at least 30 days before the current licence expires. The renewal application must include an updated safety management plan and proof of current insurance coverage. A late renewal fee of 200 crowns may apply if submitted within 15 days of expiry.

heading: Operational Safety Standards
text:
(1) All amusement rides and attractions must be operated in strict accordance with the manufacturer's operational manual and industry best practices.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, proper passenger loading and unloading procedures, adherence to height and weight restrictions, and continuous monitoring of ride operations. Operators must ensure that all safety restraints are securely fastened before the ride commences movement. Any deviation from these standards may result in immediate cessation of operation.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders are responsible for establishing and adhering to a comprehensive maintenance program for all licensed rides and attractions.
(2) This program must include daily pre-opening checks, weekly inspections by qualified technicians, and annual in-depth inspections by a certified engineer. All maintenance activities, including repairs and part replacements, must be meticulously documented and records kept for a minimum of three years. Failure to maintain these records may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders are responsible for establishing and adhering to a comprehensive maintenance program for all licensed rides and attractions.
(2) This program must include daily pre-opening checks, bi-weekly inspections by qualified technicians, and annual in-depth inspections by a certified engineer, with a full report submitted to the Authority. All maintenance activities, including repairs and part replacements, must be meticulously documented and records kept for a minimum of five years. Failure to maintain these records may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Personnel Qualifications
text:
(1) All individuals operating or maintaining amusement rides must be at least 18 years of age and possess the necessary qualifications and training.
(2) Operators must complete a certified training program specific to the ride they operate, covering emergency procedures, safety protocols, and passenger management. Maintenance personnel must hold relevant technical certifications. Records of all personnel training and qualifications must be kept on site and be made available upon request by the Nordvale Safety Authority.

heading: Daily Logbooks
text:
(1) Each licensed amusement ride or attraction must have a daily logbook maintained by the operator.
(2) The logbook shall record:
(a) Date and operating hours.
(b) Operator's name and signature.
(c) Details of daily pre-opening checks.
(d) Any unusual occurrences, incidents, or mechanical issues, however minor.
(e) Any repairs or adjustments made during the day. Logbooks must be kept for a period of one year.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text:
(1) Any incident involving an amusement ride or attraction that results in a serious injury requiring medical attention beyond first aid, or a structural failure, must be reported to the Nordvale Safety Authority within 24 hours of its occurrence.
(2) A detailed written report must follow within seven days. The ride or attraction involved in such an incident must cease operation immediately and not resume until authorized by the Authority. Failure to report within 24 hours may incur a penalty of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Public Liability Insurance
text:
(1) Licence holders must maintain valid public liability insurance coverage for a minimum amount of 5,000,000 crowns at all times.
(2) Proof of current insurance must be submitted with the initial licence application and with each renewal application. The Nordvale Safety Authority must be named as an interested party on the insurance policy. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate suspension of the licence until proof of new coverage is provided. Operating without insurance carries a fine of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Public Liability Insurance
text:
(1) Licence holders must maintain valid public liability insurance coverage for a minimum amount of 7,500,000 crowns at all times.
(2) Proof of current insurance must be submitted with the initial licence application and with each renewal application. The Nordvale Safety Authority must be named as an interested party on the insurance policy. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate suspension of the licence until proof of new coverage is provided. Operating without insurance carries a fine of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Public Liability Insurance
text:
(1) Licence holders must maintain valid public liability insurance coverage for a minimum amount of 10,000,000 crowns at all times.
(2) Proof of current insurance must be submitted with the initial licence application and with each renewal application. The Nordvale Safety Authority must be named as an interested party on the insurance policy and must be notified of any changes within 5 days. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate suspension of the licence until proof of new coverage is provided. Operating without insurance carries a fine of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Inspections by Authority
text:
(1) The Nordvale Safety Authority may conduct unannounced inspections of any licensed amusement ride or attraction at any time during its operational hours.
(2) These inspections are to ensure ongoing compliance with this Act, licence conditions, and safety standards. Licence holders must grant full access to inspectors and provide any requested documentation, including maintenance records and operator certifications. Obstruction of an inspection may lead to licence revocation and a fine of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Corrective Action Orders
text:
(1) If an inspector identifies any non-compliance or safety concern during an inspection, they may issue a corrective action order.
(2) This order will specify the nature of the non-compliance, the required corrective measures, and a deadline for completion, typically between 7 and 30 days depending on severity. Failure to comply with a corrective action order within the specified timeframe may result in suspension or revocation of the licence and further penalties.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Nordvale Safety Authority may suspend a licence if:
(a) There is an immediate threat to public safety.
(b) The licence holder fails to comply with a corrective action order.
(c) The licence holder operates without valid insurance.
(2) A suspended licence means the amusement ride or attraction must cease operation immediately. The suspension will remain in effect until the identified issues are resolved to the satisfaction of the Authority. A notice of suspension will be issued in writing.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked by the Nordvale Safety Authority for serious or repeated violations of this Act or licence conditions.
(2) Grounds for revocation include:
(a) Gross negligence in operation or maintenance.
(b) Repeated failure to comply with corrective action orders.
(c) Operation of a ride that has been deemed permanently unsafe.
(d) Falsification of records or documents. A revoked licence means the ride can no longer operate in Nordvale.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked by the Nordvale Safety Authority for serious or repeated violations of this Act or licence conditions.
(2) Grounds for revocation include:
(a) Gross negligence in operation or maintenance, leading to an incident.
(b) Failure to comply with two or more corrective action orders within a 12-month period.
(c) Operation of a ride that has been deemed permanently unsafe by a certified engineer.
(d) Falsification of records or documents, or obstruction of Authority inspectors. A revoked licence means the ride can no longer operate in Nordvale, and a new application cannot be made for 3 years.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A licence applicant or holder may appeal a decision by the Nordvale Safety Authority to deny, suspend, or revoke a licence.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Minister within 14 days of receiving notification of the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and provide any supporting documentation. The Minister will review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days. The Minister's decision is final.

heading: Signage Requirements
text:
(1) Each amusement ride or attraction must prominently display signage at its entrance.
(2) The signage must clearly indicate:
(a) The name of the ride or attraction.
(b) The licence number issued under this Act.
(c) Any applicable height, weight, or age restrictions.
(d) Specific health warnings, if any, for passengers.
(e) Emergency contact information for the operator. The text on the sign must be legible from a distance of 3 metres.

heading: Passenger Safety Briefings
text:
(1) Before the commencement of any amusement ride, operators must provide a clear and concise safety briefing to all passengers.
(2) This briefing must cover:
(a) The importance of remaining seated and keeping all body parts inside the ride vehicle.
(b) Proper use of safety restraints.
(c) What to do in case of an emergency stop.
(d) Any specific instructions for the particular ride. This briefing can be verbal or via a recorded message, but must be audible to all passengers.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text:
(1) Every licence holder must develop and implement a comprehensive emergency plan for each licensed amusement ride or attraction.
(2) This plan must detail procedures for:
(a) Fire and evacuation.
(b) Mechanical failure and passenger rescue.
(c) Medical emergencies.
(d) Severe weather conditions. All operational staff must be thoroughly trained in these procedures, with drills conducted at least twice annually. Copies of the plan must be readily accessible to all staff.

heading: First Aid Facilities
text:
(1) Adequate first aid facilities must be available at all locations where amusement rides or attractions are operated.
(2) For a single ride operation, a fully stocked first aid kit and at least one staff member trained in basic first aid must be present. For larger parks with multiple rides, a dedicated first aid station staffed by certified personnel must be maintained during all operating hours. The size and staffing of the first aid facilities should be proportionate to the expected number of patrons.

heading: Reporting Changes
text:
(1) Licence holders must notify the Nordvale Safety Authority in writing of any significant changes to a licensed amusement ride or attraction.
(2) Significant changes include:
(a) Major structural alterations.
(b) Replacement of critical safety components.
(c) Change of ownership or operating entity.
(d) Relocation of a permanent ride. Notification must be provided at least 30 days before the change takes effect, and may require a new inspection or application if deemed substantial.

heading: Transferability of Licences
text:
(1) A licence issued under this Act is not transferable from one person or entity to another without the express written approval of the Nordvale Safety Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be made by the prospective new licence holder, accompanied by a fee of 500 crowns and a full safety management plan. The Authority will review the applicant's qualifications and may require a new pre-licence inspection. Transfers are generally approved within 45 days, provided all conditions are met.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) All records pertaining to the design, manufacture, installation, maintenance, and operation of an amusement ride or attraction must be retained by the licence holder.
(2) These records, including logbooks, inspection reports, and training certificates, must be kept for the entire operational life of the ride, plus an additional five years after it ceases operation in Nordvale. They must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Safety Authority upon reasonable request, typically within 48 hours.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
(1) The Nordvale Safety Authority shall maintain a public register of all licensed amusement rides and attractions in Nordvale.
(2) This register will include the licence number, the name of the ride, the licence holder's name, and the date of issue and expiry. Information regarding corrective action orders or licence suspensions may also be made publicly available, subject to privacy considerations. Members of the public may request specific details by submitting a formal information request, which may incur a small administrative fee of 50 crowns.

heading: Jurisdiction of Municipalities
text:
(1) While this Act provides the overarching regulatory framework, municipalities retain the authority to enact local bylaws concerning the placement and operating hours of amusement rides and attractions.
(2) For instance, the municipality of Aldmark may restrict operation after 22:00, or Corvik may require a minimum setback of 15 metres from residential properties. These local bylaws must not contradict or diminish the safety standards established by this Act. Licence holders are responsible for complying with both national and local regulations.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who contravenes a provision of this Act, or fails to comply with a condition of a licence or a corrective action order, commits an offence.
(2) Unless otherwise specified, an offence under this Act is punishable by a fine of up to 20,000 crowns for a first offence, and up to 50,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 6 months for subsequent offences. Each day an offence continues may be considered a separate offence. Penalties may be doubled if serious injury or death results from the contravention.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Information designated as commercially sensitive, such as detailed design schematics or proprietary maintenance procedures, shall be treated with confidentiality by the Nordvale Safety Authority.
(2) Such information will not be disclosed to the public, except where required by law or necessary for the enforcement of this Act. Any request for such information will be assessed against a public interest test, balancing transparency with the protection of business interests. Applicants must clearly mark confidential sections within their submissions.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister may make regulations for carrying into effect the purposes and provisions of this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Minister may make regulations:
(a) Prescribing specific safety standards for different types of rides.
(b) Setting out detailed training requirements for operators and maintenance staff.
(c) Establishing forms for applications and reports.
(d) Modifying fees or penalty amounts based on economic indicators or safety trends.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister may make regulations for carrying into effect the purposes and provisions of this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Minister may make regulations:
(a) Prescribing specific safety standards for different types of rides, including new technologies.
(b) Setting out detailed training requirements for operators and maintenance staff, including mandatory refresher courses every 2 years.
(c) Establishing forms for applications and reports, which may be digital-only.
(d) Modifying fees or penalty amounts based on economic indicators or safety trends, subject to annual review.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister may make regulations for carrying into effect the purposes and provisions of this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Minister may make regulations:
(a) Prescribing specific safety standards for different types of rides, including new technologies and virtual reality attractions.
(b) Setting out detailed training requirements for operators and maintenance staff, including mandatory refresher courses every 18 months and practical assessments.
(c) Establishing forms for applications and reports, which shall be exclusively digital.
(d) Modifying fees or penalty amounts based on economic indicators or safety trends, subject to biannual review and public consultation.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any amusement ride or attraction operating in Nordvale prior to the coming into force of this Act must apply for a licence within 180 days of the Act's commencement.
(2) During this 180-day period, such rides may continue to operate provided they meet existing safety guidelines and have adequate insurance. Failure to submit an application within this timeframe will result in the immediate cessation of operation and potential penalties. The Authority will prioritize these transitional applications to minimize disruption.

heading: Enforcement of Fines
text:
(1) Fines imposed under this Act are payable to the Nordvale Safety Authority within 30 days of the date of the penalty notice.
(2) If a fine is not paid within the specified period, the Authority may initiate legal proceedings to recover the amount, including any associated court costs. An unpaid fine may also lead to a temporary suspension of any active licence held by the offending party until the debt is cleared. Interest at a rate of 10% per annum may be applied to overdue amounts.

heading: General Duty of Care
text:
(1) Every licence holder has a general duty to take all reasonable steps to ensure the safety of persons using or in the vicinity of an amusement ride or attraction.
(2) This duty extends beyond specific compliance with regulations and includes proactive measures to identify and mitigate potential hazards. For example, ensuring adequate lighting at night, maintaining clear pathways, and providing shade in hot weather. Failure to uphold this general duty may be considered a factor in assessing negligence during incident investigations.

heading: Special categories
text: A licensed tightrope performer shall pay half of the fee or allowance specified in FDA §30, whether daily or monthly.

heading: Exemptions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced by half for any person who is a registered cartographer.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for ensuring the safety of amusement rides operated at public events within the Republic of Nordvale. It mandates regular inspections, sets operational standards, and outlines responsibilities for ride operators and event organizers. The primary goal is to protect the public from hazards associated with amusement rides by enforcing rigorous safety protocols across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This Act applies to all temporary and permanent amusement ride installations intended for public use at festivals, fairs, and other gatherings where an admission fee is charged or where the event is otherwise open to the general public.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(1) 'Amusement ride' means any mechanical device or combination of devices which carries or conveys passengers along, around, or over a fixed or restricted course for the purpose of amusement, pleasure, thrills, or entertainment. This includes carousels, Ferris wheels, roller coasters, and similar attractions.
(2) 'Operator' means any person or entity responsible for the day-to-day running, maintenance, and supervision of an amusement ride.
(3) 'Inspector' means an individual certified by the Ministry of Public Safety to conduct safety inspections of amusement rides.
(4) 'Public event' refers to any gathering in a public space, lasting more than 4 hours, and attended by more than 50 individuals, where an amusement ride is present.

heading: Inspection Requirements
text: Every amusement ride operating within Nordvale must undergo a comprehensive safety inspection at least once every 12 months. Additionally, any ride that is disassembled, transported, and reassembled for a new event must be re-inspected before its public operation. These inspections must be conducted by a certified inspector who will verify compliance with all established safety standards. A certificate of inspection, valid for a maximum of 365 days, must be prominently displayed at the ride's entrance for public viewing. Failure to display a valid certificate will result in immediate operational suspension and a fine of 500 crowns per day.

heading: Inspection Requirements
text: Every amusement ride operating within Nordvale must undergo a comprehensive safety inspection at least once every 9 months. Additionally, any ride that is disassembled, transported, and reassembled for a new event must be re-inspected before its public operation. These inspections must be conducted by a certified inspector who will verify compliance with all established safety standards. A certificate of inspection, valid for a maximum of 270 days, must be prominently displayed at the ride's entrance for public viewing. Failure to display a valid certificate will result in immediate operational suspension and a fine of 750 crowns per day.

heading: Pre-Operational Checks
text: Before opening to the public each day, every amusement ride operator must perform a series of pre-operational checks. These checks include verifying the proper functioning of all restraints, emergency stop buttons, safety gates, and communication systems. A daily logbook, signed by the operator, must record the completion of these checks. This logbook must be readily available for inspection by any certified inspector or Ministry official. Negligence in conducting these daily checks, or falsifying logbook entries, may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns and temporary suspension of the ride's operating license for 30 days.

heading: Operator Certification
text: All individuals operating an amusement ride must possess a valid operator certification issued by the Ministry of Public Safety. This certification requires completion of a 40-hour training course covering ride mechanics, emergency procedures, passenger management, and first aid. The minimum age for certified operators is 18 years. Certifications are valid for 3 years and must be renewed through a 10-hour refresher course. Operating a ride without valid certification, or allowing an uncertified individual to operate a ride, carries a penalty of 2,500 crowns for the operator and 5,000 crowns for the event organizer.

heading: Operator Certification
text: All individuals operating an amusement ride must possess a valid operator certification issued by the Ministry of Public Safety. This certification requires completion of a 60-hour training course covering ride mechanics, emergency procedures, passenger management, first aid, and advanced safety diagnostics. The minimum age for certified operators is 19 years. Certifications are valid for 2 years and must be renewed through a 15-hour refresher course. Operating a ride without valid certification, or allowing an uncertified individual to operate a ride, carries a penalty of 3,000 crowns for the operator and 6,000 crowns for the event organizer.

heading: Maintenance Records
text: Detailed maintenance records for each amusement ride must be kept for a minimum of 5 years. These records shall include dates of service, nature of repairs, parts replaced, and the name and signature of the individual performing the maintenance. Records must be provided to inspectors upon request. Failure to maintain adequate records will result in a penalty of 750 crowns per missing record and may lead to a temporary operational suspension until documentation is brought up to date.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text: Each amusement ride must have a clearly defined emergency procedure plan, outlining steps to be taken in case of mechanical failure, power outage, passenger illness, or other unforeseen incidents. This plan must be displayed in a prominent location visible to all operators and staff. All staff working with the ride must be thoroughly trained in these procedures and capable of executing them swiftly and effectively. Regular drills, at least once every 6 months, are required to ensure preparedness. Non-compliance with this section may result in fines up to 3,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text: Each amusement ride must have a clearly defined emergency procedure plan, outlining steps to be taken in case of mechanical failure, power outage, passenger illness, or other unforeseen incidents. This plan must be displayed in a prominent location visible to all operators and staff, and a digital copy accessible via tablet at the control panel. All staff working with the ride must be thoroughly trained in these procedures and capable of executing them swiftly and effectively. Regular drills, at least once every 3 months, are required to ensure preparedness. Non-compliance with this section may result in fines up to 4,500 crowns and immediate ride closure.

heading: Passenger Safety Requirements
text: Operators are responsible for ensuring that all passengers meet the minimum height and age requirements for each ride, as specified by the manufacturer and approved by the Ministry. Restraints must be properly secured for every passenger before the ride commences. Clear instructions on safe riding practices must be announced or displayed. Children under 1.2 meters in height must be accompanied by an adult at least 16 years old on rides designated for family use. Failure to enforce these requirements can lead to fines of 1,500 crowns per infraction.

heading: Reporting Incidents
text: Any incident involving an amusement ride that results in injury requiring medical attention, or any mechanical failure that prevents safe operation, must be reported to the Ministry of Public Safety within 24 hours of its occurrence. A detailed written report must follow within 72 hours. Failure to report such incidents promptly can result in severe penalties, including fines up to 10,000 crowns and permanent revocation of operating licenses. All reported incidents will be investigated thoroughly by Ministry officials.

heading: Reporting Incidents
text: Any incident involving an amusement ride that results in injury requiring medical attention, or any mechanical failure that prevents safe operation, must be reported to the Ministry of Public Safety within 12 hours of its occurrence. A detailed written report must follow within 48 hours. Failure to report such incidents promptly can result in severe penalties, including fines up to 15,000 crowns and permanent revocation of operating licenses. All reported incidents will be investigated thoroughly by Ministry officials, with preliminary findings released within 14 days.

heading: Prohibited Operations
text: No amusement ride may operate if an inspector has issued a stop-order due to safety concerns. Operation is also prohibited during adverse weather conditions, including winds exceeding 40 kilometers per hour, heavy rain, or lightning. Modifications to any ride's structural or mechanical components are strictly forbidden without prior written approval from the manufacturer and the Ministry of Public Safety. Violations of this section will result in immediate ride closure, a fine of 20,000 crowns, and potential legal action against the operator and event organizer.

heading: Inspecting Authority
text: The Ministry of Public Safety is the designated authority responsible for overseeing all amusement ride inspections in Nordvale. It is empowered to appoint and certify inspectors, develop and update safety standards, investigate incidents, and enforce compliance with this Act. The Ministry may delegate specific inspection duties to approved third-party agencies, provided those agencies meet stringent accreditation criteria established by the Ministry. All inspectors must undergo annual retraining for 8 hours to maintain their certification.

heading: Inspector's Powers
text: A certified inspector has the authority to enter any premises where an amusement ride is being operated or assembled, at any reasonable time, without prior notice. Inspectors may conduct tests, examine documents, interview personnel, and issue stop-orders if immediate safety hazards are identified. Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns and immediate suspension of the ride's operating license for 90 days. Inspectors are required to present official identification upon request.

heading: Safety Standards Compliance
text: All amusement rides must comply with the safety standards established by the Ministry of Public Safety. These standards cover design, construction, operation, and maintenance. Operators are responsible for ensuring that their rides meet these standards at all times. Non-compliance identified during an inspection may result in a deficiency notice, requiring corrective action within 7 days. Failure to rectify deficiencies within the specified timeframe will lead to a fine of 1,000 crowns per day until compliance is achieved and the ride passes a re-inspection.

heading: Safety Standards Compliance
text: All amusement rides must comply with the safety standards established by the Ministry of Public Safety. These standards cover design, construction, operation, and maintenance, including new digital control system protocols. Operators are responsible for ensuring that their rides meet these standards at all times. Non-compliance identified during an inspection may result in a deficiency notice, requiring corrective action within 3 days. Failure to rectify deficiencies within the specified timeframe will lead to a fine of 1,500 crowns per day until compliance is achieved and the ride passes a re-inspection. Repeat offenders may face permanent license revocation.

heading: Annual Permit Fees
text: Operators of amusement rides must pay an annual permit fee of 1,200 crowns per ride to the Ministry of Public Safety. This fee helps cover the administrative costs associated with inspections, certification, and enforcement of this Act. The fee is due by January 31st of each year. A late payment penalty of 10% will be applied if the fee is not paid within 30 days of the due date. Operating a ride without a valid annual permit will result in a 2,000 crowns fine and immediate ride closure until the permit is acquired.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Every amusement ride operator must maintain liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns per incident. Proof of current insurance must be submitted to the Ministry of Public Safety annually and be readily available at the ride's operating location. Operation without adequate insurance is strictly prohibited and will result in a fine of 15,000 crowns and immediate suspension of all operating licenses within Nordvale, including in municipalities like Dunmere and Elsby, until proof of compliance is provided. The Ministry may request an updated certificate of insurance at any time.

heading: Manufacturer's Manuals
text: A copy of the manufacturer's operational and maintenance manual for each amusement ride must be present at the ride's operating location at all times. Operators and maintenance personnel must be familiar with the contents of these manuals. Any deviation from manufacturer-recommended procedures or specifications must be documented and approved by a certified engineer and the Ministry. Failure to have the manual available or adhere to its guidelines can lead to a fine of 800 crowns per day until compliance is achieved. These manuals are critical for safe operation.

heading: Passenger Information Display
text: At the entrance of every amusement ride, operators must clearly display important passenger information. This includes height and age restrictions, health warnings, instructions for securing restraints, and any other specific safety guidelines. The text must be legible, with a minimum font size of 20 points, and positioned at a height between 1.2 and 1.8 meters from the ground. Failure to display this information, or displaying it incorrectly, will result in a warning for the first offense and a fine of 300 crowns for subsequent offenses.

heading: Passenger Information Display
text: At the entrance of every amusement ride, operators must clearly display important passenger information. This includes height and age restrictions, health warnings, instructions for securing restraints, and any other specific safety guidelines. The text must be legible, with a minimum font size of 24 points, and positioned at a height between 1.3 and 1.7 meters from the ground. Information must also be available digitally via a QR code. Failure to display this information, or displaying it incorrectly, will result in a warning for the first offense and a fine of 450 crowns for subsequent offenses.

heading: Record Retention
text: All inspection certificates, maintenance records, operator certifications, and incident reports must be retained by the operator for a minimum period of 5 years. These records must be produced for inspection upon demand by any Ministry official. Electronic copies are permissible provided they are securely stored and readily accessible. Failure to produce requested documents within 48 hours will result in a fine of 600 crowns for each missing document. This retention period ensures accountability and transparency in ride safety.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An operator or event organizer may appeal any decision made by an inspector or the Ministry of Public Safety within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Ministry, accompanied by a fee of 500 crowns. The Appeals Board will review the case and render a decision within 60 days. Decisions of the Appeals Board are final. During the appeal process, any stop-order or suspension remains in effect. This process ensures fairness in enforcement actions.

heading: Penalties for Violations
text: Any person or entity found in violation of this Act, for which no specific penalty is provided, shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 5,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses of the same nature within a 12-month period may incur fines up to 10,000 crowns and a temporary suspension of operating privileges for up to 6 months. Serious violations that endanger public safety may result in permanent revocation of licenses and further legal action, including in municipalities like Fennick and Grauby. The Ministry retains discretion in assessing penalties based on severity.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: The Ministry of Public Safety shall maintain a public register of all certified amusement rides, including their last inspection dates and any outstanding safety deficiencies. This register will be accessible online and updated weekly. The public may request copies of inspection reports for specific rides, subject to a nominal administrative fee of 50 crowns per report. Incident reports that do not compromise ongoing investigations will also be made available. This promotes transparency and allows the public to make informed choices about amusement ride safety.

heading: Modification of Rides
text: No structural or mechanical modifications shall be made to an amusement ride without prior written approval from the original manufacturer and the Ministry of Public Safety. A detailed engineering plan of the proposed modifications must be submitted for review, and the modified ride must undergo a special inspection before being returned to service. Unauthorized modifications are considered a severe breach of safety protocols and will result in a fine of 25,000 crowns and permanent revocation of the ride's operating license within Nordvale.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text: The Ministry of Public Safety will cooperate closely with local authorities in all municipalities, including Lund Vale, to ensure effective enforcement of this Act. Local police and municipal safety officers are empowered to assist inspectors in upholding stop-orders and ensuring compliance with safety directives. Joint training exercises will be conducted at least twice a year to foster better coordination. Local authorities should report any observed safety concerns to the Ministry within 8 hours for immediate investigation and follow-up actions.

heading: Training for Inspectors
text: All certified inspectors must complete a mandatory 40-hour initial training program and an 8-hour annual refresher course. The initial program covers ride dynamics, materials science, electrical systems, and emergency response. The refresher course focuses on updates to safety standards and lessons learned from recent incidents. Inspectors failing to complete the annual refresher course will have their certification temporarily suspended until completion. The Ministry provides these training programs free of charge to ensure a high standard of expertise among its inspection staff.

heading: Funding for Enforcement
text: A portion of the annual permit fees and collected fines, amounting to 60%, shall be allocated to a dedicated fund for the enforcement of this Act. This fund will support inspector salaries, training programs, equipment purchases, and incident investigations. The remaining 40% will be directed to general public safety initiatives. The Ministry is required to publish an annual report detailing the expenditures from this fund, ensuring transparency in its financial operations and resource allocation for ride safety.

heading: Repeal of Section 26
text: Section 26 (Public Awareness Campaigns) is hereby repealed. The Ministry found that public awareness initiatives were more effectively integrated into broader public safety programs. Therefore, a standalone section dedicated to such campaigns is no longer deemed necessary for the effective functioning of this Act. Resources previously allocated to this section will be redirected to enhance technical training for inspectors, as outlined in section 24. This change streamlines administrative efforts and focuses resources on core enforcement activities.

heading: Repeal of Section 26
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All amusement ride operators and event organizers are expected to be in full compliance with all sections of this Act from this date forward. A grace period of 90 days will be granted for administrative requirements, such as permit applications and initial certification renewals, but safety standards and operational protocols must be met immediately. The Ministry will issue detailed guidelines and frequently asked questions documents before the effective date to aid in understanding and compliance.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) A licensed fireworks technician shall pay 5 crowns instead of any fee or allowance specified in FDA §38. (2) This fixed payment applies to all requests.

heading: Concessions
text: Each holder of a meteorological observer badge pays half of the annual filing fee specified in SBA §27(3).

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the criteria and procedures for the allocation of agricultural subsidies and grants to eligible farmers within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to support sustainable agricultural practices, enhance food security, and ensure the economic viability of farming operations across all regions, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. The scope covers all forms of direct financial aid and incentives designed to foster agricultural productivity and environmental stewardship. The Act aims to provide a clear and transparent framework for all subsidy applications and disbursements.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Farmer" means an individual or entity actively engaged in agricultural production for commercial purposes.
(b) "Agricultural production" includes cultivation of crops, raising of livestock, and related activities.
(c) "Ministry" refers to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development of Nordvale.
(d) "Subsidy" means a direct financial payment or grant provided by the Ministry.
(e) "Eligible land" refers to land designated for agricultural use according to municipal planning documents, exceeding 2 hectares in continuous area.
(f) "Application period" refers to the specified timeframe within which applications for subsidies must be submitted, typically between January 1st and February 28th of each year.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Subsidies
text:
(1) To be eligible for a subsidy under this Act, an applicant must:
(a) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(b) Be at least 18 years of age at the time of application.
(c) Own or lease agricultural land of at least 5 hectares within Nordvale.
(d) Demonstrate at least 3 years of active engagement in agricultural production.
(e) Have no outstanding tax liabilities with the Nordvale Revenue Service exceeding 5,000 crowns.
(2) All applicants must submit proof of land ownership or lease agreements, along with their most recent income tax statements.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Subsidies
text:
(1) To be eligible for a subsidy under this Act, an applicant must:
(a) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(b) Be at least 21 years of age at the time of application.
(c) Own or lease agricultural land of at least 4 hectares within Nordvale.
(d) Demonstrate at least 2 years of active engagement in agricultural production.
(e) Have no outstanding tax liabilities with the Nordvale Revenue Service exceeding 3,000 crowns.
(2) All applicants must submit proof of land ownership or lease agreements, along with their most recent income tax statements and a business plan for the upcoming 12 months.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications for subsidies shall be submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development via the prescribed online portal or physical form.
(2) The application period shall open on January 1st and close on February 28th each year. Late applications will not be considered.
(3) Applicants must provide all requested documentation, including proof of identity, land titles, and a detailed farming plan for the current year. Incomplete applications will be returned for rectification, with a 14-day window for resubmission.
(4) A non-refundable application fee of 150 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: General Agricultural Productivity Grant
text:
(1) A General Agricultural Productivity Grant is available to eligible farmers who cultivate a minimum of 10 hectares of land.
(2) The grant provides a fixed payment of 1,000 crowns per hectare for the first 20 hectares, and 750 crowns per hectare for any area beyond 20 hectares, up to a maximum of 50 hectares. The total grant cannot exceed 35,000 crowns.
(3) Funds from this grant must be used for expenses directly related to increasing agricultural output, such as seed purchase, fertilizer, or machinery maintenance. Receipts must be kept for 3 years.
(4) Payments are disbursed in two installments: 60% upon approval and 40% after a mid-year compliance check.

heading: General Agricultural Productivity Grant
text:
(1) A General Agricultural Productivity Grant is available to eligible farmers who cultivate a minimum of 8 hectares of land.
(2) The grant provides a fixed payment of 1,200 crowns per hectare for the first 15 hectares, and 900 crowns per hectare for any area beyond 15 hectares, up to a maximum of 40 hectares. The total grant cannot exceed 30,000 crowns.
(3) Funds from this grant must be used for expenses directly related to increasing agricultural output, such as seed purchase, fertilizer, or machinery maintenance. Receipts must be kept for 5 years.
(4) Payments are disbursed in two installments: 70% upon approval and 30% after a mid-year compliance check.

heading: Sustainable Farming Practices Incentive
text:
(1) Farmers implementing sustainable practices, such as crop rotation, reduced tillage, or organic farming methods, may apply for the Sustainable Farming Practices Incentive.
(2) Eligible practices include: (a) maintaining a minimum of 20% of arable land under cover crops, (b) reducing synthetic pesticide use by 15% compared to the previous year, or (c) certifying 5 hectares as organic.
(3) The incentive provides a payment of 500 crowns per hectare for up to 30 hectares, with a maximum total payment of 15,000 crowns. Applicants must provide detailed records of their implemented practices for verification by Ministry officials during an on-site visit.
(4) Proof of compliance must be maintained for 5 years.

heading: Sustainable Farming Practices Incentive
text:
(1) Farmers implementing sustainable practices, such as advanced crop rotation, minimum tillage, or certified organic farming methods, may apply for the Sustainable Farming Practices Incentive.
(2) Eligible practices include: (a) maintaining a minimum of 25% of arable land under cover crops, (b) reducing synthetic pesticide use by 20% compared to the previous year, or (c) certifying 8 hectares as organic.
(3) The incentive provides a payment of 600 crowns per hectare for up to 40 hectares, with a maximum total payment of 24,000 crowns. Applicants must provide detailed records of their implemented practices for verification by Ministry officials during an on-site visit, which will occur within 60 days of application approval.
(4) Proof of compliance must be maintained for 7 years.

heading: Water Conservation Grant
text:
(1) A Water Conservation Grant is available for farmers who invest in water-saving technologies or infrastructure.
(2) Eligible investments include drip irrigation systems, rainwater harvesting tanks with a capacity of at least 5,000 liters, or the conversion of flood irrigation to pivot irrigation for at least 3 hectares.
(3) The grant covers 40% of documented investment costs, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns per farm. A single farm may apply for this grant once every 5 years.
(4) Proof of purchase and installation, along with a water usage plan, must be submitted with the application. Projects must be completed within 180 days of grant approval.

heading: Soil Health Improvement Grant
text:
(1) Farmers undertaking initiatives to improve soil health and fertility may apply for this grant.
(2) Initiatives include the addition of organic matter, soil enrichment through specific cover crop rotations, or the implementation of no-till farming across at least 4 hectares. A baseline soil test must be provided.
(3) The grant provides 300 crowns per hectare for up to 50 hectares, with a maximum of 15,000 crowns. A follow-up soil test must demonstrate at least a 10% improvement in organic matter content within 2 years of the grant's approval.
(4) Failure to meet the improvement target may result in repayment of the grant, plus a 5% penalty.

heading: Livestock Welfare Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers who implement enhanced animal welfare standards for their livestock.
(2) Eligible improvements include providing increased space per animal by 20% beyond standard requirements, upgrading housing facilities to include natural light and ventilation, or investing in humane handling equipment. Applicable to farms with a minimum of 50 head of cattle or 200 head of poultry.
(3) The grant covers 30% of verifiable costs, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. Farmers must adhere to a specific animal welfare plan approved by the Ministry for a minimum of 3 years.
(4) Inspections may occur at any time during this 3-year period.

heading: Livestock Welfare Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers who implement enhanced animal welfare standards for their livestock.
(2) Eligible improvements include providing increased space per animal by 25% beyond standard requirements, upgrading housing facilities to include natural light and enhanced ventilation, or investing in humane handling equipment. Applicable to farms with a minimum of 40 head of cattle or 150 head of poultry.
(3) The grant covers 35% of verifiable costs, up to a maximum of 12,000 crowns. Farmers must adhere to a specific animal welfare plan approved by the Ministry for a minimum of 5 years.
(4) Unannounced inspections may occur at any time during this 5-year period to ensure continuous compliance. Non-compliance may lead to grant revocation and a 10% penalty.

heading: Young Farmer Start-up Grant
text:
(1) Individuals aged between 18 and 35 years who are establishing their first agricultural enterprise may apply for the Young Farmer Start-up Grant.
(2) Applicants must submit a comprehensive business plan demonstrating viability and a commitment to farming for at least 5 years. They must also have obtained a recognized agricultural qualification or have 2 years of practical farming experience.
(3) The grant provides a one-time payment of 20,000 crowns. This grant is intended to assist with initial capital investments such as land acquisition, machinery, or building construction. Funds must be utilized within 12 months of receipt.
(4) Recipients must reside in Nordvale for the duration of the 5-year commitment.

heading: Small Farm Support Grant
text:
(1) Farmers operating agricultural land between 2 and 10 hectares are eligible for the Small Farm Support Grant.
(2) This grant aims to ensure the economic sustainability of smaller farming operations. It provides a flat payment of 5,000 crowns per year, provided the farm generates at least 15,000 crowns in annual agricultural revenue.
(3) Applicants must submit a declaration of their annual agricultural revenue, verified by financial statements from the previous fiscal year. This grant can be combined with other non-hectare based grants.
(4) Payments are made once annually, following verification of eligibility and revenue. The grant is reviewed every 2 years.

heading: Small Farm Support Grant
text:
(1) Farmers operating agricultural land between 2 and 8 hectares are eligible for the Small Farm Support Grant.
(2) This grant aims to ensure the economic sustainability of smaller farming operations. It provides a flat payment of 6,500 crowns per year, provided the farm generates at least 18,000 crowns in annual agricultural revenue.
(3) Applicants must submit a declaration of their annual agricultural revenue, verified by financial statements from the previous fiscal year. This grant can be combined with other non-hectare based grants, but not exceed 75% of total eligible operating costs.
(4) Payments are made once annually, following verification of eligibility and revenue. The grant is reviewed every 3 years for continued relevance and impact.

heading: Small Farm Support Grant
text:
(1) Farmers operating agricultural land between 2 and 7 hectares are eligible for the Small Farm Support Grant.
(2) This grant aims to ensure the economic sustainability of smaller farming operations. It provides a flat payment of 7,000 crowns per year, provided the farm generates at least 20,000 crowns in annual agricultural revenue.
(3) Applicants must submit a declaration of their annual agricultural revenue, verified by financial statements from the previous fiscal year, along with a projected budget for the next 12 months. This grant can be combined with other non-hectare based grants, but not exceed 70% of total eligible operating costs.
(4) Payments are made once annually, following verification of eligibility and revenue. The grant is reviewed every 3 years for continued relevance and impact and adjustments made based on economic conditions.

heading: Crop Diversification Incentive
text:
(1) To encourage crop diversity and reduce reliance on monoculture, farmers who introduce at least two new crop types to their rotation for a minimum of 3 years may apply for this incentive.
(2) The new crop types must occupy at least 10% of the farm's arable land and must not have been cultivated on that land in the preceding 5 years. Eligible new crops include pulses, specialty grains, or specific types of vegetables.
(3) The incentive offers 400 crowns per hectare for the diversified area, up to a maximum of 20 hectares, with a total cap of 8,000 crowns. Documentation of crop history and current planting plans is required.
(4) A Ministry inspection will confirm diversification within 90 days of planting.

heading: Agricultural Technology Adoption Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers in adopting innovative agricultural technologies to improve efficiency and productivity.
(2) Eligible technologies include precision farming equipment (e.g., GPS-guided tractors), automated irrigation systems, or advanced data collection sensors. The technology must be new to the applicant's farm and demonstrate clear benefits.
(3) The grant covers 35% of the purchase and installation costs, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns. Farmers must provide invoices and proof of installation. A technology implementation plan outlining expected benefits must also be submitted.
(4) The technology must remain operational for at least 4 years following grant disbursement.

heading: Farm Safety Improvement Grant
text:
(1) To promote safer working environments on farms, this grant assists with investments in safety equipment and infrastructure upgrades.
(2) Eligible items include safety guards for machinery, improved lighting in barns, fire suppression systems, or training programs for farm workers. The improvements must comply with Nordvale's occupational safety standards.
(3) The grant covers 50% of the documented costs, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per farm. A risk assessment report, identifying safety deficiencies, must accompany the application.
(4) All improvements must be completed within 6 months of grant approval.

heading: Organic Certification Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers transitioning to or maintaining organic certification for their agricultural land.
(2) It covers 70% of the annual certification fees for an accredited organic certification body, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns per year. The grant is available for a maximum of 3 consecutive years for farms in conversion.
(3) For farms already certified, it covers 50% of annual fees, up to 3,000 crowns per year. Proof of certification and invoices for fees must be provided.
(4) A farm must demonstrate continuous adherence to organic standards as verified by the certification body. Any loss of certification will result in immediate cessation of grant payments.

heading: Regional Development Grant (Aldmark and Brenholt)
text:
(1) Farmers located in the municipalities of Aldmark and Brenholt are eligible for this grant, designed to stimulate regional agricultural development.
(2) The grant provides an additional 10% on top of any other eligible grants received under sections 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 of this Act, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns per farm. This regional incentive encourages localized investment.
(3) Applicants must provide proof of farm location within the specified municipalities. The grant aims to address specific challenges faced by farmers in these areas.
(4) Funds are disbursed simultaneously with the primary grant payments.

heading: Regional Development Grant (Corvik and Dunmere)
text:
(1) Farmers located in the municipalities of Corvik and Dunmere are eligible for this grant, aimed at fostering agricultural resilience in these areas.
(2) The grant provides an additional 8% on top of any other eligible grants received under sections 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 of this Act, up to a maximum of 6,000 crowns per farm. This incentive acknowledges the unique environmental conditions in these regions.
(3) Applicants must provide proof of farm location within the specified municipalities. The grant seeks to mitigate specific risks and support diversification.
(4) Funds are disbursed simultaneously with the primary grant payments.

heading: Emergency Relief Fund
text:
(1) An Emergency Relief Fund is established to provide immediate financial assistance to farmers affected by unforeseen natural disasters or severe market downturns.
(2) Eligibility is determined on a case-by-case basis, requiring evidence of significant crop loss (over 40%) or livestock loss (over 25%), or a verified 30% reduction in market prices for primary products over a 3-month period. A loss assessment report from an independent assessor is mandatory.
(3) The fund can provide up to 50,000 crowns per affected farm, based on the severity of losses. Applications must be submitted within 60 days of the qualifying event.
(4) This fund is separate from other grants and is intended for recovery efforts.

heading: Research and Innovation Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers engaging in research and innovation projects aimed at developing new agricultural methods or products.
(2) Projects must be approved by the Nordvale Agricultural Research Institute and demonstrate potential for significant impact on agricultural productivity or sustainability. Examples include developing drought-resistant crop varieties or novel pest control methods.
(3) The grant covers up to 60% of documented research costs, including equipment, materials, and specialized labor, with a maximum allocation of 40,000 crowns per project. Project duration must not exceed 2 years.
(4) A detailed project proposal, budget, and timeline are required.

heading: Educational and Training Subsidy
text:
(1) Farmers and their immediate family members (spouses, children over 18) attending approved agricultural training courses or workshops may apply for this subsidy.
(2) Approved courses must be offered by recognized educational institutions in Nordvale and relate directly to agricultural management, new farming techniques, or farm business skills. The course must be at least 30 hours in duration.
(3) The subsidy covers 75% of tuition fees, up to a maximum of 2,500 crowns per person per year. A maximum of two individuals per farm may claim this subsidy annually.
(4) Proof of enrollment and successful completion must be submitted for reimbursement within 30 days of course completion.

heading: Market Access Grant
text:
(1) This grant assists farmers in accessing new markets or expanding their reach in existing ones, both domestically and internationally.
(2) Eligible activities include participation in trade fairs, development of new marketing materials, investment in direct-to-consumer sales platforms, or obtaining certifications for export. A market expansion plan is required.
(3) The grant covers 40% of verifiable costs, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns. Farmers must demonstrate a clear strategy for increasing sales or market share by at least 10% over 2 years.
(4) Funds are released upon submission of invoices and a progress report.

heading: Farm Infrastructure Upgrade Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers in upgrading essential farm infrastructure to improve operational efficiency or product quality.
