(2) Eligible upgrades include construction or renovation of storage facilities, irrigation systems, fencing, or processing units. The upgrade must comply with all relevant building codes and environmental regulations.
(3) The grant covers 30% of documented construction or renovation costs, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns per project. Projects must exceed 10,000 crowns in total cost.
(4) A detailed project proposal, including blueprints and cost estimates, must be submitted. Work must commence within 90 days of approval.

heading: Farm Infrastructure Upgrade Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers in upgrading essential farm infrastructure to improve operational efficiency or product quality.
(2) Eligible upgrades include construction or renovation of storage facilities, advanced irrigation systems, secure fencing, or modern processing units. The upgrade must comply with all relevant building codes and environmental regulations and incorporate sustainable materials where possible.
(3) The grant covers 35% of documented construction or renovation costs, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns per project. Projects must exceed 12,000 crowns in total cost.
(4) A detailed project proposal, including blueprints and cost estimates from at least two certified contractors, must be submitted. Work must commence within 75 days of approval and be completed within 12 months.

heading: Native Pollinator Habitat Grant
text:
(1) Farmers who establish or restore native pollinator habitats on their land may apply for this grant.
(2) Eligible activities include planting native flowering species, creating undisturbed nesting sites for native bees, or establishing buffer strips of pollinator-friendly vegetation. A minimum of 0.5 hectares must be dedicated to this purpose.
(3) The grant provides 600 crowns per 0.1 hectare, up to a maximum of 5 hectares, with a total cap of 30,000 crowns. A habitat management plan for 5 years is required.
(4) The habitat must be maintained for a minimum of 5 years. Ministry officials will conduct annual checks for compliance.

heading: Waste Management and Recycling Grant
text:
(1) This grant encourages farmers to adopt sustainable waste management and recycling practices on their farms.
(2) Eligible investments include composting facilities, specialized recycling bins for agricultural plastics, or systems for converting farm waste into energy. Investments must reduce landfill waste by at least 20% annually.
(3) The grant covers 45% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 8,000 crowns. A waste management plan, including baseline waste generation data, must be submitted.
(4) Annual reports on waste reduction achievements are required for 3 years following the grant.

heading: Waste Management and Recycling Grant
text:
(1) This grant encourages farmers to adopt sustainable waste management and recycling practices on their farms.
(2) Eligible investments include composting facilities, specialized recycling bins for agricultural plastics and organic waste, or systems for converting farm waste into energy. Investments must reduce landfill waste by at least 25% annually.
(3) The grant covers 50% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. A comprehensive waste management plan, including baseline waste generation data and proposed reduction strategies, must be submitted.
(4) Annual reports on waste reduction achievements are required for 5 years following the grant, and failure to meet reduction targets may result in partial repayment.

heading: Erosion Control Grant
text:
(1) Farmers implementing measures to control soil erosion and protect water quality may apply for this grant.
(2) Eligible measures include establishing contour farming, terracing, riparian buffer zones, or planting shelterbelts. The measures must cover at least 3 hectares of land prone to erosion.
(3) The grant provides 500 crowns per hectare for the treated area, up to a maximum of 40 hectares, with a total cap of 20,000 crowns. An erosion risk assessment must be provided.
(4) Erosion control measures must be maintained for a minimum of 7 years. Failure to maintain these measures may lead to repayment of the grant.

heading: Value-Added Product Development Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers who process their raw agricultural products into value-added goods, such as cheeses, jams, specialty meats, or textiles.
(2) Eligible expenses include equipment for processing, packaging design, branding, and marketing for the new product line. The product must utilize at least 50% of raw materials from the applicant's farm.
(3) The grant covers 35% of verifiable costs, up to a maximum of 20,000 crowns. A detailed business plan for the value-added product, including market analysis and financial projections, is required.
(4) The product must be launched within 18 months of grant approval.

heading: Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) Grant
text:
(1) Farmers establishing or expanding a Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program may apply for this grant.
(2) The CSA program must commit to supplying fresh produce or farm products directly to at least 20 local households for a minimum of 16 weeks per year. It must include a robust communication plan with subscribers.
(3) The grant provides a one-time payment of 7,000 crowns for establishing a new CSA or 3,500 crowns for expanding an existing one by at least 10 new households. A detailed CSA operational plan is required.
(4) Funds are intended for initial setup costs, such as packaging or administrative software.

heading: Farm Succession Planning Grant
text:
(1) This grant assists farmers in developing comprehensive succession plans to ensure the smooth transition of farm ownership and management to a new generation.
(2) Eligible expenses include legal fees, financial consulting, and professional mediation services related to the succession process. The plan must involve a designated successor who is committed to continuing the farming operation.
(3) The grant covers 60% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 12,000 crowns. A clear outline of the succession goals and participants is required.
(4) The succession plan must be formalized and submitted within 24 months of grant approval.

heading: Climate Change Adaptation Grant
text:
(1) Farmers implementing measures to adapt to the impacts of climate change, such as drought or increased rainfall, may apply for this grant.
(2) Eligible measures include planting climate-resilient crop varieties, investing in advanced drainage systems, or establishing windbreaks. A climate vulnerability assessment of the farm is required.
(3) The grant covers 40% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns. The measures must demonstrate a projected improvement in resilience by at least 15% over a 5-year period.
(4) Annual progress reports on adaptation effectiveness are required. The grant supports long-term farm sustainability.

heading: Farm Energy Efficiency Grant
text:
(1) This grant encourages farmers to invest in energy-efficient equipment and renewable energy sources for their farm operations.
(2) Eligible investments include high-efficiency motors, LED lighting systems, insulation upgrades for farm buildings, or installation of solar panels or small wind turbines for on-farm use. A baseline energy audit is mandatory.
(3) The grant covers 30% of verifiable costs, up to a maximum of 18,000 crowns per farm. The investment must result in a documented energy saving of at least 20% annually.
(4) Energy consumption reports must be submitted for 3 years post-installation.

heading: Farm Energy Efficiency Grant
text:
(1) This grant encourages farmers to invest in energy-efficient equipment and renewable energy sources for their farm operations.
(2) Eligible investments include high-efficiency motors, LED lighting systems, insulation upgrades for farm buildings, or installation of solar panels or small wind turbines for on-farm use. A baseline energy audit by a certified professional is mandatory.
(3) The grant covers 35% of verifiable costs, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns per farm. The investment must result in a documented energy saving of at least 25% annually.
(4) Energy consumption reports must be submitted for 5 years post-installation. Failure to meet the energy saving target may lead to a penalty of 10% of the grant amount.

heading: Pest and Disease Management Grant
text:
(1) Farmers implementing integrated pest and disease management (IPDM) strategies to reduce reliance on chemical treatments may apply for this grant.
(2) Eligible activities include biological control methods, pest-resistant crop varieties, precision application technologies, or monitoring systems. A pest and disease assessment plan is required.
(3) The grant covers 40% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. The IPDM strategy must demonstrate a reduction in pesticide use by at least 20% within 2 years of implementation.
(4) Records of pesticide use and pest incidence must be maintained for 3 years.

heading: Pest and Disease Management Grant
text:
(1) Farmers implementing advanced integrated pest and disease management (IPDM) strategies to significantly reduce reliance on chemical treatments may apply for this grant.
(2) Eligible activities include biological control methods, genetically resistant crop varieties, advanced precision application technologies, or comprehensive monitoring and early warning systems. A detailed pest and disease risk assessment and management plan is required.
(3) The grant covers 45% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 12,000 crowns. The IPDM strategy must demonstrate a reduction in synthetic pesticide use by at least 25% within 2 years of implementation and maintain this reduction for 3 years.
(4) Comprehensive records of pesticide use and pest incidence, including photographs where relevant, must be maintained for 5 years and be available for Ministry inspection at any time.

heading: Farm Tourism Development Grant
text:
(1) This grant supports farmers diversifying their income through farm tourism activities, such as farm stays, educational tours, or agri-culinary experiences.
(2) Eligible expenses include renovation of facilities for visitors, development of interpretive materials, or marketing campaigns for farm tourism. The farm must commit to operating tourism activities for at least 3 years.
(3) The grant covers 30% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns. A detailed business plan for farm tourism, including visitor projections and financial forecasts, is required.
(4) The tourism offering must launch within 12 months of grant approval.

heading: Rural Accessibility Improvement Grant
text:
(1) This grant assists farmers in improving access to their farms, benefiting both farm operations and rural communities.
(2) Eligible improvements include repair or upgrade of farm access roads, installation of new signage, or improvements to culverts. The improvements must primarily serve agricultural purposes but may also benefit public access.
(3) The grant covers 50% of documented costs, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. A road condition assessment report from a qualified engineer is required.
(4) All improvements must adhere to municipal infrastructure standards and be completed within 9 months.

heading: Certification and Quality Assurance Grant
text:
(1) Farmers seeking to obtain or maintain recognized quality assurance certifications for their products may apply for this grant.
(2) Eligible certifications include food safety standards (e.g., HACCP), regional product designations, or specific environmental labels. The certification must be from an internationally recognized or Nordvale-approved body.
(3) The grant covers 60% of certification fees and associated audit costs, up to a maximum of 7,000 crowns per certification. A farm may claim this grant for up to two different certifications every 5 years.
(4) Proof of certification and invoices for fees are required for reimbursement within 45 days of payment.

heading: Data Collection and Reporting
text:
(1) All farmers receiving grants under this Act are required to maintain accurate records pertinent to their grant activities for a minimum of 5 years.
(2) These records include financial statements, production logs, input purchase receipts, and any other documentation specified in the individual grant sections.
(3) The Ministry reserves the right to request these records at any time for auditing purposes. Failure to provide complete and accurate records may result in the suspension or repayment of grants, plus a 10% administrative fee.
(4) Annual activity reports, outlining grant usage and outcomes, must be submitted by March 31st of the following year.

heading: Compliance and Inspections
text:
(1) The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development shall conduct regular and unannounced inspections of farms receiving grants to ensure compliance with the terms and conditions of this Act.
(2) Inspections may involve on-site visits, review of records, and interviews with farm personnel. Farmers must cooperate fully with all Ministry officials.
(3) Any non-compliance identified during an inspection may lead to sanctions, including the withholding of future grant payments, partial or full repayment of previously disbursed funds, and penalties of up to 20% of the grant amount.
(4) Findings of non-compliance will be communicated in writing within 30 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been denied or whose grant has been revoked may appeal the decision to the Agricultural Appeals Tribunal.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the Ministry's decision, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any supporting documentation. A non-refundable appeal fee of 500 crowns is required.
(3) The Tribunal shall review the appeal and render a decision within 90 days. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding.
(4) The Tribunal may request additional information or hold a hearing if deemed necessary. Legal representation is permitted.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) All personal and financial information submitted by applicants under this Act shall be treated with strict confidentiality by the Ministry and its agents.
(2) Such information shall be used solely for the purpose of assessing grant applications, administering grants, and conducting audits related to this Act.
(3) Information may be shared with other government departments only where legally required or with the explicit written consent of the applicant. Aggregate, anonymized data may be used for statistical reporting.
(4) The Ministry shall implement robust data protection measures to safeguard all submitted information in accordance with Nordvale's data privacy regulations.

heading: Prohibition of Duplication
text:
(1) A farmer may not receive multiple grants or subsidies from the Ministry or any other government body for the exact same activity, investment, or outcome during the same period.
(2) Applicants must declare any other government funding received or applied for, related to the activities proposed in their application for a grant under this Act. Failure to disclose such information constitutes fraud.
(3) Where overlap is identified, the Ministry will request clarification and may adjust or deny the application to prevent double funding. The farmer will be notified within 21 days.
(4) This provision ensures fair distribution of public funds and prevents excessive subsidization of single projects.

heading: Fraud and Misrepresentation
text:
(1) Any applicant or recipient of a grant under this Act who knowingly provides false or misleading information, or attempts to defraud the Ministry, shall be subject to severe penalties.
(2) Penalties may include immediate revocation of all grants, full repayment of all funds received plus a penalty of 50% of the disbursed amount, and prosecution under Nordvale's criminal code. Such actions may also result in disqualification from all future government support for a period of 10 years.
(3) The Ministry will investigate all allegations of fraud thoroughly. Reports of suspected fraud can be submitted anonymously. All evidence will be reviewed by a special investigative unit.
(4) Evidence of criminal intent will be forwarded to the Public Prosecutor's Office without delay.

heading: Amendment of Regulations
text:
(1) The Ministry may, from time to time, amend the regulations pertaining to the administration of this Act, including application forms, reporting requirements, and specific eligibility criteria.
(2) Any amendments shall be published in the Nordvale Government Gazette and on the Ministry's official website at least 60 days before coming into effect. Public consultations may be held for significant changes.
(3) Existing grant agreements will generally not be affected by subsequent amendments, unless explicitly stated in the amendment and with due notice to all affected parties, at least 90 days in advance.
(4) Farmers are encouraged to regularly consult the Ministry's publications for updates.

heading: Financial Allocation and Budget
text:
(1) Funds for grants and subsidies under this Act are allocated annually through the national budget process of Nordvale. The total budget for agricultural subsidies will be publicly announced by October 31st each year for the subsequent fiscal year.
(2) The Ministry of Finance, in consultation with the Ministry of Agriculture, determines the total amount available. Allocations to specific grant programs may vary each year based on governmental priorities and economic conditions.
(3) Applications will be processed on a first-come, first-served basis within each grant category until the allocated funds for that category are exhausted.
(4) The Ministry aims to disburse 95% of approved funds within 90 days of application approval.

heading: Review and Evaluation
text:
(1) This Act and its effectiveness shall be reviewed by the Ministry every 5 years to assess its impact on agricultural productivity, environmental sustainability, and farmer livelihoods.
(2) The review will involve collecting data, conducting stakeholder consultations, and commissioning independent reports. The first review is scheduled for 2023.
(3) Recommendations from the review may lead to amendments to this Act or the introduction of new grant programs. A public report on the findings of each review will be published.
(4) The review process ensures that the Act remains relevant and responsive to the evolving needs of Nordvale's agricultural sector.

heading: Disbursement Procedures
text:
(1) Approved grant funds shall be disbursed directly to the applicant's designated bank account via electronic transfer.
(2) Applicants must provide valid bank account details at the time of application. Any changes to bank details must be communicated to the Ministry in writing at least 14 days prior to a scheduled disbursement.
(3) Payments will typically be made within 60 days of application approval, or according to the specific installment schedule outlined in the relevant grant section.
(4) The Ministry is not responsible for delays caused by incorrect banking information provided by the applicant.

heading: Publicity of Grants
text:
(1) The Ministry shall publish an annual list of all grant recipients, including their names (for individuals or farm entities), the municipality where the farm is located, the specific grant received, and the total amount disbursed.
(2) This information will be made available on the Ministry's official website by December 31st each year. This promotes transparency and accountability in the use of public funds.
(3) Information deemed sensitive, such as detailed financial statements, will not be publicly disclosed. Only the essential details for public accountability will be published.
(4) Recipients implicitly agree to this publicity requirement upon accepting grant funds.

heading: Farm Safety Improvement Grant (Repealed)
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: The book allowance is reduced by 30 days for any registered chimney-sweep master, who shall instead have that period to pay the annual book allowance of 110 crowns, which is paid in September per person.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a registered certified falconry instructor, the annual waste service charge for their dwelling shall be half the amount otherwise due for their container size.

heading: Concessions
text: An accredited sign-language interpreter shall receive an annual energy rebate equal to 75% of the fee or allowance specified in HOA §6.

heading: Leisure subscriptions
text:
(1) In every Act, 'leisure subscription' means a personal right to use a public bath for swimmers or a gymnasium, run by a municipality, as often as the holder wishes during a fixed term of 30 days or of 365 days.
(2) A leisure subscription is named by its term, as a leisure subscription of 30 days or of 365 days.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for levying fees for the use of air traffic control services within the Republic of Nordvale's airspace. The fees collected are intended to cover the operational costs, maintenance, and development of air traffic control infrastructure and services. All aircraft operating within controlled airspace are subject to the provisions of this Act, ensuring fair and consistent application of charges across all users. The regulations outlined herein apply uniformly to both domestic and international flights utilizing Nordvale's air traffic control resources.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Air traffic control services" means the services provided by the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority for the safe and efficient movement of aircraft.
(2) "Aircraft" means any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from the reactions of the air other than the reactions of the air against the earth's surface.
(3) "Operator" means the person or entity responsible for the operation of an aircraft.
(4) "Controlled airspace" refers to airspace of defined dimensions within which air traffic control service is provided.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: General Fee Principle
text: Fees for air traffic control services shall be levied on all operators whose aircraft utilize controlled airspace within the Republic of Nordvale. These fees are designed to be cost-reflective, ensuring that the financial burden of providing these essential services is shared equitably among users. The methodology for calculating these fees considers factors such as aircraft weight, flight distance, and the type of service consumed. Exemptions or reductions may apply under specific circumstances as detailed in later sections of this Act.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Calculation Basis
text: The primary basis for calculating air traffic control service fees shall be the maximum certificated take-off weight (MTOW) of the aircraft, measured in metric tonnes, and the distance flown within Nordvale's controlled airspace, measured in nautical miles. A base rate per tonne-nautical mile will be established annually by the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority. Additional charges may apply for specific services, such as approach and departure control, as outlined in section 7. The minimum chargeable weight for any aircraft is 2.5 tonnes.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Standard En-Route Fee
text: The standard en-route fee for air traffic control services shall be 0.75 crowns per tonne-nautical mile. This rate applies to all aircraft transiting through Nordvale's controlled airspace without landing or taking off from a Nordvale airport. The calculation is based on the aircraft's MTOW and the great circle distance flown. For flights exceeding 500 nautical miles within Nordvale's airspace, a 5% discount on the portion of the fee exceeding this distance may be applied. The minimum en-route fee for any flight is 250 crowns.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Approach and Departure Fee – Class A Airports
text: An approach and departure fee shall be levied for each landing at or take-off from a Class A airport. This fee covers the specific air traffic control services provided during these critical phases of flight. The fee is calculated at a flat rate of 1,500 crowns per movement, plus an additional 15 crowns per tonne of the aircraft's MTOW. This applies to all aircraft with an MTOW greater than 5 tonnes. Aircraft with an MTOW of 5 tonnes or less are subject to a reduced flat fee of 500 crowns per movement.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Approach and Departure Fee – Class A Airports
text: An approach and departure fee shall be levied for each landing at or take-off from a Class A airport. This fee covers the specific air traffic control services provided during these critical phases of flight. The fee is calculated at a flat rate of 1,750 crowns per movement, plus an additional 18 crowns per tonne of the aircraft's MTOW. This applies to all aircraft with an MTOW greater than 4 tonnes. Aircraft with an MTOW of 4 tonnes or less are subject to a reduced flat fee of 600 crowns per movement.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Approach and Departure Fee – Class B Airports
text: For landings at or take-offs from a Class B airport, a distinct approach and departure fee shall be applied. This fee acknowledges the slightly reduced complexity of air traffic control services at these facilities compared to Class A airports. The fee is set at a flat rate of 900 crowns per movement, along with an additional 10 crowns per tonne of the aircraft's MTOW. This fee applies to all aircraft with an MTOW greater than 3 tonnes. Aircraft with an MTOW of 3 tonnes or less are charged a flat fee of 300 crowns per movement.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Overflight Surcharge
text: An overflight surcharge of 10% shall be added to the standard en-route fee for aircraft that do not land or take off within Nordvale's territory, but solely transit through its controlled airspace. This surcharge reflects the administrative costs associated with international coordination and tracking of such flights. The surcharge is calculated on the total en-route fee determined in section 5. This surcharge does not apply to flights that make an unscheduled landing due to an emergency, provided the emergency is duly reported.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Overflight Surcharge
text: An overflight surcharge of 12% shall be added to the standard en-route fee for aircraft that do not land or take off within Nordvale's territory, but solely transit through its controlled airspace. This surcharge reflects the administrative costs associated with international coordination and tracking of such flights. The surcharge is calculated on the total en-route fee determined in section 5. This surcharge does not apply to flights that make an unscheduled landing due to an emergency, provided the emergency is duly reported and verified by the Air Navigation Authority.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Late Payment Penalty
text: Invoices for air traffic control services are due within 30 days of the invoice date. A penalty for late payment shall be applied at a rate of 2% of the outstanding amount per month, compounded monthly, for any invoice not settled within 30 days. After 90 days, an additional administrative fee of 500 crowns may be imposed. Continued failure to pay may result in restrictions on future flight operations within Nordvale's airspace, as outlined in section 25.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Reductions for Training Flights
text: Recognizing the importance of pilot training, a fee reduction of 40% shall apply to flights specifically conducted for pilot training purposes. This reduction is applicable only if the flight is clearly designated as a training flight in its flight plan and is conducted within designated training areas or specific routes approved by the Air Navigation Authority. This reduction applies to both en-route and approach/departure fees. The aircraft must have an MTOW of less than 15 tonnes to qualify for this reduction.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Reductions for Training Flights
text: Recognizing the importance of pilot training, a fee reduction of 35% shall apply to flights specifically conducted for pilot training purposes. This reduction is applicable only if the flight is clearly designated as a training flight in its flight plan and is conducted within designated training areas or specific routes approved by the Air Navigation Authority. This reduction applies to both en-route and approach/departure fees. The aircraft must have an MTOW of less than 12 tonnes to qualify for this reduction.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Exemption for Search and Rescue
text: Aircraft engaged in officially sanctioned search and rescue (SAR) operations within Nordvale's controlled airspace are exempt from all air traffic control service fees. This exemption applies to both the aircraft performing the SAR mission and any supporting aircraft directly involved in the operation. To qualify for this exemption, the SAR operation must be coordinated with and approved by the appropriate Nordvale authorities. This exemption extends to all phases of flight related to the SAR mission.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Exemption for State Aircraft
text: Aircraft owned and operated by the Government of Nordvale or its official agencies, performing non-commercial governmental duties, are exempt from all air traffic control service fees. This exemption specifically covers flights undertaken for official state business, emergency response, or national security. It does not extend to flights chartered by government entities for commercial purposes. The aircraft must carry appropriate identification and the flight must be declared as a state flight in its flight plan.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Exemption for State Aircraft
text: Aircraft owned and operated by the Government of Nordvale or its official agencies, performing non-commercial governmental duties, are exempt from all air traffic control service fees. This exemption specifically covers flights undertaken for official state business, emergency response, or national security. It does not extend to flights chartered by government entities or commercial operations. The aircraft must carry appropriate identification, and the flight must be declared as a state flight in its flight plan, subject to verification by the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Adjustment for Night Flights
text: A supplementary fee of 15% shall be added to all air traffic control services provided during night hours, defined as between 22:00 and 06:00 local time. This adjustment accounts for the increased operational costs associated with night-time air traffic control staffing and specialized equipment. The night flight adjustment applies to both en-route and approach/departure fees. Flights delayed into or out of this period due to unforeseen circumstances or emergencies may apply for a waiver of this supplementary fee within 7 days of the flight.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Adjustment for Night Flights
text: A supplementary fee of 20% shall be added to all air traffic control services provided during night hours, defined as between 22:00 and 06:00 local time. This adjustment accounts for the increased operational costs associated with night-time air traffic control staffing and specialized equipment. The night flight adjustment applies to both en-route and approach/departure fees. Flights delayed into or out of this period due to unforeseen circumstances or emergencies may apply for a waiver of this supplementary fee within 5 days of the flight. No waiver will be granted for delays less than 60 minutes.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee Adjustment for Peak Hours
text: During peak operational hours, defined as 08:00 to 10:00 and 17:00 to 19:00 local time, an additional 8% surcharge shall be applied to all air traffic control services. This surcharge is intended to manage demand during periods of high traffic density and to contribute towards the enhanced resources required. This applies to both arrivals and departures at all controlled airports. Exemptions may be granted for humanitarian aid flights or flights experiencing emergency diversions, subject to immediate notification to air traffic control.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Invoice Issuance
text: The Nordvale Air Navigation Authority shall issue invoices to operators for air traffic control services rendered on a monthly basis. Each invoice will detail the services provided, the calculation of fees, and the total amount due in crowns. Invoices will typically be dispatched within 10 days of the end of each calendar month. Operators may request an itemized breakdown of services within 14 days of receiving an invoice. Digital invoices are the preferred method of delivery, unless otherwise requested.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees levied under this Act shall be payable in Nordvale crowns. Accepted payment methods include bank transfer, direct debit, and major credit cards. Operators may also establish pre-payment accounts with the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority, subject to an initial minimum deposit of 10,000 crowns. Payments must be received by the due date specified on the invoice. Any transaction fees incurred by the operator for payment processing are the sole responsibility of the operator.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Operators wishing to dispute an invoice or fee calculation must submit a written appeal to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority within 21 days of the invoice date. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for dispute and provide all relevant supporting documentation. The Authority will review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days. During the review period, the disputed portion of the invoice is not subject to late payment penalties, provided the undisputed portion is paid by the due date.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Record Keeping
text: The Nordvale Air Navigation Authority shall maintain accurate records of all air traffic control services provided, including flight details, aircraft identification, and calculated fees, for a minimum period of 7 years. Operators are also required to retain their flight logs and relevant operational data for a period of at least 3 years to facilitate potential audits or dispute resolution. Failure to provide requested records by an operator within 30 days may result in a default judgment on any disputed fees.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Annual Fee Review
text: The Nordvale Air Navigation Authority shall conduct an annual review of all air traffic control service fees and surcharges, to ensure they remain cost-reflective and aligned with operational expenses. Any proposed changes to fee rates shall be published for public consultation for a period of at least 60 days before implementation. New fee schedules, if approved, will typically come into effect on January 1st of the following year. Minor adjustments of less than 5% may be implemented with 30 days' notice.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Reporting Requirements for Operators
text: Operators are required to provide accurate and timely flight plan information to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority before entering Nordvale's controlled airspace. This includes, but is not limited to, aircraft type, MTOW, origin, destination, and estimated times of arrival and departure. Any significant deviations from the filed flight plan, including changes in destination or unexpected delays exceeding 30 minutes, must be reported to air traffic control immediately. Failure to provide accurate information may result in a surcharge of 1,000 crowns per incident.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Reporting Requirements for Operators (Revised)
text: Operators are required to provide accurate and timely flight plan information to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority before entering Nordvale's controlled airspace. This includes, but is not limited to, aircraft type, MTOW, origin, destination, and estimated times of arrival and departure. Any significant deviations from the filed flight plan, including changes in destination or unexpected delays exceeding 20 minutes, must be reported to air traffic control immediately. Failure to provide accurate information may result in a surcharge of 1,200 crowns per incident, or 1,500 crowns for repeated offenses.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Reporting Requirements for Operators (Revised)
text: Operators are required to provide accurate and timely flight plan information to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority before entering Nordvale's controlled airspace. This includes, but is not limited to, aircraft type, MTOW, origin, destination, and estimated times of arrival and departure. Any significant deviations from the filed flight plan, including changes in destination or unexpected delays exceeding 15 minutes, must be reported to air traffic control immediately. Failure to provide accurate information may result in a surcharge of 1,500 crowns per incident, or 2,000 crowns for repeated offenses within a 6-month period.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Special Services Fee
text: A special services fee may be levied for specific air traffic control services requested by an operator that fall outside the scope of standard en-route or approach/departure services. These may include, but are not limited to, extended holding patterns for non-operational reasons, specific routing requests for scenic flights, or dedicated air traffic control support for aerial work. The fee for such services will be determined on a case-by-case basis, with a minimum charge of 2,000 crowns per hour or part thereof, and must be agreed upon in advance.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Exemption for Humanitarian Flights
text: Aircraft engaged in officially recognized humanitarian aid missions, including disaster relief or medical evacuation flights, are exempt from all air traffic control service fees. This exemption applies provided the flight is operated by a registered humanitarian organization and is explicitly declared as a humanitarian flight in its flight plan. The Nordvale Air Navigation Authority reserves the right to request proof of the mission's humanitarian nature. This exemption does not extend to commercial cargo flights transporting aid.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Exemption for Humanitarian Flights
text: Aircraft engaged in officially recognized humanitarian aid missions, including disaster relief or medical evacuation flights, are exempt from all air traffic control service fees. This exemption applies provided the flight is operated by a registered humanitarian organization and is explicitly declared as a humanitarian flight in its flight plan and is coordinated with the Ministry of Aid. The Nordvale Air Navigation Authority reserves the right to request proof of the mission's humanitarian nature. This exemption does not extend to commercial cargo flights transporting aid, unless chartered directly by the Nordvale government.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Exemption for Diplomatic Flights
text: Aircraft operating under diplomatic clearance, carrying official diplomatic personnel or materials, are exempt from all air traffic control service fees. This exemption applies to flights that are explicitly designated as diplomatic flights and have received the necessary diplomatic clearances from the Nordvale Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The exemption covers both en-route and approach/departure services. Any claims for this exemption must be supported by appropriate documentation. The exemption does not apply to flights carrying commercial passengers even if they include diplomatic personnel.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Confidentiality of Operator Data
text: All operational and financial data provided by operators to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority for fee calculation and billing purposes shall be treated with strict confidentiality. This information will not be disclosed to third parties, except as required by law or with the express consent of the operator. Aggregate, anonymized data may be used for statistical analysis and reporting, provided individual operators cannot be identified. Breaches of confidentiality by Authority staff will be subject to disciplinary action.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Enforcement Powers
text: In cases of persistent non-payment of air traffic control service fees, the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority is empowered to impose restrictions on an operator's ability to utilize Nordvale's controlled airspace. This may include, but is not limited to, denial of entry, refusal of flight clearances, or the grounding of aircraft within Nordvale's territory. Such measures will only be taken after all avenues of dispute resolution have been exhausted and at least 120 days have passed since the initial invoice due date. A written warning will be issued 30 days prior to any enforcement action.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Application for Refunds
text: Operators may apply for a refund of fees paid in error or due to overbilling. Applications for refunds must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority within 90 days of the payment date or the date the error was discovered, whichever is later. The application must include full details of the overpayment and supporting documentation. Valid refunds will be processed within 60 days of approval. No refunds will be issued for amounts less than 100 crowns.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Application for Refunds
text: Operators may apply for a refund of fees paid in error or due to overbilling. Applications for refunds must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority within 60 days of the payment date or the date the error was discovered, whichever is later. The application must include full details of the overpayment and supporting documentation. Valid refunds will be processed within 45 days of approval. No refunds will be issued for amounts less than 150 crowns, unless the error was caused by the Authority itself.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Waiver of Fees for Emergency Landings
text: Aircraft making an unscheduled landing at a Nordvale airport due to a declared in-flight emergency are exempt from approach and departure fees for that specific emergency landing and subsequent take-off, provided the take-off occurs within 24 hours. This exemption applies only if the emergency is formally declared to air traffic control and is not a result of operator negligence. Any additional air traffic control services beyond the immediate emergency response may still incur charges.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Development Fund Contribution
text: A portion of the collected air traffic control service fees, specifically 5% of all en-route fees, shall be allocated to the Nordvale Air Navigation Development Fund. This fund is dedicated to financing significant upgrades, research, and modernization projects for air traffic control infrastructure and technology across the Republic. The fund's expenditure is overseen by a committee appointed by the Minister of Transport. This contribution is mandatory and applies to all applicable fees before any discounts or surcharges.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Development Fund Contribution (Revised)
text: A portion of the collected air traffic control service fees, specifically 7% of all en-route fees, shall be allocated to the Nordvale Air Navigation Development Fund. This fund is dedicated to financing significant upgrades, research, and modernization projects for air traffic control infrastructure and technology across the Republic. The fund's expenditure is overseen by a committee appointed by the Minister of Transport. This contribution is mandatory and applies to all applicable fees before any discounts or surcharges are applied. An additional 2% of approach and departure fees for Class A airports will also be contributed to this fund.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee for Use of Navaids
text: A separate fee of 500 crowns per flight shall be levied for each aircraft utilizing Nordvale's ground-based navigational aids (Navaids) for precision approaches or instrument departures. This fee is distinct from other air traffic control service charges and contributes specifically to the maintenance and calibration of these critical systems. This fee is automatically applied to all instrument flight rules (IFR) flights landing or taking off from Class A and Class B airports. Visual flight rules (VFR) flights are exempt.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee for Use of Navaids
text: A separate fee of 650 crowns per flight shall be levied for each aircraft utilizing Nordvale's ground-based navigational aids (Navaids) for precision approaches or instrument departures. This fee is distinct from other air traffic control service charges and contributes specifically to the maintenance and calibration of these critical systems. This fee is automatically applied to all instrument flight rules (IFR) flights landing or taking off from Class A and Class B airports. Visual flight rules (VFR) flights are exempt. Multi-segment flights landing and taking off from the same airport within 60 minutes are only charged once.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Currency Exchange Rates
text: For international operators, fees may be quoted in Nordvale crowns. Conversion from other currencies for payment purposes shall use the official exchange rate published by the Nordvale Central Bank on the date the invoice is issued. Any fluctuations in exchange rates between the invoice date and the payment date are the responsibility of the operator. Overpayments or underpayments due to exchange rate differences of less than 50 crowns will not be adjusted.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Temporary Fee Waivers
text: The Minister of Transport may, in exceptional circumstances, grant temporary fee waivers for specific categories of flights or operators for a period not exceeding 6 months. Such waivers may only be granted in response to national emergencies, significant economic downturns affecting the aviation sector, or to promote new aviation technologies. Any such waiver must be publicly announced at least 14 days prior to its effective date and clearly state the scope and duration of the waiver. A maximum of 10 such waivers can be active concurrently.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Temporary Fee Waivers (Revised)
text: The Minister of Transport may, in exceptional circumstances, grant temporary fee waivers for specific categories of flights or operators for a period not exceeding 9 months. Such waivers may only be granted in response to national emergencies, significant economic downturns affecting the aviation sector, or to promote new aviation technologies. Any such waiver must be publicly announced at least 21 days prior to its effective date and clearly state the scope and duration of the waiver. A maximum of 8 such waivers can be active concurrently.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Temporary Fee Waivers (Revised)
text: The Minister of Transport may, in exceptional circumstances, grant temporary fee waivers for specific categories of flights or operators for a period not exceeding 12 months. Such waivers may only be granted in response to national emergencies, significant economic downturns affecting the aviation sector, or to promote new aviation technologies. Any such waiver must be publicly announced at least 30 days prior to its effective date and clearly state the scope and duration of the waiver. A maximum of 6 such waivers can be active concurrently, and no single waiver can be extended beyond its initial term.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Small Aircraft Fee Cap
text: For aircraft with a maximum certificated take-off weight (MTOW) of 2 tonnes or less, the total air traffic control service fees, including all surcharges, for a single flight (one take-off and one landing) within Nordvale's controlled airspace shall not exceed a cap of 1,500 crowns. This cap is designed to support general aviation and smaller operators. This cap does not apply to international overflights. Multi-segment flights will have the cap applied per segment, provided each segment is less than 200 nautical miles.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Small Aircraft Fee Cap (Repealed)
text: (Repealed.)

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Consolidated Billing
text: Operators with multiple aircraft or frequent operations may apply to the Nordvale Air Navigation Authority for consolidated billing arrangements. Under such an arrangement, all fees incurred by the operator's fleet within a given month will be presented on a single invoice, rather than separate invoices per flight. This is subject to an agreement with the Authority, which may require a minimum number of monthly movements (e.g., 20 movements) and a good payment history over the preceding 12 months. Consolidated invoices are still subject to the same payment terms.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee for Flight Plan Amendment
text: A fee of 150 crowns shall be levied for each amendment to a filed flight plan that is submitted less than 60 minutes prior to the planned take-off time. This fee covers the administrative effort and potential re-sequencing required by air traffic control. No fee applies for amendments made due to unforeseen operational issues such as weather deviations or emergency diversions, provided such issues are promptly communicated and verified by air traffic control. Multiple amendments for the same flight within a 15-minute window will only incur one fee.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Fee for Flight Plan Amendment (Revised)
text: A fee of 200 crowns shall be levied for each amendment to a filed flight plan that is submitted less than 45 minutes prior to the planned take-off time. This fee covers the administrative effort and potential re-sequencing required by air traffic control. No fee applies for amendments made due to unforeseen operational issues such as weather deviations or emergency diversions, provided such issues are promptly communicated and verified by air traffic control. Multiple amendments for the same flight within a 10-minute window will only incur one fee. Amendments made more than once for the same flight will incur an additional 50 crowns for each subsequent amendment.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Compliance Audits
text: The Nordvale Air Navigation Authority reserves the right to conduct periodic compliance audits of operators' flight records and payment histories. Operators shall cooperate fully with these audits, providing all requested documentation within 14 days of a formal request. Audits may be conducted with 30 days' prior notice, though unannounced audits may occur in cases of suspected non-compliance. Any discrepancies identified during an audit that result in underpayment of fees will be subject to retrospective billing, plus a 10% administrative charge on the underpaid amount.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Compliance Audits (Revised)
text: The Nordvale Air Navigation Authority reserves the right to conduct periodic compliance audits of operators' flight records and payment histories. Operators shall cooperate fully with these audits, providing all requested documentation within 10 days of a formal request. Audits may be conducted with 20 days' prior notice, though unannounced audits may occur in cases of suspected non-compliance. Any discrepancies identified during an audit that result in underpayment of fees will be subject to retrospective billing, plus a 15% administrative charge on the underpaid amount. Repeated findings of underpayment within a 2-year period may result in an additional penalty of 5,000 crowns.

act_title: Air Traffic Control Service Fees Act
heading: Daytime noise permits for amateur concerts
text:
(1) The fee for a permit for daytime noise from an open-air concert is one quarter of the ordinary fee if every performer at the concert is a member of the same registered amateur ensemble (HSA §21).
(2) The noise limits and the time for applying for the permit are unchanged.
(3) This section does not apply to a permit for noise during quiet hours.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for setting, reviewing, and enforcing tariffs for air travel services that either begin in Nordvale or conclude in Nordvale. It applies to all commercial passenger and cargo flights, ensuring fair and transparent pricing for consumers and operators alike. The regulations aim to promote competition while safeguarding the economic viability of air carriers operating within Nordvale's jurisdiction. This scope includes flights originating from or destined for Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Tariff Submission Requirements
text:
(1) All air carriers operating within Nordvale must submit their proposed tariffs to the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) at least 90 days prior to their intended effective date.
(2) Submissions must include detailed breakdowns of all charges, fees, and surcharges, clearly delineating fuel costs, operational expenses, and profit margins. Any changes to existing tariffs require a similar 90-day notification period.
(3) Non-compliance with this section may result in a fine of up to 15,000 crowns for each offense.

heading: Tariff Submission Requirements
text:
(1) All air carriers operating within Nordvale must submit their proposed tariffs to the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) at least 120 days prior to their intended effective date.
(2) Submissions must include detailed breakdowns of all charges, fees, and surcharges, clearly delineating fuel costs, operational expenses, and profit margins. Any changes to existing tariffs require a similar 120-day notification period.
(3) Non-compliance with this section may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns for each offense.

heading: Tariff Review Process
text:
(1) The Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) shall review all submitted tariffs within 60 days of receipt.
(2) The review process includes assessing the reasonableness of prices, ensuring compliance with consumer protection guidelines, and evaluating the impact on market competition. The NAA may request additional documentation or clarification from the air carrier during this period.
(3) Tariffs that are deemed excessive or discriminatory may be rejected, requiring resubmission by the carrier within 30 days.

heading: Tariff Review Process
text:
(1) The Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) shall review all submitted tariffs within 45 days of receipt.
(2) The review process includes assessing the reasonableness of prices, ensuring compliance with consumer protection guidelines, and evaluating the impact on market competition. The NAA may request additional documentation or clarification from the air carrier during this period.
(3) Tariffs that are deemed excessive or discriminatory may be rejected, requiring resubmission by the carrier within 20 days. A public consultation period of 10 days will also be mandatory for all new tariff proposals.

heading: Approval of Tariffs
text:
(1) Upon satisfactory review, the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) will issue an approval for the proposed tariffs.
(2) Approved tariffs become legally binding and must be publicly displayed by the air carrier at all points of sale and on their official websites. The approval notice will specify the effective date of the tariffs.
(3) Tariffs are typically approved for a period of 12 months, after which they must be resubmitted for review.

heading: Approval of Tariffs
text:
(1) Upon satisfactory review, the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) will issue an approval for the proposed tariffs.
(2) Approved tariffs become legally binding and must be publicly displayed by the air carrier at all points of sale and on their official websites. The approval notice will specify the effective date of the tariffs.
(3) Tariffs are typically approved for a period of 9 months, after which they must be resubmitted for review. Minor adjustments of up to 5% may be permitted without full resubmission.

heading: Maximum Tariff Increases
text:
(1) Air carriers are permitted to increase their tariffs by a maximum of 8% within any 12-month period without extraordinary justification.
(2) Any proposed increase exceeding this threshold must be accompanied by detailed economic analysis and compelling evidence of significant changes in operational costs, such as a rise in fuel prices exceeding 15% or a currency fluctuation impacting operational expenses by more than 10%.
(3) Such extraordinary increases require a separate, more rigorous review by the Nordvale Aviation Authority.

heading: Maximum Tariff Decrease
text:
(1) Air carriers are permitted to decrease their tariffs by any amount within any 12-month period, provided such decrease does not lead to predatory pricing.
(2) Predatory pricing is defined as offering tariffs below the direct operational cost of the flight for a sustained period of at least 30 days, with the intent to eliminate competition. The Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) reserves the right to investigate any tariff decrease exceeding 25% within a 6-month period.
(3) Violations of predatory pricing rules may result in fines of up to 50,000 crowns and mandatory tariff adjustments.

heading: Consumer Protection
text:
(1) All approved tariffs must include clear information regarding baggage allowances, cancellation policies, and refund procedures.
(2) Air carriers are obligated to honor the tariffs advertised at the time of booking, even if subsequent tariff changes occur before the travel date. Exceptions may apply in cases of government-mandated taxes or fees.
(3) Complaints regarding tariff discrepancies or unfair practices must be addressed by the air carrier within 14 days of receipt. Failure to comply may lead to intervention by the Nordvale Aviation Authority and potential penalties of 10,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Special Promotional Tariffs
text:
(1) Air carriers may offer special promotional tariffs for limited periods, not exceeding 60 days, without a full 90-day submission.
(2) These promotional tariffs must be clearly marked as such and cannot be lower than 50% of the standard approved tariff for the same route.
(3) Notification of promotional tariffs must be provided to the Nordvale Aviation Authority at least 15 days in advance of their launch. This notification must detail the duration and specific conditions of the promotion.
(4) Each carrier is limited to 4 such promotions per route per year.

heading: Fuel Surcharges
text:
(1) Fuel surcharges may only be applied if there is a demonstrated increase in global aviation fuel prices exceeding 10% over a 30-day period.
(2) The surcharge must be directly proportional to the increase in fuel costs and cannot exceed 15% of the base tariff.
(3) Air carriers must provide detailed calculations to the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) for approval before implementing any fuel surcharge. Such surcharges must be clearly itemized on tickets and invoices.

heading: Airport Departure Fees
text:
(1) Airport departure fees for passengers departing from any Nordvale airport are set at 250 crowns per passenger.
(2) For flights originating from Aldmark, this fee is increased to 300 crowns due to higher operational costs at the capital's main airport. Children under the age of two are exempt from this fee.
(3) These fees are collected by the air carrier at the time of ticket purchase and remitted to the respective airport authorities within 15 days of collection.

heading: Airport Departure Fees
text:
(1) Airport departure fees for passengers departing from any Nordvale airport are set at 280 crowns per passenger.
(2) For flights originating from Aldmark, this fee is increased to 350 crowns due to higher operational costs at the capital's main airport. Children under the age of five are exempt from this fee.
(3) These fees are collected by the air carrier at the time of ticket purchase and remitted to the respective airport authorities within 10 days of collection.

heading: Airport Arrival Fees
text:
(1) Airport arrival fees for passengers arriving at any Nordvale airport are set at 180 crowns per passenger.
(2) For flights arriving at Aldmark, this fee is increased to 220 crowns. Infants under the age of one are exempt from this fee.
(3) These fees are collected by the air carrier at the time of ticket purchase and remitted to the respective airport authorities within 15 days of collection.

heading: Cargo Tariffs
text:
(1) Tariffs for air cargo services must be submitted to the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) in a similar manner to passenger tariffs.
(2) These submissions must include rates per kilogram or per cubic meter, special handling fees for hazardous materials, and cold chain logistics. The NAA will review cargo tariffs within 75 days of receipt.
(3) Cargo tariffs are typically approved for a period of 18 months. Any increases exceeding 10% within a 6-month period require special justification.

heading: Transparency of Tariffs
text:
(1) Air carriers must ensure that all tariffs, including all mandatory fees and surcharges, are clearly and prominently displayed to the consumer at every stage of the booking process.
(2) The final price presented to the consumer must be inclusive of all non-optional charges, with a detailed breakdown available upon request. Hidden fees are strictly prohibited.
(3) Websites and booking platforms must provide a 'total price' option that reflects all applicable taxes and fees before the final confirmation of purchase. Violations may result in fines of up to 20,000 crowns.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) The Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) shall establish a formal dispute resolution mechanism for consumers regarding tariff-related issues.
(2) Consumers must first attempt to resolve the issue directly with the air carrier. If no satisfactory resolution is reached within 30 days, the consumer may escalate the complaint to the NAA.
(3) The NAA will mediate disputes and may issue binding decisions. Air carriers failing to comply with NAA decisions may face penalties of up to 10,000 crowns per non-compliance.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Air carriers must maintain detailed records of all submitted tariffs, approved tariffs, and actual tariffs charged for a minimum period of three years.
(2) These records must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) upon request, typically within 7 days of the request. Digital records are acceptable, provided they are easily accessible and verifiable.
(3) Failure to maintain accurate records or to provide them upon request may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Air carriers must maintain detailed records of all submitted tariffs, approved tariffs, and actual tariffs charged for a minimum period of five years.
(2) These records must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) upon request, typically within 3 days of the request. Digital records are acceptable, provided they are easily accessible and verifiable.
(3) Failure to maintain accurate records or to provide them upon request may result in a fine of 8,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any air carrier found to be operating with unapproved tariffs or violating any provision of this Act may be subject to significant penalties.
(2) Initial violations may incur a fine of up to 30,000 crowns. Repeat offenses within a 12-month period will result in doubled fines, up to a maximum of 100,000 crowns.
(3) In severe cases of persistent non-compliance, the Nordvale Aviation Authority may temporarily suspend the carrier's operating license for a period of 30 to 90 days.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale legislature every five years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness.
(2) The first review will take place no later than January 1, 2023. Public consultations may be held to gather feedback from air carriers, consumers, and other stakeholders.
(3) Amendments to this Act will be proposed based on the findings of these reviews to adapt to evolving market conditions and technological advancements in air travel.

heading: Exemptions for Charter Flights
text:
(1) Charter flights, specifically those not available to the general public on a scheduled basis, are partially exempt from the standard tariff submission requirements.
(2) For these flights, only a general overview of the pricing structure and any major changes must be submitted to the Nordvale Aviation Authority at least 45 days before the first flight. The NAA will verify that these are indeed non-scheduled services.
(3) However, all consumer protection provisions of this Act, as outlined in section 7, fully apply to charter flight passengers. Fines for non-compliance are capped at 10,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Data Reporting
text:
(1) Air carriers are required to submit quarterly data reports to the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) detailing their average tariffs charged per route, passenger volumes, and cargo tonnage.
(2) These reports are due within 30 days after the end of each quarter. The data collected will be used to monitor market trends and inform future policy decisions.
(3) Failure to submit these reports on time may result in an administrative fee of 2,000 crowns for each week of delay.

heading: Data Reporting
text:
(1) Air carriers are required to submit monthly data reports to the Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) detailing their average tariffs charged per route, passenger volumes, and cargo tonnage.
(2) These reports are due within 15 days after the end of each month. The data collected will be used to monitor market trends and inform future policy decisions.
(3) Failure to submit these reports on time may result in an administrative fee of 3,500 crowns for each week of delay.

heading: Currency Exchange Rates
text:
(1) For international air travel, tariffs may be quoted in a foreign currency, but the equivalent in Nordvale crowns must also be clearly displayed.
(2) Air carriers must use a consistent and verifiable exchange rate, updated at least daily, for all transactions. The exchange rate used must be based on a recognized financial institution's published rates.
(3) Any discrepancy greater than 2% between the displayed crown equivalent and the actual crown charge is considered a violation of transparency, subject to a fine of 7,500 crowns.

heading: Youth Tariffs
text:
(1) Air carriers may offer reduced tariffs for passengers aged between 2 and 12 years, provided the discount is at least 10% off the adult fare.
(2) These youth tariffs must be consistently applied across all routes where such a discount is offered. Proof of age may be required at the time of booking and boarding.
(3) The Nordvale Aviation Authority encourages, but does not mandate, further discounts for children under 2 years of age, beyond the standard infant fare which is typically 10% of the adult fare.

heading: Youth Tariffs
text:
(1) Air carriers may offer reduced tariffs for passengers aged between 2 and 15 years, provided the discount is at least 15% off the adult fare.
(2) These youth tariffs must be consistently applied across all routes where such a discount is offered. Proof of age may be required at the time of booking and boarding.
(3) The Nordvale Aviation Authority encourages, but does not mandate, further discounts for children under 2 years of age, beyond the standard infant fare which is typically 5% of the adult fare.

heading: Senior Citizen Tariffs
text:
(1) Air carriers may offer discounted tariffs for senior citizens, defined as individuals aged 65 years or older.
(2) Any such discount must be a minimum of 5% off the standard adult fare and must be available on at least 50% of the carrier's routes originating or terminating in Nordvale.
(3) Proof of age is required. The details of these senior tariffs must be submitted to the Nordvale Aviation Authority along with regular tariff submissions, as per section 2.

heading: Group Booking Tariffs
text:
(1) Special tariffs may be offered for group bookings of 10 or more passengers traveling together on the same flight.
(2) These group tariffs must be transparently calculated and cannot exceed the total cost of individual tickets by more than 15%. Terms and conditions for group bookings, including cancellation policies, must be clearly stated.
(3) Air carriers must submit the general framework for their group booking tariffs to the Nordvale Aviation Authority for approval every 24 months.

heading: Emergency Surcharges
text:
(1) In cases of national emergency, natural disaster, or unforeseen security threats, the Nordvale Aviation Authority may authorize air carriers to implement temporary emergency surcharges.
(2) Such surcharges must be strictly limited in scope, duration (not exceeding 30 days without review), and amount (maximum 10% of the base fare).
(3) Any proposed emergency surcharge requires immediate approval from the NAA and must be communicated to the public with clear justification. The NAA will review the necessity of the surcharge every 10 days.

heading: Review of Fuel Surcharges
text:
(1) The Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) will conduct a quarterly review of all approved fuel surcharges to ensure they remain justified by prevailing fuel prices.
(2) If fuel prices decrease by more than 8% over a 60-day period, the NAA may mandate a reduction or removal of the surcharge. Air carriers must comply within 7 days of such a directive.
(3) Non-compliance with a mandated reduction may result in a daily fine of 5,000 crowns until the surcharge is adjusted.

heading: Review of Fuel Surcharges
text:
(1) The Nordvale Aviation Authority (NAA) will conduct a monthly review of all approved fuel surcharges to ensure they remain justified by prevailing fuel prices.
(2) If fuel prices decrease by more than 5% over a 30-day period, the NAA may mandate a reduction or removal of the surcharge. Air carriers must comply within 5 days of such a directive.
(3) Non-compliance with a mandated reduction may result in a daily fine of 7,000 crowns until the surcharge is adjusted.

heading: Special Exemptions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Environmental Levies
text:
(1) An environmental levy of 50 crowns is applied to all departing passengers from Nordvale as of January 1, 2018.
(2) This levy is intended to fund initiatives for sustainable aviation and carbon offset programs within Nordvale. The funds are remitted to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(3) Air carriers are responsible for collecting this levy and remitting it quarterly. Failure to remit on time may incur a penalty of 1% of the outstanding amount per month.

heading: Environmental Levies
text:
(1) An environmental levy of 75 crowns is applied to all departing passengers from Nordvale as of October 16, 2026.
(2) This levy is intended to fund initiatives for sustainable aviation and carbon offset programs within Nordvale, with 20% specifically allocated to research into alternative fuels. The funds are remitted to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(3) Air carriers are responsible for collecting this levy and remitting it monthly. Failure to remit on time may incur a penalty of 1.5% of the outstanding amount per month, with a minimum penalty of 500 crowns.

heading: Implementation of Digital Tariffs
text:
(1) Air carriers are encouraged to utilize digital platforms for the submission and display of tariffs.
(2) The Nordvale Aviation Authority will provide guidelines for digital tariff submission to ensure standardization and compatibility. Digital tariffs must be easily searchable and accessible to the public.
(3) A pilot program for fully digital tariff management will commence on July 1, 2019, involving select air carriers operating out of Brenholt and Corvik, lasting for 12 months.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered holder of a meteorological observer badge shall pay a fixed 5 crowns instead of the fee or allowance specified in SSA §13.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any certified ski patroller shall pay no fee or allowance as described in SBA §8.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act protects the welfare of animals kept by people in Nordvale.
(2) It applies to pets, farm animals and animals kept for sale.
(3) Wild animals are protected only where this Act says so.

heading: Duty of care
text:
(1) A person who keeps an animal shall give it enough food, clean water and shelter.
(2) A person shall not cause an animal unnecessary suffering.
(3) A keeper shall have a sick or injured animal examined by a veterinarian without undue delay.

heading: Minimum space for caged animals
text:
(1) A rabbit shall have at least 2 square metres of living space.
(2) A guinea pig shall have at least 1 square metre of living space.
(3) The animal shall be allowed outside the cage for at least 2 hours each day.

heading: Minimum space for caged animals
text:
(1) A rabbit shall have at least 3 square metres of living space.
(2) A guinea pig shall have at least 1.5 square metres of living space.
(3) The animal shall be allowed outside the cage for at least 2 hours each day.

heading: Dogs left alone
text:
(1) A dog shall not be left alone for more than 8 hours in any 24 hours.
(2) A puppy younger than 6 months shall not be left alone for more than 4 hours.
(3) A dog shall have access to water whenever it is left alone.

heading: Cats left alone
text:
(1) A cat shall not be left alone for more than 24 hours.
(2) A kitten younger than 6 months shall not be left alone for more than 8 hours.
(3) A cat shall have access to water and a litter tray whenever it is left alone.

heading: Transport of animals
text:
(1) An animal shall not be transported for more than 8 hours without a rest of at least 1 hour.
(2) The vehicle shall be ventilated and shall protect the animal from extreme heat and cold.
(3) A pregnant animal in the last 10 percent of its pregnancy shall not be transported.

heading: Transport of animals
text:
(1) An animal shall not be transported for more than 6 hours without a rest of at least 1 hour.
(2) The vehicle shall be ventilated and shall protect the animal from extreme heat and cold.
(3) A pregnant animal in the last 10 percent of its pregnancy shall not be transported.

heading: Pet shops
text:
(1) A person who sells animals as a business shall register with the Animal Welfare Board.
(2) A pet shop shall not sell a dog or cat younger than 8 weeks.
(3) A pet shop shall keep a record of every animal sold for at least 3 years.

heading: Breeding
text:
(1) A person who breeds more than 3 litters of dogs or cats in a calendar year shall report this to the Animal Welfare Board.
(2) A female dog shall not be bred more than once in 12 months.
(3) A breeder shall not breed an animal that is under 18 months of age.

heading: Microchipping
text:
(1) A dog shall be microchipped before it reaches the age of 12 weeks.
(2) A cat shall be microchipped before it reaches the age of 6 months.
(3) The keeper shall register the microchip number with the Animal Welfare Board within 14 days.

heading: Microchipping
text:
(1) A dog shall be microchipped before it reaches the age of 10 weeks.
(2) A cat shall be microchipped before it reaches the age of 6 months.
(3) The keeper shall register the microchip number with the Animal Welfare Board within 14 days.

heading: Vaccination
text:
(1) A dog shall be vaccinated against rabies every 3 years.
(2) A cat that goes outdoors shall be vaccinated against rabies every 3 years.
(3) The keeper shall keep the vaccination record and show it to an inspector on request.

heading: Farm animal outdoor access
text:
(1) A cow shall be allowed outdoors for at least 120 days in each year.
(2) A pig shall be allowed outdoors for at least 60 days in each year.
(3) These days need not be consecutive.

heading: Slaughter
text:
(1) An animal shall be stunned before it is killed.
(2) A person who kills animals as a business shall hold a certificate from the Animal Welfare Board.
(3) The certificate is valid for 4 years.

heading: Animal shelters
text:
(1) A municipality with at least 10,000 inhabitants shall provide an animal shelter or contract with one.
(2) A shelter shall keep a found animal for at least 21 days before rehoming it.
(3) A shelter shall publish a notice of each found animal within 3 days.

heading: Stray animals
text:
(1) A person who finds a stray animal shall report it to the municipality within 48 hours.
(2) The municipality shall pay the finder 10 crowns for each reported animal that it collects.
(3) A finder who keeps the animal without reporting it commits an offence.

heading: Stray animals
text:
(1) A person who finds a stray animal shall report it to the municipality within 48 hours.
(2) The municipality shall pay the finder 15 crowns for each reported animal that it collects.
(3) A finder who keeps the animal without reporting it commits an offence.

heading: Animal Welfare Board
text:
(1) The Animal Welfare Board supervises the application of this Act.
(2) The Board has 7 members appointed for terms of 4 years.
(3) The Board shall publish an annual report by 31 March.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) An inspector may enter premises where animals are kept between 08:00 and 18:00.
(2) The inspector shall give at least 24 hours notice unless cruelty is suspected.
(3) The inspector may order immediate treatment of an animal in need.

heading: Show animals and circuses
text:
(1) A circus shall not use wild animals in performances.
(2) A person who exhibits animals at a show shall give each animal a rest of at least 30 minutes after every 2 hours.
(3) The Animal Welfare Board may inspect a show at any time.

heading: Show animals and circuses
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Fines for neglect
text:
