(1) A person who neglects an animal in breach of section 2 shall pay a fine of 200 crowns.
(2) For a repeat offence within 2 years the fine is 400 crowns.
(3) The fine is imposed by the Animal Welfare Board.

heading: Fines for neglect
text:
(1) A person who neglects an animal in breach of section 2 shall pay a fine of 250 crowns.
(2) For a repeat offence within 2 years the fine is 500 crowns.
(3) The fine is imposed by the Animal Welfare Board.

heading: Ban on keeping animals
text:
(1) A court may ban a person from keeping animals for a period of 1 to 10 years.
(2) The Animal Welfare Board may ask the court to impose the ban.
(3) A person who keeps an animal during a ban shall pay a fine of 600 crowns.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision of the Animal Welfare Board may appeal within 30 days.
(2) The appeal shall be decided within 60 days.
(3) An appeal does not suspend an order for immediate treatment under section 16.

heading: Specialist visits after a refused donation
text:
(1) A person whom a donation centre of the national blood service has turned away as a donor because of an abnormal test result, and who is referred to a specialist doctor about that result, pays no fee for the first specialist visit about it.
(2) The referral letter of the donation centre is shown at the visit.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the rules for the construction, extension and completion of buildings in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to keep buildings safe, to protect neighbours, and to make the permit process predictable.
(3) It applies to every municipality of Nordvale.

heading: Building permit required
text:
(1) A person who builds a new building with a floor area of more than 40 square metres must hold a building permit before work starts.
(2) A permit is issued by the municipality where the building will stand.

heading: Building permit required
text:
(1) A person who builds a new building with a floor area of more than 50 square metres must hold a building permit before work starts.
(2) A permit is issued by the municipality where the building will stand.

heading: Building permit fee
text:
(1) The fee for a building permit is 120 crowns plus 2 crowns for each square metre of floor area.
(2) The fee is paid when the application is submitted.

heading: Building permit fee
text:
(1) The fee for a building permit is 140 crowns plus 3 crowns for each square metre of floor area.
(2) The fee is paid when the application is submitted.

heading: Notification of small extensions
text:
(1) An extension of up to 20 square metres to an existing building needs no permit but must be notified to the municipality at least 10 days before work starts.
(2) The notification fee is 35 crowns.

heading: Notification of garden sheds
text:
(1) A garden shed of up to 15 square metres needs no permit but must be notified to the municipality at least 5 days before work starts.
(2) The notification fee is 20 crowns.

heading: Decision period
text:
(1) The municipality must decide on a permit application within 30 days of receiving a complete application.
(2) If the municipality does not decide within that time, the applicant may ask for a decision in writing.

heading: Decision period
text:
(1) The municipality must decide on a permit application within 25 days of receiving a complete application.
(2) If the municipality does not decide within that time, the applicant may ask for a decision in writing.

heading: Appeal period
text: An applicant or a neighbour may appeal against a permit decision within 21 days of the day the decision is published. An appeal does not stop work that has already been permitted unless the appeal board orders it to stop.

heading: Inspection of foundations
text:
(1) The builder must ask for an inspection of the foundations before they are covered.
(2) The municipal inspector must carry out the inspection within 5 working days of the request.

heading: Inspection of roof structure
text:
(1) The builder must ask for an inspection of the roof structure before the roof is covered.
(2) The municipal inspector must carry out the inspection within 7 working days of the request.

heading: Smoke alarms in dwellings
text: Every dwelling must have at least one smoke alarm for each 60 square metres of floor area, and at least one alarm on each floor. The owner of the dwelling must test the alarms once a year.

heading: Fire extinguishers in apartment buildings
text:
(1) An apartment building must have at least one fire extinguisher on each floor.
(2) Each extinguisher must be checked every 12 months and replaced after 10 years.
(3) The owner of the building is responsible for the checks.

heading: Maximum height in residential zones
text: A building in a residential zone may not be higher than 12 metres measured from the ground to the highest point of the roof. Chimneys and antennas are not counted in the height.

heading: Maximum height in residential zones
text: A building in a residential zone may not be higher than 14 metres measured from the ground to the highest point of the roof. Chimneys and antennas are not counted in the height.

heading: Maximum height of fences
text: A fence between two plots may not be higher than 1.8 metres. A fence higher than 1.8 metres needs a notification under section 4 and the written consent of the neighbour.

heading: Minimum distance from the plot boundary
text:
(1) A new building must stand at least 4 metres from the boundary of the plot.
(2) A garden shed under section 5 must stand at least 2 metres from the boundary.

heading: Certificate of completion fee
text:
(1) When a building is finished, the owner must apply for a certificate of completion.
(2) The fee for the certificate is 60 crowns.
(3) The fee is paid when the application is submitted.

heading: Certificate of completion fee
text:
(1) When a building is finished, the owner must apply for a certificate of completion.
(2) The fee for the certificate is 75 crowns.
(3) The fee is paid when the application is submitted.

heading: Lapse of permit
text: A building permit lapses if work has not started within 12 months of the day the permit was issued, or if the building is not finished within 36 months of that day.

heading: Penalty for building without a permit
text: A person who builds a building that needs a permit under section 2 without holding one must pay a penalty of 500 crowns. The municipality may also order the building to be removed within 60 days.

heading: Penalty for ignoring a stop order
text: A person who continues building after the municipality has issued a stop order must pay a penalty of 800 crowns. The penalty is charged again for each further 30 days in which work continues.

heading: Temporary structures
text: A temporary structure that stands for no more than 90 days needs no building permit but must be notified to the municipality at least 3 days before it is put up and must be taken down when the 90 days end.

heading: Temporary structures
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Keeping of building records
text: The municipality must keep every permit decision, inspection report and certificate of completion for 10 years after the building is completed, and must give the owner a copy on request.

heading: Schedule of highland settlements
Schedule of highland settlements
Roadside waste collection in highland settlements
text:
(1) In a highland settlement residual waste is collected from a shared roadside point and not from each dwelling.
(2) For that reason the annual waste service charge under WSA §7 for a dwelling in a highland settlement is reduced by one quarter.
(3) The reduction is shown on the yearly invoice and needs no application.

heading: Roadside waste collection in highland settlements
text:
(1) In a highland settlement residual waste is collected from a shared roadside point and not from each dwelling.
(2) For that reason the annual waste service charge under WSA §7 for a dwelling in a highland settlement is reduced by one half.
(3) The reduction is shown on the yearly invoice and needs no application.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of grants to support initiatives aimed at the conservation of biodiversity within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants are intended to fund projects that protect endangered species, restore critical habitats, and promote sustainable land management practices across various ecosystems. The scope encompasses all regions of Nordvale, including the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Eligibility criteria and application procedures are detailed in subsequent sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Biodiversity" means the variety of life, including genetic diversity, species diversity, and ecosystem diversity.
(2) "Conservation" means the protection, maintenance, and restoration of biodiversity.
(3) "Applicant" means an individual, organization, or entity seeking a grant under this Act.
(4) "Minister" refers to the Minister responsible for Environmental Affairs.
(5) "Project" refers to any initiative funded by a grant awarded under this Act.
(6) "Eligible Costs" refers to expenses directly related to a Project, as defined in section 12.

heading: Grant eligibility criteria for individuals
text:
An individual applicant must meet the following criteria to be eligible for a grant:
(1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(2) Be at least 18 years of age at the time of application.
(3) Propose a project primarily focused on biodiversity conservation within Nordvale.
(4) Provide a detailed project plan demonstrating clear conservation objectives and measurable outcomes.
(5) Not have received a grant under this Act within the preceding 12 months for a substantially similar project.
(6) Have no outstanding debt to the Nordvale government exceeding 5,000 crowns.

heading: Grant eligibility criteria for individuals
text:
An individual applicant must meet the following criteria to be eligible for a grant:
(1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(2) Be at least 20 years of age at the time of application.
(3) Propose a project primarily focused on biodiversity conservation within Nordvale.
(4) Provide a detailed project plan demonstrating clear conservation objectives and measurable outcomes.
(5) Not have received a grant under this Act within the preceding 18 months for a substantially similar project.
(6) Have no outstanding debt to the Nordvale government exceeding 7,500 crowns.

heading: Grant eligibility criteria for organizations
text:
An organizational applicant must meet the following criteria to be eligible for a grant:
(1) Be legally registered and operating in Nordvale for at least 2 years.
(2) Have a primary mission or significant component of its activities dedicated to environmental conservation.
(3) Propose a project primarily focused on biodiversity conservation within Nordvale.
(4) Provide a detailed project plan demonstrating clear conservation objectives and measurable outcomes.
(5) Not have received a grant under this Act within the preceding 12 months for a substantially similar project.
(6) Have an annual operating budget of at least 25,000 crowns.

heading: Grant eligibility criteria for organizations
text:
An organizational applicant must meet the following criteria to be eligible for a grant:
(1) Be legally registered and operating in Nordvale for at least 3 years.
(2) Have a primary mission or significant component of its activities dedicated to environmental conservation.
(3) Propose a project primarily focused on biodiversity conservation within Nordvale.
(4) Provide a detailed project plan demonstrating clear conservation objectives and measurable outcomes.
(5) Not have received a grant under this Act within the preceding 18 months for a substantially similar project.
(6) Have an annual operating budget of at least 30,000 crowns.

heading: Application submission process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs. The application period shall be open for 60 days commencing on 1 March each year. All applications must be submitted electronically through the official government portal. Applicants must ensure all required documentation, as outlined in section 6, is attached to their submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Confirmation of receipt will be issued within 7 business days of submission.

heading: Required application documentation
text:
Each application must include the following documentation:
(1) A completed application form.
(2) A detailed project proposal, not exceeding 15 pages.
(3) A comprehensive project budget breakdown.
(4) Evidence of eligibility as per section 3 or section 4.
(5) For organizations, proof of legal registration.
(6) For individuals, a copy of identity documentation.
(7) Two letters of reference relevant to the proposed project.

heading: Required application documentation
text:
Each application must include the following documentation:
(1) A completed application form.
(2) A detailed project proposal, not exceeding 12 pages.
(3) A comprehensive project budget breakdown, including projected income and expenses.
(4) Evidence of eligibility as per section 3 or section 4.
(5) For organizations, proof of legal registration and financial statements for the past two fiscal years.
(6) For individuals, a copy of identity documentation and a declaration of relevant experience.
(7) Three letters of reference relevant to the proposed project.

heading: Application review period
text: The Ministry of Environmental Affairs will review all submitted applications. The review process will commence immediately following the close of the application period. A panel of experts will assess each application against the criteria specified in sections 3, 4, and 7. The review period shall not exceed 90 days from the application deadline. Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application within 10 days of the completion of the review.

heading: Application review period
text: The Ministry of Environmental Affairs will review all submitted applications. The review process will commence immediately following the close of the application period. A panel of experts will assess each application against the criteria specified in sections 3, 4, and 7. The review period shall not exceed 100 days from the application deadline. Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application within 15 days of the completion of the review.

heading: Project evaluation criteria
text:
Projects will be evaluated based on the following criteria:
(1) Conservation impact: Up to 40% of the total score.
(2) Feasibility and methodology: Up to 25% of the total score.
(3) Budget justification and cost-effectiveness: Up to 20% of the total score.
(4) Applicant's capacity and experience: Up to 10% of the total score.
(5) Community involvement and outreach potential: Up to 5% of the total score.
(6) Projects must achieve a minimum overall score of 70% to be considered for funding.

heading: Grant amount for individual projects
text: Individual projects may receive a grant amount between 10,000 crowns and 50,000 crowns. The exact amount awarded will be determined based on the project's scope, budget, and potential conservation impact, as assessed by the review panel. No individual project shall receive more than 75% of its total projected costs from this grant. The maximum duration for projects funded under this section is 18 months.

heading: Grant amount for individual projects
text: Individual projects may receive a grant amount between 15,000 crowns and 60,000 crowns. The exact amount awarded will be determined based on the project's scope, budget, and potential conservation impact, as assessed by the review panel. No individual project shall receive more than 80% of its total projected costs from this grant. The maximum duration for projects funded under this section is 24 months.

heading: Grant amount for organizational projects
text: Organizational projects may receive a grant amount between 50,000 crowns and 200,000 crowns. The exact amount awarded will be determined based on the project's scope, budget, and potential conservation impact, as assessed by the review panel. No organizational project shall receive more than 70% of its total projected costs from this grant. The maximum duration for projects funded under this section is 36 months.

heading: Grant amount for organizational projects
text: Organizational projects may receive a grant amount between 60,000 crowns and 250,000 crowns. The exact amount awarded will be determined based on the project's scope, budget, and potential conservation impact, as assessed by the review panel. No organizational project shall receive more than 75% of its total projected costs from this grant. The maximum duration for projects funded under this section is 42 months.

heading: Grant disbursement
text: Grants will be disbursed in installments. An initial payment of 50% of the total awarded amount will be made upon the signing of the grant agreement. A second payment of 30% will be disbursed upon submission of a satisfactory interim report, as outlined in section 14. The final payment of 20% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report, as outlined in section 15. All disbursements are subject to satisfactory progress and adherence to the project plan.

heading: Eligible costs
text:
Eligible costs for grant funding include expenses directly related to the execution of the approved project. This may include:
(1) Personnel costs directly involved in the project, up to 40% of the total grant amount.
(2) Equipment and materials essential for project activities.
(3) Travel expenses directly related to project implementation, up to 10% of the total grant amount.
(4) Subcontracted services essential for project delivery.
(5) Administrative costs directly attributable to the project, not exceeding 15% of the total grant amount. Non-eligible costs are defined in section 13.

heading: Non-eligible costs
text:
The following costs are considered non-eligible for grant funding:
(1) Costs incurred before the grant agreement is signed.
(2) General operating expenses not directly attributable to the project.
(3) Capital expenditures exceeding 20,000 crowns without prior approval.
(4) Costs for lobbying or political activities.
(5) Debt servicing or interest payments.
(6) Costs for activities that are not aligned with the biodiversity conservation objectives of this Act. Any expenditure deemed non-eligible will not be reimbursed.

heading: Interim reporting requirements
text: All grant recipients are required to submit an interim report within 6 months of the initial grant disbursement. This report must detail project progress, expenditures to date, and any challenges encountered. The report should also include an updated work plan for the remainder of the project duration. Failure to submit a satisfactory interim report within 30 days of the due date may result in a delay or suspension of subsequent grant disbursements. A template for the interim report will be provided by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs.

heading: Final reporting requirements
text: Upon completion of the project, grant recipients must submit a final report within 30 days. This report must provide a comprehensive overview of the project's outcomes, achievements, and a full financial accounting of all expenditures. It must demonstrate how the project met its conservation objectives and provide measurable results where applicable. Failure to submit a satisfactory final report may result in the clawback of previously disbursed funds, as detailed in section 17. The Ministry will provide a final report template.

heading: Monitoring and evaluation
text: The Ministry of Environmental Affairs reserves the right to monitor and evaluate projects funded under this Act. This may include site visits, reviews of project documentation, and interviews with project personnel. Such monitoring may occur at any time during the project's duration or within 12 months of project completion. Grant recipients must cooperate fully with all monitoring and evaluation activities and provide access to all relevant information and sites. The purpose of monitoring is to ensure adherence to grant conditions and effective use of public funds.

heading: Recovery of funds
text:
The Ministry of Environmental Affairs may recover grant funds if:
(1) The project is not completed as agreed in the grant agreement.
(2) Funds are used for purposes other than those specified in the approved project plan.
(3) The recipient fails to comply with any terms or conditions of the grant agreement.
(4) Fraudulent information was provided in the application.
(5) Significant deviations from the project plan occur without prior written approval. The Ministry will provide 60 days' notice for the repayment of funds.

heading: Recovery of funds
text:
The Ministry of Environmental Affairs may recover grant funds if:
(1) The project is not completed as agreed in the grant agreement.
(2) Funds are used for purposes other than those specified in the approved project plan.
(3) The recipient fails to comply with any terms or conditions of the grant agreement.
(4) Fraudulent information was provided in the application or during reporting.
(5) Significant deviations from the project plan occur without prior written approval. The Ministry will provide 45 days' notice for the repayment of funds, and may charge interest at 5% per annum on overdue amounts.

heading: Appeals process
text: Applicants who are denied a grant may appeal the decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs within 30 days of receiving the rejection notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and provide any supporting documentation. A separate appeal panel, independent from the initial review panel, will review the appeal. The decision of the appeal panel will be final and communicated within 60 days of receipt of the appeal. Only one appeal per application is permitted.

heading: Publicity and acknowledgement
text: Grant recipients are required to acknowledge the financial support of the Republic of Nordvale in all publications, reports, and public communications related to the funded project. The specific wording and logo usage guidelines will be provided by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs. Recipients may also be asked to participate in public relations activities organized by the Ministry, such as press conferences or award ceremonies, up to two times during the project duration or within 6 months of its completion. Failure to acknowledge support may impact future grant applications.

heading: Confidentiality
text: The Ministry of Environmental Affairs will treat all application information as confidential, subject to the laws of Nordvale regarding public information. Project details, once a grant is awarded, may be publicly disclosed for transparency purposes, including the project title, recipient name, and grant amount. However, proprietary information clearly marked as such by the applicant will be protected to the fullest extent permitted by law. Applicants should clearly identify any information they consider to be proprietary or sensitive.

heading: Amendments to project plans
text: Any significant amendments to an approved project plan must receive prior written approval from the Ministry of Environmental Affairs. Significant amendments include changes to project objectives, methodologies, budget allocations exceeding 15% for any single budget line item, or key personnel. Requests for amendments must be submitted in writing at least 45 days before the proposed change is to take effect. The Ministry reserves the right to approve or deny such requests based on their impact on the project's conservation objectives and the terms of the grant agreement.

heading: Record keeping
text: Grant recipients must maintain accurate and complete financial records for all expenditures related to the project for a minimum period of 5 years following project completion. These records must be readily available for inspection by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs or its appointed auditors. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in the recovery of grant funds as per section 17. All records must be in Nordvale crowns and accessible digitally or in hard copy.

heading: Record keeping
text: Grant recipients must maintain accurate and complete financial and project activity records for all expenditures related to the project for a minimum period of 7 years following project completion. These records must be readily available for inspection by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs or its appointed auditors, with 10 days' notice. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in the recovery of grant funds as per section 17. All records must be in Nordvale crowns and accessible digitally.

heading: Prevention of conflicts of interest
text: Applicants and grant recipients must disclose any potential conflicts of interest that may arise during the application process or project implementation. A conflict of interest exists where an individual or organization has a personal or financial stake in the outcome of the project. Failure to disclose such conflicts may lead to disqualification from the grant program or the recovery of funds. The Ministry will review all disclosed conflicts of interest and may require mitigation measures to ensure the integrity of the project and the grant program.

heading: Use of scientific data
text: Projects involving scientific data collection must adhere to recognized scientific methodologies and ethical guidelines. All data collected as part of a funded project must be made available to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs upon request and may be used for broader biodiversity assessments. Any publications resulting from the project's scientific work should acknowledge the grant funding, as per section 19. Data retention policies, requiring data to be held for at least 10 years, must be outlined in the project plan.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For projects with a potential to cause significant environmental impact, an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) may be required. The need for an EIA will be determined by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs during the application review process. If an EIA is required, the applicant must complete it and obtain all necessary approvals before the commencement of project activities. Costs associated with the EIA may be considered eligible expenses, subject to the limits specified in section 12.

heading: Collaboration with other entities
text: Projects that demonstrate collaboration with other conservation organizations, academic institutions, or local communities are encouraged. Evidence of such collaboration, including letters of support or memoranda of understanding, should be included in the application. Collaborative projects may receive an additional 5% weighting in the evaluation criteria under section 7, provided they involve at least two distinct organizations. The Ministry believes that collaboration enhances the reach and impact of conservation efforts across Nordvale's varied landscapes.

heading: Grant limitations per municipality
text: To ensure equitable distribution of conservation efforts, no more than 30% of the total annual grant budget shall be allocated to projects within any single municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale. The Ministry will monitor grant allocations throughout the year to adhere to this limitation. If a municipality reaches its allocation limit, subsequent eligible projects from that area may be deferred to the next funding cycle or placed on a waiting list. This ensures broad geographic coverage.

heading: Grant limitations per municipality
text: To ensure equitable distribution of conservation efforts, no more than 25% of the total annual grant budget shall be allocated to projects within any single municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale. The Ministry will monitor grant allocations throughout the year to adhere to this limitation. If a municipality reaches its allocation limit, subsequent eligible projects from that area may be deferred to the next funding cycle or placed on a waiting list. This ensures broad geographic coverage and prevents overconcentration of resources.

heading: Total annual grant budget
text: The total annual budget allocated for grants under this Act shall be 5,000,000 crowns. This amount is subject to annual review and approval by the Nordvale Parliament. The Minister for Environmental Affairs may reallocate up to 10% of the budget between individual and organizational grants based on the quality and volume of applications received in any given year. Any unspent funds at the end of the fiscal year will be carried over to the next year's budget, up to a maximum of 500,000 crowns.

heading: Total annual grant budget
text: The total annual budget allocated for grants under this Act shall be 6,000,000 crowns. This amount is subject to annual review and approval by the Nordvale Parliament. The Minister for Environmental Affairs may reallocate up to 15% of the budget between individual and organizational grants based on the quality and volume of applications received in any given year. Any unspent funds at the end of the fiscal year will be carried over to the next year's budget, up to a maximum of 750,000 crowns.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its enactment date. The review will assess the effectiveness of the grant program in achieving its biodiversity conservation objectives, the efficiency of its administration, and its financial sustainability. Public consultation will be a part of the review process, allowing stakeholders to provide feedback. The first review will commence on 1 January 2023. Amendments to the Act may be proposed based on the findings of these reviews.

heading: Reporting to Parliament
text: The Minister for Environmental Affairs shall submit an annual report to the Nordvale Parliament on the operation of this Act. This report will detail the number of applications received, the grants awarded, the total funds disbursed, and a summary of the conservation outcomes achieved by funded projects. The report will also include any challenges encountered in the administration of the Act and recommendations for future improvements. The annual report shall be submitted by 30 September each year.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Projects that commenced prior to the enactment of this Act but align with its objectives may be considered for retroactive funding only if they commenced no earlier than 6 months before the effective date of this Act and meet all eligibility criteria. Such applications must be clearly identified as transitional and will be prioritized at 75% of the standard weighting during evaluation. This provision applies only for the first 12 months following the effective date of the Act. No more than 10 transitional grants will be awarded.

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed hot-spring attendant, the fee or allowance in FDA §14 is not payable.

heading: Secondary medical consultation
text:
(1) In every Act, 'secondary medical consultation' means an attendance with a physician who confines his or her practice to a single branch of medicine, at a facility run by the state or a municipality, with or without referral by another physician.
(2) An attendance at an emergency room is not a secondary medical consultation.

heading: Therapy units for former officials
text:
(1) The first six units of restorative movement therapy that an emeritus adjudicator receives in a calendar year are free.
(2) Later units are charged at the ordinary amount.
(3) Subsection (1) applies instead of any other reduction for those units.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the tariffs and fees applicable to all new bridge construction and significant bridge repair projects within the Republic of Nordvale. It aims to ensure fair and consistent financial contributions from project developers, covering administrative costs, environmental impact assessments, and a portion of the long-term maintenance fund. The provisions herein apply to all bridges exceeding 10 meters in length and those with a projected lifespan greater than 20 years. All tariffs are expressed in Nordvalean crowns, and all deadlines are measured in calendar days. The Act applies universally across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Bridge Construction Permit Application Fee
text: An application fee for a Bridge Construction Permit must accompany every new permit submission. This fee covers the initial administrative review and processing of documentation. The standard fee is 1,500 crowns for all applications. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the permit application. Applications submitted without the correct fee will be held in abeyance for up to 30 days, after which they will be returned to the applicant. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission.

heading: Bridge Construction Permit Application Fee
text:
An application fee for a Bridge Construction Permit must accompany every new permit submission. This fee covers the initial administrative review and processing of documentation.
(1) The standard fee is 1,800 crowns for all applications.
(2) For bridges exceeding 100 meters in length, an additional 500 crowns is required.
(3) This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the permit application. Applications submitted without the correct fee will be held in abeyance for up to 20 days, after which they will be returned to the applicant. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission.

heading: Bridge Repair Permit Application Fee
text: A specific application fee applies to permits for significant bridge repair projects. A significant repair project is defined as any repair costing more than 50,000 crowns or involving more than 20% of the bridge's structural elements. The fee for such applications is 750 crowns. This fee is designed to cover the administrative costs associated with reviewing repair proposals and ensuring compliance with safety standards. Minor repairs, defined as those under 50,000 crowns and less than 20% structural involvement, are exempt from this specific fee.

heading: Bridge Repair Permit Application Fee
text:
A specific application fee applies to permits for significant bridge repair projects. A significant repair project is defined as any repair costing more than 60,000 crowns or involving more than 25% of the bridge's structural elements.
(1) The fee for such applications is 850 crowns.
(2) For repairs impacting bridge decks over 500 square meters, an additional 150 crowns is levied.
(3) This fee is designed to cover the administrative costs associated with reviewing repair proposals and ensuring compliance with safety standards. Minor repairs, defined as those under 60,000 crowns and less than 25% structural involvement, are exempt from this specific fee.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment Tariff
text: All new bridge construction projects are subject to an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) tariff. This tariff contributes to the costs of conducting and reviewing environmental studies. The tariff is calculated at 2% of the estimated total construction cost, with a minimum tariff of 10,000 crowns. For projects crossing protected natural areas, an additional 0.5% is added to this tariff. The estimated total construction cost must be verified by an independent assessor approved by the Ministry of Infrastructure.

heading: Maintenance Fund Contribution
text: A contribution to the national Bridge Maintenance Fund is mandatory for all new bridge constructions. This fund ensures the long-term upkeep and safety of Nordvale's bridge infrastructure. The contribution is calculated at 3% of the total projected construction cost. This payment is due upon final approval of the construction permit and must be remitted within 45 days of such approval. Failure to pay this contribution may result in the suspension of construction activities until payment is made in full.

heading: Maintenance Fund Contribution
text:
A contribution to the national Bridge Maintenance Fund is mandatory for all new bridge constructions and significant repair projects exceeding 100,000 crowns. This fund ensures the long-term upkeep and safety of Nordvale's bridge infrastructure.
(1) For new constructions, the contribution is calculated at 3.5% of the total projected construction cost.
(2) For significant repair projects, the contribution is 1.5% of the repair cost.
(3) This payment is due upon final approval of the construction or repair permit and must be remitted within 30 days of such approval. Failure to pay this contribution may result in the suspension of construction or repair activities until payment is made in full.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Any tariff or fee not paid by its due date will incur late payment penalties. A penalty of 5% of the outstanding amount will be applied for payments delayed by up to 30 days. For delays exceeding 30 days, an additional 1% of the outstanding amount will be charged for each subsequent 15-day period, up to a maximum penalty of 25% of the original amount. The Ministry of Infrastructure reserves the right to suspend any ongoing project until all outstanding payments and penalties are settled. Project developers will be notified in writing of any late payment penalties.

heading: Expedited Review Fee
text: Applicants may request an expedited review of their bridge construction or repair permit application for an additional fee. This fee ensures that the application is processed within 15 working days, as opposed to the standard 45 working days. The expedited review fee is 10,000 crowns for construction permits and 5,000 crowns for repair permits. This fee is separate from the application fee and is non-refundable, even if the expedited review period is exceeded due to unforeseen administrative delays. The Ministry commits to its best efforts to meet the expedited timeline.

heading: Design Approval Fee
text: A fee is required for the final approval of bridge designs. This fee covers the technical review by expert engineers to ensure compliance with Nordvalean structural and safety standards. The Design Approval Fee is 0.5% of the estimated construction cost, with a minimum of 7,500 crowns and a maximum of 50,000 crowns. This fee is payable upon submission of the final design documents for approval and must be settled before any construction work can commence. Revisions to approved designs may incur additional fees as outlined in section 9.

heading: Design Revision Fee
text: Should an applicant submit revisions to an already approved bridge design, a Design Revision Fee will be charged. This fee compensates for the additional review time required by engineering staff. The fee is 2,500 crowns for minor revisions, which are changes affecting less than 5% of the structural integrity or span. For major revisions, affecting 5% or more, the fee is 7,500 crowns. Multiple revisions for the same project will incur the fee each time, up to a maximum of three revisions without triggering a full re-application.

heading: Inspection Tariffs
text: Projects are subject to a series of mandatory inspections during construction. A tariff is levied for each scheduled inspection phase to cover the costs of inspectors' time and travel. There are three standard inspection phases: foundation, structural, and final. Each phase incurs a tariff of 3,000 crowns. Any unscheduled or additional inspections requested by the developer or deemed necessary by the authorities will be charged at 1,500 crowns per inspection. All inspection tariffs must be paid 5 days prior to the scheduled inspection date.

heading: Inspection Tariffs
text:
Projects are subject to a series of mandatory inspections during construction. A tariff is levied for each scheduled inspection phase to cover the costs of inspectors' time and travel.
(1) There are three standard inspection phases: foundation, structural, and final. Each phase incurs a tariff of 3,500 crowns.
(2) For bridges over 200 meters in length, an additional pre-tensioning inspection is required, costing 2,000 crowns.
(3) Any unscheduled or additional inspections requested by the developer or deemed necessary by the authorities will be charged at 1,800 crowns per inspection. All inspection tariffs must be paid 7 days prior to the scheduled inspection date.

heading: Material Quality Assurance Fee
text: A Material Quality Assurance Fee is charged to cover the costs associated with verifying the quality and conformity of construction materials used in bridge projects. This includes random sampling and laboratory testing of concrete, steel, and other critical components. The fee is set at 0.75% of the total material cost, with a minimum fee of 5,000 crowns. This fee is payable in two installments: 50% at the start of construction and the remaining 50% halfway through the project duration. Certified material suppliers may be eligible for a 10% reduction in this fee.

heading: Post-Construction Audit Tariff
text: Upon completion of a new bridge construction, a Post-Construction Audit Tariff is levied. This audit ensures that the completed structure aligns with the approved plans and specifications, and that all safety protocols were adhered to. The tariff is 15,000 crowns for bridges up to 50 meters in length and 25,000 crowns for bridges exceeding 50 meters. This tariff must be paid before the bridge can be officially opened for public use. The audit typically takes 10 working days to complete after payment is confirmed.

heading: Road Access and Diversion Tariff
text: Projects requiring temporary road closures or diversions during construction are subject to a Road Access and Diversion Tariff. This tariff compensates for the disruption to traffic flow and the administrative costs of planning and implementing alternative routes. The tariff is 500 crowns per day for each major road affected, with a minimum charge of 5,000 crowns. This tariff is applicable only if the road closure duration exceeds 3 days. A detailed traffic management plan must be submitted and approved prior to any road closures.

heading: Road Access and Diversion Tariff
text:
Projects requiring temporary road closures or diversions during construction are subject to a Road Access and Diversion Tariff. This tariff compensates for the disruption to traffic flow and the administrative costs of planning and implementing alternative routes.
(1) The tariff is 750 crowns per day for each major road affected, with a minimum charge of 7,500 crowns.
(2) For closures impacting more than two major roads, an additional 200 crowns per day per road is applied.
(3) This tariff is applicable only if the road closure duration exceeds 2 days. A detailed traffic management plan must be submitted and approved prior to any road closures, and a public notice must be issued 14 days in advance.

heading: Utility Relocation Tariff
text: If bridge construction or repair necessitates the relocation of existing public utilities (e.g., water pipes, power lines, communication cables), a Utility Relocation Tariff will be applied. This tariff covers the administrative oversight and coordination required for such relocations, not the direct cost of relocation itself. The tariff is 10,000 crowns per utility type requiring relocation. For projects involving more than three different utility types, the tariff is capped at 25,000 crowns. This tariff is payable before any utility relocation work commences.

heading: Demolition Permit Fee
text: A separate permit and associated fee are required for the demolition of any existing bridge structure prior to new construction. This fee covers the review of demolition plans, environmental impact of demolition, and waste disposal protocols. The Demolition Permit Fee is 4,000 crowns for structures up to 20 meters in length and 8,000 crowns for structures exceeding 20 meters. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid before any demolition activities can begin. An approved waste management plan must accompany the permit application.

heading: Temporary Structure Tariff
text: The use of temporary structures, such as scaffolding or temporary support systems, for periods exceeding 60 days will incur a Temporary Structure Tariff. This tariff addresses potential public safety concerns and the administrative burden of monitoring such structures. The tariff is 100 crowns per square meter of temporary structure footprint, per month, with a minimum charge of 2,000 crowns. This tariff is applicable from the 61st day of the temporary structure's erection until its complete removal. Structures used for less than 60 days are exempt.

heading: Waterway Protection Tariff
text: For bridges constructed over or adjacent to navigable waterways, a Waterway Protection Tariff is levied. This tariff contributes to the maintenance of waterway navigation aids and the monitoring of potential environmental impacts during construction. The tariff is 0.1% of the total construction cost for projects over major rivers and 0.05% for projects over minor streams, with a minimum of 5,000 crowns. This tariff is due 30 days before construction begins in or near the waterway. Projects impacting protected marine or freshwater habitats may incur an additional 0.05%.

heading: Noise and Vibration Management Fee
text: Projects expected to generate significant noise or vibration impacting residential areas or sensitive ecosystems are subject to a Noise and Vibration Management Fee. This fee supports monitoring efforts and potential mitigation measures. The fee is 20,000 crowns for projects within 500 meters of residential zones and 10,000 crowns for projects within 200 meters of sensitive ecosystems. A detailed noise and vibration impact assessment plan must be submitted with the permit application. This fee is payable upon permit approval.

heading: Archaeological Impact Assessment Fee
text: If preliminary site surveys indicate a potential for archaeological findings, an Archaeological Impact Assessment Fee is charged. This fee covers the costs of expert archaeological assessments and, if necessary, supervised excavation. The fee is 12,000 crowns for initial assessments. Should significant findings be confirmed, an additional tariff of 500 crowns per square meter of excavated area will be applied. This tariff is non-negotiable and essential for preserving Nordvale's cultural heritage. Work in affected areas cannot proceed until this fee is settled.

heading: Public Consultation Tariff
text: For major bridge projects exceeding 200 meters in length or having a significant visual impact, a Public Consultation Tariff is required. This tariff contributes to the costs of organizing public meetings, disseminating information, and addressing community feedback. The tariff is 8,000 crowns per public consultation phase, with a minimum of two phases required for applicable projects. This fee supports transparency and community engagement, ensuring that local residents have a voice in significant infrastructure developments. The first payment is due 60 days prior to the initial consultation.

heading: Public Consultation Tariff
text:
For major bridge projects exceeding 150 meters in length or having a significant visual impact, a Public Consultation Tariff is required. This tariff contributes to the costs of organizing public meetings, disseminating information, and addressing community feedback.
(1) The tariff is 10,000 crowns per public consultation phase, with a minimum of two phases required for applicable projects.
(2) For projects impacting more than one municipality, an additional 2,500 crowns is applied per additional municipality.
(3) This fee supports transparency and community engagement, ensuring that local residents have a voice in significant infrastructure developments. The first payment is due 75 days prior to the initial consultation, and an online platform must be maintained for feedback for at least 90 days.

heading: Safety Barrier Tariff
text: All new bridges must incorporate safety barriers meeting national standards. A Safety Barrier Tariff is levied to ensure the quality and durability of these critical components. The tariff is 50 crowns per linear meter of bridge requiring safety barriers. This tariff covers the inspection and certification of the installed safety systems. This fee is payable upon the completion of the structural phase of the bridge and before the final inspection. Bridges with integrated pedestrian walkways will incur an additional 10 crowns per linear meter for enhanced pedestrian safety features.

heading: Lighting and Signage Tariff
text: A tariff is applied for the installation and inspection of lighting and signage systems on new bridges. This ensures adequate visibility and clear directional information for public safety. The Lighting and Signage Tariff is 30 crowns per linear meter of bridge length. This tariff includes an initial inspection and certification of the electrical systems and sign placement. This fee is payable prior to the final commissioning of the bridge's electrical systems. For bridges with complex traffic intersections at their approaches, an additional 5,000 crowns is levied.

heading: Architectural Review Fee
text: For aesthetically significant bridges or those located in prominent urban areas, an Architectural Review Fee is required. This fee covers the assessment by a panel of architectural experts to ensure the bridge's design harmonizes with its surroundings and contributes positively to the urban or natural landscape. The fee is 0.2% of the total construction cost, with a minimum of 10,000 crowns and a maximum of 75,000 crowns. This fee is due upon submission of the detailed architectural plans and renders.

heading: Architectural Review Fee
text:
For aesthetically significant bridges or those located in prominent urban or protected natural areas, an Architectural Review Fee is required. This fee covers the assessment by a panel of architectural experts to ensure the bridge's design harmonizes with its surroundings and contributes positively to the urban or natural landscape.
(1) The fee is 0.25% of the total construction cost, with a minimum of 12,000 crowns and a maximum of 85,000 crowns.
(2) Bridges within the historic districts of Aldmark or Corvik incur an additional 15,000 crowns.
(3) This fee is due upon submission of the detailed architectural plans and renders, and must include a 3D model simulation.

heading: Traffic Management Plan Approval Fee
text: Every bridge construction or major repair project requires an approved Traffic Management Plan. A fee is charged for the review and approval of this plan by the municipal traffic authorities. The Traffic Management Plan Approval Fee is 3,000 crowns. This fee ensures that disruptions to public traffic are minimized and that safety measures for both workers and the public are adequate. The fee is payable upon submission of the plan. Resubmissions due to significant revisions will incur an additional 1,500 crowns fee.

heading: Site Clearance Tariff
text: A Site Clearance Tariff is applied to projects requiring significant vegetation removal or land preparation beyond the immediate bridge footprint. This tariff contributes to environmental rehabilitation efforts in affected areas. The tariff is 200 crowns per 100 square meters of land cleared beyond 10 meters from the bridge's structural elements. A minimum tariff of 2,000 crowns applies. This fee is assessed based on the approved site plan and is payable prior to any land clearance activities. Projects adhering to strict 'no-clearance' policies are exempt.

heading: Hazardous Material Management Tariff
text: Projects identifying or potentially encountering hazardous materials during construction (e.g., asbestos, contaminated soil) are subject to a Hazardous Material Management Tariff. This tariff supports the regulatory oversight and specialized disposal protocols. The tariff is 25,000 crowns per identified hazardous material type. An initial assessment fee of 5,000 crowns is due if a site survey indicates potential risk. Failure to declare known hazardous materials will result in a penalty of 50,000 crowns, in addition to the tariff.

heading: Insurance Verification Fee
text: All project developers must hold comprehensive insurance coverage for construction liability and worker safety. An Insurance Verification Fee is charged to cover the administrative costs of verifying adequate insurance policies. The fee is 1,000 crowns and must be paid annually for the duration of the construction period. Proof of insurance must be submitted to the Ministry of Infrastructure at least 30 days prior to the commencement of any work. Failure to maintain valid insurance will result in immediate project suspension.

heading: Project Extension Fee
text: If a bridge construction or major repair project exceeds its approved completion timeline, a Project Extension Fee will be applied. This fee compensates for prolonged administrative oversight and potential public inconvenience. The fee is 500 crowns per month for the first three months of extension, increasing to 1,000 crowns per month thereafter. This fee is levied starting from the day after the original approved completion date. Developers must formally apply for an extension at least 30 days before the original deadline.

heading: Project Extension Fee
text:
If a bridge construction or major repair project exceeds its approved completion timeline, a Project Extension Fee will be applied. This fee compensates for prolonged administrative oversight and potential public inconvenience.
(1) The fee is 750 crowns per month for the first two months of extension, increasing to 1,200 crowns per month thereafter.
(2) For projects in the capital, Aldmark, these fees are increased by an additional 20%.
(3) This fee is levied starting from the day after the original approved completion date. Developers must formally apply for an extension at least 45 days before the original deadline, providing justified reasons for the delay.

heading: Special Access Permit Fee
text: Projects requiring special access to restricted areas (e.g., military zones, high-security facilities, historical preserves) will incur a Special Access Permit Fee. This fee covers the additional security clearances and coordination required. The fee is 6,000 crowns per restricted area requiring access. This fee is separate from any other access-related tariffs and must be paid before any work can proceed in such areas. The processing time for such permits can be up to 90 days, so early application is advised.

heading: Heritage Bridge Preservation Tariff
text: Repair projects on bridges designated as national heritage sites are subject to a Heritage Bridge Preservation Tariff. This tariff supports specialized conservation techniques and materials. The tariff is 1.5% of the total repair cost, with a minimum of 20,000 crowns. This fee ensures that repairs respect the historical integrity and architectural significance of these structures. An expert heritage consultant, approved by the Ministry of Culture, must be engaged for the project, and proof of engagement must be submitted with the permit application.

heading: Small Bridge Exemption
text: Bridges less than 10 meters in length and designed solely for pedestrian or light vehicle access (under 5 tons) are exempt from all tariffs and fees listed in sections 2, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 17, 18, 20, 21, and 23 of this Act. However, an administrative registration fee of 500 crowns is still required, and all safety standards must be met. This exemption aims to encourage local community infrastructure development without imposing undue financial burden. The Ministry reserves the right to review this exemption for projects deemed to have significant public impact.

heading: Small Bridge Exemption
text:
Bridges less than 12 meters in length and designed solely for pedestrian or light vehicle access (under 7 tons) are exempt from all tariffs and fees listed in sections 2, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 17, 18, 20, 21, and 23 of this Act.
(1) However, an administrative registration fee of 750 crowns is still required, and all safety standards must be met.
(2) These exempted bridges are also exempt from the Public Consultation Tariff (section 20) and Architectural Review Fee (section 23).
(3) This exemption aims to encourage local community infrastructure development without imposing undue financial burden. The Ministry reserves the right to review this exemption for projects deemed to have significant public impact, or if located within 50 meters of a protected waterway.

heading: Emergency Repair Waiver
text: In cases of emergency bridge repairs, where immediate action is required to prevent collapse or ensure public safety, certain fees may be waived. The application fee (section 3) and expedited review fee (section 7) will be waived for repairs declared an emergency by the municipal authorities. All other tariffs, including the Maintenance Fund Contribution (section 5), remain applicable but may be paid within 90 days of the emergency declaration. A full report justifying the emergency status must be submitted within 7 days of commencing work.

heading: Remote Area Incentive Tariff Reduction
text: To encourage infrastructure development in remote or sparsely populated areas, a tariff reduction is offered. Projects located more than 50 kilometers from any municipality with a population exceeding 10,000 will receive a 15% reduction on all construction tariffs, excluding application fees and late payment penalties. This incentive aims to promote connectivity and economic development in regions that may otherwise face higher logistical costs. Eligibility for this reduction must be formally requested and approved by the Ministry of Infrastructure before permit application.

heading: Re-inspection Fee
text: Should an inspection (as per section 10) fail to meet the required standards, a re-inspection will be necessary. A Re-inspection Fee of 2,000 crowns will be charged for each subsequent re-inspection required for the same phase. This fee covers the additional time and resources allocated by inspectors. No further construction work in the affected area may proceed until the re-inspection passes and the fee is paid. Developers are given a maximum of 30 days to rectify deficiencies before further penalties are considered.

heading: Change of Project Scope Fee
text: Any significant alteration to the approved project scope, such as changes to bridge length by more than 10%, changes to materials affecting structural load, or alterations to the number of traffic lanes, will incur a Change of Project Scope Fee. This fee is 10,000 crowns and covers the re-evaluation of plans and permits. Minor adjustments not affecting structural integrity or environmental impact are exempt. The fee is payable upon submission of the revised project documentation and must be approved before implementation.

heading: Material Import Tariff
text: For bridge construction projects utilizing imported materials exceeding 20% of the total material cost, a Material Import Tariff is applied. This tariff is 1% of the value of the imported materials. The tariff encourages the use of domestically sourced materials where possible and contributes to local industry support. This tariff is payable upon declaration of imported materials during the material quality assurance process. Exemptions may be granted for specialized materials not produced within Nordvale, subject to Ministry approval.

heading: Construction Waste Disposal Tariff
text: A Construction Waste Disposal Tariff is levied on all projects to cover the environmental oversight of waste management. The tariff is 50 crowns per cubic meter of non-recycled construction waste generated. A detailed waste management plan, including projected waste volumes and recycling efforts, must be submitted with the permit application. This tariff is payable upon project completion, based on verified waste disposal records. Projects achieving a recycling rate of over 75% will receive a 25% reduction on this tariff.

heading: Bridge Renaming Fee
text: Should a developer or a local community wish to rename a newly constructed bridge, a Bridge Renaming Fee of 5,000 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the administrative processing, updating of records, and replacement of signage. The renaming request must be submitted within one year of the bridge's official opening. Renaming an existing bridge already named for more than 50 years will incur a fee of 15,000 crowns, and requires broader public consultation. All name proposals must be approved by the Ministry of Culture.

heading: Bridge Renaming Fee
text:
Should a developer or a local community wish to rename a newly constructed bridge, a Bridge Renaming Fee of 6,500 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the administrative processing, updating of records, and replacement of signage.
(1) The renaming request must be submitted within six months of the bridge's official opening.
(2) Renaming an existing bridge already named for more than 40 years will incur a fee of 20,000 crowns, and requires broader public consultation involving at least 3 public forums.
(3) All name proposals must be approved by the Ministry of Culture, and cannot conflict with existing place names or historical figures without exceptional justification.

heading: Annual Bridge Audit Fee
text: All privately owned bridges, or bridges developed by private entities under concession, are subject to an Annual Bridge Audit Fee. This fee covers an annual safety and structural integrity audit conducted by state-appointed engineers. The fee is 10,000 crowns per bridge, payable by January 31st each year. This ensures ongoing public safety for privately managed infrastructure. Failure to pay this fee will result in penalties as outlined in section 6 and may lead to the revocation of the concession agreement.

heading: Administrative Review Board Appeal Fee
text: Applicants wishing to appeal a decision made by the Ministry of Infrastructure regarding permit approvals, tariff assessments, or penalty applications may do so by submitting an appeal to the Administrative Review Board. An appeal fee of 3,500 crowns is required to initiate this process. This fee covers the administrative costs of convening the board and reviewing the submitted documentation. The appeal must be lodged within 60 days of the initial decision, accompanied by all relevant supporting evidence. The fee is non-refundable.

heading: Temporary Closure Tariff
text: Any bridge requiring temporary closure to traffic for construction-related work or repairs, outside of approved permit activities, will incur a Temporary Closure Tariff. This tariff is 1,000 crowns per day for each day the bridge is closed without prior approval. For closures exceeding 7 days, the tariff increases to 2,000 crowns per day. This tariff aims to deter unsanctioned disruptions to public infrastructure and ensure proper planning. Emergency closures due to unforeseen structural issues are exempt, provided a formal report is submitted within 24 hours.

heading: Temporary Closure Tariff
text: Any bridge requiring temporary closure to traffic for construction-related work or repairs, outside of approved permit activities, will incur a Temporary Closure Tariff. This tariff is 1,500 crowns per day for each day the bridge is closed without prior approval. For closures exceeding 5 days, the tariff increases to 2,500 crowns per day. Bridges within 20 kilometers of the capital, Aldmark, will incur a 20% surcharge on these rates. This tariff aims to deter unsanctioned disruptions to public infrastructure and ensure proper planning. Emergency closures due to unforeseen structural issues are exempt, provided a formal report and mitigation plan are submitted within 12 hours.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: (1) A registered cartographer shall pay an annual electric bicycle registration fee of 5 crowns. (2) This reduced fee only applies if the cartographer has been registered for at least one year.

heading: Special categories
text: (1) A registered cartographer shall pay an annual electric bicycle registration fee of 5 crowns. (2) This reduced fee applies only if the cartographer has been registered for at least one year.

heading: Special categories
text: A registered herbalist has 30 extra days to pay the moving allowance provided to job seekers who relocate for employment lasting at least six months.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a registered falconer, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for granting licences to explore for mineral deposits within the Republic of Nordvale. It outlines the application process, eligibility criteria, fees, obligations of licence holders, and the powers of the regulatory authority. The primary goal is to promote responsible and sustainable mineral exploration while ensuring fair access to Nordvale's natural resources for economic benefit and national development. All exploration activities must adhere to the provisions set forth in this Act and any regulations issued under it.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) 'Minister' means the Minister responsible for natural resources.
(b) 'Licence' means a Mineral Exploration Licence granted under this Act.
(c) 'Licence holder' means a person or entity to whom a Licence has been granted.
(d) 'Exploration area' means the specific geographical area for which a Licence is granted.
(e) 'Mineral' refers to any naturally occurring solid substance, excluding water and hydrocarbons, that can be extracted from the earth for economic use.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No person or entity shall undertake any mineral exploration activity within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Licence issued by the Minister in accordance with this Act. Any such activity conducted without a Licence shall be deemed unlawful and may be subject to penalties as described in section 34. This requirement applies to all stages of exploration, from preliminary surveys to advanced drilling operations. A Licence is distinct from any permits required for actual mining operations.

heading: Application for Licence
text: An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form. The application must include: a detailed work plan, a proposed exploration budget, evidence of financial capacity, and a map clearly delineating the proposed exploration area. The application fee of 5,000 crowns must accompany the submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days.

heading: Application for Licence
text: An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form. The application must include: a detailed work plan, a proposed exploration budget, evidence of financial capacity, a map clearly delineating the proposed exploration area, and a preliminary environmental impact assessment. The application fee of 7,500 crowns must accompany the submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text:
To be eligible for a Licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be a citizen of Nordvale or a company registered in Nordvale.
(b) Demonstrate technical competence in mineral exploration.
(c) Possess sufficient financial resources to carry out the proposed work plan, with proof of at least 150,000 crowns in available capital.
(d) Have no prior convictions for environmental offenses within the past 10 years.
(e) Be at least 18 years of age if an individual.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text:
To be eligible for a Licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be a citizen of Nordvale or a company registered in Nordvale.
(b) Demonstrate technical competence in mineral exploration, with at least two qualified geologists on staff or contracted.
(c) Possess sufficient financial resources to carry out the proposed work plan, with proof of at least 200,000 crowns in available capital.
(d) Have no prior convictions for environmental offenses within the past 15 years.
(e) Be at least 21 years of age if an individual.

heading: Consideration of Application
text: The Minister shall consider applications based on the completeness of the submission, the technical merits of the work plan, the applicant's financial capability, and the potential economic benefits to Nordvale. The Minister may request additional information or clarification from the applicant within 30 days of receiving the application. A decision to grant or refuse a Licence will generally be made within 90 days of receiving a complete application.

heading: Granting of Licence
text: Upon approval, the Minister shall grant a Licence specifying the exploration area, the minerals to be explored, the duration of the Licence, and any specific conditions attached. The Licence will be issued upon payment of the initial annual licence fee. The Minister reserves the right to impose conditions deemed necessary for the protection of the environment or the public interest. The Licence is non-transferable without the express written consent of the Minister.

heading: Licence Term
text: A Licence shall be granted for an initial period not exceeding 3 years. The exact duration will be specified in the Licence document. The Licence holder may apply for an extension in accordance with section 9. The term is calculated from the date the Licence is issued by the Minister's office. All exploration activities must cease immediately upon expiration of the Licence term unless an extension has been officially granted.

heading: Licence Term
text: A Licence shall be granted for an initial period not exceeding 2 years. The exact duration will be specified in the Licence document. The Licence holder may apply for an extension in accordance with section 9. The term is calculated from the date the Licence is issued by the Minister's office. All exploration activities must cease immediately upon expiration of the Licence term unless an extension has been officially granted.

heading: Licence Extension
text: A Licence holder may apply for an extension of their Licence for a further period not exceeding 2 years. The application for extension must be submitted at least 90 days before the current Licence expires and must include a revised work plan, a report on work completed, and the extension fee of 10,000 crowns. Only one extension may be granted. The Minister will assess the application based on compliance with the original Licence conditions and the progress made.

heading: Licence Extension
text: A Licence holder may apply for an extension of their Licence for a further period not exceeding 1 year. The application for extension must be submitted at least 120 days before the current Licence expires and must include a revised work plan, a detailed report on work completed, and the extension fee of 15,000 crowns. Only one extension may be granted. The Minister will assess the application based on compliance with the original Licence conditions, the progress made, and the environmental impact of past activities.

heading: Annual Licence Fee
text: An annual Licence fee of 20,000 crowns is payable by the Licence holder on the anniversary of the Licence issuance. Failure to pay the annual fee within 30 days of the due date may result in the suspension or revocation of the Licence as per section 28. This fee contributes to the administrative costs of regulating mineral exploration and monitoring compliance. A late payment penalty of 10% of the fee will be applied if payment is received between 31 and 60 days after the due date.

heading: Annual Licence Fee
text: An annual Licence fee of 25,000 crowns is payable by the Licence holder on the anniversary of the Licence issuance. Failure to pay the annual fee within 30 days of the due date may result in the suspension or revocation of the Licence as per section 28. This fee contributes to the administrative costs of regulating mineral exploration and monitoring compliance. A late payment penalty of 15% of the fee will be applied if payment is received between 31 and 60 days after the due date.

heading: Area Fees
text: In addition to the annual Licence fee, an area fee of 50 crowns per square kilometre of the exploration area is payable annually. This fee is calculated based on the total area specified in the Licence. The minimum area fee payable is 5,000 crowns. This fee is due on the same date as the annual Licence fee. Non-payment of the area fee will be treated in the same manner as non-payment of the annual Licence fee, as outlined in section 10.

heading: Area Fees
text: In addition to the annual Licence fee, an area fee of 75 crowns per square kilometre of the exploration area is payable annually. This fee is calculated based on the total area specified in the Licence. The minimum area fee payable is 7,500 crowns. This fee is due on the same date as the annual Licence fee. Non-payment of the area fee will be treated in the same manner as non-payment of the annual Licence fee, as outlined in section 10.

heading: Work Programme
text: Every Licence holder must adhere to the approved work programme submitted with their application or extension request. Any significant deviation from the approved work programme, including changes to exploration methods or target minerals, must receive prior written approval from the Minister. A 'significant deviation' is defined as any change affecting more than 20% of the planned expenditure or more than 15% of the planned drilling metres. Failure to comply may lead to penalties.

heading: Minimum Expenditure
text: Licence holders are required to spend a minimum of 50,000 crowns per year on exploration activities within their designated area. This minimum expenditure must be verifiable through financial records and submitted as part of the annual report. Failure to meet this minimum expenditure requirement without reasonable justification may result in the imposition of fines or the revocation of the Licence. The Minister may grant a waiver in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Minimum Expenditure
text: Licence holders are required to spend a minimum of 75,000 crowns per year on exploration activities within their designated area. This minimum expenditure must be verifiable through financial records and submitted as part of the annual report. Failure to meet this minimum expenditure requirement without reasonable justification may result in the imposition of fines or the revocation of the Licence. The Minister may grant a waiver in exceptional circumstances, but such waivers are rare.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Licence holders must submit annual reports to the Minister detailing their exploration activities, expenditures, and findings. These reports are due within 60 days of the anniversary of the Licence issuance. The report must include geological maps, assay results, and a summary of all work performed. Failure to submit timely and complete reports may result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns for each month the report is overdue, up to a maximum of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Environmental Protection
text: All exploration activities must be conducted in an environmentally responsible manner, minimizing disturbance to the land, water, and air. Licence holders must comply with all applicable environmental regulations of Nordvale. This includes proper disposal of waste materials, prevention of soil erosion, and protection of water sources. Any significant environmental incident must be reported to the Minister within 24 hours of its occurrence. Failure to adhere to these standards may lead to immediate suspension of activities.

heading: Rehabilitation of Land
text: Upon completion of exploration activities or expiration/relinquishment of the Licence, the Licence holder is responsible for rehabilitating the exploration area to a condition as close as reasonably practicable to its original state. This includes filling boreholes, removing all equipment and debris, and restoring vegetation. A rehabilitation plan must be submitted to the Minister for approval at least 90 days before the cessation of activities. Failure to rehabilitate adequately may result in financial penalties of up to 100,000 crowns.

heading: Security Deposit
text: Before commencing exploration activities, a Licence holder must provide a security deposit of 50,000 crowns to the Minister. This deposit will be held to ensure compliance with environmental protection and rehabilitation obligations. The deposit may be in the form of a cash deposit or a bank guarantee. The security deposit will be released only after the Minister is satisfied that all obligations, particularly rehabilitation, have been met. A partial release may be considered after 75% of rehabilitation is certified complete.

heading: Security Deposit
text: Before commencing exploration activities, a Licence holder must provide a security deposit of 75,000 crowns to the Minister. This deposit will be held to ensure compliance with environmental protection and rehabilitation obligations. The deposit may be in the form of a cash deposit or a bank guarantee. The security deposit will be released only after the Minister is satisfied that all obligations, particularly rehabilitation, have been met. A partial release may be considered after 80% of rehabilitation is certified complete.

heading: Access to Land
text: A Licence does not automatically grant the right of entry onto private land. Licence holders must obtain consent from landowners or lawful occupants before entering private property. If consent cannot be obtained through negotiation, the Licence holder may apply to the Minister for assistance in securing access, provided fair compensation is offered. Public lands are generally accessible, but activities must respect existing land uses and rights. Any damage caused must be promptly compensated.

heading: Compensation for Damages
text: The Licence holder is liable for any damage or loss caused to property, crops, livestock, or the environment by their exploration activities. Fair and prompt compensation must be paid to affected parties. Disputes regarding compensation shall first be attempted to be resolved through negotiation. If resolution is not achieved within 60 days, either party may refer the matter to an independent mediator appointed by the Minister. The decision of the mediator is binding if both parties agree to it beforehand.

heading: Health and Safety
text: Licence holders must ensure a safe working environment for all personnel involved in exploration activities. This includes providing appropriate safety equipment, training, and implementing robust safety procedures.
