All accidents resulting in serious injury or fatality must be reported to the Minister within 12 hours. Regular safety audits, at least once every six months, must be conducted and records kept for inspection. Failure to comply with safety standards may lead to immediate cessation of operations.

heading: Right of Inspection
text: The Minister, or any authorized officer, may enter any exploration area at any reasonable time to inspect operations, examine records, and collect samples to ensure compliance with this Act and the conditions of the Licence. Licence holders must provide full cooperation during such inspections. Obstruction of an authorized officer is an offense and may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns. A notice of inspection will generally be provided 24 hours in advance, except in emergency situations.

heading: Retention of Samples and Data
text: Licence holders must retain all core samples, cuttings, and other geological samples collected during exploration for a period of at least 5 years after the expiry or relinquishment of the Licence. All raw and processed exploration data, including geophysical survey results and analytical reports, must be securely stored for a minimum of 10 years. These materials and data must be made available to the Minister upon request for verification or research purposes. A copy of all final reports and interpretations must be submitted.

heading: Retention of Samples and Data
text: Licence holders must retain all core samples, cuttings, and other geological samples collected during exploration for a period of at least 7 years after the expiry or relinquishment of the Licence. All raw and processed exploration data, including geophysical survey results and analytical reports, must be securely stored for a minimum of 12 years. These materials and data must be made available to the Minister upon request for verification or research purposes. A copy of all final reports and interpretations must be submitted, along with digital datasets in a prescribed format.

heading: Confidentiality of Data
text: All data and reports submitted by a Licence holder shall be treated as confidential for a period of 2 years from the date of submission or until the Licence is relinquished, whichever comes first. After this period, the data may be made publicly available by the Minister for the benefit of further exploration or scientific research in Nordvale. This confidentiality period may be extended in exceptional circumstances by the Minister, based on a written request from the Licence holder explaining the commercial sensitivity.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text: A Licence may not be transferred, assigned, or encumbered without the prior written consent of the Minister. An application for transfer must be submitted with a fee of 15,000 crowns and must demonstrate that the proposed transferee meets all eligibility criteria specified in section 5. The Minister may refuse to grant consent without providing reasons. Any unauthorized transfer shall render the Licence null and void. The transferee must also agree to assume all obligations of the original Licence holder.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text: A Licence may not be transferred, assigned, or encumbered without the prior written consent of the Minister. An application for transfer must be submitted with a fee of 20,000 crowns and must demonstrate that the proposed transferee meets all eligibility criteria specified in section 5. The Minister may refuse to grant consent without providing reasons. Any unauthorized transfer shall render the Licence null and void. The transferee must also agree to assume all obligations of the original Licence holder, including any outstanding liabilities.

heading: Relinquishment of Area
text: A Licence holder may, at any time, relinquish all or part of the exploration area by giving 60 days' written notice to the Minister. Upon relinquishment, the Licence holder remains responsible for all obligations related to the relinquished area, including rehabilitation, that arose prior to the effective date of relinquishment. A final report on the relinquished area must be submitted within 30 days of the effective date. No refund of fees will be provided for relinquished areas.

heading: Reduction of Area
text: Upon application for an extension of a Licence, the Licence holder may be required to reduce the exploration area by at least 25%. This is to encourage focused exploration and allow other parties access to potentially less prospective ground. The specific area to be relinquished must be clearly delineated in the extension application. The Minister may waive this requirement in exceptional circumstances, such as for very small initial Licence areas or unique geological settings.

heading: Reduction of Area
text: Upon application for an extension of a Licence, the Licence holder may be required to reduce the exploration area by at least 30%. This is to encourage focused exploration and allow other parties access to potentially less prospective ground. The specific area to be relinquished must be clearly delineated in the extension application. The Minister may waive this requirement in exceptional circumstances, such as for very small initial Licence areas or unique geological settings, but such waivers are rare.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text: The Minister may suspend a Licence for a period not exceeding 90 days if the Licence holder fails to comply with any provision of this Act or any condition of the Licence. Before suspending a Licence, the Minister shall give written notice to the Licence holder, specifying the breach and allowing 30 days to remedy the situation. During suspension, all exploration activities must cease. Failure to remedy the breach within the suspension period may lead to revocation.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
The Minister may revoke a Licence if:
(a) The Licence holder fails to remedy a breach after a suspension period.
(b) The Licence holder provides false or misleading information in their application or reports.
(c) The Licence holder becomes insolvent or bankrupt.
(d) The Licence holder conducts activities outside the scope of the Licence.
(e) It is in the public interest to do so, following a thorough review. No fees will be refunded upon revocation.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Minister under this Act, including refusal to grant a Licence, refusal of an extension, or revocation of a Licence, may appeal the decision to an independent tribunal within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The tribunal's decision shall be final. The appeal must be submitted in writing, outlining the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 10,000 crowns. The tribunal will aim to hear the appeal within 60 days.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Minister under this Act, including refusal to grant a Licence, refusal of an extension, or revocation of a Licence, may appeal the decision to an independent tribunal within 21 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The tribunal's decision shall be final. The appeal must be submitted in writing, outlining the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 15,000 crowns. The tribunal will aim to hear the appeal within 45 days.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text: Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or any condition of a Licence commits an offence. A person found guilty of an offence is liable to a fine not exceeding 50,000 crowns for a first offence, and 100,000 crowns for a second or subsequent offence. In addition, the Minister may order the cessation of all activities and the forfeiture of any equipment used in the commission of the offence. Each day an offence continues may be considered a separate offence.

heading: Regulations
text: The Minister may make regulations for the better carrying out of the provisions of this Act. Such regulations may prescribe forms, fees, technical standards for exploration, environmental management plans, and any other matter necessary for the effective administration of mineral exploration in Nordvale. All regulations must be published in the official gazette at least 30 days before coming into effect. Public consultation may be held for significant regulatory changes.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any exploration permits or similar authorizations granted prior to the commencement of this Act shall remain valid for their original term, provided they are in substantial compliance with the spirit of this Act. Upon expiry, any renewal or extension will be subject to the full provisions of this Act. Holders of such prior authorizations must submit a report to the Minister within 180 days of this Act's commencement, detailing their current activities and compliance status. Failure to report may result in invalidation of the prior authorization.

heading: Repeal of Old Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on 1st January 2018. The Minister shall ensure that all necessary administrative structures and forms are in place by this date to facilitate the smooth implementation of the Act. Public awareness campaigns regarding the new requirements will be conducted in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik during the 60 days leading up to the commencement date. All stakeholders are advised to familiarize themselves with these new regulations.

heading: Payment terms
text: A registered peat cutter does not receive the child clothing allowance of 120 crowns per year for each child under 16 years of age.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a certified falconry instructor for at least one year, half of the fee or allowance mentioned in SBA §9 is payable.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants to community-led projects and initiatives within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants are intended to foster local development, enhance civic engagement, and support activities that benefit the broader community. This Act applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. The primary objective is to empower local groups to address their specific community needs through self-initiated projects.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Community project' refers to an initiative proposed and managed by a local group, aimed at providing a public benefit within a specific geographic area or for a particular segment of the population.
(2) 'Applicant' refers to an eligible community organization or group applying for a grant.
(3) 'Council' refers to the National Community Development Council responsible for administering this Act.
(4) 'Grant' refers to financial assistance provided in crowns under the provisions of this Act.
(5) 'Municipal Area' refers to the defined geographical boundaries of any of the Republic's municipalities.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be a non-profit organization, a registered community group, or an informal group of at least five adult residents (over 18 years old) from the same municipal area.
(2) The applicant must demonstrate a clear mission to serve the community and have been active for at least 6 months prior to the application date.
(3) The applicant must have a dedicated bank account for project funds if the grant exceeds 1,000 crowns.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be a non-profit organization, a registered community group, or an informal group of at least eight adult residents (over 18 years old) from the same municipal area.
(2) The applicant must demonstrate a clear mission to serve the community and have been active for at least 9 months prior to the application date.
(3) The applicant must have a dedicated bank account for project funds if the grant exceeds 2,000 crowns.

heading: Project Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) Eligible projects must demonstrate a clear public benefit and address an identified community need. Projects primarily benefiting a single individual or a private commercial entity are not eligible.
(2) Projects must be completed within 12 months of grant approval.
(3) The proposed project must be conducted within the municipal area of the applicant group.
(4) Projects involving the construction of new permanent structures over 10 square meters or costing more than 50,000 crowns require additional municipal approval.

heading: Project Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) Eligible projects must demonstrate a clear public benefit and address an identified community need. Projects primarily benefiting a single individual or a private commercial entity are not eligible.
(2) Projects must be completed within 9 months of grant approval.
(3) The proposed project must be conducted within the municipal area of the applicant group.
(4) Projects involving the construction of new permanent structures over 8 square meters or costing more than 40,000 crowns require additional municipal approval.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications must be submitted to the Council through the designated online portal or by post. 
(2) The application form must be fully completed and include a detailed project plan, a budget breakdown, and evidence of community support (e.g., letters of endorsement from at least 10 community members).
(3) Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, but decisions are made quarterly.

heading: Application Deadlines
text: The Council will review applications four times a year. Deadlines for submission are March 1st, June 1st, September 1st, and December 1st. Applications received after a deadline will be considered in the next review cycle. All applications must be submitted by 17:00 on the deadline day. Incomplete applications will be returned for revision and will not be considered until all necessary information is provided.

heading: Application Deadlines
text: The Council will review applications three times a year. Deadlines for submission are April 1st, August 1st, and December 1st. Applications received after a deadline will be considered in the next review cycle. All applications must be submitted by 17:00 on the deadline day. Incomplete applications will be returned for revision and will not be considered until all necessary information is provided.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) Each application must include a project proposal (maximum 5 pages), a detailed budget with itemized expenses, and a timeline for completion. 
(2) Proof of applicant status (e.g., registration documents, list of members with addresses) must be provided. 
(3) For projects requiring partnership, a letter of agreement from each partner organization is mandatory. 
(4) A risk assessment plan must also be submitted, outlining potential challenges and mitigation strategies.

heading: Grant Amounts
text:
(1) The minimum grant amount is 1,000 crowns.
(2) The maximum grant amount for a single project is 25,000 crowns.
(3) The Council reserves the right to award a partial grant amount based on project merit and available funds.
(4) No single organization may receive more than 50,000 crowns in grants within a 12-month period. This limit applies across all projects undertaken by the organization.

heading: Grant Amounts
text:
(1) The minimum grant amount is 1,500 crowns.
(2) The maximum grant amount for a single project is 20,000 crowns.
(3) The Council reserves the right to award a partial grant amount based on project merit and available funds.
(4) No single organization may receive more than 40,000 crowns in grants within a 12-month period. This limit applies across all projects undertaken by the organization.

heading: Funding Proportions
text:
(1) Grants will typically cover up to 80% of eligible project costs. 
(2) Applicants are expected to contribute at least 20% of the total project cost, which can be in the form of monetary contributions, in-kind donations, or volunteer labour (valued at 150 crowns per hour).
(3) In exceptional circumstances, the Council may approve full funding for projects deemed of critical importance, but such instances are rare and require explicit justification.

heading: Funding Proportions
text:
(1) Grants will typically cover up to 75% of eligible project costs. 
(2) Applicants are expected to contribute at least 25% of the total project cost, which can be in the form of monetary contributions, in-kind donations, or volunteer labour (valued at 175 crowns per hour).
(3) In exceptional circumstances, the Council may approve full funding for projects deemed of critical importance, but such instances are rare and require explicit justification and endorsement by the municipal council of the project's location.

heading: Expenditure Categories
text:
(1) Eligible expenditures include materials, equipment rental, professional services (up to 30% of the total grant), and reasonable administrative costs (up to 10% of the total grant).
(2) Ineligible expenditures include salaries for permanent staff, lobbying activities, political donations, and international travel.
(3) All expenditures must directly relate to the approved project activities.

heading: Grant Review Committee
text:
(1) The Council shall appoint a Grant Review Committee consisting of five members with expertise in community development, project management, and finance.
(2) Committee members serve for a term of 2 years and may be reappointed once.
(3) Decisions of the Committee are final, subject to an appeal process outlined in section 30.
(4) At least two members of the committee must reside outside the capital municipality of Aldmark.

heading: Evaluation Criteria
text:
(1) Projects will be evaluated based on community impact (40% weighting), feasibility (25% weighting), budget realism (20% weighting), and applicant capacity (15% weighting).
(2) Preference may be given to projects that demonstrate broad community engagement and sustainable outcomes beyond the grant period.
(3) Projects addressing critical needs in smaller municipalities like Elsby and Grauby may receive additional consideration.

heading: Notification of Decision
text: Applicants will be notified of the Council's decision within 45 days of the application deadline. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant agreement outlining the terms and conditions of the funding. Unsuccessful applicants will be provided with feedback on their application, highlighting areas for improvement, if requested within 14 days of notification. Notifications will be sent via email unless a postal address is specifically requested by the applicant.

heading: Notification of Decision
text: Applicants will be notified of the Council's decision within 60 days of the application deadline. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant agreement outlining the terms and conditions of the funding. Unsuccessful applicants will be provided with feedback on their application, highlighting areas for improvement, if requested within 7 days of notification. Notifications will be sent via email unless a postal address is specifically requested by the applicant.

heading: Grant Agreement
text:
(1) A legally binding grant agreement must be signed by both the applicant and the Council before any funds are disbursed. 
(2) The agreement will specify the project scope, budget, timeline, reporting requirements, and conditions for fund utilization. 
(3) Failure to sign the agreement within 30 days of receipt may result in the forfeiture of the grant offer. 
(4) Any significant deviation from the agreed project plan requires prior written approval from the Council.

heading: Fund Disbursement
text:
(1) Funds will typically be disbursed in two installments: 70% upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining 30% upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report.
(2) For grants under 5,000 crowns, a single disbursement of 100% may be made at the Council's discretion.
(3) All disbursements will be made via electronic bank transfer to the applicant's designated bank account.
(4) Funds must be used within 3 months of receipt for the initial installment and within 1 month of receipt for the final installment.

heading: Fund Disbursement
text:
(1) Funds will typically be disbursed in two installments: 60% upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining 40% upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report.
(2) For grants under 7,500 crowns, a single disbursement of 100% may be made at the Council's discretion.
(3) All disbursements will be made via electronic bank transfer to the applicant's designated bank account.
(4) Funds must be used within 2 months of receipt for the initial installment and within 1 month of receipt for the final installment.

heading: Project Monitoring
text:
(1) The Council reserves the right to monitor project progress through site visits, progress reports, and financial audits. 
(2) Applicants must provide access to project sites and relevant documentation upon request with at least 5 business days' notice. 
(3) Any significant changes to the project scope, budget, or timeline must be reported to the Council immediately.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) A mid-term progress report is required for all projects exceeding 10,000 crowns, due 6 months after the grant agreement is signed.
(2) A final report, including a detailed financial statement and photographic evidence of project completion, must be submitted within 30 days of the project's official end date.
(3) Failure to submit reports may result in delayed final payment or repayment of previously disbursed funds.
(4) The final report must also include a brief statement from at least three community members benefiting from the project.

heading: Financial Accountability
text:
(1) Grant recipients must maintain accurate financial records for all project-related expenditures for a minimum of 5 years.
(2) These records must be available for audit by the Council or its designated representatives.
(3) Any unspent funds or funds used for ineligible purposes must be returned to the Council within 60 days of project completion.
(4) All transactions exceeding 500 crowns must be supported by original receipts or invoices.

heading: Acknowledgement of Funding
text: Grant recipients are required to acknowledge the Council's financial support in all public communications related to the project, including press releases, websites, and any temporary or permanent displays at the project site. A standardized logo, provided by the Council, must be prominently displayed where feasible. Failure to comply with this requirement may affect future grant applications.

heading: Amendments to Projects
text:
(1) Any significant amendments to the approved project plan, budget, or timeline must be submitted in writing to the Council for approval at least 30 days prior to the proposed change.
(2) Minor deviations (less than 10% of any budget line item or a delay of less than 14 days) do not require prior approval but must be noted in the final report.
(3) The Council reserves the right to deny amendments that fundamentally alter the project's original intent or eligibility.

heading: Project Completion Extensions
text:
(1) Applicants may request a project completion extension of up to 3 months. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Council at least 15 days before the original project end date.
(2) Extensions will only be granted for valid reasons, such as unforeseen delays due to weather, material shortages, or other unavoidable circumstances.
(3) Only one extension per project will be considered.
(4) An approved extension will not result in additional funding.

heading: Project Completion Extensions
text:
(1) Applicants may request a project completion extension of up to 2 months. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Council at least 20 days before the original project end date.
(2) Extensions will only be granted for valid reasons, such as unforeseen delays due to weather, material shortages, or other unavoidable circumstances.
(3) Only one extension per project will be considered.
(4) An approved extension will not result in additional funding.

heading: Withdrawal of Grant
text:
(1) The Council may withdraw a grant offer or agreement if it discovers misrepresentation in the application, failure to comply with the terms of the grant agreement, or if the project becomes unviable.
(2) In such cases, the applicant may be required to repay all or part of the disbursed funds within 60 days.
(3) The Council will provide written notice of withdrawal, detailing the reasons, at least 10 days before the effective date of withdrawal.
(4) The applicant has a right to appeal the decision as per section 30.

heading: Liability
text: The Council is not liable for any debts, liabilities, or damages incurred by the applicant or any third party during the execution of the project. Grant recipients are solely responsible for ensuring adequate insurance coverage for project activities and for complying with all relevant local and national regulations. The grant is purely financial assistance and does not imply a partnership or agency relationship between the Council and the recipient.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All information submitted by applicants will be treated with confidentiality by the Council, except for project titles, applicant names, grant amounts, and a brief description of the project, which may be made public for transparency purposes.
(2) Personal data will be handled in accordance with national privacy laws.
(3) Committee members and Council staff are bound by strict confidentiality agreements regarding application details.

heading: Intellectual Property
text: Any intellectual property rights arising from projects funded under this Act shall remain with the grant recipient. However, the Council reserves a royalty-free, non-exclusive, and irrevocable license to use, reproduce, and distribute any project outcomes or reports for non-commercial purposes, primarily for promoting the grant program and sharing best practices across Nordvale.

heading: Publicity and Promotion
text: The Council may use information about funded projects for publicity and promotional purposes, including publishing project summaries, photographs, and testimonials on its website, in annual reports, and other promotional materials. Grant recipients are encouraged to cooperate with the Council in these efforts, including participation in promotional events or interviews when requested, though such participation is not mandatory.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any disputes arising from the interpretation or application of this Act or a grant agreement shall first be addressed through informal negotiation between the applicant and the Council.
(2) If a resolution cannot be reached within 30 days, either party may request mediation by an independent third party, agreed upon by both sides.
(3) The costs of mediation shall be shared equally between the parties.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Applicants or members of the public may submit a formal complaint regarding the administration of this Act or the conduct of Council staff or committee members.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing within 14 days of the incident giving rise to the complaint and will be reviewed by an independent internal ombudsman.
(3) A response will be provided within 30 days.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Applicants or members of the public may submit a formal complaint regarding the administration of this Act or the conduct of Council staff or committee members.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing within 7 days of the incident giving rise to the complaint and will be reviewed by an independent internal ombudsman.
(3) A response will be provided within 45 days.
(4) All complaints must include verifiable evidence to support the claim.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been rejected or whose grant has been withdrawn may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Panel.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing within 21 days of receiving the Council's decision and must clearly state the grounds for appeal.
(3) The Appeals Panel will consist of three individuals not involved in the original decision.
(4) The decision of the Appeals Panel is final and binding.
(5) Grounds for appeal are limited to procedural irregularities or misinterpretation of eligibility criteria, not a re-evaluation of project merit.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been rejected or whose grant has been withdrawn may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Panel.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing within 14 days of receiving the Council's decision and must clearly state the grounds for appeal.
(3) The Appeals Panel will consist of five individuals not involved in the original decision.
(4) The decision of the Appeals Panel is final and binding.
(5) Grounds for appeal are limited to procedural irregularities or misinterpretation of eligibility criteria, not a re-evaluation of project merit.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the National Assembly every 5 years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. The first review will take place no later than January 1, 2023. Public consultation will be a mandatory part of the review process, involving community groups from all municipalities, including Dunmere and Corvik, to gather feedback on the grant program's impact and administration.

heading: Amendment of Act
text: Amendments to this Act may be proposed by the Council or any member of the National Assembly. All proposed amendments must undergo a full legislative process, including public debate and a vote by the National Assembly. Minor administrative changes may be enacted by ministerial decree, provided they do not alter the fundamental principles or scope of the Act, and these changes must be published in the official gazette.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and regulations outlined herein will be effective from this date, and the Council will begin accepting applications from this commencement date. Any activities initiated before this date are not eligible for retroactive funding under this Act. The Council will publish detailed guidelines for implementation within 30 days of this Act's commencement.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: The National Assembly shall allocate an annual budget of at least 2,000,000 crowns for the community project grant program. This allocation is subject to annual review and approval as part of the national budgetary process. Any unspent funds at the end of a fiscal year will be rolled over to the next year's budget, up to a maximum of 10% of the initial allocation, to ensure continuity of funding.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: The National Assembly shall allocate an annual budget of at least 2,500,000 crowns for the community project grant program. This allocation is subject to annual review and approval as part of the national budgetary process. Any unspent funds at the end of a fiscal year will be rolled over to the next year's budget, up to a maximum of 15% of the initial allocation, to ensure continuity of funding.

heading: Special Consideration for Underserved Areas
text: Projects originating from municipalities identified as underserved or experiencing significant economic challenges, as determined by the Ministry of Regional Development, may receive up to an additional 10% in grant funding, or a waiver of up to 5% of the required applicant contribution. The Council will publish a list of such municipalities annually, with Dunmere and Corvik frequently featured due to their unique geographical and economic factors. This measure aims to promote equitable development across Nordvale.

heading: Training and Capacity Building
text:
(1) The Council will offer free workshops and training sessions for potential applicants on grant writing, project management, and financial reporting.
(2) These sessions will be held quarterly in various municipal centers, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Lund Vale.
(3) Online resources and templates will also be made available on the Council's website.
(4) Participation in these programs is highly recommended but not mandatory for applicants.

heading: Community Engagement Requirement
text: All projects must demonstrate a minimum of 20 hours of documented community engagement during their planning and implementation phases. This can include public meetings, volunteer recruitment drives, or consultation sessions with local residents. Evidence of this engagement must be submitted with the final project report. Projects that exceed 40 hours of engagement may receive an additional 500 crowns upon successful completion, demonstrating deep community involvement.

heading: Emergency Grant Provision
text:
(1) In cases of unforeseen emergencies or immediate community needs, the Council may establish an emergency grant provision of up to 10,000 crowns per project.
(2) Such grants are subject to a fast-track application and review process, with decisions made within 10 business days.
(3) Eligibility criteria may be adapted to address the specific emergency, but the project must still demonstrate clear public benefit.
(4) A maximum of 5 such grants can be awarded per fiscal year.

heading: Emergency Grant Provision
text:
(1) In cases of unforeseen emergencies or immediate community needs, the Council may establish an emergency grant provision of up to 15,000 crowns per project.
(2) Such grants are subject to a fast-track application and review process, with decisions made within 7 business days.
(3) Eligibility criteria may be adapted to address the specific emergency, but the project must still demonstrate clear public benefit.
(4) A maximum of 3 such grants can be awarded per fiscal year.

heading: Maintenance and Sustainability Plans
text:
(1) For projects involving the creation of physical assets (e.g., community gardens, public art installations), applicants must submit a detailed maintenance and sustainability plan covering a period of at least 3 years post-completion.
(2) This plan should outline how the project will be maintained, funded, and managed by the community beyond the grant period.
(3) Projects without a robust sustainability plan will not be considered for funding if their expected lifespan exceeds the project completion date by more than 12 months.

heading: Ethical Guidelines
text: All projects funded under this Act must adhere to ethical guidelines promoting fairness, inclusivity, and respect for all community members. Projects that discriminate on the basis of age, gender, origin, or any other characteristic are strictly prohibited. The Council reserves the right to immediately withdraw funding from any project found to be in violation of these ethical standards, with all disbursed funds to be repaid within 30 days.

heading: Council Powers
text: The Council is empowered to issue further regulations and guidelines consistent with this Act to facilitate its implementation and administration. These regulations will be published in the official government gazette and on the Council's website at least 30 days before their effective date. The Council may also request additional information from applicants or grant recipients as deemed necessary for the proper oversight of granted projects.

heading: Repeal of Previous Grant Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Sports passes for retired public servants
text:
(1) A retired public servant may buy a monthly pass for a municipal swimming pool or gymnasium for 28 crowns.
(2) The pass is otherwise subject to the same rules as any other monthly pass.
(3) The price of an annual pass is not reduced.

heading: Sports passes for retired public servants
text:
(1) A retired public servant may buy a monthly pass for a municipal swimming pool or gymnasium for 32 crowns.
(2) The pass is otherwise subject to the same rules as any other monthly pass.
(3) The price of an annual pass is not reduced.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the collection of levies specifically designated for the ongoing maintenance and upkeep of public burial grounds within the Republic of Nordvale. The levies are intended to ensure that these important public spaces remain well-maintained, respectful, and accessible to all citizens. This Act outlines the responsibilities for levy collection, the applicable rates, and the procedures for enforcement. It applies to all properties within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale that meet the criteria specified herein. The primary goal is to provide a sustainable funding mechanism for essential services such as landscaping, infrastructure repair, and general cleanliness of burial grounds.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(1) "Public burial ground" means any land designated by a municipality for the interment of human remains, open to the public, and maintained with public funds.
(2) "Property owner" refers to the individual or entity registered as the legal owner of a parcel of land in the municipal registry.
(3) "Annual Levy Period" means the period commencing on January 1st of a calendar year and concluding on December 31st of the same year.
(4) "Municipality" refers to any of the eight recognized administrative divisions within Nordvale.

heading: Imposition of Levy
text: A burial ground maintenance levy is hereby imposed on all assessable properties within the Republic of Nordvale. This levy is calculated annually and is due from the property owner for the respective Annual Levy Period. The purpose of this levy is to contribute to the collective funding required for the proper care, preservation, and beautification of public burial grounds, ensuring their dignified appearance and functionality for the community. The levy is a mandatory contribution and is not subject to individual service usage or direct benefit from a burial ground.

heading: Assessable Properties
text: The levy applies to all properties that are primarily residential or commercial in nature, with a land area exceeding 100 square meters. Properties used exclusively for agricultural purposes are exempt. This includes single-family homes, multi-unit residential buildings, retail establishments, and office buildings. Industrial properties with a land area exceeding 500 square meters are also included. Public lands, including parks, roads, and government buildings, are not considered assessable properties under this Act, nor are properties owned by recognized charitable organizations.

heading: Assessable Properties
text: The levy applies to all properties that are primarily residential or commercial in nature, with a land area exceeding 80 square meters. Properties used exclusively for agricultural purposes or properties with a current market value below 50,000 crowns are exempt. This includes single-family homes, multi-unit residential buildings, retail establishments, and office buildings. Industrial properties with a land area exceeding 400 square meters are also included. Public lands, including parks, roads, and government buildings, are not considered assessable properties under this Act, nor are properties owned by recognized charitable organizations.

heading: Assessable Properties
text: The levy applies to all properties that are primarily residential or commercial in nature, with a land area exceeding 75 square meters. Properties used exclusively for agricultural purposes or properties with a current market value below 60,000 crowns are exempt. This includes single-family homes, multi-unit residential buildings, retail establishments, and office buildings. Industrial properties with a land area exceeding 350 square meters are also included. Public lands, including parks, roads, and government buildings, are not considered assessable properties under this Act, nor are properties owned by recognized charitable organizations.

heading: Levy Rate for Residential Properties
text: For residential properties, the annual levy is calculated at a flat rate of 0.05% of the assessed property value. The minimum annual levy for any residential property shall be 150 crowns, and the maximum annual levy shall not exceed 1,500 crowns. The assessed property value is determined by the municipal valuation office as of January 1st of the Annual Levy Period. This rate applies uniformly across all municipalities to ensure fairness and consistency in contributions from homeowners towards burial ground upkeep.

heading: Levy Rate for Residential Properties
text: For residential properties, the annual levy is calculated at a flat rate of 0.06% of the assessed property value. The minimum annual levy for any residential property shall be 180 crowns, and the maximum annual levy shall not exceed 1,800 crowns. The assessed property value is determined by the municipal valuation office as of January 1st of the Annual Levy Period. This rate applies uniformly across all municipalities to ensure fairness and consistency in contributions from homeowners towards burial ground upkeep.

heading: Levy Rate for Residential Properties
text: For residential properties, the annual levy is calculated at a flat rate of 0.07% of the assessed property value. The minimum annual levy for any residential property shall be 200 crowns, and the maximum annual levy shall not exceed 2,000 crowns. The assessed property value is determined by the municipal valuation office as of January 1st of the Annual Levy Period. This rate applies uniformly across all municipalities to ensure fairness and consistency in contributions from homeowners towards burial ground upkeep.

heading: Levy Rate for Commercial Properties
text: For commercial properties, the annual levy is set at 0.08% of the assessed property value. The minimum annual levy for any commercial property shall be 300 crowns, and the maximum annual levy shall not exceed 3,000 crowns. The assessed property value for commercial properties is also determined by the municipal valuation office as of January 1st of the Annual Levy Period. This higher rate reflects the typically larger footprint and commercial benefit derived from operating within a municipality with well-maintained public amenities, including burial grounds which contribute to civic pride and appeal.

heading: Levy Rate for Industrial Properties
text: For industrial properties, the annual levy is fixed at 0.1% of the assessed property value. The minimum annual levy for any industrial property shall be 500 crowns, and the maximum annual levy shall not exceed 5,000 crowns. The assessed property value is determined by the municipal valuation office as of January 1st of the Annual Levy Period. Industrial properties, often having significant land holdings and contributing to the local economy, are expected to contribute proportionally more to the upkeep of essential public infrastructure, including public burial grounds.

heading: Calculation of Assessed Value
text: The assessed property value for the purpose of this Act shall be the market value of the land and any permanent structures thereon, as determined by the municipal valuation office. This valuation is updated every three years. The most recent valuation preceding the Annual Levy Period shall be used. Property owners are entitled to receive a notice of their assessed value at least 60 days before the levy is due. Appeals against the assessed value must be filed within 30 days of receiving this notice.

heading: Calculation of Assessed Value
text: The assessed property value for the purpose of this Act shall be the market value of the land and any permanent structures thereon, as determined by the municipal valuation office. This valuation is updated every two years. The most recent valuation preceding the Annual Levy Period shall be used. Property owners are entitled to receive a notice of their assessed value at least 75 days before the levy is due. Appeals against the assessed value must be filed within 45 days of receiving this notice.

heading: Notification of Levy
text: Each municipality shall issue a levy notice to every assessable property owner at least 90 days before the due date for payment. The notice shall clearly state the assessed property value, the applicable levy rate, the calculated levy amount in crowns, the due date for payment, and information regarding appeal procedures. Notices shall be delivered by mail or electronic means, as elected by the property owner, to the registered address. Failure to receive a notice does not exempt a property owner from the obligation to pay the levy.

heading: Payment Due Date
text: The annual burial ground maintenance levy shall be due and payable in full by April 30th of each Annual Levy Period. Payments received after this date will be subject to late payment penalties as outlined in section 12. Property owners may arrange for installment payments under specific conditions, as determined by the municipal finance department. These conditions typically require a formal request made at least 60 days before the due date and a demonstrated financial hardship.

heading: Payment Methods
text: Payments for the levy may be made through various methods, including direct bank transfer, online payment portals, or at designated municipal offices. Cash payments are accepted at municipal offices during regular business hours. All payments must clearly reference the property identification number provided on the levy notice to ensure proper allocation. Receipts for payment will be issued within 14 days of receipt of funds. Payments made by post must be postmarked no later than the due date.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Any levy payment received after the due date specified in section 10 shall incur a late payment penalty. A flat fee of 100 crowns will be applied immediately, followed by an additional interest charge of 0.5% per month, or part thereof, on the outstanding balance. This interest will accrue from the day following the due date until the levy and all accumulated penalties are paid in full. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 20% of the original levy amount for any given year.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Any levy payment received after the due date specified in section 10 shall incur a late payment penalty. A flat fee of 120 crowns will be applied immediately, followed by an additional interest charge of 0.75% per month, or part thereof, on the outstanding balance. This interest will accrue from the day following the due date until the levy and all accumulated penalties are paid in full. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 25% of the original levy amount for any given year.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Any levy payment received after the due date specified in section 10 shall incur a late payment penalty. A flat fee of 150 crowns will be applied immediately, followed by an additional interest charge of 1.0% per month, or part thereof, on the outstanding balance. This interest will accrue from the day following the due date until the levy and all accumulated penalties are paid in full. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 30% of the original levy amount for any given year.

heading: Recovery of Unpaid Levies
text: If a levy, including any penalties, remains unpaid for more than 180 days after the original due date, the municipality may initiate recovery proceedings. These proceedings may include placing a lien on the property, referral to a debt collection agency, or legal action in the municipal court. All costs associated with the recovery of unpaid levies, including legal fees and administrative charges, will be borne by the property owner. A formal demand letter will be sent at least 30 days prior to initiating any recovery action.

heading: Exemptions for Low-Income Households
text: Property owners who demonstrate an annual household income below 150,000 crowns and are over 65 years of age may apply for a full exemption from the levy. Applications must be submitted annually by March 1st and include verifiable income statements and proof of age. This exemption is intended to provide relief to vulnerable segments of the population while still encouraging broad community participation in burial ground maintenance. The municipality reserves the right to verify all submitted documentation.

heading: Exemptions for Low-Income Households
text: Property owners who demonstrate an annual household income below 160,000 crowns and are over 62 years of age may apply for a full exemption from the levy. Applications must be submitted annually by March 1st and include verifiable income statements and proof of age. This exemption is intended to provide relief to vulnerable segments of the population while still encouraging broad community participation in burial ground maintenance. The municipality reserves the right to verify all submitted documentation.

heading: Exemptions for Low-Income Households
text: Property owners who demonstrate an annual household income below 175,000 crowns and are over 60 years of age may apply for a full exemption from the levy. Applications must be submitted annually by March 1st and include verifiable income statements and proof of age. This exemption is intended to provide relief to vulnerable segments of the population while still encouraging broad community participation in burial ground maintenance. The municipality reserves the right to verify all submitted documentation.

heading: Partial Exemptions for Certain Non-Profits
text: Registered non-profit organizations that primarily focus on environmental conservation or historical preservation may apply for a 50% reduction in their annual levy. To qualify, the organization must be officially recognized by the Republic of Nordvale and provide evidence that at least 75% of its annual budget is dedicated to its stated charitable purpose. Applications for this partial exemption must be submitted by February 1st of each year, accompanied by annual financial reports. This partial exemption acknowledges the community contributions of these organizations.

heading: Exemptions for properties within 50 meters of an existing public burial ground
text: Properties located within 50 meters of the boundary of an existing public burial ground are exempt from the levy. This exemption recognizes that proximity to these sites may sometimes entail specific considerations for residents. The distance is measured from the nearest point of the property boundary to the nearest point of the burial ground boundary. Property owners seeking this exemption must provide a recent survey plan demonstrating their property's exact location in relation to a public burial ground. This provision applies automatically once verified by the municipality.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Property owners who dispute the imposition or amount of their levy may formally appeal to the municipal finance department within 30 days of receiving their levy notice. If the dispute remains unresolved after 60 days, the owner may escalate the matter to an independent arbitration panel appointed by the municipality. The decision of the arbitration panel shall be binding. The cost of arbitration will be shared equally between the municipality and the property owner, unless the panel determines otherwise.

heading: Use of Levy Funds
text: Funds collected through the burial ground maintenance levy shall be exclusively used for the maintenance, repair, and improvement of public burial grounds. This includes, but is not limited to, landscaping, tree care, pathway repairs, fence maintenance, signage, waste removal, and general infrastructure upkeep. A minimum of 10% of the collected funds must be allocated to long-term capital improvement projects for burial grounds, such as chapel renovations or the expansion of columbarium walls. Funds cannot be diverted for any other municipal purposes.

heading: Reporting and Transparency
text: Each municipality shall publish an annual report detailing the collection and expenditure of burial ground maintenance levies. This report must be made publicly available on the municipal website by September 30th of each year. The report shall include a breakdown of total levies collected, administrative costs (not exceeding 5% of total collections), and itemized expenditures on specific maintenance projects for each public burial ground. An audit of these funds will be conducted every two years by an independent auditor.

heading: Municipal Obligations
text: Each municipality is responsible for the efficient collection of levies, accurate assessment of properties, and proper allocation of funds for burial ground maintenance. Municipalities must maintain a dedicated fund for these levies, ensuring that the funds are not commingled with general municipal revenues. Furthermore, municipalities are obligated to respond to public inquiries regarding levies within 15 working days and address any complaints promptly and fairly. Failure to comply with these obligations may result in provincial review.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in sections 5, 6, and 7 shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Municipal Affairs every five years. This review will consider economic indicators, inflation rates, the actual costs of burial ground maintenance, and public feedback. Any proposed changes to the rates will be subject to a public consultation period of at least 60 days before being enacted. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in sections 5, 6, and 7 shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Municipal Affairs every four years. This review will consider economic indicators, inflation rates, the actual costs of burial ground maintenance, and public feedback. Any proposed changes to the rates will be subject to a public consultation period of at least 45 days before being enacted. The next review is scheduled for 2027.

heading: Amendments to Schedules
text: The Ministry of Municipal Affairs may, by order, amend any schedules attached to this Act. Such amendments may include updates to the list of public burial grounds, specific maintenance standards, or procedures for application of exemptions. Any order amending a schedule must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 30 days before its effective date. Public notice of such amendments will also be posted on municipal websites for a minimum of 60 days.

heading: Appeals Process for Exemptions
text: If an application for exemption under section 14 or section 15 is denied, the property owner or organization may appeal the decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 20 days of receiving the denial notice. The Appeals Board shall review the application and any supporting documentation and render a decision within 45 days. The decision of the Municipal Appeals Board is final and binding. No further appeals will be permitted for that Annual Levy Period.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Each municipality shall maintain accurate and detailed records of all levy assessments, collections, exemptions, and expenditures for a minimum period of seven years. These records shall be subject to audit and inspection by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs upon request. Property owners are entitled to request a copy of their individual levy assessment and payment history at any time, which must be provided within 10 working days of the request. Digital records must be securely stored and backed up weekly.

heading: Public Consultation on New Burial Grounds
text: Before establishing any new public burial grounds, a municipality must conduct a public consultation process. This process shall involve at least two public meetings, advertised 90 days in advance, and a period of 60 days for written submissions from the public. The projected maintenance costs for the new burial ground and their potential impact on future levy rates must be presented transparently during this consultation. A summary of public feedback must be included in the final proposal to the Ministry.

heading: Advisory Committee Establishment
text: Each municipality shall establish a Burial Ground Maintenance Advisory Committee, comprising five members appointed by the municipal council. The committee shall include at least one property owner, one representative from a local historical society, and one financial expert. The committee's role is to advise the municipality on maintenance priorities, budget allocations, and public engagement strategies for burial grounds. The committee shall meet at least quarterly and submit an annual report to the municipal council.

heading: Advisory Committee Establishment
text: Each municipality shall establish a Burial Ground Maintenance Advisory Committee, comprising seven members appointed by the municipal council. The committee shall include at least two property owners, one representative from a local historical society, one financial expert, and one landscaping professional. The committee's role is to advise the municipality on maintenance priorities, budget allocations, and public engagement strategies for burial grounds. The committee shall meet at least bi-monthly and submit an annual report to the municipal council. At least 40% of committee members must be women.

heading: Temporary Levy Reduction
text: In exceptional circumstances, such as a major economic downturn or a significant surplus in the burial ground maintenance fund, the Ministry of Municipal Affairs may authorize a temporary reduction in levy rates for a period not exceeding two years. Any such reduction must be uniform across all municipalities and be publicly announced at least 120 days before its implementation. The reduction amount shall not exceed 15% of the standard levy rate.

heading: Penalty for Misuse of Funds
text: Any municipal official found to have intentionally diverted funds collected under this Act for purposes other than the maintenance of public burial grounds shall be subject to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns and potential administrative sanctions. The Ministry of Municipal Affairs shall conduct thorough investigations into any allegations of misuse of funds. Funds improperly diverted must be immediately reimbursed to the burial ground maintenance fund, along with a 10% penalty charge.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Provisions
text: The 'Public Cemeteries Levy Ordinance of 1995' (Nordvale Ordinance No. 12/1995) is hereby repealed. Any outstanding levies or penalties under the repealed ordinance shall remain enforceable until fully collected. This Act supersedes all previous legislation pertaining to burial ground maintenance levies. Any ongoing legal proceedings initiated under the repealed ordinance will continue under the provisions of that ordinance until their conclusion. All municipal guidelines based on the repealed ordinance must be updated within 180 days.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1st, 2018. All provisions and regulations contained within this Act will be legally binding from this date forward. Municipalities are required to implement all necessary administrative procedures and systems to comply with the Act's requirements by the commencement date. Any interim measures needed to transition from previous regulations must be approved by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs at least 90 days prior to commencement.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A holder of a registered cave rescue badge has an additional 30 days to pay the fee for paper copies of public documents.

heading: Special categories
text: No electric bicycle registration fee is payable by any certified ski patroller, who shall instead pay 5 crowns in lieu of the fee or allowance specified in FDA §14.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates the use of boats and the operation of harbours in Nordvale.
(2) It applies to every boat used on the sea or on an inland lake.
(3) Rowing boats and canoes under 3 metres long are exempt, except for sections 6 and 14.

heading: Boat registration
text:
(1) A motor boat with an engine of more than 10 kilowatts shall be registered with the Harbour Authority.
(2) The registration fee is 60 crowns and is paid once.
(3) The registration number shall be painted on both sides of the bow.

heading: Boat registration
text:
(1) A motor boat with an engine of more than 10 kilowatts shall be registered with the Harbour Authority.
(2) The registration fee is 75 crowns and is paid once.
(3) The registration number shall be painted on both sides of the bow.

heading: Sailing boat registration
text:
(1) A sailing boat longer than 7 metres shall be registered with the Harbour Authority.
(2) The registration fee is 40 crowns and is paid once.
(3) The registration number shall be painted on both sides of the bow.

heading: Skipper's certificate
text:
(1) The skipper of a motor boat with an engine of more than 20 kilowatts shall hold a skipper's certificate.
(2) A person must be at least 16 years old to obtain the certificate.
(3) The certificate is valid for 10 years.

heading: Speed limits in harbours
text:
(1) The speed limit inside a harbour is 5 knots.
(2) The speed limit within 100 metres of a bathing area is 5 knots.
(3) The Harbour Authority may set a lower limit by public notice.

heading: Speed limits in harbours
text:
(1) The speed limit inside a harbour is 4 knots.
(2) The speed limit within 100 metres of a bathing area is 5 knots.
(3) The Harbour Authority may set a lower limit by public notice.

heading: Life jackets
text:
(1) Every person on a boat shall have a life jacket on board.
(2) A child under 12 years of age shall wear the life jacket whenever the boat is under way.
(3) A skipper who breaks this section shall pay a fine of 50 crowns.

heading: Alcohol limit for skippers
text:
(1) A skipper shall not operate a boat with a blood alcohol level above 0.5 per mille.
(2) A skipper who exceeds the limit shall pay a fine of 300 crowns.
(3) A skipper who exceeds 1.2 per mille commits a criminal offence.

heading: Alcohol limit for skippers
text:
(1) A skipper shall not operate a boat with a blood alcohol level above 0.2 per mille.
(2) A skipper who exceeds the limit shall pay a fine of 300 crowns.
(3) A skipper who exceeds 1.0 per mille commits a criminal offence.

heading: Harbour berth fees
text:
(1) The Harbour Authority shall charge a berth fee of 12 crowns per night for a boat up to 8 metres long.
(2) For a boat longer than 8 metres the fee is 20 crowns per night.
(3) The fee is paid on arrival.

heading: Harbour berth fees
text:
(1) The Harbour Authority shall charge a berth fee of 14 crowns per night for a boat up to 8 metres long.
(2) For a boat longer than 8 metres the fee is 22 crowns per night.
(3) The fee is paid on arrival.

heading: Annual berth
text:
(1) A boat owner may rent an annual berth instead of paying per night.
(2) The annual berth fee is 900 crowns for a boat up to 8 metres long.
(3) For a boat longer than 8 metres the annual berth fee is 1,500 crowns.

heading: Winter storage
text:
(1) The Harbour Authority shall offer winter storage on land from 1 October to 30 April.
(2) The storage fee is 150 crowns for a boat up to 8 metres long.
(3) A boat left after 30 April shall pay an extra 5 crowns per day.

heading: Pump-out of waste
text:
(1) A boat with a toilet shall not discharge waste within 3 nautical miles of the coast.
(2) Every harbour shall provide a pump-out station.
(3) Use of the pump-out station is free of charge for boats staying overnight.

heading: Pump-out of waste
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Fuel and spills
text:
(1) A skipper shall report an oil or fuel spill to the Harbour Authority within 2 hours.
(2) A skipper who causes a spill shall pay the cost of cleaning it up.
(3) A skipper who fails to report a spill shall pay a fine of 400 crowns.

heading: Navigation lights
text:
(1) A boat under way between sunset and sunrise shall show navigation lights.
(2) A skipper who fails to show lights shall pay a fine of 80 crowns.
(3) Lights shall be visible from at least 2 nautical miles.

heading: Distress and rescue
text:
(1) A skipper shall help any person in danger at sea, if this can be done safely.
(2) A skipper shall report an accident to the Harbour Authority within 24 hours.
(3) A rescue by the Harbour Authority is free of charge.

heading: Ferries to the islands
text:
(1) The Harbour Authority shall run a ferry to each island municipality at least once a day.
(2) A ferry ticket for an adult costs 18 crowns one way.
(3) A child under 12 years travels at half price.

heading: Ferries to the islands
text:
(1) The Harbour Authority shall run a ferry to each island municipality at least twice a day.
(2) A ferry ticket for an adult costs 20 crowns one way.
(3) A child under 12 years travels at half price.

heading: Ferry tickets for children and seniors
text:
(1) A person aged 70 or over travels on a ferry for 12 crowns one way.
(2) A child under 4 years travels free of charge.
(3) A ferry ticket is valid for 2 hours from the time of purchase.

heading: Harbour Authority
text:
(1) The Harbour Authority operates the public harbours and supervises the application of this Act.
(2) The Authority is led by a director appointed for a term of 5 years.
(3) The Authority shall publish its tariffs by 1 December each year.

heading: Inspections of boats
text:
(1) A harbour officer may inspect a boat in a harbour at any reasonable time.
(2) The officer may require the skipper to show the certificate and registration.
(3) A boat that is unsafe may be detained for up to 7 days.

heading: Abandoned boats
text:
(1) A boat left in a harbour for more than 90 days without payment may be removed by the Harbour Authority.
(2) The Authority shall send a written warning at least 30 days before removal.
(3) The Authority may sell a removed boat after 6 months.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision of the Harbour Authority may appeal within 30 days.
(2) The appeal shall be decided within 60 days.
(3) An appeal does not suspend a detention under section 18.

heading: Instruments of amateur musicians on buses and trains
text:
(1) A passenger who plays in a registered amateur ensemble (HSA §21), and who carries the musical instrument that he or she plays in it, pays no extra fare for the instrument on a bus or train, however large its case is.
(2) The passenger shows proof of membership, such as the ensemble's membership card, on request.
(3) Subsection (1) does not cover amplifiers, music stands or other equipment carried with the instrument; for these the ordinary luggage rules apply.

heading: Monthly travel pass for teachers
text:
(1) A qualified teacher pays 50 crowns for a monthly bus and train pass for journeys that start in zone A.
(2) Where the teacher is entitled to a lower price for the pass under another Act, only the lower price applies.

heading: Monthly travel pass for teachers
text:
(1) A qualified teacher pays 55 crowns for a monthly bus and train pass for journeys that start in zone A.
(2) Where the teacher is entitled to a lower price for the pass under another Act, only the lower price applies.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the mandatory deadlines for safety inspections of all publicly owned bridges within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objective is to ensure the structural integrity and public safety of these vital infrastructure assets across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Regular inspections are crucial for identifying potential hazards, scheduling necessary repairs, and preventing incidents that could endanger citizens or disrupt commerce. The provisions herein apply to all bridges regardless of their construction material, length, or traffic volume, unless explicitly exempted by subsequent sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Bridge" means a structure, including its substructure and superstructure, erected over an obstruction such as a watercourse, highway, or railway, and having a clear span of 3 meters or more between supports. This definition encompasses vehicular bridges, pedestrian bridges, and combined-use bridges.
(2) "Publicly owned" refers to any bridge where ownership, responsibility for maintenance, or operational control rests with a municipal government, a regional authority, or the national government of Nordvale. This includes bridges managed by the Ministry of Infrastructure, municipal public works departments, and inter-municipal commissions.
(3) "Inspection" refers to a detailed visual and, where necessary, non-destructive evaluation conducted by a qualified bridge engineer to assess the condition, structural integrity, and safety of a bridge.

heading: General Inspection Frequency
text: All publicly owned bridges in Nordvale, regardless of their specific classification or age, must undergo a general safety inspection at intervals not exceeding 24 months. This biennial inspection shall cover all accessible components of the bridge structure, including but not limited to the deck, superstructure, substructure, bearings, and approach roadways. The inspection report must be submitted to the relevant municipal or national authority within 30 days of the inspection's completion. Failure to adhere to this frequency may result in administrative penalties as outlined in section 38.

heading: General Inspection Frequency
text: All publicly owned bridges in Nordvale must undergo a general safety inspection at intervals not exceeding 20 months. This inspection shall cover all accessible components of the bridge structure, including but not limited to the deck, superstructure, substructure, bearings, and approach roadways. The inspection report must be submitted to the relevant municipal or national authority within 25 days of the inspection's completion. Failure to adhere to this frequency may result in administrative penalties as outlined in section 38, with fines increased by 15% for repeat offenses within a 5-year period.

heading: Newly Constructed Bridges
text: For any newly constructed publicly owned bridge, the first general safety inspection must be conducted no later than 12 months after its official opening to traffic. This initial inspection serves to establish a baseline condition report and to identify any potential construction-related defects that may have emerged during the initial period of operation. Subsequent inspections for these bridges will then follow the schedule set out in section 3. The responsible construction authority must provide all as-built drawings and material specifications to the inspecting engineer prior to the first inspection.

heading: Newly Constructed Bridges
text: For any newly constructed publicly owned bridge, the first general safety inspection must be conducted no later than 9 months after its official opening to traffic. This initial inspection serves to establish a baseline condition report and to identify any potential construction-related defects that may have emerged during the initial period of operation. Subsequent inspections for these bridges will then follow the schedule set out in section 3. The responsible construction authority must provide all as-built drawings and material specifications to the inspecting engineer prior to the first inspection, along with a detailed maintenance plan for the first 5 years of operation.

heading: Bridges Over Waterways
text: Bridges that span navigable waterways or are subject to significant water current action, such as those over the River Eldrin or major municipal canals, require more frequent inspections. In addition to the general inspection frequency, an underwater or dive inspection of the substructure components (piers, abutments, foundations) must be conducted at least once every 60 months. This specialized inspection assesses erosion, scour, and potential damage from marine traffic or debris accumulation. The municipality of Dunmere, with its numerous river crossings, must prioritize these specialized inspections.

heading: Bridges Over Waterways
text: Bridges that span navigable waterways or are subject to significant water current action require more frequent inspections. In addition to the general inspection frequency, an underwater or dive inspection of the substructure components must be conducted at least once every 48 months. For bridges identified as critical infrastructure or those with significant scour risk, this frequency is reduced to 36 months. The municipality of Dunmere, with its numerous river crossings, must prioritize these specialized inspections, especially those supporting key transportation routes.

heading: Bridges with High Traffic Volume
text: Bridges carrying daily average traffic volumes exceeding 10,000 vehicles must undergo a general safety inspection at an accelerated frequency of every 18 months. This applies particularly to major arteries in Aldmark and Brenholt. The increased frequency is necessary due to the accelerated wear and tear experienced by these structures. Traffic count data, as recorded by municipal traffic departments, shall be used to determine a bridge's classification under this section. Any bridge approaching this threshold must be monitored closely, and an accelerated inspection schedule initiated once the threshold is consistently met for three consecutive months.

heading: Bridges with Critical Defects
text: Upon identification of a critical structural defect that poses an immediate or severe risk to public safety, the bridge authority must initiate a special inspection within 7 days. This special inspection must be conducted by an independent qualified bridge engineer, distinct from the one who performed the initial discovery. The report from this special inspection must outline immediate mitigation measures and propose a plan for repair, along with a revised inspection schedule that may require monthly or even weekly monitoring until the defect is remedied. The Ministry of Infrastructure must be notified within 24 hours of a critical defect's discovery.

heading: Bridge Condition Rating System
text: All inspection reports must utilize the Nordvale Bridge Condition Rating System, a standardized numerical scale from 1 (critical condition, requiring immediate closure) to 9 (excellent condition, no defects). This system ensures uniformity in assessment and facilitates comparison across different bridges and over time. Any bridge receiving a rating of 4 or lower for any primary structural component (deck, superstructure, substructure) requires a follow-up action plan to be submitted within 60 days of the inspection report. The Ministry of Infrastructure publishes detailed guidelines for applying this rating system.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: All bridge inspection reports must be submitted electronically to the Nordvale Central Bridge Database, maintained by the Ministry of Infrastructure, within 30 days of the inspection's completion. The report must include photographic documentation of all identified defects, the overall condition rating, and detailed recommendations for repair or further investigation. Municipal authorities are responsible for ensuring timely submission. Late submissions will incur a penalty of 500 crowns for each week of delay, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns, before additional enforcement actions are considered.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: All bridge inspection reports must be submitted electronically to the Nordvale Central Bridge Database, maintained by the Ministry of Infrastructure, within 21 days of the inspection's completion. The report must include high-resolution photographic documentation of all identified defects, the overall condition rating, and detailed recommendations for repair or further investigation, including estimated costs and timelines. Municipal authorities are responsible for ensuring timely submission. Late submissions will incur a penalty of 750 crowns for each week of delay, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns, before additional enforcement actions are considered.

heading: Qualification of Inspectors
text: Bridge inspections mandated by this Act must be conducted by engineers holding a valid Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) license in Nordvale, with a specialization in structural engineering, and who have completed at least 100 hours of certified bridge inspection training. Furthermore, the inspecting engineer must have a minimum of 5 years of practical experience in bridge design, construction, or inspection. The Ministry of Infrastructure maintains a registry of qualified bridge inspectors, and only individuals on this registry are authorized to perform inspections under this Act. Unqualified inspections will be deemed invalid, and the responsible authority subject to penalties.

heading: Emergency Inspections
text: In the event of a significant natural disaster (e.g., severe earthquake, major flood, high winds exceeding 120 km/h) or any incident causing potential structural damage (e.g., vehicular collision with a primary support), an emergency inspection must be conducted within 48 hours of the event. This rapid assessment is to determine immediate safety risks and whether the bridge requires closure or load restrictions. The municipality of Corvik, known for its seismic activity, must maintain a roster of engineers available for such emergencies. A preliminary report outlining findings and immediate actions must be submitted within 72 hours.

heading: Load Rating Reassessment
text: The load rating of any bridge, which specifies the maximum permissible weight of vehicles, must be reassessed at least once every 10 years. This reassessment is crucial as bridge materials degrade over time and traffic patterns change. If a bridge's condition rating drops to 5 or below, a load rating reassessment must be conducted immediately, irrespective of the 10-year cycle. Any changes to the load rating must be clearly posted at both ends of the bridge within 7 days of the reassessment's completion. Failure to post revised load limits carries a fine of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Bridge Rehabilitation Projects
text: Upon completion of a major rehabilitation project that significantly alters the structural components of a bridge (e.g., deck replacement, substructure repair), a final inspection must be conducted within 30 days of the project's handover. This inspection serves to confirm the quality of the repairs and to establish a new baseline condition. The regular inspection schedule for that bridge is then reset, with the first general inspection due within 12 months of this final inspection. All project documentation, including material certifications, must be provided to the inspecting engineer.

heading: Access for Inspections
text: The authority responsible for a bridge must ensure that inspectors are provided with safe and adequate access to all bridge components required for a thorough inspection.
