text: Upon completion of all authorized activities, including reforestation, the permit holder is responsible for restoring the site to a condition that minimizes environmental impact and promotes natural regeneration. This includes removal of all equipment, debris, and temporary structures. Access roads not intended for long-term use must be de-commissioned and revegetated. A final site inspection by the Nordvale Forest Authority will confirm compliance with restoration requirements before the permit is formally closed.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in forestry operations must receive adequate training in their assigned tasks, including safety procedures, equipment operation, and environmental protection. Evidence of such training, including certificates or internal training records, must be kept on site and presented upon request during inspections. New hires must complete a minimum of 20 hours of introductory training before commencing work. The permit holder is responsible for ensuring compliance with these training requirements for all employees and subcontractors.

heading: Municipal Forest Management
text: Municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, are also subject to the provisions of this Act when conducting forestry activities on lands they manage. While some administrative procedures may be streamlined, all requirements regarding permits, operational plans, reforestation, and environmental protection remain fully applicable. Municipalities are encouraged to develop long-term forest management plans, which, once approved by the Nordvale Forest Authority, can facilitate the permitting process for routine operations. These plans must be reviewed every 10 years.

heading: Municipal Forest Management
text: Municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, and Elsby, are also subject to the provisions of this Act when conducting forestry activities on lands they manage. While some administrative procedures may be streamlined for maintenance, all requirements regarding permits, operational plans, reforestation (minimum 2.5 trees per harvested tree), and environmental protection remain fully applicable. Municipalities are required to develop long-term forest management plans covering a minimum of 20 years, which, once approved by the Nordvale Forest Authority, can facilitate the permitting process for routine operations. These plans must be reviewed every 5 years and include a dedicated section on climate resilience.

heading: Advisory Committee
text: The Nordvale Forest Authority shall establish an Advisory Committee on Sustainable Forestry. This committee will comprise 7 members, including representatives from environmental organizations, the forestry industry, and academic institutions. The committee's role is to provide expert advice on policy development, review significant permit applications, and recommend best practices. Members will serve 3-year terms and meet quarterly. Their recommendations are non-binding but will be given serious consideration by the Authority in its decision-making processes.

heading: Data Collection and Research
text: The Nordvale Forest Authority will collect and maintain data on all permitted forestry activities, including harvested volumes, reforestation success rates, and environmental incidents. This data will be used for research purposes to improve sustainable forestry practices and inform future policy decisions. An annual report summarizing key findings will be published and made available to the public. Permit holders are required to cooperate with data collection efforts and provide accurate information as requested by the Authority.

heading: Penalties for Unauthorized Felling
text: Any person or entity found to be conducting forestry activities without a valid permit will be subject to severe penalties. This includes an immediate cessation order for all operations, a fine of 500 crowns per cubic meter of timber harvested illegally, and an additional administrative penalty of up to 15,000 crowns. The illegally harvested timber will be confiscated, and the responsible party will be obligated to fully reforest the affected area at their own expense, with a minimum of 4 trees planted for every illegally felled tree.

heading: Fines for Non-Compliance
text: Failure to comply with any condition of a valid Forestry Management Permit or any provision of this Act will result in fines ranging from 500 crowns to 10,000 crowns, depending on the severity of the violation. Repeated offenses will incur escalating fines and may lead to permit suspension or revocation. All fines must be paid within 30 days of issuance. The Nordvale Forest Authority reserves the right to pursue legal action for persistent non-compliance or significant environmental damage.

heading: Fines for Non-Compliance
text: Failure to comply with any condition of a valid Forestry Management Permit or any provision of this Act will result in fines ranging from 1,000 crowns to 25,000 crowns, depending on the severity and environmental impact of the violation. Repeated offenses will incur escalating fines (up to 50,000 crowns for a third offense within 24 months) and may lead to permit suspension or revocation. All fines must be paid within 21 days of issuance. The Nordvale Forest Authority reserves the right to pursue legal action for persistent non-compliance or significant environmental damage, including cost recovery for remediation efforts.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The Nordvale Forest Authority is the primary body responsible for the enforcement of this Act. This includes processing permit applications, conducting inspections, investigating complaints, issuing fines, and initiating legal proceedings where necessary. The Authority has the power to issue stop-work orders for non-compliant operations and to seize equipment involved in illegal activities. All decisions made by the Authority are subject to the appeals process outlined in section 11.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a competent court of law, the remaining provisions of this Act shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of other sections. This ensures that the core regulatory framework for forestry management in Nordvale continues to operate effectively, even if minor parts are challenged or modified through legal processes, maintaining regulatory consistency.

heading: Interpretation
text: This Act shall be interpreted in a manner that promotes sustainable forestry, environmental protection, and public safety. Any ambiguities in the text shall be resolved in favour of stricter environmental protection and the long-term health of Nordvale's forests. The Nordvale Forest Authority shall issue interpretive guidelines as needed to clarify the application of specific sections, and these guidelines will be made publicly available to ensure transparency and consistent understanding across all stakeholders within the forestry sector.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any forestry operations that commenced prior to the effective date of this Act, and which would now require a permit, must apply for an appropriate permit within 180 days of this Act coming into force. During this 180-day transitional period, existing operations may continue, provided they do not pose an immediate environmental hazard. Failure to apply for a permit within this period will result in the operation being considered unauthorized and subject to penalties outlined in section 38. The Nordvale Forest Authority will prioritize these transitional applications.

heading: Definitions
text: For the purpose of this Act: (a) 'Forestry activities' means any operation involving the felling, removal, or significant alteration of trees over an area exceeding 0.05 hectares for commercial or non-commercial purposes, excluding minor tree removal for personal use; (b) 'Nordvale Forest Authority' refers to the governmental body responsible for regulating forestry within the Republic; (c) 'Reforestation' means the planting of new trees to replace those harvested, aiming for ecological restoration; (d) 'Timber' includes all wood products derived from felled trees, measured in cubic meters.

heading: Annual Review
text: The Nordvale Forest Authority shall conduct an annual review of the effectiveness of this Act and its associated regulations. This review will assess permit issuance rates, compliance levels, environmental impacts, and the overall health of Nordvale's forests. Recommendations for amendments or improvements to the Act will be submitted to the Nordvale Legislature by March 1st of each year. A public summary of the annual review will be published by April 1st, providing transparency to citizens in all municipalities, including Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Exemptions for Public Infrastructure
text: Forestry activities undertaken by Nordvale governmental bodies or their contractors specifically for the construction or maintenance of essential public infrastructure, such as roads or utility lines, may be partially exempt from certain permit requirements. However, a detailed environmental impact report must still be submitted and approved by the Nordvale Forest Authority. All reforestation obligations remain in full effect, and compensatory planting at a 1:2 ratio (two trees planted for every one removed) is generally required. These projects must still comply with all safety and environmental protection measures.

heading: Exemptions for Public Infrastructure
text: Forestry activities undertaken by Nordvale governmental bodies or their contractors specifically for the construction or maintenance of essential public infrastructure, such as major roads, high-voltage power lines, or critical communication networks, may be partially exempt from certain permit requirements, particularly regarding processing times. However, a comprehensive environmental impact report, including a biodiversity assessment, must still be submitted and approved by the Nordvale Forest Authority. All reforestation obligations remain in full effect, and compensatory planting at a 1:3 ratio (three trees planted for every one removed) is mandatory. These projects must still comply with all safety and heightened environmental protection measures, and any removed timber must be salvaged and utilized where feasible.

heading: Timber Volume Calculation
text: For the purposes of permit applications and reporting, timber volume shall be calculated using standard Nordvale forestry measurement protocols. This involves measuring the diameter at breast height (DBH) and total height of each tree or applying approved volume tables for specific species. Applicants must specify the calculation method used in their operational plan. The Nordvale Forest Authority may conduct spot checks to verify reported volumes, and any discrepancies exceeding 10% will be subject to investigation and potential penalties as outlined in section 39.

heading: Protection of Young Growth
text: During any forestry operation, reasonable care must be taken to protect existing young growth and saplings that are not designated for felling. This includes planning extraction routes to minimize damage and educating machine operators on careful maneuvering. Damage to more than 20% of non-harvested young trees within a given area will be considered a violation of the permit conditions and may incur fines. The operational plan must include specific strategies for protecting young growth during harvesting activities.

heading: Forestry Activity near Settlements
text: Forestry activities proposed within 200 meters of any established residential settlement, such as those found in Fennick or Grauby, require additional approval from the local municipal council. This is in addition to the standard Forestry Management Permit. The municipal council will assess potential impacts on residents, including visual amenity and access. A minimum 30-day notice period must be given to all affected residents, and any significant concerns must be addressed by the applicant before municipal approval is granted. Operations in these areas are subject to stricter oversight.

heading: Forestry Activity near Settlements
text: Forestry activities proposed within 300 meters of any established residential settlement, public park, or designated recreational trail, such as those found in Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale, require additional approval from the local municipal council. This is in addition to the standard Forestry Management Permit. The municipal council will assess potential impacts on residents, including visual amenity, safety, and access. A minimum 45-day notice period must be given to all affected residents, and any significant concerns must be thoroughly addressed by the applicant and documented before municipal approval is granted. Operations in these areas are subject to stricter oversight, and a dedicated public liaison officer from the operating company must be appointed.

heading: Forest Fire Prevention
text: All forestry operations must implement robust forest fire prevention measures. This includes maintaining firebreaks, ensuring immediate access to fire suppression equipment on site, and prohibiting open fires. During periods of high fire risk, as declared by the Nordvale Fire Service, all logging activities may be temporarily suspended. The permit holder is responsible for training all personnel in fire prevention and emergency response. Failure to comply with fire prevention guidelines will result in severe penalties and potential liability for fire damage.

heading: Independent Audit
text: For all Forestry Management Permits covering an area greater than 10 hectares, or involving timber volumes exceeding 500 cubic meters, an independent audit of compliance with this Act and the permit conditions is required. The audit must be conducted by a certified independent auditor, approved by the Nordvale Forest Authority, within 6 months of the completion of operations. The audit report, at the expense of the permit holder, must be submitted to the Authority. Failure to submit an audit report will incur a fine of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Indigenous Tree Species
text: Reforestation efforts must prioritize the planting of indigenous tree species native to the specific region of Nordvale where the felling occurred. A minimum of 90% of all replanted trees must be indigenous. The operational plan must specify the proposed species, their origin, and how their genetic diversity will be maintained. The introduction of non-native species for reforestation is strictly prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Nordvale Forest Authority for experimental or research purposes, and only under controlled conditions.

heading: Review of Penalties
text: The Nordvale Forest Authority shall review the schedule of penalties and fines outlined in this Act every 3 years. This review will ensure that penalties remain appropriate and effective in deterring non-compliance and promoting sustainable forestry practices. Any proposed adjustments to the penalty schedule will be subject to public consultation for a period of 60 days before being submitted to the Nordvale Legislature for approval. The first review is scheduled for the year 2027.

heading: Voluntary Certification
text: Permit holders may opt to pursue voluntary certification under internationally recognized sustainable forestry standards. While not mandatory, achieving such certification can lead to a reduction in the annual permit renewal fee by 20% and may result in expedited processing for subsequent permit applications. The Nordvale Forest Authority will recognize certifications from approved bodies and will publish a list of such bodies on its official website. This initiative aims to encourage best practices beyond minimum legal requirements.

heading: Voluntary Certification
text: Permit holders may opt to pursue voluntary certification under internationally recognized sustainable forestry standards. While not mandatory, achieving such certification can lead to a reduction in the annual permit renewal fee by 30% and may result in expedited processing for subsequent permit applications, reducing review times by up to 15 days. The Nordvale Forest Authority will recognize certifications from approved bodies and will publish a list of such bodies on its official website, updated quarterly. This initiative aims to encourage best practices beyond minimum legal requirements and reward exemplary environmental stewardship.

heading: Concessions
text: Where the person liable is a certified hoof trimmer, the period for paying the fee or allowance in HOA §10 is extended by 30 days.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered cartographer shall pay half of the fee or allowance mentioned in SBA §11.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates campsites and the use of caravans and tents in Nordvale.
(2) It applies to every campsite open to the public and to camping outside campsites.
(3) Camping for a military or rescue purpose is not covered by this Act.

heading: Campsite licence
text:
(1) A person who runs a campsite shall hold a campsite licence from the municipality.
(2) The licence fee is 200 crowns per year.
(3) The municipality shall decide on an application within 45 days.

heading: Campsite licence
text:
(1) A person who runs a campsite shall hold a campsite licence from the municipality.
(2) The licence fee is 240 crowns per year.
(3) The municipality shall decide on an application within 45 days.

heading: Standards for campsites
text:
(1) A campsite shall have at least one toilet for every 25 pitches.
(2) A campsite shall have at least one shower for every 40 pitches.
(3) Each pitch shall be at least 40 square metres.

heading: Pitch fees at campsites
text:
(1) A campsite may charge for a tent pitch at most 14 crowns per night.
(2) A campsite may charge for a caravan pitch at most 20 crowns per night.
(3) A child under 6 years stays free of charge.

heading: Pitch fees at campsites
text:
(1) A campsite may charge for a tent pitch at most 16 crowns per night.
(2) A campsite may charge for a caravan pitch at most 23 crowns per night.
(3) A child under 6 years stays free of charge.

heading: Electricity at pitches
text:
(1) A campsite may charge at most 3 crowns per night for an electricity connection.
(2) The connection shall supply at least 10 amperes.
(3) The campsite shall state the price at the entrance.

heading: Length of stay
text:
(1) A guest may stay at a campsite for at most 60 consecutive nights.
(2) After 60 nights the guest shall leave for at least 14 nights.
(3) A campsite shall keep a register of guests for 12 months.

heading: Quiet hours
text:
(1) Quiet hours at a campsite are from 23:00 to 07:00.
(2) A guest who disturbs others during quiet hours may be asked to leave.
(3) A campsite may set longer quiet hours with a notice at the entrance.

heading: Quiet hours
text:
(1) Quiet hours at a campsite are from 22:00 to 07:00.
(2) A guest who disturbs others during quiet hours may be asked to leave.
(3) A campsite may set longer quiet hours with a notice at the entrance.

heading: Camping outside campsites
text:
(1) A person may pitch a tent outside a campsite for one night on land that is not cultivated.
(2) The person shall stay at least 150 metres from an inhabited building.
(3) A person shall not light an open fire outside a campsite.

heading: Camping on private land
text:
(1) A person who camps on private land needs the landowner's consent.
(2) A landowner may allow camping for at most 28 nights in a calendar year without a campsite licence.
(3) A landowner shall not charge more than the limit in section 4 for a pitch.

heading: Caravan parking
text:
(1) A caravan may be parked on a public road for at most 48 hours.
(2) A caravan shall not be used for sleeping while parked on a public road.
(3) A municipality may mark places where caravans may stay for 72 hours.

heading: Motorhome waste disposal
text:
(1) A motorhome shall empty its waste tank only at a designated disposal point.
(2) A municipality with at least 5,000 inhabitants shall provide at least one disposal point.
(3) A disposal point shall be free of charge.

heading: Motorhome waste disposal
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Fire safety
text:
(1) A campsite shall have one fire extinguisher for every 20 pitches.
(2) A campsite shall display an escape plan at the entrance.
(3) A campsite shall hold a fire drill at least once each season.

heading: Cooking and barbecues
text:
(1) A guest may use a barbecue only in places marked by the campsite.
(2) A barbecue shall stand at least 3 metres from a tent.
(3) A guest shall not leave a lit barbecue unattended.

heading: Waste at campsites
text:
(1) A campsite shall provide waste containers within 50 metres of every pitch.
(2) A guest shall sort waste into at least 3 categories.
(3) A campsite that does not sort waste shall pay a fine of 120 crowns.

heading: Waste at campsites
text:
(1) A campsite shall provide waste containers within 40 metres of every pitch.
(2) A guest shall sort waste into at least 4 categories.
(3) A campsite that does not sort waste shall pay a fine of 150 crowns.

heading: Pets at campsites
text:
(1) A guest may bring a pet to a campsite only if the campsite allows it.
(2) A pet shall be kept on a lead no longer than 2 metres.
(3) A campsite may charge at most 3 crowns per night for a pet.

heading: Seasonal campsites
text:
(1) A seasonal campsite may be open from 1 May to 30 September.
(2) A seasonal campsite shall publish its opening dates by 1 March.
(3) A seasonal campsite shall not accept guests outside its season.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) A municipal inspector may inspect a campsite once a year without notice.
(2) The inspector may order repairs to be made within 30 days.
(3) A campsite that fails to make repairs may lose its licence for up to 6 months.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who runs a campsite without a licence shall pay a fine of 500 crowns.
(2) A guest who stays longer than allowed in section 6 shall pay a fine of 60 crowns.
(3) A person who lights an open fire in breach of section 8 shall pay a fine of 100 crowns.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who runs a campsite without a licence shall pay a fine of 600 crowns.
(2) A guest who stays longer than allowed in section 6 shall pay a fine of 75 crowns.
(3) A person who lights an open fire in breach of section 8 shall pay a fine of 120 crowns.

heading: Register of campsites
text:
(1) Each municipality shall keep a public register of the campsites in its area.
(2) The register shall be updated within 14 days of each change.
(3) The register shall state the number of pitches of each campsite.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision of a municipality under this Act may appeal within 30 days.
(2) The appeal shall be decided within 60 days.
(3) An appeal does not suspend an order under section 17.

heading: Trail pass for volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) The annual trail pass under MTA §7 costs 20 crowns for an active volunteer firefighter.
(2) The daily trail permit is charged in full.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for all applications concerning Nordvalean citizenship. It outlines the specific amounts due for various application types, including initial citizenship applications, renewals of temporary citizenship, and appeals of decisions made regarding citizenship status. The Act aims to ensure that the administrative costs associated with processing citizenship applications are partially defrayed by the applicants, while maintaining accessibility for all eligible individuals. All fees specified herein are denominated in crowns and are non-refundable, except as explicitly stated in section 28. This Act applies to all individuals seeking or holding Nordvalean citizenship, regardless of their current municipality of residence within Nordvale.

heading: Standard Application Fee
text: The standard fee for an initial application for Nordvalean citizenship is 5,000 crowns. This fee applies to all adult applicants, defined as individuals aged 18 years or older at the time of application submission. The fee covers the administrative processing of the application, including document verification, background checks, and the final decision review. This standard fee is payable at the time of application submission and must be remitted in full. Failure to pay the full amount will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without processing. No partial payments are accepted for the standard application fee.

heading: Standard Application Fee
text: The standard fee for an initial application for Nordvalean citizenship is 6,000 crowns. This fee applies to all adult applicants, defined as individuals aged 18 years or older at the time of application submission. The fee covers the administrative processing of the application, including document verification, background checks, and the final decision review. This standard fee is payable at the time of application submission and must be remitted in full. Failure to pay the full amount will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without processing. No partial payments are accepted for the standard application fee, and an additional 150 crowns administrative charge applies to returned applications.

heading: Standard Application Fee
text: The standard fee for an initial application for Nordvalean citizenship is 6,250 crowns. This fee applies to all adult applicants, defined as individuals aged 18 years or older at the time of application submission. The fee covers the administrative processing of the application, including document verification, background checks, and the final decision review. This standard fee is payable at the time of application submission and must be remitted in full. Failure to pay the full amount will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without processing. No partial payments are accepted for the standard application fee, and an additional 200 crowns administrative charge applies to returned applications.

heading: Minor Applicant Fee
text: For applicants under the age of 18, referred to as minor applicants, the fee for an initial application for Nordvalean citizenship is 1,200 crowns. This reduced fee acknowledges the different administrative requirements for minors and is intended to facilitate family applications. The minor applicant fee is applicable only when the minor is applying concurrently with at least one parent or legal guardian who is also applying for or already holds Nordvalean citizenship. If a minor applies independently, the standard application fee outlined in section 2 applies. Documentation proving legal guardianship or parental relationship must be submitted with the application.

heading: Minor Applicant Fee
text: For applicants under the age of 18, referred to as minor applicants, the fee for an initial application for Nordvalean citizenship is 1,500 crowns. This reduced fee acknowledges the different administrative requirements for minors and is intended to facilitate family applications. The minor applicant fee is applicable only when the minor is applying concurrently with at least one parent or legal guardian who is also applying for or already holds Nordvalean citizenship. If a minor applies independently, the standard application fee outlined in section 2 applies. Documentation proving legal guardianship or parental relationship must be submitted with the application, dated within 90 days of the application submission.

heading: Minor Applicant Fee
text: For applicants under the age of 18, referred to as minor applicants, the fee for an initial application for Nordvalean citizenship is 1,600 crowns. This reduced fee acknowledges the different administrative requirements for minors and is intended to facilitate family applications. The minor applicant fee is applicable only when the minor is applying concurrently with at least one parent or legal guardian who is also applying for or already holds Nordvalean citizenship. If a minor applies independently, the standard application fee outlined in section 2 applies. Documentation proving legal guardianship or parental relationship must be submitted with the application, dated within 60 days of the application submission.

heading: Family Application Discount
text: A discount is available for families applying for citizenship concurrently. If three or more individuals from the same immediate family (parents and their minor children) submit their initial citizenship applications together, a 10% reduction is applied to the total sum of their individual application fees. This discount is calculated after applying any specific minor applicant fees. All applications must be submitted within a 7-day period to qualify for this family discount. The primary applicant must indicate the intention to apply as a family unit at the time of submission to ensure proper processing of the discount.

heading: Family Application Discount
text: A discount is available for families applying for citizenship concurrently. If three or more individuals from the same immediate family (parents and their minor children) submit their initial citizenship applications together, a 12% reduction is applied to the total sum of their individual application fees. This discount is calculated after applying any specific minor applicant fees. All applications must be submitted within a 14-day period to qualify for this family discount. The primary applicant must indicate the intention to apply as a family unit at the time of submission to ensure proper processing of the discount.

heading: Family Application Discount
text: A discount is available for families applying for citizenship concurrently. If three or more individuals from the same immediate family (parents and their minor children) submit their initial citizenship applications together, a 15% reduction is applied to the total sum of their individual application fees. This discount is calculated after applying any specific minor applicant fees. All applications must be submitted within a 21-day period to qualify for this family discount. The primary applicant must indicate the intention to apply as a family unit at the time of submission to ensure proper processing of the discount. This discount does not apply to applications involving more than 5 family members.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: Applicants desiring an expedited processing of their citizenship application may opt to pay an additional fee of 2,500 crowns. This fee guarantees that the application will be reviewed within 60 days from the date of submission, provided all necessary documentation is complete and accurate. The standard processing time for applications without expedited processing is typically 180 days. The expedited processing fee is separate from the standard application fee and must be paid in full at the time of application submission. This option is available for all application types, including those for minor applicants, but does not guarantee approval.

heading: Renewal of Temporary Citizenship
text: Individuals holding temporary Nordvalean citizenship must apply for renewal prior to its expiration. The fee for renewing temporary citizenship is 800 crowns. This fee covers the administrative review of the applicant's continued eligibility and compliance with any conditions associated with their temporary status. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 30 days before the expiration date of the temporary citizenship. Failure to renew within this timeframe may result in the temporary citizenship lapsing, requiring a new initial application to be submitted, along with the corresponding standard application fee.

heading: Late Renewal Penalty
text: A late penalty of 200 crowns will be applied to all temporary citizenship renewal applications submitted less than 30 days but more than 7 days prior to the expiration date. This penalty is in addition to the standard renewal fee specified in section 6. Applications submitted 7 days or less before the expiration date will be treated as lapsed and will require a new initial application, incurring the standard application fee as per section 2. It is the responsibility of the temporary citizen to ensure timely submission of their renewal application to avoid these additional charges or the loss of their temporary status.

heading: Late Renewal Penalty
text: A late penalty of 300 crowns will be applied to all temporary citizenship renewal applications submitted less than 30 days but more than 10 days prior to the expiration date. This penalty is in addition to the standard renewal fee specified in section 6. Applications submitted 10 days or less before the expiration date will be treated as lapsed and will require a new initial application, incurring the standard application fee as per section 2. It is the responsibility of the temporary citizen to ensure timely submission of their renewal application to avoid these additional charges or the loss of their temporary status. The maximum late penalty combined with the renewal fee shall not exceed 1,500 crowns.

heading: Citizenship Ceremony Fee
text: Upon approval of a citizenship application, successful applicants are required to attend a citizenship ceremony. A nominal fee of 150 crowns is charged for participation in this ceremony. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with organizing the event, including the provision of a citizenship certificate. The ceremony fee must be paid within 30 days of receiving the approval notification. Failure to pay this fee or attend the scheduled ceremony without valid reason may result in a delay in the formal conferral of citizenship. Minor applicants are exempt from this fee.

heading: Citizenship Ceremony Fee
text: Upon approval of a citizenship application, successful applicants are required to attend a citizenship ceremony. A nominal fee of 180 crowns is charged for participation in this ceremony. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with organizing the event, including the provision of a citizenship certificate. The ceremony fee must be paid within 45 days of receiving the approval notification. Failure to pay this fee or attend the scheduled ceremony without valid reason may result in a delay in the formal conferral of citizenship. Minor applicants are exempt from this fee, and applicants over 70 years of age are also exempt.

heading: Re-scheduling Ceremony Fee
text: If an applicant needs to re-schedule their citizenship ceremony after the initial scheduling has been confirmed, a re-scheduling fee of 50 crowns applies. This fee covers the administrative effort involved in cancelling and re-booking the applicant for a new ceremony date. Re-scheduling requests must be made at least 14 days prior to the originally scheduled ceremony. Requests made less than 14 days in advance may incur an additional administrative charge of 25 crowns, unless supported by documented unforeseen circumstances such as illness or emergency.

heading: Appeal of Application Decision
text: Applicants wishing to appeal a decision regarding their citizenship application must submit an appeal within 90 days of receiving the decision notification. An appeal fee of 1,500 crowns is required to initiate the appeal process. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the appeal, including the re-evaluation of submitted documents and reconsideration of the application's merits. The appeal fee is non-refundable, even if the appeal is ultimately unsuccessful. The appeal committee will review the case within 120 days of receiving the appeal and fee.

heading: Hardship Waiver for Appeal Fee
text: Applicants facing demonstrable financial hardship may apply for a waiver of the appeal fee specified in section 10. To qualify for a waiver, applicants must provide documented evidence of their financial situation, such as recent income statements, proof of unemployment benefits, or a declaration of assets and liabilities. The waiver application will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, and approval is not guaranteed. A decision on the waiver request will be provided within 30 days of submission, and the appeal period will be extended by this review time.

heading: Certificate Replacement Fee
text: In the event that a Nordvalean citizenship certificate is lost, stolen, or damaged, a replacement can be obtained by paying a fee of 300 crowns. This fee covers the administrative cost of verifying citizenship status and issuing a new physical certificate. Applicants must provide a sworn affidavit detailing the circumstances of the loss, theft, or damage, along with any available remnants of the damaged certificate. Processing of a replacement certificate typically takes 45 days from the date of application and fee payment.

heading: Verification of Citizenship Status
text: Individuals requiring formal verification of their Nordvalean citizenship status for official purposes may request a verification letter. A fee of 100 crowns is charged for this service. The verification letter will confirm the individual's citizenship and the date of its conferral. This service is often used for international travel documents or applications for certain government benefits. The verification letter will be issued within 10 business days of receiving the request and fee. An additional 25 crowns applies for urgent requests requiring issuance within 3 business days.

heading: Declaration of Renunciation
text: Citizens of Nordvale wishing to formally renounce their citizenship must submit a declaration of renunciation. A processing fee of 2,000 crowns is associated with this declaration. This fee covers the administrative and legal review required to process the renunciation, ensuring all legal requirements are met and the individual's status is accurately updated in the national registry. The fee is non-refundable and must be paid at the time the declaration is submitted. Renunciation becomes effective 60 days after the declaration is accepted and all fees are paid.

heading: Declaration of Renunciation
text: Citizens of Nordvale wishing to formally renounce their citizenship must submit a declaration of renunciation. A processing fee of 2,200 crowns is associated with this declaration. This fee covers the administrative and legal review required to process the renunciation, ensuring all legal requirements are met and the individual's status is accurately updated in the national registry. The fee is non-refundable and must be paid at the time the declaration is submitted. Renunciation becomes effective 75 days after the declaration is accepted and all fees are paid, unless the renouncer is under 21 years of age.

heading: Affidavit for Lost Documents
text: When an applicant cannot provide original supporting documents due to loss or destruction, they may be required to submit a sworn affidavit. A fee of 50 crowns is charged for the administrative processing of such affidavits. This fee applies per affidavit submitted, and multiple affidavits may be required depending on the number of missing documents. The affidavit must be notarized by an authorized official and must clearly state the efforts made to retrieve the original documents. This fee is separate from any other application fees.

heading: Fee for Document Translation Review
text: All documents submitted in languages other than Nordvalean must be accompanied by certified translations. The Directorate of Citizenship charges a fee of 75 crowns per page for the review of these translated documents to ensure accuracy and compliance with official standards. This fee is in addition to the actual cost of translation incurred by the applicant. Documents with more than 500 words per page will be counted as two pages for fee calculation purposes. This review helps maintain the integrity of the application process and prevent fraudulent submissions.

heading: Fee for Document Translation Review
text: All documents submitted in languages other than Nordvalean must be accompanied by certified translations. The Directorate of Citizenship charges a fee of 90 crowns per page for the review of these translated documents to ensure accuracy and compliance with official standards. This fee is in addition to the actual cost of translation incurred by the applicant. Documents with more than 400 words per page will be counted as two pages for fee calculation purposes. This review helps maintain the integrity of the application process and prevent fraudulent submissions. This fee is capped at 750 crowns per application.

heading: Withdrawal of Application Fee
text: If an applicant chooses to withdraw their citizenship application after submission but before a decision is rendered, a withdrawal fee of 200 crowns applies. This fee covers the administrative work already performed on the application, including initial data entry and preliminary review. The remainder of the application fee, excluding this withdrawal fee, may be partially refunded as per section 28. Withdrawal requests must be submitted in writing and formally acknowledged by the Directorate of Citizenship to be valid.

heading: Reconsideration of Declined Appeal
text: Applicants whose initial appeal has been declined may request a reconsideration, provided new and substantive evidence is presented. A fee of 1,000 crowns is required for this second level of review. This fee covers the detailed assessment of the new evidence and the re-examination of the appeal decision. A request for reconsideration must be submitted within 60 days of the appeal decision notification. This fee is non-refundable and does not guarantee a reversal of the previous decision. Only one request for reconsideration is permitted per application.

heading: Fee for Special Circumstance Review
text: Applications requiring review based on exceptional or special circumstances, such as humanitarian grounds or significant contributions to Nordvalean society, may incur an additional review fee of 750 crowns. This fee covers the extended time and specialized expertise required to evaluate these complex cases outside of standard application criteria. The need for a special circumstance review must be identified and approved by the Directorate of Citizenship. This fee is determined on a case-by-case basis and will be communicated to the applicant if deemed necessary.

heading: Aldmark Residency Discount
text: Applicants who have resided continuously in the capital municipality of Aldmark for at least 5 years immediately preceding their application date are eligible for a 5% discount on their standard application fee. Proof of residency, such as utility bills, lease agreements, or property deeds, covering the entire 5-year period must be submitted with the application. This discount applies only to the standard application fee and cannot be combined with the family application discount. The discount will be applied automatically upon verification of residency.

heading: Aldmark Residency Discount
text: Applicants who have resided continuously in the capital municipality of Aldmark for at least 6 years immediately preceding their application date are eligible for a 7% discount on their standard application fee. Proof of residency, such as utility bills, lease agreements, or property deeds, covering the entire 6-year period must be submitted with the application. This discount applies only to the standard application fee and cannot be combined with the family application discount. The discount will be applied automatically upon verification of residency. This discount is capped at 400 crowns.

heading: Dunmere and Corvik Residency Discount
text: Applicants residing in the municipalities of Dunmere or Corvik for at least 3 years immediately preceding their application date are eligible for a 3% discount on their standard application fee. This initiative aims to encourage civic participation in these growing regions. Similar to the Aldmark discount, verifiable proof of continuous residency, such as official municipal registrations or tax statements, must be provided for the entire 3-year period. This discount is only applicable to the standard application fee and cannot be combined with other discounts.

heading: Reactivation of Lapsed Application
text: If an application lapses due to incomplete documentation or non-payment of fees and is subsequently reactivated within 6 months of the lapse date, a reactivation fee of 600 crowns will be charged. This fee covers the administrative effort to retrieve, review, and continue processing the application. After 6 months, a lapsed application cannot be reactivated, and a new application, along with all associated fees, must be submitted. This fee does not guarantee approval of the reactivated application.

heading: Fee for Oath of Allegiance Administration
text: In exceptional circumstances where an applicant cannot attend a group citizenship ceremony and requires a private administration of the Oath of Allegiance, a fee of 400 crowns applies. This fee covers the cost of arranging a special session with an authorized official to administer the oath. Requests for private administration must be accompanied by a valid reason, such as documented medical conditions or urgent travel requirements. Approval for a private oath administration is at the discretion of the Directorate of Citizenship.

heading: Correction of Errors Fee
text: If an applicant requires the Directorate of Citizenship to correct minor errors on their application form or submitted documents after submission, a correction fee of 80 crowns per error applies. This fee covers the administrative time and resources required to make the necessary amendments. Errors identified by the Directorate will be communicated to the applicant, who will then have 30 days to pay the fee and provide any required supporting information for the correction. Significant errors may lead to the application being deemed incomplete.

heading: Fee for Requesting Application Status Update
text: Applicants can typically track their application status online without charge. However, if an applicant requires a detailed, written status update or an in-person consultation regarding their application status outside of regular communication channels, a fee of 60 crowns applies. This fee covers the administrative time spent on preparing a personalized update or conducting a dedicated consultation. This fee is waived if the application has exceeded its standard processing time by more than 90 days.

heading: Fee for Requesting Application Status Update
text: Applicants can typically track their application status online without charge. However, if an applicant requires a detailed, written status update or an in-person consultation regarding their application status outside of regular communication channels, a fee of 75 crowns applies. This fee covers the administrative time spent on preparing a personalized update or conducting a dedicated consultation. This fee is waived if the application has exceeded its standard processing time by more than 75 days. Only one such paid request is allowed per 180-day period.

heading: Fee for Provisional Citizenship Document
text: In circumstances where an applicant's full citizenship certificate is pending but immediate proof of citizenship is required for urgent travel or other critical matters, a provisional citizenship document may be issued. A fee of 250 crowns applies for this service. The provisional document is valid for a maximum of 90 days and can only be issued after the application has been formally approved, but before the citizenship ceremony has taken place. This fee covers the expedited preparation and issuance of this temporary document.

heading: Refund Policy
text: All application fees are generally non-refundable. However, a partial refund of 50% of the standard application fee may be issued if an application is formally withdrawn within 14 days of submission and before any substantive processing has commenced. The withdrawal fee specified in section 17 will be deducted from any eligible refund amount. No refunds will be issued for expedited processing fees, appeal fees, or any fees related to services already rendered, such as document translation review or citizenship ceremonies, as per sections 5, 10, and 8 respectively.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in Nordvalean crowns. Acceptable payment methods include direct bank transfer, certified cheque, or credit/debit card payments processed through the official Directorate of Citizenship portal. Cash payments are only accepted for fees under 500 crowns and must be made in person at designated municipal offices in Aldmark or Brenholt. An administrative fee of 1% will be added to all credit/debit card transactions exceeding 1,000 crowns to cover processing charges. Payments must be made in full for each fee.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in Nordvalean crowns. Acceptable payment methods include direct bank transfer, certified cheque, or credit/debit card payments processed through the official Directorate of Citizenship portal. Cash payments are only accepted for fees under 300 crowns and must be made in person at designated municipal offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, or Corvik. An administrative fee of 1.5% will be added to all credit/debit card transactions exceeding 750 crowns to cover processing charges. Payments must be made in full for each fee, and a receipt will be issued for all payments over 100 crowns.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision of this Act, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Act which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this Act are severable. This ensures that the remainder of the Act remains in force and effect, preserving the general intent and regulatory framework for citizenship application fees, even if specific clauses are found to be unenforceable by the Nordvalean courts. The Directorate of Citizenship will issue guidance on any such severances.

heading: Sauna admission for regular blood donors
text:
(1) A regular blood donor pays 6 crowns for adult admission to a municipal sauna.
(2) The reduced price applies to one visit a day.
(3) The donor shows the donor record of the donation centre at the entrance.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the levying of duties on goods exported from the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all goods leaving Nordvale's customs territory, irrespective of their origin or destination. The primary purpose is to regulate trade flows and generate revenue for public services. This Act does not apply to goods in transit that do not enter Nordvale's domestic consumption.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Export duty' means any duty, tax, or charge of equivalent effect levied on goods due to their exportation from Nordvale.
(2) 'Exporter' means any natural or legal person who declares goods for export or on whose behalf the export declaration is made.
(3) 'Value' refers to the customs value of the goods determined in accordance with generally accepted valuation principles.

heading: General Duty Rate
text: Unless otherwise specified in this Act, a general export duty of 2% of the value of the goods is levied on all exported items. This general rate serves as a baseline for goods not subject to specific duty schedules. Exporters must declare the accurate value of goods to ensure correct duty calculation. Payments are due within 14 days of the export declaration.

heading: General Duty Rate
text: Unless otherwise specified in this Act, a general export duty of 2.5% of the value of the goods is levied on all exported items. This general rate serves as a baseline for goods not subject to specific duty schedules. Exporters must declare the accurate value of goods to ensure correct duty calculation. Payments are due within 10 days of the export declaration.

heading: General Duty Rate
text: Unless otherwise specified in this Act, a general export duty of 3% of the value of the goods is levied on all exported items. This general rate serves as a baseline for goods not subject to specific duty schedules. Exporters must declare the accurate value of goods to ensure correct duty calculation. Payments are due within 7 days of the export declaration. Goods with a value under 500 crowns are exempt from this general duty.

heading: Agricultural Products Duty
text: Exports of unprocessed agricultural products originating from Nordvale are subject to a duty of 1.5% of their declared value. This includes grains, raw vegetables, and fruits. Processed agricultural products are excluded from this specific duty and fall under the general duty rate specified in section 3. This duty aims to ensure sufficient domestic supply.

heading: Agricultural Products Duty
text: Exports of unprocessed agricultural products originating from Nordvale are subject to a duty of 1.8% of their declared value. This includes grains, raw vegetables, and fruits. Processed agricultural products are excluded from this specific duty and fall under the general duty rate specified in section 3. This duty aims to ensure sufficient domestic supply.

heading: Processed Goods Duty
text: Processed goods, defined as items that have undergone significant manufacturing or transformation within Nordvale, are subject to an export duty of 1% of their value. This lower rate encourages domestic value addition and supports local industries. Exporters must provide documentation proving the processing occurred within Nordvale for this reduced rate to apply.

heading: Strategic Minerals Duty
text: Certain strategic minerals, as identified by the Ministry of Resources, are subject to a higher export duty of 7% of their value. This measure is intended to conserve national resources and ensure long-term availability for domestic use. A detailed list of these minerals is published annually by the Ministry. This duty applies to raw and minimally processed forms.

heading: Strategic Minerals Duty
text: Certain strategic minerals, as identified by the Ministry of Resources, are subject to a higher export duty of 8% of their value. This measure is intended to conserve national resources and ensure long-term availability for domestic use. A detailed list of these minerals is published annually by the Ministry. This duty applies to raw and minimally processed forms. Exports exceeding 1000 kg per consignment also incur an additional fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Timber and Wood Products Duty
text: Unprocessed timber and logs exported from Nordvale are subject to a duty of 5% of their value. This encourages domestic processing and reduces raw material outflow. Sawn timber, plywood, and other processed wood products are subject to a reduced duty of 2.5% to promote local manufacturing. The volume of timber exported must be accurately measured.

heading: Timber and Wood Products Duty
text: Unprocessed timber and logs exported from Nordvale are subject to a duty of 6% of their value. This encourages domestic processing and reduces raw material outflow. Sawn timber, plywood, and other processed wood products are subject to a reduced duty of 3% to promote local manufacturing. The volume of timber exported must be accurately measured. Exports originating from the Lund Vale region receive a 0.5% reduction on these rates due to specific regional development policies.

heading: Textile Exports Duty
text: Exports of textiles manufactured in Nordvale are subject to a duty of 0.8% of their value. This low rate is designed to support the textile industry's competitiveness in international markets. This applies to finished garments, fabrics, and yarns produced within Nordvale. Exporters must maintain records of production origin for verification.

heading: Fishery Products Duty
text: Raw and unprocessed fishery products, including fresh and frozen fish, are subject to an export duty of 3.5% of their value. This aims to maintain domestic supply and support local processing industries. Canned or otherwise processed fishery products are subject to a lower rate of 1.5% as they represent higher value-added goods. Exporters must declare species and weight.

heading: Fishery Products Duty
text: Raw and unprocessed fishery products, including fresh and frozen fish, are subject to an export duty of 4% of their value. This aims to maintain domestic supply and support local processing industries. Canned or otherwise processed fishery products are subject to a lower rate of 1.8% as they represent higher value-added goods. Exporters must declare species and weight. Consignments under 50 kg are exempt from this duty.

heading: Manufacturing Machinery Duty
text: Exports of manufacturing machinery produced in Nordvale are subject to a duty of 0.5% of their value. This extremely low rate is intended to promote Nordvale's industrial engineering sector and facilitate its global reach. This applies to new machinery only; used machinery falls under the general duty rate in section 3. Proof of manufacture in Nordvale is required.

heading: Electronic Components Duty
text: Electronic components manufactured in Nordvale are subject to an export duty of 0.75% of their value. This duty supports the growing electronics sector by balancing revenue generation with export competitiveness. This applies to components, circuit boards, and integrated circuits. Finished electronic devices are subject to a separate duty schedule.

heading: Precious Metals Duty
text: Raw precious metals, including gold, silver, and platinum, are subject to an export duty of 10% of their market value. This high rate reflects their strategic importance and limited availability. Refined precious metals or those incorporated into finished products are subject to a duty of 4%. Exporters must declare purity and weight.

heading: Precious Metals Duty
text: Raw precious metals, including gold, silver, and platinum, are subject to an export duty of 12% of their market value. This high rate reflects their strategic importance and limited availability. Refined precious metals or those incorporated into finished products are subject to a duty of 5%. Exporters must declare purity and weight. Any single export consignment exceeding 1 kg of raw precious metals requires prior approval from the Ministry of Finance.

heading: Cultural Artifacts Duty
text: Exports of cultural artifacts deemed of national heritage significance are subject to a duty of 20% of their appraised value. This duty is primarily a deterrent and revenue generator for the preservation of cultural sites. Prior authorization from the Ministry of Culture is mandatory for any such export. Unauthorized export incurs severe penalties.

heading: Art and Craft Exports Duty
text: Original works of art and handcrafted items by Nordvale artists are subject to an export duty of 2% of their declared value. This encourages the growth of the domestic art market while acknowledging the cultural value of such exports. A certificate of authenticity from a recognized Nordvale art institution is required for this specific duty rate.

heading: Books and Publications Duty
text: Books, periodicals, and other printed publications exported from Nordvale are exempt from export duties. This exemption supports the free flow of information and knowledge. This applies to both newly published and second-hand materials. The exemption does not apply to publications classified as cultural artifacts under section 13.

heading: Educational Materials Duty
text: Educational materials, including textbooks, scientific journals, and learning aids, are exempt from export duties. This policy promotes international academic exchange and contributes to global education initiatives. The exporter must provide documentation confirming the educational purpose of the materials. This exemption does not cover general office supplies.

heading: Medical Supplies Duty
text: Essential medical supplies and pharmaceuticals manufactured in Nordvale are exempt from export duties. This exemption supports humanitarian efforts and the global health sector. The Ministry of Health maintains a list of qualifying essential medical supplies. This does not extend to non-essential or cosmetic medical products.

heading: High-Tech Goods Duty
text: Goods classified as high-technology products, which include advanced robotics, specialized software, and precision instruments, are subject to a reduced export duty of 0.25% of their value. This low rate is designed to foster innovation and encourage the export of sophisticated Nordvale-made products. Certification from the Ministry of Technology is required.

heading: Recycled Materials Duty
text: Exports of recycled materials, such as processed scrap metal, plastic pellets, and paper pulp, are subject to an export duty of 1% of their value. This duty encourages domestic recycling and reuse while generating revenue. Exporters must provide evidence that the materials have undergone a recycling process within Nordvale. Unsorted waste is prohibited from export.

heading: Energy Products Duty
text: Exports of crude oil, natural gas, and refined petroleum products are subject to a duty of 6% of their value. This contributes significantly to national revenue and helps regulate the supply of critical energy resources. The duty applies to all quantities exported, regardless of destination. Regular adjustments to this rate may occur based on global market prices.

heading: Energy Products Duty
text: Exports of crude oil, natural gas, and refined petroleum products are subject to a duty of 7% of their value. This contributes significantly to national revenue and helps regulate the supply of critical energy resources. The duty applies to all quantities exported, regardless of destination. Regular adjustments to this rate may occur based on global market prices. Exports of less than 100 barrels of crude oil are subject to a reduced rate of 4%.

heading: Pharmaceutical Ingredients Duty
text: Raw pharmaceutical ingredients, excluding those on the essential medical supplies list in section 17, are subject to an export duty of 2.5% of their value. This promotes domestic pharmaceutical production. Exporters must accurately declare the chemical composition and intended use of these ingredients. Final pharmaceutical products are covered by other sections.

heading: Cement and Construction Materials Duty
text: Exports of cement, bricks, and other basic construction materials originating from Nordvale are subject to a duty of 1.2% of their value. This ensures sufficient domestic supply for infrastructure projects. Specialized construction components and pre-fabricated structures may fall under different duty rates, such as those for processed goods.

heading: Special Exemptions for Aid
text: Goods exported as part of officially recognized humanitarian aid or disaster relief efforts are exempt from all export duties. Exporters must obtain certification from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs prior to shipment. This exemption applies only to goods destined for direct aid and not for commercial resale. The application must be submitted at least 15 days in advance.

heading: Duty on Exports to Specific Regions
text: Exports to regions bordering Nordvale are subject to a reduced general duty rate of 1.8% instead of the 2% specified in section 3. This policy aims to foster regional economic cooperation and trade relations. This reduced rate applies only to goods directly transported across land borders to contiguous nations. Maritime exports do not qualify.

heading: Duty on Exports to Specific Regions
text: Exports to regions bordering Nordvale are subject to a reduced general duty rate of 1.5% instead of the 2.5% specified in section 3. This policy aims to foster regional economic cooperation and trade relations. This reduced rate applies only to goods directly transported across land borders to contiguous nations. Maritime exports do not qualify. This rate is further reduced to 1% for goods manufactured in the Dunmere region.

heading: Temporary Export Exemption
text: Goods exported for temporary purposes, such as exhibition, repair, or professional equipment for a period not exceeding 180 days, may be exempt from duty. A bond equivalent to the duty amount must be deposited, which is refunded upon re-importation within the specified timeframe. Failure to re-import within 180 days results in forfeiture of the bond.

heading: Temporary Export Exemption
text: Goods exported for temporary purposes, such as exhibition, repair, or professional equipment for a period not exceeding 270 days, may be exempt from duty. A bond equivalent to 120% of the duty amount must be deposited, which is refunded upon re-importation within the specified timeframe. Failure to re-import within 270 days results in forfeiture of the bond. Goods valued under 1000 crowns are exempt from the bond requirement.

heading: Goods for Diplomatic Missions
text: Goods exported for the official use of Nordvale's diplomatic missions abroad are exempt from export duties. This exemption is granted upon official request from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It covers items necessary for the operation of embassies, consulates, and other diplomatic posts. Personal effects of diplomatic staff are not covered by this section.

heading: Penalties for Misdeclaration
text: Any exporter found to have intentionally misdeclared the value, quantity, or nature of goods to evade export duties shall be subject to a penalty of three times the evaded duty amount, with a minimum penalty of 5,000 crowns. Repeated offenses may lead to suspension of export privileges for up to 12 months. Investigations will be conducted by the customs authority.

heading: Penalties for Misdeclaration
text: Any exporter found to have intentionally misdeclared the value, quantity, or nature of goods to evade export duties shall be subject to a penalty of four times the evaded duty amount, with a minimum penalty of 10,000 crowns. Repeated offenses may lead to suspension of export privileges for up to 24 months. Investigations will be conducted by the customs authority, and a public record of offenders will be maintained for 5 years.

heading: Interest on Late Payments
text: Payments of export duties made after the due date specified in section 3 are subject to an interest charge of 0.5% per month or part thereof, calculated on the outstanding duty amount. This interest accrues from the day following the due date until the date of full payment. A grace period of 3 days may be granted in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Duty Refunds
text: Exporters may apply for a refund of duties paid in error or for goods subsequently returned to Nordvale due to defects or non-compliance. Applications must be submitted within 90 days of the export date or return date, respectively. Approved refunds will be processed within 60 days of the application. A 5% administrative fee may be deducted from the refund.

heading: Duty Refunds
text: Exporters may apply for a refund of duties paid in error or for goods subsequently returned to Nordvale due to defects or non-compliance. Applications must be submitted within 120 days of the export date or return date, respectively. Approved refunds will be processed within 45 days of the application. A 3% administrative fee may be deducted from the refund, provided the refund amount exceeds 1,000 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping Requirements
text: All exporters are required to maintain accurate and complete records of all export transactions, including invoices, customs declarations, and proof of origin, for a minimum period of 5 years. These records must be readily available for inspection by customs authorities upon request. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Exporters have the right to appeal decisions regarding duty assessments, penalties, or refunds. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Customs Appeals Board within 30 days of the contested decision. The Board will issue a decision within 90 days of receiving the appeal. A fee of 500 crowns is required to initiate an appeal.

heading: Duty on Waste Materials
text: Exports of industrial waste materials, including chemical byproducts and hazardous substances, are subject to a duty of 15% of their declared value. This high rate aims to discourage the export of waste and promote domestic responsible disposal or recycling. Specific permits from the Ministry of Environment are also required for such exports.

heading: Duty on Waste Materials
text: Exports of industrial waste materials, including chemical byproducts and hazardous substances, are subject to a duty of 18% of their declared value. This high rate aims to discourage the export of waste and promote domestic responsible disposal or recycling. Specific permits from the Ministry of Environment are also required for such exports. A minimum duty of 10,000 crowns applies to all consignments exceeding 1,000 kg.

heading: Exemption for Small Consignments
text: Consignments of goods with a total declared value not exceeding 1,000 crowns are exempt from export duties, provided they are not part of a larger, split shipment intended to circumvent duties. This exemption simplifies procedures for small-scale exporters. This threshold applies per single export declaration. The exemption does not apply to strategic minerals or cultural artifacts.

heading: Duty on Rare Earth Elements
text: Exports of raw rare earth elements are subject to a duty of 18% of their market value. This extremely high duty reflects their critical importance to advanced industries and their limited global supply. Processed rare earth compounds are subject to a duty of 9%. The Ministry of Resources closely monitors all such exports. Any export exceeding 100 grams requires a special license.

heading: Duty on Specialized Tools
text: Specialized tools and industrial equipment manufactured in Nordvale are subject to an export duty of 0.7% of their value. This encourages the export of high-quality domestic manufacturing output. This rate applies to tools designed for specific industrial applications, not general-purpose hand tools. Certification of specialization may be requested.

heading: Agricultural Machinery Duty
text: Exports of agricultural machinery produced in Nordvale are subject to a duty of 0.6% of their value. This low rate supports the agricultural equipment manufacturing sector. This applies to tractors, harvesters, and other farm implements. Used agricultural machinery may be subject to different rates based on its condition and age.

heading: Gemstone Duty
text: Uncut and unpolished gemstones originating from Nordvale are subject to an export duty of 8% of their appraised value. This policy aims to encourage domestic cutting and polishing industries. Cut and polished gemstones are subject to a lower duty of 3.5%. The appraisal must be conducted by an authorized Nordvale gemologist.

heading: Gemstone Duty
text: Uncut and unpolished gemstones originating from Nordvale are subject to an export duty of 9% of their appraised value. This policy aims to encourage domestic cutting and polishing industries. Cut and polished gemstones are subject to a lower duty of 4%. The appraisal must be conducted by an authorized Nordvale gemologist. Exports of rough diamonds exceeding 50 carats are subject to a special license fee of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Water Exports Duty
text: Bulk exports of fresh water from Nordvale are subject to a duty of 0.1 crown per liter. This duty reflects the strategic importance of water resources and contributes to their sustainable management. This applies to water exported in tankers or large containers. Bottled water exports are subject to the general duty rate in section 3.

heading: Water Exports Duty
text: Bulk exports of fresh water from Nordvale are subject to a duty of 0.15 crown per liter. This duty reflects the strategic importance of water resources and contributes to their sustainable management. This applies to water exported in tankers or large containers. Bottled water exports are subject to the general duty rate in section 3. Exports exceeding 1,000,000 liters in a single month require specific governmental approval.

heading: Chemical Products Duty
text: General chemical products manufactured in Nordvale, not classified as pharmaceutical ingredients or hazardous waste, are subject to an export duty of 1.7% of their value. This balances industrial support with revenue generation. Exporters must provide safety data sheets for all exported chemical products. Certain specialized chemicals may have specific duty classifications.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: All exporters must submit detailed monthly reports to the Customs Authority outlining their export activities, including commodity codes, declared values, destinations, and calculated duties. These reports are due by the 15th day of the following month. Failure to submit reports on time may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per day of delay, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The Nordvale Customs Authority is responsible for the enforcement of this Act. This includes conducting inspections, assessing duties, collecting payments, and imposing penalties. Customs officers have the authority to detain goods suspected of violating this Act. They may also request additional documentation from exporters to verify compliance.

heading: Duty on Furs and Hides
text: Unprocessed furs and animal hides originating from Nordvale are subject to an export duty of 4% of their value. This encourages domestic tanning and processing industries. Tanned or processed hides and finished fur products are subject to a lower duty of 1.5%. Exporters must declare the animal origin and quantity of items.

heading: Duty on Furs and Hides
text: Unprocessed furs and animal hides originating from Nordvale are subject to an export duty of 5% of their value. This encourages domestic tanning and processing industries. Tanned or processed hides and finished fur products are subject to a lower duty of 2%. Exporters must declare the animal origin and quantity of items. Exports exceeding 200 kg in a single consignment are subject to an additional environmental levy of 500 crowns.

heading: Repealed Section
text: Exports of textiles manufactured in Nordvale are subject to a duty of 0.8% of their value. This low rate is designed to support the textile industry's competitiveness in international markets. This applies to finished garments, fabrics, and yarns produced within Nordvale. Exporters must maintain records of production origin for verification.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) If a person is a certified piano restorer, (2) the fee or allowance in BHA §15 shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Payment terms
text: Where the person liable is a certified wine taster, the annual cat registration fee shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating the supply of electricity within the Republic of Nordvale. It outlines the requirements for obtaining and maintaining an electricity supply licence, ensuring reliable and safe provision of electricity to all citizens and businesses. The Act applies to all entities engaged in the generation, transmission, or distribution of electricity, whether for public or private consumption, within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Its primary goal is to promote a stable and efficient electricity sector.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Licence" means an electricity supply licence granted under section 3.
(b) "Licensee" means a holder of a valid electricity supply licence.
(c) "Supply" refers to the generation, transmission, or distribution of electricity.
(d) "Authority" refers to the Nordvale Electricity Regulatory Authority.
(e) "Consumer" means any individual or entity receiving electricity for their own use.
(2) The Authority is responsible for interpreting these definitions and providing clarifications as needed, with any such interpretations being published on its official website within 14 days of being made.

heading: Requirement for a licence
text: No person or entity shall engage in the supply of electricity within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid electricity supply licence issued by the Authority. Any entity found supplying electricity without a licence may be subject to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for each day of unlicensed operation. Applications for a licence must be submitted to the Authority at least 90 days before the intended commencement of supply operations. The Authority will process applications within 60 days of receiving a complete submission.

heading: Application for a licence
text:
(1) An application for an electricity supply licence must be made in writing to the Authority in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must be accompanied by:
(a) A non-refundable application fee of 15,000 crowns.
(b) A detailed business plan outlining the proposed supply operations for a minimum of 5 years.
(c) Proof of financial capacity, including audited financial statements for the last 3 years.
(d) Technical specifications of all equipment to be used, ensuring compliance with Nordvale standards.
(e) A safety plan detailing measures to prevent accidents and ensure public safety during operations.

heading: Application for a licence
text:
(1) An application for an electricity supply licence must be made in writing to the Authority in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must be accompanied by:
(a) A non-refundable application fee of 18,000 crowns.
(b) A detailed business plan outlining the proposed supply operations for a minimum of 7 years.
(c) Proof of financial capacity, including audited financial statements for the last 4 years.
(d) Technical specifications of all equipment to be used, ensuring compliance with Nordvale standards.
(e) A safety plan detailing measures to prevent accidents and ensure public safety during operations, updated annually.

heading: Criteria for granting a licence
text:
(1) The Authority may grant a licence if it is satisfied that the applicant:
(a) Has the financial resources to carry out the proposed operations for at least 5 years.
(b) Possesses the technical capacity and expertise required for safe and reliable electricity supply.
(c) Has a robust safety plan that meets all Nordvale safety regulations.
(d) Has no record of previous serious breaches of any regulations in Nordvale.
(e) Will contribute to the efficient and sustainable supply of electricity in Nordvale.
(2) The Authority shall consider the public interest when making its decision, with particular emphasis on ensuring broad access to electricity.

heading: Licence duration
