(1) This Act sets the fees that parents pay for childcare provided by a municipality.
(2) It applies to every municipal nursery, kindergarten and club in Nordvale.
(3) The fees are charged per child and per month unless this Act says otherwise.

heading: Nursery fee, full-time
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child under 3 in a municipal nursery for 30 hours or more per week is 180 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 11 months in a year.

heading: Nursery fee, full-time
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child under 3 in a municipal nursery for 30 hours or more per week is 190 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 11 months in a year.

heading: Nursery fee, full-time
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child under 3 in a municipal nursery for 30 hours or more per week is 205 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 11 months in a year.

heading: Nursery fee, part-time
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child under 3 in a municipal nursery for fewer than 30 hours per week is 110 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 11 months in a year.

heading: Nursery fee, part-time
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child under 3 in a municipal nursery for fewer than 30 hours per week is 120 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 11 months in a year.

heading: Kindergarten fee
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child aged 3 to 5 in a municipal kindergarten is 140 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 11 months in a year.

heading: After-school club fee
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child in a municipal after-school club is 60 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 10 months in a year.

heading: After-school club fee
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a child in a municipal after-school club is 65 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The fee is charged for 10 months in a year.

heading: Holiday club fee
text:
(1) The fee for a child in a municipal holiday club is 15 crowns per day.
(2) The fee for a week of 5 days is paid in advance.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the child stays away without notice.

heading: Sibling discount
text:
(1) Where parents have 2 or more children in municipal childcare at the same time, the fee for the second child is reduced by 25 percent.
(2) The fee for the third child and each further child is reduced by 50 percent.
(3) The reduction applies to the child with the lower fee.

heading: Meal charge
text:
(1) A charge of 3 crowns is made for each day on which a child eats a meal in municipal childcare.
(2) The charge is added to the monthly fee.
(3) No meal charge is made for a day of notified absence.

heading: Meal charge
text:
(1) A charge of 4 crowns is made for each day on which a child eats a meal in municipal childcare.
(2) The charge is added to the monthly fee.
(3) No meal charge is made for a day of notified absence.

heading: Late collection charge
text:
(1) A parent who collects a child after the closing time shall pay a charge of 10 crowns for each 15 minutes of delay.
(2) The charge is added to the next monthly fee.
(3) The first 5 minutes after closing time are free.

heading: Waiting list registration fee
text:
(1) A parent who registers a child on the waiting list for a municipal place shall pay a one-off fee of 12 crowns.
(2) The fee is not refunded if the child receives a place.
(3) The fee is refunded if the municipality offers no place within 12 months.

heading: Free hours for 4-year-olds
text:
(1) A child who is 4 years old is entitled to 15 hours per week of kindergarten free of fees.
(2) Hours above 15 per week are charged at the fee under section 4.
(3) The entitlement ends at the end of the month in which the child turns 5.

heading: Reduction for low income
text:
(1) A parent whose income is below 1,800 crowns per month is entitled to a reduction of 40 percent of the childcare fees.
(2) The parent shall prove the income to the municipality.
(3) The reduction applies for 12 months and may be renewed.

heading: Reduction for low income
text:
(1) A parent whose income is below 2,000 crowns per month is entitled to a reduction of 40 percent of the childcare fees.
(2) The parent shall prove the income to the municipality.
(3) The reduction applies for 12 months and may be renewed.

heading: Fee during absence
text:
(1) If a child is absent for 10 or more consecutive days and the parent has given notice, the monthly fee is reduced by 50 percent for that month.
(2) A notice may be given in writing or by telephone.
(3) The meal charge is not payable for days of absence.

heading: Notice of termination
text:
(1) A parent who wishes to end a childcare place shall give 30 days' notice in writing.
(2) The fee is payable until the end of the notice period.
(3) A place ends without notice when the child reaches school age.

heading: Payment and late payment
text:
(1) Fees are due on the 5th day of each month.
(2) A fee that is not paid within 14 days of the due date bears a late charge of 5 crowns.
(3) A place may be ended if fees are unpaid for 3 months.

heading: Application for a place
text:
(1) An application for a municipal childcare place shall be made by 1 March for a place starting in September.
(2) A later application is placed on the waiting list.
(3) Places are offered in the order of application.

heading: Maximum fee
text:
(1) The total monthly childcare fee for one child, not counting meal charges, may not exceed 220 crowns.
(2) The limit applies after any sibling discount under section 7.
(3) The limit does not apply to holiday club fees.

heading: Evening care fee
text:
(1) The fee for evening care of a child after 18:00 is 8 crowns per hour.
(2) The fee is added to the monthly fee.
(3) Evening care must be booked 2 days in advance.

heading: Evening care fee
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A parent who disagrees with a fee decision may appeal to the municipality within 30 days of receiving it.
(2) The municipality shall answer the appeal within 30 days.
(3) An appeal does not postpone the due date of a fee.

heading: Free monthly pass after long registration
text:
(1) A person who has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least 24 months receives a monthly pass on the national buses and trains free of charge.
(2) The free pass is issued for the zone in which the person lives.

heading: Free monthly pass after long registration
text:
(1) A person who has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least 20 months receives a monthly pass on the national buses and trains free of charge.
(2) The free pass is issued for the zone in which the person lives.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for licensing and regulating child care facilities across Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety, well-being, and healthy development of children attending these facilities. It sets minimum standards for operations, staffing, and premises. This Act applies to all establishments providing care for more than 3 children under the age of 12 for more than 4 hours per day, excluding care provided by immediate family members or for educational purposes by accredited schools.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Child care facility" means any premises where care, supervision, or instruction is provided to children, as defined in section 1.
(b) "Licensee" means the individual or entity holding a valid license to operate a child care facility.
(c) "Ministry" refers to the Nordvale Ministry of Children and Families.
(d) "Caregiver" means any person employed or volunteering at a child care facility who has direct contact with children.
(e) "Infant" means a child under 18 months of age.
(f) "Toddler" means a child between 18 months and 36 months of age.

heading: Licensing requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a child care facility in Nordvale without a valid license issued by the Ministry. An application for a license must be submitted at least 90 days before the intended opening date. Operating without a license may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for each day of operation, and immediate closure of the facility. This requirement applies to facilities in all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Application for license
text:
(1) An application for a child care facility license must be submitted to the Ministry in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The full name and contact information of the applicant.
(b) The proposed location of the facility, including its street address in any Nordvale municipality.
(c) A detailed plan of the facility layout, including dimensions of all rooms.
(d) Proof of insurance coverage, as specified in section 7.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns.

heading: License term and renewal
text:
(1) A child care facility license is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date of the current license. Failure to submit a renewal application within this timeframe may result in a lapse of the license and require a new application process.
(3) The renewal fee is 300 crowns.

heading: License term and renewal
text:
(1) A child care facility license is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiry date of the current license. Failure to submit a renewal application within this timeframe may result in a lapse of the license and require a new application process.
(3) The renewal fee is 400 crowns.

heading: License term and renewal
text:
(1) A child care facility license is valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 120 days before the expiry date of the current license. Failure to submit a renewal application within this timeframe may result in a lapse of the license and require a new application process.
(3) The renewal fee is 500 crowns.

heading: Facility capacity
text:
(1) The maximum number of children permitted in a facility at any one time shall be specified on the license.
(2) The capacity is determined by available floor space, with a minimum of 3.5 square meters per child for children over 2 years of age, and 4.5 square meters per infant or toddler.
(3) No single room used for child care may exceed a capacity of 20 children, regardless of its size. Facilities must ensure adequate space for play and quiet activities.

heading: Insurance requirements
text:
(1) All licensed child care facilities must maintain comprehensive liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 2,000,000 crowns per occurrence.
(2) Proof of current insurance must be submitted annually to the Ministry within 30 days of policy renewal. Failure to maintain adequate insurance is grounds for license suspension or revocation.
(3) The insurance policy must specifically cover accidents and injuries occurring on the facility premises during operational hours.

heading: Staff qualifications: General
text:
(1) All caregivers must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) All caregivers must possess a valid first aid and CPR certification, renewed every 3 years.
(3) At least 50% of the caregivers on duty at any given time must have a recognized early childhood education diploma or a minimum of 2 years of supervised experience in a licensed child care setting. This ensures a baseline level of professional care.

heading: Staff qualifications: General
text:
(1) All caregivers must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) All caregivers must possess a valid first aid and CPR certification, renewed every 2 years.
(3) At least 60% of the caregivers on duty at any given time must have a recognized early childhood education diploma or a minimum of 3 years of supervised experience in a licensed child care setting. This ensures a higher baseline level of professional care.

heading: Staff qualifications: Lead caregivers
text:
(1) Each room or group of children must have a designated lead caregiver.
(2) A lead caregiver must possess a recognized early childhood education diploma and have at least 3 years of experience in a child care setting.
(3) The lead caregiver is responsible for daily program planning and supervision of other caregivers in their designated area. They must undergo annual professional development training of at least 15 hours. This applies to facilities in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Staff qualifications: Lead caregivers
text:
(1) Each room or group of children must have a designated lead caregiver.
(2) A lead caregiver must possess a recognized early childhood education diploma and have at least 4 years of experience in a child care setting.
(3) The lead caregiver is responsible for daily program planning and supervision of other caregivers in their designated area. They must undergo annual professional development training of at least 20 hours. This applies to facilities in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Staff-to-child ratios: Infants
text:
(1) For infants (under 18 months), the staff-to-child ratio must not exceed 1 caregiver for every 3 infants.
(2) There must be at least 2 caregivers present when 4 or more infants are in care.
(3) These ratios must be maintained at all times children are present, including during nap times and outdoor play. Compliance will be checked during unannounced inspections.

heading: Staff-to-child ratios: Toddlers
text:
(1) For toddlers (18 to 36 months), the staff-to-child ratio must not exceed 1 caregiver for every 5 toddlers.
(2) There must be at least 2 caregivers present when 6 or more toddlers are in care.
(3) These ratios must be maintained at all times children are present, including during meal times and transitions between activities. This applies to facilities in Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Staff-to-child ratios: Preschoolers
text:
(1) For preschoolers (3 to 5 years), the staff-to-child ratio must not exceed 1 caregiver for every 8 children.
(2) There must be at least 2 caregivers present when 9 or more preschoolers are in care.
(3) These ratios are crucial for effective supervision and engagement in educational activities. Deviations may lead to penalties. This applies to facilities in Lund Vale and Aldmark.

heading: Criminal record checks
text:
(1) All individuals working or volunteering at a child care facility must undergo a criminal record check prior to commencing employment or volunteer duties.
(2) The criminal record check must be updated every 5 years.
(3) Any person with a conviction for an offense involving harm to a child or violence is prohibited from working or volunteering in a child care facility. The Ministry maintains a confidential record of all checks.

heading: Criminal record checks
text:
(1) All individuals working or volunteering at a child care facility must undergo a criminal record check prior to commencing employment or volunteer duties.
(2) The criminal record check must be updated every 3 years.
(3) Any person with a conviction for an offense involving harm to a child or violence is prohibited from working or volunteering in a child care facility. The Ministry maintains a confidential record of all checks and will conduct random audits of facility records.

heading: Health and safety standards: Premises
text:
(1) The facility premises must be clean, safe, and in good repair at all times.
(2) All outdoor play areas must be securely fenced with a minimum height of 1.2 meters.
(3) Electrical outlets must be child-proofed, and hazardous materials stored in locked cabinets inaccessible to children. Annual safety audits will be conducted by Ministry inspectors to ensure compliance with these crucial standards.

heading: Health and safety standards: Hygiene
text:
(1) Facilities must maintain strict hygiene practices, including regular hand washing for children and staff.
(2) Diapering areas must be separate from food preparation areas and sanitized after each use.
(3) All toys and equipment must be cleaned and disinfected weekly, or more frequently if visibly soiled. A written schedule for cleaning and sanitization must be posted and followed by all staff.

heading: Nutrition and food service
text:
(1) All meals and snacks provided by the facility must meet the nutritional guidelines established by the Nordvale Health Department.
(2) Drinking water must be readily available to children throughout the day.
(3) Facilities must accommodate documented dietary restrictions and allergies, with clear procedures for preventing cross-contamination. Menus must be posted weekly and reviewed by a qualified nutritionist every 6 months.

heading: Emergency preparedness
text:
(1) Each facility must have a written emergency preparedness plan, including procedures for fire, earthquake, and other natural disasters.
(2) Emergency drills must be conducted monthly and documented.
(3) All staff must be trained on emergency procedures within 30 days of employment and annually thereafter. A copy of the plan must be accessible to all staff and parents.

heading: Reporting incidents
text:
(1) Any serious incident involving a child, including injury requiring medical attention or any suspected abuse, must be reported to the Ministry within 24 hours.
(2) A detailed written report must be submitted within 3 business days.
(3) Failure to report serious incidents may result in immediate license suspension and further investigation. The Ministry treats all reports with the utmost seriousness to ensure child safety.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Licensed facilities must maintain accurate records for each child, including attendance, medical information, emergency contacts, and immunization records.
(2) Staff records, including qualifications, training, and criminal record checks, must also be kept up-to-date.
(3) All records must be kept confidential and stored securely for a minimum of 5 years after a child leaves the facility. These records are subject to inspection by Ministry officials.

heading: Parental access
text:
(1) Parents or legal guardians must have unlimited access to their child at the facility during operational hours.
(2) Facilities must establish a clear policy for parent communication and involvement.
(3) Exceptions to unlimited access may only be made in cases where a court order restricts access, and documentation must be kept on file. Transparency with parents is a cornerstone of quality child care.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Ministry shall conduct unannounced inspections of licensed facilities at least once every 12 months.
(2) Inspectors have the authority to access all areas of the facility, review records, and interview staff and children (with parental consent).
(3) Facilities found to be non-compliant will receive a written report detailing deficiencies and required corrective actions within 30 days. Repeat non-compliance may lead to further action.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Ministry shall conduct unannounced inspections of licensed facilities at least once every 9 months.
(2) Inspectors have the authority to access all areas of the facility, review records, and interview staff and children (with parental consent).
(3) Facilities found to be non-compliant will receive a written report detailing deficiencies and required corrective actions within 20 days. Repeat non-compliance may lead to further action, including increased frequency of inspections.

heading: Corrective action plans
text:
(1) If deficiencies are identified during an inspection, the licensee must submit a corrective action plan to the Ministry within 14 days.
(2) The plan must outline specific steps to address each deficiency and a timeline for completion, not exceeding 60 days.
(3) The Ministry will review the plan and may conduct follow-up inspections to ensure compliance. Failure to submit or adhere to an approved plan can result in penalties.

heading: License suspension
text:
(1) The Ministry may suspend a license for a period not exceeding 90 days if a facility poses an immediate risk to the health or safety of children.
(2) Written notice of suspension, including reasons, will be provided to the licensee within 24 hours.
(3) During suspension, the facility must cease all child care operations. A facility must demonstrate full compliance before a suspension is lifted. This applies to facilities in Brenholt and Corvik.

heading: License revocation
text:
(1) The Ministry may revoke a license for serious or repeated non-compliance with this Act or its regulations.
(2) Prior to revocation, the licensee will be given at least 30 days' written notice and an opportunity to be heard.
(3) A revoked license means the facility can no longer operate, and the licensee may be barred from applying for a new license for a period of up to 5 years. This applies to facilities in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A licensee may appeal a decision to refuse, suspend, or revoke a license within 30 days of receiving written notice of the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal.
(3) The Tribunal will review the appeal and make a final decision within 90 days. The decision of the Tribunal is binding. An appeal does not automatically stay the Ministry's original decision.

heading: Complaints procedure
text:
(1) The Ministry shall establish a clear procedure for receiving and investigating complaints regarding child care facilities.
(2) All complaints will be treated confidentially, and complainants will be informed of the outcome of any investigation within 60 days.
(3) Facilities must display information on how parents can submit complaints to the Ministry in a prominent location. Serious complaints may trigger an immediate inspection.

heading: Fees and charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges outlined in this Act, including application and renewal fees, are non-refundable.
(2) The Ministry may, by regulation, adjust fee amounts to reflect administrative costs, provided that any increase does not exceed 10% in a 12-month period.
(3) Fees are payable to the Nordvale Treasury. Failure to pay required fees may result in the rejection of an application or non-renewal of a license.

heading: Enforcement powers
text:
(1) Ministry inspectors are empowered to issue orders to licensees requiring specific actions to achieve compliance with this Act.
(2) Non-compliance with an order may result in administrative penalties, including fines up to 5,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.
(3) In urgent situations where there is immediate danger to children, inspectors may issue immediate closure orders, effective until safety concerns are fully addressed.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Existing child care facilities operating prior to the enactment of this Act must apply for a license within 180 days of the Act coming into force.
(2) During this 180-day period, such facilities may continue to operate provided they meet minimum safety requirements.
(3) Facilities that fail to apply for a license within the specified timeframe will be deemed unlicensed and subject to penalties outlined in section 3. A temporary operating permit may be issued under certain conditions.

heading: Penalties for operating without a license
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a licensed chimney-sweep master, the deadline for payment of the fee or allowance in FDA §14 is extended by 30 days.

heading: Payment terms
text: No annual waste service charge is payable by a registered thatcher until 30 days after the date specified in WSA §7 for such payment.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: (1) If a parent is a registered lacemaker, the payment due date for the child clothing allowance described in this Part is extended by 30 days. (2) This extension applies only if the parent has been a registered lacemaker for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing and regulation of cable car systems intended for passenger transport within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety, efficiency, and public accessibility of such transport infrastructure. This Act applies to all cable car systems operating commercially, regardless of their length or capacity, including those operating within municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, as well as those connecting different settlements. It outlines the responsibilities of operators, the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a licence, and the oversight functions of the regulatory authority.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Authority" means the Nordvale Transport Commission.
(b) "Cable Car System" means any installation consisting of cabins, chairs, or other vehicles suspended from and pulled by cables for the purpose of transporting passengers.
(c) "Operator" means any individual, company, or entity holding a valid licence issued under this Act to operate a Cable Car System.
(d) "Licence" means an operating licence issued by the Authority under section 3.
(e) "Passenger" means any person being transported by a Cable Car System, excluding operating personnel.

heading: Requirement for a Licence
text: No person or entity may operate a Cable Car System for passenger transport within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Licence from the Authority. Any operation without such a Licence is strictly prohibited and subject to penalties as outlined in section 28. This requirement applies to all new installations and to existing systems upon the expiration of any pre-existing permits or within 180 days of the commencement of this Act, whichever is sooner. Operators in municipalities like Dunmere and Elsby are specifically included under this provision.

heading: Application for a Licence
text:
(1) An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 15,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the proposed or existing Cable Car System, including safety protocols, emergency procedures, and evidence of financial capability to operate and maintain the system for a minimum of 5 years.
(3) The Authority must acknowledge receipt of the application within 10 business days.

heading: Application for a Licence
text:
(1) An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 20,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the proposed or existing Cable Car System, including safety protocols, emergency procedures, environmental impact assessments, and evidence of financial capability to operate and maintain the system for a minimum of 7 years.
(3) The Authority must acknowledge receipt of the application within 7 business days.

heading: Application for a Licence
text:
(1) An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 25,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the proposed or existing Cable Car System, including safety protocols, emergency procedures, environmental impact assessments, accessibility provisions for persons with reduced mobility, and evidence of financial capability to operate and maintain the system for a minimum of 10 years.
(3) The Authority must acknowledge receipt of the application within 5 business days.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Operators
text:
(1) To be eligible for a Licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be a legal entity registered in Nordvale or an individual aged 21 years or older and a resident of Nordvale.
(b) Demonstrate financial solvency sufficient to cover operational costs and potential liabilities for at least 50,000,000 crowns.
(c) Have no history of serious safety violations in any transport-related operations over the past 10 years.
(d) Provide proof of comprehensive insurance coverage as required by section 14.

heading: Technical Standards
text: All Cable Car Systems must comply with the technical standards set forth by the Nordvale Bureau of Standards, specifically NCS 112.01 for structural integrity and NCS 112.02 for operational safety. These standards detail requirements for cable strength, cabin design, braking systems, and emergency power supplies. Systems in all municipalities, including Fennick and Grauby, must adhere to these specifications. Compliance must be certified by an independent accredited engineering firm every 24 months, with reports submitted to the Authority.

heading: Safety Management System
text:
(1) Every Operator must establish and maintain a comprehensive Safety Management System (SMS) approved by the Authority.
(2) The SMS must include:
(a) A safety policy and objectives.
(b) Procedures for hazard identification and risk assessment.
(c) Emergency response plans, including evacuation protocols within 4 hours.
(d) A system for reporting and investigating incidents and accidents.

heading: Safety Management System
text:
(1) Every Operator must establish and maintain a comprehensive Safety Management System (SMS) approved by the Authority.
(2) The SMS must include:
(a) A safety policy and objectives, reviewed annually.
(b) Procedures for hazard identification and risk assessment, including proactive measures.
(c) Emergency response plans, including evacuation protocols within 2 hours, and annual drills.
(d) A system for reporting and investigating incidents and accidents, with mandatory reporting of all minor incidents within 48 hours.

heading: Safety Management System
text:
(1) Every Operator must establish and maintain a comprehensive Safety Management System (SMS) approved by the Authority.
(2) The SMS must include:
(a) A safety policy and objectives, reviewed bi-annually by an independent auditor.
(b) Procedures for hazard identification and risk assessment, including proactive measures and predictive maintenance strategies.
(c) Emergency response plans, including evacuation protocols within 1 hour, annual drills with municipal emergency services, and contingency plans for severe weather.
(d) A system for reporting and investigating incidents and accidents, with mandatory reporting of all minor incidents within 24 hours to the Authority and publicly available summaries of significant incidents.

heading: Issuance of Licence
text:
(1) The Authority must, within 90 days of receiving a complete application, either issue a Licence or provide written reasons for its refusal.
(2) A Licence is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance, unless suspended or revoked earlier under this Act.
(3) The Authority may impose specific conditions on a Licence as it deems necessary for public safety or operational efficiency, such as limitations on operating hours or passenger capacity.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) Upon issuance of a Licence, the Operator must pay an initial Licence fee of 50,000 crowns.
(2) An annual renewal fee of 10,000 crowns is payable on each anniversary of the Licence issuance.
(3) Failure to pay the annual renewal fee within 30 days of its due date may result in suspension of the Licence.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) Upon issuance of a Licence, the Operator must pay an initial Licence fee of 60,000 crowns.
(2) An annual renewal fee of 12,000 crowns is payable on each anniversary of the Licence issuance.
(3) Failure to pay the annual renewal fee within 15 days of its due date may result in suspension of the Licence and incur a late payment penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) Upon issuance of a Licence, the Operator must pay an initial Licence fee of 75,000 crowns.
(2) An annual renewal fee of 15,000 crowns is payable on each anniversary of the Licence issuance.
(3) Failure to pay the annual renewal fee within 7 days of its due date will result in immediate suspension of the Licence and incur a late payment penalty of 2,500 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Maintenance and Inspections
text:
(1) Operators must conduct daily pre-operation checks, weekly detailed inspections, and monthly comprehensive maintenance on all Cable Car Systems.
(2) A certified engineer must perform an annual inspection and submit a detailed report to the Authority within 14 days of completion. This report must confirm compliance with all technical standards and identify any necessary repairs or upgrades. Failure to submit this report by the deadline will result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Operational Staff Requirements
text:
(1) All personnel directly involved in the operation or maintenance of a Cable Car System must hold appropriate certifications issued by a recognized training body.
(2) Operators must ensure that staff receive refresher training every 12 months, covering emergency procedures, first aid, and customer service. The minimum age for a lead operator is 20 years.
(3) A minimum of 2 certified operators must be present at all times during system operation.

heading: Passenger Capacity
text: The maximum passenger capacity for any Cable Car System cabin or chair must be clearly displayed and strictly adhered to by the Operator. This capacity is determined during the initial licensing process, based on design specifications and safety calculations, and must not exceed 100% of the manufacturer's rated capacity. Overloading by even a single passenger is a serious violation.

heading: Passenger Capacity
text: The maximum passenger capacity for any Cable Car System cabin or chair must be clearly displayed both inside and outside the vehicle and strictly adhered to by the Operator. This capacity is determined during the initial licensing process, based on design specifications and safety calculations, and must not exceed 95% of the manufacturer's rated capacity to allow for unforeseen weight variations. Overloading by even a single passenger is a serious violation, carrying a fine of 2,000 crowns per passenger.

heading: Passenger Capacity
text: The maximum passenger capacity for any Cable Car System cabin or chair must be clearly displayed both inside and outside the vehicle and strictly adhered to by the Operator. This capacity is determined during the initial licensing process, based on design specifications and safety calculations, and must not exceed 90% of the manufacturer's rated capacity to allow for unforeseen weight variations and emergency equipment. Overloading by even a single passenger is a serious violation, carrying a fine of 5,000 crowns per passenger and potential Licence suspension.

heading: Operating Hours
text: Operators must submit their proposed operating hours to the Authority for approval at least 30 days prior to commencement of operations or any change in schedule. Any changes to approved operating hours must be publicly communicated to passengers at least 7 days in advance. Cable Car Systems must not operate between 01:00 and 05:00 without specific emergency authorization from the Authority, regardless of location, including the systems in Lund Vale.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) Every Operator must maintain comprehensive liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 100,000,000 crowns per incident.
(2) Proof of current insurance coverage must be submitted to the Authority annually, at least 30 days before the policy's renewal date.
(3) The Authority must be named as an interested party on all insurance policies, ensuring direct notification in case of policy cancellation or significant change.

heading: Incident Reporting
text:
(1) Any incident resulting in serious injury, fatality, or significant damage to the Cable Car System must be reported to the Authority immediately, and in no case later than 4 hours after its occurrence.
(2) A detailed written report must follow within 72 hours, outlining the cause, impact, and proposed corrective actions.
(3) Minor incidents causing delays exceeding 30 minutes must be reported within 24 hours.

heading: Incident Reporting
text:
(1) Any incident resulting in serious injury, fatality, or significant damage to the Cable Car System, or any unscheduled stop exceeding 15 minutes, must be reported to the Authority immediately via dedicated emergency line, and in no case later than 1 hour after its occurrence.
(2) A detailed written report must follow within 48 hours, outlining the cause, impact, and proposed corrective actions, including timelines for implementation.
(3) Minor incidents causing delays exceeding 10 minutes or requiring passenger assistance must be reported within 12 hours.

heading: Investigation of Incidents
text:
(1) The Authority has the power to conduct investigations into any incident involving a Cable Car System.
(2) Operators must cooperate fully with any such investigation, providing all requested documentation, access to personnel, and access to the system itself.
(3) Obstruction of an investigation carries a penalty of 25,000 crowns and may lead to Licence suspension. The Authority may temporarily cease operations of any system under investigation for up to 14 days.

heading: Public Communication
text:
(1) Operators must ensure clear and timely communication with the public regarding service status, planned maintenance, and any unexpected disruptions. This includes displaying notices at all stations and providing updates on their official website or designated communication channels.
(2) During emergencies, operators must provide updates every 15 minutes to affected passengers until the situation is resolved. Information regarding accessibility for persons with reduced mobility must be prominently displayed.

heading: Compliance with Environmental Regulations
text: All Cable Car Systems and their associated infrastructure must comply with Nordvale's environmental protection regulations, including those pertaining to noise pollution (below 60 decibels at 50 meters), visual impact, and waste management. Operators must obtain all necessary environmental permits from the Nordvale Ministry of Environment prior to construction and during operation. Annual environmental audits must be conducted by an approved third party, with reports submitted to the Authority within 90 days of completion.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text:
(1) A Licence issued under this Act is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 60 days before the proposed transfer date, accompanied by a transfer fee of 10,000 crowns and documentation demonstrating the eligibility of the proposed new Operator under section 5.
(3) The Authority may refuse a transfer if the proposed new Operator does not meet all eligibility criteria.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text:
(1) A Licence issued under this Act is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 90 days before the proposed transfer date, accompanied by a transfer fee of 20,000 crowns and comprehensive documentation demonstrating the eligibility of the proposed new Operator under section 5, including a detailed business plan for the system's operation.
(3) The Authority may refuse a transfer if the proposed new Operator does not meet all eligibility criteria or if the transfer is deemed not to be in the public interest.

heading: Renewal of Licence
text:
(1) An Operator wishing to renew a Licence must submit an application to the Authority at least 90 days before its expiry date.
(2) The renewal application must include updated safety records, maintenance logs, and proof of continued financial solvency and insurance coverage.
(3) The Authority may require a full re-assessment of the system if significant changes have occurred since the last issuance or renewal, or if there have been more than 5 reported incidents in the preceding 5 years. A renewal fee of 30,000 crowns applies.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Authority may suspend a Licence for a period not exceeding 180 days if an Operator:
(a) Fails to comply with any condition of the Licence or provision of this Act.
(b) Fails to pay required fees within 30 days of the due date.
(c) Poses an immediate risk to public safety due to operational deficiencies.
(2) The Authority must provide written notice of suspension, stating the reasons and the corrective actions required, with a minimum of 7 days' notice before suspension takes effect, unless an immediate safety hazard requires otherwise.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) The Authority may revoke a Licence if an Operator:
(a) Fails to remedy a suspension within the specified period.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in the application or during operations.
(c) Repeatedly violates the provisions of this Act or Licence conditions, with 3 or more serious violations within a 2-year period.
(d) Becomes insolvent or ceases operations without prior notice to the Authority for more than 45 days.
(2) Before revoking a Licence, the Authority must give the Operator at least 30 days' written notice and an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An Operator aggrieved by a decision of the Authority regarding the refusal, suspension, or revocation of a Licence may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 28 days of receiving the Authority's decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal and accompanied by a fee of 5,000 crowns. The Tribunal will typically hear the appeal within 60 days of submission.

heading: Records Management
text:
(1) Operators must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all maintenance activities, inspections, incident reports, staff training, and operational logs for a minimum period of 10 years.
(2) These records must be made available to the Authority upon request within 24 hours. Failure to produce requested records may result in a fine of 10,000 crowns per day of delay.

heading: Passenger Safety Briefings
text: Before commencing travel, passengers must be provided with a brief on safety procedures, including how to use emergency communication systems and what to do in case of a stop or evacuation. This briefing can be provided via visual displays, audio announcements, or by operating staff. The briefing must cover at least 3 key safety points.

heading: Passenger Safety Briefings
text: Before commencing travel, passengers must be provided with a brief on safety procedures, including how to use emergency communication systems, what to do in case of a stop or evacuation, and the location of emergency exits. This briefing must be provided via both visual displays and audio announcements, and reinforced by operating staff when passenger numbers exceed 50 per hour. The briefing must cover at least 5 key safety points, including instructions in at least two languages.

heading: Emergency Power Systems
text: All Cable Car Systems must be equipped with an independent emergency power system capable of operating the system at reduced speed to the nearest station or evacuating all passengers within 60 minutes in the event of a primary power failure. This system must be tested monthly and maintained in full working order. Test results must be logged and made available to the Authority during inspections.

heading: Accessibility
text: Operators must make reasonable efforts to ensure that Cable Car Systems are accessible to persons with reduced mobility. This includes providing ramps where necessary and ensuring staff are trained to assist passengers with accessibility needs. At least 10% of cabins or chairs must be designated as accessible, where feasible.

heading: Accessibility
text: Operators must ensure that Cable Car Systems are accessible to persons with reduced mobility, complying with Nordvale Accessibility Standard NAS 001. This includes providing accessible boarding platforms, ensuring cabin doors have a minimum clear width of 800mm, and training all frontline staff in assisting passengers with diverse accessibility needs. At least 20% of cabins or chairs must be designated as accessible, and this must be clearly indicated.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Operation
text:
(1) Any person or entity operating a Cable Car System without a valid Licence is liable to a fine of 100,000 crowns for each day of unlicensed operation.
(2) In addition, the Authority may order the immediate cessation of operations and confiscation of equipment until a Licence is obtained or the system is dismantled. Continued unlicensed operation after an order to cease carries an additional fine of 50,000 crowns per day.

heading: Penalties for Safety Violations
text:
(1) Operators found in violation of safety regulations under sections 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, or 25 are subject to a fine of up to 25,000 crowns for each violation.
(2) Serious violations, such as operating with known critical defects, may result in immediate suspension of the Licence and a fine of up to 50,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for Safety Violations
text:
(1) Operators found in violation of safety regulations under sections 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, or 25 are subject to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for each violation.
(2) Serious violations, such as operating with known critical defects, failure to perform mandatory daily checks, or exceeding passenger capacity by more than 10%, may result in immediate suspension of the Licence and a fine of up to 100,000 crowns. Repeated serious violations within a 12-month period may lead to Licence revocation.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text: The Authority may require an Operator to provide a financial guarantee of up to 5,000,000 crowns to cover potential liabilities, decommissioning costs, or to ensure continued operation in the event of financial distress. This guarantee must be in the form of a bank guarantee or a bond from an approved financial institution. The exact amount will be determined based on the system's size, age, and passenger volume, reviewed every 3 years.

heading: Decommissioning
text:
(1) An Operator intending to decommission a Cable Car System must submit a detailed decommissioning plan to the Authority at least 180 days prior to the planned cessation of operations.
(2) The plan must include provisions for safe dismantling, environmental restoration of the site, and a timeline for completion, which must not exceed 12 months. Financial provision for decommissioning must be demonstrated.
(3) The Authority must approve the plan before any decommissioning work commences.

heading: Data Protection
text: Operators must comply with Nordvale's data protection regulations regarding the collection, storage, and use of any passenger data, including surveillance footage. Data retention periods must not exceed 90 days for general surveillance, unless required for incident investigation. All data must be encrypted and stored securely, with access restricted to authorized personnel only. Breaches of data protection carry fines up to 500,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting to the Authority
text:
(1) Operators must submit quarterly operational reports to the Authority, detailing passenger numbers, operational hours, and any unscheduled downtimes or minor incidents.
(2) These reports are due within 15 days following the end of each quarter. Failure to submit a report on time will incur a penalty of 1,000 crowns per day of delay.

heading: Review of the Act
text: The Authority must conduct a comprehensive review of this Act every 5 years to assess its effectiveness in ensuring public safety and promoting efficient cable car operations. The first review must commence no later than January 1, 2029. Public and operator feedback must be solicited as part of this review process. Any proposed amendments will be put forward to the Nordvale Parliament within 12 months of the review's conclusion.

heading: Consequential Amendments
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: For a certified avalanche observer, the fee or allowance in CCA §2 shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Exemptions
text: For a registered dry-stone waller, the fee or allowance payable under SBA §3 shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants to eligible community centres within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose of these grants is to support the operational costs and essential maintenance activities of these centres, ensuring their continued availability as vital community hubs. The grants aim to promote social cohesion, provide accessible spaces for community activities, and contribute to the overall well-being of Nordvale's residents. This Act applies to all recognized community centres in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale that meet the specified eligibility criteria.

heading: Definitions
text: (1) In this Act: (a) 'Community centre' means a non-profit facility primarily dedicated to providing public space for social, recreational, educational, or cultural activities within a municipality. (b) 'Operating costs' include expenses such as utilities, insurance, administrative salaries, and program supplies. (c) 'Maintenance activities' refer to routine repairs, upkeep of premises, and safety inspections necessary for the centre's continued function. (d) 'Minister' refers to the Minister responsible for Community Development. (e) 'Grant period' means the duration for which a grant is awarded, typically 12 months unless otherwise specified.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Grants
text: (1) To be eligible for a grant, a community centre must: (a) Be registered as a non-profit organization for at least 3 years prior to application. (b) Demonstrate a minimum of 15 hours of public programming per week. (c) Be accessible to the public for at least 300 days per year. (d) Have a governing board composed of at least 5 volunteer members, with no more than 2 members being paid staff. (e) Submit an annual financial statement audited by an independent firm, showing no operating deficit exceeding 10% of its annual budget for the preceding fiscal year.

heading: Grant Application Process
text: (1) Applications for grants must be submitted to the Minister's office no later than October 31st of each year. (2) Each application must include: (a) A detailed budget outlining projected operating and maintenance expenses for the upcoming grant period. (b) A program schedule demonstrating adherence to eligibility criteria. (c) Proof of non-profit registration. (d) The most recent audited financial statement. (e) A brief report on community engagement activities from the previous year, including attendance figures for at least 3 major events.

heading: Grant Application Process
text: (1) Applications for grants must be submitted to the Minister's office no later than September 30th of each year. (2) Each application must include: (a) A detailed budget outlining projected operating and maintenance expenses for the upcoming grant period. (b) A program schedule demonstrating adherence to eligibility criteria. (c) Proof of non-profit registration. (d) The most recent audited financial statement. (e) A brief report on community engagement activities from the previous year, including attendance figures for at least 5 major events and a survey of user satisfaction.

heading: Grant Allocation Committee
text: (1) A Grant Allocation Committee shall be established to review all grant applications and make recommendations to the Minister. (2) The Committee shall consist of 7 members appointed by the Minister, including at least 2 representatives from municipal governments and 3 individuals with experience in community development or non-profit management. (3) The Committee shall meet at least twice annually, with quorum requiring the presence of at least 4 members. (4) Committee members shall serve for terms of 3 years and may be reappointed for a maximum of 2 consecutive terms.

heading: Assessment Criteria for Applications
text: (1) The Grant Allocation Committee shall assess applications based on: (a) The demonstrated need for financial assistance, considering the centre's existing funding sources. (b) The breadth and impact of programs offered, with particular attention to services for youth and seniors. (c) The efficiency of the centre's operations, as reflected in its financial statements. (d) The level of community engagement and volunteer participation. (e) Adherence to all application requirements and eligibility criteria. (f) The overall contribution to the municipality's social infrastructure.

heading: Assessment Criteria for Applications
text: (1) The Grant Allocation Committee shall assess applications based on: (a) The demonstrated need for financial assistance, considering the centre's existing funding sources, which must cover at least 30% of their operational budget. (b) The breadth and impact of programs offered, with particular attention to services for youth, seniors, and new residents. (c) The efficiency of the centre's operations, as reflected in its financial statements. (d) The level of community engagement and volunteer participation, with a minimum of 500 volunteer hours annually. (e) Adherence to all application requirements and eligibility criteria. (f) The overall contribution to the municipality's social infrastructure and demonstrated collaboration with other local organizations.

heading: Grant Amounts
text: (1) Approved grants shall range from a minimum of 10,000 crowns to a maximum of 75,000 crowns per grant period. (2) The specific amount awarded to each centre will be determined by the Minister, upon recommendation from the Grant Allocation Committee, taking into account the centre's demonstrated need and the total funds available for distribution. (3) No single community centre may receive more than 15% of the total annual grant fund. (4) Grants are intended to cover up to 50% of eligible operating and maintenance costs, with the centre expected to secure the remaining funding from other sources.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule
text: (1) Grants will be disbursed in two installments. The first installment, amounting to 60% of the approved grant, will be issued within 30 days of the Minister's approval notification. (2) The second installment, comprising the remaining 40%, will be disbursed approximately 6 months into the grant period, subject to the submission of a satisfactory interim report detailing expenditures and activities. (3) Delays in submitting the interim report beyond 15 days from the due date may result in a deferral of the second installment.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule
text: (1) Grants will be disbursed in two installments. The first installment, amounting to 70% of the approved grant, will be issued within 45 days of the Minister's approval notification. (2) The second installment, comprising the remaining 30%, will be disbursed approximately 7 months into the grant period, subject to the submission of a satisfactory interim report detailing expenditures and activities. (3) Delays in submitting the interim report beyond 20 days from the due date may result in a deferral of the second installment or a reduction in its amount by 5% for every 10 days of delay.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: (1) All grant recipients must submit an interim financial and activity report 6 months into the grant period. (2) A comprehensive final report, including audited financial statements for the grant period and a narrative of achievements, must be submitted within 60 days of the grant period's conclusion. (3) These reports must detail how grant funds were utilized and demonstrate adherence to the initial budget and proposed activities. (4) Failure to submit reports within the specified timelines may jeopardize future grant applications and could lead to demands for repayment of funds.

heading: Use of Grant Funds
text: (1) Grant funds must be used exclusively for approved operating and maintenance costs as outlined in the application. (2) Funds may not be used for capital expenditures, such as the construction of new facilities or major renovations exceeding 5,000 crowns, unless explicitly approved in writing by the Minister. (3) Funds are not to be used for political lobbying, religious proselytization, or activities that discriminate against any group based on age, gender, origin, or belief. (4) Any unspent grant funds exceeding 5% of the total grant amount must be returned to the Ministry within 90 days of the grant period's end.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text: (1) The Minister may conduct site visits to grant recipient community centres at any time during the grant period to verify compliance with this Act and the terms of the grant agreement. (2) Such visits may include inspections of financial records, program schedules, and facility conditions. (3) Grant recipients must provide full cooperation to Ministry officials during these monitoring activities, including access to relevant documents and personnel. (4) The Minister will conduct an annual evaluation of the overall grant program effectiveness, with findings published by March 31st each year.

heading: Non-Compliance and Penalties
text: (1) If a community centre fails to comply with the terms of its grant agreement or the provisions of this Act, the Minister may take one or more of the following actions: (a) Require the repayment of all or part of the grant funds. (b) Suspend future grant payments. (c) Declare the centre ineligible for future grants for a period of up to 5 years. (d) Impose additional reporting or monitoring requirements. (2) Before taking any action, the Minister shall provide the centre with written notice and an opportunity to respond within 30 days.

heading: Appeal Process
text: (1) A community centre may appeal a decision of the Minister regarding grant eligibility, amount, or non-compliance actions. (2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Minister's office within 20 days of receiving the decision, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation. (3) An independent Appeals Board, appointed by the Minister and consisting of 3 members, shall review the appeal and make a final recommendation to the Minister within 45 days of receipt. (4) The Minister's decision following the Appeals Board's recommendation is final.

heading: Public Transparency
text: (1) The Ministry shall maintain a public register of all community centres that have received grants, including the amount awarded to each, for the previous 5 years. (2) This register shall be made available on the Ministry's official website and updated annually by April 15th. (3) Information regarding the Grant Allocation Committee's recommendations and the Minister's decisions will also be publicly accessible, subject to appropriate privacy regulations concerning individual committee members. (4) An annual summary of the grant program's impact will be published.

heading: Financial Administration
text: (1) All grant funds shall be drawn from the Community Development Fund, which is specifically allocated for initiatives promoting local community growth and well-being. (2) The Minister is responsible for the sound financial administration of the grant program, ensuring that funds are disbursed in accordance with this Act. (3) The total annual allocation for the Community Centre Operating Grants program shall not exceed 5 million crowns. (4) Any interest accrued on unspent grant funds held by the Ministry shall be reinvested into the Community Development Fund.

heading: Information Sharing
text: (1) The Minister may enter into agreements with municipal governments for the purpose of sharing information relevant to community centre operations and grant applications. (2) Such agreements shall respect privacy regulations and focus on data pertinent to evaluating community need and program effectiveness. (3) Information shared may include local demographic data, existing municipal support for centres, and community feedback on services. (4) Data sharing agreements must be reviewed and renewed every 2 years to ensure continued relevance and compliance.

heading: Minister's Authority
text: (1) The Minister is authorized to issue directives and guidelines for the implementation and administration of this Act. (2) These directives may cover specific aspects of the application process, reporting requirements, and interpretation of eligibility criteria. (3) Any such directives must be published on the Ministry's website and come into effect 30 days after publication. (4) The Minister also has the authority to approve minor amendments to grant agreements, provided such amendments do not alter the core purpose or financial scope of the grant by more than 10%.

heading: Amendments to Schedules
text: (1) The Minister may, by order, amend any schedule appended to this Act. (2) Any such order must be published in the Nordvale Gazette and presented to the National Assembly within 15 sitting days of its publication. (3) Amendments to schedules may include adjustments to application deadlines, reporting templates, or lists of eligible expenses. (4) Such amendments must not contradict the main provisions of this Act and are intended to provide flexibility in response to evolving community needs or administrative efficiencies.

heading: Review of the Act
text: (1) This Act shall be reviewed by the National Assembly every 5 years from its enactment date to assess its effectiveness and relevance. (2) The first review shall commence no later than January 1st, 2023. (3) The review will include public consultations and a report submitted to the Minister with recommendations for potential amendments. (4) The review process ensures that the grant program remains responsive to the needs of Nordvale's communities and aligns with broader national development goals.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on January 1st, 2018.

heading: Grant Application Deadline
text: (1) The annual deadline for submitting grant applications is October 31st. (2) Applications received after this date will not be considered for the current grant cycle, regardless of the reason for the delay. (3) A grace period of up to 3 days may be granted in exceptional circumstances, at the sole discretion of the Minister, upon receipt of a written request detailing the unforeseen event that caused the delay. (4) No more than 1 such grace period shall be granted to any single applicant within a 5-year period.

heading: Grant Application Deadline
text: (1) The annual deadline for submitting grant applications is September 30th. (2) Applications received after this date will not be considered for the current grant cycle, regardless of the reason for the delay. (3) A grace period of up to 2 days may be granted in exceptional circumstances, at the sole discretion of the Minister, upon receipt of a written request detailing the unforeseen event that caused the delay. (4) No more than 1 such grace period shall be granted to any single applicant within a 7-year period.

heading: Minimum Public Programming Hours
text: (1) Eligible community centres must demonstrate a minimum of 15 hours of public programming per week. (2) This includes activities such as workshops, classes, open social hours, and public events. (3) Time spent on administrative tasks or private bookings not accessible to the general public does not count towards this minimum. (4) Centres must provide a detailed weekly schedule as part of their application, covering at least 10 different types of activities, to prove compliance with this requirement.

heading: Minimum Public Access Days
text: (1) Community centres seeking grants must be accessible to the public for at least 300 days per year. (2) This ensures consistent availability of the facility for community use. (3) Public accessibility means the centre is open for general use, programmed activities, or available for booking by community groups. (4) Days closed for major holidays or essential maintenance (not exceeding 14 days annually) may be counted if advance public notice is provided at least 30 days prior to closure.

heading: Minimum Public Access Days
text: (1) Community centres seeking grants must be accessible to the public for at least 310 days per year. (2) This ensures consistent availability of the facility for community use. (3) Public accessibility means the centre is open for general use, programmed activities, or available for booking by community groups for at least 6 hours per day. (4) Days closed for major holidays or essential maintenance (not exceeding 10 days annually) may be counted if advance public notice is provided at least 45 days prior to closure, and an alternative community space is offered if feasible.

heading: Board Member Requirements
text: (1) A community centre's governing board must consist of at least 5 volunteer members. (2) No more than 2 members of the board may be paid staff of the community centre. (3) Board members must be residents of Nordvale and ideally represent the diverse demographics of the community served by the centre. (4) The board is responsible for financial oversight, strategic planning, and ensuring the centre's adherence to its non-profit mandate. (5) All board members must serve for terms of at least 2 years.

heading: Audited Financial Statements
text: (1) Grant applicants must submit an annual financial statement, audited by an independent firm, for the preceding fiscal year. (2) The statement must clearly show that the centre's operating deficit did not exceed 10% of its annual budget. (3) The auditor must be a certified accountant registered in Nordvale. (4) The purpose of this requirement is to ensure sound financial management and transparency in the use of public funds. (5) New applicants must submit audited statements for their last 3 fiscal years.

heading: Audited Financial Statements
text: (1) Grant applicants must submit an annual financial statement, audited by an independent firm, for the preceding fiscal year. (2) The statement must clearly show that the centre's operating deficit did not exceed 8% of its annual budget. (3) The auditor must be a certified accountant registered in Nordvale with at least 5 years of experience. (4) The purpose of this requirement is to ensure sound financial management and transparency in the use of public funds, protecting taxpayer investments. (5) New applicants must submit audited statements for their last 5 fiscal years.

heading: Budget Submission Detail
text: (1) The detailed budget required for applications must itemize all projected operating and maintenance expenses. (2) This includes categories such as salaries (administrative and program staff), utilities (electricity, water, heating), insurance, cleaning services, minor repairs (under 2,000 crowns per incident), and program supplies. (3) Revenue projections from other sources, including membership fees, fundraising, and municipal support, must also be included. (4) The budget must project expenses for the entire 12-month grant period and demonstrate realistic financial planning based on historical data.

heading: Community Engagement Report
text: (1) The community engagement report must provide a narrative of activities from the previous year. (2) This report must include attendance figures for at least 3 major events, such as annual festivals, charity drives, or large-scale workshops. (3) It should also describe efforts to reach diverse community segments, including outreach to seniors, youth, and new residents. (4) Qualitative feedback from community members, such as testimonials or survey summaries from at least 50 respondents, is highly encouraged to demonstrate impact.

heading: Committee Member Qualifications
text: (1) Members of the Grant Allocation Committee shall possess expertise relevant to community development or non-profit management. (2) At least one member must have experience in financial auditing or accounting. (3) All members must demonstrate impartiality and have no direct financial interest in any community centre applying for a grant. (4) Prior experience on a municipal or regional advisory board is considered an asset. (5) New committee members must undergo a mandatory 2-day training program on grant assessment principles and ethical conduct.

heading: Committee Meeting Frequency
text: (1) The Grant Allocation Committee shall meet at least twice annually: once to review initial applications and once to assess interim reports. (2) Additional meetings may be called by the Committee Chair as needed, provided that at least 7 days' notice is given to all members. (3) All meetings require a quorum of at least 4 members to proceed with decision-making. (4) Minutes of all committee meetings must be recorded and made available to the Minister within 14 days of the meeting.

heading: Maximum Grant Fund Percentage
text: (1) No single community centre may receive more than 15% of the total annual grant fund. (2) This ensures equitable distribution of funds across all eligible municipalities and prevents over-reliance of any one centre on government funding. (3) If a centre's calculated grant amount exceeds this percentage, its allocation will be capped at 15%, and the remaining funds will be reallocated to other deserving applicants. (4) The total annual grant fund is published by the Minister by July 1st of each year.

heading: Maximum Grant Coverage
text: (1) Grants are intended to cover up to 50% of eligible operating and maintenance costs. (2) Community centres are expected to secure the remaining funding from other sources, such as municipal contributions, private donations, fundraising events, or earned income. (3) This co-funding model promotes financial sustainability and diverse revenue streams for community centres. (4) Centres demonstrating a higher percentage of self-generated income may be given preferential consideration during the assessment process, up to a maximum of 70% self-funding.

heading: Maximum Grant Coverage
text: (1) Grants are intended to cover up to 45% of eligible operating and maintenance costs. (2) Community centres are expected to secure the remaining funding from other sources, such as municipal contributions, private donations, fundraising events, or earned income, covering at least 55% of their budget. (3) This co-funding model promotes financial sustainability and diverse revenue streams for community centres, reducing reliance on public funds. (4) Centres demonstrating a higher percentage of self-generated income may be given preferential consideration during the assessment process, up to a maximum of 75% self-funding.

heading: Interim Report Contents
text: (1) The interim report, due 6 months into the grant period, must include a detailed financial statement of expenditures made to date. (2) It must also provide an update on the progress of planned activities and any significant deviations from the original program schedule. (3) A brief narrative highlighting key achievements and challenges encountered during the first half of the grant period is also required. (4) The report should demonstrate that at least 40% of the first installment has been expended on eligible costs.

heading: Final Report Contents
text: (1) The comprehensive final report must include audited financial statements covering the entire grant period. (2) A detailed narrative of all programs and activities undertaken, including participant numbers and impact assessments, is also required. (3) The report should explicitly state how the grant funds contributed to achieving the centre's objectives and the overall purpose of this Act. (4) Photos, testimonials, and media clippings showcasing the centre's activities are encouraged to supplement the report and demonstrate community benefit.

heading: Prohibited Use of Funds
text: (1) Grant funds shall not be used for any capital expenditures exceeding 5,000 crowns, such as major structural repairs, land acquisition, or new building construction, without explicit written consent from the Minister. (2) Funds are also strictly prohibited for political campaigning, partisan activities, or direct support of political candidates. (3) Religious instruction or proselytization activities are not eligible for grant funding. (4) Any expenditure deemed by the Minister to be inconsistent with the non-profit and community-focused nature of the centre may be subject to repayment.

heading: Repayment of Funds
text: (1) In cases of non-compliance, the Minister may require the repayment of all or part of the grant funds. (2) A repayment order will specify the amount to be repaid and the deadline for payment, typically within 60 days of the order. (3) Failure to repay funds by the specified deadline may result in legal action to recover the debt. (4) Interest may be charged on overdue repayment amounts at a rate of 5% per annum, calculated from the original repayment deadline.

heading: Ineligibility for Future Grants
text: (1) A community centre found to be in serious non-compliance with this Act may be declared ineligible for future grants for a period of up to 5 years. (2) The duration of ineligibility will be determined based on the severity and recurrence of the non-compliance. (3) This declaration will be communicated in writing to the centre's governing board. (4) Eligibility may be reinstated earlier if the centre demonstrates a clear and sustained commitment to rectifying past issues and implementing robust compliance measures, subject to a special review by the Grant Allocation Committee.

heading: Appeals Board Composition
text: (1) The independent Appeals Board shall consist of 3 members appointed by the Minister. (2) These members must not be current members of the Grant Allocation Committee or Ministry staff. (3) At least one member must have a legal background and another must have significant experience in dispute resolution. (4) Members of the Appeals Board shall serve for staggered terms of 2 years to ensure continuity and may be reappointed for one additional term. (5) All Board members must sign a confidentiality agreement before commencing their duties.

heading: Public Register of Grants
text: (1) The Ministry shall maintain a publicly accessible register of all community centres that have received grants under this Act. (2) This register will include the name of the centre, the municipality it serves, the grant amount awarded, and the grant period. (3) Information for the previous 5 years will be available, ensuring transparency in the allocation of public funds. (4) The register will be updated annually by April 15th and published on the Ministry's official website in a clear and easily searchable format.

heading: Annual Grant Allocation Limit
text: (1) The total annual allocation for the Community Centre Operating Grants program shall not exceed 5 million crowns. (2) This limit ensures fiscal responsibility and allows for sustainable funding of the program within the national budget. (3) The Minister may, in exceptional circumstances and with the approval of the National Assembly, increase this limit by up to 10% for a single fiscal year. (4) Any unspent funds from the annual allocation will revert to the general treasury at the end of the fiscal year.

heading: Annual Grant Allocation Limit
text: (1) The total annual allocation for the Community Centre Operating Grants program shall not exceed 5.5 million crowns. (2) This limit ensures fiscal responsibility and allows for sustainable funding of the program within the national budget, accounting for inflation and increased demand. (3) The Minister may, in exceptional circumstances and with the approval of the National Assembly, increase this limit by up to 15% for a single fiscal year. (4) Any unspent funds from the annual allocation will revert to the general treasury at the end of the fiscal year, after a 3% contingency fund is set aside for emergencies.

heading: Data Protection and Privacy
text: (1) All personal information collected from grant applicants and community centre participants shall be handled in strict accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations. (2) Such information will only be used for the purposes of administering this Act and evaluating program effectiveness. (3) Anonymized and aggregated data may be used for statistical reporting and public transparency, but individual identities will be protected. (4) Grant recipients are also responsible for ensuring the privacy of their service users and adherence to relevant data protection laws.

heading: Ministerial Directives
text: (1) The Minister is empowered to issue binding directives to clarify the interpretation and application of this Act. (2) These directives may specify procedures for submitting appeals, formats for financial reports, or detailed criteria for program eligibility. (3) All directives must be published on the Ministry's official website at least 30 days before they come into effect. (4) Stakeholders, including community centres and municipal governments, will be given an opportunity to provide feedback on proposed directives during a 20-day public consultation period.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (1) Any community centre that received operating funding from the Ministry prior to the enactment of this Act shall be deemed provisionally eligible for grants under this Act for the first grant cycle, provided they submit a complete application within 90 days of the Act's commencement. (2) During this transitional period, existing funding agreements will remain in effect until a decision is made on their application under this Act. (3) The Minister may grant extensions to this 90-day period in exceptional cases, not exceeding an additional 30 days. (4) This ensures a smooth transition and avoids disruption to essential community services.

heading: Emergency Funding
text: (1) In unforeseen emergencies, such as natural disasters or structural damage, a community centre may apply for a one-time emergency grant. (2) Such grants are separate from the regular operating grants and capped at 25,000 crowns or 20% of the centre's annual operating budget, whichever is lower. (3) Applications for emergency funding must be submitted within 14 days of the incident and include detailed estimates for repairs or operational continuity. (4) The Minister may approve such grants quickly, usually within 7 days, to address immediate needs.

heading: Collaboration with Municipalities
text: (1) The Minister encourages active collaboration between community centres and their respective municipal governments. (2) Evidence of municipal support, such as shared services agreements, in-kind contributions, or direct financial aid, will be viewed favorably during the grant assessment process. (3) Municipalities are encouraged to provide letters of support for grant applications, outlining their commitment to the centre's mission. (4) Up to 10% of a centre's total assessment score may be allocated based on the strength of its municipal partnerships, provided the municipality itself contributes at least 5,000 crowns annually.

heading: Public Engagement Requirements
