text: (1) Grant recipient centres must hold at least one public forum annually to gather feedback from their community members. (2) These forums should be widely publicized at least 30 days in advance and open to all residents. (3) Minutes of these forums, including questions raised and responses provided, must be submitted with the final grant report. (4) This ensures that community centres remain responsive to the evolving needs and preferences of the populations they serve. (5) Attendance at these forums must be recorded, with a minimum of 25 attendees required for it to be considered a valid public forum.

heading: Sustainability Initiatives
text: (1) Community centres are encouraged to implement sustainability initiatives, such as energy efficiency upgrades or waste reduction programs. (2) While these are not directly funded by operating grants, proposals that demonstrate a commitment to environmental stewardship may receive additional points in the assessment. (3) Up to 5 bonus points can be awarded for comprehensive sustainability plans that include measurable targets and a budget for implementation, even if funded by other sources. (4) Centres achieving a 15% reduction in energy consumption over a 3-year period will receive a special commendation from the Minister.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: (1) Any disputes arising between the Ministry and a grant recipient that cannot be resolved through the appeal process outlined in section 13 may be submitted to mediation. (2) The mediator shall be an independent third party agreed upon by both parties, with costs shared equally. (3) Mediation proceedings must be completed within 60 days of the dispute being submitted. (4) The outcome of mediation is non-binding, but parties are expected to engage in good faith to reach a mutually acceptable resolution. (5) If mediation fails, the dispute may proceed to arbitration.

heading: Reporting of Significant Changes
text: (1) Grant recipient centres must inform the Minister in writing of any significant changes to their operations, governance, or financial status within 30 days of the change occurring. (2) Significant changes include, but are not limited to, changes in leadership, substantial alterations to programming, or financial difficulties that could impact the centre's ability to operate. (3) Failure to report such changes promptly may be considered a breach of the grant agreement. (4) The Minister will assess the reported changes to determine if they affect continued grant eligibility or require adjustments to the grant terms.

heading: Maximum Administrative Costs
text: (1) Administrative costs, including salaries for administrative staff and office supplies, are capped at 25% of the total grant amount. (2) This ensures that the majority of grant funds directly support program delivery and facility maintenance, maximizing community benefit. (3) Centres must clearly delineate administrative costs from program delivery costs in their budget submissions and financial reports. (4) Any administrative expenses exceeding this 25% cap will not be eligible for reimbursement through the grant and must be covered by other funding sources.

heading: Maximum Administrative Costs
text: (1) Administrative costs, including salaries for administrative staff and office supplies, are capped at 20% of the total grant amount. (2) This ensures that the vast majority of grant funds directly support program delivery and facility maintenance, maximizing community benefit and direct service provision. (3) Centres must clearly delineate administrative costs from program delivery costs in their budget submissions and financial reports. (4) Any administrative expenses exceeding this 20% cap will not be eligible for reimbursement through the grant and must be covered by other funding sources, with a potential 10% penalty on the subsequent grant application if the cap is exceeded by more than 5%.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: (1) All community centres receiving grants must maintain adequate general liability insurance coverage, with a minimum coverage of 2 million crowns. (2) Proof of current insurance coverage must be submitted with the grant application and renewed annually. (3) The insurance policy must name the Republic of Nordvale as an additional insured party. (4) Failure to maintain valid insurance coverage will result in immediate suspension of grant payments and potential demands for repayment of previously disbursed funds. (5) Coverage must include protection against accidents involving children and vulnerable adults.

heading: Youth Program Emphasis
text: (1) Community centres that demonstrate a strong emphasis on youth programming will receive preferential consideration in the grant assessment process. (2) At least 30% of weekly public programming hours should be dedicated to activities for individuals aged 18 and younger. (3) This includes after-school programs, youth clubs, sports activities, and educational workshops. (4) Centres that partner with local schools or youth organizations to deliver programs will be awarded additional points. (5) A minimum of 2 distinct programs for youth must be offered year-round.

heading: Senior Citizen Programs
text: (1) Community centres offering dedicated programs for senior citizens will also receive favorable consideration. (2) A minimum of 10 hours of weekly programming should be allocated for individuals aged 65 and over. (3) Examples include social gatherings, health and wellness classes, and intergenerational activities. (4) Centres providing transportation assistance for seniors to access their programs will be given priority. (5) At least 1 full-time or 2 part-time staff members should be dedicated to senior programming.

heading: Volunteer Contribution
text: (1) The level of volunteer participation in a community centre's operations will be a significant factor in grant assessment. (2) Centres must demonstrate at least 500 hours of documented volunteer service annually. (3) This includes volunteer time spent on governance, program delivery, maintenance, and fundraising. (4) A detailed log of volunteer hours, signed by the volunteers and a board member, must be submitted with the application. (5) Centres exceeding 1,000 volunteer hours annually will receive a 5% bonus on their overall assessment score.

heading: Volunteer Contribution
text: (1) The level of volunteer participation in a community centre's operations will be a significant factor in grant assessment. (2) Centres must demonstrate at least 600 hours of documented volunteer service annually. (3) This includes volunteer time spent on governance, program delivery, maintenance, and fundraising. (4) A detailed log of volunteer hours, signed by the volunteers and a board member, must be submitted with the application. (5) Centres exceeding 1,200 volunteer hours annually will receive a 7% bonus on their overall assessment score, acknowledging their strong community commitment.

heading: Capital Expenditure Approval
text: (1) Any proposed capital expenditure exceeding 5,000 crowns using grant funds must receive prior written approval from the Minister. (2) The request for approval must include detailed justifications, cost estimates from at least two independent contractors, and a plan for how the expenditure benefits the centre's long-term sustainability. (3) Approval is granted only for expenditures directly related to enhancing the existing facility's functionality or safety, not for expansion. (4) Requests must be submitted at least 60 days before the planned expenditure, and retrospective approval will not be granted under any circumstances.

heading: Section 40
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: Each licensed balloon pilot receives an additional 30 calendar days to remit any fee or allowance required by FDA §11.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a certified tide-table surveyor, the admission fee for a public swimming pool is 5 crowns, replacing the standard 10 crowns adult admission charge.

heading: Exemptions for renal filtration patients
text:
(1) No amount is payable by a renal filtration patient for an indoor exercise attendance.
(2) This exemption is in place of any other abatement.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for customs declaration fees within the Republic of Nordvale. It delineates the charges applicable to various types of declarations submitted for goods entering or exiting Nordvale territory, ensuring a standardized approach across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. The primary objective is to cover administrative costs associated with processing these declarations and maintaining the customs infrastructure. All fees collected under this Act shall be remitted to the national treasury.

heading: General Declaration Fee
text: A standard fee of 150 crowns shall be levied for each customs declaration submitted, regardless of the goods' origin or destination. This fee applies to all declarations, including those for commercial shipments and personal consignments exceeding a value of 500 crowns. Declarations for goods valued at 500 crowns or less are exempt from this specific general declaration fee, but may be subject to other fees as outlined in subsequent sections. The fee must be paid in full at the time of declaration submission.

heading: General Declaration Fee
text: A standard fee of 175 crowns shall be levied for each customs declaration submitted, regardless of the goods' origin or destination. This fee applies to all declarations, including those for commercial shipments and personal consignments exceeding a value of 600 crowns. Declarations for goods valued at 600 crowns or less are exempt from this specific general declaration fee, but may be subject to other fees as outlined in subsequent sections. The fee must be paid in full at the time of declaration submission to avoid processing delays.

heading: General Declaration Fee
text: A standard fee of 200 crowns shall be levied for each customs declaration submitted, regardless of the goods' origin or destination. This fee applies to all declarations, including those for commercial shipments and personal consignments exceeding a value of 750 crowns. Declarations for goods valued at 750 crowns or less are exempt from this specific general declaration fee, but may be subject to other fees as outlined in subsequent sections. The fee must be paid in full at the time of declaration submission to avoid processing delays, with a 10% penalty for late payments.

heading: Electronic Declaration Discount
text: Declarations submitted electronically through the official Nordvale Customs Portal are eligible for a 10% discount on the General Declaration Fee specified in section 2. This encourages efficiency and reduces manual processing. To qualify for the discount, the entire declaration must be submitted digitally, without any paper components. The discount is applied automatically upon successful electronic submission and payment, and is visible on the electronic receipt issued to the declarant. This applies to all submissions in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Electronic Declaration Discount
text: Declarations submitted electronically through the official Nordvale Customs Portal are eligible for a 15% discount on the General Declaration Fee specified in section 2. This enhanced discount aims to further promote digital processing and streamline customs operations. To qualify, the complete declaration, including all supporting documents, must be submitted digitally. The discount is automatically calculated and applied upon electronic submission and payment, reflecting on the confirmation provided to the declarant.

heading: Manual Processing Surcharge
text: A surcharge of 75 crowns shall be applied to any customs declaration that requires manual processing due to errors, incomplete information, or submission in a non-electronic format where an electronic option exists. This surcharge covers the additional administrative effort involved in correcting or inputting data manually. The declarant will be notified of this surcharge within 3 business days of submission. Failure to pay the surcharge within 14 days may result in processing delays or rejection of the declaration.

heading: Urgent Processing Fee
text: For declarations requiring processing within 24 hours of submission, an urgent processing fee of 300 crowns shall apply. This fee is in addition to any other applicable declaration fees. Urgent processing is only available for specific categories of goods designated by the Nordvale Customs Authority and must be requested explicitly at the time of submission. The authority reserves the right to deny urgent processing if capacity limits are exceeded or if the declaration is found to be incomplete upon initial review.

heading: Urgent Processing Fee
text: For declarations requiring processing within 12 hours of submission, an urgent processing fee of 450 crowns shall apply. This fee is in addition to any other applicable declaration fees and is non-refundable. Urgent processing is only available for specific categories of perishable goods or critical components, as designated by the Nordvale Customs Authority, and must be requested explicitly. Such requests are subject to approval based on operational capacity at the time of submission in Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Amendment Fee (Minor Correction)
text: A fee of 50 crowns is payable for minor amendments to a submitted customs declaration, such as correcting a typographical error or an incorrect quantity by less than 5%. This fee applies only if the amendment is requested and processed before the goods have been released by customs. Multiple minor corrections to the same declaration will each incur this fee, up to a maximum of three amendments per declaration. Beyond three, a major amendment fee as outlined in section 7 will apply.

heading: Amendment Fee (Major Correction)
text: A fee of 150 crowns is payable for major amendments to a submitted customs declaration, including changes to the type of goods, the value by more than 5%, or the recipient/sender information. This fee applies if the amendment is requested after the initial processing has begun, but before final clearance. If a major amendment is requested after goods have been released, a new declaration may be required, incurring full declaration fees. This applies to changes made in Lund Vale.

heading: Amendment Fee (Major Correction)
text: A fee of 200 crowns is payable for major amendments to a submitted customs declaration, including changes to the type of goods, the value by more than 10%, or the recipient/sender information. This fee applies if the amendment is requested after the initial processing has begun, but before final clearance. If a major amendment is requested after goods have been released, a new declaration may be required, incurring full declaration fees and potentially other penalties for misdeclaration.

heading: Storage Fees for Unprocessed Goods
text: Goods awaiting customs clearance for which a declaration has been submitted, but not yet fully processed, may incur storage fees if remaining at a customs facility for more than 7 days. The fee is 25 crowns per day for the first 30 days, and 50 crowns per day thereafter. These fees are levied to encourage prompt resolution of any issues preventing clearance and to manage storage capacity. The period begins the day after submission of the declaration.

heading: Storage Fees for Unprocessed Goods
text: Goods awaiting customs clearance for which a declaration has been submitted, but not yet fully processed, may incur storage fees if remaining at a customs facility for more than 5 days. The fee is 30 crowns per day for the first 20 days, and 60 crowns per day thereafter. These fees are levied to encourage prompt resolution of any issues preventing clearance and to manage storage capacity effectively. The period begins the day after the initial declaration submission, irrespective of any amendments.

heading: Declaration for Temporary Import/Export
text: A specific fee of 100 crowns applies to declarations for temporary import or export of goods, where the goods are intended to remain in or out of Nordvale for a period not exceeding 365 days. This fee covers the administrative effort of tracking the temporary status of the goods and ensuring their eventual re-export or re-import. A deposit equivalent to the customs duties and taxes may also be required, refundable upon confirmation of the goods' departure or return.

heading: Simplified Declaration Fee
text: For low-value consignments (under 200 crowns) or for certain pre-approved regular importers, a simplified declaration process is available, incurring a fee of 75 crowns. This process reduces the number of data fields required, streamlining submission for eligible parties. Eligibility criteria are published by the Nordvale Customs Authority and reviewed annually. This simplified fee cannot be combined with the electronic declaration discount under section 3, as it is already a reduced rate.

heading: Batch Declaration Fee
text: For commercial entities submitting multiple declarations simultaneously as part of a single bulk shipment, a batch declaration fee structure applies. The first declaration in the batch incurs the full General Declaration Fee (section 2), while subsequent declarations in the same batch are charged at 50% of the General Declaration Fee, up to a maximum of 50 declarations per batch. All declarations in the batch must be for goods arriving or departing on the same conveyance and at the same time.

heading: Late Payment Penalty
text: Payments for customs declaration fees received more than 14 days after the due date will incur a late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount, with a minimum penalty of 25 crowns. This penalty is applied automatically to the outstanding balance. Continued failure to pay may result in further penalties, including the suspension of customs clearance privileges for the declarant or seizure of goods. The due date is defined as the date of formal notification of fees.

heading: Refund Processing Fee
text: A fee of 30 crowns will be deducted from any refund issued for customs declaration fees, to cover the administrative costs associated with processing the refund. This fee applies to all refunds, regardless of the reason for the refund, unless the refund is initiated due to an error made by the Nordvale Customs Authority. The fee is applied per refund transaction, not per declaration.

heading: Appeals Review Fee
text: An appeals review fee of 200 crowns is required for any formal appeal against a customs declaration fee assessment. This fee is refundable if the appeal is successful and the original assessment is overturned or significantly reduced. The appeal must be submitted in writing within 60 days of the original fee assessment. The fee covers the administrative cost of the review panel and is payable at the time of appeal submission.

heading: Appeals Review Fee
text: An appeals review fee of 250 crowns is required for any formal appeal against a customs declaration fee assessment. This fee is refundable if the appeal is successful and the original assessment is overturned or significantly reduced by more than 50%. The appeal must be submitted in writing within 45 days of the original fee assessment. The fee covers the administrative cost of the review panel and is payable at the time of appeal submission, prior to any review commencing.

heading: Fee for Declarations via Third-Party Agents
text: When a customs declaration is submitted on behalf of a declarant by a registered third-party customs agent, an additional administrative fee of 60 crowns is applicable. This fee acknowledges the additional verification steps required when dealing with intermediaries. This fee is separate from any charges levied by the third-party agent themselves. The third-party agent is responsible for collecting and remitting this fee to the Nordvale Customs Authority.

heading: Consignment of Origin Declaration Fee
text: Declarations specifically for consignments originating from specific trade agreement partners, requiring proof of origin for preferential treatment, incur a fee of 80 crowns. This covers the additional scrutiny and verification processes for certificates of origin. This fee is waived if the total value of the goods in the consignment is less than 300 crowns. The fee applies per declaration, irrespective of the number of origin certificates presented.

heading: Consignment of Origin Declaration Fee
text: Declarations specifically for consignments originating from specific trade agreement partners, requiring proof of origin for preferential treatment, incur a fee of 95 crowns. This covers the additional scrutiny and verification processes for certificates of origin. This fee is waived if the total value of the goods in the consignment is less than 400 crowns. The fee applies per declaration, irrespective of the number of origin certificates presented, and is mandatory for all such claims.

heading: High-Value Goods Declaration Fee
text: For declarations of goods with a declared value exceeding 100,000 crowns, an additional fee of 0.1% of the excess value above 100,000 crowns shall be applied, with a minimum additional fee of 50 crowns. This fee accounts for the increased risk assessment and detailed inspection protocols often associated with high-value imports and exports. This fee is calculated automatically based on the declared value submitted in the declaration.

heading: Declaration for Goods Under Special Control
text: Declarations for goods subject to special control, such as certain chemicals, artworks, or protected cultural artifacts, incur an additional fee of 120 crowns. This fee covers the specialized handling, documentation verification, and potential coordination with other regulatory bodies required for such items. A list of goods subject to special control is published annually by the Nordvale Customs Authority. This fee is mandatory for all applicable declarations in Aldmark.

heading: Re-export Declaration Fee
text: A fee of 90 crowns is applicable to declarations for goods being re-exported after having been previously imported into Nordvale. This fee covers the verification of the goods' original import status and ensures compliance with re-export regulations. This fee applies even if the original import declaration was subject to a temporary import regime. Proper documentation linking the re-export to the original import is required to avoid additional charges.

heading: Declaration for Damaged or Defective Goods
text: Declarations for goods that are declared as damaged or defective upon import, and which are intended for destruction, return, or significant repair, incur a fee of 70 crowns. This fee covers the specific administrative procedures and potential inspections required for such consignments. Documentation proving the damage or defect, such as inspection reports, must accompany the declaration. The fee is applied to each declaration, irrespective of the number of damaged items.

heading: Multiple Item Declaration Fee
text: For declarations covering more than 5 distinct types of items (Harmonized System codes), an additional fee of 10 crowns per extra item type shall be charged. This recognizes the increased complexity in processing and verifying declarations with diverse contents. The maximum additional fee under this section is capped at 200 crowns for any single declaration. This encourages consolidated shipments where practical.

heading: Multiple Item Declaration Fee
text: For declarations covering more than 3 distinct types of items (Harmonized System codes), an additional fee of 15 crowns per extra item type shall be charged. This recognizes the increased complexity in processing and verifying declarations with diverse contents. The maximum additional fee under this section is capped at 250 crowns for any single declaration. This encourages consolidated shipments where practical, especially for declarations submitted in Corvik.

heading: Advance Declaration Fee
text: A fee of 40 crowns applies to declarations submitted more than 7 days in advance of the goods' arrival or departure. This incentivizes early submission, allowing customs authorities to pre-process and plan inspections more efficiently. This fee is non-refundable even if the arrival or departure date changes, unless the change is formally notified at least 48 hours before the original scheduled time. This applies to all goods in Dunmere.

heading: Advance Declaration Fee
text: A fee of 50 crowns applies to declarations submitted more than 10 days in advance of the goods' arrival or departure. This incentivizes early submission, allowing customs authorities to pre-process and plan inspections more efficiently. This fee is non-refundable even if the arrival or departure date changes, unless the change is formally notified at least 72 hours before the original scheduled time. This fee is designed to reduce last-minute rush declarations.

heading: Declaration for Repair or Alteration
text: A fee of 85 crowns is charged for declarations covering goods imported for repair or alteration and intended for re-export. This fee facilitates the temporary import regime and tracks the goods through their repair cycle within Nordvale. Proof of the original import and the intent for repair/alteration, such as service contracts, must be provided. This applies to items that will be re-exported within 180 days of their import.

heading: Correction of Tariff Classification Fee
text: If, during the customs clearance process, it is determined that a declared tariff classification requires correction by the customs authority, a fee of 110 crowns will be applied. This covers the expert review and re-classification process. This fee is distinct from the amendment fees in sections 6 and 7, as it reflects an error identified by the authority rather than a voluntary correction by the declarant. This ensures accurate duty and tax assessment.

heading: Declaration for Returned Goods
text: Declarations for goods being returned to Nordvale after having been exported, or returned to a foreign country after having been imported, incur a fee of 70 crowns. This applies when no duty or tax is payable due to the returned nature of the goods. Documentation proving the original export or import, and the reason for return, must be submitted with the declaration. The fee helps cover the verification of the returned goods' status.

heading: Certified Copy of Declaration Fee
text: A fee of 20 crowns is charged for each certified copy of a customs declaration requested by the declarant or an authorized party. This fee covers the administrative cost of retrieving, verifying, and certifying the document. Requests for certified copies must be made in writing and specify the declaration reference number. Copies will be provided within 5 business days of the request and fee payment.

heading: Exemptions for Diplomatic Consignments
text: Consignments from accredited diplomatic missions and consular posts to Nordvale are exempt from all customs declaration fees specified in this Act. This exemption extends to personal effects of accredited diplomatic personnel, provided the consignments are clearly marked and accompanied by appropriate diplomatic documentation. This aligns with international conventions on diplomatic relations and privileges in Elsby.

heading: Exemptions for Emergency Aid
text: Customs declarations for goods imported or exported as part of officially recognized humanitarian aid or emergency relief efforts are exempt from all fees under this Act. This exemption requires certification from a recognized relief organization or a government agency. The goods must be clearly identifiable as aid, such as medical supplies or temporary shelter, and not for commercial purposes. This fosters timely response to crises.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in crowns. Accepted payment methods include direct bank transfer, credit or debit card payments at customs offices, or through the official Nordvale Customs Portal for electronic submissions. Cash payments are accepted only for fees under 500 crowns. Personal cheques are not accepted. Proof of payment is required for all declarations to proceed to clearance.

heading: Review of Fees
text: The Nordvale Customs Authority shall review all fees specified in this Act at least once every three years. This review will consider administrative costs, inflation, technological advancements, and economic conditions to ensure fees remain appropriate and effective. Any proposed changes to the fees will be published for public consultation at least 90 days before their intended implementation date. This maintains transparency and fairness in the fee structure.

heading: Penalties for False Declaration of Value
text: Any declarant found to have intentionally misrepresented the value of goods in a customs declaration by more than 20% shall be liable for a penalty of 500 crowns, in addition to any underpaid duties or taxes. Repeated offenses may lead to higher penalties, up to 2,000 crowns, and suspension of customs privileges for up to 180 days. This deters fraudulent declarations and ensures fair competition for all businesses.

heading: Penalties for False Declaration of Value
text: Any declarant found to have intentionally misrepresented the value of goods in a customs declaration by more than 15% shall be liable for a penalty of 750 crowns, in addition to any underpaid duties or taxes. Repeated offenses may lead to higher penalties, up to 3,000 crowns, and suspension of customs privileges for up to 365 days. This reinforces the importance of accurate reporting and integrity in customs procedures.

heading: Repealed Section on Express Courier Declarations
text: A specific declaration fee of 65 crowns applied to consignments handled by approved express courier services, due to their streamlined processing and bulk handling. This fee aimed to differentiate from standard declarations while acknowledging the efficiencies provided by courier services. This fee was separate from the general declaration fee and applied per consignment, up to a maximum of 10 items per consignment. It was intended to encourage the use of such services for rapid movement of goods.

heading: Repealed Section on Express Courier Declarations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2018. All provisions and fees outlined herein are effective from this date, applying to all customs declarations submitted on or after this commencement. Any declarations submitted prior to this date shall be governed by the previous regulations. The Nordvale Customs Authority will publish a comprehensive guide to this Act within 30 days of its enactment to ensure clarity for all affected parties in municipalities like Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a household that includes a licensed taxidermist for at least one year shall receive heating support reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered seed bank curator shall pay an annual licence fee of five crowns for each dog they keep.

heading: Special categories
text: No electric bicycle registration fee is payable by a licensed chimney-sweep master, who shall instead pay half of the annual registration fee of thirty crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the licensing of individuals and companies involved in commercial diving operations within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety, professionalism, and environmental responsibility of all commercial diving activities, thereby protecting divers, the public, and marine ecosystems. This Act applies to all waters within Nordvale's territorial jurisdiction, extending 12 nautical miles from its coastline. Any person or entity engaging in commercial diving without a valid licence, as prescribed by this Act, shall be subject to penalties outlined in subsequent sections. The provisions herein aim to create a clear and enforceable standard for this specialized industry.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(1) 'Commercial diving' means any diving activity conducted for remuneration or as part of a business operation, including but not limited to underwater construction, inspection, salvage, or scientific research.
(2) 'Licensing Authority' refers to the Department of Maritime Affairs, responsible for issuing and regulating licences.
(3) 'Diver' means an individual certified to perform commercial diving tasks.
(4) 'Company' means any legal entity, including partnerships or corporations, engaged in commercial diving operations.
(5) 'Deep diving' means any dive exceeding a depth of 50 meters, requiring specialized equipment and procedures.
(6) 'Shallow diving' means any dive up to a depth of 50 meters.

heading: Requirement for licence
text:
(1) No individual shall engage in commercial diving operations within Nordvale's waters without holding a valid individual commercial diving licence issued by the Licensing Authority.
(2) No company shall engage in commercial diving operations without holding a valid company commercial diving licence issued by the Licensing Authority.
(3) Exemptions may be granted for emergency operations under specific conditions, as determined by the Licensing Authority. Such exemptions are valid for a maximum of 48 hours.
(4) All licensed individuals and companies must adhere to safety standards outlined in this Act and associated regulations.

heading: Application for individual licence
text:
(1) An individual seeking a commercial diving licence must submit an application to the Licensing Authority.
(2) The application must include proof of age, demonstrating the applicant is at least 18 years old.
(3) Certified documentation of professional diving qualifications from an approved institution is required.
(4) A medical certificate, issued within the last 12 months by a physician approved by the Department of Health, confirming fitness for commercial diving, must accompany the application.
(5) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is payable upon submission.

heading: Application for individual licence
text:
(1) An individual seeking a commercial diving licence must submit an application to the Licensing Authority.
(2) The application must include proof of age, demonstrating the applicant is at least 19 years old.
(3) Certified documentation of professional diving qualifications from an approved institution is required, including at least 50 logged hours of commercial diving experience.
(4) A medical certificate, issued within the last 6 months by a physician approved by the Department of Health, confirming fitness for commercial diving, must accompany the application.
(5) A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns is payable upon submission.

heading: Application for individual licence
text:
(1) An individual seeking a commercial diving licence must submit an application to the Licensing Authority.
(2) The application must include proof of age, demonstrating the applicant is at least 20 years old.
(3) Certified documentation of professional diving qualifications from an approved institution is required, including at least 75 logged hours of commercial diving experience, with a minimum of 10 hours in deep diving conditions.
(4) A medical certificate, issued within the last 3 months by a physician approved by the Department of Health, confirming fitness for commercial diving, must accompany the application.
(5) A non-refundable application fee of 400 crowns is payable upon submission, along with proof of liability insurance coverage of at least 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Application for company licence
text:
(1) A company seeking a commercial diving licence must submit an application to the Licensing Authority.
(2) The application must include registration documents from the Nordvale Business Registry.
(3) Proof of adequate insurance coverage for commercial diving operations, with a minimum liability of 500,000 crowns, is mandatory.
(4) A list of all certified divers employed or contracted by the company, including their individual licence numbers, must be provided.
(5) A detailed safety plan, compliant with Nordvale's occupational safety regulations, must be submitted.
(6) A non-refundable application fee of 1,000 crowns is payable upon submission.

heading: Licence validity period
text:
(1) An individual commercial diving licence is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue.
(2) A company commercial diving licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(3) Both types of licences are subject to renewal upon expiry, provided all conditions for renewal are met.
(4) The Licensing Authority shall notify licence holders of impending expiry at least 90 days in advance.
(5) Failure to renew a licence before its expiry date will result in its immediate invalidation and cessation of diving activities.

heading: Licence validity period
text:
(1) An individual commercial diving licence is valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issue.
(2) A company commercial diving licence is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue.
(3) Both types of licences are subject to renewal upon expiry, provided all conditions for renewal are met.
(4) The Licensing Authority shall notify licence holders of impending expiry at least 120 days in advance.
(5) Failure to renew a licence before its expiry date will result in its immediate invalidation and cessation of diving activities. A grace period of 30 days may be granted for exceptional circumstances, subject to an additional fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Renewal of individual licence
text:
(1) To renew an individual commercial diving licence, the applicant must submit a renewal application at least 60 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The application must include an updated medical certificate, issued within the last 6 months.
(3) Proof of continuous professional development, including at least 40 hours of relevant training or documented experience, is required.
(4) A renewal fee of 200 crowns is payable.
(5) The Licensing Authority may require the applicant to undergo a practical skills assessment if deemed necessary.

heading: Renewal of company licence
text:
(1) To renew a company commercial diving licence, the applicant company must submit a renewal application at least 90 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The application must include updated registration details and proof of current insurance coverage.
(3) A revised list of all employed or contracted certified divers, along with their current individual licence numbers, must be provided.
(4) Proof of compliance with all safety regulations and an updated safety plan is required.
(5) A renewal fee of 800 crowns is payable. A late renewal fee of an additional 200 crowns applies if submitted less than 30 days before expiry.

heading: Medical fitness for divers
text:
(1) All individual commercial divers must maintain a valid medical certificate attesting to their fitness for diving.
(2) This certificate must be issued by a physician approved by the Department of Health and renewed annually.
(3) Any medical condition arising after certification that may affect diving safety must be immediately reported to the Licensing Authority and a new medical assessment obtained within 14 days.
(4) Failure to comply with medical fitness requirements shall result in the suspension of the individual's licence.
(5) A diver aged 55 or older must undergo a comprehensive medical examination every 6 months.

heading: Medical fitness for divers
text:
(1) All individual commercial divers must maintain a valid medical certificate attesting to their fitness for diving.
(2) This certificate must be issued by a physician approved by the Department of Health and renewed every 18 months, or annually for divers over 50 years of age.
(3) Any medical condition arising after certification that may affect diving safety must be immediately reported to the Licensing Authority and a new medical assessment obtained within 7 days.
(4) Failure to comply with medical fitness requirements shall result in the suspension of the individual's licence.
(5) A diver aged 60 or older must undergo a comprehensive medical examination every 6 months.

heading: Safety standards
text:
(1) All commercial diving operations must adhere to the safety standards prescribed by the Licensing Authority, including but not limited to equipment maintenance, dive planning, and emergency procedures.
(2) A designated dive supervisor, holding an advanced commercial diving certification, must be present and in charge of all diving operations.
(3) Diving equipment must be inspected and certified safe for use every 6 months by an authorized inspector.
(4) Every diving team must include at least one emergency medical technician trained in dive-related injuries.
(5) All divers must have access to a fully equipped first-aid kit and oxygen resuscitation equipment at the dive site.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text:
(1) Any accident, injury, or near-miss incident occurring during commercial diving operations must be reported to the Licensing Authority within 24 hours of its occurrence.
(2) Serious incidents, resulting in death, serious injury, or significant equipment damage exceeding 10,000 crowns, must be reported immediately by telephone, followed by a written report within 12 hours.
(3) The report must detail the circumstances of the incident, contributing factors, and measures taken to prevent recurrence.
(4) Failure to report incidents as required may result in penalties, including fines up to 5,000 crowns or licence suspension.
(5) The Licensing Authority may conduct an investigation into any reported incident.

heading: Suspension of individual licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may suspend an individual commercial diving licence for a period of up to 6 months if the holder:
(a) Fails to comply with safety regulations.
(b) Engages in unsafe diving practices.
(c) Fails to maintain medical fitness.
(d) Provides false or misleading information in an application or report.
(2) Before suspension, the licence holder shall be given 14 days' notice and an opportunity to be heard.
(3) During suspension, the individual is prohibited from engaging in any commercial diving activities.
(4) A suspended licence holder may apply for reinstatement after the suspension period, subject to fulfilling specified conditions.

heading: Suspension of individual licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may suspend an individual commercial diving licence for a period of up to 12 months if the holder:
(a) Fails to comply with safety regulations on more than one occasion.
(b) Engages in unsafe diving practices causing an incident requiring medical intervention.
(c) Fails to maintain medical fitness as per section 9.
(d) Provides false or misleading information in an application or report, or intentionally conceals critical information.
(2) Before suspension, the licence holder shall be given 21 days' notice and an opportunity to present their case in person.
(3) During suspension, the individual is strictly prohibited from engaging in any commercial diving activities, and their name will be publicly listed as suspended.
(4) A suspended licence holder may apply for reinstatement after the suspension period, subject to fulfilling specified conditions, including re-training and a practical re-assessment.

heading: Suspension of company licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may suspend a company commercial diving licence for a period of up to 12 months if the company:
(a) Fails to ensure compliance with safety standards by its employees.
(b) Operates with unlicenced divers.
(c) Fails to report incidents as required by section 11.
(d) Fails to maintain adequate insurance coverage.
(2) Before suspension, the company shall be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to present its case.
(3) During suspension, the company is prohibited from conducting any commercial diving operations.
(4) A suspended company may apply for reinstatement after the suspension period, subject to fulfilling specified conditions and demonstrating corrective actions.

heading: Revocation of individual licence
text:
(1) An individual commercial diving licence may be revoked by the Licensing Authority for severe breaches of this Act or repeated non-compliance.
(2) Grounds for revocation include:
(a) Gross negligence leading to serious injury or death.
(b) Conviction of a serious criminal offence related to diving activities.
(c) Repeated violations of safety regulations after multiple warnings and suspensions.
(3) A revoked licence means the individual is permanently barred from holding a commercial diving licence in Nordvale.
(4) The individual shall be given 30 days' notice and a hearing before revocation.
(5) Decisions of revocation are final, subject to judicial review as per section 28.

heading: Revocation of individual licence
text:
(1) An individual commercial diving licence may be revoked by the Licensing Authority for severe breaches of this Act, repeated non-compliance, or misrepresentation of credentials.
(2) Grounds for revocation include:
(a) Gross negligence leading to serious injury or death, or environmental damage exceeding 20,000 crowns.
(b) Conviction of a serious criminal offence related to diving activities, including fraud or deliberate endangerment.
(c) Accumulation of three or more suspensions within a 10-year period.
(d) Falsification of medical records or diving logs.
(3) A revoked licence means the individual is permanently barred from holding a commercial diving licence in Nordvale, and their name will be entered into a national registry of prohibited divers.
(4) The individual shall be given 45 days' notice and a formal hearing with legal representation before revocation.
(5) Decisions of revocation are final, subject to judicial review as per section 28.

heading: Revocation of company licence
text:
(1) A company commercial diving licence may be revoked by the Licensing Authority for severe breaches of this Act or systemic non-compliance.
(2) Grounds for revocation include:
(a) Repeated operation with unlicenced divers.
(b) Gross negligence leading to serious injury or death, or significant environmental damage.
(c) Persistent failure to adhere to safety standards despite warnings and previous suspensions.
(d) Falsification of company records or insurance documents.
(3) A revoked licence means the company is permanently barred from conducting commercial diving operations in Nordvale.
(4) The company shall be given 45 days' notice and a hearing before revocation.
(5) Decisions of revocation are final, subject to judicial review.

heading: Fines for individuals
text:
(1) An individual found engaging in commercial diving without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second offence, the fine shall be up to 10,000 crowns and an automatic suspension of any future licence applications for 2 years.
(3) Failure to report an incident as required by section 11 may result in a fine of up to 2,000 crowns.
(4) Non-compliance with safety equipment requirements may incur a fine of up to 1,500 crowns per violation.
(5) All fines are payable to the Licensing Authority within 30 days of the penalty notice.

heading: Fines for individuals
text:
(1) An individual found engaging in commercial diving without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of up to 7,500 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second offence, the fine shall be up to 15,000 crowns and an automatic suspension of any future licence applications for 3 years.
(3) Failure to report an incident as required by section 11 may result in a fine of up to 3,000 crowns and a mandatory safety course.
(4) Non-compliance with safety equipment requirements may incur a fine of up to 2,500 crowns per violation.
(5) All fines are payable to the Licensing Authority within 21 days of the penalty notice, with a 10% late payment fee applied thereafter.

heading: Fines for companies
text:
(1) A company found engaging in commercial diving operations without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of up to 20,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second offence, the fine shall be up to 40,000 crowns and an automatic suspension of any future licence applications for 3 years.
(3) Failure to ensure all employed divers hold valid individual licences may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns per unlicensed diver.
(4) Non-compliance with company safety plan implementation may incur a fine of up to 7,500 crowns per violation.
(5) All fines are payable to the Licensing Authority within 30 days of the penalty notice.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An individual or company aggrieved by a decision of the Licensing Authority regarding licence application, suspension, revocation, or fines, may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Maritime Affairs within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the decision and provide a ruling within 60 days of receiving the appeal.
(4) The Appeals Board's decision is final within the administrative framework of this Act.
(5) The appellant may present new evidence or arguments not previously considered by the Licensing Authority.

heading: Records keeping
text:
(1) All licensed individuals must maintain accurate logbooks of their commercial diving activities, including dive dates, locations, depths, durations, and any incidents.
(2) These logbooks must be made available for inspection by the Licensing Authority upon request, with 7 days' notice.
(3) Companies must maintain comprehensive records of all diving operations, equipment maintenance, safety drills, and employee training for a minimum of 5 years.
(4) Failure to maintain accurate and accessible records may result in fines of up to 1,000 crowns for individuals and 5,000 crowns for companies.
(5) Digital record-keeping systems are permissible, provided they meet security and accessibility standards.

heading: Records keeping
text:
(1) All licensed individuals must maintain accurate logbooks of their commercial diving activities, including dive dates, locations, maximum depths, bottom times, decompression schedules, and any incidents or unusual occurrences.
(2) These logbooks must be submitted annually to the Licensing Authority for review and must be made available for immediate inspection upon request.
(3) Companies must maintain comprehensive digital records of all diving operations, equipment maintenance, safety drills, incident reports, and employee training for a minimum of 7 years, ensuring robust backup procedures.
(4) Failure to maintain accurate and accessible records may result in fines of up to 2,500 crowns for individuals and 10,000 crowns for companies, and potential licence suspension.
(5) All records must be kept confidential and comply with Nordvale's data protection regulations.

heading: Equipment certification
text:
(1) All primary diving equipment, including breathing apparatus, dive computers, and pressure gauges, must be certified annually by an approved inspection body.
(2) Life support systems used in deep diving or saturation diving must undergo certification every 6 months.
(3) Compressors, dive bells, and recompression chambers must be inspected and certified every 12 months.
(4) Each piece of certified equipment must bear a visible tag indicating its last inspection date and next due date.
(5) Use of uncertified or expired equipment is strictly prohibited and carries a fine of 2,000 crowns per item.

heading: Environmental protection
text:
(1) All commercial diving operations must be conducted in a manner that minimizes adverse impact on the marine environment.
(2) Divers are prohibited from disturbing marine life, coral reefs, or protected underwater sites without explicit authorization.
(3) Any accidental damage to marine ecosystems must be immediately reported to the Department of Environmental Protection and the Licensing Authority.
(4) Companies must have spill prevention and response plans in place for any potential fuel or oil leaks from support vessels.
(5) Violations of environmental protection provisions may result in fines up to 15,000 crowns and potential licence revocation.

heading: Designated diving zones
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority, in consultation with the Department of Fisheries and Marine Resources, may designate specific areas as restricted or prohibited for commercial diving.
(2) These designations will be based on factors such as marine conservation, shipping lanes, or military zones.
(3) Maps and coordinates of all designated zones shall be published annually and made available to all licence holders.
(4) Commercial diving in a prohibited zone is subject to a fine of 10,000 crowns and immediate licence suspension.
(5) Prior written permission is required for any commercial diving operation within 500 meters of a restricted zone.

heading: Training requirements for divers
text:
(1) All new individual licence applicants must have successfully completed a commercial diving training program approved by the Licensing Authority.
(2) The program must include at least 200 hours of practical in-water training and 100 hours of theoretical instruction.
(3) Specific certifications for specialized diving, such as deep diving, saturation diving, or hazardous materials diving, are required for those operations.
(4) All certified divers must undertake a refresher course every 3 years, covering safety procedures and emergency response.
(5) The Licensing Authority will publish a list of approved training institutions annually.

heading: Training requirements for divers
text:
(1) All new individual licence applicants must have successfully completed a commercial diving training program approved by the Licensing Authority.
(2) The program must include at least 300 hours of practical in-water training and 150 hours of theoretical instruction, with a minimum of 20 hours focused on environmental awareness.
(3) Specific certifications for specialized diving, such as deep diving (exceeding 60 meters), saturation diving, or hazardous materials diving, are strictly required for those operations, with a minimum of 50 logged hours in each specialty.
(4) All certified divers must undertake a comprehensive refresher course every 2 years, covering advanced safety procedures, emergency response, and new technology. This course must be at least 40 hours in duration.
(5) The Licensing Authority will publish a list of approved training institutions quarterly, and only graduates from these institutions will be considered for licensing.

heading: Foreign divers and companies
text:
(1) Foreign individuals and companies wishing to conduct commercial diving operations in Nordvale's waters must obtain a temporary commercial diving licence.
(2) Applicants must demonstrate equivalent qualifications and safety standards to those required of Nordvale citizens and companies.
(3) A local sponsor company, holding a valid Nordvale commercial diving licence, is required for foreign companies.
(4) Temporary licences are valid for a maximum of 6 months and are non-renewable within a 12-month period.
(5) A higher application fee of 1,500 crowns for individuals and 3,000 crowns for companies applies to foreign applicants.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text:
(1) All personal and commercial information provided to the Licensing Authority during the application or compliance process shall be treated with strict confidentiality.
(2) Information may only be disclosed to third parties with the express written consent of the individual or company concerned, or as required by law.
(3) Statistical data, not linked to specific individuals or companies, may be published for industry analysis.
(4) Breaches of confidentiality by Licensing Authority staff may result in disciplinary action, including termination.
(5) This section does not preclude the sharing of information with other relevant Nordvale government agencies for regulatory purposes.

heading: Public register of licences
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall maintain a public register of all valid commercial diving licences, both individual and company.
(2) The register shall include the licence holder's name (or company name), licence number, type of licence, and validity period.
(3) Personal contact details, medical information, or financial data shall not be included in the public register.
(4) The register shall be accessible via the Department of Maritime Affairs website and updated monthly.
(5) Any interested party may request confirmation of a licence holder's status from the Licensing Authority.

heading: Fees and charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges specified in this Act are payable to the Licensing Authority.
(2) These fees are non-refundable, except in cases of administrative error by the Licensing Authority.
(3) The Minister of Maritime Affairs may, by regulation, amend the amounts of fees and charges.
(4) A 10% surcharge will be applied to all overdue payments after 30 days.
(5) Failure to pay prescribed fees may result in refusal to process applications or licence suspension.

heading: Fees and charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges specified in this Act are payable to the Licensing Authority, exclusively through electronic transfer.
(2) These fees are non-refundable, except in cases of administrative error by the Licensing Authority, with refunds processed within 14 business days.
(3) The Minister of Maritime Affairs shall, by regulation published annually, review and may amend the amounts of fees and charges, with any changes taking effect on January 1st of the following year.
(4) A 15% surcharge will be applied to all overdue payments after 15 days, followed by a further 5% monthly interest on the outstanding balance.
(5) Failure to pay prescribed fees may result in refusal to process applications, licence suspension, or additional administrative penalties of up to 1,000 crowns.

heading: Delegation of powers
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may delegate any of its powers or functions under this Act to an authorized officer or body, subject to such conditions as it deems fit.
(2) Any such delegation must be in writing and published in the Nordvale Official Gazette.
(3) The delegate shall exercise the delegated powers or functions in accordance with the provisions of this Act and any instructions issued by the Licensing Authority.
(4) The Licensing Authority remains ultimately responsible for the actions of its delegates.
(5) No power to revoke a licence may be delegated to an external body.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister of Maritime Affairs may make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover, but are not limited to, detailed safety procedures, equipment specifications, environmental guidelines, and specific training curricula.
(3) All regulations must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 60 days before coming into force.
(4) Public consultation on proposed regulations will be open for a minimum of 30 days.
(5) Regulations made under this section shall not contradict or exceed the scope of this Act.

heading: Judicial review
text:
(1) Any individual or company may apply to the Nordvale High Court for judicial review of a final decision made by the Appeals Board under section 18.
(2) An application for judicial review must be lodged within 90 days of the Appeals Board's decision.
(3) The Court shall consider whether the decision was made lawfully, rationally, and fairly.
(4) The Court may quash the decision, remit the matter back to the Appeals Board for reconsideration, or make any other order it deems appropriate.
(5) Legal costs for judicial review are borne by the applicant, unless otherwise ordered by the Court.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Individuals and companies engaged in commercial diving operations prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a period of 12 months to comply with its provisions.
(2) During this transitional period, existing permits or certifications recognized by the Licensing Authority will remain valid.
(3) Applications for licences from existing operators will be prioritized during the first 6 months of the transitional period.
(4) Failure to apply for a licence within the 12-month period will result in immediate cessation of commercial diving activities.
(5) The application fee for existing operators during this period is reduced by 25%.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Individuals and companies engaged in commercial diving operations prior to the commencement of this Act, or any significant amendment to it, shall have a period of 6 months to comply with its updated provisions.
(2) During this transitional period, existing permits or certifications recognized by the Licensing Authority will remain valid, provided they were issued less than 2 years prior.
(3) Applications for licences from existing operators will be prioritized during the first 3 months of the transitional period, with a guaranteed processing time of 45 days.
(4) Failure to apply for a licence or meet new requirements within the 6-month period will result in immediate cessation of commercial diving activities and a penalty fine of 5,000 crowns for companies and 1,000 crowns for individuals.
(5) The application fee for existing operators during this period is reduced by 15%, and they are offered free access to a 2-day compliance workshop.

heading: Penalties for obstruction
text:
(1) Any person who obstructs, hinders, or interferes with an authorized officer of the Licensing Authority in the performance of their duties under this Act commits an offence.
(2) This includes refusing to provide information, providing false information, or preventing access to diving sites or records.
(3) An individual found guilty of obstruction shall be liable to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 months, or both.
(4) A company found guilty of obstruction shall be liable to a fine of up to 15,000 crowns.
(5) Repeated obstruction may lead to licence suspension or revocation.

heading: Inspection powers
text:
(1) Authorized officers of the Licensing Authority may, at any reasonable time, enter any premises, vessel, or dive site where commercial diving operations are being conducted or equipment is stored.
(2) They may inspect equipment, examine records, interview personnel, and request demonstrations of procedures.
(3) Officers must present identification upon request.
(4) Any person found to be impeding an inspection may be subject to penalties as outlined in section 30.
(5) Inspections may be unannounced to ensure ongoing compliance, provided they do not unduly disrupt operations or endanger personnel.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) A person who has been a certified piano restorer for at least one year pays 25 percent less of the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle built with a front or rear load box for carrying goods or children. (2) This reduction applies only to one such bicycle per restorer.

heading: Recognised trades
text: The sibling discount is reduced by an additional 30 days for any parent who has been a registered glassblower for at least one year.

heading: Recognised trades
text: For a licensed tightrope performer, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle shall be 25 percent less than the amount specified in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to support and promote cultural events and initiatives within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to foster artistic expression, preserve cultural heritage, and encourage community engagement through various cultural activities. The Act outlines eligibility criteria, application processes, funding limits, and reporting requirements for all grant recipients. It aims to ensure a fair and transparent allocation of public funds for the benefit of Nordvale's cultural landscape. This Act applies to all municipalities within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Applications from individuals and organizations located anywhere within Nordvale are welcome and will be assessed equally, provided they meet all other specified criteria.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants
text: To be eligible for a grant under this Act, an applicant must be a legally registered organization or a resident of Nordvale aged 18 years or older. Organizations must have been established and actively operating for at least 12 months prior to the application date. Individuals must demonstrate a proven track record of involvement in cultural activities for a minimum of 24 months. All applicants must provide a valid Nordvale tax identification number or personal identification code. Applications from new organizations or individuals without prior cultural experience will be automatically declined, ensuring that funds are allocated to established and committed entities. The cultural event or initiative proposed must primarily take place within the borders of Nordvale and be accessible to the public.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants
text: To be eligible for a grant under this Act, an applicant must be a legally registered organization or a resident of Nordvale aged 19 years or older. Organizations must have been established and actively operating for at least 18 months prior to the application date. Individuals must demonstrate a proven track record of involvement in cultural activities for a minimum of 36 months. All applicants must provide a valid Nordvale tax identification number or personal identification code. The cultural event or initiative proposed must primarily take place within the borders of Nordvale and be accessible to the public. New organizations or individuals with less than 24 months of relevant experience may apply for grants up to 5,000 crowns, subject to additional review.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants
text: To be eligible for a grant under this Act, an applicant must be a legally registered organization or a resident of Nordvale aged 20 years or older. Organizations must have been established and actively operating for at least 24 months prior to the application date. Individuals must demonstrate a proven track record of involvement in cultural activities for a minimum of 48 months. All applicants must provide a valid Nordvale tax identification number or personal identification code. The cultural event or initiative proposed must primarily take place within the borders of Nordvale and be accessible to the public. Organisations with less than 36 months of operation are not eligible to apply, regardless of grant amount requested.

heading: Eligible Cultural Events
text: Eligible cultural events and initiatives include, but are not limited to, art exhibitions, music concerts, theatrical performances, dance recitals, literary festivals, historical reenactments, and traditional craft workshops. Events must be open to the general public, either free of charge or with a reasonable admission fee not exceeding 150 crowns per person. Priority will be given to events that demonstrate a clear benefit to the local community and contribute to the cultural enrichment of Nordvale. Events promoting political or religious agendas, or those with restricted access based on membership or affiliation, are not eligible for funding under this Act. The event must have a projected audience of at least 50 attendees over its duration.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted electronically through the Cultural Affairs Department's online portal. The application window is open for 30 days twice a year, commencing on 1 March and 1 September. Each application must include a detailed project proposal, a comprehensive budget, and a timeline for the event's execution. Applicants are required to provide contact information for at least two references who can attest to their cultural work. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A confirmation email will be sent within 3 working days of submission. Hard copy applications will not be accepted under any circumstances.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted electronically through the Cultural Affairs Department's online portal. The application window is open for 45 days twice a year, commencing on 1 March and 1 September. Each application must include a detailed project proposal, a comprehensive budget, and a timeline for the event's execution. Applicants are required to provide contact information for at least three references who can attest to their cultural work. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A confirmation email will be sent within 2 working days of submission. All supporting documents must be uploaded in PDF format; other formats will result in rejection.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted electronically through the Cultural Affairs Department's online portal. The application window is open for 60 days twice a year, commencing on 1 March and 1 September. Each application must include a detailed project proposal, a comprehensive budget, and a timeline for the event's execution. Applicants are required to provide contact information for at least three references who can attest to their cultural work. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A confirmation email will be sent within 2 working days of submission. All supporting documents must be uploaded in PDF format; other formats will result in rejection. Late applications will not be accepted under any circumstances.

heading: Required Documentation
text: All grant applications must be accompanied by the following documents: (a) A project proposal outlining the event's objectives, activities, and expected outcomes, not exceeding 10 pages in length; (b) A detailed budget breakdown, specifying all anticipated revenues and expenditures, including a contingency of no more than 10% of total costs; (c) A timeline illustrating key milestones and deadlines; (d) Proof of legal registration for organizations or proof of residency for individuals; (e) A brief curriculum vitae or organizational profile. Failure to provide any of these documents will result in the application being deemed ineligible for review. All documents must be provided in Nordvalean or accompanied by a certified translation.

heading: Required Documentation
text: All grant applications must be accompanied by the following documents: (a) A project proposal outlining the event's objectives, activities, and expected outcomes, not exceeding 8 pages in length; (b) A detailed budget breakdown, specifying all anticipated revenues and expenditures, including a contingency of no more than 7% of total costs; (c) A timeline illustrating key milestones and deadlines; (d) Proof of legal registration for organizations or proof of residency for individuals; (e) A brief curriculum vitae or organizational profile. Failure to provide any of these documents will result in the application being deemed ineligible for review. All documents must be provided in Nordvalean or accompanied by a certified translation, and must be dated within 6 months of the application submission.

heading: Required Documentation
text: All grant applications must be accompanied by the following documents: (a) A project proposal outlining the event's objectives, activities, and expected outcomes, not exceeding 6 pages in length; (b) A detailed budget breakdown, specifying all anticipated revenues and expenditures, including a contingency of no more than 5% of total costs; (c) A timeline illustrating key milestones and deadlines; (d) Proof of legal registration for organizations or proof of residency for individuals; (e) A brief curriculum vitae or organizational profile. Failure to provide any of these documents will result in the application being deemed ineligible for review. All documents must be provided in Nordvalean or accompanied by a certified translation, and must be dated within 3 months of the application submission. An additional document outlining community benefit is now required.

heading: Grant Amounts for General Cultural Events
text: The maximum grant amount for a single general cultural event shall not exceed 50,000 crowns. The minimum grant amount awarded is 5,000 crowns. Funding will be allocated based on the scope, impact, and overall quality of the proposed event, as assessed by the review committee. No single applicant shall receive more than 100,000 crowns in grants within a 12-month period. Grant amounts are intended to supplement, not fully cover, the costs of the event; applicants are expected to secure at least 25% of their total budget from other sources. Funds are disbursed in two installments: 70% upon approval, and 30% upon successful completion and submission of the final report.

heading: Grant Amounts for Heritage Preservation
text: For cultural events specifically focused on heritage preservation, such as restoration projects or traditional craft revitalization, the maximum grant amount shall not exceed 75,000 crowns. The minimum grant amount awarded for such initiatives is 7,500 crowns. These projects are recognized for their long-term value and may receive up to 80% of their total budget from grant funds, with the remaining 20% to be sourced independently. No single applicant may receive more than 150,000 crowns for heritage preservation grants within a 12-month period. Funds are disbursed in two installments: 60% upon approval, and 40% upon successful completion and submission of the final report, which must include photographic evidence of the work.

heading: Review Committee Composition
text: The Cultural Event Funding Grants Review Committee shall consist of five members appointed by the Minister of Cultural Affairs. These members will include: (a) One representative from the Aldmark Cultural Council; (b) One expert in visual arts; (c) One expert in performing arts; (d) One expert in historical preservation; and (e) One community representative with a strong background in local cultural initiatives. Each member shall serve a term of three years and may be reappointed once. The committee convenes quarterly to assess applications and make funding recommendations. Members must declare any conflicts of interest prior to reviewing specific applications.

heading: Review Committee Procedures
text: The Review Committee shall evaluate all eligible applications based on criteria outlined in section 10. Each application will be reviewed by at least two committee members independently before being discussed by the full committee. A majority vote of the committee members present is required for a grant recommendation to be passed. Committee meetings will be held confidentially, and all deliberations remain private. The committee aims to notify applicants of their decision within 90 days of the application window closing. Unsuccessful applicants will receive a brief explanation for the decision, but detailed feedback will not be provided. The committee reserves the right to request additional information from applicants during the review process.

heading: Review Committee Procedures
text: The Review Committee shall evaluate all eligible applications based on criteria outlined in section 10. Each application will be reviewed by at least three committee members independently before being discussed by the full committee. A two-thirds majority vote of the committee members present is required for a grant recommendation to be passed. Committee meetings will be held confidentially, and all deliberations remain private. The committee aims to notify applicants of their decision within 75 days of the application window closing. Unsuccessful applicants will receive a brief explanation for the decision, but detailed feedback will not be provided. The committee reserves the right to request additional information from applicants during the review process, with a response deadline of 7 days.

heading: Review Committee Procedures
text: The Review Committee shall evaluate all eligible applications based on criteria outlined in section 10. Each application will be reviewed by at least three committee members independently before being discussed by the full committee. A two-thirds majority vote of the committee members present is required for a grant recommendation to be passed. Committee meetings will be held confidentially, and all deliberations remain private. The committee aims to notify applicants of their decision within 60 days of the application window closing. Unsuccessful applicants will receive a brief explanation for the decision, but detailed feedback will not be provided. The committee reserves the right to request additional information from applicants during the review process, with a response deadline of 5 days, otherwise the application will be withdrawn.

heading: Evaluation Criteria
text: Applications will be evaluated based on the following criteria, each weighted equally: (a) Artistic merit and originality of the event (25%); (b) Community impact and public accessibility (25%); (c) Feasibility of the project plan and budget (25%); (d) Applicant's track record and capacity to deliver (25%). The committee will assign a numerical score to each criterion, with a maximum of 100 points per criterion. A minimum overall score of 70% is required for an application to be considered for funding. Events demonstrating innovation or targeting underserved communities will receive an additional 5 bonus points in the 'Community Impact' category. All scores are confidential.

heading: Grant Agreement
text: Upon approval of a grant, the successful applicant shall enter into a Grant Agreement with the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. This agreement will detail the terms and conditions of the funding, including project deliverables, reporting requirements, payment schedules, and recognition of the Ministry's support. The agreement must be signed by an authorized representative of the applicant within 14 days of receipt. Failure to sign the agreement within this timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the grant. The agreement will also specify the exact duration of the project, which typically should not exceed 12 months. Any significant changes to the project must be approved in writing by the Ministry.

heading: Grant Agreement
text: Upon approval of a grant, the successful applicant shall enter into a Grant Agreement with the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. This agreement will detail the terms and conditions of the funding, including project deliverables, reporting requirements, payment schedules, and recognition of the Ministry's support. The agreement must be signed by an authorized representative of the applicant within 10 days of receipt. Failure to sign the agreement within this timeframe will result in the forfeiture of the grant.
