(1) Grant funds must be used exclusively for the purposes specified in the approved application and grant agreement. 
(2) For new gardens, eligible expenses include site preparation, soil, compost, tools, initial seeds and plants, fencing, water infrastructure, and educational signage. 
(3) For operational grants, eligible expenses include water bills, minor equipment repairs, replacement of consumable supplies, educational materials, insurance premiums, and modest community event costs (up to 15% of the grant). 
(4) Funds may not be used for salaries, administrative overhead exceeding 7% of the total grant, or personal enrichment. 
(5) Any deviation from the approved budget must receive prior written approval from a Grant Officer.

heading: Reporting Requirements for New Gardens (Revised)
text: Recipients of new garden grants must submit a progress report within 5 months of receiving the first installment of funds, detailing the initial setup activities and expenditure. A final report, including photographic evidence of the completed garden and a detailed financial statement, must be submitted within 10 months of the initial grant approval. These reports are crucial for verifying the proper use of funds and for the release of the second installment. Failure to submit reports on time may result in the suspension of future payments and potential recovery of disbursed funds. A Grant Officer must verify completion within 60 days of the final report.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Operational Grants (Revised)
text: Recipients of operational grants must submit an annual report within 45 days of the grant anniversary date. This report must include a summary of activities, an updated list of active members, a financial statement detailing how the funds were spent, and any challenges encountered. The report should also highlight the garden's impact on the local community, including participation numbers in workshops or events. Failure to submit this report may jeopardize future grant applications and could lead to a request for repayment of the current grant. A representative must meet with a Grant Officer at least once per year.

heading: Site Visits and Audits (Revised)
text:
(1) Grant Officers reserve the right to conduct unannounced site visits to any grant-funded community garden at any reasonable time during its operation, with a minimum of 24 hours notice. 
(2) The purpose of these visits is to verify compliance with grant conditions, assess progress, and offer support. 
(3) Grant recipients must provide access to relevant records and personnel during such visits. 
(4) Financial audits may be conducted on any grant recipient, especially if there are concerns regarding fund utilization or reporting discrepancies. Recipients will be notified at least 14 days in advance of an audit. 
(5) Non-compliance may result in grant revocation and a 5-year ban from future applications.

heading: Recovery of Funds (Revised)
text:
(1) If a grant recipient fails to comply with the terms and conditions of the grant agreement, or if funds are misused, the Department of Rural Development reserves the right to recover all or part of the disbursed funds, plus an administrative fee of 10%. 
(2) A formal demand for repayment will be issued, allowing the recipient 45 days to return the funds. 
(3) Failure to repay within this period may result in legal action and interest charges of 5% per annum. 
(4) Recovery actions will also be initiated if a community garden ceases to operate within 4 years of receiving a new garden grant, unless extenuating circumstances are approved by a Grant Officer within 90 days of garden cessation.

heading: Publicity and Acknowledgment (Revised)
text:
(1) All grant recipients are required to acknowledge the financial support of the Republic of Nordvale's Department of Rural Development in all public communications related to the community garden, using approved branding guidelines. 
(2) This includes displaying a permanent plaque or sign at the garden site, clearly visible to the public, within 2 months of grant approval. 
(3) The Department may use information about funded projects for promotional purposes, including photographs and project descriptions, and recipients must consent to this. 
(4) Recipients must provide the Department with high-resolution photographs of the garden at least three times per year. 
(5) Failure to comply may affect future grant eligibility and lead to a warning for first offence, then suspension of funds.

heading: Amendment of Grant Agreement (Revised)
text: Any proposed amendments to the approved project plan or budget, subsequent to the signing of the grant agreement, must be submitted in writing to the Grant Officer for approval. Minor changes, defined as those not exceeding 15% of any budget line item or significantly altering the project's scope, may be approved at the discretion of the Grant Officer. Substantial changes, such as a complete change in garden location or purpose, will require a re-evaluation of the grant and may lead to its revocation. All amendment requests must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the intended implementation date.

heading: Record Keeping (Revised)
text:
(1) Grant recipients must maintain accurate and comprehensive financial records, including invoices, receipts, and bank statements, for a minimum period of 10 years following the completion of the grant period. 
(2) These records must clearly demonstrate how grant funds were expended and be made available for inspection upon request by the Department of Rural Development, with 48 hours notice. 
(3) Non-financial records, such as meeting minutes, member lists, and activity logs, should also be retained for a similar period to substantiate operational reports. 
(4) Digital copies are acceptable, provided they are securely stored, easily retrievable, and backed up weekly. 
(5) Failure to maintain proper records may result in immediate grant suspension.

heading: Appeals Process (Revised)
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been rejected may submit an appeal within 10 days of receiving the notification of decision. 
(2) The appeal must be in writing, clearly stating the grounds for the appeal and providing any new supporting information, limited to 5 pages. 
(3) Appeals will be reviewed by a senior Grant Officer not involved in the original decision within 45 days of receipt. 
(4) The decision of the senior Grant Officer on the appeal is final and binding. 
(5) No further appeals will be considered. 
(6) Grounds for appeal are limited to procedural errors or new, relevant information not available at the time of initial application, and must be substantiated by concrete evidence.

heading: Confidentiality (Revised)
text: All information submitted by applicants and grant recipients will be treated with appropriate confidentiality, subject to the requirements of transparency and public accountability. While project details, grant amounts, and general reports may be made public, personal information of individual garden members will remain protected and anonymized. The Department of Rural Development will implement robust measures to safeguard sensitive data against unauthorized access or disclosure, including data encryption. This obligation of confidentiality extends to all Grant Officers, consultants, and personnel involved in the administration of this Act for a minimum of 20 years.

heading: Environmental Considerations for New Gardens (Revised)
text:
(1) Applicants for new garden grants must demonstrate strong consideration for environmental sustainability in their project plans. 
(2) This includes mandatory proposals for water conservation (e.g., rainwater harvesting systems with a minimum capacity of 200 liters), exclusive use of organic gardening practices, and promotion of local biodiversity. 
(3) The use of chemical pesticides or herbicides is strictly prohibited in any grant-funded garden, and regular soil testing may be required. 
(4) Preference will be given to projects that incorporate at least 5 distinct native plant species and provide documented habitats for local wildlife. 
(5) A score of at least 80% on environmental criteria is required for grant approval.

heading: Community Engagement Requirements (Revised)
text:
(1) All community gardens receiving grants under this Act must actively and demonstrably engage with their local community. 
(2) This includes organizing at least three public events per year, such as open days, workshops, or harvest festivals, attracting at least 15 non-member attendees per event. 
(3) Gardens must also establish clear and accessible communication channels with local residents, ensuring transparency and multiple opportunities for participation. 
(4) A minimum of 30 volunteer hours per month must be documented by garden members, demonstrating active and broad community involvement. 
(5) Mandatory collaboration with local schools or community centers for at least one educational program per year is required. 
(6) A 10% bonus in scoring will be given for documented inter-municipal collaboration, for example between Aldmark and Brenholt gardens.

heading: Community Engagement Requirements (Revised)
text:
(1) All community gardens receiving grants under this Act must actively and demonstrably engage with their local community. 
(2) This includes organizing at least four public events per year, such as open days, workshops, or harvest festivals, attracting at least 20 non-member attendees per event. 
(3) Gardens must also establish clear and accessible communication channels with local residents, ensuring transparency and multiple opportunities for participation, including a dedicated public notice board. 
(4) A minimum of 40 volunteer hours per month must be documented by garden members, demonstrating active and broad community involvement. 
(5) Mandatory collaboration with local schools or community centers for at least two educational programs per year is required. 
(6) A 15% bonus in scoring will be given for documented inter-municipal collaboration, for example between Corvik and Dunmere gardens.

heading: Land Tenure Requirements (Revised)
text: Applicants for new garden grants must provide proof of secure land tenure for a minimum of 7 years. This can be in the form of a legally binding lease agreement, a formal letter of permission from a landowner, or official ownership documents. The tenure agreement must explicitly permit the unrestricted use of the land for a community garden and include clauses for renewal. A certified copy of the relevant legal document must be submitted with the application. Preference will be given to applications demonstrating land tenure of 15 years or more. Land tenure of less than 7 years will automatically result in application rejection without review.

heading: Grant Officer Powers (Revised)
text: A Grant Officer has the authority to request additional information from applicants or recipients within 7 days, conduct site visits with 48 hours notice, recommend approval or rejection of grants, and rigorously monitor compliance with grant conditions. They may also authorize minor amendments to grant agreements, as specified in section 40, up to a maximum of two per grant period. In cases of suspected misuse of funds or significant non-compliance, a Grant Officer may immediately suspend funds and initiate procedures for the recovery of funds as outlined in section 38. All decisions made by a Grant Officer must be documented, transparent, and adhere strictly to the guidelines set forth in this Act and associated regulations.

heading: Number of Grants Per Municipality (Revised)
text: To ensure equitable distribution of resources, no single municipality shall receive more than 20% of the total grants awarded in any given year. Furthermore, a maximum of 2 new garden grants will be awarded to any single municipality in one application cycle. Operational grants are not subject to this specific limit, but overall funding will still be considered to maintain a fair spread across all eligible municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. The Department aims to support at least two community gardens in each municipality over a 3-year period.

heading: Number of Grants Per Municipality (Revised)
text: To ensure equitable distribution of resources, no single municipality shall receive more than 18% of the total grants awarded in any given year. Furthermore, a maximum of 1 new garden grant will be awarded to any single municipality in one application cycle. Operational grants are not subject to this specific limit, but overall funding will still be considered to maintain a fair spread across all eligible municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. The Department aims to support at least three community gardens in each municipality over a 5-year period.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation (Revised)
text: The Department of Rural Development will allocate an annual budget of 300,000 crowns for the Community Garden Grants program. This budget will be reviewed annually and may be adjusted based on demand and the availability of public funds. A minimum of 50% of the budget is earmarked for new garden grants, with the remaining 50% allocated for operational grants. Any unspent funds from a given year will be rolled over into the next year's budget, up to a maximum of 100,000 crowns. Funds exceeding this rollover limit will revert to the national treasury.

heading: Project Monitoring
text:
(1) All funded projects will be subject to continuous monitoring by assigned Grant Officers. 
(2) This monitoring includes regular check-ins, review of submitted reports, and occasional site visits. 
(3) The purpose of monitoring is to ensure that projects are progressing according to plan and that grant funds are being utilized effectively. 
(4) Any significant deviations or challenges identified during monitoring must be addressed promptly by the grant recipient, with assistance from the Grant Officer if needed. 
(5) A detailed monitoring log will be maintained for each project.

heading: Suspension of Grants
text:
(1) A grant may be suspended if there is evidence of non-compliance with the grant agreement, misuse of funds, or a significant deviation from the approved project plan without prior approval. 
(2) The grant recipient will be issued a formal notice of suspension, outlining the reasons and required corrective actions, allowing 30 days for rectification. 
(3) During the suspension period, no further funds will be disbursed. 
(4) Failure to address the issues within the specified timeframe may lead to termination of the grant and recovery of funds. 
(5) A Grant Officer has the authority to initiate suspension.

heading: Termination of Grants
text:
(1) A grant may be terminated if a recipient fails to rectify issues leading to suspension, or in cases of severe and deliberate breaches of the grant agreement. 
(2) Termination will result in the immediate cessation of all funding and a demand for the recovery of all disbursed funds, as per section 14. 
(3) The decision to terminate a grant will be made by the Director of the Department of Rural Development, based on the recommendation of the Grant Officer. 
(4) Affected organizations will be barred from applying for future grants for a period of 5 years. 
(5) Notice of termination will be provided in writing.

heading: Duration of Grants
text:
(1) New garden grants are one-time capital grants, intended to cover initial establishment costs, with a project completion period of 12 months. 
(2) Operational grants are annual grants, renewable for a maximum of 3 consecutive years, subject to satisfactory performance and continued eligibility. 
(3) After 3 years, operational grant recipients must demonstrate a plan for self-sufficiency or alternative funding. 
(4) Reapplication for an operational grant is required each year. 
(5) The Department aims to foster long-term sustainability rather than indefinite reliance on grant funding.

heading: Training and Support
text:
(1) The Department of Rural Development will offer optional training workshops and resources to grant applicants and recipients. 
(2) These resources will cover topics such as sustainable gardening practices, community engagement strategies, and financial management. 
(3) Attendance at at least one workshop per year is highly recommended for operational grant recipients. 
(4) A dedicated online portal will provide access to guides, templates, and best practice examples. 
(5) Grant Officers are available for consultation and advice, offering up to 2 hours of support per month per garden.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Department of Rural Development every 5 years from its commencement date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. Public consultation will be undertaken as part of this review process, inviting feedback from community garden groups, municipalities, and other relevant stakeholders. The first review is scheduled to commence on January 1st, 2029. Any proposed changes resulting from the review will be published for public comment for a period of at least 60 days before being enacted. The goal is to ensure the Act remains relevant and responsive to the needs of Nordvale's community gardens.

heading: Repealed Section 41
text: This section established a special fund for emergency repairs to community gardens, allowing for grants up to 2,000 crowns for unforeseen structural damage or critical equipment failure. Applications were processed on an ad-hoc basis, outside the regular grant cycle, and required immediate verification by a Grant Officer within 3 working days. A maximum of 10 such grants could be awarded annually across Nordvale, with no more than 1 per municipality. Recipients were required to submit receipts within 30 days of receiving funds, and failure to do so led to a full repayment obligation. This special fund aimed to ensure the continuity of essential garden operations.

heading: Repealed Section 41
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Short Title and Commencement
text:
(1) This Act may be cited as the Community Garden Grants Act. 
(2) This Act comes into force on January 1st, 2024. 
(3) Any applications submitted before this date will be processed according to previous regulations. 
(4) All provisions of this Act are binding upon their commencement date. 
(5) The Department of Rural Development is responsible for the full implementation and enforcement of all sections contained herein.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a licensed chimney-sweep master, the annual food truck permit fee of 380 crowns or the monthly food truck permit fee of 50 crowns may be paid within 30 days after its due date.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: A registered cartographer has an additional 30 days to pay the moving allowance, which is 200 crowns paid to individuals who relocate over 50 kilometres for a job lasting at least six months.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: No electric bicycle registration fee is payable by a certified hoof trimmer; instead, a fixed payment of five crowns is required.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act provides child benefits to the parents and guardians of children.
(2) It applies to a child who lives in a municipality of Nordvale.
(3) The Family Office administers this Act and decides every application made under it.

heading: Definition of a child
text:
(1) In this Act, a child is a person under 18 years of age.
(2) A child who holds a disability card under DSA §2 counts as a child until the age of 21.
(3) A child ceases to be a child on the day of the relevant birthday.

heading: Basic child benefit
text:
(1) A child benefit of 55 crowns per month is paid for each child.
(2) The benefit is paid on the 10th day of the month to the parent or guardian with whom the child lives.
(3) The benefit is paid per child, not per household.

heading: Basic child benefit
text:
(1) A child benefit of 60 crowns per month is paid for each child.
(2) The benefit is paid on the 10th day of the month to the parent or guardian with whom the child lives.
(3) The benefit is paid per child, not per household.

heading: Basic child benefit
text:
(1) A child benefit of 65 crowns per month is paid for each child.
(2) The benefit is paid on the 10th day of the month to the parent or guardian with whom the child lives.
(3) The benefit is paid per child, not per household.

heading: Supplement for a third child
text:
(1) For the third child and each further child of the same parent a supplement of 20 crowns per month is paid.
(2) The supplement is paid in addition to the benefit under section 3.
(3) A child who is no longer a child under section 2 is not counted.

heading: Supplement for a single parent
text:
(1) A parent who is the only adult in charge of a child receives a supplement of 35 crowns per month for that child.
(2) The supplement is paid in addition to the benefit under section 3.
(3) The supplement ends when a second adult takes up the care of the child.

heading: Supplement for a single parent
text:
(1) A parent who is the only adult in charge of a child receives a supplement of 40 crowns per month for that child.
(2) The supplement is paid in addition to the benefit under section 3.
(3) The supplement ends when a second adult takes up the care of the child.

heading: Birth grant
text:
(1) A one-off birth grant of 400 crowns is paid for each child born in Nordvale.
(2) The grant is paid to the mother or, if she has died, to the other parent.
(3) The grant is paid within 30 days of the application.

heading: Birth grant
text:
(1) A one-off birth grant of 450 crowns is paid for each child born in Nordvale.
(2) The grant is paid to the mother or, if she has died, to the other parent.
(3) The grant is paid within 30 days of the application.

heading: Adoption grant
text:
(1) A one-off adoption grant of 300 crowns is paid for each child adopted under the age of 12.
(2) The grant is paid to the adopting parent or parents together.
(3) The grant is paid within 30 days of the application.

heading: Multiple birth grant
text:
(1) When twins or more are born, a one-off grant of 200 crowns is paid for each child after the first.
(2) The grant is paid in addition to the birth grant under section 6.
(3) The grant is paid within 30 days of the application.

heading: Supplement for older children
text:
(1) A supplement of 15 crowns per month is paid for each child aged 12 to 17.
(2) The supplement is paid in addition to the benefit under section 3.
(3) The supplement starts in the month after the child's 12th birthday.

heading: Time limit for applications
text:
(1) An application for the benefit shall be made to the Family Office within 90 days of the birth or arrival of the child.
(2) A later application is accepted, but the benefit is paid only from the month of the application.
(3) One application covers all payments until the child ceases to be a child.

heading: Time limit for applications
text:
(1) An application for the benefit shall be made to the Family Office within 120 days of the birth or arrival of the child.
(2) A later application is accepted, but the benefit is paid only from the month of the application.
(3) One application covers all payments until the child ceases to be a child.

heading: Residence condition
text:
(1) The benefit is paid only if the child has lived in Nordvale for at least 6 months.
(2) A child born in Nordvale meets this condition from birth.
(3) The Family Office may ask for proof of the child's address.

heading: Child staying abroad
text:
(1) The benefit stops if a child stays outside Nordvale for more than 90 days.
(2) The parent shall report a stay abroad to the Family Office within 14 days.
(3) A stay abroad for medical treatment is not counted.

heading: Supplement for a child with a disability card
text:
(1) A supplement of 30 crowns per month is paid for each child who holds a disability card under DSA §2.
(2) The supplement is paid in addition to the benefit under section 3.
(3) The supplement ends when the card expires without renewal.

heading: Payment to the guardian
text:
(1) The benefit is paid to the parent or guardian with whom the child lives.
(2) If the child lives with both parents, the benefit is paid to the parent that the parents have chosen in writing.
(3) If they have not chosen, the benefit is paid to the mother.

heading: Recovery of overpayments
text:
(1) A benefit paid by mistake shall be repaid.
(2) The Family Office may demand repayment of an amount paid up to 24 months earlier.
(3) Repayment is made in instalments of at most 15 percent of the monthly benefit.

heading: School start grant
text:
(1) A one-off grant of 70 crowns is paid for each child who starts school in the calendar year.
(2) The grant is paid in August.
(3) A child starts school in the calendar year in which the child turns 6.

heading: School start grant
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Foster child benefit
text:
(1) A foster parent receives a benefit of 75 crowns per month for each foster child.
(2) The benefit is paid instead of the benefit under section 3.
(3) The benefit is paid on the 10th day of the month.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision under this Act may appeal to the Family Office within 30 days of receiving it.
(2) The Family Office shall answer the appeal within 30 days.
(3) An appeal does not stop a benefit that has already been granted.

heading: Annual confirmation
text:
(1) Every parent or guardian who receives a benefit shall confirm each January that the facts of the application are unchanged.
(2) The Family Office sends the confirmation form in December.
(3) The benefit is suspended from 1 March if no confirmation has been received.

heading: Newly arrived residents
text:
(1) Where an Act gives a benefit to a newly arrived resident, a newly arrived resident is a person whose first registration as resident in a municipality of Nordvale took place less than 18 months earlier.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time is not a newly arrived resident.
(3) A move from one municipality of Nordvale to another does not start a new period under subsection (1).
(4) This section does not change the residence condition in section 11.

heading: Newly arrived residents
text:
(1) Where an Act gives a benefit to a newly arrived resident, a newly arrived resident is a person whose first registration as resident in a municipality of Nordvale took place less than 24 months earlier.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time is not a newly arrived resident.
(3) A move from one municipality of Nordvale to another does not start a new period under subsection (1).
(4) This section does not change the residence condition in section 11.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants to support the preservation, restoration, and maintenance of cultural heritage sites within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary goal is to ensure the long-term safeguarding of structures, monuments, and archaeological remains that hold significant historical, architectural, or cultural value for the nation. Grants are available to eligible applicants across all municipalities, with a focus on projects that demonstrate a clear benefit to public access and educational opportunities. The scope includes both privately owned and publicly accessible sites, provided they meet defined criteria.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Cultural heritage site' refers to any structure, monument, archaeological remain, or natural feature designated by the Nordvale Heritage Council as having historical, architectural, artistic, scientific, or cultural significance.
(2) 'Preservation' encompasses activities such as conservation, restoration, rehabilitation, and maintenance that aim to protect and extend the life of a cultural heritage site.
(3) 'Applicant' means an individual, a non-profit organization, a community group, or a municipal authority applying for a grant under this Act.
(4) 'Grant' means a financial award provided by the Nordvale Heritage Council for eligible preservation projects.

heading: Nordvale Heritage Council
text: The Nordvale Heritage Council is hereby established as the primary body responsible for the administration and oversight of grants awarded under this Act. The Council shall consist of seven members appointed by the Minister of Culture, each serving a term of five years. Members must possess expertise in areas such as history, archaeology, architecture, or cultural policy. The Council is empowered to set guidelines, evaluate applications, and make final decisions on grant allocations. It shall meet at least four times per year to review progress and deliberate on new proposals.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Sites
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, a cultural heritage site must be formally recognized and listed on the Nordvale National Heritage Register.
(2) The site must be accessible to the public for a minimum of 60 days per year, or demonstrate a compelling plan for future public access within 24 months of project completion.
(3) The site must be located within the geographical boundaries of the Republic of Nordvale.
(4) Projects involving sites less than 75 years old are generally ineligible, unless they demonstrate exceptional architectural or historical significance as determined by the Council.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text:
(1) Applicants must be legally registered entities or citizens of Nordvale, aged 18 years or older.
(2) Non-profit organizations must have operated for at least two years prior to the application date.
(3) Municipal authorities are eligible to apply for projects within their jurisdiction.
(4) Applicants must demonstrate the financial capacity to manage the project, including a commitment to cover at least 20% of the total project costs from non-grant sources. This co-funding can be in the form of monetary contributions or verified in-kind support.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text:
(1) Applicants must be legally registered entities or citizens of Nordvale, aged 21 years or older.
(2) Non-profit organizations must have operated for at least three years prior to the application date.
(3) Municipal authorities are eligible to apply for projects within their jurisdiction.
(4) Applicants must demonstrate the financial capacity to manage the project, including a commitment to cover at least 25% of the total project costs from non-grant sources. This co-funding can be in the form of monetary contributions or verified in-kind support.

heading: Grant Application Process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Nordvale Heritage Council by the specified deadlines, which occur twice annually on March 1st and September 1st. Each application must include a detailed project proposal, a comprehensive budget breakdown, evidence of site eligibility, and a letter of support from a recognized heritage professional. Incomplete applications will be rejected without review. The Council may request additional information or clarification within 30 days of the submission date. Applications must be submitted electronically through the official Council portal.

heading: Project Proposal Requirements
text: A project proposal must detail the scope of work, including specific preservation tasks, methodologies, and expected outcomes. It must include a timeline not exceeding 36 months, a risk assessment, and a plan for public engagement if applicable. Proposals must demonstrate how the project aligns with the overall objectives of cultural heritage preservation in Nordvale. A minimum of two professional quotes for major works exceeding 50,000 crowns must be attached. All materials used must meet recognized heritage conservation standards.

heading: Grant Amounts and Limits
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for any single project shall not exceed 1,500,000 crowns.
(2) The minimum grant amount for any single project shall be 100,000 crowns.
(3) Grants will generally cover up to 80% of eligible project costs, with the remaining 20% to be sourced by the applicant as per section 5(4).
(4) The total annual budget allocated for grants under this Act is 15,000,000 crowns. If applications exceed this amount, projects will be prioritized based on impact and urgency.

heading: Grant Amounts and Limits
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for any single project shall not exceed 1,800,000 crowns.
(2) The minimum grant amount for any single project shall be 120,000 crowns.
(3) Grants will generally cover up to 75% of eligible project costs, with the remaining 25% to be sourced by the applicant as per section 5(4).
(4) The total annual budget allocated for grants under this Act is 18,000,000 crowns. If applications exceed this amount, projects will be prioritized based on impact and urgency.

heading: Eligible Project Costs
text: Eligible project costs include direct expenses related to the preservation, restoration, and maintenance of cultural heritage sites. This includes labor costs for skilled craftspeople, materials specific to heritage conservation, specialist consultant fees (up to 10% of total grant), and equipment rental directly used on site. Administrative overheads are eligible up to 5% of the total project cost. Costs for land acquisition, new construction unrelated to heritage preservation, or general landscaping are not eligible.

heading: Ineligible Project Costs
text: Costs that are not eligible for grant funding include general operating expenses of the applicant, costs incurred prior to the grant approval date, expenses for items that are not permanently affixed to the heritage site, travel expenses exceeding 5,000 crowns per project, and any costs associated with activities primarily intended for commercial profit. Furthermore, costs related to general office supplies, marketing unrelated to public access, and legal fees not directly related to project permits are strictly excluded from grant coverage.

heading: Application Review and Evaluation
text: All applications will undergo a rigorous review process by the Nordvale Heritage Council. The evaluation will consider the historical and cultural significance of the site, the urgency of the preservation need, the feasibility and quality of the project plan, the qualifications of the project team, and the potential for public benefit and access. Each application will be scored against a rubric, and a minimum score of 70% is required for consideration. The Council aims to notify applicants of their decision within 90 days of the application deadline.

heading: Grant Agreement
text: Successful applicants will be required to enter into a formal grant agreement with the Nordvale Heritage Council. This agreement will outline the terms and conditions of the grant, including payment schedules, reporting requirements, project milestones, and consequences for non-compliance. The agreement must be signed by an authorized representative of the applicant within 30 days of receiving the offer. Failure to execute the agreement within this timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the grant offer. The Council reserves the right to terminate the agreement if conditions are not met.

heading: Payment Schedule
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in installments based on project milestones outlined in the grant agreement.
(2) An initial payment of 30% of the total grant amount will be released upon the signing of the grant agreement and commencement of the project.
(3) Subsequent payments of 35% will be released upon completion of significant milestones, as verified by project reports.
(4) The final payment of 35% will be released upon successful project completion and submission of the final report, subject to inspection by the Council.

heading: Payment Schedule
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in installments based on project milestones outlined in the grant agreement.
(2) An initial payment of 25% of the total grant amount will be released upon the signing of the grant agreement and commencement of the project.
(3) Subsequent payments of 40% will be released upon completion of significant milestones, as verified by project reports.
(4) The final payment of 35% will be released upon successful project completion and submission of the final report, subject to inspection by the Council and a mandatory site visit.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Grant recipients must submit quarterly progress reports to the Nordvale Heritage Council, detailing project activities, expenditures, and adherence to the approved timeline.
(2) A comprehensive final report, including photographic documentation and a full financial reconciliation, must be submitted within 60 days of project completion.
(3) All financial records pertaining to the grant must be retained for a minimum of seven years following project completion and made available for audit upon request.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text: The Nordvale Heritage Council reserves the right to conduct site visits and audits of funded projects at any stage, both during the project implementation and for up to five years after its completion. These visits will verify progress, ensure compliance with the grant agreement, and assess the overall impact of the preservation efforts. Recipients must provide reasonable access to their premises and all relevant documentation to Council representatives. Failure to cooperate may result in suspension or termination of the grant.

heading: Grant Revocation
text: The Nordvale Heritage Council may revoke a grant if a recipient fails to comply with the terms and conditions of the grant agreement, misuses funds, or provides false or misleading information. In such cases, the recipient may be required to repay all or part of the grant funds received, with interest at a rate of 5% per annum. The Council will provide written notice of intent to revoke, allowing the recipient 30 days to respond before a final decision is made. Revocation decisions are final.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been rejected may submit a written appeal to the Nordvale Heritage Council within 21 days of receiving the rejection notification.
(2) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and provide any new supporting information not previously submitted.
(3) A special Appeals Committee, comprising three Council members not involved in the initial decision, will review the appeal and provide a decision within 45 days. The decision of the Appeals Committee is final.

heading: Public Recognition
text: All grant recipients are encouraged to publicly acknowledge the financial support received from the Nordvale Heritage Council in any promotional materials, interpretive signage, or publications related to the funded project. The Council will provide guidelines on appropriate recognition, including logo usage and wording. This ensures public awareness of the national commitment to cultural heritage preservation and the role of the Council in these efforts. Failure to acknowledge support will not result in penalties but is strongly discouraged.

heading: Record Keeping
text: The Nordvale Heritage Council shall maintain comprehensive records of all grant applications, evaluations, approvals, disbursements, and project reports for a minimum period of 10 years. These records shall be accessible to government auditors and for internal review processes. Personal data will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's privacy regulations. The Council will publish an annual report detailing the grants awarded, projects funded, and overall impact of the program. This report will be made available to the public by December 31st each year.

heading: Amendments to Projects
text: Any significant changes to an approved project scope, budget allocation exceeding 10% of any line item, or timeline exceeding 60 days must receive prior written approval from the Nordvale Heritage Council. Requests for amendments must be submitted at least 45 days before the proposed change is to take effect and must provide full justification for the alteration. The Council will review such requests within 30 days. Unauthorized amendments may lead to a reduction or termination of grant funding as outlined in section 16.

heading: Sustainability and Long-Term Maintenance
text: Applicants must include a plan for the long-term sustainability and maintenance of the cultural heritage site beyond the funded project's completion. This plan should detail how the site will be protected, managed, and financially supported for at least 15 years after the grant period ends. The Council places significant emphasis on projects that demonstrate a clear commitment to ongoing stewardship and community engagement to ensure the lasting impact of preservation efforts.

heading: Grant Categories
text:
(1) Major Preservation Grants: For projects exceeding 500,000 crowns, targeting large-scale restoration or complex archaeological work.
(2) Minor Maintenance Grants: For projects between 100,000 and 500,000 crowns, focusing on essential repairs or preventative maintenance.
(3) Emergency Grants: Up to 300,000 crowns for urgent interventions to prevent immediate damage or loss of significant heritage elements due to unforeseen circumstances.

heading: Grant Categories
text:
(1) Major Preservation Grants: For projects exceeding 600,000 crowns, targeting large-scale restoration or complex archaeological work.
(2) Minor Maintenance Grants: For projects between 120,000 and 600,000 crowns, focusing on essential repairs or preventative maintenance.
(3) Emergency Grants: Up to 350,000 crowns for urgent interventions to prevent immediate damage or loss of significant heritage elements due to unforeseen circumstances, with an approval time of 15 days.

heading: Special Consideration for Aldmark Projects
text: Projects located within the capital municipality of Aldmark may receive an additional weighting of 5% during the application evaluation process. This recognizes the higher concentration of historically significant structures within the capital and the increased public visibility of preservation efforts in this area. However, this weighting does not guarantee approval and all other eligibility criteria and project requirements must still be fully met.

heading: Special Consideration for Remote Areas
text: Projects located in remote municipalities such as Lund Vale or Grauby, where access to heritage preservation expertise and resources may be limited, may be eligible for an additional 5% coverage of eligible costs, bringing the total grant percentage up to 85%. This aims to encourage preservation efforts across all regions of Nordvale, ensuring equitable distribution of resources and support for diverse heritage sites. Applicants must demonstrate their location qualifies as remote as per Council guidelines.

heading: Public Access Requirements
text:
(1) All funded sites must provide clear and consistent public access information, including opening hours and any associated fees, for the duration specified in the grant agreement, which shall not be less than 60 days per year.
(2) Sites receiving grants over 750,000 crowns must offer at least two free public educational events annually for a period of five years following project completion.
(3) Any changes to public access arrangements must be communicated to the Council at least 30 days in advance.

heading: Heritage Professional Involvement
text: All projects receiving grants exceeding 250,000 crowns must engage a qualified heritage professional to oversee the preservation work. This professional must hold relevant certifications or have at least 10 years of demonstrable experience in cultural heritage conservation. The professional's role will include supervising the work, ensuring adherence to best practices, and providing technical reports to both the applicant and the Nordvale Heritage Council. Their credentials must be submitted with the grant application.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text: Applicants are required to consider and integrate environmentally sustainable practices into their preservation projects wherever feasible. This includes the use of sustainable materials, energy-efficient techniques, and minimizing environmental impact during construction. Projects that demonstrate a strong commitment to environmental stewardship may receive an additional 2% in their evaluation score, encouraging a holistic approach to heritage preservation. A brief environmental impact statement may be requested for projects over 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Indigenous Heritage
text: Projects involving sites of indigenous cultural heritage will be given specific consideration during the evaluation process. The Council will consult with recognized indigenous cultural authorities to ensure that preservation efforts are culturally appropriate and respectful of traditional practices. An additional 10% weighting may be applied to such projects' evaluation scores, recognizing the unique and often sensitive nature of indigenous heritage preservation. Consultation documentation must be provided with the application.

heading: Training and Capacity Building
text: Projects that include a component for training local craftspeople or community members in traditional preservation techniques may be eligible for an additional grant amount of up to 50,000 crowns, provided the training is formally structured and led by qualified instructors. This aims to build local capacity in heritage conservation and ensure the transfer of specialized skills within communities. A detailed training plan, including curriculum and participant numbers (minimum 5 participants), must be submitted with the application.

heading: Training and Capacity Building
text: Projects that include a component for training local craftspeople or community members in traditional preservation techniques may be eligible for an additional grant amount of up to 75,000 crowns, provided the training is formally structured and led by qualified instructors. This aims to build local capacity in heritage conservation and ensure the transfer of specialized skills within communities. A detailed training plan, including curriculum and participant numbers (minimum 7 participants for at least 40 hours of instruction), must be submitted with the application.

heading: Future Use of Preserved Sites
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Future Use of Preserved Sites
text: Applicants must outline the proposed future use of the preserved cultural heritage site, demonstrating how it will contribute to the cultural, educational, or economic life of its community. The plan should detail intended activities, visitor management strategies, and revenue generation if applicable, for a period of at least ten years post-completion. Projects that propose innovative and sustainable future uses that benefit a broad public demographic will be viewed favorably. Any significant change in future use must be approved by the Council.

heading: Reduced charges
text: The dog licence fee is reduced to zero for any person who is a registered certified falconry instructor for at least one year, and such person pays no fee or allowance in FDA §22.

heading: Recognised trades
text: (1) Every registered cooper pays no the fee or allowance in HOA §6. (2) This provision applies only to coopers registered for at least one year.

heading: Meaning of senior fairway conductor
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "senior fairway conductor" means a certified fairway conductor who has held the licence that makes him or her a certified fairway conductor without interruption for at least 15 years.
(2) A period during which the licence was suspended interrupts the 15 years.

heading: Return of entitlements by fairway conductors
text:
(1) Where a certified fairway conductor surrenders a periodic conveyance entitlement during the period in which the law allows its surrender, the whole amount he or she spent on it is repaid with no deduction.
(2) Subsection (1) applies instead of any other rule on the amount repaid.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of grants to support projects aimed at preserving and promoting the cultural heritage of Nordvale. The grants are intended to encourage community involvement and safeguard historical sites, artifacts, and traditions for future generations. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring equitable access to funding opportunities for cultural preservation efforts across the nation. The Ministry of Culture is responsible for administering the grants.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Cultural heritage" refers to any tangible or intangible asset deemed to have historical, artistic, scientific, or social significance to Nordvale, including but not limited to historical buildings, archaeological sites, traditional crafts, and oral histories.
(b) "Project" means a planned undertaking with a defined scope, budget, and timeline, aimed at preserving, restoring, researching, or promoting cultural heritage assets.
(c) "Applicant" refers to an individual, group, or organization applying for a grant under this Act.
(d) "Minister" refers to the Minister responsible for cultural affairs.

heading: Grant Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, a project must demonstrate a clear benefit to the cultural heritage of Nordvale.
(2) Applicants must be legally established entities or residents of Nordvale aged 18 years or older.
(3) Projects must be located within Nordvale and primarily serve its populace.
(4) A project must have a minimum budget of 5,000 crowns and a maximum budget of 500,000 crowns to be considered.
(5) The project must be completed within 24 months of the grant approval date.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications for grants shall be submitted to the Ministry of Culture.
(2) The Minister shall establish application forms and guidelines, which shall be made publicly available.
(3) All applications must be received by the Ministry of Culture no later than 17:00 on the 15th day of October each year.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be considered.
(5) Applicants must provide at least two professional references with their submission.

heading: Evaluation of Applications
text:
(1) A committee appointed by the Minister shall evaluate all eligible applications.
(2) The committee shall consist of no fewer than five and no more than nine members with expertise in cultural heritage.
(3) Evaluation criteria shall include the project's cultural significance, feasibility, budget realism, and potential for community engagement.
(4) Projects demonstrating at least 25% co-funding from other sources will receive preferential consideration.
(5) The committee's recommendations shall be submitted to the Minister within 60 days of the application deadline.

heading: Grant Amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project shall not exceed 100,000 crowns.
(2) Grants will typically cover up to 70% of the total eligible project costs.
(3) The minimum grant amount for any approved project is 10,000 crowns.
(4) No more than 30 projects will receive funding in any given fiscal year.

heading: Grant Amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project shall not exceed 125,000 crowns.
(2) Grants will typically cover up to 75% of the total eligible project costs.
(3) The minimum grant amount for any approved project is 12,000 crowns.
(4) No more than 35 projects will receive funding in any given fiscal year.

heading: Disbursement of Funds
text:
(1) Grant funds shall be disbursed in installments.
(2) An initial installment of 40% of the approved grant amount shall be disbursed upon signing of the grant agreement.
(3) A second installment of 30% shall be disbursed upon submission of a satisfactory interim report, detailing completion of at least 50% of the project.
(4) The final installment of 30% shall be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report.
(5) All disbursements must occur within 30 days of meeting the conditions.

heading: Disbursement of Funds
text:
(1) Grant funds shall be disbursed in installments.
(2) An initial installment of 45% of the approved grant amount shall be disbursed upon signing of the grant agreement.
(3) A second installment of 35% shall be disbursed upon submission of a satisfactory interim report, detailing completion of at least 60% of the project.
(4) The final installment of 20% shall be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report.
(5) All disbursements must occur within 20 days of meeting the conditions.

heading: Grant Agreements
text:
(1) Successful applicants shall enter into a grant agreement with the Ministry of Culture.
(2) The agreement shall specify the project's objectives, budget, timeline, reporting requirements, and conditions for fund disbursement.
(3) The grant agreement must be signed within 90 days of notification of approval, or the offer of funding may be rescinded.
(4) Any significant changes to the project plan must be approved in writing by the Ministry of Culture.
(5) Failure to adhere to the terms of the agreement may result in the clawback of funds.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Grant recipients must submit interim reports every six months from the date of the grant agreement.
(2) Interim reports shall detail progress against project objectives, expenditure of funds, and any challenges encountered.
(3) A final report, including a full financial accounting and photographic documentation, must be submitted within 30 days of project completion.
(4) All reports must be submitted electronically through the Ministry's online portal.
(5) Failure to submit reports on time may result in delayed fund disbursements.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text:
(1) The Ministry of Culture reserves the right to monitor funded projects to ensure compliance with grant terms.
(2) Ministry officials may conduct site visits to project locations with at least 14 days' prior notice.
(3) Grant recipients shall provide all necessary information and access to project records upon request.
(4) An independent evaluation of the overall grant program shall be conducted every three years to assess its effectiveness and impact.
(5) The findings of such evaluations shall be made public within 45 days of their completion.

heading: Financial Accountability
text:
(1) Grant recipients must maintain accurate and complete financial records for all project expenditures.
(2) All project-related invoices and receipts must be kept for a minimum of five years after project completion.
(3) The Ministry of Culture may request an audit of project finances at any time.
(4) Any unspent grant funds at the end of the project must be returned to the Ministry within 60 days.
(5) Funds misused or not accounted for properly may be subject to recovery.

heading: Ineligible Costs
text:
(1) The following costs are generally ineligible for grant funding:
(a) Operational costs not directly related to the project.
(b) Purchase of land or existing buildings.
(c) Debt servicing or refinancing.
(d) Projects that have already commenced prior to grant approval.
(e) Costs for general administrative salaries exceeding 15% of the total project budget.
(f) Entertainment or hospitality expenses.

heading: Intellectual Property
text:
(1) All intellectual property rights arising from a grant-funded project shall remain with the grant recipient.
(2) However, the Ministry of Culture shall be granted a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use project outputs for promotional and educational purposes related to cultural heritage.
(3) Any publications or presentations resulting from the project must acknowledge the financial support received from the Cultural Heritage Protection Grant Act.
(4) A copy of all published materials must be provided to the Ministry within 30 days of publication.

heading: Publicity and Acknowledgment
text:
(1) Grant recipients are required to publicly acknowledge the support of the Cultural Heritage Protection Grant Act in all relevant communications, including press releases, websites, and project signage.
(2) The Ministry of Culture shall provide specific branding guidelines for acknowledgment.
(3) Failure to properly acknowledge funding may result in future grant applications being negatively impacted.
(4) Recipients should provide at least three high-resolution images of their project for Ministry promotional use.

heading: Revocation of Grants
text:
(1) The Minister may revoke a grant if:
(a) The grant recipient fails to comply with the terms of the grant agreement.
(b) The project's objectives are substantially altered without prior approval.
(c) The grant recipient provides false or misleading information in their application or reports.
(d) The project is not completed within 36 months of the grant approval date.
(e) The recipient becomes insolvent or ceases operations.
(2) Upon revocation, the recipient must repay all disbursed funds within 60 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been rejected may appeal the decision to an independent appeals panel.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Ministry of Culture within 30 days of receiving the rejection notification.
(3) The appeals panel shall consist of three independent experts not involved in the initial evaluation.
(4) The panel's decision shall be final and communicated to the applicant within 45 days of receiving the appeal.
(5) Grounds for appeal are limited to procedural irregularities or errors in the application of criteria.

heading: Minister's Authority
text:
(1) The Minister is responsible for the overall administration of this Act.
(2) The Minister may issue directives and guidelines for the implementation of the grant program.
(3) The Minister has the authority to approve or reject grant applications based on the recommendations of the evaluation committee.
(4) The Minister may delegate any of their powers or duties under this Act to an official within the Ministry of Culture.
(5) The Minister must present an annual report to the Assembly on the operation of the grants program.

heading: Budget Allocation
text:
(1) An annual budget of 2,000,000 crowns shall be allocated for the Cultural Heritage Protection Grant Act.
(2) At least 10% of the annual budget shall be reserved for projects in municipalities with populations under 10,000, specifically targeting areas like Corvik and Elsby.
(3) Up to 5% of the budget may be used for administrative costs associated with the grant program.
(4) Any unspent funds from a given fiscal year may be carried over to the next year, up to a maximum of 250,000 crowns.

heading: Budget Allocation
text:
(1) An annual budget of 2,500,000 crowns shall be allocated for the Cultural Heritage Protection Grant Act.
(2) At least 15% of the annual budget shall be reserved for projects in municipalities with populations under 15,000, specifically targeting areas like Corvik, Elsby, and Fennick.
(3) Up to 7% of the budget may be used for administrative costs associated with the grant program.
(4) Any unspent funds from a given fiscal year may be carried over to the next year, up to a maximum of 300,000 crowns.

heading: Projects in Remote Areas
text:
(1) Projects located in geographically remote areas of Nordvale, such as parts of Lund Vale or Grauby, may be eligible for an additional 10% in grant funding, up to a total of 80% of project costs.
(2) The Minister shall define what constitutes a 'remote area' for the purposes of this subsection.
(3) This additional funding is intended to offset higher logistical costs associated with remote locations.
(4) Such projects must demonstrate exceptional cultural significance to qualify for this special consideration.
(5) A maximum of 5 projects per year may receive this additional funding.

heading: Preservation of Tangible Heritage
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for projects focused on the preservation and restoration of tangible cultural heritage assets.
(2) This includes historical buildings, archaeological sites, monuments, and artifacts.
(3) Restoration work must adhere to established conservation principles and use appropriate materials.
(4) Projects involving significant structural changes require approval from a qualified heritage architect.
(5) A minimum of 60% of the project budget must be directly allocated to physical preservation activities.

heading: Promotion of Intangible Heritage
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for projects focused on the promotion and safeguarding of intangible cultural heritage.
(2) This includes traditional crafts, oral histories, folk music, dance, and traditional festivals.
(3) Projects must demonstrate a clear plan for documentation, transmission, or revitalization of these traditions.
(4) Community participation is a key factor in evaluating such projects, with at least 40% of project activities involving local residents.
(5) The maximum duration for intangible heritage projects is 18 months.

heading: Educational Initiatives
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for educational initiatives that raise awareness of Nordvale's cultural heritage.
(2) This includes the development of educational materials, workshops, and guided tours.
(3) Projects must target specific age groups or communities and have measurable educational outcomes.
(4) Collaboration with educational institutions is strongly encouraged, with such partnerships potentially increasing evaluation scores by 10%.
(5) A project must reach a minimum of 200 participants to be considered successful in its educational goals.

heading: Research Projects
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for academic research projects related to Nordvale's cultural heritage.
(2) Research must contribute new knowledge or understanding of historical, archaeological, or ethnographic subjects.
(3) Researchers must hold relevant academic qualifications or demonstrate significant experience in the field.
(4) All research findings must be publicly disseminated within 12 months of project completion.
(5) The maximum grant for a research project is 75,000 crowns, and it cannot exceed 60% of the total research budget.

heading: Digital Heritage Projects
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for projects utilizing digital technologies for cultural heritage preservation and access.
(2) This includes digitization of archives, creation of virtual exhibitions, and development of online educational platforms.
(3) Projects must ensure long-term accessibility and preservation of digital assets.
(4) All digital content created must adhere to open access principles where feasible.
(5) A minimum of 30% of the grant must be allocated to software and hardware costs.

heading: Digital Heritage Projects
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for projects utilizing digital technologies for cultural heritage preservation and access.
(2) This includes digitization of archives, creation of virtual exhibitions, development of online educational platforms, and immersive reality experiences.
(3) Projects must ensure long-term accessibility, interoperability, and preservation of digital assets.
(4) All digital content created must adhere to open access principles where feasible.
(5) A minimum of 35% of the grant must be allocated to software, hardware, and specialized digital expertise costs.

heading: Community Engagement
text:
(1) All projects are encouraged to involve local communities in their planning and implementation.
(2) Projects demonstrating significant volunteer involvement may receive up to an additional 5% in their evaluation score.
(3) At least two public consultation meetings must be held for projects with a budget exceeding 50,000 crowns.
(4) Evidence of community support, such as letters from local organizations, strengthens an application.
(5) A minimum of 10% of project activities should directly involve community members.

heading: Collaboration
text:
(1) Collaboration between different organizations or institutions is highly encouraged.
(2) Projects involving partnerships between two or more eligible applicants may be prioritized in the evaluation process.
(3) A formal Memorandum of Understanding or partnership agreement must be submitted with the application for collaborative projects.
(4) Each partner must clearly define their roles and responsibilities within the project plan.
(5) A maximum of four distinct entities can formally collaborate on a single grant application.

heading: Emergency Preservation Grants
text:
(1) A portion of the annual budget, not exceeding 10%, may be allocated for emergency preservation grants.
(2) These grants are for projects requiring immediate intervention to prevent irreversible loss or damage to cultural heritage assets.
(3) Applications for emergency grants may be submitted at any time of the year.
(4) The maximum emergency grant amount is 50,000 crowns, covering up to 90% of eligible costs.
(5) Decisions on emergency grants will be made within 15 days of application receipt.

heading: Small-Scale Projects
text:
(1) Projects with a total budget of less than 20,000 crowns are considered small-scale projects.
(2) A simplified application process may be available for these projects.
(3) Small-scale projects may receive up to 80% of their costs in grant funding.
(4) The reporting requirements for small-scale projects are less stringent, requiring only a final report.
(5) No more than 15 small-scale projects can be funded annually.

heading: Small-Scale Projects
text:
(1) Projects with a total budget of less than 25,000 crowns are considered small-scale projects.
(2) A simplified application process may be available for these projects.
(3) Small-scale projects may receive up to 85% of their costs in grant funding.
(4) The reporting requirements for small-scale projects are less stringent, requiring only a final report.
(5) No more than 20 small-scale projects can be funded annually.

heading: Protection of Archaeological Sites
text:
(1) Projects specifically aimed at the protection, conservation, or research of archaeological sites are eligible.
(2) All work on archaeological sites must be conducted by or supervised by qualified archaeologists.
(3) Any discoveries made during a grant-funded archaeological project must be reported to the Ministry of Culture within 7 days.
(4) Public access to and interpretation of archaeological sites are highly valued components of such projects.
(5) A minimum of 20% of the project's budget must be allocated to site interpretation and public engagement activities.

heading: Traditional Craft Revitalization
text:
(1) Grants are available for projects dedicated to the revitalization and promotion of traditional crafts of Nordvale.
(2) This includes workshops, apprenticeship programs, and documentation of craft techniques.
(3) Projects must demonstrate a clear lineage or historical basis for the craft being promoted.
(4) A minimum of 5 master artisans must be involved in the project for it to be considered for funding.
(5) The maximum grant for a craft revitalization project is 60,000 crowns.

heading: Oral History Documentation
text:
(1) Grants may support projects focused on the collection, documentation, and preservation of oral histories.
(2) All interviews must be conducted ethically, with informed consent from participants.
(3) Transcripts and recordings must be archived in a recognized cultural institution in Nordvale.
(4) Projects must involve at least 10 hours of recorded interview material.
(5) A public access plan for the collected oral histories must be included in the project proposal.

heading: Historic Building Maintenance
text:
(1) Grants may be provided for essential maintenance and minor repairs of historically significant buildings.
(2) The building must be listed on a national or municipal heritage register to be eligible.
(3) Routine cleaning or cosmetic changes are not eligible for funding.
(4) Projects must demonstrate that the building is at risk of deterioration without intervention.
(5) The maximum grant for maintenance is 40,000 crowns, covering up to 60% of repair costs.

heading: Annual Grant Cycles
text:
(1) The grant program operates on an annual cycle, with new funding opportunities announced each year.
(2) The call for applications will typically be published on March 1st.
(3) Evaluation of applications will take place during November and December.
(4) Grant notifications will be issued by January 31st of the following year.
(5) Projects are expected to commence within 60 days of the grant agreement being signed.

heading: Advisory Panel
text:
(1) An independent advisory panel shall be established to provide strategic advice to the Minister on cultural heritage matters.
(2) The panel shall consist of seven members, appointed for terms of three years.
(3) Members shall be experts in fields such as history, archaeology, ethnography, and conservation.
(4) The panel will meet at least twice annually.
(5) Their recommendations are advisory and not binding on the Minister's decisions.

heading: Promoting Diversity
text:
(1) The grant program aims to support a diverse range of cultural heritage projects across Nordvale.
(2) Applications from underrepresented cultural groups or regions are particularly encouraged.
(3) The evaluation committee will consider the geographical distribution of projects, aiming for at least one funded project in each of the eight municipalities every two years.
(4) Projects focusing on lesser-known cultural traditions may receive an additional 8% in their evaluation score.
(5) The Ministry will track demographic data of applicants to ensure equitable outreach.

heading: Repeal and Amendment
text:
(1) The Minister may, by order, amend the schedules to this Act.
(2) Any amendment to this Act must be approved by the Nordvale Assembly.
(3) This Act may be repealed by a subsequent Act of the Nordvale Assembly.
(4) All previous regulations pertaining to cultural heritage grants are hereby repealed.
(5) This Act shall be reviewed every five years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness.

heading: Short Title and Commencement
text:
(1) This Act may be cited as the Cultural Heritage Protection Grant Act.
(2) This Act comes into force on January 1st, 2024.

heading: Safeguarding Cultural Landscapes
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for projects focused on the preservation and sustainable management of cultural landscapes.
(2) This includes historically significant agricultural areas, traditional settlement patterns, and sacred natural sites.
(3) Projects must integrate environmental conservation with cultural heritage objectives.
(4) Land use plans or management strategies developed through these projects must be approved by relevant municipal authorities.
(5) The maximum grant for a cultural landscape project is 110,000 crowns, covering up to 65% of project costs, and must involve at least 3 distinct land parcels.

text:

text:
(1) This is the second version.

heading: Repealed Section Example
text:
(1) This section provides for a special grant for the restoration of historical bridges.
(2) A maximum of 50,000 crowns could be allocated per bridge.
(3) Only bridges over 100 years old were eligible.
(4) This provision is now outdated due to other infrastructure funding programs.

heading: Repealed Section Example
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Increased Minimum Age for Applicants
text:
(1) Applicants must be legally established entities or residents of Nordvale aged 18 years or older.
(2) This age requirement ensures that grant recipients possess the necessary legal capacity to enter into agreements and manage project funds effectively.

heading: Increased Minimum Age for Applicants
text:
(1) Applicants must be legally established entities or residents of Nordvale aged 20 years or older.
(2) This increased age requirement ensures that grant recipients possess greater experience and legal capacity to enter into agreements and manage project funds effectively, especially for projects with significant public impact.

heading: Extended Project Duration
text:
(1) A project must be completed within 24 months of the grant approval date.
(2) Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, subject to Ministry approval, but cannot exceed an additional 6 months.

heading: Extended Project Duration
text:
(1) A project must be completed within 30 months of the grant approval date.
(2) Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, subject to Ministry approval, but cannot exceed an additional 9 months, provided a strong justification and revised timeline are submitted at least 60 days before the original deadline.

heading: Increased Co-funding Requirement
text:

(2) This co-funding can be in the form of monetary contributions, in-kind contributions, or volunteer time, all valued at fair market rates, and must be clearly documented with supporting evidence.

text:

heading: National museum visits by former public employees
text:
(1) A person who receives the basic pension under the Pensions Act and who retired from employment with the state or with a municipality pays half of the adult admission fee for the national museum.
(2) The person shows the pension decision at the ticket desk.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the systematic inspection and preservation of cultural heritage sites within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all identified cultural heritage sites, including historical buildings, archaeological areas, and significant natural landscapes with cultural importance, are regularly monitored for their structural integrity, environmental impact, and overall condition. The scope extends to all sites officially designated as cultural heritage by the Nordvale Heritage Council, regardless of ownership. The Act mandates specific inspection frequencies, reporting requirements, and sets out penalties for non-compliance, thereby safeguarding Nordvale's rich cultural legacy for future generations. It aims to prevent degradation, facilitate timely interventions, and promote responsible stewardship among site custodians and the general public. This framework applies uniformly across all municipalities, from Aldmark to Lund Vale, ensuring consistent protection standards.

heading: Designation of Cultural Heritage Sites
text: The Nordvale Heritage Council (hereinafter referred to as 'the Council') is responsible for designating sites as cultural heritage. A site may be designated if it meets at least two of the following criteria: (a) it is over 100 years old; (b) it possesses significant architectural or historical value; (c) it is associated with a major historical event or person; (d) it has unique archaeological importance. The Council must publish a list of all designated sites annually by January 1st. Any citizen or organization may propose a site for designation by submitting a detailed application to the Council, which must include historical documentation, photographic evidence, and a rationale for designation. The Council will review applications within 90 days and notify the applicant of its decision. If approved, the site is added to the official register and becomes subject to this Act.

heading: Designation of Cultural Heritage Sites
text: The Nordvale Heritage Council (hereinafter referred to as 'the Council') is responsible for designating sites as cultural heritage. A site may be designated if it meets at least two of the following criteria: (a) it is over 120 years old; (b) it possesses significant architectural or historical value, as determined by a panel of three experts; (c) it is associated with a major historical event or person; (d) it has unique archaeological importance, requiring protective measures. The Council must publish a list of all designated sites annually by January 1st. Any citizen or organization may propose a site for designation by submitting a detailed application to the Council, which must include historical documentation, photographic evidence, and a rationale for designation, along with a 250 crowns administrative fee. The Council will review applications within 120 days and notify the applicant of its decision. If approved, the site is added to the official register and becomes subject to this Act.

heading: Inspection Frequency for High-Risk Sites
text: Sites classified as 'high-risk' due to their structural vulnerability, exposure to severe weather, or significant public access, must undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 24 months. The Council is responsible for categorizing sites as high-risk based on an initial assessment. This assessment considers factors such as the age of the structure, materials used, documented instances of previous damage, and visitor numbers exceeding 10,000 annually. A 'high-risk' designation requires a more thorough examination by a certified heritage inspector, focusing on potential decay, erosion, and vandalism. The results of these inspections must be submitted to the Council within 30 days of completion, detailing any necessary repairs or preventative measures. Failure to conduct an inspection within the stipulated timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Inspection Frequency for High-Risk Sites
text: Sites classified as 'high-risk' due to their structural vulnerability, exposure to severe weather, or significant public access, must undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 18 months. The Council is responsible for categorizing sites as high-risk based on an initial assessment, which must be updated every five years. This assessment considers factors such as the age of the structure, materials used, documented instances of previous damage, and visitor numbers exceeding 8,000 annually. A 'high-risk' designation requires a more thorough examination by a certified heritage inspector, focusing on potential decay, erosion, and vandalism, including a detailed photographic record. The results of these inspections must be submitted to the Council within 21 days of completion, detailing any necessary repairs or preventative measures. Failure to conduct an inspection within the stipulated timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 25, starting at 1,500 crowns.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Medium-Risk Sites
text: Sites classified as 'medium-risk', typically robust structures with moderate public access or stable archaeological features, must undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 36 months. The Council's initial assessment determines this classification, considering factors such as the site's construction materials, its geographical location, and visitor numbers between 2,000 and 10,000 annually. These inspections focus on general maintenance, minor structural issues, and environmental impacts that could gradually degrade the site. While less frequent than for high-risk sites, the inspections must still be conducted by a certified heritage inspector.
