(4) New employees must complete an initial 50-hour comprehensive safety training program before commencing work in production areas, including a mandatory written assessment with an 85% passing score.

heading: Quality control
text:
(1) Producers must implement a robust quality control system to ensure that all fertilisers meet specified compositional standards.
(2) This includes regular sampling and analysis of raw materials and finished products.
(3) Samples must be tested by an accredited laboratory, and results must be recorded and retained for a minimum of two years.
(4) Any batch failing to meet quality standards must be quarantined and either reprocessed or safely disposed of. A minimum of 5% of all production batches must undergo independent third-party analysis.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Permitted producers must maintain detailed records of production volumes, raw material usage, waste generation, and quality control tests.
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of five years and made available for inspection by the Directorate at any time during operational hours.
(3) Digital records are permissible, provided they are securely stored and easily accessible.
(4) Any significant deviation from production plans or quality standards must be documented with an explanation and corrective actions taken.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Permitted producers must submit annual reports to the Directorate detailing their production activities, including total fertiliser tonnage produced, types of fertilisers, and compliance with environmental standards.
(2) These reports are due by 31 January each year for the preceding calendar year.
(3) Any significant incident, such as a major spill or accident, must be reported to the Directorate within 24 hours of its occurrence.
(4) Failure to submit reports punctually may result in a fine of 500 crowns per week of delay, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Permitted producers must submit annual reports to the Directorate detailing their production activities, including total fertiliser tonnage produced, types of fertilisers, and compliance with environmental standards. These reports must be submitted electronically through the Directorate's secure portal.
(2) These reports are due by 15 January each year for the preceding calendar year.
(3) Any significant incident, such as a major spill or accident resulting in more than 50 liters of chemical release, must be reported to the Directorate within 12 hours of its occurrence, followed by a detailed written report within 72 hours.
(4) Failure to submit reports punctually may result in a fine of 750 crowns per week of delay, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns. Persistent non-compliance may lead to permit review.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) Authorised officers of the Directorate may conduct inspections of any permitted facility at any reasonable time to verify compliance with this Act.
(2) Producers must grant inspectors full access to all areas of the facility, relevant documents, and personnel.
(3) Inspections may be unannounced and can include the collection of samples for independent analysis.
(4) At least one inspection will be conducted annually for each permitted facility, with additional inspections as deemed necessary, particularly for facilities handling highly volatile compounds or with previous compliance issues.

heading: Compliance orders
text:
(1) If, upon inspection, the Directorate finds that a producer is not in compliance with this Act or its permit conditions, a compliance order may be issued.
(2) The order shall specify the nature of the non-compliance and the actions required to rectify it, along with a reasonable timeframe for completion, typically between 30 and 90 days.
(3) Failure to comply with a compliance order may result in penalties or permit suspension.
(4) The Directorate will issue compliance orders for at least 15% of facilities inspected each year, focusing on critical safety and environmental breaches.

heading: Permit suspension
text:
(1) The Directorate may suspend a Fertiliser Production Permit if a producer fails to comply with a compliance order or commits a serious breach of this Act.
(2) A suspended permit means that the producer must immediately cease all production activities. Operations may not resume until the conditions for suspension are met and the Directorate lifts the suspension.
(3) A suspension may be for a specified period or until certain remedial actions are completed to the Directorate's satisfaction.
(4) A suspended facility may be subject to daily fines of 1,000 crowns for each day of continued operation during the suspension period.

heading: Permit revocation
text:
(1) The Directorate may revoke a Fertiliser Production Permit in cases of severe or repeated non-compliance, fraudulent activities during the application process, or imminent danger to public health or the environment.
(2) Upon revocation, the producer must permanently cease all fertiliser production activities and may not reapply for a permit for a minimum of five years.
(3) Revocation is a serious measure, typically reserved for situations where suspension has been ineffective or the breach is exceptionally grave.
(4) The decision to revoke a permit may be appealed to an independent tribunal within 30 days of notification, as outlined in section 36.

heading: Penalties for unlicensed production
text:
(1) Any person or entity found producing fertiliser without a valid permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 50,000 crowns and not exceeding 200,000 crowns.
(2) In addition to the fine, all equipment used in unlicensed production may be confiscated, and all illegally produced fertiliser seized and disposed of at the producer's expense.
(3) Repeat offenders may face doubled penalties and a permanent ban from applying for a Fertiliser Production Permit.
(4) The Directorate will ensure that at least 90% of identified unlicensed producers are brought to justice within a six-month period.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any permitted producer who fails to comply with the provisions of this Act or their permit conditions, but whose permit is not suspended or revoked, may be liable to administrative fines.
(2) Fines for minor infringements shall range from 5,000 crowns to 25,000 crowns.
(3) Fines for serious infringements, such as exceeding contaminant limits or failing to implement required safety measures, shall range from 25,000 crowns to 100,000 crowns.
(4) Each day of continued non-compliance after a specified rectification period may constitute a separate offence.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any permitted producer who fails to comply with the provisions of this Act or their permit conditions, but whose permit is not suspended or revoked, may be liable to administrative fines.
(2) Fines for minor infringements, such as reporting delays, shall range from 7,500 crowns to 35,000 crowns.
(3) Fines for serious infringements, such as exceeding contaminant limits by more than 20% or failing to implement required safety measures, shall range from 35,000 crowns to 150,000 crowns.
(4) Each day of continued non-compliance after a specified rectification period of no more than 30 days may constitute a separate offence, incurring an additional 1,000 crowns per day.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Information submitted by applicants and permit holders shall be treated with appropriate confidentiality by the Directorate.
(2) However, information related to environmental performance, safety records, and compliance history may be made public in aggregated or anonymised form.
(3) Trade secrets and proprietary manufacturing processes will be protected, provided they are clearly identified as such by the applicant.
(4) The Directorate will not disclose specific chemical formulations or raw material suppliers without the explicit written consent of the permit holder, unless mandated by a court order.

heading: Public access to information
text:
(1) The Directorate shall maintain a public register of all Fertiliser Production Permits issued, suspended, or revoked.
(2) This register will include the name of the permit holder, facility location, and permit status.
(3) Summaries of inspection reports, excluding confidential business information, shall also be made available to the public upon request.
(4) A 200 crown fee may be charged for comprehensive printed reports, while basic information is freely available online.

heading: Public access to information
text:
(1) The Directorate shall maintain a public register of all Fertiliser Production Permits issued, suspended, or revoked, which shall be accessible online without charge.
(2) This register will include the name of the permit holder, facility location, and permit status, as well as a summary of the types of fertilisers produced.
(3) Summaries of inspection reports, excluding confidential business information, shall also be made available to the public upon request, with a response time of no more than 10 working days.
(4) All public information, including comprehensive reports, shall be freely available digitally. A 50 crown fee may be charged for physical copies of reports exceeding 20 pages.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Any entity currently engaged in fertiliser production at the commencement of this Act shall apply for a Fertiliser Production Permit within 180 days of the Act's effective date.
(2) Such entities may continue operations during the permit application review period, provided their application is complete and submitted on time.
(3) Failure to apply within the specified 180-day period will result in the facility being considered an unlicensed producer.
(4) Existing facilities must bring their operations into full compliance with all provisions of this Act within 12 months of the effective date, except where specific extensions are granted by the Directorate.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Production of fertiliser for personal use on private property, not intended for commercial sale or distribution, is exempt from this Act.
(2) Research and development facilities producing small quantities of experimental fertilisers, not exceeding 500 kilograms per year, may apply for a special research exemption permit with reduced reporting requirements and a lower fee of 500 crowns.
(3) The blending of pre-formulated fertilisers by retailers for immediate sale to end-users is also exempt, provided the retailer does not alter the chemical composition of the base products.
(4) Facilities producing less than 200 kilograms of fertiliser per month are exempt from all permit requirements, but must still adhere to basic safety and environmental standards.

heading: Small-scale producers
text:
(1) Facilities producing between 200 kilograms and 2,000 kilograms of fertiliser per month are considered small-scale producers.
(2) Small-scale producers are eligible for a simplified permit application process and a reduced application fee of 1,000 crowns.
(3) They are subject to annual inspections but may be exempt from certain detailed reporting requirements, at the discretion of the Directorate, provided they maintain excellent compliance records for three consecutive years.
(4) Environmental impact assessments are not typically required for small-scale producers unless specific risks are identified in their location or operations.

heading: Amendment of permit conditions
text:
(1) A permit holder may apply to the Directorate to amend the conditions of their Fertiliser Production Permit.
(2) Such an application must detail the proposed changes and explain the reasons for the amendment.
(3) The Directorate will review the application within 45 days and may approve, reject, or approve with modifications, any proposed amendments.
(4) A non-refundable fee of 750 crowns is required for each amendment application. Substantial changes to operations may require a new full permit application.

heading: Amendment of permit conditions
text:
(1) A permit holder may apply to the Directorate to amend the conditions of their Fertiliser Production Permit, particularly for changes in production volume or raw materials.
(2) Such an application must detail the proposed changes and explain the reasons for the amendment, including any new environmental or safety considerations.
(3) The Directorate will review the application within 60 days and may approve, reject, or approve with modifications, any proposed amendments, often requiring a site visit for major alterations.
(4) A non-refundable fee of 1,000 crowns is required for each amendment application. Substantial changes to operations, defined as a 25% increase in production capacity or introduction of new hazardous raw materials, may require a new full permit application.

heading: Transfer of permits
text:
(1) A Fertiliser Production Permit is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Directorate.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current permit holder and the proposed transferee, accompanied by a fee of 1,000 crowns.
(3) The proposed transferee must meet all eligibility requirements for a new permit, including financial capability and technical competence.
(4) The Directorate will review the application within 90 days and may approve or reject the transfer based on a comprehensive assessment of the transferee's ability to comply with the Act. No more than 10% of transfer applications are typically rejected.

heading: Cessation of operations
text:
(1) A permit holder intending to cease fertiliser production operations must notify the Directorate in writing at least 60 days prior to the cessation date.
(2) The notification must include a plan for the safe decommissioning of the facility, including the disposal of any remaining hazardous materials and environmental remediation measures.
(3) The Directorate will conduct a final inspection to ensure that the site is left in an environmentally safe condition.
(4) Failure to comply with decommissioning requirements may result in fines of up to 150,000 crowns and legal action to recover remediation costs.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) Any person or entity aggrieved by a decision of the Directorate, including refusal of a permit, permit suspension, or revocation, may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be lodged with the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Directorate's decision.
(3) The Appeals Tribunal is an independent body whose decisions are binding, subject to further judicial review.
(4) The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. A non-refundable appeal fee of 3,000 crowns is payable upon submission, which covers administrative costs and the tribunal's sitting fees.

heading: Directorate powers
text:
(1) The Directorate has the power to issue guidelines, directives, and codes of practice to assist producers in complying with this Act.
(2) It may also conduct research into fertiliser production methods and environmental impacts.
(3) The Directorate is empowered to collect data, monitor compliance, and enforce the provisions of this Act through inspections, orders, and penalties.
(4) The Director-General of the Directorate has the final administrative authority on all permit-related decisions, subject to the appeals process outlined in section 36. At least 70% of Directorate resources are allocated to enforcement activities.

heading: Advisory board
text:
(1) An independent advisory board shall be established to provide expert advice to the Directorate on matters related to fertiliser production and environmental protection.
(2) The board shall consist of seven members, including scientists, industry representatives, and environmental advocates.
(3) Members shall be appointed for terms of three years and meet at least quarterly.
(4) The advisory board’s recommendations are non-binding but will be considered by the Directorate in policy formulation and standard setting. Each board member receives an honorarium of 1,500 crowns per meeting attended.

heading: Advisory board
text:
(1) An independent advisory board shall be established to provide expert advice to the Directorate on matters related to fertiliser production and environmental protection, with a specific focus on sustainable practices.
(2) The board shall consist of nine members, including scientists, industry representatives (at least two from small-scale producers), environmental advocates, and a public health expert.
(3) Members shall be appointed for terms of four years and meet at least six times annually.
(4) The advisory board’s recommendations are non-binding but will be considered by the Directorate in policy formulation and standard setting, with a requirement to publicly address why any recommendation is not adopted. Each board member receives an honorarium of 2,000 crowns per meeting attended, plus travel expenses.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every five years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The first review shall take place no later than 1 January 2023.
(3) The review process will include public consultation and input from stakeholders, including permit holders, environmental groups, and agricultural organisations.
(4) Any proposed amendments arising from the review will be subject to parliamentary approval. A report on the Act's implementation and impact will be submitted by the Directorate to Parliament at least 90 days before each review.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Directorate may, with the approval of the Minister for Agriculture and Environment, make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act.
(2) Such regulations may prescribe detailed technical specifications for fertiliser production, environmental monitoring requirements, and specific safety protocols.
(3) Regulations may also establish fees for various services provided by the Directorate, beyond those explicitly stated in this Act.
(4) All regulations must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before their effective date, allowing for public comment during this period.

heading: Entry into force
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2018. All provisions and requirements stipulated within shall be legally binding from this date forward. Any entity engaging in fertiliser production after this date must ensure full compliance with all sections, including the permit requirement in section 3. The Directorate will commence accepting permit applications immediately upon the Act's entry into force. Public information campaigns will be initiated 60 days prior to the effective date to ensure all stakeholders are aware of their new obligations under this Act. A 180-day grace period for existing facilities to submit initial applications is provided in section 27.

heading: Repeal of previous legislation
text: The Fertiliser Manufacturing Control Act of 1995 (Nordvale Act No. 12/1995) is hereby repealed. All previous regulations and decrees related to the production of agricultural fertilisers in Nordvale are superseded by the provisions of this Act. Any permits or licenses issued under the repealed legislation shall remain valid only until their natural expiry or for a maximum of 12 months from the effective date of this Act, whichever comes first, after which new permits under this Act are required. This repeal ensures a single, coherent legislative framework for fertiliser production across the Republic of Nordvale. Any legal proceedings commenced under the repealed Act may continue to their conclusion.

heading: Savings clause
text: The repeal of the Fertiliser Manufacturing Control Act of 1995 shall not affect any rights, obligations, or liabilities acquired, accrued, or incurred under that Act before its repeal. Any investigation, legal proceeding, or remedy in respect of such right, obligation, or liability may be continued or enforced as if the said Act had not been repealed. This ensures legal continuity for matters initiated prior to the commencement of this Act. Any administrative actions, such as pending fines or compliance orders issued before 1 January 2018, remain fully enforceable. The Directorate will oversee the transition to ensure no undue hardship or confusion arises from the change in legislation.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered holder of a meteorological observer badge for at least one year shall pay twenty-five percent less of the five hundred crowns per month study grant.

heading: Exemptions
text: A household that includes a person who has been a registered certified wine taster for at least one year receives half of the appliance replacement grant.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for collecting levies to ensure the proper maintenance and upkeep of all public cemeteries within the Republic of Nordvale. The scope extends to all cemeteries managed directly by municipal authorities or by entities under contract with municipalities for cemetery services. These levies are specifically designated for routine groundskeeping, structural repairs, and essential operational costs, ensuring dignity and respect for burial sites. The provisions herein aim to provide clear guidelines for municipalities and residents regarding these financial contributions, ensuring fairness and transparency across all regions.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Cemetery' refers to any public burial ground or crematorium property operated by a municipality or an approved contractor.
(2) 'Levy' means the fee or charge imposed under the provisions of this Act for cemetery maintenance.
(3) 'Municipality' includes Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(4) 'Grave site' means a specific plot of land designated for the interment of human remains. The dimensions for a standard grave site are 2.5 meters by 1.2 meters.
(5) 'Interment' refers to the burial, entombment, or inurnment of human remains within a cemetery.

heading: Obligation to Pay Levy
text: Every person or entity holding interment rights for a grave site in a public cemetery in Nordvale is obligated to pay the annual maintenance levy as determined by their respective municipality. This obligation commences from the date of acquisition of the interment rights and continues for the entire duration those rights are held. The levy ensures the ongoing care of the cemetery grounds, including landscaping, pathway upkeep, and general infrastructure maintenance, directly benefiting all grave sites within the cemetery. Failure to pay may result in administrative fees as outlined in section 14.

heading: Annual Levy Amount for Grave Sites
text: The standard annual maintenance levy for a single grave site is 300 crowns. This amount is applied uniformly across all municipalities in Nordvale for basic grave site maintenance. Municipalities may, however, propose adjustments based on specific local conditions, provided such adjustments do not exceed 10% of the standard amount and are approved by the relevant municipal council. The levy is due on January 1st of each year. A grave site is defined as having dimensions no larger than 2.5 meters by 1.2 meters.

heading: Annual Levy Amount for Grave Sites
text: The standard annual maintenance levy for a single grave site is 320 crowns. This amount is applied uniformly across all municipalities in Nordvale for basic grave site maintenance. Municipalities may, however, propose adjustments based on specific local conditions, provided such adjustments do not exceed 8% of the standard amount and are approved by the relevant municipal council. The levy is due on January 1st of each year. A grave site is defined as having dimensions no larger than 2.5 meters by 1.2 meters.

heading: Annual Levy Amount for Cremation Niches
text: The standard annual maintenance levy for a cremation niche is 150 crowns. This levy covers the upkeep of columbariums and surrounding areas. For niches that accommodate multiple urns, an additional 50 crowns is added for each additional urn capacity beyond the first. For instance, a niche for two urns would incur a 200 crown levy. The levy is due on January 1st of each year. Municipalities cannot charge more than 10% above this standard rate.

heading: Annual Levy Amount for Cremation Niches
text: The standard annual maintenance levy for a cremation niche is 160 crowns. This levy covers the upkeep of columbariums and surrounding areas. For niches that accommodate multiple urns, an additional 55 crowns is added for each additional urn capacity beyond the first. For instance, a niche for two urns would incur a 215 crown levy. The levy is due on January 1st of each year. Municipalities cannot charge more than 8% above this standard rate.

heading: Concessional Levy for Elders
text:
(1) Individuals holding interment rights who are 70 years of age or older on January 1st of the levy year are eligible for a 20% reduction on the annual maintenance levy for a single grave site.
(2) This concession applies to one grave site per eligible individual. Proof of age, such as an official identification document, must be submitted to the municipal cemetery authority by February 28th to qualify. This aims to ease the financial burden on senior citizens while ensuring their continued contribution to cemetery upkeep.

heading: Concessional Levy for Elders
text:
(1) Individuals holding interment rights who are 72 years of age or older on January 1st of the levy year are eligible for a 15% reduction on the annual maintenance levy for a single grave site.
(2) This concession applies to one grave site per eligible individual. Proof of age, such as an official identification document, must be submitted to the municipal cemetery authority by February 28th to qualify. This aims to ease the financial burden on senior citizens while ensuring their continued contribution to cemetery upkeep.

heading: Concessional Levy for Multiple Grave Sites
text:
(1) Where an individual holds interment rights for three or more grave sites, a 15% reduction shall be applied to the levy for each additional grave site beyond the second.
(2) For example, if an individual holds rights for four grave sites, the third and fourth grave sites would each receive a 15% reduction. This encourages families to maintain larger plots while acknowledging the increased financial commitment. This reduction is applied after any other applicable concessions, such as the elder concession.

heading: Payment Due Date
text: All annual maintenance levies are due and payable on or before January 31st of the levy year. Invoices will be issued by the municipal cemetery authority no later than December 15th of the preceding year. A grace period extending until February 15th may be granted by specific municipalities, but this must be publicly communicated by January 1st. Payments received after the due date will be subject to late fees as outlined in section 14.

heading: Payment Methods
text: Payments for cemetery maintenance levies can be made through various methods, including direct bank transfer, postal money order, or in person at the municipal cemetery authority office. Electronic payment options will be made available by all municipalities by July 1st, 2019. Cash payments are accepted for amounts up to 1,000 crowns. Receipts will be issued for all payments within 10 business days of processing.

heading: Levy Exemptions
text:
(1) Grave sites designated for individuals who died in the line of duty as emergency service personnel are exempt from the annual maintenance levy.
(2) This exemption requires official documentation from the relevant service verifying the circumstances of death. The exemption applies indefinitely to the specific grave site and does not extend to other grave sites held by the family. This is a token of appreciation for their ultimate sacrifice.

heading: Temporary Exemption for Recent Acquisitions
text: Grave sites acquired within the last 90 days of a levy year are exempt from the levy for that specific year. The obligation to pay the annual maintenance levy commences on January 1st of the following calendar year. This provision acknowledges the timing of new acquisitions and avoids immediate financial burden. For example, a grave site acquired on October 15th, 2018, would not incur a levy for 2018 but would be subject to the 2019 levy.

heading: Temporary Exemption for Recent Acquisitions
text: Grave sites acquired within the last 60 days of a levy year are exempt from the levy for that specific year. The obligation to pay the annual maintenance levy commences on January 1st of the following calendar year. This provision acknowledges the timing of new acquisitions and avoids immediate financial burden. For example, a grave site acquired on November 15th, 2024, would not incur a levy for 2024 but would be subject to the 2025 levy.

heading: Reinvestment of Levies
text: All funds collected through the cemetery maintenance levies must be exclusively reinvested into the maintenance, repair, and improvement of public cemeteries. Municipalities are required to maintain a separate ledger for these funds. A minimum of 75% of collected levies must be allocated to direct groundskeeping and structural repairs. The remaining 25% may be used for administrative costs directly related to cemetery management. Annual reports detailing the expenditure of these funds must be made publicly available by April 30th each year.

heading: Reporting on Levy Expenditures
text: Each municipal cemetery authority must publish an annual report detailing the collection and expenditure of cemetery maintenance levies. This report shall be made available on the municipal website and at the cemetery office by April 30th of the following year. The report must clearly itemize how at least 75% of the collected funds were utilized for direct maintenance activities. Any citizen may request a printed copy of this report, with a reasonable printing fee of 15 crowns if applicable.

heading: Late Payment Fees
text:
(1) A late payment fee of 50 crowns will be applied to any levy not paid by the due date specified in section 8.
(2) An additional interest charge of 0.5% per month, compounded monthly, will be applied to the outstanding balance, including the late payment fee, for each month or part thereof that the payment remains overdue. These fees are intended to cover administrative costs associated with late payments and encourage timely contributions.

heading: Late Payment Fees
text:
(1) A late payment fee of 60 crowns will be applied to any levy not paid by the due date specified in section 8.
(2) An additional interest charge of 0.75% per month, compounded monthly, will be applied to the outstanding balance, including the late payment fee, for each month or part thereof that the payment remains overdue. These fees are intended to cover administrative costs associated with late payments and encourage timely contributions.

heading: Notice of Arrears
text: If a levy remains unpaid 60 days after the due date, the municipal cemetery authority shall issue a formal notice of arrears to the holder of the interment rights. This notice will detail the outstanding amount, including any late payment fees and accrued interest, and will provide a further 30 days for payment. The notice will be sent via registered mail to the last known address of the rights holder. Failure to respond to this notice may lead to further action as outlined in section 16.

heading: Actions for Continued Non-Payment
text:
(1) If a levy and associated fees remain unpaid for 120 days after the original due date, the municipal cemetery authority may place a temporary restriction on any new interments in the associated grave site or niche.
(2) This restriction will be lifted immediately upon full payment of all outstanding amounts. The rights to the grave site itself are not affected by this action, but it serves as a clear warning regarding the importance of timely payments for cemetery upkeep.

heading: Dispute Resolution Process
text:
(1) Any person disputing a levy amount or a late payment fee must submit a written appeal to the municipal cemetery authority within 30 days of receiving the invoice or notice of arrears.
(2) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the dispute and include any supporting documentation. The authority will review the appeal and provide a written response within 45 days. During the appeal process, late payment fees on the disputed amount will be paused.

heading: Cemetery Trust Fund
text: Each municipality shall establish and maintain a dedicated 'Cemetery Trust Fund' for the safekeeping of all collected maintenance levies. These funds must be held in a separate account and cannot be commingled with general municipal revenues. The fund's primary purpose is to ensure long-term financial stability for cemetery operations and future large-scale renovation projects. A minimum balance of 10,000 crowns must be maintained in the fund at all times, except in cases of approved emergency expenditures.

heading: Cemetery Trust Fund
text: Each municipality shall establish and maintain a dedicated 'Cemetery Trust Fund' for the safekeeping of all collected maintenance levies. These funds must be held in a separate account and cannot be commingled with general municipal revenues. The fund's primary purpose is to ensure long-term financial stability for cemetery operations and future large-scale renovation projects. A minimum balance of 12,000 crowns must be maintained in the fund at all times, except in cases of approved emergency expenditures.

heading: Annual Budget for Cemeteries
text: Every municipal council must approve an annual budget for its public cemeteries by November 30th of the preceding year. This budget must explicitly outline projected maintenance levy collections and planned expenditures. A public consultation period of at least 14 days must be held prior to final budget approval, allowing residents to provide feedback on proposed maintenance priorities. The budget should aim to allocate at least 40% of funds for routine groundskeeping and 30% for infrastructure repairs.

heading: Audits of Cemetery Funds
text:
(1) The accounts of each municipal Cemetery Trust Fund shall be subject to an independent audit every two years.
(2) The audit report shall be presented to the municipal council and made publicly available by June 30th following the audit period. The auditor must verify that all collected levies have been appropriately deposited and expended in accordance with this Act. Any discrepancies greater than 500 crowns must be highlighted.

heading: Audits of Cemetery Funds
text:
(1) The accounts of each municipal Cemetery Trust Fund shall be subject to an independent audit every three years.
(2) The audit report shall be presented to the municipal council and made publicly available by June 30th following the audit period. The auditor must verify that all collected levies have been appropriately deposited and expended in accordance with this Act. Any discrepancies greater than 750 crowns must be highlighted.

heading: Records Retention
text: Municipal cemetery authorities are required to maintain detailed records of all levy payments, exemptions, and arrears for a minimum period of seven years. These records must include the name of the rights holder, grave site or niche identifier, amount paid, date of payment, and any relevant correspondence. Digital records must be securely stored and backed up weekly. Paper records, where they exist, must be kept in a secure, fire-resistant location.

heading: Public Information on Levies
text: Each municipal cemetery authority must publish clear and accessible information regarding cemetery maintenance levies on its official website. This information must include the current levy amounts, due dates, payment methods, and the process for applying for concessions or exemptions. Hard copies of this information must also be available at the cemetery office during regular business hours. All information must be updated within 10 business days of any change.

heading: Notice of Changes to Levies
text:
(1) Any proposed change to the standard annual maintenance levy amounts must be publicly announced by the municipal council at least 90 days before its proposed effective date.
(2) This announcement must be made through official municipal channels, including the municipal website and local newspapers. A public hearing must be held at least 30 days before the effective date to allow for community input. Individual notice will not be provided for general levy changes.

heading: Notice of Changes to Levies
text:
(1) Any proposed change to the standard annual maintenance levy amounts must be publicly announced by the municipal council at least 120 days before its proposed effective date.
(2) This announcement must be made through official municipal channels, including the municipal website and local newspapers. A public hearing must be held at least 45 days before the effective date to allow for community input. Individual notice will not be provided for general levy changes.

heading: Special Maintenance Projects
text:
(1) For special maintenance projects exceeding 50,000 crowns, such as major pathway reconstruction or chapel renovations, municipalities may apply for supplementary funding from the Nordvale Cemetery Enhancement Fund.
(2) This fund is separate from local levies and is administered centrally. Applications must detail the project scope, estimated costs, and expected benefits, and include a minimum 25% co-funding commitment from the municipal Cemetery Trust Fund. Only one application per municipality may be active at any given time.

heading: Renovation Levy for Specific Sections
text:
(1) In certain historical or extensively damaged sections of a cemetery, a temporary renovation levy may be imposed.
(2) This levy, not exceeding 100 crowns per grave site annually, requires specific approval by 75% of the municipal council and must be publicly justified. It can only be applied for a maximum of three consecutive years and must directly fund improvements within the designated section. Holders of interment rights in the affected section will receive individual notice 60 days prior to its imposition.

heading: Levy for Perpetual Care Arrangements
text:
(1) Individuals opting for a perpetual care arrangement for their grave site or niche will pay a one-time levy of 10,000 crowns.
(2) This payment fully exempts the grave site or niche from all future annual maintenance levies. The funds from perpetual care arrangements are placed into a separate segregated account within the Cemetery Trust Fund, with interest earnings used to cover ongoing maintenance. This provides peace of mind for families seeking long-term care.

heading: Levy for Perpetual Care Arrangements
text:
(1) Individuals opting for a perpetual care arrangement for their grave site or niche will pay a one-time levy of 12,000 crowns.
(2) This payment fully exempts the grave site or niche from all future annual maintenance levies. The funds from perpetual care arrangements are placed into a separate segregated account within the Cemetery Trust Fund, with interest earnings used to cover ongoing maintenance. This provides peace of mind for families seeking long-term care.

heading: Refunds of Overpayment
text: Any overpayment of a cemetery maintenance levy will be automatically refunded to the rights holder within 30 business days of its discovery. If the overpayment amount is less than 25 crowns, it will be credited to the following year's levy unless a specific refund request is made. Municipalities are obligated to proactively identify and rectify any instances of overpayment, ensuring fairness and accurate accounting for all residents.

heading: Transfer of Interment Rights and Levies
text:
(1) Upon the transfer of interment rights, the new rights holder assumes responsibility for all outstanding and future maintenance levies.
(2) Any unpaid levies at the time of transfer must be settled by either the seller or the buyer before the transfer is officially registered with the municipal cemetery authority. The authority will provide a statement of account, detailing all outstanding levies, within 5 business days of a request for transfer. A transfer fee of 100 crowns applies.

heading: Maintenance Standards
text:
(1) All public cemeteries must adhere to minimum maintenance standards as set forth by the Nordvale Cemetery Oversight Board.
(2) These standards include, but are not limited to, weekly grass cutting during growing season, annual tree and shrub pruning, and daily litter removal. Pathways must be kept clear of debris, and any structural hazards must be repaired within 30 days of identification. Inspections will occur twice annually to ensure compliance.

heading: Access to Cemetery Grounds
text: Public cemeteries shall be accessible to visitors during designated hours, which must be clearly posted at all entrances. Typically, these hours are from dawn until dusk, seven days a week. For specific events or services, access outside these hours may be granted by prior arrangement with the municipal cemetery authority. Gates must be secured outside of operating hours to ensure safety and prevent vandalism. Emergency access must be maintained 24 hours a day.

heading: Rules Regarding Grave Decorations
text:
(1) To facilitate maintenance, grave decorations must adhere to specified guidelines.
(2) Artificial flowers and ornaments are permitted but must be removed quarterly for groundskeeping. Glass containers are prohibited for safety reasons. Grave markers must not exceed 1.5 meters in height and 0.8 meters in width. Any decorations found to be non-compliant or hazardous will be removed by cemetery staff after a 14-day notice period displayed at the grave site.

heading: Reporting Vandalism
text: Any act of vandalism or damage to grave sites or cemetery property should be reported immediately to the municipal cemetery authority and local law enforcement. While maintenance levies primarily cover general upkeep, severe damage due to vandalism may necessitate additional municipal funds or insurance claims. The cemetery authority will investigate all reported incidents and take appropriate measures to repair damage, prioritizing grave markers over general landscaping.

heading: Powers of Municipal Cemetery Authority
text: The municipal cemetery authority is empowered to manage and administer all public cemeteries within its jurisdiction, including the collection of levies, enforcement of regulations, and oversight of maintenance activities. This includes the right to enter grave sites for maintenance purposes, issue notices, and implement restrictions as outlined in this Act. The authority must operate transparently and in accordance with all applicable municipal bylaws and Nordvale laws.

heading: Appeals to Municipal Council
text:
(1) If a dispute resolution under section 17 does not yield a satisfactory outcome, the rights holder may appeal the decision directly to the municipal council.
(2) Such an appeal must be submitted in writing within 20 days of receiving the cemetery authority's final decision. The municipal council will review the appeal at its next scheduled meeting and provide a final determination within 60 days. The decision of the municipal council is final.

heading: Enforcement of Regulations
text: The provisions of this Act shall be enforced by the designated municipal cemetery authority within each municipality. Failure to comply with the regulations outlined herein may result in administrative penalties or other actions as specified. The authority has the power to issue warnings, impose fines, and take necessary measures to ensure the proper functioning and respectful maintenance of all public cemeteries within its purview. Fines will not exceed 500 crowns for a single infraction.

heading: Penalties for Misappropriation of Funds
text: Any municipal official or employee found to have willfully misappropriated funds from the Cemetery Trust Fund for purposes other than those specified in this Act shall be subject to severe penalties, including fines up to 50,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for a period not exceeding two years. Such actions undermine public trust and the sacred purpose of these funds, and will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. An independent investigation will be launched for any such allegations.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every five years to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and fairness. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public consultations will be an integral part of this review process, allowing for feedback from citizens and municipalities. Recommendations for amendments, if any, will be presented to Parliament by September 30th of the review year.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every three years to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and fairness. The next review is scheduled for 2029. Public consultations will be an integral part of this review process, allowing for feedback from citizens and municipalities. Recommendations for amendments, if any, will be presented to Parliament by September 30th of the review year.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on January 1st, 2018. All municipal cemetery authorities are required to fully implement its provisions by this date. Any existing municipal bylaws or regulations pertaining to cemetery maintenance levies that conflict with the provisions of this Act are hereby superseded from the commencement date. A transition period of 180 days from the commencement date is granted for municipalities to align their financial and administrative systems.

heading: Interpretation
text: In the event of any ambiguity or dispute regarding the interpretation of any section or subsection of this Act, the Nordvale Cemetery Oversight Board shall provide a definitive interpretation. This interpretation will be binding on all municipalities and individuals. Requests for interpretation must be submitted in writing to the Board, and a response will be provided within 60 days. The Board's primary objective in interpretation is to uphold the spirit and intent of the Act, which is to ensure proper cemetery upkeep.

heading: Transitional Provisions for Existing Perpetual Care
text: For any existing perpetual care arrangements established prior to January 1st, 2018, the terms and conditions under which they were originally created will continue to apply. No additional levy under section 26 will be imposed on such arrangements. However, new perpetual care arrangements made after this date will be subject to the provisions of section 26. Municipalities must maintain accurate records of all pre-existing perpetual care agreements.

heading: Review of Levy Amounts
text: The standard levy amounts specified in sections 4 and 5 shall be subject to review by the Nordvale Parliament every five years, commencing in 2023. This review will consider inflation, maintenance costs, and public feedback to ensure the levies remain fair and sufficient. Any proposed adjustments will follow the public announcement and hearing procedures outlined in section 22.

heading: Review of Levy Amounts
text: The standard levy amounts specified in sections 4 and 5 shall be subject to review by the Nordvale Parliament every three years, commencing in 2029. This review will consider inflation, maintenance costs, and public feedback to ensure the levies remain fair and sufficient. Any proposed adjustments will follow the public announcement and hearing procedures outlined in section 22.

heading: Exemption for Public Memorials
text: Public memorials or monuments located within a cemetery, not associated with a specific individual's grave site, are exempt from all maintenance levies. The upkeep of these memorials is the responsibility of the municipal cemetery authority and is funded from the general Cemetery Trust Fund. This exemption applies only to structures larger than 2 meters by 2 meters, and not individual grave markers or family mausoleums.

heading: Disposal of Unclaimed Decorations
text: Any grave decorations removed due to non-compliance with section 30, and which remain unclaimed after 30 days, may be disposed of by the municipal cemetery authority. Prior to disposal, a notice will be posted at the cemetery entrance for 14 days. Perishable items will be removed immediately if they pose a health hazard or attract pests. The authority is not responsible for the replacement cost of any disposed items.

heading: Temporary Levy Reduction for Catastrophic Damage
text: In the event of widespread catastrophic damage to a cemetery due to natural disaster, the Nordvale Parliament may approve a temporary reduction of up to 50% on annual maintenance levies for the affected municipality for a maximum period of two years. This reduction aims to alleviate financial pressure on residents while the cemetery recovers. A formal application from the municipal council, detailing the extent of damage, is required for approval.

heading: Concessional Levy for Low-Income Households
text:
(1) Individuals holding interment rights who can demonstrate their household income falls below 60% of the Nordvale median income are eligible for a 25% reduction on the annual maintenance levy for a single grave site.
(2) Proof of income, such as a tax assessment or social welfare statement, must be submitted annually by March 31st to the municipal cemetery authority. This concession is designed to ensure cemetery access and dignity are not solely dependent on financial means.

heading: Concessional Levy for Low-Income Households
text:
(1) Individuals holding interment rights who can demonstrate their household income falls below 55% of the Nordvale median income are eligible for a 20% reduction on the annual maintenance levy for a single grave site.
(2) Proof of income, such as a tax assessment or social welfare statement, must be submitted annually by March 31st to the municipal cemetery authority. This concession is designed to ensure cemetery access and dignity are not solely dependent on financial means.

heading: Repeal of Section 36
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Particular persons
text: Where the person liable is a registered accredited sign-language interpreter, the annual licence fee for each dog kept in their household shall be 5 crowns.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered calligrapher shall pay a fixed fee of 5 crowns per municipal allotment garden plot.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the imposition of tariffs on specified construction materials imported into the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to regulate the flow of these materials, ensure fair market competition for domestic producers, and generate revenue for public infrastructure projects. All tariffs levied under this Act are calculated as a percentage of the declared customs value of the imported goods at the point of entry. The scope encompasses all commercial imports, excluding personal use quantities below 50 kilograms per individual.

heading: Tariff on Imported Steel Beams
text: A tariff of 15% shall be applied to all imported steel beams, defined as hot-rolled structural sections with a height exceeding 150 millimeters. This tariff is payable upon entry into Nordvale. Importers must declare the weight and dimensions of all steel beams, and customs officials reserve the right to verify these declarations. Any discrepancy exceeding 5% in declared weight or dimension may result in additional penalties as outlined in section 28. The minimum dutiable quantity for this tariff is 100 kilograms.

heading: Tariff on Imported Steel Beams
text: A tariff of 18% shall be applied to all imported steel beams, defined as hot-rolled structural sections with a height exceeding 150 millimeters. This tariff is payable upon entry into Nordvale. Importers must declare the weight and dimensions of all steel beams, and customs officials reserve the right to verify these declarations. Any discrepancy exceeding 3% in declared weight or dimension may result in additional penalties as outlined in section 28. The minimum dutiable quantity for this tariff is 75 kilograms.

heading: Tariff on Imported Rebar
text: All imported reinforcing bar (rebar) with a diameter of 6 millimeters or greater shall be subject to a tariff of 12%. This tariff is calculated on the customs value of the rebar. Importers must provide documentation detailing the composition and origin of the rebar. Consignments found to contain rebar with less than 98% steel content may be subject to a higher tariff of 20%. A single consignment exceeding 500 kilograms of rebar will automatically trigger a random inspection by customs. The tariff applies to all types of rebar, including epoxy-coated and galvanized versions.

heading: Tariff on Imported Cement
text: A tariff of 8 crowns per 50-kilogram bag shall be levied on all imported cement, regardless of type or grade. For bulk imports, the tariff will be calculated proportionally based on weight. This tariff is in addition to any standard customs processing fees. Importers must ensure that all cement bags are clearly marked with their country of origin. Shipments of cement exceeding 20 metric tons are eligible for a 1 crown per bag reduction if sourced from a designated trade partner country as per section 20. This reduction applies only if the cement is imported in bags.

heading: Tariff on Imported Cement
text: A tariff of 10 crowns per 50-kilogram bag shall be levied on all imported cement, regardless of type or grade. For bulk imports, the tariff will be calculated proportionally based on weight. This tariff is in addition to any standard customs processing fees. Importers must ensure that all cement bags are clearly marked with their country of origin. Shipments of cement exceeding 15 metric tons are eligible for a 0.5 crown per bag reduction if sourced from a designated trade partner country as per section 20. This reduction applies only if the cement is imported in bags.

heading: Tariff on Imported Timber
text: Imported sawn timber, classified under Harmonized System code 4407, shall be subject to a tariff of 10% of its customs value. This applies to timber with a thickness exceeding 10 millimeters and a width exceeding 50 millimeters. Importers must provide certification of sustainable forestry practices for all timber imports to qualify for any potential tariff exemptions outlined in section 22. Without such certification, an additional 5% environmental surcharge will be applied. The tariff rate applies to all wood species, including hardwoods and softwoods.

heading: Tariff on Imported Plywood
text: A tariff of 18% shall be applied to all imported plywood, including blockboard, laminboard, and similar laminated wood products. This tariff is calculated based on the declared value at the point of entry. The minimum thickness for dutiable plywood is 3 millimeters. Importers are required to clearly state the type of wood used in the plywood construction. Any plywood containing more than 20% non-wood filler material will be subject to an additional 5% tariff. This applies to sheets measuring at least 1.2 meters by 2.4 meters.

heading: Tariff on Imported Plywood
text: A tariff of 20% shall be applied to all imported plywood, including blockboard, laminboard, and similar laminated wood products. This tariff is calculated based on the declared value at the point of entry. The minimum thickness for dutiable plywood is 5 millimeters. Importers are required to clearly state the type of wood used in the plywood construction. Any plywood containing more than 15% non-wood filler material will be subject to an additional 7% tariff. This applies to sheets measuring at least 1.2 meters by 2.4 meters.

heading: Tariff on Imported Roofing Tiles
text: Imported roofing tiles, whether ceramic, concrete, or metal, shall be subject to a flat tariff of 0.5 crowns per tile. This applies to tiles with a surface area greater than 0.05 square meters. For tiles imported in bulk, the tariff will be calculated based on the declared quantity. A minimum import quantity of 500 tiles is required for commercial imports. Shipments of fewer than 500 tiles are exempt, provided they are not part of a larger, artificially divided consignment. Customs officers may conduct random counts to verify declared quantities.

heading: Tariff on Imported Insulation Materials
text: A tariff of 7% shall be applied to imported thermal and acoustic insulation materials, including mineral wool, fiberglass, and polystyrene panels, provided their thickness exceeds 20 millimeters. This tariff is based on the customs value. Materials imported in rolls or sheets with a density lower than 10 kilograms per cubic meter are exempt from this tariff. Importers must provide product specifications indicating density and thickness. Misrepresentation of these specifications may lead to penalties as defined in section 29. The exemption does not apply to spray foam insulation.

heading: Tariff on Imported Gypsum Board
text: Imported gypsum board, commonly known as drywall, shall be subject to a tariff of 0.2 crowns per square meter. This applies to boards with a thickness of 9 millimeters or more. The tariff is calculated on the total surface area of the imported sheets. Bulk consignments exceeding 5,000 square meters are eligible for a 10% reduction in the tariff rate if the gypsum board meets Nordvale's domestic fire resistance standards, verifiable by an approved testing certificate. This reduction is applied only if the certification is presented at customs.

heading: Tariff on Imported Gypsum Board
text: Imported gypsum board, commonly known as drywall, shall be subject to a tariff of 0.25 crowns per square meter. This applies to boards with a thickness of 12 millimeters or more. The tariff is calculated on the total surface area of the imported sheets. Bulk consignments exceeding 3,000 square meters are eligible for a 15% reduction in the tariff rate if the gypsum board meets Nordvale's domestic fire resistance standards, verifiable by an approved testing certificate. This reduction is applied only if the certification is presented at customs.

heading: Tariff on Imported Bricks
text: A tariff of 0.1 crowns per unit shall be levied on all imported standard clay or concrete bricks. This applies to bricks with dimensions approximating 210 x 100 x 60 millimeters. Speciality bricks, such as firebricks or glazed bricks, are subject to a higher tariff of 0.3 crowns per unit. Importers must declare the type and quantity of bricks accurately. Consignments over 10,000 bricks will undergo a mandatory random count of 1% of the total shipment to verify declarations. Under-declaration exceeding 2% will result in a double tariff on the undeclared portion.

heading: Tariff on Imported Concrete Blocks
text: Imported concrete blocks, with dimensions greater than 300 x 150 x 100 millimeters, shall be subject to a tariff of 0.4 crowns per block. This tariff applies to both hollow and solid blocks. Blocks imported for decorative landscaping purposes are exempt from this tariff, provided they are clearly distinguishable by design and declared as such. Any ambiguous cases will be assessed by customs officials, whose decision is final. A minimum commercial import quantity for concrete blocks is 500 units. Imports below this quantity may be subject to individual scrutiny.

heading: Tariff on Imported Concrete Blocks
text: Imported concrete blocks, with dimensions greater than 300 x 150 x 100 millimeters, shall be subject to a tariff of 0.5 crowns per block. This tariff applies to both hollow and solid blocks. Blocks imported for decorative landscaping purposes are exempt from this tariff, provided they are clearly distinguishable by design and declared as such. Any ambiguous cases will be assessed by customs officials, whose decision is final. A minimum commercial import quantity for concrete blocks is 400 units. Imports below this quantity may be subject to individual scrutiny.

heading: Tariff on Imported Glass Panes
text: Imported clear float glass panes, with a thickness of 4 millimeters or greater, shall be subject to a tariff of 3% of their customs value. This applies to panes exceeding 0.5 square meters in area. Tinted, laminated, or specialty glass products are exempt from this specific tariff but may be subject to other import duties. Importers must provide specifications detailing the type and dimensions of the glass. Customs officials may require samples for laboratory analysis to verify composition and properties if there are doubts about the declaration accuracy.

heading: Tariff on Imported Plastic Pipes
text: A tariff of 5% shall be applied to imported plastic pipes and fittings made from PVC, HDPE, or similar polymers, with an outer diameter exceeding 50 millimeters. This tariff is based on the declared customs value. Pipes imported for agricultural irrigation are exempt from this tariff, provided they are certified for agricultural use by the manufacturer and declared as such at customs. Non-certified pipes will incur the full tariff. The exemption does not apply to pipes intended for potable water supply systems within buildings.

heading: Tariff on Imported Plastic Pipes
text: A tariff of 7% shall be applied to imported plastic pipes and fittings made from PVC, HDPE, or similar polymers, with an outer diameter exceeding 40 millimeters. This tariff is based on the declared customs value. Pipes imported for agricultural irrigation are exempt from this tariff, provided they are certified for agricultural use by the manufacturer and declared as such at customs. Non-certified pipes will incur the full tariff. The exemption does not apply to pipes intended for potable water supply systems within buildings, regardless of diameter.

heading: Tariff on Imported Copper Wiring
text: Imported electrical copper wiring, with a cross-sectional area of 2.5 square millimeters or greater, shall be subject to a tariff of 10% of its customs value. This tariff applies to both insulated and uninsulated wiring. Wiring imported as part of a pre-assembled electrical component (e.g., a motor or appliance) is exempt from this specific tariff. Importers must declare the total length and gauge of wiring in each consignment. Spot checks may be conducted to verify copper content and gauge accuracy. False declarations may lead to confiscation.

heading: Tariff on Imported Ceramic Tiles
text: A tariff of 8 crowns per square meter shall be levied on all imported ceramic floor and wall tiles. This applies to tiles with a surface area greater than 0.01 square meters. Glazed and unglazed tiles are included. Tiles explicitly designed for artistic or decorative installations, and clearly distinguishable as such, may be exempt upon review by customs officials, provided their declared value exceeds 200 crowns per square meter. Commercial consignments of tiles must be accompanied by a certificate of origin. This tariff does not apply to natural stone tiles.

heading: Tariff on Imported Ceramic Tiles
text: A tariff of 10 crowns per square meter shall be levied on all imported ceramic floor and wall tiles. This applies to tiles with a surface area greater than 0.01 square meters. Glazed and unglazed tiles are included. Tiles explicitly designed for artistic or decorative installations, and clearly distinguishable as such, may be exempt upon review by customs officials, provided their declared value exceeds 250 crowns per square meter. Commercial consignments of tiles must be accompanied by a certificate of origin. This tariff does not apply to natural stone tiles.

heading: Tariff on Imported Adhesives
text: Imported construction-grade adhesives, including tile adhesives, wood glues, and sealants, sold in containers exceeding 1 liter or 1 kilogram, shall be subject to a tariff of 5% of their customs value. Smaller containers are exempt. Adhesives certified for medical or scientific research purposes are also exempt, provided appropriate documentation is presented. Importers must declare the chemical composition of the adhesive if requested by customs for classification purposes. This tariff specifically targets products intended for structural or semi-structural applications.

heading: Tariff on Imported Fasteners
text: A tariff of 10% shall be applied to imported metal fasteners, including screws, bolts, nuts, and washers, exceeding 6 millimeters in length. This tariff is based on the customs value of the fasteners. Fasteners made from stainless steel are subject to a lower tariff of 7%, provided material certification is supplied. Bulk imports exceeding 100 kilograms are subject to random testing for material composition. Any discrepancy in declared material may lead to reclassification and additional tariffs as per section 28. This tariff does not apply to decorative fasteners.

heading: Tariff on Imported Paint
text: Imported construction-grade paint, primer, and varnish, sold in containers exceeding 5 liters, shall be subject to a tariff of 3 crowns per liter. Smaller containers are exempt. Paints certified as low-VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) according to Nordvale's national standards are eligible for a 50% reduction in this tariff, upon submission of valid certification. Importers must declare the exact volume in liters for all paint products. Customs may take samples to verify VOC content if the low-VOC reduction is claimed. This tariff applies to both water-based and oil-based paints.

heading: Tariff on Imported Paint
text: Imported construction-grade paint, primer, and varnish, sold in containers exceeding 3 liters, shall be subject to a tariff of 4 crowns per liter. Smaller containers are exempt. Paints certified as low-VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) according to Nordvale's national standards are eligible for a 40% reduction in this tariff, upon submission of valid certification. Importers must declare the exact volume in liters for all paint products. Customs may take samples to verify VOC content if the low-VOC reduction is claimed. This tariff applies to both water-based and oil-based paints.

heading: Tariff on Imported Sand and Gravel
text: A tariff of 2 crowns per metric ton shall be applied to imported construction-grade sand, gravel, and crushed stone. This tariff is levied on all bulk shipments exceeding 10 metric tons. Smaller quantities are exempt. Importers must provide a geological certification indicating the origin and composition of the aggregates. Aggregates found to contain more than 5% organic matter will be subject to an additional 1 crown per metric ton tariff. This measure aims to prevent the import of low-quality materials that could compromise construction integrity. The tariff applies to both natural and recycled aggregates.

heading: Tariff on Imported Asbestos-Free Boards
text: Imported asbestos-free fiber cement boards, with a thickness of 6 millimeters or greater, shall be subject to a tariff of 0.3 crowns per square meter. Importers must provide a certificate explicitly stating the absence of asbestos. Boards found to contain any trace of asbestos will be immediately impounded and destroyed at the importer's expense, in addition to severe penalties as detailed in section 29. Regular spot checks and laboratory analyses will be conducted to ensure compliance. This measure is paramount for public safety and health protection.

heading: Exemptions for Public Projects
text: Materials imported directly by or on behalf of the Nordvale National Infrastructure Agency for approved public works projects are exempt from all tariffs imposed by this Act. This exemption applies only to projects exceeding 10 million crowns in value and specifically designated as national priority projects by the Ministry of Construction. Documentation from the National Infrastructure Agency, signed by its director, must be presented at the point of import. The exemption is not transferable and applies solely to materials consumed within the scope of the approved project.

heading: Exemptions for Research and Development
text: Construction materials imported by certified research institutions for the sole purpose of research and development into innovative building techniques or materials are exempt from tariffs. This exemption requires prior approval from the Ministry of Innovation and Technology, with a detailed research proposal outlining the necessity for imported materials. The quantity of exempted material is limited to that reasonably required for experimental purposes, not exceeding 500 kilograms or 100 square meters per project. Any commercial use of such materials will result in retroactive tariff application.

heading: Declaration Requirements
text: All importers must submit a detailed declaration for each consignment of construction materials, specifying the type, quantity, origin, and customs value of goods. Declarations must be submitted electronically at least 48 hours prior to the estimated arrival of the shipment. Failure to submit a timely or accurate declaration may result in delays in customs clearance and administrative fees of 500 crowns per day of delay, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns. Customs officials have the authority to request additional supporting documentation at any time.

heading: Valuation of Goods
text: The customs value of imported goods shall be determined in accordance with generally accepted international valuation principles. This typically means the transaction value, which is the price actually paid or payable for the goods when sold for export to Nordvale. If the transaction value cannot be determined, alternative methods, such as the value of identical or similar goods, or deductive value, may be applied. Customs officials may request invoices, contracts, and payment records to verify the declared value. Under-valuation exceeding 10% may incur penalties.

heading: Payment of Tariffs
text: Tariffs levied under this Act are payable in Nordvale crowns to the Customs Authority within 10 working days of the official assessment notice. Interest will accrue on overdue payments at a rate of 1% per month, compounded monthly. Failure to pay tariffs within 30 days may result in the impoundment of goods and, ultimately, their auction to recover outstanding duties. Importers are responsible for ensuring that all necessary funds are available by the due date. The Customs Authority will issue a receipt for all tariff payments made.

heading: Refunds and Adjustments
text: Importers may apply for a refund or adjustment of tariffs paid if they can demonstrate that an error occurred in the calculation or assessment. Applications for refunds must be submitted within 90 days of the tariff payment date, accompanied by all relevant documentation. The Customs Authority will review applications within 60 days and issue a decision. False claims for refunds will result in severe penalties, including a fine equal to three times the claimed refund amount and potential criminal charges as detailed in section 29.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any importer dissatisfied with a tariff assessment or a refund decision may appeal to the Tariff Review Board within 30 days of receiving the official decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for the appeal and providing supporting evidence. The Tariff Review Board, comprising three independent experts appointed by the Ministry of Finance, will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 90 days. The decision of the Tariff Review Board is binding on all parties involved. A non-refundable fee of 2,000 crowns applies to all appeals.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to have deliberately under-declared the value or quantity of imported goods, or to have misrepresented their nature or origin, shall be subject to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns or three times the evaded tariff amount, whichever is greater.
(2) Repeated offenses within a 24-month period may result in a temporary ban on importing construction materials into Nordvale for a period of up to 12 months. Serious offenses, such as the import of prohibited materials or gross negligence, may lead to criminal prosecution and imprisonment for up to 5 years.
(3) The Customs Authority has the right to seize and auction any goods involved in serious non-compliance to recover unpaid tariffs and penalties. Proceeds from the auction, after deducting all costs, will be used to offset outstanding liabilities.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Importers are required to maintain detailed records of all import transactions, including invoices, customs declarations, payment receipts, and any relevant certifications, for a period of at least 7 years from the date of import. These records must be made available for inspection by the Customs Authority upon request. Failure to produce requested records within 14 days may result in an administrative fine of 10,000 crowns. Incomplete or fraudulently altered records will be treated as an act of non-compliance, subject to penalties under section 28.

heading: Review of Tariff Rates
text: The Ministry of Finance, in consultation with the Ministry of Construction, shall conduct a comprehensive review of all tariff rates imposed by this Act every 3 years. The review will assess the impact of tariffs on domestic industry, consumer prices, and government revenue. Public input will be invited as part of this review process, with a minimum 60-day public consultation period. Any proposed adjustments to tariff rates will be published in the Official Gazette at least 90 days before their effective date, allowing importers sufficient time to adapt. The next review is scheduled for 2027.

heading: Review of Tariff Rates
text: The Ministry of Finance, in consultation with the Ministry of Construction, shall conduct a comprehensive review of all tariff rates imposed by this Act every 2 years. The review will assess the impact of tariffs on domestic industry, consumer prices, and government revenue. Public input will be invited as part of this review process, with a minimum 45-day public consultation period. Any proposed adjustments to tariff rates will be published in the Official Gazette at least 75 days before their effective date, allowing importers sufficient time to adapt. The next review is scheduled for 2028.

heading: Designated Ports of Entry
text: All commercial imports of construction materials subject to tariffs under this Act must enter Nordvale through designated ports of entry. These ports are currently Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. Imports through any other port will be subject to immediate impoundment and may incur additional processing fees of up to 15,000 crowns. The Ministry of Transport, in coordination with the Customs Authority, may update the list of designated ports by issuing a public notice at least 30 days in advance. Information on designated ports is available on the Customs Authority website.

heading: Cooperation with Other Agencies
text:
(1) The Customs Authority shall cooperate with other relevant government agencies, including the National Quality Standards Agency and the Environmental Protection Department, to ensure compliance with all applicable regulations concerning imported construction materials.
(2) This cooperation may involve sharing information, conducting joint inspections, and enforcing regulations. For example, if materials are suspected of failing environmental standards, the Environmental Protection Department may be notified within 24 hours for further investigation.
(3) Such collaboration aims to create a streamlined and effective enforcement regime, minimizing redundant checks and maximizing regulatory oversight across all relevant domains. This ensures imported goods meet all national requirements, not just those related to tariffs.

heading: Special categories
text: Each registered seed bank curator receives an additional 30 days to pay any fee or allowance due under FDA §14.

heading: Recognised trades
text: A registered cartographer shall pay an annual registration fee of 22 crowns and 50 øre for an electric cargo bicycle.

heading: Schooling levy for pupils of mutual tenure members
text:
(1) Where a periodic schooling levy is chargeable for a pupil whose parent is a mutual tenure member, the levy is the amount in Schedule N, category N2.
(2) Where no levy may be charged for the pupil, this section does not create one.
(3) This amount takes the place of any other relief from that charge; where another provision leads to a smaller amount, only the smaller amount is payable.

heading: Established members and one enrolment each year
text:
(1) An established mutual tenure member pays no continuing-learning enrolment charge for the first enrolment in each calendar year.
(2) For that enrolment this exemption takes the place of any other relief. Later enrolments in the same year are charged as they would be charged for any other mutual tenure member.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the installation, operation, and maintenance of cable networks within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all entities, whether private or public, seeking to establish or expand cable infrastructure across public or private lands. The primary purpose is to ensure the orderly deployment of these networks, minimize disruption to public spaces, protect existing infrastructure, and promote fair access to connectivity. This Act covers all types of cable networks, including but not limited to those for telecommunications, data transmission, and broadcast services, and mandates specific permits for various activities related to their lifecycle.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall install, operate, or substantially alter any cable network within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Nordvale Communications Authority (hereinafter referred to as 'the Authority'). This requirement applies to new installations, extensions of existing networks exceeding 50 meters in length, and any modifications that involve excavation or significant changes to the network's physical footprint. Failure to secure the necessary permit before commencing work shall result in immediate cessation of activities and potential fines, as detailed in section 35.

heading: Application submission
text: Applications for a cable network permit must be submitted to the Authority in writing, using the prescribed forms available on the Authority's official website. Each application must include a detailed project plan, a map illustrating the proposed network route with a scale of 1:500 or greater, evidence of land access rights for private property, and a non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days, requiring resubmission with all missing documentation.

heading: Application submission
text: Applications for a cable network permit must be submitted to the Authority electronically via the dedicated online portal, using the prescribed digital forms.
