(1) Every licensed crematorium must establish a clear and accessible procedure for receiving and addressing public complaints. 
(2) All complaints must be logged, investigated promptly, and a written response provided to the complainant within 14 days of receipt. 
(3) A summary of all complaints and their resolutions must be included in the annual report submitted to the Minister. The Minister reserves the right to review any complaint and may initiate an independent investigation if deemed necessary. Repeated unresolved complaints, exceeding five in a 12-month period, may lead to an official warning and potential penalties under section 11.

heading: Public Complaints
text:
(1) Every licensed crematorium must establish a clear and accessible procedure for receiving and addressing public complaints.
(2) All complaints must be logged, investigated promptly, and a written response provided to the complainant within 7 days of receipt. A copy of the complaint and the resolution must also be submitted to the Ministry within 14 days.
(3) A summary of all complaints and their resolutions must be included in the annual report submitted to the Minister. The Minister reserves the right to review any complaint and may initiate an independent investigation if deemed necessary. Repeated unresolved complaints, exceeding three in a 12-month period, will lead to an official warning and immediate penalties under section 11, potentially including licence suspension.

heading: Enforcement Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: For a certified ski patroller, the municipality shall pay five crowns in lieu of delivering a hot meal to their home.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a licensed puppeteer registered for at least one year, the household receives fixed broadband support of 5 crowns per month, instead of the standard mobile data subscription support.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements and procedures for the registration of all charitable organisations operating within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure transparency, accountability, and public trust in the charitable sector. All organisations meeting the definition of a charitable organisation as set out in section 2 must register with the Nordvale Charities Commission before commencing any fundraising or programmatic activities within Nordvale. Failure to register may result in penalties as described in section 38 of this Act. This Act applies to all organisations, regardless of their size or the value of their annual donations, provided they solicit contributions from the public.

heading: Definition of Charitable Organisation
text: For the purposes of this Act, a 'charitable organisation' is defined as any non-profit entity established for charitable, philanthropic, religious, educational, humanitarian, or public welfare purposes, and which solicits or receives donations, grants, or other financial contributions from the public or from other entities for these purposes. This definition includes foundations, trusts, and associations that engage in such activities, irrespective of whether they have formal legal incorporation. An organisation is deemed to be 'soliciting' if it makes any public appeal for funds, whether directly or indirectly, through any medium.

heading: Nordvale Charities Commission
text: The Nordvale Charities Commission (hereinafter 'the Commission') is hereby established as the primary regulatory body responsible for overseeing the registration and compliance of charitable organisations. The Commission operates under the authority granted by this Act and is tasked with maintaining a public register of all charitable organisations. It will consist of 5 commissioners appointed by the Minister for Public Services for terms of 4 years. The Commission's headquarters shall be located in Aldmark, and it will maintain regional offices in Brenholt and Corvik to facilitate local interactions. The Commission's decisions are final, subject to the appeal process outlined in section 39.

heading: Application for Registration
text:
(1) Any organisation seeking registration as a charitable organisation must submit a formal application to the Commission.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The organisation's full legal name and any operating names.
(b) Its primary address and contact details, including a valid email address.
(c) A copy of its founding documents, such as a constitution or articles of incorporation.
(d) A detailed description of its charitable purposes and proposed activities.
(e) Names and addresses of all board members or trustees, along with their dates of birth.
(f) A declaration that the organisation will comply with all provisions of this Act.

heading: Application for Registration
text:
(1) Any organisation seeking registration as a charitable organisation must submit a formal application to the Commission.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The organisation's full legal name and any operating names.
(b) Its primary address and contact details, including a valid email address and telephone number.
(c) A copy of its founding documents, such as a constitution or articles of incorporation.
(d) A detailed description of its charitable purposes and proposed activities.
(e) Names and addresses of all board members or trustees, along with their dates of birth and a brief professional biography.
(f) A declaration that the organisation will comply with all provisions of this Act.

heading: Application for Registration
text:
(1) Any organisation seeking registration as a charitable organisation must submit a formal application to the Commission.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The organisation's full legal name and any operating names.
(b) Its primary address and contact details, including a valid email address and telephone number.
(c) A copy of its founding documents, such as a constitution or articles of incorporation.
(d) A detailed description of its charitable purposes and proposed activities, including a projected budget for the first 12 months.
(e) Names and addresses of all board members or trustees, along with their dates of birth, a brief professional biography, and a declaration of any potential conflicts of interest.
(f) A declaration that the organisation will comply with all provisions of this Act.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany every registration application. This fee is intended to cover the administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial background checks. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days. Organisations that resubmit an application must pay the fee again. There are no exemptions from this fee, regardless of the organisation's anticipated annual revenue.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns must accompany every registration application. This fee is intended to cover the administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial background checks. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days. Organisations that resubmit an application must pay the fee again. There are no exemptions from this fee, regardless of the organisation's anticipated annual revenue.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,000 crowns must accompany every registration application. This fee is intended to cover the administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial background checks. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days. Organisations that resubmit an application must pay the fee again. Organisations with projected annual revenues below 10,000 crowns may apply for a 50% reduction in the fee.

heading: Processing of Applications
text: The Commission will review all applications for completeness and compliance with the requirements set out in section 4. The Commission aims to process applications within 60 working days of receipt. If an application is incomplete or requires further information, the Commission will notify the applicant in writing within 30 working days, detailing the deficiencies. The applicant will then have 45 days to provide the requested information. Failure to respond within this period may result in the application being rejected, requiring a new submission and fee.

heading: Registration Criteria
text:
To be eligible for registration, an organisation must demonstrate that:
(a) Its primary purpose is genuinely charitable as defined in section 2.
(b) Its activities are intended for the public benefit within Nordvale or abroad.
(c) It is managed by a board of at least 3 individuals, none of whom have a history of serious financial misconduct.
(d) Its governing documents prohibit the distribution of profits or assets to its members, except for reasonable remuneration for services rendered.
(e) It maintains proper financial records and systems for accountability.

heading: Approval and Issuance of Certificate
text: Upon successful review and satisfaction of all registration criteria, the Commission will approve the application. A certificate of registration, bearing a unique registration number, will be issued to the charitable organisation within 15 working days of approval. This certificate serves as proof of official registration and must be displayed prominently at the organisation's primary place of business. The registration is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance, after which a renewal application must be submitted as detailed in section 12. The certificate will include the organisation's official name, registration number, and date of registration.

heading: Refusal of Registration
text:
(1) The Commission may refuse registration if an organisation fails to meet the criteria specified in section 7 or provides false or misleading information.
(2) If registration is refused, the Commission will provide a written explanation to the applicant within 10 working days of the decision, detailing the reasons for refusal.
(3) An organisation whose application has been refused may appeal the decision as outlined in section 39. A new application can only be submitted after 90 days from the date of refusal, and all identified deficiencies must be addressed.

heading: Public Register
text: The Commission will maintain a public register of all registered charitable organisations. This register will be accessible to the public both online and at the Commission's offices during business hours. The register will include the organisation's name, registration number, primary address, charitable purposes, and the names of its board members or trustees. Certain sensitive personal data of board members, such as full birth dates or personal addresses, will not be disclosed on the public register. The register is updated daily to reflect new registrations, renewals, or revocations.

heading: Annual Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every registered charitable organisation must submit an annual report to the Commission within 6 months of the end of its financial year.
(2) The annual report must include:
(a) Audited financial statements for the preceding financial year.
(b) A report on the organisation's activities and achievements.
(c) A declaration signed by at least two board members confirming compliance with this Act.
(d) Details of all donations received exceeding 10,000 crowns from a single donor. Organisations with annual revenues below 50,000 crowns are exempt from the audit requirement and may submit reviewed financial statements instead.

heading: Annual Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every registered charitable organisation must submit an annual report to the Commission within 5 months of the end of its financial year.
(2) The annual report must include:
(a) Audited financial statements for the preceding financial year.
(b) A report on the organisation's activities and achievements, including an impact assessment.
(c) A declaration signed by at least two board members confirming compliance with this Act.
(d) Details of all donations received exceeding 7,500 crowns from a single donor. Organisations with annual revenues below 75,000 crowns are exempt from the audit requirement and may submit reviewed financial statements instead.

heading: Annual Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every registered charitable organisation must submit an annual report to the Commission within 4 months of the end of its financial year.
(2) The annual report must include:
(a) Audited financial statements for the preceding financial year.
(b) A comprehensive report on the organisation's activities and achievements, including an impact assessment and detailed project expenditures.
(c) A declaration signed by at least two board members confirming compliance with this Act and verifying the accuracy of the submitted information.
(d) Details of all donations received exceeding 5,000 crowns from a single donor. Organisations with annual revenues below 100,000 crowns are exempt from the audit requirement and may submit reviewed financial statements instead.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text:
(1) Registration must be renewed every 3 years. An organisation must submit a renewal application at least 60 days before its current registration expires.
(2) The renewal application must include:
(a) An updated list of board members.
(b) Confirmation of any changes to the organisation's governing documents or charitable purposes.
(c) Payment of a renewal fee of 300 crowns.
(d) A declaration affirming continued compliance with all provisions of this Act.
(3) Failure to renew within the specified period may result in the lapse of registration and potential penalties.

heading: Renewal Fee
text: A renewal fee of 300 crowns is payable with each renewal application. This fee contributes to the ongoing administrative costs of maintaining the public register and ensuring compliance. The fee is non-refundable. If an organisation fails to pay the renewal fee by the due date, an additional late fee of 150 crowns will be applied for every month or part thereof that the fee remains unpaid, up to a maximum of 3 months. After this period, the registration will be automatically revoked as per section 14.

heading: Renewal Fee
text: A renewal fee of 450 crowns is payable with each renewal application. This fee contributes to the ongoing administrative costs of maintaining the public register and ensuring compliance. The fee is non-refundable. If an organisation fails to pay the renewal fee by the due date, an additional late fee of 200 crowns will be applied for every month or part thereof that the fee remains unpaid, up to a maximum of 2 months. After this period, the registration will be automatically revoked as per section 14.

heading: Revocation of Registration
text:
(1) The Commission may revoke an organisation's registration if it:
(a) Fails to comply with annual reporting requirements for more than 12 months.
(b) Fails to renew its registration within 90 days of expiry.
(c) Is found to be engaging in activities inconsistent with its charitable purposes.
(d) Provides false or misleading information to the Commission.
(e) Is found to be operating for private gain.
(2) The Commission will notify the organisation in writing of its intention to revoke registration, providing at least 30 days' notice and an opportunity to rectify the breach.

heading: Voluntary Deregistration
text:
(1) A charitable organisation may voluntarily deregister by submitting a written request to the Commission.
(2) The request must include:
(a) A statement confirming the organisation has ceased all charitable activities.
(b) Details of how its remaining assets have been or will be distributed to other registered charitable organisations.
(c) A final financial report.
(3) The Commission will review the request and, if satisfied, will remove the organisation from the public register within 45 days. Deregistered organisations cannot use the term 'registered charitable organisation'.

heading: Changes to Organisational Details
text:
Registered charitable organisations must notify the Commission of any significant changes to their organisational details within 30 days of such changes occurring. Significant changes include, but are not limited to, changes in:
(a) The organisation's name or primary address.
(b) Its charitable purposes or main activities.
(c) Its governing documents.
(d) The composition of its board of trustees or directors.
Failure to notify the Commission of these changes within the stipulated timeframe may result in a fine of 500 crowns as per section 37.

heading: Financial Transparency
text: All registered charitable organisations must maintain transparent financial records, adhering to generally accepted accounting principles. These records must clearly show all income and expenditure, including the source of donations and the application of funds to charitable activities. Financial records must be retained for a minimum of 7 years. The Commission may request access to these records at any time to verify compliance with this Act. Public access to annual financial statements, as submitted to the Commission, must be provided upon reasonable request from any member of the public.

heading: Use of Funds
text: Funds received by a charitable organisation must be used exclusively for its stated charitable purposes. A maximum of 25% of annual income may be allocated to administrative and fundraising costs. Any deviation from this principle, such as using funds for personal enrichment or non-charitable ventures, is strictly prohibited and constitutes a serious breach of this Act. The Commission has the authority to investigate any suspected misuse of funds and impose sanctions, including the recovery of misapplied assets, as outlined in section 38.

heading: Use of Funds
text: Funds received by a charitable organisation must be used exclusively for its stated charitable purposes. A maximum of 20% of annual income may be allocated to administrative and fundraising costs. Any deviation from this principle, such as using funds for personal enrichment or non-charitable ventures, is strictly prohibited and constitutes a serious breach of this Act. The Commission has the authority to investigate any suspected misuse of funds and impose sanctions, including the recovery of misapplied assets, as outlined in section 38. Exceptions to the percentage limit may be granted for new organisations in their first 2 years of operation, up to 35%.

heading: Donation Receipts
text: Registered charitable organisations must issue official receipts for all donations received that exceed 100 crowns. These receipts must include the organisation's name and registration number, the donor's name, the amount of the donation, and the date it was received. Receipts must be provided within 14 days of receiving the donation. For smaller donations below 100 crowns, a consolidated annual statement may be issued if requested by the donor. Failure to issue proper receipts may lead to fines for non-compliance as detailed in section 37.

heading: Donation Receipts
text: Registered charitable organisations must issue official receipts for all donations received that exceed 50 crowns. These receipts must include the organisation's name and registration number, the donor's name, the amount of the donation, and the date it was received. Receipts must be provided within 10 days of receiving the donation. For smaller donations below 50 crowns, a consolidated annual statement may be issued if requested by the donor. Failure to issue proper receipts may lead to fines for non-compliance as detailed in section 37.

heading: Fundraising Practices
text: All fundraising activities conducted by or on behalf of a registered charitable organisation must be ethical, transparent, and respectful. Organizations must clearly identify themselves as a registered charity and provide their registration number when soliciting funds. Coercive or misleading fundraising practices are strictly prohibited. Organisations must ensure that any third-party fundraisers they employ also comply with these standards. A minimum of 70% of gross proceeds from any fundraising campaign must directly benefit the charitable purpose, with a maximum of 30% allocated to fundraising costs. Campaigns must clearly state this ratio if it differs.

heading: Public Solicitation
text: Organisations engaging in public solicitation, such as door-to-door campaigns or street collections, must obtain a permit from the local municipal authority in which the solicitation occurs. This permit is separate from their charitable registration. Solicitation permits are typically valid for 30 days and cost 100 crowns. The municipality will verify the organisation's registration status with the Commission before issuing any permit. Collectors must carry identification and a copy of the permit. Collection bins must be clearly marked with the organisation's name and registration number.

heading: Public Solicitation
text: Organisations engaging in public solicitation, such as door-to-door campaigns or street collections, must obtain a permit from the local municipal authority in which the solicitation occurs. This permit is separate from their charitable registration. Solicitation permits are typically valid for 20 days and cost 150 crowns. The municipality will verify the organisation's registration status with the Commission before issuing any permit. Collectors must carry identification and a copy of the permit, and display their individual collector ID number prominently. Collection bins must be clearly marked with the organisation's name, registration number, and contact information.

heading: Board Member Eligibility
text:
(1) Individuals serving on the board of a registered charitable organisation must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) They must not have been convicted of any felony or a crime involving fraud or dishonesty within the past 10 years.
(3) They must not be an undischarged bankrupt.
(4) At least 50% of board members must reside in Nordvale.
(5) The Commission may request background checks on all board members as part of the registration or renewal process. Failure to meet these criteria may result in disqualification and subsequent refusal or revocation of registration.

heading: Conflicts of Interest
text:
(1) Board members and employees of registered charitable organisations must disclose any potential or actual conflicts of interest to the board.
(2) A conflict of interest arises when a board member or employee has a personal or financial stake in a transaction or decision involving the organisation.
(3) Conflicted individuals must recuse themselves from discussions and decisions related to the conflict. All conflicts of interest, and how they were managed, must be documented in the organisation's minutes. Failure to disclose or manage conflicts appropriately may lead to disciplinary action by the Commission.

heading: Indemnification of Board Members
text: A charitable organisation may indemnify its board members against liabilities incurred in the performance of their duties, provided they acted in good faith and in the best interests of the organisation. Indemnification does not extend to acts of gross negligence, willful misconduct, or actions that are outside the scope of the organisation's charitable purposes. Any such indemnification must be explicitly stated in the organisation's governing documents. The total amount of indemnification payments made in a single year cannot exceed 10,000 crowns without prior approval from the Commission.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All registered charitable organisations must maintain adequate liability insurance to protect against claims arising from their operations. The minimum coverage required is 1,000,000 crowns for general liability. Organisations engaging in specific high-risk activities may be required by the Commission to hold additional or higher levels of insurance coverage. Proof of insurance must be submitted to the Commission upon request. Failure to maintain adequate insurance may result in a temporary suspension of activities until the requirement is met, followed by fines if non-compliance persists for more than 60 days.

heading: Record Keeping
text: In addition to financial records, charitable organisations must maintain comprehensive records of their activities, including minutes of board meetings, donor lists, project documentation, and employee records. All records must be kept in a secure manner and readily accessible for inspection by the Commission for a period of at least 7 years. Electronic records are permissible, provided they are backed up regularly and can be produced in a readable format upon request. Confidential donor information must be protected in accordance with privacy laws.

heading: Investigation Powers
text:
(1) The Commission has the power to investigate any registered charitable organisation if there are reasonable grounds to suspect non-compliance with this Act.
(2) Investigations may include:
(a) Demanding access to all records and documents.
(b) Interviewing board members, employees, and volunteers.
(c) Inspecting premises.
(3) Organisations must cooperate fully with any investigation. Obstruction of an investigation is a serious offense and may lead to immediate revocation of registration and legal penalties. The Commission must provide a written notice of investigation at least 7 days before commencing.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: The Commission and its staff must treat all confidential information obtained during the registration process or investigations with strict confidentiality. This includes, but is not limited to, sensitive financial details, personal information of donors (where not publicly disclosed), and proprietary operational methods. Information may only be disclosed if required by law, court order, or with the express written consent of the organisation concerned. Breaches of confidentiality by Commission staff may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

heading: Reporting of Misconduct
text: Any person or entity with reasonable grounds to suspect misconduct or non-compliance by a registered charitable organisation may report such concerns to the Commission. Reports can be made anonymously, but the Commission may give greater weight to reports that include verifiable details and contact information for follow-up. All reports of misconduct will be assessed by the Commission within 14 days, and serious allegations will trigger an investigation as described in section 26. Whistleblowers are protected from retaliation as per the Nordvale Public Interest Disclosure Act.

heading: Dissolution of Organisations
text:
(1) If a registered charitable organisation decides to dissolve, it must notify the Commission at least 90 days prior to the proposed dissolution date.
(2) The notification must include a plan for the distribution of its remaining assets to other registered charitable organisations with similar charitable purposes.
(3) Assets cannot be distributed to individual members, directors, or for any non-charitable purpose. The Commission must approve the dissolution plan before assets are distributed. A final report, including audited financial statements up to the date of dissolution, must be submitted within 60 days of asset distribution.

heading: Dissolution of Organisations
text:
(1) If a registered charitable organisation decides to dissolve, it must notify the Commission at least 120 days prior to the proposed dissolution date.
(2) The notification must include a detailed plan for the distribution of its remaining assets to at least two other registered charitable organisations with similar charitable purposes. This plan must also specify how any liabilities will be settled.
(3) Assets cannot be distributed to individual members, directors, or for any non-charitable purpose. The Commission must approve the dissolution plan before assets are distributed. A final report, including audited financial statements up to the date of dissolution, must be submitted within 45 days of asset distribution.

heading: Mergers and Amalgamations
text:
(1) Any proposed merger or amalgamation of a registered charitable organisation with another entity must be approved by the Commission.
(2) An application for approval must be submitted at least 60 days before the proposed effective date of the merger or amalgamation.
(3) The application must demonstrate that the merged entity will continue to meet all registration criteria and that the charitable assets of the merging organisations will be protected and used for charitable purposes. The Commission will assess whether the proposed structure maintains or enhances public benefit.

heading: Foreign Charitable Organisations
text: Charitable organisations established outside of Nordvale but operating or soliciting funds within Nordvale must register with the Commission. They are subject to all provisions of this Act, with the following additional requirements: they must designate a primary representative residing in Nordvale, provide documentation verifying their charitable status in their home jurisdiction, and submit financial statements audited according to international accounting standards. Failure to comply with these provisions will result in the inability to solicit or receive funds from Nordvale residents or entities. The application fee for foreign organisations is 1,000 crowns.

heading: Foreign Charitable Organisations
text: Charitable organisations established outside of Nordvale but operating or soliciting funds within Nordvale must register with the Commission. They are subject to all provisions of this Act, with the following additional requirements: they must designate a primary representative residing in Nordvale, provide documentation verifying their charitable status in their home jurisdiction, and submit financial statements audited according to international accounting standards. Failure to comply with these provisions will result in the inability to solicit or receive funds from Nordvale residents or entities. The application fee for foreign organisations is 1,500 crowns, and an additional annual compliance fee of 500 crowns is required.

heading: Municipal Cooperation
text: The Commission will cooperate with municipal authorities across Nordvale to ensure effective oversight of charitable activities. This cooperation includes sharing information regarding registered organisations, investigating local complaints, and coordinating on public solicitation permits. Municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, are required to verify the registration status of any organisation claiming charitable status before granting local permits or concessions. The Commission will provide municipalities with access to the public register and a dedicated contact for inquiries.

heading: Data Protection
text: All registered charitable organisations must comply with Nordvale's data protection laws concerning the collection, storage, and processing of personal data, including donor information and beneficiary data. Organisations must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to safeguard personal data against unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. Donors must be informed about how their data will be used and have the right to request deletion of their personal information. The Commission may audit an organisation's data protection practices to ensure compliance, with non-compliance leading to fines of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Use of 'Registered Charity' Title
text: Only organisations officially registered with the Nordvale Charities Commission may use the title 'Registered Charitable Organisation' or any similar designation implying official recognition. This includes the use of a registered charity number on all official documents, websites, and fundraising materials. Unregistered entities found to be using this title will be subject to a penalty of 2,000 crowns for each instance of misuse. The Commission actively monitors for such misrepresentations and will pursue legal action where necessary to protect the integrity of the charitable sector.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Organisations that do not solicit funds from the public and whose annual income is solely derived from internal membership fees, government grants, or a single foundational grant exceeding 500,000 crowns are exempt from registration.
(2) Religious congregations primarily for worship purposes, provided they do not engage in extensive public fundraising beyond their direct congregants, are also exempt.
(3) These exemptions do not apply if an organisation engages in any form of public appeal for donations, regardless of the amount. Exempt organisations cannot use the title 'Registered Charitable Organisation'.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Organisations that do not solicit funds from the public and whose annual income is solely derived from internal membership fees, government grants, or a single foundational grant exceeding 750,000 crowns are exempt from registration.
(2) Religious congregations primarily for worship purposes, provided they do not engage in extensive public fundraising beyond their direct congregants or receive public donations exceeding 25,000 crowns annually, are also exempt.
(3) These exemptions do not apply if an organisation engages in any form of public appeal for donations, regardless of the amount. Exempt organisations cannot use the title 'Registered Charitable Organisation'.

heading: Administrative Fines
text: The Commission may impose administrative fines for minor breaches of this Act. These fines range from 1,000 crowns to 10,000 crowns, depending on the severity and frequency of the breach. Examples of minor breaches include late submission of annual reports (after the grace period), failure to notify changes in organisational details within 30 days, or minor inaccuracies in submitted documentation. Organisations will be given 30 days to pay the fine. Repeated minor breaches may lead to more severe penalties, including suspension or revocation of registration.

heading: Administrative Fines
text: The Commission may impose administrative fines for minor breaches of this Act. These fines range from 1,500 crowns to 15,000 crowns, depending on the severity and frequency of the breach. Examples of minor breaches include late submission of annual reports (after the grace period), failure to notify changes in organisational details within 20 days, or minor inaccuracies in submitted documentation. Organisations will be given 20 days to pay the fine. Repeated minor breaches may lead to more severe penalties, including suspension or revocation of registration. Fines may be increased by 20% for each repeated offense within a 24-month period.

heading: Penalties for Serious Breaches
text:
Serious breaches of this Act, such as operating for private gain, gross misuse of charitable funds, or repeated non-compliance after warnings, may result in severe penalties. These include:
(a) Revocation of registration and permanent ban from re-registration.
(b) Fines up to 100,000 crowns.
(c) Referral to legal authorities for criminal prosecution, particularly in cases of fraud or embezzlement.
(d) Disqualification of board members from serving on any charitable board for a period of up to 10 years. The Commission will always aim to recover misapplied funds and assets.

heading: Penalties for Serious Breaches
text:
Serious breaches of this Act, such as operating for private gain, gross misuse of charitable funds, or repeated non-compliance after warnings, may result in severe penalties. These include:
(a) Revocation of registration and permanent ban from re-registration.
(b) Fines up to 250,000 crowns.
(c) Referral to legal authorities for criminal prosecution, particularly in cases of fraud or embezzlement.
(d) Disqualification of board members from serving on any charitable board for a period of up to 15 years. The Commission will always aim to recover misapplied funds and assets and may initiate civil proceedings for their recovery.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An organisation may appeal a decision by the Commission to refuse or revoke registration, or to impose a significant fine exceeding 10,000 crowns.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Commission's decision.
(3) The Appeals Tribunal, an independent body, will review the case based on the evidence presented and make a final determination within 60 days. The Tribunal's decision is binding. The Tribunal consists of 3 legal professionals appointed by the Nordvale High Court.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act will be reviewed by the Minister for Public Services every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance to the charitable sector in Nordvale. The first review will take place no later than 2023-12-31. Public consultations will be held during the review process, allowing registered charitable organisations, donors, and other stakeholders to provide feedback. Any proposed amendments or updates resulting from the review will be presented to the Nordvale Parliament for consideration and legislative action. The Commission will also submit a report on the Act's implementation and impact.

heading: Crew rolls of lifeboat stations
text:
(1) Every lifeboat station shall keep a crew roll listing every volunteer who goes to sea on its lifeboats, with the date on which each volunteer was entered on the roll.
(2) Wherever an Act gives a relief to an "active rescue volunteer", that expression means a person who has been on the crew roll of a lifeboat station for at least 2 years and who took part in at least 12 call-outs or training exercises of that station in the previous calendar year.
(3) A helper who launches or recovers a lifeboat from the shore but does not go to sea is not entered on the crew roll.
(4) The station shall give each person on the crew roll a yearly statement of the call-outs and training exercises in which he or she took part.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act protects consumers who buy goods and services from traders in Nordvale.
(2) A consumer is a person who buys for purposes outside their trade or profession.
(3) It applies to every sale by a trader to a consumer, in a shop, at a door or at a distance.

heading: Price display
text:
(1) A trader shall show the total price, including all taxes and charges, of every product offered to consumers.
(2) A price shown shall be the price the consumer pays at the till.
(3) A trader shall show the price per kilogram or per litre for goods sold by weight or volume.

heading: Right to cancel a distance purchase
text:
(1) A consumer who buys goods at a distance may cancel the purchase within 14 days of receiving the goods.
(2) The consumer need not give a reason.
(3) The consumer pays the cost of returning the goods unless the trader agreed to pay it.

heading: Right to cancel a distance purchase
text:
(1) A consumer who buys goods at a distance may cancel the purchase within 21 days of receiving the goods.
(2) The consumer need not give a reason.
(3) The consumer pays the cost of returning the goods unless the trader agreed to pay it.

heading: Refund after cancellation
text:
(1) The trader shall refund the price within 30 days of receiving the returned goods.
(2) The refund shall be made by the same means of payment the consumer used.
(3) The trader may refuse a refund for goods that are damaged by use beyond testing.

heading: Refund after cancellation
text:
(1) The trader shall refund the price within 14 days of receiving the returned goods.
(2) The refund shall be made by the same means of payment the consumer used.
(3) The trader may refuse a refund for goods that are damaged by use beyond testing.

heading: Faulty goods
text:
(1) The trader is responsible for a fault in goods that existed when the goods were handed over.
(2) The trader's responsibility lasts for 2 years from the day the goods were handed over.
(3) The consumer shall tell the trader of the fault within 2 months of finding it.

heading: Repair or replacement
text:
(1) A consumer who receives faulty goods may ask for repair or replacement.
(2) The trader shall carry out the repair or replacement within 30 days of the request.
(3) The repair or replacement shall be free of charge to the consumer.

heading: Presumption of a fault
text:
(1) A fault that appears within 6 months of handing over is presumed to have existed when the goods were handed over.
(2) The trader may rebut the presumption by proving that the fault was caused by the consumer.

heading: Presumption of a fault
text:
(1) A fault that appears within 12 months of handing over is presumed to have existed when the goods were handed over.
(2) The trader may rebut the presumption by proving that the fault was caused by the consumer.

heading: Gift cards
text:
(1) A gift card shall be valid for at least 24 months from the day it is sold.
(2) A trader shall not charge a fee for the use of a gift card.
(3) The expiry date shall be printed on the gift card.

heading: Unfair terms
text:
(1) A term in a consumer contract that has not been individually negotiated and that creates a significant imbalance to the consumer's disadvantage is not binding.
(2) The rest of the contract remains in force.
(3) A term printed in unusually small letters is presumed to be unfair.

heading: Deposits
text:
(1) A trader shall not ask for a deposit of more than 20 percent of the price of goods ordered.
(2) A deposit shall be refunded in full if the trader fails to deliver.
(3) The trader shall give the consumer a receipt for the deposit.

heading: Door-to-door sales
text:
(1) A consumer who signs a contract at home or at work may cancel it within 10 days.
(2) The trader shall give the consumer a written cancellation form at the time of signing.
(3) The trader shall not take any payment before the 10 days have passed.

heading: Product recalls
text:
(1) A trader who learns that a product is dangerous shall tell the authority within 7 days.
(2) The trader shall tell known buyers of the product how to return it.
(3) The trader shall refund the full price of a recalled product.

heading: Fine for misleading advertising
text:
(1) A trader who advertises in a way that misleads consumers shall pay a fine of 1000 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) The authority may also order the trader to publish a correction.

heading: Fine for misleading advertising
text:
(1) A trader who advertises in a way that misleads consumers shall pay a fine of 1200 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) The authority may also order the trader to publish a correction.

heading: Sale price reference
text:
(1) A trader who advertises a reduced price shall also show the lowest price charged in the previous 30 days.
(2) The reduction shall be calculated from that lowest price.
(3) A reduction that is not calculated under subsection (2) is misleading.

heading: Delivery time
text:
(1) A trader shall deliver goods within the time agreed with the consumer.
(2) If no time was agreed, the trader shall deliver within 30 days of the order.
(3) A consumer may cancel the order if the trader does not deliver after a further reasonable period of 7 days.

heading: Subscriptions
text:
(1) A consumer may end a subscription contract with 1 month's notice.
(2) A trader shall remind the consumer at least 14 days before an automatic renewal.
(3) A renewal without such a reminder may be cancelled by the consumer without charge.

heading: Complaint handling
text:
(1) A trader shall answer a written consumer complaint within 21 days.
(2) The answer shall state whether the complaint is accepted and what the trader will do.
(3) A trader who does not answer in time is treated as having refused the complaint.

heading: Consumer board fee
text:
(1) A consumer who brings a dispute to the Consumer Board shall pay a fee of 25 crowns.
(2) The fee is refunded if the consumer wins the dispute.
(3) The Board decides a dispute within 90 days.

heading: Consumer board fee
text:
(1) A consumer who brings a dispute to the Consumer Board shall pay a fee of 35 crowns.
(2) The fee is refunded if the consumer wins the dispute.
(3) The Board decides a dispute within 90 days.

heading: Warranty information
text:
(1) A trader who gives a voluntary warranty shall state its length and conditions in writing.
(2) A voluntary warranty does not reduce the rights of a consumer under section 5.
(3) The warranty shall be written in plain language.

heading: Instalment sales register
text:
(1) A trader who sells goods in instalments shall record the contract in the instalment sales register.
(2) Registration costs 15 crowns for each contract.
(3) The trader shall give the consumer a copy of the register entry within 7 days.
(4) A contract that is not recorded may be cancelled by the consumer within 30 days of signing.

heading: Instalment sales register
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Language courses for newly arrived residents
text:
(1) A newly arrived resident pays half of the fee for an adult course in a foreign language run by a municipality.
(2) The reduction applies to one course in each calendar year.
(3) The reduction is applied to the fee for a classroom course and also to the fee for the same course offered online.

heading: Dental check-up for new residents
text:
(1) A person whose first registration as resident in a municipality of Nordvale took place less than 12 months earlier pays no fee for one dental check-up.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time does not benefit from subsection (1).

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the maximum timeframes allowed for the completion of various construction projects across the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure timely development, minimize public disruption, and promote efficient use of resources within the construction sector. It applies to all new construction, major renovations, and infrastructure projects requiring permits from municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act does not cover minor repairs or projects not requiring a municipal construction permit, nor does it override specific emergency provisions enacted by a municipal council in extraordinary circumstances.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Construction Project' means any undertaking involving the erection, alteration, or demolition of structures, or significant civil engineering works, requiring a permit from a municipal authority.
(2) 'Start Date' means the date on which the first foundation work commences or 30 days after the issuance of the construction permit, whichever is earlier.
(3) 'Completion Date' means the date on which the final inspection certificate is issued by the relevant municipal authority, confirming that the project meets all regulatory standards.
(4) 'Large Project' refers to any construction project with an estimated cost exceeding 5,000,000 crowns or a total floor area greater than 2,000 square meters.
(5) 'Small Project' refers to any construction project with an estimated cost below 1,000,000 crowns and a total floor area less than 300 square meters.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Construction Project' means any undertaking involving the erection, alteration, or demolition of structures, or significant civil engineering works, requiring a permit from a municipal authority.
(2) 'Start Date' means the date on which the first foundation work commences or 45 days after the issuance of the construction permit, whichever is earlier.
(3) 'Completion Date' means the date on which the final inspection certificate is issued by the relevant municipal authority, confirming that the project meets all regulatory standards.
(4) 'Large Project' refers to any construction project with an estimated cost exceeding 7,500,000 crowns or a total floor area greater than 2,500 square meters.
(5) 'Small Project' refers to any construction project with an estimated cost below 1,500,000 crowns and a total floor area less than 400 square meters.

heading: Residential dwellings (single-family)
text: The maximum allowable timeframe for the completion of a new single-family residential dwelling is 365 days from the Start Date. This period includes all phases of construction, from excavation to the final interior finishes and landscaping deemed essential for occupancy. Failure to meet this deadline may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. An extension of up to 90 days may be granted by the municipal authority under exceptional circumstances, such as severe weather events lasting more than 21 days or unforeseen material shortages verified by at least two independent suppliers.

heading: Residential dwellings (multi-unit)
text: For multi-unit residential buildings containing fewer than 15 units, the maximum completion timeframe is 540 days from the Start Date. This includes all common areas, individual units, and associated outdoor amenities. Projects with 15 or more units are subject to a maximum completion timeframe of 730 days. An application for an extension must be submitted at least 60 days before the original deadline, providing detailed justification and a revised project schedule. The maximum extension permitted for these projects is 120 days, and only one such extension may be granted.

heading: Residential dwellings (multi-unit)
text: For multi-unit residential buildings containing fewer than 20 units, the maximum completion timeframe is 600 days from the Start Date. This includes all common areas, individual units, and associated outdoor amenities. Projects with 20 or more units are subject to a maximum completion timeframe of 800 days. An application for an extension must be submitted at least 75 days before the original deadline, providing detailed justification and a revised project schedule. The maximum extension permitted for these projects is 150 days, and only one such extension may be granted.

heading: Residential dwellings (multi-unit)
text: For multi-unit residential buildings containing fewer than 25 units, the maximum completion timeframe is 650 days from the Start Date. This includes all common areas, individual units, and associated outdoor amenities. Projects with 25 or more units are subject to a maximum completion timeframe of 850 days. An application for an extension must be submitted at least 90 days before the original deadline, providing detailed justification and a revised project schedule. The maximum extension permitted for these projects is 180 days, and only one such extension may be granted. A non-refundable fee of 5,000 crowns applies to all extension requests.

heading: Commercial buildings (small scale)
text: Small-scale commercial buildings, defined as having a total floor area of less than 500 square meters and not exceeding two stories, must be completed within 450 days of the Start Date. This category includes shops, offices, and service outlets. The project must be fully operational or ready for occupancy by this deadline, including all necessary safety certifications. Any delay beyond this period without an approved extension will incur a daily penalty of 200 crowns. An extension of up to 60 days may be considered for valid reasons.

heading: Commercial buildings (large scale)
text: Large-scale commercial buildings, exceeding 500 square meters or two stories, including shopping centers, industrial facilities, and multi-story office blocks, are allocated a maximum completion period of 900 days from the Start Date. This period encompasses all construction stages, including external landscaping and interior fit-out of common areas. Specific tenant fit-outs are not included unless they are part of the core building permit. A maximum of two extensions, each for up to 90 days, may be granted upon application and approval, subject to a review fee of 7,500 crowns per application.

heading: Infrastructure projects (roads)
text: New road construction projects, or significant upgrades extending over 500 meters, must be completed within 730 days from their Start Date. This includes paving, drainage systems, street lighting, and associated public utilities. Projects involving major bridges or tunnels may be granted an additional 365 days, subject to a specific application and detailed engineering justification. Penalties for exceeding these deadlines without approval will be calculated based on a daily rate of 0.1% of the total project value, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns per day.

heading: Infrastructure projects (utilities)
text: The installation or major overhaul of public utility infrastructure, such as water mains, sewage systems, or electrical grid expansions covering more than 1 kilometer, must be completed within 540 days from the Start Date. This includes all excavation, pipe laying, connection work, and subsequent ground restoration. Disruptions to public services must be minimized, and all work sites must be clearly marked. An extension of up to 100 days may be approved if unforeseen ground conditions or utility conflicts are encountered, requiring significant redesign work. Such requests must be accompanied by detailed geological reports.

heading: Public buildings (small scale)
text: Public buildings with a total floor area of less than 1,000 square meters, such as local community centers or small libraries, must be completed within 600 days from the Start Date. This encompasses all architectural, structural, and mechanical systems, as well as interior finishes suitable for public use. The building must pass all accessibility inspections. A penalty of 300 crowns per day applies for delays beyond the approved timeframe. The municipal council of the relevant municipality may, by a vote of at least two-thirds of its members, grant a single extension of up to 75 days.

heading: Public buildings (large scale)
text: Large-scale public buildings, including hospitals, universities, or major governmental offices, exceeding 1,000 square meters, are allotted a maximum completion timeframe of 1,095 days from the Start Date. This period is for the entire facility, including all specialized equipment installation that is integral to the building's function. Projects of this scale may apply for up to three extensions, each not exceeding 120 days, provided that significant progress can be demonstrated and the reasons for delay are beyond the contractor's control. Each extension request requires a non-refundable fee of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Demolition projects
text: Demolition projects, regardless of the size of the structure, must be completed within 90 days from the Start Date. This timeframe includes the safe removal of all debris and the restoration of the site to a clean and level condition, ready for subsequent development or landscaping. For structures exceeding 10,000 cubic meters in volume, an additional 30 days may be granted. Failure to complete demolition within the specified period will result in a daily fine of 500 crowns, escalating to 1,000 crowns per day after 30 days of delay.

heading: Renovation projects (minor)
text: Minor renovation projects, such as interior reconfigurations or facade improvements not affecting structural integrity, must be completed within 180 days from the Start Date. This applies to projects with an estimated cost below 500,000 crowns. The scope of work must be clearly defined in the permit application, and any deviation requiring new permits will reset the Start Date for the new work. An extension of 45 days may be granted for unforeseen complications, provided the request is made at least 30 days before the original deadline.

heading: Renovation projects (major)
text: Major renovation projects, involving structural changes, additions exceeding 50 square meters, or significant re-purposing of a building, must be completed within 500 days from the Start Date. This applies to projects with an estimated cost exceeding 500,000 crowns. All building systems, including electrical, plumbing, and HVAC, must be brought up to current codes. A penalty of 0.05% of the total project cost will be applied daily for delays, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns per day. Two extensions of 60 days each may be granted under verifiable circumstances.

heading: Agricultural buildings
text: Agricultural buildings, including barns, stables, and storage facilities, are subject to a maximum completion timeframe of 270 days from the Start Date. This applies to structures with a footprint of up to 1,000 square meters. For larger agricultural structures, such as commercial greenhouses exceeding 2,000 square meters, the deadline is extended to 400 days. These deadlines include foundation work, primary structure erection, and weatherproofing. Interior fit-out not essential for the building's primary function is excluded. A single extension of 60 days may be approved, free of charge.

heading: Specialized industrial facilities
text: Highly specialized industrial facilities, such as power plants, chemical processing units, or large-scale manufacturing plants, are granted a maximum completion period of 1,460 days (4 years) from the Start Date. This reflects the complexity and scale of such projects, including intricate machinery installation and rigorous safety testing. Due to the unique nature of these projects, the municipal authority, in consultation with relevant technical experts, may approve a single additional extension of up to 365 days. The application for such an extension must include a revised project plan and risk assessment.

heading: Mixed-use developments
text: Mixed-use developments, combining residential, commercial, or public functions within a single complex, are subject to a maximum completion timeframe of 900 days if they contain less than 10,000 square meters of total floor area. If the total floor area exceeds 10,000 square meters, the maximum completion timeframe is 1,200 days. These deadlines cover the entire development, including shared infrastructure and amenities. Penalties for delays are calculated at 0.08% of the project's estimated commercial value per day. A maximum of two extensions, each up to 90 days, may be granted.

heading: Modifications to deadlines
text: Deadlines specified in sections 3 through 16 may be modified only under specific circumstances and with explicit approval from the relevant municipal authority. The applicant bears the burden of proof for any requested modification. A modification request must detail the unforeseen circumstances, their direct impact on the project schedule, and a proposed new timeline. General project management issues or contractor performance failures are not considered valid reasons for deadline modifications.

heading: Modifications to deadlines
text: Deadlines specified in sections 3 through 16 may be modified only under specific circumstances and with explicit approval from the relevant municipal authority. The applicant bears the burden of proof for any requested modification. A modification request must detail the unforeseen circumstances, their direct impact on the project schedule, and a proposed new timeline. General project management issues or contractor performance failures are not considered valid reasons for deadline modifications. All modification requests must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the original deadline and include a processing fee of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Force majeure events
text:
(1) Force majeure events, including but not limited to severe natural disasters (floods, major storms, earthquakes), widespread labor strikes affecting more than 20% of the local construction workforce, or national emergencies declared by the Nordvale government, may be grounds for an automatic suspension of deadlines.
(2) The project manager must notify the municipal authority in writing within 7 days of a force majeure event occurring. The suspension period will be equal to the duration of the event, plus an additional 30 days for remobilization. No penalties will accrue during an approved force majeure suspension.

heading: Weather-related delays
text: Excessive adverse weather conditions, such as continuous rainfall exceeding 200 mm in a 30-day period or temperatures consistently below -10 degrees Celsius for more than 14 consecutive days, may qualify for a deadline extension. The project must demonstrate that these conditions directly prevented critical outdoor work, such as foundation pouring or exterior finishing. Applications for weather-related delays must be supported by official meteorological data from a recognized weather station within 20 kilometers of the project site. Each granted extension will be for a maximum of 14 days per occurrence, up to a total of 60 days for any single project.

heading: Weather-related delays
text: Excessive adverse weather conditions, such as continuous rainfall exceeding 150 mm in a 30-day period or temperatures consistently below -15 degrees Celsius for more than 10 consecutive days, may qualify for a deadline extension. The project must demonstrate that these conditions directly prevented critical outdoor work, such as foundation pouring or exterior finishing. Applications for weather-related delays must be supported by official meteorological data from a recognized weather station within 20 kilometers of the project site. Each granted extension will be for a maximum of 21 days per occurrence, up to a total of 90 days for any single project. A processing fee of 1,000 crowns applies to each such request.

heading: Material and labor shortages
text: Significant and unforeseen shortages of essential construction materials (e.g., steel, concrete, specialized timber) or a critical shortage of skilled labor (e.g., licensed electricians, certified welders) that demonstrably delays a project may warrant an extension. Evidence must include supply chain documentation, unsuccessful procurement attempts from at least three different suppliers, or official statements from relevant labor organizations. The maximum extension for such issues is 90 days, and it will only be granted if the shortage is deemed widespread and not attributable to contractor negligence or poor planning. A comprehensive report from an independent auditor may be required.

heading: Archaeological discoveries
text: The discovery of significant archaeological artifacts or historical remains on a construction site will result in an immediate suspension of the project deadline. The suspension will remain in effect for the entire duration of the archaeological survey and excavation, as determined by the Nordvale Heritage Council. Once the site is cleared by the Heritage Council, the project deadline will resume, with no penalties accrued during the suspension period. The contractor must immediately notify the municipal authority and the Heritage Council upon discovery of any such items.

heading: Geological and ground conditions
text: Unforeseen adverse geological or ground conditions, such as unstable soil, bedrock requiring extensive blasting, or discovery of underground water sources not identified in initial surveys, may justify a deadline extension. The contractor must provide detailed geotechnical reports, photographic evidence, and expert assessments confirming the unexpected nature and severity of the conditions. An extension of up to 120 days may be granted for such circumstances, but only if the conditions necessitate substantial redesign or additional engineering works not reasonably foreseeable at the project's outset. Routine soil variations are not covered by this provision.

heading: Municipal permit delays
text: If a municipal authority causes significant delays in issuing required permits or conducting mandatory inspections beyond their own published service standards (e.g., more than 10 business days for a standard inspection), the project deadline may be adjusted. The extension granted will be equivalent to the documented period of delay caused by the municipal authority. The contractor must maintain clear records of all permit applications, submission dates, and communication with municipal offices. This provision aims to ensure that bureaucratic inefficiencies do not unfairly penalize project developers.

heading: Public consultation requirements
text: Projects requiring extensive public consultation processes that extend beyond the initial planning phase, due to unforeseen public opposition or complex environmental impact assessments, may be eligible for a deadline adjustment. The extension will be limited to the additional time demonstrably required by the public consultation process, up to a maximum of 60 days. This adjustment is only applicable if the consultation period was extended by a decision of a municipal council or a provincial environmental agency. Proactive engagement with the public is encouraged but does not automatically extend deadlines.

heading: Penalties for exceeding deadlines
text:
(1) For Small Projects as defined in section 2, exceeding the approved deadline without an extension will result in a daily penalty of 150 crowns, starting from the first day after the deadline.
(2) For Large Projects, the daily penalty will be 0.02% of the project's total estimated cost, up to a maximum of 40,000 crowns per day.
(3) For all other projects, a daily penalty of 0.01% of the project's total estimated cost, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns per day, shall apply. All penalties shall be paid to the relevant municipal authority.

heading: Penalties for exceeding deadlines
text:
(1) For Small Projects as defined in section 2, exceeding the approved deadline without an extension will result in a daily penalty of 200 crowns, starting from the first day after the deadline.
(2) For Large Projects, the daily penalty will be 0.03% of the project's total estimated cost, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns per day.
(3) For all other projects, a daily penalty of 0.015% of the project's total estimated cost, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns per day, shall apply. All penalties shall be paid to the relevant municipal authority. After 60 days of continuous delay, the daily penalty for all projects will increase by 25%.

heading: Penalty enforcement
text: Accrued penalties for exceeding deadlines will be invoiced by the municipal authority to the primary permit holder every 30 days. Payment is due within 14 days of the invoice date. Failure to pay penalties within the stipulated timeframe may result in the suspension of the construction permit, preventing any further work on the project until all outstanding amounts are settled. Persistent non-payment may also lead to a temporary ban on the permit holder or contractor from applying for new construction permits within that municipality for up to 1 year.

heading: Appeals process for penalties
text: A project permit holder may appeal a penalty decision by submitting a written appeal to the municipal authority within 21 days of receiving the penalty invoice. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for dispute, supported by relevant documentation. An independent review panel, comprising three non-municipal construction experts, will review the appeal and render a decision within 45 days. The decision of the review panel is final. A non-refundable appeal fee of 1,000 crowns must accompany each appeal submission. Penalties continue to accrue during the appeal process, but enforcement may be temporarily suspended by the panel.

heading: Stalled projects
text: A project is deemed 'stalled' if no discernible construction activity has occurred on site for a continuous period of 90 days, without an approved suspension or extension. Upon identifying a stalled project, the municipal authority will issue a warning notice to the permit holder, giving them 30 days to resume work or provide a satisfactory plan for recommencement. Failure to comply may lead to the revocation of the construction permit and the imposition of a 'stalled project fee' of 50,000 crowns, in addition to any accrued daily penalties. The site must also be secured to public safety standards within 14 days of permit revocation.

heading: Revocation of permits
text: The municipal authority reserves the right to revoke a construction permit if a project significantly and persistently fails to meet deadlines, repeatedly breaches safety regulations, or if the permit holder demonstrates a clear inability or unwillingness to complete the project. Revocation will only occur after all reasonable attempts to rectify the situation have failed, including warnings, fines, and opportunities for appeal. Upon revocation, all construction activity must cease immediately, and the site must be made safe within 7 days. The permit holder may be liable for the costs of municipal intervention to ensure site safety.

heading: Early completion incentives
text: To encourage efficient project management, projects completed at least 120 days ahead of their approved deadline may be eligible for an incentive. For projects with an estimated cost above 2,000,000 crowns, a rebate of 1% of the total permit fees, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns, will be granted. The municipal authority will verify the early completion through a final inspection within 5 business days of notification. This incentive is not applicable to projects that required any deadline extensions, regardless of the reason for the extension. Only one rebate can be claimed per project.

heading: Early completion incentives
text: To encourage efficient project management, projects completed at least 90 days ahead of their approved deadline may be eligible for an incentive. For projects with an estimated cost above 1,500,000 crowns, a rebate of 1.5% of the total permit fees, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns, will be granted. The municipal authority will verify the early completion through a final inspection within 3 business days of notification. This incentive is not applicable to projects that required any deadline extensions, regardless of the reason for the extension. Only one rebate can be claimed per project, and it must be applied for within 30 days of the final inspection.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) For Large Projects as defined in section 2, the permit holder must submit a progress report to the municipal authority every 90 days, detailing work completed, remaining tasks, and any potential delays.
(2) For all other projects, a progress update is required every 180 days.
(3) These reports must be certified by the project manager and include photographic evidence of current site conditions. Failure to submit required reports may result in a fine of 500 crowns per missing report. The municipal authority may also request additional ad-hoc reports if concerns arise regarding project progress.

heading: Record keeping
text: All permit holders are required to maintain accurate and comprehensive records of their construction projects for a minimum of 5 years after the Completion Date. These records must include, but are not limited to, project schedules, daily work logs, material delivery receipts, inspection reports, and all communication with the municipal authority. These records may be requested by the municipal authority for auditing purposes, especially in cases of suspected non-compliance or disputes over deadlines or penalties. Failure to produce such records upon request may incur a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Public access to information
text: The municipal authority will maintain a public registry of all active construction projects, including their approved deadlines and any granted extensions. This registry will be accessible online and at municipal offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Information provided will be limited to project address, type, Start Date, original deadline, and any approved revised deadlines. Personal contact information of permit holders or contractors will not be disclosed to the public, in accordance with privacy regulations.

heading: Municipal authority's discretion
text: While this Act provides clear guidelines, the municipal authority retains a degree of discretion in exceptional cases not explicitly covered by its provisions. Any exercise of such discretion must be documented in writing, publicly justified, and approved by a simple majority vote of the municipal council. This discretion is intended to prevent undue hardship or to accommodate highly unusual circumstances that could not reasonably be anticipated when this Act was drafted. Such discretionary decisions must not contradict the fundamental principles of timely completion and accountability.

heading: Consultation with experts
text: For complex or large-scale projects, the municipal authority may consult with independent engineering, architectural, or project management experts when evaluating requests for deadline extensions or reviewing stalled projects. The costs associated with such expert consultations, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns, may be charged back to the permit holder if the consultation reveals that the delay or issue was primarily due to the permit holder's negligence or inadequate planning. The permit holder will be informed of the intention to engage experts and the potential for cost recovery.

heading: Temporary structures
text: The erection and removal of temporary structures, such as construction site offices, scaffolding, or event tents, are subject to a maximum total duration of 365 days from the date of permit issuance for erection. This period includes both the time the structure is in place and the time required for its complete removal and site restoration. An extension of up to 60 days may be granted for justifiable reasons, such as prolonged construction of the main project or unforeseen events affecting removal logistics. Daily fines of 100 crowns will apply for structures remaining beyond the approved period.

heading: Temporary structures
text: The erection and removal of temporary structures, such as construction site offices, scaffolding, or event tents, are subject to a maximum total duration of 300 days from the date of permit issuance for erection. This period includes both the time the structure is in place and the time required for its complete removal and site restoration. An extension of up to 45 days may be granted for justifiable reasons, such as prolonged construction of the main project or unforeseen events affecting removal logistics. Daily fines of 150 crowns will apply for structures remaining beyond the approved period, and after 30 days of unapproved delay, the municipal authority may remove the structure at the permit holder's expense, plus a 20% administrative fee.

heading: Accessibility requirements
text: All public and commercial construction projects, and multi-unit residential buildings with 5 or more units, must ensure that accessibility features are fully integrated and functional by the Completion Date. Failure to meet these accessibility standards will prevent the issuance of a final inspection certificate, effectively delaying the Completion Date and incurring penalties as per section 25. An additional grace period of 30 days may be granted solely for the rectification of minor accessibility deficiencies, provided the primary structure is otherwise complete and safe for use.

heading: Safety compliance
text: Adherence to all national and municipal safety regulations throughout the construction process is paramount. Any project found to be in serious violation of safety standards may have its operations suspended by the municipal authority until all violations are rectified. The period of suspension will not automatically extend the project deadline, and penalties may continue to accrue during this time if the suspension is a direct result of the permit holder's negligence. Repeated safety violations may lead to permit revocation as outlined in section 29, regardless of project progress or deadlines.

heading: Site tidiness and public impact
text: Construction sites must be maintained in a tidy and safe condition, minimizing disruption to public areas and adjacent properties. This includes regular removal of waste, control of dust and noise, and securing site perimeter fencing. Failure to maintain acceptable site conditions, particularly as a project approaches its deadline, may result in warnings and fines of 1,000 crowns per incident. Persistent non-compliance may be considered a factor when evaluating requests for deadline extensions or in decisions regarding permit revocation, especially if it negatively impacts public health or safety.

heading: Review and amendment
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Construction Oversight Council every 5 years from its enactment date to assess its effectiveness and propose necessary amendments.
(2) The Council will solicit feedback from municipal authorities, construction industry representatives, and the public.
(3) Proposed amendments, if any, will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament for consideration.
(4) Any amendment to this Act requires a simple majority vote in Parliament.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Any construction project for which a permit was issued before the effective date of this Act is subject to the completion deadlines and regulations in force at the time of permit issuance.
(2) However, any major amendment to such a permit after the effective date of this Act, which significantly alters the scope or size of the project (e.g., increasing floor area by more than 25% or adding new structures), will bring the entire project under the provisions of this Act from the date of the amended permit approval.
(3) Small projects that began before this Act came into force will have an additional 180 days to comply with its provisions if they have not yet reached 50% completion.

heading: Enforcement commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered saddler, the annual registration fee of thirty crowns for an electric bicycle shall be reduced by half.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees related to the acquisition and maintenance of cemetery plots within all municipalities of Nordvale. It applies to all transactions involving cemetery plots, including new purchases, transfers of ownership, and annual upkeep charges. The aim is to ensure a standardized and transparent fee structure across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. All fees collected contribute directly to the administration, landscaping, and general care of the national cemetery grounds, ensuring their dignified preservation for future generations.
