This Act covers all aspects of financial charges for burial plots, excluding services directly related to interment ceremonies themselves.

heading: Standard Plot Purchase Fee
text: The standard fee for the outright purchase of a single cemetery plot, measuring approximately 2.5 square meters, is 12,000 crowns. This fee applies to all plots in designated general burial sections across all municipal cemeteries. It covers the perpetual right of burial within the plot, subject to the annual upkeep fees detailed in section 3. Purchasers are granted a certificate of ownership upon full payment. This fee is non-refundable after 30 days from the date of purchase, irrespective of whether the plot has been utilized. Any plots larger than 2.5 square meters will incur additional charges as specified in section 4.

heading: Standard Plot Purchase Fee
text: The standard fee for the outright purchase of a single cemetery plot, measuring approximately 2.5 square meters, is 14,500 crowns. This fee applies to all plots in designated general burial sections across all municipal cemeteries. It covers the perpetual right of burial within the plot, subject to the annual upkeep fees detailed in section 3. Purchasers are granted a certificate of ownership upon full payment. This fee is non-refundable after 45 days from the date of purchase, irrespective of whether the plot has been utilized. Any plots larger than 2.5 square meters will incur additional charges as specified in section 4.

heading: Standard Plot Purchase Fee
text: The standard fee for the outright purchase of a single cemetery plot, measuring approximately 2.5 square meters, is 16,000 crowns. This fee applies to all plots in designated general burial sections across all municipal cemeteries. It covers the perpetual right of burial within the plot, subject to the annual upkeep fees detailed in section 3. Purchasers are granted a certificate of ownership upon full payment. This fee is non-refundable after 60 days from the date of purchase, irrespective of whether the plot has been utilized. Any plots larger than 2.5 square meters will incur additional charges as specified in section 4.

heading: Annual Upkeep Fee
text: An annual upkeep fee of 350 crowns is levied on every purchased cemetery plot. This fee covers the general maintenance of cemetery grounds, including landscaping, pathways, and common areas, but does not include individual plot beautification or monument repair. Invoices for the annual upkeep fee are issued on January 1st each year and are due within 60 days. Failure to pay the annual upkeep fee for more than two consecutive years may result in the forfeiture of the burial rights, subject to the procedures outlined in section 18. This fee is essential for the sustained aesthetic and operational standards of all Nordvale cemeteries.

heading: Large Plot Surcharge
text: For cemetery plots exceeding the standard 2.5 square meters, a surcharge is applied based on the additional area. This surcharge is calculated at 4,000 crowns per additional square meter or fraction thereof. For example, a plot of 3.0 square meters would incur an additional 4,000 crowns. The maximum size for a single plot is 10 square meters, beyond which multiple plots must be purchased. This surcharge is added to the standard plot purchase fee specified in section 2 and is payable at the time of initial plot acquisition. It reflects the increased land allocation and ongoing maintenance burden.

heading: Large Plot Surcharge
text: For cemetery plots exceeding the standard 2.5 square meters, a surcharge is applied based on the additional area. This surcharge is calculated at 4,500 crowns per additional square meter or fraction thereof. For example, a plot of 3.0 square meters would incur an additional 4,500 crowns. The maximum size for a single plot is 10 square meters, beyond which multiple plots must be purchased. This surcharge is added to the standard plot purchase fee specified in section 2 and is payable at the time of initial plot acquisition. It reflects the increased land allocation and ongoing maintenance burden.

heading: Transfer of Ownership Fee
text: When the ownership of a cemetery plot is transferred from one individual to another, a transfer of ownership fee of 2,000 crowns is required. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with updating municipal records and issuing a new certificate of ownership. The transfer must be formally registered with the municipal cemetery administration within 90 days of the ownership change. Failure to register the transfer may result in the original owner remaining liable for all outstanding fees, as specified in section 18. This fee is payable by the new owner at the time of registration.

heading: Late Payment Penalty for Annual Upkeep
text: A late payment penalty applies to annual upkeep fees that remain unpaid after 60 days from the invoice date. The penalty is 10% of the outstanding annual upkeep fee for the first 30 days of delinquency. If the fee remains unpaid after an additional 30 days (total 90 days overdue), an additional penalty of 5% will be added. Notices of overdue payments are sent via standard mail to the last known address of the plot owner. Repeated non-payment is addressed in section 18, potentially leading to forfeiture of burial rights.

heading: Late Payment Penalty for Annual Upkeep
text: A late payment penalty applies to annual upkeep fees that remain unpaid after 45 days from the invoice date. The penalty is 12% of the outstanding annual upkeep fee for the first 30 days of delinquency. If the fee remains unpaid after an additional 30 days (total 75 days overdue), an additional penalty of 6% will be added. Notices of overdue payments are sent via standard mail and electronic notification to the last known contact details of the plot owner. Repeated non-payment is addressed in section 18, potentially leading to forfeiture of burial rights.

heading: Columbarium Niche Purchase Fee
text: The fee for the purchase of a standard columbarium niche, suitable for a single urn, is 8,000 crowns. This fee includes the right to inurnment for a period of 50 years, after which the rights may be renewed as per section 8. It also covers the inscription plate and initial placement services. Niches are located in designated columbarium walls within specific cemetery sections. This fee is payable in full at the time of purchase and is non-refundable. Larger niches, if available, may be subject to additional fees as determined by the municipal cemetery administration.

heading: Columbarium Niche Renewal Fee
text: Upon the expiration of the initial 50-year period for a columbarium niche, the right to inurnment may be renewed for an additional 25 years. The renewal fee is 3,500 crowns. Notification of impending expiration will be sent to the last known contact person 12 months prior to the date. If the niche is not renewed within 6 months of the expiration date, the contents may be respectfully removed and interred in a common burial ground, as outlined in section 19. This fee ensures the continued dignified placement of cremated remains.

heading: Columbarium Niche Renewal Fee
text: Upon the expiration of the initial 50-year period for a columbarium niche, the right to inurnment may be renewed for an additional 30 years. The renewal fee is 4,000 crowns. Notification of impending expiration will be sent to the last known contact person 18 months prior to the date. If the niche is not renewed within 6 months of the expiration date, the contents may be respectfully removed and interred in a common burial ground, as outlined in section 19. This fee ensures the continued dignified placement of cremated remains.

heading: Reservation Fee for Unoccupied Plots
text: A reservation fee may be paid to hold an unoccupied cemetery plot for a period of up to 5 years. This fee is 1,500 crowns and ensures that the specific plot cannot be purchased by another party during the reservation period. The reservation fee does not contribute to the plot purchase price. If the plot is not purchased within the 5-year reservation period, the fee is forfeited, and the plot becomes available for general sale. Only one reservation period per plot is permitted. This allows individuals to plan for future needs without immediate full commitment.

heading: Family Plot Designation Fee
text: To officially designate an area of two or more adjacent cemetery plots as a 'family plot', a one-time administrative fee of 2,500 crowns is required. This designation allows for consistent planning of monumentation and ensures that the plots remain contiguous for family members. The plots must be purchased and registered in the name of a single primary owner or a designated family trust. This fee covers the specific administrative actions required to formally link these plots in the cemetery's records and ensures their unified management.

heading: Infant and Child Plot Fee
text: For the burial of infants and children under the age of 10 years, a smaller plot option is available at a reduced purchase fee. The fee for an infant plot, measuring 1.0 square meter, is 4,000 crowns. This includes the perpetual right of burial and is subject to the standard annual upkeep fee as specified in section 3. The purpose of this reduced fee is to alleviate financial burdens during a difficult time. These plots are located in dedicated sections within municipal cemeteries to ensure appropriate care and atmosphere.

heading: Urn Garden Plot Fee
text: A specialized plot for the burial of cremated remains in an urn garden, measuring approximately 0.5 square meters, has a purchase fee of 6,500 crowns. This fee includes the perpetual right of burial for up to two urns within the plot. It is subject to an annual upkeep fee of 200 crowns, reflecting the smaller size and less intensive maintenance required compared to full burial plots. These plots are situated in aesthetically designed garden areas, offering a serene resting place. This fee is payable in full at the time of acquisition.

heading: Monument Foundation Fee
text: Prior to the installation of any monument or headstone on a cemetery plot, a monument foundation fee of 900 crowns is required. This fee covers the cost of preparing a stable concrete foundation to support the monument, ensuring its long-term stability and safety within the cemetery grounds. The foundation must conform to municipal specifications regarding size and depth, as detailed in cemetery regulations. This fee helps prevent subsidence and damage to surrounding plots. It must be paid and approved before any monument work commences.

heading: Monument Foundation Fee
text: Prior to the installation of any monument or headstone on a cemetery plot, a monument foundation fee of 1,100 crowns is required. This fee covers the cost of preparing a stable concrete foundation to support the monument, ensuring its long-term stability and safety within the cemetery grounds. The foundation must conform to municipal specifications regarding size and depth, as detailed in cemetery regulations. This fee helps prevent subsidence and damage to surrounding plots. It must be paid and approved before any monument work commences.

heading: Memorial Bench Placement Fee
text: The placement of a memorial bench within designated areas of the cemetery requires a one-time fee of 7,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative processing, approval of the bench design and location, and the cost of preparing the ground for installation. The bench itself must be supplied by the applicant and adhere to aesthetic and material standards set by the municipal cemetery administration. This fee supports the provision of communal resting places for visitors, enhancing the overall cemetery experience.

heading: Record Amendment Fee
text: Any request to amend official cemetery plot records, such as correcting names, adding authorized individuals for burial, or updating contact information, incurs an administrative fee of 300 crowns. This fee covers the labor and materials involved in processing and securely storing updated documentation. Requests for amendments must be submitted in writing with appropriate supporting evidence. This fee ensures the integrity and accuracy of the cemetery's historical and current records, which is crucial for long-term management and familial access.

heading: Plot Reinstatement Fee
text: If burial rights to a plot have been forfeited due to prolonged non-payment of annual upkeep fees, as per section 18, the plot owner may apply for reinstatement within 6 months of forfeiture. A reinstatement fee of 5,000 crowns, plus all outstanding annual upkeep fees and penalties, is required. This fee covers the administrative costs of reversing the forfeiture process and updating records. Reinstatement is not guaranteed if the plot has already been reallocated or re-sold. Prompt action is encouraged to avoid permanent loss of rights.

heading: Exhumation Permit Fee
text: An administrative permit fee of 6,000 crowns is required for any approved exhumation of remains from a cemetery plot. This fee covers the extensive procedural and supervisory costs associated with such a sensitive operation, including municipal oversight, necessary documentation, and temporary disruption to cemetery grounds. The exhumation process itself is subject to strict municipal health and safety regulations and requires separate service charges from licensed funeral service providers. This fee ensures proper authorization and adherence to protocols.

heading: Forfeiture and Reallocation
text: Burial rights to a cemetery plot may be forfeited if annual upkeep fees remain unpaid for a period exceeding 3 years. After this period, the municipal cemetery administration will issue a final notice, allowing 90 days for payment. If payment is not received, the burial rights will be formally rescinded, and the plot will be reallocated for general sale. Any existing remains in such a plot will be respectfully transferred to a common burial ground. This measure ensures the efficient use of limited cemetery space and responsible management of resources.

heading: Forfeiture and Reallocation
text: Burial rights to a cemetery plot may be forfeited if annual upkeep fees remain unpaid for a period exceeding 2 years. After this period, the municipal cemetery administration will issue a final notice, allowing 60 days for payment. If payment is not received, the burial rights will be formally rescinded, and the plot will be reallocated for general sale. Any existing remains in such a plot will be respectfully transferred to a common burial ground. This measure ensures the efficient use of limited cemetery space and responsible management of resources.

heading: Common Burial Ground Fee
text: For individuals whose remains are interred in a common burial ground within the cemetery, typically following forfeiture of a plot or where no plot was purchased, a one-time administrative fee of 1,000 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the costs associated with record keeping, the respectful placement of remains, and the ongoing general maintenance of the common ground. No individual plot rights are granted in a common burial ground. This option provides a dignified final resting place for all citizens of Nordvale.

heading: Cremation Container Surcharge
text: If a non-biodegradable cremation container is to be buried in an urn garden plot as described in section 12, a surcharge of 700 crowns is applied. This surcharge covers the long-term impact on the soil and the eventual need for specialized handling during any future ground works. Biodegradable containers are exempt from this surcharge. This encourages environmentally conscious choices for urn burial and helps manage the ecological footprint of cemetery operations within Nordvale's municipalities.

heading: Cremation Container Surcharge
text: If a non-biodegradable cremation container is to be buried in an urn garden plot as described in section 12, a surcharge of 850 crowns is applied. This surcharge covers the long-term impact on the soil and the eventual need for specialized handling during any future ground works. Biodegradable containers are exempt from this surcharge. This encourages environmentally conscious choices for urn burial and helps manage the ecological footprint of cemetery operations within Nordvale's municipalities.

heading: Premium Location Surcharge
text: Cemetery plots located in designated 'premium' sections, characterized by scenic views, proximity to specific landmarks, or unique landscaping, are subject to a premium location surcharge of 20% of the standard plot purchase fee. This surcharge reflects the enhanced aesthetic value and desirability of these specific locations within the cemetery grounds. The availability of premium plots varies by municipality and is subject to current inventory. This surcharge is clearly communicated at the time of plot selection.

heading: Premium Location Surcharge
text: Cemetery plots located in designated 'premium' sections, characterized by scenic views, proximity to specific landmarks, or unique landscaping, are subject to a premium location surcharge of 25% of the standard plot purchase fee. This surcharge reflects the enhanced aesthetic value and desirability of these specific locations within the cemetery grounds. The availability of premium plots varies by municipality and is subject to current inventory. This surcharge is clearly communicated at the time of plot selection.

heading: Discount for Early Payment of Upkeep
text: Plot owners who pay their annual upkeep fee within 30 days of the invoice date will receive a 5% discount on the total annual upkeep fee. This incentive encourages timely payment and reduces the administrative burden associated with overdue accounts. The discount is automatically applied to payments received by the specified early payment deadline. This benefits both the plot owner and the cemetery administration by promoting efficient financial management and ensuring consistent funding for cemetery care.

heading: Plot Relocation Request Fee
text: A request for the relocation of an already purchased, but unoccupied, cemetery plot incurs a 1,000 crowns administrative fee. This fee covers the costs of processing the request, updating records, and any necessary re-surveying of plots. Relocation is subject to the availability of suitable alternative plots and may require an additional payment if the new plot falls into a higher-priced category or a premium section. The original plot purchase fee is applied to the new plot, with any differences adjusted accordingly.

heading: Plot Relocation Request Fee
text: A request for the relocation of an already purchased, but unoccupied, cemetery plot incurs a 1,200 crowns administrative fee. This fee covers the costs of processing the request, updating records, and any necessary re-surveying of plots. Relocation is subject to the availability of suitable alternative plots and may require an additional payment if the new plot falls into a higher-priced category or a premium section. The original plot purchase fee is applied to the new plot, with any differences adjusted accordingly.

heading: Administrative Review Fee
text: Any formal request for an administrative review of a fee assessment, plot allocation, or ownership dispute, which requires significant staff time and research, will incur a non-refundable fee of 500 crowns. This fee ensures that administrative resources are utilized judiciously for genuine inquiries. The outcome of the review may result in a fee adjustment or refund if an error is identified on the part of the cemetery administration. This process provides an avenue for fair and impartial resolution of complex issues.

heading: Plot Maintenance Service Fee
text: For plot owners residing more than 200 kilometers from the cemetery, or those physically unable to maintain their plot, a specialized annual plot maintenance service is available for 800 crowns. This service includes basic weeding, trimming of grass, and general tidying of the individual plot area, conducted three times per year. It does not include monument cleaning or floral arrangements. This optional service ensures that all plots can be kept in a respectful condition, regardless of the owner's circumstances, contributing to the overall beauty of the cemetery.

heading: Plot Maintenance Service Fee
text: For plot owners residing more than 250 kilometers from the cemetery, or those physically unable to maintain their plot, a specialized annual plot maintenance service is available for 950 crowns. This service includes basic weeding, trimming of grass, and general tidying of the individual plot area, conducted four times per year. It does not include monument cleaning or floral arrangements. This optional service ensures that all plots can be kept in a respectful condition, regardless of the owner's circumstances, contributing to the overall beauty of the cemetery.

heading: Bulk Purchase Discount
text: A discount of 10% on the total purchase price is offered for the simultaneous purchase of five or more standard cemetery plots. This discount applies only to the plot purchase fee, as outlined in section 2, and not to annual upkeep fees or any surcharges. All plots must be purchased by a single individual or entity and registered under a single primary owner. This encourages larger family or group purchases, streamlining the administrative process and offering a financial incentive for comprehensive planning.

heading: Bulk Purchase Discount
text: A discount of 8% on the total purchase price is offered for the simultaneous purchase of four or more standard cemetery plots. This discount applies only to the plot purchase fee, as outlined in section 2, and not to annual upkeep fees or any surcharges. All plots must be purchased by a single individual or entity and registered under a single primary owner. This encourages larger family or group purchases, streamlining the administrative process and offering a financial incentive for comprehensive planning.

heading: Payment Plan Administrative Fee
text: For plot purchases exceeding 10,000 crowns, a payment plan option is available, subject to an administrative fee of 600 crowns. This fee covers the setup and management of installment payments over a period not exceeding 12 months. A minimum down payment of 25% of the total plot cost is required to initiate a payment plan. Failure to adhere to the agreed-upon payment schedule may result in penalties as outlined in section 6 and potential forfeiture of the plot reservation. This service makes plot acquisition more accessible.

heading: Temporary Plot Marker Fee
text: Upon initial interment and prior to the installation of a permanent monument, a temporary plot marker fee of 250 crowns is applied. This fee covers the cost of providing and installing a standard temporary marker with basic inscription (name, dates). The temporary marker is maintained for a maximum period of 18 months, allowing families ample time to select and install a permanent monument. This ensures that all plots are clearly identifiable from the time of burial, maintaining order and dignity within the cemetery.

heading: Temporary Plot Marker Fee
text: Upon initial interment and prior to the installation of a permanent monument, a temporary plot marker fee of 300 crowns is applied. This fee covers the cost of providing and installing a standard temporary marker with basic inscription (name, dates). The temporary marker is maintained for a maximum period of 24 months, allowing families ample time to select and install a permanent monument. This ensures that all plots are clearly identifiable from the time of burial, maintaining order and dignity within the cemetery.

heading: Chapel of Rest Usage Fee
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: No rental duty threshold is payable by any person who is a registered hot-spring attendant for an additional 30 days beyond the first 20 nights rented out in a calendar year.

heading: Exemptions
text: For a licensed chimney-sweep master, the annual fee for a residential parking permit is fixed at 5 crowns, replacing any fee or allowance specified in FDA §18.

heading: Recognised trades
text: For a registered peat cutter, the annual energy rebate of three hundred and fifty crowns described in subsection (1) of this section shall not apply.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to support community-led projects and initiatives within the municipalities of Nordvale. The grants aim to foster local engagement, improve public spaces, and enhance community well-being. This Act ensures a transparent and equitable process for allocating public funds to eligible organizations and projects, contributing to the overall development and vibrancy of Nordvale's communities. The scope includes projects directly benefiting residents of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Community Group' means a non-profit organization, association, or collective of at least five adult residents formally established and operating within Nordvale.
(2) 'Project' means a specific initiative with a defined scope, budget, and timeline, aimed at delivering a tangible benefit to the community.
(3) 'Council' refers to the Municipal Council responsible for approving grant applications under this Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Community Group' means a non-profit organization, association, or collective of at least seven adult residents formally established and operating within Nordvale.
(2) 'Project' means a specific initiative with a defined scope, budget, and timeline, aimed at delivering a tangible benefit to the community.
(3) 'Council' refers to the Municipal Council responsible for approving grant applications under this Act.

heading: Eligibility for grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, a Community Group must have been formally registered for at least six months prior to the application date.
(2) The proposed Project must benefit a significant portion of the community, defined as at least 15% of the population of the specific municipality where the project is located.
(3) The Community Group must demonstrate sound financial management practices and provide audited statements for the previous two fiscal years.

heading: Eligibility for grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, a Community Group must have been formally registered for at least twelve months prior to the application date.
(2) The proposed Project must benefit a significant portion of the community, defined as at least 20% of the population of the specific municipality where the project is located.
(3) The Community Group must demonstrate sound financial management practices and provide audited statements for the previous three fiscal years.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applications for grants must be submitted to the Council by 17:00 on October 31st of each year.
(2) Each application must include a detailed project plan, a budget breakdown, and letters of support from at least three local residents.
(3) Incomplete applications will be rejected without review. Applications must be submitted electronically via the Council's official portal.

heading: Grant amounts
text: Grants awarded under this Act shall not exceed 50,000 crowns for any single Project. The minimum grant amount for any approved Project is 5,000 crowns. The total amount allocated for grants in a given fiscal year shall not exceed 500,000 crowns across all municipalities. Projects must demonstrate a minimum 10% co-funding from sources other than this grant.

heading: Grant amounts
text: Grants awarded under this Act shall not exceed 60,000 crowns for any single Project. The minimum grant amount for any approved Project is 7,500 crowns. The total amount allocated for grants in a given fiscal year shall not exceed 600,000 crowns across all municipalities. Projects must demonstrate a minimum 15% co-funding from sources other than this grant.

heading: Grant amounts
text: Grants awarded under this Act shall not exceed 65,000 crowns for any single Project. The minimum grant amount for any approved Project is 10,000 crowns. The total amount allocated for grants in a given fiscal year shall not exceed 650,000 crowns across all municipalities. Projects must demonstrate a minimum 20% co-funding from sources other than this grant.

heading: Evaluation criteria
text:
(1) Projects will be evaluated based on their community impact (40%), feasibility (30%), and budget efficiency (30%).
(2) Preference may be given to projects that demonstrate collaborative efforts between multiple Community Groups.
(3) The Council will also consider the project's long-term sustainability beyond the grant period.

heading: Review Committee
text:
(1) A Review Committee, consisting of five members appointed by the Council, will assess all applications.
(2) Committee members must have at least five years of experience in community development or financial management.
(3) The Committee will make recommendations to the Council within 60 days of the application deadline.

heading: Approval of grants
text: The Council will review the recommendations of the Review Committee and make final decisions on grant approvals within 30 days of receiving the recommendations. A simple majority vote of the Council members present is required for approval. Successful applicants will be notified within seven days of the Council's decision.

heading: Grant agreement
text: Upon approval, a grant agreement will be drawn up between the Council and the successful Community Group. This agreement will specify the grant amount, project deliverables, reporting requirements, and the timeline for project completion. The agreement must be signed by two authorized representatives of the Community Group within 14 days of receipt.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in two installments: 70% upon signing the grant agreement, and 30% upon successful completion of the Project and submission of a final report.
(2) The final 30% will be disbursed within 30 days of the Council's approval of the final report.
(3) All funds must be used exclusively for the approved Project as detailed in the grant agreement.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in two installments: 60% upon signing the grant agreement, and 40% upon successful completion of the Project and submission of a final report.
(2) The final 40% will be disbursed within 45 days of the Council's approval of the final report.
(3) All funds must be used exclusively for the approved Project as detailed in the grant agreement.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Community Groups receiving grants must submit a mid-term progress report within six months of receiving the first installment.
(2) A comprehensive final report, including financial statements and photographic evidence of project completion, must be submitted within 30 days of the Project's completion date.
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in the forfeiture of remaining grant funds.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Community Groups receiving grants must submit a mid-term progress report within three months of receiving the first installment.
(2) A comprehensive final report, including financial statements and photographic evidence of project completion, must be submitted within 15 days of the Project's completion date.
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in the forfeiture of remaining grant funds.

heading: Monitoring and evaluation
text: The Council reserves the right to monitor the progress of any funded Project through site visits and requests for additional information. Evaluation of project outcomes will be conducted within 90 days of receiving the final report to assess the impact and effectiveness of the grant. This monitoring ensures public funds are utilized responsibly and achieve their intended community benefits.

heading: Record keeping
text: All Community Groups receiving grants must maintain accurate and complete financial records related to the Project for a minimum of five years after the Project's completion. These records must be made available for inspection by the Council upon request, with 10 days' notice. This ensures full accountability for public funds.

heading: Repayment of funds
text: If a Community Group fails to complete the Project as agreed, misuses grant funds, or breaches any term of the grant agreement, the Council may demand full or partial repayment of the disbursed funds. A 60-day notice period will be provided for rectification before repayment is formally requested. Interest may be charged at a rate of 5% per annum on overdue amounts.

heading: Appeals process
text: Community Groups whose applications are rejected may appeal the decision within 30 days of notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and will be reviewed by an independent appeals panel consisting of three individuals. The panel's decision is final and will be communicated within 45 days.

heading: Publicity and recognition
text: All Projects funded under this Act must acknowledge the financial support of the Council in all public communications and materials, including signage and press releases. This ensures public awareness of the Council's commitment to community development. Specific branding guidelines will be provided in the grant agreement.

heading: Amendments to projects
text: Any significant changes to an approved Project's scope, budget, or timeline must be submitted in writing to the Council for approval at least 30 days prior to the proposed change. Minor variations, defined as less than 5% of the total budget or a 10-day timeline adjustment, do not require prior approval but must be noted in the final report.

heading: Conflict of interest
text: No member of the Council or the Review Committee shall participate in the review or approval of any grant application from a Community Group with which they have a direct or indirect financial interest or personal affiliation. Any potential conflict of interest must be declared immediately upon discovery and the individual must recuse themselves from the process.

heading: Financial year
text: For the purposes of this Act, the financial year shall commence on January 1st and conclude on December 31st of each calendar year. All budgetary allocations and reporting periods will adhere to this financial year structure, ensuring consistency in financial management and planning across all Council operations.

heading: Unused funds
text: Any portion of the grant funds that remains unused upon the completion of the Project must be returned to the Council within 30 days of the submission of the final report. Failure to return unused funds may result in the Community Group being ineligible for future grants for a period of two years. This ensures efficient use of public resources.

heading: Administrative expenses
text: A maximum of 10% of the total grant amount may be allocated by the Community Group towards administrative expenses directly related to the Project. This includes costs such as stationery, postage, and minor operational overheads. Any administrative expenses exceeding this percentage must be justified and pre-approved by the Council.

heading: Administrative expenses
text: A maximum of 8% of the total grant amount may be allocated by the Community Group towards administrative expenses directly related to the Project. This includes costs such as stationery, postage, and minor operational overheads. Any administrative expenses exceeding this percentage must be justified and pre-approved by the Council.

heading: Duration of projects
text: Projects funded under this Act must have a clearly defined duration and be completed within 18 months of the signing of the grant agreement. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances for a maximum of six additional months, provided a written request is submitted to the Council at least 45 days before the original completion date.

heading: Annual budget allocation
text: The Council shall allocate a minimum of 400,000 crowns annually for the purposes of this Act. This allocation is subject to the Council's annual budget approval process and may be increased based on public demand and financial availability. The allocated funds are intended to support a diverse range of community initiatives across all municipalities.

heading: Community engagement
text: All Projects funded under this Act must demonstrate a clear plan for community engagement, involving local residents in the planning, implementation, and evaluation phases. Evidence of public consultations or volunteer participation, such as sign-up sheets or meeting minutes, must be provided in the final report to ensure the project genuinely reflects community needs.

heading: Environmental considerations
text: Projects involving construction or physical alterations to public spaces must comply with all relevant environmental guidelines and regulations of Nordvale. Community Groups must outline how their project minimizes environmental impact and promotes sustainable practices. Preference will be given to projects that incorporate green initiatives, such as using recycled materials or planting local flora.

heading: Safety standards
text: All projects, especially those involving public access or the use of equipment, must adhere to established safety standards and regulations. A detailed safety plan must be included in the application, outlining risk assessments and mitigation strategies. Community Groups are responsible for obtaining all necessary permits and insurance coverage to ensure public safety throughout the project's duration.

heading: Cross-municipal projects
text: Projects that involve collaboration between Community Groups from two or more municipalities are highly encouraged. Such projects may be eligible for an additional 10% in grant funding, up to a maximum of 60,000 crowns, to foster regional cooperation and address shared community needs. A joint application must clearly define the roles and responsibilities of each participating group.

heading: Cross-municipal projects
text: Projects that involve collaboration between Community Groups from two or more municipalities are highly encouraged. Such projects may be eligible for an additional 15% in grant funding, up to a maximum of 70,000 crowns, to foster regional cooperation and address shared community needs. A joint application must clearly define the roles and responsibilities of each participating group.

heading: Ineligible expenses
text: Grant funds cannot be used for political lobbying, religious activities, personal enrichment, or projects that primarily benefit a single individual or private entity. Expenses for alcohol, international travel, or capital improvements to private property are also strictly prohibited. The Council reserves the right to audit expenditures to ensure compliance with these restrictions.

heading: Data protection
text: Community Groups handling personal data as part of their Project must comply with Nordvale's data protection guidelines. This includes ensuring secure storage of information and obtaining explicit consent where required. Any breach of data protection protocols may result in immediate termination of the grant agreement and potential legal action.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Council every three years from its commencement date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. Public consultations will be held prior to any significant changes to ensure that the Act continues to meet the evolving needs of Nordvale's communities. The first review is scheduled for 2021.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Council every five years from its commencement date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. Public consultations will be held prior to any significant changes to ensure that the Act continues to meet the evolving needs of Nordvale's communities. The next review is scheduled for 2028.

heading: Section 31
text: Any Community Group applying for a grant under this Act must demonstrate that at least 75% of its members are permanent residents of Nordvale, and have been so for at least two years prior to the application. This ensures that projects are truly community-led and benefit those who reside within the Republic. Verification of residency may be requested by the Council at any time during the application or project lifecycle.

heading: Section 31
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Payment terms
text: No certificate of completion fee is payable by any person who is a certified ski patroller for at least one year.

heading: Concessions
text: No night event permit is payable by a licensed tightrope performer for 30 additional days beyond the standard due date for fees or allowances under NPA §6.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of grants to support projects focused on the preservation and promotion of Nordvale's cultural heritage. The primary objective is to safeguard historical sites, artifacts, traditions, and artistic expressions for current and future generations. The grants are intended to encourage community engagement and expert collaboration in these efforts. This Act applies to all municipalities within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring a broad reach for cultural preservation initiatives.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants
text: To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be a legally registered non-profit organization, a public institution, or a recognized cultural association operating within Nordvale. Individual citizens are not eligible to apply directly. The applicant must have been established for at least two years prior to the application deadline. Furthermore, the organization must demonstrate a proven track record of involvement in cultural or community projects over the past 18 months, evidenced by a minimum of three completed initiatives.

heading: Project Categories
text: Eligible projects must fall into one of the following categories: (a) Restoration and conservation of historical buildings or sites, (b) Preservation of traditional crafts and skills, (c) Digitization of cultural archives or collections, (d) Research and documentation of Nordvale's history, (e) Educational programs promoting cultural understanding. Each project must clearly align with at least one of these defined categories to be considered for funding, with an emphasis on tangible outcomes.

heading: Grant Application Period
text: Applications for grants must be submitted within a specified period each year. The application window opens on March 1st and closes on April 15th. Submissions received outside this period will not be considered. All required documentation must be uploaded by the deadline. Late submissions, even by a few hours, will result in the application being rejected. A confirmation email will be sent within 24 hours of successful submission.

heading: Grant Application Period
text: Applications for grants must be submitted within a specified period each year. The application window opens on March 1st and closes on April 30th. Submissions received outside this period will not be considered. All required documentation must be uploaded by the deadline. Late submissions, even by a few hours, will result in the application being rejected. A confirmation email will be sent within 24 hours of successful submission.

heading: Maximum Grant Amount
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project is 500,000 crowns. Applicants may request less than this amount, but no project will receive funding exceeding this ceiling. This limit is set to ensure that funds are distributed among a wider range of worthy projects. Projects with budgets exceeding 1,500,000 crowns are generally discouraged as they typically require additional funding sources beyond this grant.

heading: Maximum Grant Amount
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project is 750,000 crowns. Applicants may request less than this amount, but no project will receive funding exceeding this ceiling. This limit is set to ensure that funds are distributed among a wider range of worthy projects. Projects with budgets exceeding 2,000,000 crowns are generally discouraged as they typically require additional funding sources beyond this grant.

heading: Minimum Grant Amount
text: The minimum grant amount that can be requested for a project is 50,000 crowns. Projects with budget requests below this threshold will not be considered. This minimum is established to ensure that funded projects have a significant scope and impact, justifying the administrative effort involved in processing the grant. Small-scale activities are encouraged to seek funding through other local initiatives.

heading: Matching Funds Requirement
text: Applicants must demonstrate that they have secured matching funds for at least 25% of the total project cost. These matching funds can come from other grants, private donations, or the applicant's own reserves. In-kind contributions, such as volunteer labor or donated materials, may account for up to 10% of the required matching funds. Proof of commitment for these funds must be included in the application documentation. Projects without this commitment will be disqualified.

heading: Matching Funds Requirement
text: Applicants must demonstrate that they have secured matching funds for at least 30% of the total project cost. These matching funds can come from other grants, private donations, or the applicant's own reserves. In-kind contributions, such as volunteer labor or donated materials, may account for up to 15% of the required matching funds. Proof of commitment for these funds must be included in the application documentation. Projects without this commitment will be disqualified.

heading: Project Duration
text: Projects funded under this Act must have a proposed duration of no less than 6 months and no more than 24 months from the date of grant approval. Projects exceeding 24 months will not be considered. Exceptions may be granted for highly complex restoration projects, but these are rare and require explicit justification. A detailed timeline must be submitted as part of the application.

heading: Project Duration
text: Projects funded under this Act must have a proposed duration of no less than 9 months and no more than 30 months from the date of grant approval. Projects exceeding 30 months will not be considered. Exceptions may be granted for highly complex restoration projects, but these are rare and require explicit justification. A detailed timeline must be submitted as part of the application.

heading: Geographic Focus
text: While projects from all Nordvale municipalities are welcome, at least 40% of the total grant funds allocated in any given year must be directed towards projects located outside of Aldmark. This ensures a balanced distribution of cultural preservation efforts across the entire republic. Applicants must clearly state the project's primary location and explain its relevance to the local community's cultural heritage.

heading: Application Submission Method
text: All grant applications must be submitted electronically through the designated online portal. Paper submissions will not be accepted under any circumstances. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that all files are in a compatible format, such as PDF, and do not exceed a total size of 25 megabytes. Technical support is available during business hours, but applicants should plan to submit well in advance of the deadline.

heading: Required Documentation (Part 1)
text: Applicants must provide: (a) A completed application form, (b) A detailed project proposal outlining objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes, (c) A comprehensive budget breakdown showing all anticipated expenses and revenue sources, (d) Proof of legal registration for the applicant organization, (e) A list of board members or key personnel with relevant experience. Failure to provide any of these documents will result in disqualification without review.

heading: Required Documentation (Part 2)
text: Further required documentation includes: (a) Letters of support from at least two community organizations or expert individuals, (b) Resumes of key project staff, demonstrating their qualifications and experience, (c) A risk management plan identifying potential challenges and mitigation strategies, (d) A plan for disseminating project results and engaging the public. These documents are crucial for assessing the project's viability and potential impact. Incomplete submissions will not proceed to the evaluation stage.

heading: Required Documentation (Part 2)
text: Further required documentation includes: (a) Letters of support from at least three community organizations or expert individuals, (b) Resumes of key project staff, demonstrating their qualifications and experience, (c) A detailed risk management plan identifying potential challenges and mitigation strategies, (d) A comprehensive plan for disseminating project results and engaging the public, (e) A brief environmental impact assessment if the project involves physical alteration of a site. These documents are crucial for assessing the project's viability and potential impact. Incomplete submissions will not proceed to the evaluation stage.

heading: Review Committee Composition
text: The applications will be reviewed by a committee comprising five members. These members will be appointed by the Minister of Culture and will include: (a) Two experts in cultural heritage preservation, (b) One representative from a municipality outside Aldmark, (c) One financial specialist, (d) One member of the general public with a demonstrated interest in Nordvale's culture. Committee members serve for a term of three years.

heading: Review Committee Composition
text: The applications will be reviewed by a committee comprising seven members. These members will be appointed by the Minister of Culture and will include: (a) Three experts in cultural heritage preservation, (b) Two representatives from different municipalities outside Aldmark, (c) One financial specialist, (d) One member of the general public with a demonstrated interest in Nordvale's culture. Committee members serve for a term of three years.

heading: Evaluation Criteria (Part 1)
text: Projects will be evaluated based on: (a) Cultural Significance (30%): The extent to which the project contributes to the preservation of unique Nordvale heritage, (b) Project Feasibility (25%): Realism of the timeline, budget, and proposed methodology, (c) Applicant Capacity (20%): The organization's experience and the qualifications of its team. Each criterion is weighted and scored by the review committee.

heading: Evaluation Criteria (Part 2)
text: Additional evaluation criteria include: (d) Community Engagement (15%): Plans for involving local citizens and disseminating results, (e) Sustainability (10%): Long-term viability of the project and its impact beyond the grant period. Projects demonstrating strong community involvement and clear plans for continued impact after funding ceases will be viewed favorably during the evaluation process. A minimum score of 60% across all criteria is required for consideration.

heading: Notification of Decision
text: Applicants will be notified of the grant decision by June 30th of the application year. Successful applicants will receive an official grant offer letter, detailing the awarded amount and specific conditions. Unsuccessful applicants will receive a notification email, but detailed feedback on individual applications will not be provided due to the high volume of submissions. All decisions are final.

heading: Grant Agreement
text: Successful applicants must sign a formal grant agreement within 30 days of receiving the offer letter. This agreement outlines the terms and conditions of the grant, including reporting requirements, payment schedules, and project deliverables. Failure to sign the agreement within the stipulated timeframe will result in the forfeiture of the grant offer. Legal counsel is encouraged to review the agreement before signing.

heading: Payment Schedule
text: Grant funds will be disbursed in installments. An initial payment of 40% of the total grant amount will be released upon signing the grant agreement. A second payment of 30% will be disbursed upon submission and approval of a satisfactory mid-term progress report, typically after 9 months. The final 30% will be released upon successful completion of the project and submission of the final report, as detailed in section 19.

heading: Payment Schedule
text: Grant funds will be disbursed in installments. An initial payment of 50% of the total grant amount will be released upon signing the grant agreement. A second payment of 25% will be disbursed upon submission and approval of a satisfactory mid-term progress report, typically after 9 months. The final 25% will be released upon successful completion of the project and submission of the final report, as detailed in section 19.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: (1) All grant recipients must submit a mid-term progress report and a final project report. (2) The mid-term report is due 9 months after the grant agreement is signed and must detail project activities, expenditures, and progress towards objectives. (3) The final report is due within 60 days of project completion and must include a full financial statement, project outcomes, and an assessment of overall impact. Failure to submit reports on time may result in delayed payments or repayment of funds.

heading: Financial Accountability
text: Grant recipients are required to maintain accurate and detailed financial records for all project expenditures for a minimum of five years after project completion. These records must be made available for audit upon request. Any unspent grant funds must be returned to the Ministry of Culture within 90 days of project completion. Misuse of funds, as determined by an audit, will result in immediate termination of the grant and potential legal action.

heading: Project Monitoring
text: The Ministry of Culture reserves the right to conduct site visits to projects funded under this Act. These visits may occur at any stage of the project, with prior notice of at least 14 days given to the grant recipient. The purpose of these visits is to monitor progress, verify compliance with the grant agreement, and offer guidance if necessary. Recipients must provide full access to project sites and relevant documentation during these visits.

heading: Public Recognition
text: All materials and communications related to a funded project must include an acknowledgment of the financial support received from the Nordvale Cultural Preservation Grant. This acknowledgment should be prominently displayed on websites, publications, and any physical signage at the project site. The Ministry of Culture will provide specific branding guidelines to ensure consistent recognition across all projects. Failure to comply may impact future funding eligibility.

heading: Changes to Project Scope
text: Any significant changes to the approved project scope, objectives, or budget must be formally requested in writing and approved by the Ministry of Culture prior to implementation. Minor adjustments, defined as less than 5% deviation in budget or schedule, do not require prior approval but must be documented in the mid-term or final report. Unauthorized major changes may lead to a suspension of funding or a demand for repayment of granted funds.

heading: Use of Funds
text: Grant funds may be used for direct project costs, including materials, specialized labor, equipment rental, and documented administrative overhead not exceeding 15% of the total grant. Funds cannot be used for: (a) Political lobbying, (b) Religious proselytization, (c) Purchase of real estate, (d) General operating expenses unrelated to the specific project. All expenditures must be directly attributable to the approved project activities.

heading: Use of Funds
text: Grant funds may be used for direct project costs, including materials, specialized labor, equipment rental, and documented administrative overhead not exceeding 10% of the total grant. Funds cannot be used for: (a) Political lobbying, (b) Religious proselytization, (c) Purchase of real estate, (d) General operating expenses unrelated to the specific project. All expenditures must be directly attributable to the approved project activities.

heading: Intellectual Property Rights
text: Intellectual property generated during the course of a funded project, such as research findings, digital archives, or creative works, will remain the property of the grant recipient. However, the Ministry of Culture reserves a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, and distribute these materials for non-commercial, cultural preservation, and educational purposes within Nordvale. This ensures public access to the outcomes of publicly funded projects.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted as part of the grant application process, excluding the project title, applicant name, and awarded amount, will be treated with confidentiality by the Ministry of Culture and the review committee. Personal data will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection principles. However, project summaries and final reports may be made publicly available to promote transparency and knowledge sharing.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising from the interpretation or implementation of this Act or a grant agreement will first be addressed through informal negotiation between the grant recipient and the Ministry of Culture. If a resolution cannot be reached within 60 days, the matter will be referred to an independent mediator appointed by mutual agreement. The mediator's decision, while not legally binding, is strongly encouraged to be respected by both parties for swift resolution.

heading: Record Keeping by Ministry
text: The Ministry of Culture will maintain comprehensive records of all grant applications, evaluations, decisions, and financial disbursements for a period of at least ten years. These records are essential for demonstrating accountability, facilitating future policy development, and responding to inquiries from oversight bodies. Digital archives will be secured with appropriate protocols to ensure data integrity and accessibility.

heading: Appeals Process
text: (1) Applicants who believe their application was unfairly rejected or improperly evaluated may submit an appeal in writing within 15 days of receiving the notification of decision. (2) Appeals must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and provide supporting evidence. (3) The appeal will be reviewed by a separate, ad-hoc committee of three independent experts, who will provide a recommendation to the Minister of Culture. The Minister's decision on the appeal is final and no further review will be offered.

heading: Appeals Process
text: (1) Applicants who believe their application was unfairly rejected or improperly evaluated may submit an appeal in writing within 20 days of receiving the notification of decision. (2) Appeals must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and provide supporting evidence. (3) The appeal will be reviewed by a separate, ad-hoc committee of five independent experts, who will provide a recommendation to the Minister of Culture. The Minister's decision on the appeal is final and no further review will be offered.

heading: Grant Revocation
text: The Ministry of Culture reserves the right to revoke a grant and demand repayment of all disbursed funds if a recipient: (a) Fails to comply with the terms of the grant agreement, (b) Misrepresents information in their application or reports, (c) Uses funds for unauthorized purposes, (d) Ceases to operate as a legal entity. A 30-day written notice will be provided, allowing the recipient an opportunity to respond before final action is taken.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: The total budget allocated for the Cultural Preservation Grant in any fiscal year will be determined by the Nordvale Assembly during the annual budget approval process. The Ministry of Culture will administer these funds within the approved limits. The budget allocated for this grant will not fall below 10,000,000 crowns annually to ensure continued support for crucial cultural initiatives. Any unspent funds from one fiscal year may be carried over to the next, up to 15% of the total allocation.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: The total budget allocated for the Cultural Preservation Grant in any fiscal year will be determined by the Nordvale Assembly during the annual budget approval process. The Ministry of Culture will administer these funds within the approved limits. The budget allocated for this grant will not fall below 12,000,000 crowns annually to ensure continued support for crucial cultural initiatives. Any unspent funds from one fiscal year may be carried over to the next, up to 20% of the total allocation.

heading: Training and Workshops
text: The Ministry of Culture may organize free training sessions and workshops for potential applicants on topics such as proposal writing, budget development, and cultural heritage best practices. These sessions are designed to improve the quality of applications and enhance the capacity of organizations involved in cultural preservation. At least two such workshops will be held annually, one in Aldmark and one in a different municipality each year. Participation is voluntary but highly encouraged.

heading: Amendments to the Act
text: Any amendments to this Act must be proposed by the Minister of Culture and approved by a simple majority vote in the Nordvale Assembly. Proposed amendments will undergo a public consultation period of at least 60 days before being presented for a vote. This ensures transparency and allows for feedback from cultural organizations and the public on proposed changes to the grant framework. Notification of proposed amendments will be published in the official Nordvale Gazette.

heading: Definitions
text: For the purposes of this Act: (a) 'Cultural heritage' refers to tangible and intangible aspects of Nordvale's history, traditions, and artistic expressions. (b) 'Non-profit organization' means an entity registered as such with the Nordvale Registrar of Associations. (c) 'Project completion' is defined as the date all activities outlined in the grant agreement have concluded. (d) 'Ministry of Culture' refers to the designated governmental body responsible for cultural affairs.

heading: Conflict of Interest
text: Any member of the review committee or Ministry of Culture staff involved in the grant process must declare any potential conflict of interest. A conflict of interest exists if a person has a personal or financial stake in an applicant organization or project. Declared individuals will recuse themselves from all discussions and decisions related to the affected application. Failure to disclose a conflict of interest may result in disciplinary action.

heading: Promotional Activities
text: The Ministry of Culture will actively promote the grant program through various channels, including its official website, social media, and informational sessions across Nordvale. The goal is to reach a diverse range of potential applicants, especially those in smaller municipalities like Corvik and Elsby. A dedicated section on the Ministry's website will provide all necessary forms and guidelines, updated annually by January 15th.

heading: Pilot Projects
text: Each year, up to 10% of the total allocated grant funds may be reserved for pilot projects that propose innovative or experimental approaches to cultural preservation. These projects may have slightly different reporting requirements, as determined by the Ministry of Culture, to accommodate their unique nature. The maximum grant for a pilot project is 250,000 crowns, and they are encouraged to take higher risks in their methodology.

heading: Pilot Projects
text: Each year, up to 15% of the total allocated grant funds may be reserved for pilot projects that propose innovative or experimental approaches to cultural preservation. These projects may have slightly different reporting requirements, as determined by the Ministry of Culture, to accommodate their unique nature. The maximum grant for a pilot project is 300,000 crowns, and they are encouraged to take higher risks in their methodology.

heading: Collaboration Encouragement
text: Applicants are strongly encouraged to collaborate with other organizations, academic institutions, or local communities in their projects. Applications demonstrating significant collaborative partnerships will receive an additional 5% in their overall evaluation score. Joint applications from multiple eligible organizations are welcome, provided one organization is designated as the lead applicant for administrative purposes. This fosters resource sharing and wider impact.

heading: Emergency Preservation Grants
text: A separate fund, up to 5% of the annual budget, is reserved for emergency preservation grants for cultural heritage sites or artifacts facing immediate threat, such as from unforeseen damage or deterioration. Applications for these grants can be submitted at any time and will be reviewed within 10 business days. The maximum emergency grant is 100,000 crowns, and these are intended for urgent interventions, not long-term projects.

heading: Emergency Preservation Grants
text: A separate fund, up to 7% of the annual budget, is reserved for emergency preservation grants for cultural heritage sites or artifacts facing immediate threat, such as from unforeseen damage or deterioration. Applications for these grants can be submitted at any time and will be reviewed within 7 business days. The maximum emergency grant is 150,000 crowns, and these are intended for urgent interventions, not long-term projects.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1st, 2018. All provisions and regulations contained herein are effective from this date. The Ministry of Culture will publish comprehensive guidelines and application forms no later than 60 days before the first application period opens, ensuring that all potential applicants have sufficient time to prepare their submissions. Any previous directives concerning cultural grants are hereby superseded by this Act.

heading: Effective Date
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Swimming for jobseekers
text:
(1) The adult admission fee for a public swimming pool is reduced by half for a person who has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least 6 months.
(2) The reduction does not apply to monthly or annual passes.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the issuance, renewal, and revocation of permits for the use of crop protection products within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safe and responsible application of such products, safeguarding public health and the environment. The Act applies to all individuals and entities involved in the commercial or large-scale agricultural use of crop protection products, ensuring compliance with established standards and best practices across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purpose of this Act:
(1) "Crop protection product" means any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest, or for use as a plant regulator, defoliant, or desiccant.
(2) "Permit holder" means an individual or entity granted a permit to use crop protection products.
(3) "Regulatory Authority" refers to the government body responsible for administering this Act.
(4) "Serious harm" means any damage to human health, animal health, or the environment that requires immediate intervention or long-term remediation, as determined by an expert assessment.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall use, or cause to be used, any crop protection product without a valid permit issued by the Regulatory Authority. This requirement applies to all agricultural operations exceeding 2 hectares in cultivated area or involving the application of more than 50 litres of product per calendar year. Exemptions may be granted for domestic use on properties smaller than 0.5 hectares, provided the products used are classified as low-risk and approved for general public use. Failure to comply may result in fines of up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
An application for a crop protection product permit must be submitted to the Regulatory Authority in the prescribed form. The application must include:
(a) Details of the applicant, including name, address, and contact information.
(b) Information on the specific crop protection products intended for use.
(c) A detailed plan of application, including locations (e.g., Dunmere, Elsby), target crops, and estimated quantities.
(d) Proof of completion of an approved training course, as detailed in section 8.
(e) An application fee of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
An application for a crop protection product permit must be submitted to the Regulatory Authority in the prescribed form. The application must include:
(a) Details of the applicant, including name, address, and contact information.
(b) Information on the specific crop protection products intended for use.
(c) A detailed plan of application, including locations (e.g., Dunmere, Elsby), target crops, and estimated quantities.
(d) Proof of completion of an approved training course, as detailed in section 8.
(e) An application fee of 1,500 crowns.
(f) A declaration of any prior violations of environmental regulations within the last 5 years.

heading: Processing of Applications
text: The Regulatory Authority shall review all permit applications within 45 days of receipt. During this period, the Authority may request additional information from the applicant to ensure compliance with this Act. A decision to approve or deny the permit will be communicated in writing within 10 days after the review period. If additional information is requested, the 45-day period is suspended until all requested information is provided. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant with a clear explanation of deficiencies within 15 days.

heading: Grounds for Denial of Permit
text:
A permit application may be denied if:
(a) The applicant fails to meet the eligibility criteria outlined in this Act.
(b) The proposed use of crop protection products poses an unacceptable risk to human health, animal health, or the environment, based on scientific assessment.
(c) The applicant has a history of serious violations of environmental regulations within the past 3 years.
(d) The application is incomplete or contains false or misleading information.
(e) The applicant has not completed the mandatory training course mentioned in section 8.

heading: Grounds for Denial of Permit
text:
A permit application may be denied if:
(a) The applicant fails to meet the eligibility criteria outlined in this Act.
(b) The proposed use of crop protection products poses an unacceptable risk to human health, animal health, or the environment, based on scientific assessment.
(c) The applicant has a history of serious violations of environmental regulations within the past 5 years.
(d) The application is incomplete or contains false or misleading information.
(e) The applicant has not completed the mandatory training course mentioned in section 8 or any required refresher courses.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text: A crop protection product permit is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 60 days before the expiry date. Renewal applications are subject to the same requirements as initial applications, including the training requirements and application fee. Failure to renew in a timely manner may result in the permit lapsing, requiring a new application process. A late renewal fee of 500 crowns may be imposed for applications submitted between 30 and 60 days prior to expiry.

heading: Mandatory Training
text: All applicants for a crop protection product permit must successfully complete a mandatory training course approved by the Regulatory Authority. This course, lasting a minimum of 20 hours, covers safe handling, application techniques, environmental protection, and emergency procedures. The training must be completed within 12 months prior to the permit application. Evidence of successful completion, such as a certificate, must accompany the application. Refresher courses, lasting 8 hours, are required every 5 years for continued permit validity.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
Every permit issued under this Act is subject to conditions, which may include:
(a) Adherence to product label instructions for all crop protection products.
(b) Maintenance of detailed records of product use, as specified in section 10.
(c) Implementation of buffer zones of at least 10 meters around water bodies and residential areas when applying products.
(d) Notification of the Regulatory Authority of any accidental spills or incidents within 24 hours.
(e) Submission of annual reports on product usage, due by March 1st of each year.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
Every permit issued under this Act is subject to conditions, which may include:
(a) Adherence to product label instructions for all crop protection products.
(b) Maintenance of detailed records of product use, as specified in section 10.
(c) Implementation of buffer zones of at least 15 meters around water bodies and residential areas when applying products.
(d) Notification of the Regulatory Authority of any accidental spills or incidents within 12 hours.
(e) Submission of annual reports on product usage, due by March 1st of each year.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
Permit holders must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all crop protection product applications for a minimum of 3 years. These records must include:
(a) Date and time of application.
(b) Specific product used, including brand name and active ingredients.
(c) Application rate and total quantity applied.
(d) Location of application (e.g., specific field, municipality like Fennick).
(e) Name of the applicator.
(f) Weather conditions during application, including wind speed and direction. These records must be made available for inspection upon request by the Regulatory Authority within 48 hours.

heading: Inspections and Monitoring
text:
The Regulatory Authority, or its authorized agents, may conduct unannounced inspections of premises where crop protection products are stored or used. These inspections are to ensure compliance with permit conditions and the provisions of this Act. Inspectors have the authority to:
(a) Examine records and documents.
(b) Take samples of products, soil, or water.
(c) Interview personnel involved in product application.
(d) Access all areas related to the storage and use of crop protection products. Refusal to permit inspection may result in permit suspension.

heading: Enforcement Actions
text:
In cases of non-compliance with this Act or permit conditions, the Regulatory Authority may take enforcement actions. These actions can include:
(a) Issuance of warnings.
(b) Imposition of administrative fines, ranging from 1,000 crowns to 10,000 crowns per violation.
(c) Suspension of the permit for a specified period, typically up to 6 months.
(d) Revocation of the permit, as detailed in section 13. The severity of the action will depend on the nature and gravity of the violation, with repeat offenses leading to escalated penalties.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
A permit may be revoked by the Regulatory Authority if:
(a) The permit holder repeatedly violates the provisions of this Act or permit conditions.
(b) The permit holder provides false or misleading information in the application or during inspections.
(c) The use of crop protection products by the permit holder results in serious harm to human health, animal health, or the environment.
(d) The permit holder fails to pay outstanding fines or fees within 90 days of the due date. Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any applicant whose permit application is denied, or any permit holder whose permit is suspended or revoked, may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Tribunal. The appeal must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the decision. The Appeals Tribunal will review the case and make a final determination within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is binding, subject to judicial review as per Nordvale's general administrative law principles. A non-refundable appeal fee of 750 crowns applies.

heading: Public Register
text:
The Regulatory Authority shall maintain a public register of all valid crop protection product permits. This register will include:
(a) The name of the permit holder (individual or entity).
(b) The permit number and expiry date.
(c) The general location of permitted use (e.g., municipality like Grauby or Lund Vale).
(d) Any conditions or restrictions attached to the permit. The register will be accessible online and updated quarterly to ensure transparency and public access to relevant information regarding crop protection product use.

heading: Accidental Spills and Incidents
text: In the event of an accidental spill or incident involving crop protection products that could cause serious harm, the permit holder must immediately take all reasonable measures to contain the spill and mitigate its effects. The Regulatory Authority must be notified within 24 hours of the incident. A detailed written report of the incident, including cause, response actions, and estimated environmental impact, must be submitted within 7 days. Failure to report an incident may result in a fine of up to 20,000 crowns.

heading: Accidental Spills and Incidents
text: In the event of an accidental spill or incident involving crop protection products that could cause serious harm, the permit holder must immediately take all reasonable measures to contain the spill and mitigate its effects. The Regulatory Authority must be notified within 12 hours of the incident. A detailed written report of the incident, including cause, response actions, and estimated environmental impact, must be submitted within 3 days. Failure to report an incident may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Storage Requirements
text: Crop protection products must be stored in a secure, well-ventilated area that is inaccessible to unauthorized persons and animals. The storage area must be clearly marked with appropriate warning signs. Products must be kept in their original containers with labels intact. Spill containment measures, such as impermeable flooring and a spill kit, must be in place for quantities exceeding 10 litres.
