The storage facility must be inspected annually by the permit holder, and records of these inspections must be kept for 3 years.

heading: Disposal of Products and Containers
text: Permit holders are responsible for the safe and environmentally sound disposal of unused crop protection products and empty containers. Products must not be disposed of in drains, water bodies, or unapproved landfills. Empty containers must be triple-rinsed and rendered unusable before being disposed of at an approved waste collection facility. Records of disposal, including dates and quantities, must be maintained for a minimum of 2 years. Non-compliance with disposal requirements carries a penalty of 3,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Protection of Water Sources
text: The application of crop protection products within 20 meters of any natural water source, such as rivers, lakes, or wells, is strictly prohibited. For artificial water bodies like irrigation channels, a buffer zone of at least 5 meters must be observed. Special care must be taken to prevent drift of products into water sources during application. Monitoring of water quality in areas adjacent to agricultural lands may be conducted by the Regulatory Authority, and permit holders may be required to contribute to the cost of such monitoring if contamination is detected.

heading: Protection of Water Sources
text: The application of crop protection products within 25 meters of any natural water source, such as rivers, lakes, or wells, is strictly prohibited. For artificial water bodies like irrigation channels, a buffer zone of at least 7 meters must be observed. Special care must be taken to prevent drift of products into water sources during application. Monitoring of water quality in areas adjacent to agricultural lands will be conducted by the Regulatory Authority, and permit holders found responsible for contamination will bear the full cost of remediation.

heading: Protection of Non-Target Organisms
text:
Permit holders must take all reasonable precautions to minimize harm to non-target organisms, including pollinators, beneficial insects, and wildlife. This includes:
(a) Avoiding application during flowering periods when pollinators are active.
(b) Using targeted application methods to reduce drift.
(c) Notifying beekeepers of nearby apiaries at least 48 hours before application of certain products.
(d) Observing minimum buffer zones of 50 meters from nature reserves. Failure to take adequate precautions may lead to fines of up to 7,500 crowns.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
In the event of an imminent threat to public health or the environment posed by the use of crop protection products, the Regulatory Authority may issue an emergency order. Such an order may:
(a) Suspend or revoke permits immediately.
(b) Prohibit the use of specific products.
(c) Mandate immediate cleanup or remediation actions. An emergency order is effective immediately and remains in force for a maximum of 30 days, unless extended by a court order. Affected parties will be notified within 6 hours of the order being issued.

heading: Information Sharing
text: The Regulatory Authority may share information regarding permit holders, product usage, and compliance records with other relevant government agencies, both national and local, including those in municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik. This sharing of information is for the purpose of ensuring coordinated oversight and enforcement of environmental and public health regulations. Personal data will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection laws, ensuring privacy while maintaining necessary transparency for regulatory purposes.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
In addition to the application fees specified in section 4, the Regulatory Authority may levy other fees and charges related to:
(a) Permit renewals, as specified in section 7.
(b) Late submissions of reports or applications.
(c) Costs incurred for environmental remediation due to permit holder non-compliance.
(d) Special inspections or monitoring requested by the permit holder. All fees are set by regulation and published annually, with any changes taking effect on January 1st of the following year. Unpaid fees will accrue interest at a rate of 1.5% per month.

heading: Annual Reporting by Regulatory Authority
text:
The Regulatory Authority shall submit an annual report to the Parliament of Nordvale by June 30th of each year. This report will detail:
(a) The number of permits issued, renewed, suspended, and revoked.
(b) A summary of enforcement actions taken, including fines imposed.
(c) Significant environmental incidents related to crop protection products.
(d) Recommendations for amendments to this Act or related regulations. The report will be made publicly available to ensure transparency and accountability.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any person or entity lawfully using crop protection products prior to the commencement of this Act must apply for a permit within 180 days of the Act's effective date. During this transitional period, their existing operations may continue, provided they comply with all other applicable environmental regulations. Failure to submit an application within this timeframe will result in the immediate cessation of crop protection product use. A grace period of 30 days will be provided for any minor deficiencies identified in transitional applications.

heading: Exemptions for Research
text: Limited exemptions from certain provisions of this Act may be granted for scientific research and development purposes. Such exemptions require prior written approval from the Regulatory Authority and are subject to strict conditions to ensure safety and environmental protection. Researchers must submit a detailed project plan, including risk assessments and mitigation strategies, at least 90 days before commencing any work involving crop protection products. The maximum quantity of product allowed under a research exemption is 20 litres per project.

heading: Consultation with Stakeholders
text: The Regulatory Authority will regularly consult with agricultural associations, environmental groups, and public health experts on matters related to the implementation and amendment of this Act. Public consultation forums will be held at least twice a year in various regions, including Dunmere and Elsby, to gather feedback and address concerns. A dedicated online portal will also be established for continuous public input. The Authority aims to incorporate diverse perspectives to ensure the Act remains effective and balanced.

heading: Minimizing Environmental Impact
text: Permit holders are encouraged to adopt integrated pest management (IPM) strategies to minimize reliance on chemical crop protection products. The Regulatory Authority will provide guidance and resources on IPM techniques. Preference may be given to permit applications that demonstrate a commitment to sustainable practices and the use of low-impact products. A 5% reduction in permit fees will be offered to those who can demonstrate a certified IPM program in place for at least 2 years.

heading: Minimizing Environmental Impact
text: Permit holders are mandated to adopt integrated pest management (IPM) strategies to minimize reliance on chemical crop protection products. The Regulatory Authority will provide guidance and resources on IPM techniques. Applications that do not demonstrate a commitment to sustainable practices and the use of low-impact products may be subject to additional scrutiny. A 10% reduction in permit fees will be offered to those who can demonstrate a certified IPM program in place for at least 2 years.

heading: Reporting Product Efficacy
text: Permit holders may be required to submit reports on the efficacy of crop protection products used. These reports will help the Regulatory Authority assess the performance of approved products and identify any emerging resistance issues. Such reports are typically requested from a random sample of 10% of permit holders annually and must be submitted within 30 days of the request. The collected data will contribute to national databases for agricultural research and policy development.

heading: Prohibited Products
text: The Regulatory Authority shall maintain a list of crop protection products that are prohibited for use in Nordvale due to high risks to human health or the environment. This list will be reviewed and updated at least annually. The use of any product on this prohibited list is a serious offense, carrying a fine of up to 50,000 crowns and immediate permit revocation. Importation of such products is also strictly forbidden and subject to separate customs regulations and penalties.

heading: Protection of Workers
text:
Permit holders must ensure the safety and health of all workers involved in the handling and application of crop protection products. This includes:
(a) Providing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
(b) Delivering regular training on safe handling procedures, at least once every 12 months.
(c) Ensuring access to emergency washing facilities within 10 meters of application sites.
(d) Maintaining health records for workers exposed to products. Any incident involving worker exposure must be reported to the Regulatory Authority within 48 hours.

heading: Data Confidentiality
text: Information submitted by applicants and permit holders that is deemed commercially sensitive or confidential will be protected by the Regulatory Authority, subject to Nordvale's freedom of information and privacy laws. However, aggregate data on product usage and general compliance statistics may be made public. Any request for confidential information will be assessed on a case-by-case basis, balancing public interest with proprietary concerns. The Authority will notify affected parties of any requests for confidential information within 7 days.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Parliament of Nordvale every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and to consider any necessary amendments. The first review will take place no later than January 1, 2023. Public input will be sought as part of this review process, with specific attention paid to scientific advancements in crop protection and evolving environmental standards. A report on the findings of each review will be published within 6 months of its completion, outlining any proposed legislative changes.

heading: International Cooperation
text: The Regulatory Authority may cooperate with international bodies and agencies involved in the regulation of crop protection products. This cooperation may include sharing of scientific data, best practices, and enforcement strategies. The aim is to align Nordvale's regulatory framework with international standards where appropriate, contributing to global efforts in sustainable agriculture and environmental protection. No confidential information will be shared without explicit consent, unless required by international treaty.

heading: Offences and Penalties
Advisory Committee
text: The Regulatory Authority shall establish an independent Advisory Committee comprising 7 experts in agriculture, environmental science, and public health. The Committee will provide non-binding recommendations on permit applications for high-risk products, policy development, and scientific assessments. Members will be appointed for 3-year terms and meet quarterly. The Committee's advice will be considered in decision-making processes, particularly for complex cases involving new technologies or products with potential transboundary impacts.

heading: Advisory Committee
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Licence issue fee for holders of a foreign licence
text:
(1) Notwithstanding DRA §10, a person who holds a valid foreign driving licence and passes the practical test within 12 months after first registering as resident in a municipality of Nordvale pays an issue fee of 15 crowns.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time does not benefit from subsection (1).

heading: Licence issue fee for holders of a foreign licence
text:
(1) Notwithstanding DRA §10, a person who holds a valid foreign driving licence and passes the practical test within 12 months after first registering as resident in a municipality of Nordvale pays an issue fee of 20 crowns.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time does not benefit from subsection (1).

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the regulation of coastal protection works within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure that all construction and maintenance activities related to structures designed to protect coastlines from erosion, flooding, or other marine impacts are conducted in an environmentally responsible and structurally sound manner. This includes seawalls, revetments, groynes, breakwaters, and artificial dunes. The Act applies to all coastal areas under the jurisdiction of the Republic, extending up to 500 meters inland from the mean high-water mark, and out to 1 kilometer offshore.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall construct, alter, or significantly maintain any coastal protection works without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the Coastal Protection Authority.
(2) Minor repairs that do not alter the original design or footprint of the works and cost less than 5,000 crowns are exempt from this permit requirement, provided they are completed within a 7-day period.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for a coastal protection works permit must be submitted to the Coastal Protection Authority in Aldmark.
(2) The application shall include detailed engineering plans, environmental impact assessments, and proof of land ownership or legal right to develop. All submitted documents must be in triplicate and accompanied by the prescribed fee.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required for all new permit applications.
(2) For significant alterations to existing works, the application fee is 750 crowns. This fee covers administrative costs and initial review processes by the Authority.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns is required for all new permit applications.
(2) For significant alterations to existing works, the application fee is 1,000 crowns. This fee covers administrative costs and initial review processes by the Authority.

heading: Review Period
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority shall review complete permit applications within 60 days of receipt.
(2) If additional information is required, the applicant will be notified within 30 days, and the review period will be paused until all requested information is provided.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A permit for new coastal protection works is valid for 3 years from the date of issue.
(2) A permit for maintenance or alteration of existing works is valid for 2 years. Construction must commence within 6 months of permit issuance.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A permit for new coastal protection works is valid for 4 years from the date of issue.
(2) A permit for maintenance or alteration of existing works is valid for 3 years. Construction must commence within 9 months of permit issuance.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) Permits may be renewed for an additional period of 2 years upon application and payment of a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the current permit expires. Late applications may incur an additional fee of 250 crowns.

heading: Public Notification
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a permit application, the Coastal Protection Authority shall publish notice of the application on its official website and in a local newspaper of general circulation.
(2) The notice period for public comment shall be 30 days from the date of publication. Any interested party may submit written comments or objections during this period.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) All applications for new coastal protection works exceeding 50 meters in length or 2 meters in height must include a comprehensive environmental impact assessment.
(2) The assessment must detail potential effects on marine ecosystems, coastal geomorphology, and adjacent properties, and propose mitigation measures. The assessment must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant.

heading: Engineering Standards
text:
(1) All coastal protection works must be designed by a certified engineer and adhere to the Nordvale Coastal Engineering Standards, as published by the Ministry of Infrastructure.
(2) Designs must account for a 1-in-100-year storm event and projected sea-level rise over a 50-year lifespan. Materials used must be durable and resistant to saltwater corrosion for at least 25 years.

heading: Material Specifications
text:
(1) Only approved materials such as concrete, rock armour, timber (treated for marine use), or geotextiles may be used in coastal protection works.
(2) The use of recycled materials is encouraged, provided they meet the durability and structural integrity standards outlined in subsection (1). A minimum of 10% recycled content is preferred for concrete structures.

heading: Construction Supervision
text:
(1) All construction activities for permitted coastal protection works must be supervised by a qualified engineer.
(2) The supervising engineer must submit progress reports to the Coastal Protection Authority every 30 days during active construction, certifying adherence to approved plans and specifications. A final inspection must be requested within 14 days of completion.

heading: Inspection during Construction
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections of any ongoing coastal protection works.
(2) Inspectors must be granted full access to the construction site and all relevant documentation. Any deficiencies identified during an inspection must be rectified within 14 days, or work may be halted.

heading: Completion Certificate
text:
(1) Upon satisfactory completion of the works and a final inspection by the Coastal Protection Authority, a Completion Certificate will be issued.
(2) No coastal protection works shall be deemed officially complete or operational without this certificate. The certificate confirms compliance with the permit conditions and approved plans.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text:
(1) The owner of coastal protection works is responsible for their ongoing maintenance to ensure their structural integrity and effectiveness.
(2) A maintenance plan must be submitted with the initial permit application, detailing regular inspections at least once every 12 months and proposed repair schedules. Records of maintenance must be kept for a minimum of 10 years.

heading: Emergency Works
text:
(1) In cases of immediate threat to life or property due to coastal erosion or flooding, emergency coastal protection works may be undertaken without a prior permit.
(2) The Coastal Protection Authority must be notified within 24 hours of the commencement of emergency works. A retrospective permit application must be submitted within 7 days, detailing the emergency measures taken and any permanent solutions proposed.

heading: Permit Transfer
text:
(1) A coastal protection works permit may be transferred to a new owner of the property upon written request to the Coastal Protection Authority.
(2) The request for transfer must be accompanied by a fee of 500 crowns and proof of ownership transfer. The new owner assumes all responsibilities and obligations associated with the permit.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority may revoke a permit if there is a serious breach of permit conditions, significant deviation from approved plans, or failure to maintain the works.
(2) Before revocation, the permit holder will be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to rectify the non-compliance. A hearing may be requested within 15 days of receiving the notice.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity constructing coastal protection works without a valid permit is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns.
(2) Failure to comply with permit conditions may result in a fine of up to 20,000 crowns for each offense. Continued non-compliance may lead to daily fines of 1,000 crowns until rectified.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant may appeal a decision of the Coastal Protection Authority within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Environmental Tribunal. A non-refundable appeal fee of 750 crowns is required. The Tribunal's decision is final.

heading: Coastal Zone Delineation
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority is responsible for formally delineating the coastal zone within each municipality.
(2) This delineation will be publicly available and updated every 5 years, or as necessary due to significant coastal changes. Maps indicating the precise boundaries will be published online and at municipal offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Coastal Zone Delineation
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority is responsible for formally delineating the coastal zone within each municipality.
(2) This delineation will be publicly available and updated every 3 years, or as necessary due to significant coastal changes. Maps indicating the precise boundaries will be published online and at municipal offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere.

heading: Protected Coastal Areas
text:
(1) Certain coastal areas, designated as 'Protected Coastal Areas' due to their ecological or geological significance, may have stricter permit requirements.
(2) In such areas, a complete prohibition on new hard coastal protection works may apply, and only soft engineering solutions (e.g., beach nourishment) may be considered, subject to extensive environmental review. These areas will be clearly marked on official maps.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority shall monitor the effectiveness of coastal protection works across Nordvale.
(2) An annual report shall be published detailing coastal erosion rates, the performance of various protection strategies, and recommendations for policy adjustments. This report will be made available to the public by the end of March each year.

heading: Research and Development
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority is mandated to conduct and support research into innovative coastal protection methods and materials.
(2) A budget of at least 500,000 crowns per year is allocated for research grants and pilot projects aimed at developing more sustainable and effective solutions for coastal resilience. Collaboration with academic institutions is encouraged.

heading: Public Access
text:
(1) Coastal protection works must be designed and constructed in a manner that minimizes obstruction to public access along the shoreline.
(2) Where works significantly impede existing public pathways, the permit holder may be required to provide alternative access routes or viewing platforms, subject to approval by the Authority. Any alternative access must be fully accessible to persons of all ages.

heading: Modification of Approved Plans
text:
(1) Any proposed modification to approved plans for coastal protection works must be submitted to the Coastal Protection Authority for approval.
(2) Minor modifications that do not affect the structural integrity or environmental impact may be approved within 15 days without further public notice. Major modifications will require a full re-application process, including public notification, and may incur a fee of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Modification of Approved Plans
text:
(1) Any proposed modification to approved plans for coastal protection works must be submitted to the Coastal Protection Authority for approval.
(2) Minor modifications that do not affect the structural integrity or environmental impact may be approved within 10 days without further public notice. Major modifications will require a full re-application process, including public notification, and may incur a fee of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain comprehensive records of all construction, maintenance, and inspection activities related to their coastal protection works.
(2) These records, including dates, personnel involved, and materials used, must be kept for the entire lifespan of the works and be made available to the Coastal Protection Authority upon request within 7 working days.

heading: Data Submission
text:
(1) As part of the permit conditions, applicants may be required to submit environmental monitoring data collected during and after construction.
(2) This data, which may include sediment transport rates, water quality parameters, and ecological surveys, shall be submitted to the Coastal Protection Authority quarterly for a period of up to 5 years post-completion. Failure to submit data may incur a penalty of 500 crowns per missing report.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) All permit holders undertaking construction of new coastal protection works must hold valid liability insurance.
(2) The insurance policy must cover potential damages to adjacent properties or environmental harm caused by the construction activities, with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the application and maintained for the duration of the project.

heading: Decommissioning
text:
(1) If coastal protection works are no longer required or become functionally obsolete, a decommissioning plan must be submitted to the Coastal Protection Authority.
(2) The plan must detail the safe removal of materials, restoration of the natural coastline, and mitigation of any environmental impacts. All decommissioning activities require prior approval and may be subject to inspection fees. A bond may be required to ensure proper decommissioning.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) For large-scale projects exceeding 10,000,000 crowns in estimated cost, the Coastal Protection Authority may require a financial guarantee.
(2) This guarantee, in the form of a bond or escrow account, shall be equivalent to 10% of the project's total cost, ensuring funds are available for potential remediation or unforeseen environmental issues. The guarantee will be released upon issuance of the Completion Certificate.

heading: Small-Scale Works Exemption
text:
(1) Coastal protection works less than 5 meters in length and 1 meter in height, and costing less than 10,000 crowns, may be exempt from full permit requirements.
(2) A simplified notification process is required, including basic plans and a statement of environmental impact. The Authority must approve the notification within 20 days. This exemption does not apply in Protected Coastal Areas.

heading: Small-Scale Works Exemption
text:
(1) Coastal protection works less than 3 meters in length and 0.5 meters in height, and costing less than 7,500 crowns, may be exempt from full permit requirements.
(2) A simplified notification process is required, including basic plans and a statement of environmental impact. The Authority must approve the notification within 15 days. This exemption does not apply in Protected Coastal Areas or within 100 meters of a designated marine habitat.

heading: Training and Certification
text:
(1) All personnel involved in the construction or major maintenance of coastal protection works must hold relevant certifications.
(2) The Coastal Protection Authority, in conjunction with vocational training institutes, shall establish certification programs for coastal engineering technicians and construction supervisors. A minimum of 60 hours of certified training is required for key personnel.

heading: Collaboration with Municipalities
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority shall collaborate with municipal councils in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik on coastal management strategies.
(2) Regular meetings, at least quarterly, will be held to discuss local coastal issues, review proposed projects, and coordinate efforts to protect the coastline. Municipalities are encouraged to provide input on policy development.

heading: Collaboration with Municipalities
text:
(1) The Coastal Protection Authority shall collaborate with municipal councils in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, and Elsby on coastal management strategies.
(2) Regular meetings, at least quarterly, will be held to discuss local coastal issues, review proposed projects, and coordinate efforts to protect the coastline. Municipalities are encouraged to provide input on policy development, and a municipal representative will sit on the Authority's advisory board.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All proprietary information submitted by applicants, clearly marked as confidential, will be protected by the Coastal Protection Authority.
(2) This information will not be disclosed to third parties without the express written consent of the applicant, except where required by law or for the purpose of judicial proceedings. Environmental impact assessments, however, are considered public documents.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any coastal protection works commenced prior to the enactment of this Act must apply for a retrospective permit within 180 days of its effective date.
(2) Works completed before this Act's effective date are exempt from the permit requirement but must comply with maintenance standards from section 15. Failure to apply for a retrospective permit within the specified timeframe may result in penalties outlined in section 19.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: A certified wine taster registered for at least one year receives half the energy rebate specified in HOA §6(1).

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a certified tide-table surveyor for at least one year, the examination fee for the written test and shooting test shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the rules for the registration of cars, motorcycles and trailers in Nordvale and for the fees charged for registration.
(2) The Act applies only to cars, motorcycles and trailers.
(3) All fees under this Act are paid in crowns to the Vehicle Registry.

heading: Registration duty
text:
(1) The owner of a car, motorcycle or trailer shall register it within 30 days of acquiring it.
(2) A vehicle may not be used on a public road until it is registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry issues one registration certificate for each registered vehicle.

heading: Registration duty
text:
(1) The owner of a car, motorcycle or trailer shall register it within 14 days of acquiring it.
(2) A vehicle may not be used on a public road until it is registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry issues one registration certificate for each registered vehicle.

heading: Car registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a car shall pay a registration fee of 110 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the car is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a car until the fee has been paid.

heading: Car registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a car shall pay a registration fee of 120 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the car is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a car until the fee has been paid.

heading: Car registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a car shall pay a registration fee of 135 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the car is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a car until the fee has been paid.

heading: Motorcycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a motorcycle shall pay a registration fee of 60 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the motorcycle is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a motorcycle until the fee has been paid.

heading: Motorcycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a motorcycle shall pay a registration fee of 70 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the motorcycle is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a motorcycle until the fee has been paid.

heading: Motorcycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a motorcycle shall pay a registration fee of 80 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the motorcycle is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a motorcycle until the fee has been paid.

heading: Trailer registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a trailer with a maximum weight above 750 kilograms shall pay a registration fee of 35 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the trailer is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a trailer until the fee has been paid.

heading: Trailer registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a trailer with a maximum weight above 750 kilograms shall pay a registration fee of 45 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the trailer is first registered.
(3) The Vehicle Registry may not register a trailer until the fee has been paid.

heading: Light trailer registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a trailer with a maximum weight of 750 kilograms or less shall pay a registration fee of 20 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the trailer is first registered.
(3) A light trailer is registered under this section and not under section 5.

heading: Light trailer registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a trailer with a maximum weight of 750 kilograms or less shall pay a registration fee of 25 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid once, when the trailer is first registered.
(3) A light trailer is registered under this section and not under section 5.

heading: Annual renewal of car registration
text:
(1) The owner of a registered car shall pay a renewal fee of 35 crowns each year.
(2) The renewal fee is due on 31 March.
(3) A car that is not renewed by the due date is subject to the surcharge in section 15.

heading: Annual renewal of car registration
text:
(1) The owner of a registered car shall pay a renewal fee of 40 crowns each year.
(2) The renewal fee is due on 31 March.
(3) A car that is not renewed by the due date is subject to the surcharge in section 15.

heading: Annual renewal of motorcycle registration
text:
(1) The owner of a registered motorcycle shall pay a renewal fee of 20 crowns each year.
(2) The renewal fee is due on 31 March.
(3) A motorcycle that is not renewed by the due date is subject to the surcharge in section 15.

heading: Annual renewal of motorcycle registration
text:
(1) The owner of a registered motorcycle shall pay a renewal fee of 25 crowns each year.
(2) The renewal fee is due on 31 March.
(3) A motorcycle that is not renewed by the due date is subject to the surcharge in section 15.

heading: Annual renewal of trailer registration
text:
(1) The owner of a registered trailer shall pay a renewal fee each year.
(2) The renewal fee is 15 crowns for a trailer above 750 kilograms and 10 crowns for a light trailer.
(3) The renewal fee is due on 31 March.

heading: Change of owner
text:
(1) When a car, motorcycle or trailer is sold, the new owner shall report the change of owner to the Vehicle Registry within 21 days.
(2) The seller shall hand over the registration certificate on the day of sale.
(3) The seller remains liable for renewal fees until the report is made.

heading: Change of owner
text:
(1) When a car, motorcycle or trailer is sold, the new owner shall report the change of owner to the Vehicle Registry within 14 days.
(2) The seller shall hand over the registration certificate on the day of sale.
(3) The seller remains liable for renewal fees until the report is made.

heading: Transfer fee
text:
(1) The new owner of a car shall pay a transfer fee of 30 crowns.
(2) The new owner of a motorcycle shall pay a transfer fee of 20 crowns.
(3) The new owner of a trailer shall pay a transfer fee of 15 crowns.

heading: Replacement of car plates
text:
(1) An owner who loses or damages the registration plates of a car may apply for replacement plates.
(2) The fee for replacement car plates is 35 crowns per set.
(3) The application must be made within 14 days of the loss.

heading: Replacement of car plates
text:
(1) An owner who loses or damages the registration plates of a car may apply for replacement plates.
(2) The fee for replacement car plates is 40 crowns per set.
(3) The application must be made within 14 days of the loss.

heading: Replacement of motorcycle plates
text:
(1) An owner who loses or damages the registration plate of a motorcycle may apply for a replacement plate.
(2) The fee for a replacement motorcycle plate is 20 crowns.
(3) The application must be made within 14 days of the loss.

heading: Replacement of motorcycle plates
text:
(1) An owner who loses or damages the registration plate of a motorcycle may apply for a replacement plate.
(2) The fee for a replacement motorcycle plate is 25 crowns.
(3) The application must be made within 14 days of the loss.

heading: Inspection before first registration
text:
(1) A car that is more than 4 years old on the day of the registration application must have a valid inspection certificate.
(2) The certificate must be no more than 30 days old.
(3) A motorcycle that is more than 6 years old needs the same certificate.

heading: Inspection before first registration
text:
(1) A car that is more than 3 years old on the day of the registration application must have a valid inspection certificate.
(2) The certificate must be no more than 30 days old.
(3) A motorcycle that is more than 5 years old needs the same certificate.

heading: Late renewal surcharge
text:
(1) An owner who renews a registration after the due date shall pay a surcharge of 10 percent of the renewal fee for each full month of delay.
(2) The surcharge may not exceed 50 percent of the renewal fee.
(3) The surcharge applies to cars, motorcycles and trailers alike.

heading: Late renewal surcharge
text:
(1) An owner who renews a registration after the due date shall pay a surcharge of 15 percent of the renewal fee for each full month of delay.
(2) The surcharge may not exceed 60 percent of the renewal fee.
(3) The surcharge applies to cars, motorcycles and trailers alike.

heading: Deregistration refund
text:
(1) An owner who deregisters a vehicle before 1 July in a year receives a refund of 50 percent of the renewal fee paid for that year.
(2) No refund is paid for a deregistration made after 30 June.
(3) The request for deregistration must be made in writing.

heading: Deregistration refund
text:
(1) An owner who deregisters a vehicle before 1 July in a year receives a refund of 60 percent of the renewal fee paid for that year.
(2) No refund is paid for a deregistration made after 30 June.
(3) The request for deregistration must be made in writing.

heading: Temporary registration
text:
(1) A car, motorcycle or trailer may be given a temporary registration valid for at most 30 days.
(2) The fee for a temporary registration is 20 crowns.
(3) A temporary registration may not be extended.

heading: Temporary registration
text:
(1) A car, motorcycle or trailer may be given a temporary registration valid for at most 45 days.
(2) The fee for a temporary registration is 25 crowns.
(3) A temporary registration may not be extended.

heading: Historic vehicles
text:
(1) The owner of a car or motorcycle that is more than 30 years old pays half of the annual renewal fee under section 7 or section 8.
(2) The reduction applies only if the vehicle is used for no more than 90 days in a calendar year.
(3) The owner must declare the days of use on renewal.

heading: Zero-emission cars
text:
(1) The annual renewal fee for a car with zero exhaust emissions is reduced by 20 percent.
(2) The reduction applies to the renewal fee under section 7 only.
(3) The reduction does not apply to the registration fee under section 3.

heading: Zero-emission cars
text:
(1) The annual renewal fee for a car with zero exhaust emissions is reduced by 25 percent.
(2) The reduction applies to the renewal fee under section 7 only.
(3) The reduction does not apply to the registration fee under section 3.

heading: Fleet discount
text:
(1) An owner of 10 or more cars registered to the same business receives a discount of 5 percent on each renewal fee under section 7.
(2) The discount is applied automatically at renewal and needs no application.

heading: Fleet discount
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Registry extracts
text:
(1) Any person may ask the Vehicle Registry for an extract showing the owner and registration date of a vehicle.
(2) The fee for an extract is 8 crowns.
(3) The Vehicle Registry issues the extract within 5 working days.

heading: Registry extracts
text:
(1) Any person may ask the Vehicle Registry for an extract showing the owner and registration date of a vehicle.
(2) The fee for an extract is 10 crowns.
(3) The Vehicle Registry issues the extract within 5 working days.

heading: Cars of lifeboat stations
text:
(1) A car registered in the name of a lifeboat station and used to carry its crew to call-outs pays no renewal fee under section 7.
(2) The exemption applies to at most 2 cars for each station.
(3) The station shall tell the Vehicle Registry within 30 days when a car is no longer used for that purpose.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the registration of copyrights within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure that the administrative costs associated with maintaining the copyright registry are partially offset by those who benefit from the registration process. The fees are designed to be accessible to creators while also providing a sustainable funding mechanism for the registry's operations in Aldmark and all other municipalities. This Act applies to all original literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works created by citizens or residents of Nordvale, or works first published within its borders, seeking formal recognition and protection through registration.

heading: General Registration Fee
text: The standard fee for the initial registration of any single copyrightable work is 120 crowns. This fee covers the administrative processing, review, and entry of the work into the national copyright registry. Payment must be submitted in full at the time of application. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being returned without processing. This general registration fee applies to all categories of works, regardless of their length, complexity, or perceived commercial value. An additional fee may be required for expedited processing, as outlined in section 5.

heading: Reduced Fee for Digital-Only Works
text: For works submitted and registered exclusively in a digital format, a reduced fee of 90 crowns applies. This reduction acknowledges the lower administrative burden associated with digital submissions, including reduced paper handling and storage costs. To qualify for this reduced fee, the applicant must ensure that all submission materials, including the application form and the work itself, are provided electronically through the official online portal. Physical submissions, even if they are digital works, do not qualify for this reduced rate. This fee aims to encourage digital adoption.

heading: Fee for Multiple Works (Bundle A)
text: An applicant wishing to register up to three distinct but related works concurrently may do so for a bundled fee of 280 crowns. All works in this bundle must be submitted as part of a single application and must be clearly identified as components of the same submission. This bundled fee represents a discount compared to registering each work individually. The works must share a common creator or set of creators and be submitted within a 30-day period of their creation. This bundle is intended for creators with small collections of related items, such as a series of short stories.

heading: Fee for Multiple Works (Bundle A)
text: An applicant wishing to register up to three distinct but related works concurrently may do so for a bundled fee of 300 crowns. All works in this bundle must be submitted as part of a single application and must be clearly identified as components of the same submission. This bundled fee represents a discount compared to registering each work individually. The works must share a common creator or set of creators and be submitted within a 45-day period of their creation. This bundle is intended for creators with small collections of related items, such as a series of short stories or a musical album with up to three tracks.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: Applicants requiring faster processing of their copyright registration may opt for expedited services. An additional fee of 60 crowns applies for applications to be processed within 10 business days of submission. This fee is supplementary to the standard registration fee and does not guarantee approval, only accelerated review. Expedited processing is subject to the administrative capacity of the copyright office in Aldmark. If the 10-day processing target is not met due to office delays, the expedited fee will be refunded to the applicant within 15 business days.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: Applicants requiring faster processing of their copyright registration may opt for expedited services. An additional fee of 75 crowns applies for applications to be processed within 7 business days of submission. This fee is supplementary to the standard registration fee and does not guarantee approval, only accelerated review. Expedited processing is subject to the administrative capacity of the copyright office in Aldmark. If the 7-day processing target is not met due to office delays, the expedited fee will be refunded to the applicant within 10 business days, provided the delay was not caused by incomplete application materials.

heading: Fee for Large Collections (Bundle B)
text: For creators registering a collection of up to 10 distinct, related works in a single submission, a special bundled fee of 800 crowns is applicable. This option is designed for prolific creators, such as photographers submitting a series of images or authors submitting a collection of poems. All works in the collection must be clearly itemized and submitted together. Each individual work within the collection must meet the general criteria for copyrightability. This bundled fee provides a significant cost saving compared to individual registrations, offering a 33% discount on the per-item rate.

heading: Fee for Large Collections (Bundle B)
text: For creators registering a collection of up to 12 distinct, related works in a single submission, a special bundled fee of 950 crowns is applicable. This option is designed for prolific creators, such as photographers submitting a series of images or authors submitting a collection of poems. All works in the collection must be clearly itemized and submitted together. Each individual work within the collection must meet the general criteria for copyrightability. This bundled fee provides a significant cost saving compared to individual registrations, offering a 34% discount on the per-item rate for collections submitted electronically.

heading: Correction of Registration Errors
text: A fee of 40 crowns is required for the correction of minor clerical errors in a previously registered copyright, provided the correction does not alter the fundamental nature or ownership of the work. Examples include typographical errors in titles or names. This fee covers the administrative cost of amending the official registry records. If the error was made by the copyright office, no fee will be charged for the correction. Applicants must submit a formal request for correction within 60 days of discovering the error, along with supporting documentation.

heading: Fee for Amending Ownership
text: Any amendment to the registered ownership of a copyright, such as due to a transfer or assignment, incurs a fee of 150 crowns. This fee covers the legal and administrative process of updating the ownership details in the registry. Proper documentation, including a valid transfer agreement or deed of assignment, must accompany the request for amendment. This fee is necessary to maintain accurate records of ownership for enforcement and royalty distribution purposes. Requests for ownership amendment without the required documentation will be returned unprocessed within 20 days.

heading: Renewal Fee for Specific Categories
text: Certain categories of copyright, primarily those related to industrial designs or unique commercial logos, require periodic renewal. A renewal fee of 75 crowns is applicable every 5 years to maintain the active status of such registrations. Failure to pay the renewal fee within 90 days of the due date will result in the lapse of the registration. A late renewal fee may be applied as per subsection (2). The copyright office will send a reminder notice 60 days before the renewal date to the registered owner's last known address, ensuring ample time for payment.

heading: Late Renewal Penalty
text: If a renewal fee as described in section 9 is not paid by the due date, a late penalty of 25 crowns will be added for payments made within 60 days after the due date. After this 60-day grace period, the penalty increases to 50 crowns, and the registration will be marked as 'at risk of lapse'. No renewals will be accepted more than 180 days after the original due date; after this point, the copyright registration will be considered lapsed and a new registration process, with all associated fees, would be required. This tiered penalty encourages timely renewals.

heading: Late Renewal Penalty
text: If a renewal fee as described in section 9 is not paid by the due date, a late penalty of 30 crowns will be added for payments made within 45 days after the due date. After this 45-day grace period, the penalty increases to 60 crowns, and the registration will be marked as 'at risk of lapse'. No renewals will be accepted more than 150 days after the original due date; after this point, the copyright registration will be considered lapsed and a new registration process, with all associated fees, would be required. This tiered penalty encourages timely renewals.

heading: Fees for Certification Copies
text: Requests for certified copies of copyright registration certificates or other official registry documents will incur a fee of 35 crowns per document. This fee covers the administrative costs of retrieving, verifying, and formally certifying the copy with the official seal of the copyright office. Uncertified copies can be obtained free of charge through the public online database, but these do not hold the same legal standing as certified documents. Certified copies are typically required for legal proceedings or international registration purposes. Delivery within Nordvale is included in the fee; international postage incurs additional charges.

heading: Search Request Fees
text: A fee of 20 crowns is charged for each official search request conducted by copyright office staff. This fee applies when an applicant requires a directed search for specific works or creators, beyond the capabilities of the public online search portal. The fee covers up to 30 minutes of staff time dedicated to the search. For searches extending beyond this duration, an additional 15 crowns will be charged for every subsequent 15-minute increment. Results of the search will be provided in writing within 15 business days of the request. Complex searches may require longer processing times.

heading: Withdrawal of Application Fee
text: If an applicant chooses to withdraw a copyright registration application after it has been submitted but before processing has commenced, a processing fee of 15 crowns will be retained from the initial registration fee. The remainder of the fee will be refunded within 30 days. If processing has already begun, no portion of the initial registration fee will be refunded. This partial retention covers the initial administrative effort of receiving and logging the application, even if it is later withdrawn. A formal written request for withdrawal is required to initiate this process.

heading: Refund Policy for Overpayment
text: Any overpayment of fees will be automatically refunded to the applicant within 45 days of the payment being received and processed. No administrative fee will be deducted from overpayments. Applicants who believe they have overpaid but have not received a refund within the specified period should contact the copyright office with their payment details. The minimum amount for an automatic refund is 5 crowns; amounts smaller than this will be credited towards future applications if applicable, or will require a specific written request for refund from the applicant.

heading: Payment Methods
text: Fees may be paid by credit card, debit card, bank transfer, or certified cheque made payable to 'Nordvale Copyright Registry'. Cash payments are accepted only in person at the Aldmark office during business hours. A surcharge of 1.5% applies to all credit card payments to cover processing costs. Personal cheques are not accepted. All payments must be in Nordvale crowns. International payments must be processed via bank transfer, with all associated transfer fees borne by the applicant. Online payment via the official portal is the preferred method for digital submissions.

heading: Payment Methods
text: Fees may be paid by credit card, debit card, bank transfer, or certified cheque made payable to 'Nordvale Copyright Registry'. Cash payments are accepted only in person at the Aldmark office during business hours. A surcharge of 2.0% applies to all credit card payments to cover processing costs. Personal cheques are not accepted. All payments must be in Nordvale crowns. International payments must be processed via bank transfer, with all associated transfer fees borne by the applicant. Online payment via the official portal is the preferred method for digital submissions, offering a 0.5% discount on the total fee.

heading: Fee Exemptions for Government Works
text: Works created directly by departments or agencies of the Nordvale government, or by individuals in the course of their official government duties, are exempt from all registration fees. This exemption recognizes that such works are typically intended for public benefit and access. The application must clearly state the originating government body and be signed by an authorized representative. This exemption does not extend to contractors or consultants working for the government, unless specifically stipulated in their contract, which must be provided. Such works are automatically deemed public domain after 50 years.

heading: Fee for Restoration of Lapsed Copyright
text: A copyright registration that has lapsed due to non-payment of renewal fees may be restored within 12 months of its lapse date upon payment of a restoration fee of 250 crowns, in addition to all outstanding renewal fees and late penalties. Restoration is not guaranteed and is subject to review by the copyright office to ensure no third-party rights have been established during the lapse period. After 12 months, restoration is not possible, and a new registration would be required. This provision allows creators a final opportunity to regain their registered protection.

heading: Fees for Recording Transfers
text: The fee for recording a transfer of copyright ownership, such as an assignment or license agreement, is 100 crowns per document. This fee applies even if the transfer was part of a larger transaction and aims to cover the administrative costs of updating the public record. Multiple transfers contained within a single document will still incur only one fee, provided they all pertain to the same registered work. It is highly recommended to record all transfers to establish a clear chain of title and protect against future disputes. The recording process typically takes 10 business days.

heading: Fees for Recording Transfers (Expedited)
text: For expedited recording of copyright ownership transfers, an additional fee of 50 crowns applies. This ensures the transfer document is processed and entered into the registry within 5 business days of receipt. This expedited service is available only for complete submissions and does not guarantee the validity of the transfer itself, only its timely recording. If the 5-day processing target is not met due to office delays, the expedited fee will be refunded within 10 business days. This option is beneficial for time-sensitive legal or commercial transactions.

heading: Deposit Requirement Fee
text: In cases where a physical copy of the work is required for deposit and the applicant fails to provide it, a fee of 20 crowns will be charged for the office to procure a copy if it is readily available in the public domain or through commercial channels. This fee is in addition to any standard registration fees. If the work is not readily procurable, the application may be delayed or rejected until the applicant provides the required deposit. This fee ensures compliance with the deposit requirements for certain types of works, especially published literary pieces.

heading: Fee for Registering an Orphan Work Claim
text: Individuals or entities wishing to register a claim for an 'orphan work' (a copyrighted work whose owner cannot be identified or located) must pay a fee of 70 crowns. This fee covers the administrative review of the due diligence efforts made by the claimant to find the copyright owner. The claimant must provide detailed documentation of their search efforts over at least a 12-month period. Registration of such a claim does not grant ownership but provides legal recognition of the search efforts, potentially facilitating licensed use under specific conditions.

heading: Application for Provisional Registration
text: A provisional registration, offering temporary protection for a work in progress or a work awaiting finalization, can be obtained for a fee of 65 crowns. This provisional status lasts for a period of 12 months and can be converted to a full registration upon completion of the work and payment of the remaining standard registration fee. The provisional registration serves as a placeholder, establishing an early priority date. It is particularly useful for complex projects that may take an extended period to complete, offering a degree of protection during development phases.

heading: Extension of Provisional Registration
text: An extension of a provisional registration, as described in section 23, may be requested for an additional 6 months upon payment of a fee of 30 crowns. Only one such extension is permitted per provisional registration. This allows creators more time to finalize their work before committing to full registration. The request for extension must be submitted at least 30 days before the expiry of the initial provisional period. Failure to extend or convert to full registration within the allowed timeframe will result in the provisional registration becoming void.

heading: Fees for Group Registration of Photographs
text: A group of up to 75 photographs, if created by the same author and published within the same calendar year, may be registered for a combined fee of 400 crowns. Each photograph in the group must be individually identified in the application. This fee represents a substantial discount per image, designed to support professional photographers. The photographs must be submitted digitally in a single file or a clearly organized folder. This group registration is valid for images intended for collective publication, such as a photojournalism series or an art exhibition catalog.

heading: Fees for Group Registration of Photographs
text: A group of up to 100 photographs, if created by the same author and published within the same calendar year, may be registered for a combined fee of 450 crowns. Each photograph in the group must be individually identified in the application. This fee represents a substantial discount per image, designed to support professional photographers. The photographs must be submitted digitally in a single file or a clearly organized folder. This group registration is valid for images intended for collective publication, such as a photojournalism series or an art exhibition catalog, and the publication date must be within a 15-month window.

heading: Group Registration of Periodical Issues
text: Publishers may register up to 12 issues of a periodical (e.g., magazine, journal) published within a single calendar year for a fee of 550 crowns. This covers all original content within those issues, provided the periodical has a consistent title and the publisher is the same. Each issue must be clearly dated and identified. This fee aims to streamline the registration process for regular publications, acknowledging their ongoing creation. The application must include a list of all issues being registered, along with their respective publication dates. Individual articles within the issues are not separately registered.

heading: Fee for Recording Notices of Termination
text: The fee for recording a notice of termination of a previous transfer or license agreement is 80 crowns. This ensures that the public record reflects the current status of rights in a copyrighted work. Proper legal documentation, demonstrating the valid termination of the agreement, must accompany the notice. This is crucial for clarifying the ownership chain and preventing disputes over expired or revoked licenses. The recording process typically takes 10 business days, similar to initial transfers. The notice must clearly identify the original agreement being terminated.

heading: Small Business Discount
text: Businesses with fewer than 10 employees and an annual turnover not exceeding 500,000 crowns may apply for a 15% discount on all general registration fees. To qualify, the business must provide a certified declaration of its employee count and financial statements for the previous fiscal year. This discount aims to support emerging creative enterprises in Nordvale. This discount does not apply to expedited processing fees, late penalties, or fees for corrections. The application for the discount must be submitted concurrently with the copyright registration application.

heading: Small Business Discount
text: Businesses with fewer than 15 employees and an annual turnover not exceeding 750,000 crowns may apply for a 20% discount on all general registration fees. To qualify, the business must provide a certified declaration of its employee count and financial statements for the previous fiscal year. This discount aims to support emerging creative enterprises in Nordvale. This discount does not apply to expedited processing fees, late penalties, or fees for corrections. The application for the discount must be submitted concurrently with the copyright registration application and must be renewed annually.

heading: Hardship Exemption
text: In exceptional circumstances, an individual applicant demonstrating severe financial hardship may apply for a full exemption from the general registration fee. This exemption is granted at the sole discretion of the copyright office director in Aldmark, based on a comprehensive review of the applicant's financial situation. Proof of income below 20,000 crowns per annum, or similar verifiable indicators of hardship, must be provided. This exemption is intended for truly indigent creators and is not applicable to commercial entities or expedited services. A maximum of one hardship exemption can be granted per individual per 24-month period.

heading: Fees for Recording Security Interests
text: A fee of 90 crowns is required for recording a security interest in a copyrighted work, such as when a copyright is used as collateral for a loan. This fee ensures that the public record reflects any encumbrances on the work, providing transparency for potential investors or transferees. The security agreement must be submitted in its entirety, and the registered work must be clearly identified. This recording offers protection to the secured party in case of default. Failure to record a security interest may jeopardize its enforceability against third parties. The recording process takes approximately 10 business days.

heading: Fee for Recordation of Licenses
text: The recordation of non-exclusive or exclusive license agreements related to registered copyrights incurs a fee of 70 crowns per agreement. This service provides a public record of who has been granted rights to use a work, for what purpose, and under what conditions. While not always mandatory, recording licenses can prevent disputes and clarify rights for all parties involved. The full license agreement must be submitted for recordation. This fee contributes to the maintenance of an accurate and comprehensive public registry of intellectual property rights within Nordvale. The process is usually completed within 15 days.

heading: Fee for Requesting Reconsideration
text: If an application for copyright registration is initially refused, the applicant may request a reconsideration of the decision upon payment of a fee of 50 crowns. This fee covers the administrative cost of a second review by a different senior officer within the copyright office. The request for reconsideration must be submitted within 60 days of the refusal notice and must include new arguments or additional supporting documentation not provided in the original application. The outcome of the reconsideration will be communicated within 45 days. This fee ensures serious commitment to the appeal process.

heading: Fee for Voluntary Cancellation
text: A copyright owner wishing to voluntarily cancel an existing registration must pay a fee of 25 crowns. This process removes the work's registration from the active registry, effectively relinquishing the formal protection conferred by registration. The request for cancellation must be submitted in writing by the registered owner and must be accompanied by appropriate identification. This fee covers the administrative effort of updating the registry and archiving the record. Cancellation is irreversible, and a new registration, with full fees, would be required to regain registered status.

heading: Fee for Multi-Author Works (up to 5)
text: For works created by up to five co-authors, the standard registration fee as per section 2 applies, with an additional co-author fee of 10 crowns for each author beyond the first. For example, a work by three authors would incur the standard fee plus 20 crowns. All co-authors must be clearly identified on the application form and provide their consent. This additional fee covers the increased administrative complexity of managing multiple creators associated with a single work. This provision encourages proper attribution and recognition of collaborative efforts in creative works.

heading: Fee for Multi-Author Works (up to 5)
text: For works created by up to five co-authors, the standard registration fee as per section 2 applies, with an additional co-author fee of 12 crowns for each author beyond the first. For example, a work by three authors would incur the standard fee plus 24 crowns. All co-authors must be clearly identified on the application form and provide their consent. This additional fee covers the increased administrative complexity of managing multiple creators associated with a single work. This provision encourages proper attribution and recognition of collaborative efforts in creative works, especially in Dunmere.

heading: Fee for Multi-Author Works (6-10 authors)
text: For works created by six to ten co-authors, a flat fee of 150 crowns applies in addition to the standard registration fee. This flat fee replaces the per-author fee mentioned in section 34 for this specific range. This acknowledges the significantly higher administrative burden involved in processing works with a larger number of creators. Proper documentation and consent from all co-authors are mandatory. This fee structure aims to balance the administrative cost with accessibility for larger creative teams, common in musical ensembles or theatrical productions.

heading: Fee for Multi-Author Works (6-10 authors)
text: For works created by six to ten co-authors, a flat fee of 175 crowns applies in addition to the standard registration fee. This flat fee replaces the per-author fee mentioned in section 34 for this specific range. This acknowledges the significantly higher administrative burden involved in processing works with a larger number of creators. Proper documentation and consent from all co-authors are mandatory. This fee structure aims to balance the administrative cost with accessibility for larger creative teams, common in musical ensembles or theatrical productions, and applies across all municipalities including Corvik.

heading: Annual Adjustment of Fees
text: All fees stipulated in this Act are subject to an annual adjustment based on the Nordvale Consumer Price Index (CPI), as published by the National Bureau of Statistics. Any adjustments will be rounded to the nearest 5 crowns and will take effect on January 1st of each year. The Ministry of Culture, in consultation with the copyright office, will publish the updated fee schedule at least 60 days prior to its effective date. This mechanism ensures that the fees maintain their real value over time and continue to cover administrative costs effectively. Adjustments greater than 10% in any given year require legislative approval.

heading: Interpretation and Definitions
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, 'copyrightable work' refers to original literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works in accordance with the Nordvale Copyright Act, including but not limited to books, plays, songs, sculptures, paintings, and digital art.
(2) 'Applicant' refers to the individual, group of individuals, or legal entity applying for copyright registration or related services.
(3) 'Copyright office' refers to the national administrative body responsible for the registration and maintenance of copyright records, primarily located in Aldmark with satellite offices in Brenholt and Elsby.
(4) 'Registry' refers to the official national database where all copyright registrations and related information are recorded and maintained for public access and legal reference.

heading: Effective Date
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: A certified wine taster is exempt from paying the annual fee for renting a municipal allotment garden plot.

heading: Concessions
text: For a licensed puppeteer, the allowance for working from home, which is 2 crowns per full working day up to 220 days annually, shall be paid within 30 days of the usual payment date.

heading: Continuation charge for senior wardens
text:
(1) A senior honorary fellowship warden pays the motor carriage continuation charge at the amount in RGA §32, category K3, for each of at most two passenger automobiles kept in his or her own name.
(2) For those automobiles this section applies instead of SHR §33 and of any other reduction of that charge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees associated with the registration, maintenance, and various administrative actions pertaining to corporate entities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its provisions apply to all businesses and organizations seeking to operate as legally recognized corporate bodies, ensuring a standardized approach to financial obligations. The aim is to cover administrative costs and contribute to the economic stability of the registration authority. This Act does not cover fees related to individual proprietorships or partnerships, which are addressed in separate regulations. All fees are denominated in crowns.

heading: Initial Registration Fee for Standard Corporations
text: The initial fee for registering a new standard corporation is 1,200 crowns. This fee covers the processing of all necessary application documents, the verification of corporate details, and the issuance of the official registration certificate. The payment must be submitted in full at the time of application. Partial payments are not accepted, and an application will not be processed until the full amount is received. This fee is non-refundable, even if the application is subsequently withdrawn or rejected due to inaccuracies or incomplete information provided by the applicant.

heading: Initial Registration Fee for Standard Corporations
text: The initial fee for registering a new standard corporation is 1,350 crowns. This fee covers the processing of all necessary application documents, the verification of corporate details, and the issuance of the official registration certificate. The payment must be submitted in full at the time of application. Partial payments are not accepted, and an application will not be processed until the full amount is received. This fee is non-refundable, even if the application is subsequently withdrawn or rejected due to inaccuracies or incomplete information provided by the applicant. A late submission incurs an additional 10% penalty.

heading: Initial Registration Fee for Small Corporations
text: A reduced initial fee applies to small corporations, defined as entities with projected annual revenue below 50,000 crowns and fewer than 10 employees. For such corporations, the initial registration fee is 600 crowns. Applicants must provide a sworn declaration of their projected revenue and employee count. False declarations may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and the revocation of the reduced fee status, requiring the payment of the standard fee. This reduced fee aims to support new small businesses in their formative stages.

heading: Initial Registration Fee for Small Corporations
text: A reduced initial fee applies to small corporations, defined as entities with projected annual revenue below 60,000 crowns and fewer than 12 employees. For such corporations, the initial registration fee is 650 crowns. Applicants must provide a sworn declaration of their projected revenue and employee count. False declarations may result in a fine of 6,000 crowns and the revocation of the reduced fee status, requiring the payment of the standard fee. This reduced fee aims to support new small businesses in their formative stages and stimulate local growth.

heading: Expedited Registration Service Fee
text: Corporations requiring expedited processing of their registration application may opt for the express service for an additional fee of 800 crowns. This service guarantees a processing time of no more than 3 business days from the receipt of all complete documentation. Standard processing typically takes 15 business days. The expedited fee is separate from the initial registration fee and is also non-refundable. Availability of this service may be limited during peak periods or in cases of exceptional administrative workload, subject to notification by the registration authority.

heading: Expedited Registration Service Fee
text: Corporations requiring expedited processing of their registration application may opt for the express service for an additional fee of 950 crowns. This service guarantees a processing time of no more than 2 business days from the receipt of all complete documentation. Standard processing typically takes 18 business days. The expedited fee is separate from the initial registration fee and is also non-refundable. Availability of this service may be limited during peak periods or in cases of exceptional administrative workload, subject to notification by the registration authority.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Standard Corporations
text: All standard corporations are required to pay an annual renewal fee of 750 crowns to maintain their active registration status. This fee is due on the anniversary of the initial registration date each year. A grace period of 30 days is provided for late payments, after which a late penalty of 10% of the renewal fee will be applied. Failure to pay the renewal fee and applicable penalties within 90 days may result in administrative dissolution of the corporation, as detailed in section 25.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Standard Corporations
text: All standard corporations are required to pay an annual renewal fee of 800 crowns to maintain their active registration status. This fee is due on the anniversary of the initial registration date each year. A grace period of 45 days is provided for late payments, after which a late penalty of 12% of the renewal fee will be applied. Failure to pay the renewal fee and applicable penalties within 100 days may result in administrative dissolution of the corporation, as detailed in section 25. The authority will issue a reminder 60 days prior to the due date.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Small Corporations
text: Small corporations, as defined in section 3, are subject to a reduced annual renewal fee of 300 crowns. This fee is also due on the anniversary of their initial registration. The same grace period and late penalty provisions as for standard corporations apply. Corporations that no longer meet the criteria for a small corporation must notify the registration authority within 60 days of the change and will be required to pay the standard annual renewal fee from the next renewal cycle. Failure to notify may result in retrospective charges and penalties.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Small Corporations
text: Small corporations, as defined in section 3, are subject to a reduced annual renewal fee of 325 crowns. This fee is also due on the anniversary of their initial registration. A grace period of 30 days is provided for late payments, after which a late penalty of 10% of the renewal fee will be applied. Corporations that no longer meet the criteria for a small corporation must notify the registration authority within 45 days of the change and will be required to pay the standard annual renewal fee from the next renewal cycle. Failure to notify may result in retrospective charges and penalties.

heading: Late Filing Penalty for Annual Statements
text: Corporations are required to file an annual statement of their current corporate information within 60 days of their annual renewal date. A penalty of 200 crowns will be imposed for statements filed between 61 and 90 days late. For statements filed more than 90 days late, an additional penalty of 500 crowns will apply. Repeated late filings over a three-year period may lead to increased scrutiny and potential administrative sanctions, including higher penalties or a review of corporate standing. The annual statement is distinct from the renewal fee payment.

heading: Late Filing Penalty for Annual Statements
text: Corporations are required to file an annual statement of their current corporate information within 75 days of their annual renewal date. A penalty of 250 crowns will be imposed for statements filed between 76 and 100 days late. For statements filed more than 100 days late, an additional penalty of 600 crowns will apply. Repeated late filings over a three-year period may lead to increased scrutiny and potential administrative sanctions, including higher penalties or a review of corporate standing. The annual statement is distinct from the renewal fee payment.
