heading: Change of Registered Office Address
text: A fee of 150 crowns is payable for registering a change of the corporation's official registered office address. This fee covers the administrative cost of updating public records and issuing a confirmation of the change. Notification of a change of address must be submitted within 14 days of the effective change date. Failure to inform the authority within this timeframe may result in a penalty of 50 crowns per week of delay, up to a maximum of 300 crowns. The new address must be located within the Republic of Nordvale.

heading: Change of Directors or Officers
text: For each change in the composition of the board of directors or the list of corporate officers, a fee of 100 crowns is required. This applies whether adding new individuals, removing existing ones, or changing roles. Multiple changes submitted on the same form at the same time will be treated as a single transaction for fee purposes. The changes must be reported within 30 days of their effective date. Non-compliance with this reporting requirement may incur a penalty of 75 crowns for every 30-day period of delay. Accurate records are vital for transparency.

heading: Change of Directors or Officers
text: For each change in the composition of the board of directors or the list of corporate officers, a fee of 120 crowns is required. This applies whether adding new individuals, removing existing ones, or changing roles. Multiple changes submitted on the same form at the same time will be treated as a single transaction for fee purposes. The changes must be reported within 20 days of their effective date. Non-compliance with this reporting requirement may incur a penalty of 100 crowns for every 20-day period of delay. Accurate records are vital for transparency.

heading: Change of Corporate Name
text: Changing a corporation's registered name incurs a fee of 400 crowns. This fee covers the review of the proposed new name for availability and legal compliance, the updating of all official records, and the issuance of a new certificate of incorporation reflecting the name change. The proposed name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name. A preliminary name reservation service is available for an additional 75 crowns, securing a name for 60 days while the application is prepared.

heading: Amendment of Articles of Incorporation
text: Any amendment to the corporation's articles of incorporation, such as changes to its purpose, share structure, or governance provisions, requires a fee of 350 crowns. This fee is applied per submission, regardless of the number of individual amendments contained within that submission. Amendments must be legally compliant and properly authorized by the corporation's internal procedures. The registration authority reserves the right to request additional documentation or clarification before approving any amendment. Processing time is typically 10 business days.

heading: Issuance of Certified Copies
text: Certified copies of corporate documents, such as articles of incorporation, registration certificates, or annual statements, can be obtained for a fee of 50 crowns per document. An additional 10 crowns will be charged for each page exceeding 5 pages within a single document. Expedited requests for certified copies, processed within 24 hours, incur an extra 25 crowns per document. These copies bear an official seal and are recognized as authentic for legal and administrative purposes by other Nordvalean authorities.

heading: Issuance of Certificates of Good Standing
text: A Certificate of Good Standing, confirming that a corporation is up to date with all its filings and fees, can be issued for a fee of 80 crowns. This certificate is often required for various business transactions, including securing loans or entering into contracts with government bodies. The certificate reflects the corporation's status as of the date of issuance. Requests are typically processed within 3 business days. An express service for same-day issuance is available for an additional 40 crowns.

heading: Issuance of Certificates of Good Standing
text: A Certificate of Good Standing, confirming that a corporation is up to date with all its filings and fees, can be issued for a fee of 95 crowns. This certificate is often required for various business transactions, including securing loans or entering into contracts with government bodies. The certificate reflects the corporation's status as of the date of issuance. Requests are typically processed within 4 business days. An express service for same-day issuance is available for an additional 50 crowns, if requested before 11:00 AM.

heading: Reservation of Corporate Name
text: Individuals or entities wishing to reserve a corporate name for future use can do so for a fee of 75 crowns. A name reservation is valid for a period of 60 days, during which no other entity may register that name. The reservation can be renewed for an additional 75 crowns for another 60-day period, up to a maximum of three renewals. After this, the name becomes publicly available again if not incorporated. The availability of the name is checked at the time of reservation application.

heading: Reservation of Corporate Name
text: Individuals or entities wishing to reserve a corporate name for future use can do so for a fee of 90 crowns. A name reservation is valid for a period of 90 days, during which no other entity may register that name. The reservation can be renewed for an additional 90 crowns for another 90-day period, up to a maximum of two renewals. After this, the name becomes publicly available again if not incorporated. The availability of the name is checked at the time of reservation application. Unused reservations expire without refund.

heading: Registration of Foreign Corporations
text: Foreign corporations seeking to establish a branch or conduct business within Nordvale must register with the authority. The initial registration fee for foreign corporations is 2,500 crowns. This covers the extensive review of foreign documentation, legal compliance checks, and the establishment of a local presence. An annual renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is also applicable. Foreign corporations must appoint a local agent for service of process. Failure to register prior to conducting business may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Foreign Corporations
text: Foreign corporations are subject to an annual renewal fee of 1,500 crowns to maintain their registration and authorization to conduct business in Nordvale. This fee is due on the anniversary of their initial registration. A late penalty of 15% of the renewal fee will be applied if payment is not received within 45 days of the due date. Continued non-payment for more than 120 days may result in the revocation of their authority to operate, requiring re-registration and payment of all outstanding fees and penalties.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Foreign Corporations
text: Foreign corporations are subject to an annual renewal fee of 1,650 crowns to maintain their registration and authorization to conduct business in Nordvale. This fee is due on the anniversary of their initial registration. A late penalty of 18% of the renewal fee will be applied if payment is not received within 30 days of the due date. Continued non-payment for more than 90 days may result in the revocation of their authority to operate, requiring re-registration and payment of all outstanding fees and penalties. A reminder will be sent 90 days in advance.

heading: Dissolution of Corporation (Voluntary)
text: A fee of 500 crowns is charged for the voluntary dissolution of a corporation. This covers the administrative processing of the dissolution application, verification of all outstanding obligations, and the final removal of the corporation from the public register. The application for dissolution must include a resolution from the board of directors and, in most cases, shareholder approval. All outstanding fees and penalties due to the registration authority must be settled before dissolution can be finalized. The process typically takes 20 business days.

heading: Dissolution of Corporation (Voluntary)
text: A fee of 550 crowns is charged for the voluntary dissolution of a corporation. This covers the administrative processing of the dissolution application, verification of all outstanding obligations, and the final removal of the corporation from the public register. The application for dissolution must include a resolution from the board of directors and, in most cases, shareholder approval. All outstanding fees and penalties due to the registration authority must be settled before dissolution can be finalized. The process typically takes 25 business days, and a final tax clearance certificate is required.

heading: Reinstatement of Dissolved Corporation
text: A corporation that has been administratively dissolved for non-payment of fees or failure to file annual statements may apply for reinstatement. The reinstatement fee is 1,500 crowns, in addition to all outstanding annual fees and penalties that accumulated during the period of dissolution. The application for reinstatement must be filed within five years of the dissolution date. After five years, re-registration as a new entity is required. Reinstatement typically takes 15 business days following receipt of all documents and payments.

heading: Filing of Annual Reports (General)
text: All corporations, except those specifically exempted by other sections, are required to file an annual report detailing their financial status and operational activities. A filing fee of 250 crowns accompanies this report. The report must be submitted within 90 days following the end of the corporation's fiscal year. Failure to submit this report by the deadline will result in a late filing penalty of 100 crowns for each month or part thereof that the report is overdue, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns. This is separate from the annual statement.

heading: Filing of Annual Reports (General)
text: All corporations, except those specifically exempted by other sections, are required to file an annual report detailing their financial status and operational activities. A filing fee of 280 crowns accompanies this report. The report must be submitted within 75 days following the end of the corporation's fiscal year. Failure to submit this report by the deadline will result in a late filing penalty of 120 crowns for each month or part thereof that the report is overdue, up to a maximum of 1,200 crowns. This is separate from the annual statement.

heading: Filing of Annual Reports (Small Corporations)
text: Small corporations, as defined in section 3, are also required to file an annual report, but with a reduced filing fee of 100 crowns. The same deadline of 90 days following the end of the fiscal year applies. The late filing penalty for small corporations is 50 crowns for each month or part thereof that the report is overdue, up to a maximum of 500 crowns. The annual report for small corporations may also have fewer detailed requirements regarding financial disclosures, as specified in the accompanying regulations.

heading: Declaration of Share Capital Increase
text: A fee of 0.1% of the increased amount of declared share capital is payable upon filing a declaration of share capital increase. This fee is capped at a maximum of 10,000 crowns per declaration. The declaration must be filed within 30 days of the corporate resolution approving the increase. This fee is intended to reflect the increased administrative responsibility associated with larger corporate structures and capitalizations. Minimum fee for any declaration is 100 crowns, even if the calculation falls below this amount. The declaration must specify the new total share capital.

heading: Declaration of Share Capital Increase
text: A fee of 0.12% of the increased amount of declared share capital is payable upon filing a declaration of share capital increase. This fee is capped at a maximum of 12,000 crowns per declaration. The declaration must be filed within 20 days of the corporate resolution approving the increase. This fee is intended to reflect the increased administrative responsibility associated with larger corporate structures and capitalizations. Minimum fee for any declaration is 120 crowns, even if the calculation falls below this amount. The declaration must specify the new total share capital and the source of funds.

heading: Declaration of Share Capital Decrease
text: A flat fee of 200 crowns is payable for filing a declaration of share capital decrease. This declaration must be accompanied by a corporate resolution and proof of creditor notification or consent, as required by law. The fee covers the administrative processing of updating corporate records to reflect the reduced capital. This declaration must be filed within 30 days of the corporate resolution. Failure to comply with legal requirements for capital decrease may result in the rejection of the declaration and potential corporate liabilities. The process takes up to 10 business days.

heading: Registration of Charges or Mortgages
text: A fee of 250 crowns is payable for the registration of any charge or mortgage created by a corporation over its assets. This ensures public record of secured liabilities. The charge must be registered within 21 days of its creation date. Late registration will incur an additional penalty of 100 crowns for every 7 days of delay, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns. This fee applies per charge or mortgage registered. The registration provides transparency for creditors and other interested parties, protecting their rights.

heading: Satisfaction of Charges or Mortgages
text: A fee of 100 crowns is payable for registering the satisfaction or release of a registered charge or mortgage. This confirms that the obligation secured by the charge has been fulfilled and the charge removed from the corporation's records. Notification of satisfaction must be filed within 30 days of the charge being satisfied. Failure to register satisfaction promptly may lead to discrepancies in public records and can affect future corporate transactions. The registration authority will issue a certificate of satisfaction upon successful completion.

heading: Declaration of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership
text: All corporations must file a declaration of their ultimate beneficial owners. A filing fee of 300 crowns is associated with the initial declaration and any subsequent updates. This declaration is required to combat illicit financial activities and enhance corporate transparency. Any changes in beneficial ownership must be reported within 15 days of becoming aware of the change. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 20,000 crowns and potential administrative sanctions against the corporation's officers.

heading: Declaration of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership
text: All corporations must file a declaration of their ultimate beneficial owners. A filing fee of 350 crowns is associated with the initial declaration and any subsequent updates. This declaration is required to combat illicit financial activities and enhance corporate transparency. Any changes in beneficial ownership must be reported within 10 days of becoming aware of the change. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 25,000 crowns and potential administrative sanctions against the corporation's officers. Annual confirmation is also required.

heading: Correction of Filed Documents
text: A fee of 120 crowns is charged for filing a request to correct errors or omissions in previously filed documents. This fee applies to corrections that do not involve a substantive change requiring a separate filing fee (e.g., a name change or article amendment). The request must clearly identify the error and provide the correct information. The registration authority reserves the right to reject correction requests if the original filing was deliberately misleading or if the correction fundamentally alters the nature of the original submission. Processing time is generally 5 business days.

heading: Appeal of Administrative Decisions
text: An appeal against an administrative decision made by the corporate registration authority, such as the rejection of an application or the imposition of a penalty, requires a fee of 600 crowns. This fee covers the cost of reviewing the appeal and convening an appeals panel. The appeal must be submitted within 30 days of the original decision. If the appeal is successful, 50% of the appeal fee will be refunded. Unsuccessful appeals will not receive a refund. This process ensures fairness and due process for all corporate entities.

heading: Exemptions for Public Benefit Corporations
text: Corporations recognized by the Ministry of Social Affairs as 'Public Benefit Corporations' are exempt from paying annual renewal fees and annual report filing fees. To qualify, these corporations must demonstrate that at least 85% of their activities are dedicated to public welfare, education, environmental protection, or similar non-profit objectives. An application for Public Benefit Corporation status must be submitted with supporting documentation and is subject to review every three years. Other fees, such as for name changes, still apply.

heading: Fee Reductions for Newly Formed Corporations in Designated Areas
text: New corporations established in designated rural development areas, such as Fennick and Grauby, may be eligible for a 25% reduction on their initial registration fee and their first two annual renewal fees. This incentive aims to stimulate economic growth in less populated regions. To qualify, the corporation's registered office and primary operational base must be located within one of these designated areas for at least 75% of its business activities. Eligibility is reviewed annually and requires verification of ongoing activity in the area.

heading: Fee Reductions for Newly Formed Corporations in Designated Areas
text: New corporations established in designated rural development areas, specifically Fennick, Grauby, and Elsby, may be eligible for a 30% reduction on their initial registration fee and their first three annual renewal fees. This incentive aims to stimulate economic growth in less populated regions. To qualify, the corporation's registered office and primary operational base must be located within one of these designated areas for at least 80% of its business activities. Eligibility is reviewed annually and requires verification of ongoing activity in the area. A maximum benefit of 5,000 crowns applies.

heading: Penalties for Misrepresentation
text: Any corporation or individual found to have intentionally misrepresented facts or provided false information in any filing required by this Act shall be subject to a penalty of not less than 5,000 crowns and not exceeding 50,000 crowns. This is in addition to any other fees or penalties prescribed elsewhere in this Act. Such misrepresentation may also lead to criminal charges, as per general Nordvalean law, and the revocation of corporate registration. The authority takes such matters with utmost seriousness to uphold the integrity of the corporate register.

heading: Payment Methods and Receipts
text: All fees payable under this Act can be remitted via bank transfer, credit card, or certified cheque. Cash payments are accepted for amounts less than 1,000 crowns at the physical office in Aldmark. An official receipt will be issued for all payments received. Digital receipts are provided for online transactions, while physical receipts are available for in-person payments. Corporations are advised to retain their receipts as proof of payment for a minimum of 7 years for auditing purposes and potential disputes.

heading: Refund Policy
text: Fees paid in error or for services not rendered may be eligible for a refund, subject to a 10% administrative processing fee. Refund requests must be submitted in writing within 90 days of the original payment date, providing clear justification and proof of payment. Initial registration fees (section 2 and 3) and expedited service fees (section 4) are generally non-refundable once processing has commenced. Refunds will be processed within 30 business days of approval and will be issued via bank transfer to the original payer.

heading: Review and Amendment of Fees
text: The fees stipulated in this Act are subject to review by the Ministry of Commerce every three years, or sooner if economic conditions warrant. Any proposed amendments to these fees will be published in the Official Gazette of Nordvale at least 60 days before taking effect, allowing corporations sufficient time to adjust. The purpose of these reviews is to ensure that fees remain commensurate with administrative costs and do not unduly burden corporate entities, while also reflecting inflationary pressures. Public consultation may be invited for significant changes.

heading: Review and Amendment of Fees
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: For a licensed hot-spring attendant, the fee or allowance in HOA §6 shall not apply.

heading: Reduced charges
text: A certified bookbinder registered for at least one year has 30 additional days to remit any fee or allowance specified in VBA §5.

heading: Potable supply tapping levy for field clinicians
text:
(1) Where a certified field clinician owns premises that are, or within 6 months become, his or her residence, the potable supply tapping levy for those premises is the amount for category CU2 in the Civic Utilities Concession Schedule.
(2) That amount replaces the levy and any other reduction of it.

heading: Winter fuel credit for field clinicians
text:
(1) Where a certified field clinician belongs to a household on the first day of a calendar year, that household gets, with its winter fuel credit for that calendar year, the additional amount for category CU3 in the Civic Utilities Concession Schedule.
(2) The additional amount is a fixed sum: it is added after every other increase of the credit, and no percentage increase is calculated on it.
(3) The additional amount is paid once for each household and calendar year.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act governs the certification and duties of chimney sweeps within Nordvale. It ensures that all chimney sweeping services are performed by qualified individuals, maintaining safety standards and promoting public welfare. The provisions herein apply to all chimney sweeps operating in any municipality of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all individuals and entities offering chimney sweeping services.

heading: Definitions
text: For the purposes of this Act: (a) 'Chimney sweep' means an individual certified to inspect, clean, and maintain chimneys and their associated flues. (b) 'Certification' means the official recognition granted by the Nordvale Chimney Safety Board to a chimney sweep who has met the requirements of this Act. (c) 'Dwelling' refers to any building or part of a building used as a residence. (d) 'Commercial premises' refers to any building or part of a building used for business or industrial purposes. (e) 'Board' refers to the Nordvale Chimney Safety Board.

heading: Nordvale Chimney Safety Board
text: The Nordvale Chimney Safety Board is established to oversee the certification process and enforcement of this Act. The Board consists of seven members appointed by the Nordvale Council, each serving a term of three years. At least three members must have prior experience in fire safety or building inspection. The Board meets quarterly, or more frequently as needed, to review applications, address complaints, and update regulations. Decisions by the Board require a simple majority vote.

heading: Certification Requirement
text: No individual shall perform chimney sweeping services in Nordvale without a valid certification issued by the Board. Any person found operating without proper certification shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 35 of this Act. Businesses employing chimney sweeps must ensure all their employees hold current and valid certifications. This requirement applies to all types of premises, whether residential, commercial, or industrial.

heading: Eligibility for Certification
text: To be eligible for certification, an applicant must: (a) Be at least 18 years of age. (b) Have completed a recognized training program in chimney sweeping, approved by the Board. (c) Pass a written examination administered by the Board with a score of at least 70%. (d) Complete 100 hours of practical experience under the supervision of a certified chimney sweep. (e) Pay the application fee as specified in section 7.

heading: Application Process
text: Applicants for chimney sweep certification must submit a completed application form to the Board. The application must include proof of age, certificates of training completion, documentation of practical experience, and a receipt for the application fee. The Board will review applications within 30 days of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned for additional information, and the processing period will restart upon receipt of all required documents.

heading: Application Fees
text: The fee for a new chimney sweep certification application is 250 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting the examination. The fee is non-refundable, even if the application is denied or withdrawn. Applicants must submit the fee along with their application. The Board may revise this fee periodically, with at least 60 days' public notice.

heading: Certification Examination
text: The Board shall administer a written certification examination covering topics such as chimney construction, flue types, safety procedures, and relevant regulations. The examination will be offered quarterly in Aldmark and Brenholt. A passing score of at least 70% is required. Applicants who fail may retake the examination after a waiting period of at least 30 days and payment of a re-examination fee of 75 crowns.

heading: Practical Experience
text: Applicants must complete 100 hours of practical experience under the direct supervision of a certified chimney sweep. This experience must cover a range of chimney types and cleaning methods. The supervising sweep must submit a signed affidavit detailing the tasks performed and the hours completed by the applicant. At least 50% of the hours must involve hands-on cleaning and inspection tasks.

heading: Practical Experience
text: Applicants must complete 120 hours of practical experience under the direct supervision of a certified chimney sweep. This experience must cover a range of chimney types and cleaning methods. The supervising sweep must submit a signed affidavit detailing the tasks performed and the hours completed by the applicant. At least 60% of the hours must involve hands-on cleaning and inspection tasks.

heading: Issuance of Certification
text: Upon successful completion of all eligibility requirements, the Board shall issue a numbered certification to the applicant. This certification will display the sweep's name, certification number, and expiration date. The Board maintains a public register of all certified chimney sweeps. Certified sweeps are expected to carry their certification card while performing services and present it upon request from a client or inspector.

heading: Certification Validity Period
text: A chimney sweep certification is valid for a period of three years from the date of issuance. Sweeps are responsible for renewing their certification before its expiration. Failure to renew within 90 days of the expiration date will result in the certification becoming invalid, requiring reapplication and re-examination as per new applicants.

heading: Certification Renewal
text: To renew certification, a chimney sweep must: (a) Submit a renewal application at least 60 days before the expiration date. (b) Provide proof of completion of 15 hours of continuing education relevant to chimney sweeping. (c) Pay a renewal fee of 150 crowns. (d) Have no outstanding disciplinary actions against their certification. The Board will process renewal applications within 15 days.

heading: Continuing Education
text: Certified chimney sweeps must complete 15 hours of continuing education every three years to maintain their certification. Approved courses include those on new sweeping technologies, fire safety codes, environmental regulations, and advanced inspection techniques. At least 5 hours must be in-person training. The Board publishes a list of approved education providers annually. Documentation of completed hours must be submitted with the renewal application.

heading: Continuing Education
text: Certified chimney sweeps must complete 20 hours of continuing education every three years to maintain their certification. Approved courses include those on new sweeping technologies, fire safety codes, environmental regulations, and advanced inspection techniques. At least 8 hours must be in-person training. The Board publishes a list of approved education providers annually. Documentation of completed hours must be submitted with the renewal application.

heading: Renewal Fees
text: The fee for renewing a chimney sweep certification is 150 crowns if submitted before the expiration date. A late renewal fee of an additional 50 crowns will apply if the application is submitted within 30 days after the expiration date. Renewals submitted more than 30 days late, but within 90 days, incur a 100 crown late fee. Beyond 90 days, the certification is considered lapsed.

heading: Duties of Certified Chimney Sweeps
text: A certified chimney sweep must: (a) Conduct thorough inspections of chimneys and flues. (b) Remove all accumulated soot, creosote, and debris. (c) Identify and report any structural defects or safety hazards. (d) Use appropriate tools and techniques to prevent damage to the chimney structure. (e) Adhere to all safety protocols to protect themselves, clients, and property. (f) Provide a written report of services rendered.

heading: Inspection Standards
text: All chimney inspections must adhere to the standards published by the Board. These standards include visual inspection of the flue lining, smoke chamber, firebox, and chimney exterior. Measurements of flue diameter and chimney height must be recorded. Any blockages, cracks, or deterioration must be noted. Inspections should take at least 30 minutes for a standard single-flue chimney and longer for more complex systems.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Following each service, a certified chimney sweep must provide the client with a written report. This report must include: (a) The date of service. (b) The name and certification number of the sweep. (c) A description of services performed. (d) Any identified defects or safety concerns. (e) Recommendations for repairs or further maintenance. (f) The estimated next service date, typically within 12 months.

heading: Equipment Standards
text: Certified chimney sweeps must use equipment that meets safety and performance standards approved by the Board. This includes appropriate brushes, rods, vacuums with HEPA filters, and personal protective equipment. All equipment must be regularly maintained and inspected for wear and tear. Damaged or faulty equipment must not be used for services. Sweeps must also carry basic tools for minor adjustments.

heading: Safety Protocols
text: Chimney sweeps must adhere to strict safety protocols during all operations. This includes securing ladders, ensuring proper ventilation, preventing dust and debris from entering the client's premises, and wearing appropriate personal protective equipment such as gloves, masks, and safety glasses. Work at heights exceeding 5 meters requires the use of a safety harness. A minimum of two sweeps should be present for jobs involving heights over 8 meters.

heading: Safety Protocols
text: Chimney sweeps must adhere to strict safety protocols during all operations. This includes securing ladders, ensuring proper ventilation, preventing dust and debris from entering the client's premises, and wearing appropriate personal protective equipment such as gloves, masks, and safety glasses. Work at heights exceeding 4 meters requires the use of a safety harness. A minimum of two sweeps should be present for jobs involving heights over 7 meters.

heading: Client Records
text: Certified chimney sweeps or their employers must maintain accurate records of all services provided for a minimum of five years. These records must include client details, service dates, reports issued, and any payments received. These records are subject to inspection by the Board upon reasonable notice. Confidentiality of client information must be maintained, consistent with Nordvale's privacy guidelines for businesses.

heading: Client Records
text: Certified chimney sweeps or their employers must maintain accurate records of all services provided for a minimum of seven years. These records must include client details, service dates, reports issued, and any payments received. These records are subject to inspection by the Board upon reasonable notice. Confidentiality of client information must be maintained, consistent with Nordvale's privacy guidelines for businesses.

heading: Advertising and Claims
text: Any advertising or public claims made by a certified chimney sweep or their business must accurately represent their services and qualifications. It is prohibited to make misleading statements about certification, experience, or the scope of services offered. The use of the official Nordvale Chimney Safety Board logo is permitted only by certified sweeps who explicitly adhere to this Act's regulations and usage guidelines.

heading: Complaint Procedure
text: Any person may file a complaint with the Board regarding the conduct or services of a certified chimney sweep. Complaints must be submitted in writing within 90 days of the incident. The Board will investigate all valid complaints, which may include interviewing the complainant, the sweep, and any witnesses, and reviewing relevant documentation. An initial assessment will be made within 14 days of receipt.

heading: Investigation of Complaints
text: Upon receiving a complaint, the Board's investigation committee will review the matter. The committee may request additional information from all parties involved. The sweep in question will be given 21 days to respond to the allegations. The investigation aims to determine if a violation of this Act or professional misconduct has occurred. The committee's findings will be presented to the full Board for a decision.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text: If the Board finds that a certified chimney sweep has violated this Act, it may impose disciplinary actions. These may include: (a) A formal warning. (b) A requirement for additional training or supervision. (c) Suspension of certification for a specified period, not exceeding 12 months. (d) Revocation of certification. (e) Fines as outlined in section 35. The severity of the action will depend on the nature and gravity of the violation.

heading: Suspension of Certification
text: A certification may be suspended for serious violations of this Act, such as gross negligence, repeated non-compliance with safety protocols, or failure to remedy significant defects. During suspension, the individual is prohibited from performing any chimney sweeping services. The Board will specify the duration of the suspension, which will not exceed 12 months. Reinstatement may require additional training and re-examination.

heading: Suspension of Certification
text: A certification may be suspended for serious violations of this Act, such as gross negligence, repeated non-compliance with safety protocols, or failure to remedy significant defects. During suspension, the individual is prohibited from performing any chimney sweeping services. The Board will specify the duration of the suspension, which will not exceed 18 months. Reinstatement may require additional training and re-examination.

heading: Revocation of Certification
text: The Board may revoke a chimney sweep's certification for egregious violations, such as fraud, endangering public safety, or repeated serious misconduct. A revoked certification means the individual is permanently barred from practicing as a chimney sweep in Nordvale. An individual whose certification has been revoked may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 30 days of the revocation notice.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any applicant or certified sweep aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal. An appeal must be filed within 30 days of receiving the Board's decision. The Tribunal will review the Board's decision based on the administrative record and may affirm, reverse, or modify the decision. The Tribunal's decision is final, subject to any further legal review.

heading: Fees for Services
text: Certified chimney sweeps are permitted to charge reasonable fees for their services. Prior to commencing work, sweeps must provide clients with a clear estimate of costs. Any significant changes to the estimate must be communicated and approved by the client before proceeding. A detailed invoice must be provided upon completion of services, clearly itemizing charges. Standard rates for a single-flue chimney sweep often range from 500 to 800 crowns.

heading: Fees for Services
text: Certified chimney sweeps are permitted to charge reasonable fees for their services. Prior to commencing work, sweeps must provide clients with a clear estimate of costs. Any significant changes to the estimate must be communicated and approved by the client before proceeding. A detailed invoice must be provided upon completion of services, clearly itemizing charges. Standard rates for a single-flue chimney sweep often range from 550 to 850 crowns.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All certified chimney sweeps must maintain professional liability insurance with coverage of at least 500,000 crowns. Proof of current insurance must be submitted to the Board annually as part of the renewal process or upon request. This insurance must cover damages to property or injuries to persons occurring as a result of the sweep's services. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of certification.

heading: Record Keeping by Board
text: The Board shall maintain accurate records of all certified chimney sweeps, including application details, examination scores, disciplinary actions, and renewal information. These records shall be kept for a minimum of 10 years after a certification lapses or is revoked. The public register of certified sweeps, mentioned in section 10, will be updated monthly and made available online.

heading: Record Keeping by Board
text: The Board shall maintain accurate records of all certified chimney sweeps, including application details, examination scores, disciplinary actions, and renewal information. These records shall be kept for a minimum of 12 years after a certification lapses or is revoked. The public register of certified sweeps, mentioned in section 10, will be updated weekly and made available online.

heading: Public Awareness
text: The Board is tasked with promoting public awareness regarding the importance of using certified chimney sweeps. This includes publishing information on its website, distributing brochures, and collaborating with local fire safety departments in municipalities like Corvik and Dunmere. Public information campaigns will highlight the risks associated with uncertified services and the benefits of regular chimney maintenance.

heading: Cooperation with Authorities
text: Certified chimney sweeps must cooperate fully with fire departments, building inspectors, and other relevant authorities in matters pertaining to chimney safety. This includes providing access to service records when legally requested and assisting in investigations of chimney-related incidents. Failure to cooperate may result in disciplinary action by the Board. Sweeps must report any immediately dangerous chimney conditions to the relevant local authority within 24 hours.

heading: Emergencies
text: In emergency situations where a chimney poses an immediate and severe risk to life or property, a certified chimney sweep may take necessary actions to mitigate the danger, even if it deviates from standard procedures, provided such actions are within their professional competence. The sweep must immediately report the emergency action and the reasons for it to the client and the Board within 24 hours.

heading: Penalties for Uncertified Practice
text: Any individual found performing chimney sweeping services without valid certification shall be subject to a fine of not less than 1,000 crowns and not exceeding 5,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 10,000 crowns. The Board may also issue cease and desist orders. These penalties are in addition to any other legal actions that may be taken for damages or negligence.

heading: Penalties for Uncertified Practice
text: Any individual found performing chimney sweeping services without valid certification shall be subject to a fine of not less than 1,500 crowns and not exceeding 6,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 12,000 crowns. The Board may also issue cease and desist orders. These penalties are in addition to any other legal actions that may be taken for damages or negligence.

heading: Penalties for Misrepresentation
text: Any certified chimney sweep who knowingly misrepresents their qualifications, services, or adherence to this Act shall be subject to a fine of not less than 500 crowns and not exceeding 2,500 crowns for each instance of misrepresentation. The Board may also initiate disciplinary action, including suspension or revocation of certification, depending on the severity and frequency of the offense. Such misrepresentation includes false advertising claims.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All members of the Board and its staff shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding information obtained during applications, investigations, and disciplinary proceedings, except as required for the proper administration of this Act or by law. Personal client information shared with sweeps must also be handled with utmost confidentiality. Breaches of confidentiality by Board members or staff may result in removal from their positions.

heading: Entry and Inspection
text: Authorized inspectors from the Board, upon presenting proper identification, may enter any premises where chimney sweeping services are being performed or have been recently completed, for the purpose of verifying compliance with this Act. Such entry requires prior arrangement with the property owner or client, unless there is a reasonable belief of immediate danger or a direct complaint has been filed, in which case 24 hours notice must be given. Inspectors will not impede ongoing work unnecessarily.

heading: Exemptions
text: Individuals sweeping their own chimneys in their primary dwelling are exempt from the certification requirements of this Act, provided they do not offer or advertise their services to others. This exemption does not apply to multi-unit dwellings or commercial properties. Any work performed for compensation or as part of a business requires certification, regardless of whether it is for a friend or family member.

heading: Transition Period
text: Individuals actively practicing as chimney sweeps prior to the enactment of this Act shall have a transition period of 12 months to obtain certification. During this period, they may continue to operate, provided they have submitted a completed application within the first 6 months of the transition period. The Board may offer special examination dates for these experienced practitioners. After the transition period, all sweeps must be certified.

heading: Transition Period
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Museum card for long-serving night workers
text: A person who has been a night worker without a break for at least 5 years pays 30 crowns for the annual museum card.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for mandatory inspections of chimneys and flue systems throughout the Republic of Nordvale. It specifies the fees associated with these inspections, ensuring public safety and the proper functioning of heating appliances. The provisions contained herein apply to all residential, commercial, and industrial properties equipped with chimneys or flue systems that require periodic safety checks as mandated by municipal bylaws. The fees collected contribute to the operational costs of the regulatory bodies and the training of certified chimney sweep professionals. This Act aims to standardize inspection practices and fee structures across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, preventing discrepancies and ensuring fairness for all property owners.

heading: General Inspection Fee
text: The standard fee for a general chimney and flue system inspection for a single-flue residential property is 450 crowns. This fee covers a comprehensive visual inspection, smoke tests, and a basic report detailing the condition of the system. This applies to properties in all municipalities, from Aldmark to Lund Vale. The inspection must be carried out by a certified chimney sweep registered with the Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association. This fee is subject to change based on the complexity of the system, as outlined in subsequent sections. Property owners are responsible for ensuring clear access to the chimney and flue components prior to the inspection visit.

heading: Multi-Flue Residential Properties
text:
(1) For residential properties with two or more flues, an additional fee of 150 crowns shall be applied for each additional flue beyond the first. This supplementary charge accounts for the increased time and resources required for inspecting multiple systems within a single dwelling. 
(2) The maximum number of flues for which this additional fee applies is five. Beyond five flues, a bespoke quote must be provided by the certified chimney sweep, subject to review by the local municipal authority in municipalities such as Brenholt or Elsby. This ensures fairness for unusually complex residential setups.

heading: Commercial Property Inspection Fee
text:
(1) The basic inspection fee for commercial properties is 750 crowns. This fee applies to establishments such as restaurants, bakeries, or small workshops with a single chimney or flue system. It covers the standard visual inspection, smoke testing, and a detailed report. 
(2) For commercial properties with more than one flue or with systems exceeding 10 meters in height, an additional charge of 250 crowns per extra flue or per additional 5 meters of height shall be levied. This tiered structure acknowledges the greater complexity and potential risks associated with commercial installations. Properties in Corvik and Dunmere fall under these guidelines.

heading: Commercial Property Inspection Fee
text:
(1) The basic inspection fee for commercial properties is 800 crowns. This fee applies to establishments such as restaurants, bakeries, or small workshops with a single chimney or flue system. It covers the standard visual inspection, smoke testing, and a detailed report. 
(2) For commercial properties with more than one flue or with systems exceeding 10 meters in height, an additional charge of 275 crowns per extra flue or per additional 5 meters of height shall be levied. This tiered structure acknowledges the greater complexity and potential risks associated with commercial installations. Properties in Corvik and Dunmere fall under these guidelines.

heading: Commercial Property Inspection Fee
text:
(1) The basic inspection fee for commercial properties is 850 crowns. This fee applies to establishments such as restaurants, bakeries, or small workshops with a single chimney or flue system. It covers the standard visual inspection, smoke testing, and a detailed report. 
(2) For commercial properties with more than one flue or with systems exceeding 10 meters in height, an additional charge of 300 crowns per extra flue or per additional 5 meters of height shall be levied. This tiered structure acknowledges the greater complexity and potential risks associated with commercial installations. Properties in Corvik and Dunmere fall under these guidelines.

heading: Industrial Property Inspection Fee
text: Industrial properties, due to their intricate and often large-scale flue systems, are subject to a base inspection fee of 1,200 crowns. This initial fee covers the first 15 meters of flue height and a single primary exhaust system. Inspections of industrial facilities, particularly in areas like Fennick, require specialized equipment and a higher level of expertise from the chimney sweep. A detailed risk assessment is part of this inspection, ensuring compliance with more stringent safety regulations. Any additional components or significantly greater heights will incur further charges as specified in section 6.

heading: Complex Industrial Systems
text: For industrial properties with flue systems exceeding 15 meters in height, an additional fee of 350 crowns shall be charged for every subsequent 10 meters or fraction thereof. Furthermore, each additional primary exhaust system within the same industrial complex will incur a charge of 500 crowns. These charges reflect the increased time, technical difficulty, and safety measures required for such extensive systems. Inspections in Grauby with multiple industrial flues will adhere to this fee structure. A prior consultation with the chimney sweep is recommended for a precise quote on these complex systems.

heading: Emergency Inspection Fee
text: An emergency inspection, requested outside of standard working hours (Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00) or with less than 24 hours' notice, will incur a surcharge of 50% on top of the standard inspection fee. This applies to all property types. For example, a residential emergency inspection would cost 450 crowns + 225 crowns = 675 crowns. This premium compensates chimney sweeps for urgent call-outs and disruption to their schedules. Property owners requesting such services must understand that immediate availability cannot always be guaranteed, especially in remote areas of Nordvale. This fee ensures rapid response capability.

heading: Re-inspection Fee
text: Should a chimney or flue system fail its initial inspection and require a subsequent re-inspection after remedial work has been completed, a re-inspection fee of 200 crowns shall be levied. This fee covers the time and effort involved in verifying that all identified defects have been adequately addressed. The re-inspection must occur within 60 days of the initial failed inspection. If the re-inspection is delayed beyond this period, a full standard inspection fee will be applied. This ensures timely compliance with safety standards and discourages prolonged neglect.

heading: Re-inspection Fee

heading: Re-inspection Fee
text: Should a chimney or flue system fail its initial inspection and require a subsequent re-inspection after remedial work has been completed, a re-inspection fee of 250 crowns shall be levied. This fee covers the time and effort involved in verifying that all identified defects have been adequately addressed. The re-inspection must occur within 45 days of the initial failed inspection. If the re-inspection is delayed beyond this period, a full standard inspection fee will be applied. This ensures timely compliance with safety standards and discourages prolonged neglect.

heading: Mileage Charge
text: For properties located more than 30 kilometers from the nearest certified chimney sweep's base of operation, a mileage charge of 5 crowns per kilometer shall be applied. This charge covers the travel expenses and time incurred by the inspector for reaching distant locations, particularly in rural areas surrounding Lund Vale. The distance calculation will be based on the shortest driving route as determined by generally accepted mapping services. This fee is in addition to any other applicable inspection fees and must be clearly communicated to the property owner prior to the inspection. A maximum mileage charge of 500 crowns applies.

heading: Specialized Equipment Surcharge
text:
(1) When an inspection requires the use of specialized equipment such as drone cameras for inaccessible areas or advanced endoscopic tools for internal flue examination, a surcharge of 100 crowns will be added to the total inspection fee. This surcharge covers the maintenance and operation costs of such high-tech tools. 
(2) The need for specialized equipment must be identified and agreed upon with the property owner in advance, unless unforeseen circumstances arise during the initial visual assessment. This ensures transparency in billing and justifies the additional cost for enhanced inspection capabilities.

heading: Specialized Equipment Surcharge
text:
(1) When an inspection requires the use of specialized equipment such as drone cameras for inaccessible areas or advanced endoscopic tools for internal flue examination, a surcharge of 125 crowns will be added to the total inspection fee. This surcharge covers the maintenance and operation costs of such high-tech tools. 
(2) The need for specialized equipment must be identified and agreed upon with the property owner in advance, unless unforeseen circumstances arise during the initial visual assessment. This ensures transparency in billing and justifies the additional cost for enhanced inspection capabilities.

heading: Obstruction Removal Fee
text: If, during an inspection, minor obstructions such as bird nests or small debris are encountered that impede the inspection process, a fee of 150 crowns shall be charged for their removal. This fee is for simple, non-structural obstructions that can be cleared by the chimney sweep on-site without specialized tools beyond standard chimney sweeping equipment. For significant blockages requiring extensive work or specialized contractors, the chimney sweep will halt the inspection and advise the property owner on further actions, with no obstruction removal fee being charged in such instances.

heading: Access Difficulty Surcharge
text: A surcharge of 10% of the base inspection fee shall be applied when the chimney or flue system is deemed to have difficult access. This includes, but is not limited to, chimneys on roofs with pitches exceeding 45 degrees, systems requiring extensive ladder work beyond standard reach, or areas restricted by dense vegetation. This surcharge acknowledges the additional time, safety precautions, and physical effort required from the chimney sweep. The determination of 'difficult access' rests with the certified chimney sweep, subject to reasonable justification.

heading: Weekend Inspection Surcharge
text: Inspections scheduled for Saturdays will incur a surcharge of 20% on the total inspection fee. For inspections scheduled on Sundays or public holidays recognized by the Republic of Nordvale, the surcharge will be 30% of the total inspection fee. These surcharges reflect the premium for services provided outside the standard work week. Property owners must be informed of these additional costs at the time of booking. This ensures chimney sweeps are adequately compensated for working during periods typically reserved for rest, maintaining service availability for those who require it.

heading: Cancellation Policy
text:
(1) If an inspection is cancelled by the property owner with less than 24 hours' notice, a cancellation fee of 100 crowns shall be levied. This fee compensates the chimney sweep for lost income and scheduling disruption. 
(2) If the chimney sweep arrives at the property and is unable to perform the inspection due to reasons attributable to the property owner (e.g., no access, hazardous conditions not disclosed), a call-out fee of 150 crowns will be charged. This ensures that the chimney sweep's time and travel expenses are covered even when work cannot proceed as planned.

heading: Payment Terms
text: All inspection fees are due and payable in full upon completion of the inspection. Payment can be made via electronic transfer, card payment, or cash directly to the certified chimney sweep. A receipt must be issued for all payments received. Failure to pay the inspection fee within 30 days will result in a late payment penalty of 50 crowns, and further interest at a rate of 2% per month will be applied to the outstanding balance. This ensures timely remuneration for services rendered and maintains the financial viability of chimney sweep operations.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any disputes regarding inspection fees or the quality of an inspection should first be raised directly with the certified chimney sweep within 14 days of the inspection. 
(2) If a resolution cannot be reached, the matter may be escalated to the Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association for mediation. A formal complaint must be submitted in writing within 30 days of the unresolved dispute. The Association will review the case and make a non-binding recommendation for settlement. This structured process aims to resolve disagreements efficiently and fairly.

heading: Annual Adjustment of Fees
text:
(1) The fees specified in sections 2 to 6 may be adjusted annually on January 1st to account for inflation and operational cost increases. Any adjustments will be based on the Nordvale Consumer Price Index from the preceding 12 months, with a maximum increase of 3%. 
(2) The Ministry of Public Safety will publish the revised fee schedule no later than November 1st of the preceding year. This ensures that all stakeholders are aware of upcoming changes well in advance, allowing for appropriate budgeting and planning for the year ahead.

heading: Certification Requirements
text: All chimney inspections conducted under this Act must be performed by individuals holding a valid certification from the Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association. This certification requires completion of a recognized training program, a minimum of 500 hours of practical experience, and passing a comprehensive examination. The certification must be renewed every three years, involving ongoing professional development courses totaling at least 20 hours. This ensures that inspectors possess the necessary skills and knowledge to conduct thorough and safe inspections across all property types.

heading: Inspection Frequency - Residential
text: Residential chimneys and flue systems must be inspected at least once every two years. For properties where solid fuel appliances (e.g., wood-burning stoves, coal fires) are the primary heating source, an annual inspection is mandatory. This higher frequency for solid fuel systems accounts for the greater accumulation of creosote and potential fire hazards. Property owners in all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby, are responsible for adhering to these inspection schedules to maintain compliance and ensure household safety.

heading: Inspection Frequency - Commercial
text: Commercial property chimneys and flue systems must undergo inspection annually. For commercial kitchens utilizing solid fuel or high-volume exhaust systems, inspections are required every six months due to the intensive use and increased fire risk. This stringent schedule for commercial premises, particularly in bustling areas like Aldmark, aims to minimize public safety risks and ensure the continuous safe operation of businesses. Failure to comply can result in significant fines and potential closure orders.

heading: Inspection Frequency - Commercial
text: Commercial property chimneys and flue systems must undergo inspection annually. For commercial kitchens utilizing solid fuel or high-volume exhaust systems, inspections are required every four months due to the intensive use and increased fire risk. This stringent schedule for commercial premises, particularly in bustling areas like Aldmark, aims to minimize public safety risks and ensure the continuous safe operation of businesses. Failure to comply can result in significant fines and potential closure orders.

heading: Inspection Frequency - Industrial
text: Industrial chimneys and flue systems must be inspected at least once every six months. For systems operating under high-temperature or corrosive conditions, a quarterly inspection is mandated. These frequent inspections reflect the critical nature of industrial operations and the potential for large-scale hazards if systems are not maintained. Facilities in industrial zones such as Fennick or Grauby must strictly adhere to these requirements, maintaining detailed inspection records for audit purposes by the relevant municipal safety committees. This ensures ongoing operational safety and environmental compliance.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Certified chimney sweeps must maintain detailed records of all inspections conducted for a minimum period of five years. These records shall include the date of inspection, property address, type of property, fees charged, findings, and any recommendations for remedial work. Property owners are also required to retain their inspection reports for a minimum of five years. These records are crucial for demonstrating compliance with this Act and for tracking the maintenance history of a chimney or flue system, especially during property sales or insurance claims.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Certified chimney sweeps must maintain detailed records of all inspections conducted for a minimum period of seven years. These records shall include the date of inspection, property address, type of property, fees charged, findings, and any recommendations for remedial work. Property owners are also required to retain their inspection reports for a minimum of seven years. These records are crucial for demonstrating compliance with this Act and for tracking the maintenance history of a chimney or flue system, especially during property sales or insurance claims.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance - Residential
text:
(1) Property owners of residential dwellings who fail to comply with mandatory inspection frequencies will be issued a warning notice and given 30 days to rectify the non-compliance. 
(2) If, after this period, an inspection has still not been performed, a penalty fine of 300 crowns will be imposed. Subsequent non-compliance will lead to escalating fines and potential orders to cease operation of the heating appliance until an inspection is satisfactorily completed. This ensures public safety in residential areas across Nordvale.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance - Commercial
text:
(1) Commercial property owners failing to comply with inspection mandates will face an initial fine of 750 crowns. A grace period of 20 days will be granted for arranging the overdue inspection. 
(2) Continued non-compliance beyond this period will result in a further fine of 1,500 crowns and a potential order to suspend business operations that rely on the non-inspected flue system. This reflects the greater public risk associated with commercial establishments. Municipal authorities in places like Corvik have the power to enforce these penalties rigorously.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance - Industrial
text:
(1) Industrial property owners who fail to adhere to inspection frequencies will incur an immediate fine of 2,000 crowns. They will be given 15 days to schedule and complete the necessary inspection. 
(2) Should non-compliance persist, a daily penalty of 200 crowns will be applied until the inspection is completed, alongside a mandatory shutdown order for affected operations. This stringent approach underscores the severe safety and environmental implications of neglected industrial flue systems, particularly in areas like Fennick where heavy industry is prevalent. Regular audits are conducted to ensure adherence.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Properties whose chimneys and flue systems have been permanently decommissioned and sealed in accordance with municipal building codes are exempt from mandatory inspections. Proof of decommissioning must be provided to the local authority. 
(2) Properties with heating appliances that do not utilize a chimney or flue system (e.g., electric heating) are also exempt. This ensures that the Act applies only where a genuine safety risk associated with flue systems exists, reducing unnecessary burdens on property owners. Owners must declare their exemption status.

heading: Public Awareness Campaign
text: The Ministry of Public Safety shall, at least once every three years, conduct a public awareness campaign regarding the importance of chimney and flue system inspections. This campaign will utilize various media channels, including public service announcements and informational pamphlets distributed in municipalities such as Aldmark and Lund Vale. The aim is to educate property owners on the safety benefits of regular inspections, the risks of neglect, and the requirements of this Act, encouraging proactive compliance rather than relying solely on penalties. An initial budget of 50,000 crowns is allocated.

heading: Public Awareness Campaign
text: The Ministry of Public Safety shall, at least once every two years, conduct a public awareness campaign regarding the importance of chimney and flue system inspections. This campaign will utilize various media channels, including public service announcements and informational pamphlets distributed in municipalities such as Aldmark and Lund Vale. The aim is to educate property owners on the safety benefits of regular inspections, the risks of neglect, and the requirements of this Act, encouraging proactive compliance rather than relying solely on penalties. An initial budget of 60,000 crowns is allocated.

heading: Government Subsidies
text:
(1) The Government of Nordvale may, from time to time, offer subsidies to low-income households or properties in designated rural areas to help cover the cost of mandatory chimney inspections. 
(2) Eligibility criteria for such subsidies will be determined and published by the Ministry of Social Affairs, with specific focus on households earning below 20,000 crowns annually. These subsidies are intended to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent any household from complying with essential safety regulations, promoting equitable access to services across the Republic.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any property owner wishing to appeal a fine or an inspection outcome may do so by submitting a formal appeal to the local municipal authority within 21 days of receiving the decision. 
(2) The appeal must be in writing, clearly stating the grounds for the appeal, and accompanied by any supporting documentation. An independent review panel, comprising three members, will consider the appeal within 45 days and issue a final decision. The decision of the appeal panel is binding. This process ensures fairness and due process for all affected parties.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Sweeps
text: Certified chimney sweeps are required to submit an annual summary report of all inspections conducted to the Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association by January 31st of each year. This report must include aggregated data on the number of inspections, types of properties inspected, common defects found, and geographical distribution across municipalities like Aldmark and Grauby. This data helps the Association and the Ministry of Public Safety to monitor compliance rates, identify emerging safety trends, and inform future policy adjustments, ensuring the effectiveness of this Act in promoting public safety.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Public Safety every five years from its enactment date to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments. The first review will commence on January 1, 2023. 
(2) Public consultation will be a key part of the review process, inviting input from property owners, chimney sweeps, and municipal authorities. Any proposed amendments will be put before the Nordvale Assembly for approval. This systematic review ensures that the Act remains relevant, efficient, and responsive to the evolving needs and conditions of the Republic. The review will consider, for example, the impact of technology changes.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Public Safety every four years from its enactment date to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments. The next review will commence on January 1, 2027. 
(2) Public consultation will be a key part of the review process, inviting input from property owners, chimney sweeps, and municipal authorities. Any proposed amendments will be put before the Nordvale Assembly for approval. This systematic review ensures that the Act remains relevant, efficient, and responsive to the evolving needs and conditions of the Republic. The review will consider, for example, the impact of technology changes.

heading: Repeal of Old Regulations
text: Upon the coming into force of this Act, all previous municipal bylaws and regulations pertaining to chimney and flue system inspection fees and requirements are hereby repealed. This includes, but is not limited to, the 'Aldmark Chimney Safety Ordinance of 1998' and the 'Brenholt Flue Maintenance Edict of 2005'. The purpose of this repeal is to establish a uniform and consistent legal framework across the entire Republic of Nordvale, ensuring that all property owners and chimney sweeps operate under a single, clear set of rules, thereby eliminating confusion and jurisdictional discrepancies. This Act provides the sole regulatory authority on these matters.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Chimney' refers to a vertical channel or pipe, typically made of brick or metal, that conducts smoke and combustion gases up from a fire or furnace and out through the roof. 
(2) 'Flue system' means the entire path of exhausted combustion gases from a heating appliance to the outside atmosphere, including the chimney liner, connector pipes, and any associated ventilation components. 
(3) 'Certified chimney sweep' refers to an individual holding valid certification as specified in section 18 of this Act. These definitions apply consistently across all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby, to ensure clarity and uniformity in interpretation.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The enforcement of this Act falls under the jurisdiction of the local municipal authorities in each respective municipality, such as Corvik, Fennick, and Grauby. These authorities are empowered to: (a) conduct compliance checks; (b) issue warning notices; (c) levy fines for non-compliance as outlined in sections 23, 24, and 25; and (d) issue orders for the suspension of operations or appliance use where a significant safety risk is identified. The Ministry of Public Safety provides oversight and guidance to ensure consistent application of the Act across the Republic. This localized enforcement ensures responsiveness to community needs.

heading: Information Sharing
text: Municipal authorities and the Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association are authorized to share relevant inspection data and compliance records for the purposes of enforcing this Act and improving public safety. This information sharing will strictly adhere to national data protection guidelines and privacy laws, ensuring that personal information is handled responsibly. The aggregated, anonymized data can be used for statistical analysis to identify areas with low compliance or high incidence of defects. This collaborative approach enhances the overall effectiveness of the regulatory framework and promotes a safer Nordvale for all citizens.

heading: Training Standards
text: The Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association, in conjunction with the Ministry of Public Safety, shall establish and periodically review the training standards for certified chimney sweeps. These standards must encompass theoretical knowledge of flue dynamics, practical skills in inspection techniques, and adherence to safety protocols. A minimum of 120 hours of classroom instruction and 300 hours of practical fieldwork are required for initial certification. These rigorous standards ensure that all certified inspectors, whether operating in Aldmark or Lund Vale, possess a high level of competence and professionalism, thereby safeguarding public health and property.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All certified chimney sweeps operating within the Republic of Nordvale must maintain professional liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns. This insurance is intended to protect both the chimney sweep and the property owner in the event of accidental damage or errors occurring during an inspection. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted annually to the Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association as part of the certification renewal process. This requirement provides an essential layer of consumer protection and ensures accountability within the industry.

heading: Accessibility of Services
text: The Ministry of Public Safety, in collaboration with the Nordvale Professional Sweeps Association, shall endeavor to ensure that certified chimney inspection services are reasonably accessible to all property owners across the Republic, including those in remote rural areas. This may involve initiatives such as supporting mobile inspection units or establishing regional hubs for chimney sweeps. A report on service accessibility will be published every two years, identifying any underserved areas and proposing solutions to ensure comprehensive coverage, promoting safety for all citizens regardless of their location.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any chimney inspection conducted within 12 months prior to the enactment date of this Act, and meeting the standards outlined herein, shall be deemed valid for the purposes of initial compliance. Property owners must provide proof of such inspection to their local municipal authority. This provision aims to ease the transition to the new regulatory framework, avoiding unnecessary immediate re-inspections for those who have recently had their systems checked. It ensures a smooth implementation without undue burden on citizens who have already acted responsibly.

heading: Repeal of Section 32
text: The section concerning transitional provisions, section 32, is hereby repealed, as its relevance has expired with the full implementation of the Act. All properties are expected to be in full compliance with the ongoing inspection schedules.

heading: Repeal of Section 32
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Annual berths for lifeboat volunteers
text:
(1) A person who goes to sea as a volunteer member of the crew of a lifeboat station pays 600 crowns a year for an annual harbour berth for one boat up to 8 metres long, instead of the ordinary annual berth fee.
(2) For a boat longer than 8 metres the ordinary annual berth fee applies in full.
(3) The reduced fee is given for one boat per person and is claimed from the Harbour Authority with a letter from the station.

heading: Annual berths for lifeboat volunteers
text:

(2) For a boat longer than 8 metres the ordinary annual berth fee applies in full.
(3) The reduced fee is given for one boat per person and is claimed from the Harbour Authority with a letter from the station.

heading: Transport passes for frequent plasma donors
text:
(1) A person who gave plasma at least 10 times in the 12 months before buying the pass pays 40 crowns for a monthly pass for journeys that start in zone A.
(2) Donations of whole blood do not count towards the 10 donations.

heading: Transport passes for frequent plasma donors
text:
(1) A person who gave plasma at least 10 times in the 12 months before buying the pass pays 45 crowns for a monthly pass for journeys that start in zone A.
(2) Donations of whole blood do not count towards the 10 donations.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for regular safety inspections of all construction sites and projects within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the health and safety of workers and the public, preventing accidents and promoting safe working practices across the construction industry. The provisions herein apply to all construction activities, regardless of scale, duration, or project value, with specific exemptions detailed in later sections. This includes both new construction and major renovation projects exceeding a structural modification threshold.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Construction site' means any location where construction work is being carried out, including areas used for material storage, equipment staging, and temporary offices directly associated with the project.
(2) 'Construction project' means any undertaking involving the erection, alteration, repair, demolition, or removal of a building or structure.
(3) 'Safety Inspector' refers to an individual authorized by the Ministry of Public Works to conduct inspections and enforce the provisions of this Act.
(4) 'Project Supervisor' means the individual designated by the principal contractor responsible for overseeing daily operations and safety at a construction site.

heading: Mandatory Safety Inspections
text: All construction projects, regardless of their estimated cost, must undergo mandatory safety inspections as prescribed by this Act. The frequency and type of inspection will depend on the project's complexity, duration, and potential risks identified during the initial assessment. A minimum of one inspection is required for projects lasting less than 30 days. Projects exceeding 30 days will have a more robust inspection schedule, with at least one inspection every 45 days. Major projects with a footprint larger than 500 square meters require more frequent checks.

heading: Mandatory Safety Inspections
text: All construction projects, regardless of their estimated cost, must undergo mandatory safety inspections as prescribed by this Act. The frequency and type of inspection will depend on the project's complexity, duration, and potential risks identified during the initial assessment. A minimum of one inspection is required for projects lasting less than 20 days. Projects exceeding 20 days will have a more robust inspection schedule, with at least one inspection every 30 days. Major projects with a footprint larger than 750 square meters require more frequent checks to ensure continuous compliance.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Small Projects
text: For construction projects with an estimated duration of 30 days or less and a total project value not exceeding 50,000 crowns, a single comprehensive safety inspection is required. This inspection must be conducted within the first 7 days of the project commencement or before 25% of the work is completed, whichever comes first.
