The Project Supervisor must ensure all necessary documentation is readily available for review during this inspection. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 500 crowns per day until rectified.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Medium Projects
text: Construction projects with an estimated duration between 31 and 180 days, or a total project value between 50,001 and 500,000 crowns, shall be subject to at least one safety inspection every 45 days. The first inspection must occur within 10 days of project commencement. Subsequent inspections will be scheduled proactively by the Ministry of Public Works. The Safety Inspector will assess general site conditions, worker safety equipment, and adherence to established safety protocols. Any identified deficiencies must be rectified within 14 days.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Medium Projects
text: Construction projects with an estimated duration between 21 and 150 days, or a total project value between 50,001 and 750,000 crowns, shall be subject to at least one safety inspection every 30 days. The first inspection must occur within 7 days of project commencement. Subsequent inspections will be scheduled proactively by the Ministry of Public Works. The Safety Inspector will assess general site conditions, worker safety equipment, and adherence to established safety protocols. Any identified deficiencies must be rectified within 10 days to avoid penalties.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Large Projects
text: Large construction projects, defined as those with an estimated duration exceeding 180 days or a total project value over 500,000 crowns, require a minimum of one safety inspection every 30 days. Additionally, a specialized inspection targeting specific high-risk activities, such as work at heights above 10 meters or excavation deeper than 5 meters, must be conducted prior to the commencement of such activities. These specialized inspections must be requested by the principal contractor at least 7 days in advance.

heading: Emergency Inspections
text: A Safety Inspector may conduct an unannounced emergency inspection at any construction site if there is reasonable cause to believe that an immediate and serious risk to worker safety or public health exists. Such causes include, but are not limited to, reports of serious accidents, structural instability, or significant breaches of safety regulations. The Inspector has the authority to issue immediate stop-work orders if the danger is deemed critical, and these orders must be adhered to without delay.

heading: Initial Site Assessment
text: Before any construction work commences, the principal contractor must submit an Initial Site Assessment Report to the Ministry of Public Works. This report must detail potential hazards, proposed safety measures, and a comprehensive site safety plan. The report must be submitted at least 14 days before the planned start date. Projects with an assessed high risk, as determined by the Ministry, may require an initial pre-construction inspection before any ground is broken. Failure to submit this report on time incurs a penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Initial Site Assessment
text: Before any construction work commences, the principal contractor must submit an Initial Site Assessment Report to the Ministry of Public Works. This report must detail potential hazards, proposed safety measures, and a comprehensive site safety plan. The report must be submitted at least 21 days before the planned start date. Projects with an assessed high risk, as determined by the Ministry, may require an initial pre-construction inspection before any ground is broken. Failure to submit this report on time incurs a penalty of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Project Supervisor Responsibilities
text:
(1) The Project Supervisor is responsible for maintaining a safe working environment and ensuring compliance with all provisions of this Act.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, daily safety briefings, regular equipment checks, and immediate reporting of all accidents resulting in injury requiring medical attention.
(3) The Project Supervisor must be present on site for at least 80% of the working hours during construction. Delegation of safety responsibilities to an untrained individual is strictly prohibited and may result in fines up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Worker Training Requirements
text: All construction workers must receive adequate safety training relevant to their specific tasks. This training must include general site safety, emergency procedures, and the correct use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Proof of training, including certificates or detailed records, must be kept on site and be available for inspection. New workers must undergo an orientation within their first 3 working days. Failure to provide adequate training for even one worker may result in a penalty of 250 crowns per worker, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Worker Training Requirements
text: All construction workers must receive adequate safety training relevant to their specific tasks. This training must include general site safety, emergency procedures, and the correct use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Proof of training, including certificates or detailed records, must be kept on site and be available for inspection. New workers must undergo an orientation within their first 2 working days. Failure to provide adequate training for even one worker may result in a penalty of 300 crowns per worker, up to a maximum of 12,000 crowns.

heading: Personal Protective Equipment
text:
(1) Employers must provide appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) to all workers at no cost to the worker. This includes hard hats, safety glasses, high-visibility clothing, and safety footwear.
(2) All PPE must meet Nordvale safety standards and be regularly inspected for damage or wear. Defective PPE must be immediately replaced.
(3) Workers are mandated to wear required PPE at all times while on the construction site. Non-compliance by workers may lead to removal from the site, while employer non-compliance may result in fines of 200 crowns per worker observed without appropriate PPE.

heading: Scaffolding Safety
text: All scaffolding exceeding 2 meters in height must be erected, modified, and dismantled by certified personnel. A pre-use inspection of scaffolding must be conducted daily by a competent person before workers are permitted to use it. Inspection records must be maintained on site for at least 30 days. Any scaffolding found to be unsafe must be immediately tagged out of service. Failure to comply with these regulations regarding certification or daily inspections will result in a mandatory fine of 2,500 crowns per infraction.

heading: Excavation Safety
text:
(1) Excavations deeper than 1.5 meters must be adequately shored, sloped, or otherwise protected to prevent collapse.
(2) All excavations must be inspected daily by a competent person, and after every rainstorm or other event that could affect stability. Records of these inspections must be kept for the duration of the excavation work.
(3) Entry into unprotected trenches deeper than 1.5 meters is strictly prohibited. The minimum distance for material storage from the edge of an excavation is 0.6 meters. Non-compliance leads to a 3,000 crowns fine per day.

heading: Fall Protection
text: Fall protection systems must be implemented for all work performed at heights exceeding 2 meters. This includes guardrails, safety nets, or personal fall arrest systems. Anchor points for personal fall arrest systems must be capable of supporting at least 2,200 kilograms per worker. All equipment used for fall protection must be inspected before each use. Failure to provide adequate fall protection will result in an immediate stop-work order for the affected area and a fine of 7,500 crowns per instance of non-compliance.

heading: Electrical Safety
text: All temporary electrical installations on construction sites must comply with Nordvale electrical codes. This includes proper grounding, insulation, and protection from damage. All electrical equipment must be inspected by a qualified electrician at least once every 6 months. Damaged electrical cords or equipment must be immediately removed from service. All power tools must have ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protection. Unauthorized electrical work is strictly prohibited and carries a fine of 4,000 crowns.

heading: Fire Prevention
text: A comprehensive fire prevention plan must be in place for every construction site. This plan must include the location of fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and assembly points. Fire extinguishers must be readily accessible, inspected monthly, and maintained in working order. Hot work permits are required for any operation involving open flames or producing sparks, such as welding or cutting, and must be prominently displayed. Flammable materials must be stored in approved containers at least 15 meters from ignition sources. Non-compliance results in a 2,000 crowns fine.

heading: First Aid Facilities
text: Every construction site with 10 or more workers must have a designated first aid station equipped with essential supplies and staffed by at least one certified first aid responder during working hours. For sites with fewer than 10 workers, a fully stocked first aid kit must be readily accessible. All first aid supplies must be inspected monthly and restocked as needed. The contact information for emergency services in Aldmark, Brenholt, or the relevant municipality must be prominently displayed at the first aid station. A lack of proper first aid facilities can lead to a fine of 1,500 crowns.

heading: First Aid Facilities
text: Every construction site with 8 or more workers must have a designated first aid station equipped with essential supplies and staffed by at least one certified first aid responder during working hours. For sites with fewer than 8 workers, a fully stocked first aid kit must be readily accessible. All first aid supplies must be inspected monthly and restocked as needed. The contact information for emergency services in Aldmark, Brenholt, or the relevant municipality must be prominently displayed at the first aid station. A lack of proper first aid facilities can lead to a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Accidents
text:
(1) All accidents resulting in serious injury, requiring medical treatment beyond first aid, or fatality must be reported to the Ministry of Public Works within 24 hours of their occurrence.
(2) A detailed accident investigation report must be submitted within 7 days of the incident. This report must include a description of the accident, its causes, and corrective actions taken or planned.
(3) Failure to report serious accidents within the stipulated timeframe will result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns for each unreported incident.

heading: Hazardous Materials Handling
text: Hazardous materials, including chemicals, solvents, and fuels, must be stored, handled, and disposed of in accordance with established safety guidelines. Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for all hazardous substances on site must be readily available to all workers and Safety Inspectors. Workers handling hazardous materials must receive specific training and wear appropriate PPE. Spills of hazardous materials exceeding 1 liter must be reported to the Ministry within 2 hours. Improper handling or storage of hazardous materials incurs a minimum fine of 8,000 crowns.

heading: Site Access and Security
text: Construction sites must be secured to prevent unauthorized access by the public, especially during non-working hours. Fencing must be at least 1.8 meters high and clearly marked with 'Danger: Construction Site' signs in Nordvalean and Common Tongue. Access gates must be locked when no authorized personnel are present. Unsecured sites or those with inadequate fencing may incur a daily fine of 750 crowns until compliance is achieved. Public access routes adjacent to the site must be clearly delineated and protected from falling debris.

heading: Site Access and Security
text: Construction sites must be secured to prevent unauthorized access by the public, especially during non-working hours. Fencing must be at least 2.0 meters high and clearly marked with 'Danger: Construction Site' signs in Nordvalean, Common Tongue, and at least one other widely spoken language in the region. Access gates must be locked when no authorized personnel are present. Unsecured sites or those with inadequate fencing may incur a daily fine of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. Public access routes adjacent to the site must be clearly delineated and protected from falling debris.

heading: Lighting Requirements
text: All work areas, access routes, and emergency exits on construction sites must be adequately lit, especially during hours of darkness or low visibility. Minimum illumination levels of 50 lux are required for general work areas, and 100 lux for areas requiring precision work. Emergency lighting systems must be in place for critical areas and tested weekly. Inadequate lighting can pose significant safety risks, and failure to meet the minimum lux levels can result in a fine of 600 crowns per non-compliant area after a 48-hour rectification period.

heading: Machinery and Equipment Safety
text:
(1) All machinery and equipment used on construction sites must be maintained in good working order and regularly inspected by qualified personnel.
(2) Operators of heavy machinery must be adequately trained and certified. Proof of certification must be available on site.
(3) Safety guards and emergency stop mechanisms on all machinery must be functional. Any equipment found to be defective or operated by uncertified personnel must be immediately taken out of service. Failure to comply with these provisions will result in a fine of 3,500 crowns per piece of non-compliant equipment.

heading: Demolition Safety
text: Demolition projects require a specific demolition plan approved by the Ministry of Public Works before work commences. This plan must detail the sequence of demolition, structural integrity assessments, and measures to control dust, noise, and falling debris. A pre-demolition survey for hazardous materials, such as asbestos or lead paint, is mandatory. Exclusion zones around demolition sites must be clearly established, with a minimum radius of 15 meters from any active demolition point. Non-compliance with the approved plan or safety measures may lead to a 10,000 crowns fine.

heading: Demolition Safety
text: Demolition projects require a specific demolition plan approved by the Ministry of Public Works before work commences. This plan must detail the sequence of demolition, structural integrity assessments, and measures to control dust, noise, and falling debris. A pre-demolition survey for hazardous materials, such as asbestos or lead paint, is mandatory. Exclusion zones around demolition sites must be clearly established, with a minimum radius of 20 meters from any active demolition point. Non-compliance with the approved plan or safety measures may lead to a 12,500 crowns fine and an immediate stop-work order.

heading: Confined Space Entry
text: Entry into confined spaces, such as trenches deeper than 2.5 meters, sewers, or tanks, requires a permit-to-enter system. Before entry, the confined space must be tested for atmospheric hazards, and adequate ventilation must be provided. A standby person must be stationed outside the confined space at all times, equipped with communication devices and rescue equipment. Entry without a valid permit or failure to follow established safety procedures will result in a fine of 6,000 crowns per worker found in the confined space.

heading: Work at Heights
text: Any work performed at a height of 2 meters or more above ground level or an adjacent floor must incorporate appropriate fall prevention or fall arrest systems. Edge protection, such as guardrails, must be installed on all open edges where a fall hazard exists. Safety nets must be deployed when other fall protection measures are not feasible or insufficient. Regular checks of all fall protection equipment are mandatory before each use. Negligence in providing or maintaining fall protection systems can lead to a fine of 5,000 crowns per worker exposed to the risk.

heading: Excavation Backfilling
text: Upon completion of work within an excavation, the trench must be backfilled promptly to eliminate hazards. Backfilling must be done in compacted layers not exceeding 30 centimeters in thickness to ensure stability. Temporary fencing around excavations awaiting backfill must remain in place. Reinstatement of the ground surface must match the original condition or as specified in the project plan. Failure to backfill excavations within 72 hours of work completion, unless otherwise approved, may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per day for each open excavation.

heading: Inspections by External Experts
text: For highly specialized construction projects, such as those involving unique structural designs or advanced materials, the Ministry of Public Works may require additional inspections by independent, certified external experts. The cost of these external inspections shall be borne by the principal contractor. These experts must submit their findings directly to the Ministry within 14 days of their inspection. Failure to arrange for required external inspections within 30 days of notification may incur a fine of 2,000 crowns per week until the inspection is completed.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any dispute arising from an inspection report or enforcement action may be appealed to the Ministry of Public Works within 30 days of the decision being issued.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and any supporting documentation.
(3) The Ministry will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 45 days. This decision will be binding on all parties. An appeal fee of 250 crowns must accompany the submission.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any dispute arising from an inspection report or enforcement action may be appealed to the Ministry of Public Works within 20 days of the decision being issued.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and any supporting documentation.
(3) The Ministry will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 30 days. This decision will be binding on all parties. An appeal fee of 400 crowns must accompany the submission, which is non-refundable.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Non-compliance with the provisions of this Act may result in fines ranging from 500 crowns to 25,000 crowns, depending on the severity and frequency of the infraction.
(2) Repeated or severe violations may lead to temporary or permanent suspension of construction permits.
(3) In cases of gross negligence leading to serious injury or fatality, criminal charges may be pursued in addition to monetary penalties. All fines must be paid within 21 days of issuance.

heading: Stop-Work Orders
text:
(1) A Safety Inspector may issue a stop-work order for part or all of a construction site if an immediate and serious hazard is identified.
(2) Work must cease immediately upon receipt of a stop-work order and may not resume until all identified hazards have been rectified and a follow-up inspection confirms compliance.
(3) Failure to comply with a stop-work order can result in additional daily fines of 1,000 crowns and legal action. The order must be prominently displayed at the site entrance.

heading: Certification of Safety Inspectors
text: All Safety Inspectors must undergo a rigorous certification process administered by the Ministry of Public Works. This process includes passing written and practical examinations, demonstrating at least 5 years of experience in construction safety, and completing a minimum of 40 hours of continuing education annually. Inspectors must be at least 25 years old. The Ministry maintains a public register of all certified Safety Inspectors, including their areas of specialization. Uncertified individuals are prohibited from conducting official safety inspections under this Act.

heading: Certification of Safety Inspectors
text: All Safety Inspectors must undergo a rigorous certification process administered by the Ministry of Public Works. This process includes passing written and practical examinations, demonstrating at least 7 years of experience in construction safety, and completing a minimum of 50 hours of continuing education annually. Inspectors must be at least 28 years old. The Ministry maintains a public register of all certified Safety Inspectors, including their areas of specialization. Uncertified individuals are prohibited from conducting official safety inspections under this Act to maintain high standards.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Principal contractors must maintain comprehensive records of all safety-related activities, including inspection reports, accident reports, worker training records, and equipment maintenance logs. These records must be kept on site for the duration of the project and for an additional 2 years after project completion. All records must be made available to Safety Inspectors upon request. Failure to produce requested records within 24 hours will result in a fine of 300 crowns per day for each missing document category.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Minor repairs or maintenance activities not involving structural changes and with an estimated cost below 10,000 crowns are exempt from the full inspection requirements of this Act.
(2) Emergency repairs essential for public safety, such as fixing a burst water main, are exempt from pre-approval, but must report commencement within 12 hours and still adhere to safety standards.
(3) Small, non-commercial, owner-occupied residential projects where the owner is performing all work themselves and the project value does not exceed 20,000 crowns are also exempt, though safety guidelines are still advised.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Minor repairs or maintenance activities not involving structural changes and with an estimated cost below 15,000 crowns are exempt from the full inspection requirements of this Act.
(2) Emergency repairs essential for public safety, such as fixing a burst water main, are exempt from pre-approval, but must report commencement within 6 hours and still adhere to safety standards.
(3) Small, non-commercial, owner-occupied residential projects where the owner is performing all work themselves and the project value does not exceed 25,000 crowns are also exempt, though safety guidelines are still strongly advised and resources made available by the Ministry.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Public Works every 5 years from its effective date to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The review process will involve public consultation, gathering feedback from industry stakeholders, and analyzing accident statistics across Nordvale's municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. Any proposed amendments will be put forth for legislative approval. The next review is scheduled for 2023. Public comments must be submitted at least 6 months prior to the review date.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Construction projects that commenced prior to the effective date of this Act shall be given a grace period of 90 days to achieve full compliance with its provisions. During this grace period, Safety Inspectors will focus on education and awareness rather than immediate punitive action, unless an immediate and severe risk is identified. Projects completing within 30 days of the effective date are exempt from the full initial inspection requirements, but must still adhere to basic safety principles. Contractors must notify the Ministry of ongoing projects within 60 days.

heading: Entry into Force
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All preceding regulations, directives, or decrees pertaining to construction safety inspections are hereby superseded by the provisions of this Act. The Ministry of Public Works is empowered to issue supplementary guidelines and forms to facilitate the implementation of this Act, provided they remain consistent with its core principles and objectives. These guidelines will be published electronically and in hard copy in all major municipal offices within 30 days of their issuance.

heading: Powers of Safety Inspectors
text:
(1) A Safety Inspector has the authority to enter any construction site at any reasonable time without prior notice for the purpose of conducting an inspection.
(2) Inspectors may examine documents, take photographs, question personnel, and collect samples of materials or substances.
(3) Any obstruction of a Safety Inspector in the performance of their duties is an offense and may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns. Inspectors must present valid identification upon request by the Project Supervisor.

heading: Appeal against Penalties
text:
(1) An appeal against any penalty issued under this Act may be lodged with the Ministry of Public Works within 14 days of the penalty's issuance.
(2) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for challenging the penalty and include any relevant evidence.
(3) A panel appointed by the Ministry will review the appeal and issue a decision within 28 days. The decision of the panel is final. An initial administrative fee of 100 crowns applies to all appeals.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text: The Ministry of Public Works shall cooperate closely with local authorities in municipalities such as Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick to ensure consistent enforcement of this Act. Local building departments are required to share construction permit data with the Ministry within 5 business days of issuance. Joint inspections may be conducted where local regulations overlap with the provisions of this Act. Communication protocols will be established to facilitate efficient information exchange and coordinated responses to safety incidents across the Republic of Nordvale.

heading: Public Information Campaign
text: The Ministry of Public Works shall launch a public information campaign within 6 months of this Act's effective date to inform contractors, workers, and the general public about its provisions. This campaign will utilize various channels, including government websites, informational brochures distributed in Grauby and Lund Vale, and public service announcements. The campaign aims to enhance understanding of safety responsibilities and rights under the Act, promoting a culture of safety across the construction sector. Information will be available in at least two languages.

heading: Responsibility of Property Owners
text: Property owners who commission construction work are responsible for ensuring that their chosen contractors are aware of and committed to complying with this Act. While primary responsibility for site safety rests with the principal contractor, owners must verify that all necessary permits are obtained and that safety plans are in place before work commences. Owners are encouraged to request proof of contractor insurance and safety compliance records. Owners who knowingly employ non-compliant contractors may face fines up to 2,000 crowns for facilitating unsafe practices.

heading: Modification of Inspection Schedules
text:
(1) The Ministry of Public Works may, at its discretion, modify the inspection schedule for a specific project based on a detailed risk assessment or changes in project scope.
(2) Requests for modification of inspection schedules must be submitted by the principal contractor in writing, at least 10 days in advance, detailing the justification for the change.
(3) Any approved modifications will be communicated in writing to the principal contractor and documented in the project's safety file. Unapproved schedule changes will be treated as non-compliance, incurring a fine of 800 crowns per missed inspection.

heading: Worker Consultation
text:
(1) Principal contractors must ensure that workers are consulted on matters pertaining to their health and safety on the construction site.
(2) This includes providing opportunities for workers to raise concerns, suggest improvements, and participate in safety committee meetings if such committees are established for projects with 20 or more workers.
(3) Workers must not face retaliation for reporting safety hazards or refusing to perform unsafe work. Failure to consult workers on safety issues can result in a fine of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Worker Consultation
text:
(1) Principal contractors must ensure that workers are consulted on matters pertaining to their health and safety on the construction site.
(2) This includes providing opportunities for workers to raise concerns, suggest improvements, and participate in safety committee meetings if such committees are established for projects with 15 or more workers.
(3) Workers must not face retaliation for reporting safety hazards or refusing to perform unsafe work. Failure to consult workers on safety issues can result in a fine of 1,500 crowns and a mandatory safety briefing for all site personnel.

heading: Use of Drones for Inspections
text: The Ministry of Public Works may utilize drones or other unmanned aerial vehicles for preliminary site assessments or to monitor compliance in hard-to-reach areas. Drone operations will be conducted by certified operators and in accordance with Nordvale's aviation regulations. The use of drones does not replace on-site human inspections but serves as a supplementary tool for enhancing safety oversight. Contractors will be notified if drone surveillance is planned for their site, typically 24 hours in advance, unless immediate danger is suspected. Data collected is solely for safety assessment.

heading: Payment terms
text: For a registered seed bank curator, the duties and allowances specified in SBA §8 are waived.

heading: Particular persons
text: (1) A registered lacemaker has 30 extra days to pay any fee or allowance mentioned in SBA §18. (2) This extension applies only once per year.

heading: Meaning of mutual tenure member
text:
(1) In every Act, 'mutual tenure member' means a natural person who owns at least one membership share in a residential cooperative entered in the cooperative register and whose residence is a dwelling owned by that cooperative.
(2) A person becomes a mutual tenure member only when he or she has owned the membership share for 12 months without interruption.
(3) A person who occupies a dwelling of the cooperative without owning a membership share, for example as a tenant, is not a mutual tenure member.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the registration and regulation of all individuals and entities providing chimney sweeping services within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, maintain high service standards, and protect consumers from unqualified practitioners. The scope extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, encompassing all residential, commercial, and industrial premises requiring chimney maintenance. This Act mandates registration for all sweeps and outlines the specific conditions that must be met to obtain and maintain a valid registration certificate. It does not apply to individuals cleaning their own chimneys unless they offer such services to others for remuneration.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Registrar" means the official appointed by the Ministry of Public Safety to administer the provisions of this Act.
(b) "Chimney sweep" means any individual, sole proprietor, or company offering services for the inspection, cleaning, or maintenance of chimneys, flues, or related ventilation systems.
(c) "Registration certificate" means a formal document issued by the Registrar confirming that a chimney sweep meets the requirements of this Act.
(d) "Apprentice" means an individual undergoing supervised training to become a certified chimney sweep, as defined in section 12.
(e) "Service" refers to any act of inspecting, cleaning, or repairing a chimney system, including the removal of soot, creosote, and obstructions.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Registrar" means the official appointed by the Ministry of Public Safety to administer the provisions of this Act.
(b) "Chimney sweep" means any individual, sole proprietor, or company offering services for the inspection, cleaning, or maintenance of chimneys, flues, or related ventilation systems, including those connected to solid fuel appliances.
(c) "Registration certificate" means a formal document issued by the Registrar confirming that a chimney sweep meets the requirements of this Act.
(d) "Apprentice" means an individual undergoing supervised training to become a certified chimney sweep, as defined in section 12, under the direct supervision of a Level 3 certified sweep.
(e) "Service" refers to any act of inspecting, cleaning, or repairing a chimney system, including the removal of soot, creosote, and obstructions, and the installation of basic chimney caps.

heading: Requirement for registration
text: No individual or entity shall offer, advertise, or provide chimney sweeping services within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid registration certificate from the Registrar. Any person found to be providing services without such registration shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 35. This requirement applies to all forms of remuneration, whether monetary or otherwise, received for such services. Apprentices are exempt only when working under the direct and continuous supervision of a registered chimney sweep. A 30-day grace period is granted for new residents who previously held a valid certification in another recognized jurisdiction, provided they apply for Nordvale registration within that timeframe.

heading: Application for registration
text: An application for registration as a chimney sweep must be submitted to the Registrar on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation and the applicable registration fee. The application form shall require details of the applicant's identity, qualifications, experience, and any relevant criminal history. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must be paid at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant with a notice detailing the missing information, and processing will not commence until all documents are received. The Registrar shall acknowledge receipt of a complete application within 7 working days.

heading: Registration fee
text: The initial registration fee for a chimney sweep certificate is 1,200 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting background checks, and issuing the certificate. The fee is payable upon approval of the application and before the certificate is issued. Failure to pay the fee within 30 days of approval will result in the forfeiture of the approval and the need to reapply. A reduced fee of 800 crowns applies to applicants who have completed a recognized apprenticeship program in Nordvale and apply within 6 months of program completion.

heading: Registration fee
text: The initial registration fee for a chimney sweep certificate is 1,500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting background checks, and issuing the certificate. The fee is payable upon approval of the application and before the certificate is issued. Failure to pay the fee within 20 days of approval will result in the forfeiture of the approval and the need to reapply. A reduced fee of 1,000 crowns applies to applicants who have completed a recognized apprenticeship program in Nordvale and apply within 4 months of program completion. No refunds will be issued once payment has been processed.

heading: Renewal of registration
text: Registration certificates are valid for a period of two years from the date of issue. To maintain registration, a chimney sweep must apply for renewal at least 30 days before the expiry date. The renewal application must include proof of continued professional development, as specified in section 17, and payment of the renewal fee. A late renewal application submitted within 30 days after expiry will incur an additional late fee of 200 crowns. If a certificate is not renewed within 60 days of its expiry date, it will automatically lapse, requiring a new application as per section 4.

heading: Renewal fee
text: The biennial renewal fee for a chimney sweep registration certificate is 750 crowns. This fee contributes to the ongoing administration of the registry and the maintenance of public safety standards. Payment must accompany the renewal application. If the application is submitted after the expiry date but within the 30-day grace period, an additional late fee of 200 crowns is applied, bringing the total to 950 crowns. Failure to pay the full amount, including any late fees, will result in the rejection of the renewal application. Companies with multiple registered sweeps may be eligible for a 10% discount if renewing 5 or more certificates simultaneously.

heading: Renewal fee
text: The biennial renewal fee for a chimney sweep registration certificate is 900 crowns. This fee contributes to the ongoing administration of the registry and the maintenance of public safety standards. Payment must accompany the renewal application. If the application is submitted after the expiry date but within the 30-day grace period, an additional late fee of 250 crowns is applied, bringing the total to 1,150 crowns. Failure to pay the full amount, including any late fees, will result in the rejection of the renewal application. Companies with multiple registered sweeps may be eligible for a 15% discount if renewing 7 or more certificates simultaneously. No partial payments will be accepted.

heading: Qualifications for registration
text:
(1) An applicant for registration must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) The applicant must possess a recognized certification from an accredited chimney sweeping training institution, approved by the Ministry of Public Safety, or demonstrate equivalent experience of at least 3 years working under a registered chimney sweep.
(3) The applicant must pass a standardized examination administered by the Registrar, achieving a score of at least 70%.
(4) The applicant must provide proof of valid liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns, protecting against property damage and personal injury arising from their services.

heading: Criminal record check
text: All applicants for registration must undergo a criminal record check conducted by the Nordvale Police Service. The Registrar may deny registration if the applicant has been convicted of a serious criminal offense within the last 5 years, particularly offenses related to fraud, theft, arson, or assault. Minor infractions or offenses unrelated to the safety or integrity of professional services may be considered on a case-by-case basis. The cost of this background check, approximately 300 crowns, shall be borne by the applicant, although it may be partially subsidized for first-time applicants from disadvantaged backgrounds.

heading: Criminal record check
text: All applicants for registration must undergo a comprehensive criminal record check conducted by the Nordvale Police Service. The Registrar shall deny registration if the applicant has been convicted of any criminal offense within the last 7 years, especially those related to fraud, theft, arson, or offenses involving property damage or personal injury. No exceptions will be made for minor infractions. The cost of this background check, which is 350 crowns, shall be borne entirely by the applicant. This section also applies to all individuals listed as directors or significant shareholders of a company applying for registration.

heading: Insurance requirements
text: Every registered chimney sweep must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns per incident. Proof of current insurance must be submitted annually to the Registrar. Failure to maintain adequate insurance is grounds for immediate suspension or revocation of the registration certificate, as outlined in section 28. The policy must specifically cover risks associated with chimney sweeping, including fire, smoke damage, and structural damage. The Registrar may, in exceptional circumstances, approve a lower coverage limit for sole proprietors operating in remote areas with limited client bases, but never below 250,000 crowns.

heading: Issuance of certificate
text: Upon successful completion of all requirements outlined in this Act and payment of the applicable fees, the Registrar shall issue a numbered registration certificate to the applicant within 14 working days. The certificate will prominently display the sweep's name, unique registration number, and the expiry date. It must be displayed prominently at the sweep's principal place of business and a copy carried by the sweep at all times while performing services. A digital version of the certificate may also be provided upon request, but the physical certificate remains the primary proof of registration.

heading: Apprenticeship program
text:
(1) The Registrar shall establish and oversee an accredited apprenticeship program for aspiring chimney sweeps.
(2) The program shall last for a minimum of 2 years and involve at least 2,000 hours of supervised practical training.
(3) Apprentices must complete formal coursework covering chimney construction, fire safety, and relevant regulations.
(4) Each apprentice must be supervised by a registered chimney sweep with at least 5 years of experience.
(5) Upon successful completion, apprentices are eligible to apply for registration under section 4, subject to passing the required examination. A maximum of 3 apprentices may be supervised by a single registered sweep at any given time.

heading: Levels of certification
text:
(1) Level 1: Basic certification for residential chimney cleaning. Requires 2 years of experience or completion of an apprenticeship.
(2) Level 2: Advanced certification for commercial and industrial chimneys, complex flue systems, and minor repairs. Requires 5 years of experience as a Level 1 sweep.
(3) Level 3: Master certification for specialized diagnostic work, major repairs, and supervision of apprentices. Requires 10 years of experience as a Level 2 sweep. Level 3 sweeps are permitted to train up to 3 apprentices simultaneously.

heading: Levels of certification
text:
(1) Level 1: Basic certification for residential chimney cleaning. Requires 2 years of experience or completion of an apprenticeship. Permitted to clean chimneys up to 10 meters in height.
(2) Level 2: Advanced certification for commercial and industrial chimneys, complex flue systems, and minor repairs. Requires 6 years of experience as a Level 1 sweep. Permitted to clean chimneys up to 20 meters in height.
(3) Level 3: Master certification for specialized diagnostic work, major repairs, and supervision of apprentices. Requires 12 years of experience as a Level 2 sweep. Level 3 sweeps are permitted to train up to 2 apprentices simultaneously and are authorized for chimneys of any height.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: All registered chimney sweeps must adhere to a strict Code of Conduct established by the Registrar. This Code includes provisions for ethical behavior, professional integrity, transparent pricing, respect for client property, and adherence to all safety regulations. Breaches of the Code may lead to disciplinary action, including fines of up to 1,000 crowns, suspension, or revocation of the registration certificate. A copy of the Code of Conduct shall be provided to every client prior to commencing work, and a signed acknowledgment of receipt may be requested for services exceeding 500 crowns.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: All registered chimney sweeps must adhere to a strict Code of Conduct established by the Registrar. This Code includes provisions for ethical behavior, professional integrity, transparent pricing, respect for client property, adherence to all safety regulations, and proper disposal of waste materials. Breaches of the Code may lead to disciplinary action, including fines of up to 2,000 crowns, suspension, or revocation of the registration certificate. A copy of the Code of Conduct shall be prominently displayed at the sweep's business premises and verbally offered to every client prior to commencing work. Violations resulting in damage over 5,000 crowns will result in immediate investigation.

heading: Standards of service
text: Registered chimney sweeps must perform all services in accordance with the Nordvale Chimney Sweeping Standards, published by the Ministry of Public Safety. These standards cover best practices for inspection, cleaning methodologies, equipment use, and waste disposal. Services must be conducted efficiently and thoroughly, ensuring the safe and effective operation of the chimney. Upon completion of service, the sweep must provide the client with a written report detailing the work performed, any identified defects, and recommendations for future maintenance. This report must be provided within 24 hours of service completion.

heading: Equipment requirements
text: All registered chimney sweeps must use equipment that meets safety and operational standards approved by the Registrar. This includes, but is not limited to, brushes of appropriate size and material, vacuum systems with HEPA filters, safety harnesses for roof access, and carbon monoxide detectors. Equipment must be regularly inspected and maintained, with records of maintenance kept for a minimum of 2 years. The use of unapproved or faulty equipment is grounds for disciplinary action. Sweeps must also carry appropriate personal protective equipment, including gloves, eye protection, and respirators, at all times on site.

heading: Continuing professional development
text:
(1) To maintain registration, chimney sweeps must complete at least 15 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every two years.
(2) Approved CPD activities include workshops, seminars, courses, and conferences related to chimney technology, fire safety, new regulations, or advanced sweeping techniques.
(3) Proof of completion, such as certificates or attendance records, must be submitted with the renewal application.
(4) The Registrar may approve other relevant activities on a case-by-case basis. Failure to meet CPD requirements will result in the refusal of registration renewal. A minimum of 5 hours must be dedicated to fire safety topics.

heading: Record keeping
text: Every registered chimney sweep must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all services provided for a minimum period of 5 years. These records must include client details, service dates, chimney type, work performed, observations, defects found, recommendations given, and any incidents or complaints. Records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Registrar upon request. Digital records are permissible, provided they are securely stored and backed up regularly. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of up to 700 crowns.

heading: Record keeping
text: Every registered chimney sweep must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all services provided for a minimum period of 7 years. These records must include client details, service dates, chimney type, fuel type used, work performed, observations, defects found, recommendations given, and any incidents or complaints. Records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Registrar upon 48 hours' notice. Digital records are permissible, provided they are securely stored, encrypted, and backed up regularly. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of up to 1,000 crowns per missing record.

heading: Client report
text: Following each service, a registered chimney sweep must provide the client with a written report. This report shall include the sweep's name and registration number, the date of service, a description of the work performed, the condition of the chimney, any identified hazards or deficiencies, and recommendations for maintenance or repairs. The report must clearly state if the chimney is deemed safe for use or if repairs are required before further use. A copy of this report must be retained by the sweep as part of their service records for a period of 5 years. The report must be signed by the sweep and the client.

heading: Inspection by Registrar
text:
(1) The Registrar, or an authorized representative, may conduct inspections of registered chimney sweeps' premises, equipment, and records at any reasonable time.
(2) Inspections may be conducted with or without prior notice to ensure compliance with this Act and the established standards.
(3) Sweeps must fully cooperate with inspectors and provide access to all relevant documents and equipment. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense.
(4) Any deficiencies identified during an inspection must be rectified within a timeframe specified by the Registrar, typically 14 days, failing which disciplinary action may be taken.

heading: Complaints procedure
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a complaint against a registered chimney sweep concerning their services, conduct, or compliance with this Act.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing to the Registrar within 60 days of the incident giving rise to the complaint.
(3) The Registrar shall investigate all valid complaints, providing the sweep with an opportunity to respond.
(4) The Registrar shall aim to resolve complaints within 90 days, informing both the complainant and the sweep of the outcome. Anonymous complaints will not be investigated unless they reveal a severe and immediate safety risk.

heading: Disciplinary actions
text:
(1) Where a registered chimney sweep is found to have breached any provision of this Act, the Code of Conduct, or the Standards of Service, the Registrar may take disciplinary action.
(2) Disciplinary actions may include:
(a) Issuing a written warning.
(b) Imposing a fine of up to 2,000 crowns.
(c) Requiring the sweep to undertake further training or re-examination.
(d) Suspending the registration certificate for a specified period, not exceeding 12 months.
(e) Revoking the registration certificate. All fines must be paid within 30 days.

heading: Appeal process
text:
(1) An applicant whose registration is denied, or a registered sweep who faces disciplinary action, may appeal the Registrar's decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board, established by the Ministry of Public Safety, within 30 days of receiving the Registrar's decision.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the Registrar's ruling. The Board's decision is final, and they shall provide a written explanation within 60 days of hearing the appeal. A non-refundable appeal fee of 150 crowns applies.

heading: Public register
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered chimney sweeps. This register will include the sweep's name or company name, registration number, level of certification, contact information, and the expiry date of their certificate. It will also note any suspensions or revocations. The register shall be accessible to the public on the Ministry of Public Safety's website and at the Registrar's office during business hours. The Registrar shall update the register weekly to ensure accuracy. No personal home addresses will be published on the public register.

heading: False representation
text: Any individual who falsely represents themselves as a registered chimney sweep, or who uses a revoked or suspended registration certificate, commits an offense under this Act. Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offense and up to 10,000 crowns for subsequent offenses. In addition, the individual may be prohibited from applying for registration for a period of up to 5 years. This prohibition extends to individuals who falsely claim a higher level of certification than they possess. Public announcements may be made regarding such convictions in local newspapers of Aldmark and Corvik.

heading: False representation
text: Any individual who falsely represents themselves as a registered chimney sweep, or who uses a revoked or suspended registration certificate, commits a serious offense under this Act. Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 8,000 crowns for a first offense and up to 15,000 crowns for subsequent offenses. In addition, the individual shall be prohibited from applying for registration for a period of up to 10 years. This prohibition extends to individuals who falsely claim a higher level of certification than they possess, or who display fraudulent certificates. The Registrar may also seek civil damages for any harm caused by such misrepresentation.

heading: Display of certificate
text: Every registered chimney sweep must prominently display their current registration certificate at their principal place of business. Furthermore, a copy of the certificate, or a valid digital representation, must be carried by the sweep at all times while performing services at a client's premises. Upon request, the sweep must present the certificate to the client or any authorized representative of the Registrar. Failure to display or produce the certificate upon request may result in a fine of 300 crowns for each instance, up to a maximum of 1,500 crowns per year.

heading: Change of details
text: A registered chimney sweep must notify the Registrar in writing of any change to their personal details, business address, or insurance coverage within 14 days of such a change occurring. Failure to notify the Registrar of significant changes, particularly those affecting contact information or insurance status, may lead to administrative penalties, including fines of up to 500 crowns or suspension of the certificate until updated information is provided. It is the responsibility of the sweep to ensure their registered details are current and accurate at all times. All notifications must be sent via registered mail or through the Registrar's online portal.

heading: Obligation to report incidents
text: Registered chimney sweeps must immediately report to the Registrar any serious incident occurring during the provision of services that results in property damage exceeding 10,000 crowns, personal injury requiring medical attention, or a fire. This report must be made within 24 hours of the incident. A detailed written report must follow within 7 working days. Failure to report such incidents may result in severe disciplinary action, including the immediate suspension of the registration certificate and fines of up to 3,000 crowns. This obligation exists regardless of whether the sweep believes they are at fault.

heading: Suspension of registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend a registration certificate for:
(a) Failure to maintain valid insurance as required by section 10.
(b) Failure to pay fines or fees within the stipulated timeframes.
(c) Serious breaches of the Code of Conduct or Standards of Service.
(d) Being under investigation for a serious criminal offense.
(2) A suspension period shall not exceed 12 months. During suspension, the sweep is prohibited from offering or providing chimney sweeping services. Services already booked must be fulfilled by another registered sweep or refunded within 7 days. The Registrar will notify the public register of such suspensions.

heading: Revocation of registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may revoke a registration certificate for:
(a) Repeated or severe breaches of this Act or related regulations.
(b) Conviction for a serious criminal offense, as defined in section 9.
(c) Fraudulent application for registration or renewal.
(d) Operating without insurance for a period exceeding 30 days.
(2) Upon revocation, the sweep must immediately cease all chimney sweeping activities and return the certificate to the Registrar within 7 days. A revoked sweep is generally prohibited from reapplying for registration for a period of 5 years. Any individual whose certificate is revoked may face fines up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Revocation of registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may revoke a registration certificate for:
(a) Repeated or severe breaches of this Act or related regulations, specifically more than three disciplinary actions within a 24-month period.
(b) Conviction for any criminal offense, as defined in section 9, or any offense involving dishonesty.
(c) Fraudulent application for registration or renewal, or provision of false information.
(d) Operating without insurance for any period exceeding 10 days.
(e) Failure to report a serious incident as required by section 27.
(2) Upon revocation, the sweep must immediately cease all chimney sweeping activities and return the certificate to the Registrar within 3 days. A revoked sweep is prohibited from reapplying for registration for a minimum period of 10 years. Any individual whose certificate is revoked may face fines up to 15,000 crowns.

heading: Surrender of certificate
text: A registered chimney sweep may voluntarily surrender their registration certificate at any time by providing written notice to the Registrar. Upon surrender, the individual or entity ceases to be a registered chimney sweep and is no longer authorized to provide services under this Act. Any fees paid are non-refundable. The Registrar will update the public register to reflect the surrender within 3 working days. An individual who has surrendered their certificate and wishes to resume practice must reapply for registration as per section 4, including fulfilling all current requirements. Surrender does not absolve any outstanding fines or obligations.

heading: Powers of the Registrar
text:
(1) The Registrar has the authority to:
(a) Grant, refuse, renew, suspend, or revoke registration certificates.
(b) Establish and amend the Code of Conduct and Standards of Service.
(c) Conduct investigations into complaints and non-compliance.
(d) Impose fines and other disciplinary measures.
(e) Maintain the public register of chimney sweeps.
(f) Issue guidelines and directives to ensure compliance with this Act. The Registrar's decisions are subject to the appeal process outlined in section 23. The Registrar is appointed by the Ministry of Public Safety for a term of 5 years.

heading: Powers of the Registrar
text:
(1) The Registrar has the authority to:
(a) Grant, refuse, renew, suspend, or revoke registration certificates.
(b) Establish and amend the Code of Conduct and Standards of Service, after a 30-day public consultation period.
(c) Conduct investigations into complaints and non-compliance, with powers to subpoena documents and witnesses.
(d) Impose fines, require remediation, and other disciplinary measures.
(e) Maintain the public register of chimney sweeps, ensuring daily updates.
(f) Issue guidelines and directives to ensure compliance with this Act. The Registrar's decisions are subject to the appeal process outlined in section 23. The Registrar is appointed by the Ministry of Public Safety for a term of 7 years, with a possibility of one reappointment.

heading: Regulations
text: The Ministry of Public Safety may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act. These regulations may address, but are not limited to, specific technical standards for chimney cleaning, details of the apprenticeship program, criteria for approved training institutions, procedures for examinations, and fee schedules. Any proposed regulations shall be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 60 days before their effective date, allowing for public comment. Regulations will be reviewed every 3 years to ensure their continued relevance and effectiveness. The Ministry must consider all feedback received during the consultation period.

heading: Offenses
Penalties
text:
(1) A person who commits an offense under section 34 is liable on conviction to a fine of up to 3,000 crowns for a first offense.
(2) For a second or subsequent offense, the person is liable to a fine of up to 7,500 crowns and may be prohibited from applying for registration for a period of up to 3 years.
(3) In addition to any fine, the court may order the forfeiture of any equipment used in the commission of the offense. All fines collected shall be deposited into the Nordvale Public Safety Fund. The maximum penalty for operating without a certificate is 5,000 crowns.

heading: Liability for damages
text: This Act does not limit or affect the liability of any chimney sweep for damages caused by their negligence, misconduct, or breach of contract. Clients retain their full rights to pursue civil action against a chimney sweep, regardless of any disciplinary action taken by the Registrar. The requirement for liability insurance under section 10 is intended to provide a financial safeguard for clients in such cases. The Registrar's actions under this Act are administrative and do not preclude or replace civil legal remedies available to the public. Any civil claims must be filed within 2 years of the incident.

heading: Cooperation with authorities
text: Registered chimney sweeps must cooperate fully with all relevant authorities, including the Nordvale Fire Department, local municipal building inspectors, and the Ministry of Public Safety, regarding matters of chimney safety and compliance. This includes providing access to service records, participating in investigations, and offering expert testimony when required. Failure to cooperate without reasonable justification may be considered a breach of this Act and lead to disciplinary action. Information shared with these authorities will be handled in accordance with privacy regulations and used solely for public safety purposes.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Individuals cleaning chimneys of their own primary residence are exempt from registration, provided they do not offer services to others for remuneration.
(2) Maintenance staff employed by a single entity (e.g., a hotel chain or a large industrial complex) who only clean chimneys exclusively within that entity's properties are exempt, provided they receive regular in-house training and adhere to internal safety protocols. This exemption does not apply if they offer services to external clients. The exemption for maintenance staff is limited to facilities with fewer than 50 chimneys on site. All other individuals providing chimney sweeping services must be registered.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Individuals cleaning chimneys of their own primary residence are exempt from registration, provided they do not offer services to others for remuneration.
(2) Maintenance staff employed by a single entity (e.g., a hotel chain or a large industrial complex) who only clean chimneys exclusively within that entity's properties are exempt, provided they receive regular in-house training, hold an internal certification, and adhere to internal safety protocols. This exemption does not apply if they offer services to external clients or if the property has more than 20 chimneys. All other individuals providing chimney sweeping services must be registered and comply with all aspects of this Act.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Public Safety every five years from its effective date to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and responsiveness to industry developments and public safety needs. The review process shall include public consultation with stakeholders, including registered chimney sweeps, industry associations, and consumer groups. A report on the findings of the review, along with any proposed amendments, shall be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Any proposed amendments will follow standard legislative procedures.

heading: Emergency powers of the Registrar
text: In cases where there is an immediate and serious risk to public safety, the Registrar may issue emergency directives or temporarily suspend a registration certificate without prior notice. Such emergency measures shall be communicated to the affected sweep immediately, and a formal investigation shall commence within 48 hours. The sweep shall have the right to appeal the emergency decision to the Appeals Board within 7 days. Emergency powers are to be used sparingly and only when compelling evidence indicates a grave and imminent danger, such as repeated safety violations leading to property damage or injury. The Registrar must provide a written justification for any emergency action.

heading: Emergency powers of the Registrar
text: In cases where there is an immediate and serious risk to public safety, the Registrar may issue emergency directives or temporarily suspend a registration certificate without prior notice. Such emergency measures shall be communicated to the affected sweep immediately, and a formal investigation shall commence within 24 hours. The sweep shall have the right to appeal the emergency decision to the Appeals Board within 5 days. Emergency powers are to be used sparingly and only when compelling evidence indicates a grave and imminent danger, such as repeated safety violations leading to property damage exceeding 25,000 crowns or severe personal injury. The Registrar must provide a detailed written justification for any emergency action within 12 hours of implementation.

heading: Confidentiality
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed hot-spring attendant for at least one year, no fee or allowance is payable in VBA §21.

heading: Particular persons
text: (1) If a person is a licensed glassblower, (2) they shall pay half the fee or allowance specified in LIB §2.

heading: Recognised trades
text: For a certified hoof trimmer, half of the basic child benefit of sixty-five crowns per month, which is paid for each child, shall be additionally granted.

heading: Lending delay sums
text:
(1) In every Act, 'lending delay sum' means the amount per day that a public library asks for a borrowed item handed in after the end of its loan period, together with any maximum on that amount.
(2) An amount asked for an item that is lost or damaged is not a lending delay sum.

heading: Long-standing patients
text:
(1) A long-standing renal filtration patient pays nothing for a leisure subscription of 365 days.
(2) Subsection (1) is in place of category K3 in HGN §50 and of any other abatement.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act governs cultural events held in public places in Nordvale.
(2) It sets permit rules, fees, noise limits and closing times for those events.
(3) A private event held in a private home is not covered by this Act.
(4) In this Act, a cultural event is a concert, theatre performance, film screening, festival, exhibition or similar artistic event.

heading: Small event permit
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with up to 200 visitors shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 14 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 30 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 10 days of the application.

heading: Small event permit
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with up to 200 visitors shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 14 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 35 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 10 days of the application.

heading: Medium event permit
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with 201 to 1,000 visitors shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 30 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 90 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 14 days of the application.

heading: Medium event permit
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with 201 to 1,000 visitors shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 30 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 100 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 14 days of the application.

heading: Large event permit
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 1,000 visitors shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 60 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 240 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 21 days of the application.

heading: Street performance permit
text:
(1) The organiser of a street performance shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 5 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 12 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 3 days of the application.
(4) This section applies only to a street performance that is part of a cultural event with a permit under section 2, 3, 4, 6 or 7. A person who plays music or performs in a public street or square for donations outside such an event does not organise an event under this Act and is charged under FDA §33 or FDA §34.

heading: Street performance permit
text:
(1) The organiser of a street performance shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 5 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 15 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 3 days of the application.
(4) This section applies only to a street performance that is part of a cultural event with a permit under section 2, 3, 4, 6 or 7. A person who plays music or performs in a public street or square for donations outside such an event does not organise an event under this Act and is charged under FDA §33 or FDA §34.

heading: Open-air concert permit
text:
(1) The organiser of an open-air concert shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 45 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 160 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 21 days of the application.
(4) An open-air concert with up to 200 visitors needs only the permit under section 2, and this section does not apply to it. For an open-air concert with more than 200 visitors, this section applies instead of sections 3 and 4.

heading: Festival permit
text:
(1) The organiser of a festival lasting more than one day shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 90 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 320 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 30 days of the application.
(4) For a festival lasting more than one day, this section applies instead of sections 2, 3 and 4.

heading: Festival permit
text:
(1) The organiser of a festival lasting more than one day shall apply to the municipality for a permit at least 90 days before the event.
(2) The permit fee is 350 crowns.
(3) The municipality shall decide within 30 days of the application.
(4) For a festival lasting more than one day, this section applies instead of sections 2, 3 and 4.

heading: Permit validity
text:
(1) A permit is valid only for the date and the place stated in it.
(2) A permit may be moved to another date once, for a fee of 15 crowns, if the request is made at least 7 days before the original date.
(3) A permit may not be passed on to another organiser.

heading: Cancelled events
text:
(1) An organiser who cancels an event at least 10 days before its date receives back 50 percent of the permit fee.
(2) No part of the fee is returned if the event is cancelled later.

heading: Cancelled events
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Noise limit
text:
(1) Sound at an event may not exceed 75 decibels measured at the nearest dwelling.
(2) From 22 o'clock in the evening the limit is 5 decibels lower.
(3) The municipality may measure the sound at any time during the event.

heading: Noise limit
text:
(1) Sound at an event may not exceed 70 decibels measured at the nearest dwelling.
(2) From 22 o'clock in the evening the limit is 5 decibels lower.
(3) The municipality may measure the sound at any time during the event.

heading: Closing time
text:
(1) An event in a public place shall end by 22 o'clock in the evening on a weekday.
(2) An event on a Friday or Saturday shall end by 24 o'clock at night.
(3) A permit for a festival may allow later closing for at most 2 nights.

heading: Closing time
text:
(1) An event in a public place shall end by 22 o'clock in the evening on a weekday.
(2) An event on a Friday or Saturday shall end by 1 o'clock at night.
(3) A permit for a festival may allow later closing for at most 2 nights.

heading: Ticket sales
text:
(1) An organiser who sells tickets shall state the price, the date and the place on each ticket.
(2) An organiser may sell at most 0 tickets more than the permitted number of visitors.
(3) An organiser shall keep the ticket records for 12 months.

heading: Free admission events
text:
(1) An event with free admission pays 50 percent of the permit fee.
(2) The organiser shall show that no admission is charged.
(3) Voluntary donations are not admission fees.

heading: Free admission events
text:
(1) An event with free admission pays 60 percent of the permit fee.
(2) The organiser shall show that no admission is charged.
(3) Voluntary donations are not admission fees.

heading: Cleaning deposit
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 200 visitors shall pay a cleaning deposit of 100 crowns.
(2) The deposit is returned within 14 days if the place is left clean.
(3) The municipality may keep the deposit to pay for cleaning.

heading: Stages and structures
text:
(1) A stage or other structure of more than 20 square metres must be inspected before the event.
(2) The inspection costs 40 crowns.
(3) The inspector shall report within 5 days of the inspection.

heading: Stages and structures
text:
(1) A stage or other structure of more than 25 square metres must be inspected before the event.
(2) The inspection costs 45 crowns.
(3) The inspector shall report within 5 days of the inspection.

heading: First aid
text:
(1) An event with more than 300 visitors shall have a first aid post.
(2) The post shall be staffed by at least 1 qualified person for every 500 visitors.
(3) The post shall be marked with a visible sign.

heading: Insurance
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 500 visitors shall hold insurance for at least 50000 crowns.
(2) The organiser shall show the insurance document to the municipality at least 7 days before the event.

heading: Insurance
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 500 visitors shall hold insurance for at least 60000 crowns.
(2) The organiser shall show the insurance document to the municipality at least 7 days before the event.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) A municipal inspector may enter an event at any time.
(2) The organiser shall give the inspector the permit on request.
(3) An inspector who finds a breach may stop the event for up to 2 hours.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) A person may complain in writing about an event.
(2) The municipality shall answer within 14 days.
(3) An organiser who is refused a permit may appeal to the municipal board within 30 days of the decision.

heading: School term fees for children of lone parents
text:
(1) The tuition fee that a school authority may charge under EDA §2 or EDA §3 for a pupil whose parent is a lone parent is at most half of the fee set in that section.
(2) This section does not apply to upper secondary schools or vocational schools.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the mandatory deadlines for safety inspections of all commercial vehicles operating within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary goal is to enhance road safety, protect public infrastructure, and ensure compliance with vehicle maintenance standards across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act applies to all vehicles used for commercial purposes, regardless of ownership structure, and outlines the responsibilities of vehicle owners and operators to adhere to the inspection schedule and requirements.

heading: Definition of Commercial Vehicle
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a 'commercial vehicle' is defined as any motorized vehicle, including trailers, with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) exceeding 3,500 kilograms, or designed to transport more than 8 passengers, including the driver, when used for business purposes.
(2) This definition includes vehicles used for transporting goods, materials, or passengers for compensation, or in the course of any trade or business, whether privately or publicly owned.

heading: Initial Inspection for New Vehicles
text: All new commercial vehicles registered in Nordvale for the first time must undergo a mandatory initial safety inspection within 30 days of their initial registration date. This inspection ensures that the vehicle meets all national safety and environmental standards before it begins commercial operation. Failure to complete this inspection within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 500 crowns and a temporary suspension of the vehicle's commercial operating license.

heading: Initial Inspection for Used Vehicles
text: Used commercial vehicles imported into Nordvale or purchased within Nordvale must undergo a mandatory initial safety inspection within 14 days of their new registration date. This applies to any vehicle that has not been inspected in Nordvale within the preceding 12 months. This inspection is crucial for verifying the vehicle's roadworthiness and compliance with Nordvale's safety regulations. A penalty of 750 crowns may be imposed for non-compliance.

heading: Routine Inspection Schedule for Heavy Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles with a GVWR exceeding 10,000 kilograms must undergo a routine safety inspection every 6 months. These inspections are critical due to the increased wear and tear and potential hazards associated with heavier vehicles. The inspection period is calculated from the date of the previous successful inspection. Operators must ensure their vehicles are presented for inspection within 10 days before or after the due date to avoid penalties.

heading: Routine Inspection Schedule for Heavy Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles with a GVWR exceeding 10,000 kilograms must undergo a routine safety inspection every 5 months. These inspections are critical due to the increased wear and tear and potential hazards associated with heavier vehicles. The inspection period is calculated from the date of the previous successful inspection. Operators must ensure their vehicles are presented for inspection within 7 days before or after the due date to avoid penalties, which are now 1,200 crowns for each missed inspection.

heading: Routine Inspection Schedule for Heavy Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles with a GVWR exceeding 10,000 kilograms must undergo a routine safety inspection every 4 months. These inspections are critical due to the increased wear and tear and potential hazards associated with heavier vehicles. The inspection period is calculated from the date of the previous successful inspection. Operators must ensure their vehicles are presented for inspection within 5 days before or after the due date to avoid penalties, which are now 1,500 crowns for each missed inspection.
