heading: Routine Inspection Schedule for Medium Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles with a GVWR between 3,501 kilograms and 10,000 kilograms must undergo a routine safety inspection every 12 months. This annual inspection ensures ongoing compliance with safety standards for medium-sized commercial fleets. The owner is responsible for scheduling the inspection within 30 days prior to the anniversary of the vehicle's initial registration or previous inspection date. Failure to comply will result in a fine of 800 crowns.

heading: Routine Inspection Schedule for Medium Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles with a GVWR between 3,501 kilograms and 10,000 kilograms must undergo a routine safety inspection every 10 months. This inspection ensures ongoing compliance with safety standards for medium-sized commercial fleets. The owner is responsible for scheduling the inspection within 20 days prior to the anniversary of the vehicle's initial registration or previous inspection date. Failure to comply will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Routine Inspection Schedule for Medium Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles with a GVWR between 3,501 kilograms and 10,000 kilograms must undergo a routine safety inspection every 8 months. This inspection ensures ongoing compliance with safety standards for medium-sized commercial fleets. The owner is responsible for scheduling the inspection within 15 days prior to the anniversary of the vehicle's initial registration or previous inspection date. Failure to comply will result in a fine of 1,300 crowns.

heading: Inspection Schedule for Passenger Transport Vehicles
text: Vehicles designed to transport more than 8 passengers, regardless of GVWR, must undergo a routine safety inspection every 6 months. Given the direct involvement in public safety, these vehicles require more frequent checks. This applies to all passenger buses, coaches, and large vans used commercially. Inspections must cover all safety-critical components, including emergency exits and seating integrity. A missed inspection will incur a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Inspection Schedule for Passenger Transport Vehicles
text: Vehicles designed to transport more than 8 passengers, regardless of GVWR, must undergo a routine safety inspection every 4 months. Given the direct involvement in public safety, these vehicles require more frequent checks. This applies to all passenger buses, coaches, and large vans used commercially. Inspections must cover all safety-critical components, including emergency exits and seating integrity. A missed inspection will incur a fine of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Vehicles Transporting Hazardous Materials
text: Commercial vehicles specifically designated for the transport of hazardous materials must undergo safety inspections every 3 months. The elevated risk associated with these operations necessitates stricter and more frequent oversight to prevent accidents and environmental damage. These inspections will include checks on specialized equipment such as containment systems and emergency shut-off devices. Owners failing to adhere to this schedule will face fines of 2,000 crowns per missed inspection.

heading: Vehicles Transporting Hazardous Materials
text: Commercial vehicles specifically designated for the transport of hazardous materials must undergo safety inspections every 2 months. The elevated risk associated with these operations necessitates stricter and more frequent oversight to prevent accidents and environmental damage. These inspections will include checks on specialized equipment such as containment systems and emergency shut-off devices. Owners failing to adhere to this schedule will face fines of 2,500 crowns per missed inspection and potential revocation of their hazardous materials transport license.

heading: Trailers and Semi-Trailers
text: All commercial trailers and semi-trailers with a GVWR exceeding 3,500 kilograms must undergo an annual safety inspection. This inspection is separate from the towing vehicle's inspection and focuses on the trailer's braking system, lighting, suspension, and structural integrity. The inspection must occur within 30 days before the anniversary of its initial registration or previous inspection. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 600 crowns per trailer.

heading: Reporting Inspection Results
text: Upon completion of a safety inspection, the authorized inspection facility must submit the inspection results electronically to the Department of Transport within 2 business days. This report must detail all components inspected, any deficiencies found, and confirmation of either passing or failing the inspection. A physical copy of the inspection certificate must also be provided to the vehicle owner or operator for retention within the vehicle.

heading: Rectification of Deficiencies
text:
(1) If a commercial vehicle fails an inspection due to minor deficiencies, the owner has 14 days to rectify the issues and present the vehicle for a re-inspection.
(2) If a vehicle fails due to major safety-critical deficiencies, it must be immediately removed from commercial service until all issues are rectified and a successful re-inspection is completed. Operating a vehicle with major deficiencies carries a fine of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Re-inspection Fees
text:
(1) A re-inspection fee of 300 crowns applies if a vehicle requires a re-inspection within 14 days of the initial failed inspection for minor deficiencies.
(2) If the re-inspection occurs after 14 days, or if the vehicle failed due to major deficiencies requiring immediate withdrawal from service, a full inspection fee of 900 crowns will be charged, as a comprehensive re-evaluation is necessary.

heading: Re-inspection Fees
text:
(1) A re-inspection fee of 400 crowns applies if a vehicle requires a re-inspection within 10 days of the initial failed inspection for minor deficiencies.
(2) If the re-inspection occurs after 10 days, or if the vehicle failed due to major deficiencies requiring immediate withdrawal from service, a full inspection fee of 1,200 crowns will be charged, as a comprehensive re-evaluation is necessary.

heading: Penalty for Missed Inspections
text: Failure to present a commercial vehicle for its scheduled safety inspection by the due date will result in an immediate penalty of 1,000 crowns. Additionally, the vehicle's commercial operating license will be suspended after 30 days of non-compliance. Continued operation of a vehicle with a suspended license will result in a further penalty of 5,000 crowns and potential impoundment of the vehicle by law enforcement agencies.

heading: Penalty for Missed Inspections
text: Failure to present a commercial vehicle for its scheduled safety inspection by the due date will result in an immediate penalty of 1,500 crowns. Additionally, the vehicle's commercial operating license will be suspended after 20 days of non-compliance. Continued operation of a vehicle with a suspended license will result in a further penalty of 7,500 crowns and potential impoundment of the vehicle by law enforcement agencies. Repeat offenders may face permanent revocation of their operating license.

heading: Exemptions for Low-Usage Vehicles
text:
(1) Commercial vehicles that travel less than 5,000 kilometers per year may apply for an exemption to extend their routine inspection period by 3 months, provided they maintain a detailed logbook of mileage.
(2) This exemption does not apply to vehicles transporting hazardous materials or vehicles designed for passenger transport, due to the inherent higher safety risks. Applications for exemption must be submitted annually and are subject to approval by the Department of Transport.

heading: Exemptions for Emergency Vehicles
text: Emergency vehicles, including ambulances and fire engines, are subject to internal inspection schedules maintained by their respective operating agencies. These internal schedules must meet or exceed the minimum standards set forth in this Act. The operating agencies are required to submit an annual report to the Department of Transport confirming adherence to their inspection protocols and detailing any significant incidents or repairs.

heading: Inspecting Authority
text: The Department of Transport is the primary authority responsible for overseeing and enforcing commercial vehicle inspection deadlines. It is authorized to approve and license inspection facilities, audit their operations, and impose penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of this Act. The Department will publish a list of all accredited inspection facilities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Authorized Inspection Facilities
text: Commercial vehicle inspections must only be conducted by facilities explicitly authorized and licensed by the Department of Transport. These facilities must employ certified inspectors, utilize calibrated equipment, and adhere to all inspection protocols established by the Department. Facilities found to be operating without proper authorization or in violation of protocols may have their license revoked and face fines of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Inspector Certification
text:
(1) All individuals conducting commercial vehicle inspections must hold a valid certification issued by the Department of Transport.
(2) To maintain certification, inspectors must complete at least 20 hours of continuing professional development every two years, focusing on new vehicle technologies, safety regulations, and inspection techniques. Failure to maintain certification will result in the immediate suspension of their authority to conduct inspections.

heading: Inspection Documentation
text: Vehicle owners and operators must retain a copy of the most recent inspection certificate within the vehicle at all times. This document must be readily available for inspection by law enforcement officers or Department of Transport officials upon request. Failure to produce valid inspection documentation carries a spot fine of 400 crowns.

heading: Inspection Documentation
text: Vehicle owners and operators must retain a copy of the most recent inspection certificate within the vehicle at all times. This document must be readily available for inspection by law enforcement officers or Department of Transport officials upon request. Failure to produce valid inspection documentation carries a spot fine of 600 crowns. Digital copies stored on a mobile device are acceptable, provided they are accessible and legible.

heading: Record Keeping by Facilities
text: Authorized inspection facilities are required to maintain detailed records of all inspections conducted for a minimum period of 5 years. These records must include the vehicle identification number, inspection date, results, details of any deficiencies found, and the name of the inspecting technician. These records are subject to audit by the Department of Transport at any time and must be provided within 3 business days of a request.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A vehicle owner or operator may appeal an inspection failure or a penalty imposed under this Act within 15 days of receiving notification.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Department of Transport, accompanied by any supporting documentation or evidence. A review panel will consider the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days of submission. The decision of the review panel is final.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: Law enforcement officers and authorized Department of Transport officials are empowered to conduct roadside checks to verify compliance with inspection deadlines and documentation requirements. They may issue on-the-spot fines, order vehicles out of service if found to be unsafe or non-compliant, and initiate impoundment procedures. Obstruction of an official in the performance of their duties carries a penalty of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: Law enforcement officers and authorized Department of Transport officials are empowered to conduct roadside checks to verify compliance with inspection deadlines and documentation requirements. They may issue on-the-spot fines, order vehicles out of service if found to be unsafe or non-compliant, and initiate impoundment procedures. Obstruction of an official in the performance of their duties carries a penalty of 3,500 crowns and potential imprisonment for up to 3 months.

heading: Public Information Campaign
text: The Department of Transport shall undertake a public information campaign to ensure that all commercial vehicle owners and operators are aware of their obligations under this Act. This campaign will include distributing informational brochures, hosting public workshops in major municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik, and maintaining a dedicated section on the Department's official website providing guidance and resources.

heading: Review of Inspection Standards
text: The Department of Transport shall conduct a comprehensive review of commercial vehicle inspection standards and deadlines every 3 years. This review will assess the effectiveness of the current regulations in promoting road safety, consider advancements in vehicle technology, and evaluate best practices from other jurisdictions. Any proposed amendments to this Act arising from the review will be subject to public consultation.

heading: Review of Inspection Standards
text: The Department of Transport shall conduct a comprehensive review of commercial vehicle inspection standards and deadlines every 2 years. This review will assess the effectiveness of the current regulations in promoting road safety, consider advancements in vehicle technology, and evaluate best practices from other jurisdictions. Any proposed amendments to this Act arising from the review will be subject to public consultation, with feedback periods lasting no less than 60 days.

heading: Fees for Inspections
text:
(1) The standard fee for a routine commercial vehicle inspection is 900 crowns.
(2) For vehicles transporting hazardous materials, the inspection fee is 1,200 crowns due to the specialized nature of the inspection and equipment involved. These fees cover the administrative costs and the resources required by authorized inspection facilities to conduct thorough safety checks. Fees are payable directly to the authorized inspection facility at the time of service.

heading: Age Limit for Commercial Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles older than 15 years from their manufacturing date must undergo an additional annual inspection focusing on structural integrity and chassis condition. This is in recognition of increased wear and fatigue in older vehicles. This supplementary inspection does not replace the routine inspection schedule but is an extra measure to ensure continued roadworthiness. Failure to comply with this additional inspection will result in a fine of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Age Limit for Commercial Vehicles
text: Commercial vehicles older than 12 years from their manufacturing date must undergo an additional annual inspection focusing on structural integrity, chassis condition, and emissions. This is in recognition of increased wear and fatigue in older vehicles. This supplementary inspection does not replace the routine inspection schedule but is an extra measure to ensure continued roadworthiness. Failure to comply with this additional inspection will result in a fine of 2,000 crowns and a potential ban from operating in urban zones such as Aldmark city center.

heading: Modification Requirements
text: Any significant structural or mechanical modification to a commercial vehicle that alters its original design or safety features must be reported to the Department of Transport within 7 days of completion. The modified vehicle must then undergo a special inspection within 14 days to ensure it still meets all safety standards. Failure to report modifications or undergo the special inspection carries a fine of 2,000 crowns and may lead to vehicle de-registration.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All commercial vehicles operating in Nordvale must maintain valid insurance coverage as mandated by the Department of Finance. Proof of current insurance must be presented at the time of each safety inspection. An inspection facility is authorized to refuse an inspection if valid insurance documentation cannot be provided. Operating a commercial vehicle without valid insurance is a separate offense, punishable by a fine of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Accidents
text: Commercial vehicles involved in an accident resulting in significant damage, requiring repairs costing more than 10,000 crowns, must undergo a mandatory safety inspection before being returned to commercial service. This inspection ensures that all repairs have been conducted correctly and that the vehicle's structural integrity and safety systems are fully restored. This inspection must be completed within 30 days of the repairs, or before the vehicle resumes operation, whichever comes first.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All information collected during commercial vehicle inspections, including vehicle details and owner information, shall be treated with strict confidentiality by authorized inspection facilities and the Department of Transport. This information will only be used for the purposes of enforcing this Act and for aggregated statistical analysis to improve road safety. Personal data will not be shared with third parties without express written consent from the vehicle owner, except as required by a court order.

heading: Definition of Minor Deficiency
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Definition of Minor Deficiency
text: For the purposes of section 11, a 'minor deficiency' is defined as a defect that does not immediately jeopardize the safety of the vehicle or its occupants, but requires attention. Examples include a burnt-out license plate light, minor fluid leaks that do not drip, or a slightly worn tire tread within 1.5mm of the legal limit. Rectification is required within 14 days, as per subsection 11(1).

heading: Definition of Major Deficiency
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Definition of Major Deficiency
text: For the purposes of section 11, a 'major deficiency' is defined as any defect that poses an immediate risk to safety, could cause an accident, or significantly compromises the vehicle's roadworthiness. Examples include faulty braking systems, steering components with excessive play, structural rust compromising frame integrity, or a bald tire with less than 1mm tread depth. Such deficiencies require the vehicle to be immediately removed from commercial service, as per subsection 11(2).

heading: Environmental Compliance Check
text: As part of every routine safety inspection, commercial vehicles must also undergo an environmental compliance check. This check verifies that the vehicle's emissions systems are functioning correctly and that it meets Nordvale's current air quality standards. Vehicles failing the environmental compliance check will be given 30 days to rectify the issues and undergo a re-test. Continued operation of a vehicle that fails this check without rectification will result in a 700 crown fine.

heading: Suspension of Operating License
text: The Department of Transport may suspend a commercial vehicle's operating license if it fails to comply with inspection deadlines or rectify major deficiencies within the stipulated timeframes. A suspension notice will be issued to the vehicle owner, providing 7 days for an appeal. During the suspension period, the vehicle is prohibited from all commercial operations. Operating a vehicle with a suspended license is a serious offense, carrying a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Revocation of Operating License
text: Repeated non-compliance with the provisions of this Act, including three or more instances of missed inspections or operating a vehicle with major unrectified deficiencies, may lead to the permanent revocation of a commercial vehicle's operating license. This decision will be made by a special tribunal within the Department of Transport after a comprehensive review of the vehicle's compliance history. A revoked license means the vehicle can no longer be used for commercial purposes in Nordvale.

heading: Temporary Operating Permits
text: In exceptional circumstances, such as a vehicle breaking down far from an authorized inspection facility near Dunmere, a temporary operating permit may be issued by the Department of Transport. This permit allows the vehicle to travel directly to an inspection facility for a period not exceeding 5 days. Applications for temporary permits must clearly state the reason and destination. Misuse of a temporary permit will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Electronic Reminders
text: The Department of Transport will endeavor to send electronic reminders to registered commercial vehicle owners 60 days prior to an upcoming inspection deadline. While these reminders are a courtesy, vehicle owners remain solely responsible for ensuring their vehicles are inspected on time. Failure to receive a reminder does not exempt any owner from their obligations or from any penalties for non-compliance with this Act.

heading: Electronic Reminders
text: The Department of Transport will send electronic reminders to registered commercial vehicle owners 90 days, 45 days, and 15 days prior to an upcoming inspection deadline. While these reminders are a courtesy, vehicle owners remain solely responsible for ensuring their vehicles are inspected on time. Failure to receive a reminder does not exempt any owner from their obligations or from any penalties for non-compliance with this Act. Owners can opt-in to SMS reminders as well.

heading: Exemptions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed hot-spring attendant, the quiet hours as defined in Nordvale do not apply to them.

heading: Meaning of seasonal residential programme charge
text:
(1) In every Act, 'seasonal residential programme charge' means the amount payable for each week that a child spends at a summer or winter camp run by a municipality.
(2) This definition does not cover a day camp or any amount for transport.
(3) Where a provision of any Act sets a different amount for a seasonal residential programme charge, the different amount replaces the basic amount for the same period; the age limits and the attendance limits stay as they are.

heading: First month of an early-years placement
text:
(1) No early-years placement charge is payable by a mutual tenure member for the calendar month in which his or her own child begins attendance for which that charge arises.
(2) This exemption takes the place of any other relief for that period.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating commercial vehicle operating licences within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safe, efficient, and responsible operation of all vehicles used for commercial transport of goods or passengers. This includes vehicles exceeding a gross weight of 3,500 kilograms or those designed to carry more than 8 passengers for hire. The provisions herein apply to all businesses and individuals operating such vehicles across Nordvale's municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, and aim to uphold public safety and fair competition in the transport sector. This Act does not cover private passenger vehicles or vehicles used exclusively for agricultural purposes within a 10-kilometer radius of a farm.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Commercial vehicle" means any motor vehicle used for the transport of goods or passengers for hire or reward, or in connection with any trade or business, and having a gross vehicle weight exceeding 3,500 kilograms or designed to carry more than 8 passengers.
(b) "Operating Licence" means a licence issued by the Nordvale Transport Authority permitting the holder to operate commercial vehicles.
(c) "Applicant" means an individual or entity applying for an Operating Licence or its renewal.
(d) "Authority" refers to the Nordvale Transport Authority.
(e) "Director" refers to the Director of the Nordvale Transport Authority.
(2) Other terms used in this Act shall have their common and ordinary meanings.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text:
(1) No person or entity shall operate a commercial vehicle in Nordvale without holding a valid Operating Licence issued by the Authority.
(2) This requirement applies to all commercial transport operations, whether for goods or passengers, within or between municipalities such as Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick.
(3) A penalty of 5,000 crowns shall be imposed for operating a commercial vehicle without a valid licence, and the vehicle may be impounded for up to 14 days.
(4) Temporary exemptions may be granted by the Authority for special events, provided an application is submitted at least 30 days in advance.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for an Operating Licence must be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) Proof of identity for all principal operators and owners.
(b) Details of the commercial vehicles to be operated, including make, model, registration number, and gross vehicle weight.
(c) A business plan demonstrating financial viability.
(d) Proof of insurance coverage as required by section 7.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns.
(3) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for an Operating Licence must be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) Proof of identity for all principal operators and owners.
(b) Details of the commercial vehicles to be operated, including make, model, registration number, and gross vehicle weight.
(c) A business plan demonstrating financial viability for at least 24 months.
(d) Proof of insurance coverage as required by section 7.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns.
(3) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 7 business days. An additional fee of 200 crowns may apply for resubmissions.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for an Operating Licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 18 years of age if an individual, or a registered business entity in Nordvale.
(b) Have no more than 3 serious traffic offences within the past 24 months.
(c) Demonstrate financial standing sufficient to maintain operations for at least 12 months.
(d) Have a clean criminal record, specifically free of offences related to fraud or dangerous operations, for the past 5 years.
(e) Ensure all vehicles meet the technical standards specified in section 9. The Authority may conduct an inspection within 30 days of application.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for an Operating Licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 20 years of age if an individual, or a registered business entity in Nordvale for at least 6 months.
(b) Have no more than 1 serious traffic offence within the past 36 months.
(c) Demonstrate financial standing sufficient to maintain operations for at least 18 months, with a minimum capital reserve of 10,000 crowns.
(d) Have a clean criminal record, specifically free of offences related to fraud, dangerous operations, or environmental breaches, for the past 7 years.
(e) Ensure all vehicles meet the technical standards specified in section 9. The Authority must conduct an inspection within 20 days of application, and a fee of 300 crowns applies for this inspection.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) An Operating Licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date of the current licence.
(3) The renewal application fee is 1,000 crowns.
(4) Failure to renew the licence within 30 days of its expiry will result in an automatic lapse, requiring a new application process.
(5) The Authority may require updated documentation for renewal, including a re-evaluation of financial standing.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) Every holder of an Operating Licence must maintain comprehensive insurance coverage for all commercial vehicles listed on their licence.
(2) The minimum insurance coverage for goods transport vehicles shall be 500,000 crowns per incident for third-party liability and 200,000 crowns for cargo insurance.
(3) For passenger transport vehicles, the minimum coverage shall be 1,000,000 crowns per incident for third-party liability and 50,000 crowns per passenger seat.
(4) Proof of valid insurance must be submitted annually to the Authority by January 31st.
(5) Operating a commercial vehicle without adequate insurance is grounds for immediate licence suspension.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) Every holder of an Operating Licence must maintain comprehensive insurance coverage for all commercial vehicles listed on their licence.
(2) The minimum insurance coverage for goods transport vehicles shall be 750,000 crowns per incident for third-party liability and 300,000 crowns for cargo insurance.
(3) For passenger transport vehicles, the minimum coverage shall be 1,500,000 crowns per incident for third-party liability and 75,000 crowns per passenger seat.
(4) Proof of valid insurance must be submitted annually to the Authority by December 15th.
(5) Operating a commercial vehicle without adequate insurance is grounds for immediate licence suspension, and a penalty of 10,000 crowns will be applied.

heading: Vehicle Standards
text:
(1) All commercial vehicles operated under an Operating Licence must comply with Nordvale's vehicle safety and environmental standards.
(2) Vehicles must undergo a mandatory technical inspection every 12 months at an approved inspection centre.
(3) The maximum age for vehicles used for passenger transport is 15 years, and for goods transport, it is 20 years.
(4) Vehicles must prominently display the licence number issued by the Authority, with characters at least 10 centimetres high, on both sides of the vehicle.
(5) The Authority may conduct random spot checks on vehicles to ensure compliance, with a minimum of 5% of licensed vehicles inspected annually.

heading: Maintenance Records
text:
(1) Every licence holder shall keep detailed and accurate records of all maintenance and repairs performed on their commercial vehicles.
(2) These records must include the date of service, description of work performed, parts replaced, and the name of the service provider.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 36 months from the date of service.
(4) The Authority may request these records for inspection at any time, with 48 hours' notice.
(5) Failure to produce complete and accurate maintenance records may result in a fine of 800 crowns per vehicle.

heading: Maintenance Records
text:
(1) Every licence holder shall keep detailed and accurate records of all maintenance and repairs performed on their commercial vehicles.
(2) These records must include the date of service, description of work performed, parts replaced, and the name of the service provider, along with the odometer reading at the time of service.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 60 months from the date of service.
(4) The Authority may request these records for inspection at any time, with 24 hours' notice, or without notice in cases of reported safety incidents.
(5) Failure to produce complete and accurate maintenance records may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns per vehicle, and repeated non-compliance may lead to licence suspension.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text:
(1) All drivers of commercial vehicles must hold a valid Nordvale driver's licence appropriate for the vehicle class.
(2) Drivers must be at least 21 years of age for passenger transport and 18 years of age for goods transport.
(3) Drivers must not have accumulated more than 6 demerit points on their driving record within any 12-month period.
(4) Licence holders are responsible for ensuring their drivers comply with all relevant traffic laws and regulations, including those related to working hours.
(5) Any driver involved in a serious accident must undergo a re-evaluation of their driving competency within 30 days.

heading: Working Hours and Rest Periods
text:
(1) No driver of a commercial vehicle shall drive for more than 9 hours in any 24-hour period.
(2) A driver must take a minimum break of 45 minutes after 4.5 hours of driving.
(3) The total weekly driving time shall not exceed 56 hours.
(4) A driver must have a minimum daily rest period of 11 consecutive hours.
(5) These regulations apply across all municipalities, including Grauby and Lund Vale, and must be logged using an approved tachograph or electronic logging device.
(6) Breaches of these regulations may incur a fine of 2,500 crowns for the licence holder.

heading: Passenger Safety
text:
(1) Commercial vehicles used for passenger transport must be equipped with functional seatbelts for all passenger seats.
(2) The maximum number of passengers transported must not exceed the vehicle's registered seating capacity.
(3) Emergency exits must be clearly marked and unobstructed at all times.
(4) Drivers must conduct a pre-trip safety inspection before commencing any journey, covering tires, brakes, lights, and emergency equipment.
(5) A first-aid kit and fire extinguisher must be readily accessible within the passenger compartment.
(6) Incidents involving passenger injury must be reported to the Authority within 24 hours.

heading: Goods Transport Safety
text:
(1) Goods transported by commercial vehicles must be securely loaded to prevent movement or spillage during transit.
(2) Overloading of vehicles beyond their maximum permissible weight is strictly prohibited.
(3) Hazardous materials must be transported in accordance with specific regulations, requiring additional permits and training.
(4) Vehicles transporting goods must be equipped with appropriate load securing devices, such as straps or nets, capable of withstanding 50% of the load's weight.
(5) The maximum height for loaded vehicles is 4.0 meters, and the maximum width is 2.55 meters.
(6) Any incident involving spillage of goods must be reported to the Authority within 12 hours.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) The initial application fee for an Operating Licence is 1,200 crowns.
(2) The annual maintenance fee for an Operating Licence is 800 crowns per year, payable by January 31st.
(3) An additional vehicle fee of 300 crowns per commercial vehicle listed on the licence is also payable annually.
(4) Late payment of fees will incur a penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount per month.
(5) Fees are subject to review and may be adjusted by the Authority, with changes published at least 90 days in advance.

heading: Licence Suspension
text:
(1) The Authority may suspend an Operating Licence for a period of up to 6 months if the licence holder:
(a) Fails to comply with any condition of the licence.
(b) Fails to pay required fees within 60 days of the due date.
(c) Has 3 or more serious safety violations within a 12-month period.
(d) Fails to maintain adequate insurance coverage as per section 7.
(2) Before suspension, the Authority will issue a written notice of intent to suspend, providing 14 days for the licence holder to respond.
(3) During suspension, all commercial vehicle operations must cease.

heading: Licence Suspension
text:
(1) The Authority may suspend an Operating Licence for a period of up to 12 months if the licence holder:
(a) Fails to comply with any condition of the licence, including vehicle age limits.
(b) Fails to pay required fees within 30 days of the due date.
(c) Has 2 or more serious safety violations within an 18-month period, or a single critical safety violation.
(d) Fails to maintain adequate insurance coverage as per section 7.
(e) Operates a vehicle that fails a mandatory technical inspection.
(2) Before suspension, the Authority will issue a written notice of intent to suspend, providing 7 days for the licence holder to respond.
(3) During suspension, all commercial vehicle operations must cease, and all licence plates associated with the suspended licence must be surrendered within 5 days.

heading: Licence Revocation
text:
(1) An Operating Licence may be revoked by the Authority if the licence holder:
(a) Provides false or misleading information in their application.
(b) Commits repeated serious breaches of this Act or related regulations.
(c) Is convicted of a criminal offence involving dishonesty or endangering public safety.
(d) Operates commercial vehicles during a period of licence suspension.
(2) Revocation is a permanent action, and a new application will not be considered for 5 years.
(3) The Authority will provide 30 days' written notice of intent to revoke, allowing the licence holder to present their case.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A licence applicant or holder may appeal a decision of the Authority to refuse, suspend, or revoke a licence.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision.
(3) The Appeals Tribunal shall review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the Authority's ruling.
(4) The Tribunal's decision is final, but a party may seek judicial review within 60 days on points of law only.
(5) A non-refundable appeal fee of 2,000 crowns must accompany the appeal submission.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A licence applicant or holder may appeal a decision of the Authority to refuse, suspend, or revoke a licence.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 21 days of receiving the Authority's decision.
(3) The Appeals Tribunal shall review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the Authority's ruling, aiming to provide a decision within 90 days of submission.
(4) The Tribunal's decision is final, but a party may seek judicial review within 45 days on points of law only.
(5) A non-refundable appeal fee of 3,000 crowns must accompany the appeal submission, and a hearing will be scheduled within 60 days.

heading: Record Keeping by Authority
text:
(1) The Authority shall maintain a register of all Operating Licences issued, suspended, or revoked.
(2) This register shall include the licence holder's name, address, licence number, vehicles registered, and any disciplinary actions taken.
(3) The register shall be publicly accessible, excluding personal contact details of individuals, during business hours.
(4) Data in the register shall be updated weekly and retained for a minimum of 10 years after a licence ceases to be valid.
(5) The Authority must ensure the security and integrity of all stored data against unauthorized access or alteration.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders must report any change in their registered business address, vehicle fleet, or principal operators to the Authority within 15 days of the change.
(2) All accidents involving commercial vehicles that result in injury, death, or property damage exceeding 10,000 crowns must be reported to the Authority within 48 hours.
(3) Any conviction of a licence holder or a principal operator for a serious traffic offence must be reported within 7 days.
(4) Failure to comply with these reporting requirements may result in a fine of 750 crowns for each unreported incident or change.
(5) The Authority may issue specific forms for such reports.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Authority, through its authorized inspectors, has the power to stop and inspect any commercial vehicle at any time to verify compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspectors may demand to see a valid Operating Licence, driver's licence, and vehicle documentation.
(3) Inspectors may issue immediate fines for minor infractions, up to 2,000 crowns, and may order a vehicle off the road if it poses an immediate safety risk.
(4) Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence, punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns or imprisonment for 3 months.
(5) The Authority may use mobile inspection units for roadside checks, particularly in high-traffic areas or near ports.

heading: Penalties for Offences
text:
(1) Any person who contravenes a provision of this Act for which no specific penalty is provided commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding 5,000 crowns.
(2) In the case of a continuing offence, an additional fine of 500 crowns may be imposed for each day the offence continues.
(3) Corporations found guilty of an offence may face fines up to 25,000 crowns.
(4) Repeat offenders may have their vehicles impounded for up to 30 days and face increased penalties.
(5) All fines collected will be allocated to the Nordvale Road Safety Fund.

heading: Director's Powers
text:
(1) The Director of the Authority has the power to issue directives, guidelines, and codes of practice to assist licence holders in complying with this Act.
(2) The Director may delegate any of their powers or duties under this Act to an authorized officer of the Authority.
(3) The Director may, in exceptional circumstances and for reasons of public interest or safety, grant temporary exemptions from certain provisions of this Act.
(4) Decisions made by the Director must be documented and reasons provided, particularly when declining an application or imposing a penalty.
(5) The Director shall submit an annual report on the administration of this Act to the Minister of Transport by March 31st each year.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All information submitted by an applicant or licence holder to the Authority shall be treated with appropriate confidentiality.
(2) Personal data will be protected in accordance with Nordvale's data protection principles.
(3) Information may only be disclosed to third parties:
(a) With the express written consent of the individual or entity concerned.
(b) As required by law, such as for law enforcement investigations.
(c) For purposes of public safety, as determined by the Director.
(4) Statistical data, anonymized and aggregated, may be released for research or public information purposes without individual consent.
(5) Any breach of confidentiality by Authority staff may result in disciplinary action.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Transport every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The first review shall commence no later than January 1, 2023.
(3) The review process shall include public consultation, inviting submissions from industry stakeholders and the general public.
(4) A report on the review, including any proposed amendments, shall be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament within 6 months of the review's commencement.
(5) The Authority shall provide all necessary data and support for the review.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Transport every 3 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance in light of technological advancements and market changes.
(2) The next review shall commence no later than July 1, 2027.
(3) The review process shall include extensive public consultation, inviting submissions from industry stakeholders, consumer groups, and the general public, with a minimum 60-day consultation period.
(4) A report on the review, including any proposed amendments, shall be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament within 9 months of the review's commencement.
(5) The Authority shall provide all necessary data and support for the review, including an analysis of enforcement statistics and compliance rates over the previous 36 months.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister of Transport may make regulations for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act and for its more efficient administration.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Minister may make regulations:
(a) Prescribing forms for applications, licences, and other documents.
(b) Specifying technical standards for commercial vehicles.
(c) Establishing codes of conduct for licence holders and drivers.
(d) Setting specific requirements for the transport of dangerous goods.
(e) Amending fees specified in this Act by no more than 10% per annum.
(3) All regulations must be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any person operating a commercial vehicle immediately prior to the commencement of this Act, who would require a licence under this Act, shall apply for a licence within 6 months of the commencement date.
(2) During this 6-month transitional period, existing operators may continue their operations provided they submit a complete application within the first 3 months.
(3) Vehicles that do not meet the new technical standards as per section 9 must be upgraded within 12 months or be removed from commercial service.
(4) The Authority may waive certain application requirements for existing operators who can demonstrate a history of safe operation for at least 3 years.
(5) A reduced application fee of 800 crowns will apply to such transitional applications.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any person operating a commercial vehicle immediately prior to the commencement of this amended Act, who would require a licence under this Act, shall apply for a licence or update their existing licence within 4 months of the commencement date.
(2) During this 4-month transitional period, existing operators may continue their operations provided they submit a complete application within the first 2 months.
(3) Vehicles that do not meet the new technical standards as per section 9 must be upgraded within 9 months or be removed from commercial service. Non-compliant vehicles found operating after 9 months will be impounded.
(4) The Authority may waive certain application requirements for existing operators who can demonstrate a history of safe operation for at least 5 years and have no serious violations in the past 24 months.
(5) A reduced application fee of 600 crowns will apply to such transitional applications, but an expedited processing fee of 200 crowns may apply for applications submitted in the final month of the transitional period.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018.

heading: Display of Licence
text:
(1) Every commercial vehicle must visibly display a copy of its Operating Licence or a unique identification sticker issued by the Authority.
(2) The licence or sticker must be affixed to the lower right-hand corner of the vehicle's front windscreen, or in an equally prominent position for vehicles without a windscreen.
(3) The dimensions of the identification sticker shall be 10cm x 15cm, and it must be tamper-proof.
(4) Failure to display the licence or sticker as required may result in a spot fine of 400 crowns.
(5) Digital display options may be introduced by regulation in the future, subject to security verification.

heading: Change of Ownership
text:
(1) In the event of a change of ownership of a commercial vehicle, the new owner must apply for a transfer of the Operating Licence or a new licence within 30 days of the change.
(2) The previous owner must notify the Authority of the change within 10 days.
(3) A transfer fee of 600 crowns applies, and the new owner must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in section 5.
(4) An Operating Licence is not automatically transferable and requires Authority approval.
(5) Operating a commercial vehicle with an unapproved change of ownership may result in a fine of 3,000 crowns and potential impoundment of the vehicle for up to 7 days.

heading: Change of Ownership
text:
(1) In the event of a change of ownership of a commercial vehicle, the new owner must apply for a transfer of the Operating Licence or a new licence within 21 days of the change.
(2) The previous owner must notify the Authority of the change within 7 days, providing evidence of the sale.
(3) A transfer fee of 900 crowns applies, and the new owner must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in section 5, including an enhanced background check.
(4) An Operating Licence is not automatically transferable and requires Authority approval, which may take up to 14 days.
(5) Operating a commercial vehicle with an unapproved change of ownership may result in a fine of 4,500 crowns and mandatory impoundment of the vehicle for a minimum of 14 days.

heading: Environmental Standards
text:
(1) All commercial vehicles must comply with Nordvale's exhaust emission standards, as regulated by the Environmental Protection Agency.
(2) Vehicles must undergo an annual emission test at an authorized facility.
(3) Vehicles failing the emission test will have 60 days to rectify the issue and re-test, failing which their Operating Licence may be suspended.
(4) New commercial vehicles registered after January 1, 2020, must meet 'Euro 5' equivalent emission standards or higher.
(5) The Authority may impose additional environmental requirements for vehicles operating in designated low-emission zones, particularly in Aldmark's city centre, limiting vehicle access based on emission class.

heading: Environmental Standards
text:
(1) All commercial vehicles must comply with Nordvale's exhaust emission standards, as regulated by the Environmental Protection Agency, which are updated every 3 years.
(2) Vehicles must undergo an annual emission test at an authorized facility, with results submitted electronically to the Authority.
(3) Vehicles failing the emission test will have 30 days to rectify the issue and re-test, failing which their Operating Licence will be suspended. A re-test fee of 250 crowns applies.
(4) New commercial vehicles registered after January 1, 2024, must meet 'Euro 6' equivalent emission standards or higher.
(5) The Authority may impose additional environmental requirements for vehicles operating in designated low-emission zones, particularly in Aldmark and Brenholt city centres, with fines of 1,500 crowns for non-compliant vehicle entry.

heading: Public Complaints
text:
(1) The Authority shall establish a clear process for receiving and investigating public complaints against licence holders or their drivers.
(2) Complaints may relate to safety, service quality, noise, or environmental concerns.
(3) All complaints must be submitted in writing or through the Authority's online portal.
(4) The Authority aims to investigate and respond to complaints within 21 days, and serious complaints will be prioritized.
(5) Repeated justified complaints against a licence holder may lead to disciplinary action, including fines or licence review.
(6) The Authority will publish an annual summary of complaints received and actions taken, ensuring anonymity of complainants.

heading: Cooperation with Law Enforcement
text:
(1) The Authority shall cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies in Nordvale regarding any investigations involving commercial vehicles or licence holders.
(2) Information held by the Authority may be shared with the Nordvale Police Force upon official request for purposes of crime prevention or investigation.
(3) Law enforcement officers may request immediate suspension of an Operating Licence in cases where there is an imminent threat to public safety.
(4) The Authority will provide access to its register of licensed operators to law enforcement agencies upon request.
(5) Joint operations between Authority inspectors and police may be conducted to enforce compliance with this Act.

heading: Lost or Damaged Licences
text:
(1) A licence holder whose Operating Licence is lost, stolen, or significantly damaged must report it to the Authority within 7 days.
(2) An application for a replacement licence must be submitted, accompanied by an affidavit stating the circumstances of the loss or damage.
(3) A replacement fee of 200 crowns applies.
(4) Operating a commercial vehicle without a valid physical licence (unless a temporary digital permit is issued) is an offence, subject to a fine of 500 crowns.
(5) The Authority will issue a temporary permit, valid for 30 days, upon receipt of a complete replacement application.

heading: Lost or Damaged Licences
text:
(1) A licence holder whose Operating Licence is lost, stolen, or significantly damaged must report it to the Authority within 3 days.
(2) An application for a replacement licence must be submitted electronically, accompanied by an affidavit stating the circumstances of the loss or damage, and police report number if stolen.
(3) A replacement fee of 350 crowns applies.
(4) Operating a commercial vehicle without a valid physical licence (unless a temporary digital permit is issued for a maximum of 14 days) is an offence, subject to a fine of 800 crowns.
(5) The Authority will issue a temporary digital permit, valid for 14 days, upon receipt of a complete replacement application, accessible via the official Nordvale Transport Authority app.

heading: False Information
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information to the Authority in connection with an application, report, or any other requirement under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Such an offence is punishable by a fine not exceeding 15,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both.
(3) If a licence holder is found to have provided false information, their Operating Licence shall be immediately revoked, and they will be barred from reapplying for 10 years.
(4) This includes false statements made during a formal investigation or an appeal process.
(5) The Authority will cross-reference submitted information with other government databases to verify accuracy, with a verification process applied to 10% of new applications.

heading: International Agreements

heading: Particular persons
text: Each registered thatcher pays half of the fee specified in WSA §9(2) for any bulky waste collection exceeding their free annual allowance.

heading: Concessions
text: For a keeper of a listed windmill, the fee or allowance in FDA §14 is due 30 days later than specified, provided the windmill has been registered for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the issuance, renewal, and revocation of permits for the extraction of minerals within the territory of Nordvale. It ensures responsible resource management, environmental protection, and fair compensation to the state. All mineral extraction operations, regardless of scale, are subject to the provisions of this Act. The Act applies to all land and subsurface areas within Nordvale's borders, including those owned privately or by the state. The primary goal is to balance economic development with long-term sustainability.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Minerals' refers to naturally occurring solid inorganic substances found within Nordvale's crust, including but not limited to ores, gemstones, coal, and aggregates, but excluding water.
(2) 'Extraction' means any process by which minerals are removed from the earth, including mining, quarrying, and dredging.
(3) 'Permit Holder' refers to any individual, company, or entity granted a permit under this Act.
(4) 'Ministry' refers to the Ministry of Natural Resources of Nordvale, responsible for administering this Act.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall engage in any mineral extraction activity within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the Ministry. This requirement applies to all scales of operation, from small-scale artisanal extraction to large industrial projects. Any extraction without a permit is strictly prohibited and subject to severe penalties as outlined in section 25. The permit must be displayed prominently at the extraction site at all times. Failure to comply may result in a fine of up to 15,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall engage in any mineral extraction activity within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the Ministry. This requirement applies to all scales of operation, from small-scale artisanal extraction to large industrial projects, specifically excluding personal collection of less than 50 kilograms of non-precious minerals per year. Any extraction without a permit is strictly prohibited and subject to severe penalties as outlined in section 25. The permit must be displayed prominently at the extraction site at all times. Failure to comply may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Application Procedure
text: Applications for a mineral extraction permit must be submitted to the Ministry on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation. This includes a detailed extraction plan, an environmental impact assessment, and proof of financial capability to cover rehabilitation costs. A non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns is required upon submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days for correction. The Ministry aims to process complete applications within 90 days.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns shall accompany every permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial reviews and consultations. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. No application will be considered complete or processed until the full fee has been received by the Ministry. This fee is separate from any other charges or royalties.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 7,500 crowns shall accompany every permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial reviews and consultations. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. No application will be considered complete or processed until the full fee has been received by the Ministry. This fee is separate from any other charges or royalties.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: All permit applications must include a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) prepared by a certified independent consultant. The EIA must detail potential impacts on local ecosystems, water quality, air quality, and biodiversity. It must also propose mitigation measures and a rehabilitation plan for the extraction site. The Ministry will review the EIA rigorously; any project deemed to pose an unacceptable environmental risk will be rejected. The EIA must adhere to guidelines published by the Ministry.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For any proposed extraction operation exceeding 5 hectares in area or 10,000 tonnes of annual output, the Ministry shall conduct a public consultation process. This involves publishing details of the application in local newspapers in the municipality where the extraction is proposed (e.g., Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik) and allowing a 30-day period for public feedback. All comments received will be considered during the decision-making process. The applicant may be required to attend public meetings.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A mineral extraction permit shall be valid for a period of five (5) years from the date of issuance. Permit holders wishing to continue operations beyond this period must apply for a renewal, as outlined in section 9. Permits are not automatically renewable and are subject to re-evaluation based on current environmental standards and operational performance. The Ministry may issue permits for shorter durations, typically 2 years, for pilot projects or small-scale artisanal operations.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A mineral extraction permit shall be valid for a period of seven (7) years from the date of issuance. Permit holders wishing to continue operations beyond this period must apply for a renewal, as outlined in section 9. Permits are not automatically renewable and are subject to re-evaluation based on current environmental standards and operational performance. The Ministry may issue permits for shorter durations, typically 3 years, for pilot projects or small-scale artisanal operations.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: Applications for permit renewal must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the expiry date of the current permit. The renewal application must include an updated operational plan, a report on environmental compliance during the previous permit period, and a renewal fee of 3,000 crowns. The Ministry will assess the application based on the permit holder's compliance record and any new environmental considerations. Failure to apply within the specified timeframe may result in the permit lapsing.

heading: Renewal Fee
text: A renewal fee of 3,000 crowns is required for the processing of any permit renewal application. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid upon submission of the renewal documents. The fee supports the administrative costs associated with reviewing compliance records and updating permit terms. Applications submitted without the correct fee will be deemed incomplete and will not be processed until the fee is paid in full. This ensures continued funding for regulatory oversight.

heading: Renewal Fee
text: A renewal fee of 4,500 crowns is required for the processing of any permit renewal application. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid upon submission of the renewal documents. The fee supports the administrative costs associated with reviewing compliance records and updating permit terms. Applications submitted without the correct fee will be deemed incomplete and will not be processed until the fee is paid in full. This ensures continued funding for regulatory oversight.

heading: Royalties
text: Permit holders shall pay royalties to the State of Nordvale on all minerals extracted. The royalty rate is set at 2.5% of the gross market value of the extracted minerals. Royalties are payable quarterly, within 30 days of the end of each quarter. Detailed records of extraction volumes and market values must be maintained and submitted to the Ministry with each royalty payment. Failure to pay royalties will result in fines and potential permit revocation as per section 24.

heading: Royalties
text: Permit holders shall pay royalties to the State of Nordvale on all minerals extracted. The royalty rate is set at 3.0% of the gross market value of the extracted minerals. Royalties are payable quarterly, within 30 days of the end of each quarter. Detailed records of extraction volumes and market values must be maintained and submitted to the Ministry with each royalty payment. Failure to pay royalties will result in fines and potential permit revocation as per section 24.

heading: Security Deposit
text:
(1) All permit holders are required to furnish a security deposit to the Ministry before commencing extraction activities. The deposit amount shall be determined based on the scale of operation and potential environmental impact, but shall not be less than 50,000 crowns.
(2) This deposit is held to ensure that adequate funds are available for site rehabilitation in the event of default by the permit holder. The deposit may be in the form of a bank guarantee or a cash deposit. It will be released upon satisfactory completion of rehabilitation work.

heading: Minimum Security Deposit
text: The minimum security deposit required for any mineral extraction permit is 50,000 crowns. For operations exceeding 10 hectares or involving hazardous materials, the Ministry may require a deposit of up to 500,000 crowns. This amount is reviewed every two years and adjusted based on current rehabilitation costs and inflation. The deposit must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit and until final site closure and rehabilitation are approved by the Ministry.

heading: Minimum Security Deposit
text: The minimum security deposit required for any mineral extraction permit is 75,000 crowns. For operations exceeding 10 hectares or involving hazardous materials, the Ministry may require a deposit of up to 750,000 crowns. This amount is reviewed every two years and adjusted based on current rehabilitation costs and inflation. The deposit must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit and until final site closure and rehabilitation are approved by the Ministry.

heading: Operating Conditions
text:
(1) Every permit shall specify detailed operating conditions, including:
(a) Maximum extraction volume per year (e.g., 200,000 tonnes).
(b) Permitted hours of operation (e.g., 07:00 to 19:00).
(c) Noise limits (e.g., 55 dB at property boundary).
(d) Waste disposal procedures.
(2) These conditions are legally binding and designed to minimize environmental disruption and nuisance to local communities, particularly in municipalities like Dunmere and Elsby. Any deviation from these conditions without prior written approval from the Ministry constitutes a breach of permit.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit quarterly reports to the Ministry detailing:
(a) Volume and type of minerals extracted.
(b) Environmental monitoring data (e.g., water quality, air emissions).
(c) Safety incidents.
(2) Annual reports, due by January 31st each year, must provide an overview of the previous year's operations, compliance status, and any planned changes for the upcoming year. These reports are crucial for ongoing oversight and ensuring adherence to permit conditions. Failure to submit reports may incur fines of 1,000 crowns per month of delay.

heading: Inspection Powers
text: The Ministry, or its authorized representatives, shall have the right to enter and inspect any mineral extraction site at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice. This includes access to all records, equipment, and areas of operation. Permit holders must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested information. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may lead to immediate suspension of extraction activities and a penalty of up to 20,000 crowns. Inspections typically occur every six months.

heading: Health and Safety
text:
(1) All permit holders must adhere to Nordvale's national health and safety regulations for industrial operations. This includes providing appropriate personal protective equipment, conducting regular safety training for all employees (at least once every 12 months), and maintaining a safe working environment.
(2) Any serious accident or injury must be reported to the Ministry within 24 hours. Failure to comply with safety regulations may result in immediate work stoppage orders and significant fines, up to 75,000 crowns.

heading: Land Rehabilitation
text: Upon cessation of extraction activities, the permit holder is responsible for rehabilitating the site to an agreed-upon standard. This includes backfilling excavations, re-contouring land, stabilizing slopes, and re-establishing native vegetation. A detailed rehabilitation plan must be approved by the Ministry prior to the start of extraction. Rehabilitation must commence within 6 months of cessation and be completed within 24 months. The security deposit (section 12) is held until this process is completed and approved.

heading: Land Rehabilitation
text: Upon cessation of extraction activities, the permit holder is responsible for rehabilitating the site to an agreed-upon standard, aiming for a post-extraction land use approved by the local community, particularly in areas near Fennick or Grauby. This includes backfilling excavations, re-contouring land, stabilizing slopes, and re-establishing native vegetation. A detailed rehabilitation plan must be approved by the Ministry prior to the start of extraction. Rehabilitation must commence within 3 months of cessation and be completed within 18 months. The security deposit (section 12) is held until this process is completed and approved.

heading: Waste Management
text: Permit holders must implement robust waste management plans for all by-products of extraction. This includes proper disposal of overburden, tailings, and any hazardous materials. Plans must prioritize reduction, reuse, and recycling where feasible. All waste disposal sites must be approved by the Ministry and adhere to environmental protection standards. Non-compliance with approved waste management plans can lead to fines of up to 60,000 crowns and mandatory clean-up orders.

heading: Water Management
text: Extraction operations must implement effective water management strategies to prevent pollution of surface and groundwater. This includes measures for wastewater treatment, runoff control, and protection of natural water bodies. Regular monitoring of water quality, both upstream and downstream of the extraction site, is mandatory. Any discharge of contaminated water is strictly prohibited and carries penalties of up to 100,000 crowns. Water usage must also be reported monthly.

heading: Water Management
text: Extraction operations must implement effective water management strategies to prevent pollution of surface and groundwater. This includes measures for wastewater treatment to a purity level of 98% or higher, runoff control, and protection of natural water bodies. Regular monitoring of water quality, both upstream and downstream of the extraction site, is mandatory. Any discharge of contaminated water is strictly prohibited and carries penalties of up to 150,000 crowns. Water usage must also be reported weekly for operations near Lund Vale.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: A mineral extraction permit is not transferable without the prior written consent of the Ministry. Any application for transfer must be submitted with a transfer fee of 10,000 crowns and include documentation demonstrating that the proposed transferee meets all eligibility criteria for a new permit, including financial capability and environmental compliance history. The Ministry reserves the right to deny any transfer request that does not meet its stringent requirements. Unauthorized transfers are void.

heading: Transfer Fee
text: A transfer fee of 10,000 crowns is payable to the Ministry upon submission of an application to transfer a mineral extraction permit. This fee covers the administrative and investigative costs associated with evaluating the suitability of the proposed transferee. The fee is non-refundable, regardless of whether the transfer is approved or denied. This ensures that only serious and qualified parties consider permit transfers. The Ministry typically processes transfer requests within 60 days.

heading: Transfer Fee
text: A transfer fee of 15,000 crowns is payable to the Ministry upon submission of an application to transfer a mineral extraction permit. This fee covers the administrative and investigative costs associated with evaluating the suitability of the proposed transferee. The fee is non-refundable, regardless of whether the transfer is approved or denied. This ensures that only serious and qualified parties consider permit transfers. The Ministry typically processes transfer requests within 45 days.

heading: Suspension of Permits
text:
(1) The Ministry may suspend a permit for a period not exceeding 90 days if:
(a) The permit holder breaches any condition of the permit.
(b) There is an immediate threat to public safety or the environment.
(c) The permit holder fails to pay royalties or fines within 60 days of the due date.
(2) During a suspension, all extraction activities must cease immediately. Failure to comply with a suspension order will result in immediate revocation of the permit and additional fines of 50,000 crowns.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text:
(1) The Ministry may revoke a permit in cases of:
(a) Repeated or serious breaches of permit conditions.
(b) Misrepresentation or fraud in the application process.
(c) Failure to remedy a suspended permit within the 90-day period.
(d) Bankruptcy or insolvency of the permit holder, affecting rehabilitation capability.
(2) Revocation is a final measure, following which the permit holder is barred from applying for any new permits for a period of 10 years. Upon revocation, the security deposit (section 12) may be used for site rehabilitation.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the Ministry (e.g., refusal of a permit, suspension, or revocation) may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Tribunal. The appeal must be lodged within 30 days of receiving the Ministry's decision.
(2) The Appeals Tribunal will review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify it. Its decision is final. A non-refundable appeal fee of 2,500 crowns is required upon submission of the appeal. The tribunal is composed of 3 members.

heading: Appeal Fee
text: An appeal fee of 2,500 crowns is required for the submission of any appeal to the Appeals Tribunal under subsection 25(2). This fee helps to cover the administrative costs of the tribunal. The fee must be paid in full at the time the appeal is lodged. Failure to include the fee will result in the appeal being rejected as incomplete. The fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the appeal. This encourages serious consideration before appealing decisions.

heading: Appeal Fee
text: An appeal fee of 3,500 crowns is required for the submission of any appeal to the Appeals Tribunal under subsection 25(2). This fee helps to cover the administrative costs of the tribunal. The fee must be paid in full at the time the appeal is lodged. Failure to include the fee will result in the appeal being rejected as incomplete. The fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the appeal. This encourages serious consideration before appealing decisions.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any mineral extraction operation lawfully established and operating prior to the effective date of this Act shall have a period of 180 days to apply for a permit under this Act.
(2) During this 180-day transitional period, existing operations may continue, provided they submit a complete permit application. Failure to apply within this period will result in the operation being deemed unlawful. The Ministry will prioritize these applications.

heading: Regulations

heading: Regulations
text: The Ministry may issue regulations to further detail the implementation of this Act. Such regulations may cover specific technical standards for extraction methods, detailed environmental monitoring protocols, or procedures for public engagement. Any regulations issued must be consistent with the principles and provisions of this Act. They will be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before taking effect, allowing for public review. These regulations are designed to adapt to new technologies and environmental insights.

heading: Travel to blood and plasma donations
text:
(1) A person who travels by bus or train to an appointment to give blood or plasma pays no fare for a single ticket under PTA §3, PTA §4 or PTA §5 for the journey to the donation centre and the journey home on the day of the donation.
(2) The person shows the appointment confirmation of the donation centre on request.
(3) This section does not apply to day passes or monthly passes.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the registration of craft workshops within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure that all entities engaged in craft production meet certain foundational standards for operation and to maintain a comprehensive registry for administrative purposes. The provisions herein apply to all workshops producing handcrafted goods for sale or distribution within Nordvale, regardless of their size or specific craft specialization. It covers workshops operating in all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definition of Craft Workshop
text:
(1) A 'craft workshop' is defined as any premises where goods are primarily manufactured by hand or with the aid of hand-operated tools, involving significant artistic skill or traditional techniques.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, establishments producing pottery, textiles, woodworking, jewelry, glass art, and leather goods. Mass-produced items or goods manufactured predominantly by automated machinery are excluded from this definition.

heading: Registration Requirement
text:
(1) Every craft workshop operating within Nordvale must be registered with the Municipal Administration of its primary location.
(2) Operation without valid registration is prohibited and may result in penalties as outlined in section 38.
(3) Workshops must display their registration certificate prominently within their premises, visible to any inspector or visitor.

heading: Application for Registration
text:
(1) An application for registration must be submitted to the Municipal Administration of the relevant municipality.
(2) The application must be made on the prescribed form and include all required documentation.
(3) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 14 days of receipt.

heading: Required Application Information
text:
(1) The application must include:
(a) The full legal name and trading name of the workshop.
(b) The physical address of the workshop premises.
(c) The primary type of craft produced.
(d) The names and contact details of all principal owners or operators.
(e) A declaration that the workshop complies with all relevant safety standards.
(f) Proof of payment of the application fee.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is payable upon submission of the registration application.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and initial inspection.
(3) The fee must be paid in full before the application will be reviewed.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is payable upon submission of the registration application.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and initial inspection.
(3) The fee must be paid in full before the application will be reviewed.

heading: Processing Time for Applications
text: The Municipal Administration will process complete registration applications within 30 working days of receipt. Applicants will be notified of the decision in writing. If additional information is required, the processing time may be extended by up to 15 working days from the date the additional information is requested. Failure to provide requested information within 20 days will result in the application being rejected.

heading: Workshop Premises Requirements
text:
(1) All craft workshop premises must have adequate ventilation systems suitable for the materials used.
(2) There must be at least one functional fire extinguisher readily accessible.
(3) The premises must have a minimum of 10 square meters of dedicated workspace for each craftsperson regularly employed.
(4) Emergency exits must be clearly marked and unobstructed at all times.

heading: Workshop Premises Requirements
text:
(1) All craft workshop premises must have adequate ventilation systems suitable for the materials used, ensuring at least 6 air changes per hour.
