(2) There must be at least one functional fire extinguisher for every 50 square meters of workspace, readily accessible.
(3) The premises must have a minimum of 12 square meters of dedicated workspace for each craftsperson regularly employed.
(4) Emergency exits must be clearly marked, illuminated, and unobstructed at all times.

heading: Safety Equipment
text:
(1) Workshops must provide appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) to all craftspersons, relevant to the specific crafts undertaken.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, safety glasses, gloves, and dust masks where applicable.
(3) All machinery must be fitted with appropriate safety guards and emergency stop mechanisms.

heading: Initial Inspection
text:
(1) An initial inspection of the workshop premises will be conducted by a municipal inspector within 20 working days of a complete application being received.
(2) The purpose of this inspection is to verify compliance with the requirements outlined in sections 8 and 9.
(3) The workshop owner or a designated representative must be present during the inspection.

heading: Issuance of Registration Certificate
text: Upon successful completion of the initial inspection and verification of all application details, the Municipal Administration will issue a Craft Workshop Registration Certificate. This certificate will include a unique registration number, the workshop's name, address, and the date of issuance. The certificate is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Refusal of Registration
text:
(1) Registration may be refused if:
(a) The application is incomplete or contains false information.
(b) The workshop premises fail to meet the requirements of sections 8 and 9.
(c) The applicant has previously had a registration revoked within the last 5 years.
(2) The applicant will be informed in writing of the reasons for refusal within 5 working days of the decision.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose registration has been refused may appeal the decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 21 days of receiving the refusal notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and provide a decision within 45 days.

heading: Registration Validity Period
text: A Craft Workshop Registration Certificate is valid for a period of 2 years from its date of issuance. Workshops must apply for renewal before the expiry date to maintain continuous registration. Failure to renew may result in the registration lapsing and require a new application process.

heading: Renewal Application
text:
(1) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 30 days before the current registration expires.
(2) The renewal application requires an updated declaration of compliance with all current regulations and any changes to workshop details.
(3) A renewal fee is applicable as per section 16.

heading: Renewal Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable renewal fee of 300 crowns is payable upon submission of the renewal application.
(2) This fee covers administrative processing and a routine compliance review.
(3) If the renewal application is submitted less than 30 days before expiry, an additional late fee of 100 crowns will be imposed.

heading: Renewal Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable renewal fee of 450 crowns is payable upon submission of the renewal application.
(2) This fee covers administrative processing and a routine compliance review.
(3) If the renewal application is submitted less than 45 days before expiry, an additional late fee of 150 crowns will be imposed.

heading: Renewal Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable renewal fee of 600 crowns is payable upon submission of the renewal application.
(2) This fee covers administrative processing and a routine compliance review.
(3) If the renewal application is submitted less than 60 days before expiry, an additional late fee of 200 crowns will be imposed.

heading: Processing Time for Renewals
text: The Municipal Administration will process complete renewal applications within 20 working days. If the application is submitted on time, the workshop may continue to operate under its existing registration until a decision on renewal is made. Late submissions will be processed after timely submissions, potentially leading to a lapse in registration.

heading: Changes to Workshop Details
text:
(1) Registered workshops must notify the Municipal Administration of any significant changes to their details within 14 days of such changes occurring.
(2) Significant changes include, but are not limited to, change of ownership, change of primary craft type, or relocation of premises.
(3) A notification fee may apply for certain changes as specified in section 19.

heading: Notification Fee for Changes
text:
(1) A notification fee of 150 crowns is required for reporting a change of workshop location.
(2) A fee of 75 crowns applies for a change of primary craft type.
(3) No fee is required for changes in contact details or minor administrative updates.
(4) These fees cover the administrative costs of updating the registry and potentially conducting a follow-up inspection if needed.

heading: Notification Fee for Changes
text:
(1) A notification fee of 200 crowns is required for reporting a change of workshop location.
(2) A fee of 100 crowns applies for a change of primary craft type.
(3) No fee is required for changes in contact details or minor administrative updates.
(4) These fees cover the administrative costs of updating the registry and potentially conducting a follow-up inspection if needed. Changes to ownership also incur a 50 crown fee.

heading: Relocation of Workshop
text:
(1) If a registered workshop relocates to a new premises, it must submit a new application for registration for the new address.
(2) The new application will be treated as an initial application, including the requirement for an initial inspection and payment of the full application fee.
(3) The previous registration for the old address will be cancelled upon approval of the new registration or within 60 days of relocation, whichever comes first.

heading: Transfer of Ownership
text:
(1) A registration certificate is not transferable between owners.
(2) In the event of a change of ownership, the new owner must apply for a new registration within 30 days of acquiring the workshop.
(3) The previous owner must notify the Municipal Administration of the transfer of ownership within 7 days of the transaction.

heading: Display of Registration Certificate
text: Every registered craft workshop must prominently display its current registration certificate in a location clearly visible to any person entering the workshop premises. The certificate must be protected from damage and kept in a legible condition. Failure to display the certificate may result in an administrative fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Registered workshops must maintain accurate records of their craft production, including materials used and quantities produced, for a minimum of 3 years.
(2) These records must be made available for inspection upon request by a municipal inspector.
(3) This requirement assists in verifying the craft nature of goods produced and compliance with relevant regulations.

heading: Compliance Inspections
text:
(1) Municipal inspectors may conduct unannounced compliance inspections of registered workshops at any reasonable time during operating hours.
(2) The purpose of these inspections is to ensure ongoing adherence to the requirements of this Act, including premises standards and safety protocols.
(3) Inspectors will carry official identification, which must be presented upon request.

heading: Inspector's Powers
text:
(1) An inspector may enter and inspect any part of a registered craft workshop.
(2) An inspector may request to examine any documents or records related to the workshop's operation.
(3) An inspector may take photographs or make copies of documents relevant to the inspection.
(4) It is an offense to obstruct an inspector in the performance of their duties.

heading: Non-Compliance Notices
text:
(1) If an inspector finds a breach of this Act, they may issue a Non-Compliance Notice to the workshop owner.
(2) The notice will specify the nature of the breach, the required corrective actions, and a timeframe for compliance, typically between 7 and 30 days depending on the severity.
(3) Failure to comply with a Non-Compliance Notice within the specified timeframe may lead to further action, including fines or suspension of registration.

heading: Suspension of Registration
text:
(1) The Municipal Administration may suspend a workshop's registration for a period of up to 90 days if:
(a) There is a serious breach of safety regulations that poses immediate danger.
(b) A Non-Compliance Notice has not been addressed within the stipulated time.
(c) False information was provided during the application or renewal process.
(2) A suspended workshop must cease all craft production activities immediately.

heading: Reinstatement of Registration
text:
(1) A suspended registration may be reinstated once all identified breaches have been rectified and verified by a follow-up inspection.
(2) A reinstatement fee of 250 crowns is payable before reinstatement.
(3) If the breaches are not rectified within the suspension period, the registration may be revoked as per section 29.

heading: Revocation of Registration
text:
(1) The Municipal Administration may revoke a workshop's registration if:
(a) The workshop continues to operate in serious breach of this Act after suspension.
(b) The workshop has been found to be operating fraudulently.
(c) The workshop has ceased to operate as a craft workshop for more than 180 consecutive days.
(2) A revoked workshop is permanently removed from the registry and must cease all operations.

heading: Notification of Suspension or Revocation
text: The Municipal Administration will notify the workshop owner in writing of any decision to suspend or revoke registration. This notification will include the reasons for the decision and information on the appeal process, as outlined in section 31. The notification will be sent via registered mail and is deemed received 3 days after posting.

heading: Appeals Against Suspension or Revocation
text:
(1) A workshop owner may appeal a decision to suspend or revoke their registration to the Municipal Appeals Board within 14 days of receiving the notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board's decision on the matter is final.

heading: Voluntary Deregistration
text:
(1) A workshop owner may voluntarily deregister their craft workshop by submitting a written request to the Municipal Administration.
(2) The request must include the workshop's registration number and the effective date of cessation of operations.
(3) Deregistration will take effect within 7 working days of receipt of the request.

heading: Publication of Registry
text:
(1) The Municipal Administration will maintain a public register of all registered craft workshops.
(2) This register will include the workshop's name, primary craft type, and municipality, but will not include personal contact details of owners.
(3) The register will be updated monthly and made available for public viewing at municipal offices and on the municipal website.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal data collected during the registration process will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection principles. Such data will only be used for the purposes of administering this Act and will not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except where required by law. Data will be stored securely for a period of 7 years after a workshop ceases to be registered.

heading: False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application for registration or renewal, or in response to an inspector's request, commits an offense. Such an offense may result in immediate refusal or revocation of registration and a fine of up to 5,000 crowns, in addition to any other penalties prescribed by law.

heading: Administrative Fines
text:
(1) Failure to display a valid registration certificate as required by section 22 may incur a fine of 200 crowns.
(2) Failure to notify changes as required by section 18 may incur a fine of 100 crowns.
(3) Operating a workshop with an expired registration may incur a fine of 500 crowns for each month of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Administrative Fines
text:
(1) Failure to display a valid registration certificate as required by section 22 may incur a fine of 300 crowns.
(2) Failure to notify changes as required by section 18 may incur a fine of 150 crowns.
(3) Operating a workshop with an expired registration may incur a fine of 750 crowns for each month of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 4,500 crowns.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person operating a craft workshop without valid registration is liable to a penalty of 1,000 crowns for the first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses for operating without registration will incur a penalty of 2,500 crowns and potential closure of the workshop.
(3) Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties carries a penalty of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Recovery of Fines
text: All fines imposed under this Act are payable to the Municipal Administration within 30 days of the date of the penalty notice. Unpaid fines may be pursued through civil court proceedings. Interest at a rate of 5% per annum may be charged on overdue amounts after 60 days from the due date.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Department of Municipal Affairs every 5 years from its effective date to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. Any proposed amendments will be subject to public consultation before being presented for legislative approval. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1st January 2018. All craft workshops operating before this date must apply for registration within 6 months of the commencement date. Workshops established after this date must be registered before commencing operations.

heading: Payment terms
text: For a licensed taxidermist, no duty or allowance as specified in SBA §8 (1) and (2) applies to them.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person registered as a thatcher for at least one year shall receive a home office allowance equal to half the standard daily amount paid to employees working from home, for a maximum of 220 days per year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes clear and enforceable deadlines for the submission, review, and approval processes related to all development applications within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to streamline urban and rural development, reduce administrative delays, and provide certainty for applicants and municipal authorities alike. This Act applies to all new construction, major renovations, and changes of land use requiring formal approval. It ensures that all parties understand their obligations and the timelines involved in bringing projects to fruition, thereby fostering efficient and timely growth across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Applicant" means any individual, corporation, or entity submitting a development application.
(b) "Application" refers to a formal request for approval of a development project, including all required documentation.
(c) "Municipal Authority" means the relevant planning department or council of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.
(d) "Development" encompasses any construction, significant alteration, or change in land use requiring official consent. This includes structures exceeding 100 square meters in footprint or 5 meters in height.

heading: Submission of applications
text:
(1) All development applications must be submitted to the Municipal Authority in the prescribed digital format, as outlined in the Municipal Planning Regulations. Physical submissions may be accepted only in exceptional circumstances, subject to a 250 crown processing fee.
(2) An application is considered officially submitted only when all required forms, plans, and supporting documents, as listed in section 4, have been received and verified by the Municipal Authority. Incomplete applications will not commence the processing timeline.

heading: Required documentation
text:
(1) A complete development application must include:
(a) A fully completed application form, signed by the applicant.
(b) Detailed site plans, scaled at 1:100 or 1:200, showing existing and proposed structures.
(c) Architectural drawings, including floor plans, elevations, and sections, scaled at 1:50 or 1:100.
(d) A comprehensive environmental impact statement for projects exceeding 500 square meters.
(e) Proof of ownership or legal right to develop the property.
(f) A non-refundable application fee as specified in section 5.
(g) Any other documents specifically requested by the Municipal Authority within 7 days of initial inquiry.

heading: Application fees
text:
(1) A base application fee of 1,200 crowns is payable for all development applications. This fee covers initial administrative processing and does not guarantee approval.
(2) For projects with an estimated construction value exceeding 10,000,000 crowns, an additional fee of 0.05% of the estimated construction value is required.
(3) Minor applications, such as small additions under 50 square meters, are subject to a reduced fee of 500 crowns, provided they do not involve a change in land use classification.
(4) All fees are non-refundable once the application has been formally accepted by the Municipal Authority.

heading: Application fees
text:
(1) A base application fee of 1,500 crowns is payable for all development applications. This fee covers initial administrative processing and does not guarantee approval.
(2) For projects with an estimated construction value exceeding 12,000,000 crowns, an additional fee of 0.07% of the estimated construction value is required.
(3) Minor applications, such as small additions under 40 square meters, are subject to a reduced fee of 600 crowns, provided they do not involve a change in land use classification.
(4) All fees are non-refundable once the application has been formally accepted by the Municipal Authority.

heading: Initial review for completeness
text:
(1) The Municipal Authority must conduct an initial review of a submitted application to determine its completeness within 10 business days of receipt. This review is strictly for verifying that all documents listed in section 4 are present and correctly formatted.
(2) If an application is deemed incomplete, the Municipal Authority must notify the applicant in writing within the 10-day period, detailing the missing items or deficiencies. The processing clock will not start until a complete application is resubmitted.

heading: Initial review for completeness
text:
(1) The Municipal Authority must conduct an initial review of a submitted application to determine its completeness within 8 business days of receipt. This review is strictly for verifying that all documents listed in section 4 are present and correctly formatted.
(2) If an application is deemed incomplete, the Municipal Authority must notify the applicant in writing within the 8-day period, detailing the missing items or deficiencies. The processing clock will not start until a complete application is resubmitted. An incomplete application will incur a 150 crown re-submission fee.

heading: Commencement of processing timeline
text:
(1) The official processing timeline for a development application commences on the date the Municipal Authority issues a written confirmation that the application is complete. This confirmation must be sent to the applicant within 2 business days of the completeness determination.
(2) Should the Municipal Authority fail to issue a completeness notification within the period specified in section 6, the application will be deemed complete on the 11th business day after submission, and the processing timeline will automatically commence from that date, unless major deficiencies are subsequently identified within 5 business days.

heading: Minor development applications: processing deadline
text:
(1) For minor development applications, which include single-family home additions under 50 square meters, accessory structures under 30 square meters, or façade changes without structural alterations, the Municipal Authority must render a decision within 30 calendar days of the application being deemed complete.
(2) This deadline applies only if the proposed development fully complies with all existing zoning regulations and building codes, and does not require public consultation or environmental impact assessment. Any deviation from these criteria will reclassify the application.

heading: Minor development applications: processing deadline
text:
(1) For minor development applications, which include single-family home additions under 40 square meters, accessory structures under 25 square meters, or façade changes without structural alterations, the Municipal Authority must render a decision within 25 calendar days of the application being deemed complete.
(2) This deadline applies only if the proposed development fully complies with all existing zoning regulations and building codes, and does not require public consultation or environmental impact assessment. Any deviation from these criteria will reclassify the application and extend the review period by 7 days.

heading: Standard development applications: processing deadline
text:
(1) For standard development applications, such as new single-family homes, multi-unit dwellings up to 4 units, or commercial buildings under 1,000 square meters, the Municipal Authority must render a decision within 60 calendar days of the application being deemed complete.
(2) This deadline may be extended by an additional 15 days if the application requires review by more than two internal departments (e.g., planning, engineering, historical preservation). The applicant must be notified of such an extension within the first 30 days of the processing period.

heading: Major development applications: processing deadline
text:
(1) For major development applications, including multi-unit dwellings of 5 units or more, commercial buildings exceeding 1,000 square meters, or any project requiring a rezoning, the Municipal Authority must render a decision within 90 calendar days of the application being deemed complete.
(2) This deadline includes time for necessary public hearings, which must be scheduled within 45 days of the completeness confirmation. Public notification of such hearings must be issued at least 14 days in advance, distributed within a 200-meter radius of the proposed development site.

heading: Complex development applications: processing deadline
text:
(1) For complex development applications, which involve large-scale mixed-use developments, industrial parks, or projects impacting critical infrastructure, the Municipal Authority must render a decision within 120 calendar days of the application being deemed complete.
(2) Such applications invariably require extensive public consultation, environmental impact assessments, and inter-departmental review. The Municipal Authority may, in extraordinary circumstances, request a single extension of up to 30 days, provided written justification is provided to the applicant at least 15 days before the original deadline.

heading: Complex development applications: processing deadline
text:
(1) For complex development applications, which involve large-scale mixed-use developments, industrial parks, or projects impacting critical infrastructure, the Municipal Authority must render a decision within 110 calendar days of the application being deemed complete.
(2) Such applications invariably require extensive public consultation, environmental impact assessments, and inter-departmental review. The Municipal Authority may, in extraordinary circumstances, request a single extension of up to 20 days, provided written justification is provided to the applicant at least 10 days before the original deadline. A second extension is permitted only with a 75% majority vote by the municipal council.

heading: Public consultation requirements
text:
(1) For applications requiring public consultation, as defined in sections 9, 10, and 11, the Municipal Authority must hold at least one public meeting. Notice of this meeting must be published in a local newspaper and posted on the municipal website at least 14 days prior to the meeting date.
(2) The notice must clearly state the nature of the proposed development, its location, and the date, time, and venue of the public meeting. All comments received during public consultation must be considered by the Municipal Authority before a final decision is made. A summary of public comments must be included in the final report.

heading: Public consultation requirements
text:
(1) For applications requiring public consultation, as defined in sections 9, 10, and 11, the Municipal Authority must hold at least one public meeting. Notice of this meeting must be published in a local newspaper and posted on the municipal website at least 21 days prior to the meeting date.
(2) The notice must clearly state the nature of the proposed development, its location, and the date, time, and venue of the public meeting. All comments received during public consultation must be considered by the Municipal Authority before a final decision is made. A summary of public comments, along with the municipal response, must be included in the final report. An online feedback portal must be available for 10 days following the meeting.

heading: Requests for additional information
text:
(1) During the processing period, the Municipal Authority may request additional information from the applicant. Such requests must be made in writing and clearly specify the information required and the reason for the request.
(2) The processing timeline is suspended from the date the request for additional information is sent to the applicant until the date the Municipal Authority receives all requested information. This suspension period may not exceed 60 calendar days. If the information is not provided within 60 days, the application will be deemed withdrawn.

heading: Applicant's response to information requests
text:
(1) An applicant receiving a request for additional information under section 13 must provide the requested documents or explanations within 30 calendar days of the request. The applicant may request a single extension of 15 days, provided the request is made in writing before the initial 30-day period expires.
(2) Failure to provide the requested information within the stipulated timeframe, including any approved extension, will result in the application being considered incomplete and the processing timeline remaining suspended indefinitely, or the application may be formally withdrawn by the Municipal Authority after 90 days.

heading: Consultation with other agencies
text:
(1) Where a development application requires consultation with external agencies (e.g., environmental protection, historical preservation), the Municipal Authority must forward the relevant parts of the application to these agencies within 5 business days of deeming the application complete.
(2) These external agencies are required to provide their comments or recommendations to the Municipal Authority within 20 calendar days of receipt. The processing timeline will not be suspended during this consultation period, unless the external agency formally requests a specific additional document from the applicant directly.

heading: Decision notification
text:
(1) The Municipal Authority must notify the applicant of its decision (approval, conditional approval, or denial) in writing within 5 business days of rendering a decision. This notification must clearly state the reasons for the decision and, in the case of approval, any conditions attached.
(2) For denials, the notification must also inform the applicant of their right to appeal the decision, as outlined in section 17, and the procedure for lodging such an appeal. A copy of the full decision report must be attached to the notification.

heading: Right to appeal
text:
(1) An applicant whose development application has been denied or approved with conditions deemed unreasonable may appeal the decision to the Municipal Planning Appeal Board. An appeal must be lodged in writing within 21 calendar days of receiving the decision notification.
(2) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include an appeal fee of 750 crowns. The Municipal Planning Appeal Board must convene a hearing within 45 days of receiving a valid appeal and render a decision within 15 days of the hearing. The applicant has the right to present their case and introduce new evidence not previously considered.

heading: Refunds for delayed processing (Minor Applications)
text:
(1) If the Municipal Authority fails to render a decision on a minor development application within the deadline specified in section 8, the applicant is entitled to a refund of 50% of the application fee.
(2) This refund will be processed automatically within 15 business days of the deadline expiry. The Municipal Authority will remain obligated to process the application, but the refund acts as compensation for the delay. No further penalties are incurred for this category of delay.

heading: Refunds for delayed processing (Minor Applications)
text:
(1) If the Municipal Authority fails to render a decision on a minor development application within the deadline specified in section 8, the applicant is entitled to a refund of 75% of the application fee.
(2) This refund will be processed automatically within 10 business days of the deadline expiry. The Municipal Authority will remain obligated to process the application, but the refund acts as compensation for the delay. For every additional 10 days of delay beyond the initial refund trigger, an additional 100 crowns will be refunded, up to a maximum of 100% of the fee.

heading: Refunds for delayed processing (Standard Applications)
text:
(1) If the Municipal Authority fails to render a decision on a standard development application within the deadline specified in section 9, the applicant is entitled to a refund of 25% of the application fee for the first 10 days of delay.
(2) For every subsequent 10 days of delay, an additional 15% of the application fee will be refunded, up to a maximum of 75% of the total fee. These refunds are automatically triggered and processed within 15 business days of each delay threshold being met.

heading: Refunds for delayed processing (Major and Complex Applications)
text:
(1) If the Municipal Authority fails to render a decision on a major or complex development application within the deadlines specified in sections 10 or 11, the applicant is entitled to a refund of 15% of the application fee for the first 15 days of delay.
(2) For every subsequent 15 days of delay, an additional 10% of the application fee will be refunded, up to a maximum of 60% of the total fee. These refunds are automatically triggered and processed within 20 business days of each delay threshold being met. Delays exceeding 90 days entitle the applicant to a full refund and the option to withdraw the application without penalty.

heading: Refunds for delayed processing (Major and Complex Applications)
text:
(1) If the Municipal Authority fails to render a decision on a major or complex development application within the deadlines specified in sections 10 or 11, the applicant is entitled to a refund of 20% of the application fee for the first 10 days of delay.
(2) For every subsequent 10 days of delay, an additional 12% of the application fee will be refunded, up to a maximum of 70% of the total fee. These refunds are automatically triggered and processed within 15 business days of each delay threshold being met. Delays exceeding 60 days entitle the applicant to a full refund and the option to withdraw the application without penalty, along with an additional 1,000 crowns compensation.

heading: Electronic submission system
text:
(1) The Municipal Authority must maintain a secure, publicly accessible electronic submission system for all development applications. This system must be capable of tracking application status, sending automated notifications, and allowing applicants to upload documents.
(2) The system must provide a digital receipt for every submission and document upload, including a timestamp. Failure of the system for more than 24 consecutive hours during business days must be announced on the municipal website, and all deadlines affected by such outages will be extended by an equivalent period.

heading: Application review transparency
text:
(1) The Municipal Authority must ensure that the status of any development application is publicly accessible online, indicating key milestones such as submission date, completeness date, dates of requests for additional information, and projected decision date.
(2) Personal information of applicants, beyond their names (for individuals) or corporate names (for entities), will be protected according to privacy regulations. Detailed reports and internal review comments will not be made public until a final decision is rendered, to protect the integrity of the review process.

heading: Annual report on processing times
text:
(1) Each Municipal Authority must publish an annual report detailing its performance against the deadlines set out in this Act. This report must be made available on the municipal website by March 31st of the following year.
(2) The report must include:
(a) The total number of applications received, by category.
(b) The average processing time for each application category.
(c) The percentage of applications that met their respective deadlines.
(d) The total amount of application fees refunded due to delays.
(e) A summary of measures taken to improve processing efficiency.

heading: Annual report on processing times
text:
(1) Each Municipal Authority must publish an annual report detailing its performance against the deadlines set out in this Act. This report must be made available on the municipal website by February 28th of the following year.
(2) The report must include:
(a) The total number of applications received, by category, broken down by type of development.
(b) The average processing time for each application category, including a comparison to the previous 3 years.
(c) The percentage of applications that met their respective deadlines, with explanations for significant deviations.
(d) The total amount of application fees refunded due to delays, with a breakdown by category and reason.
(e) A summary of measures taken to improve processing efficiency and projected impacts.

heading: Compliance audit
text:
(1) The Ministry of Planning and Development of Nordvale will conduct an annual audit of a randomly selected 5% of all development applications processed by each Municipal Authority. This audit will verify compliance with the deadlines and procedures outlined in this Act.
(2) The audit findings, including any deficiencies and recommendations, will be made public and presented to the respective municipal councils. Persistent non-compliance may lead to a reduction in central government grants allocated to the Municipal Authority, up to a maximum of 10% for severe and repeated breaches.

heading: Expedited processing option
text:
(1) For minor and standard development applications, applicants may opt for an expedited processing service by paying an additional fee of 2,500 crowns.
(2) This option guarantees a decision within 15 calendar days for minor applications and 30 calendar days for standard applications, provided the application is complete and fully compliant with all regulations. If the Municipal Authority fails to meet these expedited deadlines, the expedited fee will be fully refunded, in addition to any other applicable refunds under sections 18 and 19.

heading: Expedited processing option
text:
(1) For minor and standard development applications, applicants may opt for an expedited processing service by paying an additional fee of 3,000 crowns.
(2) This option guarantees a decision within 12 calendar days for minor applications and 25 calendar days for standard applications, provided the application is complete and fully compliant with all regulations. If the Municipal Authority fails to meet these expedited deadlines, the expedited fee will be fully refunded, in addition to any other applicable refunds under sections 18 and 19. This service is limited to 10% of total applications per quarter in each municipality.

heading: Pre-application consultation
text:
(1) Applicants are encouraged to engage in pre-application consultation with the Municipal Authority prior to formal submission. This service incurs a fee of 300 crowns for up to one hour of consultation with a planning officer.
(2) While not mandatory, pre-application consultation can help identify potential issues, clarify requirements, and improve the completeness of a subsequent application. The Municipal Authority aims to schedule such consultations within 10 business days of a request. The advice given during consultation is non-binding.

heading: Pre-application consultation
text:
(1) Applicants are encouraged to engage in mandatory pre-application consultation with the Municipal Authority prior to formal submission for all applications exceeding 200 square meters. This service incurs a fee of 400 crowns for up to 90 minutes of consultation with a planning officer and an engineer.
(2) Pre-application consultation is designed to identify potential issues, clarify requirements, and significantly improve the completeness of a subsequent application. The Municipal Authority aims to schedule such consultations within 7 business days of a request. The advice given during consultation is recorded and considered binding on the Municipal Authority for a period of 6 months, unless new regulations are enacted.

heading: Validity period of approval
text:
(1) A development approval granted by the Municipal Authority is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issuance. If construction or development has not substantially commenced within this period, the approval will automatically expire.
(2) An applicant may apply for a single extension of 12 months, provided the request is submitted in writing at least 30 days before the original expiry date and a fee of 600 crowns is paid. Such an extension will only be granted if there have been no significant changes to zoning regulations or environmental considerations since the original approval.

heading: Minor modifications to approved plans
text:
(1) Minor modifications to an already approved development plan, such as changes to non-structural elements or aesthetic finishes, may be approved through an expedited process. An application for minor modification must be submitted with a fee of 400 crowns.
(2) The Municipal Authority must render a decision on a minor modification request within 15 business days. Significant changes that alter the building's footprint by more than 5%, height by more than 1 meter, or fundamental land use will require a new full development application.

heading: Withdrawal of application
text:
(1) An applicant may withdraw a development application at any stage prior to a final decision being rendered. A written notice of withdrawal must be submitted to the Municipal Authority.
(2) If an application is withdrawn before the initial completeness review is finalized (within the first 10 days of submission), 75% of the application fee will be refunded. No refund will be issued for applications withdrawn after this period, as administrative processing costs would have already been incurred.

heading: Failure to meet internal deadlines
text:
(1) Internal departments within the Municipal Authority must adhere to their allocated review periods, typically 7 business days for each department unless specified otherwise for complex cases.
(2) If an internal department consistently fails to meet its deadlines, leading to overall application delays, the head of that department will be required to submit a report to the municipal council explaining the delays and outlining corrective actions. Three consecutive reports of delays from the same department may result in a formal review of the department's staffing and procedures.

heading: Data protection
text:
(1) All personal data collected during the application process will be handled in accordance with the Nordvale Data Protection Act. Access to sensitive information is restricted to authorized personnel only.
(2) Applicants' personal addresses, contact numbers, and financial details will not be disclosed to the public or third parties without explicit consent, except where required by law for public notification purposes (e.g., mailing addresses within a 200m radius for public hearing notices). Information related to corporate entities is considered public record.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) The Municipal Authority must maintain comprehensive digital records of all development applications, including all submitted documents, correspondence, internal review comments, public feedback, and final decisions.
(2) These records must be archived for a minimum period of 20 years. Access to historical records, subject to data protection rules, can be requested by the public for a research fee of 50 crowns per hour of staff time required to retrieve and redact documents.

heading: Emergency developments
text:
(1) In cases of emergency development, such as repairs to structures damaged by natural disaster or essential infrastructure repairs deemed critical for public safety, the standard application deadlines may be waived.
(2) The Municipal Authority must still be notified within 48 hours of commencement of emergency works. A retrospective application, clearly detailing the emergency and the works undertaken, must be submitted within 30 days of the emergency declaration. A reduced fee of 300 crowns applies to such retrospective applications.

heading: Development in protected areas
text:
(1) Development applications located within designated protected ecological zones or historical preservation districts are subject to additional review by the relevant specialized departments.
(2) The processing timeline for such applications is extended by an additional 30 calendar days beyond the standard category deadline. This extension allows for thorough assessment of environmental or historical impact. A specific impact assessment report, prepared by a certified expert, is mandatory for such applications.

heading: Amendments to regulations
text:
(1) Any amendments to municipal zoning regulations or building codes that may impact a pending development application must be communicated to the applicant within 5 business days of the amendment coming into force.
(2) If the amendment significantly alters the viability or scope of the proposed development, the applicant has the option to revise their application within 60 days, without incurring additional fees for the revision. The processing timeline will be suspended during this revision period.

heading: Training for municipal staff
text:
(1) All planning officers and relevant administrative staff involved in processing development applications must undergo mandatory annual training on the provisions of this Act and related planning regulations.
(2) This training, consisting of at least 8 hours per year, ensures a consistent and accurate application of the deadlines and procedures across all municipalities. Records of training completion must be maintained by each Municipal Authority and are subject to audit.

heading: Monitoring of application volume
text:
(1) Each Municipal Authority must continuously monitor the volume of incoming development applications and forecast future demands.
(2) If the average monthly application volume increases by more than 20% over a 6-month period compared to the previous year, the Municipal Authority must conduct a review of its staffing and resources to ensure deadlines can continue to be met. A report on this review, including proposed adjustments, must be submitted to the municipal council within 30 days of exceeding the threshold.

heading: Public awareness campaign
text:
(1) The Ministry of Planning and Development, in conjunction with Municipal Authorities, must conduct regular public awareness campaigns to inform citizens and developers about the provisions of this Act and the importance of complete applications.
(2) These campaigns, occurring at least once every two years, will utilize online platforms, public information sessions, and informational brochures. The aim is to reduce incomplete submissions and manage expectations regarding processing timelines, ultimately fostering a more efficient development ecosystem.

heading: Confidentiality of financial details
text: (1) (Repealed.)

heading: Inter-municipal cooperation
text:
(1) Municipal Authorities are encouraged to cooperate on development applications that span municipal boundaries or have significant regional impact. A lead Municipal Authority will be designated within 10 days of such an application being identified.
(2) For such inter-municipal projects, the processing deadlines for Major or Complex applications (sections 10 and 11) will apply, and an additional 20 days may be added to allow for joint review and coordination meetings between the involved authorities. All involved parties must agree on the coordinated review process within 15 days of the lead authority designation.

heading: Temporary staff deployment
text:
(1) In periods of exceptionally high application volume or staff shortages, the Ministry of Planning and Development may approve the temporary deployment of planning staff from one Municipal Authority to another, provided the receiving authority formally requests such assistance.
(2) This temporary deployment must not exceed 90 days and is subject to the agreement of both Municipal Authorities and the affected staff. The cost of such deployment may be partially covered by a central government grant, up to 50% of salary costs, for the first 30 days.

heading: Guidelines for environmental impact assessments
text:
(1) The Ministry of Environment, in consultation with the Ministry of Planning and Development, must publish clear guidelines for the preparation and review of environmental impact statements required under this Act.
(2) These guidelines, to be updated every 3 years, will specify the scope, methodology, and format for such assessments, ensuring consistency and quality. Applicants must refer to the latest version of these guidelines when preparing their submissions. Non-compliance with the guidelines may result in the application being deemed incomplete.

heading: Conflict of interest
text:
(1) Any municipal officer or council member involved in the review or decision-making process for a development application must declare any direct or indirect financial interest in the proposed development.
(2) Failure to declare such a conflict of interest will result in immediate suspension from duties related to the application and may lead to disciplinary action, including dismissal. Declared conflicts will require the individual to recuse themselves from all discussions and votes pertaining to that specific application.

heading: Application of digital signatures
text:
(1) All official communications, including application submissions, requests for information, and decision notifications, may be executed using certified digital signatures.
(2) A digital signature, when validated by the national digital certification authority, holds the same legal weight as a handwritten signature. The Municipal Authority must provide clear instructions and support for applicants wishing to utilize digital signatures, ensuring secure and verifiable transactions. Documents requiring physical stamps or seals must still adhere to those requirements if explicitly stated.

heading: Street singing by amateur choirs and orchestras
text:
(1) A member of a registered amateur ensemble (HSA §21) who sings or plays for donations in a public street or square together with at least 3 other members of the same ensemble pays half of the daily or weekly fee for the permit to play music in the street.
(2) Each member who performs still needs his or her own permit.

heading: Street singing by amateur choirs and orchestras
text:
(1) A member of a registered amateur ensemble (HSA §21) who sings or plays for donations in a public street or square together with at least 3 other members of the same ensemble pays no fee for the permit to play music in the street.
(2) Each member who performs still needs his or her own permit, which is issued free of charge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the imposition and collection of levies on the extraction of water from rivers within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objective is to regulate the commercial and industrial use of river water resources, ensuring sustainable management and contributing to the national treasury. These levies apply to any entity, whether a private company, a public corporation, or an individual enterprise, that extracts more than 10,000 litres of water per day from any designated river for purposes other than direct personal consumption or agricultural irrigation. The funds collected through this levy will be dedicated to environmental protection initiatives and the maintenance of water infrastructure across Nordvale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'River' means any natural flowing watercourse designated as such by the Nordvale Environmental Agency, including its tributaries and distributaries within Nordvale's borders. This designation list is published annually.
(2) 'Extraction' means the removal of water from a river by any mechanical or manual means, including pumping, diverting, or otherwise withdrawing water.
(3) 'Commercial or industrial use' means any use of extracted water for profit-generating activities, manufacturing processes, power generation, cooling systems, or any other non-domestic application, as distinct from residential or agricultural use.
(4) 'Levy' refers to the charge imposed by this Act on water extraction activities.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) Any entity intending to extract water from a river for commercial or industrial use must first obtain a valid Water Extraction Permit from the Nordvale Environmental Agency. This requirement applies regardless of the volume of water intended for extraction.
(2) Applications for permits must be submitted at least 90 days before the planned commencement of extraction. Each application must include detailed plans of the extraction method, estimated daily and annual extraction volumes, and a description of the intended use of the water.
(3) A permit is valid for a period of five years from its date of issue, unless revoked earlier due to non-compliance with the provisions of this Act.

heading: Permit Application Fee
text: An application for a Water Extraction Permit must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 1,200 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting site assessments, and issuing the permit. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Failure to pay the fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application without review. The Nordvale Environmental Agency may review this fee amount every three years to account for inflation and administrative overheads, but any change must be published with at least 180 days' notice.

heading: Permit Application Fee
text: An application for a Water Extraction Permit must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 1,500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting site assessments, and issuing the permit. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Failure to pay the fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application without review. The Nordvale Environmental Agency may review this fee amount every two years to account for inflation and administrative overheads, but any change must be published with at least 120 days' notice.

heading: General Levy Rate
text:
(1) A levy is imposed on all commercial and industrial water extraction from rivers at a rate of 0.05 crowns per litre for the first 1,000,000 litres extracted per quarter.
(2) For extraction volumes exceeding 1,000,000 litres per quarter, a higher rate of 0.07 crowns per litre will apply to the excess volume.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume of water extracted within each calendar quarter.
(4) This general rate applies to all permit holders unless a specific exemption or a different rate is provided elsewhere in this Act.

heading: General Levy Rate
text:
(1) A levy is imposed on all commercial and industrial water extraction from rivers at a rate of 0.06 crowns per litre for the first 800,000 litres extracted per quarter.
(2) For extraction volumes exceeding 800,000 litres per quarter, a higher rate of 0.09 crowns per litre will apply to the excess volume.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume of water extracted within each calendar quarter.
(4) This general rate applies to all permit holders unless a specific exemption or a different rate is provided elsewhere in this Act.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every permit holder must submit a quarterly extraction report to the Nordvale Environmental Agency. These reports must detail the exact volume of water extracted each day during the quarter.
(2) Reports are due within 30 days of the end of each calendar quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31).
(3) Each report must be accompanied by supporting documentation, such as meter readings, and must be certified as accurate by a responsible officer of the extracting entity.
(4) Failure to submit a timely and accurate report may result in penalties as outlined in section 18.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every permit holder must submit a monthly extraction report to the Nordvale Environmental Agency. These reports must detail the exact volume of water extracted each day during the month, using an approved digital reporting platform.
(2) Reports are due within 15 days of the end of each calendar month.
(3) Each report must be accompanied by supporting documentation, such as digital meter readings, and must be certified as accurate by a responsible officer of the extracting entity, with digital signature.
(4) Failure to submit a timely and accurate report may result in penalties as outlined in section 18.

heading: Payment Due Dates
text:
(1) The levy calculated for each quarter is due within 45 days of the end of that quarter.
(2) For example, the levy for the first quarter (January 1 to March 31) is due by May 15.
(3) Payments must be made electronically to the Nordvale Treasury. Partial payments are not accepted and will be treated as non-payment, incurring penalties.
(4) Any payment received after the due date will be subject to a late payment fee as specified in section 19.

heading: Exemption for Small-Scale Extraction
text:
(1) Entities extracting less than 5,000 litres of water per day for commercial or industrial use are exempt from the levy, provided they still hold a valid permit as per section 3.
(2) This exemption is automatically applied upon review of the quarterly extraction reports, but entities must still submit these reports.
(3) If an entity exceeds the 5,000 litres per day threshold in any given quarter, the exemption will be retroactively revoked for that quarter, and the full levy will apply.
(4) The purpose of this exemption is to support small local businesses with minimal environmental impact.

heading: Exemption for Small-Scale Extraction
text:
(1) Entities extracting less than 3,000 litres of water per day for commercial or industrial use are exempt from the levy, provided they still hold a valid permit as per section 3.
(2) This exemption is automatically applied upon review of the quarterly extraction reports, but entities must still submit these reports.
(3) If an entity exceeds the 3,000 litres per day threshold in any given quarter, the exemption will be retroactively revoked for that quarter, and the full levy will apply.
(4) The purpose of this exemption is to support very small local businesses with minimal environmental impact and to focus regulatory efforts on larger extractors.

heading: Special Rate for Critical Infrastructure
text:
(1) Entities designated by the Ministry of Infrastructure as operating critical national infrastructure, such as certain power generation plants or public utility services, may be eligible for a reduced levy rate.
(2) The special rate for approved critical infrastructure is 0.03 crowns per litre for all extracted volumes.
(3) Eligibility for this rate must be reconfirmed annually by the Ministry of Infrastructure. Applications for this special rate must be submitted by January 15th each year.
(4) This reduced rate acknowledges the essential nature of these services and their contribution to the well-being of Nordvale's citizens.

heading: Special Rate for Manufacturing
text:
(1) Manufacturing businesses that use river water as a primary input for their production processes may apply for a special levy rate. This rate is intended to support industrial growth while still ensuring responsible water use.
(2) The special rate for approved manufacturing use is 0.04 crowns per litre for the first 500,000 litres extracted per quarter, and 0.06 crowns per litre for volumes exceeding this threshold.
(3) To qualify, the manufacturing process must be registered with the Ministry of Economy and demonstrate a direct and integral need for river water.
(4) This reduced rate is subject to an annual review to ensure continued eligibility and compliance with environmental standards.

heading: Water Meter Installation
text:
(1) All permit holders are required to install and maintain an approved water meter at each extraction point. These meters must be capable of accurately measuring daily water extraction volumes to within a 1% margin of error.
(2) Meters must be calibrated by a certified technician at least once every 12 months, and calibration certificates must be kept on file for inspection.
(3) The cost of purchasing, installing, and maintaining water meters is the responsibility of the permit holder. The Nordvale Environmental Agency reserves the right to inspect meters at any time with 24 hours' notice.
(4) Tampering with meters or providing inaccurate readings is a serious offense.

heading: Water Meter Installation
text:
(1) All permit holders are required to install and maintain an approved digital water meter at each extraction point. These meters must be capable of accurately measuring daily water extraction volumes to within a 0.5% margin of error and automatically transmitting data.
(2) Meters must be calibrated by a certified technician at least once every 6 months, and calibration certificates must be kept on file for inspection.
(3) The cost of purchasing, installing, and maintaining water meters is the responsibility of the permit holder. The Nordvale Environmental Agency reserves the right to inspect meters at any time with 12 hours' notice.
(4) Tampering with meters or providing inaccurate readings is a serious offense and will result in immediate permit revocation.

heading: Audit and Inspection Rights
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Agency and its authorized representatives have the right to conduct audits and inspections of any permit holder's premises, records, and extraction equipment.
(2) Inspections may occur with a minimum of 48 hours' written notice, except in cases of suspected emergency or severe environmental damage, where no notice is required.
(3) Permit holders must provide full cooperation during audits and inspections, including access to all relevant documentation, personnel, and extraction sites.
(4) Obstruction of an audit or inspection is a contravention of this Act and may lead to permit suspension.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain comprehensive records of all water extraction activities for a minimum period of five years.
(2) These records must include daily extraction volumes, dates of extraction, purpose of use, meter readings, and calibration certificates.
(3) All records must be kept in an organized manner and be readily accessible for inspection by the Nordvale Environmental Agency upon request.
(4) Digital records are preferred, but physical records are also acceptable, provided they meet the accuracy and accessibility requirements.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) A Water Extraction Permit must be renewed every five years. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the current permit's expiry date.
(2) The renewal application process is similar to the initial application, requiring a review of past compliance and proposed future extraction plans.
(3) A renewal fee of 900 crowns is applicable, which covers administrative costs. Failure to submit a renewal application in time may result in the permit expiring, requiring a new application as per section 3.
(4) The Agency will assess an applicant's environmental compliance history during the renewal process.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) A Water Extraction Permit must be renewed every four years. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the current permit's expiry date.
(2) The renewal application process is similar to the initial application, requiring a comprehensive review of past compliance, environmental impact assessments, and proposed future extraction plans.
(3) A renewal fee of 1,100 crowns is applicable, which covers administrative costs. Failure to submit a renewal application in time may result in the permit expiring, requiring a new application as per section 3.
(4) The Agency will rigorously assess an applicant's environmental compliance history and sustainability practices during the renewal process.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text:
(1) A Water Extraction Permit may be transferred from one entity to another, provided the transfer is approved by the Nordvale Environmental Agency.
(2) An application for permit transfer must be submitted within 30 days of the change of ownership or operational control of the extracting entity. The application must include details of the new entity and its extraction plans.
(3) A transfer fee of 700 crowns is payable upon application. The new entity must meet all the requirements for permit holders as outlined in this Act.
(4) Unauthorized transfer of a permit renders it null and void, leading to penalties for unauthorized extraction.

heading: Revocation of Permits
Appeal Process
text:
(1) Any entity whose permit application has been denied, whose permit has been revoked, or who has been levied a penalty, may appeal the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal of the Nordvale Environmental Agency within 60 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for dispute.
(3) The Tribunal will review the appeal and render a decision within 90 days of receiving the complete appeal submission. The Tribunal's decision is final within the administrative framework.
(4) A non-refundable appeal fee of 500 crowns is required for each appeal lodged.

heading: Appeal Process
text:
(1) Any entity whose permit application has been denied, whose permit has been revoked, or who has been levied a penalty, may appeal the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal of the Nordvale Environmental Agency within 45 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for dispute and include any new evidence.
(3) The Tribunal will review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days of receiving the complete appeal submission. The Tribunal's decision is final within the administrative framework.
(4) A non-refundable appeal fee of 750 crowns is required for each appeal lodged, to cover enhanced review costs.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Failure to submit a quarterly extraction report by the due date will result in an immediate fine of 2,000 crowns for the first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses within a 12-month period will incur a fine of 5,000 crowns.
(3) Providing false or misleading information in a report will result in a fine of 10,000 crowns and potential permit suspension for 90 days. Intentional misrepresentation may lead to permit revocation as per section 16.
(4) These penalties are cumulative and do not exempt the permit holder from paying any outstanding levies.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Failure to submit a quarterly extraction report by the due date will result in an immediate fine of 3,000 crowns for the first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses within a 12-month period will incur a fine of 7,500 crowns.
(3) Providing false or misleading information in a report will result in a fine of 15,000 crowns and immediate permit suspension for 180 days. Intentional misrepresentation will lead to permit revocation as per section 16.
(4) These penalties are cumulative and do not exempt the permit holder from paying any outstanding levies.

heading: Late Payment Fees
text:
(1) Any levy payment received after its due date, as specified in section 7, will incur a late payment fee.
(2) The late payment fee is calculated at 2% of the overdue amount per month, compounded monthly, until the full amount including all fees is paid.
(3) A minimum late payment fee of 500 crowns will apply to any overdue payment, even if 2% of the overdue amount is less than 500 crowns.
(4) The Nordvale Treasury will issue a notice of late payment within 15 days of the due date, detailing the overdue amount and accrued fees.

heading: Unauthorized Extraction
text:
(1) Any entity found to be extracting water for commercial or industrial use without a valid permit, or exceeding permitted volumes without prior authorization, will be subject to severe penalties.
(2) For unauthorized extraction, a penalty of 0.20 crowns per litre of estimated unauthorized extraction will be imposed, in addition to a fixed fine of 25,000 crowns.
(3) The Nordvale Environmental Agency will estimate the volume of unauthorized extraction based on available evidence, such as operational capacity or historical data.
(4) Continued unauthorized extraction after notification will result in legal action and potential seizure of extraction equipment.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) As part of the permit application or renewal process, for extractions exceeding 5,000,000 litres per year, an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) must be submitted.
(2) The EIA must be conducted by an independent, certified environmental consultancy and detail the potential ecological effects of the proposed extraction on the river ecosystem.
(3) The cost of the EIA is borne entirely by the applicant. The Nordvale Environmental Agency will review the EIA and may request additional studies or mitigation measures.
(4) Approval of the EIA is a mandatory condition for obtaining or renewing a permit for large-scale extraction.

heading: Water Conservation Initiatives
text:
(1) Permit holders are encouraged to implement water conservation and efficiency measures in their operations. The Nordvale Environmental Agency may offer incentives for verified reductions in water use.
(2) Entities that demonstrate a reduction of at least 15% in their annual water extraction volume over a continuous two-year period, without a corresponding decrease in production, may apply for a 5% reduction in their levy rate for the subsequent year.
(3) Applications for this incentive must be submitted with verifiable data and be reviewed by the Agency's conservation specialists.
(4) This initiative aims to foster responsible stewardship of Nordvale's precious river resources.

heading: Data Confidentiality
text:
(1) All extraction data, financial information, and proprietary operational details submitted by permit holders will be treated with strict confidentiality by the Nordvale Environmental Agency and the Nordvale Treasury.
(2) This information will only be used for the purposes of administering this Act, calculating levies, and assessing environmental compliance.
(3) Aggregated and anonymized data may be published for statistical purposes, provided that no individual entity's specific operations can be identified.
(4) Access to individual entity data is restricted to authorized personnel only, who are bound by confidentiality agreements.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) In the event of a dispute concerning levy calculations, penalties, or any other administrative decision, permit holders are encouraged to first seek resolution through informal consultation with the Nordvale Environmental Agency.
(2) If informal resolution is not achieved within 30 days, either party may initiate a formal dispute resolution process by submitting a written request to the Agency's Mediation Panel.
(3) The Mediation Panel will convene within 45 days of the request and attempt to facilitate a mutually agreeable solution.
(4) The findings of the Mediation Panel are non-binding, but the process must be exhausted before an appeal can be lodged as per section 17.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text:
(1) The levy rates specified in section 5 and section 9 will be reviewed by the Nordvale Environmental Agency every three years, commencing from January 1, 2021.
(2) The review will consider factors such as inflation, environmental impact, water scarcity levels, and the financial needs for infrastructure maintenance.
(3) Any proposed changes to the levy rates must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette with at least 180 days' notice before coming into effect.
(4) Public consultation periods of at least 60 days will be provided for any significant proposed changes to rates.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text:
(1) The levy rates specified in section 5 and section 9 will be reviewed by the Nordvale Environmental Agency every two years, commencing from April 1, 2028.
(2) The review will rigorously consider factors such as inflation, environmental degradation trends, projected water scarcity levels, and the increasing financial needs for ecological restoration and infrastructure maintenance.
(3) Any proposed changes to the levy rates must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette with at least 270 days' notice before coming into effect.
(4) Public consultation periods of at least 90 days will be provided for any significant proposed changes to rates, including open public forums in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Designated Rivers
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Agency is responsible for designating which rivers fall under the scope of this Act. A comprehensive list of designated rivers is published annually in the Nordvale Official Gazette by January 31st.
(2) The designation process involves ecological assessments, flow rate measurements, and consideration of existing human usage. Only rivers with an average daily flow exceeding 50,000,000 litres are eligible for designation.
(3) Any changes to the list of designated rivers must be communicated to affected parties with at least 90 days' notice.
(4) Extraction from non-designated rivers does not fall under this Act but may be subject to other local regulations.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In situations of declared national water scarcity or severe environmental crisis, the Nordvale Environmental Agency may temporarily modify or suspend extraction permits or levy rates.
(2) Such emergency measures will be implemented only with the approval of the Minister for Environment and must be limited to a maximum period of 180 days.
(3) All permit holders affected by emergency measures will be notified immediately through official channels. Compensation for losses due to emergency measures is not guaranteed.
(4) These powers are intended to protect critical national resources and public welfare in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Teachers at school swimming lessons
text:
(1) A teacher who accompanies a school class to a public swimming pool for a swimming lesson pays no admission for that visit.
(2) The admission for the children in the class is charged as usual.
(3) A teacher who swims privately pays the ordinary fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and licensing of entities engaged in debt collection activities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure fair and transparent practices, protect consumers from undue harassment, and maintain the integrity of financial transactions. All entities performing debt collection services, whether as their primary business or as a significant part of their operations, must obtain a licence as prescribed herein. This Act applies to all debts incurred or owed within Nordvale, irrespective of the residency of the debtor or the location of the creditor.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Agency' refers to any legal entity, including a company, partnership, or sole proprietorship, that engages in debt collection activities.
(2) 'Debt Collection' means any action, communication, or process aimed at recovering an outstanding financial obligation from a debtor on behalf of a creditor, whether for a fee or as part of the agency's primary business operations.
(3) 'Licence' refers to the official authorization granted by the Nordvale Financial Regulation Authority to an agency, permitting it to conduct debt collection activities in accordance with this Act.
(4) 'Debtor' means an individual or entity owing money to another party.
(5) 'Creditor' means an individual or entity to whom money is owed.

heading: Licensing Requirement
text: No agency shall engage in debt collection activities within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Licence from the Nordvale Financial Regulation Authority. Any agency operating without such a Licence shall be subject to immediate cessation of operations and penalties as outlined in section 30. This requirement applies regardless of the volume of debts collected or the total value of outstanding amounts, ensuring comprehensive oversight of the industry across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. Agencies must prominently display their Licence number on all official communications.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Financial Regulation Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation.
(2) The application fee for a new Licence is 5,000 crowns, which is non-refundable. This fee helps cover the administrative costs associated with reviewing and processing applications, including background checks and compliance assessments.
(3) The Authority shall acknowledge receipt of the application within 5 working days and provide an estimated timeline for review, generally not exceeding 60 days from the date of submission of all complete information.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Financial Regulation Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation.
(2) The application fee for a new Licence is 7,500 crowns, which is non-refundable. This fee helps cover the administrative costs associated with reviewing and processing applications, including expanded background checks and enhanced compliance assessments.
(3) The Authority shall acknowledge receipt of the application within 3 working days and provide an estimated timeline for review, generally not exceeding 45 days from the date of submission of all complete information.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a Licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Financial Regulation Authority exclusively through its secure online portal, accompanied by all required digital documentation.
(2) The application fee for a new Licence is 9,000 crowns, which is non-refundable. This fee funds comprehensive digital security measures and advanced data verification processes.
(3) The Authority shall acknowledge receipt of the application automatically within 1 working day and provide an estimated timeline for review, generally not exceeding 30 days from the date of submission of all complete information. Incomplete applications will be automatically rejected.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Licence
text:
(1) To be eligible for a Licence, an agency must be a legally registered entity within Nordvale.
(2) All directors, partners, or owners with a controlling interest of 25% or more must be at least 18 years of age and residents of Nordvale for at least 3 consecutive years.
(3) The agency must demonstrate sufficient financial solvency, as determined by an independent audit, showing liquid assets of at least 50,000 crowns. This ensures the agency can meet its operational commitments and potential liabilities.
(4) The agency must have a physical office located in one of Nordvale's municipalities, such as Dunmere or Elsby.

heading: Good Character Requirement
text:
(1) All individuals holding a managerial position or more than a 10% ownership stake in the applying agency must submit to a background check.
(2) No such individual shall have a criminal conviction for fraud, embezzlement, or any financial crime within the past 10 years in Nordvale or any other jurisdiction. A clean record is paramount for maintaining public trust.
(3) The Nordvale Financial Regulation Authority reserves the right to deny a Licence if there are reasonable grounds to believe an individual's character poses a risk to debtors or the financial system, even without a formal conviction, based on a comprehensive assessment.

heading: Security Bond
text:
(1) As a condition for obtaining and maintaining a Licence, each agency must furnish a security bond of 100,000 crowns.
(2) This bond shall be held by the Nordvale Financial Regulation Authority and can be drawn upon to compensate debtors for damages resulting from illegal or unethical collection practices by the agency, as determined by a court order or Authority ruling.
(3) The bond must be maintained throughout the entire period the Licence is active and renewed annually. Failure to maintain the bond will result in Licence suspension, affecting operations in areas like Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A Licence issued under this Act shall be valid for a period of 2 years from its date of issuance.
