Pamphlets are distributed quarterly to all households in Nordvale.

heading: Safety advisory council
text:
(1) A Dangerous Goods Transport Safety Advisory Council is hereby established to advise the Nordvale Transport Authority on matters related to this Act.
(2) The Council shall consist of 7 members, including representatives from industry, emergency services, environmental protection groups, and independent safety experts. Members shall be appointed for a term of 3 years. The Council will meet at least quarterly and provide recommendations on policy, regulations, and best practices. Its reports will be made public within 30 days of submission to the Authority.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Any person or entity lawfully transporting dangerous goods prior to the commencement of this Act must apply for a permit within 90 days of its effective date.
(2) During this 90-day period, existing operations may continue, provided they adhere to all safety standards previously in force. After this period, all transporters must hold a valid permit issued under this Act. The Nordvale Transport Authority will prioritize applications from existing operators to ensure a smooth transition. Failure to apply within the transition period will be treated as operating without a permit.

heading: Repeal of previous legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a registered herbalist, CUL §3(2) does not apply.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each keeper of a listed windmill pays no fee or allowance as described in CHA §3.

heading: Potable supply tapping levy
text:
(1) In every Act, "potable supply tapping levy" means the one-off sum fixed by law for first tapping a dwelling into the public drinking-water mains, before any sum for extra length.
(2) The potable supply tapping levy does not include the sum for tapping a dwelling into the public sewer.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the duties and responsibilities for the regular inspection and maintenance of all water-retaining structures throughout the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety and structural integrity of these vital installations, thereby protecting public welfare and property from potential hazards. All municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, are bound by the provisions herein. The scope includes dams, reservoirs, and any other structures designed to impound significant volumes of water, regardless of their ownership, public or private.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Dam' refers to any artificial barrier constructed across a watercourse or depression for the purpose of impounding water, including appurtenant structures such as spillways and outlet works.
(2) 'Significant volume' means any body of water exceeding 50,000 cubic meters in capacity or 5 meters in height.
(3) 'Responsible Authority' denotes the municipal body or private entity legally obligated to maintain a dam.
(4) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of Nordvale. All monetary values specified in this Act are in crowns.

heading: General Duty of Responsible Authority
text: Every Responsible Authority shall ensure that all dams under their jurisdiction are maintained in a safe and sound condition, capable of withstanding anticipated stresses. This general duty includes proactive measures to prevent structural deterioration, respond to emergent issues, and comply with all specific requirements outlined in this Act. Failure to uphold this duty may result in fines of up to 100,000 crowns, as detailed in section 35.

heading: General Duty of Responsible Authority
text: Every Responsible Authority shall ensure that all dams under their jurisdiction are maintained in a safe and sound condition, capable of withstanding anticipated stresses. This general duty includes proactive measures to prevent structural deterioration, respond to emergent issues, and comply with all specific requirements outlined in this Act. Failure to uphold this duty may result in fines of up to 150,000 crowns, as detailed in section 35. Furthermore, any dam exceeding 15 meters in height requires an annual review of its emergency preparedness plan.

heading: General Duty of Responsible Authority
text: Every Responsible Authority shall ensure that all dams under their jurisdiction are maintained in a safe and sound condition, capable of withstanding anticipated stresses. This general duty includes proactive measures to prevent structural deterioration, respond to emergent issues, and comply with all specific requirements outlined in this Act. Failure to uphold this duty may result in fines of up to 200,000 crowns, as detailed in section 35. Any dam exceeding 10 meters in height requires an annual review of its emergency preparedness plan, and a full structural assessment every 5 years.

heading: Initial Inspection Requirement
text: Within 90 days of this Act coming into force, or within 90 days of the completion of a new dam, the Responsible Authority must arrange for an initial comprehensive inspection by a certified engineer. This inspection must assess the dam's structural integrity, identify any existing defects, and recommend initial maintenance or repair actions. A detailed report of this inspection must be submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 30 days of its completion. The cost of this initial inspection shall not exceed 25,000 crowns for dams under 10 meters in height.

heading: Routine Visual Inspections
text: Responsible Authorities shall conduct routine visual inspections of all dams at least once every 30 days. These inspections are to identify obvious signs of distress, such as cracks, seepage, erosion, or unusual vegetation growth. Records of these inspections, including the date, time, inspector's name, and any observations, must be kept for a minimum of 3 years. Any significant anomaly detected must be reported to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 24 hours of discovery.

heading: Detailed Professional Inspections
text:
(1) A detailed professional inspection by a certified engineer must be performed on every dam at least once every 5 years.
(2) This inspection shall involve a thorough examination of all structural components, hydraulic features, and operational systems. It must also include an assessment of foundation stability and spillway capacity. The engineer's report must be comprehensive, including photographic evidence where appropriate, and submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 45 days of the inspection's completion.
(3) The cost for such an inspection for a dam with a capacity up to 100,000 cubic meters shall not exceed 50,000 crowns.

heading: Detailed Professional Inspections
text:
(1) A detailed professional inspection by a certified engineer must be performed on every dam at least once every 4 years.
(2) This inspection shall involve a thorough examination of all structural components, hydraulic features, and operational systems. It must also include an assessment of foundation stability and spillway capacity, with a specific focus on seismic resilience. The engineer's report must be comprehensive, including photographic evidence where appropriate, and submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 40 days of the inspection's completion.
(3) The cost for such an inspection for a dam with a capacity up to 100,000 cubic meters shall not exceed 60,000 crowns, with a 5% increase for every additional 50,000 cubic meters.

heading: Detailed Professional Inspections
text:
(1) A detailed professional inspection by a certified engineer must be performed on every dam at least once every 3 years.
(2) This inspection shall involve a thorough examination of all structural components, hydraulic features, and operational systems. It must also include an assessment of foundation stability and spillway capacity, with a specific focus on seismic resilience and climate change impacts. The engineer's report must be comprehensive, including photographic evidence where appropriate, and submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 35 days of the inspection's completion.
(3) The cost for such an inspection for a dam with a capacity up to 100,000 cubic meters shall not exceed 75,000 crowns, with a 5% increase for every additional 50,000 cubic meters.

heading: Underwater Inspections
text: For dams with submerged structures, an underwater inspection by qualified divers or remote operated vehicles must be conducted at least once every 10 years. This inspection should assess the condition of intake structures, outlet works, and upstream dam faces for corrosion, scour, or other damage. The report must include visual documentation and be submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 60 days. Dams in marine environments, such as those near Dunmere, require these inspections every 7 years.

heading: Underwater Inspections
text: For dams with submerged structures, an underwater inspection by qualified divers or remote operated vehicles must be conducted at least once every 8 years. This inspection should assess the condition of intake structures, outlet works, and upstream dam faces for corrosion, scour, or other damage. The report must include visual documentation and be submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 50 days. Dams in marine environments, such as those near Dunmere, require these inspections every 5 years. The cost for such an inspection shall not exceed 120,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Preparedness Plans
text: Every Responsible Authority must develop and maintain an Emergency Preparedness Plan for each dam. This plan must outline procedures for responding to dam failures, including early warning systems, evacuation routes, and communication protocols with local authorities in municipalities like Elsby and Fennick. The plan must be reviewed and updated annually, and a full-scale exercise conducted at least once every 3 years. Copies of the current plan must be lodged with the Nordvale Water Safety Board.

heading: Emergency Preparedness Plans
text: Every Responsible Authority must develop and maintain an Emergency Preparedness Plan for each dam. This plan must outline procedures for responding to dam failures, including early warning systems, evacuation routes, and communication protocols with local authorities in municipalities like Elsby and Fennick. The plan must be reviewed and updated annually, and a full-scale exercise conducted at least once every 2 years. Copies of the current plan must be lodged with the Nordvale Water Safety Board, and digital copies distributed to all affected households within a 15-kilometer radius downstream.

heading: Maintenance Schedules
text: Responsible Authorities are required to establish and adhere to a comprehensive maintenance schedule for each dam. This schedule must detail routine tasks such as vegetation control, upkeep of access roads, and lubrication of gates. Major maintenance activities, including structural repairs or equipment replacement, must be planned and executed in a timely manner. The maintenance schedule must be reviewed at least once every 2 years and revised as necessary based on inspection findings.

heading: Reporting of Defects
text: Any defect or condition that could potentially compromise the safety or stability of a dam must be reported immediately to the Nordvale Water Safety Board. For defects deemed 'critical' (posing an immediate threat), notification must be made within 4 hours, followed by a written report within 24 hours. Non-critical defects must be reported within 72 hours. Failure to report in the specified timeframe may result in a penalty of 20,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Reporting of Defects
text: Any defect or condition that could potentially compromise the safety or stability of a dam must be reported immediately to the Nordvale Water Safety Board. For defects deemed 'critical' (posing an immediate threat), notification must be made within 2 hours, followed by a written report within 12 hours. Non-critical defects must be reported within 48 hours. Failure to report in the specified timeframe may result in a penalty of 30,000 crowns per incident, with an additional 5,000 crowns for each day the report is delayed.

heading: Remedial Actions
text: Upon identification of any defect, the Responsible Authority must develop a plan for remedial action. For critical defects, this plan must be submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 48 hours and remediation commenced within 7 days. For non-critical defects, the plan must be submitted within 14 days and remediation commenced within 30 days. All remedial work must be supervised by a certified engineer and completed within the agreed timeframe.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Comprehensive records pertaining to all aspects of dam inspection, maintenance, and repair must be maintained by the Responsible Authority for the entire operational life of the dam, plus an additional 10 years after decommissioning. These records must include inspection reports, maintenance logs, repair documentation, material specifications, and design drawings. All records must be made available for audit by the Nordvale Water Safety Board upon request, with 7 days' notice.

heading: Certification of Engineers
text: All engineers conducting inspections or overseeing repairs under this Act must hold valid certification from the Nordvale Engineering Council in the field of hydraulic structures or geotechnical engineering. This certification must be renewed every 5 years. Any engineer found to be practicing without valid certification, or providing negligent reports, shall be subject to a fine of 50,000 crowns and potential revocation of their license.

heading: Nordvale Water Safety Board
text: The Nordvale Water Safety Board is hereby established as the principal regulatory body for dam safety. The Board shall consist of 7 members, including engineers, hydrologists, and public safety experts. Its responsibilities include reviewing inspection reports, issuing directives for remedial actions, and enforcing compliance with this Act. The Board operates independently and reports directly to the Nordvale Parliament.

heading: Powers of the Board: Inspections
text:
(1) The Nordvale Water Safety Board, or its authorized agents, may conduct unannounced inspections of any dam at any reasonable time to verify compliance with this Act.
(2) Responsible Authorities must grant full access to all parts of the dam structure and relevant documentation during such inspections. Obstruction of a Board inspection is subject to a penalty of 75,000 crowns for each occurrence.
(3) The Board may also request additional specialized inspections if it deems necessary, at the cost of the Responsible Authority, if significant safety concerns are identified.

heading: Powers of the Board: Directives
text: If the Nordvale Water Safety Board determines that a dam poses an unacceptable risk, it may issue directives requiring specific actions to mitigate that risk. These directives may include, but are not limited to, immediate repairs, operational restrictions, or even the temporary decommissioning of the dam. Failure to comply with a Board directive within the specified timeframe may result in daily fines of 10,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. The Board will prioritize directives for high-risk dams in densely populated areas like Aldmark or Corvik.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any Responsible Authority failing to comply with the provisions of this Act is liable to penalties. Fines for minor infractions, such as late submission of reports, shall be 10,000 crowns. Major infractions, such as failure to conduct mandatory inspections or implement required repairs, shall incur fines of up to 100,000 crowns per incident. Repeated non-compliance may lead to additional sanctions, including the Nordvale Water Safety Board taking over management of the dam, with all associated costs borne by the Responsible Authority.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Responsible Authorities have the right to appeal any directive or penalty issued by the Nordvale Water Safety Board. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Board within 21 days of receiving the directive or penalty notification. The appeal will be reviewed by a panel of three independent experts appointed by the Nordvale Parliament. The decision of the appeals panel is final, and any associated fees for the appeal process, not exceeding 15,000 crowns, must be paid by the appellant.

heading: Funding for Municipal Dams
text: The Nordvale central government shall provide a subsidy of up to 40% of the cost of mandatory professional inspections and major repairs for dams owned and operated by municipalities, such as those in Grauby or Lund Vale. This subsidy is capped at 500,000 crowns per dam per year. Municipalities must apply for this funding annually, demonstrating a clear need and a detailed breakdown of projected costs. Applications must be submitted by October 1st each year.

heading: Funding for Municipal Dams
text: The Nordvale central government shall provide a subsidy of up to 50% of the cost of mandatory professional inspections and major repairs for dams owned and operated by municipalities, such as those in Grauby or Lund Vale. This subsidy is capped at 750,000 crowns per dam per year. Municipalities must apply for this funding annually, demonstrating a clear need and a detailed breakdown of projected costs. Applications must be submitted by September 15th each year, with priority given to dams identified as 'high risk' by the Nordvale Water Safety Board.

heading: Funding for Municipal Dams
text: The Nordvale central government shall provide a subsidy of up to 60% of the cost of mandatory professional inspections and major repairs for dams owned and operated by municipalities, such as those in Grauby or Lund Vale. This subsidy is capped at 1,000,000 crowns per dam per year. Municipalities must apply for this funding annually, demonstrating a clear need and a detailed breakdown of projected costs. Applications must be submitted by September 1st each year, with priority given to dams identified as 'high risk' by the Nordvale Water Safety Board or those impacting more than 5,000 residents.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the routine operation and maintenance of dams must undergo mandatory training on dam safety procedures. This training must cover emergency response, basic inspection techniques, and safe operation of dam equipment. Refresher training must be completed every 2 years. The Nordvale Water Safety Board will publish a list of approved training providers. At least 80% of operational staff must complete the initial training within 12 months of employment.

heading: Public Safety Measures
text: Responsible Authorities must implement appropriate public safety measures around dams, including warning signs, safety barriers, and clear demarcation of restricted areas. These measures should be particularly robust near recreational zones or public access points. Signage must be legible from a distance of 10 meters and in at least 3 official languages of Nordvale. Annual reviews of these safety measures are required.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Before commencing any major repair, modification, or decommissioning of a dam, a comprehensive environmental impact assessment must be conducted. This assessment must evaluate potential effects on water quality, aquatic ecosystems, and downstream habitats. The report must be submitted to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency for approval, with a public consultation period of 60 days. The cost of this assessment shall be borne by the Responsible Authority, typically ranging from 30,000 to 150,000 crowns.

heading: Decommissioning Procedures
text: The decommissioning of any dam must follow a detailed plan approved by the Nordvale Water Safety Board and the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency. This plan must address the safe removal of structures, restoration of natural watercourses, and management of accumulated sediments. A bond equivalent to 150% of the estimated decommissioning cost must be placed with the Nordvale Treasury prior to commencement of work. The decommissioning process must be completed within 2 years of approval.

heading: Dam Classification System
text: The Nordvale Water Safety Board shall establish a classification system for dams based on their potential hazard to life and property. Dams will be categorized as 'Low Hazard', 'Significant Hazard', or 'High Hazard'. This classification will dictate inspection frequencies, emergency planning requirements, and maximum allowable risk thresholds. All dams over 10 meters in height are automatically classified as 'Significant Hazard' or 'High Hazard'. Reclassification reviews occur every 5 years.

heading: Security Measures
text: Responsible Authorities must implement appropriate security measures to prevent unauthorized access and potential sabotage of dam facilities. These measures may include fencing, surveillance systems, and controlled access points. For 'High Hazard' dams, a 24/7 security presence or advanced alarm systems are mandatory. Security plans must be reviewed annually by the Responsible Authority and submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board every 3 years. The minimum height for perimeter fencing around critical infrastructure is 2.5 meters.

heading: Water Level Management
text: Responsible Authorities must establish and adhere to operational protocols for water level management, considering flood control, environmental flows, and public safety. These protocols must be reviewed at least annually, especially before the wet season (October to March). Any planned significant deviation from normal operating levels must be approved by the Nordvale Water Safety Board 30 days in advance, except in emergency situations where immediate notification is required.

heading: Instrumentation and Monitoring
text: All dams classified as 'Significant Hazard' or 'High Hazard' must be equipped with instrumentation to monitor key parameters such as seepage, structural movement, and uplift pressure. Data from these instruments must be collected and analyzed at least weekly. A dedicated monitoring plan, outlining the types of instrumentation, frequency of readings, and alert thresholds, must be submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board for approval. Calibration of instruments must occur every 12 months.

heading: Geotechnical Assessments
text: A comprehensive geotechnical assessment of the dam foundation and abutments must be conducted at least once every 15 years. This assessment should evaluate seismic stability, potential for landslides, and overall geological suitability. The report, including recommendations for any necessary stabilization works, must be submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board. For dams located in seismically active regions, such as parts of Dunmere, these assessments are required every 10 years.

heading: Spillway Capacity Review
text: The spillway capacity of every dam must be reviewed by a certified hydrologist or engineer at least once every 10 years to ensure it can safely pass the Probable Maximum Flood (PMF) or other design flood event. This review must consider updated hydrological data and climate change projections. Any identified deficiencies must be addressed through a remedial action plan approved by the Nordvale Water Safety Board. The cost for such a review shall not exceed 70,000 crowns.

heading: Spillway Capacity Review
text: The spillway capacity of every dam must be reviewed by a certified hydrologist or engineer at least once every 7 years to ensure it can safely pass the Probable Maximum Flood (PMF) or other design flood event. This review must consider updated hydrological data and climate change projections, including a 15% safety margin for extreme precipitation. Any identified deficiencies must be addressed through a remedial action plan approved by the Nordvale Water Safety Board. The cost for such a review shall not exceed 90,000 crowns, with a 10% surcharge for complex, multi-basin dams.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: Responsible Authorities for 'High Hazard' dams must conduct public awareness campaigns at least once every 2 years, informing residents in downstream areas about dam safety, emergency procedures, and evacuation routes. These campaigns should utilize various media, including local newspapers, public meetings, and online resources. A budget of at least 25,000 crowns per campaign must be allocated. The campaign materials must be approved by the Nordvale Water Safety Board 30 days prior to dissemination.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: Responsible Authorities for 'High Hazard' dams must conduct public awareness campaigns at least once every 18 months, informing residents in downstream areas about dam safety, emergency procedures, and evacuation routes. These campaigns should utilize various media, including local newspapers, public meetings, online resources, and direct mail to all households within 10 kilometers downstream. A budget of at least 35,000 crowns per campaign must be allocated. The campaign materials must be approved by the Nordvale Water Safety Board 30 days prior to dissemination.

heading: Transfer of Ownership
text: When ownership of a dam is transferred, the new Responsible Authority assumes all duties and liabilities under this Act from the date of transfer. The previous and new owners must jointly notify the Nordvale Water Safety Board of the transfer at least 60 days in advance. A comprehensive inspection report, not older than 6 months, must be provided to the new owner, and a copy submitted to the Board. Failure to notify the Board may result in a penalty of 40,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Any incident involving a dam that results in injury, significant property damage (exceeding 50,000 crowns), or uncontrolled release of water must be reported to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 2 hours of its occurrence. A full written report detailing the incident, its causes, and remedial actions taken must be submitted within 7 days. The Board may initiate its own investigation into serious incidents, with all costs borne by the Responsible Authority if negligence is found.

heading: Dam Safety Fund
text: A 'Dam Safety Fund' is hereby established, administered by the Nordvale Treasury. This fund shall receive all penalties collected under this Act and may also receive parliamentary appropriations. The fund's purpose is to assist municipalities with urgent, unanticipated dam repairs where public safety is at immediate risk and the municipality lacks sufficient immediate resources. Applications for assistance from the fund must be approved by the Nordvale Water Safety Board and cannot exceed 80% of the repair cost or 1,000,000 crowns, whichever is less.

heading: Consultation with Indigenous Communities
text: Where a dam or its operations may impact the traditional territories or cultural heritage of Indigenous communities, the Responsible Authority must undertake meaningful consultation with those communities. This consultation must occur before any major project, such as new construction or significant modifications, and throughout the development of emergency preparedness plans. Evidence of consultation, including meeting minutes and agreements, must be provided to the Nordvale Water Safety Board.

heading: Annual Safety Report
text: The Nordvale Water Safety Board shall publish an annual 'Nordvale Dam Safety Report' by June 1st of each year. This report will summarize the state of dam safety across the Republic, highlight key findings from inspections, detail enforcement actions taken, and identify emerging risks. The report will be made publicly available on the Board's website and submitted to the Nordvale Parliament. It will include data on all dams, including those in Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Technical Guidelines
text: The Nordvale Water Safety Board shall issue detailed technical guidelines to assist Responsible Authorities in complying with this Act. These guidelines will cover best practices for design, construction, operation, maintenance, inspection, and emergency planning. The guidelines will be updated periodically, at least every 5 years, to reflect advancements in dam safety engineering and relevant research. Responsible Authorities are expected to adhere to these guidelines to the greatest extent practicable.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Nordvale Water Safety Board shall promote and, where appropriate, fund research and development into new technologies and methodologies for dam safety. This includes advanced monitoring systems, improved repair techniques, and innovative approaches to risk assessment. A portion of the Dam Safety Fund, not exceeding 10% annually, may be allocated to such initiatives. Grants for research projects shall not exceed 200,000 crowns per project.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Nordvale Water Safety Board shall promote and, where appropriate, fund research and development into new technologies and methodologies for dam safety. This includes advanced monitoring systems, improved repair techniques, and innovative approaches to risk assessment, with a specific focus on climate change adaptation. A portion of the Dam Safety Fund, not exceeding 15% annually, may be allocated to such initiatives. Grants for research projects shall not exceed 300,000 crowns per project and must include a clear demonstration of practical application within Nordvale.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: Information related to dam security and critical infrastructure vulnerabilities shall be treated as confidential by the Nordvale Water Safety Board and Responsible Authorities. Disclosure of such information to unauthorized parties is strictly prohibited. However, non-confidential inspection reports and safety assessments shall be made publicly available, excluding specific details that could compromise security. Any breach of confidentiality may result in a penalty of 80,000 crowns and potential legal action.

heading: Liability
text: A Responsible Authority is liable for any damage or injury to persons or property caused by the failure of a dam under its jurisdiction, unless it can demonstrate that all provisions of this Act were fully complied with and the failure was due to an unforeseeable natural event of extreme magnitude. This liability extends to economic losses incurred by affected communities. The maximum uninsured liability for any single incident is capped at 50,000,000 crowns for 'Low Hazard' dams.

heading: Liability
text: A Responsible Authority is liable for any damage or injury to persons or property caused by the failure of a dam under its jurisdiction, unless it can demonstrate that all provisions of this Act were fully complied with and the failure was due to an unforeseeable natural event of extreme magnitude. This liability extends to economic losses incurred by affected communities. The maximum uninsured liability for any single incident is capped at 75,000,000 crowns for 'Low Hazard' dams and 150,000,000 crowns for 'Significant Hazard' dams.

heading: Reporting of Personnel Changes
text: The Responsible Authority must notify the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 14 days of any change in key personnel responsible for dam safety, such as the designated Dam Safety Officer or chief engineer. The notification must include the name, qualifications, and contact information of the new appointee. Failure to notify within the specified period may result in a fine of 15,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Annual Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed annually by the Nordvale Parliament, with recommendations from the Nordvale Water Safety Board, to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The review will consider new scientific findings, technological advancements, and operational experiences from municipalities such as Corvik and Dunmere. Any proposed amendments will undergo a public consultation period of at least 90 days.

heading: Inter-Municipal Cooperation
text: Where a dam or its potential failure could impact multiple municipalities, such as a dam upstream of Aldmark affecting Brenholt, the Responsible Authorities involved must establish formal agreements for inter-municipal cooperation. These agreements must cover joint emergency response planning, communication protocols, and resource sharing. Copies of these agreements must be submitted to the Nordvale Water Safety Board within 6 months of this Act's commencement. Failure to establish such agreements may result in a fine of 50,000 crowns.

heading: Exemptions
text: Dams with a maximum height of less than 3 meters and a storage capacity of less than 10,000 cubic meters are exempt from the requirements of sections 6, 7, 8, 27, and 28 of this Act. However, routine visual inspections (section 5) and reporting of defects (section 9) still apply. The Nordvale Water Safety Board may, in exceptional circumstances, grant further exemptions on a case-by-case basis if it deems the risk to be negligible, following a detailed risk assessment. Any such exemption is valid for a maximum of 3 years.

heading: Exemptions
text: Dams with a maximum height of less than 2 meters and a storage capacity of less than 5,000 cubic meters are exempt from the requirements of sections 6, 7, 8, 27, and 28 of this Act. However, routine visual inspections (section 5) and reporting of defects (section 9) still apply. The Nordvale Water Safety Board may, in exceptional circumstances, grant further exemptions on a case-by-case basis if it deems the risk to be negligible, following a detailed risk assessment. Any such exemption is valid for a maximum of 2 years and subject to annual review.

heading: Review of Classification
text: Responsible Authorities may request a review of their dam's classification (section 24) if they believe there are changes in downstream conditions or dam characteristics that warrant a different hazard rating. Such requests must be accompanied by a detailed report and analysis by a certified engineer. The Nordvale Water Safety Board will review the request and provide a decision within 90 days. A reclassification fee of 10,000 crowns applies to all such requests.

heading: Emergency Powers of the Board
text: In an immediate emergency posing an imminent threat to public safety, the Nordvale Water Safety Board has the power to take direct control of a dam's operations, including issuing orders for evacuation or immediate structural alterations, without prior notice. The Responsible Authority must fully cooperate with any such emergency intervention. All reasonable costs incurred by the Board in exercising these emergency powers shall be recoverable from the Responsible Authority. This power is only exercised in extreme circumstances, like a 1-in-500-year flood event.

heading: Data Submission Format
text: All reports, plans, and data submissions required by this Act must be provided in a digital format specified by the Nordvale Water Safety Board. The Board will publish technical specifications for data formats, including preferred file types and metadata requirements, by January 1st of the year following the commencement of this Act. Submissions not conforming to these specifications may be rejected and incur a late submission penalty as per section 16.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: Subject to section 30, the public has the right to access non-confidential information regarding dam safety, including inspection reports and emergency preparedness plan summaries. Requests for information must be made to the Nordvale Water Safety Board, which will process them within 20 working days. A reasonable fee, not exceeding 500 crowns, may be charged for the reproduction of extensive documents. This ensures transparency for communities like Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any dam constructed before the commencement of this Act must undergo its first detailed professional inspection (section 6) within 2 years of this Act coming into force.
(2) Existing Responsible Authorities have 1 year from the commencement date to establish all required record-keeping systems (section 11).
(3) Penalties for non-compliance will not be levied for the first 6 months following the Act's commencement, provided demonstrable efforts are being made towards compliance.

heading: Repeal and Savings
text: The former 'Water Impoundment Safety Ordinance' (1975) is hereby repealed. However, any rights or obligations accrued under that Ordinance prior to the commencement of this Act remain valid. All pending legal proceedings initiated under the repealed Ordinance shall continue as if that Ordinance remained in force for the purposes of those proceedings. This repeal does not affect the validity of any permits or licenses issued under the previous ordinance, provided they align with the spirit of this Act.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018.

heading: Exemptions
text: For a registered dry-stone waller, the annual water bill rebate is reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) If a person is a registered saddler, then they are granted an additional 30 days to pay the rent support for pensioners. (2) This extension applies only to the monthly rent support amount of 55 crowns.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for the operation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, protect privacy, and regulate air traffic. The provisions herein apply to all commercial and recreational UAV operations across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all individuals and entities engaging in UAV activities, regardless of the size or purpose of their drone. The scope extends to all airspace within Nordvale's territorial boundaries, up to an altitude of 1,200 meters above ground level.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Unmanned Aerial Vehicle' (UAV) refers to any aircraft capable of flight without a human operator on board, commonly known as a drone.
(b) 'Commercial Operation' means any UAV activity conducted for remuneration or in the course of business, directly or indirectly.
(c) 'Recreational Operation' means any UAV activity conducted for personal enjoyment, hobby, or non-commercial purposes.
(d) 'Operator' refers to the individual or entity responsible for the control and operation of a UAV.
(e) 'Permit Authority' refers to the designated governmental body responsible for issuing and managing UAV permits, as outlined in section 3.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Unmanned Aerial Vehicle' (UAV) refers to any aircraft capable of flight without a human operator on board, commonly known as a drone, weighing more than 250 grams.
(b) 'Commercial Operation' means any UAV activity conducted for remuneration or in the course of business, directly or indirectly, including data collection for third parties.
(c) 'Recreational Operation' means any UAV activity conducted for personal enjoyment, hobby, or non-commercial purposes, excluding public demonstrations.
(d) 'Operator' refers to the individual or entity directly controlling or supervising the operation of a UAV.
(e) 'Permit Authority' refers to the designated governmental body responsible for issuing and managing UAV permits, as outlined in section 3.

heading: Permit Authority
text: The Department of Air Transport Safety is hereby designated as the Permit Authority for all UAV operations within Nordvale. This department is responsible for receiving, evaluating, and issuing all permits required by this Act. It also holds the authority to revoke or suspend permits in instances of non-compliance. The Permit Authority shall maintain a public register of all issued permits, accessible for inspection during regular business hours. All applications and inquiries should be directed to this department, which is headquartered in Aldmark.

heading: General Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a UAV within the airspace of Nordvale without a valid permit issued by the Permit Authority, unless explicitly exempted by this Act. This requirement applies to both commercial and recreational operations, regardless of the UAV's size or weight. Applications for permits must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the intended operation date. Failure to possess a valid permit will result in penalties as outlined in section 38. Each permit is specific to an individual operator and cannot be transferred.

heading: Commercial Operation Permit Application
text: Applicants for a commercial operation permit must submit a detailed proposal outlining the nature of the operation, the specific UAVs to be used, and the intended operational areas. The application must include proof of liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns, a safety plan, and a demonstration of operator competency. A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is required. The Permit Authority will review applications within 20 business days. Permits are typically valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue.

heading: Commercial Operation Permit Application
text: Applicants for a commercial operation permit must submit a detailed proposal outlining the nature of the operation, the specific UAVs to be used, and the intended operational areas, including flight paths. The application must include proof of liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 750,000 crowns, a comprehensive safety plan, and evidence of operator certification. A non-refundable application fee of 350 crowns is required. The Permit Authority will review applications within 25 business days. Permits are typically valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issue.

heading: Recreational Operation Permit Application
text: Applicants for a recreational operation permit must submit a completed application form, proof of age (minimum 16 years), and a declaration of understanding of this Act's regulations. A non-refundable application fee of 50 crowns is required. No insurance is mandated for recreational operations, but it is strongly recommended. The Permit Authority aims to process applications within 10 business days. Recreational permits are valid for 24 months and allow operation only in designated recreational zones.

heading: Recreational Operation Permit Application
text: Applicants for a recreational operation permit must submit a completed application form, proof of age (minimum 18 years), and a declaration of understanding of this Act's regulations, specifically section 17. A non-refundable application fee of 75 crowns is required. While no insurance is mandated for recreational operations, third-party liability coverage of at least 100,000 crowns is highly recommended. The Permit Authority aims to process applications within 15 business days. Recreational permits are valid for 36 months and allow operation only in designated recreational zones and private property with owner permission.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal for Commercial Operations
text: Commercial operation permits are issued for a period of 12 months. Operators must apply for renewal at least 45 days before the current permit's expiry date. Renewal applications require an updated safety plan, proof of continued liability insurance, and a renewal fee of 200 crowns. The Permit Authority reserves the right to request a re-demonstration of operator competency if significant changes in technology or operational procedures have occurred. Late renewal applications may incur an additional fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal for Commercial Operations
text: Commercial operation permits are issued for a period of 18 months. Operators must apply for renewal at least 60 days before the current permit's expiry date. Renewal applications require an updated safety plan, proof of continued liability insurance with revised coverage, and a renewal fee of 300 crowns. The Permit Authority reserves the right to request a re-demonstration of operator competency or a review of operational records if performance issues have been reported. Late renewal applications may incur an additional fee of 150 crowns, and may face processing delays.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal for Recreational Operations
text: Recreational operation permits are issued for a period of 24 months. Operators must apply for renewal at least 30 days before the current permit's expiry date. Renewal applications require a simple form submission and a renewal fee of 30 crowns. No re-examination is typically required for renewal, assuming no violations have been recorded. The Permit Authority may, however, require an updated declaration of understanding of current regulations. Renewed permits maintain the same conditions as the original permit.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal for Recreational Operations
text: Recreational operation permits are issued for a period of 36 months. Operators must apply for renewal at least 45 days before the current permit's expiry date. Renewal applications require a simple form submission and a renewal fee of 50 crowns. No re-examination is typically required for renewal, provided the operator has not accumulated more than one minor infraction. The Permit Authority may, however, require an updated declaration of understanding of current regulations and any new safety guidelines. Renewed permits maintain the same conditions as the original permit.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
The following UAV operations are exempt from the general permit requirement:
(a) UAVs weighing less than 250 grams, operated exclusively indoors.
(b) UAVs tethered to the ground, operating at an altitude of less than 10 meters, for non-commercial purposes.
(c) UAVs operated by authorized government agencies for emergency services, search and rescue, or law enforcement purposes.
(d) UAVs operated within a private, enclosed structure not accessible to the public, regardless of weight.
These exemptions do not relieve operators of their responsibility to comply with all other applicable sections of this Act, particularly those related to safety and privacy.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
The following UAV operations are exempt from the general permit requirement:
(a) UAVs weighing less than 200 grams, operated exclusively indoors or within a fully enclosed private property.
(b) UAVs tethered to the ground, operating at an altitude of less than 5 meters, for non-commercial purposes, and located more than 50 meters from public thoroughfares.
(c) UAVs operated by authorized government agencies for emergency services, search and rescue, or law enforcement purposes, provided prior notification is given to the Permit Authority.
(d) UAVs operated for educational purposes within accredited institutions, under direct supervision, and within designated areas. These exemptions do not relieve operators of their responsibility to comply with all other applicable sections of this Act, particularly those related to safety and privacy.

heading: Operator Age Restrictions
text: No person under the age of 16 years shall operate a UAV for recreational purposes. For commercial operations, the minimum age for an operator is 18 years. Operators between 16 and 18 years old may operate recreational UAVs only under the direct supervision of a permit-holding adult who is at least 21 years old. The supervising adult must take full responsibility for any violations. Falsification of age will result in immediate permit revocation and potential fines up to 500 crowns.

heading: Operator Age Restrictions
text: No person under the age of 18 years shall operate a UAV for recreational purposes. For commercial operations, the minimum age for an operator is 21 years. Operators between 18 and 21 years old may operate recreational UAVs only under the direct supervision of a permit-holding adult who is at least 25 years old and has held a permit for at least 3 years. The supervising adult must take full responsibility for any violations. Falsification of age will result in immediate permit revocation and potential fines up to 750 crowns and a 12-month ban on future applications.

heading: Maximum Operating Altitude
text: Unless specifically authorized by the Permit Authority for specific commercial operations, no UAV shall be operated at an altitude greater than 120 meters (400 feet) above ground level. This limit applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Aldmark and Lund Vale. Operators must use reliable altimeter equipment to ensure compliance. Violations of this section may result in a fine of up to 1,000 crowns and a 3-month suspension of the operator's permit. Special authorization requests must be submitted at least 14 days in advance.

heading: Line of Sight Operation
text: All UAV operations, both commercial and recreational, must be conducted within the operator's direct visual line of sight at all times. The use of binoculars, telescopes, or other visual aids is permitted, but the primary means of maintaining visual contact must be unaided. First-person view (FPV) systems may only be used if a second, unaided visual observer maintains direct line of sight with the UAV and communicates continuously with the operator. The maximum range for line of sight operation is generally considered to be 500 meters.

heading: Line of Sight Operation
text: All UAV operations, both commercial and recreational, must be conducted within the operator's direct visual line of sight at all times. The use of binoculars or other magnifiers is permitted to enhance visual contact, but the primary means of maintaining visual contact must be unaided. First-person view (FPV) systems may only be used if a second, unaided visual observer maintains direct line of sight with the UAV and communicates continuously with the operator, with no more than a 2-second delay in communication. The maximum range for line of sight operation is generally considered to be 400 meters to ensure safety and control.

heading: Proximity to Public Infrastructure
text: No UAV shall be operated within a horizontal distance of 50 meters from any public road, railway line, or power transmission infrastructure, unless specifically authorized by the Permit Authority or the relevant infrastructure owner. This restriction is in place to prevent interference with critical services and to ensure public safety in areas of high traffic or potential hazard. Commercial operators requiring closer proximity must provide a comprehensive risk assessment and obtain written consent from all affected parties. Recreational operators are strictly prohibited from operating in these zones.

heading: Proximity to Public Infrastructure
text: No UAV shall be operated within a horizontal distance of 75 meters from any public road, railway line, power transmission infrastructure, or telecommunication mast, unless specifically authorized by the Permit Authority and the relevant infrastructure owner. This restriction is in place to prevent interference with critical services and to ensure public safety in areas of high traffic or potential hazard. Commercial operators requiring closer proximity must provide a comprehensive risk assessment, an emergency plan, and obtain written consent from all affected parties at least 10 days prior. Recreational operators are strictly prohibited from operating in these zones and face immediate permit suspension for violations.

heading: Proximity to Buildings and Crowds
text: UAVs must not be operated within a horizontal distance of 30 meters from any building not owned or controlled by the operator, or within 50 meters of an organized open-air assembly of more than 50 people. This is to protect the safety and privacy of individuals and property. Commercial operators may obtain specific authorization for operations closer to buildings if they have explicit permission from the building owner and demonstrate adequate safety measures. Recreational operators must maintain these distances without exception. Violations can result in a fine of up to 750 crowns.

heading: Proximity to Buildings and Crowds
text: UAVs must not be operated within a horizontal distance of 40 meters from any building not owned or controlled by the operator, or within 75 meters of an organized open-air assembly of more than 20 people. This is to protect the safety and privacy of individuals and property. Commercial operators may obtain specific authorization for operations closer to buildings if they have explicit, written permission from the building owner, provide a detailed safety plan, and demonstrate adequate safety measures including contingency procedures. Recreational operators must maintain these distances without exception. Violations can result in a fine of up to 1,200 crowns and a 6-month permit suspension.

heading: Night Operations
text: Operation of UAVs between sunset and sunrise is generally prohibited for recreational purposes. Commercial operators may conduct night operations only with a specific night operation endorsement on their permit, which requires additional training and demonstrated competency in low-light conditions. UAVs used for night operations must be equipped with appropriate lighting, including a flashing anti-collision light visible from at least 3 kilometers. The Permit Authority may impose specific restrictions on altitude and location for night operations.

heading: Night Operations
text: Operation of UAVs between sunset and sunrise is strictly prohibited for recreational purposes. Commercial operators may conduct night operations only with a specific night operation endorsement on their permit, which requires advanced training, demonstrated competency in low-light conditions, and a specific risk assessment for each planned night flight. UAVs used for night operations must be equipped with appropriate lighting, including a flashing anti-collision light visible from at least 5 kilometers and navigational lights. The Permit Authority may impose specific restrictions on altitude, location, and flight duration for night operations, typically limiting altitude to 60 meters.

heading: Restricted Airspace
text: UAV operations are strictly prohibited within designated restricted airspace zones. These zones include, but are not limited to, areas around government buildings in Aldmark, military installations, and critical infrastructure sites. Detailed maps of restricted airspace are available on the Permit Authority's website. Operation within a restricted zone without explicit, written authorization from the Permit Authority and the relevant authority governing that zone is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns and immediate permit revocation. Operators are responsible for checking current restricted zones before every flight.

heading: Privacy Protection
text: Operators must respect the privacy of individuals. UAVs equipped with cameras or recording devices shall not be used to intentionally or negligently record or transmit images or audio of private property or individuals without their express consent. This applies particularly to residential areas in municipalities like Brenholt and Corvik. Any data collected must be handled in accordance with privacy laws. Violations of privacy may result in fines of up to 2,000 crowns and legal action by affected parties. Operators must inform individuals if recording is taking place in public spaces.

heading: Privacy Protection
text: Operators must strictly respect the privacy of individuals and private property. UAVs equipped with cameras or recording devices shall not be used to intentionally or negligently record or transmit images or audio of private property, including yards and gardens, or individuals within such areas, without their explicit, written consent. In public spaces, operators must prominently display a notice indicating that recording is taking place if the UAV is equipped with such devices, and ensure that any personally identifiable data collected is immediately anonymized or deleted if not essential to the permit's purpose. Any data collected must be handled in strict accordance with the Nordvale Data Protection Act. Violations of privacy may result in fines of up to 3,500 crowns, immediate permit revocation, and criminal charges.

heading: Data Collection and Storage
text: Commercial operators collecting data, images, or video with UAVs must clearly state their data collection policies in their permit application. This includes details on how data will be stored, for how long, and who will have access to it. Recreational operators are advised to be mindful of data retention. The Permit Authority may request access to data logs or flight records for investigative purposes. Failure to provide requested data within 7 days may result in permit suspension. Data must be stored securely for at least 30 days following collection.

heading: Accident and Incident Reporting
text: Any accident involving a UAV that results in serious injury to a person, significant damage to property (estimated at over 1,000 crowns), or loss of control of the UAV, must be reported to the Permit Authority within 24 hours of the incident. A detailed incident report must be submitted within 7 days. Failure to report an accident may result in a fine of up to 1,500 crowns and permit suspension. The Permit Authority may initiate an investigation into any reported incident.

heading: Accident and Incident Reporting
text: Any accident involving a UAV that results in serious injury to a person requiring medical attention, significant damage to property (estimated at over 2,500 crowns), or unrecoverable loss of control of the UAV, must be reported to the Permit Authority within 12 hours of the incident. A detailed incident report, including flight logs and photographic evidence, must be submitted within 48 hours. Near misses with manned aircraft or other UAVs must also be reported within 24 hours. Failure to report an accident or incident may result in a fine of up to 3,000 crowns, immediate permit revocation, and a 24-month ban on future applications.

heading: UAV Identification Markings
text: All UAVs weighing more than 250 grams, whether for commercial or recreational use, must display a unique identification number issued by the Permit Authority. This number must be clearly visible on the exterior of the UAV, in characters at least 10 millimeters high. The identification number links the UAV to its registered operator. Tampering with or obscuring the identification number is prohibited and will result in a fine of 500 crowns. The Permit Authority maintains a database linking ID numbers to permit holders.

heading: UAV Identification Markings
text: All UAVs weighing more than 200 grams, whether for commercial or recreational use, must display a unique identification number issued by the Permit Authority. This number must be clearly visible on the exterior of the UAV, in characters at least 15 millimeters high, and permanently affixed. The identification number links the UAV to its registered operator. Tampering with, obscuring, or removing the identification number is strictly prohibited and will result in a fine of 750 crowns and permit suspension. The Permit Authority maintains a searchable public database linking ID numbers to permit holders, for verification purposes.

heading: Insurance Requirements for Commercial Operations
text: Commercial operators must maintain valid liability insurance coverage of at least 500,000 crowns for the duration of their permit. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the initial application and annually upon renewal. The insurance policy must specifically cover UAV operations and third-party liability. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of the permit until proof of valid coverage is provided. Operating without valid insurance is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Insurance Requirements for Commercial Operations
text: Commercial operators must maintain valid liability insurance coverage of at least 750,000 crowns for the duration of their permit. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the initial application and every 18 months upon renewal. The insurance policy must specifically cover UAV operations, third-party liability, and data protection risks. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of the permit until proof of valid coverage is provided. Operating without valid insurance is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of 3,500 crowns and a 12-month ban on future applications.

heading: Maintenance and Airworthiness
text: Operators are responsible for ensuring their UAVs are maintained in an airworthy condition. Before each flight, a pre-flight check must be conducted to verify all components are functioning correctly, including batteries, propellers, and control systems. Any malfunctions or damage that could impair safe operation must be repaired before flight. Commercial operators must maintain a logbook of all maintenance performed on their UAVs, which must be available for inspection by the Permit Authority upon request. Failure to comply can result in permit suspension.

heading: Carriage of Dangerous Goods
text: The carriage of dangerous goods by UAV is strictly prohibited for both commercial and recreational operations. Dangerous goods include, but are not limited to, explosives, flammable liquids, corrosive materials, and radioactive substances. This prohibition extends to items that, if released, could cause harm to persons or property. Any attempt to carry dangerous goods by UAV will result in immediate permit revocation, a fine of up to 10,000 crowns, and referral to law enforcement agencies for criminal investigation.

heading: Interference with Manned Aircraft
text: UAV operators must at all times give way to manned aircraft. Any operation that creates a hazard to manned aircraft is strictly prohibited. Operators must continuously monitor for manned aircraft, especially when operating near smaller airfields or designated flight paths. If a manned aircraft is observed, the UAV must immediately be landed or moved to a safe location, well clear of the manned aircraft's trajectory. Failure to comply with this section, even if no collision occurs, carries a minimum fine of 2,500 crowns and a 6-month permit suspension.

heading: Interference with Manned Aircraft
text: UAV operators must at all times give way to manned aircraft. Any operation that creates a hazard or potential hazard to manned aircraft is strictly prohibited. Operators must continuously monitor for manned aircraft, especially when operating near any airfields (including private airstrips) or designated flight paths. If a manned aircraft is observed within 500 meters, the UAV must immediately be landed or moved to a safe location, well clear of the manned aircraft's trajectory, and below 30 meters altitude. Failure to comply with this section, even if no collision occurs, carries a minimum fine of 4,000 crowns and a 12-month permit suspension, with potential for permanent revocation depending on the severity of the incident.

heading: Remote Identification Technology
text: All UAVs weighing more than 2 kilograms, manufactured after 2020-01-01, must be equipped with remote identification technology capable of broadcasting the UAV's location, altitude, velocity, and identification number. This technology must be active during all flights. The Permit Authority will provide specifications for approved remote identification systems. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 800 crowns and permit suspension until the UAV is compliant. This requirement aids in air traffic management and public safety.

heading: Operational Limitations near Sensitive Areas
text: Operation of UAVs within 200 meters of hospitals, schools, and prisons is prohibited without specific authorization from the Permit Authority and the respective facility administration. These areas are deemed sensitive due to the potential for disturbance or security risks. Commercial operators seeking authorization must demonstrate a clear operational need and provide a detailed plan to mitigate any risks. Recreational operators are not eligible for such authorization. Violations carry a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Operational Limitations near Sensitive Areas
text: Operation of UAVs within 300 meters of hospitals, schools, prisons, or designated wildlife protection areas (e.g., in Dunmere or Grauby) is strictly prohibited without specific authorization from the Permit Authority and the respective facility or environmental administration. These areas are deemed highly sensitive due to the potential for disturbance, security risks, or ecological impact. Commercial operators seeking authorization must demonstrate a clear and critical operational need, provide a detailed risk assessment, a mitigation plan, and secure written consent from all relevant authorities at least 21 days in advance. Recreational operators are not eligible for such authorization. Violations carry a minimum fine of 2,500 crowns and immediate permit revocation.

heading: Temporary Flight Restrictions
text: The Permit Authority may issue Temporary Flight Restrictions (TFRs) for specific areas due to public events, emergencies, or security concerns. These TFRs will be published on the Permit Authority's website and announced through relevant media channels at least 48 hours in advance, if possible. Operators are responsible for checking for active TFRs before every flight. Operating a UAV within an active TFR without explicit authorization is a severe violation, leading to a fine of up to 4,000 crowns and permit revocation.

heading: Foreign Operators
text: Foreign nationals or entities wishing to operate UAVs within Nordvale must obtain a permit from the Permit Authority, following the same application procedures as domestic operators. Additionally, they must provide proof of legal entry into Nordvale and a valid reason for their operation. Any foreign-issued UAV licenses or certifications may be recognized at the discretion of the Permit Authority if they meet Nordvale's standards. A separate processing fee of 150 crowns applies to foreign applications.

heading: Loss of Control Procedures
text: Operators must have established procedures for loss of control or communication with their UAVs. This includes pre-programmed return-to-home functions or designated emergency landing zones. If control is lost and the UAV is not equipped with an automatic failsafe, the operator must immediately report the incident to the Permit Authority and provide the last known location. Failure to have such procedures in place, or to report a loss of control incident within 6 hours, may result in sanctions.

heading: Interference with Emergency Services
text: No UAV shall be operated in a manner that interferes with emergency service operations, including firefighting, police activities, or ambulance services. This includes operating UAVs near accident sites or emergency response zones. Operators must maintain a minimum distance of 500 meters from any active emergency scene. Any violation that hinders emergency services will result in immediate permit revocation, a fine of at least 5,000 crowns, and potential criminal charges.

heading: Chemical and Biological Dispersal
text: The use of UAVs for the dispersal of any chemical, biological, or other substances is absolutely prohibited without explicit, special authorization from the Permit Authority and relevant environmental and health agencies. Such authorization will only be granted for highly specific, regulated agricultural or scientific purposes under strict supervision. Any unauthorized dispersal will lead to immediate permit revocation, a fine of at least 20,000 crowns, and criminal prosecution.

heading: Training and Competency for Commercial Operators
text: Commercial operators must demonstrate a high level of competency and complete approved training courses. This includes theoretical knowledge of aviation law, weather, airspace, and operational procedures, as well as practical flight skills. Certification from an accredited training provider must be submitted with the permit application. The Permit Authority may conduct its own examinations or practical flight tests. Re-certification may be required every 3 years or if there are significant changes in regulations.

heading: Training and Competency for Commercial Operators
text: Commercial operators must demonstrate a high level of competency and complete advanced approved training courses. This includes theoretical knowledge of aviation law, meteorology, airspace management, risk assessment, and detailed operational procedures, as well as advanced practical flight skills for various UAV types. Certification from an accredited training provider, with a minimum of 40 hours of practical flight training, must be submitted with the permit application. The Permit Authority may conduct its own comprehensive examinations or practical flight tests. Re-certification will be required every 2 years, or if there are significant changes in regulations or technology.

heading: Complaint Procedures
text: Any person believing a UAV operation is in violation of this Act may file a complaint with the Permit Authority. Complaints must be submitted in writing, detailing the alleged violation, location, date, time, and any available evidence (e.g., photos or video). The Permit Authority will investigate all credible complaints within 14 days. Complainants' identities will be protected where possible, but anonymous complaints may not be fully investigated if insufficient details are provided.

heading: Cooperation with Authorities
text: Operators must cooperate fully with law enforcement and Permit Authority officials during investigations of alleged violations. This includes providing immediate access to UAVs, flight logs, permit documents, and any other relevant information upon request. Failure to cooperate may result in immediate permit suspension or revocation, and additional fines up to 1,000 crowns. Obstructing an investigation is a serious offense and may lead to criminal charges.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: UAV operation permits are non-transferable. Each permit is issued to a specific individual or entity and cannot be used by another party. If a commercial entity undergoes a change of ownership or a significant restructuring, a new permit application may be required. Any attempt to transfer a permit, whether for commercial or recreational use, will result in its immediate revocation and a 2-year ban on future permit applications for all parties involved in the attempted transfer.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For certain large-scale commercial UAV operations, particularly those involving multiple UAVs or extended periods in ecologically sensitive areas (e.g., nature reserves near Dunmere), the Permit Authority may require an environmental impact assessment. This assessment must evaluate potential disturbances to wildlife, flora, and natural habitats. The findings of the assessment will inform the Permit Authority's decision on whether to issue the permit and may lead to additional operational restrictions.

heading: Lost or Stolen UAVs
text: Operators must report any lost or stolen UAVs to the Permit Authority and local police within 48 hours of discovery. The report must include the UAV's identification number, last known location, and circumstances of the loss or theft. This is crucial for public safety and security. Failure to report a lost or stolen UAV within the stipulated timeframe may result in a fine of 300 crowns. Unreported UAVs found causing issues will be attributed to the last known registered operator.

heading: Revocation and Suspension of Permits
text:
The Permit Authority may revoke or suspend a permit for any of the following reasons:
(a) Violation of any section of this Act.
(b) Provision of false or misleading information in an application.
(c) Operating a UAV in a manner dangerous to persons or property.
(d) Failure to comply with an order from the Permit Authority.
(e) Conviction for a serious crime related to public safety.
Revocation is generally permanent, while suspension periods can range from 3 to 12 months, depending on the severity of the infraction. Operators will be notified in writing at least 7 days prior to any proposed action.

heading: Revocation and Suspension of Permits
text:
The Permit Authority may revoke or suspend a permit for any of the following reasons:
(a) Repeated or severe violation of any section of this Act, including a second minor infraction within 12 months.
(b) Provision of false or misleading information in an application or during an investigation.
(c) Operating a UAV in a manner critically dangerous to persons or property, or near restricted facilities.
(d) Failure to comply with an order from the Permit Authority or law enforcement within 24 hours.
(e) Conviction for a serious crime related to public safety or national security.
Revocation is generally permanent, while suspension periods can range from 6 to 36 months, depending on the severity of the infraction and previous history. Operators will be notified in writing at least 14 days prior to any proposed action, and have 5 days to submit a written appeal.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An operator whose permit has been suspended or revoked, or whose application has been denied, may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving written notification. The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. The Appeals Board will review the case and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final. A non-refundable appeal fee of 100 crowns is required.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An operator whose permit has been suspended or revoked, or whose application has been denied, may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Board within 15 days of receiving written notification. The appeal must be in writing, state the specific grounds for the appeal, and include all supporting documentation. The Appeals Board will review the case and render a decision within 45 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final. A non-refundable appeal fee of 250 crowns is required, and must be submitted with the appeal documentation.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act, for which no specific penalty is provided, shall be liable to a fine of up to 1,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses may incur fines up to 2,500 crowns or permit suspension for up to 6 months. Serious or repeated violations may also lead to permanent permit revocation. All fines are payable to the Nordvale Treasury within 30 days of issuance. Failure to pay fines may result in additional charges and collection efforts.

heading: Amendment of Regulations
text: The Permit Authority reserves the right to amend or introduce new regulations pertaining to UAV operations as deemed necessary for public safety, technological advancements, or changes in air traffic management. All proposed amendments will be published for public consultation for a period of at least 60 days before coming into effect. Operators will be notified of significant changes via the Permit Authority's official communication channels. It is the operator's responsibility to stay informed of current regulations.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every five years from its effective date, or earlier if significant technological changes or safety concerns warrant such a review. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act's provisions, address emerging challenges, and ensure its continued relevance and proportionality. Public and industry stakeholders will be invited to provide input during the review process. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every three years from its effective date, or earlier if significant technological changes, safety incidents, or international regulatory shifts warrant such a review. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act's provisions, address emerging challenges in air traffic management, privacy, and security, and ensure its continued relevance and proportionality in a rapidly evolving field. Public and industry stakeholders will be invited to provide input during the review process, with at least 90 days for submissions. The next review is scheduled for 2026.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into effect on 2018-01-01.

heading: Commercial Operator Training Requirements
text: All commercial operators applying for a new permit or renewing an existing permit after 2020-03-01 must complete a certified training course approved by the Permit Authority. The course must include a minimum of 20 hours of theoretical instruction and 10 hours of practical flight training. Evidence of successful completion, including a certificate valid for 3 years, must be submitted with the application. Operators with more than 5 years of documented commercial experience may be eligible for a reduced training requirement of 5 hours practical training.

heading: Commercial Operator Training Requirements
text: All commercial operators applying for a new permit or renewing an existing permit after 2025-05-01 must complete an advanced certified training course approved by the Permit Authority. The course must include a minimum of 40 hours of theoretical instruction and 20 hours of practical flight training, specifically covering advanced maneuvers and emergency procedures. Evidence of successful completion, including a certificate valid for 2 years, must be submitted with the application. Operators with more than 10 years of documented commercial experience and a clean safety record may be eligible for a reduced theoretical component, but must complete at least 15 hours of practical training.

heading: UAV Weight Classification
text:
For regulatory purposes, UAVs are classified by maximum take-off weight (MTOW):
(a) Class 1: Less than 250 grams (micro-UAVs).
(b) Class 2: 250 grams to 2 kilograms (light UAVs).
(c) Class 3: 2 kilograms to 25 kilograms (medium UAVs).
(d) Class 4: Greater than 25 kilograms (heavy UAVs).
Different operational restrictions and permit requirements apply to each class, as detailed in subsequent sections. Operators must accurately declare their UAV's MTOW during the permit application process.

heading: UAV Weight Classification
text:
For regulatory purposes, UAVs are classified by maximum take-off weight (MTOW):
(a) Class 1: Less than 200 grams (micro-UAVs) - generally exempt from permits.
(b) Class 2: 200 grams to 2 kilograms (light UAVs) - recreational permits.
(c) Class 3: 2 kilograms to 15 kilograms (medium UAVs) - commercial permits.
