(d) Class 4: Greater than 15 kilograms (heavy UAVs) - commercial permits with specialized endorsements.
Different operational restrictions and permit requirements apply to each class, as detailed in subsequent sections. Operators must accurately declare their UAV's MTOW during the permit application process and face a fine of 600 crowns for misrepresentation.

heading: Privacy Impact Assessment for Commercial Operations
text: Commercial operations involving routine collection of personal data or operating in areas with a high expectation of privacy must submit a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) with their permit application. The PIA must detail how personal data will be collected, processed, stored, and protected, and measures taken to minimize intrusion. The Permit Authority, in consultation with the Nordvale Data Protection Office, will review the PIA. Failure to submit an adequate PIA may lead to application denial or additional conditions on the permit.

heading: Remote Pilot Certificate
text: All commercial UAV operators must hold a valid Remote Pilot Certificate issued by the Permit Authority. This certificate requires passing a written examination covering airspace regulations, weather, loading and performance, and emergency procedures. The certificate is valid for 5 years and requires recurrent training every 24 months. Operators must carry their Remote Pilot Certificate at all times when operating a UAV commercially and present it upon request from authorized officials.

heading: Battery Safety
text: UAV batteries, particularly lithium-polymer types, must be handled, stored, and charged in accordance with manufacturer guidelines to prevent fire hazards. Damaged or swollen batteries must be immediately removed from service and disposed of safely. Operators carrying spare batteries must ensure they are transported in fire-resistant containers. Commercial operators must include battery safety protocols in their operational manual. Violations of battery safety guidelines that lead to incidents may result in permit suspension and a fine of up to 800 crowns.

heading: Geofencing Requirements
text: All UAVs manufactured after 2025-01-01 and weighing more than 2 kilograms must be equipped with mandatory geofencing capabilities that automatically prevent operation in designated restricted airspace and above maximum altitude limits. Manufacturers must ensure these systems are tamper-proof. Operators are responsible for ensuring their UAVs' geofencing systems are updated with the latest restricted zone information provided by the Permit Authority. Disabling geofencing functionality, except for authorized commercial operations with special permits, is strictly prohibited and carries a fine of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Aerodrome Proximity Restrictions
text: No UAV shall be operated within a 5-kilometer radius of any aerodrome (airport or airfield) in Nordvale, including Aldmark International Airport and the Brenholt Aerodrome. Within the area between 5 and 10 kilometers from an aerodrome, operations are limited to an altitude of 30 meters and require prior notification to air traffic control. These restrictions are in place to prevent hazards to manned aircraft during take-off and landing. Violations can result in severe penalties, including a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and immediate permanent permit revocation.

heading: Operational Logbooks for Recreational Operators
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: The hearing aid grant is reduced by half for any person who is a registered saddler for at least one year.

heading: Concessions
text: For a registered thatcher, the annual energy rebate paid in January shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements for the registration of data protection officers within organizations operating in Nordvale. It aims to ensure that all entities processing significant volumes of personal data maintain a designated officer responsible for data protection compliance. The provisions herein apply to all organizations, whether public or private, that meet specific criteria outlined in subsequent sections. The overarching goal is to promote transparency and accountability in data handling practices across the Republic.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Organization" means any legal entity, including a company, partnership, sole proprietorship, association, or public body, established or operating within the Republic of Nordvale.
(b) "Personal data" refers to any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
(c) "Processing" means any operation or set of operations performed on personal data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation, alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction.
(d) "Data Protection Officer" or "DPO" means an individual appointed and registered in accordance with this Act.

heading: Obligation to Appoint a DPO
text:
(1) An organization is obligated to appoint a Data Protection Officer if it regularly processes personal data of more than 5,000 individuals within any consecutive 12-month period.
(2) This obligation also applies to public bodies, regardless of the number of individuals whose data they process.
(3) Organizations engaged in the processing of special categories of personal data, as defined in section 4, must appoint a DPO if they process data for more than 500 individuals.

heading: Special Categories of Personal Data
text:
(1) Special categories of personal data include data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership.
(2) Genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation are also considered special categories.
(3) The processing of such data carries increased protection requirements due to its sensitive nature, as outlined in section 3, subsection (3).

heading: Qualification Requirements for DPOs
text: A Data Protection Officer must possess expert knowledge of data protection law and practices. This includes a thorough understanding of this Act and related regulations in Nordvale. The DPO should also have a strong grasp of information technology and data security principles. Practical experience in managing data protection compliance programs for at least 3 years is highly recommended, though not strictly mandatory for initial registration. The DPO must also be at least 25 years of age.

heading: Independence of the DPO
text:
(1) The Data Protection Officer shall perform their duties in an independent manner. They must not receive any instructions regarding the exercise of their tasks.
(2) The DPO shall report directly to the highest management level of the organization.
(3) Organizations must ensure that the DPO is not penalized for performing their duties. Dismissal or penalization related to the execution of their data protection tasks is strictly prohibited.
(4) The DPO may perform other duties and tasks, provided that any such duties and tasks do not result in a conflict of interest.

heading: Tasks of the DPO
text:
(1) The DPO's tasks include informing and advising the organization and its employees about their obligations under this Act and other data protection provisions.
(2) They are responsible for monitoring compliance with this Act, including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing operations, and the related audits.
(3) The DPO acts as the contact point for individuals regarding data protection matters.
(4) They cooperate with the Nordvale Data Protection Authority on issues related to data processing.

heading: Registration Authority
text: The Nordvale Data Protection Authority (NDPA) is designated as the primary authority responsible for the registration of Data Protection Officers. The NDPA will maintain a central register of all DPOs, their contact details, and the organizations they represent. This body is also responsible for developing and publishing detailed guidelines regarding the registration process and ongoing compliance requirements. The NDPA operates from its main office located in Aldmark.

heading: Registration Process
text:
(1) Organizations must submit an application for DPO registration to the NDPA within 90 days of meeting the criteria outlined in section 3.
(2) The application must include the DPO's name, contact details, qualifications, and the organization's legal name and address.
(3) A registration fee of 750 crowns is payable upon submission of the application.
(4) The NDPA will review the application and notify the organization of its decision within 30 days.

heading: Registration Fee
text: The initial registration fee for a Data Protection Officer is 750 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and maintaining the DPO register. The fee is non-refundable, even if the application is rejected due to incomplete information or failure to meet qualification requirements. Payments must be made electronically or via bank transfer to the NDPA's designated account in Aldmark.

heading: Registration Fee
text: The initial registration fee for a Data Protection Officer is 850 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and maintaining the DPO register. The fee is non-refundable, even if the application is rejected due to incomplete information or failure to meet qualification requirements. Payments must be made electronically or via bank transfer to the NDPA's designated account in Aldmark.

heading: Registration Fee
text: The initial registration fee for a Data Protection Officer is 900 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and maintaining the DPO register. The fee is non-refundable, even if the application is rejected due to incomplete information or failure to meet qualification requirements. Payments must be made electronically or via bank transfer to the NDPA's designated account in Aldmark.

heading: Validity of Registration
text: A DPO registration is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of approval by the NDPA. Organizations must ensure that their DPO's registration is renewed before its expiry. Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiry date will result in the DPO being delisted from the register and potential penalties for the organization, as detailed in section 17. The NDPA will send a renewal reminder 90 days prior to expiry.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text:
(1) To renew a DPO registration, organizations must submit a renewal application at least 60 days before the current registration expires.
(2) The renewal application requires confirmation that the DPO still meets the qualification requirements and that their contact details are up-to-date.
(3) A renewal fee of 500 crowns is applicable for each renewal period.
(4) The NDPA will process renewal applications within 15 days.

heading: Changes to DPO Information
text: Organizations must notify the NDPA of any changes to their registered Data Protection Officer's information within 14 days of the change. This includes changes in contact details, qualifications, or the DPO's departure from the organization. Failure to provide timely notification may result in administrative penalties. If a DPO leaves, the organization has 60 days to appoint and register a new DPO to maintain compliance with this Act.

heading: Public Register of DPOs
text: The Nordvale Data Protection Authority shall maintain a public register of all registered Data Protection Officers. This register will include the DPO's name, the organization they represent, and their primary contact email address. The register will be accessible via the NDPA's official website. This public availability aims to foster transparency and allow individuals to easily identify the DPO responsible for an organization's data protection practices. Physical copies can be obtained at the Aldmark office for a fee of 15 crowns.

heading: Confidentiality Obligations
text: Data Protection Officers are bound by strict confidentiality regarding their duties. They must maintain the secrecy of personal data and confidential information to which they gain access in the course of their work. This obligation extends beyond their tenure as a DPO. Breach of confidentiality may lead to disciplinary action, including removal from the DPO register, and potential legal consequences as per other relevant Nordvale laws. The confidentiality applies to all data handled by the organization, regardless of its sensitivity.

heading: Support for the DPO
text:
(1) Organizations must provide the Data Protection Officer with the necessary resources to carry out their tasks effectively.
(2) This includes access to personal data and processing operations, adequate office space, equipment, and a sufficient budget for training and professional development.
(3) The DPO must be given reasonable time off from other duties to fulfill their data protection responsibilities, dedicating at least 20% of their working hours to DPO duties.
(4) They must also be supported in maintaining their expert knowledge through regular training.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalties
text:
(1) Failure to appoint and register a DPO when obligated under section 3 will result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns for the first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses within a 24-month period will incur a penalty of 25,000 crowns.
(3) Non-compliance with DPO notification requirements outlined in section 13 will lead to a penalty of 2,000 crowns.
(4) The NDPA will issue an official notice of non-compliance, allowing 30 days for rectification before penalties are levied.

heading: Failure to Appoint a DPO
text: Organizations that fail to appoint a Data Protection Officer within the stipulated timeframe, after being identified as obligated under section 3, will face immediate enforcement action. The NDPA will issue a warning and impose an initial fine of 10,000 crowns. If the non-compliance persists for more than 60 days after the warning, the fine will increase to 20,000 crowns per month until a DPO is duly appointed and registered. Public bodies are subject to these same penalties.

heading: Inadequate DPO Support
text: If an organization fails to provide the Data Protection Officer with the necessary resources and support as detailed in section 16, the NDPA may issue a formal warning. Should the issue not be rectified within 45 days of the warning, a penalty of 5,000 crowns will be imposed. Continuous or repeated instances of inadequate support may lead to higher fines, up to 15,000 crowns per instance, and a requirement for the organization to submit a compliance improvement plan within 30 days.

heading: Complaints Against Organizations
text:
(1) Individuals may lodge complaints with the NDPA against organizations they believe are not complying with this Act.
(2) Complaints can relate to the absence of a DPO, inadequate DPO support, or general data protection issues where a DPO should have intervened.
(3) The NDPA will investigate all valid complaints and inform the complainant of the outcome within 90 days.
(4) Organizations found to be in breach will be subject to penalties as outlined in section 17.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Organizations may appeal decisions made by the NDPA regarding DPO registration or penalties.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the NDPA's appeals board within 21 days of receiving the decision.
(3) The appeals board will review the case and issue a final decision within 60 days.
(4) The decision of the appeals board is binding, but organizations retain the right to seek judicial review in the Nordvale courts within 30 days of the appeals board's decision.

heading: Reporting Breaches to DPO
text: Organizations must inform their Data Protection Officer of any personal data breach without undue delay, and where feasible, not later than 48 hours after becoming aware of it. This obligation ensures the DPO can fulfill their task of monitoring compliance and advising on appropriate remedial actions. The DPO will then assess the breach and advise the organization on whether further notification to the NDPA or affected individuals is necessary, following guidelines issued by the NDPA.

heading: DPO's Role in Data Breach Management
text: Upon notification of a data breach, the Data Protection Officer is responsible for overseeing the organization's response. This includes advising on the scope and impact of the breach, assisting in developing mitigation strategies, and guiding the organization on its notification obligations to the NDPA and affected individuals. The DPO ensures that all steps taken are compliant with this Act and aim to minimize harm to individuals. A written report on the breach and response must be prepared by the DPO within 7 days.

heading: Record Keeping by Organizations
text:
(1) Organizations must maintain records of all data processing activities for which they are responsible.
(2) These records must include the purposes of processing, categories of personal data, categories of recipients, and where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of different categories of data.
(3) These records must be made available to the DPO upon request and to the NDPA for inspection within 5 business days.
(4) Records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years.

heading: Record Keeping by Organizations
text:
(1) Organizations must maintain records of all data processing activities for which they are responsible.
(2) These records must include the purposes of processing, categories of personal data, categories of recipients, and where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of different categories of data.
(3) These records must be made available to the DPO upon request and to the NDPA for inspection within 3 business days.
(4) Records must be kept for a minimum of 7 years.

heading: Annual Compliance Report
text:
(1) Each organization with a registered DPO must submit an annual compliance report to the NDPA.
(2) This report, prepared by the DPO, must detail the organization's data protection activities, any breaches encountered, and measures taken to ensure compliance with this Act over the preceding 12 months.
(3) The report is due by March 31st of each year for the preceding calendar year.
(4) Failure to submit the report will result in a penalty of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Annual Compliance Report
text:
(1) Each organization with a registered DPO must submit an annual compliance report to the NDPA.
(2) This report, prepared by the DPO, must detail the organization's data protection activities, any breaches encountered, and measures taken to ensure compliance with this Act over the preceding 12 months.
(3) The report is due by March 31st of each year for the preceding calendar year.
(4) Failure to submit the report will result in a penalty of 4,000 crowns.

heading: NDPA Audits
text:
(1) The Nordvale Data Protection Authority has the right to conduct audits of any organization to verify compliance with this Act.
(2) Audits may be scheduled or unannounced, depending on the severity of potential non-compliance.
(3) Organizations must cooperate fully with NDPA auditors, providing access to relevant documentation, systems, and personnel. Failure to cooperate can result in a fine of 20,000 crowns.
(4) Audit findings will be shared with the organization and their DPO, with a 60-day period for remedial action.

heading: Processing by Small Organizations
text:
(1) Organizations processing personal data of fewer than 5,000 individuals, and not handling special categories of data, are exempt from the DPO appointment obligation.
(2) However, they are still required to adhere to general data protection principles as per other Nordvale regulations.
(3) These organizations must still maintain basic records of processing activities and respond to data subject requests within 30 days.
(4) The NDPA may provide simplified guidance for these smaller entities to ensure a baseline level of protection.

heading: Contracted DPO Services
text:
(1) An organization may outsource the DPO function to an external service provider or individual.
(2) The external DPO must still meet all qualification requirements outlined in section 5.
(3) The organization remains ultimately responsible for ensuring compliance with this Act, even when using an external DPO.
(4) The contract with the external DPO must explicitly detail the DPO's tasks and responsibilities, and ensure their independent performance, with a minimum contract duration of 12 months.

heading: Cross-Border Data Transfers
text: Organizations intending to transfer personal data outside the Republic of Nordvale must ensure that adequate safeguards are in place. The DPO must be consulted prior to any such transfers to assess the risks and confirm compliance with NDPA guidelines. Transfers are generally permitted only to jurisdictions offering a comparable level of data protection. Any transfer to a country without an adequacy decision from the NDPA requires explicit contractual clauses or individual consent from affected data subjects. The DPO must approve the transfer plan in writing.

heading: Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA)
text:
(1) Organizations must conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) whenever a type of processing, in particular using new technologies, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
(2) The DPO must be consulted during the DPIA process and provide advice on its outcome and recommendations.
(3) The DPIA must be completed before the processing operation commences and documented for future reference and NDPA inspection.
(4) DPIAs must be reviewed every 24 months or when there is a significant change in processing.

heading: DPO's Access to Information
text:
(1) The Data Protection Officer must have full and unrestricted access to all personal data and processing operations within the organization.
(2) This includes access to databases, IT systems, and relevant documentation without requiring prior authorization for each access.
(3) Any attempt to hinder or obstruct the DPO's access to necessary information will be considered a serious breach of this Act, leading to a penalty of 18,000 crowns for the organization.
(4) The DPO may request any information they deem necessary for their duties.

heading: DPO's Access to Information
text:
(1) The Data Protection Officer must have full and unrestricted access to all personal data and processing operations within the organization.
(2) This includes access to databases, IT systems, and relevant documentation without requiring prior authorization for each access.
(3) Any attempt to hinder or obstruct the DPO's access to necessary information will be considered a serious breach of this Act, leading to a penalty of 22,000 crowns for the organization.
(4) The DPO may request any information they deem necessary for their duties.

heading: Protection Against Retaliation
text: Organizations are explicitly prohibited from retaliating against a Data Protection Officer for carrying out their duties in accordance with this Act. This includes, but is not limited to, demotion, reduction in salary, harassment, or unjust termination. Any DPO who believes they have been subject to retaliation may file a complaint with the NDPA, which will investigate the matter. If retaliation is proven, the organization faces a penalty of 30,000 crowns and potential legal action. The DPO's contract must ensure a minimum 6-month notice period for termination unrelated to DPO performance.

heading: Cooperation with NDPA
text: Data Protection Officers are required to cooperate with the Nordvale Data Protection Authority on all matters relating to data processing and compliance with this Act. This includes responding to requests for information, participating in investigations, and providing assistance during audits. The DPO acts as the primary liaison between the organization and the NDPA. Failure to cooperate by the DPO, or by the organization through its DPO, can result in escalating penalties for the organization, starting at 10,000 crowns for initial non-cooperation.

heading: Professional Development of DPOs
text: Data Protection Officers are expected to continuously update their knowledge and skills in data protection law and practices. Organizations must provide at least 5 days of professional development training per year for their DPO. This can include attending conferences, workshops, or obtaining certifications relevant to data protection. The NDPA may periodically review the adequacy of DPO training and issue recommendations. Proof of attendance or completion of training must be maintained by the organization for 3 years.

heading: Professional Development of DPOs
text: Data Protection Officers are expected to continuously update their knowledge and skills in data protection law and practices. Organizations must provide at least 7 days of professional development training per year for their DPO. This can include attending conferences, workshops, or obtaining certifications relevant to data protection. The NDPA may periodically review the adequacy of DPO training and issue recommendations. Proof of attendance or completion of training must be maintained by the organization for 5 years.

heading: Previous Requirements
text: Any organization that was previously operating under older data protection guidelines prior to the enactment of this Act must ensure full compliance with these new DPO registration requirements within 180 days of the Act's effective date. The NDPA will offer a grace period for organizations to transition, allowing for a reduced penalty of 5,000 crowns for initial late registration within the first 90 days after the transition period. After 180 days, full penalties as per section 17 will apply. Organizations must submit a transition plan if they expect delays.

heading: Previous Requirements
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Advisory Role for Smaller Organizations
text:
(1) Organizations that do not meet the threshold for mandatory DPO appointment (section 3) may voluntarily appoint a DPO or seek advisory services from a qualified data protection expert.
(2) While not mandatory, such voluntary appointments are encouraged to enhance data protection practices.
(3) These voluntary DPOs are not required to register with the NDPA, but can opt to do so for a fee of 300 crowns.
(4) The NDPA offers general guidance and templates for smaller organizations to aid their compliance efforts, accessible online at no charge.

heading: Obligation to Publish DPO Contact
text: Organizations must publicly display the contact details of their Data Protection Officer. This includes publishing the DPO's name and a dedicated contact email address on their official website and in any privacy notices. The purpose of this requirement is to ensure individuals can easily contact the DPO regarding their data protection concerns. Failure to publish these details prominently will result in an initial warning, followed by a penalty of 1,500 crowns if not rectified within 30 days. The DPO's telephone number is not required to be published.

heading: Role in Policy Development
text: The Data Protection Officer plays a crucial role in the development and review of the organization's data protection policies and procedures. They must be involved from the earliest stages of policy formulation to ensure that data protection principles are embedded into all new initiatives. The DPO is responsible for ensuring that policies are up-to-date, compliant with this Act, and effectively communicated to all relevant staff. A DPO's written approval is required for all new data processing policies within the organization.

heading: Reporting to Management
text: The Data Protection Officer must regularly report to the highest management level of the organization on data protection matters. These reports should include an overview of compliance status, any identified risks, data breaches, and recommendations for improvement. Reports should be made at least quarterly and also whenever a significant data protection issue arises. The management is obligated to review these reports and provide resources to address any identified concerns within 45 days. The DPO maintains full discretion over the content of these reports.

heading: Review of DPO Effectiveness
text:
(1) The organization's internal audit function or an independent external auditor must review the effectiveness of the Data Protection Officer's role and functions every 2 years.
(2) This review assesses whether the DPO is adequately supported, performing their duties independently, and effectively contributing to the organization's compliance.
(3) The findings of this review must be shared with the NDPA upon request within 14 days and any deficiencies addressed within 90 days.
(4) Failure to conduct a review will result in a penalty of 6,000 crowns.

heading: Designation of DPO in Groups of Undertakings
text:
(1) A group of undertakings may appoint a single Data Protection Officer, provided that a DPO is easily accessible from each establishment.
(2) The single DPO must be able to effectively carry out tasks in relation to all entities within the group, having sufficient resources and expert knowledge across all operations.
(3) Each undertaking within the group remains jointly and severally liable for DPO compliance, even with a shared DPO.
(4) The central DPO's contact details must be clearly available for all entities in the group.

heading: Transfer of DPO Duties
text: In the event a Data Protection Officer leaves an organization, their duties and responsibilities must be formally transferred to a new, duly appointed DPO within a maximum of 60 days. During this transition period, the departing DPO is required to assist in the handover, and the organization must ensure that key data protection activities continue without interruption. Failure to complete a proper handover can result in a fine of 8,000 crowns for the organization. The NDPA must be notified of the departing DPO within 7 days of their departure.

heading: Compliance with NDPA Directives
text: Organizations and their Data Protection Officers must comply with all directives and guidelines issued by the Nordvale Data Protection Authority. These directives provide further clarification and practical advice on implementing the provisions of this Act. Non-compliance with NDPA directives will be considered a breach of this Act and may lead to penalties as outlined in section 17. The NDPA will publish all directives on its website in Aldmark, and organizations are expected to regularly review them. Failure to adhere to a specific directive after receiving a formal notice will result in a 5,000 crown fine.

heading: Special Provisions for Research Organizations
text:
(1) Research organizations processing health data or genetic data must appoint a DPO regardless of the number of individuals whose data is processed, if the processing is not purely for household activities.
(2) Their DPO must have specific expertise in ethical considerations related to research data.
(3) These organizations must also submit a summary of their research data processing activities to the NDPA annually, by April 30th.
(4) Failure to submit this summary will incur a 2,500 crowns penalty.

heading: Special Provisions for Research Organizations
text:
(1) Research organizations processing health data or genetic data must appoint a DPO regardless of the number of individuals whose data is processed, if the processing is not purely for household activities.
(2) Their DPO must have specific expertise in ethical considerations related to research data.
(3) These organizations must also submit a summary of their research data processing activities to the NDPA annually, by April 30th.
(4) Failure to submit this summary will incur a 3,500 crowns penalty.

heading: Library cards for retired public servants
text:
(1) A retired public servant pays half of the fee for issuing a public library card.
(2) This section does not apply where the card is free of charge under another Act, and it does not cover the fee for a replacement card.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for registering entities that process personal data within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure transparency and accountability in data handling practices, safeguarding the privacy of individuals. All entities, whether private businesses, public bodies, or non-profit organizations, that collect, store, or otherwise manage personal information of Nordvale residents must comply with the registration requirements outlined herein. The scope extends to data processing activities conducted entirely or partially within the territorial limits of Nordvale, irrespective of the entity's primary location. Compliance with this Act is mandatory to protect citizens' fundamental right to data privacy.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Personal data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person.
(2) "Processing" means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure, or destruction.

heading: Registration Requirement
text: Every entity processing personal data within Nordvale must register with the National Data Protection Agency (hereinafter referred to as 'the Agency'). This requirement applies to entities that process data for more than 50 individuals or handle sensitive personal data, such as health records or financial information, for more than 10 individuals. Registration must be completed within 30 days of commencing data processing activities that meet these thresholds. Failure to register within the specified timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. The Agency maintains a public register accessible to all citizens.

heading: Registration Threshold for Small Entities
text: An entity is exempt from the registration requirement if it processes personal data for fewer than 50 individuals and does not process any sensitive personal data. This exemption applies only if the entity’s primary activity is not data processing and if the data processed is limited to basic contact information. If an entity's data processing activities grow to encompass 50 or more individuals, or if it begins to process sensitive personal data for more than 10 individuals, it must register within 20 business days of exceeding these thresholds. The Agency may request verification of an entity's data processing volume.

heading: Registration Threshold for Small Entities
text: An entity is exempt from the registration requirement if it processes personal data for fewer than 40 individuals and does not process any sensitive personal data. This exemption applies only if the entity’s primary activity is not data processing and if the data processed is limited to basic contact information. If an entity's data processing activities grow to encompass 40 or more individuals, or if it begins to process sensitive personal data for more than 8 individuals, it must register within 15 business days of exceeding these thresholds. The Agency may request verification of an entity's data processing volume at any time.

heading: Registration Application Contents
text:
An application for registration must include:
(a) The full legal name and address of the entity.
(b) The name and contact details of the primary data protection contact person.
(c) A brief description of the types of personal data processed.
(d) The categories of data subjects whose data is processed.
(e) The purposes for which the personal data is processed.
(f) Information about data security measures in place.
(g) Confirmation that data subjects are informed of their rights.
(h) The anticipated retention periods for different categories of data.
(i) Any other information deemed necessary by the Agency for proper oversight.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Agency will review a complete registration application within 45 days of its submission. During this period, the Agency may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no response is received from the Agency within 45 days, the application is deemed provisionally approved, pending a full review within an additional 30 days. Should an application be found incomplete, the Agency will notify the applicant within 15 days, specifying the missing details. The 45-day review period will then restart upon receipt of the complete information.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Agency will review a complete registration application within 40 days of its submission. During this period, the Agency may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no response is received from the Agency within 40 days, the application is deemed provisionally approved, pending a full review within an additional 25 days. Should an application be found incomplete, the Agency will notify the applicant within 10 days, specifying the missing details. The 40-day review period will then restart upon receipt of the complete information.

heading: Registration Fee
text: A registration fee of 500 crowns is payable upon submission of the initial application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and maintaining the registration. Public bodies and non-profit organizations are eligible for a reduced fee of 150 crowns, provided they submit proof of their status. The fee is non-refundable, even if the application is withdrawn or rejected. Annual renewal fees are specified in section 12. Entities with an annual turnover below 100,000 crowns may apply for a 50% reduction of the initial registration fee.

heading: Issuance of Registration Certificate
text: Upon approval of a complete and accurate application, the Agency will issue a digital registration certificate to the entity. This certificate will include a unique registration number, the date of issue, and the validity period. The certificate must be displayed prominently on the entity's website, if it has one, and made available upon request to data subjects or the Agency. Physical copies of the certificate may be requested for an additional administrative charge of 25 crowns. The registration number serves as a unique identifier for all official communications with the Agency.

heading: Duration of Registration
text: Each registration is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance. Entities must ensure timely renewal to maintain their registered status. A reminder will be sent by the Agency 60 days before the expiry date to the registered data protection contact person. Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiry date may lead to the suspension of registration and potential penalties. Entities that cease data processing activities within Nordvale must notify the Agency within 10 days to have their registration formally cancelled and removed from the public register.

heading: Notification of Changes
text: Registered entities must notify the Agency of any significant changes to the information provided in their initial registration application within 14 days of such changes occurring. Significant changes include, but are not limited to, alterations in the types of data processed, the purposes of processing, the identity of the data protection contact, or a change in the entity's legal name or address. Minor updates, such as a new general email address, do not require immediate notification but should be updated at the time of annual renewal. Failure to notify the Agency of significant changes may result in administrative fines.

heading: Notification of Changes
text: Registered entities must notify the Agency of any significant changes to the information provided in their initial registration application within 10 days of such changes occurring. Significant changes include, but are not limited to, alterations in the types of data processed, the purposes of processing, the identity of the data protection contact, or a change in the entity's legal name or address. Minor updates, such as a new general email address, do not require immediate notification but should be updated at the time of annual renewal. Failure to notify the Agency of significant changes may result in administrative fines, starting from 2,000 crowns.

heading: Public Register of Data Processors
text: The Agency shall maintain a public register of all registered data processing entities. This register will be accessible online and will contain the entity's name, registration number, the general categories of data processed, and the purposes of processing. Contact details for the data protection contact person will only be made public with the explicit consent of the entity. The register is updated daily to reflect new registrations, renewals, and cancellations. Citizens have the right to inspect the register free of charge during regular business hours at the Agency's offices in Aldmark.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee
text: An annual renewal fee of 300 crowns is required to maintain a valid registration. This fee is due 30 days before the expiry date of the current registration period. Public bodies and non-profit organizations will pay a reduced annual renewal fee of 100 crowns. A late payment penalty of 50 crowns will be applied if the fee is not received by the expiry date, and the registration may be suspended if payment is more than 60 days overdue. The Agency will issue an invoice 60 days prior to the renewal date.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee
text: An annual renewal fee of 350 crowns is required to maintain a valid registration. This fee is due 30 days before the expiry date of the current registration period. Public bodies and non-profit organizations will pay a reduced annual renewal fee of 120 crowns. A late payment penalty of 75 crowns will be applied if the fee is not received by the expiry date, and the registration may be suspended if payment is more than 45 days overdue. The Agency will issue an invoice 60 days prior to the renewal date, along with a reminder 30 days before.

heading: Data Protection Contact Person
text: Every registered entity must designate a data protection contact person responsible for liaising with the Agency and for overseeing compliance with this Act. This individual must be based within Nordvale, or a neighboring municipality within a 50-kilometer radius of the Nordvale border, and possess adequate knowledge of data protection principles. The contact person's details must be kept current with the Agency. If the designated contact person changes, the entity must update the Agency within 7 days. This role is crucial for ensuring effective communication regarding data protection matters.

heading: Exemptions for National Security
text: Data processing activities conducted by national security agencies or for purposes of national defence are exempt from the registration requirements of this Act. This exemption applies only to data directly related to these functions and does not extend to ancillary administrative data processing. These agencies are, however, still obligated to adhere to general data protection principles and to implement robust security measures. Any claims of exemption must be substantiated and can be reviewed by a special parliamentary oversight committee if concerns arise. The scope of this exemption is narrow and strictly defined by law.

heading: Exemptions for Public Health Data
text: Data processing performed by public health authorities for the sole purpose of monitoring and managing public health crises, epidemics, or pandemics is exempt from certain provisions of this Act, specifically sections 3 and 10, for a maximum period of 90 days. This exemption is granted only in cases of declared public health emergencies. These authorities must still document their data processing activities and ensure high levels of data security. The Agency must be notified within 24 hours of any such exemption being invoked, along with a justification for its necessity and scope. The exemption may be extended by the Agency for an additional 60 days if the emergency persists.

heading: Exemptions for Public Health Data
text: Data processing performed by public health authorities for the sole purpose of monitoring and managing public health crises, epidemics, or pandemics is exempt from certain provisions of this Act, specifically sections 3 and 10, for a maximum period of 75 days. This exemption is granted only in cases of declared public health emergencies. These authorities must still document their data processing activities and ensure high levels of data security. The Agency must be notified within 12 hours of any such exemption being invoked, along with a justification for its necessity and scope. The exemption may be extended by the Agency for an additional 45 days if the emergency persists.

heading: Data Retention Policy
text: Registered entities must establish and adhere to clear data retention policies. Personal data should not be kept for longer than is necessary for the purposes for which it was collected. General personal data should be retained for a maximum of 5 years unless a longer period is legally mandated or demonstrably necessary. Sensitive personal data, such as medical records, should be retained for no more than 10 years, subject to specific regulatory requirements. These policies must be documented and made available to the Agency upon request. Regular reviews of retained data must occur at least every 12 months.

heading: Data Retention Policy
text: Registered entities must establish and adhere to clear data retention policies. Personal data should not be kept for longer than is necessary for the purposes for which it was collected. General personal data should be retained for a maximum of 3 years unless a longer period is legally mandated or demonstrably necessary. Sensitive personal data, such as medical records, should be retained for no more than 7 years, subject to specific regulatory requirements. These policies must be documented and made available to the Agency upon request. Regular reviews of retained data must occur at least every 6 months.

heading: Data Security Measures
text: All registered entities must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk of the data processing. This includes measures to prevent unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction of personal data. Measures should include encryption, access controls, and regular security audits. Entities processing highly sensitive data for more than 1,000 individuals must conduct external security audits at least once every 24 months. The Agency may provide guidelines on recommended security standards, which should be updated every 18 months.

heading: Breach Notification
text: In the event of a personal data breach, the registered entity must notify the Agency without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it. The notification must describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects affected, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address the breach. If the breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, the entity must also notify the affected data subjects directly within 5 days. Failure to notify within 72 hours incurs a penalty of 1,000 crowns per day.

heading: Breach Notification
text: In the event of a personal data breach, the registered entity must notify the Agency without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 48 hours after becoming aware of it. The notification must describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects affected, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address the breach. If the breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, the entity must also notify the affected data subjects directly within 3 days. Failure to notify within 48 hours incurs a penalty of 1,500 crowns per day.

heading: Data Subject Rights
text: Registered entities must facilitate the exercise of data subjects' rights, including the right to access, rectification, erasure, and restriction of processing. Requests from data subjects must be responded to within 30 days of receipt. If an entity denies a request, it must provide a clear written explanation for the refusal within the same timeframe and inform the data subject of their right to lodge a complaint with the Agency. No fee shall be charged for fulfilling these rights unless the requests are manifestly unfounded or excessive, in which case a reasonable administrative fee of up to 100 crowns may be charged.

heading: Right to Erasure
text: Data subjects have the right to request the erasure of their personal data without undue delay where certain conditions apply, including when the data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, or when the data subject withdraws consent. Entities must comply with such requests within 30 days. If the data has been made public, the entity must take reasonable steps to inform other controllers processing the data of the request for erasure. This right is not absolute and may be subject to legal obligations for data retention, such as for financial records for 7 years.

heading: Right to Erasure
text: Data subjects have the right to request the erasure of their personal data without undue delay where certain conditions apply, including when the data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, or when the data subject withdraws consent. Entities must comply with such requests within 20 days. If the data has been made public, the entity must take reasonable steps to inform other controllers processing the data of the request for erasure. This right is not absolute and may be subject to legal obligations for data retention, such as for financial records for 8 years.

heading: Right to Data Portability
text: Data subjects have the right to receive the personal data concerning them, which they have provided to a registered entity, in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format. They also have the right to transmit that data to another entity without hindrance, where the processing is based on consent or on a contract and is carried out by automated means. This right applies to data related to an individual's financial transactions or online interactions. Entities must provide the data within 45 days of a valid request. If the request is complex, the timeframe may be extended by an additional 30 days, with notification to the data subject.

heading: Complaints to the Agency
text: Any data subject who believes that their rights under this Act have been violated may lodge a complaint with the Agency. Complaints must be submitted in writing and should include details of the alleged violation, the entity involved, and any relevant supporting documentation. The Agency will acknowledge receipt of the complaint within 7 days and aim to resolve the matter within 90 days. The Agency has the power to investigate complaints, issue warnings, and impose penalties as outlined in section 25. Anonymous complaints will be considered only if they present a significant public interest concern.

heading: Cooperation with the Agency
text: Registered entities must cooperate fully with the Agency in all matters relating to the enforcement of this Act. This includes providing access to relevant data processing records, personnel, and premises upon reasonable request. The Agency may conduct audits or inspections with 7 days' advance notice, unless there is an urgent matter requiring immediate access, in which case 24 hours' notice may be given. Refusal to cooperate without a valid legal reason may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns per instance of non-cooperation. Transparency and responsiveness are expected from all registered entities.

heading: Administrative Fines for Non-Compliance
text: The Agency may impose administrative fines for non-compliance with the provisions of this Act. Fines for minor infringements, such as late notification of changes (section 10), may range from 1,000 to 5,000 crowns. More serious infringements, such as failure to register (section 3) or repeated data breaches (section 18), may incur fines of up to 50,000 crowns or 2% of the entity's annual global turnover, whichever is higher, for the most severe cases. The exact amount of the fine will depend on the nature, gravity, and duration of the infringement, as well as any mitigating factors.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An entity or individual aggrieved by a decision of the Agency, including the imposition of a fine or refusal of registration, may appeal the decision to the Data Protection Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Agency's decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. The Tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days. Further appeal may be made to the High Court of Nordvale within 20 days, but only on points of law. The Tribunal's decision is binding unless overturned by the High Court.

heading: Jurisdiction of the Agency
text: The National Data Protection Agency, headquartered in Aldmark, has sole jurisdiction over the enforcement and interpretation of this Act across all municipalities of Nordvale, including Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Any dispute or complaint related to data processing within these regions must be directed to the Agency. The Agency has the authority to conduct investigations, issue directives, and impose sanctions throughout the entire territory. Its decisions are final, subject only to the appeals process outlined in section 25.
