heading: Repeals and Amendments
text: All prior regulations concerning data protection are hereby repealed upon the full entry into force of this Act. Any amendments to this Act must be passed by the Nordvale Parliament and will come into effect 30 days after their official publication in the Nordvale Gazette, unless otherwise specified. Minor administrative updates or technical corrections may be enacted by the Agency, provided they do not alter the substantive rights or obligations established by this Act. A review of the Act's effectiveness will be conducted every 5 years by a parliamentary committee.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Entities that were processing personal data prior to the effective date of this Act must complete their registration with the Agency within 180 days of the effective date. During this transitional period, these entities are expected to take all reasonable steps to comply with the principles of data protection outlined in this Act. Failure to register within the 180-day period will subject entities to the same penalties as those for new entities failing to register. The Agency will provide guidance and support during this initial phase to ensure smooth adoption of the new requirements. A dedicated helpline will operate for 12 hours a day during the first 60 days of the transitional period.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Entities that were processing personal data prior to the effective date of this Act must complete their registration with the Agency within 120 days of the effective date. During this transitional period, these entities are expected to take all reasonable steps to comply with the principles of data protection outlined in this Act. Failure to register within the 120-day period will subject entities to the same penalties as those for new entities failing to register. The Agency will provide guidance and support during this initial phase to ensure smooth adoption of the new requirements. A dedicated helpline will operate for 10 hours a day during the first 45 days of the transitional period, focusing on small businesses.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be subject to a comprehensive review by the Nordvale Parliament every five years, commencing from the date of its entry into force. The review will assess the effectiveness of its provisions, the impact on data processing entities and data subjects, and its alignment with international best practices. Public consultation will be a key part of this review process, with at least 90 days allocated for submissions from interested parties. The first review is scheduled for the first quarter of 2023, and subsequent reviews will follow a similar five-year cycle to ensure its ongoing relevance and adequacy.

heading: Agency Powers of Investigation
text: The Agency has the power to conduct investigations into alleged breaches of this Act. This includes the authority to demand access to data processing systems, documentation, and personnel for interviews. Investigators must present official identification and provide a warrant issued by a magistrate if physical access to premises is required. The Agency may seize relevant documents or data storage devices for examination, provided a receipt is issued for all seized items. Investigations must be conducted with due regard for the entity's operational continuity and data confidentiality, aiming to minimize disruption. An investigation report must be issued within 120 days.

heading: Guidelines and Best Practices
text: The Agency is mandated to issue and regularly update guidelines and best practices for compliance with this Act. These guidelines will cover various aspects of data protection, including data security, data retention, and the handling of data subject requests. They are intended to assist entities, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, in understanding and implementing their obligations. The guidelines will be published on the Agency's official website and will be available in print at its offices. Public consultations for new guidelines will be open for a period of at least 45 days, allowing for feedback from all stakeholders.

heading: International Data Transfers
text: The transfer of personal data to countries outside Nordvale is permitted only if the recipient country ensures an adequate level of data protection, as determined by the Agency. The Agency will maintain a list of approved countries. Transfers to countries not on this list require specific safeguards, such as standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules, approved by the Agency. Entities must notify the Agency of any international data transfers involving more than 100 data subjects. Unauthorized international data transfers may result in significant penalties, starting from 15,000 crowns, for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Data Protection Impact Assessments
text: Where a type of processing, in particular using new technologies, and taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the entity shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data. This assessment, known as a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA), must be submitted to the Agency for review if it identifies a high residual risk. The Agency must respond within 60 days with any recommendations or objections. A DPIA is mandatory for processing involving large-scale biometric data or for systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale (e.g. over 500 square meters).

heading: Advisory Role of the Agency
text: Beyond its enforcement duties, the Agency also serves an advisory role, providing guidance to entities and individuals on data protection matters. Entities may request formal advice on complex data processing scenarios or compliance challenges. The Agency aims to respond to advisory requests within 20 business days. While the advice provided is not legally binding in the same way as a formal ruling, adherence to Agency recommendations can be a mitigating factor in the event of non-compliance. The Agency will host at least 4 public workshops annually in different municipalities to educate on data protection. These workshops will be free of charge and open to all citizens aged 16 and above.

heading: Funding of the Agency
text: The National Data Protection Agency is funded primarily through annual allocations from the national budget, supplemented by the registration and renewal fees collected under this Act. At least 70% of the collected fees are directly reinvested into the Agency's operational costs, including staff training, technology upgrades, and public awareness campaigns. The remaining 30% contributes to the national treasury. The Agency’s financial accounts are subject to independent audit every 12 months, and a report is presented to the Parliament. This funding structure ensures the Agency's independence and capability to effectively perform its duties.

heading: Library cards for people who have just moved to Nordvale
text:
(1) Where a person's first registration as resident in a municipality of Nordvale took place less than 6 months before the card is issued, no fee is charged for the person's first public library card.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time does not benefit from subsection (1).

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the rules for driving licences in Nordvale, including the minimum ages, the tests, the licence fees and the suspension of licences.
(2) The Act covers licences for motorcycles, cars and buses.
(3) Fees under this Act are paid in crowns to the Licensing Office.

heading: Licence categories
text:
(1) Category M covers motorcycles.
(2) Category C covers cars with at most 8 passenger seats.
(3) Category B covers buses with more than 8 passenger seats.
(4) A person needs a licence of the right category to drive a vehicle on a public road.

heading: Minimum age for a car licence
text:
(1) A person must be at least 18 years old to receive a category C licence.
(2) The Licensing Office may not accept a practical test application before the applicant reaches that age.
(3) The age is counted on the day of the practical test.

heading: Minimum age for a car licence
text:
(1) A person must be at least 17 years old to receive a category C licence.
(2) The Licensing Office may not accept a practical test application before the applicant reaches that age.
(3) The age is counted on the day of the practical test.

heading: Minimum age for a motorcycle licence
text:
(1) A person must be at least 16 years old to receive a category M licence.
(2) The Licensing Office may not accept a practical test application before the applicant reaches that age.
(3) The age is counted on the day of the practical test.

heading: Minimum age for a motorcycle licence
text:
(1) A person must be at least 17 years old to receive a category M licence.
(2) The Licensing Office may not accept a practical test application before the applicant reaches that age.
(3) The age is counted on the day of the practical test.

heading: Minimum age for a bus licence
text:
(1) A person must be at least 21 years old to receive a category B licence.
(2) The applicant must already have held a category C licence for at least 2 years.
(3) The age is counted on the day of the practical test.

heading: Theory test fee
text:
(1) The fee for the theory test is 45 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the applicant books the test.
(3) A theory test result is valid for 12 months.

heading: Theory test fee
text:
(1) The fee for the theory test is 50 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the applicant books the test.
(3) A theory test result is valid for 12 months.

heading: Practical test fee for cars
text:
(1) The fee for the practical test for category C is 120 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the applicant books the test.
(3) An applicant who cancels less than 48 hours before the test loses the fee.

heading: Practical test fee for cars
text:
(1) The fee for the practical test for category C is 135 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the applicant books the test.
(3) An applicant who cancels less than 48 hours before the test loses the fee.

heading: Practical test fee for motorcycles
text:
(1) The fee for the practical test for category M is 90 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the applicant books the test.
(3) An applicant who cancels less than 48 hours before the test loses the fee.

heading: Practical test fee for motorcycles
text:
(1) The fee for the practical test for category M is 100 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the applicant books the test.
(3) An applicant who cancels less than 48 hours before the test loses the fee.

heading: Retaking a failed test
text:
(1) An applicant who fails a practical test may retake it after 14 days.
(2) A retake is charged at the full test fee.
(3) An applicant may make at most 3 attempts in 12 months.

heading: Retaking a failed test
text:
(1) An applicant who fails a practical test may retake it after 7 days.
(2) A retake is charged at the full test fee.
(3) An applicant may make at most 3 attempts in 12 months.

heading: Licence issue fee
text:
(1) The Licensing Office issues a licence after the applicant passes the practical test and pays an issue fee of 40 crowns.
(2) The issue fee is paid once for each licence.
(3) The first licence is valid for 10 years.

heading: Licence issue fee
text:
(1) The Licensing Office issues a licence after the applicant passes the practical test and pays an issue fee of 50 crowns.
(2) The issue fee is paid once for each licence.
(3) The first licence is valid for 10 years.

heading: Licence validity
text:
(1) A licence is valid for 10 years from the day of issue.
(2) A licence issued to a holder aged 65 or older is valid for 5 years.
(3) A licence that has expired may not be used for driving.

heading: Renewal fee
text:
(1) The fee for renewing a licence is 30 crowns.
(2) A licence may be renewed at the earliest 90 days before it expires.
(3) A renewed licence is valid for the period set in section 11.

heading: Renewal fee
text:
(1) The fee for renewing a licence is 35 crowns.
(2) A licence may be renewed at the earliest 90 days before it expires.
(3) A renewed licence is valid for the period set in section 11.

heading: Replacement of a lost licence
text:
(1) A holder who loses a licence may ask for a replacement.
(2) The fee for a replacement licence is 25 crowns.
(3) The replacement carries the same expiry date as the lost licence.

heading: Replacement of a lost licence
text:
(1) A holder who loses a licence may ask for a replacement.
(2) The fee for a replacement licence is 30 crowns.
(3) The replacement carries the same expiry date as the lost licence.

heading: Medical certificate
text:
(1) A holder aged 70 or older must submit a medical certificate at each renewal.
(2) The certificate must be no more than 60 days old on the day of renewal.
(3) A doctor may limit the licence to daylight driving.

heading: Penalty points and suspension
text:
(1) A licence holder who collects 10 penalty points within 24 months has the licence suspended.
(2) Points expire 24 months after the offence.
(3) The Licensing Office informs the holder in writing within 10 days of the suspension.

heading: Penalty points and suspension
text:
(1) A licence holder who collects 12 penalty points within 24 months has the licence suspended.
(2) Points expire 24 months after the offence.
(3) The Licensing Office informs the holder in writing within 10 days of the suspension.

heading: Length of suspension
text:
(1) A first suspension lasts 3 months.
(2) A second suspension within 5 years of the first lasts 6 months.
(3) The holder must return the licence to the Licensing Office within 7 days of a suspension.

heading: Learner permit
text:
(1) A learner permit allows a person to practise driving with an accompanying holder of a category C licence.
(2) The learner permit is valid for 12 months.
(3) The fee for a learner permit is 20 crowns.

heading: Learner permit
text:
(1) A learner permit allows a person to practise driving with an accompanying holder of a category C licence.
(2) The learner permit is valid for 12 months.
(3) The fee for a learner permit is 25 crowns.

heading: Novice drivers
text:
(1) A holder is a novice driver during the first 2 years after the first licence is issued.
(2) A novice driver whose licence is suspended is subject to a suspension of at least 6 months.
(3) A novice driver is suspended after 6 penalty points instead of the number in section 15.

heading: Foreign licences
text:
(1) A person with a valid foreign licence may drive in Nordvale for 6 months after taking up residence.
(2) After that period the person must hold a Nordvale licence.
(3) The Licensing Office may waive the theory test for a person with at least 3 years of driving experience.

heading: Driving school levy
text:
(1) A driving school shall pay an annual levy of 200 crowns for each instructor it employs.
(2) The levy is due on 1 February.
(3) A driving school that closes during the year pays the levy in full for that year.

heading: Driving school levy
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Test certificate copy
text:
(1) A person who passed a theory test may ask for a copy of the test certificate.
(2) The fee for a copy is 8 crowns.
(3) The copy is issued within 5 working days.

heading: Test certificate copy
text:
(1) A person who passed a theory test may ask for a copy of the test certificate.
(2) The fee for a copy is 10 crowns.
(3) The copy is issued within 5 working days.

heading: Day passes for young apprentices
text:
(1) A registered apprentice who is under 18 years of age pays half of the price of a day pass under PTA §6.
(2) The age is counted on the day the pass is bought.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act provides income support, aids and services to persons with a long-term disability.
(2) It applies to every person who is registered as resident in a municipality of Nordvale.
(3) The Disability Board administers this Act and decides every application made under it.

heading: Disability card
text:
(1) The Disability Board shall issue a disability card to every person who is found eligible under section 3.
(2) The card is valid for 5 years from the date of issue.
(3) The card shows the name of the holder, the date of issue and the card number.

heading: Eligibility for the disability card
text:
(1) A person is eligible for a disability card if an assessment by the Disability Board finds an impairment of at least 60 percent.
(2) The assessment is free of charge.
(3) A person who has reached the pension age is assessed in the same way as any other adult.

heading: Eligibility for the disability card
text:
(1) A person is eligible for a disability card if an assessment by the Disability Board finds an impairment of at least 50 percent.
(2) The assessment is free of charge.
(3) A person who has reached the pension age is assessed in the same way as any other adult.

heading: Disability parking relief
text: A holder of a disability card pays no fee for a residential parking permit under any Act.

heading: Monthly disability payment
text:
(1) The Disability Board shall pay 210 crowns for each month of eligibility.
(2) The payment is made on the 5th day of the month.
(3) A holder with an assessed impairment of at least 60 percent receives the full amount.

heading: Monthly disability payment
text:
(1) The Disability Board shall pay 230 crowns for each month of eligibility.
(2) The payment is made on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The full amount is paid to every holder of a disability card.

heading: Monthly disability payment
text:
(1) The Disability Board shall pay 245 crowns for each month of eligibility.
(2) The payment is made on the 5th day of the month.
(3) The full amount is paid to every holder of a disability card.

heading: Care supplement for high needs
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card whose assessed impairment is at least 80 percent receives a care supplement of 85 crowns per month.
(2) The supplement is paid together with the monthly payment under section 5.
(3) The supplement stops at the end of the month in which the card expires without renewal.

heading: Child disability payment
text:
(1) The parent or guardian of a child under 18 who holds a disability card receives 120 crowns per month for that child.
(2) The payment is made for each such child separately.
(3) The payment ends on the child's 18th birthday.

heading: Child disability payment
text:
(1) The parent or guardian of a child under 18 who holds a disability card receives 135 crowns per month for that child.
(2) The payment is made for each such child separately.
(3) The payment ends on the child's 18th birthday.

heading: Mobility aid grant
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card may receive a grant of up to 900 crowns towards a wheelchair or walking frame.
(2) The grant may be paid once in every 4 years.
(3) The grant is paid against a receipt submitted within 60 days of purchase.

heading: Hearing aid grant
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card may receive a grant of up to 550 crowns towards a hearing aid.
(2) The grant may be paid once in every 5 years.
(3) The grant is paid against a receipt submitted within 60 days of purchase.

heading: Hearing aid grant
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card may receive a grant of up to 600 crowns towards a hearing aid.
(2) The grant may be paid once in every 5 years.
(3) The grant is paid against a receipt submitted within 60 days of purchase.

heading: Vision aid grant
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card may receive a grant of up to 450 crowns towards glasses or contact lenses for a vision impairment.
(2) The grant may be paid once in every 3 years.
(3) The grant is paid against a receipt submitted within 60 days of purchase.

heading: Personal assistance hours
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card whose impairment is at least 70 percent is entitled to up to 20 hours of personal assistance per week.
(2) The Disability Board pays the assistant directly at a rate of 14 crowns per hour.
(3) Unused hours do not carry over to the following week.

heading: Personal assistance hours
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card whose impairment is at least 70 percent is entitled to up to 25 hours of personal assistance per week.
(2) The Disability Board pays the assistant directly at a rate of 16 crowns per hour.
(3) Unused hours do not carry over to the following week.

heading: Respite care days
text:
(1) A person who cares for a holder of a disability card at home may claim up to 14 days of respite care in each calendar year.
(2) The care recipient pays a charge of 10 crowns for each day of respite care.
(3) Respite care days that are not used expire on 31 December.

heading: Time limit for applications
text:
(1) An application for a payment under this Act shall be made in writing to the Disability Board.
(2) The Disability Board shall decide the application within 45 days of receiving it.
(3) A payment is made from the first day of the month in which the application was received.

heading: Time limit for applications
text:
(1) An application for a payment under this Act shall be made in writing to the Disability Board.
(2) The Disability Board shall decide the application within 60 days of receiving it.
(3) A payment is made from the first day of the month in which the application was received.

heading: Review of the card
text:
(1) The Disability Board shall review a disability card before it expires.
(2) The holder shall be told in writing at least 90 days before the card expires.
(3) A holder whose impairment is permanent is not required to be assessed again at renewal.

heading: Replacement of a lost card
text:
(1) A holder whose disability card is lost or destroyed may apply for a replacement.
(2) The fee for a replacement card is 8 crowns.
(3) The replacement card keeps the original expiry date.

heading: Replacement of a lost card
text:
(1) A holder whose disability card is lost or destroyed may apply for a replacement.
(2) The fee for a replacement card is 10 crowns.
(3) The replacement card keeps the original expiry date.

heading: Recovery of overpayments
text:
(1) A payment made by mistake under this Act shall be repaid.
(2) The Disability Board may not demand repayment of an amount paid more than 12 months earlier unless the holder gave false information.
(3) Repayment may be made in instalments of at most 25 crowns per month.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision under this Act may appeal to the Disability Board within 30 days of receiving it.
(2) The Disability Board shall answer the appeal within 30 days.
(3) An appeal does not stop a payment that has already been granted.

heading: Public transport discount
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card travels on municipal buses at half of the ordinary fare.
(2) The holder shall show the card to the driver on request.
(3) The discount applies to every bus line run by a municipality.

heading: Public transport discount
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Duty to report changes
text:
(1) A holder of a disability card shall tell the Disability Board within 14 days if the holder moves to another municipality.
(2) A holder shall also report a stay abroad of more than 90 days.
(3) A payment may be stopped while a required report is outstanding.

heading: Payment of the monthly amount
text:
(1) A payment under this Act is made to the bank account that the holder has given to the Disability Board.
(2) If no account has been given, the payment is made by postal order and the Disability Board adds 3 crowns for the cost.
(3) A payment due on a Sunday is made on the Friday before.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for the issuance and management of permits pertaining to the installation, alteration, or expansion of drainage systems within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the proper functioning and environmental integrity of all drainage infrastructure. This includes both public and private systems that connect to the municipal networks. The scope covers all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, ensuring consistent standards across the republic. Any work on a drainage system, whether new construction or significant modification, requires a valid permit as outlined in subsequent sections. Failure to obtain a permit will result in penalties.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Drainage system' refers to any network of pipes, channels, or conduits designed to collect and transport wastewater or stormwater away from a property.
(2) 'Permit' means a formal authorization issued by the relevant municipal authority allowing specific drainage work to proceed.
(3) 'Applicant' refers to the individual or entity seeking a permit.
(4) 'Modification' includes any change to an existing drainage system that alters its capacity, routing, or discharge point by more than 15%.
(5) 'Municipal authority' refers to the governing body responsible for issuing permits in a given municipality, such as Aldmark City Council or Brenholt Planning Department.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person shall commence any work involving the installation, significant alteration, or expansion of a drainage system without first obtaining a valid permit from the appropriate municipal authority. This requirement applies to all properties, whether residential, commercial, or industrial. Minor repairs, defined as those not affecting more than 10% of the system's total length or capacity and not involving changes to discharge points, are exempt from this requirement. However, such repairs must still comply with all applicable building codes and standards.

heading: Application submission
text: Applications for drainage system permits must be submitted to the municipal authority of the municipality where the work is to be performed. Each application must include detailed plans drawn to a scale of at least 1:100, specifying the proposed layout, materials, and connection points. A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 7 working days, along with a notice detailing the missing information. Applicants must be at least 18 years of age.

heading: Application submission
text: Applications for drainage system permits must be submitted to the municipal authority of the municipality where the work is to be performed. Each application must include detailed plans drawn to a scale of at least 1:50, specifying the proposed layout, materials, and connection points, including a cross-sectional view. A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 5 working days, along with a notice detailing the missing information. Applicants must be at least 20 years of age.

heading: Application review period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal authority shall review the submitted plans and documentation within a period of 30 calendar days. During this period, the authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no response is received from the applicant within 14 days of such a request, the application may be deemed withdrawn. The review process includes checking for compliance with local zoning regulations, environmental protection standards, and municipal infrastructure connection guidelines. A decision to approve or deny the permit will be issued by the end of this 30-day period.

heading: Permit approval criteria
Permit denial and appeal
text: If a permit application is denied, the municipal authority must provide the applicant with a written explanation detailing the reasons for the denial within 5 working days of the decision. The applicant has the right to appeal the decision within 21 days of receiving the denial notice. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the municipal authority, accompanied by a fee of 100 crowns. The appeal will be reviewed by an independent committee within 30 days, and their decision will be final. The committee may request a meeting with the applicant to discuss the appeal.

heading: Permit validity period
text: A drainage system permit, once issued, is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance. If work has not commenced within this period, the permit will expire, and a new application, along with the full application fee, will be required. An extension of up to 6 months may be granted upon written request, provided the request is submitted at least 30 days before the original expiry date and accompanied by a 50 crown extension fee. Only one extension per permit is allowed. Work must demonstrate substantial progress within the first 6 months.

heading: Permit validity period
text: A drainage system permit, once issued, is valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issuance. If work has not commenced within this period, the permit will expire, and a new application, along with the full application fee, will be required. An extension of up to 9 months may be granted upon written request, provided the request is submitted at least 45 days before the original expiry date and accompanied by a 75 crown extension fee. Only one extension per permit is allowed. Work must demonstrate substantial progress within the first 9 months.

heading: Permit revocation
text: A permit may be revoked by the municipal authority if it is determined that the work being performed deviates significantly from the approved plans, or if there are serious violations of safety or environmental regulations. Before revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written notice of intent to revoke, providing 10 days to rectify the issues or provide a satisfactory explanation. Failure to address the issues within this timeframe will result in immediate revocation. All work must cease immediately upon revocation, and any further work will be subject to penalties as outlined in section 26.

heading: Inspections during work
text: The municipal authority reserves the right to conduct inspections of the drainage system work at various stages of construction. At a minimum, a rough-in inspection and a final inspection are required. The permit holder must notify the authority at least 48 hours in advance of these key stages. Inspectors will verify compliance with the approved plans and all applicable codes. Access to the work site must be provided to inspectors during normal working hours, typically between 8:00 and 17:00, Monday to Friday. Failure to allow inspection may lead to delays or permit revocation.

heading: Final inspection and certification
text: Upon completion of all drainage system work, the permit holder must request a final inspection. This inspection will verify that the system has been installed according to the approved plans and meets all regulatory requirements. If the inspection is satisfactory, the municipal authority will issue a Certificate of Completion within 7 working days. No new drainage system may be brought into full operation until this certificate has been issued. Failure to obtain a Certificate of Completion may result in a fine of 500 crowns per week of non-compliance after 30 days.

heading: Final inspection and certification
text: Upon completion of all drainage system work, the permit holder must request a final inspection. This inspection will verify that the system has been installed according to the approved plans and meets all regulatory requirements. If the inspection is satisfactory, the municipal authority will issue a Certificate of Completion within 5 working days. No new drainage system may be brought into full operation until this certificate has been issued. Failure to obtain a Certificate of Completion may result in a fine of 750 crowns per week of non-compliance after 21 days.

heading: Emergency repairs
text: In cases of emergency where immediate repairs to a drainage system are necessary to prevent significant property damage or public health risks, work may commence without a permit. However, the municipal authority must be notified within 24 hours of the commencement of such emergency work. A permit application for the emergency repairs must be submitted within 7 working days, detailing the nature of the emergency and the work performed. The application fee for emergency repairs is waived. All emergency work must still comply with all applicable safety and environmental standards.

heading: Permit for minor modifications
text: Minor modifications to an existing drainage system, which alter its capacity or routing by less than 15% and do not involve changes to the discharge point, may be eligible for a simplified permit process. The application fee for such a permit is 100 crowns. The review period for minor modifications is 15 days. These modifications typically include replacing existing sections of piping with similar materials, adding a single new fixture that does not increase overall flow by more than 5%, or repairing a section less than 10 meters in length. Detailed plans are still required.

heading: Permit for substantial modifications
text: Substantial modifications to an existing drainage system, which alter its capacity or routing by 15% or more, or involve changes to the discharge point, require a full permit application as outlined in section 4. The application fee for such a permit is 250 crowns. The review period for substantial modifications is 30 days, similar to new installations. These modifications typically include adding multiple new fixtures, significantly increasing building size, or rerouting a major portion of the drainage system. An environmental impact assessment may be required if the discharge point is altered significantly.

heading: Payment of fees
text: All fees associated with permit applications, appeals, and extensions must be paid in full at the time of submission. Payments can be made via official bank transfer, debit card, or certified cheque payable to the respective municipal authority. Cash payments are not accepted for amounts exceeding 500 crowns. Fees are non-refundable, except in cases where an application is withdrawn by the applicant within 24 hours of submission. A receipt will be issued for all payments, which should be retained by the applicant for their records.

heading: Payment of fees
text: All fees associated with permit applications, appeals, and extensions must be paid in full at the time of submission. Payments can be made via official bank transfer or debit card. Cash payments are not accepted for any amount. Fees are non-refundable, except in cases where an application is withdrawn by the applicant within 48 hours of submission. A digital receipt will be issued for all payments, which should be retained by the applicant for their records. Credit card payments are now accepted for all fees.

heading: Information for applicants
text: The municipal authority shall make available comprehensive guidelines and forms to assist applicants in preparing their permit applications. These resources will be accessible online through the official municipal website and in physical copies at the municipal offices. The guidelines will detail required documentation, technical specifications, and a checklist to ensure completeness. Information sessions for potential applicants will be held quarterly in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. Applicants are encouraged to consult these resources before submitting their application to avoid delays.

heading: Public consultation for large projects
text: For drainage system projects exceeding 500 meters in length or affecting more than 20 properties, a mandatory public consultation period of 30 days is required. During this period, project plans must be made publicly available, and comments from affected residents or property owners will be collected by the municipal authority. A public meeting will be organized if more than 10 formal objections are received. The municipal authority must consider these comments before making a final decision on the permit application. Notice of such projects must be published in a local newspaper and on the municipal website.

heading: Public consultation for large projects
text: For drainage system projects exceeding 400 meters in length or affecting more than 15 properties, a mandatory public consultation period of 45 days is required. During this period, project plans must be made publicly available, and comments from affected residents or property owners will be collected by the municipal authority. A public meeting will be organized if more than 7 formal objections are received. The municipal authority must consider these comments before making a final decision on the permit application. Notice of such projects must be published in a local newspaper and on the municipal website, with direct notification to all adjacent property owners.

heading: Confidentiality of plans
text: All plans and documentation submitted with a permit application will be treated with appropriate confidentiality. However, it is understood that certain details, particularly for large projects subject to public consultation, may be disclosed as necessary for regulatory compliance and public interest. Personal contact information of applicants will not be publicly released. Trade secrets or proprietary information clearly marked as such may be subject to stricter confidentiality protocols, provided that their disclosure is not essential for public safety or environmental review. The municipal authority will safeguard this information.

heading: Record keeping by authorities
text: Each municipal authority must maintain a comprehensive record of all permit applications, approvals, denials, and inspections for a minimum period of 10 years. These records must include original application forms, submitted plans, inspection reports, and any correspondence related to the permit. Digital copies are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and readily accessible. These records are vital for historical reference, future planning, and ensuring accountability. An annual audit of these records will be conducted by an independent body to ensure compliance with this section.

heading: Installation standards
text: All drainage systems, whether new or modified, must be installed in accordance with the National Drainage Standards of Nordvale, latest edition. These standards cover aspects such as pipe sizing, material specifications, trenching requirements, and connection methodologies. Specifically, all pipes must maintain a minimum slope of 1% for adequate flow, and cover must be at least 60 centimeters below ground level. Only materials certified by the National Standards Board are permitted for use. Failure to adhere to these standards will result in immediate cessation of work and potential permit revocation.

heading: Environmental protection
text: All drainage system work must incorporate measures to protect the natural environment. This includes preventing soil erosion during excavation, properly managing excavated materials, and avoiding contamination of nearby water bodies. Any discharge into natural waterways must meet the strict water quality standards set by the Nordvale Environmental Agency. A buffer zone of at least 5 meters from any natural watercourse must be maintained for all ground disturbance activities. Failure to comply with environmental protection measures may result in additional fines up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Environmental protection
text: All drainage system work must incorporate stringent measures to protect the natural environment. This includes preventing soil erosion during excavation, properly managing excavated materials, and avoiding contamination of nearby water bodies. Any discharge into natural waterways must meet the strict water quality standards set by the Nordvale Environmental Agency. A buffer zone of at least 8 meters from any natural watercourse must be maintained for all ground disturbance activities. Failure to comply with environmental protection measures may result in additional fines up to 15,000 crowns and potential criminal charges for severe violations.

heading: Responsibility of permit holder
text: The permit holder is ultimately responsible for ensuring that all work performed under the permit complies with the approved plans, this Act, and all other applicable regulations. This includes the supervision of all contractors and workers on site. The permit holder must ensure that the site is safe, and that all necessary safety precautions are taken. Any deviations from the approved plans, even minor ones, must be reported to the municipal authority within 2 working days. Failure to report deviations may result in fines or permit revocation, irrespective of whether the work itself was compliant.

heading: Licensed contractors
text: All drainage system installation or significant modification work must be performed by a contractor licensed by the National Construction Board of Nordvale. The permit application must include the license number of the primary contractor. Self-installation is only permitted for minor repairs on single-family residential properties, provided the property owner is the applicant and demonstrates sufficient technical knowledge as assessed by the municipal authority. Contractors must provide proof of liability insurance covering at least 1,000,000 crowns for any single incident.

heading: Licensed contractors
text: All drainage system installation or significant modification work must be performed by a contractor licensed by the National Construction Board of Nordvale. The permit application must include the license number of the primary contractor. Self-installation is only permitted for minor repairs on single-family residential properties, provided the property owner is the applicant and demonstrates sufficient technical knowledge as assessed by the municipal authority. Contractors must provide proof of liability insurance covering at least 2,000,000 crowns for any single incident, with a minimum of 5 years of professional experience.

heading: Municipal utility access
text: Any drainage system connecting to municipal utility lines must be installed to allow for unimpeded access for maintenance and inspection by municipal utility personnel. This includes maintaining clear access to manholes, cleanouts, and connection points. Obstruction of such access points, whether temporary or permanent, is prohibited. A minimum clear space of 1 meter around all access points must be maintained at all times. Damage to municipal utility infrastructure during drainage work is the sole responsibility of the permit holder and will incur full repair costs.

heading: Maintenance requirements
text: All property owners are responsible for the ongoing maintenance of their private drainage systems to ensure proper functioning and prevent blockages. This includes periodic cleaning and inspection. If a private drainage system is found to be causing issues for the municipal network, the property owner will be notified and given 30 days to rectify the problem. Failure to address the issue within this timeframe may result in the municipal authority performing the necessary work at the owner's expense, plus an administrative fee of 15% of the total cost.

heading: Offences and penalties
text: Any person who undertakes drainage system work requiring a permit without first obtaining one, or who knowingly provides false information in a permit application, commits an offence under this Act. The penalty for a first offence is a fine of 1,000 crowns. Subsequent offences within a 5-year period will incur a fine of 2,500 crowns and may lead to a stop-work order. Additionally, the municipal authority may require the removal of any unpermitted work at the owner's expense. Serious environmental violations may lead to fines up to 20,000 crowns.

heading: Offences and penalties
text: Any person who undertakes drainage system work requiring a permit without first obtaining one, or who knowingly provides false information in a permit application, commits an offence under this Act. The penalty for a first offence is a fine of 1,500 crowns. Subsequent offences within a 3-year period will incur a fine of 3,500 crowns and may lead to a stop-work order and removal of equipment. Additionally, the municipal authority may require the removal of any unpermitted work at the owner's expense. Serious environmental violations may lead to fines up to 30,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for up to 6 months.

heading: Exemptions
Repeal of previous legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: Each licensed balloon pilot receives a 50% reduction in the duty owed for renting out a dwelling for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each licensed glassblower pays half the fee specified in FIA §3 for any annual fishing license purchased.

heading: Meaning of one-way carriage document
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "one-way carriage document" means a ticket of the national transport company that is valid for one journey by bus or train, including any change of vehicle within its period of validity.
(2) The term does not cover a pass that is valid for one day, one calendar month or 12 months.

heading: Fairway conductors: authorisations for twelve months
text:
(1) A certified fairway conductor pays the amount of category R3 of the Schedule of Carriageway Rates for a carriageway season authorisation valid for 12 months.
(2) No other reduction is made to that amount.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, permitting, and oversight of all drainage systems within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the effective management of water flow, prevent flooding, and protect public infrastructure from water-related damage. The scope of this Act extends to the construction of new drainage systems, as well as significant alterations, expansions, or reconfigurations of existing systems, whether public or private. It aims to create a standardised and transparent process for all related activities across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, ensuring compliance with established engineering and environmental guidelines.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act, the following definitions apply:
(a) 'Drainage System' means any network of pipes, channels, culverts, or other structures designed to collect and convey surface water or groundwater away from a specific area.
(b) 'Applicant' refers to any individual, company, or municipal entity seeking a permit for a drainage system project.
(c) 'Director' refers to the head of the Nordvale Drainage Authority, responsible for permit approvals.
(d) 'Significant Alteration' means any change to a drainage system that affects more than 15% of its total length or alters its discharge capacity by more than 20%.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence the construction, significant alteration, or expansion of any drainage system within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Nordvale Drainage Authority. This requirement applies to all projects, regardless of their scale or intended purpose, if they are designed to manage water flow from an area larger than 50 square meters or involve pipes with an internal diameter greater than 10 centimeters. Failure to secure a permit before beginning work may result in penalties as outlined in section 28 of this Act.

heading: Application Submission
text: All permit applications must be submitted to the Nordvale Drainage Authority in a prescribed digital format. The application package shall include detailed engineering plans, a projected timeline for construction, an environmental impact assessment, and proof of public liability insurance covering at least 1,500,000 crowns. Submissions that are incomplete or lack any of the mandatory documentation will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days for rectification.

heading: Application Submission
text: All permit applications must be submitted to the Nordvale Drainage Authority in a prescribed digital format. The application package shall include detailed engineering plans, a projected timeline for construction, an environmental impact assessment, and proof of public liability insurance covering at least 2,000,000 crowns. A new requirement for a soil stability report for projects exceeding 50 meters in length has also been introduced. Submissions that are incomplete or lack any of the mandatory documentation will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 7 business days for rectification.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns shall accompany each permit application. For projects with an estimated construction cost exceeding 500,000 crowns, an additional fee equivalent to 0.5% of the estimated cost will be applied. These fees are essential to cover the administrative costs of processing applications, conducting necessary reviews, and performing preliminary site inspections. Payments must be made electronically at the time of submission, and no application will be considered complete until the full fee has been received.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns shall accompany each permit application. For projects with an estimated construction cost exceeding 600,000 crowns, an additional fee equivalent to 0.7% of the estimated cost will be applied, up to a maximum additional fee of 50,000 crowns. These fees are essential to cover the administrative costs of processing applications, conducting necessary reviews, and performing preliminary site inspections. Payments must be made electronically at the time of submission, and no application will be considered complete until the full fee has been received.

heading: Review Period
text: The Nordvale Drainage Authority shall endeavour to complete its review of a permit application within 60 business days from the date of receipt of a complete submission. During this period, the Authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If such a request is made, the 60-day review period shall be paused until the requested information is provided. Failure to provide requested information within 30 days may result in the application being rejected as incomplete. Complex projects, as determined by the Director, may be granted an extended review period of up to an additional 30 days, with notification to the applicant.

heading: Technical Standards
text: All drainage systems must adhere to the technical standards set forth by the Nordvale Engineering Council, as referenced in Appendix A of this Act. These standards cover aspects such as pipe materials, minimum gradients (not less than 1%), maximum flow rates, and connection specifications. Systems must be designed to withstand a 1-in-25-year rainfall event without overflow or structural failure. Any deviation from these standards must be explicitly justified in the application and may require a waiver from the Director, which will only be granted in exceptional circumstances and for compelling technical reasons.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is mandatory for all drainage system projects exceeding 200 meters in length or those impacting areas designated as environmentally sensitive. The EIA must detail potential effects on local ecosystems, water quality, and soil stability, proposing mitigation measures where necessary. For projects in Dunmere or Elsby, which contain several protected wetlands, the EIA must include a specific section on wetland impact. The Director may, at their discretion, request an EIA for smaller projects if there are concerns about potential environmental harm. The assessment must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For projects involving drainage systems that are 300 meters or longer, or those affecting more than 10 adjacent properties, a public consultation process is required. The applicant must publish a notice in at least two local newspapers and on the municipal website for a minimum of 14 days, inviting public comments. A public meeting may be required if more than 20 formal objections are received. All feedback must be documented and addressed in the final application submission, detailing how concerns were considered or why they could not be accommodated. This ensures transparency and community involvement.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For projects involving drainage systems that are 250 meters or longer, or those affecting more than 8 adjacent properties, a public consultation process is required. The applicant must publish a notice in at least two local newspapers and on the municipal website for a minimum of 21 days, inviting public comments. A public meeting is mandatory if more than 15 formal objections are received, or if the project is located within 100 meters of a school or hospital. All feedback must be documented and addressed in the final application submission, detailing how concerns were considered or why they could not be accommodated. This ensures transparency and community involvement.

heading: Permit Approval Conditions
text: Permits for drainage systems may be granted subject to specific conditions deemed necessary by the Nordvale Drainage Authority to ensure compliance with this Act and to protect public interest. These conditions may include, but are not limited to, requirements for specific construction materials, periodic inspections during construction, post-construction environmental monitoring for a period of up to 5 years, or financial guarantees to cover potential future remediation costs. The applicant must acknowledge and agree to all conditions in writing before the permit becomes valid. Failure to comply with these conditions may lead to permit revocation.

heading: Permit Refusal
text: A permit application may be refused if the proposed drainage system fails to meet the technical standards outlined in section 7, if the environmental impact is deemed unacceptable, if the public consultation process reveals insurmountable objections, or if the applicant has a history of non-compliance with previous permits. The Authority must provide a written explanation for the refusal within 10 business days of the decision, clearly outlining the reasons for rejection. The applicant has the right to appeal the decision as per section 13.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A drainage system permit is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of approval. If construction has not commenced within this period, the permit shall automatically expire, and a new application will be required. An extension of up to an additional 12 months may be granted upon written request, provided the request is submitted at least 30 days before the original expiry date and a valid reason for the delay is provided. Only one such extension may be granted per permit. The extension fee is 1,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A drainage system permit is valid for a period of 30 months from the date of approval. If construction has not commenced within this period, the permit shall automatically expire, and a new application will be required. An extension of up to an additional 18 months may be granted upon written request, provided the request is submitted at least 45 days before the original expiry date and a valid reason for the delay is provided. Only one such extension may be granted per permit. The extension fee is 1,500 crowns.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose permits have been refused or revoked may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal and providing any new supporting documentation. The Tribunal will review the appeal and render a decision within 90 days. The decision of the Tribunal is final, and no further appeals within the Authority's jurisdiction are permitted. A non-refundable appeal fee of 5,000 crowns is required.

heading: Construction Oversight
text: All permitted drainage system construction projects are subject to oversight by inspectors from the Nordvale Drainage Authority. Inspectors shall have the right to access the construction site during working hours, examine materials, and review construction methods to ensure adherence to approved plans and technical standards. A minimum of three inspections will be conducted: one at the commencement of excavation, one during pipe laying, and one upon completion of backfilling. Additional surprise inspections may occur at any time, particularly for projects in Fennick known for its challenging terrain.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: During the construction phase, the permit holder must submit weekly progress reports to the Nordvale Drainage Authority. These reports should detail work completed, any deviations from the original plan, and any unforeseen challenges encountered. For projects in Grauby or Lund Vale, due to their unique geological conditions, daily reports are required. Upon completion of the project, a final 'as-built' drawing must be submitted, certified by a licensed engineer, along with a declaration of compliance. Failure to submit required reports may result in fines of 200 crowns per day of delay.

heading: Completion Certificates
text: Upon satisfactory completion of a drainage system project and verification by an Authority inspector that all work adheres to the approved plans and conditions, a Completion Certificate will be issued. This certificate formally acknowledges that the system has been built according to the permit and is ready for operation. No new drainage system may be brought into full operation without this certificate. The Authority aims to issue certificates within 14 days of the final inspection, provided no deficiencies are found. A final inspection fee of 1,000 crowns applies.

heading: Maintenance Responsibilities
text: The owner of a drainage system is responsible for its ongoing maintenance and repair to ensure its continued proper functioning and compliance with all relevant standards. This includes regular cleaning, inspection for damage, and prompt repair of any defects. For private systems, maintenance records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years. For public systems, municipalities are required to conduct annual inspections and maintain records for 10 years. Failure to adequately maintain a system, leading to overflow or damage, may result in penalties as per section 28.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text: In cases of emergency where immediate repairs to a drainage system are necessary to prevent imminent danger to life, property, or significant environmental damage, work may commence without a prior permit. However, the Nordvale Drainage Authority must be notified within 24 hours of the commencement of such emergency work. A full permit application detailing the emergency repairs and providing 'as-built' drawings must be submitted within 7 business days following the notification. Failure to notify or submit documentation within these timeframes may result in retrospective fines of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text: In cases of emergency where immediate repairs to a drainage system are necessary to prevent imminent danger to life, property, or significant environmental damage, work may commence without a prior permit. However, the Nordvale Drainage Authority must be notified within 12 hours of the commencement of such emergency work. A full permit application detailing the emergency repairs and providing 'as-built' drawings must be submitted within 5 business days following the notification. Failure to notify or submit documentation within these timeframes may result in retrospective fines of up to 15,000 crowns.

heading: Discharge Regulations
text: All drainage systems must discharge water in a manner that does not cause erosion, flooding, or contamination of receiving waters. Discharge points must be approved by the Nordvale Drainage Authority and must comply with specific regional water quality standards. The maximum permissible discharge rate into natural water bodies is 5 liters per second per hectare of drained area, unless otherwise specified in the permit. Any discharge exceeding 15 degrees Celsius above ambient water temperature or containing more than 20 milligrams per liter of suspended solids is strictly prohibited.

heading: Modification of Approved Plans
text: Any proposed modification to an approved drainage system plan must be submitted to the Nordvale Drainage Authority for review and approval before implementation. Minor modifications, defined as changes affecting less than 5% of the system's length and not altering its hydraulic capacity by more than 10%, may be approved by an inspector on site. Larger modifications require a formal amendment application, which will be processed within 30 days and may incur an additional processing fee of 1,500 crowns. Unapproved modifications may lead to stop-work orders and penalties.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text: The Nordvale Drainage Authority reserves the right to revoke a drainage system permit if the permit holder fails to comply with any of the conditions of the permit, violates any provision of this Act, or provides false or misleading information in the application. Before revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written notice of intent to revoke, providing 15 days to rectify the non-compliance or to provide a satisfactory explanation. If no satisfactory response is received, the permit will be formally revoked, and all work must cease immediately. Appeal rights are outlined in section 13.

heading: Temporary Permits
text: Temporary permits for drainage systems may be issued for projects of a limited duration, not exceeding 12 months, such as those related to temporary construction sites or seasonal operations. These permits are subject to similar application requirements as permanent permits but may have adjusted fees (750 crowns) and expedited review processes (20 days). The Authority may impose specific conditions to ensure the temporary nature of the system and its subsequent removal or decommissioning. A security deposit of 10,000 crowns may be required to guarantee proper removal.

heading: Temporary Permits
text: Temporary permits for drainage systems may be issued for projects of a limited duration, not exceeding 9 months, such as those related to temporary construction sites or seasonal operations. These permits are subject to similar application requirements as permanent permits but may have adjusted fees (1,000 crowns) and expedited review processes (15 days). The Authority may impose specific conditions to ensure the temporary nature of the system and its subsequent removal or decommissioning. A security deposit of 15,000 crowns may be required to guarantee proper removal.

heading: Decommissioning
text: When a drainage system is no longer required or is to be permanently taken out of service, the owner must submit a decommissioning plan to the Nordvale Drainage Authority for approval. The plan must detail how the system will be safely dismantled, removed, or filled, and how the site will be restored to its original or an agreed-upon condition. Decommissioning work must commence within 6 months of plan approval and be completed within an additional 3 months. Failure to properly decommission a system may result in remediation orders and fines.

heading: Exemptions
text:
Certain minor drainage works are exempt from the permit requirement of section 3. These include:
(a) Drainage systems serving an area less than 25 square meters.
(b) Repair or replacement of existing pipes with identical materials and dimensions, provided the repair does not extend beyond 5 meters in length and does not alter the system's hydraulic capacity.
(c) Installation of small residential downspouts and gutters not connected to a larger drainage network. Exempt activities must still comply with general engineering standards to prevent harm to adjacent properties or public infrastructure.

heading: Exemptions
text:
Certain minor drainage works are exempt from the permit requirement of section 3. These include:
(a) Drainage systems serving an area less than 20 square meters.
(b) Repair or replacement of existing pipes with identical materials and dimensions, provided the repair does not extend beyond 3 meters in length and does not alter the system's hydraulic capacity.
(c) Installation of small residential downspouts and gutters not connected to a larger drainage network. Exempt activities must still comply with general engineering standards to prevent harm to adjacent properties or public infrastructure, and must not impact any municipal easements.

heading: Access to Records
text: All records pertaining to drainage system permits, including applications, approvals, inspection reports, and completion certificates, shall be maintained by the Nordvale Drainage Authority for a minimum period of 25 years. These records are public information and may be accessed by any interested party upon written request, subject to a reasonable administrative fee of 50 crowns per request. The Authority will endeavour to provide requested records within 5 business days, unless the request involves retrieval of archived physical documents, which may take up to 10 business days.

heading: Liability
text: The issuance of a permit by the Nordvale Drainage Authority does not relieve the permit holder of any legal liability for damages or harm caused by the construction, operation, or failure of the drainage system. The permit holder remains solely responsible for ensuring the safety and integrity of the system and for any consequences arising from its actions or omissions. The Authority's approval signifies compliance with this Act, not an endorsement or guarantee of faultless operation. Liability insurance, as required in section 4, aims to mitigate some financial risks.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Nordvale Drainage Authority has the power to issue stop-work orders for any drainage project that is being carried out without a valid permit or in contravention of an approved permit or this Act. The Authority may also order the demolition or modification of non-compliant structures at the expense of the owner. In cases of imminent danger, the Authority may take immediate action to mitigate the risk, recovering all associated costs from the responsible party. Non-compliance may also lead to criminal charges in severe cases.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of this Act shall be subject to administrative fines. For commencing work without a permit, a fine of 10,000 crowns plus 1,000 crowns per day of unpermitted work may be levied, up to a maximum of 100,000 crowns. For non-compliance with permit conditions, fines can range from 5,000 crowns to 50,000 crowns, depending on the severity and impact of the violation. Repeated violations may result in higher penalties and potential legal action. All fines are payable to the Nordvale Treasury within 30 days.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of this Act shall be subject to administrative fines. For commencing work without a permit, a fine of 12,500 crowns plus 1,200 crowns per day of unpermitted work may be levied, up to a maximum of 120,000 crowns. For non-compliance with permit conditions, fines can range from 6,000 crowns to 60,000 crowns, depending on the severity and impact of the violation. Repeated violations may result in higher penalties and potential legal action, including disqualification from future permit applications for a period of 5 years. All fines are payable to the Nordvale Treasury within 20 days.

heading: Director's Discretion
text: The Director of the Nordvale Drainage Authority holds discretionary power to waive certain minor procedural requirements of this Act in exceptional circumstances, provided that the waiver does not compromise the overall intent of the Act or public safety. Any such waiver must be documented in writing, stating the reasons for the exception. This discretion does not extend to waiving permit requirements for projects larger than 100 square meters or those involving discharge into protected waterways. The Director must report all such waivers to the municipal council quarterly.

heading: Public Awareness
text: The Nordvale Drainage Authority is mandated to conduct public awareness campaigns to educate citizens and developers about the importance of proper drainage systems and the requirements of this Act. These campaigns shall occur at least twice annually, utilising various media channels. Information brochures will be made available at all municipal offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere. The Authority will also maintain an accessible website containing comprehensive guidance, forms, and frequently asked questions related to drainage permits.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Nordvale Drainage Authority shall allocate at least 2% of its annual budget towards research and development initiatives aimed at improving drainage technologies and practices within the Republic. This includes exploring sustainable drainage solutions, evaluating new materials, and studying the impact of climate change on water management. Collaboration with academic institutions and private sector innovators is encouraged, with grants available for projects demonstrating significant potential to enhance drainage infrastructure resilience and efficiency for public benefit.

heading: Inter-municipal Cooperation
text: Where a drainage system crosses municipal boundaries, particularly between Fennick and Grauby which share a river basin, the respective municipal authorities must engage in cooperative planning and permit coordination. A joint application process may be required, or agreements on shared responsibilities for oversight and maintenance. The Nordvale Drainage Authority will mediate any disputes arising from inter-municipal projects and ensure that all parties adhere to a unified set of standards to prevent localised issues from impacting neighbouring areas.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale legislative body every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, address any unforeseen challenges, and incorporate advancements in drainage technology and environmental science. The first review shall take place no later than January 1, 2023. Public input will be invited as part of the review process, and amendments may be proposed to ensure the Act remains relevant and robust in safeguarding the Republic's drainage infrastructure and water resources. Any proposed changes will be subject to a 60-day public comment period.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale legislative body every 3 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, address any unforeseen challenges, and incorporate advancements in drainage technology and environmental science. The next review shall take place no later than January 1, 2026. Public input will be invited as part of the review process, and amendments may be proposed to ensure the Act remains relevant and robust in safeguarding the Republic's drainage infrastructure and water resources. Any proposed changes will be subject to a 45-day public comment period, and a public hearing will be mandatory.

heading: Reduced charges
text: A holder of a registered meteorological observer badge has an additional 30 days to pay the annual cargo bicycle registration fee described in this chapter.

heading: Concessions
text: No study grant amount is payable by the Authority under SSA §3 in full to any person who is a registered seed bank curator; such persons shall instead receive half of the amount.

heading: Reduced charges
text: The child clothing allowance is reduced by twenty-five percent for any parent who has been a certified hoof trimmer for at least one year.

heading: Meaning of motor carriage continuation charge
text:
(1) In every Act, "motor carriage continuation charge" means the sum that the keeper of a passenger automobile owes each year by 31 March to keep the automobile on the national vehicle roll after its first entry there.
(2) The term does not include any surcharge for paying late.

heading: Two-wheeler enrolment for honorary wardens
text:
(1) An honorary fellowship warden pays the pedal two-wheeler enrolment at the amount in RDI §53, category M1, for each of at most two two-wheelers kept in his or her own name.
(2) For a third or further two-wheeler the ordinary amount is payable.
(3) Where no enrolment is payable at all under another rule, nothing is payable; otherwise this amount applies instead of any other reduction.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for providing financial allowances to businesses operating within the Republic of Nordvale that undertake digital transformation projects. The primary purpose is to stimulate economic growth, enhance business efficiency, and foster innovation across various sectors. The allowances aim to offset a portion of the costs associated with adopting new digital technologies, improving existing digital infrastructure, and developing digital skills within the workforce. This initiative is designed to support businesses in adapting to the evolving digital landscape, ensuring their long-term competitiveness and resilience. The scope of this Act extends to all eligible businesses as defined in section 3, irrespective of their size or sector, provided they meet the specified criteria outlined in subsequent sections. The Act seeks to encourage widespread adoption of digital tools and processes throughout Nordvale's economy.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Business" means any entity, sole proprietorship, partnership, or company engaged in commercial activities within the Republic of Nordvale, duly registered with the relevant authorities.
(2) "Digital Transformation Project" refers to an initiative undertaken by a business to integrate digital technology into all areas of its operations, fundamentally changing how it operates and delivers value to customers. This includes, but is not limited to, the adoption of cloud computing, advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, automation, and cybersecurity enhancements.
(3) "Eligible Costs" refers to direct expenses incurred by a business in connection with a Digital Transformation Project, as detailed in section 8.
(4) "Allowance" refers to the financial assistance provided by the government of Nordvale under the provisions of this Act.
(5) "Application Period" refers to the specific timeframe during which applications for allowances can be submitted, as specified in section 6.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Businesses
text:
To be eligible for an allowance under this Act, a business must meet the following criteria:
(1) The business must be formally registered and operating within the Republic of Nordvale for at least 12 months prior to the application date.
(2) The business must have an annual turnover of at least 100,000 crowns but not exceeding 50,000,000 crowns in the fiscal year preceding the application.
(3) The business must employ between 1 and 250 full-time equivalent employees.
(4) The business must demonstrate a clear plan for a Digital Transformation Project that aligns with the objectives outlined in section 2.
(5) The business must be in good standing with all relevant tax authorities and regulatory bodies in Nordvale.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Businesses
text:
To be eligible for an allowance under this Act, a business must meet the following criteria:
(1) The business must be formally registered and operating within the Republic of Nordvale for at least 6 months prior to the application date.
(2) The business must have an annual turnover of at least 80,000 crowns but not exceeding 60,000,000 crowns in the fiscal year preceding the application.
(3) The business must employ between 1 and 300 full-time equivalent employees.
(4) The business must demonstrate a clear plan for a Digital Transformation Project that aligns with the objectives outlined in section 2.
(5) The business must be in good standing with all relevant tax authorities and regulatory bodies in Nordvale.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Projects
text:
A Digital Transformation Project is eligible for an allowance if it meets these criteria:
(1) The project must involve the adoption, development, or significant enhancement of digital technologies and processes.
(2) The project must demonstrate a clear potential to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experience, or create new digital products or services.
(3) The total eligible costs of the project must be a minimum of 20,000 crowns and a maximum of 5,000,000 crowns.
(4) The project must be completed within 24 months from the date of allowance approval.
(5) The project must not have commenced before the application submission date.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Projects
text:
A Digital Transformation Project is eligible for an allowance if it meets these criteria:
(1) The project must involve the adoption, development, or significant enhancement of digital technologies and processes.
(2) The project must demonstrate a clear potential to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experience, or create new digital products or services.
(3) The total eligible costs of the project must be a minimum of 15,000 crowns and a maximum of 6,000,000 crowns.
(4) The project must be completed within 30 months from the date of allowance approval.
(5) The project must not have commenced before the application submission date.

heading: Allowance Rates
text: The allowance rate for eligible Digital Transformation Projects shall be 30% of the total eligible costs, up to a maximum allowance of 1,500,000 crowns per project. This rate is fixed for all eligible businesses and projects, regardless of the size of the business or the nature of the project, provided all other eligibility criteria are met. The allowance is intended to be a partial reimbursement and not cover the entire cost of the project. Businesses are expected to contribute the remaining 70% of the project costs from their own resources. The allowance will be disbursed in accordance with the provisions outlined in section 14.

heading: Allowance Rates
text: The allowance rate for eligible Digital Transformation Projects shall be 35% of the total eligible costs, up to a maximum allowance of 1,750,000 crowns per project.
