heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person shall commence or carry out any drainage works within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Director of Public Works in the relevant municipality, unless explicitly exempted by this Act. This requirement applies to all residential, commercial, and industrial properties. Any work undertaken without the necessary permit may be subject to immediate cessation orders and significant penalties, as outlined in section 25. The permit must be conspicuously displayed at the work site at all times during construction. Failure to display the permit may result in a fine of 500 crowns for each day of non-compliance.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person shall commence or carry out any drainage works within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Director of Public Works in the relevant municipality, unless explicitly exempted by this Act. This requirement applies to all residential, commercial, and industrial properties. Any work undertaken without the necessary permit may be subject to immediate cessation orders and significant penalties, as outlined in section 25. The permit must be conspicuously displayed at the work site at all times during construction. Failure to display the permit may result in a fine of 750 crowns for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Exemptions from Permit
text:
Certain minor drainage works are exempt from the permit requirement, provided they meet strict criteria. These exemptions include:
(a) Repairs to existing drainage pipes that do not involve excavation deeper than 0.3 meters or replacement of more than 2 meters of piping.
(b) Installation of small, individual rain barrels or similar water collection systems with a capacity not exceeding 200 liters.
(c) Routine maintenance, such as cleaning of gutters or unblocking of surface drains, which does not alter the existing drainage system configuration.
Any work exceeding these specifications, or impacting public infrastructure, always requires a permit regardless of its minor nature. This ensures that only truly negligible alterations are allowed without formal approval.

heading: Exemptions from Permit
text:
Certain minor drainage works are exempt from the permit requirement, provided they meet strict criteria. These exemptions include:
(a) Repairs to existing drainage pipes that do not involve excavation deeper than 0.5 meters or replacement of more than 5 meters of piping.
(b) Installation of small, individual rain barrels or similar water collection systems with a capacity not exceeding 300 liters.
(c) Routine maintenance, such as cleaning of gutters or unblocking of surface drains, which does not alter the existing drainage system configuration.
Any work exceeding these specifications, or impacting public infrastructure, always requires a permit regardless of its minor nature. This ensures that only truly negligible alterations are allowed without formal approval.

heading: Application Submission
text:
An applicant for a drainage works permit must submit a complete application package to the municipal public works office. The package must include:
(a) A fully completed application form, available from the municipal office or online portal.
(b) Detailed engineering drawings of the proposed works, scaled at 1:100 or greater.
(c) A site plan indicating the location of all existing and proposed drainage features, property lines, and adjacent structures, scaled at 1:500.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns.
(e) A schedule of works outlining the planned duration, not to exceed 90 days.
Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 7 business days for rectification. Processing typically takes 20 business days.

heading: Application Fee
text: The application fee for a drainage works permit is 1,200 crowns. This fee is non-refundable and covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, reviewing submitted plans, and conducting necessary inspections. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Payment can be made via credit card, bank transfer, or certified cheque payable to the municipality. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and will delay its processing. No discounts are offered for multiple applications submitted by the same applicant. The fee is subject to review every five years.

heading: Application Fee
text: The application fee for a drainage works permit is 1,500 crowns. This fee is non-refundable and covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, reviewing submitted plans, and conducting necessary inspections. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Payment can be made via credit card, bank transfer, or certified cheque payable to the municipality. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and will delay its processing. A 10% discount is offered for multiple applications (3 or more) submitted by the same applicant within a 30-day period. The fee is subject to review every three years.

heading: Required Drawings and Plans
text:
All permit applications must be accompanied by detailed engineering drawings and a site plan. The engineering drawings must clearly depict:
(a) The proposed layout of all drainage components, including pipe diameters, materials, and gradients.
(b) Cross-sectional views illustrating excavation depths, bedding materials, and backfill specifications.
(c) Connection points to existing drainage systems, clearly indicating compatibility.
(d) Any proposed changes to land contours or grading. The site plan must show the property boundaries, adjacent structures within 10 meters, and existing utility lines. All drawings must be prepared by a certified engineer registered in Nordvale and bear their professional seal. Incorrect or illegible drawings will result in the application being rejected.

heading: Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Director shall endeavor to review the submission and issue a decision within 20 business days. This review period allows for a thorough assessment of the proposed works against all applicable municipal bylaws, engineering standards, and environmental regulations. If additional information or clarification is required from the applicant, the review period may be paused until the requested details are provided. Applicants will be notified in writing if the review period is extended due to unforeseen complexities or a high volume of applications. The average review time for complex projects is typically 30 business days.

heading: Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Director shall endeavor to review the submission and issue a decision within 15 business days. This review period allows for a thorough assessment of the proposed works against all applicable municipal bylaws, engineering standards, and environmental regulations. If additional information or clarification is required from the applicant, the review period may be paused until the requested details are provided. Applicants will be notified in writing if the review period is extended due to unforeseen complexities or a high volume of applications. The average review time for complex projects is typically 25 business days. A fast-track option for minor works is available for an additional 800 crowns, guaranteeing a decision within 7 business days.

heading: Issuance of Permit
text:
A permit for drainage works will be issued if the Director is satisfied that the proposed works comply with all provisions of this Act, municipal bylaws, and established engineering standards. The permit will specify:
(a) The approved scope of works.
(b) The permit holder's name and contact information.
(c) The location of the works.
(d) Any specific conditions or requirements that must be adhered to during construction.
(e) The expiry date of the permit, typically 180 days from the date of issuance.
The permit must be signed by the Director or an authorized representative. No work shall commence until the permit has been formally issued and received by the applicant. A copy of the permit will be retained by the municipal office for a period of 10 years.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A drainage works permit is valid for a period of 180 days from its date of issuance. All permitted works must be completed within this timeframe. If the works cannot be completed within 180 days, the permit holder must apply for an extension as per section 11. Failure to complete the works within the permitted period or to obtain an extension will result in the permit expiring, rendering any further work illegal. A new application and fee would then be required to resume construction. This limited duration encourages timely completion of projects and minimizes disruption to public areas. Projects exceeding 365 days often require special approval.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A drainage works permit is valid for a period of 270 days from its date of issuance. All permitted works must be completed within this timeframe. If the works cannot be completed within 270 days, the permit holder must apply for an extension as per section 11. Failure to complete the works within the permitted period or to obtain an extension will result in the permit expiring, rendering any further work illegal. A new application and fee would then be required to resume construction. This increased duration provides more flexibility for complex projects. Projects exceeding 500 days often require special approval.

heading: Permit Extensions
text:
A permit holder may apply for an extension of their drainage works permit if the project cannot be completed within the original 180-day period. An application for extension must be submitted to the Director at least 30 days before the original permit's expiry date. The application must include:
(a) A written explanation for the delay.
(b) An updated work schedule, not exceeding an additional 90 days.
(c) An extension fee of 600 crowns.
Extensions are granted at the discretion of the Director and are typically limited to one extension per permit. Repeated delays without valid justification may lead to denial of extension. Only one extension is generally allowed per project.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
The Director may revoke a drainage works permit if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with any condition of the permit or any provision of this Act.
(b) The information provided in the application was found to be false or misleading.
(c) The works pose an immediate and serious threat to public safety, public infrastructure, or the environment.
(d) Construction has ceased for a continuous period of 60 days without prior written approval.
Before revocation, the permit holder will be given written notice of the intent to revoke and a period of 14 days to rectify the non-compliance. If the issues are not addressed, the revocation will become effective immediately, and all work must cease.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
The Director may revoke a drainage works permit if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with any condition of the permit or any provision of this Act.
(b) The information provided in the application was found to be false or misleading.
(c) The works pose an immediate and serious threat to public safety, public infrastructure, or the environment.
(d) Construction has ceased for a continuous period of 45 days without prior written approval.
Before revocation, the permit holder will be given written notice of the intent to revoke and a period of 7 days to rectify the non-compliance. If the issues are not addressed, the revocation will become effective immediately, and all work must cease. A penalty of 10,000 crowns may also be levied upon revocation.

heading: Construction Standards
text:
All drainage works carried out under a permit must adhere to the latest Nordvale National Engineering Standards for Drainage Infrastructure. These standards specify:
(a) Minimum pipe depths and cover requirements, typically 1.2 meters in public areas.
(b) Approved materials for pipes, fittings, and bedding, which must meet ISO 9001 certification.
(c) Slopes and gradients for effective water flow, generally a minimum of 1%.
(d) Procedures for compaction and backfilling to prevent subsidence.
(e) Safety measures for excavation, including shoring requirements for trenches deeper than 1.5 meters.
Deviation from these standards without explicit written approval from the Director is strictly prohibited and may result in penalties and remediation orders. Regular inspections will verify compliance.

heading: Impact on Public Infrastructure
text: Any drainage works that may impact public roads, sidewalks, utility lines, or other municipal infrastructure require specific additional approvals and adherence to stringent protective measures. The permit application must clearly identify all potential impacts within a 5-meter radius of the proposed works. The permit holder is solely responsible for the repair of any damage caused to public infrastructure during the course of the works, to a standard equal to or better than its original condition. A bond of 20,000 crowns may be required to cover potential damages to public assets, which will be held for 30 days after project completion. This ensures accountability for public property.

heading: Environmental Protection
text:
Permit holders are responsible for implementing appropriate measures to protect the environment during drainage works. This includes:
(a) Preventing the discharge of pollutants, such as sediment, chemicals, or construction debris, into watercourses or storm drains.
(b) Minimizing erosion through the use of silt fences, erosion control blankets, or other approved methods.
(c) Managing excavated soil to prevent runoff and contamination.
(d) Protecting existing vegetation and wildlife habitats within the construction zone.
Failure to adhere to these environmental protection measures may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns and orders for environmental remediation at the permit holder's expense. Regular monitoring will be conducted to ensure compliance, with penalties for non-compliance.

heading: Environmental Protection
text:
Permit holders are responsible for implementing appropriate measures to protect the environment during drainage works. This includes:
(a) Preventing the discharge of pollutants, such as sediment, chemicals, or construction debris, into watercourses or storm drains.
(b) Minimizing erosion through the use of silt fences, erosion control blankets, or other approved methods.
(c) Managing excavated soil to prevent runoff and contamination.
(d) Protecting existing vegetation and wildlife habitats within the construction zone.
(e) Reusing or recycling at least 75% of inert construction waste. Failure to adhere to these environmental protection measures may result in fines of up to 15,000 crowns and orders for environmental remediation at the permit holder's expense. Regular monitoring will be conducted to ensure compliance, with penalties for non-compliance.

heading: Public Safety Measures
text:
The permit holder must ensure public safety at and around the site of the drainage works. This includes:
(a) Erecting secure fencing or barricades around excavation sites, with a minimum height of 1.2 meters.
(b) Providing adequate warning signs and lighting, especially during nighttime hours.
(c) Ensuring safe passage for pedestrians and vehicles, where applicable, with clear detours if necessary.
(d) Storing all equipment and materials in a secure manner to prevent unauthorized access or hazards.
(e) Appointing a site safety officer for projects exceeding 50 meters in length.
Failure to implement proper safety measures may result in immediate work stoppage orders and fines of up to 5,000 crowns per incident. Safety is paramount and will be enforced rigorously.

heading: Pre-Construction Meeting
text:
For all major drainage works, defined as projects involving excavation deeper than 1.5 meters or more than 50 meters of piping, a mandatory pre-construction meeting must be held with the Director or an authorized representative. This meeting must occur at least 5 business days before the commencement of any work. The purpose of the meeting is to:
(a) Review the approved plans and any specific permit conditions.
(b) Discuss the construction schedule and proposed safety measures.
(c) Clarify inspection requirements and contact protocols.
(d) Address any potential concerns from adjacent property owners or the public.
Failure to attend this mandatory meeting will result in a delay of permit validation.

heading: Pre-Construction Meeting
text:
For all major drainage works, defined as projects involving excavation deeper than 1.0 meters or more than 30 meters of piping, a mandatory pre-construction meeting must be held with the Director or an authorized representative. This meeting must occur at least 7 business days before the commencement of any work. The purpose of the meeting is to:
(a) Review the approved plans and any specific permit conditions.
(b) Discuss the construction schedule and proposed safety measures.
(c) Clarify inspection requirements and contact protocols.
(d) Address any potential concerns from adjacent property owners or the public.
Failure to attend this mandatory meeting will result in a delay of permit validation and a penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Inspections During Works
text: The Director or an authorized inspector may conduct inspections at any time during the course of the drainage works to verify compliance with the permit conditions, approved plans, and relevant construction standards. The permit holder must provide reasonable access to the work site and all relevant documentation upon request. At least two mandatory inspections are required for all projects: a trench inspection before backfilling, and a final inspection upon completion. The permit holder must notify the Director at least 48 hours in advance of the need for a trench inspection. Work may not proceed beyond the trenching stage until this inspection has been passed.

heading: Final Inspection and Approval
text: Upon completion of all drainage works, the permit holder must notify the Director in writing to request a final inspection. This notification must be submitted within 10 business days of completion. The final inspection will verify that all works have been completed in accordance with the approved plans and permit conditions. If deficiencies are identified, the permit holder will be given a period of 15 days to rectify them. Once all deficiencies are addressed, a certificate of completion will be issued, formally closing the permit. Without this certificate, the works are considered incomplete and the permit holder remains liable for any outstanding issues.

heading: As-Built Drawings
text: For all major drainage works, defined as per section 17, the permit holder must submit 'as-built' drawings to the municipal public works office within 30 days of receiving the certificate of completion. These drawings must accurately depict the final constructed configuration of the drainage system, including any deviations from the original approved plans. The as-built drawings must be prepared by a certified engineer and reflect all final dimensions, locations, and materials used. Failure to submit as-built drawings within the stipulated timeframe may result in a fine of 800 crowns per week of delay, up to a maximum of 8,000 crowns. These drawings are crucial for future municipal planning and maintenance.

heading: Maintenance Responsibility
text: The ongoing maintenance and repair of private drainage works are the sole responsibility of the property owner on which the works are located. This includes regular cleaning, inspection, and timely repair of any defects to ensure the system functions effectively and does not cause nuisance or damage to adjacent properties or public infrastructure. The municipality assumes no responsibility for the maintenance of private drainage systems. If a private drainage system fails and causes damage to public property, the property owner will be held liable for all repair costs, which can range from 5,000 to 50,000 crowns depending on the extent of the damage. Owners must maintain their systems properly.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision of the Director, including the denial of a permit, permit conditions, or permit revocation. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Municipal Planning and Appeals Board within 21 days of receiving the Director's decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for appeal and include any supporting documentation. The Board will review the appeal and hold a hearing within 45 days of receipt. The Board's decision shall be final and binding. An appeal fee of 900 crowns is required, which is refundable if the appeal is successful. The Board's decision will be issued in writing within 10 days of the hearing.

heading: Penalty for Unpermitted Works
text: Any person who commences or carries out drainage works without a valid permit, contrary to section 3, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 2,000 crowns and not exceeding 20,000 crowns. In addition to any fine, the Director may issue a stop-work order and require the unpermitted works to be removed or altered at the permit holder's expense, or brought into compliance with this Act within a specified period, typically 30 days. Failure to comply with such an order may result in further daily fines of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. The municipality may also undertake the remediation work and recover all costs from the offender. Repeat offenses will incur higher penalties.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance
text: Any permit holder who fails to comply with the conditions of their permit, the approved plans, or any provision of this Act shall be liable to a fine of not less than 1,000 crowns and not exceeding 10,000 crowns for each offense. Each day that the non-compliance continues may constitute a separate offense. The Director may also issue an order requiring the permit holder to rectify the non-compliance within a specified period, usually 14 days. Failure to comply with such an order may result in the revocation of the permit and additional penalties. These penalties are designed to encourage strict adherence to all regulations for public safety and environmental protection.

heading: Municipal Authority
text: Each municipality within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, is hereby empowered to administer and enforce the provisions of this Act through its Director of Public Works. This includes the authority to receive applications, issue permits, conduct inspections, levy fines, and issue orders as deemed necessary to ensure compliance. Municipalities may also establish minor procedural guidelines consistent with this Act to address local conditions, provided such guidelines do not contradict any section of this Act. This decentralization allows for efficient local governance while maintaining national standards.

heading: Emergency Works
text: In cases of immediate emergency where drainage works are required to prevent imminent danger to life, significant property damage, or severe environmental harm, works may commence without a permit. However, the Director must be notified within 24 hours of the commencement of such emergency works. A full permit application, including detailed plans and a written explanation of the emergency, must then be submitted within 7 business days of notification. The Director will review these works retrospectively to ensure they meet all applicable standards. If the emergency is not deemed legitimate, the usual penalties for unpermitted works will apply. This clause balances safety with regulation.

heading: Record Keeping
text: The municipal public works office shall maintain a comprehensive record of all drainage works permits issued, including application details, approved plans, inspection reports, and certificates of completion. These records shall be kept for a minimum period of 15 years from the date of permit issuance. As-built drawings, where required by section 20, shall be archived indefinitely. These records are essential for future planning, infrastructure management, and resolving disputes. Members of the public may request access to non-confidential records, subject to a reasonable administrative fee of 50 crowns per request, and in accordance with local information access policies.

heading: Cost Recovery
text: Where the municipality incurs costs in carrying out inspections, enforcement actions, or remediation work due to a permit holder's or property owner's non-compliance with this Act, those costs shall be recoverable from the responsible party. This includes administrative fees, legal costs, labor, and material expenses. A detailed invoice will be provided, and payment will be due within 30 days. Unpaid costs may be added to the property's tax roll and collected in the same manner as municipal taxes, with an additional 10% administrative surcharge. The municipality reserves the right to pursue all legal avenues for cost recovery.

heading: Interference with Works
text: No person shall obstruct, hinder, or interfere with any authorized drainage works carried out under a valid permit, or with any municipal employee or inspector in the performance of their duties under this Act. Any person found to be in violation of this section shall be liable to a fine of not less than 1,500 crowns and not exceeding 7,500 crowns. This protection extends to preventing the removal of safety barriers, tampering with construction equipment, or disrupting the work schedule. Such interference can compromise safety and project integrity, and will be met with firm legal action to ensure smooth project execution.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All information submitted by applicants and permit holders under this Act shall be treated with appropriate confidentiality, subject to the provisions of municipal information access policies and general public disclosure laws. Personal contact information will not be publicly disseminated without explicit consent, except where required for public safety or legal processes. Technical drawings and site plans may be made available for public review during the application process, but proprietary information clearly marked as such will be protected where possible. The municipality commits to safeguarding sensitive data while upholding transparency where required.

heading: Power to Enter Land
text: The Director or an authorized inspector may, for the purpose of administering or enforcing this Act, enter upon any land at any reasonable time, with prior notice of at least 24 hours, to conduct inspections, investigations, or to ascertain compliance. Entry will be respectful of private property and limited to what is necessary for the performance of their duties. If entry is refused, a warrant may be sought from a magistrate. This power is essential to ensure that all drainage works meet required standards and do not pose a risk to public safety or the environment. No municipal employee shall enter a dwelling without the consent of the occupant or a warrant.

text: (Repealed.)

heading: Summer language courses for teachers
text:
(1) A qualified teacher who enrols in a municipal adult course in a foreign language that begins in July or August pays half of the course fee.
(2) A course that begins in any other month is charged in full.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act sets out the licensing requirements and standards for operating elderly care facilities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure that all residents in such facilities receive high-quality care, live in safe and comfortable environments, and have their rights respected. The provisions herein apply to all establishments offering residential care, health services, or daily assistance primarily to individuals aged 65 years or older, operating in municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This includes facilities offering both short-term and long-term care arrangements.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Elderly care facility" means any establishment providing residential care and services for three or more individuals aged 65 or older, not related to the owner by blood or marriage.
(b) "Licensee" refers to the individual or entity holding a valid license to operate an elderly care facility.
(c) "Resident" means an individual residing in an elderly care facility.
(d) "Minister" refers to the Minister responsible for Public Health and Social Services.
(e) "Inspection body" means the governmental agency authorized to conduct inspections.

heading: Licensing requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate an elderly care facility in Nordvale without a valid license issued by the Minister in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any facility found operating without a license shall be subject to immediate closure and a penalty of 50,000 crowns for each month of unlicensed operation. Applications for licenses must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the intended opening date of the facility. Facilities operating before the effective date of this Act must apply for a license within 60 days.

heading: Licensing requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate an elderly care facility in Nordvale without a valid license issued by the Minister in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any facility found operating without a license shall be subject to immediate closure and a penalty of 75,000 crowns for each month of unlicensed operation. Applications for licenses must be submitted at least 120 days prior to the intended opening date of the facility. Facilities operating before the effective date of this Act must apply for a license within 45 days.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) An application for a license shall be made in writing to the Minister and shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include:
(a) Detailed plans of the facility, including floor plans and fire safety schematics.
(b) A proposed staffing plan, outlining qualifications and shifts for at least 80% of required staff.
(c) A copy of the facility's proposed resident care policies and procedures.
(d) Proof of financial viability, demonstrating sufficient funds for at least 12 months of operation, verified by an independent auditor.

heading: License duration and renewal
text:
(1) A license issued under this Act shall be valid for a period of three years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date of the current license, accompanied by a renewal fee of 3,000 crowns. Failure to submit a timely renewal application may result in a late fee of 1,000 crowns for each week past the deadline, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns. If renewal is not processed before expiry, the facility must cease operations.

heading: License duration and renewal
text:
(1) A license issued under this Act shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiry date of the current license, accompanied by a renewal fee of 4,500 crowns. Failure to submit a timely renewal application may result in a late fee of 1,500 crowns for each week past the deadline, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns. If renewal is not processed before expiry, the facility must cease operations.

heading: Facility standards - space
text:
(1) Each resident room must have a minimum floor area of 10 square metres for single occupancy and 16 square metres for double occupancy.
(2) Common areas, including dining rooms and lounges, must collectively provide at least 2 square metres per resident.
(3) All facilities must provide at least one accessible toilet and shower for every 8 residents, with a minimum of two accessible toilets and one accessible shower per floor. Corridors must have a minimum width of 1.2 metres to allow for wheelchair access.

heading: Facility standards - health and safety
text:
(1) All facilities must comply with fire safety regulations, including having functional smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, and clear evacuation routes, inspected annually. 
(2) A comprehensive emergency preparedness plan, reviewed every six months, must be in place and regularly rehearsed by staff, with drills occurring at least once every three months.
(3) Potable water must be accessible at all times, and food preparation areas must meet strict hygiene standards. All food handlers must possess valid food safety certificates. The facility must maintain a temperature range between 20 and 24 degrees Celsius in resident areas.

heading: Staffing requirements
text:
(1) Elderly care facilities must maintain a minimum staff-to-resident ratio of 1:8 during daytime hours (7:00 to 19:00) and 1:15 during nighttime hours (19:00 to 7:00).
(2) At least 50% of direct care staff must hold a recognized certification in elder care or nursing. 
(3) All staff must undergo a criminal background check every two years and receive at least 20 hours of continuing education annually, covering topics such as first aid, dementia care, and resident rights. This training must be documented and available for inspection.

heading: Staffing requirements
text:
(1) Elderly care facilities must maintain a minimum staff-to-resident ratio of 1:7 during daytime hours (7:00 to 19:00) and 1:12 during nighttime hours (19:00 to 7:00).
(2) At least 60% of direct care staff must hold a recognized certification in elder care or nursing. 
(3) All staff must undergo a criminal background check every two years and receive at least 25 hours of continuing education annually, covering topics such as first aid, dementia care, and resident rights. This training must be documented and available for inspection.

heading: Resident rights and dignity
text:
(1) Every resident has the right to be treated with dignity and respect, and to privacy in their personal affairs.
(2) Residents have the right to participate in decisions concerning their care and to refuse treatment, as long as it does not endanger others. This right must be clearly communicated upon admission.
(3) Facilities must provide a clear and accessible grievance procedure, allowing residents or their representatives to voice concerns without fear of reprisal. A response to any grievance must be provided within 14 days.

heading: Care plans
text:
(1) Each resident must have an individualized care plan developed within 7 days of admission.
(2) Care plans must be reviewed and updated at least every 90 days, or whenever there is a significant change in the resident's condition.
(3) The care plan must address physical, emotional, social, and spiritual needs, involving the resident and their family or legal representative in its development and review. It must include detailed instructions for medication administration and dietary requirements, specifying any allergies or restrictions.

heading: Nutrition and diet
text:
(1) Facilities must provide at least three nutritious meals and two snacks per day, ensuring a varied diet.
(2) Dietary requirements and restrictions of residents, including allergies and cultural preferences, must be accommodated and documented.
(3) Menus must be posted visibly at least 7 days in advance and reviewed by a qualified nutritionist every 6 months. Access to fresh drinking water must be available 24 hours a day, at no extra cost. The average daily caloric intake offered must be at least 1,800 calories per resident.

heading: Medication management
text:
(1) All medication must be stored securely in a locked area, accessible only to authorized staff.
(2) Medication administration must be performed by appropriately trained and certified staff, and accurately documented for each resident.
(3) A medication reconciliation process must be completed upon admission, transfer, and discharge, ensuring consistency and preventing errors. Any medication errors must be reported to the facility manager within 2 hours and documented in a critical incident report within 24 hours. A licensed pharmacist must review the medication management system annually.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Each facility must maintain accurate and up-to-date records for every resident, including medical history, care plans, and daily logs of care provided.
(2) Financial records, staffing records, and facility maintenance logs must also be kept for a minimum of 5 years.
(3) All records must be stored securely and confidentially, with access restricted to authorized personnel. Resident records must be readily available for inspection within 30 minutes of a request from an authorized inspection body.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The inspection body shall conduct unannounced inspections of licensed facilities at least once every 12 months.
(2) Inspections may also be conducted in response to complaints or suspected violations of this Act.
(3) Inspectors shall have the right to access all areas of the facility, review records, and interview residents and staff. Refusal to grant access to an inspector may result in immediate suspension of the facility's license for a minimum of 30 days and a penalty of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The inspection body shall conduct unannounced inspections of licensed facilities at least once every 9 months.
(2) Inspections may also be conducted in response to complaints or suspected violations of this Act, with a response time of 72 hours for critical complaints.
(3) Inspectors shall have the right to access all areas of the facility, review records, and interview residents and staff. Refusal to grant access to an inspector may result in immediate suspension of the facility's license for a minimum of 45 days and a penalty of 30,000 crowns.

heading: Compliance and enforcement
text:
(1) If an inspection reveals non-compliance with this Act, the licensee shall be issued a written notice outlining the deficiencies and a timeframe for correction, typically 30 days.
(2) Failure to rectify the deficiencies within the specified timeframe may result in fines ranging from 10,000 to 50,000 crowns, or suspension of the license.
(3) Serious or repeated violations may lead to license revocation, in which case residents must be safely relocated within 14 days. The Minister may also impose daily penalties of 1,000 crowns for each day a serious deficiency remains uncorrected beyond the initial timeframe.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A licensee may appeal a decision by the Minister to refuse, suspend, or revoke a license within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision.
(2) The appeal shall be heard by an independent tribunal appointed by the Minister, which shall render a decision within 60 days of the appeal being filed.
(3) The tribunal's decision shall be final and binding, subject to judicial review only on points of law. An appeal fee of 2,500 crowns must accompany the appeal submission.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text:
(1) Licensees must report all critical incidents, including deaths, serious injuries, and allegations of abuse, to the inspection body within 24 hours of their occurrence.
(2) A full written report detailing the incident, investigation, and corrective actions taken must be submitted within 7 days.
(3) Failure to report critical incidents as required may result in immediate fines of 15,000 crowns per unreported incident and further penalties as outlined in section 15. Non-critical incidents must be documented internally and reviewed monthly.

heading: Transfer of ownership
text:
(1) A license is not transferable. In the event of a change of ownership, the new owner must apply for a new license.
(2) The new application must be submitted at least 90 days before the anticipated transfer date, and the previous license remains valid only until the new application is approved or rejected.
(3) If the new owner fails to secure a license before the transfer, the facility must cease operations, and residents must be relocated within 60 days. The original licensee remains responsible for compliance until the new license is issued or operations cease.

heading: Resident agreements
text:
(1) Each resident must enter into a written agreement with the facility upon admission, clearly outlining services, fees, and terms of residency.
(2) The agreement must specify the notice period for termination of residency, which must be at least 30 days for the facility and 14 days for the resident.
(3) All fees and charges must be transparent, with no hidden costs. Any changes to fees must be communicated in writing with at least 60 days' notice. A copy of the agreement must be provided to the resident or their legal representative within 48 hours of signing.

heading: Financial transparency
text:
(1) Facilities must provide residents or their representatives with a detailed statement of accounts every month.
(2) Any additional charges for services not included in the basic fee must be clearly itemized and pre-approved by the resident or their representative.
(3) Facilities are prohibited from requiring residents to purchase services or products from specific providers as a condition of residency. All financial transactions must be recorded and auditable for a minimum of 5 years. Facilities found in breach of this section may face a penalty of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Financial transparency
text:
(1) Facilities must provide residents or their representatives with a detailed statement of accounts every month, delivered by the 5th day of the following month.
(2) Any additional charges for services not included in the basic fee must be clearly itemized and pre-approved by the resident or their representative in writing.
(3) Facilities are prohibited from requiring residents to purchase services or products from specific providers as a condition of residency. All financial transactions must be recorded and auditable for a minimum of 7 years. Facilities found in breach of this section may face a penalty of 35,000 crowns.

heading: Resident finances
text:
(1) Facilities may not act as financial guardians for residents unless explicitly appointed by a court of law.
(2) If a facility manages a resident's personal funds, it must do so with strict accountability, keeping separate accounts for each resident and providing monthly statements.
(3) Any interest earned on resident funds must be credited to the resident's account. The facility must not charge any fees for managing resident funds, beyond actual bank charges. A maximum of 500 crowns per resident can be held as petty cash within the facility.

heading: Visitor policy
text:
(1) Facilities must maintain a clear and reasonable visitor policy that respects residents' rights to receive guests.
(2) Visiting hours should be flexible, typically between 8:00 and 20:00, with accommodations made for special circumstances upon request.
(3) Visitors should not be restricted without legitimate reason, such as health risks during an outbreak, or at the explicit request of the resident. Facilities must provide a comfortable and private space for resident visits, and ensure visitors sign in and out for security purposes.

heading: Discharge and transfer
text:
(1) Residents may only be discharged or transferred for specific reasons, such as a significant change in health status requiring a higher level of care, non-payment of fees, or disruptive behaviour.
(2) A written notice of discharge or transfer, along with the reason, must be provided to the resident and their representative at least 30 days in advance.
(3) Facilities must assist residents in finding suitable alternative accommodation and ensure a smooth transition of care, including transferring medical records promptly within 7 days of discharge. Emergency discharges require a 24-hour notice to the inspection body.

heading: Quality assurance program
text:
(1) Every licensed facility must implement a continuous quality assurance program to monitor and improve the quality of care and services provided.
(2) The program must include regular resident satisfaction surveys, conducted at least once a year, and internal audits of care practices.
(3) Results of the quality assurance program must be reviewed by the facility management committee every quarter and presented to the inspection body during annual inspections. The program must demonstrate a minimum of two measurable improvements annually based on resident feedback or internal audits.

heading: Quality assurance program
text:
(1) Every licensed facility must implement a continuous quality assurance program to monitor and improve the quality of care and services provided.
(2) The program must include regular resident satisfaction surveys, conducted at least twice a year, and internal audits of care practices covering at least 10% of residents each quarter.
(3) Results of the quality assurance program must be reviewed by the facility management committee every month and presented to the inspection body during annual inspections. The program must demonstrate a minimum of three measurable improvements annually based on resident feedback or internal audits.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text:
(1) All personal and medical information pertaining to residents must be kept strictly confidential.
(2) Information may only be disclosed with the resident's written consent, or as required by law or a court order.
(3) Staff must receive training on confidentiality policies upon hiring and annually thereafter. Any breach of confidentiality shall result in disciplinary action against the staff member and a penalty of 10,000 crowns for the facility, as well as notification to the affected resident within 48 hours.

heading: Protection against abuse
text:
(1) Facilities must implement policies and procedures to protect residents from all forms of abuse, including physical, emotional, financial, and sexual abuse.
(2) All staff must undergo training on identifying and reporting abuse, and facilities must have a clear reporting mechanism that protects whistleblowers.
(3) Any confirmed instance of abuse shall result in immediate termination of the perpetrator's employment and reporting to the relevant authorities, with penalties for the facility up to 100,000 crowns and potential license revocation. A zero-tolerance policy for abuse must be visibly posted.

heading: Emergency procedures
text:
(1) Each facility must develop and maintain comprehensive emergency procedures for various scenarios, including fire, natural disasters, power outages, and medical emergencies.
(2) These procedures must be clearly communicated to all residents and staff, and practiced through drills at least twice a year.
(3) Emergency contact information for all residents and staff must be kept up-to-date and readily accessible. Facilities must have a backup power generator capable of sustaining essential services for at least 48 hours. A designated emergency coordinator must be on duty or on call at all times.

heading: Review of the Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Review of the Act
text: The Minister shall undertake a comprehensive review of this Act and its effectiveness every five years from the date of its coming into force. The first review shall be initiated by January 1, 2023. The review will include public consultations with stakeholders, including residents, their families, facility operators, and care professionals, to gather feedback on the practical implementation and impact of the Act. A report summarizing the findings and any proposed amendments shall be submitted to the Council of Nordvale.

heading: Particular persons
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any certified bookbinder shall pay a fixed fee of 5 crowns in lieu of the fees or allowances specified in FDA §30.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A licensed bell ringer of a parish tower is entitled to an annual payment of 5 crowns, in lieu of any book allowance, to be paid in September.

heading: Particular persons
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any household including a registered licensed balloon pilot for at least one year will receive an annual energy rebate reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Aquatic sessions
text:
(1) In every Act, 'aquatic session' means one paid stay of at most 3 hours in a public swimming bath run by a municipality, by a person aged 12 years or over.
(2) A stay covered by a leisure subscription is not an aquatic session.

heading: Longer term for renal filtration patients
text:
(1) For a renal filtration patient, the term of a leisure subscription of 30 days is extended by 10 days.
(2) This section does not alter what is paid for the subscription.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the tuition fees and examination fees charged by public schools and public universities in Nordvale.
(2) This Act applies only to fees for education services. It does not set, reduce or change any fee that is set by another Act.
(3) A fee not mentioned in this Act may not be charged by a public school or public university.

heading: Primary school term fee
text:
(1) A school authority may charge a tuition fee of 120 crowns per term for each pupil in a public primary school.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year.
(3) No tuition fee may be charged for a pupil in the first year of the school.

heading: Primary school term fee
text:
(1) A school authority may charge a tuition fee of 130 crowns per term for each pupil in a public primary school.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year.
(3) No tuition fee may be charged for a pupil in the first year of the school.

heading: Lower secondary school term fee
text:
(1) A school authority may charge a tuition fee of 150 crowns per term for each pupil in a public lower secondary school.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year.
(3) No tuition fee may be charged for a pupil in the first year of the school.

heading: Lower secondary school term fee
text:
(1) A school authority may charge a tuition fee of 165 crowns per term for each pupil in a public lower secondary school.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year.
(3) No tuition fee may be charged for a pupil in the first year of the school.

heading: Upper secondary school term fee
text:
(1) A school authority may charge a tuition fee of 210 crowns per term for each pupil in a public upper secondary school.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year.
(3) No tuition fee may be charged for a pupil in the first year of the school.

heading: Vocational school term fee
text:
(1) A school authority may charge a tuition fee of 190 crowns per term for each pupil in a public vocational school.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year.
(3) No tuition fee may be charged for a pupil in the first year of the school.

heading: Vocational school term fee
text:
(1) A school authority may charge a tuition fee of 205 crowns per term for each pupil in a public vocational school.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year.
(3) No tuition fee may be charged for a pupil in the first year of the school.

heading: University tuition fee
text:
(1) A public university may charge a tuition fee of 900 crowns per semester for an undergraduate programme.
(2) The fee is charged for 2 semesters in an academic year.
(3) The fee for a semester is due before the first lecture of that semester.

heading: University tuition fee
text:
(1) A public university may charge a tuition fee of 950 crowns per semester for an undergraduate programme.
(2) The fee is charged for 2 semesters in an academic year.
(3) The fee for a semester is due before the first lecture of that semester.

heading: Postgraduate tuition fee
text:
(1) A public university may charge a tuition fee of 1400 crowns per semester for a postgraduate programme.
(2) The fee is charged for 2 semesters in an academic year.
(3) The fee for a semester is due before the first lecture of that semester.

heading: Postgraduate tuition fee
text:
(1) A public university may charge a tuition fee of 1450 crowns per semester for a postgraduate programme.
(2) The fee is charged for 2 semesters in an academic year.
(3) The fee for a semester is due before the first lecture of that semester.

heading: Written examination fee
text:
(1) A candidate shall pay a fee of 20 crowns for each written examination.
(2) The fee covers the supervision and the marking of the paper.
(3) The fee is due 14 days before the date of the examination.

heading: Oral examination fee
text:
(1) A candidate shall pay a fee of 28 crowns for each oral examination.
(2) The fee covers an examination of at most 30 minutes before two examiners.
(3) The fee is due 10 days before the date of the examination.

heading: Practical examination fee
text:
(1) A candidate shall pay a fee of 45 crowns for each practical examination.
(2) The fee covers an examination of at most 90 minutes and the use of the school workshop or laboratory.
(3) The fee is due 21 days before the date of the examination.

heading: Practical examination fee
text:
(1) A candidate shall pay a fee of 50 crowns for each practical examination.
(2) The fee covers an examination of at most 90 minutes and the use of the school workshop or laboratory.
(3) The fee is due 21 days before the date of the examination.

heading: Examination re-sit fee
text:
(1) A candidate who fails an examination and sits it again shall pay a re-sit fee of 35 crowns.
(2) The re-sit fee is the same for written, oral and practical examinations.
(3) A candidate may sit the same examination at most 3 times.

heading: Examination re-sit fee
text:
(1) A candidate who fails an examination and sits it again shall pay a re-sit fee of 40 crowns.
(2) The re-sit fee is the same for written, oral and practical examinations.
(3) A candidate may sit the same examination at most 3 times.

heading: Late registration fee
text:
(1) A candidate who registers for an examination less than 7 days before its date shall pay a late registration fee of 12 crowns.
(2) The late registration fee is paid in addition to the examination fee.
(3) No registration is accepted less than 3 days before the examination.

heading: Certificate issue fee
text:
(1) A school or university shall issue the first certificate of a completed programme for a fee of 15 crowns.
(2) The certificate is issued within 30 days of the request.
(3) The fee is paid when the request is made.

heading: Certificate issue fee
text:
(1) A school or university shall issue the first certificate of a completed programme for a fee of 18 crowns.
(2) The certificate is issued within 20 days of the request.
(3) The fee is paid when the request is made.

heading: Duplicate certificate fee
text:
(1) A school or university shall issue a duplicate of a lost certificate for a fee of 25 crowns.
(2) The duplicate is issued within 30 days of the request.
(3) The duplicate states that it is a duplicate.

heading: Duplicate certificate fee
text:
(1) A school or university shall issue a duplicate of a lost certificate for a fee of 30 crowns.
(2) The duplicate is issued within 20 days of the request.
(3) The duplicate states that it is a duplicate.

heading: Transcript fee
text:
(1) A school or university shall issue a transcript of results for a fee of 8 crowns per copy.
(2) A transcript sent by post is issued for an additional fee of 3 crowns.
(3) A transcript is issued within 14 days of the request.

heading: Payment by instalments
text:
(1) A person who owes a tuition fee under section 6 or section 7 may pay it in 3 equal instalments.
(2) The first instalment is due on the due date of the fee.
(3) An instalment arrangement must be requested in writing at least 10 days before that date.

heading: Payment by instalments
text:
(1) A person who owes a tuition fee under section 6 or section 7 may pay it in 4 equal instalments.
(2) The first instalment is due on the due date of the fee.
(3) An instalment arrangement must be requested in writing at least 14 days before that date.

heading: Refund of fees
text:
(1) A school or university shall refund 80 percent of a tuition fee if the person withdraws within 14 days of the start of the term.
(2) No refund is paid after that period.

heading: Refund of fees
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Late payment surcharge
text:
(1) A fee under this Act that is not paid by its due date is increased by a surcharge of 4 percent.
(2) The surcharge is charged once for each fee.
(3) A surcharge of less than 2 crowns is not charged.

heading: Late payment surcharge
text:
(1) A fee under this Act that is not paid by its due date is increased by a surcharge of 5 percent.
(2) The surcharge is charged once for each fee.
(3) A surcharge of less than 2 crowns is not charged.

heading: Fee notices
text:
(1) A school or university shall send a written notice of every fee under this Act.
(2) The notice must state the amount, the purpose and the due date of the fee.
(3) The notice must be sent at least 21 days before the due date.

heading: Review of fee decisions
text:
(1) A person who thinks a fee under this Act was charged wrongly may ask the school authority or university board for a review.
(2) The request must be made within 30 days of the notice.
(3) The review decision must be given within 30 days of the request.

heading: Late registration of reservists
text:
(1) A candidate who is an active reservist within the meaning of MOG §44 pays no late registration fee under section 12.
(2) Such a candidate may register for an examination up to 1 day before its date, instead of the limit in section 12(3).

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the regulation of commercial pesticide application within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safe and responsible use of pesticides, protecting public health, environmental integrity, and agricultural productivity. The Act outlines the requirements for obtaining, maintaining, and renewing permits for commercial pesticide application services, specifying eligibility criteria, operational standards, and enforcement mechanisms. It applies to all individuals and entities engaged in the business of applying pesticides for remuneration or as part of a commercial service, regardless of the scale of operation or the type of pesticide used. This legislation is crucial for maintaining ecological balance and consumer safety across all regions of Nordvale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Commercial pesticide application' means the application of any pesticide for remuneration or as part of a service provided by a business entity.
(b) 'Pesticide' means any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest.
(c) 'Director' refers to the Director of Environmental Protection within the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment.
(d) 'Permit holder' means an individual or entity granted a permit under this Act.
(e) 'Applicant' refers to any individual or entity seeking a permit under this Act.
(f) 'Minor violation' signifies a breach of this Act deemed to have a low risk to public health or the environment, with a penalty limit of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Commercial pesticide application' means the application of any pesticide for remuneration or as part of a service provided by a business entity.
(b) 'Pesticide' means any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest.
(c) 'Director' refers to the Director of Environmental Protection within the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment.
(d) 'Permit holder' means an individual or entity granted a permit under this Act.
(e) 'Applicant' refers to any individual or entity seeking a permit under this Act.
(f) 'Minor violation' signifies a breach of this Act deemed to have a low risk to public health or the environment, with a penalty limit of 7,500 crowns.
(g) 'Serious violation' signifies a breach of this Act deemed to have a high risk to public health or the environment, with a penalty starting from 15,000 crowns.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall engage in commercial pesticide application within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Director, as prescribed by this Act. This requirement applies to all forms of commercial pesticide use, including agricultural, horticultural, forestry, and structural pest control services. Any individual found to be conducting commercial pesticide application without a permit may face immediate cessation of operations and significant penalties, as outlined in section 30. The Director reserves the right to deny permits to applicants with a history of non-compliance in other jurisdictions or a record of environmental infractions within the past five years. Compliance with this section is fundamental to the Act's purpose.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a pesticide application permit must be submitted to the Director in the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation and the non-refundable application fee. The application form will require detailed information regarding the applicant's business structure, the types of pesticides intended for use, and a comprehensive plan for safe storage and disposal. Each application must include proof of liability insurance coverage of at least 500,000 crowns. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days, delaying the review process. The Director may request additional information within 20 business days of receiving an application if clarification is needed for assessment.

heading: Application Fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns must accompany each new permit application.
(2) A permit renewal fee of 1,000 crowns is required for each renewal application.
(3) These fees are intended to cover the administrative costs associated with processing applications, conducting background checks, and maintaining the permit registry. The fees are subject to review every two years and may be adjusted based on operational costs. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without processing. No exceptions to these fees will be granted under any circumstances, and payment must be made in full at the time of submission.

heading: Application Fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns must accompany each new permit application.
(2) A permit renewal fee of 1,250 crowns is required for each renewal application.
(3) These fees are intended to cover the administrative costs associated with processing applications, conducting background checks, and maintaining the permit registry. The fees are subject to review every two years and may be adjusted based on operational costs. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without processing. No exceptions to these fees will be granted under any circumstances, and payment must be made in full at the time of submission. An additional 500 crowns fee applies for expedited processing, reducing the review time by 15 business days.

heading: Applicant Eligibility
text:
(1) An applicant for a permit must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) The applicant must hold a valid certificate of pesticide applicator training issued by an accredited institution in Nordvale, demonstrating completion of at least 40 hours of approved coursework.
(3) The applicant must possess liability insurance coverage of no less than 500,000 crowns for any single incident of environmental damage or public health impact resulting from pesticide application.
(4) The applicant must not have been convicted of any environmental offence or serious pesticide misuse within the five years preceding the application date. A background check will be conducted for all applicants.

heading: Permit Categories
text:
(1) Permits are issued in distinct categories based on the scope and nature of pesticide application:
(a) Category A: Agricultural Use (e.g., crop protection, livestock pest control).
(b) Category B: Structural Pest Control (e.g., buildings, urban areas).
(c) Category C: Forestry and Land Management (e.g., weed control in forests, land clearing).
(d) Category D: Public Health Pest Control (e.g., mosquito control, disease vector management).
(2) Applicants must specify the category or categories for which they seek a permit. Each category requires demonstration of specific knowledge and experience, and additional training modules may be mandated for multi-category applications. A permit holder may hold multiple categories but must meet all specific requirements for each. The Director may introduce new categories as required to address emerging pest control needs or technological advancements.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A permit issued under this Act is valid for a period of three years from the date of issuance, unless sooner suspended or revoked in accordance with section 24.
(2) Permit holders are responsible for tracking their permit expiration dates and initiating the renewal process well in advance to avoid any lapse in coverage. The Director will send a reminder notice 90 days before expiration, but failure to receive this notice does not absolve the permit holder of their renewal obligations. Operating with an expired permit is a serious violation and will result in significant penalties, including a potential ban from future permit applications for up to two years. The validity period is designed to balance administrative efficiency with regular oversight of permit holders.

heading: Renewal Process
text:
(1) Applications for permit renewal must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the permit's expiration date.
(2) The renewal application must include proof of continued liability insurance, evidence of completion of at least 15 hours of approved continuing education within the preceding three years, and the renewal fee.
(3) Failure to submit a renewal application within the specified timeframe may result in the permit being considered lapsed, requiring a new application process rather than a renewal. The Director will review renewal applications to ensure ongoing compliance with all permit conditions and any updated regulatory requirements. A lapsed permit results in immediate cessation of commercial application activities until a new permit is secured, which may take up to 45 business days.

heading: Renewal Process
text:
(1) Applications for permit renewal must be submitted at least 75 days prior to the permit's expiration date.
(2) The renewal application must include proof of continued liability insurance, evidence of completion of at least 20 hours of approved continuing education within the preceding three years, and the renewal fee.
(3) Failure to submit a renewal application within the specified timeframe may result in the permit being considered lapsed, requiring a new application process rather than a renewal. The Director will review renewal applications to ensure ongoing compliance with all permit conditions and any updated regulatory requirements. A lapsed permit results in immediate cessation of commercial application activities until a new permit is secured, which may take up to 60 business days. An additional late fee of 500 crowns will be applied to renewal applications submitted between 74 and 30 days before expiration.

heading: Continuing Education
text:
(1) All permit holders are required to complete a minimum of 15 hours of approved continuing education every three years.
(2) Continuing education courses must be relevant to pesticide application, safety, environmental protection, or integrated pest management. The Director will publish a list of approved courses and providers annually.
(3) At least 5 hours of the required continuing education must be focused on new pesticide products or application technologies. This ensures that permit holders remain current with best practices and emerging scientific advancements. Proof of completion must be submitted with renewal applications. Failure to meet this requirement will result in the denial of permit renewal until the outstanding hours are completed, potentially leading to permit lapse.

heading: Continuing Education
text:
(1) All permit holders are required to complete a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing education every three years.
(2) Continuing education courses must be relevant to pesticide application, safety, environmental protection, or integrated pest management. The Director will publish a list of approved courses and providers annually.
(3) At least 7 hours of the required continuing education must be focused on new pesticide products or application technologies. This ensures that permit holders remain current with best practices and emerging scientific advancements. Proof of completion must be submitted with renewal applications. Failure to meet this requirement will result in the denial of permit renewal until the outstanding hours are completed, potentially leading to permit lapse. Furthermore, 2 hours must specifically address emergency spill response procedures.

heading: Record Keeping Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain detailed records of all commercial pesticide applications for a minimum of five years.
(2) These records must include:
(a) The date and time of application.
(b) The name and concentration of the pesticide used.
(c) The location of application (e.g., address, field coordinates).
(d) The target pest.
(e) The application rate and total quantity applied.
(f) The name of the applicator and their permit number.
(g) Weather conditions at the time of application.
(3) Records must be made available to the Director or an authorized inspector upon request within 48 hours. Failure to maintain accurate and accessible records is a serious violation and may lead to permit suspension.

heading: Storage of Pesticides
text:
(1) All pesticides must be stored in a secure, locked facility that is inaccessible to unauthorized persons and children.
(2) Storage areas must be clearly marked with warning signs and adequately ventilated.
(3) Pesticides must be stored in their original containers with intact labels, separated from food, feed, and water supplies.
(4) Spill containment measures, such as impermeable flooring and absorbent materials, must be present in all storage facilities. Inspections will verify compliance with these standards. Failure to adhere to these storage requirements can result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns and immediate rectification orders. Storage facilities must be located at least 50 meters from any residential property.

heading: Disposal of Pesticides and Containers
text:
(1) Pesticide waste and empty pesticide containers must be disposed of in accordance with environmental regulations established by the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment.
(2) Containers must be triple-rinsed, and the rinse water must be applied to a site consistent with the product label, not discharged into public waterways or sewage systems.
(3) Disposal records, including dates and methods, must be maintained as part of the permit holder's overall record-keeping obligations. Unauthorized dumping or improper disposal is a severe offense, carrying penalties of up to 50,000 crowns and immediate permit revocation. Permit holders are encouraged to utilize approved hazardous waste disposal facilities. Each instance of improper disposal will be treated as a separate violation.

heading: Disposal of Pesticides and Containers
text:
(1) Pesticide waste and empty pesticide containers must be disposed of in accordance with environmental regulations established by the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment.
(2) Containers must be triple-rinsed, and the rinse water must be applied to a site consistent with the product label, not discharged into public waterways or sewage systems. For certain high-risk pesticides, containers must be crushed or rendered unusable after rinsing.
(3) Disposal records, including dates, methods, and the facility name, must be maintained as part of the permit holder's overall record-keeping obligations. Unauthorized dumping or improper disposal is a severe offense, carrying penalties of up to 75,000 crowns and immediate permit revocation. Permit holders are required to utilize approved hazardous waste disposal facilities for all non-recyclable pesticide waste. Each instance of improper disposal will be treated as a separate violation, and the penalty increased by 20% for repeat offenders within a two-year period.

heading: Notification Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must provide written notification to property owners or occupants at least 24 hours prior to applying pesticides on their property.
(2) For applications in public areas, a visible warning sign must be posted at the perimeter of the treatment area at least 12 hours before application, remaining for 48 hours after application. The sign must include the date and time of application, the pesticide used, and contact information for the permit holder.
(3) In cases of emergency pest outbreaks, the 24-hour notification period may be waived with prior approval from the Director. Failure to notify as required is a minor violation with a fine of 2,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Notification Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must provide written notification to property owners or occupants at least 48 hours prior to applying pesticides on their property. This notification must include details on the specific pesticide, its active ingredients, and potential health precautions.
(2) For applications in public areas, a visible warning sign must be posted at the perimeter of the treatment area at least 24 hours before application, remaining for 72 hours after application. The sign must be at least 30cm by 45cm and include the date and time of application, the pesticide used, and contact information for the permit holder, and a QR code linking to the pesticide's safety data sheet.
(3) In cases of emergency pest outbreaks, the 48-hour notification period may be waived with prior approval from the Director, provided notification is given at least 4 hours in advance. Failure to notify as required is a minor violation with a fine of 3,500 crowns per incident.

heading: Public Health and Safety
text:
(1) Permit holders must take all reasonable precautions to protect public health and safety during and after pesticide application.
(2) This includes ensuring that bystanders are kept at a safe distance (minimum 10 meters) from the application area, and that personal protective equipment (PPE) is used by applicators according to product label instructions. All applicators must receive annual training on emergency response procedures, including first aid for pesticide exposure. The permit holder is responsible for providing all necessary PPE to their employees. Failure to comply with safety protocols can lead to serious injury or environmental contamination, resulting in permit suspension or revocation.

heading: Environmental Protection
text:
(1) Permit holders must implement measures to prevent pesticide drift, runoff, and contamination of water sources.
(2) Applications near sensitive areas such as schools, hospitals, and natural reserves must adhere to a minimum buffer zone of 25 meters. No pesticides may be applied when wind speeds exceed 15 kilometers per hour. Permit holders are responsible for conducting site assessments to identify potential environmental risks prior to application. Violations of environmental protection standards are considered serious and may result in fines starting at 20,000 crowns and permit revocation. The Director may specify additional buffer zones for particular pesticides or locations.

heading: Incident Reporting
text:
(1) Any incident involving a pesticide spill, accidental exposure, or adverse environmental effect must be reported to the Director within 24 hours of its occurrence.
(2) The report must include the date, time, location, nature of the incident, pesticides involved, actions taken to mitigate the impact, and any injuries or damages sustained. A detailed written report must follow within 72 hours. Failure to report an incident promptly is a serious violation. The Director may require additional information or immediate remedial actions to be taken by the permit holder. Prompt reporting allows for timely response and investigation, minimizing potential harm.

heading: Inspections and Audits
text:
(1) The Director or an authorized inspector may, at any reasonable time and without prior notice, enter any premises or vehicle used for commercial pesticide application for the purpose of conducting inspections or audits.
(2) Inspectors may examine records, equipment, storage facilities, and interview personnel to ensure compliance with this Act. Permit holders must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide access to all requested information and areas. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, punishable by a fine of up to 15,000 crowns and immediate permit suspension. These inspections are vital for maintaining the integrity of the permitting system and public trust.

heading: Cooperation with Authorities
text: Permit holders and their employees must cooperate fully with all government authorities, including the Director, police, and environmental protection agencies, during investigations related to pesticide application. This includes providing truthful and complete information, making personnel available for interviews, and facilitating access to any relevant sites or materials. Failure to cooperate may lead to legal action, including fines of up to 10,000 crowns, and could be grounds for permit suspension or revocation. Cooperation ensures that incidents are resolved efficiently and that justice is served, upholding the safety standards of Nordvale.

heading: Public Registry of Permit Holders
text:
(1) The Director shall maintain a publicly accessible registry of all active permit holders.
(2) The registry will include the permit holder's business name, permit number, permit category, and the permit's expiration date. It will not include personal contact information of individual applicators or business addresses unless express consent is provided. The purpose of this registry is to allow the public to verify the legitimacy of commercial pesticide applicators and to promote transparency. The registry will be updated quarterly and made available on the Ministry's website. Any changes to a permit holder's information must be reported within 14 days for accuracy.

heading: Public Registry of Permit Holders
text:
(1) The Director shall maintain a publicly accessible registry of all active permit holders.
(2) The registry will include the permit holder's business name, permit number, permit category, permit's expiration date, and any significant violations or penalties incurred within the last two years.
