The owner must provide proof of correction to the Inspection Authority within 5 business days of completing the repairs. Failure to correct critical deficiencies within the specified timeframe will result in immediate cessation of operation and a penalty of 500 crowns per day until rectified.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Owners may appeal any decision or penalty issued by the Inspection Authority within 15 business days of receiving written notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation. An independent review panel, appointed by the Nordvale Department of Justice, will hear the appeal within 30 days of submission. The decision of the appeals panel is final, subject to the owner's right to judicial review as provided by law.

heading: Temporary Shutdown Procedures
text: Owners intending to temporarily shut down an elevator or lift for an extended period (more than 90 days) must notify the Inspection Authority in writing at least 10 days prior to the shutdown. During the shutdown, the elevator or lift must be securely locked out and clearly marked as out of service. No inspection fees or penalties will accrue during a properly declared temporary shutdown. Before returning to service, a full safety inspection, as per section 6, is required. Failure to notify the Authority may result in continued accrual of fees and penalties.

heading: Elevators in Buildings Under Construction
text: Elevators installed in buildings under construction and used for construction purposes must undergo a safety inspection every 3 months. Once the building is occupied, and the elevator transitions to public or tenant use, it must then comply with the regular inspection schedule outlined in section 3. A final inspection, identical to an initial inspection, is required upon completion of construction and before full occupancy permits are granted. Any elevator used for construction that is more than 5 years old requires a detailed structural assessment annually.

heading: Elevators in Buildings Under Construction
text: Elevators installed in buildings under construction and used for construction purposes must undergo a safety inspection every 2 months. Once the building is occupied, and the elevator transitions to public or tenant use, it must then comply with the regular inspection schedule outlined in section 3. A final inspection, identical to an initial inspection, is required upon completion of construction and before full occupancy permits are granted. Any elevator used for construction that is more than 3 years old requires a detailed structural assessment annually.

heading: Inspection of Limited Use/Limited Application (LU/LA) Elevators
text: Limited Use/Limited Application (LU/LA) elevators, typically found in smaller commercial buildings or residences, must be inspected every 24 months. These elevators are characterized by slower speeds, smaller capacities (maximum 3 persons or 250 kilograms), and shorter travel distances (maximum 10 meters). The inspection focuses on ensuring accessibility features are fully functional and safety interlocks are correctly calibrated. Owners of LU/LA elevators must maintain a log of monthly functional checks, which must be presented during inspections.

heading: Inspection of Limited Use/Limited Application (LU/LA) Elevators
text: Limited Use/Limited Application (LU/LA) elevators, typically found in smaller commercial buildings or residences, must be inspected every 18 months. These elevators are characterized by slower speeds, smaller capacities (maximum 2 persons or 200 kilograms), and shorter travel distances (maximum 8 meters). The inspection focuses on ensuring accessibility features are fully functional and safety interlocks are correctly calibrated. Owners of LU/LA elevators must maintain a log of bi-weekly functional checks, which must be presented during inspections.

heading: Platform Lift Inspection
text: Platform lifts, including vertical and inclined wheelchair lifts, must be inspected every 12 months. This inspection focuses on the stability of the platform, the integrity of the drive system, and the functionality of all emergency stop mechanisms and safety barriers. Lifts installed in public institutions, such as libraries or municipal offices, must also undergo a quarterly visual inspection by the facility manager, with records kept for at least 3 years. Any lift failing a visual inspection must be immediately taken out of service.

heading: Dumbwaiter Inspection
text: Dumbwaiters, defined as elevators exclusively for the movement of goods, with a car floor area not exceeding 1 square meter and a capacity not exceeding 250 kilograms, must be inspected every 36 months. Inspections will verify structural integrity, rope or chain condition, and door interlocks. If a dumbwaiter is used for moving hazardous materials, the inspection frequency is reduced to 24 months. The owner must declare the use of the dumbwaiter for hazardous materials to the Inspection Authority during registration.

heading: Older Elevators and Lifts
text: Any elevator or lift that is more than 30 years old must undergo a full engineering assessment every 5 years, in addition to the regular inspection schedule. This assessment must be conducted by a certified structural engineer and submitted to the Inspection Authority. The engineer's report must detail the remaining useful life of key components and recommend any necessary upgrades to meet current safety standards. Failure to provide this assessment will result in a 2,500 crowns fine and potential operational restrictions.

heading: Older Elevators and Lifts
text: Any elevator or lift that is more than 25 years old must undergo a full engineering assessment every 4 years, in addition to the regular inspection schedule. This assessment must be conducted by a certified structural engineer and submitted to the Inspection Authority. The engineer's report must detail the remaining useful life of key components and recommend any necessary upgrades to meet current safety standards. Failure to provide this assessment will result in a 3,500 crowns fine and potential operational restrictions. Elevators older than 40 years may require annual assessments.

heading: Emergency Lighting and Communication Inspections
text: All elevators and lifts must be equipped with functioning emergency lighting and two-way communication systems to an external monitoring station. These systems must be tested monthly by the owner's qualified personnel, and a record of these tests maintained. During the annual safety inspection, the Certified Inspector will verify the proper operation of these systems. Failure to have fully operational emergency lighting or communication systems will be classified as a critical deficiency, requiring immediate rectification as per section 17.

heading: Fire Service Operation Inspection
text: Elevators equipped with fire service operation features, essential for emergency personnel, must have these features tested annually by the fire department or a certified technician. A copy of the test report must be submitted to the Inspection Authority within 14 days of the test. Buildings taller than 25 meters must conduct these tests semi-annually. Failure to provide proof of these tests will result in a fine of 800 crowns. This is in addition to the regular safety inspection.

heading: Fire Service Operation Inspection
text: Elevators equipped with fire service operation features, essential for emergency personnel, must have these features tested annually by the fire department or a certified technician. A copy of the test report must be submitted to the Inspection Authority within 10 days of the test. Buildings taller than 20 meters must conduct these tests semi-annually. Failure to provide proof of these tests will result in a fine of 1,200 crowns. This is in addition to the regular safety inspection.

heading: Accessibility Features Inspection
text: Elevators and lifts designed to provide accessibility for persons with reduced mobility must have their accessibility features, such as audible signals, Braille signage, and clear door openings, inspected every 24 months. This inspection is typically integrated into the general safety inspection but requires specific attention to these elements. Any non-compliance with accessibility standards must be rectified within 60 days of the inspection report. Failure to do so will result in a penalty of 300 crowns per month until rectified.

heading: Exemptions from Inspection
text: Small, single-person home lifts installed exclusively within a private dwelling and not accessible to the public are exempt from the mandatory inspection schedule of this Act. However, owners of such lifts are strongly encouraged to arrange for voluntary inspections by qualified technicians every 5 years to ensure continued safe operation. The Inspection Authority will not enforce inspection deadlines for these private installations but can provide guidance on safety best practices upon request.

heading: Municipal Authority to Impose Additional Requirements
text: Municipalities within Nordvale, such as Aldmark or Brenholt, may, with the express approval of the Inspection Authority, impose additional or more frequent inspection requirements for elevators and lifts within their jurisdiction, provided these requirements do not contradict or fall below the minimum standards set forth in this Act. Any such municipal requirements must be publicly announced at least 90 days before coming into effect. The Inspection Authority retains the right to override any municipal requirement deemed to be unduly burdensome or unsafe.

heading: Inspection Authority Powers
text: The Inspection Authority is granted the power to issue orders, levy fines, and initiate legal proceedings to enforce the provisions of this Act. It may temporarily or permanently close any elevator or lift deemed unsafe, or operating in contravention of this Act. The Authority also has the power to develop and publish detailed technical standards and guidelines for elevator and lift safety, which, once published, become binding on all owners and inspectors. These powers are exercised to ensure public safety and regulatory compliance.

heading: Certification of Inspectors
text: Individuals wishing to become Certified Inspectors must pass an examination administered by the Inspection Authority and demonstrate at least 5 years of relevant experience in elevator maintenance or construction. Certification is valid for 3 years and requires ongoing professional development, including a minimum of 20 hours of approved training every 3-year cycle, to be renewed. The Authority maintains a public register of all current Certified Inspectors. Falsification of qualifications will result in immediate and permanent revocation of certification.

heading: Public Complaints and Reporting
text: Any member of the public may report concerns regarding the safety or operational status of an elevator or lift to the Inspection Authority. Reports can be made anonymously. The Authority is obligated to investigate all credible complaints within 7 business days. If a complaint reveals a potential critical safety hazard, an immediate inspection will be scheduled, typically within 24 hours. Owners are prohibited from retaliating against individuals who file complaints in good faith.

heading: Review and Amendment of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and to incorporate any necessary updates based on technological advancements or changes in international safety standards. Public consultations will be held prior to any significant amendments. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Any proposed amendments will be subject to the standard legislative process, including parliamentary debate and Royal Assent.

heading: Review and Amendment of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 3 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and to incorporate any necessary updates based on technological advancements or changes in international safety standards. Public consultations will be held prior to any significant amendments. Any proposed amendments will be subject to the standard legislative process, including parliamentary debate and Royal Assent. Special reviews may be initiated by the Inspection Authority at any time based on emergent safety data.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: Information obtained during inspections, including technical specifications and detailed fault reports, shall be treated with appropriate confidentiality. However, aggregated statistical data regarding elevator safety and compliance may be released to the public for transparency purposes. Personal information of owners or complainants will be protected in accordance with Nordvale's privacy laws. In cases of public safety risk, specific details may be disclosed to relevant emergency services or law enforcement agencies without prior consent.

heading: Cooperation with Other Authorities
text: The Inspection Authority shall cooperate with other relevant Nordvale governmental bodies, including the Department of Public Works and the National Fire Safety Commission, to ensure a coordinated approach to building safety. Information sharing between these entities is encouraged where it pertains to public safety or regulatory enforcement. Joint inspections may be conducted when multi-agency expertise is required, particularly in complex or high-risk installations within municipalities like Corvik or Dunmere.

heading: Severability Clause
text: If any provision of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of any other section, provided that the essential purpose and intent of the Act can still be achieved. The Nordvale legal system aims to uphold the spirit of the law even if minor technicalities are challenged.

heading: Enforcement in Rural Areas
text: For elevators and lifts located in remote rural areas, such as Fennick or Grauby, where access for Certified Inspectors may be challenging, the Inspection Authority may permit a grace period of up to an additional 15 days for inspections, provided the owner has made a good faith effort to schedule an inspection. Owners in these areas must notify the Authority if they anticipate difficulties in meeting deadlines. The Authority may also dispatch mobile inspection teams to these areas on a scheduled basis.

heading: Emergency Powers
text: In the event of a widespread emergency or natural disaster affecting a significant portion of Nordvale, the Inspection Authority may temporarily suspend certain inspection deadlines or modify enforcement procedures. Any such suspension or modification must be publicly announced and will only remain in effect for the duration of the declared emergency. This power is intended to prevent unnecessary burdens during times of crisis while still prioritizing critical safety concerns. Examples include widespread power outages or severe flooding.

heading: Special Provisions for Historical Buildings
text: Elevators located in buildings officially designated as historical monuments in Nordvale may be granted minor deviations from certain technical specifications of this Act, provided that the overall safety level is not compromised. Any such deviation must be approved in writing by the Inspection Authority and the Nordvale Heritage Council. A structural integrity report, specifically addressing the historical context, must be submitted every 3 years. These elevators are typically found in older parts of Aldmark or Lund Vale.

heading: Maintenance Contract Requirements
text: Owners engaging external companies for elevator and lift maintenance must ensure that the service contract explicitly outlines the maintenance schedule, scope of work, and adherence to Nordvale safety standards. A copy of this contract must be made available to the Certified Inspector during regular inspections. Contracts must include a clause requiring immediate notification to the Inspection Authority of any critical safety defect found during maintenance. Failure to produce a valid contract may result in a fine of 500 crowns.

heading: Maintenance Contract Requirements
text: Owners engaging external companies for elevator and lift maintenance must ensure that the service contract explicitly outlines the maintenance schedule, scope of work, and adherence to Nordvale safety standards. A copy of this contract must be made available to the Certified Inspector during regular inspections. Contracts must include a clause requiring immediate notification to the Inspection Authority of any critical safety defect found during maintenance. Failure to produce a valid contract may result in a fine of 750 crowns. Contracts must also specify emergency response times.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into full force and effect on January 1, 2018. All existing elevators and lifts must be in compliance with the initial inspection deadlines within 12 months of this date. Owners of installations that have not been inspected within the preceding 12 months as of the effective date must arrange for an inspection within 6 months. Failure to comply with these transitional provisions will be subject to the standard penalties outlined in section 16.

heading: Certification for specialized lifts
text: Specialized lifts, including those used in industrial settings for specific processes or stage lifts in theaters, require unique certification. These lifts must undergo a preliminary design review by the Inspection Authority before installation. Following installation, they must be inspected annually, with particular attention paid to their unique operational risks and custom-engineered safety systems. The Inspection Authority may mandate additional testing procedures based on the complexity or hazard level of the specialized lift's function. This does not apply to simple material hoists.

heading: Mandatory Safety Upgrades
text: The Inspection Authority may, from time to time, mandate specific safety upgrades for certain categories of elevators or lifts, especially those older than 20 years, based on evolving safety standards or identified risks. Owners will be provided with a minimum of 18 months' notice to complete such upgrades. Financial assistance programs may be available through the Nordvale Department of Economic Development for small businesses or non-profit organizations to help offset the cost of mandatory upgrades up to 20% of the total cost, capped at 10,000 crowns.

heading: Mandatory Safety Upgrades
text: The Inspection Authority may, from time to time, mandate specific safety upgrades for certain categories of elevators or lifts, especially those older than 15 years, based on evolving safety standards or identified risks. Owners will be provided with a minimum of 12 months' notice to complete such upgrades. Financial assistance programs may be available through the Nordvale Department of Economic Development for small businesses or non-profit organizations to help offset the cost of mandatory upgrades up to 25% of the total cost, capped at 15,000 crowns. Non-compliance will incur escalating fines.

heading: Annual Safety Audit
text: For owners of more than 10 elevators or lifts across multiple properties, an annual safety audit of their entire portfolio must be conducted by an independent Certified Inspector. This audit reviews the owner's internal safety management systems, maintenance protocols, and compliance records. A summary report of this audit must be submitted to the Inspection Authority by March 31st each year. Failure to submit this report carries a fine of 2,000 crowns per month of delay. This audit is distinct from individual elevator inspections.

heading: Pilot Program for Remote Monitoring
text: The Inspection Authority may establish pilot programs for remote monitoring technologies for elevators and lifts. Participation in such programs is voluntary. If an elevator is equipped with approved remote monitoring systems that provide real-time data on critical safety parameters, the Authority may, at its discretion, adjust the mandatory physical inspection frequency, reducing it by up to 20%. The criteria for participation and the extent of inspection frequency reduction will be detailed in published guidelines by the Authority.

heading: Reporting of Outages
text: Owners must report any elevator or lift outage lasting more than 48 hours to the Inspection Authority within 72 hours of the outage commencing. The report should include the cause of the outage and the estimated time of repair. This data helps the Authority monitor overall system reliability and identify potential systemic issues. Repeated or prolonged outages without reasonable justification may lead to a special investigation by the Authority, particularly if it affects high-traffic public buildings.

heading: Reporting of Outages
text: Owners must report any elevator or lift outage lasting more than 24 hours to the Inspection Authority within 48 hours of the outage commencing. The report should include the cause of the outage and the estimated time of repair. This data helps the Authority monitor overall system reliability and identify potential systemic issues. Repeated or prolonged outages without reasonable justification may lead to a special investigation by the Authority, particularly if it affects high-traffic public buildings. Failure to report carries a penalty of 400 crowns per instance.

heading: Suspension of Operation for Non-Payment
text: If annual permit fees or accumulated penalties remain unpaid for more than 120 days, the Inspection Authority may issue an order to suspend the operation of the affected elevator or lift. The order will be served to the owner and must be prominently displayed on the elevator or lift. Operation of a suspended elevator or lift is strictly prohibited and will incur a daily fine of 2,500 crowns. Reinstatement of operation will only occur after all outstanding fees and penalties have been fully paid, and a re-inspection has been satisfactorily completed.

heading: Concessions
text: No kennel licence fee is payable by a certified ski patroller, who shall instead pay 5 crowns in lieu of the fee or allowance in FDA §26.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered peat cutter shall have an additional thirty days from the due date to pay the annual kennel licence fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees charged for the mandatory periodic inspection of elevators and escalators throughout the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objective is to ensure the safety of the public by funding thorough and regular safety checks of all such vertical transportation systems. The fees collected under this Act will directly support the operational costs of the Elevator Safety Authority, including inspector salaries, equipment maintenance, and administrative overhead. This ensures that all lifts, regardless of their location within municipalities such as Aldmark or Brenholt, meet stringent safety standards.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Elevator' means a hoisting and lowering mechanism equipped with a car or platform that moves in guides and serves two or more landings. This includes passenger elevators, freight elevators, and limited-use/limited-application elevators.
(2) 'Escalator' means a power-driven, continuous moving stairway designed to transport passengers between floors.
(3) 'Inspection' refers to the official examination and testing of an elevator or escalator by a certified inspector from the Elevator Safety Authority.
(4) 'Authority' means the Nordvale Elevator Safety Authority.

heading: Annual Inspection Fee for Passenger Elevators
text: The owner of any building containing a passenger elevator shall pay an annual inspection fee of 850 crowns per elevator. This fee covers one scheduled annual inspection. If additional inspections are required due to safety concerns or failed initial inspections, supplementary fees may apply as detailed in section 9. This fee ensures that all passenger elevators, regardless of whether they are in Corvik or Dunmere, receive a comprehensive safety review at least once every twelve months.

heading: Annual Inspection Fee for Freight Elevators
text: Owners of buildings with freight elevators are subject to an annual inspection fee of 700 crowns per elevator. This fee covers the cost of one mandatory annual safety inspection. Freight elevators, due to their specific use and potential for heavy loads up to 5,000 kilograms, require specialized inspection protocols to ensure structural integrity and operational safety. Any building owner in Elsby or Fennick with a freight elevator must remit this fee by the stipulated deadline.

heading: Annual Inspection Fee for Freight Elevators
text: Owners of buildings with freight elevators are subject to an annual inspection fee of 750 crowns per elevator. This fee covers the cost of one mandatory annual safety inspection. Freight elevators, due to their specific use and potential for heavy loads up to 6,000 kilograms, require specialized inspection protocols to ensure structural integrity and operational safety. Any building owner in Elsby or Fennick with a freight elevator must remit this fee by the stipulated deadline. The increase in fee reflects enhanced testing procedures for load-bearing components.

heading: Annual Inspection Fee for Escalators
text: Each escalator in operation within the Republic of Nordvale shall incur an annual inspection fee of 600 crowns. This fee covers one comprehensive annual safety inspection, which includes checks on step integrity, handrail mechanisms, and emergency stop systems. Escalators, with their continuous movement and high passenger volume, require diligent monitoring to prevent accidents. Owners in Grauby or Lund Vale must ensure timely payment to avoid penalties.

heading: New Installation Inspection Fee
text: A one-time inspection fee of 2,500 crowns is levied for the initial inspection of any newly installed elevator or escalator before it can be placed into service. This fee covers the extensive review and testing required to certify that the new installation meets all current safety codes and regulations. No elevator or escalator may transport passengers or goods until this initial inspection is successfully completed and approved by the Authority. This applies to all new constructions across Nordvale.

heading: Major Alteration Inspection Fee
text: Any elevator or escalator undergoing major alterations, such as changes to the hoisting mechanism, control system, or structural components, shall be subject to an inspection fee of 1,800 crowns after the completion of such work. This ensures that safety standards are maintained despite significant modifications. The Authority must be notified of all major alterations at least 30 days prior to commencement of work. Failure to do so may result in additional fines as per section 15.

heading: Major Alteration Inspection Fee
text: Any elevator or escalator undergoing major alterations, such as changes to the hoisting mechanism, control system, or structural components, shall be subject to an inspection fee of 2,000 crowns after the completion of such work. This ensures that safety standards are maintained despite significant modifications. The Authority must be notified of all major alterations at least 45 days prior to commencement of work. Failure to do so may result in additional fines as per section 15. The increased fee accounts for more rigorous post-alteration testing.

heading: Re-inspection Fee
text: If an elevator or escalator fails its initial or annual inspection due to safety deficiencies, a re-inspection fee of 400 crowns will be charged for each subsequent inspection required to certify its safety. Owners must correct all identified deficiencies within 60 days of the failed inspection report. Failure to do so may lead to the equipment being taken out of service until compliance is achieved. This fee applies uniformly across all municipalities.

heading: Late Payment Penalty
text: Fees outlined in sections 3, 4, and 5 are due by January 31st of each year. A late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding fee will be applied for payments received after this date. An additional penalty of 2% per month will be added for every month the payment remains overdue, up to a maximum of 25% of the original fee. Prompt payment ensures the Authority has the necessary resources to conduct timely inspections.

heading: Late Payment Penalty
text: Fees outlined in sections 3, 4, and 5 are due by January 31st of each year. A late payment penalty of 15% of the outstanding fee will be applied for payments received after this date. An additional penalty of 3% per month will be added for every month the payment remains overdue, up to a maximum of 30% of the original fee. Prompt payment ensures the Authority has the necessary resources to conduct timely inspections and maintain public safety standards.

heading: Unscheduled Inspection Fee
text: Should the Authority deem it necessary to conduct an unscheduled inspection due to a reported incident, public complaint, or other safety concerns, a fee of 600 crowns per inspection will be charged to the owner, provided a safety deficiency is identified during said inspection. If no deficiency is found, no fee will be charged for the unscheduled inspection. This encourages owners to maintain their equipment diligently.

heading: Fee Waivers for Public Institutions
text: Public institutions, including hospitals and government administration buildings, may apply for a 25% waiver of the annual inspection fees outlined in sections 3, 4, and 5. To qualify, the institution must demonstrate that at least 75% of its services are provided directly to the public without charge. Applications for waivers must be submitted by December 1st of the preceding year and are subject to approval by the Authority's board.

heading: Fee Waivers for Public Institutions
text: Public institutions, including hospitals and government administration buildings, may apply for a 30% waiver of the annual inspection fees outlined in sections 3, 4, and 5. To qualify, the institution must demonstrate that at least 80% of its services are provided directly to the public without charge. Applications for waivers must be submitted by December 1st of the preceding year and are subject to approval by the Authority's board. This increased waiver reflects the public service contribution of these entities.

heading: Emergency Call-Out Fee
text: An emergency call-out fee of 1,200 crowns will be charged for inspections requested outside regular business hours (08:00 to 17:00, Monday to Friday) or on public holidays, provided the call-out is not initiated by the Authority due to an immediate public safety hazard. This fee covers the additional operational costs associated with emergency deployments to address urgent safety issues. This applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark.

heading: Exemptions for Historic Equipment
text: Elevators or escalators certified as historic landmarks and more than 75 years old may apply for a 50% reduction in annual inspection fees. Such equipment must primarily serve an educational or cultural purpose and carry fewer than 100 passengers per day on average. The Authority will conduct an additional assessment to ensure their continued safe operation despite their age. This encourages the preservation of Nordvale's mechanical heritage.

heading: Exemptions for Historic Equipment
text: Elevators or escalators certified as historic landmarks and more than 80 years old may apply for a 60% reduction in annual inspection fees. Such equipment must primarily serve an educational or cultural purpose and carry fewer than 75 passengers per day on average. The Authority will conduct an additional assessment to ensure their continued safe operation despite their age, including more frequent visual checks. This further supports the preservation of Nordvale's mechanical heritage, recognizing the higher maintenance costs.

heading: Fee Schedule Publication
text: The complete schedule of fees, including any amendments or new fees, shall be published annually by the Authority no later than October 1st of the preceding year. This publication will be made available on the Authority's official website and at the municipal offices of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This ensures transparency and provides ample notice to all affected parties.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees can be paid via electronic bank transfer, credit card, or certified cheque made payable to the Nordvale Elevator Safety Authority. Cash payments are not accepted for amounts exceeding 500 crowns. A receipt will be issued for all payments within 10 business days. Failure to use an approved payment method may result in the payment being considered overdue until properly processed.

heading: Use of Collected Fees
text: All fees collected under this Act shall be exclusively allocated to the operational budget of the Nordvale Elevator Safety Authority. These funds will cover the salaries of certified inspectors, procurement of inspection equipment, maintenance of records, development of safety guidelines, and public awareness campaigns related to elevator and escalator safety. A minimum of 70% of the funds must be directly used for inspection activities.

heading: Appeals Process for Fees
text: An owner may appeal a levied fee within 30 days of receiving the invoice by submitting a written appeal to the Authority. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for dispute and include any supporting documentation. The Authority will review the appeal within 45 days and issue a decision. During the appeal process, payment of the disputed fee is suspended, but other fees remain due.

heading: Record Keeping by Owners
text: Owners of elevators and escalators must maintain complete records of all inspections, maintenance, and repair work for a minimum of 10 years. These records must be made available to the Authority upon request with 7 days' notice. Failure to produce requested records may result in a fine of 300 crowns per missing record set, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns, as per section 24.

heading: Authority's Right of Access
text: Inspectors from the Authority shall have the right to access any premises at reasonable times (08:00 to 17:00, Monday to Friday) to conduct inspections of elevators and escalators. Owners must provide safe and unobstructed access to all components of the equipment. Obstruction of an inspector's duties may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns for each instance, as detailed in section 24.

heading: Certification of Inspectors
text: All inspectors employed by the Authority must hold a valid certification from a recognized national or international elevator safety organization. Inspectors must undergo a minimum of 40 hours of continuing education every two years to maintain their certification. This ensures that all inspections are conducted by highly qualified professionals, upholding the highest standards of safety for the public in all Nordvale municipalities.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Owners must immediately report any incident involving an elevator or escalator that results in injury, entrapment for more than 30 minutes, or significant damage to the equipment. Reports must be made to the Authority within 24 hours of the incident. Failure to report such incidents may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns, as specified in section 24, to ensure prompt investigation and preventative measures.

heading: Suspension of Service
text: The Authority has the power to order the immediate suspension of service for any elevator or escalator deemed an imminent danger to public safety. Service suspension will remain in effect until all identified hazards are rectified and a satisfactory re-inspection has been conducted. Owners will be responsible for all re-inspection fees as per section 8. Any use of suspended equipment incurs a 10,000 crowns fine, as per section 24.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: In addition to late payment penalties, the Authority may levy fines for various forms of non-compliance. These include a 300 crown fine for failing to display a valid inspection certificate, a 1,000 crown fine for obstructing an inspector, a 5,000 crown fine for failing to report a serious incident, and a 10,000 crown fine for operating an elevator or escalator under a suspension order. Repeated offenses may lead to higher penalties.

heading: Review of Fees
text: The Authority shall review the fee schedule established in this Act every three years. This review will consider the Authority's operating costs, inflation rates, and the overall financial health of the industry. Any proposed changes to the fees must be published for public comment for a period of 60 days before being finalized and enacted. The next review is scheduled for 2021.

heading: Review of Fees
text: The Authority shall review the fee schedule established in this Act every two years. This review will consider the Authority's operating costs, inflation rates, and the overall financial health of the industry. Any proposed changes to the fees must be published for public comment for a period of 45 days before being finalized and enacted. The next review is scheduled for 2023, reflecting a more dynamic economic environment.

heading: Display of Inspection Certificates
text: Upon successful completion of an annual or re-inspection, the Authority will issue an inspection certificate. This certificate, which must be clearly visible to the public, shall be displayed inside each elevator car or adjacent to the entrance of each escalator. The certificate must indicate the date of the last inspection and the date of the next scheduled inspection. Failure to display a valid certificate incurs a 300 crown fine, as per section 24.

heading: Maintenance Standards
text: Owners are responsible for ensuring that all elevators and escalators are maintained in accordance with the safety standards published by the Authority. This includes regular servicing by qualified technicians at intervals not exceeding 90 days. Proof of such maintenance must be kept readily available for inspection by Authority representatives. Failure to adhere to these standards may result in mandatory additional inspections at the owner's expense.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) A registered peat cutter pays no fee or allowance in SSA §3. (2) This exemption applies only if the peat cutter has been registered for at least one year.

heading: Special categories
text: For a certified bookbinder, the permit fee under CUL §6(2) shall be reduced by half.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a registered stonemason of a protected monument, their registration is extended by one year from the day it is granted.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the mandatory inspection of new and modified electrical installations throughout the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety of all citizens and property by preventing electrical hazards such as fires and shocks. The scope covers all premises, including residential, commercial, and industrial, where electrical work is performed, requiring certification of compliance with national safety standards. Exemptions are limited to minor repairs that do not alter the existing wiring or increase the electrical load, as specified in section 7.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Electrical Installation' means any wiring, apparatus, or equipment used for the conveyance of electricity within or on a building or property, including main supply cables, distribution boards, socket outlets, and light fittings.
(2) 'Authorized Inspector' means an individual certified by the National Electrical Safety Authority (NESA) with at least five years of experience in electrical engineering or a related field, authorized to conduct inspections under this Act. They must hold valid professional indemnity insurance covering at least 2,000,000 crowns per incident.
(3) 'Modification' refers to any alteration to an existing electrical installation that changes its capacity, extends its circuits, or replaces major components like the main distribution board. Minor component replacements of less than 10% of the total circuit length are not considered modifications.

heading: Requirement for Inspection
text: All new electrical installations and all significant modifications to existing electrical installations must undergo a mandatory inspection by an Authorized Inspector before being connected to the main power grid. This requirement applies to all construction projects where electrical work is integral to the structure, as well as standalone electrical upgrades. Failure to comply with this section may result in a fine of up to 15,000 crowns for the property owner and the responsible electrician. The inspection must be completed within 30 days of the electrical work being finalized.

heading: Application for Inspection
text:
(1) The property owner or the lead electrician responsible for the work shall submit an application for inspection to the local municipal office in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.
(2) The application must be submitted at least 14 working days before the desired inspection date and include a detailed schematic diagram of the electrical work performed. A non-refundable processing fee of 250 crowns must accompany the application, covering administrative costs. Incomplete applications will be returned within 7 working days.

heading: Application for Inspection
text:
(1) The property owner or the lead electrician responsible for the work shall submit an application for inspection to the local municipal office in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.
(2) The application must be submitted at least 21 working days before the desired inspection date and include a detailed schematic diagram of the electrical work performed. A non-refundable processing fee of 300 crowns must accompany the application, covering administrative costs. Incomplete applications will be returned within 10 working days.

heading: Inspection Standards
text: Inspections shall be conducted in accordance with the Nordvale National Electrical Safety Code, 2017 edition. This code specifies minimum requirements for wiring sizes, circuit breaker capacities, grounding, and insulation. Inspectors must verify that all components are properly installed and rated for the intended use. Any deviation from these standards, even minor ones, must be documented and rectified. The maximum permissible voltage drop in any circuit shall not exceed 3%.

heading: Inspector Qualifications
text: Only individuals certified by the National Electrical Safety Authority (NESA) are authorized to perform inspections under this Act. Certification requires a minimum of five years of practical experience as a licensed electrician, successful completion of a NESA-approved examination, and continuous professional development, including at least 20 hours of training every two years. Authorized Inspectors must renew their certification every three years and maintain valid liability insurance covering at least 2,500,000 crowns for each claim.

heading: Exemptions from Inspection
text:
(1) Minor repairs that do not involve altering the main electrical panel, extending circuits, or replacing more than 20% of the existing wiring in a single room are exempt from mandatory inspection. Examples include replacing a faulty light switch or a single socket outlet.
(2) The replacement of a like-for-like appliance that does not require new wiring or circuit modifications is also exempt. However, if the replacement appliance draws significantly more power (e.g., an increase of 25% or more in current draw), an inspection may be required under section 3.

heading: Inspection Report
text:
(1) Upon completion of an inspection, the Authorized Inspector must issue a detailed report within 5 working days. The report shall clearly state whether the electrical installation complies with the Nordvale National Electrical Safety Code.
(2) If deficiencies are found, the report must list them specifically, categorize their severity, and recommend corrective actions. A copy of the report shall be provided to the property owner, the electrician, and the local municipal office. For severe deficiencies, a provisional 'unsafe' rating will be issued, requiring immediate action.

heading: Rectification of Deficiencies
text:
(1) If an inspection report identifies deficiencies, the property owner or the responsible electrician must rectify all identified issues within a period of 45 days from the date the report was issued. For critical safety hazards, this period is reduced to 10 days.
(2) After rectification, a re-inspection must be scheduled to verify that all problems have been adequately addressed. Failure to rectify deficiencies within the stipulated timeframe may lead to penalties as outlined in section 14 and potential disconnection of power supply.

heading: Re-inspection Fees
text:
(1) A re-inspection fee of 1,000 crowns is payable for each subsequent inspection required to verify the rectification of deficiencies. This fee must be paid before the re-inspection takes place.
(2) If more than two re-inspections are required for the same installation, a surcharge of 50% of the re-inspection fee will be applied for each additional re-inspection. This encourages timely and thorough rectification of initial issues. Fees are collected by the municipal office.

heading: Certificate of Compliance
text: Upon successful completion of all inspections and rectification of any deficiencies, the Authorized Inspector shall issue a Certificate of Compliance. This certificate confirms that the electrical installation meets all current safety standards. A copy of this certificate must be prominently displayed near the main electrical panel of the property and a digital copy registered with the local municipal office within 7 days of issuance. Without this certificate, power connection may be refused or disconnected.

heading: False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application for inspection, an inspection report, or any related document required by this Act commits an offense. Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 50,000 crowns, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or both. If an Authorized Inspector is found to have provided false information, their certification will be immediately revoked by NESA for a period of at least five years.

heading: Obstruction of Inspector
text: No person shall obstruct, hinder, or interfere with an Authorized Inspector in the performance of their duties under this Act. This includes refusing access to the property where an electrical installation is located, or deliberately withholding relevant documentation. An offense under this section carries a penalty of a fine not exceeding 20,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses may lead to increased fines of up to 40,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any property owner or electrician who fails to comply with the mandatory inspection requirements of section 3 shall be liable to a fine of not less than 10,000 crowns and not exceeding 30,000 crowns.
(2) Continuous non-compliance, defined as failure to rectify deficiencies or obtain a Certificate of Compliance within 90 days of the initial inspection report, may result in the disconnection of electrical service to the property until compliance is achieved. An additional daily fine of 500 crowns may be imposed for each day of continued non-compliance after 90 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A property owner or electrician may appeal a decision of an Authorized Inspector regarding compliance or deficiencies within 20 working days of receiving the inspection report. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the National Electrical Safety Authority (NESA).
(2) The Appeals Board will review the case within 30 days and may request additional documentation or a second opinion from another Authorized Inspector. A fee of 750 crowns is required to lodge an appeal, which is refundable only if the appeal is successful.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All municipal offices and Authorized Inspectors must maintain detailed records of all inspection applications, reports, certificates of compliance, and any related correspondence for a minimum period of 10 years. These records must be stored securely and be readily accessible for audit purposes. Digital records are permissible, provided they are backed up at least weekly. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in administrative penalties of up to 5,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Regular Maintenance Inspections
text:
(1) For commercial and industrial premises, electrical installations must undergo a maintenance inspection every 5 years to ensure ongoing safety and compliance. This is in addition to inspections for new work or modifications.
(2) Residential properties are exempt from mandatory regular maintenance inspections, but owners are strongly encouraged to have their electrical systems checked every 10 years by a qualified electrician. This proactive approach helps identify potential issues before they become hazards.

heading: Powers of Entry
text:
(1) An Authorized Inspector, upon presentation of their identification and a valid inspection order, may enter any property at a reasonable hour to conduct an inspection required by this Act. Reasonable hour is generally defined as between 08:00 and 18:00 on weekdays.
(2) If entry is refused, the Inspector may apply to a magistrate for a warrant to enter the premises. This warrant will specify the scope of entry and the personnel authorized to accompany the inspector. Force may be used to gain entry only with a warrant and in the presence of law enforcement.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information gathered during an inspection, including details of the electrical installation and property owner's personal information, must be treated with strict confidentiality. This information shall not be disclosed to any third party except as required by law or with the express written consent of the property owner. Unauthorized disclosure may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for the individual responsible.

heading: National Electrical Safety Authority
text:
(1) The National Electrical Safety Authority (NESA) is established as the primary regulatory body responsible for overseeing the implementation of this Act. NESA's functions include setting standards, certifying inspectors, and resolving appeals.
(2) NESA is composed of a board of 7 members, appointed by the Minister of Public Works, each serving a term of 4 years. At least 3 members must be qualified electrical engineers with a minimum of 15 years of experience.

heading: Training Requirements for Electricians
text: All electricians undertaking work subject to inspection under this Act must possess a valid electrician's license issued by the Nordvale Crafts and Trades Board. This license requires a minimum of 3 years of apprenticeship and passing a comprehensive practical and theoretical examination. Furthermore, licensed electricians must complete at least 15 hours of continuing professional development every two years to stay updated with code changes and best practices.

heading: Emergency Inspections
text: In cases where an electrical installation is deemed an immediate and severe hazard to life or property, an emergency inspection may be carried out without prior application. The local municipal office, or NESA, can order such an inspection. The results of an emergency inspection must be reported within 24 hours, and immediate steps taken to disconnect power if the hazard persists. Property owners must cooperate fully with emergency inspectors.

heading: Cost of Inspection
text:
(1) The cost of the initial inspection is borne by the property owner. The standard fee for a residential property is 3,500 crowns, and for commercial properties, it ranges from 5,000 crowns to 15,000 crowns depending on the size and complexity of the installation. These fees are subject to annual review by NESA.
(2) The fees are paid directly to the Authorized Inspector upon completion of the inspection, unless otherwise agreed with the municipal office for larger projects. A detailed invoice must be provided for all services rendered.

heading: Cost of Inspection
text:
(1) The cost of the initial inspection is borne by the property owner. The standard fee for a residential property is 4,000 crowns, and for commercial properties, it ranges from 6,000 crowns to 18,000 crowns depending on the size and complexity of the installation. These fees are subject to annual review by NESA.
(2) The fees are paid directly to the Authorized Inspector upon completion of the inspection, unless otherwise agreed with the municipal office for larger projects. A detailed invoice must be provided for all services rendered.

heading: Liability of Inspectors
text: An Authorized Inspector shall not be held personally liable for any loss or damage arising from an electrical installation that has received a Certificate of Compliance, provided the inspection was conducted with due diligence and in accordance with this Act and established professional standards. However, gross negligence or wilful misconduct on the part of the inspector may lead to civil liability and the revocation of their certification by NESA. Their professional indemnity insurance must cover claims up to 3,000,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Any electrical incident resulting in serious injury, death, or significant property damage (estimated at over 50,000 crowns) must be reported to NESA within 48 hours of its occurrence. This report should include the nature of the incident, the property details, and any preliminary findings. NESA will then determine if a special investigation is warranted to identify potential systemic failures or non-compliance with electrical safety standards.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister of Public Works every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance to technological advancements and evolving safety standards. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public consultations will be held during the review process, allowing stakeholders to submit comments and recommendations. Amendments to the Act may be proposed based on the findings of these reviews.

heading: Transition Period
text: For electrical installations that were completed prior to the enactment of this Act but after 2010, property owners have a transition period of 18 months from the Act's effective date to obtain a voluntary inspection and, if necessary, a Certificate of Compliance. During this period, penalties for non-compliance with section 3 will not be applied to such existing installations, but this does not exempt them from reporting serious incidents under section 25. After 18 months, full compliance is expected.

heading: Safety Awareness Campaigns
text: NESA shall periodically conduct public awareness campaigns to educate citizens about electrical safety, the importance of professional electrical work, and the requirements of this Act. These campaigns will utilize various media channels and target different demographics. A minimum of 100,000 crowns is allocated annually for these educational initiatives, aiming to reduce electrical accidents by at least 15% within five years.

heading: Electrical Work in Public Buildings
text: All electrical installations and modifications in public buildings, including government offices, schools, and hospitals, are subject to the strictest inspection protocols. These installations must pass an additional secondary review by a NESA senior inspector after the initial inspection. The inspection frequency for public buildings is every 3 years for maintenance inspections, compared to 5 years for other commercial premises, to ensure maximum safety for the public.

heading: Temporary Installations
text: Temporary electrical installations, such as those used for construction sites or public events lasting less than 90 days, are also subject to inspection. These installations require a simplified inspection and a temporary Certificate of Compliance, valid only for the specified period. The inspection must occur at least 5 working days before connection to power, and any significant alteration to the layout requires a new temporary inspection. A fee of 1,500 crowns is charged for temporary inspections.

heading: Temporary Installations
text: Temporary electrical installations, such as those used for construction sites or public events lasting less than 120 days, are also subject to inspection. These installations require a simplified inspection and a temporary Certificate of Compliance, valid only for the specified period. The inspection must occur at least 7 working days before connection to power, and any significant alteration to the layout requires a new temporary inspection. A fee of 1,800 crowns is charged for temporary inspections.

heading: Use of Approved Materials
text: Only electrical materials and components that meet the Nordvale National Electrical Safety Code standards and are approved by NESA shall be used in any electrical installation or modification. Inspectors will verify that all cables, switches, sockets, and protective devices bear the official Nordvale Safety Mark. The use of non-approved materials is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and mandatory replacement of the non-compliant components at the electrician's expense.

heading: Appliance Connection
text: The direct connection of high-power appliances (over 3 kW) to the main electrical system, such as ovens or water heaters, must be performed by a licensed electrician. While the appliance itself may not require inspection, the circuit used to power it must be inspected if it is a new installation or a modification. Property owners are advised to retain records of such connections for future reference during inspections. Failure to use a licensed electrician for these tasks could invalidate insurance claims.

heading: Electrical Plan Submission
text: For all new constructions or major renovations involving more than 50% of the electrical system, detailed electrical plans must be submitted to the local municipal planning department for approval before any work commences. These plans must be prepared by a licensed electrical engineer and adhere to all relevant building codes and safety standards. The planning department has 30 days to review and approve or reject the plans. An application fee of 750 crowns is required for plan submission.

heading: Electrical Plan Submission
text: For all new constructions or major renovations involving more than 40% of the electrical system, detailed electrical plans must be submitted to the local municipal planning department for approval before any work commences. These plans must be prepared by a licensed electrical engineer and adhere to all relevant building codes and safety standards. The planning department has 25 days to review and approve or reject the plans. An application fee of 800 crowns is required for plan submission.

heading: Special Provisions for Renewable Energy Systems
text:
(1) Electrical installations related to renewable energy systems, such as solar panels or wind turbines, are subject to specific inspection requirements. These systems must comply with supplementary guidelines issued by NESA, focusing on grid connection, isolation, and surge protection.
(2) Installers of renewable energy systems must hold a specific NESA endorsement in addition to their standard electrician's license, demonstrating expertise in these specialized installations. A separate inspection fee of 5,000 crowns applies to these systems due to their complexity, on top of any other applicable fees.

heading: Complaints Against Inspectors
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a formal complaint against an Authorized Inspector for professional misconduct, negligence, or non-compliance with the provisions of this Act. Complaints must be submitted in writing to NESA within 90 days of the alleged incident.
(2) NESA will investigate all complaints and, if substantiated, may impose disciplinary actions ranging from a warning to the suspension or revocation of the inspector's certification. The complainant will be informed of the outcome of the investigation within 60 days.

heading: Information Sharing
text: NESA is authorized to share relevant inspection data and compliance records with municipal planning departments, local fire safety authorities, and national insurance providers, solely for the purpose of ensuring public safety and upholding the provisions of this Act. This information sharing will be conducted in accordance with national data protection regulations. No personal data beyond property ownership and compliance status will be shared without explicit consent, unless a serious safety hazard is identified.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018. All electrical work commenced on or after this date is subject to its provisions. For ongoing projects that began before this date, a grace period of 60 days is granted to comply with the new inspection requirements, provided the work is scheduled for completion within 120 days of the effective date. Any work extending beyond 120 days must fully comply immediately.

heading: Amendments to Schedules
text:
(1) The Minister of Public Works, upon recommendation from NESA, may amend the schedules attached to this Act, which detail specific technical standards and fees. These amendments must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before they take effect.
(2) Any proposed amendment must undergo a public consultation period of not less than 21 days, allowing interested parties to provide feedback. This ensures transparency and stakeholder input in the regulatory process.

heading: Interpretation
text: Any ambiguity or dispute regarding the interpretation of any provision of this Act shall be referred to the National Electrical Safety Authority (NESA) for a definitive ruling. NESA's interpretation shall be binding unless overturned by a court of competent jurisdiction. This process ensures consistent application of the law across all municipalities and industries. NESA will publish all such rulings for public access within 14 days of their decision.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Provisions
text: Sections 12 and 13 of the 'Electrical Safety Guidelines of 1995' are hereby repealed, as their subject matter is now fully covered by the provisions of this Act. Any other conflicting or overlapping legislation pertaining to electrical installation inspections is also superseded by this Act. The repeal aims to streamline and clarify the legal framework governing electrical safety. This ensures that only the most current and comprehensive regulations are in force.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Particular persons
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a household with a licensed glassblower receives a large family supplement that is 25 percent less than the standard 180 crowns per year.

heading: Particular persons
text: The repayment of the study grant is reduced by granting any licensed tightrope performer an additional thirty days to make the repayment stipulated in SSA §13.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: (1) A licensed chimney-sweep master shall pay 25 percent less of the hand cart permit fee. (2) This reduction applies only if the master has held their license for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and oversight of all electrical installation and modification work within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, prevent electrical hazards, and maintain consistent quality standards across all electrical systems. The scope extends to all residential, commercial, and industrial properties, regardless of ownership, and mandates specific permits for any work that alters or adds to existing electrical infrastructure or establishes new connections.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Electrical work' means any activity involving the installation, alteration, repair, or removal of electrical wiring, fixtures, equipment, or systems, including but not limited to, power generation, transmission, and distribution within a building or property boundary.
(2) 'Permit' means a formal authorization issued by the Municipal Electrical Authority allowing specific electrical work to proceed, subject to conditions and inspections.
(3) 'Licensed Electrician' refers to an individual holding a valid and current electrician's license issued by the Nordvale Craftsmen's Guild, demonstrating competency in electrical safety and installation practices.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence any electrical work, as defined in subsection (1) of section 2, within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Electrical Installation Permit from the relevant Municipal Electrical Authority. This requirement applies to all new installations, significant modifications exceeding 10% of the existing circuit capacity, and any work affecting the main service panel, regardless of the property type or size. Minor repairs, such as replacing a light switch or outlet without altering wiring, are exempt.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for an Electrical Installation Permit must be submitted to the Municipal Electrical Authority of the municipality where the work is to be performed. The application must be filed at least 15 business days prior to the proposed start date of the work. It must include detailed electrical plans, a scope of work, and the contact information of the licensed electrician responsible for the project. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned within 5 business days.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Municipal Electrical Authority shall review complete permit applications within a maximum of 10 business days from the date of submission. During this period, the Authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant or the licensed electrician. Failure to provide requested information within 7 business days may result in a delay in processing or rejection of the application. The Authority aims to approve 95% of eligible applications within this timeframe.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Municipal Electrical Authority shall review complete permit applications within a maximum of 7 business days from the date of submission. During this period, the Authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant or the licensed electrician. Failure to provide requested information within 5 business days may result in a delay in processing or rejection of the application. The Authority aims to approve 98% of eligible applications within this timeframe.

heading: Permit Fees
text: A non-refundable permit application fee of 250 crowns is required for all residential electrical work. For commercial and industrial projects, the fee is 750 crowns. These fees cover administrative costs and initial plan reviews. Additional inspection fees, as outlined in section 17, are separate and payable upon completion of each required inspection. Failure to pay the permit fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application.

heading: Late Application Penalties
text: Applications submitted less than 15 business days prior to the proposed start date of electrical work will incur a late fee of 500 crowns. This late fee is in addition to the standard permit fee. Applications submitted within 5 business days of the proposed start date may be automatically rejected unless extreme mitigating circumstances are documented and approved by the Municipal Electrical Authority, which occurs in less than 2% of such cases.

heading: Work by Licensed Electricians Only
text: All electrical work requiring a permit under this Act must be performed by a licensed electrician, as defined in subsection (3) of section 2, or under the direct and constant supervision of such an individual. The licensed electrician must present their valid license upon request at any stage of the project. Any work found to be conducted by unlicensed individuals will be immediately halted and subject to penalties as specified in section 30.

heading: Exemptions for Minor Repairs
text: Minor electrical repairs that do not involve altering existing wiring or adding new circuits are exempt from the permit requirement. This includes activities such as replacing faulty light bulbs, swapping out a broken wall switch with an identical type, or replacing a malfunctioning outlet. Any repair that involves cutting, splicing, or extending wires, or increasing the load on a circuit by more than 5%, is not considered a minor repair and requires a permit.

heading: Emergency Work Provisions
text: In cases of immediate danger to life or property due to electrical failure, emergency electrical work may commence without a prior permit. However, the Municipal Electrical Authority must be notified within 24 hours of the start of such work, and a permit application must be submitted within 3 business days. The application must clearly state the emergency nature of the work and include photographs or other evidence of the emergency. Failure to comply will result in a 1,000 crowns fine.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: An Electrical Installation Permit is valid for a period of 180 days from the date of issuance. If the electrical work is not completed within this timeframe, the permit holder must apply for an extension. Extensions may be granted for an additional 90 days upon payment of a 150 crowns renewal fee, provided significant progress on the work can be demonstrated. A maximum of two extensions can be granted for any single permit.

heading: Permit Validity Period - Revised
text: An Electrical Installation Permit is valid for a period of 150 days from the date of issuance. If the electrical work is not completed within this timeframe, the permit holder must apply for an extension. Extensions may be granted for an additional 60 days upon payment of a 200 crowns renewal fee, provided significant progress on the work can be demonstrated. A maximum of one extension can be granted for any single permit.

heading: Permit Display
text: The issued Electrical Installation Permit must be prominently displayed at the work site at all times while electrical work is in progress. The permit should be visible from the street or main entrance to the property. Failure to display a valid permit may result in a temporary work stoppage until compliance is achieved. Municipal inspectors will verify permit display during their visits, with a non-display penalty of 100 crowns per day.

heading: Pre-Work Inspection (Aldmark, Corvik)
text: In the municipalities of Aldmark and Corvik, a mandatory pre-work inspection is required for all new electrical installations in structures exceeding 200 square meters. This inspection ensures that the proposed site conditions are suitable and that preliminary safety measures are in place before major work begins. The inspection must be scheduled at least 3 business days before the planned start of work and will be completed within 48 hours of the scheduled time.

heading: Pre-Work Inspection (Brenholt, Dunmere)
text: In the municipalities of Brenholt and Dunmere, a mandatory pre-work inspection is required for all new electrical installations in structures exceeding 150 square meters. This inspection ensures that the proposed site conditions are suitable and that preliminary safety measures are in place before major work begins. The inspection must be scheduled at least 4 business days before the planned start of work and will be completed within 72 hours of the scheduled time.

heading: Mid-Phase Inspection
text: For all electrical work involving concealed wiring, a mandatory mid-phase inspection is required before any walls, ceilings, or floors are enclosed. This inspection will verify the correct installation of wiring, junction boxes, and grounding. The licensed electrician must notify the Municipal Electrical Authority at least 2 business days in advance to schedule this inspection. Work may not proceed beyond this point until the inspection is approved and signed off by the inspector.

heading: Inspection Fees
text: Each mandatory inspection, as outlined in sections 14, 15, and 16, incurs an inspection fee of 300 crowns. Re-inspections required due to failed initial inspections will incur an additional fee of 200 crowns. These fees are payable to the Municipal Electrical Authority and must be settled prior to the release of the final occupancy permit for the property. A 10% surcharge applies to inspection fees paid more than 30 days after the inspection date.

heading: Final Inspection Requirement
text: Upon completion of all electrical work, a final inspection by the Municipal Electrical Authority is mandatory. This inspection verifies that all work has been performed in accordance with the approved plans and all applicable safety standards. The licensed electrician must schedule this inspection within 5 business days of project completion. No electrical system may be energized for permanent use until this final inspection has been successfully passed and a Certificate of Electrical Compliance issued.

heading: Certificate of Electrical Compliance
text: A Certificate of Electrical Compliance will be issued by the Municipal Electrical Authority within 3 business days of a successful final inspection. This certificate confirms that the electrical installation meets all safety standards and regulatory requirements of Nordvale. A copy of this certificate must be provided to the property owner and retained for at least 10 years. Without this certificate, connecting the new or modified electrical system to the grid is prohibited and subject to a 2,000 crowns fine.

heading: Electrical Code Adherence
text: All electrical work performed under an Electrical Installation Permit must strictly adhere to the Nordvale Electrical Code, as published by the Ministry of Public Works. This code specifies minimum standards for wiring, components, grounding, overcurrent protection, and all other aspects of electrical installations. Any deviation from the code must be pre-approved in writing by the Municipal Electrical Authority, which occurs in less than 1% of applications annually.

heading: Material Standards
text: Only electrical materials and equipment that meet or exceed the safety standards established by the Nordvale Standards Bureau shall be used in electrical installations. All materials must bear appropriate certification marks. The use of uncertified or substandard materials is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate failure of inspection and potential penalties. Inspectors may demand proof of material certification at any point during the project, for up to 20% of materials.

heading: Electrical Diagrams and Plans
text: Detailed electrical diagrams and plans must be submitted with every permit application for new installations or significant modifications exceeding 25% of existing capacity. These plans must clearly indicate circuit layouts, panel schedules, wire gauges, conduit runs, and the location of all major electrical components. The plans must be drawn to scale and signed by the licensed electrician. For minor modifications, a simplified sketch may suffice if approved by the Authority.

heading: Electrical Diagrams and Plans
text: Detailed electrical diagrams and plans must be submitted with every permit application for new installations or significant modifications exceeding 15% of existing capacity. These plans must clearly indicate circuit layouts, panel schedules, wire gauges, conduit runs, and the location of all major electrical components. The plans must be drawn to scale and signed by the licensed electrician. For minor modifications, a simplified sketch may suffice if approved by the Authority. Digital submissions are now mandatory for all projects over 50,000 crowns.

heading: Changes to Approved Plans
text: Any significant deviation from the approved electrical plans must be submitted to the Municipal Electrical Authority for review and re-approval before the work is executed. Minor, non-structural changes that do not affect safety or code compliance, such as moving an outlet by less than 0.5 meters, may be noted on the 'as-built' plans without prior re-approval. Unapproved significant changes may lead to failed inspections and remedial work at the permit holder's expense, which historically affects 8% of projects.

heading: Record Keeping
text: The permit holder and the licensed electrician must maintain accurate records of all electrical work performed, including 'as-built' plans, material specifications, and inspection reports. These records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years following the issuance of the Certificate of Electrical Compliance and must be made available to the Municipal Electrical Authority upon request. Failure to maintain proper records may result in a fine of 500 crowns.

heading: Authority to Enter Premises
text: Duly authorized electrical inspectors of the Municipal Electrical Authority shall have the right to enter any premises where electrical work is being performed or is believed to have been performed without a permit, during reasonable hours, for the purpose of inspection. Inspectors must present official identification upon entry. Entry may be denied if reasonable suspicion of an ongoing violation is not present, or if entry is not sought within standard business hours (8 AM to 5 PM).

heading: Stop Work Orders
text: The Municipal Electrical Authority may issue a 'Stop Work Order' if electrical work is found to be proceeding without a valid permit, in violation of approved plans, or in a manner that poses an immediate safety hazard. All work must cease immediately upon receipt of such an order. Failure to comply with a 'Stop Work Order' will result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 5,000 crowns per day and potential criminal charges.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text: An Electrical Installation Permit may be revoked by the Municipal Electrical Authority if it is discovered that the permit was obtained through fraudulent means, if work is not performed by a licensed electrician, or if significant and uncorrected violations of this Act or the Nordvale Electrical Code persist after multiple warnings.
