The permit holder will be notified in writing of the revocation and given 7 business days to appeal the decision.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any person or entity aggrieved by a decision of the Municipal Electrical Authority regarding permit applications, inspections, or penalties may file an appeal with the Nordvale Electrical Appeals Board within 15 business days of receiving the decision. The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. The Appeals Board will review the case and render a decision within 30 business days, with 90% of appeals being resolved within this period.

heading: Penalties for Unpermitted Work
text: Any person or entity found to be performing electrical work without a valid permit shall be subject to a fine of not less than 2,000 crowns and not exceeding 10,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 25,000 crowns and may lead to forced demolition of the unpermitted work at the owner's expense. Additionally, all work must be brought into compliance, which often adds 50% to the project cost.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Work
text: Individuals performing electrical work without a valid electrician's license, where such a license is required, shall be subject to a fine of 5,000 crowns for the first offense. For subsequent offenses, the fine will increase to 15,000 crowns, and the individual may be permanently banned from applying for an electrician's license in Nordvale for a period of 5 years. Property owners who knowingly allow unlicensed work may also face fines of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Violations
text: Any citizen may report suspected violations of this Act to their local Municipal Electrical Authority. Reports can be made anonymously, but providing contact information may assist in investigations. The Authority will investigate all credible reports within 10 business days. Information leading to the successful prosecution of significant violations may be eligible for a reward of up to 1,000 crowns, which is paid out in about 15% of reported cases.

heading: Municipal Authority Powers
text: Each Municipal Electrical Authority in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale is empowered to enforce the provisions of this Act within its jurisdiction. This includes issuing permits, conducting inspections, imposing fines, issuing stop work orders, and revoking permits. The Authorities may also establish local administrative procedures consistent with this Act to ensure efficient operation, provided these procedures are approved by the Ministry of Public Works.

heading: Public Information Campaigns
text: The Ministry of Public Works shall conduct public information campaigns at least twice annually to educate citizens about the importance of electrical safety and the requirements for obtaining electrical permits. These campaigns will utilize various media channels and focus on increasing awareness, particularly among homeowners and small business owners. The goal is to reduce instances of unpermitted electrical work by 20% within the next three years.

heading: Training for Inspectors
text: All electrical inspectors employed by the Municipal Electrical Authorities must undergo mandatory training and certification every 2 years. This training will cover updates to the Nordvale Electrical Code, new technologies, and best practices in electrical inspection. Inspectors must pass a comprehensive examination with a score of 85% or higher to maintain their certification. Failure to maintain certification will result in suspension from inspection duties.

heading: Annual Reporting
text: Each Municipal Electrical Authority shall submit an annual report to the Ministry of Public Works by January 31st of each year. This report must detail the number of permits issued, inspections conducted, violations found, and penalties levied during the preceding calendar year. The report should also include statistics on inspection approval rates and the average time taken to process permit applications. The Ministry will consolidate these reports into a national overview.

heading: Annual Reporting
text: Each Municipal Electrical Authority shall submit an annual report to the Ministry of Public Works by January 15th of each year. This report must detail the number of permits issued, inspections conducted, violations found, and penalties levied during the preceding calendar year. The report should also include statistics on inspection approval rates and the average time taken to process permit applications, and a breakdown by residential vs. commercial projects. The Ministry will consolidate these reports into a national overview, which will be published online by March 31st.

heading: Inter-Municipal Cooperation
text: The Municipal Electrical Authorities are encouraged to cooperate and share information regarding electrical installation practices and enforcement strategies. Joint training sessions and standardized forms are recommended to ensure consistency across Nordvale. A minimum of one inter-municipal meeting must be held annually, coordinated by the Ministry of Public Works, to discuss challenges and improvements, aiming for a 90% alignment on minor procedural aspects.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Public Works every 5 years to assess its effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, and address any emerging electrical safety concerns. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public consultation will be a part of this review process, with feedback periods lasting at least 60 days. Recommendations from the review will be submitted to the Nordvale Assembly for consideration and potential amendments.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Electrical work that commenced prior to the effective date of this Act and is still in progress shall be granted a grace period of 90 days to obtain the necessary permits and comply with all provisions of this Act. During this grace period, work may continue provided there are no immediate safety hazards. After the expiration of the grace period, all ongoing work must fully comply or face immediate cessation and penalties.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Electrical Installation Permits Act shall come into full force and effect on January 1, 2018, across all municipalities of the Republic of Nordvale. All previous regulations and ordinances pertaining to electrical installation permits are hereby superseded by this Act as of this date. Any permit applications submitted before this date will be processed under the previous regulations, but any work commencing after January 1, 2018, must adhere to this Act.

heading: Data Retention Policy (Elsby, Fennick)
text: In the municipalities of Elsby and Fennick, all digital records pertaining to permit applications, inspection reports, and compliance certificates must be securely stored for a minimum period of 15 years. Physical copies must be retained for 5 years. Access to these records is restricted to authorized personnel only, and any data breach must be reported to the Ministry of Public Works within 48 hours. Penalties for non-compliance with data retention can reach 5,000 crowns.

heading: Data Retention Policy (Grauby, Lund Vale)
text: In the municipalities of Grauby and Lund Vale, all digital records pertaining to permit applications, inspection reports, and compliance certificates must be securely stored for a minimum period of 10 years. Physical copies must be retained for 3 years. Access to these records is restricted to authorized personnel only, and any data breach must be reported to the Ministry of Public Works within 72 hours. Penalties for non-compliance with data retention can reach 3,000 crowns.

heading: Installation Requirements for High-Voltage Systems
text: For electrical installations involving high-voltage systems (exceeding 600 volts), permit applications must include a detailed risk assessment report. This report must be prepared by a certified electrical engineer with at least 5 years of experience in high-voltage systems. Additionally, a dedicated safety officer must be present on site for at least 75% of the working hours during installation. Failure to provide a risk assessment will result in immediate rejection of the permit application.

heading: Installation Requirements for High-Voltage Systems
text: For electrical installations involving high-voltage systems (exceeding 480 volts), permit applications must include a detailed risk assessment report. This report must be prepared by a certified electrical engineer with at least 7 years of experience in high-voltage systems. Additionally, a dedicated safety officer must be present on site for 100% of the working hours during installation. Failure to provide a risk assessment will result in immediate rejection of the permit application, and an initial fine of 1,500 crowns will be applied.

heading: Public Access to Permit Information
text: The Municipal Electrical Authority shall make public information regarding issued permits accessible online, including the permit number, property address, and a general description of the work. Personal information of applicants or electricians will not be disclosed. This public database will be updated weekly, and information for permits issued in the last 5 years will be available. Citizens can request full permit details for a 50 crowns administrative fee.

heading: Permit for Renewable Energy Systems
text: Electrical installations for renewable energy systems, such as solar panels or wind turbines, require an Electrical Installation Permit. Applications for these systems must include specific schematics for grid connection and safety shutdown mechanisms. A simplified application process, with a reduced fee of 150 crowns, is available for residential systems generating less than 10 kilowatts. Commercial systems, however, incur the standard commercial fee.

heading: Permit for Temporary Installations
text: Temporary electrical installations, such as those for construction sites or public events lasting more than 7 days, require a Temporary Electrical Permit. This permit is valid for a maximum of 90 days and costs 400 crowns. Inspections for temporary installations must occur within 2 business days of setup and prior to energization. Extensions for temporary permits may be granted for an additional 30 days if justified, with a 100 crowns fee.

heading: Reporting of Electrical Incidents
text: Any electrical incident resulting in significant property damage (exceeding 5,000 crowns), serious injury, or fatality must be reported to the Municipal Electrical Authority within 12 hours of its occurrence. The reporting party must provide a preliminary account of the incident. Failure to report such incidents may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and an immediate investigation by the Authority and the Ministry of Public Safety.

heading: Simplified Permit for Minor Upgrades
text: A simplified permit process is available for minor electrical upgrades that involve adding no more than 2 new circuits or increasing existing capacity by less than 10% in residential properties. The fee for this simplified permit is 100 crowns, and only a final inspection is required. Applications for these upgrades are processed within 3 business days, aiming to encourage compliance for small projects.

heading: Annual License Verification
text: The Municipal Electrical Authority shall conduct an annual verification of all licensed electricians operating within its jurisdiction. This verification will confirm the validity of their licenses with the Nordvale Craftsmen's Guild and ensure they have completed any required continuing education. Any electrician found with an expired or suspended license will be barred from performing permitted work until their status is rectified, and their permits will be frozen.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each certified rope-access technician receives an additional 30 days to pay any fee or allowance specified in ELA §5.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) A registered puppeteer is entitled to have half of their study loan repaid. (2) This repayment applies to study loans obtained for an academic year, up to a maximum of 1,500 crowns per year.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for permits required for the installation, modification, and major repair of electrical systems within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety and reliability of electrical infrastructure by regulating who may perform such work and under what conditions. The Act applies to all electrical installations, whether in residential, commercial, or industrial properties, with specific exceptions detailed in later sections. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all individuals and entities undertaking electrical work.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Electrical system' refers to all components, including wiring, conduits, fixtures, and appliances, that are connected to an electrical power source.
(2) 'Installation' means the initial setup of a new electrical system or a complete replacement of an existing one.
(3) 'Modification' involves any alteration to an existing electrical system that changes its capacity, configuration, or safety features, such as adding a new circuit or upgrading a service panel.
(4) 'Licensed Electrician' denotes an individual holding a valid and current electrician's license issued by the Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence any new electrical installation or significant modification of an existing electrical system without first obtaining a valid Electrical Installation Permit from the municipal authority where the work is to be performed. This requirement applies to all works exceeding 10 amperes or 240 volts in capacity, or involving the addition of more than three new outlets or light fixtures. Failure to secure a permit before beginning work may result in penalties as outlined in section 38.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence any new electrical installation or significant modification of an existing electrical system without first obtaining a valid Electrical Installation Permit from the municipal authority where the work is to be performed. This requirement applies to all works exceeding 12 amperes or 250 volts in capacity, or involving the addition of more than four new outlets or light fixtures. Failure to secure a permit before beginning work may result in penalties as outlined in section 38.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for Electrical Installation Permits must be submitted to the relevant municipal office in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale. The application must include detailed plans of the proposed work, a list of materials to be used, and the credentials of the licensed electrician responsible for the project. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 7 business days, with a request for additional information.

heading: Application Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal authority shall review the submitted documents for compliance with Nordvale electrical codes and safety standards. This review process shall be completed within a maximum of 15 business days. If the application is approved, a permit will be issued. If it is denied, the applicant will receive a written explanation of the reasons for denial within the same timeframe.

heading: Application Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal authority shall review the submitted documents for compliance with Nordvale electrical codes and safety standards. This review process shall be completed within a maximum of 12 business days. If the application is approved, a permit will be issued. If it is denied, the applicant will receive a written explanation of the reasons for denial within the same timeframe.

heading: Permit Fees
text: A non-refundable fee of 250 crowns is required for each Electrical Installation Permit application. This fee covers administrative costs and the initial review process. For large-scale commercial or industrial projects exceeding 100 amperes, an additional fee of 150 crowns will be levied. Payment must be made at the time of application submission, either through electronic transfer or direct payment at the municipal office.

heading: Permit Fees
text: A non-refundable fee of 280 crowns is required for each Electrical Installation Permit application. This fee covers administrative costs and the initial review process. For large-scale commercial or industrial projects exceeding 120 amperes, an additional fee of 180 crowns will be levied. Payment must be made at the time of application submission, either through electronic transfer or direct payment at the municipal office.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: An Electrical Installation Permit is valid for a period of 180 days from the date of issuance. If the electrical work is not completed within this timeframe, the permit will expire, and a new application, along with associated fees, will be required. An extension of 90 days may be granted in exceptional circumstances, upon written request and payment of an extension fee of 75 crowns, provided the request is submitted at least 30 days before the original expiry date.

heading: Licensed Electrician Requirement
text: All electrical installations and modifications requiring a permit must be performed by or directly supervised by a Licensed Electrician. The name and license number of the responsible Licensed Electrician must be clearly stated on the permit application. Any work performed by an unlicensed individual or without proper supervision will be deemed non-compliant and subject to immediate cessation, as well as potential fines for both the property owner and the individual performing the work.

heading: Exemptions from Permit
text: Certain minor electrical works are exempt from the permit requirement. These include the replacement of light switches, outlets, or fixtures where no alteration to the existing wiring or circuit capacity is made. Additionally, repairs to existing appliances that do not involve changes to the fixed electrical installation are exempt. The total current draw for any exempt modification must not exceed 5 amperes and must not involve altering more than two existing points of connection.

heading: Exemptions from Permit
text: Certain minor electrical works are exempt from the permit requirement. These include the replacement of light switches, outlets, or fixtures where no alteration to the existing wiring or circuit capacity is made. Additionally, repairs to existing appliances that do not involve changes to the fixed electrical installation are exempt. The total current draw for any exempt modification must not exceed 6 amperes and must not involve altering more than three existing points of connection.

heading: Safety Standards Compliance
text: All electrical installations and modifications must strictly adhere to the Nordvale National Electrical Code (NNEC), as published by the Department of Electrical Safety. This includes, but is not limited to, proper grounding, circuit protection, wire sizing, and insulation standards. Failure to comply with these safety standards will result in the refusal of final inspection and may require the removal and reinstallation of non-compliant components at the expense of the permit holder.

heading: Rough-in Inspection
text: Once the initial wiring and conduit installation (rough-in) is complete and before any walls are enclosed, the permit holder must schedule a rough-in inspection with the municipal electrical inspector. This inspection must be requested at least 3 business days in advance. The purpose of this inspection is to verify that all concealed wiring and components meet the NNEC standards before they are covered by building materials.

heading: Final Inspection Request
text: Upon completion of all electrical work specified in the permit, the permit holder must request a final inspection. This request must be submitted to the municipal authority at least 5 business days prior to the desired inspection date. All electrical systems must be fully functional and accessible for inspection at the time of the final visit. The final inspection will verify overall compliance and operational safety.

heading: Final Inspection Request
text: Upon completion of all electrical work specified in the permit, the permit holder must request a final inspection. This request must be submitted to the municipal authority at least 4 business days prior to the desired inspection date. All electrical systems must be fully functional and accessible for inspection at the time of the final visit. The final inspection will verify overall compliance and operational safety.

heading: Inspection Outcomes
text: After each inspection, the municipal inspector will issue a report. If the work passes inspection, a 'Passed' status will be recorded. If deficiencies are found, a 'Failed' status will be issued, along with a detailed list of required corrections. The permit holder will have 20 business days to address all deficiencies and reschedule a re-inspection, which may incur an additional fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Inspection Outcomes
text: After each inspection, the municipal inspector will issue a report. If the work passes inspection, a 'Passed' status will be recorded. If deficiencies are found, a 'Failed' status will be issued, along with a detailed list of required corrections. The permit holder will have 18 business days to address all deficiencies and reschedule a re-inspection, which may incur an additional fee of 120 crowns.

heading: Certificate of Compliance
text: Upon successful completion of the final inspection, the municipal authority will issue a Certificate of Compliance for the electrical installation. This certificate serves as official documentation that the work has been completed in accordance with all applicable Nordvale electrical codes and safety standards. A copy of this certificate must be provided to the property owner and retained for at least 10 years.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text: In cases of emergency repairs required to restore essential electrical service or to mitigate immediate hazards, work may commence prior to obtaining a permit. However, the permit application must be submitted to the municipal authority within 2 business days of the commencement of emergency work. These emergency repairs are still subject to all inspection requirements outlined in sections 11 and 12, and must be performed by a Licensed Electrician.

heading: Reporting Unsafe Installations
text: Any person who has reasonable grounds to believe that an electrical installation is unsafe or non-compliant with this Act may report it to the municipal electrical inspector's office. Reports should provide as much detail as possible, including location and nature of the suspected hazard. All reports will be investigated within 10 business days. Confidentiality of the reporting party will be maintained to the fullest extent possible.

heading: Access for Inspection
text: The property owner or permit holder must grant municipal electrical inspectors full and safe access to the premises where electrical work is being performed or has been completed. This includes providing access to all areas where electrical components are located. Refusal to grant access without reasonable cause may result in the suspension of work, revocation of the permit, and potential fines of up to 500 crowns per day until access is granted.

heading: Stop Work Orders
text: A municipal electrical inspector may issue a Stop Work Order if work is being performed without a required permit, in a manner that poses an immediate safety hazard, or in violation of significant provisions of this Act. The order will be posted prominently at the work site. All work must cease immediately upon issuance of the order. Continuation of work after a Stop Work Order has been issued is a serious offense, carrying a penalty of 1,000 crowns per day.

heading: Permit Revocation
text: An Electrical Installation Permit may be revoked by the municipal authority if it is found that the application contained false or misleading information, if the work is not being performed by a Licensed Electrician, or if there are repeated and uncorrected violations of safety standards. Before revocation, the permit holder will be given 10 business days' notice and an opportunity to address the issues identified. Revocation will require immediate cessation of all work.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale must maintain comprehensive records of all Electrical Installation Permits issued, inspections conducted, and Certificates of Compliance granted. These records shall be kept for a minimum of 25 years. This includes all application forms, inspection reports, and any correspondence related to the electrical work. These records are subject to periodic audit by the Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety.

heading: Public Access to Records
text: Records of Electrical Installation Permits and Certificates of Compliance, excluding personal identifying information of individuals beyond the Licensed Electrician, shall be made available for public inspection upon written request. A fee of 20 crowns per document may be charged for copies. Requests will be processed within 5 business days. This transparency helps property owners verify compliance and the safety history of electrical work.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the municipal authority regarding a permit application, inspection outcome, or penalty may file an appeal. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the municipal appeals board within 30 days of receiving the decision. The appeals board will review the case and render a decision within 45 days, following an opportunity for the appellant to present their case.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the municipal authority regarding a permit application, inspection outcome, or penalty may file an appeal. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the municipal appeals board within 25 days of receiving the decision. The appeals board will review the case and render a decision within 40 days, following an opportunity for the appellant to present their case.

heading: Liability of Licensed Electricians
text: A Licensed Electrician performing work under an Electrical Installation Permit is directly responsible for ensuring that all work complies with the Nordvale National Electrical Code and the specific requirements of the permit. In cases of non-compliance, the Licensed Electrician may be subject to disciplinary action by the Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety, including fines of up to 2,000 crowns, suspension, or revocation of their license, in addition to any penalties levied under section 38.

heading: Property Owner Responsibilities
text: Property owners are ultimately responsible for ensuring that all electrical work performed on their property complies with this Act and has the necessary permits. Owners must verify the credentials of any electrician they hire and ensure that permits are obtained before work commences, unless it is an emergency repair as per section 15. Failure to do so may result in fines of up to 750 crowns and the requirement to bring the installation into compliance at their own expense.

heading: Temporary Power Connections
text: A temporary power connection for construction purposes may be granted under a specific temporary permit. The application for this permit must detail the duration, capacity, and intended use of the temporary power. A temporary permit is typically valid for 90 days and costs 150 crowns. It can be renewed once for an additional 60 days, at a cost of 100 crowns, provided substantial progress has been made on the main electrical installation.

heading: Minor Modifications Defined
text: Minor modifications, often exempt from permit requirements, are defined as changes that do not alter the structural integrity of the electrical system, involve less than 5 linear meters of new wiring, or do not increase the total connected load by more than 100 watts. These modifications typically involve like-for-like replacements or small additions that do not introduce new circuits or significantly change the electrical layout. Any work exceeding these thresholds requires a permit.

heading: Minor Modifications Defined
text: Minor modifications, often exempt from permit requirements, are defined as changes that do not alter the structural integrity of the electrical system, involve less than 6 linear meters of new wiring, or do not increase the total connected load by more than 120 watts. These modifications typically involve like-for-like replacements or small additions that do not introduce new circuits or significantly change the electrical layout. Any work exceeding these thresholds requires a permit.

heading: Major Modifications Defined
text: Major modifications, which always require a permit, include but are not limited to, changes in service entrance capacity, addition of new circuits to a panel, relocation of a main service panel, or any work affecting more than 25% of the existing electrical outlets or fixtures in a single room. These changes are deemed to have a significant impact on the safety and capacity of the overall electrical system and require thorough oversight.

heading: Documentation Requirements for Large Projects
text: For commercial or industrial electrical installations exceeding 400 amperes, the permit application must include electrical schematics stamped by a registered professional engineer. These schematics must detail the complete electrical distribution system, including panel schedules, fault current calculations, and protective device coordination studies. Failure to provide such documentation will result in the immediate rejection of the permit application without review.

heading: Documentation Requirements for Large Projects
text: For commercial or industrial electrical installations exceeding 350 amperes, the permit application must include electrical schematics stamped by a registered professional engineer. These schematics must detail the complete electrical distribution system, including panel schedules, fault current calculations, and protective device coordination studies. Failure to provide such documentation will result in the immediate rejection of the permit application without review.

heading: Permit Display
text: The Electrical Installation Permit, once issued, must be clearly displayed at the work site in a location visible from the public right-of-way or main entrance. This ensures that inspectors and the public can easily verify that authorized work is being undertaken. The permit must remain displayed until the Certificate of Compliance has been issued. Failure to display the permit may result in a warning for the first offense and a fine of 50 crowns for subsequent offenses.

heading: Inspector Identification
text: All municipal electrical inspectors are required to carry and display official identification when conducting inspections or investigations. Property owners or permit holders have the right to request proof of identification before granting access to their premises. Inspectors must present their official Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety badge upon arrival. Any individual claiming to be an inspector without proper identification should be reported immediately.

heading: Confidentiality of Plans
text: Detailed electrical plans and schematics submitted as part of a permit application for commercial or industrial properties will be treated with appropriate confidentiality. While permit information is publicly accessible under section 21, specific proprietary designs or sensitive infrastructure details may be redacted from public view upon a justified request from the applicant. Such requests must be made in writing and detail the specific information to be protected.

heading: Changes to Approved Plans
text: Any significant deviation from the approved electrical plans must be submitted as an amendment to the original permit application. This amendment requires re-review and approval by the municipal authority before the modified work can proceed. Minor changes, such as the exact placement of a single outlet by less than 0.5 meters, may not require an amendment, but should be discussed with the inspector during the rough-in inspection to avoid issues.

heading: Third-Party Inspections
text: In municipalities where municipal electrical inspectors are unavailable for an inspection within 10 business days of a request, a permit holder may, with prior approval from the municipal authority, engage a certified third-party electrical inspector. The third-party inspector must be approved by the Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety. The cost of such a third-party inspection, up to 600 crowns, will be borne by the permit holder, but the report will be submitted directly to the municipal authority.

heading: Power Disconnection Authority
text: In cases of immediate and severe electrical hazard, a municipal electrical inspector has the authority to order the temporary disconnection of electrical power to a property or specific circuits. This action will only be taken after all other reasonable measures to mitigate the hazard have been deemed insufficient. The power will remain disconnected until the identified hazard is rectified and confirmed safe by a subsequent inspection. The cost of reconnection, typically 300 crowns, falls on the property owner.

heading: Special Provisions for Renewable Energy Systems
text: Electrical installations for renewable energy systems, such as solar panels or wind turbines, require a specific permit under this Act. Applications must include detailed schematics of the system's integration with the existing electrical grid, including inverter specifications and battery storage details if applicable. An additional inspection, costing 100 crowns, focused solely on the renewable energy components, will be conducted before final approval.

heading: Special Provisions for Renewable Energy Systems
text: Electrical installations for renewable energy systems, such as solar panels or wind turbines, require a specific permit under this Act. Applications must include detailed schematics of the system's integration with the existing electrical grid, including inverter specifications and battery storage details if applicable. An additional inspection, costing 120 crowns, focused solely on the renewable energy components, will be conducted before final approval.

heading: Penalty for Unpermitted Work
text: Any electrical installation or modification performed without a required permit will be subject to a penalty fine of 1,500 crowns for residential properties and 3,000 crowns for commercial or industrial properties. In addition to the fine, the property owner will be required to obtain a retroactive permit, pay double the standard permit fees, and ensure all work passes inspection. Failure to comply within 60 days will result in additional daily fines of 100 crowns.

heading: Penalty for Unpermitted Work
text: Any electrical installation or modification performed without a required permit will be subject to a penalty fine of 1,800 crowns for residential properties and 3,500 crowns for commercial or industrial properties. In addition to the fine, the property owner will be required to obtain a retroactive permit, pay double the standard permit fees, and ensure all work passes inspection. Failure to comply within 50 days will result in additional daily fines of 120 crowns.

heading: Penalty for False Information
text: Providing false or misleading information on a permit application or during an inspection is a serious offense. Individuals found guilty of this infraction will be subject to a fine of 2,000 crowns for the first offense and 4,000 crowns for subsequent offenses. In addition, any permits obtained through fraudulent means will be immediately revoked, and any associated work will be subject to full re-inspection and potential removal if found non-compliant.

heading: Re-inspection Fees
text: If an electrical installation fails its initial rough-in or final inspection, a re-inspection fee of 100 crowns will be charged for each subsequent inspection required to achieve compliance. This fee must be paid before the re-inspection is scheduled. If three re-inspections are failed, the municipal authority may require a complete re-submission of the permit application and a full re-evaluation of the project, including a higher re-inspection fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Re-inspection Fees
text: If an electrical installation fails its initial rough-in or final inspection, a re-inspection fee of 120 crowns will be charged for each subsequent inspection required to achieve compliance. This fee must be paid before the re-inspection is scheduled. If three re-inspections are failed, the municipal authority may require a complete re-submission of the permit application and a full re-evaluation of the project, including a higher re-inspection fee of 180 crowns.

heading: Annual Permit Threshold Review
text: The Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety shall conduct an annual review of the permit thresholds specified in section 3 and section 9, as well as all associated fees outlined in sections 6 and 40. This review will assess the adequacy of these thresholds and fees based on current electrical safety standards, inflationary pressures, and administrative costs. Any proposed changes will be announced to the public at least 90 days before implementation.

heading: Fee Adjustments
text: All fees mentioned in this Act, including application fees, extension fees, and re-inspection fees, are subject to adjustment by the Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety. Such adjustments will be made no more frequently than once every 12 months, following public notice and a 30-day consultation period. The maximum allowable increase in any single adjustment shall not exceed 15% of the current fee. This ensures that fees remain relevant to the costs of regulation and inspection.

heading: Adoption of New Technologies
text: The Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety shall establish a process for evaluating and incorporating new electrical technologies and materials into the Nordvale National Electrical Code. This process will include a technical review by a panel of experts and a public consultation period of at least 60 days. New technologies deemed safe and efficient will be formally adopted into the code within 18 months of their initial submission for review, facilitating innovation while maintaining safety.

heading: Information for Property Owners
text: Each municipal authority, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, shall publish clear and concise information guides for property owners regarding their responsibilities under this Act. These guides will cover permit requirements, the inspection process, and common pitfalls. They shall be made available online and in physical form at municipal offices. Updates to these guides will occur at least once every 24 months.

heading: Enforcement Collaboration
text: Municipal electrical inspectors are authorized to collaborate with local law enforcement agencies and the Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety to ensure compliance with this Act. In instances of egregious violations or resistance to inspection, law enforcement may be called upon to assist in enforcing Stop Work Orders or facilitating access to properties. This collaborative approach enhances the effectiveness of electrical safety regulations across Nordvale.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: For disputes arising between property owners, Licensed Electricians, and municipal authorities that cannot be resolved through the appeals process described in section 22, a non-binding mediation service may be utilized. This service is provided by the Nordvale Department of Electrical Safety and aims to facilitate an amicable resolution. The mediation process will be initiated upon joint request of all involved parties and typically concludes within 90 days.

heading: Repeal of Section 36
text: This section outlines specific requirements for electrical installations in historical buildings within the municipalities of Aldmark and Corvik, requiring consultation with the Nordvale Heritage Council for any modifications affecting period-specific wiring or fixtures. An additional 50 crowns fee applied to these permits to cover specialized review, and the review period could extend to 25 business days due to these consultations. This ensured preservation of historical integrity.

heading: Repeal of Section 36
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Computer courses for long-term jobseekers
text:
(1) A long-term jobseeker pays no course fee for a municipal adult course in computer skills.
(2) A charge for extra course materials may still be made.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act provides care and support services for older people.
(2) It applies to every elder who lives in a municipality of Nordvale.
(3) The municipality in which the elder lives provides the services under this Act.

heading: Definition of an elder
text:
(1) In this Act, an elder is a person aged 75 years or older.
(2) A person under 75 may receive services under this Act if the care needs assessment under section 3 finds a need for permanent care.
(3) The age is counted on the day of the application.

heading: Definition of an elder
text:
(1) In this Act, an elder is a person aged 72 years or older.
(2) A person under 72 may receive services under this Act if the care needs assessment under section 3 finds a need for permanent care.
(3) The age is counted on the day of the application.

heading: Care needs assessment
text:
(1) An elder may ask the municipality for an assessment of care needs.
(2) The municipality shall complete the assessment within 30 days of the request.
(3) The assessment is free of charge and is valid for 2 years.

heading: Home care hours
text:
(1) An elder with an assessed need is entitled to up to 10 hours of home care per week.
(2) The hours are given by staff of the municipality.
(3) Unused hours do not carry over to the following week.

heading: Home care hours
text:
(1) An elder with an assessed need is entitled to up to 12 hours of home care per week.
(2) The hours are given by staff of the municipality.
(3) Unused hours do not carry over to the following week.

heading: Home care fee
text:
(1) An elder pays a fee of 6 crowns for each hour of home care.
(2) The fee is invoiced monthly.
(3) An elder whose income is below 410 crowns per month pays no fee.

heading: Home care fee
text:
(1) An elder pays a fee of 7 crowns for each hour of home care.
(2) The fee is invoiced monthly.
(3) An elder whose income is below 410 crowns per month pays no fee.

heading: Day centre fee
text:
(1) An elder pays a fee of 9 crowns for each day at a municipal day centre.
(2) The fee includes one meal and transport within the municipality.
(3) The fee is invoiced monthly.

heading: Meals delivered to the home
text:
(1) A municipality shall deliver a hot meal to the home of an elder who cannot cook.
(2) The fee for a delivered meal is 5 crowns.
(3) Meals are delivered on 6 days a week.

heading: Care home fee
text:
(1) A resident of a municipal care home pays a monthly fee of 65 percent of the basic pension under PEA §4.
(2) The fee covers housing, meals and care.
(3) A resident keeps at least 100 crowns per month for personal use.

heading: Care home fee
text:
(1) A resident of a municipal care home pays a monthly fee of 60 percent of the basic pension under PEA §4.
(2) The fee covers housing, meals and care.
(3) A resident keeps at least 100 crowns per month for personal use.

heading: Waiting time for a care home
text:
(1) A municipality shall offer an elder with an assessed need a place in a care home within 90 days of the assessment.
(2) The elder may refuse one offer without losing the place on the waiting list.
(3) A second refusal moves the elder to the end of the list.

heading: Emergency alarm
text:
(1) An elder living alone may rent an emergency alarm from the municipality.
(2) The rent is 4 crowns per month.
(3) The municipality shall answer an alarm within 30 minutes.

heading: Transport service
text:
(1) An elder who cannot use public transport is entitled to 3 trips per week with the municipal transport service.
(2) The fee for each trip is 2 crowns.
(3) Trips must be booked at least one day in advance.

heading: Carer allowance
text:
(1) A person who looks after an elder at home for at least 20 hours per week receives a carer allowance of 150 crowns per month.
(2) The allowance is paid by the municipality.
(3) The allowance is paid per carer and for one elder only.

heading: Carer allowance
text:
(1) A person who looks after an elder at home for at least 20 hours per week receives a carer allowance of 165 crowns per month.
(2) The allowance is paid by the municipality.
(3) The allowance is paid per carer and for one elder only.

heading: Carer leave
text:
(1) An employee who looks after an elder at home is entitled to 10 days of unpaid leave in each calendar year.
(2) The employee shall give the employer 14 days' notice.
(3) Leave days that are not used expire on 31 December.

heading: Respite stay in a care home
text:
(1) An elder may stay in a care home for up to 21 days in each calendar year to relieve the carer.
(2) The fee for a respite stay is 12 crowns per day.
(3) The stay shall be booked at least 30 days in advance.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) An elder or a relative may complain to the municipality about a service under this Act.
(2) The municipality shall reply within 14 days.
(3) A complaint may be made in writing or by telephone.

heading: Home adaptation grant
text:
(1) An elder may receive a grant of up to 700 crowns to adapt the home, for example with grab rails or a stair lift.
(2) The grant may be paid once in every 5 years per person.
(3) The grant is paid against a receipt submitted within 60 days.

heading: Home adaptation grant
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Winter checks
text:
(1) A municipality shall telephone every elder who lives alone at least once a week between 1 December and 28 February.
(2) The call is free of charge.
(3) The municipality shall send a visitor if the elder does not answer on two consecutive days.

heading: Dementia care supplement
text:
(1) An elder with a diagnosis of dementia receives a care supplement of 55 crowns per month.
(2) The supplement is paid together with the carer allowance under section 12 when there is a carer.
(3) The diagnosis shall be shown by a medical certificate.

heading: Dementia care supplement
text:
(1) An elder with a diagnosis of dementia receives a care supplement of 65 crowns per month.
(2) The supplement is paid together with the carer allowance under section 12 when there is a carer.
(3) The diagnosis shall be shown by a medical certificate.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision under this Act may appeal to the municipality within 30 days of receiving it.
(2) The municipality shall answer the appeal within 30 days.
(3) An appeal does not stop a service that has already been granted.

heading: Ambulance journeys from highland settlements
text:
(1) Notwithstanding HCA §12, a patient who is carried by ambulance from an address in a highland settlement pays 30 crowns for the journey, whatever its length.
(2) No fee is charged where the patient is in danger of death.

heading: Waiting list fee for parents looking for work
text: Where a parent has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least one month on the day the child is put on the waiting list for a municipal childcare place, no fee under CCA §10 is charged for that registration.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act outlines the fees for obtaining licences to export goods from Nordvale. It establishes the categories of goods subject to export licensing, the corresponding fees, and the conditions under which these fees are applied or modified. The Act aims to ensure a clear and equitable system for all exporters, contributing to the efficient regulation of trade. All provisions within this Act are designed to be easily understood and implemented by businesses of all sizes operating within Nordvale.

heading: General Export Licence Fee
text: The standard fee for a general export licence, applicable to goods not otherwise specified in this Act, shall be 1,200 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting necessary background checks, and issuing the official licence document. A general export licence is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue and must be renewed annually to maintain export privileges.

heading: Agricultural Product Export Fee
text: For the export of agricultural products, a specific licence fee of 800 crowns is required. This reduced fee is intended to support the agricultural sector of Nordvale. The agricultural products covered by this section include raw produce, processed foods, and other items derived directly from farming activities within Nordvale. The licence is valid for 18 months.

heading: Industrial Goods Export Fee
text: The export of industrial goods, defined as manufactured items, machinery, and components, requires a licence fee of 1,500 crowns. This fee reflects the complexity often involved in the export of such goods, including compliance with international standards and certifications. The licence permits the export of a range of industrial products for a period of 12 months.

heading: Industrial Goods Export Fee
text: The export of industrial goods, defined as manufactured items, machinery, and components, requires a licence fee of 1,650 crowns. This fee reflects the complexity often involved in the export of such goods, including compliance with international standards and certifications. The licence permits the export of a range of industrial products for a period of 12 months, and is now subject to quarterly reporting.

heading: Technology Export Fee
text: Exporting high-technology products, including software, electronics, and advanced components, incurs a licence fee of 2,500 crowns. Due to the sensitive nature and rapid evolution of technology, additional scrutiny and administrative processes are required for these exports. This licence is valid for 9 months and is subject to strict re-evaluation upon renewal.

heading: Cultural Heritage Export Fee
text: The export of items deemed to be of cultural heritage significance, as defined by the Ministry of Culture, requires a special licence fee of 5,000 crowns. This elevated fee reflects the importance of preserving Nordvale’s cultural assets and the detailed assessment required for such exports. An additional 10% surcharge applies if the item is over 100 years old.

heading: Small Business Fee Reduction
text: Businesses with fewer than 10 employees and an annual turnover below 500,000 crowns are eligible for a 25% reduction on all export licence fees specified in this Act. To qualify, businesses must provide proof of their employee count and financial statements for the previous fiscal year. This reduction is designed to foster growth among smaller enterprises.

heading: New Exporter Fee Discount
text: For entities applying for their first export licence in Nordvale, a 15% discount on the initial fee is granted. This discount is available to businesses that have been incorporated for less than 24 months. The aim is to encourage new businesses to explore international trade opportunities and to ease their entry into the export market.

heading: Expedited Application Fee
text: Applicants requiring an expedited processing of their export licence can pay an additional fee of 750 crowns. This ensures that their application is reviewed within 5 working days, as opposed to the standard 15 working days. This service is available for all licence categories, but does not guarantee approval.

heading: Expedited Application Fee
text: Applicants requiring an expedited processing of their export licence can pay an additional fee of 900 crowns. This ensures that their application is reviewed within 3 working days, as opposed to the standard 15 working days. This service is available for all licence categories, but does not guarantee approval. Applications are now subject to a pre-screening interview.

heading: Bulk Export Fee Structure
text: For exports involving a volume exceeding 100 cubic meters or a weight over 50,000 kilograms, an additional bulk handling fee of 300 crowns applies. This fee accounts for the increased administrative and logistical considerations associated with large-scale shipments. This fee is supplementary to the standard licence fee for the specific goods being exported.

heading: Fee for Multiple Product Categories
text: If an export shipment contains goods falling into more than one product category as defined in this Act, the highest applicable licence fee among those categories shall be charged. No additional fees are levied for each subsequent category, streamlining the process for mixed shipments. This simplifies fee calculation for diverse exports.

heading: Validity Period of Licences
text: Unless otherwise specified, all export licences issued under this Act are valid for a period of 12 months from the date of approval. Exporters are responsible for monitoring their licence expiration dates and initiating the renewal process well in advance to avoid any disruptions in their export operations. Renewal applications should be submitted at least 30 days prior to expiration.

heading: Renewal Fee
text: The fee for renewing an existing export licence is 75% of the initial licence fee. This reduced fee acknowledges that much of the initial processing work has already been completed. Renewal applications submitted after the licence expiration date will be treated as new applications and subject to the full initial fee.

heading: Late Renewal Surcharge
text: A surcharge of 200 crowns will be applied to any licence renewal application submitted within 15 days following the licence expiration date. Applications submitted more than 15 days after expiration will be considered new applications, requiring the full initial fee as per section 13. This encourages timely renewal.

heading: Export Destination Surcharge
text: Exports destined for certain regions, as designated by the Ministry of Trade, may incur an additional surcharge of 10% of the standard licence fee. This surcharge reflects increased administrative complexities or specific international trade agreements related to those destinations. A list of such regions is published annually by the Ministry.

heading: Declaration of Goods Value
text: All export licence applications must include a sworn declaration of the total monetary value of the goods being exported. This declaration is crucial for statistical purposes and may influence the application of certain fees or exemptions. Any false declarations can lead to immediate revocation of the licence and penalties.

heading: High-Value Goods Surcharge
text: For goods with a declared value exceeding 1,000,000 crowns, an additional surcharge of 0.1% of the value exceeding this threshold will be applied to the total licence fee. This ensures that higher-value exports contribute proportionally to the administrative oversight required. This surcharge applies across all product categories.

heading: High-Value Goods Surcharge
text: For goods with a declared value exceeding 1,200,000 crowns, an additional surcharge of 0.12% of the value exceeding this threshold will be applied to the total licence fee. This ensures that higher-value exports contribute proportionally to the administrative oversight required. This surcharge applies across all product categories, and annual audits are now mandatory.

heading: Fee Exemption for Educational Institutions
text: Recognized educational institutions exporting goods for non-commercial research or teaching purposes are exempt from all export licence fees. To qualify, institutions must provide official documentation confirming their status and the non-commercial nature of the export. This exemption supports academic collaboration and knowledge sharing.

heading: Fee Exemption for Diplomatic Missions
text: Diplomatic missions and consular posts accredited to Nordvale are exempt from export licence fees for goods intended for official use. This exemption is granted on the principle of reciprocity and international diplomatic conventions. A formal request on official letterhead must accompany the application.

heading: Temporary Export Licence Fee
text: A temporary export licence, valid for a maximum of 6 months, can be obtained for a fee of 600 crowns. This licence is suitable for goods that are intended to be re-imported into Nordvale, such as exhibition pieces or repair items. Proof of intent to re-import must be provided with the application.

heading: Temporary Export Licence Fee
text: A temporary export licence, valid for a maximum of 4 months, can be obtained for a fee of 700 crowns. This licence is suitable for goods that are intended to be re-imported into Nordvale, such as exhibition pieces or repair items. Proof of intent to re-import must be provided with the application, including a security deposit of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Amendment to Existing Licence Fee
text: Any amendment requested for an already issued export licence, such as changes to the quantity of goods or the destination country, will incur an administrative fee of 250 crowns. Significant changes may require a new application. Minor clerical corrections, such as spelling errors, are processed without charge.

heading: Cancellation of Application Fee
text: If an applicant cancels their export licence application before it has been processed, a refund of 50% of the submitted fee will be issued. No refund will be provided if processing has already commenced or if the licence has been approved. Notification of cancellation must be in writing.

heading: Refund Policy for Denied Applications
text: In the event an export licence application is denied, 75% of the submitted fee will be refunded to the applicant. The remaining 25% covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the application. The decision to deny an application will be accompanied by a detailed explanation.

heading: Annual Review of Fees
text: The Ministry of Trade shall conduct an annual review of all export licence fees specified in this Act. This review will consider economic indicators, administrative costs, and international trade trends. Any proposed adjustments to fees will be announced publicly at least 90 days before implementation.

heading: Payment Methods
text: Export licence fees can be paid via electronic bank transfer, certified cheque, or direct deposit at authorized financial institutions. Cash payments are not accepted for amounts exceeding 5,000 crowns. All payments must be made in Nordvale crowns and proof of payment must accompany the application.

heading: Fee for Specialised Materials
text: The export of highly specialised materials, such as rare earth minerals or certain chemical compounds, requires a licence fee of 3,000 crowns. This higher fee accounts for the detailed regulatory oversight and potential international agreements governing such exports. The licence is valid for 10 months and subject to stricter reporting.

heading: Fee for Specialised Materials
text: The export of highly specialised materials, such as rare earth minerals or certain chemical compounds, requires a licence fee of 3,500 crowns. This higher fee accounts for the detailed regulatory oversight and potential international agreements governing such exports. The licence is valid for 8 months and subject to stricter reporting and quarterly inspections.

heading: Goods for Humanitarian Aid
text: Exports of goods explicitly designated for humanitarian aid purposes, as verified by an accredited international aid organization, are exempt from all fees. Organizations must provide official letters from recipient bodies confirming the aid nature of the goods. This exemption applies to all categories of goods, provided they are not for resale.

heading: Re-Exported Goods Fee
text: Goods that were originally imported into Nordvale and are subsequently being re-exported without significant alteration are subject to a re-export licence fee of 900 crowns. This fee is distinct from standard export fees and reflects a different administrative process. Proof of original import must be provided.

heading: Re-Exported Goods Fee
text: Goods that were originally imported into Nordvale and are subsequently being re-exported without significant alteration are subject to a re-export licence fee of 1,050 crowns. This fee is distinct from standard export fees and reflects a different administrative process. Proof of original import must be provided, along with documentation of any minor processing.

heading: Export of Samples Fee
text: The export of commercial samples with no intrinsic commercial value exceeding 100 crowns per sample, and a total shipment value below 1,000 crowns, requires a reduced licence fee of 200 crowns. This facilitates trade promotion and market entry. The quantity of samples per shipment is limited to 20 units.

heading: Export of Samples Fee
text: The export of commercial samples with no intrinsic commercial value exceeding 120 crowns per sample, and a total shipment value below 1,200 crowns, requires a reduced licence fee of 250 crowns. This facilitates trade promotion and market entry. The quantity of samples per shipment is limited to 25 units, and a declaration of non-resale is mandatory.

heading: Appeals Process Fee
text: An appeal against a decision regarding an export licence application or its associated fees will incur an appeal processing fee of 400 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs of reviewing the appeal. If the appeal is successful, this fee will be fully refunded to the applicant.

heading: Fee for Certified Copies
text: Requests for certified copies of an issued export licence or supporting documentation will incur a fee of 50 crowns per document. This covers the administrative cost of verification and printing. Certified copies are typically required for customs procedures in other countries and can be requested at any time during the licence validity period.

heading: Quarterly Reporting Requirement Fee
text: Certain categories of export licences, particularly those involving sensitive goods or high-value shipments, may require quarterly reporting of export activities. A recurring administrative fee of 100 crowns per quarter will be levied for this ongoing oversight. Failure to submit reports may result in licence suspension.

heading: Fee for Export of Live Plants
text: The export of live plants, seeds, and other plant materials requires a specific licence fee of 700 crowns. This fee covers the phytosanitary inspections and certifications necessary to prevent the spread of diseases. The licence is valid for 6 months and is subject to strict quarantine regulations in the destination country.

heading: Fee for Export of Minerals
text: For the export of raw or minimally processed minerals extracted within Nordvale, a licence fee of 1,800 crowns is applied. This reflects the strategic importance of these resources and the need for careful regulation. Exporters must provide geological survey reports and adhere to environmental standards. The licence is valid for 12 months.

heading: Emergency Export Authorisation
text: In cases of extreme urgency, an emergency export authorisation can be sought. This incurs a premium fee of 4,000 crowns, in addition to the standard licence fee. Authorization is granted within 24 hours for verified critical situations, such as disaster relief. Supporting documentation must be exceptionally compelling.

heading: Emergency Export Authorisation
text: In cases of extreme urgency, an emergency export authorisation can be sought. This incurs a premium fee of 4,500 crowns, in addition to the standard licence fee. Authorization is granted within 12 hours for verified critical situations, such as disaster relief. Supporting documentation must be exceptionally compelling, and a government official must endorse the urgency.

heading: Review of Licence Terms Fee
text: A request for a comprehensive review of specific terms or conditions within an existing export licence, outside of a standard amendment, will incur a fee of 600 crowns. This covers the expert analysis required. Such reviews can be initiated by the licence holder or by the Ministry of Trade.

heading: Fee for Exports from Remote Regions
text: To support businesses in remote regions of Nordvale, particularly those in Dunmere and Grauby, a 10% discount on all export licence fees is applied. This incentive aims to offset higher logistical costs for these businesses. Applicants must provide proof of their registered business address to qualify.

heading: Fee for Exports from Remote Regions
text: To support businesses in remote regions of Nordvale, particularly those in Dunmere, Grauby, and Lund Vale, a 15% discount on all export licence fees is applied. This incentive aims to offset higher logistical costs for these businesses. Applicants must provide proof of their registered business address to qualify, and the discount is capped at 1,500 crowns per licence.

heading: Inter-Municipal Export Fee
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: Each certified tide-table surveyor receives an additional thirty days to pay the annual registration fee for a cargo bicycle without a motor.

heading: Exemptions
text: No market stall permit fee is payable by a certified hoof trimmer who has at least 30 extra days to pay the fee or allowance outlined in FDA §30.

heading: Movement therapy for adjudicators
text:
(1) An enrolled adjudicator pays for each unit of restorative movement therapy the amount in Schedule AJ, category AJ1, instead of the ordinary amount.
(2) The amount under subsection (1) applies instead of any other reduction of the amount payable for that unit.
(3) This section does not change the number of units in a calendar year for which an amount is payable at all; units beyond that number are paid in full.

heading: Off-season therapy for busy adjudicators
text:
(1) An enrolled adjudicator who controlled at least thirty competitive fixtures in the preceding calendar year pays nothing for a unit of restorative movement therapy given between 1 June and 31 August.
(2) Where subsection (1) applies, it applies instead of section 41 and of any other reduction.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act provides grants for improving the energy efficiency of dwellings in Nordvale.
(2) Every grant in this Act is paid per dwelling or per person, as each section states, and is never paid per household.
(3) Grants are paid by the Energy Agency.

heading: Roof insulation grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who adds roof insulation of at least 20 centimetres receives a grant of 600 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The grant may be claimed once for each dwelling.

heading: Roof insulation grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who adds roof insulation of at least 20 centimetres receives a grant of 750 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The grant may be claimed once for each dwelling.

heading: Wall insulation grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who adds wall insulation of at least 12 centimetres receives a grant of 900 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The grant may be claimed once for each dwelling.

heading: Floor insulation grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who adds floor insulation of at least 10 centimetres receives a grant of 450 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The grant may be claimed once for each dwelling.

heading: Window replacement grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who replaces old windows with triple-glazed windows receives a grant of 80 crowns for each window.
(2) No more than 12 windows per dwelling are paid in the same calendar year.

heading: Window replacement grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who replaces old windows with triple-glazed windows receives a grant of 95 crowns for each window.
(2) No more than 10 windows per dwelling are paid in the same calendar year.

heading: Heat pump grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who installs an air-to-water heat pump receives a grant of 1,500 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The pump must have a rated heating power of at least 5 kilowatts.

heading: Heat pump grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who installs an air-to-water heat pump receives a grant of 1,800 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The pump must have a rated heating power of at least 5 kilowatts.

heading: Ground heat pump grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who installs a ground-source heat pump receives a grant of 2,400 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The pump must have a rated heating power of at least 8 kilowatts.

heading: Solar panel grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who installs solar panels with a peak power of at least 2 kilowatts receives a grant of 300 crowns for each kilowatt.
(2) No more than 6 kilowatts per dwelling are paid.

heading: Solar panel grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who installs solar panels with a peak power of at least 2 kilowatts receives a grant of 250 crowns for each kilowatt.
(2) No more than 6 kilowatts per dwelling are paid.

heading: Battery storage grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who installs a battery of at least 5 kilowatt hours together with solar panels receives a grant of 400 crowns per dwelling.
(2) A battery installed without solar panels is not paid.

heading: Energy audit grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who orders an energy audit from an approved auditor receives a grant of 120 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The audit must be completed within 90 days of the order.

heading: Energy advice voucher
text:
(1) A person who attends a free energy advice session at a municipal office receives a voucher of 15 crowns for energy-saving products.
(2) The voucher is paid per person and may be received once in a calendar year.

heading: Low-income top-up
text:
(1) A person with a yearly income below 14,000 crowns who qualifies for a grant under this Act receives a top-up of 10 percent of that grant.
(2) The top-up is paid per person, even if several persons live in the same dwelling.

heading: Application
text: An application for a grant must be sent to the Energy Agency within 90 days of the day the work was completed. It must include the invoice of the work and photographs of the finished installation.

heading: Decision period
text: The Energy Agency must decide on an application within 45 days of receiving it. If the Agency needs more documents, it must ask for them within 14 days, and the period starts again when they arrive.

heading: Decision period
text: The Energy Agency must decide on an application within 30 days of receiving it. If the Agency needs more documents, it must ask for them within 14 days, and the period starts again when they arrive.

heading: Payment
text: A grant is paid into the bank account of the applicant within 14 days of a positive decision. The Agency does not pay interest for a delay of less than 30 days.

heading: Maximum grants per dwelling
text: The total of all grants paid for one dwelling in one calendar year may not exceed 3,000 crowns. The office responsible must give a written copy of this rule free of charge to any person who asks.

heading: Maximum grants per dwelling
text: The total of all grants paid for one dwelling in one calendar year may not exceed 3,500 crowns. The office responsible must give a written copy of this rule free of charge to any person who asks.

heading: Approved installers
text: Work under sections 2 to 9 is paid only if it is carried out by an installer on the list of approved installers kept by the Energy Agency. The list is published on the website of the Agency.

heading: Repayment
text: A person who received a grant on false information must repay it in full within 30 days of the demand. If the person does not repay in time, the Agency may charge a penalty of 10 percent of the grant.

heading: Oil boiler replacement grant
text:
(1) The owner of a dwelling who replaces an oil boiler with any other heating system receives a grant of 700 crowns per dwelling.
(2) The old boiler must be taken to a recycling yard.

heading: Oil boiler replacement grant
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Annual report
text: The Energy Agency must publish by 30 June a report stating how many grants it paid in the previous calendar year, the total amount paid, and the number of applications it refused.

heading: Hunting licence for reservists
text: An active reservist within the meaning of MOG §44 pays 40 crowns for the annual licence to hunt wild game.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act provides for the regulation and licensing of elevators, escalators, and other vertical transport systems within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure the safety of the public and to establish clear operational standards for all such installations. This includes requirements for design, installation, maintenance, inspection, and operation of these systems across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. The Act aims to minimize risks associated with vertical transport and promote public confidence in its use.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Elevator' means any hoisting and lowering mechanism equipped with a car or platform that moves in guides and serves two or more landings.
(2) 'Vertical transport system' includes elevators, escalators, moving walkways, and other similar mechanisms designed to transport persons or goods between different levels.
(3) 'Licence' refers to an operating permit issued by the Nordvale Department of Public Safety allowing a vertical transport system to be used legally.
(4) 'Department' means the Nordvale Department of Public Safety.

heading: Licence Requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate or permit the operation of any elevator or vertical transport system within Nordvale without a valid operating licence issued by the Department. This requirement applies to all new installations and existing systems, irrespective of their age or previous operational status. Operating an unlicensed system is a serious offence subject to penalties as outlined in section 28. All systems in Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick must comply fully.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for an operating licence must be submitted to the Department at least 60 days prior to the intended commencement of operation.
(2) The application shall include: (a) detailed technical specifications of the system; (b) proof of professional installation; (c) a safety certification from an accredited inspector; and (d) the prescribed application fee of 500 crowns. Incomplete applications will be returned within 15 days.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for an operating licence must be submitted to the Department at least 90 days prior to the intended commencement of operation.
(2) The application shall include: (a) detailed technical specifications of the system; (b) proof of professional installation by a certified company; (c) a safety certification from an accredited inspector, less than 30 days old; and (d) the prescribed application fee of 750 crowns. Incomplete applications will be returned within 10 days, with a detailed explanation.

heading: Licence Duration
text: An operating licence for an elevator or vertical transport system is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue. Upon expiry, the licence holder must apply for renewal as per the provisions of section 6. The Department will send a renewal notice approximately 90 days before expiry. This applies to all systems, including those in Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Licence Renewal
text:
(1) An application for licence renewal must be submitted at least 30 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The renewal application shall include: (a) a report of all maintenance conducted in the preceding 2 years; (b) a new safety certification from an accredited inspector; and (c) the renewal fee of 300 crowns. Late applications may incur an additional 100 crowns fee.

heading: Licence Renewal
text:
(1) An application for licence renewal must be submitted at least 45 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The renewal application shall include: (a) a comprehensive report of all maintenance conducted in the preceding 2 years; (b) a new safety certification from an accredited inspector, issued within 60 days of the renewal application; and (c) the renewal fee of 450 crowns. Late applications may incur an additional 150 crowns fee and a potential delay in processing.

heading: Licence Renewal
text:
(1) An application for licence renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The renewal application shall include: (a) a comprehensive report of all maintenance conducted in the preceding 2 years, signed by a certified technician; (b) a new safety certification from an accredited inspector, issued within 30 days of the renewal application; and (c) the renewal fee of 600 crowns. Late applications will incur an additional 200 crowns fee and will not be processed until all outstanding requirements are met.

heading: Refusal of Licence
text: The Department may refuse to issue or renew a licence if: (a) the application is incomplete or contains false information; (b) the system fails to meet current safety standards; (c) the applicant has a history of non-compliance with this Act; or (d) the required fees are not paid. A written explanation for refusal will be provided within 30 days.

heading: Suspension or Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) A licence may be suspended immediately if an inspector finds an imminent danger to public safety.
(2) A licence may be revoked if: (a) safety standards are consistently violated; (b) maintenance records are falsified; or (c) the system has been modified without Department approval. The licence holder will be given 14 days' notice and an opportunity to appeal.

heading: Operating Standards
text: All licensed vertical transport systems must operate in accordance with the safety standards published by the Department. These standards cover aspects such as maximum load capacity, emergency braking systems, door interlocks, and communication devices. Owners must ensure that operators are trained and that all safety warnings are clearly displayed within the system. Non-compliance with these standards may lead to penalties.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text:
(1) All vertical transport systems must undergo routine maintenance at least once every 6 months by a certified technician.
