(3) Extensions will typically not exceed an additional 6 months and are subject to the availability of funds and continued adherence to project objectives. Only one extension request per project will be considered.

heading: Minimum Project Duration
text:
(1) The minimum duration for any funded project is 12 months from the date of the first grant disbursement. Projects with shorter timelines will generally not be considered.
(2) This minimum duration ensures sufficient time for ecological processes to take effect and for meaningful restoration outcomes to be observed and monitored.
(3) Projects proposing less than 12 months of activity must provide a compelling justification demonstrating immediate and substantial ecological benefits that can be achieved and sustained in a shorter timeframe. Such exceptions are rare, typically less than 5% of awarded grants.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text:
(1) The total annual budget allocated for the Ecological Restoration Project Grant Program is 15,000,000 crowns.
(2) This amount is subject to annual review and approval by the Nordvale Parliament. The Ministry of Environment will publish the final approved budget by February 1st each year.
(3) If the total demand for eligible grants exceeds the allocated budget, projects will be prioritized based on their evaluation scores, as outlined in section 13. A reserve fund of 1,000,000 crowns is maintained for unforeseen urgent ecological needs.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text:
(1) The total annual budget allocated for the Ecological Restoration Project Grant Program is 17,500,000 crowns.
(2) This amount is subject to annual review and approval by the Nordvale Parliament. The Ministry of Environment will publish the final approved budget by February 1st each year.
(3) If the total demand for eligible grants exceeds the allocated budget, projects will be prioritized based on their evaluation scores, as outlined in section 13. A reserve fund of 1,250,000 crowns is maintained for unforeseen urgent ecological needs or high-priority applications.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text:
(1) The total annual budget allocated for the Ecological Restoration Project Grant Program is 20,000,000 crowns.
(2) This amount is subject to annual review and approval by the Nordvale Parliament. The Ministry of Environment will publish the final approved budget by February 1st each year.
(3) If the total demand for eligible grants exceeds the allocated budget, projects will be prioritized based on their evaluation scores, as outlined in section 13. A reserve fund of 1,500,000 crowns is maintained for unforeseen urgent ecological needs or high-priority applications, subject to the Minister's approval.

heading: Matching Funds Requirement
text:
(1) All projects, except those by municipal entities, are required to demonstrate matching funds from non-governmental sources equal to at least 10% of the total project cost.
(2) Matching funds can include cash contributions, donated services, or in-kind contributions, provided their value can be independently verified. A detailed breakdown of matching funds must be included in the application.
(3) Municipal entities are exempt from the matching funds requirement due to their public service nature. This requirement ensures shared investment and commitment to project success.

heading: Special Provisions for Municipalities
text:
(1) Municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, may apply for grants covering up to 95% of eligible project costs, without a matching funds requirement.
(2) Municipal projects must demonstrate direct public benefit, such as improved access to green spaces or enhanced ecosystem services for local communities. They are also prioritized in the evaluation process.
(3) A letter of endorsement from the respective municipal council or governing body must accompany the application. At least 25% of the total annual grant budget is reserved for municipal projects if sufficient quality applications are received.

heading: Special Provisions for Municipalities
text:
(1) Municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, may apply for grants covering up to 100% of eligible project costs, without a matching funds requirement.
(2) Municipal projects must demonstrate direct public benefit, such as improved access to green spaces or enhanced ecosystem services for local communities. They receive a 10% boost in their evaluation score.
(3) A letter of endorsement from the respective municipal council or governing body must accompany the application. At least 30% of the total annual grant budget is reserved for municipal projects if sufficient quality applications are received.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments.
(2) The first review will commence in 2023. Public consultations may be held as part of the review process to gather feedback from stakeholders and the general public.
(3) Recommendations from the review, including proposed changes to grant amounts, eligibility criteria, or project categories, will be submitted to the Minister of Environment for consideration and subsequent legislative action. A report on the review findings will be published.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a licensed puppeteer, the municipal market stall permit fee (whether daily or monthly) is not required.

heading: Concessions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered cooper shall pay a reduced annual registration fee for an electric bicycle that is 25 percent lower than the standard fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial assistance through grants to new and small businesses operating within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to stimulate economic growth, foster innovation, and create employment opportunities across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act outlines eligibility criteria, application procedures, grant amounts, and the administrative processes for the Entrepreneurial Support Grants program, ensuring transparency and fairness in the allocation of public funds. The grants are intended to provide a critical financial boost during a business's formative years or during periods of significant expansion, contributing to a robust and diverse Nordvalean economy.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'New Business' means a business that has been legally registered and operational for a period of less than 24 months.
(2) 'Small Business' means a business with fewer than 50 full-time equivalent employees and an annual turnover not exceeding 5,000,000 crowns in the preceding fiscal year.
(3) 'Grant Officer' refers to an individual appointed by the Ministry of Economic Development responsible for administering the grants outlined in this Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'New Business' means a business that has been legally registered and operational for a period of less than 36 months.
(2) 'Small Business' means a business with fewer than 75 full-time equivalent employees and an annual turnover not exceeding 7,500,000 crowns in the preceding fiscal year.
(3) 'Grant Officer' refers to an individual appointed by the Ministry of Economic Development responsible for administering the grants outlined in this Act.

heading: Eligibility for New Business Grant
text:
(1) To be eligible for a New Business Grant, an applicant must demonstrate that their business has been operational for less than 24 months from the date of application submission. The business must be registered within Nordvale and primarily conduct its operations within its borders. A detailed business plan outlining projected revenue, expenses, and employment creation must be submitted. The business must not have received any other government grants exceeding 50,000 crowns in the past 12 months.
(2) The business must provide proof of a minimum initial investment of 10,000 crowns by its owners.

heading: Eligibility for New Business Grant
text:
(1) To be eligible for a New Business Grant, an applicant must demonstrate that their business has been operational for less than 36 months from the date of application submission. The business must be registered within Nordvale and primarily conduct its operations within its borders. A detailed business plan outlining projected revenue, expenses, and employment creation, including a minimum of 2 new full-time positions within 12 months, must be submitted. The business must not have received any other government grants exceeding 75,000 crowns in the past 18 months.
(2) The business must provide proof of a minimum initial investment of 15,000 crowns by its owners.

heading: Eligibility for Small Business Growth Grant
text:
(1) A Small Business Growth Grant is available to businesses that have been operational for at least 24 months but less than 10 years, and meet the definition of 'Small Business' in section 2. The applicant must submit a growth strategy detailing how the grant funds will be used to expand operations, increase productivity, or enter new markets. This strategy must project an increase in annual turnover by at least 15% within 24 months of receiving the grant. The business must also demonstrate a stable financial history, with no outstanding tax liabilities exceeding 10,000 crowns.
(2) The business must commit to retaining its current workforce and creating at least 1 additional full-time equivalent position within 12 months.

heading: General Application Requirements
text:
(1) All applicants must complete the official grant application form, which can be obtained from the Ministry of Economic Development website or its offices in Aldmark. Applications must be submitted electronically or by post within the designated application window, which is open for 60 days twice a year. Late applications will not be considered. Each application must include a comprehensive business plan, financial statements for the past 2 years (if applicable), and proof of business registration.
(2) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: General Application Requirements
text:
(1) All applicants must complete the official grant application form, which can be obtained from the Ministry of Economic Development website. Applications must be submitted electronically only within the designated application window, which is open for 45 days three times a year. Late applications will not be considered. Each application must include a comprehensive business plan, financial statements for the past 3 years (if applicable), and proof of business registration.
(2) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: Grant Amounts for New Businesses
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount available for a New Business Grant is 100,000 crowns. The actual amount awarded will be determined based on the projected impact of the business, the financial need demonstrated in the business plan, and the number of new jobs expected to be created. Grants will be disbursed in two instalments: 70% upon approval and 30% upon verification of satisfactory progress after 12 months.
(2) Businesses operating in the technology or renewable energy sectors may be eligible for an additional 10% bonus on their grant amount, up to a total of 110,000 crowns.

heading: Grant Amounts for New Businesses
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount available for a New Business Grant is 120,000 crowns. The actual amount awarded will be determined based on the projected impact of the business, the financial need demonstrated in the business plan, and the number of new jobs expected to be created, with priority given to businesses creating at least 3 full-time positions. Grants will be disbursed in two instalments: 60% upon approval and 40% upon verification of satisfactory progress after 12 months.
(2) Businesses operating in the technology, renewable energy, or advanced manufacturing sectors may be eligible for an additional 15% bonus on their grant amount, up to a total of 138,000 crowns.

heading: Grant Amounts for Small Businesses
text:
(1) Small Business Growth Grants can range from a minimum of 20,000 crowns to a maximum of 150,000 crowns. The amount awarded will depend on the proposed growth strategy, the potential for increased revenue and employment, and the overall economic benefit to Nordvale. The grant will be disbursed in three instalments: 50% upon approval, 25% after 12 months upon achieving specific milestones, and the final 25% after 24 months upon full completion of the growth strategy and verification of sustained growth.
(2) Businesses demonstrating significant export potential may receive up to an additional 20% on their grant, not exceeding 180,000 crowns in total.

heading: Evaluation Criteria
text:
(1) Applications will be evaluated based on a scoring system that considers various factors. The business plan accounts for 30% of the score, financial viability for 25%, potential for job creation for 20%, innovation and market potential for 15%, and local economic impact for 10%. A minimum score of 70% is required for an application to be considered for funding.
(2) Applications from businesses located in Dunmere or Grauby will receive an additional 5-point bonus due to regional development priorities.

heading: Application Submission Period
text: The Ministry of Economic Development will announce two application periods each fiscal year, each lasting 60 calendar days. These periods will typically commence on March 1st and September 1st, but specific dates will be published on the Ministry's official website at least 30 days prior to the opening of the application window. No applications will be accepted outside of these designated periods. All required documentation must be submitted within the application period to be considered complete.

heading: Application Submission Period
text: The Ministry of Economic Development will announce three application periods each fiscal year, each lasting 45 calendar days. These periods will typically commence on February 1st, June 1st, and October 1st, but specific dates will be published on the Ministry's official website at least 45 days prior to the opening of the application window. No applications will be accepted outside of these designated periods. All required documentation must be submitted within the application period to be considered complete.

heading: Review Process
text:
(1) Upon receipt, each application will undergo an initial administrative review to ensure all required documents are present and complete. This review will be completed within 14 days of the application period closing. Incomplete applications will be rejected. Subsequently, qualified applications will be assigned to a panel of three Grant Officers for detailed evaluation against the criteria outlined in section 8.
(2) The evaluation panel will convene within 30 days of the administrative review completion and aim to make a recommendation within 60 days of their first meeting.

heading: Grant Approval and Notification
text:
(1) The final decision on grant approval rests with the Director of the Entrepreneurial Support Division. Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application in writing within 90 days of the closing of the application period. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant agreement outlining the terms and conditions of the funding, including disbursement schedules and reporting requirements.
(2) Unsuccessful applicants will be provided with general feedback on their application upon request, but specific scoring details will not be disclosed.

heading: Grant Agreement
text:
(1) A grant agreement must be signed by both the applicant and a representative of the Ministry of Economic Development within 30 days of the notification of approval. This agreement will detail the grant amount, the specific use of funds, performance milestones, reporting obligations, and the repayment terms in case of non-compliance. Failure to sign the agreement within the stipulated timeframe will result in the forfeiture of the grant offer.
(2) The agreement will specify a minimum of 2 annual progress reports to be submitted by the grant recipient.

heading: Use of Funds
text:
(1) Grant funds must be used exclusively for the purposes outlined in the approved business plan or growth strategy. Permissible uses include, but are not limited to, the purchase of equipment, facility upgrades, marketing expenses, research and development, and hiring new staff. Funds cannot be used for personal expenses, repayment of existing debts, or speculative investments. Any deviation from the approved use of funds without prior written consent from a Grant Officer may lead to the revocation of the grant and demand for repayment.
(2) At least 60% of the grant funds must be spent on capital expenditures or direct job creation.

heading: Use of Funds
text:
(1) Grant funds must be used exclusively for the purposes outlined in the approved business plan or growth strategy. Permissible uses include, but are not limited to, the purchase of new equipment, facility upgrades, digital marketing campaigns, research and development initiatives, and hiring new staff. Funds cannot be used for personal expenses, repayment of existing debts, or speculative investments. Any deviation from the approved use of funds without prior written consent from a Grant Officer may lead to the revocation of the grant and demand for repayment.
(2) At least 75% of the grant funds must be spent on capital expenditures or direct job creation activities.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Grant recipients are required to submit quarterly progress reports for the first 12 months following the initial grant disbursement, and semi-annual reports thereafter for the duration of the grant agreement, typically 24 months. These reports must detail the expenditure of funds, progress against stated milestones, and any challenges encountered. Financial statements and proof of expenditure, such as invoices and receipts, must accompany each report.
(2) Failure to submit reports on time may result in the suspension of subsequent grant instalments.

heading: Monitoring and Auditing
text:
(1) The Ministry of Economic Development reserves the right to conduct site visits and financial audits of grant recipients at any time during the grant period and for up to 36 months following the final disbursement. Recipients must maintain accurate and complete financial records related to the grant for a minimum of 5 years. Any discrepancies or misuse of funds identified during an audit will result in immediate demand for repayment of the full grant amount, plus an administrative penalty of 10%.
(2) Recipients will be given at least 14 days' notice prior to any scheduled site visit or audit.

heading: Repayment of Grants
text:
(1) A grant, or a portion thereof, will become immediately repayable if a recipient fails to comply with any term of the grant agreement, including but not limited to, misuse of funds, failure to meet performance milestones, or providing false information in the application. The Ministry will issue a written demand for repayment, specifying the amount due and the deadline for payment, typically 60 days.
(2) An interest rate of 5% per annum will be applied to overdue repayment amounts, calculated from the date of the repayment demand.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Applicants whose grant applications have been rejected may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the rejection notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Committee of the Ministry of Economic Development, clearly stating the grounds for the appeal and providing any new supporting documentation. The Appeals Committee, comprising senior officials not involved in the initial decision, will review the appeal.
(2) The decision of the Appeals Committee is final and will be communicated within 45 days of receiving the appeal.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information provided by applicants and recipients will be treated with strict confidentiality by the Ministry of Economic Development. This includes business plans, financial statements, and proprietary information. Information will only be disclosed to authorized personnel for the purpose of evaluating applications, administering grants, or for audit purposes, unless otherwise required by law. Aggregated, anonymized data may be used for statistical reporting on the overall impact of the grant program. No personal or business-specific details will be publicly shared without explicit consent.

heading: Publicity
text:
(1) Grant recipients are encouraged to acknowledge the support of the Republic of Nordvale in their promotional materials, websites, and public communications. The Ministry of Economic Development reserves the right to publish the names of grant recipients, the municipality of their operation, and the grant amount awarded, unless a specific request for anonymity is made and approved by the Director of the Entrepreneurial Support Division for compelling reasons.
(2) The Ministry may also request to feature successful businesses in its own publications and promotional activities.

heading: Conflict of Interest
text:
(1) Any Grant Officer or Ministry employee involved in the grant process who has a personal or financial interest in an applicant business must declare this conflict of interest immediately. Such individuals will be recused from all aspects of the evaluation and decision-making process concerning that specific application. Failure to declare a conflict of interest may result in disciplinary action against the employee and, if discovered post-award, revocation of the grant.
(2) Applicants must also declare any direct or indirect relationships with Ministry employees or Grant Officers on their application form.

heading: Amendment of Grant Agreement
text: Any proposed changes to the terms and conditions of a signed grant agreement must be submitted in writing to the Ministry of Economic Development for approval. This includes modifications to the business plan, project scope, or expenditure categories. Amendments will only be considered if they are minor, do not fundamentally alter the original intent of the grant, and are approved in writing by a Grant Officer. Significant changes may require a new application or lead to the termination of the existing agreement. An amendment fee of 250 crowns may apply for approved changes.

heading: Duration of Grant Support
text: The period of financial support under this Act for any single business, whether as a New Business Grant or a Small Business Growth Grant, shall not exceed 36 months from the date of the initial disbursement. A business may only receive one grant under this Act within any 5-year period. Exceptions may be considered for businesses demonstrating exceptional growth and job creation potential, subject to approval by the Director of the Entrepreneurial Support Division and a further detailed review of their updated business plan. The total cumulative grant amount for any single entity over its lifetime must not exceed 250,000 crowns.

heading: Job Creation Targets
text:
(1) New Business Grant recipients are expected to create at least 1 new full-time equivalent job within 12 months of receiving the grant. Small Business Growth Grant recipients are expected to create at least 2 new full-time equivalent jobs within 18 months. These targets will be clearly stipulated in the grant agreement.
(2) Failure to meet these job creation targets without justifiable cause, as determined by the Ministry, may result in a proportional reduction of subsequent grant instalments or a demand for partial repayment of funds already disbursed.

heading: Job Creation Targets
text:
(1) New Business Grant recipients are expected to create at least 2 new full-time equivalent jobs within 12 months of receiving the grant. Small Business Growth Grant recipients are expected to create at least 3 new full-time equivalent jobs within 18 months. These targets will be clearly stipulated in the grant agreement.
(2) Failure to meet these job creation targets without justifiable cause, as determined by the Ministry, may result in a proportional reduction of subsequent grant instalments or a demand for partial repayment of funds already disbursed, with a penalty of 10% of the unfulfilled job creation amount.

heading: Geographic Priority
text:
(1) Businesses establishing or expanding operations in municipalities identified as priority development areas by the Ministry of Economic Development will receive preferential consideration during the evaluation process. Currently, these areas include Dunmere, Grauby, and Elsby. Applicants in these areas may receive up to an additional 10 percentage points on their overall application score. The list of priority areas may be updated annually based on economic indicators and regional needs.
(2) At least 20% of the total annual grant budget will be allocated to businesses within these designated priority municipalities.

heading: Training and Mentorship
text:
(1) All successful grant recipients are required to participate in a minimum of 20 hours of entrepreneurial training workshops offered by the Ministry of Economic Development within the first 6 months of receiving the grant. These workshops cover topics such as financial management, marketing strategies, and human resources. Attendance will be monitored.
(2) Recipients will also be assigned a business mentor for a period of 12 months, with whom they must meet at least once every quarter. The mentorship program aims to provide guidance and support to new and growing businesses.

heading: Training and Mentorship
text:
(1) All successful grant recipients are required to participate in a minimum of 30 hours of entrepreneurial training workshops offered by the Ministry of Economic Development within the first 9 months of receiving the grant. These workshops cover topics such as advanced financial management, digital marketing strategies, and human resources compliance. Attendance will be strictly monitored.
(2) Recipients will also be assigned a business mentor for a period of 18 months, with whom they must meet at least once every two months. The mentorship program aims to provide intensive guidance and strategic support to new and growing businesses.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) For grant applications exceeding 75,000 crowns, a basic environmental impact statement must be submitted, outlining the business's potential environmental footprint and any measures taken to mitigate it. This statement should be no more than 5 pages. Businesses involved in industries with significant environmental risks, such as manufacturing or resource extraction, will be required to submit a more detailed environmental assessment report, prepared by a certified environmental consultant.
(2) Projects demonstrating a positive environmental impact, such as those promoting waste reduction or sustainable practices, may receive additional scoring points.

heading: Innovation Bonus
text:
(1) Businesses demonstrating significant innovation in their products, services, or business models may be eligible for an Innovation Bonus of up to 10% of their awarded grant amount, not exceeding 15,000 crowns. To qualify, applicants must provide a detailed explanation of their innovative aspect and how it differentiates them from competitors, along with any relevant intellectual property filings or research reports.
(2) The Innovation Bonus is subject to the review and recommendation of an independent panel of industry experts.

heading: Local Supplier Preference
text:
(1) Grant recipients are strongly encouraged to prioritize the use of local Nordvalean suppliers and service providers for their operational needs. Businesses committing to sourcing at least 75% of their inputs from within Nordvale will receive a 5% bonus on their grant amount, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns. Proof of local sourcing, such as contracts or invoices, will be required during reporting.
(2) This preference aims to foster a strong local economy and create a ripple effect of economic benefits across the Republic.

heading: Compliance with Labour Laws
text: All grant applicants and recipients must be in full compliance with all Nordvalean labour laws and regulations, including those pertaining to minimum wage, working hours, and workplace safety. Any history of significant labour law violations within the past 3 years will render an applicant ineligible for grants under this Act. The Ministry may request proof of compliance, such as inspection reports or certifications, at any stage of the application or grant period. Non-compliance discovered after a grant has been awarded will result in immediate termination of the grant agreement and demand for full repayment.

heading: Data Collection and Statistics
text: The Ministry of Economic Development will collect and maintain data on all grant applications and recipients for statistical analysis and program evaluation purposes. This data will include information on business sector, size, location, employment figures, and financial performance. Anonymized and aggregated data may be published in annual reports to demonstrate the impact and effectiveness of the Entrepreneurial Support Grants program. Individual business data will not be publicly disclosed unless explicitly permitted under section 19.

heading: Sunset Clause
text: This Act shall cease to be in effect on 2028-12-31, unless extended by a resolution of the Nordvalean Assembly. All grants approved before this date will continue to be administered according to the terms of their respective grant agreements until their completion. New applications will not be accepted after 2028-12-31. The Ministry of Economic Development will conduct a comprehensive review of the Act's impact and efficacy in 2028 to inform any potential extension or reformulation of the program.

heading: Community Engagement Grant
text:
(1) An additional grant, up to 25,000 crowns, is available for businesses that demonstrate a significant commitment to community engagement through local initiatives, sponsorships, or volunteer programs. This grant is supplementary to the main New Business or Small Business Growth Grants. Applicants must submit a detailed proposal outlining their community engagement plan, including projected impact and budget allocation, with at least 50% of the funds directly benefiting community projects within their municipality.
(2) Priority will be given to businesses engaging with communities in Corvik or Fennick.

heading: Community Engagement Grant
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Particular persons
text: For a holder of a meteorological observer badge, the fee or allowance in SBA §18 shall be reduced by half.

heading: Payment terms
text: Where the person liable is a licensed glassblower for at least one year, the fee or allowance in FDA §23 shall be reduced by one half.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the mandatory inspection of electrical systems within all buildings across the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, prevent electrical hazards, and maintain the integrity of electrical infrastructure. The scope of this Act extends to both new constructions and existing buildings, encompassing all types of electrical installations, including wiring, circuit breakers, outlets, and fixed appliances connected to the mains supply. Regular inspections are crucial for identifying potential faults and ensuring compliance with safety standards, thereby protecting occupants and property from electrical fires and other related incidents. All municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, are subject to these regulations.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Building' refers to any permanent structure intended for human habitation or use, including residential homes, commercial premises, industrial facilities, and public buildings.
(2) 'Electrical system' encompasses all components involved in the distribution and utilization of electrical power within a building, from the point of entry to the individual outlets and switches.
(3) 'Qualified inspector' means an individual certified by the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority to conduct electrical inspections according to the standards outlined in this Act.
(4) 'Deficiency' refers to any aspect of an electrical system that does not meet the safety standards specified in this Act, posing a potential risk to occupants or property.

heading: Mandatory Inspections for New Constructions
text: All newly constructed buildings, regardless of their intended use, must undergo a comprehensive electrical system inspection prior to occupancy. This inspection must be completed and approved by a qualified inspector before the building can be connected to the main electrical grid. The builder is responsible for scheduling and facilitating this initial inspection. A certificate of compliance, issued by the inspector, must be prominently displayed within the building for a period of at least five years from the date of issuance. Failure to comply with this section will result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Mandatory Inspections for New Constructions
text: All newly constructed buildings, regardless of their intended use, must undergo a comprehensive electrical system inspection prior to occupancy. This inspection must be completed and approved by a qualified inspector before the building can be connected to the main electrical grid. The builder is responsible for scheduling and facilitating this initial inspection. A certificate of compliance, issued by the inspector, must be prominently displayed within the building for a period of at least ten years from the date of issuance. Failure to comply with this section will result in a penalty of 2,000 crowns, and connection to the grid will be withheld.

heading: Periodic Inspections for Residential Buildings
text: Owners of residential buildings are required to arrange for a periodic electrical system inspection every 10 years. This applies to all dwellings, including single-family homes and multi-unit apartment complexes with fewer than 5 units. The inspection must be carried out by a qualified inspector and a report submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 30 days of the inspection. The cost of the inspection is the responsibility of the building owner, estimated to be around 300-500 crowns. Failure to comply with this section may result in a fine of 500 crowns per year of non-compliance.

heading: Periodic Inspections for Residential Buildings
text: Owners of residential buildings are required to arrange for a periodic electrical system inspection every 8 years. This applies to all dwellings, including single-family homes and multi-unit apartment complexes with fewer than 8 units. The inspection must be carried out by a qualified inspector and a report submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 20 days of the inspection. The cost of the inspection is the responsibility of the building owner, typically ranging from 400-600 crowns. Failure to comply with this section may result in a fine of 750 crowns per year of non-compliance.

heading: Periodic Inspections for Commercial Buildings
text: Commercial buildings, including shops, offices, and restaurants, must undergo a periodic electrical system inspection every 5 years. This applies to all commercial premises, regardless of their square footage, and covers all areas accessible to the public and staff. The inspection report must be submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 21 days of the inspection date. Owners must retain proof of inspection for a minimum of 7 years. Failure to adhere to this schedule will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns for each missed inspection period.

heading: Periodic Inspections for Commercial Buildings
text: Commercial buildings, including shops, offices, and restaurants, must undergo a periodic electrical system inspection every 4 years. This applies to all commercial premises exceeding 50 square meters, and covers all areas accessible to the public and staff. The inspection report must be submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 14 days of the inspection date. Owners must retain proof of inspection for a minimum of 10 years. Failure to adhere to this schedule will result in a penalty of 1,250 crowns for each missed inspection period.

heading: Periodic Inspections for Industrial Buildings
text: Industrial buildings, such as factories and warehouses, require more frequent electrical system inspections due to higher power demands and specialized equipment. These inspections must be conducted every 3 years. The scope of these inspections is particularly rigorous, focusing on heavy machinery connections, high-voltage systems, and specialized grounding requirements. A detailed report must be submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 15 days, highlighting any areas of concern. Failure to comply with this section carries a penalty of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Inspection of Public Buildings
text: Public buildings, including schools, hospitals, and government offices, shall have their electrical systems inspected every 2 years. Given the high occupancy and critical services provided, these inspections are of paramount importance. Special attention must be paid to emergency lighting, fire alarm systems, and backup power generators. The municipality responsible for the building, such as Dunmere or Elsby, must ensure these inspections are carried out promptly and all deficiencies are rectified within 60 days of the inspection report. A public safety certificate must be displayed at all main entrances.

heading: Emergency Inspections
text: In the event of an electrical fire, power surge, or any other significant electrical incident, an emergency inspection is mandatory within 48 hours of the event. The building owner or responsible party must immediately notify the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority. A qualified inspector will assess the damage, determine the cause, and provide recommendations for repair and remediation. No electrical system can be re-energized until an emergency inspection certificate is issued, verifying that all necessary repairs have been completed and the system is safe. Failure to report an incident promptly may incur a penalty of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Qualifications of Inspectors
text:
(1) Only individuals holding a valid certification from the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority are authorized to conduct inspections under this Act. To qualify, an inspector must possess at least 5 years of practical experience in electrical engineering or a related field, and pass a comprehensive examination demonstrating their knowledge of Nordvale's electrical codes and safety standards.
(2) Certification must be renewed every 3 years, requiring proof of ongoing professional development and a clean record of inspection practices. Inspectors are prohibited from inspecting buildings in which they have a financial interest or were involved in the original electrical installation.

heading: Inspector Responsibilities
text: Qualified inspectors are responsible for conducting thorough and impartial assessments of electrical systems. This includes visually inspecting wiring, checking circuit breaker functionality, testing outlets for proper grounding, and verifying compliance with all relevant safety codes. They must provide a detailed written report outlining any deficiencies found, along with recommendations for corrective actions. Inspectors must maintain meticulous records of all inspections performed for a minimum of 15 years. Any inspector found to be negligent or dishonest in their duties may face immediate revocation of their certification and a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Deficiencies
text:
(1) If an inspection reveals deficiencies, the qualified inspector must provide a detailed report to the building owner within 7 days of the inspection.
(2) The report must clearly categorize deficiencies as either 'minor' or 'major'. Minor deficiencies, such as loose outlet covers, must be rectified within 90 days. Major deficiencies, including exposed wiring or overloaded circuits, require immediate attention and must be rectified within 30 days.
(3) The report must also be submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 10 days of the inspection.

heading: Reporting Deficiencies
text:
(1) If an inspection reveals deficiencies, the qualified inspector must provide a detailed report to the building owner within 5 days of the inspection.
(2) The report must clearly categorize deficiencies as either 'minor', 'moderate', or 'major'. Minor deficiencies, such as missing switch plates, must be rectified within 60 days. Moderate deficiencies, like improper wire insulation, must be rectified within 30 days. Major deficiencies, including immediate fire risks, require rectification within 14 days.
(3) The report must also be submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 7 days of the inspection.

heading: Reporting Deficiencies
text:
(1) If an inspection reveals deficiencies, the qualified inspector must provide a detailed report to the building owner within 3 days of the inspection.
(2) The report must clearly categorize deficiencies as either 'minor', 'moderate', or 'critical'. Minor deficiencies, such as non-functional light switches, must be rectified within 45 days. Moderate deficiencies, like insufficient circuit protection, must be rectified within 21 days. Critical deficiencies, such as active electrical arcing, require immediate isolation of the affected circuit and rectification within 7 days.
(3) The report must also be submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 5 days of the inspection.

heading: Rectification of Deficiencies
text: Building owners are responsible for ensuring that all identified electrical deficiencies are rectified by a licensed electrician within the prescribed timeframes as specified in section 11. Upon completion of repairs, a licensed electrician must provide a certificate of completion to the building owner. This certificate must detail the repairs undertaken and confirm that the electrical system now meets all safety standards. A follow-up inspection by a qualified inspector may be required for major deficiencies, at the owner's expense. Failure to rectify deficiencies within the given period will result in a fine of 750 crowns per week of non-compliance after the initial deadline.

heading: Rectification of Deficiencies
text: Building owners are responsible for ensuring that all identified electrical deficiencies are rectified by a licensed electrician within the prescribed timeframes as specified in section 11. Upon completion of repairs, a licensed electrician must provide a certificate of completion to the building owner within 5 days of work completion. This certificate must detail the repairs undertaken and confirm that the electrical system now meets all safety standards. A follow-up inspection by a qualified inspector is mandatory for all major or critical deficiencies, at the owner's expense. Failure to rectify deficiencies within the given period will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per week of non-compliance after the initial deadline.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Building owners who disagree with an inspection report or a rectification order may file an appeal with the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 14 days of receiving the report.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the specific points of contention and providing supporting evidence. An independent review panel, comprising three senior qualified inspectors not involved in the original inspection, will review the appeal.
(3) The panel's decision will be final and communicated to the appellant within 30 days of the appeal submission. A non-refundable processing fee of 200 crowns applies to all appeals.

heading: Access for Inspections
text:
(1) Building owners and occupants must provide qualified inspectors with reasonable access to all parts of the electrical system during scheduled inspections. This includes access to electrical panels, utility rooms, and areas where wiring is installed.
(2) Inspectors must provide at least 72 hours' notice before conducting a scheduled inspection, except in cases of emergency inspections as described in section 8. In emergency situations, immediate access must be granted upon presentation of proper identification.
(3) Obstruction of an inspection, without reasonable cause, may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns and a mandatory rescheduling of the inspection within 7 days.

heading: Certification of Compliance
text:
(1) Upon successful completion of an inspection and rectification of any identified deficiencies, a qualified inspector shall issue a Certificate of Electrical Compliance.
(2) This certificate confirms that the electrical system meets all current safety standards set forth in this Act. The certificate must be displayed in a visible location within the building, such as near the main electrical panel or a prominent entrance, for the duration of its validity.
(3) Copies of all certificates must be submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority within 5 days of issuance and kept on file for at least 15 years.

heading: Certification of Compliance
text:
(1) Upon successful completion of an inspection and rectification of any identified deficiencies, a qualified inspector shall issue a Digital Certificate of Electrical Compliance.
(2) This certificate confirms that the electrical system meets all current safety standards set forth in this Act. The certificate's unique identification code must be displayed in a visible location within the building, such as near the main electrical panel or a prominent entrance, for the duration of its validity.
(3) All certificates are automatically submitted to the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority immediately upon issuance and kept on file indefinitely.

heading: Record Keeping by Owners
text: Building owners are required to maintain a comprehensive record of all electrical inspections, deficiency reports, and rectification certificates for their property. These records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years and be made available upon request by the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority or a qualified inspector. Accurate record-keeping facilitates tracking of electrical system health and ensures historical compliance. Failure to produce these records when requested may result in a fine of 400 crowns for each missing document.

heading: Record Keeping by Owners
text: Building owners are required to maintain a comprehensive record of all electrical inspections, deficiency reports, and rectification certificates for their property. These records must be kept for a minimum of 15 years and be made available upon request by the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority or a qualified inspector. For buildings over 50 years old, records must extend back 20 years. Failure to produce these records when requested may result in a fine of 600 crowns for each missing document, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalties for Owners
text: Any building owner failing to comply with the mandatory inspection schedules outlined in sections 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7 will be subject to a penalty of 1,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses within a 5-year period will incur a penalty of 2,500 crowns. Additionally, the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority may issue a compulsory inspection order, with all associated costs borne by the owner. Persistent non-compliance may lead to restrictions on building occupancy or denial of electrical supply, especially in municipalities like Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalties for Owners
text: Any building owner failing to comply with the mandatory inspection schedules outlined in sections 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7 will be subject to a penalty of 1,200 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses within a 3-year period will incur a penalty of 3,000 crowns. Additionally, the Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority will issue a compulsory inspection order, with all associated costs borne by the owner. Persistent non-compliance for more than 180 days may lead to restrictions on building occupancy or denial of electrical supply, especially in municipalities like Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Penalties for False Statements
text: Any person who knowingly makes a false or misleading statement in an inspection report, rectification certificate, or any other document required by this Act shall be liable to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns. In cases where such a false statement results in an electrical hazard, injury, or property damage, further legal action, including criminal charges, may be pursued. Qualified inspectors or licensed electricians found to be involved in making false statements will face immediate revocation of their licenses and a permanent ban from conducting work under this Act.

heading: Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority
text: The Nordvale Electrical Safety Authority (NESA) is established as the primary regulatory body responsible for overseeing the implementation and enforcement of this Act. NESA is tasked with developing and updating electrical safety standards, certifying qualified inspectors, maintaining a central database of inspection records, and investigating serious electrical incidents. NESA operates with an annual budget of 15 million crowns and employs a staff of 75 dedicated professionals. Its headquarters are located in Aldmark, the capital city.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: NESA shall regularly conduct public awareness campaigns to educate building owners and the general public about the importance of electrical safety and their responsibilities under this Act. These campaigns will utilize various media channels, including print, radio, and online platforms. Educational materials will be distributed in all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby, emphasizing the risks of faulty electrical systems and the benefits of regular inspections. A minimum of 5% of NESA's annual budget is allocated to these public outreach efforts.

heading: Review of Standards
text:
(1) The electrical safety standards detailed in this Act shall be reviewed and updated by NESA at least once every 5 years.
(2) This review process will involve consultation with industry experts, licensed electricians, qualified inspectors, and representatives from relevant government departments. The aim is to ensure that Nordvale's electrical safety standards remain current with technological advancements and best practices in electrical engineering.
(3) Any proposed changes to the standards will be subject to a 90-day public comment period before final adoption.

heading: Review of Standards
text:
(1) The electrical safety standards detailed in this Act shall be reviewed and updated by NESA at least once every 3 years.
(2) This review process will involve consultation with industry experts, licensed electricians, qualified inspectors, and representatives from relevant government departments. The aim is to ensure that Nordvale's electrical safety standards remain current with technological advancements and best practices in electrical engineering, especially concerning renewable energy integration.
(3) Any proposed changes to the standards will be subject to a 60-day public comment period before final adoption.

heading: Data Privacy
text: All data collected during electrical inspections, including personal information of building owners and details of electrical systems, shall be treated with strict confidentiality. NESA is mandated to protect this information in accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations. Data will only be used for the purposes of enforcing this Act, ensuring public safety, and statistical analysis. No personal data will be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by a court order. Data retention periods for non-compliance records are 20 years.

heading: Special Provisions for Historical Buildings
text:
(1) Buildings designated as historical landmarks, particularly those over 75 years old, may be subject to specialized inspection protocols. These protocols acknowledge the challenges of upgrading older electrical systems while preserving historical integrity.
(2) NESA, in consultation with the Nordvale Heritage Council, will develop specific guidelines for inspecting and, where necessary, upgrading electrical systems in these buildings.
(3) Owners of historical buildings may apply for exemptions from certain modern code requirements if strict adherence would compromise the building's historical value, provided an equivalent level of safety can be demonstrated. Such exemptions are reviewed every 5 years.

heading: Special Provisions for Historical Buildings
text:
(1) Buildings designated as historical landmarks, particularly those over 100 years old, are subject to specialized inspection protocols. These protocols acknowledge the challenges of upgrading older electrical systems while preserving historical integrity.
(2) NESA, in consultation with the Nordvale Heritage Council, will develop specific guidelines for inspecting and, where necessary, upgrading electrical systems in these buildings. A specialist historical electrical inspector is required for these properties.
(3) Owners of historical buildings may apply for exemptions from certain modern code requirements if strict adherence would compromise the building's historical value, provided an equivalent level of safety can be demonstrated and approved by NESA. Such exemptions are reviewed every 3 years and require a full safety report.

heading: Temporary Occupancy Permits
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, NESA may issue a temporary occupancy permit for a building before the final electrical inspection is completed.
(2) This permit will only be granted if a preliminary inspection confirms that the essential electrical systems are safe for limited use and there are no immediate hazards. Such permits are typically valid for a maximum of 30 days and are subject to strict conditions.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required, and the building owner must provide a detailed plan for completing the final inspection within the permit period. Only up to 10% of the building's floor area may be occupied under such a permit.

heading: Cost of Inspections
text:
(1) Unless otherwise specified, the cost of all mandatory electrical inspections, including initial and periodic inspections, is the sole responsibility of the building owner.
(2) Qualified inspectors are permitted to charge reasonable fees for their services, which typically range from 300 crowns for a small residential property to 2,000 crowns for a large industrial facility. NESA does not regulate specific pricing but encourages transparency.
(3) Owners can seek quotes from multiple certified inspectors. For low-income households, NESA may offer a subsidy of up to 25% of the inspection cost, provided their income is below 30,000 crowns per annum.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Minor detached structures, such as sheds or garages under 10 square meters, that do not contain living spaces and are not connected to the main electrical system, are exempt from periodic inspections.
(2) Buildings with electrical systems operating solely on low voltage (under 50 volts) and completely isolated from the main grid, such as certain off-grid solar installations, may also be exempt, subject to NESA approval.
(3) These exemptions do not apply if the structure presents a clear and present danger as determined by a local authority. All other buildings, including those in Lund Vale, must comply.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Minor detached structures, such as sheds or garages under 15 square meters, that do not contain living spaces and are not connected to the main electrical system, are exempt from periodic inspections.
(2) Buildings with electrical systems operating solely on low voltage (under 60 volts) and completely isolated from the main grid, such as certain off-grid solar installations, may also be exempt, subject to NESA approval via a 30-day application process.
(3) These exemptions do not apply if the structure presents a clear and present danger as determined by a local authority, or if it is located within 5 meters of another building. All other buildings, including those in Lund Vale, must comply.

heading: Review of Appeals Panel Decisions
text:
(1) Decisions made by the independent review panel as per subsection (2) of section 13 may be subject to a final review by the Director of NESA.
(2) This final review can only be requested in cases where there is new, substantial evidence not presented during the initial appeal, or if there is a clear procedural error that significantly impacted the panel's decision. The request for review must be submitted within 7 days of receiving the panel's decision.
(3) The Director's decision in such matters is binding and final. A fee of 750 crowns applies to this final review request.

heading: Review of Appeals Panel Decisions
text:
(1) Decisions made by the independent review panel as per subsection (2) of section 13 may be subject to a final review by the Director of NESA.
(2) This final review can only be requested in cases where there is new, substantial evidence not presented during the initial appeal, or if there is a clear procedural error that significantly impacted the panel's decision. The request for review must be submitted within 10 days of receiving the panel's decision.
(3) The Director's decision in such matters is binding and final. A fee of 900 crowns applies to this final review request.

heading: Review of Appeals Panel Decisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Power of Entry
text:
(1) A qualified inspector, accompanied by a municipal official from areas such as Corvik or Dunmere, may enter any building without prior notice if there are reasonable grounds to believe that an immediate electrical hazard exists, posing a significant threat to life or property.
(2) Before entry, the inspector must present their official identification and state the purpose of their entry. Forceable entry is only permissible with a warrant issued by a magistrate.
(3) Any evidence collected during such an entry can be used in proceedings under this Act. The inspector must provide a written report of their findings to the building owner within 24 hours of entry, detailing the hazard and any actions taken.

heading: Cooperation with Emergency Services
text: NESA and qualified inspectors shall cooperate fully with emergency services, including fire departments and municipal disaster response teams, during and after electrical incidents. This cooperation includes sharing relevant inspection reports, providing expert advice on electrical safety, and assisting in investigations to determine the cause of electrical fires or failures. Training exercises will be conducted semi-annually with emergency responders to enhance coordination and improve response times for electrical emergencies across all municipalities.

heading: Training Requirements for Electricians
text: All licensed electricians performing work on electrical systems in Nordvale must complete mandatory continuing education courses every 2 years. These courses, approved by NESA, cover updates to the electrical code, new technologies, and best safety practices. A minimum of 16 hours of training is required for each 2-year cycle. Failure to meet these training requirements will result in the suspension of an electrician's license until compliance is achieved. NESA maintains a public register of all licensed electricians and their training status.

heading: Annual Statistical Report
text: NESA shall publish an annual statistical report by March 31st of each year, detailing the number of inspections conducted, the types and frequency of deficiencies found, and the overall electrical safety trends in Nordvale. This report will also include an analysis of electrical incidents, including their causes and consequences. The report will be made publicly available on the NESA website and submitted to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure. This helps in identifying areas for improvement and allocating resources effectively, for example, identifying problematic areas in Brenholt.

heading: Amendments to Electrical Code
text:
(1) Any amendments to the Nordvale Electrical Code, which forms the basis for inspections under this Act, must be proposed by NESA and approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure.
(2) Such amendments typically follow a consultative process, as outlined in section 21, ensuring input from all stakeholders. Major amendments are usually enacted every 5 years, while minor updates can occur annually.
(3) All changes to the code will be published at least 180 days before their effective date to allow for proper implementation and training. Ignorance of updated codes is not considered a valid defense against non-compliance.

heading: Special categories
text: Each registered cartographer pays a fixed five crowns for each dog licence fee.

heading: Particular persons
text: No speed limit on motorways is payable by any licensed taxidermist; instead, such a person is liable for half of the prevailing speed limit.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates public events and public assemblies held in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to keep attendees safe and to limit nuisance to neighbours.
(3) It does not apply to private gatherings in a home or to religious services.
(4) It does not apply to cultural events, which are governed by the Cultural Events Act.

heading: Notice of a public event
text:
(1) The organiser of a public event expected to have more than 200 attendees shall notify the municipality at least 14 days before the event.
(2) The notice shall state the place, the date, the hours and the expected number of attendees.

heading: Notice of a public event
text:
(1) The organiser of a public event expected to have more than 200 attendees shall notify the municipality at least 21 days before the event.
(2) The notice shall state the place, the date, the hours and the expected number of attendees.

heading: Permit fee for a medium event
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with 201 to 500 attendees shall pay a permit fee of 80 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the notice under section 2 is submitted.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the event is cancelled less than 7 days before it starts.
(4) No fee is payable under this section for an event held in a street, square or park, for which the fee under FDA §36 is payable instead.

heading: Permit fee for a large event
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with 501 to 5,000 attendees shall pay a permit fee of 300 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the notice under section 2 is submitted.
(3) An event with more than 5,000 attendees needs a special permit from the national authority.
(4) No fee is payable under this section for an event held in a street, square or park, for which the fee under FDA §36 is payable instead.

heading: Stewards
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 200 attendees shall provide stewards.
(2) There shall be at least 1 steward for every 100 attendees expected.
(3) A steward shall wear a visible vest and shall be at least 18 years of age.

heading: Daytime noise
text:
(1) Sound from an event shall not exceed 85 decibels measured at the boundary of the event site.
(2) This limit applies between 08:00 and 22:00.
(3) The organiser shall have a person responsible for measuring the sound level during the event.

heading: Night noise
text:
(1) Sound from an event shall not exceed 55 decibels measured at the boundary of the event site between 22:00 and 08:00.
(2) An event that cannot meet this limit shall end at 22:00.
(3) The municipality may fix a lower limit for a particular site.

heading: Night noise
text:
(1) Sound from an event shall not exceed 60 decibels measured at the boundary of the event site between 22:00 and 08:00.
(2) An event that cannot meet this limit shall end at 22:00.
(3) The municipality may fix a lower limit for a particular site.

heading: Notice of an assembly
text:
(1) The organiser of a public assembly shall notify the police at least 48 hours before the assembly starts.
(2) The notice shall state the place, the time and the expected number of participants.
(3) The police may not refuse an assembly because of the opinions expressed.

heading: Notice of an assembly
text:
(1) The organiser of a public assembly shall notify the police at least 72 hours before the assembly starts.
(2) The notice shall state the place, the time and the expected number of participants.
(3) The police may not refuse an assembly because of the opinions expressed.

heading: Processions
text:
(1) The organiser of a procession shall state the route in the notice.
(2) The police shall consult the municipality about the route and may propose changes.
(3) A procession shall not block an emergency route for more than 30 minutes.

heading: Maximum duration
text:
(1) A public event shall not last longer than 12 hours in one day.
(2) A festival of several days shall have a break of at least 8 hours between days.
(3) The organiser shall state the hours in the notice.

heading: First aid
text:
(1) An event with more than 1,000 attendees shall have one first-aid post for every 1,000 attendees.
(2) Each post shall be staffed by at least 2 persons with a first-aid certificate.
(3) The first-aid posts shall be marked on the site plan.

heading: Fireworks
text:
(1) Fireworks at an event need a separate permit.
(2) The organiser shall apply at least 30 days before the event.
(3) Fireworks shall not be fired after 23:00 except on the last night of the year.

heading: Temporary structures
text:
(1) A temporary structure such as a stage or a tent shall not be higher than 6 metres without an engineer's approval.
(2) The engineer's approval shall be shown to an inspector on request.
(3) A structure shall be taken down within 48 hours after the event ends.

heading: Insurance
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 500 attendees shall hold insurance covering damage to attendees and third parties of at least 50000 crowns.
(2) The organiser shall show the insurance certificate on request.
(3) An event without the insurance shall not start.

heading: Insurance
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 500 attendees shall hold insurance covering damage to attendees and third parties of at least 75000 crowns.
(2) The organiser shall show the insurance certificate on request.
(3) An event without the insurance shall not start.

heading: Cancellation refund
text:
(1) An organiser who cancels an event at least 7 days before it starts is entitled to a refund of 50 percent of the permit fee.
(2) The organiser shall apply for the refund within 30 days of the cancellation.
(3) No refund is paid for an event cancelled later than the period in subsection (1).

heading: Capacity
text:
(1) The number of attendees shall not exceed 1 person for each 1.5 square metres of floor space in an enclosed venue.
(2) The organiser shall display the maximum capacity at every entrance.
(3) The organiser shall stop admission when the maximum capacity is reached.

heading: Waste
text:
(1) The organiser shall clear all waste from the event site within 24 hours after the event ends.
(2) The organiser shall provide at least 1 waste container for every 50 attendees.
(3) The municipality may clear the site at the organiser's cost if the organiser fails to do so.

heading: Fine for holding an event without notice
text:
(1) An organiser who holds an event without the notice required by section 2 shall pay a fine of 600 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) The police may stop an event held without notice.

heading: Fine for holding an event without notice
text:
(1) An organiser who holds an event without the notice required by section 2 shall pay a fine of 800 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) The police may stop an event held without notice.

heading: Curfew on holy days
text:
(1) No public event shall be held between 22:00 and 06:00 on a national holy day.
(2) The municipality may allow an exception for an event of fewer than 300 attendees.

heading: Curfew on holy days
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Lost children
text:
(1) The organiser of an event with more than 1,000 attendees shall set up a meeting point for lost children.
(2) The meeting point shall be staffed throughout the event by at least 2 adults.
(3) The organiser shall announce the meeting point at the start of the event and every 2 hours after that.

heading: Night bus fares for night workers
text:
(1) Notwithstanding PTA §17(1), a night worker who travels on a night service with a single ticket pays no extra charge.
(2) The night worker shows the employer's written confirmation of night work when asked by a ticket inspector.

heading: Summer street licence for growers
text: A smallholder who sells produce from the smallholder's own farmland on the street pays 20 crowns per month for the monthly licence under STA §3 for the months of June, July, August and September.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating and licensing trade exhibitions, fairs, and similar public events within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, maintain order, and protect consumers and participants. The provisions herein apply to all events where goods or services are displayed or offered for commercial purposes to a public audience, regardless of whether an entry fee is charged. The Act defines the responsibilities of organizers, sets forth application procedures, and outlines penalties for non-compliance, aiming to foster a fair and secure environment for such activities across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Exhibition' means any organized public display or presentation of goods, services, or information for commercial purposes, lasting more than 4 hours.
(b) 'Organizer' means any individual, corporation, or association responsible for planning, promoting, and executing an exhibition.
(c) 'Licensing Authority' refers to the Municipal Council of the municipality where the exhibition is to be held.
(d) 'Public' includes any person not directly involved in the organization or operation of the exhibition.
(e) 'Premises' means the specific location, indoor or outdoor, where an exhibition takes place, covering an area greater than 50 square meters.

heading: Requirement for a Licence
text:
(1) No person shall organize, promote, or conduct an exhibition within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Exhibition Licence from the relevant Licensing Authority.
(2) A separate licence is required for each individual exhibition, even if organized by the same entity or held at the same venue at different times.
(3) Any exhibition expected to attract more than 100 attendees or occupying an area greater than 150 square meters must obtain a licence. Events attracting fewer than 50 attendees are exempt from this requirement.

heading: Requirement for a Licence
text:
(1) No person shall organize, promote, or conduct an exhibition within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Exhibition Licence from the relevant Licensing Authority.
(2) A separate licence is required for each individual exhibition, even if organized by the same entity or held at the same venue at different times.
(3) Any exhibition expected to attract more than 75 attendees or occupying an area greater than 100 square meters must obtain a licence. Events attracting fewer than 40 attendees are exempt from this requirement.

heading: Requirement for a Licence
text:
(1) No person shall organize, promote, or conduct an exhibition within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Exhibition Licence from the relevant Licensing Authority.
(2) A separate licence is required for each individual exhibition, even if organized by the same entity or held at the same venue at different times.
(3) Any exhibition expected to attract more than 50 attendees or occupying an area greater than 75 square meters must obtain a licence. Events attracting fewer than 25 attendees are exempt from this requirement.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for an Exhibition Licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 90 days prior to the proposed start date of the exhibition.
(2) The application must be made on the prescribed form and accompanied by all required documentation, including a detailed event plan, safety protocols, and a site map. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission.
(3) In exceptional circumstances, the Licensing Authority may consider an application submitted less than 60 days in advance, subject to an additional late application fee of 750 crowns.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for an Exhibition Licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 120 days prior to the proposed start date of the exhibition.
(2) The application must be made on the prescribed form and accompanied by all required documentation, including a detailed event plan, safety protocols, and a site map. A non-refundable application fee of 600 crowns is required at the time of submission.
(3) In exceptional circumstances, the Licensing Authority may consider an application submitted less than 90 days in advance, subject to an additional late application fee of 1000 crowns.

heading: Content of Application
text:
The application for an Exhibition Licence shall include, but not be limited to, the following information:
(a) The full name and contact details of the organizer, including an emergency contact available 24 hours a day.
(b) The proposed dates and times of the exhibition, not exceeding 14 consecutive days.
(c) The exact location of the exhibition, including postal address and precise geographical coordinates if outdoors.
(d) A detailed description of the type of exhibition and the estimated number of exhibitors (minimum 5, maximum 200).
(e) An estimate of the maximum number of attendees expected at any one time, not to exceed 5000.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) Every organizer of an exhibition must hold valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns for any single incident.
(2) Proof of such insurance must be submitted with the licence application. The policy must cover the entire duration of the exhibition, including set-up and dismantling periods, which may extend up to 3 days before and 2 days after the event. Failure to provide adequate proof of insurance will result in the rejection of the application.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) Every organizer of an exhibition must hold valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 7,500,000 crowns for any single incident.
(2) Proof of such insurance must be submitted with the licence application. The policy must cover the entire duration of the exhibition, including set-up and dismantling periods, which may extend up to 4 days before and 3 days after the event. Failure to provide adequate proof of insurance will result in the rejection of the application.

heading: Safety Plan
text:
(1) A comprehensive safety plan must be submitted with every application for an Exhibition Licence. This plan must detail measures for fire safety, emergency evacuation procedures, first aid provisions, and crowd management.
(2) The plan must include the location of all emergency exits, fire extinguishers (one every 50 square meters), and first aid stations (at least one per 1000 attendees). It must also identify at least 5 designated safety personnel for every 1000 attendees. The plan will be reviewed by the municipal safety department.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text:
(1) Organizers must submit an environmental impact statement detailing plans for waste management, noise control, and conservation of local resources.
(2) The plan must include provisions for recycling at least 75% of all waste generated and measures to keep noise levels below 60 decibels at the nearest residential boundary after 22:00. Use of single-use plastics should be minimized, aiming for a reduction of at least 25% compared to previous similar events. A refundable environmental deposit of 2000 crowns is required.

heading: Approval Process
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Licensing Authority shall review all submitted documents within 45 days.
(2) The Authority may consult with relevant municipal departments, including fire services, health services, and planning departments. A decision to approve or deny the licence will be communicated to the organizer within 60 days of application submission. In 15% of cases, additional information may be requested, extending the review period by up to 30 days.

heading: Granting of Licence
text:
(1) An Exhibition Licence, if granted, will specify the permitted dates, times, location, and any special conditions deemed necessary by the Licensing Authority.
(2) The licence is valid only for the specific exhibition and dates for which it was issued and is not transferable. The licence document must be displayed prominently at the main entrance of the exhibition at all times. A maximum of 3 special conditions may be attached to any licence.

heading: Refusal of Licence
text:
The Licensing Authority may refuse to grant an Exhibition Licence if:
(a) The application is incomplete or contains false information.
(b) The proposed exhibition poses a significant risk to public safety or order.
(c) The organizer has a history of non-compliance with this Act or other relevant regulations within the past 3 years.
(d) The proposed location is unsuitable for the scale or nature of the exhibition, as determined by a 75% majority vote of the municipal council.
(e) The required fees or deposits have not been paid.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An organizer whose application for an Exhibition Licence has been refused may appeal the decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving notification of refusal.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 1000 crowns. The Municipal Appeals Board shall hear the appeal within 45 days and issue a decision within 15 days of the hearing. Only 1 appeal per refusal is permitted.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee mentioned in section 4, a licence fee is payable upon the granting of the licence.
(2) The licence fee is calculated based on the estimated number of attendees and the duration of the exhibition. For events up to 3 days, the fee is 1000 crowns plus 5 crowns per estimated attendee.
