For events longer than 3 days, an additional 500 crowns per day is charged. Events in Lund Vale receive a 10% discount due to remote location.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee mentioned in section 4, a licence fee is payable upon the granting of the licence.
(2) The licence fee is calculated based on the estimated number of attendees and the duration of the exhibition. For events up to 5 days, the fee is 1200 crowns plus 6 crowns per estimated attendee. For events longer than 5 days, an additional 600 crowns per day is charged. Events in Lund Vale receive a 15% discount due to remote location.

heading: Conditions of Licence
text:
(1) Every Exhibition Licence is granted subject to the general conditions outlined in this Act and any specific conditions imposed by the Licensing Authority.
(2) General conditions include maintaining public order, ensuring adequate sanitation facilities (one toilet per 50 attendees), adherence to advertised hours, and compliance with all applicable health and safety regulations. The organizer must ensure at least 2 security personnel are present for every 500 attendees during operational hours. All conditions must be strictly adhered to.

heading: Changes to Exhibition Plan
text:
(1) Any significant change to an approved exhibition plan, including changes to dates, location, or expected attendance by more than 10%, must be reported to the Licensing Authority at least 21 days prior to the change taking effect.
(2) The Licensing Authority reserves the right to approve or deny such changes, or to impose new conditions. Failure to report significant changes may result in the revocation of the licence and a penalty of up to 3000 crowns.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) Authorized officers of the Licensing Authority, including municipal inspectors and law enforcement personnel, may enter and inspect any exhibition premises at any reasonable time to ensure compliance with the terms of the licence and the provisions of this Act.
(2) Organizers must cooperate fully with all inspections and provide access to all relevant areas and documentation. At least 2 random inspections will be conducted during any exhibition lasting more than 3 days.

heading: Revocation or Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) An Exhibition Licence may be revoked or suspended by the Licensing Authority if the organizer fails to comply with any condition of the licence, any provision of this Act, or if the exhibition poses an immediate threat to public safety.
(2) Before revocation or suspension, the organizer shall be given written notice of the intent to revoke or suspend, stating the reasons, and provided an opportunity to rectify the breach within 24 hours, unless the threat is immediate. At least 3 documented breaches are typically required before revocation for minor infringements.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Exhibitions
text:
(1) Any person who organizes, promotes, or conducts an exhibition without a valid Exhibition Licence commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such person is liable to a fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns for a first offence. For subsequent offences within a 2-year period, the fine may increase to 25,000 crowns, and may include a prohibition on organizing exhibitions for up to 5 years. Each day an unlicensed exhibition operates constitutes a separate offence.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Exhibitions
text:
(1) Any person who organizes, promotes, or conducts an exhibition without a valid Exhibition Licence commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such person is liable to a fine not exceeding 15,000 crowns for a first offence. For subsequent offences within a 3-year period, the fine may increase to 35,000 crowns, and may include a prohibition on organizing exhibitions for up to 7 years. Each day an unlicensed exhibition operates constitutes a separate offence.

heading: Penalties for Breach of Licence Conditions
text:
(1) Any organizer who breaches a condition of their Exhibition Licence commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such person is liable to a fine not exceeding 5,000 crowns for each breach. Persistent or severe breaches may also lead to the suspension or revocation of the licence, as outlined in section 17. The Licensing Authority may also impose a mandatory training requirement for the organizer, lasting 3 full days.

heading: Public Nuisance
text:
(1) Organizers must ensure that their exhibition does not cause undue public nuisance, including excessive noise, traffic congestion, or accumulation of litter outside the designated premises.
(2) Any complaints received from the public regarding nuisance must be addressed promptly, typically within 2 hours of notification. Failure to mitigate identified nuisances within 4 hours may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns per incident. Repeat offenders may face an additional 5,000 crown fine for each subsequent substantiated complaint.

heading: First Aid Provisions
text:
(1) Every exhibition must have adequate first aid facilities and personnel readily available throughout its operating hours.
(2) For events with up to 500 attendees, at least one trained first aid responder and a designated first aid point are required. For every additional 500 attendees, an additional responder and basic first aid kit must be provided. All first aid personnel must hold a valid certification issued within the last 2 years. A minimum of 1 stretcher must be available for every 2000 attendees.

heading: Fire Safety
text:
(1) All exhibition premises must comply with municipal fire safety regulations, including clear access to emergency exits and the proper placement of fire suppression equipment.
(2) Fire exits must be clearly marked, unobstructed, and at least 2 meters wide. Fire extinguishers must be serviced annually and readily accessible within a 20-meter radius of any point within the exhibition area. A fire safety officer, trained and certified within the last 12 months, must be present during all operating hours. Automatic fire alarms must be tested weekly.

heading: Waste Management
text:
(1) Organizers are responsible for the efficient and environmentally sound management of all waste generated during the exhibition.
(2) Sufficient waste receptacles, clearly marked for general waste and recycling, must be provided (at least one pair per 50 square meters). Waste must be removed daily, and the premises left in a clean state within 24 hours of the exhibition's conclusion. A final inspection will be conducted, and 10% of the environmental deposit may be withheld for inadequate cleanup.

heading: Security Personnel
text:
(1) Exhibitions expected to attract more than 200 attendees must employ sufficient security personnel to ensure public order and safety.
(2) A minimum ratio of one security personnel for every 250 attendees is required during peak hours. All security personnel must be over 18 years of age, clearly identifiable, and possess valid security training certification. For events with over 1000 attendees, at least one security supervisor must be present. Security plans must be approved by the local police department 30 days prior to the event.

heading: Food and Beverage Vendors
text:
(1) All food and beverage vendors operating within an exhibition must possess valid health permits from the Municipal Health Department.
(2) Organizers are responsible for ensuring that all vendors comply with food safety standards, including proper food handling, storage, and waste disposal. At least 2 health inspections will be conducted during any exhibition lasting more than 5 days. Vendors found in violation may be immediately removed from the premises and fined up to 1500 crowns per offence. No vendor may operate without displaying their permit.

heading: Hours of Operation
text:
(1) The permitted hours of operation for exhibitions shall be specified on the Exhibition Licence.
(2) Generally, exhibitions are permitted to operate between 08:00 and 22:00 on weekdays, and between 09:00 and 20:00 on weekends. Any deviation from these hours requires special approval from the Licensing Authority, requested at least 14 days in advance, and may incur an additional fee of 300 crowns per extra hour. Exhibitions in residential zones have stricter closing times of 21:00 on weekdays.

heading: Hours of Operation
text:
(1) The permitted hours of operation for exhibitions shall be specified on the Exhibition Licence.
(2) Generally, exhibitions are permitted to operate between 07:00 and 21:00 on weekdays, and between 08:00 and 19:00 on weekends. Any deviation from these hours requires special approval from the Licensing Authority, requested at least 21 days in advance, and may incur an additional fee of 400 crowns per extra hour. Exhibitions in residential zones have stricter closing times of 20:00 on weekdays.

heading: Access for Persons with Reduced Mobility
text:
(1) All exhibition premises must be accessible to persons with reduced mobility.
(2) This includes providing ramps where necessary, ensuring clear pathways at least 1.2 meters wide, and accessible restroom facilities (at least 1 per 100 attendees). Information about accessibility features must be clearly displayed at all entrances and on any promotional materials. Any exhibition over 500 square meters must have at least 2 dedicated accessibility points. Organizers must designate at least 5% of all seating for persons with reduced mobility.

heading: Temporary Structures
text:
(1) The erection of any temporary structures, such as tents, marquees, or booths, within the exhibition premises must comply with municipal building codes and safety standards.
(2) Plans for all temporary structures exceeding 20 square meters must be submitted with the licence application for approval by the municipal planning department. Structures must be securely anchored and regularly inspected by the organizer. A certificate of structural integrity, issued by a certified engineer within the last 6 months, is required for structures over 5 meters in height. All structures must be at least 3 meters from fire exits.

heading: Advertising and Promotion
text:
(1) All advertising and promotional materials for an exhibition must be accurate and not misleading.
(2) Organizers must clearly state the name of the exhibition, the organizer, and the licence number (if issued) on all public-facing materials. Any claims of attendance numbers, exhibitors, or special features must be verifiable. Falsely advertising an exhibition may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns and a mandatory retraction notice within 7 days. Promotional materials must not be placed within 50 meters of historical monuments.

heading: Repeal of Section 30
text:
(1) This section provides for the automatic repeal of any provision of this Act that becomes obsolete or impractical due to unforeseen circumstances or technological advancements.
(2) A provision may be considered for automatic repeal if it has not been invoked or applied for a continuous period of 5 years, or if 80% of municipal councils declare it redundant. The Minister for Municipal Affairs must publish a notice of intended repeal at least 90 days before it takes effect. This section itself is subject to review every 10 years.

heading: Repeal of Section 30
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Tolls on the way to a fire
text:
(1) A member of a municipal volunteer fire brigade who drives his or her own car to answer a call-out pays no toll on the Corvik Bridge or in the Dunmere Tunnel for that journey.
(2) The member shows the brigade's record of the call-out to the Toll Authority within 30 days.
(3) Passages on the M1 motorway are charged in full.

heading: Monthly bus and train passes for lone parents
text:
(1) A lone parent pays 20 crowns less than the ordinary price for a monthly pass for buses and trains, in every zone.
(2) The lower price does not change the price of an annual pass, which is still calculated from the ordinary monthly price.
(3) Where another provision also lowers the price of the monthly pass for the same person, only the provision giving the lowest price applies.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees associated with the allocation and ongoing use of radio frequencies within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure efficient spectrum management, cover administrative costs, and promote fair access to this valuable resource. The provisions herein apply to all entities, whether private or public, that seek to obtain or maintain rights to transmit on designated frequency bands. This includes commercial broadcasters, telecommunications providers, and private organizations requiring spectrum for operational purposes. The fees specified are subject to periodic review and adjustment by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority.

heading: General Fee for Frequency Allocation
text: All applicants for new frequency allocations, regardless of the specific band or intended use, shall pay a general allocation fee. This fee is non-refundable and must be submitted with the initial application. The amount of this general fee is set at 1,500 crowns for each application. This fee covers the initial administrative processing, technical assessment, and coordination efforts undertaken by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority. Failure to pay this fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application without further review.

heading: General Fee for Frequency Allocation
text: All applicants for new frequency allocations, regardless of the specific band or intended use, shall pay a general allocation fee. This fee is non-refundable and must be submitted with the initial application. The amount of this general fee is set at 1,850 crowns for each application. This fee covers the initial administrative processing, technical assessment, and coordination efforts undertaken by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority. Applications submitted without this fee will be returned to the applicant after 10 working days if the fee remains unpaid.

heading: Annual Spectrum Usage Fee
text: Holders of allocated frequency bands are required to pay an annual spectrum usage fee. This fee is calculated based on the specific frequency band, bandwidth, and coverage area. Payments are due on the 1st of January each year, covering the subsequent 12-month period. A 5% penalty will be applied to payments received more than 30 days after the due date. Continued non-payment for more than 90 days may result in the revocation of the frequency allocation without refund of previously paid fees.

heading: Bandwidth-Based Fee for VHF
text: For frequency allocations within the Very High Frequency (VHF) band (30 MHz to 300 MHz), a specific annual fee is applied based on the allocated bandwidth. The fee is calculated at 25 crowns per kilohertz (kHz) of allocated bandwidth. This applies to all VHF allocations, including those for two-way radio communications, public safety networks, and specialized industrial uses. For example, an allocation of 20 kHz in the VHF band would incur an annual fee of 500 crowns. The minimum chargeable bandwidth for any VHF allocation is 10 kHz.

heading: Bandwidth-Based Fee for VHF
text: For frequency allocations within the Very High Frequency (VHF) band (30 MHz to 300 MHz), a specific annual fee is applied based on the allocated bandwidth. The fee is calculated at 28 crowns per kilohertz (kHz) of allocated bandwidth. This applies to all VHF allocations, including those for two-way radio communications, public safety networks, and specialized industrial uses. For example, an allocation of 20 kHz in the VHF band would incur an annual fee of 560 crowns. The minimum chargeable bandwidth for any VHF allocation is 10 kHz, and a minimum annual fee of 300 crowns applies.

heading: Bandwidth-Based Fee for UHF
text: Allocations within the Ultra High Frequency (UHF) band (300 MHz to 3 GHz) are subject to an annual fee of 40 crowns per kilohertz (kHz) of allocated bandwidth. This higher rate reflects the increased demand and complexity associated with managing UHF spectrum, which is widely used for mobile communications, broadcasting, and various commercial applications. For allocations larger than 1 MHz, a discount of 5% on the total bandwidth fee may be applied, provided the allocation is contiguous. All fees are rounded to the nearest whole crown.

heading: Bandwidth-Based Fee for UHF
text: Allocations within the Ultra High Frequency (UHF) band (300 MHz to 3 GHz) are subject to an annual fee of 45 crowns per kilohertz (kHz) of allocated bandwidth. This higher rate reflects the increased demand and complexity associated with managing UHF spectrum, which is widely used for mobile communications, broadcasting, and various commercial applications. For allocations larger than 1 MHz, a discount of 7% on the total bandwidth fee may be applied, provided the allocation is contiguous and held by a single entity. All fees are rounded to the nearest whole crown.

heading: Microwave Band Fee Structure
text: Frequency allocations above 3 GHz, falling into the microwave bands, incur an annual fee of 60 crowns per megahertz (MHz) of allocated bandwidth. Due to the high data capacity and specialized applications of these bands, a different unit of measurement is used for fee calculation. Applications for microwave allocations must specify the exact frequency range and the intended geographical coverage. A surcharge of 10% may be applied for allocations requiring exclusive national coverage across Nordvale. This surcharge is assessed annually.

heading: Broadcasting Service Fees
text: Broadcasting services, including television and radio transmissions, are subject to a specialized annual fee structure. This fee consists of a base rate plus a coverage-area component. The base rate for a broadcasting license is 15,000 crowns per annum. An additional 0.50 crowns per square kilometre of licensed broadcast coverage area is also assessed. For example, a broadcaster covering an area of 10,000 square kilometres would pay 15,000 crowns plus 5,000 crowns, totaling 20,000 crowns annually. This fee must be paid 60 days prior to the expiration of the current license term.

heading: Broadcasting Service Fees
text: Broadcasting services, including television and radio transmissions, are subject to a specialized annual fee structure. This fee consists of a base rate plus a coverage-area component. The base rate for a broadcasting license is 17,500 crowns per annum. An additional 0.65 crowns per square kilometre of licensed broadcast coverage area is also assessed. For example, a broadcaster covering an area of 10,000 square kilometres would pay 17,500 crowns plus 6,500 crowns, totaling 24,000 crowns annually. This fee must be paid 45 days prior to the expiration of the current license term. Early payment discounts are not applicable.

heading: Mobile Telephony Network Fees
text: Providers of mobile telephony services are subject to an annual fee based on their allocated spectrum and subscriber count. A base annual fee of 50,000 crowns applies to all network operators. In addition, a per-subscriber fee of 2 crowns is levied for each active subscriber reported as of 31st December of the preceding year. This subscriber count must be independently audited and submitted to the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority by 1st February. Failure to submit audited figures will result in a default subscriber count of 100,000 being applied for fee calculation.

heading: Fixed Wireless Access Fees
text: Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) providers, offering internet or voice services to fixed locations using wireless technology, shall pay an annual fee of 3,000 crowns per base station. This fee acknowledges the localized nature of FWA deployments compared to mobile networks. Each base station must be registered with the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority, including its precise geographical coordinates. New base stations must be registered within 14 days of activation. A late registration fee of 500 crowns per base station will be applied for delays exceeding 14 days.

heading: Experimental License Fees
text: Experimental licenses for research and development purposes are available for a fixed fee of 750 crowns per year. These licenses are granted for a maximum duration of 2 years and are non-renewable. They are intended for non-commercial use only and are subject to strict power and emission limitations to prevent interference with operational systems. Applicants must provide a detailed project plan outlining the scope, objectives, and technical parameters of their experimental use. Any commercial exploitation of an experimental allocation will result in immediate revocation.

heading: Experimental License Fees
text: Experimental licenses for research and development purposes are available for a fixed fee of 900 crowns per year. These licenses are granted for a maximum duration of 18 months and are non-renewable. They are intended for non-commercial use only and are subject to strict power and emission limitations to prevent interference with operational systems. Applicants must provide a detailed project plan outlining the scope, objectives, and technical parameters of their experimental use, including a clear justification for the chosen frequency band. Any commercial exploitation of an experimental allocation will result in immediate revocation and a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Temporary Use Fees
text: Temporary frequency allocations for events, short-term projects, or emergency situations can be obtained for a fee of 150 crowns per day, with a minimum charge of 3 days. The maximum duration for a temporary allocation is 30 days. Applications for temporary use must be submitted at least 7 working days prior to the intended start date. Urgent applications submitted within 3 working days will incur an additional express processing fee of 200 crowns. Temporary allocations do not grant exclusive use of the spectrum.

heading: Satellite Earth Station Fees
text: Earth stations communicating with satellites are subject to an annual fee of 10,000 crowns per station. This fee covers the coordination efforts required to prevent interference with other terrestrial and satellite systems. Each earth station must be licensed individually, and its geographical coordinates, antenna characteristics, and operational frequency bands must be accurately declared. Minor changes to operational parameters, such as antenna gain adjustments of less than 1 dB, must be reported within 30 days to avoid a potential 1,000 crowns penalty.

heading: Non-Commercial Public Service Exemptions
text: Certain non-commercial public service entities may be granted full or partial exemptions from frequency allocation fees. To qualify, an entity must demonstrate that its primary purpose is public benefit, not profit, and that the requested frequency allocation is essential for its core public service operations. Examples include emergency services, disaster relief organizations, and scientific research institutions funded entirely by the state. Applications for exemption must be submitted annually and are subject to review by a special committee. Partial exemptions may reduce fees by up to 75%.

heading: Non-Commercial Public Service Exemptions
text: Certain non-commercial public service entities may be granted full or partial exemptions from frequency allocation fees. To qualify, an entity must demonstrate that its primary purpose is public benefit, not profit, and that the requested frequency allocation is essential for its core public service operations. Examples include emergency services, disaster relief organizations, and state-funded meteorological services. Applications for exemption must be submitted annually, 90 days before the fee due date, and are subject to review by a special committee. Partial exemptions may reduce fees by up to 80%, with a minimum annual fee of 250 crowns still applicable.

heading: Educational Institution Exemptions
text: Recognized educational institutions, such as universities and colleges, may apply for a 50% reduction in annual spectrum usage fees for frequencies used exclusively for teaching and academic research. This reduction applies only to specific frequencies that are integral to their educational programs and are not used for commercial broadcasting or administrative purposes. The institution must provide a detailed justification and demonstrate that the spectrum use directly contributes to the advancement of knowledge. The exemption does not apply to the initial general allocation fee.

heading: Fee for Spectrum Transfer
text: A fee of 10,000 crowns is payable for the transfer of an allocated frequency right from one entity to another. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the transfer, updating records, and ensuring the new holder meets all regulatory requirements. Both the transferring and receiving parties must jointly submit the transfer application. The transfer fee must be paid upfront before any transfer is formally approved. Transfers involving more than 5 distinct frequency blocks will incur an additional 1,000 crowns per block beyond the fifth.

heading: Fee for Spectrum Transfer
text: A fee of 12,500 crowns is payable for the transfer of an allocated frequency right from one entity to another. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the transfer, updating records, and ensuring the new holder meets all regulatory requirements. Both the transferring and receiving parties must jointly submit the transfer application. The transfer fee must be paid upfront before any transfer is formally approved. Transfers involving more than 5 distinct frequency blocks will incur an additional 1,500 crowns per block beyond the fifth. Complex transfers involving changes to technical parameters may incur an additional 5,000 crowns assessment fee.

heading: Fee for License Modification
text: Requests for modifications to an existing frequency allocation license, such as changes in power output, antenna location, or emission characteristics, incur a processing fee of 750 crowns. This fee applies to each distinct modification request, even if multiple minor changes are grouped together in a single submission. Significant modifications that necessitate a full re-evaluation of potential interference may be subject to a higher fee of 2,000 crowns. The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority will determine the appropriate fee based on the complexity of the requested changes.

heading: Fee for License Modification
text: Requests for modifications to an existing frequency allocation license, such as changes in power output, antenna location, or emission characteristics, incur a processing fee of 900 crowns. This fee applies to each distinct modification request. If multiple minor changes are submitted simultaneously within one request, the fee is capped at 1,800 crowns. Significant modifications that necessitate a full re-evaluation of potential interference may be subject to a higher fee of 2,500 crowns. The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority will determine the appropriate fee based on the complexity of the requested changes and inform the applicant within 15 working days.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Annual spectrum usage fees not paid by their due date will incur a late payment penalty. A surcharge of 10% of the outstanding amount will be applied if payment is received between 1 and 30 days after the due date. If payment is received between 31 and 60 days after the due date, the surcharge increases to 20%. For payments more than 60 days late, an additional monthly interest rate of 1.5% will be applied to the total outstanding amount, including previous penalties, until the full amount is settled. This is in addition to any revocation procedures mentioned in section 3.

heading: Interest on Overdue Fees
text: Beyond the initial late payment penalties detailed in section 17, any fees that remain unpaid for more than 60 days will accrue interest at a rate of 1.5% per month. This interest is compounded monthly and calculated on the total outstanding amount, including any previously applied penalties. The interest calculation begins on the 61st day following the original due date and continues until the full outstanding balance, including all accrued interest, is paid. The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority reserves the right to pursue legal action for recovery of outstanding amounts.

heading: Refund Policy for Fees
text: Fees paid for frequency allocation are generally non-refundable. However, if an application for a new allocation is rejected by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority due to reasons other than incomplete submission or applicant error, 50% of the general allocation fee may be refunded. Annual usage fees are not refundable once the allocation period has commenced. Transfer and modification fees are entirely non-refundable once the processing of the request has begun. Refund requests must be made in writing within 90 days of the decision leading to the potential refund.

heading: Administrative Review Fee
text: Applicants or license holders wishing to appeal a decision made by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority regarding fee assessments or license conditions must pay an administrative review fee of 2,500 crowns. This fee is required to initiate the formal review process. If the appeal is successful and the original decision is overturned in favor of the applicant, 80% of the administrative review fee will be refunded. Unsuccessful appeals will not result in any refund. Appeals must be submitted within 30 days of the contested decision.

heading: Fee for Public Records Access
text: Requests for access to public records related to frequency allocations, such as license registers or technical specifications of specific allocations, will incur a processing fee of 50 crowns per request. If the request requires extensive retrieval or reproduction of documents, an additional charge of 5 crowns per page will be applied for printed copies, or 20 crowns per digital file for electronic provision, capped at 500 crowns per request. Requests must be made in writing and processing may take up to 15 working days.

heading: Spectrum Monitoring Fee
text: To support the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority's spectrum monitoring and enforcement activities, a separate annual spectrum monitoring fee is levied on all commercial frequency allocations. This fee is calculated as 0.1% of the total annual spectrum usage fee for each allocation, with a minimum charge of 100 crowns and a maximum charge of 5,000 crowns per allocation. This fee contributes directly to the operational costs of equipment and personnel dedicated to ensuring compliance and managing interference. This fee is due concurrently with the annual spectrum usage fee.

heading: Spectrum Monitoring Fee
text: To support the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority's spectrum monitoring and enforcement activities, a separate annual spectrum monitoring fee is levied on all commercial frequency allocations. This fee is calculated as 0.15% of the total annual spectrum usage fee for each allocation, with a minimum charge of 120 crowns and a maximum charge of 6,000 crowns per allocation. This fee contributes directly to the operational costs of equipment and personnel dedicated to ensuring compliance and managing interference. This fee is due concurrently with the annual spectrum usage fee and is non-negotiable.

heading: Exclusive Use Surcharge
text: Entities granted exclusive use of specific frequency bands within a defined geographical area, beyond the standard allocation conditions, will incur an additional annual surcharge of 20% of their base annual usage fee. This surcharge reflects the additional value and opportunity cost associated with preventing other users from accessing that spectrum. Applications for exclusive use must demonstrate a compelling need and are subject to stringent review. The exclusive use surcharge applies only to allocations covering areas larger than 100 square kilometres.

heading: Reduced Fee for Rural Coverage
text: To encourage spectrum deployment in underserved rural areas, commercial entities providing services predominantly in municipalities with a population of less than 10,000, such as Fennick or Grauby, may apply for a 15% reduction in their annual spectrum usage fees. To qualify, at least 70% of the allocated coverage area must fall within designated rural zones. This reduction applies only to the annual usage fees and not to initial allocation or administrative fees. Proof of coverage and population data must be submitted annually.

heading: Reduced Fee for Public Safety Communication
text: Organizations directly involved in public safety communications, such as police, fire, and ambulance services, receive a 75% reduction on all applicable annual spectrum usage fees. This reduction acknowledges their vital role in protecting Nordvale's citizens. The general allocation fee (section 2) is reduced by 50% for these organizations. This applies exclusively to frequencies used for their primary public safety functions and does not extend to any commercial or administrative uses. Entities must submit an annual declaration confirming the dedicated use of their allocated spectrum.

heading: Reduced Fee for Public Safety Communication
text: Organizations directly involved in public safety communications, such as police, fire, and ambulance services, receive an 80% reduction on all applicable annual spectrum usage fees. This reduction acknowledges their vital role in protecting Nordvale's citizens. The general allocation fee (section 2) is reduced by 60% for these organizations. This applies exclusively to frequencies used for their primary public safety functions and does not extend to any commercial or administrative uses. Entities must submit an annual declaration confirming the dedicated use of their allocated spectrum and provide evidence of direct operational involvement in public safety activities.

heading: Fee for Spectrum Reservation
text: Entities may apply to reserve a specific frequency band for future use for a non-refundable annual reservation fee of 5,000 crowns. A spectrum reservation ensures that a particular band remains available for the applicant for a maximum period of 3 years, without the full allocation fees becoming immediately applicable. This allows for planning and development without committing to full operational costs. If the reservation converts to an active allocation, the reservation fee paid for the current year will be credited against the first year's annual usage fee. Only contiguous blocks of spectrum exceeding 1 MHz can be reserved.

heading: Fee for Spectrum Reservation
text: Entities may apply to reserve a specific frequency band for future use for a non-refundable annual reservation fee of 6,500 crowns. A spectrum reservation ensures that a particular band remains available for the applicant for a maximum period of 2 years, without the full allocation fees becoming immediately applicable. This allows for planning and development without committing to full operational costs. If the reservation converts to an active allocation, 50% of the reservation fee paid for the current year will be credited against the first year's annual usage fee. Only contiguous blocks of spectrum exceeding 500 kHz can be reserved.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in Nordvale crowns. Acceptable payment methods include direct bank transfer, certified cheque, or approved electronic payment platforms. Cash payments are not accepted for amounts exceeding 1,000 crowns. Payments must be made to the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority's designated account, and proof of payment must be retained for at least 5 years. Any bank charges or currency conversion fees associated with the payment are the responsibility of the payer. Incomplete payments will be treated as non-payment until the full amount is settled.

heading: Invoice Issuance
text: The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority shall issue invoices for all annual spectrum usage fees at least 60 days prior to their due date. Invoices will be sent to the registered address of the license holder, either electronically or by postal service. It is the responsibility of the license holder to ensure their contact details are up to date with the Authority. Failure to receive an invoice does not absolve the license holder of their payment obligations or exempt them from late payment penalties. Reminder notices for overdue payments will be issued 15 days after the due date.

heading: Maximum Annual Fee Cap
text: For any single entity, the cumulative annual fees for all their frequency allocations within the Republic of Nordvale shall not exceed a maximum cap of 5,000,000 crowns. This cap is designed to prevent an undue financial burden on large-scale operators holding extensive spectrum portfolios, while still ensuring fair contribution. This cap applies only to annual usage fees and does not include initial allocation fees, transfer fees, modification fees, or any penalties incurred. Any excess payment beyond this cap will be refunded within 90 days of the payment date.

heading: Fee for Interference Resolution
text: If a frequency allocation holder is found to be causing harmful interference to another legitimate spectrum user due to non-compliance with their license conditions, they may be charged a fee for the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority's intervention. This interference resolution fee is set at 3,000 crowns per incident. If the resolution requires extensive technical investigation or repeated interventions, additional charges of 500 crowns per hour of staff time may be levied. This fee is distinct from any fines or penalties for license breaches.

heading: Fee for Interference Resolution
text: If a frequency allocation holder is found to be causing harmful interference to another legitimate spectrum user due to non-compliance with their license conditions, they may be charged a fee for the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority's intervention. This interference resolution fee is set at 4,000 crowns per incident. If the resolution requires extensive technical investigation or repeated interventions, additional charges of 600 crowns per hour of staff time may be levied, with a minimum charge of 2 hours. This fee is distinct from any fines or penalties for license breaches and must be paid within 30 days of invoicing.

heading: Annual Adjustment Mechanism
text: The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority is empowered to adjust all fee rates specified in this Act annually, effective 1st January. Any adjustments will be published in the Official Gazette of Nordvale by 1st October of the preceding year. These adjustments will primarily be linked to the national inflation rate, but may also consider changes in spectrum demand, technological advancements, and administrative costs. Increases or decreases in any fee rate shall not exceed 5% in any given year, except by explicit amendment to this Act.

heading: Annual Adjustment Mechanism
text: The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority is empowered to adjust all fee rates specified in this Act annually, effective 1st January. Any adjustments will be published in the Official Gazette of Nordvale by 1st October of the preceding year. These adjustments will primarily be linked to the national inflation rate and the Gross Domestic Product growth rate, but may also consider changes in spectrum demand, technological advancements, and administrative costs. Increases or decreases in any fee rate shall not exceed 6% in any given year, except by explicit amendment to this Act. Public consultation will be held for any adjustment exceeding 3%.

heading: Failure to Comply with Payment
text: Failure to pay any fees, penalties, or interest due section 3, section 17, or section 18 of this Act within 90 days of the original due date will result in the immediate suspension of the relevant frequency allocation. If payment, including all outstanding amounts, is not received within a further 30 days following suspension, the allocation will be permanently revoked. Once revoked, the spectrum becomes available for reallocation to other applicants, and the former holder must apply anew, including payment of all outstanding debt, if they wish to regain any frequency rights.

heading: Special Event Temporary Use
text: For specific high-profile national or international events, such as major sports championships or cultural festivals held in Aldmark or Brenholt, a specialized temporary use fee applies. This fee is 300 crowns per day per frequency assignment, with a minimum charge of 5 days, and covers the heightened administrative and coordination efforts required. Such allocations are limited to a maximum duration of 14 days. Applications must be submitted at least 21 days in advance of the event. Express applications within 7 days will incur a 400 crowns surcharge.

heading: Special Event Temporary Use
text: For specific high-profile national or international events, such as major sports championships or cultural festivals held in Aldmark or Brenholt, a specialized temporary use fee applies. This fee is 350 crowns per day per frequency assignment, with a minimum charge of 4 days, and covers the heightened administrative and coordination efforts required. Such allocations are limited to a maximum duration of 10 days. Applications must be submitted at least 25 days in advance of the event. Express applications within 7 days will incur a 500 crowns surcharge, and priority will be given to national media broadcasters.

heading: Exemption for Emergency Services Testing
text: Emergency services organizations, including those for police, fire, and medical response, are exempt from fees for temporary frequency allocations specifically for testing, training, and drills related to their operational readiness. This exemption is limited to a maximum of 10 days per calendar year per organization. Any such temporary use must be coordinated with and approved by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority at least 5 working days in advance, providing full details of the frequencies, locations, and durations involved. This exemption does not cover any permanent operational allocations.

heading: Reduced Fees for Small-Scale Community Radio
text: Non-profit community radio stations operating with a maximum effective radiated power of 50 watts and serving a single municipality with a population under 50,000, such as Corvik or Dunmere, are eligible for a reduced annual spectrum usage fee of 500 crowns. This reduced fee encourages local broadcasting and cultural expression. They are also exempt from the general allocation fee mentioned in section 2. To qualify, the station must provide evidence of its non-profit status and limited coverage area annually. Any increase in power or coverage above these limits will result in the application of standard broadcasting fees from section 7.

heading: Reduced Fees for Small-Scale Community Radio
text: Non-profit community radio stations operating with a maximum effective radiated power of 40 watts and serving a single municipality with a population under 40,000, such as Corvik or Dunmere, are eligible for a reduced annual spectrum usage fee of 600 crowns. This reduced fee encourages local broadcasting and cultural expression. They are also exempt from the general allocation fee mentioned in section 2. To qualify, the station must provide evidence of its non-profit status and limited coverage area annually, including audited listener figures. Any increase in power or coverage above these limits will result in the application of standard broadcasting fees from section 7.

heading: Fee for Unlicensed Operation Investigation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Fee for Unlicensed Operation Investigation
text: Entities found to be operating radio equipment without a valid frequency allocation or license are subject to an investigation fee of 7,500 crowns. This fee covers the costs incurred by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority in identifying, locating, and investigating the source of unlicensed transmissions. This fee is payable regardless of whether enforcement action, such as fines or equipment seizure, is subsequently taken. Payment of this fee does not legitimize the unlicensed operation and further legal consequences may still apply.

heading: Dispute Resolution Fee
text: Parties seeking formal dispute resolution through the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority regarding spectrum interference or conflicting allocations must pay a dispute resolution fee of 1,200 crowns. This fee applies to the party initiating the dispute. If the dispute is resolved in favor of the initiating party, 50% of this fee will be refunded. The Authority will endeavor to resolve disputes within 60 days of receiving the fee and all necessary documentation. Complex disputes requiring external expert assessment may incur additional charges, agreed upon by all parties.

heading: Short-Term Equipment Test Fee
text: Manufacturers or importers requiring temporary frequency access for the testing of new radio equipment, prior to commercial deployment, may apply for a short-term equipment test license. The fee for such a license is 400 crowns per week, with a minimum charge of one week. The license duration is limited to a maximum of 4 weeks per testing campaign. This license permits low-power, non-interfering tests within designated test frequencies only, and requires strict adherence to specified power limits and geographical boundaries. Applicants must submit a detailed test plan 10 days in advance.

heading: Fee for Renewed Application after Revocation
text: Should a frequency allocation be revoked due to non-payment of fees or non-compliance with license conditions, any subsequent application by the same entity for the same or a similar frequency band will incur a renewed application fee of 3,000 crowns, in addition to the standard general allocation fee. This fee covers the additional administrative burden of reviewing a past revocation history. Furthermore, all previously outstanding debts, penalties, and interest must be fully settled before any new allocation application will be considered.

heading: Annual Reporting Fee
text: All commercial frequency allocation holders are required to submit an annual technical and operational report to the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority by 1st March each year. A processing fee of 200 crowns is levied for the submission and review of this report. The report must detail the actual usage of the allocated spectrum, any technical modifications, and adherence to coverage obligations. Failure to submit the report on time will incur a late fee of 500 crowns for each month of delay. The information gathered informs spectrum planning and enforcement.

heading: Annual Reporting Fee
text: All commercial frequency allocation holders are required to submit an annual technical and operational report to the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority by 1st March each year. A processing fee of 250 crowns is levied for the submission and review of this report. The report must detail the actual usage of the allocated spectrum, any technical modifications, and adherence to coverage obligations. Failure to submit the report on time will incur a late fee of 600 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 3 months. The information gathered informs spectrum planning and enforcement and must be provided in an approved digital format.

heading: Fee for Priority Processing
text: Applicants may request priority processing for new frequency allocation applications by paying an additional non-refundable fee of 5,000 crowns. This fee ensures that the application is reviewed within 15 working days, rather than the standard 45 working days. Priority processing does not guarantee approval of the allocation, but only speeds up the review timeline. This option is not available for applications requiring extensive public consultation or complex technical coordination. The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority reserves the right to refuse priority processing for certain complex or sensitive allocations.

heading: Fee for Spectrum Audit
text: The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority may conduct audits of allocated spectrum to verify compliance with license conditions. If an audit reveals significant discrepancies or unauthorized use, the audited entity will be charged an audit fee of 10,000 crowns. This fee covers the costs of the inspection and analysis. If no non-compliance is found during a routine audit, no fee will be levied. Entities found to be in compliance will receive a certificate of compliance valid for 2 years. Repeated non-compliance discovered during an audit may lead to revocation of the license.

heading: Recognised trades
text: A licensed fireworks technician shall pay half of the monthly fee specified in CCA §4(1) for any child aged 3 to 5 enrolled in a municipal kindergarten. This reduced fee applies for 11 months of the year.

heading: Recognised trades
text: A licensed fireworks technician shall receive half the amount specified in HOA §18(1). This payment is subject to the conditions outlined in HOA §18(2) and (3).

heading: Particular persons
text: For a registered violin maker, any fee or allowance specified in STA §6 shall instead be a fixed payment of 5 crowns.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a certified ski patroller, the housing allowance described in subsections (1) and (2) of this section shall not be paid.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: The purpose of this Act is to mandate regular inspections of public and commercial facilities throughout Nordvale to ensure they meet established accessibility standards. This includes ensuring all citizens, regardless of physical ability, have equitable access to essential services and commercial establishments. The scope encompasses all buildings and structures accessible to the general public, including but not limited to shops, offices, restaurants, and public service buildings, to promote a universally accessible society. These standards are designed to facilitate ease of movement and use for individuals with mobility impairments, visual impairments, and other accessibility needs, thereby enhancing overall community participation.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, "facility" means any building, structure, or part thereof, that is open to the public, whether for commercial or public service purposes.
(2) "Accessibility standard" refers to the minimum requirements for design and construction that ensure facilities are usable by individuals with diverse abilities, as detailed in the Nordvale Building Code.
(3) "Inspector" means an individual appointed by the Nordvale Accessibility Board to conduct inspections and enforce compliance with this Act.
(4) "Owner" means the person or entity holding legal title to a facility or the person or entity responsible for its operation and maintenance.

heading: Nordvale Accessibility Board
text:
(1) A Nordvale Accessibility Board is hereby established to oversee the implementation and enforcement of this Act.
(2) The Board shall consist of seven members, appointed by the Minister of Public Works, with at least three members having lived experience with accessibility challenges.
(3) The Board's responsibilities include developing inspection protocols, training inspectors, issuing compliance certificates, and investigating complaints related to facility accessibility.
(4) The Board shall meet monthly, or more frequently as deemed necessary, to review inspection reports and address any emerging accessibility concerns. A quorum of four members is required for all official decisions.

heading: Inspection frequency for public facilities
text:
(1) All public facilities, such as government offices, libraries, and community centers, shall undergo a comprehensive accessibility inspection at least once every three years.
(2) New public facilities must undergo an initial inspection within 60 days of obtaining an occupancy permit.
(3) Facilities that undergo major renovations impacting accessibility features must be reinspected within 90 days of project completion.
(4) The Board may order additional inspections if a significant number of public complaints are received or if a facility's use changes in a way that impacts accessibility requirements. The cost of such additional inspections may be borne by the facility owner if non-compliance is found.

heading: Inspection frequency for public facilities
text:
(1) All public facilities, such as government offices, libraries, and community centers, shall undergo a comprehensive accessibility inspection at least once every four years.
(2) New public facilities must undergo an initial inspection within 45 days of obtaining an occupancy permit.
(3) Facilities that undergo major renovations impacting accessibility features must be reinspected within 75 days of project completion.
(4) The Board may order additional inspections if a significant number of public complaints are received or if a facility's use changes in a way that impacts accessibility requirements. The cost of such additional inspections may be borne by the facility owner if non-compliance is found.

heading: Inspection frequency for public facilities
text:
(1) All public facilities, such as government offices, libraries, and community centers, shall undergo a comprehensive accessibility inspection at least once every five years.
(2) New public facilities must undergo an initial inspection within 30 days of obtaining an occupancy permit.
(3) Facilities that undergo major renovations impacting accessibility features must be reinspected within 60 days of project completion.
(4) The Board may order additional inspections if a significant number of public complaints are received or if a facility's use changes in a way that impacts accessibility requirements. The cost of such additional inspections may be borne by the facility owner if non-compliance is found.

heading: Inspection frequency for commercial facilities
text:
(1) All commercial facilities, including retail stores, restaurants, and private offices, shall undergo an accessibility inspection at least once every five years.
(2) New commercial facilities must undergo an initial inspection within 90 days of obtaining an occupancy permit.
(3) Facilities with a public access area exceeding 500 square meters must be inspected every three years.
(4) The Board may conduct random spot inspections of 10% of commercial facilities each year to ensure ongoing compliance, particularly in areas with high public traffic like Aldmark and Brenholt. These spot checks are unannounced and serve as a deterrent to non-compliance.

heading: Inspection frequency for commercial facilities
text:
(1) All commercial facilities, including retail stores, restaurants, and private offices, shall undergo an accessibility inspection at least once every six years.
(2) New commercial facilities must undergo an initial inspection within 75 days of obtaining an occupancy permit.
(3) Facilities with a public access area exceeding 400 square meters must be inspected every three years.
(4) The Board may conduct random spot inspections of 15% of commercial facilities each year to ensure ongoing compliance, particularly in areas with high public traffic like Aldmark and Brenholt. These spot checks are unannounced and serve as a deterrent to non-compliance.

heading: Inspection frequency for commercial facilities
text:
(1) All commercial facilities, including retail stores, restaurants, and private offices, shall undergo an accessibility inspection at least once every seven years.
(2) New commercial facilities must undergo an initial inspection within 60 days of obtaining an occupancy permit.
(3) Facilities with a public access area exceeding 300 square meters must be inspected every three years.
(4) The Board may conduct random spot inspections of 20% of commercial facilities each year to ensure ongoing compliance, particularly in areas with high public traffic like Aldmark and Brenholt. These spot checks are unannounced and serve as a deterrent to non-compliance.

heading: Inspection process
text:
(1) An inspector shall notify the facility owner in writing at least 14 days before a scheduled inspection.
(2) The inspection shall assess all accessible routes, entrances, exits, restrooms, and any other public-facing areas for compliance with current accessibility standards.
(3) Inspectors shall use a standardized checklist provided by the Nordvale Accessibility Board to ensure consistency across all inspections.
(4) The inspection process includes measuring door widths, ramp slopes, grab bar heights, and ensuring clear signage for individuals with visual impairments. Any deficiencies will be documented with photographic evidence and detailed notes, which will be included in the final inspection report.

heading: Reporting inspection results
text:
(1) Within 30 days of completing an inspection, the inspector shall submit a detailed report to the Nordvale Accessibility Board and provide a copy to the facility owner.
(2) The report shall clearly state any deficiencies found, citing the specific sections of the Nordvale Building Code that are not met.
(3) If no deficiencies are found, a Certificate of Compliance will be issued to the facility owner within 15 days of the report submission. This certificate is valid until the next scheduled inspection.
(4) The report will also include recommendations for improvements beyond the minimum requirements, where applicable, to encourage a higher standard of accessibility. Owners are encouraged to address these recommendations but are not legally obligated to do so.

heading: Rectification period for minor deficiencies
text:
(1) For minor deficiencies, such as missing signage or slightly obstructed pathways, the facility owner shall be granted a period of 60 days to rectify the issues.
(2) The owner must submit evidence of rectification, such as photographs or contractor invoices, to the Nordvale Accessibility Board within this period.
(3) A follow-up inspection may be conducted if the Board deems it necessary to verify the rectification of minor issues. This follow-up inspection will be scheduled within 30 days of receiving the evidence.
(4) Failure to rectify minor deficiencies within the 60-day period may result in a fine of 500 crowns per deficiency, up to a maximum of 2,500 crowns for all minor deficiencies combined, as outlined in section 12.

heading: Rectification period for major deficiencies
text:
(1) For major deficiencies, such as inaccessible entrances, restrooms, or non-compliant ramps, the facility owner shall be granted a period of 120 days to rectify the issues.
(2) The owner must submit a detailed plan for rectification, including timelines and proposed contractors, to the Nordvale Accessibility Board within 30 days of receiving the inspection report.
(3) A mandatory follow-up inspection will be conducted within 15 days after the 120-day rectification period to verify compliance. The facility must pass this inspection.
(4) Failure to rectify major deficiencies within the specified period may result in significant fines and, in severe cases, temporary closure of the facility until compliance is achieved, as detailed in sections 13 and 14.

heading: Rectification period for major deficiencies
text:
(1) For major deficiencies, such as inaccessible entrances, restrooms, or non-compliant ramps, the facility owner shall be granted a period of 90 days to rectify the issues.
(2) The owner must submit a detailed plan for rectification, including timelines and proposed contractors, to the Nordvale Accessibility Board within 20 days of receiving the inspection report.
(3) A mandatory follow-up inspection will be conducted within 10 days after the 90-day rectification period to verify compliance. The facility must pass this inspection.
(4) Failure to rectify major deficiencies within the specified period may result in significant fines and, in severe cases, temporary closure of the facility until compliance is achieved, as detailed in sections 13 and 14.

heading: Extensions for rectification
text:
(1) Facility owners may apply to the Nordvale Accessibility Board for an extension of the rectification period.
(2) An application for extension must be submitted in writing at least 15 days before the original deadline, detailing the reasons for the delay and a proposed new completion date.
(3) The Board may grant an extension of up to 60 additional days for minor deficiencies and up to 90 additional days for major deficiencies, based on the complexity of the work and demonstrated effort by the owner.
(4) Only one extension will be granted per set of deficiencies. Subsequent requests will be denied unless exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen structural issues or material shortages, can be proven to the Board's satisfaction, requiring additional documentation and a 750 crown processing fee.

heading: Appeals process for inspection findings
text:
(1) Facility owners may appeal the findings of an inspection report within 30 days of receiving the report.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Accessibility Board, outlining the specific findings being disputed and providing supporting documentation or alternative professional assessments.
(3) The Board shall review the appeal and may request additional information or conduct a re-inspection by a different inspector within 45 days of receiving the appeal.
(4) The decision of the Nordvale Accessibility Board on the appeal shall be final. If the appeal is upheld, the original inspection findings will be amended accordingly, and any associated penalties or rectification orders will be withdrawn. If the appeal is denied, the original findings stand, and the rectification period resumes from the date of the appeal decision.

heading: Penalties for minor non-compliance
text:
(1) Failure to rectify minor deficiencies within the specified period, including any approved extensions, shall result in a penalty of 500 crowns.
(2) A further penalty of 100 crowns per week will be levied for each week the minor deficiency remains unaddressed after the initial penalty period.
(3) The total penalties for minor non-compliance shall not exceed 5,000 crowns for a single inspection cycle.
(4) These penalties are cumulative and are designed to encourage prompt action. Owners who demonstrate a good faith effort to comply, but face unavoidable delays, may apply for a reduction of up to 25% of the weekly penalties, subject to Board approval.

heading: Penalties for major non-compliance
text:
(1) Failure to rectify major deficiencies within the specified period, including any approved extensions, shall result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns.
(2) A further penalty of 500 crowns per week will be levied for each week the major deficiency remains unaddressed after the initial penalty period.
(3) The Nordvale Accessibility Board may, at its discretion, order the temporary closure of a facility if major non-compliance persists for more than 180 days.
(4) In severe cases, where major deficiencies pose an immediate safety risk to individuals with accessibility needs, the Board may issue an immediate closure order without prior warning. Reopening requires a full reinspection and a 1,000 crown reopening fee, in addition to all accumulated penalties.

heading: Obstruction of inspectors
text:
(1) Any person who obstructs or interferes with an inspector in the performance of their duties under this Act commits an offense.
(2) An offense under subsection (1) is punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for a first offense.
(3) Subsequent offenses of obstruction or interference may result in a fine of up to 20,000 crowns and potential legal action.
(4) Obstruction includes, but is not limited to, refusing entry to an inspector without valid reason, providing false information, or intentionally concealing areas of the facility relevant to the inspection. Inspectors are authorized to seek assistance from law enforcement if they are denied access or face physical obstruction during an inspection.

heading: Maintaining records
text:
(1) Facility owners shall maintain records of all accessibility inspections, rectification works, and compliance certificates for a minimum period of 10 years.
(2) These records must be made available to an inspector upon request during any scheduled or unscheduled inspection.
(3) The Nordvale Accessibility Board shall maintain a central database of all inspection reports, compliance certificates, and enforcement actions for public facilities indefinitely.
(4) For commercial facilities, the Board shall maintain records for a minimum of 20 years. Failure to maintain required records may result in an administrative fine of 250 crowns for each missing or incomplete document, up to a maximum of 2,500 crowns per audit.

heading: Public awareness and education
text:
(1) The Nordvale Accessibility Board shall launch public awareness campaigns to inform citizens and facility owners about the importance of accessibility.
(2) Educational materials, including brochures and online guides, will be made available to assist facility owners in understanding and meeting accessibility standards.
(3) The Board will host at least two public workshops annually in different municipalities, such as Corvik and Dunmere, to provide guidance on accessibility best practices.
(4) These workshops will cover topics such as universal design principles, the benefits of accessible spaces, and common pitfalls to avoid during renovation projects. Participation is voluntary, but highly encouraged for facility managers and property developers.

heading: Training of inspectors
text:
(1) All inspectors appointed under this Act must complete a mandatory training program approved by the Nordvale Accessibility Board.
(2) The training program shall cover accessibility standards, inspection techniques, ethical conduct, and communication skills for interacting with facility owners.
(3) Inspectors are required to undergo refresher training every two years to stay updated on any changes to accessibility standards or inspection protocols.
(4) New inspectors must complete a 120-hour training course and pass a certification exam with a score of at least 80% before conducting independent inspections. Experienced inspectors must complete 40 hours of refresher training biennially.

heading: Complaints from the public
text:
(1) Any member of the public may lodge a complaint with the Nordvale Accessibility Board regarding a facility's accessibility.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing and provide specific details about the alleged accessibility barrier, including the facility's name and location.
(3) The Board shall investigate all legitimate complaints within 30 days of receipt and, if warranted, schedule an unscheduled inspection of the facility.
(4) The identity of the complainant will be kept confidential, unless required by law. Facilities found to be in non-compliance as a result of a public complaint will be subject to the same rectification periods and penalties as those identified during routine inspections.

heading: Exemptions for historical buildings
text:
(1) Historical buildings recognized by the Nordvale Heritage Council may apply for partial exemptions from certain accessibility standards if compliance would significantly alter their historical integrity.
(2) An application for exemption must demonstrate that all reasonable efforts have been made to achieve accessibility without compromising historical features.
(3) The Nordvale Accessibility Board, in consultation with the Nordvale Heritage Council, will review such applications on a case-by-case basis.
(4) If an exemption is granted, the facility must still provide alternative accessibility solutions where feasible, such as virtual tours or assistance services, to ensure some form of access for individuals with disabilities. A public notice detailing the exemption and alternative provisions must be displayed prominently at the facility entrance.

heading: Cost of inspections
text:
(1) The cost of initial and routine accessibility inspections for public facilities shall be borne by the Nordvale government.
(2) For commercial facilities, the owner shall pay an inspection fee of 1,500 crowns for each routine inspection.
(3) The cost of follow-up inspections for non-compliance shall be borne by the facility owner, at a rate of 750 crowns per reinspection.
(4) Inspection fees for commercial facilities are payable within 30 days of the inspection notice. A late payment fee of 10% will be applied if not paid within this timeframe. Non-payment of fees may result in the withholding of compliance certificates.

heading: Display of compliance certificate
text:
(1) Every facility that has achieved full compliance with accessibility standards shall prominently display its Certificate of Compliance.
(2) The certificate must be displayed near the main entrance, visible to the public, at a height of between 1.5 and 2 meters from the floor.
(3) Failure to display a valid Certificate of Compliance may result in an administrative fine of 200 crowns.
(4) The certificate acts as a public assurance of accessibility and must be replaced immediately if lost or damaged, with a replacement fee of 50 crowns. Digital copies are also acceptable for display on facility websites or digital signage, provided they are easily accessible.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text:
(1) All information collected during inspections, other than the final inspection report and compliance status, shall be treated as confidential.
(2) Inspectors and Board members shall not disclose any proprietary or personal information obtained during their duties, except as required by law.
(3) Breach of confidentiality may result in disciplinary action, including termination of employment or appointment, and potential legal prosecution.
(4) This includes any financial details, business plans, or sensitive operational information observed during an inspection. The Board implements strict data protection protocols, including encrypted storage and restricted access, to safeguard all confidential data collected under this Act.

heading: Annual report to the Minister
text:
(1) The Nordvale Accessibility Board shall submit an annual report to the Minister of Public Works by March 31st of each year.
(2) The report shall detail the number of inspections conducted, compliance rates, types of deficiencies identified, and enforcement actions taken.
(3) The annual report shall also include recommendations for improvements to accessibility standards or the implementation of this Act.
(4) The Minister shall present this report to the Nordvale Assembly within 60 days of receipt. The report will be made publicly available on the Nordvale government website to ensure transparency and accountability regarding accessibility efforts across the nation, highlighting progress in municipalities like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Review of accessibility standards
text:
(1) The Nordvale Accessibility Board shall review the established accessibility standards, as detailed in the Nordvale Building Code, at least once every five years.
(2) This review shall consider advancements in accessibility technology, best practices from other jurisdictions, and feedback from individuals with accessibility needs.
(3) Any proposed changes to the standards will be subject to a 60-day public consultation period before final approval by the Minister of Public Works.
(4) The review process involves consultations with architects, engineers, disability advocacy groups, and facility owners to ensure that standards remain relevant and effective. The next scheduled review is set for 2028.

heading: Emergency access routes
text:
(1) All facilities must ensure that emergency access and exit routes are fully accessible at all times.
(2) This includes maintaining clear pathways, functioning accessible alarms, and designated assembly points that are usable by individuals with mobility impairments.
(3) Emergency exits must have a minimum clear width of 900 millimeters and be free of any obstructions.
(4) Facilities are required to conduct annual drills that specifically include protocols for assisting individuals with disabilities during emergencies, with a minimum of 2 drills per year, and records of these drills must be maintained for inspection for a period of 5 years.

heading: Emergency access routes
text:
(1) All facilities must ensure that emergency access and exit routes are fully accessible at all times.
(2) This includes maintaining clear pathways, functioning accessible alarms, and designated assembly points that are usable by individuals with mobility impairments.
(3) Emergency exits must have a minimum clear width of 1000 millimeters and be free of any obstructions.
(4) Facilities are required to conduct annual drills that specifically include protocols for assisting individuals with disabilities during emergencies, with a minimum of 3 drills per year, and records of these drills must be maintained for inspection for a period of 7 years.

heading: Accessible restrooms
text:
(1) All public and commercial facilities providing restrooms for public use must ensure at least one accessible restroom.
(2) Accessible restrooms must meet specified dimensions, including a minimum clear floor space of 1500mm by 1500mm, and be equipped with grab bars, accessible fixtures, and lever-operated controls.
(3) Signage indicating the location of accessible restrooms must be clear, legible, and include tactile characters and braille.
(4) For facilities with multiple restrooms, 20% of all restrooms must be accessible, up to a maximum of 5 accessible restrooms. The height of toilet seats in accessible restrooms must be between 430mm and 480mm from the floor, as measured to the top of the seat.

heading: Accessible restrooms
text:
(1) All public and commercial facilities providing restrooms for public use must ensure at least one accessible restroom.
(2) Accessible restrooms must meet specified dimensions, including a minimum clear floor space of 1600mm by 1600mm, and be equipped with grab bars, accessible fixtures, and lever-operated controls.
(3) Signage indicating the location of accessible restrooms must be clear, legible, and include tactile characters and braille.
(4) For facilities with multiple restrooms, 25% of all restrooms must be accessible, up to a maximum of 7 accessible restrooms. The height of toilet seats in accessible restrooms must be between 450mm and 500mm from the floor, as measured to the top of the seat.

heading: Ramps and slopes
text:
(1) Ramps installed in facilities must have a maximum slope ratio of 1:12, meaning for every 12 units of horizontal distance, there is a maximum of 1 unit of vertical rise.
(2) Ramps longer than 9 meters must include a level landing of at least 1500mm in length at intervals not exceeding 9 meters.
(3) Handrails must be provided on both sides of any ramp with a rise greater than 150mm or a horizontal projection greater than 1800mm, extending 300mm beyond the top and bottom of the ramp.
(4) The minimum clear width of a ramp shall be 915mm, and the surface must be firm, stable, and slip-resistant. A minimum of 2.5% of all entrances must be ramp-accessible, where a ramp is required.

heading: Doorways and entrances
text:
(1) All public entrances and doorways intended for general use must provide a clear opening width of at least 810 millimeters when the door is open 90 degrees.
(2) Doorways must be equipped with hardware that is easy to grasp with one hand and does not require tight grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist to operate.
(3) The threshold of an accessible doorway shall not exceed 13 millimeters in height and must be beveled.
(4) Automatic door openers are required for at least 50% of all main public entrances in facilities exceeding 1,000 square meters. The force required to open a door manually must not exceed 22 Newtons (5 pounds-force) for interior doors and 38 Newtons (8.5 pounds-force) for exterior doors.

heading: Doorways and entrances
text:
(1) All public entrances and doorways intended for general use must provide a clear opening width of at least 860 millimeters when the door is open 90 degrees.
(2) Doorways must be equipped with hardware that is easy to grasp with one hand and does not require tight grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist to operate.
(3) The threshold of an accessible doorway shall not exceed 10 millimeters in height and must be beveled.
(4) Automatic door openers are required for at least 75% of all main public entrances in facilities exceeding 800 square meters. The force required to open a door manually must not exceed 20 Newtons (4.5 pounds-force) for interior doors and 35 Newtons (7.8 pounds-force) for exterior doors.

heading: Signage and wayfinding
text:
(1) All permanent room and space identification signs must include tactile characters and braille.
(2) Directional signage to accessible features, such as restrooms and exits, must be clearly visible and strategically placed throughout the facility.
(3) The characters on signs must have a minimum height of 15 millimeters and a maximum height of 75 millimeters, with a high contrast ratio between the text and background.
(4) Overhead signs must be mounted at a minimum clear height of 2.1 meters (7 feet) to prevent head injuries. Pictograms used on signs must be universally recognizable symbols for accessibility and must be at least 150mm in height.

heading: Service counters and reception desks
text:
(1) Facilities providing service counters or reception desks must ensure that at least one section is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs.
(2) The accessible portion of the counter must have a maximum height of 860 millimeters from the floor and a clear knee space of at least 680 millimeters in height and 760 millimeters in width.
(3) Where multiple service points are available, at least 25% of all service counters must meet these accessibility requirements.
(4) In facilities with only one service counter, the entire counter must be accessible. These accessible sections must be clearly marked with the international symbol of access, and staff must be trained to offer assistance to individuals with accessibility needs, with a mandatory 2-hour training session annually.

heading: Accessible seating areas
text:
(1) Assembly areas, such as theaters, auditoriums, and waiting rooms, must provide a minimum of 1% of their total seating capacity as accessible seating locations.
(2) These accessible locations must be dispersed throughout the seating area to offer a choice of viewing angles and proximity to the stage or screen.
(3) Each accessible seating area must provide clear floor space of at least 915mm by 1220mm for a single wheelchair user.
(4) Companion seating must be provided adjacent to at least 50% of the accessible seating locations. For facilities with more than 500 seats, a minimum of 6 accessible seating locations are required, distributed across different price points if applicable.

heading: Communication accessibility
text:
(1) Public facilities shall provide communication access for individuals with hearing or visual impairments, where appropriate.
