(2) This may include providing TTY devices, sign language interpreters upon request with at least 48 hours notice, or materials in large print or braille.
(3) Websites and digital information portals maintained by public facilities must comply with internationally recognized web accessibility guidelines (WCAG 2.1 Level AA).
(4) Commercial facilities with annual revenues exceeding 5 million crowns are encouraged to provide similar communication accommodations, and 5% of their customer service staff must undergo basic training in assisting individuals with communication needs. Public announcement systems must ensure clear audio with minimal background noise.

heading: Maintenance of accessible features
text:
(1) All accessible features and equipment installed in facilities must be maintained in good working order at all times.
(2) This includes ensuring ramps are clear of snow and ice, elevators are functional, and accessible restrooms are clean and unobstructed.
(3) Any temporary disruption to an accessible feature must be immediately communicated to the public, with clear instructions on alternative accessible routes.
(4) Facilities must have a written maintenance plan for all accessible features, outlining weekly checks and annual servicing. Records of this maintenance plan and its execution must be kept for a period of 5 years and made available to inspectors upon request.

heading: Enforcement of orders
text:
(1) The Nordvale Accessibility Board may issue an order to a facility owner requiring specific actions to achieve compliance with this Act.
(2) An order shall specify the nature of the non-compliance, the required actions, and the deadline for completion.
(3) Failure to comply with an order may result in escalating penalties, including significant fines and, in extreme cases, legal action to compel compliance.
(4) All orders issued by the Board are legally binding. If an owner fails to comply, the Board may engage contractors to carry out the required work, with all costs being charged to the owner, plus an administrative fee of 20% of the total cost. This measure is a last resort, typically applied after 180 days of non-compliance and multiple warnings.

heading: Offenses by corporations
text:
(1) If a corporation commits an offense under this Act, any officer, director, or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted, or acquiesced in the offense is also guilty of the offense.
(2) Such individuals are liable to the penalties provided for in this Act, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.
(3) A corporation found guilty of repeated major non-compliance may face public listing on a 'Non-Compliant Facilities' register maintained by the Nordvale Accessibility Board for a minimum of 12 months.
(4) This public listing is intended to inform the general public and may affect the corporation's ability to obtain future permits or government contracts. The fine for a corporation's first offense of major non-compliance is 10,000 crowns, increasing to 25,000 crowns for subsequent offenses within a 3-year period.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister of Public Works may make regulations prescribing anything required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed.
(2) Regulations may include further details on accessibility standards, inspection procedures, penalty structures, and the composition and procedures of the Nordvale Accessibility Board.
(3) Before making any regulations, the Minister shall consult with the Nordvale Accessibility Board and conduct a 45-day public consultation period.
(4) All regulations must be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before they come into force, allowing for public awareness and compliance preparation. These regulations are designed to provide clarity and ensure the effective implementation of the Act across all municipalities, including Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Commencement
text:
(1) This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018.
(2) All facilities constructed or undergoing major renovations after this date must immediately comply with the provisions of this Act.
(3) Existing facilities not undergoing major renovations are granted a transitional period of five years from the commencement date to achieve full compliance with all applicable accessibility standards.
(4) During the transitional period, the Nordvale Accessibility Board will prioritize inspections of facilities with high public traffic or those that have received multiple public complaints, offering guidance and support to facilitate compliance rather than immediately imposing penalties for minor deficiencies. The full force of penalties will apply to all facilities after January 1, 2023.

heading: Hunting licence for smallholders
text:
(1) A smallholder who hunts only on the registered farmland that the smallholder farms pays 30 crowns for the annual hunting licence.
(2) The hunter's examination is still required.

heading: Hunting licence for smallholders
text:
(1) A smallholder who hunts only on the registered farmland that the smallholder farms pays 35 crowns for the annual hunting licence.
(2) The hunter's examination is still required.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation of all plumbing installation and repair work within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public health and safety by mandating permits for all such activities, thereby guaranteeing that all work adheres to established standards and is performed by qualified individuals. This scope covers both new constructions and modifications to existing plumbing systems, irrespective of the scale or complexity of the project. Compliance with this Act is compulsory for all residents, businesses, and organisations operating within the national borders of Nordvale. The provisions herein are designed to protect citizens from faulty workmanship and to maintain the integrity of our national infrastructure.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Plumbing work' refers to any installation, alteration, repair, maintenance, or replacement of pipes, fixtures, fittings, and other apparatus that transport water, wastewater, or other liquids within a building or property boundary.
(2) 'Permit' means a formal authorisation issued by the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA) in accordance with this Act.
(3) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity applying for a permit to perform plumbing work.
(4) 'Licensed Plumber' means a person holding a valid and current plumbing license issued by the Nordvale Crafts and Trades Board.
(5) 'Structure' includes any building, dwelling, or other permanent erection that contains plumbing systems requiring a permit.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall commence any plumbing installation or repair work without first obtaining a valid permit from the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA). This requirement applies to all projects, including minor repairs that involve opening or altering existing pipework, or any work affecting more than 10% of a building's water supply or drainage system. Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work may result in penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall commence any plumbing installation or repair work without first obtaining a valid permit from the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA). This requirement applies to all projects, including minor repairs that involve opening or altering existing pipework, or any work affecting more than 5% of a building's water supply or drainage system. Exemptions apply for simple fixture replacements that do not involve altering pipework. Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work may result in penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall commence any plumbing installation or repair work without first obtaining a valid permit from the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA). This requirement applies to all projects, including minor repairs that involve opening or altering existing pipework, or any work affecting more than 3% of a building's water supply or drainage system. Exemptions apply for simple fixture replacements that do not involve altering pipework. Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work may result in penalties as outlined in section 25, alongside potential remedial work orders.

heading: Application Procedure
text:
(1) Applications for plumbing permits must be submitted to the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA) in the municipality where the work is to be performed.
(2) The application must be made on the official form provided by the MPA.
(3) A complete application must include detailed plans and specifications of the proposed work.
(4) The application must be accompanied by the prescribed fee as detailed in section 8.

heading: Application Procedure
text:
(1) Applications for plumbing permits must be submitted to the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA) in the municipality where the work is to be performed, preferably through the online portal.
(2) The application must be made on the official form provided by the MPA.
(3) A complete application must include detailed plans and specifications of the proposed work, with a minimum of two scaled drawings.
(4) The application must be accompanied by the prescribed fee as detailed in section 8. Incomplete applications will be rejected after 5 business days if not rectified.

heading: Application Submission Deadline
text: All permit applications must be submitted at least 15 business days prior to the intended start date of the plumbing work. This period allows for adequate review and processing by the Municipal Plumbing Authority. Applications submitted with less than 15 business days' notice may not be processed in time for the desired start date, and no expedited processing is guaranteed.

heading: Application Submission Deadline
text: All permit applications must be submitted at least 10 business days prior to the intended start date of the plumbing work. This period allows for adequate review and processing by the Municipal Plumbing Authority. Applications submitted with less than 10 business days' notice may not be processed in time for the desired start date, and no expedited processing is guaranteed. For complex projects, a 20-business-day lead time is strongly recommended.

heading: Supporting Documentation
text:
(1) Each application must include a site plan indicating the location of the proposed work within the property boundaries.
(2) Detailed drawings of the plumbing system, including pipe sizes, materials, and fixture locations, must be provided.
(3) Proof of a valid plumbing license for the primary plumber overseeing the work must be attached.
(4) A schedule outlining the estimated duration of the project, not exceeding 120 days, must be submitted.

heading: Supporting Documentation
text:
(1) Each application must include a site plan indicating the location of the proposed work within the property boundaries, drawn to a scale of 1:100 or larger.
(2) Detailed drawings of the plumbing system, including pipe sizes, materials, and fixture locations, must be provided, signed by the licensed plumber.
(3) Proof of a valid plumbing license for the primary plumber overseeing the work must be attached, with the license number clearly visible.
(4) A schedule outlining the estimated duration of the project, not exceeding 90 days for residential projects and 150 days for commercial projects, must be submitted.

heading: Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA) will review the submitted documents for compliance with Nordvale's plumbing codes and standards. This review process typically takes 7 business days for residential projects and up to 14 business days for commercial projects. The MPA may request additional information or modifications to the plans if deemed necessary to ensure public safety and adherence to regulations.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) A standard application fee of 300 crowns is required for all residential plumbing permits.
(2) For commercial plumbing permits, the application fee is 600 crowns.
(3) An additional inspection fee of 150 crowns per inspection is charged for each required inspection.
(4) Fees are non-refundable once the review process has commenced, even if the permit is denied.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) A standard application fee of 350 crowns is required for all residential plumbing permits.
(2) For commercial plumbing permits, the application fee is 700 crowns.
(3) An additional inspection fee of 175 crowns per inspection is charged for each required inspection.
(4) Fees are non-refundable once the review process has commenced, even if the permit is denied, unless the application is withdrawn within 24 hours of submission.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) A standard application fee of 400 crowns is required for all residential plumbing permits.
(2) For commercial plumbing permits, the application fee is 800 crowns.
(3) An additional inspection fee of 200 crowns per inspection is charged for each required inspection.
(4) Fees are non-refundable once the review process has commenced, even if the permit is denied, unless the application is withdrawn within 12 hours of submission. A 10% discount applies for online submissions.

heading: Permit Issuance
text: Upon satisfactory review and approval of the application, the Municipal Plumbing Authority (MPA) will issue a plumbing permit. The permit will clearly state the scope of authorized work, the location of the project, the name of the licensed plumber, and the validity period. The permit must be conspicuously displayed at the project site throughout the duration of the plumbing work.

heading: Validity of Permit
text:
(1) A plumbing permit is valid for a period of 180 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If the work is not completed within this period, the permit will expire.
(3) An expired permit requires a new application and payment of all associated fees.
(4) Work commenced after permit expiration will be considered unpermitted work.

heading: Validity of Permit
text:
(1) A plumbing permit is valid for a period of 120 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If the work is not completed within this period, the permit will expire.
(3) An expired permit requires a new application and payment of all associated fees, with a 20% surcharge for reapplication within 30 days of expiration.
(4) Work commenced after permit expiration will be considered unpermitted work and subject to immediate cessation orders.

heading: Permit Extension
text:
(1) A single extension of a plumbing permit may be granted for an additional 90 days if requested in writing at least 15 days before the original expiry date.
(2) The applicant must provide a valid reason for the delay and pay an extension fee of 200 crowns.
(3) No further extensions will be granted; a new permit application will be required after one extension.

heading: Permit Extension
text:
(1) A single extension of a plumbing permit may be granted for an additional 60 days if requested in writing at least 20 days before the original expiry date.
(2) The applicant must provide a valid reason for the delay, backed by evidence where applicable, and pay an extension fee of 250 crowns.
(3) No further extensions will be granted; a new permit application will be required after one extension.

heading: Licensed Plumber Requirement
text: All plumbing work requiring a permit must be performed by, or directly supervised by, a licensed plumber. The licensed plumber's name and license number must be clearly indicated on the permit application and on the permit itself. Any work performed by an unlicensed individual without direct, continuous supervision by a licensed plumber will be deemed a violation of this Act.

heading: Owner's Responsibility
text: The property owner is ultimately responsible for ensuring that all plumbing work conducted on their property complies with this Act and all applicable plumbing codes. This includes verifying the plumber's license, obtaining necessary permits, and ensuring that required inspections are completed. Failure of the plumber to comply does not absolve the owner of their responsibilities.

heading: Work Standards
text: All plumbing installations and repairs must adhere to the current Nordvale Plumbing Code standards. This includes, but is not limited to, material specifications, pipe sizing, fixture installation, and adherence to established safety protocols. Any deviation from these standards without prior written approval from the Municipal Plumbing Authority will result in a failed inspection and a requirement for remedial work within 14 days.

heading: Work Standards
text: All plumbing installations and repairs must adhere to the current Nordvale Plumbing Code standards, which are updated annually on January 1st. This includes, but is not limited to, material specifications, pipe sizing, fixture installation, and adherence to established safety protocols. Any deviation from these standards without prior written approval from the Municipal Plumbing Authority will result in a failed inspection and a requirement for remedial work within 7 days. Repeated deviations may lead to further penalties.

heading: Required Inspections
text:
(1) A rough-in inspection is required before covering any plumbing work within walls or floors.
(2) A final inspection is required upon completion of all plumbing work and before the system is put into permanent use.
(3) Additional inspections may be required at the discretion of the Municipal Plumbing Authority based on the complexity of the project.

heading: Scheduling Inspections
text: Inspections must be scheduled with the Municipal Plumbing Authority at least 2 business days in advance. The licensed plumber or property owner must be present during all scheduled inspections. Failure to be present will result in a missed inspection, requiring rescheduling and potentially incurring an additional inspection fee.

heading: Scheduling Inspections
text: Inspections must be scheduled with the Municipal Plumbing Authority at least 3 business days in advance. The licensed plumber or property owner must be present during all scheduled inspections. Failure to be present will result in a missed inspection, requiring rescheduling and incurring an additional inspection fee of 150 crowns. Inspections for commercial projects require 5 business days' notice.

heading: Inspection Outcomes
text:
(1) If the plumbing work passes inspection, the Municipal Plumbing Authority inspector will issue an approval.
(2) If the work fails inspection, a written notice of deficiencies will be provided, outlining the required corrections.
(3) Corrected work must be re-inspected within 10 business days. A re-inspection fee applies.

heading: Re-inspection Fees
text: A re-inspection fee of 150 crowns will be charged for each subsequent inspection required to verify corrections made to previously failed work. This fee is payable prior to the re-inspection being scheduled. Repeated failures may result in further administrative charges or suspension of the permit.

heading: Re-inspection Fees
text: A re-inspection fee of 200 crowns will be charged for each subsequent inspection required to verify corrections made to previously failed work. This fee is payable prior to the re-inspection being scheduled. Repeated failures (more than two) may result in further administrative charges of 500 crowns or suspension of the permit for 30 days.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text:
(1) In cases of emergency repairs required to prevent property damage or public health hazards, work may commence immediately without a prior permit.
(2) A permit application for such emergency work must be submitted to the Municipal Plumbing Authority within 2 business days of the work commencing.
(3) All emergency work must still conform to Nordvale Plumbing Code standards and will be subject to inspection.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text:
(1) In cases of emergency repairs required to prevent immediate property damage or severe public health hazards, work may commence immediately without a prior permit.
(2) A permit application for such emergency work must be submitted to the Municipal Plumbing Authority within 1 business day of the work commencing, and clearly marked 'Emergency'.
(3) All emergency work must still conform to Nordvale Plumbing Code standards and will be subject to inspection within 48 hours of permit submission.

heading: Modifications to Approved Plans
text: Any significant deviation or modification from the approved plans and specifications must be submitted to the Municipal Plumbing Authority for review and approval before such modifications are implemented. Minor changes, not affecting structural integrity or code compliance, may proceed but must be documented for final inspection. A modification fee of 100 crowns may apply.

heading: Correction of Violations
text: If a violation of this Act or the Nordvale Plumbing Code is identified, the Municipal Plumbing Authority will issue a written notice to the property owner and the licensed plumber, detailing the violation and specifying a timeframe for correction. This timeframe will generally be 14 days, but may be shorter for urgent public safety concerns. Failure to correct violations within the specified time may result in further enforcement actions.

heading: Stop Work Orders
text: The Municipal Plumbing Authority has the power to issue a Stop Work Order for any plumbing work being conducted without a required permit, or for work that poses an immediate threat to public health or safety, or is in clear violation of the Nordvale Plumbing Code. A Stop Work Order must be obeyed immediately. Work may only resume once the conditions leading to the order have been rectified and approval for resumption has been granted.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Municipal Plumbing Authority may appeal that decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal.
(3) The Municipal Appeals Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days.
(4) The decision of the Municipal Appeals Board is final.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Municipal Plumbing Authority may appeal that decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 20 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and attaching all relevant documentation.
(3) The Municipal Appeals Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days.
(4) The decision of the Municipal Appeals Board is final and binding. An appeal fee of 500 crowns is required.

heading: Fines for Unpermitted Work
text: Any person or entity found to be performing plumbing work without a required permit shall be subject to a fine of 1,500 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 3,000 crowns. Each day that unpermitted work continues may be considered a separate offense. These fines are in addition to any costs associated with bringing the work into compliance or applying for a retroactive permit.

heading: Fines for Unpermitted Work
text: Any person or entity found to be performing plumbing work without a required permit shall be subject to a fine of 2,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 4,000 crowns. Each day that unpermitted work continues may be considered a separate offense, up to a maximum of 30 days. These fines are in addition to any costs associated with bringing the work into compliance or applying for a retroactive permit.

heading: Fines for Code Violations
text: Violations of the Nordvale Plumbing Code, even with a valid permit, will result in fines. A first offense for a minor code violation will incur a fine of 500 crowns. Major code violations, or repeat minor violations, will incur a fine of 1,000 crowns. These fines are levied in addition to the requirement to rectify the non-compliant work at the responsible party's expense.

heading: Penalties for Obstruction
text: Any person who obstructs or interferes with an inspector from the Municipal Plumbing Authority in the performance of their duties shall be liable to a fine of 2,000 crowns. This includes denying access to a project site where a permit has been issued or work is suspected of being performed without a permit. Repeat offenses may lead to additional fines and legal action.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text: The Municipal Plumbing Authority may revoke a plumbing permit if it is determined that false information was provided in the application, or if there is persistent and uncorrected non-compliance with the Nordvale Plumbing Code or the conditions of the permit. Revocation will be preceded by a written notice allowing 7 days for remediation, unless an immediate health or safety risk exists.

heading: Record Keeping
text: The Municipal Plumbing Authority is required to maintain a comprehensive record of all permit applications, issued permits, inspection reports, and enforcement actions for a minimum period of 10 years. These records shall be accessible to the public upon reasonable request, subject to data privacy regulations. This ensures transparency and accountability in the permitting process.

heading: Adoption of Plumbing Code
text:
(1) The Nordvale Plumbing Code, detailing specific technical requirements for all plumbing work, is hereby adopted by reference.
(2) The Nordvale Plumbing Code shall be reviewed and updated by the National Standards Committee every 3 years.
(3) The current version of the Nordvale Plumbing Code is available for public inspection at all Municipal Plumbing Authority offices and online.

heading: Adoption of Plumbing Code
text:
(1) The Nordvale Plumbing Code, detailing specific technical requirements for all plumbing work, is hereby adopted by reference.
(2) The Nordvale Plumbing Code shall be reviewed and updated by the National Standards Committee annually, with new versions taking effect on January 1st of each year.
(3) The current version of the Nordvale Plumbing Code is available for public inspection at all Municipal Plumbing Authority offices and online, with previous versions retained for historical reference.

heading: Repeal of Previous Regulations
text: All previous municipal ordinances, regulations, or resolutions pertaining to the permitting of plumbing installations and repairs are hereby repealed as of the effective date of this Act. This Act supersedes any conflicting local provisions to ensure a uniform national standard for plumbing work across Nordvale. Any permits issued prior to this Act remain valid until their expiration.

heading: Repeal of Previous Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: (1) If a person is a certified wine taster, that person has an additional thirty days to pay the market stall permit fee. (2) This extension applies only to the monthly permit fee.

heading: Reduced charges
text: No energy rebate is payable by any accredited sign-language interpreter for an additional 30 days after the standard payment date for the 350 crowns annual energy rebate.

heading: Title inscription duty for field clinicians
text:
(1) A certified field clinician who acquires a dwelling and makes it his or her residence within 90 days after the day the purchase contract takes effect pays the title inscription duty for that dwelling reduced by the percentage for category CW1 in the Civic Works Concession Schedule.
(2) The reduction is applied after any other reduction of that duty.

heading: Construction consent tariff: earlier applications
text:
(1) Where a certified field clinician seeks consent for a new structure that is to become his or her residence, the construction consent tariff is reduced by the percentage for category CW2 in the Civic Works Concession Schedule, whatever the floor space.
(2) The reduction is applied after any other reduction of that tariff.

heading: Construction consent tariff: earlier applications
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the fees and duties that a person pays to a municipality for registrations, licences, permits and copies of documents.
(2) This Act applies in every municipality of the Republic of Nordvale.
(3) Fees under this Act are paid in crowns to the municipality in which the person resides, unless a section provides otherwise.

heading: Payment of fees
text:
(1) A fee under this Act is paid to the municipality that issues the registration, licence, permit or copy.
(2) A fee may be paid by bank transfer, by card at a municipal office or through the municipal online service.
(3) A registration, licence or permit is not issued until the fee has been paid in full.

heading: Late payment surcharge
text:
(1) A person who pays an annual fee under this Act more than 30 days after it is due shall pay a surcharge of 10 percent of the fee.
(2) The surcharge is not charged when the fee is less than 5 crowns.

heading: Late payment surcharge
text:
(1) A person who pays an annual fee under this Act more than 30 days after it is due shall pay a surcharge of 15 percent of the fee.
(2) The surcharge is not charged when the fee is less than 5 crowns.

heading: Rounding of fees
text:
(1) A fee that is not a whole number of crowns is rounded to the nearest half crown.
(2) Rounding is applied only once, to the total amount payable on one fee notice.

heading: Refund of annual fees
text:
(1) A person who sells, scraps or loses a registered vehicle or animal before 1 July may apply for a refund of half of the annual fee paid for that year.
(2) No refund is made after 1 July of the year concerned.
(3) An application for a refund must be made within 60 days of the sale, scrapping or loss.

heading: Payment in instalments
text:
(1) A fee of more than 200 crowns may be paid in up to 4 equal instalments.
(2) The first instalment is due on the date the fee is due and each further instalment 3 months later.
(3) A fee of 200 crowns or less is paid in one amount.

heading: Fee notices
text:
(1) The municipality sends a fee notice for every annual fee at least 21 days before the fee is due.
(2) A fee notice states the fee, the section of this Act under which it is charged and the due date.
(3) A person who does not receive a fee notice is not excused from paying the fee.

heading: Review of fee amounts
text:
(1) The amounts of the fees under this Act are reviewed by the municipalities' joint fee board every 2 years.
(2) The board publishes its review by 30 September of the review year.
(3) A review does not change any fee; fees change only by amendment of this Act.

heading: Proof of payment
text:
(1) The municipality issues a receipt for every fee paid under this Act.
(2) A person shall keep the receipt for an annual fee for at least 2 years.
(3) An electronic receipt has the same effect as a paper receipt.

heading: Bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a bicycle without a motor shall pay an annual registration fee of 8 crowns.
(2) An owner under 18 years of age is exempt from the fee under subsection (1).
(3) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(4) This section does not apply to a bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.

heading: Bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a bicycle without a motor shall pay an annual registration fee of 10 crowns.
(2) An owner under 18 years of age is exempt from the fee under subsection (1).
(3) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(4) This section does not apply to a bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.

heading: Cargo bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a cargo bicycle without a motor shall pay an annual registration fee of 20 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(3) This section does not apply to a cargo bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.

heading: Cargo bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a cargo bicycle without a motor shall pay an annual registration fee of 25 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(3) This section does not apply to a cargo bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.

heading: Electric cargo bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of an electric bicycle built with a front or rear load box for carrying goods or children shall pay an annual registration fee of 36 crowns instead of the fee under section 14.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(3) This section does not apply to an electric cargo bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.

heading: Electric cargo bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of an electric bicycle built with a front or rear load box for carrying goods or children shall pay an annual registration fee of 45 crowns instead of the fee under section 14.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(3) This section does not apply to an electric cargo bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.
(4) Section 40 does not apply to a bicycle registered under this section.

heading: Electric scooter registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of an electric scooter shall pay an annual registration fee of 18 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(3) An electric scooter offered for public hire is registered under section 17.

heading: Electric scooter registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of an electric scooter shall pay an annual registration fee of 20 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(3) An electric scooter offered for public hire is registered under section 17.

heading: Electric bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of an electric bicycle shall pay an annual registration fee of 24 crowns.
(2) An owner under 18 years of age is exempt from the fee under subsection (1).
(3) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(4) This section does not apply to an electric bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.

heading: Electric bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of an electric bicycle shall pay an annual registration fee of 30 crowns.
(2) An owner under 18 years of age is exempt from the fee under subsection (1).
(3) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(4) This section does not apply to an electric bicycle used exclusively for commercial deliveries; such a bicycle is registered under section 15.

heading: Delivery bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a bicycle or electric bicycle used for commercial deliveries shall pay an annual registration fee of 55 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.

heading: Delivery bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a bicycle or electric bicycle used for commercial deliveries shall pay an annual registration fee of 70 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.

heading: Motorised bicycle registration fee
text:
(1) The owner of a bicycle fitted with an electric motor that is not an electric bicycle shall pay an annual registration fee of 60 crowns.
(2) The fee is due on registration and on each renewal on 1 January.
(3) No owner is exempt from the fee under subsection (1) by reason of age.

heading: Hire fleet registration fee
text:
(1) A business that offers bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters for public hire shall pay an annual registration fee of 12 crowns for each vehicle in its fleet.
(2) The fee is due on 1 January for the number of vehicles in the fleet on that day.
(3) A vehicle added to the fleet during the year is registered when it is added.

heading: Hire fleet registration fee
text:
(1) A business that offers bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters for public hire shall pay an annual registration fee of 15 crowns for each vehicle in its fleet.
(2) The fee is due on 1 January for the number of vehicles in the fleet on that day.
(3) A vehicle added to the fleet during the year is registered when it is added.

heading: Residential parking permit
text:
(1) A resident may apply for a residential parking permit for one car at an annual fee of 90 crowns.
(2) A second permit for the same household costs 180 crowns.

heading: Residential parking permit
text:
(1) A resident may apply for a residential parking permit for one car at an annual fee of 110 crowns.
(2) A second permit for the same household costs 220 crowns.

heading: Visitor parking permit
text:
(1) A resident may buy a visitor parking permit for a guest's car at a fee of 4 crowns per day.
(2) A resident may buy visitor parking permits for at most 30 days in a calendar year.
(3) A visitor parking permit is valid only in the street zone of the resident's address.

heading: Visitor parking permit
text:
(1) A resident may buy a visitor parking permit for a guest's car at a fee of 5 crowns per day.
(2) A resident may buy visitor parking permits for at most 30 days in a calendar year.
(3) A visitor parking permit is valid only in the street zone of the resident's address.

heading: Business parking permit
text:
(1) A business with premises in a residential parking zone may apply for a business parking permit for one vehicle at an annual fee of 300 crowns.
(2) A business may hold at most 3 business parking permits for the same premises.
(3) Each further permit costs the same as the first.

heading: Motorcycle parking permit
text:
(1) A resident may apply for a motorcycle parking permit for one motorcycle at an annual fee of 40 crowns.
(2) A motorcycle parking permit is valid only in marked motorcycle bays.

heading: Motorcycle parking permit
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Dog licence fee
text:
(1) The keeper of a dog older than 4 months shall pay an annual licence fee of 40 crowns per dog.
(2) For the second and each further dog kept in the same household the fee is 25 crowns per dog.

heading: Dog licence fee
text:
(1) The keeper of a dog older than 4 months shall pay an annual licence fee of 45 crowns per dog.
(2) For the second and each further dog kept in the same household the fee is 30 crowns per dog.

heading: Cat registration fee
text:
(1) The keeper of a cat older than 4 months shall pay an annual registration fee of 15 crowns per cat.
(2) For the second and each further cat kept in the same household the fee is 10 crowns per cat.

heading: Cat registration fee
text:
(1) The keeper of a cat older than 4 months shall pay an annual registration fee of 20 crowns per cat.
(2) For the second and each further cat kept in the same household the fee is 12 crowns per cat.

heading: Replacement dog tag fee
text:
(1) The keeper of a licensed dog who loses the dog's licence tag shall pay 8 crowns for a replacement tag.
(2) A replacement tag is issued free of charge if the tag was damaged and the damaged tag is returned.

heading: Dangerous dog surcharge
text:
(1) The keeper of a dog that the municipality has classified as dangerous shall pay a surcharge of 100 crowns per year in addition to the licence fee for that dog.
(2) The surcharge is due on the same day as the licence fee.
(3) The surcharge ends when the classification is lifted.

heading: Kennel licence fee
text:
(1) A person who keeps more than 6 dogs for breeding shall pay an annual kennel licence fee of 400 crowns.
(2) A kennel licence replaces the individual licence fees for the dogs kept at the kennel.
(3) The kennel must be inspected by the municipality before the first licence is issued.

heading: Horse keeping fee
text:
(1) A person who keeps a horse or pony within a municipality shall pay an annual keeping fee of 60 crowns per animal.
(2) The fee is due on 1 January or, for an animal acquired during the year, within 30 days of acquisition.

heading: Beehive registration fee
text:
(1) A beekeeper shall pay an annual registration fee of 3 crowns per hive.
(2) The total fee for one beekeeper is at most 60 crowns per year.
(3) The fee is due on 1 April for the hives kept on that day.

heading: Mobile street trading licence
text:
(1) A person who sells goods from a cart, van or bicycle in a public street shall pay a street trading fee of 20 crowns per trading day.
(2) Instead of the daily fee, the person may pay a monthly street trading fee of 250 crowns.
(3) This section applies only to goods other than food or drink sold from a van. Selling from a cart or a bicycle needs a licence under the Street Trading Act, except selling food or drink from a hand cart, which needs a permit under SBA §24. Selling food or drink from a motor vehicle needs a permit under SBA §21.

heading: Mobile street trading licence
text:
(1) A person who sells goods from a cart, van or bicycle in a public street shall pay a street trading fee of 25 crowns per trading day.
(2) Instead of the daily fee, the person may pay a monthly street trading fee of 300 crowns.
(3) This section applies only to goods other than food or drink sold from a van. Selling from a cart or a bicycle needs a licence under the Street Trading Act, except selling food or drink from a hand cart, which needs a permit under SBA §24. Selling food or drink from a motor vehicle needs a permit under SBA §21.

heading: Market stall permit fee
text:
(1) A person who sells goods from a stall at a municipal market shall pay a permit fee of 12 crowns per market day.
(2) Instead of the daily fee, the person may pay a monthly permit fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Cooked food supplement for market stalls
text:
(1) A person who sells cooked or hot food from a stall at a municipal market shall pay a supplement of 5 crowns per market day in addition to the fee under section 30.
(2) The supplement is not payable for days covered by a monthly permit under section 30(2) if a monthly supplement of 60 crowns has been paid.

heading: Cooked food supplement for market stalls
text:
(1) A person who sells cooked or hot food from a stall at a municipal market shall pay a supplement of 6 crowns per market day in addition to the fee under section 30.
(2) The supplement is not payable for days covered by a monthly permit under section 30(2) if a monthly supplement of 70 crowns has been paid.

heading: Seasonal market permit fee
text:
(1) A person who sells goods from a stall at a seasonal market organised by a municipality shall pay a permit fee of 20 crowns per market day.
(2) No monthly permit is available for a seasonal market.
(3) A seasonal market is held for at most 45 days in a calendar year.

heading: Street music permit fee
text:
(1) A person who plays music in a public street or square for donations shall hold a street music permit at a fee of 10 crowns per day.
(2) Instead of the daily fee, the person may buy a weekly permit for 50 crowns.
(3) Playing music through a loudspeaker also requires a permit under section 37.
(4) This section does not apply to music played as part of a cultural event that has a permit under the Cultural Events Act; such a performance is charged under CUL §5.

heading: Street music permit fee
text:
(1) A person who plays music in a public street or square for donations shall hold a street music permit at a fee of 12 crowns per day.
(2) Instead of the daily fee, the person may buy a weekly permit for 60 crowns.
(3) Playing music through a loudspeaker also requires a permit under section 37.
(4) This section does not apply to music played as part of a cultural event that has a permit under the Cultural Events Act; such a performance is charged under CUL §5.

heading: Street performance permit fee
text:
(1) A person who performs in a public street or square for donations, other than by playing music, shall hold a street performance permit at a fee of 8 crowns per day.
(2) Instead of the daily fee, the person may buy a weekly permit for 35 crowns.
(3) This section does not apply to a performance that is part of a cultural event that has a permit under the Cultural Events Act; such a performance is charged under CUL §5.

heading: Event permit fee
text:
(1) The organiser of a public event with up to 200 participants in a street, square or park shall pay an event permit fee of 40 crowns per event day.
(2) The application must be made at least 14 days before the event.
(3) This section does not apply to a cultural event within the meaning of CUL §1(4), which is charged under the Cultural Events Act.

heading: Event permit fee
text:
(1) The organiser of a public event with up to 200 participants in a street, square or park shall pay an event permit fee of 50 crowns per event day.
(2) The application must be made at least 14 days before the event.
(3) This section does not apply to a cultural event within the meaning of CUL §1(4), which is charged under the Cultural Events Act.

heading: Large event permit fee
text:
(1) The organiser of a public event with more than 200 participants in a street, square or park shall pay an event permit fee of 200 crowns per event day.
(2) For an event with more than 2,000 participants the fee is 500 crowns per event day.
(3) The application must be made at least 60 days before the event.
(4) This section does not apply to a cultural event within the meaning of CUL §1(4), which is charged under the Cultural Events Act.

heading: Sound amplification permit fee
text:
(1) A person who uses a loudspeaker or amplifier in a public street, square or park shall hold a sound amplification permit at a fee of 15 crowns per day.
(2) Amplified sound is permitted only between 10:00 and 21:00.

heading: Document copy fee
text:
(1) A person who requests a paper copy of a public document held by a municipality shall pay 1 crown per page.
(2) The first 10 pages of each request are free of charge.
(3) Electronic copies sent by email are free of charge.

heading: Document copy fee
text:
(1) A person who requests a paper copy of a public document held by a municipality shall pay 2 crowns per page.
(2) The first 10 pages of each request are free of charge.
(3) Electronic copies sent by email are free of charge.

heading: Certified copy fee
text:
(1) A person who requests a certified copy of a public document shall pay 10 crowns per document in addition to the copy fee under section 38.
(2) A certified copy is issued within 5 working days.

heading: Certified copy fee
text:
(1) A person who requests a certified copy of a public document shall pay 12 crowns per document in addition to the copy fee under section 38.
(2) A certified copy is issued within 5 working days.

heading: Transitional provision for bicycle fees
text:
(1) For an electric bicycle registered before 1 July 2026, the fee under section 14 as in force on 30 June 2026 continues to apply until the first renewal on or after 1 January 2027.
(2) Subsection (1) does not apply to bicycles registered under section 15.

heading: Civil register extract fee
text:
(1) A person who requests an extract from the civil register of births, marriages or deaths shall pay 15 crowns per extract.
(2) The first extract requested by a person about their own birth in a calendar year is free of charge.

heading: Civil ceremony fee
text:
(1) A couple who marry or register a partnership in a municipal hall shall pay a ceremony fee of 200 crowns on a weekday.
(2) The fee is 350 crowns for a ceremony on a Saturday or Sunday.
(3) No fee is payable for a ceremony held in the registrar's office with no more than 6 guests.

heading: Extra waste collection fee
text:
(1) A household that asks for an extra collection of household waste outside the regular schedule shall pay 20 crowns per collection.
(2) An extra collection is made within 3 working days of the request.

heading: Extra waste collection fee
text:
(1) A household that asks for an extra collection of household waste outside the regular schedule shall pay 25 crowns per collection.
(2) An extra collection is made within 3 working days of the request.

heading: Bulky waste collection fee
text:
(1) A household that asks for the collection of bulky items such as furniture or appliances shall pay 40 crowns per collection.
(2) One collection covers at most 3 items.
(3) Each further item costs 10 crowns.
(4) This section applies only to the collection of electrical and electronic appliances. The collection of other bulky waste, such as furniture, is governed by WSA §9.

heading: Allotment garden fee
text:
(1) A person who rents a municipal allotment garden plot shall pay an annual fee of 80 crowns per plot.
(2) A person may rent at most 2 plots.
(3) The fee is due on 1 March.

heading: Bicycles used for deliveries and hire
text:
(1) A bicycle or electric bicycle is registered under section 15 only if it is used exclusively for commercial deliveries; a bicycle that is also used for other purposes is registered under section 10, 11, 12 or 14.
(2) A vehicle registered under section 17 is not registered under section 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 or 16.
(3) Of the fees under this Act, the reduction for full-time students in SSA §7 applies only to the fee under section 14 and the fee under section 22.
(4) A bicycle fitted with an electric motor that is not an electric bicycle is registered under section 16 even if it is used for commercial deliveries.

heading: Rounding of reduced fees
text:
(1) Section 4 also applies to a fee that another Act reduces, such as the half fee under SSA §7; a reduced fee of 22.50 crowns, for example, stays 22.50 crowns and is not rounded to a whole crown.
(2) INT §5(3) does not apply to a fee under this Act.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing and regulation of businesses engaged in the sale, transfer, and repair of firearms within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety and maintain a transparent and controlled system for firearm commerce. The provisions of this Act apply to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definition of 'Firearm Dealer'
text: For the purposes of this Act, a 'firearm dealer' means any individual, partnership, or corporation that engages in the business of selling, leasing, or repairing firearms. This includes entities that sell more than 5 firearms or conduct more than 10 firearm repairs within any 12-month period. An entity that merely stores firearms without engaging in sales or repairs is not considered a firearm dealer.

heading: Licence Requirement
text:
(1) No person shall operate as a firearm dealer without a valid licence issued by the Ministry of Public Order.
(2) A separate licence is required for each physical business location where firearm dealing activities are conducted. A single licence cannot cover multiple premises, even if they are within 100 meters of each other.

heading: Application for Licence
text: An application for a firearm dealer licence must be submitted to the Ministry of Public Order on the prescribed form. The application must include full identification details of all principals, proof of business registration, and a detailed security plan for the premises. A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns must accompany the submission. Incomplete applications will be rejected within 14 days.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text:
(1) An applicant must be at least 21 years of age.
(2) The applicant must be a citizen of Nordvale or a permanent resident for at least 5 years.
(3) The applicant must not have a criminal record involving violent offenses or offenses related to firearms within the last 15 years.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text:
(1) An applicant must be at least 23 years of age.
(2) The applicant must be a citizen of Nordvale or a permanent resident for at least 7 years.
(3) The applicant must not have a criminal record involving violent offenses or offenses related to firearms within the last 20 years.

heading: Licence Fee
text: Upon approval of a licence application, the applicant shall pay an initial licence fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the first 24 months of operation. Failure to pay the fee within 30 days of approval notification will result in the forfeiture of the approval.

heading: Licence Fee
text: Upon approval of a licence application, the applicant shall pay an initial licence fee of 18,000 crowns. This fee covers the first 24 months of operation. Failure to pay the fee within 21 days of approval notification will result in the forfeiture of the approval.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A firearm dealer licence is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date of the current licence. The renewal fee is 10,000 crowns. Late renewal applications, submitted between 30 and 59 days before expiry, incur an additional 2,500 crowns penalty.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A firearm dealer licence is valid for a period of 36 months from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiry date of the current licence. The renewal fee is 12,000 crowns. Late renewal applications, submitted between 45 and 89 days before expiry, incur an additional 3,000 crowns penalty.

heading: Security Requirements for Premises
text:
(1) Licensed premises must be equipped with a robust alarm system monitored 24 hours a day.
(2) All firearms must be stored in a secured vault or safe when the premises are closed. The vault must have steel walls at least 5 mm thick.
(3) Access to firearms must be restricted to authorized personnel only, with at least two distinct security measures in place.

heading: Security Requirements for Premises
text:
(1) Licensed premises must be equipped with a robust alarm system monitored 24 hours a day, directly linked to a security firm.
(2) All firearms must be stored in a secured vault or safe when the premises are closed. The vault must have steel walls at least 8 mm thick and a fire rating of at least 60 minutes.
(3) Access to firearms must be restricted to authorized personnel only, with at least three distinct security measures in place, including biometric access.

heading: Inventory Records
text: Every firearm dealer must maintain accurate and up-to-date inventory records of all firearms acquired, sold, transferred, or repaired. These records must include the make, model, serial number, and calibre of each firearm, as well as the date of transaction and the full details of the other party involved. Records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years.

heading: Reporting of Transactions
text: All sales or transfers of firearms must be reported to the Ministry of Public Order within 48 hours of the transaction. The report must include all details from the inventory records as specified in section 9. Failure to report a transaction within this timeframe may result in a fine of 500 crowns per day of delay, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Lost or Stolen Firearms
text: A firearm dealer must report any loss or theft of a firearm from their inventory or premises to the Ministry of Public Order and the local police within 24 hours of discovery. The report must include all available details of the missing firearm, including its serial number. Failure to report within this period may incur a penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Inspection of Premises and Records
text:
(1) Authorised officers of the Ministry of Public Order may inspect a licensed firearm dealer's premises and records during regular business hours without prior notice.
(2) Such inspections are conducted to ensure compliance with this Act and may occur at least once every 18 months. Refusal to permit an inspection is a serious offence.

heading: Inspection of Premises and Records
text:
(1) Authorised officers of the Ministry of Public Order may inspect a licensed firearm dealer's premises and records during regular business hours without prior notice, at least once every 12 months.
(2) Refusal to permit an inspection is a serious offence and may lead to immediate suspension of the licence.

heading: Training Requirements for Staff
text: All staff directly involved in firearm sales or repairs must undergo certified training on firearm safety, legal regulations, and secure handling procedures. This training must be refreshed every 3 years. Proof of current certification for all relevant staff must be available for inspection at all times.

heading: Display of Licence
text: The firearm dealer licence must be prominently displayed in a visible location at the licensed premises, accessible to all customers. The licence must be easily readable from a distance of 1.5 meters. Failure to display the licence may result in an administrative fine of 250 crowns.

heading: Sale to Unlicensed Individuals
text: No firearm dealer shall sell or transfer a firearm to any individual who does not possess a valid firearm permit issued by the Ministry of Public Order. The dealer must verify the permit's authenticity and record its details. Selling to an unlicensed individual carries a penalty of up to 50,000 crowns and potential licence revocation.

heading: Age Restriction for Purchases
text: A firearm dealer shall not sell any firearm to a person under the age of 18 years. For certain categories of firearms, such as rifles, the minimum age is 20 years. Verification of age must be conducted using official identification documents. Violation of this section may lead to a fine of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Record of Repairs
text: Firearm dealers engaging in repairs must maintain a detailed log of all repair services, including the date of repair, the nature of the repair, and the identity of the firearm owner. These records must be kept for a minimum of 7 years and be available for inspection upon request.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Ministry of Public Order may suspend a firearm dealer's licence for a period not exceeding 90 days if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the dealer has violated any provision of this Act, or if public safety is at immediate risk.
(2) The dealer will be notified in writing within 5 days of the suspension.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Ministry of Public Order may suspend a firearm dealer's licence for a period not exceeding 180 days if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the dealer has violated any provision of this Act, or if public safety is at immediate risk.
(2) The dealer will be notified in writing within 3 days of the suspension, stating the reasons.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) A firearm dealer's licence may be revoked by the Ministry of Public Order for serious or repeated violations of this Act, fraudulent activities, or conviction for a serious crime.
(2) Before revocation, the dealer will be given 30 days to respond to the allegations in writing. A hearing may be convened if requested by the dealer.

heading: Surrender of Licence
text:
(1) A licensed firearm dealer may voluntarily surrender their licence by providing written notice to the Ministry of Public Order at least 60 days in advance.
(2) Upon surrender, all remaining firearms in inventory must be transferred to another licensed dealer or surrendered to the authorities within 90 days. A plan for firearm disposal must be submitted.

heading: Surrender of Licence
text:
(1) A licensed firearm dealer may voluntarily surrender their licence by providing written notice to the Ministry of Public Order at least 45 days in advance.
(2) Upon surrender, all remaining firearms in inventory must be transferred to another licensed dealer or surrendered to the authorities within 60 days. A detailed plan for firearm disposal must be submitted and approved within 30 days of the notice.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any applicant or licensee aggrieved by a decision of the Ministry of Public Order regarding a licence application, suspension, or revocation may appeal to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal within 45 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding, subject to judicial review as per general administrative law.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Operation
text: Any person operating as a firearm dealer without a valid licence commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to 100,000 crowns, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or both. Each day of unlicensed operation may be considered a separate offence.

heading: Prohibition on Specific Firearm Types
text: Firearm dealers are prohibited from selling, transferring, or repairing any firearm that is classified as a prohibited weapon by the Nordvale Prohibited Weapons Act. This includes automatic weapons and certain high-capacity magazines. Violations carry severe penalties including licence revocation and criminal charges.

heading: Advertisement Restrictions
text: Advertisements for firearms must include a clear disclaimer stating that a valid permit is required for purchase. Advertisements must not target individuals under 18 years of age or promote irresponsible use of firearms. Violation of this section may lead to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Change of Ownership
text: Any change in the ownership or controlling interest of a licensed firearm dealership must be reported to the Ministry of Public Order within 30 days. The new owners must meet all eligibility criteria as specified in section 5. A failure to report may lead to licence suspension.

heading: Change of Ownership
text: Any change in the ownership or controlling interest of a licensed firearm dealership must be reported to the Ministry of Public Order within 14 days. The new owners must meet all eligibility criteria as specified in section 5, and undergo a full background check. A failure to report may lead to licence revocation.

heading: Relocation of Premises
text: A licensed firearm dealer wishing to relocate their premises must submit a new application for a licence for the new location at least 90 days before the intended move. The new premises must meet all security requirements as per section 8. The existing licence remains valid for the old premises until the new one is approved.

heading: Compliance with Local Ordinances
text: In addition to complying with this Act, all firearm dealers must adhere to any relevant local ordinances enacted by their respective municipalities, such as Aldmark, Brenholt, or Corvik. These ordinances may include specific zoning requirements or local operating restrictions. Dealers are responsible for understanding and following local regulations.

heading: Indemnity and Liability
text: A licensed firearm dealer shall maintain adequate liability insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 500,000 crowns, to cover potential damages arising from their operations. The Republic of Nordvale and its ministries are not liable for any losses or damages incurred by a firearm dealer or their customers.

heading: Indemnity and Liability
text: A licensed firearm dealer shall maintain adequate liability insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 750,000 crowns, to cover potential damages arising from their operations. Proof of insurance must be provided annually. The Republic of Nordvale and its ministries are not liable for any losses or damages incurred by a firearm dealer or their customers.

heading: Ministerial Directives
text: The Ministry of Public Order may issue directives from time to time to clarify or supplement the provisions of this Act. Such directives shall be published and distributed to all licensed firearm dealers within 15 days of their promulgation. Dealers must comply with these directives within 30 days of receipt.

heading: Ministerial Directives
text: The Ministry of Public Order may issue directives from time to time to clarify or supplement the provisions of this Act. Such directives shall be published and distributed to all licensed firearm dealers within 7 days of their promulgation. Dealers must comply with these directives within 21 days of receipt, unless otherwise specified.
