text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: Each certified wine taster pays 25 percent less of the one-off birth grant paid for each child born in Nordvale.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered saddler shall pay a delivery bicycle registration fee of 52 crowns and 50 öre.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the regular inspection and certification of all fire extinguishers within commercial and public premises across the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety by maintaining functional fire suppression equipment. This includes setting standards for inspection frequency, qualifications of inspectors, and penalties for non-compliance, thereby reducing the risk of fire-related incidents and protecting lives and property within Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act applies to any building accessible to the public or used for commercial activities, regardless of its size or number of occupants.

heading: General Requirement for Fire Extinguishers
text: All commercial and public premises within Nordvale must be equipped with an adequate number of properly maintained and certified fire extinguishers. The quantity and type of extinguishers required shall be determined based on the size and nature of the premises, as further detailed in section 4. Failure to have the requisite number of extinguishers can result in a fine of 500 crowns for each missing unit, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns per premises per inspection cycle.

heading: Minimum Number of Extinguishers
text:
(1) Commercial premises with a floor area of up to 100 square meters must have at least one fire extinguisher.
(2) For every additional 100 square meters or part thereof, an additional fire extinguisher is required, up to a maximum of 20 units. 
(3) Public premises, due to higher occupancy, require one fire extinguisher for every 75 square meters of floor area, with a minimum of two extinguishers, regardless of size. The types of extinguishers must be appropriate for the potential fire hazards present.

heading: Minimum Number of Extinguishers
text:
(1) Commercial premises with a floor area of up to 120 square meters must have at least one fire extinguisher.
(2) For every additional 90 square meters or part thereof, an additional fire extinguisher is required, up to a maximum of 25 units. 
(3) Public premises, due to higher occupancy, require one fire extinguisher for every 60 square meters of floor area, with a minimum of three extinguishers, regardless of size. The types of extinguishers must be appropriate for the potential fire hazards present, as determined by a certified inspector.

heading: Inspection Frequency
text: All fire extinguishers on commercial and public premises must undergo a thorough inspection by a certified professional at least once every 12 months. This annual inspection ensures the extinguisher is fully functional, properly charged, and free from damage or obstruction. Records of these inspections must be kept on site for a minimum of 3 years and made available upon request to any authorized enforcement officer. An overdue inspection by more than 30 days will incur a penalty of 200 crowns per extinguisher.

heading: Inspection Frequency
text: All fire extinguishers on commercial and public premises must undergo a thorough inspection by a certified professional at least once every 10 months. This inspection ensures the extinguisher is fully functional, properly charged, and free from damage or obstruction. Records of these inspections must be kept on site for a minimum of 4 years and made available upon request to any authorized enforcement officer. An overdue inspection by more than 20 days will incur a penalty of 250 crowns per extinguisher, up to a maximum of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Inspection Frequency
text: All fire extinguishers on commercial and public premises must undergo a thorough inspection by a certified professional at least once every 9 months. This inspection ensures the extinguisher is fully functional, properly charged, and free from damage or obstruction. Records of these inspections must be kept on site for a minimum of 5 years and made available upon request to any authorized enforcement officer. An overdue inspection by more than 15 days will incur a penalty of 300 crowns per extinguisher, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns, and may result in further enforcement action.

heading: Monthly Visual Checks
text: In addition to the professional inspection, a responsible person on the premises must conduct a visual check of each fire extinguisher at least once every 30 days. This check should confirm that the extinguisher is in its designated location, accessible, the tamper seal is intact, and the pressure gauge (if applicable) is in the operating range. A logbook detailing these monthly checks must be maintained and produced upon request. Failure to maintain such a logbook for a period exceeding 60 days will result in a fine of 150 crowns.

heading: Certification Markings
text: Upon successful completion of a professional inspection, each fire extinguisher must be affixed with a visible certification tag or sticker. This tag must clearly indicate the date of inspection, the name or identification number of the certified inspector, and the date of the next scheduled inspection. The tag must be durable and resistant to fading, with dimensions of at least 5 cm by 3 cm. Any extinguisher found without a valid, current certification marking will be considered non-compliant and subject to immediate remedial action.

heading: Qualifications of Inspectors
text:
(1) Fire extinguisher inspections must only be carried out by individuals who hold a valid certification from the National Fire Safety Authority (NFSA).
(2) To obtain certification, an individual must complete a NFSA-approved training course, pass a written examination with a score of at least 80%, and demonstrate practical proficiency in inspecting various types of fire extinguishers. 
(3) Certification must be renewed every 3 years, requiring a refresher course and re-examination to ensure continued competence and knowledge of current standards. Inspectors must be at least 21 years of age.

heading: Inspector Responsibilities
text: Certified inspectors are responsible for thoroughly examining every component of a fire extinguisher, including the nozzle, hose, pressure gauge, pin, and cylinder. They must verify the extinguisher's charge, check for corrosion or damage, and ensure proper labeling and mounting. After inspection, they must issue a detailed report to the premises owner, outlining any deficiencies and recommended actions. A copy of this report must also be submitted to the NFSA within 7 days of the inspection. Any false or misleading report can result in the revocation of an inspector's certification.

heading: Reporting Deficiencies
text: Should an inspection reveal any deficiencies that compromise the effectiveness or safety of a fire extinguisher, the inspector must immediately notify the premises owner. The owner is then required to take corrective action within 14 days of receiving the report. This may involve repair, recharging, or replacement of the faulty unit. Failure to rectify significant deficiencies within this timeframe will result in a penalty of 750 crowns per deficient extinguisher, plus an additional 50 crowns for each day the deficiency remains unaddressed beyond the 14-day period.

heading: Replacement of Defective Extinguishers
text: Any fire extinguisher deemed unrepairable or unsafe by a certified inspector must be immediately removed from service and replaced with a new, compliant unit within 7 days. The old extinguisher must be disposed of in accordance with environmental regulations, ensuring safe handling of its contents. The replacement unit must be of the appropriate type and rating for the premises and must undergo an initial certification inspection within 30 days of installation. Failure to replace a condemned extinguisher within the specified timeframe will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Installation Requirements
text: Fire extinguishers must be installed in readily accessible locations, free from obstructions, and positioned so that the carrying handle is no more than 1.5 meters (approximately 60 inches) from the floor. They should be mounted on hangers or in cabinets, ensuring they are protected from physical damage. Extinguishers must be located along normal paths of travel and clearly marked with appropriate signage, visible from a distance of at least 5 meters. The minimum distance between any two extinguishers should not exceed 20 meters.

heading: Signage and Labeling
text: Each fire extinguisher location must be clearly indicated by a sign or symbol easily understood by all occupants. This signage must be at least 20 cm by 20 cm and feature a universally recognized pictogram of a fire extinguisher. Additionally, each extinguisher must bear a label detailing its type (e.g., water, foam, powder), its fire class rating, and simple operating instructions. This label should be in the common language of Nordvale, be at least 10 cm by 5 cm, and remain legible for the life of the extinguisher.

heading: Training for Staff
text: Owners of commercial and public premises must ensure that at least 25% of their staff, or a minimum of two individuals, whichever is greater, receive basic training in the proper use of fire extinguishers. This training should be conducted annually and cover the 'PASS' method (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep) and recognition of different fire classes. Records of staff training, including dates and attendees, must be maintained on site for 2 years. Failure to provide adequate training can result in a fine of 300 crowns per missing trained staff member.

heading: Maintenance of Records
text: All records pertaining to fire extinguisher inspections, maintenance, repairs, and staff training must be meticulously maintained on the premises for a minimum period of 3 years. These records must be presented to any authorized enforcement officer upon request within 24 hours. Failure to produce requested records or presenting incomplete records will result in an administrative penalty of 250 crowns for each instance of non-compliance. Digital records are acceptable provided they are readily accessible and verifiable.

heading: Maintenance of Records
text: All records pertaining to fire extinguisher inspections, maintenance, repairs, and staff training must be meticulously maintained on the premises for a minimum period of 5 years. These records must be presented to any authorized enforcement officer upon request within 12 hours. Failure to produce requested records or presenting incomplete records will result in an administrative penalty of 350 crowns for each instance of non-compliance. Digital records are acceptable provided they are readily accessible, verifiable, and backed up off-site to prevent loss.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The National Fire Safety Authority (NFSA) is designated as the primary enforcement body for this Act. NFSA officers have the authority to conduct unannounced inspections of commercial and public premises to verify compliance with all provisions herein. They may demand to see records, inspect equipment, and interview staff. Any obstruction of an NFSA officer in the performance of their duties will result in a significant penalty of 2,000 crowns and potential further legal action.

heading: Right of Entry
text:
(1) For the purpose of enforcing this Act, an authorized officer of the NFSA may, at any reasonable time, enter any commercial or public premises without a warrant.
(2) Prior notice of entry is not required, but officers must present official identification upon arrival.
(3) Entry will not be refused if the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that a violation of this Act is occurring or has occurred. Any refusal of entry will be met with immediate legal action and a penalty of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Compliance Orders
text: If, during an inspection, an NFSA officer identifies non-compliance with any section of this Act, they may issue a written compliance order to the premises owner. This order will detail the specific violations and specify a timeframe, typically between 7 and 30 days depending on the severity, within which the deficiencies must be corrected. Failure to comply with a compliance order within the stipulated timeframe will result in escalating fines and potential closure of the premises until compliance is achieved. A daily penalty of 100 crowns applies for each day beyond the deadline.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found in violation of this Act shall be subject to administrative fines as specified in relevant sections. 
(2) Initial violations may incur fines ranging from 200 crowns to 2,000 crowns, depending on the severity of the breach.
(3) Repeated violations of the same provision within a 24-month period will result in doubled fines for the second offense, and tripled fines for a third offense, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. Persistent non-compliance may lead to legal proceedings.

heading: Appeal Process
text:
(1) A premises owner who receives a compliance order or fine may appeal the decision to the NFSA Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the notice. 
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by a non-refundable filing fee of 100 crowns. 
(3) The Tribunal will review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the NFSA Appeals Tribunal is final and binding. No further appeals are available through judicial channels.

heading: Prohibition on Tampering
text: No person shall intentionally tamper with, remove, or render inoperative any fire extinguisher required by this Act, or any part thereof, including its seal, label, or mounting. This includes using an extinguisher for purposes other than immediate fire suppression, unless specifically authorized for training. Any individual or entity found to have tampered with a fire extinguisher will face a substantial penalty of 2,500 crowns per incident, and may be subject to criminal charges if serious harm or damage results from such actions.

heading: Clearance Around Extinguishers
text: A clear space of at least 1 meter (approximately 40 inches) in all directions must be maintained around every fire extinguisher, ensuring immediate and unimpeded access during an emergency. This area must not be used for storage of goods, waste, or any other items that could obstruct access or visibility. Any obstruction found during an inspection will result in a immediate fine of 400 crowns per obstructed unit. Repeat offenses will incur higher penalties of 600 crowns.

heading: Clearance Around Extinguishers
text: A clear space of at least 1.2 meters (approximately 48 inches) in all directions must be maintained around every fire extinguisher, ensuring immediate and unimpeded access during an emergency. This area must not be used for storage of goods, waste, or any other items that could obstruct access or visibility. Any obstruction found during an inspection will result in a immediate fine of 550 crowns per obstructed unit. Repeat offenses within 12 months will incur higher penalties of 800 crowns per unit.

heading: Protection from Damage
text: Fire extinguishers must be protected from potential physical damage, including being struck by moving equipment or vehicles, exposure to extreme temperatures, or corrosive environments. Where necessary, protective cabinets or enclosures must be installed. The enclosure must be easily opened without special tools. Extinguishers located in areas susceptible to freezing must be of a type designed for low temperatures or housed in heated cabinets. Failure to adequately protect an extinguisher can result in a fine of 600 crowns per unprotected unit.

heading: Availability During Operating Hours
text: All required fire extinguishers must be readily available and accessible at all times when the commercial or public premises are open for business or otherwise occupied. This means they must not be locked away, removed for extended periods, or rendered unusable during operating hours. A breach of this section, such as an extinguisher being locked in a cabinet without immediate key access, will result in a fine of 800 crowns per inaccessible unit during operational hours.

heading: Exemptions
text: Small commercial premises, defined as those with a total floor area of less than 50 square meters and with no more than 5 employees present at any given time, may be exempt from the requirement for monthly visual checks, provided they undergo professional inspections every 6 months. To qualify for this exemption, premises owners must formally apply to the NFSA and demonstrate low fire risk through a detailed assessment. This exemption does not apply to any public premises. The application fee for this exemption is 120 crowns.

heading: Public Awareness Campaign
text: The National Fire Safety Authority (NFSA) shall conduct annual public awareness campaigns to educate businesses and the public about the importance of fire extinguisher maintenance and proper usage. These campaigns will utilize various media channels, including leaflets distributed in municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik, and public service announcements. The NFSA will allocate a minimum of 50,000 crowns annually for these initiatives, aiming to reach at least 70% of the adult population in Nordvale.

heading: Record Keeping by NFSA
text: The NFSA shall maintain a central database of all certified fire extinguishers, inspection records, and compliance orders issued across Nordvale. This database will include information from all municipalities, including Brenholt, Dunmere, and Elsby. Data will be retained for a minimum of 10 years for each premises. This ensures comprehensive oversight and allows for trend analysis of compliance rates and common deficiencies. Access to this database will be restricted to authorized NFSA personnel only, for data protection purposes.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, and ensure it remains relevant to current fire safety standards and technological advancements. The first review will take place no later than January 1, 2029. The NFSA will submit a comprehensive report to Parliament outlining the impact of the Act, including statistics on compliance and fire incidents. Public consultations will be held in at least 3 major municipalities during the review process.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All information gathered by NFSA officers or certified inspectors during the course of their duties, particularly sensitive business data or personal information, must be treated with strict confidentiality. This information shall only be used for the purposes of enforcing this Act and shall not be disclosed to unauthorized third parties. Any breach of confidentiality by an NFSA officer or certified inspector will result in severe disciplinary action, including potential termination of employment or revocation of certification, and may lead to legal prosecution.

heading: Obstruction of Justice
text: Any person who obstructs, hinders, or interferes with an authorized officer of the NFSA or a certified inspector in the performance of their duties under this Act commits an offense. This includes providing false information, concealing relevant documents, or physically impeding access to premises or equipment. An offense under this section carries a mandatory fine of 3,000 crowns for a first offense and 6,000 crowns for any subsequent offense within a 5-year period. Serious obstruction may also result in immediate suspension of business operations.

heading: Coming into Force
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2024. All provisions and requirements shall be effective from this date, and premises owners will have a grace period of 90 days to achieve initial compliance with all new or amended regulations. During this grace period, only warnings will be issued for minor non-compliance, but serious safety breaches will be subject to immediate penalties. The NFSA will publish detailed guidance notes 60 days prior to the effective date to assist businesses in preparation.

heading: Repeal of Previous Regulations
text: The 'Fire Safety Equipment Ordinance of Nordvale, 2005' and all its subsequent amendments are hereby repealed upon the coming into force of this Act. Any regulations or directives issued under that ordinance that are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act are also repealed. However, any fines or penalties incurred under the previous ordinance prior to the effective date of this Act remain valid and enforceable. This new Act supersedes all previous legislation concerning fire extinguisher inspections in commercial and public premises.

heading: Repeal of Previous Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Delivered meals at high altitude
text:
(1) An elder whose residence is in a highland settlement lying 800 metres or more above sea level pays no fee for hot meals delivered to the home.
(2) An elder in any other highland settlement pays the ordinary fee for delivered meals.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the mandatory registration of specific categories of farm equipment within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to enhance identification, deter theft, and facilitate the recovery of stolen machinery. It also aims to improve safety standards by ensuring all registered equipment meets minimum operational requirements. The scope of this Act extends to all agricultural enterprises operating within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, encompassing both individual farmers and corporate entities engaged in agricultural production.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Farm equipment' means any machine, implement, or vehicle primarily designed and used for agricultural operations, including but not limited to tractors, combine harvesters, and irrigation systems, as specified in Schedule A.
(2) 'Registrar' refers to the official appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture to administer the registration process and maintain the national register of farm equipment.
(3) 'Owner' means the person or entity legally possessing the farm equipment and responsible for its operation and maintenance, or their duly authorized agent.

heading: Mandatory Registration
text: All farm equipment, as defined in section 2 and listed in Schedule A, must be registered with the Registrar. This mandatory registration applies to equipment with an engine power exceeding 25 horsepower or a total weight exceeding 1,000 kilograms. New equipment acquired after the commencement of this Act must be registered within 30 days of purchase or import into Nordvale. Failure to register within the stipulated period may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. The registration process requires submission of detailed equipment specifications and ownership documentation.

heading: Mandatory Registration
text: All farm equipment, as defined in section 2 and listed in Schedule A, must be registered with the Registrar. This mandatory registration applies to equipment with an engine power exceeding 30 horsepower or a total weight exceeding 1,200 kilograms. New equipment acquired after the commencement of this version of the Act must be registered within 20 days of purchase or import into Nordvale. Failure to register within the stipulated period may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. The registration process requires submission of detailed equipment specifications and ownership documentation.

heading: Exemptions from Registration
text: Certain types of farm equipment are exempt from the mandatory registration requirements under this Act. These exemptions include hand-held tools, equipment with an engine power below 25 horsepower, and equipment with a total weight under 1,000 kilograms. Additionally, equipment exclusively used for non-commercial, personal gardening on properties smaller than 0.5 hectares is exempt. The Registrar may, upon application, grant further exemptions for specialized equipment used for research purposes, provided its use is strictly controlled and limited in scope.

heading: Exemptions from Registration
text: Certain types of farm equipment are exempt from the mandatory registration requirements under this Act. These exemptions include hand-held tools, equipment with an engine power below 30 horsepower, and equipment with a total weight under 1,200 kilograms. Additionally, equipment exclusively used for non-commercial, personal gardening on properties smaller than 0.75 hectares is exempt. The Registrar may, upon application, grant further exemptions for specialized equipment used for educational purposes, provided its use is strictly controlled and limited in scope.

heading: Application for Registration
text: An application for registration must be submitted by the owner of the farm equipment to the Registrar. The application form, available electronically or at municipal offices in Aldmark and Brenholt, must be completed accurately and in full. It requires information such as the equipment's make, model, serial number, year of manufacture, and primary intended use. The owner must also provide proof of ownership, such as a bill of sale or import documents, and a valid identification document. A non-refundable application fee of 150 crowns is payable at the time of submission.

heading: Supporting Documentation
text: Every application for registration must be accompanied by specific supporting documentation. This includes an original or certified copy of the purchase invoice or other proof of ownership, valid identification of the owner (e.g., National Identity Card), and, for imported equipment, customs clearance documents. For equipment that has been significantly modified, a certificate from a qualified engineer confirming safety compliance is also required. Failure to provide all necessary documentation within 14 days of the application submission will result in the rejection of the application.

heading: Registration Fees
text: A registration fee is payable upon successful registration of farm equipment. For equipment valued up to 50,000 crowns, the fee is 300 crowns. For equipment valued between 50,001 and 150,000 crowns, the fee is 600 crowns. For equipment valued above 150,000 crowns, the fee is 1,200 crowns. These fees cover the administrative costs of maintaining the register and issuing registration certificates. The fees are subject to review every five years by the Ministry of Agriculture and may be adjusted accordingly, with public notice provided 90 days in advance.

heading: Registration Fees
text: A registration fee is payable upon successful registration of farm equipment. For equipment valued up to 75,000 crowns, the fee is 400 crowns. For equipment valued between 75,001 and 200,000 crowns, the fee is 800 crowns. For equipment valued above 200,000 crowns, the fee is 1,500 crowns. These fees cover the administrative costs of maintaining the register and issuing registration certificates. The fees are subject to review every three years by the Ministry of Agriculture and may be adjusted accordingly, with public notice provided 60 days in advance.

heading: Issuance of Registration Certificate
text: Upon successful review of the application and receipt of all applicable fees, the Registrar shall issue a registration certificate for the farm equipment. This certificate will contain a unique registration number, the equipment's key identifying details, and the owner's information. The certificate must be kept with the equipment at all times during operation or transport within Nordvale. A digital copy of the certificate may also be provided and is considered equally valid. The Registrar aims to process all complete applications within 10 business days.

heading: Issuance of Registration Certificate
text: Upon successful review of the application and receipt of all applicable fees, the Registrar shall issue a registration certificate for the farm equipment. This certificate will contain a unique registration number, the equipment's key identifying details, and the owner's information. The certificate must be kept with the equipment at all times during operation or transport within Nordvale. A digital copy of the certificate must be provided and is considered the primary valid form. The Registrar aims to process all complete applications within 7 business days.

heading: Registration Number Display
text: Every registered piece of farm equipment must prominently display its unique registration number. This number must be affixed to the equipment in a visible location, preferably on both sides, using durable, weather-resistant materials. The characters of the registration number must be at least 10 centimeters high and clearly legible from a distance of 10 meters. Failure to display the registration number as prescribed may result in a fine of 500 crowns for each instance of non-compliance, as per section 25.

heading: Validity Period of Registration
text: The initial registration of farm equipment is valid for a period of five years from the date of issuance. Owners will receive a renewal notice 90 days before the expiry date. It is the owner's responsibility to ensure timely renewal. Operating equipment with an expired registration is prohibited and may lead to penalties. The renewal process requires a re-validation of ownership and an inspection to confirm the equipment's operational safety. A renewal fee, set at 50% of the initial registration fee, applies.

heading: Validity Period of Registration
text: The initial registration of farm equipment is valid for a period of four years from the date of issuance. Owners will receive a renewal notice 60 days before the expiry date. It is the owner's responsibility to ensure timely renewal. Operating equipment with an expired registration is prohibited and may lead to penalties. The renewal process requires a re-validation of ownership and an inspection to confirm the equipment's operational safety. A renewal fee, set at 60% of the initial registration fee, applies.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text: To renew a registration, the owner must submit a renewal application to the Registrar within 60 days prior to the expiry date. The application must confirm that no significant changes have occurred to the equipment or ownership details since the last registration. A mandatory safety inspection of the equipment by an authorized inspector is required, and a certificate of inspection must accompany the renewal application. The renewal fee, as specified in section 10, must be paid at the time of submission. Late renewals may incur an additional fee of 200 crowns.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text: To renew a registration, the owner must submit a renewal application to the Registrar within 45 days prior to the expiry date. The application must confirm that no significant changes have occurred to the equipment or ownership details since the last registration. A mandatory safety inspection of the equipment by an authorized inspector is required, and a certificate of inspection must accompany the renewal application. The renewal fee, as specified in section 10, must be paid at the time of submission. Late renewals may incur an additional fee of 350 crowns.

heading: Transfer of Ownership
text: When registered farm equipment is sold or otherwise transferred to a new owner, the previous owner must notify the Registrar within 14 days of the transfer. The new owner must then apply for a transfer of registration within 30 days of acquiring the equipment. This application requires proof of ownership transfer and payment of a transfer fee of 250 crowns. Failure by the new owner to register the transfer within the specified period will result in the original registration becoming invalid, and penalties may be applied to both parties.

heading: Reporting Stolen or Lost Equipment
text: The owner of any registered farm equipment that is stolen or lost must report the incident to the local law enforcement authorities and the Registrar within 48 hours of discovery. The report to the Registrar must include the registration number, a detailed description of the equipment, and the police report number. This ensures the equipment's status is updated in the national register, assisting in its recovery and preventing fraudulent use. Failure to report within the stipulated timeframe may affect insurance claims and recovery efforts.

heading: Reporting Damage or Destruction
text: In the event of significant damage rendering registered farm equipment unserviceable, or its complete destruction, the owner must notify the Registrar within 30 days. This notification should include a description of the damage or destruction and, where possible, supporting documentation such as insurance reports or official assessments. The Registrar will then update the equipment's status in the register. If the equipment is subsequently repaired and put back into service, a new safety inspection and re-registration process may be required, subject to the Registrar's discretion.

heading: Alterations to Registered Equipment
text: Any significant alteration to registered farm equipment that affects its primary specifications, such as engine replacement, chassis modification, or changes in its fundamental operational capacity, must be reported to the Registrar within 21 days of completion. The owner must provide details of the alteration and, if deemed necessary by the Registrar, a certificate from a qualified engineer confirming that the modifications comply with safety standards. Failure to report such alterations may lead to the invalidation of the equipment's registration and potential fines.

heading: Alterations to Registered Equipment
text: Any significant alteration to registered farm equipment that affects its primary specifications, such as engine replacement, chassis modification, or changes in its fundamental operational capacity, must be reported to the Registrar within 14 days of completion. The owner must provide details of the alteration and, if deemed necessary by the Registrar, a certificate from a qualified engineer confirming that the modifications comply with safety standards. Failure to report such alterations may lead to the invalidation of the equipment's registration and potential fines.

heading: Maintenance of the Register
text: The Registrar is responsible for maintaining an accurate and up-to-date national register of all farm equipment. This register will include details of ownership, equipment specifications, registration dates, and any reported changes in status (e.g., stolen, destroyed, transferred). The register will be stored electronically in a secure database, with regular backups conducted at least weekly. Data integrity and confidentiality are paramount, and access to the register is strictly controlled, limited to authorized personnel and for legitimate purposes only.

heading: Access to Register Information
text: Access to information contained within the national register of farm equipment is primarily restricted to law enforcement agencies for investigation purposes and to the Registrar's authorized staff for administrative duties. Owners may access information pertaining to their own registered equipment free of charge. Other parties may request access to specific, non-sensitive information for legitimate purposes (e.g., insurance companies verifying ownership), subject to a formal application and a processing fee of 100 crowns. Personal data will only be disclosed with explicit consent or legal mandate.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All personal and proprietary information submitted for registration purposes or contained within the national register shall be treated with the utmost confidentiality. The Registrar and all staff involved in the administration of this Act are bound by strict confidentiality agreements. Unauthorised disclosure of information is a serious offense and may lead to disciplinary action, including termination of employment and legal prosecution. Access logs are maintained to monitor all queries made to the register, ensuring accountability and security.

heading: Duty to Provide Information
text: Owners of farm equipment are legally obligated to provide accurate and complete information to the Registrar as required by this Act. This includes promptly reporting any changes to ownership details, equipment status, or operational address within 21 days of such changes occurring. Failure to provide accurate information or knowingly providing false information constitutes an offense under this Act and may result in the imposition of fines of up to 1,000 crowns or the revocation of the equipment's registration.

heading: Inspections by Authorized Officers
text: Authorized officers, appointed by the Registrar, may conduct inspections of farm equipment to verify compliance with this Act. These inspections may occur at the owner's premises or at designated checkpoints. Owners must permit access to their equipment and provide any requested documentation, such as the registration certificate. Officers will carry official identification, and inspections will generally be conducted during daylight hours between 08:00 and 18:00. Obstruction of an authorized officer is an offense punishable by a fine of 750 crowns.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An owner aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar, such as a refusal to register equipment, a penalty imposition, or a revocation of registration, may appeal the decision. A written appeal must be submitted to the Appeals Board, an independent body, within 30 days of receiving the Registrar's decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for contention and provide any supporting evidence. The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days, which shall be final.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An owner aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar, such as a refusal to register equipment, a penalty imposition, or a revocation of registration, may appeal the decision. A written appeal must be submitted to the Appeals Board, an independent body, within 20 days of receiving the Registrar's decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for contention and provide any supporting evidence. The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 45 days, which shall be final and binding.

heading: Offenses and Penalties
text: Any person who contravenes a provision of this Act, or fails to comply with a requirement or order made under this Act, commits an offense. Penalties for offenses may include fines ranging from 500 crowns to 5,000 crowns, depending on the severity and nature of the offense. Repeated offenses may lead to higher penalties, including the possible confiscation of unregistered equipment, as decided by a competent court. Details of specific offenses and their corresponding penalties are further outlined in Schedule B.

heading: Penalties for Unregistered Equipment
text: Operating farm equipment that is required to be registered under this Act but remains unregistered constitutes a serious offense. The owner of such equipment may be liable to an immediate fine of 1,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 2,500 crowns and may lead to the impounding of the unregistered equipment until proper registration is completed and all outstanding fees and fines are paid. The owner is responsible for all costs associated with impounding, including storage fees of 50 crowns per day.

heading: Penalties for False Information
text: Providing false, misleading, or incomplete information in any application, report, or communication with the Registrar or authorized officers is a serious offense. Any person found to be in violation of this section may face a fine of up to 3,000 crowns. If the false information is determined to have been provided intentionally with intent to defraud or evade compliance, the fine may increase to 7,500 crowns, and the registration may be immediately revoked. Criminal charges may also be pursued in severe cases.

heading: Confiscation of Equipment
text: In cases of repeated or egregious non-compliance with the registration requirements of this Act, a court may order the confiscation of farm equipment. This measure is typically reserved for instances where equipment has been operated unregistered for more than 180 days after initial notice, or where it has been involved in multiple reported incidents while unregistered. Confiscated equipment may be sold at public auction, with the proceeds used to cover administrative costs, fines, and potentially restitution, as determined by the court.

heading: Confiscation of Equipment
text: In cases of repeated or egregious non-compliance with the registration requirements of this Act, a court may order the confiscation of farm equipment. This measure is typically reserved for instances where equipment has been operated unregistered for more than 120 days after initial notice, or where it has been involved in multiple reported incidents while unregistered. Confiscated equipment may be sold at public auction, with the proceeds used to cover administrative costs, fines, and potentially restitution, as determined by the court.

heading: Service of Notices
text: Any notice or document required to be served under this Act may be served personally, by registered mail to the last known address of the recipient, or by electronic mail to a registered email address. If sent by registered mail, service shall be deemed to have been effected on the fifth business day following the date of posting. If sent by electronic mail, service shall be deemed to have been effected on the next business day after transmission, provided no error message is received. It is the owner's responsibility to keep contact details updated.

heading: Regulations
text: The Minister of Agriculture may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, for the better carrying out of the provisions and purposes of this Act. These regulations may pertain to specific categories of equipment to be included or exempted from registration, the form and content of applications and certificates, procedures for inspections, and the determination of additional fees or charges. Any proposed regulations must undergo a 30-day public consultation period before being formally enacted and published in the Nordvale Gazette.

heading: Ministerial Directives
text: The Minister of Agriculture may issue directives to the Registrar concerning the administration and enforcement of this Act. These directives must be consistent with the provisions of this Act and any regulations made thereunder. Such directives may provide guidance on interpretation, operational procedures, or specific enforcement priorities. All directives issued shall be published on the Ministry's official website and communicated to affected parties within 7 days of their issuance. They are binding on the Registrar and all authorized officers.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be subject to a comprehensive review by a parliamentary committee five years after its commencement, and thereafter every five years. The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its stated purposes, identify any unintended consequences, and recommend necessary amendments to improve its implementation. Stakeholders, including farmer associations and industry representatives, will be invited to provide input during the review process, ensuring the Act remains relevant and practical.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be subject to a comprehensive review by a parliamentary committee three years after its commencement, and thereafter every three years. The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its stated purposes, identify any unintended consequences, and recommend necessary amendments to improve its implementation. Stakeholders, including farmer associations and industry representatives, will be invited to provide input during the review process, ensuring the Act remains relevant and practical.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: For farm equipment acquired prior to the commencement of this Act, owners are granted a transitional period of 180 days to complete registration without incurring late penalties. During this period, the normal registration fees apply. The Registrar will establish temporary registration centers in Dunmere and Elsby to facilitate this initial influx of applications. Equipment registered within this transitional period will receive a certificate valid for a reduced period of four years to stagger future renewal cycles.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: For farm equipment acquired prior to the commencement of this Act, owners are granted a transitional period of 90 days to complete registration without incurring late penalties. During this period, the normal registration fees apply. The Registrar will establish temporary registration centers in Dunmere and Elsby to facilitate this initial influx of applications. Equipment registered within this transitional period will receive a certificate valid for a reduced period of three years to stagger future renewal cycles.
