heading: Special categories
text: Each licensed bell ringer of a parish tower is exempt from the requirement to register dwellings rented for less than thirty consecutive nights.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered certified wine taster shall pay an annual electric bicycle registration fee of fifteen crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets hygiene rules for businesses that prepare, store or sell food in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to prevent illness caused by food.
(3) It applies to restaurants, shops, caterers and mobile food sellers, but not to food prepared at home for the cook's own family.

heading: Duty of hygiene
text:
(1) A food business shall prepare, store and serve food in a way that does not make it unsafe to eat.
(2) The person in charge of the business is responsible for compliance with this Act.
(3) The person in charge shall write down the hygiene procedures used in the business.

heading: Registration of a food business
text:
(1) A person who starts a food business shall register it at least 28 days before opening.
(2) The registration fee is 50 crowns.
(3) A food business that has not been registered shall not sell food.

heading: Registration of a food business
text:
(1) A person who starts a food business shall register it at least 28 days before opening.
(2) The registration fee is 60 crowns.
(3) A food business that has not been registered shall not sell food.

heading: Hygiene certificate
text:
(1) Every person who handles unpacked food shall hold a hygiene certificate.
(2) The certificate is valid for 3 years.
(3) The person in charge shall keep a copy of each certificate at the business.

heading: Frequency of inspection
text:
(1) A high-risk food business shall be inspected at least every 6 months.
(2) A low-risk food business shall be inspected at least every 24 months.
(3) The inspector shall give the business a written report within 7 days.

heading: Frequency of inspection
text:
(1) A high-risk food business shall be inspected at least every 4 months.
(2) A low-risk food business shall be inspected at least every 24 months.
(3) The inspector shall give the business a written report within 7 days.

heading: Cold storage
text:
(1) Chilled food shall be stored at a temperature of 5 degrees Celsius or lower.
(2) A refrigerator shall have a thermometer that can be read from outside.
(3) The temperature shall be recorded at least once a day.

heading: Frozen storage
text:
(1) Frozen food shall be stored at a temperature of minus 18 degrees Celsius or lower.
(2) Frozen food that has thawed shall not be frozen again.
(3) The temperature of a freezer shall be recorded at least once a day.

heading: Hot holding
text:
(1) Cooked food kept hot for serving shall be held at a temperature of at least 60 degrees Celsius.
(2) Food held below that temperature for more than 2 hours shall be thrown away.
(3) The temperature shall be checked at least every 2 hours.

heading: Hot holding
text:
(1) Cooked food kept hot for serving shall be held at a temperature of at least 63 degrees Celsius.
(2) Food held below that temperature for more than 2 hours shall be thrown away.
(3) The temperature shall be checked at least every 2 hours.

heading: Cooling cooked food
text:
(1) Cooked food that is to be stored shall be cooled to 10 degrees Celsius or lower within 90 minutes.
(2) Cooled food shall then be moved to cold storage under section 6.
(3) The cooling time shall be written down for each batch.

heading: Allergen information
text:
(1) A food business shall give customers information on the presence of any of the 14 listed allergens in each food sold.
(2) The information shall be shown on the menu, on the label or on request.
(3) The list of allergens is published by the authority.

heading: Allergen information
text:
(1) A food business shall give customers information on the presence of any of the 16 listed allergens in each food sold.
(2) The information shall be shown on the menu, on the label or on request.
(3) The list of allergens is published by the authority.

heading: Hand washing
text:
(1) A food business shall have at least 1 hand-washing basin with hot and cold water in every food preparation area.
(2) Soap and paper towels shall be available at all times.
(3) A basin shall not be used for washing food or equipment.

heading: Pest control
text:
(1) A food business shall take steps to keep pests out of the premises.
(2) The business shall inspect the premises for pests at least once a month.
(3) Signs of pests shall be reported to the authority within 24 hours.

heading: Records
text:
(1) A food business shall keep records of temperatures, cleaning and deliveries.
(2) The records shall be kept for 12 months.
(3) The records shall be shown to an inspector on request.

heading: Hygiene rating
text:
(1) After each inspection the authority gives the business a hygiene rating from 0 to 5.
(2) The rating shall be displayed at the entrance of the business.
(3) A business with a rating of 2 or less shall be inspected again within 30 days.

heading: Closure order
text:
(1) An inspector may order the immediate closure of a food business if there is an imminent risk to health.
(2) The closure lasts until the inspector confirms the risk has gone.
(3) The business may appeal the order within 5 days.

heading: Fine for breaking hygiene rules
text:
(1) A person in charge who breaks a rule of this Act shall pay a fine of 250 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) A second breach within 12 months doubles the fine.

heading: Fine for breaking hygiene rules
text:
(1) A person in charge who breaks a rule of this Act shall pay a fine of 350 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) A second breach within 12 months doubles the fine.

heading: Re-inspection fee
text:
(1) A food business that fails an inspection shall pay a re-inspection fee of 90 crowns.
(2) The fee is due when the re-inspection takes place.
(3) No fee is charged for a re-inspection that follows a closure order under section 15 if the closure was found unjustified.

heading: Home kitchens
text:
(1) A person who prepares food at home for sale to the public needs no registration if no more than 20 meals are sold in a week.
(2) A home kitchen shall still follow sections 6, 7 and 8.
(3) A person who sells more than 20 meals in a week shall register under section 3.

heading: Mobile food units
text:
(1) A mobile food unit shall be registered under section 3.
(2) The unit shall carry its own water tank of at least 40 litres.
(3) The unit shall return to a registered base kitchen at the end of each trading day.

heading: Medical examination of food handlers
text:
(1) A person who starts work with unpacked food shall pass a medical examination.
(2) The examination shall be repeated every 2 years.
(3) The cost of the examination shall be paid by the employer.
(4) A person who fails the examination shall not handle unpacked food until a new examination is passed.

heading: Medical examination of food handlers
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Swimming after an early-morning shift
text:
(1) A person whose employment contract provides for shifts that end between 05:00 and 08:00 pays 6 crowns as the adult admission fee to a public swimming pool for a visit that starts before 12:00 on a day on which such a shift ended.
(2) The visit lasts at most 3 hours, as for other visitors.

heading: Swimming after an early-morning shift
text:
(1) A person whose employment contract provides for shifts that end between 05:00 and 08:00 pays 7 crowns as the adult admission fee to a public swimming pool for a visit that starts before 12:00 on a day on which such a shift ended.
(2) The visit lasts at most 3 hours, as for other visitors.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates recreational and commercial fishing in the waters of Nordvale.
(2) It applies to the sea, rivers and lakes.
(3) Fishing for scientific purposes is regulated by the Fisheries Board and is not covered by this Act.

heading: Licence required
text:
(1) A person aged 16 or over shall hold a fishing licence to fish in public waters.
(2) A person under 16 may fish without a licence if accompanied by a licence holder.
(3) The licence shall be carried while fishing.

heading: Annual fishing licence
text:
(1) The annual fishing licence costs 35 crowns.
(2) It is valid from 1 January to 31 December.
(3) A licence bought after 30 June costs half the annual price.

heading: Annual fishing licence
text:
(1) The annual fishing licence costs 42 crowns.
(2) It is valid from 1 January to 31 December.
(3) A licence bought after 30 June costs half the annual price.

heading: Weekly fishing licence
text:
(1) The weekly fishing licence costs 12 crowns.
(2) It is valid for 7 consecutive days from the date stated on it.
(3) A person may buy at most 4 weekly licences in a calendar year.

heading: Day fishing licence
text:
(1) The day fishing licence costs 4 crowns.
(2) It is valid for one calendar day only.
(3) A day licence may be bought on the same day as the fishing.

heading: Day fishing licence
text:
(1) The day fishing licence costs 5 crowns.
(2) It is valid for one calendar day only.
(3) A day licence may be bought on the same day as the fishing.

heading: Senior and youth licences
text:
(1) A person aged 65 or over pays 20 crowns for the annual fishing licence.
(2) A person aged 16 or 17 pays 15 crowns for the annual fishing licence.
(3) The reduced price is shown on the licence.

heading: Commercial fishing licence
text:
(1) A person who sells fish as a business shall hold a commercial fishing licence.
(2) The annual commercial licence costs 300 crowns.
(3) The holder shall keep a catch log and submit it each year by 31 January.

heading: Catch limits for salmon
text:
(1) A person may keep at most 2 salmon per day.
(2) A salmon shorter than 60 centimetres shall be released.
(3) A person shall record each kept salmon in the catch card on the same day.

heading: Catch limits for salmon
text:
(1) A person may keep at most 1 salmon per day.
(2) A salmon shorter than 65 centimetres shall be released.
(3) A person shall record each kept salmon in the catch card on the same day.

heading: Catch limits for trout
text:
(1) A person may keep at most 5 trout per day.
(2) A trout shorter than 30 centimetres shall be released.
(3) A person shall record each kept trout in the catch card on the same day.

heading: Catch limits for pike
text:
(1) A person may keep at most 3 pike per day.
(2) A pike shorter than 45 centimetres shall be released.
(3) A pike longer than 90 centimetres shall also be released.

heading: Closed season
text:
(1) Fishing for salmon is forbidden from 1 October to 31 December.
(2) Fishing for trout is forbidden from 1 September to 30 November.
(3) The Fisheries Board may extend a closed season by up to 30 days.

heading: Closed season
text:
(1) Fishing for salmon is forbidden from 15 September to 31 December.
(2) Fishing for trout is forbidden from 1 September to 30 November.
(3) The Fisheries Board may extend a closed season by up to 30 days.

heading: Permitted equipment
text:
(1) A person may use at most 2 rods at the same time.
(2) The use of nets is forbidden for recreational fishing.
(3) The use of explosives or poison is forbidden for everyone.

heading: Night fishing
text:
(1) Fishing between 22:00 and 05:00 requires a night permit.
(2) The night permit costs 8 crowns per night.
(3) The night permit is not available in the closed seasons.

heading: Night fishing
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Ice fishing
text:
(1) Ice fishing is allowed on lakes when the ice is at least 10 centimetres thick.
(2) A hole in the ice shall be no wider than 25 centimetres.
(3) The person shall mark each hole in a way that is visible from 20 metres.

heading: Protected waters
text:
(1) Fishing is forbidden in the waters listed by the Fisheries Board as protected.
(2) The list shall be published at least 30 days before it takes effect.
(3) A person who fishes in protected waters shall pay a fine of 150 crowns.

heading: Fish farms
text:
(1) A person who runs a fish farm shall register it with the Fisheries Board.
(2) The registration fee is 100 crowns and is paid once.
(3) A fish farm shall be inspected at least once every 2 years.

heading: Fisheries Board
text:
(1) The Fisheries Board issues licences and supervises the application of this Act.
(2) The Board has 5 members appointed for terms of 3 years.
(3) The Board shall publish catch statistics every year.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) A fishing inspector may check licences, catch cards and equipment at any time.
(2) The inspector may seize equipment that is used unlawfully.
(3) Seized equipment shall be returned within 60 days unless a fine is unpaid.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who fishes without a licence shall pay a fine of 100 crowns.
(2) A person who keeps more fish than the catch limit allows shall pay a fine of 80 crowns.
(3) For a repeat offence within 2 years the fine is doubled.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who fishes without a licence shall pay a fine of 120 crowns.
(2) A person who keeps more fish than the catch limit allows shall pay a fine of 100 crowns.
(3) For a repeat offence within 2 years the fine is doubled.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision of the Fisheries Board may appeal within 30 days.
(2) The appeal shall be decided within 60 days.
(3) An appeal does not suspend the seizure of equipment under section 18.

heading: Driving theory test for reservists
text: An active reservist within the meaning of MOG §44 pays half of the fee for the theory test for a driving licence.

heading: Driving theory test for reservists
text: An active reservist within the meaning of MOG §44 pays no fee for the theory test for a driving licence.

heading: Deer tags for reservists
text: An active reservist within the meaning of MOG §44 pays no tag fee for one roe deer in a season.

heading: Deer tags for reservists
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets a levy on fuel sold or used in Nordvale and the duties of the suppliers who collect it.
(2) The levy is calculated per litre and is paid by the supplier to the Revenue Office.
(3) All amounts in this Act are in crowns.

heading: Fuels subject to the levy
text:
(1) The levy applies to petrol, diesel and heating oil.
(2) Fuel that is exported from Nordvale is not subject to the levy.
(3) A fuel that is not listed in subsection (1) is not subject to the levy unless this Act provides otherwise.

heading: Petrol levy
text:
(1) The levy on petrol is 0.45 crowns per litre.
(2) The levy arises when the supplier delivers the petrol to a filling station or to a customer.
(3) The supplier includes the levy in the price charged.

heading: Petrol levy
text:
(1) The levy on petrol is 0.50 crowns per litre.
(2) The levy arises when the supplier delivers the petrol to a filling station or to a customer.
(3) The supplier includes the levy in the price charged.

heading: Petrol levy
text:
(1) The levy on petrol is 0.55 crowns per litre.
(2) The levy arises when the supplier delivers the petrol to a filling station or to a customer.
(3) The supplier includes the levy in the price charged.

heading: Diesel levy
text:
(1) The levy on diesel is 0.40 crowns per litre.
(2) The levy arises when the supplier delivers the diesel to a filling station or to a customer.
(3) The supplier includes the levy in the price charged.

heading: Diesel levy
text:
(1) The levy on diesel is 0.48 crowns per litre.
(2) The levy arises when the supplier delivers the diesel to a filling station or to a customer.
(3) The supplier includes the levy in the price charged.

heading: Heating oil levy
text:
(1) The levy on heating oil is 0.10 crowns per litre.
(2) The levy arises when the supplier delivers the heating oil to a building.
(3) The supplier shows the levy separately on the delivery note.

heading: Heating oil levy
text:
(1) The levy on heating oil is 0.14 crowns per litre.
(2) The levy arises when the supplier delivers the heating oil to a building.
(3) The supplier shows the levy separately on the delivery note.

heading: Biofuel blends
text:
(1) A fuel that contains at least 30 percent biofuel is charged 70 percent of the levy that would otherwise apply.
(2) The supplier must keep a laboratory certificate for each delivery of blended fuel.
(3) The reduction applies to petrol and diesel only.

heading: Biofuel blends
text:
(1) A fuel that contains at least 30 percent biofuel is charged 65 percent of the levy that would otherwise apply.
(2) The supplier must keep a laboratory certificate for each delivery of blended fuel.
(3) The reduction applies to petrol and diesel only.

heading: Farm machinery
text:
(1) Diesel used in farm machinery that is not registered for road use is charged a levy of 0.20 crowns per litre.
(2) The farmer must buy the diesel from a registered supplier.
(3) The supplier shows the reduced levy on the invoice.

heading: Farm machinery
text:
(1) Diesel used in farm machinery that is not registered for road use is charged a levy of 0.24 crowns per litre.
(2) The farmer must buy the diesel from a registered supplier.
(3) The supplier shows the reduced levy on the invoice.

heading: Fishing boats
text:
(1) Diesel used in a commercial fishing boat is charged a levy of 0.15 crowns per litre.
(2) The boat owner must show a fishing licence to the supplier.
(3) The reduced levy does not apply to boats used for leisure.

heading: Fishing boats
text:
(1) Diesel used in a commercial fishing boat is charged a levy of 0.18 crowns per litre.
(2) The boat owner must show a fishing licence to the supplier.
(3) The reduced levy does not apply to boats used for leisure.

heading: Supplier registration
text:
(1) A person who supplies fuel for sale must register with the Revenue Office before the first delivery.
(2) The annual registration fee is 200 crowns.
(3) A supplier who is not registered may not collect the levy.

heading: Supplier registration
text:
(1) A person who supplies fuel for sale must register with the Revenue Office before the first delivery.
(2) The annual registration fee is 240 crowns.
(3) A supplier who is not registered may not collect the levy.

heading: Monthly return
text:
(1) A registered supplier shall file a return of the litres delivered in each month.
(2) The return is due on the 20th of the following month.
(3) The levy shown in the return is paid on the same day.

heading: Monthly return
text:
(1) A registered supplier shall file a return of the litres delivered in each month.
(2) The return is due on the 15th of the following month.
(3) The levy shown in the return is paid on the same day.

heading: Late return penalty
text:
(1) A supplier who files a return after the due date shall pay a penalty of 50 crowns.
(2) The penalty is charged once for each late return.
(3) The penalty does not replace the interest in section 12.

heading: Late return penalty
text:
(1) A supplier who files a return after the due date shall pay a penalty of 75 crowns.
(2) The penalty is charged once for each late return.
(3) The penalty does not replace the interest in section 12.

heading: Interest on late payment
text:
(1) Levy that is not paid by the due date carries interest of 1 percent for each full month of delay.
(2) Interest is calculated on the unpaid levy only.
(3) The Revenue Office sends a statement of the interest every quarter.

heading: Interest on late payment
text:
(1) Levy that is not paid by the due date carries interest of 1.5 percent for each full month of delay.
(2) Interest is calculated on the unpaid levy only.
(3) The Revenue Office sends a statement of the interest every quarter.

heading: Small suppliers
text:
(1) A supplier that delivers fewer than 100,000 litres in a calendar year may file one return for the year instead of monthly returns.
(2) The annual return is due on 31 January of the following year.
(3) A supplier that passes the limit during the year must switch to monthly returns.

heading: Public charging points
text:
(1) The operator of a public charging point for electric cars shall pay a levy of 0.05 crowns per kilowatt hour supplied.
(2) The operator shall report the kilowatt hours once a quarter.
(3) Charging at private homes is not subject to the levy.

heading: Public charging points
text:
(1) The operator of a public charging point for electric cars shall pay a levy of 0.06 crowns per kilowatt hour supplied.
(2) The operator shall report the kilowatt hours once a quarter.
(3) Charging at private homes is not subject to the levy.

heading: Export refund
text:
(1) A supplier who exports fuel on which the levy was paid may claim a refund of the levy.
(2) The claim must be made within 90 days of the export.
(3) The supplier must attach the customs record of the export.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) A supplier shall keep records of deliveries, returns and payments for 6 years.
(2) The records must show the date, the litres and the customer of each delivery.
(3) The records may be kept on paper or in electronic form.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) A supplier shall keep records of deliveries, returns and payments for 7 years.
(2) The records must show the date, the litres and the customer of each delivery.
(3) The records may be kept on paper or in electronic form.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Revenue Office may inspect a supplier's records and storage tanks.
(2) The Revenue Office shall give at least 48 hours' notice of an inspection.
(3) The supplier shall give the inspectors access during working hours.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Revenue Office may inspect a supplier's records and storage tanks.
(2) The Revenue Office shall give at least 24 hours' notice of an inspection.
(3) The supplier shall give the inspectors access during working hours.

heading: Penalty for under-declaration
text:
(1) A supplier who declares fewer litres than were delivered shall pay a penalty of 25 percent of the levy that was not declared.
(2) The penalty is added to the levy and the interest.
(3) A supplier who corrects the return before an inspection pays no penalty.

heading: Penalty for under-declaration
text:
(1) A supplier who declares fewer litres than were delivered shall pay a penalty of 30 percent of the levy that was not declared.
(2) The penalty is added to the levy and the interest.
(3) A supplier who corrects the return before an inspection pays no penalty.

heading: Emergency services
text:
(1) Fuel delivered to ambulances, fire engines and police vehicles is not subject to the levy.
(2) The authority concerned shall give the supplier a certificate for each fuel card.
(3) The certificate is valid for 12 months.

heading: Coal levy
text:
(1) The levy on coal used for heating is 12 crowns per tonne.
(2) The supplier shall show the levy separately on the delivery note.
(3) Coal that is exported from Nordvale is not subject to the levy.

heading: Coal levy
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A supplier may appeal a levy decision to the Revenue Office within 30 days of receiving it.
(2) The appeal must be in writing and must state the reasons.
(3) The Revenue Office decides the appeal within 60 days.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A supplier may appeal a levy decision to the Revenue Office within 45 days of receiving it.
(2) The appeal must be in writing and must state the reasons.
(3) The Revenue Office decides the appeal within 60 days.

heading: Monthly travel passes for apprentices
text:
(1) A registered apprentice pays 60 percent of the price of a monthly pass under PTA §7, PTA §8 or PTA §9.
(2) The reduction does not apply to an annual pass under PTA §21 or to a day pass.
(3) An apprentice who receives a student discount on a travel card under SSA §10 or SSA §11 for the same month receives no reduction under this section.

heading: Monthly travel passes for apprentices
text:
(1) A registered apprentice pays 50 percent of the price of a monthly pass under PTA §7, PTA §8 or PTA §9.
(2) The reduction does not apply to an annual pass under PTA §21 or to a day pass.
(3) An apprentice who receives a student discount on a travel card under SSA §10 or SSA §11 for the same month receives no reduction under this section.

heading: Toll passes for apprentices
text:
(1) A registered apprentice who owns a car pays 40 crowns for a monthly pass for that car on the toll roads.
(2) The reduced price does not apply to an annual pass.
(3) The pass otherwise has the same effect as any other monthly pass for a car.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, granting, and oversight of forestry management licences within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure sustainable forestry practices, protect natural resources, and provide a clear process for individuals and entities engaging in timber harvesting and related forestry operations. This Act covers all commercial forestry activities within the designated forest areas across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Forestry operation" means any activity related to the cultivation, harvesting, or processing of timber within a designated forest area, excluding incidental collection for personal use.
(b) "Licence" refers to a Forestry Management Licence issued under section 3 of this Act.
(c) "Minister" means the Minister responsible for forestry matters within the government of Nordvale.
(d) "Timber" includes standing trees, logs, poles, and other wood products derived from forestry operations.
(2) A 'designated forest area' is any land explicitly identified as such by the Nordvale Department of Natural Resources.

heading: Requirement for a Licence
text:
(1) No person or entity shall engage in any forestry operation within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid Forestry Management Licence issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act. This requirement applies to all commercial timber harvesting activities, including felling, logging, and transportation of timber originating from Nordvale's forests.
(2) Minor activities, such as collecting up to 0.5 cubic meters of firewood for personal use per year, are exempt from this licensing requirement, provided they do not involve the felling of mature trees over 30 cm in diameter at breast height. Violation of this section may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for a Forestry Management Licence must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 1,000 crowns. The application must include a detailed forestry management plan, a site survey, and proof of public liability insurance covering at least 1,000,000 crowns.
(2) Applicants must be at least 18 years of age if an individual, or a registered entity in Nordvale. The Minister may request additional information within 21 days of receiving the initial application.

heading: Licence Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a licence, an applicant must demonstrate: (a) relevant experience in forestry management for at least 3 years; (b) financial capacity to undertake the proposed operations, evidenced by assets exceeding 200,000 crowns; and (c) a clean record regarding environmental violations in Nordvale for the past 5 years.
(2) The proposed forestry management plan must align with national sustainability guidelines, including reforestation targets of at least 150 new trees planted per hectare harvested. Failure to meet any of these criteria will result in the rejection of the application.

heading: Processing of Applications
text:
(1) The Minister shall process a complete application for a licence within 60 days of its receipt. During this period, the Minister may conduct site visits, consult with environmental experts, and seek input from local authorities in the relevant municipality, such as Corvik or Dunmere.
(2) If the application is incomplete, the processing period will be suspended until all requested information is provided. A notification of completeness or deficiency will be issued within 14 days of initial submission. Decisions will be communicated in writing.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A Forestry Management Licence is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 750 crowns.
(2) Renewals are subject to a review of compliance with the original licence conditions and the submission of an updated forestry management plan. Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe will result in the licence lapsing, requiring a new application under section 4.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A Forestry Management Licence is valid for a period of 7 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 120 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 900 crowns.
(2) Renewals are subject to a review of compliance with the original licence conditions and the submission of an updated forestry management plan. Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe will result in the licence lapsing, requiring a new application under section 4.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A Forestry Management Licence is valid for a period of 10 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 180 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,200 crowns.
(2) Renewals are subject to a comprehensive review of compliance with the original licence conditions, an updated environmental impact assessment, and the submission of an updated forestry management plan. Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe will result in the licence lapsing, requiring a new application under section 4.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee mentioned in section 4, an annual licence fee of 5,000 crowns is payable within 30 days of the anniversary of the licence issue date. This fee contributes to the Nordvale Forest Conservation Fund.
(2) A late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee will be applied for payments made between 31 and 60 days late. Further delays may lead to licence suspension as per section 15. Municipalities like Aldmark and Grauby collect these fees.

heading: Conditions of Licence
text:
(1) Every licence issued under this Act is subject to the following conditions:
(a) Adherence to the approved forestry management plan.
(b) Compliance with all environmental protection regulations of Nordvale.
(c) Submission of quarterly timber harvest reports by the 15th day following the end of each quarter.
(d) Maintenance of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 1,500,000 crowns at all times.
(2) The Minister may impose additional specific conditions relevant to the particular forestry operation or location, such as in the sensitive areas near Lund Vale.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders must submit detailed reports on their forestry operations to the Minister. These reports shall include the volume of timber harvested, species felled, reforestation activities, and any environmental incidents.
(2) Quarterly reports are due by the 15th of January, April, July, and October. An annual summary report, covering the full calendar year, must be submitted by January 31st of the following year. Failure to submit reports on time may incur a penalty of 500 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders must submit detailed reports on their forestry operations to the Minister. These reports shall include the volume of timber harvested, species felled, reforestation activities, and any environmental incidents. All data must be submitted electronically.
(2) Monthly reports are due by the 7th day of the following month, covering timber volume, species, and replanting. An annual summary report, covering the full calendar year, must be submitted by January 15th of the following year. Failure to submit reports on time may incur a penalty of 750 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders must submit detailed reports on their forestry operations to the Minister. These reports shall include the volume of timber harvested, species felled, reforestation activities, and any environmental incidents. All data must be submitted electronically via the Nordvale Forestry Portal.
(2) Bi-weekly reports are due by the 3rd and 18th day of each month, covering timber volume, species, and replanting. An annual summary report, covering the full calendar year, must be submitted by January 10th of the following year. Failure to submit reports on time may incur a penalty of 1,000 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Inspection and Monitoring
text:
(1) The Minister, or an authorized agent, may conduct inspections of any licensed forestry operation at any reasonable time with 48 hours' notice. These inspections are to verify compliance with licence conditions and environmental regulations.
(2) Licence holders must grant full access to inspectors and provide all requested documents and information. Obstruction of an inspection is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Sustainable Harvesting Practices
text:
(1) All forestry operations must adhere to sustainable harvesting practices as outlined in the Nordvale Forestry Code. This includes selective logging techniques, protection of riparian zones, and minimum felling diameters of 40 cm for broadleaf trees and 35 cm for conifers.
(2) Reforestation must commence within 12 months of harvesting, with a survival rate of at least 80% for planted saplings within the first 2 years. Operations in areas like Brenholt and Elsby are subject to specific ecological considerations.

heading: Protection of Biodiversity
text:
(1) Licence holders must implement measures to protect biodiversity within their operational areas. This includes identifying and avoiding critical habitats for endangered species and maintaining buffer zones of at least 50 meters around significant water bodies.
(2) The felling of old-growth trees over 100 years old is strictly prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Minister under exceptional circumstances related to forest health. Any such authorization will involve an additional environmental assessment.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) For any forestry operation exceeding 50 hectares or involving harvesting in a previously undisturbed area, a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) must be submitted and approved by the Minister prior to commencing operations.
(2) The EIA must detail potential environmental effects, proposed mitigation measures, and a monitoring plan. The cost of the EIA, typically between 20,000 and 50,000 crowns, is borne by the applicant. This applies to large-scale operations in Fennick.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Minister may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 6 months if a licence holder:
(a) Fails to comply with any condition of the licence or any provision of this Act.
(b) Fails to pay fees within 90 days of the due date.
(c) Submits false or misleading information in reports or applications.
(2) Before suspending a licence, the Minister shall provide the licence holder with written notice of the proposed suspension and an opportunity to make representations within 14 days. This ensures fairness.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) The Minister may revoke a licence if the licence holder:
(a) Commits a serious or repeated breach of this Act or licence conditions, especially after a suspension period.
(b) Is convicted of an environmental crime in Nordvale.
(c) Becomes insolvent or ceases forestry operations for more than 12 consecutive months.
(2) Before revoking a licence, the Minister shall provide the licence holder with written notice of the proposed revocation and an opportunity to be heard within 30 days. All operations must cease immediately upon revocation.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Minister under this Act, including the refusal to grant or renew a licence, or the suspension or revocation of a licence, may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the Minister's decision.
(2) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding. The appeal must be submitted with a fee of 2,500 crowns, which is refundable if the appeal is successful. The Tribunal will hear the appeal within 90 days of submission.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Operations
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be conducting forestry operations without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of not less than 20,000 crowns and not exceeding 100,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second or subsequent offence, the fine shall be not less than 50,000 crowns and not exceeding 250,000 crowns. In addition, all timber harvested illegally may be confiscated by the State. Operations in areas like Corvik are particularly scrutinized.

heading: Penalties for Breach of Conditions
text:
(1) A licence holder who breaches any condition of their licence or any provision of this Act, other than operating without a licence, shall be liable to a fine of up to 15,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second or subsequent breach, the fine may be up to 30,000 crowns, and the Minister may also consider suspension or revocation of the licence as per sections 15 and 16. Persistent breaches will lead to severe consequences.

heading: Penalties for Breach of Conditions
text:
(1) A licence holder who breaches any condition of their licence or any provision of this Act, other than operating without a licence, shall be liable to a fine of up to 25,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second or subsequent breach, the fine may be up to 50,000 crowns, and the Minister shall also consider suspension or revocation of the licence as per sections 15 and 16. Persistent breaches will lead to severe consequences and potential asset forfeiture up to 10% of operational value.

heading: Confiscation of Equipment
text:
(1) In cases of serious or repeated violations of this Act, particularly involving unlicensed operations or severe environmental damage, the Minister may order the confiscation of equipment used in the commission of the offence.
(2) Confiscated equipment, including logging machinery and vehicles, may be sold at public auction, with the proceeds directed to the Nordvale Forest Conservation Fund. This measure is reserved for egregious breaches.

heading: Environmental Restoration Orders
text:
(1) Where a forestry operation has caused environmental damage, the Minister may issue an Environmental Restoration Order requiring the licence holder to undertake specific remedial actions within a specified timeframe, not exceeding 180 days.
(2) Failure to comply with a Restoration Order may result in a daily penalty of 1,000 crowns and the Minister engaging third parties to carry out the work, with all costs recovered from the licence holder. This applies to damage in areas like Dunmere.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) Before issuing a licence for a forestry operation exceeding 20 hectares or located within 500 meters of a residential area, the Minister shall conduct a public consultation process.
(2) This process includes publishing a notice in local newspapers and on the government website for 30 days, inviting public submissions. Concerns raised will be considered during the application review. This is crucial for projects near Aldmark.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) Before issuing a licence for a forestry operation exceeding 10 hectares or located within 200 meters of a residential area, the Minister shall conduct a public consultation process.
(2) This process includes publishing a notice in local newspapers and on the government website for 45 days, inviting public submissions and holding a public meeting if more than 50 objections are received. Concerns raised will be thoroughly considered during the application review. This is crucial for projects near Aldmark and Grauby.

heading: Designated Forest Areas
text:
(1) The Minister, in consultation with the Nordvale Department of Natural Resources, shall designate specific areas of land as 'designated forest areas' suitable for commercial forestry operations.
(2) These designations will be reviewed every 5 years and may be amended based on ecological surveys, community input, and timber resource assessments. Maps of designated areas will be publicly available online and at municipal offices.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Forestry operations conducted solely for scientific research purposes, approved by the Nordvale Scientific Council, are exempt from the licensing requirements of this Act.
(2) Similarly, land clearing for approved infrastructure projects, such as roads or public utilities, is exempt, provided it receives separate environmental clearance from the relevant Nordvale authority. Timber from such clearing must be reported.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Every licence holder shall maintain accurate records of all timber harvested, species, volumes, sales, and reforestation efforts for a period of at least 7 years.
(2) These records must be made available to the Minister or an authorized inspector upon request within 7 working days. Failure to maintain or produce records is a breach of licence conditions, leading to penalties under section 19.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text:
(1) A Forestry Management Licence is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Minister. An application for transfer must be submitted with a fee of 3,000 crowns.
(2) The proposed transferee must meet all the eligibility criteria specified in section 5 of this Act. The Minister will process transfer applications within 45 days. Unapproved transfers are invalid and constitute unlicensed operation by the transferee.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister may make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act, including but not limited to, prescribing forms, setting detailed environmental standards, and establishing specific reforestation requirements for different forest types.
(2) All regulations made under this section shall be published in the Nordvale Gazette and come into force 30 days after publication. These regulations provide granular detail for operations in various municipalities like Elsby.

heading: Special categories
text: (1) A registered cartographer may pay the grant for a hearing aid up to 30 days later than other applicants. (2) This extension applies only once per grant application.

heading: Recognised trades
text: The microchipping is reduced by half for any registered seed bank curator, covering the cost of implanting a small electronic chip beneath the animal's skin for identification.

heading: Seasonal programmes for children of mutual tenure members
text:
(1) A mutual tenure member pays the seasonal residential programme charge for his or her own child at the amount in Schedule N, category N1, for each week.
(2) This amount takes the place of any other relief from that charge; where another provision leads to a smaller amount, only the smaller amount is payable.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive permit system for forestry management practices within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the sustainable use and protection of forest resources, promoting ecological balance and long-term economic viability for the forestry sector. The scope of this Act covers all commercial and non-commercial forestry operations, including timber harvesting, reforestation, and forest road construction, on both public and private lands across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act aims to prevent deforestation and promote biodiversity.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall engage in any forestry management activity as defined in section 3 without first obtaining a valid permit from the Nordvale Forestry Authority. A separate permit is required for each distinct forestry operation. Failure to obtain the necessary permit before commencing operations may result in significant penalties, including fines of up to 5,000 crowns per day of non-compliance. The Authority maintains the right to halt any unauthorized forestry activity immediately upon discovery. Minor domestic wood collection for personal use, limited to 0.5 cubic meters per household per year, is exempt from this requirement.

heading: Definitions of forestry activities
text: For the purposes of this Act, 'forestry management activity' includes: (a) Commercial timber harvesting exceeding 10 cubic meters per hectare; (b) Reforestation projects covering an area greater than 0.25 hectares; (c) Construction or significant alteration of forest roads longer than 50 meters; (d) Pest control operations utilizing chemical agents over an area larger than 1 hectare; (e) Any land clearing for non-forestry purposes within a designated forest area that exceeds 0.1 hectares. These definitions ensure a clear scope for permit applications and enforcement actions. Smaller scale activities are generally exempt.

heading: Application process
text: Applications for forestry management permits must be submitted to the Nordvale Forestry Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation. This documentation typically includes a detailed operational plan, maps of the affected area, and an assessment of environmental impact. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is payable at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days, and the review period will not commence until all necessary information is provided. The Authority aims to process complete applications within 60 days.

heading: Application review period
text: The Nordvale Forestry Authority shall review complete permit applications within 60 days of receipt. During this period, the Authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no decision is made within this timeframe, the application is deemed rejected unless the Authority has formally extended the review period by written notice to the applicant, which can occur for complex projects. A maximum of one 30-day extension is allowed. Applicants will be notified of approval or rejection via registered mail.

heading: Application review period
text: The Nordvale Forestry Authority shall review complete permit applications within 45 days of receipt. During this period, the Authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no decision is made within this timeframe, the application is deemed rejected unless the Authority has formally extended the review period by written notice to the applicant, which can occur for complex projects. A maximum of two 15-day extensions are allowed. Applicants will be notified of approval or rejection via registered mail. The Authority aims to process 90% of applications within the initial 45-day period.

heading: Permit fees
text: Upon approval of a permit application, the applicant shall pay a permit issuance fee. For timber harvesting permits, the fee is 1,500 crowns plus an additional 50 crowns per hectare of area to be harvested. Reforestation permits incur a flat fee of 1,000 crowns. Other forestry management permits, such as for road construction or pest control, carry a fee of 1,200 crowns. These fees are separate from the application fee mentioned in section 4 and must be paid in full before the permit is officially issued. Failure to pay within 30 days of approval notice will result in permit cancellation.

heading: Permit duration
text: Forestry management permits are valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issuance, unless otherwise specified on the permit itself. Permits for reforestation projects may be issued for a longer duration, up to 60 months, to accommodate the growth cycle of young trees. It is the responsibility of the permit holder to complete all permitted activities within the specified duration. Operations continuing beyond the permit's expiry date without a valid renewal or new permit are subject to penalties outlined in section 20. An extension may be sought under specific circumstances.

heading: Permit renewal
text: Permit holders may apply for a renewal of their forestry management permit no earlier than 90 days and no later than 30 days before its expiry date. The renewal application process is similar to the initial application, requiring updated operational plans and a renewal fee of 800 crowns. The Authority will review renewal applications to ensure continued compliance with sustainability standards. Late applications for renewal, submitted less than 30 days before expiry, will be treated as new applications, incurring full new application fees and review times. A maximum of two renewals are typically granted for any single project.

heading: Permit conditions
text: All permits issued under this Act are subject to specific conditions designed to protect forest ecosystems and ensure sustainable practices. These conditions may include, but are not limited to: (a) Restrictions on harvesting methods; (b) Requirements for buffer zones around waterways; (c) Mandates for reforestation species and density; (d) Limitations on operating hours; (e) Specific measures for wildlife protection. Permit holders must strictly adhere to all conditions stipulated on their permit. Non-compliance with permit conditions may lead to suspension or revocation of the permit, as detailed in section 18.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: For forestry operations impacting areas larger than 5 hectares or located in ecologically sensitive zones, a detailed environmental impact assessment (EIA) must be submitted as part of the permit application. The EIA must identify potential environmental risks, propose mitigation strategies, and demonstrate how the operation aligns with Nordvale’s environmental protection policies. The Authority will review the EIA, potentially requiring independent expert verification, before making a decision on the permit. The cost of the EIA is borne by the applicant, and it must be conducted by an accredited professional.

heading: Public consultation
text: For all permit applications involving areas exceeding 20 hectares or those situated adjacent to residential areas, a public consultation period of 30 days is mandatory. During this period, the application details will be publicly accessible, and interested parties may submit written comments or concerns to the Nordvale Forestry Authority. The Authority will consider all feedback received during the decision-making process. The applicant is responsible for publishing a notice of the proposed activity in local community boards and newspapers in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Public consultation
text: For all permit applications involving areas exceeding 15 hectares or those situated adjacent to residential areas, a public consultation period of 45 days is mandatory. During this period, the application details will be publicly accessible, and interested parties may submit written comments or concerns to the Nordvale Forestry Authority. The Authority will consider all feedback received during the decision-making process. The applicant is responsible for publishing a notice of the proposed activity in local community boards and newspapers in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere. A public meeting may also be required at the Authority's discretion.

heading: Forestry professional requirement
text: All commercial timber harvesting operations exceeding 15 cubic meters must be supervised by a licensed forestry professional registered with the Nordvale Association of Foresters. The professional's credentials and registration number must be provided with the permit application. This requirement ensures that operations are conducted according to best practices and adhere to sustainable forestry principles. The licensed professional is also responsible for submitting post-harvest reports confirming compliance with permit conditions. Failure to engage a qualified professional may lead to permit rejection or revocation.

heading: Reforestation obligations
text: Permit holders conducting timber harvesting operations are obligated to reforest the harvested area within 12 months of completing harvesting activities. The reforestation plan, including species selection and planting density (minimum 1,500 trees per hectare), must be approved by the Nordvale Forestry Authority as part of the initial permit. A security deposit of 500 crowns per hectare may be required to ensure compliance with reforestation obligations, refundable upon successful inspection after 3 years. Native species are generally preferred unless otherwise justified by specific ecological conditions.

heading: Road construction standards
text: Construction or upgrading of forest roads must adhere to specific environmental standards to minimize erosion and watershed impact. Roads must be designed to allow for proper drainage, and stream crossings require approved culverts or bridges. The maximum width for new temporary forest roads is 4 meters, and for permanent roads, 6 meters. Plans for road construction must be detailed in the permit application, including specifications for materials and drainage systems. Post-use reclamation plans for temporary roads must also be submitted, detailing how the land will be restored within 6 months of road abandonment.

heading: Wildlife protection measures
text: All forestry operations must incorporate measures to protect local wildlife and their habitats. This includes identifying and avoiding critical habitats, maintaining buffer zones around known nesting sites or denning areas, and scheduling operations to avoid sensitive breeding seasons. A minimum 20-meter buffer must be maintained from any identified raptor nest during active breeding periods. Disturbance of any protected species listed in Nordvale’s Wildlife Protection Regulations is strictly prohibited. Any accidental harm to wildlife must be reported to the Authority within 24 hours.

heading: Water quality protection
text: Forestry operations near water bodies must implement robust measures to protect water quality. A minimum 15-meter no-harvest buffer zone must be maintained along all perennial streams and lakes. Chemical use near water bodies is prohibited. Sediment control measures, such as silt fences and vegetative filters, must be installed and maintained in areas prone to erosion. The discharge of any pollutants into watercourses is strictly forbidden. Regular water quality monitoring may be required for operations adjacent to public water sources, with reports submitted monthly to the Authority.

heading: Chemical use regulations
text: The use of pesticides, herbicides, or other chemicals in forestry operations is strictly regulated. Only chemicals approved by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency may be used, and their application must follow manufacturer guidelines and safety protocols. A detailed chemical use plan, including type, quantity, application method, and safety precautions, must be part of the permit application for any area exceeding 1 hectare. Aerial application of chemicals is generally prohibited unless a specific exemption is granted for large-scale pest outbreaks, subject to stringent conditions and public notification.

heading: Permit suspension and revocation
text: The Nordvale Forestry Authority may suspend or revoke a permit if the permit holder fails to comply with any condition of the permit, any provision of this Act, or provides false information in their application. A written notice of intent to suspend or revoke will be issued, providing the permit holder 30 days to remedy the non-compliance or provide a satisfactory explanation. In cases of severe environmental damage or repeated non-compliance, immediate suspension may occur without prior notice. Revoked permits cannot be re-applied for by the same entity for a period of 12 months.

heading: Compliance inspections
text: The Nordvale Forestry Authority shall conduct regular and unannounced inspections of permitted forestry operations to ensure compliance with this Act and permit conditions. Inspectors are authorized to enter operational sites during working hours, examine records, and collect samples. Permit holders must grant full access and cooperate with inspectors. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense, subject to immediate permit suspension and a fine of up to 10,000 crowns. A minimum of one inspection per permitted operation will be conducted annually.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of this Act or the conditions of their permit may be subject to administrative penalties. These include fines ranging from 2,000 crowns to 25,000 crowns per infraction, depending on the severity and environmental impact. Repeated offenses may result in higher fines, up to 50,000 crowns, and permanent prohibition from obtaining future forestry permits for a period of 5 years. The Authority may also order the violator to undertake remedial actions, such as reforestation or habitat restoration, at their own expense within a 90-day period.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: Permit holders are required to submit progress reports to the Nordvale Forestry Authority at specified intervals, typically every 6 months for ongoing operations. These reports must detail activities undertaken, timber volumes harvested, reforestation efforts, and any environmental incidents. A final report, including photographic evidence of site restoration, is due within 60 days of project completion. Failure to submit required reports on time may result in administrative penalties of 500 crowns for each overdue report and may impact future permit applications. Accurate record-keeping is essential for compliance.

heading: Appeals process
text: An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision of the Nordvale Forestry Authority, including permit rejections, conditions imposed, or penalties levied, within 45 days of receiving written notice of the decision. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Forestry Appeals Board, a body independent of the Authority. The Board will review the appeal and may hold a hearing within 90 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final, except as provided for by judicial review through the Nordvale administrative courts. A fee of 1,000 crowns is required to file an appeal.

heading: Record keeping by permit holders
text: Permit holders must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all forestry activities conducted under their permit. These records shall include: (a) Dates of operations; (b) Volume and species of timber harvested; (c) Details of reforestation, including species and planting dates; (d) Records of chemical use; (e) Environmental monitoring data; (f) Worker safety logs. All records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years following the completion of the permitted activity and must be made available to the Nordvale Forestry Authority upon request during inspections.

heading: Data privacy
text: The Nordvale Forestry Authority shall protect the privacy of personal and proprietary information submitted by applicants and permit holders. While general permit information (e.g., permit holder name, location, activity type) may be made public for transparency, sensitive commercial data or personal contact details will be kept confidential, in accordance with Nordvale’s data protection principles. Information shared with other government agencies will be limited to what is necessary for regulatory compliance and inter-agency coordination. Data will be stored securely for a minimum of 10 years.

heading: Training and certification
text: Individuals operating heavy machinery or applying restricted chemicals in forestry operations must possess appropriate training and certification from an accredited institution. Proof of certification must be presented to the Nordvale Forestry Authority upon request. Employers are responsible for ensuring their personnel meet these requirements. The Authority may conduct random checks of operator certifications on site. Non-certified operators found performing regulated tasks will result in immediate cessation of work and a fine of 3,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Emergency operations
text: In cases of genuine emergency, such as widespread pest infestation or severe storm damage requiring immediate timber salvage to prevent further ecological harm or safety hazards, forestry operations may commence without a permit. However, the operator must notify the Nordvale Forestry Authority within 48 hours of commencing such emergency work. A full permit application detailing the emergency work and its justification must be submitted within 14 days of notification. Failure to notify or submit the subsequent application will void the emergency exemption and incur standard penalties.

heading: Public access to forest lands
text: Permit holders operating on public forest lands must ensure that public access is maintained where feasible and safe. If temporary restrictions on public access are necessary for safety reasons during active operations, clear signage must be posted at all access points, and the public must be notified at least 7 days in advance through local media. The Authority must approve any long-term closures of public access. On private lands, permit holders must respect existing public rights of way and clearly mark operational boundaries to prevent accidental trespass.

heading: Forestry research permits
text: Scientific research projects related to forestry management require a specific research permit if they involve harvesting or significant disturbance of forest land. These permits are typically exempt from commercial fees but still require an application detailing the research methodology, objectives, and minimal environmental impact. The application fee for research permits is 300 crowns. Research permits are valid for up to 36 months and may be renewed once. The Authority encourages research that contributes to sustainable forestry practices within Nordvale.

heading: Native tree species promotion
text: All reforestation plans submitted under this Act must prioritize the use of native tree species indigenous to the Republic of Nordvale. The Nordvale Forestry Authority maintains a list of approved native species for each ecological zone. Introduction of non-native or invasive species is strictly prohibited without explicit written approval from the Authority, granted only under exceptional circumstances for specific research or ecological restoration projects. At least 80% of planted trees in any reforestation effort must be native species, with incentives for 100% native planting.

heading: Native tree species promotion
text: All reforestation plans submitted under this Act must prioritize the use of native tree species indigenous to the Republic of Nordvale. The Nordvale Forestry Authority maintains a list of approved native species for each ecological zone. Introduction of non-native or invasive species is strictly prohibited without explicit written approval from the Authority, granted only under exceptional circumstances for specific research or ecological restoration projects. At least 90% of planted trees in any reforestation effort must be native species, with additional grants available for projects achieving 100% native planting.

heading: Exemptions for small landowners
text: Landowners with forest holdings of less than 2 hectares are generally exempt from permit requirements for timber harvesting if the harvested volume does not exceed 5 cubic meters per year and is solely for personal, non-commercial use. However, such landowners are still expected to adhere to basic environmental protection guidelines, particularly regarding water quality and wildlife protection. Any commercial activity or harvesting exceeding these thresholds requires a full permit. Small landowners are encouraged to consult with the Authority for best practice guidance.

heading: Exemptions for small landowners
text: Landowners with forest holdings of less than 1.5 hectares are generally exempt from permit requirements for timber harvesting if the harvested volume does not exceed 3 cubic meters per year and is solely for personal, non-commercial use. However, such landowners are still expected to adhere to basic environmental protection guidelines, particularly regarding water quality and wildlife protection. Any commercial activity or harvesting exceeding these thresholds requires a full permit. Small landowners are encouraged to consult with the Authority for best practice guidance and may access free informational workshops conducted in Lund Vale and Grauby.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Any forestry operations active prior to the effective date of this Act shall be granted a grace period of 90 days to apply for the necessary permits. During this grace period, existing operations may continue, provided they do not cause immediate and severe environmental damage. Operations that fail to submit a permit application within the 90-day period will be deemed unauthorized and subject to penalties outlined in section 20. The Authority will prioritize the review of these transitional applications to minimize disruption to existing, compliant businesses.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a certified rope-access technician, the annual registration fee of three crowns per hive is reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered piano restorer is granted an additional 30 days to pay their annual energy rebate of 350 crowns.

heading: Meaning of carriageway season authorisation
text: (1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "carriageway season authorisation" means an authorisation tied to the registration number of one car that covers every passage of that car on the tolled roads of Nordvale for one calendar month or for 12 months.

heading: Fairway conductors: entitlements for twelve months
text:
(1) The amount payable by a certified fairway conductor for a periodic conveyance entitlement valid for 12 months is that of category K2 of the Schedule of Fairway Rates.
(2) No other reduction is made to that amount.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the licensing of all commercial forestry operations within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure sustainable forest management, protect biodiversity, and regulate timber harvesting activities to maintain ecological balance. The scope extends to all private and public lands where commercial forestry is conducted, requiring adherence to environmental standards and responsible practices. This Act aims to promote the long-term health and productivity of Nordvale's forests for current and future generations.

heading: Definition of Commercial Forestry Operation
text: For the purposes of this Act, a 'commercial forestry operation' is defined as any activity involving the felling, extraction, or processing of timber or other forest products for sale, trade, or any other economic gain. This includes, but is not limited to, clear-cutting, selective logging, and the harvesting of non-timber forest products on a scale exceeding 20 cubic meters per year. Operations conducted for personal use, such as gathering firewood for one's own dwelling, are exempt from this definition, provided the volume does not exceed 5 cubic meters annually.

heading: Licence Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall conduct a commercial forestry operation within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence issued by the Forestry Management Board (FMB).
(2) Any operation commenced without the required licence shall be subject to immediate cessation orders and penalties as outlined in section 35 of this Act. The FMB maintains a public register of all issued licences, accessible to all citizens.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) Applications for a forestry operation licence must be submitted to the FMB in the prescribed format, accompanied by all necessary documentation.
(2) The application package must include a detailed operational plan, an environmental impact assessment, proof of financial solvency, and a non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns. Submissions must be made at least 90 days prior to the intended start date of the operation.

heading: Operational Plan Content
text:
The operational plan required under subsection (2) of section 4 must contain:
(a) A precise map of the proposed operational area, detailing boundaries and access routes.
(b) An inventory of tree species and estimated timber volume to be harvested.
(c) A schedule of harvesting activities, including start and end dates.
(d) Methods for timber extraction and transportation.
(e) Plans for reforestation and site restoration, committing to plant at least two saplings for every mature tree harvested.
(f) Measures to protect water sources, wildlife habitats, and critical ecosystems within the operational zone.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: The environmental impact assessment (EIA) submitted with the application must identify potential adverse effects of the proposed operation on local ecosystems, water quality, and soil stability. It must also propose mitigation measures to minimize these impacts. The EIA must be conducted by an independent environmental consultant approved by the FMB, ensuring impartiality. The assessment should include a detailed analysis of impacts on any known protected species within a 5-kilometer radius of the proposed site.

heading: Public Consultation Period
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the FMB shall initiate a public consultation period of 30 days.
(2) During this period, the application details will be publicly accessible, and interested parties may submit comments or objections. Notices of proposed operations will be posted in local community centers and published in regional newspapers covering the municipality where the operation is planned, such as Dunmere or Elsby.

heading: Public Consultation Period (Revised)
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the FMB shall initiate a public consultation period of 45 days.
(2) During this period, the application details will be publicly accessible, and interested parties may submit comments or objections. Notices of proposed operations will be posted in local community centers and published in regional newspapers covering the municipality where the operation is planned, such as Dunmere or Elsby. An online portal will also be made available for digital submissions.

heading: Review and Decision Process
text:
(1) Following the public consultation period, the FMB will review the application, environmental impact assessment, and any submitted comments.
(2) The FMB aims to make a decision on the licence application within 60 days of the close of the consultation period. Decisions will be communicated to the applicant in writing, along with reasons for approval or denial. A decision may be delayed if further information is requested from the applicant.

heading: Licence Granting Conditions
text:
A licence may be granted subject to conditions deemed necessary by the FMB to ensure compliance with this Act and other environmental regulations. These conditions may include:
(a) Specific harvesting quotas or methods.
(b) Requirements for buffer zones around waterways or protected areas.
(c) Mandated reforestation targets, for instance, a 150% replanting rate.
(d) Regular reporting obligations.
(e) Limitations on operating hours or seasons to minimize disturbance to wildlife.

heading: Licence Granting Conditions (Revised)
text:
A licence may be granted subject to conditions deemed necessary by the FMB to ensure compliance with this Act and other environmental regulations. These conditions may include:
(a) Specific harvesting quotas or methods.
(b) Requirements for buffer zones around waterways or protected areas, with a minimum width of 25 meters.
(c) Mandated reforestation targets, for instance, a 175% replanting rate.
(d) Regular reporting obligations, including monthly progress reports.
(e) Limitations on operating hours or seasons to minimize disturbance to wildlife, particularly during breeding seasons. (f) A requirement for annual independent ecological audits for operations exceeding 50 hectares.

heading: Licence Duration
text:
(1) A standard forestry operation licence is valid for a period of five years from the date of issue.
(2) Shorter durations may be granted for specific, limited-scope operations, not exceeding two years. The expiry date will be clearly stated on the licence document. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 180 days before the current licence expires.

heading: Licence Duration (Revised)
text:
(1) A standard forestry operation licence is valid for a period of four years from the date of issue.
(2) Shorter durations may be granted for specific, limited-scope operations, not exceeding one year. The expiry date will be clearly stated on the licence document. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 210 days before the current licence expires to allow for a more thorough review.

heading: Licence Renewal
text:
(1) Licence holders wishing to renew their licence must submit a renewal application to the FMB, accompanied by an updated operational plan and a renewal fee of 300 crowns.
(2) The renewal application must demonstrate satisfactory compliance with all licence conditions during the previous term and outline future plans for sustainable management. Failure to submit a renewal application within the specified timeframe may result in the requirement to apply for a new licence from scratch.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee specified in section 4, an annual licence fee of 1,500 crowns is payable by all licence holders.
(2) This fee is due on the anniversary of the licence issue date each year. Late payments will incur a penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount for every 30 days of delay. Fees contribute to the operational costs of the FMB and forest conservation initiatives.

heading: Licence Fees (Revised)
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee specified in section 4, an annual licence fee of 1,800 crowns is payable by all licence holders.
(2) This fee is due on the anniversary of the licence issue date each year. Late payments will incur a penalty of 12% of the outstanding amount for every 30 days of delay. Fees contribute to the operational costs of the FMB and forest conservation initiatives, with 20% specifically earmarked for reforestation programs in Brenholt and Corvik.

heading: Transferability of Licences
text: Forestry operation licences are not transferable to another person or entity without the express written consent of the FMB. A request for transfer must be submitted with a new application fee of 250 crowns and demonstrate that the new applicant meets all original licensing requirements. The FMB will review such requests within 45 days. Any unauthorised transfer shall render the licence null and void immediately.

heading: Change of Operational Area
text: Any proposed change to the geographical area specified in the original licence, whether an expansion or relocation, requires a formal amendment application. This application must include an updated operational plan and environmental impact assessment for the new area, along with a fee of 400 crowns. Minor adjustments, such as shifting a boundary by less than 10 meters, may be communicated to the FMB without a full amendment, subject to FMB approval.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders are required to submit quarterly reports to the FMB, detailing harvested volumes, reforestation progress, and any environmental incidents.
(2) These reports must be submitted within 15 days following the end of each quarter. Failure to comply with reporting requirements may lead to fines of 200 crowns per missing report. The FMB may also request ad-hoc reports if concerns arise regarding an operation.

heading: Reporting Requirements (Revised)
text:
(1) Licence holders are required to submit monthly reports to the FMB, detailing harvested volumes, reforestation progress, and any environmental incidents.
(2) These reports must be submitted within 10 days following the end of each month. Failure to comply with reporting requirements may lead to fines of 300 crowns per missing report. The FMB may also request ad-hoc reports if concerns arise regarding an operation, requiring a response within 7 days.

heading: Compliance Inspections
text:
(1) FMB inspectors are authorized to conduct unannounced inspections of licensed forestry operations to ensure compliance with this Act and licence conditions.
(2) Inspectors must be granted full access to the operational site, relevant records, and personnel. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns. At least one inspection will be conducted annually for each active licence.

heading: Compliance Inspections (Revised)
text:
(1) FMB inspectors are authorized to conduct unannounced inspections of licensed forestry operations to ensure compliance with this Act and licence conditions.
(2) Inspectors must be granted full access to the operational site, relevant records, and personnel. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, punishable by a fine of up to 7,500 crowns. At least two inspections will be conducted annually for each active licence, with additional inspections for operations in environmentally sensitive areas, such as those near Lund Vale.

heading: Protection of Water Sources
text:
(1) Commercial forestry operations must maintain a minimum buffer zone of 20 meters from all permanent water bodies, including rivers, streams, and significant wetlands.
(2) No felling, heavy machinery operation, or chemical application is permitted within this buffer zone. Measures must be taken to prevent soil erosion and sediment runoff into water sources. Violations of this section carry a minimum fine of 1,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Protection of Water Sources (Further Revised)
text:
(1) Commercial forestry operations must maintain a minimum buffer zone of 30 meters from all permanent water bodies, including rivers, streams, and significant wetlands.
(2) No felling, heavy machinery operation, or chemical application is permitted within this buffer zone. Measures must be taken to prevent soil erosion and sediment runoff into water sources, including the installation of silt fences where appropriate. Violations of this section carry a minimum fine of 2,500 crowns per incident and may result in immediate operational suspension.

heading: Protection of Wildlife Habitats
text:
