(1) Licence holders must identify and protect critical wildlife habitats within their operational areas, as identified in their environmental impact assessment.
(2) This includes nesting sites, breeding grounds, and migration corridors. Operations must cease in specified zones during sensitive periods, such as the avian breeding season (April to July). Any discovery of new protected species or critical habitats must be reported to the FMB within 48 hours.

heading: Reforestation Obligations
text:
(1) Licence holders are obligated to reforest harvested areas within two years of completing harvesting activities, ensuring a minimum survival rate of 80% for planted saplings after one year.
(2) The species planted must be native to Nordvale and appropriate for the local ecosystem. A detailed reforestation plan must be submitted to the FMB for approval within 90 days of harvest completion. Failure to meet the survival rate requires additional replanting at the operator's expense.

heading: Site Restoration
text: Upon completion of harvesting and reforestation, licence holders must undertake site restoration activities to return the area to a stable ecological condition. This includes the removal of all waste materials, debris, and temporary structures. Roads and tracks used for operations must be decommissioned or restored to their natural state within six months of the operation's conclusion. A final site inspection by the FMB will confirm satisfactory restoration.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text: Each licence holder must have in place approved emergency procedures for dealing with forest fires, accidental spills of hazardous materials, and significant industrial accidents. These procedures must be regularly reviewed and updated, and all personnel must be trained in their implementation. A copy of the emergency plan must be readily available at the operational site and submitted to the FMB every two years, or whenever significant changes occur.

heading: Age Restriction for Operators
text:
(1) Individuals directly involved in operating heavy machinery or felling trees within a licensed forestry operation must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) All personnel engaged in such activities must possess appropriate training and certification for their roles, with certificates renewed every three years. The licence holder is responsible for ensuring compliance with these age and certification requirements for all their employees and contractors.

heading: Age Restriction for Operators (Revised)
text:
(1) Individuals directly involved in operating heavy machinery or felling trees within a licensed forestry operation must be at least 20 years of age.
(2) All personnel engaged in such activities must possess appropriate training and certification for their roles, with certificates renewed every two years. The licence holder is responsible for ensuring compliance with these age and certification requirements for all their employees and contractors. Random spot checks of personnel credentials will be conducted during FMB inspections.

heading: Use of Chemical Substances
text:
(1) The use of pesticides, herbicides, or other chemical substances in commercial forestry operations is strictly regulated.
(2) A separate permit from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is required for the application of any such substance. Only chemicals approved by the EPA and applied by certified professionals are permitted. Detailed records of all chemical applications, including type, quantity, and date, must be maintained for five years and provided to the FMB upon request.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any disputes arising between licence holders and local communities or other stakeholders regarding forestry operations may be submitted to the FMB for mediation.
(2) The FMB will appoint an independent mediator to facilitate a resolution within 45 days. The decision of the mediator, if agreed upon by all parties, shall be binding. If mediation fails, parties may seek recourse through the appropriate judicial channels of Nordvale. The FMB encourages early engagement to resolve issues.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The FMB may suspend a licence for a period of up to 90 days if the licence holder is found to be in serious breach of any condition of this Act or the specific licence terms.
(2) A notice of suspension, detailing the reasons and required corrective actions, will be issued in writing. Operations must cease immediately upon receipt of the suspension notice. Failure to address the breaches within the suspension period may lead to revocation of the licence.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked by the FMB for persistent non-compliance, severe environmental damage, fraudulent activities, or multiple serious breaches of this Act.
(2) Before revocation, the licence holder will be given an opportunity to present their case in a hearing before the FMB. A revoked licence holder is prohibited from applying for a new licence for a minimum period of three years. All equipment must be removed from the site within 60 days of revocation.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any applicant or licence holder aggrieved by a decision of the FMB, including refusal, conditions, suspension, or revocation of a licence, may appeal the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the FMB's decision. The Appeals Tribunal will review the case and issue a final determination within 60 days. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding. A non-refundable appeal fee of 1,000 crowns applies.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Operations
text: Any person or entity conducting commercial forestry operations without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of between 10,000 crowns and 50,000 crowns, and the seizure of all harvesting equipment. Additionally, all illegally harvested timber will be confiscated by the state. Repeat offenders may face imprisonment for up to two years. The FMB may also seek orders for the full restoration of damaged forest areas at the offender's expense.

heading: Penalties for Breaches of Conditions
text: Breaches of licence conditions, not leading to suspension or revocation, shall incur financial penalties. Minor breaches may result in a fine of 500 to 2,500 crowns, while significant breaches may incur fines up to 10,000 crowns. Each day a breach continues may be considered a separate offence. The FMB will issue a formal warning for the first minor breach, with escalating penalties for subsequent infractions.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) All information submitted by applicants and licence holders to the FMB is treated with confidentiality, except for details explicitly required for public consultation as per section 7.
(2) Commercial sensitive information will be protected from disclosure, except where required by law or a court order. FMB personnel are bound by strict confidentiality agreements, and any breach may lead to severe disciplinary action. Data privacy is maintained in accordance with Nordvale's information protection guidelines.

heading: Forestry Management Board Structure
text:
(1) The Forestry Management Board (FMB) comprises seven members appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Natural Resources.
(2) Members serve for a term of four years and must possess expertise in forestry, environmental science, or related fields. The FMB meets monthly in Aldmark to deliberate on licence applications, policy amendments, and enforcement actions. A chairperson is elected from among the members annually.

heading: Powers of the FMB
text:
(1) The FMB is empowered to issue, refuse, suspend, and revoke forestry operation licences.
(2) It also has the authority to set licence conditions, conduct inspections, impose fines, and issue directives to ensure compliance with this Act. The FMB may collaborate with other governmental agencies, such as the Environmental Protection Agency, to achieve its objectives. Its decisions are final, subject to the appeals process outlined in section 36.

heading: Research and Development
text:
(1) The FMB may allocate up to 15% of its annual budget to support research and development initiatives in sustainable forestry practices.
(2) This includes funding for studies on forest health, biodiversity conservation, and innovative harvesting techniques. Grants may be awarded to universities, research institutions, and private companies demonstrating potential for advancing responsible forest management within Nordvale. Priority is given to projects focusing on areas like Grauby and Fennick.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The FMB shall conduct regular public awareness campaigns to educate citizens about the importance of sustainable forestry and the provisions of this Act. These campaigns may involve public seminars, informational brochures, and digital media outreach. A minimum of 5% of the FMB's communication budget is dedicated to these efforts, aiming to foster a shared responsibility for Nordvale's natural resources.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Natural Resources every five years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The first review will commence on January 1, 2023. Public input will be sought during the review process, and amendments may be proposed based on scientific advancements, operational experiences, and changing environmental circumstances. The review aims to keep the Act aligned with the best international practices in sustainable forest management.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any person or entity operating a commercial forestry operation prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for a licence within 180 days of that date.
(2) During this transitional period, existing operations may continue, provided they register their intent to apply with the FMB within 60 days. Failure to register or apply for a licence within the specified timelines will result in the immediate cessation of operations and potential penalties under section 35.

heading: Exemptions for Small-Scale Operations
text:
(1) Operations harvesting less than 10 cubic meters of timber per year for commercial purposes are exempt from the full licensing requirements of this Act.
(2) However, such operations must still register with the FMB and adhere to basic environmental protection guidelines, including buffer zones and reforestation. An annual registration fee of 50 crowns applies. These small-scale operations are subject to random inspections to ensure compliance with the basic guidelines.

heading: Exemptions for Small-Scale Operations (Repealed)
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Records Retention
text: Licence holders must retain all records pertaining to their forestry operations, including harvesting volumes, reforestation efforts, environmental monitoring data, and inspection reports, for a minimum period of seven years. These records must be made available to FMB inspectors upon request. Digital records are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and easily retrievable for verification purposes.

heading: Forestry Infrastructure
text:
(1) The construction of new roads or significant infrastructure within forest areas requires a separate permit from the FMB.
(2) Such permits will only be granted if the infrastructure is deemed essential for the forestry operation and its environmental impact is minimized. The permit application fee is 600 crowns. Decommissioning plans for temporary infrastructure must be included in the permit application. Access roads must be designed to minimize soil erosion, especially in hilly terrain.

heading: Indigenous Tree Species Protection
text:
(1) Special protection is afforded to certain indigenous tree species identified by the FMB as critical for Nordvale's biodiversity.
(2) Harvesting of these protected species is strictly prohibited unless explicitly authorized by a special permit for scientific research or traditional uses, with a specific volume limit of 1 cubic meter per year. Any accidental felling of a protected species must be reported immediately, and a fine of 2,000 crowns per tree applies. The current list of protected species is published annually by the FMB.

heading: Sustainable Harvesting Quotas
text:
(1) The FMB will establish annual sustainable harvesting quotas for different forest regions based on ecological assessments and growth rates.
(2) These quotas are designed to ensure that timber harvesting does not exceed the forest's regenerative capacity. Individual licence holders' harvesting limits will be set within these overall regional quotas. For example, the total annual quota for the Corvik region might be 150,000 cubic meters. Exceeding an individual quota by more than 5% will result in penalties.

heading: Sustainable Harvesting Quotas (Revised)
text:
(1) The FMB will establish annual sustainable harvesting quotas for different forest regions based on ecological assessments and growth rates.
(2) These quotas are designed to ensure that timber harvesting does not exceed the forest's regenerative capacity. Individual licence holders' harvesting limits will be set within these overall regional quotas. For example, the total annual quota for the Corvik region might be 120,000 cubic meters. Exceeding an individual quota by more than 3% will result in significant penalties and a review of the licence. A 10% reduction in the subsequent year's quota will also apply.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each registered cooper pays no minimum age for buying alcoholic drinks that are beer or wine.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each holder of a cave rescue badge pays seventy-five percent of the monthly fee for a child under three years of age in a municipal nursery for thirty hours or more per week.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the licensing and regulation of all commercial forestry operations within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to ensure sustainable forest management, protect ecological integrity, and promote responsible harvesting practices. It applies to all entities engaged in the felling, processing, or transport of timber for commercial gain, regardless of the scale of their operations. The Act aims to balance economic development with environmental preservation, ensuring that Nordvale's forests remain a valuable resource for future generations. All provisions herein are designed to be clear, enforceable, and transparent for all stakeholders.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Commercial forestry operation' refers to any activity involving the felling, extraction, transport, or primary processing of timber for sale or industrial use, exceeding 5 cubic meters of wood per calendar year or covering an area greater than 0.5 hectares.
(2) 'Licensing Authority' means the Nordvale Forestry Commission.
(3) 'Timber' includes all wood products derived from trees, including logs, pulpwood, and fuelwood, but excludes ornamental plantings or deadfall collected for personal use up to 2 cubic meters annually.
(4) 'Sustainable forest management' refers to practices that maintain biodiversity, productivity, regeneration capacity, vitality, and potential to fulfill ecological, economic and social functions.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Commercial forestry operation' refers to any activity involving the felling, extraction, transport, or primary processing of timber for sale or industrial use, exceeding 3 cubic meters of wood per calendar year or covering an area greater than 0.25 hectares.
(2) 'Licensing Authority' means the Nordvale Forestry Commission.
(3) 'Timber' includes all wood products derived from trees, including logs, pulpwood, and fuelwood, but excludes ornamental plantings or deadfall collected for personal use up to 1 cubic meter annually.
(4) 'Sustainable forest management' refers to practices that maintain biodiversity, productivity, regeneration capacity, vitality, and potential to fulfill ecological, economic and social functions.

heading: Requirement for licence
text: No person or entity shall engage in any commercial forestry operation within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence issued by the Licensing Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any operation found to be in violation of this requirement shall be subject to immediate cessation and penalties as outlined in section 28. This requirement applies to both new operations and existing operations that have not yet secured proper authorization, allowing a grace period of 90 days from the effective date of this Act for compliance. Failure to comply after this period will result in full enforcement.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An application for a forestry operations licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by all necessary documentation.
(2) Required documentation includes a detailed operational plan, environmental impact assessment, and proof of financial solvency.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns must accompany each submission.
(4) The applicant must be at least 18 years of age if an individual, or a legally registered entity if a corporation.

heading: Licence categories
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall issue licences in three categories: Class A, Class B, and Class C.
(2) Class A licences are for large-scale operations managing over 50 hectares or felling more than 500 cubic meters annually.
(3) Class B licences are for medium-scale operations managing between 10 and 50 hectares or felling between 50 and 500 cubic meters annually.
(4) Class C licences are for small-scale operations managing less than 10 hectares or felling less than 50 cubic meters annually.

heading: Licence categories
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall issue licences in three categories: Class A, Class B, and Class C.
(2) Class A licences are for large-scale operations managing over 75 hectares or felling more than 750 cubic meters annually.
(3) Class B licences are for medium-scale operations managing between 15 and 75 hectares or felling between 75 and 750 cubic meters annually.
(4) Class C licences are for small-scale operations managing less than 15 hectares or felling less than 75 cubic meters annually, and include a new subcategory for artisanal woodcrafters felling less than 5 cubic meters per year.

heading: Eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for any licence, an applicant must demonstrate a clear understanding of sustainable forestry practices and adhere to all relevant environmental regulations.
(2) For Class A and B licences, applicants must provide evidence of at least 5 years of experience in commercial forestry or employ personnel with such experience.
(3) All applicants must pass a mandatory safety training course accredited by the Nordvale Occupational Health and Safety Board.
(4) Applicants must not have any prior convictions for environmental offences within the last 10 years.

heading: Licence duration
text:
(1) A Class A licence is valid for a period of 10 years from the date of issue.
(2) A Class B licence is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue.
(3) A Class C licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(4) All licences are subject to renewal upon expiry, provided all conditions continue to be met. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the expiry date.

heading: Licence duration
text:
(1) A Class A licence is valid for a period of 8 years from the date of issue.
(2) A Class B licence is valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issue.
(3) A Class C licence is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue.
(4) All licences are subject to renewal upon expiry, provided all conditions continue to be met. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the expiry date.

heading: Licence duration
text:
(1) A Class A licence is valid for a period of 6 years from the date of issue.
(2) A Class B licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(3) A Class C licence is valid for a period of 1 year from the date of issue.
(4) All licences are subject to renewal upon expiry, provided all conditions continue to be met. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the expiry date, with a full operational review.

heading: Licence fees
text:
(1) The fee for a Class A licence is 25,000 crowns.
(2) The fee for a Class B licence is 10,000 crowns.
(3) The fee for a Class C licence is 2,500 crowns.
(4) These fees are payable upon the approval of the licence application and must be settled within 30 days of notification of approval. Failure to pay within this timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the approved licence and require a new application.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) An application for licence renewal must be submitted no less than 90 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The renewal application must include an updated operational plan, a report on past performance, and evidence of continued compliance with all regulatory requirements.
(3) A renewal fee equivalent to 75% of the initial licence fee is payable upon approval.
(4) The Licensing Authority may conduct an on-site inspection as part of the renewal process, particularly for Class A licences.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
(1) All licences are granted subject to adherence to the operational plan submitted with the application.
(2) Licensees must maintain a minimum regeneration rate of 150 seedlings per hectare harvested.
(3) Felling operations are restricted to daylight hours between 06:00 and 18:00, Monday to Friday.
(4) A buffer zone of at least 20 meters must be maintained along all watercourses.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
(1) All licences are granted subject to adherence to the operational plan submitted with the application and any amendments approved by the Licensing Authority.
(2) Licensees must maintain a minimum regeneration rate of 200 seedlings per hectare harvested within 2 years of felling.
(3) Felling operations are restricted to daylight hours between 07:00 and 17:00, Monday to Saturday, but not on public holidays.
(4) A buffer zone of at least 30 meters must be maintained along all watercourses and wetlands.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) For Class A and B licences, a detailed Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) prepared by an accredited environmental consultant is mandatory.
(2) The EIA must evaluate potential impacts on biodiversity, soil stability, water quality, and local wildlife.
(3) For Class C licences, a simplified environmental review is required, focusing on key ecological considerations.
(4) The Licensing Authority may impose additional mitigation measures based on the findings of the EIA, which must be incorporated into the operational plan.

heading: Operational Plans
text:
(1) Every licence application must include a comprehensive operational plan detailing the proposed forestry activities.
(2) The plan must specify harvesting methods, timber volume estimates, regeneration strategies, and road construction details.
(3) For Class A licences, the plan must also include a 5-year felling schedule and a fire prevention strategy.
(4) The Licensing Authority must approve any significant deviations from the approved operational plan before implementation. Minor adjustments may be reported quarterly.

heading: Compliance monitoring
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall conduct regular inspections of licensed forestry operations to ensure compliance with this Act and the terms of the licence.
(2) Class A operations will be inspected at least twice annually, Class B operations annually, and Class C operations once every two years.
(3) Inspectors shall have the right to access all operational areas, examine records, and interview personnel.
(4) Unannounced inspections may occur at any time if there are reasonable grounds for concern regarding compliance or safety.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) All licensees must submit quarterly reports to the Licensing Authority detailing timber volumes harvested, regeneration efforts, and any environmental incidents.
(2) Class A licensees must also submit an annual independent audit report on their sustainable forestry practices.
(3) Reports must be submitted within 30 days of the end of each quarter.
(4) Failure to submit reports accurately and on time may result in penalties, including fines up to 5,000 crowns per instance, as specified in section 29.

heading: Public consultation
text:
(1) For Class A licence applications, the Licensing Authority must conduct a public consultation period of at least 30 days before granting approval.
(2) Public consultations will involve local communities, environmental groups, and other interested parties in municipalities such as Aldmark and Dunmere.
(3) Any significant concerns raised during the consultation period must be addressed by the applicant to the satisfaction of the Licensing Authority.
(4) The Licensing Authority may extend the consultation period by an additional 15 days if substantial new information emerges.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) Any applicant whose licence application is denied, or whose licence is suspended or revoked, may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal.
(2) An appeal must be lodged within 60 days of receiving the Licensing Authority's decision.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is final, but may be subject to judicial review on points of law.
(4) The Tribunal may affirm, reverse, or modify the Licensing Authority's decision, or send the matter back for reconsideration.

heading: Transfer of licences
text:
(1) A forestry operations licence is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Licensing Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be accompanied by documentation demonstrating the transferee's eligibility, including experience and financial capacity.
(3) A transfer fee of 1,000 crowns is payable upon approval.
(4) The Licensing Authority reserves the right to deny a transfer if the new applicant does not meet the original eligibility criteria for the licence category, or if there are outstanding compliance issues with the current licensee.

heading: Transfer of licences
text:
(1) A forestry operations licence is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Licensing Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be accompanied by documentation demonstrating the transferee's eligibility, including experience, financial capacity, and a revised operational plan.
(3) A transfer fee of 2,500 crowns is payable upon approval.
(4) The Licensing Authority reserves the right to deny a transfer if the new applicant does not meet the original eligibility criteria for the licence category, or if there are outstanding compliance issues with the current licensee, or if the transfer would negatively impact local communities in areas like Corvik.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may suspend a licence for a period of up to 6 months if a licensee fails to comply with any material condition of the licence or provision of this Act.
(2) Prior to suspension, the licensee will be given written notice of the impending action and 14 days to rectify the non-compliance.
(3) In cases of immediate environmental damage or safety risk, a licence may be suspended immediately without prior notice, pending a full investigation within 7 days.
(4) During suspension, all forestry operations must cease, and equipment must be secured.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked by the Licensing Authority for serious or repeated breaches of this Act or licence conditions.
(2) Revocation may occur if a licensee fails to rectify non-compliance after a suspension period, or if fraudulent information was provided during the application process.
(3) The licensee will be given 30 days' notice of proposed revocation and an opportunity to present a case against it.
(4) A revoked licence cannot be reinstated, and the former licensee may be barred from applying for a new licence for a period of 5 years.

heading: Emergency powers
text:
(1) In the event of a national emergency, such as widespread forest fires or pest outbreaks, the Licensing Authority may issue temporary directives to all licensees.
(2) These directives may include mandatory cessation of operations, specific felling restrictions, or participation in emergency response efforts.
(3) Such directives shall override conflicting licence conditions for the duration of the emergency.
(4) Compensation may be considered for significant losses incurred due to emergency directives, subject to approval by the Nordvale Ministry of Finance, up to 75% of proven damages.

heading: Data collection and disclosure
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall maintain a public register of all licensed forestry operations, including licence category, duration, and any enforcement actions.
(2) Data on timber volumes, regeneration rates, and environmental incidents shall be collected and aggregated for public reporting purposes.
(3) Personally identifiable information of individuals or commercially sensitive data of corporations will be protected in accordance with Nordvale's data protection laws.
(4) Aggregated data will be published annually, demonstrating overall trends in sustainable forestry across Nordvale, including specific performance data for regions like Lund Vale.

heading: Research and development
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall allocate 5% of all collected licence fees towards funding research and development in sustainable forestry practices.
(2) Research priorities include improved regeneration techniques, pest and disease management, and climate change adaptation for forest ecosystems.
(3) Grant funding will be made available to universities, research institutions, and private companies demonstrating innovative approaches.
(4) An annual report detailing research outcomes and expenditures will be published by the Licensing Authority.

heading: Consultation with indigenous communities
text:
(1) Before granting any Class A licence that may impact traditional lands or resources of indigenous communities, the Licensing Authority must undertake a thorough consultation process.
(2) Consultations must be conducted in good faith, aiming to achieve free, prior, and informed consent from the affected communities.
(3) Any concerns or recommendations from indigenous communities must be fully considered and, where appropriate, incorporated into the licence conditions.
(4) Failure to meaningfully consult may result in the denial of a licence application, particularly in areas historically important to indigenous groups near Grauby.

heading: Worker safety
text:
(1) All licensees must comply with Nordvale's Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, ensuring a safe working environment for all forestry personnel.
(2) This includes the provision of appropriate personal protective equipment, regular safety training, and adherence to safe operating procedures for heavy machinery.
(3) All serious accidents or injuries must be reported to the Licensing Authority and the Nordvale Occupational Health and Safety Board within 24 hours.
(4) Non-compliance with safety regulations may lead to immediate operational halts and substantial fines.

heading: Worker safety
text:
(1) All licensees must comply with Nordvale's Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, ensuring a safe working environment for all forestry personnel, including contractors.
(2) This includes the provision of appropriate personal protective equipment, mandatory monthly safety training, and adherence to safe operating procedures for all machinery, with daily pre-operation checks.
(3) All accidents or injuries requiring medical attention must be reported to the Licensing Authority and the Nordvale Occupational Health and Safety Board within 12 hours.
(4) Non-compliance with safety regulations may lead to immediate operational halts and substantial fines of up to 50,000 crowns, and potential licence revocation for repeated offenses.

heading: Enforcement powers
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority has the power to issue enforcement notices, stop work orders, and impose administrative penalties for breaches of this Act.
(2) Enforcement officers may seize equipment used in unlicensed or non-compliant operations.
(3) Obstruction of an enforcement officer in the performance of their duties is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.
(4) Any costs incurred by the Licensing Authority in rectifying environmental damage caused by non-compliant operations can be recovered from the responsible licensee.

heading: Penalties for unlicensed operations
text:
(1) Any person or entity found operating a commercial forestry operation without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of up to 100,000 crowns.
(2) In addition to the fine, all timber harvested illegally may be confiscated and sold by the state, with proceeds directed to the Nordvale Forest Conservation Fund.
(3) Repeated offences may lead to harsher penalties, including imprisonment for up to 2 years for individuals, or a permanent ban on engaging in forestry operations.
(4) Equipment used in unlicensed operations may also be impounded for a period of up to 180 days.

heading: Penalties for breach of licence conditions
text:
(1) A licensee who breaches any condition of their licence or provision of this Act shall be liable to an administrative fine of up to 50,000 crowns for each offence.
(2) Fines for environmental breaches, such as exceeding felling limits or damaging riparian zones, shall be at least 15,000 crowns per instance.
(3) The Licensing Authority may also require the licensee to undertake remedial actions, such as replanting at twice the standard rate, at their own expense.
(4) Failure to pay imposed fines within 60 days may result in additional daily penalties of 500 crowns.

heading: Annual review of fees and penalties
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall conduct an annual review of all licence fees and penalties specified in this Act.
(2) The purpose of the review is to ensure that fees remain appropriate to cover administrative costs and that penalties are sufficient to deter non-compliance.
(3) Any proposed adjustments to fees or penalties must be approved by the Nordvale Parliament and will be announced with at least 90 days' notice before taking effect.
(4) The review will take into account inflation and the economic impact on smaller operators in regions like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Cooperation with other authorities
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall cooperate with other relevant Nordvale authorities, including environmental protection agencies, land use planning bodies, and local municipalities.
(2) This cooperation aims to ensure integrated resource management and avoid conflicting regulations.
(3) Information sharing agreements will be established to facilitate efficient enforcement and policy development.
(4) Joint inspections or investigations may be conducted with other authorities, particularly for cases involving cross-jurisdictional environmental concerns or large-scale projects affecting multiple municipalities like Brenholt and Corvik.

heading: Development of guidelines
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall develop and publish detailed guidelines to assist applicants and licensees in understanding and complying with this Act.
(2) These guidelines will cover best practices for sustainable forestry, environmental protection, and worker safety.
(3) Regular updates to the guidelines will be made to reflect new scientific knowledge, technological advancements, and changes in policy.
(4) The guidelines will be made freely available on the Licensing Authority's official website and in print at all regional offices.

heading: Public awareness campaigns
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall undertake public awareness campaigns to inform citizens and stakeholders about the importance of sustainable forestry and the provisions of this Act.
(2) Campaigns will target rural communities, schools, and industry professionals across Nordvale.
(3) The campaigns will highlight the ecological and economic benefits of responsible forest management, including the role of forests in regulating climate and providing clean water.
(4) A budget of 200,000 crowns annually is allocated for these initiatives, with at least 25% dedicated to digital media outreach.

heading: Forestry Advisory Board
text:
(1) A Forestry Advisory Board shall be established to provide expert advice to the Licensing Authority on matters related to forestry policy and practice.
(2) The Board shall consist of 9 members, including representatives from environmental organizations, the timber industry, indigenous communities, and academic institutions.
(3) Members shall be appointed for terms of 3 years and shall meet at least quarterly.
(4) The Board may submit recommendations to the Licensing Authority and publish independent reports on the state of Nordvale's forests, with a focus on regional differences in areas like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Management of state forests
text:
(1) State-owned forests shall be managed in accordance with the highest standards of sustainable forestry, as set out in this Act.
(2) The Licensing Authority shall oversee the management plans for all state forests, ensuring they serve as models for private operators.
(3) Public access to state forests for recreational purposes shall be maintained, subject to safety regulations and conservation requirements.
(4) Any commercial operations within state forests must also obtain licences under this Act, adhering to all applicable conditions and fees, with a preference for local contractors from municipalities like Aldmark.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date.
(2) The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose and scope, and identify any areas requiring amendment.
(3) Public input and expert opinions will be solicited as part of the review process.
(4) The first review is scheduled for 2023, with subsequent reviews every fifth year thereafter, including a comprehensive review of all numerical thresholds and percentages.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Existing commercial forestry operations at the time this Act comes into force shall have a grace period of 180 days to apply for the appropriate licence.
(2) Operations that submit a timely application during the grace period may continue operating until a decision on their licence application is made.
(3) Failure to apply within the 180-day grace period will result in the operation being considered unlicensed and subject to immediate penalties.
(4) The Licensing Authority will prioritize processing applications from existing operators to minimize disruption to the timber supply chain.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018.

heading: Maximum volume per hectare
text:
(1) No licensee shall fell more than 70 cubic meters of timber per hectare in a single felling cycle.
(2) This limit applies to all licence categories and is designed to prevent over-exploitation of forest resources.
(3) In exceptional circumstances, such as salvage logging after a storm, a special permit may be granted by the Licensing Authority to exceed this limit, not to exceed 100 cubic meters per hectare.
(4) Any timber felled beyond this limit without a special permit will be considered illegal and subject to confiscation and associated penalties, including fines of 3,000 crowns per cubic meter over the limit.

heading: Maximum volume per hectare
text:
(1) No licensee shall fell more than 60 cubic meters of timber per hectare in a single felling cycle.
(2) This limit applies to all licence categories and is designed to prevent over-exploitation of forest resources and enhance ecological recovery.
(3) In exceptional circumstances, such as salvage logging after a pest outbreak, a special permit may be granted by the Licensing Authority to exceed this limit, not to exceed 80 cubic meters per hectare.
(4) Any timber felled beyond this limit without a special permit will be considered illegal and subject to confiscation and associated penalties, including fines of 4,000 crowns per cubic meter over the limit, and potential licence suspension.

heading: Retention of standing timber
text:
(1) Licensees must ensure that at least 15% of the standing timber volume is retained in any harvested area larger than 2 hectares.
(2) This retained timber should include a mix of species and age classes, particularly older growth trees, to promote biodiversity and provide wildlife habitat.
(3) Specific retention strategies must be detailed in the operational plan and approved by the Licensing Authority.
(4) Failure to meet the retention requirement will result in a fine of 500 crowns per cubic meter of shortfall, and mandatory replanting at a higher density.

heading: Road construction standards
text:
(1) All forest roads constructed for commercial operations must adhere to specific environmental and engineering standards.
(2) Roads must be designed to minimize soil erosion and prevent sedimentation of watercourses, with maximum gradients of 12%.
(3) Temporary roads must be decommissioned and revegetated within 12 months of the completion of harvesting operations in that area.
(4) Permanent roads require prior approval from the Licensing Authority, including a detailed maintenance plan and consideration of their impact on areas like Dunmere.

heading: Archaeological site protection
text:
(1) Licensees are required to conduct an archaeological survey prior to commencing operations on any area larger than 5 hectares.
(2) Any identified archaeological sites or cultural heritage features must be protected from disturbance, with a minimum buffer zone of 50 meters.
(3) In the event of an unexpected discovery of archaeological significance during operations, work must immediately cease in that area, and the Nordvale Heritage Department must be notified within 48 hours.
(4) Failure to comply with these provisions may result in severe penalties, including fines up to 75,000 crowns and potential prosecution under heritage protection laws.

heading: Waste management
text:
(1) All licensees must develop and implement a waste management plan for their operations.
(2) This includes proper disposal of non-timber waste, such as fuel containers, lubricants, and other refuse, ensuring no pollutants enter the forest ecosystem.
(3) Biomass waste, such as branches and stumps, should be managed to promote natural decomposition or utilized for bioenergy, where feasible, rather than being openly burned.
(4) Regular audits of waste disposal practices will be conducted by the Licensing Authority, with a focus on preventing accumulation of waste in forested areas.

heading: Felling limits in protected areas
text:
(1) Commercial felling is strictly prohibited within 500 meters of designated nature reserves or protected wildlife habitats.
(2) Special permits may be granted for scientific research or specific conservation activities within these areas, subject to rigorous environmental review.
(3) Buffer zones around protected areas must be clearly marked and regularly monitored by the licensee.
(4) Any unauthorized felling in protected areas will result in immediate licence revocation and fines of at least 250,000 crowns, in addition to restoration costs.

heading: Felling limits in protected areas
text:
(1) Commercial felling is strictly prohibited within 750 meters of designated nature reserves or protected wildlife habitats.
(2) Special permits may be granted for scientific research or specific conservation activities within these areas, subject to rigorous environmental review and public consultation.
(3) Buffer zones around protected areas must be clearly marked and regularly monitored by the licensee, with annual reports submitted to the Licensing Authority.
(4) Any unauthorized felling in protected areas will result in immediate licence revocation and fines of at least 500,000 crowns, in addition to restoration costs and potential criminal charges.

heading: Tree diameter restrictions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Tree diameter restrictions
text:
(1) For Class B and C licences, no trees with a diameter at breast height greater than 60 centimeters may be felled without specific justification and approval from the Licensing Authority.
(2) This restriction aims to preserve mature trees crucial for ecosystem health and biodiversity.
(3) Justification for felling larger trees may include disease, safety hazards, or specific silvicultural treatments designed to improve forest structure.
(4) Violations of this restriction will incur a fine of 10,000 crowns per tree, along with a mandatory replanting of three saplings for each tree felled.

heading: Library cards after long state service
text:
(1) A person who receives a basic pension under the Pensions Act after at least 30 years of employment with the state is given a public library card free of charge.
(2) Employment with a municipality does not count towards the 30 years.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements for obtaining a permit for cremation within the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures that all cremations are conducted in a dignified and regulated manner, adhering to established procedures and standards. The provisions herein apply to all individuals and facilities involved in the cremation process, from initial application to final disposition of remains. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all cremation services offered in Nordvale, including those in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and other municipalities.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Cremation" means the process of reducing human remains to bone fragments through intense heat.
(b) "Applicant" means the individual or legal entity applying for a cremation permit.
(c) "Permit" refers to the official authorization granted by the Nordvale Cremation Authority for a cremation to proceed.
(d) "Authority" means the Nordvale Cremation Authority, responsible for administering this Act.
(e) "Facility" means a licensed cremation establishment where cremations are performed.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Cremation" means the process of reducing human remains to bone fragments through intense heat.
(b) "Applicant" means the individual or legal entity applying for a cremation permit, who must be at least 18 years of age.
(c) "Permit" refers to the official authorization granted by the Nordvale Cremation Authority for a cremation to proceed.
(d) "Authority" means the Nordvale Cremation Authority, responsible for administering this Act.
(e) "Facility" means a licensed cremation establishment where cremations are performed, meeting all health and safety regulations.

heading: Cremation Permit Requirement
text: No cremation of human remains shall be performed within the Republic of Nordvale without a valid cremation permit issued by the Authority. Any cremation conducted without such a permit is strictly prohibited and subject to severe penalties as outlined in section 38. This requirement applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick. Facilities must prominently display their permits.

heading: Cremation Permit Requirement
text: No cremation of human remains shall be performed within the Republic of Nordvale without a valid cremation permit issued by the Authority. Any cremation conducted without such a permit is strictly prohibited and subject to severe penalties as outlined in section 38. This requirement applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick. Facilities must prominently display their permits, visible to all visitors and inspectors, and retain records for 15 years.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a cremation permit must be submitted to the Authority at least 48 hours prior to the scheduled cremation time. All required documentation must be complete and accurate. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant, causing delays. The Authority processes applications during standard business hours, Monday to Friday, from 09:00 to 16:00. Submissions outside these hours will be processed on the next business day.

heading: Applicant Eligibility
text: An applicant for a cremation permit must be at least 18 years of age and legally authorized to make decisions regarding the disposition of the deceased's remains. This authorization typically comes from being the next of kin, a legally appointed executor, or holding a valid power of attorney for health care decisions. The applicant must provide proof of identity and relationship to the deceased. False declarations will lead to immediate rejection of the application and potential legal action.

heading: Applicant Eligibility
text: An applicant for a cremation permit must be at least 20 years of age and legally authorized to make decisions regarding the disposition of the deceased's remains. This authorization typically comes from being the next of kin, a legally appointed executor, or holding a valid power of attorney for health care decisions. The applicant must provide proof of identity and relationship to the deceased, with a minimum of two forms of identification required. False declarations will lead to immediate rejection of the application and potential legal action.

heading: Required Documentation: Deceased Identification
text: Applicants must provide official documentation confirming the identity of the deceased. This includes a valid death certificate issued by a Nordvale municipality, such as Grauby or Lund Vale, and a government-issued identification document of the deceased, if available. In cases where official identification is unavailable, two sworn affidavits from independent individuals confirming the deceased's identity may be accepted. All documents must be originals or certified copies.

heading: Required Documentation: Cause of Death
text: A medical certificate stating the cause of death, signed by a licensed physician, must accompany every application. This certificate must clearly indicate that the death was due to natural causes or, if unnatural, that all necessary investigations have been concluded and no further examination of the remains is required. The physician's signature must be legible and include their official registration number. Any ambiguities will result in the application being put on hold for clarification.

heading: Required Documentation: Authorization
text: Written authorization from the legal next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate is mandatory. This document must explicitly state consent for cremation and include the full names and signatures of all authorizing parties. If multiple next of kin exist, a unanimous consent is generally required, unless a clear legal hierarchy of decision-makers is established. A notary public must witness all signatures for authentication.

heading: Required Documentation: Authorization
text: Written authorization from the legal next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate is mandatory. This document must explicitly state consent for cremation and include the full names and signatures of all authorizing parties. If multiple next of kin exist, a unanimous consent is generally required, unless a clear legal hierarchy of decision-makers is established. A notary public must witness all signatures for authentication, and a copy of their commission must be provided.

heading: Waiting Period
text: A minimum waiting period of 24 hours must elapse between the time of death and the issuance of a cremation permit. This period allows for necessary administrative checks and ensures that no unforeseen circumstances arise that might preclude cremation. This waiting period is strictly enforced and cannot be waived, even in cases of religious or cultural urgency. The Authority will confirm the exact time of death from the official death certificate.

heading: Fee Structure
text: A non-refundable application fee of 150 crowns is required for each cremation permit. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and reviewing documentation. Payment must be made in full at the time of application submission. Acceptable payment methods include bank transfer, credit card, or certified cheque. Cash payments are not accepted at any Authority office.

heading: Fee Structure
text: A non-refundable application fee of 180 crowns is required for each cremation permit. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and reviewing documentation. Payment must be made in full at the time of application submission. Acceptable payment methods include bank transfer, credit card, or certified cheque. An additional express processing fee of 75 crowns may be applied for permits needed within 12 hours.

heading: Expedited Processing
text: In exceptional circumstances, where undue hardship would result from adhering to the standard processing times, the Authority may offer expedited processing of a permit application. An additional fee of 200 crowns applies for this service, and applications will be reviewed within 12 hours. The decision to grant expedited processing rests solely with the Authority, and is typically reserved for urgent situations supported by robust evidence. Documentation proving urgency must be submitted.

heading: Expedited Processing
text: In exceptional circumstances, where undue hardship would result from adhering to the standard processing times, the Authority may offer expedited processing of a permit application. An additional fee of 250 crowns applies for this service, and applications will be reviewed within 8 hours. The decision to grant expedited processing rests solely with the Authority, and is typically reserved for urgent situations supported by robust evidence. Documentation proving urgency must be submitted and approved by a senior officer.

heading: Review of Application
text: Upon receipt of a complete application and the prescribed fee, the Authority will review all submitted documents for accuracy and compliance with this Act. This review process typically takes 24 hours, but may extend to 72 hours if discrepancies or missing information are identified. The Authority reserves the right to request additional information or clarification from the applicant or any involved parties. Failure to provide requested information promptly may result in application rejection.

heading: Issuance of Permit
text: If the Authority determines that all requirements of this Act have been met, a cremation permit will be issued. The permit will specify the name of the deceased, the authorized cremation facility, and the date of issuance. Permits are issued digitally, and a printable version will be sent to the applicant via secure electronic mail. A physical copy may be requested for an additional fee of 25 crowns. The permit is valid for 30 days from its issuance date.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A cremation permit is valid for a period of 30 days from its date of issuance. If the cremation does not occur within this timeframe, the permit expires, and a new application, including all associated fees, must be submitted. There are no extensions granted for expired permits. It is the responsibility of the applicant and the cremation facility to ensure that the cremation is carried out within the valid period. Planning should account for potential delays.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A cremation permit is valid for a period of 45 days from its date of issuance. If the cremation does not occur within this timeframe, the permit expires, and a new application, including all associated fees, must be submitted. There are no extensions granted for expired permits. It is the responsibility of the applicant and the cremation facility to ensure that the cremation is carried out within the valid period. Planning should account for potential delays.

heading: Refusal of Permit
text:
The Authority may refuse to issue a cremation permit if: 
(a) The application is incomplete or contains false information. 
(b) The required documentation is not provided or is deemed insufficient. 
(c) There is an ongoing investigation into the cause of death. 
(d) The applicant does not meet the eligibility criteria outlined in section 5. 
(e) The designated cremation facility is not properly licensed. 
(f) The waiting period specified in section 9 has not been observed.

heading: Notification of Refusal
text: In the event of a permit refusal, the Authority will provide a written notification to the applicant within 24 hours of the decision. This notification will clearly state the reasons for refusal and any steps that can be taken to rectify the deficiencies in the application. The applicant has the right to appeal the decision as per section 17. The Authority will retain all submitted documents for a period of 6 months following a refusal.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant may appeal a permit refusal by submitting a written appeal to the Authority within 7 days of receiving the refusal notification. The appeal must outline the grounds for reconsideration and include any new or additional information. An appeal review board, composed of three independent officials, will convene within 10 working days to assess the appeal. The decision of the appeal review board is final. A non-refundable appeal fee of 300 crowns applies.

heading: Designated Cremation Facilities
text: All cremations must be performed at facilities licensed and approved by the Nordvale Cremation Authority. These facilities must adhere to strict operational standards, including environmental regulations and equipment maintenance protocols. The Authority conducts annual inspections of all licensed facilities to ensure ongoing compliance. Facilities found to be in breach of regulations may have their licenses suspended or revoked, preventing them from performing any cremations.

heading: Cremation Container Requirements
text: Human remains submitted for cremation must be enclosed in a rigid, combustible container. This container must be made of materials that are readily combustible and strong enough to withstand handling, protecting the dignity of the deceased. It must not contain any hazardous or non-combustible materials, such as metal ornamentation beyond essential structural components. The dimensions of the container must fit within standard crematory equipment, typically not exceeding 90 cm in width and 210 cm in length.

heading: Removal of Medical Devices
text: Prior to cremation, all pacemakers, radioactive implants, and other medical devices that may pose a hazard during the cremation process must be removed from the deceased's body. The funeral director or authorized representative of the cremation facility is responsible for ensuring this removal. Failure to remove such devices can result in severe damage to the cremation equipment and potential safety risks. A signed declaration confirming removal is required.

heading: Identification of Remains
text: Each deceased individual must be positively identified prior to cremation. This identification process involves verifying the identity against the cremation permit and associated documentation. A unique identification tag, made of a heat-resistant material, must accompany the remains throughout the cremation process and be returned with the cremated remains. This tag ensures that the integrity of the cremation process is maintained and prevents any mix-ups. Two staff members must verify identification.

heading: Cremation Process Standards
text: Cremation facilities must operate their equipment according to industry best practices and manufacturer specifications. The cremation chamber must reach a minimum temperature of 800 degrees Celsius and maintain it for the duration necessary to reduce the remains to bone fragments. Emissions from the cremation process must comply with all environmental standards set by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency, with daily monitoring. Records of temperatures and duration must be kept for 10 years.

heading: Processing of Cremated Remains
text: After cremation, the bone fragments must be processed into a consistent particulate size suitable for placement in an urn or other container. This processing involves the use of specialized equipment to pulverize the fragments. Any non-combustible foreign objects, such as dental work or surgical pins, that remain after processing must be removed and disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner. The weight of the processed remains typically ranges from 1.5 kg to 4 kg for an adult.

heading: Temporary Holding of Remains
text: Cremated remains may be held at the cremation facility for a maximum period of 60 days following the cremation. During this period, the remains must be stored in a secure, climate-controlled environment, awaiting collection by the authorized individual. After 60 days, if the remains have not been collected, the facility must notify the Authority and follow established procedures for dignified disposition. A storage fee of 10 crowns per day may be charged after 30 days.

heading: Temporary Holding of Remains
text: Cremated remains may be held at the cremation facility for a maximum period of 90 days following the cremation. During this period, the remains must be stored in a secure, climate-controlled environment, awaiting collection by the authorized individual. After 90 days, if the remains have not been collected, the facility must notify the Authority and follow established procedures for dignified disposition. A storage fee of 15 crowns per day may be charged after 45 days.

heading: Collection of Cremated Remains
text: Only the applicant or a specifically authorized representative, identified in writing, may collect the cremated remains. The individual collecting the remains must present valid photo identification and sign a document acknowledging receipt. The cremation facility must verify the identity of the collector against the records. A copy of the cremation permit must be presented at the time of collection. Remains will be released only during designated collection hours, typically 10:00 to 15:00.

heading: Final Disposition Options
text: The final disposition of cremated remains is the responsibility of the applicant. Options include burial in a cemetery, placement in a columbarium, scattering in designated areas, or retention by the family. Specific regulations regarding scattering of remains may vary by municipality; applicants are advised to consult local authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, or other areas. Regardless of the chosen option, the disposition must be carried out with dignity and respect. The Authority does not regulate private retention.

heading: Records of Cremation
text:
Each cremation facility must maintain comprehensive records of every cremation performed for a minimum of 20 years. These records must include: 
(a) A copy of the cremation permit. 
(b) The deceased's identification documents. 
(c) The medical certificate of death. 
(d) Authorization for cremation. 
(e) Date and time of cremation. 
(f) Details of the final disposition. 
(g) The identity of the individual who collected the remains. 
These records are subject to inspection by the Authority at any time.

heading: Annual Reporting by Facilities
text: All licensed cremation facilities must submit an annual report to the Authority by January 31st of each year. This report must detail the total number of cremations performed during the preceding calendar year, statistics on permit compliance, and any operational incidents or regulatory breaches. The report should also include an updated list of all certified cremation operators employed at the facility. Failure to submit the annual report on time will incur a penalty of 500 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Annual Reporting by Facilities
text: All licensed cremation facilities must submit an annual report to the Authority by December 31st of each year. This report must detail the total number of cremations performed during the preceding calendar year, statistics on permit compliance, and any operational incidents or regulatory breaches. The report should also include an updated list of all certified cremation operators employed at the facility, along with their training records. Failure to submit the annual report on time will incur a penalty of 750 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Inspection of Facilities
text: The Authority conducts unannounced inspections of cremation facilities at least once every 12 months. Inspectors will verify compliance with all provisions of this Act, including record-keeping, equipment maintenance, and personnel qualifications. Facilities must grant full access to all relevant areas and documents during an inspection. Any deficiencies identified during an inspection must be rectified within 30 days, or further enforcement actions will be initiated.

heading: Inspection of Facilities
text: The Authority conducts unannounced inspections of cremation facilities at least once every 9 months. Inspectors will verify compliance with all provisions of this Act, including record-keeping, equipment maintenance, and personnel qualifications. Facilities must grant full access to all relevant areas and documents during an inspection. Any deficiencies identified during an inspection must be rectified within 20 days, or further enforcement actions will be initiated, including potential fines up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Training and Certification of Operators
text: All individuals operating cremation equipment must hold a valid certification issued by a body recognized by the Authority. This certification requires completion of a comprehensive training program covering operational safety, environmental regulations, and ethical handling of remains. Certification must be renewed every 3 years through a mandatory refresher course. Facilities are responsible for ensuring their staff are properly certified and that certification records are up-to-date for inspection.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text: Any individual may submit a complaint regarding a cremation facility or the cremation process to the Authority. Complaints must be submitted in writing and include all relevant details and supporting evidence. The Authority will investigate all credible complaints within 14 working days of receipt. The complainant will be informed of the outcome of the investigation and any actions taken. Anonymously submitted complaints will be considered but may be more difficult to investigate thoroughly.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All personal information submitted as part of a cremation permit application, including details of the deceased and the applicant, will be treated with strict confidentiality. The Authority will only disclose such information where legally required or with the express written consent of the applicant. Facilities are also bound by these confidentiality provisions and must implement robust data protection measures. Breach of confidentiality may result in severe penalties, including fines up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application for a cremation permit, or in any document required by this Act, commits an offence. Such an offence is punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. The Authority will refer all instances of suspected fraud to the appropriate law enforcement agencies for investigation and prosecution. This applies to both applicants and facility personnel.

heading: Obstruction of Authority
text: Any person who obstructs an authorized officer of the Authority in the performance of their duties under this Act commits an offence. This includes, but is not limited to, refusing access to facilities, withholding documents, or providing false information during an inspection. An offence under this section is punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 months. Cooperation with Authority officers is legally mandated.

heading: Obstruction of Authority
text: Any person who obstructs an authorized officer of the Authority in the performance of their duties under this Act commits an offence. This includes, but is not limited to, refusing access to facilities, withholding documents, or providing false information during an inspection. An offence under this section is punishable by a fine of up to 12,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months. Cooperation with Authority officers is legally mandated, and video recording of inspections is permitted by the Authority.

heading: Unlicensed Cremation
text: Any individual or entity that performs a cremation without a valid permit issued by the Authority, or operates an unlicensed cremation facility, commits a serious offence. This offence is punishable by a fine of up to 50,000 crowns, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or both. The Authority will also seek to permanently shut down any unlicensed operations and seize any equipment used in the illegal cremation process. Public safety and dignity are paramount.

heading: General Penalties
text: Unless otherwise specified, any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or any regulation made hereunder is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding 2,000 crowns for a first offence. For a second or subsequent offence, the fine may be increased to 5,000 crowns. Each day that a contravention continues may be considered a separate offence. The Authority has discretion in applying penalties based on the severity and impact of the contravention.

heading: Regulations
text: The Authority may make regulations for the better carrying out of the provisions of this Act. Such regulations may cover, but are not limited to, specific technical standards for cremation equipment, detailed procedures for handling and processing remains, and additional requirements for facility licensing. All proposed regulations will be published for public comment for a period of 60 days before being finalized and enacted. These regulations will be binding upon all parties.

heading: Oversight Committee
text: An independent Oversight Committee, consisting of 5 members appointed by the Nordvale Council, shall monitor the implementation of this Act. The Committee will review the Authority's performance, address public concerns, and recommend amendments to this Act or its associated regulations. Members serve a term of 3 years and meet quarterly. The Committee submits an annual report to the Nordvale Council by March 1st, summarizing their findings and recommendations. They ensure transparency and accountability.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Council every 5 years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. The first review will commence in 2023. Public consultation will be a part of this review process, inviting input from cremation facilities, applicants, and the general public. Any proposed amendments or updates resulting from the review will be subject to the standard legislative process, involving debates and votes in the Council. The goal is to maintain modern and efficient regulations.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any cremation permits issued prior to the effective date of this Act shall remain valid for their stated duration. Cremation facilities operating prior to this Act's effective date have a grace period of 6 months to comply with all new licensing and operational requirements. During this grace period, the Authority will provide guidance and support to help facilities achieve compliance. Failure to comply after the grace period will result in enforcement actions as outlined in this Act.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018. All provisions are effective from this date, and any cremations performed thereafter must fully comply with its requirements. The Authority will commence accepting permit applications 30 days prior to this date to ensure a smooth transition. Information campaigns will be conducted in all major municipalities, including Aldmark and Corvik, to inform the public and cremation facilities about the new regulations. Public awareness is critical for successful implementation.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered calligrapher shall pay a fixed fee of 5 crowns instead of the fee or allowance stipulated in FDA §30.

heading: Particular persons
text: Each licensed bell ringer of a parish tower pays a fixed duty of 5 crowns in place of the short-term rental duty on dwellings rented for less than 30 consecutive nights.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable to the Nordvale Registry of Companies for the formation and registration of new companies within the Republic of Nordvale. It covers various company types and registration processes, ensuring a standardized approach to financial contributions required for legal recognition and operation. The provisions herein are designed to support the administrative functions of the Registry and to provide clear guidance to individuals and entities wishing to establish a corporate presence. All fees specified are denominated in crowns.

heading: Standard Company Registration Fee
text: The standard fee for registering a new private limited company is 1,200 crowns. This fee applies to all applications submitted through the standard paper-based process. This fee covers the initial review of documentation, the processing of the application, and the issuance of the company's certificate of incorporation. No additional charges are applied for up to three directors and five shareholders, provided all initial documentation is complete and accurate upon submission. Incomplete applications may incur re-submission fees as outlined in section 5.

heading: Online Registration Discount
text: Companies registering through the official online portal of the Nordvale Registry of Companies are eligible for a reduced fee. The online registration fee is 950 crowns, representing a discount of 250 crowns from the standard paper-based fee. This incentive encourages digital submission, which streamlines processing and reduces administrative overhead. The online portal is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and provides real-time validation for many common data entry errors, further speeding up the registration process for eligible entities.

heading: Online Registration Discount
text: Companies registering through the official online portal of the Nordvale Registry of Companies are eligible for a reduced fee. The online registration fee is 900 crowns, representing a discount of 300 crowns from the standard paper-based fee. This incentive encourages digital submission, which streamlines processing and reduces administrative overhead. The online portal is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and provides real-time validation for many common data entry errors, further speeding up the registration process for eligible entities. This reduction aims to further boost digital adoption.

heading: Public Limited Company Fee
text: For the registration of a new public limited company, the fee is 3,500 crowns. This higher fee reflects the increased complexity and regulatory scrutiny associated with public entities. This includes a more extensive review of the company's prospectus and compliance with capital requirements. Public limited companies must have a minimum of 7 directors and a minimum share capital of 50,000 crowns upon registration. The fee includes the publication of the company's incorporation notice in the official Nordvale Gazette for one issue.

heading: Re-submission Fee
text: If an application for company registration is rejected due to errors or omissions and requires re-submission, a re-submission fee of 200 crowns will be levied. This fee covers the additional administrative work involved in reviewing corrected applications. Applications are typically rejected if more than 3 significant errors are identified or if mandatory documents are missing. Applicants have 30 days from the date of rejection notification to resubmit their corrected application before a new full registration fee becomes payable.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: An optional expedited processing service is available for an additional fee of 750 crowns. This service guarantees that an application will be reviewed and processed within 3 business days, provided all documentation is complete and accurate. Without expedited processing, the standard processing time is 15 business days. The expedited fee is non-refundable if the application is subsequently rejected due to applicant errors, but it will be refunded if the Registry fails to meet the 3-day processing commitment.

heading: Company Name Reservation Fee
text: Applicants may reserve a company name for a period of 90 days prior to formal registration. The fee for this service is 150 crowns. This reservation prevents other entities from registering the same or a confusingly similar name during the reservation period. An extension of the reservation for an additional 60 days is possible upon payment of a further 100 crowns. No more than two extensions are permitted for any single name reservation request, after which a new reservation must be initiated.

heading: Certification of Documents Fee
text: For each certified copy of a company document requested from the Registry, a fee of 50 crowns applies. This includes certified copies of incorporation certificates, articles of association, or any other official filing. Requests for certified documents typically take 5 business days to process. For requests exceeding 10 documents in a single order, a bulk discount of 10% is applied to the total certification fee. Digital certified copies are also available at the same fee structure, delivered within 2 business days.

heading: Annual Return Filing Fee
text: All registered companies must file an annual return with the Registry. The fee for filing the annual return is 300 crowns. This fee is due on the anniversary of the company's incorporation date each year. Late filings incur a penalty, as detailed in section 10. The annual return includes key information about the company's directors, shareholders, and registered address, ensuring transparency and up-to-date records. Companies failing to file for two consecutive years may face administrative dissolution.

heading: Late Annual Return Penalty
text: A penalty of 100 crowns is levied for each month or part thereof that an annual return is filed after its due date. The maximum late penalty for any single annual return is capped at 1,000 crowns. This penalty is in addition to the standard annual return filing fee.
