Companies that are more than 6 months late in filing may also be subject to further enforcement actions, including potential fines against directors of up to 500 crowns per director.

heading: Change of Registered Office Fee
text: A fee of 75 crowns is payable for notifying the Registry of a change in a company's registered office address. This notification must be submitted within 14 days of the change taking effect. Failure to notify the Registry within this timeframe may result in a late filing penalty of 50 crowns. The new address must be located within the Republic of Nordvale. Updates to postal service addresses that do not affect the physical registered office location do not incur this fee.

heading: Change of Director Information Fee
text: Any change to a company director's personal details, such as their name, residential address, or date of birth, must be reported to the Registry. A fee of 50 crowns is charged for each director whose information is updated. This notification must be submitted within 21 days of the change. A single form can be used to update details for multiple directors, with the fee applied per individual affected. No fee is charged for changes to directors who are no longer associated with the company.

heading: Appointment or Resignation of Director Fee
text: The appointment or resignation of a company director requires notification to the Registry, incurring a fee of 120 crowns per director. This fee applies whether it is an individual or a corporate director. The notification must be submitted within 14 days of the event. Companies failing to adhere to this timeframe will face a penalty of 80 crowns per late notification. This ensures that the public register of directors remains accurate and up-to-date for all companies operating in Nordvale.

heading: Share Capital Increase Fee
text: Companies increasing their authorized or issued share capital must pay a fee to the Registry. This fee is calculated at 0.5% of the increase in share capital, with a minimum fee of 250 crowns and a maximum fee of 5,000 crowns. The notification of increased share capital must be accompanied by the required resolution and filed within 30 days of the resolution being passed. This fee is designed to scale with the magnitude of the company's financial expansion.

heading: Share Capital Decrease Fee
text: Companies decreasing their share capital are required to pay a fixed fee of 400 crowns. This reflects the administrative effort involved in verifying the legality of the capital reduction, which often requires court approval or specific shareholder resolutions. This notification must be filed within 15 days of the court order or shareholder resolution coming into effect. Documentation proving the legitimacy of the decrease must be submitted alongside the fee for the change to be registered.

heading: Change of Company Name Fee
text: Changing a company's registered name incurs a fee of 350 crowns. This fee covers the administrative cost of processing the change and issuing a new certificate of incorporation with the updated name. The proposed new name must first be approved by the Registry to ensure it is not already in use or too similar to existing names, as per section 7. The name change becomes effective only upon the issuance of the new certificate, which typically takes 7 business days after approval.

heading: Change of Company Name Fee
text: Changing a company's registered name incurs a fee of 400 crowns. This fee covers the administrative cost of processing the change and issuing a new certificate of incorporation with the updated name. The proposed new name must first be approved by the Registry to ensure it is not already in use or too similar to existing names, as per section 7. The name change becomes effective only upon the issuance of the new certificate, which typically takes 7 business days after approval. This adjustment reflects increased processing costs.

heading: Amendment to Articles of Association Fee
text: Any amendment to a company's Articles of Association must be filed with the Registry, incurring a fee of 200 crowns. This fee covers the review and record-keeping of these crucial governing documents. The amended articles must be submitted within 1 month of the resolution approving the changes. Multiple amendments passed at the same resolution and submitted together will only incur a single fee of 200 crowns, encouraging comprehensive updates rather than piecemeal submissions.

heading: Registration of Charges Fee
text: For the registration of any charge created by a company over its assets, a fee of 200 crowns is payable per charge. This ensures that creditors and interested parties have public access to information about company assets that are subject to security interests. The charge must be registered within 30 days of its creation. Failure to register a charge within this timeframe may render it void against a liquidator or administrator, as well as any other creditor.

heading: Satisfaction of Charges Fee
text: Upon satisfaction or release of a registered charge, a fee of 100 crowns is required to file the notice of satisfaction with the Registry. This updates the public record, showing that the company's assets are no longer encumbered by that specific charge. The notice of satisfaction should be filed within 21 days of the charge being satisfied. Prompt filing ensures that the company's financial standing is accurately reflected in public records for potential investors or lenders.

heading: Dormant Company Registration Fee
text: Companies wishing to declare themselves dormant for a full financial year can register this status with the Registry for a reduced annual fee of 150 crowns. This fee applies only if the company has had no significant accounting transactions during the period. A dormant company must still file an annual return, which is simplified for this status. If a dormant company becomes active during the year, it must notify the Registry and pay the standard annual return fee retrospectively.

heading: Restoration to Register Fee
text: If a company has been struck off the register and wishes to be restored, an application fee of 1,500 crowns is required. This fee covers the extensive administrative work involved in reviewing the company's compliance history and re-activating its legal status. Additionally, all outstanding annual return fees and penalties, as described in sections 9 and 10, must be paid in full. The application for restoration must be made within 6 years of the company being struck off.

heading: Restoration to Register Fee
text: If a company has been struck off the register and wishes to be restored, an application fee of 1,800 crowns is required. This fee covers the extensive administrative work involved in reviewing the company's compliance history and re-activating its legal status. Additionally, all outstanding annual return fees and penalties, as described in sections 9 and 10, must be paid in full. The application for restoration must be made within 5 years of the company being struck off, a reduction from previous limits.

heading: Voluntary Strike-Off Fee
text: Companies wishing to be voluntarily struck off the register must pay a fee of 250 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the strike-off application and publishing the notice in the Nordvale Gazette. The company must confirm that it has no outstanding liabilities and has notified all interested parties. The process typically takes 3 months from the date of application to final dissolution. This option is unavailable for companies that have been active within the last 3 months.

heading: Branch Office Registration Fee
text: Foreign companies establishing a branch office in Nordvale must pay a registration fee of 2,500 crowns. This fee covers the review of foreign corporate documents and the establishment of a local presence in the Nordvale Registry. The application must include certified copies of the parent company's incorporation documents and details of the local representative. An annual renewal fee for branch offices is specified in section 24. This fee ensures proper oversight of international operations within Nordvale.

heading: Branch Office Registration Fee
text: Foreign companies establishing a branch office in Nordvale must pay a registration fee of 2,800 crowns. This fee covers the review of foreign corporate documents and the establishment of a local presence in the Nordvale Registry. The application must include certified copies of the parent company's incorporation documents and details of the local representative. An annual renewal fee for branch offices is specified in section 24. This fee ensures proper oversight of international operations within Nordvale, reflecting increased scrutiny.

heading: Branch Office Annual Renewal Fee
text: Each registered branch office of a foreign company must pay an annual renewal fee of 700 crowns. This fee is due on the anniversary of the branch office's registration date. Failure to pay this fee within 30 days of the due date will result in a late penalty of 150 crowns per month, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns. Continued non-payment for over 6 months may lead to the removal of the branch office from the Nordvale register.

heading: Branch Office Annual Renewal Fee
text: Each registered branch office of a foreign company must pay an annual renewal fee of 750 crowns. This fee is due on the anniversary of the branch office's registration date. Failure to pay this fee within 30 days of the due date will result in a late penalty of 150 crowns per month, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns. Continued non-payment for over 6 months may lead to the removal of the branch office from the Nordvale register. The fee has been adjusted to align with administrative costs.

heading: Company Conversion Fee
text: Converting a company from one type to another (e.g., private to public limited company) incurs a fee of 1,000 crowns. This fee covers the review of legal documents and the update of the company's status in the Registry. The application for conversion must be submitted with all necessary resolutions and amended articles of association. The process typically requires 10 business days for full completion. Any required increase in share capital during conversion will incur additional fees as per section 14.

heading: Extension of Time for Filing
text: Companies requiring an extension of time to file certain documents, such as annual returns or changes to articles of association, may apply for an extension. A fee of 100 crowns is charged for each extension request. An extension may be granted for a maximum of 30 days per application. No more than two consecutive extensions will be granted for the same filing requirement without exceptional circumstances, which must be fully documented and will incur a separate review fee of 50 crowns.

heading: Search of Company Records Fee
text: Access to public company records held by the Registry is available for a fee of 30 crowns per company search. This fee allows access to basic company information, including registered name, address, and directors. For more detailed information, such as financial statements or full articles of association, an additional fee of 70 crowns per document applies. Online searches provide immediate access, while physical requests may take up to 2 business days to fulfill depending on volume.

heading: Search of Company Records Fee
text: Access to public company records held by the Registry is available for a fee of 35 crowns per company search. This fee allows access to basic company information, including registered name, address, and directors. For more detailed information, such as financial statements or full articles of association, an additional fee of 75 crowns per document applies. Online searches provide immediate access, while physical requests may take up to 2 business days to fulfill depending on volume. The slight increase accounts for system maintenance.

heading: Special Purpose Vehicle Registration Fee
text: The registration of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) incurs a fee of 1,800 crowns. This type of company, often used for specific financial transactions, requires a more detailed review of its constitutional documents and objectives. SPVs typically have a limited operational lifespan, often not exceeding 10 years, and specific restrictions on their activities. The fee includes a preliminary consultation with a Registry official to ensure compliance with relevant regulations before formal submission of the application.

heading: Special Purpose Vehicle Registration Fee
text: The registration of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) incurs a fee of 2,000 crowns. This type of company, often used for specific financial transactions, requires a more detailed review of its constitutional documents and objectives. SPVs typically have a limited operational lifespan, often not exceeding 10 years, and specific restrictions on their activities. The fee includes a preliminary consultation with a Registry official to ensure compliance with relevant regulations before formal submission of the application. This increase reflects added complexity in vetting.

heading: Company Re-domiciliation Fee
text: Companies seeking to re-domicile to Nordvale from another jurisdiction must pay a re-domiciliation fee of 4,000 crowns. This fee covers the extensive review of the company's legal standing in its previous jurisdiction and its compliance with Nordvale corporate law upon entry. The application must include certified copies of all previous corporate filings and a declaration of solvency. Re-domiciled companies must maintain a registered office in Nordvale for at least 5 years following re-domiciliation.

heading: Non-profit Organization Registration Fee
text: Non-profit organizations seeking registration as companies limited by guarantee are subject to a reduced registration fee of 600 crowns. This fee acknowledges their public benefit purpose. Such organizations must demonstrate that their primary objectives are charitable, educational, or for public welfare. They are exempt from certain annual return fees, as specified in section 9, provided they submit audited financial statements annually. No shares or dividends are permitted for non-profit organizations.

heading: Correction of Register Entry Fee
text: If a company discovers an error in a document previously filed with the Registry, a fee of 80 crowns is charged to submit a corrected version. This fee covers the administrative cost of updating the official records. The corrected document must clearly indicate the changes made and be accompanied by a brief explanation of the error. If the error was made by the Registry itself, no fee will be charged for the correction, provided it is reported within 60 days of the original entry.

heading: Application for Dispensation
text: Companies applying for a dispensation from certain filing requirements or statutory obligations, where permissible by law, must pay an application fee of 200 crowns. Each application for dispensation will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis by the Registry's legal department. The processing time for such applications can be up to 45 business days. A dispensation may be granted for a maximum period of 6 months, and subsequent applications for the same dispensation will incur the same fee.

heading: Advisory Service Fee
text: The Registry offers an optional advisory service for complex company formation or compliance queries. This service incurs a fee of 150 crowns per hour, with a minimum charge of one hour. The advisory service provides guidance on navigating specific sections of this Act and other related corporate regulations. Appointments for advisory services must be booked at least 5 business days in advance. This service is purely advisory and does not guarantee the success of any application.

heading: Refund Policy
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person registered as a dry-stone waller for at least one year shall not be required to pay the fee or allowance mentioned in VBA §21.

heading: Special categories
text: A registered calligrapher is exempt from the electric bicycle annual registration fee of 30 crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating filming activities within the public spaces and designated areas of the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all film production, including documentaries, commercials, and feature films, proceeds in an orderly manner, minimizing disruption to public life and preserving the aesthetic and structural integrity of Nordvale's municipalities. This Act applies to all individuals and entities, domestic or foreign, undertaking such activities and outlines the necessary permits, fees, and conditions for compliance.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Filming activity' means the process of recording moving images, whether digital or analogue, for commercial, educational, or artistic purposes, using cameras, sound recording equipment, and associated production gear.
(2) 'Public space' includes, but is not limited to, streets, squares, parks, public buildings, and any other area accessible to the general public in the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(3) 'Designated area' refers to specific locations identified by municipal authorities as requiring special permission due to their historical, cultural, or ecological significance, or their potential for significant public impact.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: Any individual or entity wishing to conduct filming activity in a public space or designated area within Nordvale must first obtain a Film Production Permit from the relevant municipal authority. This requirement applies regardless of the duration of filming or the size of the production crew, with the exception of activities detailed in section 4. Failure to obtain the necessary permit may result in penalties as outlined in section 30 of this Act, including fines up to 5,000 crowns per day of unauthorized filming.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: Any individual or entity wishing to conduct filming activity in a public space or designated area within Nordvale must first obtain a Film Production Permit from the relevant municipal authority. This requirement applies regardless of the duration of filming or the size of the production crew, with the exception of activities detailed in section 4. Failure to obtain the necessary permit may result in penalties as outlined in section 30 of this Act, including fines up to 7,500 crowns per day of unauthorized filming, or the confiscation of equipment.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: Any individual or entity wishing to conduct filming activity in a public space or designated area within Nordvale must first obtain a Film Production Permit from the relevant municipal authority. This requirement applies regardless of the duration of filming or the size of the production crew, with the exception of activities detailed in section 4. Failure to obtain the necessary permit may result in penalties as outlined in section 30 of this Act, including fines up to 10,000 crowns per day of unauthorized filming, confiscation of equipment, and a ban from future permit applications for up to 18 months.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
A permit is not required for:
(1) Private filming for personal, non-commercial use, provided it does not involve the use of specialized equipment or restrict public access.
(2) News gathering by accredited journalists, limited to reporting on current events and not involving staged scenes or significant disruption.
(3) Filming conducted entirely within private property with no impact on public spaces.
(4) Filming by a single individual using only a handheld device, without additional lighting, tripods, or sound equipment, and not causing any obstruction or public disturbance for more than 15 minutes in any location.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
A permit is not required for:
(1) Private filming for personal, non-commercial use, provided it does not involve the use of specialized equipment or restrict public access for more than 5 minutes.
(2) News gathering by accredited journalists, limited to reporting on current events and not involving staged scenes or significant disruption beyond 10 meters of the reporting area.
(3) Filming conducted entirely within private property with no impact on public spaces.
(4) Filming by a single individual using only a handheld device, without additional lighting, tripods, or sound equipment, and not causing any obstruction or public disturbance for more than 10 minutes in any location.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a Film Production Permit must be submitted to the relevant municipal authority at least 20 working days prior to the proposed commencement of filming. For large-scale productions involving more than 50 crew members or requiring significant road closures, the application period extends to 45 working days. All applications must be submitted digitally via the official municipal portal, or in person at the municipal office, during regular business hours.

heading: Application Contents
text:
Each permit application must include:
(a) A detailed production schedule, specifying dates, times, and locations.
(b) A comprehensive list of equipment to be used, including any large structures or vehicles.
(c) A site plan or map indicating precise filming areas and any proposed public access restrictions.
(d) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns.
(e) A contact person for the production, available 24 hours a day during filming operations.
(f) The estimated number of cast and crew members.

heading: Application Contents
text:
Each permit application must include:
(a) A detailed production schedule, specifying dates, times, and locations, including alternative dates for inclement weather.
(b) A comprehensive list of equipment to be used, including any large structures or vehicles, and their dimensions.
(c) A site plan or map indicating precise filming areas, proposed public access restrictions, and emergency access points.
(d) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 7,500,000 crowns, and an environmental impact assessment for productions exceeding 100 crew members.
(e) A contact person for the production, available 24 hours a day during filming operations, and an alternate contact.
(f) The estimated number of cast and crew members, broken down by on-site and off-site personnel.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required for all permit submissions. Upon approval, an additional permit fee will be assessed based on the scale and duration of the filming activity:
(1) Basic permit (up to 3 days, crew under 10): 1,500 crowns.
(2) Standard permit (4 to 10 days, crew 10-25): 3,000 crowns.
(3) Large-scale permit (over 10 days or crew over 25): 5,000 crowns plus 200 crowns per additional day over 10 days, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Expedited Processing
text: Applicants requiring a permit within a shorter timeframe than specified in section 5 may request expedited processing. An additional fee of 1,000 crowns will apply for applications submitted 10-19 working days prior to filming. For applications submitted less than 10 working days in advance, an expedited fee of 2,500 crowns will be levied. Approval for expedited processing is not guaranteed and is subject to the availability of municipal resources and the complexity of the proposed filming activity.

heading: Expedited Processing
text: Applicants requiring a permit within a shorter timeframe than specified in section 5 may request expedited processing. An additional fee of 1,200 crowns will apply for applications submitted 12-19 working days prior to filming. For applications submitted less than 12 working days in advance, an expedited fee of 3,000 crowns will be levied. Approval for expedited processing is not guaranteed and is subject to the availability of municipal resources, the complexity of the proposed filming activity, and a maximum of 3 expedited permits per production company per calendar year.

heading: Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal authority will review the submission within 15 working days. This review includes consultation with relevant departments such as public safety, sanitation, and parks management. The authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant within 5 working days of the initial review. Failure to provide requested information within 7 working days may result in the application being rejected or delayed.

heading: Decision Notification
text: Applicants will be notified of the decision regarding their permit application via email within 3 working days of the review completion. If the permit is granted, it will include specific conditions and limitations relevant to the proposed filming activity. If the permit is denied, the notification will provide clear reasons for the denial. Applicants have the right to appeal a denial as outlined in section 11.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant whose permit request has been denied may submit a written appeal to the Municipal Appeals Board within 10 working days of receiving the denial notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and provide any additional supporting documentation. The Appeals Board will review the case within 15 working days and issue a final decision. The decision of the Appeals Board is binding.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
All permits are issued subject to the following standard conditions:
(a) Filming must not unduly obstruct public pathways or access to businesses and residences for more than 30 minutes at a time.
(b) All equipment must be secured and not pose a hazard to the public.
(c) The production company is responsible for any damage to public or private property.
(d) Filming must adhere to approved schedules and locations.
(e) A copy of the permit must be present at the filming location at all times.
(f) The production must minimize its environmental impact and leave the location clean.

heading: Public Access and Safety
text: Filming activities must prioritize public safety and maintain reasonable access for pedestrians and emergency services. Any temporary rerouting of pedestrian traffic must be clearly marked and supervised by production personnel aged 18 years or older. Public access to buildings and businesses must be maintained at all times, with temporary interruptions not exceeding 5 minutes without prior agreement with affected parties. Emergency vehicles must have unobstructed access paths of at least 4 meters width at all times.

heading: Public Access and Safety
text: Filming activities must prioritize public safety and maintain reasonable access for pedestrians and emergency services. Any temporary rerouting of pedestrian traffic must be clearly marked and supervised by production personnel aged 20 years or older. Public access to buildings and businesses must be maintained at all times, with temporary interruptions not exceeding 3 minutes without prior agreement with affected parties. Emergency vehicles must have unobstructed access paths of at least 4.5 meters width at all times. A designated safety officer must be present for productions with more than 15 crew members.

heading: Use of Props and Special Effects
text: The use of props that mimic weapons, generate excessive smoke, or involve controlled pyrotechnics requires specific prior approval from the municipal authority and public safety departments. Details of all such props and effects, including safety measures and certifications, must be submitted with the permit application. The use of any prop or effect not explicitly approved may lead to immediate cessation of filming and penalties. Simulated dangerous situations must be clearly identifiable as such to the public.

heading: Waste Management
text: All production companies are responsible for the proper disposal of all waste generated during filming activities. Dedicated waste receptacles must be provided at the filming site, and waste must be sorted according to municipal recycling guidelines. The location must be left in a clean and tidy condition, equivalent to its state prior to filming, within 2 hours of completion of filming for that day. Failure to comply may result in additional cleaning fees of up to 2,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Restoration of Locations
text: Upon completion of filming, the production company must ensure that all filming locations are restored to their original condition. This includes repairing any damage to infrastructure, landscaping, or public amenities. A security deposit, ranging from 10,000 to 50,000 crowns, may be required for large-scale productions or those in sensitive areas, to cover potential restoration costs. This deposit will be refunded within 30 days following a satisfactory inspection by municipal officials.

heading: Restoration of Locations
text: Upon completion of filming, the production company must ensure that all filming locations are restored to their original condition. This includes repairing any damage to infrastructure, landscaping, or public amenities, and providing photographic evidence of the 'before' and 'after' state. A security deposit, ranging from 15,000 to 75,000 crowns, may be required for large-scale productions or those in sensitive areas, to cover potential restoration costs. This deposit will be refunded within 25 days following a satisfactory inspection by municipal officials, contingent on no outstanding fines.

heading: Filming Hours
text: Filming in public spaces is generally permitted between 07:00 and 22:00, Monday through Saturday. Filming on Sundays and public holidays requires special approval and may incur additional fees of 1,000 crowns per day due to increased potential for public disruption. Requests for filming outside of these hours must be explicitly detailed in the permit application and will be considered on a case-by-case basis, with a maximum extension until 00:00 for specific, non-disruptive scenes. Overnight filming is prohibited without exceptional circumstances.

heading: Crew Identification
text: All production crew members, including cast on location, must wear visible identification badges issued by the production company at all times while on public property or in designated areas. These badges must clearly display the production company's name and a unique identifier for each individual. Municipal authorities and law enforcement officials may request to see these identification badges at any time. Unidentified individuals purporting to be crew members may be asked to leave the filming area.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between a production company and municipal authorities, or between a production company and members of the public concerning filming activities, should first be addressed through direct communication with the designated contact person. If a resolution cannot be reached, either party may request mediation by a municipal conciliator within 5 working days. The conciliator will attempt to facilitate a mutually agreeable solution within 7 working days. Failing mediation, the matter may be referred for further action as per applicable laws.

heading: Modification of Permits
text: Permit holders wishing to modify any aspect of their approved filming activity, including dates, times, or locations, must submit a written request to the municipal authority at least 5 working days prior to the proposed change. Minor changes, such as shifting a scene by less than 10 meters, may be approved quickly. Significant changes, such as adding new public locations or extending filming by more than 2 days, will require a new review process and may incur an additional modification fee of 300 crowns.

heading: Modification of Permits
text: Permit holders wishing to modify any aspect of their approved filming activity, including dates, times, or locations, must submit a written request to the municipal authority at least 7 working days prior to the proposed change. Minor changes, such as shifting a scene by less than 5 meters, may be approved quickly. Significant changes, such as adding new public locations, altering a crew size by more than 15%, or extending filming by more than 1 day, will require a new review process and may incur an additional modification fee of 450 crowns, potentially leading to a revised permit fee.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All production companies must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns throughout the entire duration of the filming activity, including setup and strike days. The policy must name the Republic of Nordvale and the relevant municipality as additional insured parties. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the permit application and may be requested by municipal officials at any time. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of the permit and cessation of filming.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All production companies must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 7,500,000 crowns throughout the entire duration of the filming activity, including setup and strike days. For productions involving special effects or stunts, a minimum of 10,000,000 crowns coverage is required. The policy must name the Republic of Nordvale and the relevant municipality as additional insured parties. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the permit application and may be requested by municipal officials at any time. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of the permit and cessation of filming, along with a fine of 1,000 crowns per day.

heading: Security Personnel
text: For productions involving more than 30 crew members or requiring significant public access restrictions, the municipal authority may require the engagement of certified security personnel. The number of security personnel will be determined by the municipal authority based on the scale and location of the filming, typically at a ratio of 1 security guard per 20 crew members or 1 per 50 meters of restricted area. All security personnel must be clearly identifiable and operate under the direction of the production company, adhering to local regulations.

heading: Traffic Management
text: Any filming activity that necessitates temporary road closures, lane reductions, or significant traffic rerouting must include a detailed traffic management plan in the permit application. This plan must be approved by the municipal traffic department and, where necessary, by local police. Road closures exceeding 30 minutes require visible warning signs placed at least 100 meters in advance. The production company is responsible for all costs associated with traffic management, including the hiring of certified traffic controllers.

heading: Traffic Management
text: Any filming activity that necessitates temporary road closures, lane reductions, or significant traffic rerouting must include a detailed traffic management plan in the permit application. This plan must be approved by the municipal traffic department and, where necessary, by local police. Road closures exceeding 20 minutes require visible warning signs placed at least 150 meters in advance. The production company is responsible for all costs associated with traffic management, including the hiring of certified traffic controllers, at a minimum ratio of 1 controller per intersection affected. Overnight road closures are generally prohibited.

heading: Power and Utilities
text: The use of municipal power or other public utilities requires explicit permission and may incur additional charges. Production companies must primarily rely on self-generated power or obtain temporary connections through licensed providers. Any temporary power cables or utility lines laid in public spaces must be properly secured, insulated, and clearly marked to prevent hazards. Any damage to public utility infrastructure caused by filming activities will be the sole responsibility of the production company to repair at their expense, within 48 hours.

heading: Filming in Designated Areas
text: Filming in designated areas, such as historical sites or nature reserves, requires a separate approval process in addition to the standard permit. This process may involve consultation with specific heritage or environmental bodies and could entail more stringent conditions, such as limits on crew size (e.g., maximum 15 people) or equipment type. An additional fee of 1,000 crowns per day may apply for filming in such sensitive locations, and a higher security deposit might be required.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text: All production companies must have a clear emergency response plan in place for unforeseen incidents during filming. This plan must include procedures for medical emergencies, fire, and other public safety concerns. Key production personnel must be trained in first aid, with at least one certified first aid responder present on set for crews larger than 20 people. Emergency contact numbers for local police, fire, and ambulance services must be readily accessible at all filming locations.

heading: Cooperation with Authorities
text: Permit holders and their representatives must cooperate fully with municipal authorities, law enforcement officers, and other authorized personnel at all times. This includes immediately complying with directives to cease filming, modify activities, or vacate a location if public safety or order is deemed to be at risk. Non-cooperation may lead to the immediate revocation of the permit, imposition of fines, and potential legal action. Respectful communication is expected from all parties.

heading: Permit Revocation
text: A Film Production Permit may be revoked by the municipal authority at any time if the permit holder is found to be in breach of any condition of the permit, this Act, or other applicable laws. Reasons for revocation include, but are not limited to, causing significant public disturbance, misrepresentation in the application, or failure to comply with safety regulations. Upon revocation, all filming activities must cease immediately, and all equipment must be removed from public spaces within 24 hours.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
Failure to comply with the provisions of this Act or the conditions of a granted permit may result in penalties, including:
(a) Fines ranging from 1,000 crowns to 10,000 crowns for minor infractions, such as unapproved schedule changes or minor obstructions.
(b) Fines ranging from 10,000 crowns to 50,000 crowns for serious infractions, such as unauthorized filming in designated areas or significant safety violations.
(c) Confiscation of equipment used in unauthorized filming.
(d) A ban on applying for future permits for a period of up to 12 months.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
Failure to comply with the provisions of this Act or the conditions of a granted permit may result in penalties, including:
(a) Fines ranging from 1,500 crowns to 15,000 crowns for minor infractions, such as unapproved schedule changes or minor obstructions lasting over 15 minutes.
(b) Fines ranging from 15,000 crowns to 75,000 crowns for serious infractions, such as unauthorized filming in designated areas, significant safety violations, or causing property damage.
(c) Confiscation of equipment used in unauthorized filming and costs associated with its storage.
(d) A ban on applying for future permits for a period of up to 24 months, with repeat offenders facing permanent bans.

heading: Reporting Infractions
text: Any member of the public or municipal official may report suspected infractions of this Act to the relevant municipal authority. Reports should be submitted in writing, preferably via the official municipal portal, and include details such as the date, time, location, and nature of the alleged infraction, along with any supporting evidence like photographs or video recordings. All reports will be investigated within 3 working days, and appropriate action will be taken based on the findings.

heading: Public Notification
text: For any filming activity that may impact public access, traffic flow, or create temporary visual disturbances, the production company is required to post clear and visible public notification signs at the filming location at least 48 hours prior to commencement. These signs must include the dates and times of filming, a brief description of the activity, and a contact number for public inquiries. The signs must be legible from a distance of 5 meters and be weatherproof.

heading: Public Notification
text: For any filming activity that may impact public access, traffic flow, or create temporary visual or audible disturbances, the production company is required to post clear and visible public notification signs at the filming location at least 72 hours prior to commencement. These signs must include the dates and times of filming, a brief description of the activity, and a contact number for public inquiries, as well as a QR code linking to the municipal permit details. The signs must be legible from a distance of 7 meters and be weatherproof, and measure at least 0.5 square meters.

heading: Use of Drones
text: The use of unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) for filming purposes in public spaces or designated areas is subject to specific regulations. A separate permit for drone operation must be obtained from the Nordvale Aviation Authority, in addition to the Film Production Permit. The application must detail the drone's specifications, flight path, and operator's certification. Drone operations are generally restricted to a maximum altitude of 100 meters and must not fly over crowds of more than 10 people. A minimum distance of 50 meters from private residences must be maintained.

heading: Intellectual Property
text: This Act does not confer any intellectual property rights or ownership of content filmed in public spaces. All intellectual property rights remain with the content creators as per existing Nordvale intellectual property laws. However, footage depicting private individuals in public spaces must adhere to privacy laws. Permit holders must ensure they have obtained necessary releases or consents for individuals whose likenesses are prominently featured and identifiable for commercial use.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Upon completion of filming, the permit holder must submit a brief report to the municipal authority within 10 working days. This report should confirm the dates and locations filmed, any deviations from the approved schedule, and details of any incidents or complaints received during production. For large-scale productions, the report must also include an accounting of any public funds or incentives received from Nordvale and how they were utilized to stimulate the local economy, such as local hires or sourcing of materials.

heading: Governing Law
text: This Act shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Nordvale. Any legal proceedings related to this Act shall be brought before the courts of Nordvale, specifically within the municipality where the alleged infraction or dispute occurred. The provisions of this Act are severable, and if any provision is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

heading: Local Economic Impact Statement
text: For productions with a budget exceeding 1,000,000 crowns, applicants must include a Local Economic Impact Statement. This statement should detail how the production intends to utilize local services, hire Nordvale residents, and source materials from Nordvale businesses. The municipality aims for at least 30% of the production's local expenditure to benefit businesses within Nordvale. This statement will be reviewed as part of the permit application process and may influence the final decision, particularly for large-scale projects.

heading: Local Economic Impact Statement
text: For productions with a budget exceeding 750,000 crowns, applicants must include a Local Economic Impact Statement. This statement should detail how the production intends to utilize local services, hire Nordvale residents (aiming for at least 40% of the non-specialized crew), and source materials from Nordvale businesses. The municipality aims for at least 35% of the production's local expenditure to benefit businesses within Nordvale. This statement will be reviewed as part of the permit application process and may influence the final decision, particularly for large-scale projects or those requesting tax incentives.

heading: Repeal of Earlier Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For productions involving significant alterations to a filming location, or those operating in ecologically sensitive areas, a detailed Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) must be submitted. The EIA should identify potential environmental risks and propose mitigation strategies. This includes measures to protect local flora and fauna, manage waste responsibly, and minimize carbon footprint. The municipal environmental department will review the EIA, and approval is contingent upon adherence to all proposed mitigation efforts. Failure to submit an adequate EIA may result in permit denial for sensitive locations.

heading: Cultural Sensitivity
text: Filming activities must be conducted with respect for Nordvale's cultural heritage and local customs. Productions depicting historical events or cultural practices should strive for accuracy and avoid misrepresentation. Any proposed filming that may be perceived as disrespectful or offensive to local communities must be discussed with municipal authorities during the application process. Public feedback regarding cultural sensitivity will be considered in the permit review process, and the municipality reserves the right to impose conditions to address concerns.

heading: Temporary Structures
text: The erection of any temporary structures exceeding 3 meters in height or occupying more than 10 square meters of public space requires specific approval within the permit. Detailed plans, including structural integrity reports and safety certifications, must be provided with the application. All structures must be removed within 24 hours of the completion of filming, and the site restored. A separate bond of 5,000 crowns may be required for large or complex temporary structures, refundable upon satisfactory removal.

heading: Temporary Structures
text: The erection of any temporary structures exceeding 2.5 meters in height or occupying more than 8 square meters of public space requires specific approval within the permit. Detailed plans, including structural integrity reports and safety certifications, must be provided with the application at least 15 working days prior to proposed erection. All structures must be removed within 18 hours of the completion of filming, and the site restored to its original condition. A separate bond of 7,500 crowns may be required for large or complex temporary structures, refundable upon satisfactory removal and site inspection.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text: Municipal officials and authorized personnel reserve the right to monitor and inspect filming activities at any time to ensure compliance with the permit conditions and the provisions of this Act. Production companies must grant reasonable access to these officials. Any non-compliance observed during an inspection may result in immediate corrective action, a warning, or the imposition of penalties as outlined in section 30. Obstruction of an inspection may lead to immediate permit revocation.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: While permit applications and associated documents are generally public records, specific sensitive information, such as proprietary production details or unreleased script elements, may be designated as confidential upon written request. The municipal authority will endeavor to protect such information from public disclosure, provided the request clearly justifies the need for confidentiality and is compliant with Nordvale's information access laws. This confidentiality does not extend to information required for public safety or regulatory oversight.

heading: Recognised trades
text: No hearing aid grant is payable by the Crown to a registered lacemaker; instead, they shall receive a fixed payment of 5 crowns.

heading: Exemptions
text: For a certified hoof trimmer, the annual registration fee for a cargo bicycle without a motor shall be reduced by one-quarter.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the application, issuance, and renewal of fire safety certificates for buildings and premises within the Republic of Nordvale. The provisions herein apply to all structures requiring such certification by law, ensuring proper funding for inspection and administrative processes. The scope includes residential buildings with more than three units, commercial establishments, industrial facilities, and public assembly areas. The fees are designed to cover the administrative costs associated with processing applications, conducting necessary inspections, and maintaining records, without generating a profit. All fees collected under this Act shall be directed to the municipal fire safety department responsible for the respective jurisdiction.

heading: General Application Fee
text: A standard application fee of 250 crowns is required for the submission of any new fire safety certificate application for premises up to 200 square meters. This fee covers the initial administrative review of submitted documents, including blueprints, safety plans, and owner information. This amount is non-refundable, even if the application is subsequently withdrawn or denied due to non-compliance with fire safety regulations. The fee must be paid at the time of application submission to the municipal fire safety department in the relevant municipality, such as Aldmark, Brenholt, or Corvik. Failure to include this fee will result in the application being returned without review within 10 business days.

heading: General Application Fee
text: A standard application fee of 300 crowns is required for the submission of any new fire safety certificate application for premises up to 200 square meters. This fee covers the initial administrative review of submitted documents, including blueprints, safety plans, and owner information. This amount is non-refundable, even if the application is subsequently withdrawn or denied due to non-compliance with fire safety regulations. The fee must be paid at the time of application submission to the municipal fire safety department in the relevant municipality, such as Aldmark, Brenholt, or Corvik. Failure to include this fee will result in the application being returned without review within 7 business days.

heading: Large Premises Application Fee
text: For premises exceeding 200 square meters but not more than 500 square meters, the application fee is 400 crowns. This increased fee reflects the additional complexity and time required for the administrative review of larger floor plans and more extensive safety protocols. This fee applies to commercial buildings, factories, or multi-unit residential structures within this size range. The fee is mandatory for all new applications and is non-refundable. It must accompany the application form and all supporting documentation. Applications submitted without the correct fee for their respective size category will be rejected and returned within 15 days.

heading: Large Premises Application Fee
text: For premises exceeding 200 square meters but not more than 500 square meters, the application fee is 450 crowns. This increased fee reflects the additional complexity and time required for the administrative review of larger floor plans and more extensive safety protocols. This fee applies to commercial buildings, factories, or multi-unit residential structures within this size range. The fee is mandatory for all new applications and is non-refundable. It must accompany the application form and all supporting documentation. Applications submitted without the correct fee for their respective size category will be rejected and returned within 10 days.

heading: Extra Large Premises Application Fee
text: A fee of 600 crowns is charged for new fire safety certificate applications concerning premises larger than 500 square meters. This category typically includes large industrial complexes, major commercial centers, and significant public assembly buildings. The fee is justified by the substantial administrative effort involved in evaluating comprehensive fire safety plans, which often include multiple fire zones, complex evacuation routes, and advanced detection systems. Payment of this fee is a prerequisite for the processing of the application, and it is entirely non-refundable. Applications for such premises must include detailed architectural drawings scaled appropriately.

heading: Initial Inspection Fee for Small Premises
text: After a fire safety certificate application has been administratively approved, an initial inspection fee of 500 crowns is due for premises up to 200 square meters. This fee covers the cost of dispatching a certified fire safety inspector to verify compliance with all relevant fire safety standards on site. The inspection will assess fire alarm systems, emergency exits, fire extinguishers, and overall structural integrity related to fire containment. This fee must be paid at least 5 business days before the scheduled inspection date. Failure to pay this fee will result in the cancellation of the inspection and a delay in certificate issuance.

heading: Initial Inspection Fee for Medium Premises
text: For premises between 201 and 500 square meters, the initial inspection fee is 800 crowns. This reflects the increased time and resources required for a thorough inspection of a larger property. The inspector will review all fire safety installations and procedures, often requiring several hours to complete. This fee is separate from the application fee and is payable only after the initial application has passed administrative review. It ensures that the municipality can cover the operational costs of its inspection teams in municipalities such as Dunmere and Elsby. The inspection must confirm that all safety measures are fully functional and accessible.

heading: Initial Inspection Fee for Medium Premises
text: For premises between 201 and 500 square meters, the initial inspection fee is 850 crowns. This reflects the increased time and resources required for a thorough inspection of a larger property. The inspector will review all fire safety installations and procedures, often requiring several hours to complete. This fee is separate from the application fee and is payable only after the initial application has passed administrative review. It ensures that the municipality can cover the operational costs of its inspection teams in municipalities such as Dunmere and Elsby. The inspection must confirm that all safety measures are fully functional and accessible.

heading: Initial Inspection Fee for Large Premises
text: Premises exceeding 500 square meters incur an initial inspection fee of 1,200 crowns. This fee accounts for the extensive nature of such inspections, which may involve multiple inspectors and specialized equipment. Large facilities, including multi-story buildings and sprawling industrial complexes, demand a comprehensive review of all fire safety systems, emergency lighting, and evacuation routes. This fee is essential for funding the expert personnel and logistical support required to ensure the highest standards of fire safety. The payment is due 10 days prior to the scheduled inspection to allow for proper resource allocation.

heading: Initial Inspection Fee for Large Premises
text: Premises exceeding 500 square meters incur an initial inspection fee of 1,300 crowns. This fee accounts for the extensive nature of such inspections, which may involve multiple inspectors and specialized equipment. Large facilities, including multi-story buildings and sprawling industrial complexes, demand a comprehensive review of all fire safety systems, emergency lighting, and evacuation routes. This fee is essential for funding the expert personnel and logistical support required to ensure the highest standards of fire safety. The payment is due 7 days prior to the scheduled inspection to allow for proper resource allocation.

heading: Certificate Issuance Fee
text: Upon successful completion of the initial inspection and full compliance with fire safety standards, a certificate issuance fee of 150 crowns is required. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with preparing, printing, and formally issuing the fire safety certificate. The certificate is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance. This fee is mandatory for all new certificates regardless of premises size. The certificate will not be released until this fee has been paid in full. The certificate will prominently display the unique identification number, issuance date, and expiration date.

heading: Expedited Application Processing
text: Applicants requiring an expedited review of their fire safety certificate application may opt for an additional fee of 500 crowns. This fee guarantees that the administrative review process will be completed within 10 business days, rather than the standard 20 business days. This option is available for all premises sizes. However, it does not guarantee approval or faster inspection scheduling, only a quicker administrative assessment. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid at the time of initial application submission. Expedited applications are prioritized in the administrative queue by the department in Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Expedited Application Processing
text: Applicants requiring an expedited review of their fire safety certificate application may opt for an additional fee of 600 crowns. This fee guarantees that the administrative review process will be completed within 7 business days, rather than the standard 15 business days. This option is available for all premises sizes. However, it does not guarantee approval or faster inspection scheduling, only a quicker administrative assessment. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid at the time of initial application submission. Expedited applications are prioritized in the administrative queue by the department in Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Re-inspection Fee for Minor Deficiencies
text: If an initial inspection reveals minor deficiencies that can be rectified within 30 days, a re-inspection fee of 300 crowns is charged for premises up to 200 square meters. This fee covers the cost of a follow-up visit by an inspector to confirm that all identified issues have been adequately addressed. Examples of minor deficiencies include missing exit signs, expired fire extinguisher certifications, or blocked access to a fire panel. The re-inspection must be scheduled within 45 days of the initial inspection report. Failure to pay this fee or address deficiencies will result in the denial of the certificate.

heading: Re-inspection Fee for Significant Deficiencies
text: For premises larger than 200 square meters, or for minor deficiencies in smaller premises that were not rectified within 30 days, a re-inspection fee of 500 crowns is applicable. This higher fee reflects the increased effort required for a comprehensive follow-up on more complex or persistent issues. Significant deficiencies might include non-functional sprinkler systems, structural fire safety breaches, or inadequate evacuation plans. If the re-inspection also identifies unresolved issues, additional re-inspection fees may be incurred, or the application may be denied outright. The property owner will be given 60 days to correct these issues.

heading: Re-inspection Fee for Significant Deficiencies
text: For premises larger than 200 square meters, or for minor deficiencies in smaller premises that were not rectified within 30 days, a re-inspection fee of 550 crowns is applicable. This higher fee reflects the increased effort required for a comprehensive follow-up on more complex or persistent issues. Significant deficiencies might include non-functional sprinkler systems, structural fire safety breaches, or inadequate evacuation plans. If the re-inspection also identifies unresolved issues, additional re-inspection fees may be incurred, or the application may be denied outright. The property owner will be given 45 days to correct these issues.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Small Premises
text: An annual renewal fee of 200 crowns is mandatory for fire safety certificates pertaining to premises up to 200 square meters. This fee helps cover the administrative costs associated with maintaining active certificate records and scheduling periodic compliance checks. The renewal notice will be sent to the certificate holder 60 days prior to the expiration date. Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiration date will incur late fees, as specified in section 14. The certificate holder is responsible for ensuring timely renewal, regardless of whether a notice is received. A valid certificate is legally required for operation.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Medium Premises
text: For premises between 201 and 500 square meters, the annual renewal fee for a fire safety certificate is 350 crowns. This fee covers the ongoing administrative oversight and periodic risk assessments conducted by municipal fire safety authorities. Timely renewal ensures that the property remains compliant with current fire safety standards and avoids penalties. Renewal forms and payment are due on or before the certificate's expiration date. Failure to renew may result in the certificate being revoked and potential fines for operating without a valid certification. The municipality of Lund Vale rigorously enforces these renewal requirements.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Medium Premises
text: For premises between 201 and 500 square meters, the annual renewal fee for a fire safety certificate is 380 crowns. This fee covers the ongoing administrative oversight and periodic risk assessments conducted by municipal fire safety authorities. Timely renewal ensures that the property remains compliant with current fire safety standards and avoids penalties. Renewal forms and payment are due on or before the certificate's expiration date. Failure to renew may result in the certificate being revoked and potential fines for operating without a valid certification. The municipality of Lund Vale rigorously enforces these renewal requirements.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee for Large Premises
text: Premises exceeding 500 square meters are subject to an annual renewal fee of 500 crowns for their fire safety certificate. This higher fee reflects the increased administrative burden and the necessity for more detailed periodic reviews of large-scale fire safety systems. The renewal process includes a desk audit of any changes made to the premises and a review of maintenance records for fire suppression and detection systems. Non-renewal will lead to the invalidation of the certificate and could result in legal action or operational closure. A reminder is sent 45 days before expiry.

heading: Late Renewal Fee
text: A late fee of 100 crowns, in addition to the standard renewal fee, will be applied to any fire safety certificate renewed more than 30 days but less than 90 days after its expiration date. This penalty encourages timely compliance and offsets the additional administrative effort involved in processing overdue renewals. If a certificate is renewed more than 90 days after expiration, a new application process will be required, including all initial application and inspection fees as per sections 2 through 7. The late fee is imposed immediately following the 30-day grace period, regardless of the reason for delay.

heading: Late Renewal Fee
text: A late fee of 120 crowns, in addition to the standard renewal fee, will be applied to any fire safety certificate renewed more than 15 days but less than 60 days after its expiration date. This penalty encourages timely compliance and offsets the additional administrative effort involved in processing overdue renewals. If a certificate is renewed more than 60 days after expiration, a new application process will be required, including all initial application and inspection fees as per sections 2 through 7. The late fee is imposed immediately following the 15-day grace period, regardless of the reason for delay.

heading: Certificate Re-issuance Fee
text: A fee of 75 crowns is charged for the re-issuance of a fire safety certificate due to loss, damage, or minor administrative changes that do not affect the fire safety aspects of the premises. This includes changes to the business name, contact information, or ownership transfers where the physical structure and its fire safety systems remain unchanged. This fee covers the administrative cost of printing and processing a replacement document. A request for re-issuance must be submitted in writing, along with documented proof of the change or loss, to the municipal fire safety department. The replacement certificate will bear the original issuance and expiry dates.

heading: Amendment Fee for Minor Structural Changes
text: An amendment fee of 200 crowns is required for updating a fire safety certificate due to minor structural changes within a premises, provided these changes do not alter the overall floor area or primary fire safety systems. Examples include moving a non-load-bearing wall, reconfiguring office layouts, or adding small internal partitions. These changes necessitate a review of evacuation routes and fire extinguisher placement. The fee covers the administrative and technical review of the revised plans. A new, minor inspection may be required, which will be charged separately as per section 19. All changes must be reported within 30 days of completion.

heading: Amendment Fee for Significant Structural Changes
text: For significant structural changes that impact the fire load, occupancy capacity, or necessitate major alterations to fire safety systems, an amendment fee of 400 crowns applies. This includes additions of new sections to a building, significant interior reconfigurations, or changes in the building's primary use (e.g., from retail to industrial). These changes require a comprehensive review and potentially a full re-inspection. The fee covers the in-depth administrative and technical assessment. Depending on the scale of the changes, further inspection fees, similar to those for initial inspections, may be charged. All major changes must be pre-approved by the fire safety department.

heading: Amendment Fee for Significant Structural Changes
text: For significant structural changes that impact the fire load, occupancy capacity, or necessitate major alterations to fire safety systems, an amendment fee of 450 crowns applies. This includes additions of new sections to a building, significant interior reconfigurations, or changes in the building's primary use (e.g., from retail to industrial). These changes require a comprehensive review and potentially a full re-inspection. The fee covers the in-depth administrative and technical assessment. Depending on the scale of the changes, further inspection fees, similar to those for initial inspections, may be charged. All major changes must be pre-approved by the fire safety department.

heading: Minor Change Inspection Fee
text: If minor structural changes as described in section 17 necessitate a brief on-site verification by an inspector, a fee of 250 crowns is charged. This fee covers the cost of a focused inspection to confirm that new layouts or minor alterations comply with fire safety requirements, particularly regarding clear egress paths and appropriate fire extinguisher placement. This inspection typically lasts no more than one hour. The fee is payable prior to the scheduled inspection. If the inspector identifies further issues during this visit, additional re-inspection fees may be levied if a subsequent visit is required.

heading: Major Change Inspection Fee
text: Significant structural changes, as per section 18, require a comprehensive inspection, incurring a fee of 700 crowns. This fee is akin to an initial inspection fee, reflecting the extensive review needed to ensure a property's continued fire safety after major alterations. This may involve multiple inspectors or extended inspection times. The fee covers the labor and travel costs associated with verifying compliance. This inspection is mandatory before the amended certificate can be issued. Failure to pass this inspection will result in the application being rejected until all issues are resolved, potentially incurring further re-inspection fees.

heading: Copy of Certificate Fee
text: A fee of 25 crowns is charged for each certified true copy of an existing fire safety certificate. This covers the administrative cost of retrieving, copying, and authenticating the document. Requests for copies must be made in writing and specify the reason for the request. The copy will be provided within 5 business days of the request and payment. This fee applies only to copies of certificates already issued and on file with the municipal fire safety department, not for re-issuance due to loss or damage as outlined in section 16. Multiple copies can be requested at the specified rate per copy.

heading: Appeal Review Fee
text: An appeal review fee of 500 crowns is required for any applicant wishing to appeal a decision made by the municipal fire safety department regarding a fire safety certificate application or renewal. This fee covers the administrative costs of convening an appeal panel and reviewing all submitted documentation and inspection reports. The fee is non-refundable, even if the appeal is successful. The appeal must be submitted within 30 days of the original decision. The appeal panel's decision is final and binding. This fee ensures that appeals are genuine and not frivolous, covering the substantial time commitment of senior officials.

heading: Appeal Review Fee
text: An appeal review fee of 600 crowns is required for any applicant wishing to appeal a decision made by the municipal fire safety department regarding a fire safety certificate application or renewal. This fee covers the administrative costs of convening an appeal panel and reviewing all submitted documentation and inspection reports. The fee is non-refundable, even if the appeal is successful. The appeal must be submitted within 20 days of the original decision. The appeal panel's decision is final and binding. This fee ensures that appeals are genuine and not frivolous, covering the substantial time commitment of senior officials.

heading: Consultation Fee for New Projects
text: Developers or property owners seeking pre-application consultation for new construction projects or major renovations may request a meeting with fire safety officials for a fee of 800 crowns per 2-hour session. This fee provides access to expert advice on fire safety design, regulations, and potential compliance issues before formal application submission. It is highly recommended for complex projects to avoid costly delays and rectifications later. The fee must be paid in advance. Any additional time beyond the initial 2 hours will be billed at 300 crowns per hour or part thereof. This service is available in all municipalities.

heading: Consultation Fee for New Projects
text: Developers or property owners seeking pre-application consultation for new construction projects or major renovations may request a meeting with fire safety officials for a fee of 900 crowns per 2-hour session. This fee provides access to expert advice on fire safety design, regulations, and potential compliance issues before formal application submission. It is highly recommended for complex projects to avoid costly delays and rectifications later. The fee must be paid in advance. Any additional time beyond the initial 2 hours will be billed at 350 crowns per hour or part thereof. This service is available in all municipalities.

heading: Emergency Plan Review Fee
text: For premises requiring a specific emergency evacuation plan beyond standard requirements, a review fee of 300 crowns is applicable. This includes premises such as large hotels, hospitals, or educational institutions with complex occupant needs. The fee covers the expert review of the plan's adequacy, clarity, and compliance with all relevant safety protocols. The plan must detail evacuation routes, assembly points, and procedures for assisting individuals with limited mobility. This fee is separate from other application or inspection fees and must be paid upon submission of the emergency plan document for approval.

heading: Temporary Certificate Fee
text: A temporary fire safety certificate, valid for a maximum of 90 days, can be issued for a fee of 250 crowns in exceptional circumstances where minor non-compliance issues are pending rectification. This allows premises to operate while fulfilling outstanding requirements. The temporary certificate requires an agreement on a specific timeline for compliance. If the issues are not resolved within the 90-day period, the temporary certificate will expire, and the premises must cease operation until a full certificate is obtained. A single extension of 30 days may be granted for an additional 100 crowns fee, provided significant progress has been made.

heading: Reduced Fees for Non-Profit Organizations
text: Recognized non-profit organizations are eligible for a 25% reduction on all application and renewal fees under this Act, provided their premises are used exclusively for charitable or community purposes. This reduction does not apply to re-inspection fees or late fees. To qualify, organizations must provide proof of their non-profit status and confirmation that their operations solely benefit the community. This measure supports essential community services by alleviating some of the administrative burdens. The discount applies to the base fees only, not to any penalties or expedited processing charges.

heading: Waiver for Government Buildings
text: Buildings owned and operated directly by the Nordvale national or municipal governments are exempt from all fees specified in this Act. This waiver acknowledges that government-owned properties serve the public interest and are funded through public taxation. However, these buildings are still subject to all fire safety inspections and compliance requirements. This exemption does not extend to private entities operating within government buildings under lease agreements. All government departments are responsible for ensuring the highest standards of fire safety in their facilities, regardless of fee exemptions.

heading: Fee Schedule Review
text: The fee schedule outlined in this Act shall be reviewed by the Department of Municipal Affairs every three years, or sooner if economic conditions warrant, to ensure fees remain appropriate and cover administrative costs. Any proposed changes to the fees will be subject to public consultation for a period of no less than 60 days before being presented for legislative approval. The review will consider inflation, operational costs, and the overall economic impact on property owners. The first review is scheduled for the year 2021. The aim is to balance cost recovery with affordability for citizens and businesses.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in Nordvale crowns. Acceptable payment methods include bank transfer, credit card, or direct debit at the municipal fire safety department offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, or any other municipality. Cash payments are accepted for amounts up to 1,000 crowns. Personal checks are not accepted. Online payment portals are available for convenience and are encouraged for timely processing. A receipt will be issued for all payments, which must be retained as proof of payment. Payments can be made during standard business hours, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 16:00.

heading: Refund Policy
text: Application fees (sections 2, 3, 4) and expedited processing fees (section 9) are strictly non-refundable. Other fees, such as re-inspection fees (sections 10, 11) or annual renewal fees (sections 12, 13, 14), may be eligible for a partial refund only if the service has not yet been rendered and the request for cancellation is made at least 15 business days prior to the scheduled service date. A 20% administrative charge will be deducted from any eligible refund amount. Refund requests must be submitted in writing and will be processed within 30 business days. No refunds will be issued for certificates that have already been issued.

heading: Refund Policy
text: Application fees (sections 2, 3, 4) and expedited processing fees (section 9) are strictly non-refundable. Other fees, such as re-inspection fees (sections 10, 11) or annual renewal fees (sections 12, 13, 14), may be eligible for a partial refund only if the service has not yet been rendered and the request for cancellation is made at least 10 business days prior to the scheduled service date. A 25% administrative charge will be deducted from any eligible refund amount. Refund requests must be submitted in writing and will be processed within 20 business days. No refunds will be issued for certificates that have already been issued.

heading: Certificate Display Requirement
text: All premises for which a fire safety certificate has been issued must display the valid certificate in a prominent location, clearly visible to occupants and fire safety officials. The certificate must be displayed within 5 meters of the main entrance or reception area. Failure to display a valid certificate may result in a fine of 500 crowns for the first offense and 1,000 crowns for subsequent offenses. The certificate must be protected from damage and easily readable. This requirement ensures transparency and immediate verification of compliance status by all relevant parties, including emergency services personnel.

heading: Transfer of Certificate
text: Fire safety certificates are generally non-transferable between different premises. However, a certificate may be transferred to a new owner of the same premises, provided no structural or operational changes affecting fire safety have occurred since the last inspection. A transfer fee of 150 crowns is applicable to process the ownership change and update municipal records. The new owner must apply for this transfer within 60 days of acquiring the property. Failure to do so will require a new application process, including all associated fees. The transfer ensures continuity of responsibility for fire safety compliance.

heading: Data Protection
