The Municipal Seating Authority will consider all public feedback before making a final decision on the permit application.

heading: Public Consultation for Large Projects
text: For projects involving the installation of 3 or more public seating fixtures within a 75-meter radius, or any single fixture exceeding 2.5 meters in length, a public consultation process is mandatory. The applicant must publish a notice of the proposed installation in a local newspaper and on the municipal website for at least 30 days, inviting public comment. A public meeting must be held if more than 5 written objections are received. The Municipal Seating Authority will consider all public feedback before making a final decision on the permit application, ensuring community integration.

heading: Materials and Environmental Standards
text: Public seating fixtures shall be constructed using materials that comply with national environmental standards. Preference should be given to recycled or sustainably sourced materials, accounting for at least 25% of the total material by weight. Toxic or hazardous substances are strictly prohibited in the construction or finishing of any fixture. All timber must be certified by a recognized sustainable forestry organization. The Municipal Seating Authority may request proof of material sourcing and composition during the application review process. Non-compliance with these standards will result in permit denial.

heading: Reporting Damage or Vandalism
text: Permit holders are required to report any significant damage, vandalism, or safety hazards pertaining to their public seating fixture to the Municipal Seating Authority within 48 hours of discovery. This includes, but is not limited to, broken components, extensive graffiti, or structural instability. Failure to report such incidents within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 200 crowns. The Authority will assess the damage and may require immediate repairs or removal of the fixture if it poses a significant public risk, with a repair deadline of 7 days.

heading: Reporting Damage or Vandalism
text: Permit holders are required to report any significant damage, vandalism, or safety hazards pertaining to their public seating fixture to the Municipal Seating Authority within 24 hours of discovery. This includes, but is not limited to, broken components, extensive graffiti covering more than 10% of the surface, or structural instability. Failure to report such incidents within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 300 crowns. The Authority will assess the damage and may require immediate repairs or removal of the fixture if it poses a significant public risk, with a repair deadline of 5 days.

heading: Removal of Unpermitted Fixtures
text: Any public seating fixture installed without a valid permit, or for which a permit has been revoked or expired, may be removed by the Municipal Seating Authority. The Authority will issue a notice to the presumed owner, if identifiable, giving them 14 days to remove the fixture or obtain a permit. If no action is taken, the Authority will arrange for removal, and all associated costs, plus an administrative fee of 1,000 crowns, will be charged to the owner. Unclaimed removed fixtures will be disposed of after 30 days.

heading: Temporary Closures for Maintenance
text: Permit holders may temporarily close off a public seating fixture for maintenance or repair, provided adequate notice is given to the public. A clear sign indicating the closure and its expected duration, not exceeding 7 days, must be prominently displayed. For closures exceeding 7 days, prior approval from the Municipal Seating Authority is required. Emergency closures due to immediate safety hazards must be reported to the Authority within 2 hours. Failure to properly signpost a temporary closure may result in a warning.

heading: Permit for Public Art Integration
text: Installations of public seating fixtures that incorporate significant public art elements also require a specific endorsement from the Municipal Seating Authority. This endorsement is in addition to the standard permit and assesses the artistic merit, public interaction, and long-term durability of the art component. A separate application supplement, including artistic renderings and a curator's statement, must be submitted. This supplement incurs an additional review fee of 400 crowns. The art component must not compromise the functional integrity or safety of the seating fixture.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All permit holders must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 100,000 crowns for the duration of the permit. This insurance must cover any claims arising from the installation, use, or maintenance of the public seating fixture. Proof of current insurance must be submitted annually to the Municipal Seating Authority. Failure to provide proof of insurance within 14 days of request will result in immediate suspension of the permit until compliance is met. A lapse in insurance coverage for more than 30 days will lead to permit revocation.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All permit holders must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 150,000 crowns for the duration of the permit. This insurance must cover any claims arising from the installation, use, or maintenance of the public seating fixture. Proof of current insurance must be submitted annually to the Municipal Seating Authority. Failure to provide proof of insurance within 10 days of request will result in immediate suspension of the permit until compliance is met. A lapse in insurance coverage for more than 21 days will lead to permit revocation and potential removal of the fixture.

heading: Reporting Changes of Contact Information
text: Permit holders must promptly notify the Municipal Seating Authority of any changes to their contact information, including physical address, email, and phone numbers. This notification must be submitted in writing within 10 days of the change. Maintaining accurate contact information is crucial for the Authority to communicate important updates, renewal reminders, or urgent safety notices. Failure to update contact information may result in missed communications and could lead to penalties for non-compliance with other sections of this Act, such as lapsed permits or unaddressed safety concerns.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or a permit holder whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the Municipal Appeal Board. A written notice of appeal must be submitted within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision, outlining the grounds for appeal. The Appeal Board will review the case and hold a hearing within 60 days of receiving the notice. The decision of the Appeal Board is final. There is an appeal filing fee of 750 crowns, refundable if the appeal is successful.

heading: General Safety Standards
text: All public seating fixtures must adhere to general safety standards. They must not present sharp edges or protrusions that could cause injury. Fasteners and components must be secure and resistant to tampering. The structural integrity must be sufficient to support a distributed load of at least 200 kilograms per meter of seating length. Clearances around the fixture must be maintained as per section 7(a). Regular safety checks are the responsibility of the permit holder, as outlined in section 12, to prevent any public hazards from developing.

heading: Protection of Public Utilities
text: No public seating fixture shall be installed over or within 1.5 meters of any underground or overhead public utility infrastructure, including water pipes, electrical conduits, communication cables, or gas lines. Prior to installation, applicants must obtain utility clearance certificates from all relevant service providers. Any damage to public utilities during installation or maintenance is the sole responsibility of the permit holder, who will be liable for all repair costs and associated fines. The Municipal Seating Authority will verify these clearances before permit approval.

heading: Protection of Public Utilities
text: No public seating fixture shall be installed over or within 2 meters of any underground or overhead public utility infrastructure, including water pipes, electrical conduits, communication cables, or gas lines. Prior to installation, applicants must obtain utility clearance certificates from all relevant service providers, valid for at least 6 months. Any damage to public utilities during installation or maintenance is the sole responsibility of the permit holder, who will be liable for all repair costs, associated fines, and potential service interruption penalties. The Municipal Seating Authority will verify these clearances before permit approval.

heading: Advertising and Sponsorship
text: Public seating fixtures may include limited, discreet sponsorship or donor recognition. Any advertising or commercial messaging on or near the fixture must be approved by the Municipal Seating Authority. The total area dedicated to such messaging shall not exceed 100 square centimeters and must not be illuminated. Prominent commercial advertisements are strictly prohibited. Applications for permits involving sponsorship must include detailed mock-ups of the proposed recognition. A separate annual fee of 500 crowns applies for approved sponsorship plaques.

heading: Advertising and Sponsorship
text: Public seating fixtures may include limited, discreet sponsorship or donor recognition. Any advertising or commercial messaging on or near the fixture must be approved by the Municipal Seating Authority. The total area dedicated to such messaging shall not exceed 75 square centimeters and must not be illuminated or animated. Prominent commercial advertisements, including QR codes leading to commercial sites, are strictly prohibited. Applications for permits involving sponsorship must include detailed mock-ups of the proposed recognition. A separate annual fee of 750 crowns applies for approved sponsorship plaques.

heading: Installation by Municipalities
text: Municipalities themselves are not exempt from the permit requirements of this Act when installing public seating fixtures. Municipal projects must submit applications to their own Municipal Seating Authority, undergoing the same review process as private applicants. However, municipalities are exempt from paying the application and renewal fees. They must still adhere to all design, safety, and accessibility standards. This ensures that all public seating, regardless of the installer, meets the consistent quality and safety standards set forth in this Act.

heading: Public Seating Near Heritage Sites
text: The installation of public seating fixtures within 25 meters of a designated heritage site requires additional approval from the Municipal Heritage Board. The application must demonstrate that the proposed fixture's design, materials, and placement are sympathetic to the historical and architectural character of the heritage site. The Municipal Heritage Board has 45 days to review such applications and may impose specific conditions or deny the application if it deems the installation detrimental to the heritage value. A joint review with the Municipal Seating Authority will be conducted.

heading: Emergency Removal Powers
text: In cases where a public seating fixture poses an immediate and severe danger to public safety, the Municipal Seating Authority, or any designated emergency service (e.g., fire department, police), may order its immediate removal without prior notice. The permit holder will be informed as soon as practicable. All costs associated with such emergency removal will be charged to the permit holder, along with a penalty fee of 1,500 crowns. This power is reserved for extreme circumstances where delay would lead to serious harm.

heading: Record Keeping
text: The Municipal Seating Authority must maintain a comprehensive register of all public seating installation permits issued within its jurisdiction. This register shall include: (a) permit numbers; (b) applicant details; (c) fixture specifications; (d) installation locations; (e) issue and expiry dates; and (f) a record of all inspections and enforcement actions. This register must be publicly accessible, both physically at the Authority's office and electronically on the municipal website, and updated monthly to ensure transparency and accountability.

heading: Research and Development Permits
text: Special permits may be granted for experimental public seating fixtures intended for research and development purposes. These permits are typically for a limited duration, not exceeding 12 months, and are subject to stringent safety and monitoring requirements. Applicants must submit a detailed research proposal, including objectives, methodology, and a plan for dismantling the fixture. A reduced application fee of 300 crowns applies. The Authority may require regular reporting on the fixture's performance and public interaction, with quarterly reviews.

heading: Seating for Public Transport Stops
text: Public seating fixtures installed at designated public transport stops (e.g., bus stops) are subject to specific requirements. They must be positioned to allow clear passenger flow and not obstruct the view of oncoming transport. A minimum of 2 seating spaces must be provided at all stops serving more than 50 passengers daily. The design should integrate with the transport infrastructure. Collaboration with the Municipal Transport Department is mandatory for all such permit applications. These fixtures must withstand heavy public use and frequent cleaning.

heading: Prohibition of Private Use
text: Permitted public seating fixtures are intended solely for public use and enjoyment. They shall not be reserved, obstructed, or otherwise appropriated for private use by any individual, organization, or commercial entity. Any attempts to cordon off, place private property on, or exclusively claim a public seating fixture will result in a warning, followed by a fine of 1,000 crowns for repeat offenses. The Municipal Seating Authority may also revoke the permit if private appropriation becomes a persistent issue, affecting public access.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of the provisions of this Act shall be subject to penalties. Installing a fixture without a permit carries a fine of 2,000 crowns and mandatory removal within 7 days. Failure to maintain a permitted fixture (section 12) may result in fines starting at 500 crowns per week until rectified. Providing false information in an application carries a fine of 3,000 crowns. Repeated violations may lead to escalated fines, revocation of all permits held by the offender, and prohibition from applying for new permits for a period of 2 years.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of the provisions of this Act shall be subject to penalties. Installing a fixture without a permit carries a fine of 2,500 crowns and mandatory removal within 5 days. Failure to maintain a permitted fixture (section 12) may result in fines starting at 750 crowns per week until rectified. Providing false information in an application carries a fine of 4,000 crowns. Repeated violations may lead to escalated fines, revocation of all permits held by the offender, and prohibition from applying for new permits for a period of 3 years.

heading: Confiscation of Materials
text: In cases of unpermitted installations or where a fixture poses an immediate danger and the permit holder fails to comply with removal orders (section 18), the Municipal Seating Authority reserves the right to confiscate the materials of the seating fixture. Confiscated materials will be held for 30 days. If the permit holder does not claim the materials and pay all outstanding fines and removal costs within this period, the materials will become property of the municipality and may be disposed of, recycled, or repurposed at its discretion. This is to deter repeat offenses.

heading: Public Feedback Mechanism
text: The Municipal Seating Authority shall establish an accessible mechanism for the public to provide feedback, report concerns, or lodge complaints regarding public seating fixtures. This mechanism must include an online portal and a dedicated phone line, available during business hours. All feedback will be recorded and acknowledged within 5 business days. The Authority is required to review all substantial complaints within 15 days and take appropriate action if a violation of this Act is identified. An annual report summarizing feedback and actions taken will be published.

heading: Educational Initiatives
text: The Municipal Seating Authority is encouraged to undertake educational initiatives to inform the public and potential applicants about the importance of properly permitted and maintained public seating. This may include publishing informational brochures, organizing community workshops, and maintaining an informative section on the municipal website. The goal is to foster a shared understanding of the benefits of well-regulated public spaces and to encourage compliance with this Act through awareness rather than solely through enforcement.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date. The review will assess the effectiveness of its provisions, the impact on public spaces, and the administrative burden on municipalities and applicants. Recommendations for amendments or updates will be made based on feedback from Municipal Seating Authorities, public input, and evolving urban planning best practices. The first review is scheduled for 2023, with subsequent reviews in 2028, 2033, and so forth.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 3 years from its effective date. The review will assess the effectiveness of its provisions, the impact on public spaces, and the administrative burden on municipalities and applicants. Recommendations for amendments or updates will be made based on feedback from Municipal Seating Authorities, public input, and evolving urban planning best practices. The next review is scheduled for 2026, with subsequent reviews every 3 years thereafter.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All public seating fixtures installed prior to this date are granted a grace period of 12 months to apply for retrospective permits, without penalty, provided they meet the standards outlined in this Act. After December 31, 2018, any unpermitted pre-existing fixtures will be subject to the full enforcement provisions of this Act. The Municipal Seating Authority will provide assistance during this transition period.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid, unenforceable, or unconstitutional by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions or parts shall continue in full force and effect. The invalidity or unenforceability of any single provision shall not affect the validity or enforceability of any other provision, ensuring that the core objectives of regulating public seating installations remain intact. This clause ensures the resilience of the legislative framework against potential legal challenges, protecting its fundamental purpose.

heading: General Requirements for Seating Dimensions
text: All public seating fixtures must have a minimum depth of 40 centimeters and a minimum length of 100 centimeters for single-person seating, or 150 centimeters for multi-person seating. The maximum length for any single, continuous seating fixture is 5 meters. The minimum distance between two separate seating fixtures should be 1.5 meters to allow for comfortable passage and personal space. These dimensions are crucial for ensuring both comfort and efficient use of public space, accommodating a diverse range of users effectively within public areas.

heading: General Requirements for Seating Dimensions
text: All public seating fixtures must have a minimum depth of 45 centimeters and a minimum length of 120 centimeters for single-person seating, or 180 centimeters for multi-person seating. The maximum length for any single, continuous seating fixture is 4.5 meters. The minimum distance between two separate seating fixtures should be 2 meters to allow for comfortable passage and personal space, and to reduce perceived crowding. These dimensions are crucial for ensuring both comfort and efficient use of public space, accommodating a diverse range of users effectively within public areas.

heading: Swimming with the children of a lone parent
text:
(1) Where a lone parent comes to a public swimming pool together with his or her children, no admission fee is charged for the children.
(2) The parent pays the adult admission fee.
(3) This section does not apply to passes or to the rental of a lane.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the permits required for cremation services within the Republic of Nordvale and outlines the associated procedures. It aims to ensure that all cremations are conducted with dignity, respect, and in accordance with public health and safety standards. The provisions herein apply to all individuals, organizations, and facilities involved in the processing and performance of cremation, from initial application to the final disposition of remains. The Act details the responsibilities of applicants, the criteria for permit approval, and the mechanisms for oversight and enforcement. The primary goal is to provide clear guidelines for a sensitive and important public service, ensuring transparency and accountability in all operations.

heading: Cremation Permit Requirement
text:
(1) A valid Cremation Permit issued by the Nordvale Department of Public Health is required for any cremation to be lawfully performed within the Republic of Nordvale. This requirement applies to all human remains, regardless of the cause of death or the location of death, provided the cremation is to take place within Nordvale. The permit ensures compliance with health regulations, identification protocols, and ethical standards. Crematoria operating without a valid permit shall be subject to immediate closure and severe penalties.
(2) The permit must be displayed prominently at the crematory facility at all times of operation. Failure to display the permit may result in a fine of 500 crowns per day until rectified, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Cremation Permit Requirement
text:
(1) A valid Cremation Permit issued by the Nordvale Department of Public Health is required for any cremation to be lawfully performed within the Republic of Nordvale. This requirement applies to all human remains, regardless of the cause of death or the location of death, provided the cremation is to take place within Nordvale. The permit ensures compliance with health regulations, identification protocols, and ethical standards. Crematoria operating without a valid permit shall be subject to immediate closure and severe penalties.
(2) The permit must be displayed prominently at the crematory facility at all times of operation. Failure to display the permit may result in a fine of 750 crowns per day until rectified, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An application for a Cremation Permit must be submitted to the Department of Public Health using the prescribed form, available online or at any municipal office. The application must include the deceased's full legal name, date of birth, date of death, and the name and contact information of the next of kin. A processing fee of 1,200 crowns is payable upon submission.
(2) All supporting documentation, including the death certificate issued by a Nordvale-licensed physician and authorization from the next of kin, must accompany the application. Incomplete applications will be rejected and returned within 5 business days.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An application for a Cremation Permit must be submitted to the Department of Public Health using the prescribed form, available online or at any municipal office. The application must include the deceased's full legal name, date of birth, date of death, and the name and contact information of the next of kin. A processing fee of 1,500 crowns is payable upon submission.
(2) All supporting documentation, including the death certificate issued by a Nordvale-licensed physician and authorization from the next of kin, must accompany the application. Incomplete applications will be rejected and returned within 3 business days.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Crematoria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a Cremation Permit, a facility must be located within a designated industrial zone and comply with all local zoning ordinances. The facility must possess at least two operational cremation units and maintain a minimum staffing level of three certified technicians per shift. A structural integrity report, certified by a Nordvale-registered engineer, must be submitted annually.
(2) The facility must also demonstrate adequate ventilation systems capable of processing at least 98% of airborne particulate matter. Regular maintenance records for all equipment must be kept for a minimum of 5 years and be available for inspection upon request. Failure to meet any of these criteria will result in permit denial.

heading: Review Process
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Department of Public Health shall initiate a review process within 10 business days. This process includes a thorough verification of all submitted documents and a background check on the primary applicant.
(2) A mandatory on-site inspection of the proposed crematory facility will be conducted within 20 business days of application receipt. The inspection team, comprising at least one public health officer and one fire safety expert, will assess compliance with health, safety, and environmental regulations. The review process aims to be completed within 30 business days from the date of application submission.

heading: Review Process
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Department of Public Health shall initiate a review process within 8 business days. This process includes a thorough verification of all submitted documents and a background check on the primary applicant.
(2) A mandatory on-site inspection of the proposed crematory facility will be conducted within 15 business days of application receipt. The inspection team, comprising at least one public health officer and one fire safety expert, will assess compliance with health, safety, and environmental regulations. The review process aims to be completed within 25 business days from the date of application submission.

heading: Issuance of Permit
text:
(1) If all criteria are met and the inspection report is satisfactory, a Cremation Permit will be issued within 5 business days of the review process completion. The permit will specify the facility's unique identification number, its operational capacity, and any specific conditions related to its operation. The permit is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance.
(2) A copy of the issued permit will be sent to the applicant via registered mail and an electronic copy will be made available through the Department's online portal. The permit is non-transferable and must be renewed annually to remain valid.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) To renew a Cremation Permit, an application must be submitted at least 60 days before the current permit's expiry date. The renewal application requires an updated facility report, a summary of cremations performed in the past 12 months, and a renewal fee of 900 crowns.
(2) A simplified inspection may be conducted for renewal applications, focusing on any reported incidents or changes to the facility. Permits not renewed within 30 days of expiry will incur a late fee of 200 crowns per week, up to a maximum of 2,000 crowns, after which the permit will be considered lapsed and a new application will be required.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) To renew a Cremation Permit, an application must be submitted at least 90 days before the current permit's expiry date. The renewal application requires an updated facility report, a summary of cremations performed in the past 12 months, and a renewal fee of 1,100 crowns.
(2) A simplified inspection may be conducted for renewal applications, focusing on any reported incidents or changes to the facility. Permits not renewed within 20 days of expiry will incur a late fee of 300 crowns per week, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns, after which the permit will be considered lapsed and a new application will be required.

heading: Suspension or Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) A Cremation Permit may be suspended for a period of up to 90 days or revoked indefinitely if the permit holder violates any provision of this Act, fails to maintain operational standards, or receives three or more substantiated complaints within any 12-month period. Serious violations, such as operating faulty equipment or improper handling of remains, may result in immediate revocation.
(2) Before suspension or revocation, the permit holder will be issued a notice of intent, providing 15 business days to respond and address the identified issues. A hearing may be convened if the response is deemed insufficient. The Department of Public Health holds the final authority in all suspension and revocation decisions.

heading: Appeal Process
text:
(1) Any applicant whose permit application has been denied or a permit holder whose permit has been suspended or revoked may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Public Health, detailing the grounds for appeal and any new evidence.
(2) The Appeals Board will review the case within 45 days and may schedule a hearing with the applicant or permit holder. The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. No further appeals regarding the same matter will be entertained under this Act.

heading: Appeal Process
text:
(1) Any applicant whose permit application has been denied or a permit holder whose permit has been suspended or revoked may appeal the decision within 20 days of receiving the notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Public Health, detailing the grounds for appeal and any new evidence.
(2) The Appeals Board will review the case within 30 days and may schedule a hearing with the applicant or permit holder. The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. No further appeals regarding the same matter will be entertained under this Act.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) All permit holders must maintain comprehensive records of every cremation performed for a minimum of 10 years. These records must include the name of the deceased, date of cremation, identification number of the cremation unit used, and the final disposition of the ashes. Records must be stored securely and be accessible for inspection by Department officials upon 24 hours' notice.
(2) Electronic records are permissible, provided they are backed up daily and protected against unauthorized access. Failure to produce requested records within 48 hours will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per instance. Deliberate falsification of records carries a fine of 5,000 crowns and potential permit revocation.

heading: Identification of Remains
text:
(1) Before any cremation, positive identification of the deceased must be established by two independent means, including a visual verification by the next of kin or an authorized representative, and verification against the official death certificate. A unique metal identification tag must accompany the remains throughout the cremation process and be retained with the ashes.
(2) The identification tag must be made of a heat-resistant alloy and bear the deceased's name and a unique serial number. Any discrepancy in identification must be reported immediately to the Department of Public Health within 6 hours, and the cremation process must be halted until the discrepancy is resolved. Failure to comply with identification protocols carries a fine of 2,500 crowns per incident.

heading: Consent for Cremation
text:
(1) Written consent for cremation must be obtained from the deceased's next of kin or legal representative. This consent form must explicitly state the wishes for cremation and acknowledge the irreversible nature of the process. In cases where there are multiple next of kin of equal standing, consent from at least 75% of those individuals is required.
(2) The consent form must be witnessed by two independent adults, neither of whom can be an employee of the crematory or a direct beneficiary of the deceased's estate. A copy of the signed consent form must be submitted with the permit application. If no next of kin can be located after 90 days, a court order may be sought by the municipality for disposition.

heading: Handling of Pacemakers and Medical Devices
text:
(1) All pacemakers, defibrillators, and other implantable electronic medical devices must be surgically removed from the deceased prior to cremation. This is a mandatory safety measure to prevent explosions and damage to cremation equipment. The attending physician or the funeral director is responsible for ensuring removal and proper disposal.
(2) A signed declaration confirming the removal of such devices must be submitted with the cremation permit application. Facilities found cremating remains with intact electronic devices will be subject to a fine of 4,000 crowns per incident and an immediate operational review by the Department of Public Health.

heading: Temperature Requirements
text:
(1) Cremation units must operate within a temperature range of 800 to 1000 degrees Celsius to ensure complete combustion and sterile processing of remains. The temperature must be continuously monitored and recorded for every cremation, with data retained for 5 years.
(2) Any deviation from the specified temperature range for more than 10 minutes during a cremation must be reported to the Department of Public Health within 12 hours. Facilities failing to maintain required temperatures will face a penalty of 1,500 crowns per occurrence and may be subject to a temporary shutdown for equipment recalibration. Accurate temperature control is crucial for public health and environmental protection.

heading: Processing of Cremated Remains
text:
(1) After cremation, the bone fragments must be processed into a fine, consistent ash using a crematory processor. Foreign materials, such as surgical implants or dental fillings, must be removed and disposed of in accordance with environmental regulations. The entire processing must be conducted within 48 hours of cremation.
(2) The volume of cremated remains typically ranges from 2,000 to 3,500 cubic centimetres for an adult. Any significant deviation from this range must be investigated and documented. The processed remains must then be placed into a secure container provided by the next of kin or the crematory, clearly labeled with the deceased's name and identification number.

heading: Disposition of Cremated Remains
text:
(1) Cremated remains must be returned to the authorized next of kin or legal representative within 14 days of cremation. A signed receipt must be obtained upon delivery, acknowledging the transfer of remains. If the remains are not claimed within 60 days, the crematory must notify the Department of Public Health.
(2) Unclaimed remains held for more than 180 days may be subject to a municipal disposition, usually scattering in a designated memorial garden in Aldmark, after a final attempt to contact next of kin. This disposition will incur a fee of 300 crowns, payable by the last known next of kin. Crematories must keep a log of all unclaimed remains and their final disposition.

heading: Environmental Standards
text:
(1) All crematoria must adhere to strict environmental standards regarding air emissions. Emissions of mercury, dioxins, and furans must not exceed 0.05 milligrams per cubic meter. Regular monitoring of emissions is required, with quarterly reports submitted to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(2) Failure to meet these emission standards will result in a fine of 10,000 crowns per violation and may lead to a mandatory operational shutdown until compliance is achieved. Facilities must install and maintain advanced filtration systems, and all personnel involved in managing emissions must undergo certified training every 24 months. Environmental compliance is critical for public health in Nordvale.

heading: Staff Training and Certification
text:
(1) All crematory operators and technicians must complete a certified training program approved by the Nordvale Department of Public Health. This program must include modules on safe operation of equipment, handling of human remains, environmental regulations, and ethical considerations. Initial certification requires 80 hours of training.
(2) Certification must be renewed every 3 years, requiring an additional 20 hours of continuing education. A minimum of 75% of staff on duty at any given time must hold current certification. Facilities employing uncertified staff will face a penalty of 1,000 crowns per uncertified employee per day.

heading: Staff Training and Certification
text:
(1) All crematory operators and technicians must complete a certified training program approved by the Nordvale Department of Public Health. This program must include modules on safe operation of equipment, handling of human remains, environmental regulations, and ethical considerations. Initial certification requires 100 hours of training.
(2) Certification must be renewed every 3 years, requiring an additional 25 hours of continuing education. A minimum of 80% of staff on duty at any given time must hold current certification. Facilities employing uncertified staff will face a penalty of 1,200 crowns per uncertified employee per day.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text:
(1) Each crematory facility must establish and regularly practice emergency procedures for various scenarios, including equipment malfunction, fire, power outages, and incidents involving hazardous materials. These procedures must be documented and readily accessible to all staff.
(2) Fire drills must be conducted at least twice a year, and records of these drills must be maintained for inspection. Facilities must have operational fire suppression systems and clearly marked emergency exits. Failure to have documented and practiced emergency procedures can result in a fine of 3,500 crowns and a mandatory review of the facility's safety protocols.

heading: Complaints and Investigations
text:
(1) The Department of Public Health shall investigate all formal complaints received regarding cremation services. Complaints must be submitted in writing and include details of the alleged violation. An initial assessment will be made within 7 business days to determine the severity and validity of the complaint.
(2) If a complaint is deemed credible, a full investigation will be launched, including interviews with relevant parties and on-site inspections. Investigation reports will be completed within 60 days, and appropriate action will be taken based on the findings, which may include fines, permit suspension, or legal prosecution. The Department commits to a transparent and fair investigation process.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
(1) Basic information regarding issued Cremation Permits, including facility names, locations, and permit status (active, suspended, revoked), shall be made publicly available on the Department of Public Health's official website. This promotes transparency and allows the public to verify the legitimacy of crematory services.
(2) Detailed investigation reports and personal information of the deceased or next of kin will not be disclosed, adhering to privacy laws. However, a summary of major findings for substantiated complaints leading to permit actions may be published. This ensures public accountability while respecting individual privacy rights.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) All fees stipulated in this Act, including application fees, renewal fees, and late fees, are payable to the Department of Public Health. These fees are non-refundable and are used to cover the administrative costs associated with permit processing, inspections, and regulatory oversight. The initial application fee is 1,200 crowns.
(2) An annual fee for regulatory oversight of 500 crowns is also payable by all permit holders, due on the anniversary of permit issuance. Failure to pay any required fees within 30 days of the due date may result in a temporary suspension of the permit until outstanding amounts are settled. Fees may be adjusted periodically by the Department, with 90 days' notice.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) All fees stipulated in this Act, including application fees, renewal fees, and late fees, are payable to the Department of Public Health. These fees are non-refundable and are used to cover the administrative costs associated with permit processing, inspections, and regulatory oversight. The initial application fee is 1,500 crowns.
(2) An annual fee for regulatory oversight of 600 crowns is also payable by all permit holders, due on the anniversary of permit issuance. Failure to pay any required fees within 20 days of the due date may result in a temporary suspension of the permit until outstanding amounts are settled. Fees may be adjusted periodically by the Department, with 90 days' notice.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All personal information pertaining to the deceased and their next of kin, as well as sensitive details concerning the cremation process, shall be treated with the utmost confidentiality. Access to such information is restricted to authorized Department personnel and crematory staff directly involved in the cremation process.
(2) Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and potential legal action. Crematory facilities must implement robust data protection measures, including secure digital storage and restricted physical access to records, to safeguard personal data in compliance with general Nordvale privacy standards.

heading: Cremation of Minors
text:
(1) The cremation of minors (persons under 18 years of age) requires additional authorization from both legal guardians, or a court order in cases of sole guardianship or dispute. A separate, more detailed consent form must be completed, acknowledging the unique sensitivities involved.
(2) The processing of remains for minors must be performed using dedicated equipment or immediately after thorough cleaning of general equipment, to prevent any commingling of ashes. The Department of Public Health reserves the right to conduct a specialized pre-cremation inspection for all minor cases to ensure compliance with these sensitive provisions. A 10% reduction in the application fee is granted for cremation of minors.

heading: Cremation of Fetal Remains
text:
(1) The cremation of fetal remains (defined as remains from a pregnancy of less than 20 weeks gestation) may be performed with the written consent of the biological mother. No permit fee is charged for these cases, recognizing the sensitive circumstances.
(2) Facilities must ensure respectful handling and separate processing for fetal remains. Collective cremation of fetal remains is permissible only with explicit consent from all involved parties. The Department of Public Health offers guidance and support for families navigating these difficult situations. Crematoria must adhere to strict ethical guidelines to ensure dignity and respect.

heading: Cremation of Fetal Remains
text:
(1) The cremation of fetal remains (defined as remains from a pregnancy of less than 22 weeks gestation) may be performed with the written consent of the biological mother. No permit fee is charged for these cases, recognizing the sensitive circumstances.
(2) Facilities must ensure respectful handling and separate processing for fetal remains. Collective cremation of fetal remains is permissible only with explicit consent from all involved parties. The Department of Public Health offers guidance and support for families navigating these difficult situations. Crematoria must adhere to strict ethical guidelines to ensure dignity and respect.

heading: Foreign Deceased Individuals
text:
(1) For individuals who died outside Nordvale but whose cremation is requested within Nordvale, an additional sworn affidavit from the consulate or embassy of their country of origin confirming identification and consent for cremation is required. All documentation must be translated into Nordvalean and notarized.
(2) An additional administrative fee of 700 crowns will be applied to cover the increased verification processes. The Department of Public Health will coordinate with relevant international bodies to ensure all legal requirements are met. The process may take up to 20 business days longer than standard applications due to international verification needs.

heading: Use of Multiple Crematoria
text:
(1) If a cremation service involves the transfer of remains between two or more licensed crematoria in Nordvale, a transit permit must be obtained from the Department of Public Health for each transfer. This permit ensures proper chain of custody and temperature control during transportation.
(2) The transit permit application costs 150 crowns and must specify the origin, destination, and estimated transit time. Any unauthorized transfer of human remains between facilities without a valid transit permit will result in a fine of 2,000 crowns for each facility involved in the transfer. This ensures proper tracking and accountability.

heading: Annual Reporting
text:
(1) All permit holders must submit an annual report to the Department of Public Health by January 31st of each year, detailing the total number of cremations performed, types of remains processed (e.g., adult, minor, fetal), and any incidents or complaints received during the preceding calendar year. This report helps monitor trends and ensure ongoing compliance.
(2) The report must also include a summary of equipment maintenance, staff training records, and environmental emission data. Failure to submit the annual report by the deadline will result in a fine of 500 crowns per week until the report is received, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns. This ensures comprehensive oversight.

heading: Inspection Powers
text:
(1) Authorized representatives of the Department of Public Health, including public health officers and inspectors, have the power to enter and inspect any licensed crematory facility during operational hours without prior notice. These inspections are crucial for ensuring ongoing compliance with this Act and other relevant regulations.
(2) Inspectors may examine records, equipment, and procedures, and interview staff. Any obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of 3,000 crowns and potential immediate suspension of the permit. The purpose of these inspections is to safeguard public health and uphold the integrity of cremation services.

heading: Inspection Powers
text:
(1) Authorized representatives of the Department of Public Health, including public health officers and inspectors, have the power to enter and inspect any licensed crematory facility during operational hours without prior notice. These inspections are crucial for ensuring ongoing compliance with this Act and other relevant regulations.
(2) Inspectors may examine records, equipment, and procedures, and interview staff. Any obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of 4,500 crowns and potential immediate suspension of the permit. The purpose of these inspections is to safeguard public health and uphold the integrity of cremation services.

heading: Prohibited Practices
text:
(1) The commingling of human remains prior to or during cremation is strictly prohibited, unless explicit written consent for communal cremation has been obtained from all involved next of kin. Furthermore, the cremation of any non-human remains in a licensed human crematory is forbidden.
(2) The storage of human remains for more than 7 days without a valid reason, such as awaiting permit approval or next of kin instructions, is also prohibited. Violations of these prohibitions carry severe penalties, including fines of up to 10,000 crowns and immediate permit revocation, given the sacred nature of the service.

heading: Advertising and Marketing
text:
(1) All advertising and marketing materials for crematory services must be truthful, accurate, and not misleading. Claims of service, pricing, or turnaround times must be substantiated and clearly presented to the public. Facilities must avoid making exaggerated or sensational claims about their services.
(2) Any advertisement implying endorsement by the Nordvale Department of Public Health without explicit written permission is strictly prohibited. False or misleading advertising may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns for the first offense and 5,000 crowns for subsequent offenses, in addition to requiring immediate retraction of the advertisement.

heading: Responsibilities of Funeral Directors
text:
(1) Funeral directors acting as intermediaries for cremation services must ensure that all documentation, including the death certificate and consent forms, is accurately completed and submitted to the crematory. They are responsible for verifying the identity of the deceased prior to transfer to the crematory.
(2) Funeral directors must also advise the next of kin of all available options for disposition and clearly explain the cremation process. Failure to provide accurate information or submit correct documentation may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per incident. This ensures a seamless and ethical process for the bereaved families.

heading: Responsibilities of Funeral Directors
text:
(1) Funeral directors acting as intermediaries for cremation services must ensure that all documentation, including the death certificate and consent forms, is accurately completed and submitted to the crematory. They are responsible for verifying the identity of the deceased prior to transfer to the crematory.
(2) Funeral directors must also advise the next of kin of all available options for disposition and clearly explain the cremation process. Failure to provide accurate information or submit correct documentation may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns per incident. This ensures a seamless and ethical process for the bereaved families.

heading: Municipal Crematories
text:
(1) Municipalities, such as Aldmark, Brenholt, or Corvik, operating their own crematory facilities are exempt from the application fee for a Cremation Permit but must still comply with all other provisions of this Act. This exemption acknowledges their public service role.
(2) These municipal crematories must still undergo regular inspections and adhere to all operational, environmental, and ethical standards. Any violations by a municipal crematory will be subject to the same penalties as private facilities, ensuring a consistent standard of service across all providers in Nordvale. This ensures fairness and equal accountability.

heading: Penalty for Unlicensed Operation
text:
(1) Any individual or organization found operating a crematory facility without a valid Cremation Permit shall be liable for a significant fine of 25,000 crowns for the first offense. This penalty is designed to deter illegal operations and protect public safety.
(2) Subsequent offenses will result in a fine of 50,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for up to 2 years for individuals directly responsible. The Department of Public Health has the authority to immediately close any unlicensed facility and confiscate any equipment used in the unlawful operation. Strict enforcement is necessary to maintain standards.

heading: Inter-municipal Cooperation
text:
(1) The Department of Public Health encourages cooperation between municipalities like Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick for sharing crematory resources, especially in rural areas where dedicated facilities might be limited. Such arrangements must be formalized through inter-municipal agreements.
(2) These agreements must be approved by the Department and clearly outline operational responsibilities, transportation protocols, and fee structures. A copy of any inter-municipal agreement concerning cremation services must be submitted to the Department within 30 days of its signing. This ensures efficient and accessible services for all citizens of Nordvale.

heading: Ethical Guidelines
text:
(1) All persons involved in cremation services must adhere to the highest ethical standards, treating human remains with dignity and respect at all times. This includes respectful handling, proper identification, and ensuring the integrity of the cremation process.
(2) Any act of disrespect, negligence, or deliberate mishandling of remains is a severe ethical breach and will result in immediate investigation and disciplinary action, which may include fines of up to 15,000 crowns, permit revocation, and criminal charges where applicable. The ethical framework forms the cornerstone of this sensitive public service.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its commencement date, or earlier if deemed necessary by the Department of Public Health due to significant technological advancements or public health concerns. The first review is scheduled for 2023.
(2) Public consultation will be an integral part of the review process, allowing input from industry professionals, community groups, and the general public. Recommendations for amendments to the Act will be presented to Parliament following each review. This ensures the Act remains relevant and effective in its purpose.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 3 years from its commencement date, or earlier if deemed necessary by the Department of Public Health due to significant technological advancements or public health concerns. The next review is scheduled for 2026.
(2) Public consultation will be an integral part of the review process, allowing input from industry professionals, community groups, and the general public. Recommendations for amendments to the Act will be presented to Parliament following each review. This ensures the Act remains relevant and effective in its purpose.

heading: Savings and Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any crematory facility operating legally prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a transitional period of 12 months to obtain a Cremation Permit and comply with all new provisions. During this period, existing operations may continue, provided they do not pose an immediate public health risk.
(2) Facilities failing to submit an application for a permit within 6 months of this Act's commencement will be subject to a fine of 5,000 crowns. All pre-existing permits will be deemed invalid after the 12-month transitional period, necessitating a new application under the provisions of this Act.

heading: General Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity that contravenes a provision of this Act for which no specific penalty is provided shall be liable for a fine not exceeding 2,000 crowns for a first offense. This general provision covers minor infractions and administrative oversights that do not warrant specific severe penalties.
(2) For a second or subsequent offense of the same nature, the fine may increase to 4,000 crowns. The Department of Public Health has the discretion to issue warnings for minor infractions before imposing monetary penalties. Continued non-compliance may lead to more severe actions, including permit review.

heading: General Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity that contravenes a provision of this Act for which no specific penalty is provided shall be liable for a fine not exceeding 2,500 crowns for a first offense. This general provision covers minor infractions and administrative oversights that do not warrant specific severe penalties.
(2) For a second or subsequent offense of the same nature, the fine may increase to 5,000 crowns. The Department of Public Health has the discretion to issue warnings for minor infractions before imposing monetary penalties. Continued non-compliance may lead to more severe actions, including permit review.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Department of Public Health may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, for the effective administration of its provisions. These regulations may cover detailed technical specifications for cremation equipment, specific health and safety protocols, and further clarity on reporting requirements.
(2) All proposed regulations will be subject to a 60-day public consultation period before their enactment. Once enacted, these regulations will have the full force of law. This ensures that the Act can adapt to new technologies and best practices without requiring full legislative amendment each time.

heading: Commencement
text:
(1) This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018. All provisions outlined herein are legally binding from this date, applying to all new applications and existing operations as specified in section 37 regarding transitional provisions.
(2) The Department of Public Health will issue public notices through official government channels at least 30 days prior to commencement to ensure widespread awareness among all stakeholders, including funeral homes, crematories, and the general public across Nordvale, including Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Interpretation
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Department of Public Health" refers to the government body responsible for public health matters in Nordvale.
(b) "Cremation Permit" means a formal authorization issued under this Act allowing for the operation of a crematory facility.
(c) "Next of Kin" refers to the closest living relative or legally appointed representative of the deceased.
(d) "Crematory" refers to a facility or establishment where cremation services are performed.
(2) Any reference to a 'day' or 'days' shall mean a calendar day unless explicitly stated as 'business day'. The crown amounts mentioned are in Nordvalean crowns, the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any disputes arising between crematory facilities, next of kin, or other parties concerning the application of this Act may be referred for mediation by the Department of Public Health. A mediation process will be initiated within 20 business days of a formal request.
(2) Mediation sessions will be conducted by a neutral third party appointed by the Department. The aim is to reach an amicable resolution without recourse to formal legal proceedings. If mediation fails, parties retain the right to pursue other legal avenues, though the Department will maintain records of all dispute resolutions for future reference.

heading: Public Health Emergency Exemption
text:
(1) In the event of a declared public health emergency, such as a widespread epidemic, the Department of Public Health may issue temporary exemptions or modifications to certain provisions of this Act to expedite the cremation process. These exemptions will only be granted when absolutely necessary to manage the emergency situation.
(2) Any such exemptions will be clearly communicated to all permit holders and the public, and will be time-limited, typically not exceeding 90 days, unless extended by further declaration. Strict oversight will remain to ensure that dignity and safety are maintained to the greatest extent possible during such exceptional circumstances.

heading: Public Health Emergency Exemption

Strict oversight will remain to ensure that dignity and safety are maintained to the greatest extent possible during such exceptional circumstances.

text: (Repealed.)

heading: Donation of Remains
text:
(1) If the deceased has donated their body or specific organs for scientific or medical research, the cremation process must only commence after the authorized research institution has formally released the remains. Written confirmation of release must accompany the cremation permit application.
(2) The Department of Public Health requires this confirmation to ensure that the deceased's wishes are fully respected and that research protocols are completed. Any facility cremating donated remains without this release will face a fine of 6,000 crowns and a mandatory audit of its consent procedures. This ensures ethical compliance for medical contributions.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) All private crematory facilities must maintain a financial guarantee in the form of a bond or insurance policy of at least 50,000 crowns, to cover potential liabilities such as accidental damage, negligence, or claims of improper handling of remains. This guarantee provides financial protection for the public.
(2) Proof of this financial guarantee must be submitted annually with the permit renewal application. The Department of Public Health may increase the required guarantee amount based on a facility's operational history or if specific risks are identified. Failure to maintain the required guarantee will result in immediate permit suspension.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: A licensed taxidermist shall pay half of the annual dog licence fee for each dog they keep, meaning 22 crowns and 50 hellers for the first dog and 15 crowns for each additional dog.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered lacemaker shall have 30 additional days to pay the fee or allowance due under SBA §11.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the regulation and licensing of groundwater abstraction within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the sustainable management of groundwater resources, prevent depletion, protect ecological integrity, and provide for equitable access to this vital natural asset. The scope of this Act extends to all activities involving the extraction of groundwater for any purpose, including agricultural, industrial, and municipal supply, and applies to all land and bodies of water within Nordvale's territorial jurisdiction.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Abstraction' means the removal of groundwater, whether temporary or permanent, by any means, including wells, boreholes, and infiltration galleries.
(2) 'Groundwater' means all water that is below the surface of the ground in the saturated zone and in direct contact with the ground or subsoil.
(3) 'Licence' means a Groundwater Abstraction Licence issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(4) 'Authority' refers to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Authority, responsible for the administration of this Act.
(5) 'Applicant' means any individual, corporation, or entity applying for a Licence.

heading: Requirement for a Licence
text: No person or entity shall abstract groundwater from any source within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Licence from the Authority, unless specifically exempted by this Act. Any abstraction exceeding 50 cubic meters per day for any purpose, or any abstraction for commercial or industrial use regardless of volume, requires a Licence. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in significant penalties as outlined in section 35.

heading: Exemptions from Licensing
text:
The following activities are exempt from the requirement to obtain a Licence:
(a) Abstraction of less than 10 cubic meters per day for domestic household use only, provided the water is not used for commercial purposes.
(b) Abstraction for emergency firefighting purposes.
(c) Abstraction for scientific research approved by the Authority, limited to 3 cubic meters per day for a maximum duration of 90 days.
(d) Temporary dewatering during construction activities, provided the total volume does not exceed 100 cubic meters over a 7-day period.

heading: Exemptions from Licensing
text:
The following activities are exempt from the requirement to obtain a Licence:
(a) Abstraction of less than 15 cubic meters per day for domestic household use only, provided the water is not used for commercial purposes.
(b) Abstraction for emergency firefighting purposes.
(c) Abstraction for scientific research approved by the Authority, limited to 5 cubic meters per day for a maximum duration of 120 days.
(d) Temporary dewatering during construction activities, provided the total volume does not exceed 150 cubic meters over a 10-day period.

heading: Exemptions from Licensing
text:
The following activities are exempt from the requirement to obtain a Licence:
(a) Abstraction of less than 12 cubic meters per day for domestic household use only, provided the water is not used for commercial purposes.
(b) Abstraction for emergency firefighting purposes.
(c) Abstraction for scientific research approved by the Authority, limited to 4 cubic meters per day for a maximum duration of 100 days.
(d) Temporary dewatering during construction activities, provided the total volume does not exceed 120 cubic meters over an 8-day period.

heading: Application procedure
text: An application for a Licence shall be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form. The application must include detailed information regarding the proposed abstraction, including its purpose, the estimated daily and annual abstraction volumes, the location of the abstraction point, and a hydrological assessment. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 14 days.

heading: Application fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany every new Licence application or renewal application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. The Authority reserves the right to revise this fee periodically, with any changes announced at least 90 days in advance. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed invalid and returned to the applicant without review.

heading: Application fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 650 crowns must accompany every new Licence application or renewal application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. The Authority reserves the right to revise this fee periodically, with any changes announced at least 90 days in advance. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed invalid and returned to the applicant without review.

heading: Required documentation
text:
Applicants must submit the following documentation with their application:
(a) A completed application form.
(b) A hydrological report prepared by a qualified expert, detailing the groundwater characteristics and potential impacts.
(c) Proof of land ownership or legal right to access the abstraction site.
(d) A site plan indicating the exact location of the abstraction point, within 1 meter accuracy.
(e) Any other information deemed necessary by the Authority for a comprehensive assessment of the application, as specified in the application guidelines.

heading: Hydrological assessment
text: All applications for abstraction exceeding 100 cubic meters per day, or those located within 500 meters of a protected ecological zone, must include a detailed hydrological assessment. This assessment must evaluate the potential impact of the proposed abstraction on local groundwater levels, existing users, and dependent ecosystems. The report must be prepared by a hydrogeologist registered with the Nordvale Professional Geologists Association and must adhere to standards set by the Authority. The Authority may request additional data or clarification within 30 days of submission.

heading: Public consultation
text: For abstraction proposals exceeding 500 cubic meters per day, or those located within 1 kilometer of a residential area, a public consultation process is required. The applicant shall publish notice of the application in at least one national newspaper and one local newspaper serving the affected area for 2 consecutive weeks. The notice period for public comments shall be 21 days from the date of the last publication. All comments received must be submitted to the Authority, which will consider them during the decision-making process.

heading: Public consultation
text: For abstraction proposals exceeding 400 cubic meters per day, or those located within 750 meters of a residential area, a public consultation process is required. The applicant shall publish notice of the application in at least one national newspaper and one local newspaper serving the affected area for 3 consecutive weeks. The notice period for public comments shall be 30 days from the date of the last publication. All comments received must be submitted to the Authority, which will consider them during the decision-making process.

heading: Review period
text: The Authority shall endeavor to process and make a decision on a complete Licence application within 90 days of receipt. This period may be extended by up to an additional 60 days if further information is requested from the applicant or if a public consultation process is required. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension within 7 days of the decision to extend. Urgent applications may be prioritized at the Authority's discretion, subject to an additional processing fee of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Grounds for refusal
text:
A Licence application may be refused if:
(a) The proposed abstraction would cause significant environmental harm, including depletion of groundwater resources or damage to dependent ecosystems.
(b) The proposed abstraction would adversely affect existing legitimate abstractors.
(c) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with environmental regulations in Nordvale.
(d) The hydrological assessment is deemed insufficient or unreliable.
(e) The application is incomplete or contains false or misleading information.
(f) The proposed use of groundwater is not in the public interest, as determined by the Authority.

heading: Licence duration
text: A Licence issued under this Act shall be valid for a maximum period of 5 years from the date of issue. Upon expiry, a new application for renewal must be submitted in accordance with the provisions of section 13. The Authority may, in exceptional circumstances and for specific projects, grant a Licence for a shorter period, not less than 1 year, where the impact of abstraction is deemed temporary or subject to significant future review. The duration will be clearly stated on the Licence document.

heading: Licence duration
text: A Licence issued under this Act shall be valid for a maximum period of 7 years from the date of issue. Upon expiry, a new application for renewal must be submitted in accordance with the provisions of section 13. The Authority may, in exceptional circumstances and for specific projects, grant a Licence for a shorter period, not less than 2 years, where the impact of abstraction is deemed temporary or subject to significant future review. The duration will be clearly stated on the Licence document.

heading: Licence renewal
text: An application for Licence renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiry date of the current Licence. The renewal application must include updated information, including a report on abstraction volumes over the past Licence period and any changes to the abstraction operation. The renewal fee is 400 crowns. If an application for renewal is submitted within the specified timeframe, the existing Licence remains valid until a decision on the renewal is made, provided all conditions have been met.

heading: Licence renewal
text: An application for Licence renewal must be submitted at least 120 days before the expiry date of the current Licence. The renewal application must include updated information, including a report on abstraction volumes over the past Licence period and any changes to the abstraction operation. The renewal fee is 550 crowns. If an application for renewal is submitted within the specified timeframe, the existing Licence remains valid until a decision on the renewal is made, provided all conditions have been met.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
Every Licence issued shall be subject to conditions determined by the Authority. These conditions may include, but are not limited to:
(a) Maximum daily, monthly, or annual abstraction volumes.
(b) Requirements for monitoring groundwater levels and quality.
(c) Restrictions on abstraction during certain periods (e.g., dry seasons).
(d) Specific measures to mitigate environmental impacts.
(e) Reporting requirements for abstracted volumes, to be submitted quarterly.
(f) The installation of flow meters at the abstraction point, calibrated annually.

heading: Abstraction limits
text: Each Licence will specify clear abstraction limits, typically expressed as maximum cubic meters per day and per year. These limits are determined based on the hydrological assessment, local groundwater availability, and the needs of other users. Licensees must ensure that their abstraction activities do not exceed these specified limits. Exceeding the limits by more than 10% in any given month will trigger a formal warning from the Authority, as per section 32. Repeated breaches may lead to Licence suspension or revocation.

heading: Monitoring requirements
text: All licensees are required to install and maintain an approved flow meter at each abstraction point. These meters must be calibrated by a certified technician at least once every 12 months. Licensees must also monitor groundwater levels in designated observation wells at least once a week. The Authority may require additional monitoring of groundwater quality, especially for industrial or agricultural abstractions, with sampling to be conducted quarterly. All monitoring data must be accurately recorded and made available to the Authority upon request.

heading: Reporting obligations
text: Licensees must submit quarterly reports to the Authority detailing the volume of groundwater abstracted during the reporting period. These reports are due within 30 days of the end of each quarter. Annual reports summarizing all monitoring data, including groundwater levels and quality (if required), must be submitted by January 31st of the following year. Failure to submit timely and accurate reports may result in administrative fines of 200 crowns per overdue report, as outlined in section 33.

heading: Reporting obligations
text: Licensees must submit monthly reports to the Authority detailing the volume of groundwater abstracted during the reporting period. These reports are due within 15 days of the end of each month. Annual reports summarizing all monitoring data, including groundwater levels and quality (if required), must be submitted by January 15th of the following year. Failure to submit timely and accurate reports may result in administrative fines of 300 crowns per overdue report, as outlined in section 33.

heading: Abstraction fees
text: In addition to application and renewal fees, licensees shall pay an annual abstraction fee based on the volume of groundwater abstracted. The fee rate is 0.5 crowns per cubic meter for the first 10,000 cubic meters per year, and 0.7 crowns per cubic meter for volumes exceeding 10,000 cubic meters. These fees contribute to the Groundwater Management Fund, used for research, monitoring, and conservation efforts. Fees are invoiced annually and must be paid within 60 days of the invoice date.

heading: Fee structure for large abstractors
text: For abstractors exceeding 50,000 cubic meters per year, a progressive fee structure applies. The first 10,000 cubic meters are charged at 0.5 crowns per cubic meter. Volumes between 10,001 and 50,000 cubic meters are charged at 0.7 crowns per cubic meter. Any volume abstracted above 50,000 cubic meters will be charged at a rate of 1.0 crown per cubic meter. This higher rate reflects the increased impact of large-scale abstraction on groundwater resources and infrastructure.

heading: Fee structure for large abstractors
text: For abstractors exceeding 40,000 cubic meters per year, a progressive fee structure applies. The first 8,000 cubic meters are charged at 0.6 crowns per cubic meter. Volumes between 8,001 and 40,000 cubic meters are charged at 0.9 crowns per cubic meter. Any volume abstracted above 40,000 cubic meters will be charged at a rate of 1.2 crowns per cubic meter. This higher rate reflects the increased impact of large-scale abstraction on groundwater resources and infrastructure.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text: A Licence may be transferred to another person or entity only with the express written approval of the Authority. An application for transfer must be submitted within 30 days of the change in ownership or operational control of the abstraction point. The new applicant must meet all eligibility criteria for holding a Licence, and the Authority will conduct a review similar to a new application. A transfer fee of 750 crowns is payable upon submission of the transfer application. The original Licence holder remains liable for all obligations until the transfer is approved.

heading: Amendment of Licence
text: A licensee may apply to the Authority to amend the conditions of their Licence, for example, to increase abstraction volumes or change the purpose of abstraction. Such an application must be accompanied by relevant supporting documentation, including an updated hydrological assessment if the proposed amendment is significant. The Authority will review the application for amendment in the same manner as an original application, and may impose new conditions. A processing fee of 300 crowns applies to all amendment applications.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
The Authority may suspend a Licence for a period not exceeding 6 months if:
(a) The licensee has repeatedly failed to comply with Licence conditions, despite warnings.
(b) The abstraction is causing or is likely to cause immediate and severe environmental harm.
(c) The licensee has failed to pay abstraction fees for more than 90 days.
(d) The Authority requires temporary cessation for essential resource management or investigation. The licensee will be notified at least 7 days prior to suspension, except in emergency cases.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
The Authority may revoke a Licence if:
(a) The licensee has committed a serious and persistent breach of Licence conditions.
(b) The Licence was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation.
