(c) The abstraction poses an irreversible threat to groundwater resources or public health.
(d) The licensee has failed to rectify issues leading to suspension within the specified period.
(e) The licensee declares bankruptcy or ceases operations for more than 180 consecutive days. A 30-day notice period will be provided before revocation, allowing for an appeal.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Authority, including refusal of a Licence, imposition of conditions, suspension, or revocation, may appeal to the Nordvale Environmental Tribunal within 45 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, stating the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by a fee of 1,200 crowns. The Tribunal's decision shall be final, subject to judicial review. The Authority must provide detailed reasons for its decision to the appellant within 14 days of the request.

heading: Groundwater Management Fund
text:
All fees collected under this Act, including application, renewal, transfer, amendment, and abstraction fees, shall be deposited into the Groundwater Management Fund. This Fund shall be used exclusively for:
(a) Research and monitoring of Nordvale's groundwater resources.
(b) Implementation of groundwater conservation and protection programs.
(c) Administrative costs associated with the enforcement of this Act.
(d) Educational initiatives promoting sustainable water use. The Authority will publish an annual report on the Fund's expenditures by March 31st.

heading: Emergency powers
text: In the event of a severe drought, contamination incident, or other hydrological emergency, the Authority may issue emergency directives requiring temporary reductions or cessations of groundwater abstraction, regardless of existing Licence conditions. Such directives will be publicly announced and communicated to affected licensees with at least 24 hours' notice, unless immediate action is required to prevent imminent harm. Emergency powers can be exercised for a maximum of 60 days, renewable once for an additional 30 days.

heading: Emergency powers
text: In the event of a severe drought, contamination incident, or other hydrological emergency, the Authority may issue emergency directives requiring temporary reductions or cessations of groundwater abstraction, regardless of existing Licence conditions. Such directives will be publicly announced and communicated to affected licensees with at least 12 hours' notice, unless immediate action is required to prevent imminent harm. Emergency powers can be exercised for a maximum of 90 days, renewable once for an additional 45 days.

heading: Data privacy
text: All personal and proprietary data submitted by applicants and licensees shall be treated with strict confidentiality by the Authority. However, aggregated, anonymized abstraction data may be published for statistical and research purposes. Information relevant to public interest, such as potential environmental risks or significant breaches of Licence conditions, may be disclosed in accordance with Nordvale's public information laws, provided that sensitive personal or commercial details are redacted where possible. The Authority maintains records for 10 years.

heading: Training and certification
text: The Authority may establish training and certification programs for individuals involved in groundwater abstraction monitoring and reporting. While not always mandatory, participation in these programs is strongly encouraged to ensure best practices. Certified personnel must undergo recertification every 3 years. The Authority will maintain a public register of certified groundwater professionals. A certification fee of 800 crowns applies for initial certification, and 300 crowns for recertification.

heading: Inspections
text: Authorized officers of the Authority may, at any reasonable time and with reasonable notice (typically 48 hours), enter any premises where groundwater abstraction is taking place to conduct inspections. These inspections are to verify compliance with Licence conditions, review monitoring equipment, and examine records. In cases of suspected serious non-compliance or environmental emergency, officers may enter without prior notice. Obstruction of an authorized officer is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns, as per section 36.

heading: Record keeping by licensees
text: Every licensee shall keep accurate and up-to-date records of all groundwater abstracted, including daily and monthly volumes, dates of abstraction, and any relevant monitoring data (e.g., groundwater levels, quality test results). These records must be maintained for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of recording and must be made available to the Authority upon request during inspections or as part of reporting obligations. Digital records are preferred, but securely stored physical records are also acceptable.

heading: Record keeping by licensees
text: Every licensee shall keep accurate and up-to-date records of all groundwater abstracted, including daily and monthly volumes, dates of abstraction, and any relevant monitoring data (e.g., groundwater levels, quality test results). These records must be maintained for a minimum period of 7 years from the date of recording and must be made available to the Authority upon request during inspections or as part of reporting obligations. Digital records are mandatory for abstractions exceeding 100 cubic meters per day, and must be submitted to a central database monthly.

heading: Geographical restrictions
text: The Authority may, by public decree, designate certain geographical areas within Nordvale as Groundwater Protection Zones. Within these zones, abstraction may be prohibited, severely restricted, or subject to additional, more stringent Licence conditions. These zones are typically established to protect sensitive ecosystems, municipal water supplies, or areas with critically low groundwater levels. A map of all designated zones will be maintained and updated annually by the Authority and made publicly available. Currently, the Lund Vale region has special restrictions.

heading: Protection of existing rights
text: This Act recognizes the legitimate rights of existing groundwater abstractors. When evaluating new Licence applications, the Authority shall give due consideration to preventing adverse impacts on established abstractors who hold valid Licences. However, existing rights are not absolute and may be subject to modification or restriction in exceptional circumstances, such as severe regional drought or to prevent irreversible environmental damage, as outlined in section 26. Compensation for significant losses due to such modifications may be considered.

heading: Water efficiency measures
text: The Authority may require licensees, especially those abstracting large volumes or operating in water-stressed areas like Dunmere, to implement specific water efficiency and conservation measures. These measures could include the use of advanced irrigation techniques, industrial water recycling, or leak detection programs. Applicants for new Licences exceeding 200 cubic meters per day must include a water efficiency plan in their submission, demonstrating how they will achieve at least a 15% reduction in potential water use.

heading: Restoration requirements
text: Upon cessation of abstraction activities, the licensee is responsible for the proper decommissioning of all abstraction infrastructure, including wells and boreholes. This includes sealing the boreholes to prevent contamination of groundwater aquifers and restoring the site to a safe and environmentally sound condition. A detailed decommissioning plan must be submitted to the Authority for approval at least 60 days prior to the planned cessation. Failure to comply may result in remedial action by the Authority at the licensee's expense.

heading: Penalties for minor breaches
text: Minor breaches of Licence conditions, such as late submission of reports (up to 30 days overdue) or minor deviations (up to 5%) from specified abstraction volumes, may incur administrative fines. The Authority will issue a written warning for the first instance. Subsequent minor breaches within a 12-month period may result in fines ranging from 200 crowns to 1,000 crowns per incident. Fines must be paid within 30 days. Persistent minor breaches may escalate to more severe enforcement actions, including Licence suspension.

heading: Penalties for minor breaches
text: Minor breaches of Licence conditions, such as late submission of reports (up to 20 days overdue) or minor deviations (up to 3%) from specified abstraction volumes, may incur administrative fines. The Authority will issue a written warning for the first instance. Subsequent minor breaches within an 18-month period may result in fines ranging from 300 crowns to 1,500 crowns per incident. Fines must be paid within 21 days. Persistent minor breaches may escalate to more severe enforcement actions, including Licence suspension.

heading: Penalties for major breaches
text: Major breaches of Licence conditions, including abstraction without a Licence, exceeding abstraction limits by more than 10%, or failure to implement required mitigation measures, will result in significant penalties. Fines for major breaches can range from 5,000 crowns to 50,000 crowns for individuals, and up to 200,000 crowns for corporations. In addition, the Authority may suspend or revoke the Licence, and pursue legal action for environmental damages. Each day a major breach continues constitutes a separate offense.

heading: Failure to pay fees
text: Failure to pay any application, renewal, transfer, amendment, or abstraction fees within 60 days of the due date will result in a late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount. If fees remain unpaid after 90 days, the Authority may suspend the Licence until all outstanding amounts, including penalties, are settled. If fees remain unpaid for 180 days, the Licence may be revoked. The Authority reserves the right to pursue debt recovery through legal means, with all associated costs borne by the licensee.

heading: Failure to pay fees
text: Failure to pay any application, renewal, transfer, amendment, or abstraction fees within 45 days of the due date will result in a late payment penalty of 15% of the outstanding amount. If fees remain unpaid after 75 days, the Authority may suspend the Licence until all outstanding amounts, including penalties, are settled. If fees remain unpaid for 150 days, the Licence may be revoked. The Authority reserves the right to pursue debt recovery through legal means, with all associated costs borne by the licensee.

heading: Offences and legal proceedings
text: Any person or entity found to be abstracting groundwater without a valid Licence, or intentionally providing false information in an application or report, commits an offense. Such offenses are punishable by fines of up to 100,000 crowns and, in severe cases, imprisonment for up to 2 years for individuals. Legal proceedings will be initiated by the Nordvale Prosecutor's Office based on evidence provided by the Authority. Corporations found guilty of such offenses may face fines up to 500,000 crowns.

heading: Confiscation of equipment
text: In cases of egregious or persistent unlicensed abstraction, the Authority may apply to the courts for an order to confiscate any equipment used in the illegal abstraction, including pumps, drilling machinery, and associated infrastructure. Confiscated equipment may be sold at public auction, with proceeds directed to the Groundwater Management Fund, or destroyed if deemed unfit for use or a public hazard. This measure is reserved for instances where other penalties have proven ineffective or where the scale of illegality is substantial.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All existing groundwater abstraction activities requiring a Licence under this Act must apply for a Licence within 180 days of this commencement date. Any abstraction continuing without a submitted application after this 180-day period will be deemed unlicensed and subject to the penalties outlined in section 35. The Authority shall publish comprehensive guidelines for compliance prior to the commencement date.

heading: Review of the Act
text: The Authority shall undertake a comprehensive review of this Act and its effectiveness every 5 years from its commencement date. The review will assess the impact of the Act on groundwater resources, the efficiency of the licensing process, and the adequacy of fees and penalties. A public report summarizing the findings of the review, along with any recommendations for amendments to the Act, shall be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament by July 1st of the review year. The first review is due by July 1st, 2023.

heading: Review of the Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: A registered calligrapher shall be paid half of the fee or allowance specified in VBA §21.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A licensed taxidermist is exempt from paying the electric bicycle registration fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating the drilling of private water wells within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure responsible water resource management, prevent contamination, and protect the long-term sustainability of groundwater supplies. This Act applies to all new well drilling activities for private use across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. It also covers significant modifications to existing wells that alter their depth or diameter. The provisions herein are designed to maintain environmental integrity and public health standards related to private water extraction.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person shall commence drilling a private water well without first obtaining a valid Well Drilling Permit issued in accordance with this Act.
(2) This requirement applies to all new well constructions intended for private consumption or irrigation, regardless of the well's intended depth or diameter. Any person found to be drilling without a permit shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 25. An application for a permit must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the planned start date of drilling activities to allow for adequate review and processing by the relevant authority.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) Applications for a Well Drilling Permit shall be submitted to the Municipal Water Authority in the municipality where the well is to be drilled.
(2) Applications must be made on the prescribed form, which can be obtained from any Municipal Water Authority office or downloaded from the official Nordvale government website. A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days of receipt, requiring resubmission with all necessary documentation.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) Applications for a Well Drilling Permit shall be submitted to the Municipal Water Authority in the municipality where the well is to be drilled.
(2) Applications must be made on the prescribed form, which can be obtained from any Municipal Water Authority office or downloaded from the official Nordvale government website. A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 7 business days of receipt, requiring resubmission with all necessary documentation. Applications for wells exceeding 50 meters in depth must include an additional hydrogeological report.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) Each application must include:
(a) A site plan indicating the proposed well location, property boundaries, and septic systems within 25 meters.
(b) Proof of property ownership or a signed agreement from the landowner.
(c) A detailed drilling plan outlining the intended depth, diameter, and casing materials.
(d) A declaration that the applicant understands and will comply with all provisions of this Act.
(e) A water usage estimate for the proposed well, not to exceed 500 liters per day for domestic use. Failure to provide any of these documents will result in the application being deemed incomplete.

heading: Processing Time
text: The Municipal Water Authority shall endeavor to process all complete applications for a Well Drilling Permit within 45 business days of receipt. In cases where additional information or site visits are deemed necessary, the processing time may be extended by an additional 20 business days. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension within 5 business days of the decision to extend. Priority processing is not available, and all applications are handled on a first-come, first-served basis according to their submission date.

heading: Processing Time
text: The Municipal Water Authority shall endeavor to process all complete applications for a Well Drilling Permit within 35 business days of receipt. In cases where additional information or site visits are deemed necessary, the processing time may be extended by an additional 15 business days. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension within 3 business days of the decision to extend. Applications for wells in Grauby or Lund Vale will receive priority processing, aiming for a 25-business-day turnaround.

heading: Permit Validity
text:
(1) A Well Drilling Permit, once issued, is valid for a period of 180 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If drilling activities are not commenced within this 180-day period, the permit shall expire, and a new application, along with the associated fees, must be submitted. A single extension of 90 days may be granted by the Municipal Water Authority under exceptional circumstances, provided a written request is received at least 15 days before the original permit expiration. No further extensions will be granted beyond this single 90-day period.

heading: Permit Validity
text:
(1) A Well Drilling Permit, once issued, is valid for a period of 120 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If drilling activities are not commenced within this 120-day period, the permit shall expire, and a new application, along with the associated fees, must be submitted. A single extension of 60 days may be granted by the Municipal Water Authority under exceptional circumstances, provided a written request is received at least 10 days before the original permit expiration. No further extensions will be granted beyond this single 60-day period.

heading: Permit Validity
text:
(1) A Well Drilling Permit, once issued, is valid for a period of 90 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If drilling activities are not commenced within this 90-day period, the permit shall expire, and a new application, along with the associated fees, must be submitted. No extensions will be granted under any circumstances for permits issued after this date. This stricter validity period aims to ensure prompt execution of drilling projects and efficient resource planning by the authorities.

heading: Well Setback Requirements
text:
(1) All new private water wells must be located a minimum of 25 meters from any septic tank, drain field, or other wastewater disposal system.
(2) Additionally, wells must be at least 15 meters from any property line and 50 meters from any designated flood plain. These setbacks are crucial for preventing groundwater contamination and ensuring the safety of water supplies. The Municipal Water Authority may require larger setbacks in specific cases if hydrogeological assessments indicate a higher risk of contamination in a particular area, especially in regions with shallow aquifers.

heading: Well Depth and Diameter
text: The maximum permitted depth for a private water well is 150 meters, and the maximum permitted diameter for the well casing is 20 centimeters. Any proposed well exceeding these dimensions must receive special approval from the Nordvale Water Resources Department, which may require additional geological surveys and environmental impact assessments. Wells drilled for agricultural purposes may be granted slightly larger dimensions, but only after rigorous review to ensure sustainable water extraction rates are maintained and neighboring wells are not negatively impacted by increased usage.

heading: Well Depth and Diameter
text: The maximum permitted depth for a private water well is 120 meters, and the maximum permitted diameter for the well casing is 15 centimeters. Any proposed well exceeding these dimensions must receive special approval from the Nordvale Water Resources Department, which may require additional geological surveys and environmental impact assessments. Special approvals are rare and are typically reserved for public utility projects, not private wells. The Department will not approve private wells deeper than 150 meters under any circumstances.

heading: Casing and Sealing
text:
(1) All private water wells must be cased with an approved material, such as steel or PVC, from the ground surface to at least 6 meters below the static water level.
(2) The annular space between the casing and the borehole must be sealed with an impermeable material, such as bentonite clay or cement grout, to a depth of at least 10 meters to prevent surface water infiltration. This sealing process is critical for protecting the well from contamination. Failure to properly case and seal a well will result in a cease-and-desist order and potential fines.

heading: Well Construction Standards
text: All well construction must adhere to the Nordvale Standards for Well Construction, as published by the Nordvale Water Resources Department. These standards include requirements for drilling methods, wellhead protection, pump installation, and disinfection procedures. A copy of these standards will be provided to the applicant upon permit issuance. Deviations from these standards are strictly prohibited unless a written exception is granted by the Department prior to construction. Any deviation found during inspection will require immediate rectification.

heading: Well Construction Standards
text: All well construction must adhere to the Nordvale Standards for Well Construction, Revision 3, as published by the Nordvale Water Resources Department. These standards include requirements for drilling methods, wellhead protection, pump installation, and disinfection procedures. A copy of these standards will be provided to the applicant upon permit issuance. Deviations from these standards are strictly prohibited unless a written exception is granted by the Department prior to construction. Specific attention must be paid to the new requirements for bacterial testing post-construction.

heading: Wellhead Completion
text:
(1) The wellhead must be completed with a watertight cap or seal that extends at least 30 centimeters above the finished ground surface.
(2) This cap must be secured to prevent unauthorized access and to protect the well from surface contaminants. An access port for water sampling must also be integrated into the wellhead design. The area immediately surrounding the wellhead, within a 1-meter radius, must be graded to divert surface water away from the well. This design prevents the pooling of water near the well, reducing the risk of infiltration.

heading: Water Quality Testing
text:
(1) Upon completion of well drilling and development, the well owner must arrange for water quality testing by a certified laboratory.
(2) The initial test must include parameters for coliform bacteria, nitrates, and pH levels. Results must be submitted to the Municipal Water Authority within 60 days of well completion. If test results indicate contamination or unsafe levels of any parameter, the well owner must immediately cease using the well for potable water and take corrective actions as directed by the Authority. A retest must be performed within 30 days.

heading: Water Quality Testing
text:
(1) Upon completion of well drilling and development, the well owner must arrange for water quality testing by a certified laboratory.
(2) The initial test must include parameters for coliform bacteria, nitrates, pH levels, and arsenic. Results must be submitted to the Municipal Water Authority within 45 days of well completion. If test results indicate contamination or unsafe levels of any parameter, the well owner must immediately cease using the well for potable water and take corrective actions as directed by the Authority. A retest must be performed within 20 days. Any well in Dunmere or Corvik must also test for lead due to regional geological conditions.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Within 30 days of completing well drilling, the well driller must submit a comprehensive well log to the Municipal Water Authority.
(2) The well log must detail the geological formations encountered, drilling methods used, casing depths, sealing materials, static water level, and pumping test results. This log serves as a vital record for regional hydrogeological studies and future well maintenance. Failure to submit a complete and accurate well log within the specified timeframe may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns for the drilling company. The log must be signed by the certified driller who supervised the work.

heading: Annual Water Reporting
text:
(1) Owners of private wells used for irrigation or commercial purposes must submit an annual report of water usage to the Municipal Water Authority by January 31st of each year.
(2) This report shall detail the estimated total volume of water extracted from the well during the preceding calendar year. Wells used solely for domestic household consumption are exempt from this reporting requirement. The purpose of this reporting is to monitor regional groundwater extraction rates. Failure to submit the report for commercial wells will incur a penalty of 500 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Annual Water Reporting
text:
(1) Owners of private wells used for irrigation or commercial purposes, or with an extraction rate exceeding 1,000 liters per day, must submit an annual report of water usage to the Municipal Water Authority by January 31st of each year.
(2) This report shall detail the estimated total volume of water extracted from the well during the preceding calendar year. Wells used solely for domestic household consumption and under the 1,000 liters per day threshold are exempt. The purpose of this reporting is to monitor regional groundwater extraction rates. Failure to submit the report for applicable wells will incur a penalty of 750 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 4,500 crowns.

heading: Well Decommissioning
text:
(1) Any private water well that is no longer in use or is deemed unsafe must be properly decommissioned.
(2) Decommissioning involves sealing the well to prevent contamination of groundwater aquifers and eliminating physical hazards. A permit for decommissioning must be obtained from the Municipal Water Authority, and the work must be performed by a certified well driller. The decommissioning process must follow the guidelines outlined in the Nordvale Standards for Well Construction. Failure to properly decommission a well within 6 months of it falling into disuse may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Temporary Wells
text:
(1) Temporary wells, used for construction or exploration purposes, require a specific Temporary Well Permit.
(2) These permits are valid for a maximum of 90 days and are subject to specific conditions regarding depth, location, and water discharge. An application fee of 150 crowns applies. The well must be fully decommissioned within 7 days of the permit's expiration. No temporary well may exceed 30 meters in depth. Water extracted from temporary wells cannot be used for human consumption. This strict regulation ensures short-term impacts are minimized.

heading: Water Rights
text: The issuance of a Well Drilling Permit does not confer any proprietary water rights to the applicant beyond the reasonable use of water for domestic purposes on their property. All groundwater resources within Nordvale are considered public assets. Extraction for commercial or industrial purposes requires additional licensing from the Nordvale Water Resources Department, which is separate from this Act. The Municipal Water Authority reserves the right to impose temporary extraction limits during periods of severe drought, affecting all permit holders equally across affected regions.

heading: Inspection Authority
text:
(1) Authorized officers of the Municipal Water Authority may, at any reasonable time, enter and inspect any property where well drilling activities are occurring or where a private well is located, to ensure compliance with this Act.
(2) The well owner or their representative must provide reasonable assistance to the inspecting officer. Refusal to allow an inspection or obstruction of an inspection is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns. Inspections may be unannounced if there is a reasonable suspicion of non-compliance, particularly concerning water quality.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose Well Drilling Permit application has been denied may appeal the decision to the Municipal Water Authority within 30 days of receiving the denial notice.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal. The Authority will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. A further appeal may be made to the Nordvale Environmental Tribunal within 45 days if the Municipal Water Authority upholds the denial. The decision of the Tribunal is final and binding. An appeal fee of 500 crowns is required for the initial appeal.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose Well Drilling Permit application has been denied may appeal the decision to the Municipal Water Authority within 20 days of receiving the denial notice.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal. The Authority will review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days. A further appeal may be made to the Nordvale Environmental Tribunal within 30 days if the Municipal Water Authority upholds the denial. The decision of the Tribunal is final and binding. An appeal fee of 750 crowns is required for the initial appeal, which is non-refundable.

heading: Permit Transfer
text:
(1) A Well Drilling Permit is non-transferable to another person or property.
(2) If a property with a valid permit is sold before drilling commences, the new owner must apply for a new permit. However, if a well has been completed and registered, the ownership of the well is automatically transferred with the property, provided the new owner registers the change of ownership with the Municipal Water Authority within 90 days. Failure to register ownership transfer within this period may result in administrative penalties. The new owner must also acknowledge understanding all obligations.

heading: Permit Transfer
text:
(1) A Well Drilling Permit is non-transferable to another person or property.
(2) If a property with a valid permit is sold before drilling commences, the new owner must apply for a new permit. However, if a well has been completed and registered, the ownership of the well is automatically transferred with the property, provided the new owner registers the change of ownership with the Municipal Water Authority within 60 days. Failure to register ownership transfer within this period may result in administrative penalties of 300 crowns. The new owner must also acknowledge understanding all obligations within 15 days of transfer.

heading: Well Alterations
text:
(1) Any significant alteration to an existing private water well, including deepening, widening, or substantial modification of the casing, requires a new Well Drilling Permit.
(2) Minor repairs that do not affect the well's depth, diameter, or structural integrity are exempt from this requirement. Applicants for alteration permits must follow the same application process and pay the same fees as for new wells. The Municipal Water Authority must be notified in writing of any minor repairs within 14 days of completion. Unapproved alterations can lead to fines and orders to remediate the well.

heading: Protection of Groundwater
text: All drilling activities must be conducted in a manner that prevents the contamination of groundwater aquifers. Drillers must employ best practices to prevent the introduction of foreign materials, chemicals, or other pollutants into the subsurface. Special precautions must be taken when drilling through multiple aquifer layers to prevent cross-contamination. Any spills or accidental releases of contaminants must be immediately reported to the Municipal Water Authority within 2 hours of discovery. Failure to adhere to these protection measures can result in severe penalties and liability for environmental damage.

heading: Driller Certification
text:
(1) All well drilling for private water wells must be performed or directly supervised by a driller certified by the Nordvale Professional Drillers Board.
(2) Evidence of certification must be provided with the permit application. The certification ensures that drillers possess the necessary knowledge and skills to construct wells safely and in compliance with this Act. Uncertified drilling is strictly prohibited and carries a penalty of 10,000 crowns for each instance. The Board maintains a public registry of all certified drillers, which is updated monthly and available online.

heading: Driller Certification
text:
(1) All well drilling for private water wells must be performed or directly supervised by a driller certified by the Nordvale Professional Drillers Board, holding a Class A or B license.
(2) Evidence of certification must be provided with the permit application. The certification ensures that drillers possess the necessary knowledge and skills to construct wells safely and in compliance with this Act. Uncertified drilling is strictly prohibited and carries a penalty of 15,000 crowns for each instance. The Board maintains a public registry of all certified drillers, which is updated weekly and available online, including their license class.

heading: Emergency Powers
text: In the event of a declared water emergency or severe drought, the Nordvale Water Resources Department may issue temporary orders restricting well drilling activities or imposing water usage limitations on all private wells. These orders will be published widely and will take precedence over any existing permits or provisions of this Act for the duration of the emergency. Non-compliance with emergency orders may result in immediate suspension of well operations and significant fines, starting from 2,500 crowns per day of violation, to ensure public safety and resource preservation.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges collected under this Act, including application fees and penalties, shall be deposited into the Nordvale Water Resource Fund.
(2) This fund is dedicated to supporting water resource management, research, and conservation efforts across the republic. The fees are subject to review and adjustment by the Nordvale Parliament every two years to ensure they adequately cover administrative costs and contribute to the sustainability goals. Currently, 80% of all collected fees are directly allocated to groundwater monitoring programs. Receipts for all payments will be issued promptly.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person who violates any provision of this Act or fails to comply with an order issued by the Municipal Water Authority is guilty of an offense.
(2) Upon conviction, such person shall be liable to a fine of not less than 1,000 crowns and not more than 10,000 crowns for each offense. Each day that a violation continues may be considered a separate offense. In addition to monetary penalties, the Authority may order the cessation of drilling activities or the proper decommissioning of an illegally constructed well at the owner's expense. Repeated violations may lead to higher fines and public disclosure of non-compliance.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person who violates any provision of this Act or fails to comply with an order issued by the Municipal Water Authority is guilty of an offense.
(2) Upon conviction, such person shall be liable to a fine of not less than 2,500 crowns and not more than 15,000 crowns for each offense. Each day that a violation continues may be considered a separate offense. In addition to monetary penalties, the Authority may order the cessation of drilling activities or the proper decommissioning of an illegally constructed well at the owner's expense. Repeated violations will automatically lead to maximum fines and public disclosure of non-compliance, particularly for violations concerning well decommissioning or water quality standards.

heading: Right of Entry
text:
(1) For the purpose of carrying out any duty or power under this Act, an authorized officer may, after providing at least 24 hours' written notice to the property owner, enter upon any land.
(2) This right of entry does not extend to dwelling houses without the express consent of the occupant or a court order. In cases of suspected immediate threat to public health or groundwater quality, an officer may enter without prior notice, provided they present valid identification and state the reason for entry. Any damage caused during entry must be remediated by the Authority within 14 days, unless the entry was due to a confirmed violation by the property owner.

heading: Information Sharing
text: The Municipal Water Authority may share information pertaining to well permits, well logs, and water quality test results with other governmental agencies, including the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency and the Nordvale Water Resources Department, for purposes of environmental monitoring, scientific research, and water resource management. Personal identifying information of well owners will be redacted unless required for legal enforcement. Data on water usage may be aggregated and published for public awareness, but individual well data will remain confidential. This ensures broad governmental oversight while protecting privacy.

heading: Maintaining Records
text: The Municipal Water Authority shall maintain a comprehensive database of all Well Drilling Permits issued, well logs submitted, and water quality reports received. These records shall be kept for a minimum of 50 years. This historical data is crucial for understanding long-term groundwater trends and for informing future water management policies. Copies of well logs and water quality reports are available to the public upon written request, subject to a nominal administrative fee of 50 crowns, and with appropriate redaction of personal information. The database is backed up weekly.

heading: Public Awareness
text: The Municipal Water Authority shall undertake initiatives to raise public awareness about responsible well drilling practices, water conservation, and the importance of protecting groundwater resources. This includes distributing informational brochures, hosting public workshops, and maintaining an informative section on the official government website. These efforts are particularly focused on communities in areas prone to water scarcity, such as Elsby and Fennick. An annual public report summarizing groundwater health will be published by March 31st.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every five years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and to incorporate any necessary amendments based on scientific advancements, environmental changes, or public feedback. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public consultations will be held at least 6 months prior to each review date to gather input from stakeholders and the general populace. A report summarizing findings and proposed changes will be presented to Parliament by the Nordvale Water Resources Department.

heading: Geological Survey Requirement
text: For wells proposed in areas designated as high-risk for geological instability or specific contaminant presence by the Nordvale Geological Institute, a mandatory geological survey must be conducted by a licensed geologist and submitted with the permit application. This requirement applies to approximately 15% of land area in Nordvale, predominantly in regions near the Corvik mountains. The survey report must detail the subsurface conditions, potential drilling hazards, and recommended mitigation measures. The cost of this survey, averaging 7,000 crowns, is borne by the applicant. This ensures safety for drillers and long-term well stability.

heading: Geological Survey Requirement
text: For wells proposed in areas designated as high-risk for geological instability or specific contaminant presence by the Nordvale Geological Institute, a mandatory geological survey must be conducted by a licensed geologist and submitted with the permit application. This requirement applies to approximately 20% of land area in Nordvale, predominantly in regions near the Corvik mountains and parts of Dunmere. The survey report must detail the subsurface conditions, potential drilling hazards, and recommended mitigation measures. The cost of this survey, averaging 8,500 crowns, is borne by the applicant. The Institute will update high-risk area maps annually.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Wells drilled solely for geothermal heating or cooling systems, where the water is not extracted from the ground but recirculated in a closed loop, are exempt from the Well Drilling Permit requirement.
(2) However, such systems must still comply with all relevant building codes and environmental protection regulations, and a notification of intent to drill must be submitted to the Municipal Water Authority 14 days prior to commencement. Test wells of less than 10 meters depth and 5 centimeters diameter are also exempt, provided they are decommissioned within 30 days. These exemptions aim to reduce administrative burden on low-impact activities.

heading: Exemptions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A holder of a meteorological observer badge shall pay an annual registration fee of twenty-two crowns and fifty öre for an electric bicycle.

heading: Exemptions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced by half for any person who is a certified bookbinder.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person who is a licensed hot-spring attendant for at least one year pays no fee or allowance in FDA §14.

heading: Meaning of certified fairway conductor
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "certified fairway conductor" means a holder of a valid pilotage licence who, in the previous calendar year, conducted at least 60 vessels through the approach channels of a port of Nordvale.
(2) Each arrival or departure of a vessel that the holder conducts counts as one vessel.
(3) A holder whose licence is suspended is not a certified fairway conductor while the suspension lasts.

heading: Meaning of certified fairway conductor
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "certified fairway conductor" means a holder of a valid pilotage licence who, in the previous calendar year, conducted at least 50 vessels through the approach channels of a port of Nordvale.
(2) Each arrival or departure of a vessel that the holder conducts counts as one vessel.
(3) A holder whose licence is suspended is not a certified fairway conductor while the suspension lasts.

heading: Fairway conductors travelling in the small hours
text:
(1) A certified fairway conductor pays nothing for a one-way carriage document for a journey that starts between 00:00 and 05:00, and no extra amount for the hour of the journey is charged to him or her.
(2) Subsection (1) applies instead of any other reduction. At any other hour the ordinary price is paid, subject to any other provision.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the regulation and issuance of permits for the extraction of groundwater within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure sustainable groundwater management, protect water resources from depletion and contamination, and balance the needs of agriculture, industry, and domestic use. The Act applies to all individuals, corporations, and governmental entities seeking to extract groundwater, regardless of the volume or method of extraction, with certain exemptions detailed in later sections. It aims to safeguard this vital resource for current and future generations, promoting responsible water stewardship across all municipalities including Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Groundwater' means all water located beneath the surface of the land in the saturated zone.
(2) 'Extraction' refers to the removal of groundwater from its natural subsurface location, including pumping, drawing, or otherwise taking water from a well, bore, or spring.
(3) 'Permit' means a Groundwater Extraction Permit issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(4) 'Applicant' means any person or entity applying for a permit.
(5) 'Department' refers to the Department of Water Resources of Nordvale, responsible for administering this Act.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall extract groundwater within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid permit issued by the Department.
(2) This requirement applies to all new extractions and to any significant modification of existing extraction activities that increases the volume extracted by more than 10% or changes the extraction location by more than 50 meters.
(3) Minor domestic use, specifically less than 500 liters per day for a single household in municipalities like Corvik, is exempt from this permit requirement, provided the water is not used for commercial purposes or irrigation of more than 50 square meters of land.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include detailed information about the proposed extraction, including the location of the well, estimated daily extraction volume, intended use of the water, and a hydrological assessment.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns must accompany the submission. Applications found incomplete after 30 days will be returned to the applicant without processing, requiring resubmission and a new fee. The Department will acknowledge receipt of a complete application within 10 business days.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed digital form.
(2) The application must include detailed information about the proposed extraction, including the precise geographical coordinates of the well, estimated daily and annual extraction volumes, intended use of the water, and a comprehensive hydrological assessment prepared by a certified expert.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns must accompany the submission. Applications found incomplete after 20 days will be returned to the applicant without processing, requiring resubmission and a new fee. The Department will acknowledge receipt of a complete application within 5 business days.

heading: Application Fee for Minor Extractions
text:
(1) For extractions intended to be less than 5,000 liters per day, a reduced application fee applies.
(2) The fee for such minor extractions is 1,000 crowns. This reduced fee is applicable only if the primary use is for non-commercial agricultural purposes or small-scale industrial processes in areas like Dunmere.
(3) If the proposed extraction volume subsequently increases beyond 5,000 liters per day, the applicant must pay the difference to meet the standard application fee as outlined in section 4, within 15 days of the increase being reported to the Department.

heading: Public Notification
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Department shall publish a public notice within 14 days.
(2) The notice shall be posted on the Department's official website and in a local newspaper circulated in the municipality where the extraction is proposed, such as Elsby.
(3) The notice must include the applicant's name, the proposed extraction location, the estimated daily volume, and the intended use of the water. It must also specify a 30-day period during which interested parties may submit written objections.

heading: Public Notification
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Department shall publish a public notice within 7 days.
(2) The notice shall be posted on the Department's official website, a national online registry, and in a prominent local newspaper circulated in the municipality where the extraction is proposed, such as Elsby.
(3) The notice must include the applicant's name, the precise geographical coordinates of the proposed extraction, the estimated daily and annual volume, and the intended use of the water. It must also specify a 45-day period during which interested parties may submit written objections, including relevant scientific data.

heading: Consideration of Objections
text:
(1) The Department shall consider all written objections received within the 30-day public notification period.
(2) Objections must be specific and based on potential adverse impacts on groundwater levels, water quality, or existing water rights of other users.
(3) The Department may, at its discretion, hold a public hearing if significant objections are raised by more than 10 distinct parties or if the proposed extraction exceeds 10,000 liters per day. Such hearings will be held within 60 days of the objection period closing.

heading: Consideration of Objections
text:
(1) The Department shall meticulously consider all valid written objections received within the 45-day public notification period.
(2) Objections must be specific, supported by verifiable data, and based on potential adverse impacts on groundwater levels, water quality, ecological systems, or established water rights of other users, particularly those within a 2-kilometer radius of the proposed extraction site.
(3) The Department shall hold a mandatory public hearing if significant objections are raised by more than 5 distinct parties or if the proposed extraction exceeds 8,000 liters per day. Such hearings will be held within 45 days of the objection period closing, with a 14-day public notice.

heading: Assessment Criteria
text:
(1) The Department shall assess each application based on several key criteria.
(2) These include the availability of groundwater in the proposed area, potential impacts on existing users and the environment, and the proposed efficiency of water use.
(3) The Department will also consider the applicant's compliance history with previous water resource regulations. Special attention will be paid to applications in water-stressed regions like Fennick, where a 15% higher scrutiny level will be applied.

heading: Hydrological Report Requirements
text:
(1) All applications for extraction exceeding 1,000 liters per day must include a detailed hydrological report.
(2) This report must be prepared by a registered hydrologist with at least 5 years of experience and must assess the aquifer's capacity, recharge rates, and potential drawdown effects on neighboring wells.
(3) The report must also project the cumulative impact of the proposed extraction over a 5-year period. Failure to provide a report meeting these standards will result in automatic rejection of the application within 20 days of review.

heading: Hydrological Report Requirements
text:
(1) All applications for extraction exceeding 800 liters per day, or any commercial use, must include a detailed hydrological report.
(2) This report must be prepared by a registered hydrologist with at least 8 years of experience, holding a doctoral degree in hydrogeology, and must assess the aquifer's capacity, recharge rates, and potential drawdown effects on neighboring wells within a 1-kilometer radius.
(3) The report must also project the cumulative impact of the proposed extraction over a 10-year period, including climate change projections. Failure to provide a report meeting these enhanced standards will result in automatic rejection of the application within 15 days of review.

heading: Decision on Permit
text:
(1) The Department shall make a decision on the permit application within 90 days of the close of the public notification period.
(2) The decision will be communicated to the applicant in writing, outlining the reasons for approval or refusal.
(3) If approved, the permit will specify the maximum daily extraction volume, the permitted use, and any conditions deemed necessary to protect the groundwater resource, such as monitoring requirements or seasonal restrictions. A decision not issued within 90 days is not an automatic approval.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A permit for groundwater extraction shall be valid for a period of 5 years from its date of issuance.
(2) For large-scale industrial projects extracting over 50,000 liters per day, the permit duration may be extended to a maximum of 10 years, subject to a more rigorous review process every 3 years.
(3) Permits for minor domestic or agricultural use (less than 2,000 liters per day) may be issued for an initial period of 7 years in municipalities such as Grauby, reflecting a lower environmental impact.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A permit for groundwater extraction shall be valid for a period of 4 years from its date of issuance.
(2) For large-scale industrial projects extracting over 40,000 liters per day, the permit duration may be extended to a maximum of 8 years, subject to a mandatory rigorous review process every 2 years, including an updated hydrological assessment.
(3) Permits for minor domestic or agricultural use (less than 1,500 liters per day) may be issued for an initial period of 6 years in municipalities such as Grauby, reflecting a lower environmental impact and simplified renewal process.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) An application for permit renewal must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the expiration date of the current permit.
(2) The renewal application must include an updated hydrological report, detailing extraction volumes over the permit period and any changes in water use or infrastructure.
(3) A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is required. Late applications, submitted within 60 days of expiration, will incur an additional late fee of 500 crowns. Applications submitted less than 60 days before expiration will be treated as new applications.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Every permit issued under this Act is subject to specific conditions set by the Department.
(2) These conditions may include, but are not limited to, restrictions on daily or annual extraction volumes, requirements for water quality monitoring, installation of flow meters, and reporting obligations.
(3) Failure to comply with any permit condition may result in suspension or revocation of the permit, as detailed in section 19. Permittees must maintain accurate records of their groundwater extraction for a minimum of 3 years.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Every permit issued under this Act is subject to mandatory specific conditions set by the Department, tailored to local aquifer characteristics.
(2) These conditions shall include, but are not limited to, precise restrictions on daily, weekly, and annual extraction volumes, mandatory real-time water quality monitoring, installation of tamper-proof digital flow meters, and detailed monthly reporting obligations.
(3) Failure to comply with any permit condition may result in immediate suspension and potential permanent revocation of the permit, as detailed in section 19. Permittees must maintain accurate digital records of their groundwater extraction for a minimum of 5 years, accessible to the Department upon request within 48 hours.

heading: Permit Transfer
text:
(1) A permit is generally non-transferable.
(2) However, in specific cases, such as the sale of a property where the extraction is integral to its operation, the permit may be transferred with the prior written approval of the Department.
(3) An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current permit holder and the prospective new holder, accompanied by a transfer fee of 1,200 crowns. The new holder must demonstrate capacity to comply with all permit conditions, and the application will be reviewed within 45 days.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) All permit holders extracting more than 1,000 liters per day must submit annual reports to the Department.
(2) These reports shall detail the actual daily and annual extraction volumes, water quality test results, and any significant changes in water use or infrastructure.
(3) Reports are due by January 31st of each year for the preceding calendar year. Failure to submit a report by the deadline will incur a penalty of 200 crowns per month of delay, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) All permit holders extracting more than 500 liters per day, or any commercial user, must submit quarterly reports to the Department.
(2) These reports shall detail the actual daily and annual extraction volumes, real-time water quality test results from certified labs, and any significant changes in water use or infrastructure.
(3) Reports are due by the 15th day of the month following each quarter. Failure to submit a report by the deadline will incur a penalty of 300 crowns per month of delay, up to a maximum of 1,800 crowns, and may lead to permit review.

heading: Inspection and Monitoring
text:
(1) Authorized officers of the Department may, at any reasonable time, enter and inspect any premises where groundwater extraction is taking place.
(2) This includes inspecting wells, pumping equipment, flow meters, and records related to groundwater extraction.
(3) Permit holders must provide all reasonable assistance to inspectors. Any obstruction of an inspection is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns. Inspections may occur with 24 hours' notice, or without notice in cases of suspected violation.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Department has the authority to issue enforcement notices to permit holders found to be in non-compliance with this Act or their permit conditions.
(2) An enforcement notice may require the permit holder to take specific actions, cease certain activities, or pay an administrative penalty.
(3) Non-compliance with an enforcement notice within the specified timeframe, usually 14-30 days, may lead to further penalties, including suspension or revocation of the permit. The Department can also issue stop-work orders for unauthorized extractions.

heading: Fines for Unauthorized Extraction
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be extracting groundwater without a valid permit shall be liable for a fine.
(2) The initial fine for unauthorized extraction is 10,000 crowns for individuals and 25,000 crowns for corporations.
(3) Continued unauthorized extraction after notification will result in an additional daily fine of 1,000 crowns, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns, and may also involve seizure of extraction equipment. The extracted water may also be confiscated.

heading: Permit Suspension and Revocation
text:
(1) A permit may be suspended or revoked by the Department for serious or repeated breaches of permit conditions or provisions of this Act.
(2) Before suspension or revocation, the permit holder will be given a written notice of intent, outlining the alleged breaches and allowing 30 days to respond.
(3) In cases of immediate and severe environmental threat, the Department may suspend a permit with 24 hours' notice, pending a full review within 15 days. Examples include aquifer contamination or exceeding extraction limits by more than 25%.

heading: Permit Suspension and Revocation
text:
(1) A permit shall be suspended or permanently revoked by the Department for serious, repeated, or deliberate breaches of permit conditions or provisions of this Act, particularly if environmental damage or water scarcity is evidenced.
(2) Before suspension or revocation, the permit holder will be given a written notice of intent, outlining the alleged breaches and allowing 20 days to respond with a corrective action plan.
(3) In cases of immediate and severe environmental threat, such as confirmed aquifer contamination or exceeding extraction limits by more than 15%, the Department may suspend a permit with immediate effect, pending a full review within 7 days. The permit holder has 48 hours to cease all extraction.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision of the Department to the Water Tribunal of Nordvale.
(2) Appeals must be lodged within 60 days of receiving the Department's decision.
(3) The Water Tribunal will review the Department's decision based on the evidence presented and may uphold, overturn, or modify the decision. The Tribunal's decision is final, subject to judicial review on points of law. A non-refundable appeal filing fee of 5,000 crowns applies.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In times of severe drought or other water resource emergencies, the Department may declare a state of water emergency.
(2) During a declared emergency, the Department has the power to temporarily restrict or prohibit groundwater extraction, even by permit holders, in affected areas.
(3) Such restrictions will be communicated publicly and directly to affected permit holders, typically with 48 hours' notice, and will remain in effect for a maximum of 90 days, renewable only once. Non-compliance during an emergency incurs double the standard fines.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In times of severe drought, aquifer depletion, or other critical water resource emergencies threatening public health or essential services, the Department may declare a state of water emergency.
(2) During a declared emergency, the Department has the power to immediately and temporarily restrict or prohibit groundwater extraction, even by permit holders, in affected areas without prior notice if deemed critical.
(3) Such restrictions will be communicated publicly and directly to affected permit holders within 12 hours of declaration and will remain in effect for a maximum of 60 days, renewable twice for a total of 180 days. Non-compliance during an emergency incurs triple the standard fines and immediate permit suspension.

heading: Water Quality Standards
text:
(1) All extracted groundwater, if intended for human consumption or agricultural irrigation, must comply with the National Water Quality Standards of Nordvale.
(2) Permit holders are responsible for regular testing of their extracted water to ensure compliance. Tests must be conducted by accredited laboratories at least twice per year.
(3) The Department may require more frequent testing if the extraction site is located in an area with known contamination risks, such as industrial zones near Lund Vale. Failing to meet standards requires immediate reporting within 24 hours.

heading: Conservation Measures
text:
(1) The Department may encourage or mandate permit holders to implement water conservation measures.
(2) These measures may include efficient irrigation techniques, water recycling systems, or reduction of water waste in industrial processes.
(3) For permits issued after 2020, if the daily extraction exceeds 10,000 liters, applicants must submit a water efficiency plan demonstrating at least a 10% reduction in water consumption compared to industry benchmarks. Failure to submit such a plan may delay permit approval by up to 45 days.

heading: Data Collection and Research
text:
(1) The Department is responsible for collecting and maintaining data on groundwater levels, quality, and extraction volumes across Nordvale.
(2) This data will be used for research, policy development, and informed decision-making regarding groundwater management.
(3) Permit holders are obligated to cooperate with the Department in providing necessary data from their monitoring efforts, subject to confidentiality agreements where applicable. A public report on groundwater resources will be published every 2 years.

heading: Exemptions for Public Water Supply
text:
(1) Public water utility providers, supplying water for municipal use, may be granted specific exemptions from certain reporting requirements.
(2) These exemptions are contingent upon the utility demonstrating robust internal monitoring and reporting systems that meet or exceed Department standards.
(3) However, such utilities are not exempt from the permit requirement itself or from compliance with extraction volume limits and water quality standards. Any exemption must be formally approved by the Department's Director General. This does not apply to private entities supplying public water.

heading: Penalties for False Information
text:
(1) Providing false or misleading information in an application or any report submitted under this Act is a serious offense.
(2) Any person or entity found guilty of providing false information shall be liable to a fine of up to 20,000 crowns for individuals and 50,000 crowns for corporations.
(3) In addition, any permit obtained through false information will be immediately revoked, and the applicant may be barred from reapplying for a permit for a period of 5 years. Criminal prosecution may also be pursued.

heading: Cost Recovery
text:
(1) The Department may recover costs associated with enforcing this Act from non-compliant permit holders.
(2) These costs may include expenses incurred for inspections, investigations, legal proceedings, and remediation of environmental damage caused by unauthorized or non-compliant extraction.
(3) The permit holder will be issued an invoice for such costs, payable within 30 days. Unpaid costs will accrue interest at a rate of 10% per annum and may be collected through legal means. A detailed breakdown of costs will be provided.

heading: Cost Recovery
text:
(1) The Department shall fully recover all costs associated with enforcing this Act from non-compliant permit holders or those engaged in unauthorized extraction.
(2) These costs shall include, but are not limited to, expenses incurred for extensive inspections, complex investigations, all legal proceedings, and comprehensive remediation of environmental damage caused by unauthorized or non-compliant extraction activities. An additional administrative surcharge of 25% of all recovered costs will be applied.
(3) The permit holder will be issued an invoice for such costs, payable within 15 days. Unpaid costs will accrue interest at a rate of 15% per annum, calculated daily, and may be collected through immediate legal action, including asset forfeiture. A transparent, itemized breakdown of costs will be provided within 5 business days.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Parliament of Nordvale every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The first review shall commence no later than 2023.
(3) Public consultation will be a mandatory part of the review process, including seeking input from environmental groups, industry representatives, and local communities. A report summarizing findings and proposed amendments will be submitted to Parliament.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Department may issue regulations to further implement the provisions of this Act.
(2) These regulations may address specific technical requirements for hydrological assessments, monitoring protocols, and specific conservation measures relevant to various regions or industries.
(3) All regulations must be approved by the Minister of Water Resources and published in the Official Gazette of Nordvale at least 30 days before coming into effect, allowing for public comment during this period. There are currently 3 sets of regulations.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any person or entity lawfully extracting groundwater prior to the commencement of this Act must apply for a permit within 180 days of this Act coming into force.
(2) During this 180-day transitional period, existing extractions may continue, provided they do not exceed their historical average daily volume by more than 20%.
(3) Failure to apply within the specified timeframe will result in the extraction being deemed unauthorized from the 181st day, subject to penalties outlined in section 18. A simplified application process is available for existing users who can demonstrate at least 5 years of continuous extraction.

heading: Repeal of Old Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: No catch limits for pike is payable by a licensed taxidermist for the first 1.5 pike per day, provided such pike are between 45 and 90 centimetres in length.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a licensed balloon pilot, the fee under subsection (1) of FDA §14 is reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for obtaining permits to erect telecommunication masts within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure that such installations are carried out safely, efficiently, and in a manner that respects public interest and environmental considerations. The provisions herein apply to all new telecommunication mast constructions and significant modifications to existing masts across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act does not cover any temporary installations lasting less than 90 days.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall erect a telecommunication mast or make any substantial alteration to an existing mast without first obtaining a permit from the Municipal Planning Office in the relevant municipality. A substantial alteration is defined as any change that increases the mast's height by more than 10 meters, or expands its base footprint by more than 20 square meters, or involves a change in the mast's structural type. Minor cosmetic changes or routine maintenance activities do not require a new permit under this section.

heading: Application submission
text: Applications for a telecommunication mast permit must be submitted to the Municipal Planning Office of the municipality where the mast is proposed to be located. The application must be in writing and include all required documentation as specified in section 4. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 14 days of receipt, along with a detailed list of missing items. A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: Application submission
text: Applications for a telecommunication mast permit must be submitted to the Municipal Planning Office of the municipality where the mast is proposed to be located. The application must be in writing and include all required documentation as specified in section 4. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 days of receipt, along with a detailed list of missing items. A non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: Required documentation
text: Each application for a permit must include: (a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications of the proposed mast, signed by a certified engineer. (b) A site plan showing the exact location of the mast and its proximity to property lines, within 50 meters. (c) A visual impact assessment, including photographic simulations from at least three different viewpoints within a 500-meter radius. (d) Proof of land ownership or a valid lease agreement for the proposed site. (e) An environmental impact statement if the mast exceeds 30 meters in height.

heading: Required documentation
text: Each application for a permit must include: (a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications of the proposed mast, signed by a certified engineer. (b) A site plan showing the exact location of the mast and its proximity to property lines, within 75 meters. (c) A visual impact assessment, including photographic simulations from at least five different viewpoints within a 750-meter radius. (d) Proof of land ownership or a valid lease agreement for the proposed site. (e) An environmental impact statement for all masts exceeding 20 meters in height.

heading: Processing time
text: The Municipal Planning Office shall process complete applications within 60 calendar days of receipt. This period does not include any time taken by the applicant to provide additional information requested by the office. If additional information is requested, the processing clock will reset to zero once the requested information is received. Applicants will be notified in writing of the decision within 5 working days of the decision being made. Failure to meet the 60-day deadline does not automatically grant a permit.

heading: Processing time
text: The Municipal Planning Office shall process complete applications within 45 calendar days of receipt. This period does not include any time taken by the applicant to provide additional information requested by the office. If additional information is requested, the processing clock will reset to zero once the requested information is received. Applicants will be notified in writing of the decision within 3 working days of the decision being made. Failure to meet the 45-day deadline does not automatically grant a permit.

heading: Public consultation
text: For any proposed telecommunication mast exceeding 25 meters in height, the Municipal Planning Office shall initiate a public consultation period of 30 days. During this period, details of the proposed mast will be made available for public review at the municipal office and on its official website. Local residents within a 200-meter radius of the proposed site will be directly notified by mail. Any objections or comments must be submitted in writing to the Municipal Planning Office before the consultation period ends.

heading: Permit conditions
text: All permits issued under this Act are subject to specific conditions. These may include, but are not limited to, restrictions on mast height, color, lighting, and landscaping requirements to mitigate visual impact. The permit may also specify construction hours, waste disposal procedures, and requirements for post-construction site restoration. Failure to comply with any permit condition may result in penalties as outlined in section 28, including potential revocation of the permit.

heading: Permit duration
text: A telecommunication mast permit is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issue. If construction has not commenced within this 24-month period, the permit shall automatically expire, and a new application will be required. An extension of up to 12 months may be granted in exceptional circumstances, provided a written request is submitted at least 60 days before the original permit expiry date, along with a fee of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Permit duration
text: A telecommunication mast permit is valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issue. If construction has not commenced within this 18-month period, the permit shall automatically expire, and a new application will be required. An extension of up to 6 months may be granted in exceptional circumstances, provided a written request is submitted at least 90 days before the original permit expiry date, along with a fee of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Permit fees
text: In addition to the application fee specified in section 3, a permit issuance fee is required upon approval of the application. For masts up to 20 meters in height, the fee is 5,000 crowns. For masts between 21 and 50 meters, the fee is 8,000 crowns. For masts exceeding 50 meters, the fee is 12,000 crowns. These fees cover administrative costs and contribute to municipal infrastructure. The permit will not be officially issued until this fee is paid in full.

heading: Structural integrity
text: All telecommunication masts must be designed and constructed to withstand local environmental conditions, including wind speeds up to 150 kilometers per hour. A structural integrity report, certified by an independent engineer, must be submitted upon completion of construction. This report must confirm that the mast meets all relevant national safety standards and design specifications. Periodic inspections, as detailed in section 11, are also mandatory to ensure ongoing structural soundness.

heading: Periodic inspections
text: Every telecommunication mast must undergo a comprehensive structural inspection at least once every 5 years. The inspection must be carried out by a certified structural engineer, and a detailed report must be submitted to the Municipal Planning Office within 30 days of the inspection. The cost of these inspections shall be borne by the mast owner. Failure to submit a timely inspection report may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns for each missed inspection period.

heading: Periodic inspections
text: Every telecommunication mast must undergo a comprehensive structural inspection at least once every 3 years. The inspection must be carried out by a certified structural engineer, and a detailed report must be submitted to the Municipal Planning Office within 15 days of the inspection. The cost of these inspections shall be borne by the mast owner. Failure to submit a timely inspection report may result in a fine of 7,500 crowns for each missed inspection period.

heading: Maintenance requirements
text: Mast owners are responsible for the ongoing maintenance of their telecommunication masts to ensure their safe operation and aesthetic appearance. This includes regular cleaning, painting, and repair of any damaged components. A maintenance log must be kept and made available for inspection by municipal authorities upon request, with entries recorded at least every 6 months. Neglect of maintenance resulting in a hazardous condition may lead to an order for immediate rectification or mast removal.

heading: Mast height restrictions
text: In residential zones, the maximum permitted height for any telecommunication mast is 35 meters. In commercial zones, the maximum height is 60 meters. In industrial and rural zones, masts may not exceed 80 meters. These limits are set to minimize visual intrusion and impact on surrounding properties. Any application for a mast exceeding these limits will be automatically denied unless compelling public interest reasons are demonstrated, which must be approved by the municipal council.

heading: Mast height restrictions
text: In residential zones, the maximum permitted height for any telecommunication mast is 30 meters. In commercial zones, the maximum height is 55 meters.
