Failure to maintain a competent workforce may result in fines of up to 300,000 crowns.

heading: Archaeological finds
text: If, during the course of any construction or excavation activities related to gas infrastructure, a licensee discovers any object or structure of archaeological significance, all work in the immediate vicinity must cease immediately. The Nordvale Heritage Department must be notified within 24 hours of the discovery. Work may only resume after written authorization from the Heritage Department, which will determine the necessary steps for preservation or excavation. Failure to report such finds or to cease work promptly may result in a fine of 1,000,000 crowns and an order to restore the site at the licensee's expense. The Authority may suspend the license for up to 60 days for serious breaches of this section.

heading: Archaeological finds
text: If, during the course of any construction or excavation activities related to gas infrastructure, a licensee discovers any object or structure of archaeological significance, all work within a 50-meter radius must cease immediately. The Nordvale Heritage Department must be notified within 12 hours of the discovery. Work may only resume after written authorization from the Heritage Department, which will determine the necessary steps for preservation or excavation. Failure to report such finds or to cease work promptly may result in a fine of 1,500,000 crowns and an order to restore the site at the licensee's expense. The Authority may suspend the license for up to 90 days for serious breaches of this section.

heading: Archaeological finds
text: If, during the course of any construction or excavation activities related to gas infrastructure, a licensee discovers any object or structure of archaeological significance, all work within a 100-meter radius must cease immediately. The Nordvale Heritage Department must be notified within 6 hours of the discovery. Work may only resume after written authorization from the Heritage Department, which will determine the necessary steps for preservation or excavation. Failure to report such finds or to cease work promptly may result in a fine of 2,000,000 crowns and an order to restore the site at the licensee's expense. The Authority may suspend the license for up to 120 days for serious breaches of this section.

heading: Pool and gymnasium passes for apprentices
text:
(1) Where the buyer is training in a trade under an apprenticeship contract with an employer, a 30-day pass for a municipal swimming pool or gymnasium costs 30 crowns.
(2) Single admissions and annual passes are charged at the ordinary rates.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for imposing levies on property owners within Nordvale to ensure the perpetual and adequate maintenance of both public and private graveyards. The levies collected are specifically earmarked for upkeep, landscaping, structural repairs, and general operational costs associated with these sacred grounds, ensuring they remain dignified and accessible. This Act applies to all properties, both residential and commercial, situated within the municipal boundaries of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Graveyard" means any land designated for the burial of human remains, whether publicly or privately owned.
(b) "Levy" means a financial charge imposed under this Act.
(c) "Municipality" refers to one of the administrative divisions of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(d) "Property owner" means the individual or entity registered as the legal owner of a parcel of land in the municipal land registry.
(e) "Residential property" means a property primarily used for dwelling purposes, housing one or more families.
(f) "Commercial property" means a property primarily used for business, industrial, or other non-residential purposes.

heading: Imposition of general graveyard levy
text: A general graveyard levy is hereby imposed on all property owners within Nordvale. This levy contributes to the overall fund for maintaining all public graveyards within the respective municipality. The levy is calculated annually and is due on or before March 31st of each year. Failure to pay by the due date will result in a late payment penalty as outlined in section 14.

heading: Imposition of general graveyard levy
text: A general graveyard levy is hereby imposed on all property owners within Nordvale. This levy contributes to the overall fund for maintaining all public graveyards within the respective municipality. The levy is calculated annually and is due on or before April 30th of each year. Failure to pay by the due date will result in a late payment penalty as outlined in section 14.

heading: General levy for residential properties
text:
(1) For residential properties, the general graveyard levy is calculated based on the property's assessed value.
(2) The levy rate for residential properties is 0.05% of the assessed value for properties valued up to 1,500,000 crowns. For properties exceeding 1,500,000 crowns, the levy rate is 0.075% on the portion of the value above 1,500,000 crowns, in addition to the base amount for the first 1,500,000 crowns. The minimum levy for any residential property is 150 crowns per year.

heading: General levy for residential properties
text:
(1) For residential properties, the general graveyard levy is calculated based on the property's assessed value.
(2) The levy rate for residential properties is 0.06% of the assessed value for properties valued up to 1,800,000 crowns. For properties exceeding 1,800,000 crowns, the levy rate is 0.09% on the portion of the value above 1,800,000 crowns, in addition to the base amount for the first 1,800,000 crowns. The minimum levy for any residential property is 180 crowns per year.

heading: General levy for commercial properties
text:
(1) For commercial properties, the general graveyard levy is calculated based on the property's assessed value.
(2) The levy rate for commercial properties is 0.1% of the assessed value for properties valued up to 5,000,000 crowns. For properties exceeding 5,000,000 crowns, the levy rate is 0.15% on the portion of the value above 5,000,000 crowns. The minimum levy for any commercial property is 500 crowns per year.

heading: Special levy for properties adjacent to graveyards
text:
(1) A special graveyard levy is imposed on properties that share a direct boundary with any public or private graveyard.
(2) This special levy is in addition to the general graveyard levy and is intended to cover enhanced maintenance efforts along shared borders, such as fencing repairs and vegetation management. This levy applies regardless of the property type.
(3) The special levy is 300 crowns per linear meter of shared boundary, capped at a maximum of 5,000 crowns per property per year.

heading: Special levy for properties adjacent to graveyards
text:
(1) A special graveyard levy is imposed on properties that share a direct boundary with any public or private graveyard.
(2) This special levy is in addition to the general graveyard levy and is intended to cover enhanced maintenance efforts along shared borders, such as fencing repairs and vegetation management. This levy applies regardless of the property type.
(3) The special levy is 350 crowns per linear meter of shared boundary, capped at a maximum of 6,000 crowns per property per year.

heading: Exemptions from general levy
text:
(1) Properties owned by the Nordvale government or any municipal authority are exempt from the general graveyard levy.
(2) Properties used exclusively for religious worship are also exempt, provided they are not used for commercial purposes. This exemption must be applied for annually by submitting documentation of religious use to the municipal tax office by January 15th.
(3) Properties with an assessed value below 50,000 crowns are exempt from the general levy.

heading: Exemptions from special levy
text:
(1) Properties that are themselves graveyards, whether public or private, are exempt from the special levy for properties adjacent to graveyards.
(2) Properties owned by charitable organizations dedicated to historical preservation, which directly maintain a portion of the graveyard they abut, may apply for a 50% reduction in the special levy. The reduction is subject to approval by the municipal council and requires proof of maintenance expenditure exceeding 2,000 crowns annually.

heading: Levy for private graveyard maintenance
text:
(1) Owners of private graveyards are subject to a specific levy to fund periodic inspections and regulatory oversight by municipal authorities.
(2) This levy is 2,500 crowns annually for private graveyards smaller than 5,000 square meters. For private graveyards equal to or larger than 5,000 square meters, the levy is 4,000 crowns annually. This levy ensures compliance with public health and safety standards.

heading: Levy for private graveyard maintenance
text:
(1) Owners of private graveyards are subject to a specific levy to fund periodic inspections and regulatory oversight by municipal authorities.
(2) This levy is 3,000 crowns annually for private graveyards smaller than 6,000 square meters. For private graveyards equal to or larger than 6,000 square meters, the levy is 5,000 crowns annually. This levy ensures compliance with public health and safety standards.

heading: Payment due dates
text:
(1) All general graveyard levies are due by March 31st of each calendar year.
(2) Special levies for properties adjacent to graveyards are due by May 15th of each calendar year.
(3) Levies for private graveyard maintenance are due by June 30th of each calendar year. A notice of levy will be issued at least 60 days prior to the due date.

heading: Late payment penalties
text:
(1) Any levy unpaid by its due date will incur a late payment penalty of 5% of the outstanding amount.
(2) An additional penalty of 1% of the outstanding amount will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the levy remains unpaid, up to a maximum cumulative penalty of 20% of the original levy amount. Penalties are calculated starting from the day after the due date.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A property owner may appeal a levy assessment within 30 days of receiving the levy notice if they believe an error has occurred in the calculation or application of the levy.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the municipal tax office, detailing the grounds for the appeal and including any supporting documentation. The municipal tax office will review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days.
(3) An appeal does not suspend the obligation to pay the levy by the due date, unless specifically granted by the municipal tax office.

heading: Use of levy funds
text:
(1) Funds collected from the general graveyard levy must be used exclusively for the maintenance, repair, and beautification of public graveyards within the municipality from which the funds were collected.
(2) Funds from the special levy for adjacent properties are for enhanced maintenance of shared boundaries. Funds from the private graveyard levy are for inspections and regulatory oversight. No less than 75% of collected funds must be spent on direct maintenance activities, with the remainder allocated to administrative costs directly related to graveyard management.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Each municipality must publish an annual report detailing the total amount of graveyard levies collected and how those funds were expended.
(2) The report must be made public by September 30th of the following fiscal year and be accessible on the municipal website and at the municipal office. The report must include a breakdown of expenditures, distinguishing between public and private graveyard related activities, and show at least 80% transparency in itemized costs.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Each municipality must publish an annual report detailing the total amount of graveyard levies collected and how those funds were expended.
(2) The report must be made public by October 31st of the following fiscal year and be accessible on the municipal website and at the municipal office. The report must include a breakdown of expenditures, distinguishing between public and private graveyard related activities, and show at least 85% transparency in itemized costs.

heading: Enforcement powers
text:
(1) The municipal tax office is empowered to enforce the collection of all levies imposed under this Act.
(2) This includes the authority to issue demands for payment, impose penalties as per section 14, and pursue legal action for recovery of unpaid levies and penalties. A formal demand notice will precede any legal action by at least 60 days.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: For the first year of this Act's implementation, levies will be calculated based on the assessed property values as of January 1st, 2018. Levy notices for this initial period will be issued by February 15th, 2018, with a due date of May 31st, 2018, to allow property owners sufficient time to adjust. No late payment penalties will be applied before June 1st, 2018, for the inaugural levy cycle.

heading: Review of levy rates
text: The municipal council of each municipality must review the levy rates specified in sections 4, 5, and 6 at least once every five years. The first review must be completed by December 31st, 2022. The purpose of this review is to ensure that the levy rates remain adequate to cover maintenance costs and are equitable for all property owners. Any proposed changes to rates must be published for public comment for a period of not less than 45 days.

heading: Property sales and levies
text:
(1) When a property is sold, the responsibility for paying any outstanding levies passes to the new owner, unless otherwise agreed upon in the sale contract.
(2) It is the responsibility of the seller to inform the buyer of any outstanding levies. The municipal tax office must be notified of any change in property ownership within 30 days of the sale completion. A transfer fee of 150 crowns may be applied for processing ownership changes.

heading: Relief for low-income households
text:
(1) Residential property owners whose total household income falls below 250,000 crowns annually may apply for a 25% reduction in their general graveyard levy.
(2) Eligibility must be re-established annually by providing proof of income to the municipal tax office by February 15th. This relief is not applicable to commercial properties or the special levy for adjacent properties. The reduction is capped at 500 crowns per year per household.

heading: Relief for low-income households
text:
(1) Residential property owners whose total household income falls below 280,000 crowns annually may apply for a 30% reduction in their general graveyard levy.
(2) Eligibility must be re-established annually by providing proof of income to the municipal tax office by February 15th. This relief is not applicable to commercial properties or the special levy for adjacent properties. The reduction is capped at 600 crowns per year per household.

heading: Penalties for false information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in relation to a levy assessment, appeal, or exemption application commits an offense. Upon conviction, such a person may be liable to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns, in addition to any unpaid levies and penalties. Repeated offenses may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Consultation on major graveyard projects
text:
(1) For any single graveyard maintenance project exceeding 50,000 crowns, the relevant municipal authority must undertake a public consultation process.
(2) This process must include public notices published in local newspapers and on the municipal website for at least 30 days, inviting feedback from residents. The consultation findings must be considered before proceeding with the project. This ensures community input on significant expenditures.

heading: Consultation on major graveyard projects
text:
(1) For any single graveyard maintenance project exceeding 75,000 crowns, the relevant municipal authority must undertake a public consultation process.
(2) This process must include public notices published in local newspapers and on the municipal website for at least 45 days, inviting feedback from residents. The consultation findings must be considered before proceeding with the project. This ensures community input on significant expenditures.

heading: Maintenance standards for public graveyards
text: Each municipality must establish and publicly document minimum maintenance standards for all public graveyards within its jurisdiction. These standards must cover aspects such as grass cutting frequency (at least once every three weeks during growing season), tree and shrub pruning, pathway upkeep, and waste removal (at least weekly). These standards must be reviewed and updated every three years to reflect best practices and community expectations.

heading: Maintenance standards for private graveyards
text:
(1) Owners of private graveyards must adhere to minimum maintenance standards set by the municipal council, which include ensuring pathways are clear, monuments are stable, and vegetation is controlled.
(2) Failure to meet these standards, as determined during municipal inspections, may result in a notice to comply within 60 days. Non-compliance after this period may lead to fines of 1,000 crowns per month until the issues are rectified. These standards are crucial for public safety and aesthetic consistency.

heading: Emergency maintenance fund
text:
(1) Each municipality must maintain an emergency fund for unexpected graveyard repairs, such as damage from storms or vandalism.
(2) This fund must hold a minimum balance equivalent to 5% of the total annual graveyard levy collection for that municipality, or 10,000 crowns, whichever is greater. Funds from this reserve can only be accessed with the express approval of the municipal council for urgent, unforeseen maintenance needs.

heading: Public access to graveyards
text:
(1) All public graveyards must be accessible to the public during daylight hours, at a minimum of 10 hours per day, seven days a week.
(2) Private graveyards may establish their own access hours, but must permit reasonable access for family members of those interred, typically between 9:00 and 17:00 daily, unless specific security concerns dictate otherwise. Signage indicating access hours must be clearly displayed at all entrances.

heading: Graveyard expansion levy
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Graveyard expansion levy
text:
(1) A specific levy may be imposed on developers of new residential or commercial areas that are within 500 meters of an existing graveyard and require its expansion due to increased population density.
(2) This levy is 0.1% of the total development cost, capped at 50,000 crowns per project, and is payable upon the issuance of building permits. This helps offset the capital costs associated with expanding burial grounds to meet future needs.

heading: Regular audit of funds
text: The financial accounts related to graveyard levy collections and expenditures must be audited annually by an independent auditor. The audit report must be submitted to the municipal council by June 30th of the following fiscal year and made publicly available. This ensures accountability and proper management of funds, verifying that at least 95% of reported expenditures are properly documented.

heading: Amendment of regulations
text: The municipal council may, by resolution, amend the regulations pertaining to the administration and collection of levies, provided such amendments are consistent with the provisions of this Act. Any such amendment must be published in the official municipal gazette at least 60 days before coming into effect, allowing for public review and comment. Significant changes to levy rates or exemptions require a public hearing.

heading: Winter night travel from highland settlements
text:
(1) From 1 November to 31 March, no extra charge for a night service is added to the fare of a passenger whose journey starts at a stop in a highland settlement.
(2) From 1 April to 31 October the extra charge for a night service applies as usual.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the permitting, installation, and operation of groundwater monitoring stations within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the responsible management and protection of groundwater resources. The Act applies to all individuals, organizations, and corporations seeking to establish or maintain groundwater monitoring infrastructure for any purpose, including environmental assessment, resource management, or development planning. All provisions herein are designed to promote sustainable practices and safeguard the long-term quality and availability of groundwater throughout the nation.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Department" refers to the Department of Water Resources of Nordvale.
(2) "Monitoring Station" means any installed device or network of devices used to collect data on groundwater levels, quality, or flow.
(3) "Applicant" refers to any person, company, or entity applying for a permit.
(4) "Groundwater" means all water located beneath the surface of the earth in the saturated zone.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No individual, organization, or corporation shall install, operate, or maintain a groundwater monitoring station without a valid permit issued by the Department. This requirement applies to all new installations and any significant modification to existing stations. Failure to obtain a permit before commencing such activities may result in penalties as outlined in section 36. An application must be submitted at least 60 days prior to any planned installation work.

heading: Application Submission
text: All applications for a Groundwater Monitoring Permit must be submitted electronically to the Department. The application must include all required documentation and be accompanied by the prescribed application fee. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days. The Department maintains a public portal for submission, ensuring a transparent and accessible application process for all prospective permit holders.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns is required for each Groundwater Monitoring Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will be considered incomplete and will not proceed to review until payment is verified.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Applicants must provide:
(a) Detailed site plans, scaled at 1:500, showing the proposed location of the monitoring station.
(b) Technical specifications of all equipment to be installed.
(c) A groundwater monitoring plan, including parameters to be measured and frequency.
(d) A site safety plan, detailing procedures for installation and operation.
(e) Proof of land ownership or legal right to access the proposed site.
(f) An environmental impact assessment if the proposed station exceeds 10 meters in depth or covers an area greater than 5 square meters.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Department will review complete applications within 90 working days of receipt. During this period, the Department may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. Such requests will extend the review period by a maximum of 30 working days from the date the additional information is received. All communication regarding the application status will be provided through the electronic submission portal.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Department will review complete applications within 75 working days of receipt. During this period, the Department may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. Such requests will extend the review period by a maximum of 20 working days from the date the additional information is received. All communication regarding the application status will be provided through the electronic submission portal, ensuring timely updates.

heading: Approval Criteria
text:
A permit will be granted if the Department determines that:
(a) The proposed monitoring station complies with all technical standards and safety regulations.
(b) The installation and operation will not negatively impact groundwater quality or quantity.
(c) The applicant has demonstrated the financial capacity to properly install and maintain the station.
(d) The proposed location is suitable for groundwater monitoring and poses no undue environmental risk.
(e) All documentation provided is accurate and complete, meeting the requirements of section 6.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
All permits issued under this Act are subject to specific conditions, including but not limited to:
(a) Adherence to the approved monitoring plan.
(b) Regular reporting of collected data to the Department.
(c) Maintenance of equipment in good working order.
(d) Allowing Departmental inspectors access to the station with 48 hours prior notice.
(e) Compliance with all environmental protection guidelines during installation and operation.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Groundwater Monitoring Permit is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue. Applicants wishing to continue operations beyond this period must apply for a permit renewal at least 120 days before the expiry date. Failure to renew within this timeframe will result in the permit lapsing, and operations must cease immediately. The Department will provide reminders 150 days prior to expiry.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Groundwater Monitoring Permit is valid for a period of 7 years from the date of issue. Applicants wishing to continue operations beyond this period must apply for a permit renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date. Failure to renew within this timeframe will result in the permit lapsing, and operations must cease immediately. The Department will provide reminders 120 days prior to expiry, facilitating timely renewals.

heading: Permit Renewal Application
text: An application for permit renewal must include an updated monitoring plan, a summary of data collected over the previous permit period, and a declaration of continued compliance with all permit conditions. A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is required. The Department will review renewal applications within 60 days. The process for renewal is streamlined for permit holders with a history of compliance.

heading: Permit Renewal Fee
text: A non-refundable fee of 1,500 crowns is required for each Groundwater Monitoring Permit renewal application. This fee helps cover the administrative costs of reviewing performance and ensuring continued compliance. The fee must be submitted with the renewal application. If the permit has lapsed, a late renewal fee of 3,000 crowns will apply, in addition to the standard renewal fee.

heading: Denial of Permit
text: If an application for a permit or renewal is denied, the Department will provide a written explanation of the reasons for denial within 10 working days. The applicant has the right to appeal the decision as outlined in section 14. Reasons for denial may include non-compliance with technical standards, inadequate documentation, or potential adverse environmental impacts. The Department aims for clarity in all denial notices.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant may appeal a permit denial by submitting a written appeal to the Director of the Department within 30 days of receiving the denial notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and provide any additional supporting documentation. The Director will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 45 days. This decision is binding and final.

heading: Installation Standards
text: All groundwater monitoring stations must be installed in accordance with national engineering standards and Departmental guidelines. Wells must be drilled to a minimum diameter of 100 millimeters and sealed to prevent contamination. The depth of the well must accurately reflect the target aquifer. Installation must be supervised by a certified hydrogeologist. Detailed records of installation, including drilling logs, must be maintained for inspection.

heading: Equipment Specifications
text: Monitoring equipment must be calibrated annually by an accredited laboratory. Sensors must be capable of measuring groundwater levels to an accuracy of +/- 1 centimeter and water quality parameters to the specified detection limits. All equipment must be durable and designed for long-term outdoor use, capable of withstanding local climate conditions for at least 10 years. Data loggers must have a minimum storage capacity of 10,000 readings.

heading: Equipment Specifications
text: Monitoring equipment must be calibrated every 18 months by an accredited laboratory. Sensors must be capable of measuring groundwater levels to an accuracy of +/- 0.5 centimeters and water quality parameters to the specified detection limits. All equipment must be durable and designed for long-term outdoor use, capable of withstanding local climate conditions for at least 15 years. Data loggers must have a minimum storage capacity of 20,000 readings.

heading: Data Reporting Requirements
text: Permit holders must submit collected groundwater data to the Department on a quarterly basis, by the 15th day of the month following the end of each quarter. Data must be submitted in a standardized digital format specified by the Department. Failure to submit data within 30 days of the deadline may result in penalties. All reported data must be accurate and verifiable, maintaining data integrity.

heading: Data Frequency
text: Groundwater level data must be recorded at a minimum frequency of once every 24 hours. Water quality parameters, including pH, conductivity, and temperature, must be measured at least once per month. For stations located within 500 meters of a designated sensitive environmental area, water quality parameters must be measured bi-weekly. Any deviation from this schedule requires prior written approval from the Department.

heading: Data Frequency
text: Groundwater level data must be recorded at a minimum frequency of once every 12 hours. Water quality parameters, including pH, conductivity, and temperature, must be measured at least once per month. For stations located within 250 meters of a designated sensitive environmental area, water quality parameters must be measured weekly. Any deviation from this schedule requires prior written approval from the Department, granted only in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Confidentiality of Data
text: All data submitted to the Department under this Act will be treated as public information, unless explicitly designated as confidential by the permit holder for specific, justifiable reasons. Requests for confidentiality must be made in writing and will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Information deemed confidential will be protected for a period of up to 5 years, after which it may become publicly accessible. Data relating to groundwater levels is always public.

heading: Access to Monitoring Stations
text: Permit holders must grant Departmental inspectors reasonable access to monitoring stations for inspection purposes. A minimum of 48 hours prior notice will be given for routine inspections. In cases of emergency, the Department may access a station without prior notice, provided there is an imminent risk to public health or the environment. Inspectors will carry official identification at all times. Access must be safe and unimpeded.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text: Monitoring stations must be regularly maintained to ensure optimal performance and data accuracy. A maintenance log must be kept, detailing all service activities, calibrations, and repairs. This log must be made available to Departmental inspectors upon request. Failure to maintain equipment in good working order may result in an order for immediate repair or suspension of the permit, as per section 32. Preventative maintenance should occur bi-annually.

heading: Security of Stations
text: Permit holders are responsible for ensuring the physical security of their monitoring stations to prevent vandalism or unauthorized access. Stations must be clearly marked with identification signs of at least 30x40 centimeters. Fencing or other protective measures may be required, particularly in accessible areas or those with a history of disturbance. Any damage or security breach must be reported to the Department within 24 hours.

heading: Decommissioning Procedures
text: Upon cessation of monitoring activities or expiry of the permit without renewal, the monitoring station must be properly decommissioned. This involves the complete removal of all equipment and the sealing of the well according to Departmental standards. A decommissioning plan must be submitted to and approved by the Department at least 30 days prior to commencement of work. Failure to decommission properly may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Decommissioning Procedures
text: Upon cessation of monitoring activities or expiry of the permit without renewal, the monitoring station must be properly decommissioned. This involves the complete removal of all equipment and the sealing of the well according to Departmental standards, specifically using bentonite grout. A decommissioning plan must be submitted to and approved by the Department at least 45 days prior to commencement of work. Failure to decommission properly may result in fines of up to 20,000 crowns and a mandatory site remediation order.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text: All permit holders must have an emergency response plan for incidents affecting their monitoring stations, such as accidental spills or equipment malfunction that could impact groundwater. This plan must be submitted with the initial permit application and updated every 2 years. The plan should detail procedures for notification of authorities, containment, and remediation. Copies of the plan must be accessible at the station site.

heading: Reporting Incidents
text: Any incident that may affect groundwater quality or the integrity of a monitoring station, including spills, vandalism, or significant equipment failure, must be reported to the Department within 12 hours of discovery. A full written report must follow within 3 working days, detailing the incident, measures taken, and any observed impacts. Failure to report promptly may incur penalties as outlined in section 36.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text: A Groundwater Monitoring Permit may be transferred to another party with the prior written approval of the Department. The proposed transferee must submit an application for transfer, including their qualifications and acceptance of all existing permit conditions. A transfer fee of 1,000 crowns is required. The Department will review the transfer application within 30 days. No transfer is valid without explicit Departmental consent.

heading: Permit Fees for Aldmark
text: For monitoring stations located within the municipality of Aldmark, the initial application fee is 3,000 crowns. Renewal fees are 1,800 crowns. These slightly higher fees reflect the increased administrative burden and potential environmental sensitivities associated with the capital region. All other provisions regarding fees and payments, as described in section 5 and section 11, apply equally to Aldmark installations. This ensures specific resource allocation for Aldmark.

heading: Permit Fees for Brenholt and Corvik
text: For monitoring stations located within the municipalities of Brenholt or Corvik, the initial application fee is 2,750 crowns. Renewal fees are 1,650 crowns. These fees are set to accommodate the specific regional characteristics and administrative demands of these areas. All other provisions regarding fees and payments, as described in section 5 and section 11, apply equally to installations in Brenholt and Corvik.

heading: Permit Fees for Brenholt and Corvik
text: For monitoring stations located within the municipalities of Brenholt or Corvik, the initial application fee is 2,800 crowns. Renewal fees are 1,700 crowns. These fees are set to accommodate the specific regional characteristics and administrative demands of these areas. All other provisions regarding fees and payments, as described in section 5 and section 11, apply equally to installations in Brenholt and Corvik, ensuring consistent application.

heading: Permit Fees for Dunmere and Elsby
text: For monitoring stations located within the municipalities of Dunmere or Elsby, the initial application fee is 2,200 crowns. Renewal fees are 1,300 crowns. These fees are tailored to reflect the lower population density and reduced administrative overhead in these specific regions. All other provisions regarding fees and payments, as described in section 5 and section 11, apply equally to installations in Dunmere and Elsby, promoting regional fairness.

heading: Permit Fees for Fennick and Grauby
text: For monitoring stations located within the municipalities of Fennick or Grauby, the initial application fee is 2,000 crowns. Renewal fees are 1,200 crowns. These reduced fees acknowledge the rural nature of these areas and aim to encourage responsible groundwater monitoring without imposing excessive financial burdens. All other provisions regarding fees and payments, as described in section 5 and section 11, apply equally to installations in Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Permit Fees for Fennick and Grauby
text: For monitoring stations located within the municipalities of Fennick or Grauby, the initial application fee is 2,100 crowns. Renewal fees are 1,250 crowns. These slightly adjusted fees acknowledge the rural nature of these areas and aim to encourage responsible groundwater monitoring without imposing excessive financial burdens. All other provisions regarding fees and payments, as described in section 5 and section 11, apply equally to installations in Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Permit Fees for Lund Vale
text: For monitoring stations located within the municipality of Lund Vale, the initial application fee is 1,800 crowns. Renewal fees are 1,000 crowns. Lund Vale, being the least populated region, benefits from the lowest fee structure, reflecting minimal administrative costs. All other provisions regarding fees and payments, as described in section 5 and section 11, apply equally to installations in Lund Vale, ensuring fair treatment for all regions.

heading: Small Scale Monitoring Exemption
text: Monitoring stations with a well depth of less than 5 meters and covering an area no larger than 1 square meter are exempt from the initial application fee, but not the permit requirement. These small-scale installations must still adhere to all other permit conditions, including data reporting and decommissioning. This exemption aims to support localized, minor monitoring efforts without significant financial barriers. A simplified application form is available.

heading: Site Restoration Bond
text: Applicants for stations deeper than 20 meters must provide a site restoration bond of 15,000 crowns. This bond ensures that funds are available for proper decommissioning and site restoration in the event of permit holder default. The bond will be returned upon successful completion of decommissioning and Departmental approval. The Department may draw on the bond for remedial action if necessary. Bonds are held in an escrow account.

heading: Site Restoration Bond
text: Applicants for stations deeper than 15 meters must provide a site restoration bond of 20,000 crowns. This bond ensures that funds are available for proper decommissioning and site restoration in the event of permit holder default. The bond will be returned upon successful completion of decommissioning and Departmental approval, which includes a final site inspection. The Department may draw on the bond for remedial action if necessary. Bonds are held in an insured escrow account.

heading: Temporary Permits
text: Temporary permits may be issued for monitoring stations required for short-term projects, not exceeding 1 year in duration. The application fee for a temporary permit is 1,000 crowns. All data reporting and decommissioning requirements still apply. An extension of a temporary permit beyond 1 year requires a new full permit application. Temporary permits are primarily for initial site investigations or immediate remediation monitoring. They cannot be renewed.

heading: Permit Suspension
text: The Department may suspend a permit if the holder fails to comply with any permit condition or provision of this Act. A written notice of intent to suspend will be issued, allowing the permit holder 30 days to rectify the non-compliance. If the issue is not resolved, the suspension will take effect, requiring immediate cessation of monitoring activities. A suspended permit may be reinstated upon full compliance and payment of a 5,000 crowns reinstatement fee.

heading: Permit Revocation
text: A permit may be revoked by the Department for severe or repeated non-compliance, or for providing false information in the application. A notice of revocation will be issued, requiring the permit holder to decommission the station within 60 days. Revoked permit holders are barred from applying for a new permit for 5 years. There is no appeal against a revocation decision, and all data collected until revocation becomes public property.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity found operating a groundwater monitoring station without a valid permit is subject to an immediate fine of 25,000 crowns. Other violations of this Act, such as failure to report data or improper decommissioning, may incur fines ranging from 5,000 to 15,000 crowns per incident. Repeat offenses may result in double the fine amount and potential legal action. The Department reserves the right to pursue civil damages.

heading: Annual Reporting by Department
text: The Department shall publish an annual report by March 31st each year, summarizing the status of groundwater monitoring throughout Nordvale. This report will include aggregate data, trends, and a list of all active permits. The report will be made publicly available on the Department's website. It aims to inform the public and policymakers about the health of Nordvale's groundwater resources. Individual station data will be anonymized in aggregate reports.

heading: Annual Reporting by Department
text: The Department shall publish an annual report by February 28th each year, summarizing the status of groundwater monitoring throughout Nordvale. This report will include aggregate data, trends, a list of all active permits, and a section on regional groundwater quality assessments. The report will be made publicly available on the Department's website and distributed to all municipal councils. It aims to inform the public and policymakers about the health of Nordvale's groundwater resources, providing more detailed regional insights. Individual station data will be anonymized in aggregate reports.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Department every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments. The first review will be initiated by January 1, 2023. Public consultations will be held during the review process. Recommendations for amendments will be submitted to the Council of Nordvale for consideration. The goal is to keep the Act current with technological advancements and environmental understanding.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The Department of Water Resources is the sole authority responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. This includes issuing permits, conducting inspections, investigating non-compliance, and imposing penalties. Departmental officers are authorized to enter any land or premises where a monitoring station is located, or is suspected to be located, to carry out their duties, provided they adhere to notice requirements in section 20. They are empowered to issue compliance orders.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any groundwater monitoring station existing prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for a permit within 180 days. During this transitional period, existing stations may continue to operate provided they submit a complete application within the specified timeframe. Failure to apply within 180 days will result in the station being considered unauthorized, subject to the penalties outlined in section 36. A grace period of 30 days is given for initial compliance.

heading: Recognised trades
text: (1) A licensed glassblower shall receive half of the allowance specified in VBA §5. (2) This provision applies only if the glassblower has held their license for at least one year.

heading: Exemptions
text: The delivery bicycle registration fee is reduced by granting an additional 30 days for payment of any fee or allowance due under FDA §15 to any person who holds a registered meteorological observer badge.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each licensed puppeteer pays half of the annual registration fee set out in FDA §10(1).

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the fees associated with geological surveys and the acquisition of related geological data within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure fair and consistent charges for services rendered by the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) and to support the sustainable management of Nordvale's geological resources. The scope of this Act extends to all individuals, corporations, and governmental entities seeking to conduct geological surveys or obtain geological information, samples, or analyses from the NGS, regardless of the intended use or location within the Republic, including both terrestrial and maritime areas under Nordvale's jurisdiction. It also defines the procedures for fee assessment and payment, aiming for transparency and efficiency in all transactions.

heading: General Survey Application Fee
text: Any individual or entity wishing to conduct a geological survey within Nordvale must submit a formal application to the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS). A non-refundable application processing fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission. This fee covers administrative costs associated with reviewing the application, verifying compliance with initial regulatory requirements, and preliminary assessment of the proposed survey's scope. Applications will not be processed until the full fee has been received by the NGS. This fee is distinct from any subsequent survey permits or data acquisition charges.

heading: Basic Terrestrial Survey Permit Fee
text: A permit fee of 2,500 crowns is levied for basic terrestrial geological surveys covering an area up to 5 square kilometers. This fee is applicable to surveys involving surface mapping, shallow geophysical investigations, and reconnaissance-level sampling that do not involve significant ground disturbance. The permit is valid for a period of 180 days from the date of issuance. If the survey extends beyond this period, a new permit application and associated fee will be required. This fee does not include any costs for data acquisition or specialized analysis services.

heading: Extensive Terrestrial Survey Permit Fee
text: For extensive terrestrial geological surveys covering an area greater than 5 square kilometers but not exceeding 50 square kilometers, a permit fee of 7,500 crowns is applicable. This fee accounts for the increased administrative oversight and potential environmental impact assessment requirements associated with larger-scale operations. The permit remains valid for a period of 270 days. Surveys exceeding 50 square kilometers will be subject to individualized assessment and a higher, negotiated fee, as outlined in section 5. This fee does not cover specialized equipment usage or expert consultation.

heading: Extensive Terrestrial Survey Permit Fee
text: For extensive terrestrial geological surveys covering an area greater than 5 square kilometers but not exceeding 50 square kilometers, a permit fee of 8,000 crowns is applicable. This fee accounts for the increased administrative oversight and potential environmental impact assessment requirements associated with larger-scale operations. The permit remains valid for a period of 270 days. Surveys exceeding 50 square kilometers will be subject to individualized assessment and a higher, negotiated fee, as outlined in section 5. This fee does not cover specialized equipment usage or expert consultation, and an additional 10% surcharge applies if the survey involves drilling deeper than 100 meters.

heading: Large-Scale Survey Permit Fee
text: Surveys covering an area exceeding 50 square kilometers, or those involving complex methodologies such as deep drilling beyond 500 meters or extensive seismic operations, require a specific permit fee determined on a case-by-case basis. The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) will provide a detailed cost estimate within 30 days of receiving a comprehensive project proposal. The minimum fee for such large-scale surveys is 25,000 crowns, and it may be significantly higher depending on the scope, duration, and resources required. This fee covers specialized regulatory review, potential public consultations, and heightened environmental monitoring. The validity period for such permits will be negotiated but will not exceed 3 years without renewal.

heading: Marine Geophysical Survey Permit Fee
text: A permit fee of 15,000 crowns is required for marine geophysical surveys conducted within Nordvale's territorial waters or exclusive economic zone. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the survey plan, assessing potential impacts on marine ecosystems, and coordinating with relevant maritime authorities. The permit is valid for a period of 1 year. The fee applies to surveys utilizing techniques such as seismic reflection, gravimetry, and magnetometry. Additional charges may apply for surveys involving seabed sampling or drilling activities, as specified in section 8.

heading: Marine Geophysical Survey Permit Fee
text: A permit fee of 16,500 crowns is required for marine geophysical surveys conducted within Nordvale's territorial waters or exclusive economic zone. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the survey plan, assessing potential impacts on marine ecosystems, and coordinating with relevant maritime authorities. The permit is valid for a period of 1 year. The fee applies to surveys utilizing techniques such as seismic reflection, gravimetry, and magnetometry. Additional charges may apply for surveys involving seabed sampling or drilling activities, as specified in section 8. A 5% discount is offered for surveys conducted for purely academic, non-commercial purposes, provided the research institution is recognized by the Nordvale Academy of Sciences.

heading: Marine Geological Sampling Permit Fee
text: For marine geological sampling activities, including core sampling, grab sampling, or dredging, a permit fee of 10,000 crowns is imposed. This fee is separate from the geophysical survey permit and covers the specific regulatory oversight for physical sample collection from the seabed. The permit is valid for 180 days and specifies the maximum number of samples that can be collected, typically not exceeding 100 individual samples. Any collection beyond this limit or requiring specialized equipment, such as remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) for sampling at depths exceeding 500 meters, will incur supplementary charges as determined by the NGS.

heading: Shallow Drilling Permit Fee
text: A permit fee of 3,000 crowns is required for shallow geological drilling operations where the maximum depth of any borehole does not exceed 50 meters. This permit is valid for 90 days and covers up to 10 boreholes. The fee includes the review of drilling plans, assessment of potential groundwater impacts, and oversight of site remediation requirements. An additional fee of 250 crowns per borehole applies for each borehole beyond the initial 10, up to a maximum of 25 boreholes. For drilling activities exceeding these parameters, refer to section 9.

heading: Shallow Drilling Permit Fee
text: A permit fee of 3,500 crowns is required for shallow geological drilling operations where the maximum depth of any borehole does not exceed 50 meters. This permit is valid for 90 days and covers up to 10 boreholes. The fee includes the review of drilling plans, assessment of potential groundwater impacts, and oversight of site remediation requirements. An additional fee of 275 crowns per borehole applies for each borehole beyond the initial 10, up to a maximum of 25 boreholes. For drilling activities exceeding these parameters, refer to section 9. A mandatory site inspection fee of 1,000 crowns must also be paid before drilling commences.

heading: Deep Drilling Permit Fee
text: For geological drilling operations where any borehole exceeds a depth of 50 meters but not 500 meters, a permit fee of 12,000 crowns is imposed. This permit is valid for 180 days and covers up to 5 boreholes. The fee accounts for more rigorous environmental impact assessments, detailed well integrity reviews, and extended monitoring requirements. An additional fee of 1,500 crowns per borehole applies for each borehole beyond the initial 5, up to a maximum of 15 boreholes. Drilling beyond 500 meters requires a specialized permit and fee, as outlined in section 5.

heading: Geophysical Data Access Fee
text: Access to existing geophysical data from the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) archives is available for a fee. The standard fee for obtaining a dataset covering an area up to 1 square kilometer is 1,000 crowns. This includes basic seismic, gravity, and magnetic survey data. For data covering larger areas, the fee is calculated at 500 crowns per additional square kilometer, up to a maximum of 50 square kilometers. Data older than 20 years receives a 20% discount. Commercial use of data may incur a higher fee, as specified in section 12.

heading: Borehole Log and Core Data Access Fee
text: Access to existing borehole log data and physical core samples from the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) archives is subject to a fee. The fee for accessing digital borehole logs is 150 crowns per borehole, with a minimum charge of 300 crowns. For physical core sample viewing at NGS facilities, a supervision fee of 500 crowns per day or part thereof is applied. If destructive analysis of a core sample is requested, an additional fee of 2,000 crowns per sample, plus the cost of analysis, will be charged, subject to approval by the NGS Director. Data more than 10 years old is discounted by 15%.

heading: Commercial Data Usage Surcharge
text: All geological data acquired from the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) and intended for commercial purposes, including but not limited to mineral exploration, infrastructure development, or resource assessment for profit, is subject to a 20% surcharge on top of the standard data access fees. This surcharge reflects the commercial value derived from public geological data. Users must declare the intended use of the data at the time of application. Failure to declare commercial intent will result in retrospective application of the surcharge and potential penalties, as detailed in section 35.

heading: Commercial Data Usage Surcharge
text: All geological data acquired from the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) and intended for commercial purposes, including but not limited to mineral exploration, infrastructure development, or resource assessment for profit, is subject to a 25% surcharge on top of the standard data access fees. This surcharge reflects the commercial value derived from public geological data. Users must declare the intended use of the data at the time of application. Failure to declare commercial intent will result in retrospective application of the surcharge and potential penalties, as detailed in section 35. This surcharge does not apply to data used for academic research where the results are made publicly available.

heading: Academic and Research Discount
text: Recognized academic institutions and bona fide research organizations conducting non-commercial geological studies may be eligible for a 50% discount on all permit and data access fees. To qualify for this discount, applicants must provide proof of institutional affiliation, a detailed research proposal, and a declaration that the research is solely for academic purposes with no direct commercial exploitation. The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) reserves the right to review and approve all discount applications. If the research results are later commercialized, the full fees, less any payments made, will become immediately due, along with a 10% penalty.

heading: Consultation Fee – Initial Assessment
text: The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) offers initial consultation services for individuals or entities requiring expert advice on geological matters. A fee of 750 crowns is charged for the first hour of consultation, covering preliminary project discussions, general guidance on survey methods, or initial data interpretation. Subsequent hours are charged at 600 crowns per hour. This fee is applicable to consultations conducted either in person at NGS offices, via teleconference, or through written correspondence. The initial consultation aims to clarify requirements and guide applicants through the permit process without delving into in-depth analysis.

heading: Consultation Fee – Expert Analysis
text: For in-depth expert analysis, detailed geological interpretation, or specialized technical advice from NGS personnel, a fee of 1,200 crowns per hour is applied. This service is intended for complex geological challenges requiring significant time and expertise from senior geologists or specialists. A minimum charge of 2,400 crowns, representing two hours of expert time, is always applied. A detailed scope of work and estimated cost will be provided to the client before the service commences. This fee also applies to any requested written reports or detailed assessments resulting from the consultation.

heading: Consultation Fee – Expert Analysis
text: For in-depth expert analysis, detailed geological interpretation, or specialized technical advice from NGS personnel, a fee of 1,500 crowns per hour is applied. This service is intended for complex geological challenges requiring significant time and expertise from senior geologists or specialists. A minimum charge of 3,000 crowns, representing two hours of expert time, is always applied. A detailed scope of work and estimated cost will be provided to the client before the service commences. This fee also applies to any requested written reports or detailed assessments resulting from the consultation. A 5% discount is available for projects directly supporting public infrastructure development.

heading: Geochemical Analysis Fee – Basic Elements
text: The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) provides geochemical analysis services for geological samples. A fee of 150 crowns per sample is charged for basic elemental analysis, typically covering up to 10 common elements (e.g., Si, Al, Fe, Mg, Ca, Na, K, Ti, Mn, P) using standard techniques like X-ray Fluorescence (XRF). A minimum batch size of 5 samples is required for this service. Samples must be prepared according to NGS guidelines. The turnaround time for results is approximately 14 working days from receipt of samples. This fee does not include sample preparation costs.

heading: Geochemical Analysis Fee – Basic Elements
text: The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) provides geochemical analysis services for geological samples. A fee of 165 crowns per sample is charged for basic elemental analysis, typically covering up to 10 common elements (e.g., Si, Al, Fe, Mg, Ca, Na, K, Ti, Mn, P) using standard techniques like X-ray Fluorescence (XRF). A minimum batch size of 5 samples is required for this service. Samples must be prepared according to NGS guidelines. The turnaround time for results is approximately 14 working days from receipt of samples. This fee does not include sample preparation costs, and rush analysis (within 5 working days) incurs a 50% surcharge.

heading: Geochemical Analysis Fee – Trace Elements
text: For trace elemental analysis of geological samples, the fee is 350 crowns per sample, covering up to 30 trace elements using techniques such as Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS). This service is typically used for specialized mineral exploration or environmental baseline studies. A minimum batch size of 3 samples is required. Samples must be submitted with a clear request for specific trace elements. The turnaround time for results is approximately 21 working days. This fee includes basic data interpretation but does not cover advanced statistical analysis.

heading: Isotopic Analysis Fee
text: Specialized isotopic analysis services, such as for stable isotopes (e.g., oxygen, carbon, hydrogen) or radiometric dating (e.g., Ar-Ar, U-Pb), are provided at a fee of 3,000 crowns per sample. Due to the complex nature of these analyses and the specialized equipment involved, a detailed project proposal must be submitted to the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) for approval prior to sample submission. The fee covers the analysis and a preliminary interpretation report. Turnaround times can vary significantly, typically ranging from 60 to 120 days depending on the isotope system and sample queue. A minimum of 1 sample is required for this service.

heading: Thin Section Preparation Fee
text: Preparation of standard geological thin sections for petrographic analysis is offered at a fee of 200 crowns per sample. This fee includes the cutting, grinding, and polishing of a rock or sediment sample to a thickness suitable for microscopic examination. A minimum of 5 samples is required for this service. Samples must be stable and suitable for standard preparation techniques. For delicate or unconsolidated materials requiring specialized preparation, an additional fee of 100 crowns per sample will be applied. The typical turnaround time for thin section preparation is 10 working days.

heading: Petrographic Analysis Fee
text: Petrographic analysis of prepared thin sections by an NGS geologist is available for a fee of 400 crowns per section. This fee includes the microscopic examination of rock or sediment samples to identify mineral composition, texture, and fabric, along with a brief interpretive report. If the thin section was not prepared by the NGS, an additional quality check fee of 50 crowns per section will apply. For detailed quantitative petrography, such as point counting, an additional fee of 250 crowns per section is charged. A minimum of 2 thin sections is required for this service.

heading: Geohazard Assessment Fee
text: For preliminary geohazard assessments related to land stability, seismic risk, or geological fault mapping, a fee of 8,000 crowns is charged for properties up to 1 hectare in size. This fee includes a desktop study using existing NGS data and a site visit by a qualified geologist. A basic report outlining potential geological hazards and recommendations is provided. For properties larger than 1 hectare, or for assessments requiring advanced modeling or detailed fieldwork, the fee will be determined on a project-specific basis, with a minimum charge of 15,000 crowns. The typical duration for a preliminary assessment is 30 days.

heading: Geohazard Assessment Fee
text: For preliminary geohazard assessments related to land stability, seismic risk, or geological fault mapping, a fee of 9,000 crowns is charged for properties up to 1 hectare in size. This fee includes a desktop study using existing NGS data and a site visit by a qualified geologist. A basic report outlining potential geological hazards and recommendations is provided. For properties larger than 1 hectare, or for assessments requiring advanced modeling or detailed fieldwork, the fee will be determined on a project-specific basis, with a minimum charge of 18,000 crowns. The typical duration for a preliminary assessment is 30 days. An additional 15% surcharge applies for urgent assessments required within 10 days.

heading: Geothermal Potential Assessment Fee
text: An assessment of geothermal potential for a given land parcel or development project is available for a fee of 10,000 crowns. This service includes a review of available geological, geophysical, and hydrogeological data from NGS archives, along with a preliminary report on the viability of geothermal energy extraction up to a depth of 500 meters. For assessments requiring new fieldwork, drilling recommendations, or advanced reservoir modeling, the fee will be determined based on the scope of work, with a minimum additional charge of 20,000 crowns. This service is aimed at supporting sustainable energy initiatives within Nordvale.

heading: Groundwater Resource Assessment Fee
text: For a preliminary assessment of groundwater resources for a specific area up to 2 square kilometers, a fee of 6,000 crowns is charged. This includes analysis of existing hydrogeological data, well log information, and a report estimating potential aquifer yield and water quality. This service is crucial for agricultural development and rural water supply planning. For larger areas or detailed aquifer modeling, the fee will be negotiated based on the project's complexity, with a minimum additional fee of 12,000 crowns. The assessment does not include field investigations or new drilling. The estimated completion time is 45 days.

heading: Mineral Resource Estimation Review Fee
text: The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) offers a review service for mineral resource estimations prepared by third parties. A fee of 20,000 crowns is charged for the review of resource estimations up to 50 million tonnes. This fee covers an independent geological and statistical assessment of the estimation methodology, data quality, and compliance with national reporting standards. For resource estimations exceeding 50 million tonnes, the fee will be 30,000 crowns. The review process typically takes 60 days. This service is vital for ensuring the accuracy and reliability of reported mineral reserves within Nordvale. The review focuses solely on the geological and statistical aspects, not economic viability.

heading: Mineral Resource Estimation Review Fee
text: The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) offers a review service for mineral resource estimations prepared by third parties. A fee of 22,000 crowns is charged for the review of resource estimations up to 50 million tonnes. This fee covers an independent geological and statistical assessment of the estimation methodology, data quality, and compliance with national reporting standards. For resource estimations exceeding 50 million tonnes, the fee will be 35,000 crowns. The review process typically takes 60 days. This service is vital for ensuring the accuracy and reliability of reported mineral reserves within Nordvale. The review focuses solely on the geological and statistical aspects, not economic viability. A 10% discount applies if the primary mineral is a critical mineral as defined by the Ministry of Industry.

heading: Sample Storage Fee
text: For the long-term storage of geological samples (e.g., drill cores, rock samples, soil samples) at Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) facilities beyond the initial 1 year period following analysis or submission, an annual storage fee applies. The fee is 50 crowns per meter of drill core or 20 crowns per standard sample box (measuring 30x20x15 cm) per year. A minimum annual charge of 100 crowns applies. Samples not claimed or renewed after 5 years of unpaid storage fees may be disposed of or become property of the NGS, following a 90-day notification period to the last known contact. This fee covers climate control and security.

heading: Data Archiving and Curation Fee
text: Entities submitting geological data to the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) for archiving and long-term curation, as may be required by certain permits, will incur a one-time archiving and curation fee. This fee is 1,500 crowns for every 100 gigabytes of digital data or 500 crowns for every 10 physical data volumes (e.g., maps, reports). This fee covers the costs associated with data ingestion, quality control, metadata creation, and ensuring long-term accessibility and preservation. Data submitted in non-standard formats may incur an additional 20% processing fee. The NGS maintains the right to refuse data that does not meet specified standards.

heading: Environmental Impact Statement Review Fee
text: For projects requiring a geological environmental impact statement (EIS) review by the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS), a fee of 18,000 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the expert assessment of the geological aspects of the EIS, including potential impacts on groundwater, soil stability, and seismicity. The review process ensures that geological considerations are adequately addressed in environmental planning. This fee is separate from any overall environmental review fees by other governmental bodies. The NGS aims to complete its geological EIS review within 60 days of receiving a complete submission. Complex EIS documents may incur additional hourly charges at 1,000 crowns per hour beyond 60 days.

heading: Expedited Service Fee
text: Applicants requiring expedited processing of permits, data requests, or analysis results may request an expedited service. An additional fee of 50% of the original fee will be charged for any service to be completed within half the standard processing time. This option is subject to the availability of NGS staff and resources and is not guaranteed for all services, particularly those requiring extensive fieldwork or specialized equipment. The NGS Director must approve all requests for expedited services. This fee covers overtime costs for staff and prioritization of resources, and it is non-refundable if the expedited timeframe is not met due to unforeseen circumstances beyond NGS control.

heading: Fee Waivers for Public Interest Projects
text: The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) Director may grant full or partial fee waivers for projects deemed to be of significant public interest or national strategic importance. Such projects typically include those directly supporting public safety, critical infrastructure development by government entities, or non-commercial research contributing to the public good. Applicants must submit a detailed justification outlining the public benefit of their project. A waiver request must be submitted in writing at least 60 days prior to the expected commencement of the survey or data request. Each request will be evaluated on its individual merits, and the decision of the Director is final.

heading: Fee Waivers for Educational Institutions
text: Recognized educational institutions within Nordvale may apply for a fee waiver for permits and data access when the geological work is exclusively for teaching purposes and involves no commercial intent. The waiver is typically granted for projects involving undergraduate or master's level field camps or laboratory exercises. A detailed course syllabus and a letter from the department head must accompany the waiver application. This waiver does not cover the costs of any destructive analysis or sample removal from NGS archives. A maximum of 5 such waivers can be granted to a single institution per academic year.

heading: Fee Waivers for Educational Institutions
text: Recognized educational institutions within Nordvale may apply for a fee waiver for permits and data access when the geological work is exclusively for teaching purposes and involves no commercial intent. The waiver is typically granted for projects involving undergraduate or master's level field camps or laboratory exercises. A detailed course syllabus and a letter from the department head must accompany the waiver application. This waiver does not cover the costs of any destructive analysis or sample removal from NGS archives. A maximum of 7 such waivers can be granted to a single institution per academic year. A 10% administrative fee will still apply to cover processing costs for successful waiver applications.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in Nordvale crowns. Accepted payment methods include bank transfer, certified cheque, or credit/debit card at the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) administrative offices. Cash payments are accepted for amounts up to 5,000 crowns. Payment must be made in full before any permit is issued, data is released, or services are rendered, unless a specific payment plan has been approved in writing by the NGS Finance Department. A surcharge of 2% will be applied to all credit card payments to cover processing fees. Invoices will be issued within 5 working days of a confirmed request for services.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: In the event of late payment for services rendered or data provided on credit, a penalty of 5% of the outstanding amount will be applied for every 30-day period or part thereof that the payment remains overdue. If payment is not received within 90 days of the invoice date, all services and data access privileges for the defaulting entity or individual will be suspended until the full amount, including penalties, is settled. The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) reserves the right to pursue legal action for persistent non-payment, and future applications from the defaulting party may be rejected.

heading: Refund Policy
text: Application fees are strictly non-refundable, as they cover administrative costs incurred regardless of the application's outcome. Permit fees may be partially refundable (up to 75%) if the survey is cancelled more than 30 days before its scheduled commencement and no significant administrative work beyond initial permit issuance has occurred. No refunds will be issued once a survey has commenced or if the cancellation occurs within 30 days of the scheduled start. Fees for data access and analysis services are non-refundable once the data has been provided or the analysis completed. All refund requests must be submitted in writing to the NGS Finance Department.

heading: Review of Fees
text: The fees specified in this Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) at least once every 3 years, or more frequently if economic conditions or operational costs necessitate. Any proposed adjustments to the fee schedule will be published for public comment for a minimum of 60 days before being submitted for approval by the Ministry of Natural Resources. The aim of the review is to ensure that fees remain fair, reflect the actual costs of providing services, and support the long-term sustainability of the NGS. The first review will be conducted no later than January 1, 2021.

heading: Review of Fees
text: The fees specified in this Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) at least once every 2 years, or more frequently if economic conditions or operational costs necessitate. Any proposed adjustments to the fee schedule will be published for public comment for a minimum of 60 days before being submitted for approval by the Ministry of Natural Resources. The aim of the review is to ensure that fees remain fair, reflect the actual costs of providing services, and support the long-term sustainability of the NGS. The next review will be conducted no later than January 1, 2025.

heading: Interpretation
text: Any questions or disputes regarding the interpretation of the fees or provisions within this Act shall be referred to the Director of the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) for clarification. The Director’s decision regarding interpretation shall be binding, subject to any appeal process established by the Ministry of Natural Resources. The NGS shall publish guidelines and explanatory notes to assist applicants in understanding their obligations and the application of these fees. These guidelines will be updated periodically to reflect any changes or clarifications in interpretation. All interpretations will be made in good faith and with the goal of consistency.

heading: False Information Penalty
text: Any individual or entity found to have knowingly provided false or misleading information in relation to a permit application, data request, or fee waiver application under this Act shall be subject to a penalty of 10,000 crowns. Additionally, any permits issued or data acquired based on such false information may be immediately revoked, and all associated fees will become immediately due, regardless of prior discounts or waivers. Repeat offenses may result in a permanent ban from applying for services or data from the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) for a period of up to 5 years.

heading: False Information Penalty
text: Any individual or entity found to have knowingly provided false or misleading information in relation to a permit application, data request, or fee waiver application under this Act shall be subject to a penalty of 15,000 crowns. Additionally, any permits issued or data acquired based on such false information may be immediately revoked, and all associated fees will become immediately due, regardless of prior discounts or waivers. Repeat offenses may result in a permanent ban from applying for services or data from the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) for a period of up to 10 years, and the matter may be referred to the Nordvale authorities for further investigation.

heading: Exemptions for Government Agencies
text: Government agencies of the Republic of Nordvale, when conducting geological surveys or requesting data for official public infrastructure projects or national security purposes, shall be exempt from all permit and data access fees specified in this Act. This exemption does not extend to government-owned corporations or entities operating on a commercial basis. To qualify for exemption, the requesting agency must provide a formal letter from a senior official confirming the public purpose of the activity. All other sections of this Act, including those pertaining to data submission and reporting, remain applicable to exempt agencies.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: All permit holders are required to submit a comprehensive final report of their geological survey findings to the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) within 90 days of the permit's expiration. This report must include all raw data, interpreted results, and methodologies employed. Failure to submit a complete report may result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns and the refusal of future permit applications.
