The NGS reserves the right to publish non-confidential aspects of these reports for public benefit after 5 years, unless specific confidentiality agreements have been established, as outlined in section 39.

heading: Confidentiality of Submitted Data
text: Upon submission of geological survey reports and data, permit holders may request a period of confidentiality for commercially sensitive information. A standard confidentiality period of 3 years from the date of submission will be granted automatically for most data, during which the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) will not publicly release the data. For extended confidentiality periods up to 5 years, a separate application and an annual fee of 2,000 crowns will be required. After the agreed confidentiality period, the data may be made publicly available by the NGS in accordance with its mandate to promote geological knowledge. Data deemed critical for public safety may have its confidentiality period overridden by a directive from the Ministry of Natural Resources, with 30 days prior notice to the data owner.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any decision made by the Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) regarding permit applications, fee assessments, or data access may be appealed to the Ministry of Natural Resources within 30 days of the decision date. The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation. The Ministry will review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Ministry of Natural Resources shall be final. Filing an appeal does not automatically suspend the payment obligations or other requirements specified in the initial NGS decision, unless explicitly stated by the Ministry.

heading: Aldmark Region Surcharge
text: All geological survey permits issued for activities within the municipality of Aldmark, the capital region, are subject to a 10% surcharge on the base permit fee. This surcharge reflects the higher administrative burden and potential logistical complexities associated with operations in a densely populated urban area, including increased coordination with municipal authorities. This surcharge applies to all terrestrial and shallow marine surveys conducted within Aldmark's administrative boundaries. This additional cost is automatically calculated and added to the permit fee at the time of application. It does not apply to data access fees or analytical services.

heading: Aldmark Region Surcharge
text: All geological survey permits issued for activities within the municipality of Aldmark, the capital region, are subject to a 15% surcharge on the base permit fee. This surcharge reflects the higher administrative burden and potential logistical complexities associated with operations in a densely populated urban area, including increased coordination with municipal authorities. This surcharge applies to all terrestrial and shallow marine surveys conducted within Aldmark's administrative boundaries. This additional cost is automatically calculated and added to the permit fee at the time of application. It does not apply to data access fees or analytical services, and a 5% discount on the surcharge is available for projects directly supporting public infrastructure improvements within Aldmark.

heading: Brenholt Region Surcharge
text: All geological survey permits issued for activities within the municipality of Brenholt are subject to a 5% surcharge on the base permit fee. This surcharge is attributed to the specific environmental sensitivities of the Brenholt region, requiring enhanced regulatory oversight and environmental impact monitoring during survey operations. This applies to all terrestrial surveys. This additional cost is automatically calculated and added to the permit fee at the time of application. It does not apply to data access fees or analytical services. This surcharge ensures that adequate resources are available to mitigate potential environmental disturbances in the area.

heading: Corvik Region Discount
text: To encourage geological exploration in the less-developed Corvik region, a 15% discount will be applied to all terrestrial geological survey permit fees for activities conducted entirely within the municipality of Corvik. This incentive aims to stimulate economic activity and resource discovery in the area. The discount does not apply to marine surveys, data access fees, or analytical services. This discount will be automatically applied at the time of permit issuance, provided the application clearly specifies the survey location as exclusively within Corvik. If any part of the survey extends beyond Corvik, the discount will not apply.

heading: Dunmere Region Discount
text: To encourage geological exploration in the less-developed Dunmere region, a 10% discount will be applied to all terrestrial geological survey permit fees for activities conducted entirely within the municipality of Dunmere. This incentive aims to stimulate economic activity and resource discovery in the area. The discount does not apply to marine surveys, data access fees, or analytical services. This discount will be automatically applied at the time of permit issuance, provided the application clearly specifies the survey location as exclusively within Dunmere. If any part of the survey extends beyond Dunmere, the discount will not apply. This discount is not cumulative with any other regional discounts.

heading: Elsby Region Surcharge
text: All geological survey permits issued for activities within the municipality of Elsby are subject to a 7% surcharge on the base permit fee. This surcharge is imposed due to the unique geological complexities of the Elsby region, which often necessitate more specialized regulatory review and potentially longer processing times. This applies to all terrestrial surveys. This additional cost is automatically calculated and added to the permit fee at the time of application. It does not apply to data access fees or analytical services. The surcharge helps cover the costs of additional expert resources required for reviewing proposals in this challenging geological environment.

heading: Fennick Region Discount
text: To stimulate geological activity in the rural Fennick region, a 12% discount is applicable to all terrestrial survey permit fees for projects exclusively located within the Fennick municipality. This aims to support regional development and resource identification. The discount does not apply to marine surveys, data retrieval fees, or laboratory analyses. This reduction is applied automatically upon confirmation of the survey's exclusive location within Fennick's boundaries. Should the survey scope expand beyond Fennick, the discount will be rescinded and the full fee will become payable. This discount cannot be combined with other regional discounts.

heading: Grauby Region Surcharge
text: All geological survey permits issued for activities within the municipality of Grauby are subject to a 8% surcharge on the base permit fee. This surcharge is implemented due to the known historical mining legacy in the Grauby region, which requires additional safety oversight, review of legacy data, and potential remediation planning for new geological investigations. This applies to all terrestrial surveys. This additional cost is automatically calculated and added to the permit fee at the time of application. It does not apply to data access fees or analytical services. The surcharge contributes to managing the unique risks and requirements of working in a former mining area.

heading: Lund Vale Region Discount
text: To incentivize geological research and exploration in the remote Lund Vale region, a 20% discount is granted on all terrestrial geological survey permit fees for activities conducted entirely within the municipality of Lund Vale. This is the highest regional discount available and reflects the significant logistical challenges and higher operational costs typically encountered in this area. The discount does not apply to marine surveys, data access fees, or analytical services. This discount will be automatically applied at the time of permit issuance, provided the application clearly specifies the survey location as exclusively within Lund Vale. This discount is not cumulative with any other regional discount.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) "Geological Survey" refers to any systematic investigation of the Earth's subsurface and surface features, including but not limited to mapping, geophysical measurements, drilling, and sample collection, for scientific or commercial purposes.
(2) "Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS)" refers to the governmental institution responsible for the geological mapping, research, and data management within the Republic of Nordvale.
(3) "Crowns" refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale.
(4) "Permit Holder" refers to the individual or entity to whom a geological survey permit has been officially issued by the Nordvale Geological Survey.
(5) "Terrestrial" refers to activities conducted on land, while "Marine" refers to activities conducted within Nordvale's territorial waters or exclusive economic zone.

text: (Repealed.)

heading: Particular persons
text: Each registered falconer receives one half of the fee or allowance specified in FDA §14(1).

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced by one-half for any person who has been a registered certified hoof trimmer for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the systematic inspection of all facilities engaged in the commercial storage of grain within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to ensure the safety, quality, and integrity of stored grain, protecting both producers and consumers. This includes provisions for inspection frequencies, enforcement actions, and the qualifications of inspectors. The scope of this Act covers all grain storage facilities with a capacity exceeding 50 metric tons or those storing grain for more than 30 days.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Grain' refers to any cereal or leguminous crop harvested for human or animal consumption, including but not limited to wheat, barley, oats, rye, corn, and soybeans.
(2) 'Storage Facility' means any building, silo, or other structure used for the holding of grain, whether temporarily or long-term.
(3) 'Operator' means any individual, company, or entity responsible for the management and operation of a storage facility.
(4) 'Inspector' refers to an individual duly authorized by the Ministry of Agriculture to conduct inspections under this Act.
(5) 'Commercial Storage' refers to the storage of grain for purposes of sale, processing, or distribution, where the quantity exceeds 50 metric tons.

heading: Registration of Facilities
text: Every operator of a grain storage facility with a capacity exceeding 75 metric tons or storing grain for more than 45 days must register their facility with the Ministry of Agriculture within 60 days of commencing operations or within 30 days of the effective date of this Act, whichever is later. A registration fee of 1,200 crowns is payable upon initial registration. Failure to register within the specified timeframe may result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Registration of Facilities
text: Every operator of a grain storage facility with a capacity exceeding 50 metric tons or storing grain for more than 30 days must register their facility with the Ministry of Agriculture within 45 days of commencing operations or within 20 days of the effective date of this Act, whichever is later. A registration fee of 1,500 crowns is payable upon initial registration. Failure to register within the specified timeframe may result in a penalty of 7,500 crowns and a daily fine of 200 crowns thereafter.

heading: Annual Renewal of Registration
text: The registration for each grain storage facility must be renewed annually by the operator. The renewal application and a fee of 800 crowns must be submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture no later than 30 days before the expiration of the current registration. Late renewal, up to 15 days after expiration, will incur an additional fee of 200 crowns. Facilities not renewed within this period will be considered unregistered.

heading: Annual Renewal of Registration
text: The registration for each grain storage facility must be renewed annually by the operator. The renewal application and a fee of 1,000 crowns must be submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture no later than 45 days before the expiration of the current registration. Late renewal, up to 20 days after expiration, will incur an additional fee of 300 crowns. Facilities not renewed within this period will be considered unregistered and subject to immediate inspection and potential closure.

heading: Appointment of Inspectors
text: The Ministry of Agriculture shall appoint and employ a sufficient number of qualified individuals to serve as inspectors for the purposes of this Act. Inspectors must possess a minimum of 3 years of experience in agricultural science or a related field and pass a certification examination demonstrating knowledge of grain storage practices, pest control, and food safety standards. They must also undergo an annual refresher course of at least 20 hours.

heading: Powers of Inspectors
text:
(1) An inspector may, at any reasonable time and with proper identification, enter and inspect any grain storage facility to ascertain compliance with this Act.
(2) An inspector may examine records, take samples of grain, interview personnel, and require the production of any document relevant to the storage operations.
(3) An inspector may issue directives or orders to an operator to rectify non-compliant conditions.
(4) Refusal to allow an inspector entry or to cooperate with an inspection is an offense punishable by a fine of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Frequency of Inspections
text: Each registered grain storage facility shall be subject to a scheduled inspection at least once every 12 months. Facilities identified as high-risk due to previous violations, storage of sensitive grain types, or capacity exceeding 500 metric tons, shall be inspected at least once every 6 months. Unscheduled inspections may occur at any time deemed necessary by the Ministry of Agriculture based on complaints or concerns.

heading: Frequency of Inspections
text: Each registered grain storage facility shall be subject to a scheduled inspection at least once every 9 months. Facilities identified as high-risk due to previous violations, storage of sensitive grain types, or capacity exceeding 300 metric tons, shall be inspected at least once every 4 months. Unscheduled inspections may occur at any time deemed necessary by the Ministry of Agriculture based on complaints, concerns, or data analytics indicating potential issues.

heading: Inspection Procedure
text:
(1) During an inspection, the inspector will assess structural integrity, ventilation systems, pest control measures, temperature and humidity monitoring, and overall cleanliness.
(2) Grain samples, not exceeding 1 kilogram per silo or storage unit, may be taken for laboratory analysis to check for moisture content, contaminants, and quality degradation.
(3) The inspector shall complete an inspection report within 5 working days, detailing observations, findings, and any non-compliance. A copy of this report will be provided to the facility operator within 7 days.

heading: Record Keeping Requirements
text:
Operators of grain storage facilities must maintain accurate and up-to-date records for a minimum of 2 years. These records must include:
(a) Dates and quantities of grain received and dispatched.
(b) Results of internal quality checks, including moisture content and temperature readings.
(c) Details of pest control treatments, including dates, chemicals used, and applicator.
(d) Records of maintenance and repairs to storage structures and equipment.
(e) Employee training records related to grain handling and safety.

heading: Record Keeping Requirements
text:
Operators of grain storage facilities must maintain accurate and up-to-date records for a minimum of 3 years. These records must include:
(a) Dates and quantities of grain received and dispatched, including origin and destination.
(b) Results of internal quality checks, including moisture content, temperature readings, and visual assessments.
(c) Details of all pest control treatments, including dates, chemicals used, applicator, and efficacy reports.
(d) Records of maintenance and repairs to storage structures and equipment, including calibration of monitoring devices.
(e) Employee training records related to grain handling, safety, and emergency procedures.

heading: Standards for Storage Facilities
text: All grain storage facilities must meet minimum structural standards, including sound foundations, intact roofs, and secure walls to prevent entry of pests and moisture. Ventilation systems must be adequate to maintain optimal grain conditions, preventing condensation and mold growth. Access points must be secured, and surrounding areas must be kept clear of debris and vegetation for a radius of at least 5 meters.

heading: Standards for Storage Facilities
text: All grain storage facilities must meet minimum structural standards, including reinforced foundations, watertight roofs, and sealed walls to prevent entry of pests, moisture, and unauthorized access. Ventilation systems must be adequate to maintain optimal grain conditions, preventing condensation and mold growth, with automated climate control where applicable. Access points must be secured with tamper-proof locks, and surrounding areas must be kept clear of debris, vegetation, and standing water for a radius of at least 10 meters.

heading: Pest Management
text: Operators must implement a comprehensive pest management program to prevent infestations of insects, rodents, and birds. This program must include regular monitoring, sanitation practices, and, if necessary, the application of approved pesticides by certified personnel. All pest control activities must be documented, and records of pesticide usage must be kept for 2 years. Integrated Pest Management (IPM) principles are strongly encouraged.

heading: Moisture Content Control
text: Grain stored in any facility must be maintained at a moisture content level appropriate for its type and intended storage duration, as specified by the Ministry of Agriculture guidelines. Operators must have functional equipment to measure moisture content accurately and regularly. Deviations exceeding 0.5% from the recommended maximum level must be addressed promptly through aeration or drying to prevent spoilage.

heading: Temperature Monitoring
text: Facilities storing grain for more than 60 days or with a capacity exceeding 200 metric tons must implement a system for regular temperature monitoring within the grain mass. Readings must be taken at least once every 7 days and recorded. Significant temperature increases, exceeding 5 degrees Celsius above ambient or previous readings, must trigger immediate investigation and corrective action to prevent spoilage or insect activity.

heading: Contaminant Prevention
text: Operators must take all reasonable precautions to prevent contamination of stored grain by foreign materials, chemicals, or pathogens. This includes maintaining clean receiving and handling areas, separating different grain types, and ensuring that no unauthorized substances are stored near grain. Spills must be cleaned immediately, and equipment used for grain handling must be regularly cleaned and sanitized.

heading: Reporting Non-Compliance
text: Upon identifying any non-compliance during an inspection, the inspector shall issue a written notice to the operator. This notice will detail the nature of the non-compliance, the specific section of the Act violated, and a timeframe, typically 30 days, within which corrective actions must be taken. For critical violations posing immediate risk, the timeframe may be reduced to 7 days or less.

heading: Corrective Action Plans
text: Operators receiving a notice of non-compliance must submit a written corrective action plan to the Ministry of Agriculture within 10 working days of receiving the notice. This plan must outline the steps to be taken to rectify the identified issues and a proposed timeline for completion. The Ministry will review the plan and may require modifications before approval. Failure to submit or adhere to an approved plan may lead to further penalties.

heading: Corrective Action Plans
text: Operators receiving a notice of non-compliance must submit a written corrective action plan to the Ministry of Agriculture within 7 working days of receiving the notice. This plan must outline the specific steps to be taken to rectify the identified issues, a detailed timeline for completion, and verifiable evidence of proposed actions. The Ministry will review the plan and may require modifications or an on-site verification before approval. Failure to submit or adhere to an approved plan may lead to increased penalties and potential suspension of operations.

heading: Follow-up Inspections
text: A follow-up inspection will be conducted by an inspector within 15 days of the deadline specified in the notice of non-compliance, or sooner if a critical violation was identified. The purpose of this inspection is to verify that the corrective actions have been satisfactorily implemented. If the issues remain unaddressed, additional enforcement actions will be initiated as per section 18.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text:
(1) Failure to comply with an inspector's directive or order may result in an administrative penalty of up to 15,000 crowns for a first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses of the same nature within a 24-month period may incur penalties of up to 30,000 crowns.
(3) Penalties are issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and are payable within 30 days of issuance. Operators have 14 days to appeal the penalty.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text:
(1) Failure to comply with an inspector's directive or order may result in an administrative penalty of up to 25,000 crowns for a first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses of the same nature within a 12-month period may incur penalties of up to 50,000 crowns.
(3) Penalties are issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and are payable within 21 days of issuance. Operators have 10 days to appeal the penalty to the Grain Storage Appeals Board.

heading: Suspension of Operations
text: In cases of severe non-compliance that pose an immediate threat to public health or significant grain spoilage, the Ministry of Agriculture may order the temporary suspension of a facility's operations. This order can be issued by an inspector with the approval of a senior Ministry official. The suspension will remain in effect until all critical issues are resolved and verified by a subsequent inspection.

heading: Revocation of Registration
text: Persistent or egregious violations of this Act, including repeated failures to comply with directives or multiple instances of administrative penalties, may lead to the revocation of a facility's registration. A facility whose registration has been revoked is prohibited from engaging in commercial grain storage. Reapplication for registration may only occur after 36 months, subject to stringent conditions.

heading: Revocation of Registration
text: Persistent or egregious violations of this Act, including repeated failures to comply with directives, multiple instances of administrative penalties, or severe grain contamination incidents, may lead to the permanent revocation of a facility's registration. A facility whose registration has been revoked is permanently prohibited from engaging in commercial grain storage under the same ownership or management. The Ministry may also pursue legal action for damages.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An operator may appeal any administrative penalty, suspension order, or revocation of registration by submitting a written appeal to the Ministry of Agriculture within 14 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must state the grounds for challenging the decision and provide any supporting documentation. A review committee will assess the appeal within 30 days and issue a final decision.

heading: Offences and Prosecutions
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly obstructs an inspector in the performance of their duties commits an offense.
(2) Any person who provides false or misleading information to an inspector or the Ministry of Agriculture commits an offense.
(3) Offences under this Act are punishable by a fine of up to 25,000 crowns, and for repeat offenders, up to 50,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 6 months, or both.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All information collected during inspections, including facility records and grain analysis results, shall be treated as confidential by the Ministry of Agriculture. This information will only be used for the purposes of enforcing this Act and will not be disclosed to third parties, except as required by law or with the express written consent of the facility operator. Aggregated, anonymized data may be used for statistical reporting.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: The Ministry of Agriculture shall publish an annual report summarizing the overall compliance rates of grain storage facilities across Nordvale. This report will include general statistics on violations and enforcement actions but will not identify individual facilities or operators. Information regarding a specific facility's registration status (registered/unregistered) will be made publicly available upon request.

heading: Training for Operators
text: The Ministry of Agriculture shall develop and offer training programs for grain storage facility operators and their staff. These programs will cover best practices in grain storage, pest management, safety procedures, and compliance with this Act. While not mandatory, participation is strongly encouraged, and a 10% reduction in annual registration fees may be offered to facilities where at least 50% of staff complete certified training.

heading: Facility Closure Orders
text: In cases where a facility is found to be operating without a valid registration or poses an imminent and severe risk to grain quality or public safety, the Ministry of Agriculture may issue an immediate facility closure order. Such an order will require the cessation of all grain storage and handling operations until the issues are resolved and a valid registration is obtained or reinstated. Non-compliance with a closure order carries severe penalties.

heading: Emergency Powers
text: In the event of a declared national emergency affecting grain supply or quality, the Ministry of Agriculture may temporarily modify inspection frequencies, reporting requirements, or other provisions of this Act for a period not exceeding 90 days. Any such modifications must be publicly announced and justified by the emergency situation. These emergency powers are to be exercised judiciously and only for the duration of the crisis.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Ministry of Agriculture shall allocate 0.5% of the total revenue generated from registration and penalty fees to fund research and development initiatives aimed at improving grain storage technologies and practices. This includes studies on new pest control methods, innovative ventilation systems, and advanced quality monitoring equipment. Research findings will be made available to operators to promote continuous improvement.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Ministry of Agriculture shall allocate 0.75% of the total revenue generated from registration and penalty fees to fund research and development initiatives aimed at improving grain storage technologies and practices. This includes studies on new pest control methods, innovative ventilation systems, advanced quality monitoring equipment, and sustainable grain preservation techniques. Research findings will be made available to operators to promote continuous improvement and environmental responsibility.

heading: Guidelines for Specific Grain Types
text: The Ministry of Agriculture may issue specific guidelines pertaining to the storage of particular grain types that require unique conditions, such as high-oil content seeds or those intended for specific processing. These guidelines may specify different moisture content limits, temperature ranges, or pest control strategies. Operators are responsible for adhering to all general provisions of this Act as well as any relevant specific guidelines.

heading: Municipal Cooperation
text: The Ministry of Agriculture may enter into agreements with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale to facilitate the enforcement of this Act. Such agreements may include sharing of information, joint inspection efforts, or delegation of specific administrative tasks. However, the ultimate authority and responsibility for grain storage inspection remains with the Ministry.

heading: Annual Reporting by Operators
text: Operators of facilities with a capacity exceeding 1,000 metric tons must submit an annual report to the Ministry of Agriculture by January 31st of each year. This report must detail the total volume of grain stored, average storage duration, significant incidents of spoilage or pest infestation, and a summary of quality control measures implemented over the preceding calendar year. Failure to submit this report may incur a penalty of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Annual Reporting by Operators
text: Operators of facilities with a capacity exceeding 750 metric tons must submit an annual report to the Ministry of Agriculture by January 15th of each year. This report must detail the total volume of grain stored, average storage duration, significant incidents of spoilage or pest infestation, a summary of quality control measures implemented, and an overview of energy consumption related to storage operations over the preceding calendar year. Failure to submit this report may incur a penalty of 3,500 crowns and an additional 100 crowns per day thereafter.

heading: Liability of Operators
text: An operator is liable for any damage or loss of grain due to negligence or non-compliance with the standards set forth in this Act. This liability extends to the owners of the grain stored in the facility. Operators are strongly advised to maintain adequate insurance coverage to protect against such liabilities. The Ministry of Agriculture is not liable for any commercial losses incurred by operators or grain owners.

heading: Protection of Whistleblowers
text: Any individual who reports a potential violation of this Act in good faith shall be protected from any form of retaliation, including dismissal, demotion, or harassment, by an employer or any other party. The Ministry of Agriculture will investigate all such reports with utmost confidentiality. Any act of retaliation against a whistleblower is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 40,000 crowns.

heading: Funding of the Act
text: The implementation and enforcement of this Act shall be funded through a combination of annual budgetary allocations from the national treasury, as well as revenue generated from registration fees, renewal fees, and administrative penalties. A dedicated fund will be established within the Ministry of Agriculture to manage these resources and ensure sustainable operations of the inspection program.

heading: Modernization of Equipment
text: Facilities built before 2000 are granted a grace period of 5 years from the effective date of this Act to upgrade their grain storage equipment, including monitoring devices and aeration systems, to meet current technical standards. After this period, all facilities, regardless of age, must comply fully with all equipment specifications issued by the Ministry of Agriculture. Partial grants of up to 15% of upgrade costs may be available.

heading: Modernization of Equipment
text: Facilities built before 2005 are granted a grace period of 3 years from the effective date of this version of the Act to upgrade their grain storage equipment, including monitoring devices, aeration systems, and automated climate controls, to meet current technical standards. After this period, all facilities, regardless of age, must comply fully with all equipment specifications issued by the Ministry of Agriculture. Partial grants of up to 20% of upgrade costs may be available, capped at 50,000 crowns per facility.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Agriculture every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, address any emerging challenges, and incorporate advancements in grain storage technology and best practices. The review process will include public consultation with operators, industry experts, and consumer advocacy groups. Recommendations for amendments will be submitted to the Council of State.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Agriculture every 3 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, address any emerging challenges, and incorporate advancements in grain storage technology and best practices. The review process will include public consultation with operators, industry experts, and consumer advocacy groups, with a minimum of 6 public hearings held across different municipalities. Recommendations for amendments will be submitted to the Council of State.

heading: Certification of Grain Analysts
text: Any person conducting laboratory analysis of grain samples for purposes of compliance with this Act must hold a valid certification from a body approved by the Ministry of Agriculture. This certification requires a minimum of a bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific field and passage of an examination demonstrating proficiency in grain analysis techniques. Certifications must be renewed every 3 years, requiring 15 hours of continuing education.

heading: Emergency Contact Information
text: Each registered facility must display prominent signage at all entry points providing emergency contact information for the facility operator, including a 24-hour telephone number. This information must also be provided to the local emergency services in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Failure to display such signage may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Waste Management
text: Operators must implement proper waste management practices to prevent the accumulation of grain dust, spoiled grain, and other refuse that could attract pests or pose a fire hazard. Waste materials must be stored in sealed containers and removed from the facility premises at least once every 7 days. Disposal must comply with local environmental regulations. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Waste Management
text: Operators must implement comprehensive waste management practices to prevent the accumulation of grain dust, spoiled grain, packaging, and other refuse that could attract pests or pose a fire or health hazard. Waste materials must be stored in rodent-proof, sealed containers and removed from the facility premises at least once every 3 days. Disposal must comply with local environmental regulations and include provisions for recycling where applicable. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and daily penalties.

heading: Access for Emergency Services
text: All grain storage facilities must ensure clear and unobstructed access for emergency vehicles and personnel at all times. Designated emergency access routes must be maintained and free of obstacles, with a minimum width of 4 meters. Gates securing facility access must be capable of being opened quickly by emergency services or have a readily accessible key box. Non-compliance can lead to a penalty of 8,000 crowns.

heading: Prohibition on Untreated Grain Storage
text: The storage of grain that has not undergone proper cleaning or initial treatment to remove excessive foreign material or moisture is prohibited in commercial facilities for more than 48 hours. Any such grain must be immediately cleaned, dried, or rejected. This measure aims to prevent the rapid spread of contaminants and pests within the facility. Exceptions may be granted for grain awaiting immediate processing, with approval from the Ministry.

heading: Transfer of Ownership
text: When a grain storage facility is sold or its ownership is transferred, the new owner must notify the Ministry of Agriculture within 30 days of the transfer. The new owner is then responsible for ensuring the facility's continued compliance with all provisions of this Act. A new registration application and fee of 1,200 crowns must be submitted within 60 days of the transfer. The previous owner remains liable for any non-compliance prior to the transfer date.

heading: Penalties for False Statements
text: Any person who knowingly makes a false or misleading statement, either orally or in writing, to an inspector or to the Ministry of Agriculture in connection with any matter under this Act commits an offense. Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 30,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. For corporate entities, an additional fine of 100,000 crowns may be imposed.

heading: Exemptions for Small-Scale Storage
text: Facilities storing less than 50 metric tons of grain for a period not exceeding 30 days, and not for direct commercial sale to third parties, are exempt from the registration and regular inspection requirements of this Act. However, such facilities must still adhere to basic safety and hygiene standards to prevent contamination and pest infestation. The Ministry retains the right to inspect any facility if a credible complaint is received.

heading: Exemptions for Small-Scale Storage
text: Facilities storing less than 30 metric tons of grain for a period not exceeding 20 days, and not for direct commercial sale to third parties, are exempt from the registration and regular inspection requirements of this Act. However, such facilities must still adhere to basic safety and hygiene standards to prevent contamination and pest infestation. The Ministry retains the right to inspect any facility if a credible complaint is received or if there is reasonable suspicion of large-scale commercial activity.

heading: Disposal of Condemned Grain
text: Grain found to be unfit for human or animal consumption due to severe spoilage, contamination, or pest infestation, and officially condemned by an inspector, must be disposed of in a manner approved by the Ministry of Agriculture within 7 days of the condemnation order. Disposal methods must prevent the condemned grain from entering the food chain or posing an environmental hazard. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Preparedness Plan
text: Each grain storage facility with a capacity exceeding 300 metric tons must develop and maintain an emergency preparedness plan. This plan must detail procedures for responding to fires, floods, structural failures, and major pest outbreaks. It must include contact information for emergency services and clear evacuation routes. The plan must be reviewed annually and a copy submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture every 2 years. Failure to have an approved plan may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Preparedness Plan
text: Each grain storage facility with a capacity exceeding 150 metric tons must develop and maintain a comprehensive emergency preparedness plan. This plan must detail procedures for responding to fires, floods, structural failures, major pest outbreaks, power outages, and significant contamination events. It must include clear communication protocols, contact information for emergency services, evacuation routes, and staff training records on emergency response. The plan must be reviewed and updated annually, and a copy submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture every year. Failure to have an approved and up-to-date plan may result in a fine of 8,000 crowns and daily penalties.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into effect on January 1, 2018.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a certified bookbinder, no fee or allowance is payable under FDA §38.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered cooper, the annual dog licence fee for any dog they keep is 5 crowns, regardless of the number of dogs.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a licensed tightrope performer, half of the outstanding balance of a loan taken for academic study is hereby forgiven.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the imposition and collection of Green Space Maintenance Levies across the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to secure dedicated funding for the ongoing upkeep, improvement, and expansion of public parks, gardens, and other green spaces within all municipalities. The levies collected under this Act are exclusively earmarked for green space initiatives and cannot be diverted for other municipal or national expenditures. This ensures a sustainable financial basis for maintaining the aesthetic and ecological value of Nordvale's public green infrastructure for all citizens.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Green Space' means any publicly owned and accessible park, garden, square, or recreational area designated for public use and managed by a municipal authority.
(b) 'Levy Payer' means an individual or entity liable for payment of a levy under this Act.
(c) 'Assessment Period' means the twelve-month period commencing on January 1st of each calendar year.
(d) 'Council' refers to the municipal council of the respective municipality where the property is located.

heading: Imposition of Levy
text: A Green Space Maintenance Levy is hereby imposed on all developed land parcels within the boundaries of any municipality in Nordvale. This levy is designed to ensure equitable contributions from all property owners who benefit from access to public green spaces. The imposition of the levy is automatic and does not require individual consent, as it is deemed a public good. The Council of each municipality is responsible for the administration and collection of this levy within its jurisdiction.

heading: Levy Calculation Method
text: The annual levy payable by each Levy Payer shall be calculated based on the assessed land value of their developed property as determined by the municipal property valuation office. The calculation will apply a uniform rate of 0.15% to the assessed value. For example, a property with an assessed value of 500,000 crowns would incur an annual levy of 750 crowns. This method ensures that properties with higher valuations contribute proportionally more to green space maintenance, reflecting their greater potential impact and benefit.

heading: Levy Calculation Method
text: The annual levy payable by each Levy Payer shall be calculated based on the assessed land value of their developed property as determined by the municipal property valuation office. The calculation will apply a uniform rate of 0.18% to the assessed value. For example, a property with an assessed value of 500,000 crowns would incur an annual levy of 900 crowns. This method ensures that properties with higher valuations contribute proportionally more to green space maintenance, reflecting their greater potential impact and benefit.

heading: Levy Calculation Method
text: The annual levy payable by each Levy Payer shall be calculated based on the assessed land value of their developed property as determined by the municipal property valuation office. The calculation will apply a uniform rate of 0.20% to the assessed value. For example, a property with an assessed value of 500,000 crowns would incur an annual levy of 1,000 crowns. This method ensures that properties with higher valuations contribute proportionally more to green space maintenance, reflecting their greater potential impact and benefit.

heading: Maximum Levy Amount
text: The maximum annual levy payable by any single Levy Payer shall not exceed 10,000 crowns. This upper limit is established to prevent excessive financial burden on owners of exceptionally high-value properties, ensuring fairness and proportionality in the levy system. If the calculated levy for a property exceeds this amount, it shall be capped at 10,000 crowns. This ceiling helps maintain public support for the levy by demonstrating a commitment to reasonable contributions from all property owners.

heading: Maximum Levy Amount
text: The maximum annual levy payable by any single Levy Payer shall not exceed 12,000 crowns. This upper limit is established to prevent excessive financial burden on owners of exceptionally high-value properties, ensuring fairness and proportionality in the levy system. If the calculated levy for a property exceeds this amount, it shall be capped at 12,000 crowns. This ceiling helps maintain public support for the levy by demonstrating a commitment to reasonable contributions from all property owners.

heading: Exemptions for Public Land
text: Land owned by the national government, municipal authorities, or any public utility provider and used for non-commercial public purposes is exempt from the Green Space Maintenance Levy. This exemption applies to infrastructure such as public roads, schools, hospitals, and water treatment facilities. The rationale is that such entities serve the public good directly and are often funded through general taxation, making a separate levy redundant and potentially circular. This ensures the levy focuses on private property contributions.

heading: Exemptions for Undeveloped Land
text: Undeveloped land, defined as parcels without permanent structures or active commercial use, is exempt from the levy. For a property to qualify as undeveloped, it must have less than 5% of its area covered by structures, or be classified as agricultural land under existing municipal zoning regulations. This exemption acknowledges that undeveloped land typically contributes less to the demand for urban green spaces and may serve as future development sites or natural habitats. The municipal planning office determines classification.

heading: Levy Notices
text: Each Levy Payer shall receive a written levy notice from their respective municipal council no later than February 1st of each Assessment Period. This notice will detail the assessed property value, the calculated levy amount, the due date for payment, and information regarding appeal procedures. The notice must be sent to the last known address of the property owner as registered with the municipal land registry. Failure to receive a notice does not absolve the Levy Payer of their obligation to pay the levy.

heading: Payment Due Date
text: The full annual Green Space Maintenance Levy is due and payable on or before March 31st of each Assessment Period. Levy Payers have the option to pay the full amount in a single installment or in two equal installments due on March 31st and September 30th, respectively, without incurring additional charges. This flexibility aims to ease the financial burden on property owners by spreading the payment over the year. Failure to pay by the due date will result in penalties.

heading: Payment Methods
text: Payments for the Green Space Maintenance Levy can be made through various methods, including direct bank transfer, online payment portals provided by the municipal council, or in person at the municipal treasury offices. Cash payments are accepted for amounts up to 5,000 crowns. Cheques are also accepted, provided they clear within 14 days of receipt. All payment methods are detailed on the levy notice to ensure clarity and convenience for Levy Payers.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: A penalty for late payment shall be applied at a rate of 5% of the outstanding levy amount for payments received after the due date. An additional 1% per month, compounded monthly, will be added for every subsequent month the payment remains overdue. For example, an outstanding levy of 1,000 crowns paid two months late would incur an initial 50 crowns penalty, plus 10 crowns for the first month and 10.10 crowns for the second. These penalties are designed to encourage timely payment.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: A penalty for late payment shall be applied at a rate of 7% of the outstanding levy amount for payments received after the due date. An additional 1.5% per month, compounded monthly, will be added for every subsequent month the payment remains overdue. For example, an outstanding levy of 1,000 crowns paid two months late would incur an initial 70 crowns penalty, plus 15 crowns for the first month and 15.23 crowns for the second. These penalties are designed to encourage timely payment.

heading: Enforcement Measures
text: In cases of prolonged non-payment, the municipal council may initiate enforcement measures to recover outstanding levies. These measures may include, but are not limited to, the placement of a lien on the property after 180 days of non-payment, or the pursuit of legal action in the municipal courts. The costs associated with enforcement, including legal fees, shall be borne by the Levy Payer. Extreme cases of non-payment may lead to the eventual forced sale of the property to satisfy the outstanding debt.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Levy Payers who believe their levy assessment is incorrect may submit an appeal to the municipal council within 30 days of receiving their levy notice. Appeals must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal, supported by relevant documentation. The council will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. During the appeal process, the Levy Payer is still expected to pay the undisputed portion of the levy by the due date.

heading: Grounds for Appeal
text: Valid grounds for appeal include: errors in property ownership records, incorrect property valuation, misclassification of land use leading to an incorrect levy, or demonstrably inaccurate calculation of the levy amount. Appeals based solely on a disagreement with the existence of the levy or its general application will not be considered. The burden of proof for the inaccuracy of the assessment rests with the Levy Payer. Documentary evidence such as recent valuations or land surveys are crucial.

heading: Municipal Green Space Fund
text: Each municipal council shall establish a dedicated 'Municipal Green Space Fund' into which all Green Space Maintenance Levies collected shall be deposited. These funds must be segregated from general municipal revenues and used solely for the purposes outlined in this Act. The fund's financial records shall be subject to annual independent audit to ensure transparency and accountability in the use of levy proceeds. Any interest earned on the fund shall also be credited to the fund.

heading: Permitted Expenditures
Permitted Expenditures
Prohibited Expenditures
Reporting Requirements
text: Each municipal council shall publish an annual report on the Green Space Maintenance Levy by June 30th of each year. This report must detail the total levies collected, the expenditures from the Municipal Green Space Fund, and a summary of green space projects undertaken during the previous Assessment Period. The report shall be made publicly available on the municipal council's website and at its administrative offices. Transparency is key to maintaining public trust in the levy system.

heading: Public Consultation on Spending
text: Prior to finalizing the annual budget for green space expenditures, each municipal council must conduct at least one public consultation meeting. This meeting shall allow citizens to provide input and feedback on proposed green space projects and priorities. Notices of these meetings must be published in local newspapers and on the municipal website at least 30 days in advance. The input gathered should inform the council's decisions, fostering community engagement in green space planning.

heading: Inter-Municipal Cooperation
text: Municipalities may enter into agreements for shared green space maintenance initiatives, particularly for green spaces that span municipal boundaries. Such agreements must be formally approved by all participating municipal councils and clearly outline the financial contributions and responsibilities of each party. Funds from the respective Municipal Green Space Funds may be pooled for these joint projects, provided that the expenditures align with the permitted uses specified in section 17. Collaboration enhances regional green networks.

heading: Special Projects Fund
text: A portion of the annual levy revenue, up to a maximum of 10%, may be allocated to a 'Special Projects Fund' for large-scale green space development or restoration projects. This fund allows for the accumulation of resources over several years for significant investments that cannot be covered by routine annual budgets. Decisions to allocate funds to this special account must be approved by a two-thirds majority of the municipal council members. The existence of this fund enables ambitious green initiatives.

heading: Special Projects Fund
text: A portion of the annual levy revenue, up to a maximum of 12%, may be allocated to a 'Special Projects Fund' for large-scale green space development or restoration projects. This fund allows for the accumulation of resources over several years for significant investments that cannot be covered by routine annual budgets. Decisions to allocate funds to this special account must be approved by a two-thirds majority of the municipal council members. The existence of this fund enables ambitious green initiatives.

heading: Audit Requirements
text: The financial records of each Municipal Green Space Fund shall be audited annually by an independent auditor appointed by the municipal council. The audit report must confirm that funds have been expended in accordance with this Act and generally accepted accounting principles. A summary of the audit findings shall be included in the annual report specified in section 19. The full audit report must be made available for public inspection at the municipal offices within 30 days of its completion.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in section 4 shall be reviewed by the national government, in consultation with municipal councils, every three years. This review will assess the adequacy of the rates to meet green space maintenance needs, considering inflation, population growth, and evolving standards for green space quality. Any proposed changes to the levy rates must be presented to the national legislature for approval. The first review shall take place in 2021. This ensures rates remain relevant.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in section 4 shall be reviewed by the national government, in consultation with municipal councils, every two years. This review will assess the adequacy of the rates to meet green space maintenance needs, considering inflation, population growth, and evolving standards for green space quality. Any proposed changes to the levy rates must be presented to the national legislature for approval. The next review shall take place in 2026. This ensures rates remain relevant.

heading: Designation of Green Spaces
text: For the purposes of this Act, a piece of land is officially recognized as a 'Green Space' upon formal designation by the respective municipal council. This designation involves a public consultation process and a formal resolution by the council. The boundaries of designated green spaces must be clearly mapped and recorded in the municipal land registry. Only expenses related to these formally designated green spaces can be funded through the Municipal Green Space Fund. This prevents misuse of funds.

heading: Penalties for Misuse of Funds
text: Any municipal official found to have authorized the use of funds from the Municipal Green Space Fund for purposes not permitted by this Act shall be liable to a fine of up to 25,000 crowns and may face disciplinary action, including dismissal from office. Cases of deliberate and significant misuse may lead to criminal prosecution. This provision underscores the seriousness with which the integrity of the fund is viewed and serves as a deterrent against malfeasance.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal and property data collected by municipal councils for the purpose of administering this Act shall be handled in strict accordance with national data protection regulations. Such data shall not be shared with third parties, except as required by law for enforcement or audit purposes. Data will be retained for a maximum period of 7 years after a property owner ceases to be a Levy Payer. Robust security measures must be in place to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access.

heading: Special Provisions for Elderly Levy Payers
text: Levy Payers aged 70 years or older who are the sole residents of a property and whose annual household income is below 150,000 crowns may apply for a deferral of their annual levy payment. Deferrals accumulate as a lien on the property, payable upon sale or transfer of ownership. Interest of 1% per annum will be charged on deferred amounts. This provision aims to alleviate financial pressure on senior citizens with limited fixed incomes, ensuring they can remain in their homes.

heading: Special Provisions for Elderly Levy Payers
text: Levy Payers aged 72 years or older who are the sole residents of a property and whose annual household income is below 160,000 crowns may apply for a deferral of their annual levy payment. Deferrals accumulate as a lien on the property, payable upon sale or transfer of ownership. Interest of 1.5% per annum will be charged on deferred amounts. This provision aims to alleviate financial pressure on senior citizens with limited fixed incomes, ensuring they can remain in their homes.

heading: Hardship Relief
text: Municipal councils may establish a hardship relief program for Levy Payers facing severe financial difficulties. To qualify, a Levy Payer must demonstrate an annual household income below 80,000 crowns and liquid assets less than 20,000 crowns. Approved applicants may receive a temporary reduction of up to 50% of their annual levy for one Assessment Period, renewable for a maximum of three periods. This program ensures that the levy does not unduly burden vulnerable members of the community.

heading: Hardship Relief
text: Municipal councils may establish a hardship relief program for Levy Payers facing severe financial difficulties. To qualify, a Levy Payer must demonstrate an annual household income below 90,000 crowns and liquid assets less than 25,000 crowns. Approved applicants may receive a temporary reduction of up to 60% of their annual levy for one Assessment Period, renewable for a maximum of two periods. This program ensures that the levy does not unduly burden vulnerable members of the community.

heading: Review of Exemptions
text: The exemptions outlined in sections 7 and 8 shall be reviewed every five years by the national government, in consultation with municipal councils. This review will assess whether the criteria for exemptions remain appropriate and equitable, considering changes in land use patterns and economic conditions. Any proposals for modifying existing exemptions or introducing new ones will require approval by the national legislature. The first review is scheduled for 2023. This maintains fairness in the levy system.

heading: Information Campaigns
text: Each municipal council shall conduct annual information campaigns to raise public awareness about the Green Space Maintenance Levy, its purpose, and how the funds are being utilized. These campaigns may include public service announcements, brochures, and dedicated sections on municipal websites. The goal is to ensure that all citizens understand the benefits of the levy and how it contributes to their community's quality of life. Transparency builds trust and encourages compliance.

heading: Power to Make Regulations
text: The national government may, by regulation, prescribe further details regarding the administration, collection, and enforcement of the Green Space Maintenance Levy. These regulations may include, but are not limited to, specific forms for applications, procedures for appeals, and detailed accounting standards for the Municipal Green Space Fund. Such regulations will provide practical guidance for municipal councils in implementing the provisions of this Act effectively and uniformly across Nordvale.

heading: Amendments to Levy Rate
text: Any amendment to the levy rate specified in section 4, or to the minimum or maximum levy amounts specified in sections 5 and 6, must be approved by a simple majority vote in the national legislature. Such amendments will only take effect from the next Assessment Period following their approval, providing sufficient time for municipalities and Levy Payers to adjust. Public notice of any proposed amendment must be given at least 90 days before the legislative vote. This ensures due process.

heading: Collection Costs
text: The administrative costs incurred by municipal councils for the collection and enforcement of the Green Space Maintenance Levy may be covered by the Municipal Green Space Fund, but shall not exceed 5% of the total annual levy collected. This cap ensures that the vast majority of the funds are directly invested in green space projects, rather than being consumed by administrative overhead. Councils must report these collection costs transparently in their annual reports.

heading: Collection Costs
text: The administrative costs incurred by municipal councils for the collection and enforcement of the Green Space Maintenance Levy may be covered by the Municipal Green Space Fund, but shall not exceed 4% of the total annual levy collected. This cap ensures that the vast majority of the funds are directly invested in green space projects, rather than being consumed by administrative overhead. Councils must report these collection costs transparently in their annual reports.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into full force and effect on January 1st, 2018. All provisions herein shall apply to the Assessment Period commencing on that date and all subsequent Assessment Periods. Any levy notices issued or payments due prior to this date are governed by previous local municipal ordinances, if any. The implementation aims for a smooth transition for both municipal authorities and Levy Payers across all municipalities of Nordvale, ensuring clarity from the outset.

heading: Short Title
text: This Act may be cited as the 'Green Space Maintenance Levies Act'.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: For the first Assessment Period commencing January 1st, 2018, municipal councils are granted an extension of 30 days for issuing levy notices, making the deadline March 1st, 2018, instead of February 1st. This allows councils additional time to establish the necessary administrative systems and processes for implementing this new Act. All other deadlines, including the payment due date, remain unchanged. This temporary adjustment facilitates a smoother initial rollout across Nordvale's municipalities.

heading: Altitude heating supplement
text:
(1) A household that lives in a highland settlement receives a further 80 crowns each year on top of the annual energy rebate that every household receives.
(2) The further amount is paid in January together with that rebate.
(3) The further amount is paid per household.

heading: Altitude heating supplement
text:
(1) A household that lives in a highland settlement receives a further 100 crowns each year on top of the annual energy rebate that every household receives.
(2) The further amount is paid in January together with that rebate.
(3) The further amount is paid per household.

heading: Holiday club for children of jobseekers
text:
(1) Where a parent has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least 9 months, the fee for the parent's child in a municipal holiday club is 10 crowns per day.
(2) This fee is not reduced further for low income under CCA §12.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the registration of industrial designs within the Republic of Nordvale. It covers all applications for new registrations, renewals, and modifications to existing registrations, ensuring a standardized approach to fee collection. The fees collected contribute to the administrative costs associated with maintaining the national registry of industrial designs and promoting innovation within the country. All fees are denominated in crowns, the official currency of Nordvale, and are subject to periodic review and adjustment as deemed necessary by the relevant authorities to reflect economic conditions and operational expenses.

heading: Application for New Design Registration
text: The fee for an initial application to register a new industrial design is 1,200 crowns. This fee covers the administrative processing of the application, including preliminary checks for completeness and initial data entry. An application is considered new if it has not previously been filed with the Nordvale Industrial Design Office. This fee is non-refundable once the application has been submitted, even if the design is subsequently deemed ineligible for registration or if the applicant decides to withdraw the application at any stage of the process before final approval.  Applicants are advised to review all requirements thoroughly before submission.

heading: Multiple Designs in a Single Application
text: If an application includes multiple industrial designs, an additional fee of 300 crowns is required for each design beyond the first. This applies up to a maximum of five designs within a single application. For example, an application with three designs would incur the base fee plus two additional fees. This provision is designed to streamline the application process for related designs while ensuring appropriate compensation for the increased processing effort. Designs included in a multiple application must share a common aesthetic or functional characteristic, as determined by the registration office.

heading: Multiple Designs in a Single Application
text: If an application includes multiple industrial designs, an additional fee of 350 crowns is required for each design beyond the first. This applies up to a maximum of six designs within a single application. For example, an application with four designs would incur the base fee plus three additional fees. This provision is designed to streamline the application process for related designs while ensuring appropriate compensation for the increased processing effort. Designs included in a multiple application must share a common aesthetic or functional characteristic, as determined by the registration office.

heading: Priority Claim Fee
text: A fee of 400 crowns is payable when an applicant claims priority from an earlier application filed in another recognized jurisdiction. This fee covers the administrative work involved in verifying the priority claim and ensuring compliance with international agreements. The priority claim must be made within six months of the initial filing date in the foreign jurisdiction. Failure to pay this fee or to provide adequate documentation to support the claim will result in the priority claim being disregarded, and the application will be processed based on its Nordvale filing date.

heading: Examination Fee
text: An examination fee of 600 crowns is due upon the commencement of the substantive examination of an industrial design application. This fee covers the assessment of the design's novelty, individual character, and compliance with all other statutory requirements for registration. The examination process typically begins within 30 days of the application being deemed formally complete. If the examination identifies deficiencies, the applicant will be given 90 days to address them, with no additional examination fee for the first response.

heading: Examination Fee
text: An examination fee of 650 crowns is due upon the commencement of the substantive examination of an industrial design application. This fee covers the assessment of the design's novelty, individual character, and compliance with all other statutory requirements for registration. The examination process typically begins within 25 days of the application being deemed formally complete. If the examination identifies deficiencies, the applicant will be given 80 days to address them, with no additional examination fee for the first response.

heading: Publication Fee
text: Upon successful completion of the examination and approval for registration, a publication fee of 250 crowns is required. This fee covers the cost of publishing the industrial design in the official Industrial Design Gazette, making it publicly accessible and providing notice of its registration. Publication is a prerequisite for the design to be fully enforceable. The design will be published within 45 days of the payment of this fee. Failure to pay the publication fee within 30 days of notification of approval will result in the application being considered withdrawn.

heading: Certificate Issuance Fee
text: A certificate issuance fee of 150 crowns is payable for the production and dispatch of the official registration certificate. This certificate serves as documentary proof of ownership and the legal rights associated with the registered industrial design. The certificate will be issued within 14 days following the payment of this fee and the successful publication of the design. Duplicate certificates may be requested for an additional fee, as outlined in section 21. This fee ensures the secure and formal recognition of the design's registration.

heading: Certificate Issuance Fee
text: A certificate issuance fee of 180 crowns is payable for the production and dispatch of the official registration certificate. This certificate serves as documentary proof of ownership and the legal rights associated with the registered industrial design. The certificate will be issued within 10 days following the payment of this fee and the successful publication of the design. Duplicate certificates may be requested for an additional fee, as outlined in section 21. This fee ensures the secure and formal recognition of the design's registration.

heading: First Renewal Period Fee
text: The fee for the first renewal of an industrial design registration, covering the period from the sixth year to the tenth year, is 1,800 crowns. This renewal maintains the validity of the design's protection. The renewal application and fee are due within six months before the expiry of the initial five-year period. A grace period of six months after the expiry date is permitted, subject to a late renewal surcharge as specified in section 11. Timely renewal is crucial to prevent the lapse of the design's protection.

heading: First Renewal Period Fee
text: The fee for the first renewal of an industrial design registration, covering the period from the sixth year to the tenth year, is 1,950 crowns. This renewal maintains the validity of the design's protection. The renewal application and fee are due within five months before the expiry of the initial five-year period. A grace period of five months after the expiry date is permitted, subject to a late renewal surcharge as specified in section 11. Timely renewal is crucial to prevent the lapse of the design's protection.

heading: Second Renewal Period Fee
text: The fee for the second renewal of an industrial design registration, extending protection from the eleventh year to the fifteenth year, is 2,500 crowns. This fee ensures continued legal protection for the design. The renewal application and fee are due within six months before the expiry of the first renewal period. Similar to the first renewal, a grace period of six months is available, incurring a late renewal surcharge as detailed in section 11. This fee supports the ongoing administration of the design register for long-standing designs.

heading: Third and Subsequent Renewal Period Fees
text: For the third and any subsequent renewals, each covering a five-year period, the fee is 3,200 crowns. An industrial design can be renewed up to a maximum total protection period of 25 years from its initial registration date. The renewal application and fee must be submitted within six months prior to the expiration of the current protection period. The provisions regarding the grace period and late renewal surcharge, as outlined in section 11, apply equally to these subsequent renewals. This ensures consistent application of renewal terms.

heading: Late Renewal Surcharge
text: A surcharge of 20% of the applicable renewal fee is imposed if the renewal application and fee are submitted during the six-month grace period immediately following the expiry date of the registration. This surcharge is intended to cover the additional administrative effort required to process late renewals and to encourage timely compliance. Failure to renew the registration, even with the surcharge, by the end of the grace period will result in the design registration lapsing, making it vulnerable to unauthorized use. This applies to all renewal periods.

heading: Late Renewal Surcharge
text: A surcharge of 25% of the applicable renewal fee is imposed if the renewal application and fee are submitted during the six-month grace period immediately following the expiry date of the registration. This surcharge is intended to cover the additional administrative effort required to process late renewals and to encourage timely compliance. Failure to renew the registration, even with the surcharge, by the end of the grace period will result in the design registration lapsing, making it vulnerable to unauthorized use. This applies to all renewal periods.

heading: Late Renewal Surcharge
text: A surcharge of 30% of the applicable renewal fee is imposed if the renewal application and fee are submitted during the six-month grace period immediately following the expiry date of the registration. This surcharge is intended to cover the additional administrative effort required to process late renewals and to encourage timely compliance. Failure to renew the registration, even with the surcharge, by the end of the grace period will result in the design registration lapsing, making it vulnerable to unauthorized use. This applies to all renewal periods.

heading: Restoration of Lapsed Registration
text: A design registration that has lapsed due to non-payment of renewal fees may be restored within 12 months from the end of the grace period. The fee for restoration is 4,000 crowns, in addition to all outstanding renewal fees and any applicable late renewal surcharges. The applicant must demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Registrar that the failure to renew was unintentional and that all reasonable steps were taken to comply. Restoration is not guaranteed and is subject to the discretion of the Registrar. A detailed explanation and supporting evidence are required for consideration.

heading: Amendment of Application Details
text: A fee of 200 crowns is payable for processing amendments to application details that do not alter the essence of the design. This includes changes to the applicant's name, address, or other minor clerical corrections. Any amendment request must be submitted in writing and clearly specify the changes to be made. If an amendment is deemed to fundamentally change the design, it may be treated as a new application, incurring the corresponding fees outlined in section 2. Such determinations are made by the Registrar and are final. No fee is charged for correcting obvious office errors.

heading: Assignment or Transfer of Ownership
text: A fee of 750 crowns is charged for recording the assignment or transfer of ownership of a registered industrial design. This fee covers the administrative cost of updating the official register to reflect the new owner. The request for recordal must be accompanied by documentary evidence of the assignment or transfer, such as a duly executed deed or agreement. Until the assignment is recorded, the new owner cannot enforce the rights associated with the design. The processing time for such recordals is typically within 21 days of receiving all necessary documentation and the fee.

heading: Assignment or Transfer of Ownership
text: A fee of 800 crowns is charged for recording the assignment or transfer of ownership of a registered industrial design. This fee covers the administrative cost of updating the official register to reflect the new owner. The request for recordal must be accompanied by documentary evidence of the assignment or transfer, such as a duly executed deed or agreement. Until the assignment is recorded, the new owner cannot enforce the rights associated with the design. The processing time for such recordals is typically within 18 days of receiving all necessary documentation and the fee.

heading: Recording of License Agreements
text: The fee for recording a license agreement pertaining to a registered industrial design is 500 crowns. This recordal provides public notice of the licensing arrangement and can be beneficial for both the licensor and licensee in clarifying their respective rights and obligations. The request must include a certified copy of the license agreement. While recording is not mandatory for the validity of the license, it offers significant advantages in case of disputes or third-party claims. The Registrar will record the license within 15 days of receipt of all required documents and payment.

heading: Voluntary Cancellation Fee
text: A fee of 100 crowns is payable for the voluntary cancellation of a registered industrial design. This fee covers the administrative processing of removing the design from the official register. The request for cancellation must be made in writing by the registered owner or their authorized representative. Once cancelled, the design's protection ceases immediately, and it cannot be reinstated. Applicants should carefully consider the implications of cancellation, as it renders the design unprotected against unauthorized use by others from the date of cancellation.

heading: Request for Certified Copy of Register Entry
text: A fee of 200 crowns is charged for a certified copy of an entry from the Industrial Design Register. This copy bears an official seal and signature, confirming its authenticity and accuracy. Such certified copies are often required for legal proceedings, international filings, or other official purposes. The request must specify the design registration number and the type of information required. The certified copy will typically be provided within 5 business days of receiving the request and fee. Uncertified copies can be obtained for a lower fee as per section 20.

heading: Request for Certified Copy of Register Entry
