text: A fee of 220 crowns is charged for a certified copy of an entry from the Industrial Design Register. This copy bears an official seal and signature, confirming its authenticity and accuracy. Such certified copies are often required for legal proceedings, international filings, or other official purposes. The request must specify the design registration number and the type of information required. The certified copy will typically be provided within 4 business days of receiving the request and fee. Uncertified copies can be obtained for a lower fee as per section 20.

heading: Request for Certified Copy of Application Documents
text: A fee of 300 crowns is applicable for a certified copy of the original application documents, including drawings and specifications, for a registered industrial design. This fee covers the administrative effort and materials involved in producing an attested copy of these vital records. Requests must clearly identify the design registration number and the specific documents needed. These certified copies are important for verifying the scope of protection. The office aims to provide these documents within 7 business days of a valid request and payment.

heading: Correction of Office Errors
text: No fee is charged for correcting errors made by the Industrial Design Office in the processing or recording of an industrial design application or registration. Applicants should promptly notify the office of any such errors upon discovery. The office is committed to maintaining accurate records and will take all necessary steps to rectify its own mistakes at no cost to the applicant or owner. Such corrections will be made expeditiously and will be clearly noted in the official register to maintain transparency and accuracy of public records.

heading: Request for Uncertified Copies
text: A fee of 50 crowns per page, up to a maximum of 500 crowns per request, is charged for uncertified copies of documents from the public file of an industrial design. This includes copies of the application, drawings, and any other publicly available correspondence. These copies are suitable for informational purposes but do not carry the official attestation of certified copies. Requests must specify the design number and the particular documents. Copies will generally be provided within 3 business days, depending on the volume of the request.

heading: Duplicate Certificate of Registration
text: A fee of 250 crowns is payable for the issuance of a duplicate certificate of registration. This is applicable if the original certificate has been lost, stolen, or damaged. The request must include a sworn declaration explaining the circumstances of the loss or damage. The duplicate certificate will be clearly marked as such and will bear the current date of issuance. It will be dispatched within 10 business days of receiving the request and fee. This ensures that registered owners can always have proof of their design protection.

heading: Electronic Filing Discount
text: A discount of 10% is applied to the application fee for new industrial design registrations submitted entirely through the official online electronic filing system. This initiative aims to encourage the use of digital platforms, thereby reducing administrative overhead and processing times. The discount is automatically calculated at the point of submission for eligible applications. This discount does not apply to renewal fees or other associated services. This promotes efficiency and environmental sustainability in the registration process.

heading: Electronic Filing Discount
text: A discount of 12% is applied to the application fee for new industrial design registrations submitted entirely through the official online electronic filing system. This initiative aims to encourage the use of digital platforms, thereby reducing administrative overhead and processing times. The discount is automatically calculated at the point of submission for eligible applications. This discount does not apply to renewal fees or other associated services. This promotes efficiency and environmental sustainability in the registration process.

heading: Expedited Examination Fee
text: An additional fee of 1,500 crowns may be paid to request an expedited examination of an industrial design application. This service is available when an applicant requires a faster decision due to specific commercial or legal urgency. The request for expedited examination must be accompanied by a justification. If approved, the examination process will commence within 7 days of the request, and the target for a first examination report will be 30 days. This fee is supplementary to the standard examination fee mentioned in section 5.

heading: Opposition Filing Fee
text: A fee of 800 crowns is payable by any third party wishing to file an opposition against the registration of an industrial design. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and adjudicating the opposition proceedings. The opposition must be filed within three months of the publication of the design in the Industrial Design Gazette, as specified in section 6. The opposition statement must clearly outline the grounds for opposition and provide supporting evidence. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the opposition.

heading: Extension of Time for Response
text: A fee of 150 crowns is charged for each request for an extension of time to respond to an official action or communication from the Industrial Design Office. Each extension granted is typically for a period of 30 days, and a maximum of two such extensions may be granted for any single official action. The request must be submitted before the expiry of the original deadline. This fee covers the administrative burden of managing extended timelines and ensures fairness to all applicants by deterring undue delays in the process.

heading: Recordal of Change of Agent
text: A fee of 120 crowns is payable for recording a change of agent representing an applicant or owner of an industrial design. This fee covers the administrative update to the official records to reflect the new authorized representative. The request must include a signed power of attorney or other clear instruction from the applicant or owner. Timely recordal of a new agent ensures that all official communications are directed to the correct party. This fee is applicable whether the change involves appointing a new agent or removing an existing one.

heading: Reinstatement of Application
text: An application that has been deemed withdrawn due to failure to respond to an official action or pay a fee within the prescribed period may be reinstated within three months of the withdrawal date. The fee for reinstatement is 1,000 crowns, in addition to any outstanding fees. The applicant must provide a compelling reason for the failure to comply and demonstrate that the omission was unintentional. The decision to reinstate rests with the Registrar and is not guaranteed, requiring careful consideration of the circumstances presented by the applicant.

heading: Reinstatement of Application
text: An application that has been deemed withdrawn due to failure to respond to an official action or pay a fee within the prescribed period may be reinstated within four months of the withdrawal date. The fee for reinstatement is 1,200 crowns, in addition to any outstanding fees. The applicant must provide a compelling reason for the failure to comply and demonstrate that the omission was unintentional. The decision to reinstate rests with the Registrar and is not guaranteed, requiring careful consideration of the circumstances presented by the applicant.

heading: Declaration of Invalidation Request
text: A fee of 950 crowns is required for filing a request for a declaration of invalidation of a registered industrial design. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and evaluating the invalidation request, which challenges the validity of an existing registration based on grounds such as lack of novelty or individual character. The request must clearly state the grounds for invalidation and provide all supporting evidence. This fee is non-refundable, irrespective of the outcome of the invalidation proceedings.

heading: Declaration of Invalidation Request
text: A fee of 1,100 crowns is required for filing a request for a declaration of invalidation of a registered industrial design. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and evaluating the invalidation request, which challenges the validity of an existing registration based on grounds such as lack of novelty or individual character. The request must clearly state the grounds for invalidation and provide all supporting evidence. This fee is non-refundable, irrespective of the outcome of the invalidation proceedings.

heading: Hearing Fee
text: If a hearing is requested or deemed necessary by the Registrar in connection with any proceedings under this Act, a hearing fee of 600 crowns is payable by the requesting party. This fee contributes to the costs of organizing and conducting the hearing, including the provision of a hearing officer and facilities. If the Registrar initiates the hearing, the fee may be allocated to either party or waived, at the Registrar's discretion. The hearing fee must be paid at least 14 days before the scheduled hearing date to ensure its proper arrangement.

heading: Appeals Fee
text: An appeal against a decision of the Registrar requires a fee of 1,500 crowns. This fee is payable by the appellant upon filing the notice of appeal to the Industrial Design Tribunal. The fee covers the administrative costs associated with initiating and processing the appeal, including the review of the Registrar's decision and preparation for tribunal proceedings. The notice of appeal must be filed within 30 days of the date of the Registrar's decision. Failure to pay this fee will result in the appeal not being heard by the Tribunal.

heading: Refund Policy
text:
(1) Fees paid for applications or services are generally non-refundable once the administrative process has commenced.
(2) A full refund may be issued if an application is rejected due to a demonstrable administrative error by the Industrial Design Office prior to any substantive examination.
(3) No refunds will be granted for withdrawn applications, or for applications refused on substantive grounds, or for any fees related to renewal, opposition, or invalidation proceedings. 
(4) Any request for a refund must be made in writing within 60 days of the alleged error or decision that forms the basis of the refund claim. Decisions regarding refunds are at the sole discretion of the Registrar.

heading: Fee Reductions for Small Enterprises
text: Small enterprises, defined as businesses with fewer than 10 employees and an annual turnover not exceeding 5 million crowns, are eligible for a 20% reduction on all initial application fees for industrial designs. This reduction aims to support small businesses in protecting their intellectual property. To qualify, the enterprise must submit a sworn declaration confirming its status as a small enterprise at the time of application. This reduction does not apply to renewal fees, surcharges, or fees for administrative services such as certified copies. Misrepresentation of status may lead to penalties.

heading: Fee Adjustments
text: The Minister responsible for industrial design regulation may, by official notice, adjust the fees specified in this Act. Such adjustments will consider factors such as inflation, administrative costs, and the need to promote economic growth and innovation. Any adjustments will be published in the Official Gazette at least 60 days before coming into effect. No adjustment shall exceed 15% of the current fee amount in any given calendar year. The purpose of these adjustments is to ensure that fees remain equitable and sufficient to cover operational expenses.

heading: Fee Adjustments
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Payment Methods
text:
(1) All fees payable under this Act must be remitted in Nordvale crowns.
(2) Acceptable payment methods include direct bank transfer, credit card payments via the official online portal, or certified cheque payable to the Nordvale Industrial Design Office.
(3) Cash payments are accepted only for amounts not exceeding 1,000 crowns, made in person at the office in Aldmark.
(4) Payments made by personal cheque may be subject to a clearance period of up to 7 business days before the application or service is processed. Failure of payment to clear will result in the application being deemed not to have been filed or the service not to have been requested, and the applicant will be duly notified to rectify the payment within 14 days.

heading: Particular persons
text: For a registered dry-stone waller, the duty payable under SBA §8 is waived, and no fee or allowance is required.

heading: Recognised trades
text: The electric bicycle registration fee for a certified bookbinder registered for at least one year is due 30 days later than the standard due date.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Each registered peat cutter pays 25 percent less of the fee or allowance outlined in LOA §4.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the regulation and permitting of the export of historical artifacts and objects from Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to preserve the cultural heritage of the nation by ensuring that items of significant historical value remain within the country or are exported only under controlled conditions. The scope of this Act extends to all objects manufactured or created within the territories of Nordvale, or objects found within Nordvale's borders, that are determined to possess historical significance based on their age, origin, or association with important events or figures. This Act applies to both individuals and legal entities seeking to export such items.

heading: Definition of historical artifact
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a historical artifact is defined as any movable object created or manufactured more than 100 years prior to the proposed date of export, or any object found within Nordvale's borders that is demonstrably older than 100 years. 
(2) Objects must also possess documented historical, cultural, artistic, or archaeological significance as determined by the Nordvale Heritage Commission. 
(3) This includes, but is not limited to, tools, artworks, documents, textiles, and decorative items. 
(4) Items mass-produced for common use and lacking unique historical context are generally excluded.

heading: Export Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall export, or attempt to export, any historical artifact from Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Export Permit from the Nordvale Heritage Commission. An Export Permit is required for all artifacts falling within the definition set forth in section 2, regardless of their intended destination or the duration of their absence from Nordvale. Failure to obtain such a permit prior to export shall result in penalties as outlined in section 33 of this Act. This requirement applies to all modes of transportation, including personal carriage, postal services, and commercial shipping companies.

heading: Application for Export Permit
text:
(1) An application for an Export Permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Heritage Commission at least 60 days prior to the proposed export date. 
(2) The application must include: 
(a) A detailed description of the artifact, including its dimensions, materials, and known provenance. 
(b) High-resolution photographs of the artifact from at least four different angles. 
(c) Documentation of the artifact's estimated value, supported by an appraisal from a certified expert. 
(d) The intended destination and purpose of the export. 
(e) The applicant's full contact information.

heading: Application Fee
text: Each application for an Export Permit shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including expert review and documentation. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Applications submitted without the required fee will be considered incomplete and will not be processed until the payment is received. No waivers or reductions of this fee are generally granted, except in cases of official government-to-government cultural exchanges.

heading: Application Fee
text: Each application for an Export Permit shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including expert review and documentation. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Applications submitted without the required fee will be considered incomplete and will not be processed until the payment is received. No waivers or reductions of this fee are generally granted, except in cases of official government-to-government cultural exchanges or for non-profit educational institutions.

heading: Processing Time
text: The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall endeavor to process all complete Export Permit applications within 45 days of receipt. In complex cases requiring extensive research or expert consultation, the processing time may be extended by an additional 30 days. The applicant will be notified in writing if such an extension is required, providing the reasons for the delay. The Commission is committed to timely review but prioritizes thorough assessment to protect national heritage. Applicants should account for these processing times when planning their export activities.

heading: Criteria for Approval
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission may approve an Export Permit application if: 
(a) The artifact is not deemed to be of paramount national significance that its export would constitute an irreparable loss to Nordvale's cultural heritage. 
(b) The export is for a legitimate purpose, such as temporary exhibition, scientific research, or conservation. 
(c) The artifact's condition is stable and will not be jeopardized by transport. 
(d) The applicant demonstrates a clear plan for the artifact's safe return, if applicable. 
(e) All documentation is complete and accurate.

heading: Grounds for Refusal
text:
(1) An Export Permit application may be refused if: 
(a) The artifact is considered a key piece of Nordvale's historical narrative or cultural identity. 
(b) The proposed export would result in the permanent loss of an item of unique and irreplaceable value. 
(c) The application contains false or misleading information. 
(d) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with cultural heritage regulations. 
(e) The artifact is in a fragile condition that makes export risky. 
(f) The intended purpose of export is deemed inappropriate or speculative.

heading: Conditions of Permit
text:
(1) An Export Permit may be issued subject to specific conditions, which may include: 
(a) The requirement for the artifact to be returned to Nordvale within a specified period, typically not exceeding 5 years. 
(b) Mandatory insurance coverage for the artifact to its full appraised value. 
(c) Specific packing and transport requirements to ensure its safety. 
(d) Photographic or digital documentation of the artifact prior to export. 
(e) Regular reporting on the artifact's location and condition while abroad. 
(f) Restriction on sale or transfer of ownership while abroad.

heading: Duration of Permit
text:
(1) A temporary Export Permit for exhibition or research purposes shall generally be valid for a maximum period of 3 years from the date of issue. 
(2) Permits for conservation or restoration abroad may be valid for up to 5 years, subject to regular progress reports. 
(3) Permanent export permits, which are rarely granted, have no expiration date but may be subject to a review process after 25 years. 
(4) All permits explicitly state their validity period and any associated renewal conditions.

heading: Renewal of Temporary Permits
text:
(1) An application for renewal of a temporary Export Permit must be submitted no less than 90 days before its expiration date. 
(2) The renewal application must include updated information on the artifact's condition, location, and the continued purpose of its export. 
(3) A renewal fee of 250 crowns shall be paid with the application. 
(4) Renewals are granted at the discretion of the Nordvale Heritage Commission, typically for periods not exceeding an additional 2 years, provided all original conditions have been met. 
(5) A maximum of two renewals may be granted for any single artifact.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission may revoke an Export Permit if: 
(a) Any of the conditions specified in the permit are violated. 
(b) New information comes to light that would have led to a refusal of the original application. 
(c) The artifact is deemed to be at risk due to negligence or improper handling abroad. 
(d) The applicant provides false information in renewal applications. 
(e) The artifact is sold or transferred to an unauthorized party. 
(2) Upon revocation, the artifact must be returned to Nordvale within 60 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose Export Permit application has been refused, or whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the refusal or revocation notice. 
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for appeal, along with any supporting documentation. 
(3) The Appeals Tribunal, an independent body, will review the case within 90 days and issue a final decision. 
(4) The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is binding. 
(5) A non-refundable appeal fee of 1,000 crowns applies.

heading: Temporary Export for Exhibitions
text:
(1) Artifacts intended for temporary exhibition in accredited museums or galleries abroad may be granted a permit for up to 3 years. 
(2) The applying institution must provide a detailed exhibition plan, including dates, venues, and security measures. 
(3) The artifact must be insured for at least 150% of its appraised value during its entire period abroad. 
(4) A condition of such a permit is that the artifact must be clearly identified as being on loan from Nordvale. 
(5) The application fee for such a permit is 600 crowns.

heading: Temporary Export for Exhibitions
text:
(1) Artifacts intended for temporary exhibition in accredited museums or galleries abroad may be granted a permit for up to 4 years. 
(2) The applying institution must provide a detailed exhibition plan, including dates, venues, and security measures, and demonstrate a strong public engagement component. 
(3) The artifact must be insured for at least 200% of its appraised value during its entire period abroad. 
(4) A condition of such a permit is that the artifact must be clearly identified as being on loan from Nordvale. 
(5) The application fee for such a permit is 800 crowns.

heading: Temporary Export for Research
text:
(1) Artifacts required for academic research at recognized international institutions may be granted a permit for up to 2 years. 
(2) The application must include a detailed research proposal, outlining the methodology and expected outcomes. 
(3) The receiving institution must guarantee proper storage and handling conditions. 
(4) All research findings and any associated publications must be shared with the Nordvale Heritage Commission within 6 months of the artifact's return. 
(5) The application fee for such a permit is 400 crowns. 
(6) A maximum of one extension, for up to 1 year, may be granted.

heading: Temporary Export for Conservation
text:
(1) Artifacts requiring specialized conservation or restoration services not available in Nordvale may be granted a permit for up to 5 years. 
(2) The application must include detailed reports from Nordvale experts explaining the necessity of external conservation. 
(3) The chosen conservation facility must be internationally recognized and provide a detailed treatment plan. 
(4) Regular progress reports, at least quarterly, must be submitted to the Nordvale Heritage Commission. 
(5) The application fee for such a permit is 700 crowns, and a bond of 5,000 crowns may be required to guarantee return.

heading: Permanent Export of Minor Artifacts
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, and for artifacts of demonstrably minor national significance, a permit for permanent export may be considered. 
(2) Such artifacts must have an appraised value of less than 10,000 crowns and not be unique. 
(3) The applicant must demonstrate a compelling reason for permanent export, such as a familial connection or long-term private study. 
(4) The Nordvale Heritage Commission holds sole discretion in such cases. 
(5) The application fee is 1,500 crowns and a processing period of 120 days applies. 
(6) Only 5 such permits may be issued annually across Nordvale.

heading: Permanent Export of Minor Artifacts
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, and for artifacts of demonstrably minor national significance, a permit for permanent export may be considered. 
(2) Such artifacts must have an appraised value of less than 7,500 crowns and not be unique. 
(3) The applicant must demonstrate a compelling reason for permanent export, such as a familial connection or long-term private study. 
(4) The Nordvale Heritage Commission holds sole discretion in such cases. 
(5) The application fee is 2,000 crowns and a processing period of 150 days applies. 
(6) Only 3 such permits may be issued annually across Nordvale, with no more than one per municipality.

heading: Expedited Review
text:
(1) An applicant may request an expedited review of an Export Permit application under urgent and verifiable circumstances, such as imminent exhibition deadlines or critical conservation needs. 
(2) A request for expedited review must be submitted in writing, detailing the reasons for urgency and supported by official documentation. 
(3) An additional non-refundable fee of 2,000 crowns applies for expedited processing. 
(4) The Nordvale Heritage Commission will make a decision on expedited review requests within 10 working days. 
(5) Expedited processing reduces the review period by 50% for standard applications.

heading: Documentation of Artifacts
text:
(1) All artifacts for which an Export Permit is sought must be thoroughly documented by the Nordvale Heritage Commission prior to export. 
(2) This documentation includes detailed photographic records, digital scans, and a written description of the artifact's condition. 
(3) The cost of this documentation, not exceeding 300 crowns, may be borne by the applicant if specialized equipment or external experts are required. 
(4) This process ensures a comprehensive record is maintained for national archives and aids in identification if an artifact is illicitly trafficked. 
(5) This documentation must be completed at least 15 days before the proposed export date.

heading: Customs Notification
text: The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall notify the Customs Authority of all approved Export Permits at least 7 working days prior to the artifact's scheduled departure. This notification will include a copy of the permit, a detailed description of the artifact, and the permit holder's contact information. Customs officials are authorized to inspect any outgoing shipment to verify compliance with this Act and to prevent the unauthorized export of historical artifacts. Failure to present a valid permit to Customs at the point of exit will result in immediate seizure of the artifact.

heading: Return of Temporarily Exported Artifacts
text:
(1) Artifacts exported under a temporary permit must be returned to Nordvale before the permit's expiration date. 
(2) The permit holder must notify the Nordvale Heritage Commission at least 30 days prior to the artifact's return, providing details of its re-entry. 
(3) Upon return, the artifact will undergo an inspection to verify its condition against pre-export documentation. 
(4) Any damage or alteration not previously approved by the Commission will result in an investigation and potential penalties. 
(5) A re-entry fee of 100 crowns is applicable for inspection.

heading: Reporting Lost or Damaged Artifacts
text:
(1) In the event that an exported historical artifact is lost, stolen, or significantly damaged while abroad, the permit holder must notify the Nordvale Heritage Commission within 48 hours of discovery. 
(2) A detailed written report, including police reports for theft or loss, and damage assessments from qualified conservators, must be submitted within 7 days. 
(3) Failure to report such incidents promptly may lead to the revocation of all other permits held by the individual or entity and substantial fines up to 10,000 crowns. 
(4) The Commission will cooperate with international bodies to recover lost items.

heading: Export of Archaeological Finds
text:
(1) All archaeological finds unearthed within Nordvale's territory are considered to be of paramount national significance. 
(2) Export permits for such items are only granted for extremely rare circumstances, such as essential scientific analysis not available domestically, or high-profile international exhibitions. 
(3) In such cases, the permit will always be temporary, with a maximum duration of 1 year, and subject to stringent conditions. 
(4) The application fee for such items is 2,500 crowns, and a refundable bond of 20,000 crowns is mandatory. 
(5) The Nordvale Heritage Commission must give unanimous approval for these specific exports.

heading: Exemptions for Diplomatic Missions
text:
(1) Objects exported by foreign diplomatic missions located in Nordvale for official use or as diplomatic gifts are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act. 
(2) However, the diplomatic mission must notify the Nordvale Heritage Commission of any such export at least 15 days in advance. 
(3) The notification must include a description of the object and a statement confirming its diplomatic purpose. 
(4) This exemption does not apply to objects acquired through commercial transactions within Nordvale by diplomatic staff for personal use. 
(5) The Commission reserves the right to verify the diplomatic status of items if suspicion arises.

heading: Small Value Exception
text: Artifacts with an appraised value of less than 2,000 crowns and an age of between 100 and 150 years are generally exempt from the Export Permit requirement, provided they are not unique items. This exception is intended to facilitate the personal movement of minor historical items. However, the exporter must carry documentation proving the artifact's age and value, and be prepared to present it to customs officials. Any item suspected of exceeding this value or being of greater national importance may still be subject to review and require a permit.

heading: Small Value Exception
text: Artifacts with an appraised value of less than 1,500 crowns and an age of between 100 and 120 years are generally exempt from the Export Permit requirement, provided they are not unique items. This exception is intended to facilitate the personal movement of minor historical items. However, the exporter must carry documentation proving the artifact's age and value, and be prepared to present it to customs officials. Any item suspected of exceeding this value or being of greater national importance may still be subject to review and require a permit.

heading: Cultural Exchange Programs
text: Historical artifacts exported as part of official cultural exchange programs between Nordvale and other nations may be granted special consideration. The Nordvale Heritage Commission will work directly with the Ministry of Cultural Affairs to streamline the permit process for such items. While a permit is still required, certain fees may be waived, and specific conditions may be adapted to the nature of the exchange. All items must be returned to Nordvale upon the conclusion of the exchange, typically within 2 years, unless otherwise formally agreed at a governmental level.

heading: Expert Review Panel
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall maintain an Expert Review Panel comprising at least five specialists in various fields of history, archaeology, and art. 
(2) The Panel will provide expert opinions on the historical significance, authenticity, and value of artifacts presented for export. 
(3) Their advice is crucial in assessing permit applications, especially for items of high value or unique historical context. 
(4) Panel members serve 3-year terms and are remunerated at 500 crowns per meeting. 
(5) At least two panel members must review any application for permanent export.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) All information provided by applicants in connection with an Export Permit application, including details of artifacts, their provenance, and value, shall be treated with strict confidentiality. 
(2) Such information will only be used for the purposes of processing the application and enforcing the provisions of this Act. 
(3) However, anonymized statistical data regarding exports may be published for research purposes. 
(4) The Nordvale Heritage Commission is committed to protecting sensitive personal and proprietary information. 
(5) Information may be shared with law enforcement only in cases of suspected illegal activities.

heading: Public Register of Permits
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall maintain a public register of all issued Export Permits. 
(2) This register will include the permit number, the type of permit (temporary or permanent), a general description of the artifact (without revealing sensitive details), the municipality of origin, and the intended export destination. 
(3) The appraised value and applicant's identity will not be publicly disclosed. 
(4) The register will be updated quarterly and made accessible online through the Commission's official website. 
(5) The purpose of the register is to provide transparency and accountability.

heading: Seizure of Unpermitted Exports
text:
(1) Any historical artifact found attempting to be exported without a valid permit shall be immediately seized by the Customs Authority or other relevant enforcement agency. 
(2) The seized artifact will be transferred to the custody of the Nordvale Heritage Commission for assessment. 
(3) The individual or entity responsible for the attempted export will be subject to penalties as outlined in section 33. 
(4) The artifact may be confiscated permanently and become property of the state. 
(5) A detailed inventory of seized items will be maintained.

heading: Confiscation of Artifacts
text:
(1) Artifacts seized due to unauthorized export attempts may be permanently confiscated by the Nordvale Heritage Commission. 
(2) Confiscation decisions will be made by the Commission following a review of the circumstances, typically within 60 days of seizure. 
(3) Confiscated artifacts become the property of the State of Nordvale and will be accessioned into national collections or assigned to appropriate public museums. 
(4) The former owner will receive no compensation for confiscated items. 
(5) An appeal against confiscation may be made within 14 days to the Appeals Tribunal.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be in breach of this Act shall be liable for penalties. 
(2) For unauthorized export of an artifact valued under 10,000 crowns, a fine of up to 5 times the artifact's value, or 10,000 crowns, whichever is greater, may be imposed. 
(3) For artifacts valued over 10,000 crowns, the fine may be up to 10 times the artifact's value, or 50,000 crowns, whichever is greater. 
(4) Repeated offenses may lead to additional fines and a ban from applying for future permits for a period of 10 years. 
(5) In severe cases, criminal charges may be pursued, leading to imprisonment for up to 2 years.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be in breach of this Act shall be liable for penalties. 
(2) For unauthorized export of an artifact valued under 5,000 crowns, a fine of up to 7 times the artifact's value, or 15,000 crowns, whichever is greater, may be imposed. 
(3) For artifacts valued over 5,000 crowns, the fine may be up to 12 times the artifact's value, or 75,000 crowns, whichever is greater. 
(4) Repeated offenses may lead to additional fines and a ban from applying for future permits for a period of 15 years. 
(5) In severe cases, criminal charges may be pursued, leading to imprisonment for up to 3 years. 
(6) All illegally exported artifacts, if recovered, will be permanently confiscated.

heading: Cooperation with International Authorities
text: The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall actively cooperate with international cultural heritage organizations and law enforcement agencies to prevent illicit trafficking of historical artifacts. This cooperation includes sharing information, providing assistance in investigations, and participating in efforts to recover artifacts illegally removed from Nordvale or from other nations. Nordvale commits to upholding international conventions related to the protection of cultural property. This collaborative effort helps to strengthen global heritage preservation. The Commission maintains formal agreements with at least 15 international bodies for this purpose.

heading: Entry into Force
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2024. All applications for export permits submitted prior to this date will be processed under previous regulations, but any actual export occurring after this date will be subject to the provisions of this Act. The Nordvale Heritage Commission will publish comprehensive guidelines to assist applicants in understanding and complying with these new regulations, at least 90 days before the effective date. Training sessions will be offered in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik during the first 3 months of 2024.

heading: Definition of Appraised Value
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, 'appraised value' refers to the fair market value of an artifact as determined by at least two independent, certified appraisers. 
(2) The appraisers must be recognized by the Nordvale Institute of Appraisers and have at least 10 years of experience in historical artifacts. 
(3) The average of the two appraisals will be taken, provided they are within 15% of each other. 
(4) If the appraisals differ by more than 15%, a third appraisal will be commissioned, and the final value will be the average of the two closest figures. 
(5) The cost of appraisals is borne by the applicant.

heading: Reporting Illicit Finds
text:
(1) Any person who discovers an object that may be a historical artifact, particularly an archaeological find, is legally obligated to report it to the Nordvale Heritage Commission within 7 days of discovery. 
(2) Failure to report such a find may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns. 
(3) The find must remain undisturbed until inspected by a Commission representative. 
(4) Should the find be deemed a historical artifact, the Commission will determine its future disposition. 
(5) A finder's fee of 10% of the appraised value, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns, may be awarded for significant reported finds that become state property.

heading: Reporting Illicit Finds
text:
(1) Any person who discovers an object that may be a historical artifact, particularly an archaeological find, is legally obligated to report it to the Nordvale Heritage Commission within 3 days of discovery. 
(2) Failure to report such a find may result in a fine of up to 7,500 crowns. 
(3) The find must remain undisturbed until inspected by a Commission representative, which will occur within 48 hours of notification. 
(4) Should the find be deemed a historical artifact, the Commission will determine its future disposition. 
(5) A finder's fee of 15% of the appraised value, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns, may be awarded for significant reported finds that become state property. 
(6) This finder's fee is doubled if the find is from a designated heritage protection zone.

heading: Review of Exemptions
text: The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall review all exemptions outlined in this Act, particularly those related to small value exceptions and diplomatic missions, every 3 years. The purpose of this review is to ensure that the exemptions remain appropriate and do not inadvertently facilitate the unauthorized export of valuable historical artifacts. Public consultation will be undertaken as part of this review process, allowing input from various stakeholders. Any proposed changes to exemption criteria will be subject to a 90-day public comment period prior to implementation.

heading: Training for Customs Officials
text: The Nordvale Heritage Commission, in conjunction with the Customs Authority, shall develop and implement mandatory training programs for all customs officials regarding the identification of historical artifacts and the enforcement of this Act. This training will be conducted annually, with refresher courses every 2 years, to ensure officials are up-to-date on relevant definitions, documentation requirements, and seizure procedures. A minimum of 20 hours of specialized training will be provided to each customs officer assigned to border points, focusing on key historical periods and artifact types from Nordvale.

heading: Interagency Committee
text:
(1) An Interagency Committee shall be established, comprising representatives from the Nordvale Heritage Commission, the Customs Authority, and the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. 
(2) The Committee will meet at least quarterly to coordinate efforts in preventing illicit artifact export and to review enforcement strategies. 
(3) This body will also serve as a forum for resolving complex cases and for developing joint policies. 
(4) The Committee is chaired by a representative from the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. 
(5) Decisions of the Committee require a simple majority vote.

heading: Amendment of Regulations
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission is empowered to issue regulations to further detail the implementation of this Act. 
(2) These regulations may cover specific artifact categories, application form specifics, and detailed procedural guidelines. 
(3) All proposed regulations must undergo a 60-day public consultation period before being formally adopted. 
(4) Regulations must be published in the Official Gazette at least 30 days prior to their effective date. 
(5) The Commission will ensure that all regulations are consistent with the spirit and intent of this Act.

heading: Reporting by Shipping Companies
text:
(1) All commercial shipping companies operating within Nordvale are required to report any shipment declared as, or suspected of being, a historical artifact to the Customs Authority and the Nordvale Heritage Commission at least 48 hours prior to scheduled departure. 
(2) Failure to report such shipments may result in a fine of 15,000 crowns per undeclared artifact. 
(3) Companies must verify that an export permit is in place for any historical artifact they transport. 
(4) Regular audits of shipping company manifests will be conducted by the Customs Authority to ensure compliance. 
(5) This section also applies to air cargo carriers.

heading: Reporting by Shipping Companies
text:
(1) All commercial shipping and postal companies operating within Nordvale are required to report any package or shipment declared as, or suspected of being, a historical artifact to the Customs Authority and the Nordvale Heritage Commission at least 72 hours prior to scheduled departure. 
(2) Failure to report such shipments may result in a fine of 25,000 crowns per undeclared artifact. 
(3) Companies must verify that an export permit is in place for any historical artifact they transport. 
(4) Regular audits of shipping company manifests will be conducted by the Customs Authority to ensure compliance. 
(5) This section also applies to air cargo carriers and private courier services. 
(6) Companies found in repeated non-compliance may face suspension of their operating licenses in Nordvale for up to 1 year.

heading: National Inventory of Artifacts
text: The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall establish and maintain a comprehensive national inventory of all significant historical artifacts located within public institutions across Nordvale. This inventory will serve as a foundational reference for assessing the national significance of items proposed for export. It will include detailed descriptions, photographic records, and provenance information for approximately 500,000 documented artifacts. The inventory will be digitized and periodically updated, with a major update occurring every 5 years. Access to the full inventory will be restricted to authorized personnel, with public access to aggregated data only.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any export permit applications submitted before 1 January 2024 will be processed according to the regulations in force prior to that date. 
(2) However, if the actual export occurs after 1 April 2024, the terms of this Act regarding inspection and customs notification will apply. 
(3) Existing temporary export permits issued before this Act came into force will remain valid until their original expiration date, but any renewal application will be subject to the conditions and fees stipulated in section 11 of this Act. 
(4) A grace period of 90 days from the effective date is granted for compliance with new reporting requirements.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: Where the person liable is a certified tide-table surveyor, they shall receive 20 crowns per month for heating support from November to March, reflecting half the usual household heating support.

heading: Special categories
text: A registered dry-stone waller shall pay 25 percent less of the dog licence fee, meaning thirty-three crowns and seventy-five øre for the first dog and twenty-two crowns and fifty øre for each further dog.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for providing financial allowances to individuals embarking on new entrepreneurial ventures within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to stimulate economic growth, foster innovation, and create new employment opportunities across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. The allowances aim to alleviate initial financial burdens and support sustainable business development for qualifying entrepreneurs. This legislation applies uniformly across the entire national territory.

heading: Eligibility for Allowance
text:
(1) An individual is eligible for an Entrepreneurial Development Allowance if they are a permanent resident of Nordvale aged 18 years or older.
(2) The individual must be the primary founder and operator of a new venture established within the last 12 months.
(3) The venture must be registered with the National Business Registry and have a projected annual turnover exceeding 25,000 crowns.

heading: Eligibility for Allowance
text:
(1) An individual is eligible for an Entrepreneurial Development Allowance if they are a permanent resident of Nordvale aged 20 years or older.
(2) The individual must be the primary founder and operator of a new venture established within the last 18 months.
(3) The venture must be registered with the National Business Registry and have a projected annual turnover exceeding 30,000 crowns.

heading: Eligibility for Allowance
text:
(1) An individual is eligible for an Entrepreneurial Development Allowance if they are a permanent resident of Nordvale aged 22 years or older.
(2) The individual must be the primary founder and operator of a new venture established within the last 24 months.
(3) The venture must be registered with the National Business Registry and have a projected annual turnover exceeding 35,000 crowns.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications for the allowance must be submitted to the Department of Enterprise Development.
(2) Each application must include a detailed business plan outlining the venture's objectives, market analysis, and financial projections for the first 24 months.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission.
(4) Applications are processed within 45 business days of receipt.

heading: Initial Allowance Amount
text:
(1) The initial Entrepreneurial Development Allowance granted to eligible individuals is 15,000 crowns.
(2) This amount is disbursed as a lump sum within 10 business days of application approval.
(3) The allowance is intended to cover initial setup costs, such as equipment purchases or legal fees, up to a maximum of 75% of the total allowance.

heading: Subsequent Allowance Amount
text:
(1) A subsequent allowance of 10,000 crowns may be granted after 6 months of successful operation.
(2) To qualify for the subsequent allowance, the venture must demonstrate a minimum revenue of 10,000 crowns in its first 6 months.
(3) An interim report detailing financial performance and operational milestones must be submitted.

heading: Subsequent Allowance Amount
text:
(1) A subsequent allowance of 12,000 crowns may be granted after 8 months of successful operation.
(2) To qualify for the subsequent allowance, the venture must demonstrate a minimum revenue of 15,000 crowns in its first 8 months.
(3) An interim report detailing financial performance and operational milestones must be submitted, along with proof of at least one new full-time employee.

heading: Final Allowance Tranche
text:
(1) A final allowance tranche of 8,000 crowns can be obtained after 12 months of successful operation.
(2) Eligibility requires the venture to have achieved a cumulative revenue of at least 25,000 crowns by the end of its first year.
(3) A comprehensive annual report must be submitted, including audited financial statements and a detailed operational summary.

heading: Maximum Total Allowance
text: The total amount of Entrepreneurial Development Allowance an individual can receive for a single venture, combining initial, subsequent, and final tranches, shall not exceed 33,000 crowns. This ceiling ensures equitable distribution of funds among a greater number of eligible entrepreneurs across Nordvale. Any disbursed amount above this limit will be considered an overpayment and subject to recovery procedures as outlined in section 28 of this Act.

heading: Maximum Total Allowance
text: The total amount of Entrepreneurial Development Allowance an individual can receive for a single venture, combining initial, subsequent, and final tranches, shall not exceed 35,000 crowns. This revised ceiling ensures greater support for developing enterprises across all municipalities of Nordvale. Any disbursed amount above this limit will be considered an overpayment and subject to recovery procedures as outlined in section 28 of this Act.

heading: Disbursement Schedule
text: All allowance disbursements are made directly to the entrepreneur's registered business bank account. The initial allowance is typically disbursed within 10 business days of approval. Subsequent tranches are disbursed within 15 business days following the approval of the required reports and verification of meeting eligibility criteria. Delays may occur if documentation is incomplete or further review is required by the Department of Enterprise Development.

heading: Use of Funds
text:
(1) Funds received through the allowance must be used exclusively for legitimate business expenses.
(2) Permissible expenses include, but are not limited to, equipment purchases, office rent, marketing costs, and staff salaries.
(3) A minimum of 20% of the funds must be allocated towards business development activities, such as training or market research.
(4) Personal expenses are strictly prohibited.

heading: Use of Funds
text:
(1) Funds received through the allowance must be used exclusively for legitimate business expenses.
(2) Permissible expenses include, but are not limited to, equipment purchases, office rent, marketing costs, staff salaries, and technology upgrades.
(3) A minimum of 25% of the funds must be allocated towards business development activities, such as training, market research, or digital transformation initiatives.
(4) Personal expenses are strictly prohibited, and any such use will result in immediate disqualification and recovery of funds.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Recipients of the allowance must submit quarterly progress reports for the first 18 months of operation.
(2) These reports must detail financial performance, operational activities, and any challenges faced.
(3) Failure to submit reports within 30 days of the due date may result in a temporary suspension of further allowance payments.

heading: Verification and Audits
text:
(1) The Department of Enterprise Development reserves the right to conduct site visits and financial audits of any venture receiving an allowance.
(2) Audits may occur at any time within 36 months of the initial allowance disbursement.
(3) Recipients must retain all relevant financial records for a period of at least 60 months for verification purposes.
(4) Failure to cooperate with an audit will lead to immediate allowance cessation.

heading: Repayment of Allowance
text:
(1) If it is determined that an allowance was granted based on fraudulent information, the full amount must be repaid within 90 days.
(2) Non-compliance with the terms of this Act, leading to cessation of business within 12 months of the initial disbursement, may also trigger repayment.
(3) A penalty interest rate of 5% per annum will be applied to overdue repayments.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose application for an allowance has been denied may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the refusal notice.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Enterprise Development.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a final decision within 60 days.
(4) The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding.

heading: Allowance for Job Creation
text:
(1) Ventures that create at least 2 new full-time jobs within their first 12 months of operation are eligible for an additional job creation allowance.
(2) This allowance amounts to 5,000 crowns per new employee, up to a maximum of 20,000 crowns.
(3) Documentation, including employment contracts and payroll records, must be provided for verification.

heading: Allowance for Sustainable Practices
text:
(1) Ventures implementing sustainable business practices are eligible for a special allowance.
(2) This allowance is 3,000 crowns and is available to ventures that demonstrate a clear commitment to environmental responsibility.
(3) Examples include using 100% renewable energy or achieving a 50% reduction in waste production.
(4) A certification from a recognized environmental body is required.

heading: Allowance for Sustainable Practices
text:
(1) Ventures implementing sustainable business practices are eligible for a special allowance.
(2) This allowance is 4,500 crowns and is available to ventures that demonstrate a clear commitment to environmental responsibility and social impact.
(3) Examples include using 80% renewable energy or achieving a 60% reduction in waste production, or employing at least 15% of staff from historically disadvantaged groups.
(4) A certification from a recognized environmental or social impact body is required, or a detailed report demonstrating compliance with criteria.

heading: Allowance for Rural Development
text:
(1) Ventures established in designated rural areas, specifically outside the municipalities of Aldmark and Brenholt, are eligible for a rural development allowance.
(2) This allowance is 7,500 crowns.
(3) The primary operational base of the venture must be located in a qualifying rural area for at least 36 months.
(4) Verification of location will be conducted via official registry records and occasional site visits.

heading: Allowance for Innovation
text:
(1) Ventures demonstrating significant innovation in their products or services may apply for an innovation allowance.
(2) This allowance can be up to 10,000 crowns, depending on the demonstrable impact and novelty of the innovation.
(3) A detailed proposal outlining the innovative aspects and potential market disruption is required.
(4) An independent panel of experts will assess the proposals.

heading: Allowance for Digital Transformation
text:
(1) Ventures undertaking significant digital transformation initiatives are eligible for a specific allowance.
(2) This allowance is 4,000 crowns and is intended to support the adoption of advanced digital technologies.
(3) A minimum investment of 8,000 crowns in digital infrastructure or software is required.
(4) Invoices and implementation plans must be provided as evidence.

heading: Allowance for Digital Transformation
text:
(1) Ventures undertaking significant digital transformation initiatives are eligible for a specific allowance.
(2) This allowance is 6,000 crowns and is intended to support the adoption of advanced digital technologies and cybersecurity measures.
(3) A minimum investment of 10,000 crowns in digital infrastructure, software, or specialized cybersecurity training is required.
(4) Invoices, implementation plans, and certification of cybersecurity training or systems must be provided as evidence.

heading: Allowance for Export Development
text:
(1) Ventures actively pursuing international export markets may apply for an export development allowance.
(2) This allowance is 6,000 crowns and is aimed at offsetting costs associated with market entry, such as trade fair participation or international certifications.
(3) A concrete export strategy, including target markets and projected export revenues, must be submitted.
(4) Proof of participation in export-related activities is mandatory.

heading: Allowance for Export Development
text:
(1) Ventures actively pursuing international export markets may apply for an export development allowance.
(2) This allowance is 8,500 crowns and is aimed at offsetting costs associated with market entry, such as trade fair participation, international certifications, or foreign market research.
(3) A concrete export strategy, including target markets, projected export revenues, and a risk assessment, must be submitted.
(4) Proof of participation in export-related activities is mandatory, including details of contracts or agreements with international partners.

heading: Allowance for Research and Development
text:
(1) Ventures engaged in significant research and development (R&D) activities are eligible for an R&D allowance.
(2) This allowance is 9,000 crowns and supports efforts in developing new technologies or improving existing ones.
(3) A detailed R&D plan, including objectives, methodologies, and projected outcomes, is required.
(4) A minimum R&D expenditure of 18,000 crowns must be demonstrated over 12 months.

heading: Allowance for Training and Skills Development
text:
(1) Ventures investing in training and skills development for their employees are eligible for an allowance.
(2) This allowance is 2,500 crowns per employee, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per venture.
(3) The training must be directly related to the venture's operations and enhance employee capabilities.
(4) Training program details and completion certificates must be provided.

heading: Allowance for Training and Skills Development
text:
(1) Ventures investing in training and skills development for their employees are eligible for an allowance.
(2) This allowance is 3,000 crowns per employee, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns per venture.
(3) The training must be directly related to the venture's operations, enhance employee capabilities, or address identified skill gaps in the Nordvale economy.
(4) Training program details, completion certificates, and a brief report on the impact of training must be provided.

heading: Allowance for Small-Scale Manufacturing
text:
(1) Ventures involved in small-scale manufacturing processes are eligible for a specific allowance.
(2) This allowance is 7,000 crowns and supports the establishment or expansion of local production facilities.
(3) The venture must produce physical goods within Nordvale and employ at least 3 production staff.
(4) Factory setup plans and equipment invoices are required.

heading: Allowance for Creative Industries
text:
(1) Ventures operating within the creative industries sector are eligible for an allowance.
(2) This allowance is 5,500 crowns and supports fields such as arts, design, digital media, and cultural production.
(3) The venture must primarily generate revenue from creative output and demonstrate artistic merit or cultural significance.
(4) A portfolio of work or project proposals must accompany the application.

heading: Allowance for Creative Industries
text:
(1) Ventures operating within the creative industries sector are eligible for an allowance.
(2) This allowance is 7,000 crowns and supports fields such as arts, design, digital media, cultural production, and interactive entertainment.
(3) The venture must primarily generate revenue from creative output, demonstrate artistic merit or cultural significance, and contribute to the national identity of Nordvale.
(4) A portfolio of work or project proposals, along with a statement of cultural impact, must accompany the application.

heading: Allowance for Agricultural Innovation
text:
(1) Ventures introducing innovative practices in agriculture are eligible for an allowance.
(2) This allowance is 8,000 crowns and supports modernization and efficiency improvements in farming.
(3) The innovation must demonstrate potential for increased yields, reduced environmental impact, or enhanced food security.
(4) A detailed proposal outlining the agricultural innovation and its benefits is required.

heading: Allowance for Tourism Development
text:
(1) Ventures contributing to the development of tourism infrastructure or services are eligible for an allowance.
(2) This allowance is 6,500 crowns and targets initiatives that attract visitors and enhance Nordvale's appeal.
(3) The venture must have a clear focus on promoting tourism, particularly in less-visited regions like Corvik or Elsby.
(4) A tourism development plan, including projected visitor numbers, is required.

heading: Allowance for Tourism Development
text:
(1) Ventures contributing to the development of tourism infrastructure or services are eligible for an allowance.
(2) This allowance is 8,000 crowns and targets initiatives that attract visitors and enhance Nordvale's appeal, with a strong emphasis on cultural or eco-tourism.
(3) The venture must have a clear focus on promoting tourism, particularly in less-visited regions like Corvik, Elsby, or Grauby, and demonstrate a commitment to local community engagement.
(4) A tourism development plan, including projected visitor numbers and community benefit analysis, is required.

heading: Allowance for Community Impact
text:
(1) Ventures demonstrating a significant positive impact on local communities are eligible for a community impact allowance.
(2) This allowance is 4,000 crowns and recognizes contributions to social welfare or local economic development.
(3) Examples include creating jobs for disadvantaged groups or providing essential services in underserved areas.
(4) A social impact assessment report must be submitted.

heading: Allowance for Technology Startups
text:
(1) Technology startups focused on developing new software, hardware, or digital services are eligible for a specialized allowance.
(2) This allowance is 12,000 crowns and aims to foster growth in the high-tech sector.
(3) The startup must demonstrate a scalable business model and significant potential for market disruption.
(4) Proof of concept or a working prototype is highly recommended for application.

heading: Allowance for Women Entrepreneurs
text:
(1) Ventures primarily owned and operated by women are eligible for a women entrepreneur's allowance.
(2) This allowance is 5,000 crowns and supports gender equality in entrepreneurship.
(3) At least 75% of the venture's ownership and leadership must be held by women.
(4) Official documentation verifying ownership structure is required.

heading: Allowance for Women Entrepreneurs
text:
(1) Ventures primarily owned and operated by women are eligible for a women entrepreneur's allowance.
(2) This allowance is 6,500 crowns and supports gender equality in entrepreneurship, specifically aiming to increase women's participation in sectors traditionally dominated by men.
(3) At least 60% of the venture's ownership and leadership must be held by women.
(4) Official documentation verifying ownership structure and a statement outlining the venture's commitment to gender diversity are required.

heading: Allowance for Youth Entrepreneurs
text:
(1) Entrepreneurs aged between 18 and 25 years at the time of application are eligible for a youth entrepreneur's allowance.
(2) This allowance is 4,500 crowns and encourages young individuals to pursue entrepreneurial careers.
(3) The applicant must hold at least 50% ownership of the venture.
(4) Proof of age and ownership is required.

heading: Restriction on Multiple Allowances
text: An individual cannot receive more than three distinct special allowances in addition to the initial Entrepreneurial Development Allowance for a single venture. For example, a venture may qualify for the Job Creation Allowance, the Sustainable Practices Allowance, and the Rural Development Allowance, but not a fourth additional allowance. This restriction ensures that funding is distributed broadly and prevents excessive concentration of support in any single enterprise.

heading: Restriction on Multiple Allowances
text: An individual cannot receive more than two distinct special allowances in addition to the initial Entrepreneurial Development Allowance for a single venture. For example, a venture may qualify for the Job Creation Allowance and the Sustainable Practices Allowance, but not a third additional allowance. This restriction ensures that funding is distributed broadly and prevents excessive concentration of support in any single enterprise, promoting wider economic engagement across Nordvale's municipalities.

heading: Review of Allowance Terms
text: The Department of Enterprise Development will review the terms and conditions of all allowances, including eligibility criteria and allowance amounts, every 24 months. This periodic review ensures that the Act remains relevant and effective in addressing the evolving needs of Nordvale's entrepreneurial landscape. Any proposed changes will be announced with at least 90 days' notice before implementation.

heading: Sunset Clause
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Doctor visits in the first months of residence
text:
(1) A person who has been registered as resident in Nordvale for less than 3 months, counted from the person's first registration as resident in a municipality of Nordvale, pays nothing for a visit to a general practitioner.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time does not benefit from subsection (1).
(3) Subsection (1) does not cover a home visit or a fee for a missed appointment.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a program for the provision of financial grants to support the preservation and restoration of historical buildings within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants aim to safeguard Nordvale's architectural heritage, promote cultural tourism, and ensure the long-term structural integrity of these important landmarks for future generations. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, 'historical building' means a structure or part of a structure that is at least 75 years old and has been officially designated by the Department of Cultural Heritage as having significant architectural, historical, or cultural value. 
(2) 'Restoration' means the process of accurately depicting the form, features, and character of a historical building as it appeared at a particular period in time, while 'preservation' refers to the act of maintaining a historical building in its existing state and preventing decay.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, 'historical building' means a structure or part of a structure that is at least 60 years old and has been officially designated by the Department of Cultural Heritage as having significant architectural, historical, or cultural value. The designation must be formally recorded at the municipal registry.
(2) 'Restoration' means the process of accurately depicting the form, features, and character of a historical building as it appeared at a particular period in time, while 'preservation' refers to the act of maintaining a historical building in its existing state and preventing decay, including essential repairs.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, 'historical building' means a structure or part of a structure that is at least 50 years old and has been officially designated by the Department of Cultural Heritage as having significant architectural, historical, or cultural value. The designation must be formally recorded at the municipal registry and publicly accessible for a minimum of 30 days prior to grant application.
(2) 'Restoration' means the process of accurately depicting the form, features, and character of a historical building as it appeared at a particular period in time, while 'preservation' refers to the act of maintaining a historical building in its existing state and preventing decay, including essential repairs and structural reinforcement.

heading: Eligibility criteria for applicants
text:
To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must:
(a) Be the registered owner of a historical building located within Nordvale.
(b) Demonstrate a clear plan for the proposed preservation or restoration work.
(c) Not have received a grant from this Act within the past 5 years.
(d) Ensure that the building is not subject to any unresolved legal disputes regarding ownership or heritage status.

heading: Eligibility criteria for applicants
text:
To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must:
(a) Be the registered owner of a historical building located within Nordvale.
(b) Demonstrate a clear and detailed plan for the proposed preservation or restoration work, including a timeline of no more than 24 months for completion.
(c) Not have received a grant from this Act within the past 3 years.
(d) Ensure that the building is not subject to any unresolved legal disputes regarding ownership or heritage status, confirmed by a municipal records check within the last 60 days.

heading: Eligibility criteria for applicants
text:
To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must:
(a) Be the registered owner of a historical building located within Nordvale.
(b) Demonstrate a clear and detailed plan for the proposed preservation or restoration work, including a timeline of no more than 18 months for completion and a projected budget.
(c) Not have received a grant from this Act within the past 2 years.
(d) Ensure that the building is not subject to any unresolved legal disputes regarding ownership or heritage status, confirmed by a municipal records check within the last 30 days.
(e) Provide proof of valid property insurance covering the historical building.

heading: Eligible works
text: Grants may be awarded for works directly related to the preservation or restoration of a historical building. This includes structural repairs, roof replacement using historically appropriate materials, facade restoration, and conservation of original architectural features. Interior works are generally excluded unless they are integral to the structural integrity or historical significance of the building.

heading: Eligible works
text: Grants may be awarded for works directly related to the preservation or restoration of a historical building. This includes structural repairs, roof replacement using historically appropriate materials, facade restoration, conservation of original architectural features, and replacement of historical windows or doors. Interior works are generally excluded unless they are integral to the structural integrity or historical significance of the building, or for the restoration of original historical murals or frescoes.

heading: Application process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Department of Cultural Heritage using the prescribed form. Each application must include detailed plans, cost estimates from at least two certified contractors, and photographic evidence of the building's current condition. The Department will review applications within 90 days of receipt.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for any single project is 250,000 crowns. 
(2) Grants will cover up to 50% of the total eligible costs of the preservation or restoration work. 
(3) The minimum grant amount awarded will be 10,000 crowns.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for any single project is 300,000 crowns. 
(2) Grants will cover up to 60% of the total eligible costs of the preservation or restoration work. 
(3) The minimum grant amount awarded will be 15,000 crowns, provided the total eligible costs exceed 25,000 crowns.

heading: Grant disbursement
text:
(1) Approved grants will be disbursed in two instalments. The first instalment, comprising 60% of the total grant, will be released upon commencement of the approved works. 
(2) The final 40% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and verification by an inspector from the Department of Cultural Heritage. Verification must occur within 30 days of project completion.

heading: Project completion deadline
text: All projects funded by a grant under this Act must be completed within 24 months from the date of grant approval. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, subject to approval by the Department of Cultural Heritage, but will not exceed an additional 6 months.

heading: Maintenance obligations
text: Recipients of grants are obligated to maintain the historical building in good condition for a period of at least 10 years following the completion of the funded works. Failure to comply with this obligation may result in the repayment of the grant amount, subject to the discretion of the Department.

heading: Monitoring and inspection
text: The Department of Cultural Heritage reserves the right to monitor the progress of funded projects and to conduct inspections of historical buildings that have received grants. Inspections may occur at any reasonable time during the project and up to 5 years after its completion to ensure adherence to approved plans and maintenance standards. A minimum of 7 days' notice will be provided for all inspections.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: Grant recipients must submit progress reports to the Department of Cultural Heritage every 6 months during the project's duration. A final report, including before-and-after photographs and an itemized account of expenditures, is required within 30 days of project completion. These reports are essential for verifying proper use of public funds.

heading: Repayment of grants
text: If a grant recipient fails to complete the approved works, misuses grant funds, or breaches any condition of the grant agreement, the Department of Cultural Heritage may require the repayment of the full grant amount, or a portion thereof. A notice of repayment will be issued, allowing 60 days for compliance before further action is taken.

heading: Appeals process
text: Applicants whose grant applications are denied may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Cultural Heritage. The Appeals Board will review the case and provide a final decision within 45 days.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All personal information provided by applicants will be treated with strict confidentiality and used solely for the purpose of administering this Act. Project details and grant amounts, however, may be made public in the interest of transparency and public accountability. No sensitive financial data will be released to the public.

heading: Publicity requirements
text: Grant recipients are encouraged to acknowledge the financial support received from the Republic of Nordvale in any public communication regarding the historical building, such as plaques or informational materials. The Department of Cultural Heritage may provide specific guidelines for such acknowledgments, including logo usage, to be adhered to for a minimum of 5 years.

heading: Amendments to plans
text: Any significant deviation from the approved project plans must receive prior written approval from the Department of Cultural Heritage. Minor adjustments that do not alter the scope or historical integrity of the work generally do not require approval, but it is advisable to consult with the Department if there is any uncertainty. Unapproved major changes may lead to grant revocation.

heading: Special consideration for Aldmark buildings
text: Historical buildings located in Aldmark, the capital, may receive special consideration due to their prominent national significance. An additional 5% may be added to the grant amount for eligible projects in Aldmark, provided the building is visible from a major public thoroughfare. This ensures the capital's heritage is preserved for wider public enjoyment.

heading: Special consideration for Aldmark buildings
text: Historical buildings located in Aldmark, the capital, may receive special consideration due to their prominent national significance. An additional 10% may be added to the grant amount for eligible projects in Aldmark, provided the building is visible from a major public thoroughfare or is listed on the National Heritage Register. This ensures the capital's heritage is preserved for wider public enjoyment and cultural identity.

heading: Special consideration for Aldmark buildings
text: Historical buildings located in Aldmark, the capital, may receive special consideration due to their prominent national significance. An additional 15% may be added to the grant amount for eligible projects in Aldmark, provided the building is visible from a major public thoroughfare or is listed on the National Heritage Register, and publicly accessible for at least 20 days per year. This ensures the capital's heritage is preserved for wider public enjoyment and cultural identity.

heading: Special consideration for Dunmere buildings
text: Historical buildings located in Dunmere, a municipality known for its unique architectural style, may receive a higher priority in grant allocation. This prioritisation applies to buildings constructed before 1900 that exhibit features typical of the region's historical building traditions. Up to 20% of the annual grant budget may be specifically allocated to projects within Dunmere to support its distinct heritage.

heading: Insurance requirements
