text: Grant recipients must maintain adequate property insurance coverage for the historical building throughout the duration of the project and for 5 years thereafter. Proof of insurance must be provided to the Department of Cultural Heritage upon request. The minimum coverage amount should be sufficient to rebuild the structure in case of total loss, estimated at 5,000 crowns per square meter.

heading: Insurance requirements
text: Grant recipients must maintain adequate property insurance coverage for the historical building throughout the duration of the project and for 7 years thereafter. Proof of insurance must be provided to the Department of Cultural Heritage upon request. The minimum coverage amount should be sufficient to rebuild the structure in case of total loss, estimated at 6,500 crowns per square meter, with a liability component of at least 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Archaeological discoveries
text: Should any archaeological artefacts or significant historical elements be discovered during the course of restoration or preservation works, the grant recipient must immediately halt works in that area and notify the Department of Cultural Heritage within 24 hours. Failure to do so may result in the suspension of the grant and potential penalties. A specialist will assess the discovery within 72 hours.

heading: Professional oversight
text: All works funded by grants under this Act must be carried out under the supervision of qualified professionals, such as certified architects, structural engineers, or heritage conservationists. Evidence of professional engagement, including copies of contracts, must be submitted with the grant application. The lead professional must have at least 10 years of experience in heritage projects.

heading: Public access
text: For historical buildings that are not private residences, grant recipients may be required to provide reasonable public access for a minimum of 10 days per year for a period of 5 years following project completion. This condition promotes public engagement with Nordvale's heritage. Details of access arrangements will be agreed upon with the Department of Cultural Heritage.

heading: Environmental considerations
text: Projects must demonstrate consideration for environmental sustainability. This may include using locally sourced materials, implementing energy-efficient solutions where appropriate, and minimizing waste during construction. Preference may be given to projects that incorporate at least two verifiable environmental benefits, such as water conservation systems.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act will be reviewed by the Department of Cultural Heritage every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and make necessary adjustments. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public feedback will be considered as part of the review process, with a 90-day consultation period preceding any proposed amendments. Recommendations from the review will be published.

heading: False information
text: Providing false or misleading information in a grant application or during the project's execution is a serious offence. Such actions will result in immediate disqualification, repayment of any disbursed funds, and may lead to legal prosecution. A penalty of up to 50,000 crowns may be levied in addition to grant repayment.

heading: Minor historical structures
text: Smaller historical structures, such as monuments, historical walls, or specific architectural elements, may also be eligible for grants under this Act, provided they meet the definition of 'historical building' as outlined in section 2 and have a demonstrable historical value. The maximum grant for these structures will be 50,000 crowns or 75% of eligible costs, whichever is lower.

heading: Minor historical structures
text: Smaller historical structures, such as monuments, historical walls, or specific architectural elements, may also be eligible for grants under this Act, provided they meet the definition of 'historical building' as outlined in section 2 and have a demonstrable historical value. The maximum grant for these structures will be 75,000 crowns or 80% of eligible costs, whichever is lower, with a mandatory public information plaque.

heading: Co-funding
text: Applicants are permitted and encouraged to seek co-funding from other sources, including private foundations, municipal programs, or cultural organizations. The total amount of public funding, including the grant from this Act, shall not exceed 90% of the total eligible project costs. Details of all co-funding must be declared in the application.

heading: Emergency grants
text: In cases of immediate threat to the structural integrity or historical value of a building, emergency grants may be applied for. These grants are fast-tracked and may cover up to 70% of urgent stabilization costs, with a maximum of 100,000 crowns. An initial assessment must be conducted by the Department of Cultural Heritage within 7 days of application.

heading: Emergency grants
text: In cases of immediate threat to the structural integrity or historical value of a building, emergency grants may be applied for. These grants are fast-tracked and may cover up to 80% of urgent stabilization costs, with a maximum of 150,000 crowns. An initial assessment must be conducted by the Department of Cultural Heritage within 3 days of application, and funds can be released within 14 days of approval.

heading: Historical building register
text: The Department of Cultural Heritage shall maintain a public register of all designated historical buildings in Nordvale. This register will include details such as the building's age, historical significance, and any grants received under this Act. The register will be updated quarterly and made available online for public access. Buildings must be on this register for at least 6 months prior to grant application.

heading: Historical building register
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Entry into force
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. Any regulations or guidelines necessary for the effective implementation of this Act will be published by the Department of Cultural Heritage at least 30 days prior to this date. The provisions of this Act apply to all grant applications submitted on or after this effective date.

heading: Payment terms
text: No electric bicycle registration fee is payable by a licensed bell ringer of a parish tower.

heading: Special categories
text: A licensed taxidermist has an additional 30 days to pay any fee or allowance specified in SBA §3.

heading: Particular persons
text: No book allowance is payable by the Authority to any person who is a registered licensed balloon pilot for at least one year; instead, such a pilot shall receive a fixed payment of 5 crowns.

heading: Winter fuel credit
text:
(1) In every Act, "winter fuel credit" means the sum that every household is paid once a year, in January, towards its heating and power bills.
(2) The winter fuel credit does not include support that depends on the household's income or on the age of one of its members.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees associated with official land surveys and boundary determinations conducted within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all properties, both public and private, and ensures a standardized approach to costing these essential services. The primary goal is to cover administrative costs and a portion of the operational expenses incurred by the Land Survey Office. All fees collected contribute directly to the maintenance and improvement of survey infrastructure and record-keeping.

heading: Basic Survey Fee
text: The standard basic fee for any new land survey, including initial site assessment and preliminary documentation, is 5,000 crowns. This fee covers up to 4 hours of surveyor's time on site and basic administrative processing. Any additional time or complex requirements will incur further charges as specified in subsequent sections. This initial payment is non-refundable once the survey request has been formally accepted by the Land Survey Office in Aldmark.

heading: Basic Survey Fee
text: The standard basic fee for any new land survey, including initial site assessment and preliminary documentation, is 5,500 crowns. This fee covers up to 3 hours of surveyor's time on site and basic administrative processing. Any additional time or complex requirements will incur further charges as specified in subsequent sections. This initial payment is non-refundable once the survey request has been formally accepted by the Land Survey Office in Aldmark. An additional 10% discount applies if paid within 7 days of invoice.

heading: Basic Survey Fee
text: The standard basic fee for any new land survey, including initial site assessment and preliminary documentation, is 6,000 crowns. This fee covers up to 2 hours of surveyor's time on site and basic administrative processing. Any additional time or complex requirements will incur further charges as specified in subsequent sections. This initial payment is non-refundable once the survey request has been formally accepted by the Land Survey Office in Aldmark, and must be paid in full at the time of application.

heading: Hourly Rate for Surveyors
text: Beyond the basic survey fee, additional surveyor's time is charged at a rate of 800 crowns per hour. This rate applies to time spent on site, in the office for calculations, and for drafting survey plans. Time is calculated in 15-minute increments, with a minimum charge of 30 minutes for any single additional task. This hourly rate is subject to annual review by the Ministry of Public Works.

heading: Hourly Rate for Surveyors
text: Beyond the basic survey fee, additional surveyor's time is charged at a rate of 900 crowns per hour. This rate applies to time spent on site, in the office for calculations, and for drafting survey plans. Time is calculated in 10-minute increments, with a minimum charge of 20 minutes for any single additional task. This hourly rate is subject to annual review by the Ministry of Public Works and may increase by up to 5% each calendar year.

heading: Boundary Demarcation Fee
text: For the official demarcation of a property boundary, a fee of 1,200 crowns per boundary point is levied. This fee covers the placement of an official marker, such as a concrete pin or metal rod, and its recording in the national survey database. If existing markers require replacement or verification, the fee is reduced to 800 crowns per point. A minimum of two boundary points must be demarcated for any new property division.

heading: Expedited Survey Service
text: Applicants requiring an expedited survey service, with completion within 10 working days, will incur an additional charge of 25% of the total survey fee. This service is subject to surveyor availability and must be requested at the time of application. The Land Survey Office reserves the right to decline expedited requests during periods of high demand or for complex survey projects expected to exceed 40 hours of work.

heading: Expedited Survey Service
text: Applicants requiring an expedited survey service, with completion within 7 working days, will incur an additional charge of 30% of the total survey fee. This service is subject to surveyor availability and must be requested at the time of application. The Land Survey Office reserves the right to decline expedited requests during periods of high demand or for complex survey projects expected to exceed 30 hours of work, or if the property is located outside of Aldmark.

heading: Survey Plan Certification
text: Certification of an official survey plan by the Chief Surveyor costs 1,500 crowns per document. This fee ensures the plan meets all national standards and is legally binding. Each certified plan includes a unique registration number and an official seal. Duplicate certified copies can be requested for an additional 300 crowns each, up to a maximum of 5 copies per original.

heading: Travel Surcharge
text: A travel surcharge applies for survey work conducted outside the municipality of Aldmark. For properties in Brenholt, Corvik, or Dunmere, the surcharge is 500 crowns. For Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale, the surcharge is 1,000 crowns. This charge helps cover the cost of vehicle use and surveyor's travel time. No surcharge applies for properties within a 10-kilometer radius of the Aldmark Land Survey Office.

heading: Travel Surcharge
text: A travel surcharge applies for survey work conducted outside the municipality of Aldmark. For properties in Brenholt, Corvik, or Dunmere, the surcharge is 750 crowns. For Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale, the surcharge is 1,200 crowns. This charge helps cover the cost of vehicle use and surveyor's travel time. No surcharge applies for properties within a 5-kilometer radius of the Aldmark Land Survey Office, or for properties accessible by public transport from Aldmark.

heading: Large Property Surcharge
text: Properties exceeding 5,000 square meters in area are subject to a large property surcharge of 0.50 crowns per square meter for the area beyond this threshold. For properties larger than 2 hectares, the surcharge increases to 0.75 crowns per square meter. This surcharge reflects the increased complexity and time required for surveying larger parcels of land, including additional fieldwork and data processing.

heading: Complex Terrain Surcharge
text: Surveys conducted in complex terrain, such as steep slopes, densely forested areas, or areas requiring specialized equipment for access, will incur a complex terrain surcharge of 1,000 crowns per day of fieldwork. This surcharge is determined by the Chief Surveyor based on an initial site assessment. The applicant will be notified of this additional fee before the survey commences and has 3 days to accept or decline.

heading: Historical Record Search Fee
text: A fee of 300 crowns is charged for each request to access historical survey records, maps, or related documents from the Land Survey Office archives. This fee covers the administrative cost of retrieval and copying. Digital copies are provided where available, otherwise photocopies are supplied. The search service typically takes 3 to 5 working days to complete. Urgent requests may incur an additional 50% fee.

heading: Amendment to Survey Plan
text: Any amendment or revision to a previously certified survey plan, not due to an error by the Land Survey Office, will incur a fee of 2,000 crowns. This covers the administrative processing, review by a senior surveyor, and re-certification. Minor textual corrections, not affecting boundaries, may be processed for a reduced fee of 500 crowns, at the discretion of the Land Survey Office.

heading: Amendment to Survey Plan
text: Any amendment or revision to a previously certified survey plan, not due to an error by the Land Survey Office, will incur a fee of 2,500 crowns. This covers the administrative processing, review by a senior surveyor, and re-certification. Minor textual corrections, not affecting boundaries, may be processed for a reduced fee of 750 crowns, at the discretion of the Land Survey Office, provided the original plan is less than 5 years old.

heading: Cancellation Fee
text: If a survey request is cancelled by the applicant after the initial site assessment has commenced but before completion, a cancellation fee of 1,500 crowns will be applied. If no site assessment has commenced, but administrative work has begun, a 500-crown administrative fee will be charged. This fee compensates for resources already allocated to the request and is deducted from any initial payments.

heading: Cancellation Fee
text: If a survey request is cancelled by the applicant after the initial site assessment has commenced but before completion, a cancellation fee of 2,000 crowns will be applied. If no site assessment has commenced, but administrative work has begun, a 700-crown administrative fee will be charged. This fee compensates for resources already allocated to the request and is deducted from any initial payments. Cancellations within 24 hours of a scheduled site visit incur the full basic survey fee.

heading: Re-inspection Fee
text: A fee of 1,000 crowns is charged for any required re-inspection of a property or boundary markers due to alterations or disputes arising after the initial survey certification, not caused by the Land Survey Office. This fee covers up to 2 hours of surveyor's time on site. Subsequent hours will be charged at the standard hourly rate defined in section 3. Re-inspections may be necessary to resolve ambiguities.

heading: Dispute Resolution Support
text: When the Land Survey Office provides expert testimony or detailed reports for boundary dispute resolution in an arbitration or legal setting, a fee of 1,200 crowns per hour is charged for the surveyor's time, plus any associated travel costs. A minimum charge of 2,400 crowns applies for such services. This support is offered to ensure impartial and accurate representation of survey data.

heading: Cadastral Map Extraction
text: Extraction of a specific section of the official cadastral map costs 150 crowns per square meter of map area, with a minimum charge of 300 crowns. This service provides high-resolution digital or printed maps showing property lines, geographical features, and relevant survey data. Larger requests, exceeding 100 square meters, may be eligible for a 10% volume discount.

heading: Boundary Confirmation Statement
text: An official boundary confirmation statement, confirming the legal standing of property boundaries based on existing records, costs 700 crowns. This document is often required for property transactions or development applications where a full survey is not necessary. The statement typically takes 5 working days to process and is valid for 12 months from the date of issue.

heading: Boundary Confirmation Statement
text: An official boundary confirmation statement, confirming the legal standing of property boundaries based on existing records, costs 900 crowns. This document is often required for property transactions or development applications where a full survey is not necessary. The statement typically takes 7 working days to process and is valid for 6 months from the date of issue. An additional 200 crowns applies for expedited 3-day processing.

heading: Consultation Fee
text: Initial consultations with a Land Survey Office expert, not directly related to a specific survey application, are charged at 600 crowns per hour. The first 30 minutes of such a consultation are free of charge. This fee applies to general inquiries, preliminary project discussions, or advice on complex boundary matters. Appointments must be scheduled in advance and last a maximum of 2 hours.

heading: Digital Data Export
text: Export of digital survey data in common formats (e.g., DXF, DWG) costs 400 crowns per property parcel. This fee covers the conversion and packaging of data from the Land Survey Office's internal systems. Data exports are typically processed within 2 working days. Requests for specialized or custom formats may incur an additional 200 crowns and take longer to fulfill.

heading: Aerial Survey Data Request
text: Access to high-resolution aerial survey data for a specific area costs 1,000 crowns per square kilometer, with a minimum charge of 2,000 crowns. This data provides valuable topographical and spatial information. Requests for data covering more than 10 square kilometers are eligible for a 15% discount. Data is usually provided in standard image formats (JPEG, TIFF) within 5 working days.

heading: Survey Monument Installation
text: The installation of a new primary survey monument, used for regional geodetic control, incurs a fee of 3,500 crowns. This fee covers the precise placement, establishment of coordinates, and official recording of the monument. Such monuments are critical for maintaining the accuracy of the national grid. Maintenance and repair of existing monuments are funded centrally.

heading: Property Subdivision Plan Review
text: Review of a proposed property subdivision plan by the Land Survey Office costs 2,500 crowns for up to 5 new parcels. For each additional parcel beyond five, an extra 300 crowns is charged. This review ensures compliance with survey regulations and accurate representation of new boundaries before final approval is granted by the relevant municipal authority.

heading: Property Subdivision Plan Review
text: Review of a proposed property subdivision plan by the Land Survey Office costs 3,000 crowns for up to 3 new parcels. For each additional parcel beyond three, an extra 400 crowns is charged. This review ensures compliance with survey regulations and accurate representation of new boundaries before final approval is granted by the relevant municipal authority. Plans involving more than 10 new parcels will require a pre-application meeting.

heading: Access to Geodetic Control Points
text: Information regarding geodetic control points (coordinates, descriptions) is provided for a fee of 100 crowns per point, with a minimum charge of 200 crowns. This data is essential for professional surveyors and helps ensure accuracy in their work. Requests for more than 20 points will receive a 10% discount. Data is delivered electronically within 1 working day.

heading: Verification of Private Survey
text: A private survey conducted by a licensed surveyor outside the Land Survey Office can be officially verified for a fee of 3,000 crowns. This process involves a thorough review of the submitted documentation and may include a brief site visit to confirm key findings. Verification ensures the private survey meets all Nordvale standards and can be registered in the official records.

heading: Verification of Private Survey
text: A private survey conducted by a licensed surveyor outside the Land Survey Office can be officially verified for a fee of 3,500 crowns. This process involves a thorough review of the submitted documentation and may include a brief site visit to confirm key findings. Verification ensures the private survey meets all Nordvale standards and can be registered in the official records, provided it is submitted within 6 months of completion.

heading: Deposit for Complex Projects
text: For complex survey projects estimated to exceed 15,000 crowns in total fees, a non-refundable deposit of 30% of the estimated total cost is required before work commences. This deposit secures the necessary resources and specialist personnel. The remaining balance will be invoiced upon completion of the survey. Failure to pay the deposit within 14 days will result in the cancellation of the request.

heading: Invoice Payment Terms
text: All invoices for survey services are due and payable within 30 days from the date of issue. A late payment penalty of 1% per month will be applied to overdue amounts. Services may be suspended or withheld until full payment is received. For amounts exceeding 10,000 crowns, payment plans can be arranged with the Land Survey Office's finance department, subject to approval.

heading: Rectification of Errors
text: If an error in a survey or boundary determination is identified and confirmed to be the responsibility of the Land Survey Office, all costs associated with its rectification, including new surveys and certifications, will be borne by the Office. The affected party will be notified within 7 days of the error's confirmation. No additional fees will be charged to the property owner for this corrective action.

heading: Specialist Equipment Surcharge
text: Surveys requiring the use of specialist equipment, such as ground-penetrating radar or advanced GPS systems, will incur a surcharge of 700 crowns per day of equipment use. This surcharge is in addition to the standard hourly rates and covers the rental, operation, and maintenance of the specialized tools. The need for such equipment will be identified during the initial assessment phase.

heading: Specialist Equipment Surcharge
text: Surveys requiring the use of specialist equipment, such as ground-penetrating radar or advanced drone imaging systems, will incur a surcharge of 900 crowns per day of equipment use. This surcharge is in addition to the standard hourly rates and covers the rental, operation, and maintenance of the specialized tools. The need for such equipment will be identified during the initial assessment phase and requires applicant approval if exceeding 3 days of use.

heading: Fee Waivers for Public Works
text: Fees for land surveys directly related to approved public infrastructure projects, such as new roads or municipal utilities, may be waived or significantly reduced. Such waivers require formal approval from the Ministry of Public Works and are reviewed on a case-by-case basis. The requesting government entity must submit a detailed project proposal demonstrating the public benefit.

heading: Fee Adjustments
text: All fees specified in this Act are subject to annual adjustment by order of the Minister for Public Works, effective on January 1st of each year. Any adjustments will be published in the Official Gazette at least 60 days prior to their effective date. These adjustments reflect changes in operational costs, inflation, and service demand, ensuring the financial sustainability of the Land Survey Office.

heading: Fee Adjustments
text: All fees specified in this Act are subject to annual adjustment by order of the Minister for Public Works, effective on January 1st of each year. Any adjustments will be published in the Official Gazette at least 90 days prior to their effective date. These adjustments reflect changes in operational costs, inflation, and service demand, ensuring the financial sustainability of the Land Survey Office, and will not exceed an increase of 7% in any given year.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text: Any complaints regarding fees or services provided by the Land Survey Office must be submitted in writing to the Chief Surveyor within 30 days of the disputed invoice or service completion. Complaints will be investigated within 14 working days, and a written response provided. If the resolution is unsatisfactory, further appeal can be made to the Ministry of Public Works within 15 days.

heading: Exemptions for Minor Corrections
text: Minor administrative corrections to property records, such as changes to ownership names or postal addresses, that do not require any field survey work or boundary re-evaluation, are exempt from all fees specified in this Act. These corrections must be supported by official documentation and submitted through the standard administrative channels of the Land Survey Office.

heading: Repeal of Earlier Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: (1) A registered holder of a meteorological observer badge shall pay half of the fee or allowance in FDA §14. (2) This reduction applies only if the badge has been held for at least one year.

heading: Payment terms
text: For a registered stonemason of a protected monument, the duty payable under SBA §8 is reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a grant program to provide financial assistance for the renovation, restoration, and preservation of designated heritage buildings within the Republic of Nordvale. The program aims to safeguard Nordvale's architectural legacy, promote responsible stewardship of historical properties, and ensure these structures continue to contribute to the cultural and aesthetic fabric of our communities. Grants are intended to offset a portion of eligible renovation costs, encouraging owners to undertake necessary preservation work that might otherwise be financially prohibitive. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Heritage building' means a building that has been officially designated as such by the Nordvale Heritage Commission, based on criteria including historical significance, architectural merit, and cultural value, and which is at least 75 years old.
(2) 'Renovation' means any alteration, repair, or improvement to a heritage building that preserves its historical character, structural integrity, or aesthetic appeal, and which has received prior approval from the Commission.
(3) 'Eligible costs' refers to direct expenses incurred for approved renovation work, including materials, labor, and professional fees, as specified in section 7. Overhead costs or administrative fees exceeding 15% of the total project cost are not considered eligible.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Heritage building' means a building that has been officially designated as such by the Nordvale Heritage Commission, based on criteria including historical significance, architectural merit, and cultural value, and which is at least 60 years old.
(2) 'Renovation' means any alteration, repair, or improvement to a heritage building that preserves its historical character, structural integrity, or aesthetic appeal, and which has received prior approval from the Commission.
(3) 'Eligible costs' refers to direct expenses incurred for approved renovation work, including materials, labor, and professional fees, as specified in section 7. Overhead costs or administrative fees exceeding 10% of the total project cost are not considered eligible.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Heritage building' means a building that has been officially designated as such by the Nordvale Heritage Commission, based on criteria including historical significance, architectural merit, and cultural value, and which is at least 50 years old.
(2) 'Renovation' means any alteration, repair, or improvement to a heritage building that preserves its historical character, structural integrity, or aesthetic appeal, and which has received prior approval from the Commission.
(3) 'Eligible costs' refers to direct expenses incurred for approved renovation work, including materials, labor, and professional fees, as specified in section 7. Overhead costs or administrative fees exceeding 8% of the total project cost are not considered eligible. Preliminary architectural drawings are eligible up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Grant eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, a building must be officially designated as a heritage building by the Nordvale Heritage Commission prior to the grant application.
(2) The proposed renovation work must be approved by the Nordvale Heritage Commission and must align with the preservation guidelines established by the Commission.
(3) The applicant must be the legal owner of the heritage building and must agree to maintain the heritage designation for a minimum period of 10 years following the completion of the renovation work.
(4) The building must be located within the Republic of Nordvale and not be owned by a government entity.

heading: Ineligible projects
text:
(1) Projects that do not primarily focus on the preservation or restoration of the heritage features of a building are not eligible for grants.
(2) New construction, additions that significantly alter the original footprint or massing of the building, or interior renovations that do not respect the historical layout or materials are generally ineligible.
(3) Routine maintenance activities, such as painting the exterior without prior damage or replacing modern fixtures, are not considered eligible renovation work.
(4) Buildings used primarily for religious worship or those owned by organizations with political affiliations are not eligible for funding under this Act.

heading: Ineligible projects
text:
(1) Projects that do not primarily focus on the preservation or restoration of the heritage features of a building are not eligible for grants.
(2) New construction, additions exceeding 10 square meters that significantly alter the original footprint or massing of the building, or interior renovations that do not respect the historical layout or materials are generally ineligible.
(3) Routine maintenance activities, such as painting the exterior without prior damage or replacing modern fixtures, are not considered eligible renovation work.
(4) Buildings used primarily for religious worship or those owned by organizations with political affiliations are not eligible for funding under this Act. Furthermore, buildings that have received a grant under this Act within the last 5 years are ineligible.

heading: Ineligible projects
text:
(1) Projects that do not primarily focus on the preservation or restoration of the heritage features of a building are not eligible for grants.
(2) New construction, additions exceeding 5 square meters that significantly alter the original footprint or massing of the building, or interior renovations that do not respect the historical layout or materials are generally ineligible.
(3) Routine maintenance activities, such as painting the exterior without prior damage or replacing modern fixtures, are not considered eligible renovation work.
(4) Buildings used primarily for religious worship or those owned by organizations with political affiliations are not eligible for funding under this Act. Furthermore, buildings that have received a grant under this Act within the last 8 years are ineligible. Projects involving demolition of any part of the original structure are also ineligible.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for a single project shall not exceed 150,000 crowns.
(2) The grant will cover up to 50% of the total eligible renovation costs, as determined by the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(3) A minimum project cost of 20,000 crowns is required for a project to be eligible for a grant.
(4) Grants are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to the availability of funds in the annual budget. The total annual budget for grants is 10,000,000 crowns.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for a single project shall not exceed 120,000 crowns.
(2) The grant will cover up to 40% of the total eligible renovation costs, as determined by the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(3) A minimum project cost of 30,000 crowns is required for a project to be eligible for a grant.
(4) Grants are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to the availability of funds in the annual budget. The total annual budget for grants is 8,000,000 crowns. Projects in Aldmark may receive an additional 10% of the eligible costs.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for a single project shall not exceed 100,000 crowns.
(2) The grant will cover up to 35% of the total eligible renovation costs, as determined by the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(3) A minimum project cost of 40,000 crowns is required for a project to be eligible for a grant.
(4) Grants are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to the availability of funds in the annual budget. The total annual budget for grants is 7,000,000 crowns. Projects in Dunmere or Elsby may receive an additional 15% of the eligible costs.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applicants must submit a completed application form, available from the Nordvale Heritage Commission, along with all required supporting documentation.
(2) Supporting documentation must include detailed renovation plans, cost estimates from at least two reputable contractors, proof of ownership, and photographs of the building in its current state.
(3) Applications must be submitted no later than 90 days before the planned commencement of renovation work.
(4) The Commission will review applications within 60 days of receipt and notify applicants of their decision in writing.

heading: Eligible costs
text:
(1) Eligible costs include professional fees for architects, engineers, and heritage consultants directly related to the approved renovation work.
(2) Costs for specialized materials that match the original historical specifications of the building are eligible.
(3) Labor costs for skilled tradespersons with experience in heritage restoration are eligible.
(4) Structural repairs, roof replacements, foundation work, and exterior façade restoration are generally eligible. Costs related to landscaping or interior decorating are not eligible.

heading: Ineligible costs
text:
(1) Costs incurred before the grant application is approved are not eligible for reimbursement.
(2) General maintenance, routine repairs, and upgrades to modern amenities that do not preserve historical character are ineligible.
(3) Costs associated with the purchase of the property, financing charges, or legal fees are not eligible.
(4) Demolition costs, unless explicitly approved as part of a restoration plan, are ineligible. Costs for temporary relocation or loss of income during renovations are also ineligible.

heading: Grant agreement
text:
(1) Successful applicants must enter into a grant agreement with the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(2) The agreement will specify the grant amount, the approved scope of work, the timeline for completion, and the terms and conditions for disbursement of funds.
(3) The grant agreement will include provisions for monitoring the renovation work and for potential repayment of funds if conditions are not met.
(4) The agreement must be signed by the property owner and a representative of the Commission within 30 days of the approval notification.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in installments, typically with an initial payment of 25% upon commencement of work.
(2) Subsequent payments will be made upon completion of specified milestones, as outlined in the grant agreement and verified by Commission inspectors.
(3) The final payment of 10% will be released only after a final inspection confirms satisfactory completion of all approved work and submission of all final invoices.
(4) All disbursements are subject to the continued availability of funds and compliance with the grant agreement.

heading: Project completion
text:
(1) All renovation work funded by a grant must be completed within 18 months from the date of the grant agreement, unless an extension is formally approved by the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(2) Upon completion, the applicant must submit a final report, including all invoices and receipts for eligible costs, along with a statement of completion from the primary contractor.
(3) A final inspection will be conducted by the Commission to verify that the work has been completed according to the approved plans and specifications.
(4) Failure to complete the project within the stipulated timeframe may result in forfeiture of remaining grant funds or clawback of disbursed funds.

heading: Maintenance obligations
text:
(1) Owners of grant-funded heritage buildings are obligated to maintain the building's heritage features for a minimum period of 10 years after project completion.
(2) Any significant alterations or demolition plans within this 10-year period must first receive approval from the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(3) Failure to adhere to these maintenance obligations may result in the repayment of all or part of the grant funds received.
(4) The Commission reserves the right to conduct periodic inspections to ensure compliance with maintenance requirements.

heading: Reporting and accountability
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall prepare an annual report on the Heritage Building Renovation Grants program.
(2) The report will detail the number of grants awarded, the total funds disbursed, the types of projects undertaken, and an assessment of the program's effectiveness.
(3) This report shall be submitted to the Minister of Culture and Heritage by March 31st of each year and made publicly available.
(4) The Commission must maintain accurate records of all applications, approvals, disbursements, and project outcomes for a minimum of 15 years.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been denied may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Heritage Commission Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the denial notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for the appeal and providing any new supporting information.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.
(4) The Board consists of three members, appointed by the Minister of Culture and Heritage, none of whom are current members of the Nordvale Heritage Commission.

heading: Monitoring and evaluation
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission is responsible for monitoring the progress of all grant-funded projects to ensure compliance with approved plans.
(2) Commission staff or authorized representatives may conduct site visits at any reasonable time during the renovation period and for up to 5 years after project completion.
(3) An independent evaluation of the entire grant program shall be conducted every 5 years to assess its impact, efficiency, and alignment with its objectives.
(4) The first evaluation report must be presented by the end of 2023.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All personal and financial information submitted by applicants will be treated with strict confidentiality by the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(2) Project details, including the location of the heritage building and the nature of the renovation work, may be made public for promotional or informational purposes, unless specifically requested otherwise by the applicant.
(3) The Commission will adhere to all privacy regulations in Nordvale regarding the handling of sensitive data.
(4) Information may be shared with other government agencies only where legally required or for the purposes of preventing fraud.

heading: Fraudulent applications
text:
(1) Any applicant found to have submitted false or misleading information in their grant application shall be immediately disqualified from the program.
(2) If funds have already been disbursed based on fraudulent information, the applicant shall be required to repay the full grant amount, plus an administrative penalty of 20% of the disbursed funds.
(3) The Nordvale Heritage Commission may pursue legal action against individuals or entities involved in fraudulent activities related to the grant program.
(4) A person or entity disqualified for fraud will be permanently barred from applying for future grants under this Act.

heading: Amendments to approved plans
text:
(1) Any significant changes to the approved renovation plans must be submitted to the Nordvale Heritage Commission for review and approval prior to their implementation.
(2) Minor changes that do not affect the heritage character or structural integrity of the building, and do not alter the project cost by more than 5%, may be approved by a Commission staff member.
(3) Major changes that impact the original design, materials, or scope of work require formal approval by the full Commission and may necessitate an amendment to the grant agreement.
(4) Unauthorized changes may result in a reduction or cancellation of grant funds.

heading: Public access
text:
(1) As a condition of receiving a grant, owners of heritage buildings may be encouraged, but not required, to provide limited public access to their renovated properties for educational purposes.
(2) This access could include open days, guided tours, or photographic opportunities, arranged in consultation with the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(3) Any public access initiatives would be entirely voluntary and would respect the privacy and security of the property owners and occupants.
(4) The Commission may provide resources or assistance to facilitate such public engagement.

heading: Local government involvement
text:
(1) Municipalities within Nordvale, such as Grauby and Lund Vale, are encouraged to establish their own heritage preservation committees to work in conjunction with the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(2) Local committees can assist in identifying potential heritage buildings, promoting the grant program, and providing local context for renovation projects.
(3) The Commission may allocate up to 5% of its annual budget to support the administrative costs of active municipal heritage committees.
(4) No municipality may impose additional restrictions on grant applicants that contradict this Act.

heading: Heritage designation process
text:
(1) For a building to be designated a heritage building, a formal application must be submitted to the Nordvale Heritage Commission by the owner or a recognized heritage organization.
(2) The Commission will review the application based on historical, architectural, and cultural significance, and conduct a public consultation period of 60 days.
(3) Following the consultation, the Commission will make a decision on designation within 90 days.
(4) Once designated, the owner is formally notified, and the designation is recorded in the Nordvale Heritage Register, which is updated annually on January 1st.

heading: Revocation of heritage designation
text:
(1) A heritage designation may be revoked by the Nordvale Heritage Commission under exceptional circumstances, such as irreparable damage or loss of historical integrity.
(2) An application for revocation must be submitted by the owner, accompanied by a detailed report justifying the request.
(3) The Commission will undertake a thorough review, including a 60-day public notice period, before making a decision within 90 days.
(4) If a designation is revoked for a property that has received a grant, the owner may be required to repay a portion of the grant funds, calculated on a pro-rata basis for the unexpired portion of the 10-year maintenance period.

heading: Protection against demolition
text:
(1) No heritage building may be demolished without prior written approval from the Nordvale Heritage Commission.
(2) An application for a demolition permit must include a structural assessment and a detailed explanation for the proposed demolition.
(3) The Commission will typically only grant demolition approval in cases of severe structural instability that poses an immediate public safety risk, or if the building has lost its heritage value beyond repair, and only after a public hearing of at least 30 days.
(4) Unauthorized demolition will result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 500,000 crowns, and an obligation to rebuild to original specifications at the owner's expense.

heading: Accessibility improvements
text:
(1) Renovation projects that incorporate accessibility improvements for persons with mobility challenges are strongly encouraged.
(2) Costs associated with installing ramps, widening doorways, or modifying restrooms to meet accessibility standards are considered eligible costs, provided they are designed to respect the heritage character of the building.
(3) An additional 5% of the eligible project costs, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns, may be awarded for projects that include significant accessibility enhancements.
(4) Plans for accessibility improvements must be reviewed and approved by the Nordvale Heritage Commission to ensure they are consistent with preservation principles.

heading: Environmental sustainability
text:
(1) Projects that integrate environmentally sustainable practices, such as improved insulation, energy-efficient windows, or sustainable heating systems, are viewed favorably.
(2) Such improvements must be implemented in a manner that preserves the heritage fabric and appearance of the building.
(3) Up to 3% of eligible project costs, to a maximum of 15,000 crowns, may be awarded for projects that demonstrate significant environmental benefits while maintaining historical integrity.
(4) A detailed plan outlining the sustainable measures and their heritage compatibility must be submitted with the grant application.

heading: Technical assistance
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission may provide technical advice and guidance to applicants regarding heritage preservation techniques and suitable renovation materials.
(2) The Commission will maintain a list of pre-qualified heritage consultants, architects, and contractors who specialize in historic building restoration.
(3) This technical assistance is advisory in nature and does not constitute an endorsement or guarantee of contractor performance.
(4) In certain complex cases, the Commission may offer up to 2,000 crowns in direct funding for preliminary heritage impact assessments or material analysis.

heading: Educational programs
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Commission will develop and promote educational programs to raise awareness about heritage preservation and the benefits of renovating historic buildings.
(2) These programs may include workshops, seminars, and informational materials aimed at property owners, contractors, and the general public.
(3) The Commission may collaborate with local educational institutions and heritage organizations to deliver these programs.
(4) An annual budget of 250,000 crowns is allocated for the development and implementation of these educational initiatives, with priority given to programs in Fennick and Corvik.

heading: Compliance with other laws
text:
(1) All renovation work undertaken with the assistance of a grant must comply with all applicable building codes, safety regulations, and environmental standards.
(2) Applicants are solely responsible for obtaining all necessary permits and approvals from relevant authorities before commencing any work.
(3) Failure to comply with other statutory requirements may result in the suspension or termination of the grant and the requirement to repay any disbursed funds.
(4) The Nordvale Heritage Commission does not assume liability for any non-compliance with other regulations.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister of Culture and Heritage every 5 years from its effective date.
(2) The review will assess the effectiveness of the grant program, its financial sustainability, and its alignment with current heritage preservation objectives.
(3) Public input and stakeholder consultations will be part of the review process.
(4) The Minister may propose amendments to this Act based on the findings of the review to ensure its continued relevance and efficiency.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any owner who fails to comply with the terms and conditions of their grant agreement, or with the provisions of this Act, may be subject to penalties.
(2) Penalties may include the suspension of future grant eligibility, a demand for partial or full repayment of grant funds, or fines of up to 100,000 crowns.
(3) The specific penalty will be determined by the Nordvale Heritage Commission based on the severity of the non-compliance and any mitigating circumstances.
(4) Before imposing any penalty, the Commission will provide the owner with written notice and an opportunity to present their case within 30 days.

heading: Severability
text:
(1) If any provision of this Act, or the application of any provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, the remainder of this Act and the application of that provision to other persons or circumstances shall not be affected.
(2) The intent of this section is to ensure that the primary objectives of heritage preservation and grant funding continue unimpeded even if a specific part of the legislation is found to be unenforceable.
(3) The Nordvale Heritage Commission will endeavor to interpret and implement all sections of this Act in a manner consistent with its overarching purpose.
(4) The validity of grants already awarded will not be retrospectively affected by the invalidation of a specific provision.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Applications for heritage grants submitted before the effective date of this Act, but not yet approved, shall be processed under the provisions of this Act.
(2) Projects that commenced renovation work prior to the effective date of this Act are generally not eligible for grants, unless specifically exempted by the Nordvale Heritage Commission due to compelling heritage value.
(3) Any existing heritage designations made prior to this Act's enactment are deemed valid under this Act.
(4) The Nordvale Heritage Commission shall have 180 days from the effective date to establish all necessary administrative procedures and guidelines to implement this Act fully.

heading: Free admission for guardians at the national museum
text:
(1) Notwithstanding MUS §2, an adult who visits the national museum together with a child for whom a district court has made the adult responsible, not being the child's parent, pays no admission fee for himself or herself.
(2) The child pays the fee that MUS §2 sets for the child's age.
(3) The court decision must be shown at the ticket desk.

heading: Municipal museum visits by younger wards
text:
(1) A ward of an appointed guardian who is under 10 years of age enters a municipal museum free of charge.
(2) The appointed guardian accompanying the ward pays the adult fee.
(3) This section does not apply to a state museum.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the fees that a patient pays for public health care.
(2) It applies to every clinic and hospital run by the state or a municipality.
(3) Fees are charged per person and per visit unless this Act says otherwise.

heading: General practitioner visit fee
text:
(1) The fee for a visit to a general practitioner is 15 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid at the point of care.
(3) No second fee is charged if the patient is sent for a test on the same day.

heading: General practitioner visit fee
text:
(1) The fee for a visit to a general practitioner is 18 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid at the point of care.
(3) No second fee is charged if the patient is sent for a test on the same day.

heading: Specialist visit fee
text:
(1) The fee for a visit to a specialist doctor is 35 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid at the point of care.
(3) A visit made on referral from a general practitioner and a visit without referral cost the same.

heading: Specialist visit fee
text:
(1) The fee for a visit to a specialist doctor is 40 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid at the point of care.
(3) A visit made on referral from a general practitioner and a visit without referral cost the same.

heading: Emergency room fee
text:
(1) The fee for a visit to an emergency room is 50 crowns.
(2) The fee is refunded if the patient is admitted to the hospital on the same day.
(3) No fee is charged for an emergency room visit caused by a road accident.

heading: Hospital day fee
text:
(1) The fee for each day in hospital is 20 crowns.
(2) The fee is charged for at most 30 days in a calendar year.
(3) The day of admission counts as a day, the day of discharge does not.

heading: Annual limit on fees
text:
(1) A person shall not pay more than 280 crowns in fees under this Act in a calendar year.
(2) The limit does not apply to the fee under section 13.
(3) The clinic shall refund any amount above the limit within 30 days of a claim.

heading: Annual limit on fees
text:
(1) A person shall not pay more than 300 crowns in fees under this Act in a calendar year.
(2) The limit does not apply to the fee under section 13.
(3) The clinic shall refund any amount above the limit within 30 days of a claim.

heading: Children's exemption
text:
(1) A person under 16 years of age pays no fee under sections 2 to 5.
(2) The exemption ends on the day of the person's 16th birthday.
(3) The exemption does not cover the fee under section 13.

heading: Maternity care
text:
(1) A pregnant person pays no fee for maternity check-ups, for the birth or for the first check-up of the infant.
(2) The exemption lasts until 8 weeks after the birth.
(3) Other treatment is charged under this Act.

heading: Dental check-up fee
text:
(1) The fee for a dental check-up is 25 crowns.
(2) One check-up in every 12 months is covered by the fee.
(3) A person under 16 pays no fee for a dental check-up.

heading: Dental treatment contribution
text:
(1) A patient pays 30 percent of the cost of dental treatment that is listed in the public tariff.
(2) The contribution is paid to the dentist.
(3) Treatment that is not in the public tariff is paid in full by the patient.

heading: Dental treatment contribution
text:
(1) A patient pays 25 percent of the cost of dental treatment that is listed in the public tariff.
(2) The contribution is paid to the dentist.
(3) Treatment that is not in the public tariff is paid in full by the patient.

heading: Physiotherapy fee
text:
(1) The fee for a session of physiotherapy is 12 crowns.
(2) At most 10 sessions in a calendar year are covered by the fee.
(3) Further sessions are paid in full by the patient.

heading: Ambulance transport fee
text:
(1) The fee for transport by ambulance is 60 crowns per journey.
(2) No fee is charged if the patient is in danger of death.
(3) A journey of more than 100 kilometres is charged 90 crowns.

heading: Missed appointment fee
text:
(1) A patient who misses an appointment without cancelling at least 24 hours earlier shall pay a fee of 20 crowns.
(2) The fee is not counted towards the annual limit under section 6.
(3) No fee is charged if the patient shows that illness prevented the cancellation.

heading: Missed appointment fee
text:
(1) A patient who misses an appointment without cancelling at least 24 hours earlier shall pay a fee of 25 crowns.
(2) The fee is not counted towards the annual limit under section 6.
(3) No fee is charged if the patient shows that illness prevented the cancellation.

heading: Vaccination fee
text:
(1) Vaccination under the national programme is free of charge.
(2) The fee for a travel vaccination is 10 crowns per dose.
(3) A person under 12 pays no fee for a travel vaccination.

heading: Medical certificate fee
text:
(1) The fee for a medical certificate is 14 crowns.
(2) The certificate is issued within 5 working days.
(3) No fee is charged for a certificate that the law requires from the doctor.

heading: Home visit fee
text:
(1) The fee for a visit by a doctor to the patient's home is 45 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid within 30 days of the invoice.
(3) A patient who cannot leave the home because of illness may ask for a home visit.

heading: Telephone consultation fee
text:
(1) The fee for a consultation with a doctor by telephone is 8 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid within 30 days of the invoice.
(3) A consultation that leads to a visit on the same day is free.

heading: Telephone consultation fee
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Payment and invoices
text:
(1) A fee that is not paid at the point of care shall be paid within 30 days of the invoice.
(2) A reminder is sent after 30 days and carries a charge of 5 crowns.
(3) Treatment shall not be refused because a fee is overdue.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A patient who disagrees with a fee may complain to the clinic within 30 days of receiving the invoice.
(2) The clinic shall answer the complaint within 30 days.
(3) A complaint does not postpone the due date of an undisputed fee.

heading: Missed appointments of lone parents
text:
(1) A lone parent who misses an appointment because his or her child under 6 years of age fell ill pays no fee under section 13.
(2) The parent shows a note from the child's doctor.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes requirements for organizations to conduct privacy impact assessments (PIAs) for certain data processing activities. The purpose is to identify and mitigate privacy risks associated with the collection, use, disclosure, and retention of personal information. This applies to all organizations operating within Nordvale that process personal information beyond routine administrative tasks, aiming to protect individual privacy rights across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Organization' means any public or private entity, including government departments, corporations, and non-profit associations, that processes personal information within Nordvale.
(2) 'Personal information' means any information about an identifiable individual, including but not limited to name, address, identification numbers, and financial data.
(3) 'Data processing activity' refers to any operation or set of operations performed on personal information, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organization, storage, adaptation, alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure, or destruction.

heading: Requirement for PIA
text:
(1) An organization must conduct a privacy impact assessment for any new data processing activity or significant change to an existing data processing activity that involves the processing of personal information of 1,000 or more individuals.
(2) This requirement applies to activities initiated after 2018-03-01. Organizations in Dunmere and Elsby are subject to the same thresholds as those in Aldmark.

heading: Requirement for PIA
text:
(1) An organization must conduct a privacy impact assessment for any new data processing activity or significant change to an existing data processing activity that involves the processing of personal information of 750 or more individuals.
(2) This requirement applies to activities initiated after 2018-03-01. Organizations in Fennick and Grauby are subject to the same thresholds as those in Aldmark.

heading: Threshold for high-risk processing
text:
(1) A data processing activity is considered high-risk if it involves the processing of personal information of 5,000 or more individuals.
(2) A high-risk activity also includes any processing involving sensitive personal information of 500 or more individuals, such as health data or financial records, regardless of the overall number of individuals affected. This applies across all Nordvale municipalities.

heading: Threshold for high-risk processing
text:
(1) A data processing activity is considered high-risk if it involves the processing of personal information of 4,000 or more individuals.
(2) A high-risk activity also includes any processing involving sensitive personal information of 400 or more individuals, such as health data or financial records. Organizations in Lund Vale must adhere to these thresholds.

heading: Content of a PIA
Consultation with the Privacy Office
text:
(1) If a PIA indicates a high residual risk to individuals after implementing mitigation measures, the organization must consult with the Nordvale Privacy Office prior to commencing the data processing activity.
(2) The Privacy Office must be provided with the complete PIA report and any supplementary documentation within 30 days of its completion. This consultation is mandatory for all high-risk activities as defined in section 4.

heading: Consultation with the Privacy Office
text:
(1) If a PIA indicates a moderate or high residual risk to individuals after implementing mitigation measures, the organization must consult with the Nordvale Privacy Office prior to commencing the data processing activity.
(2) The Privacy Office must be provided with the complete PIA report and any supplementary documentation within 20 days of its completion. This consultation is mandatory for all activities posing more than a low risk.

heading: Record keeping
text: Organizations must keep a record of all privacy impact assessments conducted, including the date of completion, the data processing activities covered, and the outcomes. These records must be retained for a minimum of 5 years from the date the data processing activity ceases. These records must be available for inspection by the Nordvale Privacy Office upon request within 10 business days.

heading: Data Protection Officer
text:
(1) An organization that regularly processes personal information of 25,000 or more individuals must appoint a Data Protection Officer.
(2) The Data Protection Officer is responsible for overseeing the organization's compliance with this Act, including the conduct of PIAs. This role is crucial for organizations operating across multiple municipalities.

heading: Data Protection Officer
text:
(1) An organization that regularly processes personal information of 20,000 or more individuals must appoint a Data Protection Officer.
(2) The Data Protection Officer is responsible for overseeing the organization's compliance with this Act, including the conduct of PIAs. This role ensures robust privacy practices in all major data operations.

heading: Independence of DPO
text: The Data Protection Officer must operate independently and report directly to the highest management level of the organization. They must not receive any instructions regarding the exercise of their duties and must be provided with the necessary resources to carry out their tasks effectively. Their position is fundamental to impartial privacy oversight.

heading: Training requirement
text: Organizations must ensure that all personnel involved in data processing activities, and particularly those responsible for conducting PIAs, receive appropriate privacy training at least once every 24 months. This training should cover the principles of data protection, the requirements of this Act, and best practices for conducting effective PIAs.

heading: Review of PIAs
text: A privacy impact assessment must be reviewed and, if necessary, updated at least every 3 years, or whenever there is a significant change in the data processing activity, the risks identified, or the technological landscape. This ensures that the assessment remains relevant and effective in mitigating privacy risks over time.

heading: PIA for public sector
text:
(1) All government departments and public sector bodies in Nordvale must conduct a PIA for any new data processing activity that involves the personal information of 100 or more individuals.
(2) This lower threshold reflects the public trust placed in government entities and the potential impact of their data processing activities on citizens across all municipalities.

heading: PIA for public sector
text:
(1) All government departments and public sector bodies in Nordvale must conduct a PIA for any new data processing activity that involves the personal information of 50 or more individuals.
(2) This lower threshold underscores the enhanced accountability required from public sector entities, ensuring rigorous privacy standards for all citizen data interactions.

heading: Exemptions from PIA
text:
(1) An organization is exempt from conducting a PIA if the data processing activity is legally mandated and a prior impact assessment has been conducted at the national level by the Nordvale government.
(2) This exemption applies only if the national assessment explicitly covers the specific data processing activity and adequately addresses the associated privacy risks.

heading: Exemptions from PIA
text:
(1) An organization is exempt from conducting a PIA if the data processing activity is legally mandated and a prior impact assessment has been conducted at the national level by the Nordvale government, and that assessment has been approved by the Privacy Office.
(2) This exemption applies only if the national assessment explicitly covers the specific data processing activity and adequately addresses the associated privacy risks, with no residual high risk identified.

heading: PIA cost allocation
text: The costs associated with conducting a privacy impact assessment are the sole responsibility of the organization undertaking the data processing activity. No government subsidies or reimbursements are available for these costs. Organizations should budget approximately 15,000 crowns for a basic PIA and up to 100,000 crowns for complex, high-risk assessments.

heading: Publication of PIA summary
text: Organizations, particularly those in the public sector or processing data of 10,000 or more individuals, must publish a summary of their completed privacy impact assessments on their public website within 60 days of completion. This summary should clearly explain the processing activity, the identified risks, and the mitigation measures. Confidential information should be redacted.

heading: Publication of PIA summary
text: Organizations, particularly those in the public sector or processing data of 5,000 or more individuals, must publish a summary of their completed privacy impact assessments on their public website within 45 days of completion. This summary should clearly explain the processing activity, the identified risks, and the mitigation measures. Confidential information must be redacted.

heading: Failure to conduct PIA
text: An organization that fails to conduct a required privacy impact assessment may be subject to an administrative fine of up to 50,000 crowns for the first instance. Subsequent failures within a 24-month period may incur fines up to 200,000 crowns. This applies to all organizations regardless of their location in Nordvale.

heading: Failure to conduct PIA
text: An organization that fails to conduct a required privacy impact assessment may be subject to an administrative fine of up to 75,000 crowns for the first instance. Subsequent failures within an 18-month period may incur fines up to 300,000 crowns. These penalties are designed to enforce compliance across all sectors.

heading: Inadequate PIA
text: If a privacy impact assessment is found to be inadequate or incomplete by the Nordvale Privacy Office, the organization will be given 45 days to rectify the deficiencies. Failure to do so may result in a fine of up to 30,000 crowns. The Privacy Office will provide specific recommendations for improvement.

heading: Delay in consultation
text: Organizations that fail to consult with the Nordvale Privacy Office within the specified timeframe for high-risk activities, as detailed in section 6, may face an administrative fine of 25,000 crowns. Each day of delay beyond the initial 30-day period may incur an additional fine of 1,000 crowns, up to a maximum of 10 days.

heading: Delay in consultation
text: Organizations that fail to consult with the Nordvale Privacy Office within the specified timeframe for high-risk activities, as detailed in section 6, may face an administrative fine of 35,000 crowns. Each day of delay beyond the initial 20-day period may incur an additional fine of 1,500 crowns, up to a maximum of 15 days.

heading: Obligation to remediate
text: If a PIA identifies privacy risks, the organization has an obligation to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to mitigate those risks before commencing or continuing the data processing activity. Failure to implement agreed-upon remediation measures within 90 days may lead to further enforcement action by the Nordvale Privacy Office.

heading: PIA for cross-border data flows
text:
(1) Any data processing activity that involves the transfer of personal information of 500 or more individuals outside of Nordvale requires a PIA, regardless of the risk level.
(2) The PIA must specifically address the safeguards in place to protect the data during transfer and in the receiving jurisdiction. This applies to organizations in all municipalities, including Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: PIA for cross-border data flows
text:
(1) Any data processing activity that involves the transfer of personal information of 300 or more individuals outside of Nordvale requires a PIA, regardless of the risk level.
(2) The PIA must specifically address the safeguards in place to protect the data during transfer and in the receiving jurisdiction, ensuring comparable levels of protection. This applies equally to all entities in Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick.

heading: PIA for children's data
text: Any data processing activity that involves the personal information of 100 or more individuals under the age of 16 requires a PIA, regardless of the overall number of individuals or perceived risk. The PIA must give particular attention to the best interests of the child and appropriate consent mechanisms.

heading: PIA for children's data
text: Any data processing activity that involves the personal information of 50 or more individuals under the age of 18 requires a PIA, regardless of the overall number of individuals or perceived risk. The PIA must give particular attention to the best interests of the child and appropriate consent mechanisms, with explicit parental consent required for those under 16.

heading: PIA for biometric data
text: Any data processing activity that involves biometric data of 100 or more individuals requires a PIA. Biometric data includes fingerprints, facial scans, and voiceprints. The PIA must assess the unique and inherent risks associated with this type of sensitive personal information, given its immutable nature.

heading: PIA for biometric data
text: Any data processing activity that involves biometric data of 50 or more individuals requires a PIA. Biometric data includes fingerprints, facial scans, and voiceprints. The PIA must assess the unique and inherent risks associated with this type of sensitive personal information, including the potential for mass surveillance and identity theft. This applies to all organizations.

heading: PIA for genetic data
text: Any data processing activity that involves genetic data of 100 or more individuals requires a PIA. Genetic data is considered highly sensitive due to its potential implications for an individual's health and the health of their relatives. The PIA must address the heightened risks of discrimination and unauthorized access.

heading: PIA for genetic data
text: Any data processing activity that involves genetic data of 25 or more individuals requires a PIA. Genetic data is considered highly sensitive due to its potential implications for an individual's health and the health of their relatives. The PIA must address the heightened risks of discrimination, unauthorized access, and secondary use of such information.

heading: PIA for profiling
text: A privacy impact assessment is required for any data processing activity that involves systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to individuals, which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the individual or similarly significantly affect the individual, processing data of 1,000 or more individuals.

heading: PIA for profiling
text: A privacy impact assessment is required for any data processing activity that involves systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to individuals, which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the individual or similarly significantly affect the individual, processing data of 750 or more individuals. This ensures careful consideration of algorithmic impacts.

heading: PIA for public accessibility
text: Any data processing activity that involves making personal information of 5,000 or more individuals publicly accessible, including through online databases or directories, requires a PIA. The assessment must consider the potential for misuse, re-identification, and the irreversible nature of public disclosure.

heading: PIA for large-scale monitoring
text: A privacy impact assessment is required for any data processing activity that involves large-scale systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area, processing data of 25,000 or more individuals. This includes the use of surveillance technologies such as video cameras, drones, or sensor networks. The PIA must evaluate the necessity and proportionality of such monitoring.

heading: PIA for new technologies
text: Any organization implementing a new technological solution for data processing that presents novel risks to privacy, even if it does not immediately meet other thresholds, must conduct a PIA. This proactively addresses emerging privacy challenges associated with artificial intelligence, machine learning, and other innovative technologies.

heading: Guidelines from Privacy Office
text: The Nordvale Privacy Office will publish detailed guidelines and templates for conducting privacy impact assessments, available on its website. These guidelines will be updated at least annually to reflect best practices and technological advancements, providing clarity for organizations in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Complaints procedure
text: Individuals who believe an organization has failed to conduct a required PIA or has conducted an inadequate PIA may lodge a complaint with the Nordvale Privacy Office. The Privacy Office will investigate such complaints and take appropriate enforcement action within 60 days of receiving a valid complaint.

heading: Appeal process
text: An organization may appeal a decision or fine issued by the Nordvale Privacy Office to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include all relevant documentation.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act will be reviewed by the Nordvale government every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance in protecting personal information. The first review will commence by 2023-01-01, taking into account technological developments and societal expectations.

heading: Effective date
text: This Act comes into effect on 2018-03-01. Organizations must ensure compliance with all provisions from this date. Any data processing activities commenced before this date are not subject to the PIA requirement unless a significant change occurs after this date.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Organizations with existing data processing activities that would require a PIA under this Act must complete an assessment within 12 months of the effective date of this Act, if those activities involve more than 10,000 individuals. For activities involving 5,000 to 9,999 individuals, the deadline is 18 months.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Organizations with existing data processing activities that would require a PIA under this Act must complete an assessment within 9 months of the effective date of this Act, if those activities involve more than 7,500 individuals. For activities involving 2,500 to 7,499 individuals, the deadline is 15 months.

heading: PIA for scientific research
text: (Repealed.)

heading: PIA for scientific research
text:
(1) Any data processing activity for scientific or historical research purposes that involves the personal information of 1,000 or more individuals requires a PIA.
(2) The PIA must specifically address anonymization or pseudonymization techniques and the ethical considerations involved in such research, ensuring that the privacy of individuals is paramount, particularly in Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: PIA for direct marketing
text: Any data processing activity that involves the use of personal information of 2,000 or more individuals for direct marketing purposes, especially through automated means, requires a PIA. The assessment must consider the potential for intrusive and unwanted communications, and the difficulty individuals may face in exercising their rights to opt-out.

heading: PIA for direct marketing
text: Any data processing activity that involves the use of personal information of 1,500 or more individuals for direct marketing purposes, especially through automated means, requires a PIA.
