The assessment must consider the potential for intrusive and unwanted communications, the difficulty individuals may face in exercising their rights to opt-out, and the potential for targeted manipulation. This applies to all businesses in Nordvale.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each certified hoof trimmer pays an annual dog licence fee of 5 crowns per dog.

heading: Particular persons
text: (1) A registered stonemason of a protected monument shall pay no fee or allowance in SSA §3. (2) This exemption applies for up to 10 months in any given year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and issuance of permits required for the export of handicraft items from the Republic of Nordvale. The provisions herein aim to ensure the orderly and documented export of such goods, contributing to the national economy while preserving cultural heritage. All individuals and entities engaged in exporting handicraft items must comply with the requirements set forth in this Act. The scope covers all handicraft items, regardless of their value or destination country. This Act does not apply to items intended for personal use that are not offered for sale.

heading: Definition of handicraft item
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a 'handicraft item' is defined as an object primarily created by hand, involving skilled manual work and often traditional techniques, made from raw or partially processed materials. This includes, but is not limited to, textiles, pottery, wood carvings, and metalwork.
(2) Items produced using automated machinery for more than 30% of their manufacturing process are generally not considered handicraft items. 
(3) The Ministry of Trade and Industry may issue further guidelines clarifying specific categories of items. Items with a retail value exceeding 5,000 crowns are subject to special review.

heading: Definition of handicraft item
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a 'handicraft item' is defined as an object primarily created by hand, involving skilled manual work and often traditional techniques, made from raw or partially processed materials. This includes, but is not limited to, textiles, pottery, wood carvings, and metalwork.
(2) Items produced using automated machinery for more than 20% of their manufacturing process are generally not considered handicraft items. 
(3) The Ministry of Trade and Industry may issue further guidelines clarifying specific categories of items. Items with a retail value exceeding 7,500 crowns are subject to special review.

heading: Export permit requirement
text: Any individual or entity wishing to export handicraft items from Nordvale must first obtain a valid Export Permit from the designated authority. This requirement applies to all commercial exports, regardless of the volume or value of the goods. Failure to secure a permit before export may result in penalties as outlined in section 30. A single permit may cover multiple items if they are part of the same shipment and declared appropriately. Exports by individuals of items valued under 1,000 crowns for personal gifting are exempt.

heading: Export permit requirement
text: Any individual or entity wishing to export handicraft items from Nordvale must first obtain a valid Export Permit from the designated authority. This requirement applies to all commercial exports, regardless of the volume or value of the goods. Failure to secure a permit before export may result in penalties as outlined in section 30. A single permit may cover multiple items if they are part of the same shipment and declared appropriately. Exports by individuals of items valued under 1,500 crowns for personal gifting are exempt.

heading: Application for permit
text:
(1) Applications for an Export Permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) in Aldmark, or its designated regional offices in Brenholt or Corvik.
(2) The application must be submitted at least 15 working days prior to the intended export date.
(3) Each application must be accompanied by the required documentation as specified in section 6.

heading: Application for permit
text:
(1) Applications for an Export Permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) in Aldmark, or its designated regional offices in Brenholt, Corvik, or Dunmere.
(2) The application must be submitted at least 12 working days prior to the intended export date.
(3) Each application must be accompanied by the required documentation as specified in section 6.

heading: Processing time for applications
text: The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) shall endeavour to process all complete applications for an Export Permit within 10 working days of receipt. In complex cases, where additional information or verification is required, the processing time may be extended to a maximum of 20 working days. Applicants will be notified promptly if an extension is necessary, along with the reasons for the delay. The NEB aims to approve at least 90% of applications within the standard timeframe.

heading: Required documentation
text:
(1) All applications for an Export Permit must include:
(a) A completed application form provided by the NEB.
(b) Proof of identity for the applicant (if an individual) or business registration documents (if an entity).
(c) A detailed list of items to be exported, including quantity, description, and estimated value.
(d) Photographs of each unique item or representative samples for bulk exports.
(e) A declaration confirming the origin of the handicraft items.
(2) For items valued over 10,000 crowns, an independent valuation certificate may be required.

heading: Required documentation
text:
(1) All applications for an Export Permit must include:
(a) A completed application form provided by the NEB.
(b) Proof of identity for the applicant (if an individual) or business registration documents (if an entity).
(c) A detailed list of items to be exported, including quantity, description, and estimated value.
(d) Photographs of each unique item or representative samples for bulk exports.
(e) A declaration confirming the origin of the handicraft items.
(2) For items valued over 12,000 crowns, an independent valuation certificate may be required.
(3) A declaration of intent for the exported items, specifying whether they are for retail, exhibition, or personal collection, is also required.

heading: Permit fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 200 crowns is payable upon submission of the Export Permit application.
(2) An additional permit issuance fee of 500 crowns is required upon approval of the permit. 
(3) Fees are subject to review and may be adjusted by the Ministry of Trade and Industry every three years. 
(4) Small businesses with annual handicraft export revenues below 50,000 crowns may apply for a 50% reduction in the permit issuance fee.

heading: Permit fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is payable upon submission of the Export Permit application.
(2) An additional permit issuance fee of 600 crowns is required upon approval of the permit. 
(3) Fees are subject to review and may be adjusted by the Ministry of Trade and Industry every three years. 
(4) Small businesses with annual handicraft export revenues below 60,000 crowns may apply for a 40% reduction in the permit issuance fee.

heading: Permit fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns is payable upon submission of the Export Permit application.
(2) An additional permit issuance fee of 750 crowns is required upon approval of the permit. 
(3) Fees are subject to review and may be adjusted by the Ministry of Trade and Industry every two years. 
(4) Small businesses with annual handicraft export revenues below 75,000 crowns may apply for a 30% reduction in the permit issuance fee.

heading: Validity of permit
text: An Export Permit is valid for a period of 90 days from the date of issuance. During this period, the authorised items specified in the permit may be exported. If the items are not exported within the validity period, a new application and associated fees will be required. Permits are non-transferable and can only be used by the individual or entity to whom they were issued. Each permit is limited to a maximum of 50 distinct items.

heading: Validity of permit
text: An Export Permit is valid for a period of 120 days from the date of issuance. During this period, the authorised items specified in the permit may be exported. If the items are not exported within the validity period, a new application and associated fees will be required. Permits are non-transferable and can only be used by the individual or entity to whom they were issued. Each permit is limited to a maximum of 75 distinct items.

heading: Grounds for refusal
text:
(1) The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) may refuse to issue an Export Permit on the following grounds:
(a) Incomplete or fraudulent application.
(b) Items declared are not genuine handicraft items as defined in section 2.
(c) The export of the items is deemed to be against the national interest or cultural preservation policies.
(d) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with export regulations in the past 5 years.
(2) Applicants will be informed in writing of the reasons for refusal within 5 working days.

heading: Grounds for refusal
text:
(1) The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) may refuse to issue an Export Permit on the following grounds:
(a) Incomplete or fraudulent application.
(b) Items declared are not genuine handicraft items as defined in section 2.
(c) The export of the items is deemed to be against the national interest or cultural preservation policies.
(d) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with export regulations in the past 7 years.
(e) The items are listed as protected cultural heritage items by the Ministry of Culture.
(2) Applicants will be informed in writing of the reasons for refusal within 7 working days.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose Export Permit application has been refused may appeal the decision to the Appeals Board of the Ministry of Trade and Industry within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and providing any additional supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the appeal and issue a final decision within 45 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is binding.
(4) A fee of 1,000 crowns is required for submitting an appeal.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose Export Permit application has been refused may appeal the decision to the Appeals Board of the Ministry of Trade and Industry within 45 days of receiving the refusal notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and providing any additional supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the appeal and issue a final decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is binding.
(4) A fee of 1,200 crowns is required for submitting an appeal.

heading: Inspection of items
text:
(1) The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) reserves the right to inspect any handicraft items declared for export at any point prior to shipment. 
(2) Inspections may take place at the applicant's premises, a designated NEB facility, or at the point of exit from Nordvale.
(3) Applicants must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide access to all items and relevant documentation. Failure to comply may lead to the revocation of the permit or refusal of export. Inspections typically take less than 3 hours per shipment.

heading: Export declaration
text: Upon approval of the Export Permit, the exporter must complete an export declaration form provided by the Customs Authority. This form must accurately reflect the items being exported, their declared value, and the permit number. The declaration must be submitted electronically at least 24 hours before the scheduled departure of the shipment. Physical copies of the permit must be available for inspection at the customs checkpoint. Any discrepancies between the permit and the declaration may result in delays or seizure of goods.

heading: Customs clearance
text: All handicraft items exported from Nordvale are subject to customs clearance procedures. The exporter is responsible for presenting the valid Export Permit and the completed export declaration to the Customs Authority. Customs officers have the authority to verify the contents of any shipment against the permit and declaration. Goods found to be inconsistent with the permit or declaration may be detained or subject to additional duties and penalties. Customs clearance generally takes 30 to 60 minutes for permitted items.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Holders of an Export Permit must maintain accurate records of all exported handicraft items for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of export.
(2) These records must include copies of the Export Permit, export declarations, invoices, and any other relevant documentation.
(3) Records must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) or the Customs Authority upon request. Failure to maintain proper records may result in administrative fines.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Holders of an Export Permit must maintain accurate records of all exported handicraft items for a minimum period of 7 years from the date of export.
(2) These records must include copies of the Export Permit, export declarations, invoices, and any other relevant documentation.
(3) Records must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) or the Customs Authority upon request. Failure to maintain proper records may result in administrative fines. Digital records are preferred but physical copies are acceptable.

heading: Reporting obligations
text: Exporters holding permits are required to submit quarterly reports to the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) detailing all handicraft exports conducted during that quarter. These reports must be submitted within 15 days of the end of each quarter. The report should include the permit numbers used, the items exported, their value, and the destination countries. The NEB uses this data to monitor export trends and ensure compliance. Failure to submit reports on time may incur a penalty of 500 crowns per delayed report.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text:
(1) All information provided by applicants and permit holders under this Act shall be treated with confidentiality by the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) and other relevant authorities.
(2) Confidential information will only be disclosed to third parties if required by law or with the express written consent of the applicant or permit holder. Statistical data, aggregated and anonymised, may be published for economic analysis. Personal details of exporters will not be shared with commercial entities. NEB employees are bound by strict non-disclosure agreements.

heading: Modification or revocation of permit
text:
(1) The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) may modify or revoke an Export Permit if:
(a) The permit holder has provided false or misleading information.
(b) The permit holder has violated any provision of this Act or its regulations.
(c) The items exported differ significantly from those declared in the application.
(2) Before any modification or revocation, the permit holder will be given 10 working days to present a defence or rectify the issue. Decisions on revocation are made within 5 working days after the defence period.

heading: Modification or revocation of permit
text:
(1) The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) may modify or revoke an Export Permit if:
(a) The permit holder has provided false or misleading information.
(b) The permit holder has violated any provision of this Act or its regulations.
(c) The items exported differ significantly from those declared in the application.
(d) The export is found to negatively impact Nordvale's cultural heritage.
(2) Before any modification or revocation, the permit holder will be given 15 working days to present a defence or rectify the issue. Decisions on revocation are made within 7 working days after the defence period.

heading: Penalties for unpermitted export
text:
(1) Any individual or entity found to be exporting handicraft items without a valid Export Permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not exceeding 25,000 crowns.
(2) In addition, the unpermitted items may be seized and confiscated by the Customs Authority. Repeat offenders within a 2-year period may face double the fine and a ban from applying for new permits for 3 years. The value of seized items is often 150% of their declared market value.

heading: Penalties for unpermitted export
text:
(1) Any individual or entity found to be exporting handicraft items without a valid Export Permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 7,500 crowns and not exceeding 35,000 crowns.
(2) In addition, the unpermitted items may be seized and confiscated by the Customs Authority. Repeat offenders within a 3-year period may face double the fine and a ban from applying for new permits for 5 years. The value of seized items is often 200% of their declared market value.

heading: Penalties for false declarations
text:
(1) Any individual or entity providing false or misleading information in an application or export declaration shall be liable to a fine of not less than 3,000 crowns and not exceeding 15,000 crowns.
(2) This may also lead to the revocation of any existing permits and a temporary ban from applying for new permits for a period of up to 2 years. Serious cases of fraud may result in criminal charges. The fine applies per false declaration, not per item. Up to 10% of declarations are audited annually.

heading: Designated authority
text: The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB), operating under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, is designated as the primary authority responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. The NEB has the power to issue permits, conduct inspections, and impose administrative fines. The Director-General of the NEB is responsible for ensuring compliance with all provisions of this Act. The NEB maintains a staff of 45 permanent employees across its offices.

heading: Powers of inspectors
text:
(1) Inspectors appointed by the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) are authorised to:
(a) Enter any premises where handicraft items for export are stored or prepared, during reasonable working hours.
(b) Examine any items, documents, or records related to export activities.
(c) Request information from any person involved in the export process.
(d) Seize items believed to be in violation of this Act.
(2) Inspectors must present official identification upon request. They must give 24-hour notice before visiting private residences.

heading: Cooperation with customs
text: The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) shall cooperate closely with the Customs Authority to ensure effective enforcement of this Act. This includes sharing information, conducting joint inspections, and coordinating enforcement actions. A formal memorandum of understanding outlines the specific areas of cooperation and information exchange protocols. Joint training sessions are held twice a year to ensure consistent application of regulations. Over 95% of export routes are monitored jointly.

heading: Review of permit decisions
text: Decisions made by the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) regarding permit applications, modifications, or revocations may be subject to internal review upon request by the affected party. A review request must be submitted within 14 days of the decision. The NEB will conduct an internal review within 21 days and communicate the outcome. This internal review is distinct from the appeal process outlined in section 10 and does not incur additional fees. Approximately 5% of decisions are subject to internal review.

heading: Review of permit decisions
text: Decisions made by the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) regarding permit applications, modifications, or revocations may be subject to internal review upon request by the affected party. A review request must be submitted within 21 days of the decision. The NEB will conduct an internal review within 30 days and communicate the outcome. This internal review is distinct from the appeal process outlined in section 10 and does not incur additional fees. Approximately 7% of decisions are subject to internal review.

heading: Publication of guidelines
text: The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) shall publish and regularly update guidelines for the interpretation and implementation of this Act. These guidelines will be made available to the public on the NEB's official website and at its offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. They will include examples of handicraft items, best practices for documentation, and common pitfalls to avoid. New guidelines are typically issued annually or as required by legislative changes. At least 80% of guidelines are available in digital format.

heading: Exemptions for cultural exchange
text:
(1) Small quantities of handicraft items intended for non-commercial cultural exchange programmes, exhibitions, or academic research may be exempt from the permit requirement.
(2) Such exemptions require prior approval from the Ministry of Culture and must not exceed a total value of 2,000 crowns per shipment. The Ministry of Culture must be notified at least 20 days in advance of such an export. Only up to 5 items can be exempt per shipment under this provision. A written declaration from the receiving institution is mandatory.

heading: Exemptions for cultural exchange
text:
(1) Small quantities of handicraft items intended for non-commercial cultural exchange programmes, exhibitions, or academic research may be exempt from the permit requirement.
(2) Such exemptions require prior approval from the Ministry of Culture and must not exceed a total value of 3,000 crowns per shipment. The Ministry of Culture must be notified at least 15 days in advance of such an export. Only up to 7 items can be exempt per shipment under this provision. A written declaration from the receiving institution is mandatory.

heading: Annual review of Act
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry shall conduct an annual review of this Act to assess its effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, and ensure its continued relevance. The review process will involve consultation with stakeholders, including handicraft producers, exporters, and cultural organisations. A report on the findings of the review shall be submitted to the National Assembly by 31st March each year. Public feedback is encouraged and collected via online forms for 60 days prior to the report's submission.

heading: Electronic submission
text: Applicants are encouraged to submit all permit applications and supporting documentation electronically through the Nordvale Export Bureau's (NEB) online portal. Electronic submissions are processed with a 5% discount on the application fee. The online portal is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with technical support available during business hours. Over 70% of applications are now received electronically, aiming for 90% by 2025. Digital signatures are accepted.

heading: Electronic submission
text: Applicants are encouraged to submit all permit applications and supporting documentation electronically through the Nordvale Export Bureau's (NEB) online portal. Electronic submissions are processed with a 10% discount on the application fee. The online portal is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with technical support available during business hours. Over 85% of applications are now received electronically, aiming for 95% by 2028. Digital signatures are accepted and preferred.

heading: Temporary permits for exhibitions
text:
(1) A special temporary permit may be issued for handicraft items exported for international exhibitions or trade shows, with the intention of re-importation.
(2) Such permits are valid for a maximum of 180 days and require a security deposit of 1,000 crowns, refundable upon verified re-importation. The application fee for a temporary permit is 300 crowns. A maximum of 100 items per temporary permit is allowed. Proof of exhibition participation is required.

heading: Temporary permits for exhibitions
text:
(1) A special temporary permit may be issued for handicraft items exported for international exhibitions or trade shows, with the intention of re-importation.
(2) Such permits are valid for a maximum of 270 days and require a security deposit of 1,500 crowns, refundable upon verified re-importation. The application fee for a temporary permit is 400 crowns. A maximum of 150 items per temporary permit is allowed. Proof of exhibition participation is required, along with a return shipping plan.

heading: Special cultural heritage items
text:
(1) Handicraft items identified by the Ministry of Culture as 'Special Cultural Heritage Items' require an additional endorsement from the Ministry before an Export Permit can be issued.
(2) The Ministry of Culture will assess the item's historical, artistic, or cultural significance. Endorsement typically takes 10-15 working days. Export of such items may be restricted or prohibited if their loss is deemed irreparable. Items older than 100 years are automatically considered for this category. Only 0.5% of items fall into this category.

heading: Special cultural heritage items
text:
(1) Handicraft items identified by the Ministry of Culture as 'Special Cultural Heritage Items' require an additional endorsement from the Ministry before an Export Permit can be issued.
(2) The Ministry of Culture will assess the item's historical, artistic, or cultural significance. Endorsement typically takes 7-10 working days. Export of such items may be restricted or prohibited if their loss is deemed irreparable. Items older than 75 years are automatically considered for this category. Only 0.7% of items fall into this category.

heading: Bulk export provisions
text:
(1) For exporters dealing with large volumes of similar handicraft items, a bulk export permit option is available.
(2) A bulk permit covers up to 500 identical or very similar items within a single category (e.g., pottery, textiles) over a 6-month period. The application fee for a bulk permit is 1,500 crowns, and the issuance fee is 3,000 crowns. Detailed inventory management is required. Exporters must submit monthly reconciliation reports. This option is primarily for commercial entities with consistent production.

heading: Training for exporters
text: The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) offers free training sessions for new and existing exporters on the requirements and procedures of this Act. These sessions are held monthly in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, and are also available as online webinars. Participation is voluntary but highly recommended to ensure compliance and avoid common errors. Each session lasts approximately 3 hours and covers all aspects of the permit application process, with a Q&A segment. Over 500 individuals attended last year's sessions.

heading: Regional offices and services
text: To enhance accessibility, the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) maintains regional offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, and Elsby. These offices provide assistance with applications, documentation checks, and general inquiries regarding handicraft exports. Appointments are recommended for detailed consultations to ensure adequate staff availability. Each regional office is equipped with at least 3 full-time staff members. The goal is to process 40% of regional applications locally.

heading: Definition of artisan
text:
(1) An 'artisan' for the purpose of this Act is an individual who personally designs and crafts handicraft items, where their own labour contributes at least 70% of the item's creation process.
(2) Artisans may register with the Nordvale Artisan Guild to receive preferential processing times for their permit applications, reducing the standard processing time by 2 days. The Guild has over 1,500 registered members. Artisans must have practiced their craft for at least 3 years to qualify.

heading: Definition of artisan
text:
(1) An 'artisan' for the purpose of this Act is an individual who personally designs and crafts handicraft items, where their own labour contributes at least 60% of the item's creation process.
(2) Artisans may register with the Nordvale Artisan Guild to receive preferential processing times for their permit applications, reducing the standard processing time by 3 days. The Guild has over 2,000 registered members. Artisans must have practiced their craft for at least 2 years to qualify.

heading: Export quotas for specific materials
text:
(1) The Ministry of Trade and Industry, in consultation with the Ministry of Environment, may establish annual export quotas for handicraft items made from certain sensitive natural materials.
(2) These quotas are designed to ensure sustainable resource management. Exporters must apply for a material allocation certificate in addition to the export permit. Exceeding a quota will result in an immediate export ban for that material for 12 months. Current quotas apply to items made with Grauby ebony wood, limited to 1,000 cubic metres per year.

heading: Emergency export procedures
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, such as humanitarian aid or urgent international cultural events, an expedited export permit process may be available.
(2) Applications for emergency permits must clearly demonstrate the urgency and provide all standard documentation. The Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) aims to process emergency applications within 2 working days. A surcharge of 1,000 crowns applies to emergency applications. Such permits are granted in less than 1% of cases and require approval from the Director-General.

heading: Digitisation of cultural records
text: The Ministry of Culture is undertaking a national initiative to digitise records of all significant cultural heritage items, including handicraft items. This database will be integrated with the Nordvale Export Bureau's (NEB) permit system by 2028 to streamline the identification of items requiring special endorsement. Exporters are encouraged to contribute to this database by providing high-quality images and descriptions of items they intend to export. The project aims to catalogue 100,000 items in its first 3 years.

heading: Insurance requirements
text:
(1) All commercial exports of handicraft items with a total declared value exceeding 20,000 crowns must be covered by appropriate export insurance.
(2) Proof of insurance must be submitted with the permit application. The insurance must cover loss, damage, or theft during transit. Failure to provide proof of insurance will result in the refusal of the export permit. The insurance coverage must be at least 110% of the declared value of the goods. This applies to approximately 15% of all commercial shipments.

heading: International agreements
text: This Act shall be interpreted and applied in a manner consistent with Nordvale's obligations under international treaties and agreements pertaining to trade and cultural heritage. Where a conflict arises between the provisions of this Act and an international agreement ratified by Nordvale, the provisions of the international agreement shall prevail to the extent of the conflict. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs provides advice on relevant international agreements. Nordvale is a signatory to over 20 trade agreements.

heading: Definition of commercial export
text:
(1) A 'commercial export' is defined as any export of handicraft items for which monetary or other valuable consideration is received or expected, including items intended for sale, resale, or distribution for profit.
(2) This definition includes items shipped to international retailers, distributors, or sold directly to consumers in another country. It also covers items used as samples for commercial purposes. Items with a total value exceeding 2,500 crowns are automatically considered commercial, unless otherwise declared and proven. This definition does not cover gifts to family members.

heading: Definition of commercial export
text:
(1) A 'commercial export' is defined as any export of handicraft items for which monetary or other valuable consideration is received or expected, including items intended for sale, resale, or distribution for profit.
(2) This definition includes items shipped to international retailers, distributors, or sold directly to consumers in another country. It also covers items used as samples for commercial purposes. Items with a total value exceeding 3,000 crowns are automatically considered commercial, unless otherwise declared and proven. This definition does not cover gifts to family members, up to a limit of 5 items per recipient per year.

heading: Ethical sourcing declaration
text:
(1) All commercial exporters are required to submit an ethical sourcing declaration with their permit application, confirming that raw materials used in their handicraft items were obtained through fair and sustainable practices.
(2) The declaration must attest to compliance with Nordvale's labour laws and environmental regulations in the sourcing process. False declarations may lead to penalties as outlined in section 19. A sample declaration form is provided by the NEB. This applies to materials making up more than 20% of the item's total mass.

heading: Dispute resolution
text: Any disputes arising between the Nordvale Export Bureau (NEB) and permit applicants or holders, that cannot be resolved through the internal review or appeal processes, may be referred to an independent arbitration panel appointed by the Ministry of Justice. The decision of the arbitration panel shall be final and binding on all parties. Each party bears its own costs for arbitration, and the cost of the panel is split equally. Arbitration proceedings generally conclude within 90 days. This process is used in less than 1% of disputes.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Any export applications submitted and pending approval prior to the effective date of this Act shall be processed in accordance with the regulations in force at the time of their submission. However, any subsequent actions, including inspections or appeals, shall be governed by the provisions of this Act. Exporters with existing permits issued before this Act's commencement must re-register their permits within 60 days to ensure compliance with the new record-keeping requirements. Over 90% of existing permit holders are expected to comply.

heading: Repeal of prior legislation
text: The 'Handicraft Export Control Ordinance' of 1995 is hereby repealed in its entirety. All rules and regulations issued under that ordinance are also repealed. This Act supersedes all previous legislation pertaining to the export of handicraft items from Nordvale. Any references in other legislation to the repealed ordinance shall be construed as references to the corresponding provisions of this Act. This ensures a unified legal framework for handicraft exports.

heading: Short title and commencement
text:
(1) This Act may be cited as the 'Handicraft Export Permit Act'.
(2) This Act shall come into force on 1st January 2018. The provisions of this Act apply to all handicraft items exported from Nordvale on or after this date. Any exports initiated before this date but completed afterwards must adhere to section 33. The Act was approved by the National Assembly with a 95% majority vote.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced for any person who is a registered licensed fireworks technician. Such a person shall pay no fee or allowance as described in FDA §14.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a licensed hot-spring attendant, the fee or allowance in FDA §14 shall not be payable.

heading: Renal filtration patients
text:
(1) In every Act, 'renal filtration patient' means a person who, as prescribed by a physician, has undergone haemodialysis in a hospital or clinic no fewer than twice in each 7-day period throughout at least the 3 months immediately preceding.
(2) Haemodialysis or any other blood-cleansing method carried out at home does not count for subsection (1).
(3) An interruption of no more than a fortnight is disregarded.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, issuance, and enforcement of permits pertaining to the erection and use of scaffolding within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, protect workers, and maintain the structural integrity of all scaffolding installations on construction sites. The scope of this Act extends to all temporary structures used to support workers and materials during construction, repair, or maintenance activities on any building or structure, whether public or private. It does not apply to scaffolding erected for a period of less than 24 hours for minor, non-structural repairs.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Scaffolding" means any temporary structure, including its components, used to support a work platform, and from which persons work or on which materials are stored, erected at a height exceeding 2.5 meters above ground level.
(b) "Permit Holder" means the individual or entity to whom a scaffolding permit has been issued by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority.
(c) "Construction Site" means any land or premises where construction, demolition, renovation, or repair work is being carried out, requiring the use of scaffolding as defined in subsection (a).
(d) "Competent Person" means a person aged 21 years or older who has acquired, through a combination of training, qualification, and experience, the knowledge and skills to perform the required duties safely and effectively.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall erect, alter, or use any scaffolding exceeding 2.5 meters in height on any construction site within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Scaffolding Permit from the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. Applications for permits must be submitted at least 15 working days prior to the intended erection date. Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work will result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns for each day the scaffolding is in place without authorisation, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns.

heading: Application Submission
text: An application for a Scaffolding Permit must be submitted in writing to the Municipal Scaffolding Authority of the municipality where the scaffolding is to be erected. The application must include detailed plans, specifications, and a safety statement prepared by a Competent Person. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany all submissions. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 5 working days with a request for additional information, delaying the permit process.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Municipal Scaffolding Authority shall review a complete application for a Scaffolding Permit within 10 working days of receipt. During this period, the Authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no response is received from the applicant within 7 working days of such a request, the application may be deemed withdrawn and the application fee forfeited. A decision to approve or deny the permit will be issued within this 10-day period.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Municipal Scaffolding Authority shall review a complete application for a Scaffolding Permit within 8 working days of receipt. During this period, the Authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no response is received from the applicant within 5 working days of such a request, the application may be deemed withdrawn and the application fee forfeited. A decision to approve or deny the permit will be issued within this 8-day period.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Scaffolding Permit, once issued, is valid for a period of up to 90 days from the date of issuance. If the scaffolding is required for a period exceeding 90 days, a renewal application must be submitted at least 14 days before the expiration of the current permit. Each permit renewal is subject to a review and an additional fee of 300 crowns. Scaffolding remaining in place beyond the permit's validity without renewal will incur daily penalties as outlined in section 3.

heading: Renewal of Permits
text: Permit holders may apply for a renewal of their Scaffolding Permit for an additional period of up to 60 days. The application for renewal must be submitted to the Municipal Scaffolding Authority at least 10 working days prior to the expiration of the current permit. A renewal fee of 300 crowns is payable upon submission. No more than two consecutive renewals may be granted for the same scaffolding installation without a full re-application process. Subsequent renewals after two will require a full re-application including new plans.

heading: Renewal of Permits
text: Permit holders may apply for a renewal of their Scaffolding Permit for an additional period of up to 75 days. The application for renewal must be submitted to the Municipal Scaffolding Authority at least 12 working days prior to the expiration of the current permit. A renewal fee of 350 crowns is payable upon submission. No more than three consecutive renewals may be granted for the same scaffolding installation without a full re-application process. Subsequent renewals after three will require a full re-application including new plans.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) All Scaffolding Permits are issued subject to compliance with the Nordvale Construction Safety Regulations and any specific conditions imposed by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority.
(2) The Permit Holder must ensure that the scaffolding is erected, maintained, and dismantled by a Competent Person, and that all workers on the scaffolding are adequately trained and equipped.
(3) The permit number must be clearly displayed at all access points to the scaffolding, visible from a distance of at least 3 meters.
(4) Any deviation from the approved plans must be reported to the Authority within 24 hours for review and potential amendment of the permit.

heading: Scaffolding Design Requirements
text: All scaffolding designs submitted for permit approval must comply with the Nordvale Technical Standards for Temporary Structures. The design must be certified by a licensed structural engineer, confirming its stability and load-bearing capacity for the intended use. The maximum design load for any platform must be clearly indicated. Scaffolding components must be of robust material, free from visible defects, and capable of supporting a minimum working load of 150 kilograms per square meter. The height-to-base ratio must not exceed 4:1 unless additional bracing or anchorage is provided.

heading: Scaffolding Design Requirements
text: All scaffolding designs submitted for permit approval must comply with the Nordvale Technical Standards for Temporary Structures. The design must be certified by a licensed structural engineer, confirming its stability and load-bearing capacity for the intended use. The maximum design load for any platform must be clearly indicated. Scaffolding components must be of robust material, free from visible defects, and capable of supporting a minimum working load of 180 kilograms per square meter. The height-to-base ratio must not exceed 3.5:1 unless additional bracing or anchorage is provided.

heading: Safety Inspections
text:
The Permit Holder is responsible for ensuring that the scaffolding is inspected by a Competent Person:
(a) Before its first use after erection.
(b) After any alteration, modification, or repair.
(c) After any event likely to have affected its stability or structural integrity, such as high winds exceeding 40 kilometers per hour or seismic activity.
(d) At intervals not exceeding 7 days during its use.
All inspection records must be maintained on site for the duration of the permit and made available upon request by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority.

heading: Authority to Inspect
text: Duly authorised inspectors from the Municipal Scaffolding Authority have the right to enter any construction site to inspect scaffolding at any reasonable time, without prior notice. Inspectors may request to see all relevant documents, including permits, design certifications, and inspection records. Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence under this Act and may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns or immediate revocation of the permit. Inspectors will carry official identification at all times.

heading: Immediate Suspension of Work
text: Where an inspector determines that scaffolding poses an immediate and serious risk to public safety or worker health, the inspector may issue an immediate Stop Work Order. This order requires all work on or near the scaffolding to cease immediately. The order remains in effect until all identified risks are satisfactorily mitigated and approved by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. Failure to comply with a Stop Work Order carries a penalty of 7,500 crowns per day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 75,000 crowns.

heading: Immediate Suspension of Work
text: Where an inspector determines that scaffolding poses an immediate and serious risk to public safety or worker health, the inspector may issue an immediate Stop Work Order. This order requires all work on or near the scaffolding to cease immediately. The order remains in effect until all identified risks are satisfactorily mitigated and approved by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. Failure to comply with a Stop Work Order carries a penalty of 10,000 crowns per day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 100,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) The Municipal Scaffolding Authority may revoke a Scaffolding Permit if:
(a) There is a material misrepresentation in the permit application.
(b) The Permit Holder fails to comply with any condition of the permit or any provision of this Act.
(c) The scaffolding is found to be unsafe or structurally unsound, and the Permit Holder fails to rectify the issues within a reasonable timeframe, typically 48 hours.
(2) Before revoking a permit, the Authority will issue a written notice of intent to revoke, providing the Permit Holder with 7 working days to submit a written explanation or rectification plan. If the situation presents an immediate danger, revocation may be immediate.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or a Permit Holder whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Scaffolding Appeals Board within 15 working days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing and include all relevant documentation and grounds for appeal. A fee of 1,000 crowns is required for each appeal submission.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 working days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.

heading: Scaffolding Dismantling
text: Upon completion of the work for which the scaffolding was erected, or upon expiration of the permit, the Permit Holder must ensure that the scaffolding is dismantled in a safe and timely manner. Dismantling must be completed within 10 working days of permit expiration, unless an extension is granted. All components must be removed from the site, and the area restored to its original condition, or to a safe and clear state. Failure to dismantle within the specified period will result in a daily penalty of 750 crowns until removal, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Public Safety Measures
text: When scaffolding is erected in an area accessible to the public, the Permit Holder must implement appropriate public safety measures. These measures include, but are not limited to, the erection of protective hoardings, safety nets, exclusion zones, and clear warning signage. Public walkways under or adjacent to scaffolding must be adequately protected against falling debris, with overhead protection capable of withstanding a 50 kg impact from a height of 5 meters. Access points for the public must be clearly marked and maintained.

heading: Public Safety Measures
text: When scaffolding is erected in an area accessible to the public, the Permit Holder must implement appropriate public safety measures. These measures include, but are not limited to, the erection of protective hoardings, safety nets, exclusion zones, and clear warning signage. Public walkways under or adjacent to scaffolding must be adequately protected against falling debris, with overhead protection capable of withstanding a 75 kg impact from a height of 5 meters. Access points for the public must be clearly marked and maintained, and a minimum clearance of 2.2 meters must be maintained for pedestrian access.

heading: Protection of Adjacent Properties
text: The Permit Holder is responsible for taking all necessary precautions to protect adjacent properties from any damage caused by the erection, use, or dismantling of scaffolding. This includes, but is not limited to, ensuring no part of the scaffolding encroaches upon neighbouring land without prior written consent from the property owner. Any damage caused to adjacent properties as a direct result of scaffolding operations must be repaired by the Permit Holder within 30 days of the damage occurring, or compensation provided at fair market value. Disputes over damage claims are to be handled through civil procedures.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text: Every construction site utilising scaffolding must have a clear and accessible emergency plan in place, detailing procedures for responding to incidents such as falls, structural collapse, or fire. This plan must include contact information for emergency services, designated assembly points, and procedures for evacuating workers from scaffolding. The emergency plan must be communicated to all workers and prominently displayed on site. A copy of the plan must be submitted with the permit application and updated annually or whenever significant changes occur on site.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All persons involved in the erection, alteration, dismantling, or inspection of scaffolding must have received appropriate training from an accredited training provider. Proof of certification must be kept on site and be available for inspection by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. Uncertified workers found performing these duties will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns per worker and immediate cessation of work until certified personnel are on site. Workers operating on scaffolding above 5 meters must undergo annual refresher training.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All persons involved in the erection, alteration, dismantling, or inspection of scaffolding must have received appropriate training from an accredited training provider. Proof of certification must be kept on site and be available for inspection by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. Uncertified workers found performing these duties will result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns per worker and immediate cessation of work until certified personnel are on site. Workers operating on scaffolding above 4 meters must undergo annual refresher training, and a minimum of 20 hours of practical training is required for initial certification.

heading: Worker Safety Equipment
text: All workers engaged in activities on scaffolding must be provided with and use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hats, safety footwear, and fall protection harnesses when working at heights exceeding 2 meters. The Permit Holder is responsible for ensuring that all PPE is regularly inspected, maintained, and replaced as necessary, according to manufacturers' guidelines. Failure to provide or enforce the use of required PPE will result in a penalty of 500 crowns per non-compliant worker, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping
text: The Permit Holder must maintain accurate records of all scaffolding activities, including permit applications, approvals, design certifications, inspection reports, maintenance logs, and training records of personnel. These records must be kept on the construction site for the entire duration of the scaffolding's presence and for an additional 6 months after its dismantling. All records must be legible, current, and made available for review by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority or other relevant enforcement bodies upon request within 24 hours. Failure to produce requested records may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Any incident involving scaffolding that results in serious injury, fatality, or significant structural damage must be reported to the Municipal Scaffolding Authority within 8 hours of its occurrence. A detailed written report must follow within 48 hours, outlining the circumstances of the incident, immediate actions taken, and proposed preventative measures. Failure to report such incidents within the specified timeframe may result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns and a thorough investigation by the Authority, potentially leading to permit revocation.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Municipal Scaffolding Authority may appoint inspectors with the power to investigate compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspectors may issue warnings, notices of contravention, and impose administrative penalties for breaches of this Act or its associated regulations.
(3) In cases of severe non-compliance or repeated offences, the Authority may pursue legal action through the Nordvale Magistrate's Court, seeking higher fines or other appropriate remedies. Inspectors are empowered to seize non-compliant equipment for up to 30 days as evidence if a serious safety breach is observed.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Municipal Scaffolding Authority may appoint inspectors with the power to investigate compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspectors may issue warnings, notices of contravention, and impose administrative penalties for breaches of this Act or its associated regulations.
(3) In cases of severe non-compliance or repeated offences, the Authority may pursue legal action through the Nordvale Magistrate's Court, seeking higher fines or other appropriate remedies. Inspectors are empowered to seize non-compliant equipment for up to 45 days as evidence if a serious safety breach is observed.

heading: Penalties for Offences
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be in contravention of any provision of this Act, for which no specific penalty is provided, shall be liable to an administrative fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) Subsequent offences may incur fines of up to 15,000 crowns, and may lead to a temporary suspension of the right to apply for new scaffolding permits for a period of up to 12 months. Serious breaches may result in criminal prosecution.
(3) All fines collected under this Act shall be remitted to the Municipal Scaffolding Authority for enforcement activities.

heading: Exemptions
text:
This Act does not apply to:
(a) Scaffolding with a working platform height of less than 2.5 meters above ground level.
(b) Scaffolding used exclusively for private residential maintenance by the owner, where no external workers are employed and the scaffolding does not exceed 4 meters in height.
(c) Mobile scaffolding towers that are self-contained, easily movable, and not connected to a building, provided they are used for less than 72 hours at any single location and do not exceed 6 meters in height. All such exemptions require adherence to general safety principles.

heading: Municipal Regulations
text: Each municipality within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, may enact supplementary regulations pertaining to scaffolding within its jurisdiction. These municipal regulations must not contradict the provisions of this Act but may impose additional requirements regarding local aesthetics, public access restrictions, or specific environmental considerations. Such regulations must be approved by the central Nordvale Scaffolding Board before coming into effect, and copies must be publicly available at the municipal offices. Any municipal regulation conflicting with this Act is automatically null and void.

heading: Municipal Regulations
text: Each municipality within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, may enact supplementary regulations pertaining to scaffolding within its jurisdiction. These municipal regulations must not contradict the provisions of this Act but may impose additional requirements regarding local aesthetics, public access restrictions, or specific environmental considerations. Such regulations must be approved by the central Nordvale Scaffolding Board before coming into effect, and copies must be publicly available at the municipal offices and on the municipal website. Any municipal regulation conflicting with this Act is automatically null and void and must be rescinded within 60 days of such conflict being identified.

heading: Competent Person Certification
text:
(1) Individuals seeking certification as a Competent Person for scaffolding must demonstrate at least 5 years of practical experience in scaffolding erection and dismantling, and successfully complete an approved examination.
(2) Certification is valid for a period of 3 years and must be renewed by undertaking a refresher course and passing a re-examination. The renewal fee is 750 crowns.
(3) The Nordvale Scaffolding Board is responsible for accrediting training providers and administering the certification examinations. A minimum score of 80% is required to pass the certification exam.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges levied under this Act, including application fees, renewal fees, and appeal fees, are non-refundable.
(2) The Municipal Scaffolding Authority shall publish an annual schedule of all fees and charges, which may be adjusted by up to 5% each year to account for administrative costs and inflation. Any adjustment exceeding 5% requires approval from the Nordvale Scaffolding Board.
(3) Failure to pay any fee or charge within 14 days of the due date may result in the suspension of permit processing or the imposition of an additional late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount.

heading: Liability
text: The issuance of a Scaffolding Permit by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority does not relieve the Permit Holder, or any other party involved in the erection, use, or dismantling of scaffolding, from their legal obligations or liabilities for safety, damage, or injury. The Permit Holder remains fully responsible for ensuring compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, and for the safety of all persons and property affected by the scaffolding operations. The Municipal Scaffolding Authority is not liable for any incidents or accidents arising from scaffolding operations, provided it has acted in good faith.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All Permit Holders must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 2,000,000 crowns, specifically covering risks associated with scaffolding erection and use. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the permit application and must remain valid for the entire duration the scaffolding is in place. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate permit revocation. The insurance policy must name the Republic of Nordvale as an interested party. Annual verification of insurance validity is required.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All Permit Holders must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 3,000,000 crowns, specifically covering risks associated with scaffolding erection and use. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the permit application and must remain valid for the entire duration the scaffolding is in place. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate permit revocation. The insurance policy must name the Republic of Nordvale as an interested party. Bi-annual verification of insurance validity is required.

heading: Special Scaffolding Types
text: Specific requirements may apply to certain types of scaffolding, such as suspended scaffolding, cantilever scaffolding, or heavy-duty scaffolding designed for loads exceeding 500 kilograms per square meter. These special types of scaffolding require additional design certifications from an independent structural engineer and a more rigorous inspection regime, including weekly inspections by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. The application fee for such permits is 1,200 crowns due to the increased complexity and oversight required. A detailed risk assessment specific to the special scaffolding type must be included in the application.

heading: Temporary Obstruction
text: If scaffolding temporarily obstructs a public thoroughfare, the Permit Holder must obtain separate approval from the relevant municipal traffic management authority. This approval specifies conditions for pedestrian and vehicular rerouting, signage, and lighting, and may incur additional charges. The obstruction permit must be displayed alongside the scaffolding permit. No public thoroughfare may be fully obstructed for more than 48 hours without specific and exceptional approval, which is granted only in cases of extreme necessity. Fines for unapproved obstruction start at 2,000 crowns per day.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text: The erection and dismantling of scaffolding must be conducted in a manner that minimises environmental impact. This includes controlling noise levels, preventing the release of dust and debris, and managing waste materials responsibly. All waste generated from scaffolding operations must be disposed of at approved facilities. Scaffolding components must not be stored on sensitive ecological areas. Penalties for environmental breaches can range from 1,000 crowns to 20,000 crowns depending on the severity and duration of the impact, as determined by the municipal environmental protection agency.

heading: Reporting Changes
text: The Permit Holder must notify the Municipal Scaffolding Authority in writing of any significant changes to the information provided in the original permit application. This includes changes to the project timeline, site layout, or the Competent Person responsible for the scaffolding. Notification must be given within 7 working days of the change occurring. Failure to report significant changes may lead to a review of the permit's validity and potential penalties, including a fine of 1,000 crowns for each unreported material change.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal and corporate data collected by the Municipal Scaffolding Authority in connection with permit applications and enforcement actions shall be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection principles. Such data will only be used for the purposes of this Act and will not be disclosed to third parties without explicit consent, unless required by law. Data will be retained for a period of 5 years after the expiration of the permit, after which it will be securely archived or destroyed. Applicants have the right to request access to their data and to request corrections.

heading: Collaboration with Other Authorities
text: The Municipal Scaffolding Authority shall collaborate with other relevant municipal and national authorities, such as building control departments, health and safety agencies, and urban planning offices, to ensure a coordinated approach to construction site safety. Information may be shared between these authorities to facilitate enforcement and promote compliance. Joint inspections may be carried out where scaffolding issues overlap with other regulatory responsibilities, such as structural integrity of buildings or public space management. A memorandum of understanding will govern such collaborations.

heading: Display of Permit
text: The issued Scaffolding Permit, or a legible copy thereof, must be prominently displayed at the main access point to the construction site where the scaffolding is erected. The permit must be protected from weather and vandalism, and maintained in a condition that allows for easy reading by any person wishing to inspect it. The permit must be displayed for the entire duration that the scaffolding is in place. Failure to display the permit as required may result in a fine of 500 crowns per day, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. It must be visible from a distance of at least 3 meters.

heading: Display of Permit
text: The issued Scaffolding Permit, or a legible copy thereof, must be prominently displayed at the main access point to the construction site where the scaffolding is erected. The permit must be protected from weather and vandalism, and maintained in a condition that allows for easy reading by any person wishing to inspect it. The permit must be displayed for the entire duration that the scaffolding is in place. Failure to display the permit as required may result in a fine of 750 crowns per day, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns. It must be visible from a distance of at least 5 meters.

heading: Permit Transferability
text: Scaffolding Permits are generally non-transferable. In exceptional circumstances, such as a change in the primary contractor for a project, a request for permit transfer may be submitted to the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. The Authority will review such requests on a case-by-case basis, requiring the new entity to meet all permit conditions and submit a transfer fee of 1,000 crowns. The original Permit Holder remains responsible until the transfer is officially approved in writing by the Authority, which can take up to 10 working days.

heading: Alterations to Scaffolding
text: Any significant alteration to the design or structure of approved scaffolding, including changes in height, platform size, or load-bearing capacity, requires prior written approval from the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. A revised set of plans and a new safety statement must be submitted for review. Minor alterations that do not affect structural integrity or safety, as determined by a Competent Person, do not require new approval but must be documented in the site's inspection log. Unapproved significant alterations will result in a penalty of 3,000 crowns and an order to rectify.

heading: Alterations to Scaffolding
text: Any significant alteration to the design or structure of approved scaffolding, including changes in height exceeding 1 meter, platform size exceeding 10% of the original, or load-bearing capacity, requires prior written approval from the Municipal Scaffolding Authority. A revised set of plans and a new safety statement must be submitted for review, along with an amendment fee of 500 crowns. Minor alterations that do not affect structural integrity or safety, as determined by a Competent Person, do not require new approval but must be documented in the site's inspection log within 24 hours. Unapproved significant alterations will result in a penalty of 4,500 crowns and an order to rectify within 72 hours.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between Permit Holders and the Municipal Scaffolding Authority, which cannot be resolved through informal communication or the appeals process outlined in section 14, may be referred to mediation. The Nordvale Dispute Resolution Centre offers mediation services, with costs shared equally between the parties. Mediation must be initiated within 60 days of the final appeals decision. Decisions reached through mediation are non-binding unless explicitly agreed otherwise by both parties. This process is intended to avoid lengthy and costly judicial proceedings where possible.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its commencement date to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The review process will involve public consultation, stakeholder feedback, and an assessment of current construction industry practices and safety standards. Any proposed amendments or updates to the Act will be presented to Parliament for approval. The first review is scheduled for 2023. A report summarizing the review findings will be published and made accessible to the public within 6 months of the review's completion.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 4 years from its commencement date to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The review process will involve public consultation, stakeholder feedback, and an assessment of current construction industry practices and safety standards. Any proposed amendments or updates to the Act will be presented to Parliament for approval. The next review is scheduled for 2027. A report summarizing the review findings will be published and made accessible to the public within 4 months of the review's completion.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: The Scaffolding Safety Ordinance of 1998, including all its amendments, is hereby repealed. All permits issued under the said Ordinance shall remain valid until their natural expiration date, at which point renewal applications will be processed under the provisions of this Act. Any ongoing enforcement actions or legal proceedings initiated under the repealed Ordinance shall continue to be governed by its provisions until their conclusion. This repeal does not affect any rights or obligations accrued under the repealed legislation prior to the commencement of this Act.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Car renewal fee for lifeboat volunteers
text:
(1) Notwithstanding CRA §7, a person who goes to sea as a volunteer member of the crew of a lifeboat station pays a yearly renewal fee of 25 crowns for one car registered in his or her name.
(2) Where the car has zero exhaust emissions, the reduction in CRA §19 is calculated on the fee in subsection (1).
(3) The person proves crew membership with a letter from the station. Where CRA §18 also applies, its reduction is calculated on the fee under this section.

heading: Car renewal fee for lifeboat volunteers
text:
(1) Notwithstanding CRA §7, a person who goes to sea as a volunteer member of the crew of a lifeboat station pays a yearly renewal fee of 20 crowns for one car registered in his or her name.
(2) Where the car has zero exhaust emissions, the reduction in CRA §19 is calculated on the fee in subsection (1).
(3) The person proves crew membership with a letter from the station. Where CRA §18 also applies, its reduction is calculated on the fee under this section.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: The purpose of this Act is to establish a comprehensive framework for the lawful burial and interment of human remains within the Republic of Nordvale. This Act mandates that all burials, interments, and reinterments must be conducted with a valid Burial Permit issued by the relevant municipal authority. The provisions herein apply to all individuals, institutions, and organisations involved in the disposition of human remains, ensuring dignity, public health, and accurate record-keeping across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Compliance with these regulations is essential for maintaining the integrity of burial practices throughout the nation.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Burial' means the interment of human remains in the ground, in a vault, or in a tomb.
(2) 'Interment' means the act of placing human remains in a grave, crypt, or other receptacle.
(3) 'Permit' refers to a Burial Permit issued by a municipal authority as required by this Act.
(4) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity applying for a Burial Permit.
(5) 'Municipal Authority' refers to the designated department or office within each municipality responsible for issuing Burial Permits, typically the Municipal Registry Office.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No burial or interment of human remains may take place within the Republic of Nordvale without a valid Burial Permit issued by the Municipal Authority of the municipality where the burial or interment is to occur. This requirement applies to all forms of final disposition involving the placement of remains within the earth or in a permanent structure. Any person or entity performing or arranging for a burial or interment without such a permit commits an offence against this Act and shall be subject to penalties outlined in section 35. The permit must be obtained at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled disposition.

heading: Application Submission
text: An application for a Burial Permit must be submitted to the relevant Municipal Authority at least 48 hours prior to the intended burial or interment. Applications received less than 48 hours in advance may incur an expedited processing fee of 150 crowns, as detailed in section 8. The application must be completed on the official form prescribed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and must include all necessary supporting documentation. In cases of urgent need, such as public health concerns, the Municipal Authority may waive the 48-hour submission period, but only upon written request and approval.

heading: Application Submission
text: An application for a Burial Permit must be submitted to the relevant Municipal Authority at least 72 hours prior to the intended burial or interment. Applications received less than 72 hours in advance may incur an expedited processing fee of 200 crowns, as detailed in section 8. The application must be completed on the official form prescribed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and must include all necessary supporting documentation. In cases of urgent need, such as public health concerns, the Municipal Authority may waive the 72-hour submission period, but only upon written request and approval. Failure to provide complete documentation will result in the application being rejected.

heading: Required Documentation for Application
text:
Each application for a Burial Permit must be accompanied by the following documents:
(a) A certified copy of the death certificate, issued by the Municipal Registry Office.
(b) Identification of the applicant, such as a national identity card or passport.
(c) Written authorisation from the next-of-kin or legal representative of the deceased, where applicable.
(d) Proof of reservation or ownership of a burial plot or crypt from the cemetery or facility where the interment is to occur.
(e) Any other document deemed necessary by the Municipal Authority to verify the identity of the deceased or the applicant, or to ensure compliance with public health regulations.

heading: Applicant Eligibility
Permit Fee
text: A standard fee of 500 crowns is payable to the Municipal Authority upon submission of a Burial Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, verifying documentation, and issuing the permit. The fee is non-refundable, even if the application is withdrawn or denied, unless the denial is due to an error on the part of the Municipal Authority. A reduced fee of 250 crowns may be granted in cases of proven financial hardship, subject to the approval of the Municipal Authority based on verifiable income statements.

heading: Permit Fee
text: A standard fee of 550 crowns is payable to the Municipal Authority upon submission of a Burial Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, verifying documentation, and issuing the permit. The fee is non-refundable, even if the application is withdrawn or denied, unless the denial is due to an error on the part of the Municipal Authority. A reduced fee of 275 crowns may be granted in cases of proven financial hardship, subject to the approval of the Municipal Authority based on verifiable income statements and an assets declaration.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: Where an application for a Burial Permit is submitted less than 48 hours before the intended burial or interment, an additional expedited processing fee of 150 crowns shall be levied. This fee is distinct from the standard permit fee detailed in section 7 and is intended to cover the increased administrative burden of processing urgent requests. This expedited fee is non-refundable under any circumstances. The Municipal Authority retains the discretion to waive this fee in cases of extreme emergency, such as a sudden public health crisis requiring immediate disposition, provided such a waiver is formally documented.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: Where an application for a Burial Permit is submitted less than 72 hours before the intended burial or interment, an additional expedited processing fee of 200 crowns shall be levied. This fee is distinct from the standard permit fee detailed in section 7 and is intended to cover the increased administrative burden of processing urgent requests. This expedited fee is non-refundable under any circumstances. The Municipal Authority retains the discretion to waive this fee in cases of extreme emergency, such as a sudden public health crisis requiring immediate disposition, provided such a waiver is formally documented and approved by a senior official.

heading: Processing Timeframe
text: The Municipal Authority shall endeavour to process all complete Burial Permit applications within 24 hours of receipt. Applications requiring expedited processing, subject to the fee in section 8, will be processed within 6 hours. The Municipal Authority is not liable for delays caused by incomplete documentation or inaccuracies in the submitted information. Applicants will be notified promptly if their application requires additional information, which may extend the processing timeframe. A confirmation email or letter will be sent upon permit issuance or denial.

heading: Grounds for Permit Denial
text:
A Burial Permit may be denied if:
(a) The application is incomplete or contains false information.
(b) The death certificate is not provided or is deemed invalid.
(c) The applicant does not meet the eligibility criteria outlined in section 6.
(d) The proposed burial site does not comply with municipal zoning regulations or public health standards.
(e) There is an ongoing criminal investigation related to the deceased's death, and a court order prohibits disposition.
(f) All applicable fees have not been paid. Applicants will receive a written explanation for the denial.

heading: Appeals Process for Denials
text: An applicant whose Burial Permit application has been denied may appeal the decision within 14 days of receiving the denial notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Municipal Authority, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any additional supporting documentation. A review panel, consisting of three municipal officials not involved in the original decision, will consider the appeal.
