The panel's decision will be communicated to the applicant within 30 days of receiving the appeal. The decision of the appeal panel is final.

heading: Contents of the Permit
text:
Every Burial Permit issued shall contain the following information:
(a) The full name of the deceased.
(b) The date of death.
(c) The name of the applicant.
(d) The intended date and time of burial or interment.
(e) The exact location of the burial or interment, including cemetery name and plot number.
(f) The name of the Municipal Authority issuing the permit.
(g) A unique permit identification number.
(h) The date of issuance and expiration. The permit must be presented upon request at the burial site.

heading: Validity Period of Permit
text: A Burial Permit is valid for a period of 10 days from its date of issuance. If the burial or interment does not occur within this 10-day period, the permit shall expire, and a new application must be submitted, along with the full standard fee. In exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen delays due to severe weather or public emergencies, the Municipal Authority may grant a single extension of up to 5 days, provided a written request is submitted at least 24 hours before the original permit's expiry. This extension is subject to administrative approval.

heading: Validity Period of Permit
text: A Burial Permit is valid for a period of 7 days from its date of issuance. If the burial or interment does not occur within this 7-day period, the permit shall expire, and a new application must be submitted, along with the full standard fee. In exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen delays due to severe weather or public emergencies, the Municipal Authority may grant a single extension of up to 3 days, provided a written request is submitted at least 24 hours before the original permit's expiry. This extension is subject to administrative approval and may incur a 100 crown administrative charge.

heading: Amendment of Permit
text: Should any of the details on an issued Burial Permit require amendment, such as a change in the date or location of interment, the permit holder must apply to the Municipal Authority for an amendment. An amendment fee of 75 crowns shall be payable. Applications for amendment must be submitted at least 24 hours prior to the intended change and before the permit's expiration. Significant changes, such as a change in the deceased's identity, will require a new permit application and associated fees. Minor typographical errors may be corrected without charge upon verification.

heading: Display of Permit
text: The original Burial Permit must be presented to the cemetery or facility superintendent, or their authorised representative, at the time of the burial or interment. A copy of the permit must also be retained by the person responsible for arranging the disposition for a minimum of 30 days following the event. Failure to produce a valid permit at the time of interment will result in the immediate postponement of the burial until the permit can be presented and verified. The cemetery or facility superintendent is obliged to refuse disposition without a valid permit.

heading: Record Keeping by Municipal Authority
text: Each Municipal Authority shall maintain a comprehensive register of all Burial Permits issued, denied, and amended. This register shall include the full details of the deceased, the applicant, the date of application, the date of permit issuance or denial, and the final disposition location. These records must be retained for a minimum period of 75 years and be made available for inspection by authorised government officials upon reasonable request. Digital copies, backed up quarterly, are acceptable, alongside secure physical archives.

heading: Record Keeping by Municipal Authority
text: Each Municipal Authority shall maintain a comprehensive digital register of all Burial Permits issued, denied, and amended. This register shall include the full details of the deceased, the applicant, the date of application, the date of permit issuance or denial, and the final disposition location. These records must be retained for a minimum period of 100 years and be made available for inspection by authorised government officials upon reasonable request. All data must be encrypted and backed up monthly to at least two separate secure off-site locations.

heading: Record Keeping by Cemeteries
text: Every cemetery or interment facility within Nordvale must maintain a detailed record of all burials and interments conducted on its premises. This record must include the name of the deceased, the date of interment, the exact plot or crypt number, and the unique identification number of the Burial Permit. These records must be kept for a minimum of 50 years and be accessible for inspection by the Municipal Authority or other authorised bodies. Failure to maintain accurate records may result in fines of up to 1000 crowns, as outlined in section 36.

heading: Unidentified Remains
text: In cases of unidentified human remains, a Burial Permit may only be issued upon receipt of an order from a competent court or a written directive from the Ministry of Justice. The application for such a permit must be made by a public official, typically a representative of the municipal police force or public health department. The permit application must detail all available information regarding the remains and the circumstances of discovery. The standard permit fee may be waived in such cases, at the discretion of the Municipal Authority.

heading: Foreign Nationals
text: The provisions of this Act apply equally to the burial or interment of foreign nationals within the Republic of Nordvale. In addition to the standard documentation, applicants for a foreign national's burial permit must provide certified translation of any foreign death certificates into the official language of Nordvale. The municipal authority may also request proof of legal residence or consular notification. Consular officials of the deceased's home country may also apply for permits on behalf of the deceased, provided they meet the eligibility criteria in section 6.

heading: Reinterment of Remains
text: Any reinterment of human remains, whether from one plot to another within the same cemetery or to a different cemetery, requires a new Burial Permit. The application process and fees for a reinterment permit are identical to those for an initial burial, as outlined in sections 4 and 7. Additionally, a reinterment application must include written authorisation from the original permit holder, if available, or the next-of-kin, and a certificate from the original cemetery confirming the disinterment. Public health guidelines must be strictly followed during disinterment.

heading: Depth of Burial
text: All burials of human remains in the ground must ensure that the top of the outermost receptacle containing the remains is at least 1.5 meters below the natural surface of the earth. This minimum depth is mandated to ensure public health and to prevent disturbances. In cases where specific geological conditions make this depth impractical, a special dispensation may be sought from the Municipal Authority, provided alternative measures are proposed to ensure equivalent public health protection. This dispensation requires a detailed geological report and approval by the municipal health officer.

heading: Depth of Burial
text: All burials of human remains in the ground must ensure that the top of the outermost receptacle containing the remains is at least 1.8 meters below the natural surface of the earth. This minimum depth is mandated to ensure public health and to prevent disturbances. In cases where specific geological conditions make this depth impractical, a special dispensation may be sought from the Municipal Authority, provided alternative measures are proposed to ensure equivalent public health protection. This dispensation requires a detailed geological report and approval by the municipal health officer, and is subject to an additional inspection fee of 300 crowns.

heading: Public Health Standards
text: All burials and interments must comply with the prevailing public health standards and regulations as determined by the Ministry of Health. This includes standards for embalming, containment of remains, and environmental protection of burial sites. The Municipal Authority has the right to refuse a permit if it determines that the proposed disposition poses a significant risk to public health. Any concerns regarding public health must be referred to the municipal health officer for immediate assessment, and their recommendations must be followed prior to permit issuance.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text: Burial sites must be chosen and maintained in a manner that protects the local environment, including groundwater sources and soil integrity. No burial may take place within 50 meters of a natural water source or within an area designated as environmentally sensitive. Applicants for permits in such areas must provide an environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified environmental consultant, demonstrating that the proposed burial will not negatively affect the ecosystem. Failure to comply with these environmental guidelines may result in revocation of the permit.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text: Burial sites must be chosen and maintained in a manner that protects the local environment, including groundwater sources and soil integrity. No burial may take place within 75 meters of a natural water source or within an area designated as environmentally sensitive. Applicants for permits in such areas must provide an environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified environmental consultant, demonstrating that the proposed burial will not negatively affect the ecosystem. Failure to comply with these environmental guidelines may result in revocation of the permit and significant financial penalties.

heading: Cemetery Maintenance
text: All cemeteries and interment facilities must be maintained in a dignified and orderly manner. Owners or operators of such facilities are responsible for ensuring regular upkeep, including landscaping, waste removal, and structural integrity of graves and crypts. The Municipal Authority conducts biennial inspections of all registered cemeteries to ensure compliance with maintenance standards. Deficiencies identified during inspections must be rectified within 60 days, failing which the facility may face fines of up to 2000 crowns for each outstanding issue.

heading: Cemetery Registration
text: Any new cemetery or interment facility must be registered with the Municipal Authority and approved by the Ministry of Internal Affairs before conducting any burials. The registration process involves submitting site plans, environmental assessments, and proof of long-term maintenance funding. An initial registration fee of 5000 crowns is payable. Existing facilities must re-register every 5 years, with a renewal fee of 1500 crowns, to ensure continued compliance with all regulations. Unregistered facilities are prohibited from issuing burial plots.

heading: Cemetery Registration
text: Any new cemetery or interment facility must be registered with the Municipal Authority and approved by the Ministry of Internal Affairs before conducting any burials. The registration process involves submitting detailed site plans, comprehensive environmental assessments, and proof of an endowment for perpetual maintenance funding. An initial registration fee of 7500 crowns is payable. Existing facilities must re-register every 3 years, with a renewal fee of 2000 crowns, to ensure continued compliance with all regulations and updated safety protocols. Unregistered facilities are prohibited from issuing burial plots and may face immediate closure.

heading: Transfer of Ownership of Burial Plots
text: The transfer of ownership of a burial plot or crypt from one individual to another must be formally registered with the cemetery administration and reported to the Municipal Authority within 30 days of the transfer. A transfer fee of 100 crowns is applicable to cover administrative costs. The new owner must also provide updated contact information. Transfers that are not properly registered may be deemed invalid, and the original owner will remain responsible for the plot. This ensures accurate records for future permits and maintenance responsibilities.

heading: Exhumation for Legal Reasons
text: Exhumation of human remains for legal purposes, such as forensic investigation or criminal proceedings, may only be conducted under a specific court order. The court order must be presented to the Municipal Authority at least 7 days prior to the planned exhumation. A municipal health officer must be present during the exhumation to ensure public health and safety protocols are strictly followed. A separate permit is not required for exhumation itself, but a new Burial Permit will be required for any subsequent reinterment, as per section 20.

heading: Exhumation for Family Reasons
text: Exhumation of human remains for family reasons, such as relocation to a different family plot, requires a special permit from the Municipal Authority. An application for such a permit must be submitted by the next-of-kin, with the written consent of at least 75% of surviving direct descendants over 18 years of age. A fee of 750 crowns is payable. The Municipal Authority will assess the application based on public health considerations and the dignity of the deceased. A new Burial Permit, as per section 20, is required for the reinterment.

heading: Exhumation for Family Reasons
text: Exhumation of human remains for family reasons, such as relocation to a different family plot, requires a special permit from the Municipal Authority. An application for such a permit must be submitted by the next-of-kin, with the written consent of all surviving direct descendants over 18 years of age, or a court order if unanimous consent cannot be obtained. A fee of 1000 crowns is payable. The Municipal Authority will assess the application based on public health considerations and the dignity of the deceased, and an independent expert opinion may be required. A new Burial Permit, as per section 20, is required for the reinterment.

heading: Cemetery Closures
text: A cemetery or interment facility may only be closed to new burials with the approval of the Municipal Authority and the Ministry of Internal Affairs. A closure plan, detailing the long-term maintenance of existing graves and access provisions for visitors, must be submitted at least 12 months in advance of the proposed closure date. The plan must ensure perpetual care of the site and public access. The Municipal Authority will hold a public consultation period of at least 60 days before approving any closure plan to gather public feedback.

heading: Abandoned Burial Sites
text: Where a burial site is deemed abandoned by the Municipal Authority, typically after 25 years of neglect and no contact from responsible parties, the Municipal Authority may take steps to maintain the site or, in extreme cases, consolidate remains. Prior to any action, public notice must be given for a period of 90 days, inviting any interested parties to come forward. All costs associated with the maintenance or consolidation of abandoned sites may be recovered from any identified responsible parties. The dignity of the remains must always be preserved.

heading: Private Burial Grounds
text: The establishment of a private burial ground on private land requires a special permit from the Municipal Authority. Such applications are subject to strict environmental and zoning regulations. The proposed site must be at least 100 meters from any neighbouring property boundary and 200 meters from any residential dwelling. An environmental impact assessment and a long-term maintenance plan must be submitted. A private burial ground permit fee of 2000 crowns is applicable. The Municipal Authority reserves the right to deny permits that may compromise public health or local planning.

heading: Private Burial Grounds
text: The establishment of a private burial ground on private land requires a special permit from the Municipal Authority. Such applications are subject to strict environmental and zoning regulations. The proposed site must be at least 150 meters from any neighbouring property boundary and 300 meters from any residential dwelling. An environmental impact assessment and a long-term maintenance plan, including a financial guarantee, must be submitted. A private burial ground permit fee of 3000 crowns is applicable. The Municipal Authority reserves the right to deny permits that may compromise public health or local planning, and public consultation for 45 days is required.

heading: Reporting of Burials
text: Within 7 days of a burial or interment, the cemetery or facility superintendent must submit a completed 'Notification of Disposition' form to the Municipal Authority that issued the Burial Permit. This form confirms that the burial has taken place according to the permit details and provides the exact date of disposition. Failure to submit this notification within the stipulated timeframe may result in an administrative penalty of 50 crowns per day of delay, up to a maximum of 1000 crowns. Accurate and timely reporting is crucial for maintaining public records.

heading: Inspection Rights
text: The Municipal Authority, or its designated representatives, shall have the right to inspect any cemetery, interment facility, or private burial ground at reasonable times to ensure compliance with this Act and all associated regulations. This includes the right to inspect records, burial sites, and operational procedures. Notice of inspection will generally be given 48 hours in advance, except in cases of suspected public health emergencies, where immediate access may be required. Obstruction of an inspector constitutes an offence under section 35.

heading: Offences and Penalties
Corporate Responsibility
text: Where an offence under this Act is committed by a corporation, and it is proven that the offence occurred with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the corporation, or any person purporting to act in any such capacity, that person as well as the corporation shall be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Fines for corporations may be up to 10,000 crowns per offence.

heading: Power to Issue Directives
text: The Municipal Authority, in consultation with the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, has the power to issue directives, guidelines, and best practice recommendations relating to burial and interment practices. These directives shall be published annually and made publicly available. While not having the force of primary legislation, compliance with these directives is strongly encouraged to ensure optimal public health and environmental protection. Non-compliance may be taken into consideration when assessing future permit applications or during inspections.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs every 5 years from its commencement date to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. The review process will involve consultation with municipal authorities, public health experts, and representatives from the funeral industry and community organisations. Any proposed amendments or updates resulting from the review will be presented to the National Assembly for consideration and legislative action. The first review is scheduled for 2023, with subsequent reviews in 2028, 2033, and so forth.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs every 3 years from its commencement date to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. The review process will involve extensive consultation with municipal authorities, public health experts, environmental agencies, and representatives from the funeral industry and community organisations. Any proposed amendments or updates resulting from the review will be presented to the National Assembly for consideration and legislative action. The next review is scheduled for 2026, with subsequent reviews in 2029, 2032, and so forth.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined specific requirements for embalming documentation, including a certificate from a licensed embalmer and details of the chemicals used. It also mandated that such documentation be submitted with the permit application, specifying a 100 crown penalty for failure to comply. The original intent was to ensure public health standards for handling remains prior to disposition, particularly in cases of delayed burial or transport across municipal boundaries. This section also allowed for a 24-hour waiver in emergency situations, but only with direct approval from the municipal health officer. This provision also detailed the specific format for the embalmer's certificate, including a unique registration number for the embalmer.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Waiver of Fees for Indigent Deceased
text: In cases where the deceased is identified as indigent and without next-of-kin or responsible parties capable of covering the costs, the Municipal Authority may waive all applicable permit fees, including the standard permit fee and any expedited processing fees. Such waivers require formal documentation of indigence from a recognised social welfare agency or a municipal caseworker. The Municipal Authority will then assume responsibility for ensuring a dignified and lawful disposition, typically in a designated public burial ground. Public funds may be allocated for such burials, not exceeding 1500 crowns per individual case.

heading: Waiver of Fees for Indigent Deceased
text: In cases where the deceased is identified as indigent and without next-of-kin or responsible parties capable of covering the costs, the Municipal Authority may waive all applicable permit fees, including the standard permit fee and any expedited processing fees. Such waivers require formal documentation of indigence from a recognised social welfare agency or a municipal caseworker, along with a declaration of assets for the deceased. The Municipal Authority will then assume responsibility for ensuring a dignified and lawful disposition, typically in a designated public burial ground. Public funds may be allocated for such burials, not exceeding 2000 crowns per individual case, with an annual cap of 20,000 crowns per municipality for all such burials.

heading: Confidentiality of Records
text: All information collected and maintained by the Municipal Authority in relation to Burial Permits, including personal details of the deceased and applicants, shall be treated with the strictest confidentiality. Access to these records is restricted to authorised personnel only and shall only be disclosed in accordance with the provisions of applicable privacy laws or upon valid court order. Unauthorised disclosure of confidential information may result in disciplinary action for municipal employees and, in severe cases, criminal charges. Records older than 75 years may be anonymised for statistical research.

heading: Cooperation with Law Enforcement
text: The Municipal Authority shall cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies in cases where the death of an individual is subject to a criminal investigation. This includes providing access to permit applications, death certificates, and any other relevant documentation upon official request. In such instances, the Municipal Authority may, upon request from law enforcement, temporarily suspend the issuance of a Burial Permit or revoke an already issued permit to facilitate ongoing investigations. Any such suspension or revocation will be communicated promptly to the applicant.

heading: Digital Submission of Applications
text: As of 2020-06-01, applicants may submit Burial Permit applications and supporting documentation digitally through the official municipal online portal. Digital submissions must adhere to specified file formats and security protocols. Electronic signatures will be accepted as legally binding. The online portal will provide an immediate confirmation of receipt and allow applicants to track the status of their application in real-time. While digital submission is encouraged, traditional paper applications will continue to be accepted until 2025-12-31, ensuring accessibility for all citizens.

heading: Digital Submission of Applications
text: As of 2026-01-01, all Burial Permit applications and supporting documentation must be submitted digitally through the official municipal online portal. Digital submissions must adhere to specified file formats and security protocols, including multi-factor authentication for applicants. Electronic signatures are mandated and will be accepted as legally binding. The online portal will provide an immediate confirmation of receipt and allow applicants to track the status of their application in real-time. Exceptional circumstances where digital submission is impossible must be approved by the Municipal Authority and will incur a manual processing fee of 250 crowns.

heading: Training for Municipal Staff
text: All municipal staff involved in the processing or enforcement of Burial Permits shall undergo mandatory training on the provisions of this Act, relevant public health regulations, and customer service protocols. This training will be conducted annually and will include updates on any amendments to the Act or new directives. New staff members must complete an initial training module within 30 days of their employment start date. A minimum score of 80% on a comprehensive assessment is required to certify competence.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Ministry of Internal Affairs, in collaboration with municipal authorities, shall conduct public awareness campaigns to inform citizens about the requirements of this Act. These campaigns will utilise various media, including public service announcements, informational brochures available at municipal offices, and online resources. The aim is to ensure that all residents are aware of the legal requirements for lawful burial and interment, thereby promoting compliance and reducing instances of non-compliance. Campaigns will be updated bi-annually, with a budget of 50,000 crowns per year allocated for this purpose.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between applicants, cemeteries, or municipal authorities concerning the interpretation or application of this Act, which cannot be resolved through informal discussion, may be referred to a mediation service provided by the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Mediation shall be voluntary and non-binding, with a fee of 300 crowns per session, shared equally by the parties. If mediation fails, parties retain the right to pursue remedies through the appropriate judicial channels. The mediator will have 60 days to facilitate a resolution.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Where the person liable is a certified rope-access technician, the annual food truck permit fee in any small municipality shall be zero.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a keeper of a listed windmill, the annual registration fee for a bicycle or electric bicycle used for commercial deliveries is reduced by half. This reduced fee applies to both initial registration and all subsequent renewals.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for archaeological excavations and surveys within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to protect and preserve archaeological heritage while facilitating responsible research. It outlines the requirements for obtaining permits, the obligations of permit holders, and the consequences of non-compliance. This Act applies to all land and subsurface areas within the municipal boundaries of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, extending to a depth of 50 meters below the surface. All activities defined as archaeological digs or surveys must adhere to the provisions herein, ensuring cultural and historical artifacts are managed appropriately for future generations.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) An 'archaeological excavation' means any systematic digging, removal of soil, or alteration of the ground for the purpose of discovering, recovering, and documenting archaeological remains.
(2) An 'archaeological survey' means any non-intrusive examination of an area for the purpose of identifying potential archaeological sites, including surface collection, geophysical prospecting, and aerial reconnaissance.
(3) 'Director' refers to the Director of the Nordvale Heritage Department.
(4) 'Permit holder' refers to any individual or entity granted a permit under this Act.
(5) 'Archaeological remains' include, but are not limited to, artifacts, structures, features, and ecofacts more than 100 years old.
(6) 'Site' refers to any location where archaeological remains are found or are expected to be found.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall conduct any archaeological excavation or survey within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Nordvale Heritage Department. This requirement applies regardless of land ownership, including private property. Any unauthorized activity discovered will result in immediate cessation orders and potential fines as outlined in section 25. A permit is specifically required for any activity that disturbs the ground to a depth greater than 10 centimeters over an area exceeding 10 square meters, or any systematic surface collection involving more than 5 distinct collection units, each larger than 1 square meter. Failure to secure the necessary permit before commencing work is a serious infraction.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for archaeological permits must be submitted to the Nordvale Heritage Department at least 90 days prior to the proposed commencement date of the work. Each application must include a detailed project proposal, a curriculum vitae of the principal archaeologist, a financial plan demonstrating sufficient resources, and proof of public liability insurance covering at least 500,000 crowns. An application fee of 500 crowns is required for all new submissions. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days, with a detailed explanation of missing components, and the 90-day processing period will restart upon resubmission of a complete application.

heading: Application Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Nordvale Heritage Department will review the proposal within 60 days. This review includes an assessment of the project's scientific merit, the archaeological significance of the proposed site, and the qualifications of the project team. The Department may consult with up to three external experts if the project is deemed to be of exceptional scale or complexity. A site visit may be conducted by Department officials, requiring 7 days' advance notice to the applicant. The Director will make a final decision on the permit application within 30 days following the completion of the review process, including any consultations or site visits.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text:
(1) An archaeological permit, if granted, is valid for a maximum period of 12 months from the date of issue. 
(2) A permit holder may apply for a renewal of an existing permit by submitting a renewal application at least 60 days before the current permit's expiry date. 
(3) Renewal applications must include a progress report, an updated project plan for the subsequent period, and a renewal fee of 300 crowns. 
(4) The Department will process renewal applications within 45 days. A permit may be renewed for a maximum of two consecutive 12-month periods, unless exceptional circumstances are demonstrated and approved by the Director.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) All archaeological activities must be supervised by a qualified archaeologist with at least 5 years of field experience.
(2) The permit holder must ensure that all archaeological remains are treated with due care and documented meticulously.
(3) The permit holder must submit weekly progress reports to the Nordvale Heritage Department via email by 17:00 every Friday during active fieldwork.
(4) Any significant discovery, defined as an artifact or feature of potentially national importance, must be reported to the Department within 24 hours of its finding.
(5) Access to the site must be granted to Department officials for inspection purposes with 48 hours' notice.
(6) A detailed conservation plan for all recovered artifacts must be submitted within 30 days of the permit's expiry or project completion, whichever comes first.

heading: Site Access and Landowner Consent
text:
(1) Applicants for a permit must provide written consent from the landowner for any proposed archaeological activity on private property. This consent must be current, dated within 3 months of the application, and explicitly state permission for the proposed scope and duration of work.
(2) For activities on public land, applicants must obtain written approval from the relevant municipal authority or the national land management agency, as applicable.
(3) Failure to provide proper landowner or authority consent will result in the immediate rejection of the permit application. The Department will not mediate disputes between applicants and landowners regarding access. Any permit granted without proper consent, if discovered later, shall be immediately revoked, and all associated work must cease.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Discoveries
text:
(1) The permit holder is obligated to report all archaeological discoveries, regardless of their perceived significance, to the Nordvale Heritage Department.
(2) For minor finds, a comprehensive list and basic description must be included in the monthly progress reports.
(3) For significant discoveries, as defined in section 7, an immediate preliminary report must be submitted within 24 hours of the find. This report should include location details, a preliminary description, and initial photographs. The Department may then request a site visit within 48 hours. Failure to report significant discoveries promptly may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns per unreported item or feature.

heading: Treatment of Human Remains
text:
(1) The discovery of human remains during archaeological activities requires immediate cessation of work in that specific area.
(2) The permit holder must notify the Nordvale Heritage Department and the local police authority within 6 hours of discovery. 
(3) No human remains shall be disturbed or removed until explicit written instructions are provided by the Department, in consultation with relevant cultural and forensic experts. 
(4) All human remains must be treated with the utmost respect and dignity. A specialized protocol for the excavation, analysis, and reburial or long-term curation of human remains will be provided by the Department upon notification. Violation of this section carries severe penalties, including immediate permit revocation and fines up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Artifact Curation
text:
(1) All archaeological artifacts recovered under a permit issued by this Act are the property of the Republic of Nordvale.
(2) The permit holder is responsible for the initial cleaning, conservation, and inventory of all recovered artifacts.
(3) A detailed inventory, including photographs and descriptions, must be submitted to the Nordvale Heritage Department within 90 days of the completion of fieldwork.
(4) All artifacts must be securely stored in suitable environmental conditions throughout the project duration. 
(5) Final curation of all artifacts will be at a designated national repository, as specified by the Department. The permit holder is responsible for the safe transfer of artifacts to this repository within 180 days of project completion, bearing all associated costs up to 2,000 crowns.

heading: Publication and Dissemination
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to publish the results of their archaeological work in a peer-reviewed academic journal or a report series approved by the Nordvale Heritage Department.
(2) A final project report, including full archaeological documentation, analysis, and conclusions, must be submitted to the Department within 24 months of the permit's expiry date.
(3) Failure to submit the final report within the stipulated timeframe may result in a penalty of 500 crowns per month of delay, up to a maximum of 6,000 crowns, and may prejudice future permit applications. 
(4) The Department also encourages public dissemination of findings through lectures, exhibitions, or online platforms, with a minimum of one public outreach event per project. All publications must acknowledge the Nordvale Heritage Department's permit.

heading: Confidentiality of Site Locations
text:
(1) The exact geographical coordinates and specific locations of sensitive archaeological sites, particularly those containing vulnerable remains or unexcavated deposits, shall be kept confidential.
(2) Permit holders are prohibited from publicly disclosing precise site locations without prior written approval from the Nordvale Heritage Department.
(3) This measure is implemented to prevent unauthorized disturbance, looting, or vandalism of significant cultural heritage. General descriptions of regions or broader areas are permissible for academic publications.
(4) Violation of this confidentiality clause may lead to immediate permit revocation and a fine of 5,000 crowns for each instance of unauthorized disclosure, in addition to potential legal action for damages to heritage sites.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) The Director may revoke an archaeological permit if the permit holder fails to comply with any section of this Act or any specific condition attached to the permit.
(2) Reasons for revocation may include, but are not limited to, significant deviations from the approved project plan, gross negligence in handling archaeological remains, failure to report significant finds, or consistent late submission of reports.
(3) Prior to revocation, the Department will issue a written warning, giving the permit holder 14 days to rectify the breach. If the breach is not rectified, the permit will be revoked, and all work must cease immediately. The permit holder has 30 days to appeal the decision to the Nordvale Heritage Council, whose decision is final.

heading: Suspension of Activities
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Department reserves the right to suspend archaeological activities temporarily if unforeseen circumstances arise that threaten the safety of personnel or the integrity of archaeological remains.
(2) Such circumstances may include severe weather conditions, discovery of hazardous materials, or unexpected structural instability at the site.
(3) A suspension order will be issued in writing, detailing the reasons and conditions for resuming work. The permit holder must comply immediately with all suspension directives. The Department will review the situation within 7 days and inform the permit holder of any necessary adjustments to the project plan or timeline. Refusal to comply with a suspension order may lead to permit revocation as per section 14.

heading: Safety Regulations
text:
(1) All archaeological activities must adhere to the national safety regulations applicable to excavation and fieldwork.
(2) The permit holder is responsible for ensuring a safe working environment for all personnel on site. This includes providing appropriate safety equipment, conducting daily safety briefings, and having a trained first-aid responder present at all times during active fieldwork.
(3) A detailed site-specific health and safety plan must be submitted as part of the permit application. The Department may request revisions to this plan if it is deemed insufficient. Non-compliance with safety regulations resulting in serious injury or death will lead to immediate permit revocation and potential legal proceedings.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text:
(1) The permit holder must establish and prominently display clear emergency procedures at the archaeological site.
(2) These procedures must include contact information for local emergency services (police, fire, ambulance), designated assembly points, and protocols for handling injuries or other incidents.
(3) All site personnel must be familiar with these emergency procedures, and drills should be conducted at least once per month during active fieldwork. A copy of the emergency plan must be provided to the Nordvale Heritage Department and local authorities prior to the commencement of work. Failure to have a readily accessible and comprehensive emergency plan may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns and a temporary suspension of activities.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) All permit holders must maintain comprehensive public liability insurance with coverage of no less than 500,000 crowns for the entire duration of the archaeological project.
(2) Proof of valid insurance must be submitted annually or upon renewal of the permit. The insurance policy must specifically cover risks associated with archaeological fieldwork, including damage to property and injury to third parties.
(3) The Nordvale Heritage Department must be named as an interested party on the insurance policy. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate permit suspension until valid proof of coverage is provided, and may lead to full revocation if not resolved within 14 days.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) All permit holders must maintain comprehensive public liability insurance with coverage of no less than 750,000 crowns for the entire duration of the archaeological project.
(2) Proof of valid insurance must be submitted annually or upon renewal of the permit. The insurance policy must specifically cover risks associated with archaeological fieldwork, including damage to property and injury to third parties.
(3) The Nordvale Heritage Department must be named as an interested party on the insurance policy. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate permit suspension until valid proof of coverage is provided, and may lead to full revocation if not resolved within 10 days.

heading: Indemnification
text: The permit holder shall indemnify and hold harmless the Republic of Nordvale, the Nordvale Heritage Department, and any associated municipal authorities from and against any and all claims, liabilities, damages, losses, costs, and expenses (including reasonable legal fees) arising out of or in connection with the permit holder's archaeological activities. This indemnification covers claims for property damage, personal injury, or death that occur during or as a result of the permitted activities. The permit holder assumes full responsibility for all actions and omissions of their personnel, contractors, and agents involved in the project. This clause remains in effect even after the completion of the project and the expiry of the permit.

heading: Research Moratorium
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Department may impose a temporary moratorium on archaeological activities in specific areas if significant new information or concerns about site integrity arise.
(2) A moratorium will be issued in writing, specifying the affected area, the reasons for the moratorium, and its expected duration, which will not exceed 6 months initially but may be extended for further 6-month periods.
(3) During a moratorium, no new permits will be issued for the affected area, and existing permits may be suspended or modified. Compensation for costs incurred due to such a moratorium will generally not be provided, unless exceptional circumstances are approved by the Nordvale Heritage Council, limited to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per project.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or a permit holder whose permit has been revoked or suspended, may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Heritage Council.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Council within 30 days of receiving the Department's decision, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation.
(3) The Council will convene a review panel within 45 days of receiving the appeal. The applicant or permit holder will be invited to present their case in person or via written submission. The Council's decision, reached within 15 days of the review panel meeting, is final and binding. No further appeals are available under this Act.

heading: Reporting of Damage
text:
(1) Any damage to archaeological remains, sites, or artifacts resulting from archaeological activities or external factors must be reported to the Nordvale Heritage Department within 12 hours of discovery.
(2) The report must include details of the damage, its presumed cause, and immediate remedial actions taken. The Department may dispatch an official to inspect the damage within 24 hours.
(3) If the damage is determined to be a direct result of the permit holder's negligence or failure to adhere to permit conditions, the permit holder will be responsible for all costs associated with repair, restoration, or mitigation, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns. Failure to report damage promptly may result in additional fines of 2,500 crowns per incident.

heading: Special Permits for Sensitive Sites
text:
(1) Archaeological sites designated as 'highly sensitive' due to their exceptional historical value, fragility, or unique nature require a 'Special Permit for Sensitive Sites'.
(2) Such designation is determined by the Nordvale Heritage Department. Applications for these special permits involve an extended review process of 120 days and require additional documentation, including a detailed risk assessment and a comprehensive conservation strategy.
(3) The application fee for a Special Permit is 1,500 crowns. Conditions for these permits are more stringent and may include continuous on-site monitoring by Department officials, strict limitations on equipment, and specific environmental controls, with daily reporting requirements.
(4) Only principal archaeologists with at least 10 years of experience in similar sensitive contexts are eligible to apply.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Department is authorized to monitor and inspect any archaeological site at any time, with or without prior notice.
(2) Department officials will carry official identification, which they will present upon arrival. Permit holders and their staff must grant full access to the site, all documentation, and recovered materials during inspections.
(3) Inspections are conducted to ensure compliance with this Act and the specific conditions of the permit. Any non-compliance observed may result in immediate corrective orders, temporary suspension of activities, or other enforcement actions as deemed appropriate by the inspecting official. Refusal to grant access for inspection will result in immediate permit suspension for 72 hours, followed by revocation if access is still denied.

heading: Interference with Activities
text:
(1) No person shall obstruct, hinder, or interfere with any archaeological activity being conducted by a duly authorized permit holder.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, unauthorized entry onto a permitted site, removal of artifacts, tampering with equipment, or intentional disruption of fieldwork. Any such interference should be reported immediately to the local police and the Nordvale Heritage Department.
(3) Individuals found to be in violation of this section may face fines of up to 10,000 crowns or other legal penalties as determined by a court of law. The permit holder may also seek civil remedies for any damages incurred due to such interference.

heading: Public Consultation for Major Projects
text:
(1) For archaeological projects covering an area greater than 5,000 square meters or projected to last longer than 18 months, the applicant must conduct a public consultation.
(2) This consultation must involve at least one public meeting in the nearest municipality, advertised in local newspapers at least 21 days in advance. The purpose is to inform local residents about the project's scope and potential impact.
(3) A summary of public feedback and how it has been addressed in the project plan must be included in the permit application. The Department will consider this feedback during its review. Failure to conduct the required consultation will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant for rectification.

heading: Public Consultation for Major Projects
text:
(1) For archaeological projects covering an area greater than 2,500 square meters or projected to last longer than 12 months, the applicant must conduct a public consultation.
(2) This consultation must involve at least two public meetings in the nearest municipality, advertised in local newspapers at least 30 days in advance. The purpose is to inform local residents about the project's scope and potential impact and gather feedback.
(3) A detailed report on public feedback and how it has been incorporated or addressed in the revised project plan must be included in the permit application. The Department will give significant weight to this feedback during its review. Failure to conduct the required consultation, or to adequately address public concerns, will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant for rectification.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) The application fee for a standard archaeological excavation permit is 500 crowns.
(2) The application fee for an archaeological survey permit is 250 crowns.
(3) A permit renewal fee is 300 crowns.
(4) Fees for special permits, expedited reviews, or specific technical assessments will be determined by the Nordvale Heritage Department on a case-by-case basis, not exceeding 2,000 crowns, and will be communicated to the applicant in advance. All fees are non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the permit application or any subsequent revocation. Payments must be made in full at the time of submission via approved methods.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) The application fee for a standard archaeological excavation permit is 750 crowns.
(2) The application fee for an archaeological survey permit is 350 crowns.
(3) A permit renewal fee is 400 crowns.
(4) Fees for special permits, expedited reviews, or specific technical assessments will be determined by the Nordvale Heritage Department on a case-by-case basis, not exceeding 3,000 crowns, and will be communicated to the applicant in advance. All fees are non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the permit application or any subsequent revocation. Payments must be made in full at the time of submission via approved methods.

heading: Expedited Review
text:
(1) An applicant may request an expedited review of a permit application in cases of urgent or time-sensitive projects, such as those related to imminent construction or development activities.
(2) An expedited review reduces the standard review period from 60 days to 30 days. This service incurs an additional fee of 1,000 crowns, payable at the time of application.
(3) Approval for expedited review is at the sole discretion of the Director and is not guaranteed. The Director will assess the urgency and justification provided by the applicant. Expedited review does not guarantee permit approval, only a faster processing time. If the request is denied, the expedited review fee will be refunded, and the application will proceed through the standard review process.

heading: Penalties for Unauthorized Activity
text:
(1) Any person or entity found conducting archaeological excavations or surveys without a valid permit will be subject to a fine of not less than 15,000 crowns and not more than 50,000 crowns for the first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 100,000 crowns, and may include seizure of equipment and mandatory restoration of the affected site at the offender's expense. The Nordvale Heritage Department may also pursue civil action for damages to archaeological heritage.
(3) All archaeological remains unlawfully recovered will be confiscated and become the property of the Republic of Nordvale without compensation. The Department may also prohibit the responsible parties from applying for future permits for a period of up to 5 years.

heading: Penalties for Unauthorized Activity
text:
(1) Any person or entity found conducting archaeological excavations or surveys without a valid permit will be subject to a fine of not less than 20,000 crowns and not more than 75,000 crowns for the first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 150,000 crowns, and may include seizure of equipment and mandatory restoration of the affected site at the offender's expense. The Nordvale Heritage Department may also pursue civil action for damages to archaeological heritage.
(3) All archaeological remains unlawfully recovered will be confiscated and become the property of the Republic of Nordvale without compensation. The Department may also prohibit the responsible parties from applying for future permits for a period of up to 10 years.

heading: Special categories
text: The bicycle registration fee is reduced by 25 percent for any person who has been the registered keeper of a listed windmill for at least one year.

heading: Special categories
text: For a registered violin maker, the annual registration fee for each vehicle in their hire fleet is 5 crowns instead of the standard 15 crowns.

heading: Meaning of operator authorisation prolongation
text:
(1) In every Act, "operator authorisation prolongation" means extending, for a new term of validity, an expiring document that entitles its holder to drive motor vehicles of one or more categories.
(2) Where an Act states an amount for an operator authorisation prolongation, that amount is the charge for the extension.

heading: Quayside lodging for honorary wardens
text:
(1) An honorary fellowship warden pays half of the quayside lodging tariff for at most 10 overnight stays in a calendar year.
(2) The halving is applied after any other reduction of that tariff.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the regulation and permitting of hydroponic farming operations throughout the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to promote sustainable agricultural practices, ensure public health and safety, and maintain environmental integrity. This Act applies to all individuals, businesses, and organizations engaged in the cultivation of plants using hydroponic methods, regardless of scale or commercial intent. It sets out the requirements for obtaining and maintaining permits, outlines inspection procedures, and details the responsibilities of permit holders within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Hydroponic farming" means the cultivation of plants in nutrient-rich water solutions, without soil.
(b) "Permit" means a Hydroponic Farming Permit issued under section 3 of this Act.
(c) "Permit holder" means an individual or entity granted a Permit.
(d) "Regulating authority" means the Nordvale Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security.
(e) "Small-scale operation" means a hydroponic farming setup with a cultivation area not exceeding 20 square meters.
(f) "Large-scale operation" means a hydroponic farming setup with a cultivation area exceeding 20 square meters.

heading: Permit requirement
text:
(1) Any person or entity intending to establish or operate a hydroponic farming operation within Nordvale must first obtain a valid Permit from the Regulating Authority.
(2) Operating a hydroponic farm without a Permit is strictly prohibited and may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. This requirement applies to all operations, whether commercial or non-commercial, exceeding a minimum cultivation area of 5 square meters. Operations below this threshold are exempt from the permit requirement but must still adhere to general health and safety regulations.

heading: Application for permit
text:
(1) An application for a Permit must be submitted to the Regulating Authority in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The applicant's full legal name and contact information.
(b) The precise location of the proposed hydroponic farming operation, including a site plan.
(c) A detailed description of the hydroponic system, including its size, water source, and nutrient management plan.
(d) Proof of ownership or legal right to occupy the premises.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns.

heading: Application for permit
text:
(1) An application for a Permit must be submitted to the Regulating Authority in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The applicant's full legal name and contact information.
(b) The precise location of the proposed hydroponic farming operation, including a detailed site plan.
(c) A detailed description of the hydroponic system, including its size, water source, nutrient management plan, and proposed waste disposal methods.
(d) Proof of ownership or legal right to occupy the premises for a minimum of 2 years.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns.

heading: Application for permit
text:
(1) An application for a Permit must be submitted to the Regulating Authority through its online portal.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The applicant's full legal name, contact information, and Nordvale national identification number.
(b) The precise location of the proposed hydroponic farming operation, including a detailed site plan certified by a licensed surveyor.
(c) A comprehensive description of the hydroponic system, including its size, water source analysis, nutrient management plan, and proposed waste disposal and recycling methods.
(d) Proof of ownership or legal right to occupy the premises for a minimum of 3 years.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 350 crowns.

heading: Eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a Permit, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 18 years of age.
(b) Not have any outstanding fines or penalties related to agricultural violations within Nordvale for the past 5 years.
(c) Demonstrate access to a reliable and safe water supply.
(d) Propose an operation that complies with all local zoning and building codes. The Regulating Authority may request additional documentation to verify compliance with these criteria during the application review process.

heading: Permit review and approval
text:
(1) The Regulating Authority will review complete Permit applications within 60 days of receipt.
(2) During the review period, the Regulating Authority may conduct a site visit to assess the proposed operation.
(3) A Permit will be issued if the Regulating Authority determines that the applicant meets all eligibility criteria and the proposed operation complies with the provisions of this Act. The Regulating Authority will provide written notification of its decision within 7 days of the decision being made.

heading: Permit review and approval
text:
(1) The Regulating Authority will review complete Permit applications within 45 days of receipt.
(2) During the review period, the Regulating Authority will conduct a mandatory site visit to assess the proposed operation.
(3) A Permit will be issued if the Regulating Authority determines that the applicant meets all eligibility criteria and the proposed operation complies with the provisions of this Act and all relevant environmental protection guidelines. The Regulating Authority will provide written notification of its decision, including reasons for approval or denial, within 5 days of the decision being made.

heading: Permit duration and renewal
text:
(1) A Permit is valid for a period of 3 years from its date of issue.
(2) A Permit holder may apply for renewal no earlier than 90 days and no later than 30 days before the Permit's expiry date.
(3) The renewal application must include a renewal fee of 150 crowns and a declaration confirming continued compliance with all relevant regulations. Failure to renew within the specified timeframe will result in the Permit expiring, requiring a new application process.

heading: Permit duration and renewal for small-scale operations
text:
(1) For small-scale operations, a Permit is valid for a period of 5 years from its date of issue.
(2) A Permit holder may apply for renewal no earlier than 120 days and no later than 60 days before the Permit's expiry date.
(3) The renewal application must include a renewal fee of 100 crowns and a declaration confirming continued compliance with all relevant regulations. Small-scale operations benefit from a longer permit validity to reduce administrative burden.

heading: Transfer of permits
text:
(1) A Permit is generally non-transferable.
(2) In exceptional circumstances, such as the sale of an established hydroponic farming business, a Permit may be transferred with the prior written approval of the Regulating Authority.
(3) An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current Permit holder and the proposed new Permit holder, accompanied by a transfer fee of 500 crowns. The new applicant must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in section 5. The Regulating Authority retains the right to deny any transfer request without providing specific reasons.

heading: Conditions of permit
text:
(1) Every Permit is subject to the following conditions:
(a) The Permit holder must operate the hydroponic farm in accordance with the plans submitted in the application.
(b) The Permit holder must maintain accurate records of nutrient usage, water consumption, and crop yields for a minimum of 2 years.
(c) The Permit holder must allow authorized inspectors access to the premises during regular business hours for compliance checks.
(d) The Permit holder must notify the Regulating Authority of any significant changes to the operation within 30 days.

heading: Water quality standards
text:
(1) All water used in hydroponic farming operations must meet the minimum quality standards set by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency for agricultural use.
(2) Permit holders are required to conduct water quality testing at least once every 6 months and submit the results to the Regulating Authority. The testing must include pH levels, conductivity, and levels of heavy metals. Records of these tests must be kept on site for inspection for a period of 3 years. Any deviation from prescribed standards must be reported within 24 hours.

heading: Nutrient management
text:
(1) Permit holders must implement a nutrient management plan designed to prevent the discharge of excess nutrients into the environment.
(2) The plan must detail the types and quantities of nutrients used, storage procedures, and disposal methods for spent nutrient solutions. All nutrient solutions must be stored in secure, leak-proof containers away from water sources. Disposal of spent solutions must follow approved environmental guidelines to prevent contamination of local ecosystems. Records of nutrient purchases and disposal must be maintained for 2 years.

heading: Waste disposal
text:
(1) All waste generated by hydroponic farming operations, including plant matter, packaging, and spent growing media, must be disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner.
(2) Permit holders must have a waste management plan that includes recycling or composting options where feasible. Disposal of hazardous waste materials, such as certain nutrient residues, must be conducted by licensed waste disposal services. Records of waste disposal, including receipts from certified waste management companies, must be retained for at least 1 year.

heading: Pest and disease management
text:
(1) Permit holders must implement appropriate pest and disease management strategies to prevent outbreaks.
(2) The use of pesticides and fungicides must comply with the Nordvale Agricultural Chemical Regulations. Integrated Pest Management (IPM) practices are strongly encouraged. Records of all pesticide and fungicide applications, including product name, application rate, and date, must be kept for a minimum of 1 year. Any significant pest or disease outbreak must be reported to the Regulating Authority within 72 hours.

heading: Structural requirements
text:
(1) All structures used for hydroponic farming must be sound, safe, and comply with the Nordvale Building Code.
(2) This includes adequate ventilation systems, proper electrical installations, and safe access for workers. Structures must be designed to withstand local weather conditions, including wind speeds up to 100 kilometers per hour. Regular maintenance checks, at least annually, are required to ensure structural integrity and operational safety. Any significant structural damage must be reported to the Regulating Authority within 48 hours.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain comprehensive records of their operations.
(2) These records must include:
(a) Permit documentation and renewal certificates.
(b) Water quality test results.
(c) Nutrient purchase and disposal logs.
(d) Waste disposal manifests.
(e) Pest and disease management logs, including chemical applications.
(f) Production data, including planting and harvesting dates and yields. All records must be kept for a minimum of 2 years and be available for inspection upon request.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit an annual report to the Regulating Authority by January 31st each year.
(2) The annual report must summarize:
(a) Total water consumption in cubic meters.
(b) Total nutrient usage in kilograms.
(c) Total waste generated and disposed of.
(d) Any significant operational changes or incidents.
(e) An update on compliance with environmental standards. The report helps the Regulating Authority monitor overall trends and ensure ongoing compliance with this Act.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit an annual report to the Regulating Authority by December 15th each year.
(2) The annual report must summarize:
(a) Total water consumption in cubic meters, categorized by source.
(b) Total nutrient usage in kilograms, broken down by chemical type.
(c) Total waste generated and disposed of, specifying quantities sent for recycling, composting, or landfill.
(d) Any significant operational changes or incidents, including mitigation efforts.
(e) A detailed update on compliance with environmental standards and any challenges encountered. This report will be subject to a compliance audit by the Regulating Authority.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit an annual report to the Regulating Authority through the online portal by November 30th each year.
(2) The annual report must summarize:
(a) Total water consumption in cubic meters, categorized by source, with efficiency metrics.
(b) Total nutrient usage in kilograms, broken down by chemical type, with a nutrient balance analysis.
(c) Total waste generated and disposed of, specifying quantities sent for recycling, composting, or landfill, and any innovative waste reduction strategies.
(d) Any significant operational changes or incidents, including detailed mitigation efforts and outcomes.
(e) A comprehensive update on compliance with environmental standards, any challenges encountered, and proposed improvements for the coming year. Failure to submit this report by the deadline will incur a late fee of 100 crowns per week.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Regulating Authority may conduct scheduled or unscheduled inspections of any permitted hydroponic farming operation.
(2) Inspections will be carried out by authorized personnel to verify compliance with the conditions of the Permit and the provisions of this Act. Permit holders must grant inspectors full access to all areas of the operation and provide any requested documentation. At least one inspection will be conducted within the first 12 months of a Permit being issued. Refusal to allow an inspection may lead to Permit suspension.

heading: Correction of deficiencies
text:
(1) If an inspection reveals any deficiencies or non-compliance, the Regulating Authority will issue a written notice to the Permit holder.
(2) The notice will specify the deficiencies, the required corrective actions, and a deadline for completion, typically 30 days. The Permit holder must rectify the deficiencies and provide evidence of compliance by the specified deadline. Failure to correct deficiencies within the given timeframe may result in further enforcement actions, including fines or Permit suspension. An extension may be granted in extenuating circumstances, not exceeding an additional 15 days.

heading: Suspension of permit
text:
(1) The Regulating Authority may suspend a Permit if the Permit holder:
(a) Fails to comply with a notice to correct deficiencies within the specified timeframe.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in their application or reports.
(c) Operates the hydroponic farm in a manner that poses a significant risk to public health or the environment.
(d) Fails to pay the annual permit fee for more than 60 days. A suspended Permit renders the operation illegal, and activities must cease immediately.

heading: Revocation of permit
text:
(1) The Regulating Authority may revoke a Permit if:
(a) The Permit holder fails to remedy the grounds for suspension within 90 days of the suspension.
(b) The Permit holder commits repeated or serious violations of this Act.
(c) The operation is found to be causing severe and irreversible environmental damage.
(d) The Permit holder ceases operation for more than 180 consecutive days without notifying the Regulating Authority. Revocation is a permanent measure, and a new application would be required to resume operations.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person whose application for a Permit has been denied, or whose Permit has been suspended or revoked, may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for challenging the decision and include any supporting documentation. The Board will review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.

heading: Fees
text:
(1) The following fees apply under this Act:
(a) Application fee: 250 crowns (non-refundable).
(b) Renewal fee: 150 crowns.
(c) Transfer fee: 500 crowns.
(d) Annual permit maintenance fee: 100 crowns, payable by March 1st each year. All fees are designed to cover the administrative costs associated with processing applications, renewals, transfers, and conducting oversight. Failure to pay any fee by its due date may result in penalties, including Permit suspension.

heading: Fees
text:
(1) The following fees apply under this Act:
(a) Application fee: 300 crowns (non-refundable).
(b) Renewal fee: 175 crowns.
(c) Transfer fee: 600 crowns.
(d) Annual permit maintenance fee: 120 crowns, payable by February 15th each year. All fees are subject to review every 3 years and may be adjusted to reflect changes in administrative costs or inflation. A late payment fee of 25 crowns per month will be applied to overdue annual maintenance fees.

heading: Penalties for operating without a permit
text:
(1) Any person or entity found operating a hydroponic farming operation without a valid Permit is liable to a fine of 1,000 crowns for a first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 2,500 crowns and may result in the mandatory cessation of operations. The Regulating Authority may also order the removal of all hydroponic equipment at the operator's expense. Each day of continued operation without a Permit constitutes a separate offense. This is to ensure compliance and deter illegal operations.

heading: Penalties for operating without a permit
text:
(1) Any person or entity found operating a hydroponic farming operation without a valid Permit is liable to a fine of 1,500 crowns for a first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 3,500 crowns and may result in the mandatory cessation of operations and confiscation of all hydroponic equipment. The Regulating Authority may also seek recovery of any profits gained from the illegal operation. Each week of continued operation without a Permit constitutes a separate, escalating offense. Repeat offenders may face legal action beyond monetary penalties.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance with conditions
text:
(1) A Permit holder who fails to comply with any condition of their Permit or any provision of this Act, after receiving a notice of deficiency, may be subject to a fine of 300 crowns for a first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses for the same violation will incur a fine of 700 crowns. The Regulating Authority may also impose additional conditions on the Permit or shorten its validity period. These penalties are in addition to any other enforcement actions, such as suspension or revocation, as outlined in sections 20 and 21.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All information provided by applicants and Permit holders will be treated with confidentiality by the Regulating Authority.
(2) Information will only be disclosed as required by law or with the express written consent of the Permit holder. This includes operational details, financial information, and personal data. Aggregate statistical data, however, may be used for policy analysis and public reporting, provided individual operations cannot be identified. The Regulating Authority maintains strict data protection protocols to safeguard sensitive information.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Small-scale non-commercial hydroponic setups with a total cultivation area of less than 5 square meters are exempt from the Permit requirement.
(2) These exempt operations must still adhere to general health, safety, and environmental protection regulations applicable in Nordvale. The Regulating Authority may, at its discretion, provide guidance to these exempt operations upon request. The exemption is intended to avoid unnecessary regulatory burdens on hobbyist growers who do not engage in commercial activity.

heading: Exemptions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Regulating Authority may make regulations prescribing anything that is required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed.
(2) These regulations may include:
(a) Specific technical standards for hydroponic systems.
(b) Detailed reporting forms and procedures.
(c) Guidelines for water and nutrient waste disposal.
(d) Any other matter necessary for the effective administration of this Act. Regulations will be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 30 days before their effective date to allow for public review and comment.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) The Regulating Authority will conduct a comprehensive review of this Act every 5 years.
(2) The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose, identify any areas for improvement, and consider technological advancements in hydroponic farming. Stakeholders, including Permit holders and environmental groups, will be invited to provide input during the review process. The first review is scheduled to commence on January 1, 2023. Any proposed amendments will follow standard legislative procedures.

heading: Commencement
text:
(1) This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018.
(2) All hydroponic farming operations established prior to this date must apply for a Permit within 180 days of the commencement date to avoid penalties. The Regulating Authority will prioritize applications from existing operations during this initial transition period to ensure a smooth implementation of the new regulatory framework. Public awareness campaigns will be launched in all municipalities to inform citizens of these new requirements well in advance.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: (1) If a person is a licensed taxidermist, (2) the annual trail pass payment due date for that person is extended by 30 days.

heading: Payment terms
text: Each certified wine taster pays no annual energy rebate.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for environmental impact assessment fees within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that the costs associated with evaluating the environmental consequences of proposed projects are fairly distributed and recovered. The scope of this Act extends to all projects requiring an environmental impact assessment as determined by the Ministry of Environmental Protection, encompassing a wide range of developments across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. These fees contribute to the resources necessary for thorough and impartial assessments, safeguarding Nordvale’s natural heritage and promoting sustainable development practices for future generations.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Project Proponent' refers to any individual, corporation, or entity proposing a development that necessitates an environmental impact assessment.
(2) 'Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)' signifies the process of evaluating the likely environmental impacts of a proposed project, including the preparation of a report detailing these impacts.
(3) 'Ministry' refers to the Nordvale Ministry of Environmental Protection.
(4) 'Small-scale Project' denotes a project with a total estimated construction cost of less than 5,000,000 crowns and an area disturbance of less than 2,500 square meters.
(5) 'Large-scale Project' denotes a project with a total estimated construction cost of 25,000,000 crowns or more and an area disturbance of 10,000 square meters or more.

heading: General Fee Principle
text: All project proponents, as defined in subsection (1) of section 2, are responsible for paying fees associated with their environmental impact assessments. This principle ensures that the financial burden of the assessment process does not fall solely upon the public purse, but is instead borne by those initiating projects that may have significant environmental consequences. The fees cover administrative costs, expert reviews, public consultations, and monitoring activities related to the assessment process. The specific amounts and payment schedules are detailed in subsequent sections of this Act, ensuring transparency and predictability for all stakeholders involved in development projects across Nordvale.

heading: Application Fee for Initial Review
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required for the initial screening and review of any project proposal to determine if an Environmental Impact Assessment is necessary.
