(2) The application form, available on the NEPA website, must be completed in full and accompanied by all required documentation, including safety data sheets for all materials. 
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must be paid at the time of submission.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a hazardous material transport permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency at least 45 days prior to the planned transport date. 
(2) The application form, available on the NEPA website, must be completed in full and accompanied by all required documentation, including safety data sheets for all materials. 
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns must be paid at the time of submission.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) Applicants must provide proof of vehicle registration and valid insurance coverage for hazardous material transport, with a minimum liability of 1,000,000 crowns. 
(2) Details of the planned route, including all municipalities to be traversed such as Dunmere and Elsby, must be included. 
(3) A copy of the driver’s hazardous materials endorsement for their license is mandatory. 
(4) An emergency response plan must also be submitted, detailing procedures for incidents.

heading: Vehicle Requirements
text:
(1) All vehicles used for hazardous material transport must be inspected and certified by a Nordvale-approved inspection facility within the last 12 months. 
(2) Vehicles must display appropriate hazardous material placards on all four sides, visible from at least 20 meters away. 
(3) Transport vehicles must be equipped with at least two 10-kilogram fire extinguishers and spill containment kits capable of handling 200 liters of liquid.

heading: Vehicle Requirements
text:
(1) All vehicles used for hazardous material transport must be inspected and certified by a Nordvale-approved inspection facility within the last 6 months. 
(2) Vehicles must display appropriate hazardous material placards on all four sides, visible from at least 30 meters away. 
(3) Transport vehicles must be equipped with at least three 10-kilogram fire extinguishers and spill containment kits capable of handling 250 liters of liquid.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text:
(1) Drivers must be at least 21 years of age. 
(2) Drivers must possess a valid Nordvale commercial driver's license with a hazardous materials endorsement. 
(3) Drivers must complete a certified hazardous materials safety training program every 24 months. 
(4) A clean driving record for the past 36 months, with no more than 2 minor traffic violations, is required.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text:
(1) Drivers must be at least 23 years of age. 
(2) Drivers must possess a valid Nordvale commercial driver's license with a hazardous materials endorsement. 
(3) Drivers must complete a certified hazardous materials safety training program every 18 months. 
(4) A clean driving record for the past 48 months, with no more than 1 minor traffic violation, is required.

heading: Permit Issuance
text: The Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency will issue a permit within 20 business days of receiving a complete and satisfactory application. The permit will specify the hazardous materials authorized for transport, the approved routes, and any special conditions or restrictions. Permits are valid for a single transport journey or for a period not exceeding 12 months for repeated transport.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A standard hazardous material transport permit is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance. For single-trip permits, the validity period will be specified on the permit, not exceeding 30 days. Permits must be renewed before their expiration to maintain compliance. There will be no grace period for expired permits; transport with an expired permit is considered unpermitted.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A standard hazardous material transport permit is valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issuance. For single-trip permits, the validity period will be specified on the permit, not exceeding 45 days. Permits must be renewed before their expiration to maintain compliance. There will be no grace period for expired permits; transport with an expired permit is considered unpermitted.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) Applications for permit renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the current permit's expiration date. 
(2) The renewal application requires an updated set of all documentation and a renewal fee of 300 crowns. 
(3) NEPA reserves the right to request new vehicle inspections or driver training certificates if circumstances have changed or if safety concerns arise.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) The initial permit application fee is 500 crowns. 
(2) The annual renewal fee for a multi-trip permit is 300 crowns. 
(3) A single-trip permit fee is 200 crowns. 
(4) Expedited processing, reducing the application time to 10 business days, is available for an additional fee of 700 crowns. All fees are non-refundable and payable to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) The initial permit application fee is 600 crowns. 
(2) The annual renewal fee for a multi-trip permit is 350 crowns. 
(3) A single-trip permit fee is 250 crowns. 
(4) Expedited processing, reducing the application time to 7 business days, is available for an additional fee of 900 crowns. All fees are non-refundable and payable to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.

heading: Categorization of Hazardous Materials
text:
(1) Hazardous materials are categorized into three classes: Class A (High Risk), Class B (Medium Risk), and Class C (Low Risk). 
(2) Class A materials include explosives and highly toxic gases. 
(3) Class B includes flammable liquids and corrosive substances. 
(4) Class C includes irritating substances and certain environmental hazards. The specific classification of each material will determine the transport requirements and restrictions.

heading: Class A Material Requirements
text:
(1) Transport of Class A materials requires two certified drivers per vehicle, operating in shifts. 
(2) Vehicles must be equipped with real-time GPS tracking accessible by NEPA at all times. 
(3) Transport is restricted to designated routes only, avoiding population centers with more than 10,000 residents. 
(4) A police escort may be required for quantities exceeding 500 kilograms, decided on a case-by-case basis by the authorities.

heading: Class B Material Requirements
text:
(1) Transport of Class B materials requires one certified driver. 
(2) Vehicles must carry a communications device capable of immediate contact with emergency services. 
(3) Routes must avoid sensitive environmental areas, such as nature reserves or water sources, to the extent practicable. 
(4) For quantities exceeding 1,000 liters, a secondary containment system is mandatory for liquid transport.

heading: Class C Material Requirements
text:
(1) Transport of Class C materials requires one driver with standard hazardous materials certification. 
(2) Vehicles must be equipped with basic safety equipment, including first aid kits and appropriate personal protective equipment. 
(3) No specific route restrictions apply, but transporters are encouraged to use efficient routes. 
(4) For quantities exceeding 2,000 kilograms, a manifest must be carried detailing contents.

heading: Route Planning and Approval
text:
(1) All proposed transport routes for Class A and Class B hazardous materials must be submitted to and approved by NEPA. 
(2) Routes must minimize exposure to densely populated areas, schools, and hospitals. 
(3) Alternative routes for emergencies must also be identified and submitted. 
(4) Changes to approved routes require prior notification and approval, at least 48 hours in advance, unless in an emergency.

heading: Route Planning and Approval
text:
(1) All proposed transport routes for Class A, Class B, and Class C hazardous materials must be submitted to and approved by NEPA. 
(2) Routes must minimize exposure to densely populated areas, schools, and hospitals, avoiding areas with more than 5,000 inhabitants. 
(3) Alternative routes for emergencies must also be identified and submitted. 
(4) Changes to approved routes require prior notification and approval, at least 72 hours in advance, unless in an emergency.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text:
(1) Every transporter must have a detailed emergency response plan outlining procedures for spills, accidents, and other incidents involving hazardous materials. 
(2) The plan must include contact information for local emergency services, such as the Fennick Fire Department and Grauby Police. 
(3) It must also detail spill containment and cleanup procedures, personal protective equipment requirements, and communication protocols. 
(4) The plan must be reviewed and updated annually.

heading: Spill Reporting
text:
(1) Any spill or accidental release of hazardous materials exceeding 1 liter of liquid or 1 kilogram of solid must be reported immediately to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency and local emergency services. 
(2) Reports must be made within 15 minutes of discovery. 
(3) A detailed written report must follow within 24 hours, describing the incident, materials involved, and actions taken. 
(4) Failure to report promptly may result in significant fines.

heading: Spill Reporting
text:
(1) Any spill or accidental release of hazardous materials exceeding 0.5 liters of liquid or 0.5 kilograms of solid must be reported immediately to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency and local emergency services. 
(2) Reports must be made within 10 minutes of discovery. 
(3) A detailed written report must follow within 12 hours, describing the incident, materials involved, and actions taken. 
(4) Failure to report promptly may result in significant fines.

heading: Container and Packaging Standards
text:
(1) All hazardous materials must be transported in containers and packaging that comply with Nordvale's national safety standards, as published by the Ministry of Transport. 
(2) Containers must be clearly labeled with the material's name, hazard class, and appropriate warning symbols, readable from 5 meters. 
(3) Packaging must be robust enough to withstand normal transport conditions and minor impacts, capable of withstanding a drop from 1.2 meters without rupture.

heading: Loading and Unloading Procedures
text:
(1) Loading and unloading of hazardous materials must be conducted in designated areas, away from public access, at least 10 meters from any building. 
(2) Personnel involved in these operations must wear appropriate personal protective equipment, including safety goggles and chemical-resistant gloves. 
(3) Vehicles must be properly secured and grounded during transfer operations to prevent accidental movement or static discharge. 
(4) A supervisor must be present during all Class A material transfers.

heading: Inspection Authority
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency and Nordvale police have the authority to conduct random inspections of vehicles transporting hazardous materials. 
(2) These inspections may occur at any point along the approved route or at designated checkpoints. 
(3) Transporters must provide all requested documentation, including permits, manifests, and driver licenses, within 5 minutes of the request. 
(4) Refusal to cooperate with an inspection may lead to immediate permit suspension.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Transporters must maintain detailed records of all hazardous material shipments for a minimum of 36 months. 
(2) These records must include dates of transport, materials transported, quantities, routes taken, and any incidents that occurred. 
(3) Records must be made available to NEPA upon request within 48 hours. 
(4) Digital records are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and readily retrievable.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Transporters must maintain detailed records of all hazardous material shipments for a minimum of 60 months. 
(2) These records must include dates of transport, materials transported, quantities, routes taken, and any incidents that occurred. 
(3) Records must be made available to NEPA upon request within 24 hours. 
(4) Digital records are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and readily retrievable.

heading: Training Requirements
text:
(1) All personnel involved in the handling or transport of hazardous materials must undergo certified training every 24 months. 
(2) This training must cover hazardous material identification, emergency procedures, safety protocols, and regulatory compliance. 
(3) Proof of training completion must be kept with the personnel and accessible during working hours. 
(4) New hires must complete initial training within 30 days of employment.

heading: Signage and Labeling
text:
(1) All containers and vehicles transporting hazardous materials must display clear and legible warning signs and labels. 
(2) Labels must conform to Nordvale's national standards for hazard communication and be resistant to weather conditions for at least 12 months. 
(3) Vehicle placards must be at least 25 cm by 25 cm in size and visible from all sides. 
(4) Labels must indicate the primary and secondary hazards of the material.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) Information submitted by applicants for permits, including proprietary business details and specific routes, will be treated with appropriate confidentiality by NEPA. 
(2) This information will only be disclosed to relevant government agencies for safety and regulatory purposes. 
(3) Any requests for information from external parties will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's public information access policies. 
(4) NEPA maintains secure digital and physical storage for all submitted documents.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Small quantities of hazardous materials, specifically those less than 25 kilograms or 25 liters, are exempt from permit requirements, provided they are packaged and labeled according to safety guidelines. 
(2) Materials transported for personal use, in quantities not exceeding 5 kilograms or 5 liters, are also exempt. 
(3) Emergency response vehicles carrying hazardous materials for immediate response purposes are exempt. 
(4) Scientific research samples, under 1 kilogram, are also exempt if properly secured.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Small quantities of hazardous materials, specifically those less than 10 kilograms or 10 liters, are exempt from permit requirements, provided they are packaged and labeled according to safety guidelines. 
(2) Materials transported for personal use, in quantities not exceeding 2 kilograms or 2 liters, are also exempt. 
(3) Emergency response vehicles carrying hazardous materials for immediate response purposes are exempt. 
(4) Scientific research samples, under 0.5 kilograms, are also exempt if properly secured.

heading: Temporary Permits
text:
(1) Temporary permits may be issued for unforeseen or urgent transport needs, valid for a maximum of 7 days. 
(2) The application for a temporary permit must demonstrate immediate necessity and include a simplified emergency plan. 
(3) A temporary permit fee of 400 crowns applies. 
(4) No more than two temporary permits may be issued to the same transporter within a 90-day period. 
(5) These permits are typically processed within 24 hours.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) A permit may be revoked by NEPA if the transporter fails to comply with any provision of this Act or the conditions of the permit. 
(2) Serious violations, such as a major spill due to negligence, will result in immediate revocation. 
(3) The transporter will be notified in writing of the revocation and the reasons for it, with a 10-day period to appeal. 
(4) Revoked permits render all hazardous material transport by that entity illegal.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any applicant or transporter whose permit application is denied or whose permit is revoked may appeal the decision. 
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the NEPA Appeals Board within 15 days of receiving the decision. 
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 30 days. 
(4) The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. 
(5) A non-refundable appeal fee of 200 crowns is required.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity transporting hazardous materials without a valid permit is subject to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for the first offense. 
(2) Subsequent offenses may incur fines up to 25,000 crowns and seizure of the offending vehicle. 
(3) Violations of permit conditions, such as unauthorized routes or improper labeling, may result in fines from 1,000 to 5,000 crowns. 
(4) Serious violations leading to environmental damage will incur additional penalties.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity transporting hazardous materials without a valid permit is subject to a fine of up to 15,000 crowns for the first offense. 
(2) Subsequent offenses may incur fines up to 40,000 crowns and seizure of the offending vehicle. 
(3) Violations of permit conditions, such as unauthorized routes or improper labeling, may result in fines from 2,000 to 7,500 crowns. 
(4) Serious violations leading to environmental damage will incur additional penalties.

heading: Environmental Damage Penalties
text:
(1) In cases where hazardous material transport results in environmental damage, the responsible party will be liable for all cleanup and restoration costs. 
(2) This includes damages to land, water, and air quality. 
(3) Additional fines of up to 50,000 crowns may be imposed, depending on the severity and extent of the damage. 
(4) NEPA will assess the damage and determine the appropriate restitution. 
(5) Failure to pay these penalties within 90 days may result in further legal action.

heading: Public Safety Measures
text:
(1) Transporters must ensure that their operations do not endanger public safety. 
(2) This includes maintaining safe distances from residential areas during loading/unloading and avoiding transport during peak public activity times in areas like Lund Vale. 
(3) Public notification may be required for large-scale hazardous material movements, with details provided to local authorities 48 hours in advance. 
(4) The transport of certain highly dangerous materials may be restricted to specific hours, for example, between 1:00 AM and 5:00 AM.

heading: Coordination with Municipalities
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency will coordinate with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and other affected areas regarding hazardous material transport routes and emergency plans. 
(2) Municipalities have the right to request adjustments to routes within their jurisdiction for specific local safety concerns. 
(3) Local police forces are authorized to assist in enforcement of this Act within their municipal boundaries. 
(4) NEPA will host quarterly meetings with municipal representatives.

heading: Reporting Requirements for NEPA
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency shall publish an annual report detailing hazardous material transport activities. 
(2) This report will include statistics on permits issued, incidents reported, and enforcement actions taken. 
(3) The report will be made publicly available on the NEPA website by March 31st of each year. 
(4) Specific permit holder details will remain confidential, only aggregated data will be published. 
(5) This promotes transparency and informs public discourse.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every five years from its effective date. The first review will occur no later than 2023-01-01. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the regulations, address emerging hazardous material concerns, and incorporate best practices. Public consultation will be a part of the review process, with feedback periods lasting at least 60 days.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every three years from its effective date. The first review will occur no later than 2023-01-01. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the regulations, address emerging hazardous material concerns, and incorporate best practices. Public consultation will be a part of the review process, with feedback periods lasting at least 90 days.

heading: International Agreements
text: Where a hazardous material transport involves crossing Nordvale's borders, this Act shall be applied in conjunction with any relevant international agreements or treaties to which Nordvale is a signatory. In cases of conflict, the stricter regulation designed to ensure public safety and environmental protection shall prevail. Transporters are responsible for understanding and adhering to both national and international requirements, particularly when dealing with neighboring nations.

heading: Amendment Procedures
text:
(1) Any amendment to this Act must be proposed by a member of the Nordvale Parliament and undergo a full legislative process. 
(2) Public consultation periods of at least 45 days will be held for all significant proposed amendments. 
(3) Amendments will take effect 90 days after their official publication in the Nordvale Gazette, unless otherwise specified. 
(4) NEPA will issue guidance documents for any new or revised sections within 60 days of their effective date.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency is the primary enforcement authority for this Act. 
(2) NEPA investigators are granted powers to inspect vehicles, demand documentation, and issue compliance orders. 
(3) The Nordvale Police Force is authorized to assist NEPA in enforcement activities, including stopping vehicles and impounding those found in serious violation. 
(4) All enforcement actions are subject to the oversight of the Nordvale courts. 
(5) Enforcement personnel must carry valid identification.

heading: Protection of Whistleblowers
text:
(1) Any individual who reports a violation of this Act in good faith shall be protected from retaliation by their employer or any other party. 
(2) Employers are prohibited from taking adverse employment action, such as dismissal or demotion, against a whistleblower. 
(3) Violations of this protection will result in fines of up to 20,000 crowns and potential legal action. 
(4) Reports can be made anonymously through a dedicated NEPA hotline.

heading: Cooperation with Industry
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency will foster cooperation with the hazardous materials transport industry to promote best practices and ensure compliance. 
(2) Regular workshops and informational sessions will be held at least twice a year to disseminate information and gather feedback. 
(3) NEPA will establish a voluntary compliance program, offering reduced initial inspection frequency for companies with demonstrated excellent safety records over 36 consecutive months. 
(4) This collaborative approach aims to enhance overall safety standards.

heading: Cost Recovery
text:
(1) Any costs incurred by NEPA or other government agencies due to non-compliance with this Act, including inspection costs, cleanup expenses, or emergency response efforts, shall be recoverable from the responsible party. 
(2) An administrative fee of 10% will be added to all recovered costs. 
(3) NEPA will issue an invoice detailing all recoverable expenses, which must be paid within 60 days. 
(4) Unpaid invoices may lead to additional interest charges at 5% per month.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of a provision of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a competent court, the remaining provisions of this Act shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of other sections. This ensures that the core purpose of regulating hazardous material transport is maintained even if minor parts are legally challenged.

heading: Jurisdiction
text: All legal proceedings related to this Act shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Nordvale court system. Cases will typically be heard in the municipal court where the alleged violation occurred, or in the capital's superior court for matters of significant national importance. The decisions of these courts shall be binding. Appeals must follow established Nordvale judicial procedures. This centralizes legal oversight.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into full force and effect on January 1, 2018. All permits issued prior to this date under previous regulations will remain valid until their natural expiration, but renewal will be subject to the provisions of this Act. Transporters are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the new requirements well in advance of the effective date to ensure continuous compliance.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) For a period of 6 months following the effective date of this Act, minor non-compliance issues will be addressed with warnings rather than immediate fines, provided there is no immediate threat to public safety. 
(2) Transporters with existing permits must submit an updated emergency response plan within 90 days of the effective date. 
(3) NEPA will conduct informational workshops during this period to assist with the transition. 
(4) All new applications must fully comply from day one.

heading: Relationship to Other Regulations
text: This Act operates in conjunction with, and does not supersede, other Nordvale environmental protection regulations or general traffic laws. Where there is an overlap, the more stringent requirement shall apply to ensure maximum safety and environmental protection. For example, local speed limits must still be obeyed even if a hazardous materials route suggests faster travel time. Compliance with this Act does not exempt from other legal obligations.

heading: Mandatory Insurance
text:
(1) All transporters of hazardous materials must maintain valid third-party liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 1,000,000 crowns for Class B and C materials, and 2,000,000 crowns for Class A materials. 
(2) Proof of insurance must be provided with the permit application and carried in the transport vehicle at all times. 
(3) Insurance policies must cover environmental damage and personal injury arising from hazardous material incidents. 
(4) Failure to maintain valid insurance will result in immediate permit suspension.

heading: Mandatory Insurance
text:
(1) All transporters of hazardous materials must maintain valid third-party liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 1,500,000 crowns for Class B and C materials, and 3,000,000 crowns for Class A materials. 
(2) Proof of insurance must be provided with the permit application and carried in the transport vehicle at all times. 
(3) Insurance policies must cover environmental damage and personal injury arising from hazardous material incidents. 
(4) Failure to maintain valid insurance will result in immediate permit suspension.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency will periodically conduct public awareness campaigns to inform residents about hazardous material transport safety, emergency procedures, and how to report concerns. These campaigns will utilize public service announcements, online resources, and community meetings in municipalities like Aldmark and Lund Vale. The goal is to enhance public understanding and trust in the safety measures implemented by this Act.

heading: Reporting to International Bodies
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reporting to International Bodies
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Electronic Permit System
text:
(1) NEPA will implement an electronic permit application and tracking system by 2023-01-01. 
(2) This system will allow for online submission of applications, payment of fees, and real-time permit status checks. 
(3) Digital permits will be accepted as valid proof of authorization, viewable on mobile devices. 
(4) A dedicated support team will be available during business hours, 08:00 to 17:00, to assist users with the new system. 
(5) This initiative aims to streamline the process.

heading: Concessions
text: No late filing surcharge is payable by an accredited sign-language interpreter for the first 30 days following the due date of the annual statement.

heading: Exemptions
text: No certificate of completion fee is payable by a registered stonemason of a protected monument for more than half of the total amount.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a registered calligrapher, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle shall be 15 crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act provides allowances that help households and persons meet the costs of energy, heating, home working, children's clothing and broadband.
(2) Each section of this Act states whether its allowance is paid per household or per person; an allowance that a section gives to "every household" or to "a household" is paid per household.
(3) A grant under this Act is an allowance; an increase under MRA §5 is added after the maximum amount of the grant is applied.

heading: Applicants
text:
(1) An allowance paid per household is claimed by one adult member of the household on behalf of the household.
(2) An allowance paid per person or per employee is claimed by that person, or for a child by a parent.
(3) Only one claim for a per-household allowance is paid for each household and period.

heading: Claims
text:
(1) A claim for an allowance under this Act is made within 6 months after the end of the period it covers.
(2) A claim made later than that is refused.
(3) Allowances are paid into the bank account named in the claim.

heading: Heating support
text:
(1) A household with an annual income below 30,000 crowns receives heating support of 35 crowns per month for the months November to March.
(2) Heating support is paid per household.

heading: Heating support
text:
(1) A household with an annual income below 30,000 crowns receives heating support of 40 crowns per month for the months November to March.
(2) Heating support is paid per household.

heading: Home office allowance
text:
(1) An employee who works from home receives an allowance of 2 crowns for each full working day worked from home.
(2) The allowance is paid for at most 220 days in a calendar year.
(3) The allowance is paid per employee, not per household.

heading: Energy rebate
text:
(1) Every household receives an annual energy rebate of 300 crowns.
(2) The rebate is paid in January.

heading: Energy rebate
text:
(1) Every household receives an annual energy rebate of 350 crowns.
(2) The rebate is paid in January.

heading: Child clothing allowance
text:
(1) A parent receives a child clothing allowance of 100 crowns per year for each child under 16 years of age.
(2) The allowance is paid in August.
(3) The allowance is paid per child, not per household.

heading: Child clothing allowance
text:
(1) A parent receives a child clothing allowance of 120 crowns per year for each child under 16 years of age.
(2) The allowance is paid in August.
(3) The allowance is paid per child, not per household.

heading: School start allowance
text:
(1) A parent receives a school start allowance of 60 crowns for each child who starts the first school year.
(2) The allowance is paid once per child, in August.
(3) The allowance is paid per child, not per household.

heading: Broadband support
text:
(1) A household whose residence cannot get a fixed internet connection of at least 100 megabits per second receives broadband support of 10 crowns per month towards a mobile data subscription.
(2) Broadband support is paid per household.

heading: Broadband support
text:
(1) A household whose residence cannot get a fixed internet connection of at least 100 megabits per second receives broadband support of 12 crowns per month towards a mobile data subscription.
(2) Broadband support is paid per household.

heading: Commuting allowance in small municipalities
text:
(1) An employee whose residence is in a small municipality and who travels more than 30 kilometres one way to work receives a commuting allowance of 25 crowns per month.
(2) The allowance is paid per employee, not per household.

heading: Water bill rebate
text:
(1) Every household receives an annual water bill rebate of 50 crowns.
(2) The rebate is paid in March.
(3) The rebate is paid per household.

heading: Water bill rebate
text:
(1) Every household receives an annual water bill rebate of 60 crowns.
(2) The rebate is paid in March.
(3) The rebate is paid per household.

heading: Large family supplement
text:
(1) A household in which at least 3 children under 18 years of age live receives a large family supplement of 180 crowns per year.
(2) The supplement is paid in February.
(3) The supplement is paid per household.

heading: Pensioner heating supplement
text:
(1) A person aged 67 or older receives a heating supplement of 15 crowns per month for the months November to March.
(2) The supplement is paid in addition to heating support under section 4.
(3) The supplement is paid per person, not per household.

heading: Television licence rebate
text:
(1) Every household receives an annual television licence rebate of 20 crowns.
(2) The rebate is paid per household.

heading: Television licence rebate
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Appliance replacement grant
text:
(1) A household that replaces a refrigerator or washing machine with an energy-efficient model receives a grant of 30 percent of the purchase price, at most 150 crowns.
(2) A household receives at most one grant under this section in any period of 5 years.
(3) The grant is paid per household.

heading: Home insulation grant
text:
(1) A household that insulates the walls or roof of its residence receives a grant of 40 percent of the cost, at most 1,200 crowns.
(2) The grant is paid per household.

heading: Home insulation grant
text:
(1) A household that insulates the walls or roof of its residence receives a grant of 35 percent of the cost, at most 1,000 crowns.
(2) The grant is paid per household.

heading: Heat pump grant
text:
(1) A household that installs an electric heat pump in its residence receives a grant of 25 percent of the cost, at most 900 crowns.
(2) A household that receives a grant under section 16 for the same works receives no grant under this section.
(3) The grant is paid per household.

heading: Moving allowance for job seekers
text:
(1) A person who moves more than 50 kilometres to take up a job lasting at least 6 months receives a moving allowance of 200 crowns.
(2) The allowance is paid once in any period of 3 years.
(3) The allowance is paid per person, not per household.

heading: Rounding
text:
(1) An allowance under this Act is rounded to the nearest whole crown.
(2) An amount of exactly half a crown is rounded up.

heading: Recovery of allowances
text:
(1) An allowance paid without entitlement is repaid within 60 days of the repayment notice.
(2) An allowance paid per household is repaid by the member who claimed it.

heading: Grants under the Energy Efficiency Grants Act
text:
(1) A grant under section 16 or section 17 and a grant under the Energy Efficiency Grants Act for the same works are both paid in full; neither grant reduces or excludes the other.
(2) A grant under this Act does not count towards the maximum total of grants for one dwelling in ENA §16.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for the permitting process of rainwater harvesting systems within the Republic of Nordvale. It outlines the requirements for obtaining, maintaining, and renewing permits, ensuring sustainable water management practices across all municipalities. The Act aims to promote the efficient collection and utilization of rainwater, contributing to water conservation efforts and reducing reliance on municipal water supplies. All systems, whether for domestic or commercial use, that collect and store rainwater for non-potable purposes are subject to the provisions of this Act.

heading: Definitions
text: For the purposes of this Act: (a) 'Harvesting System' means any structure or device designed to collect, store, and distribute rainwater from a surface, typically a rooftop. (b) 'Permit' refers to the official authorization issued by the Nordvale Environmental Agency allowing the installation and operation of a rainwater harvesting system. (c) 'Agency' means the Nordvale Environmental Agency, responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. (d) 'Applicant' means an individual, business, or organization applying for a permit. (e) 'Non-potable use' means water used for purposes other than drinking, cooking, or personal hygiene, such as irrigation, toilet flushing, or laundry.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person shall install, operate, or modify a rainwater harvesting system within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Agency. This requirement applies to all systems with a storage capacity exceeding 200 liters. Systems with a capacity of 200 liters or less are exempt from the permit requirement but must still adhere to general safety and health guidelines established by the Agency. Failure to comply with this section may result in penalties as outlined in section 30.

heading: Application submission
text: An applicant for a rainwater harvesting permit must submit a complete application form to the Agency, either online or in person at any municipal office. The application must include detailed plans of the proposed system, including its location, design specifications, storage capacity, and intended uses of the harvested water. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days with a list of deficiencies.

heading: Application review period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Agency shall review the submission within 30 business days. During this period, the Agency may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no additional information is requested, or if the requested information is provided, the Agency will issue a decision to approve or deny the permit. The 30-day period may be extended by an additional 15 business days if complex engineering assessments are required, with prior notification to the applicant.

heading: Permit approval criteria
text: The Agency shall approve a permit application if the proposed rainwater harvesting system meets all technical specifications and safety standards outlined in Agency regulations. Key criteria include structural integrity, appropriate sizing for runoff collection, proper filtration mechanisms, and clear labeling for non-potable use. The system must also demonstrate a minimal risk of contamination to potable water supplies and not impede public access or safety on the property. All components must be certified by an accredited Nordvale standards body.

heading: Permit approval criteria - revised
text: The Agency shall approve a permit application if the proposed rainwater harvesting system meets all technical specifications and safety standards outlined in Agency regulations. Key criteria include structural integrity, appropriate sizing for runoff collection, proper filtration mechanisms, and clear labeling for non-potable use. The system must also demonstrate a minimal risk of contamination to potable water supplies and not impede public access or safety on the property. All components must be certified by an accredited Nordvale standards body. Additionally, for systems exceeding 5,000 liters, a detailed hydrological impact assessment must be submitted and approved.

heading: Permit denial grounds
text: A permit application may be denied if the proposed system fails to meet any of the criteria specified in section 6, if the application is incomplete or contains false information, or if the installation of the system would violate any other municipal or national building codes or environmental regulations. Applicants will be provided with a written explanation for the denial, detailing the specific reasons and outlining any deficiencies that can be rectified. An applicant may reapply after addressing the identified issues.

heading: Permit denial grounds - updated
text: A permit application may be denied if the proposed system fails to meet any of the criteria specified in section 6, if the application is incomplete or contains false information, or if the installation of the system would violate any other municipal or national building codes or environmental regulations. Furthermore, applications for systems intended for installation within 50 meters of a protected natural water source will be automatically denied. Applicants will be provided with a written explanation for the denial, detailing the specific reasons and outlining any deficiencies that can be rectified. An applicant may reapply after addressing the identified issues.

heading: Permit fee
text: Upon approval of a permit, the applicant must pay a permit issuance fee of 1,500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with issuing the permit and conducting an initial inspection. The permit will not be officially issued until this fee is paid in full. Payments can be made via electronic transfer, credit card, or in person at Agency offices. No permit will be valid until the fee is confirmed received by the Agency. This fee is separate from the non-refundable application fee.

heading: Permit fee - adjusted
text: Upon approval of a permit, the applicant must pay a permit issuance fee of 1,800 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with issuing the permit and conducting an initial inspection. The permit will not be officially issued until this fee is paid in full. Payments can be made via electronic transfer, credit card, or in person at Agency offices. No permit will be valid until the fee is confirmed received by the Agency. This fee is separate from the non-refundable application fee.

heading: Permit fee - further adjusted
text: Upon approval of a permit, the applicant must pay a permit issuance fee of 2,200 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with issuing the permit and conducting an initial inspection. The permit will not be officially issued until this fee is paid in full. Payments can be made via electronic transfer, credit card, or in person at Agency offices. No permit will be valid until the fee is confirmed received by the Agency. This fee is separate from the non-refundable application fee.

heading: Permit validity period
text: A rainwater harvesting permit is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. Permitholders are responsible for ensuring that their systems remain compliant with all relevant regulations throughout this period. Prior to the expiry date, permitholders will receive a notification from the Agency, typically 90 days in advance, reminding them to initiate the renewal process. Failure to renew a permit will result in its expiration and potential enforcement actions if the system continues to operate.

heading: Permit validity period - extended
text: A rainwater harvesting permit is valid for a period of 7 years from the date of issuance. Permitholders are responsible for ensuring that their systems remain compliant with all relevant regulations throughout this period. Prior to the expiry date, permitholders will receive a notification from the Agency, typically 120 days in advance, reminding them to initiate the renewal process. Failure to renew a permit will result in its expiration and potential enforcement actions if the system continues to operate.

heading: Permit renewal process
text: To renew a permit, the permitholder must submit a renewal application to the Agency at least 60 days before the current permit's expiry. The renewal application must include a declaration that the system remains in good working order and complies with all current regulations. A renewal fee of 750 crowns is required. The Agency may, at its discretion, request an inspection of the system before approving the renewal. Renewals submitted less than 30 days before expiry may incur a late fee of 200 crowns.

heading: Permit renewal process - revised
text: To renew a permit, the permitholder must submit a renewal application to the Agency at least 90 days before the current permit's expiry. The renewal application must include a declaration that the system remains in good working order and complies with all current regulations, along with photographic evidence of key components. A renewal fee of 900 crowns is required. The Agency may, at its discretion, request an inspection of the system before approving the renewal. Renewals submitted less than 60 days before expiry may incur a late fee of 300 crowns.

heading: System inspection
text: The Agency reserves the right to conduct inspections of permitted rainwater harvesting systems at any reasonable time, with prior notice of at least 5 business days, to ensure compliance with this Act and associated regulations. Inspections may be routine or initiated in response to a complaint. Permitholders must provide safe access for Agency inspectors. If an inspection reveals non-compliance, the permitholder will be issued a notice of violation and given 30 days to rectify the issues.

heading: System inspection - enhanced
text: The Agency reserves the right to conduct inspections of permitted rainwater harvesting systems at any reasonable time, with prior notice of at least 10 business days for routine inspections. Inspections may be routine or initiated in response to a complaint. Permitholders must provide safe access for Agency inspectors and have all system documentation readily available. If an inspection reveals non-compliance, the permitholder will be issued a notice of violation and given 20 days to rectify the issues, with a mandatory follow-up inspection within 45 days.

heading: Maintenance requirements
text: Permitholders are responsible for the proper maintenance of their rainwater harvesting systems to ensure their efficient and safe operation. This includes regular cleaning of collection surfaces, filters, and storage tanks. Maintenance records must be kept for a minimum of 3 years and made available to the Agency upon request. Any damage or malfunction that could compromise water quality or system integrity must be repaired promptly, ideally within 14 days of discovery. Failure to maintain the system adequately may lead to permit revocation.

heading: Water quality standards
text: All harvested rainwater intended for non-potable indoor uses, such as toilet flushing or laundry, must meet minimum water quality standards as set forth by the Nordvale Health Authority. These standards include limits on total suspended solids and microbial contaminants. Regular testing, at least annually, is recommended for systems used indoors, and records of these tests should be kept. While not for potable use, the Agency emphasizes the importance of preventing any cross-contamination with the municipal potable water supply.

heading: System modifications
text: Any significant modification to a permitted rainwater harvesting system, such as increasing its storage capacity by more than 20% or changing its primary use, requires a new permit application. Minor repairs or replacements of components with equivalent specifications do not require a new permit but should be documented by the permitholder. Permitholders must notify the Agency in writing of any modifications exceeding 10% of the original system's footprint or capacity within 30 days of completion.

heading: System modifications - stricter
text: Any significant modification to a permitted rainwater harvesting system, such as increasing its storage capacity by more than 15% or changing its primary use, requires a new permit application. Minor repairs or replacements of components with equivalent specifications do not require a new permit but should be documented by the permitholder. Permitholders must notify the Agency in writing of any modifications exceeding 5% of the original system's footprint or capacity within 15 days of completion. Failure to comply may lead to a penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Permit transferability
text: A rainwater harvesting permit is generally transferable to a new property owner upon sale of the property, provided the new owner applies for a transfer of ownership within 60 days of the property transaction. The new owner must submit a transfer request form and pay a transfer fee of 300 crowns. The Agency will review the request and may require an inspection to ensure the system remains compliant. If no transfer is applied for, the permit will become void 90 days after the property sale.

heading: Permit transferability - modified
text: A rainwater harvesting permit is generally transferable to a new property owner upon sale of the property, provided the new owner applies for a transfer of ownership within 30 days of the property transaction. The new owner must submit a transfer request form and pay a transfer fee of 450 crowns. The Agency will review the request and may require an inspection to ensure the system remains compliant. If no transfer is applied for, the permit will become void 60 days after the property sale.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text: Permitholders must report any significant incidents involving their rainwater harvesting system to the Agency within 24 hours of discovery. Such incidents include, but are not limited to, contamination of the stored water, structural failure of the collection or storage components, or any event that poses a risk to public health or safety. A detailed written report must follow the initial notification within 7 days. Failure to report incidents promptly may result in fines or permit suspension.

heading: Emergency provisions
text: In the event of a national or regional water emergency, the Agency may issue temporary directives regarding the operation or use of rainwater harvesting systems. These directives may include restrictions on water usage, mandatory reporting of stored volumes, or temporary cessation of system operation to prioritize specific water management strategies. Permitholders are required to comply with all such emergency directives immediately upon notification, for the duration specified by the Agency. Non-compliance during an emergency carries severe penalties.

heading: Appeals process
text: An applicant or permitholder may appeal a decision made by the Agency within 21 days of receiving written notification of that decision. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal of the Nordvale Environmental Agency, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any supporting documentation. The Appeals Tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 45 days. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final.

heading: Appeals process - revised
text: An applicant or permitholder may appeal a decision made by the Agency within 14 days of receiving written notification of that decision. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal of the Nordvale Environmental Agency, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any supporting documentation. A non-refundable appeal fee of 1,000 crowns must accompany the submission. The Appeals Tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final.

heading: Enforcement actions
text: The Agency is authorized to take enforcement actions against any person found to be in violation of this Act or its associated regulations. Enforcement actions may include issuing warnings, imposing administrative fines, suspending permits, or revoking permits. In cases of severe or repeated non-compliance, the Agency may also initiate legal proceedings to compel compliance or recover damages. All enforcement actions will be documented and communicated to the affected party in writing within 10 business days.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text: Any person who installs or operates a rainwater harvesting system without a valid permit, or who fails to comply with a condition of their permit, is liable to an administrative fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses may incur fines of up to 10,000 crowns and may lead to the permanent revocation of all related permits. For each day an unpermitted system operates, a daily fine of 200 crowns may be imposed after an initial warning period of 7 days.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance - increased
text: Any person who installs or operates a rainwater harvesting system without a valid permit, or who fails to comply with a condition of their permit, is liable to an administrative fine of up to 7,500 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses may incur fines of up to 15,000 crowns and may lead to the permanent revocation of all related permits. For each day an unpermitted system operates, a daily fine of 300 crowns may be imposed after an initial warning period of 5 days.

heading: Public awareness and education
text: The Agency shall develop and implement public awareness campaigns and educational programs to inform the citizens of Nordvale about the benefits of rainwater harvesting and the requirements of this Act. These programs will provide guidance on best practices for system installation, operation, and maintenance, and will be accessible through various media, including online resources, community workshops, and informational brochures available at municipal offices. The goal is to encourage voluntary adoption and compliance.

heading: Grants and incentives
text: The Nordvale government may offer grants or other financial incentives to encourage the installation of rainwater harvesting systems that exceed minimum requirements or serve public benefit. These incentives may include partial rebates on permit fees, tax credits, or subsidies for specific high-efficiency components. Details of such programs, including eligibility criteria and application procedures, will be published annually by the Nordvale Department of Finance in consultation with the Agency. Currently, a 10% rebate on system costs up to 2,000 crowns is available for residential systems in Dunmere.

heading: Grants and incentives - updated
text: The Nordvale government may offer grants or other financial incentives to encourage the installation of rainwater harvesting systems that exceed minimum requirements or serve public benefit. These incentives may include partial rebates on permit fees, tax credits, or subsidies for specific high-efficiency components. Details of such programs, including eligibility criteria and application procedures, will be published annually by the Nordvale Department of Finance in consultation with the Agency. Currently, a 15% rebate on system costs up to 3,000 crowns is available for residential systems in Dunmere, Elsby, and Grauby.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text: Information submitted as part of a permit application or during inspections shall be treated as confidential by the Agency, subject to the provisions of Nordvale's public information access laws. Personal details of applicants and proprietary system designs will not be disclosed to third parties without express written consent, except where required for legal enforcement or public safety purposes. Aggregated and anonymized data on rainwater harvesting trends may be used for statistical reporting and policy development.

heading: Record keeping by Agency
text: The Agency shall maintain comprehensive records of all permit applications, issued permits, inspection reports, enforcement actions, and appeals decisions. These records shall be securely stored for a minimum of 10 years and be readily retrievable for auditing or review purposes. Digital records must be backed up weekly, and physical records stored in a fire-resistant facility. This ensures transparency and accountability in the administration of this Act and facilitates long-term data analysis regarding water management in Nordvale.

heading: Reporting to Parliament
text: The Agency shall submit an annual report to the Parliament of Nordvale on the implementation and effectiveness of this Act. The report will include statistics on the number of permits issued, renewals, denials, and enforcement actions taken across all municipalities. It will also provide an overview of water conservation achievements attributable to rainwater harvesting and recommend any necessary amendments to this Act or related regulations to improve its functionality and reach. The report is due by 31 March each year.

heading: Consultation with municipalities
text: The Agency shall consult with the municipal councils of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale at least twice annually regarding the local impacts and administration of this Act. These consultations will address specific municipal concerns, discuss local implementation challenges, and seek input on potential policy adjustments. Such collaboration ensures that the Act is responsive to diverse local conditions and promotes effective coordination between national and local governance structures.

heading: Review of regulations
text: The Agency shall undertake a comprehensive review of all regulations made under this Act every 3 years. This review will assess the regulations' continued relevance, effectiveness, and alignment with best practices in water management. Stakeholder input from permitholders, environmental groups, and industry experts will be actively solicited during the review process. Any proposed changes to the regulations will be published for public comment for at least 60 days before finalization. The first review is scheduled for 2021.

heading: Review of regulations - revised
text: The Agency shall undertake a comprehensive review of all regulations made under this Act every 2 years. This review will assess the regulations' continued relevance, effectiveness, and alignment with best practices in water management. Stakeholder input from permitholders, environmental groups, and industry experts will be actively solicited during the review process, with at least two public forums held in different municipalities. Any proposed changes to the regulations will be published for public comment for at least 90 days before finalization. The next review is scheduled for 2028.

heading: Funding for Agency operations
text: The operational costs of the Agency related to the administration of this Act shall be primarily covered by an annual allocation from the national budget of Nordvale. Supplementing these funds, a maximum of 25% of the total revenue generated from application, permit, and renewal fees may be directly allocated to Agency activities, including staff salaries, equipment, and public outreach programs. Any surplus funds from fees will be directed to the Nordvale Water Conservation Fund.

heading: Public access to information
text: Subject to section 24, the public has the right to access general information pertaining to the number of permits issued, the locations of permitted systems (excluding specific addresses for residential properties), and aggregate data on harvested water volumes. This information will be made available on the Agency's official website and in its annual reports. Requests for specific, non-confidential data points can be made in writing and will be processed within 15 business days.

heading: Liability of permitholders
text: Permitholders are solely responsible for any damage, injury, or adverse environmental impact resulting from the installation, operation, or maintenance of their rainwater harvesting system. The issuance of a permit by the Agency does not imply endorsement of the system's design or absolve the permitholder of their liability. Permitholders are strongly advised to obtain adequate insurance coverage to protect against potential liabilities associated with their systems.

heading: Regulations by the Agency
text: The Agency may make regulations prescribing: (a) further technical standards for rainwater harvesting systems; (b) specific health and safety requirements for different uses of harvested water; (c) procedures for inspections and enforcement actions; (d) forms for applications, permits, and reports; and (e) any other matter necessary for the effective administration of this Act. All proposed regulations must undergo public consultation for a minimum of 45 days before being enacted.

heading: Regulations by the Agency - expanded
text: The Agency may make regulations prescribing: (a) further technical standards for rainwater harvesting systems, including minimum material quality and installation guidelines; (b) specific health and safety requirements for different uses of harvested water, including mandatory warning labels; (c) detailed procedures for inspections, enforcement actions, and appeals; (d) forms for applications, permits, reports, and incident notifications; (e) criteria for granting financial incentives; and (f) any other matter necessary for the effective administration of this Act. All proposed regulations must undergo public consultation for a minimum of 60 days before being enacted.

heading: Permit revocation
text: The Agency may revoke a permit if a permitholder: (a) fails to comply with any provision of this Act or its regulations; (b) provides false or misleading information in an application or report; (c) fails to rectify a notice of violation within the specified timeframe; or (d) operates a system that poses an imminent threat to public health or the environment. Before revocation, the permitholder will be issued a written notice of intent to revoke, allowing 30 days to provide reasons against revocation.

heading: Permit suspension
text: The Agency may suspend a permit for a period not exceeding 90 days if a permitholder: (a) fails to maintain their system as required by section 14; (b) fails to report an incident as required by section 18; or (c) is found to be in minor non-compliance that does not pose an immediate threat. During a suspension, the permitholder must cease all collection and use of rainwater. The suspension will be lifted once all deficiencies are corrected and verified by an Agency inspection, at the permitholder's expense (500 crowns).

heading: Permit suspension - adjusted
text: The Agency may suspend a permit for a period not exceeding 60 days if a permitholder: (a) fails to maintain their system as required by section 14; (b) fails to report an incident as required by section 18; or (c) is found to be in minor non-compliance that does not pose an immediate threat. During a suspension, the permitholder must cease all collection and use of rainwater. The suspension will be lifted once all deficiencies are corrected and verified by an Agency inspection, at the permitholder's expense (800 crowns), within 14 days of remediation.

heading: Exemptions for research purposes
text: The Agency may grant specific exemptions from certain provisions of this Act for rainwater harvesting systems used solely for scientific research or educational purposes, provided such systems do not pose a risk to public health or the environment. Applicants for such exemptions must submit a detailed research proposal, outlining the project's objectives, duration, and safety protocols. These exemptions are granted on a case-by-case basis and are subject to annual review by the Agency. An exemption fee of 100 crowns may apply.

heading: Exemptions for research purposes - revised
text: The Agency may grant specific exemptions from certain provisions of this Act for rainwater harvesting systems used solely for scientific research or educational purposes by accredited institutions, provided such systems do not pose a significant risk to public health or the environment. Applicants for such exemptions must submit a detailed research proposal, outlining the project's objectives, duration, safety protocols, and a risk assessment. These exemptions are granted for a maximum of 3 years and are subject to annual reporting requirements by the Agency. An exemption fee of 250 crowns applies.

heading: Transition period for existing systems
text: Owners of rainwater harvesting systems installed and operational prior to the effective date of this Act have a transition period of 12 months to apply for a permit. During this transition period, existing systems are deemed to have a temporary permit, provided they register their system with the Agency within 6 months of this Act coming into force. Systems registered within this initial 6-month window will receive a 50% discount on the permit issuance fee. Failure to register or apply for a permit within the transition period will result in standard penalties.

heading: Transition period for existing systems - extended
text: Owners of rainwater harvesting systems installed and operational prior to the effective date of this Act have a transition period of 18 months to apply for a permit. During this transition period, existing systems are deemed to have a temporary permit, provided they register their system with the Agency within 9 months of this Act coming into force. Systems registered within this initial 9-month window will receive a 75% discount on the permit issuance fee. Failure to register or apply for a permit within the transition period will result in standard penalties.

heading: Delegation of authority
text: The Director of the Agency may delegate any of their powers or duties under this Act to any employee of the Agency, provided such delegation is in writing and specifies the scope of the delegated authority. A copy of any such delegation must be publicly accessible on the Agency's website. However, the power to revoke permits as outlined in section 33 cannot be delegated below the level of a senior manager within the Agency, ensuring a high level of oversight for serious decisions.

heading: Cooperation with other agencies
text: The Agency shall cooperate with the Nordvale Department of Health, the Nordvale Building Authority, and other relevant government agencies to ensure a coordinated approach to water management and public safety. This cooperation may involve sharing data, conducting joint inspections, and developing integrated guidelines. Memoranda of Understanding will be established between the Agency and these bodies to formalize collaboration protocols and delineate responsibilities, especially concerning potential cross-contamination risks.

heading: Amendments to schedules
text: The Minister responsible for the Agency may, by order, amend any schedule appended to this Act. Such amendments may include updates to fee structures, technical specifications for systems, or lists of certified components. Any proposed amendment to a schedule must be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before its effective date, allowing for public notification. This ensures flexibility in adapting to new technologies and economic conditions without requiring a full legislative amendment.

heading: Repeal of previous Acts
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Effectiveness and commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018. All provisions of this Act are effective from this date, and any applications for rainwater harvesting systems submitted prior to this date will be processed according to the provisions of this Act. Public announcements regarding the commencement of this Act were made in all major Nordvale newspapers and on national radio channels for a period of 90 days leading up to its effective date, ensuring broad public awareness.

heading: Interpretation
text: This Act shall be interpreted in a manner that promotes sustainable water resource management, protects public health, and encourages innovation in rainwater harvesting technologies. Where there is any ambiguity, preference shall be given to interpretations that support the environmental objectives of the Republic of Nordvale and ensure the long-term viability of water resources for all citizens. The Agency may issue interpretative guidance documents to clarify provisions of this Act, which will be published online.

heading: Reduced charges
text: No dog licence fee is payable by a registered seed bank curator for at least one year, for one quarter of the payable fee.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) If a person is a registered glassblower, (2) they shall have an additional thirty days to pay any fee or allowance specified in FIA §4.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants by the government of Nordvale to support the preservation, restoration, and ongoing maintenance of properties deemed to hold significant cultural or historical heritage value within the Republic. The grants aim to ensure that these valuable assets are protected for future generations, contributing to the nation's identity and educational resources. This Act applies to all heritage properties as defined in section 2, regardless of their ownership status, provided they meet the eligibility criteria outlined herein. The objective is to safeguard properties that reflect Nordvale's rich past, encouraging both public and private efforts in their upkeep.

heading: Definition of Heritage Property
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a 'heritage property' means any building, structure, or site that has been officially designated by the National Heritage Council as being of outstanding historical, architectural, or cultural significance to Nordvale.
(2) Such designation is based on criteria including, but not limited to, age, architectural style, association with significant events or persons, and rarity. A property must be at least 75 years old to be considered for designation, although exceptions may be made for properties of exceptional significance that are at least 50 years old.
(3) The designation process requires a public consultation period of at least 60 days, allowing for community input before a final decision is made.

heading: Establishment of the Heritage Grants Fund
text:
(1) A fund, to be known as the Heritage Grants Fund, is hereby established to provide the financial resources for grants awarded under this Act.
(2) The fund shall be administered by the Ministry of Culture and Heritage and shall receive its primary funding through annual appropriations from the national budget of Nordvale.
(3) Additional contributions may be received from private donations, endowments, and other sources, all of which shall be directed exclusively to the purposes of this fund. The fund will maintain an annual minimum balance of 2,000,000 crowns for grant disbursements.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text:
(1) Any owner of a designated heritage property may apply for a grant under this Act.
(2) Eligible applicants include private individuals, non-profit organizations, and municipal authorities. Commercial entities are eligible if the property is publicly accessible for at least 150 days per year.
(3) Applicants must demonstrate legal ownership or a long-term lease (minimum 25 years) of the heritage property at the time of application and for the duration of the grant project. Failure to meet these basic criteria will result in immediate disqualification of the application.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
text:
(1) Any owner of a designated heritage property may apply for a grant under this Act.
(2) Eligible applicants include private individuals, non-profit organizations, and municipal authorities. Commercial entities are eligible if the property is publicly accessible for at least 180 days per year.
(3) Applicants must demonstrate legal ownership or a long-term lease (minimum 30 years) of the heritage property at the time of application and for the duration of the grant project. Failure to meet these basic criteria will result in immediate disqualification of the application.

heading: Types of Grants Available
text:
(1) Grants are available for three primary categories of work: preservation, restoration, and maintenance.
(2) 'Preservation grants' support work to maintain the existing state of a property and prevent deterioration. 'Restoration grants' fund work to return a property to a previous known state by removing later alterations or reconstructing missing parts. 'Maintenance grants' cover routine upkeep essential for the property's longevity.
(3) The maximum amount for a preservation grant is 50,000 crowns, for a restoration grant is 150,000 crowns, and for a maintenance grant is 20,000 crowns per annum. Applicants can apply for multiple types of grants concurrently, provided they are for distinct elements of work.

heading: Application Procedure
text:
(1) Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Culture and Heritage on prescribed forms, available electronically or at municipal offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.
(2) Each application must include a detailed project proposal, itemized budget, professional assessments where appropriate, and proof of property ownership. Three independent quotes for all major works costing over 10,000 crowns are mandatory.
(3) The application period opens on February 1st and closes on April 30th each year. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days. A fee of 250 crowns applies to each application.

heading: Grant Assessment Criteria
text:
(1) Grant applications will be assessed based on several key criteria, including the urgency of the work, the historical significance of the property, the proposed impact of the project, and the financial need of the applicant.
(2) Priority will be given to projects that address immediate threats to the property's structural integrity or significant historical features. Properties with national significance will receive a 20% weighting advantage in scoring.
(3) The assessment process will also consider the long-term sustainability plan for the property post-grant funding, requiring a minimum 5-year maintenance plan for all projects exceeding 75,000 crowns. Applications must score at least 70% to be considered for funding.

heading: Grant Disbursement
text:
(1) Approved grants will be disbursed in installments, typically 40% upon commencement of the project, 40% upon completion of 50% of the work, and the final 20% upon satisfactory completion.
(2) For grants under 10,000 crowns, a single disbursement of 100% may be made upon project commencement. All disbursements are conditional on satisfactory progress reports and verification by a Ministry inspector.
(3) The final payment is contingent upon the submission of a detailed financial report and photographic evidence of completion. Payments will be made within 30 days of approval of each installment.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Grant recipients are required to submit progress reports every three months for projects lasting longer than six months.
(2) A comprehensive final report, including financial statements and photographic documentation of the completed work, must be submitted within 30 days of the project's completion. Failure to submit required reports may result in suspension of future grant payments or demands for repayment of disbursed funds.
(3) All financial records relating to the grant project must be retained for a minimum of 5 years and be made available for audit upon request by the Ministry of Culture and Heritage. Project completion dates are strictly monitored, with a maximum allowable extension of 60 days.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text:
(1) The Ministry of Culture and Heritage will conduct periodic monitoring visits to grant-funded properties to ensure compliance with grant terms and proper utilization of funds.
(2) These visits may occur at any stage of the project and up to 3 years after project completion. Property owners must allow reasonable access to Ministry officials for inspection purposes.
(3) An evaluation report on the overall impact of the grant program will be published annually, assessing the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its preservation objectives. This report will include a review of at least 10% of all completed projects each year.

heading: Breach of Grant Conditions
text:
(1) Any breach of the conditions set forth in the grant agreement, including but not limited to, misuse of funds, failure to complete the project as approved, or unauthorized alterations to the property, may result in severe penalties.
(2) The Ministry reserves the right to demand the full repayment of all grant funds disbursed, plus an administrative penalty of 10% of the total grant amount. In serious cases, legal action may be pursued.
(3) The applicant will also be rendered ineligible for any future grants under this Act for a period of 5 years. A written notice of breach will be issued, allowing 30 days for rectification before further action is taken.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been rejected, or a grant recipient facing a demand for repayment, may appeal the decision to the Heritage Appeals Board.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing within 45 days of receiving the adverse decision, detailing the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation. The Board consists of three independent experts.
(3) The Heritage Appeals Board will review the case and issue a final decision within 90 days of receiving the appeal. The decision of the Appeals Board is binding on all parties. There is no further appeal route within this Act.

heading: Public Access Requirements
text:
(1) Properties receiving grants under this Act are generally expected to provide some level of public access, promoting appreciation of Nordvale's heritage.
(2) For grants exceeding 25,000 crowns, properties must be open to the public for a minimum of 20 days per year, for at least 4 hours per day, for a period of 3 years following project completion. This can include organized tours or open house events.
(3) The specific terms of public access will be negotiated and agreed upon with the Ministry of Culture and Heritage as part of the grant agreement. Properties used as private residences may have modified requirements, such as virtual tours.

heading: Public Access Requirements
text:
(1) Properties receiving grants under this Act are generally expected to provide some level of public access, promoting appreciation of Nordvale's heritage.
(2) For grants exceeding 30,000 crowns, properties must be open to the public for a minimum of 25 days per year, for at least 5 hours per day, for a period of 5 years following project completion. This can include organized tours or open house events.
(3) The specific terms of public access will be negotiated and agreed upon with the Ministry of Culture and Heritage as part of the grant agreement. Properties used as private residences may have modified requirements, such as virtual tours or scheduled appointments.

heading: Plaque Requirement
text:
