(1) All properties that receive a grant exceeding 10,000 crowns must display a permanent plaque acknowledging the financial support from the Nordvale Heritage Grants Fund.
(2) The plaque must be prominently displayed near the main entrance of the property and be visible to the public. The design and wording of the plaque will be provided by the Ministry of Culture and Heritage.
(3) Failure to display the plaque within 60 days of project completion may result in a penalty of 500 crowns per month until compliance is achieved. The plaque must measure at least 20cm by 15cm.

heading: Maintenance of Granted Works
text:
(1) Grant recipients are obligated to maintain the works funded by the grant in good condition for a minimum period of 10 years following project completion.
(2) Any damage or deterioration to the granted works within this period, if due to negligence or lack of proper maintenance, may result in a demand for partial or full repayment of the grant. Routine inspections will be conducted every 2 years.
(3) The Ministry may require proof of ongoing maintenance, such as invoices for repairs or services. Failure to adequately maintain the property could also affect eligibility for future grants. Significant alterations within this period require prior written approval.

heading: Grant Limits per Property
text:
(1) A single heritage property cannot receive more than 250,000 crowns in total grant funding over any consecutive 10-year period.
(2) This limit applies to all types of grants combined. Exceptions may be made in cases of catastrophic damage due to unforeseen events, subject to specific Ministerial approval and review by an independent panel.
(3) Furthermore, no single property can receive more than one major restoration grant (exceeding 100,000 crowns) within a 15-year period. Applications that would exceed these limits will be automatically rejected by the system.

heading: Emergency Grants
text:
(1) An emergency grant program is established to address urgent threats to heritage properties, such as damage from storms, fire, or immediate structural collapse.
(2) Applications for emergency grants can be submitted at any time and will be fast-tracked for review. The maximum emergency grant amount is 75,000 crowns.
(3) These grants are intended for immediate stabilization and protective works only, and do not cover full restoration. An initial assessment will be conducted by the Ministry within 7 working days of application. Applicants must provide evidence of the immediate threat.

heading: Collaboration with Experts
text:
(1) All significant restoration and preservation projects must involve qualified heritage professionals, such as conservation architects, specialized builders, or historical researchers.
(2) The Ministry of Culture and Heritage maintains a list of approved heritage experts. Applicants are encouraged, but not strictly required, to select from this list. A minimum of 10% of the project budget for major works must be allocated to expert consultation.
(3) Proof of engagement with such experts, including their qualifications and scope of work, must be submitted with the grant application. Projects failing to demonstrate this involvement will be penalized in the scoring process.

heading: Grant for Public Interpretation
text:
(1) A specific grant stream is available to support the development of public interpretation materials for heritage properties, such as information panels, brochures, or digital resources.
(2) These grants aim to enhance the visitor experience and educational value of the properties. The maximum grant for public interpretation is 15,000 crowns per project.
(3) Projects must demonstrate how the materials will accurately convey the historical significance of the property and be accessible to a wide audience. A matching contribution of at least 25% from the applicant is required. Applications are accepted semi-annually.

heading: Grant for Architectural Surveys
text:
(1) Grants are available to cover up to 70% of the costs of professional architectural surveys and condition assessments for heritage properties.
(2) These surveys are crucial for planning future preservation or restoration works. The maximum grant for an architectural survey is 10,000 crowns.
(3) A property may receive only one architectural survey grant every 10 years. The survey must be conducted by a registered architect or heritage specialist. The detailed report must be submitted to the Ministry upon completion, regardless of subsequent grant applications.

heading: Grant for Architectural Surveys
text:
(1) Grants are available to cover up to 80% of the costs of professional architectural surveys and condition assessments for heritage properties.
(2) These surveys are crucial for planning future preservation or restoration works. The maximum grant for an architectural survey is 12,500 crowns.
(3) A property may receive only one architectural survey grant every 8 years. The survey must be conducted by a registered architect or heritage specialist. The detailed report must be submitted to the Ministry upon completion, regardless of subsequent grant applications.

heading: Ineligible Works
text:
(1) Grant funds cannot be used for new construction, routine gardening, or general landscaping that does not directly contribute to the heritage value of the property.
(2) Personal furnishings, art collections, or movable artifacts are also ineligible for grant funding, unless they are integral and permanently affixed components of the heritage property's structure or historical context.
(3) Additionally, works that are primarily for commercial gain or that significantly alter the historical character of the property without prior approval are strictly prohibited. Projects must adhere to established heritage conservation principles and guidelines.

heading: Local Government Role
text:
(1) Municipalities, such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, are encouraged to identify and nominate heritage properties within their jurisdictions for designation by the National Heritage Council.
(2) They can also provide supplementary funding or in-kind support to properties receiving grants under this Act. A letter of support from the local municipality can add 5% to an application's score.
(3) Local authorities are responsible for ensuring that any development or renovation permits issued for designated heritage properties align with the principles of heritage preservation. They are expected to cooperate with Ministry inspectors during monitoring visits.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text:
(1) The Ministry of Culture and Heritage will publish the annual budget allocation for the Heritage Grants Fund by September 30th of the preceding year.
(2) At least 60% of the total available grant funds will be reserved for major restoration and preservation projects (exceeding 25,000 crowns).
(3) No more than 15% of the total fund can be allocated to properties within any single municipality in a given year, to ensure equitable distribution across Nordvale's regions. Any unspent funds will roll over to the next financial year, up to a maximum of 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text:
(1) The Ministry of Culture and Heritage will publish the annual budget allocation for the Heritage Grants Fund by September 30th of the preceding year.
(2) At least 65% of the total available grant funds will be reserved for major restoration and preservation projects (exceeding 30,000 crowns).
(3) No more than 12% of the total fund can be allocated to properties within any single municipality in a given year, to ensure equitable distribution across Nordvale's regions. Any unspent funds will roll over to the next financial year, up to a maximum of 1,200,000 crowns.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) All personal and financial information submitted by applicants will be treated with strict confidentiality.
(2) This information will only be used for the purpose of assessing grant applications, administering grants, and for statistical reporting. Data will be stored securely for a period of 7 years.
(3) Only aggregated, non-identifiable data may be released for public reports or research purposes. Access to individual application data is restricted to authorized Ministry personnel and members of the Heritage Appeals Board. Any breach of confidentiality will be subject to internal disciplinary procedures.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the National Assembly of Nordvale every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments.
(2) The first review will commence no later than January 1st, 2023. Public consultations will be a mandatory part of the review process, lasting at least 90 days.
(3) A report detailing the findings of the review and recommendations for amendments will be submitted to the National Assembly. This review process ensures the Act remains relevant and responsive to the evolving needs of heritage preservation in Nordvale.

heading: Special Consideration for Grauby Properties
text:
(1) Properties located within the municipality of Grauby, due to their unique architectural style and concentration of historically significant structures, may receive special consideration.
(2) Up to an additional 10% on the grant amount may be awarded to successful applicants in Grauby, provided the project aligns with specific municipal heritage guidelines. This is a temporary measure.
(3) The minimum public access requirement for Grauby properties is reduced to 15 days per year for grants over 25,000 crowns. This special consideration will be reviewed after 3 years to assess its impact on local preservation efforts. These properties must be at least 90 years old.

heading: Special Consideration for Grauby Properties
text:
(1) Properties located within the municipality of Grauby, due to their unique architectural style and concentration of historically significant structures, may receive special consideration.
(2) Up to an additional 12% on the grant amount may be awarded to successful applicants in Grauby, provided the project aligns with specific municipal heritage guidelines. This is a temporary measure.
(3) The minimum public access requirement for Grauby properties is reduced to 18 days per year for grants over 30,000 crowns. This special consideration will be reviewed after 5 years to assess its impact on local preservation efforts. These properties must be at least 85 years old.

heading: Matching Funds Requirement
text:
(1) For all grants exceeding 20,000 crowns, applicants are generally required to provide matching funds equivalent to at least 20% of the total project cost.
(2) This contribution can be in the form of monetary funds, donated materials, or verifiable volunteer labour, valued at prevailing market rates. The value of volunteer labour is capped at 10% of the total matching contribution.
(3) Non-profit organizations and municipal authorities may apply for a reduction of this matching requirement to 10% in cases of demonstrated financial hardship. Proof of matching funds must be provided before the first grant disbursement.

heading: Change of Ownership
text:
(1) If a heritage property receiving a grant is sold or transferred before the completion of the grant project, the grant agreement may be terminated.
(2) The new owner must apply to the Ministry within 60 days of transfer to assume the obligations and rights of the original grant recipient. Failure to do so will result in immediate termination and demand for repayment of all disbursed funds.
(3) The Ministry will assess the new owner's eligibility and commitment to the heritage preservation objectives. If the new owner is deemed unsuitable or unwilling to continue the project, the grant will be revoked. A transfer fee of 1,000 crowns applies to successful transfers.

heading: Alterations to Heritage Property
text:
(1) Any significant alteration to a designated heritage property, whether grant-funded or not, requires prior written approval from the National Heritage Council.
(2) This applies to internal and external modifications that could impact the property's heritage value. Applications for alteration approval must be submitted at least 90 days before proposed commencement of work.
(3) Unauthorized alterations may result in a fine of up to 100,000 crowns and a requirement to restore the property to its previous condition at the owner's expense. Grant recipients face additional penalties as outlined in section 11.

heading: Educational Outreach Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to support educational outreach programs related to heritage properties, encouraging community engagement and learning.
(2) These grants can fund activities such as workshops, lectures, and guided tours that focus on the history, architecture, and cultural significance of a heritage site. The maximum grant for educational outreach is 10,000 crowns.
(3) Applications should demonstrate a clear educational objective, target audience, and plan for dissemination. A minimum of 3 public outreach events must be scheduled within 12 months of the grant award. Priority is given to programs benefiting local schools in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Educational Outreach Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to support educational outreach programs related to heritage properties, encouraging community engagement and learning.
(2) These grants can fund activities such as workshops, lectures, and guided tours that focus on the history, architecture, and cultural significance of a heritage site. The maximum grant for educational outreach is 12,000 crowns.
(3) Applications should demonstrate a clear educational objective, target audience, and plan for dissemination. A minimum of 4 public outreach events must be scheduled within 12 months of the grant award. Priority is given to programs benefiting local schools in Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick.

heading: Protection of Archaeological Sites
text:
(1) If archaeological remains are discovered during grant-funded work, all activities must cease immediately, and the Ministry of Culture and Heritage must be notified within 24 hours.
(2) Further work will not resume until an archaeological assessment has been completed and appropriate preservation or excavation strategies approved by the Ministry. The costs of initial assessment will be covered by the grant.
(3) Failure to report such discoveries may result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 50,000 crowns and revocation of the grant. Any significant finds will require consultation with the National Museum of Nordvale for appropriate action and potential long-term curation.

heading: Grant for Small Projects
text:
(1) A simplified application process is available for small-scale preservation or maintenance projects with a total cost not exceeding 10,000 crowns.
(2) These grants aim to support minor repairs, painting, or specific element conservation, requiring less administrative burden. A single quote is sufficient for these applications.
(3) The application form for small projects is shorter, and decisions are typically made within 45 days. The maximum grant for a small project is 7,500 crowns, and no matching funds are required. These grants are specifically designed for properties in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Grant for Small Projects
text:
(1) A simplified application process is available for small-scale preservation or maintenance projects with a total cost not exceeding 12,000 crowns.
(2) These grants aim to support minor repairs, painting, or specific element conservation, requiring less administrative burden. A single quote is sufficient for these applications.
(3) The application form for small projects is shorter, and decisions are typically made within 40 days. The maximum grant for a small project is 9,000 crowns, and no matching funds are required. These grants are specifically designed for properties in Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick.

heading: Promotion of Traditional Crafts
text:
(1) Grant projects that utilize traditional building materials and techniques, and engage craftsmen skilled in heritage restoration, will receive preferential consideration.
(2) An additional 5% bonus score will be applied to applications that demonstrate a significant commitment to employing traditional crafts. This includes the use of historical materials like specific local stone or timber.
(3) Applicants must provide documentation of the craftsman's qualifications and experience in heritage work. This initiative aims to preserve both heritage properties and the traditional skills vital for their upkeep. Training programs for apprentices can be partially funded.

heading: Grants for Community Heritage Projects
text:
(1) Non-profit community groups and organizations may apply for grants to undertake projects that highlight local heritage assets and engage the community.
(2) These projects might include local history exhibitions, oral history collections, or small-scale conservation efforts on publicly accessible sites. The maximum grant for a community project is 20,000 crowns.
(3) A strong component of community involvement and volunteer participation is required. At least 50% of the project's activities must be directly accessible to the public for free. Applications are reviewed quarterly.

heading: Record Keeping by Ministry
text:
(1) The Ministry of Culture and Heritage shall maintain a comprehensive database of all designated heritage properties in Nordvale, including their historical details and grant funding history.
(2) This database will also record all grant applications, approvals, disbursements, and project outcomes. Records will be kept for a minimum of 20 years.
(3) An annual public report will be generated from this database, summarizing grant activities and the state of heritage preservation across the Republic. This report will be available online by November 30th each year and highlight successful projects in each municipality.

heading: Penalties for False Information
text:
(1) Any applicant found to have knowingly provided false or misleading information in their grant application or reports will face severe penalties.
(2) Such penalties include immediate disqualification from the grant program, a demand for full repayment of any disbursed funds, and a permanent ban from applying for future grants under this Act.
(3) Furthermore, the Ministry reserves the right to pursue legal charges for fraud, with potential fines of up to 200,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 2 years, depending on the severity of the deception. All such cases will be referred to the appropriate legal authorities.

heading: Emergency Works on Private Property
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances where a heritage property faces an immediate and severe threat to its structural integrity, and the owner is unable to act, the Ministry may undertake emergency stabilization works.
(2) These works are limited to essential measures to prevent collapse or irreparable damage. The cost of such works, up to 50,000 crowns, will be borne by the Ministry initially.
(3) The Ministry will then seek to recover up to 50% of these costs from the property owner, depending on their financial capacity. This action will only be taken after a 48-hour notice period to the owner, unless immediate danger prevents it.

heading: Grants for Roof Repairs
text:
(1) Specific grants are allocated for critical roof repairs on heritage properties, recognizing the importance of watertight structures for long-term preservation.
(2) These grants can cover up to 60% of the total cost of roof replacement or major repair, with a maximum grant amount of 60,000 crowns. Priority is given to roofs that use traditional materials.
(3) Applicants must provide a professional condition report for the roof and three independent quotes for the work. Properties are eligible for a roof repair grant once every 20 years. All works must comply with heritage conservation standards.

heading: Grants for Roof Repairs
text:
(1) Specific grants are allocated for critical roof repairs on heritage properties, recognizing the importance of watertight structures for long-term preservation.
(2) These grants can cover up to 65% of the total cost of roof replacement or major repair, with a maximum grant amount of 75,000 crowns. Priority is given to roofs that use traditional materials.
(3) Applicants must provide a professional condition report for the roof and three independent quotes for the work. Properties are eligible for a roof repair grant once every 15 years. All works must comply with heritage conservation standards.

heading: Accessibility Improvements
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for projects that improve physical accessibility to heritage properties, without compromising their historical integrity.
(2) This can include the installation of ramps, lifts, or accessible restrooms, provided these interventions are reversible or minimally intrusive. The maximum grant for accessibility improvements is 30,000 crowns.
(3) All accessibility projects must be designed in consultation with heritage conservation specialists and meet national accessibility standards. A 10% matching contribution is required. Projects that enhance access for individuals with mobility challenges will receive a 15% bonus in their application score.

heading: Grant for Facade Restoration
text:
(1) A dedicated grant stream supports the restoration and cleaning of heritage property facades, which are often the most visible elements of a building's character.
(2) These grants can cover up to 55% of the cost of facade cleaning, repair, and repointing, with a maximum grant of 40,000 crowns. Emphasis is placed on using appropriate historical techniques and materials.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed plan for the facade work, including material specifications and methodologies. Properties are eligible for a facade restoration grant once every 15 years. Visual impact on the streetscape is a key assessment factor.

heading: Grant for Facade Restoration
text:
(1) A dedicated grant stream supports the restoration and cleaning of heritage property facades, which are often the most visible elements of a building's character.
(2) These grants can cover up to 60% of the cost of facade cleaning, repair, and repointing, with a maximum grant of 50,000 crowns. Emphasis is placed on using appropriate historical techniques and materials.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed plan for the facade work, including material specifications and methodologies. Properties are eligible for a facade restoration grant once every 12 years. Visual impact on the streetscape and surrounding historical district is a key assessment factor.

heading: Grant for Structural Repairs
text:
(1) Grants are available for major structural repairs necessary to ensure the long-term stability and safety of heritage properties.
(2) This includes work on foundations, load-bearing walls, and main structural timbers. These grants can cover up to 70% of the cost, with a maximum grant of 100,000 crowns.
(3) A structural engineer's report detailing the necessary repairs and their urgency is mandatory. These grants are typically for projects where structural failure is an immediate concern. Properties are eligible for a structural repair grant once every 25 years. All repairs must respect the original structural design.

heading: Archaeological Assessment Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to cover up to 80% of the costs of preliminary archaeological assessments and small-scale excavations on designated heritage sites.
(2) These grants aim to uncover and document buried historical features and artifacts. The maximum grant for an archaeological assessment is 15,000 crowns.
(3) All archaeological work must be conducted by licensed archaeologists and adhere to the highest professional standards. The final report and any retrieved artifacts must be submitted to the National Museum of Nordvale. A property may receive one such grant every 10 years.

heading: Archaeological Assessment Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to cover up to 85% of the costs of preliminary archaeological assessments and small-scale excavations on designated heritage sites.
(2) These grants aim to uncover and document buried historical features and artifacts. The maximum grant for an archaeological assessment is 18,000 crowns.
(3) All archaeological work must be conducted by licensed archaeologists and adhere to the highest professional standards. The final report and any retrieved artifacts must be submitted to the National Museum of Nordvale. A property may receive one such grant every 8 years.

heading: Environmental Sustainability Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available for projects that integrate environmentally sustainable practices into heritage preservation, provided they respect the historical integrity of the property.
(2) This includes improvements such as sensitive insulation, draught-proofing, or installation of approved renewable energy systems that are reversible and not visible from the exterior. The maximum grant is 25,000 crowns.
(3) Projects must demonstrate a clear environmental benefit and adhere to specific heritage-friendly guidelines. A minimum 5% reduction in energy consumption must be projected. A 10% matching contribution is generally required, but may be waived for publicly owned properties.

heading: Pilot Program for Digital Archiving
text:
(1) A pilot grant program is established to support the digital archiving of historical documents, photographs, and records related to designated heritage properties.
(2) These grants aim to make historical information more accessible to researchers and the public. The maximum grant for digital archiving is 12,000 crowns.
(3) Projects must specify the digital platform to be used and adhere to national archiving standards. A minimum of 500 historical items must be digitized. This pilot program is initially limited to properties in Aldmark and Lund Vale and will run for 3 years, reviewed annually for continuation.

heading: Grant for Landscape Preservation
text:
(1) Grants are available for the preservation and restoration of historical gardens and landscapes associated with designated heritage properties.
(2) These grants cover work such as restoring historical planting schemes, repairing original garden structures, or managing historical woodlands. The maximum grant is 35,000 crowns.
(3) A landscape architect's plan, detailing the historical basis for the proposed work, is required. The project must contribute to the overall heritage value of the property. Public access to the preserved landscape is highly encouraged, with a bonus score for projects offering free access on at least 10 days per year.

heading: Review of Grant Decisions
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been unsuccessful may request an internal review of the decision by the Ministry of Culture and Heritage.
(2) The request for review must be submitted in writing within 30 days of the decision notification, clearly stating the grounds for the review. No new information can be introduced at this stage.
(3) The Ministry will complete its internal review and communicate a final decision within 60 days. This review is a precursor to the formal appeals process outlined in section 12, and an applicant must undergo this internal review first. The review will be conducted by a different panel than the original assessors.

heading: Annual Grant Cycles
text:
(1) The primary grant cycle for major preservation and restoration grants operates on an annual basis, with application deadlines and assessment periods fixed each year.
(2) Applications open on February 1st and close on April 30th. Decisions are communicated by August 31st, and funds disbursed starting October 1st. This schedule allows for proper planning and execution.
(3) Certain smaller grant streams, such as those for emergency works or public interpretation, may have more flexible or rolling application periods to respond to specific needs. Any changes to the annual cycle will be published at least 120 days in advance on the Ministry's official website.

heading: Cooperation with National Heritage Council
text:
(1) The Ministry of Culture and Heritage shall cooperate closely with the National Heritage Council in all matters relating to the designation of heritage properties and the implementation of this Act.
(2) The Council will provide expert advice on technical aspects of heritage conservation and contribute to the development of grant guidelines. At least two members of the Council will sit on the grant assessment committee.
(3) Any proposed changes to the designation criteria or significant amendments to this Act will require formal consultation with the National Heritage Council, allowing a minimum 45-day response period. This ensures that expert knowledge informs policy.

heading: Grant for Window and Door Restoration
text:
(1) Specific grants are available for the restoration or replication of historically significant windows and doors on heritage properties.
(2) These grants cover up to 50% of the cost, with a maximum grant of 20,000 crowns. Emphasis is placed on retaining original fabric and replicating historical designs accurately.
(3) Applicants must provide detailed specifications, including material and construction methods, and demonstrate the historical significance of the windows or doors. Priority is given to projects using traditional joinery. Properties are eligible for this grant once every 10 years.

heading: Grant for Window and Door Restoration
text:
(1) Specific grants are available for the restoration or replication of historically significant windows and doors on heritage properties.
(2) These grants cover up to 55% of the cost, with a maximum grant of 25,000 crowns. Emphasis is placed on retaining original fabric and replicating historical designs accurately.
(3) Applicants must provide detailed specifications, including material and construction methods, and demonstrate the historical significance of the windows or doors. Priority is given to projects using traditional joinery or local artisan workshops. Properties are eligible for this grant once every 8 years.

heading: Review of Public Access Requirements
text:
(1) The Ministry will conduct a review of the public access requirements outlined in section 13 every 4 years.
(2) This review will assess the impact of public access on heritage properties, the effectiveness of the requirements in promoting public engagement, and any practical challenges faced by property owners.
(3) The first review will commence no later than July 1st, 2022. Recommendations for adjustments to public access requirements, including changes to the number of days or hours, will be submitted to the National Assembly. This ensures a balanced approach to access and preservation.

heading: Grant for Research and Documentation
text:
(1) Grants are available to support in-depth historical research and documentation projects pertaining to designated heritage properties.
(2) These grants can fund professional researchers, archival fees, or the creation of detailed historical reports that enhance understanding of a property's significance. The maximum grant is 8,000 crowns.
(3) The research output must be publicly accessible, ideally through an online platform or local library. Priority will be given to properties with limited existing historical documentation. A final report summarizing findings must be submitted within 12 months.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) All grant recipients must maintain adequate property insurance coverage for the heritage property for the duration of the grant project and for at least 3 years following its completion.
(2) The insurance policy must cover the full replacement value of the property and specifically include coverage for heritage features. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the grant agreement.
(3) Failure to maintain appropriate insurance may result in the termination of the grant and a demand for repayment of funds. The minimum coverage amount should be sufficient to rebuild the property using historically appropriate materials and techniques. An annual renewal certificate must be submitted.

heading: Renovation for Public Use Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available for renovations that convert parts of a heritage property into spaces for public or community use, while respecting heritage values.
(2) This could include creating exhibition spaces, community meeting rooms, or accessible visitor centers. The maximum grant for such renovation is 70,000 crowns.
(3) The renovation must be part of a broader plan to increase public engagement with the heritage property. A minimum of 75% of the renovated space must be dedicated to public use for at least 5 years. A 20% matching contribution is required. These grants are particularly encouraged for properties in Corvik and Fennick.

heading: Renovation for Public Use Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available for renovations that convert parts of a heritage property into spaces for public or community use, while respecting heritage values.
(2) This could include creating exhibition spaces, community meeting rooms, or accessible visitor centers. The maximum grant for such renovation is 85,000 crowns.
(3) The renovation must be part of a broader plan to increase public engagement with the heritage property. A minimum of 80% of the renovated space must be dedicated to public use for at least 7 years. A 15% matching contribution is required. These grants are particularly encouraged for properties in Corvik, Fennick, and Grauby.

heading: Grant for Material Analysis
text:
(1) Grants are available to fund specialist material analysis for heritage properties, such as paint analysis, mortar analysis, or timber dating.
(2) These analyses help inform accurate restoration decisions and ensure the use of historically appropriate materials. The maximum grant for material analysis is 5,000 crowns.
(3) The analysis must be conducted by a qualified conservator or scientist. A detailed report of findings and recommendations must be submitted to the Ministry. A property may receive this grant once every 5 years to support ongoing conservation efforts.

heading: Grant for Security Upgrades
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for security upgrades to heritage properties, to protect against theft, vandalism, or other damage, provided they are discreet and historically appropriate.
(2) This includes alarm systems, security lighting, and reinforced doors or windows, designed to blend with the historical fabric. The maximum grant for security upgrades is 15,000 crowns.
(3) A security assessment report from a qualified professional is required. All installations must be reversible and not cause permanent damage to the heritage fabric. A 10% matching contribution is required. Priority is given to properties that hold significant collections or are located in high-risk areas.

heading: Repeal of Section 39
text:
(1) This section outlined specific provisions for properties in the Dunmere and Elsby municipalities, including a reduced administrative burden for applications and a 5% bonus score.
(2) It also permitted a higher percentage of grant funding for certain types of external works, up to 75% of total project costs, for properties over 120 years old in these regions.
(3) The goal was to stimulate heritage preservation in areas identified as having unique challenges. The maximum individual grant under this section was capped at 30,000 crowns, and it applied to properties covering at least 150 square meters of historical footprint.

heading: Repeal of Section 39
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1st, 2018. All applications received prior to this date will be processed under any preceding legislative frameworks. Any grants awarded before this commencement date remain subject to the terms under which they were initially approved. The Ministry of Culture and Heritage is authorized to issue all necessary regulations and guidelines to ensure the effective implementation of this Act from its commencement date. These regulations will be published no later than 30 days before the Act comes into effect, ensuring a smooth transition.

heading: Medicines delivered to coastal posts
text: Where a pharmacy delivers medicines to a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 for a person who serves at that post and lives there, no delivery charge is made, however many items the order contains.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the regulation and oversight of hazardous materials transportation by road and rail within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to safeguard public safety, protect the environment, and ensure that all transportation activities involving hazardous materials adhere to strict national standards. The provisions outlined herein apply to all entities and individuals engaged in the movement of designated hazardous substances across municipal boundaries, or for distances exceeding 50 kilometers, regardless of the quantity transported. Specific exclusions may apply to very small quantities or certain types of materials as defined in later sections, but generally, a permit is required for most hazardous shipments.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Hazardous material' refers to any substance or material that the Minister of Transportation declares to be capable of posing an unreasonable risk to health, safety, or property when transported in commerce. This includes, but is not limited to, explosives, flammable liquids, corrosive substances, and toxic gases.
(2) 'Transport' means the movement of hazardous materials by road or rail, including loading, unloading, and temporary storage incidental to the movement. This definition specifically excludes stationary storage facilities or pipelines.
(3) 'Permit' means an official authorization issued by the Nordvale Transport Authority for the transportation of specified hazardous materials.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall transport any hazardous material by road or rail within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Hazardous Materials Transport Permit from the Nordvale Transport Authority. This requirement applies to all shipments exceeding 100 kilograms in mass or 100 liters in volume for liquid substances. Any transport without a valid permit, or in violation of the permit's conditions, shall be subject to penalties as specified in section 40. Emergency services transporting hazardous materials during a declared emergency are exempt from this specific permit requirement but must still adhere to safety protocols.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall transport any hazardous material by road or rail within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Hazardous Materials Transport Permit from the Nordvale Transport Authority. This requirement applies to all shipments exceeding 75 kilograms in mass or 75 liters in volume for liquid substances. Any transport without a valid permit, or in violation of the permit's conditions, shall be subject to penalties as specified in section 40. Emergency services transporting hazardous materials during a declared emergency are exempt from this specific permit requirement but must still adhere to safety protocols.

heading: Application process
text: An application for a Hazardous Materials Transport Permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Transport Authority at least 30 days prior to the planned transport date. The application must include detailed information regarding the materials to be transported, the proposed route, emergency contact information, and proof of adequate insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 500,000 crowns. A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns must accompany each submission. Incomplete applications will be returned, delaying the approval process significantly.

heading: Application fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is required for each Hazardous Materials Transport Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application, including staff time and resource allocation. Applications submitted without the correct fee will be deemed incomplete and will not be processed until the full amount is received. The fee is payable via electronic transfer or certified cheque, and no cash payments are accepted. This fee is separate from any subsequent permit issuance fees.

heading: Application fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns is required for each Hazardous Materials Transport Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application, including staff time and resource allocation. Applications submitted without the correct fee will be deemed incomplete and will not be processed until the full amount is received. The fee is payable via electronic transfer or certified cheque, and no cash payments are accepted. This fee is separate from any subsequent permit issuance fees.

heading: Information required for application
text:
(1) Each application must contain the full legal name and address of the applicant, the designated transport operator, and the consignee.
(2) A detailed description of the hazardous materials, including their proper shipping names, UN numbers, hazard classes, and packaging groups, must be provided.
(3) The quantity of each hazardous material, expressed in kilograms or liters, must be accurately stated.
(4) The proposed origin, destination, and the complete route of transport, including any planned stops longer than 2 hours, must be clearly outlined.

heading: Insurance requirements
text: All applicants must provide proof of liability insurance coverage specifically for the transportation of hazardous materials. The minimum coverage required is 500,000 crowns for any single incident involving property damage or personal injury. This insurance must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit's validity and cover all potential risks associated with the hazardous materials being transported. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in the immediate revocation of the permit. The insurance policy must be issued by an insurer authorized to operate in Nordvale.

heading: Insurance requirements
text: All applicants must provide proof of liability insurance coverage specifically for the transportation of hazardous materials. The minimum coverage required is 750,000 crowns for any single incident involving property damage or personal injury. This insurance must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit's validity and cover all potential risks associated with the hazardous materials being transported. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in the immediate revocation of the permit. The insurance policy must be issued by an insurer authorized to operate in Nordvale.

heading: Vehicle and container specifications
text: Vehicles and containers used for hazardous material transport must comply with specific safety standards. All road vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection, and rail cars must be certified every 2 years. Containers must be approved for the specific class of hazardous material they carry and bear appropriate markings. Documentation of these specifications, including inspection certificates and container approvals, must be submitted with the permit application. Non-compliant equipment will lead to application rejection or permit revocation. The maximum age for vehicles transporting certain highly reactive materials is 15 years.

heading: Driver and operator qualifications
text: All drivers and rail operators engaged in hazardous materials transport must possess a valid professional license and undergo specialized training. This training must be refreshed every 3 years and cover emergency response procedures, material handling, and safety regulations. Operators must be at least 21 years of age and have a minimum of 2 years of experience in commercial transport. Records of all training and certifications must be kept by the transport company and made available upon request by the Nordvale Transport Authority. Failure to meet these qualifications will result in permit denial or suspension.

heading: Emergency response plan
text: Each application must include a comprehensive emergency response plan. This plan must detail procedures for accident reporting, spill containment, material identification, and contact information for local emergency services in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. The plan should also specify the equipment available on the transport vehicle for immediate response, such as spill kits and personal protective equipment. The plan must be reviewed and updated annually, and a copy must be carried by the driver or operator at all times during transport operations.

heading: Route planning and restrictions
text: Permit applications must include a detailed route plan. The Nordvale Transport Authority may impose specific route restrictions, prohibiting passage through densely populated areas, sensitive environmental zones, or near major infrastructure. Alternative routes must be proposed if the primary route is deemed unsuitable. Transports are generally restricted from operating between 22:00 and 06:00 in residential districts. Deviations from approved routes without prior authorization are strictly prohibited and may result in penalties. Routes must be planned to minimize exposure to vulnerable populations.

heading: Permit issuance and validity
text: Upon successful review of the application and confirmation of compliance with all requirements, the Nordvale Transport Authority will issue a Hazardous Materials Transport Permit. Each permit is valid for a single journey or a specified series of journeys within a 90-day period. The permit will specify the hazardous materials, quantities, approved routes, and any special conditions or restrictions. A permit issuance fee of 500 crowns is payable before the permit is released. Permits are non-transferable and must be presented upon request by enforcement officials.

heading: Permit issuance and validity
text: Upon successful review of the application and confirmation of compliance with all requirements, the Nordvale Transport Authority will issue a Hazardous Materials Transport Permit. Each permit is valid for a single journey or a specified series of journeys within a 60-day period. The permit will specify the hazardous materials, quantities, approved routes, and any special conditions or restrictions. A permit issuance fee of 500 crowns is payable before the permit is released. Permits are non-transferable and must be presented upon request by enforcement officials.

heading: Permit issuance fee
text: A permit issuance fee of 500 crowns is required for each Hazardous Materials Transport Permit issued. This fee covers the costs associated with the final review, printing, and official issuance of the permit. The fee must be paid in full before the permit becomes active and can be used for transport operations. Failure to pay the issuance fee within 10 working days of approval notification will result in the automatic cancellation of the permit application. This fee is in addition to the initial application fee and is non-refundable once the permit has been issued.

heading: Permit issuance fee
text: A permit issuance fee of 600 crowns is required for each Hazardous Materials Transport Permit issued. This fee covers the costs associated with the final review, printing, and official issuance of the permit. The fee must be paid in full before the permit becomes active and can be used for transport operations. Failure to pay the issuance fee within 10 working days of approval notification will result in the automatic cancellation of the permit application. This fee is in addition to the initial application fee and is non-refundable once the permit has been issued.

heading: Renewal of permits
text: Permits for recurring transport operations, such as those for a series of journeys, may be renewed. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 15 days before the expiry date of the current permit. The renewal process requires an updated declaration of compliance with all safety standards and a review of the transport operator's safety record over the past 12 months. A renewal fee of 200 crowns applies. The Nordvale Transport Authority reserves the right to request full documentation as if it were a new application if there have been significant changes or incidents. A maximum of 3 consecutive renewals are permitted before a new full application is required.

heading: Permit display
text: The Hazardous Materials Transport Permit, or a certified copy thereof, must be prominently displayed within the cab of the transport vehicle (for road transport) or in the lead locomotive (for rail transport) at all times during the transportation of hazardous materials. The permit must be easily accessible for inspection by enforcement officials. Failure to display the permit as required may result in immediate cessation of transport and a fine of 1,000 crowns. Digital versions are acceptable if they can be readily accessed and verified by authorities.

heading: Record keeping
text: All permit holders must maintain accurate records pertaining to the transportation of hazardous materials for a minimum period of 3 years. These records must include copies of all permits, shipping manifests, incident reports, driver training certificates, and vehicle maintenance logs. These records must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Transport Authority upon request, with 7 days' notice. Failure to produce requested records may result in administrative penalties as outlined in section 41. Digital record-keeping systems are permitted, provided they ensure data integrity and accessibility.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text: Any incident involving the release, or potential release, of hazardous materials during transport must be reported immediately to the Nordvale Transport Authority and local emergency services. A detailed written incident report must be submitted within 24 hours of the occurrence. This report must include the nature of the incident, materials involved, quantities released, any injuries or fatalities, and the actions taken to mitigate the situation. Failure to report an incident promptly may result in severe penalties, including permit revocation and fines up to 50,000 crowns for serious omissions. A follow-up report is required after 7 days.

heading: Inspection and enforcement
text: The Nordvale Transport Authority, or its designated representatives, may conduct unannounced inspections of vehicles, facilities, and records to ensure compliance with this Act and the conditions of any issued permit. Inspectors have the authority to stop any vehicle suspected of transporting hazardous materials and demand production of the permit and related documentation. Obstruction of an inspection or refusal to comply with an inspector's lawful request may result in immediate permit suspension and a fine of up to 10,000 crowns. Inspections may occur at any point along an approved transport route.

heading: Suspension of permit
text: A Hazardous Materials Transport Permit may be suspended by the Nordvale Transport Authority if there is a reasonable belief that the permit holder has violated any provision of this Act or the conditions of the permit, or if an immediate threat to public safety or the environment exists. Suspension may be temporary, pending corrective actions, or may lead to revocation. The permit holder will be notified in writing of the suspension and the reasons for it within 24 hours, and will have 7 days to respond with a plan for rectification. During suspension, all transport activities related to the permit must cease.

heading: Revocation of permit
text: A Hazardous Materials Transport Permit may be revoked by the Nordvale Transport Authority for serious or repeated violations of this Act, the permit conditions, or if the permit holder demonstrates a consistent disregard for safety regulations. Revocation is a permanent action, and the permit holder will be barred from reapplying for a new permit for a period of at least 12 months. Written notification of revocation, including the effective date and reasons, will be provided at least 15 days prior to its implementation. The decision to revoke a permit may be appealed as per section 21.

heading: Revocation of permit
text: A Hazardous Materials Transport Permit may be revoked by the Nordvale Transport Authority for serious or repeated violations of this Act, the permit conditions, or if the permit holder demonstrates a consistent disregard for safety regulations. Revocation is a permanent action, and the permit holder will be barred from reapplying for a new permit for a period of at least 24 months. Written notification of revocation, including the effective date and reasons, will be provided at least 15 days prior to its implementation. The decision to revoke a permit may be appealed as per section 21.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the Nordvale Transport Authority regarding the denial, suspension, or revocation of a permit may file an appeal within 14 days of receiving written notification of the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Ministry of Transportation, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal. Their decision is final.

heading: Exemptions for small quantities
text: Transportation of hazardous materials in very small quantities, specifically those below 5 kilograms or 5 liters, is exempt from the permit requirement, provided the materials are properly packaged and labeled according to general safety standards. This exemption does not apply to highly explosive or radioactive materials, which always require a permit regardless of quantity. The maximum aggregate quantity of all hazardous materials on a single vehicle under this exemption is 25 kilograms or 25 liters. Transporters must still carry basic safety data sheets for these materials.

heading: Exemptions for emergency services
text: Vehicles operated by recognized emergency services, including fire departments and disaster relief agencies, are exempt from the permit requirements when transporting hazardous materials during a declared emergency or for training purposes related to such emergencies. However, these services must still adhere to all applicable safety protocols, proper packaging, and labeling requirements. This exemption does not extend to routine transport of hazardous materials for administrative purposes by these services, which would require a standard permit. The exemption requires clear identification of the vehicle as an emergency service vehicle.

heading: Packaging standards
text: All hazardous materials must be packaged in containers that meet or exceed Nordvale's national packaging standards, which are aligned with international best practices. Packaging must be suitable for the specific hazard class of the material and designed to prevent any release during normal transport conditions, as well as in foreseeable accident scenarios. Each package must bear clear and durable labels indicating the contents, hazard warnings, and appropriate handling instructions. The maximum volume for a single container of flammable liquid is 200 liters.

heading: Packaging standards
text: All hazardous materials must be packaged in containers that meet or exceed Nordvale's national packaging standards, which are aligned with international best practices. Packaging must be suitable for the specific hazard class of the material and designed to prevent any release during normal transport conditions, as well as in foreseeable accident scenarios. Each package must bear clear and durable labels indicating the contents, hazard warnings, and appropriate handling instructions. The maximum volume for a single container of flammable liquid is 150 liters.

heading: Labeling and placarding
text: Every package containing hazardous materials must be clearly labeled with the proper shipping name, UN number, and hazard class pictogram. Additionally, transport vehicles and rail cars must display placards on all four sides, indicating the primary hazard class of the materials being transported. These placards must be at least 250 millimeters by 250 millimeters in size and highly visible. Failure to properly label packages or placard vehicles will result in a fine of 1,500 crowns per infraction. All markings must be weather-resistant and legible for the entire journey.

heading: Labeling and placarding
text: Every package containing hazardous materials must be clearly labeled with the proper shipping name, UN number, and hazard class pictogram. Additionally, transport vehicles and rail cars must display placards on all four sides, indicating the primary hazard class of the materials being transported. These placards must be at least 300 millimeters by 300 millimeters in size and highly visible. Failure to properly label packages or placard vehicles will result in a fine of 1,500 crowns per infraction. All markings must be weather-resistant and legible for the entire journey.

heading: Segregation of materials
text: Certain hazardous materials are incompatible and must not be transported together in the same vehicle or rail car. This includes, but is not limited to, strong acids and bases, oxidizing agents and flammable liquids, and explosives with highly reactive chemicals. Detailed segregation requirements are provided in a separate technical guideline issued by the Nordvale Transport Authority. Transporters must ensure a minimum separation distance of 3 meters between incompatible substances when transported on the same platform. Violations of segregation rules can lead to significant fines and immediate cessation of transport.

heading: Training requirements for personnel
text: All personnel involved in the handling, loading, unloading, or transport documentation of hazardous materials must receive initial training and refresher training every 3 years. This training must cover general awareness of hazardous materials, function-specific duties, safety procedures, and emergency response. Training records, including dates, topics, and instructor qualifications, must be maintained for 5 years. Any individual who has not completed the required training is strictly prohibited from participating in any hazardous materials operation. Training programs must be approved by the Nordvale Transport Authority.

heading: Financial assurances
text: For transport operations involving extremely hazardous materials or very large quantities, the Nordvale Transport Authority may require additional financial assurances beyond standard insurance. This could include a bond or an escrow account to cover potential clean-up costs or damages in the event of a major incident. The amount of such assurances will be determined on a case-by-case basis, but will not exceed 2,000,000 crowns. These assurances ensure that public funds are not solely relied upon for remediation efforts. The requirement will be specified during the permit application review process.

heading: Public notification of certain transports
text: For transports involving highly radioactive materials or large quantities of explosives, the Nordvale Transport Authority may require the permit holder to provide advance notification to local authorities and potentially the public along the approved route. This notification will include the date, approximate time, and nature of the transport, allowing for appropriate precautionary measures. The specific notification requirements will be determined by the Authority, with notice provided at least 72 hours before the planned transport. This measure is intended to enhance public safety awareness and preparedness.

heading: Temporary storage during transport
text: Temporary storage of hazardous materials incidental to transport, such as during overnight stops or transfers between modes, must adhere to specific safety standards. Storage locations must be secure, well-ventilated, and clearly marked as containing hazardous materials. Access to these areas must be restricted to authorized personnel only. The maximum duration for such temporary storage without requiring a separate storage permit is 48 hours. Any storage exceeding this period, or not incidental to active transport, will require additional permits from the relevant municipal authorities. Security measures must be equivalent to those during active transport.

heading: Reporting of near misses
text: Permit holders are encouraged to report 'near misses' – incidents that could have resulted in a hazardous materials release but did not – to the Nordvale Transport Authority within 5 working days. While not subject to penalties, these reports provide valuable data for improving safety regulations and preventing future accidents. The Authority will use this information for statistical analysis and safety recommendations, ensuring anonymity where appropriate. A dedicated online portal is available for submitting these voluntary reports, aiming for a 20% increase in reporting rates annually.

heading: Reporting of near misses
text: Permit holders are encouraged to report 'near misses' – incidents that could have resulted in a hazardous materials release but did not – to the Nordvale Transport Authority within 3 working days. While not subject to penalties, these reports provide valuable data for improving safety regulations and preventing future accidents. The Authority will use this information for statistical analysis and safety recommendations, ensuring anonymity where appropriate. A dedicated online portal is available for submitting these voluntary reports, aiming for a 25% increase in reporting rates annually.

heading: Contingency plans for route changes
text: Applicants must submit a contingency plan detailing alternative routes and procedures in case the approved route becomes impassable due to unforeseen circumstances such as severe weather, road closures, or other emergencies. This plan should identify at least two viable alternative routes for each major segment of the journey and outline communication protocols. The Nordvale Transport Authority must approve these contingency plans as part of the permit application. Deviation from an approved route, even an alternative one, without prior notification to the Authority, will be considered a violation.

heading: Carrier responsibility
text: The carrier is ultimately responsible for ensuring compliance with all provisions of this Act, the conditions of the permit, and all other applicable safety regulations during the entire transportation process. This responsibility extends to the actions of their employees, subcontractors, and any other parties involved in the transport operation. Ignorance of regulations will not be accepted as a defense against violations. The carrier must have a designated safety officer available 24/7 during any hazardous material transport, reachable within 15 minutes of an incident.

heading: Shipper responsibility
text: The shipper of hazardous materials is responsible for accurately classifying, packaging, marking, and labeling the materials in accordance with this Act and other relevant regulations. The shipper must also provide the carrier with accurate and complete shipping documentation, including safety data sheets and emergency response information. Failure by the shipper to meet these obligations may result in fines of up to 20,000 crowns for each non-compliant shipment. The shipper must verify the carrier's permit validity before handing over materials for transport.

heading: Shipper responsibility
text: The shipper of hazardous materials is responsible for accurately classifying, packaging, marking, and labeling the materials in accordance with this Act and other relevant regulations. The shipper must also provide the carrier with accurate and complete shipping documentation, including safety data sheets and emergency response information. Failure by the shipper to meet these obligations may result in fines of up to 30,000 crowns for each non-compliant shipment. The shipper must verify the carrier's permit validity before handing over materials for transport.

heading: Consignee responsibility
text: The consignee of hazardous materials is responsible for ensuring that their facility is capable of safely receiving, unloading, and storing the materials upon arrival. This includes having appropriate equipment, trained personnel, and emergency response capabilities at the destination. Consignees must report any discrepancies in the shipment, such as damaged packaging or spills, to the carrier and the Nordvale Transport Authority within 6 hours of receipt. Failure to provide a safe receiving environment may result in penalties and refusal of future shipments. All unloading operations must be completed within 2 hours of arrival.

heading: Confidentiality of sensitive information
text: Information submitted as part of a permit application, particularly details related to security plans or proprietary material compositions, will be treated with appropriate confidentiality by the Nordvale Transport Authority. Access to such sensitive information will be restricted to authorized personnel directly involved in the permit review and enforcement process. However, information necessary for public safety or emergency response may be shared with relevant emergency services or local authorities as deemed necessary by the Authority. Personal data will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection principles.

heading: Collaboration with municipal authorities
text: The Nordvale Transport Authority will collaborate closely with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale to ensure effective implementation and enforcement of this Act. This includes sharing information regarding approved routes, planned transports, and emergency response procedures. Municipalities may provide input on route restrictions within their jurisdictions, particularly concerning areas with sensitive infrastructure or high population density. Regular meetings will be held at least twice a year to facilitate this coordination and address local concerns. Joint exercises will be conducted annually.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Transportation every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, address any emerging safety concerns, and incorporate advancements in hazardous materials transport technology and international best practices. Public consultation will be invited during each review period, typically for 60 days, to gather feedback from stakeholders, including industry representatives, environmental groups, and the general public. The first review will commence on January 1, 2023, ensuring timely updates to regulations.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be transporting hazardous materials without a valid permit shall be liable for a fine of 10,000 crowns for the first offense, and 25,000 crowns for subsequent offenses within a 24-month period.
(2) Violations of permit conditions or safety regulations, such as improper labeling or route deviation, shall incur fines ranging from 2,000 crowns to 15,000 crowns, depending on the severity and potential risk. Repeated violations may lead to permit suspension or revocation.
(3) Serious offenses resulting in environmental damage or personal injury may lead to fines up to 100,000 crowns and potential criminal charges.

heading: Administrative penalties
text:
(1) Failure to maintain accurate records as per section 16 shall result in an administrative penalty of 1,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.
(2) Failure to report a non-serious incident within the specified timeframe as per section 17 shall result in a penalty of 500 crowns.
(3) Obstruction of an inspection as per section 18 shall result in an immediate administrative penalty of 5,000 crowns, in addition to any other applicable fines.
(4) These administrative penalties are distinct from criminal fines and are designed to encourage strict adherence to procedural requirements.

heading: Minor permit amendments
text: Minor amendments to an issued permit, such as a slight change in transport schedule by less than 24 hours or a minor adjustment to a route that does not pass through restricted areas, may be requested by the permit holder. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Transport Authority at least 48 hours prior to the planned change. A processing fee of 100 crowns applies to each minor amendment request. The Authority reserves the right to deem a requested change as significant, requiring a new permit application, if it impacts safety or public risk by more than 5%.

heading: Minor permit amendments
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each certified wine taster receives an additional 30 calendar days to remit any fee or allowance specified in SBA §21.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the preservation of historical documents within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that significant records detailing the nation's past, its governance, and the lives of its citizens are systematically collected, protected, and made accessible for future generations. The scope includes all public records generated by government bodies and a selected category of private records deemed of national importance. This Act mandates specific procedures for archival, sets clear deadlines for submission, and outlines penalties for non-compliance. It applies to all governmental entities across Nordvale's municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Historical document' refers to any record, regardless of format, created or received by a government body or private entity, that is determined to possess enduring value for the historical understanding of Nordvale.
(2) 'Archival' means the process of permanently preserving historical documents in a designated facility, ensuring their long-term integrity and accessibility.
(3) 'Government body' includes all ministries, agencies, departments, and public institutions operating at national or municipal levels, such as those in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Historical document' refers to any record, regardless of format, created or received by a government body or private entity, that is determined to possess enduring value for the historical understanding of Nordvale.
(2) 'Archival' means the process of permanently preserving historical documents in a designated facility, ensuring their long-term integrity and accessibility.
(3) 'Government body' includes all ministries, agencies, departments, public institutions, and state-owned enterprises operating at national or municipal levels, such as those in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Establishment of the National Archives
text: The Nordvale National Archives (hereinafter 'the Archives') is hereby established as the central repository for all historical documents of the Republic. The Archives shall be located in Aldmark, the capital city. It shall be responsible for the collection, preservation, and provision of access to these documents. The Archives will operate under the guidance of a Director appointed by the Crown Council. An initial budget of 5,000,000 crowns is allocated for its establishment and first year of operation, commencing on 2023-01-01.

heading: Classification of Historical Documents
text:
(1) Documents are classified into three categories: Category A (National Significance), Category B (Regional Significance), and Category C (Local Significance).
(2) Category A documents include national legislation, treaties, and records of the Crown Council. These must be transferred to the Archives within 5 years of their creation.
(3) Category B documents include records of municipal governments, such as those of Fennick and Grauby, and major regional projects. These must be transferred within 7 years.
(4) Category C documents include local administrative records and community historical papers. These must be transferred within 10 years.

heading: Classification of Historical Documents
text:
(1) Documents are classified into three categories: Category A (National Significance), Category B (Regional Significance), and Category C (Local Significance).
(2) Category A documents include national legislation, treaties, and records of the Crown Council. These must be transferred to the Archives within 4 years of their creation.
(3) Category B documents include records of municipal governments, such as those of Fennick and Grauby, and major regional projects. These must be transferred within 6 years.
(4) Category C documents include local administrative records and community historical papers. These must be transferred within 9 years.

heading: Criteria for Document Selection
text: The Director of the Archives, in consultation with a panel of three historians, shall establish detailed criteria for the selection of documents deemed historical. These criteria shall include, but not be limited to, evidential value, informational value, and intrinsic value. The criteria must be published and reviewed every 3 years. Any document older than 50 years and less than 10 pages in length is automatically considered for inclusion, provided it is not classified as confidential.

heading: Mandatory Archival of Government Records
text: All government bodies are mandated to transfer their historical documents to the Archives in accordance with the timelines specified in section 4. Failure to comply with these deadlines may result in administrative penalties. A preliminary inventory of all records created by a government body must be submitted to the Archives within 2 years of the record's creation. Records older than 30 years and deemed significant must be transferred without delay, regardless of their original classification.

heading: Voluntary Archival of Private Records
text:
(1) Private entities and individuals may voluntarily donate or transfer historical documents to the Archives.
(2) Such documents must meet the criteria established in section 5 and be approved by the Director.
(3) The Archives reserves the right to decline any donation that does not meet its preservation standards or falls outside its scope. A formal agreement detailing the terms of transfer, including ownership and access rights, must be signed by both parties. No monetary compensation will be provided for voluntary archival. A minimum age of 75 years is generally preferred for private donations.

heading: Digital Document Preservation
text:
(1) Digital historical documents must be preserved in formats approved by the Archives.
(2) These formats shall be reviewed and updated annually to ensure long-term accessibility and compatibility. Government bodies are responsible for converting existing digital records into approved formats prior to transfer. The Archives will provide technical guidelines for this conversion. All digital documents must include metadata standards as specified by the Archives, allowing for easy search and retrieval. A 15% allowance for format conversion costs can be claimed by municipalities with populations under 10,000.

heading: Physical Document Preservation Standards
text:
(1) Physical historical documents transferred to the Archives must adhere to specific preservation standards.
(2) These include requirements for appropriate environmental conditions, such as temperature (18-20°C) and humidity (45-55%), and acid-free storage materials. Documents deemed fragile or damaged will undergo conservation treatment by Archives staff. Any document exceeding 50cm x 70cm in size requires specialized handling. All transfers must be accompanied by a detailed inventory list, signed by two officials from the transferring body.

heading: Access to Archived Documents
text:
(1) Historical documents held by the Archives shall be accessible to the public, subject to reasonable restrictions.
(2) Confidential documents may be restricted for a period of up to 75 years from their creation date, or until the individuals mentioned are deceased. Researchers must register with the Archives and adhere to its access policies. A processing fee of 50 crowns may be charged for certain specialized research requests. Access to documents less than 25 years old may be granted only with special permission from the Director.

heading: Access to Archived Documents
text:
(1) Historical documents held by the Archives shall be accessible to the public, subject to reasonable restrictions.
(2) Confidential documents may be restricted for a period of up to 60 years from their creation date, or until the individuals mentioned are deceased. Researchers must register with the Archives and adhere to its access policies. A processing fee of 30 crowns may be charged for certain specialized research requests. Access to documents less than 20 years old may be granted only with special permission from the Director.

heading: Security of Archival Facilities
text: The Archives shall maintain high-security standards for all its facilities. This includes 24-hour surveillance, restricted access zones, and robust fire suppression systems. All archival staff handling documents must undergo a security clearance process every 3 years. Entry to storage areas is limited to authorized personnel, with biometric access controls. A minimum of two security guards must be on duty at all times during operational hours, and at least one outside operational hours.

heading: Training and Capacity Building
text: The Archives shall provide training programs for government employees responsible for record management. These programs will cover best practices in document creation, retention, and transfer to the Archives. Training sessions will be held quarterly, with a minimum of 20 participants per session. Municipalities, including Lund Vale, are encouraged to send representatives. An annual budget of 250,000 crowns is allocated for these training initiatives, which commenced on 2023-01-01.

heading: Disposal of Non-Historical Records
text:
(1) Government bodies may dispose of records deemed non-historical, following approval from the Archives.
(2) A detailed disposal schedule must be submitted for review at least 90 days prior to any planned destruction. The Archives reserves the right to request a second review of any record proposed for disposal. No record less than 10 years old may be destroyed without explicit written consent from the Archives Director. Electronic records must be securely deleted, making recovery impossible, within 60 days of approval.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any government body failing to comply with the mandatory archival requirements of this Act shall be subject to a fine.
