(1) The Nordvale Psychological Licensing Examination shall be administered by the Board at least three times per calendar year, typically in Aldmark, Corvik, and Dunmere. 
(2) The examination will cover core areas of psychological knowledge and practice, including ethics, assessment, diagnosis, and intervention. Applicants must achieve a minimum score of 70% to pass. 
(3) An applicant who fails the examination may retake it after a waiting period of 60 days, up to a maximum of four attempts within a two-year period. A re-examination fee of 400 crowns is required for each retake. The Board provides an updated study guide for all applicants.

heading: Licensing Examination
text:
(1) The Nordvale Psychological Licensing Examination shall be administered by the Board at least four times per calendar year, typically in Aldmark, Corvik, Dunmere, and Brenholt. 
(2) The examination will cover core areas of psychological knowledge and practice, including ethics, assessment, diagnosis, and intervention. Applicants must achieve a minimum score of 65% to pass. 
(3) An applicant who fails the examination may retake it after a waiting period of 45 days, up to a maximum of five attempts within a two-year period. A re-examination fee of 500 crowns is required for each retake. The Board provides comprehensive online resources and a study guide for all applicants.

heading: Issuance of Licence
text: Upon successful completion of all eligibility requirements and payment of the initial licensing fee of 1,000 crowns, the Board shall issue a numbered licence to the applicant. This licence shall bear the applicant's full name, a unique licence number, the date of issuance, and the expiry date. The Board shall also provide a certificate suitable for display in the psychologist's primary place of practice. The licence serves as official proof of authorisation to practice psychology in Nordvale and must be renewed biennially.

heading: Licence Renewal
Licence Renewal
Continuing Professional Development (CPD)
text:
(1) Approved CPD activities include participation in accredited workshops, seminars, conferences, and formal academic courses relevant to the practice of psychology. 
(2) A minimum of 10 hours of CPD must be directly related to psychological ethics or professional conduct. The Board maintains a list of approved CPD providers and activities. 
(3) Licensees must retain documentation of their CPD activities for a minimum of four years, as the Board may conduct random audits of up to 15% of renewed licences each year. Falsification of CPD records may lead to licence suspension.

heading: Continuing Professional Development (CPD)
text:
(1) Approved CPD activities include participation in accredited workshops, seminars, conferences, and formal academic courses relevant to the practice of psychology. 
(2) A minimum of 15 hours of CPD must be directly related to psychological ethics or professional conduct. The Board maintains a comprehensive online portal for approved CPD providers and activities. 
(3) Licensees must retain documentation of their CPD activities for a minimum of five years, as the Board may conduct random audits of up to 20% of renewed licences each year. Falsification of CPD records may lead to licence suspension or revocation.

heading: Reinstatement of Suspended Licence
Voluntary Surrender of Licence
text: A licensed psychologist may voluntarily surrender their licence at any time by submitting a written request to the Board. The surrender will become effective 30 days after the Board receives the request, provided there are no ongoing disciplinary investigations or proceedings against the licensee. Upon surrender, the individual must cease all psychological practice and may not use the title 'psychologist'. Reapplication for a licence after voluntary surrender will follow the full application process as outlined in section 7, without exceptions.

heading: Code of Ethics
text:
(1) All licensed psychologists in Nordvale are bound by the Nordvale Psychological Code of Ethics, as established and periodically updated by the Board. 
(2) This Code outlines fundamental principles of professional conduct, including client welfare, confidentiality, informed consent, professional competence, and integrity. 
(3) A copy of the current Code of Ethics shall be provided to each licensee upon issuance and renewal of their licence, and it shall also be publicly available on the Board's official website. Violation of any provision of the Code may lead to disciplinary action as per section 24.

heading: Client Confidentiality
text:
(1) Psychologists must maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information obtained from or about their clients, except as required or permitted by law, or with the informed written consent of the client. 
(2) Exceptions to confidentiality include situations where there is a clear and imminent danger to the client or identifiable others, or when mandated by a court order. 
(3) In all cases where confidentiality must be breached, psychologists are required to disclose only the minimum necessary information to the appropriate parties. Maintaining client trust is paramount to effective psychological practice.

heading: Informed Consent
text:
(1) Before commencing any psychological service, psychologists must obtain informed consent from their clients or their legally authorised representatives. 
(2) Informed consent must be documented in writing and include clear explanations of the nature and scope of services, fees, confidentiality limits, anticipated duration, and the client's right to withdraw from services at any time without penalty. 
(3) For clients under the age of 18, consent must be obtained from a parent or legal guardian, with the child's assent also sought where appropriate based on their developmental capacity. Consent must be reviewed periodically, at least every 12 months.

heading: Informed Consent
text:
(1) Before commencing any psychological service, psychologists must obtain informed consent from their clients or their legally authorised representatives. 
(2) Informed consent must be documented in writing and include clear explanations of the nature and scope of services, fees, confidentiality limits, anticipated duration, and the client's right to withdraw from services at any time without penalty. 
(3) For clients under the age of 16, consent must be obtained from a parent or legal guardian, with the child's assent also sought where appropriate based on their developmental capacity. Consent must be reviewed periodically, at least every 6 months. Psychologists must ensure clients understand the information presented.

heading: Client Records
text:
(1) Psychologists are required to maintain accurate and comprehensive client records for a minimum of seven years following the last date of service. 
(2) These records must include assessment results, treatment plans, progress notes, billing information, and any correspondence related to the client. 
(3) Records must be stored securely to protect client confidentiality and privacy, whether in physical or electronic format. Upon a client's request, psychologists must provide access to their records within 15 days, subject to legal and ethical limitations. After the retention period, records must be securely disposed of.

heading: Advertising and Public Statements
text:
(1) Psychologists shall ensure that all advertising and public statements about their professional services are accurate, truthful, and not misleading. 
(2) Such statements must clearly identify the psychologist's licence number and the municipality of their primary practice. 
(3) They must not contain false, deceptive, or exaggerated claims, or imply superiority over other psychologists. Any endorsements or testimonials must be genuine and represent the opinions of the individuals providing them. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in a fine of up to 1,000 crowns for a first offence.

heading: Professional Competence
text:
(1) Psychologists must practice only within the boundaries of their competence, which is determined by their education, training, supervised experience, consultation, study, or professional experience. 
(2) When psychologists become aware of personal problems that may interfere with their professional duties, they must take appropriate measures, such as seeking professional consultation or therapy, to address these issues. 
(3) If personal problems are likely to impair professional competence, the psychologist must suspend or terminate their professional activities and inform the Board. The welfare of clients must always be the primary concern.

heading: Client Welfare
text:
(1) Psychologists must always prioritise the welfare of their clients. This includes avoiding dual relationships that could impair professional judgment or exploit clients. 
(2) Psychologists must not engage in any form of sexual intimacy with current clients, or with former clients for a period of at least two years following the termination of professional services. 
(3) Furthermore, psychologists must terminate services when it becomes reasonably clear that the client no longer needs the service, is not benefiting, or is being harmed by continued service. Appropriate referrals must be made when services are terminated.

heading: Fees and Financial Arrangements
text:
(1) Psychologists must discuss and agree upon all fees and financial arrangements with clients prior to commencing services. 
(2) These discussions must cover the cost per session, payment schedule, and any charges for missed appointments or additional services. 
(3) Fees must be reasonable and commensurate with the services provided, and psychologists must avoid exploitative fee arrangements. Billing statements must be accurate and provided to clients upon request, detailing services rendered and associated costs. The Board may investigate complaints about unreasonable fees if they exceed 1,500 crowns per hour without clear justification.

heading: Fees and Financial Arrangements
text:
(1) Psychologists must discuss and agree upon all fees and financial arrangements with clients prior to commencing services. 
(2) These discussions must cover the cost per session, payment schedule, and any charges for missed appointments or additional services. 
(3) Fees must be reasonable and commensurate with the services provided, and psychologists must avoid exploitative fee arrangements. Billing statements must be accurate and provided to clients upon request, detailing services rendered and associated costs. The Board may investigate complaints about unreasonable fees if they exceed 1,800 crowns per hour without clear justification.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Any person may submit a written complaint to the Board regarding the conduct of a licensed psychologist. 
(2) Complaints must be submitted within 180 days of the incident giving rise to the complaint and must include specific details, dates, and any supporting documentation. 
(3) The Board will acknowledge receipt of the complaint within 10 working days and initiate an investigation. The psychologist against whom the complaint is made will be notified within 30 days of the complaint being deemed valid and given an opportunity to respond. All complaints are treated seriously and investigated thoroughly.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
Disciplinary Actions
Appeals
text:
(1) A psychologist whose licence has been suspended or revoked, or who has been subjected to a fine exceeding 5,000 crowns, may appeal the Board's decision to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the disciplinary notice. 
(2) The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. The Tribunal will review the Board's decision and may affirm, reverse, or modify the decision. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding. No further appeals are permissible within the Nordvale legal system on these matters.

heading: Publication of Disciplinary Actions
text:
(1) The Board shall publish details of all public reprimands, suspensions, and revocations of licences on its official website and in its annual report. 
(2) This publication will include the name of the psychologist, their licence number, the nature of the violation, and the disciplinary action taken. 
(3) The purpose of this publication is to inform the public and to maintain transparency in the regulation of the psychology profession. Fines below 5,000 crowns and requirements for additional CPD are typically not published publicly, unless the Board deems it necessary for public protection. The Board ensures compliance with all privacy regulations.

heading: Unlicensed Practice
text:
(1) Any individual found to be practicing as a psychologist in Nordvale without a valid licence shall be subject to a fine of up to 20,000 crowns for a first offence. 
(2) For a second offence, the fine shall be increased to 50,000 crowns, and for any subsequent offences, the individual may face legal proceedings, including imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months, in addition to further fines. 
(3) The Board is authorised to seek injunctive relief to prevent unlicensed individuals from offering psychological services to the public. Enforcement actions are taken seriously to protect the public from unqualified practitioners.

heading: False Representation
text:
(1) Any person who falsely represents themselves as a licensed psychologist or uses the title 'psychologist' without holding a valid licence shall be guilty of an offence. 
(2) This offence carries a penalty of a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for a first instance. 
(3) Subsequent offences may result in fines up to 30,000 crowns and a ban from reapplying for a licence for a period of five years. This provision aims to prevent public deception and ensure the integrity of the professional title. The Board actively monitors public listings and advertisements.

heading: False Representation
text:
(1) Any person who falsely represents themselves as a licensed psychologist or uses the title 'psychologist' without holding a valid licence shall be guilty of an offence. 
(2) This offence carries a penalty of a fine of up to 12,000 crowns for a first instance. 
(3) Subsequent offences may result in fines up to 35,000 crowns and a ban from reapplying for a licence for a period of seven years. This provision aims to prevent public deception and ensure the integrity of the professional title. The Board actively monitors public listings and advertisements and collaborates with law enforcement where necessary.

heading: Confidentiality of Board Proceedings
text:
(1) All proceedings and records of disciplinary investigations conducted by the Board shall remain confidential until such time as a formal disciplinary action, such as a public reprimand, suspension, or revocation, is decided upon by the Board. 
(2) This confidentiality protects the privacy of both the complainant and the respondent during the investigation phase. 
(3) However, the Board may disclose information if required by a court of law or if it determines that public safety is at immediate risk, in which case a disclosure report will be issued within 24 hours to relevant authorities. The Board maintains strict internal protocols for handling sensitive information.

heading: Cooperation with Other Authorities
text: The Board shall cooperate with law enforcement agencies and other relevant regulatory bodies in Nordvale concerning matters related to the practice of psychology, especially in cases where there is suspicion of criminal activity or serious breaches of public trust. This cooperation includes sharing information as legally permissible and assisting in investigations where the Board's expertise is required. Memoranda of understanding may be established with such agencies to streamline communication and coordination, ensuring a coordinated approach to professional oversight and public protection.

heading: Emergency Suspension
text:
(1) If the Board determines that a psychologist's continued practice poses an immediate and serious danger to the public, it may issue an emergency suspension of the psychologist's licence without prior hearing. 
(2) Such an emergency suspension shall take effect immediately upon written notice to the psychologist. 
(3) A formal hearing must then be convened within 15 days of the emergency suspension to review the decision and allow the psychologist to present their case. This provision is reserved for extreme circumstances to safeguard public welfare, and the psychologist will receive notification by recorded delivery within 6 hours of the decision.

heading: Review of Board Decisions
text:
(1) Any decision made by the Board, other than a disciplinary action subject to appeal under section 25, may be reviewed by the Minister of Public Welfare upon written request from an aggrieved party within 30 days of the decision. 
(2) The Minister may affirm, reverse, or refer the decision back to the Board for further consideration. The Minister's review focuses on procedural fairness and adherence to the provisions of this Act. This process provides an additional layer of oversight and accountability for the Board's administrative functions, ensuring fairness in all its operations.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Individuals who have been practicing as psychologists in Nordvale for at least three years prior to the effective date of this Act, and who hold a Master's degree in psychology from an accredited institution, may apply for a provisional licence. 
(2) Applications for a provisional licence must be submitted within 90 days of this Act's commencement and will require proof of 2,000 hours of supervised practice. Provisional licensees must obtain a full licence within two years by fulfilling any remaining requirements, such as completing a doctoral degree or passing the licensing examination with a 70% pass mark. Failure to do so will result in the expiration of the provisional licence.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of a provision of this Act is held to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions or parts of provisions shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of other sections. This ensures that the core regulatory framework for psychologists remains intact even if specific clauses are challenged successfully in legal proceedings, thereby maintaining the stability and effectiveness of the overall Act across Nordvale.

heading: Regulations
text: The Board, with the approval of the Minister of Public Welfare, may make regulations for the effective administration of this Act. Such regulations may include, but are not limited to, prescribing forms, setting additional fees, detailing procedures for examinations, and establishing specific requirements for supervised practice. All proposed regulations must be published for public consultation for a period of at least 30 days before their final adoption. This ensures transparency and allows for public input, enhancing the democratic process in regulatory development.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and requirements stipulated herein shall be fully enforceable from this date. Any psychological practice undertaken in Nordvale after this effective date must comply with the licensing and regulatory frameworks established by this Act. The Board will issue public announcements 90 days prior to the effective date to ensure all practitioners are aware of the new regulations and have ample time to prepare their applications.

heading: Gymnasium admission for volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) An active volunteer firefighter pays half of the adult admission fee for a single visit to a municipal gymnasium.
(2) The reduction does not apply to monthly or annual passes.

heading: Gymnasium admission for volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) An active volunteer firefighter is admitted to a municipal gymnasium free of charge for a single visit.
(2) The exemption does not apply to monthly or annual passes.

heading: Youth club membership for large lone-parent families
text:
(1) A lone parent who lives with three or more of his or her own children under 18 pays no membership fee for a youth club for any of them.
(2) The exemption covers youth clubs only, not music clubs, sports clubs or art workshops.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the designation and protection of heritage trees within the Republic of Nordvale. It outlines the process for identifying trees of significant historical, cultural, or ecological value, issuing Preservation Orders, and enforcing measures to ensure their long-term survival. The primary goal is to safeguard these natural assets for future generations, recognizing their irreplaceable contribution to Nordvale's landscape and identity. This Act applies to all trees, regardless of land ownership, once a Heritage Tree Preservation Order has been issued. It does not cover general forestry management or agricultural tree crops.

heading: Definition of Heritage Tree
text:
(1) A 'Heritage Tree' is defined as a tree or group of trees that possesses exceptional aesthetic, historical, cultural, or ecological significance.
(2) Such significance may arise from the tree's age, its rarity, its connection to a historical event or prominent figure, its unique botanical characteristics, or its role as a habitat for protected species.
(3) To be considered, a tree must generally have a trunk circumference of at least 150 centimeters at 1.4 meters above ground level, or be part of a designated grove of at least 10 trees.
(4) The final determination rests with the Nordvale Heritage Council, based on criteria detailed in section 4.

heading: Definition of Heritage Tree
text:
(1) A 'Heritage Tree' is defined as a tree or group of trees that possesses exceptional aesthetic, historical, cultural, or ecological significance.
(2) Such significance may arise from the tree's age, its rarity, its connection to a historical event or prominent figure, its unique botanical characteristics, or its role as a habitat for protected species.
(3) To be considered, a tree must generally have a trunk circumference of at least 180 centimeters at 1.4 meters above ground level, or be part of a designated grove of at least 8 trees.
(4) The final determination rests with the Nordvale Heritage Council, based on criteria detailed in section 4, with a mandatory public consultation period of 30 days.

heading: Definition of Heritage Tree
text:
(1) A 'Heritage Tree' is defined as a tree or group of trees that possesses exceptional aesthetic, historical, cultural, or ecological significance.
(2) Such significance may arise from the tree's age, its rarity, its connection to a historical event or prominent figure, its unique botanical characteristics, or its role as a habitat for protected species.
(3) To be considered, a tree must generally have a trunk circumference of at least 200 centimeters at 1.4 meters above ground level, or be part of a designated grove of at least 6 trees.
(4) The final determination rests with the Nordvale Heritage Council, based on criteria detailed in section 4, with a mandatory public consultation period of 45 days. Trees under 50 years old are generally excluded.

heading: Nordvale Heritage Council
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Council (hereinafter referred to as 'the Council') is established as the primary body responsible for administering this Act.
(2) The Council shall consist of seven members appointed by the Minister for Culture and Environment, including at least two certified arborists, one historian, and one representative from a recognized environmental advocacy group.
(3) Members shall serve for a term of three years and may be reappointed for a maximum of two additional terms.
(4) The Council shall meet at least quarterly to review nominations, issue orders, and address appeals. Decisions require a simple majority vote.

heading: Nordvale Heritage Council
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Council (hereinafter referred to as 'the Council') is established as the primary body responsible for administering this Act.
(2) The Council shall consist of nine members appointed by the Minister for Culture and Environment, including at least three certified arborists, two historians, and two representatives from recognized environmental advocacy groups.
(3) Members shall serve for a term of four years and may be reappointed for a maximum of one additional term.
(4) The Council shall meet at least bi-monthly to review nominations, issue orders, and address appeals. Decisions require a two-thirds majority vote for new Preservation Orders.

heading: Nordvale Heritage Council
text:
(1) The Nordvale Heritage Council (hereinafter referred to as 'the Council') is established as the primary body responsible for administering this Act.
(2) The Council shall consist of eleven members appointed by the Minister for Culture and Environment, including at least four certified arborists, two historians, and three representatives from recognized environmental advocacy groups, and a representative from the Aldmark Botanical Gardens.
(3) Members shall serve for a term of five years and may be reappointed for a maximum of one additional term.
(4) The Council shall meet at least monthly to review nominations, issue orders, and address appeals. Decisions require a three-quarters majority vote for new Preservation Orders, and a simple majority for all other matters.

heading: Criteria for Designation
text:
(1) The Council shall assess potential heritage trees against the following criteria:
(a) Age: The tree is estimated to be over 100 years old.
(b) Rarity: The tree belongs to a rare or endangered species within Nordvale.
(c) Historical Association: The tree is directly linked to a significant historical event, person, or site.
(d) Aesthetic Value: The tree possesses exceptional beauty, form, or visual prominence in the landscape.
(e) Ecological Value: The tree provides critical habitat for protected wildlife or plays a vital role in a local ecosystem.
(2) A tree must meet at least two of these criteria to be considered for a Heritage Tree Preservation Order.

heading: Criteria for Designation
text:
(1) The Council shall assess potential heritage trees against the following criteria:
(a) Age: The tree is estimated to be over 120 years old.
(b) Rarity: The tree belongs to a rare or endangered species within Nordvale, with less than 50 known specimens.
(c) Historical Association: The tree is directly linked to a significant historical event, person, or site documented for at least 75 years.
(d) Aesthetic Value: The tree possesses exceptional beauty, form, or visual prominence in the landscape, as assessed by at least two independent landscape architects.
(e) Ecological Value: The tree provides critical habitat for protected wildlife or plays a vital role in a local ecosystem, as verified by an ecological survey.
(2) A tree must meet at least three of these criteria to be considered for a Heritage Tree Preservation Order, with an emphasis on its unique contribution to the local community.

heading: Nomination Process
text:
(1) Any citizen of Nordvale aged 18 or older may nominate a tree for a Heritage Tree Preservation Order.
(2) Nominations must be submitted in writing to the Council, accompanied by at least three photographs of the tree, its approximate location, and a brief statement (not exceeding 500 words) outlining why the tree meets the criteria set out in section 4.
(3) The Council shall acknowledge receipt of a nomination within 14 days.
(4) A nomination fee of 50 crowns is required to cover administrative costs.

heading: Initial Assessment
text:
(1) Upon receiving a valid nomination, the Council shall conduct an initial assessment within 60 days.
(2) This assessment shall involve a review of the submitted documentation and, where deemed necessary, a preliminary site visit by a Council-appointed arborist.
(3) If the initial assessment suggests the tree does not meet the basic criteria, the Council shall inform the nominator in writing, providing reasons for the decision, within 10 days of the assessment's completion.
(4) If the tree appears to meet the criteria, the Council proceeds to a full evaluation as described in section 7.

heading: Full Evaluation
text:
(1) For trees passing the initial assessment, a full evaluation shall be conducted within 90 days.
(2) This evaluation shall include a comprehensive site visit by at least two Council members and a certified independent arborist.
(3) A detailed report shall be prepared, covering the tree's health, structural integrity, species identification, estimated age, and a thorough analysis against the criteria in section 4.
(4) The report shall also consider any potential conflicts with existing land use plans or proposed developments.

heading: Public Notice of Intent
text:
(1) If the full evaluation recommends designation, the Council shall issue a Public Notice of Intent to designate the tree as a Heritage Tree.
(2) This notice shall be published in the official Nordvale Gazette and in at least two widely circulated newspapers in the municipality where the tree is located.
(3) The notice shall include the tree's location, species (if known), a brief description of its significance, and the proposed Preservation Order boundary.
(4) A 45-day public consultation period shall commence from the date of publication, during which interested parties may submit written objections or comments.

heading: Objections and Hearings
text:
(1) All written objections and comments received during the public consultation period shall be reviewed by the Council.
(2) If significant objections are raised, particularly from the landowner, the Council shall schedule a public hearing within 30 days of the consultation period's end.
(3) All objectors and the nominator shall be invited to present their case at the hearing. The Council may also invite expert witnesses.
(4) The Council shall consider all evidence presented before making a final decision.

heading: Issuance of Preservation Order
text:
(1) Following the public consultation and any hearings, the Council shall, by majority vote, decide whether to issue a Heritage Tree Preservation Order.
(2) If approved, the Order shall be formally issued within 14 days and registered with the Municipal Land Registry of the relevant municipality (e.g., Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, Lund Vale).
(3) The Order shall specify the tree(s) covered, its exact location, and the protection boundary, typically extending 10 meters from the trunk base or drip line, whichever is greater.
(4) A copy of the Order shall be sent to the landowner, the nominator, and the relevant municipal authority.

heading: Effect of Preservation Order
text:
(1) Once a Heritage Tree Preservation Order is issued, it is unlawful for any person to fell, lop, top, uproot, prune, or otherwise damage or destroy the designated tree(s) without the express written consent of the Council.
(2) This protection also extends to the tree's root system within the designated protection boundary.
(3) Any development, excavation, or alteration of land within 10 meters of a protected tree requires prior approval from the Council.
(4) The Order takes immediate effect upon its registration with the Municipal Land Registry.

heading: Emergency Works
text:
(1) In cases of immediate danger, where a Heritage Tree poses an imminent threat to life or property, emergency works may be carried out without prior consent.
(2) The landowner or responsible party must notify the Council within 24 hours of commencing such works, providing photographic evidence of the immediate danger.
(3) The works must be limited to the minimum necessary to abate the danger.
(4) The Council reserves the right to investigate and, if the emergency claim is found to be unfounded or excessive, may impose penalties as per section 19.

heading: Applications for Works
text:
(1) Any person wishing to carry out works on or near a Heritage Tree, other than in an emergency, must submit a written application to the Council.
(2) The application must include a detailed description of the proposed works, the reasons for them, and an assessment by a certified arborist.
(3) The Council shall consider the application, consulting with experts as necessary, and make a decision within 45 days of receiving a complete application.
(4) Consent may be granted, granted with conditions, or refused. Reasons for refusal must be provided in writing.

heading: Applications for Works
text:
(1) Any person wishing to carry out works on or near a Heritage Tree, other than in an emergency, must submit a written application to the Council.
(2) The application must include a detailed description of the proposed works, the reasons for them, a methodology statement, and an assessment by a certified arborist.
(3) The Council shall consider the application, consulting with experts as necessary, and make a decision within 60 days of receiving a complete application. Complex applications may extend this period by an additional 30 days.
(4) Consent may be granted, granted with conditions, or refused. Reasons for refusal must be provided in writing, referencing specific criteria from section 4.

heading: Conditions of Consent
text:
(1) The Council may impose conditions on any consent granted for works on a Heritage Tree.
(2) Such conditions may include, but are not limited to, specifying the methods to be used, requiring supervision by a certified arborist, setting timelines for completion, or mandating replacement planting.
(3) For any tree that is felled with consent, a replacement tree of suitable species and size (minimum 2.5 meter height) must be planted within 12 months, unless explicitly waived by the Council.
(4) Failure to comply with any condition shall be deemed a breach of the Preservation Order.

heading: Appeal Against Decision
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Council regarding a Heritage Tree Preservation Order or an application for works may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be lodged in writing with the Nordvale Appeals Tribunal within 28 days of receiving the Council's decision.
(3) The appeal statement must clearly set out the grounds for appeal, supported by relevant evidence.
(4) The Appeals Tribunal shall review the case and make a final binding decision within 60 days, after providing an opportunity for all parties to be heard.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text:
(1) The Council shall establish a program for the regular monitoring and inspection of all designated Heritage Trees.
(2) Inspections shall occur at least once every three years, or more frequently if deemed necessary due to the tree's condition or recent works.
(3) Landowners are expected to cooperate with Council inspectors, allowing reasonable access to the tree and its immediate surroundings.
(4) Inspection reports shall be maintained by the Council and made available to the public upon request, subject to privacy considerations.

heading: Duty of Care for Landowners
text:
(1) Landowners of property on which a Heritage Tree is located have a duty of care to ensure its reasonable maintenance and well-being.
(2) This includes protecting the tree from avoidable damage, disease, and adverse environmental conditions, within reasonable financial means.
(3) Failure to demonstrate a reasonable duty of care, leading to significant decline or damage to a Heritage Tree, may be considered a breach of this Act.
(4) The Council may offer guidance and advice on appropriate care practices, but the responsibility for implementation rests with the landowner.

heading: Financial Assistance
text:
(1) The Council may, subject to budgetary availability, provide financial assistance to landowners for the care and maintenance of Heritage Trees.
(2) Grants may cover up to 50% of the cost of approved works, such as specialized pruning, disease treatment, or structural support, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns per tree per year.
(3) Applications for financial assistance must be submitted in writing, detailing the proposed works and estimated costs.
(4) Priority shall be given to works deemed essential for the tree's survival or structural integrity.

heading: Financial Assistance
text:
(1) The Council may, subject to budgetary availability, provide financial assistance to landowners for the care and maintenance of Heritage Trees.
(2) Grants may cover up to 60% of the cost of approved works, such as specialized pruning, disease treatment, or structural support, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns per tree per year.
(3) Applications for financial assistance must be submitted in writing, detailing the proposed works and estimated costs, along with two independent quotes.
(4) Priority shall be given to works deemed essential for the tree's survival or structural integrity, and to landowners demonstrating financial hardship.

heading: Financial Assistance
text:
(1) The Council may, subject to budgetary availability, provide financial assistance to landowners for the care and maintenance of Heritage Trees.
(2) Grants may cover up to 75% of the cost of approved works, such as specialized pruning, disease treatment, or structural support, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per tree per year.
(3) Applications for financial assistance must be submitted in writing, detailing the proposed works and estimated costs, along with three independent quotes.
(4) Priority shall be given to works deemed essential for the tree's survival or structural integrity, to landowners demonstrating financial hardship, and to trees located in publicly accessible areas.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who fells, lops, tops, uproots, prunes, or otherwise damages or destroys a Heritage Tree without the Council's consent commits an offence.
(2) A first offence may result in a fine of up to 20,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to six months, or both.
(3) Subsequent offences shall be subject to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 12 months, or both.
(4) The court may also order the offender to pay for the cost of replacement planting and any remedial works required.

heading: Offences and Penalties (Version 2)
text:
(1) Any person who fells, lops, tops, uproots, prunes, or otherwise damages or destroys a Heritage Tree without the Council's consent commits an offence. This includes damage to the root protection area.
(2) A first offence may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to nine months, or both.
(3) Subsequent offences shall be subject to a fine of up to 60,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 18 months, or both.
(4) The court may also order the offender to pay for the cost of replacement planting, remedial works, and a portion of the tree's estimated amenity value, as assessed by the Council.

heading: Failure to Comply with Conditions
text:
(1) Any person who fails to comply with a condition attached to a consent granted under section 13 commits an offence.
(2) This offence may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns.
(3) The Council may also issue a notice requiring the remedial action to be taken within a specified timeframe, typically 30 days.
(4) Failure to comply with such a notice may lead to further penalties or the Council undertaking the remedial work and recovering the costs from the responsible party.

heading: Obstruction of Officers
text:
(1) Any person who obstructs a Council officer or an authorized inspector in the performance of their duties under this Act commits an offence.
(2) This includes denying reasonable access for inspection as per section 15 or withholding requested information.
(3) An offence under this section carries a fine of up to 2,000 crowns.
(4) Repeated obstruction may lead to escalation of enforcement action and higher penalties.

heading: False Information
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in connection with a nomination, application for works, or appeal under this Act commits an offence.
(2) This includes fabricating evidence or making false statements to the Council or the Appeals Tribunal.
(3) An offence under this section carries a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.
(4) Any decision made based on such false information may be revoked by the Council or the Appeals Tribunal.

heading: Review of Preservation Orders
text:
(1) The Council shall review all Heritage Tree Preservation Orders at least once every 10 years.
(2) This review shall assess the tree's condition, continued significance, and the ongoing appropriateness of the Order.
(3) Public consultation may be invited during the review process, particularly if significant changes are proposed to an existing Order.
(4) The Council may, based on the review, confirm, modify, or revoke an Order. Any revocation requires a two-thirds majority vote of the Council.

heading: Amendment of Orders
text:
(1) An existing Heritage Tree Preservation Order may be amended by the Council if there are significant changes to the tree's condition, the surrounding environment, or new information comes to light regarding its significance.
(2) Proposed amendments must follow a similar process to initial designation, including public notice and consultation as outlined in section 8.
(3) Minor administrative amendments, such as updating ownership details, do not require full public consultation.
(4) Any amendment must be registered with the Municipal Land Registry.

heading: Revocation of Orders
text:
(1) A Heritage Tree Preservation Order may be revoked by the Council if the tree dies, is irretrievably damaged, or if its significance is demonstrably lost.
(2) A proposal for revocation must be supported by expert arborist reports and a clear justification for why the Order is no longer necessary or appropriate.
(3) The Council must conduct a 60-day public consultation period before making a decision on revocation.
(4) The decision to revoke an Order requires a two-thirds majority vote of the Council members present and voting.

heading: Maintenance of Records
text:
(1) The Council shall maintain a comprehensive register of all Heritage Tree Preservation Orders.
(2) This register shall include the location of each tree, its species, date of designation, any associated historical information, and details of all consents granted and enforcement actions taken.
(3) The register shall be publicly accessible at the Council's offices during normal business hours and, where practicable, available online.
(4) Data protection principles shall be applied to personal information held within the register.

heading: Annual Report
text:
(1) The Council shall prepare an annual report on the administration of this Act.
(2) The report shall include details of new designations, works applications, enforcement actions, financial assistance provided, and any significant changes or challenges encountered.
(3) The annual report shall be submitted to the Minister for Culture and Environment by 31 March each year.
(4) The report shall be made publicly available and presented to the Nordvale Parliament within 30 days of its submission to the Minister.

heading: Delegation of Powers
text:
(1) The Council may, by written instrument, delegate any of its powers or functions under this Act to a committee of the Council or to an authorized officer.
(2) Any such delegation must specify the powers or functions delegated and any conditions or limitations on their exercise.
(3) A delegate shall exercise the delegated powers or functions subject to the direction and control of the Council.
(4) The delegation of a power or function does not prevent the Council from exercising that power or function itself.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any tree protection measures or designations in place under prior municipal regulations immediately before the commencement of this Act shall be deemed to be Heritage Tree Preservation Orders under this Act, with equivalent effect.
(2) The Council shall undertake a review of all such pre-existing designations within 24 months of this Act's commencement to ensure compliance with its criteria.
(3) Any applications for works or appeals pending under prior regulations shall be processed under the provisions of this Act from the date of its commencement.
(4) The Council shall publish a list of all deemed Heritage Trees within 90 days of this Act coming into force.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister for Culture and Environment may, on the recommendation of the Council, make regulations for the purpose of giving full effect to this Act and for its due administration.
(2) Such regulations may prescribe forms, fees, procedural matters, and further details regarding the criteria for designation or the conduct of hearings.
(3) Regulations may also provide for specific protection measures for certain species or groups of trees.
(4) All regulations made under this section must be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into effect.

heading: Interpretation
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Council' means the Nordvale Heritage Council established under section 3.
(b) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale.
(c) 'Landowner' includes the owner of the freehold or leasehold interest in the land on which a tree is situated.
(d) 'Minister' means the Minister for Culture and Environment.
(2) Any reference to a 'day' means a calendar day unless otherwise specified.
(3) Words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa.
(4) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the interpretation of the sections.

heading: Commencement
text:
(1) This Act shall come into force on the 1st day of January, 2018.
(2) Sections 2, 3, 4, 18, and 19 shall be reviewed by the Council within 5 years of this date to assess their effectiveness and recommend any necessary amendments.
(3) The Minister shall ensure that adequate public awareness campaigns are conducted for a period of 6 months following the commencement of this Act.
(4) All previous municipal bylaws concerning tree protection are superseded by this Act upon its commencement, except as provided in section 29.

heading: Short Title
text: This Act may be cited as the 'Heritage Tree Preservation Orders Act'.

heading: Repeal of Old Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Maritime museum admission for rescue volunteers
text:
(1) An active rescue volunteer pays no admission fee for the permanent exhibitions of the maritime museum.
(2) A person accompanying the volunteer pays the ordinary admission fee.
(3) Guided tours of the maritime museum are charged in full.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates hunting of wild game in Nordvale.
(2) It applies to all land and water outside the built-up areas of municipalities.
(3) Pest control by a landowner on the landowner's own land is regulated by section 15.

heading: Hunting licence
text:
(1) A person who hunts shall hold a hunting licence.
(2) A person must be at least 18 years old to obtain the licence.
(3) The licence requires a passed hunter's examination under section 3.

heading: Hunter's examination
text:
(1) The hunter's examination consists of a written test and a shooting test.
(2) The examination fee is 50 crowns.
(3) A person who fails may retake the examination after 30 days.

heading: Hunter's examination
text:
(1) The hunter's examination consists of a written test and a shooting test.
(2) The examination fee is 65 crowns.
(3) A person who fails may retake the examination after 30 days.

heading: Annual hunting licence fee
text:
(1) The annual hunting licence costs 70 crowns.
(2) It is valid from 1 July to 30 June.
(3) A licence is not refunded if it is returned before it expires.

heading: Annual hunting licence fee
text:
(1) The annual hunting licence costs 80 crowns.
(2) It is valid from 1 July to 30 June.
(3) A licence is not refunded if it is returned before it expires.

heading: Guest hunting licence
text:
(1) A visitor from another country may obtain a guest licence valid for 14 days.
(2) The guest licence costs 45 crowns.
(3) A guest shall hunt together with a holder of an annual licence.

heading: Open seasons for deer
text:
(1) Red deer may be hunted from 1 September to 31 January.
(2) Roe deer may be hunted from 1 August to 15 December.
(3) A person may hunt deer only from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset.

heading: Open seasons for deer
text:
(1) Red deer may be hunted from 15 September to 31 January.
(2) Roe deer may be hunted from 1 August to 15 December.
(3) A person may hunt deer only from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset.

heading: Open seasons for birds
text:
(1) Wild duck may be hunted from 1 September to 31 December.
(2) Pheasant may be hunted from 1 October to 31 January.
(3) A person may take at most 10 birds in one day.

heading: Bag limits for deer
text:
(1) A hunter may take at most 2 red deer in one season.
(2) A hunter may take at most 3 roe deer in one season.
(3) Each animal taken shall be tagged with a numbered tag within one hour.

heading: Tag fees
text:
(1) A tag for a red deer costs 30 crowns.
(2) A tag for a roe deer costs 18 crowns.
(3) The tag is valid only for the season for which it is bought.

heading: Tag fees
text:
(1) A tag for a red deer costs 36 crowns.
(2) A tag for a roe deer costs 22 crowns.
(3) The tag is valid only for the season for which it is bought.

heading: Forbidden methods
text:
(1) Hunting with poison, snares or traps that kill slowly is forbidden.
(2) Hunting from a motor vehicle is forbidden.
(3) Hunting with a rifle of a calibre below 6 millimetres is forbidden for deer.

heading: Firearm storage
text:
(1) A firearm shall be stored unloaded in a locked cabinet.
(2) Ammunition shall be stored separately from the firearm.
(3) A person who breaks this section shall pay a fine of 100 crowns.

heading: Hunting near homes
text:
(1) A person shall not hunt within 150 metres of an inhabited building.
(2) A person shall not shoot across a public road.
(3) A person shall not hunt within 50 metres of a public path used by walkers.

heading: Hunting near homes
text:
(1) A person shall not hunt within 200 metres of an inhabited building.
(2) A person shall not shoot across a public road.
(3) A person shall not hunt within 50 metres of a public path used by walkers.

heading: Hunting dogs
text:
(1) A person may use a dog for hunting only if the dog has passed a hunting dog test.
(2) The test is valid for 5 years.
(3) A hunting dog shall be kept under control at all times.

heading: Hunting on private land
text:
(1) A hunter needs the written consent of the landowner to hunt on private land.
(2) The consent shall state the dates and the game to be hunted.
(3) A hunter shall carry the consent while hunting.

heading: Pest control
text:
(1) A landowner may shoot foxes and crows on the landowner's own land throughout the year.
(2) The landowner needs a hunting licence to do so.
(3) The landowner shall report the number shot to the Hunting Board once a year.

heading: Wounded animals
text:
(1) A hunter who wounds an animal shall follow it for at least 2 hours.
(2) The hunter shall report an animal that cannot be found to the Hunting Board within 24 hours.
(3) The Hunting Board may send a tracking dog free of charge.

heading: Hunting for sale
text:
(1) Game taken under this Act may be sold only with a receipt of origin.
(2) The receipt shall be kept for 2 years.
(3) A person who sells game without a receipt shall pay a fine of 90 crowns.

heading: Hunting for sale
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Hunting Board
text:
(1) The Hunting Board issues licences and supervises the application of this Act.
(2) The Board has 7 members appointed for terms of 4 years.
(3) The Board shall publish game statistics each year.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who hunts without a licence shall pay a fine of 150 crowns.
(2) A person who hunts outside an open season shall pay a fine of 200 crowns.
(3) For a repeat offence within 3 years the fine is doubled and the licence is suspended for one year.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who hunts without a licence shall pay a fine of 180 crowns.
(2) A person who hunts outside an open season shall pay a fine of 240 crowns.
(3) For a repeat offence within 3 years the fine is doubled and the licence is suspended for one year.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision of the Hunting Board may appeal within 30 days.
(2) The appeal shall be decided within 60 days.
(3) An appeal does not suspend a suspension of a licence under section 19.

heading: Art gallery admission for long-standing blood donors
text:
(1) A person who has given blood at least 50 times in his or her life receives free admission to the state art gallery.
(2) The person shows the donor record of the national blood service at the entrance.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating heavy vehicle movements within the Republic of Nordvale, specifically addressing the requirement for route permits. The purpose is to ensure the safety and integrity of the national road network, minimize infrastructure damage, and manage traffic flow efficiently, particularly in areas with sensitive infrastructure or high population density. It applies to all vehicles exceeding specified weight or dimension limits operating on public roads, with the exception of emergency service vehicles responding to urgent calls. This Act defines the types of permits available, the application process, and the penalties for non-compliance. All provisions herein are designed to protect public assets and ensure fair access to transportation routes.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Heavy Vehicle" means any vehicle or combination of vehicles with a gross vehicle mass (GVM) exceeding 15,000 kilograms, or a width exceeding 2.6 meters, or a height exceeding 4.2 meters, or a length exceeding 20 meters.
(b) "Permit Authority" refers to the Nordvale Department of Transport.
(c) "Designated Route" means a road or section of road specifically approved by the Permit Authority for the passage of heavy vehicles.
(d) "Oversize Load" means any load that, when transported, causes the vehicle or combination of vehicles to exceed the standard dimensions or weight limits defined in subsection (1)(a).
(e) "Applicant" means an individual or entity applying for a heavy vehicle route permit.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) A heavy vehicle must not be operated on any public road within Nordvale unless a valid heavy vehicle route permit has been issued by the Permit Authority for that specific journey or route.
(2) This requirement applies to all heavy vehicles and oversize loads as defined in section 2, regardless of their origin or destination, if any part of their journey takes place on Nordvale's public road network. Failure to possess a valid permit constitutes an offense under this Act and may result in penalties as outlined in section 28. Exemptions may apply in specific, limited circumstances, such as during declared emergencies, as determined by the Permit Authority on a case-by-case basis.

heading: Types of Permits
text:
(1) The Permit Authority may issue the following types of heavy vehicle route permits:
(a) Single Journey Permit: Valid for a single, non-recurring trip on a specified route, typically issued for unique oversize loads.
(b) Restricted Area Permit: Valid for multiple journeys within a clearly defined geographic area, such as a specific municipality or industrial zone, for a period not exceeding 90 days.
(c) Corridor Permit: Valid for multiple journeys along a pre-approved corridor of roads, often used for regular transport routes, for a period not exceeding 180 days.
(d) Annual Permit: Valid for recurring journeys on approved routes for a full 365-day period, subject to regular review and compliance checks.

heading: Types of Permits
text:
(1) The Permit Authority may issue the following types of heavy vehicle route permits:
(a) Single Journey Permit: Valid for a single, non-recurring trip on a specified route, typically issued for unique oversize loads. The validity period for this permit type is limited to 7 days from the approved start date.
(b) Restricted Area Permit: Valid for multiple journeys within a clearly defined geographic area, such as a specific municipality or industrial zone, for a period not exceeding 120 days.
(c) Corridor Permit: Valid for multiple journeys along a pre-approved corridor of roads, often used for regular transport routes, for a period not exceeding 270 days.
(d) Annual Permit: Valid for recurring journeys on approved routes for a full 365-day period, subject to regular review and compliance checks.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a heavy vehicle route permit must be submitted to the Permit Authority at least 14 working days prior to the intended start date of the journey. Applications must be submitted through the official online portal or at designated municipal offices in Aldmark or Brenholt.
(2) The application must include:
(a) Vehicle identification details, including registration number and GVM.
(b) Load specifications, if applicable.
(c) Proposed route, including all intermediate points and desired start/end dates.
(d) Payment of the non-refundable application fee as specified in section 8.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a heavy vehicle route permit must be submitted to the Permit Authority at least 21 working days prior to the intended start date of the journey. Applications must be submitted exclusively through the official online portal.
(2) The application must include:
(a) Vehicle identification details, including registration number, GVM, and axle configuration.
(b) Load specifications, if applicable, including precise dimensions and weight distribution.
(c) Proposed route, including all intermediate points, alternative routes, and desired start/end dates.
(d) Payment of the non-refundable application fee as specified in section 8.
(e) A safety plan outlining measures to mitigate risks associated with the heavy vehicle's operation.

heading: Application Review
text:
(1) The Permit Authority will review each application within 10 working days of receipt to assess its completeness and compliance with this Act.
(2) During the review process, the Permit Authority will consider:
(a) The structural capacity of bridges and roads on the proposed route.
(b) Potential traffic congestion and public safety concerns.
(c) Any planned road works or events that may conflict with the proposed journey.
(d) The environmental impact of the proposed route, especially in sensitive areas like Lund Vale.
(3) The Authority may consult with municipal authorities, such as those in Corvik or Dunmere, if the proposed route traverses their jurisdiction.

heading: Permit Issuance
text:
(1) Upon successful review and approval, the Permit Authority will issue a heavy vehicle route permit within 3 working days of the decision.
(2) The permit will specify:
(a) The authorized vehicle or vehicles.
(b) The approved route, including any specific time restrictions or escort requirements.
(c) The validity period of the permit.
(d) Any special conditions imposed to ensure public safety or infrastructure protection, such as restrictions on travel during peak hours (e.g., 07:00-09:00 and 16:00-18:00).
(3) The permit must be carried in the heavy vehicle at all times during its operation on a designated route.

heading: Permit Issuance
text:
(1) Upon successful review and approval, the Permit Authority will issue a heavy vehicle route permit within 5 working days of the decision, provided all fees are paid.
(2) The permit will specify:
(a) The authorized vehicle or vehicles, including precise identification numbers.
(b) The approved route, including any specific time restrictions, mandatory rest stops, or escort requirements.
(c) The validity period of the permit, clearly stating the start and end dates.
(d) Any special conditions imposed to ensure public safety or infrastructure protection, such as restrictions on travel during peak hours (e.g., 06:30-09:30 and 15:30-18:30) or during adverse weather conditions.
(3) The permit must be displayed prominently in the heavy vehicle's windshield and carried electronically or physically at all times during its operation on a designated route.

heading: Application Fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is required for all permit applications, regardless of the permit type.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. It is separate from any permit issuance fees outlined in section 9. Failure to pay the application fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application, and the review process will not commence until full payment is received. The fee can be paid via electronic transfer or at authorized payment points in Aldmark.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, the following permit issuance fees apply:
(a) Single Journey Permit: 750 crowns.
(b) Restricted Area Permit: 1,500 crowns.
(c) Corridor Permit: 2,500 crowns.
(d) Annual Permit: 5,000 crowns.
(2) These fees are payable upon approval of the permit and prior to its issuance. A 10% discount may be applied for companies holding more than 5 annual permits.
(3) All fees are subject to an annual review and may be adjusted by up to 5% based on inflation and administrative costs.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, the following permit issuance fees apply:
(a) Single Journey Permit: 800 crowns.
(b) Restricted Area Permit: 1,650 crowns.
(c) Corridor Permit: 2,750 crowns.
(d) Annual Permit: 5,500 crowns.
(2) These fees are payable upon approval of the permit and prior to its issuance. A 15% discount may be applied for companies holding more than 7 annual permits.
(3) All fees are subject to an annual review and may be adjusted by up to 8% based on inflation and administrative costs. Payments must be finalized within 14 days of permit approval.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, the following permit issuance fees apply:
(a) Single Journey Permit: 850 crowns.
(b) Restricted Area Permit: 1,800 crowns.
(c) Corridor Permit: 2,900 crowns.
(d) Annual Permit: 5,800 crowns.
(2) These fees are payable upon approval of the permit and prior to its issuance. A 20% discount may be applied for companies holding more than 10 annual permits and demonstrating a clean compliance record for the past 24 months.
(3) All fees are subject to a biennial review and may be adjusted by up to 10% based on infrastructure development costs and administrative overheads. Payments must be finalized within 7 days of permit approval, or the approval may be rescinded.

heading: Exemptions for Emergency Vehicles
text:
(1) Vehicles operated by emergency services, including fire, police, and ambulance, are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act when responding to an emergency call.
(2) This exemption applies only when the vehicle is actively engaged in an emergency response, indicated by the use of flashing lights and sirens. The GVM or dimensions of such vehicles must still adhere to general road safety regulations where practically possible. Once the emergency response concludes, or if the vehicle is used for routine operations, all permit requirements apply. This provision is designed to ensure swift response times for public safety.

heading: Vehicle Specifications
text:
(1) All heavy vehicles operating under a permit must comply with the national vehicle safety standards as published by the Nordvale Road Safety Board. This includes regular maintenance and safety inspections every 6 months.
(2) Vehicles with a GVM exceeding 25,000 kilograms or a length exceeding 25 meters must be equipped with advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), including lane departure warnings and automatic emergency braking, certified to Nordvale standards.
(3) Any modifications to a heavy vehicle's structure or engine must be approved by a certified engineer and registered with the Permit Authority within 30 days of completion.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text:
(1) Drivers of heavy vehicles requiring a permit must hold a valid Nordvale Class E driving license for at least 3 years and be over the age of 21.
(2) Additionally, drivers must complete a specialized heavy vehicle operation course approved by the Permit Authority every 5 years. This course includes modules on load securing, route planning, and emergency procedures specific to oversized or overweight loads. Records of these qualifications must be presented upon request by enforcement officers. Failure to meet these qualifications will result in permit invalidation.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text:
(1) Drivers of heavy vehicles requiring a permit must hold a valid Nordvale Class E driving license for at least 5 years and be over the age of 23.
(2) Additionally, drivers must complete a specialized heavy vehicle operation course approved by the Permit Authority every 3 years. This course includes modules on advanced load securing techniques, intricate route planning, and comprehensive emergency procedures specific to oversized or overweight loads. Drivers must also complete a mandatory 2-day defensive driving course every 2 years. Records of these qualifications must be presented upon request by enforcement officers. Failure to meet these qualifications will result in immediate permit invalidation and potential fines.

heading: Escort Requirements
text:
(1) Oversize loads exceeding 3.5 meters in width or 30 meters in length must be accompanied by at least one certified escort vehicle.
(2) Loads exceeding 4.5 meters in width or 40 meters in length, or with a GVM over 100,000 kilograms, require two certified escort vehicles and may necessitate police escort in densely populated areas like Aldmark or Brenholt. Escort vehicles must be equipped with appropriate warning signs and flashing amber lights, and their drivers must be certified by the Permit Authority. These requirements ensure maximum visibility and safety for other road users.

heading: Escort Requirements
text:
(1) Oversize loads exceeding 3.2 meters in width or 28 meters in length must be accompanied by at least one certified escort vehicle.
(2) Loads exceeding 4.2 meters in width or 38 meters in length, or with a GVM over 90,000 kilograms, require two certified escort vehicles and may necessitate police escort in densely populated areas like Aldmark or Brenholt. Escort vehicles must be equipped with appropriate warning signs and flashing amber lights, and their drivers must be certified by the Permit Authority and undergo an annual refresher course. These requirements ensure maximum visibility and safety for other road users, especially on narrow roads in areas like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Load Securing
text:
(1) All loads transported by heavy vehicles must be properly secured to prevent movement, shifting, or falling during transit.
(2) Loads must comply with Nordvale's load securing standards, requiring at least 80% of the load's weight to be secured against forward movement and 50% against sideways and rearward movement. Straps, chains, or other securing devices must have a combined breaking strength of at least twice the weight of the secured load. Inspections for load security may be carried out by enforcement officers at any point along the route, particularly at designated checkpoints near major junctions. Non-compliance can lead to immediate cessation of travel.

heading: Route Deviations
text:
(1) Any deviation from the approved route specified in the permit is strictly prohibited unless pre-approved by the Permit Authority due to unforeseen circumstances.
(2) In cases of emergencies, such as road closures due to accidents or natural disasters, a temporary deviation may be permitted, provided the driver notifies the Permit Authority within 60 minutes of the deviation. The alternative route must be deemed safe and suitable for heavy vehicles by the Permit Authority. Unauthorized deviations will result in penalties as outlined in section 28. Routes through sensitive areas like Grauby are particularly restricted.

heading: Route Deviations
text:
(1) Any deviation from the approved route specified in the permit is strictly prohibited unless pre-approved in writing by the Permit Authority due to unforeseen circumstances.
(2) In cases of emergencies, such as road closures due to accidents or natural disasters, a temporary deviation may be permitted, provided the driver notifies the Permit Authority immediately, within 30 minutes of the deviation. The proposed alternative route must be submitted for real-time assessment and approval by the Permit Authority. Unauthorized deviations will result in severe penalties, including increased fines as outlined in section 28 and potential permit revocation. Routes through sensitive areas like Grauby and Lund Vale are under strict monitoring.

heading: Time Restrictions
text:
(1) Heavy vehicles operating under a permit may be subject to specific time restrictions to minimize disruption to general traffic and local communities.
(2) For instance, travel through urban centers like Aldmark or Brenholt may be prohibited between 07:00 and 09:00, and again between 16:00 and 18:00, Monday to Friday. Oversize loads may only be permitted to travel between 22:00 and 05:00 on weekdays, and at any time on weekends, provided they do not pass through residential areas. These restrictions will be clearly stipulated on the issued permit. Violation of time restrictions may lead to fines of up to 1,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Bridge and Structure Protection
text:
(1) The Permit Authority reserves the right to impose specific conditions related to bridge and structure crossings for heavy vehicles, particularly for loads exceeding 50,000 kilograms GVM.
(2) These conditions may include speed restrictions of 10 kilometers per hour when crossing certain bridges, mandatory single-lane passage, or requirements for engineering assessments prior to approval. Any damage caused to public infrastructure by a heavy vehicle operating under a permit will be the full financial responsibility of the permit holder, and repair costs may exceed 50,000 crowns per incident, recoverable by the Permit Authority.

heading: Bridge and Structure Protection
text:
(1) The Permit Authority reserves the right to impose specific conditions related to bridge and structure crossings for heavy vehicles, particularly for loads exceeding 45,000 kilograms GVM or exceeding 4.8 meters in height.
(2) These conditions may include speed restrictions of 5 kilometers per hour when crossing certain bridges, mandatory single-lane passage with a minimum 50-meter clear distance from other vehicles, or requirements for independent engineering assessments and structural reinforcement plans prior to approval. Any damage caused to public infrastructure by a heavy vehicle operating under a permit will be the full financial responsibility of the permit holder, and repair costs may exceed 100,000 crowns per incident, recoverable by the Permit Authority, in addition to potential criminal charges.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must report any accidents, incidents, or significant delays involving permitted heavy vehicles to the Permit Authority within 24 hours of occurrence.
(2) This report must include details of the incident, any damage caused, and measures taken to mitigate further risks. Failure to report within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 500 crowns and a review of the permit holder's compliance record. The Permit Authority utilizes this data to improve route planning and safety protocols across Nordvale's road network.

heading: Permit Suspension
text:
(1) The Permit Authority may suspend a heavy vehicle route permit for a period of up to 90 days if the permit holder breaches any condition of the permit or any provision of this Act.
(2) Reasons for suspension include, but are not limited to, operating off the designated route, repeated violations of time restrictions, or significant safety breaches. The permit holder will be notified in writing of the suspension, including the reasons and duration, and will have 7 days to provide a written response. During the suspension period, the vehicle is prohibited from operating on Nordvale's roads under that specific permit.

heading: Permit Suspension
text:
(1) The Permit Authority may suspend a heavy vehicle route permit for a period of up to 180 days if the permit holder breaches any condition of the permit or any provision of this Act, or accumulates more than 3 minor infractions within a 12-month period.
(2) Reasons for suspension include, but are not limited to, operating off the designated route, repeated violations of time restrictions, significant safety breaches, or failure to maintain required vehicle specifications. The permit holder will be notified in writing of the suspension, including the detailed reasons and duration, and will have 3 days to provide a written response. During the suspension period, the vehicle is strictly prohibited from operating on Nordvale's roads under that specific permit, and any attempt to do so will result in immediate revocation.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) A heavy vehicle route permit may be permanently revoked by the Permit Authority for serious or repeated breaches of this Act or permit conditions.
(2) Examples include causing severe damage to infrastructure (exceeding 25,000 crowns), multiple unauthorized route deviations (more than 3 incidents), or sustained non-compliance with safety regulations. Revocation means the permit holder is prohibited from applying for a new permit for a minimum period of 12 months. The Permit Authority will provide written notice of the revocation, and the permit holder may appeal the decision as per section 21.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain accurate records of all journeys undertaken under a permit, including dates, routes, vehicle details, and driver information.
(2) These records must be retained for a minimum of 24 months and made available for inspection by the Permit Authority or enforcement officers upon request within 48 hours. Digital records are preferred, but physical logs are also acceptable. Failure to produce requested records may result in a fine of 750 crowns and a review of permit compliance. This requirement ensures accountability and aids in incident investigation.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision of the Permit Authority, including permit refusal, suspension, or revocation, within 30 days of receiving the decision notice.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board, an independent body overseeing transport regulations. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and provide any supporting documentation. The Appeals Board will review the case within 60 days and issue a final decision, which will be binding on both parties. A non-refundable appeal fee of 1,000 crowns applies.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) Designated enforcement officers, including municipal police and transport inspectors, have the authority to stop and inspect any heavy vehicle operating on Nordvale's roads.
(2) Officers may demand to see a valid heavy vehicle route permit, driver's license, vehicle registration, and load securing documentation. They may also conduct physical inspections of the vehicle and its load to ensure compliance with permit conditions and safety standards. Officers have the power to issue immediate fines, order a vehicle to cease travel, or impound a vehicle if serious safety risks or permit violations are identified. Resisting an inspection carries a penalty of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Fines for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Operating a heavy vehicle without a valid permit is an offense punishable by a fine of 5,000 crowns for a first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses within a 12-month period will incur a fine of 10,000 crowns and may lead to permit revocation or a ban on applying for new permits for a period of 6 months. Minor infractions, such as failing to display the permit or minor route deviations, may incur a fine of 1,500 crowns per incident. All fines are payable within 28 days of issuance.

heading: Heavy Vehicle Zones
text:
(1) The Permit Authority may designate specific "Heavy Vehicle Zones" in areas like industrial parks or port facilities where permits may be streamlined or waived under specific conditions.
(2) Within these zones, vehicles up to 20,000 kilograms GVM may operate without a specific route permit, provided they comply with all other national vehicle regulations. These zones are clearly marked with appropriate signage indicating the relaxed permit requirements and are subject to regular review by the Permit Authority to ensure continued suitability. Operations outside these zones immediately revert to standard permit requirements.

heading: Heavy Vehicle Zones
text:
(1) The Permit Authority may designate specific "Heavy Vehicle Zones" in areas like industrial parks, port facilities, or major construction sites, where permits may be streamlined or waived under specific conditions.
(2) Within these zones, vehicles up to 22,000 kilograms GVM or up to 2.8 meters in width may operate without a specific route permit, provided they comply with all other national vehicle regulations and operate strictly within the defined zone boundaries. These zones are clearly marked with appropriate signage indicating the relaxed permit requirements and are subject to quarterly review by the Permit Authority to ensure continued suitability and public safety. Operations outside these zones immediately revert to standard permit requirements, and non-compliance within 100 meters of a zone boundary will incur full penalties.

heading: Infrastructure Damage Levy
text:
(1) An additional levy of 5% of the permit fee is charged for all permits to contribute to the Nordvale Infrastructure Maintenance Fund.
(2) This fund is specifically allocated for the repair and upkeep of roads and bridges frequently used by heavy vehicles. The levy is automatically added to the total permit cost and is non-refundable. The Permit Authority publishes an annual report detailing how these funds are utilized, with a minimum of 70% of the funds directed to projects in municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, which experience high heavy vehicle traffic.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) Before establishing new designated routes or significantly altering existing ones, the Permit Authority will conduct a public consultation period of at least 45 days.
(2) This process involves publishing proposed changes in official gazettes and local newspapers, holding public meetings in affected municipalities (e.g., Elsby, Fennick), and inviting written submissions from interested parties. All feedback received will be considered before final decisions are made. A summary of public input and the Authority's response will be published. This ensures transparency and community involvement in route planning.
