heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The review process will include an assessment of permit statistics, enforcement outcomes, infrastructure impacts, and feedback from permit holders and the public. Recommendations for amendments to the Act, including adjustments to fees, penalties, or permit types, will be submitted to Parliament following each review. The first review is scheduled for 2023, with subsequent reviews every five years thereafter, ensuring that the legislation remains current and responsive to changing needs.

heading: Power to Make Regulations
text:
(1) The Permit Authority has the power to make regulations for the effective administration and enforcement of this Act.
(2) These regulations may include, but are not limited to, prescribing detailed application forms, setting specific technical requirements for heavy vehicles and escort vehicles, defining procedures for incident reporting, and establishing guidelines for the conduct of enforcement officers. Any new regulations must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 60 days before coming into force, allowing for public review and comment. All regulations must be consistent with the provisions of this Act.

heading: Information Sharing
text:
(1) The Permit Authority may share information regarding permit applications, issuances, and violations with other relevant government agencies, including the Department of Roads and Bridges and municipal police forces.
(2) This information sharing is for the purpose of ensuring coordinated enforcement, infrastructure planning, and public safety. Personal data will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations. Aggregate data, such as total permit numbers per month or common violation types, may also be published for statistical and public awareness purposes, ensuring transparency while respecting individual privacy.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any heavy vehicle permits issued under previous regulations prior to the commencement of this Act shall remain valid for a period of 6 months from the effective date of this Act.
(2) During this 6-month transitional period, holders of existing permits are encouraged to apply for new permits under the provisions of this Act. After the transitional period, all previous permits will become invalid, and all heavy vehicles must operate under permits issued in accordance with this Act. The Permit Authority will provide assistance and guidance to facilitate a smooth transition for all affected operators.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text:
(1) This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018.
(2) The Permit Authority will publish comprehensive guidelines and frequently asked questions documents on its official website by 1 December 2017 to assist the public and industry stakeholders in understanding and complying with the new requirements. Public awareness campaigns, including informational sessions in major transport hubs such as Aldmark and Brenholt, will also be conducted during the month of December 2017 to ensure broad dissemination of information before the Act takes full effect.

heading: Payment terms
text: For a certified bookbinder, the surcharge mentioned in FDA §25(1) is due 30 days after the licence fee.

heading: Special categories
text: No electric bicycle registration fee is payable by a registered lacemaker, who shall instead pay twenty-two crowns and fifty öre.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the licensing and regulation of facilities and services involved in the disposal of hazardous waste within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to protect public health and the environment from the risks associated with improper hazardous waste management. This includes setting standards for licence applications, operational requirements, inspection protocols, and enforcement measures. The scope of this Act extends to all entities, whether private or public, engaged in the collection, transport, storage, treatment, or final disposal of materials classified as hazardous waste within the national borders.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(1) "Hazardous waste" means any waste material that, due to its quantity, concentration, or physical, chemical, or infectious characteristics, may cause or significantly contribute to an increase in mortality or an increase in serious incapacitating reversible or irreversible illness, or pose a substantial present or potential hazard to human health or the environment when improperly treated, stored, transported, or disposed of, or otherwise managed.
(2) "Facility" means any site, property, structure, or equipment used for the handling, treatment, storage, or disposal of hazardous waste.
(3) "Licence" means a Hazardous Waste Disposal Licence issued under this Act.
(4) "Director" refers to the Director of Environmental Protection.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No person or entity shall operate a hazardous waste disposal facility or provide hazardous waste disposal services within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence issued by the Director. This requirement applies regardless of the scale of operation, whether it processes 5 tonnes per month or 500 tonnes per month. Any operation found to be in violation of this section shall cease operations immediately upon notification and may be subject to penalties as outlined in section 25. An interim period of 60 days may be granted for existing facilities to apply for a licence upon the commencement of this Act.

heading: Application Process
text: An application for a licence must be submitted to the Director in the prescribed form, accompanied by all necessary documentation. This includes a detailed operational plan, an environmental impact assessment, proof of financial solvency, and a non-refundable application fee of 15,000 crowns. The application must address how the facility will comply with all relevant environmental standards and safety protocols. Incomplete applications will be returned within 30 days of receipt, requiring resubmission with all missing information.

heading: Application Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Director shall review the submission within 90 days. During this period, the Director may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. A site inspection will be conducted within the first 60 days of the review period. The Director will provide a written decision to the applicant within 10 days following the conclusion of the review period, either granting or denying the licence.

heading: Application Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Director shall review the submission within 75 days. During this period, the Director may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. A site inspection will be conducted within the first 45 days of the review period. The Director will provide a written decision to the applicant within 7 days following the conclusion of the review period, either granting or denying the licence. Applications for renewal will be processed within 50 days.

heading: Licence Term
text: A licence issued under this Act shall be valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue. Applicants must submit a renewal application at least 120 days before the expiry date of their current licence. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe may result in the expiration of the licence and the requirement to apply for a new licence, including the full application fee and review process.

heading: Licence Term
text: A licence issued under this Act shall be valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issue. Applicants must submit a renewal application at least 150 days before the expiry date of their current licence. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe may result in the expiration of the licence and the requirement to apply for a new licence, including the full application fee and review process.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: To renew a licence, the applicant must submit an updated operational plan, a summary of compliance records over the previous licence term, and a renewal fee of 7,500 crowns. The Director will review renewal applications to ensure continued compliance with all applicable regulations. A site re-inspection may be conducted if there have been significant operational changes or documented compliance issues. Renewals are generally processed more quickly than initial applications, typically within 60 days.

heading: Operational Requirements
text: All licensed facilities must adhere to strict operational standards, including maintaining appropriate safety equipment, implementing spill prevention and response plans, and ensuring proper ventilation systems. Facilities must have at least 2 trained personnel on site at all times during operational hours. Waste storage areas must be secured, and access restricted to authorized personnel only. Detailed records of waste received, treated, and disposed of must be kept for a minimum of 10 years.

heading: Operational Requirements
text: All licensed facilities must adhere to strict operational standards, including maintaining appropriate safety equipment, implementing spill prevention and response plans, and ensuring proper ventilation systems. Facilities must have at least 3 trained personnel on site at all times during operational hours. Waste storage areas must be secured, and access restricted to authorized personnel only. Detailed records of waste received, treated, and disposed of must be kept for a minimum of 12 years.

heading: Environmental Standards
text: Licensed facilities must operate in a manner that minimizes environmental impact. This includes adhering to emission limits for air and water pollutants, which must not exceed 0.5 parts per million for specific hazardous substances. Discharges into waterways must be monitored daily, and soil contamination levels within the facility's perimeter must not exceed established thresholds, currently set at 100 milligrams per kilogram for heavy metals. Regular environmental audits are required every 6 months.

heading: Emergency Preparedness
text: Each licensed facility must develop and implement a comprehensive emergency response plan. This plan must be reviewed and updated annually, and drills must be conducted at least twice a year. The plan must include procedures for fire, explosions, spills, and other potential incidents, and detail communication protocols with local emergency services, which must be notified within 15 minutes of any major incident. All facility personnel must receive emergency response training every 12 months.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Licensed operators are required to maintain accurate and detailed records of all hazardous waste activities. This includes waste manifests, treatment logs, disposal certificates, and monitoring data. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Director or authorized representatives for a minimum period of 10 years. Any discrepancies exceeding 2% between received and disposed volumes must be reported within 24 hours of discovery. Records must be stored both electronically and in physical form.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Licence holders must submit quarterly reports to the Director detailing their hazardous waste operations. These reports, due within 30 days of the end of each quarter, must include total volumes of waste processed, types of waste handled, and any incidents or non-compliance events. An annual summary report, due by March 31st of the following year, must also be submitted. Failure to submit reports on time may result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Licence holders must submit monthly reports to the Director detailing their hazardous waste operations. These reports, due within 15 days of the end of each month, must include total volumes of waste processed, types of waste handled, and any incidents or non-compliance events. An annual summary report, due by February 28th of the following year, must also be submitted. Failure to submit reports on time may result in a penalty of 7,500 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Transportation of Waste
text: The transportation of hazardous waste must comply with specific regulations, including the use of approved vehicles and containers. All transport vehicles must be clearly marked with hazardous waste placards, measuring at least 30 cm by 30 cm, and be equipped with spill containment kits. Drivers must possess special training certificates and be at least 21 years of age. A manifest must accompany every shipment, detailing the waste type, quantity, origin, and destination, with three copies distributed to relevant parties.

heading: Security Measures
text: Licensed facilities must implement robust security measures to prevent unauthorized access to hazardous waste. This includes perimeter fencing of at least 2 meters in height, 24-hour surveillance cameras covering all entry points and storage areas, and controlled access systems. Security personnel must be present on site during all non-operational hours. Any breach of security must be reported to the Director within 12 hours of discovery, and a full incident report submitted within 48 hours.

heading: Public Notification
text: In the event of a significant hazardous waste incident, such as a major spill or release that poses a risk to the public, the licence holder must notify the local authorities and the public within 6 hours. This notification must include details of the incident, potential risks, and any necessary precautions. The Director must approve the content of any public notification before its release. A dedicated hotline for public inquiries must be established within 24 hours of such an incident.

heading: Inspections
text: The Director or an authorized inspector may conduct unannounced inspections of any licensed facility at any reasonable time. These inspections will verify compliance with the terms of the licence and the provisions of this Act. Inspectors will have access to all operational areas, records, and personnel. Refusal to permit an inspection may result in the immediate suspension of the licence for a minimum of 7 days, as per section 23.

heading: Compliance Orders
text: If, during an inspection, the Director identifies any non-compliance with the Act or the licence conditions, a compliance order will be issued. This order will specify the nature of the non-compliance, the corrective actions required, and a deadline for completion, typically ranging from 7 to 30 days depending on the severity. Failure to comply with a compliance order by the specified deadline may lead to further enforcement actions, including penalties or licence suspension.

heading: Appeals
text: An applicant or licence holder may appeal a decision of the Director, including the denial of a licence, the imposition of a compliance order, or the suspension or revocation of a licence. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Director's decision. The Appeals Tribunal will review the case and render a decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: All licence holders must maintain financial assurance to cover the costs of potential environmental remediation and closure of the facility. The amount of financial assurance required will be determined by the Director based on the scale and nature of the operations, but will not be less than 500,000 crowns and not more than 5,000,000 crowns. This assurance may be in the form of a bond, trust fund, or letter of credit, and must be reviewed annually.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: All licence holders must maintain financial assurance to cover the costs of potential environmental remediation and closure of the facility. The amount of financial assurance required will be determined by the Director based on the scale and nature of the operations, but will not be less than 750,000 crowns and not more than 7,000,000 crowns. This assurance may be in the form of a bond, trust fund, or letter of credit, and must be reviewed annually to ensure it covers at least 110% of estimated costs.

heading: Closure Plan
text: Each licensed facility must submit a detailed closure plan as part of its licence application. This plan must outline the procedures for decommissioning the facility, decontaminating the site, and ensuring long-term environmental safety. The estimated cost of closure must be updated every 3 years. The Director must approve any modifications to the closure plan. A facility must provide at least 180 days' notice before initiating closure procedures.

heading: Post-Closure Care
text: Following the closure of a hazardous waste facility, the former licence holder remains responsible for post-closure care for a period of at least 30 years. This includes ongoing environmental monitoring, maintenance of any containment structures, and reporting to the Director. The post-closure care plan must be fully funded through the financial assurance mechanism established under section 19. Any changes in ownership during the post-closure period must be approved by the Director 90 days in advance.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the handling, treatment, storage, or disposal of hazardous waste must undergo mandatory training. This training must cover hazardous waste identification, safety procedures, emergency response, and regulatory compliance. Initial training must be completed within 60 days of employment, and refresher training must be conducted annually. Records of all training must be kept on site for a minimum of 5 years and made available upon inspection.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the handling, treatment, storage, or disposal of hazardous waste must undergo mandatory training. This training must cover hazardous waste identification, safety procedures, emergency response, and regulatory compliance, including specific modules for new types of waste. Initial training must be completed within 30 days of employment, and refresher training must be conducted every 9 months. Records of all training must be kept on site for a minimum of 7 years and made available upon inspection.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text: A licence issued under this Act is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Director. An application for transfer must be submitted at least 90 days before the proposed transfer date and include full details of the prospective new owner, including their financial capabilities and operational plans. The Director will review the application to ensure the new owner meets all eligibility and operational requirements. A transfer fee of 10,000 crowns is applicable.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text: The Director may suspend a licence for serious non-compliance with this Act or its regulations, or for any action that poses an immediate threat to public health or the environment. A suspension order will be issued in writing, detailing the reasons for the suspension and the conditions for reinstatement. During a suspension, all hazardous waste operations must cease, except for those necessary to mitigate immediate risks. A suspension period will generally not exceed 90 days.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text: A licence may be revoked by the Director for persistent or egregious non-compliance, failure to rectify issues after a suspension, or providing false information in a licence application. Before revocation, the licence holder will be given an opportunity to present their case, typically within 14 days of notification. Once revoked, the entity is prohibited from operating a hazardous waste facility or service in Nordvale for a period of at least 5 years. Any financial assurance may be utilized for site remediation.

heading: Penalties for Offences
text: Any person or entity found to be operating a hazardous waste facility or service without a valid licence shall be subject to a fine of not less than 50,000 crowns and not exceeding 500,000 crowns for a first offence. Subsequent offences may incur fines up to 1,000,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for individuals for up to 2 years. Each day of non-compliance after a warning may be considered a separate offence, incurring an additional daily fine of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for Offences
text: Any person or entity found to be operating a hazardous waste facility or service without a valid licence shall be subject to a fine of not less than 75,000 crowns and not exceeding 750,000 crowns for a first offence. Subsequent offences may incur fines up to 1,500,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for individuals for up to 3 years. Each day of non-compliance after a warning may be considered a separate offence, incurring an additional daily fine of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Offences by Corporations
text: Where an offence under this Act is committed by a corporation, any director, officer, or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted, or acquiesced in the commission of the offence is also guilty of the offence and liable to the penalties provided for in section 25, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted. The maximum fine for a corporation for a single offence is 1,500,000 crowns, increasing to 3,000,000 crowns for repeat offences within a 5-year period.

heading: Jurisdiction
text: All legal proceedings and enforcement actions related to this Act shall fall under the jurisdiction of the courts of Nordvale. Specifically, disputes arising in Aldmark, Brenholt, or Corvik will be heard in the Aldmark Regional Court. Cases from Dunmere, Elsby, or Fennick will be directed to the Dunmere Circuit Court. Matters pertaining to Grauby or Lund Vale will be heard by the Grauby District Court. The Director's office is located in Aldmark.

heading: Regulations
text: The Director, with the approval of the Council of Ministers, may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act. These regulations may include, but are not limited to, specifying types of hazardous waste, setting more detailed operational standards, prescribing additional fees, and establishing specific monitoring requirements. Any new regulation will undergo a 60-day public consultation period before enactment. Regulations are published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before taking effect.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any entity operating a hazardous waste facility or service immediately prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a period of 180 days from the effective date to apply for a licence. During this transitional period, such entities may continue their operations, provided they submit an application within the first 60 days. Failure to apply within 60 days will result in immediate cessation of operations. All provisions of this Act related to compliance and penalties will apply after the 180-day period.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a registered organ tuner, they shall have 30 additional days to pay the annual licence fee of forty-five crowns per dog, and thirty crowns for each further dog.

heading: Particular persons
text: No pensioner heating supplement is payable by a licensed hot-spring attendant; instead, a fixed payment of 5 crowns replaces any fee or allowance specified in HOA §13.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A holder of a cave rescue badge shall receive five crowns in place of the annual water bill rebate.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the permitting and regulation of hazardous waste storage facilities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to safeguard public health and the environment from the risks associated with improper hazardous waste management. The Act specifies the conditions under which hazardous waste can be stored, including safety protocols, site requirements, and operational standards. All entities, whether public or private, that store hazardous waste exceeding a specified threshold must obtain and maintain a valid permit in accordance with the provisions outlined herein. The scope covers all types of hazardous waste as defined in section 3.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, 'hazardous waste' refers to any solid, liquid, or gaseous waste material or combination of materials that, because of its quantity, concentration, or physical, chemical, or infectious characteristics, may cause or significantly contribute to an increase in mortality or an increase in serious irreversible, or incapacitating reversible, illness; or pose a substantial present or potential hazard to human health or the environment when improperly treated, stored, transported, or disposed of, or otherwise managed.
(2) 'Storage facility' means any land or structure used for the holding of hazardous waste for a temporary period, not exceeding 365 days, prior to its treatment, disposal, or further transportation.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall store hazardous waste in quantities exceeding 50 kilograms at any single location for more than 48 hours without first obtaining a Hazardous Waste Storage Permit from the Department of Environmental Protection, as mandated by this Act. This requirement applies to all commercial, industrial, and governmental operations handling hazardous materials. Failure to possess a valid permit for such storage activities will result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 100,000 crowns per day of non-compliance. Exemptions may apply to certain small-scale generators as specified in section 7.

heading: Permit Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a Hazardous Waste Storage Permit must be submitted to the Department of Environmental Protection on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 5,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the storage facility, an emergency response plan, a waste management plan, and proof of financial assurance.
(3) The Department shall review the application within 90 days of receipt and may request additional information.

heading: Permit Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a Hazardous Waste Storage Permit must be submitted to the Department of Environmental Protection on the prescribed digital form, accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 7,500 crowns.
(2) The application must include detailed digital blueprints of the storage facility, an updated emergency response plan, a waste management plan detailing disposal routes, and proof of financial assurance.
(3) The Department shall review the application within 75 days of receipt and may request additional information or on-site inspections.

heading: Application Content Requirements
text: Each permit application must contain, at a minimum, the following information: the legal name and address of the applicant; the precise location of the proposed storage facility, including GPS coordinates; a detailed description of the types and estimated maximum quantities of hazardous waste to be stored; a site-specific contingency plan for spills or releases; and a certification that the applicant has sufficient financial resources to operate the facility safely and to close it properly. Failure to provide any of this information may result in the application being rejected as incomplete.

heading: Application Content Requirements
text: Each permit application must contain, at a minimum, the following information: the legal name and address of the applicant; the precise location of the proposed storage facility, including GPS coordinates to within 5 meters; a detailed description of the types and estimated maximum quantities of hazardous waste to be stored, categorized by hazard class; a site-specific contingency plan for spills or releases, updated every 12 months; and a certification that the applicant has sufficient financial resources, evidenced by a bond of at least 250,000 crowns, to operate the facility safely and to close it properly. Failure to provide any of this information may result in the application being rejected as incomplete within 30 days.

heading: Permit Issuance Conditions
text: A permit may be issued only if the Department of Environmental Protection determines that the proposed storage facility meets all technical and safety standards outlined in this Act and its accompanying regulations. The applicant must demonstrate that the facility design prevents releases to the environment, provides adequate security, and includes provisions for regular monitoring and inspection. Furthermore, the applicant must not have a history of significant environmental violations within the past 5 years. Any permit issued will be valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
(1) Small quantity generators producing less than 50 kilograms of hazardous waste per month are exempt from the permit requirement, provided they store the waste for no longer than 180 days and dispose of it through an approved hazardous waste transporter.
(2) Households are generally exempt from this Act, but specific household hazardous waste collection programs may be subject to certain provisions.
(3) Emergency storage necessitated by an unforeseen event, lasting no longer than 72 hours, is also exempt, provided the Department is notified within 24 hours.

heading: Duration and Renewal of Permits
text: Each Hazardous Waste Storage Permit shall be valid for a period of 5 years from its date of issuance. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the permit's expiration date. The renewal process requires a re-evaluation of the facility's compliance with current regulations and a review of its operational history. A renewal fee of 3,000 crowns applies. Failure to apply for renewal within the stipulated timeframe may result in the permit expiring, necessitating a new application as per section 4.

heading: Duration and Renewal of Permits
text: Each Hazardous Waste Storage Permit shall be valid for a period of 7 years from its date of issuance. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 120 days prior to the permit's expiration date. The renewal process requires a comprehensive re-evaluation of the facility's compliance with current regulations, including an on-site inspection, and a review of its operational history for the past 7 years. A renewal fee of 4,500 crowns applies. Failure to apply for renewal within the stipulated timeframe may result in the permit expiring, necessitating a new application as per section 4.

heading: Modification of Permits
text:
(1) Any significant modification to a permitted hazardous waste storage facility, such as an expansion of storage capacity by more than 10%, a change in the types of waste stored, or a substantial alteration of the facility's design, requires a permit modification.
(2) An application for modification must be submitted to the Department, detailing the proposed changes, and will be subject to review and approval processes similar to an initial permit application. A modification fee of 2,000 crowns applies.
(3) Minor administrative changes, such as a change in contact information, may be reported without a formal modification application.

heading: Modification of Permits
text:
(1) Any significant modification to a permitted hazardous waste storage facility, such as an expansion of storage capacity by more than 5%, a change in the types or hazard classes of waste stored, or a substantial alteration of the facility's design affecting safety protocols, requires a permit modification.
(2) An application for modification must be submitted to the Department at least 60 days prior to implementation of the changes, detailing the proposed changes, and will be subject to review and approval processes similar to an initial permit application, including public notice. A modification fee of 3,500 crowns applies.
(3) Minor administrative changes, such as a change in contact information or emergency personnel details, may be reported to the Department within 14 days without a formal modification application.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text: The Department of Environmental Protection may revoke a Hazardous Waste Storage Permit if the permit holder fails to comply with any provision of this Act, the permit conditions, or applicable regulations. Grounds for revocation include, but are not limited to, repeated violations of safety protocols, significant unauthorized releases of hazardous waste, misrepresentation of information in the permit application, or failure to pay fines within 60 days. Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be given 30 days' written notice and an opportunity to be heard or to rectify the non-compliance.

heading: Facility Design Standards
text:
(1) All hazardous waste storage facilities must be designed to prevent the release of hazardous waste to the soil, groundwater, and air.
(2) This includes impermeable flooring, secondary containment systems capable of holding 110% of the largest container's volume, and appropriate ventilation systems.
(3) Storage areas must be constructed of materials compatible with the stored waste and resistant to corrosion and degradation.
(4) Access to the facility must be restricted to authorized personnel only, with secure fencing at least 2 meters high.

heading: Operational Requirements
text:
(1) Permitted facilities must maintain a detailed inventory of all hazardous waste stored, including its type, quantity, and storage location. This inventory must be updated weekly.
(2) Waste containers must be clearly labeled with their contents, hazard warnings, and accumulation start dates.
(3) Personnel handling hazardous waste must receive annual training on safe handling procedures and emergency response.
(4) Regular inspections of storage containers and areas must be conducted at least once every 7 days to detect leaks or deterioration.

heading: Operational Requirements
text:
(1) Permitted facilities must maintain a detailed digital inventory of all hazardous waste stored, including its type, exact quantity in kilograms or liters, and specific storage location within the facility. This inventory must be updated daily at the end of each operational shift.
(2) Waste containers must be clearly labeled with their contents, hazard warnings, accumulation start dates, and a unique identification code. Labels must be visible from a distance of 3 meters.
(3) All personnel handling hazardous waste must receive biannual (every 6 months) training on safe handling procedures, emergency response protocols, and spill prevention techniques.
(4) Regular inspections of storage containers, secondary containment, and storage areas must be conducted at least once every 24 hours to detect leaks, deterioration, or security breaches.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text:
(1) Every permitted facility must develop and maintain an up-to-date emergency response plan, approved by the Department and local emergency services.
(2) The plan must describe procedures for responding to fires, explosions, or releases of hazardous waste, including evacuation plans, notification procedures for authorities (within 15 minutes of discovery), and emergency equipment lists.
(3) All facility personnel must be familiar with the plan, and drills must be conducted at least annually.
(4) A copy of the plan must be readily accessible at the facility at all times.

heading: Financial Assurance
text:
(1) Permittees must demonstrate financial assurance for closure and post-closure care of their hazardous waste storage facilities.
(2) This assurance can be in the form of a trust fund, surety bond, letter of credit, or insurance policy, guaranteeing at least 150,000 crowns for closure costs.
(3) The amount of financial assurance required will be reviewed by the Department every 3 years and adjusted based on current cost estimates.
(4) Proof of financial assurance must be submitted annually.

heading: Financial Assurance
text:
(1) Permittees must demonstrate robust financial assurance for closure and post-closure care of their hazardous waste storage facilities for a period of 5 years after cessation of operations.
(2) This assurance can be in the form of a trust fund, surety bond, letter of credit, or insurance policy, guaranteeing at least 250,000 crowns for closure costs, plus 50,000 crowns for post-closure monitoring.
(3) The amount of financial assurance required will be reviewed by the Department every 2 years and adjusted based on current cost estimates and inflation.
(4) Proof of financial assurance must be submitted annually by January 31st.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) All permit holders must maintain comprehensive records related to hazardous waste management for a minimum of 5 years.
(2) These records include waste manifests, inspection logs, training records, incident reports, and monitoring data.
(3) Records must be made available to Department inspectors upon request within 24 hours.
(4) Digital copies of records are permissible, provided they are securely stored and backed up.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permitted facilities must submit an annual report to the Department of Environmental Protection by January 31st each year, summarizing their hazardous waste activities for the preceding calendar year.
(2) This report must include the types and quantities of waste stored, any incidents or spills, and a summary of training conducted.
(3) Any unauthorized release of hazardous waste exceeding 5 liters or 5 kilograms must be reported to the Department within 2 hours of discovery.
(4) Serious injuries resulting from hazardous waste handling must be reported within 1 hour.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permitted facilities must submit a biannual report (every six months) to the Department of Environmental Protection by July 31st and January 31st each year, summarizing their hazardous waste activities for the preceding six-month period.
(2) This report must include the types and quantities of waste stored, detailed records of any incidents or spills including remedial actions taken, and a summary of all training conducted during the period.
(3) Any unauthorized release of hazardous waste exceeding 2 liters or 2 kilograms, or any release impacting beyond the containment area, must be reported to the Department within 30 minutes of discovery, followed by a written report within 24 hours.
(4) Serious injuries or fatalities resulting from hazardous waste handling must be reported immediately by phone within 15 minutes, followed by a written report within 6 hours.

heading: Inspections and Monitoring
text:
(1) The Department of Environmental Protection shall conduct unannounced inspections of permitted facilities at least once every 12 months to ensure compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspectors shall have the right to enter any part of the facility, examine records, and collect samples.
(3) Facilities must implement a continuous monitoring system for air emissions if storing volatile hazardous waste exceeding 1,000 kilograms.
(4) Groundwater monitoring wells are required if the facility is located within 500 meters of a public water source.

heading: Inspections and Monitoring
text:
(1) The Department of Environmental Protection shall conduct unannounced inspections of permitted facilities at least once every 6 months to ensure compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspectors shall have the right to enter any part of the facility, examine records, and collect samples, and facility personnel must cooperate fully.
(3) Facilities must implement a continuous monitoring system for air emissions if storing volatile hazardous waste exceeding 500 kilograms, with data transmitted digitally to the Department weekly.
(4) Groundwater monitoring wells are required if the facility is located within 250 meters of a public water source or within 100 meters of any natural waterway.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) Information submitted to the Department of Environmental Protection under this Act is generally considered public record.
(2) However, trade secrets or proprietary business information may be designated as confidential by the applicant, provided adequate justification is presented.
(3) The Department will protect such designated information from public disclosure, except when legally compelled to release it for judicial proceedings.
(4) Information pertaining to hazardous waste types, quantities, and potential environmental impact cannot be designated as confidential.

heading: Public Participation
text:
(1) Before issuing or significantly modifying a Hazardous Waste Storage Permit, the Department shall provide public notice of the proposed action.
(2) This notice will be published in at least one major newspaper circulating in the affected municipality, such as the Aldmark Gazette or Corvik Chronicle, and on the Department's official website.
(3) A public comment period of at least 30 days shall be provided, during which interested parties may submit written comments or request a public hearing.
(4) The Department shall consider all comments received before making a final decision.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Department of Environmental Protection regarding a permit application, modification, or revocation may appeal the decision to the Environmental Appeals Board within 45 days of receiving written notification.
(2) The appeal must be in writing and state the specific grounds for the appeal.
(3) The Environmental Appeals Board shall hold a hearing within 60 days of receiving the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days thereafter.
(4) Decisions of the Board may be further appealed to the Nordvale Administrative Court.

heading: Transportation of Hazardous Waste
text:
(1) The transportation of hazardous waste to and from storage facilities must comply with all applicable national transportation regulations and require specific manifests.
(2) All transporters must be licensed by the Department of Transportation and carry proof of insurance of at least 500,000 crowns.
(3) Waste must be packaged and labeled according to international standards before transportation.
(4) Routes for hazardous waste transport must be approved by local authorities in municipalities like Brenholt and Dunmere, avoiding densely populated areas where possible.

heading: Closure of Facilities
text:
(1) When a hazardous waste storage facility ceases operation, the permit holder must implement an approved closure plan.
(2) The closure plan must detail procedures for the removal of all hazardous waste, decontamination of the facility, and environmental monitoring for a period of 2 years post-closure.
(3) A closure report, certified by an independent environmental engineer, must be submitted to the Department within 90 days of completion of closure activities.
(4) Failure to properly close a facility may result in the Department utilizing the financial assurance to perform closure at the permit holder's expense.

heading: Post-Closure Care
text:
(1) For facilities that pose a long-term environmental risk, the Department may require post-closure care for a period of up to 5 years.
(2) This care may include groundwater monitoring, maintenance of containment systems, and periodic inspections.
(3) The costs of post-closure care are to be covered by the financial assurance mechanism established under section 14.
(4) A post-closure care plan must be submitted for approval before the cessation of operations.

heading: Post-Closure Care
text:
(1) For facilities that pose a long-term environmental risk, the Department may require post-closure care for a period of up to 10 years, or longer if significant contamination is detected.
(2) This care may include groundwater and soil monitoring, maintenance of containment and leachate collection systems, and periodic inspections by certified environmental specialists.
(3) The costs of post-closure care are to be covered by the financial assurance mechanism established under section 14, with a minimum dedicated fund of 100,000 crowns.
(4) A detailed post-closure care plan, including specific monitoring frequencies and trigger levels for corrective action, must be submitted for approval at least 180 days before the cessation of operations.

heading: Enforcement Actions
text:
(1) The Department of Environmental Protection has the authority to issue compliance orders, impose administrative penalties, and initiate legal proceedings against individuals or entities violating this Act.
(2) Non-compliance may result in daily fines of up to 50,000 crowns, permit suspension, or permit revocation.
(3) In cases of imminent and substantial endangerment to public health or the environment, the Department may issue an emergency order requiring immediate corrective action.
(4) Criminal charges may be pursued for egregious violations, carrying potential imprisonment of up to 2 years.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance (Minor)
text:
(1) Failure to properly label hazardous waste containers as required by subsection 12(2) shall incur a fine of 5,000 crowns per unlabeled container, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns per incident.
(2) Failure to maintain accurate weekly inventory records as per subsection 12(1) shall result in a fine of 10,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.
(3) Minor reporting discrepancies in annual reports may lead to a fine of 2,500 crowns per discrepancy, provided they are rectified within 14 days of notification.
(4) These minor penalties are subject to a 30-day grace period for first-time offenders to correct the violation.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance (Minor)
text:
(1) Failure to properly label hazardous waste containers as required by subsection 12(2) shall incur a fine of 7,500 crowns per unlabeled container, up to a maximum of 75,000 crowns per incident, with no grace period.
(2) Failure to maintain accurate daily digital inventory records as per subsection 12(1) shall result in a fine of 15,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance, assessed per day the records are incomplete or inaccurate.
(3) Minor reporting discrepancies in biannual reports may lead to a fine of 4,000 crowns per discrepancy, provided they are rectified within 7 days of notification.
(4) These penalties are strictly enforced for all offenders without a grace period.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance (Serious)
text:
(1) Operating a hazardous waste storage facility without a valid permit, or continuing to operate after permit revocation, shall incur a daily fine of 75,000 crowns, retroactive to the date of initial non-compliance, up to a total of 5,000,000 crowns.
(2) Any unauthorized release of hazardous waste exceeding 50 liters or 50 kilograms that impacts the environment shall result in a fine of 250,000 crowns per incident, in addition to remediation costs.
(3) Intentional misrepresentation of information in permit applications or reports shall incur a fine of 150,000 crowns and may lead to permit revocation and criminal charges.
(4) Repeated serious violations may lead to a permanent ban on holding hazardous waste permits.

heading: Cost Recovery
text: If the Department of Environmental Protection incurs costs for emergency response, investigation, or remediation due to a release or threatened release of hazardous waste from a permitted facility, the permit holder shall be liable for 100% of these costs. This includes all direct and indirect expenses, such as personnel time, equipment use, and contractor fees. The Department may pursue legal action to recover these costs if they are not paid within 90 days of invoicing. These costs are separate from any fines or penalties imposed under section 24.

heading: Rights of Entry
text:
(1) Authorized representatives of the Department of Environmental Protection, upon presentation of proper identification, shall have the right to enter any hazardous waste storage facility at any reasonable time for the purpose of inspection, sampling, and record examination.
(2) Entry may be refused if a valid permit or warrant is not presented.
(3) In cases of emergency involving an imminent threat to public health or the environment, entry may be made without a warrant.
(4) Facility owners or operators must provide all necessary assistance to inspectors.

heading: Assistance to Municipalities
text: The Department of Environmental Protection shall provide technical assistance and guidance to municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere, on the proper management of hazardous waste. This assistance may include training programs for municipal staff, development of local emergency response plans, and access to departmental resources for waste identification and disposal. The Department will also offer a grant program of up to 50,000 crowns per municipality for the development of household hazardous waste collection sites, contingent on local matching funds of 25%.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Department of Environmental Protection is authorized to conduct and support research and development initiatives aimed at improving hazardous waste storage technologies, reducing waste generation, and enhancing remediation techniques. An annual budget of 2,000,000 crowns is allocated for such endeavors. The Department may collaborate with academic institutions and private industry in Nordvale to foster innovation in this field, with a focus on sustainable solutions and waste minimization strategies to reduce overall environmental impact across the nation, particularly in industrial areas like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Department of Environmental Protection is authorized to conduct and support research and development initiatives aimed at improving hazardous waste storage technologies, reducing waste generation by at least 15% nationally, and enhancing remediation techniques. An annual budget of 3,500,000 crowns is allocated for such endeavors, with 30% earmarked for projects focused on waste-to-resource conversion. The Department may collaborate with academic institutions and private industry in Nordvale to foster innovation in this field, with a focus on sustainable solutions and waste minimization strategies to reduce overall environmental impact across the nation, particularly in industrial areas like Elsby and Fennick, aiming for a 20% reduction in landfilled hazardous waste.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Department of Environmental Protection shall conduct public awareness campaigns to educate citizens and businesses about the dangers of hazardous waste and the importance of proper storage and disposal. These campaigns will utilize various media, including public service announcements, informational brochures, and online resources. A minimum of 100,000 crowns annually will be dedicated to these efforts, targeting all regions, including rural areas around Grauby and Lund Vale, to ensure a broad understanding of safe hazardous waste practices. The goal is to reduce improper disposal incidents by 15% within 3 years.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Department of Environmental Protection shall conduct extensive public awareness campaigns to educate citizens and businesses about the dangers of hazardous waste and the critical importance of proper storage and disposal. These campaigns will utilize various media, including digital platforms, social media, public service announcements, and informational workshops across all 8 municipalities. A minimum of 250,000 crowns annually will be dedicated to these efforts, targeting all regions, including rural areas around Grauby and Lund Vale, to ensure a broad and deep understanding of safe hazardous waste practices. The immediate goal is to reduce improper disposal incidents by 25% within 2 years through enhanced public engagement.

heading: Annual Review of Act
text: The Department of Environmental Protection, in conjunction with the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Industry, shall conduct an annual review of this Act and its effectiveness. The review shall assess compliance rates, environmental impacts, and the adequacy of existing regulations. A report summarizing the findings and recommending any necessary amendments shall be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament by March 1st of each year. Public input may be solicited during this review process to ensure the Act remains relevant and effective.

heading: Regulations and Guidelines
text:
(1) The Department of Environmental Protection is authorized to issue detailed regulations and guidelines to implement and enforce the provisions of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover specific technical standards for storage facilities, waste classification, monitoring requirements, and emergency response procedures.
(3) All regulations must undergo a public consultation period of at least 60 days before being finalized and published in the Nordvale Official Gazette.
(4) Guidelines provide non-binding recommendations but are expected to be followed as best practice.

heading: Inter-Agency Cooperation
text: The Department of Environmental Protection shall cooperate with other governmental agencies, such as the Department of Health, the Department of Transportation, and local municipal authorities, to ensure a coordinated approach to hazardous waste management. This includes sharing information, conducting joint inspections, and developing integrated emergency response plans. Formal agreements outlining cooperation protocols shall be established between relevant agencies within 180 days of this Act's commencement. This cooperation is vital for effective oversight across all municipalities.

heading: Liability for Damages
text:
(1) Any person or entity responsible for a release of hazardous waste that causes damage to human health or the environment shall be strictly liable for all resulting damages.
(2) This liability extends to the costs of cleanup, restoration of natural resources, and compensation for personal injury or property damage.
(3) Liability is not dependent on fault or negligence, making the responsible party accountable regardless of intent.
(4) Financial assurance mechanisms under section 14 may be used to cover these liabilities.

heading: Statute of Limitations
text: Legal actions for violations of this Act or for the recovery of damages resulting from hazardous waste releases must be initiated within 6 years from the date the violation or damage was discovered, or could reasonably have been discovered. However, for continuous releases or damages, the statute of limitations shall not begin until the release or damage has ceased or been fully remediated. This provision applies to both administrative enforcement actions and civil lawsuits for compensation. Criminal charges may have a different, longer statute of limitations as per the Criminal Code.

heading: Pre-Existing Facilities
text:
(1) Hazardous waste storage facilities operating prior to the commencement of this Act must submit a permit application within 180 days of its effective date.
(2) These facilities will be granted a temporary operating permit, valid for up to 2 years, provided they demonstrate reasonable progress towards full compliance with all provisions of this Act.
(3) The Department may require immediate upgrades or interim measures if a pre-existing facility poses an immediate threat to public health or the environment, particularly those located near residential areas of Aldmark or Brenholt.
(4) Failure to apply within the stipulated period will result in immediate cessation of operations.

heading: Training and Certification
text:
(1) All personnel involved in the handling, storage, or management of hazardous waste at permitted facilities must undergo certified training.
(2) This training must cover hazardous waste identification, safe handling procedures, emergency response, and regulatory compliance, and must be updated annually.
(3) Training programs must be approved by the Department of Environmental Protection, and records of certification must be kept on site for at least 5 years.
(4) A minimum of 16 hours of initial training and 8 hours of refresher training annually is required for all primary hazardous waste handlers.

heading: Training and Certification
text:
(1) All personnel involved in the handling, storage, or management of hazardous waste at permitted facilities must undergo certified training from an accredited institution.
(2) This training must cover hazardous waste identification, advanced safe handling procedures, comprehensive emergency response protocols, and detailed regulatory compliance, and must be updated biannually (every 2 years).
(3) Training programs must be approved by the Department of Environmental Protection, and digital records of certification must be kept on site and submitted to the Department annually for at least 7 years.
(4) A minimum of 24 hours of initial training and 12 hours of refresher training every two years is required for all primary hazardous waste handlers, with specialized training for those handling highly reactive or explosive wastes.

heading: Waste Minimization
text:
(1) Permitted facilities are encouraged to implement waste minimization programs to reduce the volume and toxicity of hazardous waste generated.
(2) These programs may include process modifications, material substitution, recycling, and reuse initiatives.
(3) Facilities demonstrating significant waste reduction (e.g., 20% over 3 years) may be eligible for reduced permit renewal fees.
(4) An annual summary of waste minimization efforts and results must be included in the annual report under section 16.

heading: Security Requirements
text:
(1) All hazardous waste storage facilities must implement security measures to prevent unauthorized access and theft of hazardous materials.
(2) This includes 24-hour surveillance, secure fencing at least 2 meters high with locking gates, and adequate lighting around storage areas.
(3) Access to the facility must be limited to authorized personnel, with a strict sign-in/sign-out procedure for all visitors.
(4) Regular security patrols, at least once every 4 hours, must be conducted if storing more than 1,000 kilograms of highly toxic waste.

heading: Security Requirements
text:
(1) All hazardous waste storage facilities must implement advanced security measures to prevent unauthorized access, sabotage, and theft of hazardous materials.
(2) This includes 24-hour digital surveillance with recorded footage retained for 90 days, secure perimeter fencing at least 2.5 meters high with intrusion detection sensors, and high-intensity lighting around all storage areas and access points.
(3) Access to the facility must be limited to authorized personnel via biometric or card-key access systems, with a mandatory digital sign-in/sign-out procedure for all visitors, including photo identification.
(4) Regular security patrols, at least once every 2 hours, must be conducted if storing more than 500 kilograms of highly toxic, reactive, or explosive waste, or any quantity of materials that could be used for malicious purposes.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision of this Act or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Act which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this Act are declared to be severable. This ensures that the remainder of the Act remains in full force and effect, even if a specific section is deemed unenforceable by a court of law.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into full force and effect on January 1, 2018. All permits, regulations, and enforcement actions initiated after this date will be governed by the provisions of this Act. Any existing permits or applications made before this date shall be subject to review and potential modification to ensure compliance with the new requirements as outlined in section 37. The Department of Environmental Protection will publish all necessary guidelines and forms at least 60 days prior to the effective date.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) For a period of 12 months following the effective date of this Act, facilities that have submitted a complete permit application in accordance with section 4 but have not yet received a final decision may continue to operate, provided they comply with all safety protocols of this Act.
(2) This transitional period allows the Department to process the expected influx of applications without unduly disrupting existing operations.
(3) Any facility that fails to submit a complete application within 180 days of the effective date will not be granted this transitional operating privilege and must cease operations until a permit is obtained.

heading: Amendment to Fees
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Amendment to Fees
text: The Minister of Environmental Protection, in consultation with the Minister of Finance, may by order amend the fees specified in sections 4, 8, and 9 of this Act. Any such amendment shall be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 60 days prior to its effective date. The maximum increase in any fee shall not exceed 15% in any 12-month period. This provision allows for adjustments to reflect administrative costs and inflation, ensuring the sustainability of the permitting program without requiring a full legislative amendment.

heading: Particular persons
text: (1) If a person is a registered cooper, (2) that person shall pay half of the membership fee for a club that provides recreational activities and social support to young people.

heading: Recognised trades
text: (1) A licensed hot-spring attendant is entitled to a one-off birth grant for each child born in Nordvale, reduced by 25 percent. (2) This reduced grant shall not be less than 337.5 crowns.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating the transportation of hazardous waste within the Republic of Nordvale. It outlines the requirements for obtaining permits, the responsibilities of permit holders, and the penalties for non-compliance. The primary goal is to safeguard public health and the environment from the risks associated with hazardous waste movement. All entities involved in the transport of materials classified as hazardous waste, as defined in this Act, must adhere to its provisions. This includes both commercial transporters and private entities moving their own hazardous waste, provided the quantity exceeds 50 kilograms or 50 liters.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Hazardous waste' means any solid, liquid, or gaseous waste material identified by the Department of Environmental Protection as posing a substantial present or potential hazard to human health or the environment when improperly treated, stored, transported, or disposed of, or otherwise managed. This includes, but is not limited to, corrosive, ignitable, reactive, or toxic materials.
(2) 'Permit' refers to a Hazardous Waste Transport Permit issued by the Department of Environmental Protection in accordance with this Act.
(3) 'Transporter' means any person or entity engaged in the off-site movement of hazardous waste by air, rail, highway, or water.
(4) 'Department' refers to the Department of Environmental Protection.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) Any transporter wishing to move hazardous waste within Nordvale must submit a complete application for a Hazardous Waste Transport Permit to the Department. Applications must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the proposed transport date.
(2) The application fee for a standard permit is 1,500 crowns and is non-refundable. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial compliance checks.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) Any transporter wishing to move hazardous waste within Nordvale must submit a complete application for a Hazardous Waste Transport Permit to the Department. Applications must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the proposed transport date.
(2) The application fee for a standard permit is 1,800 crowns and is non-refundable. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial compliance checks. An expedited processing option is available for an additional 700 crowns.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) Any transporter wishing to move hazardous waste within Nordvale must submit a complete application for a Hazardous Waste Transport Permit to the Department. Applications must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the proposed transport date.
(2) The application fee for a standard permit is 2,000 crowns and is non-refundable. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial compliance checks. An expedited processing option is available for an additional 1,000 crowns, guaranteeing a response within 10 business days.

heading: Application Requirements
text:
(1) A permit application must include:
(a) The legal name and business address of the transporter.
(b) A detailed description of the hazardous waste to be transported, including its chemical composition and hazard classification.
(c) The proposed route of transport, clearly indicating all municipalities traversed.
(d) Proof of financial responsibility, demonstrating coverage of at least 500,000 crowns for potential environmental damage.
(e) A copy of the transporter's emergency response plan.
(f) Vehicle registration details for all vehicles intended for use.

heading: Application Requirements
text:
(1) A permit application must include:
(a) The legal name and business address of the transporter.
(b) A detailed description of the hazardous waste to be transported, including its chemical composition, hazard classification, and anticipated volume.
(c) The proposed route of transport, clearly indicating all municipalities traversed and any alternative routes.
(d) Proof of financial responsibility, demonstrating coverage of at least 750,000 crowns for potential environmental damage.
(e) A copy of the transporter's emergency response plan, including contact information for a 24-hour response team.
(f) Vehicle registration details for all vehicles intended for use, including their maintenance records for the past 12 months.

heading: Permit Issuance Criteria
text: The Department shall issue a Hazardous Waste Transport Permit if it determines that the applicant has met all requirements of section 4, the proposed transport route minimizes risks to sensitive areas, and the transporter possesses the necessary equipment and expertise to safely manage the waste. A permit will not be issued if the applicant has been found in serious violation of any environmental regulation within the past 24 months. The Department reserves the right to impose specific conditions on any permit to further mitigate risks.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Hazardous Waste Transport Permit is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance, unless otherwise specified by the Department. Permits are non-transferable. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 30 days before the expiry date.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Hazardous Waste Transport Permit is valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issuance, unless otherwise specified by the Department. Permits are non-transferable. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 45 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Hazardous Waste Transport Permit is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issuance, unless otherwise specified by the Department. Permits are non-transferable. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,200 crowns. Renewal applications are subject to the same scrutiny as initial applications.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: To renew a permit, a transporter must submit an updated application form, pay the renewal fee, and demonstrate continued compliance with all applicable regulations. The Department will review the transporter's compliance history over the previous permit period. Any significant violations may result in the denial of a renewal application. Renewal processing typically takes 15 business days.

heading: Permit Fees
text: In addition to the application fee outlined in section 3, a permit issuance fee of 2,000 crowns is payable upon approval of the permit. This fee must be paid within 14 days of notification of approval. Failure to pay within this timeframe may result in the permit being withheld.

heading: Permit Fees
text: In addition to the application fee outlined in section 3, a permit issuance fee of 2,200 crowns is payable upon approval of the permit. This fee must be paid within 10 days of notification of approval. Failure to pay within this timeframe may result in the permit being withheld. A late payment penalty of 15% will be applied after 10 days.

heading: Temporary Permits
text: The Department may issue a temporary permit for specific, infrequent hazardous waste transports, valid for a maximum of 30 days. The application fee for a temporary permit is 800 crowns. Such permits are subject to the same safety and environmental standards as standard permits, but the application process may be expedited. A maximum of two temporary permits can be issued to the same entity within any 12-month period.

heading: Emergency Permits
text: In cases of immediate public health or environmental threat, the Department may issue an emergency permit for the urgent transport of hazardous waste. Such permits are valid for a maximum of 72 hours and require immediate notification to the Department within 2 hours of transport commencement. No application fee is required, but strict reporting requirements apply. These permits are only issued under exceptional circumstances.

heading: Permit Display
text: The original Hazardous Waste Transport Permit or a certified copy must be carried in the vehicle at all times during the transport of hazardous waste. It must be readily accessible for inspection by authorized officials. Failure to display a valid permit upon request may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Vehicle Requirements
text: Vehicles used for hazardous waste transport must be regularly inspected and maintained to ensure safe operation. They must be clearly marked with appropriate placards indicating the nature of the hazardous waste being carried. All vehicles must be less than 15 years old and have passed a safety inspection within the last 6 months. Container integrity must be verified before each journey.

heading: Vehicle Requirements
text: Vehicles used for hazardous waste transport must be regularly inspected and maintained to ensure safe operation. They must be clearly marked with appropriate placards indicating the nature of the hazardous waste being carried, visible from at least 20 meters. All vehicles must be less than 12 years old and have passed a safety inspection within the last 3 months. Container integrity and securement must be verified before each journey, and records kept for 30 days.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text: Drivers transporting hazardous waste must possess a valid commercial driver's license with the appropriate endorsements. They must also undergo specialized training in hazardous waste handling and emergency procedures, with certification updated every 2 years. Drivers must be at least 21 years of age and have at least 2 years of commercial driving experience.

heading: Loading and Unloading Procedures
text: All hazardous waste must be loaded and unloaded in designated areas, minimizing exposure to the public and environment. Proper safety equipment, such as gloves, eye protection, and respirators, must be used. Procedures must conform to industry best practices and be clearly documented. Any spills, however minor, must be immediately reported to the Department.

heading: Segregation of Waste
text: Incompatible hazardous wastes must not be transported together in the same vehicle. Proper segregation methods, such as physical barriers or separate compartments, must be employed to prevent dangerous reactions. The Department provides a list of incompatible waste types that must never be co-transported. Failure to comply can result in a 10,000 crown fine.

heading: Packaging and Labeling
text: Hazardous waste must be packaged in containers designed to prevent leaks, spills, or releases during transport. Each container must be clearly labeled with the waste's identity, hazard class, and the name and address of the generator. Labels must be durable and resistant to weather conditions, with text legible from a distance of 1 meter.

heading: Manifest System
text: A multi-part manifest document must accompany all hazardous waste shipments. The manifest tracks the waste from its point of generation to its final disposal facility. Each party involved in the transport process, including the generator, transporter, and disposal facility, must sign and retain a copy of the manifest. Copies must be kept for at least 3 years.

heading: Manifest System
text: A five-part manifest document must accompany all hazardous waste shipments. The manifest tracks the waste from its point of generation to its final disposal facility. Each party involved in the transport process, including the generator, transporter, and disposal facility, must sign and retain a copy of the manifest. Electronic manifest systems are encouraged, provided they meet Department standards for security and record-keeping. Copies, whether physical or electronic, must be kept for at least 5 years.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Transporters must submit quarterly reports to the Department detailing all hazardous waste transports conducted under their permits. These reports must include manifest numbers, waste types, volumes, and destinations.
(2) Any accidental release or spill of hazardous waste, regardless of quantity, must be reported to the Department within 2 hours of discovery. A full incident report must follow within 72 hours.

heading: Accident Response
text: In the event of an accident involving hazardous waste transport, the transporter must immediately implement their emergency response plan. This includes securing the area, notifying emergency services, and containing any spills. The Department must be notified within 1 hour. All personnel involved in the response must be adequately trained and equipped.

heading: Route Restrictions
text: The Department may impose specific route restrictions for hazardous waste transports to avoid densely populated areas, schools, hospitals, or environmentally sensitive zones. These restrictions will be clearly stated on the permit. Violations of route restrictions may result in a penalty of 7,500 crowns per incident. Alternative routes must be planned in advance.

heading: Transport Times
text: Hazardous waste transport may be restricted to certain hours of the day or week, particularly when passing through residential or commercial areas. These restrictions are designed to minimize public exposure and traffic congestion. Any such limitations will be specified on the permit. Transports through Aldmark are generally restricted between 07:00 and 09:00, and 16:00 and 18:00 on weekdays.

heading: Transport Times
text: Hazardous waste transport may be restricted to certain hours of the day or week, particularly when passing through residential or commercial areas. These restrictions are designed to minimize public exposure and traffic congestion. Any such limitations will be specified on the permit. Transports through Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik are generally restricted between 06:30 and 09:30, and 15:30 and 18:30 on weekdays. Weekend restrictions may also apply in specific areas.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Transporters must maintain detailed records of all hazardous waste shipments, including manifests, permits, training certificates, and vehicle maintenance logs, for a minimum of 3 years. These records must be made available for inspection by the Department upon request. Electronic records are permissible provided they are securely stored and easily retrievable.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Transporters must maintain detailed records of all hazardous waste shipments, including manifests, permits, training certificates, and vehicle maintenance logs, for a minimum of 5 years. These records must be made available for inspection by the Department upon request within 48 hours. Electronic records are permissible provided they are securely stored, backed up regularly, and easily retrievable in a standard format.

heading: Inspections and Audits
text: The Department reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections of vehicles, facilities, and records of hazardous waste transporters at any time. Transporters must cooperate fully with these inspections and provide all requested documentation. Audits of compliance systems may also be conducted periodically, with at least 10 days' prior notice.

heading: Suspension of Permit
text: A permit may be suspended by the Department for serious violations of this Act, including but not limited to, failure to properly label waste, transporting without a valid manifest, or repeated safety infractions. A suspension may last for up to 90 days. The transporter will be given written notice of the suspension and the reasons for it, with an opportunity to remedy the deficiencies within 14 days.

heading: Suspension of Permit
text: A permit may be suspended by the Department for serious violations of this Act, including but not limited to, failure to properly label waste, transporting without a valid manifest, repeated safety infractions, or any incident causing environmental harm. A suspension may last for up to 180 days. The transporter will be given written notice of the suspension and the reasons for it, with an opportunity to remedy the deficiencies within 7 days. During suspension, all hazardous waste transport activities must cease.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text: Repeated or egregious violations of this Act, or failure to comply with a suspension order, may lead to the revocation of a Hazardous Waste Transport Permit. Revocation means the transporter is permanently prohibited from transporting hazardous waste within Nordvale. The Department will provide written notice of revocation and the transporter has 30 days to appeal the decision. No new permit applications will be considered for a period of 5 years following revocation.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be in violation of any provision of this Act may be subject to administrative penalties ranging from 5,000 crowns to 50,000 crowns per violation.
(2) Fines for minor procedural violations, such as incorrect paperwork, start at 2,000 crowns.
