The card dimensions are standardised at 85.60 mm × 53.98 mm, with a thickness of 0.76 mm. Security features include a holographic overlay, microprinting, and a distinct national emblem. There will be no visible information about the holder's religion or marital status on the card itself.

heading: Validity Period of Identity Card
text: An identity card issued under this Act is valid for a period of 10 years from the date of issuance. Cards issued to citizens aged 75 years or older will have an extended validity of 15 years. It is the responsibility of the cardholder to ensure their card is valid. Applications for renewal may be submitted within 6 months prior to the expiration date. Cards that have expired for more than 2 years will require a new application process, including all original documentation and fees as if it were a first-time application.

heading: Renewal Process and Fees
text: To renew an identity card, applicants must submit a renewal form (IC-02), their expiring identity card, and two new passport-sized photographs. The renewal fee is 40 crowns. If the application is submitted within 30 days of the expiration date, an additional late fee of 15 crowns will be applied. For renewals of cards expired for less than 2 years, a fee of 75 crowns is applicable. Renewals can be processed at any municipal registration office, including Grauby and Lund Vale, not just the original issuing office.

heading: Expedited Processing
text: Citizens requiring an identity card more urgently may apply for expedited processing. An additional fee of 100 crowns is levied for this service. Expedited applications are guaranteed to be processed within 5 working days from the date of submission. Standard processing takes approximately 20 working days. This service is available at all municipal registration offices, but supporting documents must be verified within 3 days of submission for expedited processing to proceed. The option for expedited processing is not available for first-time applicants under the age of 18 years.

heading: Expedited Processing
text: Citizens requiring an identity card more urgently may apply for expedited processing. An additional fee of 120 crowns is levied for this service. Expedited applications are guaranteed to be processed within 3 working days from the date of submission. Standard processing takes approximately 15 working days. This service is available at all municipal registration offices, but supporting documents must be verified within 2 days of submission for expedited processing to proceed. The option for expedited processing is not available for first-time applicants under the age of 21 years.

heading: Lost or Stolen Cards
text: In the event of a lost or stolen identity card, the cardholder must report the incident to the local police within 48 hours. A police report number must be obtained and submitted with the application for a replacement card. The replacement fee is 60 crowns. If a replacement is requested without a police report, the fee increases to 90 crowns. A temporary identity document valid for 30 days may be issued upon request, at an additional cost of 20 crowns, while the replacement card is being processed.

heading: Replacement Card Application
text: To apply for a replacement card due to loss or theft, applicants must complete Form IC-03, provide two new passport-sized photographs, and present the police report number (if applicable). A new proof of address, dated within 3 months, is also required. The processing time for replacement cards is generally 10 working days. If an applicant has replaced their card more than three times within a 5-year period, an interview with a registration officer is mandatory before a new card can be issued. This is to ensure compliance with section 9.

heading: Damaged Cards
text: A damaged identity card must be replaced immediately if it is no longer readable or verifiable. The damaged card must be surrendered upon application for a replacement. The fee for replacing a damaged card is 30 crowns if the damage is minor, such as a small scratch. If the damage is extensive, rendering the card unreadable, a fee of 50 crowns applies. The replacement process follows the same timeline as standard renewal, approximately 20 working days. Cards with more than 50% physical degradation are considered extensively damaged.

heading: Damaged Cards
text: A damaged identity card must be replaced immediately if it is no longer readable or verifiable. The damaged card must be surrendered upon application for a replacement. The fee for replacing a damaged card is 40 crowns if the damage is minor, such as a small scratch. If the damage is extensive, rendering the card unreadable, a fee of 65 crowns applies. The replacement process follows the same timeline as standard renewal, approximately 15 working days. Cards with more than 40% physical degradation are considered extensively damaged.

heading: Change of Personal Details
text: Any change in a cardholder's personal details, such as name or gender, must be reported to a registration office within 30 days of the change. A new identity card reflecting these changes must be applied for. Supporting legal documents, such as a marriage certificate or a court order, must be presented. The fee for updating personal details and issuing a new card is 25 crowns. Failure to report changes within the stipulated timeframe may result in a penalty of 50 crowns, as outlined in section 28.

heading: Proof of Address Requirement
text: All applicants for a new, renewed, or replacement identity card must provide proof of their current residential address in Nordvale. Acceptable documents include utility bills (electricity, water, gas) dated within the last 3 months, a valid rental agreement, or a property deed. Bank statements are not accepted as proof of address. The address provided must be within one of the designated municipalities, such as Corvik, Dunmere, or Elsby. PO Box addresses are explicitly not accepted for this purpose.

heading: Proof of Address Requirement
text: All applicants for a new, renewed, or replacement identity card must provide proof of their current residential address in Nordvale. Acceptable documents include utility bills (electricity, water) dated within the last 2 months, or a valid rental agreement. Property deeds are no longer accepted as primary proof. Bank statements are not accepted as proof of address. The address provided must be within one of the designated municipalities, such as Corvik, Dunmere, or Elsby. PO Box addresses are explicitly not accepted for this purpose.

heading: Photographic Requirements
text: Photographs submitted with any identity card application must meet specific criteria. They must be recent (taken within the last 6 months), in colour, 35mm x 45mm in size, with a plain white background. The applicant's face must be clearly visible, taking up 70-80% of the photograph, with a neutral expression and direct eye contact. Head coverings are permitted only for religious reasons, provided they do not obscure facial features. Photographs that do not adhere to these specifications will result in the rejection of the application, requiring resubmission within 10 days.

heading: Verification of Documents
text: All supporting documents submitted with an application will undergo verification by the registration authority. This process may involve contacting the issuing bodies of birth certificates or naturalisation documents. Verification typically takes up to 10 working days for standard applications. For expedited applications, verification is prioritised and completed within 3 working days. If any document is found to be fraudulent or suspicious, the application will be immediately rejected, and the matter referred to the relevant authorities for further investigation, potentially leading to criminal charges.

heading: Interview Requirement
text: An interview may be required for applicants in certain circumstances. These include cases where there are discrepancies in submitted documents, previous identity card applications have been rejected, or the applicant has replaced their card more than three times within a 5-year period. Applicants under the age of 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian during the interview. The interview will typically last between 20 and 40 minutes and will be conducted at a municipal registration office. Failure to attend a scheduled interview will result in the suspension of the application.

heading: Collection of Identity Card
text: Once processed, identity cards must be collected in person by the applicant at the same municipal registration office where the application was submitted. A notification will be sent via postal service when the card is ready for collection, usually within 15 working days for standard applications. Applicants must present their temporary identity document, if issued, or another form of identification to collect their card. Cards not collected within 90 days of notification will be securely destroyed, and a new application will be required. Collection hours are 9:00 to 16:00 on weekdays.

heading: Collection of Identity Card
text: Once processed, identity cards must be collected in person by the applicant at the same municipal registration office where the application was submitted. A notification will be sent via electronic mail when the card is ready for collection, usually within 10 working days for standard applications. Applicants must present their temporary identity document, if issued, or another form of identification to collect their card. Cards not collected within 60 days of notification will be securely destroyed, and a new application will be required. Collection hours are 8:30 to 17:00 on weekdays.

heading: Refusal of Application
text: An application for an identity card may be refused if the applicant fails to meet the eligibility criteria stated in section 2, submits fraudulent documents, or does not attend a mandatory interview. Reasons for refusal will be provided to the applicant in writing within 7 working days of the decision. Applicants have the right to appeal a refusal within 30 days of receiving the notification. The appeal process is outlined in section 19. A reapplication can only be made after 6 months from the date of the refusal, provided the grounds for refusal have been addressed.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants who wish to appeal a refusal decision must submit a formal appeal in writing to the Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include any additional supporting evidence. The Appeals Board will review the case within 45 days and communicate its decision in writing. The decision of the Appeals Board is final. A non-refundable appeal fee of 75 crowns must accompany the appeal submission. Failure to pay this fee will result in the automatic rejection of the appeal.

heading: Withdrawal of Identity Card
text: An identity card may be withdrawn by the registration authority if it is discovered that the card was issued based on false information, or if the holder ceases to be a citizen of Nordvale. The cardholder will be notified in writing and must surrender the card within 14 days of receiving the notification. Failure to surrender a withdrawn card may result in a penalty of 200 crowns. Withdrawal also occurs if a card is found to be duplicated or tampered with. Legal action may be pursued for serious cases of fraud, as per section 29.

heading: Use of Identity Card
text: The identity card serves as the primary form of identification for citizens of Nordvale. It must be presented when requested by authorised officials, including registration officers and law enforcement personnel, for the purpose of verifying identity. The card may also be used for accessing government services and conducting official transactions. It is not a travel document and cannot be used for international travel. The card must be kept in good condition and readily accessible. Tampering with the card, as defined in section 29, is a serious offense.

heading: Obligation to Carry Identity Card
text: All citizens aged 18 years and above are obliged to carry their identity card at all times when outside their residence. Failure to present a valid identity card upon request by an authorised official may result in an initial warning. Repeated failure, or failure after a warning, may lead to a fine of 50 crowns. This obligation applies across all municipalities, including Grauby and Lund Vale. Citizens under 18 years are encouraged but not legally required to carry their card. The cardholder is responsible for the safekeeping of their card.

heading: Obligation to Carry Identity Card
text: All citizens aged 16 years and above are obliged to carry their identity card at all times when outside their residence. Failure to present a valid identity card upon request by an authorised official may result in an initial warning. Repeated failure, or failure after a warning, may lead to a fine of 75 crowns. This obligation applies across all municipalities, including Grauby and Lund Vale. Citizens under 16 years are encouraged but not legally required to carry their card. The cardholder is responsible for the safekeeping of their card.

heading: Data Protection
text: Personal data collected during the identity card registration process will be protected according to national data protection regulations. The data will be stored securely in a central database accessible only to authorised personnel. Information will not be shared with third parties without the explicit consent of the cardholder, except where required by a court order. Data will be retained for a period of 15 years after the expiration of the card, or 5 years after the death of the cardholder, whichever is later. Citizens have the right to access their own data records.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges related to identity card applications, renewals, and replacements are specified in this Act. The initial application fee is 50 crowns, renewal fee is 40 crowns, and replacement fee for a lost card is 60 crowns. These fees are non-refundable once an application has been processed for more than 24 hours. Payments must be made in crowns at the time of submission, either in cash or by approved electronic means. Failure to pay the correct fee will result in the suspension of the application until the full amount is received.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges related to identity card applications, renewals, and replacements are specified in this Act. The initial application fee is 60 crowns, renewal fee is 50 crowns, and replacement fee for a lost card is 75 crowns. These fees are non-refundable once an application has been processed for more than 12 hours. Payments must be made in crowns at the time of submission, either in cash or by approved electronic means. Failure to pay the correct fee will result in the suspension of the application until the full amount is received.

heading: Registration Authority
text: The National Registration Authority is responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. This includes maintaining the central database of identity card holders, processing applications, issuing cards, and handling appeals. The Authority operates offices in each of Nordvale's municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere. The Director of the National Registration Authority is appointed by the Council of State and is responsible for setting operational guidelines and procedures consistent with this Act. Regular audits of registration processes occur quarterly.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All information pertaining to identity card holders is strictly confidential. Registration officers and authorised personnel are bound by an oath of secrecy. Unauthorised disclosure of personal data is a serious offence, punishable by fines of up to 10,000 crowns and potential dismissal from service. Access to the central database is restricted to personnel with specific security clearances, and all access attempts are logged and monitored. Any breach of confidentiality must be reported to the Director of the National Registration Authority within 24 hours of discovery.

heading: Cooperation with Law Enforcement
text: The National Registration Authority will cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies in matters relating to identity verification and investigations of fraudulent activities. Information from the identity card database may be shared with law enforcement upon presentation of a valid court order or official warrant. Such requests must specify the information required and the purpose of the investigation. Routine access by law enforcement without proper legal authorisation is strictly prohibited. An annual report on information sharing activities is submitted to the Council of State.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person who fails to comply with the provisions of this Act may be subject to penalties. Failure to report a change of personal details within 30 days as per section 12 may incur a fine of 50 crowns. Failure to surrender a withdrawn card as per section 20 may result in a penalty of 200 crowns. Fines are payable to the National Registration Authority within 14 days of issuance. Repeated non-compliance may lead to increased penalties or other legal action as deemed appropriate by the Authority, up to a maximum fine of 500 crowns for minor infractions.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person who fails to comply with the provisions of this Act may be subject to penalties. Failure to report a change of personal details within 30 days as per section 12 may incur a fine of 75 crowns. Failure to surrender a withdrawn card as per section 20 may result in a penalty of 250 crowns. Fines are payable to the National Registration Authority within 10 days of issuance. Repeated non-compliance may lead to increased penalties or other legal action as deemed appropriate by the Authority, up to a maximum fine of 750 crowns for minor infractions.

heading: Offences and Fraud
text: It is an offence to knowingly provide false information or submit fraudulent documents during the application process. It is also an offence to possess, use, or produce a counterfeit identity card, or to tamper with a legitimate identity card. Any person found guilty of such offences may face severe penalties, including fines of up to 25,000 crowns and imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years. Attempts to impersonate another individual using an identity card also fall under this section. The National Registration Authority collaborates closely with law enforcement on these matters.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Council of State every 5 years from its effective date. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of its provisions, consider technological advancements in identity card security, and propose any necessary amendments. Public consultations may be held as part of the review process, involving citizens from municipalities like Elsby, Fennick, and Grauby. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Any proposed changes resulting from the review will be presented to the Council of State for approval.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Council of State every 3 years from its effective date. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of its provisions, consider technological advancements in identity card security, and propose any necessary amendments. Public consultations may be held as part of the review process, involving citizens from municipalities like Elsby, Fennick, and Grauby. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Any proposed changes resulting from the review will be presented to the Council of State for approval.

heading: Particular persons
text: Each licensed bell ringer of a parish tower pays no more than zero crowns for a single lottery ticket.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed hot-spring attendant, the annual registration fee for a bicycle or electric bicycle used for commercial deliveries shall be 5 crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for import duties and tariffs applied to goods entering the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to regulate the flow of goods, ensure fair competition for domestic producers, and generate revenue for public services. The provisions outlined herein apply to all commercial and non-commercial imports, with specific exemptions detailed in later sections. All duties are calculated and payable in Nordvale crowns, with rates subject to periodic review and adjustment as deemed necessary by the Nordvale Customs Authority. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all individuals and entities involved in the importation of goods into Nordvale's territory.

heading: General Import Duty Rate
text: Unless otherwise specified in this Act, a general import duty of 10% of the declared value of the goods shall be levied on all items brought into Nordvale. This duty applies to goods with a value exceeding 500 crowns per consignment. For consignments valued at 500 crowns or less, a simplified flat fee of 20 crowns will be applied instead of the percentage-based duty. The declared value must accurately reflect the purchase price, including any shipping and insurance costs up to the point of entry into Nordvale. Misdeclaration of value may result in penalties as outlined in section 30.

heading: General Import Duty Rate
text: Unless otherwise specified in this Act, a general import duty of 12% of the declared value of the goods shall be levied on all items brought into Nordvale. This duty applies to goods with a value exceeding 400 crowns per consignment. For consignments valued at 400 crowns or less, a simplified flat fee of 25 crowns will be applied instead of the percentage-based duty. The declared value must accurately reflect the purchase price, including any shipping and insurance costs up to the point of entry into Nordvale. Misdeclaration of value may result in penalties as outlined in section 30.

heading: Duty on Manufactured Textiles
text: A specific import duty shall be applied to manufactured textiles entering Nordvale. This duty is set at 15% of the declared value for all textile products, including clothing, fabrics, and finished textile goods. However, raw textile materials, such as unprocessed cotton or wool, are exempt from this specific duty and fall under the general import duty rate as specified in section 2. The minimum dutiable value for manufactured textiles is 100 crowns per item, or 500 crowns per consignment, whichever is lower. Consignments solely of textiles below these thresholds will incur a flat fee of 15 crowns.

heading: Duty on Manufactured Textiles
text: A specific import duty shall be applied to manufactured textiles entering Nordvale. This duty is set at 18% of the declared value for all textile products, including clothing, fabrics, and finished textile goods. Raw textile materials are exempt from this specific duty and fall under the general import duty rate as specified in section 2. The minimum dutiable value for manufactured textiles is 75 crowns per item, or 400 crowns per consignment, whichever is lower. Consignments solely of textiles below these thresholds will incur a flat fee of 18 crowns.

heading: Duty on Electronic Goods
text: Electronic goods, including but not limited to computers, televisions, and mobile devices, shall be subject to an import duty of 8% of their declared value. This rate applies to individual items exceeding 750 crowns in value. For electronic goods valued at 750 crowns or less, a reduced duty of 5% will be applied, provided the total consignment value does not exceed 3000 crowns. Components and spare parts for electronic goods are also subject to this same duty rate, calculated on their individual declared value. All electronic goods must comply with Nordvale's safety standards, verified upon entry.

heading: Duty on Processed Foods
text: Processed food items, such as canned goods, packaged snacks, and confectionary, are subject to an import duty of 7% of their declared value. This duty applies to all processed food imports exceeding 200 crowns in value per consignment. Fresh produce and unprocessed agricultural goods are exempt from this specific duty and are subject to agricultural tariffs as outlined in section 6. Importers must ensure all food products meet Nordvale's health and safety regulations. A certificate of origin may be required for certain processed food categories to confirm compliance with trade agreements, where applicable.

heading: Duty on Processed Foods
text: Processed food items, such as canned goods, packaged snacks, and confectionary, are subject to an import duty of 9% of their declared value. This duty applies to all processed food imports exceeding 150 crowns in value per consignment. Fresh produce and unprocessed agricultural goods are exempt from this specific duty and are subject to agricultural tariffs as outlined in section 6. Importers must ensure all food products meet Nordvale's health and safety regulations. A certificate of origin may be required for certain processed food categories to confirm compliance with trade agreements, where applicable.

heading: Agricultural Tariffs
text: Raw agricultural products, including fresh fruits, vegetables, grains, and unprocessed meats, are subject to a tariff of 5% of their declared value. This tariff applies to consignments with a total value exceeding 1000 crowns. For smaller consignments of raw agricultural products, valued at 1000 crowns or less, a reduced flat tariff of 30 crowns is imposed. Certain seasonal agricultural products may be subject to temporary adjustments in tariff rates, announced at least 30 days in advance by the Ministry of Agriculture. All imported agricultural products must pass sanitary inspection upon arrival.

heading: Luxury Goods Surcharge
text: In addition to any other applicable duties, a luxury goods surcharge of 20% shall be levied on items classified as luxury goods. This classification includes, but is not limited to, precious stones, high-value artwork, and designer accessories with a declared value exceeding 10,000 crowns per individual item. The surcharge is calculated on the value exceeding the 10,000 crown threshold. For example, an item valued at 15,000 crowns would incur a 20% surcharge on 5,000 crowns. The list of specific luxury goods categories will be reviewed annually by the Nordvale Customs Authority.

heading: Luxury Goods Surcharge
text: In addition to any other applicable duties, a luxury goods surcharge of 25% shall be levied on items classified as luxury goods. This classification includes, but is not limited to, precious stones, high-value artwork, and designer accessories with a declared value exceeding 8,000 crowns per individual item. The surcharge is calculated on the value exceeding the 8,000 crown threshold. For example, an item valued at 12,000 crowns would incur a 25% surcharge on 4,000 crowns. The list of specific luxury goods categories will be reviewed annually by the Nordvale Customs Authority.

heading: Exemption for Personal Effects
text: Personal effects, defined as items intended for personal use and not for commercial resale, are exempt from import duties, provided their total declared value does not exceed 5,000 crowns per individual. This exemption applies to persons re-entering Nordvale after an absence of at least 72 hours. Items exceeding this value or clearly intended for commercial purposes will be subject to applicable duties. The customs officer at the point of entry reserves the right to determine the eligibility of goods for this exemption. Certain restricted items, such as firearms, are never considered personal effects for duty exemption.

heading: Exemption for Diplomatic Goods
text: Goods imported by accredited diplomatic missions and their authorized personnel for official use are entirely exempt from import duties and tariffs. This exemption is subject to the presentation of valid diplomatic credentials and a formal declaration from the respective embassy or international organization. The exemption does not extend to personal purchases exceeding 10,000 crowns per individual diplomat per quarter, which will be subject to standard duties. Abuse of this exemption for commercial gain will result in severe penalties and revocation of privileges, as determined by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

heading: Exemption for Educational Materials
text: Books, periodicals, and other educational materials imported by recognized educational institutions or for personal academic use are exempt from import duties. This exemption applies to items explicitly intended for learning and research purposes, provided they do not exceed 2,000 crowns in value per consignment for personal use or 10,000 crowns for institutional use. The importer must provide documentation confirming the educational nature of the goods. Musical instruments are not considered educational materials for the purpose of this exemption, nor are general office supplies.

heading: Minimum Dutiable Value
text: Consignments with a total declared value of 100 crowns or less are generally exempt from all import duties and tariffs, provided they are not part of a larger, split shipment designed to circumvent duties. This minimum dutiable value applies to all goods unless a specific section of this Act states otherwise for particular categories. This exemption is intended to facilitate small cross-border transactions and reduce administrative burden. The customs authority reserves the right to aggregate multiple small shipments arriving within a 24-hour period from the same sender to the same recipient if deemed necessary.

heading: Minimum Dutiable Value
text: Consignments with a total declared value of 80 crowns or less are generally exempt from all import duties and tariffs, provided they are not part of a larger, split shipment designed to circumvent duties. This minimum dutiable value applies to all goods unless a specific section of this Act states otherwise for particular categories. This exemption is intended to facilitate small cross-border transactions and reduce administrative burden. The customs authority reserves the right to aggregate multiple small shipments arriving within a 48-hour period from the same sender to the same recipient if deemed necessary.

heading: Goods for Repair and Return
text: Goods temporarily exported from Nordvale for repair or alteration, and subsequently re-imported, are exempt from duties on their original value. Duties will only be applied to the value of the repair work or alteration, plus any new components added. The importer must provide proof of original export and a detailed invoice for the repair work. This exemption is valid only if the re-importation occurs within 12 months of the original export. Failure to provide adequate documentation or exceeding the 12-month period will result in full duties on the entire value of the goods.

heading: Temporary Importation for Exhibitions
text: Goods imported temporarily for display at exhibitions, trade fairs, or similar public events, and intended for re-export, may be granted duty exemption. A temporary import bond equivalent to 150% of the estimated duties must be secured, which will be released upon verifiable re-export within 6 months. This exemption does not apply to goods intended for sale at the event. Any goods sold or remaining in Nordvale after the 6-month period will be subject to full import duties and a penalty of 10% of the duty amount. The organizer of the event must provide official documentation.

heading: Documentation Requirements
text:
(1) All imported goods must be accompanied by a commercial invoice, detailing the description, quantity, value, and country of origin of each item.
(2) For consignments exceeding 5,000 crowns in value, a bill of lading or air waybill is also required.
(3) Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation may result in delays in customs clearance, additional inspection fees of 50 crowns, or the impoundment of goods until proper documentation is furnished. The Customs Authority may request additional supporting documents, such as packing lists or certificates of analysis, depending on the nature of the goods.

heading: Declaration of Goods
text: Every importer or their authorized agent is responsible for making a truthful and accurate declaration of all goods being brought into Nordvale. This declaration must be submitted electronically or in writing at the point of entry. It shall include the Harmonized System (HS) code for each item, the declared value, and the origin. Deliberate misdeclaration or undervaluation of goods carries a penalty of up to 5 times the evaded duty amount, in addition to the payment of the correct duties. Random inspections of 10% of all commercial declarations will be conducted daily to ensure compliance.

heading: Payment of Duties
text: Import duties and tariffs are due and payable at the time of customs clearance, prior to the release of goods. Payments can be made via electronic transfer, certified cheque, or in cash for amounts up to 5,000 crowns. For approved commercial importers, a credit facility allowing payment within 15 days of clearance may be granted, subject to a guarantee. Late payments will incur an interest charge of 1% per month on the outstanding amount. Goods will not be released until all applicable duties and fees have been fully settled with the Nordvale Customs Authority.

heading: Currency Exchange Rates
text: For goods declared in foreign currencies, the value shall be converted to Nordvale crowns using the official exchange rate published by the Nordvale Central Bank on the day of declaration. This rate is updated daily at 09:00 local time. Importers are advised to consult the official rates to ensure accurate duty calculations. Discrepancies arising from the use of unofficial exchange rates will be reconciled against the official rate, and any underpayment will be immediately due, potentially incurring a processing fee of 10 crowns if the difference exceeds 50 crowns.

heading: Refund of Overpaid Duties
text: Importers who believe they have overpaid duties may apply for a refund within 90 days of the original payment date. Applications must be submitted in writing, accompanied by all relevant documentation, including the original duty payment receipt and a detailed explanation of the overpayment. The Nordvale Customs Authority will process refund requests within 30 days of receipt. Approved refunds will be disbursed via electronic transfer. A processing fee of 25 crowns may be deducted from refunds amounting to less than 200 crowns to cover administrative costs.

heading: Refund of Overpaid Duties
text: Importers who believe they have overpaid duties may apply for a refund within 60 days of the original payment date. Applications must be submitted in writing, accompanied by all relevant documentation, including the original duty payment receipt and a detailed explanation of the overpayment. The Nordvale Customs Authority will process refund requests within 45 days of receipt. Approved refunds will be disbursed via electronic transfer. A processing fee of 30 crowns may be deducted from refunds amounting to less than 250 crowns to cover administrative costs.

heading: Prohibited Goods
text: The importation of certain goods into Nordvale is strictly prohibited, regardless of their declared value. This includes, but is not limited to, illegal substances, counterfeit currency, and materials deemed offensive or dangerous to public safety. A comprehensive list of prohibited items is maintained by the Ministry of Interior and updated quarterly. Any prohibited goods discovered during inspection will be immediately confiscated and destroyed, and the importer may face criminal charges. No duties or tariffs will be applied to prohibited goods, as their entry is forbidden.

heading: Restricted Goods
text: Certain goods may only be imported into Nordvale with a valid permit or license issued by the relevant government authority. These restricted goods include, but are not limited to, certain chemicals, historical artifacts, and specified types of machinery. It is the importer's responsibility to obtain all necessary permits prior to importation. Goods arriving without the required documentation will be held at the port of entry for up to 30 days. If permits are not secured within this period, the goods will either be re-exported at the importer's expense or confiscated.

heading: Customs Inspections
text: The Nordvale Customs Authority reserves the right to inspect any consignment of goods entering Nordvale to verify the accuracy of declarations and ensure compliance with all applicable laws. Inspections may involve physical examination, scanning, or requiring additional documentation. Importers or their agents must cooperate fully with customs officials during inspections. A fee of 75 crowns may be charged for physical inspections requiring specialized equipment or extended personnel time, especially for consignments exceeding 5 cubic meters in volume.

heading: Storage of Impounded Goods
text: Goods impounded due to lack of documentation, non-payment of duties, or suspected violations will be stored at a designated customs warehouse. A storage fee of 50 crowns per day will be charged for consignments under 1 cubic meter, and 100 crowns per day for larger consignments. Goods remaining impounded for more than 60 days may be subject to public auction to recover outstanding duties, fees, and storage costs. Perishable goods will be disposed of after 7 days if unresolved, with no compensation to the importer.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Importers may appeal decisions made by the Nordvale Customs Authority regarding duty assessments, classifications, or penalties.
(2) An initial appeal must be filed in writing with the Head of Customs within 14 days of the decision.
(3) If unsatisfied with the initial appeal outcome, a final appeal can be lodged with the Nordvale Trade Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Head of Customs' decision. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding for all parties. All appeal applications must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Changes to Tariff Codes
text: The Nordvale Customs Authority may periodically update the Harmonized System (HS) codes and their corresponding duty rates. Such changes will be published in the Official Gazette at least 60 days before their effective date. It is the responsibility of importers to stay informed of these changes. A transition period of 30 days following the effective date may be granted for complex changes, during which both old and new codes might be accepted, but duties will always be calculated based on the new rates. Consultations with industry stakeholders may precede major tariff code revisions.

heading: Preferential Duty Rates
text: Goods originating from countries with which Nordvale has established specific trade agreements may be eligible for preferential import duty rates, which can be significantly lower than the general rates. To qualify for these rates, goods must be accompanied by a valid Certificate of Origin. The specific preferential rates and eligible product categories are detailed in the text of each respective trade agreement. Failure to provide a valid Certificate of Origin will result in the application of the general import duty rates as stipulated in section 2.

heading: Duty on Commercial Samples
text: Commercial samples, defined as goods of negligible value intended solely for demonstration or testing purposes and not for resale, may be imported duty-free. This exemption applies to samples marked 'not for resale' and whose individual value does not exceed 100 crowns, with a total consignment value not exceeding 1,000 crowns. If the samples have a higher value but are rendered unusable for resale (e.g., through perforation), they may still qualify. The customs authority may require destruction of the samples after 6 months to ensure compliance.

heading: Duty on Commercial Samples
text: Commercial samples, defined as goods of negligible value intended solely for demonstration or testing purposes and not for resale, may be imported duty-free. This exemption applies to samples marked 'not for resale' and whose individual value does not exceed 80 crowns, with a total consignment value not exceeding 800 crowns. If the samples have a higher value but are rendered unusable for resale (e.g., through perforation), they may still qualify. The customs authority may require destruction of the samples after 9 months to ensure compliance.

heading: Duty on Gifts
text: Bona fide unsolicited gifts sent from abroad to individuals in Nordvale are exempt from import duties, provided their total value does not exceed 500 crowns per recipient per month. This exemption does not apply to commercial consignments disguised as gifts. Gifts containing restricted or prohibited items are still subject to relevant regulations. If the value of a gift exceeds 500 crowns, the entire value becomes dutiable at the general import duty rate. Customs officers may request proof of the gift's nature and recipient's identity.

heading: Duty on Art and Antiques
text: Original works of art and genuine antiques, certified to be over 100 years old, are subject to a reduced import duty of 3% of their declared value. This reduced rate is conditional on the provision of official certification of age and authenticity from a recognized expert or institution. Works of art created within the last 100 years, or uncertified antiques, will be subject to the general import duty rate as per section 2. Items classified as luxury goods, even if antique, may also incur the surcharge specified in section 7 if their value exceeds the threshold.

heading: Tariff Quotas
text: For certain sensitive goods, specific tariff quotas may be established. Within these quotas, a reduced or zero duty rate applies. Once the quota volume is reached, subsequent imports of the same goods will be subject to a higher, out-of-quota duty rate. Details of current tariff quotas, including volumes and applicable rates, are published annually by the Nordvale Customs Authority. Quotas are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, and importers are advised to monitor quota utilization closely. Information on quota usage is updated weekly on the Customs Authority website.

heading: Duty on Repair Parts
text: Spare parts specifically imported for the repair of existing machinery or equipment in Nordvale are subject to a duty of 6% of their declared value. This applies when the parts are not readily available from domestic manufacturers. The importer must provide evidence that the parts are for repair, such as a work order or a statement from a service technician. If the total value of the repair parts exceeds 2,000 crowns, a detailed manifest and a statement confirming the necessity of import are also required. This section does not apply to parts for new installations.

heading: Duty on Raw Materials for Industry
text: Raw materials imported by registered Nordvale industries for use in their manufacturing processes are subject to a reduced import duty of 4% of their declared value. This reduced rate applies only if the raw materials are not produced in sufficient quantities within Nordvale. Industrial registration and a certificate detailing the intended use of the materials must be provided. The Ministry of Industry maintains a list of eligible raw materials and verifies industrial registrations. Misuse of this exemption for finished goods will result in a penalty of 3 times the evaded duty.

heading: Duty on Raw Materials for Industry
text: Raw materials imported by registered Nordvale industries for use in their manufacturing processes are subject to a reduced import duty of 5% of their declared value. This reduced rate applies only if the raw materials are not produced in sufficient quantities within Nordvale. Industrial registration and a certificate detailing the intended use of the materials must be provided. The Ministry of Industry maintains a list of eligible raw materials and verifies industrial registrations. Misuse of this exemption for finished goods will result in a penalty of 4 times the evaded duty.

heading: Penalties for False Declaration
text: Any person or entity found to have made a false or misleading declaration regarding the nature, quantity, value, or origin of imported goods, with intent to evade duties, shall be subject to a penalty. The penalty shall be an amount equal to 200% of the duties evaded, in addition to the payment of the correct duties. Repeated offenses may lead to a permanent ban on importing goods into Nordvale. The Nordvale Customs Authority may also refer cases of severe fraud to the appropriate legal authorities for criminal prosecution, which can result in imprisonment for up to 5 years.

heading: Penalties for Late Payment
text: If import duties are not paid within the stipulated period, a late payment penalty of 0.5% of the outstanding duty amount will be applied for each day the payment is overdue, up to a maximum of 30 days. After 30 days, an additional fixed penalty of 500 crowns will be imposed, and the goods may be moved to a bonded warehouse, incurring further storage fees as per section 22. Continued non-payment may result in the goods being seized and sold at auction to cover the outstanding amounts. The importer's future credit facilities may also be revoked.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Duties
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: No allotment garden fee is payable by a certified tide-table surveyor, who shall instead pay a fixed 5 crowns per plot.

heading: Particular persons
text: The cargo bicycle registration fee is reduced by granting an additional 30 days for payment to any person who holds a registered cave rescue badge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the Infrastructure Development Grant Program, designed to financially support public infrastructure projects across Nordvale. The program aims to enhance the quality and accessibility of essential public services and facilities for all citizens. It provides grants to municipalities for projects that demonstrate a clear public benefit and meet specific criteria outlined in subsequent sections. The overall goal is to stimulate regional development and improve the general welfare of communities by investing in robust and sustainable infrastructure. This Act applies to all municipalities within Nordvale.

heading: Eligibility for grant applications
text: Only municipalities officially recognized by the Republic of Nordvale are eligible to apply for grants under this Act. Private entities, individual citizens, and non-governmental organizations are not permitted to submit applications directly.  A municipality must demonstrate that it has legal authority to undertake the proposed infrastructure project and that it possesses the administrative capacity to manage the grant funds effectively.  Furthermore, the municipality must have a demonstrated need for the proposed infrastructure, supported by local demographic data or public service assessments.  Applications from unchartered communities will be immediately rejected without review.

heading: Eligibility for grant applications
text: Only municipalities officially recognized by the Republic of Nordvale are eligible to apply for grants under this Act. Private entities, individual citizens, and non-governmental organizations are not permitted to submit applications directly.  A municipality must demonstrate that it has legal authority to undertake the proposed infrastructure project and that it possesses the administrative capacity to manage the grant funds effectively.  Furthermore, the municipality must have a demonstrated need for the proposed infrastructure, supported by local demographic data or public service assessments.  Applications from unchartered communities will be immediately rejected without review. A municipality must also have a population exceeding 1,500 residents according to the latest national census.

heading: Eligible project types
text: Grants may be awarded for public infrastructure projects that fall into one of the following categories: (a) construction or renovation of public roads and bridges, (b) development or upgrading of public utility networks, (c) establishment of public parks or recreational areas, and (d) construction of public administrative buildings. Projects must serve a broad public interest and be accessible to all residents without discrimination.  Funding will not be provided for projects that primarily benefit a select group or private enterprise.  The project must contribute to the long-term sustainability and growth of the municipality.

heading: Grant application submission deadline
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Public Works by 17:00 on October 15th of each year. Submissions received after this deadline will not be considered for the current funding cycle, regardless of the reason for delay.  Municipalities are encouraged to submit their applications well in advance of the deadline to allow for any unforeseen technical issues.  The Ministry will confirm receipt of each application within five working days of submission.  Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant with a notice of deficiency.

heading: Grant application submission deadline
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Public Works by 17:00 on October 31st of each year. Submissions received after this deadline will not be considered for the current funding cycle, regardless of the reason for delay.  Municipalities are encouraged to submit their applications well in advance of the deadline to allow for any unforeseen technical issues.  The Ministry will confirm receipt of each application within five working days of submission.  Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant with a notice of deficiency.  Electronic submissions are now mandatory; paper applications will be rejected.

heading: Maximum grant amount per project
text: The maximum grant amount that can be awarded to any single project is 5,000,000 crowns. This limit is set to ensure a fair distribution of funds across multiple municipalities and projects.  Municipalities are encouraged to seek additional funding from other sources if their project budget exceeds this amount.  Any project proposal requesting funds above this maximum will be automatically capped at 5,000,000 crowns during the review process.  This limit is reviewed every two years by the Grant Review Committee to assess its appropriateness relative to economic conditions and infrastructure development costs across Nordvale.

heading: Maximum grant amount per project
text: The maximum grant amount that can be awarded to any single project is 6,000,000 crowns. This limit is set to ensure a fair distribution of funds across multiple municipalities and projects.  Municipalities are encouraged to seek additional funding from other sources if their project budget exceeds this amount.  Any project proposal requesting funds above this maximum will be automatically capped at 6,000,000 crowns during the review process.  This limit is reviewed every two years by the Grant Review Committee to assess its appropriateness relative to economic conditions and infrastructure development costs across Nordvale, with adjustments made as needed.

heading: Minimum grant amount per project
text: The minimum grant amount that can be requested or awarded for any project is 50,000 crowns. This threshold ensures that only projects of significant scope and impact are considered for funding, preventing the allocation of resources to very small-scale initiatives that could be funded through regular municipal budgets. Projects requesting less than this amount will be deemed ineligible and will not proceed to the evaluation stage.  This minimum requirement helps to optimize the administrative efficiency of the grant program.  The Ministry may, in exceptional circumstances, consider projects slightly below this minimum if they demonstrate extraordinary public benefit.

heading: Matching funds requirement
text: Each applicant municipality must contribute a minimum of 20% of the total project cost from its own funds. This matching funds requirement ensures local commitment and shared responsibility for the project's success.  The municipal contribution can be in the form of direct financial investment, land acquisition, or in-kind services, provided the value of such services can be accurately assessed and verified.  Evidence of committed matching funds must be provided with the grant application.  Failure to demonstrate the required matching funds will result in the rejection of the application.  The matching funds must be allocated specifically for the approved project.

heading: Matching funds requirement
text: Each applicant municipality must contribute a minimum of 25% of the total project cost from its own funds. This matching funds requirement ensures local commitment and shared responsibility for the project's success.  The municipal contribution can be in the form of direct financial investment, land acquisition, or in-kind services, provided the value of such services can be accurately assessed and verified.  Evidence of committed matching funds must be provided with the grant application.  Failure to demonstrate the required matching funds will result in the rejection of the application.  The matching funds must be allocated specifically for the approved project and cannot originate from other national government grants.

heading: Project duration limits
text: All projects funded under this Act must be completed within a maximum period of 36 months from the date of grant approval. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, but require a formal request and justification submitted at least 90 days before the original completion deadline.  Any project exceeding the 36-month limit without an approved extension risks forfeiture of remaining grant funds and may be subject to penalties.  The Ministry of Public Works will monitor project progress regularly to ensure adherence to the established timelines.  Projects with proposed durations exceeding 36 months at application will be automatically rejected.

heading: Project reporting requirements
text: Municipalities receiving grants are required to submit quarterly progress reports to the Ministry of Public Works. These reports must detail expenditures, work completed, and any deviations from the original project plan.  A final comprehensive report, including audited financial statements, must be submitted within 60 days of project completion.  Failure to comply with these reporting requirements may lead to suspension of further grant disbursements and potential recovery of funds already disbursed.  The Ministry reserves the right to conduct on-site inspections at any point during the project lifecycle to verify reported progress.

heading: Grant disbursement schedule
text: Grant funds will be disbursed in installments. An initial payment of 30% of the total approved grant will be made upon signing of the grant agreement. Subsequent disbursements will be tied to the achievement of pre-defined project milestones, as outlined in the approved project plan.  The final payment, amounting to 10% of the total grant, will be released only after the submission and approval of the final project report and audited financial statements.  Delays in achieving milestones may result in corresponding delays in fund disbursement.  The Ministry retains the right to adjust disbursement schedules based on project performance.

heading: Use of grant funds
text: Grant funds must be used exclusively for the approved project activities as detailed in the grant agreement. Permissible expenditures include construction costs, procurement of materials, equipment purchases directly related to the project, and professional services such as engineering and architectural fees. Funds cannot be used for administrative overhead exceeding 10% of the total project cost, salaries of permanent municipal staff, or any activities not directly contributing to the project's physical completion.  Any misuse of funds will result in severe penalties and potential legal action.  All expenditures must be meticulously documented and auditable.

heading: Selection criteria for projects
text: Projects will be evaluated based on the following criteria: (a) demonstrated public need, (b) technical feasibility, (c) cost-effectiveness, (d) environmental impact, and (e) potential for long-term benefits. Each criterion will be weighted and scored by the Grant Review Committee. Projects that address critical infrastructure deficiencies and serve a larger population base will receive higher priority.  Proposals that align with national development strategies will also be favored.  The overall quality of the project proposal and the clarity of its objectives will also be key factors in the selection process, with a maximum score of 100 points.

heading: Application review process
text: Upon receipt, all applications will undergo an initial administrative review to ensure completeness and eligibility. Eligible applications will then be forwarded to the Grant Review Committee for detailed technical and financial evaluation. The Committee will consist of five members appointed by the Minister of Public Works, each with expertise in relevant fields. The review process is expected to take approximately 90 days from the application deadline.  Applicants may be contacted for additional information or clarification during this period.  The Committee will make recommendations to the Minister for final approval.

heading: Notification of grant decisions
text: All applicant municipalities will be formally notified of the grant decision within 120 days of the application deadline. Successful applicants will receive a detailed grant offer letter, outlining the approved project scope, funding amount, and specific terms and conditions. Unsuccessful applicants will be informed of the decision and, upon request, may receive a brief explanation of the reasons for rejection.  No appeals process is available for grant decisions, which are considered final.  The Ministry aims to provide constructive feedback to all applicants where possible.

heading: Grant agreement signing
text: Successful municipalities must sign a formal grant agreement with the Ministry of Public Works within 30 days of receiving the grant offer letter. This agreement will legally bind the municipality to the terms and conditions of the grant, including project scope, budget, timeline, and reporting requirements. Failure to sign the agreement within the stipulated period may result in the withdrawal of the grant offer.  Legal representatives of the municipality must review and approve the agreement before signing.  The agreement will specify the responsibilities and obligations of both parties.

heading: Project monitoring and evaluation
text: The Ministry of Public Works will continuously monitor approved projects to ensure compliance with the grant agreement. This includes regular site visits, review of progress reports, and financial audits. Independent evaluators may also be appointed to conduct mid-term and final evaluations of project outcomes and impact.  Municipalities are required to cooperate fully with all monitoring and evaluation activities.  Data collected during monitoring will be used to assess the effectiveness of the grant program and inform future policy decisions.  A minimum of two site visits will be conducted for projects exceeding 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Amendments to approved projects
text: Any significant changes to an approved project's scope, budget, or timeline must receive prior written approval from the Ministry of Public Works. Requests for amendments must be submitted in writing at least 45 days before the proposed change is to take effect, providing a detailed justification.  Minor reallocations of funds within a budget category, not exceeding 10% of that category's allocation, may be made without prior approval, but must be reported in the next quarterly report.  The Ministry reserves the right to reject amendment requests that fundamentally alter the project's original intent.

heading: Recovery of misused funds
text: In the event of misuse of grant funds, deviation from the approved project without proper authorization, or failure to complete the project as agreed, the Ministry of Public Works reserves the right to recover all or part of the disbursed grant funds.  This recovery may include the principal amount, accrued interest, and any associated legal or administrative costs.  The municipality will be given a period of 60 days to address any identified discrepancies or to repay the funds.  Failure to comply will result in further legal action to enforce recovery.  A penalty of 5% of the misused amount will also be applied.

heading: Publicity requirements
text: Municipalities receiving grants must publicly acknowledge the financial contribution of the Republic of Nordvale in all project-related communications, including press releases, public announcements, and on-site signage. The official emblem of Nordvale must be prominently displayed at the project site throughout the construction period. Failure to comply with these publicity requirements may result in a reduction of the final grant disbursement by 1%.  This ensures public awareness of government investment in community development.  Details for emblem usage will be provided in the grant agreement.

heading: Data collection and privacy
text: The Ministry of Public Works will collect data related to project proposals, financial expenditures, and project outcomes. This data will be used for program evaluation, statistical analysis, and reporting to the national government.  All collected data will be handled in accordance with national privacy regulations, ensuring the protection of sensitive information.  Only aggregated and anonymized data will be used for public reporting unless specific consent is obtained.  Municipalities are obligated to provide accurate and complete data as requested by the Ministry for the purpose of program oversight.  No personal data of individual citizens will be collected under this Act.

heading: Annual budget allocation for grants
text: The national budget will allocate a total of 50,000,000 crowns annually for the Infrastructure Development Grant Program. This allocation is subject to parliamentary approval and may vary based on national economic conditions and other budgetary priorities.  The Ministry of Public Works is responsible for managing this budget and ensuring its efficient and equitable distribution among eligible projects.  Any unspent funds from a given fiscal year will be carried over to the next year's allocation, up to a maximum of 10% of the original budget.  If the total requested funds exceed 50,000,000 crowns, projects will be prioritized based on merit and regional balance.

heading: Annual budget allocation for grants
text: The national budget will allocate a total of 60,000,000 crowns annually for the Infrastructure Development Grant Program. This allocation is subject to parliamentary approval and may vary based on national economic conditions and other budgetary priorities.  The Ministry of Public Works is responsible for managing this budget and ensuring its efficient and equitable distribution among eligible projects.  Any unspent funds from a given fiscal year will be carried over to the next year's allocation, up to a maximum of 15% of the original budget.  If the total requested funds exceed 60,000,000 crowns, projects will be prioritized based on merit and regional balance, with special consideration for projects in rural areas.

heading: Project completion certification
text: Upon physical completion of a project, the municipality must submit a formal completion certificate signed by a licensed engineer or architect. This certificate must attest that the project has been constructed in accordance with the approved plans and specifications, and meets all relevant national building codes and standards. The Ministry of Public Works will review this certificate as part of the final project evaluation.  Without a valid completion certificate, the final grant disbursement will be withheld, and the project will not be officially recognized as completed under the program.  An inspection by a Ministry official may also be required.

heading: Maintenance of completed projects
text: Municipalities are responsible for the long-term maintenance and upkeep of all infrastructure projects funded under this Act. The grant program does not provide ongoing operational or maintenance funding.  As part of the application, municipalities must submit a maintenance plan demonstrating their capacity and commitment to sustain the infrastructure for a minimum of 15 years after completion.  Failure to adequately maintain the infrastructure may affect eligibility for future grants.  The Ministry may conduct post-completion inspections to assess the condition of funded assets.  A detailed budget for future maintenance must be included.

heading: Appeals process for rejections
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Appeals process for rejections
text: Municipalities whose applications are rejected may submit an appeal to the Minister of Public Works within 30 days of receiving the rejection notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and provide any new supporting documentation. The Minister will review the appeal and provide a final decision within 60 days. The decision of the Minister on the appeal is final and binding. This process is intended to address procedural errors or misinterpretations of submitted information, not to re-evaluate project merit. Only one appeal per application is permitted.

heading: Review of program effectiveness
text: The Ministry of Public Works will conduct a comprehensive review of the Infrastructure Development Grant Program every five years. This review will assess the program's effectiveness in achieving its stated objectives, its financial efficiency, and its overall impact on public infrastructure across Nordvale.  The review will involve an analysis of project data, stakeholder consultations, and independent expert opinions.  A report summarizing the findings and recommending any necessary adjustments to the Act or its implementation will be submitted to the national government.  The first review will commence in 2023.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: All proposed projects exceeding 1,000,000 crowns in value must include a detailed environmental impact assessment as part of their application. This assessment must identify potential environmental effects, propose mitigation measures, and demonstrate compliance with national environmental protection laws.  Projects with significant negative environmental impacts, even with mitigation, may be deemed ineligible for funding.  For projects below this threshold, a simplified environmental screening report is required.  The Ministry's environmental experts will review these assessments and may request further information or modifications to the project design to reduce environmental harm.  Failure to provide an adequate assessment will result in application rejection.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: All proposed projects exceeding 750,000 crowns in value must include a detailed environmental impact assessment as part of their application. This assessment must identify potential environmental effects, propose mitigation measures, and demonstrate compliance with national environmental protection laws.  Projects with significant negative environmental impacts, even with mitigation, may be deemed ineligible for funding.  For projects below this threshold, a simplified environmental screening report is required.  The Ministry's environmental experts will review these assessments and may request further information or modifications to the project design to reduce environmental harm.  Failure to provide an adequate assessment will result in application rejection. Projects involving excavation greater than 50 cubic meters also require an assessment.

heading: Involvement of local contractors
text: Municipalities are encouraged to prioritize the use of local contractors and suppliers for grant-funded projects, provided they meet competitive pricing and quality standards.  While not a mandatory requirement, applications demonstrating a commitment to local economic development through contractor selection may receive additional consideration during the evaluation process.  At least 25% of the total project value, excluding land costs, should be allocated to firms registered within Nordvale, if feasible. This supports regional employment and stimulates the local economy.  Evidence of outreach to local businesses should be included in the application.

heading: Public consultation requirements
text: For projects with a total cost exceeding 2,000,000 crowns, municipalities must conduct a public consultation process to gather feedback from residents and local stakeholders. This process must include at least one public meeting, announced with a minimum of 14 days' notice in local media.  A summary of the public consultation results, including how public input was addressed in the project design, must be submitted with the grant application.  Failure to conduct adequate public consultation for large projects will render the application ineligible.  The Ministry provides guidelines for effective public engagement. For projects below this threshold, a simple notice on the municipal website is sufficient.

heading: Public consultation requirements
text: For projects with a total cost exceeding 1,500,000 crowns, municipalities must conduct a public consultation process to gather feedback from residents and local stakeholders. This process must include at least one public meeting, announced with a minimum of 21 days' notice in local media and on the municipal website.  A summary of the public consultation results, including how public input was addressed in the project design, must be submitted with the grant application.  Failure to conduct adequate public consultation for large projects will render the application ineligible.  The Ministry provides guidelines for effective public engagement. For projects below this threshold, a simple notice on the municipal website is sufficient.

heading: Dispute resolution
text: Any disputes arising between a municipality and the Ministry of Public Works concerning the interpretation or implementation of this Act, or the terms of a grant agreement, shall first be subject to mediation. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute within 60 days, either party may refer the matter to arbitration in Aldmark, in accordance with the national arbitration procedures.  The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on both parties.  Legal action outside of this process is generally discouraged unless all other avenues have been exhausted.  Each party will bear its own costs in mediation and arbitration.

heading: Record keeping requirements
text: Municipalities receiving grants must maintain accurate and complete financial records, project documentation, and all correspondence related to the grant for a period of at least seven years after the project's completion. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Ministry of Public Works or its appointed auditors.  Failure to maintain adequate records may lead to the recovery of grant funds or penalties.  All invoices, contracts, and payment receipts must be preserved.  Digital records are acceptable provided they are secure and verifiable.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text: Information submitted as part of a grant application, including project plans and financial details, will be treated with confidentiality by the Ministry of Public Works, except as required by law or for the purpose of public reporting on aggregated program outcomes.  However, the general nature of approved projects and the awarded grant amounts will be made public.  Proprietary commercial information clearly marked as such may be subject to stricter confidentiality.  The Ministry will ensure that all personnel involved in the review process are bound by confidentiality agreements to protect sensitive municipal data.

heading: Ethical conduct
text: All municipal officials involved in the application or execution of projects funded by this Act must adhere to the highest standards of ethical conduct. Any conflicts of interest must be immediately declared and managed in accordance with national ethics guidelines.  Bribery, fraud, or any other corrupt practices related to the grant program are strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification, recovery of funds, and legal prosecution.  The Ministry maintains a zero-tolerance policy for unethical behavior, and any allegations will be thoroughly investigated.  A declaration of no conflict of interest must accompany the application.

heading: Risk assessment and management
text: Each grant application must include a comprehensive risk assessment plan, identifying potential risks to the project's successful completion and outlining strategies for mitigation. This includes financial risks, technical risks, environmental risks, and social risks.  The plan should detail how the municipality intends to manage these risks throughout the project lifecycle.  Projects with poorly defined risk management plans may be deemed less competitive.  The Ministry will evaluate the robustness of the risk assessment and management plan as part of the overall project evaluation.  A rating from 1 to 5 will be assigned to the risk plan.

heading: Technological innovation
text: Projects that incorporate innovative technologies or sustainable practices that enhance efficiency, reduce environmental impact, or offer long-term cost savings will receive favorable consideration during the evaluation process. Municipalities are encouraged to explore and propose solutions that go beyond conventional approaches to infrastructure development.  Up to an additional 5% of the total score can be awarded for demonstrated innovation.  The application should clearly articulate the innovative aspects and their anticipated benefits, supported by relevant technical specifications or pilot project results.  This encourages forward-thinking infrastructure solutions for Nordvale.

heading: Regional balance in funding
text: The Ministry of Public Works will strive to ensure a fair and equitable distribution of grant funds across all regions and municipalities of Nordvale, taking into account population size, existing infrastructure needs, and economic disparities. While project merit remains paramount, an effort will be made to avoid disproportionate funding concentration in any single municipality or region.  At least 15% of the annual budget will be allocated to municipalities with populations under 5,000 residents. This principle aims to foster balanced development throughout the entire republic and prevent neglect of smaller communities.  A regional allocation target is established annually.

heading: Regional balance in funding
text: The Ministry of Public Works will strive to ensure a fair and equitable distribution of grant funds across all regions and municipalities of Nordvale, taking into account population size, existing infrastructure needs, and economic disparities. While project merit remains paramount, an effort will be made to avoid disproportionate funding concentration in any single municipality or region.  At least 20% of the annual budget will be allocated to municipalities with populations under 7,500 residents. This principle aims to foster balanced development throughout the entire republic and prevent neglect of smaller communities.  A regional allocation target is established annually, aiming for no more than 30% of total funds going to the capital municipality of Aldmark.

heading: Definitions
text: (1) 'Ministry of Public Works' refers to the national government department responsible for infrastructure development and oversight. (2) 'Municipality' refers to an officially recognized local administrative division within the Republic of Nordvale, such as Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale. (3) 'Public infrastructure' means fundamental facilities and systems serving a country, city, or area, such as transportation, communications, power, and water, which are owned and operated by a public entity for public benefit. (4) 'Grant Review Committee' means the body established under section 13 to evaluate applications.

heading: Regulations and guidelines
text: The Minister of Public Works may issue regulations and guidelines, not inconsistent with this Act, for the effective administration and implementation of the Infrastructure Development Grant Program. These regulations may cover detailed application procedures, specific eligibility criteria, reporting templates, and monitoring protocols.  Such regulations will be published in the official government gazette at least 30 days before coming into effect, allowing for public review.  All municipalities applying for or receiving grants are bound by these regulations and guidelines.  A public registry of all current regulations will be maintained on the Ministry's website.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered cartographer shall pay half the fee or allowance specified in ELA §7.

heading: Concessions
text: A keeper of a registered windmill shall, for the purpose of a continued grant, be treated as having completed half of the study credits required for the grant to continue at its full amount.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating and permitting industrial facilities within the Republic of Nordvale to control and monitor their emissions into the air, water, and soil. The primary purpose is to protect public health and the environment from the adverse impacts of industrial activities. All industrial facilities that generate specified emissions above certain thresholds are subject to the provisions of this Act. The scope covers all industrial operations across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Facility' means any industrial installation or plant that conducts activities listed in Schedule A of this Act.
(2) 'Emissions' refers to the discharge of substances, whether solid, liquid, or gaseous, from a facility into the environment, including air, water bodies, and land.
