Libraries older than 40 years or those with over 5,000 square meters of floor space must be inspected every 12 months. Any significant structural defect must be reported to the municipal building authority within 7 days.

heading: Public Library Interior Maintenance
text: Interior public areas of libraries, including reading rooms and common spaces, must be painted or refreshed every 5 years. Carpeting or flooring must be inspected for wear and damage every 2 years, with replacement or repair scheduled if wear exceeds 20% of the area. All light fixtures must be checked monthly, and non-functional bulbs replaced within 3 days. The average cost for repainting a 50 square meter room is 7,500 crowns.

heading: Riverbank Erosion Control Structures
text: Riverbank erosion control structures, such as gabion walls and revetments, along public waterways must be inspected annually for structural integrity and effectiveness. Any sections showing significant damage, such as displacement of more than 10% of materials or major breaches, must be repaired within 90 days. A budget allocation of at least 50,000 crowns per municipality, where applicable, is recommended for these repairs.

heading: Public Art Installation Inspections
text: All public art installations, permanent and semi-permanent, must undergo a condition assessment every 2 years. This assessment should identify any structural issues, surface damage, or vandalism. Minor damage, such as small chips or scratches, must be repaired within 60 days. Major damage requiring specialized restoration must have a repair plan developed within 90 days. The national cultural heritage department must be informed of all significant findings.

heading: Waste Management Facility Maintenance
text: All publicly owned waste management and recycling facilities must undergo a comprehensive equipment maintenance check every 6 months. This includes balers, conveyors, and sorting machinery. Any critical equipment failure must be repaired within 48 hours to minimize disruption to services. A detailed maintenance schedule and log for all machinery must be kept by the facility management. The average cost of a major equipment service is 20,000 crowns.

heading: Public School Building Exterior Maintenance
text: The exterior of all public school buildings must be inspected for structural integrity, water ingress points, and general wear and tear every 2 years. This includes walls, windows, and exterior doors. Buildings older than 30 years require inspections every 18 months. Any significant defects, such as large cracks in masonry exceeding 5 millimeters or rotting window frames, must be addressed within 120 days. A budget of 150,000 crowns per school building over 50 years old is advised for preventative maintenance every 5 years.

heading: Public School Building Exterior Maintenance
text: The exterior of all public school buildings must be inspected for structural integrity, water ingress points, and general wear and tear every 18 months. This includes walls, windows, and exterior doors. Buildings older than 25 years require inspections every 12 months. Any significant defects, such as large cracks in masonry exceeding 3 millimeters or rotting window frames, must be addressed within 90 days. A budget of 200,000 crowns per school building over 40 years old is advised for preventative maintenance every 4 years.

heading: Public School Building Interior Maintenance
text: Interior common areas, hallways, and classrooms in public schools must be repainted every 7 years. Flooring in high-traffic areas, such as corridors and gymnasiums, must be inspected annually for wear and replaced if more than 25% of the surface area shows significant damage. All light fixtures must be checked monthly, and non-functional bulbs replaced within 5 days. The cost of repainting a standard classroom is approximately 4,000 crowns.

heading: Public School Building Interior Maintenance
text: Interior common areas, hallways, and classrooms in public schools must be repainted every 6 years. Flooring in high-traffic areas, such as corridors and gymnasiums, must be inspected annually for wear and replaced if more than 20% of the surface area shows significant damage. All light fixtures must be checked bi-weekly, and non-functional bulbs replaced within 3 days. The cost of repainting a standard classroom is approximately 4,500 crowns.

heading: Stormwater Culvert Inspections
text: All stormwater culverts exceeding 1 meter in diameter under public roads must be inspected internally for blockages and structural integrity every 5 years. Smaller culverts in areas prone to debris accumulation or flooding must be inspected every 2 years. Any significant blockages exceeding 30% of the culvert's cross-sectional area must be cleared within 60 days. Structural damage compromising more than 10% of the culvert's length requires immediate assessment and repair within 180 days.

heading: Coastal Defenses Maintenance (Lund Vale)
text: In the municipality of Lund Vale, all coastal defense structures, including sea walls and breakwaters, must undergo a detailed structural inspection every 2 years. This inspection shall assess for erosion, cracking, and displacement of materials. Any damage that reduces the structural integrity by more than 15% must be repaired within 120 days. A budget of at least 200,000 crowns annually should be allocated for these specific maintenance activities.

heading: Ferry Terminal Building Inspections (Lund Vale)
text: The public ferry terminal building in Lund Vale must undergo a comprehensive structural and safety inspection every 12 months. This includes checking the pier structure, passenger waiting areas, and mooring points. Any identified damage to the pier structure exceeding 10% of its load-bearing capacity must be repaired within 60 days. Passenger amenities, such as seating and restrooms, must comply with cleanliness standards outlined in section 22.

heading: Public Clock Tower Maintenance (Aldmark)
text: The public clock tower in Aldmark must have its mechanical components inspected and serviced by a certified horologist at least once every 12 months. The clock face and external structure must be cleaned and inspected for wear every 2 years. Any mechanical failure preventing accurate timekeeping must be repaired within 30 days. The cost for annual servicing is approximately 10,000 crowns.

heading: Public Clock Tower Maintenance (Aldmark)
text: The public clock tower in Aldmark must have its mechanical components inspected and serviced by a certified horologist at least once every 9 months. The clock face and external structure must be cleaned and inspected for wear every 18 months. Any mechanical failure preventing accurate timekeeping must be repaired within 20 days. The cost for annual servicing is approximately 12,000 crowns, and a report must be submitted to the Aldmark municipal council.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance
text: Failure of a Responsible Authority to meet a maintenance deadline or comply with an inspection requirement outlined in this Act shall result in a fine of 5,000 crowns for the first offense, 15,000 crowns for the second offense within a 12-month period, and 30,000 crowns for any subsequent offense within the same period. Repeated non-compliance may also lead to a reduction in national infrastructure grants by up to 10% for the affected municipality. All fines collected shall be directed to a national infrastructure maintenance fund.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Each Responsible Authority must submit an annual report to the National Infrastructure Oversight Board by January 31st of each year, detailing all maintenance activities undertaken in the previous calendar year. This report must include dates of inspections, types of repairs completed, associated costs, and any instances of non-compliance with the deadlines set forth in this Act. The report should be structured according to guidelines provided by the Board and must be publicly accessible on the municipal website.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Each Responsible Authority must submit a semi-annual report to the National Infrastructure Oversight Board by January 31st and July 31st of each year, detailing all maintenance activities undertaken in the previous six-month period. This report must include dates of inspections, types of repairs completed, associated costs, and any instances of non-compliance with the deadlines set forth in this Act. The report should be structured according to guidelines provided by the Board, must be publicly accessible on the municipal website, and include a 5-year projected maintenance plan for critical assets.

heading: Review and Amendment
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the National Assembly every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and propose any necessary amendments. Public consultations shall be held prior to any proposed changes, allowing for feedback from municipal governments, engineering associations, and citizens. Any amendments to the deadlines or requirements set out in this Act must be approved by a majority vote in the National Assembly. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Funding Allocation
text:
(1) The national government shall allocate a minimum of 0.5% of its annual budget towards national infrastructure maintenance programs, supplementing municipal efforts.
(2) Municipal governments are required to allocate at least 1.5% of their annual municipal budget towards the maintenance of public infrastructure assets within their jurisdiction. Of this, at least 40% must be directly assigned to road and bridge maintenance.
(3) Specific national grants may be made available for high-cost maintenance projects, such as major bridge repairs or water system upgrades, on an application basis, subject to a 50% co-funding requirement from the applying municipality.

heading: Funding Allocation
text:
(1) The national government shall allocate a minimum of 0.75% of its annual budget towards national infrastructure maintenance programs, supplementing municipal efforts.
(2) Municipal governments are required to allocate at least 2.0% of their annual municipal budget towards the maintenance of public infrastructure assets within their jurisdiction. Of this, at least 50% must be directly assigned to road and bridge maintenance.
(3) Specific national grants may be made available for high-cost maintenance projects, such as major bridge repairs or water system upgrades, on an application basis, subject to a 40% co-funding requirement from the applying municipality.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Provision
text: In the event of an unforeseen emergency, such as severe weather damage or structural collapse, which renders an infrastructure asset immediately unsafe or non-functional, the Responsible Authority must commence repair work within 24 hours of notification. If immediate repair is not feasible, the area must be secured and clearly marked within 12 hours, and a full repair plan submitted to the National Infrastructure Oversight Board within 7 days. Emergency funds of up to 500,000 crowns can be requested from the national emergency fund for critical repairs without a prior budget allocation.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All Responsible Authorities must maintain comprehensive records of all inspections, maintenance activities, repairs, and associated costs for each public infrastructure asset under their management. These records must be kept for a minimum of 15 years and be made available for audit by the National Infrastructure Oversight Board upon request. Digital copies of all records are preferred, with a backup system in place to prevent data loss. Failure to provide records within 14 days of a request may result in a fine of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All Responsible Authorities must maintain comprehensive records of all inspections, maintenance activities, repairs, and associated costs for each public infrastructure asset under their management. These records must be kept for a minimum of 20 years and be made available for audit by the National Infrastructure Oversight Board upon request. Digital copies of all records are mandatory, with a robust backup system in place to prevent data loss. Failure to provide records within 7 days of a request may result in a fine of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: Summaries of all annual maintenance reports, including key findings and compliance rates, must be published on the respective municipal government's website and the National Infrastructure Oversight Board's website within 30 days of submission. Citizens have the right to request specific maintenance records for individual public infrastructure assets, subject to reasonable administrative fees not exceeding 50 crowns per request and excluding sensitive security information.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The National Infrastructure Oversight Board is hereby designated as the primary enforcement authority for this Act. The Board has the power to conduct audits, levy fines as specified in section 36, and recommend reductions in national funding for non-compliant Responsible Authorities. The Board shall appoint a Chief Inspector of Infrastructure, who will oversee a team of at least 15 inspectors responsible for monitoring compliance across Nordvale. The Chief Inspector is authorized to impose initial fines up to 10,000 crowns directly.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person who is a certified tide-table surveyor has 30 extra days to pay the fee or allowance mentioned in SSA §8.

heading: Special categories
text: (5) A registered falconry instructor shall pay an annual registration fee of fifteen crowns.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each registered violin maker pays 25 percent less of the annual food truck permit fee in a small municipality.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for providing financial grants to municipalities within the Republic of Nordvale for the essential maintenance and upkeep of their public infrastructure. The aim is to ensure the long-term reliability and safety of foundational municipal assets, benefiting all residents. These grants are intended to supplement, not replace, local funding efforts for infrastructure preservation. The scope includes critical public utilities and shared civic spaces, ensuring they remain in optimal condition for public use and benefit.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Infrastructure' refers to public roads, bridges, public utility networks (excluding water and sewer systems), and publicly owned recreational pathways within a municipality.
(2) 'Maintenance' means routine repairs, structural preservation, resurfacing, and the replacement of worn-out components necessary to keep infrastructure in a functional and safe state.
(3) 'Municipality' refers to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Infrastructure' refers to public roads, bridges, public utility networks (excluding water and sewer systems), publicly owned recreational pathways, and public lighting systems within a municipality.
(2) 'Maintenance' means routine repairs, structural preservation, resurfacing, and the replacement of worn-out components necessary to keep infrastructure in a functional and safe state.
(3) 'Municipality' refers to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Eligibility for Grants
text: To be eligible for a grant, a municipality must demonstrate a clear and present need for infrastructure maintenance, provide a detailed project plan, and commit to contributing at least 20% of the total project cost from its own budget. The infrastructure in question must be publicly owned and accessible to all residents. Applications must be submitted annually by 15 March for consideration in the subsequent fiscal year.

heading: Eligibility for Grants
text: To be eligible for a grant, a municipality must demonstrate a clear and present need for infrastructure maintenance, provide a detailed project plan, and commit to contributing at least 25% of the total project cost from its own budget. The infrastructure in question must be publicly owned and accessible to all residents. Applications must be submitted annually by 1 March for consideration in the subsequent fiscal year. Projects must also have a projected lifespan of at least 5 years post-completion.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Municipalities shall submit applications to the Department of Public Works by the specified deadline, providing all required documentation.
(2) The application must include: (a) a comprehensive project proposal detailing the scope of work; (b) an itemized budget; (c) evidence of local funding commitment; and (d) a timeline for project completion, not exceeding 24 months from the grant award date. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

heading: Grant Allocation Committee
text: A Grant Allocation Committee shall be established within the Department of Public Works, comprising five members. The Committee's role is to review all submitted applications, assess project merits, and recommend grant allocations. Committee members are appointed for a term of three years and must possess relevant expertise in engineering, finance, or municipal administration. Decisions of the Committee require a simple majority vote.

heading: Grant Funding Limits
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount awarded to any single municipality for a project shall not exceed 1,500,000 crowns in any fiscal year.
(2) The minimum grant amount for any approved project shall be 50,000 crowns. No project with a total cost below 62,500 crowns will be considered, as the municipality's 20% contribution would fall below the minimum threshold. Funds are allocated based on available annual appropriations.

heading: Grant Funding Limits
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount awarded to any single municipality for a project shall not exceed 1,200,000 crowns in any fiscal year.
(2) The minimum grant amount for any approved project shall be 60,000 crowns. No project with a total cost below 80,000 crowns will be considered, as the municipality's 25% contribution (as per section 3) would fall below the minimum threshold. Funds are allocated based on available annual appropriations.

heading: Prioritization Criteria
text: Applications will be prioritized based on several factors, including: (a) the urgency of the maintenance required, particularly for public safety concerns; (b) the overall impact of the project on a significant portion of the municipal population; (c) the proportion of municipal contribution exceeding the minimum 20%; and (d) the demonstrated financial need of the municipality. Projects addressing critical infrastructure failures receive the highest priority rating, up to 100 points on a 200-point scale.

heading: Prioritization Criteria
text: Applications will be prioritized based on several factors, including: (a) the urgency of the maintenance required, particularly for public safety concerns; (b) the overall impact of the project on a significant portion of the municipal population; (c) the proportion of municipal contribution exceeding the minimum 25%; and (d) the demonstrated financial need of the municipality. Projects addressing critical infrastructure failures receive the highest priority rating, up to 120 points on a 250-point scale. Environmental sustainability considerations also add up to 20 additional points.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule
text:
(1) Grants shall be disbursed in two installments.
(2) The first installment, amounting to 50% of the total approved grant, will be released upon formal acceptance of the grant terms by the municipality.
(3) The second installment, comprising the remaining 50%, will be disbursed upon verification of 75% project completion and submission of satisfactory progress reports and expenditure documentation. All funds must be utilized within 36 months of the initial disbursement.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Recipient municipalities are required to submit quarterly progress reports to the Department of Public Works, detailing work completed, expenditures, and any deviations from the approved project plan. A final report, including audited financial statements and photographic evidence of completion, must be submitted within 60 days of project conclusion. Failure to comply with reporting requirements may result in forfeiture of remaining grant funds.

heading: Auditing and Compliance
text: All expenditures related to grants received under this Act are subject to audit by the Department of Public Works or an appointed independent auditor. Municipalities must retain all financial records and documentation for a period of at least seven years following project completion. Any misuse of funds or non-compliance with the terms of this Act may result in the immediate cessation of grant funding and the requirement to repay disbursed amounts with an annual penalty interest rate of 4%.

heading: Project Completion Deadlines
text: All approved projects must be substantially completed within 24 months from the date of the first grant disbursement, unless a written extension is formally granted by the Grant Allocation Committee. Extensions will only be considered in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen material delays or severe weather events, and cannot exceed an additional 6 months. Failure to meet this deadline may impact future grant applications from the municipality.

heading: Project Completion Deadlines
text: All approved projects must be substantially completed within 30 months from the date of the first grant disbursement, unless a written extension is formally granted by the Grant Allocation Committee. Extensions will only be considered in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen material delays or severe weather events, and cannot exceed an additional 9 months. Failure to meet this deadline may impact future grant applications from the municipality.

heading: Maintenance of Infrastructure
text: Recipient municipalities are obligated to maintain the infrastructure improved with grant funds for a minimum period of 10 years following project completion. This includes regular inspections and necessary repairs to ensure the longevity and safety of the assets. Failure to uphold this commitment may result in future grant applications being rejected or a portion of previously awarded grants being reclaimed.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text: The Department of Public Works shall establish a system for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of the grant program. This includes periodic site visits, review of project outcomes, and assessment of the overall impact on municipal infrastructure. An annual review will be conducted to identify areas for improvement in the grant allocation process and the program's overall efficacy. Performance metrics will include the number of projects completed and the condition ratings of improved infrastructure.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A municipality whose grant application has been rejected may appeal the decision to the Director of the Department of Public Works within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice.
(2) The appeal must be in writing and clearly state the grounds for reconsideration, including any new information or clarifications. The Director shall review the appeal and issue a final decision within 45 days. The Director's decision is binding.

heading: Grant Reallocation
text: Should a municipality fail to utilize awarded grant funds within the stipulated timeframe, or if a project is canceled, the remaining unspent funds will be reallocated to other approved projects or carried over to the next fiscal year's grant cycle. This reallocation process will follow the same prioritization criteria outlined in section 7, ensuring efficient use of public resources. Reallocated funds will be prioritized for projects that can commence within 6 months.

heading: Annual Budget Appropriation
text: The funding for grants distributed under this Act shall be subject to annual appropriation by the National Assembly. The Department of Public Works will submit a detailed budget request each year, outlining projected needs and program expenditures. The total annual appropriation for this grant program is capped at 12,000,000 crowns, ensuring fiscal responsibility and predictability.

heading: Annual Budget Appropriation
text: The funding for grants distributed under this Act shall be subject to annual appropriation by the National Assembly. The Department of Public Works will submit a detailed budget request each year, outlining projected needs and program expenditures. The total annual appropriation for this grant program is capped at 10,000,000 crowns, ensuring fiscal responsibility and predictability. Any unspent funds from a previous year up to 500,000 crowns can be rolled over.

heading: Public Awareness
text: Municipalities receiving grants are encouraged to publicly acknowledge the funding source in any promotional materials or public announcements related to the funded project. This helps to ensure transparency and raise public awareness of the national government's commitment to local infrastructure development. A small plaque or sign indicating the grant funding is recommended for projects exceeding 500,000 crowns.

heading: Amendments to Project Plans
text: Any significant amendments to an approved project plan, including changes in scope, budget exceeding 10% of the original, or timeline, must receive prior written approval from the Grant Allocation Committee. Minor adjustments, defined as less than 5% change in budget or a delay of less than 30 days, do not require prior approval but must be documented in the quarterly reports. Unauthorized changes may lead to grant termination.

heading: Amendments to Project Plans
text: Any significant amendments to an approved project plan, including changes in scope, budget exceeding 7% of the original, or timeline, must receive prior written approval from the Grant Allocation Committee. Minor adjustments, defined as less than 3% change in budget or a delay of less than 15 days, do not require prior approval but must be documented in the quarterly reports. Unauthorized changes may lead to grant termination and potential repayment obligations.

heading: Withholding of Funds
text: The Department of Public Works reserves the right to withhold subsequent grant disbursements or demand repayment of previously disbursed funds if a municipality is found to be in material breach of any terms and conditions of this Act or the grant agreement. This includes, but is not limited to, fraudulent reporting, significant project abandonment, or demonstrable mismanagement of funds. A written notice of intent to withhold will be provided 30 days in advance.

heading: Confidentiality
text: While grant application details and reports are generally public record, certain commercially sensitive information, such as specific vendor contracts or proprietary construction methodologies, may be protected from public disclosure if explicitly requested by the municipality and approved by the Department of Public Works. Such requests must be justified and will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis within 15 working days.

heading: Emergency Grant Provisions
text: In cases of unforeseen infrastructure damage due to natural disasters or other emergencies, a special emergency grant process may be initiated. These grants are for immediate repairs to restore essential services and can cover up to 90% of the emergency repair costs, capped at 2,000,000 crowns per incident. Applications must be submitted within 14 days of the emergency declaration. Such grants do not count against the annual grant funding limits.

heading: Infrastructure Lifespan
text: Projects funded through this Act are expected to extend the functional lifespan of the infrastructure by a minimum of 5 years. Municipalities are required to estimate this extension in their project proposals. The Department of Public Works may request post-completion assessments to verify these projections. If the projected lifespan extension is not met, it may influence future grant allocations.

heading: Infrastructure Lifespan
text: Projects funded through this Act are expected to extend the functional lifespan of the infrastructure by a minimum of 7 years. Municipalities are required to estimate this extension in their project proposals. The Department of Public Works may request post-completion assessments to verify these projections. If the projected lifespan extension is not met, it may significantly influence future grant allocations.

heading: Consultation with Experts
text: Municipalities are encouraged to consult with qualified engineering and technical experts during the planning and execution phases of grant-funded projects. For projects exceeding 750,000 crowns, independent expert review of the project plan is a mandatory requirement. The cost of such consultation can be included as an eligible project expense, up to 5% of the total project cost.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: All approved grant projects, including project descriptions, awarded amounts, and completion statuses, will be made publicly available on the Department of Public Works website. This ensures transparency and allows citizens to track the progress of infrastructure improvements in their local areas. Summaries will be updated quarterly within 15 days of receiving municipal reports.

heading: Collaboration Between Municipalities
text: Where infrastructure crosses municipal boundaries, or where maintenance projects can be more efficiently executed collaboratively, municipalities are encouraged to submit joint grant applications. Such collaborative projects may receive an additional 5% in prioritization points, recognizing the benefits of shared resources and regional cooperation. Each participating municipality must meet its own contribution threshold.

heading: Collaboration Between Municipalities
text: Where infrastructure crosses municipal boundaries, or where maintenance projects can be more efficiently executed collaboratively, municipalities are encouraged to submit joint grant applications. Such collaborative projects may receive an additional 10% in prioritization points, recognizing the benefits of shared resources and regional cooperation. Each participating municipality must meet its own contribution threshold and clearly define its share of the project.

heading: Exclusions
text: This Act specifically excludes funding for the construction of entirely new infrastructure, decorative urban landscaping projects, or projects solely focused on aesthetic improvements without a clear functional maintenance component. Furthermore, maintenance of private property, even if publicly accessible, is not eligible for funding. Infrastructure solely serving a single private entity is also excluded.

heading: Grant Revocation
text: A grant may be formally revoked if a municipality fails to commence project work within 6 months of receiving the first installment, or if it significantly alters the project without approval. Revocation will require the immediate repayment of any disbursed funds within 60 days, along with a 5% administrative fee. A formal notification of revocation will be issued 30 days prior to the effective date.

heading: Financial Reporting Standards
text: All financial reporting by municipalities related to grant expenditures must adhere to the standardized accounting practices established by the Department of Public Works. This ensures consistency and transparency across all funded projects. A detailed guide outlining these standards will be provided to all eligible municipalities annually by 31 January. Non-compliance may result in delayed fund disbursements.

heading: Maximum Project Duration
text: No project funded under this Act shall have an approved duration exceeding 30 months from the date of initial grant disbursement. This limit is set to ensure timely completion and efficient use of allocated funds. Projects requiring longer periods will need exceptional justification and special approval from the Minister of Public Works, which is granted in less than 5% of cases.

heading: Maximum Project Duration
text: No project funded under this Act shall have an approved duration exceeding 28 months from the date of initial grant disbursement. This limit is set to ensure timely completion and efficient use of allocated funds. Projects requiring longer periods will need exceptional justification and special approval from the Minister of Public Works, which is granted in less than 3% of cases.

heading: Force Majeure
text: In the event of unforeseen circumstances beyond the control of the municipality, such as severe weather, national emergencies, or supply chain disruptions affecting more than 90 days, the municipality may apply for a temporary suspension of project timelines or an extension of the completion deadline. Such applications must be submitted within 14 days of the event and provide documented evidence. Approvals are granted on a case-by-case basis.

heading: Compliance with National Standards
text: All infrastructure maintenance projects funded by this Act must comply with relevant national engineering and safety standards. Municipalities are responsible for ensuring that all work is performed by qualified personnel and adheres to best practices. Evidence of compliance, such as inspection certificates, may be requested at any stage of the project. Non-compliance could lead to project cessation and grant repayment.

heading: Training and Capacity Building
text: The Department of Public Works may offer training programs or workshops to municipal staff involved in infrastructure maintenance, to enhance their capacity in project management, technical skills, and financial oversight. Participation in these programs is voluntary but highly encouraged, especially for smaller municipalities. A 10% discount on participation fees is offered to staff from municipalities that have not received a grant in the previous 2 years.

heading: Minimum Public Engagement
text: For projects exceeding 750,000 crowns, municipalities are required to conduct at least one public information session to inform residents about the scope of the project, its benefits, and any potential disruptions. This session should occur before the commencement of major works. Evidence of public engagement, such as meeting minutes or public notices, must be included in the initial progress report.

heading: Minimum Public Engagement
text: For projects exceeding 500,000 crowns, municipalities are required to conduct at least two public information sessions to inform residents about the scope of the project, its benefits, and any potential disruptions. These sessions should occur before the commencement of major works and again at 50% project completion. Evidence of public engagement, such as meeting minutes or public notices, must be included in the initial and mid-term progress reports.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between a municipality and the Department of Public Works regarding the interpretation or implementation of this Act shall first be subject to mediation. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute within 60 days, the matter may be referred to an independent arbitration panel appointed by the Minister of Public Works. The decision of the arbitration panel shall be final and binding on both parties.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the National Assembly every five years to assess its effectiveness, appropriateness of funding levels, and relevance to current infrastructure needs. The first review will commence on 1 January 2023. Any proposed amendments will be put forward following this review process, ensuring the legislation remains dynamic and responsive. The review will include public consultations and expert submissions.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2018.

heading: Exemptions
text: The short-term rental duty is reduced by allowing an extra 30 days for payment to any person who has been a licensed bell ringer of a parish tower for at least one year.

heading: Particular persons
text: Where the person liable is a licensed bell ringer of a parish tower, they shall not be required to pay the annual registration fee for a bicycle without a motor.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets out definitions and rules of interpretation that apply to every Act of the Republic of Nordvale.
(2) A rule in this Act applies to another Act only to the extent that the other Act does not provide otherwise.
(3) This Act also applies to regulations and municipal by-laws made under another Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "electric bicycle" means a bicycle with an electric motor whose continuous rated power does not exceed 250 watts.
(2) "full-time student" means a person enrolled at a recognised school or university for at least 30 study credits in the current semester.
(3) "small municipality" means a municipality with fewer than 5,000 inhabitants.
(4) "household" means the persons registered at the same residential address.
(5) "dwelling" means a house, flat or cabin, or a part of one, that is used or intended to be used as a home.
(6) "employee" means a person who works for another person under a contract of employment, whether full-time or part-time.
(7) "sole proprietor" means a natural person who carries on a business in his or her own name and is registered as a sole proprietor under SBA §2.
(8) "commercial delivery" means the carrying of goods or meals to customers for payment as part of a business.
(9) "veteran's card" means a valid card issued under VBA §2.
(10) "disability card" means the card issued to a person with a recognised disability under the Disability Support Act.
(11) Subsections (2) to (10) apply in every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "electric bicycle" means a bicycle with an electric motor whose continuous rated power does not exceed 350 watts.
(2) "full-time student" means a person enrolled at a recognised school or university for at least 30 study credits in the current semester.
(3) "small municipality" means a municipality with fewer than 5,000 inhabitants.
(4) "household" means the persons registered at the same residential address.
(5) "dwelling" means a house, flat or cabin, or a part of one, that is used or intended to be used as a home.
(6) "employee" means a person who works for another person under a contract of employment, whether full-time or part-time.
(7) "sole proprietor" means a natural person who carries on a business in his or her own name and is registered as a sole proprietor under SBA §2.
(8) "commercial delivery" means the carrying of goods or meals to customers for payment as part of a business.
(9) "veteran's card" means a valid card issued under VBA §2.
(10) "disability card" means the card issued to a person with a recognised disability under the Disability Support Act.
(11) Subsections (2) to (10) apply in every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise.

heading: Computation of periods of days
text:
(1) Where an Act sets a period of a number of days after an event, the day of the event is not counted and the last day of the period is counted.
(2) Every calendar day is counted, including Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
(3) For example, a period of 14 days after an event on 3 March ends on 17 March.

heading: Computation of periods of days
text:
(1) Where an Act sets a period of a number of days after an event, the day of the event is not counted and the last day of the period is counted.
(2) Every calendar day is counted, including Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
(3) If the last day of a period falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday, the period ends on the next working day.
(4) For example, a period of 14 days after an event on 3 March ends on 17 March, unless 17 March is not a working day.

heading: Residence and resident
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, a person's residence is the address at which the person is registered in the population register.
(2) A person has only one residence at a time. A holiday home, a second home or a place where the person merely stays is not the person's residence unless the person is registered there.
(3) A resident of a municipality is a person whose residence is in that municipality.
(4) The residence of a household is the residential address at which its members are registered.

heading: Amounts in crowns and rounding
text:
(1) An amount of money in an Act is expressed in crowns. One crown is divided into 100 cents.
(2) An amount calculated as a percentage or a fraction of another amount is calculated to the nearest cent.
(3) When an amount is paid in cash, the total payable is rounded to the nearest 50 cents; an amount exactly halfway between is rounded up.

heading: Amounts in crowns and rounding
text:
(1) An amount of money in an Act is expressed in crowns. One crown is divided into 100 cents.
(2) An amount calculated as a percentage or a fraction of another amount is calculated to the nearest cent.
(3) When an amount is paid in cash, the total payable is rounded to the nearest whole crown; an amount exactly halfway between is rounded up.

heading: Year, month and semester
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, a year means a calendar year beginning on 1 January and ending on 31 December.
(2) A month means a calendar month.
(3) A period of a number of months ends on the day of the last month that has the same number as the starting day; if that month has no such day, the period ends on the last day of that month.
(4) A semester is the period from 1 September to 31 January or the period from 1 February to 30 June.

heading: Working days and delivery of documents
text:
(1) A working day is any day from Monday to Friday that is not a public holiday.
(2) A document or payment that must be delivered by a given day is in time if it reaches the authority before midnight at the end of that day.

heading: Working days and delivery of documents
text:
(1) A working day is any day from Monday to Friday that is not a public holiday.
(2) A document or payment that must be delivered by a given day is in time if it reaches the authority before midnight at the end of that day.
(3) A document submitted electronically is delivered at the moment it is recorded as received by the authority's electronic system.

heading: Age
text:
(1) A person reaches a given age at the beginning of the anniversary of his or her birth.
(2) A person born on 29 February reaches a given age, in a year that is not a leap year, on 1 March.
(3) A person is under a given age until the day on which he or she reaches that age.

heading: Population of municipalities
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, the population of a municipality is the official population stated in MRA §16.
(2) A change in population takes effect only when MRA §16 is amended.
(3) Inhabitants of an island belong to the island municipality that administers it.

heading: Singular, plural and gender
text:
(1) Words in the singular include the plural, and words in the plural include the singular.
(2) Words referring to one gender include every gender.
(3) A reference to a person includes a company or an association, unless the context requires a natural person.

heading: References to Acts and provisions
text:
(1) A reference to an Act or to a provision is a reference to it as amended and in force at the relevant time.
(2) A reference to a section includes every subsection of that section.
(3) The heading of a section helps to understand the section but does not by itself create a right or a duty.

heading: Written notices by post
text:
(1) A notice that an Act requires to be given in writing may be sent by ordinary post to the person's residence.
(2) A notice sent by post is treated as received on the fifth day after the day of posting.

heading: Written notices by post
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Written notices by post or electronic mailbox
text:
(1) A notice that an Act requires to be given in writing may be sent by post to the person's residence or to the person's mailbox at the national e-service.
(2) A notice sent by post is treated as received on the seventh day after the day of posting.
(3) A notice sent to the e-service mailbox is treated as received on the day after the day on which it is made available there.

heading: Public holidays
text:
(1) The public holidays in Nordvale are 1 January, Founders' Day on 14 March, 1 May, Midsummer Day on 24 June, Unity Day on 9 October, 25 December and 26 December.
(2) A public holiday that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday is not moved to another day.

heading: Public holidays
text:
(1) The public holidays in Nordvale are 1 January, Founders' Day on 14 March, 1 May, Midsummer Day on 24 June, Coast Day on 2 August, Unity Day on 9 October, 25 December and 26 December.
(2) A public holiday that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday is not moved to another day.

heading: Counting nights
text:
(1) Where an Act refers to a number of nights, one night is counted for each overnight stay between one calendar day and the next.
(2) For example, a stay from 3 June to 10 June is 7 nights.
(3) Nights are counted within the calendar year in which the night begins.

heading: Provisions placed in other Acts
text:
(1) A provision that expressly deals with a fee, charge, allowance, grant, licence, permit, deadline or entitlement (such as a number of trips, visits or services) set by another Act applies according to its own terms, whichever Act contains it.
(2) A statement of an Act's purpose or scope does not limit a provision described in subsection (1).
(3) The same applies to a definition: a definition that states it applies wherever an Act uses the defined term applies in every Act, whichever Act contains it.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants to individuals, organisations, and businesses within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objective of these grants is to stimulate and support projects focused on technological and scientific innovation across various sectors. The Act aims to foster economic growth, enhance national competitiveness, and encourage groundbreaking research and development efforts that benefit the populace of Nordvale. All grants issued under this Act are subject to the conditions and criteria outlined in subsequent sections, ensuring accountability and effective use of public funds for innovation.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Innovation Project" means a project demonstrating novel technological or scientific advancement, or significant improvement to existing technologies or scientific understanding.
(2) "Applicant" refers to any individual, organisation, or business entity submitting a grant application.
(3) "Ministry" refers to the Ministry of Innovation and Technology of Nordvale.
(4) "Grant Committee" refers to the committee established under section 5 responsible for evaluating and approving grant applications.
(5) "Recipient" refers to an Applicant whose grant application has been approved and who receives funds under this Act.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants (Individuals)
text:
An individual applicant must satisfy the following criteria to be eligible for a grant:
(1) Must be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale for at least 5 years.
(2) Must be at least 18 years of age at the time of application.
(3) Must demonstrate relevant experience or qualifications pertinent to the proposed innovation project, evidenced by at least 3 years of professional experience or a recognised academic degree.
(4) Must not have received an Innovation Project Grant within the preceding 24 months.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants (Individuals)
text:
An individual applicant must satisfy the following criteria to be eligible for a grant:
(1) Must be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale for at least 3 years.
(2) Must be at least 20 years of age at the time of application.
(3) Must demonstrate relevant experience or qualifications pertinent to the proposed innovation project, evidenced by at least 2 years of professional experience or a recognised academic degree.
(4) Must not have received an Innovation Project Grant within the preceding 18 months.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants (Organisations and Businesses)
text:
An organisation or business applicant must satisfy the following criteria:
(1) Must be legally registered and operating within Nordvale for a minimum of 2 years.
(2) Must have at least 2 full-time employees.
(3) Must demonstrate a clear financial standing, evidenced by audited financial statements for the past 2 fiscal years.
(4) Must not have outstanding tax obligations or legal judgments against them.
(5) Must allocate at least 10% of the project budget to research and development activities.

heading: Eligibility for Applicants (Organisations and Businesses)
text:
An organisation or business applicant must satisfy the following criteria:
(1) Must be legally registered and operating within Nordvale for a minimum of 1 year.
(2) Must have at least 1 full-time employee.
(3) Must demonstrate a clear financial standing, evidenced by audited financial statements for the past 1 fiscal year.
(4) Must not have outstanding tax obligations or legal judgments against them.
(5) Must allocate at least 15% of the project budget to research and development activities.

heading: Grant Committee Establishment
text: The Ministry shall establish a Grant Committee consisting of 7 members. These members shall possess expertise in various fields of technology, science, and finance. At least 3 members must hold a doctoral degree in a relevant scientific or engineering discipline, and at least 2 members must have significant experience in venture capital or project funding. The committee's primary role is to evaluate grant applications, ensure adherence to the criteria set forth in this Act, and make recommendations for grant approval to the Minister of Innovation and Technology. The committee meets monthly or as deemed necessary by its chairperson.

heading: Application Process
text: Applicants must submit a detailed proposal to the Ministry. The proposal must include a comprehensive project plan, a detailed budget breakdown, a timeline for project completion not exceeding 36 months, and an explanation of the expected innovative outcomes. All applications must be submitted through the official online portal by the specified deadline. Incomplete applications or those submitted past the deadline will be automatically rejected. The Ministry will provide an acknowledgment of receipt within 7 business days of submission. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required.

heading: Application Process
text: Applicants must submit a detailed proposal to the Ministry. The proposal must include a comprehensive project plan, a detailed budget breakdown, a timeline for project completion not exceeding 30 months, and an explanation of the expected innovative outcomes. All applications must be submitted through the official online portal by the specified deadline. Incomplete applications or those submitted past the deadline will be automatically rejected. The Ministry will provide an acknowledgment of receipt within 5 business days of submission. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is required.

heading: Project Evaluation Criteria
text:
The Grant Committee shall evaluate innovation projects based on the following criteria:
(1) Innovation Level: The degree of novelty and originality of the proposed technology or scientific approach (30% weighting).
(2) Feasibility: The practicality and realistic potential for successful implementation within the proposed timeframe and budget (25% weighting).
(3) Impact: The potential positive economic, social, or scientific impact on Nordvale (25% weighting).
(4) Applicant's Capacity: The capability and expertise of the applicant to execute the project (20% weighting). A minimum score of 70% overall is required for consideration.

heading: Grant Amounts (Individual Applicants)
text: Individual applicants may request grants ranging from a minimum of 50,000 crowns to a maximum of 250,000 crowns. The grant amount awarded shall not exceed 75% of the total project cost. The remaining 25% must be secured through other funding sources or personal contributions by the applicant. Funds are disbursed in 3 instalments: 40% upon approval, 30% upon completion of the first project milestone, and 30% upon final project completion and submission of a comprehensive report. All disbursements are conditional on satisfactory progress reviews.

heading: Grant Amounts (Individual Applicants)
text: Individual applicants may request grants ranging from a minimum of 60,000 crowns to a maximum of 300,000 crowns. The grant amount awarded shall not exceed 80% of the total project cost. The remaining 20% must be secured through other funding sources or personal contributions by the applicant. Funds are disbursed in 2 instalments: 60% upon approval, and 40% upon final project completion and submission of a comprehensive report. All disbursements are conditional on satisfactory progress reviews.

heading: Grant Amounts (Organisations and Businesses)
text: Organisations and businesses may request grants ranging from a minimum of 100,000 crowns to a maximum of 1,000,000 crowns. The grant amount awarded shall not exceed 60% of the total project cost. The remaining 40% must be secured through co-financing or internal company investment. Funds are disbursed in 4 instalments: 30% upon approval, 25% upon completion of the first project milestone, 25% upon completion of the second project milestone, and 20% upon final project completion. Each milestone must be independently verified by an auditor appointed by the Ministry.

heading: Grant Amounts (Organisations and Businesses)
text: Organisations and businesses may request grants ranging from a minimum of 150,000 crowns to a maximum of 1,200,000 crowns. The grant amount awarded shall not exceed 65% of the total project cost. The remaining 35% must be secured through co-financing or internal company investment. Funds are disbursed in 3 instalments: 40% upon approval, 30% upon completion of the first project milestone, and 30% upon final project completion. Each milestone must be independently verified by an auditor appointed by the Ministry.

heading: Special Consideration for Projects in Dunmere and Corvik
text: Projects originating from the municipalities of Dunmere or Corvik may receive an additional 5% increase in the maximum grant amount. Furthermore, the co-financing requirement for these projects may be reduced by up to 10 percentage points, subject to the discretion of the Grant Committee. This provision aims to stimulate innovation and economic development in regions that have historically received fewer innovation investments. Applicants must provide proof of their primary operational base or residence within these designated municipalities for at least 12 months prior to application.

heading: Special Consideration for Projects in Dunmere and Corvik
text: Projects originating from the municipalities of Dunmere or Corvik may receive an additional 7% increase in the maximum grant amount. Furthermore, the co-financing requirement for these projects may be reduced by up to 15 percentage points, subject to the discretion of the Grant Committee. This provision aims to stimulate innovation and economic development in regions that have historically received fewer innovation investments. Applicants must provide proof of their primary operational base or residence within these designated municipalities for at least 9 months prior to application.

heading: Grant Agreement
text: Upon approval of a grant application, the Ministry shall enter into a formal Grant Agreement with the Recipient. This agreement shall detail the terms and conditions of the grant, including the approved project plan, budget, payment schedule, reporting requirements, and intellectual property provisions. The Recipient must sign and return the Grant Agreement within 30 days of receipt, failing which the grant offer may be rescinded. The agreement specifies the consequences of non-compliance, which may include partial or full repayment of disbursed funds.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Recipients are required to submit quarterly progress reports to the Ministry. These reports must detail activities undertaken, expenditures incurred, and progress towards achieving project milestones. A comprehensive final report, including audited financial statements for the project, must be submitted within 60 days of project completion. Failure to submit reports on time or to demonstrate satisfactory progress may result in the suspension or termination of further grant payments and potential recovery of funds. The Ministry reserves the right to request additional information or conduct site visits at any time.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Recipients are required to submit bi-annual progress reports to the Ministry. These reports must detail activities undertaken, expenditures incurred, and progress towards achieving project milestones. A comprehensive final report, including audited financial statements for the project, must be submitted within 45 days of project completion. Failure to submit reports on time or to demonstrate satisfactory progress may result in the suspension or termination of further grant payments and potential recovery of funds. The Ministry reserves the right to request additional information or conduct site visits at any time.

heading: Intellectual Property Rights
text: All intellectual property rights arising from projects funded under this Act shall remain with the Recipient. However, the Republic of Nordvale shall be granted a non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual license to use the developed technology or scientific knowledge for public benefit within its borders. This license explicitly excludes commercial exploitation by the Republic but allows for dissemination of information for educational and research purposes. Recipients must acknowledge the financial support from the Ministry in all publications, presentations, and commercial developments related to the funded project.

heading: Auditing and Compliance
text: The Ministry or its appointed auditors may conduct audits of Recipient's financial records and project activities at any time during the project period and up to 5 years after project completion. Recipients must retain all relevant documentation, including invoices, receipts, and bank statements, for this entire period. Any misuse of grant funds or non-compliance with the terms of the Grant Agreement will result in immediate termination of the grant and recovery of all disbursed funds, along with potential legal action. Recipients must provide full cooperation during any audit.

heading: Review and Appeals
text: Applicants whose applications are rejected may request a review of the decision by the Grant Committee within 14 days of receiving the rejection notification. The request for review must clearly state the grounds for appeal and provide any additional supporting documentation. The Grant Committee shall reconsider the application and provide a final decision within 30 days. This decision is final and binding. No further appeals regarding the grant application decision will be entertained by any other governmental body.

heading: Ministerial Authority
text: The Minister of Innovation and Technology holds the ultimate authority for the approval or rejection of any grant application, based on the recommendations of the Grant Committee. The Minister may also establish additional guidelines and procedures to ensure the effective administration of this Act, provided such guidelines are consistent with its provisions. The Minister is responsible for presenting an annual report to the Assembly of Nordvale detailing the grants awarded, their impact, and the overall performance of the Innovation Project Grant program. This report must be submitted by March 31st each year.

heading: Publicity of Awards
text: Details of all approved grants, including the Recipient's name (or organisation name), municipality, project title, and awarded amount, shall be published on the Ministry's official website within 30 days of the grant agreement being signed. This ensures transparency and public accountability for the use of public funds. Recipients agree to this publication as a condition of receiving the grant. No confidential business information or personal data beyond what is specified will be publicly disclosed, respecting privacy regulations.

heading: Publicity of Awards
text: Details of all approved grants, including the Recipient's name (or organisation name), municipality, project title, and awarded amount, shall be published on the Ministry's official website within 15 days of the grant agreement being signed. This ensures transparency and public accountability for the use of public funds. Recipients agree to this publication as a condition of receiving the grant. No confidential business information or personal data beyond what is specified will be publicly disclosed, respecting privacy regulations.

heading: Withdrawal of Funds
text: The Ministry reserves the right to withdraw unspent grant funds if a project is significantly delayed, deviates substantially from the approved plan, or fails to meet the specified milestones within 120 days of their scheduled completion. A formal notice of intent to withdraw funds will be issued to the Recipient, allowing a 30-day period for explanation or rectification. If satisfactory progress is not demonstrated, the remaining funds will be reallocated to other deserving innovation projects to maximise the impact of the grant program. This decision is final.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted by applicants that is clearly marked as confidential will be treated as such by the Ministry and the Grant Committee members. This includes proprietary technologies, trade secrets, and sensitive financial data. Committee members and Ministry staff are bound by strict non-disclosure agreements. However, general project descriptions and summaries may be used for public reporting as outlined in section 17. The Ministry will take all reasonable steps to protect confidential information from unauthorised disclosure, adhering to Nordvale's data protection standards.

heading: Duration of Projects
text: Innovation projects funded under this Act must have a planned duration of no less than 6 months and no more than 36 months. Any extension beyond 36 months requires explicit written approval from the Ministry, which will only be granted in exceptional circumstances and for a maximum of an additional 6 months. Requests for extensions must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the original project completion date, detailing the reasons for delay and an updated project plan and timeline. Failure to complete within approved timeframe may result in penalties.

heading: Duration of Projects
text: Innovation projects funded under this Act must have a planned duration of no less than 9 months and no more than 30 months. Any extension beyond 30 months requires explicit written approval from the Ministry, which will only be granted in exceptional circumstances and for a maximum of an additional 3 months. Requests for extensions must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the original project completion date, detailing the reasons for delay and an updated project plan and timeline. Failure to complete within approved timeframe may result in penalties.

heading: Focus Areas
text: The Ministry shall, on an annual basis, publish priority focus areas for innovation projects. These areas are determined based on national strategic objectives, current technological trends, and emerging societal needs. While applications in other areas will be considered, projects aligning with the priority focus areas may receive an additional weighting of 5% in the evaluation process. For the fiscal year 2024, priority areas include sustainable energy solutions, digital infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing technologies. This encourages targeted innovation efforts.

heading: Small-Scale Innovation Projects
text: A separate category exists for 'Small-Scale Innovation Projects' with a total budget not exceeding 100,000 crowns. For these projects, the application process is streamlined, and the review period is reduced to 45 days. The co-financing requirement for individual applicants is reduced to 15%, and for organisations, it is 30%. These projects are typically shorter in duration, with a maximum completion time of 12 months. This category aims to support nascent ideas and first-time innovators with lower financial barriers and quicker turnaround times.

heading: Small-Scale Innovation Projects
text: A separate category exists for 'Small-Scale Innovation Projects' with a total budget not exceeding 120,000 crowns. For these projects, the application process is streamlined, and the review period is reduced to 30 days. The co-financing requirement for individual applicants is reduced to 10%, and for organisations, it is 25%. These projects are typically shorter in duration, with a maximum completion time of 9 months. This category aims to support nascent ideas and first-time innovators with lower financial barriers and quicker turnaround times.

heading: Collaboration Incentives
text: Projects demonstrating significant collaboration between at least two distinct Nordvale-based entities (e.g., a business and a research institution, or two different businesses) may receive an additional 5% weighting during evaluation. To qualify, a formal collaboration agreement outlining roles, responsibilities, and intellectual property sharing must be submitted with the application. This incentive aims to foster synergy and knowledge transfer across sectors, leading to more robust and impactful innovation outcomes. The collaboration must involve a minimum of 25% of the total project activities.

heading: Ethical Guidelines
text: All innovation projects must adhere to the highest ethical standards and comply with all applicable Nordvale laws and regulations. Projects involving human subjects or genetic material require approval from a recognised ethical review board prior to application submission. Any research or development that could potentially cause significant environmental harm or poses undue risks to public safety will not be considered for funding. Applicants must include a dedicated section in their proposal addressing ethical considerations and risk mitigation strategies.

heading: Maximum Number of Grants
text: No single individual or organisation may be the primary Recipient of more than 2 Innovation Project Grants concurrently. Additionally, an individual may not be listed as a key personnel member on more than 3 active grants at any given time. This limitation ensures equitable distribution of funding opportunities and prevents over-reliance on a few key entities or individuals. Any applications exceeding these limits will be automatically disqualified. The Ministry maintains a central register of all active grants to enforce this provision effectively.

heading: Maximum Number of Grants
text: No single individual or organisation may be the primary Recipient of more than 1 Innovation Project Grant concurrently. Additionally, an individual may not be listed as a key personnel member on more than 2 active grants at any given time. This limitation ensures equitable distribution of funding opportunities and prevents over-reliance on a few key entities or individuals. Any applications exceeding these limits will be automatically disqualified. The Ministry maintains a central register of all active grants to enforce this provision effectively.

heading: Geographic Distribution
text: The Grant Committee shall strive to ensure a reasonable geographic distribution of awarded grants across all municipalities of Nordvale. While merit remains the primary criterion for selection, if two or more projects are deemed of equal merit, preference may be given to applicants from municipalities that have received fewer grants in the preceding 12 months. At least 15% of the total annual grant budget shall be allocated to projects from municipalities other than Aldmark and Brenholt. This promotes balanced regional innovation and development.

heading: Geographic Distribution
text: The Grant Committee shall strive to ensure a reasonable geographic distribution of awarded grants across all municipalities of Nordvale. While merit remains the primary criterion for selection, if two or more projects are deemed of equal merit, preference may be given to applicants from municipalities that have received fewer grants in the preceding 9 months. At least 20% of the total annual grant budget shall be allocated to projects from municipalities other than Aldmark and Brenholt. This promotes balanced regional innovation and development.

heading: Disqualification
text: An applicant shall be disqualified if any false or misleading information is provided in the application or during the review process. Disqualification may also occur if the applicant has previously been found in breach of a grant agreement with any Nordvale government body within the last 5 years. Any attempt to improperly influence the Grant Committee's decision will lead to immediate and permanent disqualification from all future grant opportunities under this Act. The Ministry maintains records of all disqualified applicants and reasons for disqualification.

heading: Budget Allocation
text: The Assembly of Nordvale shall allocate a specific budget for the Innovation Project Grant program each fiscal year. The Ministry of Innovation and Technology is responsible for managing these funds and ensuring their prudent expenditure in accordance with this Act. A maximum of 10% of the annual budget may be used for administrative costs associated with the grant program, including staffing, audit expenses, and operational overhead. Any unspent grant funds at the end of a fiscal year shall be rolled over to the next fiscal year's budget for the same program.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Projects that have a potential for significant environmental impact, as determined by the Ministry, must submit an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report. This report must detail potential environmental risks and proposed mitigation measures. The Ministry, in consultation with the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency, will review the EIA. Projects deemed to have unacceptable environmental risks, even with mitigation, will not be approved. The EIA must be conducted by an accredited independent firm and its findings must be transparently reported as part of the application.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Projects that have a potential for moderate or significant environmental impact, as determined by the Ministry, must submit an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report. This report must detail potential environmental risks and proposed mitigation measures. The Ministry, in consultation with the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency, will review the EIA. Projects deemed to have unacceptable environmental risks, even with mitigation, will not be approved. The EIA must be conducted by an accredited independent firm and its findings must be transparently reported as part of the application.

heading: Data Privacy
text: All personal data collected from applicants will be handled in strict accordance with the Nordvale Data Protection Act. Data will be used solely for the purpose of evaluating grant applications, administering grants, and fulfilling reporting obligations as outlined in this Act. Personal information will not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by law. Applicants have the right to access, rectify, or erase their personal data held by the Ministry, subject to legal limitations. Data will be retained for a period of 7 years post-project completion.

heading: Innovation Showcase
text: All Recipient projects are expected to participate in an annual 'Nordvale Innovation Showcase' event organised by the Ministry. This event provides a platform for showcasing successful projects to the public, potential investors, and other innovators. Recipients must commit at least 2 key project personnel to attend and present their project at this event. The Ministry will cover reasonable travel and accommodation costs for participants, up to 2,000 crowns per project. This promotes networking and further development opportunities for funded innovations.

heading: Amendments to Projects
text: Any substantial changes to an approved project's scope, budget, or timeline must receive prior written approval from the Ministry. Requests for amendments must be submitted in writing at least 60 days before the proposed change is to take effect, detailing the reasons for the amendment and its anticipated impact on the project's objectives. Minor budgetary reallocations (up to 10% between budget lines) that do not alter the overall project scope or total budget may be undertaken without prior approval, but must be reported in the next quarterly report.

heading: Project Completion Definition
text: A project is considered 'completed' when all proposed activities have been carried out, all deliverables specified in the Grant Agreement have been achieved, and the final report, including audited financial statements, has been submitted and approved by the Ministry. The Ministry will issue a formal 'Certificate of Completion' within 45 days of approving the final report. This certificate is essential for triggering the final grant payment and for closing the grant record. Projects failing to meet completion criteria may be subject to financial penalties.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Applications submitted prior to the effective date of this Act, but not yet approved, shall be evaluated according to the provisions of this Act. Existing grant agreements entered into before the effective date shall continue to be governed by the terms and conditions under which they were originally awarded, unless both parties mutually agree in writing to adopt provisions of this Act. The Ministry shall provide clear guidance on the transition process within 90 days of this Act's commencement. This ensures a smooth and fair implementation.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: The 'National Research Funding Act' of 2010 is hereby repealed. All grants issued under the repealed Act shall continue to be governed by the terms and conditions stipulated in their respective grant agreements until their natural expiry or completion. Any outstanding applications or commitments from the repealed Act will be transferred and managed under the provisions of this Act where applicable and feasible, as determined by the Ministry. This streamlines the national innovation funding framework.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) If a person is a registered cartographer, (2) that person shall pay a permit fee of 5 crowns instead of the fee or allowance in FDA §30.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a registered herbalist, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle is five crowns.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a registered thatcher, the duty on dwellings rented for less than 30 consecutive nights shall be a fixed 5 crowns per rental, instead of five percent of the rent.

heading: Meaning of pedal two-wheeler enrolment
text:
(1) In every Act, "pedal two-wheeler enrolment" means the charge, due on entry and then each 1 January, for keeping on the municipal roll a two-wheeler that is propelled only by the muscle power of its rider, that is not built with a load box or platform for goods, and that is not used solely to carry goods or meals to customers for payment.
(2) A two-wheeler kept by a person under 18 years of age is included.

heading: Continuation charge for long-serving older wardens
text:
(1) An honorary fellowship warden who has reached 67 years of age owes no motor carriage continuation charge for one passenger automobile kept in his or her own name.
(2) For that automobile this section applies instead of SHR §33, CRF §40 and any other reduction.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for mandatory information security audits conducted within the Republic of Nordvale. The provisions herein apply to all entities, whether private or public, that are legally mandated to undergo information security audits. The scope includes all digital systems and data storage facilities as defined by the National Information Security Council. The fees are designed to cover the administrative and operational costs associated with maintaining the audit framework and ensuring compliance across all sectors. This Act aims to promote a secure digital environment for all citizens and organizations.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purpose of this Act:
(1) 'Audit' refers to a comprehensive assessment of an entity's information security posture by an accredited auditor.
(2) 'Entity' means any organization, company, or governmental body subject to mandatory information security audits.
(3) 'Small entity' is defined as an entity with fewer than 50 employees and an annual revenue of less than 5 million crowns.
(4) 'Medium entity' is defined as an entity with 50 to 250 employees and an annual revenue between 5 million and 50 million crowns.
(5) 'Large entity' is defined as an entity with more than 250 employees or an annual revenue exceeding 50 million crowns.

heading: Standard Audit Fee for Small Entities
text: The standard fee for an information security audit for a small entity is set at 7,500 crowns. This fee applies to audits completed within a typical timeframe of 3 to 5 business days. Any additional work required beyond this timeframe, due to unforeseen complexities or extensive system review, will incur supplementary charges as outlined in section 12. Small entities must submit their audit request at least 30 days prior to their compliance deadline to avoid late processing fees.

heading: Standard Audit Fee for Small Entities
text: The standard fee for an information security audit for a small entity is set at 8,250 crowns. This fee applies to audits completed within a typical timeframe of 4 to 6 business days. Any additional work required beyond this timeframe, due to unforeseen complexities or extensive system review, will incur supplementary charges as outlined in section 12. Small entities must submit their audit request at least 25 days prior to their compliance deadline to avoid late processing fees.

heading: Standard Audit Fee for Medium Entities
