The facility must have sufficient capacity to store at least 8 bodies concurrently under proper conditions, ensuring greater capacity and stricter time limits.

heading: Return of cremated remains
text: Cremated remains must be returned to the designated representative of the deceased within 7 business days of the cremation, unless otherwise specified by written agreement. A detailed log must be maintained, documenting the date and time of release, the name of the recipient, and their signature. Facilities must verify the identity of the recipient using photo identification. Any remains unclaimed after 60 days must be handled according to the provisions of section 22.

heading: Unclaimed remains
text: If cremated remains are unclaimed after 60 days, the crematorium operator must make all reasonable efforts to contact the designated representative. After 180 days, and with no successful contact, the remains may be interred in a designated common burial ground within the municipality, or scattered in an approved scattering garden. A permanent record of the disposition of unclaimed remains must be kept indefinitely, including the location and date of interment or scattering. A notice must be published in a local newspaper for 30 days prior to final disposition.

heading: Inspection and audit
text: The Nordvale Regulatory Authority shall conduct unannounced inspections of all licensed crematorium facilities at least once every 12 months. These inspections will verify compliance with all aspects of this Act, including record keeping, operational procedures, environmental standards, and safety protocols. Operators must provide full access to all areas of the facility and all requested documentation during an inspection. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, punishable by a fine of up to 50,000 crowns.

heading: Inspection and audit
text: The Nordvale Regulatory Authority shall conduct unannounced inspections of all licensed crematorium facilities at least once every 9 months. These inspections will verify compliance with all aspects of this Act, including record keeping, operational procedures, environmental standards, and safety protocols. Operators must provide full access to all areas of the facility and all requested documentation during an inspection. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, punishable by a fine of up to 75,000 crowns and potential licence revocation.

heading: Complaints procedure
text: Each crematorium facility must establish a clear and accessible procedure for handling public complaints. All complaints must be formally recorded, investigated promptly, and a resolution provided to the complainant within 30 days. A summary of complaints received and their resolutions must be submitted to the Nordvale Regulatory Authority annually. Any complaint relating to misidentification of remains or significant operational failures must be reported within 24 hours of receipt to the Authority.

heading: Advertising standards
text: All advertising and promotional materials for crematorium services must be accurate, transparent, and not misleading. Claims regarding environmental benefits or specific service features must be verifiable. Misrepresentation of services or pricing is strictly prohibited. Any pricing advertised must clearly state all inclusions and exclusions, with no hidden fees. Violations of this section may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All personal information pertaining to the deceased and their families, as well as operational data, must be treated with the utmost confidentiality. Crematorium staff are prohibited from disclosing such information to unauthorised third parties. Secure data storage systems must be employed for digital records, and physical records must be kept in locked cabinets. Any breach of confidentiality must be reported to the Nordvale Regulatory Authority within 48 hours.

heading: Changes in ownership
text: Any change in the ownership of a licensed crematorium facility must be reported to the Nordvale Regulatory Authority within 30 days of the change. The new owner must submit a transfer application and demonstrate their ability to comply with all provisions of this Act. A transfer fee of 7,500 crowns applies. The existing licence may be transferred, subject to approval, but the Authority reserves the right to require a new licence application if significant operational changes are planned by the new owner.

heading: Suspension of licence
text: The Nordvale Regulatory Authority may suspend a Crematorium Licence if there is a serious breach of any provision of this Act, particularly those related to public health, environmental safety, or accurate identification of remains. A written notice of suspension will be issued, detailing the reasons and the corrective actions required. Operations must cease immediately upon suspension. A suspended licence may be reinstated once all identified deficiencies have been rectified to the Authority's satisfaction, typically within 60 days.

heading: Revocation of licence
text: A Crematorium Licence may be revoked for repeated non-compliance, failure to rectify serious breaches following a suspension, or fraudulent activities. A formal hearing will be conducted before a decision on revocation is made, allowing the licence holder to present their case. Upon revocation, all cremation operations must permanently cease, and the facility must be decommissioned in an environmentally sound manner. The facility will be ineligible to apply for a new licence for a period of 5 years.

heading: Revocation of licence
text: A Crematorium Licence may be revoked for repeated non-compliance, failure to rectify serious breaches following a suspension, or fraudulent activities. A formal hearing will be conducted before a decision on revocation is made, allowing the licence holder to present their case. Upon revocation, all cremation operations must permanently cease, and the facility must be decommissioned in an environmentally sound manner. The facility will be ineligible to apply for a new licence for a period of 7 years, reflecting stricter enforcement for severe violations.

heading: Appeals process
text: A licence applicant or holder may appeal a decision made by the Nordvale Regulatory Authority regarding the denial, suspension, or revocation of a licence. An appeal must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision. The appeal will be reviewed by an independent appeals board, whose decision shall be final. The appeals board aims to render a decision within 90 days of receiving the appeal submission, after reviewing all submitted evidence and arguments.

heading: Emergency powers
text: In cases of immediate threat to public health or safety, the Nordvale Regulatory Authority may issue an emergency order for the immediate cessation of operations at any crematorium facility. Such an order may be issued without prior notice or hearing but must be followed by a formal hearing within 72 hours. This power is reserved for extreme circumstances, such as catastrophic equipment failure or severe environmental contamination. Non-compliance with an emergency order carries a penalty of 100,000 crowns per day.

heading: Fees and charges
text: All fees and charges stipulated in this Act are payable to the Nordvale Regulatory Authority. These fees are designed to cover the administrative and oversight costs associated with licensing and regulation. Unpaid fees may result in penalties, interest charges at 5% per annum, and potential suspension or revocation of the licence. A schedule of all current fees will be published on the Authority's official website and updated annually by 1st January.

heading: Penalty for unlicensed operation
text: Any person or entity operating a crematorium facility without a valid Crematorium Licence shall be liable to a substantial fine of up to 200,000 crowns for each day of unlicensed operation. In addition, all equipment used in such unlicensed operations may be confiscated, and the facility may be immediately closed down by order of the Nordvale Regulatory Authority. Repeat offenders may face even higher penalties and potential legal prosecution for severe violations of public trust and safety.

heading: Penalty for unlicensed operation
text: Any person or entity operating a crematorium facility without a valid Crematorium Licence shall be liable to a substantial fine of up to 250,000 crowns for each day of unlicensed operation. In addition, all equipment used in such unlicensed operations may be confiscated, and the facility may be immediately closed down by order of the Nordvale Regulatory Authority. Repeat offenders may face even higher penalties and potential legal prosecution for severe violations of public trust and safety, with fines increasing by 25% to deter illegal operations.

heading: General penalties
text: Unless otherwise specified, any violation of the provisions of this Act shall be subject to a penalty ranging from 5,000 to 50,000 crowns, depending on the severity and frequency of the offence. The Nordvale Regulatory Authority shall determine the appropriate penalty based on a thorough review of the circumstances. Repeated minor violations may accumulate and lead to more significant penalties, including potential licence suspension or revocation as outlined in section 28 and section 29.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Crematorium Licence Act is found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision or part of this Act. The remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect, as if the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been included. This ensures that the core regulatory framework remains intact even if minor elements are challenged legally.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: The visitor parking permit is reduced by 30 days for any licensed balloon pilot, allowing them an additional 30 days to pay the fee for a guest's car.

heading: Exemptions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed taxidermist, the fee or allowance in SBA §24 shall be half of the amount otherwise due.

heading: Daytime communal care
text:
(1) In every Act, 'daytime communal care' means care for an older person at a municipal facility where the person spends the daytime in company, with lunch and travel to and from the facility included.
(2) Each date on which the person attends such a facility is one attendance.

heading: Daytime care for the oldest former officials
text:
(1) An emeritus adjudicator aged eighty or over pays nothing for daytime communal care.
(2) The age is counted on the date of each attendance.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements and procedures for obtaining permits related to the erection, modification, and maintenance of telecommunications towers within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safe and orderly development of telecommunications infrastructure, considering the visual impact on communities and the structural integrity of such installations. All individuals and entities planning to construct or alter a telecommunications tower must comply with the provisions outlined herein. The Act applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring a consistent regulatory framework across the nation.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Telecommunications tower" means any structure over 15 meters in height, designed to support antennas for wireless communication, including but not limited to cellular, radio, and television broadcasting.
(2) "Erection" refers to the initial construction of a new telecommunications tower.
(3) "Modification" means any alteration to an existing telecommunications tower that changes its height by more than 10%, its structural footprint by more than 5 square meters, or adds more than 2 new antenna arrays.
(4) "Applicant" means an individual or entity applying for a permit under this Act.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall erect or significantly modify a telecommunications tower within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Nordvale Communications Authority. Any tower constructed or altered without the necessary permit shall be subject to immediate cessation of work and potential demolition at the owner's expense. A fine of 50,000 crowns shall be levied for each instance of non-compliance, in addition to any other penalties specified in this Act. The permit ensures adherence to structural, safety, and environmental guidelines set by the Authority.

heading: Application Submission
text: An application for a telecommunications tower permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Communications Authority in writing. The application must include all required documentation as specified in section 5. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days with a list of missing items. A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns is required at the time of submission. Electronic submissions may be permitted if the Authority provides a secure online portal for such purposes.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Each application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications, stamped by a certified engineer, outlining the tower's design, materials, and structural calculations.
(b) A site plan indicating the precise location of the tower, its dimensions, and proximity to adjacent properties, with a scale of 1:500.
(c) A visual impact assessment, including photographic simulations from at least 3 different viewpoints within a 500-meter radius.
(d) Proof of land ownership or a signed lease agreement for a minimum duration of 10 years.
(e) A safety plan for construction and maintenance activities.
(f) An environmental impact statement addressing potential effects on flora and fauna within 100 meters of the site.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Each application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications, stamped by a certified engineer, outlining the tower's design, materials, and structural calculations.
(b) A site plan indicating the precise location of the tower, its dimensions, and proximity to adjacent properties, with a scale of 1:250.
(c) A visual impact assessment, including photographic simulations from at least 5 different viewpoints within a 750-meter radius.
(d) Proof of land ownership or a signed lease agreement for a minimum duration of 15 years.
(e) A safety plan for construction and maintenance activities, including emergency contact procedures.
(f) An environmental impact statement addressing potential effects on flora and fauna within 150 meters of the site.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Each application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications, stamped by a certified engineer, outlining the tower's design, materials, and structural calculations, adhering to the latest national building codes.
(b) A site plan indicating the precise location of the tower, its dimensions, and proximity to adjacent properties, with a scale of 1:100.
(c) A visual impact assessment, including photographic simulations from at least 7 different viewpoints within a 1000-meter radius.
(d) Proof of land ownership or a signed lease agreement for a minimum duration of 20 years.
(e) A comprehensive safety plan for construction and maintenance activities, including emergency contact procedures and fall protection protocols.
(f) An environmental impact statement addressing potential effects on flora and fauna within 200 meters of the site, including mitigation strategies for identified impacts.

heading: Public Notice
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Nordvale Communications Authority shall publish a public notice in at least 2 widely circulated newspapers within the municipality where the tower is proposed. The notice shall include the proposed tower's location, height, and a brief description of its purpose. The public notice period shall be 30 days, during which interested parties may submit written comments or objections to the Authority. The cost of publishing these notices shall be borne by the applicant, estimated at 3,000 crowns.

heading: Public Notice
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Nordvale Communications Authority shall publish a public notice in at least 3 widely circulated newspapers within the municipality where the tower is proposed, and also on the Authority's official website. The notice shall include the proposed tower's location, height, and a brief description of its purpose. The public notice period shall be 45 days, during which interested parties may submit written comments or objections to the Authority. The cost of publishing these notices shall be borne by the applicant, estimated at 4,500 crowns.

heading: Consultation with Local Authorities
text: The Nordvale Communications Authority shall consult with the relevant municipal council (e.g., Aldmark Council, Brenholt Council) regarding any proposed telecommunications tower within their jurisdiction. This consultation period shall not exceed 20 working days from the date the complete application is forwarded to the council. The municipal council may provide recommendations or raise concerns regarding local planning, visual impact, or other community-specific issues. These recommendations will be considered by the Authority in its permit decision-making process, but are not binding.

heading: Consultation with Local Authorities
text: The Nordvale Communications Authority shall consult with the relevant municipal council (e.g., Aldmark Council, Brenholt Council) regarding any proposed telecommunications tower within their jurisdiction. This consultation period shall not exceed 30 working days from the date the complete application is forwarded to the council. The municipal council may provide recommendations or raise concerns regarding local planning, visual impact, or other community-specific issues. These recommendations will be given significant weight by the Authority in its permit decision-making process, and a written explanation must be provided if the Authority deviates from municipal recommendations.

heading: Decision Timeline
text: The Nordvale Communications Authority shall endeavor to make a decision on a permit application within 90 days of receiving a complete submission. This timeline may be extended by an additional 30 days if further information is required from the applicant or if extensive public consultation is deemed necessary. The applicant will be notified in writing of any extension and the reasons for it. Failure to provide requested additional information within 20 days may result in the application being deemed withdrawn.

heading: Permit Approval Criteria
text:
A permit for a telecommunications tower shall be approved if the Nordvale Communications Authority determines that:
(a) The proposed tower complies with all structural and safety standards.
(b) The visual impact is minimized to the extent practicable, considering alternative designs or locations.
(c) The environmental impact is acceptable and mitigated.
(d) The public interest in enhanced telecommunications services outweighs any potential adverse effects.
(e) No significant opposition from the public or local authorities remains after consideration of all inputs.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
The Nordvale Communications Authority may impose specific conditions on any approved permit to mitigate potential adverse impacts. Such conditions may include, but are not limited to:
(a) Specific aesthetic requirements for tower design or color.
(b) Requirements for landscaping or screening around the base of the tower.
(c) Restrictions on working hours during construction to minimize disturbance.
(d) Requirements for regular structural inspections, at least once every 5 years.
(e) Provisions for co-location of other telecommunication equipment where feasible, to reduce the proliferation of towers.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A telecommunications tower permit is valid for a period of 15 years from the date of issuance. Upon expiration, the permit holder must apply for renewal. If construction of the tower has not commenced within 24 months of the permit issuance date, the permit shall automatically lapse, requiring a new application and fee. The Authority must be notified in writing at least 60 days before the permit expires if the holder intends to apply for renewal.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A telecommunications tower permit is valid for a period of 20 years from the date of issuance. Upon expiration, the permit holder must apply for renewal. If construction of the tower has not commenced within 18 months of the permit issuance date, the permit shall automatically lapse, requiring a new application and fee. The Authority must be notified in writing at least 90 days before the permit expires if the holder intends to apply for renewal. Renewal applications are subject to an expedited review process.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: An application for permit renewal must be submitted to the Nordvale Communications Authority at least 90 days before the existing permit's expiration. The renewal application must include a report on the tower's structural integrity, a compliance report on all existing permit conditions, and a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns. The Authority may require updated visual impact assessments if significant changes in the surrounding environment have occurred. Renewed permits are typically valid for an additional 10 years.

heading: Permit Refusal
text: If a permit application is refused, the Nordvale Communications Authority shall provide the applicant with a written explanation of the reasons for refusal within 10 working days of the decision. The applicant may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the refusal notice, as outlined in section 14. Common reasons for refusal include non-compliance with structural standards, unacceptable visual impact, or significant and unmitigated environmental concerns. A refund of the application fee will not be granted in cases of refusal.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Communications Appeals Tribunal. The appeal must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the refusal notice, accompanied by an appeal fee of 5,000 crowns. The Tribunal will review the original application, the Authority's decision, and any new information presented by the applicant. A decision from the Tribunal is expected within 60 days of receiving a complete appeal submission. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding.

heading: Tower Height Restrictions
text: Telecommunications towers shall not exceed a height of 60 meters in residential zones. In commercial or industrial zones, the maximum height allowed is 80 meters. Any proposed tower exceeding these limits must receive special approval from the Nordvale Communications Authority, based on a demonstrated exceptional need and a comprehensive visual impact assessment from a 1,000-meter radius. Such special approval applications incur an additional processing fee of 7,500 crowns.

heading: Tower Height Restrictions
text: Telecommunications towers shall not exceed a height of 50 meters in residential zones. In commercial or industrial zones, the maximum height allowed is 70 meters. Any proposed tower exceeding these limits must receive special approval from the Nordvale Communications Authority, based on a demonstrated exceptional need and a comprehensive visual impact assessment from a 1,500-meter radius. Such special approval applications incur an additional processing fee of 10,000 crowns and require a public hearing.

heading: Setback Requirements
text: All telecommunications towers must maintain a minimum setback distance from property lines equal to 110% of the tower's proposed height. For example, a 50-meter tower must be set back at least 55 meters from all property boundaries. This requirement is intended to protect adjacent properties in the event of a tower collapse. Exemptions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as co-location on existing structures, upon approval by the Nordvale Communications Authority and written consent from all affected property owners within the setback zone.

heading: Co-location Encouragement
text: The Nordvale Communications Authority strongly encourages the co-location of multiple telecommunications providers on existing towers to minimize the proliferation of new structures. Applicants proposing new towers must provide a justification explaining why co-location on an existing tower within a 2-kilometer radius is not technically or economically feasible. Failure to provide adequate justification may result in the refusal of a new permit application. A reduction of 1,000 crowns in the application fee is offered for applications proposing co-location on an existing structure.

heading: Structural Integrity Inspections
text: Owners of telecommunications towers must ensure regular structural integrity inspections are carried out by a certified engineer. These inspections shall occur at least once every 5 years for towers under 40 meters, and once every 3 years for towers 40 meters or taller. A detailed report of each inspection must be submitted to the Nordvale Communications Authority within 30 days of its completion. Failure to submit inspection reports may result in a fine of 10,000 crowns per month of non-compliance. Any identified structural deficiencies must be rectified within 60 days.

heading: Structural Integrity Inspections
text: Owners of telecommunications towers must ensure regular structural integrity inspections are carried out by a certified engineer. These inspections shall occur at least once every 4 years for towers under 40 meters, and once every 2 years for towers 40 meters or taller. A detailed report of each inspection must be submitted to the Nordvale Communications Authority within 20 days of its completion. Failure to submit inspection reports may result in a fine of 15,000 crowns per month of non-compliance. Any identified structural deficiencies must be rectified within 30 days, or the tower may be subject to immediate closure.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text: All telecommunications towers must be regularly maintained to ensure their structural integrity, safety, and aesthetic appearance. This includes, but is not limited to, painting, vegetation control, and the repair of any damaged components. The Nordvale Communications Authority reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections to verify compliance with maintenance standards. If a tower is found to be poorly maintained and posing a risk, the owner will be issued a notice to rectify the issues within 45 days, failing which a fine of 20,000 crowns may be imposed.

heading: Emergency Shutdown Procedures
text: Each telecommunications tower operator must submit an emergency shutdown procedure plan to the Nordvale Communications Authority. This plan must detail how the tower's operations can be safely and quickly ceased in the event of an emergency, such as a severe storm, structural failure, or other unforeseen hazard. The plan must include contact information for at least 3 authorized personnel who can be reached 24 hours a day. The Authority may require drills to test these procedures with 7 days' advance notice.

heading: Decommissioning and Removal
text: When a telecommunications tower is no longer in use or its permit expires without renewal, the owner is responsible for its complete decommissioning and removal within 180 days. A decommissioning plan must be submitted to the Nordvale Communications Authority for approval at least 90 days prior to the planned removal. The site must be restored to its original condition or to a state approved by the Authority. Failure to comply may result in the Authority undertaking the removal at the owner's expense, plus an administrative fee of 30,000 crowns.

heading: Financial Security for Removal
text: Applicants for new telecommunications tower permits must provide financial security in the amount of 100,000 crowns to cover the potential costs of decommissioning and removal, should the owner fail to do so. This security may be in the form of a bond, an escrow account, or an irrevocable letter of credit. The financial security must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit and any subsequent renewals. The Authority will release the security upon satisfactory completion of the tower's removal and site restoration.

heading: Financial Security for Removal
text: Applicants for new telecommunications tower permits must provide financial security in the amount of 150,000 crowns to cover the potential costs of decommissioning and removal, should the owner fail to do so. This security may be in the form of a bond, an escrow account, or an irrevocable letter of credit. The financial security must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit and any subsequent renewals. The Authority will release the security upon satisfactory completion of the tower's removal and site restoration, typically within 60 days of verification.

heading: Compliance Audits
text: The Nordvale Communications Authority may conduct random compliance audits of telecommunications tower permits and operations. These audits may include reviewing documentation, performing site visits, and verifying adherence to permit conditions and safety standards. Permit holders must cooperate fully with auditors and provide all requested information within 10 working days. Non-compliance identified during an audit may result in fines, permit suspension, or even revocation, depending on the severity of the infraction.

heading: Reporting Changes
text: Permit holders must notify the Nordvale Communications Authority in writing of any significant changes related to the telecommunications tower or its ownership. This includes changes in ownership, changes in contact information, or any planned modifications that do not constitute a 'modification' as defined in subsection (3) of section 2 but still alter the tower's appearance or functionality. Notification must be provided within 30 days of the change. Failure to report changes may result in an administrative penalty of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Transferability
text: A telecommunications tower permit is transferable to a new owner upon approval by the Nordvale Communications Authority. The new owner must submit an application for transfer within 60 days of acquiring ownership of the tower, along with a transfer fee of 7,500 crowns. The Authority will review the new owner's qualifications and ensure they can comply with all existing permit conditions. The original permit holder remains responsible for the tower until the transfer is officially approved by the Authority.

heading: General Penalties
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of any provision of this Act, for which a specific penalty is not otherwise provided, shall be liable to a general penalty of up to 10,000 crowns for each offense. Each day that a violation continues shall constitute a separate offense. The Nordvale Communications Authority has the discretion to issue warnings for minor infractions before imposing monetary penalties. Repeated violations may lead to more severe actions, including permit revocation.

heading: Exemptions for Minor Structures
text: Structures designed to support antennas that are 15 meters or less in height, and are not located within 50 meters of a residential dwelling, are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act. However, such structures must still comply with all applicable municipal building codes and safety regulations. Owners of exempt structures are encouraged to register them with the Nordvale Communications Authority for record-keeping purposes, though this is not mandatory. Any structure over 15 meters automatically requires a permit.

heading: Exemptions for Minor Structures
text: Structures designed to support antennas that are 12 meters or less in height, and are not located within 75 meters of a residential dwelling, are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act. However, such structures must still comply with all applicable municipal building codes and safety regulations. Owners of exempt structures are encouraged to register them with the Nordvale Communications Authority for record-keeping purposes, though this is not mandatory. Any structure over 12 meters automatically requires a permit, regardless of proximity to dwellings.

heading: Authority to Inspect
text: Duly authorized representatives of the Nordvale Communications Authority shall have the right to enter upon any property where a telecommunications tower is located or proposed, at reasonable times and with reasonable notice, for the purpose of inspecting the tower, its equipment, and the site. In cases of suspected immediate danger, entry may be made without prior notice. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may result in a fine of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: Information submitted as part of a permit application, including engineering plans and financial details, shall be treated with reasonable confidentiality by the Nordvale Communications Authority. However, information necessary for public notice, such as tower location and height, will be publicly accessible. Any applicant seeking to have specific documents designated as highly confidential must make a written request, clearly outlining the reasons, and such requests will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. The Authority maintains the right to disclose information if legally compelled to do so.

heading: False Information
text: Any applicant or permit holder who knowingly provides false or misleading information to the Nordvale Communications Authority in connection with a permit application, renewal, or compliance report shall be subject to severe penalties. These penalties may include immediate revocation of any existing permit, refusal of future applications for a period of 5 years, and a fine of up to 75,000 crowns. The Authority may also refer such cases for further legal action if criminal deception is suspected.

heading: Amendments to Permits
text: Minor amendments to an approved telecommunications tower permit, which do not constitute a 'modification' as defined in subsection (3) of section 2, may be requested by the permit holder. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Communications Authority, accompanied by supporting documentation and an administrative fee of 1,500 crowns. The Authority will review the request and respond within 30 working days. Significant changes will require a new application process as per section 4.

heading: Review of Decisions
text: Any decision made by the Nordvale Communications Authority related to a telecommunications tower permit may be subject to internal review upon written request from an affected party. A request for review must be submitted within 20 days of the decision and should clearly state the grounds for review. The Authority will endeavor to complete the internal review within 45 days. This internal review process is distinct from the formal appeals process outlined in section 14.

heading: Emergency Powers of Authority
text: In situations posing an immediate and severe threat to public safety or property due to a telecommunications tower, the Nordvale Communications Authority may exercise emergency powers. These powers include, but are not limited to, ordering the immediate cessation of operations, temporary closure of the tower, or mandatory emergency repairs. The Authority will provide written justification for such actions within 48 hours. Non-compliance with emergency orders may result in a fine of 50,000 crowns per day.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined specific requirements for lightning protection systems for all towers over 40 meters, including detailed specifications for grounding and surge protection. It mandated that such systems be inspected annually by a certified electrician and reports submitted to the Authority within 14 days of inspection. Failure to comply resulted in a 5,000 crowns fine. It also specified the use of materials conforming to national electrical safety standards.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Monthly travel for highland residents
text:
(1) A passenger whose residence is in a highland settlement pays 20 crowns less than the ordinary price of a monthly pass on the national buses and trains.
(2) The reduction is given for one monthly pass per month.
(3) Where another reduction of the pass price also applies, this reduction is deducted after it.

heading: Monthly travel for highland residents
text:
(1) A passenger whose residence is in a highland settlement pays 30 crowns less than the ordinary price of a monthly pass on the national buses and trains.
(2) The reduction is given for one monthly pass per month.
(3) Where another reduction of the pass price also applies, this reduction is deducted after it.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for wildlife management permits within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure sustainable wildlife populations, protect biodiversity, and manage interactions between humans and wildlife responsibly. The Act applies to all activities involving the capture, relocation, culling, or any other direct intervention with wild animals across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This includes permits for research, conservation, and nuisance wildlife control. All permits issued under this Act are subject to review and potential revocation if conditions are not met.

heading: Permit Requirement for Wildlife Intervention
text: No person may engage in any activity that involves the capture, relocation, culling, or significant disturbance of wild animals without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources. This requirement applies to both individual citizens and organized groups or agencies. Certain minor, non-lethal deterrent actions, as specified in section 8, are exempt from this permit requirement. Failure to secure a necessary permit before conducting such activities may result in fines of up to 1,500 crowns per incident.

heading: Application for General Wildlife Permit
text: An application for a general wildlife permit must be submitted to the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 300 crowns. The application must include: (a) the full name and address of the applicant; (b) a detailed description of the proposed activities; (c) the specific species targeted; (d) the intended location(s) of the activities; and (e) the estimated duration, not exceeding 12 months. All information provided must be accurate to the best of the applicant's knowledge, with false statements potentially leading to application rejection or permit revocation.

heading: Application for General Wildlife Permit (Revised)
text: An application for a general wildlife permit must be submitted to the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 450 crowns. The application must include: (a) the full name and address of the applicant; (b) a detailed description of the proposed activities, including methodology; (c) the specific species targeted and an estimate of the number of individuals; (d) the intended location(s) of the activities with precise geographical coordinates; and (e) the estimated duration, not exceeding 9 months. Additionally, applicants must provide proof of relevant experience or certification.

heading: Application for General Wildlife Permit (Further Revised)
text: An application for a general wildlife permit must be submitted to the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources via the digital portal, accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 500 crowns. The application must include: (a) the full name and Nordvale identification number of the applicant; (b) a detailed description of the proposed activities, including methodology and justifications; (c) the specific species targeted, an estimate of the number of individuals, and their age class if relevant; (d) the intended location(s) of the activities with precise geographical coordinates and a 500-meter buffer zone; and (e) the estimated duration, not exceeding 6 months. Additionally, applicants must provide proof of relevant experience or certification, dated within the last 3 years.

heading: Permit Review Period
text: The Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources shall review all permit applications within 45 days of receipt. During this review period, the Ministry may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. Failure to provide requested information within 15 days of the request may result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant. The review period will restart upon receipt of all requested supplementary materials. Complex applications involving endangered species or large-scale interventions may require an extended review period of up to 60 days.

heading: Permit Review Period (Revised)
text: The Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources shall review all permit applications within 30 days of receipt. During this review period, the Ministry may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. Failure to provide requested information within 10 days of the request may result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant. The review period will restart upon receipt of all requested supplementary materials. Complex applications, such as those targeting species listed under conservation priority 1 or involving activities covering an area larger than 50 hectares, may require an extended review period of up to 50 days.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A general wildlife permit, once issued, is valid for a period not exceeding 12 months from the date of issuance. The exact validity period will be specified on the permit itself. Permittees must ensure that all approved activities are completed within this timeframe. Any activities extending beyond the specified validity period require a new permit application. Permits are non-transferable and may only be used by the individual or organization to whom they were originally issued. Misuse of a permit will result in immediate revocation and potential penalties.

heading: Permit Validity Period (Revised)
text: A general wildlife permit, once issued, is valid for a period not exceeding 9 months from the date of issuance. The exact validity period will be clearly specified on the permit. Permittees must ensure that all approved activities are completed within this timeframe. Any activities extending beyond the specified validity period require a new permit application, which must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the expiration of the current permit. Permits are non-transferable and may only be used by the individual or organization to whom they were originally issued, with a maximum of 3 named operators.

heading: Exemptions for Minor Deterrent Actions
text: Certain minor, non-lethal deterrent actions intended to discourage wildlife from entering or damaging property are exempt from the permit requirement. These include: (a) the use of fences not exceeding 2 meters in height; (b) the installation of visual or auditory deterrents that do not cause physical harm to animals; and (c) the removal of food attractants. Any deterrent action that involves direct contact with an animal, or has the potential to cause injury, stress, or displacement of animals beyond 100 meters, requires a permit. Property owners must still adhere to general animal welfare guidelines.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Permitted Activities
text: All holders of a wildlife management permit must submit a detailed report of their activities to the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources within 30 days of the permit's expiration. The report must include: (a) the dates and locations of all interventions; (b) the number and species of animals affected; (c) the methods used; and (d) the outcomes of the activities, including any mortalities or injuries. Failure to submit a timely and complete report may result in a fine of 750 crowns and may affect future permit applications. Electronic submission through the Ministry’s portal is preferred.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Permitted Activities (Revised)
text: All holders of a wildlife management permit must submit a detailed report of their activities to the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources within 15 days of the permit's expiration. The report must include: (a) the precise dates, times, and GPS coordinates of all interventions; (b) the exact number and species of animals affected, categorized by age and sex where possible; (c) the specific methods used and their efficacy; and (d) the outcomes of the activities, including any mortalities, injuries, or relocations. Photographic or video evidence may be requested. Failure to submit a timely and complete report will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns and a 12-month ban on future permit applications.

heading: Permit for Wildlife Relocation
text: A specific permit is required for the relocation of any wild animal. This permit mandates a comprehensive plan detailing: (a) the capture method, ensuring minimal stress to the animal; (b) a veterinary health assessment for the animal; (c) the proposed release site, which must be at least 20 kilometers from the capture site and possess suitable habitat; and (d) a post-release monitoring plan for a minimum of 30 days. The fee for a wildlife relocation permit is 600 crowns. Release sites must not exceed a population density of 1 animal per 10 hectares for the target species.

heading: Permit for Wildlife Relocation (Revised)
text: A specific permit is required for the relocation of any wild animal. This permit mandates a comprehensive plan detailing: (a) the capture method, ensuring minimal stress to the animal and approved by a certified wildlife veterinarian; (b) a full veterinary health assessment and disease screening for the animal; (c) the proposed release site, which must be at least 50 kilometers from the capture site, possess suitable habitat, and have no existing overpopulation of the target species; and (d) a post-release monitoring plan for a minimum of 60 days using tracking devices. The fee for a wildlife relocation permit is 900 crowns, plus an additional 200 crowns per animal for veterinary checks.

heading: Permit for Wildlife Culling
text: A specific permit for wildlife culling may be issued only when deemed absolutely necessary for population control, disease management, or to mitigate severe agricultural damage. The application must demonstrate that all non-lethal alternatives have been attempted and failed. The permit will specify: (a) the exact species and maximum number of animals to be culled; (b) the permissible methods of culling, which must be humane; (c) the specific dates and locations of the culling; and (d) requirements for disposal of carcasses. The fee for a culling permit is 800 crowns, and a 10% success rate on non-lethal methods is required for consideration.

heading: Permit for Wildlife Culling (Revised)
text: A specific permit for wildlife culling may be issued only when deemed absolutely necessary for population control, disease management, or to mitigate severe agricultural damage, confirmed by an independent assessment. The application must demonstrate that all non-lethal alternatives have been attempted and failed for a minimum of 6 months. The permit will specify: (a) the exact species, age class, and maximum number of animals to be culled, not exceeding 15% of the local population; (b) the permissible methods of culling, which must be humane and approved by a Nordvale-certified wildlife expert; (c) the specific dates and locations of the culling, limited to areas within 500 meters of documented damage; and (d) strict requirements for disposal of carcasses, including post-mortem examination where relevant. The fee for a culling permit is 1,200 crowns, and a 20% success rate on non-lethal methods is required for consideration.

heading: Permit for Scientific Research on Wildlife
text: Researchers conducting studies that involve direct interaction with wildlife, such as capture, tagging, or sampling, must obtain a scientific research permit. The application must include: (a) a detailed research proposal outlining objectives, methodology, and ethical considerations; (b) proof of institutional review board approval; (c) qualifications of all personnel involved; and (d) a plan for data dissemination. The fee for this permit is 200 crowns. Permits are valid for up to 24 months and are subject to annual progress reports. Any research involving invasive procedures requires additional Ministry approval.

heading: Permit for Scientific Research on Wildlife (Revised)
text: Researchers conducting studies that involve direct interaction with wildlife, such as capture, tagging, sampling, or tracking, must obtain a scientific research permit. The application must include: (a) a detailed research proposal outlining objectives, methodology, statistical power, and ethical considerations for each species; (b) proof of institutional review board approval from a recognized academic institution; (c) comprehensive qualifications and experience of all personnel involved, including a lead researcher with at least 5 years of relevant experience; and (d) a plan for data dissemination, including a commitment to publish findings within 36 months. The fee for this permit is 350 crowns. Permits are valid for up to 36 months and are subject to semi-annual progress reports. Any research involving invasive procedures or requiring anesthesia requires a separate veterinary protocol approval and a 500 crown surcharge.

heading: Permit Conditions
text: All permits issued under this Act are subject to specific conditions designed to ensure animal welfare and ecological sustainability. These conditions may include: (a) limitations on the number of animals; (b) specific methodologies to be employed; (c) seasonal or temporal restrictions; (d) requirements for qualified personnel; and (e) mandates for data collection and reporting. Violation of any permit condition may lead to immediate revocation of the permit and imposition of penalties, including fines of up to 2,000 crowns per violation. Permittees must carry their physical permit at all times during activities.

heading: Compliance Monitoring
text: The Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections of any site where permitted wildlife activities are taking place. Authorized Ministry agents may enter such sites, observe activities, and request to review records pertinent to the permit. Permittees must cooperate fully with these inspections. Obstruction of a Ministry agent during an inspection is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of up to 3,000 crowns and immediate permit revocation. At least 10% of all active permits will be subject to random inspection annually.

heading: Permit Revocation
text: A permit may be revoked by the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources if the permittee: (a) fails to comply with any condition of the permit; (b) provides false or misleading information in their application or reports; (c) is found to be causing undue harm or stress to wildlife; or (d) violates any provision of this Act or other relevant wildlife protection statutes. Before revocation, the Ministry will issue a written notice of intent to revoke, providing the permittee 14 days to respond with a written explanation. Emergency revocations may occur without prior notice if there is an immediate threat to wildlife or public safety.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any applicant whose permit application has been denied, or any permittee whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Wildlife Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the Ministry's decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal, and accompanied by a fee of 500 crowns. The Appeals Board will review the case and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final, except in cases where new evidence, previously unavailable, emerges within 90 days.

heading: Penalties for Unpermitted Activities
text: Any person found engaging in wildlife intervention activities without a valid permit is subject to severe penalties. For a first offense, a fine of up to 2,500 crowns may be imposed. Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 5,000 crowns and a prohibition from applying for any wildlife permit for a period of 2 years. In cases involving endangered or protected species, the fine for a first offense rises to 7,500 crowns, in addition to potential confiscation of equipment used in the unpermitted activity. Each individual animal illegally impacted may constitute a separate offense.

heading: Penalties for Unpermitted Activities (Revised)
text: Any person found engaging in wildlife intervention activities without a valid permit is subject to severe penalties. For a first offense, a fine of up to 4,000 crowns may be imposed. Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 8,000 crowns and a prohibition from applying for any wildlife permit for a period of 5 years. In cases involving endangered or protected species, the fine for a first offense rises to 15,000 crowns, in addition to mandatory confiscation of all equipment used in the unpermitted activity. Each individual animal illegally impacted will constitute a separate offense, with a minimum fine of 1,000 crowns per animal.

heading: Permit for Trapping Nuisance Wildlife
text: A specific permit is required for trapping nuisance wildlife on private property. This permit allows for the live-trapping and relocation of specific species identified as causing damage. The application must specify the species, type of trap, and proposed relocation site, which must be within 10 kilometers of the capture site. Traps must be checked every 24 hours. The fee for this permit is 150 crowns and is valid for 30 days. Relocation must be to areas where the species is naturally found and not overpopulated.

heading: Permit for Trapping Nuisance Wildlife (Revised)
text: A specific permit is required for trapping nuisance wildlife on private property. This permit allows for the live-trapping and relocation of specific species identified as causing damage to property or posing a health risk. The application must specify the species, type of trap (approved by the Ministry), and proposed relocation site, which must be at least 15 kilometers but no more than 30 kilometers from the capture site. Traps must be checked every 12 hours. The fee for this permit is 250 crowns and is valid for 21 days. Relocation must be to designated wilderness areas, and the animal must be released within 4 hours of capture.

heading: Permit for Trapping Nuisance Wildlife (Further Revised)
text: A specific permit is required for trapping nuisance wildlife on private property. This permit allows for the live-trapping and relocation of specific species identified as causing documented damage to property or posing a verified health risk. The application must specify the species, type of trap (approved by the Ministry from a list of humane options), and proposed relocation site, which must be at least 25 kilometers but no more than 50 kilometers from the capture site, and must be designated as a suitable habitat with no existing overpopulation. Traps must be checked every 8 hours. The fee for this permit is 350 crowns and is valid for 14 days. Relocation must be to designated wilderness areas, and the animal must be released within 2 hours of capture, after a brief health check by the permittee.

heading: Emergency Permits
text: In urgent situations where immediate action is required to protect public safety or prevent significant property damage, the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources may issue an emergency permit. Applications for emergency permits can be made verbally or electronically and will be reviewed within 24 hours. Such permits are typically valid for a maximum of 72 hours and are subject to stringent reporting requirements immediately following the emergency intervention. The fee for an emergency permit is 100 crowns. Documentation proving the emergency situation must be provided within 5 days of application.

heading: Emergency Permits (Revised)
text: In urgent situations where immediate action is required to protect public safety, verified by local authorities, or prevent significant property damage, confirmed by an independent assessor, the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources may issue an emergency permit. Applications for emergency permits can be made verbally or electronically and will be reviewed within 12 hours. Such permits are typically valid for a maximum of 48 hours and are subject to stringent reporting requirements, including photographic evidence, immediately following the emergency intervention. The fee for an emergency permit is 200 crowns. Comprehensive documentation proving the emergency situation must be provided within 3 days of application.

heading: Record Keeping by Permittees
text: All permittees must maintain accurate and detailed records of all activities conducted under their permit. These records must include: (a) dates and times of activities; (b) specific locations (GPS coordinates); (c) species and number of animals involved; (d) methods used; (e) outcomes (e.g., released, culled, injured); and (f) any unusual observations. These records must be kept for a minimum of 3 years following the expiration of the permit and made available to the Ministry upon request. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of 500 crowns per instance and affect future permit applications.

heading: Public Access to Permit Information
text: Information regarding issued wildlife management permits, including the permittee's name, general activity description, species involved, and location (municipality level), shall be made publicly available on the Ministry's official website. This information will be updated quarterly. Specific details deemed sensitive for reasons of animal welfare or security, such as precise capture locations for highly endangered species, may be withheld at the discretion of the Ministry. Personal contact information of individual permittees will not be disclosed, ensuring privacy while maintaining transparency.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text: Permittees are required to cooperate with local authorities, including municipal councils in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, when conducting activities that may impact local residents or infrastructure. This includes providing reasonable notice of planned activities to relevant local officials, especially for operations involving significant noise or public presence. Local authorities may impose additional, non-conflicting conditions on activities within their jurisdiction, provided such conditions do not contradict the terms of the Ministry-issued permit. Failure to cooperate may lead to temporary suspension of activities.

heading: Amendments to Permits
text: A permittee may apply to the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources for an amendment to an existing permit if unforeseen circumstances require a change in activity, species, or location. The application for amendment must be submitted in writing, detailing the proposed changes and the reasons for them, and accompanied by a fee of 100 crowns. Minor amendments may be approved within 10 days, while significant changes may require a full review process, similar to a new application. Activities outside the scope of the original permit or approved amendment are strictly prohibited.

heading: Amendments to Permits (Revised)
text: A permittee may apply to the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources for an amendment to an existing permit if unforeseen circumstances require a change in activity, species, or location, provided the changes do not fundamentally alter the permit's original intent. The application for amendment must be submitted in writing, detailing the proposed changes, the justifications, and any new risk assessments, and accompanied by a fee of 180 crowns. Minor amendments, such as a 10% change in location, may be approved within 7 days. Significant changes, including adding a new species or increasing animal numbers by more than 25%, will require a full review process, similar to a new application. Activities outside the scope of the original permit or approved amendment are strictly prohibited and will be treated as unpermitted activities.

heading: Permit for Animal Rehabilitation
text: Individuals or organizations wishing to operate a wildlife rehabilitation facility or provide care for injured or orphaned wild animals must obtain a specialized rehabilitation permit. This permit requires: (a) proof of suitable facilities meeting minimum size and hygiene standards; (b) qualifications of staff, including veterinary oversight; (c) a plan for eventual release of rehabilitated animals into appropriate natural habitats; and (d) detailed record-keeping protocols. The fee for this permit is 300 crowns and it is valid for 3 years, subject to annual inspections. Rehabilitated animals must be released within 10 kilometers of their capture site unless otherwise approved.

heading: Permit for Animal Rehabilitation (Revised)
text: Individuals or organizations wishing to operate a wildlife rehabilitation facility or provide care for injured or orphaned wild animals must obtain a specialized rehabilitation permit. This permit requires: (a) proof of suitable facilities meeting stringent minimum size, hygiene, and species-specific enclosure standards; (b) qualifications of all staff, including a Nordvale-certified wildlife veterinarian providing direct oversight; (c) a comprehensive plan for eventual release of rehabilitated animals into appropriate natural habitats, supported by pre-release health assessments; and (d) detailed record-keeping protocols, including individual animal logs. The fee for this permit is 450 crowns and it is valid for 5 years, subject to bi-annual inspections. Rehabilitated animals must be released within 5 kilometers of their capture site or a designated alternative site approved by the Ministry.

heading: Definition of 'Wild Animal'
text: For the purpose of this Act, a 'wild animal' is defined as any animal species that is not domesticated and lives independently of human control. This includes all native Nordvale species, as well as non-native species that have established self-sustaining populations in the wild. Animals held in captivity, such as those in zoos or private collections, are not considered 'wild animals' under this Act unless they escape and establish themselves in the natural environment for a period exceeding 48 hours. The Ministry maintains an official list of species covered by this definition, updated annually.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text: For certain large-scale or high-risk wildlife management projects, the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources may require the permittee to provide a financial guarantee, such as a bond or an escrow account. This guarantee, which can range from 5,000 to 25,000 crowns depending on project scope and potential impact, ensures that funds are available for any necessary remedial actions, environmental restoration, or unforeseen costs related to the permitted activities. The specific amount and terms of the guarantee will be determined on a case-by-case basis and outlined in the permit conditions. The guarantee will be released within 90 days of successful completion and reporting.

heading: Financial Guarantees (Revised)
text: For certain large-scale or high-risk wildlife management projects, or those involving more than 50 animals, the Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources shall require the permittee to provide a financial guarantee, such as a bond or an escrow account. This guarantee, which can range from 10,000 to 50,000 crowns depending on project scope, species criticality, and potential environmental impact, ensures that funds are available for any necessary remedial actions, habitat restoration, or unforeseen costs related to the permitted activities. The specific amount and terms of the guarantee will be determined on a case-by-case basis by the Ministry's financial review committee and outlined in the permit conditions. The guarantee will be released within 120 days of successful completion, reporting, and a final site inspection.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any person or organization engaged in activities requiring a permit under this Act prior to its effective date must apply for the appropriate permit within 90 days of the effective date. During this 90-day transitional period, existing activities may continue, provided they are conducted in a humane and environmentally responsible manner. Failure to submit an application within this period will result in the immediate cessation of activities and potential penalties as outlined in section 23. The Ministry will prioritize the review of applications from existing operations.

heading: Annual Review of Fees
text: The Ministry of Wildlife and Natural Resources shall review all fees specified in this Act annually, on or before January 31st. The purpose of this review is to ensure that fees remain commensurate with the administrative costs of processing applications, conducting inspections, and managing the permit system. Any proposed changes to the fee schedule will be published for public consultation for a period of 30 days before being finalized and implemented. Changes to fees will not apply to applications already submitted prior to their implementation date.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined specific guidelines for the use of non-lethal acoustic deterrents within 100 meters of residential areas. It mandated a maximum sound level of 60 decibels and required prior written consent from property owners within a 50-meter radius. The Ministry found that these guidelines were impractical to enforce due to variable environmental factors and frequent complaints regarding effectiveness. The permit system will now address acoustic deterrents on a case-by-case basis through general permit conditions under section 19, allowing for more flexible and site-specific regulations. This change aims to streamline the permitting process for such tools.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: (1) If a person is a registered falconer, they shall pay a fixed fee of 5 crowns. (2) This fixed fee replaces any fee or allowance specified in SSA §9.

heading: Concessions
text: The short-term rental duty is reduced by 25 percent of the fee or allowance in SBA §8 for any person who is a registered dry-stone waller.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for providing financial assistance, referred to as Legal Aid Grants, to individuals who are unable to afford legal representation for certain legal matters. The primary purpose is to ensure access to justice for eligible residents of Nordvale. This scope includes both civil and criminal proceedings as defined in subsequent sections, subject to specific financial and case merit criteria. The administration of these grants is overseen by the Nordvale Ministry of Justice, in conjunction with designated legal aid committees across the country's municipalities.

heading: Eligibility for individuals
text: An individual may be eligible for a Legal Aid Grant if they are a resident of Nordvale for at least 12 months immediately preceding the application date. Additionally, their annual household income must not exceed 250,000 crowns, and their total liquid assets, excluding their primary residence, must not exceed 75,000 crowns. Applicants must also demonstrate that they have a reasonable chance of success in their legal matter, or that their case involves a fundamental right or severe hardship, as assessed by the Legal Aid Committee. Minors aged 16 or 17 may apply with parental consent, or independently if legally emancipated.

heading: Income threshold for eligibility
text: To qualify for a Legal Aid Grant, an applicant's gross annual household income must not exceed a specific threshold. For a single individual, this threshold is set at 250,000 crowns. For a household with two adults, the combined gross annual income must not exceed 350,000 crowns. An additional allowance of 50,000 crowns is granted for each dependent child in the household, up to a maximum of three children. Income from all sources, including employment, investments, and social benefits, is considered in this calculation.

heading: Income threshold for eligibility
text: To qualify for a Legal Aid Grant, an applicant's gross annual household income must not exceed a specific threshold. For a single individual, this threshold is set at 275,000 crowns. For a household with two adults, the combined gross annual income must not exceed 380,000 crowns. An additional allowance of 55,000 crowns is granted for each dependent child in the household, up to a maximum of three children. Income from all sources, including employment, investments, and social benefits, is considered in this calculation.

heading: Asset threshold for eligibility
text: The total liquid assets of an applicant's household, excluding their primary residence and up to one vehicle used for essential transportation, must not exceed 75,000 crowns. Liquid assets include savings accounts, checking accounts, stocks, bonds, and other easily convertible financial instruments. The value of any secondary properties or luxury items with a value exceeding 15,000 crowns will also be factored into this asset assessment. The Legal Aid Committee may make exceptions in cases of extraordinary hardship or if the assets are inaccessible for a period exceeding 24 months.

heading: Application process
text: An application for a Legal Aid Grant must be submitted to the Legal Aid Committee in the applicant's municipality of residence. The application form requires detailed financial information, a summary of the legal matter, and supporting documentation. Applicants must provide proof of identity, residency, and income for the preceding 12 months. All applications must be signed and dated by the applicant, and in some cases, an interview with a committee member may be required to clarify details. Incomplete applications will be returned for additional information within 14 days.

heading: Application review period
text: The Legal Aid Committee shall review all complete applications within 30 business days of receipt. During this period, the committee may request additional information or documentation from the applicant. If no further information is requested, a decision will be issued within the 30-day timeframe. If additional information is required, the review period will be extended by an additional 15 business days from the date the requested information is received. Urgent cases, such as those involving immediate threats to safety or freedom, will be prioritized and reviewed within 7 business days.

heading: Grant amount for civil cases
text: For approved civil cases, the Legal Aid Grant will cover up to 80% of the reasonable legal fees and disbursements, with a maximum grant amount of 150,000 crowns. The specific percentage and maximum will be determined by the Legal Aid Committee based on the complexity of the case and the applicant's financial circumstances. The grant does not cover fees for appeals unless specifically approved by the committee due to exceptional circumstances, such as a significant error in the initial judgment. Applicants are responsible for the remaining 20% of costs or any amount exceeding the grant limit.

heading: Grant amount for civil cases
text: For approved civil cases, the Legal Aid Grant will cover up to 85% of the reasonable legal fees and disbursements, with a maximum grant amount of 175,000 crowns. The specific percentage and maximum will be determined by the Legal Aid Committee based on the complexity of the case and the applicant's financial circumstances. The grant does not cover fees for appeals unless specifically approved by the committee due to exceptional circumstances, such as a significant error in the initial judgment. Applicants are responsible for the remaining 15% of costs or any amount exceeding the grant limit.

heading: Grant amount for criminal cases
text: For approved criminal cases, the Legal Aid Grant will cover up to 90% of the reasonable legal fees and disbursements, with a maximum grant amount of 200,000 crowns. This higher percentage reflects the fundamental right to legal representation in criminal proceedings. The grant may cover legal representation for serious indictable offenses, but typically not for minor infractions carrying only a fine. The Legal Aid Committee will assess the gravity of the charges and the potential penalties when determining the grant amount. Appeals in criminal cases are generally covered if there are strong grounds for appeal.

heading: Grant amount for criminal cases
text: For approved criminal cases, the Legal Aid Grant will cover up to 95% of the reasonable legal fees and disbursements, with a maximum grant amount of 225,000 crowns. This higher percentage reflects the fundamental right to legal representation in criminal proceedings. The grant may cover legal representation for serious indictable offenses, but typically not for minor infractions carrying only a fine. The Legal Aid Committee will assess the gravity of the charges and the potential penalties when determining the grant amount. Appeals in criminal cases are generally covered if there are strong grounds for appeal.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text: Grant funds are disbursed directly to the legal practitioner representing the applicant, not to the applicant themselves. Payments will be made in installments, typically 50% upon commencement of the case, 30% at a significant milestone (e.g., discovery completion), and the remaining 20% upon resolution of the case. All disbursements must be itemized and approved by the Legal Aid Committee. Legal practitioners must submit detailed invoices for all work performed and expenses incurred to receive payment. Any unspent funds will be returned to the Ministry of Justice within 30 days of case conclusion.

heading: Selection of legal representation
text: Applicants may select any legal practitioner licensed to practice law in Nordvale. However, the chosen legal practitioner must agree to accept the fee schedule established by the Legal Aid Committee. If the chosen legal practitioner's standard fees exceed the committee's schedule, the applicant is responsible for the difference, in addition to their co-payment. The Legal Aid Committee maintains a list of legal practitioners who regularly accept Legal Aid Grants and their associated fee structures to assist applicants in their selection. Legal practitioners must be in good standing with the Nordvale Bar Association.

heading: Legal Aid Committee establishment
text: A Legal Aid Committee shall be established in each of the following municipalities: Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Each committee shall consist of five members: two legal practitioners with at least 10 years of experience, two community representatives appointed by the municipal council, and one representative from the Ministry of Justice. Committee members serve a term of three years and may be reappointed for a maximum of two consecutive terms. Meetings must occur at least once every month, with a quorum of three members required for any decision.

heading: Responsibilities of the Committee
text:
(1) The Legal Aid Committee is responsible for assessing applications for Legal Aid Grants, determining eligibility, and approving appropriate grant amounts.
(2) The committee also monitors the progress of cases supported by grants and ensures that legal practitioners adhere to the established fee schedules and reporting requirements. 
(3) Furthermore, the committee provides guidance to applicants regarding the application process and the selection of legal representation. 
(4) Each committee must submit a quarterly report to the Ministry of Justice detailing the number of applications received, approved, and rejected, along with the total amount of grants disbursed.

heading: Appeals against Committee decisions
text: An applicant may appeal a decision by the Legal Aid Committee within 21 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Ministry of Justice, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any new supporting information. A specialized appeals panel within the Ministry will review the appeal within 45 days. The panel's decision is final and binding. The appeals panel consists of three senior legal experts, none of whom serve on any municipal Legal Aid Committee. There is no fee for filing an appeal.

heading: Fraudulent applications
text: Any individual who knowingly provides false or misleading information in their application for a Legal Aid Grant shall be required to repay the full amount of any grant received, plus an administrative penalty of 10% of the grant amount. Furthermore, such individuals may be subject to prosecution for fraud, carrying a potential fine of up to 100,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 2 years. The Legal Aid Committee has the authority to initiate investigations into suspicious applications or reports of fraud received from the public. Legal practitioners who knowingly participate in fraudulent activity will be reported to the Nordvale Bar Association.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information provided by applicants and related to their legal matters is strictly confidential. Members of the Legal Aid Committee and Ministry of Justice staff involved in the administration of this Act are bound by strict confidentiality agreements. Disclosure of confidential information to unauthorized third parties is prohibited and may result in disciplinary action or legal penalties. Statistical data may be collected and reported, but it must be fully anonymized to prevent the identification of any individual applicant. This confidentiality extends beyond the conclusion of the legal matter.

heading: Review of grant terms
text: The Ministry of Justice shall review the terms and conditions of Legal Aid Grants, including income and asset thresholds, grant amounts, and eligible case types, at least once every three years.
