(1) If land is cleared without a permit or in violation of a permit, the Director may issue a restoration order.
(2) A restoration order requires the responsible party to restore the land to its original or a suitable alternative ecological state within a specified timeframe, typically 90 days. This may include replanting native vegetation and implementing erosion control measures. Failure to comply with a restoration order may result in the Department undertaking the restoration work and recovering costs from the responsible party, plus a 20% administrative fee.

heading: Protected natural areas
text:
(1) The Director may designate specific areas as protected natural areas where land clearing is strictly prohibited or severely restricted.
(2) These designations are based on ecological significance, presence of endangered species, or historical importance. Any clearing activity within a protected natural area, even below the normal permit threshold, requires special approval and will only be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as for critical research or public safety, and is subject to rigorous environmental assessment. A comprehensive list of protected areas is maintained by the Department.

heading: Consultation with local authorities
text: Before issuing a permit, the Department of Environmental Protection must consult with the relevant municipality (Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, Lund Vale) where the land clearing is proposed. This consultation period should not exceed 15 working days. The municipality may provide recommendations or raise concerns regarding the proposed clearing, which the Director must consider during the decision-making process. However, the final decision rests with the Director, balancing local input with national environmental objectives.

heading: Public notice of applications
text:
(1) For land clearing projects exceeding 500 square meters, the Department of Environmental Protection must publish a public notice of the permit application.
(2) The notice must be published in a widely circulated newspaper in Nordvale and on the Department's official website for a period of at least 14 days. It must include details of the proposed clearing and provide an opportunity for public comment within 21 days. All public comments received will be considered by the Director before making a decision on the permit.

heading: Public hearings for large projects
text:
(1) For land clearing projects exceeding 2,000 square meters, the Director must hold a public hearing in the relevant municipality.
(2) The public hearing provides an additional opportunity for citizens to express their views and concerns regarding the proposed clearing. Notice of the public hearing must be given at least 30 days in advance. The Director or a designated representative will chair the hearing, and a summary of the proceedings will be made publicly available as part of the permit decision record.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text:
(1) A comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) is required for any land clearing project exceeding 1,000 square meters.
(2) The EIA must be conducted by an independent qualified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application. The EIA should identify potential environmental risks, propose mitigation measures, and assess cumulative impacts. The cost of the EIA is borne by the applicant, and the report must adhere to guidelines published by the Department of Environmental Protection.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text:
(1) A comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) is required for any land clearing project exceeding 750 square meters.
(2) The EIA must be conducted by an independent qualified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application. The EIA should identify potential environmental risks, propose mitigation measures, and assess cumulative impacts. The cost of the EIA is borne by the applicant, and the report must adhere to guidelines published by the Department of Environmental Protection. The Department will provide a list of approved consultants.

heading: Mitigation measures
text: Applicants must propose detailed mitigation measures to offset any adverse environmental impacts identified in the environmental impact assessment or during the application review process. These measures may include habitat restoration, creation of wildlife corridors, or financial contributions to a local environmental fund. The effectiveness of proposed mitigation measures will be a significant factor in the Director's decision to grant a permit. The Department may also impose additional mitigation requirements as conditions of the permit.

heading: Replanting requirements
text:
(1) If a permit is granted for clearing land containing significant tree cover, a condition for replanting may be imposed.
(2) The replanting requirement typically mandates the planting of native species at a ratio of 2 new trees for every 1 tree removed, for areas exceeding 250 square meters. The replanted area must be maintained for a minimum of 3 years. A bond of 500 crowns per cleared hectare, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns, may be required to ensure compliance with replanting obligations.

heading: Soil erosion control
text: All land clearing activities must incorporate appropriate soil erosion control measures to prevent sediment runoff into waterways and protect soil stability. This includes, but is not limited to, the installation of silt fences, sediment basins, and the use of temporary ground cover. Plans for erosion control must be submitted with the permit application and approved by the Department. Failure to implement effective erosion control measures will result in immediate enforcement action and potential fines of up to 2,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Protection of watercourses
text:
(1) No land clearing activities are permitted within 20 meters of any natural watercourse, including rivers, streams, and lakes.
(2) This buffer zone is established to protect water quality, aquatic ecosystems, and riparian habitats. Any proposed activity within this buffer zone requires a separate special permit and rigorous justification, demonstrating no adverse impact on the watercourse. This special permit application will incur an additional fee of 400 crowns.

heading: Protection of watercourses
text:
(1) No land clearing activities are permitted within 25 meters of any natural watercourse, including rivers, streams, and lakes.
(2) This buffer zone is established to protect water quality, aquatic ecosystems, and riparian habitats. Any proposed activity within this buffer zone requires a separate special permit and rigorous justification, demonstrating no adverse impact on the watercourse. This special permit application will incur an additional fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Waste disposal
text: All vegetation and debris generated from land clearing activities must be disposed of in an environmentally sound manner. Burning of cleared vegetation is generally prohibited, unless a specific fire permit has been obtained from the local fire authority and approved by the Department of Environmental Protection. Otherwise, debris must be chipped, mulched, or transported to an approved waste disposal facility. Illegal dumping of clearing waste will result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 5,000 crowns and cleanup costs.

heading: Cultural heritage protection
text:
(1) If archaeological or cultural heritage sites are discovered during land clearing, all work must cease immediately.
(2) The permit holder must notify the Department of Cultural Heritage within 24 hours of the discovery. Work can only resume with the express written permission of the Department of Cultural Heritage, which may impose additional conditions or require further investigations. Failure to report such discoveries may result in prosecution and fines up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Monitoring and inspection
text:
(1) The Department of Environmental Protection has the right to conduct unannounced inspections of any land clearing site, whether or not a permit has been issued.
(2) Inspectors may enter the premises, examine records, take samples, and request information relevant to compliance with this Act. Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offense, punishable by a fine of up to 3,000 crowns. Regular monitoring ensures adherence to permit conditions and environmental standards throughout the clearing process.

heading: Record keeping
text: Permit holders must maintain accurate records of all land clearing activities, including dates of work, quantities of material removed, and details of waste disposal. These records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years after the completion of the clearing and made available to the Department of Environmental Protection upon request. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of 750 crowns and may hinder future permit applications.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text: Information provided in permit applications will be treated with appropriate confidentiality, especially commercially sensitive data, subject to the provisions of public information access laws. However, general details of approved permits, including location and scope of work, will be made publicly available to ensure transparency. Applicants may request specific information to be withheld from public disclosure if it meets criteria for trade secrets or personal privacy, which will be assessed on a case-by-case basis by the Department.

heading: False information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in a permit application or during an investigation under this Act commits an offense. The penalty for such an offense is a fine of up to 15,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. This also extends to providing false information during public hearings or consultations, emphasizing the importance of honesty in all interactions with the Department. Such actions may also lead to the immediate revocation of any existing permits.

heading: Offenses
text:
A person commits an offense if they:
(a) Clear land without a permit when one is required.
(b) Clear land in violation of a permit condition.
(c) Fail to comply with a stop work order or restoration order.
(d) Obstruct an inspector in the performance of their duties.
(e) Provide false or misleading information.
(f) Dispose of clearing waste illegally. Each distinct breach constitutes a separate offense.

heading: Penalties for offenses
text:
(1) A person who commits an offense under section 37(a) or 37(c) is liable to a fine not exceeding 25,000 crowns for a first offense, and up to 50,000 crowns or 9 months imprisonment for subsequent offenses.
(2) For offenses under section 37(b), 37(d), 37(e), or 37(f), the penalty is a fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns for a first offense, and up to 20,000 crowns for subsequent offenses. Daily penalties may apply for continuing offenses.

heading: Penalties for offenses
text:
(1) A person who commits an offense under section 37(a) or 37(c) is liable to a fine not exceeding 35,000 crowns for a first offense, and up to 75,000 crowns or 12 months imprisonment for subsequent offenses.
(2) For offenses under section 37(b), 37(d), 37(e), or 37(f), the penalty is a fine not exceeding 15,000 crowns for a first offense, and up to 30,000 crowns for subsequent offenses. Daily penalties of 1,000 crowns may apply for continuing offenses.

heading: Recovery of costs
text: If the Department of Environmental Protection incurs costs in rectifying environmental damage caused by unauthorized clearing or non-compliance with a permit, these costs may be recovered from the responsible party. This includes the costs of investigations, cleanup, restoration, and administrative overhead. A 15% administrative charge will be added to all recovered costs. Legal action may be taken to recover these costs if the responsible party fails to pay within 60 days of receiving an invoice.

heading: Power to make regulations
text:
(1) The Director, with the approval of the Minister of Environment, may make regulations for the purpose of carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
(2) These regulations may prescribe forms, fees, technical standards, environmental guidelines, and procedures for specific types of clearing activities. Regulations will be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force, allowing for public review. These regulations are essential for the practical implementation of the Act.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: (1) Any land clearing activities that commenced before the effective date of this Act and are ongoing must apply for a permit within 90 days of this Act coming into force. During this 90-day period, such activities may continue, provided they do not cause immediate and severe environmental harm. Applications will be reviewed with consideration given to the stage of development already achieved. Failure to apply within the specified period will result in the activity being deemed unauthorized.

heading: Repeal and saving
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed fireworks technician, they shall have 30 additional days to pay any fee or allowance specified in FDA §14.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Where the person liable is a registered seed bank curator, the annual energy rebate of 350 crowns will be reduced by half. This reduced rebate is also paid in January.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for permitting the installation of public art pieces within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all permanent and temporary art installations intended for public display in areas accessible to the general public, regardless of the artwork's size, material, or duration. The primary goal is to ensure public safety, aesthetic coherence, and proper maintenance of public spaces. This Act outlines the application process, criteria for approval, and responsibilities of applicants and permit holders. It aims to provide clear guidelines for artists, organizations, and municipalities involved in public art projects across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Public art installation' means any artistic creation, whether permanent or temporary, intended for public display in an outdoor or publicly accessible indoor space.
(2) 'Permanent installation' refers to an artwork intended to remain in place for more than 365 consecutive days.
(3) 'Temporary installation' refers to an artwork intended to remain in place for 365 consecutive days or less.
(4) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity submitting a permit application for a public art installation.
(5) 'Municipality' refers to the local governing body of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.
(6) 'Permit' means the official authorization granted by a municipality for a public art installation.

heading: Permit requirement
text:
(1) A permit from the relevant municipality is required for all public art installations, whether permanent or temporary, before any work commences.
(2) Installations without a valid permit are subject to immediate removal by the municipality, and the responsible party may incur removal costs and penalties as specified in section 28.
(3) This requirement applies to all locations within the municipal boundaries, including public parks, plazas, and publicly owned buildings. Exemptions are detailed in section 4.
(4) Failure to obtain a permit may result in fines of up to 5,000 crowns for each day of non-compliance.

heading: Exemptions from permit requirement
text:
(1) The following public art installations are exempt from the permit requirement:
(a) Artworks displayed for less than 72 hours and not exceeding 2 meters in any dimension.
(b) Artworks displayed entirely within private property and not visible from any public right-of-way or public park.
(c) Artworks created for educational purposes within school grounds, provided they are removed within 30 days of completion.
(2) These exemptions do not absolve the responsible party from ensuring public safety or compliance with other municipal regulations. Any artwork exceeding these specifications requires a permit.

heading: Exemptions from permit requirement
text:
(1) The following public art installations are exempt from the permit requirement:
(a) Artworks displayed for less than 48 hours and not exceeding 1.5 meters in any dimension.
(b) Artworks displayed entirely within private property and not visible from any public right-of-way or public park.
(c) Artworks created for educational purposes within school grounds, provided they are removed within 20 days of completion.
(2) These exemptions do not absolve the responsible party from ensuring public safety or compliance with other municipal regulations. Any artwork exceeding these specifications requires a permit.

heading: Application submission
text:
(1) All permit applications must be submitted to the relevant municipal planning department.
(2) Applications must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the proposed installation date for temporary installations, and 120 days for permanent installations.
(3) The application must include all documents and fees specified in section 6 and section 7. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 14 days.
(4) Applications can be submitted electronically or in physical form at the municipal office during regular business hours.

heading: Required application documents for temporary installations
text:
(1) For temporary art installations, the application must include:
(a) A completed application form with contact details.
(b) A detailed project proposal, including artistic concept, dimensions (height, width, depth), materials, and proposed duration of display.
(c) A site plan indicating the exact location of the installation and its relationship to surrounding structures and public pathways.
(d) Proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 1,000,000 crowns.
(e) A safety plan outlining installation and removal procedures, including any potential hazards.
(f) Visual representations of the artwork, such as sketches, renderings, or photographs.

heading: Required application documents for permanent installations
text:
(1) For permanent art installations, the application must include:
(a) All documents required for temporary installations as per section 6.
(b) Detailed engineering plans and structural calculations, stamped by a licensed engineer, confirming the stability and safety of the installation for its intended lifespan.
(c) A maintenance plan outlining routine cleaning, inspection, and repair schedules for a minimum of 10 years.
(d) A detailed budget for the project, including installation, maintenance, and potential removal costs.
(e) An environmental impact assessment if the installation exceeds 5 meters in height or covers an area larger than 25 square meters.
(f) A community engagement plan, demonstrating how local residents have been consulted.

heading: Application fees for temporary installations
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required for all temporary art installations.
(2) For temporary installations proposed to be on display for more than 180 days, an additional fee of 250 crowns is applicable.
(3) These fees cover administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial site reviews. The fee must be paid at the time of application submission.
(4) Municipalities may offer a 50% discount on fees for non-profit organizations, provided they submit proof of their non-profit status with their application.

heading: Application fees for temporary installations
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is required for all temporary art installations.
(2) For temporary installations proposed to be on display for more than 120 days, an additional fee of 300 crowns is applicable.
(3) These fees cover administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial site reviews. The fee must be paid at the time of application submission.
(4) Municipalities may offer a 40% discount on fees for non-profit organizations, provided they submit proof of their non-profit status with their application.

heading: Application fees for permanent installations
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required for all permanent art installations.
(2) For permanent installations exceeding 5 meters in height or covering an area larger than 25 square meters, an additional fee of 1,000 crowns is applicable.
(3) These fees cover the extensive review process, including engineering and aesthetic assessments. The fee must be paid at the time of application submission.
(4) Municipalities may offer a 50% discount on fees for projects initiated directly by municipal cultural departments, provided proper documentation is submitted.

heading: Application fees for permanent installations
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns is required for all permanent art installations.
(2) For permanent installations exceeding 4 meters in height or covering an area larger than 20 square meters, an additional fee of 1,200 crowns is applicable.
(3) These fees cover the extensive review process, including engineering and aesthetic assessments. The fee must be paid at the time of application submission.
(4) Municipalities may offer a 40% discount on fees for projects initiated directly by municipal cultural departments, provided proper documentation is submitted.

heading: Review process for temporary installations
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application for a temporary installation, the municipality will conduct an initial review within 14 days.
(2) A public notice period of 21 days will commence, allowing residents to provide feedback on the proposed installation.
(3) The municipal planning department will assess the application based on public safety, aesthetic impact, and adherence to municipal guidelines.
(4) A decision to approve, conditionally approve, or reject the application will be issued within 45 days of the public notice period closing. A 75% approval rate from public feedback is generally required for straightforward acceptance.

heading: Review process for permanent installations
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application for a permanent installation, the municipality will conduct an initial review within 30 days.
(2) A public notice period of 45 days will commence, allowing residents and community groups to provide detailed feedback on the proposed installation.
(3) The municipal planning department, in consultation with relevant experts, will assess the application based on structural integrity, long-term aesthetic impact, maintenance feasibility, and community benefit.
(4) A decision to approve, conditionally approve, or reject the application will be issued within 90 days of the public notice period closing. A public hearing may be scheduled if more than 10 individuals formally object to the proposal.

heading: Criteria for approval
text:
(1) Permit applications will be evaluated based on the following criteria:
(a) Public safety: The installation must pose no risk to public health or safety during its entire lifecycle.
(b) Structural integrity: For permanent installations, the design must meet all engineering standards.
(c) Aesthetic compatibility: The artwork should generally complement the character of the surrounding area without causing undue visual disruption.
(d) Maintenance plan: A feasible plan for ongoing care and eventual removal must be presented.
(e) Public accessibility: The installation should not unduly obstruct public pathways or access to municipal services.
(f) Compliance with municipal regulations: The project must adhere to all applicable municipal bylaws and planning schemes.

heading: Conditions of permit
text:
(1) All permits are issued subject to specific conditions, which may include:
(a) A requirement for the applicant to maintain public liability insurance for the duration of the installation.
(b) Specific maintenance and inspection schedules for the artwork.
(c) Limitations on the duration of the installation for temporary pieces.
(d) Requirements for specific materials or construction techniques to ensure durability and safety.
(e) Provisions for the safe removal of the artwork at the end of its permitted duration.
(f) Requirements to provide a bond or security deposit as specified in section 14.

heading: Security deposit for temporary installations
text:
(1) For temporary installations, a security deposit of 2,000 crowns is required, refundable upon satisfactory removal of the artwork and restoration of the site.
(2) If the municipality incurs costs for site restoration or removal due to applicant's failure, these costs will be deducted from the security deposit.
(3) The deposit must be paid no later than 14 days before the scheduled installation date. Failure to pay may result in permit revocation.
(4) For temporary installations with an estimated value below 5,000 crowns, the security deposit may be reduced to 1,000 crowns upon request and municipal approval.

heading: Security deposit for temporary installations
text:
(1) For temporary installations, a security deposit of 3,000 crowns is required, refundable upon satisfactory removal of the artwork and restoration of the site.
(2) If the municipality incurs costs for site restoration or removal due to applicant's failure, these costs will be deducted from the security deposit.
(3) The deposit must be paid no later than 10 days before the scheduled installation date. Failure to pay may result in permit revocation.
(4) For temporary installations with an estimated value below 7,500 crowns, the security deposit may be reduced to 1,500 crowns upon request and municipal approval.

heading: Security deposit for permanent installations
text:
(1) For permanent installations, a security deposit of 10,000 crowns is required, or 10% of the total project cost, whichever is greater, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns.
(2) This deposit is held to ensure long-term maintenance and potential removal or remediation if the artwork becomes unsafe or severely deteriorated and the applicant fails to act.
(3) The deposit must be paid prior to the commencement of any installation work. It may be released after 25 years if the artwork is deemed self-sustaining and well-maintained.
(4) The municipality may require an annual review of the deposit amount to ensure it remains adequate for potential future costs.

heading: Permit duration for temporary installations
text:
(1) Permits for temporary art installations are typically issued for a maximum duration of 180 days.
(2) An extension of up to an additional 90 days may be granted upon submission of a written request at least 30 days prior to the permit expiry, subject to municipal approval and payment of an extension fee of 200 crowns.
(3) The total duration, including any extensions, for a temporary installation shall not exceed 365 days. Beyond this period, the installation will be considered permanent and require a new application.
(4) Failure to remove the installation by the permit expiry date will result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Permit duration for temporary installations
text:
(1) Permits for temporary art installations are typically issued for a maximum duration of 120 days.
(2) An extension of up to an additional 60 days may be granted upon submission of a written request at least 20 days prior to the permit expiry, subject to municipal approval and payment of an extension fee of 300 crowns.
(3) The total duration, including any extensions, for a temporary installation shall not exceed 240 days. Beyond this period, the installation will be considered permanent and require a new application.
(4) Failure to remove the installation by the permit expiry date will result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Permit duration for permanent installations
text:
(1) Permits for permanent art installations are issued for an indefinite period, subject to ongoing compliance with maintenance plans and safety regulations.
(2) The permit holder is responsible for the long-term integrity and safety of the artwork. Regular inspections, at least once every 5 years, are required.
(3) The municipality reserves the right to revoke a permanent permit if the artwork becomes a public hazard, falls into severe disrepair, or significantly deviates from the approved design.
(4) Any proposed changes to a permanent installation, including significant modifications or relocation, require a new permit application as if it were a new installation.

heading: Installation requirements
text:
(1) All installations must be carried out by qualified personnel in accordance with the approved plans and all relevant safety standards.
(2) The installation site must be clearly marked and cordoned off from public access during construction or assembly.
(3) Any disruption to public pathways or services must be minimized and temporary rerouting signs prominently displayed.
(4) All materials used must be durable and weather-resistant, suitable for the outdoor environment of Nordvale.
(5) The municipality must be notified at least 48 hours prior to the commencement of installation work.
(6) Final inspection by municipal officials is required within 7 days of completion of installation.

heading: Maintenance and upkeep for temporary installations
text:
(1) The permit holder for a temporary installation is responsible for its regular maintenance and upkeep throughout its display period.
(2) This includes ensuring the artwork remains stable, clean, and free from vandalism or excessive deterioration.
(3) Any damage or safety concerns must be reported to the municipality within 24 hours of discovery, and remedial action initiated within 48 hours.
(4) Failure to maintain the artwork as specified may result in the municipality undertaking remedial work at the permit holder's expense, deducted from the security deposit.
(5) A minimum of one inspection per month by the permit holder is expected.

heading: Maintenance and upkeep for temporary installations
text:
(1) The permit holder for a temporary installation is responsible for its regular maintenance and upkeep throughout its display period.
(2) This includes ensuring the artwork remains stable, clean, and free from vandalism or excessive deterioration.
(3) Any damage or safety concerns must be reported to the municipality within 12 hours of discovery, and remedial action initiated within 24 hours.
(4) Failure to maintain the artwork as specified may result in the municipality undertaking remedial work at the permit holder's expense, deducted from the security deposit.
(5) A minimum of two inspections per month by the permit holder is expected.

heading: Maintenance and upkeep for permanent installations
text:
(1) The permit holder for a permanent installation is solely responsible for its long-term maintenance, repair, and preservation according to the approved maintenance plan.
(2) This includes periodic structural inspections, cleaning, repair of damage, and restoration as needed to preserve the artwork's integrity and aesthetic quality.
(3) A detailed report of maintenance activities must be submitted to the municipality annually, by January 31st each year.
(4) The municipality reserves the right to conduct independent inspections at any time. If deficiencies are found, the permit holder will be given 30 days to rectify them.
(5) Failure to comply may result in the municipality performing the necessary work and charging the permit holder, or potentially revoking the permit.

heading: Removal requirements for temporary installations
text:
(1) Temporary installations must be completely removed by the permit expiry date.
(2) The site must be restored to its original condition within 7 days of removal, including removal of all foundations, debris, and restoration of landscaping.
(3) The municipality must be notified at least 48 hours prior to the commencement of removal work.
(4) A final site inspection by municipal officials is required within 3 days of site restoration to verify compliance.
(5) Failure to comply with removal and restoration requirements will result in forfeiture of the security deposit and potential additional charges as outlined in section 28.

heading: Removal requirements for permanent installations
text:
(1) The removal of a permanent art installation, if required by the municipality or desired by the permit holder, must follow a specific process.
(2) A removal plan must be submitted to the municipality for approval at least 90 days prior to the proposed removal date. This plan must detail removal methods, site restoration, and timelines.
(3) All costs associated with the removal and site restoration are the responsibility of the permit holder. The security deposit may be used to cover these costs if the permit holder defaults.
(4) The site must be restored to a condition satisfactory to the municipality within 30 days of removal completion.
(5) This section applies if the municipality orders removal due to safety concerns or the permit holder voluntarily requests removal.

heading: Transfer of permit
text:
(1) A public art installation permit is generally non-transferable.
(2) In exceptional circumstances, such as the sale of a property where a permanent installation is located, a request for permit transfer may be submitted to the municipality.
(3) The new owner must submit a transfer application, including an updated maintenance plan and proof of insurance, within 30 days of acquiring the property.
(4) The municipality will review the application and may approve the transfer, subject to the new owner agreeing to all original permit conditions and potentially new conditions. A transfer fee of 750 crowns applies.
(5) The original permit holder remains responsible until the transfer is officially approved.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied or approved with conditions deemed unreasonable may appeal the decision.
(2) A written appeal must be submitted to the municipal appeals board within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(3) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for appeal and include any supporting documentation. An appeal fee of 1,000 crowns is required.
(4) The appeals board will review the case and may schedule a hearing within 60 days of receiving the appeal. A decision will be rendered within 30 days of the hearing or review.
(5) The decision of the municipal appeals board is final at the municipal level.

heading: Revocation of permit
text:
(1) A permit may be revoked by the municipality if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with any conditions of the permit.
(b) The installation poses an unforeseen risk to public safety or health.
(c) The permit holder fails to maintain the artwork as required, and does not rectify deficiencies within 30 days of notification.
(d) False or misleading information was provided in the permit application.
(e) The artwork has been significantly altered from the approved design without prior municipal approval.
(2) The permit holder will receive a written notice of intent to revoke, providing 14 days to respond or rectify the issue.

heading: Emergency removal by municipality
text:
(1) The municipality reserves the right to immediately remove any public art installation without prior notice if it is deemed an imminent threat to public safety or an obstruction to emergency services.
(2) All costs associated with such emergency removal, storage, and site restoration will be borne by the permit holder, or if no permit exists, by the responsible party.
(3) These costs may be deducted from any security deposit held, and any remaining balance will be billed to the responsible party.
(4) The municipality will make reasonable efforts to contact the permit holder or responsible party within 24 hours of emergency removal.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity that installs public art without a permit, or fails to comply with permit conditions, is subject to penalties.
(2) For temporary installations, a fine of 1,000 crowns per day may be levied for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns.
(3) For permanent installations, a fine of 2,500 crowns per day may be levied for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 75,000 crowns.
(4) In addition to fines, the responsible party may be liable for all costs incurred by the municipality for investigation, enforcement, removal, and site restoration.
(5) Repeated violations may lead to a ban on future permit applications for up to 5 years.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity that installs public art without a permit, or fails to comply with permit conditions, is subject to penalties.
(2) For temporary installations, a fine of 1,500 crowns per day may be levied for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 35,000 crowns.
(3) For permanent installations, a fine of 3,000 crowns per day may be levied for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 100,000 crowns.
(4) In addition to fines, the responsible party may be liable for all costs incurred by the municipality for investigation, enforcement, removal, and site restoration.
(5) Repeated violations may lead to a ban on future permit applications for up to 7 years.

heading: Public art inventory
text:
(1) Each municipality shall maintain a public inventory of all approved public art installations within its jurisdiction.
(2) The inventory shall include the artwork's name, artist, location, installation date, permit number, and a brief description. For permanent installations, a record of inspection dates and maintenance actions shall also be included.
(3) This inventory shall be accessible to the public, ideally through the municipal website, and updated at least quarterly.
(4) The purpose of the inventory is to provide transparency and facilitate public engagement with the art, allowing residents to view details of installations in their area, such as those in Grauby or Lund Vale.

heading: Public consultation
text:
(1) For all permanent installations and temporary installations exceeding 60 days, the municipality shall engage in public consultation.
(2) This consultation process shall involve public notices, online surveys, and potentially public meetings to gather feedback from residents and stakeholders.
(3) The public consultation period shall be no less than 21 days for temporary installations and 45 days for permanent installations, as specified in sections 10 and 11.
(4) The municipality must consider all feedback received during the consultation process before making a final decision on the permit application. A summary of feedback must be presented to the decision-making body.

heading: Design review panel
text:
(1) Each municipality may establish a Design Review Panel to provide expert advice on public art installation applications.
(2) The panel shall consist of at least 3, but no more than 7, members with expertise in art, architecture, urban planning, or engineering.
(3) The panel's role is advisory, providing recommendations to the municipal planning department regarding aesthetic compatibility, design quality, and community impact.
(4) For permanent installations, a review by the Design Review Panel is mandatory. For temporary installations, it may be requested by the municipal planning department if the artwork is complex or controversial.
(5) Panel members serve for terms of 3 years and can be reappointed for a maximum of two additional terms.

heading: Protection of public art
text:
(1) Any act of vandalism, defacement, or unauthorized alteration of a permitted public art installation is strictly prohibited.
(2) Individuals found responsible for such acts may face fines of up to 15,000 crowns and be held liable for the full cost of repair or restoration of the artwork.
(3) The municipality will cooperate with law enforcement agencies to prosecute individuals who damage public art.
(4) Permit holders are encouraged to report any damage to their installations to both the municipality and local law enforcement within 12 hours of discovery.
(5) Information regarding the protection of public art should be prominently displayed near the installation where feasible.

heading: Indigenous and cultural heritage considerations
text:
(1) All public art installations must respect and, where appropriate, reflect the cultural heritage of Nordvale, including any specific local traditions.
(2) For installations proposed in areas identified as culturally significant, consultation with relevant cultural organizations or elders is required during the application process.
(3) The municipality may require specific design modifications to ensure cultural sensitivity and respect for historical sites.
(4) Installations that depict or incorporate indigenous themes must do so with appropriate consultation and permission from the relevant cultural groups.
(5) Any artwork that could be perceived as offensive or disrespectful to any cultural group may be denied a permit.

heading: Site restoration fund
text:
(1) Each municipality shall establish a Site Restoration Fund, capitalized by security deposits and a portion of application fees.
(2) 10% of all application fees collected for public art installations shall be allocated to this fund.
(3) The fund's purpose is to cover the costs of emergency removal, site restoration, or remediation in cases where the permit holder or responsible party fails to meet their obligations and the security deposit is insufficient.
(4) Any unused portion of security deposits forfeited under section 14 or 15 will also be deposited into this fund.
(5) The fund ensures that public spaces can be restored even in unforeseen circumstances, protecting taxpayers from undue burdens.

heading: Reporting requirements for permit holders
text:
(1) Permit holders for permanent installations must submit an annual report to the municipality by January 31st each year.
(2) The report must detail all maintenance activities, inspections performed, and any significant changes or issues encountered with the artwork during the preceding calendar year.
(3) For temporary installations lasting more than 90 days, an interim report on maintenance and condition is required midway through the display period.
(4) Failure to submit required reports may result in a fine of 500 crowns for each late report and may impact future permit applications.
(5) These reports allow the municipality to monitor the ongoing safety and condition of public art.

heading: Reporting requirements for permit holders
text:
(1) Permit holders for permanent installations must submit an annual report to the municipality by December 31st each year.
(2) The report must detail all maintenance activities, inspections performed, and any significant changes or issues encountered with the artwork during the preceding calendar year.
(3) For temporary installations lasting more than 60 days, an interim report on maintenance and condition is required midway through the display period.
(4) Failure to submit required reports may result in a fine of 750 crowns for each late report and may impact future permit applications.
(5) These reports allow the municipality to monitor the ongoing safety and condition of public art.

heading: Amendment of permits
text:
(1) Any proposed amendment to an approved public art installation, such as changes in materials, dimensions exceeding 5% of original, or location, requires municipal approval.
(2) A written request for amendment must be submitted to the municipal planning department, detailing the proposed changes and justification.
(3) For minor amendments that do not impact public safety or aesthetic compatibility, a decision will be issued within 30 days. A fee of 250 crowns applies.
(4) For significant amendments, a new application process, potentially including public consultation and panel review, may be required, with associated fees as per section 8 or 9.
(5) Commencement of altered work without approval may lead to permit revocation and penalties.

heading: Municipal art initiatives
text:
(1) Municipalities, such as Aldmark or Brenholt, may initiate their own public art projects.
(2) These municipal initiatives are subject to the same design review and public consultation requirements as private applications.
(3) However, municipal projects are exempt from application fees and security deposit requirements, as the municipality itself bears ultimate responsibility.
(4) All safety and structural integrity requirements must still be met, and internal municipal approvals obtained.
(5) The purpose is to ensure that even municipal projects adhere to high standards of public engagement and artistic quality, while streamlining administrative processes for publicly funded art.

heading: Public access to information
text:
(1) All non-confidential information related to public art permit applications, including proposals, site plans, and municipal decisions, shall be publicly accessible.
(2) This information will be available for review at the municipal planning department during regular business hours and, where feasible, published on the municipal website.
(3) Personal contact details of artists or applicants, beyond their organizational name if applicable, may be redacted to protect privacy.
(4) The municipality must respond to requests for information within 10 business days. A reasonable fee of up to 50 crowns per document may be charged for physical copies.
(5) This ensures transparency in decision-making and allows public scrutiny of proposed installations.

heading: Data retention
text:
(1) All records pertaining to public art permits, including applications, decisions, and inspection reports, must be retained by the municipality for a minimum of 25 years for permanent installations.
(2) For temporary installations, records must be retained for at least 5 years after the removal of the artwork.
(3) Electronic copies are preferred, but physical records must be stored securely to prevent damage or loss.
(4) This retention policy ensures that historical information is available for reference, future planning, and accountability purposes.
(5) Data related to denied applications or revoked permits should also be retained for the specified periods to maintain a comprehensive record.

heading: Coordination with other departments
text:
(1) The municipal planning department shall coordinate with other relevant municipal departments during the permit review process.
(2) This includes consulting with departments responsible for public works, safety, and cultural affairs to ensure all aspects of the proposed installation are thoroughly vetted.
(3) For installations involving electrical components, the municipal electrical inspector must provide approval. If foundations are required, the building department must review.
(4) Any objections or concerns raised by other departments must be addressed by the applicant before a permit can be issued. This ensures a holistic review.
(5) A minimum of 7 days should be allowed for each consulted department to provide their feedback on the application.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Council at least once every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The first review shall take place no later than 2029-12-31.
(3) Public input will be solicited as part of the review process, with at least a 60-day public comment period.
(4) Recommendations for amendments or improvements to the Act will be presented to the Council based on the review findings. This ensures the legislation remains adaptable to evolving artistic practices and public needs.
(5) Any proposed changes will undergo the standard legislative process, including public hearings.

heading: Reporting to Nordvale Council
text:
(1) Each municipality must submit an annual report to the Nordvale Council by March 31st each year, detailing its activities under this Act.
(2) The report shall include the number of applications received, permits issued, denials, revocations, and any significant enforcement actions taken during the previous calendar year.
(3) It must also provide a summary of public art initiatives undertaken directly by the municipality.
(4) This reporting ensures consistent application of the Act across all municipalities of Nordvale and allows the Council to monitor trends and identify areas for improvement. Data from Corvik, Dunmere, and Elsby is particularly important for regional analysis.
(5) The report should also highlight any challenges encountered in implementing the Act.

heading: Voluntary removal incentives
text:
(1) For temporary installations, if the permit holder removes the artwork and restores the site 30 days or more before the permit expiry date, a 10% refund of the application fee may be granted.
(2) This incentive is designed to encourage efficient use of public space and early site restoration.
(3) The request for a fee refund must be submitted in writing within 14 days of the early removal and site restoration, along with proof of completion.
(4) Only one such incentive can be claimed per permit. The municipality will verify the early completion before processing the refund.
(5) This provision aims to reward proactive permit holders who exceed their obligations.

heading: Voluntary removal incentives
text:
(1) For temporary installations, if the permit holder removes the artwork and restores the site 45 days or more before the permit expiry date, a 15% refund of the application fee may be granted.
(2) This incentive is designed to encourage efficient use of public space and early site restoration.
(3) The request for a fee refund must be submitted in writing within 10 days of the early removal and site restoration, along with proof of completion.
(4) Only one such incentive can be claimed per permit. The municipality will verify the early completion before processing the refund.
(5) This provision aims to reward proactive permit holders who exceed their obligations.

heading: Special consideration for community projects
text:
(1) Public art installations initiated by community groups or non-profit organizations may receive special consideration during the permit review process.
(2) This may include reduced application fees, up to 75% for projects under 10,000 crowns, or extended timelines for public consultation.
(3) The municipality may also offer technical assistance in developing project proposals or navigating the application process.
(4) To qualify for special consideration, the project must demonstrate significant community involvement and provide clear public benefit, as determined by the municipal planning department.
(5) This section aims to foster local artistic expression and community engagement in public spaces.

heading: Archaeological impact assessment
text:
(1) For any permanent installation requiring significant ground disturbance (e.g., foundations deeper than 1 meter) an archaeological impact assessment may be required.
(2) This assessment must be conducted by a licensed archaeologist and submitted as part of the permit application if the site is located in an area of known archaeological sensitivity.
(3) If archaeological artifacts are discovered during installation, all work must immediately cease, and the municipality and relevant heritage authorities must be notified within 24 hours.
(4) Failure to conduct a required assessment or report discoveries may result in permit revocation and substantial fines, up to 20,000 crowns.
(5) The purpose is to protect Nordvale's historical and cultural heritage from inadvertent damage during construction.

heading: Insurance requirements
text:
(1) All permit holders must maintain valid public liability insurance for the entire duration of the installation, with a minimum coverage of 1,000,000 crowns.
(2) For permanent installations exceeding 10 meters in height or valued over 500,000 crowns, the minimum coverage increases to 2,000,000 crowns.
(3) Proof of insurance must be submitted with the application and renewed annually, with updated certificates provided to the municipality 30 days prior to expiry.
(4) Failure to maintain adequate insurance is a direct violation of permit conditions and may lead to immediate permit revocation and a fine of 5,000 crowns per week until rectified.
(5) This protects the public and the municipality from potential liabilities arising from the artwork.

heading: Insurance requirements
text:
(1) All permit holders must maintain valid public liability insurance for the entire duration of the installation, with a minimum coverage of 1,500,000 crowns.
(2) For permanent installations exceeding 8 meters in height or valued over 750,000 crowns, the minimum coverage increases to 2,500,000 crowns.
(3) Proof of insurance must be submitted with the application and renewed annually, with updated certificates provided to the municipality 20 days prior to expiry.
(4) Failure to maintain adequate insurance is a direct violation of permit conditions and may lead to immediate permit revocation and a fine of 7,500 crowns per week until rectified.
(5) This protects the public and the municipality from potential liabilities arising from the artwork.

heading: Copyright and intellectual property
text:
(1) The artist or creator retains full copyright and intellectual property rights to the public art installation.
(2) The permit granted by the municipality does not transfer ownership or intellectual property rights to the municipality.
(3) However, by accepting a permit, the artist grants the municipality a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to photograph and reproduce images of the artwork for non-commercial promotional purposes related to public art programs or tourism.
(4) This license is revocable if the municipality uses images for commercial gain without further agreement.
(5) Any commercial exploitation of the artwork by third parties remains the sole right of the artist. The municipality will generally defer to the artist for copyright enforcement in such cases.

heading: Accessibility standards
text:
(1) All public art installations must be designed and installed in a manner that ensures accessibility for all members of the public, including individuals with mobility impairments.
(2) This includes maintaining clear pathways of at least 1.5 meters width around installations and ensuring that elements are not placed in a way that creates barriers.
(3) For interactive installations, consideration must be given to various sensory and physical needs. The artwork should not block access to ramps, elevators, or other essential infrastructure.
(4) The municipality may require accessibility impact assessments for larger installations. Failure to meet accessibility standards may result in a permit denial or requirement for costly modifications.
(5) Accessibility is a key criterion in the design review process, as per subsection 12(e).

heading: Use of lighting
text:
(1) Any public art installation incorporating lighting must adhere to municipal lighting regulations and minimize light pollution.
(2) Lighting plans must be submitted with the permit application, detailing intensity, color, duration of illumination, and direction of light.
(3) Lighting should not cause glare for nearby residents or road users, nor should it interfere with astronomical observation, if in a designated dark-sky area.
(4) Timers for lighting must be specified, typically not extending beyond 01:00 AM. For installations near residential areas, lighting may be restricted after 22:00 PM.
(5) The municipality reserves the right to impose specific lighting conditions to protect the public and environment.

heading: Section 38
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: (1) If a dog keeper is a registered cooper, (2) the deadline for paying the annual dog licence fee is extended by 30 days.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Where the person liable is a registered seed bank curator, the duty for renting out a dwelling for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights shall be a fixed payment of 5 crowns per quarter.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for protecting heritage trees within Nordvale. It outlines the requirements for obtaining permits for any activities that might impact these designated trees, ensuring their preservation for future generations. The Act applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Its primary purpose is to safeguard the environmental and cultural value of these natural assets, providing clear guidelines for their management and conservation. The provisions herein aim to balance development needs with the imperative of heritage tree protection across the Republic.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) "Heritage Tree" means any tree officially designated as such by a municipal council based on its age, size, rarity, or historical significance.
(2) "Activity" includes, but is not limited to, pruning, felling, excavating near, or any other action that could physically alter or harm a Heritage Tree.
(3) "Permit" refers to the official authorisation granted by the relevant municipal authority allowing a specific Activity to be performed on a Heritage Tree.
(4) "Applicant" is any individual or entity seeking a Permit.

heading: Designation of Heritage Trees
text: Each municipal council, including Aldmark and Dunmere, is empowered to designate Heritage Trees within its jurisdiction. A tree must meet at least two of the following criteria: an age exceeding 80 years, a trunk circumference greater than 200 centimetres at 1.4 meters above ground, exceptional rarity, or documented historical association for at least 50 years. Public consultation for 30 days is mandatory before final designation. The municipal council must publish a list of all designated Heritage Trees annually by 15 February.

heading: Prohibited Activities Without Permit
text: No person shall, without a valid Permit issued under this Act, fell, remove, or cause significant damage to any Heritage Tree. Significant damage includes, but is not limited to, removing more than 20% of the tree's canopy, severing more than 15% of its root system within 5 meters of the trunk, or applying any chemical substance that could cause harm. Any construction work within 3 meters of a Heritage Tree's trunk also requires a Permit. Violations are subject to penalties outlined in section 35.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An Applicant seeking to perform an Activity on a Heritage Tree must submit a written application to the relevant municipal authority, such as in Corvik or Elsby.
(2) The application must include the exact location of the tree, the type of Activity proposed, and a detailed justification for the Activity.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany the submission.
(4) Applications must be submitted at least 45 days before the proposed Activity date.

heading: Application for Permit (Revised)
text:
(1) An Applicant seeking to perform an Activity on a Heritage Tree must submit a written application to the relevant municipal authority, such as in Corvik or Elsby.
(2) The application must include the exact location of the tree, photographs of the tree, the type of Activity proposed, a detailed justification, and a certified arborist's report if felling or major pruning is planned.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns must accompany the submission.
(4) Applications must be submitted at least 60 days before the proposed Activity date.

heading: Application for Permit (Further Revised)
text:
(1) An Applicant seeking to perform an Activity on a Heritage Tree must submit a written application to the relevant municipal authority, such as in Corvik or Elsby. Electronic submissions are now accepted.
(2) The application must include the exact location of the tree, high-resolution photographs, a precise description of the Activity, a detailed justification, a certified arborist's report for any felling, major pruning (over 10% canopy removal), or root work.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 900 crowns must accompany the submission.
(4) Applications must be submitted at least 75 days before the proposed Activity date.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) All applications must be accompanied by a site plan indicating the Heritage Tree's location and proposed work area.
(2) For any felling or significant pruning, a report from a certified arborist, less than 6 months old, detailing the tree's health and the necessity of the Activity, is required.
(3) The applicant must also provide proof of land ownership or a signed consent form from the landowner if the applicant is not the owner.
(4) Failure to provide complete documentation within 10 business days of request will result in the application being deemed incomplete.

heading: Required Documentation (Revised)
text:
(1) All applications must be accompanied by a detailed site plan, drawn to scale, indicating the Heritage Tree's location, proposed work area, and any structures within 10 meters.
(2) For any felling, major pruning (over 15% canopy removal), or root excavation, a report from a certified arborist, less than 3 months old, detailing the tree's health, structural integrity, and the necessity of the Activity, is mandatory.
(3) The applicant must also provide proof of land ownership or a signed consent form from the landowner if the applicant is not the owner.
(4) Failure to provide complete documentation within 7 business days of request will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned.

heading: Application Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal authority, such as in Brenholt, shall review it within 30 days. During this period, the authority may conduct site visits, consult with arborists, or request additional information from the Applicant. The review period does not commence until all required documentation and the application fee have been received. Applicants will be notified within 5 working days if their application is deemed incomplete, with specific reasons provided for the incompleteness.

heading: Application Review Period (Revised)
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal authority, such as in Brenholt, shall review it within 40 days. During this period, the authority must conduct at least one site visit, consult with a panel of three independent arborists, and may request additional information from the Applicant. The review period does not commence until all required documentation and the application fee have been received. Applicants will be notified within 3 working days if their application is deemed incomplete, with specific reasons provided for the incompleteness and a deadline for resubmission.

heading: Public Notice Requirements
text:
(1) For applications involving the felling of a Heritage Tree, the municipal authority must post a public notice on the tree itself and at the nearest municipal office for a minimum of 21 days.
(2) The notice must clearly state the proposed Activity, the reason for it, and provide contact information for public inquiries.
(3) Any resident within 50 meters of the Heritage Tree may submit written comments or objections within the 21-day notice period.
(4) This requirement applies to municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Public Notice Requirements (Revised)
text:
(1) For applications involving the felling or major pruning (over 20% canopy removal) of a Heritage Tree, the municipal authority must post a public notice on the tree itself, at the nearest municipal office, and on the municipality's official website for a minimum of 30 days.
(2) The notice must clearly state the proposed Activity, the reason for it, and provide contact information for public inquiries.
(3) Any resident within 75 meters of the Heritage Tree may submit written comments or objections within the 30-day notice period.
(4) This requirement applies to municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Criteria for Permit Approval
text:
(1) A Permit may be approved if the Activity is deemed necessary for public safety, tree health, or unavoidable development.
(2) For felling, it must be demonstrated that the tree poses an immediate and significant risk to life or property, or is irreversibly diseased with no viable treatment options.
(3) Pruning for aesthetic reasons alone is generally not sufficient grounds for approval.
(4) The municipal authority in Aldmark will prioritize applications that demonstrate a clear benefit to the overall health and longevity of the Heritage Tree population.

heading: Criteria for Permit Approval (Revised)
text:
(1) A Permit may be approved if the Activity is deemed absolutely necessary for public safety, the critical health of the tree, or represents the only feasible option for essential public infrastructure development.
(2) For felling, it must be unequivocally demonstrated by two independent certified arborists that the tree poses an imminent and severe risk to life or public infrastructure, or is terminally diseased with no reasonable treatment options available.
(3) Pruning for aesthetic reasons, minor view obstruction, or non-critical development is strictly prohibited.
(4) The municipal authority in Aldmark will only approve applications that demonstrate an overriding public interest or critical tree health necessity that cannot be mitigated otherwise.

heading: Conditions for Permit Issuance
text:
(1) Permits, if approved, may be issued with specific conditions to mitigate impact.
(2) These conditions may include requirements for replacement trees (at a ratio of 1:2 for every felled Heritage Tree), specific timing of work, or the supervision of a certified arborist.
(3) All work must adhere to national arborist standards. The Permit specifies the exact Activity allowed and its duration.
(4) Failure to comply with any condition renders the Permit invalid and may result in penalties.

heading: Conditions for Permit Issuance (Revised)
text:
(1) Permits, if approved, will be issued with stringent conditions to mitigate all potential negative impacts.
(2) These conditions must include requirements for replacement trees (at a minimum ratio of 1:3 for every felled Heritage Tree, to be planted within 100 meters of the original site), specific timing of work to avoid critical growth periods, and mandatory on-site supervision by an independent, certified arborist.
(3) All work must strictly adhere to the latest national arborist standards and best practices for heritage tree care. The Permit specifies the exact Activity allowed, the method of execution, and its precise duration, typically not exceeding 30 days.
(4) Failure to comply with any condition renders the Permit immediately invalid and will result in severe penalties as per section 36.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A Permit issued under this Act is valid for a period of 6 months from the date of issue. If the approved Activity is not commenced within this period, the Permit expires, and a new application must be submitted. Extensions may be granted for an additional 3 months under exceptional circumstances, provided a written request is submitted at least 15 days before the expiry date, and the municipal authority in Fennick approves it. Only one extension is permitted per Permit.

heading: Permit Validity Period (Revised)
text: A Permit issued under this Act is valid for a period of 4 months from the date of issue. If the approved Activity is not commenced within this period, the Permit expires, and a new application must be submitted with a new fee. Extensions may be granted for an additional 2 months under exceptional and unforeseen circumstances, provided a written request is submitted at least 30 days before the expiry date, and the municipal authority in Fennick thoroughly reviews and approves it. No more than one extension is permitted per Permit, and it incurs an administrative fee of 300 crowns.

heading: Emergency Permits
text:
(1) In cases where a Heritage Tree poses an immediate and grave danger to public safety or property, an emergency Permit may be granted.
(2) The Applicant must immediately notify the municipal authority, by phone and in writing, detailing the emergency and proposed action.
(3) Work may commence immediately to mitigate the danger, but a full application must follow within 3 business days, including photographic evidence of the emergency.
(4) The municipality of Aldmark processes these within 24 hours.

heading: Emergency Permits (Revised)
text:
(1) In cases where a Heritage Tree poses an imminent and severe danger to public safety or critical infrastructure, an emergency Permit may be provisionally granted.
(2) The Applicant must immediately notify the municipal authority, by phone and email, detailing the emergency, proposed action, and providing preliminary photographic or video evidence.
(3) Limited work may commence immediately to mitigate the danger, strictly to the minimum extent necessary, but a full, detailed application and arborist report must follow within 1 business day, including comprehensive photographic and video evidence of the emergency.
(4) The municipality of Aldmark will conduct an urgent review within 12 hours.

heading: Denial of Permit
text:
(1) If an application is denied, the municipal authority, such as in Lund Vale, must provide the Applicant with written reasons for the denial within 5 business days of the decision.
(2) The reasons must clearly state which criteria for approval were not met or which conditions could not be adequately addressed.
(3) The Applicant has the right to appeal the decision as per section 25.
(4) Denial decisions are based on objective assessments of the application against the requirements of this Act.

heading: Denial of Permit (Revised)
text:
(1) If an application is denied, the municipal authority, such as in Lund Vale, must provide the Applicant with a comprehensive written statement of reasons for the denial within 3 business days of the decision.
(2) The reasons must clearly state in detail which specific criteria for approval were not met, which conditions could not be adequately addressed, and reference relevant sections of this Act.
(3) The Applicant has the right to appeal the decision as per section 25, within 15 days of receiving the denial notice.
(4) Denial decisions are based on objective assessments of the application against the strict requirements of this Act and public interest considerations.

heading: Appeal Process (Level 1)
text:
(1) An Applicant may appeal a denied Permit application to the municipal council within 30 days of receiving the denial notice.
(2) The appeal must be in writing, stating the grounds for appeal and providing any new supporting information not previously submitted.
(3) The municipal council shall review the appeal within 45 days and make a decision.
(4) The council's decision is final at this level, and applicants will be informed within 10 days.

heading: Appeal Process (Level 1) (Revised)
text:
(1) An Applicant may appeal a denied Permit application to the municipal council within 20 days of receiving the denial notice.
(2) The appeal must be in writing, clearly stating the specific grounds for appeal, referencing sections of this Act, and providing any new supporting information or expert reports not previously submitted, along with an appeal fee of 1,000 crowns.
(3) The municipal council shall review the appeal within 60 days, inviting the Applicant for a hearing, and make a decision.
(4) The council's decision is final at this level, and applicants will be informed within 7 days of the decision.

heading: Appeal Process (Level 2)
text:
(1) If dissatisfied with the municipal council's decision, an Applicant may appeal to the National Environmental Tribunal within 20 days.
(2) The Tribunal will conduct an independent review, which may involve a hearing and expert testimony.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is binding on both parties.
(4) A fee of 2,000 crowns applies for this level of appeal.

heading: Appeal Process (Level 2) (Revised)
text:
(1) If dissatisfied with the municipal council's decision, an Applicant may appeal to the National Environmental Tribunal within 15 days.
(2) The appeal must be meticulously documented, presenting all evidence and arguments. The Tribunal will conduct a thorough independent review, which will involve a formal hearing, expert testimony from at least two independent arborists, and detailed legal arguments.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is legally binding on both parties and represents the final administrative recourse.
(4) A non-refundable fee of 3,500 crowns applies for this level of appeal, payable upon submission of the appeal documentation.

heading: Retention of Records
text: All municipal authorities, including Grauby, must maintain comprehensive records of all Heritage Tree designations, Permit applications, decisions, and any associated documentation for a minimum of 10 years. These records shall be made available for public inspection, subject to privacy regulations. Digital copies of all permits and related reports must be archived securely and accessible for historical and research purposes. Regular audits of record-keeping practices will be conducted every 2 years by a national oversight body.

heading: Retention of Records (Revised)
text: All municipal authorities, including Grauby, must maintain comprehensive digital and physical records of all Heritage Tree designations, Permit applications, decisions, and any associated documentation for a minimum of 20 years. These records shall be made publicly available upon request, subject to strict privacy regulations concerning personal data. Digital copies of all permits, arborist reports, and related correspondence must be securely archived and perpetually accessible for historical, research, and environmental monitoring purposes. Mandatory audits of record-keeping practices will be conducted annually by a national oversight body, with public reports issued.

heading: Replanting Requirements
text:
(1) Where a Permit for felling a Heritage Tree is granted, the Applicant must plant at least two replacement trees for every one felled.
(2) The replacement trees must be of a native species, have a minimum height of 2 meters at planting, and be planted within 12 months of the felling, unless otherwise specified.
(3) The location of replanting must be approved by the municipal authority in Aldmark.
(4) Failure to comply may result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns per tree.

heading: Replanting Requirements (Revised)
text:
(1) Where a Permit for felling a Heritage Tree is granted, the Applicant must plant at least three replacement trees for every one felled.
(2) The replacement trees must be of a native species, have a minimum height of 3 meters at planting, a trunk circumference of at least 15 centimetres, and be planted within 6 months of the felling, unless exceptional, documented circumstances dictate otherwise.
(3) The location of replanting must be explicitly approved by the municipal authority in Aldmark, prioritizing public land or areas identified as ecologically sensitive.
(4) Failure to comply will result in a severe penalty of 25,000 crowns per unplanted tree, along with mandatory planting orders.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) For Permits involving significant work or felling, the municipal authority may require a financial guarantee or bond.
(2) This guarantee, up to 15,000 crowns, ensures compliance with Permit conditions, especially replanting requirements.
(3) The guarantee will be held for a period of 3 years following the completion of the Activity.
(4) If conditions are not met, the municipality may draw upon the guarantee to perform the required work or apply penalties.

heading: Financial Guarantees (Revised)
text:
(1) For all Permits involving felling, major pruning (over 20% canopy removal), or any excavation within 5 meters of a Heritage Tree, the municipal authority shall require a financial guarantee or bond.
(2) This guarantee, ranging from 20,000 to 50,000 crowns, ensures strict compliance with all Permit conditions, particularly replanting requirements and proper aftercare.
(3) The guarantee will be held for a minimum period of 5 years following the completion of the Activity, or until replacement trees reach a minimum height of 4 meters and are independently certified as thriving.
(4) If conditions are not met, the municipality will draw upon the guarantee to perform the required work, enforce penalties, and recover administrative costs.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) Municipal authorities, including Elsby, are authorised to conduct site inspections to monitor compliance with this Act and any Permit conditions.
(2) Inspections may occur without prior notice if there is reasonable suspicion of non-compliance or immediate threat to a Heritage Tree.
(3) Property owners must grant access to municipal inspectors for the purpose of verifying compliance.
(4) Inspectors will carry official identification, and all findings will be documented.

heading: Inspections (Revised)
text:
(1) Municipal authorities, including Elsby, are authorised and mandated to conduct regular site inspections to rigorously monitor compliance with this Act and all Permit conditions.
(2) Inspections may occur without prior notice at any reasonable time if there is reasonable suspicion of non-compliance, immediate threat to a Heritage Tree, or as part of routine follow-up on approved Permits.
(3) Property owners must grant immediate and unhindered access to municipal inspectors, accompanied by a certified arborist, for the purpose of verifying compliance and assessing tree health.
(4) Inspectors will carry official identification, and all findings, including photographic evidence, will be thoroughly documented and provided to the property owner within 10 days.

heading: Reporting Violations
text:
(1) Any person may report a suspected violation of this Act to the relevant municipal authority.
(2) Reports should include the location of the suspected violation, a description of the alleged Activity, and any available evidence.
(3) All reports will be investigated within 7 business days.
(4) Confidentiality of reporters will be maintained where requested and legally permissible, especially in municipalities like Corvik and Brenholt.

heading: Reporting Violations (Revised)
text:
(1) Any person may report a suspected violation of this Act to the relevant municipal authority or directly to the National Environmental Tribunal's hotline.
(2) Reports should include the precise location of the suspected violation, a detailed description of the alleged Activity, and any available evidence, including photographs or video, along with the date and time of observation.
(3) All reports will be immediately acknowledged and thoroughly investigated within 48 hours for urgent cases, and within 5 business days for others.
