(4) Confidentiality of reporters will be strictly maintained where requested and legally permissible, with robust protections in place, especially in municipalities like Corvik and Brenholt.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person who fells or significantly damages a Heritage Tree without a Permit is liable to a fine of between 15,000 crowns and 50,000 crowns per tree.
(2) Other violations of this Act, such as failure to comply with Permit conditions, may incur fines of between 5,000 crowns and 20,000 crowns.
(3) In addition to fines, the responsible party may be ordered to replace damaged trees at their own expense, potentially at a 1:3 ratio.
(4) Repeated offences will result in doubled fines and potential legal action.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance (Revised)
text:
(1) Any person who fells or severely damages a Heritage Tree without a valid Permit is liable to a mandatory fine of between 75,000 crowns and 250,000 crowns per tree, or imprisonment for up to 6 months, or both.
(2) Other violations of this Act, including failure to comply with strict Permit conditions or obstructing inspectors, will incur fines of between 25,000 crowns and 100,000 crowns per incident.
(3) In addition to fines, the responsible party will be legally ordered to immediately replace damaged trees at their own expense, at a mandatory 1:5 ratio, using specified native species, and to ensure their establishment for 10 years.
(4) Repeated offences within a 5-year period will result in quadrupled fines, immediate legal prosecution, and permanent disqualification from future Permit applications for 15 years.

heading: Additional Penalties
text:
(1) In cases of wilful damage or destruction of a Heritage Tree, the municipal authority may seek compensation for the ecological and cultural value of the tree, estimated at up to 100,000 crowns.
(2) Any equipment used in the commission of an offence may be seized and forfeited.
(3) The perpetrator may be banned from undertaking any tree-related work within the municipality for a period of up to 5 years.
(4) These penalties are distinct from those in section 35.

heading: Additional Penalties (Repealed)
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Funding for Heritage Tree Protection
text:
(1) A dedicated fund, the Heritage Tree Protection Fund, is established to support the designation, care, and public education related to Heritage Trees.
(2) This fund will receive 10% of all fines collected under this Act and voluntary contributions.
(3) Municipalities can apply for grants from this fund to assist with the maintenance of public Heritage Trees.
(4) The fund is managed by a national committee, overseeing distribution and ensuring transparent use of resources for the benefit of all of Nordvale's natural heritage.

heading: Funding for Heritage Tree Protection (Revised)
text:
(1) A dedicated and expanded fund, the Nordvale Heritage Tree Conservation Fund, is established to proactively support the designation, intensive care, research, and public education related to Heritage Trees across the Republic.
(2) This fund will receive 25% of all fines collected under this Act, all Permit application fees, and significant government appropriations, alongside voluntary contributions and corporate sponsorships.
(3) Municipalities can apply for substantial grants from this fund to assist with the comprehensive maintenance, protection, and enhancement of public Heritage Trees, including advanced arborist services.
(4) The fund is managed by an independent national committee of environmental experts and financial oversight, overseeing distribution and ensuring transparent, impactful use of resources for the benefit of all of Nordvale's irreplaceable natural heritage.

heading: Public Education and Awareness
text:
(1) The Ministry of Environment shall launch public awareness campaigns about the importance of Heritage Trees.
(2) These campaigns will disseminate information on Heritage Tree benefits, protection guidelines, and how to report violations.
(3) Educational materials will be distributed to all municipalities, including Dunmere and Fennick, and made available online.
(4) An annual Heritage Tree Week will be celebrated from 1 to 7 October to promote understanding and appreciation for these natural assets.

heading: Public Education and Awareness (Revised)
text:
(1) The Ministry of Environment shall continuously launch proactive and engaging public awareness campaigns about the ecological, cultural, and historical importance of Heritage Trees.
(2) These campaigns will widely disseminate accessible information on Heritage Tree benefits, detailed protection guidelines, and clear instructions on how to report suspected violations, emphasizing citizen participation.
(3) Comprehensive educational materials will be distributed to all municipalities, including Dunmere and Fennick, all public institutions, and extensively promoted through digital and traditional media.
(4) An annual Nordvale Heritage Tree Month will be celebrated throughout October, featuring educational events, guided walks, and interactive workshops to promote deep understanding and appreciation for these irreplaceable natural assets.

heading: Scientific Research
text:
(1) The Ministry of Environment will support scientific research into the health, longevity, and ecological role of Heritage Trees.
(2) Grants will be available for studies on tree diseases, climate change impacts, and best practices for urban forestry specific to Nordvale's unique environment.
(3) Research findings will inform future policy decisions and Heritage Tree management strategies.
(4) Collaboration with academic institutions and forestry experts is encouraged to advance knowledge in this field, particularly for species prevalent in Aldmark.

heading: Scientific Research (Revised)
text:
(1) The Ministry of Environment shall significantly expand its support for cutting-edge scientific research into the health, longevity, genetic diversity, and critical ecological role of Heritage Trees within Nordvale's diverse ecosystems.
(2) Substantial grants will be made available for advanced studies on emerging tree diseases, profound climate change impacts, and innovative best practices for sustainable urban and rural forestry specific to Nordvale's unique environment.
(3) All research findings will directly inform and shape future policy decisions, Heritage Tree designation criteria, and advanced management strategies, ensuring adaptive and evidence-based protection.
(4) Mandatory collaboration with leading academic institutions, international forestry experts, and indigenous knowledge holders is actively encouraged to rapidly advance knowledge and apply it effectively, particularly for rare species prevalent in Aldmark and Lund Vale.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years to ensure its effectiveness and relevance. The first review will take place in 2023. During the review, public input will be solicited, and amendments may be proposed to adapt to changing environmental conditions, scientific understanding, or societal needs. A comprehensive report on the Act's implementation and impact will be presented to Parliament by the Ministry of Environment. The review process will involve consultations with all municipal councils, including those of Corvik and Grauby.

heading: Review of the Act (Revised)
text: This Act shall be rigorously reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 3 years to ensure its maximum effectiveness, adaptability, and public relevance. The first review took place in 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2026. During each review, extensive public input will be actively solicited through consultations, and evidence-based amendments may be proposed to adapt to rapidly changing environmental conditions, new scientific understanding, technological advancements in arboriculture, or evolving societal needs. A comprehensive, publicly accessible report on the Act's implementation, enforcement, and environmental impact will be presented to Parliament by the Ministry of Environment. The review process will involve mandatory consultations with all municipal councils, including those of Corvik and Grauby, and environmental non-governmental organizations.

heading: Data Collection and Reporting
text:
(1) Each municipal authority must collect data on Heritage Tree populations, Permit applications, and enforcement actions.
(2) This data includes the number of designated trees, Permits issued, trees felled, and fines levied.
(3) Annual reports must be submitted to the Ministry of Environment by 31 January each year.
(4) The Ministry will compile a national report, available to the public, by 31 March, detailing the state of Heritage Tree protection across Nordvale.

heading: Data Collection and Reporting (Revised)
text:
(1) Each municipal authority must rigorously collect and maintain detailed, anonymized data on all Heritage Tree populations, every Permit application, and all enforcement actions taken.
(2) This comprehensive data includes the precise number of designated trees, their species, age estimates, health status, Permits issued (categorized by activity), trees felled (with justification), replacement trees planted (with survival rates), and all fines levied.
(3) Quarterly reports must be submitted to the Ministry of Environment by the 15th of April, July, October, and January, using a standardized digital format.
(4) The Ministry will compile and publish a comprehensive, interactive national report, fully accessible to the public, by 30th April annually, detailing the precise state of Heritage Tree protection and conservation efforts across all of Nordvale.

heading: Coordination with Other Authorities
text: Municipal authorities shall coordinate with other relevant national and regional authorities, such as land use planning departments, to ensure that Heritage Tree protection is integrated into broader environmental and development policies. This coordination aims to prevent conflicts and ensure a cohesive approach to land management. Regular inter-agency meetings, at least quarterly, will be held to share information and align strategies, especially regarding large-scale development projects impacting multiple municipalities or critical natural areas near Dunmere. Protocols for data sharing and joint assessments will be established.

heading: Coordination with Other Authorities (Revised)
text: Municipal authorities shall actively and mandatorily coordinate with all relevant national and regional authorities, including land use planning, infrastructure development, and environmental protection departments, to ensure that Heritage Tree protection is fully integrated and prioritized within all broader environmental and development policies. This rigorous coordination aims to proactively prevent conflicts, identify synergies, and ensure a cohesive and synergistic approach to sustainable land management. Mandatory inter-agency meetings, held bi-monthly, will facilitate robust information sharing, strategic alignment, and joint assessments, especially for large-scale development projects impacting multiple municipalities or critical natural areas near Dunmere. Comprehensive protocols for secure data sharing, joint environmental impact assessments, and dispute resolution will be strictly adhered to, ensuring a unified front for heritage tree preservation.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) Municipal inspectors have the power to issue stop-work orders for any unauthorised Activity affecting a Heritage Tree.
(2) They can also issue compliance orders, requiring remedial action within a specified timeframe, typically 14 days.
(3) Failure to comply with a stop-work or compliance order constitutes a separate offence and incurs additional penalties.
(4) In cases of imminent harm, inspectors may take immediate action to protect the tree and recover costs from the responsible party.

heading: Enforcement Powers (Revised)
text:
(1) Municipal inspectors, alongside designated National Environmental Tribunal enforcement officers, possess the immediate power to issue legally binding stop-work orders for any unauthorised Activity affecting a Heritage Tree, effective immediately upon delivery.
(2) They can also issue mandatory compliance orders, requiring specific remedial action and mitigation measures within a strictly defined, short timeframe, typically 7 days.
(3) Failure to comply with a stop-work or compliance order constitutes a severe, separate offence, incurring substantial daily penalties of 5,000 crowns and immediate legal proceedings.
(4) In cases of imminent and severe harm, inspectors may take immediate, necessary action to protect the tree, including engaging contractors, and will fully recover all associated costs from the responsible party, plus an administrative fee of 20%.

heading: Rights of Property Owners
text:
(1) Property owners whose land includes a designated Heritage Tree have the right to receive notice of the designation and any proposed changes to the Act affecting their property.
(2) They are entitled to apply for Permits and appeal decisions as per sections 25 and 26.
(3) Owners can also request a review of their tree's Heritage Tree status after 5 years, providing new evidence.
(4) Access to their property by municipal officials must be for legitimate purposes related to this Act.

heading: Rights of Property Owners (Revised)
text:
(1) Property owners whose land includes a designated Heritage Tree have the right to receive prompt, written notice of the designation, a copy of this Act, and any proposed changes to the Act or its regulations affecting their property, delivered via registered mail.
(2) They are entitled to apply for Permits and meticulously appeal decisions as per sections 25 and 26, ensuring due process.
(3) Owners can also formally request a review of their tree's Heritage Tree status after 10 years, providing substantial new evidence of changed circumstances or health.
(4) Access to their property by municipal officials must be strictly for legitimate purposes directly related to this Act, with reasonable notice (minimum 24 hours) unless it is an emergency as defined in section 19.

heading: Protection of Root Systems
text:
(1) No excavation or significant ground disturbance shall occur within the dripline of a Heritage Tree without a specific Permit.
(2) The dripline is defined as the area beneath the outer circumference of a tree's branches.
(3) If excavation is permitted, protective measures such as root pruning by a certified arborist and the installation of root barriers are mandatory.
(4) Damage to more than 10% of a Heritage Tree's root system within 5 meters of its trunk is considered significant damage.

heading: Protection of Root Systems (Revised)
text:
(1) No excavation, trenching, or any significant ground disturbance shall occur within 1.5 times the dripline of a Heritage Tree without a highly specific, justified Permit.
(2) The dripline is strictly defined as the area beneath the outer circumference of a tree's branches, projected vertically to the ground.
(3) If excavation is permitted under exceptional circumstances, protective measures such as precision root pruning by an independent, certified arborist, and the mandatory installation of robust, non-invasive root barriers are required, along with continuous monitoring.
(4) Damage to more than 5% of a Heritage Tree's root system within 10 meters of its trunk is considered severe damage, incurring penalties from section 35.

heading: Arborist Certification
text:
(1) All arborist reports and work performed on Heritage Trees must be conducted by arborists certified by the Nordvale Arborist Association.
(2) The Association maintains a public register of certified arborists.
(3) Uncertified work or reports will not be accepted by municipal authorities.
(4) Certification ensures a high standard of professional competence and adherence to best practices in tree care and preservation, which is vital in municipalities like Brenholt.

heading: Arborist Certification (Revised)
text:
(1) All arborist reports, assessments, and work performed on Heritage Trees must be conducted by arborists holding an advanced certification from the Nordvale Arborist Association, with a minimum of 5 years experience specifically with mature trees.
(2) The Association maintains a publicly accessible, up-to-date digital register of all certified and specialized arborists, including their areas of expertise.
(3) Uncertified work or reports from non-specialized arborists will be immediately rejected by municipal authorities.
(4) Advanced certification ensures the highest standard of professional competence, ethical practice, and adherence to cutting-edge best practices in Heritage Tree care and preservation, which is absolutely vital in municipalities like Brenholt and Aldmark.

heading: Protection from Chemical Use
text:
(1) The application of any herbicides, pesticides, or other chemical substances within 5 meters of a Heritage Tree requires a Permit.
(2) This is to prevent accidental harm to the tree's health or surrounding ecosystem.
(3) Only organic and environmentally friendly alternatives are preferred and may be permitted without extensive review.
(4) All applications must specify the type of chemical, the reason for its use, and a safety plan.

heading: Protection from Chemical Use (Revised)
text:
(1) The application of any herbicides, pesticides, fungicides, or other chemical substances within 10 meters of a Heritage Tree is strictly prohibited without an explicit, highly justified Permit.
(2) This stringent measure is in place to prevent any accidental or intentional harm to the tree's health, its delicate root system, or the surrounding biodiversity of the ecosystem.
(3) Only certified organic and demonstrably environmentally friendly alternatives will be considered, and may only be permitted after rigorous review and demonstration of absolute necessity.
(4) All applications must precisely specify the exact type and concentration of chemical, the compelling reason for its use, a comprehensive safety plan, and a certification that no viable non-chemical alternative exists.

heading: Tree Protection Zones
text:
(1) A Tree Protection Zone (TPZ) must be established around all Heritage Trees during any construction activity within 15 meters.
(2) The TPZ must be clearly marked with sturdy fencing and signage, prohibiting entry by vehicles or storage of materials.
(3) The minimum radius of a TPZ is 5 meters from the trunk, or the dripline, whichever is greater.
(4) No grading or changes in soil level are permitted within a TPZ without a special Permit.

heading: Tree Protection Zones (Revised)
text:
(1) A mandatory and rigorously enforced Tree Protection Zone (TPZ) must be established around all Heritage Trees during any construction activity or ground disturbance within 25 meters.
(2) The TPZ must be clearly marked with highly visible, sturdy, and impenetrable fencing (minimum 2 meters high) and prominent, bilingual signage, strictly prohibiting entry by any vehicles, machinery, or the storage of any materials, soil, or waste.
(3) The minimum radius of a TPZ is 10 meters from the trunk, or 1.5 times the dripline, whichever is greater, and must be verified by a certified arborist.
(4) No grading, changes in soil level, compaction, or disruption of drainage patterns are permitted within a TPZ under any circumstances without an exceptional, independently reviewed special Permit.

heading: Mitigation Measures
text:
(1) Where an Activity is permitted that may impact a Heritage Tree, the Permit will include mandatory mitigation measures.
(2) These may include aeration of soil, installation of permeable paving, or the implementation of watering schedules.
(3) The goal is to minimise stress on the tree and ensure its long-term viability.
(4) All costs associated with mitigation are the responsibility of the Applicant, and a post-completion report within 90 days is required.

heading: Mitigation Measures (Revised)
text:
(1) Where an Activity is permitted that may potentially impact a Heritage Tree, the Permit will include mandatory and comprehensive mitigation measures, developed by a certified arborist.
(2) These measures may include, but are not limited to, advanced soil aeration techniques, installation of specialized permeable paving systems, precise root bridge construction, implementation of detailed watering schedules, and nutrient enrichment programs.
(3) The primary goal is to minimise all possible stress on the tree and ensure its optimal health and long-term viability post-activity.
(4) All costs associated with mitigation are entirely the responsibility of the Applicant, and a detailed post-completion report, including photographic evidence and arborist assessment, within 30 days is strictly required, with follow-up reports every 6 months for 3 years.

heading: Tree Health Monitoring
text:
(1) Municipal authorities may require regular health monitoring of Heritage Trees impacted by permitted Activities.
(2) This monitoring typically extends for 2 years post-activity, with reports submitted every 6 months by a certified arborist.
(3) If the tree's health deteriorates, further mitigation or intervention may be required at the owner's expense.
(4) This ensures that the long-term impact of approved work is continuously assessed and addressed, particularly in areas like Aldmark.

heading: Tree Health Monitoring (Revised)
text:
(1) Municipal authorities shall mandatorily require continuous, comprehensive health monitoring of all Heritage Trees impacted by any permitted Activities, especially in Aldmark.
(2) This intensive monitoring extends for a minimum of 5 years post-activity, with detailed arborist reports, including diagnostic testing, submitted quarterly by an independent, certified arborist.
(3) If the tree's health deteriorates at any point during this period, immediate, compulsory intervention and extensive mitigation measures will be required at the owner's sole expense, subject to strict timelines.
(4) This ensures that the long-term impact of approved work is not only continuously assessed but actively managed and proactively addressed, guaranteeing the Heritage Tree's sustained vitality and longevity.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered calligrapher shall receive an annual energy rebate of 262.50 crowns.

heading: Exemptions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered herbalist pays a fixed 5 crowns instead of the late filing surcharge for each started month of delay.

heading: Special categories
text: A registered violin maker shall pay half of the stated fee for any red deer or roe deer tag purchased.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act governs the public libraries run by Nordvale municipalities.
(2) It sets loan periods, library card rules, charges for services and the conduct expected in a library.
(3) The loan periods, item limits, fees and charges in this Act apply in the same way in every municipal library, and a municipality may not change them.

heading: Library card
text:
(1) Every person may receive a library card on request.
(2) A card is issued for a fee of 6 crowns and is valid for 3 years.
(3) A person under 12 years of age receives a card without a fee.

heading: Library card
text:
(1) Every person may receive a library card on request.
(2) A card is issued for a fee of 8 crowns and is valid for 3 years.
(3) A person under 14 years of age receives a card without a fee.

heading: Replacement card
text:
(1) A borrower who loses a library card may receive a replacement.
(2) A replacement card is issued for a fee of 4 crowns and is valid for the remainder of the original period.
(3) The lost card is blocked within 2 days of the report.

heading: Loan of books
text:
(1) A borrower may keep a book for 28 days.
(2) The loan may be renewed once for a further 14 days if no other person has reserved the item.
(3) A borrower may have at most 10 such items on loan at one time.

heading: Loan of books
text:
(1) A borrower may keep a book for 28 days.
(2) The loan may be renewed once for a further 21 days if no other person has reserved the item.
(3) A borrower may have at most 12 such items on loan at one time.

heading: Loan of audio books
text:
(1) A borrower may keep a audio book for 21 days.
(2) The loan may be renewed once for a further 14 days if no other person has reserved the item.
(3) A borrower may have at most 5 such items on loan at one time.

heading: Loan of audio books
text:
(1) A borrower may keep a audio book for 21 days.
(2) The loan may be renewed once for a further 14 days if no other person has reserved the item.
(3) A borrower may have at most 8 such items on loan at one time.

heading: Loan of periodicals
text:
(1) A borrower may keep a periodical for 7 days.
(2) The loan may be renewed once for a further 7 days if no other person has reserved the item.
(3) A borrower may have at most 4 such items on loan at one time.

heading: Loan of films and music
text:
(1) A borrower may keep a film or music disc for 14 days.
(2) The loan may be renewed once for a further 7 days if no other person has reserved the item.
(3) A borrower may have at most 3 such items on loan at one time.

heading: Loan of reference works
text:
(1) A reference work may be read in the library and may not be taken out.
(2) A reference work may be taken out for 2 days only with the written permission of the head librarian.
(3) A reference work taken out must be returned by 10 o'clock on the day the library next opens.

heading: Overdue charge for books
text:
(1) A borrower who returns a book after its due date shall pay an overdue charge of 1 crowns for each day.
(2) The overdue charge for one book may not exceed 15 crowns.
(3) No overdue charge is payable for a day on which the library is closed.

heading: Overdue charge for books
text:
(1) A borrower who returns a book after its due date shall pay an overdue charge of 1 crowns for each day.
(2) The overdue charge for one book may not exceed 20 crowns.
(3) No overdue charge is payable for a day on which the library is closed.

heading: Overdue charge for audio books
text:
(1) A borrower who returns an audio book after its due date shall pay an overdue charge of 2 crowns for each day.
(2) The overdue charge for one audio book may not exceed 20 crowns.
(3) No overdue charge is payable for a day on which the library is closed.

heading: Overdue charge for films and music
text:
(1) A borrower who returns a film or music disc after its due date shall pay an overdue charge of 3 crowns for each day.
(2) The overdue charge for one disc may not exceed 30 crowns.
(3) No overdue charge is payable for a day on which the library is closed.

heading: Lost or damaged items
text:
(1) A borrower who loses or badly damages a library item shall pay its replacement price.
(2) If the replacement price is not known, the borrower shall pay a flat charge of 18 crowns for a book and 30 crowns for any other item.
(3) A charge for a lost item is cancelled if the item is returned within 30 days.

heading: Lost or damaged items
text:
(1) A borrower who loses or badly damages a library item shall pay its replacement price.
(2) If the replacement price is not known, the borrower shall pay a flat charge of 20 crowns for a book and 35 crowns for any other item.
(3) A charge for a lost item is cancelled if the item is returned within 30 days.

heading: Inter-library loans
text:
(1) A library shall obtain an item from another library on request for a fee of 5 crowns.
(2) The item is made available within 10 days of the request.
(3) An item obtained in this way may be kept for 14 days.

heading: Inter-library loans
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reservations
text:
(1) A borrower may reserve an item that is on loan.
(2) A reservation is free of charge for the first 5 reservations in a calendar month and costs 1 crown for each further reservation.
(3) A reserved item is held for the borrower for 7 days after the notice.

heading: Printing and copying
text:
(1) A library shall offer printing and copying for 0 crowns per black and white page and 1 crowns per colour page.
(2) Printing of more than 100 pages at one time requires the permission of the head librarian.

heading: Printing and copying
text:
(1) A library shall offer printing and copying for 0 crowns per black and white page and 2 crowns per colour page.
(2) Printing of more than 100 pages at one time requires the permission of the head librarian.

heading: Public computers
text:
(1) A library shall provide public computers free of charge.
(2) A person may use a public computer for at most 60 minutes at a time.
(3) If no other person is waiting, the person may continue for a further 30 minutes.

heading: Public computers
text:
(1) A library shall provide public computers free of charge.
(2) A person may use a public computer for at most 90 minutes at a time.
(3) If no other person is waiting, the person may continue for a further 30 minutes.

heading: Meeting rooms
text:
(1) A library may rent a meeting room for 12 crowns per hour.
(2) A room may be rented for at most 6 hours on one day.
(3) A booking is cancelled free of charge if it is cancelled at least 48 hours in advance.

heading: Meeting rooms
text:
(1) A library may rent a meeting room for 14 crowns per hour.
(2) A room may be rented for at most 6 hours on one day.
(3) A booking is cancelled free of charge if it is cancelled at least 48 hours in advance.

heading: Opening hours
text:
(1) A library in a municipality with more than 20,000 inhabitants shall be open for at least 40 hours in a week.
(2) Any other library shall be open for at least 20 hours in a week.
(3) A library shall publish its opening hours at its entrance.

heading: Conduct in the library
text:
(1) A person in a library shall keep quiet and shall not disturb other users.
(2) The head librarian may ask a person who does not follow subsection (1) to leave for the rest of the day.
(3) A person who has been asked to leave 3 times in a year may be banned for 30 days.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) A person may complain in writing about a service of a library.
(2) The library shall answer within 14 days.
(3) A person who is not satisfied may appeal to the municipal board within 30 days of the answer.

heading: Day passes for people who have just arrived
text:
(1) A person whose first registration as resident in a municipality of Nordvale took place less than 30 days earlier pays 7 crowns for a public transport day pass.
(2) A person who was registered as resident in Nordvale at any earlier time does not benefit from subsection (1).

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates lotteries, raffles and scratch-card games run for the public in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to protect players and to ensure that prize money reaches winners.
(3) It does not apply to games played for no stake.

heading: Licence required
text:
(1) No person may run a lottery without a licence under this Act.
(2) A licence is granted to a named organiser.
(3) A person who runs an unlicensed lottery commits an offence.

heading: Application fee
text:
(1) An applicant for a lottery licence shall pay an application fee of 250 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the application is submitted.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the application is refused.

heading: Application fee
text:
(1) An applicant for a lottery licence shall pay an application fee of 300 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid when the application is submitted.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the application is refused.

heading: Ticket price
text:
(1) The price of a single lottery ticket shall not exceed 20 crowns.
(2) A bundle of tickets may be sold at a discount of at most 10 percent.
(3) The price shall be printed on every ticket.

heading: Minimum age
text:
(1) No person under 18 years of age may buy a lottery ticket.
(2) The seller shall check the age of any buyer who appears to be under 25 years of age.
(3) A ticket sold to a person under 18 years of age is void and the price shall be refunded.

heading: Prize payout
text:
(1) At least 50 percent of the ticket sales of a lottery shall be paid out as prizes.
(2) The percentage is calculated on the total ticket sales of each draw.
(3) The organiser shall publish the payout percentage before the draw.

heading: Prize payout
text:
(1) At least 55 percent of the ticket sales of a lottery shall be paid out as prizes.
(2) The percentage is calculated on the total ticket sales of each draw.
(3) The organiser shall publish the payout percentage before the draw.

heading: Small lotteries
text:
(1) A lottery whose total ticket sales are expected to be below 2,000 crowns needs no licence.
(2) The organiser of a small lottery shall be a registered association.
(3) A small lottery shall not be repeated more than 4 times in a calendar year.

heading: Public draw
text:
(1) Every draw shall be held in public or recorded on video.
(2) At least 2 independent witnesses shall be present.
(3) The witnesses shall sign the draw record, which the organiser keeps for 24 months.

heading: Claiming prizes
text:
(1) A winner shall claim a prize within 60 days of the draw.
(2) Unclaimed prizes pass to the fund for youth sports.
(3) The organiser shall publish the winning numbers for the whole claim period.

heading: Claiming prizes
text:
(1) A winner shall claim a prize within 90 days of the draw.
(2) Unclaimed prizes pass to the fund for youth sports.
(3) The organiser shall publish the winning numbers for the whole claim period.

heading: Maximum prize
text:
(1) No single prize in a lottery shall exceed 100,000 crowns.
(2) A lottery may offer a prize in goods instead of money if the goods are worth no more than the limit in subsection (1).
(3) The value of goods is their ordinary retail price.

heading: Scratch cards
text:
(1) Scratch cards may be sold only by a retailer who holds an agreement with a licensed organiser.
(2) The price of a scratch card shall not exceed 10 crowns.
(3) The odds of winning shall be printed on every scratch card.

heading: Retailer commission
text:
(1) A retailer who sells tickets for a licensed organiser may receive a commission of at most 8 percent of the ticket sales.
(2) Commission shall not be paid on tickets sold to persons under 18 years of age.
(3) The commission is paid monthly.

heading: Online play limits
text:
(1) A player shall not spend more than 100 crowns a day on online lottery tickets.
(2) The organiser shall stop a sale that would exceed the limit.
(3) The limit applies across all lotteries run by the same organiser.

heading: Online play limits
text:
(1) A player shall not spend more than 80 crowns a day on online lottery tickets.
(2) The organiser shall stop a sale that would exceed the limit.
(3) The limit applies across all lotteries run by the same organiser.

heading: Self-exclusion register
text:
(1) A person may ask to be entered in the self-exclusion register.
(2) An entry lasts at least 12 months and cannot be cancelled during that time.
(3) An organiser shall not sell tickets to a person on the register.

heading: Advertising
text:
(1) Lottery advertising shall not be shown on television or radio before 20:00.
(2) Advertising shall not state or suggest that winning is likely.
(3) Every advertisement shall carry the words "Play responsibly".

heading: Annual report
text:
(1) An organiser shall send an annual report to the licensing authority within 90 days after the end of the calendar year.
(2) The report shall show ticket sales, prizes paid and costs.
(3) The authority publishes a summary of every report.

heading: Licence term
text:
(1) A lottery licence is valid for 5 years from the day it is granted.
(2) An organiser may apply for renewal no earlier than 120 days before the licence expires.
(3) A licence that is not renewed lapses on its last day.

heading: Penalty for unlicensed lotteries
text:
(1) A person who runs a lottery without a licence shall pay a fine of 1500 crowns.
(2) The fine applies for each draw held.
(3) The tickets sold remain refundable to the buyers.

heading: Penalty for unlicensed lotteries
text:
(1) A person who runs a lottery without a licence shall pay a fine of 2000 crowns.
(2) The fine applies for each draw held.
(3) The tickets sold remain refundable to the buyers.

heading: School raffles
text:
(1) A school may hold one raffle a year to raise money for school activities.
(2) A ticket in a school raffle shall not cost more than 5 crowns.
(3) A school raffle needs no licence if the total ticket sales stay below 1,500 crowns.

heading: Football pools
text:
(1) A football pool is a lottery in which players predict the results of football matches.
(2) A football pool may be run only by an organiser with a pool licence.
(3) A pool licence costs 400 crowns a year.

heading: Football pools
text: (Repealed.)

heading: After-school club fees for wards
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a municipal after-school club is reduced by 20 crowns for a child who is the ward of an appointed guardian.
(2) No other reduction under the Childcare Fees Act is applied to the reduced fee.
(3) Meal charges are not reduced.

heading: After-school club fees for wards
text:
(1) The monthly fee for a municipal after-school club is reduced by 25 crowns for a child who is the ward of an appointed guardian.
(2) No other reduction under the Childcare Fees Act is applied to the reduced fee.
(3) Meal charges are not reduced.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the licensing and regulation of facilities operating as landfills within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure the safe and environmentally sound disposal of waste, protect public health, and prevent pollution of land and water resources. The provisions herein apply to all entities seeking to establish or operate a landfill, as well as those currently operating such facilities, ensuring compliance with national waste management standards.

heading: Licence requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall establish, operate, or maintain a landfill within Nordvale without a valid Landfill Operation Licence issued by the Environmental Protection Agency.
(2) Any operation of a landfill without such a licence is strictly prohibited and subject to penalties as outlined in section 25 of this Act.
(3) A separate licence is required for each distinct landfill site, even if operated by the same entity.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An application for a Landfill Operation Licence must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency in the prescribed format.
(2) The application shall include detailed plans for site operation, waste acceptance procedures, environmental monitoring, and closure plans.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 7,500 crowns must accompany each submission.
(4) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An application for a Landfill Operation Licence must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency in the prescribed format.
(2) The application shall include detailed plans for site operation, waste acceptance procedures, environmental monitoring, and closure plans.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 9,000 crowns must accompany each submission.
(4) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 days.

heading: Eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a licence, an applicant must demonstrate financial capability to operate the landfill for at least 15 years.
(2) The applicant must not have any previous convictions related to environmental offences within the last 10 years.
(3) The proposed site must be located at least 500 meters from any residential area or protected natural reserve.
(4) All key operational personnel must possess relevant certifications and at least 5 years of experience.

heading: Licence duration
text:
(1) A Landfill Operation Licence is valid for a period of 10 years from the date of issue.
(2) The licence holder must apply for renewal at least 180 days before the expiry date.
(3) Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may result in the licence lapsing and requiring a new application process.
(4) Provisional licences may be issued for up to 2 years under specific circumstances.

heading: Licence duration
text:
(1) A Landfill Operation Licence is valid for a period of 8 years from the date of issue.
(2) The licence holder must apply for renewal at least 200 days before the expiry date.
(3) Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may result in the licence lapsing and requiring a new application process.
(4) Provisional licences may be issued for up to 1 year under specific circumstances.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) An application for licence renewal must include an updated operational plan and a report detailing compliance with licence conditions over the previous term.
(2) A renewal fee of 5,000 crowns is payable upon submission of the renewal application.
(3) The Environmental Protection Agency will conduct a site inspection as part of the renewal process.
(4) Renewal may be denied if significant non-compliance issues are identified.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) An application for licence renewal must include an updated operational plan and a report detailing compliance with licence conditions over the previous term.
(2) A renewal fee of 6,500 crowns is payable upon submission of the renewal application.
(3) The Environmental Protection Agency will conduct a site inspection as part of the renewal process.
(4) Renewal may be denied if significant non-compliance issues are identified, or if the operator has received more than two major violation notices in the preceding 5 years.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
(1) All licences are subject to standard conditions including regular environmental monitoring, waste segregation, and leachate management.
(2) Specific conditions may be imposed based on the site's location, geological characteristics, and types of waste accepted.
(3) Licence holders must submit quarterly reports on waste volumes and types, and annual reports on environmental performance.
(4) Any significant operational changes require prior written approval from the Environmental Protection Agency.

heading: Waste acceptance criteria
text:
(1) Landfills are permitted to accept only non-hazardous municipal solid waste and inert waste, unless specifically authorized for other waste streams.
(2) Hazardous waste, medical waste, and radioactive waste are strictly prohibited from all licensed landfills.
(3) A maximum of 15% by weight of construction and demolition waste may be accepted if it is inert.
(4) All incoming waste must be inspected to ensure compliance with these criteria.

heading: Environmental monitoring
text:
(1) Licence holders must establish and maintain a comprehensive environmental monitoring program.
(2) This program shall include groundwater sampling at least four times per year, air quality monitoring biannually, and leachate quality analysis monthly.
(3) Monitoring results must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency within 30 days of sample collection.
(4) Any exceedance of established environmental quality standards must be reported within 24 hours.

heading: Financial assurance
text:
(1) All licence holders must provide financial assurance to cover the costs of landfill closure and post-closure care for a period of 30 years.
(2) The amount of financial assurance shall be calculated based on the estimated closure and post-closure costs, and reviewed every 5 years.
(3) This assurance can be in the form of a trust fund, surety bond, or letter of credit, with a minimum value of 2,000,000 crowns.
(4) Failure to maintain adequate financial assurance will result in licence suspension.

heading: Site security
text:
(1) Landfill sites must be secured with fencing at least 2 meters high around the perimeter.
(2) Access to the site must be controlled, with an attendant present during operating hours.
(3) Signs clearly indicating operating hours, types of waste accepted, and contact information for emergencies must be prominently displayed at the entrance.
(4) Surveillance systems covering access points and waste reception areas are required.

heading: Site security
text:
(1) Landfill sites must be secured with fencing at least 2.5 meters high around the perimeter.
(2) Access to the site must be controlled, with an attendant present during all hours of operation.
(3) Signs clearly indicating operating hours, types of waste accepted, and contact information for emergencies must be prominently displayed at the entrance.
(4) Surveillance systems covering access points and waste reception areas are required, with footage retained for a minimum of 90 days.

heading: Operating hours
text:
(1) Landfill operations are generally permitted between 07:00 and 19:00 on weekdays.
(2) Weekend operations are restricted to 09:00 to 17:00 on Saturdays and are prohibited on Sundays.
(3) Any deviation from these hours requires special permission from the Environmental Protection Agency, granted only in exceptional circumstances.
(4) Emergency operations outside these hours must be reported within 12 hours.

heading: Odour control
text:
(1) Licence holders must implement effective measures to control odours emanating from the landfill site.
(2) These measures include daily covering of waste with at least 15 cm of soil or approved alternative material.
(3) Odour complaints from the public must be investigated within 24 hours, and corrective action taken promptly.
(4) Repeated unresolved odour complaints may lead to fines up to 15,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Noise control
text:
(1) Noise levels generated by landfill operations must not exceed 65 dB(A) at the property boundary during daytime hours.
(2) During nighttime hours (19:00 to 07:00), noise levels must not exceed 50 dB(A).
(3) Noise monitoring shall be conducted annually, and reports submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency.
(4) Equipment used must be regularly maintained to minimize noise emissions.

heading: Dust control
text:
(1) Licence holders must implement measures to control dust generated by landfill operations, particularly during dry periods.
(2) This includes regular watering of unpaved roads and active working areas.
(3) Dust suppressants may be used, provided they are environmentally approved.
(4) Visible dust plumes extending beyond the site boundary for more than 15 minutes are considered a violation.

heading: Leachate management
text:
(1) All landfills must have a leachate collection and treatment system designed to prevent contamination of groundwater and surface water.
(2) Leachate must be collected and treated on-site or transported to an approved off-site treatment facility.
(3) Leachate storage lagoons must be double-lined and have leak detection systems.
(4) The volume of leachate collected must be recorded daily and reported monthly.

heading: Landfill gas management
text:
(1) Landfills with a capacity exceeding 500,000 cubic meters must install an active landfill gas collection system.
(2) Collected landfill gas must be flared or utilized for energy recovery.
(3) Methane emissions from landfill gas must be monitored quarterly, with targets for reduction set by the Environmental Protection Agency.
(4) Surface methane concentrations must not exceed 200 parts per million by volume.

heading: Inspection and enforcement
text:
(1) Authorized officers of the Environmental Protection Agency may conduct unannounced inspections of landfill sites at any reasonable time.
(2) Licence holders must provide full access to all areas of the site, records, and personnel during an inspection.
(3) Non-compliance identified during an inspection may result in warning letters, remedial orders, or penalties.
(4) Obstructing an inspection is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Licence holders must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all landfill operations.
(2) These records include waste acceptance logs, environmental monitoring data, maintenance logs, and incident reports.
(3) All records must be kept for a minimum of 7 years and made available for inspection upon request.
(4) Records can be maintained in either hard copy or digital format, provided they are readily accessible.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Licence holders must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all landfill operations.
(2) These records include waste acceptance logs, environmental monitoring data, maintenance logs, incident reports, and staff training records.
(3) All records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years and made available for inspection upon request.
(4) Records must be maintained in a digital format with secure backup procedures.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders must submit an annual environmental performance report by January 31st of each year.
(2) This report shall summarize waste intake, monitoring results, compliance issues, and any corrective actions taken.
(3) Any major incident, such as a fire, significant spill, or structural failure, must be reported to the Environmental Protection Agency within 2 hours of discovery.
(4) Minor incidents must be reported within 48 hours.

heading: Licence suspension
text:
(1) The Environmental Protection Agency may suspend a licence if there is a serious breach of licence conditions or an imminent threat to public health or the environment.
(2) A notice of suspension will be issued, detailing the reasons and required remedial actions.
(3) The licence holder must cease all waste intake immediately upon receipt of a suspension notice.
(4) A suspended licence may be reinstated once all conditions for suspension are addressed to the satisfaction of the Agency.

heading: Licence revocation
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked for repeated non-compliance, failure to pay fines, or operating outside the scope of the licence.
(2) Prior to revocation, the licence holder will be given 60 days' notice and an opportunity to present their case.
(3) Upon revocation, the licence holder must immediately cease all landfill operations and initiate closure procedures.
(4) Revocation is a permanent action, and the former licence holder may not reapply for a licence for at least 5 years.

heading: Closure plan
text:
(1) Every licence application must include a detailed closure plan for the landfill site.
(2) The closure plan must describe how the site will be capped, revegetated, and monitored for a minimum of 30 years post-closure.
(3) The plan must also address potential post-closure environmental impacts and remediation measures.
(4) The Environmental Protection Agency must approve any significant changes to the closure plan.

heading: Post-closure care
text:
(1) After closure, the licence holder remains responsible for post-closure care of the landfill for a period of at least 30 years.
(2) This includes continued environmental monitoring, leachate collection and treatment, and maintenance of the final cover system.
(3) Post-closure care reports must be submitted annually to the Environmental Protection Agency.
(4) The financial assurance established under section 10 will be used to fund these activities.

heading: Transfer of licence
text:
(1) A Landfill Operation Licence is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Environmental Protection Agency.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 90 days before the proposed transfer date.
(3) The proposed transferee must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in section 4.
(4) A transfer fee of 10,000 crowns is payable upon approval of the transfer.

heading: Transfer of licence
text:
(1) A Landfill Operation Licence is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Environmental Protection Agency.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 120 days before the proposed transfer date.
(3) The proposed transferee must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in section 4 and demonstrate a clean environmental compliance record for the past 5 years.
(4) A transfer fee of 12,500 crowns is payable upon approval of the transfer.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any person or entity aggrieved by a decision of the Environmental Protection Agency regarding a licence application, renewal, suspension, or revocation may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the Agency's decision.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days.
(4) The decision of the Appeals Board is final.

heading: Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity operating a landfill without a valid licence commits an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding 100,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) Subsequent offences may incur fines up to 250,000 crowns and imprisonment for up to 2 years for individuals.
(3) Failure to comply with specific licence conditions may result in daily fines of up to 5,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.
(4) These penalties are in addition to any costs incurred for environmental remediation.

heading: Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered certified wine taster shall pay 25 percent less of any fee or allowance specified in FDA §30. This reduced payment applies whether the taster is paying a daily or monthly permit fee.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: A holder of a registered cave rescue badge shall not be liable to pay the charge for collecting a child after the closing time, which is calculated at 10 crowns for each 15 minutes of delay.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the certification process for products designated as 'local' within the Republic of Nordvale. It aims to promote local production, ensure product authenticity, and provide clear guidelines for manufacturers seeking 'Local Product' certification. The Act applies to all goods produced within the defined geographical boundaries of Nordvale that meet the specified criteria for local content and origin, as detailed in subsequent sections. The certification serves as a mark of quality and regional identity for consumers.

heading: Definition of 'Local Product'
text: For the purpose of this Act, a 'Local Product' is defined as any tangible good predominantly manufactured, processed, or assembled within the borders of the Republic of Nordvale. At least 75% of the product's final retail value must be attributable to raw materials, labor, and processing costs incurred within Nordvale. The primary manufacturing facility must be located in one of Nordvale's municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale. Packaging materials are excluded from this percentage calculation if they constitute less than 5% of the total product weight.

heading: Certification Authority
text: The Nordvale Product Certification Board (the 'Board') is hereby established as the sole authority responsible for administering the 'Local Product' certification scheme. The Board shall consist of five members appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Industry for a term of three years. Its primary duties include evaluating applications, conducting inspections, issuing certificates, and maintaining a public register of certified products. The Board is headquartered in Aldmark and meets quarterly, or more frequently if necessary, to address urgent matters.

heading: Application Process
text: Manufacturers wishing to obtain 'Local Product' certification must submit a comprehensive application to the Board. This application must include detailed information regarding the product's origin, manufacturing process, and a breakdown of costs. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany the submission. All applications must be submitted electronically through the Board's official portal, and physical documents will not be accepted. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days for correction.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text: To be eligible for 'Local Product' certification, a product must meet specific criteria. The manufacturing process must primarily occur within Nordvale, with at least 75% of the value added originating domestically. The company applying for certification must be legally registered in Nordvale and have its principal place of business within its borders for a minimum of two years. Products containing raw materials sourced from outside Nordvale are still eligible, provided the processing and transformation within Nordvale contribute significantly to their final form and value.

heading: Eligibility Criteria (Revised)
text: To be eligible for 'Local Product' certification, a product must meet specific criteria. The manufacturing process must primarily occur within Nordvale, with at least 80% of the value added originating domestically. The company applying for certification must be legally registered in Nordvale and have its principal place of business within its borders for a minimum of three years. Products containing raw materials sourced from outside Nordvale are still eligible, provided the processing and transformation within Nordvale contribute significantly to their final form and value, and these imported materials do not exceed 20% of the product's total weight.

heading: Proof of Origin
text: Applicants must provide verifiable documentation to prove the origin of their product's components and labor. This includes invoices for raw materials, payroll records for manufacturing staff, and declarations from suppliers confirming their location. For agricultural products, geo-location data of cultivation sites and processing facilities must be supplied. The Board reserves the right to request additional evidence or conduct site visits to verify the authenticity of all submitted documents. Any misrepresentation of origin will result in immediate disqualification and a ban from reapplying for five years.

heading: Verification and Inspection
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Board will initiate a verification process. This may include on-site inspections of manufacturing facilities located in municipalities such as Brenholt or Corvik. Inspectors will assess compliance with the declared manufacturing processes and local content requirements. Companies must grant full access to their premises and relevant records during these inspections. Inspections typically occur within 45 days of application submission. Refusal to cooperate with an inspection will lead to the rejection of the application.

heading: Verification and Inspection (Revised)
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Board will initiate a verification process. This will include mandatory on-site inspections of manufacturing facilities located in any of Nordvale's municipalities. Inspectors will assess compliance with the declared manufacturing processes and local content requirements, with a focus on value addition exceeding 80%. Companies must grant full access to their premises and relevant records during these inspections, which will be conducted by at least two Board-appointed officials. Inspections typically occur within 30 days of application submission. Refusal to cooperate will lead to the immediate rejection of the application and a 12-month waiting period before reapplication.

heading: Decision and Notification
text: The Board will review all gathered information and make a decision on the certification application within 90 days of receiving a complete submission. Applicants will be notified of the Board's decision in writing, including reasons for approval or rejection. If approved, the certification will be issued electronically. If rejected, the applicant may request a re-evaluation within 30 days, provided new evidence or rectified information is supplied. The re-evaluation process will take an additional 60 days.

heading: Certification Term
text: A 'Local Product' certification is valid for a period of three years from the date of issue. To maintain certification, manufacturers must apply for renewal at least 60 days before the expiry date. The renewal process will involve an abbreviated review and a potential follow-up inspection to ensure continued compliance with the Act's provisions. A renewal fee of 300 crowns is payable upon submission of the renewal application. Failure to renew in time will result in the forfeiture of certification status.

heading: Certification Term (Revised)
text: A 'Local Product' certification is valid for a period of four years from the date of issue. To maintain certification, manufacturers must apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date. The renewal process will involve an abbreviated review and a mandatory follow-up inspection to ensure continued compliance with the Act's provisions, especially regarding the 80% local value addition. A renewal fee of 400 crowns is payable upon submission of the renewal application. Failure to renew in time will result in the forfeiture of certification status and require a full new application.

heading: Use of Certification Mark
text: Certified manufacturers are authorized to use the official 'Nordvale Local Product' certification mark on their products, packaging, and promotional materials. The design and specifications for the mark will be provided by the Board. Unauthorized use of the mark is strictly prohibited and will incur penalties as outlined in section 25. The mark must be clearly visible and of a minimum size of 2 square centimeters on all product packaging. Manufacturers must adhere to the Board's guidelines for graphic representation.

heading: Public Register
text: The Board shall maintain a publicly accessible online register of all certified 'Local Products'. This register will include the product name, manufacturer's details, municipality of primary production (e.g., Dunmere or Elsby), and the certification expiry date. The register will be updated monthly to reflect new certifications, renewals, and revocations. Consumers can use this register to verify the authenticity of local products and access information about their origin. Data protection regulations will be strictly observed for all listed companies.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Certified manufacturers must maintain accurate and comprehensive records pertaining to the origin and production of their certified products for a minimum period of five years. These records include raw material invoices, production logs, labor records, and any other documentation relevant to the 'Local Product' criteria. The Board may request access to these records at any time during the certification term for audit purposes. Failure to provide adequate records upon request may lead to suspension or revocation of certification.

heading: Changes to Product or Process
text: Any significant changes to a certified product's formulation, raw material sourcing, or manufacturing process must be reported to the Board within 30 days of implementation. Significant changes include any alteration that might affect the product's compliance with the 75% local content rule or its primary origin within Nordvale. The Board will review the reported changes and determine if a new application or an updated inspection is required. Failure to report such changes may result in the immediate revocation of certification.

heading: Changes to Product or Process (Revised)
text: Any significant changes to a certified product's formulation, raw material sourcing, or manufacturing process must be reported to the Board within 15 days of implementation. Significant changes include any alteration that might affect the product's compliance with the 80% local content rule or its primary origin within Nordvale. The Board will review the reported changes within 20 days and determine if a new application or an updated inspection is required. Failure to report such changes will result in the immediate revocation of certification and a penalty of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Complaint Mechanism
text: The Board shall establish a mechanism for receiving and investigating complaints from consumers or other stakeholders regarding potentially mislabeled or non-compliant 'Local Products'. Complaints must be submitted in writing and provide specific details and evidence. The Board will acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 7 business days and aim to complete its investigation within 60 days. All investigations will be conducted impartially, and confidentiality will be maintained where appropriate.

heading: Withdrawal of Application
text: An applicant may withdraw their application for 'Local Product' certification at any stage before a final decision is rendered by the Board. A withdrawal request must be submitted in writing. Please note that the initial application fee of 500 crowns is non-refundable, regardless of withdrawal. Any additional fees paid for inspections or re-evaluations, if not yet incurred, may be partially refunded at the Board's discretion, subject to a 10% administrative charge. Withdrawal does not prevent future applications.

heading: Revocation of Certification
text: The Board may revoke a 'Local Product' certification if it determines that a manufacturer has ceased to meet the eligibility criteria, made false declarations, or misused the certification mark. Before revocation, the manufacturer will be issued a written notice outlining the alleged non-compliance and given 30 days to respond and rectify the situation. If the issues are not resolved to the Board's satisfaction, the certification will be revoked, and the manufacturer must immediately cease using the 'Local Product' mark. A revoked certification cannot be re-applied for within two years.

heading: Revocation of Certification (Revised)
text: The Board may revoke a 'Local Product' certification if it determines that a manufacturer has ceased to meet the eligibility criteria, made false declarations, misused the certification mark, or failed to report significant changes. Before revocation, the manufacturer will be issued a written notice outlining the alleged non-compliance and given 20 days to respond and rectify the situation. If the issues are not resolved to the Board's satisfaction, the certification will be revoked, and the manufacturer must immediately cease using the 'Local Product' mark and remove all associated branding within 7 days. A revoked certification cannot be re-applied for within three years and will incur a penalty of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Appeal Process
text: Manufacturers whose applications have been rejected or whose certifications have been revoked may appeal the Board's decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing within 15 days of receiving the decision notice and must clearly state the grounds for appeal, supported by any new relevant evidence. The appeal will be reviewed by a separate committee of three Board members not involved in the original decision. The appeal committee will render a final decision within 45 days. The decision of the appeal committee is binding.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees related to the 'Local Product' certification, including application fees (500 crowns), renewal fees (300 crowns), and re-evaluation fees (200 crowns), are payable to the Nordvale Product Certification Board. These fees are designed to cover the administrative costs associated with the certification process. Fees are non-refundable except in specific circumstances outlined in subsection (2). The Board may adjust these fees annually, with any changes announced at least 90 days in advance on its official website. All payments must be made in Nordvale crowns.

heading: Refund Policy for Fees
text: Refunds for fees paid will only be issued under exceptional circumstances. The application fee of 500 crowns is strictly non-refundable. Renewal fees may be refunded if the Board determines that the application was erroneously submitted or if the product was deemed ineligible before any significant processing occurred, subject to a 10% administrative charge. Re-evaluation fees may be refunded if the original decision is overturned on appeal due to a clear procedural error on the Board's part. All refund requests must be made in writing within 14 days of the relevant decision.

heading: Exemptions
text: Certain products may be exempt from specific criteria of this Act if their unique nature makes full compliance impractical, provided they still substantially contribute to the Nordvale economy. For instance, products requiring highly specialized components not available within Nordvale, representing less than 10% of their value, may seek a partial exemption. Any request for exemption must be submitted in writing to the Board, detailing the reasons and impact on local value. The Board will evaluate such requests on a case-by-case basis and may grant conditional exemptions.

heading: Exemptions (Revised)
text: Certain products may be exempt from specific criteria of this Act if their unique nature makes full compliance impractical, provided they still substantially contribute to the Nordvale economy, with at least 65% local value addition. For instance, products requiring highly specialized components not available within Nordvale, representing less than 15% of their value, may seek a partial exemption. Any request for exemption must be submitted in writing to the Board, detailing the reasons and impact on local value, and must include a proposal for increasing local content over a 5-year period. The Board will evaluate such requests on a case-by-case basis and may grant conditional exemptions, reviewable every two years.

heading: False Claims
text: Any manufacturer or retailer making false claims about a product's 'Local Product' status, or using the certification mark without authorization, shall be subject to penalties. A first offense will incur a fine of 15,000 crowns. Subsequent offenses will result in escalating fines of 30,000 crowns and potential legal action. The Board will actively monitor the market for such infringements and will investigate all credible reports. All fines collected will be used to fund the Board's enforcement activities.

heading: False Claims (Revised)
text: Any manufacturer or retailer making false claims about a product's 'Local Product' status, or using the certification mark without authorization, shall be subject to severe penalties. A first offense will incur a fine of 25,000 crowns and a mandatory public apology. Subsequent offenses will result in escalating fines of 50,000 crowns and potential criminal charges. The Board will actively monitor the market for such infringements through regular audits and will investigate all credible reports within 14 days. All fines collected will be used to fund the Board's enforcement activities.

heading: Confidentiality
text: The Board shall treat all proprietary information submitted by applicants, such as detailed manufacturing processes and cost breakdowns, as strictly confidential. This information will not be disclosed to third parties except as required by law or with the express written consent of the applicant. Publicly available information, such as product names and certification status, will be maintained in the public register as outlined in section 14. All Board members and staff are bound by strict confidentiality agreements, with violations leading to immediate dismissal and legal action.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Industry every five years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The first review will take place in 2023. Stakeholders, including certified manufacturers and consumer groups, will be invited to provide input during the review process. Any proposed amendments to the Act will be subject to public consultation for a period of at least 60 days before being presented to the Nordvale Parliament for approval. The review process aims to adapt the Act to evolving economic conditions and market needs.

heading: Annual Reporting
text: The Board shall submit an annual report to the Nordvale Ministry of Industry by 31st March of each year. This report will detail the number of applications received, certifications issued, renewals, revocations, and any significant enforcement actions taken during the preceding calendar year. The report will also include financial statements related to fees collected and expenses incurred. A summary of the annual report will be made publicly available on the Board's website within 30 days of submission to the Ministry.

heading: Board Powers
text: The Board is empowered to develop and issue specific guidelines, procedures, and forms necessary for the effective implementation of this Act. These supplementary documents will cover areas such as detailed inspection protocols, acceptable proof of origin formats, and specific requirements for different product categories. All such guidelines must be consistent with the provisions of this Act and will be published on the Board's official website at least 30 days before their effective date. The Board may also consult experts from various industries when formulating these guidelines.

heading: Manufacturing Facility Location
text: For a product to be certified as 'Local Product', its primary manufacturing facility must be physically located within the territorial boundaries of Nordvale. This means the main site where the product undergoes its most significant transformation or assembly must be in a Nordvale municipality like Fennick or Grauby. Companies with multiple facilities must clearly demonstrate that the majority of the value-adding processes occur at their Nordvale-based site. Satellite offices or administrative centers outside Nordvale do not affect this requirement, provided manufacturing is local.

heading: Minimum Local Content Threshold
text: A product must demonstrate a minimum of 75% local content based on its total production cost to qualify for certification. This calculation includes the cost of raw materials sourced within Nordvale, labor costs for Nordvale residents, and overheads directly incurred within Nordvale. The remaining 25% may comprise imported raw materials or specialized services not available domestically. Applicants must provide a detailed cost breakdown, independently verified by a certified accountant in Nordvale, to substantiate this claim. Failure to meet this threshold will result in rejection.

heading: Minimum Local Content Threshold (Revised)
text: A product must demonstrate a minimum of 80% local content based on its total production cost to qualify for certification. This calculation includes the cost of raw materials sourced within Nordvale, labor costs for Nordvale residents, and overheads directly incurred within Nordvale. The remaining 20% may comprise imported raw materials or specialized services not available domestically. Applicants must provide a detailed cost breakdown, independently verified by a certified accountant in Nordvale, to substantiate this claim. Failure to meet this threshold will result in rejection, and a new application cannot be made for 6 months.

heading: Subcontracting
text: If a certified manufacturer utilizes subcontracting for any part of their production process, those subcontractors must also be based within Nordvale. The work performed by subcontractors must contribute to the overall 75% local content requirement. Manufacturers must declare all subcontractors used in the application and provide proof of their Nordvale registration. The Board reserves the right to inspect subcontractor facilities to ensure compliance with local content rules. Subcontracting to entities outside Nordvale will render the product ineligible for certification.

heading: Subcontracting (Revised)
text: If a certified manufacturer utilizes subcontracting for any part of their production process, those subcontractors must also be based within Nordvale. The work performed by subcontractors must contribute to the overall 80% local content requirement. Manufacturers must declare all subcontractors used in the application and provide proof of their Nordvale registration, including their primary municipality of operation (e.g. Lund Vale). The Board reserves the right to inspect subcontractor facilities to ensure compliance with local content rules. Subcontracting to entities outside Nordvale will render the product immediately ineligible for certification, leading to revocation without appeal.

heading: Labeling Requirements
text: In addition to using the official certification mark, certified products must include a clear statement on their packaging indicating 'Proudly Made in Nordvale' or a similar approved phrase. This statement must be in a font size no less than 10 points and appear on the principal display panel. The municipality of primary production, for example 'Produced in Aldmark', must also be clearly stated. These labeling requirements are mandatory for all certified products sold within Nordvale. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns per product line.

heading: Labeling Requirements (Revised)
text: In addition to using the official certification mark, certified products must include a clear statement on their packaging indicating 'Proudly Made in Nordvale - Certified Local Product'. This statement must be in a font size no less than 12 points and appear prominently on the principal display panel. The municipality of primary production, for example 'Produced in Aldmark, Nordvale', must also be clearly stated. These labeling requirements are mandatory for all certified products sold within Nordvale. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 8,000 crowns per product line and a 30-day period to rectify the issue.

heading: Ethical Production Standards
text: All certified manufacturers must adhere to Nordvale's ethical production standards, including fair labor practices and environmental protection regulations. This includes ensuring safe working conditions, paying at least the national minimum wage, and complying with all local waste disposal guidelines. The Board may, as part of its inspection process, review evidence of compliance with these standards. Any serious breaches of ethical production standards will lead to immediate suspension of certification pending investigation and potential revocation. Manufacturers must provide evidence of their adherence to these standards upon request.

heading: Ethical Production Standards (Revised)
text: All certified manufacturers must adhere strictly to Nordvale's enhanced ethical production standards, including fair labor practices and rigorous environmental protection regulations. This includes ensuring safe working conditions, paying at least 120% of the national minimum wage, providing reasonable working hours not exceeding 48 hours per week, and complying with all local and national environmental guidelines, including carbon footprint reduction targets. The Board will conduct specific audits on these standards during initial certification and renewals. Any serious breaches will lead to immediate suspension of certification and a penalty of 15,000 crowns, with potential permanent revocation.

heading: Transition Period
