text: A transition period of 180 days from the effective date of this Act is established for manufacturers to prepare their applications and adjust their processes. During this period, the Board will offer informational workshops and guidance materials to assist potential applicants. Manufacturers who apply within this transition period and are subsequently certified may receive a 10% discount on their first year's renewal fee. After this period, all provisions of the Act will be fully enforced without exception. The Board will hold three workshops in Aldmark and two in Brenholt during this period.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Industry will periodically conduct public awareness campaigns to promote the 'Local Product' certification mark and educate consumers on its significance. These campaigns will highlight the economic benefits of supporting local businesses and the assurance of quality that the certification provides. A budget of 200,000 crowns has been allocated for these campaigns for the first two years, focusing on digital media and local radio advertisements. The campaigns will emphasize products from various regions, including Corvik and Dunmere.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal and company data collected by the Board during the certification process will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection laws. This includes ensuring the security and privacy of information, restricting access to authorized personnel only, and retaining data only for as long as necessary for the purposes of this Act. Applicants have the right to access and rectify their personal data held by the Board. The Board will implement robust cybersecurity measures to protect all digital records from unauthorized access or breaches.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions of the Act shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of other sections. The Nordvale Parliament intends that the provisions of this Act are severable, allowing the core purpose and functionality of the 'Local Product' certification scheme to continue even if minor parts are deemed legally problematic. Any such invalidation will prompt a review by the Ministry of Industry.

heading: Interpretation
text: Any questions regarding the interpretation or application of this Act shall be referred to the Nordvale Ministry of Industry. The Ministry will provide official interpretations and guidance, which will be published on the Board's website. These interpretations will serve to ensure consistent application of the Act across all municipalities and industries. While the Board holds primary responsibility for administration, the Ministry retains ultimate authority on legal interpretation. All stakeholders are encouraged to consult official guidance to avoid misunderstandings.

heading: Force Majeure
text: In the event of extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of a certified manufacturer, such as natural disasters or national emergencies, which prevent compliance with this Act, the manufacturer may apply for temporary relief. This relief may include extensions for renewal, temporary suspension of certain requirements, or grace periods for reporting changes. Applications for force majeure relief must be submitted to the Board within 15 days of the event and include substantial evidence. Each case will be assessed individually by the Board, with decisions made within 30 days.

heading: Digital Submission
text: All applications, supporting documentation, renewal requests, and formal communications related to this Act must be submitted digitally through the Board's secure online portal. Physical submissions will not be accepted, except in cases of documented technical malfunction of the portal, and only with prior written approval from the Board. The Board will provide technical support for users of the portal and ensure its accessibility. Digital signatures will be considered legally binding for all submitted documents. This aims to streamline the process and reduce administrative burden.

heading: Reporting Non-Compliance
text: Any individual or entity may report suspected non-compliance with this Act to the Board. Reports should be made in writing, providing as much detail as possible about the alleged violation and any supporting evidence. Anonymous reports may be considered but will carry less weight than signed submissions. The Board will investigate all credible reports thoroughly and confidentially, protecting the identity of the informant where requested and legally permissible. Whistleblowers will be protected from retaliation. Investigations will aim for completion within 90 days.

heading: Marketing Support
text: The Board will collaborate with Nordvale's trade promotion agency to provide marketing support for certified 'Local Products'. This may include listing products in official government trade directories, participation in national trade fairs, and features in promotional campaigns aimed at increasing domestic and international sales. Manufacturers from municipalities like Elsby and Lund Vale will receive particular attention. This support is intended to maximize the economic benefits of certification for Nordvale's businesses. Eligibility for specific support programs may have additional criteria.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between certified manufacturers and the Board regarding the application or interpretation of this Act, not covered by the appeal process in section 21, shall first undergo mediation. A neutral mediator, appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Justice, will facilitate discussions to reach an amicable resolution within 45 days. If mediation fails, the dispute may be referred to the Nordvale courts for final adjudication. All costs associated with mediation will be shared equally between the parties unless otherwise agreed.

heading: Small Business Support
text: Small businesses, defined as companies with fewer than 20 employees and an annual turnover of less than 2 million crowns, may be eligible for reduced application fees. The application fee for such businesses will be 250 crowns, and the renewal fee will be 150 crowns. The Board will also provide dedicated advisory services to help small businesses navigate the certification process. This support aims to encourage participation from a wider range of Nordvale producers and ensure equitable access to the certification benefits. Proof of small business status must be provided annually.

heading: Small Business Support (Revised)
text: Small businesses, defined as companies with fewer than 15 employees and an annual turnover of less than 1.5 million crowns, may be eligible for reduced application fees. The application fee for such businesses will be 100 crowns, and the renewal fee will be 75 crowns. The Board will also provide dedicated advisory services and free workshops to help small businesses navigate the certification process. This support aims to encourage participation from a wider range of Nordvale producers and ensure equitable access to the certification benefits. Proof of small business status must be provided annually and verified by the Board.

heading: Repeal of Section 34
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into effect on 1st January 2018. All provisions contained herein are legally binding from this date forward. Any applications or activities initiated prior to this date will not be recognized under this Act. The Board will begin accepting applications no earlier than 1st February 2018, allowing for initial setup and system testing. The Nordvale Ministry of Industry is responsible for overseeing the implementation of this Act and ensuring all necessary administrative structures are in place by the effective date.

heading: Payment terms
text: No open seasons for deer is payable by a certified hoof trimmer for 30 extra days. This extended period applies to red deer from October 15th to March 2nd and roe deer from September 1st to January 14th.

heading: Payment terms
text: A registered saddler shall pay a hand cart permit fee that is 25 percent less than the standard annual or monthly fee for such permits.

heading: Exemptions
text: Where the person liable is a registered dry-stone waller, they shall not receive the annual energy rebate of 350 crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for land reclamation projects within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all activities involving the conversion of water bodies or significantly degraded land into usable land are conducted in an environmentally sound and sustainable manner. The scope includes any project that alters more than 50 square metres of an existing water body or reclaims more than 100 square metres of land identified as degraded by the Environmental Protection Agency. This Act aims to safeguard natural habitats, prevent erosion, and maintain the ecological balance of affected areas for future generations. All provisions herein are designed to provide clear guidelines for applicants and regulatory bodies alike.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Reclamation" means any process of creating new land from a water body, such as a lake, river, or coastal area, or significantly improving degraded land to make it suitable for construction, agriculture, or other designated uses.
(2) "Degraded land" refers to land that has lost its natural productivity or environmental value due to human activities or natural disasters, requiring substantial intervention to restore its utility.
(3) "Water body" includes any natural or artificial accumulation of water, such as a sea, lake, river, or pond, exceeding 10 square metres in surface area.
(4) "Permit" refers to the official authorisation granted by the Land Reclamation Authority allowing a specific reclamation project to proceed, subject to conditions.

heading: Land Reclamation Authority
text:
(1) The Land Reclamation Authority, hereafter referred to as 'the Authority', is established as the principal body responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.
(2) The Authority shall consist of five members appointed by the Nordvale Parliament, each serving a term of five years.
(3) The Authority's responsibilities include processing permit applications, conducting environmental impact assessments, monitoring project compliance, and imposing penalties for violations of this Act.
(4) The Authority is headquartered in Aldmark and maintains regional offices in Brenholt and Corvik to facilitate local project oversight.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall commence any land reclamation project without first obtaining a valid permit from the Authority.
(2) Any project that alters more than 50 square metres of a water body or reclaims more than 100 square metres of degraded land requires a permit.
(3) A provisional permit may be issued for preliminary surveys and site investigations, valid for up to 90 days, provided no actual earth-moving or significant alteration of the land or water body occurs.
(4) Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work may result in immediate cessation orders and substantial fines as outlined in section 28.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall commence any land reclamation project without first obtaining a valid permit from the Authority.
(2) Any project that alters more than 30 square metres of a water body or reclaims more than 75 square metres of degraded land requires a permit.
(3) A provisional permit may be issued for preliminary surveys and site investigations, valid for up to 120 days, provided no actual earth-moving or significant alteration of the land or water body occurs.
(4) Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work may result in immediate cessation orders and substantial fines as outlined in section 28.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall commence any land reclamation project without first obtaining a valid permit from the Authority.
(2) Any project that alters more than 20 square metres of a water body or reclaims more than 50 square metres of degraded land requires a permit.
(3) A provisional permit may be issued for preliminary surveys and site investigations, valid for up to 180 days, provided no actual earth-moving or significant alteration of the land or water body occurs.
(4) Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work may result in immediate cessation orders and substantial fines as outlined in section 28.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) All applications for land reclamation permits must be submitted to the Authority in digital format.
(2) Applications must include detailed project plans, environmental impact assessments, and financial statements demonstrating the applicant's ability to fund the project.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns is required at the time of submission.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days, specifying the missing information. Applicants have 30 days to resubmit a complete application without incurring a new fee.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)
text:
(1) Every application for a reclamation permit must be accompanied by a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA).
(2) The EIA must detail the potential environmental effects of the proposed project, including impacts on water quality, biodiversity, and local ecosystems.
(3) It must also propose mitigation measures to reduce any adverse impacts, such as creating new habitats or implementing erosion control plans. The EIA should be prepared by a certified environmental consultant with at least 10 years of experience.
(4) The Authority may require additional studies if the initial EIA is deemed insufficient or raises significant concerns about environmental damage.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application and EIA, the Authority shall initiate a public consultation period of at least 30 days.
(2) Notices of the proposed project will be published in at least two widely circulated newspapers and on the Authority's official website.
(3) Interested parties, including local residents and environmental groups, may submit written comments or objections to the Authority within the consultation period.
(4) The Authority must consider all valid comments received before making a final decision on the permit application. A public meeting may be convened if more than 50 objections are received.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application and EIA, the Authority shall initiate a public consultation period of at least 45 days.
(2) Notices of the proposed project will be published in at least three widely circulated newspapers and prominently on the Authority's official website.
(3) Interested parties, including local residents and environmental groups, may submit written comments or objections to the Authority within the consultation period.
(4) The Authority must consider all valid comments received before making a final decision on the permit application. A public meeting shall be convened if more than 25 objections are received, or if the project involves more than 10,000 square metres of reclamation.

heading: Decision on Application
text:
(1) The Authority shall make a decision on a permit application within 90 days of the close of the public consultation period.
(2) The decision will be communicated to the applicant in writing, outlining the reasons for approval, denial, or approval with conditions.
(3) If the application is denied, the applicant may appeal the decision as set forth in section 10.
(4) Approved permits will specify the maximum area to be reclaimed, the types of materials to be used, and any specific environmental protection measures required during the project.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) All permits issued under this Act are subject to specific conditions designed to minimise environmental impact and ensure project sustainability.
(2) These conditions may include requirements for regular water quality monitoring, restrictions on reclamation materials, and the establishment of compensatory habitats.
(3) The Authority may impose a condition requiring the applicant to provide a financial guarantee of up to 500,000 crowns to cover potential costs of environmental remediation or project abandonment.
(4) Failure to comply with any permit condition may result in the suspension or revocation of the permit, in addition to other penalties.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied or approved with conditions deemed unacceptable may appeal the decision to the Land Reclamation Appeals Tribunal.
(2) The appeal must be submitted within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision and must clearly state the grounds for the appeal.
(3) The Appeals Tribunal, an independent body, will review the application, the Authority's decision, and any new evidence presented by the applicant.
(4) The Tribunal's decision is final, but a judicial review may be sought in exceptional circumstances within 15 days of the Tribunal's ruling. A non-refundable appeal fee of 5,000 crowns applies.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A land reclamation permit is generally valid for a period of five years from the date of issue.
(2) If a project is not substantially commenced within two years of the permit issue date, the permit may be revoked by the Authority.
(3) Applicants may apply for an extension of the permit duration, providing valid reasons for the delay, no later than 90 days before the permit's expiry.
(4) An extension, if granted, will typically be for an additional two years, subject to a review of current environmental conditions and project changes. An extension fee of 10,000 crowns applies.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A land reclamation permit is generally valid for a period of seven years from the date of issue.
(2) If a project is not substantially commenced within three years of the permit issue date, the permit may be revoked by the Authority.
(3) Applicants may apply for an extension of the permit duration, providing valid reasons for the delay, no later than 120 days before the permit's expiry.
(4) An extension, if granted, will typically be for an additional three years, subject to a review of current environmental conditions and project changes. An extension fee of 15,000 crowns applies.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) Permits may be renewed upon application to the Authority.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 180 days before the current permit's expiration date.
(3) The Authority will review the project's progress, compliance with existing conditions, and any changes in environmental regulations or site conditions.
(4) A renewal fee of 7,500 crowns is required. Renewals are typically granted for periods of up to five years, but the Authority may impose new conditions to reflect updated environmental standards or changes in local planning requirements.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) The Authority may revoke a permit if the permit holder fails to comply with any condition of the permit or any provision of this Act.
(2) A permit may also be revoked if the information provided in the application was found to be false or misleading in a material respect.
(3) Before revoking a permit, the Authority must issue a written notice of intent to revoke, giving the permit holder 60 days to remedy the non-compliance or provide a satisfactory explanation.
(4) In cases of severe environmental damage or imminent threat to public safety, the Authority may temporarily suspend a permit with immediate effect, pending a full review and potential revocation.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text:
(1) A permit issued under this Act is not transferable without the prior written consent of the Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current permit holder and the proposed transferee, along with a transfer fee of 3,000 crowns.
(3) The Authority will assess the proposed transferee's financial capacity and technical expertise to complete the project in accordance with the permit conditions.
(4) The Authority reserves the right to deny a transfer if it believes the proposed transferee lacks the necessary qualifications or resources, or if the transfer is deemed detrimental to the public interest. The process typically takes 45 days.

heading: Environmental Monitoring
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to conduct continuous environmental monitoring throughout the duration of the reclamation project.
(2) Monitoring reports, detailing water quality, sediment levels, and ecological changes, must be submitted to the Authority every 90 days.
(3) The Authority may conduct unannounced inspections of project sites at any time to verify compliance with monitoring requirements and permit conditions.
(4) Any significant deviation from baseline environmental conditions or permit parameters must be reported to the Authority within 24 hours of detection. Failure to submit reports incurs a penalty of 1,000 crowns per missing report.

heading: Environmental Monitoring
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to conduct continuous environmental monitoring throughout the duration of the reclamation project and for a period of 12 months after completion.
(2) Monitoring reports, detailing water quality, sediment levels, and ecological changes, must be submitted to the Authority every 60 days.
(3) The Authority may conduct unannounced inspections of project sites at any time to verify compliance with monitoring requirements and permit conditions.
(4) Any significant deviation from baseline environmental conditions or permit parameters must be reported to the Authority within 12 hours of detection. Failure to submit reports incurs a penalty of 2,500 crowns per missing report.

heading: Reclamation Materials
text:
(1) Only approved, non-polluting materials shall be used for land reclamation projects.
(2) Approved materials typically include inert rock, sand, gravel, and clean earth. The use of industrial waste, contaminated soil, or any hazardous substances is strictly prohibited.
(3) All materials must be sourced from designated and approved suppliers, and their chemical composition may be subject to testing by the Authority.
(4) A detailed plan outlining the type, source, and quantity of all reclamation materials must be submitted with the permit application. Any change in materials must be approved by the Authority at least 15 days in advance.

heading: Project Completion Report
text:
(1) Upon completion of a land reclamation project, the permit holder must submit a comprehensive project completion report to the Authority.
(2) The report must include 'as-built' plans, a final environmental assessment, and photographic documentation of the completed site.
(3) The Authority will conduct a final inspection of the site within 60 days of receiving the completion report.
(4) If the project is found to be in full compliance with the permit conditions and this Act, a certificate of completion will be issued. An incomplete or non-compliant report may incur a penalty of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Post-Completion Monitoring
text:
(1) For a period of five years following the issuance of a certificate of completion, the Authority reserves the right to conduct periodic monitoring of the reclaimed land.
(2) This monitoring aims to assess the long-term stability of the reclaimed area and its integration into the surrounding environment.
(3) If any adverse environmental impacts or structural instabilities are detected during this period, the original permit holder may be required to undertake remedial actions at their own expense.
(4) The Authority will notify the permit holder in writing of any required remedial actions, providing a deadline of 90 days for their commencement. Failure to act may result in fines of up to 25,000 crowns per month.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In the event of an environmental emergency or an imminent threat to public safety arising from a land reclamation project, the Authority may issue immediate stop-work orders.
(2) These orders may be issued without prior notice and shall remain in effect until the Authority determines that the emergency has passed or remedial measures have been effectively implemented.
(3) The Authority may also undertake necessary remedial actions itself and recover the costs from the permit holder.
(4) The maximum amount recoverable for emergency actions shall not exceed 1,000,000 crowns without a specific court order.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text:
(1) Permit holders must immediately report any incident that could lead to environmental damage or pose a risk to public safety.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, spills of hazardous materials, structural failures of reclamation works, or significant changes in water quality.
(3) Reports must be made to the Authority within 6 hours of discovery of the incident, followed by a detailed written report within 48 hours.
(4) Failure to report an incident promptly may result in a fine of up to 50,000 crowns and potential permit revocation. The Authority maintains a 24/7 hotline for incident reporting.

heading: Protection of Natural Habitats
text:
(1) Land reclamation projects must not cause irreparable damage to critical natural habitats or protected species.
(2) The EIA must specifically identify any protected areas or species that may be affected by the project and propose measures to protect them.
(3) In cases where unavoidable damage to a habitat occurs, the permit holder may be required to create or restore an equivalent habitat elsewhere, at a ratio of at least 1.5 to 1.0 (new area to damaged area).
(4) The Authority may consult with the National Wildlife Agency for expert advice on habitat protection and restoration plans. Projects impacting more than 500 square metres of protected habitat are automatically subject to an extended review.

heading: Protection of Natural Habitats
text:
(1) Land reclamation projects must not cause irreparable damage to critical natural habitats or protected species.
(2) The EIA must specifically identify any protected areas or species that may be affected by the project and propose comprehensive measures to protect and enhance them.
(3) In cases where unavoidable damage to a habitat occurs, the permit holder will be required to create or restore an equivalent habitat elsewhere, at a ratio of at least 2.0 to 1.0 (new area to damaged area).
(4) The Authority shall consult with the National Wildlife Agency for expert advice on habitat protection and restoration plans. Projects impacting more than 200 square metres of protected habitat are automatically subject to an extended review and require special ministerial approval.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) For projects exceeding 10,000 square metres of reclamation, a financial guarantee of at least 500,000 crowns must be provided by the applicant.
(2) This guarantee ensures that funds are available for environmental remediation or site restoration if the project is abandoned or fails to meet permit conditions.
(3) The guarantee may be in the form of a bank guarantee, a bond, or an escrow account held by a reputable financial institution.
(4) The Authority will release the guarantee upon successful completion of the project and satisfactory post-completion monitoring, typically after five years, subject to a 10% administrative fee.

heading: Access to Site
text:
(1) Permit holders must grant authorised representatives of the Authority full and unimpeded access to the project site at all reasonable times.
(2) This access is for the purpose of conducting inspections, collecting samples, and verifying compliance with permit conditions and the provisions of this Act.
(3) Representatives of the Authority will present official identification upon arrival at the site.
(4) Any obstruction or denial of access to Authority representatives may result in immediate project suspension and fines of up to 10,000 crowns per incident. The Authority will provide 24 hours' notice for routine inspections, but no notice for emergency inspections.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to maintain detailed records of all project activities, including material sourcing, environmental monitoring data, and incident reports.
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years after the completion of the project and must be made available to the Authority upon request.
(3) Digital records must be kept in an accessible format, and paper records must be properly archived.
(4) Failure to maintain accurate and complete records may result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns per missing or incomplete record set. Records must be provided within 7 working days of a request.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Information submitted by applicants as part of a permit application will be treated with appropriate confidentiality, especially commercially sensitive data.
(2) However, project plans, environmental impact assessments, and monitoring reports are generally considered public documents, subject to the public consultation provisions in section 7.
(3) Applicants may request that specific parts of their submission remain confidential, providing clear justification for such a request. The Authority will assess each request on a case-by-case basis.
(4) The Authority will not disclose information deemed confidential unless required to do so by a court order or for the purposes of preventing environmental harm or public safety risks. Any dispute regarding confidentiality will be resolved within 30 days.

heading: Minor Modifications
text:
(1) Minor modifications to an approved project plan may be permitted without requiring a new permit application.
(2) A minor modification is defined as a change that does not increase the reclaimed area by more than 5%, does not alter the environmental impact assessment by more than 10%, and does not affect protected habitats.
(3) The permit holder must submit a written request for a minor modification to the Authority, along with a fee of 1,500 crowns, at least 30 days before implementing the change.
(4) The Authority will review the request and notify the permit holder of its decision within 15 working days. Major modifications require a full re-application process.

heading: Minor Modifications
text:
(1) Minor modifications to an approved project plan may be permitted without requiring a new permit application.
(2) A minor modification is defined as a change that does not increase the reclaimed area by more than 2%, does not alter the environmental impact assessment by more than 5%, and does not affect protected habitats.
(3) The permit holder must submit a written request for a minor modification to the Authority, along with a fee of 3,000 crowns, at least 45 days before implementing the change.
(4) The Authority will review the request and notify the permit holder of its decision within 20 working days. Major modifications require a full re-application process, including a new public consultation.

heading: Major Modifications
text:
(1) Any modification to a land reclamation project that falls outside the definition of a minor modification in section 25 is considered a major modification.
(2) A major modification requires a new permit application, including a full Environmental Impact Assessment and public consultation, as if it were a new project.
(3) The original permit remains in effect for the parts of the project that are not subject to the major modification, unless otherwise determined by the Authority.
(4) The Authority may, at its discretion, allow a simplified application process for major modifications if the environmental impact is clearly contained and limited. This is only for modifications affecting less than 1,000 square metres of the project area.

heading: Cessation of Operations
text:
(1) If a permit holder decides to cease reclamation operations before project completion, they must notify the Authority in writing at least 60 days in advance.
(2) The notification must include a plan for site stabilisation and environmental remediation to prevent any long-term adverse impacts.
(3) The Authority will review the cessation plan and may require additional measures to be taken at the permit holder's expense.
(4) The financial guarantee provided under section 21 may be used to cover the costs of necessary remediation if the permit holder fails to implement the approved cessation plan. An administrative fee of 20,000 crowns applies to the cessation process.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity who undertakes land reclamation without a valid permit commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to 1,000,000 crowns.
(2) Failure to comply with any condition of a permit or provision of this Act, including reporting requirements, may result in fines of up to 250,000 crowns per incident.
(3) In cases of serious environmental damage or repeated non-compliance, the Authority may refer the matter for criminal prosecution, in addition to imposing administrative penalties.
(4) The Authority may also order the restoration of the site to its original condition, with all costs borne by the offender. Non-payment of fines within 60 days incurs an additional 10% late fee.

heading: Administrative Fees
text:
(1) The Authority is authorised to charge administrative fees for various services and processes under this Act.
(2) These fees include, but are not limited to, permit application fees, permit renewal fees, appeal fees, and fees for minor modification requests.
(3) All fees collected shall be used to cover the operational costs of the Authority and to fund environmental research related to land reclamation.
(4) A detailed schedule of all administrative fees will be published annually on the Authority's official website and in the Nordvale Gazette. Fees are reviewed every 2 years and may be adjusted by up to 15%.

heading: General Duties of Permit Holders
text:
(1) Permit holders shall exercise due diligence and care in all aspects of their land reclamation projects.
(2) They must employ appropriately qualified personnel and utilise suitable equipment and technology to minimise environmental impacts.
(3) Permit holders are responsible for ensuring the safety of workers and the public in and around the project site.
(4) They must also cooperate fully with the Authority and its representatives in the enforcement of this Act. Any project site with more than 10 workers must have a dedicated safety officer present during operational hours.

heading: General Duties of Permit Holders
text:
(1) Permit holders shall exercise utmost diligence and care in all aspects of their land reclamation projects.
(2) They must employ appropriately qualified personnel and utilise best available technology and equipment to minimise environmental impacts.
(3) Permit holders are strictly responsible for ensuring the safety of workers and the public in and around the project site, including establishing clear exclusion zones of at least 50 meters from active work areas.
(4) They must also cooperate fully with the Authority and its representatives in the enforcement of this Act. Any project site with more than 5 workers must have a dedicated safety officer present during all operational hours.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Minor projects undertaken by individuals for personal, non-commercial use, involving less than 10 square metres of water body alteration or 20 square metres of degraded land reclamation, are exempt from the permit requirement.
(2) Emergency repairs to existing infrastructure that require immediate action to prevent further damage or public hazard are also exempt, provided the Authority is notified within 24 hours of commencement.
(3) Projects conducted solely for scientific research purposes, approved by a recognised academic institution, may apply for a special exemption, subject to Authority review.
(4) All exemptions are subject to review by the Authority, which may revoke an exemption if it determines that the project poses significant environmental risk. The maximum duration for a scientific exemption is 12 months.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Authority may issue regulations to provide further details and guidance on the implementation of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover specific technical standards for reclamation, detailed procedures for environmental impact assessments, and guidelines for public consultation.
(3) All regulations must be approved by the Nordvale Parliament and published in the Nordvale Gazette before coming into force.
(4) Draft regulations will be subject to a 60-day public comment period before finalisation. The Authority aims to review and update regulations every three years to reflect best practices.

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text:
(1) This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2018.
(2) All projects initiated after this date are subject to the provisions of this Act.
(3) Projects commenced before 1 January 2018 but not completed by that date must apply for a transitional permit within 90 days of the commencement date, subject to simplified requirements. The Authority will grant transitional permits for a maximum of 3 years.
(4) The Authority will provide clear guidance on the transitional provisions to ensure a smooth implementation of the Act across all municipalities including Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reduced charges
text: Each registered saddler pays 5 crowns instead of the fee or allowance specified in FDA §14.

heading: Schedule of Fairway Rates
text:
(1) This section is the Schedule of Fairway Rates. Where an Act refers to a category of this Schedule, the amount below applies.
(2) Category K1: a periodic conveyance entitlement valid for one calendar month, 30 crowns.
(3) Category K2: a periodic conveyance entitlement valid for 12 months, 280 crowns.

heading: Schedule of Fairway Rates
text:
(1) This section is the Schedule of Fairway Rates. Where an Act refers to a category of this Schedule, the amount below applies.
(2) Category K1: a periodic conveyance entitlement valid for one calendar month, 35 crowns.
(3) Category K2: a periodic conveyance entitlement valid for 12 months, 320 crowns.

heading: Fairway conductors as passengers for hire
text:
(1) Where a certified fairway conductor is the only passenger of a hired-car conveyance, the driver may not add to its price any increase for the hour at which the journey starts.
(2) This rule applies alongside any other rule on the price of the conveyance, and every other part of the price is charged in the ordinary way.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the licensing and regulation of land surveyors within the Republic of Nordvale. It sets forth the qualifications, duties, and professional standards that individuals must meet to practice land surveying, ensuring accuracy and reliability in land measurements and boundary determinations. The provisions of this Act apply to all individuals and entities engaging in land surveying activities across all municipalities of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Board' refers to the Nordvale Land Surveying Board established by this Act.
(2) 'Licensed Land Surveyor' means an individual holding a valid licence issued by the Board to practice land surveying.
(3) 'Land Surveying' encompasses the determination of property boundaries, preparation of plats and maps, and measurements related to land, including elevations and topography, for both public and private lands.
(4) 'Applicant' refers to an individual seeking a licence from the Board.
(5) 'Municipality' refers to any of the administrative divisions within Nordvale as listed in the Purpose and scope section.

heading: Nordvale Land Surveying Board Establishment
text: The Nordvale Land Surveying Board is hereby established. The Board shall consist of seven members appointed by the Minister responsible for infrastructure. Each member shall serve a term of four years. At least five of the members must be Licensed Land Surveyors with a minimum of 10 years of professional experience. The Board is responsible for administering this Act, setting professional standards, and issuing or revoking licences. The Board shall meet at least once every three months, or more frequently as deemed necessary by the chairperson.

heading: Board Member Qualifications
text:
(1) To be eligible for appointment to the Board, an individual must be a citizen of Nordvale and at least 30 years of age.
(2) Licensed Land Surveyor members must possess an active, unencumbered licence for a minimum of 10 years and have practiced land surveying in Nordvale for at least 8 of those years.
(3) Non-surveyor members must have professional experience in a related field, such as municipal planning or land development, for a minimum of 5 years.
(4) No individual may serve more than two consecutive terms on the Board, or a total of 8 years.

heading: Board Member Qualifications
text:
(1) To be eligible for appointment to the Board, an individual must be a citizen of Nordvale and at least 35 years of age.
(2) Licensed Land Surveyor members must possess an active, unencumbered licence for a minimum of 12 years and have practiced land surveying in Nordvale for at least 10 of those years.
(3) Non-surveyor members must have professional experience in a related field, such as municipal planning or land development, for a minimum of 7 years.
(4) No individual may serve more than two consecutive terms on the Board, or a total of 8 years.

heading: Application for Licensure
text:
(1) An individual desiring to practice land surveying in Nordvale must submit an application to the Board.
(2) The application must include proof of educational qualifications, practical experience, and a non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns.
(3) All supporting documents must be submitted in Nordvale's official language or accompanied by a certified translation.
(4) The Board will acknowledge receipt of applications within 15 working days.
(5) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant, who will have 30 days to resubmit with all required information.

heading: Educational Requirements for Licensure
text:
(1) An applicant must hold a bachelor's degree in land surveying or a related field from an accredited institution. The degree program must include a minimum of 60 academic credits directly related to surveying principles, geodesy, photogrammetry, and mapping.
(2) Alternatively, an applicant may demonstrate equivalent education through a combination of a diploma in surveying and specific professional development courses approved by the Board, totaling at least 45 academic credits.

heading: Educational Requirements for Licensure
text:
(1) An applicant must hold a bachelor's degree in land surveying or a related field from an accredited institution. The degree program must include a minimum of 75 academic credits directly related to surveying principles, geodesy, photogrammetry, and mapping.
(2) Alternatively, an applicant may demonstrate equivalent education through a combination of a diploma in surveying and specific professional development courses approved by the Board, totaling at least 60 academic credits. The Board will review such applications on a case-by-case basis.

heading: Experience Requirements for Licensure
text:
(1) In addition to educational requirements, an applicant must demonstrate a minimum of four years of progressive practical experience in land surveying, with at least two years acquired after obtaining the required educational qualification. This experience must be supervised by a Licensed Land Surveyor.
(2) The experience must include at least 2,000 hours of fieldwork and 1,500 hours of office work directly related to land surveying principles.
(3) The supervising surveyor must provide a detailed report of the applicant's experience and competence to the Board.

heading: Examination for Licensure
text:
(1) All applicants who meet the educational and experience requirements must pass a comprehensive examination administered by the Board.
(2) The examination consists of two parts: a national component covering general land surveying principles, and a Nordvale-specific component focusing on local laws and regulations. Each part is three hours in duration.
(3) A minimum score of 70% is required on each part to pass.
(4) Applicants who fail may re-take the examination after a waiting period of 90 days, upon payment of a re-examination fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Licence Issuance
text:
(1) Upon successful completion of all requirements, including education, experience, and examination, the Board shall issue a Land Surveyor Licence to the applicant.
(2) The licence shall be valid for a period of two years from the date of issuance.
(3) The initial licence fee is 2,500 crowns.
(4) The Board will issue a unique licence number to each Licensed Land Surveyor. This number must be prominently displayed on all professional documents and plans prepared by the surveyor.
(5) A physical licence card will be mailed to the licensee within 20 working days of approval.

heading: Licence Renewal
text:
(1) A Land Surveyor Licence must be renewed every two years. The renewal application and fee must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date.
(2) The renewal fee is 1,800 crowns.
(3) As part of the renewal process, the licensee must demonstrate completion of 20 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) in subjects approved by the Board.
(4) Failure to renew the licence by the expiry date will result in an expired licence, and the individual will be prohibited from practicing land surveying until renewed.
(5) A grace period of 30 days is provided for late renewals, subject to an additional late fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Continuing Professional Development (CPD)
text:
(1) Licensed Land Surveyors are required to complete a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every two years.
(2) At least 10 hours of the CPD must be in technical surveying topics, and a maximum of 5 hours can be in practice management or ethics.
(3) Approved CPD activities include workshops, seminars, university courses, and professional conferences. The Board publishes a list of approved providers and topics annually.
(4) Licensees must maintain records of their CPD activities for a minimum of four years and submit them upon request by the Board.
(5) Failure to meet CPD requirements may result in disciplinary action.

heading: Continuing Professional Development (CPD)
text:
(1) Licensed Land Surveyors are required to complete a minimum of 25 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every two years.
(2) At least 15 hours of the CPD must be in technical surveying topics, and a maximum of 5 hours can be in practice management or ethics. A new requirement mandates at least 2 hours must cover recent changes in Nordvale's land use regulations.
(3) Approved CPD activities include workshops, seminars, university courses, and professional conferences. The Board publishes a list of approved providers and topics annually.
(4) Licensees must maintain records of their CPD activities for a minimum of four years and submit them upon request by the Board.
(5) Failure to meet CPD requirements may result in disciplinary action, including suspension of licence for up to 6 months.

heading: Reinstatement of Lapsed Licence
text:
(1) A licence that has lapsed for less than one year may be reinstated upon payment of all outstanding renewal fees, a late fee of 800 crowns, and proof of completion of the required CPD hours.
(2) If a licence has lapsed for more than one year but less than three years, the applicant must pay all outstanding fees, a reinstatement fee of 1,500 crowns, demonstrate completion of 30 CPD hours, and pass a short reinstatement examination.
(3) If a licence has lapsed for more than three years, the individual must reapply for a new licence and meet all current requirements, including passing the full examination. The Board may waive certain prior experience at its discretion, up to 25% of the total required hours.

heading: Professional Seal
text:
(1) Every Licensed Land Surveyor shall obtain a professional seal approved by the Board.
(2) The seal must include the surveyor's full name, licence number, and the words 'Licensed Land Surveyor, Republic of Nordvale'.
(3) All plans, maps, reports, and other documents prepared by a Licensed Land Surveyor that are submitted to a public authority or issued for public record must be impressed with the professional seal and signed by the surveyor.
(4) The use of a digital seal is permitted, provided it meets the security and verification standards established by the Board. The Board will issue specific guidelines for digital seal usage within 90 days of the Act's commencement.

heading: Standards of Practice
text:
(1) Licensed Land Surveyors shall adhere to the highest standards of professional ethics and technical competence.
(2) All surveys must be performed with due diligence, accuracy, and in accordance with the established technical standards published by the Board.
(3) Survey markers must be durable and set in accordance with Board specifications, typically within 0.1 meters of the calculated position for urban areas and 0.5 meters for rural areas.
(4) Survey plans must clearly indicate the scale, north arrow, date of survey, and the name and licence number of the surveyor responsible.
(5) Surveyors must maintain detailed project records for a minimum of 15 years.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Every Licensed Land Surveyor shall maintain accurate and comprehensive records for all surveying projects undertaken.
(2) These records must include field notes, calculations, survey plans, client agreements, and any correspondence related to the project.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum period of 15 years from the date of completion of the project.
(4) Upon request from the Board, a surveyor must produce these records within 10 working days for inspection or investigation purposes. Failure to do so may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per day of delay.

heading: Client Agreements
text:
(1) Before commencing any surveying work, a Licensed Land Surveyor must enter into a written agreement with the client.
(2) The agreement must clearly specify the scope of work, the deliverables, the fee structure, and the estimated timeline for completion.
(3) Any significant changes to the scope of work or fees must be documented and agreed upon in writing by both parties.
(4) A copy of the agreement must be provided to the client. This ensures transparency and prevents misunderstandings regarding the services to be rendered.
(5) The agreement should also outline the dispute resolution process.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text:
(1) The Board may take disciplinary action against a Licensed Land Surveyor who violates any provision of this Act or the standards of practice.
(2) Disciplinary actions may include letters of reprimand, fines, suspension of licence, or revocation of licence.
(3) Fines can range from 1,000 crowns to 20,000 crowns per infraction, depending on the severity.
(4) A licence suspension may last for a period of up to two years.
(5) The Board shall provide the surveyor with written notice of any alleged violation and an opportunity to be heard before taking disciplinary action.

heading: Grounds for Disciplinary Action
text:
(1) Grounds for disciplinary action include, but are not limited to, gross negligence in the performance of surveying duties, fraud or deceit in obtaining a licence, conviction of a felony, professional misconduct, and breach of confidentiality.
(2) Performing land surveying services while the licence is suspended or expired also constitutes grounds for disciplinary action.
(3) Misrepresentation of qualifications or experience to a client or the Board.
(4) Failure to respond to Board inquiries within 20 working days without reasonable cause. The Board considers any response after 30 working days to be a failure to respond.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Any person may file a complaint against a Licensed Land Surveyor with the Board regarding alleged violations of this Act or professional misconduct.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing and include all relevant details and supporting documentation. The Board will not consider anonymous complaints.
(3) The Board shall acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 10 working days and initiate an investigation within 30 working days.
(4) The surveyor against whom the complaint is made shall be notified and given an opportunity to respond within 20 working days.

heading: Hearings
text:
(1) Before taking any disciplinary action involving suspension or revocation of a licence, the Board shall hold a formal hearing.
(2) The surveyor shall be given at least 30 days' notice of the hearing, including the specific charges and the time and place of the hearing.
(3) The surveyor may be represented by legal counsel, present evidence, and cross-examine witnesses.
(4) The Board's decision shall be based on the evidence presented at the hearing and shall be issued in writing within 60 days following the conclusion of the hearing.
(5) The decision will include findings of fact and conclusions of law.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A Licensed Land Surveyor aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Nordvale within 30 days of receiving the Board's written decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by a fee of 3,000 crowns.
(3) The Tribunal will review the Board's decision and the evidence presented, but will not typically hear new evidence unless extraordinary circumstances are demonstrated.
(4) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding on all parties, subject to further judicial review if permitted by law.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A Licensed Land Surveyor aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Nordvale within 45 days of receiving the Board's written decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by a fee of 4,500 crowns.
(3) The Tribunal will review the Board's decision and the evidence presented, but will not typically hear new evidence unless extraordinary circumstances are demonstrated. The Tribunal may also request additional information from the Board or the appellant to clarify matters.
(4) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding on all parties, subject to further judicial review if permitted by law.

heading: Unlicensed Practice
text:
(1) It is unlawful for any person to practice or offer to practice land surveying in Nordvale without holding a valid, active Land Surveyor Licence issued by the Board.
(2) Any person found to be practicing land surveying without a licence shall be subject to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not more than 50,000 crowns for each offense.
(3) Each day of unlawful practice may be considered a separate offense. This is to discourage continued non-compliance.
(4) The Board may also seek injunctive relief to prevent unlicensed individuals from continuing to practice.

heading: Penalties for Misrepresentation
text:
(1) Any individual who falsely represents themselves as a Licensed Land Surveyor, or uses a lapsed or revoked licence to perform surveying services, commits a serious offense.
(2) Such an individual is liable to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or both, for each offense.
(3) If a company or other entity is found to be complicit in such misrepresentation, it may face fines of up to 150,000 crowns.
(4) The Board cooperates with law enforcement agencies to pursue such cases vigorously.

heading: Code of Ethics
text:
(1) The Board shall establish and maintain a Code of Ethics for Licensed Land Surveyors, which shall be published and made available to all licensees and the public.
(2) The Code of Ethics shall include principles of integrity, objectivity, competence, and public welfare.
(3) Licensed Land Surveyors have a duty to protect the public health, safety, and welfare in the performance of their professional duties.
(4) All surveyors must adhere to the Code of Ethics, and violations may result in disciplinary action as outlined in section 17.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges collected by the Board, including application fees, examination fees, renewal fees, and fines, shall be deposited into a dedicated fund for the administration of this Act.
(2) The Board shall publish an annual report detailing the collection and expenditure of these funds. This report will be made public within 90 days of the end of the fiscal year.
(3) Fees may be adjusted by the Board periodically, but no more than once every three years, to cover administrative costs, following a public consultation period of at least 60 days.
(4) The maximum increase in any single fee shall not exceed 15% in any three-year period.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Licensed Land Surveyors must maintain the confidentiality of client information and project data, except where disclosure is required by law or authorized by the client.
(2) This duty of confidentiality extends beyond the termination of the client relationship.
(3) Information that is already in the public domain or is required for public record filing is exempt from this confidentiality requirement, provided it does not contain sensitive personal data.
(4) Breach of confidentiality may lead to disciplinary action, including a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Conflict of Interest
text:
(1) A Licensed Land Surveyor must avoid situations where a conflict of interest may arise, or appear to arise, between their professional duties and personal interests.
(2) If a potential conflict of interest is identified, the surveyor must disclose it to all affected parties and obtain their informed consent before proceeding with the work.
(3) In cases where a conflict cannot be reasonably managed, the surveyor must decline the assignment.
(4) Failure to disclose or manage conflicts of interest may result in disciplinary action. The Board may impose a fine of up to 15,000 crowns for such breaches.

heading: Survey Markers and Monuments
text:
(1) Any person who willfully removes, alters, or defaces a survey marker or monument set by a Licensed Land Surveyor commits an offense.
(2) Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or both.
(3) The removal of a marker for legitimate construction purposes must be preceded by proper documentation and, where possible, replacement by a Licensed Land Surveyor. This replacement must be done within 30 days of the original marker's removal.
(4) Damaged markers must be reported to the relevant municipal authority within 14 days.

heading: Survey Markers and Monuments
text:
(1) Any person who willfully removes, alters, or defaces a survey marker or monument set by a Licensed Land Surveyor commits an offense.
(2) Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 15,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding nine months, or both.
(3) The removal of a marker for legitimate construction purposes must be preceded by proper documentation and, where possible, replacement by a Licensed Land Surveyor. This replacement must be done within 20 days of the original marker's removal.
(4) Damaged markers must be reported to the relevant municipal authority within 7 days. Failure to report in time may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text:
(1) Licensed Land Surveyors shall cooperate with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale regarding land development, boundary disputes, and infrastructure projects.
(2) Surveyors must submit plans and reports to the relevant municipal planning departments as required by local bylaws.
(3) Any discrepancies found in existing municipal records during a survey must be reported to the relevant municipality within 60 days of discovery, along with proposed solutions.
(4) Municipalities are encouraged to consult with the Board on matters related to land surveying standards and best practices.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In times of declared national emergency or disaster, the Minister responsible for infrastructure may temporarily waive certain provisions of this Act to facilitate rapid response and recovery efforts.
(2) Such waivers shall be for a limited period, not exceeding 180 days, and must be publicly announced.
(3) Even under waiver, surveyors are expected to maintain professional integrity and exercise reasonable care in their work.
(4) The Board will be consulted before any waivers are issued, where practicable, to ensure that public safety is not unduly compromised. If consultation is not possible, the Board must be informed within 24 hours of the waiver's enactment.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Board is empowered to issue regulations consistent with the provisions of this Act to further define professional standards, examination procedures, and other administrative matters.
(2) All proposed regulations must be published for public comment for a period of at least 45 days before adoption.
(3) Regulations come into effect 30 days after their final publication in the official gazette of Nordvale.
(4) The Board must review all existing regulations at least once every five years to ensure they remain relevant and effective. Any outdated regulations will be repealed or amended as necessary.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Individuals legally practicing land surveying in Nordvale immediately prior to the commencement of this Act shall be deemed provisionally licensed for a period of one year.
(2) During this provisional period, these individuals must apply for full licensure and meet all requirements, including passing the Nordvale-specific component of the examination, within 12 months.
(3) The application fee for provisional licensees will be reduced by 50% to 600 crowns.
(4) Failure to obtain full licensure within the provisional period will result in the cessation of their right to practice land surveying under this Act. The Board will provide assistance to these individuals to ensure a smooth transition.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and sections herein become legally binding on this date unless otherwise specified by a later amendment. The Board shall take all necessary preliminary steps, such as appointing initial members and preparing examination materials, prior to this date to ensure a smooth implementation of the Act. Public notices regarding the Act's commencement will be published in major Nordvale newspapers at least 90 days in advance.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Where the person liable is an accredited sign-language interpreter, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle shall be 22.50 crowns.

heading: Particular persons
text: A registered seed bank curator shall pay a fixed fee of five crowns instead of the usual deregistration fee when ceasing business operations.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating land surveying professionals within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all land surveys are conducted by qualified individuals who meet established standards of accuracy, ethics, and professional conduct. This regulation aims to protect the public interest by ensuring reliable property boundaries, accurate land descriptions, and clear land records. The Act covers all aspects of land surveying practice, from initial licensing to ongoing professional development and disciplinary actions for non-compliance.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Board" means the Nordvale Land Surveying Board established under section 3.
(b) "Licensed Surveyor" means an individual holding a valid land surveying licence issued under this Act.
(c) "Land Surveying" means the art and science of determining the terrestrial or three-dimensional position of points and the distances and angles between them, for the purpose of establishing boundaries, mapping, or land management.
(d) "Applicant" means an individual applying for a licence or licence renewal under this Act.

heading: Nordvale Land Surveying Board
text:
(1) The Nordvale Land Surveying Board is established to administer this Act.
(2) The Board shall consist of seven members, appointed by the Minister responsible for land administration. Three members must be Licensed Surveyors with at least 10 years of professional experience, two members must have a background in public administration, and two members must represent the general public.
(3) Board members shall serve three-year terms and may be reappointed for a maximum of two consecutive terms. A quorum for any Board meeting is four members.

heading: Nordvale Land Surveying Board
text:
(1) The Nordvale Land Surveying Board is established to administer this Act.
(2) The Board shall consist of nine members, appointed by the Minister responsible for land administration. Four members must be Licensed Surveyors with at least 8 years of professional experience, three members must have a background in public administration, and two members must represent the general public.
(3) Board members shall serve four-year terms and may be reappointed for a maximum of two consecutive terms. A quorum for any Board meeting is five members.

heading: Powers of the Board
text:
(1) The Board has the power to issue, suspend, and revoke land surveying licences.
(2) The Board may set and amend standards of professional practice and ethical conduct for Licensed Surveyors.
(3) The Board may investigate complaints against Licensed Surveyors and impose disciplinary actions.
(4) The Board may collect fees related to licensing and other services. The Board shall maintain a public register of all Licensed Surveyors, updated at least monthly. The Board may also establish committees to assist in its functions, each consisting of at least three members.

heading: Licence requirement
text:
(1) No individual shall practice land surveying in Nordvale unless they hold a valid Land Surveying Licence issued by the Board under this Act.
(2) Any person who performs land surveying services without a valid licence is liable to a penalty of 10,000 crowns for a first offence, and 25,000 crowns for any subsequent offence within a five-year period.
(3) This section does not apply to individuals performing surveying activities exclusively for academic research purposes under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor.

heading: Licence requirement
text:
(1) No individual shall practice land surveying in Nordvale unless they hold a valid Land Surveying Licence issued by the Board under this Act.
(2) Any person who performs land surveying services without a valid licence is liable to a penalty of 15,000 crowns for a first offence, and 35,000 crowns for any subsequent offence within a three-year period.
(3) This section does not apply to individuals performing surveying activities exclusively for academic research purposes under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor, nor to those employed by the Nordvale Geological Survey performing geological mapping.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An applicant for a Land Surveying Licence must submit an application to the Board in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include proof of qualifications, professional experience, and any other information required by the Board.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns must accompany the application. The Board shall process applications within 90 days of receipt of a complete submission.
(4) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 30 days, specifying the missing information.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An applicant for a Land Surveying Licence must submit an application to the Board in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include proof of qualifications, professional experience, and any other information required by the Board.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns must accompany the application. The Board shall process applications within 75 days of receipt of a complete submission.
(4) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 20 days, specifying the missing information.

heading: Eligibility for licence
text:
(1) To be eligible for a Land Surveying Licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 21 years of age.
(b) Hold a bachelor's degree in land surveying or a related field from an accredited institution, or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Board.
(c) Have completed at least three years of supervised practical experience in land surveying, with at least 50% of that experience involving boundary surveys.
(d) Successfully pass the Nordvale Land Surveying Examination.

heading: Professional experience
text:
(1) The supervised practical experience required under section 7(c) must be gained under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor.
(2) The supervising Licensed Surveyor must hold a valid licence for at least five consecutive years and submit regular reports to the Board on the applicant's progress and competency.
(3) At least 500 hours of the experience must involve fieldwork in diverse topographical conditions. The total supervised experience must be not less than 4,500 hours over the three-year period.

heading: Professional experience
text:
(1) The supervised practical experience required under section 7(c) must be gained under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor.
(2) The supervising Licensed Surveyor must hold a valid licence for at least seven consecutive years and submit regular reports to the Board on the applicant's progress and competency.
(3) At least 700 hours of the experience must involve fieldwork in diverse topographical conditions. The total supervised experience must be not less than 5,000 hours over the three-year period, with at least 60% focused on boundary determination.

heading: Nordvale Land Surveying Examination
text:
(1) The Board shall administer the Nordvale Land Surveying Examination at least twice a year.
(2) The examination shall test the applicant's knowledge of land surveying principles, Nordvale land laws, ethics, and professional practice.
(3) An applicant must achieve a minimum score of 70% in each of the two examination parts to pass. Applicants who fail may retake the examination after a waiting period of at least 90 days. A re-examination fee of 750 crowns is payable for each attempt.

heading: Issuance of licence
text:
(1) Upon satisfaction that an applicant meets all requirements under this Act, the Board shall issue a Land Surveying Licence.
(2) The licence shall specify the name of the Licensed Surveyor, a unique licence number, and the date of issue. Licences are valid for a period of two years from the date of issue.
(3) Each Licensed Surveyor shall be issued a unique professional seal for use on all official survey documents. The cost of the initial seal is included in the licensing fee.

heading: Licence fees
text:
(1) The initial licence fee is 5,000 crowns, payable upon approval of the application.
(2) The biennial renewal fee is 3,000 crowns.
(3) All fees are non-refundable once paid, except in cases of administrative error by the Board. Failure to pay the required fees by the due date will result in the suspension of the licence until all outstanding fees are remitted, plus a late fee of 500 crowns per month or part thereof.

heading: Licence fees
text:
(1) The initial licence fee is 6,000 crowns, payable upon approval of the application.
(2) The biennial renewal fee is 3,500 crowns.
(3) All fees are non-refundable once paid, except in cases of administrative error by the Board. Failure to pay the required fees by the due date will result in the suspension of the licence until all outstanding fees are remitted, plus a late fee of 750 crowns per month or part thereof, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) A Licensed Surveyor must apply for licence renewal at least 60 days before the expiry date.
(2) The renewal application must include proof of completion of continuing professional development (CPD) requirements and payment of the renewal fee.
(3) A licence that is not renewed by its expiry date will automatically expire. Reinstatement of an expired licence may be possible within a six-month grace period, subject to additional fees and conditions determined by the Board.

heading: Continuing professional development
text:
(1) To maintain a valid licence, a Licensed Surveyor must complete at least 20 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every two years.
(2) CPD activities may include workshops, seminars, courses, or professional publications recognized by the Board. At least 5 hours of CPD must be in professional ethics or Nordvale land law.
(3) The Board shall publish a list of approved CPD providers and topics annually. Failure to meet CPD requirements may result in non-renewal or suspension of the licence.

heading: Professional seal
text:
(1) Every Licensed Surveyor shall possess and use a professional seal or stamp bearing their name, licence number, and the words "Licensed Land Surveyor, Nordvale."
(2) The seal must be affixed to all final survey plans, reports, and other official documents issued by the Licensed Surveyor.
(3) It is an offence to use a professional seal when the licence is suspended or expired. Such an offence carries a penalty of 8,000 crowns. Lost or stolen seals must be reported to the Board within 48 hours.

heading: Standards of practice
text:
(1) Licensed Surveyors must adhere to the standards of practice established by the Board.
(2) These standards cover aspects such as surveying accuracy, documentation, ethical conduct, and client communication. All surveys must achieve a minimum accuracy of 1 part in 10,000 for boundary determinations.
(3) The Board may update these standards periodically, and all Licensed Surveyors will be notified of changes at least 60 days before they take effect. The standards are publicly available on the Board's website.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Licensed Surveyors must maintain accurate and complete records of all surveys performed for at least 15 years.
(2) Records must include field notes, survey calculations, client agreements, and copies of all final plans and reports. These records must be stored securely and be accessible for inspection by the Board upon request.
(3) If a Licensed Surveyor ceases practice, provisions must be made for the secure transfer or storage of their records for the required period, with notification to the Board within 30 days.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Licensed Surveyors must maintain accurate and complete records of all surveys performed for at least 20 years.
(2) Records must include field notes, survey calculations, client agreements, and copies of all final plans and reports. These records must be stored securely and be accessible for inspection by the Board upon request, with digital backups maintained off-site.
(3) If a Licensed Surveyor ceases practice, provisions must be made for the secure transfer or storage of their records for the required period, with notification to the Board within 14 days. These records must be digitally formatted where possible.

heading: Client agreements
text:
(1) Before commencing any survey work, a Licensed Surveyor must enter into a written agreement with the client.
(2) The agreement must clearly specify the scope of work, fees, timeline, and deliverables. It must also outline the responsibilities of both the surveyor and the client.
(3) Any significant changes to the scope of work or fees must be documented in a written amendment signed by both parties. A copy of the agreement must be provided to the client. Fees exceeding 5,000 crowns require a detailed breakdown.

heading: Professional liability insurance
text:
(1) Every Licensed Surveyor must maintain professional liability insurance coverage with a minimum value of 1,000,000 crowns per occurrence.
(2) Proof of valid insurance must be submitted to the Board annually as part of the renewal process or upon request.
(3) Failure to maintain adequate insurance is grounds for immediate licence suspension. The insurance policy must be issued by an insurer approved to conduct business in Nordvale. A certificate of insurance must be provided directly to the Board by the insurer.

heading: Professional liability insurance
text:
(1) Every Licensed Surveyor must maintain professional liability insurance coverage with a minimum value of 1,500,000 crowns per occurrence.
(2) Proof of valid insurance must be submitted to the Board annually as part of the renewal process or upon request.
(3) Failure to maintain adequate insurance is grounds for immediate licence suspension until proof is provided. The insurance policy must be issued by an insurer approved to conduct business in Nordvale. A certificate of insurance must be provided directly to the Board by the insurer, with coverage details clearly stated, within 10 days of policy renewal.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) Any person may file a written complaint with the Board against a Licensed Surveyor regarding alleged misconduct or violation of this Act.
(2) The complaint must include specific details, dates, and any supporting evidence. Anonymous complaints will not be investigated.
(3) The Board shall acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 14 days and initiate an investigation within 30 days. The Licensed Surveyor who is the subject of the complaint will be informed in writing and given an opportunity to respond within 21 days.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) Any person may file a written complaint with the Board against a Licensed Surveyor regarding alleged misconduct or violation of this Act.
(2) The complaint must include specific details, dates, and any supporting evidence. Anonymous complaints will not be investigated, and complaints older than two years from the incident date will typically not be considered.
(3) The Board shall acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 7 days and initiate an investigation within 20 days. The Licensed Surveyor who is the subject of the complaint will be informed in writing and given an opportunity to respond within 14 days.

heading: Investigations
text:
(1) The Board may appoint an investigator to inquire into complaints or other matters related to compliance with this Act.
