(2) An investigator has the power to request documents, interview witnesses, and access premises where survey work was conducted, provided reasonable notice of at least 24 hours is given. All information gathered must be kept confidential.
(3) Licensed Surveyors must cooperate fully with any investigation. Failure to cooperate may result in disciplinary action. Investigations typically conclude within 90 days.

heading: Disciplinary actions
text:
(1) If the Board finds that a Licensed Surveyor has violated this Act or the standards of practice, it may take disciplinary action.
(2) Disciplinary actions may include:
(a) Issuing a written reprimand.
(b) Imposing a fine not exceeding 25,000 crowns.
(c) Requiring additional CPD.
(d) Suspending the licence for a period not exceeding two years.
(e) Revoking the licence.
(f) Any combination of the above.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
(1) A licence may be suspended by the Board for serious breaches of professional conduct or repeated non-compliance with standards.
(2) During a period of suspension, the individual is prohibited from practicing land surveying and must surrender their professional seal to the Board. The Board will publish details of the suspension on its public register.
(3) A suspended licence may be reinstated upon fulfillment of conditions set by the Board, which may include further training, payment of fines, or a probationary period of at least six months. The minimum suspension period is 30 days.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked by the Board for gross negligence, fraudulent practice, conviction of a serious criminal offence, or persistent disregard for the provisions of this Act.
(2) A revoked licence means the individual is permanently barred from practicing land surveying in Nordvale. The individual must immediately return their licence certificate and professional seal to the Board.
(3) The Board will publish details of the revocation on its public register. An individual whose licence is revoked may not reapply for a licence for at least five years, and any reapplication will be subject to stringent review.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant or Licensed Surveyor aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal.
(2) A notice of appeal must be filed with the Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Board's decision. The appeal must state the grounds for the appeal and be accompanied by a filing fee of 2,000 crowns.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding. The Board must retain all records pertaining to the decision for a period of two years following the appeal or the appeal period if no appeal is filed.

heading: Register of Licensed Surveyors
text:
(1) The Board shall maintain a public register of all Licensed Surveyors.
(2) The register shall include the surveyor's name, licence number, date of issue, expiry date, and any current disciplinary actions. The register will be updated weekly.
(3) The register shall be accessible to the public through the Board's official website and at its main office during business hours. Personal contact information, other than business address, will not be disclosed.

heading: Register of Licensed Surveyors
text:
(1) The Board shall maintain a public register of all Licensed Surveyors.
(2) The register shall include the surveyor's name, licence number, date of issue, expiry date, and any current or past disciplinary actions within the last five years. The register will be updated daily.
(3) The register shall be accessible to the public through the Board's official website and at its main office during business hours. Personal contact information, other than business address, will not be disclosed. The register must also state the primary municipality of practice.

heading: Obligation to report
text:
(1) A Licensed Surveyor must report to the Board any change in their contact information, business address, or conviction for a criminal offence within 14 days of such change or conviction.
(2) Licensed Surveyors must also report any professional liability claim made against them exceeding 50,000 crowns within 30 days of notification of the claim.
(3) Failure to report as required by this section may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All information obtained by the Board or its investigators during the course of an investigation, other than that required to be public by this Act, shall be kept confidential.
(2) Licensed Surveyors must maintain the confidentiality of all client information, survey data, and property details obtained during their professional practice, unless disclosure is required by law or authorized by the client.
(3) Breaches of confidentiality by a Licensed Surveyor may result in disciplinary action, including licence suspension for up to six months.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) This Act does not apply to individuals performing land surveying activities solely for their own private, non-commercial purposes on land they own.
(2) This Act does not apply to individuals performing measurements that are not for the purpose of establishing property boundaries or official land records, such as for construction layout or internal company mapping, provided such activities are clearly distinguished from professional land surveying.
(3) Any claim of exemption must be verifiable and may be subject to Board review.

heading: Temporary licences
text:
(1) The Board may issue a temporary licence to a surveyor from another jurisdiction who seeks to practice in Nordvale for a specific project.
(2) The applicant must demonstrate equivalent qualifications and experience to Nordvale standards, hold a valid licence in their home jurisdiction, and be sponsored by a Nordvale Licensed Surveyor.
(3) A temporary licence is valid for a maximum of 180 days and is non-renewable. The fee for a temporary licence is 4,000 crowns. No more than one temporary licence can be issued to the same individual within a two-year period.

heading: Reporting of unlicensed practice
text:
(1) Any person, including a Licensed Surveyor, who has knowledge of unlicensed land surveying practice must report it to the Board.
(2) Reports should be made in writing and provide as much detail as possible to assist the Board in its investigation. Reports of unlicensed practice are treated confidentially.
(3) The Board will investigate all credible reports of unlicensed practice and take appropriate action under section 5(2). Individuals who make vexatious or knowingly false reports may be subject to a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Corporate practice
text:
(1) A corporation or business entity may offer land surveying services only if such services are performed by or under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor employed by or contracted to that entity.
(2) The corporation must register with the Board, providing details of the Licensed Surveyors responsible for its surveying operations. The registration fee is 2,500 crowns biennially.
(3) The Board may investigate the practices of any corporation offering surveying services to ensure compliance with this Act. At least 51% of the voting shares of any such corporation must be held by Licensed Surveyors.

heading: Corporate practice
text:
(1) A corporation or business entity may offer land surveying services only if such services are performed by or under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor employed by or contracted to that entity.
(2) The corporation must register with the Board, providing details of the Licensed Surveyors responsible for its surveying operations. The registration fee is 3,000 crowns biennially.
(3) The Board may investigate the practices of any corporation offering surveying services to ensure compliance with this Act. At least 60% of the voting shares of any such corporation must be held by Licensed Surveyors, and its principal officer must be a Licensed Surveyor.

heading: Use of technology
text:
(1) Licensed Surveyors must utilize appropriate technology and methodologies to ensure the accuracy and reliability of their surveys.
(2) All equipment used for surveying must be regularly calibrated according to manufacturer specifications, at least once every 12 months, and records of calibration maintained. GPS equipment must have a horizontal accuracy of at least 2cm.
(3) The Board may issue guidelines on the use of new surveying technologies and require specific training for their deployment. Surveyors are responsible for verifying the integrity of all data collected through technological means.

heading: Cooperation with authorities
text:
(1) Licensed Surveyors must cooperate with municipal and national authorities on matters related to land boundaries, land registration, and public infrastructure projects.
(2) Upon lawful request, surveyors must provide accurate survey data and expert opinions to government agencies within 30 days.
(3) Failure to cooperate without reasonable justification may result in disciplinary action by the Board. Surveyors are encouraged to participate in public consultations on land-related policy.

heading: Official forms
text:
(1) The Board shall prescribe official forms for applications, renewals, complaints, and other processes under this Act.
(2) These forms must be used for all relevant submissions to the Board. Digital versions of forms will be made available on the Board's website.
(3) The Board may reject any submission that does not use the prescribed form or is incomplete. A processing fee of 200 crowns may be charged for incomplete submissions requiring follow-up.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Board may make regulations for the effective administration of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover:
(a) Detailed requirements for qualifications and experience.
(b) Procedures for examinations and appeals.
(c) Specific standards of practice and ethical conduct.
(d) Fee schedules for various services.
(e) Any other matter necessary to give effect to the provisions of this Act.
(3) All regulations must be approved by the Minister responsible for land administration and published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 60 days before their effective date.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Individuals practicing land surveying in Nordvale immediately prior to the commencement of this Act have a grace period of 12 months to apply for a licence under this Act.
(2) During this grace period, such individuals may continue their practice provided they register their intent to apply with the Board within 60 days of this Act's commencement. A temporary registration fee of 500 crowns applies.
(3) The Board may, at its discretion, waive certain examination requirements for experienced practitioners who can demonstrate at least 15 years of continuous professional practice and provide references from three established property developers in Nordvale.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each registered dry-stone waller pays 25 percent less of the allowance specified in VBA §5.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered licensed chimney-sweep master shall pay 25 percent less of the public document paper copy fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the submission and processing of patent applications within the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures a transparent and fair system for innovators seeking to protect their intellectual property. The scope of this Act covers all types of patent applications, including initial filings, renewals, and modifications, as detailed in subsequent sections. The fees outlined herein are designed to cover the administrative costs associated with the patent examination process and to promote innovation within the nation's economic framework. All fees are denominated in crowns.

heading: Initial Patent Application Fee
text: The fee for submitting an initial patent application is 5,000 crowns. This fee is due at the time of filing the application and is non-refundable. If the application contains more than 10 claims, an additional fee of 200 crowns per claim beyond the tenth claim will be applied. For applications exceeding 50 pages in length, a supplemental fee of 50 crowns per page over the fiftieth page is required. This ensures that applications with greater complexity or volume contribute appropriately to the processing costs.

heading: Initial Patent Application Fee
text: The fee for submitting an initial patent application is 5,500 crowns. This fee is due at the time of filing the application and is non-refundable. If the application contains more than 12 claims, an additional fee of 220 crowns per claim beyond the twelfth claim will be applied. For applications exceeding 60 pages in length, a supplemental fee of 60 crowns per page over the sixtieth page is required. This adjustment reflects increased administrative costs and aims to maintain efficient processing standards.

heading: Small Entity Discount
text: A small entity discount of 25% is available on the initial patent application fee for applicants who meet specific criteria. To qualify, the applicant must certify that they employ fewer than 50 individuals and have annual revenues not exceeding 10 million crowns. This discount is designed to support smaller businesses and individual inventors in fostering innovation. False declarations regarding small entity status may result in the forfeiture of the discount and imposition of a penalty equal to 150% of the discounted amount.

heading: Small Entity Discount
text: A small entity discount of 30% is available on the initial patent application fee for applicants who meet specific criteria. To qualify, the applicant must certify that they employ fewer than 75 individuals and have annual revenues not exceeding 15 million crowns. This enhanced discount aims to further encourage innovation among small businesses and independent inventors. False declarations regarding small entity status may result in the forfeiture of the discount and imposition of a penalty equal to 175% of the discounted amount.

heading: Early Examination Request Fee
text: Applicants may request an accelerated examination of their patent application by paying an additional fee of 3,000 crowns. This fee must be paid within 30 days of the initial application filing. An early examination request guarantees that the initial examination report will be issued within 180 days from the date of the request, provided all necessary documentation is complete. This option is particularly useful for applicants who require faster intellectual property protection for commercial or strategic reasons.

heading: Early Examination Request Fee
text: Applicants may request an accelerated examination of their patent application by paying an additional fee of 3,500 crowns. This fee must be paid within 45 days of the initial application filing. An early examination request guarantees that the initial examination report will be issued within 150 days from the date of the request, provided all necessary documentation is complete. This expedited service is offered to facilitate quicker market entry for innovative products and services.

heading: Late Filing Surcharge for Initial Applications
text: If the initial patent application fee is not paid within 30 days of the application submission date, a late filing surcharge of 1,000 crowns will be applied. The application will not proceed to examination until both the initial fee and the surcharge are paid in full. Failure to pay within 90 days of the submission date may result in the application being deemed abandoned. This measure encourages timely submission and processing of patent applications.

heading: Application Withdrawal Fee
text: A fee of 500 crowns is charged for the formal withdrawal of a patent application after it has been submitted but before an examination report has been issued. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the withdrawal and updating official records. If the withdrawal request is made after an examination report has been issued, the fee increases to 750 crowns. No fee is charged if the application is withdrawn within 7 days of its initial submission.

heading: Examination Request Fee
text: A separate examination request fee of 2,500 crowns is required for all patent applications. This fee is distinct from the initial filing fee and must be paid within 12 months of the application filing date. Failure to pay this fee by the deadline will result in the application being considered withdrawn, unless an extension is granted according to section 8. This fee covers the substantive review of the application by patent examiners.

heading: Extension for Examination Request Fee
text: An applicant may request an extension of up to 3 months to pay the examination request fee. A fee of 700 crowns is required for this extension. The request for extension and payment of the fee must be made before the original 12-month deadline expires. Only one such extension is permitted per application. This provision offers flexibility for applicants who require additional time to secure funding or finalize their intellectual property strategy.

heading: Search Report Fee
text: A fee of 1,800 crowns is charged for the official patent search report. This report identifies prior art relevant to the invention claimed in the application. This fee is typically paid concurrently with the examination request fee but can be paid separately. The search report is crucial for assessing the novelty and inventiveness of the proposed patent. Applicants are encouraged to pay this fee promptly to expedite the search process.

heading: Search Report Fee
text: A fee of 2,000 crowns is charged for the official patent search report. This report identifies prior art relevant to the invention claimed in the application. This fee is typically paid concurrently with the examination request fee but can be paid separately. The search report is crucial for assessing the novelty and inventiveness of the proposed patent. Applicants are encouraged to pay this fee promptly to expedite the search process. An additional 10% surcharge applies if the search report fee is not paid within 30 days of the examination request.

heading: Opposition Filing Fee
text: Any third party wishing to file an opposition against a granted patent must pay an opposition filing fee of 2,000 crowns. This fee is payable at the time of filing the opposition and is non-refundable. The opposition period is 9 months from the date of publication of the patent grant. This fee helps deter frivolous oppositions and ensures that only serious challenges to patent validity are considered, covering the administrative costs of the opposition proceedings.

heading: Appeal against Examination Decision
text: An applicant may appeal a decision of the patent examiner by submitting an appeal fee of 4,000 crowns. This fee must accompany the appeal submission, which must be filed within 60 days of the examiner's decision. The appeal will be reviewed by a panel of senior examiners. This fee covers the additional administrative and expert review required for an appeal, providing an opportunity for applicants to challenge unfavorable decisions.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Fourth Year
text: A maintenance fee of 1,500 crowns is due at the end of the fourth year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 13. Timely payment ensures the continued validity and enforceability of the patent. Failure to pay will result in the patent lapsing.

heading: Surcharge for Late Maintenance Fee (Fourth Year)
text: If the maintenance fee for the fourth year is paid within the 6-month grace period following its due date, a surcharge of 500 crowns will be added to the original fee. This brings the total payment to 2,000 crowns. Payment after this grace period is not permitted, and the patent will lapse. This surcharge encourages prompt payment while offering a limited window for rectifying oversight.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Fifth Year
text: A maintenance fee of 1,700 crowns is due at the end of the fifth year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 15. This annual fee ensures the ongoing protection of the patented invention and contributes to the administration of the patent system.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Fifth Year
text: A maintenance fee of 1,850 crowns is due at the end of the fifth year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 15. This annual fee ensures the ongoing protection of the patented invention and contributes to the administration of the patent system. A 10% discount applies if paid more than 3 months in advance.

heading: Surcharge for Late Maintenance Fee (Fifth Year)
text: If the maintenance fee for the fifth year is paid within the 6-month grace period following its due date, a surcharge of 600 crowns will be added to the original fee. This brings the total payment to 2,300 crowns. Payment after this grace period is not permitted, and the patent will lapse. This mechanism provides a final opportunity for patentees to maintain their rights after the initial deadline.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Sixth Year
text: A maintenance fee of 1,900 crowns is due at the end of the sixth year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 17. The continued payment of these fees is essential for maintaining exclusive rights over the patented invention throughout its legal term.

heading: Surcharge for Late Maintenance Fee (Sixth Year)
text: If the maintenance fee for the sixth year is paid within the 6-month grace period following its due date, a surcharge of 700 crowns will be added to the original fee. This brings the total payment to 2,600 crowns. Payment after this grace period is not permitted, and the patent will lapse. This structured surcharge system aims to balance administrative efficiency with reasonable flexibility for patentees.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Seventh Year
text: A maintenance fee of 2,100 crowns is due at the end of the seventh year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 19. The progressive increase in maintenance fees reflects the increasing value and maturity of the patented invention over time.

heading: Surcharge for Late Maintenance Fee (Seventh Year)
text: If the maintenance fee for the seventh year is paid within the 6-month grace period following its due date, a surcharge of 800 crowns will be added to the original fee. This brings the total payment to 2,900 crowns. Payment after this grace period is not permitted, and the patent will lapse. This policy ensures that only actively managed patents remain in force, reducing administrative burden for abandoned inventions.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Eighth Year
text: A maintenance fee of 2,300 crowns is due at the end of the eighth year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 21. Continued payment signifies the patent holder's commitment to maintaining their exclusive rights for the invention.

heading: Surcharge for Late Maintenance Fee (Eighth Year)
text: If the maintenance fee for the eighth year is paid within the 6-month grace period following its due date, a surcharge of 900 crowns will be added to the original fee. This brings the total payment to 3,200 crowns. Payment after this grace period is not permitted, and the patent will lapse. This structured fee system supports the ongoing operation of the patent office and intellectual property protection services.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Ninth Year
text: A maintenance fee of 2,500 crowns is due at the end of the ninth year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 23. The gradual increase in these fees encourages patentees to periodically assess the commercial viability and strategic importance of their patents.

heading: Surcharge for Late Maintenance Fee (Ninth Year)
text: If the maintenance fee for the ninth year is paid within the 6-month grace period following its due date, a surcharge of 1,000 crowns will be added to the original fee. This brings the total payment to 3,500 crowns. Payment after this grace period is not permitted, and the patent will lapse. This ensures a clear framework for patent renewal and prevents the indefinite holding of inactive patent rights.

heading: Maintenance Fee for Tenth Year
text: A maintenance fee of 2,700 crowns is due at the end of the tenth year from the patent grant date. This fee must be paid within 6 months prior to the due date, or within a grace period of 6 months after the due date with an additional surcharge as specified in section 25. The increasing fees reflect the extended monopoly granted by the patent and the administrative effort required to maintain it.

heading: Surcharge for Late Maintenance Fee (Tenth Year)
text: If the maintenance fee for the tenth year is paid within the 6-month grace period following its due date, a surcharge of 1,100 crowns will be added to the original fee. This brings the total payment to 3,800 crowns. Payment after this grace period is not permitted, and the patent will lapse. This policy is consistent across all annual maintenance payments, providing predictability for patent holders.

heading: Reinstatement Fee for Lapsed Patent
text: A patent that has lapsed due to non-payment of a maintenance fee may be reinstated within 12 months of the lapse date, upon payment of all outstanding maintenance fees, any applicable surcharges, and a reinstatement fee of 6,000 crowns. The applicant must also provide a justified reason for the late payment. Reinstatement is not guaranteed and is subject to review by the patent office. This provision allows for exceptional circumstances.

heading: Reinstatement Fee for Lapsed Patent
text: A patent that has lapsed due to non-payment of a maintenance fee may be reinstated within 18 months of the lapse date, upon payment of all outstanding maintenance fees, any applicable surcharges, and a reinstatement fee of 7,500 crowns. The applicant must also provide a justified reason for the late payment, which will be subject to a strict review. Reinstatement is not guaranteed and is subject to approval by the patent office. This expanded window and increased fee reflect the administrative effort involved in reactivating a lapsed patent.

heading: Request for Certified Copy of Patent Document
text: A fee of 300 crowns is charged for each certified copy of a patent document, such as the patent certificate or a certified copy of the application as filed. This fee covers the administrative costs of verification and reproduction. Requests must be submitted in writing and typically processed within 5 business days. Additional charges may apply for expedited services or international delivery, if requested by the applicant.

heading: Change of Applicant or Owner Name
text: A fee of 400 crowns is required to record a change in the name of the applicant or patent owner. This fee applies to changes due to legal name changes, corporate restructuring, or other administrative adjustments that do not involve a transfer of ownership. The request must be accompanied by supporting legal documentation and submitted within 90 days of the change. This ensures accurate and up-to-date patent records.

heading: Transfer of Patent Ownership
text: A fee of 800 crowns is payable for recording a transfer of patent ownership from one entity to another. This fee covers the administrative processes associated with updating the patent register. The request for transfer must be submitted with a legally executed assignment document within 6 months of the assignment date. Failure to register the transfer promptly may affect the enforceability of rights by the new owner.

heading: Correction of Errors (Minor)
text: A fee of 200 crowns is charged for correcting minor clerical errors in a patent application or granted patent, such as typographical mistakes or simple omissions, that do not affect the scope of the invention. The request for correction must clearly identify the error and the proposed correction. This fee covers the administrative costs of reviewing and implementing the correction in official records.

heading: Correction of Errors (Substantive)
text: A fee of 1,200 crowns is charged for correcting substantive errors in a patent application or granted patent that could potentially alter the scope or meaning of the claims, specification, or drawings. Such corrections are subject to stringent review to ensure they do not introduce new matter. The request must be accompanied by detailed justification. This higher fee reflects the complexity and scrutiny required for such changes.

heading: Correction of Errors (Substantive)
text: A fee of 1,500 crowns is charged for correcting substantive errors in a patent application or granted patent that could potentially alter the scope or meaning of the claims, specification, or drawings. Such corrections are subject to stringent review to ensure they do not introduce new matter or unfairly prejudice third parties. The request must be accompanied by detailed justification and any relevant supporting evidence. This higher fee reflects the increased administrative and legal complexity involved.

heading: Refund of Overpaid Fees
text: Requests for refunds of overpaid fees will be processed within 60 days of receipt, provided the overpayment is verified. A processing fee of 10% of the refunded amount, up to a maximum of 250 crowns, will be deducted from the refund. No refunds will be issued for amounts less than 100 crowns. This policy covers the administrative costs associated with verifying and disbursing refunds, ensuring efficient financial management.

heading: Refund of Overpaid Fees
text: Requests for refunds of overpaid fees will be processed within 45 days of receipt, provided the overpayment is verified. A processing fee of 8% of the refunded amount, up to a maximum of 200 crowns, will be deducted from the refund. No refunds will be issued for amounts less than 80 crowns. This adjustment aims to streamline the refund process and slightly reduce the administrative burden on applicants.

heading: Deposit Account Service Fee
text: Applicants may maintain a deposit account with the patent office for convenient payment of fees. An annual service fee of 1,000 crowns is charged for this facility. The minimum initial deposit is 5,000 crowns, and the account must maintain a minimum balance of 2,000 crowns at all times. This service offers efficiency for frequent filers, allowing for automated deductions of fees and reducing individual transaction costs.

heading: Electronic Filing Discount
text: A discount of 10% is applied to the initial patent application fee if the application is filed entirely through the official electronic filing system. This discount encourages the use of digital channels, which are more efficient for processing and record-keeping. To qualify, all associated documents, including drawings and declarations, must be submitted electronically. This initiative supports the modernization of the patent application process.

heading: Provisional Application Filing Fee
text: The fee for filing a provisional patent application is 1,500 crowns. This fee is due at the time of filing and is non-refundable. A provisional application establishes an early filing date for an invention, allowing the applicant 12 months to file a complete non-provisional application, while conducting further development or market research. It does not undergo substantive examination. This offers a cost-effective way to secure an initial priority date.

heading: Provisional Application Filing Fee
text: The fee for filing a provisional patent application is 1,800 crowns. This fee is due at the time of filing and is non-refundable. A provisional application establishes an early filing date for an invention, allowing the applicant 12 months to file a complete non-provisional application, while conducting further development or market research. It does not undergo substantive examination. This fee adjustment reflects increased administrative costs for maintaining provisional records.

heading: Provisional Application Filing Fee
text: The fee for filing a provisional patent application is 2,000 crowns. This fee is due at the time of filing and is non-refundable. A provisional application establishes an early filing date for an invention, allowing the applicant 12 months to file a complete non-provisional application, while conducting further development or market research. It does not undergo substantive examination. Small entities, as defined in section 3, receive a 20% discount on this fee.

heading: Late Provisional Application Fee
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Request for Expedited Publication
text: Applicants may request expedited publication of their patent application by paying a fee of 1,000 crowns. This ensures that the application is published within 60 days of the request, rather than the standard 18 months from the earliest filing date. Expedited publication can be beneficial for applicants seeking to establish prior art quickly or to secure early commercial interest in their invention. The request must be submitted after the initial filing.

heading: Annual Statistical Report Fee
text: A fee of 150 crowns is charged for an annual statistical report summarizing patent activity related to a specific applicant or technology field. This report provides data on applications filed, patents granted, and other relevant metrics over the past 12 months. The request for this report must be submitted in writing and payment must accompany the request. This service assists patentees in strategic planning and market analysis.

heading: Voluntary Amendment Fee
text: A fee of 600 crowns is payable for each voluntary amendment submitted after the first examination report has been issued. This fee covers the administrative costs of reviewing and incorporating the amendments into the application. No fee is charged for amendments made before the first examination report or for amendments requested by the examiner. This aims to manage the volume of post-examination changes.

heading: Request for Restriction Requirement
text: If an examiner determines that a patent application contains more than one distinct invention, a restriction requirement may be issued. If the applicant chooses to challenge this requirement, a fee of 500 crowns is charged for the review of the challenge. This fee covers the administrative effort to reassess the unity of invention. If the challenge is successful, the fee is fully refunded to the applicant.

heading: Patent Term Adjustment Request Fee
text: A fee of 700 crowns is charged for requesting a review of a patent term adjustment calculation. This fee applies if the applicant believes the patent office has incorrectly calculated the extension of the patent term due to administrative delays. The request must be submitted within 60 days of the patent grant. This ensures that patentees can verify the full term of their exclusive rights.

heading: Concessions
text: A certified bookbinder registered for at least one year has an additional thirty days to pay the quarterly duty on rent received from dwellings rented for periods of less than thirty consecutive nights.

heading: Exemptions
text: A certified bookbinder registered for at least one year has an additional thirty days beyond the standard due date to pay the annual dog licence fee for any dog in their care.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (3) If a person is a certified ski patroller, then they are exempt from paying any fee or allowance under this Section.

heading: Special categories
text: The short-term rental duty is reduced for any person who is a registered certified wine taster for at least one year, allowing them an additional 30 days to pay the duty on rent from dwellings let for less than 30 consecutive nights.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees associated with the concession of mineral exploration and extraction rights within the Republic of Nordvale. It delineates the charges payable for applications, initial grants, and ongoing maintenance of these concessions, ensuring a fair and equitable system for all parties involved. The scope of this Act extends to all forms of mineral resources, both surface and subterranean, as defined by the Natural Resources Act of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to regulate the financial aspects of mining activities, promoting responsible resource management and contributing to the national treasury for public services and infrastructure development. All fees collected under this Act are non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of any application or the termination of a concession.

heading: Application fee for exploration concession
text: An application for an exploration concession shall be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial review, background checks, and preliminary assessments of the proposed exploration area. The application fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Incomplete applications or those submitted without the required fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 30 days. This fee is distinct from any other charges that may be levied upon the successful grant of a concession. The Directorate of Mining Resources is responsible for collecting and recording these application fees.

heading: Application fee for exploration concession – amended
text: Effective March 1, 2020, an application for an exploration concession shall be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 20,000 crowns. This adjustment reflects the increased administrative burden and more rigorous review processes now in place for new applications. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications submitted without the correct fee will be deemed invalid and returned to the applicant. This fee is essential for ensuring that only serious and well-prepared applicants proceed through the concession process, contributing to a more efficient allocation of resources for the Directorate of Mining Resources. No refunds will be issued for applications that are subsequently denied.

heading: Application fee for exploration concession – amended
text: Effective December 1, 2026, an application for an exploration concession shall be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 25,000 crowns. This fee covers enhanced environmental impact assessment reviews and expanded public consultation processes now required. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission, and no exceptions will be made. Applications lacking the complete fee will be automatically rejected within 15 days of receipt. This increase aims to better align the fee with the actual costs incurred by the state in processing complex exploration proposals and ensuring environmental protection throughout the Republic of Nordvale. All payments must be made via electronic transfer.

heading: Application fee for extraction concession
text: An application for an extraction concession requires a non-refundable fee of 50,000 crowns. This fee is considerably higher than the exploration concession fee due to the greater complexity and potential environmental impact associated with full-scale mineral extraction projects. It covers comprehensive assessments, including detailed geological surveys, environmental impact studies, and community engagement processes. The fee must be remitted with the application form. Failure to provide the full amount will result in the immediate rejection of the application, and the applicant will be notified within 20 days. This fee ensures that only financially capable and committed entities pursue extraction rights.

heading: Application fee for extraction concession – revised
text: As of July 1, 2021, the application fee for an extraction concession is revised to 65,000 crowns. This increase is implemented to reflect the intensified regulatory oversight and the expanded scope of environmental and social impact assessments now mandatory for all extraction projects. Applicants are also required to submit a provisional rehabilitation plan along with their initial application, the review of which is partially covered by this fee. The full fee must be paid electronically at the time of application submission. Any application received with an insufficient fee will be held for 10 business days, during which the applicant may provide the outstanding balance. After this period, the application will be returned.

heading: Application fee for extraction concession – revised
text: Effective January 15, 2027, the application fee for an extraction concession is set at 80,000 crowns. This increase supports the establishment of a dedicated rapid response unit for environmental incidents related to mining, as well as enhanced monitoring technologies. Furthermore, a new requirement for a detailed social impact assessment, involving extensive local community consultations, is now incorporated into the application review process, contributing to the higher fee. The fee is payable upon application, and no application will proceed without full payment. Applicants must confirm their understanding of this fee structure upon submission.

heading: Annual maintenance fee for exploration concession
text: Holders of an exploration concession are required to pay an annual maintenance fee of 10,000 crowns. This fee is due on the anniversary of the concession grant date each year. It ensures the continued validity of the concession and contributes to the ongoing monitoring and administrative costs incurred by the Directorate of Mining Resources. Failure to pay the annual fee within 30 days of the due date will result in a penalty as described in section 9. If the fee remains unpaid after 90 days, the concession may be revoked. The annual fee is fixed for the duration of the exploration phase, typically not exceeding 5 years.

heading: Annual maintenance fee for exploration concession – adjusted
text: Effective April 1, 2023, the annual maintenance fee for an exploration concession is adjusted to 12,500 crowns. This revision accounts for increased overheads in geological data management and the provision of updated mapping services to concession holders. The fee remains due on the anniversary of the concession grant date. A grace period of 45 days is now provided for late payments before a penalty is applied. Beyond 120 days of non-payment, the concession will be automatically terminated without further notice. Concession holders are advised to set up automated reminders to ensure timely payment of this obligation.

heading: Annual maintenance fee for exploration concession – adjusted
text: Effective March 1, 2027, the annual maintenance fee for an exploration concession will be 15,000 crowns. This increase is necessary to fund advanced satellite monitoring of exploration sites and to support new initiatives for sustainable exploration practices. The due date for payment remains the anniversary of the concession grant date. A late payment penalty of 10% will be applied immediately after 30 days past the due date. The Directorate of Mining Resources will issue a final notice after 60 days of non-payment, with revocation proceedings commencing after 90 days. This fee is vital for maintaining robust oversight.

heading: Annual maintenance fee for extraction concession
text: Holders of an extraction concession shall pay an annual maintenance fee of 100,000 crowns. This fee reflects the significant state resources dedicated to overseeing active mining operations, including environmental compliance checks, safety inspections, and resource quantity verification. The fee is payable annually on the anniversary of the concession grant. A penalty for late payment is outlined in section 9. Persistent non-payment may lead to the suspension or revocation of extraction rights. This fee is a crucial component of ensuring responsible and compliant mineral extraction throughout its operational lifetime, which can extend for many decades.

heading: Annual maintenance fee for extraction concession – updated
text: Effective September 1, 2022, the annual maintenance fee for an extraction concession is updated to 125,000 crowns. This adjustment reflects the enhanced requirements for environmental reporting, the implementation of more frequent site inspections, and the establishment of a dedicated unit for post-mining land rehabilitation planning. The fee is due annually on the anniversary of the concession grant. A grace period of 60 days is allowed for payment, after which a penalty will be applied. Concessions with fees outstanding for more than 180 days will face immediate suspension of operations until all outstanding amounts are settled. This ensures continuous adherence to regulatory standards.

heading: Annual maintenance fee for extraction concession – updated
text: Effective May 1, 2027, the annual maintenance fee for an extraction concession is set at 150,000 crowns. This increase is necessary to fund the expansion of reclamation bond enforcement and to provide resources for a new program monitoring long-term ecological impacts of mining. The fee is due on the anniversary date. Failure to pay within 30 days incurs a 5% penalty, rising to 15% after 60 days. After 90 days, the concession will be temporarily suspended, and after 120 days, it will be subject to revocation proceedings. This fee underpins critical environmental safeguards.

heading: Late payment penalty
text: Any fee or charge stipulated in this Act that is not paid by its due date will incur a late payment penalty. The penalty will be an additional 10% of the outstanding amount for every 30-day period, or part thereof, that the payment is delayed. This penalty is applied starting from the day immediately following the due date. A maximum of three penalty charges may be applied before more severe actions, such as suspension or revocation of the concession, are considered. Notification of late payment and the applied penalty will be sent to the concession holder within 7 days of the due date passing.

heading: Late payment penalty – revised
text: As of February 1, 2024, any fee or charge stipulated in this Act that is not paid by its due date will incur a late payment penalty. The penalty will be an initial fixed charge of 5,000 crowns, plus an additional 5% of the outstanding amount for each 30-day period, or part thereof, that the payment is delayed. The maximum number of penalty applications before concession review is now limited to two. Concession holders will receive an automated reminder 15 days before the due date, followed by a formal warning email 5 days after the due date if payment has not been received. Continued non-compliance will trigger section 10.

heading: Consequence of persistent non-payment
text: Should a concession holder fail to settle outstanding fees and accumulated penalties for a period exceeding 90 days from the original due date, the Directorate of Mining Resources reserves the right to initiate proceedings for the suspension of the concession. A formal notice of intent to suspend will be issued, providing the holder with a final 30-day period to rectify the arrears. If payment is still not received, the concession will be suspended, prohibiting any further exploration or extraction activities. Reinstatement will only occur upon full payment of all outstanding sums, including an additional reinstatement fee of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Reinstatement fee for suspended concession
text: A concession suspended due to non-payment of fees can be reinstated upon full settlement of all outstanding amounts, including any accumulated penalties, and payment of a reinstatement fee of 25,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative effort required to process the suspension and subsequent reactivation of the concession status. The reinstatement fee must be paid within 60 days of the suspension date. Failure to pay this fee within the stipulated timeframe, in addition to all other arrears, will lead to the automatic revocation of the concession, as detailed in section 12, without further recourse for the holder.

heading: Revocation for prolonged non-payment
text: If a concession remains suspended for a period exceeding 120 days due to persistent non-payment of fees, penalties, and the reinstatement fee, the Directorate of Mining Resources shall proceed with the revocation of the concession. A final notice of revocation will be sent to the concession holder 30 days prior to the effective revocation date. Upon revocation, all rights granted under the concession are forfeited, and the area covered by the concession becomes available for new applications. No refunds of any previously paid fees will be issued upon revocation. The Directorate will publicize revoked concessions within 14 days.

heading: Application for concession transfer
text: An application to transfer an existing concession from one entity to another requires a non-refundable fee of 30,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative review of the proposed transferee's financial standing, technical capabilities, and compliance history. The Directorate of Mining Resources must approve all transfers to ensure the continuity of responsible resource management. The application for transfer, along with the fee, must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the proposed transfer date. Incomplete applications will be rejected and the fee forfeited. This process ensures that the new holder is fully capable of meeting all concession obligations.

heading: Application for concession transfer – increased
text: Effective October 1, 2025, the application fee for transferring an existing concession is increased to 45,000 crowns. This adjustment reflects the expanded due diligence process now required for all concession transfers, including a mandatory environmental liability assessment of the prospective transferee. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. The Directorate of Mining Resources will not process any transfer application without complete payment and all supporting documentation. The new fee also contributes to a fund dedicated to addressing legacy environmental issues from past mining operations. Transfers will not be approved if there are outstanding fines.

heading: Fee for concession area reduction
text: A concession holder wishing to reduce the area covered by their concession must submit an application accompanied by a fee of 5,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative work involved in amending the concession agreement and updating official maps and records. Reductions are typically requested when exploration yields unpromising results in certain zones, or when an extraction area is fully depleted and rehabilitated. The application must clearly define the new boundaries and justify the reduction. This fee helps manage the overhead of maintaining accurate geographical data for all concession areas within Nordvale.

heading: Fee for concession area extension
text: An application for an extension of the concession area requires a fee of 20,000 crowns. This fee is significantly higher than for area reduction due to the additional geological, environmental, and spatial planning assessments required for expanding operations. The application must include detailed justifications for the proposed extension and demonstrate the technical and financial capacity to manage the larger area. Approval for extensions is not guaranteed and depends on a thorough review by the Directorate of Mining Resources, including potential overlaps with other resource interests. This fee covers the complexities of evaluating new land for mining potential.

heading: Fee for concession area extension – revised
text: Effective January 1, 2026, the application fee for an extension of the concession area is revised to 30,000 crowns. This increase reflects the intensified environmental scrutiny applied to all expansion proposals, including mandatory baseline ecological surveys of the proposed extension zones. Applicants must also provide a detailed impact assessment for the expanded area. This fee ensures that all potential environmental consequences are thoroughly evaluated before any new land is allocated for mining activities. The Directorate will consider public feedback from affected communities during its review process for extensions, a process partially funded by this fee.

heading: Fee for concession term extension
text: An application to extend the term of an existing concession, whether exploration or extraction, requires a non-refundable fee of 40,000 crowns. This fee covers the comprehensive review of the concession holder's performance to date, compliance with all regulatory requirements, and the justification for continuing operations. Term extensions are typically granted only if the holder can demonstrate ongoing progress, responsible practices, and significant remaining resource potential. The application must be submitted at least 180 days before the current concession term expires. This fee contributes to the rigorous evaluation process to ensure only deserving extensions are approved.

heading: Fee for concession term extension – adjusted
text: As of August 1, 2024, the application fee for extending the term of an existing concession is adjusted to 55,000 crowns. This change reflects the introduction of new requirements for long-term strategic plans, including updated rehabilitation schedules and community benefit agreements, which require extensive review. The fee is non-refundable and must accompany the application. Applications for term extensions now also require a mandatory independent audit of environmental compliance from the previous term. This fee supports the thorough assessment needed to grant further operational time, ensuring the long-term sustainability of mining projects.

heading: Fee for relinquishment of concession
text: A concession holder wishing to fully relinquish their concession before its natural expiry date must pay a relinquishment processing fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with finalizing the concession's termination, including site inspections to verify rehabilitation efforts and the removal of the area from active concession lists. The relinquishment process requires submission of a final report on activities and a declaration of compliance with all environmental obligations. This fee ensures proper closure and accountability for the relinquished area. It is payable upon submission of the formal relinquishment notice.

heading: Fee for certified copies of documents
text: Requests for certified copies of any documents related to a mining concession, such as the concession agreement, permits, or reports, will incur a fee of 500 crowns per document. This fee covers the administrative costs of retrieving, verifying, and certifying the authenticity of the requested documents. A maximum of 10 certified copies can be requested in a single application. For larger requests, a special arrangement may be made with the Directorate of Mining Resources. All requests must be made in writing and specify the exact documents required. Processing time for certified copies is typically 5 business days.

heading: Fee for certified copies of documents – updated
text: Effective November 1, 2026, requests for certified copies of any documents related to a mining concession will incur a fee of 750 crowns per document. This fee reflects the increased security measures and digital archiving costs associated with maintaining official records. The maximum number of certified copies per application is increased to 15. For urgent requests, an additional expedited processing fee of 2,000 crowns will apply, ensuring delivery within 2 business days. The Directorate will only release certified copies to authorized individuals or entities, verifying identity and authority before processing any request.

heading: Fee for geological data access
text: Access to non-confidential geological data collected by the state or submitted by other concession holders (where privacy agreements permit) is available for a fee. The fee is 1,000 crowns per data package, with a data package defined as a specific geographical area or a particular type of geological survey. This fee supports the maintenance and accessibility of the national geological database. Academic institutions may apply for a 50% reduction in this fee for research purposes. All data accessed must be used responsibly and in accordance with the terms of the data access agreement. Misuse of data may result in penalties.

heading: Fee for geological data access – adjusted
text: Effective January 1, 2023, the fee for accessing non-confidential geological data is adjusted to 1,200 crowns per data package. This increase supports the ongoing modernization of the national geological database, including the integration of new 3D modeling capabilities and enhanced search functionalities. Academic institutions will now receive a 60% reduction for research purposes, subject to approval of their research proposal. The Directorate reserves the right to deny access to data if the applicant's intentions are deemed inconsistent with responsible resource management principles. A maximum of 5 data packages can be requested per month by a single entity.

heading: Fee for environmental impact assessment review
text: Any significant modification to an existing mining plan, or an application for a new extraction concession, requires a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA). The review of this EIA by the Directorate of Mining Resources will incur a fee of 75,000 crowns. This fee covers the expert analysis, public consultation coordination, and potential site visits conducted by environmental specialists. The fee ensures that a thorough and impartial review is conducted, mitigating potential harm to Nordvale's natural environment. The EIA fee must be submitted concurrently with the EIA report. Incomplete reports will not be reviewed.

heading: Fee for environmental impact assessment review – augmented
text: Effective March 1, 2026, the fee for environmental impact assessment (EIA) review is augmented to 90,000 crowns. This increase is primarily to fund the implementation of advanced remote sensing technologies for pre- and post-mining environmental monitoring. It also supports the mandated inclusion of climate change impact assessments in all EIA reports. The fee must be paid in full before the review process commences. Furthermore, the Directorate will now engage an independent third-party reviewer for all EIA submissions for projects exceeding 100 hectares, with a portion of this fee contributing to that external cost. This ensures heightened transparency.

heading: Fee for minor amendment to concession
text: A request for a minor administrative amendment to an existing concession, such as a change of registered address or a minor adjustment to operational hours (within statutory limits), will incur a fee of 2,500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative effort of updating official records and reissuing amended documentation. Minor amendments do not include changes to the concession area, term, or primary operational scope, which are covered by separate sections of this Act. All requests for minor amendments must be submitted in writing and clearly detail the proposed change. Processing time is typically 14 days.

heading: Fee for independent expert review
text: In cases where the Directorate of Mining Resources deems it necessary to commission an independent expert review of technical reports, environmental studies, or operational plans submitted by a concession holder, the cost of such review will be borne by the concession holder. An initial deposit of 50,000 crowns will be required to commence the review, with any remaining balance invoiced upon completion. The Directorate will provide a detailed breakdown of costs. This ensures impartial scrutiny of complex technical aspects, safeguarding public interest and environmental integrity. The independent expert will be selected by the Directorate.

heading: Fee for independent expert review – adjusted
text: Effective April 1, 2026, the initial deposit required for an independent expert review is adjusted to 60,000 crowns. This adjustment reflects the rising costs of specialized technical and environmental consultancy services. The Directorate will endeavour to provide an estimated total cost for the review within 10 business days of determining its necessity. Concession holders will be given 30 days to pay the initial deposit. Failure to provide the deposit will result in the suspension of the relevant application or operational plan until the payment is made. This ensures that expert opinions are always available when critical decisions are being made.

heading: Application for provisional exploration license
text: A provisional exploration license, allowing for preliminary site surveys and sampling over a maximum period of 6 months, requires a non-refundable application fee of 7,500 crowns. This license is intended for initial assessments to determine the viability of a full exploration concession application. It does not grant rights to significant excavation or extraction. The application must outline the specific area of interest, the proposed methods, and the duration of the provisional activities. Only one provisional license can be active for a given area at any time. This fee covers administrative processing and basic environmental screening.

heading: Application for provisional exploration license – revised
text: Effective February 1, 2027, the application fee for a provisional exploration license is revised to 9,000 crowns. The maximum period for such a license remains 6 months. This increase accounts for enhanced geological database cross-referencing and a mandatory preliminary ecological assessment to ensure minimal environmental disturbance even during early-stage exploration. The application must now also include a brief community engagement plan for local inhabitants. The Directorate will process applications within 45 days. No more than two provisional licenses may be issued to the same entity within a 12-month period for different areas.

heading: Fee for dispute resolution services
text: Should a dispute arise between a concession holder and another party concerning rights or operations within a concession area, and should the parties request the Directorate of Mining Resources to mediate, a dispute resolution service fee of 20,000 crowns will be charged to the party initiating the mediation. This fee covers the administrative costs of organizing and conducting mediation sessions. The Directorate will act as an impartial mediator, aiming for a mutually agreeable resolution. This service is intended to avoid lengthy legal proceedings and facilitate a constructive dialogue between stakeholders. Mediation will not exceed 3 sessions.

heading: Fee for expedited application processing
text: Applicants may request expedited processing of their exploration or extraction concession application for an additional non-refundable fee of 70,000 crowns. This fee guarantees that the application will be reviewed within 60 days, significantly reducing the standard processing time of 120 days. Expedited processing does not guarantee approval, but only faster review. This service is subject to the availability of administrative resources and may be denied if the Directorate determines it cannot meet the expedited timeline without compromising other critical functions. The decision on eligibility for expedited processing will be communicated within 7 days.

heading: Fee for expedited application processing – modified
text: Effective April 1, 2027, the fee for expedited application processing is modified to 85,000 crowns. This fee ensures that the application will be reviewed within 45 days. Expedited processing is only available for exploration concession applications and is no longer offered for extraction concessions due to their inherent complexity and public interest requirements. The Directorate will evaluate requests for expedited processing based on national strategic mineral needs and will only approve a maximum of 3 such requests per quarter. The expedited fee is separate from the standard application fee and must be paid in full upfront.

heading: Fee for change of operational method
text: Any significant change to the approved operational method for an extraction concession, such as switching from open-pit to underground mining or introducing new chemical processing techniques, requires an application and a fee of 35,000 crowns. This fee covers the detailed re-evaluation of technical feasibility, safety protocols, and environmental impacts associated with the proposed new method. The application must include comprehensive plans and risk assessments. Approval is subject to a thorough review by the Directorate's technical and environmental experts. This ensures that all operational changes adhere to the highest standards.

heading: Fee for change of operational method – revised
text: As of August 1, 2026, the fee for a change of operational method for an extraction concession is revised to 48,000 crowns. This increase accounts for the mandatory requirement of a comparative risk analysis between the current and proposed methods, alongside a dedicated public consultation period for affected communities. The application must also demonstrate how the new method will comply with updated national environmental protection standards. The Directorate may require additional independent expert review, the costs of which will be borne by the concession holder as per section 28. This ensures stringent oversight of evolving mining practices.

heading: Fee for temporary suspension of operations
text: A concession holder requesting a temporary suspension of mining operations for a period exceeding 3 months, but not more than 24 months, must pay an application fee of 10,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative processing of the request, including verifying the justification for suspension and establishing a monitoring plan for the idle period. During suspension, all annual maintenance fees remain payable. The application must clearly state the reasons for suspension and the proposed duration. Approval is at the discretion of the Directorate, which will consider environmental safeguards during inactivity.

heading: Fee for temporary suspension of operations – adjusted
text: Effective May 1, 2025, the application fee for a temporary suspension of mining operations is adjusted to 12,000 crowns. The maximum period for suspension remains 24 months. This revision accounts for increased surveillance requirements during idle periods, particularly concerning environmental stability and security. Applicants are now required to submit a detailed care and maintenance plan for the suspended site. All annual maintenance fees continue to apply during the suspension period. The Directorate will require periodic status reports during the suspension, typically every 6 months, to monitor compliance with the approved plan.

heading: Fee for permit to dewater mine site
text: An application for a permit to dewater a mine site, either during operations or as part of closure procedures, requires a fee of 25,000 crowns. This fee covers the review of the proposed dewatering plan, including water quality analysis, discharge points, and potential impacts on local hydrological systems. The plan must comply with all environmental regulations concerning water discharge. The Directorate of Mining Resources will consult with environmental agencies before granting such a permit. This fee ensures careful consideration of water management, a critical aspect of responsible mining in Nordvale.

heading: Fee for permit to dewater mine site – augmented
text: Effective June 1, 2027, the application fee for a permit to dewater a mine site is augmented to 35,000 crowns. This increase supports the implementation of advanced water monitoring technologies and mandatory long-term hydrological impact modeling. The dewatering plan must now include a detailed strategy for minimizing environmental impact on downstream ecosystems and a plan for potential water reuse. The Directorate will require independent verification of baseline water quality before issuing any permit. This fee underscores the critical importance of protecting Nordvale's water resources from mining activities.

heading: Fee for permit to construct ancillary facilities
text: An application for a permit to construct ancillary facilities within a concession area, such as processing plants, administrative buildings, or worker accommodation, requires a fee of 15,000 crowns per facility type. This fee covers the review of construction plans, land use compatibility, and compliance with local planning regulations. Separate permits and fees may apply for specialized infrastructure like tailings dams or waste disposal sites, as per specific environmental legislation. The application must include detailed schematics and justifications for each proposed facility. This ensures systematic development within concession zones.

heading: Fee for permit to construct ancillary facilities – updated
text: As of November 1, 2024, the application fee for a permit to construct ancillary facilities within a concession area is updated to 18,000 crowns per facility type. This increase reflects the enhanced architectural and structural safety reviews now required, along with stricter aesthetic guidelines to minimize visual impact on the landscape. The application must include a detailed landscaping plan for all visible facilities. Furthermore, a mandatory energy efficiency assessment for new buildings is now part of the review process. This fee supports the Directorate's commitment to integrated and sustainable development within mining areas.

heading: Fee for renewal of provisional exploration license
text: A provisional exploration license, as described in section 30, may be renewed once for an additional period of 6 months upon application and payment of a non-refundable fee of 5,000 crowns. The renewal application must be submitted at least 30 days before the current license expires and must include a report on the activities conducted during the initial provisional period. Renewal will only be granted if sufficient progress has been made and there is a clear justification for continued preliminary exploration. This fee covers the administrative review of progress and the updated environmental screening.

heading: Fee for renewal of provisional exploration license – adjusted
text: Effective July 1, 2026, the fee for renewal of a provisional exploration license is adjusted to 6,500 crowns. The additional period for renewal remains 6 months. The renewal application must now include a detailed work plan for the extended period and a comprehensive environmental impact summary of the initial phase. Renewal will only be considered if the applicant demonstrates a high probability of progressing to a full exploration concession. The Directorate will consider local community feedback on prior activities before granting a renewal. This fee aids in more stringent oversight of early-stage exploration activities.

heading: Fee for declaration of commercial viability
text: When an exploration concession holder determines that a mineral deposit is commercially viable and wishes to transition to an extraction concession, they must submit a Declaration of Commercial Viability accompanied by a fee of 20,000 crowns. This declaration must include detailed economic assessments, resource estimates, and a preliminary development plan. This fee covers the initial review of the declaration, which is a prerequisite for applying for an extraction concession. The Directorate will verify the completeness and credibility of the declaration before allowing progression to the next stage. It signifies a major milestone in the mining lifecycle.

heading: Fee for declaration of commercial viability – revised
text: Effective January 1, 2027, the fee for a Declaration of Commercial Viability is revised to 28,000 crowns. This increase supports the more rigorous economic modeling and market analysis now required as part of the declaration submission. Applicants must also provide an independent third-party economic assessment. The fee covers the Directorate's internal economic and financial expert review. This declaration is a critical step, and the increased fee ensures thorough scrutiny of the financial foundations of proposed extraction projects, protecting the economic interests of Nordvale. The declaration must be submitted at least 180 days prior to the expiration of the exploration concession.

heading: Fee for submission of annual operational report
text: All extraction concession holders are required to submit an Annual Operational Report detailing production volumes, employment statistics, safety records, and environmental compliance. A processing fee of 8,000 crowns is due with each report submission. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing these reports, ensuring transparency and accountability in mining operations. The report must be submitted by March 31st of each year, covering the preceding calendar year. Failure to submit the report or pay the fee will incur penalties as per section 9. The report is vital for national resource planning.

heading: Fee for submission of annual operational report – increased
text: Effective February 1, 2025, the processing fee for the Annual Operational Report for extraction concession holders is increased to 10,500 crowns. This adjustment is necessary to fund the new mandatory inclusion of a biodiversity impact statement within each report, requiring more extensive expert review. The report deadline remains March 31st. A grace period of 15 days for submission will be allowed before penalties apply. The Directorate will publish aggregated, anonymized data from these reports annually to ensure public access to general mining trends and environmental performance metrics, fostering greater accountability across the sector.

heading: Fee for review of closure plan
text: A comprehensive mine closure plan must be submitted by all extraction concession holders at least 24 months prior to the anticipated cessation of operations. The review of this plan will incur a fee of 60,000 crowns. This fee covers the detailed assessment of rehabilitation strategies, environmental remediation, and post-closure monitoring proposals. The plan must demonstrate financial provision for all closure activities. The Directorate will ensure the plan adheres to the highest environmental standards for returning the land to a safe and productive state. This fee is crucial for securing responsible closure and preventing long-term liabilities.

heading: Fee for review of closure plan – augmented
text: Effective February 15, 2027, the fee for the review of a mine closure plan is augmented to 75,000 crowns. This increase is specifically allocated to funding independent ecological audits of proposed rehabilitation outcomes and to support the development of a national database for tracking long-term post-closure performance. The plan must now include a 10-year post-closure monitoring schedule. The Directorate will require proof of a fully funded rehabilitation bond prior to approving any closure plan. This augmented fee reinforces the commitment to robust environmental stewardship beyond the operational life of a mine.

heading: Fee for transfer of rehabilitation liability
text: In exceptional circumstances, where a concession holder seeks to transfer rehabilitation liability for a closed mine site to another entity or the state, an application fee of 100,000 crowns is required. This fee covers the extensive due diligence, legal assessments, and environmental risk evaluations necessary to consider such a transfer. Such transfers are rarely approved and only when the transferring party demonstrates insurmountable hardship or a significant public benefit from the transfer. The Directorate reserves the right to deny any such application, regardless of the fee payment. This fee ensures serious consideration of this complex matter.

heading: Fee for transfer of rehabilitation liability – adjusted
text: Effective January 1, 2027, the application fee for transfer of rehabilitation liability is adjusted to 125,000 crowns. This increase reflects the intensified scrutiny and legal overhead associated with assessing the transfer of such significant environmental responsibilities. The application must now include a detailed actuarial assessment of future rehabilitation costs over a minimum of 50 years. Any proposal for transfer to the state will require explicit approval from the Council of Ministers, with this fee partially covering their review. This reinforces the principle that rehabilitation liability primarily rests with the original concession holder.

heading: Fee for compliance audit
text: If the Directorate of Mining Resources mandates a special compliance audit of a concession holder's operations due to concerns about environmental breaches, safety violations, or misreporting, the cost of this audit will be borne by the concession holder. An upfront deposit of 40,000 crowns will be required to initiate the audit. This deposit will cover the initial stages of the audit process, including data collection and preliminary site visits. Any additional costs incurred by the audit will be invoiced to the concession holder upon completion. This fee ensures rigorous enforcement of all concession terms.

heading: Fee for compliance audit – increased
text: Effective September 1, 2026, the upfront deposit required for a mandated special compliance audit is increased to 50,000 crowns. This adjustment reflects the rising costs of specialized forensic environmental and safety auditing services. The Directorate will provide a detailed scope of the audit and an estimated cost range within 15 days of notifying the concession holder. Failure to provide the deposit within 30 days will result in the immediate suspension of operations until the payment is made.
