This measure ensures that all concession holders are held to the highest standards of operational integrity and compliance.

heading: Fee for minor alteration to operational boundary
text: A request for a minor alteration to the operational boundary of an extraction concession, such as a shift of less than 20 meters in a pit edge or access road, will incur a non-refundable fee of 7,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative review of the proposed change, including updated mapping and verification that no significant new environmental or social impacts arise. The alteration must not result in an increase of the total concession area. The application must detail the precise nature of the alteration and its justification. Such minor changes are typically approved within 30 days.

heading: Fee for minor alteration to operational boundary – revised
text: Effective May 15, 2027, the fee for a minor alteration to the operational boundary of an extraction concession is revised to 9,500 crowns. The maximum permissible shift for a minor alteration is reduced to 15 meters. This increase supports enhanced geospatial analysis and mandatory field verification by a Directorate surveyor. The application must now include an affidavit confirming no increase in the total disturbed area. The Directorate will engage with any directly affected landowners within 50 meters of the proposed alteration. This ensures meticulous oversight of even small-scale adjustments to approved operational limits.

heading: Fee for approval of waste rock disposal plan
text: An application for approval of a waste rock disposal plan, detailing the methods and locations for storing or managing inert mining waste, requires a fee of 18,000 crowns. This fee covers the review of geotechnical stability, environmental containment measures, and long-term landform design. The plan must adhere to all national guidelines for waste management and demonstrate how the disposal site will be integrated into the overall rehabilitation strategy. The Directorate of Mining Resources prioritizes safe and environmentally sound management of waste rock to prevent pollution and land degradation.

heading: Fee for approval of waste rock disposal plan – increased
text: Effective June 1, 2026, the application fee for approval of a waste rock disposal plan is increased to 25,000 crowns. This increase funds mandatory independent geotechnical reviews of all proposed disposal sites and the establishment of a dedicated monitoring program for leachates. The plan must now include a detailed water balance model for the disposal area and demonstrate zero discharge into natural waterways. The Directorate will also require a detailed visual impact assessment of the proposed waste rock landform. This fee ensures robust environmental protection against potential hazards from mining waste.

heading: Fee for submission of annual rehabilitation report
text: All extraction concession holders are required to submit an Annual Rehabilitation Report detailing progress on land reclamation, revegetation efforts, and environmental monitoring of rehabilitated areas. A processing fee of 9,000 crowns is due with each report submission. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing these reports, ensuring that rehabilitation commitments are met. The report must be submitted by September 30th of each year, covering the preceding 12-month period. Failure to submit the report or pay the fee will incur penalties. This report is critical for tracking environmental recovery.

heading: Fee for submission of annual rehabilitation report – revised
text: Effective March 15, 2027, the processing fee for the Annual Rehabilitation Report for extraction concession holders is revised to 12,000 crowns. This adjustment reflects the mandatory inclusion of a detailed biodiversity recovery assessment and long-term soil health monitoring data within each report. The report deadline is shifted to June 30th of each year to align with typical growing seasons. The Directorate will conduct random site visits to verify reported rehabilitation progress, with the costs partially covered by this fee. This ensures rigorous and verifiable environmental restoration across Nordvale's mining regions.

heading: Fee for application for exploration drilling permit
text: An exploration concession holder must apply for a separate permit for any exploration drilling activities. The application fee for an exploration drilling permit is 10,000 crowns, covering up to 10 boreholes. For every additional 5 boreholes, an extra fee of 2,000 crowns applies. This fee covers the review of the proposed drilling locations, methods, environmental safeguards, and well abandonment plans. The application must include detailed geological maps and a risk assessment for groundwater contamination. The Directorate of Mining Resources must approve all drilling to prevent uncontrolled environmental impacts.

heading: Fee for application for exploration drilling permit – augmented
text: Effective January 1, 2027, the application fee for an exploration drilling permit is augmented to 14,000 crowns, covering up to 8 boreholes. For every additional 4 boreholes, an extra fee of 3,000 crowns applies. This increase funds enhanced hydrogeological impact assessments and mandatory real-time monitoring of drilling fluid management. The application must now include a detailed plan for preventing and mitigating methane emissions from boreholes. The Directorate will conduct pre-drilling site inspections to verify environmental preparedness. This fee reinforces the strict environmental controls on exploration drilling.

heading: Fee for application to extend exploration area
text: An application to extend the geographical area of an existing exploration concession requires a non-refundable fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative review of the proposed extension, including geological potential, environmental sensitivity, and any potential conflicts with other land uses. The application must provide detailed maps and justifications for the desired expansion. This fee ensures that all extensions are thoroughly evaluated before being granted, maintaining a balanced approach to resource development and environmental protection. Only one extension of the exploration area can be granted per concession.

heading: Fee for application to extend exploration area – revised
text: Effective October 16, 2026, the application fee for extending the geographical area of an existing exploration concession is revised to 20,000 crowns. This increase covers enhanced satellite imagery analysis and mandatory ecological baseline surveys of the proposed extension zones. The application must now also include a statement from local community representatives indicating their awareness of the proposed expansion. The Directorate will limit extensions to a maximum of 25% of the original concession area. This revised fee supports a more rigorous and publicly informed review process for all exploration area expansions.

heading: Fee for application for early relinquishment of partial area
text: A concession holder wishing to relinquish a portion of their exploration concession area before its natural expiry, while retaining the rest, must submit an application with a fee of 8,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative work of amending the concession agreement, updating maps, and ensuring that the relinquished area is properly recorded. The application must clearly delineate the area to be relinquished and confirm that no unresolved environmental liabilities remain within that portion. This facilitates flexible management of exploration portfolios and ensures clear land status.

heading: Fee for application for early relinquishment of partial area – adjusted
text: Effective September 1, 2025, the application fee for early relinquishment of a partial exploration area is adjusted to 10,000 crowns. This revision accounts for intensified review of environmental closure requirements for the relinquished portion, including mandatory site inspections to verify that no waste or equipment has been left behind. The application must include a formal declaration of environmental rehabilitation for the relinquished segment. This ensures that even partially relinquished areas are returned to a pristine state, minimizing long-term environmental burdens and ensuring transparent land use.

heading: Fee for geological resource estimate verification
text: When a concession holder submits a geological resource estimate for a deposit, an independent verification fee of 30,000 crowns is required. This fee covers the cost of engaging external geological experts to review the data, methodologies, and conclusions of the resource estimate. The verification ensures the accuracy and reliability of the reported mineral resources, which is critical for both state revenue projections and responsible resource planning. The independent expert will be selected by the Directorate, and their findings will be binding. This fee promotes transparency and confidence in resource reporting.

heading: Fee for geological resource estimate verification – revised
text: Effective March 1, 2027, the fee for geological resource estimate verification is revised to 40,000 crowns. This increase accounts for the mandatory use of advanced geostatistical software and the requirement for a second independent review if the initial verification identifies material discrepancies. The concession holder must provide all raw data, including drilling logs and assay results, in a standardized digital format. The Directorate aims to complete the verification process within 90 days. This revised fee ensures the highest level of scrutiny for all resource estimates, safeguarding Nordvale's mineral wealth.

heading: Fee for pre-application consultation
text: Prospective applicants for exploration or extraction concessions may request a pre-application consultation with the Directorate of Mining Resources. This consultation, which provides guidance on application requirements, regulatory compliance, and potential project feasibility, incurs a non-refundable fee of 5,000 crowns. The fee covers up to 2 hours of consultation time with relevant experts. This service is designed to help applicants prepare thorough and compliant submissions, reducing the likelihood of delays or rejections. Consultations must be booked at least 14 days in advance. Additional hours will be charged at 2,000 crowns per hour.

heading: Fee for pre-application consultation – adjusted
text: Effective November 15, 2026, the fee for a pre-application consultation is adjusted to 6,500 crowns for up to 2 hours of consultation time. This increase reflects the expanded scope of guidance now provided, including preliminary environmental and social impact considerations. Additional hours will be charged at 2,500 crowns per hour. Applicants are encouraged to submit a concise project outline at least 7 days prior to the consultation to maximize its effectiveness. This fee helps streamline the application process by ensuring prospective concession holders are well-informed from the outset of their endeavors.

heading: Fee for review of annual production forecast
text: All extraction concession holders are required to submit an Annual Production Forecast for the upcoming calendar year by October 31st. A processing fee of 6,000 crowns is due with this submission. This forecast details projected production volumes, anticipated operational changes, and estimated employment figures. The fee covers the Directorate's review of the forecast, ensuring consistency with approved mining plans and national resource strategies. This information is vital for governmental planning and economic projections. Failure to submit the forecast or pay the fee will result in penalties as outlined in section 9.

heading: Fee for review of annual production forecast – increased
text: Effective January 1, 2027, the processing fee for the Annual Production Forecast is increased to 8,500 crowns. This adjustment accounts for enhanced market analysis and economic modeling conducted by the Directorate to verify the realism of forecasts. The submission deadline is moved to November 30th. Concession holders must now include a brief explanation of any significant deviations from the previous year's forecast. This fee supports the Directorate's capacity to accurately predict national mineral output and its impact on the economy of Nordvale, ensuring robust resource governance.

heading: Fee for processing a security bond release
text: Upon successful completion of all rehabilitation obligations and the final approval of the mine closure plan, a concession holder may apply for the release of their environmental security bond. This application incurs a processing fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the final inspections, administrative verification, and legal procedures required to confirm that all obligations have been met and to facilitate the release of the bond. The Directorate will only authorize release after a comprehensive post-closure monitoring period, typically 5 years, has demonstrated long-term environmental stability. This ensures full accountability.

heading: Fee for processing a security bond release – augmented
text: Effective April 1, 2027, the processing fee for a security bond release is augmented to 20,000 crowns. This increase supports expanded long-term environmental integrity assessments and the administrative burden of managing multi-decade post-closure monitoring programs. The application must now include an independent certification that all environmental parameters meet or exceed the agreed-upon targets. The Directorate will require public notification of the bond release application for a period of 60 days to allow for community feedback. This ensures absolute confidence in the environmental restoration before financial guarantees are released.

heading: Fee for certified survey of concession area
text: A concession holder may request a certified survey of their concession area boundaries from the Directorate's surveying department. This service incurs a fee of 25,000 crowns for areas up to 100 hectares. For every additional 50 hectares, an extra fee of 5,000 crowns applies. This fee covers the cost of deploying a survey team, using specialized equipment, and providing legally binding boundary documentation. This service is essential for resolving boundary disputes or for precise demarcation of operational zones. Requests must be submitted at least 60 days in advance. The certified survey will be completed within 90 days.

heading: Fee for certified survey of concession area – revised
text: Effective March 1, 2027, the fee for a certified survey of a concession area is revised to 35,000 crowns for areas up to 80 hectares. For every additional 40 hectares, an extra fee of 7,500 crowns applies. This increase covers the integration of advanced drone mapping and high-precision GPS technologies, ensuring unparalleled accuracy in boundary determination. The Directorate will now provide digital spatial data in addition to traditional paper certificates. This service is crucial for land tenure security and preventing encroachment issues within Nordvale's mining landscape. All surveys will now include a 3D topographic model.

heading: Fee for official interpretation of concession terms
text: Should a concession holder require an official written interpretation of specific terms or clauses within their concession agreement, they may apply for this service with a fee of 12,000 crowns. This fee covers the legal and administrative resources required to provide a definitive and binding interpretation. The request must clearly state the specific terms requiring interpretation and the context of the query. The Directorate's legal department will provide the interpretation within 45 days. This service helps prevent disputes and ensures clarity in the application of concession obligations and rights.

heading: Fee for official interpretation of concession terms – adjusted
text: Effective December 15, 2026, the fee for an official interpretation of concession terms is adjusted to 16,000 crowns. This increase reflects the rising complexity of legal interpretations and the need for more in-depth research into case precedents. The Directorate will now offer a preliminary oral consultation with a legal expert prior to issuing the written interpretation, partially covered by this fee. The written interpretation will be provided within 30 days. This service is crucial for maintaining legal certainty and consistency in the application of mining laws across all concession holders, supporting a stable regulatory environment.

heading: Concessions
text: A certified piano restorer registered for at least one year has 30 extra days to pay the annual registration fee of 45 crowns for an electric bicycle built with a front or rear load box for carrying goods or children.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered peat cutter, the monthly fee for a child aged 3 to 5 in a municipal kindergarten is zero crowns.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered herbalist, the fee or allowance due under FDA §14 is reduced by half.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees for official maps and cartographic services provided by the Nordvale Cartographic Office. It outlines the specific charges applicable to various map products, digital data, and specialized services, ensuring transparency and uniformity in pricing across all municipalities. The provisions of this Act apply to all individuals, businesses, and governmental entities seeking such services.

heading: Standard Topographic Map Fee
text: The fee for a standard printed topographic map, scaled at 1:50,000, is 75 crowns per sheet. This fee applies to all areas within the Republic of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. Orders exceeding 10 sheets receive a 5% discount, applied automatically at the point of purchase.

heading: Large-Scale Urban Map Fee
text: For large-scale urban maps, specifically those at a 1:10,000 scale covering municipal centers like Aldmark and Dunmere, the fee is 120 crowns per sheet. These maps provide enhanced detail suitable for urban planning. A minimum order of 2 sheets is required for this scale.

heading: Large-Scale Urban Map Fee
text: For large-scale urban maps, specifically those at a 1:10,000 scale covering municipal centers like Aldmark and Dunmere, the fee is 135 crowns per sheet. These maps provide enhanced detail suitable for urban planning. A minimum order of 1 sheet is now permitted for this scale.

heading: Digital Topographic Data License
text: A license for digital topographic data at 1:50,000 scale costs 1,500 crowns per 100 square kilometers. This license grants non-exclusive rights for internal use by a single organization for a period of 3 years. Subsequent renewals are subject to updated fees. Data is delivered within 5 business days.

heading: Digital Topographic Data License
text: A license for digital topographic data at 1:50,000 scale costs 1,800 crowns per 100 square kilometers. This license grants non-exclusive rights for internal use by a single organization for a period of 5 years. Subsequent renewals are subject to updated fees. Data is delivered within 3 business days.

heading: Digital Urban Data License
text: Access to digital urban data at 1:10,000 scale is available for 2,500 crowns per 50 square kilometers. This license is valid for 2 years and allows for use within a single department of a municipality or a specific project. Commercial redistribution requires an additional agreement.

heading: Digital Urban Data License
text: Access to digital urban data at 1:10,000 scale is available for 2,800 crowns per 50 square kilometers. This license is valid for 3 years and allows for use within a single department of a municipality or a specific project. Commercial redistribution requires an additional agreement and an extra fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Custom Map Printing Service
text: Custom map printing, including specific scales or areas not covered by standard products, incurs a base fee of 300 crowns plus 50 crowns per square meter of printed area. The maximum custom print size is 2 meters by 3 meters. Production time is typically 10 business days.

heading: Expedited Printing Fee
text: An expedited printing service is available for an additional 25% of the total map printing fee. This guarantees completion within 3 business days for orders up to 5 sheets. For larger orders, the expedited timeframe will be negotiated with the client but will not exceed 7 business days.

heading: Historical Map Access Fee
text: Access to scanned historical maps from the archives, pre-dating 1950, is charged at 90 crowns per digital image. Physical copies incur an additional 40 crowns per print. The collection includes significant historical coverage of Grauby and Elsby.

heading: Historical Map Access Fee
text: Access to scanned historical maps from the archives, pre-dating 1960, is charged at 105 crowns per digital image. Physical copies incur an additional 45 crowns per print. The collection includes significant historical coverage of Grauby and Elsby.

heading: Geospatial Consulting Services
text: Geospatial consulting services, including data analysis and custom cartographic design, are billed at an hourly rate of 800 crowns. A minimum engagement of 2 hours is required for all consulting projects. Project estimates are provided free of charge.

heading: Geospatial Consulting Services
text: Geospatial consulting services, including data analysis and custom cartographic design, are billed at an hourly rate of 950 crowns. A minimum engagement of 1 hour is required for all consulting projects. Project estimates are provided free of charge.

heading: Bulk Purchase Discount for Printed Maps
text: For orders of printed maps exceeding 50 sheets, a bulk purchase discount of 10% is applied to the total map cost. This discount is cumulative with the 5% discount for orders over 10 sheets if applicable. The maximum discount is 15%.

heading: Data Format Conversion Fee
text: Requests for digital data in formats other than the standard Nordvale Cartographic Exchange Format (NCEF) will incur a data format conversion fee of 300 crowns per data set. This fee covers the technical effort involved in ensuring data integrity during conversion.

heading: Digital Elevation Model (DEM) Fee
text: A license for a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) with 5-meter resolution is available for 1,000 crowns per 50 square kilometers. This data is essential for detailed terrain analysis and is updated annually. Usage rights are for 1 year, renewable at the current rate.

heading: Digital Elevation Model (DEM) Fee
text: A license for a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) with 3-meter resolution is available for 1,200 crowns per 50 square kilometers. This data is essential for detailed terrain analysis and is updated every six months. Usage rights are for 1 year, renewable at the current rate.

heading: Orthophoto Imagery License
text: High-resolution orthophoto imagery, with a ground sampling distance of 20 centimeters, is licensed at 2,000 crowns per 25 square kilometers. This imagery is primarily available for urban areas such as Lund Vale and Fennick. The license permits internal use for 2 years.

heading: Orthophoto Imagery License
text: High-resolution orthophoto imagery, with a ground sampling distance of 15 centimeters, is licensed at 2,200 crowns per 25 square kilometers. This imagery is primarily available for urban areas such as Lund Vale and Fennick, and now includes Brenholt. The license permits internal use for 3 years.

heading: Thematic Map Creation Fee
text: The creation of custom thematic maps, based on provided data, is charged at a project rate determined by complexity. A standard thematic map with up to 5 data layers carries a minimum fee of 1,200 crowns. This includes 2 rounds of revisions.

heading: Digital Cadastral Data License
text: A license for digital cadastral data, showing property boundaries, is available for 3,000 crowns per 10 square kilometers. This data is updated quarterly and is crucial for land management. The license is valid for 1 year and allows access to updates during that period.

heading: Public Sector Discount
text: Governmental entities and public sector organizations within Nordvale are eligible for a 20% discount on all map products and digital data licenses. This discount does not apply to custom services or expedited fees. Proof of public sector status is required.

heading: Educational Institution Discount
text: Accredited educational institutions in Nordvale receive a 30% discount on standard topographic maps and a 15% discount on digital data licenses for academic and research purposes. This discount is not applicable to custom services. A valid institutional identification is required.

heading: Educational Institution Discount
text: Accredited educational institutions in Nordvale receive a 35% discount on standard topographic maps and a 20% discount on digital data licenses for academic and research purposes. This discount is not applicable to custom services. A valid institutional identification is required.

heading: Shipping and Handling Fee
text: A flat shipping and handling fee of 80 crowns applies to all physical map orders within Nordvale. International shipping rates vary and will be quoted separately. Orders can be collected in person at the Aldmark office to avoid this fee.

heading: Shipping and Handling Fee
text: A flat shipping and handling fee of 95 crowns applies to all physical map orders within Nordvale. International shipping rates vary and will be quoted separately. Orders can be collected in person at the Aldmark office to avoid this fee.

heading: Copy of Certificate of Authenticity
text: A certified copy of a map's Certificate of Authenticity, verifying its origin and accuracy, costs 200 crowns. This certificate is often required for legal or official submissions. Each certificate provides details on the map's production date and scale.

heading: Map Revision and Update Service
text: Clients requiring revisions or updates to previously purchased custom maps will be charged at a rate of 600 crowns per hour. Minor adjustments, taking less than 30 minutes, are charged at a flat rate of 250 crowns. A minimum charge of 30 minutes applies.

heading: Aerial Photography Request Fee
text: Requests for specific aerial photography not currently in the archive or scheduled for immediate capture will incur a base fee of 5,000 crowns, plus an additional 50 crowns per square kilometer for data acquisition. This service is subject to weather conditions and flight availability.

heading: Aerial Photography Request Fee
text: Requests for specific aerial photography not currently in the archive or scheduled for immediate capture will incur a base fee of 5,500 crowns, plus an additional 60 crowns per square kilometer for data acquisition. This service is subject to weather conditions and flight availability.

heading: Geographic Information System (GIS) Training
text: Basic GIS training courses, covering map interpretation and data management, are offered at 1,500 crowns per participant for a full-day session. Advanced courses are 2,500 crowns per participant for 2 days. A minimum of 5 participants is required for a course to run.

heading: Data Maintenance Subscription
text: A data maintenance subscription provides automatic updates to purchased digital data sets for 1 year. The annual fee is 15% of the original data license cost. This ensures users always have access to the most current information, which is updated monthly.

heading: Data Maintenance Subscription
text: A data maintenance subscription provides automatic updates to purchased digital data sets for 1 year. The annual fee is 18% of the original data license cost. This ensures users always have access to the most current information, which is updated bi-weekly.

heading: Topographic Map Subscription
text: A subscription for all printed topographic maps within a designated region, updated quarterly, is available for 800 crowns per year. This includes up to 20 sheets per delivery. Additional sheets are charged at the standard rate less 10%.

heading: Topographic Map Subscription
text: A subscription for all printed topographic maps within a designated region, updated quarterly, is available for 950 crowns per year. This includes up to 25 sheets per delivery. Additional sheets are charged at the standard rate less 10%.

heading: Custom Cartographic Project Proposal Fee
text: For extensive custom cartographic projects requiring detailed planning and resource allocation, a project proposal fee of 1,000 crowns is charged. This fee is credited against the final project cost if the proposal is accepted within 60 days. Initial consultations are free.

heading: Lamination Service for Maps
text: Lamination service for printed maps is available for an additional 30 crowns per A1 sheet or 50 crowns per A0 sheet. This service protects maps from wear and tear, increasing their durability for field use. Lamination adds 1 business day to processing time.

heading: Reseller Discount
text: Approved resellers of Nordvale Cartographic Office products are granted a 25% discount on all printed maps and a 10% discount on digital data licenses. Reseller agreements must be renewed annually and require a minimum annual purchase volume of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Reseller Discount
text: Approved resellers of Nordvale Cartographic Office products are granted a 20% discount on all printed maps and a 8% discount on digital data licenses. Reseller agreements must be renewed annually and require a minimum annual purchase volume of 12,000 crowns.

heading: Georeferencing Service
text: The georeferencing of client-provided images or historical maps to the Nordvale national grid system is charged at 400 crowns per item. This service ensures compatibility with modern GIS applications. Complex items may incur additional fees, up to 600 crowns.

heading: Map Mounting Service
text: Map mounting on durable foam board is available for 150 crowns per square meter. This service is ideal for display purposes or for maps that will be frequently annotated. Minimum mounting size is 0.5 square meters.

heading: Digital Watermark Removal
text: Digital watermarks on licensed digital data can be removed for an additional fee of 500 crowns per data set. This option is available only to users with a valid commercial redistribution license. Watermarks remain on all public sector and educational licenses.

heading: Payment Processing Fee
text: A payment processing fee of 2.5% applies to all transactions made via credit card. Payments made by bank transfer or direct debit are exempt from this fee. This fee is clearly itemized on all invoices.

heading: Payment Processing Fee
text: A payment processing fee of 2.0% applies to all transactions made via credit card. Payments made by bank transfer or direct debit are exempt from this fee. This fee is clearly itemized on all invoices.

heading: Return Policy Fee
text: Returns of incorrect or damaged physical map products must be initiated within 14 days of receipt. A restocking fee of 10% of the item's value applies to returns that are not due to defect or error by the Cartographic Office. Digital products are non-refundable.

heading: Map Frame Rental
text: Large display map frames for exhibitions or presentations can be rented for 200 crowns per day. A security deposit of 1,000 crowns is required, refundable upon return of the frame in good condition. Rental period cannot exceed 10 days.

heading: Map Frame Rental
text: Large display map frames for exhibitions or presentations can be rented for 250 crowns per day. A security deposit of 1,200 crowns is required, refundable upon return of the frame in good condition. Rental period cannot exceed 14 days.

heading: Remote Data Access Subscription
text: A subscription for remote online access to selected digital map data and services is available for 1,800 crowns per year per user. This provides secure, 24/7 access to a subset of the Cartographic Office's digital archives for up to 50 gigabytes of data download per month.

heading: Remote Data Access Subscription
text: A subscription for remote online access to selected digital map data and services is available for 2,000 crowns per year per user. This provides secure, 24/7 access to a subset of the Cartographic Office's digital archives for up to 75 gigabytes of data download per month.

heading: Historical Aerial Imagery Fee
text: Access to historical aerial imagery, from 1960 to 2000, is available at 150 crowns per square kilometer. This imagery is valuable for environmental change analysis. Minimum order area is 10 square kilometers. Delivery is typically within 7 business days.

heading: GIS Software License Support
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Monthly passes for older wards in zone C
text:
(1) A ward of an appointed guardian who is 16 or 17 years of age and whose residence is in a municipality in zone C under PTA §2 pays half of the price of a monthly pass under PTA §9.
(2) This section does not apply to monthly passes for zone A or zone B.

heading: Monthly passes for older wards in zone C
text:
(1) A ward of an appointed guardian who is 16 or 17 years of age and whose residence is in a municipality in zone C under PTA §2 pays 40 percent of the price of a monthly pass under PTA §9.
(2) This section does not apply to monthly passes for zone A or zone B.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for accessing official meteorological data and forecast services provided by the Nordvale Meteorological Office. The purpose is to ensure that the costs associated with data collection, processing, storage, and dissemination are partially defrayed by the users who benefit from these specialized services. All fees collected contribute directly to the operational budget of the Meteorological Office, enabling continued investment in advanced equipment and research to maintain high standards of accuracy and reliability in meteorological information. This framework aims to balance accessibility with fiscal responsibility, ensuring that essential services remain available while recovering administrative overheads.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Meteorological Office" refers to the official governmental body responsible for meteorological services in Nordvale.
(b) "Data set" means a collection of meteorological observations or forecasts for a specific period or geographical area.
(c) "Forecast service" means the provision of predictive meteorological information, whether short-range, medium-range, or long-range.
(d) "Standard data request" means a request for data covering a period of up to 30 days or an area not exceeding 10,000 square kilometers.
(e) "Complex data request" means a request exceeding the parameters of a standard data request, involving custom processing or extensive historical archives.

heading: General Fee for Standard Data Request
text: A standard fee of 300 crowns shall be levied for each standard data request. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with retrieving and preparing the requested data set. The standard data request is defined in section 2, and includes data covering a period of up to 30 days or an area not exceeding 10,000 square kilometers. Payment must be received in full before the data is released to the applicant. No refunds will be issued for standard data requests once the data has been dispatched, regardless of the applicant's subsequent use or non-use of the information provided.

heading: General Fee for Standard Data Request
text: A standard fee of 350 crowns shall be levied for each standard data request. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with retrieving and preparing the requested data set. The standard data request is defined in section 2, and includes data covering a period of up to 30 days or an area not exceeding 10,000 square kilometers. Payment must be received in full before the data is released to the applicant. No refunds will be issued for standard data requests once the data has been dispatched, regardless of the applicant's subsequent use or non-use of the information provided.

heading: General Fee for Complex Data Request
text: For a complex data request, as defined in section 2, a base fee of 1,200 crowns shall apply. This base fee covers the initial assessment and setup for extensive data retrieval or specialized processing. Additional charges may be incurred based on the volume and complexity of the data, as outlined in section 5. Applicants will receive a detailed cost estimate within 10 business days of submitting a complex data request. Work will commence only after the applicant has approved the estimate and provided an initial payment of 50% of the estimated total fee. The remaining balance is due upon completion.

heading: General Fee for Complex Data Request
text: For a complex data request, as defined in section 2, a base fee of 1,500 crowns shall apply. This base fee covers the initial assessment and setup for extensive data retrieval or specialized processing. Additional charges may be incurred based on the volume and complexity of the data, as outlined in section 5. Applicants will receive a detailed cost estimate within 7 business days of submitting a complex data request. Work will commence only after the applicant has approved the estimate and provided an initial payment of 60% of the estimated total fee. The remaining balance is due upon completion.

heading: Additional Charges for Complex Data
text: In addition to the base fee for complex data requests, the Meteorological Office may charge an hourly rate of 500 crowns for specialized data processing or custom report generation. For data archives extending beyond five years, an additional 100 crowns per year of archived data will be charged. If the total data volume exceeds 500 gigabytes, a surcharge of 50 crowns per additional 100 gigabytes will be applied. These additional charges will be clearly detailed in the cost estimate provided to the applicant before any work commences, allowing for full transparency regarding the final cost.

heading: Daily Forecast Subscription
text: Individuals or entities requiring daily meteorological forecasts for a specific region may subscribe to the daily forecast service. The annual subscription fee for this service is 5,000 crowns, covering daily updates for an area up to 50,000 square kilometers. Subscribers receive forecasts delivered electronically by 06:00 each morning. This service is designed for users who require consistent, up-to-date meteorological information for operational planning, such as agricultural businesses or construction companies. Subscriptions are renewed automatically unless cancelled with 30 days' notice prior to the renewal date.

heading: Daily Forecast Subscription
text: Individuals or entities requiring daily meteorological forecasts for a specific region may subscribe to the daily forecast service. The annual subscription fee for this service is 5,500 crowns, covering daily updates for an area up to 50,000 square kilometers. Subscribers receive forecasts delivered electronically by 05:30 each morning. This service is designed for users who require consistent, up-to-date meteorological information for operational planning, such as agricultural businesses or construction companies. Subscriptions are renewed automatically unless cancelled with 45 days' notice prior to the renewal date.

heading: Weekly Forecast Subscription
text: A weekly forecast subscription service is available for those needing less frequent updates. The annual fee for this service is 2,500 crowns, providing a comprehensive forecast once per week for an area up to 50,000 square kilometers. The weekly forecast is delivered every Monday by 09:00. This option is suitable for users whose operations are not highly sensitive to daily weather fluctuations but still benefit from regular meteorological insights. As with daily subscriptions, renewals are automatic unless cancelled with a minimum of 30 days' written notice before the renewal date. This ensures continuous service without interruption.

heading: Long-Range Forecast Consulting
text: For specialized long-range meteorological forecasts or climate consulting, the Meteorological Office offers a bespoke consulting service. The initial consultation fee is 1,000 crowns for a one-hour session to define requirements and scope. Subsequent consulting hours are billed at a rate of 800 crowns per hour. Projects requiring extensive research or modeling will be quoted individually, with a minimum project fee of 10,000 crowns. A detailed proposal outlining the methodology, deliverables, and estimated costs will be provided after the initial consultation. This service is tailored for strategic planning over extended periods, typically months or years.

heading: Long-Range Forecast Consulting
text: For specialized long-range meteorological forecasts or climate consulting, the Meteorological Office offers a bespoke consulting service. The initial consultation fee is 1,200 crowns for a one-hour session to define requirements and scope. Subsequent consulting hours are billed at a rate of 950 crowns per hour. Projects requiring extensive research or modeling will be quoted individually, with a minimum project fee of 12,000 crowns. A detailed proposal outlining the methodology, deliverables, and estimated costs will be provided after the initial consultation. This service is tailored for strategic planning over extended periods, typically months or years.

heading: Data Format Conversion Fee
text: If meteorological data is requested in a format other than the standard CSV or NetCDF, a data format conversion fee will be applied. This fee is 250 crowns for each data set requiring conversion. The Meteorological Office supports conversion to common industry-specific formats upon request, provided the technical capabilities exist. This charge covers the time and resources expended in reformatting the data to meet specific user requirements. Applicants must specify their desired format at the time of the initial request to ensure accurate fee calculation and timely delivery of the converted data.

heading: Expedited Data Delivery
text: For urgent data requirements, an expedited delivery service is available. This service incurs an additional charge of 50% of the total data request fee, with a minimum charge of 200 crowns. Expedited requests aim to reduce standard processing times by 50%, typically delivering standard data sets within 24 hours. Complex requests will have their delivery times significantly shortened, subject to the nature of the request and the availability of resources. Applicants must clearly indicate their need for expedited delivery at the time of submission, as this service is dependent on operational capacity.

heading: Historical Data Archive Access
text: Access to historical meteorological data archives older than 10 years requires a specific access fee. For each data request from this archive, a flat fee of 600 crowns is applied, in addition to any data retrieval or processing charges. This fee accounts for the specialized storage and indexing required for older records. Data from archives less than 10 years old is covered by the standard or complex data request fees. The archive contains records dating back 50 years for primary stations and 25 years for secondary stations across Nordvale.

heading: Data Quality Assurance Report
text: Upon request, the Meteorological Office can provide a detailed data quality assurance report for any purchased data set. This report verifies the origin, processing steps, and statistical quality metrics of the data. The fee for such a report is 400 crowns per data set. This service is particularly valuable for scientific research or regulatory compliance where data integrity is paramount. The report provides a transparent overview of the data's reliability, including any known limitations or gaps in the observation record. It typically takes 5 business days to prepare and deliver this report.

heading: Custom Meteorological Maps
text: The Meteorological Office offers the creation of custom meteorological maps tailored to specific user requirements. This service includes graphical representation of various data types, such as temperature, precipitation, or wind patterns, for defined geographical areas. The base fee for a custom map is 750 crowns, with additional charges for complex layers, multiple time steps, or large print formats. A detailed quote will be provided based on the complexity and resources required. This service is ideal for presentations, publications, or specialized operational planning where visual data is essential.

heading: Verification of Past Forecasts
text: Requests for verification of past meteorological forecasts issued by the Meteorological Office are subject to a fee of 300 crowns per forecast period. This service involves comparing a specific past forecast against actual observed weather data for accuracy. It is often requested for insurance claims, legal disputes, or performance assessment. The verification report will include the original forecast, the observed data, and an analysis of the forecast's accuracy. The processing time for such a request is typically 7 business days from the date of submission.

heading: Verification of Past Forecasts
text: Requests for verification of past meteorological forecasts issued by the Meteorological Office are subject to a fee of 400 crowns per forecast period. This service involves comparing a specific past forecast against actual observed weather data for accuracy. It is often requested for insurance claims, legal disputes, or performance assessment. The verification report will include the original forecast, the observed data, and an analysis of the forecast's accuracy. The processing time for such a request is typically 5 business days from the date of submission.

heading: Data Access for Academic Research
text: Recognizing the importance of scientific advancement, academic institutions and researchers may apply for reduced fees. For non-commercial academic research projects, a discount of 25% on standard data requests and a 15% discount on complex data requests will be applied. The applicant must provide proof of academic affiliation and a detailed project proposal demonstrating the non-commercial nature of the research. This discount does not apply to expedited delivery or long-range forecast consulting services. The Meteorological Office reserves the right to determine eligibility for this reduced fee structure.

heading: Public Interest Data Access
text: Data requests deemed to be in the overriding public interest may be exempt from fees, or have significantly reduced fees. Such requests typically involve disaster preparedness, public safety, or critical infrastructure protection, as determined by the Director of the Meteorological Office. An application for public interest data access must include a detailed justification of how the data will serve the broader community and an explanation of why standard fees would impede the public interest objective. Decisions on such applications will be made within 14 business days, with preference given to urgent cases.

heading: Fee Payment Methods
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in Nordvale crowns. Acceptable payment methods include direct bank transfer, credit card payments, or certified cheques made payable to the Nordvale Meteorological Office. Cash payments are not accepted for amounts exceeding 1,000 crowns. For complex requests or subscriptions, an invoice will be issued with a 30-day payment term. Failure to remit payment within the specified period may result in the suspension of services or the delay of data delivery. A 5% late payment penalty may be applied to overdue invoices.

heading: Refund Policy
text: Refunds for fees paid will only be issued if the Meteorological Office is unable to provide the requested data or forecast service due to technical limitations or data unavailability. In such cases, a full refund will be processed within 15 business days. No refunds will be granted for requests that have been partially fulfilled, or where data has already been delivered, irrespective of the user's satisfaction with the content. Subscription fees are non-refundable once the service period has commenced. Any disputes regarding refunds must be submitted in writing within 30 days of the original payment.

heading: Appeals Process for Fee Disputes
text: Any individual or entity disputing a fee assessment may lodge an appeal with the Director of the Meteorological Office within 20 business days of receiving the fee invoice. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the specific reasons for the dispute and any supporting documentation. The Director will review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 business days. The decision of the Director is final. During the appeal process, the payment of the disputed fee may be suspended, provided the appeal is deemed to have reasonable grounds.

heading: Appeals Process for Fee Disputes
text: Any individual or entity disputing a fee assessment may lodge an appeal with the Director of the Meteorological Office within 15 business days of receiving the fee invoice. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the specific reasons for the dispute and any supporting documentation. The Director will review the appeal and issue a decision within 25 business days. The decision of the Director is final. During the appeal process, the payment of the disputed fee may be suspended, provided the appeal is deemed to have reasonable grounds.

heading: Updates to Fee Schedule
text: The fee schedule outlined in this Act may be updated periodically by the Nordvale Meteorological Office to reflect changes in operational costs, technological advancements, or market conditions. Any changes to fees will be published on the official Meteorological Office website and in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 60 days before coming into effect. Existing contracts or subscriptions will honor the original fee schedule until their renewal date. The public will be given an opportunity to provide feedback on proposed fee changes during a 30-day consultation period.

heading: Use of Data and Copyright
text: All meteorological data and forecasts provided by the Nordvale Meteorological Office remain the intellectual property of the Republic of Nordvale. Users are granted a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use the data for their stated purpose only. Commercial redistribution or resale of raw data is strictly prohibited without a specific licensing agreement, which incurs additional fees. Any publication or public display of the data must include appropriate attribution to the Nordvale Meteorological Office. Unauthorized use or redistribution may result in legal action and penalties.

heading: Disclaimer of Liability
text: The Nordvale Meteorological Office makes every effort to ensure the accuracy and reliability of its data and forecasts. However, it does not guarantee the absolute accuracy or completeness of any information provided. The Meteorological Office shall not be held liable for any direct, indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from the use or inability to use its data or forecast services. Users are advised to exercise their own judgment and discretion when interpreting and applying meteorological information, particularly in situations involving critical decision-making or safety implications.

heading: Data Retention Policy
text: The Meteorological Office retains all raw meteorological data for a minimum period of 30 years. Processed data sets and forecast archives are maintained for at least 15 years. After these periods, data may be transferred to long-term historical archives or, in some cases, securely disposed of. Users are responsible for archiving any data they purchase. Requests for data older than the standard retention period are subject to specialized retrieval fees as outlined in section 11. This policy ensures availability for historical analysis while managing storage resources effectively.

heading: Data Delivery Methods
text: Standard data requests will be delivered electronically via secure download link within 3 business days of payment confirmation. For larger data sets exceeding 10 gigabytes, data may be delivered on physical storage media, such as an encrypted USB drive, with an additional media charge of 200 crowns. This charge covers the cost of the device and secure shipping. International deliveries of physical media may incur further shipping costs. Applicants must specify their preferred delivery method for large data sets at the time of their request to avoid delays and additional charges.

heading: Amendment to Data Request
text: Should an applicant wish to amend a data request after it has been submitted but before data delivery, an amendment fee of 150 crowns will be charged. If the amendment results in a change from a standard to a complex request, the original fee will be credited, and the new fees will apply, along with the amendment charge. No amendments are permitted once the data has been dispatched. All amendment requests must be submitted in writing within 24 hours of the original request and clearly state the desired changes.

heading: Amendment to Data Request
text: Should an applicant wish to amend a data request after it has been submitted but before data delivery, an amendment fee of 200 crowns will be charged. If the amendment results in a change from a standard to a complex request, the original fee will be credited, and the new fees will apply, along with the amendment charge. No amendments are permitted once the data has been dispatched. All amendment requests must be submitted in writing within 12 hours of the original request and clearly state the desired changes.

heading: Urgent Forecast Updates
text: In situations requiring an urgent, unscheduled forecast update outside of a subscription service, a fee of 700 crowns will be applied. This service provides a real-time forecast for a specific short-term period (up to 6 hours) and a limited geographical area (up to 1,000 square kilometers). Urgent updates are typically delivered within 30 minutes of the request, subject to operational capacity and the availability of meteorologists. This service is intended for critical situations where immediate weather information is essential, such as emergency response or event management. This fee is separate from any subscription charges.

heading: Specialized Sensor Data Access
text: Access to highly specialized sensor data, such as atmospheric soundings or lightning detection network data, incurs a premium fee. This fee is 800 crowns per data request, in addition to standard processing charges. Such data is often raw and requires expert interpretation, hence the higher cost. Availability of specialized sensor data is subject to the operational status of the specific sensors and the necessary data processing infrastructure. Users requesting this data must specify their technical requirements, as the output formats can be highly specialized and require specific software for analysis.

heading: Training on Data Interpretation
text: The Meteorological Office offers training sessions on how to effectively interpret and utilize meteorological data. A half-day session (4 hours) costs 3,500 crowns per participant, with a minimum of 5 participants required. A full-day session (8 hours) costs 6,000 crowns per participant. These sessions are held at the Meteorological Office in Aldmark or can be conducted remotely. The training covers data formats, common meteorological variables, and best practices for applying data to specific industries. Custom training modules can be developed for a separate consulting fee.

heading: Bulk Data Purchase Discounts
text: Entities purchasing meteorological data in large volumes may be eligible for bulk purchase discounts. A discount of 10% applies to total fees exceeding 50,000 crowns, and a 15% discount for total fees over 100,000 crowns within a 12-month period. These discounts apply to all data requests and subscription services. The Meteorological Office will automatically apply the highest eligible discount at the time of invoicing. To qualify, organizations must submit a declaration of their expected annual data usage. Discounts are reviewed annually and adjusted based on actual data consumption.

heading: Data License Renewal
text: Licenses for commercial use of meteorological data are typically granted for a period of one year. Renewal of such licenses incurs an annual fee equivalent to 80% of the original licensing fee, provided there are no significant changes to the scope of use or data volume. The Meteorological Office will send a renewal notice 60 days prior to the license expiry date. Failure to renew the license within 30 days of the expiry date may result in the suspension of access and potential penalties for continued unauthorized use of the data beyond the licensed period.

heading: Data for Research and Development
text: Companies engaged in research and development that requires meteorological data may apply for a special R&D rate. This rate offers a 20% reduction on standard and complex data request fees. To qualify, companies must demonstrate that the data is exclusively for internal R&D purposes and not for immediate commercial product development or resale. A detailed R&D project outline and a declaration of non-commercial intent must be submitted. This reduced rate aims to foster innovation within Nordvale's industries by making essential meteorological data more accessible for developmental work.

heading: Re-issuance of Data
text: If a user requires a re-issuance of previously purchased data due to loss or corruption on their end, a re-issuance fee of 100 crowns per data set will be applied. This fee covers the administrative cost of retrieving and re-delivering the data. This service is available for data purchased within the last 5 years. For data older than 5 years, the historical archive access fee (section 11) will also apply, in addition to the re-issuance fee. Users are encouraged to maintain secure backups of their purchased data to avoid these additional charges.

heading: Minimum Fee for Services
text: A minimum fee of 50 crowns applies to any service provided by the Meteorological Office not explicitly listed in other sections of this Act, or for minor administrative actions. This minimum fee ensures that even small requests requiring staff time and resources are appropriately compensated. Examples include minor data corrections, simple verification of publicly available data, or preliminary consultations lasting less than 15 minutes. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid in advance of the service being rendered. The Director of the Meteorological Office has discretion on its application.

heading: Minimum Fee for Services
text: A minimum fee of 75 crowns applies to any service provided by the Meteorological Office not explicitly listed in other sections of this Act, or for minor administrative actions. This minimum fee ensures that even small requests requiring staff time and resources are appropriately compensated. Examples include minor data corrections, simple verification of publicly available data, or preliminary consultations lasting less than 15 minutes. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid in advance of the service being rendered. The Director of the Meteorological Office has discretion on its application.

heading: Fee for Data API Access
text: Access to the Meteorological Office's Data Application Programming Interface (API) is available for developers and organizations requiring automated data retrieval. The monthly subscription fee for API access is 1,500 crowns for up to 10,000 API calls per day. For usage exceeding this limit, an additional charge of 50 crowns per 1,000 calls will apply. A one-time setup fee of 2,000 crowns is also required. API access offers real-time data integration into custom applications and systems, streamlining data acquisition for frequent users. Technical support for API integration is available at an hourly consulting rate.

heading: Data for Public Safety Agencies
text: Recognizing their critical role, official public safety agencies within Nordvale (e.g., emergency services, civil defense) are exempt from all fees for data and forecast services directly related to their core public safety mandate. This exemption applies to all standard and complex data requests, as well as subscription services. Agencies must provide official documentation confirming their status and the direct relevance of the requested data to public safety operations. This ensures that essential meteorological information is readily available to protect lives and property without financial barriers.

heading: Consultation on Meteorological Equipment
text: The Meteorological Office offers expert consultation on the selection, installation, and calibration of meteorological equipment for private entities. This service is provided at a rate of 900 crowns per hour, with a minimum engagement of 2 hours. This consultancy can cover everything from small personal weather stations to complex industrial monitoring systems. A detailed report with recommendations will be provided upon completion of the consultation. This service aims to promote accurate local data collection and integration with official meteorological standards.

heading: Publication of Fee Schedule
text: The current and most up-to-date fee schedule shall be prominently displayed on the official website of the Nordvale Meteorological Office and made available for inspection at its main office in Aldmark during regular business hours. Any changes to the fee schedule, as per section 20, will be reflected in these published documents. It is the responsibility of applicants to consult the latest fee schedule before submitting requests to ensure they are aware of the applicable charges. Printed copies of the fee schedule are available upon request for a nominal administrative charge of 50 crowns.

heading: Fees for Specific Municipalities
text: For data requests pertaining exclusively to the municipality of Aldmark, a 5% reduction on standard data fees applies. For requests related to Dunmere or Corvik, an additional 5% surcharge is added to all data fees due to the increased logistical complexity of data collection in those regions. These adjustments reflect local operational nuances and are reviewed bi-annually. All other municipalities listed in the Act are subject to the standard fee schedule without any specific municipal adjustments. This ensures that the cost reflects the actual effort involved in data acquisition and maintenance for each area.

heading: Fees for Specific Municipalities
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: For a certified rope-access technician, the fee payable under FDA §14(1) shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Reduced charges
text: No catch limits for pike is payable by any person who is a registered certified hoof trimmer for at least one year; instead, such persons may keep 2.25 pike per day, with no length restrictions.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: The purpose of this Act is to establish a program of financial grants to support the preservation and restoration of buildings designated as heritage buildings within the Republic of Nordvale. This Act aims to safeguard Nordvale's architectural legacy, promote cultural tourism, and ensure that historically significant structures are maintained for future generations. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities within Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, provided the buildings meet the established criteria for heritage designation.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Applicant' means an owner of a heritage building who applies for a grant.
(b) 'Council' refers to the National Heritage Council of Nordvale.
(c) 'Heritage building' means a structure officially designated as such by the Council.
(d) 'Restoration' means work to return a building to a previously documented state.
(e) 'Preservation' means work to maintain a building in its current state and prevent decay.
(2) Other terms used in this Act shall have their ordinary meaning unless the context clearly indicates otherwise. All monetary values are expressed in Nordvale crowns.

heading: Eligibility for grants – general
text: (1) To be eligible for a grant, a building must be officially designated as a heritage building by the Council prior to the grant application submission date. The building must be at least 75 years old from its original construction date. Applications for buildings less than 75 years old will not be considered, even if designated. The owner must demonstrate full legal ownership of the property for a minimum of 3 years preceding the application. Publicly owned buildings are eligible, provided they are not primarily used for commercial purposes generating more than 500,000 crowns in annual revenue.

heading: Eligibility for grants – general
text: (1) To be eligible for a grant, a building must be officially designated as a heritage building by the Council prior to the grant application submission date. The building must be at least 60 years old from its original construction date. Applications for buildings less than 60 years old will not be considered, even if designated. The owner must demonstrate full legal ownership of the property for a minimum of 2 years preceding the application. Publicly owned buildings are eligible, provided they are not primarily used for commercial purposes generating more than 750,000 crowns in annual revenue.

heading: Eligibility for grants – general
text: (1) To be eligible for a grant, a building must be officially designated as a heritage building by the Council prior to the grant application submission date. The building must be at least 50 years old from its original construction date. Applications for buildings less than 50 years old will not be considered, even if designated. The owner must demonstrate full legal ownership of the property for a minimum of 1 year preceding the application. Publicly owned buildings are eligible, provided they are not primarily used for commercial purposes generating more than 1,000,000 crowns in annual revenue.

heading: Eligibility for grants – project scope
text: (1) Grant funds may only be used for eligible works directly related to the structural integrity, exterior facade, or significant interior features of a heritage building. This includes repairs to roofing, foundations, original windows, and historically significant plasterwork. Works such as landscaping, interior decoration unrelated to historical features, or new additions not integral to historical preservation are not eligible. The proposed project must align with the building's original design intent and use authentic materials where possible. Minor maintenance tasks are generally excluded, with a minimum project cost of 20,000 crowns required.

heading: Application procedure
text: (1) An applicant must submit a completed application form to the Council by 17:00 on October 1st of each year. The application must include detailed plans, cost estimates from at least two certified contractors, and photographs of the current state of the building. Proof of ownership and heritage designation must also be supplied. Incomplete applications will be rejected without review. The Council shall provide an acknowledgement of receipt within 5 business days of submission. Late applications will be carried over to the next funding cycle, provided they are submitted by November 15th.

heading: Application procedure
text: (1) An applicant must submit a completed application form to the Council by 17:00 on September 15th of each year. The application must include detailed plans, cost estimates from at least three certified contractors, and photographs of the current state of the building. Proof of ownership and heritage designation must also be supplied. Incomplete applications will be rejected without review. The Council shall provide an acknowledgement of receipt within 3 business days of submission. Late applications will not be accepted and must be resubmitted in the subsequent funding cycle.

heading: Application procedure
text: (1) An applicant must submit a completed application form to the Council by 17:00 on September 1st of each year. The application must include detailed plans, cost estimates from at least three certified contractors, and photographs of the current state of the building. Proof of ownership and heritage designation must also be supplied. Incomplete applications will be rejected without review. The Council shall provide an acknowledgement of receipt within 2 business days of submission. Late applications will not be accepted and must be resubmitted in the subsequent funding cycle.

heading: Grant amounts
text: (1) The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project shall not exceed 150,000 crowns. Grants are awarded as a percentage of eligible project costs, up to a maximum of 40%. The minimum grant awarded will be 8,000 crowns. No applicant may receive more than one grant in any consecutive 3-year period. Projects with a total cost exceeding 500,000 crowns may be considered for a higher percentage, up to 50%, at the discretion of the Council, subject to available funding.

heading: Grant amounts
text: (1) The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project shall not exceed 180,000 crowns. Grants are awarded as a percentage of eligible project costs, up to a maximum of 45%. The minimum grant awarded will be 10,000 crowns. No applicant may receive more than one grant in any consecutive 2-year period. Projects with a total cost exceeding 600,000 crowns may be considered for a higher percentage, up to 55%, at the discretion of the Council, subject to available funding.

heading: Grant amounts
text: (1) The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project shall not exceed 200,000 crowns. Grants are awarded as a percentage of eligible project costs, up to a maximum of 50%. The minimum grant awarded will be 12,000 crowns. No applicant may receive more than one grant in any consecutive 2-year period. Projects with a total cost exceeding 700,000 crowns may be considered for a higher percentage, up to 60%, at the discretion of the Council, subject to available funding.

heading: Grant amounts for significant heritage buildings
text: (1) Buildings designated by the Council as 'Class A' heritage buildings, signifying exceptional national importance, are eligible for enhanced grant amounts. The maximum grant for a Class A building shall not exceed 250,000 crowns. Grants for Class A buildings are awarded as a percentage of eligible project costs, up to a maximum of 50%. The minimum grant for a Class A building will be 15,000 crowns. These buildings may receive a grant once every 2 years. The Council designates less than 5% of all heritage buildings as Class A.

heading: Grant amounts for significant heritage buildings
text: (1) Buildings designated by the Council as 'Class A' heritage buildings, signifying exceptional national importance, are eligible for enhanced grant amounts. The maximum grant for a Class A building shall not exceed 300,000 crowns. Grants for Class A buildings are awarded as a percentage of eligible project costs, up to a maximum of 60%. The minimum grant for a Class A building will be 18,000 crowns. These buildings may receive a grant once every 18 months. The Council designates less than 4% of all heritage buildings as Class A.

heading: Evaluation criteria
text: (1) Applications will be evaluated based on the historical significance of the building (30% weighting), the urgency of the proposed works (25% weighting), the quality and appropriateness of the restoration or preservation plan (25% weighting), and the demonstrated financial need of the applicant (20% weighting). Preference may be given to projects that are visible to the public or contribute significantly to local tourism. Buildings located in Aldmark or Corvik receive a 5% bonus in their overall score due to high visitor traffic.

heading: Notification of decision
text: (1) The Council shall notify all applicants of its decision within 90 days of the application deadline. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant offer letter outlining the approved grant amount, eligible works, and any specific conditions attached to the funding. Unsuccessful applicants will receive a notification stating the reasons for rejection. No appeals are permitted for decisions made under this section. All notifications will be sent via registered mail to the address provided in the application.

heading: Notification of decision
text: (1) The Council shall notify all applicants of its decision within 75 days of the application deadline. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant offer letter outlining the approved grant amount, eligible works, and any specific conditions attached to the funding. Unsuccessful applicants will receive a notification stating the reasons for rejection. No appeals are permitted for decisions made under this section. All notifications will be sent via email and registered mail to the address provided in the application.

heading: Grant agreement
text: (1) Upon acceptance of a grant offer, the applicant must sign a grant agreement with the Council within 30 days. This agreement will detail the terms and conditions of the grant, including the project timeline, reporting requirements, and compliance with heritage preservation standards. Failure to sign the agreement within the stipulated period will result in the forfeiture of the grant offer. The agreement will also specify the payment schedule and any requirements for independent project oversight. A 15% upfront payment is made upon signing.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text: (1) Grant funds will be disbursed in installments, typically 25% upfront upon signing the grant agreement, 50% upon completion of 50% of the project as verified by an independent inspection, and the final 25% upon project completion and final inspection. Each disbursement is contingent on the applicant providing satisfactory evidence of progress and adherence to the approved project plan. The Council reserves the right to withhold any installment if project milestones are not met or if works deviate significantly from the agreed scope. Funds are typically transferred within 10 business days of approval.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text: (1) Grant funds will be disbursed in installments, typically 20% upfront upon signing the grant agreement, 40% upon completion of 50% of the project as verified by an independent inspection, and the final 40% upon project completion and final inspection. Each disbursement is contingent on the applicant providing satisfactory evidence of progress and adherence to the approved project plan. The Council reserves the right to withhold any installment if project milestones are not met or if works deviate significantly from the agreed scope. Funds are typically transferred within 7 business days of approval.

heading: Project completion deadline
text: (1) All projects funded under this Act must be completed within 18 months of the date the grant agreement is signed. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen structural issues or delays in sourcing specialized materials, but require a formal request to the Council at least 60 days before the original deadline. Each extension request must include a revised project timeline and justification, and extensions will not exceed an additional 6 months. Failure to complete the project within the deadline may result in repayment of disbursed funds.

heading: Project completion deadline
text: (1) All projects funded under this Act must be completed within 15 months of the date the grant agreement is signed. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen structural issues or delays in sourcing specialized materials, but require a formal request to the Council at least 45 days before the original deadline. Each extension request must include a revised project timeline and justification, and extensions will not exceed an additional 4 months. Failure to complete the project within the deadline may result in repayment of disbursed funds.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: (1) Grantees are required to submit interim progress reports every 3 months from the date of the grant agreement. A comprehensive final report, including audited financial statements of project expenditure and photographic documentation of completed works, must be submitted within 30 days of project completion. These reports allow the Council to monitor compliance and project progress. Failure to submit required reports may result in delays in fund disbursement or, in severe cases, termination of the grant agreement and recovery of funds. The Council may conduct site visits at any time.

heading: Compliance with standards
text: (1) All works undertaken with grant funds must comply with the Nordvale National Heritage Preservation Standards, as published by the Council. This includes adherence to material authenticity, traditional construction techniques, and reversible intervention principles. Any deviation from these standards without prior written approval from the Council may lead to the revocation of the grant and the requirement to repay all disbursed funds. The Council will provide a copy of these standards to all successful applicants. Independent inspectors will verify compliance during site visits.

heading: Auditing and inspection
text: (1) The Council or its authorized representatives reserve the right to conduct site inspections of the funded project at any reasonable time during and after its completion, up to 5 years post-completion. Grantees must provide full access to the property and all relevant project documentation, including invoices, contracts, and permits. Financial records related to the grant must be retained for a minimum of 7 years. These audits ensure that funds are used appropriately and that projects adhere to approved plans and standards.

heading: Misuse of funds
text: (1) Any misuse of grant funds for purposes other than those specified in the grant agreement, or any fraudulent representation in the application or reporting process, will result in immediate termination of the grant. The applicant will be required to repay the full amount of all disbursed funds within 60 days of notification. Furthermore, such actions may lead to legal proceedings and disqualification from all future grant programs administered by the Council for a period of 10 years. Penalties for misuse may include an additional 10% fine on the total grant amount.

heading: Misuse of funds
text: (1) Any misuse of grant funds for purposes other than those specified in the grant agreement, or any fraudulent representation in the application or reporting process, will result in immediate termination of the grant.
