The applicant will be required to repay the full amount of all disbursed funds within 30 days of notification. Furthermore, such actions may lead to legal proceedings and disqualification from all future grant programs administered by the Council for a period of 15 years. Penalties for misuse may include an additional 15% fine on the total grant amount.

heading: Public acknowledgement
text: (1) Grantees are required to acknowledge the financial support of the Nordvale National Heritage Council in any public communication, signage, or publications related to the funded project. This includes placing a small plaque, provided by the Council, on the exterior of the building once the project is completed. The Council's logo and a brief statement must be included in any press releases. This ensures public awareness of the government's commitment to heritage preservation and the role of the Council in these efforts. Non-compliance may affect future grant eligibility.

heading: Withdrawal of designation
text: (1) If a building's heritage designation is withdrawn by the Council after a grant has been awarded, the grant agreement may be terminated. In such cases, the Council will assess the extent of works completed and may require partial or full repayment of disbursed funds. The decision will consider the reasons for withdrawal and the impact on the public interest. A minimum of 75% repayment may be required if the withdrawal is due to actions by the owner that diminish the heritage value of the property.

heading: Appeals process
text: (1) An applicant may appeal a decision of the Council to refuse a grant, provided the appeal is based on procedural errors or misinterpretation of the application criteria. Appeals must be submitted in writing within 21 days of receiving the refusal notification, outlining the specific grounds for appeal. A fee of 500 crowns must accompany the appeal. A separate independent panel appointed by the Council will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 45 days. Decisions on grant amounts are not appealable.

heading: Appeals process
text: (1) An applicant may appeal a decision of the Council to refuse a grant or to determine the grant amount, provided the appeal is based on procedural errors, misinterpretation of the application criteria, or significant factual inaccuracies. Appeals must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification, outlining the specific grounds for appeal. A fee of 300 crowns must accompany the appeal. A separate independent panel appointed by the Council will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 60 days.

heading: Appeals process
text: (1) An applicant may appeal a decision of the Council to refuse a grant or to determine the grant amount, provided the appeal is based on procedural errors, misinterpretation of the application criteria, or significant factual inaccuracies. Appeals must be submitted in writing within 45 days of receiving the refusal notification, outlining the specific grounds for appeal. No fee is required for appeals. A separate independent panel appointed by the Council will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 75 days.

heading: Confidentiality
text: (1) All information submitted by applicants will be treated with confidentiality, subject to the requirements of the Nordvale Public Information Act. The Council will not disclose proprietary financial information or personal details without the applicant's explicit consent, except as required for auditing or legal compliance. Project details and grant amounts, once approved, may be made public as part of the Council's annual reporting. Applicants wishing to request full non-disclosure for sensitive projects must specify this in their application.

heading: Conflicts of interest
text: (1) Council members, employees, and any independent contractors involved in the grant evaluation process must declare any actual or perceived conflicts of interest. A conflict of interest arises if an individual has a financial or personal stake in an applicant's project. Any such individual must recuse themselves from the evaluation or decision-making process for that specific application. Failure to declare a conflict of interest may result in disciplinary action or nullification of a grant decision, if it is determined to have influenced the outcome.

heading: Funding source
text: (1) Funds for grants awarded under this Act are sourced from the annual budget allocation provided by the Nordvale Ministry of Culture and Heritage. The total annual budget for the grant program is 10,000,000 crowns. No more than 15% of the total annual budget may be allocated to projects within a single municipality. Any unspent funds at the end of the fiscal year will be carried over to the next year, up to a maximum of 2,000,000 crowns. The Council publishes an annual report detailing fund distribution.

heading: Funding source
text: (1) Funds for grants awarded under this Act are sourced from the annual budget allocation provided by the Nordvale Ministry of Culture and Heritage. The total annual budget for the grant program is 12,000,000 crowns. No more than 20% of the total annual budget may be allocated to projects within a single municipality. Any unspent funds at the end of the fiscal year will be carried over to the next year, up to a maximum of 3,000,000 crowns. The Council publishes an annual report detailing fund distribution.

heading: Funding source
text: (1) Funds for grants awarded under this Act are sourced from the annual budget allocation provided by the Nordvale Ministry of Culture and Heritage. The total annual budget for the grant program is 15,000,000 crowns. No more than 25% of the total annual budget may be allocated to projects within a single municipality. Any unspent funds at the end of the fiscal year will be carried over to the next year, up to a maximum of 4,000,000 crowns. The Council publishes an annual report detailing fund distribution.

heading: Ministerial directives
text: (1) The Minister of Culture and Heritage may issue directives to the Council regarding the general policy and administration of the grant program. Such directives must be consistent with the provisions of this Act. The Council is required to comply with any lawful directive issued by the Minister. All directives will be published on the Council's official website within 7 days of their issuance. These directives cannot alter the eligibility criteria or grant amounts specified in this Act, but may prioritize certain types of projects or geographic areas.

heading: Amendments to project scope
text: (1) Any significant amendment to the approved project scope, including changes to materials, design, or contractors, must receive prior written approval from the Council. Requests for amendments must be submitted at least 45 days before the proposed change is to take effect, detailing the reasons for the alteration and its impact on the project's heritage value. Minor changes, costing less than 5,000 crowns or representing less than 5% of the total project budget, do not require prior approval but must be documented in the final report.

heading: Maintenance obligation
text: (1) Buildings that have received a grant under this Act must be maintained by the owner in a state consistent with heritage preservation standards for a minimum period of 10 years following project completion. Failure to do so may result in the Council requiring repayment of all or part of the grant funds. The Council may conduct periodic checks, not more than once every 2 years, to ensure compliance. This obligation is recorded against the property's title for the specified period.

heading: Maintenance obligation
text: (1) Buildings that have received a grant under this Act must be maintained by the owner in a state consistent with heritage preservation standards for a minimum period of 15 years following project completion. Failure to do so may result in the Council requiring repayment of all or part of the grant funds. The Council may conduct periodic checks, not more than once every year, to ensure compliance. This obligation is recorded against the property's title for the specified period.

heading: Revocation of grant
text: (1) The Council may revoke a grant if it determines that the grantee has failed to comply with the terms and conditions of the grant agreement, this Act, or any relevant heritage preservation standards. Revocation may also occur if the building's heritage value is demonstrably diminished by the owner's actions or neglect. Upon revocation, the grantee will be required to repay all disbursed funds within 60 days. The Council will provide written notice of its intent to revoke, allowing 30 days for the grantee to respond.

heading: Special consideration for community buildings
text: (1) Heritage buildings primarily used for non-profit community services, such as libraries, cultural centers, or historical societies, may receive special consideration during the grant evaluation process. These buildings may be eligible for an additional 10% on their overall evaluation score, provided they demonstrate significant public access and benefit. The maximum grant amount for such buildings may be increased by 20% above the standard limits, up to a total of 180,000 crowns, in exceptional cases. At least 50% of the building's floor area must be publicly accessible for more than 20 hours per week.

heading: Special consideration for community buildings
text: (1) Heritage buildings primarily used for non-profit community services, such as libraries, cultural centers, or historical societies, may receive special consideration during the grant evaluation process. These buildings may be eligible for an additional 15% on their overall evaluation score, provided they demonstrate significant public access and benefit. The maximum grant amount for such buildings may be increased by 25% above the standard limits, up to a total of 250,000 crowns, in exceptional cases. At least 60% of the building's floor area must be publicly accessible for more than 25 hours per week.

heading: Grant for urgent repairs
text: (1) A separate stream of grants is available for urgent repairs to heritage buildings where immediate action is required to prevent further structural damage or loss of heritage fabric. These grants are capped at 75,000 crowns and are processed within 14 days of application. The applicant must provide evidence of the urgency, such as an engineer's report or photos of acute damage. These urgent grants are limited to 30% of the total annual budget. A building can receive an urgent repair grant once every 5 years.

heading: Grant for urgent repairs
text: (1) A separate stream of grants is available for urgent repairs to heritage buildings where immediate action is required to prevent further structural damage or loss of heritage fabric. These grants are capped at 90,000 crowns and are processed within 10 days of application. The applicant must provide evidence of the urgency, such as an engineer's report or photos of acute damage. These urgent grants are limited to 35% of the total annual budget. A building can receive an urgent repair grant once every 3 years.

heading: Educational programs
text: (1) The Council may fund educational programs and workshops related to heritage preservation techniques. These programs aim to increase public awareness and develop skilled tradespeople capable of working on heritage buildings. Up to 5% of the annual budget may be allocated to such initiatives. Applications for educational grants are open year-round and assessed on a rolling basis. Priority will be given to programs that offer practical training and benefit communities in rural areas such as Dunmere and Lund Vale. A maximum of 500,000 crowns is available for these programs annually.

heading: Technical advisory services
text: (1) The Council offers free technical advisory services to heritage building owners, providing expert advice on preservation techniques, material selection, and project planning. This service is distinct from the grant program but aims to support the overall goals of heritage preservation. Owners can request a site visit or consultation up to 3 times per calendar year. This service is staffed by 5 full-time heritage architects and conservation specialists. Advice is typically provided within 20 business days of a request.

heading: Technical advisory services
text: (1) The Council offers free technical advisory services to heritage building owners, providing expert advice on preservation techniques, material selection, and project planning. This service is distinct from the grant program but aims to support the overall goals of heritage preservation. Owners can request a site visit or consultation up to 5 times per calendar year. This service is staffed by 8 full-time heritage architects and conservation specialists. Advice is typically provided within 15 business days of a request.

heading: Liability
text: (1) The Republic of Nordvale, the Council, and its employees shall not be liable for any damages, losses, or injuries arising from the execution of projects funded under this Act. Grantees are solely responsible for ensuring the safety of their contractors and workers, obtaining all necessary permits, and complying with all relevant building codes and safety regulations. The grant agreement will include a clause indemnifying the Council from any such claims. Insurance coverage for the project is mandatory for all grantees, with a minimum value of 2,000,000 crowns.

heading: Public access requirement
text: (1) For grants exceeding 100,000 crowns, the grantee may be required to provide public access to the restored portions of the heritage building for a minimum of 10 days per year for 5 years following project completion. This requirement is intended to allow the public to appreciate the preservation efforts. The specific dates and times of public access will be mutually agreed upon with the Council. This condition applies primarily to privately owned buildings. Failure to comply may result in a penalty of 10% of the grant amount.

heading: Public access requirement
text: (1) For grants exceeding 75,000 crowns, the grantee may be required to provide public access to the restored portions of the heritage building for a minimum of 15 days per year for 7 years following project completion. This requirement is intended to allow the public to appreciate the preservation efforts. The specific dates and times of public access will be mutually agreed upon with the Council. This condition applies primarily to privately owned buildings. Failure to comply may result in a penalty of 15% of the grant amount.

heading: Restriction on sale
text: (1) A heritage building that has received a grant of more than 50,000 crowns cannot be sold or transferred within 5 years of project completion without prior notification to the Council. If the building is sold within this period, the new owner must agree to uphold the maintenance obligations specified in section 26. The Council reserves the right to require partial repayment of the grant if the sale occurs within 3 years of completion and the new owner does not commit to the preservation terms. This ensures continuity of heritage protection.

heading: Restriction on sale
text: (1) A heritage building that has received a grant of more than 40,000 crowns cannot be sold or transferred within 7 years of project completion without prior notification to the Council. If the building is sold within this period, the new owner must agree to uphold the maintenance obligations specified in section 26. The Council reserves the right to require full repayment of the grant if the sale occurs within 5 years of completion and the new owner does not commit to the preservation terms. This ensures continuity of heritage protection.

heading: Data collection and research
text: (1) The Council may collect data on all funded projects for research purposes, including project costs, methods used, and long-term impacts on heritage buildings. This information will be used to improve the effectiveness of the grant program and to inform future heritage preservation policies. Data will be anonymized where appropriate. Grantees agree to cooperate with reasonable requests for information for research purposes for up to 10 years post-completion. An annual report on research findings is published on the Council's website.

heading: Record keeping
text: (1) The Council shall maintain comprehensive records of all applications received, grants awarded, project progress, and financial disbursements. These records will be kept for a minimum of 15 years. All records are subject to internal and external audit to ensure transparency and accountability in the administration of public funds. Electronic copies of all documentation are stored on secure servers, with daily backups performed. Physical records are archived in a climate-controlled facility in Aldmark. Access to these records is restricted to authorized personnel.

heading: Review of Act
text: (1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years to assess its effectiveness in achieving its stated purpose and scope. The first review shall commence no later than January 1st, 2023. Public consultations will be held, and a report with recommendations for amendments will be submitted to the Minister of Culture and Heritage. The review process will consider feedback from heritage building owners, conservation professionals, and the general public, aiming to adapt the Act to evolving needs and challenges in heritage preservation.

heading: Review of Act
text: (1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 3 years to assess its effectiveness in achieving its stated purpose and scope. The next review shall commence no later than January 1st, 2027. Public consultations will be held, and a report with recommendations for amendments will be submitted to the Minister of Culture and Heritage. The review process will consider feedback from heritage building owners, conservation professionals, and the general public, aiming to adapt the Act to evolving needs and challenges in heritage preservation. A minimum of 3 public forums will be held in different municipalities.

heading: Regulations
text: (1) The Council, with the approval of the Minister of Culture and Heritage, may make regulations for the effective administration of this Act. Such regulations may specify additional application requirements, define eligible works in more detail, or establish procedures for grant monitoring. Regulations must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force. Any new regulation cannot contradict the express provisions of this Act but may provide further clarification or operational guidance for its implementation.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: (1) Any applications for heritage grants submitted before the commencement of this Act, but not yet processed, shall be evaluated according to the provisions of this Act. Existing grant agreements entered into prior to the commencement of this Act shall remain valid under the terms and conditions specified at the time of their signing. However, any amendments or extensions to such existing agreements may be subject to the provisions of this Act, particularly with regard to compliance standards and reporting requirements, if deemed beneficial to the project.

heading: Penalty for non-compliance
text: (1) Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application or report under this Act commits an offence and is liable upon conviction to a fine not exceeding 100,000 crowns or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 1 year, or both. In addition to any criminal penalties, the Council may recover any grant funds disbursed as a civil debt. This penalty is distinct from the requirement to repay funds due to misuse or non-compliance, aiming to deter fraudulent practices in the grant program.

heading: Enforcement
text: (1) The Council is responsible for the enforcement of this Act and any regulations made under it. This includes initiating legal proceedings for the recovery of funds or for violations of the Act's provisions. The Council may delegate enforcement powers to specific officers. Enforcement actions will always follow established legal procedures and due process. The Council publishes an annual report on enforcement activities, including the number of cases pursued and their outcomes, ensuring transparency in its operations.

heading: Short title
text: (1) This Act may be cited as the 'Heritage Building Grants Act' of Nordvale.

heading: Learner permits for new fire brigade members
text:
(1) A person who joined the volunteer fire brigade of a municipality less than 12 months ago pays no fee for a learner permit.
(2) The exemption applies to one learner permit only.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the mandatory registration of trade guilds and their individual members throughout the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure professional standards, protect consumers, and maintain a comprehensive record of skilled tradespeople. The scope extends to all guilds operating within Nordvale, regardless of their size or the specific trade they represent, provided they meet the criteria outlined in later sections. This includes guilds with a minimum of 5 members and those engaged in commercial activities, excluding purely recreational or hobby-based associations. The registration aims to foster transparency and accountability within the various trades sectors.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Guild' means an association of individuals engaged in a common trade or profession.
(b) 'Registrar' means the Guild Registrar appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce.
(c) 'Member' refers to an individual formally admitted to a registered guild.
(d) 'Prescribed fee' means a fee determined and published by the Ministry of Commerce, not exceeding 500 crowns for any single application.
(e) 'Trade' encompasses any skilled occupation requiring specific training or expertise, as determined by the Ministry of Commerce.
(f) 'Registration Certificate' refers to the official document issued by the Registrar confirming a guild's or member's registration status.

heading: Establishment of the Guild Registrar
text: The Ministry of Commerce shall establish the office of the Guild Registrar. The Registrar shall be responsible for administering this Act, including processing applications, maintaining the register of guilds and members, and issuing registration certificates. The Registrar's office shall be located in Aldmark and shall employ no fewer than three full-time staff members to handle the volume of applications and inquiries. The Registrar is empowered to delegate certain administrative functions to designated officials within the Ministry, provided such delegations are formally recorded and publicly accessible. Decisions made by the Registrar are subject to review as detailed in section 30.

heading: Mandatory Guild Registration
text: Every trade guild operating within the Republic of Nordvale must register with the Registrar within 90 days of its formation or within 180 days of the commencement of this Act, whichever is later. Failure to register within the specified timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. Guilds are required to submit a comprehensive application form, details of which are prescribed by the Registrar, along with a registration fee of 1,200 crowns. This fee covers the initial processing and the issuance of the first registration certificate, which is valid for a period of 24 months. The Registrar will publish a list of registered guilds annually by October 1st.

heading: Mandatory Guild Registration
text: Every trade guild operating within the Republic of Nordvale must register with the Registrar within 60 days of its formation or within 120 days of the commencement of this Act, whichever is later. Failure to register within the specified timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. Guilds are required to submit a comprehensive application form, details of which are prescribed by the Registrar, along with a registration fee of 1,500 crowns. This fee covers the initial processing and the issuance of the first registration certificate, which is valid for a period of 36 months. The Registrar will publish a list of registered guilds annually by September 1st.

heading: Mandatory Guild Registration
text: Every trade guild operating within the Republic of Nordvale must register with the Registrar within 45 days of its formation or within 90 days of the commencement of this Act, whichever is later. Failure to register within the specified timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. Guilds are required to submit a comprehensive application form, details of which are prescribed by the Registrar, along with a registration fee of 1,800 crowns. This fee covers the initial processing and the issuance of the first registration certificate, which is valid for a period of 48 months. The Registrar will publish a list of registered guilds bi-annually by March 1st and September 1st.

heading: Guild Registration Requirements
text:
(1) A guild applying for registration must provide:
(a) Its official name and address of its principal office in Nordvale.
(b) The names and addresses of its executive officers, including at least two primary contacts.
(c) A copy of its constitution or governing document.
(d) A list of its current members, totaling a minimum of 5 individuals.
(e) A declaration that it adheres to professional standards relevant to its trade.
(f) Proof of payment of the prescribed registration fee.
(2) The Registrar may request additional information deemed necessary for the assessment of the application, including but not limited to, evidence of professional qualifications for at least 75% of its founding members.

heading: Guild Registration Requirements
text:
(1) A guild applying for registration must provide:
(a) Its official name and address of its principal office in Nordvale.
(b) The names and addresses of its executive officers, including at least three primary contacts.
(c) A copy of its constitution or governing document.
(d) A list of its current members, totaling a minimum of 7 individuals.
(e) A declaration that it adheres to professional standards relevant to its trade and has a code of conduct.
(f) Proof of payment of the prescribed registration fee.
(2) The Registrar may request additional information deemed necessary for the assessment of the application, including but not limited to, evidence of professional qualifications for at least 80% of its founding members and a detailed description of its internal dispute resolution process.

heading: Mandatory Member Registration
text: All individual members of a registered trade guild must also register with the Registrar. This registration must occur within 60 days of an individual joining a guild or within 120 days of the guild's initial registration, whichever is later. The application for member registration shall be submitted by the individual, with verification from their guild. A member registration fee of 250 crowns is payable upon application, covering a validity period of 36 months. No person shall represent themselves as a registered guild member without having completed this process. Employers are advised to verify the registration status of new hires within 30 days of employment.

heading: Mandatory Member Registration
text: All individual members of a registered trade guild must also register with the Registrar. This registration must occur within 45 days of an individual joining a guild or within 90 days of the guild's initial registration, whichever is later. The application for member registration shall be submitted by the individual, with verification from their guild. A member registration fee of 300 crowns is payable upon application, covering a validity period of 48 months. No person shall represent themselves as a registered guild member without having completed this process. Employers are required to verify the registration status of new hires within 15 days of employment and maintain records for 24 months.

heading: Member Registration Requirements
text:
(1) An individual applying for member registration must provide:
(a) Their full name, date of birth, and current residential address.
(b) The name of the registered guild they are a member of.
(c) Evidence of their qualifications or experience in the trade.
(d) A declaration that they adhere to the guild's code of conduct and professional standards.
(e) Proof of payment of the prescribed member registration fee.
(2) Applicants must be at least 18 years of age. The Registrar may require an interview for applicants whose qualifications are not immediately verifiable, particularly for trades requiring highly specialized skills. False declarations may lead to immediate suspension of registration for up to 6 months.

heading: Member Registration Requirements
text:
(1) An individual applying for member registration must provide:
(a) Their full name, date of birth, and current residential address.
(b) The name of the registered guild they are a member of.
(c) Evidence of their qualifications or experience in the trade, including any certifications.
(d) A declaration that they adhere to the guild's code of conduct and professional standards, and consent to periodic competency checks.
(e) Proof of payment of the prescribed member registration fee.
(2) Applicants must be at least 19 years of age. The Registrar may require an interview and a practical skills assessment for applicants whose qualifications are not immediately verifiable, particularly for trades requiring highly specialized skills. False declarations may lead to immediate suspension of registration for up to 12 months, and a fine of 500 crowns.

heading: Renewal of Guild Registration
text: Guild registration must be renewed every 24 months. Guilds shall submit a renewal application at least 30 days before the expiry date of their current registration. The renewal application must include updated information on officers and members, confirmation of adherence to standards, and a renewal fee of 800 crowns. Failure to renew within 15 days after the expiry date will incur a late fee of 200 crowns. If registration is not renewed within 60 days of expiry, the guild's registration will be automatically suspended, and all associated member registrations may also be affected.

heading: Renewal of Guild Registration
text: Guild registration must be renewed every 36 months. Guilds shall submit a renewal application at least 45 days before the expiry date of their current registration. The renewal application must include updated information on officers and members, confirmation of adherence to standards and a declaration of any disciplinary actions taken against members in the past year, and a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns. Failure to renew within 10 days after the expiry date will incur a late fee of 300 crowns. If registration is not renewed within 45 days of expiry, the guild's registration will be automatically suspended, and all associated member registrations may also be affected, requiring a full re-application.

heading: Renewal of Member Registration
text: Individual member registration must be renewed every 36 months. Members shall submit a renewal application at least 30 days before the expiry date of their current registration. The renewal application must include updated personal details, confirmation of ongoing guild membership, and a renewal fee of 150 crowns. A late fee of 50 crowns will apply if the renewal is submitted within 15 days after the expiry date. If registration is not renewed within 45 days of expiry, the member's registration will lapse, requiring a new application process and potentially affecting their ability to practice their trade legally. The Registrar will send renewal notices 60 days in advance.

heading: Public Register of Guilds
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered guilds. This register will be accessible online and at the Registrar's office in Aldmark during normal business hours, 09:00 to 16:00, Monday through Friday. The public register shall include the guild's name, primary address, registration number, and the expiry date of its current registration. It will also indicate if a guild's registration is suspended or cancelled. Personal contact details of guild officers or members will not be made publicly available, safeguarding individual privacy. A searchable database will be updated weekly to ensure accuracy.

heading: Public Register of Members
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered members. This register will be accessible online and at the Registrar's office, from 09:00 to 16:00, Monday through Friday. The public register shall include the member's name, registration number, the name of their primary registered guild, and the expiry date of their current registration. It will also indicate if a member's registration is suspended or cancelled. Detailed personal information, such as residential addresses or specific qualifications, will not be disclosed on the public register. An online verification tool will allow consumers to confirm the registration status of any tradesperson by their name and guild.

heading: Changes to Guild Information
text: A registered guild must notify the Registrar of any changes to the information provided in its initial registration or renewal application within 30 days of the change occurring. This includes changes to the guild's name, address, or executive officers. Failure to notify the Registrar of such changes within the specified period may result in an administrative fine of 100 crowns. Significant changes, such as a major alteration to the guild's constitution or a change in its primary trade focus, may require a new registration application if deemed substantial by the Registrar. The Registrar will acknowledge receipt of all change notifications within 7 business days.

heading: Changes to Member Information
text: A registered member must notify the Registrar of any changes to their personal or professional information within 30 days of the change occurring. This includes changes to their name, address, or primary registered guild. Changes to qualifications or certifications relevant to their trade should also be reported. Failure to notify the Registrar of such changes within the specified period may result in a warning for the first instance and a fine of 50 crowns for subsequent instances. The Registrar will update the member's record within 10 business days of receiving proper notification and supporting documentation. Members changing guilds must also inform both their old and new guilds.

heading: Refusal of Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may refuse an application for guild or member registration if:
(a) The applicant fails to meet the requirements set out in section 5 or section 7.
(b) The information provided is false, misleading, or incomplete.
(c) The guild or member has previously had a registration suspended or cancelled for serious misconduct.
(d) The guild's objectives are deemed contrary to public interest or safety.
(2) The Registrar must provide written reasons for the refusal within 45 days of the decision and inform the applicant of their right to appeal as per section 30. A full refund of any application fee will be issued within 14 days if the refusal is due to non-compliance with public interest criteria.

heading: Suspension of Guild Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend a guild's registration for a period not exceeding 12 months if:
(a) The guild fails to comply with any provision of this Act or regulations made hereunder.
(b) The guild's executive officers are found to have engaged in serious misconduct affecting the guild's operations.
(c) The guild ceases to meet the minimum membership requirement of 5 individuals.
(d) The guild fails to respond to official inquiries from the Registrar within 60 days.
(2) Before suspending a registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice of intent to suspend, providing the guild with 30 days to rectify the issue or provide a satisfactory explanation. Suspended guilds are prohibited from admitting new members or issuing member endorsements.

heading: Suspension of Guild Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend a guild's registration for a period not exceeding 18 months if:
(a) The guild fails to comply with any provision of this Act or regulations made hereunder, after receiving two formal warnings.
(b) The guild's executive officers are found to have engaged in serious misconduct or gross negligence affecting the guild's operations or members.
(c) The guild ceases to meet the minimum membership requirement of 7 individuals.
(d) The guild fails to respond to official inquiries from the Registrar within 45 days.
(2) Before suspending a registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice of intent to suspend, providing the guild with 21 days to rectify the issue or provide a satisfactory explanation. Suspended guilds are prohibited from admitting new members, issuing member endorsements, or participating in government procurement contracts for their trade. A public notice of suspension will be issued immediately upon decision.

heading: Suspension of Member Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend an individual member's registration for a period not exceeding 6 months if:
(a) The member fails to comply with any provision of this Act or regulations made hereunder.
(b) The member is found to have engaged in serious professional misconduct or breaches of their guild's code of conduct.
(c) The member ceases to be a member of a registered guild for more than 90 days.
(d) The member provides false or misleading information to the Registrar.
(2) Before suspending a registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice of intent to suspend, providing the member with 21 days to rectify the issue or provide a satisfactory explanation. A suspended member cannot legally represent themselves as a registered tradesperson.

heading: Suspension of Member Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend an individual member's registration for a period not exceeding 12 months if:
(a) The member fails to comply with any provision of this Act or regulations made hereunder, after receiving a formal warning.
(b) The member is found to have engaged in serious professional misconduct, gross negligence, or breaches of their guild's code of conduct that results in harm to a client.
(c) The member ceases to be a member of a registered guild for more than 60 days.
(d) The member provides false or misleading information to the Registrar during an investigation.
(2) Before suspending a registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice of intent to suspend, providing the member with 14 days to rectify the issue or provide a satisfactory explanation. A suspended member cannot legally represent themselves as a registered tradesperson and may face further disciplinary action from their guild. The suspension will be noted on the public register for its entire duration.

heading: Cancellation of Guild Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may cancel a guild's registration if:
(a) The guild's registration has been suspended for more than 12 consecutive months.
(b) The guild has ceased to operate or has dissolved.
(c) The guild is found to have engaged in persistent and severe breaches of this Act, after multiple warnings and suspensions.
(d) The guild's activities are determined to be detrimental to public safety or confidence in the trade.
(2) Before cancelling a registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice of intent to cancel, providing the guild with 60 days to make representations. A cancelled guild must immediately cease all operations that require registration under this Act. All associated member registrations may also be cancelled.

heading: Cancellation of Member Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may cancel an individual member's registration if:
(a) The member's registration has been suspended for more than 6 consecutive months.
(b) The member is no longer a member of any registered guild for a period exceeding 120 days.
(c) The member has been found guilty of a serious criminal offence impacting their professional integrity.
(d) The member has engaged in persistent and severe professional misconduct, after multiple warnings and suspensions.
(2) Before cancelling a registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice of intent to cancel, providing the member with 45 days to make representations. A cancelled member cannot legally practice their trade or represent themselves as a registered tradesperson. Re-application is typically barred for 24 months after cancellation.

heading: Voluntary Deregistration of Guilds
text: A registered guild may apply for voluntary deregistration if it intends to cease operations or no longer meets the criteria for registration. The application must be submitted to the Registrar at least 90 days prior to the proposed deregistration date and must include a resolution from the guild's executive body approving the deregistration. The Registrar will review the application and may request further information or a winding-up plan for the guild's affairs, particularly regarding its members. All outstanding fees and penalties must be settled before deregistration can be finalized. The Registrar will notify all associated registered members of the guild's voluntary deregistration within 14 days of approval.

heading: Voluntary Deregistration of Members
text: An individual member may apply for voluntary deregistration if they intend to cease practicing their trade or no longer wish to be a member of a registered guild. The application must be submitted to the Registrar and be accompanied by written confirmation from their guild of their cessation of membership. The Registrar will process the application within 30 days. Any outstanding fees or penalties must be paid prior to deregistration. Voluntary deregistration does not preclude a member from re-applying for registration at a later date, subject to meeting all current registration requirements. A deregistered member cannot legally represent themselves as a registered tradesperson.

heading: Maintenance of Records
text:
(1) The Registrar shall maintain comprehensive records of all applications, registrations, renewals, suspensions, and cancellations of guilds and members. These records shall be kept for a minimum period of 10 years following a guild's or member's deregistration or cancellation.
(2) Guilds are required to maintain accurate records of their members, including admission dates, qualifications, and any disciplinary actions taken, for a minimum of 5 years. These records must be made available to the Registrar upon request within 14 days.
(3) Failure by a guild to maintain proper records as per subsection (2) may result in a fine of 750 crowns. The Registrar may conduct periodic audits of guild records to ensure compliance.

heading: Maintenance of Records
text:
(1) The Registrar shall maintain comprehensive records of all applications, registrations, renewals, suspensions, and cancellations of guilds and members. These records shall be kept for a minimum period of 15 years following a guild's or member's deregistration or cancellation, or indefinitely in cases of serious misconduct.
(2) Guilds are required to maintain accurate records of their members, including admission dates, qualifications, continuous professional development, and any disciplinary actions taken, for a minimum of 7 years. These records must be made available to the Registrar upon request within 7 days.
(3) Failure by a guild to maintain proper records as per subsection (2) may result in a fine of 1,200 crowns and potential suspension of registration. The Registrar may conduct periodic and unannounced audits of guild records to ensure compliance, with a minimum of 20% of all registered guilds audited annually.

heading: Reporting Obligations of Guilds
text:
(1) Every registered guild must submit an annual report to the Registrar by January 31st of each year. This report must include:
(a) A list of current executive officers.
(b) A summary of membership changes, including new admissions and cessations.
(c) A declaration that the guild continues to meet all registration requirements.
(d) Any significant changes to the guild's constitution or operational procedures.
(2) Failure to submit the annual report by the due date may result in a penalty of 300 crowns for every month of delay, up to a maximum of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Reporting Obligations of Guilds
text:
(1) Every registered guild must submit an annual report to the Registrar by December 31st of each year. This report must include:
(a) A list of current executive officers and their contact details.
(b) A detailed summary of membership changes, including new admissions, cessations, and any internal disciplinary actions taken against members.
(c) A declaration that the guild continues to meet all registration requirements and a report on its continuous professional development activities for members.
(d) Any significant changes to the guild's constitution, operational procedures, or trade standards.
(e) A financial statement for the preceding year, certified by a guild officer.
(2) Failure to submit the annual report by the due date may result in a penalty of 500 crowns for every month of delay, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns, and may trigger a review of the guild's registration status.

heading: Powers of Investigation
text:
(1) The Registrar, or an authorised inspector, may investigate any alleged breach of this Act or concerns regarding the conduct of a registered guild or member.
(2) For the purpose of an investigation, the Registrar or inspector may:
(a) Request access to any relevant records, documents, or premises of a guild during business hours, with 72 hours' notice.
(b) Interview any guild officer, member, or other relevant person.
(3) Any person who obstructs an investigation commits an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 crowns. Refusal to cooperate with an investigation may lead to immediate suspension of the relevant registration.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All personal information collected by the Registrar, beyond what is required for the public register, shall be treated as confidential. This includes residential addresses, specific qualifications, and personal financial details. Such information shall not be disclosed to any third party except as required by law or with the express written consent of the individual concerned. The Registrar shall implement robust data protection measures to safeguard all confidential information, including encrypted databases and restricted access protocols. Breaches of confidentiality by Registrar staff may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment and personal fines up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Offences and Penalties for Unregistered Guilds
text:
(1) Any association representing itself as a trade guild within Nordvale without being duly registered under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such an association is liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not exceeding 15,000 crowns for a first offence.
(3) For subsequent offences, the fine shall be not less than 10,000 crowns and not exceeding 30,000 crowns. Additionally, the responsible officers of the unregistered guild may be personally liable for a fine of up to 5,000 crowns each. The Registrar may also seek an injunction to prevent the unregistered guild from operating.

heading: Offences and Penalties for Unregistered Members
text:
(1) Any individual representing themselves as a registered trade guild member within Nordvale without being duly registered under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such an individual is liable to a fine of not less than 500 crowns and not exceeding 2,000 crowns for a first offence.
(3) For subsequent offences, the fine shall be not less than 1,000 crowns and not exceeding 5,000 crowns. The individual may also be prohibited from applying for registration for a period of up to 12 months. Employers who knowingly engage unregistered members may also face penalties as per section 28.

heading: Offences and Penalties for Unregistered Members
text:
(1) Any individual representing themselves as a registered trade guild member within Nordvale without being duly registered under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such an individual is liable to a fine of not less than 800 crowns and not exceeding 3,000 crowns for a first offence.
(3) For subsequent offences, the fine shall be not less than 1,500 crowns and not exceeding 7,500 crowns. The individual may also be prohibited from applying for registration for a period of up to 24 months, and their name may be publicly listed as a non-compliant tradesperson. Employers who knowingly engage unregistered members may also face penalties as per section 28, potentially including a 10% reduction in eligible government grants.

heading: Penalties for Providing False Information
text:
(1) Any person or guild that knowingly provides false or misleading information in connection with an application, report, or any other document required by this Act commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such a person is liable to a fine of not less than 1,000 crowns and not exceeding 5,000 crowns, and immediate cancellation of any existing registration. Guilds are liable to a fine of not less than 3,000 crowns and not exceeding 10,000 crowns, and immediate cancellation of their registration. Additionally, any benefits or privileges derived from such false information shall be revoked. Prosecution will be pursued for severe cases.

heading: Penalties for Providing False Information
text:
(1) Any person or guild that knowingly provides false or misleading information in connection with an application, report, or any other document required by this Act commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such a person is liable to a fine of not less than 2,000 crowns and not exceeding 8,000 crowns, and immediate cancellation of any existing registration, with a re-application ban of 36 months. Guilds are liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not exceeding 20,000 crowns, and immediate cancellation of their registration, with its executive officers potentially facing individual fines of up to 7,500 crowns. Additionally, any benefits or privileges derived from such false information shall be revoked. The Registrar will actively pursue prosecution for all instances of knowingly false information, and publicize such convictions.

heading: Penalties for Employers
text:
(1) Any employer who knowingly employs an individual to perform a trade requiring registration under this Act, where that individual is not a registered member, commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such an employer is liable to a fine of not less than 2,000 crowns and not exceeding 8,000 crowns for a first offence.
(3) For subsequent offences, the fine shall be not less than 5,000 crowns and not exceeding 20,000 crowns. The Registrar may also publish the names of non-compliant employers on the public register for a period of 6 months. Employers are expected to conduct due diligence by checking the public member register.

heading: Fines and Enforcement
text: All fines imposed under this Act shall be paid to the Nordvale Ministry of Finance within 30 days of the conviction or penalty notice. Failure to pay fines within this period may result in an additional late payment penalty of 10% of the original fine, and further legal action for recovery. The Registrar is empowered to initiate proceedings in the Nordvale District Courts for the enforcement of penalties and fines. Monies collected from fines will be allocated to a special fund for the promotion of trade skills and vocational training across Nordvale's municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This fund will be managed with oversight from the Ministry of Commerce.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any guild or individual aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar under this Act, including refusal, suspension, or cancellation of registration, may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal.
(2) An appeal must be lodged within 30 days of receiving written notification of the Registrar's decision.
(3) The Tribunal shall hear the appeal and make a determination within 90 days of the appeal being lodged. The Tribunal's decision is final, subject only to judicial review on points of law. The Tribunal's costs for such an appeal will typically be 1,500 crowns.

heading: Immunity of Registrar
text: The Registrar and any person acting under the authority of the Registrar shall not be personally liable for any act done or omitted to be done in good faith in the exercise or purported exercise of any power or duty conferred or imposed by this Act. This immunity does not extend to acts of gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Any claims related to such actions shall be directed against the Ministry of Commerce, not the individual officer, protecting public servants who act diligently within their prescribed duties. The Ministry of Commerce will investigate all complaints of misconduct.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister of Commerce may make regulations for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), such regulations may provide for:
(a) Specific requirements for different types of trades and guilds.
(b) The form and content of applications, certificates, and other documents.
(c) Procedures for investigations and disciplinary actions.
(d) The amount of any fees or charges not explicitly set out in this Act, provided they do not exceed 500 crowns for minor administrative tasks.
(3) All regulations must be published in the Nordvale Government Gazette at least 60 days before coming into force, allowing for public consultation.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister of Commerce may make regulations for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act, following a minimum 45-day public comment period.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), such regulations may provide for:
(a) Specific, detailed requirements for different types of trades and guilds, including competency standards and continuous professional development quotas.
(b) The form and content of applications, certificates, and other documents, including electronic submission standards.
(c) Detailed procedures for investigations, disciplinary actions, and the handling of consumer complaints.
(d) The amount of any fees or charges not explicitly set out in this Act, provided they do not exceed 750 crowns for minor administrative tasks, with a detailed justification for any new fees.
(e) Guidelines for the ethical conduct of guilds and their members.
(3) All regulations must be published in the Nordvale Government Gazette at least 90 days before coming into force, accompanied by an impact assessment report.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Commerce every 5 years from its commencement date. The review shall assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose, the impact on registered guilds and members, and the overall state of professional standards in Nordvale. A report on the review, including any recommendations for amendments, shall be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament. Public feedback will be invited as part of the review process, with at least 60 days allocated for submissions from guilds, members, and the general public. The first review is scheduled for 2023-01-01.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Commerce every 3 years from its commencement date. The review shall assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose, the impact on registered guilds and members, the overall state of professional standards in Nordvale, and its alignment with economic development goals in regions like Dunmere and Elsby. A comprehensive report on the review, including any recommendations for amendments, shall be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament, with specific attention to quantitative data regarding compliance rates and consumer protection outcomes. Public feedback will be actively solicited as part of the review process, with at least 90 days allocated for submissions from guilds, members, and the general public, including public forums in at least three municipalities.

heading: Transitional Provisions for Existing Guilds
text: Existing trade guilds that were operational prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a period of 180 days from the commencement date to apply for registration. During this transitional period, such guilds may continue to operate without penalties, provided they submit a complete application within the timeframe. The Registrar shall prioritize these applications. Guilds that fail to apply within 180 days will be subject to the penalties outlined in section 25, starting from day 181. A temporary certificate of application will be issued upon receipt of a valid application, allowing continued operation during processing.

heading: Transitional Provisions for Existing Members
text: Individual members of existing trade guilds, where those guilds are registered or have applied for registration, shall have a period of 120 days from the date their guild becomes registered to apply for individual member registration. During this period, these members may continue to practice their trade without penalties. Failure to apply within 120 days will result in the individual being considered an unregistered member, subject to penalties under section 26. Guilds are responsible for informing their members of these requirements within 30 days of their own registration. The Registrar will waive the initial late fee for member applications received within 30 days after the 120-day grace period.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision of this Act or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of the Act which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application. To this end, the provisions of this Act are declared to be severable. The remainder of the Act shall continue in full force and effect. This ensures that the core objectives of guild and member registration remain enforceable even if minor parts of the legislation are found to be legally problematic.

heading: Short Title and Commencement
text: This Act may be cited as the 'Trade Guild Registration Act'. It shall come into force on January 1, 2018. The Minister of Commerce is responsible for ensuring the public dissemination of this Act, including publishing it in all official languages of Nordvale and making it available online by November 1, 2017. All relevant government departments and agencies are instructed to prepare for its implementation well in advance of the commencement date, with internal training completed by December 15, 2017. This early publication is crucial for widespread awareness.

heading: Guild Training Requirements
text:
(1) All registered guilds must ensure that their members undertake a minimum of 10 hours of approved continuous professional development (CPD) training every 24 months. This training should be relevant to their specific trade and aims to maintain or enhance their professional skills.
(2) Guilds shall keep records of their members' CPD activities and submit a summary to the Registrar with their annual report as per section 22. The Registrar may approve training providers and courses. Failure to comply with these training requirements may lead to a warning for the first instance and a fine of 500 crowns for the guild for subsequent instances. Individual members who fail to meet the CPD hours may have their registration suspended.

heading: Guild Training Requirements
text:
(1) All registered guilds must ensure that their members undertake a minimum of 15 hours of approved continuous professional development (CPD) training every 24 months. At least 5 hours of this training must be focused on ethical practices and client communication. This training should be relevant to their specific trade and aims to maintain or significantly enhance their professional skills.
(2) Guilds shall keep detailed, verifiable records of their members' CPD activities, including attendance certificates, and submit a comprehensive summary to the Registrar with their annual report as per section 22. The Registrar will actively vet and approve training providers and courses. Failure to comply with these training requirements may lead to a fine of 800 crowns for the guild for the first instance, and immediate suspension of the guild's ability to endorse new members for subsequent instances. Individual members who fail to meet the CPD hours may have their registration suspended for up to 6 months and be required to complete an additional 5 hours of training to reinstate.

heading: Consumer Complaint Mechanism
text:
(1) The Registrar shall establish and maintain a mechanism for members of the public to lodge complaints against registered guilds or members. This mechanism will be accessible online and via a dedicated helpline operating 5 days a week, 09:00 to 16:00.
(2) All complaints will be acknowledged within 5 business days and investigated within 45 days. The Registrar may refer complaints to the relevant guild for internal resolution in the first instance, requiring a report back within 30 days. Unresolved complaints or those indicating serious misconduct will be directly investigated by the Registrar. A summary of anonymized complaints and resolutions will be published annually.

heading: Data Protection and Security
text:
(1) The Registrar shall implement and maintain robust data protection and cybersecurity measures to safeguard all data collected under this Act. This includes personal information, guild records, and financial details, which must be encrypted and stored on secure servers located within Nordvale.
(2) Regular security audits shall be conducted at least twice annually by independent third-party experts. Any data breach must be reported to the affected individuals and the Nordvale Data Protection Authority within 72 hours of discovery. Failure to comply with data protection standards may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns for the Registrar's office, and disciplinary action against responsible staff members.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text: The Registrar shall establish formal cooperation agreements with the municipalities of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. These agreements will facilitate the sharing of information regarding local trade practices, unlicensed operations, and consumer protection initiatives. The Registrar will hold at least one public outreach event per year in each of these municipalities to engage with local guilds, members, and the public, promoting awareness of the Act and addressing specific regional concerns. Joint enforcement actions with municipal authorities will be undertaken as necessary, with mutual information sharing occurring weekly.

heading: Appeals Tribunal Fees
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Appeals Tribunal Fees
text:
(1) An appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal, as mentioned in section 30, shall incur a non-refundable fee of 2,000 crowns, payable upon lodging the appeal. This fee is intended to cover administrative costs and discourage frivolous appeals.
(2) The Tribunal may, in exceptional circumstances and upon application, waive or reduce the appeal fee if it determines that payment would cause undue financial hardship to the appellant, provided the appellant's annual income is below 40,000 crowns. Such applications for fee reduction must be submitted with supporting financial documentation at least 14 days prior to the appeal hearing.
(3) If an appeal is successful, 50% of the appeal fee may be reimbursed to the appellant by the Registrar. This reimbursement will occur within 30 days of the Tribunal's final decision. This section reintroduces fees that were previously repealed to better manage the volume of appeals.

heading: Payment terms
text: A licensed balloon pilot has an additional 30 days to pay any fee or allowance required by FDA §25. This extension applies automatically to all such pilots.

heading: Concessions
text: Each holder of a meteorological observer badge pays 5 crowns instead of the required minimum living space for caged animals, specifically 3 square metres for a rabbit and 1.5 square metres for a guinea pig.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for levies imposed on the extraction of minerals from the territory of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure a fair return to the Republic for the depletion of its natural resources and to fund public services. The scope extends to all commercial mineral extraction operations within Nordvale's land borders and its territorial waters. The levies are designed to be predictable and transparent, encouraging responsible mining practices while generating revenue for the common good of all citizens of Nordvale. This Act applies to all individuals and entities engaged in mineral extraction activities, regardless of their size or ownership structure.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Mineral' means any naturally occurring inorganic substance found in the Earth's crust that can be extracted for economic gain, including but not limited to ores, coal, precious metals, and industrial minerals.
(b) 'Extraction' refers to the process of removing minerals from the Earth, including mining, quarrying, and dredging.
(c) 'Extractor' means any person or entity holding a valid license or permit to extract minerals in Nordvale.
(d) 'Gross Revenue' means the total income derived from the sale of extracted minerals, before any deductions for expenses.
(e) 'Net Revenue' means Gross Revenue less direct operating costs of extraction, as defined in section 7.

heading: General Levy Rate
text: A general levy of 8% shall be applied to the Net Revenue derived from the extraction of all minerals, unless otherwise specified in subsequent sections of this Act. This levy is payable by the extractor to the Department of Natural Resources within 30 days of the end of each fiscal quarter. The calculation of Net Revenue for the purpose of this general levy must adhere strictly to the guidelines set forth in section 7. Failure to pay within the stipulated period will result in penalties as outlined in section 28. This rate serves as the baseline for all mineral extraction activities across Nordvale.

heading: General Levy Rate
text: A general levy of 9% shall be applied to the Net Revenue derived from the extraction of all minerals, unless otherwise specified in subsequent sections of this Act. This levy is payable by the extractor to the Department of Natural Resources within 30 days of the end of each fiscal quarter. The calculation of Net Revenue for the purpose of this general levy must adhere strictly to the guidelines set forth in section 7. Failure to pay within the stipulated period will result in penalties as outlined in section 28. This rate serves as the baseline for all mineral extraction activities across Nordvale.

heading: General Levy Rate
text: A general levy of 10% shall be applied to the Net Revenue derived from the extraction of all minerals, unless otherwise specified in subsequent sections of this Act. This levy is payable by the extractor to the Department of Natural Resources within 30 days of the end of each fiscal quarter. The calculation of Net Revenue for the purpose of this general levy must adhere strictly to the guidelines set forth in section 7. Failure to pay within the stipulated period will result in penalties as outlined in section 28. This rate serves as the baseline for all mineral extraction activities across Nordvale, with an aim to further bolster national infrastructure projects.

heading: Levy on Precious Metals
text: The extraction of precious metals, including gold, silver, and platinum, shall be subject to a special levy rate. This rate is fixed at 12% of the Net Revenue generated from their sale. This higher rate reflects the inherent value and limited availability of these resources. Extractor companies must separately account for precious metal revenues and costs. Payments are due quarterly, within 45 days of the quarter's end. Any failure to declare or under-declare precious metal extraction will be subject to severe fines as detailed in section 29, in addition to the standard penalties for late payment.

heading: Levy on Precious Metals
text: The extraction of precious metals, including gold, silver, and platinum, shall be subject to a special levy rate. This rate is fixed at 13.5% of the Net Revenue generated from their sale. This higher rate reflects the inherent value and limited availability of these resources. Extractor companies must separately account for precious metal revenues and costs. Payments are due quarterly, within 45 days of the quarter's end. Any failure to declare or under-declare precious metal extraction will be subject to severe fines as detailed in section 29, in addition to the standard penalties for late payment. The increased rate aims to capture more value for the Republic.

heading: Levy on Industrial Minerals
text: Industrial minerals, such as limestone, gypsum, and aggregates, are subject to a reduced levy rate due to their widespread use in construction and lower market value. The levy for these minerals is set at 6% of the Net Revenue. This rate is intended to support the national construction sector and local development projects. Extractor companies dealing primarily in industrial minerals must submit their levy payments semi-annually, within 60 days of the end of the fiscal half-year. Simplified reporting procedures may apply, as determined by the Department of Natural Resources.

heading: Levy on Rare Earth Elements
text: Extraction of rare earth elements, vital for advanced technologies, shall be subject to a premium levy. This levy is set at 15% of the Net Revenue. Given their strategic importance and complex extraction processes, specific environmental impact assessments are mandated before extraction permits are issued. Revenue from this levy will be directed towards the National Innovation Fund, as stipulated in section 34. Payments are required monthly, within 20 days of the month's end, reflecting the rapid market fluctuations often associated with these materials.

heading: Levy on Rare Earth Elements
text: Extraction of rare earth elements, vital for advanced technologies, shall be subject to a premium levy. This levy is set at 18% of the Net Revenue. Given their strategic importance and complex extraction processes, specific environmental impact assessments are mandated before extraction permits are issued. Revenue from this levy will be directed towards the National Innovation Fund, as stipulated in section 34. Payments are required monthly, within 20 days of the month's end, reflecting the rapid market fluctuations often associated with these materials. This increased rate acknowledges the growing global demand and scarcity.

heading: Calculation of Net Revenue
text:
Net Revenue for levy purposes shall be calculated by subtracting direct operating costs from Gross Revenue. Direct operating costs eligible for deduction include:
(a) Wages and salaries directly attributable to extraction operations, up to 70% of total payroll.
(b) Cost of materials and supplies consumed in the extraction process, limited to 95% of documented expenditure.
(c) Fuel and energy costs directly used for extraction machinery.
(d) Depreciation of extraction equipment, calculated on a straight-line basis over 10 years.
(e) Transportation costs from the mine site to the first point of sale, capped at 15% of Gross Revenue. Administrative and marketing expenses are not deductible.

heading: Calculation of Net Revenue
text:
Net Revenue for levy purposes shall be calculated by subtracting direct operating costs from Gross Revenue. Direct operating costs eligible for deduction include:
(a) Wages and salaries directly attributable to extraction operations, up to 75% of total payroll.
(b) Cost of materials and supplies consumed in the extraction process, limited to 90% of documented expenditure.
(c) Fuel and energy costs directly used for extraction machinery.
(d) Depreciation of extraction equipment, calculated on a straight-line basis over 8 years.
(e) Transportation costs from the mine site to the first point of sale, capped at 12% of Gross Revenue. Administrative, marketing, and corporate overhead expenses are not deductible.

heading: Minimum Annual Levy
text: Every extractor, regardless of their Net Revenue, shall pay a minimum annual levy of 10,000 crowns. This minimum ensures that all licensed operations contribute a baseline amount towards resource management and environmental oversight. If the calculated levy based on Net Revenue for the fiscal year is less than 10,000 crowns, the extractor must still pay the minimum amount. This provision applies to all types of mineral extraction and is due by the 31st of March of the following fiscal year. Exemptions may be granted by the Department of Natural Resources under exceptional circumstances.

heading: Levy Exemption for Small-Scale Operations
text: Small-scale extraction operations with annual Gross Revenue below 50,000 crowns are exempt from all levies under this Act. This exemption is intended to support artisanal miners and local community ventures, provided they adhere to all environmental and safety regulations. To qualify for this exemption, an extractor must apply annually to the Department of Natural Resources and demonstrate that their revenue falls below the threshold. This exemption does not relieve them of reporting obligations, which must still be fulfilled quarterly to monitor activity levels.

heading: Community Development Levy
text: An additional community development levy of 1% of Gross Revenue shall be imposed on all extraction operations. This levy is specifically earmarked for projects benefiting the communities in the immediate vicinity of extraction sites, such as road improvements, water infrastructure, and local schools. The funds collected under this section will be managed by the local municipal councils of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, in consultation with affected communities. Extractor companies are required to pay this levy directly to the respective municipal council quarterly.

heading: Community Development Levy
text: An additional community development levy of 1.5% of Gross Revenue shall be imposed on all extraction operations. This levy is specifically earmarked for projects benefiting the communities in the immediate vicinity of extraction sites, such as road improvements, water infrastructure, and local schools. The funds collected under this section will be managed by the local municipal councils of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, in consultation with affected communities. Extractor companies are required to pay this levy directly to the respective municipal council quarterly. The increase aims to provide greater support to these communities.

heading: Environmental Restoration Fund Levy
text: A levy of 2% of Net Revenue shall be contributed to the Environmental Restoration Fund. This fund is dedicated to rehabilitating land and ecosystems damaged by past or present mineral extraction activities. Payments are due semi-annually. All extractors, regardless of mineral type or scale, are obligated to contribute. The Department of Environmental Protection manages this fund and oversees restoration projects. Extractors failing to pay this levy face a penalty of 15% of the unpaid amount, in addition to interest, and may have their operating permits suspended.

heading: Exploration Levy Exemption
text: Activities solely related to mineral exploration, not involving actual extraction for commercial purposes, are exempt from all levies under this Act. This exemption aims to encourage investment in discovering new mineral deposits within Nordvale. To qualify, an extractor must demonstrate that their activities are limited to geological surveys, drilling for sampling, and feasibility studies. Should exploration lead to commercial extraction, levies will apply from the first day of commercial operation. Detailed records of exploration expenditures and activities must be maintained for inspection.

heading: New Mine Development Incentive
text: New mines commencing operations after the effective date of this Act shall receive a reduced levy rate for their first three years of commercial production. The general levy rate as specified in section 3 shall be reduced by 2 percentage points for this initial period. This incentive is designed to stimulate investment in new mining ventures and create employment opportunities. To qualify, a mine must be demonstrably new and not an expansion of an existing operation. The reduced rate will apply from the date of the first commercial sale of minerals.

heading: New Mine Development Incentive
text: New mines commencing operations after the effective date of this Act shall receive a reduced levy rate for their first four years of commercial production. The general levy rate as specified in section 3 shall be reduced by 2.5 percentage points for this initial period. This incentive is designed to stimulate investment in new mining ventures and create employment opportunities. To qualify, a mine must be demonstrably new and not an expansion of an existing operation. The reduced rate will apply from the date of the first commercial sale of minerals, aiming to further encourage capital inflow.

heading: New Mine Development Incentive
text: New mines commencing operations after the effective date of this Act shall receive a reduced levy rate for their first five years of commercial production. The general levy rate as specified in section 3 shall be reduced by 3 percentage points for this initial period. This incentive is designed to stimulate investment in new mining ventures and create employment opportunities. To qualify, a mine must be demonstrably new and not an expansion of an existing operation. The reduced rate will apply from the date of the first commercial sale of minerals, providing substantial long-term benefits to new investors.

heading: Deep Mining Incentive
text: Extraction from deposits located more than 500 meters below the surface shall qualify for a 1 percentage point reduction in the applicable levy rate. This incentive acknowledges the increased technical challenges and costs associated with deep mining operations. Extractor companies must provide verifiable geological surveys and operational data to prove the depth of extraction.
