The reduction applies only to the Net Revenue directly attributable to minerals extracted from these depths. This provision aims to promote the extraction of deeper, harder-to-reach mineral resources.

heading: Remote Area Extraction Incentive
text: Extraction operations located more than 100 kilometers from any municipality listed in section 10 shall receive a 0.5 percentage point reduction in their applicable levy rate. This incentive encourages development in remote areas of Nordvale. Companies must demonstrate the remote nature of their operations through mapping and logistics data. The reduction is applied to the general levy rate and aims to offset higher logistical costs. This incentive will be reviewed every five years to ensure its continued relevance and impact on regional development.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Every extractor must submit quarterly reports to the Department of Natural Resources detailing Gross Revenue, direct operating costs, and the resulting Net Revenue. These reports are due within 30 days of the end of each fiscal quarter. Reports must also include the type and quantity of minerals extracted, their origin within Nordvale, and the market prices received. Falsification of reports is a serious offense, punishable under section 29. The Department may require additional information as deemed necessary for verification.

heading: Audit and Verification
text: The Department of Natural Resources has the authority to conduct audits of any extractor's financial records and operational data at any time. Extractor companies must retain all relevant documents for a minimum of 7 years. Failure to cooperate with an audit, or to provide requested documentation within 14 days, may result in an immediate levy assessment based on departmental estimates, plus a penalty of 20% of the estimated levy. Auditors may visit extraction sites with 48 hours' notice to verify operational practices.

heading: Payment Due Dates
text: Unless otherwise specified, all levies under this Act are due within 30 days following the end of the reporting period (quarterly, semi-annually, or annually). If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, payment is due on the next business day. Extractor companies are responsible for ensuring timely payment. Electronic payment methods are preferred, and details for such payments are available on the Department of Natural Resources' official portal. Post-dated checks are not accepted as valid payment.

heading: Interest on Late Payments
text: Any levy payment not received by the due date shall accrue interest at a rate of 1% per month, compounded monthly, on the unpaid balance. This interest will be calculated from the day following the due date until the date of full payment. This rate is applied uniformly across all types of levies and all extractors. The Department of Natural Resources will issue a notice of outstanding payment and accrued interest within 15 days of the payment being overdue. Continued non-payment will lead to further enforcement actions.

heading: Interest on Late Payments
text: Any levy payment not received by the due date shall accrue interest at a rate of 1.2% per month, compounded monthly, on the unpaid balance. This interest will be calculated from the day following the due date until the date of full payment. This rate is applied uniformly across all types of levies and all extractors. The Department of Natural Resources will issue a notice of outstanding payment and accrued interest within 10 days of the payment being overdue. Continued non-payment will lead to further enforcement actions as detailed in section 28.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: In addition to interest on late payments, extractors who fail to submit reports or pay levies on time may face penalties. A penalty of 5% of the unpaid levy will be applied for the first 30 days of delay, increasing to 10% for delays between 31 and 60 days. Delays exceeding 60 days may result in suspension of the extraction license for a minimum of 90 days. Repeated non-compliance within a 24-month period will lead to a review of the extractor's license with possible revocation.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An extractor may appeal any levy assessment, penalty, or decision made by the Department of Natural Resources within 60 days of receiving the official notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Levy Appeals Board, detailing the grounds for the appeal and providing supporting documentation. The Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 90 days. During the appeal process, the extractor is still obligated to pay the original levy amount to avoid further penalties, though disputed amounts may be held in escrow.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All financial and operational data submitted by extractors under this Act shall be treated as confidential by the Department of Natural Resources, subject to the provisions of public information laws. Information will not be disclosed to third parties without the extractor's written consent, except as required for auditing, legal proceedings, or statistical reporting where individual company data is anonymized. Any departmental employee found to have breached confidentiality will face disciplinary action and potential legal prosecution, with fines up to 50,000 crowns.

heading: Force Majeure
text: In cases of force majeure, such as natural disasters, war, or unforeseen governmental actions, an extractor may apply for a temporary deferral of levy payments. The application must be submitted within 15 days of the force majeure event occurring, providing evidence of its impact on extraction operations and financial capacity. The Department of Natural Resources will review each application on a case-by-case basis and may grant deferrals for up to 90 days. Interest on deferred payments may still accrue, but penalties for late payment may be waived.

heading: Exclusion for Research Purposes
text: The extraction of small quantities of minerals solely for scientific research or educational purposes is exempt from all levies. The total quantity extracted for such purposes must not exceed 500 kilograms annually per institution. Institutions must apply for a specific research extraction permit from the Department of Natural Resources and submit annual reports detailing the quantities extracted and the nature of the research. Commercialization of any minerals extracted under this exemption will immediately void the exemption and trigger all applicable levies.

heading: Sustainable Mining Practices Incentive
text: Extractors who implement certified sustainable mining practices may qualify for a 0.5 percentage point reduction in their applicable levy rate. Certification must be granted by an independent, government-approved environmental auditor. This incentive aims to promote environmentally responsible extraction methods, such as water recycling, reduced energy consumption, and advanced land rehabilitation. The certification must be renewed every two years. The Department of Environmental Protection will publish a list of approved auditors and sustainable practice criteria annually.

heading: Sustainable Mining Practices Incentive
text: Extractors who implement certified sustainable mining practices may qualify for a 0.75 percentage point reduction in their applicable levy rate. Certification must be granted by an independent, government-approved environmental auditor. This incentive aims to promote environmentally responsible extraction methods, such as water recycling, reduced energy consumption, and advanced land rehabilitation. The certification must be renewed every two years. The Department of Environmental Protection will publish a list of approved auditors and sustainable practice criteria annually. This increased incentive reflects a stronger commitment to ecological preservation.

heading: Local Employment Incentive
text: Extractors who employ at least 80% of their workforce from within a 50-kilometer radius of the extraction site may receive a 0.25 percentage point reduction in their applicable levy rate. This incentive supports local economies and provides stable employment in mining regions. Companies must submit verifiable employment records, including addresses of employees, to qualify. The Department of Labor will verify compliance annually. This incentive applies only to direct employees involved in extraction operations, not administrative or corporate staff.

heading: Investment in Processing Incentive
text: Extractors who invest a minimum of 5,000,000 crowns in local mineral processing facilities within Nordvale shall receive a 1 percentage point reduction on their general levy rate for five years. This incentive aims to add value to raw materials domestically and create downstream industries. The investment must be verified by audited financial statements. The reduction applies from the date the processing facility becomes operational. The Department of Commerce will oversee the approval process for eligible investments.

heading: Investment in Processing Incentive
text: Extractors who invest a minimum of 7,500,000 crowns in local mineral processing facilities within Nordvale shall receive a 1.25 percentage point reduction on their general levy rate for seven years. This incentive aims to add value to raw materials domestically and create downstream industries. The investment must be verified by audited financial statements. The reduction applies from the date the processing facility becomes operational. The Department of Commerce will oversee the approval process for eligible investments. This enhanced incentive is designed to significantly boost industrial capacity.

heading: Penalties for Evasion
text: Any extractor found to be deliberately evading levies through misrepresentation of revenue, fraudulent reporting of costs, or other deceptive practices shall be subject to severe penalties. In addition to paying the full amount of evaded levies with accumulated interest, a fine of 50% of the evaded amount shall be imposed. The extraction license may be immediately revoked, and the individuals responsible may face criminal charges and imprisonment for up to 5 years. A public registry of convicted evaders will be maintained by the Department of Justice.

heading: Refunds and Adjustments
text: If an extractor overpays a levy, they may apply for a refund within 12 months of the overpayment date. The application must include proof of overpayment and a detailed explanation. The Department of Natural Resources will review the application and issue a refund within 60 days of approval. Adjustments for errors in reporting can be made within 6 months of the original submission, provided they are supported by verifiable documentation. No interest will be paid on overpayments or adjustments by the Department.

heading: Levy Review Committee
text: A permanent Levy Review Committee shall be established to periodically assess the effectiveness and fairness of the levies established by this Act. The Committee shall consist of five members: two appointed by the Department of Natural Resources, two by the Department of Finance, and one independent expert. The Committee will meet at least once annually and submit recommendations for amendments to this Act to the Nordvale Assembly. Its mandate includes evaluating market conditions, technological changes, and their impact on extraction profitability.

heading: Exclusion for Construction Material
text: Extraction of aggregates, sand, and gravel solely for use in public infrastructure projects within Nordvale, directly undertaken by municipal governments or the national government, is exempt from all levies. This exemption applies only to materials that are not sold commercially but used directly in projects such as roads, bridges, and public buildings. The responsible government entity must provide documentation confirming the exclusive use of the materials for public works. Private contractors performing public works are not eligible for this exemption.

heading: Emergency Levy Powers
text: In times of national emergency declared by the Nordvale Assembly, the Department of Finance, in consultation with the Department of Natural Resources, may temporarily increase or decrease any levy rate by up to 2 percentage points for a maximum period of 12 months. Any such change must be published in the official gazette at least 30 days before its effective date. This provision ensures flexibility in funding critical national needs during unforeseen crises, such as widespread natural disasters requiring extensive national reconstruction.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any existing mineral extraction agreements or licenses issued before the effective date of this Act shall be subject to the provisions of this Act from their next renewal date, or within 3 years, whichever comes first. During this transitional period, the terms of the previous agreements shall remain in effect. Extractors are encouraged to review their existing arrangements and adjust their operations to comply with the new levy structure. The Department of Natural Resources will provide guidance during this transition period.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between an extractor and the Department of Natural Resources regarding the interpretation or application of this Act, that cannot be resolved through the appeals process under section 21, shall be submitted to binding arbitration. The arbitration panel shall consist of three independent arbitrators, one appointed by each party, and a third mutually agreed upon. The decision of the arbitration panel shall be final and binding on both parties, and legal costs will be borne by the losing party.

heading: Special Levy Rate for Uranium
text: The extraction of uranium shall be subject to a special levy rate of 20% of the Net Revenue. This elevated rate reflects the strategic importance and potential risks associated with this mineral. All revenue generated from this levy will be directed towards the National Energy Security Fund, as established by separate legislation. Extractor companies dealing with uranium must adhere to stringent security and environmental protocols, as defined by the Department of Energy. Payments are due monthly, within 15 days of the end of the month.

heading: Special Levy Rate for Uranium
text: The extraction of uranium shall be subject to a special levy rate of 25% of the Net Revenue. This elevated rate reflects the strategic importance and potential risks associated with this mineral. All revenue generated from this levy will be directed towards the National Energy Security Fund, as established by separate legislation. Extractor companies dealing with uranium must adhere to stringent security and environmental protocols, as defined by the Department of Energy. Payments are due monthly, within 15 days of the end of the month, reinforcing national energy independence.

heading: Levy on Coal
text: The extraction of coal is subject to a levy of 7% of Net Revenue. This rate is intended to balance the energy needs of Nordvale with the environmental considerations associated with coal mining. Extractor companies must submit quarterly reports detailing coal production and sales. A specific portion of the revenue, 1.5% of Net Revenue, will be allocated to the Air Quality Improvement Fund, managed by the Department of Environmental Protection. Payments are due within 30 days of the end of each fiscal quarter.

heading: Phosphate Extraction Levy
text: The extraction of phosphates, crucial for agricultural fertilizers, shall be subject to a levy of 6.5% of Net Revenue. This rate supports the agricultural sector by keeping input costs manageable while ensuring a fair return to the Republic. Companies extracting phosphates must also contribute 0.5% of Gross Revenue to a dedicated Soil Health Research Fund. Payments are due semi-annually, within 45 days of the end of the fiscal half-year, and reports must include details on the quantity and grade of phosphate extracted.

heading: Dredged Materials Levy
text: Commercial extraction of sand, gravel, and other aggregates through dredging operations in Nordvale's territorial waters is subject to a levy of 5% of Net Revenue. This levy accounts for the environmental impact on aquatic ecosystems. A further 0.5% of Gross Revenue from dredged materials must be allocated to the Marine Habitat Protection Fund. Permits for dredging operations are issued by the Department of Maritime Affairs, which also monitors compliance with environmental regulations. Payments are due quarterly.

heading: Limestone Quarry Levy
text: Limestone quarries are subject to a specific levy of 5.5% of Net Revenue. This rate recognizes the high volume and relatively low unit value of limestone, which is primarily used in cement production and construction. Companies operating limestone quarries must also contribute 0.25% of Gross Revenue to a Land Reclamation Fund specifically for quarry sites. Payments are due semi-annually, within 60 days of the fiscal half-year end. Annual site inspections are mandatory to ensure adherence to safety and environmental standards.

heading: Gypsum Extraction Levy
text: The extraction of gypsum is subject to a levy of 6% of Net Revenue. This mineral is important for construction and agriculture. Payments are due quarterly, within 30 days of the end of the fiscal quarter. Extractor companies must provide detailed reports on the volume of gypsum extracted and its intended use. Any gypsum extracted for direct use in the extractor's own manufacturing processes, without an external sale, must be valued at fair market price for levy calculation purposes, as determined by the Department of Natural Resources.

heading: Bauxite Levy
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Bauxite Levy
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: (1) Any person who is a registered saddler shall not pay any loan fees for books. (2) This exemption applies to books borrowed for personal use, up to a maximum of 20 items at one time.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: The summer camp fee in YTA §2 is reduced for any child of a licensed bell ringer of a parish tower, who has 30 extra days to pay the fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a levy on the extraction of minerals within the territory of Nordvale. The purpose of this levy is to ensure that the extraction of valuable natural resources contributes fairly to the public finances, supporting essential services across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This levy applies to all individuals and entities engaged in mineral extraction activities, regardless of the scale of their operations. The provisions of this Act are designed to be clear and equitable for all involved parties, promoting responsible resource management and economic stability for the nation.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Mineral" means any naturally occurring inorganic substance extracted from the earth, including but not limited to ores, aggregates, and precious stones, excluding water, oil, and natural gas.
(b) "Extraction" means the process of removing minerals from the ground, including quarrying, mining, and dredging.
(c) "Extractor" means any person, company, or other entity engaged in the business of mineral extraction.
(d) "Levy" refers to the charge imposed by this Act.

heading: Levy imposition
text: A levy is hereby imposed on all minerals extracted within Nordvale. The levy shall be calculated based on the gross value of the extracted minerals at the point of extraction, prior to any processing or refinement. This applies to all extraction sites, whether temporary or permanent, and across all types of minerals specified in section 2(a). The levy is a mandatory payment, and all extractors are responsible for its accurate calculation and timely remittance to the national treasury. Failure to comply will result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Basic levy rate
text: The basic levy rate for all extracted minerals is set at 3% of the gross value. This rate applies universally to all mineral types unless a specific exception or higher rate is provided for elsewhere in this Act. The gross value is determined at the moment the mineral is removed from the ground. This foundational rate ensures a consistent contribution from all extraction operations towards the national income. Extractors must use this rate as a baseline for their calculations.

heading: Basic levy rate
text: The basic levy rate for all extracted minerals is set at 3.5% of the gross value. This rate applies universally to all mineral types unless a specific exception or higher rate is provided for elsewhere in this Act. The gross value is determined at the moment the mineral is removed from the ground. This foundational rate ensures a consistent contribution from all extraction operations towards the national income. Extractors must use this rate as a baseline for their calculations.

heading: Basic levy rate
text: The basic levy rate for all extracted minerals is set at 4% of the gross value. This rate applies universally to all mineral types unless a specific exception or higher rate is provided for elsewhere in this Act. The gross value is determined at the moment the mineral is removed from the ground. This foundational rate ensures a consistent contribution from all extraction operations towards the national income. Extractors must use this rate as a baseline for their calculations.

heading: Precious metals levy rate
text: For precious metals, including but not limited to gold, silver, and platinum, a higher levy rate of 5% of the gross value applies. This special rate reflects the inherent high market value and scarcity of these particular minerals. Extractors dealing with precious metals must differentiate these from other minerals in their reporting and apply this specific rate. The determination of what constitutes a precious metal will be guided by established market classifications and national standards.

heading: Precious metals levy rate
text: For precious metals, including but not limited to gold, silver, and platinum, a higher levy rate of 6% of the gross value applies. This special rate reflects the inherent high market value and scarcity of these particular minerals. Extractors dealing with precious metals must differentiate these from other minerals in their reporting and apply this specific rate. The determination of what constitutes a precious metal will be guided by established market classifications and national standards.

heading: Rare earth elements levy rate
text: A levy rate of 4.5% of the gross value is imposed on rare earth elements. This rate acknowledges the strategic importance and specialized extraction processes often associated with these minerals. Extractors involved in the recovery of rare earth elements must ensure accurate classification and application of this specific levy rate. Clear documentation distinguishing these elements from other mineral types is essential for compliance purposes.

heading: Rare earth elements levy rate
text: A levy rate of 5.5% of the gross value is imposed on rare earth elements. This rate acknowledges the strategic importance and specialized extraction processes often associated with these minerals. Extractors involved in the recovery of rare earth elements must ensure accurate classification and application of this specific levy rate. Clear documentation distinguishing these elements from other mineral types is essential for compliance purposes.

heading: Aggregates levy rate
text: For aggregates such as sand, gravel, and crushed stone, a reduced levy rate of 2% of the gross value is applied. This lower rate reflects the high volume and relatively lower unit value of these essential construction materials. This aims to support infrastructure development and reduce the cost burden on the construction sector. Extractors of aggregates must clearly separate these materials in their reporting to qualify for this reduced rate.

heading: Aggregates levy rate
text: For aggregates such as sand, gravel, and crushed stone, a reduced levy rate of 2.5% of the gross value is applied. This lower rate reflects the high volume and relatively lower unit value of these essential construction materials. This aims to support infrastructure development and reduce the cost burden on the construction sector. Extractors of aggregates must clearly separate these materials in their reporting to qualify for this reduced rate.

heading: Semi-precious stones levy rate
text: A levy rate of 4% of the gross value is applicable to semi-precious stones. This category includes minerals like quartz, amethyst, and topaz, which hold significant commercial value but are distinct from precious metals. This specific rate ensures a fair contribution from this segment of the extraction industry. Extractors must accurately classify and report their semi-precious stone output for levy calculation.

heading: Quarterly reporting requirement
text: All extractors are required to submit a detailed report of their mineral extraction activities on a quarterly basis. Each report must cover the preceding three-month period and be submitted within 30 days of the end of that quarter. The report must include the types and quantities of minerals extracted, their gross value, and the calculated levy amount. These reports are crucial for accurate levy collection and national resource monitoring.

heading: Quarterly reporting requirement
text: All extractors are required to submit a detailed report of their mineral extraction activities on a quarterly basis. Each report must cover the preceding three-month period and be submitted within 20 days of the end of that quarter. The report must include the types and quantities of minerals extracted, their gross value, and the calculated levy amount. These reports are crucial for accurate levy collection and national resource monitoring.

heading: Payment deadline
text: The full amount of the levy for each quarter must be remitted to the national treasury no later than 45 days after the end of that quarter. Payments can be made via electronic transfer or certified cheque. Timely payment is essential for avoiding late payment penalties as stipulated in section 28. Extractors are encouraged to establish internal processes to ensure adherence to this strict deadline.

heading: Payment deadline
text: The full amount of the levy for each quarter must be remitted to the national treasury no later than 35 days after the end of that quarter. Payments can be made via electronic transfer or certified cheque. Timely payment is essential for avoiding late payment penalties as stipulated in section 28. Extractors are encouraged to establish internal processes to ensure adherence to this strict deadline.

heading: Exemption for research samples
text: Small quantities of minerals extracted solely for scientific research or geological survey purposes, not exceeding 10 kilograms per calendar year per extractor, are exempt from the levy. This exemption supports scientific advancement and understanding of Nordvale's geology. Extractors must obtain prior approval from the relevant authority and maintain detailed records to qualify for this exemption. Any commercial use of such samples nullifies the exemption.

heading: Exemption for research samples
text: Small quantities of minerals extracted solely for scientific research or geological survey purposes, not exceeding 5 kilograms per calendar year per extractor, are exempt from the levy. This exemption supports scientific advancement and understanding of Nordvale's geology. Extractors must obtain prior approval from the relevant authority and maintain detailed records to qualify for this exemption. Any commercial use of such samples nullifies the exemption.

heading: Exemption for small-scale operations
text: Extractors whose total annual gross value of extracted minerals does not exceed 50,000 crowns are exempt from the levy. This exemption aims to support very small-scale operations and individual prospectors. Such extractors must still register with the authorities and submit an annual declaration confirming their eligibility for this exemption. If the threshold is exceeded, the levy becomes applicable to the entire annual gross value.

heading: Exemption for small-scale operations
text: Extractors whose total annual gross value of extracted minerals does not exceed 30,000 crowns are exempt from the levy. This exemption aims to support very small-scale operations and individual prospectors. Such extractors must still register with the authorities and submit an annual declaration confirming their eligibility for this exemption. If the threshold is exceeded, the levy becomes applicable to the entire annual gross value.

heading: Value determination for unprocessed minerals
text: The gross value of unprocessed minerals shall be determined by their market price at the nearest major trading hub in Nordvale at the time of extraction. If no direct market price is available, a valuation shall be made based on comparable minerals, adjusted for quality and quantity. The national treasury department will publish guidance on acceptable valuation methodologies. Any disputes regarding valuation can be escalated as per section 25.

heading: Value determination for processed minerals
text: If minerals are processed or refined by the extractor before sale, the gross value for levy purposes shall be the market price of the raw, unprocessed mineral at the point of extraction. The value added through processing is not subject to this levy. This ensures fairness and prevents double taxation on value-added activities. Extractors must maintain separate records for raw mineral valuation and processing costs.

heading: Records retention
text: All extractors must maintain detailed records of their extraction activities, including quantities extracted, sales invoices, valuation reports, and levy calculations, for a minimum period of five years. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by national authorities. Failure to produce requested records within 14 days may result in penalties. Good record-keeping is vital for transparency and compliance with this Act.

heading: Records retention
text: All extractors must maintain detailed records of their extraction activities, including quantities extracted, sales invoices, valuation reports, and levy calculations, for a minimum period of seven years. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by national authorities. Failure to produce requested records within 10 days may result in penalties. Good record-keeping is vital for transparency and compliance with this Act.

heading: Audit and inspection rights
text: National treasury officials, or their appointed representatives, have the right to audit and inspect any extractor's premises, records, and operations during normal business hours to verify compliance with this Act. Extractors must cooperate fully with such audits. A minimum of 7 days' written notice will typically be provided for routine inspections, except in cases of suspected fraud or serious non-compliance, where immediate inspection may occur.

heading: Obligation to register
text: Every person or entity commencing mineral extraction activities in Nordvale must register with the national treasury department within 30 days of starting operations. Registration involves providing details of the extractor, location of extraction sites, and the types of minerals intended for extraction. This registration process ensures that all extractors are known to the authorities and are aware of their obligations under this Act.

heading: Obligation to register
text: Every person or entity commencing mineral extraction activities in Nordvale must register with the national treasury department within 21 days of starting operations. Registration involves providing details of the extractor, location of extraction sites, and the types of minerals intended for extraction. This registration process ensures that all extractors are known to the authorities and are aware of their obligations under this Act.

heading: Changes to registration details
text: Any significant changes to an extractor's registration details, such as changes in ownership, primary extraction location, or types of minerals extracted, must be reported to the national treasury department within 60 days of the change. This ensures that the national registry of extractors remains accurate and up-to-date. Failure to report changes may lead to administrative fines as per section 29.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text: Information provided by extractors for the purpose of this Act shall be treated as confidential by the national authorities and shall not be disclosed to third parties, except as required by law or for the purpose of enforcing this Act. Aggregate statistical data, not identifying individual extractors, may be published for public information. All officials handling this data are bound by strict confidentiality agreements.

heading: Appeals process
text: An extractor may appeal a levy assessment or penalty decision within 30 days of receiving notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the national treasury department, detailing the grounds for appeal and providing supporting documentation. The department will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. Further appeal options may be available through established administrative tribunals.

heading: Voluntary disclosure
text: Extractors who voluntarily disclose errors or omissions in their levy reporting before being contacted by the authorities may be subject to reduced penalties. The reduction can be up to 50% of the standard penalty, at the discretion of the national treasury department. This encourages self-correction and compliance, fostering a cooperative environment between extractors and authorities. Disclosure must be complete and accompanied by rectified reports and payments.

heading: Environmental contribution deduction
text: Extractors undertaking approved environmental remediation or restoration projects at their extraction sites may deduct up to 15% of the costs of such projects from their total annual levy liability. The projects must be pre-approved by the national environmental agency and directly related to the impact of their extraction activities. This incentive promotes responsible environmental stewardship. A maximum deduction of 50,000 crowns per year applies.

heading: Environmental contribution deduction
text: Extractors undertaking approved environmental remediation or restoration projects at their extraction sites may deduct up to 12% of the costs of such projects from their total annual levy liability. The projects must be pre-approved by the national environmental agency and directly related to the impact of their extraction activities. This incentive promotes responsible environmental stewardship. A maximum deduction of 40,000 crowns per year applies.

heading: Local community development credit
text: Extractors contributing to approved local community development projects in the municipalities where extraction occurs (e.g., Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick) may receive a credit against their levy. The credit is limited to 10% of the project's value, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns annually per extractor. Projects must be verified by the respective municipal council and approved by the national treasury to qualify for this credit, encouraging local investment.

heading: Local community development credit
text: Extractors contributing to approved local community development projects in the municipalities where extraction occurs (e.g., Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick) may receive a credit against their levy. The credit is limited to 8% of the project's value, up to a maximum of 20,000 crowns annually per extractor. Projects must be verified by the respective municipal council and approved by the national treasury to qualify for this credit, encouraging local investment.

heading: Infrastructure improvement incentive
text: Extractors investing in significant local infrastructure improvements directly related to their operations, such as road upgrades or utility expansions, may claim a levy reduction. The reduction is capped at 20% of the documented investment cost, up to 100,000 crowns per project. Approval from the national infrastructure department is mandatory, ensuring projects align with national development plans. This encourages private sector involvement in public works.

heading: Hardship provisions
text: In cases of severe financial hardship, an extractor may apply to the national treasury department for a temporary deferral of levy payments or a payment plan. Such applications must be submitted in writing, with comprehensive financial documentation, at least 30 days before the payment deadline. Deferrals are typically granted for a maximum of six months, subject to review. This ensures flexibility in unforeseen economic difficulties.

heading: Anti-avoidance measures
text: Any schemes or arrangements designed primarily to avoid or reduce the levy payable under this Act shall be disregarded. The national treasury department may re-assess the levy based on the true economic substance of the transaction. Penalties for deliberate avoidance can be severe, including fines up to 200% of the evaded levy and potential legal action. This provision ensures the integrity of the levy system.

heading: Late payment penalty
text: A penalty of 1% of the unpaid levy amount shall be applied for each month, or part thereof, that a payment is overdue. This penalty is in addition to the original levy amount. An additional fixed charge of 500 crowns will also be applied for payments outstanding for more than 90 days. This graduated penalty system is designed to encourage prompt payment and deter delays in remittances to the treasury.

heading: Late payment penalty
text: A penalty of 1.5% of the unpaid levy amount shall be applied for each month, or part thereof, that a payment is overdue. This penalty is in addition to the original levy amount. An additional fixed charge of 750 crowns will also be applied for payments outstanding for more than 60 days. This graduated penalty system is designed to encourage prompt payment and deter delays in remittances to the treasury.

heading: Administrative fines for non-compliance
text: Failure to submit required reports (as per section 9) or provide accurate information may result in an administrative fine of 2,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance. Repeated non-compliance within a 12-month period may lead to increased fines of up to 5,000 crowns per instance. These fines are intended to ensure administrative efficiency and data accuracy, supporting the effective operation of the levy system.

heading: False reporting penalty
text: Any extractor found to have deliberately provided false or misleading information in their reports or during an audit shall be subject to a penalty of 100% of the levy understated or avoided, with a minimum penalty of 10,000 crowns. This is a serious offense and may also lead to further legal proceedings. The intent to deceive will be a key factor in determining the application of this severe penalty.

heading: Revocation of extraction license
text: In cases of persistent and severe non-compliance, including repeated failure to pay levies or egregious false reporting, the national authority may initiate proceedings to revoke an extractor's mineral extraction license. A warning will be issued after three instances of major non-compliance within a 24-month period. Revocation is a last resort, ensuring that only responsible operators continue to extract minerals in Nordvale.

heading: Enforcement powers
text: The national treasury department is empowered to take all necessary actions to enforce the provisions of this Act, including issuing demands for payment, imposing penalties, and initiating legal proceedings for recovery of outstanding levies and fines. These powers are critical for maintaining the integrity and effectiveness of the mineral extraction levy system. All actions will be conducted in accordance with national administrative procedures.

heading: Allocation of levy funds
text: Funds collected through this levy shall be allocated to the national general budget, with 20% specifically earmarked for infrastructure projects in rural areas and 15% for environmental protection initiatives across Nordvale, including Grauby and Lund Vale. The remaining funds support a broad range of public services. This allocation strategy ensures that the benefits of mineral extraction are widely distributed for the good of all citizens.

heading: Allocation of levy funds
text: Funds collected through this levy shall be allocated to the national general budget, with 25% specifically earmarked for infrastructure projects in rural areas and 10% for environmental protection initiatives across Nordvale, including Grauby and Lund Vale. The remaining funds support a broad range of public services. This allocation strategy ensures that the benefits of mineral extraction are widely distributed for the good of all citizens.

heading: Review of levy rates
text: The national treasury department shall review the levy rates specified in sections 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 every three years. This review will consider economic conditions, market prices of minerals, environmental impacts, and the overall contribution of the levy to public finances. Recommendations for adjustments will be submitted to the national assembly for consideration, ensuring the levy remains fair and effective over time.

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Car registration renewal for volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) The yearly fee for renewing the registration of a car is 15 crowns lower for one car owned by an active volunteer firefighter.
(2) This reduction is applied after any other reduction of that fee.
(3) The reduction does not apply to motorcycles or trailers.

heading: Car registration renewal for volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) The yearly fee for renewing the registration of a car is 20 crowns lower for one car owned by an active volunteer firefighter.
(2) This reduction is applied after any other reduction of that fee.
(3) The reduction does not apply to motorcycles or trailers.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act governs the issuance, renewal, suspension, and revocation of permits for mineral exploration activities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to regulate the search for mineral deposits, ensuring responsible practices, environmental protection, and the efficient use of national resources. The scope includes all exploration activities, from preliminary surveys to extensive drilling, conducted on both public and private lands, excluding activities related to petroleum or natural gas, which are covered by separate legislation.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Minister' means the Minister for Mineral Resources.
(b) 'Exploration Permit' means a permit issued under section 3 allowing for mineral exploration activities.
(c) 'Mineral' means any naturally occurring inorganic substance found in the Earth's crust, excluding water, petroleum, and natural gas.
(d) 'Applicant' means a person or entity applying for an Exploration Permit.
(2) 'Exploration activities' include geological mapping, geophysical surveys, geochemical sampling, trenching, drilling, and bulk sampling for the purpose of identifying mineral deposits.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) No person or entity shall conduct any mineral exploration activity within Nordvale without holding a valid Exploration Permit issued by the Minister.
(2) Any exploration activity undertaken without a permit is an offence and may result in penalties as outlined in section 30.
(3) This requirement applies to all areas, including state-owned land, private property, and offshore territories up to 12 nautical miles from the Nordvale coastline.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for an Exploration Permit must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) A detailed work program outlining proposed activities for the first 24 months.
(b) A map of the proposed exploration area with a scale of at least 1:25,000.
(c) Proof of financial capacity to cover exploration costs and potential rehabilitation, amounting to at least 150,000 crowns.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for an Exploration Permit must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) A detailed work program outlining proposed activities for the first 36 months.
(b) A map of the proposed exploration area with a scale of at least 1:10,000.
(c) Proof of financial capacity to cover exploration costs and potential rehabilitation, amounting to at least 200,000 crowns.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 7,500 crowns.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for an Exploration Permit must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) A detailed work program outlining proposed activities for the first 36 months.
(b) A map of the proposed exploration area with a scale of at least 1:10,000, clearly identifying all sensitive ecological zones.
(c) Proof of financial capacity to cover exploration costs and potential rehabilitation, amounting to at least 250,000 crowns.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Applicant Eligibility
text:
(1) To be eligible for an Exploration Permit, an applicant must be:
(a) A citizen of Nordvale aged 18 years or older, or
(b) A company registered in Nordvale with at least 51% of its shares owned by Nordvale citizens.
(2) The applicant must not have any outstanding fines or penalties under this Act or any other environmental protection legislation.
(3) The applicant must demonstrate a clean record regarding previous exploration or mining activities, with no significant environmental breaches in the past 10 years.

heading: Area Limits
text:
(1) The maximum area that may be granted under a single Exploration Permit is 150 square kilometres.
(2) No single applicant or related entities may hold permits covering more than 750 square kilometres at any given time across all of Nordvale.
(3) The minimum area for which a permit can be issued is 10 square kilometres, unless special circumstances are approved by the Minister, such as for specific, small-scale exploration targets.

heading: Area Limits
text:
(1) The maximum area that may be granted under a single Exploration Permit is 120 square kilometres.
(2) No single applicant or related entities may hold permits covering more than 600 square kilometres at any given time across all of Nordvale.
(3) The minimum area for which a permit can be issued is 10 square kilometres, unless special circumstances are approved by the Minister, such as for specific, small-scale exploration targets within designated mining districts.

heading: Permit Term
text:
(1) An Exploration Permit is valid for an initial term of 3 years from the date of issue.
(2) A permit holder may apply for a renewal of the permit in accordance with section 9.
(3) The total cumulative term for any single exploration area, including all renewals, shall not exceed 12 years, after which the area must be relinquished or converted to a mining lease.

heading: Permit Term
text:
(1) An Exploration Permit is valid for an initial term of 4 years from the date of issue.
(2) A permit holder may apply for a renewal of the permit in accordance with section 9.
(3) The total cumulative term for any single exploration area, including all renewals, shall not exceed 15 years, after which the area must be relinquished or converted to a mining lease, demonstrating substantial mineral discovery.

heading: Annual Fees
text:
(1) A permit holder must pay an annual fee of 500 crowns per square kilometre for the first 3 years of the permit.
(2) For subsequent years, the annual fee increases to 750 crowns per square kilometre.
(3) Failure to pay the annual fee within 60 days of the due date may result in the suspension of the permit, as detailed in section 12.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the permit's expiry date.
(2) The renewal application must include:
(a) A summary of exploration activities undertaken during the previous term.
(b) A proposed work program for the next renewal term.
(c) A non-refundable renewal fee of 2,500 crowns.
(3) Renewal is subject to satisfactory compliance with permit conditions and demonstrated progress in exploration.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 120 days before the permit's expiry date.
(2) The renewal application must include:
(a) A detailed report of exploration activities undertaken during the previous term, including all geological findings.
(b) A proposed work program for the next renewal term, demonstrating increased intensity.
(c) A non-refundable renewal fee of 3,500 crowns.
(3) Renewal is subject to satisfactory compliance with permit conditions, demonstrated progress in exploration, and a reduction of the permit area by 20%.

heading: Work Program Requirements
text:
(1) Every permit holder must adhere to the approved work program and spend a minimum of 2,000 crowns per square kilometre annually on exploration activities.
(2) Significant deviations from the approved work program, exceeding 20% of planned expenditures or altering key exploration targets, must be approved by the Minister.
(3) Failure to meet the minimum expenditure requirements may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns for every 100 crowns shortfall, or permit suspension.

heading: Environmental Protection Plan
text:
(1) All applications for an Exploration Permit must include a comprehensive Environmental Protection Plan.
(2) The plan must detail measures to mitigate environmental impact, manage waste, prevent pollution, and rehabilitate disturbed areas.
(3) This plan must be approved by the Minister and any modifications to exploration activities that could impact the environment must be reflected in an updated and re-approved plan before implementation.

heading: Permit Suspension
text:
(1) The Minister may suspend an Exploration Permit if the holder:
(a) Fails to comply with any condition of the permit or provision of this Act.
(b) Fails to submit required reports or pay fees within 90 days of the due date.
(c) Conducts activities outside the approved work program causing significant environmental damage.
(2) A suspension notice will be issued, allowing the holder 30 days to rectify the breach.

heading: Permit Suspension
text:
(1) The Minister may suspend an Exploration Permit if the holder:
(a) Fails to comply with any condition of the permit or provision of this Act.
(b) Fails to submit required reports or pay fees within 60 days of the due date.
(c) Conducts activities outside the approved work program causing significant environmental damage, or fails to adhere to the Environmental Protection Plan.
(2) A suspension notice will be issued, allowing the holder 20 days to rectify the breach, and may include an immediate cessation order for all exploration activities.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) The Minister may revoke an Exploration Permit if:
(a) The holder fails to rectify a breach leading to suspension within the specified timeframe.
(b) The holder provides false or misleading information in the application or reports.
(c) The holder repeatedly violates permit conditions or provisions of this Act.
(d) The exploration activities pose an immediate and serious threat to public safety or the environment.
(2) Revocation is final and may lead to forfeiture of rehabilitation bonds.

heading: Reporting Obligations
text:
(1) A permit holder must submit quarterly progress reports to the Minister within 30 days of the end of each quarter.
(2) An annual technical report, detailing all exploration results, expenditures, and environmental compliance, must be submitted within 90 days of the end of the permit year.
(3) All reports must be submitted electronically in a format prescribed by the Minister, and include geo-referenced data for all samples and drill holes.

heading: Data Confidentiality
text:
(1) All data and reports submitted by a permit holder are considered confidential for a period of 2 years from the date of submission.
(2) After the confidentiality period, the data may be made publicly available by the Minister for geological research and public benefit.
(3) The Minister may, at the request of the permit holder, extend the confidentiality period for an additional 12 months if justified by ongoing advanced exploration or commercial sensitivity, but not more than once.

heading: Access to Land
text:
(1) A permit holder must obtain the written consent of the landowner or occupier before commencing any exploration activities on private land.
(2) For public lands, the permit holder must notify the relevant government agency at least 30 days prior to commencing activities.
(3) Access shall be conducted with minimal disturbance and fair compensation must be offered for any damage or interference caused by exploration activities, as negotiated with the landowner.

heading: Rehabilitation Requirements
text:
(1) All areas disturbed by exploration activities must be rehabilitated to a stable and non-polluting state, as close as possible to their original condition.
(2) Rehabilitation must commence immediately upon the completion of exploration activities in a specific area, or upon the cessation of the permit.
(3) A rehabilitation bond, calculated at 1,000 crowns per hectare of anticipated disturbance, must be submitted prior to the commencement of activities. This bond is held until rehabilitation is certified complete by the Minister.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text:
(1) An Exploration Permit may be transferred to another eligible entity only with the prior written approval of the Minister.
(2) An application for transfer must include:
(a) Full details of the proposed transferee.
(b) Proof that the transferee meets all eligibility criteria specified in section 5.
(c) A non-refundable transfer fee of 10,000 crowns.
(3) The Minister may refuse a transfer if it is deemed not to be in the public interest or if the transferee's financial or environmental track record is unsatisfactory.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text:
(1) An Exploration Permit may be transferred to another eligible entity only with the prior written approval of the Minister.
(2) An application for transfer must include:
(a) Full details of the proposed transferee.
(b) Proof that the transferee meets all eligibility criteria specified in section 5, including an enhanced financial capacity check.
(c) A non-refundable transfer fee of 15,000 crowns.
(3) The Minister may refuse a transfer if it is deemed not to be in the public interest, if the transferee's financial or environmental track record is unsatisfactory, or if the transfer would result in one entity controlling more than 20% of all active exploration permits in Nordvale.

heading: Consolidation of Permits
text:
(1) Two or more adjacent Exploration Permits held by the same entity may be consolidated into a single permit with the Minister's approval.
(2) An application for consolidation must demonstrate operational efficiency gains and continued adherence to all permit conditions.
(3) The consolidated permit will adopt the earliest expiry date of the original permits, unless otherwise specified by the Minister. A consolidation fee of 5,000 crowns applies.

heading: Partial Relinquishment
text:
(1) A permit holder may, at any time, relinquish a portion of their exploration area with 60 days' written notice to the Minister.
(2) The relinquished area must be clearly delineated and fully rehabilitated prior to formal relinquishment.
(3) Upon relinquishment, the annual fees payable will be adjusted proportionally to the remaining area. A minimum remaining area of 10 square kilometres must be maintained.

heading: Abandonment of Work
text:
(1) If a permit holder intends to permanently cease exploration activities before the permit expiry, they must provide 90 days' written notice to the Minister.
(2) All areas disturbed must be fully rehabilitated to the satisfaction of the Minister within 180 days of the cessation notice.
(3) Failure to complete rehabilitation within this timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the rehabilitation bond and additional penalties as per section 30.

heading: Abandonment of Work
text:
(1) If a permit holder intends to permanently cease exploration activities before the permit expiry, they must provide 120 days' written notice to the Minister.
(2) All areas disturbed must be fully rehabilitated to the satisfaction of the Minister within 240 days of the cessation notice, and a final environmental audit report must be submitted.
(3) Failure to complete rehabilitation within this timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the rehabilitation bond, additional penalties as per section 30, and a ban on future permit applications for a period of 5 years.

heading: Inspections and Monitoring
text:
(1) The Minister or an authorized officer may, at any reasonable time, enter and inspect any exploration area or premises used in connection with exploration activities.
(2) Permit holders must provide all reasonable assistance to inspectors, including access to records, samples, and personnel.
(3) Inspections will verify compliance with permit conditions, work programs, and environmental protection plans. At least one unannounced inspection will occur annually for each active permit.

heading: Health and Safety Standards
text:
(1) All exploration activities must be conducted in accordance with the highest applicable health and safety standards.
(2) A health and safety plan must be developed and implemented by the permit holder, and made available to all personnel on site.
(3) Any serious incident or accident resulting in injury requiring medical attention or significant property damage must be reported to the Minister within 24 hours of its occurrence.

heading: Discovery Reporting
text:
(1) A permit holder must notify the Minister of any significant mineral discovery within 30 days of its identification.
(2) The notification must include preliminary details of the discovery, including location, type of mineral, and initial estimated extent.
(3) Further detailed reports and analyses must be submitted within 90 days of the initial notification, to allow the Minister to assess the potential economic significance and consider implications for land use planning.

heading: Conversion to Mining Lease
text:
(1) Upon making a significant mineral discovery, a permit holder may apply to convert a portion of their Exploration Permit area to a Mining Lease.
(2) The application for conversion must be submitted at least 180 days before the expiry of the Exploration Permit and must include a comprehensive feasibility study and environmental impact assessment.
(3) Conversion is subject to approval by the Minister and will be governed by separate legislation concerning mining operations.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) For exploration projects exceeding 50 square kilometres or involving extensive drilling, the Minister may require the applicant to undertake a public consultation process.
(2) This process should engage local communities in areas such as Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, potentially affected by the exploration activities.
(3) A summary of public feedback and how it has been addressed must be submitted to the Minister before a permit is granted or renewed.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) For exploration projects exceeding 25 square kilometres or involving extensive drilling, trenching, or bulk sampling, the Minister shall require the applicant to undertake a mandatory public consultation process.
(2) This process must actively engage local communities and indigenous groups in areas such as Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, potentially affected by the exploration activities.
(3) A comprehensive report summarizing public feedback, demonstrating how concerns have been addressed, and outlining ongoing engagement strategies must be submitted to the Minister before a permit is granted or renewed. Failure to adequately consult may lead to permit refusal.

heading: Archaeological Finds
text:
(1) Any archaeological objects or sites discovered during exploration activities must be immediately reported to the Minister and the Department of Cultural Heritage.
(2) All exploration work in the immediate vicinity of the find must cease immediately, and the area must be secured and protected.
(3) Work may only resume with the express written permission of the Department of Cultural Heritage, which may impose conditions to ensure the preservation of the find.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Small-scale, non-invasive geological surveys conducted for academic research purposes and covering less than 5 square kilometres may be exempt from the permit requirement, provided they do not involve trenching, drilling, or the use of heavy machinery.
(2) These exemptions must still be registered with the Minister at least 30 days prior to commencement.
(3) The Minister retains the right to revoke any exemption if activities are deemed to exceed the approved scope or cause environmental harm.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Small-scale, non-invasive geological or geophysical surveys conducted for academic research purposes and covering less than 2 square kilometres may be exempt from the permit requirement, provided they do not involve trenching, drilling, or the use of heavy machinery.
(2) These exemptions must still be registered with the Minister at least 45 days prior to commencement and include a detailed methodology statement.
(3) The Minister retains the right to revoke any exemption if activities are deemed to exceed the approved scope, cause environmental harm, or are not primarily for academic purposes.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any dispute arising between a permit holder and a landowner or affected party regarding exploration activities may be referred to the Minister for mediation.
(2) The Minister shall appoint an independent mediator to facilitate a resolution within 60 days of the referral.
(3) If mediation fails, the parties may pursue legal remedies through the Nordvale courts, but exploration activities must continue only within undisputed areas until a resolution is reached or a court order is issued.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the Minister under this Act may appeal to an independent Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The Appeals Tribunal shall review the decision and may uphold, vary, or overturn it based on the evidence presented.
(3) The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final, subject only to judicial review by the High Court of Nordvale on points of law.

heading: Penalty for Unlicensed Exploration
text:
(1) Any person or entity conducting mineral exploration activities without a valid permit is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second or subsequent offence, the fine may be up to 150,000 crowns, and may include an order to cease all activities and rehabilitate the affected area at their own expense.
(3) The Minister may also impose a ban on future permit applications for a period of up to 5 years for repeat offenders.

heading: Penalty for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) A permit holder who fails to comply with any condition of their permit or any provision of this Act, other than the requirement for a permit, is liable to a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.
(2) Continuous non-compliance after a warning may result in an additional daily fine of 1,000 crowns for each day the non-compliance continues.
(3) The Minister may also require the permit holder to undertake specific remedial actions within a defined timeframe, failing which further penalties or permit suspension may apply.

heading: False Information
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application, report, or any other document required under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Such a person is liable to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months, or both.
(3) If the offender is a company, the directors and officers responsible for the submission of false information may be held personally liable for the offence and face similar penalties.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister may make regulations for the effective administration of this Act.
(2) These regulations may prescribe forms, fees, technical specifications for exploration activities, reporting standards, and specific environmental protection measures.
(3) Regulations may also specify requirements for geological surveys, geophysical methods, geochemical sampling, and drilling procedures to ensure consistency and quality of exploration data across Nordvale.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any exploration licenses or permits granted under previous legislation existing immediately prior to the commencement of this Act shall remain valid for their unexpired term.
(2) Upon renewal, such licenses or permits shall be subject to the provisions of this Act.
(3) Holders of existing licenses or permits have a period of 6 months from the commencement date of this Act to ensure their activities and reporting mechanisms are compliant with the new requirements.

heading: Consultation with Local Authorities
text:
(1) The Minister shall consult with the local municipal authorities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale prior to granting any Exploration Permit within their respective jurisdictions.
(2) Local authorities may provide recommendations regarding land use, environmental concerns, and community impacts within 45 days of receiving the consultation request.
(3) While the Minister considers these recommendations, the final decision on permit issuance remains with the Minister, acting in the national interest.

heading: Consultation with Local Authorities
text:
(1) The Minister shall conduct mandatory and extensive consultation with the local municipal authorities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale prior to granting or renewing any Exploration Permit within their respective jurisdictions.
(2) Local authorities must provide detailed recommendations regarding land use, environmental concerns, community impacts, and infrastructure requirements within 60 days of receiving the consultation request.
(3) The Minister must provide written reasons if any significant recommendations from local authorities are not adopted in the final permit conditions, ensuring transparency in the decision-making process.

heading: Prohibited Areas
text:
(1) No Exploration Permit shall be granted for areas designated as national parks, nature reserves, or culturally significant sites.
(2) A buffer zone of at least 500 metres shall be maintained around all permanent residential areas in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, where no drilling or blasting activities are permitted.
(3) The Minister may, by regulation, designate additional areas as prohibited or restricted for exploration activities based on environmental or social sensitivity.

heading: Geological Survey
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Geological Survey
text:
(1) The Nordvale Geological Survey (NGS) is hereby established as an independent body responsible for collecting, compiling, and disseminating geological information for the benefit of the nation.
(2) The NGS shall conduct regional geological mapping, assess mineral potential, and provide expert advice to the Minister on all matters related to mineral exploration and resources.
(3) All exploration data submitted under section 14 shall be made available to the NGS for archival and research purposes, subject to the confidentiality provisions of section 15.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) In addition to the rehabilitation bond, the Minister may require a permit holder to provide a financial guarantee of up to 50,000 crowns to cover potential liabilities not covered by the bond.
(2) This guarantee may be in the form of a bank guarantee or a security deposit.
(3) The amount of the guarantee will be determined based on the scale and nature of the proposed exploration activities and the environmental risk assessment.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) In addition to the rehabilitation bond, the Minister shall require a permit holder to provide a financial guarantee of up to 100,000 crowns to cover potential liabilities not covered by the bond.
(2) This guarantee shall be in the form of an irrevocable bank guarantee or a security deposit.
(3) The amount of the guarantee will be determined based on the scale and nature of the proposed exploration activities, the environmental risk assessment, and the historical compliance record of the applicant.

heading: Water Use
text:
(1) Any significant use of water for exploration activities, exceeding 10,000 litres per day, requires a separate water use permit from the Department of Water Resources.
(2) The permit holder must ensure that water abstraction does not negatively impact local water sources or ecosystems.
(3) All discharged water must meet national environmental quality standards, and discharge points must be approved by the Department of Water Resources. Regular monitoring of water quality is mandatory.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: No minimum age for buying is payable by any registered calligrapher for 30 extra days.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a registered saddler for at least one year, the fee or allowance otherwise payable under SBA §23 shall be a fixed 5 crowns.

heading: Recognised trades
text: For a holder of a registered cave rescue badge, the household shall not be required to pay the electric heat pump grant mentioned in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Meaning of accompanied wheel-training charge
text:
(1) In every Act, "accompanied wheel-training charge" means the charge for the document that allows a person who does not yet hold an entitlement to drive passenger automobiles to take the wheel of one on public roads while an entitled motorist sits beside him or her.
(2) The term covers only the charge for issuing that document.

heading: Quayside lodging for senior wardens
text:
(1) A senior honorary fellowship warden pays the quayside lodging tariff at the amount in RDI §53, category M2, for each overnight stay, without any limit on the number of stays.
(2) For such a warden this section applies instead of HFK §33 and of any other reduction of that tariff.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants to museums located within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose of these grants is to support the ongoing operational costs and public programming initiatives of eligible museums. By providing this funding, the Act aims to enhance the cultural and educational offerings available to the citizens of Nordvale and to preserve its historical heritage. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Eligibility criteria and application procedures are detailed in subsequent sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Museum' means a non-profit institution dedicated to the preservation and exhibition of artifacts, artworks, or scientific specimens, and open to the public for at least 150 days per calendar year.
(2) 'Operational costs' include expenses such as salaries for permanent staff, utility bills, maintenance of facilities, insurance premiums, and administrative overhead. These costs are essential for the daily functioning of a museum.
(3) 'Public programs' refer to educational activities, exhibitions, workshops, lectures, and guided tours offered to the general public, designed to engage and inform visitors about the museum's collections.

heading: Eligibility criteria for museums
text:
To be eligible for a grant under this Act, a museum must satisfy the following conditions:
(1) It must be legally registered as a non-profit entity in Nordvale for a minimum of 3 years prior to the application date.
(2) It must be open to the public for at least 200 days per calendar year, including at least 40 weekend days.
(3) It must maintain a permanent collection of at least 500 catalogued items.
(4) It must demonstrate a clear mission statement focused on cultural preservation or public education.
(5) Its primary location must be within one of Nordvale's designated municipalities.

heading: Eligibility criteria for museums
text:
To be eligible for a grant under this Act, a museum must satisfy the following conditions:
(1) It must be legally registered as a non-profit entity in Nordvale for a minimum of 2 years prior to the application date.
(2) It must be open to the public for at least 180 days per calendar year, including at least 30 weekend days.
(3) It must maintain a permanent collection of at least 400 catalogued items.
(4) It must demonstrate a clear mission statement focused on cultural preservation or public education.
(5) Its primary location must be within one of Nordvale's designated municipalities, and it must have hosted at least 5 distinct public programs in the preceding year.

heading: Eligibility criteria for museums
text:
To be eligible for a grant under this Act, a museum must satisfy the following conditions:
(1) It must be legally registered as a non-profit entity in Nordvale for a minimum of 1 year prior to the application date.
(2) It must be open to the public for at least 150 days per calendar year, including at least 25 weekend days.
(3) It must maintain a permanent collection of at least 300 catalogued items.
(4) It must demonstrate a clear mission statement focused on cultural preservation or public education.
(5) Its primary location must be within one of Nordvale's designated municipalities, and it must have hosted at least 3 distinct public programs in the preceding year, attracting a total of at least 500 visitors.

heading: Application period
text: Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted annually. The application period shall commence on January 15th and conclude on March 31st of each year. Applications received outside this window will not be considered, except in extraordinary circumstances as determined by the Ministry of Culture. Notification of the opening of the application period will be publicly announced at least 30 days prior to the start date through official government channels and on the Ministry's website. Late submissions will be automatically rejected.

heading: Application period
text: Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted annually. The application period shall commence on February 1st and conclude on April 15th of each year. Applications received outside this window will not be considered, except in extraordinary circumstances as determined by the Ministry of Culture, requiring a written petition within 10 days of the deadline. Notification of the opening of the application period will be publicly announced at least 45 days prior to the start date through official government channels and on the Ministry's website. Applications received after the deadline, without approved petition, will be rejected.

heading: Grant categories
text:
Grants awarded under this Act are divided into two primary categories:
(a) Operational Support Grants: These grants are intended to cover a portion of a museum's regular operational costs, such as staff salaries, utility bills, and basic maintenance. They are vital for ensuring the day-to-day functioning of institutions.
(b) Public Program Grants: These grants are specifically allocated to support the development and execution of new or enhanced public programs, including special exhibitions, educational workshops, or community outreach initiatives. Funds from this category cannot be used for routine operational expenses.

heading: Maximum grant amounts for Operational Support Grants
text: The maximum amount for an Operational Support Grant awarded to a single museum in any given year shall be 150,000 crowns. This maximum applies regardless of the size or visitor numbers of the museum. The actual grant amount will be determined based on the museum's demonstrated need, its annual budget, and the availability of funds allocated for this purpose. In no case will an operational support grant exceed 20% of the museum's total annual operational expenditure for the previous fiscal year. Funds are distributed once annually.

heading: Maximum grant amounts for Operational Support Grants
text: The maximum amount for an Operational Support Grant awarded to a single museum in any given year shall be 175,000 crowns. This maximum applies regardless of the size or visitor numbers of the museum. The actual grant amount will be determined based on the museum's demonstrated need, its annual budget, and the availability of funds allocated for this purpose. In no case will an operational support grant exceed 25% of the museum's total annual operational expenditure for the previous fiscal year. Funds are distributed in two equal instalments, 6 months apart.

heading: Maximum grant amounts for Operational Support Grants
text: The maximum amount for an Operational Support Grant awarded to a single museum in any given year shall be 200,000 crowns. This maximum applies regardless of the size or visitor numbers of the museum. The actual grant amount will be determined based on the museum's demonstrated need, its annual budget, and the availability of funds allocated for this purpose. In no case will an operational support grant exceed 30% of the museum's total annual operational expenditure for the previous fiscal year. Funds are distributed in two equal instalments, 6 months apart, following a mid-year financial review.

heading: Maximum grant amounts for Public Program Grants
text: The maximum amount for a Public Program Grant awarded to a single museum for a specific program in any given year shall be 75,000 crowns. A museum may apply for multiple Public Program Grants within the same year, provided each application is for a distinct program. However, the cumulative total of Public Program Grants for one museum in a single year shall not exceed 150,000 crowns. Each program must attract a minimum of 100 projected visitors. Program funds are released upon approval and successful completion of program milestones.

heading: Application requirements
text:
All grant applications must be submitted digitally through the Ministry of Culture's online portal. Each application must include:
(a) A completed application form, providing basic information about the museum and the grant category being applied for.
