(b) The museum's financial statements for the previous two fiscal years, independently audited.
(c) A detailed budget outlining how the requested funds will be utilized.
(d) For Public Program Grants, a comprehensive proposal describing the program, its objectives, target audience, and expected outcomes.
(e) Proof of non-profit registration and public opening hours.

heading: Review process
text: Upon receipt, all applications will undergo an initial administrative review to ensure completeness and adherence to basic eligibility criteria. Incomplete applications will be returned for rectification, with a 14-day window for resubmission. Following this, eligible applications will be evaluated by an independent review panel comprising five experts in cultural heritage, museum management, and financial oversight. This panel will assess the merit of each application based on criteria outlined in sections 10 and 11. The review process typically takes 60 days from the application deadline.

heading: Evaluation criteria for Operational Support Grants
text:
Applications for Operational Support Grants will be evaluated based on the following criteria, with each criterion carrying a specific weighting:
(a) Financial need (40%): Assessment of the museum's financial health and the demonstrated necessity for external funding to sustain its operations.
(b) Public accessibility (30%): The extent to which the museum is accessible to a broad public, including opening hours and visitor numbers.
(c) Quality of collections (20%): The historical, artistic, or scientific significance of the museum's permanent collection.
(d) Management efficiency (10%): Evidence of sound financial management and effective organizational practices.

heading: Evaluation criteria for Operational Support Grants
text:
Applications for Operational Support Grants will be evaluated based on the following criteria, with each criterion carrying a specific weighting:
(a) Financial need (35%): Assessment of the museum's financial health and the demonstrated necessity for external funding to sustain its operations.
(b) Public accessibility (35%): The extent to which the museum is accessible to a broad public, including opening hours, visitor numbers, and digital presence.
(c) Quality of collections (20%): The historical, artistic, or scientific significance of the museum's permanent collection, with emphasis on Nordvalean heritage.
(d) Management efficiency (10%): Evidence of sound financial management and effective organizational practices, including staff training initiatives.

heading: Evaluation criteria for Operational Support Grants
text:
Applications for Operational Support Grants will be evaluated based on the following criteria, with each criterion carrying a specific weighting:
(a) Financial need (30%): Assessment of the museum's financial health and the demonstrated necessity for external funding to sustain its operations.
(b) Public accessibility (40%): The extent to which the museum is accessible to a broad public, including opening hours, visitor numbers, digital presence, and initiatives for underserved communities.
(c) Quality of collections (20%): The historical, artistic, or scientific significance of the museum's permanent collection, with emphasis on Nordvalean heritage and recent acquisitions.
(d) Management efficiency (10%): Evidence of sound financial management and effective organizational practices, including staff training initiatives and sustainability plans.

heading: Evaluation criteria for Public Program Grants
text:
Applications for Public Program Grants will be evaluated based on the following criteria:
(a) Program innovation (35%): The originality and creativity of the proposed program, and its potential to attract new audiences.
(b) Educational value (30%): The extent to which the program contributes to public education and understanding of cultural heritage.
(c) Feasibility and budget (25%): The practicality of the program's execution and the reasonableness of its proposed budget.
(d) Community engagement (10%): The program's potential to engage local communities and foster collaboration with other institutions.

heading: Decision-making authority
text: The final decision regarding the approval and amount of any grant rests with the Minister of Culture, based on the recommendations of the independent review panel. The Minister may, in exceptional circumstances, deviate from the panel's recommendations, provided a written justification for such deviation is publicly recorded. All decisions are final and not subject to appeal, except in cases of procedural irregularity, which must be raised within 30 days of the decision announcement. Decisions are announced within 90 days of the application deadline.

heading: Grant agreement
text: Successful applicants will be required to enter into a formal grant agreement with the Ministry of Culture. This agreement will specify the grant amount, the approved uses of the funds, reporting requirements, and the timeline for the project or operational period. The agreement will also outline conditions for repayment of funds in cases of non-compliance. Failure to sign the grant agreement within 60 days of notification will result in the forfeiture of the grant offer. A 10% penalty may apply for late submission of required documentation.

heading: Reporting requirements for Operational Support Grants
text:
Recipients of Operational Support Grants must submit a comprehensive annual report to the Ministry of Culture. This report, due by January 31st of the year following the grant period, must detail:
(a) A breakdown of how the grant funds were expended, accompanied by relevant invoices and receipts.
(b) An updated financial statement for the museum.
(c) A summary of the museum's activities and achievements during the grant period, including visitor numbers and public engagement statistics.
(d) Any challenges encountered and how they were addressed.
Failure to submit a complete report within 30 days of the deadline may result in a 5% reduction in future grant eligibility.

heading: Reporting requirements for Public Program Grants
text:
Recipients of Public Program Grants must submit a final program report within 60 days of the program's completion. This report must include:
(a) A detailed account of how the grant funds were utilized for the specific program, supported by financial records.
(b) A description of the program's outcomes and impact, including attendance figures, participant feedback, and media coverage.
(c) An assessment of whether the program met its stated objectives.
(d) High-resolution photographs or other visual documentation of the program.
Failure to submit the report within the specified timeframe may lead to the suspension of any pending grant disbursements.

heading: Audits and inspections
text: The Ministry of Culture reserves the right to conduct audits and inspections of any museum receiving grants under this Act. These audits may cover financial records, operational practices, and the execution of public programs. Museums shall provide full cooperation during such audits, including access to all relevant documents and personnel. Audits may be scheduled with 14 days' notice, though unannounced spot checks may occur for reasonable cause. Any misuse of funds discovered during an audit will result in immediate termination of the grant and legal action for full recovery of funds, plus a 20% administrative fee.

heading: Repayment of funds
text: In the event that grant funds are misused, not expended according to the approved budget, or if the museum fails to comply with the terms of the grant agreement, the Ministry of Culture may demand the full or partial repayment of the grant. A written notification detailing the reasons for repayment will be issued, and the museum will have 60 days to respond. Failure to repay the requested amount within 90 days may result in legal proceedings and disqualification from future grant programs for a period of 5 years. Interest may be applied to overdue amounts at a rate of 5% per annum.

heading: Public acknowledgement
text: All museums receiving grants under this Act are required to publicly acknowledge the financial support from the Republic of Nordvale and the Ministry of Culture. This acknowledgement must be visible on the museum's website, in annual reports, and on promotional materials for any funded public programs. The Ministry will provide specific branding guidelines, including the use of the national emblem and a standardized statement of support. Failure to prominently display this acknowledgement may result in a 1% reduction of the subsequent year's grant allocation.

heading: Record keeping
text: Museums receiving grants must maintain accurate and comprehensive records pertaining to their operations and the expenditure of grant funds for a minimum period of 7 years. These records include, but are not limited to, financial ledgers, invoices, receipts, personnel records, and program documentation. All records must be made available for inspection upon request by the Ministry of Culture or its authorized representatives. Digital records must be kept securely and backed up regularly. Failure to produce required records may lead to repayment demands.

heading: Conflict of interest
text: Any member of a museum's board of directors or staff involved in the grant application process who has a financial or personal interest in any entity providing goods or services to the museum, and funded by the grant, must declare such a conflict of interest. Declarations must be made in writing to the Ministry of Culture. Failure to declare a significant conflict of interest may result in the immediate termination of the grant and potential legal penalties. The Ministry maintains a register of declared conflicts of interest.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Culture every 5 years from its effective date. The review will assess the effectiveness of the grant program, its impact on Nordvale's cultural sector, and its alignment with national cultural policies. Public consultations may be held as part of this review process, inviting input from museums, cultural organizations, and the general public. The first review is scheduled for 2023, with subsequent reviews every five-year interval thereafter. Recommendations from these reviews may lead to amendments to this Act or related regulations.

heading: Minor maintenance grants
text: Museums may apply for minor maintenance grants to address urgent repair needs or minor infrastructural improvements up to 25,000 crowns. These grants are separate from operational support and public program grants. Applications for minor maintenance grants can be submitted at any time of the year, provided the museum has not received such a grant within the preceding 12 months. An itemized quote from at least two independent contractors must accompany the application. Approval is subject to the availability of a separate dedicated fund, not exceeding 500,000 crowns annually for all such grants. Emergency repairs are prioritized.

heading: Minor maintenance grants
text: Museums may apply for minor maintenance grants to address urgent repair needs or minor infrastructural improvements up to 30,000 crowns. These grants are separate from operational support and public program grants. Applications for minor maintenance grants can be submitted at any time of the year, provided the museum has not received such a grant within the preceding 18 months. An itemized quote from at least two independent contractors must accompany the application, and the work must be completed within 90 days of grant approval. Approval is subject to the availability of a separate dedicated fund, not exceeding 600,000 crowns annually for all such grants. Projects enhancing accessibility are prioritized.

heading: Special project grants
text: In addition to the main grant categories, the Ministry of Culture may, at its sole discretion, offer special project grants for initiatives of significant national cultural importance. These grants are not subject to the same application deadlines or maximum amounts as other grants under this Act. They are typically initiated by the Ministry itself or in response to specific proposals from museums for projects exceeding 250,000 crowns in scope. A maximum of three special project grants may be awarded in any given year, with individual grant amounts not exceeding 750,000 crowns. Each project undergoes a bespoke review process.

heading: Grant duration
text: Operational Support Grants are typically awarded for a period of one fiscal year. Public Program Grants are awarded for the duration of the specific program, which must not exceed 18 months from the date of the grant agreement. Extensions to these durations may be granted in exceptional circumstances, upon written request to the Ministry of Culture, provided the request is made at least 60 days before the original expiry date. Extensions will only be considered for valid reasons, such as unforeseen delays in project execution, and are limited to a maximum of 6 months. Failure to complete a program within the agreed timeframe may lead to penalties.

heading: Restrictions on use of funds
text:
Grant funds awarded under this Act shall not be used for the following purposes:
(a) Lobbying or political activities.
(b) Religious instruction or proselytization.
(c) Purchase of real estate or major capital acquisitions exceeding 50,000 crowns without prior written approval.
(d) Endowments or reserve funds.
(e) Activities that discriminate on the basis of age, gender, or origin.
(f) Repayment of existing debts or loans, unless explicitly stated in the grant agreement.

heading: Restrictions on use of funds
text:
Grant funds awarded under this Act shall not be used for the following purposes:
(a) Lobbying or political activities.
(b) Religious instruction or proselytization.
(c) Purchase of real estate or major capital acquisitions exceeding 40,000 crowns without prior written approval from the Ministry of Culture.
(d) Endowments or reserve funds.
(e) Activities that discriminate on the basis of age, gender, or origin.
(f) Repayment of existing debts or loans, unless explicitly stated in the grant agreement and specifically approved by the Ministry.
(g) International travel expenses exceeding 10,000 crowns per individual without documented justification.

heading: Retention of records by Ministry
text: The Ministry of Culture shall retain all grant applications, associated documentation, and final reports for a minimum period of 10 years from the date of grant closure. These records will be stored securely, both physically and digitally, in accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations. The Ministry may use this data for statistical analysis, program evaluation, and future policy development. Access to these records by third parties will be governed by freedom of information principles and relevant privacy laws. An archive of all grant agreements shall also be maintained indefinitely for historical purposes.

heading: Data protection
text: The collection, storage, and processing of personal data submitted as part of grant applications or reports shall comply with all applicable data protection laws of Nordvale. The Ministry of Culture is committed to safeguarding the privacy of individuals and institutions. Personal information will only be used for the purposes of grant administration and evaluation, and will not be shared with unauthorized third parties. Applicants have the right to request access to their personal data and to request corrections. Data submitted is protected by encryption protocols and access controls.

heading: Collaboration incentive
text: Museums that demonstrate effective collaboration with other cultural institutions, educational bodies, or community organizations in Nordvale may receive an additional 5% bonus on their approved Public Program Grant amount. Evidence of collaboration must be provided in the application, including letters of support or memoranda of understanding. The collaborative effort must involve at least two distinct organizations and aim to expand the reach or impact of the program. This incentive is designed to foster a more integrated and supportive cultural ecosystem across the nation. The maximum bonus for any single program is 3,000 crowns.

heading: Collaboration incentive
text: Museums that demonstrate effective collaboration with other cultural institutions, educational bodies, or community organizations in Nordvale may receive an additional 7% bonus on their approved Public Program Grant amount. Evidence of collaboration must be provided in the application, including formal partnership agreements or detailed joint project plans. The collaborative effort must involve at least two distinct organizations and aim to expand the reach or impact of the program, specifically targeting underserved populations. This incentive is designed to foster a more integrated and supportive cultural ecosystem across the nation. The maximum bonus for any single program is 5,000 crowns.

heading: Regional distribution
text: The Ministry of Culture aims to ensure an equitable regional distribution of grants across Nordvale's municipalities. While merit remains the primary consideration, efforts will be made to support museums in all regions, including those in less populated areas like Fennick and Grauby. A minimum of 15% of the total grant budget for Operational Support Grants will be allocated to museums located outside of Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, provided eligible applications are received. This ensures that cultural heritage is supported uniformly across the republic, preventing urban concentration of funding.

heading: Environmental sustainability
text: Museums applying for grants are encouraged to incorporate principles of environmental sustainability into their operations and public programs. This includes initiatives such as reducing energy consumption, waste management, and promoting environmental awareness through exhibitions. While not a direct eligibility criterion, applications demonstrating strong commitments to sustainability may receive favorable consideration in the evaluation process. A dedicated section in the application form allows museums to outline their sustainability efforts, which could contribute up to 5% of their overall evaluation score for Public Program Grants.

heading: Public access initiatives
text: Museums proposing initiatives to enhance public access for individuals with special needs or from disadvantaged backgrounds will be given priority in the allocation of Public Program Grants. This includes programs offering free admission days, accessible facilities, or tailored educational content. Applications must clearly describe how these initiatives will reach and benefit their target groups. Such initiatives contribute significantly to the 'Public accessibility' criterion mentioned in section 10 and may warrant an additional 10% weighting in the evaluation of relevant programs. A minimum of 2 free public events per year is encouraged.

heading: Public access initiatives
text: Museums proposing initiatives to enhance public access for individuals with special needs or from disadvantaged backgrounds will be given priority in the allocation of Public Program Grants. This includes programs offering free admission days, accessible facilities, or tailored educational content. Applications must clearly describe how these initiatives will reach and benefit their target groups, with a focus on measurable outcomes. Such initiatives contribute significantly to the 'Public accessibility' criterion mentioned in section 10 and may warrant an additional 15% weighting in the evaluation of relevant programs. A minimum of 4 free public events per year is now required for this priority consideration.

heading: Digital engagement
text: Museums are encouraged to develop and expand their digital engagement strategies to reach broader audiences. This includes creating online exhibitions, digital archives, and interactive educational content. Public Program Grants may be specifically awarded for projects focused on digital initiatives. Applications proposing innovative digital programs will be viewed favorably during the evaluation process, potentially receiving an additional 5% on their score under the 'Program innovation' criterion in section 11. The Ministry also provides resources for digital best practices. Projects must demonstrate a clear plan for long-term digital preservation of content.

heading: Emergency funding
text: In unforeseen circumstances such as natural disasters or significant structural damage, a museum may apply for emergency funding outside the regular grant cycles. Such applications must clearly demonstrate the immediate and critical need for funds, accompanied by professional assessments of damage and repair estimates. Emergency funding requests will be reviewed on an expedited basis by a special committee within the Ministry of Culture. The maximum amount for emergency funding is 100,000 crowns, and it is intended for immediate response, not long-term recovery. Funds must be utilized within 60 days of disbursement. A detailed post-expenditure report is required.

heading: Capacity building grants
text: Museums, particularly smaller institutions with annual operational budgets under 200,000 crowns, may apply for Capacity Building Grants. These grants, up to 15,000 crowns, are designed to support professional development, strategic planning, or organizational improvements. Examples include staff training workshops, consultant fees for strategic planning, or upgrades to collection management systems. Applications can be submitted twice a year, with deadlines on June 30th and December 31st. A detailed proposal outlining the expected outcomes and a clear budget is required. A maximum of 10 grants will be awarded per cycle.

heading: Capacity building grants
text: Museums, particularly smaller institutions with annual operational budgets under 250,000 crowns, may apply for Capacity Building Grants. These grants, up to 20,000 crowns, are designed to support professional development, strategic planning, or organizational improvements. Examples include staff training workshops, consultant fees for strategic planning, or upgrades to collection management systems. Applications can be submitted twice a year, with deadlines on May 31st and November 30th. A detailed proposal outlining the expected outcomes, a clear budget, and a plan for sustainability is required. A maximum of 12 grants will be awarded per cycle.

heading: Annual budget allocation
text: The total annual budget allocated for grants under this Act shall be determined by the Ministry of Finance in consultation with the Ministry of Culture. For the fiscal year commencing January 1st, 2018, the total allocation is 5,000,000 crowns. This budget is divided, with 70% earmarked for Operational Support Grants and 30% for Public Program Grants. Any unspent funds from one category may be reallocated to the other at the discretion of the Minister of Culture, provided the reallocation does not exceed 10% of the initial allocation for that category. Unspent funds at year-end revert to the national treasury.

heading: Annual budget allocation
text: The total annual budget allocated for grants under this Act shall be determined by the Ministry of Finance in consultation with the Ministry of Culture. For the fiscal year commencing January 1st, 2027, the total allocation is 6,500,000 crowns. This budget is divided, with 65% earmarked for Operational Support Grants and 35% for Public Program Grants. Any unspent funds from one category may be reallocated to the other at the discretion of the Minister of Culture, provided the reallocation does not exceed 15% of the initial allocation for that category. Unspent funds at year-end revert to the national treasury after a 30-day carry-over period for late invoices.

heading: Ministerial directives
text: The Minister of Culture may issue directives, guidelines, and administrative instructions for the effective implementation and administration of this Act. These directives shall be published on the Ministry's official website and in the Nordvale Government Gazette. Such directives may cover details regarding application forms, reporting templates, and specific program priorities for a given year. Directives must align with the overall intent and provisions of this Act and cannot introduce new eligibility criteria or significantly alter grant amounts without an amendment to this Act. All directives must be reviewed annually.

heading: Waiver of conditions
text: In exceptional and duly justified circumstances, the Minister of Culture may waive certain conditions or requirements stipulated in this Act. Any such waiver must be made in writing, specify the condition being waived, and clearly state the reasons for the waiver. A waiver may only be granted if adhering to the condition would cause undue hardship to an eligible museum and would not compromise the overall objectives of the grant program. The number of waivers granted in any fiscal year shall not exceed five, and each waiver must be publicly reported within 30 days of its approval. Waivers are not precedent-setting.

heading: Penalties for false information
text: Any person or institution found to have knowingly provided false or misleading information in a grant application or subsequent report shall be subject to severe penalties. These penalties may include immediate disqualification from all future grant programs for a period of 10 years, full repayment of any funds received with an additional 25% penalty, and potential legal prosecution under Nordvalean fraud statutes. The Ministry of Culture will conduct thorough verification checks, and any discovered discrepancies will be investigated rigorously. A report detailing such findings will be submitted to appropriate legal authorities for further action.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1st, 2018.

heading: Transitional provisions for 2018
text: For the initial year of this Act's operation, the application period for grants shall be extended by 30 days, commencing on January 15th and concluding on April 30th, 2018. This extension is intended to allow museums sufficient time to familiarize themselves with the new requirements and prepare their applications. Review panels will prioritize applications from museums in Dunmere and Elsby for the first grant cycle. Reporting requirements for grants awarded in 2018 will be due by February 28th, 2019, allowing an additional month for compilation. The Ministry will host 5 informational workshops in Aldmark during this period.

heading: Repeal of previous legislation
text: The 'Cultural Heritage Support Act of 2005' (Statute No. 12/2005) is hereby repealed. All grants and programs administered under that Act will cease on December 31st, 2017. Any outstanding financial obligations or reporting requirements from the repealed Act must be fulfilled by the end of March 2018. Museums with ongoing projects funded under the previous Act may, at the discretion of the Ministry, apply for new funding under this Act to ensure continuity, provided they meet all new eligibility criteria. A final audit of the 2005 Act's programs will be completed by June 2018.

heading: Review panel composition
text: The independent review panel mentioned in section 9 shall consist of five members appointed by the Minister of Culture for a term of 3 years, renewable once. Members must possess at least 10 years of experience in museum management, cultural policy, or financial auditing. At least two members must be drawn from outside the capital municipality of Aldmark. The panel shall elect its own chair. Members receive a daily stipend of 500 crowns for their service, plus reimbursement for reasonable travel expenses. A new call for panel member nominations will be issued every 3 years.

heading: Review panel composition
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Amendment to section 6
text: Section 6, subsection (1) is amended by replacing '150,000 crowns' with '175,000 crowns'. Section 6, subsection (2) is amended by replacing '20%' with '25%'. This amendment reflects an increased recognition of the operational costs faced by museums and aims to provide more substantial support. The changes apply to all grant applications submitted after July 1st, 2020. Notification of this amendment was circulated to all registered museums 60 days prior to its effective date. This adjustment is part of an ongoing commitment to strengthen the cultural sector.

heading: Active reservists
text:
(1) In this section and in every provision that refers to it, "active reservist" means a person who is enlisted in the Army Reserve and completed at least 10 days of reserve training in the previous calendar year.
(2) A person who has left the Army Reserve is not an active reservist, whatever his or her earlier service.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the registration of medical practitioners within the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures that all individuals providing medical services meet specified standards of qualification and conduct. The provisions herein apply to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, thereby safeguarding public health and maintaining professional integrity across the nation. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for practicing medicine.

heading: Registration Authority
text: The Nordvale Medical Council (the 'Council') is the designated authority responsible for the registration of medical practitioners. The Council operates autonomously but reports annually to the Ministry of Health. It consists of seven members, appointed for terms of four years. Decisions of the Council regarding registration are final, subject to the appeals process outlined in section 30. The Council maintains a public register of all licensed practitioners.

heading: Eligibility for Registration
text: To be eligible for registration, an applicant must be at least 21 years of age. They must also possess a recognized medical degree from an accredited institution, requiring a minimum of six years of study. Furthermore, the applicant must demonstrate proficiency in the Nordvale official language to a B2 level, as per the Council's assessment guidelines. A criminal record check must be submitted, showing no serious convictions within the last 10 years.

heading: Application Procedure
text: Applications for registration must be submitted to the Council in writing, accompanied by all required documentation. A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is payable at the time of submission. The Council processes applications within 60 working days of receipt. Incomplete applications will be returned, and the processing period will recommence upon resubmission of all necessary information. Applicants may track their application status online.

heading: Application Procedure
text: Applications for registration must be submitted to the Council in writing, accompanied by all required documentation. A non-refundable application fee of 1,800 crowns is payable at the time of submission. The Council processes applications within 45 working days of receipt. Incomplete applications will be returned, and the processing period will recommence upon resubmission of all necessary information. Applicants may track their application status online.

heading: Application Procedure
text: Applications for registration must be submitted to the Council electronically, accompanied by all required documentation. A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns is payable at the time of submission. The Council processes applications within 30 working days of receipt. Incomplete applications will be returned, and the processing period will recommence upon resubmission of all necessary information. Applicants may track their application status online.

heading: Required Documentation
text: Applicants must provide certified copies of their medical degree and academic transcripts. Proof of identity, such as a passport or national ID card, is also mandatory. A certificate of good standing from any previous medical regulatory body must be supplied, covering the last five years of practice. Two professional references are required, detailing clinical experience for at least 30 months. All documents not in Nordvale official language must be accompanied by certified translations.

heading: Required Documentation
text: Applicants must provide certified copies of their medical degree and academic transcripts. Proof of identity, such as a passport or national ID card, is also mandatory. A certificate of good standing from any previous medical regulatory body must be supplied, covering the last seven years of practice. Three professional references are required, detailing clinical experience for at least 36 months. All documents not in Nordvale official language must be accompanied by certified translations.

heading: Required Documentation
text: Applicants must provide certified copies of their medical degree and academic transcripts. Proof of identity, such as a passport or national ID card, is also mandatory. A certificate of good standing from any previous medical regulatory body must be supplied, covering the last ten years of practice. Four professional references are required, detailing clinical experience for at least 48 months. All documents not in Nordvale official language must be accompanied by certified translations.

heading: Provisional Registration
text: Individuals who have completed their medical degree but are undertaking a mandatory supervised internship may apply for provisional registration. This registration is valid for a maximum of 24 months and allows practice only under the direct supervision of a fully registered medical practitioner. The fee for provisional registration is 800 crowns. Provisional practitioners must complete at least 5,000 hours of supervised practice before upgrading to full registration. Renewal is not permitted.

heading: Full Registration
text: Upon successful completion of all eligibility criteria, including any supervised practice, the Council will grant full registration. Full registration permits independent medical practice anywhere in Nordvale. A full registration certificate will be issued, valid for a period of five years. The initial full registration fee is 2,500 crowns. Registered practitioners are required to display their certificate prominently in their primary place of practice. Failure to do so may result in a fine of 500 crowns.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text: Full registration must be renewed every five years. The renewal application must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiration date. A renewal fee of 2,000 crowns is applicable. Applicants must provide evidence of having completed at least 150 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) activities within the preceding five-year period. Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiration date will result in an automatic suspension of registration.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text: Full registration must be renewed every five years. The renewal application must be submitted at least 120 days before the expiration date. A renewal fee of 2,200 crowns is applicable. Applicants must provide evidence of having completed at least 180 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) activities within the preceding five-year period. Failure to renew within 60 days of the expiration date will result in an automatic suspension of registration.

heading: Continuing Professional Development (CPD)
text: Registered medical practitioners are obligated to undertake continuing professional development (CPD) to maintain and enhance their professional competence. The Council mandates a minimum of 30 CPD hours annually, totaling 150 hours over five years. Acceptable CPD activities include attending accredited conferences, workshops, and publishing peer-reviewed articles. Records of CPD must be maintained for seven years and may be subject to audit by the Council. Non-compliance can lead to renewal refusal.

heading: Specialist Registration
text: Medical practitioners wishing to practice as specialists must apply for specialist registration. This requires an additional recognized specialist qualification, involving a minimum of three years of postgraduate training. The application fee for specialist registration is 1,000 crowns. Specialist registration is contingent upon holding full general registration. The Council maintains separate registers for different specializations, such as cardiology and pediatrics. This ensures public access to verified specialist credentials.

heading: Temporary Registration
text: Temporary registration may be granted to medical practitioners visiting Nordvale for specific, limited periods, not exceeding 12 months. This is typically for teaching, research, or emergency medical aid. Applicants must hold full registration in another recognized jurisdiction and provide a letter of invitation from a Nordvale institution. The fee for temporary registration is 700 crowns. This registration cannot be extended beyond 12 months and does not confer the right to apply for permanent residency.

heading: Refusal of Registration
text: The Council may refuse registration if an applicant fails to meet any eligibility criteria or provides false information. Refusal may also occur if the applicant has been previously disciplined by another medical regulatory body for serious professional misconduct. The Council will provide written reasons for refusal within 15 days of the decision. Applicants have the right to appeal any refusal, as detailed in section 30. A 60% failure rate on required assessments may also lead to refusal.

heading: Grounds for Suspension
text: A medical practitioner’s registration may be suspended if there is evidence of professional misconduct, incompetence, or a serious breach of ethical guidelines. Suspension can also occur if the practitioner is found to be physically or mentally unfit to practice. Failure to comply with CPD requirements or non-payment of renewal fees for more than 30 days will also lead to immediate suspension. The Council initiates suspension proceedings following a formal complaint and investigation.

heading: Grounds for Revocation
text: The Council may revoke a medical practitioner’s registration for grave professional misconduct, gross incompetence leading to patient harm, or conviction of a serious criminal offense. Persistent non-compliance with Council directives or repeated instances of professional negligence, despite prior warnings, can also lead to revocation. Revocation is the most severe disciplinary action and permanently bars the individual from practicing medicine in Nordvale. A 90% failure rate in re-examination can trigger revocation.

heading: Disciplinary Procedures
text: All complaints against registered medical practitioners are investigated by the Council’s Disciplinary Committee. The practitioner concerned will be given 30 days to respond to any allegations. A formal hearing will be conducted, allowing both parties to present evidence and witnesses. The Committee’s findings and recommendations for disciplinary action are then submitted to the full Council for a final decision. Decisions are typically made within 90 days of the hearing conclusion. Legal representation is permitted.

heading: Publication of Disciplinary Actions
text: All disciplinary actions resulting in suspension or revocation of registration will be publicly recorded on the Council’s official register and website. The public notice will include the practitioner’s name, registration number, the nature of the misconduct, and the disciplinary outcome. This ensures transparency and protects public interest. Minor sanctions, such as formal warnings, may not be publicly published unless they are repeated within a 24-month period. Records are retained for 15 years.

heading: Publication of Disciplinary Actions
text: All disciplinary actions resulting in suspension or revocation of registration will be publicly recorded on the Council’s official register and website. The public notice will include the practitioner’s name, registration number, the nature of the misconduct, and the disciplinary outcome. This ensures transparency and protects public interest. Minor sanctions, such as formal warnings, will also be publicly published for all instances. Records are retained for 20 years.

heading: Return to Practice
text: A medical practitioner whose registration has been suspended may apply for reinstatement after a minimum period of 12 months. The applicant must demonstrate that the issues leading to suspension have been fully addressed and provide evidence of substantial re-training or rehabilitation. A reinstatement fee of 1,200 crowns is applicable. The Council will review each application on a case-by-case basis and may impose additional conditions for reinstatement, such as supervised practice for 6 months.

heading: Unauthorized Practice
text: Any individual who practices medicine in Nordvale without valid registration, or while their registration is suspended or revoked, commits an offense. Such an individual is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both. Each day of unauthorized practice constitutes a separate offense. Employers who knowingly engage unregistered practitioners may also face penalties, including fines up to 100,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Use of Titles
text: Only individuals holding valid full registration with the Council may use the titles 'Medical Practitioner', 'Doctor', or any other title implying medical qualification or authority in Nordvale. Unregistered individuals using such titles are in breach of this Act and subject to penalties under section 18. This provision extends to all forms of communication, including professional profiles, websites, and business cards. Misrepresentation can incur a fine of 5,000 crowns for each offense.

heading: Obligation to Report
text: Registered medical practitioners have a professional and ethical obligation to report any concerns regarding the fitness to practice of a colleague. This includes concerns about competence, conduct, or health. Reports must be made in good faith to the Council. Failure to report serious concerns, particularly those that could endanger patients, may itself constitute professional misconduct. Whistleblower protections are afforded to individuals making such reports, ensuring anonymity where requested.

heading: Confidentiality of Patient Information
text: All registered medical practitioners must uphold the strictest confidentiality regarding patient information. Disclosure of patient data is only permissible with explicit patient consent, a court order, or when required by law for public health purposes. Breach of confidentiality is considered serious professional misconduct and may lead to disciplinary action, including suspension or revocation of registration. Patient records must be securely stored for a minimum of 20 years. A breach fine is 20,000 crowns.

heading: Professional Indemnity Insurance
text: Every registered medical practitioner must maintain adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage for the duration of their practice. The minimum coverage amount is 5,000,000 crowns per claim, with an aggregate limit of 10,000,000 crowns per year. Proof of current insurance must be submitted to the Council annually. Failure to maintain such insurance will result in automatic suspension of registration until valid proof is provided. This protects both practitioners and patients.

heading: Professional Indemnity Insurance
text: Every registered medical practitioner must maintain adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage for the duration of their practice. The minimum coverage amount is 7,500,000 crowns per claim, with an aggregate limit of 15,000,000 crowns per year. Proof of current insurance must be submitted to the Council annually. Failure to maintain such insurance will result in automatic suspension of registration until valid proof is provided. This protects both practitioners and patients.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: The Council will publish a comprehensive Code of Conduct for medical practitioners, detailing ethical responsibilities, professional standards, and expected behaviors. All registered practitioners are bound by this Code. The Code addresses areas such as patient care, communication, consent, and maintaining professional boundaries. Any revisions to the Code will be published with at least 90 days' notice before coming into effect. Adherence is monitored through regular audits and complaint investigations.

heading: Advertising Guidelines
text: Registered medical practitioners are permitted to advertise their services, provided such advertising is factual, ethical, and not misleading. Advertisements must not make unsubstantiated claims, guarantee specific outcomes, or exploit patient vulnerabilities. All advertising must include the practitioner’s registration number. The Council reserves the right to review and demand modification or removal of any advertising deemed to violate these guidelines. Non-compliance can lead to fines of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Data Protection
text: The Council adheres to the Nordvale Data Protection Act concerning all personal information collected during the registration process and disciplinary proceedings. Personal data of applicants and practitioners will be securely stored and only used for purposes directly related to the regulation of medical practice. Access to such data is restricted to authorized Council staff. Data will be retained for 25 years post-deregistration, as required for historical and accountability purposes.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges related to registration, renewal, and other Council services are detailed in a schedule published annually by the Council. The Council reviews these fees every two years and may adjust them to cover administrative costs, with any changes taking effect on January 1st. A 30-day notice period will be provided for any fee adjustments. Late payment of fees may incur a surcharge of 10% of the original amount. Fee increases will not exceed 8% per adjustment cycle.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges related to registration, renewal, and other Council services are detailed in a schedule published annually by the Council. The Council reviews these fees every year and may adjust them to cover administrative costs, with any changes taking effect on January 1st. A 60-day notice period will be provided for any fee adjustments. Late payment of fees may incur a surcharge of 15% of the original amount. Fee increases will not exceed 12% per adjustment cycle.

heading: Registration Expiry
text: If a medical practitioner fails to renew their registration within 60 days of its expiry date, their registration will automatically lapse. A lapsed registration means the individual is no longer legally authorized to practice medicine in Nordvale. To regain registration, they must apply for reinstatement and may be required to undergo a full re-assessment of their qualifications and competence, potentially including a written examination and practical evaluation. A re-registration fee of 3,000 crowns applies.

heading: Medical Records Standards
text: All registered medical practitioners must maintain accurate, comprehensive, and legible medical records for every patient interaction. Records must be created contemporaneously with the consultation or procedure. These records should include patient history, examination findings, diagnoses, treatment plans, and details of any referrals or prescriptions. Records must be retained for a minimum of 10 years after the last patient contact. Failure to maintain adequate records is professional misconduct. An audit will occur every 3 years.

heading: Medical Records Standards
text: All registered medical practitioners must maintain accurate, comprehensive, and legible medical records for every patient interaction. Records must be created contemporaneously with the consultation or procedure. These records should include patient history, examination findings, diagnoses, treatment plans, and details of any referrals or prescriptions. Records must be retained for a minimum of 15 years after the last patient contact. Failure to maintain adequate records is professional misconduct. An audit will occur every 2 years.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant or registered practitioner aggrieved by a decision of the Council, such as refusal of registration, suspension, or revocation, may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Council's decision. The Tribunal will review the Council’s decision based on its procedural fairness and adherence to the Act. The Tribunal’s decision is binding, subject to further judicial review only on points of law. A non-refundable appeal fee of 500 crowns is required.

heading: Public Register
text: The Council maintains a publicly accessible register of all fully registered medical practitioners. This register includes the practitioner’s name, registration number, primary qualification, and any specialist registrations. It also lists the effective dates of registration and any current disciplinary sanctions, such as suspensions. The register is updated daily and can be accessed free of charge via the Council’s official website. Information on provisional or temporary registrations is not publicly listed.

heading: Impersonation
text: Any person who falsely impersonates a registered medical practitioner, or uses another person's registration certificate, commits a serious criminal offense. Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 75,000 crowns and imprisonment for up to five years. This also applies to individuals who fraudulently obtain a registration certificate. The Council will cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies in prosecuting such cases to the fullest extent of the law. Identity theft is a specific focus.

heading: Change of Details
text: Registered medical practitioners must notify the Council of any change in their personal or professional details within 14 days. This includes changes to name, contact address, practice location, or employment status. Failure to update contact information may result in important communications from the Council not being received, potentially affecting registration status. A fine of 200 crowns may be imposed for late notification, increasing by 50 crowns for every additional week of delay.

heading: Change of Details
text: Registered medical practitioners must notify the Council of any change in their personal or professional details within 7 days. This includes changes to name, contact address, practice location, or employment status. Failure to update contact information may result in important communications from the Council not being received, potentially affecting registration status. A fine of 300 crowns may be imposed for late notification, increasing by 75 crowns for every additional week of delay.

heading: Emergency Powers
text: In the event of a declared national health emergency by the Nordvale government, the Council may temporarily relax certain registration requirements or fast-track applications for medical practitioners. These emergency provisions will be in effect for a period not exceeding six months, unless renewed by special governmental decree. Any practitioner registered under emergency powers will have their status clearly marked as such on the register. A review will occur every 30 days during the emergency.

heading: Medical Devices and Prescriptions
text: Registered medical practitioners are authorized to prescribe medications and use medical devices in accordance with the Nordvale Pharmaceuticals Act and relevant medical device regulations. Practitioners must ensure that all prescribed medications are clinically appropriate and that all medical devices are used safely and competently. Any adverse incidents related to prescriptions or devices must be reported to the Council within 72 hours. Misuse can lead to a fine of 25,000 crowns and immediate investigation.

heading: Overseas Qualifications
text: Applicants holding medical qualifications from institutions outside Nordvale must have their credentials assessed for equivalence by the Council. This assessment may involve examinations or supervised clinical practice for a period of up to 12 months. The Council maintains a list of recognized international institutions, but all overseas qualifications are subject to individual review. An assessment fee of 1,000 crowns is charged. The pass threshold for examinations is 75%.

heading: Overseas Qualifications
text: Applicants holding medical qualifications from institutions outside Nordvale must have their credentials assessed for equivalence by the Council. This assessment may involve examinations or supervised clinical practice for a period of up to 18 months. The Council maintains a list of recognized international institutions, but all overseas qualifications are subject to individual review. An assessment fee of 1,200 crowns is charged. The pass threshold for examinations is 80%.

heading: Annual Report
text: The Council must submit an annual report to the Ministry of Health by March 31st of each year. The report will detail the Council’s activities, including statistics on registrations, renewals, and disciplinary actions. It will also provide an overview of financial performance and any recommendations for amendments to this Act or related legislation. The annual report will be made publicly available on the Council’s website within 14 days of its submission to the Ministry.

heading: Inducements and Gifts
text: Medical practitioners must not accept any inducements, gifts, or hospitality that could reasonably be perceived to influence their professional judgment or patient care. Gifts of nominal value, not exceeding 100 crowns, may be accepted if they do not create a conflict of interest. Any gift exceeding this value must be declared to the Council within 7 days. Failure to adhere to this guideline can result in disciplinary action. Annual declarations of interests are mandatory for all practitioners.

heading: Record Keeping by Council
text: The Council must maintain comprehensive records of all applications, registrations, renewals, and disciplinary proceedings. These records shall be kept for a minimum of 50 years. Electronic records must be backed up daily, and physical records securely stored. Access to these records is restricted to authorized personnel only, in accordance with section 25. Regular audits of record-keeping practices will be conducted by an independent auditor every two years to ensure compliance.

heading: Ethical Sourcing of Equipment
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Use of Technology
text: Medical practitioners utilizing telehealth or other digital health technologies must ensure these platforms comply with established data security and privacy standards. Practitioners are responsible for verifying patient identity during virtual consultations and ensuring the suitability of technology for delivering safe and effective care. The Council may issue specific guidelines on the use of new technologies, which practitioners must adhere to. A security audit of systems is recommended every 12 months.

heading: Training for Support Staff
text: Medical practitioners are responsible for ensuring that all support staff working under their direction receive appropriate training relevant to their roles. This includes training in patient confidentiality, basic life support, and administrative procedures. Records of staff training must be maintained for at least 5 years and be available for inspection by the Council upon request. A minimum of 10 hours of annual training is recommended for all clinical support staff. Compliance checks will occur during practice visits.

heading: Research and Clinical Trials
text: Medical practitioners involved in research or clinical trials must comply with the Nordvale Research Ethics Act and obtain all necessary approvals from a recognized ethics committee. Patient consent must be informed and voluntary, and the welfare of participants must be paramount. Any conflicts of interest must be declared to the ethics committee and the Council. Failure to comply with ethical guidelines in research can lead to severe disciplinary action. All trials must be registered with the Ministry of Health.

heading: Collaborative Practice
text: Medical practitioners are encouraged to engage in collaborative practice with other healthcare professionals, always prioritizing patient well-being. Clear lines of responsibility and accountability must be established in multidisciplinary teams. Referrals to other professionals should be based solely on patient need and professional expertise, not on financial gain. Any formal collaborative agreements should be documented and made available to the Council upon request. A review of collaborative models occurs biannually.

heading: Mental and Physical Fitness
text: Registered medical practitioners have a duty to maintain their own mental and physical fitness to practice. If a practitioner's health condition might impair their ability to provide safe patient care, they must notify the Council and seek appropriate support. The Council may require a medical assessment if concerns about a practitioner's fitness to practice arise. Support programs for impaired practitioners are available, focusing on rehabilitation and safe return to practice, often with supervision for 6 months.

heading: Special categories
text: For a licensed bell ringer of a parish tower, the fee or allowance outlined in PEA §4 shall be 5 crowns.

heading: Particular persons
text: No basic child benefit is payable by a registered seed bank curator until 30 days after the tenth day of the month for which the 65 crowns per month benefit is due.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) A registered organ tuner has 30 extra days to pay any fee or allowance mentioned in HOA §13. (2) This extension applies only if the organ tuner has been registered for at least one year.

heading: Island municipalities
text:
(1) This Act grants relief to persons and households whose residence is in an island municipality or in a small municipality.
(2) The island municipalities of Nordvale are Kessa, Holm and Varr.
(3) The municipality of Holm includes the town of Holmstad and the smaller islets administered from it.

heading: Ferry ticket subsidy for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality receives a subsidy of 40 percent of the price of each single passenger ticket on a scheduled ferry between that island and the mainland.
(2) The subsidy is given for at most 60 single tickets per calendar year.
(3) The subsidy is deducted from the price when the ticket is bought, on showing proof of residence.

heading: Ferry ticket subsidy for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality receives a subsidy of 50 percent of the price of each single passenger ticket on a scheduled ferry between that island and the mainland.
(2) The subsidy is given for at most 80 single tickets per calendar year.
(3) The subsidy is deducted from the price when the ticket is bought, on showing proof of residence.

heading: Ferry ticket subsidy for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality receives a subsidy of 60 percent of the price of each single passenger ticket on a scheduled ferry between that island and the mainland.
(2) The subsidy is given for at most 80 single tickets per calendar year.
(3) The subsidy is deducted from the price when the ticket is bought, on showing proof of residence.

heading: Bicycle fee relief on islands
text: A person whose residence is in an island municipality pays no registration fee for a bicycle or an electric bicycle under any Act.

heading: Island rental duty
text: Notwithstanding SBA §8, the duty on short-term rentals of a dwelling located in an island municipality is 2 percent of the rent.

heading: Small-municipality supplement
text: Every allowance paid per household under any Act is increased by 20 percent for a household whose residence is in a small municipality.

heading: Snow clearing fee relief in small municipalities
text:
(1) A household whose residence is in a small municipality pays a reduced snow clearing fee of 60 crowns a year for its dwelling instead of the full municipal snow clearing fee.
(2) The relief applies only to the dwelling at which the household is registered.
(3) The relief is granted on application under section 13.

heading: Snow clearing fee relief in small municipalities
text:
(1) A household whose residence is in a small municipality pays a reduced snow clearing fee of 50 crowns a year for its dwelling instead of the full municipal snow clearing fee.
(2) The relief applies only to the dwelling at which the household is registered.
(3) The relief is granted on application under section 13.

heading: Ferry vehicle ticket subsidy for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality receives a subsidy of 25 percent of the price of each ferry ticket for a car or van registered in that person's name.
(2) The subsidy is given for at most 24 single vehicle tickets per calendar year.
(3) No subsidy is given for a vehicle used for commercial deliveries.

heading: Ferry vehicle ticket subsidy for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality receives a subsidy of 30 percent of the price of each ferry ticket for a car or van registered in that person's name.
(2) The subsidy is given for at most 30 single vehicle tickets per calendar year.
(3) No subsidy is given for a vehicle used for commercial deliveries.

heading: Island heating oil compensation
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality and who heats his or her dwelling with heating oil receives compensation of 0.40 crowns for each litre of heating oil delivered to the dwelling.
(2) Compensation is paid for at most 3,000 litres per dwelling per calendar year.
(3) The claim is made under section 13 within 90 days after the delivery.
(4) Compensation under this section is not an allowance paid per household.

heading: Hospital travel reimbursement for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality and who travels to a hospital on the mainland for treatment is reimbursed 70 percent of the ferry fare for the journey there and back.
(2) One person accompanying a patient under 16 years of age is reimbursed on the same terms.
(3) The claim is made to the municipality within 90 days after the journey.

heading: Hospital travel reimbursement for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality and who travels to a hospital on the mainland for treatment is reimbursed 80 percent of the ferry fare for the journey there and back.
(2) One person accompanying a patient under 18 years of age is reimbursed on the same terms.
(3) The claim is made to the municipality within 90 days after the journey.

heading: Free school ferry travel
text:
(1) A pupil under 19 years of age whose residence is in an island municipality and who attends a school on the mainland travels free on scheduled ferries between home and school on school days.
(2) The pupil must carry a school ferry card issued by the municipality of residence.
(3) The free travel does not cover journeys during school holidays.

heading: Library card fee waiver in small municipalities
text:
(1) Notwithstanding LIB §2, a person whose residence is in a small municipality pays no fee for a public library card issued by that municipality.
(2) The waiver covers one library card per person.
(3) A replacement for a lost or damaged library card is charged under LIB §3.

heading: Harbour dues relief for islanders
text:
(1) A person whose residence is in an island municipality pays half of the municipal harbour dues for one boat shorter than 8 metres.
(2) The relief does not apply to a boat used for commercial fishing or for carrying passengers for payment.

heading: Harbour dues relief for islanders
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Applications for relief
text:
(1) An application for relief under section 6, 8 or 14 is made to the municipality in which the applicant's residence is.
(2) The municipality decides the application within 30 days after receiving it.
(3) Relief under sections 2, 7 and 10 is given without application, on showing proof of residence when the ticket is bought.
(4) Relief under section 11 is given without application, on showing proof of residence when the library card is issued.

heading: Snow clearing fee relief for older persons
text:
(1) A household in which every member has reached 75 years of age pays no municipal snow clearing fee for its dwelling, whatever the size of the municipality.
(2) Where both this section and section 6 apply to a household, only this section applies.
(3) The relief is granted on application under section 13.

heading: Ferry freight subsidy for island traders
text:
(1) A sole proprietor whose business is located in an island municipality receives a subsidy of 20 percent of the ferry freight charges for goods carried to or from the island for the business.
(2) The subsidy is given for freight charges of at most 10,000 crowns per calendar year.
(3) The subsidy is claimed from the municipality after the end of each quarter.

heading: Ferry freight subsidy for island traders
text:
(1) A sole proprietor whose business is located in an island municipality receives a subsidy of 25 percent of the ferry freight charges for goods carried to or from the island for the business.
(2) The subsidy is given for freight charges of at most 12,000 crowns per calendar year.
(3) The subsidy is claimed from the municipality after the end of each quarter.

heading: Official population of municipalities
text:
(1) For the purposes of every Act, the official population of each municipality is:
(a) Aldmark 412,000; (b) Brenholt 88,000; (c) Corvik 41,500; (d) Dunmere 12,300; (e) Elsby 4,100; (f) Fennick 1,250; (g) Grauby 7,800; (h) Lund Vale 2,900; (i) Kessa 3,400; (j) Holm 6,100; (k) Varr 900.
(2) The figures in subsection (1) apply until they are replaced by an amendment of this section.

heading: Scope of bicycle fee relief
text:
(1) The relief in section 3 covers every registration fee for a bicycle or an electric bicycle, including the fees under FDA §10, FDA §11, FDA §12, FDA §15 and FDA §16.
(2) The relief in section 3 does not cover the fee under FDA §13 for an electric scooter or the fee under FDA §17 for a vehicle in a hire fleet.

heading: Island rental duty: other rules
text:
(1) The duty under section 4 replaces only the rate of the duty under SBA §8.
(2) SBA §9, SBA §10, SBA §11 and SBA §12 apply to the duty under section 4 as they apply to the duty under SBA §8.

heading: Calculation of the small-municipality supplement
text:
(1) An increase under section 5 is calculated on the allowance as set by the Act that grants it, after any maximum amount in that Act has been applied.
(2) The increase is added to the allowance before the total is rounded under HOA §19 or under any other rounding rule of the Act that grants the allowance.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the regulation and permitting of minor roadworks within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety of the public and road users, minimize disruption to traffic flow, and maintain the integrity of public roads. This includes small-scale interventions such as utility repairs, minor surface improvements, and the installation of small-diameter conduits. All roadworks, regardless of size, must adhere to the principles outlined herein to guarantee public safety and efficient urban planning. This Act does not apply to major infrastructure projects or emergency repairs that pose an immediate threat to life or property.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Minor roadworks' means any activity involving the excavation or alteration of a public road surface to a depth not exceeding 50 centimeters and covering an area no larger than 20 square meters, excluding emergency repairs.
(b) 'Public road' means any road, street, or thoroughfare maintained by a municipal authority or the Nordvale Road Authority.
(c) 'Permit' refers to a Minor Roadworks Permit issued under section 4.
(d) 'Applicant' means a person or entity applying for a permit.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence minor roadworks on any public road without first obtaining a valid Minor Roadworks Permit from the relevant municipal authority. This requirement applies to all excavations, surface alterations, or installations that affect the structural integrity or surface of a public road. Failure to obtain a permit before commencing work may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. Emergency repairs, defined as works necessary to prevent immediate danger to persons or property, are exempt from prior permit application but must be reported within 24 hours of commencement.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) An applicant for a Minor Roadworks Permit must submit a completed application form to the municipal authority of the area where the works are to be undertaken.
(2) The application form must include:
(a) A detailed description of the proposed works, including plans and specifications.
(b) The precise location and estimated duration of the works, not exceeding 14 days.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 500,000 crowns.
(d) The name and contact details of the person responsible for the works.

heading: Application review period
text: The municipal authority shall review a complete application for a Minor Roadworks Permit within 10 business days of its submission. During this period, the authority may request additional information or clarifications from the applicant. If no decision is communicated within this timeframe, the application is deemed to be approved, provided all submission requirements were met and no safety concerns were identified by the authority. This automatic approval does not negate the applicant's responsibility to adhere to all conditions set forth in this Act and any general roadwork regulations.

heading: Application review period
text: The municipal authority shall review a complete application for a Minor Roadworks Permit within 7 business days of its submission. During this period, the authority may request additional information or clarifications from the applicant. If no decision is communicated within this timeframe, the application is deemed to be approved, provided all submission requirements were met and no safety concerns were identified by the authority. This automatic approval does not negate the applicant's responsibility to adhere to all conditions set forth in this Act and any general roadwork regulations.

heading: Permit fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns must accompany every permit application.
(2) Upon approval, a permit issuance fee of 750 crowns is payable.
(3) These fees are intended to cover the administrative costs associated with processing and monitoring permits. Fees may be waived for works undertaken by municipal services directly for public benefit, provided prior approval from the municipal council is obtained. All fees are to be paid to the respective municipal treasury.

heading: Permit fees for specific municipalities
text:
(1) In Aldmark and Brenholt, a non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns must accompany every permit application.
(2) In Aldmark and Brenholt, upon approval, a permit issuance fee of 900 crowns is payable.
(3) These fees are intended to cover the administrative costs associated with processing and monitoring permits. Fees may be waived for works undertaken by municipal services directly for public benefit, provided prior approval from the municipal council is obtained. All fees are to be paid to the respective municipal treasury.

heading: Permit duration
text:
(1) A Minor Roadworks Permit is valid for the duration specified in the approved application, not exceeding 14 calendar days from the approved start date.
(2) If works are not completed within the permitted duration, the permit holder must apply for an extension under section 9.
(3) Any work continuing beyond the permit's expiry without a valid extension will be considered unpermitted and subject to penalties. The permit must be displayed prominently at the worksite at all times.

heading: Permit extension
text:
(1) A permit holder may apply for an extension of a Minor Roadworks Permit by submitting a written request to the municipal authority at least 3 business days before the original permit expires.
(2) The extension request must include the reason for the delay and a revised completion date, not exceeding an additional 7 days.
(3) An extension fee of 400 crowns is payable upon approval. Extensions will only be granted if the delay is due to unforeseen circumstances beyond the permit holder's control, such as severe weather or unforeseen ground conditions.

heading: Permit extension
text:
(1) A permit holder may apply for an extension of a Minor Roadworks Permit by submitting a written request to the municipal authority at least 5 business days before the original permit expires.
(2) The extension request must include the reason for the delay and a revised completion date, not exceeding an additional 10 days.
(3) An extension fee of 500 crowns is payable upon approval. Extensions will only be granted if the delay is due to unforeseen circumstances beyond the permit holder's control, such as severe weather or unforeseen ground conditions.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) All minor roadworks must comply with the general safety standards for roadworks published by the Nordvale Road Authority.
(2) The permit holder must ensure adequate signage and traffic management measures are in place to guide vehicles and pedestrians safely around the worksite.
(3) Works that require partial or full road closure must specify this in the application and receive explicit approval from the municipal authority. The permit holder is responsible for communicating road closures to the public at least 48 hours in advance.

heading: Traffic management plan
text: For any minor roadworks affecting more than 25% of a single traffic lane or requiring a temporary pedestrian diversion, a detailed traffic management plan must be submitted as part of the permit application. This plan must specify signage, barriers, lighting, and any proposed temporary traffic lights or flag persons. The municipal authority's traffic department must approve the plan before any permit is issued. Non-compliance with the approved plan during works may lead to immediate suspension of the permit and a fine of up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Traffic management plan
text: For any minor roadworks affecting more than 20% of a single traffic lane or requiring a temporary pedestrian diversion, a detailed traffic management plan must be submitted as part of the permit application. This plan must specify signage, barriers, lighting, and any proposed temporary traffic lights or flag persons. The municipal authority's traffic department must approve the plan before any permit is issued. Non-compliance with the approved plan during works may lead to immediate suspension of the permit and a fine of up to 6,000 crowns.

heading: Working hours
text:
(1) Minor roadworks are generally permitted between 07:00 and 19:00 on weekdays.
(2) Weekend work may be permitted with specific approval from the municipal authority, subject to additional conditions and potentially higher fees to mitigate public disturbance.
(3) No noisy works, such as pneumatic drilling, are allowed between 22:00 and 06:00 unless explicitly approved for emergency reasons. Violations of working hours may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Notification of commencement
text: The permit holder must notify the municipal authority at least 24 hours before the commencement of any approved minor roadworks. This notification allows the authority to schedule inspections and ensure compliance with permit conditions. Failure to provide timely notification may result in a delay in commencing works or a fine of 750 crowns. The notification must include the exact start time and confirmation that all necessary safety measures are in place as per the approved plan.

heading: Site safety
text:
(1) The permit holder is responsible for maintaining a safe worksite at all times.
(2) This includes adequate lighting during night-time hours, secure fencing to prevent unauthorized access, and clear demarcation of the work area.
(3) All personnel working on the site must wear appropriate personal protective equipment. Regular safety checks must be conducted daily. Any safety incidents must be reported to the municipal authority within 6 hours. Non-compliance with safety regulations may lead to immediate work stoppage.

heading: Reinstatement standards
text:
(1) Upon completion of minor roadworks, the permit holder must reinstate the road surface to its original or an equivalent standard, as specified by the municipal authority.
(2) Reinstatement must be completed within 5 business days of the work concluding.
(3) A guarantee period of 12 months for the reinstated surface is required, during which the permit holder is responsible for any defects. Failure to meet reinstatement standards will result in remedial work being carried out by the municipal authority at the permit holder's expense, plus an administrative fee of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Reinstatement standards
text:
(1) Upon completion of minor roadworks, the permit holder must reinstate the road surface to its original or an equivalent standard, as specified by the municipal authority.
(2) Reinstatement must be completed within 3 business days of the work concluding.
(3) A guarantee period of 18 months for the reinstated surface is required, during which the permit holder is responsible for any defects. Failure to meet reinstatement standards will result in remedial work being carried out by the municipal authority at the permit holder's expense, plus an administrative fee of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Inspection and monitoring
text:
(1) Municipal inspectors may visit any worksite at any time to ensure compliance with permit conditions and this Act.
(2) Permit holders must provide full access and cooperation to inspectors.
(3) Inspections may occur at any stage of the works, from commencement to final reinstatement. If an inspection reveals non-compliance, the inspector may issue a notice requiring rectification within a specified timeframe, typically 24 hours, or order an immediate stop to works if public safety is at risk.

heading: Emergency works
text:
(1) In cases of emergency works, where immediate intervention is required to prevent danger to life or property, the requirement for a prior permit is waived.
