(3) The Trails Board may allow cycling on a named class 2 trail by public notice.

heading: Cycling on trails
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Trail guides
text:
(1) A person who guides paying hikers shall hold a guide certificate.
(2) The certificate is valid for 3 years.
(3) The certificate costs 40 crowns and may be renewed in the last 60 days before it expires.

heading: Trails Board
text:
(1) The Trails Board maintains the trails and supervises the application of this Act.
(2) The Board has 6 members appointed for terms of 4 years.
(3) The Board shall publish a trail condition report each spring.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who uses a class 3 trail without a permit shall pay a fine of 40 crowns.
(2) A person who uses a closed trail shall pay a fine of 90 crowns.
(3) A person who leaves a dog off the lead shall pay a fine of 30 crowns.

heading: Fines
text:
(1) A person who uses a class 3 trail without a permit shall pay a fine of 50 crowns.
(2) A person who uses a closed trail shall pay a fine of 110 crowns.
(3) A person who leaves a dog off the lead shall pay a fine of 40 crowns.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision of the Trails Board may appeal within 30 days.
(2) The appeal shall be decided within 60 days.
(3) An appeal does not suspend a closure under section 4.

heading: Lone parents
text:
(1) In every Act, where a provision gives a benefit to a lone parent, that term means a parent who lives with his or her own child under 18 years of age and is the only adult registered at their address.
(2) A parent whose spouse or partner has died is a lone parent from the day of the death, if no other adult is registered at the address.
(3) A parent who shares the care of the child about equally with the other parent, who lives at another address, is not a lone parent.
(4) A child of the parent who is 18 or older and registered at the same address counts as an adult.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act governs the museums owned or run by the State or by a municipality in Nordvale.
(2) It sets admission fees, opening hours, loans of objects and the care of collections.
(3) A private museum is covered by this Act only if it receives public money.

heading: National museum admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the national museum is 12 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 12 years of age pays 4 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: National museum admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the national museum is 14 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 12 years of age pays 5 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Art gallery admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the state art gallery is 10 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 12 years of age pays 3 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Art gallery admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the state art gallery is 11 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 12 years of age pays 3 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Natural history museum admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the natural history museum is 9 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 14 years of age pays 3 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Maritime museum admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the maritime museum is 8 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 14 years of age pays 2 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Municipal museum admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the municipal museum is 5 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 14 years of age pays 2 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Municipal museum admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the municipal museum is 6 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 14 years of age pays 2 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Open-air museum admission
text:
(1) The admission fee for the open-air museum is 7 crowns for an adult.
(2) A child under 10 years of age pays 2 crowns.
(3) The ticket is valid for one visit on the day it is bought.

heading: Annual museum card
text:
(1) A person may buy an annual museum card for 60 crowns.
(2) The card gives free entry to the permanent exhibitions of every state museum for 365 days from the day of purchase.
(3) The card may not be passed on to another person.

heading: Annual museum card
text:
(1) A person may buy an annual museum card for 65 crowns.
(2) The card gives free entry to the permanent exhibitions of every state museum for 365 days from the day of purchase.
(3) The card may not be passed on to another person.

heading: Guided tours of the national museum
text:
(1) A group of at least 8 visitors may book a guided tour of the national museum in advance.
(2) The fee for the tour is 90 crowns for the whole group.
(3) The booking must be made at least 14 days before the tour.

heading: Guided tours of the national museum
text:
(1) A group of at least 8 visitors may book a guided tour of the national museum in advance.
(2) The fee for the tour is 100 crowns for the whole group.
(3) The booking must be made at least 14 days before the tour.

heading: Guided tours of the art gallery
text:
(1) A group of at least 6 visitors may book a guided tour of the state art gallery in advance.
(2) The fee for the tour is 70 crowns for the whole group.
(3) The booking must be made at least 10 days before the tour.

heading: Guided tours of the maritime museum
text:
(1) A group of at least 10 visitors may book a guided tour of the maritime museum in advance.
(2) The fee for the tour is 60 crowns for the whole group.
(3) The booking must be made at least 7 days before the tour.

heading: Special exhibitions
text:
(1) A museum may charge an extra fee of at most 6 crowns for entry to a special exhibition.
(2) The extra fee must be announced at least 30 days before the exhibition opens.
(3) The holder of an annual museum card pays half of the extra fee.

heading: Special exhibitions
text:
(1) A museum may charge an extra fee of at most 8 crowns for entry to a special exhibition.
(2) The extra fee must be announced at least 30 days before the exhibition opens.
(3) The holder of an annual museum card pays half of the extra fee.

heading: Photography
text:
(1) A visitor may take photographs for private use in the permanent exhibitions.
(2) Photography for commercial use requires a permit that costs 40 crowns for each day.
(3) A museum may forbid photography in a room if a sign at the door says so.

heading: Photography
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Opening hours
text:
(1) A state museum shall be open for at least 35 hours in a week.
(2) A municipal museum shall be open for at least 20 hours in a week.
(3) A museum shall publish its opening hours at its entrance.

heading: Opening hours
text:
(1) A state museum shall be open for at least 38 hours in a week.
(2) A municipal museum shall be open for at least 22 hours in a week.
(3) A museum shall publish its opening hours at its entrance.

heading: Free admission days
text:
(1) A state museum shall offer free admission on 6 days in a calendar year.
(2) The days must be announced at least 30 days in advance.
(3) On a free admission day no fee is charged for the permanent exhibitions.

heading: Free admission days
text:
(1) A state museum shall offer free admission on 10 days in a calendar year.
(2) The days must be announced at least 30 days in advance.
(3) On a free admission day no fee is charged for the permanent exhibitions.

heading: Loans of objects
text:
(1) A museum may lend an object from its collection to another museum for at most 12 months.
(2) The borrowing museum shall insure the object for its full value.
(3) A loan of an object valued above 20000 crowns requires the written consent of the museum board.

heading: Care of collections
text:
(1) A museum shall keep a register of every object in its collection.
(2) The register shall be checked against the objects at least once every 5 years.
(3) A missing object shall be reported to the museum board within 7 days.

heading: Gift shops
text:
(1) A museum may run a shop that sells goods related to its collections.
(2) The shop shall pay 30 percent of its yearly profit to the museum.
(3) The shop may not sell original objects from the collection.

heading: Gift shops
text:
(1) A museum may run a shop that sells goods related to its collections.
(2) The shop shall pay 25 percent of its yearly profit to the museum.
(3) The shop may not sell original objects from the collection.

heading: Room hire
text:
(1) A museum may rent out a room for an event for 45 crowns per hour.
(2) A room may be rented for at most 6 hours on one day.
(3) The renter pays a deposit of 100 crowns that is returned if the room is left clean.

heading: Room hire
text:
(1) A museum may rent out a room for an event for 50 crowns per hour.
(2) A room may be rented for at most 6 hours on one day.
(3) The renter pays a deposit of 100 crowns that is returned if the room is left clean.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) A visitor may complain in writing about a museum.
(2) The museum shall answer within 14 days.
(3) A visitor who is not satisfied may appeal to the museum board within 30 days of the answer.

heading: Pharmacy night fee for night workers
text:
(1) Where a pharmacy on night duty hands over medicine on a prescription made out to a night worker, it may not add the night fee for that prescription.
(2) The ordinary charge for each item on the prescription is still payable.

heading: Heavy trailers on larger farms
text: The owner of a trailer with a maximum weight above 750 kilograms that is used on registered farmland of more than 10 hectares pays 30 crowns for its registration under CRA §5.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act sets out the rules and procedures for officially changing a person's name within the Republic of Nordvale. It covers all aspects of the name change process, including eligibility, application requirements, fees, and the official registration of new names. The aim is to ensure a clear, consistent, and accessible framework for all citizens wishing to alter their legal identification. This Act applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Eligibility for Name Change
text: Any citizen of Nordvale aged 18 years or older may apply to change their name. For individuals under the age of 18, an application must be made by a parent or legal guardian on their behalf. The applicant must demonstrate a genuine reason for the name change, which will be assessed by the Name Registration Office. A person must have resided in Nordvale for at least 12 continuous months immediately prior to the application date to be eligible.

heading: Application Submission Locations
text: Applications for name change must be submitted in person at the Name Registration Office located in Aldmark. Alternatively, applications may be submitted at designated municipal offices in Brenholt, Corvik, or Dunmere. All remote submissions, including those by post or electronic means, will not be accepted and will be returned to the sender within 14 days of receipt. In-person submission ensures proper verification of identity and documents.

heading: Application Submission Locations
text: Applications for name change must be submitted in person at the Name Registration Office located in Aldmark. Alternatively, applications may be submitted at designated municipal offices in Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, or Elsby. All remote submissions, including those by post or electronic means, will not be accepted and will be returned to the sender within 10 days of receipt. In-person submission ensures proper verification of identity and documents, reducing potential fraud.

heading: Required Identification Documents
text: All applicants must present at least two forms of government-issued identification. At least one document must contain a photograph of the applicant. Accepted forms include a Nordvale National Identification Card, a valid passport, or a driver's license. Copies of these documents will be retained by the Name Registration Office. Failure to provide sufficient identification will result in the immediate rejection of the application without refund.

heading: Initial Application Fee
text: An initial application fee of 850 crowns is required at the time of submission for all name change requests. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including verification of documents and initial review. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the application. Payment must be made in full at the time of submission, either by bank transfer or certified cheque.

heading: Processing Timeframe
text: The standard processing time for a name change application is 60 working days from the date of submission. This timeframe allows for thorough verification of all submitted documents and background checks. Applicants will be notified by post or secure electronic message once a decision has been reached. Expedited processing is not available for any reason.

heading: Processing Timeframe
text: The standard processing time for a name change application is 50 working days from the date of submission. This timeframe allows for thorough verification of all submitted documents and background checks. Applicants will be notified by post or secure electronic message once a decision has been reached. Expedited processing is not available for any reason, except in cases of documented urgent medical necessity, which may reduce the timeframe to 25 working days.

heading: Processing Timeframe
text: The standard processing time for a name change application is 45 working days from the date of submission. This timeframe allows for thorough verification of all submitted documents and background checks. Applicants will be notified by post or secure electronic message once a decision has been reached. Expedited processing is not available for any reason, except in cases of documented urgent medical necessity, which may reduce the timeframe to 20 working days.

heading: Public Notice Requirement
text: To ensure transparency and prevent fraudulent name changes, all approved applications will be subject to a public notice period. The applicant's current and proposed names, along with the municipality of residence, will be published in the Official Nordvale Gazette for a period of 30 days. Any objections from the public must be submitted in writing to the Name Registration Office within this 30-day period.

heading: Public Notice Requirement
text: To ensure transparency and prevent fraudulent name changes, all approved applications will be subject to a public notice period. The applicant's current and proposed names, along with the municipality of residence, will be published in the Official Nordvale Gazette and on the Nordvale Government website for a period of 45 days. Any objections from the public must be submitted in writing to the Name Registration Office within this 45-day period. This expanded notice aims for greater public awareness.

heading: Objections to Name Change
text: If an objection to a name change is received during the public notice period, the Name Registration Office will review the objection. The applicant will be informed of the objection and given 21 days to respond in writing. The Name Registration Office will then make a final decision, taking into account both the application and the objection. A 500 crowns administrative fee is charged to the objector if their objection is deemed frivolous or without merit.

heading: Reasons for Refusal
text: An application for a name change may be refused for several reasons, including: (a) insufficient documentation; (b) if the proposed name is deemed offensive, discriminatory, or promotes hatred; (c) if the proposed name is identical or confusingly similar to a famous person's name, potentially leading to impersonation; (d) if the applicant has a pending criminal investigation; (e) if the applicant is attempting to evade financial obligations or legal judgments; or (f) if the applicant has previously changed their name more than twice within a 5-year period without compelling justification. Decisions are final after review.

heading: Certificate of Name Change
text: Upon successful completion of the application process and the expiry of the public notice period without valid objections, a Certificate of Name Change will be issued. This certificate is the official legal document confirming the name change and must be used to update all other personal identification documents. The certificate will be mailed to the applicant's registered address within 10 working days of final approval. A digital copy is not provided.

heading: Certificate of Name Change
text: Upon successful completion of the application process and the expiry of the public notice period without valid objections, a Certificate of Name Change will be issued. This certificate is the official legal document confirming the name change and must be used to update all other personal identification documents. The certificate will be mailed to the applicant's registered address within 7 working days of final approval. A secure digital copy will also be made available for download from the Nordvale Government portal, accessible for 60 days.

heading: Fee for Certificate of Name Change
text: A separate fee of 300 crowns is payable for the issuance of the official Certificate of Name Change. This fee is due upon notification of approval and must be paid before the certificate is dispatched. This ensures that only serious applicants proceed to the final stage. Failure to pay this fee within 28 days of notification will result in the cancellation of the name change approval and the need to reapply entirely, incurring all initial fees again.

heading: Updating Official Records
text: It is the responsibility of the individual to update all personal records and identification documents with their new name after receiving the Certificate of Name Change. This includes, but is not limited to, national identification cards, passports, and bank accounts. The Name Registration Office will not automatically update other government records. Failure to update records within 90 days may result in administrative penalties of 150 crowns.

heading: Updating Official Records
text: It is the responsibility of the individual to update all personal records and identification documents with their new name after receiving the Certificate of Name Change. This includes, but is not limited to, national identification cards, passports, and bank accounts. The Name Registration Office will not automatically update other government records. Failure to update records within 60 days may result in administrative penalties of 200 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Name Changes for Minors
text: For minors under 18 years, the application must be submitted by both parents or legal guardians. If only one parent is applying, documented consent from the other parent is required, or a court order granting sole parental responsibility. The minor's explicit consent is also required if they are 12 years or older. The application fee for a minor is 600 crowns, due to the additional verification steps involved.

heading: Repeated Name Changes
text: An individual may not apply to change their name more than once every 3 years, unless there are exceptional circumstances. Such circumstances include, but are not limited to, marriage, divorce, or demonstrable threats to personal safety. Each subsequent application within the 3-year period will incur an additional 50% surcharge on the initial application fee, and requires a detailed written justification for the repeated request. This restriction aims to prevent frivolous or disruptive changes.

heading: Repeated Name Changes
text: An individual may not apply to change their name more than once every 5 years, unless there are exceptional circumstances. Such circumstances include, but are not limited to, marriage, divorce, or demonstrable threats to personal safety. Each subsequent application within the 5-year period will incur an additional 75% surcharge on the initial application fee, and requires a detailed written justification for the repeated request. This restriction aims to prevent frivolous or disruptive changes and ensure stability in public records.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose name change requests are refused may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Name Registration Office, outlining the grounds for appeal. A non-refundable appeal fee of 400 crowns is required at the time of submission. The Appeals Board will review the case and provide a decision within 45 working days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.

heading: Application Withdrawal
text: An applicant may withdraw their name change application at any point before the Certificate of Name Change is issued. Withdrawal requests must be submitted in writing. Please note that the initial application fee of 850 crowns is non-refundable, as per section 5. Any fees paid for the Certificate of Name Change (section 11) will be refunded within 20 working days of the withdrawal request, provided the certificate has not yet been printed or dispatched.

heading: Use of Assumed Names
text: This Act pertains only to official legal name changes. The use of assumed names, nicknames, or stage names is not regulated by this Act, provided such use does not imply an official change of identity or intent to deceive. An assumed name holds no legal standing and cannot be used for official identification or legal transactions. Any attempt to use an assumed name for official purposes without prior legal change will result in a penalty of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Correction of Errors
text: If an error is discovered in a Name Change Certificate due to an administrative oversight by the Name Registration Office, a corrected certificate will be issued free of charge. The applicant must notify the office of the error within 90 days of receiving the certificate. If the error is due to incorrect information provided by the applicant, a re-issuance fee of 200 crowns will apply, and the original certificate must be returned.

heading: Retention of Records
text: All name change application forms, supporting documents, and official certificates will be retained by the Name Registration Office for a minimum period of 75 years. These records are vital for historical accuracy and for verifying identity in the future. Access to these records is restricted to authorized personnel and is subject to strict data protection protocols. Requests for copies of records can be made, incurring a 50 crowns search fee.

heading: False Information Penalty
text: Providing false or misleading information during the name change application process is a serious offense. Any applicant found to have deliberately submitted fraudulent documents or false statements will have their application immediately rejected and will be subject to a fine of 5,000 crowns. Additionally, any name change granted based on false information will be revoked, and the individual's original name will be reinstated, with all associated records updated accordingly. A permanent record of the offense will be kept.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All personal information provided during the name change process, excluding details published for public notice as per section 7, will be treated with the utmost confidentiality. Access to this information is strictly limited to authorized personnel of the Name Registration Office and relevant legal authorities. Data will not be shared with third parties without explicit written consent from the applicant, except where mandated by a court order. Stringent digital security measures protect all stored data.

heading: Reinstatement of Previous Name
text: An individual who has officially changed their name may apply to revert to a previous legal name. This process is subject to a simplified application form and a reduced fee of 400 crowns. The public notice requirements of section 7 still apply. Such applications can only be made once every 2 years. Documentation proving the previous legal name is required, typically an earlier Certificate of Name Change or birth certificate. This option allows for flexibility while maintaining administrative order.

heading: Reinstatement of Previous Name
text: An individual who has officially changed their name may apply to revert to a previous legal name. This process is subject to a simplified application form and a reduced fee of 350 crowns. The public notice requirements of section 7 still apply. Such applications can only be made once every 3 years. Documentation proving the previous legal name is required, typically an earlier Certificate of Name Change or birth certificate. This option allows for flexibility while maintaining administrative order and reducing frequent changes.

heading: Fees for Additional Copies
text: Additional certified copies of the Certificate of Name Change may be requested by the individual. Each additional copy will incur a fee of 100 crowns. Requests must be made in writing and include the original application reference number. Copies will be mailed to the registered address within 14 working days of the request and payment. A maximum of 5 additional copies can be requested at any one time to prevent misuse.

heading: Emergency Name Change
text: In exceptional and documented emergency situations, such as immediate threats to life or severe personal safety risks, an expedited name change process may be initiated. Such applications require a court order specifically endorsing the emergency nature of the request. The processing fee for an emergency name change is 2,500 crowns, and the process aims to be completed within 7 working days. The public notice requirements of section 7 may be partially waived by court order.

heading: Emergency Name Change
text: In exceptional and documented emergency situations, such as immediate threats to life or severe personal safety risks, an expedited name change process may be initiated. Such applications require a court order specifically endorsing the emergency nature of the request. The processing fee for an emergency name change is 2,800 crowns, and the process aims to be completed within 5 working days. The public notice requirements of section 7 may be partially waived by court order, with alternative, more discreet verification methods implemented.

heading: Digital Application Pilot Program
text: A pilot program for digital application submission will commence on 2023-01-01, available only to residents of Lund Vale and Grauby. This program allows for online submission of forms and digital copies of identification, with a mandatory in-person identity verification at designated municipal offices. The digital application fee is 750 crowns, representing a 10% discount from the standard fee. The pilot will run for 18 months, after which its efficacy will be reviewed.

heading: Digital Application Pilot Program
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Review of Fees
text: All fees stipulated in this Act are subject to review every 2 years by the Nordvale Ministry of Interior. Any proposed changes to the fees will be published in the Official Nordvale Gazette at least 90 days before coming into effect. The purpose of these reviews is to ensure that the fees remain appropriate for covering administrative costs and reflect changes in economic conditions. Public consultation on fee adjustments may be initiated at the Ministry's discretion.

heading: Enforcement and Penalties
text: The Name Registration Office is responsible for the enforcement of this Act. Any person or entity found to be in violation of the provisions of this Act, beyond those specified in individual sections, may be subject to administrative penalties ranging from 200 crowns to 2,000 crowns, depending on the severity and nature of the infraction. Continued non-compliance may lead to further legal action. All penalties are payable within 30 days of notification.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any name change applications submitted before the effective date of this Act will be processed according to the laws in force at the time of their submission. Applications pending on the effective date of this Act that have not yet reached final approval will be subject to the provisions of this Act from that date forward, with any fees already paid being credited towards the new fee structure. Clear communication will be provided to affected applicants within 20 days.

heading: Recognised trades
text: No energy rebate is payable by any licensed tightrope performer, who instead receives half of the annual energy rebate of 350 crowns paid in January.

heading: Concessions
text: A holder of a registered cave rescue badge for at least one year is exempt from paying the annual food truck permit fee or the monthly food truck permit fee.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements and procedures for obtaining permits for any excavation, cutting, or disturbance of public roads within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure the safety of the public, maintain the integrity of public infrastructure, and manage the impact of road works on traffic flow and community life. All works affecting the surface or sub-surface of any public road, whether temporary or permanent, are subject to the provisions of this Act, unless specifically exempted by other regulations issued by the Ministry of Infrastructure.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Public Road' means any road, street, highway, lane, or thoroughfare owned or maintained by a municipality or the national government, including its shoulders, verges, and associated drainage systems.
(b) 'Excavation' or 'Cutting' means any activity that disturbs, penetrates, or removes material from the surface or sub-surface of a public road, including trenching, boring, and pavement removal.
(c) 'Applicant' means any individual, company, or organization applying for a Road Cutting Permit.
(d) 'Ministry' refers to the Ministry of Infrastructure of Nordvale.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall commence any excavation or cutting on a public road without first obtaining a valid Road Cutting Permit from the Ministry.
(2) Failure to possess a valid permit for such works constitutes an offense under this Act and is subject to penalties as outlined in section 25.
(3) This requirement applies to all public roads in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, regardless of the size or duration of the proposed works, unless specifically exempted.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) Applications for Road Cutting Permits must be submitted to the Ministry at least 20 working days prior to the proposed commencement date of the works.
(2) Each application must be accompanied by the prescribed fee and all required documentation, as detailed in section 5.
(3) Applications submitted with incomplete information or lacking the correct fee will be returned to the applicant and will not be processed until all deficiencies are rectified. The 20-day processing period will recommence upon resubmission.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) All applications must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans showing the precise location, dimensions, and depth of the proposed excavation.
(b) A traffic management plan, approved by a certified traffic engineer, detailing how disruption will be minimized.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns.
(d) A proposed work schedule, including start and end dates.
(e) A restoration plan detailing how the road surface will be reinstated to its original condition or better.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) All applications must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans showing the precise location, dimensions, and depth of the proposed excavation, including a cross-section of the road structure.
(b) A traffic management plan, approved by a certified traffic engineer, detailing how disruption will be minimized and signed by a municipal traffic officer.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 7,500,000 crowns.
(d) A proposed work schedule, including start and end dates, with specific daily operational hours.
(e) A restoration plan detailing how the road surface will be reinstated to its original condition or better, with a guaranteed maintenance period of 12 months.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) All applications must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans showing the precise location, dimensions, and depth of the proposed excavation, including a cross-section of the road structure and details of any affected utilities.
(b) A traffic management plan, approved by a certified traffic engineer, detailing how disruption will be minimized and signed by a municipal traffic officer, with a focus on peak hour mitigation.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 10,000,000 crowns.
(d) A proposed work schedule, including start and end dates, with specific daily operational hours and contingency plans for delays.
(e) A restoration plan detailing how the road surface will be reinstated to its original condition or better, with a guaranteed maintenance period of 24 months, including material specifications.

heading: Application Fees
text:
(1) The standard application fee for a Road Cutting Permit is 500 crowns for minor works (less than 10 square meters of road surface affected) and 1,500 crowns for major works (10 square meters or more).
(2) An additional non-refundable processing fee of 150 crowns applies to all applications.
(3) Fees are payable upon submission and are non-refundable, regardless of the permit outcome. Exceptions may be granted for government-initiated works.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text:
(1) Applicants requiring a permit decision within 10 working days may opt for expedited processing.
(2) An expedited processing fee of 1,000 crowns is applicable for minor works, and 2,500 crowns for major works, in addition to the standard application fees.
(3) Expedited processing does not guarantee permit approval, only a faster review. All other requirements of this Act must still be met for approval.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text:
(1) Applicants requiring a permit decision within 7 working days may opt for expedited processing.
(2) An expedited processing fee of 1,500 crowns is applicable for minor works, and 3,500 crowns for major works, in addition to the standard application fees.
(3) Expedited processing does not guarantee permit approval, only a faster review. All other requirements of this Act must still be met for approval. Only works deemed essential for public safety or utility repair are eligible for expedited processing.

heading: Permit Issuance
text:
(1) The Ministry shall review all applications for compliance with this Act and other relevant regulations.
(2) A permit may be issued if the Ministry is satisfied that the proposed works will be carried out safely, with minimal disruption, and that proper restoration will occur.
(3) The Ministry reserves the right to impose specific conditions on any permit, including work hours, traffic control measures, and material specifications, to ensure public safety and road integrity. These conditions must be strictly adhered to by the permit holder.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A standard Road Cutting Permit is valid for a period of 30 calendar days from the approved start date of the works.
(2) For projects exceeding 30 days, applicants must justify the extended duration in their application, and the Ministry may grant a permit valid for up to 90 days.
(3) Permits automatically expire upon the completion of the works or the specified end date, whichever comes first. Works continuing beyond the permit's expiry without extension are subject to penalties.

heading: Permit Extension
text:
(1) An applicant may apply for an extension to an existing permit at least 5 working days before its expiry.
(2) Extension applications must include a revised work schedule, a justification for the delay, and a fee of 300 crowns.
(3) Extensions are granted at the discretion of the Ministry and may be subject to additional conditions, particularly if the delays impact significant public infrastructure or traffic flow. Only one extension is typically granted per permit.

heading: Permit Extension
text:
(1) An applicant may apply for an extension to an existing permit at least 10 working days before its expiry.
(2) Extension applications must include a revised work schedule, a detailed justification for the delay, and a fee of 500 crowns.
(3) Extensions are granted at the discretion of the Ministry and may be subject to additional conditions, particularly if the delays impact significant public infrastructure or traffic flow. A maximum of two extensions may be granted per permit, each not exceeding 30 days.

heading: Emergency Works
text:
(1) In cases of emergency works, such as immediate repairs to essential utility services (water, gas, electricity) that pose an imminent threat to public safety or infrastructure, works may commence without a prior permit.
(2) The Ministry must be notified verbally within 4 hours of the commencement of emergency works and a formal application for a retroactive permit submitted within 24 hours.
(3) All emergency works must still comply with safety standards and a traffic management plan, even if provisional, must be in place. Failure to notify and apply within the stipulated times will result in penalties.

heading: Notification of Commencement
text:
(1) The permit holder must notify the Ministry and the relevant municipal authority at least 24 hours before the actual commencement of works.
(2) This notification must include the precise start time, confirmation of on-site personnel and equipment, and any minor adjustments to the approved schedule.
(3) Failure to provide timely notification may result in a delay of the works or a penalty of 200 crowns, as municipal inspectors require time to schedule site visits and ensure compliance.

heading: Notification of Commencement
text:
(1) The permit holder must notify the Ministry and the relevant municipal authority at least 48 hours before the actual commencement of works.
(2) This notification must be submitted via the Ministry's online portal and include the precise start time, confirmation of on-site personnel and equipment, and any minor adjustments to the approved schedule.
(3) Failure to provide timely notification may result in a delay of the works or a penalty of 400 crowns, as municipal inspectors require time to schedule site visits and ensure compliance, and potentially impact public communication campaigns.

heading: Site Safety Requirements
text:
(1) All work sites must be clearly marked with appropriate signage and barriers, visible from at least 50 meters in all directions.
(2) Adequate lighting must be provided for works conducted during hours of darkness.
(3) Personal protective equipment must be worn by all personnel on site, and a designated safety officer must be present during all operational hours. Failure to comply with these safety standards will result in immediate suspension of works.

heading: Traffic Management Compliance
text:
(1) The permit holder must strictly adhere to the approved traffic management plan at all times during the works.
(2) Any deviation from the plan requires prior written approval from the Ministry and the municipal traffic authority.
(3) Failure to implement the approved traffic management plan, or any unauthorized deviation, will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per day and may lead to the revocation of the permit. Public safety is paramount and traffic flow must be managed effectively.

heading: Restoration Standards
text:
(1) Upon completion of the excavation, the road surface must be restored to a condition equivalent to or better than its original state.
(2) Restoration must comply with the specifications outlined in the approved restoration plan, including material quality and compaction standards.
(3) The permit holder is responsible for the quality of the restoration for a period of 6 months following completion. Any defects appearing within this period must be rectified at no additional cost to the municipality.

heading: Restoration Standards
text:
(1) Upon completion of the excavation, the road surface must be restored to a condition equivalent to or better than its original state, as per national road construction standards.
(2) Restoration must comply with the specifications outlined in the approved restoration plan, including material quality, compaction standards, and surface finish requirements for all layers of the road structure.
(3) The permit holder is responsible for the quality of the restoration for a period of 12 months following completion, which includes regular inspections by municipal engineers. Any defects appearing within this period must be rectified at no additional cost to the municipality within 14 days of notification.

heading: Completion Notification
text:
(1) Within 5 working days of the completion of all works, including full restoration, the permit holder must notify the Ministry and the relevant municipal authority.
(2) This notification must include a signed declaration that all works have been completed in accordance with the permit conditions and approved plans.
(3) A final inspection will be scheduled by the municipal authority within 10 working days of receiving the completion notification to verify compliance. Permits are not officially closed until this inspection is passed.

heading: Warranty Period
text:
(1) The permit holder shall guarantee the quality of the road restoration for a period of 6 months from the date of final inspection.
(2) During this warranty period, any subsidence, cracking, or other defects directly attributable to the permitted works must be repaired by the permit holder at their own expense within 14 days of notification.
(3) Failure to rectify defects within the specified timeframe will result in the Ministry engaging a third party to undertake the repairs, with all costs billed to the original permit holder, plus an administrative fee of 15%.

heading: Indemnity
text:
(1) The permit holder shall indemnify and hold harmless the Republic of Nordvale and its municipalities against all claims, demands, and liabilities arising from the permitted works.
(2) This includes claims for personal injury, property damage, or financial loss incurred by third parties as a result of the works.
(3) The permit holder's insurance coverage, as specified in section 5, must remain valid throughout the duration of the works and the warranty period.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) The Ministry may revoke a Road Cutting Permit if the permit holder fails to comply with any condition of the permit or any provision of this Act.
(2) Grounds for revocation include, but are not limited to, serious safety violations, significant deviations from approved plans, or repeated failure to manage traffic effectively.
(3) Upon revocation, all works must cease immediately, and the permit holder must restore the site to a safe condition within 24 hours. The Ministry may undertake such restoration if the permit holder fails to act, billing all costs to the permit holder.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the Appeals Board of the Ministry within 15 working days of receiving notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, outlining the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by any supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the appeal within 30 working days and issue a final decision. The decision of the Appeals Board is binding. A fee of 750 crowns applies to all appeal submissions.

heading: Inspection Authority
text:
(1) Authorized officers of the Ministry and municipal authorities have the right to enter and inspect any work site at any reasonable time.
(2) These officers may demand to see the valid permit, approved plans, and any other relevant documentation.
(3) Obstruction of an authorized officer in the performance of their duties constitutes an offense under this Act and may result in penalties or permit revocation. Regular inspections are crucial for ensuring compliance and public safety.

heading: Penalties for Unpermitted Works
text:
(1) Any person or entity found undertaking excavation or cutting on a public road without a valid permit shall be liable to a fine of 5,000 crowns for the first offense.
(2) Subsequent offenses shall incur a fine of 10,000 crowns and may result in a prohibition from applying for future permits for a period of 12 months.
(3) In addition to fines, the Ministry may order immediate cessation of works and require the site to be restored at the expense of the offender within 48 hours.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Failure to comply with any permit condition or provision of this Act, other than operating without a permit, shall incur a fine of 1,000 crowns per day for each day the non-compliance persists.
(2) Serious or repeated non-compliance may lead to permit suspension or revocation, in addition to fines.
(3) Examples of non-compliance include inadequate safety measures, unapproved traffic diversions, or failure to meet restoration standards. All fines are payable within 30 days of issuance.

heading: Protection of Utilities
text:
(1) The permit holder is solely responsible for identifying and protecting all underground utilities (water, sewage, gas, electricity, telecommunications) in the vicinity of the proposed works.
(2) 'Call Before You Dig' services must be utilized at least 3 working days before any excavation, and their recommendations strictly followed.
(3) Any damage to public or private utilities caused during the works is the sole financial responsibility of the permit holder. The Ministry bears no liability for such damages. Damage must be reported within 1 hour.

heading: Archaeological Finds
text:
(1) If any object of historical or archaeological significance is discovered during excavation, all works must cease immediately.
(2) The Ministry of Cultural Heritage and the Ministry of Infrastructure must be notified within 2 hours of the discovery.
(3) Works may only resume upon written authorization from the Ministry of Cultural Heritage, which may impose further conditions or require specific archaeological procedures. Failure to report such finds may result in severe penalties and legal action.

heading: Environmental Protection
text:
(1) The permit holder must take all reasonable measures to prevent environmental pollution, including controlling dust, noise, and runoff, during the works.
(2) All waste materials generated by the works must be disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner, in accordance with national waste management regulations.
(3) Special care must be taken to prevent contaminants from entering drainage systems or natural waterways. Any environmental damage caused by the works will result in immediate cessation and significant fines.

heading: Maintenance Period
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Maintenance Period
text:
(1) Following the final inspection and successful restoration, the permit holder is responsible for the maintenance of the restored section of road for a period of 12 months.
(2) This maintenance includes monitoring for settlement, cracking, or surface deterioration, and undertaking any necessary repairs without charge to the municipality.
(3) A security deposit, calculated at 10% of the estimated restoration cost (minimum 2,000 crowns), must be held by the Ministry throughout this maintenance period. The deposit will be released upon satisfactory completion of the 12-month period.

heading: Review and Amendment
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Infrastructure every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) Any proposed amendments or updates to this Act will be subject to public consultation for a period of no less than 60 days prior to their enactment.
(3) Recommendations for amendments may be submitted by municipal authorities, professional organizations, or members of the public at any time to the Ministry for consideration during the review process.

heading: Concessions
text: Each registered stonemason of a protected monument is exempt from paying the electric bicycle registration fee.

heading: Particular persons
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any licensed tightrope performer shall receive an annual energy rebate of seven hundred crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the registration of topography rights for integrated circuits within the Republic of Nordvale. The purpose is to ensure that the administrative costs associated with processing and maintaining these registrations are adequately covered, while also providing a clear and predictable fee structure for innovators. All fees collected under this Act shall be remitted to the Nordvale Central Treasury. This Act applies to all applications for topography right registration and related services submitted on or after the effective date. It covers initial registration, renewal, amendments, and certified copies of registration documents, as detailed in subsequent sections.

heading: Initial Application Fee for Original Topography
text: An initial application fee of 1,200 crowns shall be paid for the registration of an original topography. This fee is non-refundable and must accompany the application form. If the application is submitted without the correct fee, it will be held for a maximum of 30 days, during which time the applicant must remit the full amount. Failure to pay within this period will result in the application being rejected, and a new application will be required. This fee covers the administrative processing of the application, initial examination for compliance with formal requirements, and the first year of registration.

heading: Initial Application Fee for Original Topography
text: An initial application fee of 1,350 crowns shall be paid for the registration of an original topography. This fee is non-refundable and must accompany the application form. If the application is submitted without the correct fee, it will be held for a maximum of 25 days, during which time the applicant must remit the full amount. Failure to pay within this period will result in the application being rejected, and a new application will be required. This fee covers the administrative processing of the application, initial examination for compliance with formal requirements, and the first year of registration.

heading: Initial Application Fee for Derivative Topography
text: For a derivative topography, where the original topography is already registered in Nordvale, the initial application fee shall be 800 crowns. This reduced fee acknowledges the existing administrative record. The applicant must clearly reference the registration number of the original topography in their application. If the original topography is not registered in Nordvale, the fee outlined in section 2 applies. This fee is also non-refundable and must be paid upon submission of the application. Applications for derivative topographies must demonstrate a minimum of 20% original creative content to qualify.

heading: Initial Application Fee for Derivative Topography
text: For a derivative topography, where the original topography is already registered in Nordvale, the initial application fee shall be 950 crowns. This reduced fee acknowledges the existing administrative record. The applicant must clearly reference the registration number of the original topography in their application. If the original topography is not registered in Nordvale, the fee outlined in section 2 applies. This fee is also non-refundable and must be paid upon submission of the application. Applications for derivative topographies must demonstrate a minimum of 25% original creative content to qualify.

heading: Expedited Examination Fee
text: Applicants may request expedited examination of their topography registration application for an additional fee of 2,500 crowns. This fee guarantees that the initial examination process will be completed within 15 working days from the date of payment, provided all required documentation is complete. This does not guarantee registration, only expedited processing. The expedited examination fee is separate from the initial application fee and must be paid at the time of the request. Requests for expedited examination made after the initial application submission may incur an additional 5% administrative surcharge.

heading: Expedited Examination Fee
text: Applicants may request expedited examination of their topography registration application for an additional fee of 2,750 crowns. This fee guarantees that the initial examination process will be completed within 12 working days from the date of payment, provided all required documentation is complete. This does not guarantee registration, only expedited processing. The expedited examination fee is separate from the initial application fee and must be paid at the time of the request. Requests for expedited examination made after the initial application submission may incur an additional 7% administrative surcharge.

heading: Annual Renewal Fee
text: A topography right registration shall be renewed annually by paying a fee of 500 crowns. This fee is due on the anniversary of the initial registration date. Failure to pay the renewal fee within 30 days after the due date will result in a late payment penalty as specified in section 6. Continued failure to pay will lead to the lapse of the registration. The renewal fee covers the costs of maintaining the registration on the national register and ensuring its legal validity for another year. A notice will be sent 60 days prior to the renewal date.

heading: Late Renewal Fee
text: If the annual renewal fee is not paid by its due date, a late renewal fee of 150 crowns shall be imposed for payments made within 60 days after the due date. For payments made between 61 and 120 days after the due date, the late renewal fee shall be 300 crowns. No renewals will be accepted more than 120 days after the due date; the registration will lapse, and a new application process will be required to re-establish rights. The late fee is cumulative with the annual renewal fee.

heading: Reinstatement Fee for Lapsed Registration
text: A lapsed topography registration may be reinstated within 180 days of its lapse, subject to a reinstatement fee of 1,500 crowns, in addition to all outstanding annual and late renewal fees. Reinstatement is only possible if there has been no intervening third-party registration of a substantially similar topography. The applicant must submit a written request for reinstatement and provide a valid reason for the lapse. After 180 days, reinstatement is not possible, and a new application must be filed according to section 2. The decision to reinstate is at the discretion of the registration office.

heading: Reinstatement Fee for Lapsed Registration
text: A lapsed topography registration may be reinstated within 150 days of its lapse, subject to a reinstatement fee of 1,800 crowns, in addition to all outstanding annual and late renewal fees. Reinstatement is only possible if there has been no intervening third-party registration of a substantially similar topography. The applicant must submit a written request for reinstatement and provide a valid reason for the lapse. After 150 days, reinstatement is not possible, and a new application must be filed according to section 2. The decision to reinstate is at the discretion of the registration office.

heading: Transfer of Ownership Fee
text: A fee of 400 crowns shall be paid for the registration of a transfer of ownership of a topography right. This fee applies whether the transfer is by sale, inheritance, or any other legal means. The request for transfer must be submitted within 90 days of the effective date of transfer, accompanied by verifiable documentation of the change in ownership. Failure to register the transfer within this period will result in a 20% penalty fee on top of the standard transfer fee. The transfer will only be legally recognized upon its registration.

heading: Amendment of Registered Information Fee
text: A fee of 250 crowns is required for any amendment to the registered information of a topography right, such as changes to the owner's address, name, or representative details. This fee applies per amendment request, regardless of the number of individual changes within that request. Amendments must be supported by appropriate documentation. If multiple amendments are submitted as separate requests on the same day, each will incur the full fee. Minor clerical corrections initiated by the registration office are exempt from this fee.

heading: Certified Copy of Registration Document Fee
text: A fee of 100 crowns shall be charged for each certified copy of a topography registration document. This fee includes the cost of printing, certification, and standard postal delivery within Nordvale. For international delivery, an additional 50 crowns postal surcharge will apply. Requests for multiple certified copies submitted simultaneously will incur the fee for each copy. Copies are typically dispatched within 7 working days of receiving the request and payment. Expedited delivery within 24 hours is available for an extra 150 crowns.

heading: Certified Copy of Registration Document Fee
text: A fee of 120 crowns shall be charged for each certified copy of a topography registration document. This fee includes the cost of printing, certification, and standard postal delivery within Nordvale. For international delivery, an additional 60 crowns postal surcharge will apply. Requests for multiple certified copies submitted simultaneously will incur the fee for each copy. Copies are typically dispatched within 5 working days of receiving the request and payment. Expedited delivery within 24 hours is available for an extra 180 crowns.

heading: Search Request Fee
text: A fee of 300 crowns is required for a formal search request concerning existing topography registrations. This fee covers a search for specific criteria, such as a particular applicant, a range of registration numbers, or keywords related to the topography's function. The results of the search will be provided in a written report within 10 working days. This fee does not include any certified copies of documents found during the search; these must be requested separately under section 10. Complex search requests may incur an additional hourly fee of 75 crowns after the first hour.

heading: Opposition Filing Fee
text: A fee of 750 crowns shall be paid by any party filing an opposition against a pending topography registration application. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the opposition proceedings. The opposition must be filed within 60 days of the publication of the application. Failure to pay the opposition fee will result in the rejection of the opposition filing. This fee contributes to the administrative costs of reviewing and processing the opposition, including notifications to the applicant and preliminary legal assessments.

heading: Extension of Time Fee (Application)
text: Applicants may request a single extension of 30 days to respond to an office action or deficiency notice, subject to a fee of 150 crowns. This fee must accompany the extension request. Only one such extension is permitted per office action. Subsequent extensions or extensions beyond 30 days will not be granted, and failure to respond within the extended period will lead to the application being deemed abandoned. This fee covers the administrative effort of managing and monitoring extended deadlines for applications.

heading: Extension of Time Fee (Application)
text: Applicants may request a single extension of 20 days to respond to an office action or deficiency notice, subject to a fee of 200 crowns. This fee must accompany the extension request. Only one such extension is permitted per office action. Subsequent extensions or extensions beyond 20 days will not be granted, and failure to respond within the extended period will lead to the application being deemed abandoned. This fee covers the administrative effort of managing and monitoring extended deadlines for applications.

heading: Extension of Time Fee (Opposition)
text: Parties to an opposition proceeding may request a single extension of 45 days to file arguments or evidence, subject to a fee of 200 crowns. This fee must accompany the extension request. Only one such extension is permitted per stage of the opposition process. Subsequent extensions or extensions beyond 45 days will not be granted. Failure to comply with deadlines, even with an extension, may result in the dismissal of the opposition or the granting of the registration. This fee supports the administrative overhead of managing extensions in contentious matters.

heading: Disclaimer of Rights Fee
text: A fee of 100 crowns shall be paid for the registration of a disclaimer of rights in a topography. This applies when a registered owner wishes to explicitly state that certain aspects of their topography are not claimed as part of their exclusive rights. The disclaimer must be clear and precise, and the fee must accompany the submission. This registration provides clarity for third parties and is irreversible once recorded. The fee covers the administrative cost of updating the public register with this new information and cross-referencing.

heading: Correction of Error Fee
text: A fee of 120 crowns is required for the correction of an error in a registered topography or its associated documentation that was not caused by the registration office. This fee applies to errors of fact, transcription errors by the applicant, or other similar mistakes. If the error was caused by the registration office, no fee will be charged. The request for correction must be accompanied by supporting evidence and must be submitted within 6 months of discovery of the error. After 6 months, an additional 50% surcharge will apply.

heading: Voluntary Cancellation Fee
text: A fee of 50 crowns shall be paid for the voluntary cancellation of a topography right registration by the owner. This fee applies when the owner decides to surrender their rights before the natural expiry or lapse of the registration. The request for cancellation must be in writing and signed by all registered owners. Once cancelled, the topography cannot be re-registered under the same owner for a period of 5 years unless it constitutes a substantially new design. The fee covers the administrative costs of processing and recording the cancellation.

heading: Revocation Request Fee
text: A fee of 600 crowns shall be paid by any party requesting the revocation of a topography right registration. This fee is non-refundable. The request must be based on valid grounds, such as the topography not meeting the originality requirements or being in prior public use for more than two years before the application date. The fee supports the administrative process of reviewing the revocation request, conducting an investigation if necessary, and issuing a decision. The owner of the topography will be notified of the request within 14 days.

heading: Ex Parte Re-examination Fee
text: A fee of 900 crowns shall be paid for requesting an ex parte re-examination of a registered topography right. This request can be made by the owner or a third party, without immediate involvement of the other party. The re-examination assesses whether new prior art or other relevant information affects the validity of the registration. The fee is non-refundable and covers the administrative and technical review process. If the re-examination leads to a finding of invalidity, the original registration may be partially or wholly cancelled.

heading: Inter Partes Review Fee
text: A fee of 1,500 crowns shall be paid by the party requesting an inter partes review of a registered topography right. This fee is non-refundable. An inter partes review is a formal proceeding where both the petitioner and the topography owner participate, presenting arguments and evidence. The fee covers the administrative costs of conducting this quasi-judicial process, including hearings, evidence management, and decision issuance. Such a review can challenge the validity of a topography right based on specified grounds, and the decision is legally binding.

heading: Recordal of License Agreement Fee
text: A fee of 350 crowns shall be paid for the recordal of a license agreement pertaining to a registered topography right. This fee applies to both exclusive and non-exclusive licenses. The recordal provides public notice of the license and helps protect the rights of both the licensor and licensee. The license agreement itself is not examined for validity, only its existence and the parties involved are recorded. The fee covers the administrative cost of updating the public register with this contractual information. Failure to record a license may impact its enforceability against third parties.

heading: Recordal of License Agreement Fee
text: A fee of 400 crowns shall be paid for the recordal of a license agreement pertaining to a registered topography right. This fee applies to both exclusive and non-exclusive licenses. The recordal provides public notice of the license and helps protect the rights of both the licensor and licensee. The license agreement itself is not examined for validity, only its existence and the parties involved are recorded. The fee covers the administrative cost of updating the public register with this contractual information. Failure to record a license may impact its enforceability against third parties.

heading: Renewal of Recorded License Fee
text: A fee of 150 crowns shall be paid for the renewal of a recorded license agreement for a topography right. This fee is due every five years from the date of initial recordal, or upon the renewal of the underlying topography right, whichever occurs first. Failure to renew the recordal of the license may render it unenforceable against third parties, though it remains valid between the contracting parties. The fee covers the administrative cost of maintaining the license details on the public register and sending reminder notices.

heading: Recordal of Security Interest Fee
text: A fee of 250 crowns shall be paid for the recordal of a security interest, such as a mortgage or pledge, granted over a topography right. This recordal provides public notice to creditors and other interested parties. The fee covers the administrative cost of processing and updating the register with this financial encumbrance. Documentation proving the security interest must accompany the request. The recordal is valid for the term of the security interest or the topography right, whichever is shorter, and must be renewed if the terms extend.

heading: Cancellation of Recorded Security Interest Fee
text: A fee of 75 crowns shall be paid for the cancellation of a recorded security interest in a topography right. This fee applies once the security interest has been discharged or terminated. A written request from the secured party or the topography owner, along with proof of discharge, must be submitted. This ensures that the public register accurately reflects the current status of encumbrances. The fee covers the administrative process of removing the recordal from the public registry.

heading: Withdrawal of Application Fee
text: A fee of 50 crowns shall be paid for the formal withdrawal of a topography registration application by the applicant before examination has commenced. If examination has commenced, the fee increases to 100 crowns. This fee covers the administrative handling of the withdrawal request and updating of records. Any initial application fees paid are non-refundable, as stated in section 2. This withdrawal ensures that the application is formally removed from the processing queue and is not mistakenly processed further.

heading: Payment Methods
text: All fees payable under this Act may be remitted via bank transfer, credit card, or certified cheque made payable to the 'Nordvale Central Treasury'. Cash payments are only accepted for amounts under 500 crowns at the Aldmark registration office. Payments must be made in Nordvale crowns. Any bank charges or currency conversion fees are the responsibility of the remitter. Payments received after 16:00 on a working day will be processed on the next working day, affecting the effective date of payment for deadlines.

heading: Refund Policy
text: Fees paid under this Act are generally non-refundable, with the exception of overpayments or payments made for services not rendered due to administrative error. Requests for refunds must be submitted in writing within 90 days of the payment date, detailing the reason for the refund claim. Approved refunds will be processed within 30 working days. No refunds will be issued for applications rejected due to applicant error or for fees associated with requests that are voluntarily withdrawn by the applicant after processing has begun.

heading: Fee Adjustments
text: The Minister of Commerce, in consultation with the Nordvale Central Treasury, may adjust the fees specified in this Act. Any adjustments will be announced at least 60 days prior to their effective date through publication in the Official Gazette of Nordvale. Adjustments shall not exceed a 10% increase or decrease in any given 12-month period. The primary criteria for adjustment include changes in administrative costs, inflation rates as published by the National Statistics Office, and the need to maintain financial sustainability of the registration system.

heading: Applicability to Government Agencies
text: Government agencies of Nordvale are exempt from paying fees outlined in sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of this Act when applying for or maintaining topography rights for technologies developed by or for the public sector. However, all other fees, including those for certified copies, search requests, and opposition filings, shall apply. This exemption is intended to facilitate public interest innovation and streamline governmental administrative processes related to intellectual property. The agency must clearly identify itself as a government entity in the application.

heading: Applicability to Government Agencies
text: Government agencies of Nordvale are exempt from paying fees outlined in sections 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of this Act when applying for or maintaining topography rights for technologies developed by or for the public sector. However, all other fees, including those for certified copies, search requests, and opposition filings, shall apply. This exemption is intended to facilitate public interest innovation and streamline governmental administrative processes related to intellectual property. The agency must clearly identify itself as a government entity in the application.

heading: Fee for Public Inspection
text: A fee of 20 crowns per hour, or any part thereof, shall be charged for public inspection of topography registration files at the Aldmark registration office. This fee covers the administrative cost of retrieving and supervising access to physical files. Digital access to non-confidential information in the public register is free of charge. Inspection requests must be made at least 24 hours in advance. Large-scale or repeated inspection requests by the same individual or entity may be subject to a special arrangement fee determined by the office director, not to exceed 150 crowns per day.

heading: Annual Statistical Report Fee
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Annual Statistical Report Fee
text: A fee of 500 crowns shall be paid for a copy of the annual statistical report on topography right registrations. This report, published annually by 31 March, includes data on application volumes, granted registrations, renewals, and other relevant statistics for the preceding calendar year. The fee covers the cost of compiling, publishing, and distributing the report. Subscribers to the Nordvale Official Gazette receive a digital copy of the report automatically without charge. Physical copies can be requested for the specified fee.

heading: Doctor visits for regular blood donors
text:
(1) A regular blood donor pays 8 crowns for a visit to a general practitioner, instead of the ordinary fee.
(2) The donor shows the donor record of the donation centre at the visit.
(3) The amount paid counts towards the yearly limit on health care fees.

heading: Doctor visits for regular blood donors
text:
(1) A regular blood donor pays no fee for a visit to a general practitioner.
(2) The donor shows the donor record of the donation centre at the visit.
(3) A visit for which no fee is charged under this section does not count towards the yearly limit on health care fees.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for assessing the environmental impact of proposed projects within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all developments likely to have significant effects on the environment are thoroughly evaluated before construction or implementation commences. The scope of this Act extends to all public and private projects exceeding certain size or capacity thresholds, as detailed in subsequent sections. The aim is to mitigate potential harm to natural resources, ecosystems, and human well-being, fostering sustainable development across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, 'project' means any construction work, installation, or other intervention in the natural surroundings or landscape, including those involving the extraction of natural resources.
(2) 'Environmental impact assessment' (EIA) means the process of identifying, predicting, evaluating, and mitigating the biophysical, social, and other relevant effects of development proposals prior to major decisions being taken and commitments made.
(3) 'Competent authority' refers to the Environmental Protection Department of Nordvale, responsible for administering this Act.
(4) 'Significant environmental impact' denotes an effect that is likely to cause substantial harm or alteration to the environment, as determined by criteria outlined in section 5.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) A permit from the competent authority is required for any project that may have a significant environmental impact. No project shall commence construction or operation without first obtaining such a permit.
(2) The permit requirement applies to new projects as well as modifications to existing projects if those modifications themselves meet the criteria for a significant environmental impact.
(3) Failure to obtain a required permit before commencing work may result in penalties as outlined in section 38.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) A permit from the competent authority is required for any project that may have a significant environmental impact. No project shall commence construction or operation without first obtaining such a permit.
(2) The permit requirement applies to new projects as well as modifications to existing projects if those modifications themselves meet the criteria for a significant environmental impact, or if the total cumulative impact of the modification combined with the existing project exceeds the thresholds.
(3) Failure to obtain a required permit before commencing work may result in penalties as outlined in section 38, including potential fines up to 150,000 crowns.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
(1) Projects primarily serving national security interests may be exempted from the permit requirement by executive decree, provided that such decree specifies alternative environmental safeguards.
(2) Small-scale projects with a total construction area less than 500 square meters and not located in a designated environmentally sensitive area are generally exempt.
(3) Emergency repairs to existing infrastructure are exempt, but a report must be submitted to the competent authority within 10 days of commencement.
(4) Projects with a total estimated cost of less than 1,000,000 crowns are exempt, unless they involve hazardous materials.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
(1) Projects primarily serving national security interests may be exempted from the permit requirement by executive decree, provided that such decree specifies alternative environmental safeguards and is reviewed annually.
(2) Small-scale projects with a total construction area less than 300 square meters and not located in a designated environmentally sensitive area are generally exempt.
(3) Emergency repairs to existing infrastructure are exempt, but a report must be submitted to the competent authority within 7 days of commencement.
(4) Projects with a total estimated cost of less than 750,000 crowns are exempt, unless they involve hazardous materials or are located near a critical water source.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
(1) Projects primarily serving national security interests may be exempted from the permit requirement by executive decree, provided that such decree specifies alternative environmental safeguards and is reviewed annually by an independent panel.
(2) Small-scale projects with a total construction area less than 200 square meters and not located in a designated environmentally sensitive area are generally exempt.
(3) Emergency repairs to existing infrastructure are exempt, but a report must be submitted to the competent authority within 5 days of commencement.
(4) Projects with a total estimated cost of less than 500,000 crowns are exempt, unless they involve hazardous materials or are located near a critical water source or protected habitat.

heading: Criteria for Significant Environmental Impact
text:
A project is deemed to have a significant environmental impact if it meets any of the following criteria:
(a) It involves the physical alteration of an area greater than 10,000 square meters.
(b) It necessitates the removal of more than 50 mature trees.
(c) It is located within 200 meters of a designated nature reserve or protected wetland.
(d) It involves the discharge of more than 100 cubic meters of wastewater per day into a natural water body.
(e) It is likely to generate more than 500 tonnes of solid waste annually.
(f) It requires the extraction of more than 1,000 cubic meters of aggregate material.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for an Environmental Impact Assessment Permit must be submitted to the competent authority in the prescribed form.
