(2) The application shall include a detailed project description, site plans, and preliminary assessment of potential environmental effects.
(3) The applicant must submit 10 copies of the application, along with an electronic version, to facilitate review by various departments.
(4) A non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns shall accompany the submission.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for an Environmental Impact Assessment Permit must be submitted to the competent authority in the prescribed form.
(2) The application shall include a detailed project description, site plans, and preliminary assessment of potential environmental effects.
(3) The applicant must submit 15 copies of the application, along with an electronic version, to facilitate review by various departments.
(4) A non-refundable application fee of 7,500 crowns shall accompany the submission, payable via electronic transfer only.

heading: Preliminary Environmental Review
text:
(1) Upon receipt of an application, the competent authority shall conduct a preliminary environmental review within 30 days.
(2) The purpose of this review is to determine whether a full Environmental Impact Assessment is required or if a less intensive assessment is sufficient.
(3) The authority may request additional information from the applicant during this period.
(4) If the review determines that no significant impact is likely, the application may be approved without a full EIA, or returned if further information is needed, within 45 days of submission.

heading: Decision on EIA Requirement
text:
(1) Following the preliminary environmental review, the competent authority shall issue a decision within 45 days, stating whether a full EIA is required.
(2) If an EIA is required, the decision shall also include a scoping document outlining the key environmental issues to be addressed.
(3) The decision will be communicated in writing to the applicant and made publicly available for 14 days.
(4) An applicant may appeal this decision within 10 days of its publication, as outlined in section 40.

heading: Scoping Document
text:
(1) The scoping document shall specify the boundaries of the assessment, including geographical and temporal limits.
(2) It shall identify the specific environmental components that must be analyzed, such as air quality, water resources, biodiversity, and soil stability.
(3) The document will also stipulate the methodologies to be used for impact prediction and evaluation.
(4) Key stakeholders, including local communities in Aldmark or Grauby, whose input is required for the assessment, will be identified in the scoping document.

heading: Environmental Impact Statement (EIS)
text:
(1) If a full EIA is required, the applicant must prepare an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) in accordance with the scoping document.
(2) The EIS must provide a comprehensive analysis of the project's potential environmental impacts, including direct, indirect, and cumulative effects.
(3) It shall propose mitigation measures for all identified adverse impacts and outline a monitoring plan.
(4) The EIS must also consider reasonable alternatives to the proposed project, including a 'no project' alternative, and explain why the chosen option is preferred.

heading: Content of EIS
text:
(1) The EIS shall include a non-technical summary accessible to the general public.
(2) It must detail the project's characteristics, including its size, land use requirements, and production processes.
(3) A description of the existing environment likely to be affected, with baseline data collected over at least 12 months, is mandatory.
(4) The EIS must quantify, where possible, the predicted impacts, for example, a 15% increase in local traffic or a 5% reduction in air quality.

heading: Content of EIS
text:
(1) The EIS shall include a non-technical summary accessible to the general public, translated into at least two common regional languages if relevant to the project location, for example in Dunmere or Elsby.
(2) It must detail the project's characteristics, including its size, land use requirements, production processes, and resource consumption rates.
(3) A description of the existing environment likely to be affected, with baseline data collected over at least 18 months, is mandatory.
(4) The EIS must quantify, where possible, the predicted impacts, for example, a 20% increase in local traffic or a 7% reduction in air quality, with clear confidence intervals.

heading: Public Consultation on EIS
text:
(1) The competent authority shall make the EIS publicly available for a minimum of 45 days for consultation.
(2) Public notices announcing the availability of the EIS and inviting comments shall be published in at least two national newspapers and posted on the authority's website.
(3) Public meetings may be organized in affected municipalities, such as Corvik or Fennick, to gather feedback.
(4) All comments received during the consultation period must be considered by the competent authority before making a decision on the permit.

heading: Review of EIS
text:
(1) The competent authority, assisted by independent experts, shall review the EIS within 60 days of the close of the public consultation period.
(2) The review will assess the adequacy of the EIS in addressing all aspects of the scoping document and the accuracy of its impact predictions.
(3) The authority may request clarification or further information from the applicant during this review period.
(4) A review report, summarizing findings and recommendations, will be prepared and made publicly available.

heading: Decision on Permit Application
text:
(1) Based on the EIS, public comments, and review report, the competent authority shall make a decision on the permit application within 90 days.
(2) The decision can be to approve the permit, approve it with conditions, or reject it.
(3) A permit shall be rejected if the project's adverse environmental impacts cannot be adequately mitigated or if it poses an unacceptable risk to human health or the environment.
(4) The decision, along with reasons, shall be communicated in writing to the applicant and made publicly available for at least 30 days.

heading: Decision on Permit Application
text:
(1) Based on the EIS, public comments, and review report, the competent authority shall make a decision on the permit application within 120 days.
(2) The decision can be to approve the permit, approve it with specific and measurable conditions, or reject it entirely.
(3) A permit shall be rejected if the project's adverse environmental impacts cannot be adequately mitigated, if it poses an unacceptable risk to human health or the environment, or if it conflicts with existing environmental protection plans.
(4) The decision, along with detailed reasons, shall be communicated in writing to the applicant and made publicly available for at least 45 days, including a summary in a minimum of three local languages if applicable to the project site.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Approved permits may be subject to specific conditions designed to prevent, reduce, or offset adverse environmental impacts.
(2) Conditions may include requirements for specific construction methods, pollution control technologies, or habitat restoration measures.
(3) A bond or financial guarantee of at least 100,000 crowns may be required to ensure compliance with permit conditions.
(4) Non-compliance with permit conditions may lead to revocation of the permit and imposition of penalties.

heading: Validity of Permit
text:
(1) An Environmental Impact Assessment Permit is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of its issuance.
(2) If the project has not commenced within this 5-year period, the permit shall expire, and a new application must be submitted.
(3) A permit holder may apply for an extension of up to 2 years, provided that no significant changes to the project or the environmental conditions have occurred.
(4) The application for extension must be submitted at least 90 days before the original permit's expiry date, accompanied by a fee of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Validity of Permit
text:
(1) An Environmental Impact Assessment Permit is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of its issuance.
(2) If the project has not commenced within this 3-year period, the permit shall expire, and a new application must be submitted.
(3) A permit holder may apply for an extension of up to 1 year, provided that no significant changes to the project or the environmental conditions have occurred.
(4) The application for extension must be submitted at least 120 days before the original permit's expiry date, accompanied by a fee of 4,000 crowns and an updated environmental review.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting
text:
(1) The permit holder is responsible for monitoring the environmental impacts of the project throughout its construction and operational phases.
(2) Monitoring reports must be submitted to the competent authority annually, detailing compliance with permit conditions and the effectiveness of mitigation measures.
(3) The authority may conduct unannounced site inspections to verify monitoring data and compliance.
(4) Any significant unforeseen environmental impacts must be reported to the competent authority within 48 hours of discovery.

heading: Post-Construction Audit
text:
(1) Within 6 months of project completion, a post-construction environmental audit must be conducted by an independent third party.
(2) The audit shall assess the actual environmental impacts against the predictions made in the EIS and evaluate the effectiveness of implemented mitigation measures.
(3) The audit report must be submitted to the competent authority and made publicly available.
(4) If the audit reveals significant unmitigated impacts, the permit holder may be required to implement additional remedial measures, with a maximum cost of 250,000 crowns.

heading: Environmental Management Plan
text:
(1) For all projects requiring a full EIA, an Environmental Management Plan (EMP) must be developed and approved by the competent authority.
(2) The EMP shall detail the specific actions, responsibilities, and timelines for implementing mitigation measures and monitoring programs.
(3) It must include emergency response procedures for potential environmental incidents.
(4) The EMP shall be a living document, subject to review and updates every 2 years or upon significant changes to project operations.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) Information submitted as part of an EIA application is generally public, except for commercially sensitive data.
(2) An applicant may request certain information to be treated as confidential, provided that the request is justified and the information does not pertain to environmental risks.
(3) The competent authority shall review such requests within 15 days and make a decision.
(4) Information relating to potential adverse environmental impacts or public health must never be kept confidential.

heading: Access to Information
text:
(1) All non-confidential documents related to EIA permits, including applications, EIS, and decisions, shall be publicly accessible.
(2) Copies of these documents can be obtained from the competent authority upon payment of a reasonable administrative fee, not exceeding 50 crowns per document.
(3) Electronic versions of key documents will be available on the authority's website within 7 days of their official release.
(4) The public has the right to inspect physical copies of documents at the authority's offices during regular business hours, free of charge.

heading: Data Protection
text:
(1) Personal data collected during the application and review process shall be handled in accordance with general data protection principles.
(2) Such data shall only be used for the purposes of this Act and shall not be disclosed to third parties without consent, except as required by law.
(3) Data will be retained for a minimum of 10 years after project completion.
(4) Individuals have the right to access and correct their personal data held by the competent authority.

heading: Competent Authority Powers
text:
(1) The competent authority has the power to issue stop-work orders for projects proceeding without a required permit or in violation of permit conditions.
(2) It may require additional studies or data collection from the applicant at any stage of the EIA process.
(3) The authority can revise permit conditions if new environmental information comes to light that indicates a greater risk than initially assessed.
(4) It has the power to impose administrative fines for non-compliance, up to 100,000 crowns per violation.

heading: Competent Authority Powers
text:
(1) The competent authority has the power to issue immediate stop-work orders for projects proceeding without a required permit or in flagrant violation of permit conditions.
(2) It may require additional studies or data collection from the applicant at any stage of the EIA process, at the applicant's expense.
(3) The authority can revise permit conditions if new environmental information comes to light that indicates a greater risk than initially assessed, or if monitoring reports show insufficient mitigation.
(4) It has the power to impose administrative fines for non-compliance, up to 200,000 crowns per violation per week of non-compliance, with a maximum total fine of 2,000,000 crowns for severe and prolonged breaches.

heading: Enforcement Actions
text:
(1) If a project is found to be in non-compliance with this Act or its permit conditions, the competent authority shall issue a written notice to the permit holder.
(2) The notice shall specify the nature of the non-compliance and set a reasonable period, not exceeding 30 days, for rectification.
(3) If the non-compliance is not rectified within the specified period, the authority may impose fines, suspend the permit, or issue a mandatory clean-up order.
(4) In cases of severe environmental damage, the authority may initiate legal proceedings to recover costs and impose further penalties.

heading: Collaboration with Other Authorities
text:
(1) The competent authority shall collaborate with other relevant national and municipal authorities, such as those in Brenholt or Lund Vale, to ensure integrated environmental protection.
(2) Other authorities are required to provide information and expertise to the competent authority upon request, within 20 days.
(3) Joint reviews of projects may be undertaken where there are overlapping jurisdictional responsibilities.
(4) Memoranda of Understanding may be established to formalize cooperation procedures and information sharing protocols.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Parliament of Nordvale every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The first review shall take place no later than 2023.
(3) Public input shall be sought as part of the review process, including consultations with environmental organizations and industry representatives.
(4) Amendments to the Act may be proposed following each review, aiming to improve environmental outcomes and streamline administrative processes.

heading: Financial Provisions
text:
(1) All fees collected under this Act shall be deposited into a dedicated Environmental Protection Fund.
(2) The fund shall be used exclusively for the administration of this Act, environmental research, and monitoring activities.
(3) An annual budget for the competent authority, not exceeding 20,000,000 crowns, shall be approved by Parliament.
(4) The competent authority shall submit an annual financial report detailing expenditures from the fund.

heading: Financial Provisions
text:
(1) All fees collected under this Act shall be deposited into a dedicated Environmental Protection Fund.
(2) The fund shall be used exclusively for the administration of this Act, environmental research, monitoring activities, and ecological restoration projects.
(3) An annual budget for the competent authority, not exceeding 25,000,000 crowns, shall be approved by Parliament and subject to quarterly review.
(4) The competent authority shall submit an annual financial report detailing expenditures from the fund, audited by an independent firm.

heading: Capacity Building
text:
(1) The competent authority shall provide training and guidance to municipal staff and project proponents on EIA procedures.
(2) A budget of at least 500,000 crowns per year shall be allocated for capacity building initiatives.
(3) This includes the development of best practice guides and the organization of workshops in various municipalities.
(4) The authority may also support academic research into improved EIA methodologies, with grants up to 100,000 crowns per project.

heading: Scientific Advisory Committee
text:
(1) A Scientific Advisory Committee comprising 7 independent experts shall be established to provide technical advice to the competent authority.
(2) Committee members shall have expertise in fields such as ecology, hydrology, geology, and environmental engineering.
(3) The committee shall meet at least quarterly and submit an annual report to the competent authority.
(4) Members shall be appointed for 3-year terms and may be reappointed once.

heading: Guidelines and Standards
text:
(1) The competent authority shall publish detailed guidelines for the preparation of Environmental Impact Statements.
(2) These guidelines shall be updated at least every 3 years to reflect advances in scientific knowledge and best practices.
(3) Environmental quality standards for air, water, and soil, consistent with international norms, shall be established and regularly reviewed.
(4) Adherence to these guidelines and standards is mandatory for all projects subject to this Act.

heading: Regional Environmental Plans
text:
(1) The competent authority shall develop regional environmental plans for each of Nordvale's administrative regions, including the areas around Dunmere and Elsby.
(2) These plans shall identify sensitive ecosystems, critical habitats, and areas suitable for industrial development.
(3) Project proposals must be consistent with the objectives and spatial designations of the relevant regional environmental plan.
(4) Regional plans shall be reviewed and updated every 10 years, with public participation.

heading: Cumulative Impacts
text:
(1) The assessment of environmental impacts shall consider cumulative effects resulting from the proposed project in conjunction with other existing or approved projects.
(2) Applicants must provide information on other projects within a 5-kilometer radius that may contribute to cumulative impacts.
(3) The competent authority may require a regional cumulative impact assessment if multiple projects are concentrated in a specific area, like the industrial zone of Aldmark.
(4) Where cumulative impacts are significant, a project may be rejected even if its individual impact is deemed acceptable.

heading: Strategic Environmental Assessment
text:
(1) Major plans and programs at the national or regional level, such as land-use plans or infrastructure development strategies, shall undergo a Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA).
(2) An SEA shall evaluate the environmental implications of such plans before they are adopted.
(3) The findings of an SEA must be integrated into the decision-making process for the plan or program.
(4) Guidelines for conducting SEAs shall be published by the competent authority within 2 years of this Act coming into force.

heading: Environmental Liability
text:
(1) Any person or entity causing environmental damage through activities related to a project shall be held liable for remediation costs.
(2) Liability extends to both direct and indirect damages, including harm to natural resources and ecosystems.
(3) The polluter pays principle shall apply, requiring the responsible party to bear the costs of prevention and remediation.
(4) Insurance coverage of at least 500,000 crowns for environmental liability may be mandated for high-risk projects.

heading: Remediation and Restoration
text:
(1) In cases of environmental damage, the permit holder or responsible party shall be required to undertake remediation and restoration measures.
(2) A remediation plan, approved by the competent authority, must be submitted within 60 days of the damage being identified.
(3) The goal of restoration is to return the affected environment to its pre-damage condition or, where not feasible, to an equivalent ecological state.
(4) Failure to implement an approved remediation plan may result in the authority undertaking the work and recovering all costs plus a 20% administrative fee from the responsible party.

heading: Offsets and Compensation
text:
(1) Where significant residual adverse impacts remain after all feasible mitigation and remediation, environmental offsets or compensation may be required.
(2) Offsets must be ecologically equivalent and located within the same biogeographical region, for example, within the Lund Vale region.
(3) The value of the offset or compensation must be at least 1.5 times the estimated value of the residual impact.
(4) Compensation may take the form of financial contributions to environmental protection projects or direct land acquisition for conservation, with a minimum value of 250,000 crowns.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Projects that commenced before the effective date of this Act are not required to obtain a permit, provided they have all other necessary approvals.
(2) However, significant expansions or modifications to such projects after this date will fall under the purview of this Act.
(3) Any EIA applications already submitted and undergoing review at the time of this Act's commencement shall continue under the previous regulations, but the competent authority may request additional information to meet new standards.
(4) This section expires on 2028-12-31.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Projects that commenced before the effective date of this Act are not required to obtain a permit, provided they have all other necessary approvals.
(2) However, any expansion or modification exceeding 10% of the original project's footprint or capacity after this date will fall under the purview of this Act.
(3) Any EIA applications already submitted and undergoing review at the time of this Act's commencement shall continue under the previous regulations, but the competent authority may request additional information to meet new standards, especially concerning biodiversity impacts.
(4) This section expires on 2028-12-31.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: The Environmental Review Act of 1995 (Act No. 12/1995) is hereby repealed. Any regulations or decrees issued under the repealed Act shall remain in force to the extent that they are consistent with this Act, until new regulations are promulgated. This repeal does not affect any rights or obligations that accrued under the previous legislation prior to the effective date of this Act.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The competent authority may issue regulations for the effective implementation of this Act.
(2) Such regulations may specify detailed procedures for application, review, public consultation, and monitoring.
(3) Regulations must be published for public comment for a minimum of 30 days before their final adoption.
(4) All regulations shall be consistent with the principles and provisions of this Act.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity that commences a project requiring a permit without first obtaining one commits an offence.
(2) Any person or entity that provides false or misleading information in an application or EIS commits an offence.
(3) Penalties for offences under this Act may include fines up to 250,000 crowns, imprisonment for up to 6 months, or both.
(4) Repeat offenders may face doubled fines and longer periods of imprisonment, up to 1 year.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity that commences a project requiring a permit without first obtaining one commits an offence, punishable by an immediate fine of 300,000 crowns.
(2) Any person or entity that provides false or misleading information in an application or EIS commits an offence, and may be barred from submitting future applications for 5 years.
(3) Penalties for offences under this Act may include fines up to 500,000 crowns, imprisonment for up to 1 year, or both.
(4) Repeat offenders may face tripled fines and imprisonment for up to 2 years, along with forfeiture of any profits derived from the illegal activity.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant may appeal a decision of the competent authority to the Environmental Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) Appeals can relate to the requirement for an EIA, the conditions of a permit, or the rejection of a permit application.
(3) The Tribunal shall review the appeal and issue a decision within 90 days.
(4) The decision of the Environmental Appeals Tribunal is final, subject only to judicial review on points of law.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, the competent authority may levy charges for specific services, such as expedited reviews or additional site visits.
(2) These charges shall be based on the actual cost of providing the service and shall not exceed 10,000 crowns for any single service.
(3) A schedule of all fees and charges shall be published annually and made publicly available.
(4) Fees are non-refundable once the service has been initiated.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, the competent authority may levy charges for specific services, such as expedited reviews, additional site visits, or specialized expert consultations.
(2) These charges shall be based on the actual cost of providing the service and shall not exceed 15,000 crowns for any single service, with a total maximum of 50,000 crowns for a project.
(3) A detailed schedule of all fees and charges shall be published annually and made publicly available in print and electronic formats.
(4) Fees are non-refundable once the service has been initiated, and any outstanding fees must be paid before a permit can be issued.

heading: Declaration of Environmentally Sensitive Areas
text:
(1) The Parliament may, by decree, declare specific geographical areas as 'Environmentally Sensitive Areas' (ESAs).
(2) Projects within ESAs are subject to stricter EIA requirements and may face more stringent permit conditions.
(3) The declaration of an ESA shall be based on scientific criteria, such as high biodiversity, unique ecosystems, or critical water sources.
(4) Public consultation for 60 days shall precede any formal declaration of an ESA.

heading: International Cooperation
text:
(1) The competent authority shall cooperate with environmental agencies of neighboring countries on transboundary environmental impact assessments.
(2) This includes sharing information and coordinating assessment procedures for projects with potential cross-border effects.
(3) Nordvale shall adhere to international agreements concerning environmental impact assessment and transboundary pollution.
(4) A budget of 1,000,000 crowns annually is allocated for international cooperation activities related to environmental protection.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on 2018-01-01.

heading: Short Title
text: This Act may be cited as the Environmental Impact Assessment Permit Act.

heading: Annual Environmental Report
text:
(1) The competent authority shall prepare and publish an Annual Environmental Report by March 31st of each year.
(2) The report shall detail the state of the environment in Nordvale, the number of EIA permits issued, and key environmental trends.
(3) It shall also include a summary of enforcement actions taken and the financial performance of the Environmental Protection Fund.
(4) The report will be presented to Parliament and made widely available to the public.

heading: Annual Environmental Report
text:
(1) The competent authority shall prepare and publish an Annual Environmental Report by February 28th of each year.
(2) The report shall detail the state of the environment in Nordvale, the number of EIA permits issued and refused, and key environmental trends, including specific data for each municipality.
(3) It shall also include a summary of enforcement actions taken, the financial performance of the Environmental Protection Fund, and a forecast for the upcoming year.
(4) The report will be presented to Parliament, including a public hearing, and made widely available to the public in both print and accessible digital formats.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text:
(1) A permit may be revoked by the competent authority if there is a serious breach of permit conditions or if the information provided in the application was materially false.
(2) Before revocation, the permit holder shall be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to be heard.
(3) Revocation decisions can be appealed to the Environmental Appeals Tribunal within 15 days.
(4) If a permit is revoked, all project activities must cease immediately, and the site must be remediated at the permit holder's expense.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In the event of an imminent threat to public health or the environment, the competent authority may exercise emergency powers to suspend or modify project activities without prior notice.
(2) Such emergency measures shall be temporary and shall not extend beyond 30 days unless formally ratified by an executive order.
(3) The permit holder must be notified immediately of any emergency action taken.
(4) The costs incurred due to emergency measures, if caused by the project, shall be borne by the permit holder.

heading: Review of Project Changes
text:
(1) Any proposed significant changes to a permitted project must be submitted to the competent authority for review.
(2) A 'significant change' is defined as any alteration increasing the project's footprint by more than 5% or its environmental impact by more than 10%.
(3) The authority will determine whether a new EIA or a permit amendment is required within 45 days.
(4) Failure to report significant changes may result in revocation of the permit.

heading: Review of Project Changes
text:
(1) Any proposed changes to a permitted project that affect its environmental impact must be submitted to the competent authority for review.
(2) A 'significant change' is defined as any alteration increasing the project's footprint by more than 2% or its environmental impact by more than 5%, or any change introducing new types of hazardous materials.
(3) The authority will determine whether a new EIA or a permit amendment is required within 60 days, and may require public consultation for major changes.
(4) Failure to report significant changes may result in revocation of the permit and substantial fines, up to 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Protection of Whistleblowers
text:
(1) Individuals who report potential violations of this Act in good faith shall be protected from retaliation.
(2) Employers are prohibited from taking adverse action against employees who report environmental concerns to the competent authority.
(3) Confidentiality of whistleblowers shall be maintained to the greatest extent possible, consistent with legal requirements.
(4) Any act of retaliation against a whistleblower may result in fines up to 50,000 crowns for the perpetrator.

heading: Incentives for Green Technology
text:
(1) Projects that incorporate certified green technologies or achieve environmental performance significantly beyond minimum requirements may receive preferential treatment.
(2) This could include reduced application fees by up to 25% or expedited review processes, shortening the review period by 15 days.
(3) The competent authority shall publish criteria for qualifying green technologies and superior environmental performance.
(4) Eligibility for incentives is reviewed on a case-by-case basis, with a maximum incentive value of 250,000 crowns.

heading: Incentives for Green Technology
text:
(1) Projects that incorporate certified green technologies or achieve environmental performance significantly beyond minimum requirements may receive preferential treatment.
(2) This could include reduced application fees by up to 50% or expedited review processes, shortening the review period by 30 days.
(3) The competent authority shall publish updated criteria annually for qualifying green technologies and superior environmental performance, emphasizing carbon reduction.
(4) Eligibility for incentives is reviewed on a case-by-case basis, with a maximum incentive value of 500,000 crowns, and an additional 100,000 crowns for projects in less developed municipalities like Fennick or Grauby.

heading: Exemptions
text: For a certified avalanche observer, the re-inspection fee of 90 crowns, normally due when a re-inspection takes place after failing an inspection, shall not be charged.

heading: Concessions
text: The housing allowance is reduced by 25 percent for any household that includes a registered herbalist.

heading: Particular persons
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person who is a registered certified falconry instructor for at least one year shall receive rent support of 300 crowns per month.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates noise that is made by events, building work and machines in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to protect the rest of residents while allowing reasonable activity.
(3) A municipality may issue the permits described in this Act.
(4) A permit under this Act is needed in addition to any event permit required by another Act.

heading: Quiet hours
text:
(1) Quiet hours in Nordvale run from 22:00 to 07:00 on every day.
(2) During quiet hours no person may make noise that can be heard inside a neighbouring dwelling, except as allowed by a permit under this Act.

heading: Quiet hours
text:
(1) Quiet hours in Nordvale run from 23:00 to 07:00 on every day.
(2) During quiet hours no person may make noise that can be heard inside a neighbouring dwelling, except as allowed by a permit under this Act.

heading: Maximum noise level by day
text: Between 07:00 and 22:00 the noise measured at the boundary of a residential plot may not exceed 55 decibels. A higher level is allowed only with a permit under section 5.

heading: Maximum noise level at night
text: Between 22:00 and 07:00 the noise measured at the boundary of a residential plot may not exceed 40 decibels. A higher level is allowed only with a permit under section 6.

heading: Daytime event permit
text:
(1) A permit for an event with noise of up to 70 decibels between 07:00 and 22:00 costs 30 crowns.
(2) The application must be submitted at least 7 days before the event.

heading: Daytime event permit
text:
(1) A permit for an event with noise of up to 70 decibels between 07:00 and 22:00 costs 40 crowns.
(2) The application must be submitted at least 7 days before the event.

heading: Night event permit
text:
(1) A permit for an event with noise of up to 60 decibels during quiet hours costs 90 crowns.
(2) The application must be submitted at least 14 days before the event.
(3) A night permit is valid for one night only.

heading: Building work hours
text: Building work that makes noise may take place on working days between 07:00 and 18:00 and on Saturdays between 09:00 and 15:00. It may not take place on Sundays or on public holidays.

heading: Emergency building work
text: Urgent repair work needed to prevent danger to people or property may be carried out at any time without a permit, even during quiet hours. The person doing the work must tell the municipality within 2 working days.

heading: Garden machine hours
text: Lawn mowers, hedge trimmers and similar garden machines may be used between 08:00 and 20:00 on working days and between 10:00 and 18:00 on Sundays and public holidays. Machines with a noise level above 80 decibels may not be used on Sundays.

heading: Leaf blower ban
text: The use of petrol-powered leaf blowers is forbidden in residential zones, and the ban applies to private gardens as well as public land. Electric leaf blowers are allowed only during the hours in section 9.

heading: Leaf blower ban
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Music in public places
text:
(1) Amplified music in a public place needs a permit under section 5 or section 6.
(2) A street musician with no amplifier needs no permit under this Act but must not play in the same spot for more than 2 hours.

heading: Noise from restaurants and bars
text: A restaurant or bar with outdoor seating must keep its noise below 60 decibels at the boundary of the nearest residential plot after 22:00, and must close its outdoor area by midnight on every day of the week.

heading: Noise from restaurants and bars
text: A restaurant or bar with outdoor seating must keep its noise below 60 decibels at the boundary of the nearest residential plot after 22:00, and must close its outdoor area by 23:30.

heading: Fireworks permit
text:
(1) A permit to set off fireworks costs 50 crowns.
(2) Fireworks may be set off only between 18:00 and 23:00.
(3) The application must be submitted at least 10 days before the display.

heading: Noise measurement
text: A municipal inspector measures noise with a certified meter. A measurement counts only if it is taken for at least 5 minutes and is repeated twice with a gap of at least 10 minutes.

heading: Warning before penalty
text: A person who breaks this Act for the first time in a calendar year receives a written warning. A person who breaks it again in the same calendar year must pay a penalty under section 16.

heading: Penalty for noise offences
text:
(1) The penalty for a noise offence is 100 crowns.
(2) The penalty for a noise offence during quiet hours is 150 crowns.
(3) The penalty is paid to the municipality.

heading: Penalty for noise offences
text:
(1) The penalty for a noise offence is 120 crowns.
(2) The penalty for a noise offence during quiet hours is 180 crowns.
(3) The penalty is paid to the municipality.

heading: Complaints
text: A resident may complain to the municipality about noise, in writing or by telephone. The municipality must reply within 14 days and must send an inspector within 3 days if the complaint concerns quiet hours.

heading: Appeals
text: A decision on a noise permit or penalty may be appealed within 14 days of the day it is delivered. The appeal is free of charge and may be written on a simple form.

heading: Permit for industrial machines
text:
(1) A business that runs machines above 70 decibels at its boundary needs an annual noise permit.
(2) The annual permit costs 200 crowns.
(3) The permit must be renewed every year.

heading: Reports to the Ministry
text: Each municipality must send the Ministry a yearly report by 31 March, stating how many noise permits it issued and how many penalties it charged in the previous calendar year.

heading: Reports to the Ministry
text: Each municipality must send the Ministry a yearly report by 28 February, stating how many noise permits it issued and how many penalties it charged in the previous calendar year.

heading: Theory test fee for young apprentices
text:
(1) A registered apprentice who is under 25 years of age on the day the theory test is booked pays 25 crowns for the theory test for a driving licence.
(2) A retake of the theory test is charged at the same reduced fee.

heading: Theory test fee for young apprentices
text:
(1) A registered apprentice who is under 25 years of age on the day the theory test is booked pays 20 crowns for the theory test for a driving licence.
(2) A retake of the theory test is charged at the same reduced fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the registration and regulation of non-profit associations throughout Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure transparency, accountability, and the proper functioning of such organizations. All associations operating for non-profit purposes within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale must comply with the provisions of this Act to gain and maintain legal recognition. This includes any group of 3 or more individuals who gather for a common non-commercial objective.

heading: Definition of Non-Profit Association
text: A non-profit association is defined as a voluntary organization formed for a purpose other than generating profit for its members. Its primary activities must be directed towards social, cultural, educational, charitable, or other public benefit objectives. Any surplus funds generated by the association must be reinvested into its stated objectives and not distributed to its members. The association must have at least 5 founding members, each at least 18 years of age, to be considered eligible for registration.

heading: Registration Authority
text: The Non-Profit Association Registry (hereafter 'the Registry'), operating under the national administration, is responsible for managing all aspects of association registration. This includes receiving applications, maintaining the public register, and issuing registration certificates. The Registry's main office is located in Aldmark, with satellite offices in Brenholt and Corvik to assist applicants from those regions. All official correspondence with associations will be conducted by the Registry.

heading: Application for Registration
text: An application for registration must be submitted to the Registry within 30 days of the association's formation. The application must include the association's name, its founding purpose, a list of its initial board members, and its proposed articles of association. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned within 10 business days for rectification.

heading: Application for Registration
text: An application for registration must be submitted to the Registry within 45 days of the association's formation. The application must include the association's name, its founding purpose, a list of its initial board members, and its proposed articles of association. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned within 7 business days for rectification, and a 100 crown re-submission fee may apply.

heading: Articles of Association
text: The articles of association must clearly state the association's name, its registered address, its objectives, membership criteria, and procedures for amending the articles. They must also detail the composition and responsibilities of the governing body, financial management practices, and dissolution procedures. At least 7 clauses must be dedicated to ensuring democratic internal processes, such as voting rights and meeting protocols. A template is available from the Registry.

heading: Minimum Membership
text: Every non-profit association must maintain a minimum of 5 active members at all times. Should membership fall below this threshold for a period exceeding 60 consecutive days, the association must notify the Registry. Failure to restore the minimum membership within a further 90 days may result in the revocation of its registration. New members must be formally accepted by the governing body according to the association's articles.

heading: Minimum Membership
text: Every non-profit association must maintain a minimum of 7 active members at all times. Should membership fall below this threshold for a period exceeding 45 consecutive days, the association must notify the Registry. Failure to restore the minimum membership within a further 75 days may result in the revocation of its registration. New members must be formally accepted by the governing body according to the association's articles, and their details recorded within 14 days of acceptance.

heading: Association Name
text: The proposed name of the association must not be misleading or identical to an already registered association. It must clearly indicate its non-profit nature if not otherwise apparent from its objectives. The Registry reserves the right to reject names deemed offensive or inappropriate. Names containing more than 30 characters may require special approval. A preliminary name check can be performed online through the Registry's portal.

heading: Review of Application
text: The Registry will review complete applications within 20 business days of receipt. During this period, the Registry may request additional information or clarification from the applicants. If the application meets all requirements of this Act and its regulations, the association will be registered. If deficiencies are found, the applicants will be notified and given 15 business days to make the necessary corrections. A second review will then be conducted within 10 business days.

heading: Review of Application
text: The Registry will review complete applications within 15 business days of receipt. During this period, the Registry may request additional information or clarification from the applicants. If the application meets all requirements of this Act and its regulations, the association will be registered. If deficiencies are found, the applicants will be notified and given 10 business days to make the necessary corrections. A second review will then be conducted within 7 business days.

heading: Issuance of Certificate
text: Upon successful registration, the Registry will issue a Certificate of Registration to the association. This certificate will include the association's unique registration number, its official name, and the date of registration. The certificate serves as legal proof of the association's registered status. A digital copy will be made available, and a physical copy will be mailed to the registered address within 5 business days.

heading: Public Register
text: The Registry will maintain a public register of all registered non-profit associations. This register will be accessible to the public both online and at the Registry's main office during business hours. It will contain the association's name, registration number, registered address, and primary objectives. Personal details of members or board members will not be publicly displayed, respecting privacy laws and regulations.

heading: Annual Reporting Requirements
text: Every registered association must submit an annual report to the Registry by March 31st of each year. This report must include a summary of its activities, a list of current board members, and a financial statement covering the preceding calendar year. The financial statement must clearly show all income and expenditure, and confirm that no profits were distributed to members. A late submission fee of 200 crowns applies after the deadline.

heading: Annual Reporting Requirements
text: Every registered association must submit an annual report to the Registry by February 28th of each year. This report must include a summary of its activities, a list of current board members, and a financial statement covering the preceding calendar year. The financial statement must clearly show all income and expenditure, and confirm that no profits were distributed to members. A late submission fee of 350 crowns applies after the deadline, with an additional 50 crowns for every month thereafter.

heading: Financial Records
text: Associations must maintain accurate and complete financial records for a minimum of 5 years. These records must be made available for inspection by the Registry upon request with at least 14 days' notice. All transactions exceeding 1,000 crowns must be properly documented with receipts or invoices. Failure to maintain adequate financial records may lead to penalties or revocation of registration.

heading: Changes to Association Details
text: Any changes to the association's name, registered address, or articles of association must be reported to the Registry within 30 days of the change. Changes to the board of directors must be reported within 60 days. A nominal fee of 150 crowns applies for each reported change, except for changes of board members which incur no fee. Supporting documentation, such as meeting minutes, may be required.

heading: Changes to Association Details
text: Any changes to the association's name, registered address, or articles of association must be reported to the Registry within 20 days of the change. Changes to the board of directors must be reported within 45 days. A nominal fee of 200 crowns applies for each reported change, including changes of board members. Supporting documentation, such as certified meeting minutes, must be provided for all changes.

heading: Amendment of Articles
text: Amendments to the articles of association must be approved by a special resolution of the association's members, requiring at least a two-thirds majority vote. The amended articles, along with the minutes of the meeting where the amendment was approved, must be submitted to the Registry within 30 days of the resolution. The Registry will review the amendments to ensure compliance with this Act.

heading: Registered Address
text: Every registered association must maintain a physical registered address within Nordvale. This address must be a location where official correspondence can be received and where records may be inspected. A post office box is not acceptable as a registered address. Any change of registered address must be reported to the Registry as per section 13. The Registry may conduct random checks to verify registered addresses.

heading: Governing Body
text: Each association must have a governing body (e.g., a board of directors or committee) responsible for its management and operations. This body must consist of at least 3 members, all of whom must be at least 18 years of age. Members of the governing body are fiduciaries and must act in the best interests of the association. No more than 50% of the governing body can be related by blood or marriage.

heading: Meetings of Members
text: Associations must hold at least one general meeting of members annually. Notice of such meetings must be given to all members at least 14 days in advance. The annual general meeting must include the presentation of the annual report and financial statement, and the election of the governing body. Minutes of all general meetings must be kept and made available to members upon request.

heading: Dissolution of Association
text: An association may be voluntarily dissolved by a special resolution of its members, requiring a three-quarters majority vote. Notice of the proposed dissolution must be given to the Registry within 7 days of the resolution. The association must then submit a final financial report and a plan for the distribution of any remaining assets. Assets must be transferred to another registered non-profit organization with similar objectives.

heading: Involuntary Dissolution
text: The Registry may initiate involuntary dissolution proceedings if an association fails to comply with key provisions of this Act, such as persistent failure to submit annual reports, maintain minimum membership, or adhere to its stated non-profit objectives. Before initiating dissolution, the Registry will issue a warning and allow the association 90 days to rectify the non-compliance. If rectification is not achieved, a formal dissolution order will be issued.

heading: Involuntary Dissolution
text: The Registry may initiate involuntary dissolution proceedings if an association fails to comply with key provisions of this Act, such as persistent failure to submit annual reports, maintain minimum membership, or adhere to its stated non-profit objectives. Before initiating dissolution, the Registry will issue a warning and allow the association 60 days to rectify the non-compliance. If rectification is not achieved, a formal dissolution order will be issued, and the association will be removed from the public register within 30 days.

heading: Distribution of Assets upon Dissolution
text: Upon dissolution, any remaining assets of the association, after settling all debts and liabilities, must be transferred to another registered non-profit association or a public benefit entity within Nordvale. Under no circumstances may assets be distributed among the association's members. The distribution plan must be approved by the Registry. Any assets not distributed within 180 days will be transferred to a national public fund.

heading: Obligation to Inform
text: Associations have an ongoing obligation to inform the Registry of any significant changes that may affect their non-profit status or ability to comply with this Act. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in primary objectives or cessation of core activities. Such notifications must be made within 30 days of the change. Failure to inform the Registry may result in penalties as outlined in section 27.

heading: Use of Funds
text: All funds generated or received by a non-profit association must be used exclusively for the pursuit of its stated objectives. Funds may not be used for personal gain by members or for any commercial activities unrelated to the association's purpose. Reasonable administrative costs, not exceeding 25% of annual expenditure, are permitted. Any single expenditure over 5,000 crowns must be approved by at least two board members.

heading: Use of Funds
text: All funds generated or received by a non-profit association must be used exclusively for the pursuit of its stated objectives. Funds may not be used for personal gain by members or for any commercial activities unrelated to the association's purpose. Reasonable administrative costs, not exceeding 20% of annual expenditure, are permitted. Any single expenditure over 3,000 crowns must be approved by at least two board members, and documented with clear justification.

heading: Transparency and Accountability
text: Associations must operate with a high degree of transparency and accountability. Members should have reasonable access to financial records and meeting minutes. The governing body is responsible for ensuring that the association's activities align with its stated objectives and that all legal requirements are met. An internal audit of financial records should be conducted at least every 3 years for associations with annual incomes exceeding 50,000 crowns.

heading: Right to Appeal
text: An association or prospective association has the right to appeal any decision made by the Registry regarding its registration, revocation, or any imposed penalty. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the Registry's decision. The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.

heading: Fees for Services
text: The Registry may levy reasonable fees for specific services, such as issuing duplicate certificates, providing certified copies of documents, or processing late submissions. A schedule of fees will be published on the Registry's official website and updated annually. Fees will not exceed the administrative cost of providing the service, plus a 10% administrative surcharge. All fees are payable in crowns.

heading: Fees for Services
text: The Registry may levy reasonable fees for specific services, such as issuing duplicate certificates, providing certified copies of documents, or processing late submissions. A schedule of fees will be published on the Registry's official website and updated semi-annually. Fees will not exceed the administrative cost of providing the service, plus a 15% administrative surcharge. All fees are payable in crowns, and electronic payment options will be made available.

heading: Inspections and Audits
text: The Registry has the authority to conduct inspections or audits of registered associations to ensure compliance with this Act. Such inspections may be conducted with 14 days' prior notice, or without notice if there is reasonable suspicion of serious non-compliance. Associations must cooperate fully with Registry officials during inspections, providing access to records and relevant personnel. Refusal to cooperate may lead to penalties.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Failure to comply with the provisions of this Act may result in penalties, including fines ranging from 1,000 crowns to 10,000 crowns, suspension of registration, or revocation of registration. The severity of the penalty will depend on the nature and extent of the non-compliance. Repeated offenses may lead to higher fines or immediate revocation. A formal warning will generally precede any fine exceeding 5,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Failure to comply with the provisions of this Act may result in penalties, including fines ranging from 2,000 crowns to 20,000 crowns, suspension of registration for up to 6 months, or revocation of registration. The severity of the penalty will depend on the nature and extent of the non-compliance. Repeated offenses may lead to higher fines or immediate revocation. A formal warning will generally precede any fine exceeding 7,500 crowns, allowing 30 days for rectification.

heading: Offenses by Individuals
text: Individuals found to be deliberately misrepresenting an association's activities or finances, or intentionally defrauding the Registry or the public under the guise of a non-profit association, may face personal fines up to 50,000 crowns. Such individuals may also be barred from serving on the governing body of any registered association for a period of 5 years. These actions are distinct from penalties imposed on the association itself.

heading: Reporting Suspected Violations
text: Any person may report suspected violations of this Act by a registered association to the Registry. Reports should be made in writing and should include all available evidence. The Registry will investigate all credible reports. The identity of the reporter will be kept confidential to the extent permitted by law, unless the report is found to be malicious or without basis. Anonymous reports will be considered if sufficient detail is provided.

heading: Registry's Power to Request Information
text: The Registry may, at any time, request additional information or documentation from a registered association to verify compliance with this Act. Such requests must be made in writing and specify a reasonable timeframe for response, typically between 14 and 30 days. Failure to provide the requested information within the specified timeframe without valid justification may be considered non-compliance and subject to penalties under section 27.

heading: Exemptions
text: Certain very small, informal groups with annual income below 10,000 crowns and fewer than 10 members may apply for an exemption from full registration requirements. Such groups must still notify the Registry of their existence and purpose. The Registry will assess each application for exemption on a case-by-case basis. Exempted groups are still subject to general principles of non-profit conduct and transparency.

heading: Cooperation with Other Authorities
text: The Registry may cooperate with other national administrative bodies to ensure effective oversight of non-profit associations. This includes sharing relevant information, where legally permissible, to prevent fraud or misuse of funds. Such cooperation will always adhere to national data protection and privacy regulations. Cross-referencing of financial data may occur for associations with annual revenues exceeding 100,000 crowns.

heading: Regulations
text: The national administration may issue regulations to provide further detail and guidance on the implementation of this Act. These regulations will cover aspects such as specific forms for applications, detailed reporting formats, and procedures for inspections. All regulations will be published publicly and come into effect 30 days after their official publication. A public consultation period of 60 days will precede the finalization of new regulations.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Associations established prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for registration within 180 days of the Act coming into force. During this transitional period, existing associations are considered provisionally compliant, provided they submit their application within the stipulated timeframe. A reduced application fee of 250 crowns applies to all pre-existing associations registering within the first 90 days.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions apply from this date unless otherwise specified in subsequent amendments. The Registry will begin accepting applications for registration starting on this effective date. Information campaigns will be launched in all municipalities, including Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, 60 days prior to the effective date to ensure widespread awareness.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A licensed balloon pilot is exempt from the fee or allowance in FDA §14.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a registered lacemaker, the fee for a temporary sign permit under SBA §17(1) is reduced by half.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the mandatory inspection of drainage systems within all municipalities of the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the functional integrity, efficiency, and environmental safety of these critical infrastructure components. The scope encompasses all main and secondary drainage pipelines, culverts, pumping stations, and associated infrastructure managed by municipal authorities. Adherence to the provisions outlined herein is essential for public health, flood prevention, and the long-term sustainability of urban and rural development across Nordvale. This Act does not apply to private household drainage connections or agricultural field drainage systems, which fall under separate regulations.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Drainage system" means any network of pipes, channels, culverts, or other structures designed to collect and convey stormwater or wastewater from an area to a discharge point, owned or operated by a municipality.
(b) "Inspection" means a systematic examination of a drainage system, including visual assessments, structural integrity checks, and flow capacity evaluations, conducted by a qualified inspector.
(c) "Municipality" refers to any of the administrative divisions of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(d) "Minister" means the Minister responsible for infrastructure development.

heading: Inspection frequency for main pipelines
text: All main drainage pipelines within a municipality, defined as pipelines with an internal diameter exceeding 600 millimeters or serving more than 500 residential units, must undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 5 years. This inspection must assess structural integrity, presence of blockages, and overall hydraulic performance. Records of these inspections, including detailed reports and any identified deficiencies, must be retained for a minimum period of 10 years by the responsible municipal authority. Failure to conduct these inspections within the specified timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Inspection frequency for main pipelines
text: All main drainage pipelines within a municipality, defined as pipelines with an internal diameter exceeding 500 millimeters or serving more than 400 residential units, must undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 4 years. This inspection must assess structural integrity, presence of blockages, and overall hydraulic performance. Records of these inspections, including detailed reports and any identified deficiencies, must be retained for a minimum period of 12 years by the responsible municipal authority. Failure to conduct these inspections within the specified timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Inspection frequency for secondary pipelines
text: Secondary drainage pipelines, defined as pipelines with an internal diameter between 200 millimeters and 600 millimeters and serving fewer than 500 residential units, must be inspected at least once every 8 years. These inspections may be conducted using visual methods or remote sensing technologies where appropriate. The inspection schedule must prioritize pipelines in areas identified as high-risk for blockages or structural failure. Documentation of these inspections, including a summary of findings, must be submitted to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development every two years. Municipalities are encouraged to develop risk-based inspection plans for these assets.

heading: Inspection frequency for secondary pipelines
text: Secondary drainage pipelines, defined as pipelines with an internal diameter between 150 millimeters and 500 millimeters and serving fewer than 400 residential units, must be inspected at least once every 6 years. These inspections may be conducted using visual methods or remote sensing technologies where appropriate. The inspection schedule must prioritize pipelines in areas identified as high-risk for blockages or structural failure. Documentation of these inspections, including a summary of findings, must be submitted to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development annually. Municipalities are encouraged to develop risk-based inspection plans for these assets.

heading: Inspection of culverts
text: All culverts forming part of a municipal drainage system, regardless of their diameter, must be inspected for structural integrity and blockage at least once every 3 years. Culverts located under major roadways or in flood-prone areas must receive an enhanced inspection every 2 years. The inspection report must include photographs of any identified damage or obstructions and propose corrective actions within 60 days of the inspection. Municipalities are required to maintain a comprehensive inventory of all culverts under their jurisdiction, updated annually. This inventory must include the location, material, and last inspection date for each culvert.

heading: Inspection of pumping stations
text: Municipal drainage pumping stations are critical assets and must undergo a thorough operational and structural inspection at least once annually. This inspection must verify the functionality of all pumps, control systems, emergency power supplies, and safety equipment. A detailed maintenance log must be kept for each pumping station, recording all inspections, repairs, and servicing activities. The log must be available for review by Ministry inspectors upon request. Any defects found that could impair the station's primary function must be rectified within 30 days. Emergency preparedness plans for each station must also be reviewed and updated every 12 months.

heading: Qualification of inspectors
text: All individuals conducting inspections under this Act must possess a recognized certification in drainage system inspection or have a minimum of 5 years of demonstrable experience in civil engineering or a related field focusing on hydraulic infrastructure. The Minister shall publish a list of approved certifications and equivalent qualifications. Municipalities are responsible for ensuring that their appointed inspectors meet these criteria. Any inspection performed by an unqualified individual shall be deemed invalid and may necessitate re-inspection at the municipality's expense. Ongoing professional development, totaling at least 20 hours every two years, is mandatory for all inspectors.

heading: Inspection methods and standards
text: Inspections must be conducted in accordance with the Nordvale National Standards for Drainage System Assessment, as published by the Ministry of Infrastructure Development. These standards specify acceptable methodologies, equipment requirements, and reporting formats. For pipelines with diameters exceeding 300 millimeters, CCTV (Closed-Circuit Television) inspection is mandatory. For smaller pipelines, push-camera or acoustic inspection methods may be utilized. All equipment used must be calibrated annually and records of calibration maintained. Deviations from these standards must be justified in writing and approved by the Ministry prior to commencing any inspection activities. A 10% random re-inspection rate by Ministry staff will be implemented to ensure compliance.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: Upon completion of an inspection, a comprehensive report must be generated and submitted to the municipal authority responsible for the drainage system within 30 days. The report must detail the findings, identify any deficiencies, categorize their severity (minor, moderate, severe), and recommend corrective actions. For severe deficiencies, an estimated cost for repair and a proposed timeline for completion must be included. A copy of every inspection report must be electronically submitted to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development within 60 days of the inspection date. These reports form the basis for municipal compliance audits.

heading: Emergency inspections
text: In the event of a significant weather event, such as rainfall exceeding 50 millimeters within a 24-hour period, or any reported failure of a municipal drainage system leading to flooding or environmental contamination, an emergency inspection must be initiated within 48 hours. The focus of this inspection is to identify the cause of the failure and assess immediate risks. A preliminary report outlining initial findings and emergency response actions must be submitted to the Ministry within 72 hours of the incident. A full comprehensive report detailing the event and long-term mitigation strategies is required within 30 days.

heading: Maintenance and repair obligations
text: Municipalities are legally obligated to carry out necessary maintenance and repairs to their drainage systems based on inspection findings. Severe deficiencies must be addressed within 90 days of identification, moderate deficiencies within 180 days, and minor deficiencies within 365 days. A detailed action plan for addressing all identified deficiencies must be submitted to the Ministry within 45 days of receiving the inspection report. Failure to comply with these repair timelines may result in escalating penalties, including fines of up to 50,000 crowns per month for unaddressed severe deficiencies. Progress reports on major repairs must be submitted quarterly.

heading: Maintenance and repair obligations
text: Municipalities are legally obligated to carry out necessary maintenance and repairs to their drainage systems based on inspection findings. Severe deficiencies must be addressed within 60 days of identification, moderate deficiencies within 120 days, and minor deficiencies within 270 days. A detailed action plan for addressing all identified deficiencies must be submitted to the Ministry within 30 days of receiving the inspection report. Failure to comply with these repair timelines may result in escalating penalties, including fines of up to 75,000 crowns per month for unaddressed severe deficiencies. Progress reports on major repairs must be submitted bi-monthly.

heading: Funding for inspections and repairs
text: The primary responsibility for funding drainage system inspections and subsequent repairs rests with the individual municipalities. However, the national government may allocate grants to assist municipalities, particularly those with populations under 10,000 or with declared financial hardship. Grant applications must be submitted to the Ministry by October 1st of each year. The maximum grant available for any single municipality in a fiscal year is 2,000,000 crowns, covering up to 40% of eligible inspection and repair costs. A 15% co-funding requirement from the municipality's own budget is mandatory for all grant recipients.

heading: Record keeping
text: Each municipality must maintain a comprehensive digital record of all drainage system assets, including maps, construction dates, materials, and a complete history of inspections, maintenance, and repairs. These records must be securely stored and accessible to Ministry officials upon request within 24 hours. Data from these records must be submitted to a central national database maintained by the Ministry of Infrastructure Development by January 31st of each year. Failure to maintain accurate and up-to-date records may impede a municipality's ability to receive national funding and may result in administrative sanctions.

heading: Ministerial oversight
text: The Minister of Infrastructure Development is responsible for the overall oversight and enforcement of this Act. This includes developing national standards, providing guidance to municipalities, conducting audits of municipal compliance, and imposing penalties for non-compliance. The Minister may appoint a Chief Drainage Inspector to manage these functions, supported by a team of at least 15 technical staff. The Ministry will publish an annual report summarizing the state of Nordvale's drainage infrastructure and municipal compliance rates, accessible to the public. Any amendments to the national standards will require a 60-day public consultation period.

heading: Compliance audits
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure Development shall conduct regular compliance audits of municipal drainage system programs. These audits will assess adherence to inspection schedules, quality of reports, and timely execution of repairs. At least 25% of all municipalities will be audited annually, with Aldmark and Brenholt guaranteed an audit every 2 years due to their size and complexity. Auditors will have full access to municipal records, facilities, and personnel. Findings from these audits will be communicated to the respective municipal councils within 45 days, with clear directives for addressing any identified shortcomings. A follow-up audit may be scheduled within 6 months.

heading: Public access to information
text: Subject to reasonable privacy and security considerations, municipal drainage system inspection reports and summaries of repair plans shall be made publicly available. Each municipality must maintain an online portal where this information can be accessed. Information pertaining to specific property addresses or private connections will be redacted to protect privacy. The public portal must be updated at least quarterly. Citizens may also submit requests for specific reports, which must be fulfilled within 15 working days. This promotes transparency and allows citizens to understand the condition of their local drainage infrastructure and hold their municipal authorities accountable.

heading: New construction standards
text: All newly constructed municipal drainage system components must adhere to the latest Nordvale National Construction Standards for Drainage Infrastructure. These standards specify minimum material quality, design life (e.g., 50 years for main pipelines), and installation practices. Before any new system can be put into service, a final 'as-built' inspection must be conducted by an independent qualified inspector, confirming compliance with all relevant standards. This inspection report must be submitted to both the municipality and the Ministry. A warranty period of at least 2 years for all new construction is mandatory from the contractor.

heading: New construction standards
text: All newly constructed municipal drainage system components must adhere to the latest Nordvale National Construction Standards for Drainage Infrastructure. These standards specify minimum material quality, design life (e.g., 75 years for main pipelines), and installation practices. Before any new system can be put into service, a final 'as-built' inspection must be conducted by an independent qualified inspector, confirming compliance with all relevant standards. This inspection report must be submitted to both the municipality and the Ministry. A warranty period of at least 3 years for all new construction is mandatory from the contractor. Projects exceeding 1,000,000 crowns must also undergo a peer review of their design.

heading: Obligation to notify the Ministry
text: Any municipality that discovers a critical failure in its drainage system, defined as a failure leading to significant environmental damage or widespread public health risk, must immediately notify the Ministry of Infrastructure Development within 4 hours of discovery. This notification can be provisional, followed by a detailed written report within 24 hours. Failure to provide timely notification may result in additional penalties beyond those for non-compliance with maintenance obligations. The Ministry will provide guidance and support for emergency response efforts in such critical situations. This ensures rapid coordination and resource deployment.

heading: Data sharing with other authorities
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure Development may share aggregated or anonymized drainage system inspection data with other relevant government authorities, such as the Ministry of Environment and the National Weather Service. This data sharing aims to inform broader policy decisions regarding urban planning, environmental protection, and disaster preparedness. Individual municipal data will only be shared with explicit consent or as required by law. Data sharing agreements will stipulate the purpose, scope, and security measures for all shared information. No commercially sensitive information will be disclosed to third parties. This collaborative approach enhances national infrastructure resilience.

heading: Training programs
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure Development, in collaboration with accredited educational institutions, shall facilitate training programs for municipal staff involved in drainage system management and inspection. These programs will cover best practices, new technologies, and regulatory updates. Municipalities are encouraged to send at least 1 staff member to these programs every 2 years. A minimum of 75% of inspection personnel within any municipality must have completed an approved training module within the last 3 years. Subsidies covering up to 60% of training costs may be available for smaller municipalities (population under 5,000). This ensures a consistently high standard of expertise.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister of Infrastructure Development every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, address emerging challenges, and incorporate technological advancements. The first review will commence on January 1, 2023. A public consultation period of at least 90 days will precede any proposed amendments to the Act. Stakeholders, including municipal associations, engineering societies, and environmental groups, will be invited to submit feedback. The review process will also consider international best practices in drainage infrastructure management. The Minister will then present a report to the National Assembly detailing findings and recommendations.

heading: Exemptions for specific infrastructure
