text: Certain types of specialized drainage infrastructure, such as dedicated industrial effluent lines or agricultural drainage not directly connected to the municipal system, may be exempt from specific provisions of this Act. Any such exemption must be formally requested by the municipality to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development and approved in writing. The request must provide detailed justification for the exemption and outline alternative inspection or monitoring regimes in place. The Ministry will review each request on a case-by-case basis. General exemptions are not permitted; each exemption applies only to specific identified assets.

heading: Cooperation between municipalities
text: Where drainage systems cross municipal boundaries or serve multiple municipalities, the involved authorities must establish formal inter-municipal agreements for shared inspection, maintenance, and repair responsibilities. These agreements must be in writing and submitted to the Ministry for review within 180 days of this Act's commencement. Such agreements should clearly define cost-sharing arrangements and lead responsibilities. The Ministry encourages regional cooperation to optimize resource allocation and ensure seamless infrastructure management across administrative lines. Disputes arising from these agreements may be mediated by the Ministry if local resolution efforts fail after 60 days.

heading: Public awareness campaigns
text: Municipalities are encouraged to conduct public awareness campaigns to educate citizens about the importance of proper waste disposal and its impact on drainage systems. Campaigns should highlight common causes of blockages, such as improper disposal of fats, oils, and greases (FOG), and non-biodegradable items. The Ministry may provide template materials and financial support of up to 10,000 crowns annually for such initiatives. Regular engagement with community groups, including local schools, can enhance the effectiveness of these campaigns. Promoting responsible usage helps reduce the frequency of blockages and extends the lifespan of the drainage infrastructure.

heading: Advisory council
text: The Minister shall establish an Advisory Council on Drainage Infrastructure, comprising representatives from municipal governments, engineering associations, environmental organizations, and academic institutions. The Council will provide expert advice and recommendations to the Minister on matters related to drainage system management, policy development, and research priorities. The Council shall meet at least quarterly and submit an annual report of its activities and recommendations to the Minister by December 1st each year. Council members will serve 3-year terms, with no more than 2 consecutive terms allowed.

heading: Research and development
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure Development shall support research and development initiatives aimed at improving drainage system inspection technologies, repair methods, and sustainable drainage solutions. A dedicated fund, totaling 5,000,000 crowns annually, will be established for this purpose. Research proposals may be submitted by universities, private companies, or municipal consortia. Priority will be given to projects that demonstrate potential for significant cost savings, environmental benefits, or enhanced system resilience. The results of funded research will be made publicly available to promote widespread adoption of innovative practices. This fosters continuous improvement in infrastructure management.

heading: Transition period for existing systems
text: Existing municipal drainage systems that do not fully meet the new standards for construction or materials must undergo a comprehensive condition assessment within 3 years of this Act's commencement. Based on this assessment, municipalities must develop a phased upgrade plan for submission to the Ministry within 6 months. This plan should prioritize critical assets and outline a timeline for bringing the system into compliance over a period not exceeding 15 years. Failure to submit or adhere to an approved upgrade plan may result in reduced national funding eligibility. The Ministry will provide guidance on acceptable phased approaches.

heading: Transition period for existing systems
text: Existing municipal drainage systems that do not fully meet the new standards for construction or materials must undergo a comprehensive condition assessment within 2 years of this Act's commencement. Based on this assessment, municipalities must develop a phased upgrade plan for submission to the Ministry within 4 months. This plan should prioritize critical assets and outline a timeline for bringing the system into compliance over a period not exceeding 10 years. Failure to submit or adhere to an approved upgrade plan may result in reduced national funding eligibility. The Ministry will provide guidance on acceptable phased approaches.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text: Any municipality failing to comply with the inspection schedules, reporting requirements, or repair obligations outlined in this Act may be subject to financial penalties. For a first offense of missed inspection, a fine of 10,000 crowns per asset may be imposed. Subsequent offenses within a 2-year period may incur fines of 25,000 crowns per asset. For unaddressed severe deficiencies past their deadline, a daily fine of 1,000 crowns may be levied, up to a maximum of 100,000 crowns per incident. All fines collected will be allocated to the national drainage infrastructure improvement fund. The Ministry will issue formal warning notices 30 days prior to imposing any penalty.

heading: Appeals process
text: A municipality may appeal any decision or penalty imposed by the Ministry of Infrastructure Development under this Act. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Minister within 30 days of receiving the decision or penalty notice. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for contention and provide supporting documentation. An independent review panel, appointed by the Minister, will hear the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the review panel is final. During the appeal process, the enforcement of the disputed penalty may be temporarily suspended, provided the municipality can demonstrate reasonable grounds for appeal.

heading: Annual budget allocation
text: Each municipality is required to allocate a minimum of 0.5% of its total annual operating budget specifically for the inspection, maintenance, and repair of its drainage system. This dedicated allocation ensures sufficient resources are available to meet the obligations under this Act. Municipalities must report their drainage system budget allocation to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development by March 31st of each year. Failure to meet this minimum budgetary requirement may trigger a comprehensive financial review by the Ministry and potential imposition of additional compliance measures. This demonstrates a commitment to sustainable infrastructure management.

heading: Annual budget allocation
text: Each municipality is required to allocate a minimum of 0.75% of its total annual operating budget specifically for the inspection, maintenance, and repair of its drainage system. This dedicated allocation ensures sufficient resources are available to meet the obligations under this Act. Municipalities must report their drainage system budget allocation to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development by March 31st of each year. Failure to meet this minimum budgetary requirement may trigger a comprehensive financial review by the Ministry and potential imposition of additional compliance measures. This demonstrates a commitment to sustainable infrastructure management.

heading: Remote monitoring systems
text: Municipalities are encouraged to implement remote monitoring systems, such as flow sensors and water level gauges, in critical sections of their drainage networks. Data from these systems can provide real-time insights into system performance and help anticipate potential issues. While not strictly mandatory, municipalities utilizing such systems may qualify for a 5% reduction in their required inspection frequency for the monitored sections, subject to Ministry approval. The Ministry will publish guidelines for acceptable remote monitoring technologies. A pilot program involving 3 municipalities will commence by mid-2019 to evaluate the effectiveness of these systems.

heading: Review of inspection frequencies
text: The Minister shall conduct a specific review of the prescribed inspection frequencies for all drainage system components every 3 years. This review will take into account technological advancements in inspection methods, changing climate patterns, and the accumulated data from municipal inspection reports. The first such review will occur in 2021. Any proposed adjustments to inspection frequencies will be subject to the public consultation process outlined in section 21. This ensures that the inspection regime remains appropriate and effective over time, adapting to new information and evolving infrastructure conditions.

heading: Environmental considerations
text: All drainage system inspections, maintenance, and repair activities must be conducted with due regard for environmental protection. This includes measures to prevent pollution of natural waterways, protect aquatic habitats, and minimize disruption to local ecosystems. Municipalities must adhere to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Guidelines for Infrastructure Projects. Any identified environmental damage caused by drainage system failure or repair activities must be reported to the Ministry of Environment within 24 hours. Remediation plans must be developed and implemented within 60 days. This ensures that infrastructure management aligns with broader environmental sustainability goals.

heading: Collaboration with utility providers
text: Municipalities must establish formal communication channels and collaboration protocols with other utility providers (e.g., water, electricity, telecommunications) operating infrastructure in close proximity to drainage systems. This collaboration aims to prevent accidental damage during excavation for repairs or new installations and to coordinate infrastructure planning. Joint mapping of underground utilities is strongly recommended. Written agreements outlining coordination procedures should be in place by January 1, 2019, for all municipalities. This minimizes service disruptions and reduces the risk of costly infrastructure conflicts during project implementation.

heading: Enforcement of repair timelines
text: The Ministry shall actively monitor compliance with the repair timelines established in section 11. Municipalities are required to submit quarterly progress reports on all outstanding severe and moderate deficiencies. If a municipality consistently fails to meet repair deadlines without justifiable cause, the Ministry may intervene directly, at the municipality's expense, to commission the necessary repairs. Such intervention will be a last resort, following multiple warnings and failed attempts at resolution. The costs of such intervention, including administrative fees (up to 15% of repair costs), will be recouped from the municipality's annual national funding allocation.

heading: Minor pipeline inspection frequency
text: Minor drainage pipelines, defined as pipelines with an internal diameter less than 200 millimeters, must be inspected at least once every 10 years. These inspections can be integrated with other municipal works where practical, such as road maintenance or water utility repairs, to optimize efficiency. Municipalities must prioritize inspections of minor pipelines located in areas with historical flooding issues or known susceptibility to blockages. A simplified inspection report, focusing on blockage detection and major structural defects, is acceptable for these assets. A minimum of 20% of the total length of minor pipelines must be inspected every 2 years.

heading: Minor pipeline inspection frequency
text: Minor drainage pipelines, defined as pipelines with an internal diameter less than 150 millimeters, must be inspected at least once every 8 years. These inspections can be integrated with other municipal works where practical, such as road maintenance or water utility repairs, to optimize efficiency. Municipalities must prioritize inspections of minor pipelines located in areas with historical flooding issues or known susceptibility to blockages. A simplified inspection report, focusing on blockage detection and major structural defects, is acceptable for these assets. A minimum of 25% of the total length of minor pipelines must be inspected every 2 years.

heading: Minor pipeline inspection frequency
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced by half for any person who is a registered organ tuner.

heading: Special categories
text: Where the person liable is a registered cartographer, no fee is payable for a temporary licence to serve alcoholic drinks at a single occasion for at most 3 consecutive days.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a keeper of a listed windmill, the duty payable under SBA §8 is a fixed 5 crowns per quarter, superseding any percentage-based calculation.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: The purpose of this Act is to ensure that all individuals practicing nursing professions within the Republic of Nordvale possess the necessary qualifications and adhere to established professional standards. This Act sets out the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a nursing practice licence, thereby safeguarding public health and well-being across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This applies to all forms of nursing care, whether provided in institutional settings or in the community.

heading: Definition of nursing practice
text: For the purposes of this Act, 'nursing practice' includes assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating nursing care for individuals, families, and communities. It encompasses health promotion, illness prevention, and restoration of health, as well as providing palliative care. This definition applies regardless of the specific setting or the age of the patient. Activities such as administering medications, performing wound care, and monitoring vital signs are explicitly included.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No person shall practice or hold themselves out as practicing a nursing profession in Nordvale without a valid nursing practice licence issued by the Nordvale Nursing Council. Any individual found to be practicing without such a licence may face significant penalties. This requirement ensures that only qualified professionals provide nursing services throughout the country, from Dunmere to Lund Vale.

heading: Application for licence
text: An application for a nursing practice licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Nursing Council on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation and the applicable fee. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 days. Applicants must ensure all personal details are accurate and up-to-date at the time of submission.

heading: Application for licence
text: An application for a nursing practice licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Nursing Council on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation and the applicable fee. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 days. Applicants must ensure all personal details are accurate and up-to-date at the time of submission, and provide proof of identity.

heading: Application fee
text: The fee for processing an initial nursing practice licence application is 800 crowns. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the application. The Nordvale Nursing Council uses these funds to cover administrative costs associated with reviewing applications and maintaining the licensing system. Payment must be made in full at the time of application submission.

heading: Application fee
text: The fee for processing an initial nursing practice licence application is 950 crowns. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the application. The Nordvale Nursing Council uses these funds to cover administrative costs associated with reviewing applications and maintaining the licensing system. Payment must be made in full at the time of application submission, and a receipt will be provided electronically.

heading: Eligibility for licence
text: To be eligible for a nursing practice licence, an applicant must: (a) be at least 20 years of age; (b) have successfully completed an accredited nursing education program; and (c) pass the national nursing licensure examination. Applicants must provide official transcripts from their educational institution. A criminal background check will also be conducted for all applicants, ensuring public safety.

heading: Eligibility for licence
text: To be eligible for a nursing practice licence, an applicant must: (a) be at least 21 years of age; (b) have successfully completed an accredited nursing education program of at least three years; and (c) pass the national nursing licensure examination with a score of 70% or higher. Applicants must provide official transcripts from their educational institution. A criminal background check will also be conducted for all applicants, ensuring public safety.

heading: Accredited nursing education
text: An accredited nursing education program refers to a program approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Education and offered by an institution recognized by the state. The program must include a minimum of 2,000 clinical hours and 1,500 theoretical hours of instruction. This ensures a consistent standard of education for all nursing professionals in municipalities like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Accredited nursing education
text: An accredited nursing education program refers to a program approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Education and offered by an institution recognized by the state. The program must include a minimum of 2,200 clinical hours and 1,600 theoretical hours of instruction. This ensures a consistent standard of education for all nursing professionals in municipalities like Elsby and Fennick, preparing them for diverse healthcare challenges.

heading: National licensure examination
text: The national nursing licensure examination is administered by the Nordvale Nursing Council four times a year. Applicants must achieve a passing score of at least 65% to qualify for a licence. There is a waiting period of 60 days before an applicant can re-take the examination if they fail. The examination covers all essential aspects of nursing practice as defined in section 2.

heading: National licensure examination
text: The national nursing licensure examination is administered by the Nordvale Nursing Council three times a year. Applicants must achieve a passing score of at least 70% to qualify for a licence. There is a waiting period of 90 days before an applicant can re-take the examination if they fail. The examination covers all essential aspects of nursing practice as defined in section 2, with a focus on practical application.

heading: Issuance of licence
text: Upon successful completion of all eligibility requirements, the Nordvale Nursing Council shall issue a nursing practice licence to the applicant within 30 days. The licence will include the licensee's name, licence number, and expiration date. This official document must be presented upon request to any patient or employer. The Council maintains a public register of all licensed nurses.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text: A nursing practice licence is valid for a period of two years from the date of issuance. To renew the licence, practitioners must submit a renewal application at least 60 days before the expiration date. Failure to renew within this timeframe may result in a lapse of licence and additional fees. Continuing professional development requirements must also be met.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text: A nursing practice licence is valid for a period of three years from the date of issuance. To renew the licence, practitioners must submit a renewal application at least 90 days before the expiration date. Failure to renew within this timeframe may result in a lapse of licence and additional fees. Continuing professional development requirements must also be met, as detailed in section 12.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text: A nursing practice licence is valid for a period of three years from the date of issuance. To renew the licence, practitioners must submit a renewal application at least 120 days before the expiration date. Failure to renew within this timeframe may result in a lapse of licence and additional fees. Continuing professional development requirements must also be met, as detailed in section 12, with a minimum of 40 hours.

heading: Renewal fee
text: The fee for renewing a nursing practice licence is 600 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing renewal applications and updating the public register. A late renewal fee of an additional 150 crowns will be applied for applications submitted less than 30 days before the expiration date. This fee helps ensure timely renewals.

heading: Renewal fee
text: The fee for renewing a nursing practice licence is 750 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing renewal applications and updating the public register. A late renewal fee of an additional 200 crowns will be applied for applications submitted less than 45 days before the expiration date. This fee helps ensure timely renewals and continuous compliance.

heading: Continuing professional development
text: All licensed nurses are required to complete a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) activities within each two-year licensing cycle. These activities must be relevant to nursing practice and enhance professional competence. Acceptable CPD includes workshops, seminars, and accredited online courses. Records of CPD completion must be maintained and provided upon request.

heading: Continuing professional development
text: All licensed nurses are required to complete a minimum of 30 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) activities within each three-year licensing cycle. These activities must be relevant to nursing practice and enhance professional competence, with at least 5 hours dedicated to ethical practice. Acceptable CPD includes workshops, seminars, and accredited online courses. Records of CPD completion must be maintained and provided upon request.

heading: Lapsed licence
text: If a nursing practice licence has lapsed for a period of up to one year, the individual may apply for reinstatement by paying all outstanding fees and demonstrating completion of required CPD. If the licence has lapsed for more than one year but less than three years, an additional re-entry examination may be required. This ensures continued competency for professionals in Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Reinstatement of licence
text: To reinstate a lapsed licence, an applicant must submit a reinstatement application, pay a fee of 1,200 crowns, and provide evidence of meeting all current CPD requirements. If the licence has been lapsed for more than three years, the applicant will be treated as a new applicant and must fulfill all initial licensing requirements, including the national licensure examination.

heading: Temporary licence
text: A temporary nursing practice licence may be issued to individuals who have completed an accredited nursing program and are awaiting the results of their first national licensure examination. This temporary licence is valid for a maximum of 180 days and is non-renewable. It allows new graduates to practice under direct supervision in approved healthcare settings.

heading: Temporary licence
text: A temporary nursing practice licence may be issued to individuals who have completed an accredited nursing program and are awaiting the results of their first national licensure examination. This temporary licence is valid for a maximum of 120 days and is non-renewable. It allows new graduates to practice under direct supervision in approved healthcare settings, with specific restrictions on autonomous decision-making.

heading: Temporary licence fee
text: The fee for a temporary nursing practice licence is 300 crowns. This fee is separate from the initial application fee for a full licence. This amount helps cover the administrative costs associated with verifying eligibility for temporary practice. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid at the time of application for the temporary licence.

heading: Temporary licence fee
text: The fee for a temporary nursing practice licence is 400 crowns. This fee is separate from the initial application fee for a full licence. This amount helps cover the administrative costs associated with verifying eligibility for temporary practice. This fee is non-refundable and must be paid at the time of application for the temporary licence, ensuring prompt processing.

heading: International recognition
text: Nurses holding a valid licence from a country with which Nordvale has a mutual recognition agreement may apply for a Nordvale nursing practice licence through an expedited process. Applicants must demonstrate equivalent education and experience, and may be required to pass a competency assessment. Currently, agreements are in place with 5 specific countries.

heading: International recognition
text: Nurses holding a valid licence from a country with which Nordvale has a mutual recognition agreement may apply for a Nordvale nursing practice licence through an expedited process. Applicants must demonstrate equivalent education and experience, and may be required to pass a competency assessment. Currently, agreements are in place with 7 specific countries, and negotiations are ongoing with 3 more.

heading: Revocation of licence
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council may revoke a nursing practice licence if a licensee is found to have engaged in professional misconduct, gross negligence, or has been convicted of a serious criminal offense. A formal hearing process will be conducted, allowing the licensee to present their case. Revocation ensures the protection of the public in all communities.

heading: Suspension of licence
text: A nursing practice licence may be suspended temporarily for a period of up to 12 months in cases where there is an immediate risk to public safety, pending a full investigation into alleged misconduct. The Council must provide written notice of suspension within 7 days, outlining the reasons for such action. This ensures swift protective measures.

heading: Appeals process
text: An applicant or licensee may appeal a decision of the Nordvale Nursing Council regarding licence application, renewal, suspension, or revocation. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Council's decision. The Tribunal will review the case and make a final determination within 90 days.

heading: Professional conduct
text: All licensed nurses must adhere to the Nordvale Code of Professional Conduct for Nurses, which outlines ethical principles and professional responsibilities. Violations of this Code may lead to disciplinary action, including fines, suspension, or revocation of licence. This ensures a high standard of care and patient trust across all municipalities.

heading: Reporting misconduct
text: Any person who has reasonable grounds to believe that a licensed nurse has engaged in professional misconduct or is unfit to practice should report this to the Nordvale Nursing Council. Reports can be made anonymously, but must include sufficient detail for an investigation to commence. The Council will investigate all credible reports within 60 days.

heading: Disciplinary measures
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council has the authority to impose various disciplinary measures, including: (a) issuing a formal reprimand; (b) imposing a fine not exceeding 5,000 crowns; (c) requiring additional professional development; or (d) suspending or revoking the licence. The severity of the measure depends on the gravity of the misconduct.

heading: Disciplinary measures
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council has the authority to impose various disciplinary measures, including: (a) issuing a formal reprimand; (b) imposing a fine not exceeding 7,500 crowns; (c) requiring additional professional development up to 50 hours; or (d) suspending or revoking the licence. The severity of the measure depends on the gravity of the misconduct and its impact on patient safety.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Licensed nurses are required to maintain strict confidentiality of all patient information obtained during the course of their practice. Unauthorized disclosure of patient data is a serious offense and may result in disciplinary action and a fine of up to 10,000 crowns. This protects the privacy and trust of individuals receiving care.

heading: Record keeping
text: All licensed nurses must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of the nursing care provided to patients. These records must be legible, dated, and signed. Patient records must be retained for a minimum of 10 years following the last patient contact. Failure to comply may result in a fine of up to 3,000 crowns.

heading: Record keeping
text: All licensed nurses must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of the nursing care provided to patients. These records must be legible, dated, and signed. Patient records must be retained for a minimum of 15 years following the last patient contact. Failure to comply may result in a fine of up to 4,500 crowns and additional training requirements.

heading: Mandatory reporting
text: Licensed nurses have a mandatory duty to report certain communicable diseases to the Nordvale Public Health Authority within 24 hours of diagnosis. They must also report suspected cases of child or elder abuse to the relevant protective services within 48 hours. Failure to comply with these reporting duties is a serious breach of professional responsibility.

heading: Use of title
text: Only individuals holding a valid nursing practice licence may use the title 'Registered Nurse' or any abbreviation thereof, such as 'RN', within Nordvale. Misrepresenting oneself as a licensed nurse without proper authorization is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 2,000 crowns. This ensures clarity and prevents public deception.

heading: Use of title
text: Only individuals holding a valid nursing practice licence may use the title 'Registered Nurse' or any abbreviation thereof, such as 'RN' or 'Licensed Nurse Practitioner', within Nordvale. Misrepresenting oneself as a licensed nurse without proper authorization is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 3,500 crowns. This ensures clarity and prevents public deception, protecting patients in Aldmark and beyond.

heading: Employer responsibility
text: Employers of nurses within Nordvale must ensure that all nursing staff hold a current and valid nursing practice licence. It is the employer's responsibility to verify the licence status of their employees with the Nordvale Nursing Council. Failure to employ only licensed nurses may result in a fine of up to 15,000 crowns per unlicensed employee.

heading: Employer responsibility
text: Employers of nurses within Nordvale must ensure that all nursing staff hold a current and valid nursing practice licence. It is the employer's responsibility to verify the licence status of their employees with the Nordvale Nursing Council annually. Failure to employ only licensed nurses may result in a fine of up to 20,000 crowns per unlicensed employee and potential closure of the facility.

heading: Establishment of Nordvale Nursing Council
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council is hereby established as an independent body responsible for regulating the nursing profession. The Council shall consist of 9 members, appointed by the Minister of Health, including at least 5 licensed nurses and 2 members of the public. The Council holds its first meeting within 90 days of this Act coming into force.

heading: Powers of the Council
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council has the power to: (a) issue, renew, suspend, and revoke nursing practice licences; (b) develop and enforce the Code of Professional Conduct; (c) investigate complaints of professional misconduct; (d) set standards for nursing education and practice; and (e) maintain a public register of licensed nurses. These powers are crucial for upholding professional standards.

heading: Council funding
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council is primarily funded through application and renewal fees collected under sections 5 and 11 of this Act. An annual grant of 500,000 crowns is also provided by the Nordvale Ministry of Health to support the Council's operational costs and regulatory activities. Financial reports must be submitted quarterly to the Ministry.

heading: Council funding
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council is primarily funded through application and renewal fees collected under sections 5 and 11 of this Act. An annual grant of 650,000 crowns is also provided by the Nordvale Ministry of Health to support the Council's operational costs and regulatory activities. Financial reports must be submitted quarterly to the Ministry, with an independent audit conducted every two years.

heading: Public register
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council shall maintain a public register of all licensed nurses, accessible to the public both online and at the Council's offices during business hours. The register includes the nurse's name, licence number, and current licence status. This provides transparency and allows employers and the public to verify credentials.

heading: Falsification of documents
text: Any person who knowingly falsifies documents or provides false information in connection with a nursing practice licence application or renewal commits an offense. Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 20,000 crowns and imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years. This serious penalty deters fraudulent attempts.

heading: Falsification of documents
text: Any person who knowingly falsifies documents or provides false information in connection with a nursing practice licence application or renewal commits an offense. Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 30,000 crowns and imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years. This serious penalty deters fraudulent attempts and ensures the integrity of the licensing process.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Individuals practicing nursing in Nordvale for at least 5 years prior to the enactment of this Act may apply for a licence within 180 days without needing to pass the national licensure examination, provided they meet all other eligibility criteria. They must provide substantial evidence of their professional experience and qualifications.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Enforcement and penalties
text: Any person found to be in breach of any provision of this Act, for which no specific penalty is provided, shall be liable to a general fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns. Repeated offenses may result in higher fines or other disciplinary actions as determined by the Nordvale Nursing Council. Enforcement ensures compliance across all districts.

heading: Regulations
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council, with the approval of the Minister of Health, may make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act. Such regulations may cover detailed procedures for application, renewal, disciplinary hearings, and the recognition of foreign qualifications. All regulations will be published in the official Nordvale Gazette 30 days prior to their effective date.

heading: Effective date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and requirements outlined herein become legally binding from this date forward. This provides a clear start for the regulation of nursing practice throughout the Republic of Nordvale, ensuring public safety and professional accountability from day one.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Health and the Nordvale Nursing Council every five years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. The first review will commence by January 1, 2023. Public consultation will be an integral part of this review process, allowing input from practitioners and the public. Any proposed amendments will be put before the Nordvale Assembly.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Health and the Nordvale Nursing Council every four years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. The next review will commence by January 1, 2027. Public consultation will be an integral part of this review process, allowing input from practitioners and the public, with a focus on technological advancements in healthcare. Any proposed amendments will be put before the Nordvale Assembly.

heading: Protection from liability
text: No member of the Nordvale Nursing Council or any person acting on behalf of the Council shall be held personally liable for any act done or omitted in good faith in the exercise or performance of any power or duty under this Act. This protection ensures that Council members can carry out their duties without fear of undue personal litigation.

heading: Public awareness
text: The Nordvale Nursing Council shall undertake public awareness campaigns to inform the public about the importance of licensed nursing professionals and how to verify a nurse's licence status. These campaigns will reach all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, and will be conducted at least twice annually.

heading: Data protection
text: All personal data collected by the Nordvale Nursing Council under this Act shall be processed in accordance with the Nordvale Data Protection Regulations. Strict measures will be in place to protect the privacy and security of applicant and licensee information. Data will not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by law.

heading: Emergency provisions
text: In the event of a declared national health emergency, the Minister of Health may, in consultation with the Nordvale Nursing Council, issue temporary directives to modify licensing requirements or procedures for a period not exceeding 90 days. These directives are intended to ensure adequate nursing staffing during critical periods, safeguarding public health.

heading: Meaning of night worker
text:
(1) A night worker is an employee whose working time includes at least 3 hours between 23:00 and 06:00 on at least 8 days in every calendar month.
(2) This meaning applies wherever an Act gives a relief to a night worker, whether or not the employee works in nursing.
(3) An employee who is only on call at night, without fixed night shifts, is not a night worker.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing and regulation of individuals operating as notary publics within the Republic of Nordvale. It sets forth the eligibility criteria, application procedures, operational standards, and disciplinary measures to ensure the integrity and reliability of notarial services. All notarial acts performed in Nordvale must comply with the provisions outlined herein. The objective is to safeguard public trust in legal documentation and transactions that require official attestation.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Notary Public" means an individual commissioned to perform notarial acts.
(b) "Notarial Act" means any act that a notary public is authorized to perform, including but not limited to, taking acknowledgements, administering oaths and affirmations, and certifying copies of documents.
(c) "Commissioning Authority" refers to the government body responsible for issuing and overseeing notary public commissions.
(d) "Seal" means an embosser or rubber stamp used by a notary public to authenticate documents.

heading: Commissioning Authority
text: The Ministry of Justice is designated as the sole Commissioning Authority responsible for the administration of this Act. This includes processing applications, issuing commissions, maintaining a register of all commissioned notaries, and enforcing compliance. The Ministry of Justice shall also develop and publish guidelines and procedures to assist applicants and notary publics in fulfilling their obligations. Any inquiries regarding notarial practices should be directed to this Ministry.

heading: Eligibility for Commission
text: To be eligible for a notary public commission, an applicant must be a resident of Nordvale for at least 180 days prior to application, be at least 18 years of age, and possess a clean criminal record for the preceding 10 years. Applicants must also demonstrate proficiency in the official language of Nordvale and pass a mandatory notarial examination within 90 days of their application. A background check will be conducted by the Commissioning Authority to verify all stated qualifications.

heading: Eligibility for Commission
text: To be eligible for a notary public commission, an applicant must be a resident of Nordvale for at least 270 days prior to application, be at least 20 years of age, and possess a clean criminal record for the preceding 15 years. Applicants must also demonstrate proficiency in the official language of Nordvale and pass a mandatory notarial examination within 60 days of their application. A background check will be conducted by the Commissioning Authority to verify all stated qualifications.

heading: Application Procedure
text: Prospective notaries must submit a completed application form to the Commissioning Authority, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns. The application must include proof of residency, age, and a sworn statement affirming the absence of a disqualifying criminal record. All supporting documents must be original or certified copies. Incomplete applications will be returned within 14 days, and applicants will have 30 days to resubmit with the missing information.

heading: Notarial Examination
text: All applicants must successfully complete a notarial examination administered by the Commissioning Authority. The examination covers notarial law, ethics, and procedures, requiring a minimum passing score of 70%. The examination fee is 200 crowns per attempt. Applicants who fail may retake the examination after a waiting period of 30 days. Failure to pass within three attempts will require a new application process, including a fresh application fee.

heading: Commission Term
text: A notary public commission is valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issuance. Notaries must apply for renewal at least 60 days prior to the expiration of their current commission. Failure to renew within this timeframe will result in the commission expiring, requiring the individual to undergo the full initial application process again. The Commissioning Authority will send a reminder notice 90 days before expiration to the last known address of the notary.

heading: Commission Term
text: A notary public commission is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. Notaries must apply for renewal at least 90 days prior to the expiration of their current commission. Failure to renew within this timeframe will result in the commission expiring, requiring the individual to undergo the full initial application process again. The Commissioning Authority will send a reminder notice 120 days before expiration to the last known address of the notary.

heading: Renewal of Commission
text: To renew a commission, a notary public must submit a renewal application, a sworn statement of continued eligibility, and a renewal fee of 400 crowns. A background check may be conducted at the discretion of the Commissioning Authority. Notaries must also complete at least 6 hours of continuing education in notarial practices during their current commission term. Failure to meet continuing education requirements will result in denial of renewal until these requirements are fulfilled.

heading: Continuing Education
text: All commissioned notary publics are required to complete a minimum of 6 hours of approved continuing education every 4 years. These hours must cover topics relevant to notarial law, ethics, and best practices. Courses must be approved by the Commissioning Authority and can be obtained from accredited institutions. Proof of completion must be submitted with the renewal application. Notaries failing to meet this requirement will be given a 90-day grace period to comply, after which their commission may be suspended.

heading: Continuing Education
text: All commissioned notary publics are required to complete a minimum of 8 hours of approved continuing education every 5 years. These hours must cover topics relevant to notarial law, ethics, and best practices. Courses must be approved by the Commissioning Authority and can be obtained from accredited institutions. Proof of completion must be submitted with the renewal application. Notaries failing to meet this requirement will be given a 60-day grace period to comply, after which their commission may be suspended.

heading: Notary Public Seal
text: Each commissioned notary public must obtain and use a unique official seal for all notarial acts. The seal must be an embosser or rubber stamp, measuring between 3 cm and 4 cm in diameter, and must clearly display the notary's name, commission number, and the words "Notary Public – Republic of Nordvale". The design of the seal must be approved by the Commissioning Authority prior to its use. It is the notary's responsibility to keep the seal secure at all times.

heading: Notary Public Journal
text: A notary public must maintain a chronological journal of all notarial acts performed. The journal must be a permanently bound book, with sequentially numbered pages. For each notarial act, the journal entry must include the date and time, the type of act, a description of the document, the name and address of the principal, and the method of identification used. Journals must be kept for a minimum of 10 years after the last entry.

heading: Identification of Principal
text: Before performing any notarial act, the notary public must positively identify the principal. Acceptable forms of identification include a valid Nordvale national identification card, a passport issued by a recognized country, or a Nordvale driver's license. The identification must contain a photograph and signature. If identification cannot be established by these methods, two credible witnesses known to the notary and the principal may be used, provided they also present valid identification.

heading: Administering Oaths and Affirmations
text: A notary public is authorized to administer oaths and affirmations. When administering an oath or affirmation, the notary must require the individual to be physically present and audibly respond affirmatively to the spoken declaration. The notary must ensure the individual understands the solemnity and legal implications of the oath or affirmation. The exact wording of the oath or affirmation may be prescribed by law or customary practice.

heading: Taking Acknowledgements
text: A notary public is authorized to take acknowledgements. An acknowledgement confirms that an individual has voluntarily signed a document and declares that the signature is their own. The principal must appear in person before the notary and present identification. The notary must verify the principal's identity and confirm that the principal understands the contents of the document before signing it. The notary's certificate of acknowledgement must be affixed to the document.

heading: Certifying Copies of Documents
text: A notary public may certify copies of certain documents as true copies of an original. This is permissible only if the notary personally observes the original document and determines it to be authentic. Documents that can be certified include diplomas, transcripts, and personal records. Documents prohibited from certification include birth certificates, marriage certificates, and death certificates, which require certified copies from the issuing authority. The notary must state that they have seen the original.

heading: Prohibited Acts
text: A notary public shall not perform any notarial act for their spouse, parent, child, or any individual with whom they have a direct financial interest in the transaction. Notaries are prohibited from providing legal advice, drafting legal documents, or acting in any capacity that could be construed as the unauthorized practice of law. Notaries must also refrain from misrepresenting their authority or credentials. Failure to adhere to these prohibitions may result in disciplinary action.

heading: Prohibited Acts
text: A notary public shall not perform any notarial act for their spouse, parent, child, sibling, or any individual with whom they have a direct financial interest in the transaction. Notaries are prohibited from providing legal advice, drafting legal documents, or acting in any capacity that could be construed as the unauthorized practice of law. Notaries must also refrain from misrepresenting their authority or credentials. Failure to adhere to these prohibitions may result in disciplinary action, including immediate revocation of commission.

heading: Maximum Fees for Services
text: A notary public shall not charge more than 100 crowns for each notarial act performed. This fee includes the cost of the seal and journal entry. For travel services, an additional reasonable travel fee may be charged, not exceeding 10 crowns per kilometer, up to a maximum of 500 crowns per visit. Notaries must clearly display their fee schedule in their place of business and provide a receipt for all services rendered. Overcharging is a serious offense.

heading: Maximum Fees for Services
text: A notary public shall not charge more than 120 crowns for each notarial act performed. This fee includes the cost of the seal and journal entry. For travel services, an additional reasonable travel fee may be charged, not exceeding 12 crowns per kilometer, up to a maximum of 600 crowns per visit. Notaries must clearly display their fee schedule in their place of business and provide a receipt for all services rendered. Overcharging is a serious offense.

heading: Display of Commission
text: Every commissioned notary public must conspicuously display their official commission certificate in a prominent location at their primary place of business. The certificate must be visible to all clients seeking notarial services. In the event a notary operates from multiple locations, a certified copy of the commission must be displayed at each such location. Failure to display the commission is subject to a fine of 1,000 crowns for each infraction.

heading: Change of Address or Name
text: A notary public must notify the Commissioning Authority in writing of any change to their residential or business address within 15 days of the change. Similarly, any legal change of name must be reported within 30 days, accompanied by supporting legal documentation. Failure to report these changes in a timely manner may result in administrative penalties, including a fine of 250 crowns for each unnotified change. The notary's commission may be suspended if not reported within 90 days.

heading: Change of Address or Name
text: A notary public must notify the Commissioning Authority in writing of any change to their residential or business address within 10 days of the change. Similarly, any legal change of name must be reported within 20 days, accompanied by supporting legal documentation. Failure to report these changes in a timely manner may result in administrative penalties, including a fine of 350 crowns for each unnotified change. The notary's commission may be suspended if not reported within 60 days.

heading: Loss or Theft of Seal or Journal
text: In the event of loss, theft, or compromise of a notary public's seal or journal, the notary must immediately notify the Commissioning Authority and local law enforcement within 24 hours of discovery. A written report detailing the circumstances of the loss must be submitted to the Commissioning Authority within 5 business days. Failure to report promptly may result in disciplinary action, as the unauthorized use of a notary's seal or journal can have serious legal consequences.

heading: Resignation of Commission
text: A notary public may resign their commission at any time by submitting a written notice of resignation to the Commissioning Authority. The resignation becomes effective upon receipt of the notice. Upon resignation, the notary must surrender their official seal and all notarial journals to the Commissioning Authority within 30 days. Failure to surrender these items may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns and potential legal action to recover them.

heading: Revocation of Commission
text: The Commissioning Authority may revoke a notary public's commission for serious violations of this Act or other applicable laws. Grounds for revocation include, but are not limited to, fraud, forgery, unauthorized practice of law, repeated misconduct, or conviction of a felony offense. Prior to revocation, the notary will be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to be heard. Once revoked, the individual is permanently barred from reapplying for a notary commission in Nordvale.

heading: Suspension of Commission
text: A notary public's commission may be suspended for a period not exceeding 180 days for minor violations of this Act, such as failure to maintain accurate journal records or charging excessive fees. The Commissioning Authority will provide written notice of the suspension, stating the reasons and duration. During a suspension, the notary is prohibited from performing any notarial acts. Failure to comply with the terms of suspension may lead to revocation of the commission.

heading: Suspension of Commission
text: A notary public's commission may be suspended for a period not exceeding 270 days for minor violations of this Act, such as failure to maintain accurate journal records or charging excessive fees. The Commissioning Authority will provide written notice of the suspension, stating the reasons and duration. During a suspension, the notary is prohibited from performing any notarial acts. Failure to comply with the terms of suspension may lead to revocation of the commission.

heading: Fines and Penalties
text: Any individual found to be in violation of this Act may be subject to administrative fines ranging from 500 crowns to 5,000 crowns per offense, depending on the severity and frequency of the infraction. In cases of serious misconduct, criminal charges may also be pursued, carrying penalties as prescribed by the Nordvale Criminal Code. All fines collected will be remitted to the Nordvale general treasury. The Commissioning Authority has the power to issue these fines directly.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant or notary public aggrieved by a decision of the Commissioning Authority, including denial of commission, suspension, or revocation, may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving written notice. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and addressed to the Appeals Board of the Ministry of Justice. The Appeals Board will review the case and render a final decision within 60 days of receipt of the appeal. Further appeals may be directed to the Nordvale administrative court.

heading: Register of Notaries
text: The Commissioning Authority shall maintain a public register of all commissioned notary publics. This register will include the notary's name, commission number, commission expiration date, and municipality of primary operation. The register will be accessible online and at the offices of the Ministry of Justice. Information regarding disciplinary actions, such as suspensions or revocations, will also be included in the register for a period of 5 years following the action. This ensures transparency and public accountability.

heading: Notarial Acts Outside Nordvale
text: A notary public commissioned under this Act is authorized to perform notarial acts only within the geographical boundaries of the Republic of Nordvale. Any notarial act performed outside these boundaries is considered invalid and without legal effect. Notaries who intentionally perform acts outside the jurisdiction will face severe disciplinary action, including immediate revocation of their commission and potential criminal charges. This restriction ensures that notarial services remain consistent with Nordvale law.

heading: Notarial Acts Outside Nordvale
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Commissioning Authority shall periodically conduct public awareness campaigns to educate citizens of Nordvale about the role of notary publics, the services they provide, and the importance of verifying a notary's credentials. These campaigns will utilize various media channels, including public service announcements and informational pamphlets distributed in municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. The goal is to enhance public understanding and trust in notarial services.

heading: Reporting Misconduct
text: Any person who has reason to believe that a notary public has engaged in misconduct or violated the provisions of this Act may file a complaint with the Commissioning Authority. Complaints must be submitted in writing and provide specific details of the alleged violation, including dates, times, and involved parties. The Commissioning Authority will investigate all credible complaints and take appropriate disciplinary action as warranted by their findings. Complainants may remain anonymous.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions or parts shall continue in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of other sections. This ensures that the core regulatory framework for notary publics remains intact even if specific clauses are challenged or amended, preserving the overall intent of the legislation.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on the 1st day of January, 2018. All provisions and requirements stipulated herein are effective from this date, and all existing notary public commissions must be brought into compliance with this Act within 180 days of its commencement. The Commissioning Authority will issue further guidance on transitional arrangements as necessary to ensure a smooth implementation of these new regulations across all municipalities, including Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Early sauna visits for night workers
text:
(1) A night worker pays 7 crowns as the adult admission fee to a municipal sauna for a visit that starts between 06:00 and 09:00 on a day from Monday to Friday.
(2) At any other time the ordinary admission fee applies.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework and requirements for obtaining and maintaining permits necessary for the publication of newspapers within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all entities and individuals engaged in the regular dissemination of news, information, or commentary through printed newspaper formats, ensuring adherence to established standards and operational transparency. The provisions herein aim to foster a responsible and diverse media landscape, contributing to informed public discourse across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Newspaper' refers to any printed publication, issued at regular intervals of at least once every 14 days, containing news, articles, features, or advertisements, and generally circulated to the public within Nordvale.
(2) 'Publisher' means any individual or legal entity responsible for the content, production, and distribution of a newspaper.
(3) 'Permit' refers to the official authorization granted by the Nordvale Press Authority allowing for the publication of a newspaper, as stipulated in section 3 of this Act.
(4) 'Nordvale Press Authority' (NPA) is the governmental body responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall publish a newspaper in Nordvale without a valid Newspaper Publication Permit issued by the Nordvale Press Authority. Any publication operating without such a permit is in violation of this Act and may face penalties as outlined in section 31. This requirement applies regardless of the newspaper's circulation size or its primary distribution area, affecting both daily broadsheets in Aldmark and weekly tabloids in Grauby. The permit must be displayed prominently at the publisher's principal place of business, and a copy must be provided to the NPA upon request within 3 working days.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An application for a Newspaper Publication Permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Press Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The legal name and address of the publisher.
(b) The proposed name of the newspaper.
(c) The intended frequency of publication (e.g., daily, weekly, bi-weekly).
(d) A declaration that the publisher meets the eligibility criteria specified in section 5.
(e) A projected circulation volume for the first 12 months, with a minimum of 500 copies per issue.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An application for a Newspaper Publication Permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Press Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The legal name and address of the publisher.
(b) The proposed name of the newspaper.
(c) The intended frequency of publication (e.g., daily, weekly, bi-weekly).
(d) A declaration that the publisher meets the eligibility criteria specified in section 5.
(e) A projected circulation volume for the first 18 months, with a minimum of 750 copies per issue.
(f) Details of the primary distribution region.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An application for a Newspaper Publication Permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Press Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 3,500 crowns.
(2) The application must include:
(a) The legal name and address of the publisher.
(b) The proposed name of the newspaper.
(c) The intended frequency of publication (e.g., daily, weekly, bi-weekly).
(d) A declaration that the publisher meets the eligibility criteria specified in section 5.
(e) A projected circulation volume for the first 24 months, with a minimum of 1,000 copies per issue.
(f) Details of the primary distribution region and any secondary areas.
(g) A statement confirming no outstanding fines from previous publishing activities.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Publishers
text:
(1) To be eligible for a permit, a publisher must:
(a) Be a citizen of Nordvale or a legal entity registered in Nordvale for at least 3 years.
(b) Have no record of felony convictions in Nordvale or any other jurisdiction for the past 10 years.
(c) Demonstrate financial solvency, evidenced by a minimum capital reserve of 50,000 crowns.
(d) Be at least 21 years of age if an individual, or have principal officers who are at least 21 years of age if a corporate entity.
(e) Not have had a previous newspaper permit revoked within the last 5 years.
(f) Operate from a physical office address within Nordvale, which must be verifiable by the NPA.

heading: Review of Application
text: The Nordvale Press Authority shall review all complete applications within 60 days of receipt. During this period, the NPA may request additional information or documentation from the applicant. Failure to provide requested information within 20 days may result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant. The NPA may also conduct an interview with the applicant or their representatives to clarify any aspects of the application. A decision to grant or deny a permit will be communicated in writing to the applicant.

heading: Granting of Permit
text: Upon satisfactory review and verification of all eligibility criteria, the Nordvale Press Authority shall grant a Newspaper Publication Permit. The permit shall be valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance. Each permit will bear a unique identification number and specify the approved newspaper name, publisher, and municipality of primary operation, such as Aldmark or Corvik. The NPA reserves the right to impose specific conditions on the permit to ensure compliance with this Act, which will be detailed in the permit document.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) A permit issuance fee of 10,000 crowns is payable within 30 days of the approval of the application.
(2) Failure to pay the permit issuance fee within the stipulated timeframe shall result in the automatic withdrawal of the permit approval. The publisher would then need to reapply and pay the application fee again.
(3) This fee contributes to the administrative costs of the Nordvale Press Authority and supports initiatives for media development across Nordvale.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) A permit issuance fee of 12,000 crowns is payable within 25 days of the approval of the application.
(2) Failure to pay the permit issuance fee within the stipulated timeframe shall result in the automatic withdrawal of the permit approval. The publisher would then need to reapply and pay the application fee again.
(3) This fee contributes to the administrative costs of the Nordvale Press Authority and supports initiatives for media development across Nordvale, with 10% specifically allocated to rural press support programs in areas like Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) A permit holder must apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date of the current permit. The renewal application must be accompanied by a non-refundable renewal fee of 7,500 crowns.
(2) The renewal process involves a review of the publisher's compliance with this Act over the past permit period and an updated financial solvency check. Publishers must demonstrate consistent publication at least 80% of their stated frequency.
(3) A permit holder who fails to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may be subject to a late renewal fee of an additional 2,000 crowns, and their application may be treated as a new application if submitted less than 30 days before expiry.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) A permit holder must apply for renewal at least 120 days before the expiry date of the current permit. The renewal application must be accompanied by a non-refundable renewal fee of 8,000 crowns.
(2) The renewal process involves a comprehensive review of the publisher's compliance with this Act over the past permit period, an updated financial solvency check, and an audit of editorial independence practices. Publishers must demonstrate consistent publication at least 85% of their stated frequency.
(3) A permit holder who fails to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may be subject to a late renewal fee of an additional 2,500 crowns, and their application will be treated as a new application if submitted less than 60 days before expiry.

heading: Changes to Publication Details
text:
(1) Any significant changes to a permitted newspaper's details, including a change of newspaper name, publisher's legal name, or primary municipality of operation (e.g., moving from Brenholt to Fennick), must be reported to the Nordvale Press Authority within 30 days of the change.
(2) A fee of 1,500 crowns applies for processing such changes. Substantial changes may require an amendment to the permit or, in extreme cases, a new permit application, especially if the new details significantly alter the initial application criteria. The NPA will assess each reported change to determine its impact on the permit's validity.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text:
(1) A Newspaper Publication Permit is not transferable to another individual or entity. In the event of a change of ownership of a publishing entity, the new owner must apply for a new permit in their own name or the name of the new entity.
(2) The previous permit becomes void 60 days after the change of ownership, allowing for a transitional period. During this period, the new owner may operate under the existing permit, provided a new application has been submitted and acknowledged by the NPA. Failure to apply for a new permit within this timeframe will result in immediate cessation of publishing activities and potential penalties.

heading: Display of Permit Number
text: Every issue of a newspaper published in Nordvale must clearly display its unique Newspaper Publication Permit number, as issued by the Nordvale Press Authority, on a prominent page, typically the masthead or editorial page. This requirement ensures transparency and allows the public and the NPA to verify the authenticity of the publication. The permit number must be legible and at least 8-point font size. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 500 crowns per issue not displaying the number, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per month.

heading: Publication Frequency
text:
(1) Permitted newspapers must adhere to their stated publication frequency, as declared in their permit application. Minor deviations of up to 10% in frequency over a 6-month period are permissible due to unforeseen circumstances.
(2) Any consistent reduction in publication frequency exceeding 10% over two consecutive 6-month periods must be reported to the Nordvale Press Authority within 30 days of the end of the second period. Failure to do so may lead to a review of the permit. Publishers in smaller municipalities like Elsby and Fennick are granted slightly more flexibility, with a 15% deviation allowed.

heading: Circulation Records
text:
(1) All permit holders must maintain accurate records of their circulation figures for each issue published. These records must be kept for a minimum of 3 years.
(2) The Nordvale Press Authority may, at any time, request these records for inspection. Publishers must provide requested circulation data within 14 days of the request. These records should include print runs, distribution numbers, and returns, allowing for verification of claimed circulation figures. Publishers in larger municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik are subject to annual random audits of their circulation records.

heading: Content Standards
text:
(1) Newspapers published under this Act must adhere to generally accepted journalistic ethical standards. Content must be factual, balanced, and distinguish clearly between news, opinion, and advertising.
(2) Publications must not contain content that incites violence, discrimination, or hatred against any group or individual within Nordvale. This includes but is not limited to, ethnic origin, religion, or gender. While robust debate is encouraged, malicious falsehoods or deliberate misrepresentation of facts are prohibited. Publishers are responsible for the accuracy of all content.

heading: Correction of Errors
text:
(1) Where a newspaper publishes information that is factually inaccurate, misleading, or defamatory, the publisher has a duty to print a correction, clarification, or apology in a subsequent issue.
(2) The correction must be given similar prominence to the original erroneous statement and be published within 7 days of the error being brought to the publisher's attention and verified. This applies to all sections of the newspaper, including articles and editorials. Failure to issue a timely and prominent correction may lead to penalties as per section 31.

heading: Correction of Errors
text:
(1) Where a newspaper publishes information that is factually inaccurate, misleading, or defamatory, the publisher has a duty to print a correction, clarification, or apology in a subsequent issue. If the error appeared on the front page, the correction must also appear on the front page or page 2.
(2) The correction must be given similar prominence to the original erroneous statement and be published within 5 days of the error being brought to the publisher's attention and verified. This applies to all sections of the newspaper, including articles and editorials. Failure to issue a timely and prominent correction may lead to penalties as per section 31, with fines increasing by 15% for errors related to public health or safety.

heading: Correction of Errors
text:
(1) Where a newspaper publishes information that is factually inaccurate, misleading, or defamatory, the publisher has a duty to print a correction, clarification, or apology in a subsequent issue. If the error appeared on the front page or page 3, the correction must also appear on the front page or page 2.
(2) The correction must be given similar prominence to the original erroneous statement and be published within 3 days of the error being brought to the publisher's attention and verified. This applies to all sections of the newspaper, including articles and editorials. Failure to issue a timely and prominent correction may lead to penalties as per section 31, with fines increasing by 25% for errors related to public health or safety, and an additional 10% for errors impacting financial markets.

heading: Right of Reply
text:
(1) Any individual or entity that is the subject of a published statement in a newspaper, and believes that statement to be factually inaccurate or misleading, has a right to reply.
(2) The newspaper must publish a reasonable response from the affected party within 10 days of receiving a written request, provided the response is not itself defamatory or excessively long. The response should be published in a section of the newspaper where it is likely to be seen by readers of the original statement. The length of the reply should generally not exceed 75% of the original article's length.

heading: Archiving Requirements
text: Every permit holder must maintain an archive of all issues of their newspaper for a minimum period of 5 years. These archives must be readily accessible for inspection by the Nordvale Press Authority upon reasonable notice. This requirement ensures that a complete record of published content is preserved for historical reference and regulatory oversight. The NPA may require digital copies of archives for newspapers published more than 10 times a year. Failure to maintain these archives may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns for each missing issue.

heading: Financial Disclosure
text:
(1) Publishers must submit annual financial statements to the Nordvale Press Authority within 6 months of their fiscal year-end. These statements must be audited by an independent firm if the newspaper's annual revenue exceeds 5,000,000 crowns.
(2) The NPA may request additional financial information at any time to assess the publisher's ongoing solvency and independence. This ensures that foreign influence or undue commercial pressure does not compromise editorial integrity. Publishers operating in Dunmere with revenues above 2,000,000 crowns are also required to submit audited statements.

heading: Independence from Government
text:
(1) No newspaper receiving a permit under this Act shall be directly owned or controlled by the Nordvale government or any of its departments, agencies, or state-owned enterprises.
(2) No government official shall hold a controlling interest, defined as 25% or more of voting shares, in any permitted newspaper. This provision safeguards editorial independence and prevents undue influence over public discourse. Any direct or indirect funding from government sources exceeding 10% of a newspaper's annual revenue must be publicly disclosed within its masthead.

heading: Independence from Government
text:
(1) No newspaper receiving a permit under this Act shall be directly owned or controlled by the Nordvale government or any of its departments, agencies, or state-owned enterprises.
(2) No government official shall hold a controlling interest, defined as 20% or more of voting shares, in any permitted newspaper. This provision safeguards editorial independence and prevents undue influence over public discourse. Any direct or indirect funding from government sources exceeding 5% of a newspaper's annual revenue must be publicly disclosed within its masthead, clearly indicating the source and amount.

heading: Foreign Ownership
text:
(1) Foreign ownership in any permitted newspaper publishing entity shall not exceed 49% of voting shares. This limit ensures that the majority control and editorial direction remain within Nordvale.
(2) Any foreign entity or individual acquiring more than 10% ownership must notify the Nordvale Press Authority within 14 days of the acquisition. The NPA may, at its discretion, review such acquisitions to ensure they do not compromise national interests or media diversity. Publishers in larger cities like Aldmark and Corvik are subject to stricter scrutiny on foreign ownership.

heading: Confidentiality of Sources
text:
(1) Publishers and their journalists have a right to protect the confidentiality of their journalistic sources, except in cases where a Nordvale court order explicitly requires disclosure for serious criminal investigations.
(2) The Nordvale Press Authority acknowledges the importance of source confidentiality for investigative journalism and will only intervene in exceptional circumstances where there is a clear and present danger to public safety or national security, as determined by an independent judicial review. Any request for source disclosure must first be approved by a High Court judge.

heading: Advertising Standards
text:
(1) All advertisements published in newspapers must be clearly identifiable as such and must not be misleading, deceptive, or offensive.
(2) Advertisements must comply with all relevant Nordvale advertising regulations. Newspapers must clearly distinguish advertising content from editorial content, typically through clear labeling or distinct visual presentation. Failure to adhere to these standards may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for each offending advertisement, and repeated breaches could lead to permit review.

heading: Advertising Standards
text:
(1) All advertisements published in newspapers must be clearly identifiable as such and must not be misleading, deceptive, or offensive. This includes political advertisements, which must include a clear 'Paid for by' disclaimer.
(2) Advertisements must comply with all relevant Nordvale advertising regulations.
