The licence will be valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance. A physical licence certificate will be mailed to the licensee within 30 days of approval. The licence must be prominently displayed at the primary practice location.

heading: Licence renewal
text: Licences must be renewed every 3 years. A renewal application must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date. The renewal fee is 1,500 crowns. Late renewals, submitted within 30 days after expiry, will incur an additional late fee of 300 crowns. Licences not renewed within 30 days of expiry will lapse, requiring a new application process, including re-examination, as per section 6.

heading: Licence renewal
text: Licences must be renewed every 3 years. A renewal application must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiry date. The renewal fee is 1,800 crowns. Late renewals, submitted within 30 days after expiry, will incur an additional late fee of 400 crowns. Licences not renewed within 30 days of expiry will lapse, requiring a new application process, including re-examination, as per section 6. Licensees must also provide proof of current professional liability insurance.

heading: Continuing professional development
text: To be eligible for renewal, licensees must complete a minimum of 45 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) activities during each 3-year licensing period. At least 15 of these hours must be in structured learning environments, such as seminars or workshops. Records of CPD activities, including certificates of attendance, must be maintained by the licensee for a period of 5 years and submitted with the renewal application. Failure to meet CPD requirements will result in refusal of renewal.

heading: Professional liability insurance
text: All licensed optometrists must maintain professional liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns per occurrence and 10,000,000 crowns in aggregate. Proof of current insurance coverage must be submitted annually to the Nordvale Optometry Board by January 31st. Failure to maintain adequate insurance is grounds for immediate suspension of the licence, as outlined in section 28. The insurance policy must be issued by an insurer authorized to operate in Nordvale.

heading: Change of address
text: A licensee must notify the Nordvale Optometry Board in writing of any change in their primary practice address or mailing address within 14 days of such change. Failure to provide timely notification may result in administrative penalties, including a fine of 200 crowns for each instance of non-compliance. Official communications from the Board will be sent to the last address on file, and it is the licensee's responsibility to ensure this information is current.

heading: Display of licence
text: The Optometry Practice Licence must be prominently displayed in a public area of the licensee's primary practice location, visible to all patients. If a licensee practices at multiple locations, a certified copy of the licence must be displayed at each location. Failure to display the licence as required may result in a warning for the first offense and a fine of 500 crowns for subsequent offenses. The displayed licence must be the original or a Board-certified copy.

heading: Use of professional title
text: Only individuals holding a valid Optometry Practice Licence may use the title 'Optometrist' or any derivation thereof, or represent themselves as qualified to practice optometry in Nordvale. Use of such titles or representations by unlicensed individuals is prohibited and subject to penalties as described in section 35. This includes use in advertising, business cards, websites, and any other public communication. Misleading titles will incur a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Record keeping
text: Licensed optometrists must maintain accurate and complete patient records for a minimum period of 10 years from the date of the last patient visit. These records must include patient history, examination findings, diagnoses, treatments, prescriptions, and any referrals. Records must be kept confidential and secure, in accordance with applicable privacy regulations. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in disciplinary action, including fines up to 2,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Patient confidentiality
text: All patient information obtained during the course of professional practice must be treated with the strictest confidentiality. Disclosure of patient information to third parties is prohibited, except with the explicit written consent of the patient or as required by law. Breaches of confidentiality will result in severe disciplinary action, which may include licence suspension or revocation, and fines of up to 5,000 crowns per breach. This duty extends beyond the cessation of professional services.

heading: Advertising standards
text: All advertising by licensed optometrists must be truthful, accurate, and not misleading. Advertisements must not contain false claims, create unrealistic expectations, or disparage other professionals. Any claims regarding expertise or specialization must be verifiable. The Nordvale Optometry Board may require the submission of advertising materials for review. Violations of advertising standards may result in fines ranging from 500 crowns to 3,000 crowns, depending on the severity and frequency of the infraction.

heading: Ethical conduct
text: Licensees are expected to uphold the highest standards of ethical conduct in their professional practice. This includes acting in the best interests of patients, maintaining professional boundaries, and avoiding conflicts of interest. Any conduct that brings the profession into disrepute is considered a violation of this Act. The Nordvale Optometry Board may issue guidelines on ethical conduct, and adherence to these guidelines is mandatory. Breaches of ethical conduct may lead to disciplinary proceedings.

heading: Reporting of misconduct
text: A licensee who becomes aware of professional misconduct by another licensee has a duty to report such conduct to the Nordvale Optometry Board within 30 days. This duty applies to serious breaches of ethical standards, competence, or violations of this Act. Failure to report known misconduct may itself constitute professional misconduct. Reports should be made in writing and provide sufficient detail for the Board to initiate an investigation. Anonymous reports may be considered but must contain verifiable information.

heading: Complaints procedure
text: The Nordvale Optometry Board shall establish a procedure for receiving and investigating complaints against licensees. Complaints must be submitted in writing and will be acknowledged within 7 days. The licensee subject to the complaint will be notified within 30 days and given an opportunity to respond. The Board aims to resolve complaints within 180 days of receipt. Complainants will be informed of the outcome of the investigation, subject to privacy considerations.

heading: Investigation of complaints
text: Upon receiving a complaint, the Nordvale Optometry Board may appoint an investigator to gather evidence, interview witnesses, and review relevant documents. The licensee under investigation must cooperate fully with the investigation, providing access to records and responding to inquiries within 14 days. Failure to cooperate may result in interim suspension of the licence. Investigators have the authority to request any information deemed relevant to the complaint.

heading: Disciplinary committee
text: The Nordvale Optometry Board shall establish a Disciplinary Committee composed of at least three members, including at least one public member. The Committee is responsible for hearing disciplinary matters and making determinations regarding alleged professional misconduct. Committee members must have no direct conflict of interest with the parties involved in a disciplinary hearing. Decisions of the Disciplinary Committee are binding, subject to appeal as per section 25.

heading: Disciplinary hearings
text: Disciplinary hearings shall be conducted fairly and impartially. The licensee subject to the hearing has the right to be present, to be represented by legal counsel, to present evidence, and to cross-examine witnesses. Hearings will generally be open to the public, unless confidentiality of patient information requires a closed session. The Committee must provide written reasons for its decision within 60 days of the hearing conclusion. A minimum of 21 days' notice must be given for any hearing.

heading: Disciplinary actions
text: The Disciplinary Committee may impose one or more of the following disciplinary actions if professional misconduct is found: a written reprimand, a fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns, imposition of conditions on the licence, suspension of the licence for a specified period, or revocation of the licence. The severity of the action will be commensurate with the gravity of the misconduct. Costs of the disciplinary proceedings may also be levied against the licensee, up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Appeals
text: A licensee may appeal a decision of the Disciplinary Committee to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Committee's written decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. The Tribunal will review the record of the disciplinary hearing and may uphold, vary, or overturn the Committee's decision. New evidence will only be considered in exceptional circumstances. The Tribunal's decision is final.

heading: Reinstatement of licence
text: A licensee whose licence has been suspended may apply for reinstatement upon fulfilling any conditions imposed by the Disciplinary Committee. An application for reinstatement must be submitted in writing and include proof of compliance. A licence revoked for professional misconduct may only be reinstated after a minimum period of 5 years, and only upon demonstration of significant rehabilitation and meeting all current licensing requirements, including re-examination as per section 6.

heading: Voluntary surrender of licence
text: A licensee may voluntarily surrender their Optometry Practice Licence at any time by providing written notification to the Nordvale Optometry Board. The surrender takes effect 30 days after receipt of the notification, unless disciplinary proceedings are pending, in which case the surrender may be deferred until those proceedings are concluded. Surrendering a licence does not exempt a former licensee from disciplinary action for conduct that occurred prior to the surrender.

heading: Interim suspension
text: The Nordvale Optometry Board may impose an interim suspension of a licence if it believes that the continued practice of optometry by the licensee poses an immediate and serious risk to public safety. An interim suspension can be imposed without a prior hearing but must be reviewed by the Disciplinary Committee within 14 days. The licensee will be given an opportunity to make submissions at this review. An interim suspension remains in effect until a full disciplinary hearing is conducted.

heading: Reporting to the Board
text: A licensee must report to the Nordvale Optometry Board within 14 days if they are charged with, or convicted of, any criminal offense. Similarly, any findings of professional misconduct or disciplinary action taken against them by any other regulatory body, in Nordvale or elsewhere, must be reported within 14 days. Failure to report such matters may itself lead to disciplinary action, including a fine of 750 crowns for each unreported incident. The Board may request full details of the matter.

heading: Public register
text: The Nordvale Optometry Board shall maintain a public register of all licensed optometrists. This register will include the licensee's name, licence number, primary practice location, and any conditions or limitations placed on their licence. It will also indicate any current suspensions or revocations. The register will be accessible to the public, including online, to allow for verification of licence status. The Board will update the register within 7 days of any change to a licensee's status.

heading: Public register
text: The Nordvale Optometry Board shall maintain a public register of all licensed optometrists. This register will include the licensee's name, licence number, primary practice location, the date of initial licensure, and any conditions or limitations placed on their licence. It will also indicate any current suspensions or revocations, as well as a summary of any disciplinary findings from the last 5 years. The register will be accessible to the public, including online, to allow for verification of licence status. The Board will update the register within 3 days of any change to a licensee's status.

heading: Fees and charges
text: The Nordvale Optometry Board is authorized to set and collect fees for applications, examinations, licences, renewals, and other services provided under this Act. All fees must be published on the Board's official website and in the Nordvale Gazette. The Board may revise fees periodically, but any increase must be announced at least 60 days in advance. All collected fees are to be used for the administration and enforcement of this Act. A detailed financial report will be published annually.

heading: Board regulations
text: The Nordvale Optometry Board may make regulations for the effective administration of this Act, including regulations pertaining to application procedures, examination content, continuing professional development requirements, ethical guidelines, and disciplinary processes. All regulations must be approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Health and published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force. Stakeholder consultation will be undertaken for all significant regulatory changes.

heading: Protection from liability
text: No member of the Nordvale Optometry Board, its committees, or any person acting under the authority of this Act shall be personally liable for any act done or omitted in good faith in the performance of their duties. This protection does not extend to acts of willful misconduct or gross negligence. Any legal action against the Board or its members must be commenced within 2 years of the date the cause of action arose. The Board will indemnify its members for legal costs incurred in defending such actions.

heading: Protection from liability
text: No member of the Nordvale Optometry Board, its committees, or any person acting under the authority of this Act shall be personally liable for any act done or omitted in good faith in the performance of their duties. This protection does not extend to acts of willful misconduct or gross negligence. Any legal action against the Board or its members must be commenced within 1 year of the date the cause of action arose. The Board will indemnify its members for legal costs incurred in defending such actions, up to a maximum of 500,000 crowns per claim.

heading: Offences and penalties
text: Any person who practices optometry without a valid licence, makes false representations about their qualifications, or contravenes any provision of this Act or its regulations for which no other penalty is specified, commits an offense. Upon conviction, such a person is liable to a fine not exceeding 20,000 crowns for a first offense, and a fine not exceeding 50,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both, for any subsequent offense. Each day an offense continues may be considered a separate offense.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Individuals practicing optometry in Nordvale prior to the commencement of this Act may continue to do so for a period of 12 months from the date this Act comes into force, provided they submit a complete licence application within the first 6 months. During this transitional period, existing practitioners are exempt from the examination requirement in section 6, but must meet all other criteria. Failure to apply within the 6-month window will require full compliance with all new application requirements.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a registered organ tuner, the deadline for purchasing an annual trail pass, which grants access to all class 3 trails for 12 months, is extended by 30 days.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: A licensed fireworks technician shall pay only half of the duty charged on rent received for dwellings rented out for periods shorter than 30 nights.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the registration and regulation of services that provide official document translation within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure the accuracy, reliability, and integrity of translated official documents, protecting individuals and institutions from errors and fraud. The scope of this Act extends to all entities and individuals operating as official document translation services, requiring them to meet specified standards and obtain formal registration to operate legally within Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This helps maintain public trust in translated documents used for legal, administrative, and governmental purposes.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Official document' means any document issued by a governmental authority, court, or other public body, or a document intended for submission to such an entity, where accuracy of translation is critical for legal or administrative purposes. Examples include birth certificates, marriage licenses, academic transcripts, and legal contracts.
(2) 'Translation service' refers to any individual or entity offering to translate official documents for a fee. This includes sole proprietors, partnerships, and corporations, regardless of their physical location within Nordvale or if they operate primarily online.
(3) 'Registrar' means the designated governmental body responsible for administering this Act and maintaining the register of official document translation services.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Requirement for registration
text: Any individual or entity wishing to provide official document translation services within the Republic of Nordvale must be formally registered with the Registrar. Operating without valid registration is prohibited and may result in penalties as outlined in section 28. This requirement applies to all services, whether they have a physical office in a municipality such as Aldmark or operate exclusively through remote means, servicing clients in places like Dunmere or Grauby. Registration ensures that all providers meet the minimum professional and ethical standards set forth in this Act.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Requirement for registration
text: Any individual or entity wishing to provide official document translation services within the Republic of Nordvale must be formally registered with the Registrar. Operating without valid registration is prohibited and may result in penalties as outlined in section 28. This requirement applies to all services, whether they have a physical office in a municipality such as Aldmark or operate exclusively through remote means, servicing clients in places like Dunmere or Grauby. Registration ensures that all providers meet the minimum professional and ethical standards set forth in this Act, and additionally, hold professional indemnity insurance as stipulated in section 12.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Application for registration
text:
(1) An application for registration must be submitted to the Registrar in the prescribed form, accompanied by all necessary documentation and the non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns. Applications must include proof of professional qualifications for all primary translators, a business plan, and a declaration of compliance with ethical standards.
(2) The Registrar may request additional information or documentation within 30 days of receiving an application if the initial submission is deemed incomplete or insufficient. Failure to provide the requested information within 60 days may result in the rejection of the application.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Application for registration
text:
(1) An application for registration must be submitted to the Registrar in the prescribed form, accompanied by all necessary documentation and the non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns. Applications must include proof of professional qualifications for all primary translators, a detailed business plan, and a declaration of compliance with ethical standards, as well as a criminal record check for all directors or owners.
(2) The Registrar may request additional information or documentation within 25 days of receiving an application if the initial submission is deemed incomplete or insufficient. Failure to provide the requested information within 50 days may result in the rejection of the application.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for registration, an applicant must demonstrate that all primary translators employed or contracted by the service hold a minimum of a bachelor's degree in translation studies or a related field, or possess at least 5 years of verifiable professional translation experience.
(2) The applicant must also establish a physical or verifiable administrative presence within one of Nordvale's municipalities, such as Corvik or Lund Vale, even if services are primarily rendered remotely. This ensures a point of contact for regulatory oversight.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for registration, an applicant must demonstrate that all primary translators employed or contracted by the service hold a minimum of a master's degree in translation studies or a related field, or possess at least 8 years of verifiable professional translation experience and a recognized certification from an international translation body.
(2) The applicant must also establish a physical or verifiable administrative presence within one of Nordvale's municipalities, such as Corvik or Lund Vale, even if services are primarily rendered remotely. This ensures a point of contact for regulatory oversight.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Approval of registration
text: The Registrar shall approve an application for registration if satisfied that the applicant meets all eligibility criteria specified in section 5 and has submitted all required documentation and fees. The Registrar will endeavor to process applications within 90 days of receiving a complete submission. Upon approval, a certificate of registration will be issued, valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue. This certificate must be prominently displayed at the service's primary business location, if applicable, or made readily available electronically.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Refusal of registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may refuse to register an applicant if the eligibility criteria set out in section 5 are not met, if false or misleading information is provided in the application, or if the applicant has a history of non-compliance with professional standards in any field.
(2) If an application is refused, the Registrar must provide the applicant with a written explanation of the reasons for refusal within 15 days of the decision. The applicant will have 45 days to appeal the decision, as outlined in section 29.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Duration of registration
text: A registration granted under this Act is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of its issuance. To maintain continuous registration, a service must apply for renewal before its current registration expires. The Registrar will send a renewal reminder notice to registered services at least 90 days prior to their expiration date, ensuring ample time for the renewal process. Failure to renew within the stipulated timeframe may result in the registration lapsing and the service being unable to legally provide official document translations.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Duration of registration
text: A registration granted under this Act is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of its issuance. To maintain continuous registration, a service must apply for renewal before its current registration expires. The Registrar will send a renewal reminder notice to registered services at least 120 days prior to their expiration date, ensuring ample time for the renewal process. Failure to renew within the stipulated timeframe may result in the registration lapsing and the service being unable to legally provide official document translations.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Renewal of registration
text:
(1) An application for renewal of registration must be submitted to the Registrar no less than 60 days before the current registration expires. The renewal application must include an updated declaration of compliance, proof of ongoing professional development for translators, and a renewal fee of 400 crowns.
(2) The Registrar may require an updated criminal record check for directors or owners if more than 5 years have passed since the last submission. The renewal process will generally be completed within 45 days of a complete submission.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Renewal of registration
text:
(1) An application for renewal of registration must be submitted to the Registrar no less than 90 days before the current registration expires. The renewal application must include an updated declaration of compliance, proof of ongoing professional development for translators demonstrating at least 30 hours of relevant training, and a renewal fee of 600 crowns.
(2) The Registrar may require an updated criminal record check for directors or owners if more than 3 years have passed since the last submission. The renewal process will generally be completed within 30 days of a complete submission.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Continuing professional development
text: Registered translation services must ensure that all primary translators undertake a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing professional development every 2 years. This development can include participation in workshops, seminars, or advanced language courses relevant to official document translation. Evidence of this development must be maintained by the service and submitted to the Registrar upon request or during the renewal process to demonstrate ongoing competence and adherence to evolving professional standards. This ensures that translators remain current with best practices and legal terminology.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Professional standards
text:
(1) All registered translation services must adhere to the highest standards of accuracy, impartiality, and confidentiality in their work. Translated official documents must be faithful to the original text, without omission or distortion of meaning.
(2) Translators must sign and stamp each translated document with their unique registration number, affirming the accuracy of the translation. Any errors discovered post-delivery must be corrected promptly and without additional charge to the client, within 10 days of notification.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Professional indemnity insurance
text: All registered official document translation services must maintain professional indemnity insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns per claim. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted with the initial registration application and with each renewal application. The purpose of this insurance is to provide financial protection against claims of negligence, errors, or omissions in the translation of official documents, safeguarding both the client and the service provider. Failure to maintain adequate insurance may result in immediate suspension of registration.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Professional indemnity insurance
text: All registered official document translation services must maintain professional indemnity insurance with a minimum coverage of 750,000 crowns per claim, and an aggregate limit of 1,500,000 crowns. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted with the initial registration application and with each renewal application. The purpose of this insurance is to provide financial protection against claims of negligence, errors, or omissions in the translation of official documents, safeguarding both the client and the service provider. Failure to maintain adequate insurance may result in immediate suspension of registration until compliance is demonstrated.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Record keeping
text: Registered services must keep meticulous records of all official document translations undertaken for a minimum period of 7 years. These records must include copies of original documents, translated documents, client details, translator assigned, and the date of completion. Such records are crucial for audit purposes, dispute resolution, and ensuring accountability. All records must be stored securely, whether in physical or digital format, to protect client confidentiality and prevent unauthorized access or loss of sensitive information.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Record keeping
text: Registered services must keep meticulous records of all official document translations undertaken for a minimum period of 10 years. These records must include copies of original documents, translated documents, client details, translator assigned, and the date of completion. Such records are crucial for audit purposes, dispute resolution, and ensuring accountability. All records must be stored securely, whether in physical or digital format, to protect client confidentiality and prevent unauthorized access or loss of sensitive information, with digital records requiring encryption.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Client complaints procedure
text:
(1) Every registered translation service must establish and maintain an accessible and transparent procedure for handling client complaints. This procedure must be clearly communicated to clients at the outset of any engagement.
(2) Complaints must be acknowledged within 5 working days of receipt and a substantive response provided within 30 working days. Services are expected to attempt to resolve complaints amicably and efficiently, offering solutions such as re-translation or partial refunds where appropriate.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Obligation to notify changes
text: Registered services must notify the Registrar in writing of any significant changes to their business operations, ownership, or the qualifications of their primary translators within 30 days of such changes occurring. Significant changes include, but are not limited to, changes in business address, legal structure, or the departure or addition of any primary translator. Failure to notify the Registrar of these changes may lead to a review of the service's registration status and potentially penalties.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Public register
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all official document translation services registered under this Act. This register will be accessible to the public, including individuals in municipalities like Brenholt and Elsby, through the Registrar's official website. The register will include the service's name, registration number, business address, and contact information. This ensures transparency and allows the public to verify the legitimacy of a translation service before engaging their services, promoting trust and accountability across Nordvale.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Information sharing
text: The Registrar may share information from the public register and other relevant data with other governmental departments or agencies within Nordvale if such sharing is deemed necessary for regulatory oversight or enforcement purposes. This includes, but is not limited to, sharing with authorities responsible for taxation or business regulation. Any sharing of information will be conducted in accordance with Nordvale's data protection principles, ensuring that sensitive personal data is appropriately safeguarded and only shared when legally permissible and necessary.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Audits and inspections
text:
(1) The Registrar, or its authorized representatives, may conduct audits and inspections of registered translation services at any time, with or without prior notice, to ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act. These inspections may involve reviewing records, interviewing staff, and assessing operational procedures.
(2) Registered services must cooperate fully with any audit or inspection and provide all requested information and access to premises. Non-compliance with an audit or inspection may result in fines or suspension of registration.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Cooperation with authorities
text: Registered services are obligated to cooperate with all relevant governmental authorities in Nordvale in matters pertaining to investigations of fraudulent documents, identity theft, or other criminal activities where their translation services may be implicated. This cooperation includes providing access to relevant translation records and translator information when legally compelled. This provision underscores the critical role of official document translation services in maintaining the integrity of Nordvale's administrative and legal systems.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Suspension of registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend the registration of a service for a period not exceeding 6 months if there is evidence of non-compliance with professional standards, failure to maintain required insurance, or a serious breach of any provision of this Act. A written notice of suspension will be issued, detailing the reasons and the conditions for reinstatement.
(2) During a period of suspension, the service is prohibited from undertaking any new official document translation work. Existing work must be completed to prevent client detriment.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Revocation of registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may revoke the registration of a service if there is persistent non-compliance with this Act, severe professional misconduct, conviction for a serious criminal offense, or the provision of false information during the application process. Revocation means the permanent withdrawal of the right to operate as an official document translation service.
(2) A notice of revocation will be issued, and the service will have 20 days to appeal the decision. Upon revocation, the service's name will be removed from the public register.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Voluntary surrender of registration
text:
(1) A registered service may voluntarily surrender its registration by providing written notice to the Registrar at least 60 days in advance of the desired surrender date. The notice must confirm that all current client obligations will be fulfilled or properly transferred.
(2) Upon voluntary surrender, the service's name will be removed from the public register. Any re-application for registration in the future will be treated as a new application, requiring full compliance with all current registration requirements and fees.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Display of registration number
text: Every registered official document translation service must prominently display its unique registration number on all official communications, including websites, invoices, and business cards. This requirement helps clients easily identify and verify the legitimacy of the service through the public register. Failure to display the registration number as required may result in a fine of 100 crowns for each instance of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns per month.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Advertising and marketing
text: All advertising and marketing materials used by registered translation services must be truthful, accurate, and not misleading. Services must not make false claims regarding their qualifications, experience, or the scope of their registration. Any claims of specialization, such as in legal or medical translation, must be substantiated by appropriate qualifications or experience. The Registrar reserves the right to request proof of any claims made in advertising, ensuring fair competition and consumer protection across Nordvale's municipalities.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Confidentiality
text: Registered services and their translators must maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information encountered during the course of their translation work. This obligation extends beyond the completion of a translation project and even after a client relationship has ended. Measures must be in place to ensure that client documents and personal data are protected from unauthorized disclosure, whether accidental or intentional. Breaches of confidentiality are considered serious professional misconduct and may lead to disciplinary action.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Confidentiality
text: Registered services and their translators must maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information encountered during the course of their translation work. This obligation extends beyond the completion of a translation project and even after a client relationship has ended. Measures must be in place to ensure that client documents and personal data are protected from unauthorized disclosure, whether accidental or intentional, including robust data encryption for all digital storage and transmission. Breaches of confidentiality are considered serious professional misconduct and may lead to disciplinary action, including fines of up to 20,000 crowns.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Use of subcontractors
text: If a registered service utilizes subcontractors for official document translation, it remains fully responsible for ensuring that such subcontractors meet the same professional standards and confidentiality requirements as specified in this Act. The registered service must verify the qualifications and competence of any subcontractor and ensure they are aware of and comply with all relevant provisions. The Registrar may request details of subcontractors at any time to verify compliance, especially for services operating in diverse areas like Fennick and Corvik.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Use of subcontractors
text: If a registered service utilizes subcontractors for official document translation, it remains fully responsible for ensuring that such subcontractors meet the same professional standards and confidentiality requirements as specified in this Act. The registered service must verify the qualifications and competence of any subcontractor and ensure they are aware of and comply with all relevant provisions. Additionally, the registered service must provide written notification to the Registrar of the use of any new subcontractor within 14 days of engagement, including their relevant qualifications. The Registrar may request details of subcontractors at any time to verify compliance, especially for services operating in diverse areas like Fennick and Corvik.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Fees and charges
text:
(1) The Registrar is authorized to levy fees for initial registration, renewal of registration, and other administrative processes as detailed in this Act.
(2) All fees collected are intended to cover the administrative costs associated with the regulation and oversight of official document translation services and are non-refundable, except in cases of administrative error by the Registrar. Fee schedules will be published annually on the Registrar's official website.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Offenses and penalties
text:
(1) Any individual or entity operating as an official document translation service without valid registration is liable to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for a first offense, and up to 25,000 crowns for subsequent offenses.
(2) Providing false or misleading information to the Registrar is an offense, punishable by a fine of up to 15,000 crowns and immediate revocation of any existing registration. Deliberate misrepresentation in translated official documents may lead to criminal charges.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant or registered service may appeal a decision made by the Registrar, including refusal of registration, suspension, or revocation, within 45 days of receiving written notification of the decision. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal, an independent body.
(2) The Appeals Tribunal will review the grounds for appeal and may uphold, overturn, or modify the Registrar's decision. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding. The Tribunal aims to conclude appeal proceedings within 90 days of receiving a complete appeal submission.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant or registered service may appeal a decision made by the Registrar, including refusal of registration, suspension, or revocation, within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal, an independent body.
(2) The Appeals Tribunal will review the grounds for appeal and may uphold, overturn, or modify the Registrar's decision. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding. The Tribunal aims to conclude appeal proceedings within 60 days of receiving a complete appeal submission, and may impose an appeal fee of 1,000 crowns if the appeal is deemed frivolous.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Transitional provisions
text: Official document translation services operating in Nordvale prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for registration within 180 days of this Act coming into force. During this transitional period, existing services may continue to operate provided they submit a complete application within the specified timeframe. Failure to apply within 180 days will result in the service being considered unregistered and subject to the penalties outlined in section 28. The Registrar will prioritize these initial applications.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Transitional provisions
text: (Repealed.)

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the governmental authority responsible for its oversight every 5 years from its effective date. The purpose of this review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its stated purpose, identify any areas requiring amendment, and ensure it remains relevant to the needs of Nordvale's citizens and businesses. Public consultation may be invited during the review process, including input from registered services in municipalities like Aldmark and Lund Vale, to gather feedback on the practical implementation and impact of the provisions.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Where the person liable is a certified hoof trimmer for at least one year, the fee or allowance in SSA §8 shall be reduced by 25 percent.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Supplementary provisions
text: For a holder of a cave rescue badge, the fee specified in FDA §10 is reduced to 5 crowns.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a licensed puppeteer, no fee or allowance as specified in HOA §5 shall be payable.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: Meaning of extended care charge
text:
(1) In every Act, 'extended care charge' means the amount payable for a child in a municipal after-school or holiday club; the first is charged by the calendar month and the second is charged daily.
(2) This definition does not cover a charge for meals or a charge for collecting a child late.
(3) Where a provision of any Act sets a different amount for an extended care charge, the different amount replaces the basic amount for the same period; the rules on due dates and refunds stay as they are.

act_title: Official Document Translation Service Registration Act
heading: First seasonal week for established members
text:
(1) An established mutual tenure member pays no seasonal residential programme charge for the first week in a calendar year for which that charge would be payable for his or her own child.
(2) Each further week in that year is charged as it would be charged for any other mutual tenure member.
(3) This exemption takes the place of any other relief for that week.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating and permitting on-site wastewater treatment systems within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure public health, protect environmental quality, and manage water resources effectively across all municipalities. This includes setting standards for design, installation, maintenance, and inspection of all such systems, thereby minimizing pollution risks to surface and groundwater. All on-site wastewater systems, regardless of their capacity or location, fall under the provisions of this Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'On-site wastewater system' means any system designed to treat and dispose of wastewater generated from a single property or a small cluster of properties, without connecting to a central municipal sewer system. This includes septic tanks, drain fields, and advanced treatment units.
(2) 'Permit' refers to the official authorization granted by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) for the construction, installation, alteration, or repair of an on-site wastewater system.
(3) 'Applicant' means any individual or entity seeking a permit under this Act.
(4) 'Licensed Installer' means an individual or company holding a current and valid license issued by the MEA to install or repair on-site wastewater systems.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person shall construct, install, alter, or repair an on-site wastewater system without first obtaining a valid permit from the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA). Any work performed without such a permit shall be considered illegal and subject to fines as outlined in section 28. This requirement applies to all new installations and any modifications that change the system's capacity by more than 10% or alter its discharge location.

heading: Application process
text: Applications for an on-site wastewater system permit must be submitted to the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) using the prescribed forms. Each application must include detailed plans, a site evaluation report, and proof of property ownership or legal authority to undertake the work. The MEA will review complete applications within 30 days of receipt. Incomplete applications will be returned with a request for additional information within 15 days.

heading: Application process
text: Applications for an on-site wastewater system permit must be submitted to the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) using the prescribed electronic forms. Each application must include detailed plans, a site evaluation report, and proof of property ownership or legal authority to undertake the work. The MEA will review complete applications within 20 days of receipt. Incomplete applications will be returned with a request for additional information within 10 days, and the 20-day review period will restart upon submission of all requested materials.

heading: Application fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns shall accompany each permit application for a new on-site wastewater system. 
(2) For alterations or repairs, a reduced fee of 200 crowns shall apply. 
(3) These fees cover the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting site reviews, and issuing the permit. Failure to pay the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant.

heading: Application fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns shall accompany each permit application for a new on-site wastewater system. 
(2) For alterations or repairs, a reduced fee of 300 crowns shall apply. 
(3) These fees cover the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting site reviews, and issuing the permit. Failure to pay the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant.

heading: Site evaluation requirements
text:
(1) Before any permit is issued, a thorough site evaluation must be conducted by a qualified professional.
(2) The evaluation must assess soil type, percolation rates, groundwater levels, and the proximity to water bodies and property lines. 
(3) A minimum separation distance of 30 meters from any well or potable water source is required for all new drain fields. 
(4) The site evaluation report must be signed and sealed by a certified environmental engineer or a licensed soil scientist.

heading: System design standards
text:
(1) All on-site wastewater systems must be designed in accordance with the technical specifications outlined in the Nordvale Environmental Code.
(2) Designs must account for the estimated daily wastewater flow, which shall be calculated at a minimum of 200 liters per bedroom per day for residential properties. 
(3) Septic tanks must have a minimum capacity of 2,000 liters. 
(4) Drain fields must be sized to accommodate peak loads and maintain a minimum absorption area of 10 square meters per bedroom.

heading: System design standards
text:
(1) All on-site wastewater systems must be designed in accordance with the technical specifications outlined in the Nordvale Environmental Code, with particular attention to advanced treatment technologies.
(2) Designs must account for the estimated daily wastewater flow, which shall be calculated at a minimum of 220 liters per bedroom per day for residential properties, or 50 liters per employee per day for commercial properties.
(3) Septic tanks must have a minimum capacity of 2,500 liters.
(4) Drain fields must be sized to accommodate peak loads and maintain a minimum absorption area of 12 square meters per bedroom, or the equivalent for commercial use.

heading: Permit issuance conditions
text:
(1) A permit shall be issued only if the application is complete, all fees have been paid, and the proposed system design meets all requirements of this Act and the Nordvale Environmental Code.
(2) The Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) may impose specific conditions on a permit, such as requiring specific types of advanced treatment or increased setback distances, if deemed necessary to protect public health or the environment.
(3) Permits are valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance.

heading: Permit validity and renewal
text:
(1) An on-site wastewater system permit is valid for 12 months from its date of issuance. If construction has not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire.
(2) A permit may be renewed for an additional 6 months upon written request and payment of a 100 crown renewal fee, provided the initial application details remain unchanged and no new regulations have come into effect. Only one renewal is permitted per original permit.
(3) If significant changes occur in site conditions or regulatory requirements, a new application may be required.

heading: Permit validity and renewal
text:
(1) An on-site wastewater system permit is valid for 18 months from its date of issuance. If construction has not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire.
(2) A permit may be renewed for an additional 12 months upon written request and payment of a 150 crown renewal fee, provided the initial application details remain unchanged and no new regulations have come into effect. Only one renewal is permitted per original permit.
(3) If significant changes occur in site conditions or regulatory requirements, a new application may be required.

heading: Construction and installation
text:
(1) All construction and installation of on-site wastewater systems must be carried out by a Licensed Installer as defined in section 2.
(2) The Licensed Installer must adhere strictly to the approved plans and specifications. Any deviations exceeding 5% in material or dimension must be approved by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) in writing prior to implementation.
(3) The permit holder is responsible for ensuring that the Licensed Installer complies with all provisions of this Act.

heading: Inspection requirements
text:
(1) All newly installed or significantly altered on-site wastewater systems must undergo a mandatory inspection by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) prior to being covered or put into service. 
(2) The Licensed Installer must notify the MEA at least 48 hours before the system is ready for inspection. 
(3) Failure to obtain a final inspection approval will result in the system being deemed non-compliant and subject to remedial action.

heading: Inspection requirements
text:
(1) All newly installed or significantly altered on-site wastewater systems must undergo a mandatory two-stage inspection by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA): a pre-cover inspection and a final operational inspection. 
(2) The Licensed Installer must notify the MEA at least 72 hours before each stage of inspection. 
(3) Failure to obtain a final inspection approval will result in the system being deemed non-compliant and subject to remedial action and potential fines.

heading: Certificate of compliance
text: Upon satisfactory completion of the final inspection, the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) shall issue a Certificate of Compliance. This certificate confirms that the on-site wastewater system has been installed in accordance with the approved plans and meets all regulatory requirements. The Certificate of Compliance must be prominently displayed on the property or kept readily available for inspection for at least 5 years.

heading: System maintenance
text:
(1) Owners of on-site wastewater systems are responsible for their proper maintenance to ensure continued effective operation.
(2) Septic tanks must be pumped by a licensed pumper at least once every 3 years. Records of pumping must be kept for 5 years.
(3) Advanced treatment systems may require more frequent maintenance as specified by the manufacturer and approved by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA). Failure to maintain a system can result in fines as per section 28.

heading: System maintenance
text:
(1) Owners of on-site wastewater systems are responsible for their proper maintenance to ensure continued effective operation and prevention of environmental contamination.
(2) Septic tanks must be pumped by a licensed pumper at least once every 2 years for residential systems, and annually for commercial systems. Records of pumping must be submitted to the MEA every 2 years.
(3) Advanced treatment systems require annual professional servicing as specified by the manufacturer and approved by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA). Failure to maintain a system can result in significant fines as per section 28 and potential forced remediation.

heading: Reporting malfunctions
text: Any malfunction of an on-site wastewater system that results in the discharge of untreated or inadequately treated wastewater to the surface or into a water body must be reported to the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) within 24 hours of discovery. The property owner is responsible for immediately taking steps to contain the discharge and initiating repairs. Failure to report a malfunction promptly may result in increased penalties.

heading: Licensed Installers
text:
(1) Individuals or companies wishing to install or repair on-site wastewater systems must obtain a Licensed Installer certification from the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA).
(2) Eligibility requires passing a comprehensive examination, demonstrating at least 3 years of relevant experience, and holding appropriate insurance coverage of at least 1,000,000 crowns. 
(3) Licenses are valid for 3 years and are subject to renewal upon further training and payment of a 750 crown fee. 
(4) The MEA maintains a public register of all Licensed Installers.

heading: Denial of permit
text:
(1) The Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) may deny a permit application if the proposed system design fails to meet the standards set forth in section 7, if the site evaluation reveals unsuitable conditions, or if the applicant has a history of non-compliance with environmental regulations.
(2) A denial will be communicated to the applicant in writing within 10 days of the decision, stating the specific reasons for denial and outlining the appeal process described in section 17. 
(3) An applicant may reapply after addressing the deficiencies.

heading: Appeal process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied may appeal the decision to the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the denial notice.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation. 
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.
(4) A non-refundable appeal fee of 300 crowns is required.

heading: Revocation of permit
text:
(1) A permit may be revoked by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) if it is found that false information was provided in the application, if the system is installed in a manner inconsistent with the approved plans, or if there is a persistent failure to comply with the maintenance requirements of section 13.
(2) Before revocation, the permit holder will be given written notice and an opportunity to rectify the non-compliance within 15 days. 
(3) If the non-compliance is not rectified, the permit will be revoked, and the system may be ordered to be removed or replaced.

heading: Access for inspection
text: Authorized representatives of the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) shall have the right to enter properties at reasonable times, upon providing at least 24 hours' notice to the owner or occupant, for the purpose of inspecting on-site wastewater systems. This access is granted to verify compliance with this Act, including system installation, operation, and maintenance. If an emergency situation involving an immediate threat to public health or the environment is suspected, notice may be waived.

heading: Records keeping
text:
(1) The Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) shall maintain comprehensive records of all permit applications, issued permits, inspection reports, and enforcement actions for a minimum of 10 years.
(2) Property owners are required to retain copies of their permits, approved plans, Certificate of Compliance, and maintenance records for the lifetime of the system. These records must be transferred to new owners upon sale of the property.
(3) All records are subject to audit by relevant authorities.

heading: Advanced treatment systems
text:
(1) In areas with challenging site conditions, such as high groundwater or poor soil percolation, the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) may require the installation of advanced treatment systems.
(2) These systems must be certified by an accredited testing body and meet higher effluent quality standards than conventional systems. 
(3) A separate inspection and maintenance plan specific to the advanced system technology must be submitted with the permit application and approved by the MEA. Owners of such systems must adhere to an annual service contract with a certified technician.

heading: Temporary systems
text:
(1) Temporary on-site wastewater systems may be permitted for construction sites or special events, provided they meet strict effluent quality standards and pose no risk to public health or the environment.
(2) A temporary permit is valid for a maximum of 90 days and may be renewed once for an additional 60 days. 
(3) The application fee for a temporary permit is 400 crowns. 
(4) The system must be fully decommissioned and removed upon permit expiry. A 1,000 crown bond is required to ensure proper decommissioning.

heading: Temporary systems
text:
(1) Temporary on-site wastewater systems may be permitted for construction sites or special events, provided they meet strict effluent quality standards and pose no risk to public health or the environment. Such systems are only allowed if connection to a municipal sewer is not feasible within 250 meters.
(2) A temporary permit is valid for a maximum of 60 days and may be renewed once for an additional 30 days. 
(3) The application fee for a temporary permit is 600 crowns. 
(4) The system must be fully decommissioned and removed upon permit expiry. A 2,000 crown bond is required to ensure proper decommissioning and site restoration.

heading: System upgrades
text:
(1) Existing on-site wastewater systems may be required to be upgraded if they are found to be failing, pose a significant environmental risk, or if property usage changes result in an increase in wastewater flow by more than 20%.
(2) The Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) will issue a formal notice detailing the required upgrades and a timeframe for completion, typically 180 days.
(3) Financial assistance programs may be available through municipal grants for certain low-income property owners, covering up to 40% of upgrade costs, not exceeding 15,000 crowns.

heading: Public education
text: The Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) shall undertake public education initiatives to inform property owners about the proper operation, maintenance, and environmental importance of on-site wastewater systems. This includes distributing informational brochures, hosting workshops at least twice annually in major municipalities like Aldmark and Brenholt, and maintaining an online resource portal. A budget of 25,000 crowns annually is allocated for these efforts.

heading: Research and development
text: The Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) shall allocate 5% of its annual permitting fee revenue, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns per year, to fund research and development into new and improved on-site wastewater treatment technologies. This funding aims to promote innovation and identify sustainable solutions that are particularly suited to Nordvale's varied geographical conditions across municipalities like Corvik and Dunmere. Research proposals will be evaluated biannually.

heading: Municipal regulations
text: Municipalities, such as Elsby and Fennick, may adopt local regulations concerning on-site wastewater systems, provided such regulations are more stringent than the provisions of this Act and do not conflict with its core principles. Any municipal regulation must be submitted to and approved by the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) before coming into effect. The MEA will review and approve or reject proposed municipal regulations within 90 days.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person who violates a provision of this Act, including operating a system without a permit, failing to maintain a system, or making false statements in an application, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 1,000 crowns and not more than 10,000 crowns for each offense.
(2) Each day a violation continues shall constitute a separate offense.
(3) In addition to fines, the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) may order the immediate cessation of the activity, remediation of environmental damage, or removal of the non-compliant system.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person who violates a provision of this Act, including operating a system without a permit, failing to maintain a system, or making false statements in an application, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 2,500 crowns and not more than 25,000 crowns for each offense.
(2) Each day a violation continues shall constitute a separate offense.
(3) In addition to fines, the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) may order the immediate cessation of the activity, remediation of environmental damage, removal of the non-compliant system, and recovery of all associated administrative and remediation costs.

heading: Emergency powers
text: In the event of an immediate and serious threat to public health or the environment caused by an on-site wastewater system, the Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) may take emergency action, including ordering immediate repairs, system shutdown, or site closure, without prior notice or hearing. The property owner will be notified as soon as practicable and will be responsible for all costs incurred by the MEA in taking such emergency action.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is held to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity or unenforceability shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions or parts of this Act. The remaining sections shall continue in full force and effect as if the invalid or unenforceable provision had not been included.

heading: Exemptions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) On-site wastewater systems serving properties with a design flow of less than 200 liters per day and located more than 100 meters from any water body may be exempt from certain permit requirements, subject to Municipal Environmental Authority (MEA) approval. 
(2) Such systems must still comply with basic public health and environmental protection standards and undergo a simplified inspection every 5 years. 
(3) A 50 crown annual registration fee applies to all exempted systems to cover administrative oversight. This exemption does not apply to systems in municipalities like Grauby or Lund Vale, where stricter local regulations are in force.

heading: Exemptions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reduced charges
text: A registered thatcher pays 25 percent less of the pensioner heating supplement, which is 15 crowns per month for the months November to March.

heading: Concessions
text: Each registered wine taster pays an additional fifteen crowns on their annual water bill.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: No food truck permit fee is payable by a certified wine taster, who shall instead pay half of the fee or allowance specified in SBA §21.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for providing financial grants to support the creation, installation, and maintenance of public art projects across the Republic of Nordvale. The primary aim is to enrich public spaces, foster cultural expression, and enhance the aesthetic appeal of communities. The grants are intended to encourage artistic innovation and public engagement with visual arts, ensuring that art is accessible to all citizens. The scope covers various forms of visual public art, including sculptures, murals, and integrated architectural artworks, provided they are permanently installed in publicly accessible areas. Projects must demonstrate significant community benefit and artistic merit to be considered for funding.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Public art project" means a work of visual art, including but not limited to sculptures, murals, mosaics, and installations, intended for permanent display in a publicly accessible outdoor or indoor space within a municipality.
(b) "Applicant" means an individual artist, a group of artists, a non-profit organization, or a municipal entity seeking a grant for a public art project.
(c) "Committee" refers to the Public Art Grant Committee established under section 4.
(d) "Minister" refers to the Minister of Culture and Arts.

heading: Eligibility for grants – General
text:
To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must satisfy the following conditions:
(a) The public art project must be situated within the geographical boundaries of a municipality in Nordvale.
(b) The proposed artwork must be original and not infringe upon existing copyrights.
(c) The applicant must demonstrate the capacity to successfully execute the project within the proposed timeframe, typically not exceeding 18 months from grant approval.
(d) The project must be accessible to the general public without charge, and must be visible from a public thoroughfare or within a public building during standard operating hours for at least 80% of the year. Projects inside private buildings are not eligible.

heading: Eligibility for grants – General
text:
To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must satisfy the following conditions:
(a) The public art project must be situated within the geographical boundaries of a municipality in Nordvale.
(b) The proposed artwork must be original and not infringe upon existing copyrights.
(c) The applicant must demonstrate the capacity to successfully execute the project within the proposed timeframe, typically not exceeding 24 months from grant approval.
(d) The project must be accessible to the general public without charge, and must be visible from a public thoroughfare or within a public building during standard operating hours for at least 90% of the year. Projects inside private buildings are not eligible.

heading: Public Art Grant Committee
text: The Minister shall establish a Public Art Grant Committee comprising seven members. These members shall be appointed for terms of three years and must possess demonstrated expertise in visual arts, urban planning, or community development. At least two members must be active professional artists with a minimum of 10 years of experience. The Committee’s primary responsibility is to review grant applications and make recommendations to the Minister regarding funding approvals based on the criteria outlined in this Act.

heading: Application process
text: Applicants must submit a detailed proposal to the Committee by the annual deadline of October 1st. The proposal must include a project description, an artistic statement, a detailed budget, a timeline for completion, proof of site approval, and a portfolio of previous works. All submissions must be made electronically through the official government portal. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission to cover administrative costs.

heading: Application process
text: Applicants must submit a detailed proposal to the Committee by the annual deadline of September 15th. The proposal must include a project description, an artistic statement, a detailed budget, a timeline for completion, proof of site approval, and a portfolio of previous works. All submissions must be made electronically through the official government portal. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is required at the time of submission to cover administrative costs, with a 20% discount for applicants from municipalities with populations under 10,000.

heading: Grant amounts – Maximum
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for any single public art project shall not exceed 500,000 crowns. This limit is set to ensure a broad distribution of funds across multiple projects and municipalities, fostering diverse artistic expressions throughout Nordvale. Projects with total budgets exceeding this amount may still be eligible, but the grant will only cover a portion of the total cost, requiring co-funding from other sources. The Committee may recommend a lower amount based on project scope and budgetary constraints.

heading: Grant amounts – Maximum
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for any single public art project shall not exceed 650,000 crowns. This limit is set to ensure a broad distribution of funds across multiple projects and municipalities, fostering diverse artistic expressions throughout Nordvale. Projects with total budgets exceeding this amount may still be eligible, but the grant will only cover a portion of the total cost, requiring co-funding from other sources. The Committee may recommend a lower amount based on project scope and budgetary constraints, but in no case shall it exceed 75% of the total project cost.

heading: Grant amounts – Minimum
text: The minimum grant amount awarded for any single public art project shall be 50,000 crowns. This threshold ensures that only projects of significant scale and artistic ambition receive funding, preventing the allocation of resources to very small or minor artistic interventions. Projects with budgets below this minimum are generally considered self-fundable or suitable for local community grants. The Committee retains discretion to recommend slightly lower amounts in exceptional circumstances, but never below 30,000 crowns, for projects demonstrating extraordinary public benefit or innovative approaches to community engagement.

heading: Funding allocation – General
text: Approximately 60% of the total annual grant budget shall be allocated to projects in municipalities with populations exceeding 25,000 residents. The remaining 40% shall be distributed among municipalities with populations of 25,000 or fewer residents. This distribution aims to balance support for large-scale urban projects with the need to stimulate artistic activity in smaller communities. The Committee monitors this allocation to ensure equitable distribution, and may adjust percentages by up to 5% in any given year, provided there is a compelling justification related to the quality of applications received.

heading: Funding allocation – Specific
text: A minimum of 15% of the total annual grant budget shall be reserved for projects proposed by individual artists or artist collectives, distinct from municipal or non-profit organizational applications. This ensures direct support for independent artistic practice and reduces barriers for artists who may not have institutional backing. These funds are specifically for the creation and installation of artworks, and may not be used for administrative overhead exceeding 10% of the granted amount. Projects must still adhere to all other eligibility criteria outlined in this Act to qualify for this reserved funding.

heading: Criteria for evaluation – Artistic merit
text: The Committee shall evaluate the artistic merit of each proposed project, which accounts for 40% of the overall scoring. This evaluation includes the originality of the concept, the quality of the proposed design, the artist's professional track record, and the potential for the artwork to evoke thought, emotion, or cultural dialogue. The Committee will review submitted portfolios, artist statements, and detailed project renderings. Projects demonstrating innovative use of materials or technologies will receive additional consideration. A minimum score of 70% in this category is generally required for a project to advance to the next stage of review.

heading: Criteria for evaluation – Public benefit
text: The public benefit of a project constitutes 30% of the evaluation score. This includes the artwork's potential to enhance public spaces, its relevance to the local community, and its capacity to engage a broad audience. Proposals must demonstrate how the artwork will contribute to the cultural landscape of Nordvale and provide lasting value to residents and visitors. Engagement strategies, such as community workshops or educational components, will be viewed favorably. Projects that address specific community needs or reflect local history will also receive higher scores. Accessibility for all ages and physical abilities is a significant factor.

heading: Criteria for evaluation – Feasibility
text: The feasibility of a project, encompassing 20% of the evaluation, considers the realism of the budget, the practicality of the timeline, and the applicant's experience in managing similar projects. The Committee will scrutinize financial plans, construction methodologies, and maintenance schedules. Applicants must provide evidence of secure site access and necessary permissions from property owners or municipal authorities. Projects with clear, achievable goals and well-defined execution plans will score higher. A contingency fund of at least 10% of the total project cost is strongly recommended within the budget proposal to cover unforeseen expenses.

heading: Criteria for evaluation – Budget efficiency
text: Budget efficiency accounts for 10% of the total evaluation score. This assesses how effectively the proposed budget utilizes grant funds to achieve the project's artistic and public benefit goals. The Committee looks for projects that demonstrate good value for money, reasonable material costs, and appropriate artist fees. Overheads should not exceed 15% of the total project cost. Applicants must justify all significant expenditures, and projects with a higher proportion of funding directly allocated to artistic creation and installation will generally receive better scores. Co-funding from other sources also positively influences this score.

heading: Review and recommendation
text: The Committee shall review all eligible applications and provide recommendations to the Minister within 90 days of the application deadline. Each application will be scored by at least three Committee members, and the average score will determine its ranking. The Committee will compile a shortlist of recommended projects, along with a detailed rationale for each recommendation, including potential grant amounts.
