The Minister is not bound by the Committee's recommendations but must provide written justification for any significant departure from them.

heading: Review and recommendation
text: The Committee shall review all eligible applications and provide recommendations to the Minister within 75 days of the application deadline. Each application will be scored by at least three Committee members, and the average score will determine its ranking. The Committee will compile a shortlist of recommended projects, along with a detailed rationale for each recommendation, including potential grant amounts. The Minister is not bound by the Committee's recommendations but must provide written justification for any significant departure from them, particularly if rejecting a project ranked in the top 10% by the Committee.

heading: Minister’s decision
text: The Minister shall make final decisions on all grant applications within 30 days of receiving the Committee's recommendations. Approved applicants will be notified in writing within 7 days of the Minister's decision. Unsuccessful applicants will also be notified and may request a summary of the reasons for their application's rejection. The Minister’s decision is final and binding, and no further appeals regarding the decision itself will be entertained. The total amount of grants approved annually shall not exceed the budget allocated by the government for public art initiatives.

heading: Grant agreement
text: Upon approval, successful applicants must enter into a formal grant agreement with the Ministry of Culture and Arts within 60 days. This agreement will detail the project scope, payment schedule, reporting requirements, and all terms and conditions of the grant. Failure to sign the agreement within this timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the grant offer. The agreement will also specify intellectual property rights, ensuring that the artist retains ownership while granting the Ministry rights for promotional purposes for a period of 20 years. Construction must commence within 90 days of signing the agreement.

heading: Disbursement of funds – Initial payment
text: An initial payment of 30% of the total grant amount will be disbursed upon the signing of the grant agreement. This upfront funding is intended to assist applicants with initial project costs, such as material procurement and preparatory work. To receive this payment, the applicant must provide proof of established project accounts and any necessary initial permits. The funds must be used exclusively for approved project expenditures as detailed in the grant agreement. Any misuse of funds may lead to the immediate termination of the grant and require repayment of all disbursed amounts.

heading: Disbursement of funds – Mid-project payment
text: A second payment, constituting 40% of the total grant, will be released upon successful completion of 50% of the project, as verified by a progress report and photographic evidence. This stage typically involves significant construction or fabrication milestones. The applicant must submit a detailed interim financial report demonstrating the proper utilization of the initial payment. An on-site inspection by a Ministry representative may be required to confirm progress before this payment is issued. This payment will only be released if the project is on track to meet its specified completion date.

heading: Disbursement of funds – Final payment
text: The final payment, comprising the remaining 30% of the grant, will be disbursed upon the project's official completion and final approval by the Ministry. This requires the submission of a comprehensive final report, including an audited financial statement, high-resolution photographs of the completed artwork, and confirmation of all necessary municipal approvals. A mandatory final inspection by the Committee or Ministry officials will verify that the artwork has been installed as per the approved proposal and is publicly accessible. Any deviations from the original plan must be pre-approved in writing.

heading: Project completion deadline
text: All public art projects funded under this Act must be completed within 18 months from the date of the grant agreement. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen construction delays or material shortages, but must be requested in writing at least 60 days before the original deadline. Any extension will not exceed an additional 6 months. Failure to complete the project within the stipulated timeframe, without an approved extension, may result in the forfeiture of the remaining grant funds and potential repayment requirements for previously disbursed amounts. A penalty of 5% of the total grant amount may be applied for unapproved delays.

heading: Project completion deadline
text: All public art projects funded under this Act must be completed within 24 months from the date of the grant agreement. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen construction delays or material shortages, but must be requested in writing at least 90 days before the original deadline. Any extension will not exceed an additional 12 months. Failure to complete the project within the stipulated timeframe, without an approved extension, may result in the forfeiture of the remaining grant funds and potential repayment requirements for previously disbursed amounts. A penalty of 2% of the total grant amount may be applied for unapproved delays.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: Grant recipients are required to submit quarterly progress reports to the Ministry, detailing project milestones achieved, expenditures incurred, and any challenges encountered. A comprehensive interim financial report must be submitted after the disbursement of the initial payment. All financial reports must be accompanied by receipts and invoices for expenditures exceeding 5,000 crowns. Failure to submit timely and accurate reports may lead to the suspension of grant payments. The Ministry reserves the right to conduct unannounced site visits to verify project progress and compliance with the grant agreement terms.

heading: Maintenance and preservation
text: The grant recipient is responsible for the ongoing maintenance and preservation of the public artwork for a minimum period of 10 years following its installation. This includes routine cleaning, repairs, and protection against vandalism. A detailed maintenance plan, including estimated annual costs and funding sources, must be submitted as part of the initial grant application. The Ministry may conduct periodic inspections to ensure proper upkeep. Should the artwork fall into disrepair due to neglect, the Ministry reserves the right to seek financial compensation for restoration costs from the grant recipient. A maintenance fund of at least 5% of the total project cost is highly recommended.

heading: Maintenance and preservation
text: The grant recipient is responsible for the ongoing maintenance and preservation of the public artwork for a minimum period of 15 years following its installation. This includes routine cleaning, repairs, and protection against vandalism. A detailed maintenance plan, including estimated annual costs and funding sources, must be submitted as part of the initial grant application. The Ministry may conduct periodic inspections to ensure proper upkeep. Should the artwork fall into disrepair due to neglect, the Ministry reserves the right to seek financial compensation for restoration costs from the grant recipient. A maintenance fund of at least 10% of the total project cost is mandatory for projects exceeding 300,000 crowns.

heading: Acknowledgment of funding
text: All public art projects funded under this Act must include a permanent plaque or inscription acknowledging the financial support from the Republic of Nordvale Public Art Grant. The plaque must be prominently displayed near the artwork, with lettering of at least 2 cm in height. The exact wording and design of the acknowledgment must be approved by the Ministry prior to fabrication and installation. Failure to properly acknowledge the funding may result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns, deducted from the final grant payment. Digital acknowledgments on relevant municipal or artist websites are also encouraged.

heading: Insurance requirements
text: Grant recipients must obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance coverage for the duration of the project's creation and installation, with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns. Additionally, property insurance for the artwork itself, covering loss or damage, must be maintained for the minimum 10-year maintenance period. Proof of insurance must be submitted to the Ministry before any funds are disbursed. The Republic of Nordvale and the Ministry of Culture and Arts must be named as additional insured parties on all relevant policies. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of payments and potential grant termination.

heading: Ownership of artwork
text: Unless otherwise specified in the grant agreement, ownership of the public artwork shall typically transfer to the municipality or public entity upon its successful completion and final approval. The artist will retain intellectual property rights, including copyright, for the artwork. The grant agreement will specify conditions for reproduction and public display of images of the artwork. If the artwork is removed or relocated within the 10-year maintenance period, the artist must be consulted, and efforts made to find a suitable alternative public location. The artist receives a 2% royalty on any commercial reproductions of the artwork.

heading: Ownership of artwork
text: Unless otherwise specified in the grant agreement, ownership of the public artwork shall typically transfer to the municipality or public entity upon its successful completion and final approval. The artist will retain intellectual property rights, including copyright, for the artwork. The grant agreement will specify conditions for reproduction and public display of images of the artwork. If the artwork is removed or relocated within the 15-year maintenance period, the artist must be consulted, and efforts made to find a suitable alternative public location. The artist receives a 3% royalty on any commercial reproductions of the artwork, and a one-time relocation fee of 15,000 crowns if the artwork is moved more than 500 meters.

heading: Modification or removal of artwork
text: Any proposed modification, alteration, or removal of a public artwork funded under this Act within 10 years of its installation requires prior written approval from the Ministry and consultation with the artist. Reasons for modification or removal must be compelling, such as public safety concerns, structural integrity issues, or significant changes in the site's use. If removal is approved, reasonable efforts must be made to relocate the artwork to another publicly accessible site. The artist has the right of first refusal to purchase the artwork at fair market value if permanent removal without relocation is proposed. A public consultation process is mandatory for any permanent removal.

heading: Appeals process – Administrative review
text: An applicant whose grant application is rejected may request an administrative review of the decision. This request must be submitted in writing to the Ministry within 30 days of receiving the rejection notification. The review will focus solely on whether the application process was followed correctly and whether the Committee’s evaluation adhered to the criteria set forth in sections 10 to 13. It will not re-evaluate the artistic merit or subjective judgments made by the Committee. A senior Ministry official, not involved in the initial decision, will conduct the review and provide a response within 45 days. No new information can be submitted during this review.

heading: Appeals process – Final appeal
text: Following an administrative review, if the applicant believes there was a procedural error or a misapplication of the Act's criteria, a final appeal may be submitted to the Minister within 15 days of receiving the administrative review decision. The Minister's decision on such an appeal is final and binding. This final appeal addresses only significant procedural irregularities that may have impacted the outcome. It is not an opportunity to re-argue the merits of the project or introduce new material. The Minister will aim to provide a decision within 60 days. Only 5% of all rejected applicants typically proceed to this stage.

heading: Revocation of grant
text: The Ministry reserves the right to revoke a grant and demand the repayment of all disbursed funds if the recipient fails to comply with the terms of the grant agreement, this Act, or any relevant regulations. Grounds for revocation include, but are not limited to, significant project delays, misrepresentation in the application, misuse of funds, failure to complete the project, or abandonment of the artwork. Before revocation, the Ministry will issue a written warning, providing the recipient 60 days to rectify the breach. If the breach is not remedied, formal revocation proceedings will commence. A 10% interest rate may be applied to repaid funds.

heading: Amendments to the Act
text: The Minister may, from time to time, propose amendments to this Act to reflect evolving cultural policies, address administrative challenges, or adapt to changing financial landscapes. Any proposed amendments will be subject to a public consultation period of at least 45 days to gather feedback from artists, municipal bodies, and the general public. All amendments must be approved by the Parliament of Nordvale. Minor administrative adjustments, such as changes to deadlines or specific reporting forms, may be implemented by ministerial order without parliamentary approval, provided they do not alter the fundamental principles of the Act.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018. Applications for grants may be submitted starting on this date, and the Public Art Grant Committee will commence its review processes in accordance with the timelines established herein. All provisions of this Act are immediately applicable from the commencement date, and any public art projects initiated after this date, seeking public funding, must adhere to the requirements and procedures outlined in this legislation. Transitional provisions for projects already underway before this date may be established by separate ministerial decree to ensure fairness and continuity.

heading: Particular persons
text: (1) If a person is a certified falconry instructor, the admission fee for a public swimming pool is 5 crowns. (2) This reduced fee applies for a single visit lasting at most 3 hours.

heading: Exemptions
text: For a registered lacemaker, the annual licence fee for keeping a dog is waived.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating the application of pesticides within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that pesticides are applied safely and responsibly, protecting public health, the environment, and agricultural productivity. This Act applies to all individuals and companies engaging in the professional application of pesticides on any land or property within Nordvale, regardless of the scale of operation. It sets out the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a pesticide application licence, outlines the duties of licence holders, and specifies the penalties for non-compliance. The provisions of this Act are designed to promote best practices and minimize risks associated with pesticide use.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Applicant" means an individual or company applying for a pesticide application licence.
(b) "Company" means any legal entity, including a partnership or corporation, engaged in pesticide application.
(c) "Licence" means a pesticide application licence issued under this Act.
(d) "Pesticide" means any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest.
(e) "Registrar" means the Registrar of Pesticide Licences appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment.
(f) "Application area" means the specific location where pesticides are applied.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No individual or company shall apply pesticides professionally within Nordvale without holding a valid licence issued in accordance with this Act. This requirement applies to all commercial, agricultural, and public land applications. Any person found applying pesticides without a valid licence may face immediate cessation of activities and substantial penalties as outlined in section 28. Exemptions may apply for personal use on private property not exceeding 0.5 hectares, provided the pesticides used are classified for domestic garden use only. All other applications, including those on land greater than 0.5 hectares, require a licence.

heading: Types of licences
text:
(1) The Registrar may issue the following types of licences:
(a) Individual Applicator Licence: for individuals directly applying pesticides.
(b) Company Application Licence: for companies employing licensed individual applicators.
(2) Each licence type has specific requirements and limitations detailed in subsequent sections. An Individual Applicator Licence permits the holder to apply pesticides, while a Company Application Licence permits the company to operate a pesticide application business, provided all its applicators hold valid Individual Applicator Licences. Companies must designate a primary contact person who holds an Individual Applicator Licence.

heading: Types of licences
text:
(1) The Registrar may issue the following types of licences:
(a) Individual Applicator Licence: for individuals directly applying pesticides.
(b) Company Application Licence: for companies employing licensed individual applicators.
(c) Specialist Application Licence: for individuals applying restricted-use pesticides.
(2) Each licence type has specific requirements and limitations detailed in subsequent sections. An Individual Applicator Licence permits the holder to apply general-use pesticides, while a Company Application Licence permits the company to operate a pesticide application business, provided all its applicators hold valid Individual Applicator Licences. Specialist Application Licences require additional training and certification for specific chemical classes. Companies must designate a primary contact person who holds an Individual Applicator Licence or a Specialist Application Licence if applicable.

heading: Application for individual licence
text:
(1) An individual applying for a licence must:
(a) Be at least 18 years of age.
(b) Have completed an approved pesticide safety course of at least 40 hours duration.
(c) Pass a written examination administered by the Registrar with a score of at least 70%.
(d) Pay an application fee of 500 crowns.
(e) Provide proof of residency in Nordvale for at least 12 months. The application must be submitted to the Registrar using the prescribed form, accompanied by all supporting documentation. Incomplete applications will be returned.

heading: Application for individual licence
text:
(1) An individual applying for a licence must:
(a) Be at least 20 years of age.
(b) Have completed an approved pesticide safety course of at least 60 hours duration.
(c) Pass a written examination administered by the Registrar with a score of at least 75%.
(d) Pay an application fee of 750 crowns.
(e) Provide proof of residency in Nordvale for at least 24 months. The application must be submitted to the Registrar using the prescribed form, accompanied by all supporting documentation. Incomplete applications will be returned within 14 days with reasons for rejection.

heading: Application for company licence
text:
(1) A company applying for a licence must:
(a) Be registered as a business entity in Nordvale.
(b) Employ at least one individual holding a valid Individual Applicator Licence.
(c) Provide proof of general liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns.
(d) Pay an application fee of 1,500 crowns.
(e) Submit a detailed safety plan outlining procedures for pesticide handling, storage, and emergency response. The company must also provide a list of all employees involved in pesticide application, along with their respective licence numbers. Failure to meet any of these criteria will result in the application's rejection within 30 days.

heading: Licence duration and renewal for individuals
text:
(1) An Individual Applicator Licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(2) To renew a licence, an individual must:
(a) Apply for renewal at least 60 days before the expiry date.
(b) Complete 20 hours of approved continuing education in pesticide safety and application techniques.
(c) Pay a renewal fee of 300 crowns.
(d) Not have any outstanding fines or penalties under this Act. Late renewals may incur an additional fee of 150 crowns if submitted within 30 days after expiry, after which a new application is required.

heading: Licence duration and renewal for individuals
text:
(1) An Individual Applicator Licence is valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issue.
(2) To renew a licence, an individual must:
(a) Apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date.
(b) Complete 25 hours of approved continuing education in pesticide safety and application techniques.
(c) Pay a renewal fee of 400 crowns.
(d) Not have any outstanding fines or penalties under this Act. Late renewals may incur an additional fee of 200 crowns if submitted within 45 days after expiry, after which a new application is required and a late submission will result in a 3-month processing delay.

heading: Licence duration and renewal for companies
text:
(1) A Company Application Licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(2) To renew a licence, a company must:
(a) Apply for renewal at least 60 days before the expiry date.
(b) Confirm that all employed applicators hold valid Individual Applicator Licences.
(c) Provide updated proof of general liability insurance with minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns.
(d) Pay a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns.
(e) Submit an updated safety plan if any material changes have occurred. Failure to renew on time may result in a temporary suspension of operations until the licence is reinstated.

heading: Licence duration and renewal for companies
text:
(1) A Company Application Licence is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue.
(2) To renew a licence, a company must:
(a) Apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date.
(b) Confirm that all employed applicators hold valid Individual Applicator Licences.
(c) Provide updated proof of general liability insurance with minimum coverage of 750,000 crowns.
(d) Pay a renewal fee of 1,200 crowns.
(e) Submit an updated safety plan if any material changes have occurred, or confirm no changes have been made. Failure to renew on time may result in a temporary suspension of operations until the licence is reinstated, potentially incurring a penalty of 500 crowns per day of non-compliance.

heading: Registrar's powers
text:
(1) The Registrar has the power to:
(a) Issue, renew, suspend, or revoke licences.
(b) Set standards for pesticide safety courses and examinations.
(c) Conduct inspections of premises and records related to pesticide application.
(d) Investigate complaints regarding pesticide application.
(e) Impose administrative penalties for non-compliance with this Act.
(f) Collect and maintain a public register of all licensed applicators and companies. The Registrar may delegate certain powers to qualified inspectors, provided such delegation is in writing and publicly accessible.

heading: Duty to report incidents
text: Any licence holder must report to the Registrar any incident involving the misuse of pesticides, accidental spills exceeding 5 litres, or adverse health effects experienced by any person or animal suspected to be caused by their pesticide application. Such reports must be made within 24 hours of the incident occurring. Failure to report a significant incident within the specified timeframe may result in immediate licence suspension and a fine of up to 10,000 crowns. Minor spills, under 5 litres, must be recorded in the application logbook but do not require immediate notification to the Registrar.

heading: Record keeping requirements
text:
(1) Every licence holder must maintain accurate records for all pesticide applications, including:
(a) Date and time of application.
(b) Location of application (address or precise coordinates).
(c) Type and quantity of pesticide used.
(d) Target pest.
(e) Name and licence number of the applicator.
(f) Environmental conditions (temperature, wind speed).
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years and be made available to the Registrar upon request within 7 working days. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns per missing record entry, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns per year.

heading: Record keeping requirements
text:
(1) Every licence holder must maintain accurate records for all pesticide applications, including:
(a) Date and time of application.
(b) Location of application (address or precise coordinates, minimum 6 decimal places for coordinates).
(c) Type and quantity of pesticide used (batch number required).
(d) Target pest and observed efficacy.
(e) Name and licence number of the applicator.
(f) Environmental conditions (temperature, wind speed, humidity, precipitation).
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of 7 years and be made available to the Registrar upon request within 3 working days. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns per missing record entry, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns per year, and potential licence suspension.

heading: Storage of pesticides
text: All pesticides must be stored in a secure, well-ventilated area that is inaccessible to unauthorized persons and animals. Storage facilities must be clearly labelled with warning signs. Pesticides must be kept in their original containers with labels intact. Flammable pesticides must be stored separately in fire-resistant cabinets. A log of stored pesticides, including quantities and expiry dates, must be maintained and updated monthly. Failure to comply with storage requirements may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns for each non-compliant item or condition, and immediate confiscation of improperly stored materials.

heading: Application safety standards
text:
(1) Licence holders must ensure that all pesticide applications are conducted in a manner that minimizes drift and exposure to non-target areas.
(2) Applicators must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) as specified on the pesticide label.
(3) No pesticides shall be applied when wind speeds exceed 15 kilometers per hour or during heavy rainfall. Buffers of at least 10 meters must be maintained from water bodies and sensitive areas such as schools or hospitals during application. Prior notification to adjacent property owners within 50 meters is required 24 hours before application of restricted-use pesticides.

heading: Application safety standards
text:
(1) Licence holders must ensure that all pesticide applications are conducted in a manner that minimizes drift and exposure to non-target areas, utilizing best available technology.
(2) Applicators must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) as specified on the pesticide label, and ensure it is properly maintained and inspected quarterly.
(3) No pesticides shall be applied when wind speeds exceed 10 kilometers per hour or during any precipitation. Buffers of at least 20 meters must be maintained from water bodies and sensitive areas such as schools, hospitals, or public parks during application. Prior notification to adjacent property owners within 100 meters is required 48 hours before application of restricted-use pesticides, including details of the pesticide and application time.

heading: Public notification of application
text: For any outdoor application of pesticides in public areas or areas adjacent to residential properties, the licence holder must post visible warning signs at all primary access points to the treated area. These signs must be at least 30cm by 30cm, in clear language, stating that pesticides have been applied, the date of application, and a contact number for inquiries. Signs must remain in place for at least 48 hours after application. Failure to post appropriate signage will result in a fine of 750 crowns per day of non-compliance.

heading: Disposal of pesticide waste
text: All pesticide waste, including empty containers, unused pesticide formulations, and contaminated materials, must be disposed of in accordance with national waste management regulations. It is prohibited to dispose of pesticide waste in public landfills, waterways, or by burning. Licence holders must use approved waste disposal contractors and retain disposal manifests for a minimum of 3 years. Any contravention of these disposal rules will lead to a minimum fine of 5,000 crowns and mandatory remediation costs.

heading: Inspections and audits
text:
(1) The Registrar, or an authorized inspector, may conduct unannounced inspections of any premises where pesticides are stored, mixed, or applied, and may audit records required to be kept under this Act.
(2) Inspectors must present valid identification upon arrival. Licence holders must grant immediate access to relevant areas and provide all requested documentation. Interference with an inspection is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 15,000 crowns and immediate licence suspension for 6 months. Refusal to cooperate may lead to licence revocation.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 6 months if the holder:
(a) Fails to comply with any provision of this Act or its regulations.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in an application or report.
(c) Endangers public health or the environment through negligent pesticide application.
(2) Before suspension, the Registrar must provide written notice detailing the reasons for the proposed suspension and allow the licence holder 14 days to respond. An immediate suspension may occur in cases of grave danger.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) The Registrar may revoke a licence if the holder:
(a) Has a licence suspended more than once within a 5-year period.
(b) Commits a serious offence under this Act, resulting in significant environmental damage or harm to human health.
(c) Fails to pay fines or penalties within 90 days of issuance.
(d) Is convicted of a criminal offence related to environmental harm or fraudulent business practices.
(2) A revoked licence cannot be reapplied for a period of 5 years. A hearing will be offered prior to final revocation.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) The Registrar may revoke a licence if the holder:
(a) Has a licence suspended more than once within a 3-year period.
(b) Commits a serious offence under this Act, resulting in significant environmental damage or harm to human health, as determined by an expert panel.
(c) Fails to pay fines or penalties within 60 days of issuance.
(d) Is convicted of a criminal offence related to environmental harm, fraudulent business practices, or a serious safety violation.
(2) A revoked licence cannot be reapplied for a period of 7 years. A formal hearing will be conducted by an independent tribunal prior to final revocation, allowing the licence holder full opportunity to present their case. Decisions are appealable within 30 days.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant or licence holder may appeal a decision of the Registrar regarding licence issuance, renewal, suspension, or revocation.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the Registrar's decision. The Appeals Board, consisting of three independent experts, will review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the Registrar's ruling. The Board's decision is final and binding. No further appeals are permitted under this Act.

heading: Restricted-use pesticides
text: The Ministry of Agriculture and Environment may designate certain pesticides as 'restricted-use' based on their toxicity, environmental persistence, or potential for misuse. Application of restricted-use pesticides requires specific endorsement on an Individual Applicator Licence, obtained by completing additional specialized training and passing a supplementary examination with a score of at least 80%. Failure to hold the correct endorsement when applying a restricted-use pesticide will result in a fine of 20,000 crowns and immediate licence suspension for 12 months.

heading: Pesticide purchase and transfer
text: Only individuals or companies holding a valid licence under this Act may purchase or acquire restricted-use pesticides. Records of all purchases and transfers of restricted-use pesticides must be maintained by both the seller and the buyer for a period of 5 years. It is prohibited to sell or transfer restricted-use pesticides to unlicensed individuals or entities. A breach of this section carries a penalty of 10,000 crowns per infraction and potential revocation of any associated business permits.

heading: Training institutions
text: Institutions offering pesticide safety courses must be approved by the Registrar. Approval requires a curriculum that meets established standards, qualified instructors with a minimum of 5 years experience in pesticide management, and facilities suitable for practical training. The Registrar will conduct biennial audits of approved institutions to ensure continued compliance. Any institution found to be non-compliant may have its approval revoked, with a 2-year waiting period before reapplying. Course fees are capped at 3,000 crowns per participant.

heading: Examination standards
text: The written examination for Individual Applicator Licences shall cover topics including pesticide types, safe handling, environmental impact, integrated pest management, and relevant laws. The examination will consist of at least 50 multiple-choice questions and must be completed within 90 minutes. A passing score is 70%. Individuals who fail may retake the examination after a waiting period of 14 days, with a maximum of three attempts per year. A fee of 100 crowns is charged for each re-examination.

heading: Continuing education providers
text: Providers of continuing education units (CEUs) for licence renewal must be approved by the Registrar. CEU courses must focus on advancements in pesticide technology, environmental protection, or regulatory changes. Each CEU hour must involve at least 50 minutes of instructional time. Providers must submit course outlines and instructor qualifications for approval at least 60 days prior to offering any course. The Registrar reserves the right to audit any CEU course for quality assurance. Unapproved CEU credits will not count towards licence renewal requirements.

heading: Fees
text:
(1) All fees payable under this Act are non-refundable.
(2) The Registrar may adjust fees annually by no more than 5% to account for administrative costs and inflation. Any fee adjustment must be published in the official gazette at least 90 days before coming into effect. Current fees are:
(a) Individual Application: 500 crowns.
(b) Company Application: 1,500 crowns.
(c) Individual Renewal: 300 crowns.
(d) Company Renewal: 1,000 crowns.
(e) Examination Retake: 100 crowns.
(f) Late Renewal Penalty: 150 crowns.

heading: Fees
text:
(1) All fees payable under this Act are non-refundable.
(2) The Registrar may adjust fees annually by no more than 3% to account for administrative costs and inflation. Any fee adjustment must be published in the official gazette at least 120 days before coming into effect. Current fees are:
(a) Individual Application: 750 crowns.
(b) Company Application: 1,800 crowns.
(c) Specialist Endorsement: 250 crowns.
(d) Individual Renewal: 400 crowns.
(e) Company Renewal: 1,200 crowns.
(f) Examination Retake: 150 crowns.
(g) Late Renewal Penalty: 200 crowns.

heading: Penalty for unlicensed application
text: Any individual found applying pesticides without a valid Individual Applicator Licence shall be subject to a fine of 5,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 15,000 crowns and a mandatory ban from applying for any licence under this Act for 3 years. Any company employing an unlicensed applicator will face a fine of 20,000 crowns per incident and potential suspension of its Company Application Licence for 6 months. All illegally applied pesticides will be confiscated.

heading: General penalties
text:
(1) Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act for which no specific penalty is provided is liable to a fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns for a first offense.
(2) For a second or subsequent offense, the fine may be up to 25,000 crowns and may include a suspension of the licence for up to 12 months. Each day that a contravention continues may be considered a separate offense. The Registrar may also order the offender to take corrective actions within a specified timeframe, with non-compliance leading to further penalties.

heading: Emergency powers of the Registrar
text: In cases of immediate and severe threat to public health or the environment caused by pesticide application, the Registrar may issue emergency orders to cease operations, recall products, or restrict activities without prior notice. Such orders are effective immediately and remain in force for a maximum of 72 hours, during which time a formal review must be initiated. Non-compliance with an emergency order is subject to a penalty of 50,000 crowns and immediate licence revocation without possibility of reapplication for 10 years.

heading: Public register of licences
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all issued Individual Applicator Licences and Company Application Licences. This register will include the licence holder's name (or company name), licence number, type of licence, issue date, expiry date, and any current suspension or revocation status. The register will be accessible online and updated weekly. Personal addresses of individual applicators will not be disclosed, only the municipality of registration. The Registrar will ensure data protection principles are adhered to in maintaining the register.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Any individual or company engaged in pesticide application prior to the enactment of this Act shall have a period of 180 days from the effective date to apply for the appropriate licence.
(2) During this 180-day period, such individuals or companies may continue to operate, provided they submit a complete application within the first 90 days. Failure to apply within the initial 180 days will result in immediate cessation of operations and penalties as per section 27. The Registrar may grant extensions in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Ministry of Agriculture and Environment may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Ministry may make regulations:
(a) Prescribing forms for applications and reports.
(b) Establishing specific safety protocols for various pesticide types.
(c) Setting maximum residue limits for pesticides in agricultural products.
(d) Specifying requirements for training course content and instructor qualifications.
(e) Defining sensitive areas where pesticide application is restricted or prohibited. All regulations must undergo a 60-day public consultation period before enactment.

heading: Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered peat cutter, the duty of 5 percent of the rent charged for dwelling rentals of less than 30 consecutive nights shall be payable 30 days after the end of each quarter.

heading: Payment terms
text: The pensioner heating supplement is reduced by twenty-five percent for any person who is a registered certified avalanche observer for at least one year.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) If a dog owner is a registered ski patroller, the annual license fee for their first dog is 5 crowns. (2) For any additional dogs, the fee is 5 crowns per dog.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a grant program to support the maintenance and improvement of public amenities within the municipalities of Nordvale. The primary goal is to ensure that parks, town squares, and other publicly accessible green spaces remain well-kept, safe, and enjoyable for all residents. The grants provided under this Act are intended to supplement, not replace, existing municipal budgets for amenity upkeep, focusing on enhancements and significant repair projects. This Act applies to all recognized municipalities in Nordvale.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purpose of this Act:
(a) "Public amenity" means any land or facility owned or managed by a municipality that is freely accessible to the general public for recreational or aesthetic purposes, including but not limited to parks, gardens, town squares, and public walkways.
(b) "Maintenance" refers to activities necessary to preserve the condition and function of a public amenity, including cleaning, minor repairs, and horticultural care.
(c) "Improvement" refers to activities that enhance the quality, usability, or aesthetic value of a public amenity, such as installing new features or significant landscaping.

heading: Eligibility for grants
text: Any municipality within the Republic of Nordvale is eligible to apply for grants under this Act. To qualify, a municipality must demonstrate ownership or long-term management responsibility for the public amenity for which the grant is sought. Applications must be submitted by the municipal council or its designated department. Private entities, even those managing public spaces, are not eligible to apply directly; applications must come through the relevant municipal authority. A municipality can submit up to three distinct applications in a single funding cycle.

heading: Grant application period
text: Applications for grants must be submitted between 1 February and 31 March each year. Applications received outside this period will not be considered for the current funding cycle. The Ministry of Public Works will announce the opening of the application window no later than 15 January. Late submissions, even by one day, will be automatically rejected. Municipalities are advised to prepare their applications well in advance of the deadline to ensure timely submission and to address any potential technical issues.

heading: Grant application period
text: Applications for grants must be submitted between 15 January and 15 March each year. Applications received outside this period will not be considered for the current funding cycle. The Ministry of Public Works will announce the opening of the application window no later than 1 January. Late submissions will be accepted only if accompanied by a valid reason and submitted within 5 days of the deadline. Municipalities are advised to prepare their applications well in advance to ensure timely submission.

heading: Grant application period
text: Applications for grants must be submitted between 1 January and 28 February each year. Applications received outside this period will not be considered for the current funding cycle. The Ministry of Public Works will announce the opening of the application window no later than 15 December of the preceding year. No late submissions will be accepted under any circumstances. All applications must be submitted electronically through the designated municipal portal.

heading: Application requirements
text:
Each application must include:
(a) A detailed project proposal outlining the scope of work, objectives, and expected outcomes.
(b) An itemized budget for the proposed maintenance or improvement, including estimated costs for materials, labor, and any professional services.
(c) Proof of municipal ownership or management responsibility for the amenity.
(d) A timeline for project completion, not exceeding 18 months from the grant award date.
(e) A declaration that the municipality will adhere to all relevant local regulations and standards during project execution.

heading: Grant limits for maintenance projects
text: The maximum grant amount for a single maintenance project involving existing infrastructure or horticulture is 75,000 crowns. Municipalities may apply for multiple maintenance grants, but the total awarded to any single municipality for maintenance in one funding cycle shall not exceed 200,000 crowns. Projects primarily focused on routine cleaning or minor horticultural tasks will typically receive no more than 15,000 crowns. At least 25% of the project cost must be covered by municipal funds.

heading: Grant limits for maintenance projects
text: The maximum grant amount for a single maintenance project involving existing infrastructure or horticulture is 80,000 crowns. Municipalities may apply for multiple maintenance grants, but the total awarded to any single municipality for maintenance in one funding cycle shall not exceed 220,000 crowns. Projects primarily focused on routine cleaning or minor horticultural tasks will typically receive no more than 18,000 crowns. At least 20% of the project cost must be covered by municipal funds.

heading: Grant limits for improvement projects
text: The maximum grant amount for a single improvement project, such as the installation of new public facilities or significant landscaping, is 150,000 crowns. The total awarded to any single municipality for improvement projects in one funding cycle shall not exceed 350,000 crowns. Projects involving the creation of new public spaces or significant ecological enhancements may be eligible for up to 200,000 crowns. A minimum of 30% of the project cost must be contributed by the applying municipality.

heading: Grant limits for improvement projects
text: The maximum grant amount for a single improvement project, such as the installation of new public facilities or significant landscaping, is 175,000 crowns. The total awarded to any single municipality for improvement projects in one funding cycle shall not exceed 400,000 crowns. Projects involving the creation of new public spaces or significant ecological enhancements may be eligible for up to 225,000 crowns. A minimum of 25% of the project cost must be contributed by the applying municipality.

heading: Review process
text: Applications will be reviewed by a committee appointed by the Ministry of Public Works. The committee will consist of five members with expertise in urban planning, public works, and financial management. The review process will assess the project's feasibility, community benefit, cost-effectiveness, and alignment with the objectives of this Act. The committee aims to complete its review and make recommendations within 60 days of the application deadline. All decisions are final.

heading: Grant allocation criteria
text:
Grants will be allocated based on:
(a) The demonstrated need for the project within the community.
(b) The project's potential to significantly improve public access, safety, or aesthetic value.
(c) The clarity and thoroughness of the project proposal and budget.
(d) The municipality's financial contribution to the project, with higher contributions generally viewed favorably.
(e) The environmental sustainability aspects of the proposed work, if applicable.

heading: Notification of decisions
text: All applicant municipalities will be notified of the decision regarding their grant application by 30 June of the application year. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant offer detailing the approved amount, terms, and conditions. Unsuccessful applicants will be informed of the reasons for rejection. There is no appeal process for grant decisions. The Ministry will provide feedback to unsuccessful applicants to help improve future submissions.

heading: Acceptance of grant offer
text: A municipality offered a grant must formally accept the offer within 30 days of the notification date. Failure to accept within this period will result in the offer being withdrawn. The acceptance must be in writing, signed by an authorized municipal representative, and confirm agreement to all terms and conditions outlined in the grant offer. If the offer is declined or withdrawn, the funds may be reallocated to other eligible projects at the discretion of the Ministry.

heading: Disbursement of funds for maintenance
text: For approved maintenance projects, 50% of the grant amount will be disbursed upon formal acceptance of the grant offer. The remaining 50% will be disbursed upon submission and approval of a final project report, including verified expenditures, within 30 days of project completion. The initial disbursement will typically occur within 14 days of receiving the acceptance. Municipalities must ensure all expenditures are properly documented with receipts and invoices.

heading: Disbursement of funds for maintenance
text: For approved maintenance projects, 40% of the grant amount will be disbursed upon formal acceptance of the grant offer. A further 30% will be disbursed upon submission of an interim progress report after 50% of the project is complete. The final 30% will be disbursed upon submission and approval of a final project report, including verified expenditures, within 30 days of project completion. All financial documentation must be retained for at least 3 years.

heading: Disbursement of funds for improvements
text: For approved improvement projects, 40% of the grant amount will be disbursed upon formal acceptance of the grant offer. An additional 30% will be disbursed upon completion of 50% of the project as verified by an interim report and on-site inspection. The final 30% will be disbursed upon submission and approval of a final project report and successful final inspection, within 60 days of project completion. Delays in reporting or inspections may delay subsequent disbursements.

heading: Disbursement of funds for improvements
text: For approved improvement projects, 35% of the grant amount will be disbursed upon formal acceptance of the grant offer. An additional 35% will be disbursed upon completion of 60% of the project as verified by an interim report and on-site inspection. The final 30% will be disbursed upon submission and approval of a final project report and successful final inspection, within 45 days of project completion. All inspections will be scheduled within 10 business days of notification.

heading: Project completion deadline
text: All projects funded under this Act must be completed within 18 months from the date of formal grant acceptance. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen material shortages or severe weather events, for a maximum of 6 months. Requests for extension must be submitted in writing at least 30 days before the original deadline, detailing the reasons for the delay and a revised completion timeline. Only one extension per project will be considered.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
Grant recipients are required to submit a final project report within 30 days of project completion. This report must include:
(a) A narrative summary of the work undertaken and outcomes achieved.
(b) A detailed financial statement showing all project expenditures, supported by copies of invoices and receipts.
(c) Photographic evidence of the completed work.
(d) A declaration from the municipal council confirming satisfactory completion of the project.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
Grant recipients are required to submit a final project report within 30 days of project completion. This report must include:
(a) A narrative summary of the work undertaken and outcomes achieved.
(b) A detailed financial statement showing all project expenditures, supported by copies of invoices and receipts.
(c) At least five high-resolution photographs of the completed work, from different angles.
(d) A declaration from the municipal council confirming satisfactory completion of the project and adherence to all grant conditions.
(e) A brief section on community feedback received during or after the project.

heading: Auditing and inspection
text: The Ministry of Public Works reserves the right to conduct audits of project finances and on-site inspections of funded projects at any time during the project period and up to 24 months after final disbursement. Municipalities must provide full access to all relevant documents, records, and project sites upon request. Refusal to comply with an audit or inspection may result in the suspension or clawback of grant funds. All records related to the grant must be kept for a minimum of 5 years.

heading: Misuse of funds
text: Any funds found to be misused, misallocated, or not spent in accordance with the approved project proposal and the terms of this Act will be subject to immediate repayment to the Ministry. Misuse includes, but is not limited to, using funds for ineligible expenses, purchasing items not specified in the budget, or failing to complete the project as described. The Ministry may also levy an administrative penalty of up to 10% of the misused amount. Future grant applications from municipalities found to have misused funds may be denied for a period of up to 3 years.

heading: Revocation of grants
text: A grant may be revoked if the municipality fails to comply with any term or condition of this Act or the grant offer. Reasons for revocation include significant deviation from the approved project plan, failure to meet reporting deadlines, or evidence of fraudulent activity. In such cases, all disbursed funds must be repaid to the Ministry within 60 days of the revocation notice. The Ministry will provide a 30-day notice period for the municipality to rectify any breaches before final revocation.

heading: Public acknowledgement
text: All public amenities improved or maintained with funds from this Act must visibly acknowledge the grant. This typically involves the installation of a small plaque or sign, no smaller than 15cm by 10cm, at a prominent location within the amenity, stating: 'This project was supported by the Public Amenity Maintenance Grant Act.' The sign must be durable and weather-resistant. The cost of the signage can be included as an eligible project expense, up to 500 crowns.

heading: Public acknowledgement
text: All public amenities improved or maintained with funds from this Act must visibly acknowledge the grant. This typically involves the installation of a small plaque or sign, no smaller than 20cm by 15cm, at a prominent location within the amenity, stating: 'This project was supported by the Nordvale Public Amenity Maintenance Grant Act.' The sign must be durable and weather-resistant. The cost of the signage can be included as an eligible project expense, up to 750 crowns. The design of the sign must be approved by the Ministry.

heading: Ineligible expenses
text:
Grant funds cannot be used for:
(a) Administrative overhead costs exceeding 10% of the total project budget.
(b) Purchase of land or property.
(c) Expenses incurred prior to the grant acceptance date.
(d) Political or lobbying activities.
(e) Projects that are primarily commercial in nature or generate private profit.
(f) Costs covered by other funding sources or grants.
(g) Salaries for permanent municipal staff unless directly involved in project execution and clearly itemized.

heading: Environmental considerations
text: Projects involving significant landscaping or changes to natural habitats must adhere to national environmental protection guidelines. Municipalities are encouraged to use environmentally sustainable practices and materials where feasible. Projects that demonstrate a clear benefit to local biodiversity or water conservation may receive preferential consideration during the allocation process. All relevant environmental impact assessments must be completed before commencing any work.

heading: Maintenance of improved amenities
text: Municipalities receiving grants for improvements are expected to maintain the improved amenity in good condition for a minimum of 5 years following project completion. Failure to adequately maintain the amenity may impact eligibility for future grants. The Ministry may conduct follow-up inspections within this 5-year period to assess the ongoing condition of the amenity. Municipalities should allocate sufficient internal resources for long-term upkeep.

heading: Aldmark special provisions
text: As the capital city, Aldmark may apply for up to 10% higher grant amounts for both maintenance and improvement projects, provided the projects are of significant civic importance or benefit a wider regional population. The total annual grant ceiling for Aldmark is 600,000 crowns. These special provisions acknowledge the unique role and higher visitor traffic in the capital's public spaces. All other eligibility and reporting requirements remain the same for Aldmark.

heading: Aldmark special provisions
text: As the capital city, Aldmark may apply for up to 15% higher grant amounts for both maintenance and improvement projects, provided the projects are of significant civic importance or benefit a wider regional population. The total annual grant ceiling for Aldmark is 750,000 crowns. These special provisions acknowledge the unique role and higher visitor traffic in the capital's public spaces. Aldmark must also demonstrate a 40% municipal contribution for any project exceeding 250,000 crowns.

heading: Brenholt and Corvik provisions
text: Municipalities of Brenholt and Corvik, due to their historical significance and tourist appeal, are eligible for an additional 5% in grant funding for projects that specifically enhance heritage areas or tourist-facing public spaces. This special provision applies to up to two projects per year per municipality. The maximum additional funding per project under this provision is 10,000 crowns. Documentation of heritage significance must be provided with the application.

heading: Rural municipality considerations
text: For municipalities with a population under 5,000, the minimum municipal contribution requirement outlined in section 6 and section 7 is reduced by 5 percentage points. These municipalities may also submit up to four applications per funding cycle. This aims to support smaller communities with potentially limited local resources in maintaining their public amenities. Population figures will be based on the most recent official census data.

heading: Rural municipality considerations
text: For municipalities with a population under 7,500, the minimum municipal contribution requirement outlined in section 6 and section 7 is reduced by 7 percentage points. These municipalities may also submit up to five applications per funding cycle. This aims to support smaller communities with potentially limited local resources in maintaining their public amenities. Population figures will be based on the most recent official census data, verified by the Ministry of Interior.

heading: Collaboration projects
text: Two or more municipalities may jointly apply for a single grant for a project that spans municipal boundaries or provides a shared regional benefit. In such cases, the maximum grant amount can be increased by 25% for that specific project. A lead municipality must be designated for administrative purposes, and a formal inter-municipal agreement detailing responsibilities and financial contributions must accompany the application. Joint projects are limited to one per funding cycle per collaborating group.

heading: Grant review committee membership
text: The Grant Review Committee, as mentioned in section 8, shall comprise a chairperson and four members. The chairperson is appointed by the Minister of Public Works. Two members are appointed by the National Association of Municipalities, and the remaining two members are selected from a pool of qualified experts in urban planning and environmental science. All members serve for a term of 3 years and can be reappointed for one additional term. A quorum of three members is required for all official decisions.

heading: Financial year alignment
text: All grant funding cycles and project timelines are aligned with the national financial year, which runs from 1 January to 31 December. Project budgets submitted must reflect costs expected to be incurred within this framework. Any unspent grant funds at the end of a project's allocated financial year may need to be returned to the Ministry if not formally carried over with approval. Municipalities should plan their project expenditures accordingly to avoid any forfeiture of funds.

heading: Annual report to the National Assembly
text: The Ministry of Public Works shall submit an annual report to the National Assembly by 1 October each year, detailing the grants awarded under this Act during the preceding financial year. The report will include the names of recipient municipalities, the projects funded, the amounts disbursed, and a summary of the overall impact of the grant program. The report may also include recommendations for amendments to this Act or future funding priorities. This ensures transparency and accountability in grant distribution.

heading: Annual report to the National Assembly
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: Each certified tide-table surveyor pays no fee or allowance as described in DRA §7.

heading: Particular persons
text: (1) A registered certified bookbinder shall pay half of the licence fee. (2) This reduction applies to the first two dogs kept by the bookbinder.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act outlines the duties and responsibilities for the ongoing maintenance and preservation of public art installations across the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all publicly accessible artworks, including sculptures, murals, and installations, whether permanent or temporary, that are situated on public land or within publicly accessible spaces. The primary goal is to ensure the longevity, safety, and aesthetic integrity of these valuable cultural assets for the enjoyment of all citizens and visitors. This Act establishes clear guidelines for municipal authorities and other responsible parties regarding their obligations.

heading: Definition of Public Art
text: For the purposes of this Act, 'public art' refers to any work of visual art that is permanently or semi-permanently installed in a public space, intended for public viewing. This includes, but is not limited to, sculptures, murals, mosaics, and integrated architectural artworks. An artwork is considered public art if it is accessible to the general public for at least 300 days per year and has an acquisition value exceeding 5,000 crowns. Temporary installations lasting less than 60 days are exempt from certain maintenance provisions, as detailed in section 14.

heading: Responsible Authorities
text: The primary responsibility for public art maintenance rests with the municipality in which the art is located. For art situated within Aldmark, the Aldmark City Council is the responsible authority. In other municipalities such as Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, the respective municipal councils hold this duty. Where public art spans municipal boundaries, the involved municipalities must establish a joint maintenance agreement within 90 days of installation, outlining shared responsibilities and cost allocation, typically based on the percentage of the artwork within each jurisdiction.

heading: Maintenance Plans
text: Each responsible authority must develop and maintain a comprehensive maintenance plan for all public art under its purview. This plan must be updated at least once every 24 months. It shall detail cleaning schedules, inspection protocols, repair procedures, and budget allocations. For any artwork valued over 25,000 crowns, the plan must include a professional conservation assessment every 5 years. The plan must be publicly accessible on the municipality's website and a physical copy kept at the municipal offices.

heading: Inspection Schedules
text: All public art installations must undergo a routine visual inspection at least once every 6 months. For artworks located in high-traffic areas or those made of delicate materials, inspections must occur quarterly, every 3 months. A detailed condition report must be filed after each inspection, noting any damage, wear, or environmental impact. These reports must be kept for a minimum of 10 years and be made available for public review upon request within 14 days.

heading: Cleaning Protocols
text: Public art must be cleaned regularly to prevent the accumulation of dirt, grime, and pollutants. The frequency of cleaning depends on the artwork's material and location, but a general cleaning should occur at least once per year. Specialized cleaning, using methods approved by a professional conservator, is required for sensitive materials or for the removal of graffiti. Any graffiti must be removed within 72 hours of discovery, or within 24 hours if it contains offensive content.

heading: Repair and Restoration
text: Damage to public art must be repaired promptly. Minor repairs, costing less than 1,000 crowns, must be completed within 30 days of discovery. Major repairs or restoration projects, exceeding 1,000 crowns, require a detailed proposal from a qualified conservator and must be initiated within 90 days of approval. For artworks over 50 years old or those deemed historically significant, all repair and restoration work must be supervised by a conservator specializing in that art form and period. Any repair work must aim to maintain the original artistic intent.

heading: Documentation Requirements
text: Each public art installation must have a comprehensive documentation file. This file must include: (a) acquisition records and costs; (b) artist information; (c) material specifications; (d) installation photographs; (e) all inspection reports; (f) records of all maintenance, repair, and conservation treatments; and (g) any public feedback or concerns. These files must be digitized and stored securely, with physical copies retained for at least 25 years. This documentation is crucial for informing future conservation efforts and understanding the artwork's history.

heading: Budget Allocation
text: Municipalities are required to allocate a specific portion of their annual budget for public art maintenance. This allocation must be no less than 0.5% of the total value of public art within their jurisdiction, or a minimum of 5,000 crowns, whichever is greater. These funds are to be exclusively used for inspections, cleaning, repairs, and conservation of public artworks. Any unspent funds designated for public art maintenance must be rolled over to the next fiscal year for the same purpose, up to a maximum of 20% of the original allocation.

heading: Budget Allocation
text: Municipalities are required to allocate a specific portion of their annual budget for public art maintenance. This allocation must be no less than 0.75% of the total value of public art within their jurisdiction, or a minimum of 7,500 crowns, whichever is greater. These funds are to be exclusively used for inspections, cleaning, repairs, and conservation of public artworks. Any unspent funds designated for public art maintenance must be rolled over to the next fiscal year for the same purpose, up to a maximum of 25% of the original allocation.

heading: Budget Allocation
text: Municipalities are required to allocate a specific portion of their annual budget for public art maintenance. This allocation must be no less than 1% of the total value of public art within their jurisdiction, or a minimum of 10,000 crowns, whichever is greater. These funds are to be exclusively used for inspections, cleaning, repairs, and conservation of public artworks. Any unspent funds designated for public art maintenance must be rolled over to the next fiscal year for the same purpose, up to a maximum of 30% of the original allocation. Municipalities must also provide a detailed financial report on these expenditures annually.

heading: Public Access and Safety
text: Public art must be maintained in a manner that ensures public safety. Any structural instability, sharp edges, or other hazards must be immediately addressed and rectified. If an artwork poses an immediate danger, it must be cordoned off within 4 hours and appropriate warning signs displayed. Permanent repairs or removal must be completed within 60 days. Regular safety audits, conducted by a qualified engineer, are required for all installations over 3 meters in height or weighing more than 500 kilograms, every 3 years.

heading: Environmental Protection
text: Maintenance practices must consider the environmental impact of chemicals and materials used. Only environmentally friendly cleaning agents and conservation materials should be utilized where possible. Runoff from cleaning procedures must be managed to prevent contamination of local water sources or soil. For artworks located near sensitive ecological areas, such as nature reserves or protected waterways, a specific environmental impact assessment must be conducted prior to any major maintenance work, and approved by the regional environmental protection agency.

heading: Decommissioning and Relocation
text: The decommissioning or relocation of public art requires careful planning and justification. A decision to decommission must be based on factors such as irreparable damage, prohibitive maintenance costs exceeding 75% of original value, or significant public safety concerns. Public consultation for at least 45 days is required for any permanent removal. Relocations must also be justified and carried out by qualified professionals to prevent damage. All decommissioned artworks must be properly documented and archived, even if no longer publicly displayed.

heading: Reporting Damage
text: Members of the public are encouraged to report any damage or concerns regarding public art installations to the relevant municipal authority. Each municipality must provide a clear and accessible method for reporting, such as a dedicated phone line, email address, or online portal, available 24 hours a day. All reports must be acknowledged within 2 business days, and an initial assessment of the reported damage must be conducted within 7 days. Critical safety concerns should be addressed immediately, as per section 10.

heading: Temporary Art Installations
text: Temporary public art installations, defined as those displayed for a period between 60 days and 2 years, require a simplified maintenance plan. This plan must include weekly visual inspections and a clear schedule for the removal of the artwork at the end of its designated display period. The artist or commissioning body is primarily responsible for maintenance during this period. The municipality must ensure the site is restored to its original condition within 14 days of the artwork's removal. Installations shorter than 60 days are generally exempt from this section, but must still comply with safety regulations.

heading: Conservation Specialists
text: For any public art valued over 15,000 crowns, or for any artwork older than 30 years, consultation with a professional art conservator is mandatory for all major repairs, restorations, or significant cleaning operations. Conservators must be certified by a recognized national or international professional body, with at least 5 years of experience in the specific materials of the artwork. Their recommendations must be followed unless compelling reasons, documented in writing, necessitate an alternative approach. Any deviation must be approved by the municipal cultural heritage committee.

heading: Training of Personnel
text: Personnel responsible for the day-to-day maintenance of public art must receive appropriate training. This training should cover basic art handling, understanding of different art materials, safe cleaning practices, and early detection of damage. A minimum of 8 hours of specialized training per year is required for all staff directly involved in public art maintenance. Municipalities may collaborate to organize joint training programs to ensure consistent standards across Nordvale. Records of staff training must be kept for audit purposes.

heading: Public Engagement
text: Municipalities are encouraged to engage the public in the appreciation and care of public art. This can include educational programs, public tours, and accessible information about artworks and their maintenance. Public engagement initiatives, such as 'adopt-an-artwork' programs, should be considered to foster community ownership and vigilance. Any such program must adhere strictly to established maintenance protocols and not involve direct intervention with the artwork by untrained volunteers. Information panels near artworks should be updated every 5 years.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All public art installations with an acquisition value exceeding 10,000 crowns must be adequately insured against damage, theft, and vandalism. The insurance policy must cover at least 80% of the artwork's current market valuation, or its full replacement cost if replacement is feasible and desired. Insurance reviews must be conducted annually to ensure coverage remains appropriate. For artworks of exceptional value, exceeding 250,000 crowns, a specialized fine art insurance policy is mandatory.

heading: Vandalism Prevention
text: Municipalities should implement measures to deter vandalism, such as adequate lighting, landscaping that does not conceal artworks, and, where appropriate, surveillance. For artworks with a history of repeated vandalism, enhanced protective coatings or increased monitoring frequency may be necessary. Information campaigns discouraging vandalism should be periodically conducted, especially in areas with high incidence rates. Reports of vandalism should be filed with local law enforcement within 24 hours.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any person or organization aggrieved by a decision made by a municipal authority regarding public art maintenance under this Act may appeal the decision. An initial appeal must be lodged with the municipal council within 30 days of the decision. If unsatisfied with the municipal council's response, a further appeal may be made to the Nordvale Ministry of Culture within 60 days. The Ministry will review the appeal and issue a final determination within 90 days. Decisions related to immediate safety hazards are not subject to appeal until the hazard is resolved.

heading: Annual Reporting
text: Each municipal authority must submit an annual report to the Nordvale Ministry of Culture by March 31st of each year. This report must detail: (a) the current inventory of public art; (b) maintenance activities undertaken in the past year; (c) expenditures on public art maintenance; (d) any incidents of damage or vandalism; and (e) planned maintenance for the upcoming year. The report should also include an assessment of the overall condition of the public art collection within the municipality. Failure to submit this report may result in penalties outlined in section 27.

heading: Review of Maintenance Plans
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Culture will conduct a review of municipal public art maintenance plans every 3 years. This review will assess compliance with this Act, the effectiveness of the plans, and identify best practices. Municipalities found to have inadequate plans or consistent non-compliance may be required to revise their plans within 90 days and submit them for re-approval. The Ministry may also offer guidance and resources to assist municipalities in improving their maintenance strategies.

heading: Review of Maintenance Plans
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Culture will conduct a review of municipal public art maintenance plans every 2 years. This review will assess compliance with this Act, the effectiveness of the plans, and identify best practices. Municipalities found to have inadequate plans or consistent non-compliance may be required to revise their plans within 60 days and submit them for re-approval. The Ministry may also offer guidance and resources to assist municipalities in improving their maintenance strategies. A public summary of these reviews will be published online.

heading: Review of Maintenance Plans
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Culture will conduct a review of municipal public art maintenance plans annually. This review will assess compliance with this Act, the effectiveness of the plans, and identify best practices. Municipalities found to have inadequate plans or consistent non-compliance will be required to revise their plans within 45 days and submit them for re-approval. The Ministry will also offer guidance and resources to assist municipalities in improving their maintenance strategies. A public summary of these reviews will be published online within 30 days of completion.

heading: Use of Public Funds
text: All public funds allocated for the maintenance and preservation of public art must be used judiciously and transparently. Detailed records of all expenditures, including invoices and contractor agreements, must be maintained for a minimum of 7 years. These records are subject to audit by the Nordvale Audit Office. Any misuse of funds or unauthorized expenditures for purposes other than public art maintenance may result in disciplinary action against the responsible municipal officials and require repayment of misspent funds. Transparency reports on spending must be made available to the public.

heading: Collaboration with Artists
text: Where feasible and practical, municipalities should attempt to consult with the original artist during major conservation or restoration projects. This is particularly important for artworks less than 20 years old. Artists should be given the opportunity to provide input on proposed treatments, especially if the treatment might alter the artwork's appearance or integrity. If the artist is deceased or cannot be located after reasonable effort (documented attempts over 90 days), decisions should be made by qualified conservators in consultation with art historians. A consultation fee of up to 500 crowns can be offered to living artists.

heading: Material and Technique Specifications
text: When new public art is commissioned or acquired, the artist must provide detailed specifications regarding the materials used and recommended maintenance techniques. This information, including supplier details and expected lifespan of materials, must be included in the artwork's documentation file (as per section 8). This requirement applies to all artworks with an acquisition value exceeding 2,000 crowns. Municipalities should consider the long-term durability and maintenance costs of proposed materials during the selection process for new art.
