Materials with an expected lifespan of less than 10 years should generally be avoided for permanent installations.

heading: Enforcement and Penalties
text: Failure by a municipal authority to comply with the provisions of this Act may result in penalties. For minor infractions, a written warning will be issued, requiring rectification within 60 days. Persistent non-compliance or serious breaches, such as neglecting safety hazards, may lead to financial penalties of up to 10,000 crowns per infraction. These penalties may be levied by the Nordvale Ministry of Culture. Funds collected from penalties will be directed to a central fund for public art conservation initiatives across Nordvale. Repeat offenders may face increased fines, up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Enforcement and Penalties
text: Failure by a municipal authority to comply with the provisions of this Act may result in penalties. For minor infractions, a written warning will be issued, requiring rectification within 45 days. Persistent non-compliance or serious breaches, such as neglecting safety hazards, may lead to financial penalties of up to 15,000 crowns per infraction. These penalties may be levied by the Nordvale Ministry of Culture. Funds collected from penalties will be directed to a central fund for public art conservation initiatives across Nordvale. Repeat offenders may face increased fines, up to 35,000 crowns, and potentially a reduction in cultural grants.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Municipalities have a period of 12 months from the enactment date of this Act to bring all existing public art maintenance practices into full compliance. This includes establishing maintenance plans, conducting initial inspections, and allocating necessary budget funds. For public art installed prior to this Act, documentation requirements (section 8) must be fulfilled as far as reasonably possible within 18 months. New public art installed after the enactment date must comply immediately with all provisions of this Act from the date of installation. The Ministry of Culture will provide guidance during this transitional period.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: The Public Art Care Ordinance of 1995 is hereby repealed. All provisions of that ordinance are superseded by this Act. Any regulations or guidelines issued under the Public Art Care Ordinance of 1995 that are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act shall remain in force until such time as new regulations are issued under this Act. Any legal proceedings commenced under the repealed ordinance may continue as if the ordinance had not been repealed, unless specifically altered by this Act.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Short Title and Commencement
text: This Act may be cited as the 'Public Art Maintenance Duties Act'. It shall come into force on the first day of the month following its proclamation. This date will be publicly announced by the Nordvale Ministry of Justice at least 30 days prior to commencement. All provisions of this Act apply uniformly across all municipalities of the Republic of Nordvale from the commencement date. Any subsequent amendments to this Act will also specify their own commencement dates.

heading: Concessions
text: The civil ceremony fee is reduced by half for any person who has been a registered licensed hot-spring attendant for at least one year.

heading: Special categories
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a certified bookbinder pays no fee or allowance as specified in SPA §6.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the periodic inspection and maintenance of public art installations across Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety of the public, preserve the artistic and cultural value of these installations, and prevent deterioration due to neglect or environmental factors. All public art installations, whether owned by the state, municipalities, or public-private partnerships, are subject to the provisions outlined herein. The Act covers a wide range of artistic mediums, including sculptures, murals, and fixed installations, ensuring their longevity for future generations.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Public Art Installation' refers to any permanent or semi-permanent artistic work displayed in a publicly accessible space, including but not limited to parks, squares, public buildings, and transportation hubs.
(2) 'Inspection Authority' refers to the designated municipal or state body responsible for conducting inspections.
(3) 'Maintenance Report' refers to a formal document detailing the condition of an installation and recommended actions.
(4) 'Urgent Repair' signifies a repair deemed necessary within 72 hours to avert immediate danger to public safety or prevent irreversible damage to the artwork.
(5) 'Minor Repair' indicates a repair that can be completed within 30 days and costs less than 5,000 crowns.

heading: Inspection Authority Designation
text: Each municipality in Nordvale shall designate an Inspection Authority responsible for overseeing public art inspections within its jurisdiction. This authority may be an existing municipal department or a newly formed committee. The designation must be formally communicated to the Ministry of Culture within 30 days of this Act coming into force. The Inspection Authority must comprise at least three members with expertise in art conservation, engineering, or public safety. The city of Aldmark, as the capital, will establish a central oversight committee.

heading: Inspection Authority Designation
text: Each municipality in Nordvale shall designate an Inspection Authority responsible for overseeing public art inspections within its jurisdiction. This authority may be an existing municipal department or a newly formed committee. The designation must be formally communicated to the Ministry of Culture within 60 days of this Act coming into force. The Inspection Authority must comprise at least five members with expertise in art conservation, engineering, public safety, or urban planning. The city of Aldmark, as the capital, will establish a central oversight committee with at least 7 members.

heading: Frequency of Inspections
text: All public art installations shall be subjected to a routine maintenance inspection at least once every 24 months. Installations identified as high-risk, due to their materials, location, or age exceeding 50 years, shall be inspected annually. The Inspection Authority in each municipality is responsible for maintaining an updated schedule of these inspections. Newly installed artworks require their first inspection within 12 months of installation, irrespective of their risk classification. A minimum of 40% of all public artworks must be inspected each calendar year.

heading: Frequency of Inspections
text: All public art installations shall be subjected to a routine maintenance inspection at least once every 18 months. Installations identified as high-risk, due to their materials, location, or age exceeding 30 years, shall be inspected every nine months. The Inspection Authority in each municipality is responsible for maintaining an updated schedule of these inspections. Newly installed artworks require their first inspection within 6 months of installation, irrespective of their risk classification. A minimum of 60% of all public artworks must be inspected each calendar year.

heading: High-Risk Classification Criteria
text: An artwork is classified as high-risk if it meets one or more of the following criteria: (a) it is situated in a high-traffic area with over 5,000 daily visitors; (b) it incorporates fragile materials such as glass, unfired clay, or aged wood; (c) its structural integrity relies on complex engineering, involving elements over 10 meters in height; (d) it has previously undergone major repairs costing more than 20,000 crowns within the last 5 years; or (e) it is located within 50 meters of a coastal area or major river prone to flooding.

heading: Inspection Procedures
text: Inspections shall be conducted by qualified personnel, including certified art conservators or structural engineers, as appropriate for the artwork's nature. Each inspection must include a visual assessment, photographic documentation, and a detailed written report. Special attention shall be paid to structural stability, material degradation, public safety hazards, and vandalism. The inspection team must consist of at least two individuals, one of whom must hold a relevant professional certification. Any observed damage exceeding a 5 cm dimension must be recorded.

heading: Inspection Report Content
text: Every inspection report shall include: (a) the date and time of inspection; (b) the names and qualifications of inspecting personnel; (c) a comprehensive description of the artwork's current condition, including any detected deterioration or damage; (d) an assessment of public safety risks; (e) recommended maintenance or repair actions, categorized by urgency; (f) estimated costs for each recommended action exceeding 1,000 crowns; and (g) a photographic log of the artwork from at least three different angles, highlighting any areas of concern.

heading: Submission of Inspection Reports
text: All completed inspection reports must be submitted to the relevant Municipal Inspection Authority within 14 calendar days of the inspection. The Authority shall review the report for completeness and accuracy within an additional 7 days. If the report identifies an 'Urgent Repair', the Authority must be notified verbally within 24 hours of discovery, followed by the written report within 3 days. A digital copy of all reports shall be maintained for a minimum of 10 years, and a physical copy for 5 years.

heading: Maintenance and Repair Timelines
text:
(1) Urgent Repairs identified in an inspection report must be initiated within 72 hours of the report's submission to the Inspection Authority.
(2) Minor Repairs must be initiated within 30 days.
(3) All other recommended repairs or maintenance tasks must be initiated within 90 days.
(4) Failure to adhere to these timelines without justifiable cause may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. The responsible party must provide a detailed plan for urgent repairs within 24 hours of notification.

heading: Maintenance and Repair Timelines
text:
(1) Urgent Repairs identified in an inspection report must be initiated within 48 hours of the report's submission to the Inspection Authority.
(2) Minor Repairs must be initiated within 21 days.
(3) All other recommended repairs or maintenance tasks must be initiated within 60 days.
(4) Failure to adhere to these timelines without justifiable cause may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. The responsible party must provide a detailed plan for urgent repairs within 12 hours of notification.

heading: Funding for Maintenance
text: Funding for the maintenance and repair of public art installations is primarily the responsibility of the entity that owns or is legally responsible for the artwork. The national government will allocate a Public Art Maintenance Fund of 5,000,000 crowns annually to assist municipalities with significant repair costs, particularly for urgent repairs exceeding 100,000 crowns. Municipalities can apply for up to 75% reimbursement for eligible repair expenses from this fund. Applications must demonstrate that local funds are insufficient to cover 100% of the cost.

heading: Public Access to Reports
text: Summaries of all inspection reports, excluding sensitive information pertaining to security or proprietary repair methods, shall be made publicly available on the respective municipal websites within 30 days of their approval by the Inspection Authority. Full reports can be accessed by members of the public upon written request, with a processing fee of 50 crowns per report. Personal identifying information of individuals involved in the inspection or ownership will be redacted. A minimum of 20% of public artworks' full reports must be available for public viewing without a fee.

heading: Role of the Ministry of Culture
text: The Ministry of Culture is responsible for establishing national standards and guidelines for public art inspections and maintenance. It will also serve as an appeal body for disputes arising from inspection findings or recommended actions. The Ministry will conduct an annual review of municipal inspection programs to ensure compliance with this Act and provide training resources for inspectors. A dedicated team of three experts within the Ministry will oversee these functions, meeting quarterly to discuss program effectiveness.

heading: Training and Certification
text: All individuals conducting public art inspections must complete a certified training program approved by the Ministry of Culture. This program will cover art conservation techniques, structural assessment, safety protocols, and report writing. Certification must be renewed every 3 years. Municipalities are responsible for ensuring their inspection personnel meet these certification requirements. At least 80% of all inspectors across Nordvale must hold valid certification by the end of 2025. The initial training course will be 40 hours in duration.

heading: Training and Certification
text: All individuals conducting public art inspections must complete a certified training program approved by the Ministry of Culture. This program will cover art conservation techniques, structural assessment, safety protocols, and report writing. Certification must be renewed every 2 years. Municipalities are responsible for ensuring their inspection personnel meet these certification requirements. At least 95% of all inspectors across Nordvale must hold valid certification by the end of 2028. The initial training course will be 60 hours in duration.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text: In cases where a public art installation poses an immediate and severe threat to public safety, the Inspection Authority or local emergency services may order its immediate closure, partial dismantling, or removal. Such actions must be documented within 24 hours, and a full report submitted within 7 days. The cost of emergency procedures shall be borne by the municipality initially, with potential reimbursement from the national fund if criteria are met. Public access must be restricted within a 10-meter radius of any immediate danger.

heading: Database of Public Art
text: The Ministry of Culture, in collaboration with municipal authorities, shall establish and maintain a national database of all public art installations. This database will include location, artist, date of installation, materials, and a complete history of inspection reports and maintenance activities. Each artwork will be assigned a unique identification number. This database must be fully operational and contain at least 75% of existing public artworks by the end of 2025. Access to this database will be restricted to authorized personnel.

heading: Review of Inspection Guidelines
text: The Ministry of Culture shall review the national inspection guidelines and protocols at least once every 5 years to incorporate new best practices in art conservation and public safety. Input from municipalities, art experts, and the public will be considered during this review process. Any proposed changes to the guidelines will be published for public comment for a period of 60 days before final adoption. The first review must commence no later than 2028.

heading: Reporting Vandalism
text:
(1) Any act of vandalism against a public art installation must be reported to the local police and the Municipal Inspection Authority within 24 hours of its discovery.
(2) The Inspection Authority shall assess the damage within 48 hours and determine if urgent repair is required.
(3) A detailed report, including photographs and an estimated repair cost, must be submitted within 7 days.
(4) Municipalities are encouraged to install surveillance cameras within 20 meters of high-value or frequently vandalized artworks.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All owners of public art installations, whether state or municipal, must maintain adequate insurance coverage for damage, theft, and third-party liability. The minimum coverage for property damage must be 500,000 crowns, and for third-party liability, 1,000,000 crowns. Proof of insurance must be provided to the Inspection Authority annually. Public-private partnerships are required to maintain joint insurance policies meeting these thresholds. This insurance must cover at least 90% of the artwork's estimated value.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any party aggrieved by an Inspection Authority's decision regarding inspection findings or required maintenance may lodge an appeal with the Ministry of Culture within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The Ministry will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days.
(3) The Ministry's decision is final and binding. An appeal fee of 200 crowns applies, which is refundable if the appeal is successful.
(4) The Ministry must establish an independent three-member panel to hear all appeals, ensuring impartiality.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Ministry of Culture and municipal authorities shall collaborate on public awareness campaigns to educate citizens about the value of public art and the importance of its preservation. These campaigns will highlight the negative impact of vandalism and encourage reporting of damage or suspicious activities. A minimum of 100,000 crowns shall be allocated annually for these campaigns, reaching at least 25% of the population through various media channels. Educational materials will be distributed in all schools within 500 meters of public art.

heading: Biennial Municipal Reporting
text: Each Municipal Inspection Authority shall submit a comprehensive report to the Ministry of Culture every two years, detailing their inspection activities, maintenance expenditures, and any challenges encountered. This report must include statistics on the number of inspections conducted, the types of repairs undertaken, and the average cost of repairs. The report is due by March 31st following the end of the biennial period. A minimum of 90% compliance with inspection schedules must be demonstrated.

heading: Access to Sites
text: Owners and responsible parties must grant inspectors safe and unimpeded access to public art installations for the purpose of conducting inspections. At least 48 hours' notice must be provided for routine inspections. In cases of urgent or emergency inspections, access must be granted immediately. Failure to provide access without justifiable reason may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns per incident. Inspectors must carry official identification at all times and present it upon request.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All records pertaining to public art installations, including acquisition documents, artist contracts, installation details, and a complete history of maintenance and repairs, must be diligently maintained by the responsible parties for the lifetime of the artwork plus 10 years. These records shall be made available to the Inspection Authority upon request. Digital records must be backed up weekly, and physical records stored in a secure, climate-controlled environment.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) For new public art installations, an environmental impact assessment must be conducted prior to installation if the artwork is larger than 5 cubic meters or involves materials that may degrade into the surrounding ecosystem.
(2) This assessment shall consider potential impacts on local flora, fauna, and water sources.
(3) The assessment report must be submitted to the Municipal Inspection Authority and approved by the Ministry of Environment. Installation cannot proceed without this approval, which must be obtained at least 90 days before proposed installation.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Failure to conduct mandatory inspections or submit reports within specified timelines may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per instance for minor infractions, and up to 10,000 crowns for repeated or severe non-compliance.
(2) Failure to undertake Urgent Repairs within the required timeframe will incur a daily fine of 500 crowns until the repair is initiated.
(3) Persistent non-compliance may lead to the Ministry of Culture commissioning the repairs directly and billing the responsible party at a 20% premium over actual costs.
(4) Fines exceeding 50,000 crowns can lead to legal action to recover costs.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Failure to conduct mandatory inspections or submit reports within specified timelines may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns per instance for minor infractions, and up to 25,000 crowns for repeated or severe non-compliance.
(2) Failure to undertake Urgent Repairs within the required timeframe will incur a daily fine of 1,500 crowns until the repair is initiated.
(3) Persistent non-compliance may lead to the Ministry of Culture commissioning the repairs directly and billing the responsible party at a 50% premium over actual costs.
(4) Fines exceeding 100,000 crowns can lead to legal action to recover costs.

heading: Review of Penalties
text: The Ministry of Culture shall review the schedule of penalties outlined in section 25 every 3 years to ensure they remain appropriate and effective in deterring non-compliance. Any adjustments to the penalty amounts or categories will be subject to public consultation for a period of 45 days. The first review must be completed by the end of 2027. This review will include an analysis of compliance rates across all municipalities and the impact of existing penalties on repair completion.

heading: Collaboration with Art Experts
text: Municipal Inspection Authorities are encouraged to establish advisory panels comprising local art historians, conservators, and artists to provide expertise on specific artworks or complex conservation challenges. These panels should meet at least twice a year and provide non-binding recommendations. The Ministry of Culture will maintain a registry of qualified art experts for municipalities to consult. At least 50% of the members of such panels should have over 10 years of experience in their respective fields.

heading: New Art Installation Requirements
text: Proposals for new public art installations exceeding 2 meters in any dimension or costing more than 50,000 crowns must include a detailed maintenance plan and an estimated lifecycle cost analysis. This plan must be approved by the Municipal Inspection Authority prior to installation. The design must also consider future accessibility for inspection and maintenance. Failure to submit such a plan will result in rejection of the proposal. The plan must project costs for at least 30 years into the future.

heading: New Art Installation Requirements
text: Proposals for new public art installations exceeding 1.5 meters in any dimension or costing more than 25,000 crowns must include a detailed maintenance plan and an estimated lifecycle cost analysis. This plan must be approved by the Municipal Inspection Authority prior to installation. The design must also consider future accessibility for inspection and maintenance. Failure to submit such a plan will result in rejection of the proposal. The plan must project costs for at least 50 years into the future and detail annual maintenance budgets.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: Each municipality is required to allocate a minimum of 0.05% of its total annual budget towards the inspection, maintenance, and repair of public art installations. This allocation must be clearly itemized in the municipal budget. The Ministry of Culture will monitor these allocations and may provide additional grants to municipalities that demonstrate exceptional need or commitment to public art preservation. Municipalities with over 100 public artworks must allocate at least 0.1% of their budget.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: Each municipality is required to allocate a minimum of 0.08% of its total annual budget towards the inspection, maintenance, and repair of public art installations. This allocation must be clearly itemized in the municipal budget. The Ministry of Culture will monitor these allocations and may provide additional grants to municipalities that demonstrate exceptional need or commitment to public art preservation. Municipalities with over 50 public artworks must allocate at least 0.15% of their budget, and submit quarterly spending reports.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2024. All municipalities and relevant bodies are expected to have established the necessary structures and procedures by this date. Any public art installed prior to this date will be brought into compliance with this Act within 12 months. Public artworks installed on or after this date are subject to immediate compliance. The Ministry of Culture will issue a detailed implementation guide within 3 months of this commencement date.

heading: Reduced charges
text: The repayment of the study grant is reduced for any person who is a registered tide-table surveyor for at least one year, allowing them an additional 30 days to commence repayments as outlined in SSA §13.

heading: Particular persons
text: Where the person liable is a licensed bell ringer of a parish tower, the fee or allowance in HOA §6 shall be fixed at 5 crowns.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Each registered lacemaker receives a fixed payment of 5 crowns annually in March, instead of the water bill rebate.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing of venues within the Republic of Nordvale that host performing arts events. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, maintain appropriate standards for facilities, and promote a thriving and regulated cultural sector. This Act applies to any establishment, whether permanent or temporary, that is used for live theatrical performances, musical concerts, dance shows, or similar artistic presentations for which an admission fee is typically charged or where the public is invited to attend. It does not cover private gatherings or events without public access or commercial intent. All venues falling under this scope must obtain and maintain a valid licence as detailed in subsequent sections.

heading: Definitions
text: (1) 'Venue' means any building, structure, or designated area primarily used for the presentation of performing arts events to an audience of 50 individuals or more. This includes theatres, concert halls, and temporary event spaces. (2) 'Performing Arts Event' refers to any live presentation of theatre, music, dance, opera, or spoken word, intended for public entertainment or cultural enrichment. (3) 'Licensing Authority' means the Nordvale Cultural Directorate, responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. (4) 'Applicant' refers to any individual, partnership, or corporate entity seeking to obtain or renew a licence under this Act. (5) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale.

heading: Licence Requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a performing arts venue within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid Performing Arts Venue Licence issued by the Licensing Authority. This requirement applies to all venues irrespective of their seating capacity, provided they host performing arts events accessible to the public. Operating a venue without a valid licence may result in immediate closure and a penalty fee of 2,000 crowns for each day of unlicensed operation, up to a maximum of 60,000 crowns. The Licensing Authority reserves the right to impose additional sanctions as deemed appropriate.

heading: Application Process
text: (1) An application for a Performing Arts Venue Licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 90 days prior to the intended opening date of the venue or the expiry of an existing licence. (2) The application shall be made on the prescribed form, available from the Licensing Authority's offices or website. (3) A non-refundable application fee of 1,000 crowns must accompany all initial applications. (4) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days, and the 90-day processing period will recommence upon receipt of a fully completed application. (5) The applicant must be at least 18 years of age.

heading: Application Process
text: (1) An application for a Performing Arts Venue Licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 120 days prior to the intended opening date of the venue or the expiry of an existing licence. (2) The application shall be made on the prescribed form, available from the Licensing Authority's offices or website. (3) A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns must accompany all initial applications. (4) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 days, and the 120-day processing period will recommence upon receipt of a fully completed application. (5) The applicant must be at least 21 years of age and a resident of Nordvale for at least 3 years.

heading: Application Process
text: (1) An application for a Performing Arts Venue Licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 150 days prior to the intended opening date of the venue or the expiry of an existing licence. (2) The application shall be made exclusively through the online portal on the prescribed form, available from the Licensing Authority's website. (3) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns must accompany all initial applications. (4) Incomplete applications will be rejected immediately, and a new application must be submitted. (5) The applicant must be at least 25 years of age and a citizen of Nordvale.

heading: Required Documentation
text: (1) All applications must include a detailed floor plan of the venue, scaled at 1:100, indicating exits, seating arrangements, and stage dimensions. (2) Proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 500,000 crowns must be provided. (3) A copy of the fire safety certificate issued by the Nordvale Fire Service, not older than 12 months, is mandatory. (4) A comprehensive operational plan, outlining event management procedures, security measures, and crowd control protocols, must be submitted. (5) Evidence of ownership or a valid lease agreement for the venue property must also be included with the application package.

heading: Inspection and Assessment
text: (1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Licensing Authority shall arrange for an inspection of the proposed venue. (2) This inspection shall be conducted by a minimum of two authorized inspectors within 60 days of the application submission. (3) The inspectors will assess the venue's compliance with all relevant safety standards, accessibility requirements, and operational readiness as outlined in the submitted plans. (4) The applicant must ensure that the venue is fully prepared for inspection and that all necessary personnel are available to assist the inspectors. (5) Failure to cooperate with an inspection may result in the rejection of the application without refund.

heading: Licence Categories
text: (1) Performing Arts Venue Licences are categorized based on venue capacity. (2) Category A is for venues with a maximum audience capacity of 100 individuals. (3) Category B is for venues with a maximum audience capacity between 101 and 500 individuals. (4) Category C is for venues with a maximum audience capacity exceeding 500 individuals. (5) Each category has specific requirements regarding safety features, staffing levels, and insurance coverage, detailed in separate guidelines issued by the Licensing Authority.

heading: Licence Categories
text: (1) Performing Arts Venue Licences are categorized based on venue capacity and primary event type. (2) Category A is for venues with a maximum audience capacity of 75 individuals, primarily hosting experimental theatre or recitals. (3) Category B is for venues with a maximum audience capacity between 76 and 400 individuals, suitable for musical concerts or dance. (4) Category C is for venues with a maximum audience capacity exceeding 400 individuals, designated for large-scale productions. (5) Each category has specific requirements regarding safety features, staffing levels, and insurance coverage, detailed in separate guidelines issued by the Licensing Authority, with Category C venues requiring 24-hour security personnel.

heading: Licence Categories
text: (1) Performing Arts Venue Licences are categorized based on venue capacity, primary event type, and duration of operation. (2) Category A is for venues with a maximum audience capacity of 50 individuals, primarily hosting experimental theatre or recitals, and operating for less than 100 days per year. (3) Category B is for venues with a maximum audience capacity between 51 and 300 individuals, suitable for musical concerts or dance, operating for 100-250 days per year. (4) Category C is for venues with a maximum audience capacity exceeding 300 individuals, designated for large-scale productions, operating for more than 250 days per year. (5) Each category has specific requirements regarding safety features, staffing levels, and insurance coverage, detailed in separate guidelines issued by the Licensing Authority, with Category C venues requiring 24-hour security personnel and a dedicated medical team.

heading: Licence Fees
text: (1) Annual licence fees are determined by the venue category. (2) For Category A venues, the annual fee is 3,000 crowns. (3) For Category B venues, the annual fee is 7,500 crowns. (4) For Category C venues, the annual fee is 15,000 crowns. (5) These fees are due on the anniversary of the licence issuance date and must be paid in full within 30 days to avoid late penalties of 500 crowns per month.

heading: Licence Fees
text: (1) Annual licence fees are determined by the venue category and location. (2) For Category A venues, the annual fee is 3,500 crowns, increasing to 4,000 crowns in Aldmark. (3) For Category B venues, the annual fee is 8,000 crowns, increasing to 9,000 crowns in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. (4) For Category C venues, the annual fee is 16,000 crowns, increasing to 18,000 crowns in any municipality. (5) These fees are due on the anniversary of the licence issuance date and must be paid in full within 20 days to avoid late penalties of 750 crowns per month, capped at 4,500 crowns per year.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text: (1) A Performing Arts Venue Licence is valid for a period of one year from its date of issuance. (2) Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiry date of the current licence. (3) The renewal application requires a declaration that no significant structural changes have occurred and an updated fire safety certificate. (4) A renewal fee equivalent to the annual licence fee for the respective category is payable upon submission. (5) Failure to renew a licence before its expiry date will result in the licence becoming invalid, and the venue must cease operations until a new licence is obtained.

heading: Conditions of Licence
text: (1) All licensed venues must prominently display their licence certificate near the main entrance. (2) The maximum audience capacity stated on the licence must not be exceeded under any circumstances. (3) All emergency exits must be kept clear and unobstructed at all times. (4) Fire suppression systems and alarm systems must be regularly inspected and maintained in accordance with Nordvale Fire Service regulations, with records kept for at least 24 months. (5) Staff trained in first aid and emergency procedures must be present during all performing arts events.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text: (1) The Licensing Authority may revoke a Performing Arts Venue Licence if the licence holder fails to comply with any condition of the licence or any provision of this Act. (2) A written notice of intent to revoke, detailing the grounds for revocation, will be issued at least 30 days prior to the effective date of revocation. (3) The licence holder has the right to appeal the decision within 15 days of receiving the notice. (4) Severe breaches of safety regulations, such as exceeding capacity by 20% or more, may result in immediate temporary suspension followed by revocation. (5) The venue must cease operations upon revocation.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text: (1) A Performing Arts Venue Licence may be temporarily suspended by the Licensing Authority for serious non-compliance issues that pose an immediate risk to public safety. (2) Such suspension may be issued without prior notice if the risk is deemed critical. (3) The suspension notice will specify the duration of the suspension, typically not exceeding 30 days, and the corrective actions required for reinstatement. (4) During a suspension period, the venue is strictly prohibited from hosting any performing arts events. (5) Failure to comply with a suspension order may result in an additional penalty of 5,000 crowns per day.

heading: Appeals Process
text: (1) Any applicant whose licence application has been denied, or any licence holder whose licence has been revoked or suspended, may appeal the decision. (2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal within 21 days of receiving the decision notice. (3) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include any supporting documentation. (4) The Tribunal will review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. (5) The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: (1) Licence holders must report any significant incidents occurring at the venue to the Licensing Authority within 24 hours. (2) Significant incidents include, but are not limited to, fires, structural failures, serious injuries requiring hospitalization, or any event leading to the evacuation of 25% or more of the audience. (3) A detailed written report must follow within 7 days of the incident. (4) Failure to report an incident may result in a penalty of up to 10,000 crowns. (5) The Licensing Authority may conduct its own investigation into reported incidents.

heading: Structural Integrity
text: (1) All licensed venues must undergo a structural integrity assessment by a certified engineer every 5 years. (2) A copy of the engineer's report, certifying the safety and stability of the building, must be submitted to the Licensing Authority. (3) Any recommendations for structural repairs or modifications outlined in the report must be addressed within 6 months of the report date. (4) Venues built before 1970 must undergo this assessment every 3 years. (5) Failure to submit a valid certificate may result in licence suspension.

heading: Structural Integrity
text: (1) All licensed venues must undergo a structural integrity assessment by a certified engineer every 3 years. (2) A copy of the engineer's report, certifying the safety and stability of the building, must be submitted to the Licensing Authority within 30 days of completion. (3) Any recommendations for structural repairs or modifications outlined in the report must be addressed within 4 months of the report date. (4) Venues built before 1980 must undergo this assessment every 2 years. (5) Failure to submit a valid certificate may result in immediate licence suspension and a penalty of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Preparedness
text: (1) Each venue must have a comprehensive emergency preparedness plan, reviewed and updated annually. (2) This plan must include procedures for evacuation, medical emergencies, and security threats. (3) All venue staff must receive training on emergency procedures at least twice a year. (4) Fire drills must be conducted at least once every 12 months, with attendance records maintained for inspection. (5) The plan must be readily accessible to all staff and provided to the Licensing Authority upon request.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text: (1) All licensed venues must comply with Nordvale's accessibility standards for public buildings. (2) This includes providing accessible entrances, restrooms, and designated seating areas for individuals with mobility impairments. (3) For venues with capacities exceeding 100 individuals, at least 5% of all seating must be readily accessible, with clear pathways. (4) Ramps must have a slope not exceeding 1:12, and doorways must be at least 90cm wide. (5) New venues or those undergoing major renovations must integrate full accessibility features during construction.

heading: Fire Safety Equipment
text: (1) All venues must be equipped with appropriate fire extinguishers, located within 15 meters of any point in the audience area. (2) Fire alarm systems must be tested monthly, and sprinkler systems annually, with documented records. (3) Emergency lighting must activate automatically upon power failure and remain functional for at least 90 minutes. (4) All fire safety equipment must be certified and maintained by a Nordvale-approved vendor. (5) A minimum of one fire blanket must be present backstage and in any kitchen area.

heading: Public Health Standards
text: (1) Venues must maintain high standards of cleanliness and hygiene in all public and staff areas. (2) Restrooms must be cleaned at least once every 4 hours during operating times. (3) Adequate ventilation systems must be in place to ensure good air quality throughout the venue. (4) Hand washing facilities with soap and running water must be available in all restrooms and staff areas. (5) Any food or beverage service within the venue must adhere to separate public health regulations and obtain additional permits if required.

heading: Insurance Coverage
text: (1) Licence holders must maintain valid public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns for Category A venues, 1,000,000 crowns for Category B, and 2,000,000 crowns for Category C. (2) Proof of current insurance must be submitted annually with the licence renewal application. (3) The Licensing Authority must be named as an interested party on the insurance policy. (4) Any lapse in insurance coverage exceeding 7 days will result in immediate suspension of the licence. (5) Insurance policies must cover injury to patrons and property damage.

heading: Security Measures
text: (1) Venues with a capacity exceeding 200 individuals must employ at least one licensed security guard during all public events. (2) For venues exceeding 500 individuals, a minimum of three security personnel are required. (3) Security personnel must be visible and easily identifiable. (4) An emergency communication system must be in place, linking security staff to management. (5) Regular patrols of the venue perimeter during events are mandatory to ensure external safety.

heading: Security Measures
text: (1) Venues with a capacity exceeding 150 individuals must employ at least one licensed security guard during all public events. (2) For venues exceeding 400 individuals, a minimum of four security personnel are required, and at least one must be a certified first responder. (3) Security personnel must be visible, easily identifiable, and wear body cameras during all shifts. (4) An emergency communication system must be in place, linking security staff to management and local emergency services. (5) Regular patrols of the venue perimeter during events are mandatory to ensure external safety, occurring at intervals no longer than 30 minutes.

heading: Ticketing and Admission
text: (1) All tickets issued for events at licensed venues must clearly state the venue name, event date, and specific seating or standing area if applicable. (2) The number of tickets sold for any event must not exceed the venue's approved maximum audience capacity. (3) Venues must implement a system to verify tickets upon entry. (4) Admission must be denied to any individual causing a disturbance or appearing to be under the influence of illicit substances. (5) Re-entry policies must be clearly communicated to patrons upon admission.

heading: Waste Management
text: (1) All venues must have an effective waste management plan to handle refuse generated during operations. (2) Waste receptacles must be readily available and emptied regularly to prevent overflow. (3) Recycling facilities for paper, plastic, and glass must be provided for patrons and staff. (4) Waste must be stored in secure, rodent-proof containers awaiting collection. (5) Waste disposal must comply with all local environmental regulations of the specific municipality, ensuring responsible handling of materials.

heading: Storage of Materials
text: (1) All stage props, sets, and other performance materials must be stored safely and securely when not in use. (2) Flammable materials must be stored in designated fire-rated areas, separate from public access routes. (3) Storage areas must be kept tidy and free from obstructions. (4) A clear inventory of all stored materials must be maintained, especially for items considered hazardous. (5) Access to storage areas must be restricted to authorized personnel only to prevent unauthorized tampering or theft.

heading: Staff Training
text: (1) All venue staff, including ushers, box office personnel, and technical crew, must receive initial training on venue policies and emergency procedures within 30 days of employment. (2) Refresher training sessions must be conducted at least annually. (3) Staff responsible for first aid must hold a valid certification from a recognized Nordvale medical training provider. (4) A record of all staff training, including dates and attendees, must be maintained for a minimum of 3 years. (5) New staff members must undergo a probationary period of 90 days.

heading: Maintenance and Upkeep
text: (1) Licensed venues must be maintained in a good state of repair, both structurally and aesthetically. (2) Regular inspections of seating, flooring, and electrical systems must be carried out at least quarterly. (3) Any defects or hazards identified must be rectified within 7 days, or immediately if they pose a significant safety risk. (4) A maintenance log detailing all inspections and repairs must be kept on site for at least 5 years. (5) All electrical wiring and appliances must be inspected by a certified electrician every 2 years.

heading: Maintenance and Upkeep
text: (1) Licensed venues must be maintained in an excellent state of repair, both structurally and aesthetically. (2) Regular inspections of seating, flooring, and electrical systems must be carried out at least monthly. (3) Any defects or hazards identified must be rectified within 3 days, or immediately if they pose a significant safety risk. (4) A digital maintenance log detailing all inspections and repairs must be kept on site for at least 10 years, accessible via an online portal. (5) All electrical wiring and appliances must be inspected by a certified electrician every 18 months, with a full report submitted to the Licensing Authority.

heading: CCTV Surveillance
text: (1) Venues with a capacity exceeding 300 individuals must install and maintain a functional CCTV surveillance system covering all public areas, entrances, and exits. (2) Recordings must be retained for a minimum of 30 days and made available to the Licensing Authority or law enforcement upon request. (3) Clear signage must be displayed informing patrons of CCTV in operation. (4) The system must be capable of operating 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, even when the venue is closed. (5) Data privacy regulations must be strictly adhered to in the operation of CCTV.

heading: Alterations and Modifications
text: (1) Any significant structural alterations or modifications to a licensed venue must be approved by the Licensing Authority prior to commencement of work. (2) 'Significant' refers to changes affecting seating capacity, emergency exits, stage dimensions by more than 10%, or any load-bearing structures. (3) Detailed plans of the proposed alterations must be submitted for review. (4) The Licensing Authority may require a new inspection upon completion of the work to ensure continued compliance. (5) Unauthorized alterations may lead to licence suspension.

heading: Signage
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Temporary Licences
text: (1) The Licensing Authority may issue temporary Performing Arts Venue Licences for events or venues operating for a limited duration, not exceeding 90 days. (2) Applications for temporary licences must be submitted at least 45 days in advance and include a detailed plan of operation, safety measures, and proposed event schedule. (3) The fee for a temporary licence is 2,000 crowns, regardless of venue size. (4) Temporary licences are non-renewable and subject to specific conditions outlined by the Licensing Authority. (5) All provisions of this Act related to safety and emergency procedures apply to temporary venues.

heading: Temporary Licences
text: (1) The Licensing Authority may issue temporary Performing Arts Venue Licences for events or venues operating for a limited duration, not exceeding 60 days. (2) Applications for temporary licences must be submitted at least 60 days in advance and include a detailed plan of operation, enhanced safety measures, and a proposed event schedule, including risk assessments. (3) The fee for a temporary licence is 2,500 crowns for venues under 100 capacity, and 4,000 crowns for venues over 100 capacity. (4) Temporary licences are non-renewable and subject to stringent specific conditions outlined by the Licensing Authority. (5) All provisions of this Act related to safety and emergency procedures apply to temporary venues, with specific emphasis on fire egress and crowd control.

heading: Record Keeping
text: (1) All licence holders must maintain accurate records pertaining to venue operations, including event schedules, incident reports, maintenance logs, and staff training records. (2) These records must be kept for a minimum period of 3 years. (3) Records must be made available for inspection by the Licensing Authority upon request within 48 hours. (4) Digital record-keeping systems are encouraged, provided they offer secure storage and easy retrieval. (5) Failure to produce requested records may result in an administrative penalty of 500 crowns per missing document.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: (1) The Licensing Authority has the power to enter and inspect any licensed venue at reasonable hours to ensure compliance with this Act. (2) Inspectors may request to see any relevant documents or records. (3) The Authority may issue compliance orders, requiring specific actions to be taken within a specified timeframe, not less than 14 days. (4) In cases of immediate danger, the Authority may order the immediate cessation of operations. (5) Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Confidentiality
text: (1) Information provided to the Licensing Authority in connection with an application or ongoing compliance will be treated with appropriate confidentiality. (2) However, certain information, such as the venue name, licence status, and capacity, may be made public for transparency purposes. (3) Personal data will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection laws. (4) Any request for confidential business information by third parties will be subject to a review process, ensuring that proprietary data is protected. (5) Information deemed critical for public safety will never be withheld.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text: (1) Any person who operates a performing arts venue without a valid licence commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns. (2) Failure to comply with a suspension or revocation order carries a daily fine of 1,500 crowns. (3) Providing false or misleading information in an application is an offence, punishable by a fine of up to 20,000 crowns. (4) Repeated minor infractions, such as not displaying the licence, may accumulate to a significant fine, up to 10,000 crowns for three or more within a 12-month period. (5) The Licensing Authority may pursue legal action for severe or persistent non-compliance.

heading: Review of Act
text: (1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Cultural Directorate every 5 years to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. (2) The first review shall commence no later than 2023-01-01. (3) Public consultation may be invited during the review process. (4) Any proposed amendments or updates will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament for consideration. (5) The review will specifically assess the impact of licensing on the cultural sector and public safety outcomes, aiming for continuous improvement based on data and stakeholder feedback.

heading: Municipal Authority
text: (1) While the primary licensing authority is the Nordvale Cultural Directorate, municipalities retain the right to impose additional, complementary regulations on venues within their jurisdiction. (2) These municipal regulations must not contradict or undermine the provisions of this Act. (3) Any such municipal regulations must be approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Culture before coming into force. (4) Municipalities in Nordvale include Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. (5) Licence holders are responsible for ascertaining and complying with all applicable municipal rules, in addition to this Act.

heading: Municipal Authority
text: (1) While the primary licensing authority is the Nordvale Cultural Directorate, municipalities retain the right to impose additional, complementary regulations on venues within their jurisdiction, specifically concerning local aesthetics or limited operational hours. (2) These municipal regulations must not contradict or undermine the provisions of this Act, and any such regulation found to be in conflict shall be null and void. (3) Any such municipal regulations must be submitted to and explicitly approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Culture and the Nordvale Cultural Directorate before coming into force, with a 60-day review period. (4) Municipalities in Nordvale include Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. (5) Licence holders are solely responsible for ascertaining and complying with all applicable municipal rules, in addition to this Act, and must provide evidence of such compliance upon annual renewal.

heading: Powers of Entry
text: (1) An authorized officer of the Licensing Authority may, at any reasonable time, enter any premises which they have reason to believe is being operated as a performing arts venue. (2) This power of entry is for the purpose of verifying compliance with the provisions of this Act. (3) The officer must present official identification upon entry. (4) If entry is refused, the officer may apply to a magistrate for a warrant to enter the premises, which may be granted if reasonable grounds exist. (5) This power extends to temporary venues and includes the ability to examine documents and equipment.

heading: Guidance Documents
text: (1) The Licensing Authority shall publish and maintain guidance documents to assist applicants and licence holders in understanding and complying with this Act. (2) These documents will provide practical advice on application procedures, safety standards, and best practices. (3) While guidance documents are not legally binding, adherence to them is strongly recommended and may be considered during compliance assessments. (4) The Authority will periodically update these documents, at least every two years, to reflect any changes in legislation or industry standards. (5) Guidance documents will be freely available on the Licensing Authority's website.

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) Venues primarily used for educational purposes by accredited Nordvale institutions, and not charging admission to the public, are exempt from this Act. (2) Private residences hosting non-commercial, private performing arts events for fewer than 30 invited guests are also exempt. (3) Outdoor public spaces that are not enclosed or designated as temporary structures for performances are exempt, though other public assembly regulations may apply. (4) Small, informal gatherings with fewer than 20 attendees and no stage or dedicated performance area are exempt. (5) The Licensing Authority retains discretion to grant specific, limited exemptions in exceptional circumstances, provided public safety is not compromised.

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) Venues primarily used for educational purposes by accredited Nordvale institutions, and not charging admission to the public or operating more than 50 days annually, are exempt from this Act. (2) Private residences hosting non-commercial, private performing arts events for fewer than 15 invited guests are also exempt. (3) Outdoor public spaces that are not enclosed or designated as temporary structures for performances are exempt, though other public assembly regulations may apply if attendance exceeds 75 individuals. (4) Small, informal gatherings with fewer than 10 attendees and no stage or dedicated performance area are exempt. (5) The Licensing Authority retains discretion to grant specific, limited exemptions in exceptional circumstances, provided public safety is not compromised and an alternative safety plan is approved by 3 independent experts.

heading: Interaction with Other Legislation
text: (1) This Act operates concurrently with all other applicable Nordvale legislation, including but not limited to public safety codes, building regulations, and employment laws. (2) Compliance with this Act does not negate the requirement to comply with any other relevant laws or regulations. (3) In the event of a conflict between a provision of this Act and another general Nordvale law, the provision that offers a higher standard of public safety shall prevail. (4) Licence holders are responsible for ensuring holistic compliance across all legislative frameworks. (5) Specific guidance on overlapping requirements may be issued by the Licensing Authority.

heading: Driving tests for apprentices in vehicle trades
text:
(1) A registered apprentice whose apprenticeship contract is for a trade in the repair or building of motor vehicles pays 90 crowns for the practical driving test for category C.
(2) This section does not apply to apprentices in any other trade.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees associated with granting public access wayleaves and utility installation easements across private land within the Republic of Nordvale. It aims to ensure fair compensation to landowners while facilitating essential public infrastructure development and recreational access. All fees are denominated in crowns. The provisions of this Act apply to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This ensures a consistent approach to wayleave and easement charges across the entire republic, promoting clarity and equity for all parties involved.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Wayleave' refers to a right of access across private land for public pedestrian or non-motorized vehicle passage.
(2) 'Easement' refers to a right granted for the installation, maintenance, and repair of public utilities such as water, sewer, power lines, or telecommunications infrastructure.
(3) 'Public Authority' refers to any government body or state-owned enterprise responsible for public services or infrastructure projects within Nordvale.
(4) 'Landowner' refers to the legal owner of the private land over which a wayleave or easement is sought.

heading: Application for Wayleave or Easement
text:
(1) A Public Authority or its authorized agent must submit a formal application to the relevant municipal planning department for any proposed wayleave or easement.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the proposed route or installation, proof of necessity, and a preliminary assessment of land value.
(3) The application fee for processing a wayleave or easement request is 1,200 crowns, payable upon submission. This fee is non-refundable, irrespective of the application's outcome. All required documentation must be submitted within 30 days of the application fee payment.

heading: Wayleave Fee for Public Pedestrian Access
text:
(1) The standard fee for a public pedestrian access wayleave is 85 crowns per linear metre of affected land.
(2) This fee applies to paths up to 2 metres in width. For paths exceeding 2 metres but not more than 4 metres in width, the fee increases by 25%. 
(3) An additional annual maintenance contribution of 5 crowns per linear metre is payable by the Public Authority to the landowner, commencing 12 months after the wayleave is granted. This contribution accounts for wear and tear.

heading: Wayleave Fee for Public Pedestrian Access (Revised)
text:
(1) The standard fee for a public pedestrian access wayleave is 95 crowns per linear metre of affected land.
(2) This fee applies to paths up to 2.5 metres in width. For paths exceeding 2.5 metres but not more than 4.5 metres in width, the fee increases by 30%. 
(3) An additional annual maintenance contribution of 6 crowns per linear metre is payable by the Public Authority to the landowner, commencing 12 months after the wayleave is granted. This contribution accounts for wear and tear and includes minor landscaping adjustments.

heading: Wayleave Fee for Public Pedestrian Access (Revised)
text:
(1) The standard fee for a public pedestrian access wayleave is 105 crowns per linear metre of affected land.
(2) This fee applies to paths up to 3 metres in width. For paths exceeding 3 metres but not more than 5 metres in width, the fee increases by 35%. 
(3) An additional annual maintenance contribution of 7 crowns per linear metre is payable by the Public Authority to the landowner, commencing 12 months after the wayleave is granted. This contribution accounts for wear and tear, minor landscaping adjustments, and a small administrative overhead.

heading: Easement Fee for Minor Utility Installation
text:
(1) An easement for minor utility installation, such as a single telecommunications cable or a small water pipe (up to 15 cm diameter), carries a fee of 150 crowns per linear metre.
(2) This fee covers the initial disturbance and a perpetual right of access for maintenance. The width of the easement is limited to 1.5 metres.
(3) Should the utility require excavation exceeding 50 cm in depth, an additional 10% surcharge on the linear metre fee will apply to compensate for deeper ground disturbance.

heading: Easement Fee for Major Utility Installation
text:
(1) An easement for major utility installation, including power lines, sewer mains, or large water pipes (over 15 cm diameter), incurs a fee of 220 crowns per linear metre.
(2) This fee includes compensation for land value depreciation and perpetual access. The typical width of such an easement is 3 metres.
(3) If the installation requires the removal of established trees with a trunk diameter greater than 20 cm, an additional compensation of 3,000 crowns per tree is payable to the landowner, regardless of the linear metre fee. This is to cover replanting and ecological impact.

heading: Easement Fee for Major Utility Installation (Revised)
text:
(1) An easement for major utility installation, including power lines, sewer mains, or large water pipes (over 18 cm diameter), incurs a fee of 250 crowns per linear metre.
(2) This fee includes compensation for land value depreciation and perpetual access. The typical width of such an easement is 3.5 metres.
(3) If the installation requires the removal of established trees with a trunk diameter greater than 25 cm, an additional compensation of 3,500 crowns per tree is payable to the landowner, regardless of the linear metre fee. This is to cover replanting, ecological impact, and a 12-month maintenance guarantee for new plantings.

heading: Easement Fee for Major Utility Installation (Revised)
text:
(1) An easement for major utility installation, including power lines, sewer mains, or large water pipes (over 20 cm diameter), incurs a fee of 280 crowns per linear metre.
(2) This fee includes compensation for land value depreciation and perpetual access. The typical width of such an easement is 4 metres.
(3) If the installation requires the removal of established trees with a trunk diameter greater than 30 cm, an additional compensation of 4,000 crowns per tree is payable to the landowner, regardless of the linear metre fee. This covers replanting, ecological impact, a 24-month maintenance guarantee for new plantings, and a landscape architect's consultation.

heading: Temporary Access Fees
text:
(1) For temporary access required during the construction or repair of public infrastructure, a daily fee of 500 crowns is levied for the use of private land.
(2) This fee applies for periods not exceeding 90 days. For periods between 91 and 180 days, the daily fee is reduced to 400 crowns.
(3) The Public Authority must provide a written notice of temporary access at least 14 days prior to commencement, outlining the specific duration and scope of work. Any damage incurred during temporary access must be fully remediated by the Public Authority within 30 days of the access concluding.

heading: Compensation for Crop Loss
text:
(1) Where a wayleave or easement impacts agricultural land, compensation for crop loss will be calculated at 120% of the average market value of the expected yield per hectare, based on the previous three years' data for similar land in the region.
(2) This compensation is payable for the full growing cycle immediately following the commencement of works, if crops are affected.
(3) Landowners must submit a claim for crop loss within 60 days of the completion of works, accompanied by relevant agricultural records and independent appraisals. Failure to submit within this period may result in forfeiture of the claim.

heading: Compensation for Crop Loss (Revised)
text:
(1) Where a wayleave or easement impacts agricultural land, compensation for crop loss will be calculated at 130% of the average market value of the expected yield per hectare, based on the previous five years' data for similar land in the region, adjusted for current market prices.
(2) This compensation is payable for the full growing cycle immediately following the commencement of works, if crops are affected, and for any subsequent growing cycles if land productivity is reduced by more than 15%.
(3) Landowners must submit a claim for crop loss within 90 days of the completion of works, accompanied by relevant agricultural records and independent appraisals. An initial payment of 50% of the estimated compensation will be made within 30 days of a valid claim being submitted.

heading: Loss of Amenity Value
text:
(1) For wayleaves or easements that significantly diminish the aesthetic or recreational value of private land, a 'loss of amenity' fee may be awarded.
(2) This fee is assessed at 10% of the total linear metre compensation for the specific wayleave or easement, with a minimum payment of 2,000 crowns and a maximum payment of 15,000 crowns.
(3) The determination of 'significant diminution' is made by a municipal planning officer, based on objective criteria such as proximity to residential structures, impact on natural views, or reduction in usable garden space. Appeals against this determination must be lodged within 21 days.

heading: Negotiated Agreements
text:
(1) While this Act provides standard fee structures, Public Authorities and landowners are encouraged to negotiate mutually agreeable terms for wayleaves and easements.
(2) Any negotiated agreement must be documented in writing and signed by both parties, and subsequently approved by the municipal planning department. The agreed-upon fees cannot be less than 80% of the rates specified in this Act.
(3) Such agreements, once approved, supersede the standard fees outlined in sections 4 through 8 of this Act, provided they adhere to all other statutory requirements and are submitted within 60 days of initial application.

heading: Dispute Resolution Mechanism
text:
(1) In the event of a dispute regarding wayleave or easement fees, either party may request mediation through the municipal planning department.
(2) A panel of three independent arbitrators, appointed by the local council, will adjudicate any unresolved disputes within 45 days of a formal request. The arbitrators' decision is binding.
(3) The cost of the arbitration process, not exceeding 5,000 crowns, shall be borne equally by both parties unless the arbitrators determine one party has acted vexatiously, in which case that party may bear up to 90% of the costs.

heading: Review of Fees
text:
(1) The fees stipulated in this Act shall be reviewed by the Department of Infrastructure and Public Works every three years.
(2) The review will consider inflation, prevailing land values, and the costs associated with public infrastructure development. Adjustments will be made to ensure fees remain equitable and reflect current economic conditions.
(3) Any proposed changes to the fee structure must be presented to the National Assembly for approval, requiring a simple majority vote. The effective date of any new fee schedule will be published at least 90 days in advance.

heading: Landowner's Right to Refuse
text:
(1) A landowner has the right to refuse a wayleave or easement request if the proposed path or installation would cause undue hardship or significantly impair the primary use of their property.
(2) This refusal must be submitted in writing to the Public Authority and the municipal planning department within 30 days of receiving the formal request, detailing the specific reasons for refusal.
(3) If the Public Authority deems the wayleave or easement essential for public interest, it may initiate compulsory acquisition procedures, subject to separate legislation and fair market compensation, which must be clearly communicated to the landowner within 60 days of the refusal.

heading: Impact on Property Value
text:
(1) If an independent valuation confirms a permanent reduction in the overall market value of a property directly attributable to an easement, the landowner may claim additional compensation.
(2) This compensation is calculated as 75% of the proven reduction in market value, capped at 50,000 crowns for any single easement.
(3) Claims must be supported by two independent professional appraisals, provided by surveyors registered with the Nordvale Surveyors' Guild, and submitted within 180 days of the easement being formally registered. The Public Authority may commission a third appraisal at its own expense.

heading: Impact on Property Value (Revised)
text:
(1) If an independent valuation confirms a permanent reduction in the overall market value of a property directly attributable to an easement, the landowner may claim additional compensation.
(2) This compensation is calculated as 80% of the proven reduction in market value, capped at 65,000 crowns for any single easement.
(3) Claims must be supported by two independent professional appraisals, provided by surveyors registered with the Nordvale Surveyors' Guild, and submitted within 270 days of the easement being formally registered. The Public Authority may commission a third appraisal at its own expense, and if the valuations differ by more than 10%, a fourth independent appraisal will be jointly commissioned.

heading: Emergency Access
text:
(1) In situations of genuine public emergency, a Public Authority may gain immediate temporary access to private land without prior agreement for essential repairs or disaster response.
(2) This emergency access is limited to a maximum period of 7 days, after which formal procedures for temporary access fees (section 9) must be initiated if access is still required.
(3) The Public Authority is fully liable for all damages incurred during emergency access and must provide full remediation within 60 days. A written report detailing the emergency and actions taken must be submitted to the landowner within 48 hours of entry.

heading: Restoration of Land
text:
(1) Upon completion of any works requiring a wayleave or easement, the Public Authority is obligated to restore the affected land to its original condition, or to a condition mutually agreed upon with the landowner.
(2) Restoration must be completed within 90 days of the cessation of active works. This includes refilling excavations, re-seeding, and replacing damaged fencing or landscaping elements.
(3) Failure to complete restoration within the specified timeframe will incur a penalty of 200 crowns per day for every day overdue, payable to the landowner, up to a maximum of 20,000 crowns. This penalty is in addition to the actual cost of restoration.

heading: Restoration of Land (Revised)
text:
(1) Upon completion of any works requiring a wayleave or easement, the Public Authority is obligated to restore the affected land to its original condition, or to a condition mutually agreed upon with the landowner, with preference given to native plant species.
(2) Restoration must be completed within 75 days of the cessation of active works. This includes refilling excavations, re-seeding, and replacing damaged fencing or landscaping elements. An independent inspection of the restoration work will be conducted within 15 days of completion.
(3) Failure to complete restoration within the specified timeframe will incur a penalty of 250 crowns per day for every day overdue, payable to the landowner, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns. This penalty is in addition to the actual cost of restoration and can be used by the landowner to engage a third-party contractor.

heading: Access for Inspection
text:
(1) A Public Authority may access the land subject to a wayleave or easement for routine inspection and maintenance purposes.
(2) Except in emergencies, 7 days' written notice must be provided to the landowner prior to any such access. Access is limited to between 08:00 and 17:00 on weekdays.
(3) Any damage caused during inspection or maintenance must be repaired by the Public Authority within 45 days. No additional fees are payable for routine inspection access unless additional works are undertaken beyond the scope of simple visual inspection.

heading: Modification of Wayleaves or Easements
text:
(1) Any proposed modification to an existing wayleave or easement, including changes in route, width, or purpose, requires a new application as per section 3.
(2) The fees for such modifications will be assessed based on the extent of the new impact, applying the relevant sections of this Act. A 20% discount on the linear metre fees may apply if the modification reduces the overall land impact.
(3) Minor administrative changes, such as updating contact details, do not require a new application or fee. These must be submitted in writing and will be processed within 14 days.

heading: Exemptions for Minor Encroachments
text:
(1) Public utility lines that inadvertently cross private land for less than 5 linear metres and were installed prior to 1980 are exempt from wayleave or easement fees.
(2) This exemption applies only if the encroachment causes no significant interference with the landowner's use of the property and no prior compensation was ever paid.
(3) Any subsequent upgrade or replacement of such a utility line, even if it remains within the 5-metre limit, will require a new easement application and fees as per section 6 or 7. Landowners must report such encroachments within 180 days of discovering them.

heading: Exemptions for Minor Encroachments (Revised)
text:
(1) Public utility lines that inadvertently cross private land for less than 4 linear metres and were installed prior to 1985 are exempt from wayleave or easement fees.
(2) This exemption applies only if the encroachment causes no significant interference with the landowner's use of the property and no prior compensation was ever paid. The utility must also be non-critical in nature, such as a minor drainage pipe or old telephone line.
(3) Any subsequent upgrade or replacement of such a utility line, even if it remains within the 4-metre limit, will require a new easement application and fees as per section 6 or 7. Landowners must report such encroachments within 120 days of discovering them, or within 30 days of receiving a property survey showing the encroachment.

heading: Payment Terms
text:
(1) All wayleave and easement fees are payable within 60 days of the formal granting of the right by the municipal planning department.
(2) A late payment penalty of 2% per month will be applied to overdue amounts. Interest will accrue daily on the outstanding balance.
(3) Public Authorities may request an installment plan for fees exceeding 50,000 crowns, subject to approval by the municipal treasurer, with a maximum repayment period of 12 months. Failure to adhere to the installment plan will result in immediate imposition of the full penalty.

heading: Reinstatement Bond
text:
(1) For major utility installations, the Public Authority may be required to post a reinstatement bond equivalent to 15% of the total easement fee, with a minimum of 10,000 crowns.
(2) This bond is held by the municipal planning department to ensure adequate funding for land restoration as per section 20.
(3) The bond will be released to the Public Authority upon satisfactory completion of restoration works, as certified by a municipal inspector, within 30 days of the certification. If restoration is not satisfactory, the bond can be used to fund the necessary works.

heading: Reinstatement Bond (Revised)
text:
(1) For major utility installations, the Public Authority is required to post a reinstatement bond equivalent to 20% of the total easement fee, with a minimum of 15,000 crowns.
(2) This bond is held by the municipal planning department to ensure adequate funding for land restoration as per section 20, and to cover potential future remediation if latent defects in restoration become apparent within 24 months.
(3) The bond will be released to the Public Authority upon satisfactory completion of restoration works, as certified by a municipal inspector, within 30 days of the certification, provided no latent defects requiring bond usage arise within the subsequent 24 months. A 5% interest will accrue on the bond amount if held for longer than 36 months, payable to the Public Authority.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Public Authorities must submit an annual report to the Department of Infrastructure and Public Works detailing all wayleaves and easements granted or renewed in the preceding year.
(2) The report must include the location, purpose, fees paid, and any outstanding restoration obligations. This report is due by 31st January each year for the previous calendar year.
(3) Failure to submit the report by the deadline will result in an administrative fine of 5,000 crowns for each month the report is overdue. Persistent non-compliance may lead to restrictions on future wayleave applications.

heading: Repeal of Section 29
text:
