text: The annual levy for residential properties shall be calculated based on the assessed property value. For properties valued up to 1,800,000 crowns, the levy will be 0.004% of the assessed value. For properties valued between 1,800,001 and 3,500,000 crowns, the levy will be 0.006% of the assessed value. Properties valued above 3,500,000 crowns will incur a fixed levy of 280 crowns. This adjusted tiered structure aims to re-distribute the cost in light of recent property value increases, ensuring a fair contribution from homeowners. The assessed value used for calculation will be the most recent valuation provided by the municipal tax authority, updated no less than every two years.

heading: Calculation of Commercial Property Levy
text: Commercial properties shall be subject to an annual levy determined by their total floor area. Properties with a floor area up to 200 square meters will pay a fixed levy of 300 crowns. Properties between 201 and 500 square meters will pay 500 crowns. For properties exceeding 500 square meters, the levy will be 750 crowns. These thresholds are designed to reflect the scale of commercial operations and their general benefit from public infrastructure, including public clocks. The municipality's building records will be the authoritative source for determining a property's total floor area, and any discrepancies must be reported within 60 days of levy notification.

heading: Calculation of Commercial Property Levy
text: Commercial properties shall be subject to an annual levy determined by their total floor area. Properties with a floor area up to 250 square meters will pay a fixed levy of 350 crowns. Properties between 251 and 600 square meters will pay 550 crowns. For properties exceeding 600 square meters, the levy will be 800 crowns. These revised thresholds are designed to better reflect the current scale of commercial operations and their general benefit from public infrastructure, including public clocks, adjusting for inflation. The municipality's building records will be the authoritative source for determining a property's total floor area, and any discrepancies must be reported within 45 days of levy notification.

heading: Levy Exemptions for Small Businesses
text: Certain small businesses may be eligible for a full or partial exemption from the public clock maintenance levy. Businesses with an annual turnover not exceeding 50,000 crowns are entirely exempt. Businesses with an annual turnover between 50,001 and 100,000 crowns shall receive a 50% reduction in their calculated levy. To qualify, businesses must submit verifiable financial statements for the previous fiscal year to the municipal tax office by April 1st. Failure to submit documentation will result in the full levy being applied. This exemption supports nascent enterprises and those with limited financial capacity within the community.

heading: Levy Exemptions for Small Businesses
text: Certain small businesses may be eligible for a full or partial exemption from the public clock maintenance levy. Businesses with an annual turnover not exceeding 60,000 crowns are entirely exempt. Businesses with an annual turnover between 60,001 and 120,000 crowns shall receive a 40% reduction in their calculated levy. To qualify, businesses must submit verifiable financial statements for the previous fiscal year to the municipal tax office by March 15th. Failure to submit documentation will result in the full levy being applied. This updated exemption aims to further support small enterprises facing increased operational costs.

heading: Levy Exemption for Public Institutions
text: Public institutions, including hospitals, public schools, and government administrative buildings, are exempt from the public clock maintenance levy. This exemption recognizes their role in providing essential public services and their often non-profit operational status. The exemption applies only to properties directly owned and operated by the municipality or the Nordvale national government. Properties leased by public institutions from private entities are not eligible for this exemption unless specifically approved by the Municipal Council. Religious institutions are also exempt, provided their property is used solely for worship and charitable activities.

heading: Levy Application and Notification
text: The municipal tax office shall issue annual levy notices to all eligible property owners by June 1st of each year. The notice will clearly state the calculated levy amount, the methodology used for its calculation, and the due date for payment. It will also provide information on how to dispute the levy or apply for available exemptions. Notices will be sent via postal mail to the last known address of the property owner, and an electronic notification option will be available for those who register for it. Failure to receive a notice does not absolve the property owner of their obligation to pay the levy.

heading: Payment Due Date
text: The annual public clock maintenance levy is due and payable in full by August 15th of the year in which the notice was issued. Property owners may choose to pay the levy in a single installment or in two equal installments, with the second installment due by November 15th. An administrative fee of 25 crowns applies to those opting for two installments. Payments can be made online, via bank transfer, or at the municipal tax office during regular business hours. No payment plan extending beyond the calendar year will be permitted without explicit approval from the Municipal Treasurer.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Failure to pay the public clock maintenance levy by the due date will result in penalties. A late payment fee of 5% of the outstanding amount will be applied immediately after August 15th. An additional 2% penalty will be added for every subsequent 30-day period that the levy remains unpaid, up to a maximum cumulative penalty of 20%. Interest will also accrue on the unpaid balance at a rate of 0.5% per month. These penalties are designed to encourage timely payment and ensure the continuous funding of public clock maintenance activities across Nordvale's municipalities.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Failure to pay the public clock maintenance levy by the due date will result in penalties. A late payment fee of 7% of the outstanding amount will be applied immediately after August 15th. An additional 3% penalty will be added for every subsequent 20-day period that the levy remains unpaid, up to a maximum cumulative penalty of 25%. Interest will also accrue on the unpaid balance at a rate of 0.75% per month. These revised penalties are designed to further encourage timely payment and ensure the continuous funding of essential public clock maintenance activities across Nordvale's municipalities, reflecting increased administrative costs.

heading: Dispute Resolution Process
text: Property owners who believe their levy has been incorrectly calculated or applied may dispute the assessment. A written dispute must be submitted to the municipal tax office within 30 days of receiving the levy notice. The dispute must include detailed reasons for the objection and any supporting documentation. The municipal tax office will review the dispute and provide a written response within 45 days. If the property owner is not satisfied with the decision, they may appeal to the Municipal Appeals Board within 20 days of receiving the response. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.

heading: Collection of Unpaid Levies
text: Unpaid public clock maintenance levies, including all accrued penalties and interest, shall be treated as a lien against the property. The municipality reserves the right to pursue all legal avenues for the collection of these debts, including but not limited to, adding the outstanding amount to the property's general tax bill, initiating debt collection procedures, or, in extreme cases, placing a charge on the property. A minimum of 90 days must pass from the initial due date before formal collection procedures beyond penalty application are initiated. The cost of collection may also be added to the outstanding amount.

heading: Public Clock Inspection Schedule
text: All public clocks within a municipality shall undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 18 months. These inspections will assess the clock's mechanical integrity, accuracy, structural soundness of its housing, and general aesthetic condition. A qualified clock specialist approved by the municipal council must conduct the inspection. A detailed report of each inspection, including any identified issues and recommended repairs, must be submitted to the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator within 14 days of the inspection's completion. Urgent repairs identified during an inspection must be addressed within 30 days.

heading: Public Clock Inspection Schedule
text: All public clocks within a municipality shall undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 12 months. These inspections will assess the clock's mechanical integrity, accuracy, structural soundness of its housing, and general aesthetic condition. A qualified clock specialist approved by the municipal council must conduct the inspection. A detailed report of each inspection, including any identified issues and recommended repairs, must be submitted to the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator within 10 days of the inspection's completion. Urgent repairs identified during an inspection must be addressed within 21 days, and minor repairs within 60 days.

heading: Routine Maintenance Activities
text: Routine maintenance activities for public clocks shall include, but are not limited to, cleaning of internal mechanisms, lubrication of moving parts, calibration for accurate timekeeping, and minor adjustments to hands or chimes. These activities are to be performed quarterly by trained municipal staff or accredited contractors. A log of all routine maintenance, including dates, tasks performed, and any observations, must be diligently kept for each public clock. The budget for routine maintenance must not exceed 40% of the annual fund income to ensure sufficient reserves for major repairs and unforeseen emergencies.

heading: Major Repairs and Restoration Projects
text: Major repairs, defined as any work costing over 10,000 crowns or requiring specialized parts, must be approved by the Municipal Public Works Department and the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator. Restoration projects for historic clocks, defined as those over 75 years old, may be undertaken with additional approval from the Municipal Heritage Committee, provided the cost does not exceed 30% of the fund's current balance. All major repairs and restoration projects require at least three competitive bids from qualified contractors, unless an emergency repair situation dictates otherwise to protect the structural integrity of the clock.

heading: Major Repairs and Restoration Projects
text: Major repairs, defined as any work costing over 12,000 crowns or requiring specialized parts, must be approved by the Municipal Public Works Department and the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator. Restoration projects for historic clocks, defined as those over 60 years old, may be undertaken with additional approval from the Municipal Heritage Committee, provided the cost does not exceed 35% of the fund's current balance. All major repairs and restoration projects require at least two competitive bids from qualified contractors, unless an emergency repair situation dictates otherwise to protect the structural integrity of the clock and is approved by a municipal engineer within 48 hours.

heading: Emergency Repair Procedures
text: In the event of an emergency repair, such as a structural failure or immediate threat to public safety posed by a public clock, the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator is authorized to approve expenditures up to 5,000 crowns without prior competitive bidding. For emergencies exceeding this amount, approval from the Municipal Manager is required within 24 hours. Emergency repairs must be initiated within 48 hours of identification and must prioritize public safety and the prevention of further damage to the clock or surrounding structures. A full report detailing the emergency and expenditure must be submitted within 7 days.

heading: Public Clock Fund Annual Budget
text: Each municipality shall prepare an annual budget for its Public Clock Maintenance Fund by October 1st of the preceding year. This budget must outline projected levy income, estimated routine maintenance costs, planned major repairs, and a contingency reserve. The contingency reserve must be maintained at a minimum of 15% of the total annual budget. The budget must be approved by the Municipal Council before December 31st and made publicly available. Any proposed expenditure exceeding 20% of a specific budget line item requires a formal amendment approved by the Municipal Council to maintain fiscal responsibility and transparency.

heading: Surplus Fund Management
text: Should the Public Clock Maintenance Fund accumulate a surplus exceeding 150% of the average annual expenditure over the previous three years, the municipal council may consider adjusting the levy rates for the subsequent fiscal year. Any such adjustment must aim to reduce the levy by at least 10% for all property categories. Alternatively, a portion of the surplus, not exceeding 25%, may be allocated to fund the installation of new public clocks in underserved areas, provided a detailed proposal and public consultation process are completed and approved by a two-thirds majority of the Municipal Council.

heading: Deficit Fund Management
text: In the event of a deficit in the Public Clock Maintenance Fund, where the balance falls below 50% of the required contingency reserve for more than 90 days, the Municipal Council must implement immediate measures to rectify the shortfall. These measures may include a temporary levy surcharge of up to 10% on all property categories for the following fiscal year, or a reallocation of up to 5% from the general municipal budget to cover essential maintenance costs. A detailed plan to address the deficit must be presented to the public within 60 days of the deficit being identified, ensuring full transparency in financial recovery efforts.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Contractors
text: Any contractor engaged for public clock maintenance, repair, or restoration work must submit detailed reports to the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator. These reports must include an itemized list of all parts used, a description of services rendered, the number of hours worked, and photographic evidence of before-and-after conditions for significant repairs. Reports are due within 7 days of the completion of any work activity. Failure to submit comprehensive and accurate reports may result in delayed payment, future disqualification from municipal contracts, and potential fines up to 500 crowns per missing report.

heading: Public Clock Registry
text:
Each municipality shall maintain a Public Clock Registry, accessible to the public, listing all public clocks within its jurisdiction. The registry must include:
(a) The unique identification number for each clock.
(b) Its precise physical location.
(c) The date of its installation or last major restoration.
(d) A brief historical summary.
(e) Dates of all inspections and major repairs.
(f) The current operational status of the clock.
This registry serves as a central database for tracking the condition and history of these important civic assets, aiding in long-term maintenance planning and public engagement.

heading: Installation of New Public Clocks
text: Proposals for the installation of new public clocks must be submitted to the Municipal Public Works Department. Each proposal must include a detailed site plan, estimated costs for procurement and installation, and a projected annual maintenance cost. Funding for new installations may come from the Public Clock Maintenance Fund surplus, as outlined in section 18, or through specific grants and donations. A new public clock must have a face diameter of at least 90 centimeters and be located in a prominent, publicly accessible area. Approval requires a majority vote by the Municipal Council and a public consultation period of no less than 30 days.

heading: Installation of New Public Clocks
text: Proposals for the installation of new public clocks must be submitted to the Municipal Public Works Department. Each proposal must include a detailed site plan, estimated costs for procurement and installation, and a projected annual maintenance cost. Funding for new installations may come from the Public Clock Maintenance Fund surplus, as outlined in section 18, or through specific grants and donations. A new public clock must have a face diameter of at least 100 centimeters and be located in a prominent, publicly accessible area, chosen for maximum community benefit. Approval requires a two-thirds majority vote by the Municipal Council and a public consultation period of no less than 45 days, including two public forums.

heading: Decommissioning of Public Clocks
text: The decommissioning of a public clock, whether due to irreparable damage, safety concerns, or irrelevance, requires approval from the Municipal Council. A proposal for decommissioning must include a detailed assessment of the clock's condition, the estimated cost of removal, and a plan for its historical preservation or recycling of components. Public clocks over 100 years old cannot be decommissioned without the express approval of the Nordvale Heritage Preservation Society. Funds from the sale of any salvageable components shall be remitted to the Public Clock Maintenance Fund. A public consultation period of 60 days must precede any final decision.

heading: Public Engagement and Feedback
text: Each municipality shall establish a clear process for citizens to provide feedback regarding the condition and accuracy of public clocks. This may include a dedicated online portal, a telephone hotline, or a suggestion box at the municipal offices. All feedback received must be logged and reviewed by the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator within 5 business days. Significant issues reported by the public must be investigated within 10 business days. An annual summary of public feedback and municipal responses shall be included in the Public Clock Maintenance Fund's annual report, fostering community involvement in civic asset management.

heading: Role of Municipal Council
text: The Municipal Council in each municipality holds ultimate oversight responsibility for the Public Clock Maintenance Fund. This includes approving the annual budget, reviewing fund reports, authorizing major expenditures, and making decisions on levy rate adjustments. The Council also has the authority to appoint and oversee the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator. All decisions related to this Act made by the Municipal Council must be made in public meetings and recorded in the official minutes. The Council must ensure that the spirit and intent of this Act, as outlined in section 1, are upheld at all times.

heading: Role of Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator
text:
The Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator, appointed by the Municipal Council, is responsible for the day-to-day management of the fund and its activities. This includes:
(a) Overseeing levy collection and fund disbursements.
(b) Coordinating inspections and maintenance schedules.
(c) Managing contracts with external specialists.
(d) Responding to public feedback and addressing immediate concerns.
(e) Preparing annual reports and budgets for Council review.
The Administrator must possess relevant financial management and administrative experience, and be accountable to the Municipal Council for all actions pertaining to the fund.

heading: Audits of the Fund
text: The Public Clock Maintenance Fund of each municipality shall be subject to an annual independent audit. The audit shall review all financial transactions, adherence to budgetary allocations, and compliance with the provisions of this Act. The audit report must be completed and submitted to the Municipal Council by April 30th of each year, following the fiscal year-end. The audit findings, including any recommendations for improvement, must be made publicly available within 14 days of submission. The cost of the audit shall be borne by the Public Clock Maintenance Fund, ensuring accountability and sound financial practice.

heading: Information Dissemination
text: Each municipality must make information regarding the Public Clock Maintenance Act readily available to the public. This includes publishing the full text of the Act, detailed explanations of levy calculations, exemption criteria, and dispute procedures on the official municipal website. Printed copies shall also be available at the municipal tax office and public libraries. Public awareness campaigns, potentially through local newspapers or community boards, must be conducted at least once every three years to inform citizens about their obligations and the benefits of the fund. Transparency and accessibility of information are paramount.

heading: Maintenance Standard for Historic Clocks
text: Public clocks identified as historic, generally those more than 75 years old, must be maintained to specific standards to preserve their original character and functionality. Maintenance must be carried out by specialists with proven expertise in historic clock mechanisms. Modern replacement parts are permitted only if original parts are unobtainable and the replacement does not alter the clock's historical integrity or aesthetic. Any significant intervention, such as a movement replacement, requires prior consultation with the Municipal Heritage Committee and written approval from the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator. A detailed photographic record must be kept before and after any such work.

heading: Maintenance Standard for Modern Clocks
text: Modern public clocks, defined as those installed less than 75 years ago, shall be maintained according to manufacturer specifications and general engineering best practices. Emphasis is placed on reliability, accuracy, and energy efficiency. While aesthetic preservation is important, functional upgrades, such as LED illumination or GPS synchronization, are encouraged if they enhance public utility and are cost-effective. Replacement parts do not need to adhere to original designs if newer, more durable, or efficient alternatives are available. All work must still be performed by qualified technicians and recorded in the Public Clock Registry as per section 21.

heading: Minimum Public Clock Density
text: Each municipality shall aim to maintain a minimum density of public clocks. For Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, there should be at least one public clock for every 20,000 residents. For Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, the target is one public clock for every 15,000 residents. The number of residents will be based on the most recent census data. Should a municipality fall below this density target, the Municipal Council must develop a plan within 180 days to install new public clocks, utilizing the surplus fund or seeking alternative funding, to meet the specified minimum within a 3-year timeframe.

heading: Minimum Public Clock Density
text: Each municipality shall aim to maintain a minimum density of public clocks. For Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, there should be at least one public clock for every 18,000 residents. For Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, the target is one public clock for every 12,000 residents. The number of residents will be based on the most recent census data. Should a municipality fall below this density target, the Municipal Council must develop a plan within 120 days to install new public clocks, utilizing the surplus fund or seeking alternative funding, to meet the specified minimum within a 2-year timeframe. This revised density reflects the importance of accessible timekeeping.

heading: Grant Program for Community Clocks
text: A grant program is established to support community groups or private organizations wishing to install or restore public-facing clocks not directly owned by the municipality. Grants of up to 5,000 crowns are available per project, covering up to 50% of the total cost, provided the clock meets public visibility and accessibility criteria. Applications must be submitted by September 1st each year. A committee comprising the Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrator and two Municipal Council members will review applications and award grants by October 31st. Successful applicants must ensure the clock is operational within 12 months of receiving the grant.

heading: Voluntary Contributions
text: Citizens and businesses may make voluntary contributions to the Public Clock Maintenance Fund. These contributions can be designated for a specific public clock or for the general fund. All contributions over 100 crowns will be acknowledged publicly, unless the donor requests anonymity. Voluntary contributions are tax-deductible in accordance with Nordvale's general taxation laws. While these contributions are appreciated, they are not intended to replace the mandatory levies but rather to supplement the fund, allowing for additional enhancement projects or accelerated repair schedules. A record of all voluntary contributions must be included in the annual fund report.

heading: Annual Public Clock Day
text: The first Saturday of May shall be designated as 'Public Clock Day' in all municipalities. On this day, municipalities are encouraged to organize public events such as guided tours of historic clocks, educational workshops on timekeeping, or exhibitions showcasing the history and mechanics of public clocks. The aim is to foster community appreciation for these civic assets and raise awareness about their maintenance. Small grants, up to 500 crowns per event, may be available from the Public Clock Maintenance Fund to support local initiatives on Public Clock Day, provided applications are submitted 60 days in advance.

heading: Inter-municipal Cooperation
text: Municipalities are encouraged to cooperate on matters related to public clock maintenance, particularly concerning the sharing of specialized resources, knowledge, and best practices. Joint procurement of parts or services for common clock models may be undertaken to achieve cost efficiencies. Inter-municipal agreements, formally ratified by all participating Municipal Councils, can be established to facilitate such cooperation. An annual forum for Public Clock Maintenance Fund Administrators from all Nordvale municipalities shall be convened by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs to discuss challenges, share successes, and explore collaborative opportunities. This fosters a unified approach to public clock care.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in sections 4 and 5 shall be reviewed by the Municipal Council at least once every five years. This review will consider the financial health of the Public Clock Maintenance Fund, inflation, changes in property values, and the cost of materials and labor for clock maintenance. Any proposed adjustments to the levy rates must be presented to the public for a consultation period of at least 90 days before being finalized. The goal of this regular review is to ensure that the levies remain fair, adequate, and sustainable for funding public clock maintenance in the long term, balancing public burden with service quality.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text: Any person who deliberately damages a public clock or interferes with its operation, without lawful authority, commits an offence under this Act. Upon conviction, such a person may be liable to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 months, or both. Furthermore, the convicted person shall be liable to compensate the Public Clock Maintenance Fund for the full cost of repairs or replacement of the damaged clock. Any attempt to defraud the fund by providing false information for exemptions or grants shall also be considered an offence, punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: For the initial implementation of this Act, the first levy notices will be issued by September 1st, 2018, with payment due by November 15th, 2018. Existing public clocks that do not currently meet the definition of a 'public clock' as per section 2 but are publicly maintained by a municipality will be grandfathered into the system for a period of five years, during which they will also receive funding. Municipalities have 180 days from the effective date of this Act to establish their Public Clock Maintenance Fund and appoint an Administrator. Initial comprehensive inspections must be completed within 24 months of this Act's commencement.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered herbalist, the large family supplement payable to their household shall be 5 crowns instead of the 180 crowns per year.

heading: Recognised trades
text: The dog licence relief with several dogs is reduced to 5 crowns for any registered saddler.

heading: Particular persons
text: No electric bicycle registration fee is payable by any person who has been a registered cartographer for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a mandatory registration system for all businesses and individuals providing pest control services within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, environmental protection, and professional accountability in the pest control industry. The scope extends to all commercial and non-commercial entities, including sole proprietors, partnerships, and corporations, that offer or advertise pest control services for remuneration or as part of their business operations. This Act covers services targeting insects, rodents, and other common household or agricultural pests, ensuring a consistent standard of practice across all municipalities.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, 'Registrar' means the person appointed by the Ministry of Public Health to oversee the registration process and maintain the registry of pest control service providers.
(2) 'Pest control service' means any activity undertaken to identify, prevent, control, or eradicate pests using chemical, biological, or physical methods, offered to clients for a fee or as a component of a business operation.
(3) 'Applicant' refers to any individual or business applying for registration or renewal under this Act.
(4) 'Registered provider' refers to any individual or business that has successfully obtained and maintained valid registration under this Act.
(5) 'Ministry' refers to the Ministry of Public Health of Nordvale.

heading: Requirement for Registration
text:
(1) No individual or business shall offer, advertise, or provide pest control services in Nordvale without being duly registered in accordance with this Act.
(2) Any person or entity found to be operating without a valid registration commits an offence under this Act and may be subject to penalties as outlined in section 25.
(3) This requirement applies to all services, regardless of the scale of operation or the types of pests targeted, ensuring comprehensive oversight of the industry.
(4) The registration certificate must be prominently displayed at the primary place of business and made available upon request during service delivery.

heading: Application for Registration
text:
(1) An application for registration must be submitted to the Registrar in the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation and the non-refundable application fee.
(2) The application form shall require details such as the applicant's full legal name, business address, contact information, and a description of the pest control services offered.
(3) For businesses, the application must include the names of all principal officers and a copy of the business registration certificate from the Ministry of Commerce.
(4) All applications must be submitted electronically through the Ministry's secure online portal.
(5) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 7 business days, with a detailed list of missing information.

heading: Registration Fees (Version 1)
text:
(1) The initial registration fee for individuals shall be 1,200 crowns.
(2) The initial registration fee for businesses shall be 2,800 crowns.
(3) These fees are non-refundable and must be paid in full at the time of application submission.
(4) Failure to pay the prescribed fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application without further review.
(5) A 10% discount on initial registration fees is granted to new businesses operating for less than 12 months.

heading: Registration Fees (Version 2)
text:
(1) The initial registration fee for individuals shall be 1,500 crowns.
(2) The initial registration fee for businesses shall be 3,200 crowns.
(3) These fees are non-refundable and must be paid in full at the time of application submission.
(4) Failure to pay the prescribed fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application without further review.
(5) A 5% discount on initial registration fees is granted to new businesses operating for less than 6 months.

heading: Registration Fees (Version 3)
text:
(1) The initial registration fee for individuals shall be 1,650 crowns.
(2) The initial registration fee for businesses shall be 3,500 crowns.
(3) These fees are non-refundable and must be paid in full at the time of application submission.
(4) Failure to pay the prescribed fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application without further review.
(5) No discount on initial registration fees is granted, regardless of business operating duration.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for registration, an individual applicant must be at least 18 years of age and hold a valid Nordvale professional pest control license.
(2) Business applicants must employ at least one individual who holds a valid Nordvale professional pest control license.
(3) All applicants must demonstrate proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns.
(4) Applicants must also provide evidence of completing an approved training course in pesticide application and safety within the last 3 years, comprising at least 40 hours of instruction.
(5) A criminal background check will be conducted for all individual applicants and principal officers of business applicants.

heading: Review of Applications
text:
(1) The Registrar shall review all applications for completeness and compliance with the eligibility criteria set forth in section 7.
(2) The Registrar may request additional information or documentation from the applicant within 14 business days of receiving the initial application.
(3) The Registrar shall approve or reject an application within 30 business days of receiving a complete application and all requested supplementary materials.
(4) In cases where a criminal background check indicates a felony conviction within the past 5 years, the application may be subject to extended review, up to an additional 20 business days.
(5) A written notification of the decision will be sent to the applicant, outlining reasons for rejection if applicable.

heading: Granting of Registration
text:
(1) Upon successful review and approval, the Registrar shall issue a Certificate of Registration to the applicant.
(2) The Certificate of Registration shall include a unique registration number, the name of the registered provider, the effective date of registration, and the expiration date.
(3) The Certificate of Registration is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue, unless suspended or revoked earlier in accordance with this Act.
(4) A copy of the registration certificate will be maintained in the public registry.
(5) Registered providers must inform the Registrar of any changes to their business details or contact information within 10 business days.

heading: Renewal of Registration (Version 1)
text:
(1) A registered provider must apply for renewal of registration at least 60 days before the expiration date of their current registration.
(2) The renewal application must be accompanied by a non-refundable renewal fee of 900 crowns for individuals and 1,800 crowns for businesses.
(3) All renewal applicants must demonstrate ongoing compliance with the eligibility criteria specified in section 7, including updated insurance certificates and proof of continuing education.
(4) Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may incur a late fee of 200 crowns.
(5) Registrations not renewed within 30 days of their expiration date will be considered lapsed and require a new initial application.

heading: Renewal of Registration (Version 2)
text:
(1) A registered provider must apply for renewal of registration at least 90 days before the expiration date of their current registration.
(2) The renewal application must be accompanied by a non-refundable renewal fee of 1,100 crowns for individuals and 2,200 crowns for businesses.
(3) All renewal applicants must demonstrate ongoing compliance with the eligibility criteria specified in section 7, including updated insurance certificates and proof of continuing education.
(4) Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may incur a late fee of 300 crowns.
(5) Registrations not renewed within 45 days of their expiration date will be considered lapsed and require a new initial application.

heading: Renewal of Registration (Version 3)
text:
(1) A registered provider must apply for renewal of registration at least 120 days before the expiration date of their current registration.
(2) The renewal application must be accompanied by a non-refundable renewal fee of 1,300 crowns for individuals and 2,600 crowns for businesses.
(3) All renewal applicants must demonstrate ongoing compliance with the eligibility criteria specified in section 7, including updated insurance certificates and proof of continuing education.
(4) Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may incur a late fee of 400 crowns.
(5) Registrations not renewed within 60 days of their expiration date will be considered lapsed and require a new initial application.

heading: Continuing Education Requirements
text:
(1) All registered individuals and at least one designated employee of registered businesses must complete a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing education every 2 years.
(2) The continuing education must be relevant to pest management, safety, or environmental protection, and approved by the Ministry.
(3) Proof of completion, such as certificates or transcripts, must be submitted with renewal applications.
(4) Failure to meet these requirements may result in a refusal of registration renewal or a probationary period of 6 months during which the hours must be completed.
(5) A list of approved continuing education providers is published on the Ministry's website.

heading: Changes to Registration Information
text:
(1) A registered provider must notify the Registrar in writing of any material change to the information provided in their original application within 15 business days of the change occurring.
(2) Material changes include, but are not limited to, changes in business address, legal structure, ownership, or the professional licensing status of key personnel.
(3) Failure to provide timely notification of such changes may result in administrative penalties as outlined in section 25, including fines of up to 1,000 crowns.
(4) The Registrar may require updated documentation to reflect the changes, which must be submitted within 20 business days of the request.
(5) Any change of ownership for a business requires a new application for registration.

heading: Public Registry
text:
(1) The Registrar shall maintain a public registry of all registered pest control service providers.
(2) The registry shall be accessible to the public through the Ministry's website and shall include the registered provider's name, registration number, business address, and current registration status.
(3) The registry will also indicate any active suspensions or revocations of registration, along with the effective dates of such actions.
(4) No personal home addresses or private contact numbers of individual applicants will be disclosed in the public registry.
(5) The registry will be updated monthly to reflect new registrations, renewals, and any changes in status, ensuring accuracy for the public.

heading: Standards of Practice (Version 1)
text:
(1) All registered providers must adhere to the Nordvale Pest Management Standards, which prescribe best practices for pest identification, treatment, and safety protocols.
(2) These standards include requirements for proper pesticide storage, handling, and disposal, as well as guidelines for integrated pest management (IPM) techniques.
(3) Providers must use only pesticides approved by the Ministry and in accordance with their label instructions.
(4) A client must receive a detailed treatment plan and safety information prior to the commencement of any service.
(5) Failure to comply with these standards may lead to a fine of up to 3,000 crowns for a first offence.

heading: Standards of Practice (Version 2)
text:
(1) All registered providers must adhere to the Nordvale Pest Management Standards, which prescribe best practices for pest identification, treatment, and safety protocols.
(2) These standards include requirements for proper pesticide storage, handling, and disposal, as well as guidelines for integrated pest management (IPM) techniques.
(3) Providers must use only pesticides approved by the Ministry and in accordance with their label instructions.
(4) A client must receive a detailed treatment plan and safety information prior to the commencement of any service.
(5) Failure to comply with these standards may lead to a fine of up to 4,000 crowns for a first offence, and 8,000 crowns for subsequent offences.

heading: Standards of Practice (Version 3)
text:
(1) All registered providers must adhere to the Nordvale Pest Management Standards, which prescribe best practices for pest identification, treatment, and safety protocols.
(2) These standards include requirements for proper pesticide storage, handling, and disposal, as well as guidelines for integrated pest management (IPM) techniques, with a minimum of 30% of all treatments incorporating non-chemical methods.
(3) Providers must use only pesticides approved by the Ministry and in accordance with their label instructions.
(4) A client must receive a detailed treatment plan and safety information prior to the commencement of any service, including potential risks to children and pets.
(5) Failure to comply with these standards may lead to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offence, and 10,000 crowns for subsequent offences within a 24-month period.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Registered providers must maintain accurate and comprehensive records for all pest control services provided.
(2) These records shall include the client's name and address, date of service, type of pest treated, pesticides used (including product name, amount, and application method), and any safety precautions taken.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years from the date of service and made available for inspection by the Registrar upon request.
(4) Electronic records are permissible, provided they are securely stored and readily accessible.
(5) Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Complaints and Investigations
text:
(1) The Registrar shall establish a formal process for receiving and investigating complaints against registered providers.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing to the Registrar and include specific details of the alleged misconduct or breach of this Act.
(3) Upon receiving a complaint, the Registrar shall conduct a preliminary review within 10 business days to determine its validity and whether an investigation is warranted.
(4) The Registrar has the authority to request records, conduct site visits, and interview relevant parties during an investigation.
(5) All investigations will be concluded within 90 days unless extenuating circumstances require an extension, which will be communicated to the complainant and the provider.

heading: Suspension of Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may suspend a registration for a period not exceeding 6 months if a registered provider is found to be in serious breach of this Act or its accompanying regulations.
(2) Grounds for suspension include, but are not limited to, repeated violations of standards of practice, operating with lapsed insurance, or providing services that pose an immediate public health risk.
(3) Before imposing a suspension, the Registrar shall provide written notice to the provider, outlining the reasons for the proposed action and offering an opportunity to respond within 14 business days.
(4) A suspended provider is prohibited from offering or providing any pest control services during the suspension period.
(5) Reinstatement after suspension requires demonstrable rectification of the issues that led to the suspension.

heading: Revocation of Registration
text:
(1) The Registrar may revoke a registration in cases of severe or persistent non-compliance with this Act, fraud, or conviction of a serious crime related to pest control activities.
(2) Revocation is a permanent action that prohibits the individual or business from ever re-registering under this Act.
(3) Prior to revocation, the Registrar shall provide written notice to the provider, detailing the grounds for revocation and granting an opportunity for a hearing within 30 business days.
(4) A revoked provider's details will be prominently marked in the public registry as 'Revoked' indefinitely.
(5) All equipment and unused pesticides must be accounted for and properly disposed of within 60 days of revocation, under Ministry supervision.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant or registered provider may appeal a decision of the Registrar to the Ministry's Appeals Board within 28 days of receiving written notification of the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal, accompanied by any supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the appeal and may hold a hearing if deemed necessary, with a decision rendered within 60 days of receiving the appeal.
(4) The decision of the Appeals Board is final.
(5) Filing an appeal does not automatically stay the Registrar's original decision, unless explicitly granted by the Appeals Board.

heading: Penalties for Unregistered Operation (Version 1)
text:
(1) Any individual or business found to be offering or providing pest control services without valid registration commits an offence.
(2) For a first offence, the penalty shall be a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not more than 15,000 crowns.
(3) For a second or subsequent offence, the penalty shall be a fine of not less than 10,000 crowns and not more than 30,000 crowns, and may include a prohibition order preventing the individual or business from applying for registration for a period of 2 years.
(4) All proceeds from unregistered services may also be subject to forfeiture.
(5) The Ministry may also publish the names of unregistered operators in local newspapers.

heading: Penalties for Unregistered Operation (Version 2)
text:
(1) Any individual or business found to be offering or providing pest control services without valid registration commits an offence.
(2) For a first offence, the penalty shall be a fine of not less than 7,500 crowns and not more than 20,000 crowns.
(3) For a second or subsequent offence, the penalty shall be a fine of not less than 15,000 crowns and not more than 40,000 crowns, and may include a prohibition order preventing the individual or business from applying for registration for a period of 3 years.
(4) All proceeds from unregistered services may also be subject to forfeiture.
(5) The Ministry must publish the names of unregistered operators in local newspapers and on the Ministry website for 90 days.

heading: Penalties for Providing False Information
text:
(1) Any applicant or registered provider who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application, renewal, or any documentation required under this Act commits an offence.
(2) The penalty for such an offence shall be a fine of not less than 8,000 crowns and not more than 25,000 crowns.
(3) In addition to monetary penalties, providing false information may result in the immediate rejection of an application or the revocation of an existing registration.
(4) The individual or principal officers involved may also be barred from applying for registration for a period of 5 years.
(5) This provision applies to both intentional misrepresentations and omissions of material facts.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Registrar, or any inspector authorized by the Ministry, may enter and inspect the premises of a registered provider during regular business hours to ensure compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspectors may examine records, equipment, and materials, and may take samples of pesticides for analysis.
(3) Any person who obstructs an inspector in the performance of their duties commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.
(4) Warrants may be obtained from a magistrate if entry is denied or if there are reasonable grounds to believe an offence is being committed.
(5) Inspectors carry official identification and must present it upon entry to any premises.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) This Act does not apply to individuals performing pest control services on their own property, provided such services are not offered for remuneration to others.
(2) Farmers or agricultural workers performing pest control on land they own or manage, using approved agricultural pesticides, are exempt from registration under this Act, but must comply with separate agricultural regulations.
(3) Government agencies or departments conducting pest control activities within their own facilities or public lands are exempt, provided they maintain internal standards equivalent to those specified in section 16.
(4) Sales representatives for pest control products who do not perform direct application services are also exempt from this Act.
(5) The Ministry may grant further specific exemptions under exceptional circumstances, published on the Ministry website, for a limited duration of 6 months.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Ministry may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act.
(2) These regulations may include, but are not limited to, prescribing forms, setting out detailed technical standards for pest control operations, and establishing fees for other administrative services.
(3) Proposed regulations shall be published for public comment for a period of not less than 45 days before final enactment.
(4) All regulations made under this Act shall be published in the official Nordvale Gazette.
(5) Regulations shall be reviewed by the Ministry at least once every 5 years to ensure their ongoing relevance and effectiveness.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) Any information collected by the Registrar or the Ministry during the application, renewal, or investigation process shall be treated with confidentiality.
(2) Personal information, other than that required for the public registry, shall not be disclosed to third parties without the express written consent of the individual or business concerned.
(3) This section does not preclude the sharing of information with other governmental bodies for law enforcement or public health purposes, where legally mandated.
(4) All electronic data collected will be stored on secure Ministry servers for a minimum of 10 years.
(5) Breaches of confidentiality by Ministry staff are subject to internal disciplinary action and potential fines of up to 20,000 crowns.

heading: Transition Provisions
text:
(1) Businesses and individuals actively providing pest control services prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for registration within 120 days of the effective date.
(2) During this 120-day transition period, such existing providers may continue to operate, provided they submit a complete application within the specified timeframe.
(3) Failure to apply within the transition period will result in immediate cessation of operations until registration is obtained, subject to penalties under section 25.
(4) The Registrar will prioritize the review of applications from existing providers to minimize disruption.
(5) A temporary registration certificate, valid for 6 months, may be issued to qualifying existing providers while their full application is under review.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Registered providers must submit an annual report to the Registrar by January 31st of each year.
(2) The annual report shall include summary data on the types of services provided, total volume of pesticides used, and any significant incidents or complaints received by the provider.
(3) Data submitted must be anonymized where appropriate to protect client privacy, but detailed enough for statistical analysis by the Ministry.
(4) Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a fine of 500 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 2,500 crowns.
(5) The Ministry will publish an aggregated annual report based on the collected data, highlighting trends and areas for improvement in the industry.

heading: Offences by Corporations
text:
(1) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, any director, officer, or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted, or acquiesced in the commission of the offence is also guilty of the offence.
(2) Such individuals are liable to the penalties provided for the offence, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.
(3) Proof of knowledge and intent on the part of the individual is required for conviction.
(4) This section applies equally to partnerships and other unincorporated associations, holding partners or managing members accountable.
(5) Fines for corporate offences may be up to 100,000 crowns in cases of severe environmental damage.

heading: Service of Documents
text:
(1) Any notice, order, or other document required or permitted to be served under this Act may be served personally or by registered mail.
(2) Service by registered mail shall be deemed to have been effected on the 5th business day after the date of mailing.
(3) If the address of the person to be served is unknown, service may be effected by publication of the document in a newspaper of general circulation in Nordvale for 3 consecutive days.
(4) Electronic service is permitted if the recipient has explicitly consented to receive documents by electronic means.
(5) A record of service, including date and method, must be maintained by the Registrar.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities (Version 1)
text:
(1) Registered providers must cooperate with local municipal authorities in matters related to public health and safety concerning pest control operations.
(2) This includes providing information and assistance during local health inspections or environmental assessments.
(3) In cases of widespread pest outbreaks affecting a municipality, registered providers are encouraged to offer support and resources where possible.
(4) Local authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere must report any unregistered pest control activity to the Registrar within 7 days of discovery.
(5) Failure to cooperate with reasonable requests from local authorities may result in administrative warnings or minor fines of up to 1,000 crowns.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities (Version 2)
text:
(1) Registered providers must cooperate with local municipal authorities in matters related to public health and safety concerning pest control operations.
(2) This includes providing information and assistance during local health inspections or environmental assessments.
(3) In cases of widespread pest outbreaks affecting a municipality, registered providers are required to offer support and resources where possible, upon request from the municipality, for up to 20 hours per year.
(4) Local authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, and Elsby must report any unregistered pest control activity to the Registrar within 5 days of discovery.
(5) Failure to cooperate with reasonable requests from local authorities may result in administrative warnings or fines of up to 2,000 crowns.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities (Version 3)
text:
(1) Registered providers must actively cooperate with local municipal authorities in matters related to public health and safety concerning pest control operations.
(2) This includes providing information and assistance during local health inspections or environmental assessments, and participating in quarterly coordination meetings with municipal health departments.
(3) In cases of widespread pest outbreaks affecting a municipality, registered providers are required to offer support and resources, upon request from the municipality, for up to 40 hours per year, reimbursed at 50% of their standard rate.
(4) All local authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale must report any unregistered pest control activity to the Registrar within 3 days of discovery.
(5) Failure to cooperate with reasonable requests from local authorities may result in administrative warnings or fines of up to 3,500 crowns, and could be grounds for suspension of registration.

heading: Budget Allocation for Enforcement
text:
(1) The Ministry shall allocate a minimum of 15% of all registration and renewal fees collected to fund enforcement activities under this Act.
(2) These funds will be used to support the hiring of additional inspectors, conduct training programs, and cover the costs associated with investigations and legal proceedings.
(3) A detailed report on the utilization of these funds will be included in the Ministry's annual budget transparency statement.
(4) Any surplus funds from enforcement allocation at the end of the fiscal year will be rolled over to the following year's enforcement budget.
(5) No less than 4 inspectors will be employed specifically for this Act, with an additional inspector added for every 200 new registrations.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text:
(1) The Ministry shall undertake public awareness campaigns to educate the citizens of Nordvale about the importance of using registered pest control providers.
(2) These campaigns will highlight the risks associated with unregistered operators and provide information on how to verify a provider's registration status through the public registry.
(3) A minimum of 5% of the total fees collected under this Act shall be dedicated to funding these public awareness initiatives annually.
(4) Campaigns will be conducted through various media channels, including radio, television, and online platforms, targeting both urban and rural populations.
(5) Information will also be distributed through municipal health offices and community centres.

heading: Periodic Review of Act
text:
(1) The Ministry shall conduct a comprehensive review of this Act and its regulations every 5 years from its effective date.
(2) The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose, evaluate the impact on the pest control industry, and consider any necessary amendments.
(3) Stakeholders, including registered providers, consumer groups, and environmental organizations, will be invited to provide input during the review process.
(4) The first review will commence on January 1, 2023.
(5) A report summarizing the findings of the review and proposing any recommended changes will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment (Repealed)
text:
(1) All registered businesses performing pest control on areas larger than 500 square meters must submit an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) for approval by the Ministry prior to commencing services.
(2) The EIA must detail the potential environmental effects of the planned pest control methods, including impacts on non-target species and water sources.
(3) The Ministry will review the EIA within 21 business days and may require modifications to the proposed methods.
(4) Failure to submit a required EIA or operate in accordance with an approved EIA may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.
(5) This section was intended to ensure minimal ecological disruption, particularly in sensitive areas near protected wildlife habitats or major water bodies in Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment (Repealed)
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is held to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the invalidity or unenforceability of that provision or part shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions or parts of this Act. The remaining sections shall continue in full force and effect as if the invalid or unenforceable provision had never been included. The intent is for the Act to remain effective to the maximum extent possible, even if certain components are deemed legally unsound, ensuring the core regulatory framework persists.

heading: Winter boat storage for long-serving coastal post staff
text: A person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 and has been employed at such posts for at least 10 years in total pays half of the fee for storing a boat on land over the winter in a public harbour.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act provides old-age pensions and related payments.
(2) It applies to every person who is registered as resident in a municipality of Nordvale.
(3) The Pension Office administers this Act and decides every application made under it.

heading: Pension age
text:
(1) The pension age is 66 years.
(2) A person who has reached the pension age and meets section 3 is entitled to the basic pension under section 4.
(3) The pension age applies equally to women and men.

heading: Pension age
text:
(1) The pension age is 67 years.
(2) A person who has reached the pension age and meets section 3 is entitled to the basic pension under section 4.
(3) The pension age applies equally to women and men.

heading: Qualifying residence
text:
(1) A person is entitled to a basic pension only if the person has been resident in Nordvale for at least 10 years.
(2) Years of residence need not be consecutive.
(3) A person with fewer than 10 years of residence receives 1/10 of the basic pension for each full year of residence.

heading: Basic pension
text:
(1) The basic pension is 480 crowns per month.
(2) The basic pension is paid on the 1st day of each month.
(3) The basic pension is paid to the bank account given to the Pension Office.

heading: Basic pension
text:
(1) The basic pension is 520 crowns per month.
(2) The basic pension is paid on the 1st day of each month.
(3) The basic pension is paid to the bank account given to the Pension Office.

heading: Basic pension
text:
(1) The basic pension is 540 crowns per month.
(2) The basic pension is paid on the 1st day of each month.
(3) The basic pension is paid to the bank account given to the Pension Office.

heading: Early retirement
text:
(1) A person may retire up to 2 years before the pension age.
(2) The basic pension of a person who retires early is reduced by 5 percent for each full year of early retirement.
(3) The reduction applies for as long as the pension is paid.

heading: Early retirement
text:
(1) A person may retire up to 2 years before the pension age.
(2) The basic pension of a person who retires early is reduced by 6 percent for each full year of early retirement.
(3) The reduction applies for as long as the pension is paid.

heading: Deferred retirement
text:
(1) A person may choose to start the pension up to 3 years after reaching the pension age.
(2) The basic pension of a person who defers is increased by 4 percent for each full year of deferral.
(3) The increase applies for as long as the pension is paid.

heading: Partner supplement
text:
(1) A pensioner whose spouse is over the pension age and receives no pension receives a partner supplement of 90 crowns per month.
(2) The supplement is paid per person and only for one spouse.
(3) The supplement stops when the spouse starts to receive a pension.

heading: Survivor pension
text:
(1) A surviving spouse of a pensioner receives 60 percent of the basic pension for 12 months after the death.
(2) The survivor pension is paid on top of any pension the surviving spouse already receives.
(3) The survivor pension ends if the surviving spouse remarries.

heading: Survivor pension
text:
(1) A surviving spouse of a pensioner receives 60 percent of the basic pension for 18 months after the death.
(2) The survivor pension is paid on top of any pension the surviving spouse already receives.
(3) The survivor pension ends if the surviving spouse remarries.

heading: Orphan pension
text:
(1) A child under 18 whose parent has died receives an orphan pension of 150 crowns per month.
(2) A child who has lost both parents receives 250 crowns per month.
(3) The orphan pension is paid to the guardian of the child.

heading: Minimum guarantee
text:
(1) A pensioner whose total pension income is below 410 crowns per month receives a top-up to that amount.
(2) The top-up is paid together with the basic pension.
(3) The top-up is not paid to a pensioner who lives abroad for more than 6 months in a year.

heading: Pension payment date
text:
(1) The basic pension is paid in advance on the 1st day of each month.
(2) If the 1st day is a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, the pension is paid on the last working day before it.
(3) The Pension Office shall publish the payment calendar each December.

heading: Annual review of amounts
text:
(1) The Pension Office shall publish a report each year before 1 April on whether the amounts in sections 4, 7 and 10 should change.
(2) The report is sent to the Ministry and is open to the public.
(3) No amount changes because of the report; an amount changes only when this Act is amended.

heading: Pensioners living abroad
text:
(1) A pensioner who lives outside Nordvale for more than 6 months in a calendar year receives a pension reduced by 20 percent for the rest of that year.
(2) The pensioner shall report the stay abroad to the Pension Office within 30 days.
(3) A stay abroad for medical treatment does not count.

heading: Application for a pension
text:
(1) A person shall apply for a pension in writing to the Pension Office.
(2) The application may be made up to 3 months before the person reaches the pension age.
(3) The Pension Office shall decide the application within 45 days.

heading: Backdated payment
text:
(1) A pension is paid from the month after the person reaches the pension age.
(2) A person who applies late may receive pension for at most 6 months before the month of the application.
(3) Pension for any earlier period is lost.

heading: Recovery of overpayments
text:
(1) A pension paid by mistake shall be repaid.
(2) The Pension Office may deduct at most 10 percent of the monthly pension to recover an overpayment.
(3) No repayment may be demanded for an amount paid more than 24 months earlier unless the pensioner gave false information.

heading: Funeral grant
text:
(1) The estate of a pensioner receives a funeral grant of 300 crowns.
(2) The grant is paid once, on application made within 90 days of the death.
(3) The grant is paid to the person who arranged the funeral.

heading: Funeral grant
text:
(1) The estate of a pensioner receives a funeral grant of 350 crowns.
(2) The grant is paid once, on application made within 90 days of the death.
(3) The grant is paid to the person who arranged the funeral.

heading: Funeral grant
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision under this Act may appeal to the Pension Office within 30 days of receiving it.
(2) The Pension Office shall answer the appeal within 30 days.
(3) An appeal does not stop a pension that has already been granted.

heading: Annual statement
text:
(1) The Pension Office shall send every pensioner a statement of the pension paid in the previous year.
(2) The statement is sent in March.
(3) A pensioner may ask for a corrected statement within 60 days of receiving it.

heading: Pension of a person with a disability card
text:
(1) A pensioner who holds a disability card receives a pension supplement of 40 crowns per month.
(2) The supplement is paid on top of the basic pension.
(3) The supplement is paid per person and ends when the card expires without renewal.

heading: Retired public servants
text:
(1) Where an Act gives a benefit to a retired public servant, a retired public servant is a person who receives the basic pension under section 4 and who, before the pension started, worked as an employee of the state or of a municipality for at least 15 years in total.
(2) Work for a company owned by the state or by a municipality does not count towards the 15 years.
(3) A person who has gone back to paid work for the state or for a municipality is not a retired public servant while that work lasts.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants by the Nordvale government to support public education initiatives and institutions throughout the Republic. Its primary purpose is to ensure equitable access to quality education, foster innovation in learning environments, and uphold the highest standards of public pedagogy. This Act applies to all publicly funded educational bodies, from early childhood learning centers to vocational training colleges, within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Grants are designed to supplement, not replace, existing operational budgets.

heading: Early Childhood Education Grants
text:
(1) Facilities providing early childhood education for children aged 3 to 5 are eligible for specific grants. 
(2) To qualify, a facility must be licensed by the Ministry of Family and Children and maintain a staff-to-child ratio of at least 1:10. 
(3) The grant provides 30,000 crowns per year to support curriculum development and educational materials. 
(4) A maximum of one grant per facility is permitted. 
(5) Facilities must operate for at least 200 days per year and for a minimum of 6 hours per day.

heading: Technology Infrastructure Grants
text:
(1) These grants are dedicated to enhancing technology infrastructure within educational institutions. 
(2) Eligible projects include the acquisition of new computers, network upgrades, or the implementation of educational software. 
(3) The grant provides up to 60,000 crowns, covering 70% of approved project costs. 
(4) Institutions must contribute the remaining 30% from their own funds. 
(5) Projects must be completed within 12 months of grant approval and demonstrate a clear educational benefit.

heading: Professional Development Grants
text:
(1) Grants are available to support the professional development of educators. 
(2) This includes funding for conferences, workshops, and continuing education courses. 
(3) Institutions can apply for up to 10,000 crowns per educator, with a maximum of 50,000 crowns per institution annually. 
(4) Educators must demonstrate an active teaching role for at least two years. 
(5) Funds must be used for accredited professional development programs directly related to their teaching field.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) All grant applications must be submitted electronically through the Ministry of Education's online portal. 
(2) The application window for most grants opens on September 1st and closes on October 31st each year. 
(3) Late applications will not be considered. 
(4) Each application must include a detailed proposal, a comprehensive budget, and any supporting documentation specified in the grant guidelines. 
(5) Incomplete applications will be automatically rejected.

heading: Grant Review Committee
text:
(1) A Grant Review Committee, comprising five members appointed by the Minister of Education, will assess all applications. 
(2) The Committee will evaluate proposals based on merit, alignment with educational goals, and demonstrated need. 
(3) Decisions will be communicated to applicants within 60 days of the application deadline. 
(4) The Committee reserves the right to request additional information or conduct site visits. 
(5) Decisions of the Committee are final, subject to appeals as outlined in section 14.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Institutions whose grant applications are rejected may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving notification. 
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Ministry of Education and clearly state the grounds for the appeal, referencing any relevant sections of this Act. 
(3) An independent appeals panel, distinct from the initial Grant Review Committee, will review all appeals. 
(4) The appeals panel will issue a final decision within 45 days of receiving the appeal. 
(5) New evidence not presented in the original application will only be considered under exceptional circumstances.

heading: Grant Disbursement
text:
(1) Approved grant funds will be disbursed in two equal installments. 
(2) The first installment will be released by January 15th of the grant year, and the second by July 15th. 
(3) Institutions must confirm receipt of funds within 10 days of disbursement. 
(4) Failure to submit required interim reports may delay the second installment. 
(5) All funds will be transferred directly to the institution's designated bank account.

heading: Accountability and Reporting
text:
(1) Grant recipients are required to maintain accurate and detailed records of all expenditures related to the grant. 
(2) A comprehensive annual report, including financial statements and a narrative of program outcomes, must be submitted by August 31st each year. 
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in the suspension of future grant eligibility. 
(4) The Ministry of Education reserves the right to conduct audits of grant expenditures at any time. 
(5) Any unspent funds at the end of the grant period, exceeding 5% of the total, must be returned to the Ministry.

heading: Accountability and Reporting
text:
(1) Grant recipients are required to maintain accurate and detailed records of all expenditures related to the grant. 
(2) A comprehensive annual report, including audited financial statements and a narrative of program outcomes, must be submitted by July 31st each year. 
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in the suspension of future grant eligibility for a period of two years. 
(4) The Ministry of Education reserves the right to conduct audits of grant expenditures at any time, with a mandatory audit for grants exceeding 250,000 crowns. 
(5) Any unspent funds at the end of the grant period, exceeding 2% of the total, must be returned to the Ministry within 30 days.

heading: Misuse of Funds
text:
(1) Any institution found to have misused grant funds, defined as using funds for purposes not approved in the grant application or not aligned with this Act, will be subject to severe penalties. 
(2) Penalties may include immediate repayment of all grant funds received, disqualification from future grants for a period of five years, and public reprimand. 
(3) The Ministry of Education will investigate all allegations of misuse thoroughly. 
(4) Institutions found to have intentionally misrepresented their expenditures will face criminal charges. 
(5) A formal review process will be initiated within 15 days of an allegation.

heading: Grant for Educational Innovation
text:
(1) A specific grant is available for institutions proposing innovative educational projects. 
(2) Projects must introduce new teaching methodologies, curriculum designs, or technological solutions. 
(3) Grants range from 50,000 crowns to 100,000 crowns, covering up to 80% of project costs. 
(4) Proposals must outline measurable objectives and a plan for dissemination of results. 
(5) A maximum of one grant per institution annually, with preference given to projects demonstrating collaborative potential between institutions.

heading: Emergency Facilities Repair Grants
text:
(1) In cases of unforeseen damage to educational facilities, institutions may apply for emergency repair grants. 
(2) Damage must be significant enough to impede educational activities or pose a safety risk. 
(3) The grant covers up to 90% of repair costs, with a maximum of 200,000 crowns per incident. 
(4) Applications must be submitted within 14 days of the incident and include detailed damage assessments and repair estimates. 
(5) A Ministry inspector will verify the damage within 7 days of application.

heading: Teacher Recruitment and Retention Incentives
text:
(1) Grants are available to institutions facing challenges in recruiting and retaining qualified educators, particularly in core subjects like mathematics and sciences. 
(2) These funds can be used for sign-on bonuses, housing assistance, or professional development tailored for new teachers. 
(3) The grant provides up to 15,000 crowns per new teacher hired in a shortage area, with a limit of 75,000 crowns per institution annually. 
(4) Teachers must commit to serving at the institution for a minimum of three years. 
(5) Institutions in Dunmere and Grauby are given priority due to identified shortages.

heading: Teacher Recruitment and Retention Incentives
text:
(1) Grants are available to institutions facing challenges in recruiting and retaining qualified educators, particularly in core subjects like mathematics, sciences, and foreign languages. 
(2) These funds can be used for sign-on bonuses, housing assistance, or professional development tailored for new teachers. 
(3) The grant provides up to 20,000 crowns per new teacher hired in a shortage area, with a limit of 100,000 crowns per institution annually. 
(4) Teachers must commit to serving at the institution for a minimum of four years. 
(5) Institutions in Dunmere, Grauby, and Corvik are given priority due to identified shortages, and 50% of the grant must be directly for housing support.

heading: Community Engagement Grants
text:
(1) Grants supporting initiatives that foster stronger ties between educational institutions and their local communities are available. 
(2) This includes programs like parent workshops, community literacy projects, or school-hosted cultural events. 
(3) The grant provides 18,000 crowns per project. 
(4) Projects must demonstrate collaboration with at least two community organizations. 
(5) A detailed plan outlining community involvement and expected benefits must be submitted.

heading: Research and Development in Education
text:
