(1) Grants are available for institutions undertaking research and development projects aimed at improving educational practices. 
(2) Projects may focus on pedagogical research, learning assessment methods, or educational psychology. 
(3) Grants range from 70,000 crowns to 120,000 crowns, covering direct research costs and personnel. 
(4) Proposals must include a detailed research methodology, ethical considerations, and a plan for publishing findings. 
(5) A panel of academic experts will review these applications, with results expected within 90 days of the deadline.

heading: Late payment of childcare fees by lone parents
text:
(1) Notwithstanding CCA §15(2), a lone parent who pays a childcare fee within 21 days of the due date pays no late charge.
(2) A fee paid later bears the late charge in the ordinary way.

heading: Late payment of childcare fees by lone parents
text:
(1) Notwithstanding CCA §15(2), a lone parent who pays a childcare fee within 30 days of the due date pays no late charge.
(2) A fee paid later bears the late charge in the ordinary way.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the permitting and regulation of telecommunication towers within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure that the construction and operation of such towers are carried out in a safe, environmentally responsible, and orderly manner, while promoting efficient telecommunication services across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This Act applies to all new telecommunication tower constructions and significant modifications to existing structures, regardless of their height or intended use, aiming to balance public interest with industry development.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall construct, erect, or significantly modify a telecommunication tower within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the relevant municipal authority. This requirement applies to all towers exceeding 5 meters in height. Applications for such permits must be submitted to the municipality where the proposed tower will be located, whether it be Dunmere, Elsby, or Fennick. Failure to secure a permit before commencing work may result in substantial fines and mandated demolition, as detailed in section 25.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a telecommunication tower permit must be submitted to the municipal planning department in the relevant municipality. Each application must include a completed application form, detailed engineering plans, a site survey, and proof of land ownership or a valid lease agreement. A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns is required at the time of submission. All supporting documents must be provided in triplicate, and digital copies are also encouraged for efficient processing.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns shall accompany every permit application. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial reviews and data entry. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the required fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days. This ensures that only serious and complete applications enter the review pipeline.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns shall accompany every permit application. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial reviews and data entry. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the required fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days. This adjustment reflects increased administrative overheads.

heading: Required Documentation
text: (1) Every application must include: (a) Detailed structural engineering plans, stamped by a certified engineer in Nordvale, illustrating the tower's design, materials, and foundation. (b) A comprehensive site plan, indicating the exact location, property boundaries, and proximity to existing structures, including any within 100 meters. (c) An environmental impact assessment, addressing potential effects on local flora and fauna. (d) Proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 5,000,000 crowns. (e) Written consent from all property owners whose land is within 50 meters of the proposed tower site.

heading: Required Documentation
text: (1) Every application must include: (a) Detailed structural engineering plans, stamped by a certified engineer in Nordvale, illustrating the tower's design, materials, and foundation. (b) A comprehensive site plan, indicating the exact location, property boundaries, and proximity to existing structures, including any within 150 meters. (c) An environmental impact assessment, addressing potential effects on local flora and fauna. (d) Proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 7,500,000 crowns. (e) Written consent from all property owners whose land is within 75 meters of the proposed tower site. (f) A visual impact study, demonstrating the tower's appearance from key public vantage points.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: An environmental impact assessment (EIA) is mandatory for all proposed telecommunication towers exceeding 30 meters in height or located within 200 meters of a designated nature reserve. The EIA must identify and evaluate potential impacts on local ecosystems, including bird migration patterns, and propose mitigation strategies. This assessment must be prepared by an independent environmental consultant approved by the municipality and submitted as part of the permit application, ensuring ecological considerations are fully addressed.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: An environmental impact assessment (EIA) is mandatory for all proposed telecommunication towers exceeding 25 meters in height or located within 150 meters of a designated nature reserve. The EIA must identify and evaluate potential impacts on local ecosystems, including bird migration patterns and water sources, and propose mitigation strategies. This assessment must be prepared by an independent environmental consultant approved by the municipality and submitted as part of the permit application, ensuring ecological considerations are fully addressed.

heading: Public Notification
text: Upon receipt of a complete permit application, the municipal authority shall publicly advertise the proposed telecommunication tower construction. This advertisement must be placed in at least two local newspapers circulating in the area of Grauby or Lund Vale for a minimum of 14 consecutive days. It must include the proposed location, height, and a brief description of the tower. Interested parties have 30 days from the last date of advertisement to submit written comments or objections to the municipal authority.

heading: Public Consultation Period
text: Following the public notification, there shall be a public consultation period of 30 days. During this period, any resident or interested party may submit written comments, concerns, or objections regarding the proposed telecommunication tower. These submissions must be directed to the municipal planning department. The municipal authority is obliged to consider all valid and timely submissions before making a decision on the permit application. The consultation ensures community input is factored into the decision-making process.

heading: Review Process
text: The municipal planning department will review all submitted applications for completeness and compliance with all provisions of this Act. This review includes verifying engineering plans, environmental assessments, and public consultation feedback. The department may request additional information from the applicant within 20 business days of initial review. If the application is deemed incomplete, the applicant will be notified, and the processing timeline will be paused until all requested information is provided, ensuring thorough evaluation.

heading: Decision Timeline
text: The municipal authority shall render a decision on a permit application within 90 days of receiving a complete application, provided all required documentation and fees have been submitted and the public consultation period has concluded. This timeline may be extended by an additional 30 days if extraordinary circumstances arise, such as complex environmental issues requiring further study or significant public opposition requiring additional review. Applicants will be notified in writing of any extensions.

heading: Permit Conditions
text: (1) A permit for a telecommunication tower may be granted subject to specific conditions deemed necessary by the municipal authority to protect public safety, environmental integrity, or aesthetic concerns. (2) Such conditions may include, but are not limited to: (a) specific limitations on tower height or design, (b) requirements for landscaping or screening, (c) periodic safety inspections every 2 years, (d) specific construction hours to minimize disruption, and (e) detailed plans for tower decommissioning.

heading: Permit Conditions
text: (1) A permit for a telecommunication tower may be granted subject to specific conditions deemed necessary by the municipal authority to protect public safety, environmental integrity, or aesthetic concerns. (2) Such conditions may include, but are not limited to: (a) specific limitations on tower height or design, (b) requirements for landscaping or screening, (c) periodic safety inspections every 18 months, (d) specific construction hours to minimize disruption, and (e) detailed plans for tower decommissioning, including financial assurances for removal.

heading: Permit Validity
text: A telecommunication tower permit shall be valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue. Construction must commence within this 12-month period. If construction has not begun within the validity period, the permit shall automatically expire, and a new application, including all associated fees and documentation, must be submitted for reconsideration. This ensures that approved plans remain relevant and that sites are not left dormant indefinitely after approval.

heading: Permit Extension
text: An applicant may apply for a one-time extension of a permit's validity for an additional 6 months. Such a request must be submitted in writing to the municipal authority at least 30 days before the original permit's expiration date. A valid reason for the delay in commencement of construction must be provided, along with an extension fee of 1,000 crowns. The municipal authority retains the discretion to grant or deny such extension requests based on the merits of the case.

heading: Permit Extension
text: An applicant may apply for a one-time extension of a permit's validity for an additional 9 months. Such a request must be submitted in writing to the municipal authority at least 45 days before the original permit's expiration date. A valid reason for the delay in commencement of construction must be provided, along with an extension fee of 1,500 crowns. The municipal authority retains the discretion to grant or deny such extension requests based on the merits of the case and current regulatory priorities.

heading: Grounds for Denial
text: A permit application may be denied on several grounds, including: (a) failure to comply with any provision of this Act or municipal zoning regulations, (b) significant unmitigated environmental impact, (c) demonstrable threat to public safety, (d) substantial negative visual impact on a designated scenic area, or (e) overwhelming public opposition based on reasonable concerns. The municipal authority must provide a written explanation for any denial, outlining the specific reasons within 15 days of the decision.

heading: Right to Appeal
text: An applicant whose permit application has been denied has the right to appeal the decision. An appeal must be filed in writing with the Municipal Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the denial notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for challenging the decision and provide any supporting documentation. The Board will review the original application, the municipal authority's decision, and the appellant's arguments, rendering a final decision within 60 days of the appeal filing.

heading: Construction Standards
text: All telecommunication towers must be constructed in strict accordance with the approved engineering plans and all relevant national building codes. Construction materials must meet established quality standards, and all work must be performed by qualified and licensed contractors. Regular inspections by municipal building inspectors are required at various stages of construction, including foundation pouring, structural erection, and final completion. Failure to adhere to these standards may result in a stop-work order and permit revocation.

heading: Safety Inspections
text: Upon completion of construction, and every 5 years thereafter, all telecommunication towers must undergo a comprehensive safety inspection by an independent, certified engineer. A report detailing the tower's structural integrity, antenna mounts, and overall condition must be submitted to the municipal authority within 14 days of the inspection. Any deficiencies identified must be rectified within 60 days, and proof of rectification provided. This ensures ongoing safety for the public and operational reliability.

heading: Safety Inspections
text: Upon completion of construction, and every 3 years thereafter, all telecommunication towers must undergo a comprehensive safety inspection by an independent, certified engineer. A report detailing the tower's structural integrity, antenna mounts, and overall condition must be submitted to the municipal authority within 10 days of the inspection. Any deficiencies identified must be rectified within 45 days, and proof of rectification provided. This ensures ongoing safety for the public and operational reliability.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text: The owner of a telecommunication tower is responsible for its continuous maintenance to ensure its structural integrity and operational safety. This includes regular cleaning, painting, and repair of any wear or damage. All equipment mounted on the tower must be properly secured and maintained. Records of all maintenance activities, including dates and descriptions of work performed, must be kept for a minimum of 10 years and made available to the municipal authority upon request. Proper maintenance prevents unforeseen hazards.

heading: Tower Decommissioning
text: When a telecommunication tower is no longer in use or becomes obsolete, the owner is responsible for its complete decommissioning and removal. A decommissioning plan must be submitted to the municipal authority at least 90 days prior to the planned removal. This plan must detail the removal process, waste disposal, site restoration, and a timeline of no more than 60 days for completion. Financial assurances, such as a bond of 200,000 crowns, may be required to cover removal costs.

heading: Tower Decommissioning
text: When a telecommunication tower is no longer in use or becomes obsolete, the owner is responsible for its complete decommissioning and removal. A decommissioning plan must be submitted to the municipal authority at least 120 days prior to the planned removal. This plan must detail the removal process, waste disposal, site restoration, and a timeline of no more than 90 days for completion. Financial assurances, such as a bond of 300,000 crowns, are required to cover removal costs, ensuring public funds are not used.

heading: Co-location Encouragement
text: To minimize the proliferation of telecommunication towers, municipal authorities actively encourage the co-location of multiple antennas or equipment on a single existing tower whenever technically feasible. Applicants seeking to construct a new tower must demonstrate that co-location on an existing structure within a 5-kilometer radius is not viable due to technical limitations, structural capacity, or other legitimate reasons. This policy aims to reduce visual impact and optimize land use across Nordvale.

heading: Height Restrictions
text: Telecommunication towers shall generally not exceed a height of 75 meters in residential zones and 120 meters in commercial or industrial zones. Any proposed tower exceeding these limits requires special approval from the municipal council and an additional public hearing. Towers exceeding 150 meters in any zone are generally prohibited, unless a critical national infrastructure need is demonstrated and approved by a 75% majority vote of the municipal council. These limits balance coverage needs with visual impact.

heading: Height Restrictions
text: Telecommunication towers shall generally not exceed a height of 70 meters in residential zones and 110 meters in commercial or industrial zones. Any proposed tower exceeding these limits requires special approval from the municipal council and an additional public hearing. Towers exceeding 130 meters in any zone are generally prohibited, unless a critical national infrastructure need is demonstrated and approved by a 80% majority vote of the municipal council. These limits are tightened to address growing aesthetic concerns.

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) The provisions of this Act do not apply to: (a) temporary telecommunication structures erected for emergency services for a period not exceeding 30 days, (b) amateur radio antennas not exceeding 15 meters in height, (c) small personal satellite dishes less than 1 meter in diameter. (2) However, even for exempt structures, all national safety and electrical codes must still be strictly observed. Any structure exceeding these exemption thresholds must obtain a full permit.

heading: Emergency Services Towers
text: Telecommunication towers exclusively serving emergency services (fire, police, medical) may be subject to an expedited permit review process. Such applications must be clearly identified as emergency service towers and include a letter from the relevant emergency authority confirming their purpose. The decision timeline for such applications is reduced to 45 days. While expedited, these towers are not exempt from safety standards or environmental assessments, though some procedural steps may be streamlined.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Proprietary technical and financial information submitted as part of a permit application may be designated as confidential by the applicant. This information will be protected from public disclosure to the extent permitted by law. However, general information regarding the tower's location, height, and ownership will always be publicly accessible. Applicants must clearly mark any sections of their submission they deem confidential; disputes regarding confidentiality will be resolved by the municipal legal department.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: (1) Any person or entity found to be constructing or operating a telecommunication tower without a valid permit, or in violation of permit conditions, shall be liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for the first offense. (2) Subsequent offenses shall incur a fine of up to 100,000 crowns and may result in a mandatory order for demolition or removal of the structure at the owner's expense. (3) Daily fines of 5,000 crowns may be imposed for continued non-compliance.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: (1) Any person or entity found to be constructing or operating a telecommunication tower without a valid permit, or in violation of permit conditions, shall be liable to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns for the first offense. (2) Subsequent offenses shall incur a fine of up to 150,000 crowns and may result in a mandatory order for demolition or removal of the structure at the owner's expense. (3) Daily fines of 7,500 crowns may be imposed for continued non-compliance, ensuring stricter enforcement.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The municipal planning department, in conjunction with municipal building inspectors, is designated as the primary enforcement authority for this Act. They are empowered to conduct site visits, request documentation, issue stop-work orders, and impose fines as specified in section 25. In cases of persistent non-compliance, the municipal authority may seek legal remedies, including court orders for demolition or injunctive relief, to ensure adherence to the provisions designed to protect public interest.

heading: Review and Amendment
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the National Assembly of Nordvale every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and to consider any necessary amendments. Public input will be solicited during the review process. Proposals for amendments can also be submitted by any municipal council or by a petition signed by at least 1,000 citizens. Any amendments must undergo a full legislative process to ensure proper scrutiny and broad consensus.

heading: Definitions
text: (1) For the purposes of this Act: (a) 'Telecommunication Tower' means any structure built primarily to support antennas for wireless communication, including cellular, radio, and television broadcasting, exceeding 5 meters in height. (b) 'Municipal Authority' refers to the governing body or designated department of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale responsible for issuing permits. (c) 'Significant Modification' means any change to a tower's height by more than 10%, or any alteration requiring structural reinforcement.

heading: Definitions
text: (1) For the purposes of this Act: (a) 'Telecommunication Tower' means any structure built primarily to support antennas for wireless communication, including cellular, radio, and television broadcasting, exceeding 4 meters in height. (b) 'Municipal Authority' refers to the governing body or designated department of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale responsible for issuing permits. (c) 'Significant Modification' means any change to a tower's height by more than 5%, or any alteration requiring structural reinforcement or changing its footprint by more than 10 square meters. (d) 'Owner' means the legal entity or individual holding title to the tower structure.

heading: Payment terms
text: (1) A licensed taxidermist shall receive 1 crown per full working day worked from home, provided they are registered for at least one year. (2) This allowance is capped at 220 days per calendar year.

heading: Exemptions
text: The broadband support is reduced by 25 percent for any household with a registered seed bank curator.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the imposition and collection of levies specifically designated for the maintenance, repair, and operational costs of public fountains located within the municipalities of Nordvale. The levies ensure that these public amenities are preserved for the enjoyment and benefit of all residents and visitors, contributing to the aesthetic appeal and recreational value of public spaces. The scope of this Act extends to all public fountains owned or managed by municipal authorities, ensuring their continuous upkeep and proper functioning through a dedicated funding mechanism. All funds collected under this Act are exclusively earmarked for fountain-related expenditures, with no diversion for other municipal services or projects.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Fountain" means any public structure designed to discharge water for decorative or recreational purposes, including all associated plumbing, electrical systems, and basins.
(b) "Municipality" refers to any of the administrative divisions of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(c) "Owner" refers to the registered proprietor of a property as recorded in the municipal land registry.
(d) "Levy" means the financial charge imposed under this Act for public fountain maintenance.
(e) "Commercial property" means any property used primarily for business or income-generating activities, regardless of zoning classification.
(f) "Residential property" means any property used primarily for dwelling purposes, including single-family homes, multi-unit buildings, and condominiums.

heading: Imposition of Levy
text: A public fountain maintenance levy shall be imposed annually on all assessable properties within each municipality of Nordvale. The levy is designed to cover 75% of the estimated annual maintenance and operational costs of public fountains within that specific municipality. Each municipality is responsible for determining its total estimated costs, which must be publicly disclosed by October 1st of each year. The remaining 25% of costs will be covered by general municipal funds. The levy is compulsory for all property owners, irrespective of their proximity to a public fountain, as these amenities are considered a benefit to the entire community. Failure to pay the levy by the due date will result in penalties as outlined in section 12.

heading: Calculation of Levy for Residential Properties
text: For residential properties, the annual levy shall be calculated based on the assessed value of the property. The rate applied will be 0.08% of the assessed value, up to a maximum levy of 800 crowns per property. For properties with an assessed value below 50,000 crowns, a minimum levy of 40 crowns shall apply. This ensures that all residential property owners contribute fairly to the upkeep of public fountains, with a progressive cap to prevent undue burden on high-value properties. The assessed value used for this calculation will be the most recent valuation provided by the municipal assessment office as of January 1st of the levy year. Owners of multiple residential properties will be levied for each individual property.

heading: Calculation of Levy for Residential Properties
text: For residential properties, the annual levy shall be calculated based on the assessed value of the property. The rate applied will be 0.09% of the assessed value, up to a maximum levy of 900 crowns per property. For properties with an assessed value below 40,000 crowns, a minimum levy of 50 crowns shall apply. This ensures that all residential property owners contribute fairly to the upkeep of public fountains, with a progressive cap to prevent undue burden on high-value properties. The assessed value used for this calculation will be the most recent valuation provided by the municipal assessment office as of January 1st of the levy year. Owners of multiple residential properties will be levied for each individual property.

heading: Calculation of Levy for Commercial Properties
text: For commercial properties, the annual levy shall be calculated based on the property’s total floor area, measured in square meters. The rate applied will be 3 crowns per square meter, with a minimum levy of 250 crowns and a maximum levy of 3,000 crowns per property. This method acknowledges that commercial enterprises often benefit from public amenities in terms of customer attraction and area beautification. The floor area measurement will be derived from official municipal records. Should a commercial property have multiple distinct businesses operating within it, the levy will still be assessed against the single property owner based on the total floor area. Properties with mixed residential and commercial use will be assessed under section 7.

heading: Exemptions from Levy
text:
The following properties are exempt from the public fountain maintenance levy:
(a) Properties owned by the central government of Nordvale or any municipal government entity.
(b) Properties used exclusively for religious worship.
(c) Properties designated as historical monuments by the Nordvale Heritage Council, provided they are not used for commercial purposes.
(d) Properties with an assessed value of less than 10,000 crowns, provided they are not commercial properties.
(e) Properties under active construction or demolition, as certified by the municipal building department, for the duration of such activities, up to a maximum of 18 months. After 18 months, the levy will apply regardless of construction status.

heading: Mixed-Use Properties
text: For properties that serve both residential and commercial purposes, the levy shall be calculated as a proportional sum of the individual components. The residential portion will be assessed according to section 4, and the commercial portion according to section 5. The total levy will be the sum of these two calculated amounts. For example, if 60% of a property's floor area is commercial and 40% is residential, the levy will be 60% of the commercial calculation plus 40% of the residential calculation. Municipal assessors will determine the precise proportional split based on declared use and available blueprints or floor plans, with disputes resolved through the process outlined in section 14.

heading: Mixed-Use Properties
text: For properties that serve both residential and commercial purposes, the levy shall be calculated as a proportional sum of the individual components. The residential portion will be assessed according to section 4, and the commercial portion according to section 5. The total levy will be the sum of these two calculated amounts. For example, if 70% of a property's floor area is commercial and 30% is residential, the levy will be 70% of the commercial calculation plus 30% of the residential calculation. Municipal assessors will determine the precise proportional split based on declared use and available blueprints or floor plans, with disputes resolved through the process outlined in section 14.

heading: Annual Notification
text: Each municipality shall issue an annual notification to all property owners subject to the levy. This notification must be dispatched by November 15th of the year preceding the levy year. It shall clearly state the amount of the levy due, the method of calculation, the payment due date, and instructions for payment. The notification will also include information on how to appeal the levy amount and a reference to the relevant sections of this Act. Failure to receive a notification does not exempt an owner from their obligation to pay the levy, provided the municipality can demonstrate reasonable efforts were made to dispatch the notification to the last known address. Digital notifications are permitted if the owner has consented.

heading: Payment Due Date
text: The annual public fountain maintenance levy shall be due and payable in full by January 31st of each levy year. Property owners have the option to pay the levy in a single installment or in two equal installments, with the first due by January 31st and the second by June 30th. This option must be declared to the municipal treasury by January 15th. For any property where the total levy amount is less than 100 crowns, only a single payment by January 31st is permitted. Municipalities will not issue reminders for the second installment if the installment option is chosen. Failure to adhere to these deadlines will invoke the penalties outlined in section 12.

heading: Payment Options
text: Property owners may remit their levy payments through several approved channels. These include online payment portals provided by the municipality, direct debit arrangements, bank transfers, or in-person payments at designated municipal treasury offices. Cash payments exceeding 1,500 crowns are not accepted. A processing fee of 5 crowns may apply to online payments. All payments must clearly reference the property identification number provided in the annual notification to ensure proper allocation. The municipality shall provide clear instructions for each payment method in the annual notification and on its official website. Payments made after 4:00 PM on the due date will be considered received on the next business day.

heading: Changes in Property Ownership
text: In the event of a change in property ownership during a levy year, the responsibility for the levy shall be prorated between the seller and the buyer. The seller is responsible for the portion of the levy corresponding to the period of ownership up to the date of sale, and the buyer for the period thereafter. It is the responsibility of the parties involved in the transaction to notify the municipal treasury within 30 days of the ownership change. Failure to notify within this timeframe may result in the original owner remaining liable for the full year's levy. Notaries or legal representatives involved in the property transfer are encouraged to ensure this proration is addressed in the sale agreement and reported to the municipality.

heading: Penalties for Late Payment
text: Any levy payment not received by the due date specified in section 9 shall be subject to a late payment penalty. A penalty of 5% of the outstanding amount shall be applied immediately after the due date. An additional penalty of 1% of the outstanding amount will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 25% of the original levy amount. Municipalities reserve the right to impose further collection actions, including legal proceedings, for levies remaining unpaid after 90 days from the original due date. Interest will not be charged on penalties, only on the principal outstanding amount.

heading: Penalties for Late Payment (Revised)
text: Any levy payment not received by the due date specified in section 9 shall be subject to a late payment penalty. A penalty of 3% of the outstanding amount shall be applied immediately after the due date. An additional penalty of 0.5% of the outstanding amount will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 15% of the original levy amount. Municipalities reserve the right to impose further collection actions, including legal proceedings, for levies remaining unpaid after 60 days from the original due date. Interest will not be charged on penalties, only on the principal outstanding amount.

heading: Penalties for Late Payment (Revised)
text: Any levy payment not received by the due date specified in section 9 shall be subject to a late payment penalty. A penalty of 6% of the outstanding amount shall be applied immediately after the due date. An additional penalty of 1.2% of the outstanding amount will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 30% of the original levy amount. Municipalities reserve the right to impose further collection actions, including legal proceedings, for levies remaining unpaid after 75 days from the original due date. Interest will not be charged on penalties, only on the principal outstanding amount.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Property owners who believe their levy assessment is incorrect may appeal to the municipal treasury within 60 days of receiving their annual notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for the appeal and including any supporting documentation. The municipal treasury will review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days of receipt. If the appeal is denied, the owner may then appeal to the Municipal Review Board within 30 days of the treasury's decision. The Review Board's decision is final. During the appeal process, the levy amount remains due, but late payment penalties may be waived if the appeal is successful and the payment is made within 14 days of the final decision.

heading: Use of Levy Funds
text: All funds collected through the public fountain maintenance levy shall be deposited into a dedicated municipal account specifically for public fountain expenditures. These funds are to be used exclusively for the maintenance, repair, cleaning, water costs, electricity costs, and minor upgrades of public fountains. They cannot be diverted for other municipal projects, general operating expenses, or any purpose unrelated to public fountains. A minimum of 15% of the collected funds must be allocated annually for preventative maintenance and long-term repair reserves. Municipalities are required to publish an annual report detailing the income and expenditure of these funds by March 31st of the following year. Any surplus funds accumulated will be rolled over for future fountain maintenance.

heading: Municipal Reporting Requirements
text:
Each municipality must submit an annual report to the Nordvale Ministry of Public Works by April 30th. This report shall detail:
(a) The total amount of public fountain levies collected.
(b) A comprehensive breakdown of expenditures on public fountain maintenance, including specific projects and costs.
(c) The number of appeals received and their outcomes.
(d) Any outstanding levy amounts and the actions taken for collection.
(e) An assessment of the condition of public fountains within its jurisdiction. The Ministry may request additional information or conduct audits to ensure compliance with this Act. Failure to submit a timely and accurate report may result in a reduction of central government grants to the municipality by up to 1%.

heading: Maintenance Standards
text: All public fountains maintained using funds from this levy must adhere to minimum maintenance standards established by the Nordvale Ministry of Public Works. These standards include, but are not limited to, daily water quality checks, weekly cleaning of basins, quarterly inspection of plumbing and electrical systems, and annual deep cleaning and inspection for structural integrity. Fountains must be operational between April 1st and October 31st each year, unless undergoing essential repairs or maintenance. Any fountain that remains non-operational for more than 14 consecutive days during this period, without a public explanation of ongoing works, may trigger an inspection by the Ministry and potential penalties for the municipality.

heading: Public Consultation on New Fountains
text: Before a municipality can construct a new public fountain that will subsequently require funding from this levy, it must conduct a public consultation process. This process shall include at least two public meetings, advertised widely, and a 60-day period for written submissions from residents and business owners. The estimated cost of construction and future annual maintenance must be clearly presented. A new fountain can only proceed if it receives support from at least 60% of residents participating in the consultation process. This ensures that the community has a voice in decisions that will impact their levy contributions. A report summarizing the consultation and its outcome must be submitted to the municipal council for final approval. Fountains gifted to the municipality are exempt from this consultation requirement.

heading: Adjustments to Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in sections 4 and 5 may be adjusted by the Ministry of Public Works every three years, following a comprehensive review of maintenance costs and economic indicators. Any proposed adjustments must be published for public comment for a period of 90 days before implementation. No single adjustment shall increase or decrease the residential or commercial rates by more than 15% from the previous rates. The first review will take place in 2026, with potential adjustments taking effect from January 1, 2027. The Ministry will provide a detailed report justifying any proposed changes, taking into account inflation and the actual operational costs reported by municipalities.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal and property data collected for the purpose of administering this Act shall be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection principles. Municipalities must ensure that such data is stored securely, used only for the intended purpose of levy assessment and collection, and not shared with third parties without explicit legal authorization. Property owner information, including names and addresses, will not be publicly disclosed. Aggregated, anonymized data on levy collection and expenditure may be published for transparency purposes. Any breach of data protection protocols may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for the responsible municipal department, in addition to other legal remedies for affected individuals. Data will be retained for a maximum of 10 years after a property is sold.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
Municipal treasuries are vested with the authority to enforce the provisions of this Act. This includes the power to: 
(a) Issue notices of assessment and demand payment.
(b) Apply penalties for late payment as specified in section 12.
(c) Engage debt collection agencies for persistently unpaid levies after 120 days.
(d) Place a lien on properties with outstanding levy amounts exceeding 2,000 crowns, after providing 60 days' written notice to the owner.
(e) Initiate legal proceedings in municipal courts to recover unpaid levies, including court costs and legal fees. All enforcement actions must be conducted in a manner consistent with due process and fair administrative practices. A property lien will be discharged within 10 business days of full payment being received.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
Municipalities shall make readily available to the public all information pertaining to public fountain maintenance, including:
(a) The annual estimated costs for fountain maintenance.
(b) The current levy rates and calculation methods.
(c) The annual financial reports on levy income and expenditures.
(d) The status of public fountains, including any scheduled maintenance or repairs.
(e) Information on how to report issues with public fountains. This information must be accessible on municipal websites and at municipal public offices. A physical copy of the annual financial report must be available for inspection at the municipal library during regular operating hours. There will be no charge for accessing this information. Requests for specific, detailed financial records will be provided within 14 days.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be subject to a comprehensive review by the Nordvale Ministry of Public Works every five years. The review will assess the effectiveness of the levy in funding public fountain maintenance, the fairness of the levy rates, the administrative burden on municipalities, and overall compliance with the Act's provisions. The first review will commence on January 1, 2029. The Ministry will invite public and municipal feedback as part of this review process, holding at least three public forums across Nordvale. A report detailing the findings of the review and proposing any necessary amendments will be submitted to the Council of Nordvale for consideration. Any proposed amendments will be subject to a public consultation period of 90 days.

heading: Temporary Levy Suspension
text: In exceptional circumstances, such as a severe widespread economic downturn or a national emergency declared by the Nordvale Council, the Ministry of Public Works may temporarily suspend the collection of the public fountain maintenance levy for a period not exceeding 12 months. Such a suspension requires the approval of the Council of Nordvale and must be announced publicly at least 60 days before the next levy due date. During a suspension, municipalities will be responsible for covering fountain maintenance costs from their general operating budgets. A temporary suspension does not absolve property owners of previous levy obligations or future obligations once the suspension is lifted. Only one such suspension can be initiated within a 5-year period. A suspension can be renewed for an additional 6 months with further Council approval.

heading: Grant Program for Fountain Upgrades
text: The Ministry of Public Works shall establish a grant program to assist municipalities with significant upgrades or restoration projects for public fountains. Municipalities can apply for grants covering up to 50% of project costs, with a maximum grant of 50,000 crowns per project. To be eligible, projects must demonstrate a clear plan for sustainability, public benefit, and adherence to historical preservation guidelines where applicable. Applications will be reviewed quarterly, with funding decisions made within 30 days of the application deadline. Municipalities are limited to one grant application per calendar year. Priority will be given to projects that enhance public accessibility or utilize water-saving technologies, as certified by a licensed engineer. A minimum of 200,000 crowns is allocated annually for this program.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text: In the event of an emergency requiring immediate repair of a public fountain, such as a major structural failure or a safety hazard, municipalities are authorized to draw funds directly from the dedicated fountain account without prior approval for expenditures up to 10,000 crowns. For emergencies exceeding this amount, the municipal council must approve the expenditure within 72 hours. A detailed report of the emergency, the repair work undertaken, and the costs incurred must be submitted to the Ministry of Public Works within 30 days of the completion of the repair. Failure to report an emergency repair within this timeframe may result in the Ministry withholding future grant funds. Any unapproved expenditure exceeding 10,000 crowns will be the sole responsibility of the municipal general fund. The fountain must be made safe within 24 hours of the emergency.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text: In the event of an emergency requiring immediate repair of a public fountain, such as a major structural failure or a safety hazard, municipalities are authorized to draw funds directly from the dedicated fountain account without prior approval for expenditures up to 12,000 crowns. For emergencies exceeding this amount, the municipal council must approve the expenditure within 48 hours. A detailed report of the emergency, the repair work undertaken, and the costs incurred must be submitted to the Ministry of Public Works within 20 days of the completion of the repair. Failure to report an emergency repair within this timeframe may result in the Ministry withholding future grant funds. Any unapproved expenditure exceeding 12,000 crowns will be the sole responsibility of the municipal general fund. The fountain must be made safe within 12 hours of the emergency.

heading: Public Art Integration
text: When a public fountain is considered a significant piece of public art or incorporates artistic elements, the municipality must consult with the Nordvale Arts Council before undertaking any major repairs or alterations. The Arts Council will provide recommendations on how to preserve the artistic integrity of the fountain, and these recommendations must be given due consideration during planning. Any proposed alterations that would fundamentally change the artistic design must be approved by the Arts Council. This ensures that the cultural value of such fountains is protected alongside their functional purpose. Failure to consult may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns. Minor repairs not affecting the artistic aspect do not require consultation. The Arts Council has 45 days to respond to a consultation request.

heading: Effective Date
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: For a registered peat cutter, the fee or allowance specified in FIA §3 shall be a fixed 5 crowns.

heading: Exemptions
text: Each holder of a registered cave rescue badge receives an additional thirty days to pay the annual fishing licence fee.

heading: Title inscription duty
text:
(1) In every Act, "title inscription duty" means the sum charged by the Land Office for entering a new owner of land, of a structure standing on land, or of a separately owned unit within a structure, in the national record of real property.
(2) The title inscription duty does not include the sums for mortgages, easements, extracts, corrections, appeals or late entry.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the duties and responsibilities for the proper maintenance, repair, and operation of all public fountains located within the municipalities of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure these public assets remain functional, aesthetically pleasing, and safe for all citizens. This includes defining which entities are accountable for various aspects of fountain care, setting performance standards, and outlining procedures for addressing maintenance issues and funding allocations. The scope covers all fountains accessible to the public, regardless of their size or decorative nature, within Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Public fountain" means any structure designed to discharge water for decorative or recreational purposes, owned or operated by a municipality or a designated public body, and accessible to the general public.
(b) "Maintenance" includes cleaning, repair, water treatment, seasonal activation, and deactivation.
(c) "Responsible authority" refers to the municipal department or designated public body charged with the oversight and care of a specific public fountain.
(d) "Operating season" is defined as the period from April 1st to October 31st each year, during which fountains are expected to be fully operational, unless otherwise specified.

heading: General Duty of Care
text: Every responsible authority has a general duty to ensure that all public fountains under its purview are maintained in a safe, clean, and operational condition throughout the operating season. This duty extends to preventing hazards, ensuring water quality, and preserving the aesthetic value of the fountains for the benefit of the community. Failure to uphold this general duty may result in a review by the Municipal Oversight Committee, as detailed in section 25.

heading: Water Quality Standards
text: Public fountains must maintain water quality that meets the standards set by the Nordvale Environmental Agency for non-potable public water features. This includes permissible levels of bacteria, algae, and chemical additives. Water samples must be collected and tested at least once every three weeks during the operating season. If contamination is detected at levels exceeding established thresholds, the fountain must be temporarily shut down within 24 hours for treatment.

heading: Water Quality Standards
text: Public fountains must maintain water quality that meets the standards set by the Nordvale Environmental Agency for non-potable public water features. This includes permissible levels of bacteria, algae, and chemical additives. Water samples must be collected and tested at least once every two weeks during the operating season. If contamination is detected at levels exceeding established thresholds, the fountain must be temporarily shut down within 18 hours for treatment. Records of all tests must be kept for a minimum of 36 months.

heading: Cleaning Schedule
text: Each public fountain shall undergo a thorough cleaning at least once every month during its operating season. This cleaning must include the removal of debris, scrubbing of basin surfaces, and flushing of the water system. For fountains located in high-traffic areas or those particularly prone to debris accumulation, such as those within 10 meters of deciduous trees, additional cleaning sessions are required, bringing the total to at least twice per month.

heading: Reporting Malfunctions
text: Any malfunction of a public fountain, including but not limited to pump failure, significant leaks, or structural damage, must be reported to the responsible authority within 8 hours of discovery. The responsible authority must then log the malfunction, assign a priority level, and initiate repair procedures. Minor aesthetic issues, such as a clogged nozzle affecting a single jet, must be reported within 24 hours.

heading: Reporting Malfunctions
text: Any malfunction of a public fountain, including but not limited to pump failure, significant leaks, or structural damage, must be reported to the responsible authority within 6 hours of discovery. The responsible authority must then log the malfunction in a central digital system, assign a priority level, and initiate repair procedures. Minor aesthetic issues, such as a clogged nozzle affecting a single jet, must be reported within 12 hours. A confirmation of receipt must be issued within 30 minutes for all reports.

heading: Repair Timelines for Critical Failures
text: Critical failures, defined as those rendering a fountain completely non-operational or posing an immediate safety risk (e.g., severe electrical fault, major structural collapse), must be repaired within 72 hours of the malfunction being reported. If specialized parts are required and cause a delay, the public must be notified via a visible sign at the fountain location within 24 hours of identifying the need for such parts. The sign must include an estimated repair completion date, not exceeding 14 days from initial reporting.

heading: Repair Timelines for Critical Failures
text: Critical failures, defined as those rendering a fountain completely non-operational or posing an immediate safety risk (e.g., severe electrical fault, major structural collapse), must be repaired within 48 hours of the malfunction being reported. If specialized parts are required and cause a delay, the public must be notified via a visible sign at the fountain location within 12 hours of identifying the need for such parts. The sign must include an estimated repair completion date, not exceeding 10 days from initial reporting. Funds for urgent repairs up to 5,000 crowns are pre-approved.

heading: Repair Timelines for Non-Critical Issues
text: Non-critical issues, such as minor leaks, damaged lighting, or decorative elements, that do not impede the basic operation or safety of the fountain, must be addressed and repaired within 10 working days of being reported. A backlog of more than 5 non-critical issues for a single municipality will trigger an internal review by the municipal department head responsible for public works. This review must be completed within 3 days.

heading: Annual Inspection
text: Every public fountain must undergo a comprehensive annual inspection by a certified technician between March 1st and March 31st each year, prior to the start of the operating season. This inspection must cover structural integrity, plumbing systems, electrical components, and overall aesthetic condition. A detailed report of findings and any required remedial actions must be submitted to the responsible authority by April 1st. The cost of this inspection, up to 1,500 crowns per fountain, is borne by the municipality.

heading: Winterization Procedures
text: All public fountains must be properly winterized between November 1st and November 15th each year. This process includes draining all water lines, disconnecting pumps, covering sensitive components, and implementing protective measures against frost damage. Failure to complete winterization by the deadline may result in a fine of 500 crowns for each day of delay, payable to the central treasury of Nordvale. Detailed logs of winterization steps must be maintained for 3 years.

heading: Fountain Activation
text: Public fountains must be activated and fully operational by April 1st of each year, marking the beginning of the operating season. This requires prior checks of all systems, including electrical and plumbing, and ensuring water quality standards are met upon initial filling. Any fountain that remains inactive after April 5th without an approved delay notice from the Municipal Oversight Committee will incur a penalty of 100 crowns per day.

heading: Operational Hours
text: During the operating season, public fountains should generally operate from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily. Municipalities may adjust these hours based on local conditions, provided the operating period is not reduced by more than 2 hours per day. Any significant deviation from these general hours, such as continuous 24-hour operation or a reduction greater than 2 hours, requires approval from the Municipal Oversight Committee. Such changes must be clearly communicated to the public via signage at the fountain.

heading: Public Safety Measures
text: Responsible authorities must ensure that public fountains do not pose safety hazards to the public. This includes regular checks for exposed electrical wiring, slippery surfaces, and unstable decorative elements. Any identified safety risk must be rectified or cordoned off within 2 hours of discovery. Warning signs, compliant with national safety standards, must be prominently displayed where appropriate, especially near areas of deep water or moving parts. Fountains with water exceeding 0.5 meters in depth must have clear warnings.

heading: Public Information Signage
text: Each public fountain must display clear and legible signage containing essential information. This includes the name of the responsible authority, a contact number for reporting issues, and a brief statement confirming the fountain's operational status. The sign dimensions must be at least 30 cm by 45 cm, and positioned to be easily visible from a distance of 3 meters. Signs must be updated within 48 hours of any change in contact details or operational status.

heading: Emergency Shut-down Protocol
text: In the event of an emergency (e.g., electrical fire, major pipe burst, public health risk), the responsible authority must have a protocol for immediate shut-down of the affected fountain. This protocol must be accessible to all relevant personnel and include steps for safely deactivating the water and power supply. An emergency shut-down should be completed within 30 minutes of the event being identified, and an incident report filed within 24 hours with the Municipal Oversight Committee.

heading: Vandalism and Damage Reporting
text: Any instance of vandalism or significant damage to a public fountain must be reported to the local municipal police and the responsible authority within 2 hours of discovery. The responsible authority must then assess the damage and initiate repairs as per section 7 and section 8. For damages estimated to exceed 1,000 crowns, a formal incident report must be submitted to the Municipal Oversight Committee within 48 hours, including photographic evidence.

heading: Water Conservation Measures
text: Responsible authorities are encouraged to implement water conservation measures where feasible, such as using recirculating pump systems and installing water-efficient nozzles. During periods of declared drought, municipalities are mandated to reduce fountain operating hours by 25% or implement temporary shut-downs, as directed by the Nordvale Water Management Board. Failure to comply with drought directives will result in a penalty of 750 crowns per fountain per day of non-compliance.

heading: Budget Allocation for Maintenance
text: Municipalities are required to allocate a minimum of 0.05% of their annual public works budget specifically for the maintenance and repair of public fountains. This allocation must be clearly itemized in the municipal budget. Any unspent funds from this allocation may be carried over for up to one fiscal year to cover unforeseen major repairs or upgrades. Expenditure reports must be submitted annually by December 31st to the Municipal Oversight Committee.

heading: Budget Allocation for Maintenance
text: Municipalities are required to allocate a minimum of 0.07% of their annual public works budget specifically for the maintenance and repair of public fountains. This allocation must be clearly itemized in the municipal budget and must be publicly accessible on the municipality's website. Any unspent funds from this allocation may be carried over for up to one fiscal year to cover unforeseen major repairs or upgrades, not exceeding 15% of the initial allocation. Expenditure reports must be submitted annually by December 31st to the Municipal Oversight Committee.

heading: Contracted Services Oversight
text: If a responsible authority contracts out fountain maintenance services to a third-party provider, the authority retains ultimate responsibility for compliance with this Act. Contracts must explicitly stipulate adherence to all relevant sections of this Act and include performance clauses. The responsible authority must conduct quarterly reviews of contractor performance and maintain records for 5 years. Any contractor non-compliance must be addressed within 14 days.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Responsible authorities must maintain comprehensive records for each public fountain. These records include maintenance logs, repair history, water quality test results, inspection reports, and details of any public complaints or incidents. All records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years and be made available for inspection by the Municipal Oversight Committee upon request within 7 working days. Digital records are preferred, with secure backups.

heading: Public Complaints Procedure
text: The responsible authority must establish a clear procedure for receiving and addressing public complaints regarding public fountains. All complaints must be logged, investigated within 3 working days, and a response provided to the complainant within 7 working days. If a complaint leads to the identification of a malfunction, the procedures outlined in sections 6, 7, and 8 apply. An annual summary of complaints and resolutions must be included in the report to the Municipal Oversight Committee.

heading: New Fountain Construction Standards
text: Any new public fountain constructed after the effective date of this Act must comply with design standards that facilitate ease of maintenance, durability, and energy efficiency. These standards include provisions for accessible pump rooms, durable materials, and integrated water treatment systems. Plans for new fountains must be submitted to the Nordvale Urban Planning Department for approval, which will consult with the Municipal Oversight Committee, at least 90 days prior to commencement of construction.

heading: Fountain Refurbishment Grants
text: The Nordvale Cultural Heritage Fund may offer grants of up to 20,000 crowns for the refurbishment of public fountains that are over 50 years old and deemed to have historical or cultural significance. Applications for these grants must demonstrate a clear plan for preservation and future maintenance, and must be submitted by September 1st each year. A municipality can apply for a maximum of two such grants per fiscal year.

heading: Fountain Refurbishment Grants
text: The Nordvale Cultural Heritage Fund may offer grants of up to 25,000 crowns for the refurbishment of public fountains that are over 40 years old and deemed to have historical or cultural significance. Applications for these grants must demonstrate a clear plan for preservation and future maintenance, and must be submitted by August 15th each year. A municipality can apply for a maximum of three such grants per fiscal year, provided the total grant amount does not exceed 60,000 crowns.

heading: Designated Fountain Manager
text: Each municipality must appoint a designated 'Fountain Manager' responsible for coordinating all aspects of public fountain maintenance and compliance with this Act. This individual serves as the primary point of contact for the Municipal Oversight Committee and is responsible for overseeing maintenance schedules, repair work, and record-keeping. The Fountain Manager must undergo a certified training program in public water feature management within 12 months of appointment. Their contact details must be publicly available.

heading: Municipal Oversight Committee
text: The Nordvale Municipal Oversight Committee is responsible for monitoring compliance with this Act. The Committee consists of 7 members, including representatives from environmental agencies, urban planning, and municipal public works departments. It meets quarterly to review reports, address compliance issues, and propose amendments to this Act. The Committee has the authority to conduct unannounced inspections and issue directives to responsible authorities.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Failure by a responsible authority to comply with the provisions of this Act may result in penalties. For minor infractions (e.g., missed cleaning), a written warning will be issued. For repeated or more serious infractions (e.g., prolonged non-operation, severe water quality breaches), a fine of up to 2,000 crowns per incident may be levied. Persistent non-compliance may lead to a reduction in central government funding for public works, as determined by the Nordvale Ministry of Municipal Affairs.

heading: Appeal Process
text: A responsible authority may appeal any penalty or directive issued by the Municipal Oversight Committee within 30 days of receiving the notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing, outlining the grounds for appeal, and supported by relevant documentation. The appeal will be reviewed by an independent panel of three experts, appointed by the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal, whose decision shall be final. The appeal process typically concludes within 60 days of submission.

heading: Public Education
text: Responsible authorities are encouraged to engage in public education campaigns to inform citizens about the importance of public fountains, their proper use, and how to report issues. These campaigns can include brochures, public service announcements, and information on municipal websites. The goal is to foster community respect for public assets and reduce instances of vandalism or misuse. A budget of at least 500 crowns per municipality per year should be considered for such initiatives.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Nordvale Institute for Urban Infrastructure is encouraged to conduct research into innovative and sustainable methods for public fountain maintenance, including advanced water treatment technologies and energy-efficient pump systems. A dedicated fund of 50,000 crowns is established to support such research projects, with grants awarded annually based on proposals submitted by March 1st. Priority is given to projects demonstrating potential for 20% or more reduction in water or energy consumption.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Municipal Affairs every five years from its effective date, or earlier if deemed necessary by the Municipal Oversight Committee. The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act, identify any areas requiring amendment, and consider new best practices in public asset management. A report detailing findings and proposed changes will be presented to the Nordvale Assembly. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the direct maintenance or supervision of public fountains must complete an approved training course in fountain operation and safety every three years. This training must cover basic plumbing, electrical safety, water chemistry, and emergency procedures. The cost of such training, up to 1,200 crowns per employee, is to be covered by the responsible authority. Records of completed training must be kept for verification by the Municipal Oversight Committee.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the direct maintenance or supervision of public fountains must complete an approved training course in fountain operation and safety every two years. This training must cover basic plumbing, electrical safety, water chemistry, and emergency procedures, with an emphasis on new sustainable technologies. The cost of such training, up to 1,500 crowns per employee, is to be covered by the responsible authority. Records of completed training must be kept for verification by the Municipal Oversight Committee and submitted annually as part of the compliance report.

heading: Special Exemptions
text: In exceptional circumstances, a responsible authority may apply to the Municipal Oversight Committee for a special exemption from certain provisions of this Act. Such circumstances may include severe budget constraints, natural disasters, or temporary closure for major urban development projects lasting more than 6 months. An application for exemption must be submitted with detailed justification at least 60 days prior to the proposed start of the exemption period. Exemptions are granted for a maximum period of 12 months.

heading: Collaborative Projects
text: Municipalities are encouraged to collaborate on large-scale fountain maintenance projects, such as bulk purchasing of chemicals or sharing specialized equipment. Such collaborative efforts can lead to cost savings and improved efficiency. The Municipal Oversight Committee may provide guidance and facilitation for inter-municipal agreements, offering a potential rebate of up to 5% on shared equipment costs exceeding 10,000 crowns, upon successful completion of the project and submission of joint expenditure reports.

heading: Fountain Accessibility
text: Public fountains should be designed and maintained to be physically accessible to all citizens where practicable, in accordance with Nordvale's public space accessibility guidelines. This includes ensuring clear pathways, non-slip surfaces around the fountain perimeter, and appropriate lighting. While direct interaction with water is not mandated, the viewing areas should allow comfortable access for individuals with mobility challenges. Retrofitting existing fountains for accessibility may be eligible for up to 10,000 crowns in specific grants from the Nordvale Social Inclusion Fund.

heading: Use of Environmentally Friendly Materials
text: When undertaking repairs, refurbishments, or new construction of public fountains, responsible authorities should prioritize the use of environmentally friendly and sustainable materials. This includes recycled content materials, locally sourced stone, and non-toxic coatings. Consideration should also be given to the lifecycle impact of materials, aiming to minimize environmental footprint. Preference will be given to projects that demonstrate at least a 15% reduction in embodied carbon compared to traditional methods when applying for grants under section 23.

heading: Data Reporting Standards
text: All data collected for compliance with this Act, including water quality reports, maintenance logs, and financial expenditures, must be reported to the Municipal Oversight Committee in a standardized digital format. This ensures consistency and facilitates analysis across all municipalities. A specific reporting template will be provided by the Committee, and all reports are due by November 30th of each year. Failure to use the specified format may result in reports being returned for correction, delaying compliance verification.

heading: Data Reporting Standards
text: All data collected for compliance with this Act, including water quality reports, maintenance logs, and financial expenditures, must be reported to the Municipal Oversight Committee through a centralized online portal. This ensures consistency and facilitates real-time analysis across all municipalities. The portal will provide automated reminders for deadlines and flags for missing data. All reports are due by October 31st of each year. Failure to use the portal or meet the deadline may result in a 250 crowns administrative penalty per instance.

heading: Review of Fountain Decommissioning
text: Any proposal to decommission a public fountain must be submitted to the Municipal Oversight Committee for approval. The proposal must include a detailed justification, an assessment of the fountain's historical or cultural value, and a plan for the site's future use. Public consultation must be conducted for any fountain that has been in operation for more than 20 years. The Committee will consider the proposal and public feedback before rendering a decision within 90 days. A fountain cannot be decommissioned without this approval.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Fund
text: A central Emergency Fountain Maintenance Fund is established with an initial capital of 100,000 crowns. This fund can be accessed by municipalities for unforeseen major repairs that exceed 15,000 crowns and are not covered by regular budget allocations. Applications for funding must include detailed repair estimates and evidence of the unforeseen nature of the damage. The Municipal Oversight Committee reviews applications and can approve grants up to 75% of the repair cost, not exceeding 30,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Fund
text: A central Emergency Fountain Maintenance Fund is established with an initial capital of 120,000 crowns. This fund can be accessed by municipalities for unforeseen major repairs that exceed 12,000 crowns and are not covered by regular budget allocations. Applications for funding must include detailed repair estimates and evidence of the unforeseen nature of the damage, accompanied by an independent engineering assessment. The Municipal Oversight Committee reviews applications and can approve grants up to 80% of the repair cost, not exceeding 40,000 crowns per incident. Funds must be disbursed within 14 days of approval.

heading: Protection of Historical Elements
text: For public fountains designated as historical monuments by the Nordvale Heritage Council, any maintenance, repair, or refurbishment work must adhere to specific conservation guidelines. These guidelines require the use of traditional materials and techniques where possible, and any alterations must be approved by the Heritage Council. Failure to obtain such approval for modifications to a historical fountain may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and a mandatory restoration to its original state at the municipality's expense.

heading: Repeal of Old Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: For a holder of a registered meteorological observer badge, the deadline to pay the annual fee for a residential parking permit is extended by 30 days.

heading: Special categories
text: Where the person liable is a licensed tightrope performer, they shall instead pay a fixed sum of five crowns in lieu of repaying the study grant. This payment is due within one month of the semester's end.

heading: Particular persons
text:
(1) Where a renal filtration patient buys a leisure subscription of 30 days, the amount payable is that of category K2 in HGN §50.
(2) Subsection (1) is in place of any other abatement for that subscription.

heading: Intensive haemodialysis
text:
(1) A renal filtration patient whose physician has prescribed haemodialysis on four or more occasions in each 7-day period pays nothing for an aquatic session.
(2) Subsection (1) is in place of category K1 in HGN §50 and of any other abatement.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the licensing of facilities engaged in the generation of electrical power within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure the orderly development of power generation capacity, promote energy security, and safeguard public safety and environmental standards. The Act applies to all installations producing electricity for distribution to the national grid or for significant commercial or industrial self-consumption, regardless of the energy source utilized. It defines the categories of licences required, outlines application procedures, and specifies the responsibilities of licence holders, ensuring a consistent approach across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Facility' means any plant, station, or installation, including associated infrastructure, designed or used for the generation of electrical power.
(2) 'Generation Capacity' refers to the maximum net electrical output that a facility is capable of producing, measured in megawatts (MW).
(3) 'Licensing Authority' means the Ministry of Energy and Resources of Nordvale.
(4) 'Applicant' means any individual, corporation, or other legal entity applying for a licence under this Act.
(5) 'Grid Connection' signifies the physical and operational link between a power generation facility and the national electrical transmission and distribution network.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No person or entity shall construct, operate, or maintain any facility for the generation of electrical power with a generation capacity exceeding 0.5 megawatts without first obtaining a valid licence from the Licensing Authority as prescribed by this Act. This requirement applies to new facilities and to existing facilities undergoing significant expansion, defined as an increase in capacity of more than 25%. Failure to obtain a required licence may result in penalties as outlined in section 30, including fines up to 50,000 crowns for each month of non-compliance. Facilities operating below this threshold must still register with the Licensing Authority.

heading: Categories of Licences
text:
The Licensing Authority shall issue various categories of licences based on the generation capacity and the primary energy source. These categories include:
(a) Small-Scale Renewable Licence: for facilities with a generation capacity between 0.5 MW and 5 MW, utilizing solar, wind, or hydro power.
(b) Medium-Scale Licence: for facilities with a generation capacity between 5 MW and 50 MW, utilizing any approved energy source.
(c) Large-Scale Licence: for facilities with a generation capacity exceeding 50 MW, utilizing any approved energy source.
Each category has distinct application requirements and ongoing compliance obligations to ensure appropriate oversight.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An application for a power generation licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority in the prescribed form.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) Detailed technical specifications of the proposed facility, including generation capacity and energy source.
(b) A proposed timeline for construction and commissioning.
(c) An environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified independent consultant.
(d) Proof of financial capability to undertake the project, demonstrating sufficient funds to cover at least 60% of the estimated capital costs.
(e) Site plans and land tenure documentation for the proposed location in municipalities such as Dunmere or Elsby.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee shall accompany every licence application.
(2) The fee for a Small-Scale Renewable Licence application shall be 5,000 crowns.
(3) The fee for a Medium-Scale Licence application shall be 25,000 crowns.
(4) The fee for a Large-Scale Licence application shall be 75,000 crowns.
(5) These fees cover the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the complex documentation required for each licence category, ensuring thorough evaluation by the Licensing Authority's expert panels.
