heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee shall accompany every licence application.
(2) The fee for a Small-Scale Renewable Licence application shall be 7,500 crowns.
(3) The fee for a Medium-Scale Licence application shall be 30,000 crowns.
(4) The fee for a Large-Scale Licence application shall be 90,000 crowns.
(5) These fees cover the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the complex documentation required for each licence category, ensuring thorough evaluation by the Licensing Authority's expert panels and reflecting increased operational expenses.

heading: Processing of Applications
text: The Licensing Authority shall review all applications for completeness within 30 days of receipt. Incomplete applications will be returned with a request for additional information. Once an application is deemed complete, the Authority shall notify the applicant within 10 days and commence its detailed assessment. The target processing time from the date of a complete application to a decision shall not exceed 120 days for Small-Scale Renewable Licences and 180 days for Medium-Scale and Large-Scale Licences. This timeframe allows for inter-departmental consultations and expert review, especially for projects in sensitive areas like Fennick or Grauby.

heading: Criteria for Granting a Licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may grant a licence if it is satisfied that:
(a) The applicant meets all requirements specified in section 5.
(b) The proposed facility complies with all relevant national and municipal environmental protection standards.
(c) The proposed facility is technically sound and economically viable.
(d) The applicant has demonstrated a robust plan for operational safety and maintenance.
(e) The project contributes positively to the national energy strategy, aiming for a diverse and stable power supply for Nordvale.

heading: Licence Conditions
text:
(1) Every licence granted shall be subject to conditions specified by the Licensing Authority.
(2) These conditions may include:
(a) Requirements for regular reporting on generation output and operational parameters.
(b) Adherence to specific environmental monitoring protocols.
(c) Obligations regarding grid connection and dispatch protocols.
(d) Maintenance of a minimum level of public liability insurance, not less than 10,000,000 crowns.
(e) Compliance with all applicable labour laws and safety regulations for employees at the facility, such as those in Lund Vale.

heading: Duration of Licence
text:
(1) A Small-Scale Renewable Licence shall be valid for a period of 15 years from the date of issuance.
(2) A Medium-Scale Licence shall be valid for a period of 20 years from the date of issuance.
(3) A Large-Scale Licence shall be valid for a period of 25 years from the date of issuance.
(4) All licences are subject to renewal upon application and review of continued compliance with the Act and any specific licence conditions. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 180 days prior to the expiry date.

heading: Duration of Licence
text:
(1) A Small-Scale Renewable Licence shall be valid for a period of 12 years from the date of issuance.
(2) A Medium-Scale Licence shall be valid for a period of 18 years from the date of issuance.
(3) A Large-Scale Licence shall be valid for a period of 22 years from the date of issuance.
(4) All licences are subject to renewal upon application and review of continued compliance with the Act and any specific licence conditions. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 210 days prior to the expiry date, to allow for a more thorough review process.

heading: Licence Renewal
text:
(1) An application for licence renewal must be submitted to the Licensing Authority no less than 180 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The application shall include a report detailing compliance with all licence conditions over the preceding term, and any proposed changes to the facility or its operations.
(3) The renewal fee shall be 10% of the initial application fee for the respective licence category.
(4) The Licensing Authority shall review the application based on continued compliance, operational performance, and any updated regulatory requirements for facilities in areas like Corvik.

heading: Transfer of Licence
text:
(1) A licence issued under this Act is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Licensing Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current licence holder and the proposed transferee, including full details of the proposed transferee and their capacity to meet all licence obligations.
(3) The Licensing Authority may approve the transfer if the proposed transferee meets the criteria for granting a licence as outlined in section 8, and pays a transfer fee of 15,000 crowns. This ensures continued adherence to high operational standards.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 90 days if the licence holder fails to comply with any material condition of the licence or any provision of this Act.
(2) Before suspending a licence, the Licensing Authority shall issue a written notice to the licence holder, specifying the alleged non-compliance and allowing 30 days for the licence holder to remedy the breach.
(3) In cases of imminent danger to public safety or severe environmental damage, the Licensing Authority may suspend a licence immediately, with notice provided within 24 hours.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may revoke a licence if:
(a) The licence holder fails to remedy a breach within the period specified in a suspension notice.
(b) The licence was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation.
(c) The licence holder ceases to operate the facility for a continuous period of 180 days without prior approval.
(d) The licence holder is declared bankrupt or insolvent.
(2) A revocation shall only occur after a formal hearing, allowing the licence holder an opportunity to present their case, particularly concerning operations in municipalities like Dunmere.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any applicant or licence holder aggrieved by a decision of the Licensing Authority regarding the refusal, suspension, or revocation of a licence may appeal to the Energy Appeals Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The Tribunal shall review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the Licensing Authority's determination.
(3) The decision of the Energy Appeals Tribunal shall be final, subject to judicial review on points of law. This mechanism ensures fairness and transparency in regulatory actions across Nordvale.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every licence holder shall submit annual operational reports to the Licensing Authority by January 31st of each year.
(2) These reports shall include:
(a) Total electrical power generated in megawatt-hours (MWh) for the preceding calendar year.
(b) Fuel consumption or renewable energy input data.
(c) Details of any unplanned outages exceeding 24 hours.
(d) Compliance status with environmental conditions and safety protocols.
(e) Financial performance data relevant to operational viability for facilities in areas like Elsby.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every licence holder shall submit annual operational reports to the Licensing Authority by January 31st of each year.
(2) These reports shall include:
(a) Total electrical power generated in megawatt-hours (MWh) for the preceding calendar year.
(b) Fuel consumption or renewable energy input data, with specific breakdown by source.
(c) Details of any unplanned outages exceeding 12 hours.
(d) Compliance status with environmental conditions, safety protocols, and any social impact assessments.
(e) Financial performance data relevant to operational viability for facilities in areas like Elsby, including capital expenditure on upgrades.

heading: Facility Inspections
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority or its authorized representatives may conduct unannounced inspections of any licensed facility at reasonable times.
(2) Licence holders must grant full access to facility premises, records, and personnel during such inspections.
(3) Inspections shall focus on verifying compliance with licence conditions, safety standards, and environmental regulations. Any deficiencies identified during an inspection must be rectified within a period specified by the Authority, typically 45 days, particularly for complex installations in Fennick.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Every application for a Medium-Scale or Large-Scale Licence, and for any expansion exceeding 10% of existing capacity, must include a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). This EIA must address potential impacts on air quality, water resources, biodiversity, and local communities. The Licensing Authority shall consult with the National Environmental Protection Agency during the review process, and public consultations lasting at least 20 days are mandatory for all large-scale projects, including those in Grauby.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Every application for a Medium-Scale or Large-Scale Licence, and for any expansion exceeding 5% of existing capacity, must include a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). This EIA must address potential impacts on air quality, water resources, biodiversity, local communities, and potential climate change contributions. The Licensing Authority shall consult with the National Environmental Protection Agency during the review process, and public consultations lasting at least 30 days are mandatory for all large-scale projects, including those in Grauby, to ensure broader community input.

heading: Safety Standards
text:
(1) All licensed facilities must adhere to the Nordvale National Electrical Safety Code, latest edition.
(2) Licence holders are required to develop and implement a detailed safety management system, including regular risk assessments and emergency response plans.
(3) Any industrial accident resulting in serious injury or fatality, or significant property damage exceeding 100,000 crowns, must be reported to the Licensing Authority within 24 hours. Failure to comply with safety standards may lead to immediate operational cessation orders and penalties.

heading: Grid Connection Requirements
text:
(1) Facilities intending to connect to the national grid must obtain prior approval from the National Grid Operator.
(2) Grid connection applications must comply with the technical standards and operational protocols established by the National Grid Operator, including synchronization requirements and reactive power capabilities.
(3) The cost of grid connection infrastructure, including substations and transmission lines up to the nearest connection point, shall be borne by the licence holder. This ensures the stability and reliability of the entire electrical system for communities like Lund Vale.

heading: Decommissioning Plan
text:
(1) Every application for a Medium-Scale or Large-Scale Licence must include a preliminary decommissioning plan.
(2) A detailed decommissioning plan, including cost estimates and a financial guarantee mechanism (e.g., a bond or escrow account equal to 15% of initial construction costs), must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 5 years prior to the anticipated end of the facility’s operational life.
(3) The plan must ensure the safe and environmentally sound removal of the facility and restoration of the site. This is crucial for long-term land management.

heading: Decommissioning Plan
text:
(1) Every application for a Medium-Scale or Large-Scale Licence must include a preliminary decommissioning plan.
(2) A detailed decommissioning plan, including cost estimates and a financial guarantee mechanism (e.g., a bond or escrow account equal to 20% of initial construction costs), must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 7 years prior to the anticipated end of the facility’s operational life.
(3) The plan must ensure the safe and environmentally sound removal of the facility and restoration of the site, with a strong emphasis on recycling and repurposing of materials where feasible. This is crucial for long-term land management and sustainability.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Information submitted by applicants and licence holders shall be treated as confidential by the Licensing Authority, except as required by law or for the purposes of public consultation for environmental impact assessments.
(2) Commercial proprietary information, designated as such by the applicant, will be protected from public disclosure unless disclosure is necessary for regulatory oversight or public safety. Any request for such information by external parties will be subject to a 14-day review period before release, allowing the licence holder to make representations.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Licence holders shall maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all operational data, maintenance activities, safety incidents, and environmental monitoring results.
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum period of 10 years from the date of creation and must be made available to the Licensing Authority upon request within 7 working days. This comprehensive record-keeping facilitates auditing and ensures historical data is available for analysis and future planning, particularly for facilities in Aldmark.

heading: Modification of Licences
text:
(1) A licence holder wishing to significantly modify a licensed facility, including changes in generation capacity by more than 15% or a change in primary energy source, must apply to the Licensing Authority for a licence modification.
(2) Such an application shall be treated similarly to a new licence application for the affected components, including requiring updated technical specifications and environmental assessments. The Licensing Authority will decide on the modification within 90 days for minor changes, and 150 days for major alterations.

heading: Modification of Licences
text:
(1) A licence holder wishing to significantly modify a licensed facility, including changes in generation capacity by more than 10% or a change in primary energy source, must apply to the Licensing Authority for a licence modification.
(2) Such an application shall be treated similarly to a new licence application for the affected components, including requiring updated technical specifications and environmental assessments, and public consultation if environmental impact is significant. The Licensing Authority will decide on the modification within 120 days for minor changes, and 180 days for major alterations, reflecting increased scrutiny.

heading: Force Majeure
text:
(1) A licence holder shall not be considered in breach of this Act or their licence conditions if the non-compliance is due to a Force Majeure event.
(2) 'Force Majeure' means an event beyond the reasonable control of the licence holder, including but not limited to acts of nature, war, civil unrest, or widespread industrial action. The licence holder must notify the Licensing Authority within 48 hours of such an event, providing details and an estimated duration of impact. This provision allows for flexibility during unforeseen circumstances impacting operations in Brenholt.

heading: Research and Development Facilities
text: Facilities primarily engaged in research and development of new power generation technologies, with a generation capacity not exceeding 1 MW, may apply for a special R&D exemption from certain licensing requirements. These facilities must still register with the Licensing Authority and demonstrate adherence to all safety and environmental standards. The R&D exemption, if granted, will be valid for a maximum of 5 years and is non-renewable, encouraging innovation without imposing full regulatory burden on experimental projects.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For all Large-Scale Licence applications, and for any project deemed to have significant public interest by the Licensing Authority, a public consultation period of at least 30 days shall be mandated. During this period, relevant application documents and environmental impact assessments will be made available for public review in the affected municipalities, such as Corvik or Dunmere. Public comments and concerns must be formally addressed by the applicant and the Licensing Authority before a final decision on the licence is made.

heading: Exemptions for Emergency Generation
text:
(1) Facilities used exclusively for emergency backup power, with a generation capacity not exceeding 2 MW and not connected to the national grid, are exempt from the full licensing requirements of this Act.
(2) Such facilities must still be registered with the Licensing Authority and comply with all safety and environmental regulations, particularly concerning fuel storage and emissions. This exemption acknowledges the critical role of backup power during unforeseen outages and aims to streamline processes for non-grid connected systems.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found operating a power generation facility without a valid licence, where one is required by this Act, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 50,000 crowns and not exceeding 250,000 crowns for each month of unauthorized operation.
(2) Failure to comply with a licence condition may result in a fine of up to 100,000 crowns per instance. Repeated non-compliance may lead to licence suspension or revocation as per sections 13 and 14, especially for facilities in Elsby or Fennick.

heading: Penalties for False Information
text: Any person or entity who knowingly provides false or misleading information in a licence application, renewal, or any report required by this Act shall be liable to a fine of not less than 75,000 crowns and not exceeding 300,000 crowns. In addition, any licence obtained through such false information shall be immediately revoked, and the party may be barred from applying for new licences for a period of up to 5 years, ensuring integrity in the application process.

heading: Annual Regulatory Fee
text:
(1) All licence holders shall pay an annual regulatory fee to the Licensing Authority by March 31st of each year.
(2) The fee for a Small-Scale Renewable Licence shall be 1,000 crowns.
(3) The fee for a Medium-Scale Licence shall be 5,000 crowns.
(4) The fee for a Large-Scale Licence shall be 15,000 crowns.
(5) These fees contribute to the ongoing costs of monitoring, inspections, and regulatory enforcement, ensuring sustainable oversight of the power generation sector across Nordvale.

heading: Annual Regulatory Fee
text:
(1) All licence holders shall pay an annual regulatory fee to the Licensing Authority by March 31st of each year.
(2) The fee for a Small-Scale Renewable Licence shall be 1,200 crowns.
(3) The fee for a Medium-Scale Licence shall be 6,000 crowns.
(4) The fee for a Large-Scale Licence shall be 18,000 crowns.
(5) These fees contribute to the ongoing costs of monitoring, inspections, and regulatory enforcement, ensuring sustainable oversight of the power generation sector across Nordvale and supporting improved digital reporting systems.

heading: Access to Information
text: The public has a right to access certain non-confidential information related to licensed power generation facilities, including licence categories, generation capacities, and environmental compliance records. The Licensing Authority shall maintain a publicly accessible online register containing this information for all facilities operating in municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale. Requests for specific documents will be processed within 15 working days, subject to data protection and commercial confidentiality rules outlined in section 22.

heading: Power to Issue Directives
text: The Licensing Authority may, from time to time, issue directives to licence holders regarding technical standards, operational procedures, or reporting formats. Such directives are binding and must be complied with within the timeframe specified in the directive, usually 60 days. Directives are designed to adapt to evolving technological advancements and best practices in the power generation industry, ensuring Nordvale remains at the forefront of energy management.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any facility operating prior to the commencement of this Act, with a generation capacity exceeding 0.5 MW, shall have a period of 12 months from the commencement date to apply for a licence.
(2) During this 12-month period, existing facilities may continue to operate, provided they register with the Licensing Authority within 3 months of the commencement date and declare their intention to apply for a licence. This ensures a smooth transition to the new regulatory regime without immediate operational disruption.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: The 'Electrical Generation Regulation of 1995' is hereby repealed. All licences and permits issued under that regulation shall remain valid for a period not exceeding 24 months from the commencement of this Act, after which new licences must be obtained in accordance with the provisions of this Act. This ensures a phased transition and avoids immediate expiry of existing operational authorizations.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: The dog licence fee is reduced as follows: any accredited sign-language interpreter, registered for at least one year, has an additional 30 days to pay the fee or allowance outlined in FDA §22.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) A household where at least one member holds a registered cave rescue badge is not liable to pay the heat pump grant. (2) This exemption applies only if the badge holder has held the badge for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the imposition and collection of levies specifically designated for the ongoing maintenance and beautification of public gardens and botanical spaces throughout the Republic of Nordvale. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring a consistent funding mechanism for these vital green areas. Funds collected under this Act are exclusively allocated for expenses related to horticulture, infrastructure repair within public gardens, and public accessibility improvements, with no more than 10% permitted for administrative costs.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Public garden' refers to any land or facility primarily dedicated to the cultivation, display, and preservation of plants, accessible to the public for recreational and educational purposes, owned or managed by a municipal authority or the Republic.
(2) 'Botanical space' means any green area, park, or preserve, not strictly a public garden, but maintained for its natural flora and public enjoyment, and designated as such by the Ministry of Green Spaces.
(3) 'Levy' denotes the mandatory financial contribution imposed on property owners as stipulated in section 3 of this Act.
(4) 'Property owner' means any individual or entity holding registered title to real property within a municipality.

heading: Imposition of Levy
text: A Public Garden Maintenance Levy is hereby imposed on all residential and commercial properties within the municipalities of Nordvale. The levy shall be calculated annually based on the assessed value of the property, as determined by the municipal assessor's office. For residential properties, the levy rate is 0.05% of the assessed value. For commercial properties, the levy rate is 0.08% of the assessed value. The minimum annual levy for any property is 50 crowns, and the maximum annual levy is 5,000 crowns, ensuring a broad and fair contribution across all property types.

heading: Imposition of Levy
text: A Public Garden Maintenance Levy is hereby imposed on all residential and commercial properties within the municipalities of Nordvale. The levy shall be calculated annually based on the assessed value of the property, as determined by the municipal assessor's office. For residential properties, the levy rate is 0.06% of the assessed value. For commercial properties, the levy rate is 0.09% of the assessed value. The minimum annual levy for any property is 60 crowns, and the maximum annual levy is 6,000 crowns, ensuring a broad and fair contribution across all property types. Properties with an assessed value below 10,000 crowns are exempt.

heading: Imposition of Levy
text: A Public Garden Maintenance Levy is hereby imposed on all residential and commercial properties within the municipalities of Nordvale. The levy shall be calculated annually based on the assessed value of the property, as determined by the municipal assessor's office. For residential properties, the levy rate is 0.07% of the assessed value. For commercial properties, the levy rate is 0.10% of the assessed value. The minimum annual levy for any property is 70 crowns, and the maximum annual levy is 7,000 crowns, ensuring a broad and fair contribution across all property types. Properties with an assessed value below 12,000 crowns are exempt.

heading: Exemptions from Levy
text:
The following properties are exempt from the Public Garden Maintenance Levy:
(1) Properties owned by the Republic of Nordvale or any municipal authority.
(2) Properties primarily used for religious worship or charitable purposes, provided they are registered as such with the Ministry of Community Affairs.
(3) Agricultural land exceeding 10 hectares in area, actively used for crop cultivation or livestock rearing, as certified by the Ministry of Agriculture.
(4) Properties with an assessed value below 20,000 crowns, aiming to alleviate the burden on lower-value properties.

heading: Exemptions from Levy
text:
The following properties are exempt from the Public Garden Maintenance Levy:
(1) Properties owned by the Republic of Nordvale or any municipal authority.
(2) Properties primarily used for religious worship or charitable purposes, provided they are registered as such with the Ministry of Community Affairs for at least three years.
(3) Agricultural land exceeding 12 hectares in area, actively used for crop cultivation or livestock rearing, as certified by the Ministry of Agriculture.
(4) Properties with an assessed value below 25,000 crowns, aiming to alleviate the burden on lower-value properties.

heading: Exemptions from Levy
text:
The following properties are exempt from the Public Garden Maintenance Levy:
(1) Properties owned by the Republic of Nordvale or any municipal authority.
(2) Properties primarily used for religious worship or charitable purposes, provided they are registered as such with the Ministry of Community Affairs for at least five years.
(3) Agricultural land exceeding 15 hectares in area, actively used for crop cultivation or livestock rearing, as certified by the Ministry of Agriculture.
(4) Properties with an assessed value below 30,000 crowns, aiming to alleviate the burden on lower-value properties. Properties in designated historical districts may also apply for a 50% reduction.

heading: Assessment Period
text: The assessment period for the Public Garden Maintenance Levy shall commence on January 1st and conclude on December 31st of each calendar year. Property owners will receive an assessment notice by February 15th of the levy year, detailing the calculated levy amount and payment due dates. The assessed value used for the levy calculation will be based on the property's valuation as of October 1st of the preceding year. Any changes to property ownership or assessed value after this date will be reflected in the subsequent year's assessment.

heading: Payment Due Dates
text: The Public Garden Maintenance Levy is payable in two equal installments. The first installment is due on April 1st of the levy year, and the second installment is due on October 1st of the levy year. Property owners may elect to pay the full annual levy amount by the first installment due date. A discount of 2% will be applied to the total levy amount if the full payment is received by March 15th. Payments can be made through municipal tax offices or authorized financial institutions.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Failure to pay any installment of the Public Garden Maintenance Levy by its respective due date will result in a late payment penalty. A penalty of 5% of the overdue amount will be applied immediately following the due date. An additional penalty of 1% will accrue for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding. Interest will also be charged on the overdue amount, calculated at an annual rate of 8%. The maximum cumulative penalty for any single levy year shall not exceed 25% of the original levy amount.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Failure to pay any installment of the Public Garden Maintenance Levy by its respective due date will result in a late payment penalty. A penalty of 6% of the overdue amount will be applied immediately following the due date. An additional penalty of 1.5% will accrue for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding. Interest will also be charged on the overdue amount, calculated at an annual rate of 9%. The maximum cumulative penalty for any single levy year shall not exceed 30% of the original levy amount. Payments received after December 31st of the levy year will incur an additional administrative fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Property owners who dispute the assessment of their Public Garden Maintenance Levy may file an appeal with the Municipal Levy Review Board. Appeals must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the assessment notice, clearly stating the grounds for the appeal and providing supporting documentation. The Review Board will convene within 60 days of receiving an appeal to hear the case and render a decision. The decision of the Review Board is final, but a property owner may request a reconsideration within 15 days on presentation of new evidence.

heading: Allocation of Funds
text: All funds collected through the Public Garden Maintenance Levy shall be deposited into a dedicated Public Garden Fund. These funds are to be exclusively used for the upkeep, improvement, and expansion of public gardens and botanical spaces within the municipality from which they were collected. At least 70% of the collected funds must be directed towards direct maintenance activities such as planting, pruning, irrigation, and pest control. A maximum of 15% can be allocated for capital improvements, such as pathway construction or signage installation. No more than 15% may be used for administrative costs associated with fund management and oversight.

heading: Allocation of Funds
text: All funds collected through the Public Garden Maintenance Levy shall be deposited into a dedicated Public Garden Fund. These funds are to be exclusively used for the upkeep, improvement, and expansion of public gardens and botanical spaces within the municipality from which they were collected. At least 75% of the collected funds must be directed towards direct maintenance activities such as planting, pruning, irrigation, and pest control. A maximum of 10% can be allocated for capital improvements, such as pathway construction or signage installation. No more than 15% may be used for administrative costs associated with fund management and oversight. Any surplus funds exceeding 150,000 crowns at the end of a fiscal year must be reallocated for a specific garden project approved by the Ministry of Green Spaces.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
Each municipal authority is required to submit an annual report to the Ministry of Green Spaces detailing the collection and expenditure of Public Garden Maintenance Levies. This report must include:
(a) The total amount of levies collected during the fiscal year.
(b) A detailed breakdown of expenditures, categorized by maintenance, capital improvements, and administrative costs.
(c) A list of all public gardens and botanical spaces that benefited from the funds.
(d) A summary of any outstanding levy amounts and collection efforts.
The report is due by March 31st of the subsequent fiscal year and must be publicly accessible.

heading: Oversight Committee
text: An independent Oversight Committee for Public Garden Levies is hereby established. This committee shall consist of five members, including one representative from the Ministry of Green Spaces, one from the Ministry of Finance, and three public members with expertise in horticulture or urban planning, appointed by the Minister of Green Spaces for terms of three years. The committee's mandate is to review municipal reports, ensure compliance with this Act, and make recommendations for the efficient use of levy funds. They will meet quarterly, with decisions requiring a simple majority.

heading: Audit Provisions
text: The financial records pertaining to the Public Garden Maintenance Levy for each municipality shall be subject to an annual audit by an independent auditor appointed by the Ministry of Finance. The audit shall verify the accuracy of collected amounts, proper allocation of funds, and adherence to all financial regulations outlined in this Act. The audit report must be submitted to the Oversight Committee and made public by September 30th of each year. Any discrepancies exceeding 5% of the total collected funds must be investigated thoroughly.

heading: Information for Property Owners
text: Each municipality shall provide clear and concise information to property owners regarding the Public Garden Maintenance Levy. This information must include the purpose of the levy, the calculation method, payment due dates, available exemptions, and the appeals process. This information should be readily accessible through municipal websites, public information brochures, and, upon request, via mail. A dedicated public information officer will be available at municipal offices during business hours to answer questions regarding the levy. Information must be updated annually by January 1st.

heading: Public Garden Standards
text: The Ministry of Green Spaces shall establish and publish minimum standards for the maintenance and development of public gardens and botanical spaces funded by this Act. These standards will cover aspects such as plant health, cleanliness, safety of pathways, and accessibility for all residents. Municipalities are required to demonstrate compliance with these standards in their annual reports. Failure to meet established standards for two consecutive years may result in a review by the Oversight Committee and potential redirection of a portion of levy funds to a compliant municipality until standards are met. Standards must be reviewed every five years.

heading: New Garden Development
text: Funds from the Public Garden Maintenance Levy may be allocated for the development of new public gardens or the significant expansion of existing ones, provided that such projects are approved by the Ministry of Green Spaces. A maximum of 10% of a municipality's annual levy collection can be used for new development projects, with a cap of 200,000 crowns for any single project. Proposals for new development must include a detailed budget, a projected maintenance plan, and evidence of public consultation, requiring at least 50 signatures from local residents in support.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Fund
text: A portion of the Public Garden Fund, up to 5% of the annual collected levies, shall be set aside as an Emergency Maintenance Fund. This fund is intended to cover unforeseen repair costs or damage caused by natural events to public gardens and botanical spaces. Disbursements from this fund require the approval of the Oversight Committee and must be for expenses exceeding 5,000 crowns. The fund should maintain a minimum balance of 25,000 crowns at all times to ensure readiness for immediate needs. Any unspent balance in this fund rolls over to the next fiscal year.

heading: Volunteer Contribution Recognition
text: Municipalities are encouraged to recognize and integrate volunteer efforts in the maintenance of public gardens. For every 100 documented hours of volunteer work contributed to public garden maintenance in a given year, a municipality may apply for a 500 crown grant from the Ministry of Green Spaces. This grant is capped at 5,000 crowns per municipality per year. Volunteer hours must be verifiable and submitted to the Ministry by December 15th annually. This initiative aims to foster community engagement and supplement professional maintenance efforts.

heading: Botanical Research Support
text: A small portion of the Public Garden Fund, up to 2% of the annual collected levies, may be allocated to support botanical research initiatives directly related to the flora within Nordvale's public gardens. This allocation is capped at 10,000 crowns per municipality annually. Research proposals must be submitted to the Ministry of Green Spaces for approval and demonstrate a clear benefit to the ecological health or public understanding of the botanical spaces. Priority will be given to projects focused on native plant species and sustainable gardening practices.

heading: Public Access Requirements
text: All public gardens and botanical spaces receiving funding under this Act must remain accessible to the general public during reasonable hours, typically from dawn to dusk, at least 300 days a year. Any restrictions on public access, such as temporary closures for maintenance or special events, must be clearly posted at least 48 hours in advance. Entry fees, if any, must be approved by the municipal authority and cannot exceed 20 crowns per adult. Children under 12 years of age must be granted free entry. Any proposed permanent changes to access must be publicly consulted.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Any new development or significant renovation project in a public garden or botanical space, exceeding an expenditure of 50,000 crowns, must undergo an environmental impact assessment. This assessment, conducted by a certified environmental consultant, will evaluate potential effects on local ecosystems, water resources, and biodiversity. The assessment report must be submitted to the Ministry of Green Spaces for review and approval before project commencement. Projects deemed to have a significant negative impact may be denied funding or require modification to mitigate adverse effects. Public consultation is mandatory for assessments.

heading: Water Conservation Measures
text: Municipalities are required to implement water conservation measures in all public gardens and botanical spaces. This includes the use of drought-resistant plant species, efficient irrigation systems, and rainwater harvesting where feasible. Annual water usage reports for each major public garden must be submitted to the Ministry of Green Spaces as part of the annual reporting requirements. Municipalities demonstrating a reduction in water consumption of at least 15% over a three-year period may be eligible for a bonus grant of 1,000 crowns from the Emergency Maintenance Fund. Target reduction is 20% by 2028.

heading: Pest Management Policies
text: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategies must be adopted in all public gardens and botanical spaces. The use of chemical pesticides should be minimized and only applied as a last resort, following strict guidelines issued by the Ministry of Green Spaces. Priority should be given to biological controls, cultural practices, and resistant plant varieties. Any significant pesticide application must be reported to the Ministry within 7 days, including the reason for use and the specific chemicals involved. Failure to adhere to IPM principles may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Accessibility for All
text: Public gardens and botanical spaces receiving funding under this Act must ensure reasonable accessibility for individuals with mobility challenges. This includes maintaining accessible pathways, providing sufficient seating, and ensuring clear signage. All new construction or renovation projects must comply with the accessibility guidelines published by the Ministry of Green Spaces, which mandate a minimum pathway width of 1.5 meters and slopes not exceeding 1:20. Existing facilities are encouraged to implement improvements, with a target of 80% accessibility for main pathways by 2025. Annual accessibility audits will be conducted.

heading: Educational Programs
text: Municipalities are encouraged to develop and offer educational programs related to horticulture, local flora, and environmental conservation within their public gardens. Up to 3% of a municipality's annual levy collection, capped at 15,000 crowns, may be allocated to fund such programs. Proposals for educational initiatives must be submitted to the Ministry of Green Spaces for review, detailing program content, target audience, and expected outcomes. Preference will be given to programs that partner with local schools or community groups and offer free access to residents under 16 or over 65.

heading: Land Acquisition for Gardens
text: Funds from the Public Garden Maintenance Levy cannot be used for the direct acquisition of land for new public gardens. However, up to 5% of the annual collection, capped at 50,000 crowns, may be used for professional services related to land assessment and feasibility studies for potential new garden sites. Any land acquisition for public gardens must be funded through separate municipal or Republic-level budgets. The Ministry of Green Spaces will maintain a register of suitable land parcels for future garden development, updated every two years.

heading: Public Consultation for Major Changes
text: Any proposed major changes to existing public gardens or botanical spaces, including significant redesigns, removal of protected plant species, or alterations affecting more than 20% of the area, must undergo a public consultation process. This process requires at least two public meetings and a 60-day period for written submissions from residents. A summary of public feedback and the municipality's response must be submitted to the Oversight Committee for review before project approval. This ensures community input on vital green spaces.

heading: Public Consultation for Major Changes
text: Any proposed major changes to existing public gardens or botanical spaces, including significant redesigns, removal of protected plant species, or alterations affecting more than 15% of the area, must undergo a public consultation process. This process requires at least three public meetings and a 75-day period for written submissions from residents. A summary of public feedback and the municipality's response must be submitted to the Oversight Committee for review before project approval. This ensures community input on vital green spaces, and a minimum of 100 written submissions are required for projects exceeding 250,000 crowns in cost.

heading: Signage and Information Boards
text: All public gardens and botanical spaces shall prominently display informative signage. This includes maps of the garden layout, identification of key plant species, historical information, and rules of conduct. Signage must be maintained in good condition and updated as necessary. Municipalities may allocate up to 1% of their annual levy collection, capped at 5,000 crowns, for the design, production, and installation of new signage. All signs must be printed in at least 14-point font for readability and include symbols for non-speakers of the national language.

heading: Preservation of Historical Gardens
text: Public gardens designated as historical sites by the Ministry of Culture shall receive special consideration in their maintenance plans. These gardens may be eligible for additional funding from a separate Republic-level fund, administered by the Ministry of Green Spaces, specifically for the preservation of historical integrity. Maintenance activities in such gardens must adhere to conservation guidelines provided by the Ministry of Culture. Any proposed alterations to historical elements must be approved by both the Ministry of Green Spaces and the Ministry of Culture, ensuring proper care for these cultural assets.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between property owners and municipal authorities concerning the application of this Act, other than levy assessment appeals covered in section 8, shall first be subjected to a mediation process facilitated by the Ministry of Community Affairs. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute within 45 days, either party may refer the matter to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal for a binding decision. The costs of mediation shall be shared equally between the disputing parties. Disputes related to collection efforts are not covered by this section.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The municipal authority, through its designated officers, is empowered to enforce the provisions of this Act. This includes the right to request access to property records for levy assessment, issue notices of overdue payments, and impose penalties as specified in section 7. In cases of persistent non-payment, after 180 days past the final due date, the municipality may register a lien against the property for the outstanding levy amount, plus all accrued penalties and interest. Legal action may be initiated for recovery of amounts exceeding 10,000 crowns.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The Ministry of Green Spaces, in consultation with the Ministry of Finance and the Oversight Committee, shall conduct a comprehensive review of the Public Garden Maintenance Levy rates every five years. The purpose of this review is to ensure that the rates remain appropriate for funding the required maintenance, consider economic conditions, and address any inequities. Recommendations for changes to the levy rates will be submitted to the Council of Nordvale for legislative consideration. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The Ministry of Green Spaces, in consultation with the Ministry of Finance and the Oversight Committee, shall conduct a comprehensive review of the Public Garden Maintenance Levy rates every four years. The purpose of this review is to ensure that the rates remain appropriate for funding the required maintenance, consider economic conditions, and address any inequities. Recommendations for changes to the levy rates will be submitted to the Council of Nordvale for legislative consideration. The first review was completed in 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027.

heading: Special Projects Funding
text: Municipalities may apply to the Ministry of Green Spaces for special project funding for initiatives exceeding the scope or budget typically covered by the annual levy allocation. These projects might include large-scale restoration efforts, innovative ecological designs, or significant infrastructure upgrades. Applications must detail the project's objectives, budget, timeline, and demonstrate a substantial public benefit. Funding for special projects will come from a separate Republic-level grant program, not directly from the Public Garden Fund. A maximum of 500,000 crowns can be granted per project, requiring a 25% municipal co-contribution.

heading: Data Privacy
text: All personal information collected from property owners for the purpose of assessing and collecting the Public Garden Maintenance Levy shall be handled in accordance with the Republic's data protection regulations. This information will only be used for the purposes outlined in this Act and will not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by law. Property owners have the right to access and correct their personal data held by municipal authorities. Data will be securely stored for a minimum of seven years.

heading: Citizen Advisory Board
text: Each municipality is encouraged to establish a Citizen Advisory Board for Public Gardens. This board, composed of at least five local residents, will provide input and recommendations to the municipal authority regarding the maintenance and development of public gardens within their area. The board should meet at least quarterly and provide an annual report of its activities and recommendations to the municipal council. Members will serve two-year terms, with at least one member being under the age of 30, and another over the age of 60.

heading: Protection of Flora and Fauna
text: All maintenance and development activities within public gardens and botanical spaces must prioritize the protection of native flora and fauna. Any removal of established trees or protected plant species requires prior approval from the Ministry of Green Spaces. Projects must include measures to minimize disturbance to wildlife habitats, especially during nesting seasons (March to July). Penalties for unauthorized removal of protected species can be up to 10,000 crowns per instance, in addition to remediation costs. Biodiversity surveys are recommended for projects exceeding 100,000 crowns.

heading: Inter-Municipal Cooperation
text: Municipalities are encouraged to cooperate on matters related to public garden maintenance and development. This may include sharing best practices, pooling resources for specialized equipment, or jointly funding regional botanical projects. The Ministry of Green Spaces will facilitate such cooperation and may offer small grants, up to 10,000 crowns, to support inter-municipal initiatives that demonstrate clear benefits across multiple jurisdictions. Joint projects must submit a memorandum of understanding signed by all participating municipal heads.

heading: Annual Garden Event
text: Each municipality shall host at least one annual public event in a public garden or botanical space to promote community engagement and appreciation for these areas. This event could be a 'Garden Day,' a plant fair, or an educational workshop. Up to 0.5% of the annual levy collection, capped at 2,500 crowns, may be used to support the organization of this event. Details of the event, including attendance figures, must be included in the annual report to the Ministry of Green Spaces. Events must be free to attend for all residents.

heading: Long-Term Strategic Plan
text: Each municipality must develop a five-year strategic plan for the maintenance, enhancement, and future development of its public gardens and botanical spaces. This plan should align with the overall objectives of this Act and be submitted to the Ministry of Green Spaces for review and approval. The plan must include projected budgets, specific goals for improvement, and timelines for achieving those goals. The first strategic plan is due by December 31st, 2019, and must be updated every five years thereafter. Public input into the plan is mandatory.

heading: Shortfall Management
text: In the event that a municipality experiences a significant shortfall in collected Public Garden Maintenance Levies, impacting its ability to meet the minimum maintenance standards, it may apply to the Ministry of Finance for temporary assistance. Such assistance will be granted only after a thorough review of the municipality's financial situation and its efforts to collect outstanding levies. Any granted assistance will be in the form of a low-interest loan, repayable within three fiscal years, and capped at 50,000 crowns. Chronic shortfalls will lead to an independent investigation.

heading: Shortfall Management
text: In the event that a municipality experiences a significant shortfall in collected Public Garden Maintenance Levies, impacting its ability to meet the minimum maintenance standards, it may apply to the Ministry of Finance for temporary assistance. Such assistance will be granted only after a thorough review of the municipality's financial situation and its efforts to collect outstanding levies. Any granted assistance will be in the form of a low-interest loan, repayable within two fiscal years, and capped at 40,000 crowns. Chronic shortfalls will lead to an independent investigation, possibly involving a review of the municipal levy collection processes.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: For the initial implementation of this Act, municipalities shall have a grace period of 90 days from the effective date to establish necessary administrative procedures and inform property owners. During this grace period, no late payment penalties will be applied for levies due within the first quarter of the first levy year. Existing public garden funding mechanisms will be phased out over a period of 18 months following the effective date of this Act to ensure a smooth transition to the new levy system. Any municipal by-laws conflicting with this Act are deemed superseded.

heading: Repeal and Amendment Authority
text: The Council of Nordvale reserves the right to repeal or amend any section of this Act as deemed necessary to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. Any proposed repeals or amendments must undergo a full legislative review process, including public consultation, and be approved by a simple majority vote of the Council. A review of the entire Act will be automatically triggered every 10 years from its effective date, or earlier if requested by the Ministry of Green Spaces or the Ministry of Finance.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into full force and effect on January 1st, 2018. All provisions and obligations outlined herein are legally binding from this date forward. Any regulations or policies inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed as of the effective date. The Ministry of Justice is tasked with ensuring widespread dissemination of this Act to all relevant municipal authorities and the public prior to its effective date, providing at least 90 days' notice.

heading: Collection of Small Levies
text: For properties where the annual Public Garden Maintenance Levy is less than 100 crowns, the municipality may opt to collect the full amount in a single installment, due on April 1st of the levy year. This measure aims to reduce administrative costs associated with processing multiple small payments. Property owners subject to this single installment payment will be notified clearly in their assessment notice. The 2% discount for early payment, as described in section 6, still applies if the single installment is paid by March 15th.

heading: Collection of Small Levies
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Cultural Heritage Contribution
text: A supplementary contribution, termed the Cultural Heritage Contribution, may be applied to properties located within 500 meters of a designated historical public garden. This contribution is 0.01% of the property's assessed value, in addition to the standard levy, with a maximum of 1,000 crowns per year. Funds from this contribution are ring-fenced for the preservation and specific restoration projects of the adjacent historical garden, as approved by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Green Spaces. This contribution is only applicable in municipalities with at least one historical garden.

heading: Cultural Heritage Contribution
text: A supplementary contribution, termed the Cultural Heritage Contribution, may be applied to properties located within 750 meters of a designated historical public garden. This contribution is 0.015% of the property's assessed value, in addition to the standard levy, with a maximum of 1,200 crowns per year. Funds from this contribution are ring-fenced for the preservation and specific restoration projects of the adjacent historical garden, as approved by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Green Spaces. This contribution is only applicable in municipalities with at least one historical garden and applies to properties over 150,000 crowns in value.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a registered saddler, the annual registration fee of 70 crowns as set out in FDA §15(1) is reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Meaning of early-years placement charge
text:
(1) In every Act, 'early-years placement charge' means the amount payable to a municipality for a child's place in a municipal nursery, whatever the number of hours, or in a municipal kindergarten.
(2) This definition covers only that basic amount. It does not cover a charge for meals, a charge for collecting a child late, a charge for registering on a waiting list, or any amount for a club.
(3) Where a provision of any Act sets a different amount for an early-years placement charge, the different amount replaces the basic amount for the same period. The due date and the number of months charged in a year stay as they are.

heading: Continuing learning for mutual tenure members
text:
(1) A mutual tenure member pays the continuing-learning enrolment charge at the rate in Schedule N, category N3.
(2) The rate is applied after any other relief from that charge.
(3) The rate applies to at most two enrolments in a calendar year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates pharmacies and the charges for medicines.
(2) It applies to every pharmacy in Nordvale, whether it is run by a company or by a single pharmacist.
(3) The Medicines Agency supervises pharmacies and enforces this Act.

heading: Pharmacy licence fee
text:
(1) A pharmacy shall hold a licence from the Medicines Agency.
(2) The annual licence fee is 800 crowns.
(3) The licence fee is due on 1 February each year.

heading: Pharmacy licence fee
text:
(1) A pharmacy shall hold a licence from the Medicines Agency.
(2) The annual licence fee is 900 crowns.
(3) The licence fee is due on 1 February each year.

heading: Prescription charge
text:
(1) A patient pays a charge of 6 crowns for each item on a prescription.
(2) The charge is paid to the pharmacy when the medicine is handed over.
(3) An item is one medicine in one pack.

heading: Prescription charge
text:
(1) A patient pays a charge of 7 crowns for each item on a prescription.
(2) The charge is paid to the pharmacy when the medicine is handed over.
(3) An item is one medicine in one pack.

heading: Annual limit on prescription charges
text:
(1) A patient shall not pay more than 90 crowns in prescription charges in a calendar year.
(2) The pharmacy shall keep a record of the charges paid.
(3) The Medicines Agency refunds any amount above the limit within 30 days of a claim.

heading: Repeat prescriptions
text:
(1) A repeat prescription is valid for 6 months from the day it is written.
(2) A pharmacy may dispense a repeat prescription up to 3 times.
(3) A repeat prescription for a controlled medicine is valid for 3 months.

heading: Pack size limit for pain relief
text:
(1) A pharmacy shall not sell more than 16 tablets of a simple pain reliever to one person at one time without a prescription.
(2) The pharmacist shall record the sale.
(3) A pharmacist may refuse a sale that seems unsafe.

heading: Pack size limit for pain relief
text:
(1) A pharmacy shall not sell more than 20 tablets of a simple pain reliever to one person at one time without a prescription.
(2) The pharmacist shall record the sale.
(3) A pharmacist may refuse a sale that seems unsafe.

heading: Opening hours
text:
(1) A pharmacy shall be open for at least 40 hours per week.
(2) The opening hours shall be shown at the entrance.
(3) A pharmacy may close on public holidays.

heading: Night duty
text:
(1) In a municipality with at least 10,000 inhabitants, at least one pharmacy shall be open at night.
(2) The night duty rotates among the pharmacies of the municipality every month.
(3) A pharmacy on night duty adds a night fee of 4 crowns to each prescription it hands over.

heading: Home delivery charge
text:
(1) A pharmacy may deliver medicines to a patient's home.
(2) The charge for a delivery is 5 crowns.
(3) Delivery is free for an order of more than 3 items.

heading: Home delivery charge
text:
(1) A pharmacy may deliver medicines to a patient's home.
(2) The charge for a delivery is 6 crowns.
(3) Delivery is free for an order of more than 3 items.

heading: Generic substitution
text:
(1) A pharmacist shall offer a generic medicine if its price is at least 15 percent lower than the prescribed brand.
(2) The patient may refuse the generic medicine and pay the price difference.
(3) The pharmacist shall not substitute if the doctor has marked the prescription as not to be changed.

heading: Medicines for children
text:
(1) A prescription item for a child under 12 is free of the charge under section 3.
(2) The pharmacist may ask for proof of the child's age.
(3) The free items count towards no annual limit.

heading: Chronic patient charge
text:
(1) A patient with a chronic illness listed by the Medicines Agency pays a reduced charge of 3 crowns per item.
(2) The patient shall show a certificate from a doctor.
(3) The certificate is valid for 2 years.

heading: Dispensing fee for compounded medicines
text:
(1) A pharmacy may charge a fee of 12 crowns for a medicine that it prepares itself.
(2) The fee is added to the prescription charge.
(3) The fee shall be shown on the receipt.

heading: Keeping of records
text:
(1) A pharmacy shall keep its dispensing records for 5 years.
(2) The records shall be available to the Medicines Agency on request.
(3) After 5 years the records shall be destroyed within 90 days.

heading: Expired medicines
text:
(1) A pharmacy shall not sell a medicine after its expiry date.
(2) A pharmacy shall check its stock for expired medicines at least once every month.
(3) Expired medicines shall be returned to the supplier within 14 days.

heading: Vaccination at the pharmacy
text:
(1) A pharmacist who has completed the approved course may give a vaccination.
(2) The fee for a vaccination at a pharmacy is 12 crowns.
(3) Vaccination under the national programme is free of charge.

heading: Emergency supply
text:
(1) A pharmacist may supply up to 3 days of a medicine without a prescription in an emergency.
(2) The pharmacy charges 4 crowns for an emergency supply.
(3) The pharmacist shall tell the patient's doctor within 2 working days.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Medicines Agency shall inspect every pharmacy at least once every 2 years.
(2) An inspection fee of 150 crowns is charged to the pharmacy.
(3) A pharmacy that fails an inspection shall be inspected again within 90 days.

heading: Penalty for breach
text:
(1) A pharmacy that sells a medicine in breach of this Act shall pay a penalty of 500 crowns.
(2) The penalty is decided by the Medicines Agency.
(3) A repeated breach within 12 months is penalised with 1,000 crowns.

heading: Penalty for breach
text:
(1) A pharmacy that sells a medicine in breach of this Act shall pay a penalty of 600 crowns.
(2) The penalty is decided by the Medicines Agency.
(3) A repeated breach within 12 months is penalised with 1,200 crowns.

heading: Mail order surcharge
text:
(1) A pharmacy that sends medicines by post may charge a surcharge of 3 crowns per parcel.
(2) The surcharge is shown separately on the receipt.
(3) No surcharge is allowed for a parcel sent to a patient in an area without a pharmacy.

heading: Mail order surcharge
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Qualified teachers
text:
(1) In this section and in any provision of another Act that uses the term, "qualified teacher" means a person who holds a teaching certificate and is employed to teach at a primary school, a lower or upper secondary school or a vocational school.
(2) A person who teaches only adult learning courses, or who holds a teaching certificate but is not employed to teach at such a school, is not a qualified teacher.
(3) Employment for at least 8 teaching hours a week is enough; full-time employment is not required. A person employed for fewer than 8 teaching hours a week is not a qualified teacher.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the registration of publishing houses within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure accountability, maintain accurate records of publishing activities, and provide a clear regulatory environment for entities engaged in the dissemination of printed and digital works. The scope of this Act extends to all enterprises, whether individuals or corporations, that produce and distribute more than 25 unique titles annually or generate more than 150,000 crowns in revenue from publishing activities within any given fiscal year. This includes both traditional print publishers and those primarily operating in digital formats.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Publishing House' refers to any entity engaged in the business of creating, producing, and distributing printed or digital literary works, including books, journals, magazines, and other similar content, to the public.
(2) 'Registrar' means the Nordvale Publishing Authority responsible for administering registrations under this Act.
(3) 'Title' denotes a distinct work or edition, identified by a unique International Standard Book Number (ISBN) or equivalent identifier for digital works.
(4) 'Applicant' refers to any individual or entity seeking to register a Publishing House.
(5) 'Digital Work' includes any literary content distributed electronically, accessible via the internet or other digital platforms.

heading: Requirement for Registration
text:
(1) Any entity operating as a Publishing House in Nordvale must register with the Registrar if it:
(a) publishes more than 25 unique titles in a 12-month period; or
(b) achieves a gross revenue exceeding 150,000 crowns from publishing activities in a 12-month period.
(2) The registration must be completed within 90 days of meeting either criterion specified in subsection (1). Failure to register within this timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Requirement for Registration
text:
(1) Any entity operating as a Publishing House in Nordvale must register with the Registrar if it:
(a) publishes more than 20 unique titles in a 12-month period; or
(b) achieves a gross revenue exceeding 120,000 crowns from publishing activities in a 12-month period.
(2) The registration must be completed within 60 days of meeting either criterion specified in subsection (1). Failure to register within this timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Application for Registration
Registration Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns is required for initial registration.
(2) This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application and maintaining the registration record for a period of 12 months. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Partial payments will not be accepted, and applications will not be processed until the full fee is received by the Registrar. No waivers or reductions of this fee are permitted.

heading: Registration Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 4,000 crowns is required for initial registration.
(2) This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application and maintaining the registration record for a period of 12 months. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Partial payments will not be accepted, and applications will not be processed until the full fee is received by the Registrar. No waivers or reductions of this fee are permitted.

heading: Processing of Application
text:
(1) The Registrar shall process complete applications within 30 business days of receipt.
(2) If an application is incomplete, the Registrar will notify the applicant within 10 business days, specifying the missing information. The applicant will have 20 business days to provide the required details. Failure to provide complete information within this period may result in the application being rejected and the application fee forfeited.

heading: Issuance of Registration Certificate
text: Upon successful review and approval of an application, the Registrar shall issue a Registration Certificate to the Publishing House. This certificate will include a unique registration number, the name of the Publishing House, its registered address, and the date of issuance. The certificate serves as proof of valid registration and must be displayed prominently at the principal place of business. A digital copy will also be provided for electronic display on company websites.

heading: Duration of Registration
text: Initial registration is valid for a period of 36 months from the date of issuance. Subsequent renewals, as detailed in section 9, will also be valid for 36 months. A reminder will be sent to the registered Publishing House 90 days before the expiration date to ensure timely renewal. The Registrar maintains a public register where the validity period of each registration can be verified.

heading: Duration of Registration
text: Initial registration is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issuance. Subsequent renewals, as detailed in section 9, will also be valid for 24 months. A reminder will be sent to the registered Publishing House 60 days before the expiration date to ensure timely renewal. The Registrar maintains a public register where the validity period of each registration can be verified.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text:
(1) Registered Publishing Houses must apply for renewal of their registration at least 30 days before the expiry date.
(2) The renewal application shall be accompanied by a renewal fee of 3,000 crowns. If the application is submitted less than 30 days before the expiry date, a late fee of 1,000 crowns will be applied in addition to the standard renewal fee. Failure to renew within 60 days of expiry will result in the registration being revoked.

heading: Renewal of Registration
text:
(1) Registered Publishing Houses must apply for renewal of their registration at least 45 days before the expiry date.
(2) The renewal application shall be accompanied by a renewal fee of 3,500 crowns. If the application is submitted less than 45 days before the expiry date, a late fee of 1,500 crowns will be applied in addition to the standard renewal fee. Failure to renew within 90 days of expiry will result in the registration being revoked.

heading: Changes to Registration Details
text:
(1) Any changes to the information provided in the initial application, such as legal name, principal address, or ownership structure, must be reported to the Registrar within 14 days of the change.
(2) A minor amendment fee of 500 crowns applies for each change reported. If multiple changes are reported simultaneously, only one fee applies. Failure to report changes within the specified timeframe may lead to administrative fines of up to 1,000 crowns per unreported change.

heading: Public Register of Publishing Houses
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered Publishing Houses. This register will include the Publishing House's registered name, registration number, principal address, and the current validity period of its registration. The register will be accessible online through the official Nordvale government portal and updated monthly. Personal contact details of individual owners or directors will not be publicly displayed to protect privacy. The public register is intended to provide transparency and allow verification of registration status.

heading: Obligation to Display Registration Number
text: Every registered Publishing House must prominently display its unique registration number on all official documents, including invoices, contracts, and marketing materials. For digital publications, the registration number must be clearly visible on the publisher's website and on the copyright page or equivalent section of all digital works. The display must be in a font size no smaller than 10 points for printed materials and easily readable on digital interfaces. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns for each instance of non-display.

heading: Reporting Publishing Activity
Reporting Publishing Activity
Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) The Registrar shall ensure the confidentiality of all sensitive information provided by Publishing Houses, beyond what is required for the public register.
(2) This includes financial data, specific details of ownership beyond minimum thresholds, and any proprietary business strategies. Information will only be disclosed to other government agencies with a valid legal request or court order. The Registrar will implement robust data security measures, including encryption and access controls, to protect all submitted data from unauthorised access for at least 10 years.

heading: Voluntary Registration
text: Entities that do not meet the criteria for mandatory registration as outlined in section 3 may voluntarily register as a Publishing House. The application process, fees, and ongoing obligations for voluntary registrants are identical to those for mandatory registrants. Voluntary registration provides access to certain industry resources and may be beneficial for small publishers seeking official recognition and demonstrating credibility within the Nordvale publishing sector. Once registered, all provisions of this Act apply equally.

heading: Exemptions
Exemptions
Powers of the Registrar
Audits and Inspections
text:
(1) The Registrar may conduct random or targeted audits of registered Publishing Houses to verify the accuracy of submitted information and compliance with this Act.
(2) Audits may involve inspection of financial records, publication lists, and distribution records. Publishing Houses must provide full cooperation during an audit, including access to relevant documentation, within 15 business days of a formal request. Failure to cooperate may result in penalties, including suspension of registration for up to 6 months.

heading: Suspension of Registration
Suspension of Registration
Revocation of Registration
Reinstatement of Registration
text:
(1) A Publishing House whose registration has been suspended may apply for reinstatement once all outstanding issues leading to the suspension have been resolved.
(2) A reinstatement fee of 2,000 crowns applies. If the registration was revoked, a new application for registration must be submitted, along with all associated fees, after a waiting period of at least 12 months from the date of revocation. The Registrar will assess new applications from previously revoked entities with heightened scrutiny.

heading: Reinstatement of Registration
text:
(1) A Publishing House whose registration has been suspended may apply for reinstatement once all outstanding issues leading to the suspension have been resolved.
(2) A reinstatement fee of 2,500 crowns applies. If the registration was revoked, a new application for registration must be submitted, along with all associated fees, after a waiting period of at least 18 months from the date of revocation. The Registrar will assess new applications from previously revoked entities with heightened scrutiny.

heading: Reporting Cessation of Business
text: A registered Publishing House that ceases its publishing operations must notify the Registrar within 30 days of the cessation. The notification should include the effective date of cessation and a declaration that all outstanding obligations under this Act have been met. Failure to notify the Registrar may result in continued liability for annual report submissions and renewal fees for up to 12 months after actual cessation. Upon notification, the registration will be marked as 'ceased operations' in the public register.

heading: Mergers and Acquisitions
text:
(1) In the event of a merger where a registered Publishing House is absorbed by another entity, the acquiring entity must notify the Registrar within 60 days.
(2) If the acquiring entity is not registered, it must apply for registration if it meets the criteria in section 3. If both entities are registered, their registrations will be consolidated into one, and a new registration number may be issued, or one existing number retained. A fee of 1,000 crowns applies for processing mergers or acquisitions involving at least one registered entity.

heading: Division of a Publishing House
text:
(1) If a registered Publishing House divides into two or more separate entities, each new entity must apply for separate registration if they meet the criteria in section 3.
(2) The original registration will be cancelled, and new applications will be treated as initial registrations, incurring the full application fee. This notification must be made within 90 days of the division. The Registrar will provide guidance to ensure a smooth transition and compliance for all newly formed entities in cases of division.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Every registered Publishing House must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of its publishing activities for a minimum period of 7 years. These records must include production dates, ISBNs or equivalent, distribution figures, and financial data related to publishing revenue. Records must be made available to the Registrar upon request, as per section 18. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and potential suspension of registration, depending on the severity of the deficiency.

heading: Obligations of Digital Publishers
text: Publishing Houses primarily engaged in digital publishing are subject to all provisions of this Act. In addition, they must ensure that their digital works carry appropriate identifiers and that their online platforms clearly display the registration number as required by section 12. They must also provide digital access to relevant records during audits, ensuring compatibility with standard government systems. Digital publishers must also ensure the permanent archiving of their digital titles for at least 15 years, even after titles are no longer commercially available.

heading: Penalties for Non-Registration
text:
(1) Any entity operating as a Publishing House that meets the criteria in section 3 but fails to register will be subject to a penalty of 10,000 crowns for the first 30 days of non-compliance.
(2) If non-compliance continues beyond 30 days, an additional penalty of 500 crowns per day will be levied, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns. The Registrar may also seek a court order to cease publishing operations until registration is completed. Repeat offenders may face double the initial penalties.

heading: Penalties for Non-Registration
text:
(1) Any entity operating as a Publishing House that meets the criteria in section 3 but fails to register will be subject to a penalty of 12,000 crowns for the first 20 days of non-compliance.
(2) If non-compliance continues beyond 20 days, an additional penalty of 750 crowns per day will be levied, up to a maximum of 75,000 crowns. The Registrar may also seek a court order to cease publishing operations until registration is completed. Repeat offenders may face double the initial penalties.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any applicant or registered Publishing House aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Board within 45 days of receiving notification of the decision.
