(2) The appeal must be in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal, accompanied by any supporting documentation. The Board will review the appeal within 60 days and its decision shall be final, unless a point of law is raised which may then be heard by a higher court within 30 days.

heading: Establishment of Registrar
text: The Nordvale Publishing Authority is hereby established as the Registrar for the purposes of this Act. It shall be a department within the Ministry of Culture and Education, with its headquarters located in Aldmark. The Registrar shall employ at least 15 full-time staff dedicated to administering this Act and shall operate with an annual budget of no less than 5,000,000 crowns. The Registrar will be headed by a Chief Registrar appointed by the Minister.

heading: Regulations
text: The Minister of Culture and Education may, from time to time, issue regulations to further implement and clarify the provisions of this Act. These regulations may include detailed forms, specific reporting requirements, and precise definitions for technical terms. All regulations must be published in the Official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force. Any new regulation will undergo a public consultation period of at least 45 days before final adoption, inviting feedback from stakeholders.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Entities operating as Publishing Houses before the effective date of this Act and meeting the criteria in section 3 must apply for registration within 180 days of the effective date.
(2) During this transitional period, no penalties for non-registration will be levied, provided an application is submitted within the specified timeframe. However, all other provisions of this Act apply from the effective date. A special helpline will be established for 90 days to assist existing businesses with their initial applications.

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Payment terms
text: Each licensed hot-spring attendant pays an annual electric bicycle registration fee of 5 crowns.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Each licensed bell ringer of a parish tower pays 25 percent less of the fee or allowance specified in FDA §38.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for fees associated with the application, issuance, and renewal of Nordvalean passports. It defines the various categories of passport services and the corresponding charges, ensuring fair and transparent pricing for all citizens. The scope includes standard passport applications, expedited services, and special circumstances requiring adjusted fees. All fees collected contribute to the administrative costs of the passport issuance system and related security enhancements. This Act applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Standard Passport Application Fee
text:
(1) The standard fee for a new Nordvalean passport application is 500 crowns.
(2) This fee applies to all citizens applying for their first passport or renewing an expired passport, where the previous passport expired more than 12 months prior to the new application date.
(3) The standard processing time for such applications is approximately 20 business days from the date of submission.

heading: Standard Passport Application Fee
text:
(1) The standard fee for a new Nordvalean passport application is 550 crowns.
(2) This fee applies to all citizens applying for their first passport or renewing an expired passport, where the previous passport expired more than 18 months prior to the new application date.
(3) The standard processing time for such applications is approximately 25 business days from the date of submission.

heading: Standard Passport Application Fee
text:
(1) The standard fee for a new Nordvalean passport application is 600 crowns.
(2) This fee applies to all citizens applying for their first passport or renewing an expired passport, where the previous passport expired more than 24 months prior to the new application date.
(3) The standard processing time for such applications is approximately 30 business days from the date of submission.

heading: Passport Renewal Fee
text:
(1) The fee for renewing a Nordvalean passport that expired within the last 12 months, or is still valid, is 400 crowns.
(2) This reduced fee acknowledges the continuous validity of the applicant's identity information within recent records.
(3) The processing time for such renewals is generally 15 business days.

heading: Passport Renewal Fee
text:
(1) The fee for renewing a Nordvalean passport that expired within the last 18 months, or is still valid, is 425 crowns.
(2) This reduced fee acknowledges the continuous validity of the applicant's identity information within recent records.
(3) The processing time for such renewals is generally 18 business days.

heading: Minor's Passport Fee
text:
(1) For applicants under the age of 18, the passport application fee is 300 crowns.
(2) This reduced fee is applicable for both initial applications and renewals for minors, provided parental consent forms are duly completed.
(3) Passports issued to minors are valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Minor's Passport Fee
text:
(1) For applicants under the age of 18, the passport application fee is 320 crowns.
(2) This reduced fee is applicable for both initial applications and renewals for minors, provided parental consent forms are duly completed and verified.
(3) Passports issued to minors are valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance, and a new photograph is required for each renewal.

heading: First-Time Applicant Fee Exemption
text:
(1) Citizens applying for their very first Nordvalean passport are exempt from 20% of the standard application fee, if they are between the ages of 18 and 25.
(2) This exemption is intended to encourage young adults to obtain official travel documentation.
(3) To qualify, the applicant must present verifiable proof of age and that they have never held a Nordvalean passport previously.

heading: First-Time Applicant Fee Exemption
text:
(1) Citizens applying for their very first Nordvalean passport are exempt from 15% of the standard application fee, if they are between the ages of 18 and 23.
(2) This exemption is intended to encourage young adults to obtain official travel documentation.
(3) To qualify, the applicant must present verifiable proof of age and a declaration affirming they have never held a Nordvalean passport previously, which will be cross-referenced with national records.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee (Tier 1)
text:
(1) An additional fee of 300 crowns applies for expedited processing, guaranteeing issuance within 7 business days.
(2) This service is available for urgent travel needs, provided all documentation is complete and accurate at the time of application.
(3) Applicants must specify their need for expedited service at the time of submission and provide proof of imminent travel, such as flight bookings, if requested.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee (Tier 1)
text:
(1) An additional fee of 350 crowns applies for expedited processing, guaranteeing issuance within 5 business days.
(2) This service is available for urgent travel needs, provided all documentation is complete and accurate at the time of application.
(3) Applicants must specify their need for expedited service at the time of submission and provide proof of imminent travel, such as flight bookings, if requested, for validation by passport officials.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee (Tier 2)
text:
(1) A higher additional fee of 500 crowns applies for super-expedited processing, guaranteeing issuance within 3 business days.
(2) This premium service is reserved for extremely urgent cases, requiring immediate verification and priority handling.
(3) Availability of this service may be limited based on current demand and operational capacity in each municipality.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee (Tier 2)
text:
(1) A higher additional fee of 550 crowns applies for super-expedited processing, guaranteeing issuance within 2 business days.
(2) This premium service is reserved for extremely urgent cases, requiring immediate verification and priority handling by dedicated staff.
(3) Availability of this service may be limited based on current demand and operational capacity in each municipality, and applicants are advised to confirm availability before applying.

heading: Lost or Stolen Passport Replacement Fee
text:
(1) The fee for replacing a lost or stolen passport is 700 crowns.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs of invalidating the previous passport and issuing a new one, including enhanced security checks.
(3) A police report documenting the loss or theft must accompany the application for replacement, filed within 14 days of discovery.

heading: Lost or Stolen Passport Replacement Fee
text:
(1) The fee for replacing a lost or stolen passport is 750 crowns.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs of invalidating the previous passport and issuing a new one, including enhanced security checks and re-verification of identity.
(3) A police report documenting the loss or theft must accompany the application for replacement, filed within 10 days of discovery, and the report number must be provided on the application form.

heading: Damaged Passport Replacement Fee
text:
(1) A fee of 600 crowns is charged for replacing a significantly damaged Nordvalean passport.
(2) A passport is considered significantly damaged if its integrity is compromised to the extent it cannot be used for identification or travel, or if key information is illegible.
(3) The damaged passport must be surrendered with the replacement application.

heading: Passport Card Fee
text:
(1) An optional passport card, valid for domestic travel and land/sea borders with neighbouring countries, can be obtained for an additional fee of 200 crowns.
(2) This card is issued in conjunction with a full passport application or renewal.
(3) The passport card is valid for the same duration as the associated passport, up to a maximum of 10 years.

heading: Passport Card Fee
text:
(1) An optional passport card, valid for domestic travel and land/sea borders with specific neighbouring countries, can be obtained for an additional fee of 220 crowns.
(2) This card is issued in conjunction with a full passport application or renewal, and cannot be applied for independently.
(3) The passport card is valid for the same duration as the associated passport, up to a maximum of 10 years, and contains a secure embedded chip for verification.

heading: Additional Visa Pages Fee
text:
(1) Applicants requiring additional visa pages for extensive international travel may request a passport with 50 pages instead of the standard 30 pages for an extra 100 crowns.
(2) This option must be selected at the time of application or renewal.
(3) No additional pages can be added to an existing passport once it has been issued.

heading: Correction of Errors Fee
text:
(1) If a passport contains an error attributable to the applicant (e.g., incorrect date of birth provided), a fee of 150 crowns will be charged for correction and re-issuance.
(2) If the error is attributable to the issuing authority, no fee will be charged.
(3) The request for correction must be made within 90 days of the passport's issuance.

heading: Correction of Errors Fee
text:
(1) If a passport contains an error attributable to the applicant (e.g., incorrect spelling of name provided), a fee of 180 crowns will be charged for correction and re-issuance.
(2) If the error is attributable to the issuing authority, no fee will be charged, and the new passport will be expedited at no extra cost.
(3) The request for correction must be made within 60 days of the passport's issuance, accompanied by original supporting documents.

heading: Fee for Applicants Residing Abroad
text:
(1) Nordvalean citizens residing outside Nordvale must pay an additional processing fee of 100 crowns for any passport service.
(2) This fee covers the increased administrative and postage costs associated with international applications.
(3) Applications are submitted through the nearest Nordvalean diplomatic mission or consulate.

heading: Urgent Minor's Passport Fee
text:
(1) For minors requiring an expedited passport, the standard expedited fee of 300 crowns applies in addition to the minor's passport fee.
(2) This ensures prompt issuance for urgent family travel or emergency situations.
(3) Parental consent for expedited processing must be explicitly provided in writing.

heading: Urgent Minor's Passport Fee
text:
(1) For minors requiring an expedited passport, the standard expedited fee of 350 crowns applies in addition to the minor's passport fee.
(2) This ensures prompt issuance for urgent family travel or emergency situations, requiring documented proof of urgency.
(3) Parental consent for expedited processing must be explicitly provided in writing and witnessed by a passport official.

heading: Group Application Discount
text:
(1) A 10% discount on the standard application fee is granted for groups of 5 or more individuals applying for passports simultaneously.
(2) All applications in the group must be submitted at the same time and location, for processing together.
(3) This discount applies only to standard applications, not expedited or special services.

heading: Senior Citizen Passport Fee
text:
(1) Applicants aged 65 or older receive a 15% discount on the standard passport application or renewal fee.
(2) This acknowledges the contributions of senior citizens and aims to ease access to travel documentation.
(3) Proof of age, such as a national identity card, must be provided with the application.

heading: Senior Citizen Passport Fee
text:
(1) Applicants aged 67 or older receive a 10% discount on the standard passport application or renewal fee.
(2) This acknowledges the contributions of senior citizens and aims to ease access to travel documentation, provided they are not applying for expedited services.
(3) Proof of age, such as a national identity card, must be provided with the application and verified against national records.

heading: Extended Validity Passport Fee
text:
(1) For an additional fee of 200 crowns, adults aged 26 to 64 may opt for a passport with 10-year validity instead of the standard 5-year validity.
(2) This option provides convenience for frequent travelers and reduces the frequency of renewal.
(3) The eligibility for this extended validity is subject to a clean record of previous passport adherence.

heading: Extended Validity Passport Fee
text:
(1) For an additional fee of 250 crowns, adults aged 25 to 60 may opt for a passport with 10-year validity instead of the standard 5-year validity.
(2) This option provides convenience for frequent travelers and reduces the frequency of renewal, subject to a complete and verified application.
(3) The eligibility for this extended validity is subject to a clean record of previous passport adherence and no previous instances of passport loss or damage.

heading: Special Emergency Passport Fee
text:
(1) A special emergency passport, valid for a single journey or a period of 6 months, costs 800 crowns.
(2) This passport is issued in critical emergencies, such as immediate medical treatment abroad or death in the family, with issuance within 24 hours.
(3) Documentary evidence of the emergency is mandatory for consideration of this service.

heading: Passport Delivered by Registered Mail
text:
(1) Applicants wishing to receive their new passport via registered mail within Nordvale will incur an additional fee of 50 crowns.
(2) This service ensures secure delivery and requires a signature upon receipt.
(3) Standard delivery is via ordinary mail at no additional charge, but with no tracking.

heading: Passport Delivered by Registered Mail
text:
(1) Applicants wishing to receive their new passport via registered mail within Nordvale will incur an additional fee of 60 crowns.
(2) This service ensures secure delivery and requires a signature upon receipt by the applicant or a designated adult.
(3) Standard delivery is via ordinary mail at no additional charge, but with no tracking or insurance.

heading: Application Withdrawal Fee
text:
(1) If an applicant withdraws their passport application after submission but before issuance, a withdrawal fee of 100 crowns will be retained from the initial payment.
(2) The remaining balance of the application fee will be refunded.
(3) No withdrawal fee applies if the application is rejected due to administrative error by the passport office.

heading: Fee for Verification of Citizenship
text:
(1) For applicants whose citizenship status requires extensive verification, an additional fee of 250 crowns applies.
(2) This fee covers the costs of detailed record checks and potentially consulting with other government agencies.
(3) This typically applies to individuals born outside Nordvale or those with complex lineage claims.

heading: Non-Refundable Processing Component
text:
(1) A non-refundable portion of 150 crowns from each standard passport application fee covers initial processing and administrative overheads.
(2) This component is retained even if the application is subsequently rejected due to applicant errors or incomplete documentation.
(3) This ensures that resources expended on initial review are partially recovered.

heading: Fee for Name Change on Passport
text:
(1) For a name change on an existing valid passport, a fee of 350 crowns is charged for re-issuance.
(2) This requires official documentation of the name change, such as a marriage certificate or deed poll.
(3) The new passport will carry the same validity period as the original passport.

heading: Replacement of Expired Emergency Passport
text:
(1) The fee for replacing an expired special emergency passport with a full standard passport is 500 crowns.
(2) This acknowledges the prior emergency issuance and applies the standard new application rate.
(3) All standard documentation requirements for a full passport apply.

heading: Fee for Remote Application Assistance
text:
(1) Applicants requiring remote assistance for their application, such as video consultations or extended phone support, will be charged an additional 80 crowns.
(2) This service is available for citizens residing in remote areas or those with specific accessibility needs.
(3) Appointments for remote assistance must be scheduled at least 3 business days in advance.

heading: Passport Photo Rejection Fee
text:
(1) If an application is initially submitted with a photo that does not meet the specified requirements, and a new photo is subsequently required, a re-submission fee of 20 crowns applies.
(2) This covers the administrative cost of processing the new photo and updating the application.
(3) Applicants are encouraged to review photo guidelines carefully to avoid this fee.

heading: Refund Policy for Overpayment
text:
(1) Any overpayment of fees will be refunded to the applicant within 30 business days of the overpayment being identified.
(2) Refunds will be issued via the original payment method unless otherwise specified by the applicant in writing.
(3) A minimum overpayment of 10 crowns is required for a refund to be processed, to cover administrative costs.

heading: Fee Adjustment Mechanism
text:
(1) The fees stipulated in this Act may be adjusted annually by up to 5% based on inflation and operational costs.
(2) Any proposed adjustments will be published for public consultation at least 60 days before implementation.
(3) Such adjustments aim to maintain the financial sustainability of the passport issuance system.

heading: Replacement of Lost Passport Card
text:
(1) The fee for replacing a lost or stolen passport card is 250 crowns.
(2) This fee is separate from any passport replacement fee and applies even if the full passport is still valid.
(3) A police report is required for replacing a stolen passport card.

heading: Fee for Express Mail Overseas
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Fee for Express Mail Overseas
text:
(1) For Nordvalean citizens residing abroad, an express mail fee of 150 crowns applies for courier delivery of passports.
(2) This service ensures faster and trackable delivery to international addresses.
(3) Standard international mail is available at a reduced fee of 75 crowns.

heading: Fee for Express Mail Overseas
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reduced charges
text: Each holder of a registered cave rescue badge pays an annual dog licence fee of 5 crowns per dog.

heading: Exemptions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced by granting a registered peat cutter an additional 30 days to pay the annual registration fee of 30 crowns.

heading: Particular persons
text: The library card is reduced by twenty-five percent for any person who is an accredited sign-language interpreter registered for at least one year.

heading: Missing entitlements of fairway conductors
text:
(1) Where a periodic conveyance entitlement held by a certified fairway conductor has gone missing, the substitute issued for the same period is given to him or her without charge.
(2) Subsection (1) applies instead of any other reduction of the charge for the substitute.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for the installation, operation, and maintenance of public information kiosks within the civic areas of the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that such kiosks contribute positively to the public realm, provide accurate and accessible information, and do not unduly obstruct pedestrian traffic, obscure signage, or create visual clutter. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, covering all publicly accessible spaces such as plazas, squares, and designated public thoroughfares. It mandates that all such installations must secure a permit prior to placement.

heading: Definition of Public Information Kiosk
text: A 'public information kiosk' is defined as any freestanding, permanent, or semi-permanent structure, greater than 1.5 meters in height and less than 4.0 meters in width, installed in a public civic area primarily for the purpose of disseminating information to the general public. This information may include maps, local event listings, public service announcements, or interactive digital displays. The definition specifically excludes bus shelters, advertising billboards, and structures solely dedicated to commercial sales or services. Structures smaller than 1.5 meters in height or larger than 4.0 meters in width are subject to separate municipal regulations.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person, organization, or entity shall install, erect, or operate a public information kiosk in any civic area within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the relevant municipal authority as prescribed by this Act. Any kiosk found to be installed without a permit is subject to immediate removal and penalties as outlined in section 30. This requirement applies to both new installations and any existing kiosks undergoing significant structural modification or relocation. A permit must be prominently displayed on the kiosk at all times.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications for a Public Information Kiosk Permit must be submitted to the municipal planning department of the respective municipality where the kiosk is proposed to be located.
(2) Each application shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns.
(3) The application package must include detailed structural designs, proposed content outlines, site plans indicating precise location and dimensions, and an impact assessment on pedestrian flow. Applicants must also provide proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 500,000 crowns. Incomplete applications will be returned within 14 days.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications for a Public Information Kiosk Permit must be submitted to the municipal planning department of the respective municipality where the kiosk is proposed to be located.
(2) Each application shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns.
(3) The application package must include detailed structural designs, proposed content outlines, site plans indicating precise location and dimensions, and an impact assessment on pedestrian flow. Applicants must also provide proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 750,000 crowns. Incomplete applications will be returned within 10 days, and a digital submission is now mandatory alongside any physical copies.

heading: Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal planning department shall have a period of 60 days to review the application and make a determination. This period allows for consultation with relevant departments, including public works, urban design, and local historical preservation societies. If additional information is requested from the applicant, the 60-day review period will be paused until such information is provided. Failure to provide requested information within 30 days may result in the application being deemed withdrawn.

heading: Review Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the municipal planning department shall have a period of 45 days to review the application and make a determination. This period allows for consultation with relevant departments, including public works, urban design, and local historical preservation societies. If additional information is requested from the applicant, the 45-day review period will be paused until such information is provided. Failure to provide requested information within 20 days may result in the application being deemed withdrawn. Priority review may be granted for an additional fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Permit Issuance Conditions
text:
(1) A permit may be issued if the proposed kiosk:
(a) Does not obstruct pedestrian or vehicular traffic, maintaining a clear path of at least 2.5 meters on all sides.
(b) Is aesthetically compatible with the surrounding civic area, as determined by the municipal urban design committee.
(c) Poses no undue safety risks to the public.
(d) Provides information primarily of benefit to the public, rather than solely commercial advertising.
(2) The municipal authority reserves the right to impose specific conditions on the permit, such as operating hours or content restrictions, to ensure public benefit.

heading: Maximum Kiosk Dimensions
text: The maximum permissible dimensions for any public information kiosk are 3.5 meters in height, 3.0 meters in width, and 1.0 meter in depth. These dimensions are inclusive of any structural elements, decorative features, or external displays. Any proposed kiosk exceeding these dimensions will be automatically rejected. In exceptional circumstances, a variance may be sought, but only for height, and only if it does not exceed 4.0 meters and is explicitly approved by 75% of the municipal council members.

heading: Maximum Kiosk Dimensions
text: The maximum permissible dimensions for any public information kiosk are 3.0 meters in height, 2.5 meters in width, and 0.8 meters in depth. These dimensions are inclusive of any structural elements, decorative features, or external displays. Any proposed kiosk exceeding these dimensions will be automatically rejected. Variances are no longer permitted for any dimension. This restriction aims to reduce visual clutter and ensure more consistent urban aesthetics across all municipalities.

heading: Minimum Clearance from Buildings
text: All public information kiosks must be situated at a minimum distance of 2.0 meters from the facade of any building, including residential, commercial, or public structures. This clearance is necessary to ensure adequate access to building entrances and windows, as well as to preserve the architectural integrity and visibility of the surrounding structures. Exceptions may be granted by the municipal planning department for kiosks integrated into existing public infrastructure, provided a minimum clearance of 1.0 meter can still be maintained and approved by 60% of the local planning committee.

heading: Minimum Clearance from Intersections
text: Public information kiosks shall not be installed within 10 meters of any street intersection or crosswalk. This requirement is crucial for maintaining clear sightlines for pedestrians and drivers, thereby enhancing public safety and preventing traffic hazards. The measurement shall be taken from the nearest point of the kiosk to the nearest edge of the intersection pavement or crosswalk marking. Municipalities may designate specific zones where this minimum distance can be reduced to 7 meters, but only after a comprehensive traffic safety assessment.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text: A Public Information Kiosk Permit shall be valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. Prior to the expiry of the permit, the holder may apply for renewal. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiry date and shall be accompanied by a renewal fee of 150 crowns. The renewal process will include a review of the kiosk's operational history, maintenance records, and compliance with all current regulations. Failure to apply for renewal in time will result in the permit expiring, requiring a new application process.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text: A Public Information Kiosk Permit shall be valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance. Prior to the expiry of the permit, the holder may apply for renewal. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 120 days before the expiry date and shall be accompanied by a renewal fee of 200 crowns. The renewal process will include a comprehensive review of the kiosk's operational history, maintenance records, content relevance, and full compliance with all current regulations. Failure to apply for renewal in time will result in the permit expiring, requiring a new application process with an additional late fee of 50 crowns if renewal is still desired within 60 days of expiry.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text: Permit holders are responsible for the continuous maintenance of their public information kiosks, ensuring they remain in good repair, free from graffiti, damage, or excessive wear. All digital displays must be functional and clear. Any damage or malfunction must be repaired within 72 hours of its occurrence or discovery. Failure to comply with these maintenance standards may result in a formal warning from the municipal authority, followed by potential fines of 100 crowns per day for continued non-compliance after a 7-day grace period. Regular inspections will be conducted at least twice annually.

heading: Content Guidelines
text: The content displayed on public information kiosks must primarily serve the public interest. This includes local government announcements, cultural event listings, public transportation information, and maps. Commercial advertising is permitted only if it constitutes less than 20% of the total display area and is clearly distinguishable from public information. Content must be suitable for all ages and must not contain offensive, discriminatory, or political campaign material. The municipal authority reserves the right to demand removal of any content deemed inappropriate within 24 hours.

heading: Ownership Identification
text: Every public information kiosk must clearly display the name of the permit holder and a contact telephone number for public inquiries or reporting of issues. This identification must be legibly printed in a minimum font size of 24 points and placed in a readily visible location on the kiosk, at a height between 1.0 meter and 1.8 meters from the ground. Failure to properly identify the kiosk owner may result in a fine of 75 crowns for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Ownership Identification
text: Every public information kiosk must clearly display the name of the permit holder, a contact telephone number, and a unique permit identification number for public inquiries or reporting of issues. This identification must be legibly printed in a minimum font size of 28 points and placed in a readily visible location on the kiosk, at a height between 1.2 meters and 1.6 meters from the ground. Failure to properly identify the kiosk owner may result in a fine of 100 crowns for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 2,000 crowns, and potential permit suspension.

heading: Relocation of Kiosks
text: Should a public information kiosk require relocation, a new permit application must be submitted for the proposed new location, complete with all required documentation and fees, as if it were a new installation. The original permit is valid only for the location specified therein. Minor repositioning within the same immediate area (less than 1.5 meters from the original spot) may be permitted with written approval from the municipal planning department, provided it does not violate any other section of this Act. Any unauthorized relocation will be treated as an unpermitted installation.

heading: Removal of Kiosks
text: Upon expiry, revocation, or non-renewal of a permit, the permit holder is responsible for the removal of the public information kiosk within 30 days. The site must be restored to its original condition, free of any debris or structural remnants. Failure to remove the kiosk within the specified timeframe will result in the municipal authority undertaking the removal at the permit holder's expense, plus an additional penalty of 500 crowns. An invoice for removal costs will be issued to the permit holder, payable within 45 days.

heading: Emergency Removal
text: In cases of emergency, such as a direct threat to public safety, an obstruction to emergency services, or an immediate public works project, the municipal authority reserves the right to immediately remove any public information kiosk without prior notice. The permit holder will be notified as soon as practicable after removal. The cost of such emergency removal will be borne by the municipal authority unless the emergency was caused by the permit holder's negligence or non-compliance, in which case the costs will be recovered from the permit holder.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or a permit holder whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 21 days of receiving notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, outlining the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 100 crowns.
(3) The Municipal Appeals Board shall review the appeal and render a decision within 45 days. The decision of the Board is final at the municipal level. Further appeals must be pursued through the Nordvale judicial system.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of any section of this Act, for which no specific penalty is otherwise prescribed, shall be subject to a fine of not less than 100 crowns and not more than 1,000 crowns for each offense. Each day that a violation continues shall be considered a separate offense. Repeated violations, defined as three or more distinct instances within a 12-month period, may result in the revocation of the permit and a prohibition on future permit applications for a period of 2 years. Fines are payable within 30 days of issuance.

heading: Reporting Violations
text: Members of the public are encouraged to report any suspected violations of this Act to their respective municipal planning department. Reports can be made via telephone, email, or an online portal. All reports will be investigated within 5 business days. Anonymous reports will be accepted, but priority may be given to reports from identifiable sources providing contact information. The identity of individuals reporting violations will be kept confidential to the fullest extent permitted by law.

heading: Public Liability Insurance
text: All permit holders must maintain public liability insurance coverage of at least 500,000 crowns for the entire duration of the permit. This insurance must cover any damages, injuries, or losses incurred by the public as a direct result of the kiosk's installation, operation, or maintenance. Proof of current insurance must be submitted annually to the municipal planning department. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of the permit until proof of valid coverage is provided, and a fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Public Liability Insurance
text: All permit holders must maintain public liability insurance coverage of at least 750,000 crowns for the entire duration of the permit. This insurance must cover any damages, injuries, or losses incurred by the public as a direct result of the kiosk's installation, operation, or maintenance. Proof of current insurance must be submitted annually to the municipal planning department. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of the permit until proof of valid coverage is provided, and a fine of 300 crowns. The municipality must be named as an additional insured party on the policy.

heading: Design Standards for Accessibility
text: Public information kiosks must be designed and installed in a manner that ensures accessibility for all members of the public, including those with mobility impairments. This includes ensuring that interactive screens or information panels are positioned at heights between 0.8 meters and 1.2 meters from the ground. Sufficient clear ground space of at least 1.5 meters by 1.5 meters must be provided in front of any interactive components. All text must be legible, with a minimum font size of 18 points, and a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1. Audio output for digital kiosks is encouraged.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text: Applicants are encouraged to utilize environmentally friendly materials and sustainable practices in the construction and operation of public information kiosks. Materials should be durable and recyclable where possible. Digital kiosks should employ energy-efficient displays and power management systems. The use of solar power is highly recommended, and kiosks powered solely by renewable energy sources may be eligible for a 10% reduction in permit renewal fees. All waste generated during installation or maintenance must be disposed of responsibly.

heading: Data Privacy for Digital Kiosks
text: For public information kiosks that incorporate digital or interactive elements, stringent data privacy protocols must be observed. No personal data of users shall be collected, stored, or transmitted without explicit, informed consent. Any data collected, even with consent, must be anonymized and aggregated where possible, and used solely for improving the kiosk service. Kiosks must clearly display a privacy policy statement that is easily accessible to users. Non-compliance with data privacy standards may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Restriction on Commercial Advertising
text: Commercial advertising on public information kiosks is strictly limited to 20% of the total available display area. This percentage is calculated based on the cumulative surface area dedicated to advertising over a 24-hour cycle for digital displays, or the static physical area for non-digital kiosks. Advertising must be clearly distinct from public service information and shall not interfere with the primary purpose of public information dissemination. Violations of this restriction will incur a fine of 250 crowns per day until rectified.

heading: Restriction on Commercial Advertising
text: Commercial advertising on public information kiosks is strictly limited to 15% of the total available display area. This percentage is calculated based on the cumulative surface area dedicated to advertising over a 24-hour cycle for digital displays, or the static physical area for non-digital kiosks. Advertising must be clearly distinct from public service information and shall not interfere with the primary purpose of public information dissemination. Violations of this restriction will incur a fine of 300 crowns per day until rectified. Repeat offenders may have their permits revoked.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For any proposed public information kiosk in a prominent civic area, such as a main square or historical district, the municipal planning department shall conduct a public consultation period of at least 30 days. During this period, detailed plans and designs will be made available for public review, and feedback will be actively solicited. A public meeting may be convened if more than 50 written objections are received. The results of the public consultation must be considered in the final permit decision, with a summary of feedback provided to the applicant.

heading: Historical and Heritage Zones
text: The installation of public information kiosks within designated historical or heritage zones is subject to additional scrutiny and requires approval from the Nordvale Heritage Commission. Kiosks in these areas must blend harmoniously with the historical character, utilizing materials, colors, and designs appropriate to the setting. The maximum height for kiosks in heritage zones is reduced to 2.5 meters. A detailed heritage impact assessment must be submitted with the application, and the Commission may impose specific aesthetic requirements beyond standard guidelines.

heading: Illumination Standards
text: Any illumination of public information kiosks, whether internal or external, must comply with municipal light pollution ordinances. Illumination should be directed downwards and adequately shielded to prevent light spill into adjacent properties or the night sky. The maximum permitted luminance for digital screens is 300 nits during nighttime hours, and 800 nits during daytime hours. Flashing or rapidly changing lights are prohibited. Non-compliance with illumination standards may result in a fine of 100 crowns per day until adjusted.

heading: Illumination Standards
text: Any illumination of public information kiosks, whether internal or external, must comply with municipal light pollution ordinances. Illumination should be directed downwards and adequately shielded to prevent light spill into adjacent properties or the night sky. The maximum permitted luminance for digital screens is 250 nits during nighttime hours, and 700 nits during daytime hours. Flashing or rapidly changing lights are prohibited. All kiosks must incorporate automatic dimming based on ambient light levels. Non-compliance with illumination standards may result in a fine of 150 crowns per day until adjusted, and potential permit suspension.

heading: Graffiti and Vandalism Prevention
text: Kiosk designs should incorporate features that deter graffiti and vandalism, such as anti-graffiti coatings and robust, tamper-resistant materials. Any graffiti or acts of vandalism must be reported to the municipal authority within 24 hours of discovery and removed or repaired within 48 hours. The permit holder is solely responsible for the costs associated with graffiti removal and repair. Failure to comply with removal timelines will result in a fine of 50 crowns per day, in addition to the cost of municipal clean-up if undertaken by the authority.

heading: Accessibility for Maintenance and Repair
text: Kiosks must be designed and located to allow safe and unimpeded access for maintenance and repair personnel. This includes ensuring adequate clearance around the kiosk for tools and equipment, typically a minimum of 1.0 meter on all accessible sides. Any internal components requiring regular access must be easily reachable. Obstruction of public pathways during maintenance activities must be minimized, with temporary barriers and signage deployed to ensure public safety, and work completed within 4 hours if it causes significant public inconvenience.

heading: Municipal Kiosk Program Exemption
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Kiosks in Parks and Green Spaces
text: The installation of public information kiosks in public parks, gardens, or designated green spaces is subject to additional review by the municipal parks and recreation department. Kiosks in these areas must use natural-toned materials and designs that complement the natural environment. Their placement should avoid disrupting existing flora or fauna and must maintain a minimum distance of 5 meters from any mature tree. The maximum height in such areas is limited to 2.8 meters. Environmental impact assessments are mandatory for such applications.

heading: Emergency Information Capability
text: All digital public information kiosks must incorporate the capability to display urgent public safety announcements and emergency alerts issued by municipal or national authorities. This functionality must be prioritized over all other content, immediately overriding any scheduled displays or advertisements. Testing of this emergency override system must be conducted annually by the permit holder, with a report submitted to the municipal emergency services department. Failure to provide this capability or a successful test report may result in a 300 crowns fine.

heading: Coordination with Public Utilities
text: Applicants must coordinate with all relevant public utility providers (electricity, water, telecommunications) prior to installation to ensure that the kiosk does not interfere with existing utility lines, infrastructure, or access points. Detailed utility plans must be submitted as part of the permit application. Any costs associated with the relocation or protection of utility infrastructure due to kiosk installation will be borne by the permit holder. Underground utility lines must be marked and surveyed before any excavation begins.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) A permit may be revoked by the municipal authority if the permit holder:
(a) Fails to comply with any provision of this Act or the conditions specified in the permit.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in their application.
(c) Fails to maintain public liability insurance as required by section 20.
(d) Has three or more separate violations of this Act within a 12-month period.
(2) Prior to revocation, the permit holder shall be given written notice of the intent to revoke and a period of 30 days to rectify the non-compliance.

heading: Annual Inspection Fee
text: Each permit holder shall pay an annual inspection fee of 75 crowns to the municipal authority. This fee covers the cost of routine inspections conducted by municipal staff to ensure ongoing compliance with the provisions of this Act, including maintenance, content, and structural integrity. Invoices for the annual fee will be issued on the anniversary of the permit's issuance and are payable within 60 days. Failure to pay the annual inspection fee may result in a late penalty of 25 crowns and potential permit suspension after 90 days.

heading: Annual Inspection Fee
text: Each permit holder shall pay an annual inspection fee of 100 crowns to the municipal authority. This fee covers the cost of routine inspections conducted by municipal staff to ensure ongoing compliance with the provisions of this Act, including maintenance, content, and structural integrity. Invoices for the annual fee will be issued on the anniversary of the permit's issuance and are payable within 45 days. Failure to pay the annual inspection fee may result in a late penalty of 35 crowns and potential permit suspension after 75 days, leading to potential revocation if unpaid for 120 days.

heading: Kiosk Placement Density
text: To prevent visual clutter and ensure equitable distribution of public information resources, there shall be a minimum distance of 50 meters between any two public information kiosks. This density restriction applies to all civic areas within a municipality. Exceptions may be granted in designated large public squares or transportation hubs, where the minimum distance can be reduced to 30 meters, provided that pedestrian flow is not impeded and the total number of kiosks does not exceed one per 500 square meters of public space. The municipal planning department maintains a public map of all approved kiosk locations.

heading: Prohibited Locations
text: Public information kiosks are expressly prohibited from being installed in certain sensitive locations. These include, but are not limited to, the immediate vicinity (within 20 meters) of national monuments, war memorials, hospitals, and fire stations. Kiosks are also prohibited within 5 meters of any designated public art installation. The municipal authority maintains a list of all prohibited locations, which is updated annually and made available on its website. Any application proposing a kiosk in a prohibited location will be summarily rejected without fee refund.

heading: Display of Permit Number
text: Every public information kiosk must prominently display its unique permit identification number issued by the municipal authority. This number must be clearly visible and legible, with characters at least 5 cm in height, placed at an accessible height between 1.5 meters and 2.0 meters from the ground. The permit number assists in identifying authorized kiosks and facilitates the reporting of issues by the public. Failure to display the permit number as required will result in a fine of 25 crowns for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 500 crowns.

heading: Display of Permit Number
text: Every public information kiosk must prominently display its unique permit identification number issued by the municipal authority. This number must be clearly visible and legible, with characters at least 7 cm in height, placed at an accessible height between 1.3 meters and 1.8 meters from the ground. The permit number assists in identifying authorized kiosks and facilitates the reporting of issues by the public. Failure to display the permit number as required will result in a fine of 40 crowns for each day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 800 crowns, and may lead to additional inspection fees.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Urban Development and Public Works every 5 years from its effective date. The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose, evaluate the impact of kiosks on public spaces, and consider any necessary amendments or updates to reflect technological advancements or changes in urban planning best practices. The first review will be initiated no later than January 1, 2023. Public feedback will be invited during the review process for a period of 90 days.

heading: Building permits at altitude
text:
(1) Where a new building will stand in a highland settlement that lies 700 metres or more above sea level, the applicant pays only the part of the building permit fee that is charged for each square metre of floor area; the fixed part of that fee is not charged.
(2) For a building in a highland settlement that lies lower than 700 metres, the building permit fee is charged in full.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the licensing and regulation of private investigators within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all individuals and entities offering private investigation services operate with integrity, competence, and adherence to established ethical standards. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. No person or company may perform private investigation duties for compensation without a valid licence issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act. This regulation is crucial for protecting public interest and maintaining the public trust in investigative services across Nordvale.

heading: Definition of Private Investigator
text:
For the purposes of this Act, a 'private investigator' is defined as any individual who, for direct or indirect compensation, performs any of the following activities:
(1) Obtains or furnishes information concerning crimes or wrongs done or threatened against the Republic of Nordvale or any municipality.
(2) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the identity, habits, conduct, movements, whereabouts, affiliations, transactions, reputation, or character of any person.
(3) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the credibility of witnesses or other persons.
(4) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the location or recovery of lost or stolen property.
(5) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the causes or responsibility for fires, accidents, or damage to property. This definition ensures clarity regarding who is subject to the licensing requirements.

heading: Definition of Private Investigator
text:
For the purposes of this Act, a 'private investigator' is defined as any individual who, for direct or indirect compensation, performs any of the following activities:
(1) Obtains or furnishes information concerning crimes or wrongs done or threatened against the Republic of Nordvale or any municipality.
(2) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the identity, habits, conduct, movements, whereabouts, affiliations, transactions, reputation, or character of any person.
(3) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the credibility of witnesses or other persons.
(4) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the location or recovery of lost or stolen property.
(5) Obtains or furnishes information concerning the causes or responsibility for fires, accidents, damage to property, or any other civil liability matter. This updated definition expands the scope to include civil liability investigations.

heading: Licence Requirement
text: No person shall act as a private investigator in Nordvale unless they hold a valid licence issued by the Nordvale Regulatory Authority for Private Investigations (NRAPI) in accordance with this Act. A person found to be operating without a licence shall be subject to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offence and 10,000 crowns for subsequent offences. This requirement applies to all individuals, including those operating as sole proprietors, partners, or employees of investigative firms. The NRAPI maintains a public register of all licensed investigators, which must be updated monthly to reflect new licences or revocations.

heading: Application for Licence
text: An application for a private investigator licence must be submitted to the NRAPI on the prescribed form. The application must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 800 crowns. Applicants must also provide three character references, proof of Nordvale residency for at least 36 months, and a detailed curriculum vitae outlining relevant experience. All supporting documents must be submitted in Nordvalean and certified by a notary public. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant after 30 days if not rectified.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Licensure
text:
To be eligible for a private investigator licence, an applicant must:
(1) Be at least 21 years of age.
(2) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(3) Have completed at least 360 hours of approved training in investigative techniques or have 2 years of verifiable experience in a related field.
(4) Not have been convicted of any felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude within the last 10 years.
(5) Pass a comprehensive background check conducted by the Nordvale Security Service. This background check assesses an applicant's financial stability, criminal history, and overall trustworthiness.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Licensure
text:
To be eligible for a private investigator licence, an applicant must:
(1) Be at least 20 years of age.
(2) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(3) Have completed at least 400 hours of approved training in investigative techniques or have 3 years of verifiable experience in a related field.
(4) Not have been convicted of any felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude within the last 15 years.
(5) Pass a comprehensive background check conducted by the Nordvale Security Service. The background check now also includes a psychological evaluation by a certified psychologist.

heading: Licence Examination
text: All applicants for a private investigator licence must pass a written examination administered by the NRAPI. The examination covers topics such as Nordvalean law, investigative ethics, evidence collection, and report writing. A score of at least 75% is required to pass. Applicants who fail the examination may re-take it after a waiting period of 60 days, up to a maximum of three attempts within a 12-month period. A re-examination fee of 300 crowns applies to each subsequent attempt. Study materials are available from the NRAPI for a fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Licence Examination
text: All applicants for a private investigator licence must pass a written examination administered by the NRAPI. The examination covers topics such as Nordvalean law, investigative ethics, evidence collection, report writing, and digital forensics. A score of at least 80% is required to pass. Applicants who fail the examination may re-take it after a waiting period of 90 days, up to a maximum of two attempts within a 12-month period. A re-examination fee of 400 crowns applies to each subsequent attempt. Study materials are now provided digitally free of charge.

heading: Issuance of Licence
text: Upon successful completion of all application requirements, including the background check and examination, the NRAPI shall issue a private investigator licence. The licence will be valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issuance. Each licence will display the investigator's name, photograph, unique licence number, and expiration date. It is the responsibility of the licence holder to keep their licence secure and to notify the NRAPI within 15 days of any change of address or contact information. Failure to do so may result in administrative penalties.

heading: Renewal of Licence
text: A private investigator licence must be renewed every 24 months. The application for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the expiration date and include a renewal fee of 600 crowns. Renewal requires verification of ongoing eligibility criteria and proof of completion of at least 16 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) during the preceding licence period. Late renewal applications, submitted within 30 days after expiration, will incur an additional late fee of 200 crowns. Licences not renewed within 30 days of expiration will be considered lapsed and require a new application.

heading: Renewal of Licence
text: A private investigator licence must be renewed every 36 months. The application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the expiration date and include a renewal fee of 750 crowns. Renewal requires verification of ongoing eligibility criteria and proof of completion of at least 24 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) during the preceding licence period. Late renewal applications, submitted within 45 days after expiration, will incur an additional late fee of 300 crowns. Licences not renewed within 45 days of expiration will be considered lapsed and require a new application.

heading: Continuing Professional Development
text: All licensed private investigators are required to complete a minimum of 16 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every 24 months to maintain their licence. These hours must be earned through courses, seminars, or workshops approved by the NRAPI. At least 4 hours of CPD must be directly related to ethical practices and Nordvalean law. Records of CPD completion must be submitted with renewal applications. Failure to meet CPD requirements may result in the refusal of licence renewal or the imposition of a penalty of 100 crowns per missing hour.

heading: Display of Licence
text: Every licensed private investigator shall carry their licence identification card at all times while performing investigative duties. When requested by a member of the public or an official of the Nordvale authorities, the investigator must present their licence for inspection. Failure to produce a valid licence upon request may result in a fine of 250 crowns for a first offence and 500 crowns for subsequent offences. This ensures transparency and accountability in the execution of investigative services. The licence card must be clearly visible and un-obscured.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Licensed private investigators are required to maintain detailed records of all investigations undertaken for a period of at least 5 years. These records must include client details, objectives of the investigation, methods employed, and findings. Upon request from the NRAPI, these records must be made available for inspection within 10 business days. Investigators must also submit an annual report to the NRAPI, summarizing their activities, no later than January 31st of each year. Failure to comply with reporting requirements may lead to a penalty of up to 1,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Licensed private investigators are required to maintain detailed records of all investigations undertaken for a period of at least 7 years. These records must include client details, objectives of the investigation, methods employed, findings, and any significant expenses incurred. Upon request from the NRAPI, these records must be made available for inspection within 7 business days. Investigators must also submit an annual report to the NRAPI, summarizing their activities and any ethical complaints received, no later than January 31st of each year. Failure to comply with reporting requirements may lead to a penalty of up to 1,500 crowns.

heading: Confidentiality
text: A private investigator shall not divulge any information obtained during the course of an investigation to any unauthorized person. All client information and investigative findings are to be treated with the utmost confidentiality. This obligation of confidentiality continues even after the conclusion of the investigation and the termination of the client relationship. Exceptions to this rule include disclosures required by Nordvalean law or court order. Breaching confidentiality can result in severe penalties, including licence suspension for 6 months and a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for the first offence.

heading: Ethical Conduct
text: Every private investigator must adhere to a strict code of ethical conduct. This includes, but is not limited to, refraining from illegal activities, misrepresentation, harassment, or entrapment. Investigators must conduct themselves professionally and with integrity at all times. They must not accept assignments that are unethical, illegal, or beyond their professional competence. Any breach of ethical conduct may lead to disciplinary action, ranging from a formal warning to licence revocation, depending on the severity of the infraction. A committee of five experienced investigators reviews all ethical complaints.

heading: Prohibited Activities
text:
Private investigators are strictly prohibited from engaging in the following activities:
(1) Impersonating law enforcement officers or any other government official.
(2) Making false or misleading statements to clients or other parties.
(3) Using intimidation or coercion during an investigation.
(4) Engaging in any form of electronic surveillance without a valid court order.
(5) Carrying firearms or any other weapon while on duty, unless specifically authorized by a separate permit. Violations of these prohibitions carry significant penalties, including immediate licence suspension for 12 months and a fine of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Use of Force
text: Private investigators are not authorized to use physical force against any person, except in cases of immediate self-defence or the defence of another from imminent bodily harm. Any use of force must be reported to the Nordvale Security Service and the NRAPI within 24 hours of the incident. Excessive or unjustified use of force will result in immediate suspension of the licence pending investigation and potential revocation. Training on de-escalation techniques is mandatory for all investigators and forms part of the CPD requirements.

heading: Client Contracts
text:
All private investigation services must be provided under a written contract between the investigator and the client. The contract must clearly state:
(1) The scope of services to be rendered.
(2) The agreed-upon fees and payment schedule.
(3) The estimated duration of the investigation.
(4) A clear statement regarding the confidential nature of the investigation.
(5) The circumstances under which the contract may be terminated. A copy of the signed contract must be provided to the client before any work commences. Failure to provide a written contract may result in a fine of 750 crowns.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: Private investigators must ensure that all fees and charges are fair, reasonable, and fully disclosed to the client in advance. No hidden fees or unexpected charges are permitted. Any changes to the agreed-upon fees must be communicated to the client in writing and explicitly agreed upon before additional costs are incurred. Investigators are prohibited from charging contingency fees based on the outcome of an investigation. A detailed invoice must be provided to the client upon completion of the investigation or at regular intervals as agreed in the contract. Disputes over fees can be arbitrated by the NRAPI.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Every licensed private investigator must maintain professional indemnity insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns and public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 1,000,000 crowns. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted to the NRAPI annually, along with the annual report. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in the immediate suspension of the licence until such coverage is re-established. The NRAPI may request an updated certificate of insurance at any time within 10 days' notice.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Every licensed private investigator must maintain professional indemnity insurance with a minimum coverage of 750,000 crowns and public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 1,500,000 crowns. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted to the NRAPI annually, along with the annual report. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in the immediate suspension of the licence until such coverage is re-established. The NRAPI may request an updated certificate of insurance at any time within 7 days' notice, and insurers must directly confirm coverage.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text: Any person may lodge a complaint against a licensed private investigator for alleged breaches of this Act or the code of ethical conduct. Complaints must be submitted in writing to the NRAPI within 90 days of the alleged incident. The NRAPI will investigate all complaints and, where appropriate, hold a hearing to determine the validity of the allegations. The investigator concerned will be given 30 days to respond to the complaint. All complaints are recorded and accessible for audit purposes, ensuring transparency in the process.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text:
Upon finding a private investigator in violation of this Act or the ethical code, the NRAPI may impose various disciplinary actions, including:
(1) Issuing a formal written warning.
(2) Imposing administrative fines ranging from 1,000 to 10,000 crowns.
(3) Suspending the licence for a period not exceeding 24 months.
(4) Revoking the licence permanently.
(5) Requiring the completion of additional training or supervised practice. The severity of the action will depend on the nature and gravity of the violation, as well as any prior disciplinary history of the investigator.

heading: Licence Suspension
text: During a period of licence suspension, a private investigator is prohibited from performing any investigative duties for compensation. Any attempt to operate during suspension will be considered a serious offence, leading to immediate licence revocation and a fine of 25,000 crowns. The NRAPI will notify all relevant authorities, including the local police in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, of any licence suspension. Suspended investigators must surrender their licence card to the NRAPI within 7 days of the suspension order.

heading: Licence Revocation
text: Revocation of a private investigator licence is the most severe disciplinary action. An investigator whose licence has been revoked is permanently barred from applying for a new licence in Nordvale. In exceptional circumstances, after a minimum of 10 years, an individual may petition the NRAPI for a review of their case, but reinstatement is not guaranteed. All revoked licences are published on the NRAPI's public register and communicated to all municipalities. Revocation is typically reserved for grave breaches of ethics, criminal convictions, or repeated serious violations of this Act.

heading: Appeals
text: An applicant or licence holder aggrieved by a decision of the NRAPI regarding licensure, renewal, or disciplinary action may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal. An appeal must be lodged within 30 days of receiving the NRAPI's decision. The Tribunal will review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the NRAPI's ruling. The decision of the Administrative Appeals Tribunal is final unless there is a point of law that can be challenged in a higher court. A fee of 1,200 crowns is required to file an appeal.

heading: Appeals
text: An applicant or licence holder aggrieved by a decision of the NRAPI regarding licensure, renewal, or disciplinary action may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal. An appeal must be lodged within 21 days of receiving the NRAPI's decision. The Tribunal will review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the NRAPI's ruling. The decision of the Administrative Appeals Tribunal is final unless there is a point of law that can be challenged in a higher court. A fee of 1,500 crowns is required to file an appeal, and applicants must attend a mandatory mediation session prior to a full hearing.

heading: Register of Licensed Investigators
text: The NRAPI shall maintain a public register of all licensed private investigators. This register will include the investigator's name, licence number, and current licence status (active, suspended, revoked). It will not include personal contact information or details of ongoing investigations. The register shall be accessible via the NRAPI's official website and updated weekly. Any member of the public may consult this register to verify the credentials of an individual claiming to be a private investigator. The NRAPI will ensure that all information in the register is accurate and up-to-date.

heading: Corporate Licensure
text: Any firm or company offering private investigation services must also hold a corporate licence issued by the NRAPI. The corporate licence application requires a fee of 1,500 crowns and must designate at least one director or principal as a fully licensed private investigator under this Act. All employees performing investigative duties must also hold individual private investigator licences. The corporate licence is valid for 36 months and is subject to renewal requirements similar to individual licences. Corporate entities are responsible for ensuring all their investigators comply with this Act.

heading: Corporate Licensure
text: Any firm or company offering private investigation services must also hold a corporate licence issued by the NRAPI. The corporate licence application requires a fee of 2,000 crowns and must designate at least one director or principal as a fully licensed private investigator under this Act. All employees performing investigative duties must also hold individual private investigator licences. The corporate licence is valid for 24 months and is subject to renewal requirements similar to individual licences. Corporate entities are responsible for ensuring all their investigators comply with this Act and must submit an annual compliance audit to the NRAPI.

heading: Operating Name
text: A licensed private investigator or licensed corporate entity must operate under the name registered with the NRAPI. Any change in an operating name must be reported to the NRAPI within 14 days and may require a new application if the change is substantial. Using an unregistered or misleading operating name is prohibited and may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns. This provision ensures that clients and the public can clearly identify the licensed entity they are dealing with and facilitates regulatory oversight. All business cards and official correspondence must clearly display the registered operating name.

heading: Jurisdiction
text: This Act applies to all private investigation activities conducted within the geographical boundaries of the Republic of Nordvale, including all its municipalities. Any investigation initiated in Nordvale, even if it involves gathering information in other jurisdictions, falls under the purview of this Act. Investigators operating from outside Nordvale but conducting investigations within Nordvale must also comply with these licensing requirements. The NRAPI has the authority to investigate and prosecute violations that occur anywhere within Nordvale territory, irrespective of the investigator's primary base of operation.

heading: Cooperation with Authorities
text: Licensed private investigators are required to cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies and other Nordvalean authorities in the course of their duties. This includes providing information, subject to client confidentiality and legal privilege, when legally compelled to do so by a court order or warrant. Failure to cooperate with official inquiries may lead to disciplinary action, including licence suspension for 3 months. Investigators must promptly report any observed criminal activity to the appropriate authorities. This cooperation is vital for maintaining public safety and the integrity of the justice system.

heading: False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information to the NRAPI in connection with an application, renewal, or any other requirement of this Act commits an offence. Such an offence is punishable by a fine of up to 15,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. If a licensed investigator is found to have provided false information, their licence will be immediately revoked. This provision is designed to ensure the integrity of the licensing process and to deter fraudulent representations.

heading: NRAPI Authority
text:
The Nordvale Regulatory Authority for Private Investigations (NRAPI) is the designated body responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. The NRAPI has the power to:
(1) Issue, renew, suspend, and revoke private investigator licences.
(2) Conduct investigations into alleged violations of this Act.
(3) Impose disciplinary actions and administrative penalties.
(4) Develop and disseminate guidelines and regulations to support this Act.
(5) Maintain a register of licensed investigators. The NRAPI is comprised of a board of seven members, appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Justice, serving 4-year terms.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The NRAPI, through its authorized officers, has the power to inspect the premises and records of any licensed private investigator or corporate entity during regular business hours, with 24 hours' written notice. These inspections are to ensure compliance with this Act and its regulations. Officers may request to see licence cards, insurance certificates, client contracts, and investigative records. Obstruction of an authorized officer in the performance of their duties is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 5,000 crowns for individuals and 10,000 crowns for corporate entities. Officers will carry official NRAPI identification.

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each certified hoof trimmer pays no fee or allowance as specified in HOA §6.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) A resident who is a licensed chimney-sweep master shall pay half the fee or allowance stated in FDA §18. (2) This reduction applies to one permit per household.

heading: Prolongation for senior wardens
text:
(1) A senior honorary fellowship warden owes nothing for an operator authorisation prolongation.
(2) For such a warden this section applies instead of EPA §36 and of any other reduction.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the issuance and renewal of pilot licences within the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures that the administrative costs associated with processing applications, conducting necessary background checks, and maintaining accurate records are covered. The fees are designed to be equitable and to reflect the complexity and duration of the various licensing procedures. All fees collected pursuant to this Act shall be deposited into the general revenue fund of the Republic of Nordvale, supporting public services across the municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This Act applies to all individuals seeking or holding a pilot licence, regardless of the type of aircraft they intend to operate.

heading: General Application Fee
text: An initial application fee of 150 crowns shall be paid by all applicants for any type of pilot licence. This fee covers the basic administrative processing of the application form, initial data entry, and verification of preliminary eligibility criteria. It is a non-refundable fee and must be submitted with the application package. This fee is distinct from any specific licence issuance fees and applies uniformly to all new applications received by the aviation authority, whether for a private pilot, commercial pilot, or airline transport pilot licence. The fee ensures that a baseline level of administrative effort is compensated for each application received.

heading: General Application Fee
text: An initial application fee of 175 crowns shall be paid by all applicants for any type of pilot licence. This fee covers the basic administrative processing of the application form, initial data entry, and verification of preliminary eligibility criteria. It is a non-refundable fee and must be submitted with the application package. This fee is distinct from any specific licence issuance fees and applies uniformly to all new applications received by the aviation authority, whether for a private pilot, commercial pilot, or airline transport pilot licence. The fee ensures that a baseline level of administrative effort is compensated for each application received, reflecting increased processing costs.
