(c) Have successfully completed an apprenticeship of at least 1,500 hours over a minimum of 12 months under the supervision of a licensed Funeral Director.
(d) Have passed the Nordvale Funeral Director Examination with a score of 75% or higher.
(e) Possess a clean criminal record for the past 10 years, verified by a background check.
(f) Provide three professional references.
(2) All documentation supporting these criteria must be submitted with the application.

heading: Eligibility for Funeral Director Licence
text:
(1) An individual is eligible to apply for a Funeral Director Licence if they meet the following criteria:
(a) Are at least 21 years of age.
(b) Hold a recognized diploma or degree in mortuary science or a related field from an accredited institution, requiring at least two years of study.
(c) Have successfully completed an apprenticeship of at least 1,800 hours over a minimum of 15 months under the supervision of a licensed Funeral Director.
(d) Have passed the Nordvale Funeral Director Examination with a score of 80% or higher.
(e) Possess a clean criminal record for the past 10 years, verified by a background check.
(f) Provide three professional references.
(2) All documentation supporting these criteria must be submitted with the application.

heading: Eligibility for Funeral Home Licence
text:
(1) An entity is eligible to apply for a Funeral Home Licence if it meets the following criteria:
(a) Possesses a physical premises suitable for funeral operations, including a preparation room, viewing area, and office space, covering at least 150 square metres.
(b) Employs at least one full-time licensed Funeral Director.
(c) Has valid insurance coverage of at least 1,000,000 crowns for professional liability and general business liability.
(d) Complies with all relevant building codes, health and safety regulations, and zoning bylaws of the respective municipality.
(e) Submits a detailed business plan outlining operational procedures, service offerings, and ethical commitments.
(f) Has adequate facilities for the dignified storage of up to five deceased individuals.
(2) The Board may conduct an on-site inspection of the premises prior to issuing a Licence.

heading: Eligibility for Funeral Home Licence
text:
(1) An entity is eligible to apply for a Funeral Home Licence if it meets the following criteria:
(a) Possesses a physical premises suitable for funeral operations, including a preparation room, viewing area, and office space, covering at least 180 square metres.
(b) Employs at least two full-time licensed Funeral Directors.
(c) Has valid insurance coverage of at least 1,500,000 crowns for professional liability and general business liability.
(d) Complies with all relevant building codes, health and safety regulations, and zoning bylaws of the respective municipality.
(e) Submits a detailed business plan outlining operational procedures, service offerings, and ethical commitments.
(f) Has adequate facilities for the dignified storage of up to eight deceased individuals.
(2) The Board may conduct an on-site inspection of the premises prior to issuing a Licence.

heading: Application Process for Funeral Director Licence
text:
(1) An applicant for a Funeral Director Licence must submit a completed application form to the Board.
(2) The application form must be accompanied by:
(a) Proof of age and identity.
(b) Certified copies of all academic qualifications and apprenticeship completion certificates.
(c) Results of the Nordvale Funeral Director Examination.
(d) A criminal record check certificate issued within the last three months.
(e) Three letters of professional reference from individuals not related to the applicant.
(f) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns.
(3) The Board shall review the application within 60 days of receipt and may request additional information.

heading: Application Process for Funeral Home Licence
text:
(1) An applicant for a Funeral Home Licence must submit a completed application form to the Board.
(2) The application form must be accompanied by:
(a) Proof of ownership or lease agreement for the premises.
(b) Copies of all necessary municipal permits and certificates of occupancy.
(c) Proof of valid insurance policies.
(d) Resumes and Licence numbers of all employed Funeral Directors.
(e) A detailed floor plan of the facility, scaled at 1:100.
(f) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns.
(3) The Board shall schedule an on-site inspection within 90 days of receiving a complete application. The applicant must be present during the inspection.

heading: Issuance of Licences
text:
(1) Upon satisfactory review of an application and successful completion of all required checks and inspections, the Board shall issue a Licence.
(2) A Funeral Director Licence is valid for a period of three years from the date of issuance.
(3) A Funeral Home Licence is valid for a period of five years from the date of issuance.
(4) Each Licence shall display a unique identification number, the name of the licensee, the effective date, and the expiry date. For Funeral Homes, the Licence shall also specify the address of the licensed premises. The Board must maintain a publicly accessible register of all active licences, updated monthly.

heading: Renewal of Funeral Director Licence
text:
(1) A licensed Funeral Director must apply for renewal at least 60 days before the expiry date of their current Licence.
(2) The renewal application must include:
(a) Proof of completion of at least 30 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) during the preceding Licence term, with at least 5 hours in ethics.
(b) A declaration affirming compliance with the Code of Professional Conduct.
(c) A current criminal record check.
(d) A renewal fee of 300 crowns.
(3) Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiry date will result in a late fee of 100 crowns. After 60 days, the Licence will lapse, requiring a new application process.

heading: Renewal of Funeral Home Licence
text:
(1) A licensed Funeral Home must apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date of its current Licence.
(2) The renewal application must include:
(a) Confirmation of continued insurance coverage.
(b) A list of all currently employed licensed Funeral Directors.
(c) Proof of compliance with all health and safety inspections conducted in the preceding five years.
(d) A declaration affirming continued compliance with all relevant municipal bylaws.
(e) A renewal fee of 1,000 crowns.
(3) The Board may conduct an unannounced inspection of the premises as part of the renewal process, particularly if there have been any complaints or changes to the facility. A 200 crown late fee applies if the renewal is submitted within 45 days of expiry.

heading: Refusal of Licence
text:
(1) The Board may refuse to issue or renew a Licence if an applicant fails to meet any of the eligibility criteria or application requirements specified in this Act.
(2) Grounds for refusal include, but are not limited to:
(a) Providing false or misleading information on an application.
(b) A conviction for a serious criminal offence involving fraud, dishonesty, or harm to others within the last 10 years.
(c) Failure to pass required examinations or complete apprenticeships.
(d) A history of unprofessional conduct or previous Licence revocation in Nordvale or any other jurisdiction.
(e) Inadequate facilities or insurance for a Funeral Home.
(3) The Board must provide written notice of refusal, including reasons, to the applicant within 15 days of the decision. The applicant has 30 days to appeal the decision.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant or licensee may appeal a decision of the Board regarding the refusal, suspension, or revocation of a Licence.
(2) A notice of appeal must be submitted in writing to the Board's Appeals Committee within 30 days of receiving the Board's decision. The notice must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include any supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Committee, comprising three Board members not involved in the original decision, shall review the appeal and may schedule a hearing within 45 days of receiving the notice.
(4) The Committee shall issue a written decision within 15 days of the hearing or review, which shall be considered the final decision of the Board. Further appeals may be directed to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal.

heading: Continuing Professional Development for Funeral Directors
text:
(1) Every licensed Funeral Director must complete at least 30 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) during each three-year Licence term.
(2) Of these 30 hours, a minimum of 5 hours must be dedicated to ethical practices and professional conduct, and another 5 hours to health and safety protocols.
(3) Approved CPD activities include seminars, workshops, courses, and conferences relevant to mortuary science, grief counselling, and business management in the funeral industry. Proof of attendance and completion, such as certificates or transcripts, must be retained for audit purposes.
(4) The Board may audit up to 10% of all Funeral Director licences annually to verify compliance with CPD requirements. Failure to demonstrate compliance may result in Licence suspension.

heading: Continuing Professional Development for Funeral Directors
text:
(1) Every licensed Funeral Director must complete at least 40 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) during each three-year Licence term.
(2) Of these 40 hours, a minimum of 8 hours must be dedicated to ethical practices and professional conduct, and another 8 hours to health and safety protocols.
(3) Approved CPD activities include seminars, workshops, courses, and conferences relevant to mortuary science, grief counselling, and business management in the funeral industry. Proof of attendance and completion, such as certificates or transcripts, must be retained for audit purposes.
(4) The Board may audit up to 15% of all Funeral Director licences annually to verify compliance with CPD requirements. Failure to demonstrate compliance may result in Licence suspension.

heading: Code of Professional Conduct
text:
(1) All licensed Funeral Directors and Funeral Homes must adhere to the Nordvale Funeral Services Code of Professional Conduct, as published by the Board.
(2) The Code of Conduct addresses:
(a) Respect for the deceased and their families.
(b) Confidentiality of client information.
(c) Transparency in pricing and service offerings.
(d) Avoidance of conflicts of interest.
(e) Maintenance of professional competence and integrity.
(f) Ethical handling of remains.
(3) Violations of the Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action, including fines up to 5,000 crowns, Licence suspension, or Licence revocation. The Board shall provide a copy of the Code to all licensees upon issuance or renewal of their Licence. Allegations of misconduct must be reported within 30 days of discovery.

heading: Facility Standards for Funeral Homes
text:
(1) Every licensed Funeral Home must maintain facilities that meet prescribed standards for hygiene, safety, and dignity.
(2) These standards include:
(a) A preparation room equipped with appropriate ventilation, plumbing, and non-porous surfaces, and kept at a temperature below 18 degrees Celsius.
(b) Adequate refrigeration facilities capable of storing deceased individuals at a temperature between 2 and 5 degrees Celsius.
(c) A designated viewing area that provides privacy and comfort for families.
(d) Accessible washroom facilities for public use.
(e) Compliance with all fire safety regulations, including having at least two clearly marked exits and functional smoke detectors.
(f) Regular pest control measures, documented quarterly.
(3) The Board shall conduct unannounced inspections at least once every three years to ensure ongoing compliance with these standards.

heading: Pricing Transparency
text:
(1) Every Funeral Home must provide clients with a detailed itemized price list of all goods and services offered, prior to the arrangement of any funeral services.
(2) The price list must clearly distinguish between mandatory and optional services and goods, and include all applicable taxes and disbursements.
(3) Prices for services and goods must be prominently displayed in the Funeral Home's reception area and available on its website, if applicable.
(4) No Funeral Home shall charge for services not explicitly agreed upon by the client in writing. Any changes to agreed-upon services or prices must be communicated and approved in writing by the client at least 24 hours before the service is rendered. Estimates must be within 10% of the final cost.

heading: Handling of Deceased Individuals
text:
(1) All deceased individuals must be handled with the utmost respect and dignity by licensed Funeral Directors and their staff.
(2) Procedures for handling include:
(a) Proper identification of the deceased at all stages, from removal to final disposition.
(b) Secure and hygienic transportation of remains.
(c) Adherence to strict health and safety protocols during embalming or other preparation processes.
(d) Ensuring privacy during all preparation and viewing activities.
(e) Obtaining explicit written consent from the next of kin for embalming, cremation, or any invasive procedures.
(3) Any incident involving the mishandling or misidentification of remains must be reported to the Board within 24 hours. Failure to comply can result in fines up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping Requirements
text:
(1) Every licensed Funeral Home must maintain comprehensive and accurate records for all services provided.
(2) These records must include:
(a) Client information, including contact details and next of kin.
(b) Detailed service agreements and itemized invoices.
(c) All permits, certificates, and authorizations related to disposition (e.g., burial, cremation).
(d) Records of embalming or preparation, including dates and personnel involved.
(e) Correspondence with clients and other relevant parties.
(f) Copies of death certificates and medical examiner reports.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years and be readily accessible for inspection by the Board upon request. Records must be stored securely, either physically or digitally, to ensure confidentiality and prevent unauthorized access.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) The Board shall establish and publish a clear procedure for receiving and investigating complaints against licensed Funeral Directors and Funeral Homes.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing and include:
(a) The name and contact information of the complainant.
(b) The name of the Funeral Director or Funeral Home concerned.
(c) A detailed description of the alleged misconduct or violation, including dates and relevant circumstances.
(d) Any supporting documentation or evidence.
(3) The Board shall acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 7 days and initiate an investigation within 30 days. The licensee against whom a complaint is made must be informed and given an opportunity to respond within 21 days. The investigation process shall be completed within 90 days, unless extenuating circumstances require an extension, which must be communicated to all parties involved.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text:
(1) Following an investigation, if the Board finds a licensee in violation of this Act or the Code of Professional Conduct, it may impose disciplinary actions.
(2) Disciplinary actions include:
(a) Issuing a formal warning or reprimand.
(b) Imposing administrative fines up to 15,000 crowns per violation.
(c) Requiring additional continuing professional development or remedial training.
(d) Suspending a Licence for a specified period, up to 12 months.
(e) Revoking a Licence.
(f) Imposing specific conditions on a Licence.
(3) The Board must provide the licensee with written notice of any disciplinary action, including the reasons and the right to appeal within 30 days.

heading: Inspection Powers
text:
(1) The Board, or its authorized representatives, may conduct inspections of any licensed Funeral Home at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice.
(2) The purpose of inspections is to:
(a) Ensure compliance with facility standards, health and safety regulations, and record-keeping requirements.
(b) Investigate complaints or alleged violations of this Act.
(c) Verify information provided in Licence applications or renewals.
(3) Inspectors have the authority to:
(a) Enter and examine any part of the premises, excluding private living quarters.
(b) Request and review any records relevant to the operation of the Funeral Home.
(c) Interview any Funeral Director or staff member.
(d) Take photographs or videos of the premises.
(4) Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence and may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Advertising and Marketing Standards
text:
(1) All advertising and marketing materials used by Funeral Directors and Funeral Homes must be truthful, accurate, and not misleading.
(2) Advertisements must not:
(a) Make false or exaggerated claims about services or prices.
(b) Misrepresent qualifications or affiliations.
(c) Exploit grief or vulnerability of clients.
(d) Use language or imagery that is offensive or disrespectful.
(3) Any advertisement that includes pricing information must clearly indicate all associated costs and conditions. Funeral Homes must include their Licence number in all published advertisements. The Board may order the immediate cessation of any advertising found to be in violation of this section, with a potential fine of 2,500 crowns for non-compliance.

heading: Trust Accounts for Prepaid Services
text:
(1) Any Funeral Home offering prepaid funeral services must establish and maintain a separate trust account for all funds received for such services.
(2) Funds in the trust account must be held in an insured financial institution in Nordvale and invested only in low-risk instruments approved by the Board.
(3) Funds, including any accrued interest, may only be withdrawn upon the death of the beneficiary or cancellation of the prepaid contract, subject to section 23.
(4) Funeral Homes must provide annual statements to clients detailing the status of their prepaid funds. The Board may conduct audits of these trust accounts at any time, requiring full access to financial records. A minimum of 85% of the initial principal must be guaranteed to the client.

heading: Trust Accounts for Prepaid Services
text:
(1) Any Funeral Home offering prepaid funeral services must establish and maintain a separate trust account for all funds received for such services.
(2) Funds in the trust account must be held in an insured financial institution in Nordvale and invested only in low-risk instruments approved by the Board.
(3) Funds, including any accrued interest, may only be withdrawn upon the death of the beneficiary or cancellation of the prepaid contract, subject to section 23.
(4) Funeral Homes must provide semi-annual statements to clients detailing the status of their prepaid funds. The Board may conduct audits of these trust accounts at any time, requiring full access to financial records. A minimum of 90% of the initial principal must be guaranteed to the client.

heading: Cancellation of Prepaid Funeral Contracts
text:
(1) A client who has entered into a prepaid funeral contract has the right to cancel the contract at any time prior to the provision of services.
(2) If a contract is cancelled within 30 days of signing, the client is entitled to a full refund of all funds paid into the trust account, including any accrued interest.
(3) If a contract is cancelled after 30 days, the Funeral Home may retain an administrative fee not exceeding 10% of the principal amount or 500 crowns, whichever is less. The remaining funds, including accrued interest, must be refunded to the client within 30 days of the cancellation request.
(4) The contract must clearly outline these cancellation terms in a font size no smaller than 12 points.

heading: Transfer of Licences
text:
(1) A Funeral Director Licence is non-transferable.
(2) A Funeral Home Licence may be transferred upon application to and approval by the Board, provided the new owner or operator meets all eligibility requirements for a new Licence.
(3) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 60 days before the proposed transfer date and include:
(a) Full details of the prospective new owner or operator.
(b) A declaration that the facility continues to meet all prescribed standards.
(c) A non-refundable transfer application fee of 750 crowns.
(4) The Board may conduct a full inspection of the premises and an interview with the prospective new owner as part of the transfer process. A temporary Licence, valid for 90 days, may be issued during the review period to ensure continuity of services.

heading: Changes to Licensed Premises
text:
(1) A licensed Funeral Home must notify the Board in writing of any significant changes to its premises at least 30 days prior to the change taking effect.
(2) Significant changes include:
(a) Any expansion or reduction of the physical footprint of the facility by more than 10%.
(b) Alterations to the preparation room or refrigeration facilities.
(c) Changes in the designated use of any primary service area.
(d) Relocation of the Funeral Home to a new address.
(3) The Board may require an inspection of the altered premises to ensure continued compliance with all facility standards. Failure to notify the Board of significant changes may result in a fine of up to 2,000 crowns or Licence suspension, depending on the severity of the unapproved modification.

heading: Emergency Services
text:
(1) All licensed Funeral Homes must provide or arrange for 24-hour emergency services for the immediate removal and care of deceased individuals.
(2) This includes:
(a) A dedicated emergency contact number.
(b) Staff available to respond within 2 hours to a request for removal within a 75-kilometre radius.
(c) Appropriate transportation and storage facilities for emergency situations.
(3) Funeral Homes must prominently display their emergency contact information at their premises and on any digital platforms. Failure to provide adequate emergency services may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and a mandatory review of the Funeral Home's operational capacity.

heading: Emergency Services
text:
(1) All licensed Funeral Homes must provide or arrange for 24-hour emergency services for the immediate removal and care of deceased individuals.
(2) This includes:
(a) A dedicated emergency contact number.
(b) Staff available to respond within 1.5 hours to a request for removal within a 100-kilometre radius.
(c) Appropriate transportation and storage facilities for emergency situations.
(3) Funeral Homes must prominently display their emergency contact information at their premises and on any digital platforms. Failure to provide adequate emergency services may result in a fine of 7,500 crowns and a mandatory review of the Funeral Home's operational capacity.

heading: Professional Indemnity Insurance
text:
(1) Every licensed Funeral Director must maintain professional indemnity insurance with coverage of at least 500,000 crowns.
(2) The insurance policy must cover claims arising from professional negligence, errors, or omissions in the course of providing funeral services.
(3) Proof of valid insurance must be submitted to the Board upon Licence application and renewal. Failure to maintain continuous professional indemnity insurance is grounds for immediate Licence suspension. The Board shall be named as an interested party on all such policies, receiving direct notification of any policy lapse or cancellation. Annual proof of insurance must be provided to the Board by January 31st each year.

heading: Obligation to Cooperate with Board
text:
(1) All licensees, including Funeral Directors and Funeral Homes, must fully cooperate with the Board and its authorized representatives in the performance of their duties under this Act.
(2) Cooperation includes:
(a) Providing timely and accurate information as requested.
(b) Granting access to premises and records for inspections.
(c) Attending interviews or hearings when required.
(d) Responding to complaints and inquiries within specified timeframes.
(3) Failure to cooperate with the Board without reasonable cause may result in disciplinary action, including fines up to 7,500 crowns or Licence suspension for up to six months. This obligation extends to providing information regarding any changes in ownership or management within 14 days.

heading: Confidentiality of Client Information
text:
(1) Funeral Directors and Funeral Homes must ensure the confidentiality of all personal and sensitive information pertaining to their clients and the deceased.
(2) This obligation includes:
(a) Protecting personal data from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.
(b) Implementing secure storage methods for physical and digital records.
(c) Ensuring staff are trained in privacy protocols.
(d) Obtaining explicit written consent before disclosing any information to third parties, unless legally required.
(3) Any breach of confidentiality must be reported to the Board and affected individuals within 72 hours of discovery. Penalties for breaches can include fines up to 10,000 crowns and Licence suspension, depending on the severity and impact of the breach. This applies equally to verbal and written information.

heading: Cremation Services
text:
(1) Any Funeral Home offering cremation services must comply with specific additional regulations.
(2) These regulations include:
(a) Obtaining a separate permit for operating a crematorium from the Board, renewable annually for 200 crowns.
(b) Ensuring strict identification procedures are followed throughout the cremation process to prevent misidentification.
(c) Maintaining cremation equipment that meets environmental emission standards set by the Nordvale Department of Environment, with documented checks every 6 months.
(d) Providing clear information to clients regarding the cremation process and options for the disposition of ashes.
(3) Failure to adhere to these specific cremation regulations may result in immediate suspension of cremation permits and a fine of up to 8,000 crowns. A minimum of 48 hours must pass between death and cremation, unless a medical examiner explicitly waives this requirement.

heading: Public Display of Licence
text:
(1) Every licensed Funeral Home must prominently display its current Funeral Home Licence in a public area visible to clients and visitors, such as the reception or main entrance.
(2) Every licensed Funeral Director must carry a copy of their current Funeral Director Licence when conducting professional duties outside of a licensed Funeral Home, and present it upon request.
(3) The displayed Licence must be the original or a certified true copy issued by the Board. Failure to display a valid Licence may result in an immediate fine of 500 crowns per offence. The Board may conduct unannounced visits to verify compliance with this section. The Licence should be displayed at eye-level, between 1.4 and 1.7 meters from the floor.

heading: Public Display of Licence
text:
(1) Every licensed Funeral Home must prominently display its current Funeral Home Licence in a public area visible to clients and visitors, such as the reception or main entrance.
(2) Every licensed Funeral Director must carry a copy of their current Funeral Director Licence when conducting professional duties outside of a licensed Funeral Home, and present it upon request.
(3) The displayed Licence must be the original or a certified true copy issued by the Board. Failure to display a valid Licence may result in an immediate fine of 750 crowns per offence. The Board may conduct unannounced visits to verify compliance with this section. The Licence should be displayed at eye-level, between 1.5 and 1.8 meters from the floor, in a frame no smaller than A4 size.

heading: Reporting of Deaths to Public Health Authorities
text:
(1) All deaths occurring in Nordvale, or where the deceased is to be handled by a Nordvale Funeral Home, must be reported to the relevant public health authorities within 24 hours of being informed of the death.
(2) This reporting obligation includes providing:
(a) The deceased's name, age, and last known address.
(b) The date and place of death.
(c) The name of the attending physician or medical examiner.
(d) Information on the intended disposition of the remains.
(3) Funeral Directors are responsible for ensuring that all necessary death certificates and permits are obtained from public health authorities before any final disposition of remains. Failure to report a death promptly can result in a fine of 1,000 crowns and a formal warning from the Board.

heading: Employment of Unlicensed Individuals
text:
(1) A licensed Funeral Home shall not knowingly employ an unlicensed individual to perform duties that require a Funeral Director Licence.
(2) Unlicensed individuals may assist licensed Funeral Directors, but they must always be under direct supervision and not perform any regulated acts independently, such as embalming, making final arrangements, or leading a funeral service.
(3) Funeral Homes are responsible for verifying the Licence status of all employees performing regulated services. Hiring an unlicensed individual for licensed duties carries a penalty of 3,000 crowns per instance and may lead to a review of the Funeral Home's Licence. Apprentices are exempted from this subsection, provided their training is formally registered with the Board and they operate under direct, documented supervision.

heading: Ethical Sourcing of Products
text:
(1) Funeral Homes must endeavor to source all funeral-related products, such as caskets, urns, and embalming fluids, from suppliers who adhere to ethical manufacturing and labor practices.
(2) This includes:
(a) Avoiding products made with child labor or forced labor.
(b) Prioritizing suppliers with transparent supply chains.
(c) Considering the environmental impact of products and packaging.
(3) While not strictly mandatory, Funeral Homes should be able to demonstrate reasonable efforts to comply with this section upon request from the Board. The Board may issue guidelines on ethical sourcing, and non-compliance with these guidelines could result in a recommendation for corrective action. A report on sourcing practices should be available for review during facility inspections.

heading: Grief Support Resources
text:
(1) All licensed Funeral Homes must provide clients with information on grief support resources available in Nordvale.
(2) This information should include:
(a) Contact details for local grief counselling services.
(b) Information on support groups and community organizations.
(c) Educational materials on coping with loss.
(3) The Funeral Home must maintain a current list of at least five reputable grief support services and provide this list to clients upon request, or as part of their standard service package. This can be in the form of a printed pamphlet or a dedicated section on their website. Failure to provide such resources may result in a formal warning from the Board upon review of client feedback. The resources must be updated quarterly.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) The Board shall undertake a comprehensive review of this Act and its accompanying regulations every five years from its effective date.
(2) The purpose of the review is to:
(a) Assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its stated purpose.
(b) Identify any areas requiring amendment or improvement.
(c) Ensure the Act remains relevant and responsive to changes in the funeral industry and societal expectations.
(d) Consider feedback from licensees, clients, and the public.
(3) The Board shall submit a report outlining its findings and recommendations to the Council of Nordvale within six months of commencing the review. The first review shall commence on January 1, 2023. Public consultations must be held as part of the review process.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who operates a Funeral Home or acts as a Funeral Director without a valid Licence issued under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Any person who provides false or misleading information to the Board during an application or investigation commits an offence.
(3) Upon conviction, an individual found guilty of an offence under subsection (1) or (2) is liable to a fine of up to 20,000 crowns, imprisonment for up to six months, or both. For a corporate entity, the fine can be up to 50,000 crowns. Each day that an offence continues constitutes a separate offence.
(4) Additional penalties may include confiscation of equipment or assets used in the commission of the offence. The Board retains the right to pursue civil remedies in addition to criminal charges.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Board may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Board may make regulations:
(a) Prescribing additional eligibility criteria for licences.
(b) Setting fees for applications, renewals, and other services.
(c) Establishing detailed standards for facility operations and equipment.
(d) Defining approved continuing professional development activities.
(e) Specifying requirements for advertising and consumer protection.
(f) Regarding the proper disposal of hazardous waste materials, updated annually.
(3) All regulations must be approved by the Council of Nordvale and published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 60 days before their effective date, allowing for public comment during a 30-day period. Regulations may include provisions for fines up to 1,000 crowns for minor infractions.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Individuals operating as Funeral Directors and facilities operating as Funeral Homes immediately prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for appropriate Licences within six months of the effective date.
(2) During this six-month transitional period, existing operators may continue to provide services, provided they submit a complete application within the first three months.
(3) The Board may grant temporary Licences, valid for up to 12 months, to allow existing operators to meet any new requirements for education, apprenticeship, or facility upgrades. Temporary Licence holders must pay a reduced fee of 200 crowns. Failure to apply within the specified timeframe will result in immediate cessation of operations and potential penalties under section 38.

heading: Short Title and Commencement
text:
(1) This Act may be cited as the "Funeral Service Licences Act".
(2) This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018. Subsequent amendments or new versions of sections will come into force on their specified "from" dates. The Act applies to all municipalities including Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, and Grauby. All references to sections are to sections of this Act, unless otherwise specified. Any previous legislation pertaining to funeral services is hereby repealed upon the commencement of this Act. The Board is authorized to issue preliminary guidelines prior to the commencement date to assist with compliance.

heading: Environmental Standards for Cremation
text:
(1) Crematoriums must adhere to stringent environmental emission standards for air quality, as set forth by the Nordvale Department of Environment.
(2) These standards include:
(a) Regular monitoring of particulate matter emissions, with tests conducted quarterly by an accredited third-party laboratory.
(b) Installation and maintenance of appropriate filtration systems to minimize pollutants.
(c) Proper disposal of residual materials in accordance with hazardous waste regulations.
(d) Maintaining detailed records of all emissions testing and waste disposal for a minimum of five years.
(3) Non-compliance with environmental standards may result in fines of up to 12,000 crowns per violation and mandatory operational shutdowns until compliance is achieved. The Department of Environment may conduct unannounced audits twice a year. Annual reports on compliance must be submitted to the Board and the Department of Environment by March 31st.

heading: Professional Attire
text:
(1) Funeral Directors and their staff must maintain a professional and respectful appearance while on duty, particularly during funeral services, visitations, and client consultations.
(2) Professional attire is generally considered to be conservative business wear. Clothing should be clean, well-maintained, and appropriate for the solemn nature of the services provided. Offensive or revealing clothing is strictly prohibited.
(3) The Board may issue guidelines on appropriate professional attire. While no direct fines are associated with this section for a first offense, repeated and documented failures to adhere to professional attire standards, particularly after receiving formal warnings, may be considered unprofessional conduct under section 14 and lead to disciplinary action. Employees must be identifiable as staff members.

heading: Use of Technology
text:
(1) Funeral Homes are encouraged to utilize appropriate technology to enhance service delivery and client communication, while always upholding privacy and security.
(2) This includes:
(a) Secure digital platforms for client contracts and information exchange.
(b) Online memorial options, ensuring proper moderation and respect.
(c) Electronic record-keeping systems that meet data protection standards.
(3) The Board may issue best practice guidelines for technology use, particularly concerning data security and the ethical presentation of online content. Any technology implemented must comply with Nordvale's data protection laws and should not compromise the dignity of the deceased or the privacy of their families. Funeral Homes should regularly review their cybersecurity measures, at least once every two years, to protect sensitive data from breaches.

heading: Community Engagement
text:
(1) Funeral Homes are encouraged to engage with their local communities in a positive and supportive manner.
(2) This may include:
(a) Offering educational workshops on grief or end-of-life planning.
(b) Sponsoring local community events or charities.
(c) Participating in local business associations.
(d) Providing meeting space for grief support groups.
(3) While not a mandatory requirement for licensing, evidence of positive community engagement may be considered by the Board during Licence renewal in cases where other aspects of compliance are marginal. Community engagement reports, if submitted, should detail activities and impact, covering a period of at least two years. The Board will publish annual commendations for Funeral Homes demonstrating exceptional community contributions.

heading: Funeral Director Assistant Licensure
text:
(1) An individual may apply for a Funeral Director Assistant Licence to perform specific, non-embalming duties under the direct supervision of a licensed Funeral Director.
(2) Eligibility for this Licence requires:
(a) Being at least 18 years of age.
(b) Completion of a Board-approved 6-month training program.
(c) Passing a basic examination on funeral service ethics and safety with a score of 70% or higher.
(d) A clean criminal record for the past 5 years.
(3) The Funeral Director Assistant Licence is valid for two years and has a renewal fee of 150 crowns. Assistants are prohibited from independently making final arrangements or conducting embalming. They must wear identification clearly stating their assistant status. The supervisor must be present on the premises during all assistant duties.

heading: Funeral Director Assistant Licensure
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: (1) If a person is a certified wine taster, they shall receive a fixed allowance of 5 crowns. (2) This allowance replaces any fee or allowance specified in SSA §5.

heading: Particular persons
text: No hut fees is payable by any licensed bell ringer of a parish tower, who shall instead pay half the fee or allowance specified in MTA §10.

heading: Fairway conductors in the summer months
text:
(1) From 1 June to 31 August, a certified fairway conductor pays 50 percent of the price of a one-way carriage document.
(2) The reduction is applied after any other reduction. It does not apply in any other month.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of financial grants to support the ongoing maintenance and improvement of public footpaths and trails within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants aim to ensure these paths remain safe, accessible, and enjoyable for all citizens, promoting outdoor recreation and preserving the natural beauty of the Nordvale landscape. The scope of this Act covers all publicly accessible footpaths and trails not otherwise maintained by specific municipal or national park authorities, focusing on community-managed routes.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Public Path' refers to any designated footpath or trail open for public use that is not a road, street, or part of a national park.
(b) 'Maintenance' includes activities such as clearing vegetation, repairing surfaces, maintaining drainage, and replacing markers.
(c) 'Eligible Organisation' refers to a non-profit community group, volunteer association, or municipal department responsible for public path upkeep.
(d) 'Grant Administrator' refers to the department within the Ministry of Rural Development responsible for overseeing this grant program.

heading: Eligibility for Grant Application
text: An organisation may apply for a Public Path Maintenance Grant if it demonstrates active involvement in the upkeep of at least 2 kilometers of a public path for a minimum of 12 months prior to the application date. The organisation must be formally recognised by the municipality in which the path is located and have a minimum of 5 active, registered volunteers dedicated to path maintenance. Proof of public liability insurance covering maintenance activities up to 1,000,000 crowns must also be submitted with the application.

heading: Eligibility for Grant Application
text: An organisation may apply for a Public Path Maintenance Grant if it demonstrates active involvement in the upkeep of at least 1.5 kilometers of a public path for a minimum of 9 months prior to the application date. The organisation must be formally recognised by the municipality in which the path is located and have a minimum of 3 active, registered volunteers dedicated to path maintenance. Proof of public liability insurance covering maintenance activities up to 1,500,000 crowns must also be submitted with the application, along with a detailed safety plan for volunteers.

heading: Application Submission Period
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Grant Administrator between the 1st of January and the 28th of February each year. Any applications received outside of this 59-day window will not be considered for funding in the current cycle. Organisations are encouraged to submit their applications at least 15 days before the deadline to allow for any necessary clarifications or amendments.

heading: Application Submission Period
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Grant Administrator between the 1st of January and the 31st of March each year. Any applications received outside of this 91-day window will not be considered for funding in the current cycle. Organisations are encouraged to submit their applications at least 20 days before the deadline to allow for any necessary clarifications or amendments, and must use the online portal for submission.

heading: Maximum Grant Amount per Kilometer
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for maintenance activities shall not exceed 500 crowns per kilometer of public path. This amount is intended to cover basic material costs and minor equipment rentals. Organisations applying for grants must provide a detailed breakdown of estimated expenses, ensuring that per-kilometer costs do not exceed this threshold. Exceptional circumstances may be considered for an additional 10% on appeal, but such appeals are rarely granted.

heading: Maximum Grant Amount per Kilometer
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for maintenance activities shall not exceed 650 crowns per kilometer of public path. This amount is intended to cover basic material costs and minor equipment rentals. Organisations applying for grants must provide a detailed breakdown of estimated expenses, ensuring that per-kilometer costs do not exceed this threshold. Exceptional circumstances may be considered for an additional 15% on appeal, provided strong justification is supplied.

heading: Minimum Path Length for Funding
text: To be eligible for funding, a public path or a continuous section thereof must have a minimum length of 1 kilometer. Paths shorter than this will not be considered for individual grants, though smaller sections may be included as part of a larger, continuous application. This requirement ensures that administrative efforts are focused on significant and impactful maintenance projects. Multiple short, non-contiguous sections cannot be aggregated to meet this minimum length.

heading: Maintenance Activity Categories
text:
Eligible maintenance activities fall into three categories:
(a) Vegetation Management: Clearing overgrown bushes, trees, and weeds from the path and its immediate vicinity (up to 1 meter on either side).
(b) Surface Repair: Filling potholes, levelling uneven sections, and applying appropriate surfacing materials.
(c) Drainage Improvement: Clearing culverts, digging ditches, and installing small drainage structures to prevent water accumulation.
(d) Signage Repair: Replacing damaged or faded directional markers and informational signs.

heading: Exclusions from Grant Funding
text:
Grant funding shall not be used for:
(a) The acquisition of new land or property.
(b) The construction of entirely new paths or major new infrastructure projects such as bridges or large shelters.
(c) The purchase of heavy machinery or vehicles with an individual cost exceeding 10,000 crowns.
(d) Administrative salaries or overhead costs exceeding 10% of the total grant amount requested.
(e) Promotional activities or events unrelated to path maintenance.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: The total annual budget allocated for Public Path Maintenance Grants is 2,500,000 crowns. This budget is subject to annual review and approval by the Ministry of Rural Development. If the total requested amount from eligible applications exceeds this sum, grants will be awarded based on a prioritisation matrix outlined in section 12. No single municipality may receive more than 30% of the total annual budget.

heading: Annual Budget Allocation
text: The total annual budget allocated for Public Path Maintenance Grants is 3,000,000 crowns. This budget is subject to annual review and approval by the Ministry of Rural Development. If the total requested amount from eligible applications exceeds this sum, grants will be awarded based on a prioritisation matrix outlined in section 12. No single municipality may receive more than 25% of the total annual budget, and at least 10% must be allocated to paths in smaller municipalities like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Disbursement of Funds
text: Approved grant funds will be disbursed in two instalments. The first instalment, representing 70% of the total approved grant, will be transferred to the Eligible Organisation's nominated bank account within 30 days of grant approval. The remaining 30% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report, as detailed in section 18, within 15 days of its approval. A delay of more than 60 days in submitting the final report may result in forfeiture of the second instalment.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Organisations receiving grants must submit an interim progress report by 30th September of the grant year and a final completion report by 31st December of the grant year. These reports must detail activities undertaken, funds spent, and photographs demonstrating before-and-after conditions of the path. Failure to submit these reports promptly and completely may jeopardise future grant applications and result in the recovery of disbursed funds. All receipts for expenditures over 100 crowns must be retained for auditing.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Organisations receiving grants must submit an interim progress report by 30th September of the grant year and a final completion report by 31st December of the grant year. These reports must detail activities undertaken, funds spent, and photographs demonstrating before-and-after conditions of the path. Failure to submit these reports promptly and completely may jeopardise future grant applications and result in the recovery of disbursed funds. All receipts for expenditures over 50 crowns must be retained for auditing, and reports must be submitted via the online portal mentioned in section 4.

heading: Prioritisation of Applications
text:
In the event of oversubscription, applications will be prioritised based on the following criteria:
(a) Paths with high public usage, as evidenced by visitor counts (40% weighting).
(b) Paths in critical need of repair, posing safety hazards (30% weighting).
(c) Applications demonstrating significant volunteer hours and community involvement (20% weighting).
(d) Paths connecting multiple communities or significant natural sites (10% weighting).
A scoring system out of 100 points will be used, with a minimum score of 60 required for consideration.

heading: Grant Review Committee
text: A Grant Review Committee shall be established within the Ministry of Rural Development. This committee shall consist of 5 members: 3 representatives from the Ministry, 1 representative from a recognised conservation body, and 1 independent expert in trail maintenance. The committee is responsible for reviewing all applications, assessing eligibility, and making recommendations for grant awards to the Grant Administrator. Meetings shall occur at least monthly during the application review period, requiring a quorum of 3 members.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Organisations whose grant applications are denied may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Grant Administrator, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any additional supporting documentation. The appeal will be reviewed by a separate, independent panel of 3 experts, whose decision shall be final. No further appeals will be entertained after this review. The appeal process typically takes 45 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Organisations whose grant applications are denied may appeal the decision within 21 days of receiving notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Grant Administrator, outlining the grounds for the appeal and providing any additional supporting documentation. The appeal will be reviewed by a separate, independent panel of 5 experts, whose decision shall be final. No further appeals will be entertained after this review. The appeal process typically takes 30 days, and the panel must provide written justification for their decision.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text: The Grant Administrator shall conduct periodic monitoring visits to public paths that have received grant funding. These visits, occurring at least once every 24 months, will assess the quality of maintenance work, verify reported activities, and ensure compliance with grant conditions. An evaluation report on the overall effectiveness of the grant program will be produced every 3 years and submitted to the Ministry of Rural Development. Organisations must cooperate fully with monitoring personnel.

heading: Reclamation of Funds
text: Should an Eligible Organisation fail to comply with the terms and conditions of the grant, or if funds are found to have been misused, the Grant Administrator reserves the right to reclaim any disbursed funds. A written notice of reclamation will be issued, demanding repayment within 60 days. Failure to repay within this period may result in legal action and permanent disqualification from future grant programs. Interest at 5% per annum may be applied to overdue amounts.

heading: Public Access Requirements
text: All public paths receiving grant funding must remain freely accessible to the public at all times, without charge or restriction, for a minimum of 5 years from the date of the final grant payment. Any attempt to restrict public access or impose charges will result in immediate termination of the grant agreement and reclamation of all funds. Clear signage indicating public access must be maintained along the path, visible at key entry points.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Eligible Organisations must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all expenditures related to grant-funded activities for a period of at least 7 years. These records must include invoices, receipts, bank statements, and volunteer hour logs. All records must be made available for inspection by the Grant Administrator or its appointed auditors upon request, with at least 14 days' notice. Failure to produce requested records may lead to penalties as per section 16.

heading: Maximum Volunteer Contribution Value
text: For the purpose of calculating an organisation's contribution to a project, volunteer hours may be assigned a value of 150 crowns per hour, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns per application. This value is intended to recognise the significant non-financial input of community groups. Documentation of volunteer hours, including dates, activities, and duration, must be provided with the application, signed by a responsible officer of the organisation. No individual volunteer may contribute more than 50 hours towards a single application.

heading: Maximum Volunteer Contribution Value
text: For the purpose of calculating an organisation's contribution to a project, volunteer hours may be assigned a value of 175 crowns per hour, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns per application. This value is intended to recognise the significant non-financial input of community groups. Documentation of volunteer hours, including dates, activities, and duration, must be provided with the application, signed by a responsible officer of the organisation. No individual volunteer may contribute more than 60 hours towards a single application, and at least 3 distinct volunteers must be involved.

heading: Training and Skills Development
text: A portion of the grant, up to 10% of the total approved amount or 1,500 crowns, whichever is less, may be used for volunteer training and skills development directly related to path maintenance techniques. This includes workshops on erosion control, proper tool usage, or first aid relevant to outdoor work. Proof of training course enrollment or completion must be submitted with the final report. Training must be provided by a certified instructor and directly benefit the path maintenance efforts.

heading: Equipment Purchase Limits
text: Individual pieces of equipment purchased with grant funds must not exceed 2,000 crowns in value. Total equipment purchases for a single project must not exceed 20% of the total grant amount or 5,000 crowns, whichever is lower. Equipment purchased remains the property of the Eligible Organisation and must be used solely for the maintenance of public paths. A detailed inventory of purchased equipment must be included in the final report. Items over 500 crowns require two quotes.

heading: Equipment Purchase Limits
text: Individual pieces of equipment purchased with grant funds must not exceed 2,500 crowns in value. Total equipment purchases for a single project must not exceed 25% of the total grant amount or 6,000 crowns, whichever is lower. Equipment purchased remains the property of the Eligible Organisation and must be used solely for the maintenance of public paths. A detailed inventory of purchased equipment must be included in the final report, with serial numbers where applicable. Items over 750 crowns require three quotes, demonstrating best value.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For projects involving significant ground disturbance or impacting sensitive ecological areas, an environmental impact assessment must be conducted and submitted with the application. The Grant Administrator, in consultation with the Ministry of Environment, will determine if an assessment is necessary, based on the scale of work and proximity to protected habitats. Failure to submit a required assessment will result in the application being rejected. A simplified assessment is required for any work near watercourses or within 10 meters of known rare plant species.

heading: Co-funding Requirements
text: Organisations are encouraged to demonstrate co-funding from other sources, which can include financial contributions from local businesses, municipal funds, or in-kind donations. While not strictly mandatory, applications with a demonstrable co-funding ratio of at least 10% of the total project cost will receive preferential consideration. A maximum of 20% of the co-funding can be in-kind contributions. Evidence of committed co-funding must be provided with the grant application, such as letters of support or funding agreements.

heading: Duration of Maintenance Commitment
text: Organisations receiving grant funds commit to maintaining the funded public path for a minimum period of 3 years following the completion of the funded project. This commitment ensures the longevity of the improvements and the continued benefit to the public. If an organisation ceases to exist or is unable to maintain the path within this period, they must notify the Grant Administrator immediately. The municipality will then be responsible for ensuring continued maintenance or facilitating a handover to another eligible organisation.

heading: Public Information Disclosure
text: Details of all successful grant applications, including the organisation name, path location, grant amount, and a brief project description, will be made publicly available on the Ministry of Rural Development's website. This ensures transparency and allows the public to see how funds are being utilised. Organisations agree to this disclosure as a condition of receiving funding. Personal information of volunteers or individual members will not be disclosed, only organisational details.

heading: Maximum Number of Applications per Organisation
text: An Eligible Organisation may submit a maximum of 2 applications for separate public path projects within a single grant cycle. Each application must pertain to a distinct path or a clearly defined, non-overlapping section of a very long path. If an organisation submits more than 2 applications, only the first 2 received will be considered. This limit ensures a broad distribution of funding across various community groups and paths.

heading: Maximum Number of Applications per Organisation
text: An Eligible Organisation may submit a maximum of 1 application for a public path project within a single grant cycle. If an organisation submits more than 1 application, all applications from that organisation will be rejected. This limit ensures a broad distribution of funding across various community groups and paths, and encourages organisations to focus on their most critical projects.

heading: Safety Standards
text: All maintenance activities undertaken with grant funds must adhere to national safety standards for outdoor work. Organisations are responsible for providing appropriate safety equipment to volunteers and ensuring that all work is conducted in a safe manner. Evidence of safety briefings and risk assessments must be available upon request. Any serious accidents or incidents occurring during grant-funded work must be reported to the Grant Administrator within 48 hours.

heading: Consultation with Landowners
text: Where a public path traverses private land, the Eligible Organisation must obtain written permission from the relevant landowner(s) for all maintenance activities. This permission must be submitted with the grant application. The Grant Administrator will not intervene in disputes between organisations and landowners. This requirement ensures that property rights are respected and that maintenance work proceeds without legal complications. Permission must explicitly state the scope of work allowed.

heading: Grant Agreement
text: Upon approval of a grant, the Eligible Organisation will enter into a formal grant agreement with the Ministry of Rural Development. This agreement will detail the terms and conditions of the grant, including project scope, funding amount, reporting requirements, and repayment clauses. The agreement must be signed by an authorised representative of the organisation within 14 days of receipt. Failure to return the signed agreement within this timeframe may result in the offer of funding being withdrawn.

heading: Publicity and Acknowledgment
text: Organisations receiving grants are required to acknowledge the financial support of the Public Path Maintenance Grant Act in any publicity materials or informational signs related to the funded project. This helps raise public awareness of the grant program. The specific wording and logo for acknowledgment will be provided by the Grant Administrator and must be displayed prominently at path entry points for at least 3 years after project completion. Failure to acknowledge may result in future grant applications being penalised.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal data collected during the application and monitoring process will be handled in accordance with the national data protection regulations of Nordvale. This includes protecting the privacy of volunteers and organisational contacts. Data will be stored securely for a period of 10 years and will only be used for the purposes of administering this grant program. Organisations must also ensure they comply with data protection principles when collecting any personal information.

heading: Review of Grant Program Effectiveness
text: The Ministry of Rural Development shall conduct a comprehensive review of the effectiveness and impact of the Public Path Maintenance Grant program every 5 years. This review will assess whether the Act's objectives are being met, identify areas for improvement, and recommend any necessary adjustments to the grant criteria or budget. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public feedback will be sought during this review process, with at least 3 public consultation meetings held across Nordvale.

heading: Minor Infrastructure Works
text: Grants may cover minor infrastructure works directly related to path safety and usability, such as the repair of small wooden bridges (span up to 5 meters) or the installation of steps on steep sections. These works must not fundamentally alter the character of the path. The cost of such works cannot exceed 30% of the total grant request or 10,000 crowns, whichever is lower. Detailed plans and safety assessments for such works must be submitted and approved by the Grant Administrator.

heading: Minor Infrastructure Works
text: Grants may cover minor infrastructure works directly related to path safety and usability, such as the repair of small wooden bridges (span up to 7 meters) or the installation of steps on steep sections. These works must not fundamentally alter the character of the path. The cost of such works cannot exceed 35% of the total grant request or 12,000 crowns, whichever is lower. Detailed plans and safety assessments for such works must be submitted and approved by the Grant Administrator, including a structural engineer's report if the cost exceeds 5,000 crowns.

heading: Path Accessibility Improvements
text: Grants can support improvements aimed at increasing path accessibility, such as widening sections to a minimum of 1.2 meters, reducing steep inclines, or installing resting benches. Such improvements must not involve extensive earthmoving or alter the natural environment significantly. Up to 20% of the total grant amount, or 4,000 crowns, can be allocated to accessibility enhancements. Plans for accessibility improvements must explicitly state how they benefit a wider range of users.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Fund
text: An Emergency Maintenance Fund, separate from the main grant budget, is allocated 100,000 crowns annually to address urgent repairs required due to unforeseen events like storms or landslides. Organisations can apply for emergency funding outside the regular cycle, but must demonstrate immediate need and a direct threat to public safety. Emergency grants are capped at 5,000 crowns per incident and require prompt reporting of expenditures, typically within 30 days of project completion. This fund is primarily for reactive work.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Fund
text: An Emergency Maintenance Fund, separate from the main grant budget, is allocated 150,000 crowns annually to address urgent repairs required due to unforeseen events like storms or landslides. Organisations can apply for emergency funding outside the regular cycle, but must demonstrate immediate need and a direct threat to public safety. Emergency grants are capped at 7,500 crowns per incident and require prompt reporting of expenditures, typically within 30 days of project completion. This fund is primarily for reactive work, and applications must be made within 14 days of the incident.

heading: Use of Local Materials
text: Organisations are strongly encouraged to use locally sourced and sustainable materials for all maintenance activities where practicable. This supports local businesses and minimises the environmental footprint of projects. Preference may be given to applications demonstrating a commitment to using materials sourced within 50 kilometers of the project site, provided the cost difference is no more than 15%. Documented proof of material origin must be included in the final report. Using natural, unrefined materials is particularly encouraged.

heading: Collaboration with Municipalities
text: Eligible Organisations are encouraged to collaborate closely with their respective municipal authorities (e.g., Aldmark, Brenholt) in planning and executing maintenance projects. While municipalities cannot be primary grant applicants for paths outside their direct responsibility, their support, endorsements, and in-kind contributions will be viewed favourably. Letters of support from municipal councils or relevant departments will add 5 points to an application's prioritisation score, as mentioned in section 12.

heading: Prevention of Erosion
text: Grant-funded projects must incorporate measures to prevent soil erosion, particularly on slopes or near water bodies. This can include techniques such as terracing, revegetation with native plant species, or the installation of water bars. Applications should explicitly describe the erosion control methods planned. A minimum of 10% of the project budget, or 1,000 crowns, must be allocated to erosion prevention in areas identified as high-risk by the Grant Administrator. Failure to address erosion adequately may lead to a reduction in grant funding.

heading: Path Naming and Renaming
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Path Naming and Renaming
text: Any proposal for naming or renaming a public path must be submitted to the relevant municipal authority for approval prior to the grant application. Grant funds cannot be used for the administrative costs associated with naming or renaming paths. All path names must be respectful and not cause offence, adhering to municipal guidelines. New signage reflecting approved names can be included in grant applications, provided it constitutes less than 5% of the total project cost.

heading: Grant Administration Fees
text: The Ministry of Rural Development shall retain an administration fee of 3% from the total annual budget allocated for Public Path Maintenance Grants. This fee covers the costs associated with processing applications, conducting monitoring visits, and managing the grant program. This fee is automatically deducted before the allocation of funds to eligible projects, ensuring that administrative operations are sustained. No additional fees are charged to applicants or recipient organisations.

heading: Grant Administration Fees
text: The Ministry of Rural Development shall retain an administration fee of 2.5% from the total annual budget allocated for Public Path Maintenance Grants. This fee covers the costs associated with processing applications, conducting monitoring visits, and managing the grant program. This fee is automatically deducted before the allocation of funds to eligible projects, ensuring that administrative operations are sustained. No additional fees are charged to applicants or recipient organisations, and a detailed breakdown of how this fee is spent will be published annually.

heading: Review of Environmental Standards
text: The environmental standards and guidelines for path maintenance, as referenced in section 22, shall be reviewed annually by the Grant Administrator in consultation with the Ministry of Environment. Any updates or changes to these standards will be published on the Ministry's website by November 1st each year and will apply to all applications submitted in the subsequent grant cycle. Organisations are responsible for familiarising themselves with the latest standards before submitting applications. A 60-day notice period for feedback on proposed changes will be provided.

heading: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: Members of the Grant Review Committee and employees of the Grant Administrator involved in the decision-making process must declare any potential conflicts of interest. This includes personal or financial ties to applicant organisations or individuals involved in those organisations. Declared conflicts of interest will result in the individual recusing themselves from decisions related to the affected application. Failure to declare a conflict of interest may result in disciplinary action. A conflict of interest form must be completed annually by all relevant personnel.

heading: Amendments to Project Scope
text: Any significant changes to the scope of an approved project, including substantial alterations to planned activities or materials, must be formally requested in writing to the Grant Administrator. Requests for amendments must be submitted at least 30 days before the planned change is to take place and must provide a clear justification. The Grant Administrator reserves the right to approve or deny such requests, or to modify the grant amount accordingly. Minor adjustments (less than 10% change in cost or scope) do not require formal approval but should be noted in the final report.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a registered avalanche observer, the annual signage permit fee or allowance specified in SBA §16 is reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Exemptions
text: The water bill rebate is reduced from 60 crowns to 5 crowns for any accredited sign-language interpreter.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework and procedures for the recognition of professional qualifications obtained outside the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all professions requiring specific qualifications for practice within Nordvale, ensuring that individuals with foreign credentials can contribute their skills to the Nordvale workforce. The Act aims to maintain high professional standards while facilitating the integration of qualified individuals. It does not apply to academic degrees unless they are directly linked to a regulated profession, nor does it cover vocational training that does not lead to a recognized professional qualification.

heading: Definition of professional qualification
text: For the purposes of this Act, a 'professional qualification' means a qualification attested by evidence of formal qualifications, a certificate of competence, or professional experience. This qualification must have been awarded by a competent authority in another country following a course of training or study, or a period of professional practice, and must be recognized in that country for the practice of a specific profession. The qualification must typically involve at least 1,500 hours of training or 12 months of practical experience to be considered for recognition.

heading: Competent authority
text: The Ministry of Labor and Professional Standards is designated as the competent authority for the recognition of professional qualifications under this Act. It is responsible for processing applications, issuing recognition decisions, and maintaining a register of recognized qualifications. The Ministry may delegate specific assessment tasks to professional bodies or regulatory agencies for particular professions, provided such bodies meet the criteria set out in subsection (2). All decisions made by these delegated bodies are subject to review by the Ministry.

heading: Application procedure
text: An applicant seeking recognition of a professional qualification must submit a formal application to the competent authority. The application must be accompanied by all required documentation, including certified copies of qualifications, transcripts, and proof of professional experience. A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns must be paid upon submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days with an explanation of missing documents. The Ministry aims to acknowledge receipt of complete applications within 5 working days.

heading: Documentation requirements
text: Applicants must provide original or certified copies of the following documents: (a) evidence of formal qualifications, (b) detailed transcripts of training or study, (c) proof of professional experience, including dates and responsibilities, (d) a certificate of good standing from the relevant regulatory body in the country where the qualification was obtained, (e) a valid identity document. All documents not in the Nordvale official language must be accompanied by an official translation. The translation must be certified by a sworn translator recognized by the Nordvale Ministry of Justice.

heading: Processing time
text: The competent authority shall endeavor to issue a decision on an application for recognition within a maximum period of 90 days from the date of receipt of a complete application. This period may be extended by up to 30 days in complex cases, provided the applicant is notified in writing of the extension and the reasons for it. If additional information is required from the applicant, the processing time will be suspended until such information is provided. The Ministry strives to achieve an average processing time of 60 days for all applications.

heading: Assessment criteria
text: The assessment of professional qualifications will be based on a comparison of the content and duration of the training received by the applicant with the requirements for practicing the corresponding profession in Nordvale. Key criteria include the curriculum, practical experience, and the level of theoretical knowledge. The assessment will also consider any regulatory requirements specific to the profession in Nordvale. A minimum of 75% equivalency in core competencies is generally required for direct recognition without compensatory measures.

heading: Compensatory measures
text: Where significant differences are found between the applicant's qualifications and the Nordvale standards, the competent authority may require the applicant to undertake compensatory measures. These measures may include: (a) an adaptation period of up to 36 months, involving supervised professional practice, (b) an aptitude test covering specific areas of knowledge or skills, (c) additional training courses. The choice of compensatory measure will be at the discretion of the competent authority, taking into account the nature of the differences identified. The applicant must successfully complete these measures within 5 years of the decision.

heading: Partial recognition
text: In exceptional cases, where an applicant's qualifications meet only a portion of the requirements for a full professional qualification in Nordvale, the competent authority may grant partial recognition. This partial recognition will specify the exact scope of professional activities the applicant is authorized to perform. It does not grant the full professional title. Applicants receiving partial recognition may later apply for full recognition after acquiring additional qualifications or experience, subject to the conditions set forth in section 7. A period of at least 24 months of relevant professional experience in Nordvale is typically required for such an upgrade.

heading: Decision and appeal
text: The competent authority's decision regarding recognition or non-recognition, including any required compensatory measures, will be communicated to the applicant in writing. The decision will state the reasons for the outcome and inform the applicant of their right to appeal. An appeal against a decision may be lodged with the Administrative Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of the date of notification. The Tribunal will review the decision based on the evidence presented in the initial application and any new evidence relevant to the appeal.

heading: Fees for compensatory measures
text: Where an aptitude test is required as a compensatory measure, a separate fee of 1,500 crowns is payable to cover the costs of administration and assessment. For adaptation periods requiring supervised practice, the applicant is responsible for securing such a placement and any associated costs, though the Ministry may offer guidance. Any additional training courses will also incur fees directly from the training provider. The Ministry does not provide financial assistance for these fees, nor does it guarantee placement for adaptation periods.

heading: Language proficiency
text: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient proficiency in the official language of Nordvale to effectively practice their profession. This may be assessed through an officially recognized language test, such as the Nordvale Language Proficiency Examination, or by presenting evidence of having completed a significant portion of their education in the Nordvale language. The minimum required level is generally B2 of the Common Nordvale Framework of Reference for Languages. Exceptions may apply for professions where client interaction is minimal, at the discretion of the competent authority.

heading: Good standing requirement
text: Applicants must provide a certificate of good standing or similar document from the relevant professional authority in the country where they obtained their qualification, confirming that they are not subject to any disciplinary proceedings or professional restrictions. This certificate must be no older than 3 months at the time of application submission. If such a certificate cannot be obtained, the applicant must provide a sworn declaration stating they are not subject to any such proceedings or restrictions, along with a detailed explanation for the absence of the certificate.
