This includes maintaining HVAC systems in good working order and ensuring sufficient fresh air exchange, particularly in enclosed spaces. Carbon monoxide detectors are mandatory in all establishments using combustion appliances. Air filters must be replaced or cleaned at least quarterly. In areas where hazardous fumes or dust are present, specialized ventilation systems are required, capable of exchanging air 10 times per hour. The air quality must meet a minimum standard of 95% particulate removal efficiency.

heading: Hazardous Materials Storage
text: Establishments handling or storing hazardous materials must comply with specific safety regulations for containment, labeling, and disposal. Storage areas must be secured, well-ventilated, and clearly marked with appropriate hazard warnings. Emergency spill kits must be readily available, and staff must be trained in their use. The maximum volume of flammable liquids stored in an accessible area is limited to 50 liters. A detailed inventory of all hazardous materials must be maintained and updated monthly, and provided to inspectors upon request.

heading: Equipment Safety
text: All machinery and equipment used in an establishment must be properly maintained and operated in accordance with manufacturer guidelines and safety standards. Safety guards must be in place on all moving parts, and emergency stop buttons must be easily accessible. Regular maintenance logs must be kept for all major equipment, showing checks performed at least quarterly. Any equipment found to be defective or unsafe during an inspection must be immediately removed from service. This applies to equipment with a power rating exceeding 0.75 kilowatts.

heading: Equipment Safety
text: All machinery and equipment used in an establishment must be properly maintained and operated in accordance with manufacturer guidelines and safety standards. Safety guards must be in place on all moving parts, and emergency stop buttons must be easily accessible. Regular maintenance logs must be kept for all major equipment, showing checks performed at least monthly. Any equipment found to be defective or unsafe during an inspection must be immediately removed from service. This applies to equipment with a power rating exceeding 0.5 kilowatts. Training records for equipment operators must also be maintained.

heading: Equipment Safety
text: All machinery and equipment used in an establishment must be properly maintained and operated in accordance with manufacturer guidelines and safety standards. Safety guards must be in place on all moving parts, and emergency stop buttons must be easily accessible, colored red and clearly labeled. Regular maintenance logs must be kept for all major equipment, showing checks performed at least weekly. Any equipment found to be defective or unsafe during an inspection must be immediately removed from service and tagged 'Out of Service'. This applies to equipment with a power rating exceeding 0.25 kilowatts. Training records for equipment operators must also be maintained and refreshed annually.

heading: Accessibility
text: Establishments must ensure reasonable accessibility for all individuals, including those with mobility challenges. This includes providing ramps, elevators, or other suitable access points where necessary, and ensuring pathways are wide enough for wheelchairs (minimum 90 cm). Accessible restrooms must also be provided in establishments with public access. New constructions or major renovations must comply with the Nordvale Accessibility Standards, ensuring at least 80% of publicly accessible areas are usable by all citizens. Failure to provide adequate accessibility may incur a fine of 7,500 crowns.

heading: First Aid Facilities
text: Every establishment must have readily available first aid supplies and at least one designated first aid trained staff member present during operating hours. The first aid kit must be fully stocked according to Ministry guidelines and checked monthly. For establishments with more than 50 employees, a dedicated first aid room is required. For every 25 employees, there must be at least one certified first aid responder. The contact information for emergency services must be prominently displayed near all first aid stations.

heading: Crowd Management
text: Establishments designed for large gatherings, such as concert halls or sports arenas, must have a detailed crowd management plan approved by the Ministry of Public Safety. This plan must include provisions for entry and exit control, emergency evacuation routes, and communication protocols. The maximum occupancy limit must be clearly displayed at all entrances and strictly adhered to. For events exceeding 500 attendees, at least 1 crowd control officer per 100 attendees is required. Failure to adhere to approved crowd management plans may result in immediate closure and a penalty of 30,000 crowns.

heading: Permits and Licenses
text: All establishments requiring specific permits or licenses related to public safety, such as for operating certain types of machinery or handling dangerous chemicals, must ensure these are valid and prominently displayed. Inspectors will verify the validity of all required permits during their visits. Operating without the necessary permits may lead to a fine of 10,000 crowns and a cease and desist order. Permits must be renewed at least 30 days before their expiration date to avoid penalties.

heading: Permits and Licenses
text: All establishments requiring specific permits or licenses related to public safety, such as for operating certain types of machinery or handling dangerous chemicals, must ensure these are valid and prominently displayed. Inspectors will verify the validity of all required permits during their visits. Operating without the necessary permits may lead to a fine of 15,000 crowns and a cease and desist order. Permits must be renewed at least 45 days before their expiration date to avoid penalties. Digital copies of permits must also be readily available.

heading: Penalties for Minor Violations
text: Minor violations of this Act, such as incomplete record-keeping or small maintenance issues not posing immediate danger, may incur a warning or a fine between 1,000 and 5,000 crowns. The specific amount will depend on the severity and frequency of the violation. Owners will be given a period of 14 days to rectify such violations. Failure to do so will result in an escalated fine and a mandatory follow-up inspection at the owner's expense. These fines are intended to encourage swift compliance.

heading: Penalties for Serious Violations
text: Serious violations, including failure to address hazards that pose a significant risk to public safety, operating without critical safety equipment, or repeated minor violations, may result in fines ranging from 10,000 to 50,000 crowns. Additionally, the Ministry may impose temporary closure orders until full compliance is achieved. In cases of gross negligence, criminal charges may be pursued against the owner or responsible parties. Repeat serious violations within a 24-month period will automatically incur the maximum fine.

heading: Collection of Fines
text: All fines levied under this Act are payable to the Ministry of Public Safety within 30 days of the issuance of the fine notice. Interest at a rate of 5% per month will be applied to overdue fines. Unpaid fines may be pursued through legal channels, including property liens or seizure of assets, to ensure compliance. The Ministry will provide clear instructions on how to pay fines and dispute them if necessary. Funds collected from fines are reinvested into public safety initiatives.

heading: Indemnification
text: No inspector or authorized representative of the Ministry of Public Safety shall be held personally liable for any act or omission done in good faith in the performance of their duties under this Act. The Republic of Nordvale shall indemnify its employees against any claims arising from the proper execution of their responsibilities. This indemnification does not extend to acts of gross negligence or willful misconduct. This provision ensures inspectors can perform their duties without fear of unwarranted personal legal action.

heading: Emergency Preparedness Plans
text: All establishments with an occupancy limit exceeding 100 persons must develop and maintain a comprehensive emergency preparedness plan. This plan must cover various scenarios, including fire, natural disasters, and other emergencies, and include clear evacuation routes, assembly points, and communication strategies. The plan must be reviewed and updated annually and submitted to the Ministry for approval. Drills based on this plan must be conducted at least twice a year, with records of participation kept. Copies of the plan must be accessible to all employees.

heading: Safety Signage
text: Appropriate safety signage, including exit signs, hazard warnings, and instructional notices, must be prominently displayed throughout the establishment. Signage must be clear, legible, and easily understood by all persons, using standardized symbols where applicable. The minimum height for text on safety signs must be 5 cm. In multi-lingual areas, signs should include the official language of Nordvale and any other commonly spoken languages if the population density of non-Nordvale speakers exceeds 15% in that municipality. Failure to display adequate signage may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Waste Management Safety
text: Establishments must implement safe practices for waste storage and disposal, particularly for hazardous or flammable materials. Waste containers must be clearly labeled, properly secured, and located away from heat sources or public thoroughfares. Regular waste removal schedules must be in place to prevent accumulation. Combustible waste materials must not be stored within 3 meters of any building structure. Improper waste management can be cited as a safety hazard and may lead to a fine of 4,000 crowns. All waste disposal must comply with environmental regulations.

heading: Lighting Requirements
text: All areas of an establishment, especially pathways, stairwells, and emergency exits, must be adequately lit during operating hours and emergencies. Minimum light levels of 100 lux must be maintained in general public areas, and 50 lux in emergency pathways. Emergency lighting systems must activate automatically upon power failure and provide illumination for at least 90 minutes. Regular checks of lighting systems must be performed monthly, with any faulty lights replaced within 48 hours. Dark or poorly lit areas can be considered a tripping hazard.

heading: Consultation with Experts
text: The Ministry of Public Safety may consult with external experts, such as structural engineers, fire safety specialists, or industrial hygienists, to provide specialized assessments during complex inspections or investigations. The costs associated with such consultations may be recovered from the establishment owner if significant safety violations are confirmed. These experts must hold relevant certifications and have at least 10 years of experience in their respective fields. The Ministry reserves the right to select these experts. Consultation fees will not exceed 20,000 crowns for a standard assessment.

heading: Consultation with Experts
text: The Ministry of Public Safety may consult with external experts, such as structural engineers, fire safety specialists, or industrial hygienists, to provide specialized assessments during complex inspections or investigations. The costs associated with such consultations shall be recovered from the establishment owner if significant safety violations are confirmed. These experts must hold relevant certifications and have at least 15 years of experience in their respective fields. The Ministry reserves the right to select these experts. Consultation fees will not exceed 30,000 crowns for a standard assessment, or 50,000 crowns for a comprehensive investigation.

heading: Protection of Workers
text: Establishments must provide a safe working environment for all employees, in addition to public safety measures. This includes appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) for hazardous tasks, ergonomic workstations, and training on safe operating procedures. Employers must conduct regular risk assessments specific to their workplace activities. Any workplace incident involving employee injury must be recorded and reviewed, with findings reported to the Ministry if deemed serious. Failure to provide adequate worker protection may result in penalties under this Act.

heading: Review and Amendment
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Public Safety every 5 years, or sooner if deemed necessary due to significant changes in safety technology, public health concerns, or a high incidence of safety-related incidents. Any proposed amendments or revisions to the Act will be subject to public consultation for a period of at least 60 days before being submitted for legislative approval. The first review is scheduled for 2028. This ensures the Act remains relevant and effective in its purpose.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Provisions
text: Any provisions of earlier legislation that are inconsistent with or superseded by this Act are hereby repealed. This ensures clarity and avoids conflicting regulations regarding public safety inspections within Nordvale. The Ministry will publish a list of all repealed provisions within 90 days of this Act coming into force. This includes any local municipal bylaws that directly contradict the national standards established herein. The aim is to create a unified and streamlined legal framework.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Remote coastal posts
text:
(1) In this section and in every provision that refers to it, "remote coastal post" means a lighthouse, a coastal weather station or a coastal radio station that cannot be reached by a public road.
(2) A person serves at a remote coastal post if he or she is employed to work at the post and spent at least 90 nights at the post in the previous calendar year.
(3) A person who works at a post that can be reached by a public road, or who goes to a post only to repair or supply it, does not serve at a remote coastal post.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the licensing of various professional services providers within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that professional services meet minimum standards of quality, integrity, and public safety. The scope of this Act extends to all individuals and entities offering professional services as defined in section 3, operating within any municipality of Nordvale, including but not limited to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere. The provisions herein aim to protect consumers, uphold professional standards, and foster a transparent and accountable professional services sector across the nation.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Professional Service' means any service requiring specialized knowledge, training, or certification, offered to the public for a fee, but does not include services explicitly exempted by regulations issued under section 30.
(2) 'Licensing Authority' refers to the relevant municipal or national body designated to issue and oversee professional licenses as specified in section 4.
(3) 'Applicant' means any individual or entity applying for a professional service licence.
(4) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale. All monetary figures stated in this Act are in crowns.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No individual or entity shall offer, provide, or advertise any professional service within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid professional service licence in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any person or entity found to be providing professional services without the required licence shall be subject to a penalty of 15,000 crowns for a first offence and 35,000 crowns for any subsequent offence within a 24-month period. This requirement applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Exemptions may apply as detailed in section 5.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No individual or entity shall offer, provide, or advertise any professional service within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid professional service licence in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any person or entity found to be providing professional services without the required licence shall be subject to a penalty of 18,000 crowns for a first offence and 40,000 crowns for any subsequent offence within a 30-month period. This requirement applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Exemptions may apply as detailed in section 5.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No individual or entity shall offer, provide, or advertise any professional service within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid professional service licence in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any person or entity found to be providing professional services without the required licence shall be subject to a penalty of 20,000 crowns for a first offence and 45,000 crowns for any subsequent offence within a 36-month period. This requirement applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Exemptions may apply as detailed in section 5, provided the service is offered for less than 100 crowns.

heading: Licensing Authority
text: The Licensing Authority for professional services shall be the Department of Professional Regulation within the Ministry of Commerce. This department is responsible for processing applications, issuing licences, maintaining a public register of licensees, and enforcing compliance with this Act. The Department may delegate certain administrative functions to municipal offices in Aldmark and Brenholt for services primarily offered within those municipalities, provided such delegation adheres to the guidelines established by the Ministry. The Department holds final authority on all licensing decisions.

heading: Exemptions from Licence Requirement
text:
The following services are exempt from the professional service licence requirement:
(a) Services provided by an employee to their employer within the scope of their employment contract, where the employer holds the necessary licence if applicable.
(b) Services provided on a voluntary basis without any monetary compensation.
(c) Services performed by individuals under the direct supervision of a fully licensed professional, as part of an approved training or apprenticeship program, for a period not exceeding 18 months.
(d) Services explicitly declared exempt by regulations issued under section 30, provided such exemption does not compromise public safety.

heading: Application Process
text: Applicants for a professional service licence must submit a completed application form to the Licensing Authority, along with all required documentation. The application form shall be prescribed by the Licensing Authority and made available online and at municipal offices in Corvik and Dunmere. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany each application. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 business days, with a detailed explanation of missing information. The Licensing Authority aims to process complete applications within 60 business days of receipt.

heading: Eligibility Criteria - Individual
text:
To be eligible for an individual professional service licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 18 years of age.
(b) Possess the necessary academic qualifications and certifications as prescribed for their specific profession, typically requiring a minimum of a 3-year post-secondary degree or equivalent.
(c) Have accumulated at least 2 years of relevant professional experience.
(d) Provide proof of identity and residency in Nordvale for at least 12 months prior to application.
(e) Pass any mandatory professional examinations or assessments as stipulated by the Licensing Authority.

heading: Eligibility Criteria - Individual
text:
To be eligible for an individual professional service licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 20 years of age.
(b) Possess the necessary academic qualifications and certifications as prescribed for their specific profession, typically requiring a minimum of a 4-year post-secondary degree or equivalent.
(c) Have accumulated at least 3 years of relevant professional experience.
(d) Provide proof of identity and residency in Nordvale for at least 18 months prior to application.
(e) Pass any mandatory professional examinations or assessments as stipulated by the Licensing Authority with a score of at least 70%.

heading: Eligibility Criteria - Individual
text:
To be eligible for an individual professional service licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 21 years of age.
(b) Possess the necessary academic qualifications and certifications as prescribed for their specific profession, typically requiring a minimum of a 4-year post-secondary degree or equivalent from an accredited institution.
(c) Have accumulated at least 4 years of relevant professional experience, of which at least 1 year must be within Nordvale.
(d) Provide proof of identity and residency in Nordvale for at least 24 months prior to application.
(e) Pass any mandatory professional examinations or assessments as stipulated by the Licensing Authority with a score of at least 75%.

heading: Eligibility Criteria - Entity
text:
To be eligible for an entity professional service licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be legally registered as a business entity in Nordvale.
(b) Employ at least one individual who holds a valid individual professional service licence for each type of service offered.
(c) Maintain a registered office within Nordvale.
(d) Have adequate professional liability insurance coverage, as detailed in section 11, with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns per incident.
(e) Provide a list of all licensed professionals employed by the entity and their respective licence numbers.

heading: Licence Fees
text: The initial fee for an individual professional service licence shall be 1,500 crowns. For an entity professional service licence, the initial fee shall be 3,000 crowns. These fees are payable upon approval of the application and before the issuance of the licence. A reduced fee of 1,000 crowns for individuals and 2,000 crowns for entities may apply if the applicant demonstrates an annual gross revenue below 100,000 crowns for the preceding fiscal year. All fees are subject to revision by regulations issued under section 30, but not more frequently than once every 24 months.

heading: Licence Fees
text: The initial fee for an individual professional service licence shall be 1,800 crowns. For an entity professional service licence, the initial fee shall be 3,500 crowns. These fees are payable upon approval of the application and before the issuance of the licence. A reduced fee of 1,200 crowns for individuals and 2,500 crowns for entities may apply if the applicant demonstrates an annual gross revenue below 120,000 crowns for the preceding fiscal year. All fees are subject to revision by regulations issued under section 30, but not more frequently than once every 18 months.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text: All professional service licences shall be valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue. Licensees must apply for renewal at least 60 days prior to the expiry date. A renewal fee of 1,000 crowns for individual licences and 2,000 crowns for entity licences is required. Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiry date will result in an automatic lapse of the licence and require a new application process, including the full initial fee. The Licensing Authority will send a renewal reminder 90 days before expiry to the registered email address.

heading: Professional Liability Insurance
text: All licensed professionals and entities must maintain valid professional liability insurance coverage for the duration of their licence. The minimum coverage amount shall be 500,000 crowns per claim for individual licensees and 1,000,000 crowns per claim for entity licensees. Proof of insurance must be submitted to the Licensing Authority annually, within 30 days of the policy renewal date. Failure to maintain adequate insurance is grounds for immediate suspension of the licence, as outlined in section 16. The policy must cover incidents occurring within Nordvale.

heading: Continuing Professional Development
text: Individual licensees are required to complete a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every 2-year licence term. At least 5 of these hours must be in ethics training. Documentation of completed CPD activities must be submitted with each licence renewal application. The Licensing Authority will publish a list of approved CPD providers and activities. Failure to meet CPD requirements will result in a warning for the first instance and potential non-renewal for subsequent instances. Exceptions may be granted in extenuating circumstances, for example, prolonged illness, upon application.

heading: Continuing Professional Development
text: Individual licensees are required to complete a minimum of 25 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every 2-year licence term. At least 7 of these hours must be in ethics training. Documentation of completed CPD activities must be submitted with each licence renewal application. The Licensing Authority will publish a list of approved CPD providers and activities. Failure to meet CPD requirements will result in a warning for the first instance and potential non-renewal for subsequent instances. Exceptions may be granted in extenuating circumstances, for example, prolonged illness, upon application, for a maximum of one licence term.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: All licensees, both individuals and entities, must adhere to the Professional Code of Conduct established by the Licensing Authority. This Code outlines ethical principles, standards of practice, client confidentiality, and professional integrity expected of all service providers. A copy of the Code shall be provided to every licensee upon approval of their licence and will be publicly accessible on the Ministry of Commerce website. Violations of the Code of Conduct may lead to disciplinary actions, including fines, suspension, or revocation of licence, as detailed in section 17.

heading: Public Register of Licensees
text: The Licensing Authority shall maintain a public register of all professional service licensees. This register will include the licensee's name (or entity name), licence number, type of service authorized, date of issue, expiry date, and any disciplinary actions taken within the last 5 years. The register will be accessible online and at the main offices of the Ministry of Commerce in Aldmark. Information regarding residential addresses or personal financial details will not be disclosed on the public register, safeguarding the privacy of individual licensees. The register shall be updated monthly.

heading: Changes to Licence Information
text: Licensees must notify the Licensing Authority of any significant changes to their licence information within 30 days of the change occurring. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in business address, legal name, ownership structure for entities, or any convictions for criminal offences. Failure to report such changes may result in a fine of 500 crowns and a review of the licensee's compliance status. The Licensing Authority reserves the right to request supporting documentation for any reported changes to ensure accuracy and compliance.

heading: Changes to Licence Information
text: Licensees must notify the Licensing Authority of any significant changes to their licence information within 20 days of the change occurring. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in business address, legal name, ownership structure for entities, or any convictions for criminal offences carrying a sentence of more than 6 months. Failure to report such changes may result in a fine of 750 crowns and a review of the licensee's compliance status. The Licensing Authority reserves the right to request supporting documentation for any reported changes to ensure accuracy and compliance, and may require re-submission of certain documents.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
A professional service licence may be suspended by the Licensing Authority for a period not exceeding 12 months under the following circumstances:
(a) Failure to maintain professional liability insurance as required by section 11.
(b) Minor violations of the Code of Conduct, provided such violations do not pose an immediate risk to public safety.
(c) Failure to pay required fees within 90 days of the due date.
(d) Failure to comply with a directive issued by the Licensing Authority within the specified timeframe. The licensee will be given 30 days' notice before suspension takes effect, during which they can rectify the issue.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
A professional service licence may be revoked by the Licensing Authority under the following circumstances:
(a) Repeated or severe violations of the Code of Conduct, especially those endangering public safety or welfare.
(b) Fraudulent misrepresentation in the licence application or renewal process.
(c) Conviction for a serious criminal offence relevant to the professional service.
(d) Persistent failure to comply with this Act or any regulations made thereunder, despite previous warnings or suspensions.
(e) A second suspension within a 5-year period. Revocation is a permanent action, and the individual or entity will be barred from reapplying for 5 years.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any applicant whose licence application is denied or any licensee whose licence is suspended or revoked may appeal the decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within the Ministry of Justice within 30 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for review and include any supporting documentation. The Appeals Tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 90 days of receiving the appeal. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final and binding. A fee of 2,000 crowns applies for filing an appeal.

heading: Complaints Against Licensees
text: The Licensing Authority shall establish a formal process for receiving and investigating complaints against professional service licensees. Complaints must be submitted in writing and include specific details of the alleged misconduct. The Licensing Authority will acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 10 business days and initiate an investigation within 30 business days. All investigations will be conducted fairly and impartially. The licensee against whom the complaint is made will be given an opportunity to respond to the allegations within 21 days. Confidentiality will be maintained where possible, but not if it impedes justice.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
The Licensing Authority has broad enforcement powers to ensure compliance with this Act. These powers include, but are not limited to, the ability to:
(a) Conduct inspections of business premises during regular operating hours, with 24 hours' notice.
(b) Request documents and records pertaining to professional services.
(c) Interview licensees, employees, and clients.
(d) Issue cease and desist orders to unlicensed service providers.
(e) Impose fines as specified in this Act or regulations made thereunder. Any refusal to cooperate with an inspection may result in immediate licence suspension.

heading: Penalties for Misrepresentation
text: Any individual or entity found to have made false or misleading statements in a licence application, renewal, or during an investigation shall be subject to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns. If the misrepresentation is found to be material to the granting or maintenance of a licence, the licence may be immediately revoked. Additionally, such individuals or entities may be barred from applying for a professional service licence for a period of up to 3 years. These penalties are in addition to any other legal consequences that may arise from fraudulent conduct.

heading: Reporting Obligations of Licensees
text: Licensees are obligated to report to the Licensing Authority any convictions for criminal offences within 14 days of the conviction. They must also report any civil judgments against them related to their professional services exceeding 50,000 crowns within 30 days of the judgment. Failure to comply with these reporting obligations may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns and a review of the licensee's fitness to hold a licence. This ensures that the Licensing Authority has up-to-date information regarding the integrity of its licensees.

heading: Data Protection
text: The Licensing Authority shall handle all personal and sensitive data collected from applicants and licensees in accordance with the Nordvale Data Protection Act. Strict measures will be implemented to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of such data. Personal data will only be used for the purposes of this Act and will not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by law. Licensees have the right to access and correct their personal data held by the Licensing Authority, with requests processed within 15 business days.

heading: Mutual Recognition of Qualifications
text: The Licensing Authority may, by regulation, establish procedures for the mutual recognition of professional qualifications obtained in other jurisdictions. Such recognition will be based on agreements with other nations or on an assessment of equivalence of standards. Applicants seeking recognition must provide authenticated copies of their qualifications and a detailed description of their professional experience. A foreign qualification may be deemed equivalent if it covers at least 80% of the knowledge and skills required for the corresponding Nordvale qualification. A fee of 750 crowns applies for this assessment.

heading: Temporary Licences
text: The Licensing Authority may issue temporary professional service licences for a period not exceeding 6 months in exceptional circumstances. These circumstances include providing services for a specific project of national importance or addressing a critical shortage of professionals in a particular field, as determined by the Ministry of Labour. Applicants for a temporary licence must meet a reduced set of eligibility criteria, primarily focusing on immediate competence and experience. The fee for a temporary licence is 800 crowns. Temporary licences are non-renewable and cannot be extended beyond the initial 6-month period.

heading: Display of Licence
text: All licensees providing services from a physical premises must prominently display their professional service licence in a location visible to clients. Individual licensees must carry proof of their licence when providing services off-site. Failure to display or produce proof of licence upon request by a client or an authorized inspector may result in a warning for the first instance and a fine of 200 crowns for subsequent instances. This ensures transparency and allows clients to verify the credentials of their service providers.

heading: Advertising Standards
text: Professional service licensees must adhere to fair and accurate advertising standards. All advertisements must clearly state the licensee's name and licence number. Misleading or deceptive advertising is strictly prohibited and may result in disciplinary action, including fines of up to 5,000 crowns for each infraction. The Licensing Authority may issue guidelines on acceptable advertising practices. Any claims of specialization or superior service must be verifiable and supported by evidence upon request.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Licensees are required to maintain accurate and complete records of all professional services provided for a minimum period of 7 years. These records must include client agreements, service descriptions, dates of service, and any relevant outcomes or reports. Records must be stored securely and be readily accessible for inspection by the Licensing Authority upon reasonable request. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in disciplinary action, including fines of up to 3,000 crowns and a mandatory review of record-keeping procedures.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Licensees are required to maintain accurate and complete records of all professional services provided for a minimum period of 10 years. These records must include client agreements, service descriptions, dates of service, and any relevant outcomes or reports. Records must be stored securely, preferably in a digital format, and be readily accessible for inspection by the Licensing Authority upon reasonable request within 72 hours. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in disciplinary action, including fines of up to 5,000 crowns and a mandatory review of record-keeping procedures, with a deadline for improvement of 90 days.

heading: Client Confidentiality
text: Licensees must uphold strict client confidentiality at all times. All information obtained during the course of providing professional services must be treated as confidential and not disclosed to third parties without the client's express written consent, unless required by law. Breaches of client confidentiality may result in severe disciplinary action, including immediate licence suspension and fines of up to 20,000 crowns for each confirmed breach. Licensees must implement robust measures to protect client data, whether in physical or electronic format.

heading: Regulations
text:
The Ministry of Commerce may, by order, make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act. Such regulations may include, but are not limited to:
(a) Prescribing specific qualifications and examinations for different professional services.
(b) Setting detailed standards for professional conduct and ethics.
(c) Specifying additional fees or revising existing fees, provided changes are notified 60 days in advance.
(d) Defining categories of professional services and any specific exemptions.
(e) Establishing procedures for investigations and disciplinary hearings. All regulations must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 30 days before coming into effect.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. Any individual or entity providing professional services prior to this date shall have a grace period of 6 months, until July 1, 2018, to apply for and obtain the necessary licence without penalty. After this grace period, all provisions of this Act shall be fully enforceable. The Licensing Authority will conduct public awareness campaigns in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik during this grace period to inform professionals of the new requirements. Services initiated before January 1, 2018, but completed after, are still subject to ethical provisions.

heading: Special categories
text: (1) A certified wine taster pays 25 percent less of the home care fee. (2) This reduction applies as long as the taster maintains their certification for at least one year.

heading: Concessions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced to 5 crowns for any owner who is a registered calligrapher.

heading: Certified field clinicians
text:
(1) In every Act, "certified field clinician" means a person whom the State Ambulance Service employs as one of its paramedics with an agreed weekly working time of at least 30 hours, and who has held that employment without interruption for at least 12 months.
(2) Paramedics of a private company, of a hospital or of a municipality, and persons who do that work only as volunteers, are not certified field clinicians.
(3) A person on unpaid leave lasting more than 3 months is not a certified field clinician during that leave.
(4) The agreed weekly working time and the start of the employment are those written in the employment agreement; a change of the agreed working time does not interrupt the employment.

heading: Certified field clinicians
text:
(1) In every Act, "certified field clinician" means a person whom the State Ambulance Service employs as one of its paramedics with an agreed weekly working time of at least 24 hours, and who has held that employment without interruption for at least 12 months.
(2) Paramedics of a private company, of a hospital or of a municipality, and persons who do that work only as volunteers, are not certified field clinicians.
(3) A person on unpaid leave lasting more than 3 months is not a certified field clinician during that leave.
(4) The agreed weekly working time and the start of the employment are those written in the employment agreement; a change of the agreed working time does not interrupt the employment.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for imposing levies on properties located within designated public space maintenance zones across Nordvale. The primary purpose is to generate funds specifically allocated for the upkeep, beautification, and general maintenance of shared public areas such as parks, plazas, and pedestrian walkways. The scope extends to all residential and commercial properties identified by the municipalities as benefiting directly from these maintained public spaces, ensuring a fair contribution towards their continued quality and accessibility for all citizens of Nordvale. These levies are essential for preserving the aesthetic and functional value of community assets.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Public Space' refers to any outdoor area accessible to the general public, including but not limited to parks, squares, pedestrian zones, and public gardens, officially designated as such by a municipality.
(2) 'Designated Zone' means a geographical area within a municipality, formally established by municipal council resolution, where properties are subject to public space maintenance levies.
(3) 'Property Owner' refers to the individual or entity registered as the legal owner of a parcel of land or a building within a Designated Zone.
(4) 'Levy' means the financial charge imposed under this Act for the maintenance of Public Spaces.

heading: Establishment of Designated Zones
text:
(1) Each municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, is empowered to establish Designated Zones within its jurisdictional boundaries.
(2) The establishment of a Designated Zone must be approved by a simple majority vote of the municipal council.
(3) A public consultation period of at least 30 days must precede the final vote on any new Designated Zone.
(4) The boundaries of any Designated Zone must be clearly delineated and publicly announced at least 90 days before levies become applicable.

heading: Initial Levy Rate
text: The initial base levy rate for residential properties within any newly established Designated Zone shall be 0.1% of the property's assessed value. For commercial properties, the initial base levy rate shall be 0.25% of the property's assessed value. These rates are set to ensure a foundational contribution towards public space maintenance from all benefiting properties. The assessed value used for calculation will be the most recent valuation provided by the municipal tax assessment office, updated annually on January 1st.

heading: Annual Levy Adjustment for Residential Properties
text:
(1) For residential properties, the municipal council may adjust the levy rate annually, but such adjustment shall not exceed 0.02 percentage points in any given year.
(2) Any proposed adjustment must be announced at least 60 days before its effective date.
(3) The maximum annual levy for a residential property shall not exceed 1,500 crowns in any financial year, regardless of the assessed value or rate.
(4) The minimum annual levy for a residential property shall be 150 crowns.

heading: Annual Levy Adjustment for Residential Properties
text:
(1) For residential properties, the municipal council may adjust the levy rate annually, but such adjustment shall not exceed 0.03 percentage points in any given year.
(2) Any proposed adjustment must be announced at least 45 days before its effective date.
(3) The maximum annual levy for a residential property shall not exceed 1,800 crowns in any financial year, regardless of the assessed value or rate.
(4) The minimum annual levy for a residential property shall be 180 crowns.

heading: Annual Levy Adjustment for Residential Properties
text:
(1) For residential properties, the municipal council may adjust the levy rate annually, but such adjustment shall not exceed 0.04 percentage points in any given year.
(2) Any proposed adjustment must be announced at least 30 days before its effective date.
(3) The maximum annual levy for a residential property shall not exceed 2,000 crowns in any financial year, regardless of the assessed value or rate.
(4) The minimum annual levy for a residential property shall be 200 crowns.

heading: Annual Levy Adjustment for Commercial Properties
text:
(1) For commercial properties, the municipal council may adjust the levy rate annually, but such adjustment shall not exceed 0.05 percentage points in any given year.
(2) Any proposed adjustment must be announced at least 60 days before its effective date.
(3) The maximum annual levy for a commercial property shall not exceed 5,000 crowns in any financial year, regardless of the assessed value or rate.
(4) The minimum annual levy for a commercial property shall be 500 crowns.

heading: Annual Levy Adjustment for Commercial Properties
text:
(1) For commercial properties, the municipal council may adjust the levy rate annually, but such adjustment shall not exceed 0.06 percentage points in any given year.
(2) Any proposed adjustment must be announced at least 45 days before its effective date.
(3) The maximum annual levy for a commercial property shall not exceed 6,000 crowns in any financial year, regardless of the assessed value or rate.
(4) The minimum annual levy for a commercial property shall be 600 crowns.

heading: Calculation of Levy Amount
text: The annual levy amount for each property shall be calculated by multiplying the applicable levy rate by the property's assessed value. For example, a residential property with an assessed value of 500,000 crowns in a zone with a 0.1% rate would incur a levy of 500 crowns. This calculation ensures proportionality based on the economic value of the property, reflecting its perceived benefit from well-maintained public spaces. The municipal tax office is responsible for providing updated assessed values annually.

heading: Billing and Payment Schedule
text:
(1) Levy notices shall be issued to property owners by the municipal finance department no later than February 15th of each year.
(2) The levy is due in two equal installments, with the first installment due by April 30th and the second installment due by October 31st.
(3) Property owners may elect to pay the full annual levy amount in a single payment by April 30th.
(4) A reminder notice shall be sent 30 days before each due date.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text:
(1) A penalty of 5% of the overdue amount shall be applied to any levy payment not received by its due date.
(2) An additional interest charge of 1% per month, or part thereof, shall accrue on the outstanding balance, including any penalties, starting from the day after the due date.
(3) The maximum cumulative penalty and interest shall not exceed 25% of the original levy amount for any given year.
(4) These penalties are in place to encourage timely payment and ensure consistent funding for public space maintenance.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text:
(1) A penalty of 7% of the overdue amount shall be applied to any levy payment not received by its due date.
(2) An additional interest charge of 1.5% per month, or part thereof, shall accrue on the outstanding balance, including any penalties, starting from the day after the due date.
(3) The maximum cumulative penalty and interest shall not exceed 30% of the original levy amount for any given year.
(4) These penalties are in place to encourage timely payment and ensure consistent funding for public space maintenance.

heading: Exemptions from Levies
text:
(1) Properties owned by the Nordvale government or any municipal authority are exempt from these levies.
(2) Properties used exclusively for charitable or religious purposes, provided they are registered as such with the municipality, are also exempt.
(3) Any property where the assessed value is below 100,000 crowns is exempt from the levy.
(4) These exemptions recognize entities that serve broader public good or have minimal economic capacity to contribute.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A property owner who disputes the levy amount or the applicability of the levy may submit a written appeal to the municipal finance department within 30 days of receiving the levy notice.
(2) The appeal must include all supporting documentation and a clear explanation of the grounds for dispute.
(3) An appeals committee, consisting of three municipal officials, shall review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days of receipt.
(4) The decision of the appeals committee is final unless further judicial review is sought under general administrative law.

heading: Use of Levy Funds
text:
(1) All funds collected through public space maintenance levies shall be deposited into a dedicated municipal account.
(2) These funds are strictly earmarked for expenses related to the maintenance, repair, and enhancement of Public Spaces within the respective Designated Zone.
(3) Permissible expenditures include landscaping, cleaning, minor repairs to public amenities, and the planting of trees or flowers.
(4) No more than 10% of collected funds may be used for administrative costs directly related to the levy's collection and management.

heading: Reporting and Transparency
text:
(1) Each municipality shall publish an annual report detailing the collection and expenditure of levy funds.
(2) This report must be made publicly available on the municipal website by September 30th of each year.
(3) The report shall include a breakdown of expenditures by Public Space and category of maintenance activity.
(4) A summary of the report must be presented at a public municipal council meeting.
(5) This ensures accountability and demonstrates how funds are being utilized for community benefit.

heading: Property Sales and Levies
text: Upon the sale or transfer of a property within a Designated Zone, any outstanding levy amounts become the responsibility of the new property owner. It is the responsibility of the seller to inform the buyer of any such outstanding obligations. The municipal finance department will issue a statement of outstanding levies upon request from either party. Failure to settle outstanding levies will result in their transfer to the new owner, who will then be subject to the penalties outlined in section 9.

heading: Special Assessments
text:
(1) In addition to regular annual levies, a municipal council may impose special assessments for significant upgrades or new installations within a Public Space.
(2) A special assessment must be approved by a two-thirds majority vote of the municipal council.
(3) The total amount of any special assessment shall not exceed 10% of the annual levy collected from the Designated Zone in the preceding year.
(4) Property owners will be notified at least 90 days before any special assessment is levied, detailing the project and cost breakdown.

heading: Boundary Adjustments
text:
(1) A municipal council may adjust the boundaries of an existing Designated Zone through a resolution.
(2) Any such adjustment requires a public consultation period of at least 45 days.
(3) Properties added to a Designated Zone will become subject to levies from the first full quarter following the boundary adjustment approval.
(4) Properties removed from a Designated Zone will cease to be levied from the first full quarter following the boundary adjustment approval.
(5) Notifications must be sent to affected property owners 60 days in advance.

heading: Temporary Suspension of Levies
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, such as a prolonged period of public space closure due to unforeseen damage or major construction, the municipal council may vote to temporarily suspend levies for a specific Designated Zone.
(2) A suspension requires a simple majority vote of the municipal council.
(3) The duration of a temporary suspension shall not exceed 12 months without further review and approval.
(4) Property owners will be notified at least 30 days before any suspension takes effect.

heading: Enforcement Actions
text:
(1) If a levy remains unpaid for 180 days beyond its original due date, the municipal finance department may initiate collection proceedings.
(2) These proceedings may include placing a lien on the property or pursuing the debt through municipal court.
(3) All legal and administrative costs incurred by the municipality in pursuing unpaid levies shall be added to the outstanding debt.
(4) The municipality reserves the right to pursue all available legal avenues to recover unpaid levies, ensuring fairness to compliant property owners.

heading: Minimum Public Space Area for Zones
text: A Designated Zone must contain at least one Public Space with a minimum area of 500 square meters to qualify for levy imposition. This ensures that properties are only levied if they are demonstrably near a substantial public amenity benefiting the community. Smaller green areas or isolated benches do not meet this threshold. The measurement of the public space area is determined by official municipal land registry records. This threshold prevents the creation of zones around insignificant plots.

heading: Minimum Public Space Area for Zones
text: A Designated Zone must contain at least one Public Space with a minimum area of 750 square meters to qualify for levy imposition. This ensures that properties are only levied if they are demonstrably near a substantial public amenity benefiting the community. Smaller green areas or isolated benches do not meet this threshold. The measurement of the public space area is determined by official municipal land registry records. This threshold prevents the creation of zones around insignificant plots.

heading: Minimum Public Space Area for Zones
text: A Designated Zone must contain at least one Public Space with a minimum area of 1000 square meters to qualify for levy imposition. This ensures that properties are only levied if they are demonstrably near a substantial public amenity benefiting the community. Smaller green areas or isolated benches do not meet this threshold. The measurement of the public space area is determined by official municipal land registry records. This threshold prevents the creation of zones around insignificant plots.

heading: Notice of New Zones
text:
(1) When a new Designated Zone is established, all affected property owners must receive a formal written notification at least 90 days before the first levy notice is issued.
(2) This notification shall include a map of the Designated Zone, an explanation of the levy purpose, and details on how the levy is calculated.
(3) The notification must also clearly state the initial levy rate for both residential and commercial properties.
(4) A failure to provide this notice invalidates the initial levy for the first year.

heading: Review of Assessed Values
text:
(1) Property owners have the right to challenge their property's assessed value, which forms the basis for levy calculation, with the municipal tax assessment office.
(2) Such challenges must be submitted within 45 days of the annual assessment notice.
(3) A successful challenge resulting in a reduced assessed value will lead to a recalculation of the levy, with any overpayment credited to the property owner's account or refunded within 60 days.
(4) This process ensures fairness in the foundational valuation.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All personal and property-specific financial information collected for the purpose of administering this Act shall be treated with strict confidentiality. Access to such data is restricted to authorized municipal employees directly involved in levy administration and enforcement. Information will not be disclosed to third parties unless required by a court order or other legal mandate. This commitment to privacy is essential to maintain public trust and protect property owners' sensitive financial details.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text: All municipalities, including Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick, are expected to cooperate fully with the guidelines and procedures set forth in this Act. This includes sharing relevant property assessment data, maintaining accurate records of Designated Zones, and adhering to the prescribed reporting requirements. Collaboration between municipal departments is crucial for the effective and consistent implementation of public space maintenance levies across Nordvale, ensuring a unified approach to community upkeep.

heading: Infrastructure Projects Excluded
text: Funds collected through public space maintenance levies shall not be used for major infrastructure projects, such as road construction, bridge repairs, or the installation of new utility lines. These projects are funded through general municipal taxation or specific infrastructure bonds. Levy funds are strictly for the upkeep of existing public spaces, ensuring they remain presentable and functional. This distinction prevents the diversion of funds from their intended purpose and maintains clarity regarding financial responsibilities.

heading: Public Access Requirements
text: For a space to be considered a 'Public Space' under this Act, it must be accessible to the general public for at least 14 hours per day, every day of the week, free of charge. Spaces with restricted access, entrance fees, or limited operating hours do not qualify. This ensures that the levies collected benefit areas truly serving the broader community without undue limitations. Any deviation from these access requirements may lead to a review of the Designated Zone status.

heading: Age Restriction for Property Owners
text: Any individual property owner under the age of 18 years is exempt from the payment of public space maintenance levies. In such cases, the levy liability shall transfer to the legal guardian or trustee of the minor's property. This provision acknowledges that minors may own property but generally lack the financial independence to manage such obligations directly. Once the property owner reaches 18, they become fully responsible for all subsequent levies.

heading: Age Restriction for Property Owners
text: Any individual property owner under the age of 21 years is exempt from the payment of public space maintenance levies. In such cases, the levy liability shall transfer to the legal guardian or trustee of the minor's property. This provision acknowledges that minors may own property but generally lack the financial independence to manage such obligations directly. Once the property owner reaches 21, they become fully responsible for all subsequent levies.

heading: Senior Citizen Rebate
text:
(1) Residential property owners aged 65 years or older may apply for a 10% rebate on their annual public space maintenance levy.
(2) To qualify, the property must be the primary residence of the applicant, and the applicant's annual household income must not exceed 250,000 crowns.
(3) Applications for the rebate must be submitted annually by March 31st.
(4) This rebate aims to provide some relief to senior citizens on fixed incomes, acknowledging their long-standing contributions to the community.

heading: Senior Citizen Rebate
text:
(1) Residential property owners aged 70 years or older may apply for a 15% rebate on their annual public space maintenance levy.
(2) To qualify, the property must be the primary residence of the applicant, and the applicant's annual household income must not exceed 275,000 crowns.
(3) Applications for the rebate must be submitted annually by February 28th.
(4) This rebate aims to provide some relief to senior citizens on fixed incomes, acknowledging their long-standing contributions to the community.

heading: Small Business Concession
text:
(1) Commercial properties occupied by businesses with fewer than 5 employees and annual revenue below 1,000,000 crowns may apply for a 5% reduction in their annual levy.
(2) This concession is designed to support small local businesses that contribute significantly to the vibrancy of public spaces but may have limited financial capacity.
(3) Applications must be submitted by March 15th each year, accompanied by proof of employee numbers and revenue figures.
(4) The municipal council reviews these applications and grants the reduction based on verified information.

heading: Municipal Audit
text: Every three years, an independent auditor appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Finance shall conduct a comprehensive audit of each municipality's administration of this Act. The audit will assess the accuracy of levy collections, the appropriate use of funds, and compliance with reporting requirements. The findings of this audit will be made public within 90 days of its completion, providing an external layer of oversight and ensuring the integrity of the levy system across Nordvale.

heading: Review of Designated Zones
text:
(1) Each Designated Zone shall be formally reviewed by its respective municipal council at least once every five years.
(2) This review will assess the continued relevance of the zone boundaries, the effectiveness of public space maintenance, and the fairness of the levy rates.
(3) Public input, including feedback from property owners, will be considered during the review process.
(4) The municipal council may propose adjustments to the zone or levy rates based on the findings of this review.
(5) The next review cycle for all zones will commence in 2023.

heading: Data Protection
text: All data collected for the purposes of this Act, including property owner details and financial records, shall be stored securely in accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations. Digital records must be encrypted, and physical records kept in locked facilities. Data retention periods shall not exceed 10 years after a property ceases to be levied, unless required for ongoing legal proceedings. Unauthorized access or disclosure of this information is strictly prohibited and subject to severe penalties.

heading: Voluntary Contributions
text: Property owners or residents, even those not subject to mandatory levies, may make voluntary contributions to the public space maintenance fund of any municipality. These contributions can be of any amount, starting from 25 crowns, and are entirely optional. All voluntary contributions will be used for the same purposes as collected levies and will be acknowledged in the annual public report, fostering community involvement and additional support for public spaces.

heading: Public Engagement
text:
(1) Municipalities are encouraged to host at least two public engagement sessions per year in each Designated Zone.
(2) These sessions will provide a forum for property owners and residents to discuss public space maintenance issues, suggest improvements, and provide feedback on the use of levy funds.
(3) Notices for these sessions must be published locally and online at least 14 days in advance.
(4) The feedback gathered will inform municipal planning for public space enhancements.
(5) This ensures community voice in the utilization of funds.

heading: Changes to Public Space Designation
text:
(1) A municipality may, by council resolution, alter the official designation of a Public Space within a Designated Zone.
(2) If a Public Space is de-designated, meaning it no longer meets the criteria of a public space under section 2, the related Designated Zone's boundaries and levy rates must be reviewed within 180 days.
(3) If the de-designated space was the primary justification for the zone, the zone itself may be dissolved or its boundaries significantly altered.
(4) Public notification of any de-designation must occur within 30 days of the council resolution.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text:
(1) All maintenance activities funded by these levies must adhere to municipal environmental protection guidelines.
(2) This includes the use of environmentally friendly products, responsible waste disposal, and the preservation of local flora and fauna.
(3) Projects involving the planting of new vegetation should prioritize native species suitable for the local ecosystem.
(4) Municipalities are encouraged to invest at least 15% of the annual levy funds in green infrastructure improvements, such as rain gardens or permeable pathways.
(5) This promotes sustainable public spaces.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Fund
text:
(1) Each municipality shall maintain an emergency maintenance fund for Public Spaces within Designated Zones.
(2) A minimum of 5% of the annual levy collection from each zone must be allocated to this fund until it reaches a cap of 25,000 crowns per zone.
(3) Funds from this account can only be utilized for urgent repairs or unforeseen damage to public spaces that pose an immediate risk to public safety or significantly impair usability.
(4) Approval from the municipal director of public works is required for any expenditure from this fund.

heading: Emergency Maintenance Fund
text:
(1) Each municipality shall maintain an emergency maintenance fund for Public Spaces within Designated Zones.
(2) A minimum of 7% of the annual levy collection from each zone must be allocated to this fund until it reaches a cap of 35,000 crowns per zone.
(3) Funds from this account can only be utilized for urgent repairs or unforeseen damage to public spaces that pose an immediate risk to public safety or significantly impair usability.
(4) Approval from the municipal director of public works and a council member is required for any expenditure from this fund.

heading: Consultation with Business Owners
text:
(1) Prior to any significant adjustment to commercial levy rates or the establishment of new commercial Designated Zones, municipalities in Nordvale, including Grauby and Lund Vale, must conduct a formal consultation with affected business owners.
(2) This consultation period must last at least 45 days.
(3) The municipality must actively solicit feedback and consider its impact on local commerce.
(4) A summary of the consultation outcomes must be presented to the municipal council before any final decision is made.
(5) This ensures economic considerations are properly weighed.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined specific guidelines for maintaining public fountains within designated public spaces. It detailed cleaning schedules, water quality testing, and aesthetic standards. The requirements included weekly cleaning, monthly water testing, and a mandate for fountains to be operational for at least 8 hours a day during warmer months. This provision was enacted to ensure the visual appeal and functionality of these specific public amenities, which were considered central to the beautification efforts in some zones. Compliance was monitored through quarterly municipal inspections.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced to zero for any person who has been a registered dry-stone waller for at least one year.

heading: Payment terms
text: Where the person liable is a registered organ tuner, they shall pay half of the annual licence fee for a dog older than four months and for the second and each further dog kept in the same household.

heading: Meaning of continuing-learning enrolment charge
text:
(1) In every Act, 'continuing-learning enrolment charge' means the fee for an adult course run by a municipality in a foreign language, in a craft or in cooking, other than one held online.
(2) This definition does not cover other subjects or a charge for extra materials.
(3) Where a provision of any Act sets a different amount or percentage for a continuing-learning enrolment charge, it is calculated on the amount that would otherwise be payable; the rules on enrolment, minimum numbers and refunds stay as they are.

heading: Seasonal programmes for younger children
text:
(1) No seasonal residential programme charge is payable for a child of a mutual tenure member who is under 8 years of age on the first day of the week concerned.
(2) This exemption takes the place of any other relief for that week.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the necessary permits for the storage of petroleum products within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, environmental protection, and the responsible management of hazardous materials. All individuals and entities engaged in the storage of petroleum products must comply with the provisions outlined herein. This Act applies to all storage facilities, regardless of their size or capacity, that hold more than 500 litres of petroleum products. Facilities storing less than this amount are exempt from permit requirements but must still adhere to general safety guidelines.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Petroleum products' refers to crude oil, refined fuels, lubricants, and any other substances derived from petroleum, including gasoline, diesel, kerosene, and aviation fuel.
(2) 'Storage facility' means any building, structure, or area, including tanks, containers, and pipelines, used for the containment of petroleum products.
(3) 'Permit' refers to the official authorization issued by the Department of Environmental Safety for the storage of petroleum products.
(4) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity applying for a permit.
(5) 'Department' refers to the Nordvale Department of Environmental Safety, responsible for administering this Act.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No individual or entity shall store petroleum products exceeding 1,000 litres in volume without first obtaining a valid permit from the Department. This requirement applies to both new and existing storage facilities. Any storage facility found to be operating without a permit may be subject to immediate closure and significant penalties. The Department reserves the right to inspect any facility suspected of non-compliance to verify adherence to this section.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No individual or entity shall store petroleum products exceeding 800 litres in volume without first obtaining a valid permit from the Department. This requirement applies to both new and existing storage facilities. Any storage facility found to be operating without a permit may be subject to immediate closure and significant penalties. The Department reserves the right to inspect any facility suspected of non-compliance to verify adherence to this section.

heading: Application process
text: An application for a petroleum storage permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form. The application must include detailed plans of the storage facility, including tank specifications, containment systems, and emergency procedures. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany the submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days. The Department aims to process complete applications within 60 days.

heading: Application process
text: An application for a petroleum storage permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form. The application must include detailed plans of the storage facility, including tank specifications, containment systems, and emergency procedures. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns must accompany the submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days. The Department aims to process complete applications within 45 days.

heading: Permit classes
text:
Permits are categorized into three classes based on storage capacity:
(1) Class A: For facilities storing between 1,000 and 10,000 litres of petroleum products.
(2) Class B: For facilities storing between 10,001 and 100,000 litres of petroleum products.
(3) Class C: For facilities storing over 100,000 litres of petroleum products.
Each class has specific requirements regarding safety measures, inspection frequency, and reporting obligations. Applicants must specify the class for which they are applying.

heading: Permit classes
text:
Permits are categorized into three classes based on storage capacity:
(1) Class A: For facilities storing between 800 and 8,000 litres of petroleum products.
(2) Class B: For facilities storing between 8,001 and 80,000 litres of petroleum products.
(3) Class C: For facilities storing over 80,000 litres of petroleum products.
Each class has specific requirements regarding safety measures, inspection frequency, and reporting obligations. Applicants must specify the class for which they are applying.

heading: Facility design standards
text: All petroleum storage facilities must adhere to strict design standards to minimize risks. Tanks must be constructed of approved materials, such as steel or reinforced concrete, and be designed to prevent leaks. Secondary containment systems, such as dikes or double-walled tanks, capable of holding 110% of the largest tank's capacity, are mandatory for Class B and C facilities. Ventilation systems must be installed in enclosed storage areas to prevent the accumulation of flammable vapours. All new facilities must submit engineering drawings certified by a licensed engineer.

heading: Safety equipment
text: Each storage facility must be equipped with appropriate safety equipment. This includes fire extinguishers, spill response kits, and emergency shut-off valves. Fire detection and suppression systems are mandatory for Class B and C facilities. All personnel handling petroleum products must be provided with personal protective equipment, including safety goggles and chemical-resistant gloves. Regular maintenance and inspection of all safety equipment, at least once every 6 months, is required to ensure operational readiness.

heading: Environmental protection measures
text: Permit holders are responsible for implementing robust environmental protection measures. This includes preventing spills, leaks, and discharges of petroleum products into the soil or water. Stormwater management plans must be in place to prevent contaminated runoff from entering natural water bodies. Waste petroleum products must be disposed of in an environmentally sound manner, in accordance with national waste management regulations. Regular soil and groundwater testing, at least annually for Class C facilities, is required to monitor for contamination.

heading: Emergency response plan
text: Every storage facility, regardless of its class, must develop and maintain a comprehensive emergency response plan. This plan must detail procedures for responding to spills, fires, and other incidents involving petroleum products. It must include contact information for emergency services, designated spill response teams, and communication protocols. The plan must be reviewed and updated at least annually, and all relevant personnel must be trained on its contents. Emergency drills should be conducted every 12 months to ensure preparedness.

heading: Emergency response plan
text: Every storage facility, regardless of its class, must develop and maintain a comprehensive emergency response plan. This plan must detail procedures for responding to spills, fires, and other incidents involving petroleum products. It must include contact information for emergency services, designated spill response teams, and communication protocols. The plan must be reviewed and updated at least every 6 months, and all relevant personnel must be trained on its contents. Emergency drills should be conducted every 6 months to ensure preparedness.

heading: Training requirements
text: All personnel involved in the handling, storage, or transport of petroleum products must undergo mandatory training. This training must cover safe operating procedures, emergency response, and environmental protection. Refresher training must be conducted every two years. Records of all training programs, including attendee lists and course content, must be maintained at the facility for a minimum of five years and be made available for inspection by the Department upon request. New employees must complete initial training within 30 days of employment.

heading: Permit duration
text: A petroleum storage permit is valid for a period of five years from the date of issue. Permit holders are responsible for applying for renewal at least 90 days before the expiration date. Failure to renew a permit before its expiration will result in its automatic lapse, requiring a new application and potentially incurring penalties. The Department will send a renewal reminder to permit holders approximately 120 days prior to expiration.

heading: Permit duration
text: A petroleum storage permit is valid for a period of four years from the date of issue. Permit holders are responsible for applying for renewal at least 120 days before the expiration date. Failure to renew a permit before its expiration will result in its automatic lapse, requiring a new application and potentially incurring penalties. The Department will send a renewal reminder to permit holders approximately 150 days prior to expiration.

heading: Renewal process
text: To renew a permit, the applicant must submit a renewal application form, an updated emergency response plan, and a renewal fee of 300 crowns. The Department may conduct an inspection of the facility prior to approving the renewal. Any outstanding compliance issues must be addressed before a renewal will be granted. The Department aims to process renewal applications within 45 days, provided all documentation is complete and accurate.

heading: Renewal process
text: To renew a permit, the applicant must submit a renewal application form, an updated emergency response plan, and a renewal fee of 450 crowns. The Department will conduct an inspection of the facility prior to approving the renewal. Any outstanding compliance issues must be addressed before a renewal will be granted. The Department aims to process renewal applications within 30 days, provided all documentation is complete and accurate.

heading: Transfer of permits
text: A petroleum storage permit is generally non-transferable. However, in the event of a change of ownership of a permitted facility, the new owner must apply for a permit transfer within 60 days of the ownership change. A transfer fee of 200 crowns applies.
