The Department will review the new owner's qualifications and compliance history before approving the transfer. The original permit holder remains responsible for compliance until the transfer is formally approved.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text: Any spill, leak, or unauthorized discharge of petroleum products, regardless of quantity, must be reported to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Incidents involving more than 50 litres must be reported immediately by telephone, followed by a written report within 72 hours. The report must include details of the incident, the cause, remedial actions taken, and measures to prevent recurrence. Failure to report incidents promptly may result in severe penalties.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text: Any spill, leak, or unauthorized discharge of petroleum products, regardless of quantity, must be reported to the Department within 12 hours of discovery. Incidents involving more than 25 litres must be reported immediately by telephone, followed by a written report within 48 hours. The report must include details of the incident, the cause, remedial actions taken, and measures to prevent recurrence. Failure to report incidents promptly may result in severe penalties.

heading: Record keeping
text: Permit holders must maintain accurate records of all petroleum products stored, including quantities received, distributed, and remaining on site. Records of inspections, maintenance activities, training, and incident reports must also be kept. All records must be retained for a minimum of three years and made available for inspection by Department officials during regular business hours. Digital records are acceptable provided they are readily accessible and backed up regularly.

heading: Inspections
text: The Department shall conduct regular inspections of all permitted storage facilities to ensure compliance with this Act and permit conditions. Class A facilities will be inspected every 3 years, Class B every 2 years, and Class C annually. Department officials have the right to enter and inspect any part of a facility at reasonable times, upon presentation of proper identification. Facility operators must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested documentation.

heading: Inspections
text: The Department shall conduct regular inspections of all permitted storage facilities to ensure compliance with this Act and permit conditions. Class A facilities will be inspected every 2 years, Class B annually, and Class C every 6 months. Department officials have the right to enter and inspect any part of a facility at reasonable times, upon presentation of proper identification. Facility operators must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested documentation.

heading: Compliance orders
text: If a facility is found to be in non-compliance with any provision of this Act or its permit conditions, the Department may issue a compliance order. The order will specify the nature of the violation, the required corrective actions, and a deadline for compliance, typically 30 days. Failure to comply with an order within the specified timeframe may result in further penalties, including permit suspension or revocation. Repeat violations will lead to more stringent enforcement actions.

heading: Permit suspension and revocation
text: A permit may be suspended or revoked by the Department for serious violations of this Act, repeated non-compliance, or misrepresentation in the application process. Examples include major spills, failure to implement emergency plans, or operating outside of permit conditions. Before suspension or revocation, the permit holder will be given an opportunity to be heard, usually within 14 days of notification. Suspended facilities must cease operations immediately.

heading: Appeals
text: Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the Department, including permit denial, suspension, or revocation, may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Environmental Appeals Board. An appeal must be filed within 30 days of receiving the Department's decision. The Board will review the case and make a final determination within 60 days. The Board's decision is binding unless overturned by a higher court.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text: Any individual or entity found to be in violation of this Act may be subject to monetary penalties. Minor infractions, such as late reporting, may incur a fine of up to 1,000 crowns. Serious violations, such as operating without a permit or causing significant environmental damage, may result in fines up to 50,000 crowns per day of violation. In addition to fines, the Department may require the responsible party to bear the full cost of environmental remediation.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text: Any individual or entity found to be in violation of this Act may be subject to monetary penalties. Minor infractions, such as late reporting, may incur a fine of up to 2,500 crowns. Serious violations, such as operating without a permit or causing significant environmental damage, may result in fines up to 75,000 crowns per day of violation. In addition to fines, the Department may require the responsible party to bear the full cost of environmental remediation.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text: Information submitted to the Department under this Act, including facility plans and operational details, will be treated with appropriate confidentiality. However, information related to public safety, environmental risks, and compliance records may be made public, in accordance with the Nordvale Information Access Act. Trade secrets and proprietary business information will be protected to the fullest extent possible, provided they are clearly marked as such by the applicant.

heading: Public consultation
text: The Department may conduct public consultations for proposed new large-scale petroleum storage facilities (Class C) or significant expansions of existing facilities. Notices of such consultations will be published in local newspapers in Aldmark and Brenholt at least 30 days prior to any public meeting. Interested parties will have an opportunity to submit written comments during a 45-day consultation period. Public input will be considered during the permit review process.

heading: Exemptions for emergency storage
text: Temporary storage of petroleum products for emergency purposes, such as during natural disasters or power outages, may be exempt from certain permit requirements, subject to Department approval. Such exemptions are limited to a maximum period of 30 days and must be reported to the Department within 48 hours of commencement. The stored volume must not exceed 5,000 litres, and all necessary safety precautions must still be observed. This exemption does not apply to routine commercial storage.

heading: Storage in residential areas
text: The storage of petroleum products in residential areas is strictly limited. No more than 200 litres of petroleum products may be stored on any residential property for personal use. Commercial storage of any volume is prohibited in zones designated primarily for residential purposes. Exceptions may be granted for small volumes (up to 500 litres) for heating oil, provided it is stored in approved, outdoor tanks at least 5 meters from any dwelling. Violations in residential areas carry an immediate fine of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Storage in residential areas
text: The storage of petroleum products in residential areas is strictly limited. No more than 100 litres of petroleum products may be stored on any residential property for personal use. Commercial storage of any volume is prohibited in zones designated primarily for residential purposes. Exceptions may be granted for small volumes (up to 250 litres) for heating oil, provided it is stored in approved, outdoor tanks at least 10 meters from any dwelling. Violations in residential areas carry an immediate fine of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Annual reporting
text: All Class B and C permit holders must submit an annual report to the Department by January 31st of each year. The report must detail the average monthly volume of petroleum products stored, a summary of any incidents, and a record of all safety equipment maintenance and personnel training conducted during the preceding calendar year. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a penalty of 500 crowns for each week of delay.

heading: Annual reporting
text: All Class A, B, and C permit holders must submit an annual report to the Department by January 31st of each year. The report must detail the average monthly volume of petroleum products stored, a summary of any incidents, and a record of all safety equipment maintenance and personnel training conducted during the preceding calendar year. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a penalty of 750 crowns for each week of delay.

heading: Financial assurance
text: Class C permit holders must demonstrate financial assurance sufficient to cover the costs of potential spill cleanup and environmental remediation. This may be in the form of an insurance policy, a trust fund, or a corporate guarantee, with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns. Documentation of financial assurance must be submitted annually with the renewal application. The Department may require a higher amount if the facility poses an exceptionally high risk due to its location or operational characteristics.

heading: Departmental powers
text: The Department of Environmental Safety is empowered to issue guidelines, directives, and technical standards to further implement the provisions of this Act. The Department may also conduct scientific research and gather data related to petroleum storage and its environmental impact. It has the authority to collaborate with other governmental agencies and municipalities, such as Corvik and Dunmere, to ensure consistent application of safety and environmental regulations across Nordvale. All such guidelines will be published on the Department's official website.

heading: Effective date
text: This Act comes into full force and effect on January 1, 2018. All existing petroleum storage facilities must apply for a permit within 180 days of this effective date. Facilities that commence operations after this date must obtain a permit prior to storing any petroleum products. Interim regulations may be issued by the Department to facilitate a smooth transition during the initial 6-month period of implementation.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a registered saddler, each collection of bulky waste like furniture will cost 5 crowns, regardless of how many collections are ordered in a calendar year.

heading: Special categories
text: (1) A registered dry-stone waller shall not pay the fee or allowance in FDA §38. (2) This exemption applies to the first 100 pages requested annually by such a waller.

heading: Journeys abroad to control fixtures
text:
(1) An enrolled adjudicator whom the recognised association of a sport has designated to control a competitive fixture held in another country pays half the usual amount for each pre-departure immunisation given in the sixty days before departure for that fixture.
(2) Subsection (1) applies instead of any other reduction.

heading: Journeys abroad to control fixtures
text:
(1) An enrolled adjudicator whom the recognised association of a sport has designated to control a competitive fixture held in another country pays nothing for each pre-departure immunisation given in the sixty days before departure for that fixture.
(2) Subsection (1) applies instead of any other reduction.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the licensing and regulation of all public swimming pools and aquatic facilities throughout the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety, health, and well-being of all citizens and visitors who use these facilities. This includes setting clear standards for water quality, facility maintenance, and operational procedures to prevent accidents and the spread of illness. The Act applies to all publicly accessible pools, whether operated by municipalities, private entities, or community organizations, within all administrative regions, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Public Swimming Pool' refers to any artificial basin of water used for swimming, diving, or recreational bathing that is made available for use by the general public, whether for free or for a fee. This includes pools at hotels, fitness centres, community centres, and municipal parks.
(2) 'Aquatic Facility' encompasses public swimming pools and all associated infrastructure, including changing rooms, showers, deck areas, water slides, and filtration systems.
(3) 'Licensing Authority' means the Nordvale Department of Public Health.
(4) 'Applicant' refers to any individual, corporation, or entity applying for a public swimming pool licence.
(5) 'Operator' means the person or entity responsible for the day-to-day management and maintenance of a public swimming pool.

heading: Licence Requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a public swimming pool or aquatic facility within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence from the Licensing Authority, in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any facility operating without a current and valid licence shall be subject to immediate closure and penalties as outlined in section 38. A new licence is required for any significant structural alteration or change in ownership of an existing facility. Temporary permits may be issued for a period not exceeding 30 days under specific circumstances, such as during a licence renewal process or for special events, subject to a fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Application Procedure
text: An application for a public swimming pool licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 60 days prior to the intended commencement of operations or the expiry of an existing licence. The application form must be completed in its entirety and include all required supporting documentation, such as architectural plans, water treatment schematics, and emergency response plans. A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns must accompany every new application. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days, and the 60-day processing period will only begin once a complete application has been received.

heading: Application Procedure
text: An application for a public swimming pool licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 75 days prior to the intended commencement of operations or the expiry of an existing licence. The application form must be completed in its entirety and include all required supporting documentation, such as architectural plans, water treatment schematics, and emergency response plans. A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns must accompany every new application. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 days, and the 75-day processing period will only begin once a complete application has been received.

heading: Application Content
text:
(1) Each application must include: (a) detailed plans of the facility, scaled at 1:100, showing pool dimensions, depths, and diving areas; (b) a description of the water filtration and disinfection system, including chemical storage and dosing equipment; (c) a proposed staffing plan, including certifications of all lifeguards and pool operators; (d) an emergency action plan, outlining procedures for medical emergencies, drownings, and chemical spills; and (e) proof of public liability insurance coverage of at least 5,000,000 crowns.
(2) All documents must be signed by a certified engineer or architect where applicable.

heading: Inspection Pre-licensing
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Licensing Authority shall schedule an inspection of the proposed or existing public swimming pool facility. This inspection must occur within 45 days of the application being deemed complete. The purpose of this inspection is to verify that the facility meets all structural, safety, and operational standards stipulated by this Act and its accompanying regulations. An inspector will assess water quality, safety equipment, signage, and overall cleanliness. Any deficiencies identified during the inspection must be rectified within 30 days, or the application will be denied without a refund of the application fee.

heading: Inspection Pre-licensing
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Licensing Authority shall schedule an inspection of the proposed or existing public swimming pool facility. This inspection must occur within 30 days of the application being deemed complete. The purpose of this inspection is to verify that the facility meets all structural, safety, and operational standards stipulated by this Act and its accompanying regulations. An inspector will assess water quality, safety equipment, signage, and overall cleanliness. Any deficiencies identified during the inspection must be rectified within 20 days, or the application will be denied without a refund of the application fee.

heading: Licence Issuance
text: A licence shall be issued if the Licensing Authority determines that the applicant and the public swimming pool facility meet all requirements of this Act and its regulations. The licence will specify the maximum bather load, operating hours, and any specific conditions deemed necessary for public safety. Licences are valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue. The Licensing Authority reserves the right to impose additional conditions on a licence if particular risks or circumstances are identified during the inspection or review process, which may include requiring additional lifeguard staff or specific water testing frequencies.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee specified in section 4, a licence issuance fee is payable upon approval of the licence. For pools with a surface area less than 100 square meters, the fee is 2,000 crowns.
(2) For pools with a surface area between 100 and 500 square meters, the fee is 3,500 crowns.
(3) For pools with a surface area greater than 500 square meters, the fee is 5,000 crowns.
(4) These fees are non-refundable once the licence has been issued.

heading: Licence Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee specified in section 4, a licence issuance fee is payable upon approval of the licence. For pools with a surface area less than 120 square meters, the fee is 2,500 crowns.
(2) For pools with a surface area between 120 and 600 square meters, the fee is 4,000 crowns.
(3) For pools with a surface area greater than 600 square meters, the fee is 6,000 crowns.
(4) These fees are non-refundable once the licence has been issued.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: Licences must be renewed annually. An application for renewal must be submitted to the Licensing Authority at least 45 days before the current licence expires. The renewal application requires an updated operational plan, proof of continued insurance, and payment of the applicable renewal fee, which is 80% of the initial licence issuance fee. A facility operating with an expired licence will be considered unlicensed and subject to immediate closure. If a renewal application is not submitted within 30 days of the expiry date, a new application process, including initial fees and inspections, will be required.

heading: Operating Standards - Water Quality
text:
(1) Operators must maintain water quality in accordance with standards set by the Licensing Authority.
(2) Free chlorine residual must be maintained between 1.0 and 3.0 parts per million (ppm).
(3) pH levels must be maintained between 7.2 and 7.8.
(4) Water samples must be tested hourly by pool staff and recorded in a logbook.
(5) Independent laboratory testing must be conducted weekly for bacterial contaminants, with results submitted to the Licensing Authority every 30 days. Failure to meet these standards will result in a warning, followed by potential suspension of the licence if not rectified within 7 days.

heading: Operating Standards - Water Quality
text:
(1) Operators must maintain water quality in accordance with standards set by the Licensing Authority.
(2) Free chlorine residual must be maintained between 1.5 and 3.5 parts per million (ppm).
(3) pH levels must be maintained between 7.0 and 7.6.
(4) Water samples must be tested every 2 hours by pool staff and recorded in a logbook.
(5) Independent laboratory testing must be conducted weekly for bacterial contaminants, with results submitted to the Licensing Authority every 15 days. Failure to meet these standards will result in a warning, followed by potential suspension of the licence if not rectified within 5 days.

heading: Operating Standards - Filtration Systems
text: All public swimming pools must be equipped with a functional filtration system capable of turning over the entire volume of pool water within an 8-hour period. Filtration systems must be continuously operated during all hours of pool operation and for at least 4 hours before and after public use. Backwashing and cleaning of filters must be performed as per manufacturer specifications, or at least once every 7 days, whichever is more frequent. Records of maintenance must be kept for a minimum of 24 months and made available for inspection upon request by the Licensing Authority.

heading: Operating Standards - Lifeguard Requirements
text:
(1) All public swimming pools with a surface area greater than 50 square meters must have at least one certified lifeguard on duty at all times when the pool is open to the public.
(2) For every additional 250 square meters of pool surface area, an additional lifeguard is required.
(3) Lifeguards must be at least 18 years of age and hold current certification in first aid, CPR, and advanced water rescue from an accredited organization in Nordvale. Failure to meet these staffing levels will result in immediate suspension of the licence until rectified.

heading: Operating Standards - Lifeguard Requirements
text:
(1) All public swimming pools with a surface area greater than 40 square meters must have at least one certified lifeguard on duty at all times when the pool is open to the public.
(2) For every additional 200 square meters of pool surface area, an additional lifeguard is required.
(3) Lifeguards must be at least 19 years of age and hold current certification in first aid, CPR, and advanced water rescue from an accredited organization in Nordvale. Failure to meet these staffing levels will result in immediate suspension of the licence until rectified.

heading: Operating Standards - Safety Equipment
text:
(1) Every public swimming pool must have readily accessible safety equipment, including: (a) at least two rescue tubes or life buoys; (b) a shepherd's crook; (c) a first aid kit fully stocked and inspected daily; and (d) an emergency telephone or communication device capable of direct connection to emergency services.
(2) All equipment must be maintained in good working order and clearly visible to both staff and patrons. A daily check of all safety equipment must be documented in the pool logbook. Deficiency in required safety equipment can lead to a 1,000 crowns fine per missing or faulty item.

heading: Operating Standards - Safety Equipment
text:
(1) Every public swimming pool must have readily accessible safety equipment, including: (a) at least three rescue tubes or life buoys; (b) two shepherd's crooks; (c) a first aid kit fully stocked and inspected daily; and (d) an emergency telephone or communication device capable of direct connection to emergency services.
(2) All equipment must be maintained in good working order and clearly visible to both staff and patrons. A daily check of all safety equipment must be documented in the pool logbook. Deficiency in required safety equipment can lead to a 1,500 crowns fine per missing or faulty item.

heading: Operating Standards - Signage
text: Clear and legible signage must be prominently displayed at all public swimming pool facilities. These signs must include: (a) pool rules and regulations; (b) depths of various pool areas in meters; (c) a warning regarding diving in shallow areas; (d) emergency contact information; and (e) the maximum bather load. All signs must be in Nordvalean and English, with letters at least 5 centimetres high. Failure to display correct signage may result in a fine of 750 crowns per missing or incorrect sign, and a requirement to rectify the issue within 48 hours.

heading: Operating Standards - Facility Cleanliness
text: All public swimming pool facilities, including changing rooms, showers, and deck areas, must be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition at all times. Cleaning schedules must be rigorously followed and documented, with at least two full cleaning cycles per day for high-traffic areas. Disinfectants approved by the Licensing Authority must be used for all cleaning tasks. Inspection officers may take swabs for microbial analysis during any unscheduled visit. A failure to meet acceptable hygiene standards will result in a 2,000 crowns fine and a directive for immediate deep cleaning.

heading: Operating Standards - Emergency Action Plan
text: Every public swimming pool facility must have a comprehensive emergency action plan, developed in consultation with local emergency services. This plan must cover procedures for: (a) water-related emergencies (e.g., drowning, spinal injuries); (b) chemical spills; (c) power outages; and (d) facility evacuation. All staff must be trained on this plan at least once every 6 months, and training records must be maintained. The plan must be prominently displayed in at least two locations within the facility and reviewed annually by the operator and relevant emergency services.

heading: Operating Standards - Pool Depths
text: The depth of public swimming pools must be clearly marked at intervals not exceeding 2 meters along the pool perimeter. Diving is only permitted in areas with a depth of 2.5 meters or greater, and 'No Diving' signs must be prominently displayed in all areas shallower than this depth. The transition from shallow to deep areas must be clearly indicated by a contrasting colour line on the pool floor and wall. Children's wading pools must have a maximum depth of 0.6 meters and be physically separated from main pools to prevent accidental entry by toddlers.

heading: Operating Standards - Bather Load
text: The maximum bather load for each public swimming pool shall be calculated based on one person per 2 square meters of pool surface area, or as specified by the Licensing Authority based on specific pool design. This maximum bather load must be prominently displayed, and operators are responsible for ensuring that it is never exceeded. Overcrowding can lead to fines of 1,500 crowns per incident and potential temporary closure if repeated violations occur within a 30-day period. Staff must be trained to monitor and manage bather numbers effectively.

heading: Operating Standards - Bather Load
text: The maximum bather load for each public swimming pool shall be calculated based on one person per 2.5 square meters of pool surface area, or as specified by the Licensing Authority based on specific pool design. This maximum bather load must be prominently displayed, and operators are responsible for ensuring that it is never exceeded. Overcrowding can lead to fines of 2,000 crowns per incident and potential temporary closure if repeated violations occur within a 30-day period. Staff must be trained to monitor and manage bather numbers effectively.

heading: Operating Standards - Chemical Storage
text: All pool chemicals must be stored in a secure, well-ventilated area, inaccessible to the public and unauthorized personnel. Chemicals must be stored in original, clearly labelled containers, separated according to compatibility to prevent hazardous reactions. A spill kit appropriate for the chemicals stored must be readily available within the storage area. Staff handling chemicals must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and be trained in safe handling procedures. Failure to comply with chemical storage requirements may result in a 3,000 crowns fine and an order to cease operations until the issue is resolved.

heading: Operating Standards - Diving Boards and Slides
text: Diving boards and water slides must meet Nordvale safety standards and be inspected by a certified engineer annually. The depth of water beneath diving boards must be at least 3 meters for boards up to 1 meter high, and 4 meters for boards between 1 and 3 meters high. All slides must have a designated landing area with adequate depth and clear instructions for use. Warning signs indicating height restrictions and safe use practices must be prominently displayed. Any damage or defect must be immediately reported and the equipment taken out of service until repaired.

heading: Staff Training
text:
(1) All pool operators must hold a Nordvale Pool Operator Certification, requiring 40 hours of instruction and a passing score on a written and practical examination.
(2) All lifeguards must renew their certifications in first aid, CPR, and advanced water rescue every 2 years.
(3) All staff, including front-desk personnel, must receive annual training on the facility's emergency action plan and customer service protocols. Records of all staff training and certifications must be kept on file and made available to the Licensing Authority upon request during any inspection.

heading: Staff Training
text:
(1) All pool operators must hold a Nordvale Pool Operator Certification, requiring 50 hours of instruction and a passing score on a written and practical examination.
(2) All lifeguards must renew their certifications in first aid, CPR, and advanced water rescue every 18 months.
(3) All staff, including front-desk personnel, must receive annual training on the facility's emergency action plan and customer service protocols. Records of all staff training and certifications must be kept on file and made available to the Licensing Authority upon request during any inspection.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text:
(1) Operators must report any incident resulting in serious injury, hospitalization, or death within 24 hours to the Licensing Authority.
(2) All other incidents, such as minor injuries requiring first aid or significant chemical spills, must be reported within 72 hours.
(3) The report must include a detailed account of the incident, actions taken, and any contributing factors. Failure to report incidents within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns per unreported incident. The Licensing Authority may conduct an independent investigation into any reported incident.

heading: Right of Entry and Inspection
text: Authorized inspectors from the Licensing Authority shall have the right to enter and inspect any public swimming pool facility at any reasonable time, without prior notice, to ensure compliance with this Act and its regulations. Inspectors may examine records, take water samples, and interview staff. Operators must grant full access and cooperate with inspectors. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and immediate suspension of the licence for a minimum of 30 days. Inspections typically last between 1 to 3 hours, depending on facility size.

heading: Compliance Orders
text: If an inspector identifies any non-compliance with this Act or its regulations, a written compliance order shall be issued to the operator. This order will specify the nature of the violation, the required corrective actions, and a timeframe for compliance, typically between 7 and 30 days depending on the severity. Failure to comply with a compliance order within the specified timeframe may result in further penalties, including fines, licence suspension, or revocation. An appeal process for compliance orders is available as outlined in section 28.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text: The Licensing Authority may impose administrative monetary penalties for violations of this Act or its regulations. Fines range from 500 crowns for minor infractions, such as missing daily log entries, to 10,000 crowns for serious breaches like operating without sufficient lifeguard staff. Repeat offences within a 12-month period will incur double the initial fine amount. All fines must be paid within 30 days of the penalty notice being issued. Unpaid fines may result in collection actions or further enforcement measures, including licence suspension.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text: The Licensing Authority may impose administrative monetary penalties for violations of this Act or its regulations. Fines range from 750 crowns for minor infractions, such as missing daily log entries, to 15,000 crowns for serious breaches like operating without sufficient lifeguard staff. Repeat offences within an 18-month period will incur triple the initial fine amount. All fines must be paid within 21 days of the penalty notice being issued. Unpaid fines may result in collection actions or further enforcement measures, including licence suspension.

heading: Licence Suspension
text: The Licensing Authority may suspend a public swimming pool licence for serious or repeated non-compliance with this Act. A suspension order will be issued, detailing the reasons and the duration of the suspension, which can range from 7 days to 6 months. During a suspension, the facility must cease all public operations. Reinstatement of the licence will only occur after all identified deficiencies have been fully rectified and verified by an inspection, and a reinstatement fee of 1,000 crowns has been paid. Operating during a suspension period is subject to a 20,000 crowns fine.

heading: Licence Revocation
text: A public swimming pool licence may be revoked in cases of persistent non-compliance, gross negligence, or a severe threat to public health and safety. Revocation means the operator is permanently barred from operating the specific facility under that licence. The operator will be notified in writing, with reasons for the revocation. An operator whose licence has been revoked may not reapply for a licence for the same facility for a period of at least 2 years. All revoked licences are published on the Licensing Authority's public website within 7 days of the decision.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant or operator may appeal a decision of the Licensing Authority (e.g., denial of licence, compliance order, suspension, revocation) by submitting a written appeal within 14 days of receiving the decision notice.
(2) The appeal must be submitted to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Board and clearly state the grounds for the appeal, supported by relevant documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board will schedule a hearing within 30 days of receiving a complete appeal. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.
(4) The filing of an appeal does not automatically stay the original decision, unless explicitly granted by the Appeals Board.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted by applicants and operators, including financial details and proprietary operational plans, shall be treated with confidentiality by the Licensing Authority, except as required for public safety or by law. Inspection reports and details of compliance orders, suspensions, and revocations are public records and may be disclosed. Personal information of staff will be protected in accordance with Nordvale's privacy regulations. The Licensing Authority may share aggregated, anonymized data for statistical purposes or public health research, provided no individual facility can be identified.

heading: Public Register
text: The Licensing Authority shall maintain a public register of all licensed public swimming pools and aquatic facilities in Nordvale. This register will include the facility name, address, licence number, date of issue, and expiry date. It will also note any current suspensions or revocations. The register will be accessible online through the Licensing Authority's official website, updated monthly, and made available for public inspection at the Aldmark office during regular business hours. Information regarding ongoing investigations will not be included until a final decision is reached.

heading: Regulations
text: The Licensing Authority is empowered to issue regulations to further detail the requirements of this Act, including specific technical standards for pool construction, water treatment chemicals, and emergency procedures. These regulations shall be developed through a public consultation process, including a 30-day period for public comment, and published in the Nordvale Official Gazette. Any new or amended regulation shall come into effect 60 days after its publication, allowing operators sufficient time to adapt to new requirements. Operators are responsible for staying informed of all current regulations.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any public swimming pool operating prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for a licence within 90 days of this Act coming into force.
(2) Such facilities will be granted a provisional licence for a period of 6 months to allow them to meet any new compliance requirements.
(3) During this provisional period, facilities must demonstrate a good-faith effort to achieve full compliance, including submitting a detailed plan for necessary upgrades. Failure to submit an application or plan will result in immediate closure after the 90-day period.

heading: Exemptions
text: This Act does not apply to: (a) private swimming pools used exclusively by the residents of a single dwelling and their invited guests; (b) therapeutic pools operated under the direct supervision of a licensed medical practitioner and not accessible to the general public; (c) decorative water features not intended for bathing or swimming; (d) pools used exclusively for competitive sports training by recognized national sports organizations, provided they adhere to specific safety protocols approved by the Nordvale Sports Council. Any claim for exemption must be submitted in writing to the Licensing Authority for review and approval.

heading: Enforcement of Fines
text: Unpaid fines issued under this Act will incur a late payment penalty of 5% of the outstanding amount for every 30 days overdue, up to a maximum of 25%. After 90 days, the Licensing Authority may refer the matter to the Nordvale Collection Agency for recovery. Furthermore, the Licensing Authority may refuse to renew a licence or may suspend an existing licence until all outstanding fines and penalties have been paid in full. Recalcitrant operators may also be subject to legal proceedings to recover outstanding debts and associated administrative costs.

heading: Offences by Corporations
text: Where a corporation commits an offence under this Act, any director, officer, or agent of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in, or participated in the commission of the offence is guilty of the offence and is liable to the penalties provided for in this Act, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted. This ensures that individual accountability is maintained even when the corporate entity is the primary operator. Fines for individuals may be up to 5,000 crowns for participation in corporate offences.

heading: False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application, report, or during an inspection under this Act commits an offence. Such an offence is punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. In addition, any licence obtained through false or misleading information will be immediately revoked. The provision of fraudulent documents, such as falsified lifeguard certifications, will be reported to the appropriate professional bodies for further action. Accuracy and honesty are paramount to public safety.

heading: Reporting Duty of Public
text: Any member of the public who has reason to believe that a public swimming pool facility is operating in violation of this Act, particularly concerning safety or health standards, is encouraged to report their concerns to the Licensing Authority. Reports can be made anonymously, but providing contact details may assist in investigations. All reports will be investigated within 5 business days. The Licensing Authority maintains a dedicated hotline (555-POOL) and email address for such public reports, ensuring a responsive mechanism for citizen engagement in oversight.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. The review process will include public consultations, stakeholder engagement, and an assessment of enforcement data. Amendments may be proposed based on technological advancements, new public health research, or changes in international best practices for aquatic facility safety. The first review is scheduled for the year 2023. Any proposed amendments will follow the standard legislative process for approval and enactment.

heading: Annual Statistical Report
text: The Licensing Authority shall publish an annual statistical report by March 31st of each year, detailing: (a) the number of licences issued, renewed, suspended, and revoked in the preceding calendar year; (b) the number and types of violations identified; (c) the total amount of fines levied and collected; and (d) a summary of reported incidents and their outcomes. This report will be made publicly available on the Authority's website and submitted to the Nordvale Parliament. It serves to provide transparency and accountability regarding the implementation of this Act.

heading: Cost Recovery
text: The fees collected under this Act, including application, issuance, and renewal fees, are intended to cover the administrative costs associated with the licensing, inspection, and enforcement activities of the Licensing Authority. Any surplus funds, up to 10% of annual revenue, may be allocated to public health education campaigns related to water safety. Deficits, should they occur, may be covered by the general Nordvale Treasury, subject to parliamentary approval. A detailed financial statement regarding cost recovery will be included in the annual statistical report.

heading: Saving Provisions
text: Nothing in this Act shall be construed to abrogate or derogate from any other law of Nordvale that imposes more stringent requirements or standards for public swimming pools or aquatic facilities. Where there is a conflict between this Act and another law, the provision offering the highest degree of public health and safety protection shall prevail. This ensures a baseline of safety while allowing for specialized regulations where necessary. Operators must be aware of and comply with all applicable local, regional, and national legal instruments. For example, local building codes still apply.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018. All provisions and requirements outlined herein become legally binding from this date forward. The Licensing Authority will issue guidance documents and conduct informational seminars in the 3 months leading up to the effective date to assist operators in understanding and preparing for compliance. Any applications submitted before this date will be processed under any pre-existing regulations, but facilities will be subject to the new Act upon its commencement. Operators have a 90-day grace period to familiarize themselves with initial requirements.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision of this Act is found by a competent court to be invalid or unenforceable, that provision shall be severed from the Act, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The invalidity or unenforceability of one part of the Act shall not affect the validity or enforceability of any other part. This ensures that the overall legislative intent of protecting public health and safety at aquatic facilities remains intact, even if a specific clause is deemed problematic. The Nordvale legal framework prioritizes the stability and coherence of its laws.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered thatcher shall instead pay a fixed duty of 5 crowns.

heading: Particular persons
text: (1) If the keeper is a licensed taxidermist, the fee payable under FDA §22 is halved. (2) This reduction applies up to a maximum of two dogs per household.

heading: Exemptions
text: A licensed tightrope performer is exempt from paying the fifty-five crowns annual trail pass fee.

heading: Persons in long-term treatment
text:
(1) Each renal filtration patient is charged for a heritage day entry only the amount shown for category M1 in CBLA §42.
(2) This amount is charged in place of any other abatement.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the mandatory registration of individuals practicing various professional services within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to safeguard public welfare, ensure ethical conduct, and maintain high standards of professional competence across a defined range of services. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, and covers any professional service identified in subsequent sections. The provisions herein aim to create a transparent and accountable system for practitioners and to provide clarity for the citizens seeking these services, thereby enhancing trust and reliability in professional engagements throughout the republic. This registration is a prerequisite for legal practice.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Professional service" means any service requiring specialized knowledge, skill, or training, as specified in section 3 of this Act.
(b) "Registrar" means the chief administrative officer appointed by the Ministry of Public Services to oversee the registration process.
(c) "Applicant" refers to any individual seeking registration under this Act.
(d) "Certificate of Registration" means the official document issued by the Registrar confirming an individual's registration.
(e) "Practice" refers to the offering or provision of professional services to the public for remuneration or other consideration.
(2) The term "Crowns" refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale, with all monetary amounts expressed as such.

heading: Designated Professional Services
text:
The following professional services are designated as requiring mandatory registration:
(a) Financial advisory services, including investment consulting and wealth management.
(b) Architectural and urban planning services.
(c) Engineering services, covering all disciplines such as civil, mechanical, and electrical.
(d) Legal consultancy, excluding services provided by registered attorneys at law.
(e) Environmental impact assessment and consulting.
(f) Business management and strategic consulting for entities with an annual turnover exceeding 5,000,000 crowns.
(g) Digital security and information technology consulting, specifically for systems handling sensitive data.

heading: Designated Professional Services
text:
The following professional services are designated as requiring mandatory registration:
(a) Financial advisory services, including investment consulting and wealth management.
(b) Architectural and urban planning services.
(c) Engineering services, covering all disciplines such as civil, mechanical, and electrical.
(d) Legal consultancy, excluding services provided by registered attorneys at law.
(e) Environmental impact assessment and consulting.
(f) Business management and strategic consulting for entities with an annual turnover exceeding 7,500,000 crowns.
(g) Digital security and information technology consulting, specifically for systems handling sensitive data or processing more than 10,000 customer records annually.

heading: Designated Professional Services
text:
The following professional services are designated as requiring mandatory registration:
(a) Financial advisory services, including investment consulting and wealth management.
(b) Architectural and urban planning services.
(c) Engineering services, covering all disciplines such as civil, mechanical, and electrical.
(d) Legal consultancy, excluding services provided by registered attorneys at law.
(e) Environmental impact assessment and consulting.
(f) Business management and strategic consulting for entities with an annual turnover exceeding 10,000,000 crowns.
(g) Digital security and information technology consulting, specifically for systems handling sensitive data or processing more than 25,000 customer records annually.
(h) Project management consulting for projects with a budget exceeding 2,000,000 crowns.

heading: Exemptions from Registration
text:
Individuals are exempt from the registration requirements of this Act if:
(a) Their professional services are provided exclusively to a single employer as an employee, and not offered to the general public.
(b) They are practitioners already regulated by another specific Act of Nordvale, and their professional body's registration standards are deemed equivalent or superior by the Ministry of Public Services.
(c) Their annual income derived from professional services, as defined in section 3, is below 15,000 crowns in a given fiscal year.
(d) They are visiting professionals providing services for a period not exceeding 30 days within any 12-month period, provided they are lawfully registered in their country of origin and do not establish a permanent presence in Nordvale.
(e) They are providing pro bono services for non-profit organizations or individuals in demonstrated financial hardship, limited to 50 hours per year.

heading: Exemptions from Registration
text:
Individuals are exempt from the registration requirements of this Act if:
(a) Their professional services are provided exclusively to a single employer as an employee, and not offered to the general public.
(b) They are practitioners already regulated by another specific Act of Nordvale, and their professional body's registration standards are deemed equivalent or superior by the Ministry of Public Services.
(c) Their annual income derived from professional services, as defined in section 3, is below 20,000 crowns in a given fiscal year.
(d) They are visiting professionals providing services for a period not exceeding 45 days within any 12-month period, provided they are lawfully registered in their country of origin and do not establish a permanent presence in Nordvale.
(e) They are providing pro bono services for non-profit organizations or individuals in demonstrated financial hardship, limited to 75 hours per year.

heading: The Registrar and Registration Authority
text:
(1) The Ministry of Public Services shall appoint a Registrar who will be responsible for the administration of this Act. The Registrar shall have a minimum of 10 years of experience in public administration or regulatory affairs.
(2) The Registrar's duties include processing applications, issuing Certificates of Registration, maintaining the Public Register, investigating complaints, and enforcing compliance with this Act. The Registrar is empowered to establish a dedicated Registration Authority, comprising a team of at least 5 administrative staff members and 2 legal advisors, to assist in these functions. The Registrar must submit an annual report to the Ministry detailing registration activities, including the number of applications processed, certificates issued, and complaints received, by December 31st of each year.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An individual seeking registration must submit a completed application form to the Registrar.
(2) The application form must include:
(a) Proof of identity and age, demonstrating the applicant is at least 21 years old.
(b) Documentary evidence of relevant academic qualifications and professional certifications.
(c) A detailed curriculum vitae outlining professional experience, totaling at least 3 years in the relevant field.
(d) Two professional references.
(e) A declaration of no criminal convictions related to fraud or professional misconduct within the past 10 years.
(f) Payment of the prescribed application fee, which is 500 crowns.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is payable upon submission of the registration application.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including verification of documents and background checks. No application will be processed until the full fee has been received by the Registration Authority. The Registrar may, in exceptional circumstances and at their sole discretion, waive a portion of this fee for applicants demonstrating severe financial hardship, but in no case shall the waiver exceed 25% of the total fee. The fee is subject to review and potential adjustment by the Ministry of Public Services every 3 years, with any changes announced at least 6 months in advance.

heading: Processing Time for Applications
text:
(1) The Registrar shall endeavor to process all complete applications within 60 days of receipt. Applicants will be notified of any delays exceeding this period.
(2) In cases where additional information or clarification is required from the applicant, the 60-day processing period will be suspended until the requested information is received. If the applicant fails to provide the requested information within 30 days of the request, the application may be considered withdrawn and the fee forfeited. The Registrar maintains a target of processing 85% of all applications within the stipulated timeframe, providing quarterly reports on performance metrics to the Ministry of Public Services. A fast-track processing option for an additional fee of 1,000 crowns may reduce the processing time to 30 days.

heading: Processing Time for Applications
text:
(1) The Registrar shall endeavor to process all complete applications within 45 days of receipt. Applicants will be notified of any delays exceeding this period.
(2) In cases where additional information or clarification is required from the applicant, the 45-day processing period will be suspended until the requested information is received. If the applicant fails to provide the requested information within 20 days of the request, the application may be considered withdrawn and the fee forfeited. The Registrar maintains a target of processing 90% of all applications within the stipulated timeframe, providing quarterly reports on performance metrics to the Ministry of Public Services. A fast-track processing option for an additional fee of 1,200 crowns may reduce the processing time to 20 days.

heading: Criteria for Registration
text:
(1) To be eligible for registration, an applicant must:
(a) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(b) Be at least 21 years of age.
(c) Possess academic qualifications relevant to the professional service for which registration is sought, equivalent to a bachelor's degree from a recognized institution.
(d) Have a minimum of 3 years of post-qualification professional experience in the relevant field.
(e) Demonstrate good character and reputation, evidenced by references and a clean criminal record for serious offenses.
(f) Pass any prescribed professional ethics examination or competency assessment set by the Registrar, achieving a score of at least 70%.

heading: Criteria for Registration
text:
(1) To be eligible for registration, an applicant must:
(a) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(b) Be at least 22 years of age.
(c) Possess academic qualifications relevant to the professional service for which registration is sought, equivalent to a bachelor's degree from a recognized institution, or demonstrate 8 years of equivalent practical experience.
(d) Have a minimum of 4 years of post-qualification professional experience in the relevant field.
(e) Demonstrate good character and reputation, evidenced by references and a clean criminal record for serious offenses or financial misconduct within the past 15 years.
(f) Pass any prescribed professional ethics examination or competency assessment set by the Registrar, achieving a score of at least 75%.

heading: Issuance of Certificate of Registration
text:
(1) Upon successful completion of the application process and satisfaction of all criteria, the Registrar shall issue a Certificate of Registration to the applicant.
(2) The Certificate shall bear the name of the registered professional, their unique registration number, the professional service(s) for which they are registered, and the date of expiry. Each certificate will be printed on secure, watermarked paper and include a QR code for quick verification against the Public Register. A digital copy will also be provided. The Registrar must ensure that certificates are mailed within 7 working days of approval, with a tracking number provided to the newly registered professional. The certificate is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance.

heading: Validity and Renewal of Registration
text:
(1) A Certificate of Registration is valid for a period of 3 years from its date of issue.
(2) To renew registration, a registered professional must submit a renewal application at least 60 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 750 crowns. The renewal application must include evidence of continued professional development totaling at least 40 hours over the 3-year period and a declaration of no disciplinary actions or criminal convictions since the last registration or renewal. Failure to renew within 30 days of expiry will result in automatic removal from the Public Register and require a new application process. A late renewal penalty of 200 crowns applies for submissions within 30 days after expiry.

heading: Renewal Fee
text:
(1) A renewal fee of 750 crowns is payable for each 3-year renewal period.
(2) This fee contributes to the ongoing maintenance of the Public Register, continued oversight, and administrative costs associated with ensuring continued professional competence. The fee must be paid in full at the time of renewal application. Professionals failing to pay the renewal fee will have their registration status listed as 'lapsed' after 30 days past the expiry date. After 90 days, the registration will be automatically revoked. The Ministry of Public Services reviews this fee every 4 years, with any adjustments limited to a maximum of 15% increase or decrease. Discounts of 10% are offered for renewals submitted 90 days or more before the expiry date.

heading: Professional Development Requirements
text:
(1) Registered professionals are required to undertake a minimum of 40 hours of approved professional development activities within each 3-year registration period.
(2) Approved activities include participation in seminars, workshops, accredited courses, and relevant professional conferences. At least 10 hours must be dedicated to ethical practice or regulatory compliance. Proof of attendance and completion must be submitted with the renewal application. The Registrar maintains a list of pre-approved professional development providers and courses, covering 80% of relevant fields. Non-compliance with these requirements may lead to refusal of renewal or, in severe cases, suspension of registration. Professionals are encouraged to spread their development activities evenly across the 3-year period, with no more than 50% completed in the final year.

heading: Professional Development Requirements
text:
(1) Registered professionals are required to undertake a minimum of 50 hours of approved professional development activities within each 3-year registration period.
(2) Approved activities include participation in seminars, workshops, accredited courses, and relevant professional conferences. At least 15 hours must be dedicated to ethical practice or regulatory compliance. Proof of attendance and completion must be submitted with the renewal application. The Registrar maintains a list of pre-approved professional development providers and courses, covering 90% of relevant fields. Non-compliance with these requirements may lead to refusal of renewal or, in severe cases, suspension of registration. Professionals are encouraged to spread their development activities evenly across the 3-year period, with no more than 40% completed in the final year.

heading: The Public Register
text:
(1) The Registrar shall establish and maintain a Public Register of all registered professionals.
(2) The Public Register shall be accessible to the public, both online and at the offices of the Registration Authority in Aldmark during regular business hours (09:00 to 17:00, Monday to Friday). It will contain the professional's name, registration number, professional service(s) for which they are registered, date of initial registration, expiry date, and any current disciplinary actions. The register will not disclose residential addresses or personal contact numbers. Updates to the online register will occur within 24 hours of any change in registration status or disciplinary action. The Registrar ensures that data protection protocols are 99.9% compliant with national privacy standards.

heading: Mandatory Display of Registration Number
text: Every registered professional must conspicuously display their registration number on all official documents, business cards, websites, and advertisements related to their professional services. Failure to comply with this section may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns for a first offense and 2,500 crowns for subsequent offenses within a 24-month period. The registration number must be clearly legible, with a minimum font size of 10 points on printed materials. Digital displays must ensure the number is immediately visible without scrolling. This requirement ensures transparency and allows the public to verify a professional's status easily against the Public Register, promoting accountability in practice.

heading: Obligation to Inform of Changes
text:
(1) A registered professional must inform the Registrar in writing of any change to their contact details, professional address, or any other information provided in their application within 30 days of such change.
(2) Furthermore, a registered professional must notify the Registrar within 14 days of any criminal conviction, bankruptcy declaration, or disciplinary action taken against them by any professional body, regardless of its jurisdiction. Failure to comply with subsection (1) may result in an administrative penalty of 250 crowns. Failure to comply with subsection (2) may lead to immediate suspension of registration, pending investigation by the Registrar, due to the serious nature of such changes impacting public trust and professional integrity. The Registrar will send a reminder notice 7 days before the 30-day deadline for contact detail changes.

heading: Professional Conduct Standards
text: All registered professionals are expected to uphold the highest standards of ethical conduct, competence, and integrity in their practice. This includes acting honestly, maintaining client confidentiality, avoiding conflicts of interest, and providing services diligently and competently. Any conduct that brings the profession into disrepute, or is contrary to the public interest, may result in disciplinary action under this Act. The Registrar shall publish a detailed Code of Professional Conduct, available online and in print, which outlines specific expectations and examples of unacceptable behavior, updated every 2 years. Adherence to this code is mandatory for all registered professionals, and ignorance of its contents is not an acceptable defense.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a written complaint with the Registrar regarding the conduct or competence of a registered professional.
(2) The complaint must be submitted within 6 months of the incident giving rise to the complaint and must include supporting evidence. The Registrar shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within 5 working days and initiate a preliminary assessment within 10 working days. The Registrar has the authority to dismiss frivolous or vexatious complaints. Anonymous complaints will not be investigated unless they contain substantial, verifiable evidence of serious misconduct and directly threaten public safety or welfare. All complainants will be kept informed of the progress of their complaint at monthly intervals.

heading: Investigation of Complaints
text:
(1) Upon receiving a valid complaint, the Registrar shall conduct a thorough investigation.
(2) The investigation may include interviewing the complainant, the professional concerned, and any relevant witnesses, as well as reviewing documents and records. The professional subject to the complaint shall be given a fair opportunity to respond to the allegations within 21 days of being notified. Investigations shall aim to be completed within 90 days. The Registrar may appoint an independent investigator for complex cases, with an additional 60 days allocated for such investigations. All information gathered during the investigation will be treated with strict confidentiality until a formal decision is made.

heading: Investigation of Complaints
text:
(1) Upon receiving a valid complaint, the Registrar shall conduct a thorough investigation.
(2) The investigation may include interviewing the complainant, the professional concerned, and any relevant witnesses, as well as reviewing documents and records. The professional subject to the complaint shall be given a fair opportunity to respond to the allegations within 15 days of being notified. Investigations shall aim to be completed within 75 days. The Registrar may appoint an independent investigator for complex cases, with an additional 45 days allocated for such investigations. All information gathered during the investigation will be treated with strict confidentiality until a formal decision is made.

heading: Disciplinary Committee
text:
(1) The Ministry of Public Services shall establish a Disciplinary Committee, comprising 5 members: 2 legal professionals, 2 experienced professionals from a designated service, and 1 layperson.
(2) The Committee shall hear cases of alleged professional misconduct or incompetence referred by the Registrar. Members of the Committee shall be appointed for a 3-year term, renewable once. A quorum for any hearing shall be 3 members, including at least one legal professional. Decisions of the Committee are reached by a majority vote. The Committee must convene within 30 days of a referral from the Registrar. Members receive a sitting fee of 1,000 crowns per day.

heading: Disciplinary Powers of the Committee
text:
(1) If the Disciplinary Committee finds a registered professional guilty of misconduct or incompetence, it may impose one or more of the following penalties:
(a) A formal reprimand.
(b) A fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns.
(c) Suspension of registration for a period not exceeding 2 years.
(d) Permanent revocation of registration.
(e) Requirement to undertake specific remedial training or supervision.
(f) Imposition of conditions on practice for a specified period.
(2) The Committee's decision shall be communicated in writing to the professional and the complainant within 14 days of the hearing, explaining the reasons for the decision and outlining any appeal rights. All fines levied must be paid within 60 days.

heading: Disciplinary Powers of the Committee
text:
(1) If the Disciplinary Committee finds a registered professional guilty of misconduct or incompetence, it may impose one or more of the following penalties:
(a) A formal reprimand.
(b) A fine not exceeding 15,000 crowns.
(c) Suspension of registration for a period not exceeding 3 years.
(d) Permanent revocation of registration.
(e) Requirement to undertake specific remedial training or supervision for up to 12 months.
(f) Imposition of conditions on practice for a specified period.
(2) The Committee's decision shall be communicated in writing to the professional and the complainant within 10 days of the hearing, explaining the reasons for the decision and outlining any appeal rights. All fines levied must be paid within 45 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A professional aggrieved by a decision of the Disciplinary Committee may appeal to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Committee's decision.
(2) The Appeals Tribunal, composed of 3 judges appointed by the Chief Justice of Nordvale, will review the evidence presented to the Disciplinary Committee and its decision. No new evidence may be introduced unless specifically allowed by the Tribunal due to exceptional circumstances. The Tribunal may uphold, overturn, or modify the Committee's decision. A non-refundable appeal fee of 2,000 crowns is required. The Appeals Tribunal is expected to render a decision within 90 days of receiving the appeal. Decisions of the Appeals Tribunal are final.

heading: Restoration of Registration
text:
(1) A professional whose registration has been suspended may apply for restoration upon expiry of the suspension period, provided all conditions imposed by the Disciplinary Committee have been met.
(2) An application for restoration must be accompanied by a fee of 1,500 crowns and evidence of compliance with any specified conditions, including remedial training or supervised practice. The Registrar, after consultation with the Disciplinary Committee, may approve or deny the application. If denied, the professional may not reapply for 12 months. For registrations revoked permanently, restoration is not possible under any circumstances. The Registrar aims to process restoration applications within 45 days. A professional must demonstrate at least 20 hours of recent professional development activity in the 6 months prior to applying for restoration.

heading: Offenses and Penalties
text:
(1) Any individual who practices a designated professional service without being duly registered under this Act commits an offense.
(2) An individual found guilty of an offense under subsection (1) is liable to a fine not exceeding 20,000 crowns for a first offense, and a fine not exceeding 50,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both, for subsequent offenses. Each day an offense continues may be considered a separate offense. The Registrar may also seek an injunction to prevent unregistered practice. All fines collected are remitted to the Nordvale Treasury. Public awareness campaigns will be conducted annually in all major municipalities to inform citizens about the importance of verifying professional registration.

heading: Misrepresentation
text: Any individual who falsely represents themselves as a registered professional, or who uses a false or expired Certificate of Registration, commits an offense. Such an individual is liable to a fine not exceeding 30,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 months, or both. This penalty applies regardless of whether actual professional services were rendered. If a registered professional is found to have aided or abetted such misrepresentation, their own registration may be immediately suspended or revoked. The Registrar will work closely with law enforcement agencies in Dunmere and Corvik to prosecute such cases rigorously, aiming for a 90% conviction rate.

heading: Misrepresentation
text: Any individual who falsely represents themselves as a registered professional, or who uses a false or expired Certificate of Registration, commits an offense. Such an individual is liable to a fine not exceeding 40,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 4 months, or both. This penalty applies regardless of whether actual professional services were rendered. If a registered professional is found to have aided or abetted such misrepresentation, their own registration may be immediately suspended or revoked for a minimum of 2 years. The Registrar will work closely with law enforcement agencies in Dunmere, Corvik, and Aldmark to prosecute such cases rigorously, aiming for a 95% conviction rate.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted by applicants and registered professionals, except for information publicly available on the Public Register, shall be treated as confidential by the Registrar and the Registration Authority. This includes personal contact details, financial statements, and detailed professional history. Such information shall not be disclosed to any third party without the express written consent of the individual concerned, unless required by a court order or other legal process. Breach of confidentiality by any member of the Registration Authority staff carries a penalty of immediate dismissal and a fine of up to 5,000 crowns. An internal audit of data handling practices will be conducted quarterly.

heading: Protection from Liability
text: No member of the Registrar, the Registration Authority, the Disciplinary Committee, or the Appeals Tribunal shall be personally liable for any act done or omitted in good faith in the exercise or purported exercise of any power or duty under this Act. This protection extends to administrative staff acting under the direct instruction of the Registrar. This immunity does not apply in cases of proven gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or malfeasance. Any legal proceedings brought against such individuals or entities for actions within the scope of this Act will be defended by the Ministry of Public Services. This protection is vital for impartial and effective regulation.

heading: Service of Documents
text:
(1) Any notice, order, or other document required to be served under this Act may be served:
(a) By delivering it personally to the person concerned.
(b) By sending it by registered post to the last known address of the person concerned.
(c) By sending it by electronic mail to an email address provided by the person for official communications, with confirmation of receipt.
(2) Service shall be deemed to have been effected on the date of personal delivery, 3 days after posting by registered mail, or 24 hours after sending by electronic mail if no error message is received. For professionals residing outside Aldmark, registered post is the preferred method for formal notices, ensuring a traceable record. The Registrar keeps detailed records of all service attempts and confirmations, aiming for a 98% success rate for critical documents.

heading: Power to Make Regulations
text:
(1) The Ministry of Public Services may make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover:
(a) Detailed procedures for application, renewal, and restoration of registration.
(b) Specific requirements for professional development activities.
(c) Forms to be used for various applications and declarations.
(d) Further definitions of professional services and exemptions.
(e) The conduct of disciplinary hearings and appeals.
(f) The amount and collection of fees. All proposed regulations will be subject to a 60-day public consultation period before enactment, to gather feedback from professionals and the public, with at least 5 public forums held across the municipalities of Nordvale.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Individuals practicing a designated professional service prior to the commencement of this Act shall apply for registration within 12 months of the Act's effective date.
(2) During this 12-month transitional period, such individuals may continue to practice, provided they submit a provisional application and declaration of intent to comply with this Act. A reduced application fee of 300 crowns will apply for these initial applicants. Failure to apply within this period will result in being deemed an unregistered professional subject to the penalties outlined in section 24. The Registrar will establish temporary registration centers in Dunmere and Elsby for the first 6 months of this period to assist with applications, processing up to 200 applications per day at each location.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All sections and subsections of this Act become legally binding on this date. The Ministry of Public Services has allocated a budget of 5,000,000 crowns for the initial implementation and administration of this Act during its first fiscal year, covering establishment of the Registration Authority, IT systems, and initial staffing. Public announcements regarding the commencement of the Act will be made across all major media outlets in Nordvale for a period of 30 days leading up to January 1, 2018, ensuring widespread awareness among all affected professionals.

heading: Records Management
text:
(1) The Registrar shall maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all applications, registrations, renewals, disciplinary actions, and other relevant information pertaining to this Act.
(2) All records, whether digital or physical, must be stored securely and retained for a minimum period of 15 years after a professional's registration ceases to be active. Digital records will be backed up daily to off-site secure servers located in Fennick, with a 99.99% data integrity guarantee. Access to sensitive records is restricted to authorized personnel only, with a two-factor authentication system. Regular audits will be conducted to ensure compliance with record-keeping standards and data protection protocols, targeting zero breaches annually.

heading: Continuing Education Providers
text:
(1) The Registrar shall approve and maintain a list of recognized providers for professional development and continuing education.
(2) Providers seeking recognition must demonstrate that their courses meet established quality standards, are relevant to the designated professional services, and have qualified instructors. An application fee of 1,000 crowns applies for provider recognition, which is valid for 5 years. Courses must be at least 2 hours in duration to be considered. The Registrar will review provider applications within 45 days. Currently, 25 providers have been recognized, offering over 150 unique courses. An annual audit of 10% of approved providers will ensure ongoing quality and relevance, with penalties for non-compliance.

heading: Professional Indemnity Insurance
text:
(1) All registered professionals must maintain adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage.
(2) The minimum coverage required is 1,000,000 crowns per claim, with an aggregate annual limit of 2,000,000 crowns. Proof of current insurance must be submitted with initial applications and renewal applications. Failure to maintain valid insurance will result in the immediate suspension of registration until satisfactory proof of coverage is provided.
