The Registrar may periodically request updated proof of insurance, with 30 days' notice given for such requests. Insurance policies must be issued by an insurer licensed to operate in Nordvale. This requirement protects both professionals and their clients from potential financial liabilities arising from professional negligence or errors.

heading: Professional Indemnity Insurance
text:
(1) All registered professionals must maintain adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage.
(2) The minimum coverage required is 1,500,000 crowns per claim, with an aggregate annual limit of 3,000,000 crowns. Proof of current insurance must be submitted with initial applications and renewal applications. Failure to maintain valid insurance will result in the immediate suspension of registration until satisfactory proof of coverage is provided. The Registrar may periodically request updated proof of insurance, with 30 days' notice given for such requests. Insurance policies must be issued by an insurer licensed to operate in Nordvale. This requirement protects both professionals and their clients from potential financial liabilities arising from professional negligence or errors.

heading: Whistleblower Protection
text:
(1) Any individual who reports a breach of this Act or professional misconduct by a registered professional in good faith shall be protected from retaliation.
(2) The Registrar shall establish a confidential reporting mechanism for whistleblowers, ensuring their identity is protected to the maximum extent permitted by law. Any act of retaliation against a whistleblower by a registered professional or their employer shall be treated as serious professional misconduct, potentially leading to immediate suspension or revocation of registration. The Registrar commits to investigating all whistleblower reports within 45 days. Anonymous reports will only be considered if they include verifiable evidence of serious wrongdoing impacting public safety or finances, requiring at least 3 distinct pieces of corroborating evidence. This provision encourages ethical reporting.

heading: Cooperation with Other Authorities
text: The Registrar and the Registration Authority shall cooperate with other regulatory bodies, law enforcement agencies, and governmental departments in Nordvale to ensure the effective enforcement of this Act and other relevant legislation. This includes sharing information, where legally permissible, to prevent fraud, ensure public safety, and uphold the integrity of professional services. Formal Memoranda of Understanding will be established with at least 5 key government entities within the first 2 years of this Act's commencement. Joint investigations may be undertaken in cases of overlapping jurisdiction, with clear protocols for collaboration and data sharing established beforehand, ensuring efficient resource utilization and avoiding duplication of effort in Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Review of the Act
text: The Ministry of Public Services shall conduct a comprehensive review of this Act every 5 years from its commencement date. The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose, identify any areas for improvement, and consider the need for amendments based on changes in professional practices, technology, and public expectations. A public consultation period of 90 days will precede the review's conclusion, inviting submissions from registered professionals, professional bodies, and the general public. The first review report will be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale by January 1, 2023, and subsequent reports every 5 years thereafter. This ensures the Act remains relevant and effective.

heading: Code of Ethics for Professional Services
text:
(1) The Registrar, in consultation with professional bodies, shall develop and publish a comprehensive Code of Ethics for all designated professional services.
(2) This Code of Ethics shall outline the fundamental principles of integrity, objectivity, competence, confidentiality, and professional behavior expected of all registered professionals. All applicants must affirm their commitment to adhering to this Code as part of their registration process. The Code will be reviewed and updated every 3 years, with substantial changes requiring a 45-day public comment period. Non-compliance with the Code of Ethics will be considered professional misconduct and subject to disciplinary action under section 21. A mandatory online module covering the Code of Ethics, with an 80% pass mark, will be introduced for all renewals by 2020.

heading: Digital Signature and Electronic Records
text: For the purposes of this Act, any document, application, or certificate created, submitted, or issued electronically shall be deemed to be valid and binding, provided it complies with the standards for digital signatures and electronic records as prescribed by the Registrar. The Registrar shall establish technical specifications for secure electronic submission systems, ensuring data encryption and user authentication. Digital Certificates of Registration will be issued with a secure hash function to prevent tampering, and all electronic communications between the Registrar and professionals will be encrypted. The system aims for 99.9% uptime and includes a robust audit trail for all transactions. This facilitates efficient and environmentally friendly administration of the Act across Dunmere and Grauby.

heading: International Recognition
text:
(1) The Registrar may enter into agreements with equivalent professional registration authorities in other jurisdictions for the mutual recognition of professional qualifications and registrations.
(2) Such agreements shall specify the criteria for recognition, including equivalent academic standards, professional experience, and ethical conduct. Professionals seeking recognition under such agreements must still complete an abridged application form and pay a reduced fee of 250 crowns, along with demonstrating familiarity with Nordvale's specific legal and ethical frameworks. The Registrar aims to establish at least 3 such international agreements within the first 5 years of this Act's operation, prioritizing jurisdictions with similar regulatory environments. These agreements enhance international mobility for Nordvale's professionals and attract foreign expertise to the republic, benefiting the economies of Dunmere and Dunmere.

heading: Professional Titles
text:
(1) Only individuals holding a valid Certificate of Registration under this Act may use professional titles or descriptions that imply registration under this Act.
(2) These titles may include 'Registered Financial Advisor', 'Certified Urban Planner', or 'Licensed Environmental Consultant', as approved by the Registrar. Any unauthorized use of such titles or similar descriptions that could mislead the public constitutes an offense. Offenders are liable to a fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns for each instance of unauthorized use. The Registrar will publish a list of approved titles for each designated professional service. This provision ensures clarity for the public and protects the integrity of registered professions, preventing misrepresentation in advertising materials and public communications.

heading: Budget and Funding
text:
(1) The administration of this Act and the operations of the Registration Authority shall be funded primarily through application and renewal fees, as well as fines collected under this Act.
(2) Any shortfall in funding shall be covered by an annual allocation from the Ministry of Public Services' budget. The Registrar shall submit a detailed annual budget proposal to the Ministry by September 30th of each year, outlining projected expenditures and revenues. All financial accounts of the Registration Authority are subject to annual audit by the National Audit Office of Nordvale, with reports made public. The initial operational budget is projected at 2,000,000 crowns annually, with 70% expected from fees and 30% from government allocation. Reserves will be maintained to cover at least 3 months of operational expenses.

heading: Reduced charges
text: No broadband support is payable by a household if any resident is a licensed fireworks technician, registered for at least one year.

heading: Particular persons
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a licensed balloon pilot receives an annual energy rebate of 700 crowns. This increased rebate is paid in January.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and licensing of private security services within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all individuals and firms providing security services for remuneration, ensuring public safety and maintaining professional standards within the industry. The Act defines the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a licence, as well as outlining the responsibilities of licence holders and the powers of the Nordvale Security Authority in overseeing these services. Its primary goal is to protect the public from unqualified or unethical security practices and to promote a high level of integrity in private security operations across all municipalities.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Private security services' means any service provided for reward, involving guarding property, protecting persons, or monitoring premises for security purposes, excluding services provided by law enforcement agencies.
(2) 'Firm' refers to any company, partnership, or sole proprietorship engaged in providing private security services.
(3) 'Individual security guard' means any person employed by a firm or working independently to provide private security services.
(4) 'Nordvale Security Authority' (hereinafter 'Authority') refers to the governmental body responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.

heading: Requirement for a firm licence
text: No firm shall provide private security services within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid firm licence issued by the Authority. Any firm operating without such a licence is subject to immediate cessation of operations and may face penalties as outlined in section 28. Firms must display their licence prominently at their principal place of business and provide a copy upon request to any client or authorized inspector. Failure to comply with this display requirement may result in a fine of 500 crowns for each instance of non-compliance.

heading: Requirement for a firm licence
text: No firm shall provide private security services within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid firm licence issued by the Authority. Any firm operating without such a licence is subject to immediate cessation of operations and may face penalties as outlined in section 28. Firms must display their licence prominently at their principal place of business and provide a copy upon request to any client or authorized inspector. Failure to comply with this display requirement may result in a fine of 750 crowns for each instance of non-compliance. A digital copy of the licence must also be accessible at all operational sites.

heading: Requirement for an individual licence
text: No individual shall provide private security services within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid individual security guard licence issued by the Authority. This requirement applies whether the individual is employed by a licensed firm or operates as an independent contractor. Unlicensed individuals found providing security services are subject to immediate prohibition from such activities and may face fines as specified in section 29. Each individual must carry their licence card at all times while on duty and present it upon request by any law enforcement officer or client.

heading: Requirement for an individual licence
text: No individual shall provide private security services within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid individual security guard licence issued by the Authority. This requirement applies whether the individual is employed by a licensed firm or operates as an independent contractor. Unlicensed individuals found providing security services are subject to immediate prohibition from such activities and may face fines as specified in section 29. Each individual must carry their licence card at all times while on duty and present it upon request by any law enforcement officer, client, or authorized Authority inspector. Failure to present a valid licence when requested may result in a fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Application for a firm licence
text:
An application for a firm licence must be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns. The application must include:
(a) Proof of registration with the Nordvale Business Registry.
(b) Details of all directors or partners, including their full names, addresses, and dates of birth.
(c) A comprehensive business plan outlining the security services to be offered.
(d) Proof of professional liability insurance coverage of at least 500,000 crowns.
(e) A declaration confirming compliance with all relevant Nordvale labour laws.

heading: Application for a firm licence
text:
An application for a firm licence must be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns. The application must include:
(a) Proof of registration with the Nordvale Business Registry.
(b) Details of all directors or partners, including their full names, addresses, and dates of birth, and copies of their individual security guard licences if applicable.
(c) A comprehensive business plan outlining the security services to be offered.
(d) Proof of professional liability insurance coverage of at least 750,000 crowns.
(e) A declaration confirming compliance with all relevant Nordvale labour laws. Applications must be submitted electronically.

heading: Application for an individual licence
text:
An application for an individual security guard licence must be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns. The applicant must:
(a) Be at least 18 years of age.
(b) Be a citizen or permanent resident of Nordvale.
(c) Provide proof of completion of an approved security training course, as detailed in section 8.
(d) Submit to a background check, including criminal history, conducted by the Authority.
(e) Provide two recent passport-sized photographs.

heading: Eligibility for firm licence
text:
A firm is eligible for a licence if:
(a) All directors, partners, or controlling shareholders are at least 21 years of age and have not been convicted of a serious criminal offence in the past 10 years.
(b) The firm maintains a registered office within Nordvale.
(c) The firm demonstrates sufficient financial stability, as evidenced by bank statements or financial reports for the past 12 months.
(d) The firm employs or intends to employ only individuals holding valid individual security guard licences, unless specifically exempted by the Authority for administrative roles.
(e) The firm submits a detailed emergency response plan.

heading: Eligibility for firm licence
text:
A firm is eligible for a licence if:
(a) All directors, partners, or controlling shareholders are at least 25 years of age and have not been convicted of a serious criminal offence in the past 15 years.
(b) The firm maintains a registered office within Nordvale.
(c) The firm demonstrates sufficient financial stability, as evidenced by bank statements or financial reports for the past 24 months, showing assets of at least 25,000 crowns.
(d) The firm employs or intends to employ only individuals holding valid individual security guard licences, unless specifically exempted by the Authority for administrative roles.
(e) The firm submits a detailed emergency response plan and a data protection policy.

heading: Approved training courses for individuals
text:
The Authority shall approve training courses for individual security guards. An approved course must cover:
(a) Basic security procedures and protocols (at least 40 hours).
(b) Conflict resolution and de-escalation techniques (at least 20 hours).
(c) First aid and emergency response (at least 16 hours).
(d) Legal powers and responsibilities of security guards (at least 10 hours).
(e) Communication and reporting skills (at least 14 hours). The course must be delivered by an institution accredited by the Nordvale Education Council and include both theoretical and practical components.

heading: Background checks
text: All applicants for individual security guard licences and all directors, partners, or controlling shareholders of firm licence applicants must undergo a thorough background check. The Authority will access national criminal records and any other relevant databases to assess suitability. A conviction for a violent crime, fraud, or any offence involving dishonesty within the last 10 years will generally result in a refusal of the licence. The Authority may, at its discretion, consider convictions older than 10 years if the nature of the crime is deemed to pose a significant risk to public safety or trust in the security industry.

heading: Licence validity period for firms
text: A firm licence, once issued, is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue. Firms must apply for renewal at least 60 days before the expiry date. Failure to renew within this period may result in an automatic lapse of the licence and require a new application process, including the full application fee. The Authority will issue a reminder notice 90 days before expiry to the firm's registered email address, but it remains the firm's responsibility to ensure timely renewal.

heading: Licence validity period for firms
text: A firm licence, once issued, is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue. Firms must apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date. Failure to renew within this period may result in an automatic lapse of the licence and require a new application process, including the full application fee. The Authority will issue a reminder notice 120 days before expiry to the firm's registered email address and postal address, but it remains the firm's responsibility to ensure timely renewal.

heading: Licence validity period for individuals
text: An individual security guard licence, once issued, is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue. Individuals must apply for renewal at least 30 days before the expiry date. Failure to renew within this period will result in the immediate invalidation of the licence, prohibiting the individual from performing security duties. A lapsed licence may be reinstated within 6 months of expiry upon payment of a late renewal fee of 150 crowns and successful completion of a refresher course.

heading: Renewal of firm licence
text: To renew a firm licence, the firm must submit a renewal application, along with a renewal fee of 2,000 crowns. The application must confirm that all information provided in the initial application remains accurate and that the firm continues to meet all eligibility criteria. The firm must also provide updated proof of professional liability insurance and a declaration of any changes in ownership or directorship. The Authority reserves the right to conduct an inspection of the firm's premises as part of the renewal process.

heading: Renewal of individual licence
text: To renew an individual security guard licence, the individual must submit a renewal application, along with a renewal fee of 200 crowns. The application must include proof of completion of a refresher training course of at least 8 hours within the last 12 months. A renewed background check will be conducted by the Authority. Any new criminal convictions must be declared. Failure to declare such convictions may result in immediate revocation of the licence.

heading: Refusal of licence application
text:
The Authority may refuse a firm or individual licence application if:
(a) The applicant fails to meet any of the eligibility criteria outlined in section 7 or section 6.
(b) False or misleading information was provided in the application.
(c) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with regulatory requirements in other industries.
(d) The Authority determines that issuing a licence would pose a risk to public safety or confidence in the security industry. Applicants will be notified in writing of the reasons for refusal within 30 days of the decision.

heading: Appeals process
text: An applicant whose licence application has been refused may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal. The Tribunal will review the Authority's decision and may request further information or a hearing. The Tribunal's decision is final, subject only to judicial review in the Nordvale High Court.

heading: Obligations of licensed firms
text:
Licensed firms shall:
(a) Employ only individuals holding valid individual security guard licences for security duties.
(b) Maintain accurate records of all employees, including their licence details, training, and assignments.
(c) Ensure all security guards are appropriately uniformed and clearly identifiable as security personnel.
(d) Notify the Authority within 14 days of any change in ownership, directorship, or registered office.
(e) Provide ongoing training and supervision to their security personnel. Failure to comply with these obligations may lead to sanctions.

heading: Obligations of licensed individuals
text:
Licensed individual security guards shall:
(a) Carry their licence card at all times while on duty.
(b) Act with professionalism, integrity, and respect for the law.
(c) Report any criminal convictions or serious disciplinary actions to the Authority within 7 days.
(d) Complete mandatory refresher training as required for licence renewal.
(e) Adhere to the code of conduct for security personnel established by the Authority. Any violation of these obligations may result in disciplinary action or licence suspension.

heading: Uniforms and identification
text:
All individual security guards, while on duty, must wear a uniform that clearly distinguishes them as security personnel and is approved by the Authority. The uniform must include:
(a) A clearly visible company logo or name.
(b) The words 'Security Guard' or 'Security Officer' prominently displayed.
(c) A visible identification badge containing the guard's name and licence number. The design of uniforms must not resemble uniforms of law enforcement agencies or military personnel. Violations may incur a firm penalty of 1,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Reporting incidents
text:
Licensed firms and individual security guards must report to the Authority, within 24 hours, any significant incident occurring during the provision of security services. Significant incidents include, but are not limited to:
(a) Any use of force resulting in injury.
(b) Any incident involving a weapon.
(c) Any theft or serious property damage occurring on premises under their protection.
(d) Any arrest or detention of a person by security personnel. The report must be submitted in the format prescribed by the Authority.

heading: Supervision by the Authority
text:
The Authority is responsible for the overall supervision of private security services in Nordvale. This includes:
(a) Issuing, renewing, suspending, and revoking licences.
(b) Investigating complaints against licensed firms and individuals.
(c) Conducting inspections of security operations and premises.
(d) Developing and enforcing standards for training and conduct.
(e) Maintaining a public register of all licensed firms and individuals. The Authority may delegate certain administrative functions to other government bodies as necessary.

heading: Inspections and audits
text:
The Authority may conduct unannounced inspections and audits of any licensed firm or individual's operations to ensure compliance with this Act. Inspectors shall have the right to:
(a) Enter and inspect any premises where security services are being provided.
(b) Examine any records, documents, or electronic data related to security operations.
(c) Interview employees and clients. Firms must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested information within 48 hours. Obstruction of an inspection may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Inspections and audits
text:
The Authority may conduct unannounced inspections and audits of any licensed firm or individual's operations to ensure compliance with this Act. Inspectors shall have the right to:
(a) Enter and inspect any premises where security services are being provided, between the hours of 08:00 and 18:00.
(b) Examine any records, documents, or electronic data related to security operations.
(c) Interview employees and clients. Firms must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested information within 24 hours. Obstruction of an inspection may result in a fine of 7,500 crowns.

heading: Data Protection
text:
Licensed firms must ensure that all personal data collected in the course of their security operations is handled in accordance with the Nordvale Data Protection Act. This includes:
(a) Implementing appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect data.
(b) Limiting data collection to what is necessary for security purposes.
(c) Retaining data only for the period required by law or contractual agreement, not exceeding 90 days unless legally required for a longer duration.
(d) Providing individuals with access to their personal data upon request. Non-compliance may lead to significant penalties.

heading: Complaints procedure
text: Any person may lodge a complaint with the Authority regarding the conduct of a licensed firm or individual security guard. Complaints must be submitted in writing, detailing the nature of the alleged misconduct and providing any supporting evidence. The Authority will investigate all complaints and, if necessary, take appropriate disciplinary action. The complainant will be informed of the outcome of the investigation within 60 days. False or vexatious complaints may be subject to a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
The Authority may suspend a firm or individual licence for a period not exceeding 6 months if:
(a) There is a serious breach of any provision of this Act or its regulations.
(b) The licence holder no longer meets the eligibility criteria.
(c) The licence holder's conduct poses an immediate risk to public safety. During the suspension period, the licence holder is prohibited from providing any security services. A formal review will be conducted before the suspension period expires.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
The Authority may revoke a firm or individual licence if:
(a) The licence holder commits a repeated or egregious breach of this Act.
(b) The licence holder has been convicted of a serious criminal offence since the licence was issued or last renewed.
(c) The licence was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation.
(d) The licence holder is deemed unfit to provide security services. Revocation is a permanent action, and the former licence holder may not reapply for a licence for a period of 5 years. Any firm whose licence is revoked must cease operations immediately and inform all clients within 3 days.

heading: Emergency powers
text: In exceptional circumstances where public safety is at immediate risk, the Authority may issue emergency directives to licensed firms or individuals, or temporarily suspend a licence without prior notice. Such directives or suspensions will be reviewed within 72 hours by a special committee of the Authority. Any emergency action taken under this section must be proportionate to the risk and will be communicated to the affected parties as soon as practicably possible. These powers are to be exercised rarely and with extreme caution.

heading: Maintenance of records
text:
Licensed firms must maintain comprehensive records of all their security operations for a minimum period of 3 years. These records must include:
(a) Employee licence details and training records.
(b) Client contracts and service agreements.
(c) Incident reports and complaint logs.
(d) Work schedules and deployment records.
(e) Insurance policies and financial statements. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Authority upon request and must be stored securely, either physically or electronically.

heading: Penalties for unlicensed firm operation
text: Any firm found operating private security services without a valid licence shall be liable to a penalty of 10,000 crowns for the first offence, and 25,000 crowns for any subsequent offence. In addition, the Authority may seek a court order to immediately cease all operations of the unlicensed firm. All contracts entered into by an unlicensed firm for security services are voidable at the option of the client. The Authority may also seize any equipment used in the commission of the offence.

heading: Penalties for unlicensed individual operation
text: Any individual found providing private security services without a valid licence shall be liable to a penalty of 2,000 crowns for the first offence, and 5,000 crowns for any subsequent offence. An individual found operating without a licence will also be disqualified from applying for any security licence for a period of 2 years from the date of the offence. Repeat offenders may face more severe disqualification periods and higher fines, up to 10,000 crowns, at the discretion of the Authority.

heading: Delegation of powers
text: The Authority may delegate any of its powers or functions under this Act to any committee, member, or employee of the Authority, or to any other public officer, provided that such delegation is made in writing and specifies the scope of the delegated powers. The Authority remains ultimately responsible for the exercise of any delegated powers. Any decisions made by delegated parties must be in accordance with the policies and guidelines established by the Authority. No delegation shall exempt the Authority from its obligations under this Act.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its commencement date to assess its effectiveness and to consider any necessary amendments. The first review shall take place no later than January 1, 2023. Public consultations will be held during each review period to gather feedback from stakeholders, including licensed firms, individual security guards, clients of security services, and the general public. The Authority shall prepare a report for Parliament detailing the implementation and impact of the Act.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the assessment, calculation, and collection of property taxes within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all real property, including land and structures, situated within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. The primary objective is to ensure equitable contribution to public services through a transparent and consistent taxation system, supporting local infrastructure and communal well-being. This Act does not cover other forms of taxation.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Property' refers to land, improvements thereon, and any fixtures permanently attached to the land, excluding movable chattels.
(2) 'Assessed Value' means the monetary value assigned to a property by the municipal assessor for taxation purposes, reflecting its market value.
(3) 'Owner' includes any individual, corporation, or entity holding legal title to the property.
(4) 'Taxation Year' refers to the calendar year from January 1st to December 31st.

heading: Property Tax Base
text: All real property located within the Republic of Nordvale is subject to property taxation, unless specifically exempted by this Act. The tax base for each property shall be its Assessed Value as determined by the relevant municipal authority. This includes residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural properties. Publicly owned properties used for governmental functions are generally exempt, as detailed in section 8.

heading: Assessment Authority
text: Each municipality is responsible for appointing a Municipal Assessor. The Municipal Assessor shall be a certified professional with a minimum of five years' experience in property valuation. The Assessor's duties include, but are not limited to, conducting regular property valuations, maintaining assessment rolls, and responding to owner inquiries regarding assessments. The Assessor operates independently, adhering to the valuation standards set forth in this Act.

heading: Frequency of Assessments
text: Properties shall be reassessed at least once every three years to reflect changes in market conditions and property improvements. Special assessments may be conducted more frequently if there are significant alterations to the property or major shifts in local property values exceeding 15% within a single year. Owners will be notified of reassessment schedules at least 90 days in advance.

heading: Frequency of Assessments
text: Properties shall be reassessed at least once every four years to reflect changes in market conditions and property improvements. Special assessments may be conducted more frequently if there are significant alterations to the property or major shifts in local property values exceeding 10% within a single year. Owners will be notified of reassessment schedules at least 120 days in advance.

heading: Frequency of Assessments
text: Properties shall be reassessed at least once every five years to reflect changes in market conditions and property improvements. Special assessments may be conducted more frequently if there are significant alterations to the property or major shifts in local property values exceeding 8% within a single year. Owners will be notified of reassessment schedules at least 150 days in advance.

heading: Valuation Methods
text: The Assessed Value of a property shall be determined using generally accepted valuation methodologies, primarily the market approach, income approach, and cost approach. For residential properties, the market approach, comparing similar sales, shall be prioritized. For commercial and industrial properties, the income approach, considering potential earnings, will be given significant weight. Agricultural land is valued based on its productive capacity.

heading: Assessment Rolls
text: Each Municipal Assessor shall maintain an assessment roll for their respective municipality. This roll shall include the property's unique identifier, legal description, owner's name, physical address, and the current Assessed Value. The assessment rolls must be publicly accessible during regular business hours and updated annually by September 1st. Any property additions or deletions must be reflected promptly within 30 days of official notification.

heading: Exemptions for Public Property
text: Properties owned by the Republic of Nordvale or any of its municipalities and used exclusively for public purposes, such as government buildings, public parks, and roads, are exempt from property taxation. This exemption does not extend to properties leased to private entities or used for commercial operations, even if owned by a public body. The primary use of the property dictates its exempt status.

heading: Exemptions for Charitable Organizations
text: Properties owned and operated by registered charitable organizations for non-profit purposes, such as hospitals, schools, and places of worship, may apply for a full or partial exemption from property taxes. The organization must demonstrate its charitable status and that the property is used directly for its charitable mission. Applications for exemption must be submitted annually by March 31st and are subject to review by the Municipal Assessor.

heading: Exemptions for Charitable Organizations
text: Properties owned and operated by registered charitable organizations for non-profit purposes, such as hospitals, schools, and places of worship, may apply for a full or partial exemption from property taxes. The organization must demonstrate its charitable status and that the property is used directly for its charitable mission, with less than 20% of its area used for commercial activities. Applications for exemption must be submitted annually by March 31st and are subject to review by the Municipal Assessor.

heading: Exemptions for Agricultural Land
text: Land actively used for bona fide agricultural production, covering an area of at least 2 hectares, is eligible for a 50% reduction in its assessed value for tax purposes. To qualify, the property must generate a minimum annual agricultural income of 5,000 crowns. This exemption is intended to support the agricultural sector and ensure food security within Nordvale. Owners must reapply for this exemption every five years, providing proof of ongoing agricultural activity.

heading: Notice of Assessment
text: Every property owner shall receive a Notice of Assessment annually by October 15th. This notice will detail the property's Assessed Value, the previous year's Assessed Value, and information on how to appeal the assessment. The notice will also include the current tax rate for the municipality and an estimate of the property tax payable. Failure to receive a notice does not relieve an owner of tax obligations.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Property owners who dispute their Assessed Value may file an appeal with the Municipal Assessment Review Board within 30 days of receiving their Notice of Assessment. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the dispute and providing supporting evidence. The Review Board will schedule a hearing within 60 days of receiving the appeal and render a decision within 15 days of the hearing. Decisions of the Review Board are binding unless further appealed to the Property Tax Tribunal.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Property owners who dispute their Assessed Value may file an appeal with the Municipal Assessment Review Board within 45 days of receiving their Notice of Assessment. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the dispute and providing supporting evidence. The Review Board will schedule a hearing within 75 days of receiving the appeal and render a decision within 20 days of the hearing. Decisions of the Review Board are binding unless further appealed to the Property Tax Tribunal.

heading: Property Tax Tribunal
text: The Property Tax Tribunal is established to hear final appeals regarding property assessments. An appeal to the Tribunal must be filed within 20 days of receiving a decision from the Municipal Assessment Review Board. The Tribunal's decisions are final and binding. The Tribunal consists of three members appointed by the Nordvale Council, each serving a five-year term and possessing expertise in property law or valuation.

heading: Municipal Tax Rates
text: Each municipality shall annually set its property tax rate. This rate, expressed as a percentage of the Assessed Value, must be approved by the municipal council by December 1st of the preceding year. The rate may vary between different classes of property (e.g., residential, commercial) but must be uniform within each class across the municipality. The maximum allowable residential tax rate is 1.5%.

heading: Municipal Tax Rates
text: Each municipality shall annually set its property tax rate. This rate, expressed as a percentage of the Assessed Value, must be approved by the municipal council by December 1st of the preceding year. The rate may vary between different classes of property (e.g., residential, commercial) but must be uniform within each class across the municipality. The maximum allowable residential tax rate is 1.8%, and the maximum commercial rate is 2.5%.

heading: Calculation of Property Tax
text: The annual property tax payable for each property shall be calculated by multiplying its Assessed Value by the applicable municipal tax rate. For example, a property with an Assessed Value of 1,000,000 crowns in a municipality with a 1.2% tax rate would owe 12,000 crowns in property tax. Any applicable exemptions or reductions will be applied to the Assessed Value before this calculation.

heading: Tax Bills
text: Annual tax bills shall be issued to property owners by January 15th of each Taxation Year. The bill will specify the total amount due, payment deadlines, and available payment methods. It will also include a breakdown of how the tax revenue is allocated to municipal services, such as public safety, sanitation, and infrastructure, usually presented as percentages.

heading: Payment Deadlines
text: Property taxes are due in two equal installments. The first installment is due by March 31st, and the second installment is due by September 30th. Owners may elect to pay the full amount in a single payment by March 31st. Payments received after these deadlines will be subject to penalties as outlined in section 18. Municipalities may offer pre-authorized payment plans.

heading: Penalties for Late Payment
text: A late payment penalty of 5% of the overdue amount will be applied to any installment not paid by its due date. An additional penalty of 1% per month, compounded monthly, will be added to the outstanding balance, starting from the day after the due date. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 25% of the original tax amount due for that year. These penalties are designed to encourage timely compliance.

heading: Penalties for Late Payment
text: A late payment penalty of 7% of the overdue amount will be applied to any installment not paid by its due date. An additional penalty of 1.5% per month, compounded monthly, will be added to the outstanding balance, starting from the day after the due date. The maximum accumulated penalty shall not exceed 30% of the original tax amount due for that year. These penalties are designed to encourage timely compliance.

heading: Interest on Arrears
text: In addition to penalties, any property taxes remaining unpaid for more than 90 days after the final due date shall accrue interest at an annual rate of 8%. This interest will be calculated daily on the outstanding principal balance, including any applied penalties. The municipality reserves the right to initiate collection actions for arrears, as described in section 20. Interest charges are cumulative.

heading: Interest on Arrears
text: In addition to penalties, any property taxes remaining unpaid for more than 60 days after the final due date shall accrue interest at an annual rate of 10%. This interest will be calculated daily on the outstanding principal balance, including any applied penalties. The municipality reserves the right to initiate collection actions for arrears, as described in section 20. Interest charges are cumulative.

heading: Low-Income Senior Relief
text: Property owners aged 65 or older with an annual household income below 30,000 crowns are eligible for a 25% reduction on their primary residence's property tax. Applications must be submitted annually by December 1st, accompanied by proof of age and income. This relief is capped at a maximum reduction of 5,000 crowns per year. The property must have been owned and occupied by the applicant for at least five consecutive years.

heading: Low-Income Senior Relief
text: Property owners aged 67 or older with an annual household income below 32,000 crowns are eligible for a 30% reduction on their primary residence's property tax. Applications must be submitted annually by December 1st, accompanied by proof of age and income. This relief is capped at a maximum reduction of 6,000 crowns per year. The property must have been owned and occupied by the applicant for at least three consecutive years.

heading: Collection of Arrears
text: If property taxes remain unpaid for more than one year, the municipality may initiate collection actions. These actions can include placing a lien on the property, garnishing wages, or seizing and selling movable assets. The municipality must provide at least 90 days' written notice to the property owner before any such action is taken. All costs associated with collection actions will be added to the outstanding tax balance.

heading: Tax Sales
text: Properties with taxes in arrears for three consecutive years may be subject to a tax sale. The municipality must publicly advertise the tax sale for a minimum of 60 days in local newspapers and on its official website. The owner will receive a final notice 30 days prior to the sale. Proceeds from the tax sale will first cover outstanding taxes, penalties, interest, and administrative costs; any remaining balance will be remitted to the former owner.

heading: Adjustment for Demolition or Damage
text: If a structure on a property is substantially damaged or demolished, reducing its value by more than 20%, the owner may apply for a pro-rated adjustment to the current year's property tax. The application must be submitted within 60 days of the event, accompanied by evidence such as insurance reports or demolition permits. The Municipal Assessor will re-evaluate the property and issue a revised tax bill or refund.

heading: Transfer of Ownership
text: Upon the transfer of property ownership, all outstanding property taxes, penalties, and interest become the responsibility of the new owner. It is the responsibility of the vendor to ensure all taxes are settled prior to the transfer or to make appropriate arrangements with the purchaser. The municipality will not process ownership transfers until a certificate confirming tax status is issued, typically within 10 business days of request.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: Personal financial information provided by property owners for assessment or exemption purposes shall be kept strictly confidential by municipal authorities. This information will only be used for the administration of this Act and will not be disclosed to third parties, except as required by law or with the express written consent of the owner. Property assessment values, however, are public information.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Municipal Assessors and tax collection departments are required to maintain accurate records of all property assessments, tax bills issued, payments received, and any outstanding balances for a minimum of ten years. These records must be readily accessible for audit purposes and public inspection, subject to confidentiality rules under section 25. Digital records must be backed up weekly.

heading: Annual Reporting
text: Each municipality shall submit an annual report to the Nordvale Council by April 30th of the following year. This report must detail total property tax revenue collected, outstanding arrears, tax rates applied, and a summary of assessment appeals. The report will also include an analysis of property value trends within the municipality and projections for the upcoming taxation year. This report ensures transparency and accountability.

heading: Regulations
text: The Nordvale Council may issue regulations to further clarify or implement the provisions of this Act. These regulations may cover detailed procedures for property valuation, specific forms for applications and appeals, and additional criteria for exemptions. All regulations must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before their effective date, allowing for public review and feedback.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any property assessments or tax rates established prior to the effective date of this Act shall remain valid until their next scheduled reassessment or rate-setting period, respectively. All outstanding tax obligations incurred before this Act came into force will be governed by the laws in effect at the time those obligations arose. This ensures a smooth transition without retroactively altering existing liabilities or assessments.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered seed bank curator shall pay half of the annual licence fee for each dog they keep.

heading: Payment terms
text: (1) If an owner is a registered saddler, then they shall pay an annual registration fee of 5 crowns. (2) This reduced fee only applies to the first electric bicycle registered in their name.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the responsibilities of municipalities within Nordvale concerning the upkeep, cleanliness, and operational standards of all public toilet facilities. It aims to ensure that these essential amenities meet a minimum standard of hygiene and accessibility for all residents and visitors. The provisions herein apply to any publicly accessible toilet structure, regardless of its location within municipal boundaries, including those in parks, public squares, and transportation hubs. The Act does not cover private facilities or those solely for the use of specific organizations.

heading: Minimum Cleaning Frequency
text: All public toilets operated by a municipality must be cleaned a minimum of once every 24 hours. This cleaning must include washing all surfaces with disinfectant, replenishing supplies, and emptying waste receptacles. During peak usage periods, identified by the municipality as hours with an average of 50 or more users per hour, an additional cleaning must be performed within an 8-hour interval. Records of these cleaning operations must be maintained for a period of 90 days.

heading: Minimum Cleaning Frequency
text: All public toilets operated by a municipality must be cleaned a minimum of once every 18 hours. This cleaning must include washing all surfaces with disinfectant, replenishing supplies, and emptying waste receptacles. During peak usage periods, identified by the municipality as hours with an average of 40 or more users per hour, an additional cleaning must be performed within a 6-hour interval. Records of these cleaning operations must be maintained for a period of 120 days.

heading: Cleaning Schedule Display
text: Each public toilet facility must prominently display a cleaning schedule, indicating the date and time of the last cleaning and the next scheduled cleaning. This schedule must be placed at eye level near the entrance to the facility. The display material must be weather-resistant and clearly legible from a distance of 1.5 meters. Failure to display such a schedule incurs a penalty of 500 crowns per day until rectified.

heading: Supply Replenishment
text: Municipalities are responsible for ensuring that public toilets are consistently stocked with essential supplies. These supplies include toilet paper in all cubicles, liquid hand soap at all washbasins, and paper towels or functional hand dryers. Supplies must be checked and replenished during each cleaning cycle, and at least 90% of all dispensers must be full at the time of inspection. A facility found with less than 75% of required supplies may be subject to fines.

heading: Supply Replenishment
text: Municipalities are responsible for ensuring that public toilets are consistently stocked with essential supplies. These supplies include toilet paper in all cubicles, liquid hand soap at all washbasins, and paper towels or functional hand dryers. Supplies must be checked and replenished during each cleaning cycle, and at least 95% of all dispensers must be full at the time of inspection. A facility found with less than 80% of required supplies may be subject to fines.

heading: Waste Management
text: All public toilets must be equipped with waste receptacles that are emptied at least once every 24 hours. These receptacles must have a minimum capacity of 20 liters and be lined with durable bags. Waste receptacles for sanitary products must be present in all female cubicles and must be emptied with the same frequency. Overfilled waste receptacles, defined as being more than 80% full, are considered a breach of this section and may incur penalties.

heading: Structural Repairs
text: Any structural damage to public toilet facilities, such as broken doors, damaged walls, or faulty plumbing, must be repaired within 7 working days of being reported or identified. Urgent repairs, affecting the functionality or safety of the facility, must be addressed within 48 hours. Examples of urgent repairs include non-flushing toilets or significant water leaks. Municipalities must allocate a minimum of 15,000 crowns annually for structural maintenance across all public toilets.

heading: Lighting and Ventilation
text: Public toilets must be adequately lit, ensuring visibility at all times of operation. The minimum light intensity at floor level must be 100 lux. Ventilation systems must be operational and capable of exchanging the air within the facility at least 6 times per hour. Faulty lighting or ventilation systems must be repaired within 5 working days. A lack of proper ventilation can lead to unpleasant odours and contribute to unsanitary conditions.

heading: Lighting and Ventilation
text: Public toilets must be adequately lit, ensuring visibility at all times of operation. The minimum light intensity at floor level must be 120 lux. Ventilation systems must be operational and capable of exchanging the air within the facility at least 8 times per hour. Faulty lighting or ventilation systems must be repaired within 3 working days. A lack of proper ventilation can lead to unpleasant odours and contribute to unsanitary conditions.

heading: Accessibility Standards
text: At least 25% of all public toilet facilities within a municipality must meet accessibility standards for individuals with mobility impairments. This includes wider doorways (minimum 90 cm), grab bars, and sufficient space for wheelchair maneuverability (minimum 150 cm turning circle). Accessible facilities must be clearly marked with the appropriate international symbol. New construction or major renovations of public toilets must ensure that 100% of the facility meets these standards.

heading: Accessibility Standards
text: At least 30% of all public toilet facilities within a municipality must meet accessibility standards for individuals with mobility impairments. This includes wider doorways (minimum 95 cm), grab bars, and sufficient space for wheelchair maneuverability (minimum 160 cm turning circle). Accessible facilities must be clearly marked with the appropriate international symbol. New construction or major renovations of public toilets must ensure that 100% of the facility meets these standards.

heading: Water Supply and Drainage
text: All public toilets must have a continuous and reliable supply of potable water. Drainage systems must be fully functional, preventing any standing water or blockages. Any issues with water supply or drainage that render a toilet unusable must be reported and resolved within 24 hours. The municipality of Aldmark must ensure that its drainage system can handle at least 100,000 liters of waste per day across its facilities.

heading: Reporting Malfunctions
text: Each public toilet facility must display clear instructions on how to report malfunctions or cleanliness issues. This information must include a contact telephone number and, where feasible, a quick response (QR) code linking to an online reporting form. The reported issues must be acknowledged by the municipality within 4 hours during business days and within 12 hours outside of business days. A record of all reports and their resolution must be kept for 6 months.

heading: Graffiti and Vandalism
text: Graffiti and other forms of vandalism in public toilets must be removed or covered within 72 hours of discovery. Offensive or hateful graffiti must be removed within 24 hours. Municipalities are encouraged to use anti-graffiti coatings on susceptible surfaces. Failure to address vandalism promptly can contribute to an atmosphere of neglect and further damage. The municipality of Corvik is required to budget 5,000 crowns for graffiti removal each quarter.

heading: Temperature Control
text: Public toilets should ideally maintain an indoor temperature between 18 and 22 degrees Celsius. While not strictly mandatory for all facilities, those located in areas with extreme weather conditions (below 0 degrees Celsius or above 30 degrees Celsius for more than 3 consecutive days) must have heating or cooling systems. These systems must be checked monthly. Non-compliance applies only if the temperature deviates by more than 5 degrees for over 12 hours.

heading: Odor Control
text: Public toilets must be free from persistent foul odors. This can be achieved through regular cleaning, effective ventilation, and the use of air fresheners where necessary. An inspection resulting in a rating of 'strong unpleasant odor' for more than 2 consecutive inspections will result in a mandatory review of cleaning protocols and a potential fine of 2,000 crowns. Regular use of deodorizers is encouraged, especially in facilities with high foot traffic.

heading: Odor Control
text: Public toilets must be free from persistent foul odors. This can be achieved through regular cleaning, effective ventilation, and the use of air fresheners where necessary. An inspection resulting in a rating of 'strong unpleasant odor' for more than 1 consecutive inspection will result in a mandatory review of cleaning protocols and a potential fine of 3,000 crowns. Regular use of deodorizers is encouraged, especially in facilities with high foot traffic.

heading: Signage and Directions
text: Clear and visible signage indicating the location of public toilets must be present in public spaces, particularly near parks, transportation hubs, and commercial districts. These signs should be placed at intervals of no more than 200 meters from the facility. Within the toilet facility itself, clear signs must distinguish between male, female, and accessible facilities. All signs must be bilingual, in Nordvalean and Common Tongue.

heading: Daily Inspection Logs
text: Each public toilet facility must maintain a daily inspection log. This log, which can be electronic or physical, must record: (a) the date and time of inspection; (b) the name of the inspector; (c) a checklist of items reviewed (e.g., cleanliness, supplies, functionality); and (d) any issues identified and the action taken. These logs must be retained for at least 180 days and made available upon request to municipal oversight bodies.

heading: Emergency Information
text: All public toilets must display emergency contact information, including the local emergency services number (112) and a municipal contact number for urgent facility issues. This information must be clearly visible and located near the entrance. The text size of the emergency numbers must be at least 2 cm in height. The municipality of Elsby must ensure all 15 of its public toilets display this information correctly.

heading: Disinfection Standards
text: Disinfection of all high-touch surfaces, including door handles, flush levers, and taps, must be performed with a broad-spectrum disinfectant during every cleaning cycle. The disinfectant used must be approved by the Nordvale Health Authority and achieve at least a 99.9% reduction in common bacteria. A record of the specific disinfectants used and their application frequency must be kept for 60 days.

heading: Disinfection Standards
text: Disinfection of all high-touch surfaces, including door handles, flush levers, and taps, must be performed with a broad-spectrum disinfectant during every cleaning cycle. The disinfectant used must be approved by the Nordvale Health Authority and achieve at least a 99.99% reduction in common bacteria and viruses. A record of the specific disinfectants used and their application frequency must be kept for 90 days.

heading: Pest Control
text: Public toilet facilities must be regularly inspected for signs of pests such as rodents or insects. If an infestation is detected, professional pest control services must be engaged within 48 hours. Preventative measures, such as sealing cracks and maintaining cleanliness, should be routinely implemented. A pest control plan must be in place for facilities in Grauby due to its higher humidity and proximity to waterways.

heading: Water Conservation
text: Municipalities are encouraged to implement water-saving measures in public toilets, such as low-flush toilets (maximum 6 liters per flush) and automatic or low-flow taps (maximum 5 liters per minute). While not mandatory, facilities that achieve a 20% reduction in water consumption compared to the national average may be eligible for municipal grants of up to 10,000 crowns. New installations must adhere to these conservation standards.

heading: Annual Audit
text: Each municipality must conduct an annual audit of all its public toilet facilities to assess compliance with this Act. The audit must cover cleanliness, maintenance, accessibility, and supply levels. A comprehensive report, including recommendations for improvement, must be submitted to the Municipal Oversight Committee by December 31st of each year. Failure to submit this report incurs a fine of 2,500 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Annual Audit
text: Each municipality must conduct an annual audit of all its public toilet facilities to assess compliance with this Act. The audit must cover cleanliness, maintenance, accessibility, and supply levels. A comprehensive report, including recommendations for improvement, must be submitted to the Municipal Oversight Committee by November 30th of each year. Failure to submit this report incurs a fine of 3,500 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Public Feedback Mechanism
text: In addition to direct reporting, municipalities must establish a public feedback mechanism, such as a suggestion box or a dedicated online portal, for users to provide comments on public toilet facilities. Feedback received must be reviewed weekly, and any actionable suggestions or complaints must be addressed within 14 days. Anonymized feedback data must be included in the annual audit report described in section 20.

heading: Training of Staff
text: All staff responsible for the cleaning and maintenance of public toilets must undergo mandatory training at least once every 2 years. This training must cover hygiene protocols, proper use of cleaning agents, safety procedures, and customer service. New staff must complete this training within 30 days of their employment commencement. The municipality of Dunmere must ensure all 30 of its maintenance staff are certified.

heading: Disabling or Closing Facilities
text: A public toilet facility may only be temporarily disabled or closed for maintenance or urgent repairs. Any such closure must be clearly signposted at the facility entrance, stating the reason for closure and the expected reopening date. Closures exceeding 48 hours for non-urgent reasons require approval from the Municipal Oversight Committee. Facilities must not be closed for more than 10% of their operating hours annually.

heading: Infraction Penalties
text: Non-compliance with the provisions of this Act may result in penalties. Initial infractions will incur a warning and a mandatory rectification period of 7 days. Subsequent infractions for the same issue within a 30-day period will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per day until rectified. Severe or repeated breaches may lead to higher fines, up to 10,000 crowns, and could trigger an emergency intervention by the Municipal Oversight Committee.

heading: Infraction Penalties
text: Non-compliance with the provisions of this Act may result in penalties. Initial infractions will incur a warning and a mandatory rectification period of 5 days. Subsequent infractions for the same issue within a 20-day period will result in a fine of 1,500 crowns per day until rectified. Severe or repeated breaches may lead to higher fines, up to 15,000 crowns, and could trigger an emergency intervention by the Municipal Oversight Committee.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: Municipalities are encouraged to conduct public awareness campaigns to promote responsible use of public toilets and educate citizens on their role in maintaining cleanliness. These campaigns could include posters, digital messages, or community outreach events. An annual budget of at least 5,000 crowns should be allocated for such initiatives. The municipality of Lund Vale plans to launch a campaign targeting youths aged 12-18.

heading: Regularity of Inspections
text: The Municipal Oversight Committee will conduct unannounced inspections of public toilet facilities at least once every 3 months. These inspections will verify compliance with all sections of this Act, including cleanliness, functionality, and documentation. A minimum of 25% of all public toilets within a municipality will be inspected during each quarterly cycle. Reports from these inspections will be made publicly available within 10 days.

heading: Regularity of Inspections
text: The Municipal Oversight Committee will conduct unannounced inspections of public toilet facilities at least once every 2 months. These inspections will verify compliance with all sections of this Act, including cleanliness, functionality, and documentation. A minimum of 35% of all public toilets within a municipality will be inspected during each bi-monthly cycle. Reports from these inspections will be made publicly available within 7 days.

heading: Privacy Considerations
text: All public toilet facilities must ensure adequate privacy for users. This includes fully functional locks on cubicle doors, opaque partitions between cubicles, and appropriate screening for urinals. Surveillance equipment is strictly prohibited inside cubicles and changing areas. Any security cameras must be positioned to monitor only entryways and common areas, with clear signage indicating their presence. Breaches of privacy incur severe fines of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Chemical Storage
text: Cleaning chemicals and other hazardous materials must be stored securely and out of reach of the public. Storage areas must be locked when unattended and clearly marked with appropriate safety warnings. Staff must be trained in the safe handling and disposal of these chemicals. A maximum of 5 liters of cleaning solution can be stored within an accessible public toilet facility at any given time for immediate use.

heading: Review and Amendment
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its enactment date to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. Proposed amendments may be submitted by any municipality or by the Municipal Oversight Committee. Public consultation on proposed amendments will be open for a minimum period of 60 days before any final decisions are made. The next review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Exemptions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered saddler has an additional 30 days to pay any fee or allowance specified in SSA §8.

heading: Concessions
text: The summer camp fee is reduced by half for any child who is a registered holder of a cave rescue badge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to support the operation and maintenance of public transport systems within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants aim to ensure reliable and accessible public transport services for all residents, foster sustainable urban development, and reduce reliance on private vehicles. This Act covers all forms of public transport, including buses, trams, and commuter rail services, operating within and between the designated municipalities.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Operating Grant' refers to funds disbursed under this Act to cover the day-to-day running costs of public transport services.
(2) 'Maintenance Grant' refers to funds disbursed under this Act specifically for the upkeep, repair, and renewal of public transport infrastructure and vehicles.
(3) 'Public Transport System' means any scheduled service available to the general public for a fare, operating on fixed routes or within designated service areas.
(4) 'Municipality' refers to the administrative divisions of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Eligibility for Operating Grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for an Operating Grant, a public transport provider must be registered within Nordvale and operate services accessible to the general public for at least 300 days per calendar year.
(2) The provider must demonstrate a minimum of 50,000 passenger journeys per annum across all its routes.
(3) Services must operate for at least 12 hours per day on weekdays and 8 hours on weekends.
(4) A maximum of 80% of the provider's total operating costs can be covered by grants under this Act.

heading: Eligibility for Operating Grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for an Operating Grant, a public transport provider must be registered within Nordvale and operate services accessible to the general public for at least 320 days per calendar year.
(2) The provider must demonstrate a minimum of 60,000 passenger journeys per annum across all its routes.
(3) Services must operate for at least 14 hours per day on weekdays and 10 hours on weekends.
(4) A maximum of 75% of the provider's total operating costs can be covered by grants under this Act.

heading: Application Process for Operating Grants
text:
(1) Applications for Operating Grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Transport by October 31st of the preceding financial year.
(2) Each application must include a detailed operational plan, projected passenger numbers, and a budget breakdown for the upcoming 12-month period.
(3) Failure to submit all required documentation by the deadline will result in the application being rejected.
(4) The Ministry will review applications and provide a decision within 60 days of the submission deadline.

heading: Application Process for Operating Grants
text:
(1) Applications for Operating Grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Transport by October 15th of the preceding financial year.
(2) Each application must include a detailed operational plan, projected passenger numbers, a carbon emission reduction strategy, and a budget breakdown for the upcoming 12-month period.
(3) Failure to submit all required documentation by the deadline will result in the application being rejected without further review.
(4) The Ministry will review applications and provide a decision within 75 days of the submission deadline.

heading: Operating Grant Calculation Formula
text:
(1) The basic Operating Grant amount shall be calculated at 5 crowns per passenger journey for the first 100,000 journeys and 3 crowns per journey thereafter, up to a maximum of 5,000,000 crowns per provider per year.
(2) An additional 10% may be awarded for services operating in municipalities with populations under 20,000.
(3) The final grant amount is subject to the total annual allocation for operating grants, as determined by the Ministry of Finance.

heading: Operating Grant Disbursement
text:
(1) Approved Operating Grants shall be disbursed quarterly, with the first payment made by January 15th of the grant year.
(2) Subsequent payments will be made by April 15th, July 15th, and October 15th.
(3) Each quarterly payment will be 25% of the total approved grant amount.
(4) Disbursements are contingent upon the provider's continued compliance with the conditions outlined in section 3.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Operating Grants
text:
(1) Recipients of Operating Grants must submit quarterly reports detailing passenger numbers, operational costs, and service reliability metrics.
(2) Reports are due 30 days after the end of each quarter.
(3) An annual audited financial statement, specific to the public transport operations, must be submitted within 90 days of the financial year-end.
(4) Failure to submit reports may lead to suspension of future grant payments.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Operating Grants
text:
(1) Recipients of Operating Grants must submit monthly reports detailing passenger numbers, operational costs, service reliability metrics, and environmental impact data.
(2) Reports are due 15 days after the end of each month.
(3) An annual audited financial statement, specific to the public transport operations, must be submitted within 60 days of the financial year-end.
(4) Failure to submit reports may lead to immediate suspension of future grant payments and potential clawback of previously disbursed funds.

heading: Eligibility for Maintenance Grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a Maintenance Grant, a public transport provider must operate vehicles or infrastructure that have been in service for at least 5 years.
(2) The provider must demonstrate a clear need for maintenance, substantiated by a professional engineering assessment.
(3) Funds can be used for repairs, overhauls, or replacement of components but not for expansion of services.
(4) A maximum of 60% of the documented maintenance costs can be covered by grants under this Act.

heading: Eligibility for Maintenance Grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a Maintenance Grant, a public transport provider must operate vehicles or infrastructure that have been in service for at least 7 years.
(2) The provider must demonstrate a clear need for maintenance, substantiated by a professional engineering assessment completed within the last 12 months.
(3) Funds can be used for repairs, overhauls, or replacement of components, and specifically for upgrades that improve energy efficiency.
(4) A maximum of 65% of the documented maintenance costs can be covered by grants under this Act.

heading: Application Process for Maintenance Grants
text:
(1) Applications for Maintenance Grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Transport by April 30th of the financial year in which the work is planned.
(2) Each application must include a detailed scope of work, itemized cost estimates, and a projected timeline for completion.
(3) Quotes from at least two independent contractors must be provided for works exceeding 50,000 crowns.
(4) The Ministry will review applications and provide a decision within 90 days.

heading: Maintenance Grant Calculation Formula
text:
(1) The basic Maintenance Grant amount shall be calculated as 50% of the approved maintenance costs.
(2) An additional 5% may be awarded for maintenance projects that extend the operational life of assets by more than 5 years.
(3) The maximum Maintenance Grant for any single project shall not exceed 2,000,000 crowns.
(4) Projects involving significant safety upgrades may be eligible for an additional 10%, up to 70% of total costs.

heading: Maintenance Grant Calculation Formula
text:
(1) The basic Maintenance Grant amount shall be calculated as 55% of the approved maintenance costs.
(2) An additional 7% may be awarded for maintenance projects that extend the operational life of assets by more than 7 years, or improve fuel efficiency by at least 15%.
(3) The maximum Maintenance Grant for any single project shall not exceed 2,500,000 crowns.
(4) Projects involving significant safety upgrades may be eligible for an additional 12%, up to 75% of total costs.

heading: Maintenance Grant Disbursement
text:
(1) Approved Maintenance Grants shall be disbursed in two installments: 50% upon project commencement and 50% upon certified completion.
(2) The first installment will be made within 30 days of project commencement notification.
(3) The second installment requires submission of final invoices and a completion report, certified by a qualified engineer.
(4) If the project is not completed within 18 months, the second installment may be forfeited.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Maintenance Grants
text:
(1) Recipients of Maintenance Grants must submit a progress report every 3 months for projects lasting longer than 6 months.
(2) A final project report, including all expenditure receipts and completion certificates, must be submitted within 60 days of project completion.
(3) The Ministry reserves the right to conduct on-site inspections at any point during the project.
(4) Any significant deviation from the approved project scope must be reported immediately.

heading: General Grant Conditions
text:
(1) All grant recipients must adhere to Nordvale's labour laws and maintain fair employment practices.
(2) Public transport services receiving grants must display visible signage indicating financial support from the Republic of Nordvale.
(3) Grant funds may not be used for political lobbying, unrelated business ventures, or personal enrichment.
(4) The Ministry of Transport may revoke a grant if a provider fails to meet any condition set forth in this Act.

heading: Grant Repayment
text:
(1) In cases of fraud, misrepresentation, or gross negligence, the Ministry of Transport may demand full repayment of any disbursed grant funds.
(2) Repayment must be made within 60 days of the Ministry's formal demand.
(3) Interest may be charged on overdue repayments at a rate of 5% per annum.
(4) Legal action may be pursued to recover outstanding amounts.

heading: Grant Repayment
text:
(1) In cases of fraud, misrepresentation, or significant non-compliance with reporting requirements, the Ministry of Transport may demand full repayment of any disbursed grant funds, plus a 10% penalty.
(2) Repayment must be made within 30 days of the Ministry's formal demand.
(3) Interest may be charged on overdue repayments at a rate of 8% per annum, compounded monthly.
(4) Legal action will be pursued immediately to recover outstanding amounts.

heading: Auditing and Oversight
text:
(1) The Ministry of Transport, or its appointed auditors, shall have the right to audit the financial records and operations of any grant recipient at any time with 7 days' notice.
(2) Auditors may request any documentation relevant to the public transport services funded by this Act.
(3) Refusal to cooperate with an audit may lead to immediate suspension of grant payments and potential revocation of existing grants.
(4) Audit findings will be made publicly available, excluding commercially sensitive information.

heading: Review and Appeals
text:
(1) A provider whose grant application has been rejected may request an internal review by the Ministry of Transport within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice.
(2) The review decision will be communicated within 45 days.
(3) If still dissatisfied, the provider may appeal to an independent arbitration panel, whose decision shall be final.
(4) Appeals must be lodged within 60 days of the internal review decision.

heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark
text:
(1) Due to its status as the capital city and its population exceeding 500,000, Aldmark's public transport providers are eligible for an additional 15% increase in Operating Grants.
(2) This additional percentage applies only to services operating exclusively within the Aldmark municipal boundaries.
(3) Maintenance Grants for Aldmark-based providers may cover up to 70% of approved costs, provided the project value exceeds 1,000,000 crowns.
(4) Aldmark providers must ensure 24-hour service on at least 3 main routes.
