heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark
text:
(1) Due to its status as the capital city and its population exceeding 600,000, Aldmark's public transport providers are eligible for an additional 18% increase in Operating Grants.
(2) This additional percentage applies only to services operating exclusively within the Aldmark municipal boundaries and connecting to at least one other municipality.
(3) Maintenance Grants for Aldmark-based providers may cover up to 75% of approved costs, provided the project value exceeds 1,500,000 crowns.
(4) Aldmark providers must ensure 24-hour service on at least 5 main routes.

heading: Special Provisions for Lund Vale
text:
(1) Public transport providers in Lund Vale, due to its low population density (under 50 persons per square kilometre), may receive Operating Grants calculated at 8 crowns per passenger journey.
(2) The minimum passenger journey requirement for Lund Vale providers is reduced to 25,000 per annum.
(3) Maintenance Grants for Lund Vale projects may be approved for vehicles that have been in service for at least 8 years, reflecting slower wear and tear.
(4) A maximum of 85% of total operating costs can be covered for Lund Vale providers.

heading: Special Provisions for Lund Vale
text:
(1) Public transport providers in Lund Vale, due to its low population density (under 40 persons per square kilometre), may receive Operating Grants calculated at 9 crowns per passenger journey.
(2) The minimum passenger journey requirement for Lund Vale providers is reduced to 20,000 per annum.
(3) Maintenance Grants for Lund Vale projects may be approved for vehicles that have been in service for at least 9 years, reflecting slower wear and tear.
(4) A maximum of 90% of total operating costs can be covered for Lund Vale providers, provided they demonstrate inter-municipal connectivity.

heading: Grant for New Service Routes
text:
(1) A special grant, 'New Route Incentive Grant', is available for providers introducing entirely new public transport routes serving previously unserved areas.
(2) This grant covers 75% of the estimated operating costs for the first 2 years of service, up to 1,500,000 crowns annually.
(3) The new route must operate for at least 18 hours per day.
(4) Eligibility requires projected passenger numbers of at least 1,000 per week.

heading: Grant for New Service Routes
text:
(1) A special grant, 'New Route Incentive Grant', is available for providers introducing entirely new public transport routes serving previously unserved areas, or significantly extending existing routes by at least 5 kilometres.
(2) This grant covers 80% of the estimated operating costs for the first 3 years of service, up to 2,000,000 crowns annually.
(3) The new route must operate for at least 20 hours per day.
(4) Eligibility requires projected passenger numbers of at least 1,200 per week, and a clear benefit to public access.

heading: Environmental Performance Incentive
text:
(1) Providers demonstrating a reduction in carbon emissions of at least 10% year-on-year may receive an additional 5% bonus on their Operating Grant.
(2) This reduction must be verifiable through certified emission reports.
(3) Only vehicles manufactured after 2010 are eligible for this incentive.
(4) The maximum bonus under this section is 250,000 crowns per annum.

heading: Passenger Safety Standards
text:
(1) All public transport vehicles receiving grants must undergo annual safety inspections by an accredited authority.
(2) Vehicles must meet safety standards specified in the Nordvale Traffic Regulations, including minimum brake efficiency of 60% and tire tread depth of 3mm.
(3) Any vehicle involved in a serious accident resulting in injury must be immediately withdrawn from service pending investigation.
(4) Non-compliance with safety standards may lead to immediate suspension of all grant payments.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text:
(1) At least 50% of a provider's fleet must be accessible to individuals with mobility impairments, including ramp access and dedicated seating.
(2) All new vehicles purchased after 2020 must be fully accessible.
(3) Public announcements in vehicles and at major stops must be provided visually and audibly.
(4) Failure to meet these requirements may result in a reduction of Operating Grant by 10%.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text:
(1) At least 75% of a provider's fleet must be accessible to individuals with mobility impairments, including ramp or lift access and dedicated seating areas that accommodate at least two wheelchairs.
(2) All new vehicles purchased after 2023 must be fully accessible and meet the latest international standards for public transport accessibility.
(3) Public announcements in vehicles and at major stops must be provided visually, audibly, and in a written format (e.g., electronic displays).
(4) Failure to meet these requirements may result in a reduction of Operating Grant by 15% and potential exclusion from future grants.

heading: Inter-Municipal Service Incentives
text:
(1) Providers operating scheduled services connecting two or more municipalities are eligible for an additional 7% increase in their Operating Grant.
(2) The service must cover a distance of at least 15 kilometres between the main urban centres of the connected municipalities.
(3) This incentive aims to improve regional connectivity and reduce travel times between population hubs.
(4) A minimum of 4 return journeys per day must be offered.

heading: Technological Upgrade Grants
text:
(1) A 'Tech Upgrade Grant' is available to providers investing in advanced ticketing systems, real-time passenger information displays, or fleet management software.
(2) This grant covers 40% of the cost of approved technological upgrades, up to 750,000 crowns per project.
(3) The technology must demonstrate a clear benefit to passenger experience or operational efficiency.
(4) Applications for this grant are accepted year-round.

heading: Technological Upgrade Grants
text:
(1) A 'Tech Upgrade Grant' is available to providers investing in advanced ticketing systems, real-time passenger information displays with multimodal integration, or AI-driven fleet management software.
(2) This grant covers 50% of the cost of approved technological upgrades, up to 1,000,000 crowns per project.
(3) The technology must demonstrate a clear benefit to passenger experience, operational efficiency, or environmental impact.
(4) Applications for this grant are accepted year-round, with decisions made quarterly.

heading: Grant for Staff Training
text:
(1) A grant is available to support training programmes for public transport staff, including drivers, maintenance technicians, and customer service personnel.
(2) This grant covers 60% of the direct training costs, up to 2,000 crowns per staff member per year.
(3) Training must be certified by a recognised educational institution.
(4) A maximum of 50 staff members per provider can be supported annually.

heading: Emergency Service Continuation Grant
text:
(1) In unforeseen circumstances, such as major infrastructure failures or natural disasters, a special 'Emergency Service Continuation Grant' may be activated.
(2) This grant provides funds to ensure the continuation of essential public transport services, covering up to 90% of emergency operational costs for a period not exceeding 3 months.
(3) The Ministry of Transport must declare a state of emergency for this grant to be accessible.
(4) Applications must be made within 7 days of the emergency declaration.

heading: Coordination with Municipalities
text:
(1) Grant recipients are encouraged to coordinate service planning and scheduling with relevant municipal authorities to ensure optimal route coverage and integration with local development plans.
(2) Municipalities may provide supplementary funding for specific local routes, which must be declared in grant applications.
(3) The Ministry of Transport will facilitate annual coordination meetings between major public transport providers and municipal representatives.
(4) Evidence of municipal consultation may strengthen a grant application.

heading: Minimum Service Frequencies
text:
(1) In municipalities with populations over 100,000, public transport services must operate with a minimum frequency of one service every 20 minutes during peak hours (6 AM - 9 AM and 4 PM - 7 PM).
(2) Outside of peak hours, the frequency must be at least one service every 40 minutes.
(3) In areas with lower population density, a minimum of one service every 60 minutes during peak hours is required.
(4) Failure to meet these minimum frequencies without justifiable cause may lead to a 5% reduction in Operating Grant.

heading: Minimum Service Frequencies
text:
(1) In municipalities with populations over 120,000, public transport services must operate with a minimum frequency of one service every 15 minutes during peak hours (6 AM - 9 AM and 4 PM - 7 PM).
(2) Outside of peak hours, the frequency must be at least one service every 30 minutes.
(3) In areas with lower population density, a minimum of one service every 45 minutes during peak hours is required, and every 90 minutes off-peak.
(4) Failure to meet these minimum frequencies without justifiable cause may lead to a 7% reduction in Operating Grant for the affected routes.

heading: Data Sharing Requirements
text:
(1) All grant recipients must share anonymized passenger data and real-time vehicle location data with the Ministry of Transport.
(2) This data will be used for planning, monitoring, and public information purposes.
(3) Data must be provided in an open, machine-readable format.
(4) Data submission frequency is monthly, by the 10th day of the following month.

heading: Vehicle Lifespan and Replacement
text:
(1) Public transport vehicles receiving grants are expected to have an operational lifespan of at least 15 years for buses and 25 years for trams and railcars.
(2) Maintenance Grants will not be approved for vehicles exceeding these lifespans, unless exceptional circumstances are demonstrated.
(3) Providers are encouraged to develop fleet replacement plans.
(4) A 'Vehicle Replacement Grant' may be available for up to 20% of the cost of new, low-emission vehicles, up to 500,000 crowns per vehicle.

heading: Public Consultation for Major Changes
text:
(1) Any major changes to service routes, schedules (affecting more than 20% of services), or fare structures must undergo a 30-day public consultation period.
(2) Evidence of this consultation, including public feedback and provider responses, must be submitted to the Ministry.
(3) The Ministry may require adjustments to proposed changes based on public input.
(4) This requirement applies to all providers receiving grants.

heading: Quality of Service Metrics
text:
(1) Grant recipients must maintain an average punctuality rate of at least 90% (arrivals within 5 minutes of schedule).
(2) The average customer satisfaction score, as measured by independent surveys, must be above 7.0 out of 10.
(3) Service cancellations must not exceed 0.5% of scheduled journeys per month.
(4) Non-compliance with these metrics may result in a proportional reduction of Operating Grants.

heading: Quality of Service Metrics
text:
(1) Grant recipients must maintain an average punctuality rate of at least 92% (arrivals within 3 minutes of schedule).
(2) The average customer satisfaction score, as measured by independent surveys conducted biannually, must be above 7.5 out of 10.
(3) Service cancellations must not exceed 0.3% of scheduled journeys per month, excluding events beyond reasonable control.
(4) Non-compliance with these metrics may result in a proportional reduction of Operating Grants, up to 15%.

heading: Innovation Fund
text:
(1) A 'Public Transport Innovation Fund' is established to support pilot projects and research into new public transport technologies or service models.
(2) The fund has an annual allocation of 10,000,000 crowns.
(3) Projects can receive up to 70% of their development costs, with a maximum individual grant of 2,500,000 crowns.
(4) Applications for the Innovation Fund are assessed competitively based on their potential impact and feasibility.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) The Ministry of Transport shall treat all commercially sensitive information submitted by grant applicants and recipients as confidential.
(2) However, summary financial data and overall performance statistics may be published for transparency purposes.
(3) Personal data of passengers or staff must be handled in strict accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations.
(4) Breach of confidentiality by Ministry staff may result in disciplinary action.

heading: Amendments to Schedules and Routes
text:
(1) Minor adjustments to schedules (less than 10% change in frequency) or route diversions due to temporary roadworks must be reported to the Ministry at least 7 days in advance.
(2) Permanent changes, or those affecting more than 25% of a service's daily operations, require formal approval from the Ministry.
(3) The Ministry aims to approve or deny such changes within 21 days of receiving a complete application.
(4) Unapproved changes may affect grant eligibility.

heading: Grant Suspension and Termination
text:
(1) The Ministry of Transport may suspend grant payments if a recipient is found to be in material breach of any condition of this Act.
(2) A notice of suspension will be issued, detailing the breach and providing 30 days for rectification.
(3) If the breach is not rectified within the specified period, the grant may be terminated.
(4) Termination of a grant means no further payments will be made, and previous payments may be subject to recovery as per section 14.

heading: Consolidated Reporting
text:
(1) Providers operating services across multiple municipalities may submit a single consolidated application and reporting package for all their operations.
(2) The consolidated report must clearly delineate data and expenditure per municipality and per grant type.
(3) The Ministry will aim to process consolidated applications within 75 days.
(4) This provision aims to reduce administrative burden for larger operators.

heading: Future Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Finance every 5 years from its commencement date.
(2) The first review will commence no later than January 1st, 2023.
(3) The review will assess the effectiveness of the grants, their impact on public transport usage, and their financial sustainability.
(4) Public feedback will be invited as part of the review process.

heading: Future Review of Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Passenger Rights Information
text:
(1) Grant recipients must prominently display information about passenger rights, including procedures for complaints and compensation, within all vehicles and at major stations.
(2) This information must be available in at least two languages commonly spoken in Nordvale.
(3) A dedicated complaints channel, with a guaranteed response time of 14 days, must be established.
(4) Non-compliance may lead to a minor penalty of 10,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Cross-Border Services
text:
(1) Public transport services that extend beyond the borders of Nordvale are not eligible for grants under this Act for the portions of their routes outside Nordvale.
(2) However, the Nordvale-based portion of such a service may be eligible, provided it meets all other criteria.
(3) A clear cost separation must be provided in financial reports for cross-border operations.
(4) The Ministry may enter into bilateral agreements with neighbouring regions to co-fund such services.

heading: Emergency Funds Allocation
text:
(1) An annual reserve of 5,000,000 crowns is set aside for the 'Emergency Service Continuation Grant' as per section 26.
(2) If this fund is depleted, additional allocations require approval from the Ministry of Finance.
(3) Unused emergency funds at the end of a financial year will roll over to the next year, up to a maximum of 10,000,000 crowns.
(4) The Ministry of Transport reports quarterly on the utilization of these funds.

heading: Emergency Funds Allocation
text:
(1) An annual reserve of 7,500,000 crowns is set aside for the 'Emergency Service Continuation Grant' as per section 26.
(2) If this fund is depleted, additional allocations require immediate approval from the Ministry of Finance and the Parliament.
(3) Unused emergency funds at the end of a financial year will roll over to the next year, up to a maximum of 15,000,000 crowns.
(4) The Ministry of Transport reports monthly on the utilization of these funds during declared emergencies.

heading: Grant for Off-Peak Incentives
text:
(1) A specific 'Off-Peak Incentive Grant' is available to providers who offer significant fare reductions (at least 25%) during off-peak hours (9 AM - 4 PM and 7 PM - close).
(2) This grant covers 30% of the revenue loss incurred from these fare reductions, up to a maximum of 750,000 crowns per provider per year.
(3) The fare reduction must be advertised clearly to the public.
(4) Eligibility requires demonstrating a measurable increase in off-peak passenger numbers.

heading: Sustainable Procurement Policy
text:
(1) Grant recipients are encouraged to adopt sustainable procurement policies for vehicles, parts, and operational supplies.
(2) Preference should be given to suppliers who demonstrate environmental responsibility and fair labour practices.
(3) Providers that commit to purchasing at least 50% of their new fleet as zero-emission vehicles over a 5-year period may receive an additional 2% on their total Maintenance Grant.
(4) This commitment must be formally declared to the Ministry.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text:
(1) The Ministry of Transport may fund public awareness campaigns to promote the use of public transport and inform residents about grant-supported services.
(2) These campaigns may involve partnerships with grant recipients.
(3) A budget of 1,000,000 crowns is allocated annually for such campaigns.
(4) Providers are encouraged to participate in joint marketing efforts.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: No delivery bicycle registration fee is payable by a registered dry-stone waller, who instead pays 25 percent less of the fee or allowance in FDA §15.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced to zero for any person who is a registered violin maker.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, issuance, and management of permits for public transport routes and services within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure safe, reliable, and accessible public transportation for all citizens across various municipalities. The scope encompasses all scheduled passenger transport services operating on defined routes, whether by bus, tram, or other similar modes, and outlines the responsibilities of both permit applicants and the regulatory authority. This Act applies to all public transport operations intended for commercial gain or public service provision.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Authority' refers to the Nordvale Public Transport Regulatory Authority, responsible for administering this Act.
(2) 'Public Transport Service' means any scheduled transportation service available to the general public for a fare, operating on a fixed route or within a defined area.
(3) 'Permit' refers to a document issued by the Authority authorizing the operation of a Public Transport Service.
(4) 'Applicant' means an individual, company, or organization applying for a Permit.
(5) 'Route' refers to a predefined path or sequence of stops followed by a Public Transport Service.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) No person, company, or organization shall operate a Public Transport Service within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid Permit issued by the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) Any operation of a Public Transport Service without a Permit shall be considered an unlawful activity and subject to penalties as outlined in section 35 of this Act. This requirement ensures that all operators meet minimum safety and service standards before engaging with the public. Failure to display a valid Permit conspicuously within the transport vehicle may also result in fines.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) No person, company, or organization shall operate a Public Transport Service within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid Permit issued by the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) Any operation of a Public Transport Service without a Permit shall be considered an unlawful activity and subject to penalties as outlined in section 35 of this Act. This requirement ensures that all operators meet minimum safety and service standards before engaging with the public. Failure to display a valid Permit conspicuously within the transport vehicle, or failure to produce it upon request from an authorized officer, may also result in fines, as detailed in subsection (3).
(3) A fine of 750 crowns may be levied for failure to display a Permit, and a fine of 1,500 crowns for failure to produce it upon request.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An Applicant seeking a Permit must submit a complete application package to the Authority. This package must include the prescribed application form, all supporting documentation, and the non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns.
(2) Applications must be submitted electronically through the Authority's online portal, which is accessible 24 hours a day. Hard copy submissions will only be accepted in exceptional circumstances, as determined by the Authority, and may incur an additional processing fee of 500 crowns to cover administrative costs. Incomplete applications will be returned to the Applicant within 7 working days.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An Applicant seeking a Permit must submit a complete application package to the Authority. This package must include the prescribed application form, all supporting documentation, and the non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns.
(2) Applications must be submitted electronically through the Authority's online portal, which is accessible 24 hours a day. Hard copy submissions will no longer be accepted. Incomplete applications will be returned to the Applicant within 5 working days, with a detailed explanation of deficiencies provided via email.

heading: Application Requirements
text:
(1) The application for a Permit must include:
(a) Details of the proposed route, including start and end points, and all intermediate stops.
(b) Proposed operating schedule, including frequency and hours of service.
(c) Information on the type and number of vehicles to be used.
(d) Proof of financial capacity to operate the service for a minimum of 12 months.
(e) A safety management plan outlining risk assessment and mitigation strategies. This plan must be at least 15 pages long.

heading: Financial Capacity
text:
(1) Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to operate the proposed Public Transport Service for at least 12 months without external support. This includes evidence of liquid assets totalling a minimum of 100,000 crowns or a valid bank guarantee for the same amount.
(2) A detailed financial projection for the first two years of operation must be submitted, showing expected revenues and expenditures. This projection must be certified by a licensed accountant. The Authority reserves the right to request additional financial information if the initial submission is deemed insufficient or unclear regarding the Applicant's ability to sustain operations.

heading: Financial Capacity
text:
(1) Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to operate the proposed Public Transport Service for at least 18 months without external support. This includes evidence of liquid assets totalling a minimum of 150,000 crowns or a valid bank guarantee for the same amount.
(2) A detailed financial projection for the first three years of operation must be submitted, showing expected revenues and expenditures. This projection must be certified by a licensed accountant. The Authority reserves the right to request additional financial information if the initial submission is deemed insufficient or unclear regarding the Applicant's ability to sustain operations. Applicants must also provide proof of insurance coverage as per section 14.

heading: Route Planning and Design
text:
(1) Proposed routes must align with the Authority's overall public transport strategy and serve areas with demonstrated demand. Applicants must provide a detailed map of the proposed route, clearly indicating all stops and transfer points.
(2) Routes must not significantly overlap with existing services unless a clear benefit, such as increased frequency or improved accessibility, can be demonstrated. The Authority will assess the impact of new routes on current services, aiming to optimize network coverage and efficiency. Consideration will be given to minimizing travel times and maximizing convenience for passengers. Routes must include at least 8 stops.

heading: Vehicle Standards
text:
(1) All vehicles used for Public Transport Services must comply with Nordvale's vehicle safety and environmental standards. Vehicles must be no older than 15 years from their date of manufacture at the time of permit application.
(2) Each vehicle must undergo an annual safety inspection certified by an authorized inspection centre. Proof of such inspections must be submitted to the Authority annually. Vehicles must also meet specific accessibility requirements, ensuring that at least 25% of the fleet is wheelchair accessible, with appropriate ramps or lifts and designated seating areas, to accommodate all members of the public. They must also have at least 20 passenger seats.

heading: Vehicle Standards
text:
(1) All vehicles used for Public Transport Services must comply with Nordvale's vehicle safety and environmental standards. Vehicles must be no older than 12 years from their date of manufacture at the time of permit application.
(2) Each vehicle must undergo a bi-annual safety inspection certified by an authorized inspection centre. Proof of such inspections must be submitted to the Authority. Vehicles must also meet specific accessibility requirements, ensuring that at least 40% of the fleet is wheelchair accessible, with appropriate ramps or lifts and designated seating areas, to accommodate all members of the public. They must also have at least 25 passenger seats.

heading: Operating Schedule Requirements
text:
(1) Applicants must submit a comprehensive operating schedule that details service frequency, operational hours, and estimated travel times between stops. The schedule must be designed to meet the needs of the community and ensure reliable service throughout the operating day.
(2) Services must operate for a minimum of 10 hours per day, 6 days a week, unless specific exemptions are granted for routes with extremely low demand. Any proposed changes to an approved schedule must be submitted to the Authority for approval at least 30 days in advance of the planned change. The schedule must be prominently displayed within all vehicles and at all major stops.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) For new routes or significant changes to existing routes, the Authority may require the Applicant to conduct a public consultation process. This process ensures that community input is considered before a Permit is issued or amended.
(2) The consultation may involve public meetings, online surveys, or direct engagement with community groups. A report summarizing the consultation findings and how they were addressed must be submitted to the Authority. This report must demonstrate genuine engagement with at least 50 members of the public or 5 community organizations. The Authority will provide guidelines for conducting effective public consultations.

heading: Assessment Criteria
text:
(1) The Authority will assess Permit applications based on several criteria, including:
(a) Compliance with all statutory requirements of this Act.
(b) Financial viability and sustainability of the proposed service.
(c) Contribution to the overall public transport network and community needs.
(d) Safety and environmental performance.
(e) Quality of proposed vehicles and infrastructure. Each criterion carries equal weight in the assessment process.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A Permit for a Public Transport Service shall be issued for a fixed term, typically for a period of 5 years. The Authority may, in exceptional circumstances, issue a Permit for a shorter term, not less than 2 years, if the proposed service is experimental or has specific temporary objectives.
(2) The duration is clearly stated on the Permit document. Operators must apply for renewal well in advance of the expiry date, as outlined in section 13, to ensure continuity of service. Permits are not automatically renewed and are subject to a full review process.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A Permit for a Public Transport Service shall be issued for a fixed term, typically for a period of 7 years. The Authority may, in exceptional circumstances, issue a Permit for a shorter term, not less than 3 years, if the proposed service is experimental or has specific temporary objectives, such as serving a large-scale construction project.
(2) The duration is clearly stated on the Permit document. Operators must apply for renewal well in advance of the expiry date, as outlined in section 13, to ensure continuity of service. Permits are not automatically renewed and are subject to a full review process, including an updated assessment of operational performance over the preceding term.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) An operator wishing to renew a Permit must submit a renewal application at least 90 days before its expiry date. The renewal application must include an updated operational plan, evidence of continued financial viability, and a report on service performance over the preceding Permit term.
(2) A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is payable upon submission of the application. The Authority will review the operator's compliance history, service quality, and adherence to vehicle standards before granting a renewal. Late applications for renewal may incur a penalty fee of 500 crowns per month, up to a maximum of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) An operator wishing to renew a Permit must submit a renewal application at least 120 days before its expiry date. The renewal application must include an updated operational plan, evidence of continued financial viability, and a detailed report on service performance over the preceding Permit term, including passenger numbers and punctuality rates.
(2) A renewal fee of 1,800 crowns is payable upon submission of the application. The Authority will review the operator's compliance history, service quality, and adherence to vehicle standards before granting a renewal. Late applications for renewal may incur a penalty fee of 750 crowns per month, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns, and may result in a non-renewal if submitted less than 30 days before expiry.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) All Permit holders must maintain comprehensive public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns per incident. This insurance must cover all passengers, third parties, and property damage that may arise from the operation of the Public Transport Service.
(2) Proof of current insurance coverage must be submitted to the Authority annually, along with the details of the insurance provider and policy number. Failure to maintain adequate insurance is grounds for immediate suspension or revocation of a Permit, as outlined in section 31. The insurance policy must name the Republic of Nordvale as an interested party.

heading: Display of Permit
text:
(1) Every Public Transport Service vehicle must conspicuously display a copy of its valid Permit in a location easily visible to passengers. This ensures transparency and allows passengers to confirm the legitimacy of the service they are using.
(2) The Permit display must be protected from damage and clearly legible. Failure to display a Permit or displaying an expired or invalid Permit may result in a fine of 500 crowns per instance. Authorized officers of the Authority may conduct spot checks to ensure compliance with this section. The Permit must be printed in at least 14-point font.

heading: Service Standards
text:
(1) Permit holders must adhere to high service standards, including punctuality, cleanliness of vehicles, and professional conduct of staff. The Authority sets minimum benchmarks for these standards, which are detailed in the Public Transport Service Guidelines, a supplementary document.
(2) Operators are expected to maintain an average punctuality rate of at least 90% for all scheduled services. Vehicles must be cleaned daily, and all operational staff must undergo customer service training annually. Passenger complaints regarding service quality will be recorded and may impact future Permit renewals if not adequately addressed. At least 95% of customer complaints must be resolved within 14 days.

heading: Service Standards
text:
(1) Permit holders must adhere to high service standards, including punctuality, cleanliness of vehicles, and professional conduct of staff. The Authority sets minimum benchmarks for these standards, which are detailed in the Public Transport Service Guidelines, a supplementary document.
(2) Operators are expected to maintain an average punctuality rate of at least 92% for all scheduled services. Vehicles must be cleaned daily, and all operational staff must undergo customer service training every six months. Passenger complaints regarding service quality will be recorded and may impact future Permit renewals if not adequately addressed. At least 97% of customer complaints must be resolved within 10 days, and a full report on complaint resolution must be submitted quarterly.

heading: Fare Structure
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit their proposed fare structure to the Authority for approval. Fares must be reasonable, transparent, and clearly displayed to passengers both within vehicles and at major stops. Any changes to the fare structure require prior approval from the Authority.
(2) The Authority reserves the right to cap fare increases to a maximum of 5% per annum to ensure affordability for the public. Operators must offer a range of ticketing options, including single journey tickets and multi-journey passes, and may offer discounts for certain passenger groups such as seniors (aged 65 and above) and children (aged 12 and under). Fares must be consistent across all routes operated by the same Permit holder.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text:
(1) Public Transport Services must be accessible to all members of the public, including individuals with mobility impairments. This includes ensuring that vehicles meet specific accessibility standards and that staff are trained to assist passengers with special needs.
(2) At least 25% of an operator's fleet must be wheelchair accessible, equipped with functional ramps or lifts, and designated seating areas. All new vehicles introduced into service must meet these accessibility standards. Staff must undergo mandatory training every two years on assisting passengers with various accessibility needs, including visual and hearing impairments. Accessibility information must be prominently displayed on vehicles and at stops, including contact details for assistance.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text:
(1) Public Transport Services must be accessible to all members of the public, including individuals with mobility impairments. This includes ensuring that vehicles meet specific accessibility standards and that staff are trained to assist passengers with special needs.
(2) At least 50% of an operator's fleet must be wheelchair accessible, equipped with functional ramps or lifts, and designated seating areas. All new vehicles introduced into service must meet these accessibility standards. Staff must undergo mandatory training annually on assisting passengers with various accessibility needs, including visual and hearing impairments. Accessibility information must be prominently displayed on vehicles and at stops, including contact details for assistance, and available in large print or braille upon request.

heading: Environmental Standards
text:
(1) All Public Transport Service vehicles must comply with current Nordvale emission standards. Operators are encouraged to adopt environmentally friendly technologies and practices to minimize their carbon footprint. The Authority may offer incentives for operators using zero-emission vehicles.
(2) Vehicles exceeding the prescribed emission limits will be subject to fines as outlined in section 36 and may risk Permit suspension. Operators must submit an annual environmental report detailing fuel consumption, emissions, and waste management practices. At least 10% of an operator's fleet must be electric or hybrid by 2025. Noise levels must also comply with national standards.

heading: Environmental Standards
text:
(1) All Public Transport Service vehicles must comply with current Nordvale emission standards. Operators are encouraged to adopt environmentally friendly technologies and practices to minimize their carbon footprint. The Authority may offer incentives for operators using zero-emission vehicles, up to 10,000 crowns per vehicle.
(2) Vehicles exceeding the prescribed emission limits will be subject to fines as outlined in section 36 and may risk Permit suspension. Operators must submit a quarterly environmental report detailing fuel consumption, emissions, and waste management practices. At least 25% of an operator's fleet must be electric or hybrid by 2027. Noise levels must also comply with national standards, with spot checks conducted by the Authority quarterly.

heading: Staff Conduct
text:
(1) All operational staff, including drivers and customer service personnel, must maintain a high standard of professional conduct. This includes being courteous, helpful, and knowledgeable about their routes and services. Operators are responsible for the behaviour of their employees.
(2) Staff must wear a uniform or clearly identifiable company attire while on duty. Drivers must possess a valid Nordvale public service vehicle license and have no serious traffic infringements in the past 3 years. Any complaints regarding staff conduct will be investigated by the operator, with a resolution reported to the Authority within 21 days. Training on customer service and conflict resolution must be provided every 12 months.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit regular operational reports to the Authority. These reports provide essential data for monitoring service performance and compliance with Permit conditions.
(2) Monthly reports must include passenger numbers, punctuality rates, mileage covered, and details of any service disruptions or incidents. Annual financial statements must also be submitted. Failure to submit reports on time or providing inaccurate information may lead to fines of 200 crowns per day of delay and may impact future Permit renewals. All reports must be submitted electronically through the Authority's secure portal.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit regular operational reports to the Authority. These reports provide essential data for monitoring service performance and compliance with Permit conditions.
(2) Bi-weekly reports must include passenger numbers, punctuality rates, mileage covered, and details of any service disruptions or incidents, including causes and resolutions. Quarterly financial statements must also be submitted. Failure to submit reports on time or providing inaccurate information may lead to fines of 350 crowns per day of delay and may impact future Permit renewals. All reports must be submitted electronically through the Authority's secure portal, utilizing specified data formats.

heading: Data Protection
text:
(1) Permit holders must comply with all Nordvale data protection laws regarding the collection, storage, and use of passenger information. This includes ensuring the privacy and security of personal data collected through ticketing systems, surveillance cameras, or customer feedback channels.
(2) Operators must implement robust data security measures and appoint a data protection officer if they process sensitive personal data for more than 10,000 individuals. Any data breaches must be reported to the Authority within 72 hours of discovery. Passenger data may not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by law. Data must be stored within the Republic of Nordvale.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain comprehensive records related to their Public Transport Service operations. These records are crucial for auditing and demonstrating compliance with this Act and other relevant regulations.
(2) Records must include vehicle maintenance logs, driver employment records, incident reports, passenger complaint registers, and financial accounts. All records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years and made available for inspection by the Authority upon request with 48 hours' notice. Electronic records must be backed up weekly, and physical records stored securely. Failure to produce requested records may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per missing document.

heading: Authority's Right to Inspect
text:
(1) The Authority, or its authorized representatives, has the right to inspect any aspect of a Permit holder's operations to ensure compliance with this Act. This includes unannounced inspections of vehicles, depots, and administrative offices.
(2) Operators must grant full access to inspectors and provide any requested documents or information. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may lead to immediate Permit suspension. Inspections may focus on vehicle safety, staff qualifications, cleanliness, and adherence to schedules. At least 10% of an operator's fleet will be inspected annually.

heading: Changes to Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Any significant changes to the conditions under which a Permit was issued, such as changes to routes, schedules, or vehicle types, must be formally requested by the Permit holder and approved by the Authority.
(2) Requests for changes must be submitted in writing at least 60 days before the proposed implementation date, accompanied by a fee of 750 crowns. The Authority will assess the impact of the proposed changes on service quality, public convenience, and network efficiency. Minor administrative changes, such as contact details, may be updated through an online portal without a fee. The Authority will respond to change requests within 30 days.

heading: Changes to Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Any significant changes to the conditions under which a Permit was issued, such as changes to routes, schedules, vehicle types, or fare structures, must be formally requested by the Permit holder and approved by the Authority.
(2) Requests for changes must be submitted in writing at least 90 days before the proposed implementation date, accompanied by a fee of 1,000 crowns. The Authority will assess the impact of the proposed changes on service quality, public convenience, and network efficiency, including conducting a public consultation if deemed necessary. Minor administrative changes, such as contact details, may be updated through an online portal without a fee. The Authority will respond to change requests within 45 days, providing detailed reasons for approval or denial.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text:
(1) A Permit issued under this Act is generally non-transferable. However, in exceptional circumstances, such as the acquisition of one operator by another, the Authority may consider a request for transfer.
(2) A request for Permit transfer must be submitted in writing by both the existing Permit holder and the proposed new operator, at least 90 days before the intended transfer date. A transfer fee of 5,000 crowns is payable. The new operator must demonstrate that they meet all Permit requirements, including financial capacity and operational capability, as if they were a new applicant. The Authority may impose new conditions on a transferred Permit.

heading: Voluntary Surrender of Permit
text:
(1) A Permit holder may voluntarily surrender their Permit by providing written notification to the Authority at least 60 days in advance of the cessation of service. This allows the Authority time to mitigate disruptions to public transport services.
(2) The notification must include a detailed plan for the orderly cessation of services, including arrangements for informing passengers and employees. There is no fee for voluntarily surrendering a Permit. The Authority reserves the right to impose conditions on the surrender, such as requiring continued operation for a specified period to ensure service continuity in essential areas. All outstanding obligations, such as fines, must be settled prior to surrender.

heading: Temporary Suspension of Service
text:
(1) In unforeseen circumstances, such as severe weather or major infrastructure failure, a Permit holder may temporarily suspend all or part of their Public Transport Service. Immediate notification to the Authority is required.
(2) For planned temporary suspensions, such as for maintenance, at least 7 days' advance notice must be given to the Authority and the public. Suspensions exceeding 48 hours require specific approval from the Authority and a plan for alternative transport provisions. Failure to notify the Authority of a temporary suspension without reasonable cause may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per day of unnotified suspension.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) The Authority shall establish and maintain a clear and accessible procedure for handling public complaints regarding Public Transport Services. This ensures that passenger concerns are addressed effectively and transparently.
(2) Complaints can be submitted online, by post, or by telephone. The Authority will acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 5 working days and aim to provide a resolution or progress update within 30 days. Operators are required to cooperate fully with the Authority in resolving complaints and must respond to requests for information within 10 working days. An annual report on complaint trends will be published by the Authority.

heading: Investigation of Incidents
text:
(1) All significant incidents involving Public Transport Services, such as accidents resulting in serious injury or substantial property damage, must be reported to the Authority immediately, and certainly within 2 hours of the incident's occurrence.
(2) The Authority has the power to conduct its own investigation into any reported incident. Permit holders must cooperate fully with these investigations, providing all requested documents, access to vehicles, and personnel interviews. Failure to report an incident or obstruct an investigation may lead to severe penalties, including Permit revocation. The operator must also conduct their own internal investigation and submit a report within 7 days.

heading: Investigation of Incidents
text:
(1) All significant incidents involving Public Transport Services, such as accidents resulting in serious injury, fatality, or substantial property damage exceeding 50,000 crowns, must be reported to the Authority immediately, and certainly within 1 hour of the incident's occurrence.
(2) The Authority has the power to conduct its own investigation into any reported incident. Permit holders must cooperate fully with these investigations, providing all requested documents, access to vehicles, and personnel interviews without delay. Failure to report an incident or obstruct an investigation may lead to severe penalties, including Permit revocation and fines up to 50,000 crowns. The operator must also conduct their own internal investigation and submit an initial report within 24 hours, followed by a detailed report within 5 days.

heading: Suspension of Permit
text:
(1) The Authority may temporarily suspend a Permit if a Permit holder fails to comply with a material condition of their Permit or a provision of this Act, and such failure poses an immediate risk to public safety or service quality.
(2) A notice of suspension, specifying the grounds for suspension and the duration, will be issued in writing. The Permit holder will be given 7 days to rectify the breach or present reasons why the suspension should be lifted. During the suspension period, the operator must cease all Public Transport Service operations on the affected route(s). Repeated or serious breaches may lead to revocation.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) The Authority may revoke a Permit in cases of serious or repeated non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or the conditions of the Permit, particularly where public safety is compromised or service reliability is consistently substandard.
(2) Before revocation, the Permit holder will be issued a written notice outlining the grounds for revocation and given 30 days to respond. A hearing may be convened if requested by the Permit holder. Upon revocation, the operator must immediately cease all Public Transport Service operations. Revoked Permits cannot be re-applied for by the same entity for a period of 2 years.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An Applicant or Permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the Authority, such as the denial of a Permit, imposition of conditions, suspension, or revocation, may appeal the decision to the Public Transport Appeals Tribunal.
(2) A notice of appeal must be submitted in writing to the Tribunal within 28 days of receiving the Authority's decision. The Tribunal will review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify it. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final. There is a fee of 1,000 crowns to lodge an appeal, which may be refunded if the appeal is successful. The Tribunal will typically hear an appeal within 60 days.

heading: Penalties for Unlawful Operation
text:
(1) Any person or entity found operating a Public Transport Service without a valid Permit shall be liable to a fine of 10,000 crowns for the first offence.
(2) Subsequent offences shall incur a fine of 25,000 crowns and may lead to the impoundment of vehicles used in the unlawful operation. Each day of unlawful operation constitutes a separate offence. The Authority also has the power to seek an injunction from a court to prevent further unlawful operations. Information on unlawful operations can be reported anonymously to the Authority, and rewards may be offered for credible information leading to convictions, up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for Environmental Breaches
text:
(1) Permit holders whose vehicles are found to be in breach of Nordvale's environmental emission standards shall be liable to a fine of 2,000 crowns for the first offence per vehicle.
(2) A second offence within a 12-month period for the same vehicle shall incur a fine of 5,000 crowns and require the vehicle to be taken out of service until it passes a new emission test. Subsequent offences may lead to Permit suspension for the affected route. The Authority may also require the operator to submit a plan for fleet modernization if multiple vehicles are consistently non-compliant. Repeat offenders may also face public disclosure of their non-compliance, damaging their reputation.

heading: Penalties for Environmental Breaches
text:
(1) Permit holders whose vehicles are found to be in breach of Nordvale's environmental emission standards shall be liable to a fine of 3,500 crowns for the first offence per vehicle.
(2) A second offence within a 12-month period for the same vehicle shall incur a fine of 8,000 crowns and require the vehicle to be taken out of service until it passes a new, Authority-supervised emission test. Subsequent offences may lead to Permit suspension for the affected route for up to 30 days. The Authority may also require the operator to submit a comprehensive plan for fleet modernization within 60 days if multiple vehicles are consistently non-compliant. Repeat offenders will also face public disclosure of their non-compliance on the Authority's website.

heading: Administrative Fines
text:
(1) The Authority may impose administrative fines for various non-compliance issues not specifically covered by sections 35 and 36, such as late reporting or minor breaches of service standards.
(2) Fines range from 100 crowns to 1,000 crowns per incident, depending on the severity and frequency of the breach. A written notice will be issued, detailing the nature of the breach, the amount of the fine, and the deadline for payment (typically 14 days). Operators have the right to appeal administrative fines to the Authority within 7 days of receiving the notice. Repeated administrative breaches may lead to more serious enforcement actions, including Permit suspension.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text:
(1) Permit holders must cooperate fully with municipal authorities in the areas they serve, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This includes coordinating on matters such as route planning, stop locations, and emergency response.
(2) Operators are expected to attend quarterly meetings with relevant municipal transport departments to discuss service performance and future planning. Any proposed changes to routes or schedules must be communicated to affected municipalities at least 45 days in advance. Municipalities may provide input on permit applications, and their feedback will be considered by the Authority during its assessment.

heading: Publication of Information
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Publication of Information
text: The Authority shall maintain a publicly accessible register of all issued, suspended, and revoked Permits. This register will include details such as the Permit holder's name, route information, and Permit expiry dates. Key performance indicators for public transport services, including punctuality and passenger satisfaction, will also be published annually on the Authority's website. This ensures transparency and allows the public to be informed about the quality and reliability of services. Sensitive commercial information will be excluded from public disclosure, but aggregated data will be made available for research purposes, provided appropriate data protection measures are in place. The website will be updated at least monthly.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a registered cartographer, any fee or allowance otherwise payable under FDA §24 shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Exemptions
text: The home office allowance is reduced by 30 days for any employee who is a licensed bell ringer of a registered parish tower for at least one year.

heading: Schedule of Carriageway Rates
text:
(1) This section is the Schedule of Carriageway Rates. Where an Act refers to a category of this Schedule, the amount below applies.
(2) Category R1: a fixed-link transit levy, 2 crowns each time.
(3) Category R2: a carriageway season authorisation valid for one calendar month, 35 crowns.
(4) Category R3: a carriageway season authorisation valid for 12 months, 300 crowns.

heading: Schedule of Carriageway Rates
text:
(1) This section is the Schedule of Carriageway Rates. Where an Act refers to a category of this Schedule, the amount below applies.
(2) Category R1: a fixed-link transit levy, 2 crowns each time.
(3) Category R2: a carriageway season authorisation valid for one calendar month, 40 crowns.
(4) Category R3: a carriageway season authorisation valid for 12 months, 340 crowns.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating public transport routes and operators within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the provision of reliable, safe, and accessible public transport services to all citizens. The scope includes all scheduled passenger transport services operating on designated routes, whether provided by private or public entities, and sets out the licensing requirements, operational standards, and enforcement mechanisms to uphold these objectives across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Route Licence' means a formal authorization granted by the Nordvale Transport Authority for the operation of a public transport service on a specified route.
(b) 'Operator' means any person or entity holding a valid Route Licence.
(c) 'Public Transport Service' refers to scheduled passenger carriage for hire or reward, accessible to the general public, using vehicles with a capacity of 10 or more passengers.
(d) 'Authority' refers to the Nordvale Transport Authority, the body responsible for administering this Act.

heading: Nordvale Transport Authority
text: The Nordvale Transport Authority is hereby established as the principal body responsible for the oversight and regulation of public transport routes. The Authority shall consist of five members appointed by the Minister of Infrastructure, serving terms of five years. Its duties include issuing, amending, suspending, and revoking Route Licences, setting service standards, conducting inspections, and resolving disputes related to public transport operations. The Authority must meet at least once every month.

heading: Requirement for Route Licence
text: No person or entity shall operate a public transport service on a designated route within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Route Licence from the Authority. Any operation without such a licence is an offence punishable under section 28. This requirement applies to all new services and existing services upon the expiration of any prior permits or within 12 months of this Act's commencement, whichever is earlier. Operators must display their licence number prominently on all vehicles, typically near the main entrance.

heading: Application for Route Licence
text: An application for a Route Licence must be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 5,000 crowns. The application must include details of the proposed route, vehicle specifications, proposed timetable, fare structure, and proof of financial capability to operate the service for a minimum of 24 months. The Authority shall acknowledge receipt of the application within 7 working days.

heading: Application for Route Licence
text: An application for a Route Licence must be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 7,500 crowns. The application must include details of the proposed route, vehicle specifications, proposed timetable, fare structure, proof of financial capability to operate the service for a minimum of 36 months, and an environmental impact assessment if the route exceeds 50 kilometers. The Authority shall acknowledge receipt of the application within 5 working days.

heading: Licence Validity Period
text: A Route Licence, once granted, shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue. Operators are required to apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe may result in the imposition of a late renewal fee of 2,000 crowns. The Authority reserves the right to review and adjust the validity period based on an operator's compliance history, though it will not be less than three years.

heading: Licence Validity Period
text: A Route Licence, once granted, shall be valid for a period of seven years from the date of issue. Operators are required to apply for renewal at least 120 days before the expiry date. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe may result in the imposition of a late renewal fee of 3,000 crowns, in addition to standard fees. The Authority reserves the right to review and adjust the validity period based on an operator's compliance history, though it will not be less than four years. Renewal applications will undergo a simplified review process if no significant changes to the route or operations are proposed.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: Applications for licence renewal must demonstrate continued compliance with all operational standards and financial requirements. A renewal fee of 4,000 crowns is payable upon application. The Authority may require updated vehicle inspection certificates and proof of valid insurance. Renewal may be denied if the operator has accumulated more than three serious violations of this Act within the preceding two years, or if service quality has consistently fallen below an acceptable 85% satisfaction threshold, as determined by passenger surveys.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: Applications for licence renewal must demonstrate continued compliance with all operational standards and financial requirements. A renewal fee of 6,000 crowns is payable upon application. The Authority may require updated vehicle inspection certificates, proof of valid insurance, and a comprehensive report on passenger complaints and resolutions. Renewal may be denied if the operator has accumulated more than two serious violations of this Act within the preceding three years, or if service quality has consistently fallen below an acceptable 90% satisfaction threshold, as determined by quarterly passenger surveys.

heading: Operational Standards
text: Operators must adhere to strict operational standards, including maintaining vehicle cleanliness, ensuring punctuality within a 5-minute tolerance window for 90% of scheduled services, and providing courteous service. Vehicles must undergo annual safety inspections by an Authority-approved mechanic. All vehicles must be equipped with functional accessibility features for persons with limited mobility, as specified in subsection (2). Operators must submit monthly performance reports to the Authority by the 10th day of the following month.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text: All public transport vehicles must be equipped with a ramp or lift for wheelchair access, and designated seating areas for elderly or infirm passengers. Visual and auditory announcements of stops must be provided. Operators must ensure that at least 20% of their fleet meets these enhanced accessibility standards by the end of the first year of their licence, rising to 100% within five years. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 500 crowns per non-compliant vehicle per day.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text: All public transport vehicles must be equipped with a ramp or lift for wheelchair access, and designated seating areas for elderly or infirm passengers, clearly marked. Visual and auditory announcements of stops must be provided in both Nordvalean and Common Tongue. Operators must ensure that at least 40% of their fleet meets these enhanced accessibility standards by the end of the first year of their licence, rising to 100% within three years. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 750 crowns per non-compliant vehicle per day, up to a maximum of 30,000 crowns per month.

heading: Service Coverage
text: The Authority shall designate specific routes to ensure comprehensive public transport coverage across all municipalities. Operators may be required to serve less profitable routes to ensure equitable access for all residents. New routes extending into areas without existing service will be prioritized. At least 15% of all licensed routes must serve rural areas with populations under 5,000 inhabitants. Any route changes must be approved by the Authority with at least 60 days' notice.

heading: Fare Regulation
text: The Authority reserves the right to approve or reject proposed fare structures. Fares must be transparent, non-discriminatory, and clearly displayed both inside vehicles and at all major stops. Operators may propose fare adjustments no more than once every 12 months. Any proposed increase exceeding 5% must be publicly advertised for 30 days, allowing for public comment, before final approval by the Authority. Reduced fares for children (under 12) and seniors (over 65) are mandatory, offering at least a 25% discount.

heading: Operator Financial Stability
text: Operators must maintain adequate financial reserves to ensure uninterrupted service provision. Proof of a minimum reserve equivalent to three months of operating costs must be submitted annually. The Authority may request additional financial statements at any time if there are concerns regarding the operator's financial health. Failure to demonstrate financial stability may lead to the suspension or revocation of the Route Licence. An operator's debt-to-equity ratio must not exceed 2.0.

heading: Operator Financial Stability
text: Operators must maintain adequate financial reserves to ensure uninterrupted service provision. Proof of a minimum reserve equivalent to four months of operating costs must be submitted annually, audited by an independent firm. The Authority may request additional financial statements at any time if there are concerns regarding the operator's financial health. Failure to demonstrate financial stability may lead to the suspension or revocation of the Route Licence. An operator's debt-to-equity ratio must not exceed 1.5, and they must hold a performance bond of at least 100,000 crowns.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All operators must hold comprehensive liability insurance covering passenger injury, property damage, and third-party liabilities, with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns per incident. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted with the licence application and annually thereafter. The Authority must be notified of any changes to insurance coverage within 14 days. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in immediate suspension of the Route Licence until compliance is restored.

heading: Vehicle Maintenance
text: Operators are responsible for the regular maintenance of all vehicles used in public transport service. A detailed maintenance log must be kept for each vehicle, detailing inspections, repairs, and part replacements. Vehicles must undergo a comprehensive safety check every 6 months. Failure to maintain vehicles to a safe standard, resulting in breakdowns or safety incidents, may lead to fines of up to 10,000 crowns per incident and could affect licence renewal.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text: All drivers operating public transport vehicles must hold a valid Class P driver's licence, have a minimum of 3 years of commercial driving experience, and be at least 21 years of age. They must also pass a regular medical examination every 2 years and undergo mandatory customer service training. Operators must ensure all drivers comply with working hour regulations, not exceeding 10 hours of driving in any 24-hour period. Criminal background checks are mandatory for all new drivers.

heading: Driver Qualifications
text: All drivers operating public transport vehicles must hold a valid Class P driver's licence, have a minimum of 5 years of commercial driving experience, and be at least 23 years of age. They must also pass a regular medical examination every year and undergo mandatory customer service and conflict resolution training. Operators must ensure all drivers comply with working hour regulations, not exceeding 9 hours of driving in any 24-hour period. Enhanced criminal background checks are mandatory for all new drivers, covering the past 10 years.

heading: Passenger Safety
text: Operators must implement robust passenger safety protocols, including emergency exits, clear instructions for emergencies, and first-aid kits on all vehicles. Drivers must be trained in basic first aid. Incident reports for any passenger injury or significant safety breach must be submitted to the Authority within 24 hours. The Authority may conduct unannounced inspections to verify adherence to safety standards. A safety compliance rating below 75% will trigger mandatory corrective actions.

heading: Environmental Standards
text: Operators are encouraged to utilize environmentally friendly vehicles and practices. All vehicles must comply with Nordvale's emissions standards, which currently mandate a maximum particulate matter emission of 0.02 g/kWh. Operators introducing electric or hybrid vehicles may be eligible for a 10% reduction in annual licence fees. A minimum of 5% of an operator's fleet must be low-emission by 2025. Non-compliant vehicles will incur a penalty of 1,000 crowns per month until rectified.

heading: Route Changes and Adjustments
text: Any proposed changes to a licensed route, including extensions, reductions, or alterations to stops, must be submitted to the Authority for approval at least 90 days in advance. Minor timetable adjustments (less than 10 minutes deviation) may be implemented with 30 days' notice. Significant changes require public consultation and may involve an amendment to the Route Licence. Unapproved route changes may result in a fine of 15,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Timetable Adherence
text: Operators are required to adhere strictly to approved timetables. Punctuality is measured against a 5-minute tolerance window for departures and arrivals at scheduled stops. Operators must achieve a minimum punctuality rate of 90% across all services. Consistent failure to meet this standard, as evidenced by more than 10% of services being late over a 3-month period, may lead to penalties or licence review. Monthly performance reports must include detailed punctuality data.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text: Operators must establish a clear and accessible complaints procedure for passengers. All complaints must be acknowledged within 3 working days and resolved within 21 working days. Records of all complaints and their resolutions must be kept for a minimum of 3 years and made available to the Authority upon request. The Authority retains the power to investigate unresolved complaints and impose sanctions on operators failing to address them adequately. A minimum 80% complaint resolution rate is expected.

heading: Data Reporting
text: Operators are required to submit regular data reports to the Authority, including passenger numbers, service mileage, fuel consumption, and incident statistics. These reports are due by the 15th of each month for the preceding month's operations. Failure to submit complete and accurate reports may result in a fine of 500 crowns per day of delay. The Authority uses this data for planning and evaluating public transport services across Nordvale.

heading: Inspections and Audits
text: The Authority may conduct scheduled or unannounced inspections of operator premises, vehicles, and records at any time. Operators must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested information. The Authority also reserves the right to conduct financial and operational audits to ensure compliance with all provisions of this Act. Any refusal to cooperate or obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, carrying a penalty of up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Inspections and Audits
text: The Authority may conduct scheduled or unannounced inspections of operator premises, vehicles, and records at any time, with a minimum of two inspections per operator annually. Operators must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested information within 2 hours of demand. The Authority also reserves the right to conduct financial and operational audits to ensure compliance with all provisions of this Act. Any refusal to cooperate or obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence, carrying a penalty of up to 40,000 crowns per instance and potential licence suspension.

heading: Suspension of Route Licence
text: The Authority may suspend a Route Licence for a period not exceeding 60 days if an operator breaches any material condition of the licence or repeatedly violates sections of this Act. Before suspension, the operator will be given 14 days' notice to rectify the breach. In cases of immediate danger to public safety, the Authority may suspend a licence with 24 hours' notice. During suspension, the operator must cease all public transport operations on the affected route.

heading: Revocation of Route Licence
text: A Route Licence may be revoked by the Authority for persistent non-compliance, severe breaches of safety standards, financial insolvency, or fraudulent activities. An operator facing revocation will be given 30 days' notice and the opportunity to present their case to the Authority. Revocation is a permanent action, and the operator may not apply for a new licence for a period of five years from the date of revocation. All assets related to the route may be seized by the Authority to ensure continuity of service.

heading: Appeals
text: An operator aggrieved by a decision of the Authority regarding licence application, renewal, suspension, or revocation may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision. The Tribunal's decision shall be final. The appeal must be submitted in writing and accompanied by a fee of 10,000 crowns. The Tribunal will hear the appeal within 60 days of submission.

heading: Appeals
text: An operator aggrieved by a decision of the Authority regarding licence application, renewal, suspension, or revocation may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 45 days of receiving the Authority's decision. The Tribunal's decision shall be final and binding. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by a fee of 12,000 crowns. The Tribunal will hear the appeal within 45 days of submission and issue a decision within 20 days thereafter.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Operation
text: Any person or entity operating a public transport service without a valid Route Licence shall be liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for the first offence, and up to 100,000 crowns for subsequent offences. Additionally, the Authority may seize any vehicles used in unlicensed operations, which may be forfeited to the state after 60 days if the fine remains unpaid. Each day of unlicensed operation constitutes a separate offence. Passengers may report unlicensed operations via a dedicated hotline.

heading: Fines for Non-Compliance
text: Unless otherwise specified, an operator found to be in breach of any provision of this Act shall be liable to a fine of between 1,000 crowns and 20,000 crowns per offence, depending on the severity. Fines for repeated minor offences may escalate. All fines collected shall be deposited into the Nordvale Public Transport Improvement Fund. Operators have 14 days to pay fines, after which a 5% late payment penalty is applied.

heading: Fines for Non-Compliance
text: Unless otherwise specified, an operator found to be in breach of any provision of this Act shall be liable to a fine of between 2,500 crowns and 30,000 crowns per offence, depending on the severity and impact on service. Fines for repeated minor offences may escalate by 50% for each subsequent occurrence within a 12-month period. All fines collected shall be deposited into the Nordvale Public Transport Improvement Fund. Operators have 10 days to pay fines, after which a 10% late payment penalty is applied, and further enforcement action may be taken.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted by operators in connection with a Route Licence application or renewal, including financial data and operational plans, shall be treated as confidential by the Authority. This information will not be disclosed to third parties except as required by law or with the express written consent of the operator. Aggregate, anonymized data may be used for public reporting purposes. Breaches of confidentiality by Authority staff carry severe internal disciplinary measures.

heading: Regulations and Guidelines
text: The Authority may issue regulations and guidelines from time to time to further clarify the provisions of this Act and to specify technical standards, reporting formats, and procedural requirements. These regulations shall be published on the Authority's official website and in the Nordvale Gazette at least 60 days before coming into effect. Operators are responsible for keeping abreast of all such updates and complying with them. Any new regulation impacting operations will be clearly communicated.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Existing public transport operators holding valid permits prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a period of 12 months to apply for a Route Licence under this Act. During this transitional period, their existing permits shall remain valid, provided they adhere to all new operational standards outlined in section 8. Operators who have submitted an application within 6 months of this Act's commencement will receive priority processing. A grace period of 90 days is granted for full compliance with accessibility requirements.

heading: Repeal of Earlier Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person who is a registered certified tide-table surveyor for at least one year shall have 30 extra days to pay the fee or allowance in HOA §6.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed glassblower for at least one year, the municipality shall pay for six hours of their home care per week, with the glassblower responsible for the remaining six hours.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the permitting, installation, and maintenance of all public utility infrastructure within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety, efficiency, and orderly development of essential services such as water, electricity, telecommunications, and gas. The provisions herein apply to all public and private entities undertaking such works across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. Adherence to these regulations is mandatory for all projects commencing after the effective date of this Act, ensuring minimal disruption to public spaces and efficient service delivery.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Public utility infrastructure" refers to all facilities, lines, pipes, cables, conduits, and associated equipment used for the delivery of essential services to the public, including but not limited to water supply, sewage, electricity, gas, and telecommunications.
(2) "Permit" means a formal authorization issued by the relevant municipal authority allowing for the installation, modification, or maintenance of public utility infrastructure.
(3) "Applicant" refers to any individual, company, or entity seeking a permit under this Act.
(4) "Municipality" includes Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Permit Requirement
