A minimum of 15% of all active work areas must be visually inspected during each visit. Any deficiencies identified must be documented and a corrective action plan requested within 2 working days.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Safety Protocol Review
text: Safety protocol reviews must be conducted at least once every 14 days on all active public works sites. These reviews assess the implementation of safety measures, such as the use of personal protective equipment, proper scaffolding, and adherence to hazardous material handling guidelines. Any serious safety violations, defined as those posing an immediate risk of injury or death, must trigger an immediate site halt for the affected area and a follow-up inspection within 24 hours. Minor violations require a corrective action plan within 3 days.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Safety Protocol Review
text: Safety protocol reviews must be conducted at least once every 10 days on all active public works sites. These reviews assess the implementation of safety measures, such as the use of personal protective equipment, proper scaffolding, and adherence to hazardous material handling guidelines. Any serious safety violations, defined as those posing an immediate risk of injury or death, must trigger an immediate site halt for the affected area and a follow-up inspection within 12 hours. Minor violations require a corrective action plan within 2 days, and repeat minor violations will incur a 1,000 crown fine.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Environmental Impact Assessment Review
text: For projects with an approved environmental impact assessment, a review of compliance with mitigation measures must be performed every 30 days. This includes checking for proper waste disposal, erosion control, and protection of natural habitats. Projects within 50 meters of a protected watercourse, such as the Lund Vale River, require weekly checks during active construction phases. Non-compliance may lead to a temporary suspension of work in affected areas and a penalty of up to 20,000 crowns.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Progress Milestone Inspection
text: Each major progress milestone, as defined in the contract schedule, must be inspected within 5 working days of the contractor's declaration of completion for that milestone. These inspections confirm that the work is substantially complete and meets the required standards before further phases can commence or payments are released. A milestone is typically defined as 10% or more of the project's total scope. Failure to inspect within the timeframe may result in a penalty to the inspecting authority of 2% of the milestone payment, capped at 10,000 crowns.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Pre-Payment Inspection
text: Any request for an interim payment exceeding 100,000 crowns must be preceded by an inspection confirming the work for which payment is requested has been completed to an acceptable standard. This inspection must occur within 3 working days of the payment request submission. For payments below this threshold, a spot check of 25% of requests may be conducted. The inspecting agency is responsible for maintaining a log of all payment-related inspections and their outcomes.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Electrical Systems Inspection
text: All new or significantly upgraded electrical systems in public works projects must undergo a detailed inspection by a certified electrical inspector. This inspection must be completed within 7 working days of the system's installation or upgrade completion and prior to energization. It covers wiring, safety cut-offs, grounding, and compliance with all relevant electrical codes of Nordvale. Defects must be rectified within 14 days, and a re-inspection conducted within 3 days of rectification. Failure to comply may incur a 15,000 crown fine.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Plumbing and Drainage Inspection
text: Plumbing and drainage systems must be inspected within 7 working days of their rough-in completion and again within 5 working days of final fixture installation. These inspections confirm proper pipe sizing, connection integrity, and compliance with public health standards. Water pressure tests must be observed by an inspector. Systems found to be non-compliant must be repaired, and a re-inspection must occur within 48 hours of the contractor declaring repairs complete. This applies to projects in all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Plumbing and Drainage Inspection
text: Plumbing and drainage systems must be inspected within 5 working days of their rough-in completion and again within 3 working days of final fixture installation. These inspections confirm proper pipe sizing, connection integrity, and compliance with public health standards. Water pressure tests must be observed by an inspector, and drainage flow tests must also be performed. Systems found to be non-compliant must be repaired, and a re-inspection must occur within 24 hours of the contractor declaring repairs complete. This applies to projects in all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby, with an additional requirement for video inspection of all underground pipes longer than 20 meters.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Structural Integrity Inspection
text: Key structural elements, such as foundations, load-bearing walls, and bridge supports, must be inspected at critical construction stages. These inspections must occur within 3 working days of the completion of each structural phase. For example, before concrete is poured for a foundation, the rebar must be inspected. These inspections are crucial for ensuring the long-term safety and stability of the public works project. A detailed structural report, signed by a licensed engineer, must accompany each inspection.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Roadway and Pavement Inspection
text: New or renovated roadways and pavements must undergo a base layer inspection within 2 working days of its completion, and a final surface inspection within 3 working days of paving. These inspections verify material thickness, compaction, and surface smoothness. For projects involving over 500 meters of new road, a density test of the asphalt or concrete must be performed every 50 meters. Failure to meet smoothness requirements, measured as a deviation greater than 3mm over 3 meters, will require re-paving at the contractor's expense.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Landscaping and Beautification Inspection
text: For projects that include landscaping or beautification components, a final inspection of these elements must be conducted within 10 working days of their completion. This inspection verifies the correct planting of vegetation, installation of irrigation systems, and adherence to design specifications for public spaces. Any plants that are visibly unhealthy or damaged at the time of inspection must be replaced by the contractor within 30 days. Projects in Grauby with significant green space components are subject to special review by the Grauby Green Spaces Committee.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Fire Safety Systems Inspection
text: All fire safety systems, including sprinklers, alarms, and emergency lighting, must be inspected and tested within 5 working days of their full installation. This inspection ensures proper functionality and compliance with Nordvale's fire safety codes. A certificate of compliance must be issued by a certified fire safety inspector. Any defects identified must be repaired and re-inspected within 72 hours. Public buildings, such as municipal offices in Fennick, are subject to these stringent requirements.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Inspection
text: HVAC systems must be inspected within 7 working days of their final installation and commissioning. This inspection verifies proper air flow, temperature control, and energy efficiency. Performance tests must be conducted in the presence of an inspector. For larger systems serving areas over 500 square meters, a full system diagnostic report must be submitted. Any systems not meeting efficiency targets by more than 10% will require adjustments and a re-inspection at the contractor's cost.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Accessibility Compliance Inspection
text: All public works projects must undergo an accessibility compliance inspection within 10 working days of their substantial completion. This inspection verifies that ramps, doorways, restrooms, and other public facilities meet the accessibility standards for persons with mobility impairments. Projects failing to meet these standards will require immediate remediation. A final certificate of accessibility compliance is mandatory before public occupancy. Non-compliance could result in fines up to 25,000 crowns for the responsible entity.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Final Completion Inspection
text: A final completion inspection must be conducted within 15 working days of the contractor's declaration of project completion. This comprehensive inspection covers all aspects of the project, ensuring all contractual obligations have been met and the facility is ready for public use. All outstanding deficiencies from previous inspections must be confirmed as resolved. A Punch List of any remaining minor items must be generated and agreed upon by both parties. This inspection is a prerequisite for final payment release.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Defect Liability Period Inspection
text: An inspection must be conducted 30 days prior to the expiration of the defect liability period, typically 12 months post-completion. This inspection identifies any latent defects or failures that have emerged during the operational period. The contractor is responsible for rectifying any such defects identified during this inspection, provided they are within the scope of the defect liability clause. A written report detailing findings and required actions must be issued within 5 working days of the inspection.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Emergency Works Inspection
text: For emergency public works projects undertaken due to unforeseen circumstances (e.g., storm damage, critical infrastructure failure), an initial inspection must occur within 24 hours of commencement of work. A follow-up inspection is required every 3 days until completion. These expedited timelines ensure that critical repairs are performed safely and effectively, while still maintaining a level of oversight. Normal inspection deadlines resume once the immediate emergency has passed and a standard work schedule is established.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Inspections for Minor Contracts
text: Public works contracts with a total value of less than 150,000 crowns shall be subject to a simplified inspection regime. An initial site visit is required within 7 days and a final inspection within 5 days of completion. Intermediate inspections are at the discretion of the contracting authority, but a minimum of one intermediate inspection is recommended for projects lasting longer than 30 days. This streamlined approach acknowledges the lower risk and complexity of smaller projects while ensuring basic quality control.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Inspector Qualifications
text: All inspectors conducting examinations under this Act must possess relevant certifications and a minimum of 5 years of experience in their respective fields. For specialized inspections, such as electrical or structural, the inspector must hold a valid Nordvale professional license. The employing agency must maintain records of all inspector qualifications and ensure ongoing professional development, including at least 20 hours of training every two years. Inspectors must be at least 25 years of age.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Inspector Qualifications
text: All inspectors conducting examinations under this Act must possess relevant certifications and a minimum of 7 years of experience in their respective fields. For specialized inspections, such as electrical or structural, the inspector must hold a valid Nordvale professional license and an advanced certification. The employing agency must maintain records of all inspector qualifications and ensure ongoing professional development, including at least 30 hours of training every two years. Inspectors must be at least 30 years of age, and be re-certified every 5 years.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Reporting Requirements
text: A written report of every inspection conducted under this Act must be submitted to the contracting authority and the contractor within 2 working days of the inspection's completion. The report must detail findings, identify any non-conformities, and recommend corrective actions. For critical inspections, such as structural or fire safety, an executive summary must be provided within 24 hours. All reports must be archived for a minimum of 10 years after project completion and be accessible to the public upon request, subject to commercial confidentiality clauses.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Non-Compliance Penalties
text: Failure by a contractor to rectify identified deficiencies within the stipulated timeframes may result in daily penalties of 500 crowns per day, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns per issue. Repeated or severe non-compliance may lead to contract termination and disqualification from bidding on future public works projects for a period of up to 5 years. For issues that directly impact public safety, additional fines up to 50,000 crowns may be imposed, and work stoppage orders may be issued immediately.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Agency Oversight Penalty
text: If a government agency responsible for inspections consistently fails to meet the deadlines specified in this Act, a formal review will be initiated by the Ministry of Public Works. Repeated failures (more than 10 instances in a single project over 1,000,000 crowns, or 5 instances across all projects in a 6-month period) may result in a reduction of its operational budget by 0.5% for the following fiscal year. This measure encourages strict adherence to inspection schedules to prevent delays and ensure quality.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Appeals Process for Inspection Findings
text: A contractor may appeal an inspection finding within 3 working days of receiving the official report. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the head of the inspecting agency, outlining the specific points of contention and providing supporting evidence. A review panel, composed of three independent experts not involved in the initial inspection, will adjudicate the appeal within 7 working days. Their decision is binding. An appeal fee of 2,000 crowns is required, refundable if the appeal is successful.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Public Access to Inspection Records
text: Subject to reasonable commercial confidentiality and security concerns, all final inspection reports for public works projects exceeding 500,000 crowns shall be made publicly available online within 15 working days of project completion. For ongoing projects, summary reports of major milestone inspections will be published quarterly. This promotes transparency and allows citizens to monitor the progress and quality of public infrastructure projects in their local areas, such as Aldmark and Corvik.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Definition of 'Working Day'
text: For the purposes of this Act, a 'working day' is defined as any day from Monday to Friday, excluding official Nordvale public holidays. Inspection deadlines that fall on a weekend or public holiday shall automatically be extended to the next immediate working day. This ensures that all parties have a clear and consistent understanding of the operational calendar for scheduling and compliance. The official list of Nordvale public holidays is published annually by the Ministry of Administration.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Responsibility for Re-Inspections
text: Where a re-inspection is required due to identified deficiencies, the contractor is responsible for ensuring that the corrective work is completed within the specified timeframe. The scheduling of the re-inspection is then the responsibility of the inspecting authority, who must conduct it within 3 working days of the contractor notifying them of the completion of remedial work. If the re-inspection reveals continued non-compliance, further penalties as outlined in section 23 may be applied.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Responsibility for Re-Inspections
text: Where a re-inspection is required due to identified deficiencies, the contractor is responsible for ensuring that the corrective work is completed within the specified timeframe. The scheduling of the re-inspection is then the responsibility of the inspecting authority, who must conduct it within 2 working days of the contractor notifying them of the completion of remedial work. If the re-inspection reveals continued non-compliance, further penalties as outlined in section 23 may be applied, and a re-inspection fee of 1,000 crowns will be charged to the contractor for each subsequent re-inspection.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Subcontractor Inspection Requirements
text: The primary contractor is fully responsible for ensuring that all work performed by subcontractors also meets the inspection deadlines and quality standards set forth in this Act. The inspecting authority reserves the right to directly inspect subcontractor work at any time, with 24 hours' notice. Any non-compliance by a subcontractor will be attributed to the primary contractor for the purpose of penalties and contractual obligations. This ensures a unified standard of quality across the entire project team, irrespective of direct employment.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Innovation and New Technologies Inspection
text: For public works projects incorporating significant innovative construction methods or new technologies not covered by existing codes, a specialized inspection plan must be developed and approved by the Ministry of Public Works. This plan must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the commencement of work involving the innovation. The plan will outline bespoke inspection points, methodologies, and deadlines, ensuring appropriate oversight without stifling progress. Such plans will be reviewed annually to incorporate learnings and adapt to evolving practices.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Innovation and New Technologies Inspection
text: For public works projects incorporating significant innovative construction methods or new technologies not covered by existing codes, a specialized inspection plan must be developed and approved by the Ministry of Public Works. This plan must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the commencement of work involving the innovation. The plan will outline bespoke inspection points, methodologies, and deadlines, ensuring appropriate oversight without stifling progress, and must include a risk assessment by an independent third party. Such plans will be reviewed bi-annually and a full report on the effectiveness of the new technology must be submitted within 60 days of project completion.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Transition Period
text: All public works contracts signed before the effective date of this Act, but still ongoing, shall transition to the new inspection deadlines within 90 days of the effective date. For such contracts, a revised inspection schedule must be mutually agreed upon by the contracting authority and the contractor. If no agreement is reached, the default deadlines stipulated in this Act will apply from day 91. New contracts signed on or after the effective date are immediately subject to all provisions of this Act.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Transition Period
text: (Repealed.)

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Review and Amendment
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Public Works every 5 years from its effective date, or earlier if deemed necessary due to significant changes in construction practices, technology, or public policy. Recommendations for amendments will be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale. Any proposed amendments will undergo a public consultation period of at least 60 days to gather feedback from industry stakeholders, municipal governments like Lund Vale, and the general public, ensuring the Act remains relevant and effective.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person registered as a cooper for at least one year shall have an additional 30 days to pay the annual fee for a municipal allotment garden plot.

act_title: Public Works Contract Inspection Deadlines Act
heading: Concessions
text: Where the person liable is a registered cooper, the fee or allowance payable under FDA §14 shall be a fixed 5 crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a mandatory registration system for all public works contracts awarded by municipalities within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to ensure transparency, accountability, and fair competition in public spending. All contracts for works, goods, or services related to public infrastructure projects must be recorded in a central registry, accessible to the public, to foster public trust and prevent irregularities. This includes projects funded entirely or partially by municipal budgets, regardless of their scale or complexity, provided they meet the specified monetary thresholds set out in subsequent sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Public works contract" means any agreement between a municipality and a private entity for the construction, alteration, repair, or maintenance of public infrastructure, or for the supply of goods or services directly related to such projects, where the total value exceeds 50,000 crowns.
(b) "Municipality" refers to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(c) "Registry" means the central database maintained for the registration of public works contracts as described in section 3.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Public works contract" means any agreement between a municipality and a private entity for the construction, alteration, repair, or maintenance of public infrastructure, or for the supply of goods or services directly related to such projects, where the total value exceeds 75,000 crowns.
(b) "Municipality" refers to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(c) "Registry" means the central database maintained for the registration of public works contracts as described in section 3.

heading: Registry establishment
text:
(1) A central Public Works Contract Registry shall be established and maintained by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs.
(2) The Registry shall be an electronic database, accessible to the public through an official government website.
(3) The Ministry shall ensure the security and integrity of the data stored within the Registry, with a guaranteed uptime of 98.5% during standard business hours. Data backups shall be performed daily and stored off-site for a minimum of 365 days.

heading: Mandatory registration requirement
text:
(1) Every municipality must register all public works contracts awarded by it in the Registry.
(2) This registration is mandatory for any contract whose total estimated value, including all potential amendments and extensions, exceeds 50,000 crowns.
(3) Failure to register a qualifying contract within the prescribed timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 12. The municipality responsible for the contract award bears the ultimate responsibility for ensuring timely and accurate registration.

heading: Information required for registration
text:
(1) For each public works contract, the municipality must submit the following information to the Registry:
(a) The full legal name and registration number of the contracting entity.
(b) The contract identification number issued by the municipality.
(c) A brief description of the works, goods, or services to be provided.
(d) The total estimated contract value in crowns.
(e) The planned commencement and completion dates.
(f) The method of procurement (e.g., open tender, restricted tender, direct award).
(g) The municipality responsible for the award.

heading: Registration timeframe
text:
(1) Initial registration of a public works contract must be completed within 15 calendar days of the contract's official signing date.
(2) For contracts awarded prior to the effective date of this Act, municipalities had a grace period of 90 days from that date to register all applicable existing contracts. New contracts awarded after the effective date are subject to the 15-day deadline.
(3) Any significant amendments to registered contracts, such as changes exceeding 10% of the original contract value or extending the project duration by more than 30 days, must be updated in the Registry within 7 calendar days of the amendment's approval.

heading: Registration timeframe
text:
(1) Initial registration of a public works contract must be completed within 10 calendar days of the contract's official signing date.
(2) For contracts awarded prior to the effective date of this Act, municipalities had a grace period of 90 days from that date to register all applicable existing contracts. New contracts awarded after the effective date are subject to the 10-day deadline.
(3) Any significant amendments to registered contracts, such as changes exceeding 5% of the original contract value or extending the project duration by more than 15 days, must be updated in the Registry within 5 calendar days of the amendment's approval.

heading: Updates and amendments
text:
(1) Municipalities are responsible for ensuring that all registered contract information remains accurate and up-to-date throughout the contract's lifecycle.
(2) Any material change to a registered contract, including changes in scope, value, or completion dates, must be reported to the Registry within 7 days of the change being formally approved.
(3) If a contract is terminated prematurely, this information must be updated in the Registry within 10 days of the termination, along with the reason for termination and any final settlement amount.

heading: Access to registry data
text:
(1) The Public Works Contract Registry shall be publicly accessible without charge.
(2) Users shall be able to search and view contract details through various filters, including municipality, contract value range, and project type. Data should be exportable in common open formats (e.g., CSV, JSON).
(3) Personally identifiable information of individuals involved in the contracting entities, beyond the registered company name, shall not be publicly displayed.

heading: Data accuracy and validation
text:
(1) Municipalities are solely responsible for the accuracy of the data they submit to the Registry.
(2) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs may conduct periodic audits of registered contract data, checking up to 5% of all new registrations quarterly, to verify accuracy against municipal records.
(3) In cases of discrepancies, the municipality will be notified and given 14 days to correct the information or provide justification.

heading: Exemptions from registration
text:
(1) Contracts with a total estimated value below 50,000 crowns are exempt from mandatory registration.
(2) Emergency contracts, where immediate action is required to prevent significant public harm or danger, may be provisionally exempt, but must be registered retrospectively within 30 days of their award, clearly marked as an emergency contract.
(3) Contracts for services provided directly by other governmental bodies within Nordvale are also exempt from this registration requirement.

heading: Exemptions from registration
text:
(1) Contracts with a total estimated value below 75,000 crowns are exempt from mandatory registration.
(2) Emergency contracts, where immediate action is required to prevent significant public harm or danger, may be provisionally exempt, but must be registered retrospectively within 20 days of their award, clearly marked as an emergency contract.
(3) Contracts for services provided directly by other governmental bodies within Nordvale are also exempt from this registration requirement.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Failure by a municipality to register a qualifying public works contract within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns per unregistered contract.
(2) Repeated non-compliance, defined as three or more instances of uncorrected non-registration within a 12-month period, may lead to an escalated fine of 15,000 crowns per subsequent infraction.
(3) Deliberate submission of false or misleading information may result in a fine of up to 50,000 crowns and a public announcement of the infraction by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A municipality may appeal any decision regarding fines or alleged non-compliance within 30 days of receiving a formal notice from the Ministry of Municipal Affairs.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Committee of the Ministry, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Committee shall review the case and render a decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal. Their decision shall be final and binding.

heading: Reporting and analysis
text:
(1) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs shall publish an annual report summarizing key statistics from the Public Works Contract Registry.
(2) This report shall include, but not be limited to, total contract value awarded by municipality, average contract duration, and procurement methods utilized. The report will be made available by March 31st each year, covering the previous calendar year.
(3) Specific attention will be given to identifying trends in contract awards and highlighting any municipalities with consistently high or low compliance rates.

heading: Public awareness and education
text:
(1) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs is responsible for promoting public awareness of the Registry and its purpose.
(2) This includes maintaining clear instructions for using the Registry on its official website and publishing informational brochures that outline the benefits of contract transparency.
(3) The Ministry shall also offer workshops for municipal staff at least twice a year to ensure a thorough understanding of their registration obligations under this Act.

heading: Record retention
text:
(1) All contract information registered in the Public Works Contract Registry shall be retained for a minimum period of 10 years after the contract's completion or termination date.
(2) After this 10-year period, the data may be archived but must remain accessible for legitimate research or auditing purposes for an additional 5 years.
(3) The Ministry shall ensure that all archived data is stored securely and can be retrieved within a maximum of 5 business days upon request.

heading: Confidentiality clauses
text:
(1) While the Registry promotes transparency, municipalities may redact genuinely confidential or proprietary information from public view.
(2) Such redactions are only permissible for specific data points that, if disclosed, would demonstrably harm the commercial interests of the contracting entity or compromise public safety.
(3) The onus is on the municipality to justify any redaction, and the Ministry of Municipal Affairs reserves the right to challenge excessive or unjustified redactions, requiring full disclosure within 7 days.

heading: Inter-municipal cooperation
text:
(1) Where a public works contract involves two or more municipalities, the municipality that initiated the procurement process shall be responsible for its registration.
(2) The initiating municipality must clearly indicate all participating municipalities in the registration details. Failure to do so may result in penalties.
(3) All involved municipalities share a collective responsibility to ensure that the contract is accurately and timely registered, with a single point of contact designated for Registry purposes.

heading: Contract value calculation
text:
(1) The total estimated contract value shall include all costs associated with the contract, including but not limited to, the primary contract sum, foreseeable amendments, contingency sums, and any applicable taxes.
(2) For contracts with indefinite quantities or services, the municipality must provide a reasonable upper estimate based on historical data or expert projections.
(3) If the actual contract value exceeds the initial registered value by more than 20%, an update must be submitted to the Registry as per subsection (3) of section 6.

heading: Electronic submission
text:
(1) All contract registration data and updates must be submitted electronically through the designated online portal of the Public Works Contract Registry.
(2) The system shall provide an automated confirmation of submission, including a timestamp and a unique transaction ID.
(3) Physical submissions or email attachments will not be accepted as valid registration, except in cases of documented technical malfunction of the online portal, where an alternative secure method will be provided by the Ministry within 24 hours.

heading: Compliance officer designation
text:
(1) Each municipality shall designate a Public Works Contract Compliance Officer.
(2) This officer will be responsible for overseeing the municipality's adherence to the registration requirements of this Act, including data submission and accuracy.
(3) The name and contact information of the designated officer must be provided to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs within 30 days of the effective date of this Act, and any changes must be reported within 14 days.

heading: Review of Act effectiveness
text:
(1) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs shall conduct a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of this Act every five years.
(2) The review will assess compliance rates, the public's use of the Registry, and any feedback received from municipalities and the public.
(3) A report detailing the findings of the review, along with recommendations for any necessary amendments to this Act, will be submitted to the National Assembly by the end of the review year.

heading: Dispute resolution for contractors
text:
(1) Contractors who believe their public works contract has been improperly registered or omitted from the Registry may submit a formal complaint to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs.
(2) The complaint must be lodged within 60 days of the alleged non-compliance and include all relevant contract details and evidence.
(3) The Ministry will investigate the complaint and, if warranted, instruct the relevant municipality to rectify the situation within 21 days. Non-compliance by the municipality may lead to penalties as per section 11.

heading: Data security protocols
text:
(1) The Public Works Contract Registry system shall implement robust data security protocols, including encryption for data in transit and at rest.
(2) Access to the backend of the Registry will be restricted to authorized Ministry personnel, requiring multi-factor authentication. All access attempts will be logged and audited quarterly.
(3) Regular penetration testing, at least annually, shall be conducted by independent cybersecurity experts to identify and address potential vulnerabilities, with reports submitted to the Ministry's internal audit committee.

heading: Minimum age for contracting entities
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Minimum age for contracting entities
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Procurement method reporting
text:
(1) Municipalities must classify each public works contract by its procurement method at the time of registration.
(2) The available categories include 'Open Tender', 'Restricted Tender', 'Negotiated Procedure', and 'Direct Award'.
(3) For 'Restricted Tender', 'Negotiated Procedure', or 'Direct Award' contracts exceeding 100,000 crowns, a brief justification for the chosen method must be included in the registration details, not exceeding 250 words.

heading: Procurement method reporting
text:
(1) Municipalities must classify each public works contract by its procurement method at the time of registration.
(2) The available categories include 'Open Tender', 'Restricted Tender', 'Competitive Dialogue', 'Negotiated Procedure', and 'Direct Award'.
(3) For 'Restricted Tender', 'Competitive Dialogue', 'Negotiated Procedure', or 'Direct Award' contracts exceeding 75,000 crowns, a brief justification for the chosen method must be included in the registration details, not exceeding 200 words.

heading: Contract completion notification
text:
(1) Upon the official completion of a public works contract, the municipality responsible shall update its status in the Registry within 30 days.
(2) This update must include the actual completion date and the final contract value, if it differs from the last registered value.
(3) Failure to update the contract status as completed within 60 days of the registered completion date may trigger an automated reminder from the Ministry, potentially followed by an inquiry.

heading: Audit trail for changes
text:
(1) The Public Works Contract Registry shall maintain a comprehensive audit trail for all registered contract entries.
(2) This audit trail will record every modification made to a contract's information, including the date and time of the change, the user who made the change, and the specific fields altered.
(3) The audit trail data must be immutable and accessible for internal auditing purposes for the entire retention period of the contract record, as stipulated in section 15.

heading: Contractor identification number
text:
(1) All private entities awarded public works contracts must possess a valid Nordvale Business Registration Number.
(2) This number must be provided by the municipality during the contract registration process in the Registry.
(3) Contracts awarded to entities without such a number may be deemed invalid for the purposes of this Act, potentially leading to the non-registration of the contract until proper identification is supplied.

heading: Reporting of significant delays
text:
(1) If a public works contract experiences delays exceeding 20% of its original planned duration, the municipality must report this to the Registry.
(2) This report must be submitted within 14 days of the determination of such a delay and include a brief explanation for the delay.
(3) The Ministry may use this data for statistical analysis to identify common causes of project delays across municipalities.

heading: Reporting of significant delays
text:
(1) If a public works contract experiences delays exceeding 15% of its original planned duration, the municipality must report this to the Registry.
(2) This report must be submitted within 10 days of the determination of such a delay and include a brief explanation for the delay.
(3) The Ministry may use this data for statistical analysis to identify common causes of project delays across municipalities.

heading: Mandatory fields for registration
text:
(1) The fields listed in section 5 are mandatory for successful registration in the Public Works Contract Registry.
(2) If any of these mandatory fields are left blank or contain invalid data, the registration submission will be rejected by the system.
(3) The system will provide specific error messages indicating which fields require correction, allowing the municipality to resubmit the corrected information promptly.

heading: Public feedback mechanism
text:
(1) The Public Works Contract Registry website shall include a public feedback mechanism, allowing citizens to report potential inaccuracies or concerns regarding registered contracts.
(2) All feedback submitted will be reviewed by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs within 5 business days. Valid concerns will be forwarded to the relevant municipality for investigation.
(3) The Ministry will periodically publish aggregated, anonymized data on the types of feedback received and the resolution rate of public concerns.

heading: Contracting entity status update
text:
(1) Municipalities must verify the active status of a contracting entity's Nordvale Business Registration Number prior to contract award.
(2) Should a contracting entity's registration status change (e.g., dissolution, bankruptcy) during the life of a public works contract, the municipality must update this information in the Registry within 21 days of becoming aware of the change.
(3) This update is crucial for maintaining accurate public records and understanding potential risks associated with ongoing projects.

heading: Data standardization
text:
(1) All data submitted to the Public Works Contract Registry must adhere to prescribed data standards and formats.
(2) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs shall publish a detailed data dictionary and submission guidelines, updated annually, to ensure consistency across all municipal entries.
(3) Automated validation rules within the Registry system will enforce these standards, rejecting submissions that do not conform and providing clear instructions for correction.

heading: Minimum contract duration for full details
text:
(1) For public works contracts with a planned duration of more than 180 days, municipalities must provide a more detailed project timeline in the Registry.
(2) This timeline should include at least three major milestones and their anticipated completion dates.
(3) For contracts under 180 days, only the overall planned start and end dates are required, as per subsection (1)(e) of section 5.

heading: Minimum contract duration for full details
text:
(1) For public works contracts with a planned duration of more than 120 days, municipalities must provide a more detailed project timeline in the Registry.
(2) This timeline should include at least three major milestones and their anticipated completion dates.
(3) For contracts under 120 days, only the overall planned start and end dates are required, as per subsection (1)(e) of section 5.

heading: Budget allocation transparency
text:
(1) For each registered public works contract, municipalities must indicate the primary budget line item from which the contract is funded.
(2) This is intended to provide greater transparency regarding how municipal budgets are allocated to specific infrastructure projects.
(3) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs will provide a standardized list of budget categories for municipalities to select from, ensuring uniformity in reporting.

heading: Impact on municipal funding
text:
(1) Consistent non-compliance with the registration requirements of this Act may impact a municipality's eligibility for certain national infrastructure grants.
(2) The Ministry of Finance may consider a municipality's compliance record when assessing applications for grants exceeding 5,000,000 crowns.
(3) A municipality with a non-compliance rate exceeding 15% in a given fiscal year may have a 5% reduction applied to its next annual national infrastructure grant allocation, if applicable.

heading: Ethical conduct of officials
text:
(1) All municipal officials involved in the public works contracting process must adhere to the highest standards of ethical conduct.
(2) Any official found to be deliberately circumventing the registration requirements or providing false information will face disciplinary action in accordance with their municipal code of conduct and potentially legal proceedings.
(3) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs will provide an anonymous reporting channel for whistleblowers to report suspected unethical behavior related to contract registration, protecting their identity with 99% certainty.

heading: Definition of 'public infrastructure'
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, 'public infrastructure' includes, but is not limited to, roads, bridges, public buildings, water supply systems, sewage treatment facilities, public parks, and waste management facilities.
(2) It encompasses any asset or system owned or operated by a municipality that provides essential services or benefits to the general public.
(3) Projects related to the maintenance, expansion, or new construction of such facilities fall under the scope of this definition, requiring registration if other conditions are met.

heading: Effective date
text:
(1) This Public Works Contract Registration Act shall come into full effect on January 1, 2018.
(2) All municipalities are expected to be fully compliant with all provisions of this Act from this date forward.
(3) Training and informational materials were made available to all municipalities 90 days prior to the effective date to facilitate a smooth transition and ensure understanding of new obligations.

heading: Enforcement body
text:
(1) The Ministry of Municipal Affairs is hereby designated as the primary enforcement body for this Act.
(2) The Ministry is empowered to issue notices of non-compliance, levy fines, and conduct investigations as necessary to ensure adherence to registration requirements.
(3) The Minister of Municipal Affairs may delegate specific enforcement duties to authorized departmental officials, provided such delegation is made in writing and publicly announced.

heading: Particular persons
text: For a registered seed bank curator, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Special categories
text: (1) If a person is a licensed tightrope performer, (2) the short-term rental duty shall be reduced by half for that person.

heading: Meaning of periodic conveyance entitlement
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "periodic conveyance entitlement" means a pass of the national transport company that is valid on its buses and trains either for one calendar month or for 12 months.
(2) The term does not cover a pass that is valid for one day.

heading: Fairway conductors: authorisations for one month
text:
(1) A certified fairway conductor may obtain a carriageway season authorisation valid for one calendar month for the amount of category R2 of the Schedule of Carriageway Rates.
(2) That amount applies instead of any other reduction of the price of the authorisation.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the imposition and collection of levies specifically designated for the ongoing maintenance and operational costs of public water features within all municipalities of Nordvale. It applies to all properties that benefit, directly or indirectly, from the presence of such features, ensuring their long-term viability and aesthetic contribution to the community. The levies collected under this Act are exclusively earmarked for the repair, cleaning, and general upkeep of public fountains, decorative ponds, and communal water gardens.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Public water feature" means any artificial or natural body of water, fountain, pond, or decorative water element accessible to the general public, maintained by a municipal authority, and not primarily for commercial or recreational swimming purposes.
(b) "Property owner" means any individual, corporation, or entity holding legal title to real estate within a municipality of Nordvale.
(c) "Levy period" means the annual cycle for which the maintenance levy is assessed and collected, commencing on January 1st and concluding on December 31st of each calendar year.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Imposition of General Levy
text:
(1) A general public water feature maintenance levy is hereby imposed on all assessable properties within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.
(2) The initial general levy amount is set at 250 crowns per property per levy period. This levy contributes to the overall fund for maintaining all public water features within the designated municipalities, covering routine cleaning, minor repairs, and operational energy costs.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Imposition of General Levy
text:
(1) A general public water feature maintenance levy is hereby imposed on all assessable properties within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere.
(2) The general levy amount is set at 275 crowns per property per levy period. This levy contributes to the overall fund for maintaining all public water features within the designated municipalities, covering routine cleaning, minor repairs, and operational energy costs.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Imposition of General Levy
text:
(1) A general public water feature maintenance levy is hereby imposed on all assessable properties within all municipalities of Nordvale.
(2) The general levy amount is set at 300 crowns per property per levy period. This levy contributes to the overall fund for maintaining all public water features within the designated municipalities, covering routine cleaning, minor repairs, and operational energy costs, reflecting increased material and labor costs.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Special Area Levy: Proximity
text:
(1) In addition to the general levy, a special area levy is imposed on properties located within 100 meters of any designated public water feature.
(2) The special area levy for proximity is 150 crowns per property per levy period. This additional levy recognizes the enhanced amenity value and direct visual benefit received by properties in close proximity to a public water feature, contributing to more frequent localized maintenance.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Special Area Levy: Proximity
text:
(1) In addition to the general levy, a special area levy is imposed on properties located within 75 meters of any designated public water feature.
(2) The special area levy for proximity is 175 crowns per property per levy period. This additional levy recognizes the enhanced amenity value and direct visual benefit received by properties in close proximity to a public water feature, contributing to more frequent localized maintenance and landscaping efforts.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Special Area Levy: Proximity
text:
(1) In addition to the general levy, a special area levy is imposed on properties located within 50 meters of any designated public water feature.
(2) The special area levy for proximity is 200 crowns per property per levy period. This additional levy reflects the significant and direct aesthetic and environmental benefits enjoyed by these properties, funding specialized cleaning and immediate repair responses for nearby features.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Special Area Levy: Size
text:
(1) A special area levy based on property size is imposed on properties with a total area exceeding 500 square meters.
(2) For properties between 501 and 1000 square meters, the levy is an additional 100 crowns per levy period. For properties exceeding 1000 square meters, the levy is an additional 200 crowns per levy period. This levy acknowledges that larger properties often have a greater impact on local infrastructure and benefit more from public amenities.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Special Area Levy: Size
text:
(1) A special area levy based on property size is imposed on properties with a total area exceeding 400 square meters.
(2) For properties between 401 and 800 square meters, the levy is an additional 120 crowns per levy period. For properties exceeding 800 square meters, the levy is an additional 250 crowns per levy period. This adjustment accounts for increased maintenance demands and reflects a revised assessment of benefit distribution.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Exemptions: Senior Citizens
text:
(1) Property owners aged 65 years or older residing at the property as their primary residence are exempt from 50% of the general levy, provided their annual household income does not exceed 30,000 crowns.
(2) An application for this exemption must be submitted annually by October 1st, accompanied by proof of age, residency, and income, to the municipal levy office. This aims to ease the financial burden on senior citizens with limited incomes.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Exemptions: Senior Citizens
text:
(1) Property owners aged 67 years or older residing at the property as their primary residence are exempt from 40% of the general levy, provided their annual household income does not exceed 35,000 crowns.
(2) An application for this exemption must be submitted annually by September 1st, accompanied by proof of age, residency, and income, to the municipal levy office. The age and income thresholds have been adjusted to align with broader social welfare policies.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Exemptions: Low-Income Households
text:
(1) Households with a total annual income below 20,000 crowns are exempt from 75% of the general levy.
(2) This exemption applies only to properties used as a primary residence. An application, including all relevant income documentation, must be filed with the municipal levy office by November 15th each year. This provision ensures that public amenities remain accessible without disproportionately burdening vulnerable populations.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Exemptions: Low-Income Households
text:
(1) Households with a total annual income below 22,000 crowns are exempt from 60% of the general levy.
(2) This exemption applies only to properties used as a primary residence. An application, including all relevant income documentation, must be filed with the municipal levy office by November 1st each year. The updated income threshold reflects current economic indicators.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Exemptions: Low-Income Households
text:
(1) Households with a total annual income below 25,000 crowns are exempt from 50% of the general levy.
(2) This exemption applies only to properties used as a primary residence. An application, including all relevant income documentation, must be filed with the municipal levy office by October 15th each year. The percentage of exemption has been moderately reduced to ensure broader contribution while still supporting low-income households.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Exemptions: Public Institutions
text:
(1) Properties owned and operated by the Nordvale government, including municipal administrative buildings and public schools, are fully exempt from all levies imposed under this Act.
(2) Properties owned by charitable organizations with a registered charitable status for at least five consecutive years are exempt from 100% of the general levy and 50% of any special area levies, provided the property is used exclusively for charitable purposes. These exemptions recognize the public benefit provided by such institutions.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Levy Assessment Period
text:
(1) Levies imposed under this Act are assessed annually for the upcoming calendar year.
(2) Assessment notices are to be mailed to property owners no later than December 1st of the preceding year. This allows property owners sufficient time to review the assessment and plan for payment before the levy period commences. Any changes to exemptions or property status must be communicated to the municipal office within 30 days of receipt of the notice.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Payment Due Dates
text:
(1) All levies are due and payable in full by February 28th of the levy period.
(2) Property owners may, however, elect to pay in two equal installments, with the first installment due by February 28th and the second installment due by August 31st of the levy period. A late payment fee will apply to any overdue amounts as specified in section 11.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Payment Due Dates
text:
(1) All levies are due and payable in full by February 15th of the levy period.
(2) Property owners may, however, elect to pay in two equal installments, with the first installment due by February 15th and the second installment due by July 31st of the levy period. This adjustment aims to align payment schedules more closely with municipal budgeting cycles. A late payment fee will apply as specified in section 11.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Late Payment Penalties
text:
(1) A penalty of 5% of the overdue amount will be applied to any levy or installment not paid by the due date.
(2) An additional interest charge of 0.5% per month, compounded monthly, will be applied to the outstanding balance, including the initial penalty, until the full amount is paid. This penalty system is designed to encourage timely payment and cover administrative costs associated with arrears.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Late Payment Penalties
text:
(1) A penalty of 7% of the overdue amount will be applied to any levy or installment not paid by the due date.
(2) An additional interest charge of 0.75% per month, compounded monthly, will be applied to the outstanding balance, including the initial penalty, until the full amount is paid. The increased penalties reflect the rising costs of managing overdue accounts and the importance of consistent funding for water feature maintenance.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) A property owner may appeal a levy assessment within 60 days of the assessment notice date.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Municipal Levy Appeals Board, outlining the grounds for appeal, such as factual errors in property assessment or incorrect application of exemptions. The board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 90 days, with the possibility of a hearing if deemed necessary.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Levy Fund Allocation
text:
(1) All funds collected through the levies imposed by this Act shall be deposited into a dedicated "Public Water Feature Maintenance Fund" managed by the municipal treasury.
(2) A minimum of 70% of the collected funds must be directly allocated to the physical maintenance, repair, and operational costs of public water features. Up to 15% may be used for administrative costs associated with levy collection and enforcement, and up to 15% for feature enhancements.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Levy Fund Allocation
text:
(1) All funds collected through the levies imposed by this Act shall be deposited into a dedicated "Public Water Feature Maintenance Fund" managed by the municipal treasury.
(2) A minimum of 75% of the collected funds must be directly allocated to the physical maintenance, repair, and operational costs of public water features. Up to 12% may be used for administrative costs associated with levy collection and enforcement, and up to 13% for feature enhancements or new installations. This shift prioritizes direct maintenance.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Each municipality shall publish an annual report detailing the collection and expenditure of the Public Water Feature Maintenance Fund.
(2) This report must be made publicly available by June 30th of the following levy period and include a breakdown of funds spent on cleaning, repairs, energy, and administrative overhead. The report should also list significant maintenance projects undertaken in the previous year, promoting transparency.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Enforcement Actions
text:
(1) In the event of persistent non-payment, the municipal authority may take legal action to recover outstanding levy amounts, including penalties and interest.
(2) After 180 days of non-payment, a lien may be placed on the property for the full amount owed, which may affect property transfers. This measure is a last resort to ensure the financial stability of the maintenance fund.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Enforcement Actions
text:
(1) In the event of persistent non-payment, the municipal authority may take legal action to recover outstanding levy amounts, including penalties and interest.
(2) After 120 days of non-payment, a lien may be placed on the property for the full amount owed, which may affect property transfers. This accelerated timeline for lien placement is intended to improve collection rates and reduce the burden on compliant property owners.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Municipal Water Feature Registry
text:
(1) Each municipality shall maintain an up-to-date registry of all public water features within its jurisdiction.
(2) This registry must include details such as location, dimensions, type of feature, and the last major maintenance date. It shall be accessible for public inspection at the municipal office during regular business hours and will be updated quarterly to reflect any new installations or decommissioning of features.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Property Sales and Levies
text:
(1) Any outstanding levies, penalties, and interest remain attached to the property and become the responsibility of the new owner upon transfer of title.
(2) It is the responsibility of the seller to inform prospective buyers of any outstanding public water feature maintenance levies. A certificate of current levy status can be obtained from the municipal levy office for a fee of 50 crowns, valid for 30 days.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Property Sales and Levies
text:
(1) Any outstanding levies, penalties, and interest remain attached to the property and become the responsibility of the new owner upon transfer of title.
(2) It is the responsibility of the seller to inform prospective buyers of any outstanding public water feature maintenance levies. A certificate of current levy status can be obtained from the municipal levy office for a fee of 75 crowns, valid for 45 days. The increased fee covers administrative processing costs.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: New Construction Levy
text:
(1) A one-time public water feature maintenance connection levy of 500 crowns is imposed on all newly constructed residential or commercial properties.
(2) This levy is payable upon the issuance of the occupancy permit and contributes to the expansion and enhancement of public water features that may serve new developments. This ensures that new growth also contributes to the maintenance of public amenities from which residents will benefit.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Commercial Property Rate
text:
(1) Commercial properties are subject to a public water feature maintenance levy at a rate 1.5 times the general levy applicable to residential properties.
(2) This increased rate acknowledges that commercial establishments often benefit from enhanced public aesthetics, drawing customers and increasing property values, and typically have a greater capacity to contribute. This multiplier does not apply to special area levies.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Commercial Property Rate
text:
(1) Commercial properties are subject to a public water feature maintenance levy at a rate 1.75 times the general levy applicable to residential properties.
(2) This increased rate acknowledges that commercial establishments often benefit from enhanced public aesthetics, drawing customers and increasing property values, and typically have a greater capacity to contribute. This multiplier does not apply to special area levies, ensuring fairness in the overall assessment.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Agricultural Property Rate
text:
(1) Properties primarily used for agricultural purposes, covering more than 2 hectares, are subject to a reduced general levy of 50%.
(2) This reduction recognizes that agricultural properties may derive less direct benefit from urban public water features compared to residential or commercial properties. However, they are still subject to any applicable special area levies if they meet the criteria.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Review of Levy Rates
text:
(1) The municipal council shall review all levy rates and exemption thresholds every three years to ensure they remain fair and adequate for the maintenance of public water features.
(2) Any proposed changes to the rates or thresholds must be subject to a public consultation period of at least 60 days before being enacted. This process allows for community input and helps to maintain public support for the levy system.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Review of Levy Rates
text:
(1) The municipal council shall review all levy rates and exemption thresholds every two years to ensure they remain fair and adequate for the maintenance of public water features.
(2) Any proposed changes to the rates or thresholds must be subject to a public consultation period of at least 45 days before being enacted. The increased frequency of review and slightly shorter consultation period are designed to allow for more agile adjustments to economic conditions and maintenance needs.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Voluntary Contributions
text:
(1) Individuals or organizations may make voluntary contributions to the Public Water Feature Maintenance Fund.
(2) These contributions are entirely optional and are separate from the mandatory levies. They can be designated for specific features or for general use. All voluntary contributions will be publicly acknowledged in the annual report, unless anonymity is specifically requested by the contributor.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Maintenance Standards
text:
(1) All public water features are to be maintained to a standard that ensures cleanliness, safety, and proper functionality.
(2) Regular cleaning schedules, determined by feature type and location, must be adhered to, with a minimum of one thorough cleaning every 14 days for high-traffic fountains. Emergency repairs addressing safety hazards must commence within 24 hours of notification, ensuring public well-being.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Maintenance Standards
text:
(1) All public water features are to be maintained to a standard that ensures cleanliness, safety, and proper functionality.
(2) Regular cleaning schedules, determined by feature type and location, must be adhered to, with a minimum of one thorough cleaning every 7 days for high-traffic fountains. Emergency repairs addressing safety hazards must commence within 12 hours of notification, demonstrating a commitment to immediate public safety.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Damage to Public Water Features
text:
(1) Any person or entity found responsible for causing damage to a public water feature shall be liable for the full cost of repairs.
(2) This liability is separate from any criminal charges that may be filed. The municipal authority will assess the damage and issue an invoice for repair costs, which must be paid within 30 days. Failure to pay may result in legal action to recover the costs.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Use of Public Water Features
text:
(1) Public water features are intended for aesthetic enjoyment and passive recreation only.
(2) Direct contact with the water, such as bathing or wading, is prohibited in most features unless specifically designated for such use by clear signage. Deposit of litter or foreign objects into water features is strictly forbidden, with fines up to 500 crowns for violations.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Use of Public Water Features
text:
(1) Public water features are intended for aesthetic enjoyment and passive recreation only.
(2) Direct contact with the water, such as bathing or wading, is prohibited in most features unless specifically designated for such use by clear signage. Deposit of litter or foreign objects into water features is strictly forbidden, with fines up to 750 crowns for violations. This increase in penalty reflects the rising cost of specialized cleaning and repair.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Public Notification of Works
text:
(1) The municipal authority must provide public notification at least 7 days in advance of any planned major maintenance or repair works on a public water feature.
(2) This notification should include the estimated duration of the disruption and any potential impact on public access. For emergency repairs, notification should be issued as soon as practically possible, within 24 hours of work commencing.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Consultation for New Features
text:
(1) Before installing any new public water feature, the municipal authority must conduct a public consultation process.
(2) This process includes public meetings and a comment period of at least 45 days, allowing residents to provide feedback on proposed designs, locations, and potential impacts. This ensures community involvement in the development of new public amenities.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Water Conservation Measures
text:
(1) All public water features must incorporate water conservation measures where technically feasible and economically viable.
(2) This includes the use of recirculating pump systems, efficient filtration, and the implementation of automatic shut-off systems during periods of heavy rainfall. The goal is to minimize water waste and promote environmental responsibility in their operation.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) The municipal levy office shall keep detailed records of all levy assessments, payments, exemptions, and arrears for a minimum period of 7 years.
(2) These records are essential for audit purposes and for resolving any disputes related to levy payments. Access to these records is restricted to authorized personnel, ensuring data privacy and security.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) All personal and financial information collected for the purpose of levy assessment and exemption applications shall be treated with strict confidentiality.
(2) Such information shall not be disclosed to third parties without the express written consent of the property owner, except as required by law or for the purpose of debt collection as outlined in section 15. This commitment to privacy is paramount.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Delegation of Authority
text:
(1) The municipal council may delegate specific administrative functions related to levy collection and enforcement to a designated municipal department or officer.
(2) This delegation must be formally approved by a council resolution and clearly define the scope of authority granted. The ultimate oversight and accountability for the proper administration of this Act remain with the municipal council, ensuring proper governance.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Transition Provisions
text:
(1) For the initial levy period commencing January 1st, 2018, all assessment notices shall be issued by January 15th, 2018, with the first installment due by March 31st, 2018.
(2) Existing municipal regulations regarding public water feature maintenance shall remain in effect until superseded by provisions of this Act or subsequent municipal bylaws enacted to implement this Act. This ensures a smooth transition to the new levy system.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Regulations

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Repeal of Obsolete Sections
text: This section outlines the process for repealing outdated or irrelevant provisions of this Act. Any section found to be no longer applicable or contradictory to newer legislation will be formally repealed through an amendment to this Act, ensuring the legislative framework remains current and efficient. A public review process will precede any such repeal, allowing for community input on proposed changes.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Repeal of Obsolete Sections
text: (Repealed.)

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Special categories
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered certified wine taster shall instead pay a fixed allowance of 5 crowns instead of the fee or allowance outlined in SBA §8.

act_title: Public Water Feature Maintenance Levies Act
heading: Particular persons
text: The electric scooter registration fee is reduced to 5 crowns for any person who is a registered piano restorer.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating activities with potential environmental impact within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to protect natural resources, maintain ecological balance, and safeguard public health by controlling and mitigating pollution. The Act applies to all industrial, commercial, and agricultural operations that discharge pollutants into air, water, or soil, or generate significant waste streams. It mandates that such operations obtain a Pollution Control Permit, ensuring compliance with established environmental standards and best practices. The scope extends across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) Any person or entity planning to undertake an activity that may cause environmental pollution must obtain a Pollution Control Permit from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) prior to commencing operations.
(2) This requirement applies if the activity involves the discharge of more than 50 cubic meters of wastewater per day, emits more than 10 kilograms of sulfur dioxide per month, or generates over 200 kilograms of hazardous waste per year.
(3) Failure to obtain a required permit will result in a fine of 5,000 crowns for each month of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 60,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) Any person or entity planning to undertake an activity that may cause environmental pollution must obtain a Pollution Control Permit from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) prior to commencing operations.
(2) This requirement applies if the activity involves the discharge of more than 40 cubic meters of wastewater per day, emits more than 8 kilograms of sulfur dioxide per month, or generates over 150 kilograms of hazardous waste per year.
(3) Failure to obtain a required permit will result in a fine of 7,500 crowns for each month of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 90,000 crowns.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for a Pollution Control Permit must be submitted to the EPA at least 90 days before the planned commencement of the activity.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) A detailed description of the proposed activity and its location.
(b) An assessment of potential environmental impacts.
(c) Proposed measures for pollution control and mitigation.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 1,000 crowns.
(3) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 15 days, requiring resubmission and potentially delaying the process.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for a Pollution Control Permit must be submitted to the EPA at least 120 days before the planned commencement of the activity.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) A detailed description of the proposed activity and its location, including a geographical coordinates reference.
(b) An assessment of potential environmental impacts, including cumulative effects.
(c) Proposed measures for pollution control and mitigation, with a 5-year projection.
(d) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns.
(3) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 days, requiring resubmission and potentially delaying the process significantly.

heading: Application Review Process
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the EPA will conduct a thorough review within 60 days.
(2) The review process involves:
(a) Evaluation of the proposed pollution control measures against national standards.
(b) Consultation with relevant experts and, if necessary, local authorities.
(c) Site visits to assess the environmental context of the proposed activity.
(3) The EPA may request additional information from the applicant within 30 days of initial submission. The applicant must provide this information within 20 days.

heading: Application Review Process
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the EPA will conduct a thorough review within 75 days.
(2) The review process involves:
(a) Evaluation of the proposed pollution control measures against national and international best practice standards.
(b) Consultation with relevant experts, local authorities, and affected communities within a 5-kilometer radius.
(c) Site visits to assess the environmental context of the proposed activity, conducted by at least two independent inspectors.
(3) The EPA may request additional information from the applicant within 25 days of initial submission. The applicant must provide this information within 15 days, failing which the application may be rejected.

heading: Public Notice and Comment
text:
