(1) For all applications deemed significant, the EPA shall publish a public notice within 10 days of completing its initial review.
(2) The notice will be published in at least one widely circulated newspaper in the affected municipality and on the EPA's official website.
(3) The public will have a period of 30 days from the date of publication to submit written comments or objections regarding the proposed activity.
(4) All comments received will be considered by the EPA before making a final decision on the permit application.

heading: Permit Decision
text:
(1) The EPA shall make a decision on the permit application within 30 days after the close of the public comment period, or within 90 days if no public notice was required.
(2) Permits may be:
(a) Granted, with specific conditions and limitations.
(b) Granted, with modifications to the proposed activity or control measures.
(c) Denied, if the activity poses an unacceptable risk to the environment or public health.
(3) A notice of decision, including reasons for the decision, will be issued to the applicant within 7 days of the decision date.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Every Pollution Control Permit shall include specific conditions tailored to the nature of the permitted activity and its potential environmental impact.
(2) These conditions may include:
(a) Emission limits for specific pollutants, such as 25 ppm for nitrogen oxides or 0.5 mg/L for heavy metals in wastewater.
(b) Requirements for specific pollution control technologies, such as electrostatic precipitators or biological treatment plants.
(c) Monitoring and reporting requirements, including daily readings and quarterly reports.
(d) Waste management protocols, specifying disposal methods for at least 95% of generated waste.
(3) Non-compliance with any permit condition may lead to revocation of the permit.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Every Pollution Control Permit shall include specific conditions tailored to the nature of the permitted activity and its potential environmental impact, revised every 3 years.
(2) These conditions may include:
(a) Emission limits for specific pollutants, such as 20 ppm for nitrogen oxides or 0.2 mg/L for heavy metals in wastewater, enforced by continuous monitoring.
(b) Requirements for specific pollution control technologies, such as advanced oxidation processes or multi-stage filtration systems.
(c) Enhanced monitoring and reporting requirements, including hourly readings and monthly reports submitted electronically.
(d) Waste management protocols, specifying circular economy approaches and aiming for at least 98% waste reduction or recycling.
(3) Non-compliance with any permit condition may lead to immediate suspension and potential revocation of the permit, alongside penalties.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text:
(1) A Pollution Control Permit is valid for a period of 5 years from its date of issue.
(2) An application for permit renewal must be submitted at least 180 days before the expiry date of the current permit.
(3) The renewal application will undergo a review process similar to an initial application, but with a focus on past compliance history and updated environmental standards.
(4) A renewal fee of 750 crowns is required with the application. If the application is submitted less than 90 days before expiry, a late fee of 500 crowns will be applied.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text:
(1) A Pollution Control Permit is valid for a period of 4 years from its date of issue.
(2) An application for permit renewal must be submitted at least 210 days before the expiry date of the current permit.
(3) The renewal application will undergo a comprehensive review process, including an updated environmental impact assessment, with a strong emphasis on continuous improvement and adherence to the latest environmental standards.
(4) A renewal fee of 1,200 crowns is required with the application. If the application is submitted less than 120 days before expiry, a late fee of 800 crowns will be applied.

heading: Permit Transferability
text:
(1) A Pollution Control Permit is generally not transferable to another person or entity.
(2) In exceptional circumstances, such as a change of ownership of the permitted facility, an application for transfer may be submitted to the EPA.
(3) The new owner must apply for a transfer within 30 days of the change of ownership and demonstrate the capacity to comply with all existing permit conditions.
(4) A transfer fee of 2,000 crowns is payable upon application. The EPA will review the application within 45 days.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text:
(1) The EPA shall conduct regular monitoring and inspections of all permitted activities to ensure compliance with permit conditions and environmental regulations.
(2) Inspections will occur at least once every 12 months for high-risk activities and every 24 months for medium-risk activities.
(3) Authorized EPA officers have the right to enter any premises subject to a permit at reasonable times, without prior notice, to conduct inspections, collect samples, and access records.
(4) Any obstruction of an EPA officer in the performance of their duties is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all monitoring data, inspection reports, and pollution control measures.
(2) These records must be kept on-site for a minimum of 3 years and be made available to EPA officers upon request within 24 hours.
(3) Records should include details of any incidents, malfunctions, or breaches of permit conditions, along with corrective actions taken within 72 hours of discovery.
(4) Falsification of records is a serious offense, carrying a penalty of 15,000 crowns and potential permit revocation.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to submit regular reports to the EPA detailing their compliance with permit conditions and environmental performance.
(2) For activities with significant environmental impact, quarterly reports are mandatory, due within 30 days after the end of each quarter.
(3) For activities with moderate impact, semi-annual reports are required, due within 45 days after the end of each reporting period.
(4) Any non-compliance or environmental incident must be reported to the EPA within 24 hours of its occurrence, followed by a detailed written report within 5 days.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to submit regular reports to the EPA detailing their compliance with permit conditions and environmental performance, utilizing the EPA's designated online portal.
(2) For activities with significant environmental impact, monthly reports are mandatory, due within 15 days after the end of each month.
(3) For activities with moderate impact, quarterly reports are required, due within 20 days after the end of each reporting period.
(4) Any non-compliance or environmental incident must be reported to the EPA immediately, within 4 hours of its discovery, followed by a detailed written report within 24 hours via the online portal.

heading: Enforcement Actions
text:
(1) The EPA has the authority to take enforcement actions against permit holders who fail to comply with the provisions of this Act or their permit conditions.
(2) Enforcement actions may include:
(a) Issuance of warning letters for minor infractions.
(b) Imposition of administrative fines, ranging from 1,000 to 50,000 crowns per violation.
(c) Issuance of compliance orders requiring specific actions to rectify non-compliance within a set timeframe, typically 30 days.
(d) Suspension or revocation of the Pollution Control Permit.
(3) For serious or repeated violations, the EPA may initiate legal proceedings.

heading: Administrative Fines
text:
(1) Administrative fines may be imposed for various infractions, with the specific amount determined by the severity and duration of the violation.
(2) Fines for minor reporting errors may start at 500 crowns per instance.
(3) Fines for exceeding emission limits by less than 10% may range from 5,000 to 20,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.
(4) Fines for unauthorized discharges resulting in environmental damage can be up to 100,000 crowns per incident, plus remediation costs. Repeated offenses within a 12-month period incur double the initial fine.

heading: Administrative Fines
text:
(1) Administrative fines may be imposed for various infractions, with the specific amount determined by the severity, duration, and environmental impact of the violation.
(2) Fines for minor reporting errors may start at 750 crowns per instance, and increase by 100 crowns for each subsequent error within a quarter.
(3) Fines for exceeding emission limits by less than 10% may range from 7,500 to 30,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.
(4) Fines for unauthorized discharges resulting in environmental damage can be up to 150,000 crowns per incident, plus full remediation costs. Repeated offenses within a 24-month period incur triple the initial fine.

heading: Compliance Orders
text:
(1) A compliance order specifies actions that a permit holder must take to rectify a violation within a specified period.
(2) Failure to comply with a compliance order within 30 days may result in additional fines of 2,000 crowns per day of non-compliance, up to a maximum of 60,000 crowns.
(3) The order may require:
(a) Installation of new pollution control equipment.
(b) Implementation of improved operational procedures.
(c) Remediation of environmental damage caused by the violation.
(4) The EPA may perform the required actions and recover costs from the permit holder if the order is not met.

heading: Permit Suspension and Revocation
text:
(1) A Pollution Control Permit may be suspended for serious or repeated non-compliance with permit conditions or this Act.
(2) Suspension typically lasts for a period of 60 days, during which the permit holder must cease the polluting activity and implement corrective measures.
(3) A permit may be revoked if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with a suspension order.
(b) There is persistent and egregious non-compliance.
(c) The activity poses an imminent and severe threat to public health or the environment.
(4) Upon revocation, all operations related to the permit must cease immediately, and the permit holder may be prohibited from applying for a new permit for a period of 2 years.

heading: Permit Suspension and Revocation
text:
(1) A Pollution Control Permit may be suspended immediately for serious or repeated non-compliance with permit conditions or this Act, or for any unauthorized discharge posing significant risk.
(2) Suspension typically lasts for a period of 90 days, during which the permit holder must cease the polluting activity and demonstrate full implementation of corrective measures, verified by an independent audit.
(3) A permit may be revoked if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with a suspension order within 10 days.
(b) There is persistent and egregious non-compliance, defined as 3 or more significant violations within a 12-month period.
(c) The activity poses an imminent and severe threat to public health or the environment, as determined by an emergency assessment.
(4) Upon revocation, all operations related to the permit must cease immediately, and the permit holder may be prohibited from applying for a new permit for a period of 5 years. A public notice of revocation will be issued within 7 days.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the EPA regarding a permit application, permit condition, or enforcement action may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Environmental Appeals Board (EAB) within 30 days of receiving the EPA's decision.
(3) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and include all relevant supporting documentation.
(4) The EAB will review the appeal and make a determination within 60 days. The decision of the EAB is final.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In cases of imminent and severe environmental pollution or threat to public health, the EPA may take immediate action to prevent or mitigate harm.
(2) These emergency powers include:
(a) Issuing emergency orders to cease operations or take specific remedial actions.
(b) Directing clean-up operations, with costs recoverable from the responsible party.
(c) Entering private property without a warrant to address the emergency.
(3) Any emergency action taken shall be valid for a period not exceeding 14 days, unless extended by judicial order.
(4) The EPA must notify affected parties within 24 hours of exercising emergency powers.

heading: Offenses and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly or negligently causes environmental pollution without a permit, or in violation of a permit, commits an offense.
(2) Upon conviction, an individual may face a fine of up to 200,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 1 year, or both.
(3) A corporate entity may face a fine of up to 1,000,000 crowns for similar offenses.
(4) Each day an offense continues constitutes a separate offense. If the pollution causes significant and irreversible damage, penalties may be increased by up to 50%.

heading: Offenses and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly or negligently causes environmental pollution without a permit, or in violation of a permit, or fails to report an incident, commits an offense.
(2) Upon conviction, an individual may face a fine of up to 300,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or both. Directors or senior managers may be held personally liable.
(3) A corporate entity may face a fine of up to 2,000,000 crowns for similar offenses, or 5% of its annual turnover, whichever is greater.
(4) Each day an offense continues constitutes a separate offense. If the pollution causes significant and irreversible damage, penalties may be increased by up to 100%, and mandatory remediation orders will be issued.

heading: Remediation and Restoration
text:
(1) Any person or entity responsible for environmental pollution must bear the full cost of remediation and restoration of the affected environment.
(2) The EPA will determine the scope and extent of remediation required, based on scientific assessments and best available techniques.
(3) If the responsible party fails to undertake remediation, the EPA may carry out the work and recover all costs, plus a 15% administrative fee, from the responsible party.
(4) A remediation plan must be submitted to the EPA within 30 days of a pollution incident causing significant harm, with implementation commencing within 60 days of approval.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) For activities posing a high risk of environmental pollution, the EPA may require a financial guarantee to cover potential remediation costs.
(2) The guarantee may take the form of a bank guarantee, an insurance policy, or a dedicated escrow account.
(3) The amount of the financial guarantee will be determined by the EPA, based on an assessment of environmental risk and potential remediation costs, ranging from 50,000 crowns to 5,000,000 crowns.
(4) The guarantee must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit and for a period of 2 years after cessation of the activity.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) For all activities posing a high or medium risk of environmental pollution, the EPA shall require a financial guarantee to cover potential remediation costs.
(2) The guarantee may take the form of a bank guarantee, an environmental liability insurance policy from an approved provider, or a dedicated escrow account, verified annually.
(3) The amount of the financial guarantee will be determined by the EPA, based on an updated assessment of environmental risk and potential remediation costs, ranging from 100,000 crowns to 10,000,000 crowns, and reviewed every 3 years.
(4) The guarantee must be maintained for the entire duration of the permit and for a period of 5 years after cessation of the activity, ensuring complete environmental recovery.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) Information submitted to the EPA in a permit application or report is generally considered public information.
(2) An applicant may request certain information to be treated as confidential if its disclosure would cause significant commercial harm.
(3) The EPA will review such requests and determine within 30 days whether the information qualifies for confidential treatment, based on strict criteria.
(4) Information relating to pollutant emissions, discharges, or waste generation will never be treated as confidential.

heading: Data Management
text:
(1) The EPA shall establish and maintain a centralized database of all Pollution Control Permits, monitoring data, and enforcement actions.
(2) This database will be accessible to the public, with appropriate safeguards for genuinely confidential commercial information.
(3) Data shall be retained for a minimum period of 10 years after a permit expires or is revoked.
(4) The EPA will publish an annual report summarizing environmental performance and compliance rates across Nordvale.

heading: Training and Certification
text:
(1) Operators of certain high-risk pollution control equipment must undergo certified training.
(2) The EPA will specify the types of equipment and activities requiring certified operators, and approve training providers.
(3) Certification must be renewed every 3 years through refresher courses.
(4) Any facility operating without the required certified personnel will face a fine of 10,000 crowns per month of non-compliance.

heading: Research and Development
text:
(1) The EPA shall promote and support research and development into new and improved pollution control technologies and practices.
(2) A portion of collected fines, not exceeding 10%, will be allocated to a dedicated fund for environmental research.
(3) The EPA may collaborate with academic institutions and private companies on joint research projects.
(4) Permit holders are encouraged to adopt innovative technologies that demonstrate a 20% or more reduction in pollution compared to conventional methods.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Existing facilities that would require a Pollution Control Permit under this Act must apply for a permit within 180 days of the Act's commencement.
(2) During this transitional period, existing facilities may continue operations, provided they submit a declaration of intent to comply and a preliminary environmental assessment.
(3) Facilities that fail to submit an application within the specified timeframe will be deemed to be operating without a permit and subject to enforcement actions.
(4) The EPA will prioritize review of applications from existing facilities.

heading: Review of Standards
text:
(1) The EPA shall periodically review and update environmental quality standards and emission limits set forth in this Act.
(2) Reviews will occur at least once every 5 years, or more frequently if new scientific evidence or international best practices emerge.
(3) Any proposed changes to standards will undergo a public consultation process for a period of 60 days before being finalized.
(4) The aim is to achieve continuous improvement in environmental protection, targeting an annual 2% reduction in overall pollutant load.

heading: Review of Standards
text:
(1) The EPA shall periodically review and update environmental quality standards and emission limits set forth in this Act, incorporating the latest technological advancements.
(2) Reviews will occur at least once every 3 years, or more frequently if new scientific evidence, international best practices, or significant environmental incidents emerge.
(3) Any proposed changes to standards will undergo a public consultation process for a period of 90 days, including stakeholder workshops, before being finalized.
(4) The aim is to achieve continuous improvement in environmental protection, targeting an annual 3% reduction in overall pollutant load and a 1% improvement in ecosystem health indicators.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text:
(1) The EPA shall cooperate with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale on matters relating to pollution control.
(2) Municipalities may provide recommendations on permit applications for activities within their jurisdiction, which the EPA will consider within 20 days.
(3) The EPA may delegate certain monitoring or initial inspection functions to municipal environmental departments, subject to formal agreements and capacity assessments.
(4) Joint enforcement actions may be undertaken in specific instances, with responsibilities and cost-sharing agreed upon in advance.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) For new projects exceeding a certain size or environmental sensitivity, a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is mandatory.
(2) The thresholds for requiring an EIA include projects affecting more than 10 hectares of land, or those expected to increase regional air pollutant emissions by more than 5%.
(3) The EIA report must be prepared by an independent, accredited consultant and submitted with the permit application.
(4) The EPA will review the EIA for thoroughness and accuracy, involving a 45-day public review period.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
(1) Subject to subsection (4) of section 21, all permit applications, issued permits, monitoring reports, and enforcement actions are public documents.
(2) These documents will be made available for public inspection at the EPA's main office during regular business hours.
(3) Digital copies of key documents will be accessible on the EPA's website, updated monthly.
(4) A reasonable fee, not exceeding 5 crowns per page, may be charged for physical copies of extensive documents.

heading: Pollution Prevention Plans
text:
(1) Permit holders for activities generating more than 500 kilograms of hazardous waste annually must develop and implement a Pollution Prevention Plan.
(2) The plan must identify sources of pollution, set specific reduction targets (e.g., 10% reduction in waste by volume over 2 years), and outline strategies to achieve these targets.
(3) The Pollution Prevention Plan must be submitted to the EPA for approval within 6 months of permit issuance and updated every 3 years.
(4) Failure to submit an approved plan may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and a compliance order.

heading: Pollution Prevention Plans
text:
(1) Permit holders for activities generating more than 300 kilograms of hazardous waste annually or consuming more than 10,000 cubic meters of water annually must develop and implement a comprehensive Pollution Prevention Plan.
(2) The plan must identify all sources of pollution, set ambitious reduction targets (e.g., 15% reduction in waste by volume and 7% reduction in water consumption over 2 years), and outline detailed strategies, including technological upgrades, to achieve these targets.
(3) The Pollution Prevention Plan must be submitted to the EPA for approval within 3 months of permit issuance and updated every 2 years, with demonstrable progress reports.
(4) Failure to submit an approved plan or demonstrate sufficient progress may result in a fine of 10,000 crowns, a mandatory compliance order, and a public notice of non-compliance.

heading: Best Available Techniques (BAT)
text:
(1) Permit conditions shall, where practicable, require the use of Best Available Techniques (BAT) for pollution control.
(2) BAT refers to the most effective and advanced stage in the development of activities and their methods of operation, which indicates the practical suitability of particular techniques for providing in principle the basis for emission limit values.
(3) The EPA will publish guidance documents on BAT for various industrial sectors, updated every 4 years.
(4) Permit holders are expected to review and, where economically feasible, adopt newer BAT as they become available, aiming for a 3% improvement in efficiency annually.

heading: Best Available Techniques (BAT)
text:
(1) Permit conditions shall mandate the use of Best Available Techniques (BAT) for pollution control, with specific implementation timelines.
(2) BAT refers to the most effective and advanced stage in the development of activities and their methods of operation, which indicates the practical suitability of particular techniques for providing in principle the basis for stringent emission limit values and overall environmental protection, considering economic viability.
(3) The EPA will regularly publish and update comprehensive guidance documents on BAT for various industrial sectors, with mandatory reviews every 2 years.
(4) Permit holders are expected to continuously review and adopt newer BAT as they become available, aiming for a 5% improvement in efficiency annually and demonstrating this through independent audits every 18 months.

heading: Site Decommissioning Plans
text:
(1) For activities involving significant environmental risk or long-term operations, a Site Decommissioning Plan must be submitted with the permit application.
(2) The plan must detail how the site will be safely closed, pollutants contained, and the land restored to an environmentally sound condition after operations cease.
(3) The plan must include a cost estimate for decommissioning, which will inform the required financial guarantee as per section 20.
(4) The plan must be reviewed and updated every 5 years, or whenever there are significant changes to the site or operations.

heading: Cost Recovery
text:
(1) The EPA may recover all costs incurred in connection with issuing, administering, monitoring, and enforcing permits under this Act from the permit holders.
(2) These costs include application fees, annual administrative fees (e.g., 500 crowns for low-risk, 2,500 crowns for high-risk permits), inspection fees (e.g., 1,000 crowns per inspection), and enforcement costs.
(3) Unpaid fees or costs will accrue interest at a rate of 5% per annum after 30 days past due.
(4) The EPA may take legal action to recover outstanding amounts.

heading: Technical Guidance Documents
text:
(1) The EPA shall develop and publish technical guidance documents to assist permit applicants and holders in complying with this Act.
(2) These documents will cover topics such as best available monitoring techniques, specific emission limits for certain industries, and detailed reporting formats.
(3) Guidance documents will be regularly updated, at least every 2 years, to reflect new regulations and scientific advancements.
(4) Compliance with guidance documents is strongly recommended and may be considered during permit review and enforcement actions.

heading: Environmental Audits
text:
(1) Certain high-risk permit holders may be required to conduct independent environmental audits every 3 years.
(2) The audit report must be submitted to the EPA within 30 days of its completion.
(3) The audit must assess compliance with permit conditions, the effectiveness of environmental management systems, and opportunities for pollution reduction.
(4) Facilities found to have significant deficiencies in their audit may incur an additional annual administrative fee of 1,500 crowns until rectified.

heading: Protection of Sensitive Areas
text:
(1) Activities proposed within 500 meters of designated environmentally sensitive areas (e.g., nature reserves, wetlands) will be subject to stricter permit conditions.
(2) The EPA maintains a registry of all environmentally sensitive areas, updated annually.
(3) Permit applications for such areas will require a more detailed environmental impact assessment and a higher level of financial guarantee.
(4) In some cases, activities within 100 meters of highly sensitive areas may be prohibited entirely to prevent irreversible damage.

heading: Sustainable Practices Incentive
text:
(1) The EPA may offer incentives for permit holders who adopt sustainable practices that go beyond minimum compliance requirements.
(2) Incentives may include reduced annual administrative fees (up to 20% reduction) or priority processing for permit renewals.
(3) To qualify, facilities must demonstrate a consistent reduction in pollutant generation by at least 15% over a 3-year period.
(4) An application for incentive qualification must be submitted annually, along with supporting data.

heading: Definition of Pollutant
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, 'pollutant' means any substance or energy form which, when discharged, emitted, or deposited into the environment, has or may have an adverse effect on human health, the environment, or property.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, solid waste, liquid effluents, gaseous emissions, noise, vibration, heat, and radiation.
(3) The EPA shall publish a detailed list of regulated pollutants and their respective thresholds, updated biannually.
(4) Substances not on the list but demonstrated to be harmful may still be regulated on a case-by-case basis.

heading: Definition of Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
text:
(1) The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is the primary regulatory body responsible for implementing and enforcing this Act.
(2) The EPA is an independent agency of the Nordvale government, comprised of environmental scientists, engineers, and legal experts.
(3) The EPA is headquartered in Aldmark and maintains regional offices in Brenholt, Corvik, and Lund Vale.
(4) The Director-General of the EPA is appointed by the Council of Nordvale for a term of 5 years.

heading: Consultation with Indigenous Communities
text:
(1) Where a proposed activity may affect the traditional lands or cultural heritage of Indigenous communities, the EPA shall ensure meaningful consultation.
(2) Consultation must occur at the earliest possible stage of the permit application process, prior to public notice.
(3) The permit application must include a report detailing the consultation process and how Indigenous concerns have been addressed.
(4) The EPA will give significant weight to documented concerns and traditional ecological knowledge provided by Indigenous communities, with a minimum 60-day consultation period.

heading: Ethical Conduct of Officials
text:
(1) All officials involved in the administration and enforcement of this Act must adhere to a strict code of ethical conduct.
(2) This includes avoiding conflicts of interest, maintaining impartiality, and upholding the highest standards of integrity.
(3) Any allegations of misconduct against EPA officials will be thoroughly investigated by an independent ethics committee.
(4) Officials found to be in breach of the code of conduct may face disciplinary action, including dismissal and criminal prosecution if applicable.

heading: Annual Environmental Report
text:
(1) The EPA shall publish an Annual Environmental Report by March 31st of each year.
(2) The report will summarize the state of the environment in Nordvale, pollution trends, and the effectiveness of this Act in achieving its objectives.
(3) It will include data on permit issuance, compliance rates, enforcement actions, and significant environmental incidents.
(4) The report will also identify emerging environmental challenges and recommend policy adjustments for the upcoming 12-month period.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text:
(1) The Environmental Protection Ordinance of 1995 is hereby repealed.
(2) Any permits issued under the Environmental Protection Ordinance of 1995 shall remain valid until their expiry date, subject to the provisions of this Act.
(3) All legal proceedings initiated under the repealed ordinance shall continue under the provisions of that ordinance until their conclusion.
(4) References to the repealed ordinance in any other enactment shall be construed as references to this Act.

heading: Repeal of Previous Legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered violin maker has 30 extra days to pay the fee or allowance specified in HSA §2.

heading: Exemptions
text: For a registered cartographer, the outstanding balance of any study loan, as described in this statute, shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Meaning of hired-car conveyance
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "hired-car conveyance" means a journey in a vehicle that holds a taxi licence and is hired for that journey.
(2) The price of a hired-car conveyance is the total shown on the taximeter at the end of the journey.

heading: Senior fairway conductors as passengers for hire
text:
(1) No amount for the beginning of the journey may be charged to a senior fairway conductor for a hired-car conveyance.
(2) Subsection (1) is applied after any other rule on the price of the conveyance.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing and regulation of public weighbridges within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure accuracy and fairness in the measurement of vehicle loads for commercial and regulatory purposes. This includes setting standards for operation, maintenance, and the qualifications of weighbridge operators. All public weighbridges, regardless of ownership, must comply with the provisions outlined herein to operate legally within any municipality of Nordvale. The scope extends to all aspects of public weighbridge use, from initial application to ongoing compliance and enforcement actions.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Public weighbridge' means any weighing device used for determining the weight of vehicles and their loads, offered for public use, whether for a fee or free of charge.
(2) 'Operator' means any individual responsible for the day-to-day operation of a public weighbridge, including recording weights and issuing weight tickets.
(3) 'Licence' means a permit issued by the Nordvale Department of Weights and Measures allowing the operation of a public weighbridge.
(4) 'Department' refers to the Nordvale Department of Weights and Measures.

heading: Requirement for licence
text: No person or entity may operate a public weighbridge within Nordvale without a valid licence issued by the Department. Any weighbridge found operating without a current and valid licence may be subject to immediate closure and penalties as outlined in section 29. A grace period of 30 days is allowed for licence renewals, provided an application for renewal has been submitted prior to the expiry date. Operating a weighbridge during this grace period without a submitted renewal application is prohibited.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An application for a public weighbridge licence must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include:
(a) Details of the weighbridge location, including its municipal address.
(b) Specifications of the weighbridge equipment, including its maximum capacity and manufacturer.
(c) Proof of calibration by an accredited service within the last 6 months.
(d) The names and qualifications of all proposed operators.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Licence term and renewal
text: A public weighbridge licence is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the current licence expires. The renewal fee is 300 crowns. If a renewal application is submitted less than 30 days before expiry, an additional late fee of 100 crowns will be applied. Licences not renewed within 90 days of expiry will be considered lapsed, requiring a new application process.

heading: Licence term and renewal (amended)
text: A public weighbridge licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the current licence expires. The renewal fee is 350 crowns. If a renewal application is submitted less than 45 days before expiry, an additional late fee of 150 crowns will be applied. Licences not renewed within 120 days of expiry will be considered lapsed, requiring a new application process.

heading: Licence term and renewal (amended)
text: A public weighbridge licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the current licence expires. The renewal fee is 380 crowns. If a renewal application is submitted less than 45 days before expiry, an additional late fee of 180 crowns will be applied. Licences not renewed within 120 days of expiry will be considered lapsed, requiring a new application process. A reminder will be sent 120 days prior to expiry.

heading: Weighbridge specifications
text:
(1) All public weighbridges must have a maximum capacity of at least 30,000 kilograms.
(2) The weighbridge platform must be at least 18 metres long and 3 metres wide.
(3) The display unit must be clearly visible to both the operator and the vehicle driver.
(4) The weighbridge must be capable of displaying weights in increments of no more than 20 kilograms.

heading: Operator qualifications
text:
(1) Every individual operating a public weighbridge must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) Operators must successfully complete a Department-approved training course on weighbridge operation and record-keeping.
(3) A valid operator certificate, issued by the Department, must be held by all individuals operating the weighbridge.
(4) Certificates are valid for 5 years and must be renewed by undertaking a refresher course.

heading: Operator qualifications (amended)
text:
(1) Every individual operating a public weighbridge must be at least 20 years of age.
(2) Operators must successfully complete a Department-approved training course on weighbridge operation and record-keeping, achieving a minimum score of 75% on the final assessment.
(3) A valid operator certificate, issued by the Department, must be held by all individuals operating the weighbridge.
(4) Certificates are valid for 4 years and must be renewed by undertaking a refresher course and passing a short examination.

heading: Operator qualifications (amended)
text:
(1) Every individual operating a public weighbridge must be at least 20 years of age and hold a valid Class B Nordvale driving licence.
(2) Operators must successfully complete a Department-approved training course on weighbridge operation and record-keeping, achieving a minimum score of 80% on the final assessment.
(3) A valid operator certificate, issued by the Department, must be held by all individuals operating the weighbridge.
(4) Certificates are valid for 4 years and must be renewed by undertaking a refresher course and passing a short examination. The cost for the refresher course is 200 crowns.

heading: Maintenance and calibration
text:
(1) Each licensed weighbridge must be calibrated by a Department-approved technician at least once every 12 months.
(2) Records of all maintenance and calibration activities must be kept for a minimum of 3 years.
(3) The accuracy of the weighbridge must be within ±0.05% of the measured load.
(4) Any repair work affecting the accuracy of the weighbridge requires immediate re-calibration.

heading: Maintenance and calibration (amended)
text:
(1) Each licensed weighbridge must be calibrated by a Department-approved technician at least once every 9 months.
(2) Records of all maintenance and calibration activities must be kept for a minimum of 4 years.
(3) The accuracy of the weighbridge must be within ±0.03% of the measured load for loads exceeding 10,000 kilograms.
(4) Any repair work affecting the accuracy of the weighbridge requires immediate re-calibration and notification to the Department within 48 hours.

heading: Maintenance and calibration (amended)
text:
(1) Each licensed weighbridge must be calibrated by a Department-approved technician at least once every 9 months. An additional spot check calibration may be required by the Department.
(2) Records of all maintenance and calibration activities must be kept for a minimum of 5 years and made available for inspection within 24 hours.
(3) The accuracy of the weighbridge must be within ±0.02% of the measured load for loads exceeding 10,000 kilograms and ±0.05% for loads below this threshold.
(4) Any repair work affecting the accuracy of the weighbridge requires immediate re-calibration by an approved technician and notification to the Department within 24 hours via an online portal.

heading: Weighing procedure
text:
(1) Vehicles must be positioned centrally on the weighbridge platform.
(2) The engine of the vehicle must be switched off during the weighing process.
(3) The operator must ensure no other objects are on the weighbridge during weighing.
(4) A tare weight must be obtained for unloaded vehicles if required for net weight calculation.
(5) The weight must be stable for at least 5 seconds before recording.

heading: Issuance of weight tickets
text:
(1) Upon completion of a weighing, the operator must issue a weight ticket to the driver.
(2) The weight ticket must include:
(a) The licence number of the weighbridge.
(b) The date and time of weighing.
(c) The gross weight, tare weight (if applicable), and net weight in kilograms.
(d) The vehicle registration number.
(e) The name or identification of the operator.
(f) A unique ticket number.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) A log of all weighings must be maintained by the licence holder.
(2) The log must contain all information required on a weight ticket, as per section 13.
(3) These records must be kept for a minimum of 2 years from the date of weighing.
(4) Records must be made available for inspection by Department officials upon request within 2 business days.

heading: Record keeping (amended)
text:
(1) A log of all weighings must be maintained by the licence holder, either in physical or electronic format.
(2) The log must contain all information required on a weight ticket, as per section 13, and additionally the type of goods being weighed.
(3) These records must be kept for a minimum of 3 years from the date of weighing.
(4) Records must be made available for inspection by Department officials upon request within 24 hours. Electronic records must be exportable in a standard format.

heading: Record keeping (amended)
text:
(1) A digital log of all weighings must be maintained by the licence holder, uploaded to the Department's secure portal within 24 hours of each weighing.
(2) The log must contain all information required on a weight ticket, as per section 13, and additionally the type of goods being weighed and the origin/destination municipality if known.
(3) These records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years from the date of weighing, both locally and on the Department's system.
(4) Records must be accessible for inspection by Department officials at any time through the portal. Manual log entries are permitted only in case of system failure, with immediate notification to the Department.

heading: Fees for weighing services
text:
(1) The maximum fee for a single vehicle weighing (determining gross weight) is 150 crowns.
(2) The maximum fee for a weigh-in/weigh-out service (gross and tare weight) is 250 crowns.
(3) These fees must be clearly displayed at the weighbridge location.
(4) No additional surcharges may be applied for issuing a weight ticket or for basic record-keeping.

heading: Fees for weighing services (amended)
text:
(1) The maximum fee for a single vehicle weighing (determining gross weight) is 180 crowns.
(2) The maximum fee for a weigh-in/weigh-out service (gross and tare weight) is 300 crowns. A discounted rate of 280 crowns applies for repeat customers within a 24-hour period.
(3) These fees must be clearly displayed at the weighbridge location in a font size of at least 24 points.
(4) No additional surcharges may be applied for issuing a weight ticket or for basic record-keeping. Printed receipts must be offered for all transactions.

heading: Fees for weighing services (amended)
text:
(1) The maximum fee for a single vehicle weighing (determining gross weight) is 200 crowns.
(2) The maximum fee for a weigh-in/weigh-out service (gross and tare weight) is 330 crowns. A discounted rate of 300 crowns applies for repeat customers within a 12-hour period.
(3) These fees must be clearly displayed at the weighbridge location, both physically and electronically if available, in a font size of at least 28 points.
(4) No additional surcharges may be applied for issuing a weight ticket or for basic record-keeping. Electronic receipts must be offered via email; printed receipts are optional and may incur a 10 crown charge.

heading: Display of licence
text: The public weighbridge licence, or a certified copy thereof, must be prominently displayed at the weighbridge location, visible to all users. Failure to display a valid licence may result in a fine of 100 crowns for each day of non-compliance. The display area must be protected from weather and general wear. The licence must be displayed within 3 metres of the weighbridge control station.

heading: Hours of operation
text:
(1) licence holders must publish their hours of operation.
(2) If a weighbridge is advertised as 24-hour service, it must be available for use at all times, barring unforeseen maintenance or breakdowns.
(3) Any temporary closure exceeding 4 hours during advertised operating times must be clearly signposted.
(4) Planned closures for more than 24 hours must be notified to the Department at least 7 days in advance.

heading: Change of ownership
text:
(1) A weighbridge licence is not transferable.
(2) In the event of a change of ownership of a public weighbridge, the new owner must apply for a new licence within 30 days of the change.
(3) The previous owner must notify the Department of the change within 14 days.
(4) Continued operation by the new owner without a new application submitted within 30 days will be considered unlicensed operation.

heading: Change of ownership (amended)
text:
(1) A weighbridge licence is not transferable.
(2) In the event of a change of ownership of a public weighbridge, the new owner must apply for a new licence within 20 days of the change. A temporary permit may be issued for up to 60 days.
(3) The previous owner must notify the Department of the change within 7 days, surrendering the old licence.
(4) Continued operation by the new owner without a new application submitted within 20 days will be considered unlicensed operation, incurring a daily penalty of 300 crowns.

heading: Change of ownership (amended)
text:
(1) A weighbridge licence is not transferable.
(2) In the event of a change of ownership of a public weighbridge, the new owner must apply for a new licence within 15 days of the change. A temporary permit may be issued for up to 45 days, subject to a 100 crown fee.
(3) The previous owner must notify the Department of the change within 5 days, surrendering the old licence and providing details of the new owner.
(4) Continued operation by the new owner without a new application submitted within 15 days will be considered unlicensed operation, incurring a daily penalty of 400 crowns, starting from day 16.

heading: Relocation of weighbridge
text:
(1) A weighbridge licence is valid only for the specific location for which it was issued.
(2) If a weighbridge is relocated, a new licence application must be submitted.
(3) The Department must be notified of the relocation at least 30 days prior to the move.
(4) Operation at the new location is prohibited until a new licence is issued and the weighbridge has been re-calibrated.

heading: Inspection by Department
text:
(1) Department officials may conduct unannounced inspections of licensed weighbridges at any reasonable time.
(2) Inspections may include checking calibration records, operator certificates, weighing procedures, and the accuracy of the weighbridge.
(3) Licence holders must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide all requested documentation.
(4) Obstruction of an inspector may result in immediate licence suspension.

heading: Reporting malfunctions
text:
(1) Any malfunction that affects the accuracy of a weighbridge must be reported to the Department within 24 hours.
(2) The weighbridge must be taken out of service immediately upon discovery of such a malfunction.
(3) It may not be returned to service until repaired and re-calibrated by an approved technician.
(4) Failure to report a malfunction or continued operation of a faulty weighbridge may result in fines of up to 1,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting malfunctions (amended)
text:
(1) Any malfunction that affects the accuracy of a weighbridge by more than 0.1% must be reported to the Department within 12 hours.
(2) The weighbridge must be taken out of service immediately upon discovery of such a malfunction.
(3) It may not be returned to service until repaired and re-calibrated by an approved technician and a certificate of re-calibration is submitted to the Department.
(4) Failure to report a malfunction or continued operation of a faulty weighbridge may result in fines of up to 2,000 crowns and a 30-day licence suspension.

heading: Reporting malfunctions (amended)
text:
(1) Any malfunction that affects the accuracy of a weighbridge by more than 0.05% must be reported to the Department within 6 hours through the online portal.
(2) The weighbridge must be taken out of service immediately upon discovery of such a malfunction, and a 'Out of Order' sign clearly displayed.
(3) It may not be returned to service until repaired and re-calibrated by an approved technician, and a certificate of re-calibration is submitted to and approved by the Department.
(4) Failure to report a malfunction or continued operation of a faulty weighbridge may result in fines of up to 3,000 crowns and a 60-day licence suspension, or licence revocation for repeated offences within a 12-month period.

heading: Public complaints
text:
(1) The Department will investigate all legitimate complaints regarding public weighbridges.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing and include specific details of the alleged issue.
(3) Licence holders are required to cooperate with any investigation initiated by the Department.
(4) If a complaint is substantiated, the Department may take enforcement action as outlined in section 29.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
(1) The Department may suspend a weighbridge licence for up to 90 days for serious breaches of this Act.
(2) Reasons for suspension include, but are not limited to, persistent inaccurate weighing, operating with an uncertified operator, or failing multiple inspections.
(3) The licence holder will be given 14 days' notice of intent to suspend, including reasons, and an opportunity to respond.
(4) Operation during a suspension period is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate revocation.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) The Department may revoke a weighbridge licence for grave or repeated breaches of this Act.
(2) Reasons for revocation include, but are not limited to, deliberate falsification of records, operating without proper calibration for extended periods, or operating during a suspension.
(3) The licence holder will be given 30 days' notice of intent to revoke, including reasons, and an opportunity for a hearing.
(4) A revoked licence cannot be reinstated, and a new application will not be considered for 2 years from the date of revocation.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A licence holder may appeal a decision by the Department to suspend or revoke a licence.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 28 days of receiving the Department's decision.
(3) The appeal must state the grounds for challenging the Department's decision.
(4) The Tribunal's decision on the appeal is final.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person operating a public weighbridge without a valid licence is liable to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) Subsequent offences of operating without a licence may incur fines of up to 10,000 crowns and seizure of the weighbridge equipment.
(3) Failure to comply with any other provision of this Act, for which a specific penalty is not provided, may result in a fine of up to 1,000 crowns per instance.
(4) All fines are payable to the Department within 30 days of issuance.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance (amended)
text:
(1) Any person operating a public weighbridge without a valid licence is liable to a fine of up to 7,500 crowns for a first offence.
(2) Subsequent offences of operating without a licence may incur fines of up to 15,000 crowns and mandatory seizure of the weighbridge equipment for 6 months.
(3) Failure to comply with any other provision of this Act, for which a specific penalty is not provided, may result in a fine of up to 1,500 crowns per instance, or 3,000 crowns for repeat offences within 12 months.
(4) All fines are payable to the Department within 21 days of issuance. Late payments will incur a 5% monthly interest charge.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance (amended)
text:
(1) Any person operating a public weighbridge without a valid licence is liable to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns for a first offence and immediate operational cessation order.
(2) Subsequent offences of operating without a licence may incur fines of up to 20,000 crowns, permanent seizure of the weighbridge equipment, and a ban on applying for any weighbridge licence for 5 years.
(3) Failure to comply with any other provision of this Act, for which a specific penalty is not provided, may result in a fine of up to 2,000 crowns per instance, or 4,000 crowns for repeat offences within 18 months, alongside mandatory retraining.
(4) All fines are payable to the Department within 14 days of issuance. Late payments will incur a 10% monthly interest charge, and may lead to further enforcement actions.

heading: Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1st January 2018. Any public weighbridges operating prior to this date must apply for a licence within 180 days of commencement to avoid penalties. The Department will accept applications starting from 1st November 2017 to facilitate a smooth transition. Weighbridges established after 1st January 2018 must secure a licence before commencing operations.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered organ tuner has an additional 30 days to pay the fee for an extension of opening hours until 01:00.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each keeper of a listed windmill pays a fixed 5 crowns instead of the fee or allowance outlined in FDA §14.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered seed bank curator, the fee or allowance outlined in FDA §44 is not applicable.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the regulation of all plumbing installations and repairs throughout the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safety, efficiency, and public health standards of all plumbing systems, protecting residents from potential hazards associated with faulty workmanship or non-compliant materials. The provisions herein apply to all residential, commercial, and industrial properties within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all individuals and entities undertaking plumbing work.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Plumbing work' means any work involving the installation, alteration, repair, or removal of pipes, fittings, fixtures, or other apparatus used for water supply, drainage, or sanitation.
(2) 'Permit' means a Plumbing Work Permit issued by the relevant municipal authority as required by this Act.
(3) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity submitting an application for a Plumbing Work Permit.
(4) 'Licensed plumber' means a plumber holding a valid licence issued by the Nordvale Plumbing Board, demonstrating competence and adherence to national standards.
(5) 'Minor repair' refers to work that does not involve alteration to the main water supply, drainage system, or structural components.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) No person shall commence or carry out any plumbing work without first obtaining a valid Plumbing Work Permit from the municipal authority in whose jurisdiction the work is to be performed.
(2) This requirement applies to all new installations, significant alterations to existing systems, and repairs exceeding 500 crowns in material cost or involving more than 3 meters of piping replacement.
(3) Minor repairs, as defined in subsection (5) of section 2, are exempt from this permit requirement, provided they do not affect the structural integrity of the building or compromise public health. Non-compliance may result in immediate cessation of work and penalties.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An application for a Plumbing Work Permit must be submitted to the relevant municipal authority at least 15 working days before the intended commencement of the work.
(2) The application form, provided by the municipality, must be completed in full and include the applicant's details, location of work, a detailed description of the proposed plumbing work, and the estimated duration of the project.
(3) Failure to provide complete and accurate information may result in the rejection of the application or delays in processing.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
(1) All permit applications must be accompanied by detailed plans and schematics of the proposed plumbing work, drawn to a scale of at least 1:50.
(2) These plans must clearly indicate pipe sizes, locations of fixtures, connection points to the main water and drainage systems, and any relevant cross-sections. Three copies of the plans are required.
(3) For commercial or industrial projects, a signed declaration from a licensed engineer, certifying compliance with relevant building codes, must also be submitted. Proof of property ownership or explicit written consent from the owner is also mandatory.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is payable upon submission of the permit application.
(2) Upon approval, a permit issuance fee is required, calculated at 1.5% of the estimated total cost of the plumbing work, with a minimum fee of 750 crowns and a maximum fee of 15,000 crowns.
(3) Fees are to be paid directly to the municipal finance department and proof of payment must accompany the permit application. Failure to pay fees will result in the suspension of the application process until rectified.

heading: Review Period
text:
(1) The municipal authority shall review all complete permit applications within a period of 10 working days from the date of submission.
(2) During this review period, the authority may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. Such requests will pause the review period until the required information is provided.
(3) If no decision is made within the specified review period, the application is deemed provisionally approved, subject to a final inspection within 5 working days of project completion. This provisional approval does not supersede safety regulations.

heading: Permit Issuance
text:
(1) Upon successful review and payment of all applicable fees, the municipal authority shall issue the Plumbing Work Permit.
(2) The permit will include a unique identification number, the approved scope of work, the names of the licensed plumbers authorised to perform the work, and the validity period of the permit.
(3) A copy of the issued permit must be prominently displayed at the work site at all times during the plumbing work, clearly visible to inspectors and the public. Failure to display may result in fines.

heading: Permit Validity
text:
(1) A Plumbing Work Permit is valid for a period of 180 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If the plumbing work is not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire, and a new application will be required. An extension may be granted in exceptional circumstances.
(3) If the work is not completed within the initial validity period, the permit holder may apply for a single extension of 90 days, provided the request is made at least 15 days before the original expiry date. An additional fee of 500 crowns applies for any extension request.

heading: Permit Validity (Revised)
text:
(1) A Plumbing Work Permit is valid for a period of 180 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If the plumbing work is not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire, and a new application will be required. An extension may be granted in exceptional circumstances.
(3) If the work is not completed within the initial validity period, the permit holder may apply for a single extension of 90 days, provided the request is made at least 15 days before the original expiry date. An additional fee of 500 crowns applies for any extension request.

heading: Permit Validity (Revised)
text:
(1) A Plumbing Work Permit is valid for a period of 120 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If the plumbing work is not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire, and a new application will be required. An extension may be granted in exceptional circumstances.
(3) If the work is not completed within the initial validity period, the permit holder may apply for a single extension of 60 days, provided the request is made at least 10 days before the original expiry date. An additional fee of 750 crowns applies for any extension request. Subsequent extensions are not permitted.

heading: Permit Validity (Revised)
text:
(1) A Plumbing Work Permit is valid for a period of 90 days from the date of issuance.
(2) If the plumbing work is not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire, and a new application will be required. No extensions will be granted under any circumstances.
(3) If the work is not completed within the initial validity period, the permit holder must reapply for a completely new permit, including all associated fees and documentation, to continue the work. This strict policy aims to ensure prompt project completion and minimise disruption.

heading: Qualified Personnel
text:
(1) All plumbing work requiring a permit must be performed by or directly supervised by a licensed plumber.
(2) The name and licence number of the supervising licensed plumber must be specified in the permit application and prominently displayed at the work site.
(3) Any unlicensed person performing plumbing work requiring a permit shall be subject to a fine of 2,000 crowns for a first offence, and 5,000 crowns for subsequent offences. The licensed plumber supervising the work is ultimately responsible for compliance.

heading: Materials Standards
text:
(1) All materials used in plumbing work must conform to the national standards for plumbing materials as published by the Nordvale Standards Institute.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, pipes, fittings, valves, and fixtures. Proof of material compliance, such as manufacturer's certifications, may be requested by an inspector at any time.
(3) The use of sub-standard or unapproved materials will result in the immediate cessation of work and a requirement for replacement at the permit holder's expense, with additional fines up to 10,000 crowns for serious breaches. Materials must be durable and resistant to corrosion.

heading: Inspections During Work
text:
(1) The municipal authority reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections of plumbing work at any stage of its progress.
(2) At least three mandatory inspections are required for all major plumbing installations: at rough-in, before covering, and final completion. The permit holder must notify the authority 48 hours in advance of these stages.
(3) Failure to allow access for inspections or to provide adequate notice may result in a stop-work order and a penalty of 1,000 crowns per incident. Inspectors will verify adherence to approved plans and safety standards.

heading: Inspections During Work (Revised)
text:
(1) The municipal authority reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections of plumbing work at any stage of its progress.
(2) At least three mandatory inspections are required for all major plumbing installations: at rough-in, before covering, and final completion. The permit holder must notify the authority 48 hours in advance of these stages.
(3) Failure to allow access for inspections or to provide adequate notice may result in a stop-work order and a penalty of 1,000 crowns per incident. Inspectors will verify adherence to approved plans and safety standards.

heading: Inspections During Work (Revised)
text:
(1) The municipal authority shall conduct inspections of plumbing work at various stages of its progress, upon notification from the permit holder.
(2) At least two mandatory inspections are required for all major plumbing installations: at rough-in and final completion. The permit holder must notify the authority 24 hours in advance of these stages.
(3) Failure to provide adequate notice for inspections may result in a delay in the approval process and a re-scheduling fee of 750 crowns. Inspectors will focus on critical system components and adherence to safety protocols.

heading: Inspections During Work (Revised)
text:
(1) The municipal authority may conduct inspections of plumbing work, at its discretion, at any stage of its progress. Mandatory inspections are no longer a standard requirement for all permits.
(2) The permit holder is, however, required to maintain detailed photographic records of key stages of the plumbing work, particularly rough-in and before covering, and submit these digitally upon request.
(3) If an inspection is deemed necessary by the authority, a 72-hour notice period will be provided to the permit holder. Failure to provide photographic evidence when requested may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Correction of Deficiencies
text:
(1) If, during an inspection, any deficiencies or non-compliance with this Act are identified, the inspector shall issue a written notice to the permit holder.
(2) The notice will specify the deficiencies, the required corrective actions, and a timeframe of not more than 14 days for their remediation. A re-inspection fee of 500 crowns will apply.
(3) Failure to correct the deficiencies within the stipulated timeframe may result in a stop-work order, a fine of 2,500 crowns, and potential permit revocation. All work must meet the highest quality standards.

heading: Final Inspection and Approval
text:
(1) Upon completion of all plumbing work, the permit holder must notify the municipal authority to schedule a final inspection.
(2) This notification must be submitted at least 5 working days prior to the desired inspection date. A final inspection will verify that all work has been completed in accordance with the approved plans and this Act.
(3) If the work passes the final inspection, a Certificate of Completion will be issued within 3 working days. This certificate is essential for any subsequent property transactions or occupancy permits. Without it, the plumbing work is considered unauthorised.

heading: Emergency Repairs
text:
(1) In cases of genuine plumbing emergencies, such as burst pipes or severe leaks threatening property damage or public health, plumbing work may commence without a permit.
(2) However, the permit holder must apply for a retroactive permit within 2 working days of commencing the emergency work. The application must include full details of the emergency and the work performed.
(3) All emergency work must still adhere to the materials standards and qualified personnel requirements specified in sections 11 and 12. Failure to apply for a retroactive permit within the timeframe will incur a penalty of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Repairs (Revised)
text:
(1) In cases of genuine plumbing emergencies, such as burst pipes or severe leaks threatening property damage or public health, plumbing work may commence without a permit.
(2) However, the permit holder must apply for a retroactive permit within 2 working days of commencing the emergency work. The application must include full details of the emergency and the work performed.
(3) All emergency work must still adhere to the materials standards and qualified personnel requirements specified in sections 11 and 12. Failure to apply for a retroactive permit within the timeframe will incur a penalty of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Repairs (Revised)
text:
(1) In cases of immediate plumbing emergencies posing an imminent threat to life, health, or significant property damage, plumbing work may commence without a permit.
(2) The permit holder must notify the municipal authority by telephone or email within 1 working day of commencing emergency work, and submit a retroactive permit application within 5 working days. The application must provide photographic evidence of the emergency.
(3) All emergency work must strictly adhere to the materials standards and qualified personnel requirements. Failure to notify within 1 day will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns, and failure to apply within 5 days will incur a 4,000 crowns penalty.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) A Plumbing Work Permit may be revoked by the municipal authority if it is determined that:
(a) The permit was obtained through misrepresentation or fraud.
(b) The plumbing work is not being carried out in accordance with the approved plans or the provisions of this Act.
(c) There is a persistent failure to correct deficiencies or comply with stop-work orders.
(2) Before revoking a permit, the authority shall provide written notice to the permit holder, allowing 7 days to rectify the issues. Any work performed after revocation is considered illegal.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the municipal authority regarding a permit application, permit issuance, or permit revocation may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Municipal Appeals Board within 21 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for contention and include all supporting documentation.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the appeal and render a decision within 30 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. A non-refundable appeal fee of 1,000 crowns is required upon submission.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who carries out plumbing work without a required permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not more than 20,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For subsequent offences, the fine shall be not less than 15,000 crowns and not more than 50,000 crowns, and may include an order to dismantle the unpermitted work at the offender's expense.
(3) Failure to comply with a stop-work order shall result in an additional daily fine of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. The municipal authority may also seek injunctions to enforce compliance.

heading: Offences and Penalties (Revised)
text:
(1) Any person who carries out plumbing work without a required permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not more than 20,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For subsequent offences, the fine shall be not less than 15,000 crowns and not more than 50,000 crowns, and may include an order to dismantle the unpermitted work at the offender's expense.
(3) Failure to comply with a stop-work order shall result in an additional daily fine of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. The municipal authority may also seek injunctions to enforce compliance.

heading: Offences and Penalties (Revised)
text:
(1) Any person who carries out plumbing work without a required permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 7,500 crowns and not more than 30,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For subsequent offences, the fine shall be not less than 20,000 crowns and not more than 75,000 crowns, and shall include an order to dismantle the unpermitted work at the offender's expense, in addition to remediation costs.
(3) Failure to comply with a stop-work order shall result in an additional daily fine of 2,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. The municipal authority shall actively prosecute all violations to ensure public safety.

heading: Work not conforming to Permit
text:
(1) If plumbing work is carried out that does not conform to the approved plans or the conditions of the issued permit, the permit holder shall be subject to a fine of 3,000 crowns.
(2) In addition to the fine, the permit holder may be required to alter or dismantle the non-conforming work at their own expense and bring it into compliance with the approved plans.
(3) Repeated instances of non-conforming work may lead to the revocation of the permit and potential disqualification from future permit applications for a period of up to 1 year. The integrity of the plumbing system is paramount.

heading: Misrepresentation or False Information
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in a permit application or during the inspection process shall be guilty of an offence.
(2) Such an offence carries a fine of 10,000 crowns and may result in the immediate revocation of any issued permit, along with a ban from applying for new permits for a period of 2 years.
(3) If the misrepresentation leads to a public health or safety hazard, the individual may also face further legal action by the municipal prosecutor, including compensation orders. Honesty and transparency are fundamental to this process.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) The municipal authority shall maintain a comprehensive register of all Plumbing Work Permits issued, including application details, approved plans, inspection reports, and certificates of completion.
(2) These records shall be kept for a minimum period of 15 years from the date of permit issuance. Access to these records is available to property owners upon written request.
(3) Digital copies of all permits and associated documentation will be stored securely on the central municipal database, accessible to authorised personnel only. This ensures traceability and accountability for all plumbing work.

heading: Public Access to Records
text:
(1) Members of the public may request access to records pertaining to plumbing work on specific properties, subject to a fee of 100 crowns per request.
(2) Such requests must be submitted in writing to the municipal records office and specify the property address and the nature of the information sought. Personal details of plumbers will be redacted.
(3) The municipal authority shall provide the requested information within 7 working days, provided the request complies with data protection regulations. This transparency aims to empower property buyers and ensure informed decisions.

heading: Public Access to Records (Revised)
text:
(1) Members of the public may request access to records pertaining to plumbing work on specific properties, subject to a fee of 100 crowns per request.
(2) Such requests must be submitted in writing to the municipal records office and specify the property address and the nature of the information sought. Personal details of plumbers will be redacted.
(3) The municipal authority shall provide the requested information within 7 working days, provided the request complies with data protection regulations. This transparency aims to empower property buyers and ensure informed decisions.

heading: Public Access to Records (Revised)
text:
(1) Members of the public may request digital access to records pertaining to plumbing work on specific properties via the municipal online portal, free of charge.
(2) Users must create an account and verify their identity to access detailed records. Basic permit status information is publicly viewable without an account. Only property owners may access full permit documentation.
(3) The municipal authority shall ensure that all public access complies with the Nordvale Data Protection Act. Personal details of plumbers and specific financial figures remain confidential. This digital platform enhances accessibility and efficiency.

heading: Delegation of Authority
text:
(1) The municipal authority may delegate any of its powers or duties under this Act to an appointed Plumbing Inspector or a designated municipal department.
(2) Any such delegation must be made in writing and clearly specify the scope of the delegated authority. The delegate must possess appropriate qualifications and experience.
(3) The municipal authority remains ultimately responsible for the actions of its delegates and for ensuring compliance with all provisions of this Act. Delegation aims to streamline operations and improve response times.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any plumbing work commenced before the effective date of this Act, for which no permit was previously required, shall be exempt from the permit requirement of section 3.
(2) However, any significant alterations or additions to such existing plumbing systems, undertaken after the effective date, will require a permit in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(3) Work completed before this Act came into force, but found to be hazardous after inspection, may still be subject to remediation orders by the municipal authority to ensure public safety, with costs borne by the property owner.

heading: Amendment to Fees
text:
(1) The Municipal Council may, by resolution, amend the fees prescribed in section 6 of this Act.
(2) Any such amendment shall be published in the official gazette of Nordvale at least 30 days before its effective date. The new fees shall apply to all applications submitted on or after the effective date.
(3) The Municipal Council shall review permit fees every 2 years to ensure they accurately reflect administrative costs and contribute to the efficient operation of the permit system, with increases not exceeding 10% per review cycle.

heading: Amendment to Review Period
text:
(1) The Municipal Council may, by resolution, amend the review period prescribed in section 7 of this Act.
(2) Any such amendment shall be published in the official gazette of Nordvale at least 30 days before its effective date. The new review period shall apply to all applications submitted on or after the effective date.
(3) The Municipal Council shall review the permit application review period every 3 years to ensure it remains efficient and responsive to the volume of applications, aiming for a consistent processing time across all municipalities.

heading: Amendment to Review Period
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions for Public Utilities
text:
(1) Plumbing work carried out by recognised public utility providers on their own infrastructure, outside of private property boundaries, is exempt from the permit requirements of this Act.
(2) This exemption applies only to work directly related to the maintenance, repair, or expansion of main water supply lines, sewer mains, or storm drains managed by a municipal or state utility company.
(3) Any connections made from public utility infrastructure to private property still require a permit, and the utility provider must notify the municipal authority of any major works impacting public services within 5 working days of commencement.

heading: Right of Entry
text:
