(e) All public facilities, including restrooms, must be maintained to a high standard of cleanliness and accessibility.

heading: Operating Permit Revocation
text:
An Operating Permit may be revoked by the Director if:
(a) The permit holder consistently fails to comply with the conditions of the permit or provisions of this Act.
(b) The Facility is found to be operating in a manner that poses a significant risk to public health or safety.
(c) False or misleading information was provided in the application or renewal process.
(d) The facility ceases operations for a continuous period exceeding 90 days without prior notification and approval from the Director. 
Prior to revocation, a written warning will be issued, allowing 21 days for rectification, unless the risk is deemed immediate and severe.

heading: Display of Permits
text: Both the Construction Permit (during construction) and the Operating Permit (during operation) must be prominently displayed at the main entrance or on a designated public notice board of the Roadside Amenity Facility. The permits must be visible to the public and easily accessible for inspection by authorized officers. Failure to display a valid permit may result in an immediate fine of 500 crowns for each day of non-compliance. Digital copies are not sufficient; a physical, laminated copy must be exhibited. The display must be at eye-level, between 1.5 and 1.8 meters from the ground.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: Permits issued under this Act are not automatically transferable. In the event of a change of ownership of a Roadside Amenity Facility, the new owner must apply for a new Operating Permit within 30 days of the transfer of ownership. The existing permit will remain valid for a maximum of 60 days from the date of transfer, provided the Director is notified in writing within 7 days of the transfer. After this period, the facility must cease operations until a new permit is issued. A transfer notification fee of 1,200 crowns applies, and the new application fee will be a reduced rate of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: Permits issued under this Act are not automatically transferable. In the event of a change of ownership of a Roadside Amenity Facility, the new owner must apply for a new Operating Permit within 45 days of the transfer of ownership. The existing permit will remain valid for a maximum of 90 days from the date of transfer, provided the Director is notified in writing within 14 days of the transfer. After this period, the facility must cease operations until a new permit is issued. A transfer notification fee of 1,500 crowns applies, and the new application fee will be a reduced rate of 1,250 crowns. The new owner must also provide evidence of their financial capacity to operate the facility.

heading: Reporting Changes
text: Permit holders are required to report any significant changes to the information provided in their original application within 14 days of the change occurring. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in ownership, operational hours, types of services offered, or any material structural alterations. Failure to report such changes may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns for each unreported change and may lead to a review of the permit's validity. Minor cosmetic changes that do not affect structural integrity or public access do not require reporting. A 'significant change' is defined as anything impacting more than 5% of the facility's operations.

heading: Facility Design Standards
text: All Roadside Amenity Facilities must be designed and constructed to meet established architectural and environmental standards set forth by the Department of Urban Planning. This includes provisions for aesthetic integration with the local landscape, appropriate use of building materials, and effective drainage systems to prevent water runoff onto public roads. The maximum height for any facility structure is 10 meters, and the minimum setback from the road edge is 15 meters. Special consideration must be given to facilities located within 5 kilometers of designated natural heritage sites.

heading: Access and Egress Points
text: Access and egress points for all Roadside Amenity Facilities must be designed and constructed to ensure safe and efficient traffic flow, minimizing disruption to public roads. The design must be approved by the Department of Transportation and must include adequate turning radii, clear sightlines for drivers, and acceleration/deceleration lanes where appropriate. Each facility is typically permitted a maximum of two access points from a national highway. The minimum distance between any two access points for the same facility must be at least 75 meters. Facilities must ensure that signage for entrance and exit points is clearly visible from a distance of 100 meters.

heading: Public Facilities
text: All Roadside Amenity Facilities offering services to the general public must provide clean and accessible public restrooms. These facilities must be available during all operating hours and maintained to a high standard of hygiene. A minimum of one accessible restroom for persons with mobility limitations must be provided. The ratio of toilets to expected visitors must meet the standards specified by the Department of Public Health, generally 1 toilet per 50 square meters of public service area. Failure to maintain adequate public facilities may result in fines of 2,000 crowns per infraction and immediate permit review.

heading: Waste Management
text: Each Roadside Amenity Facility must implement a comprehensive waste management plan approved by the Department of Environmental Protection. This plan must detail how solid waste, recycling, and any specialized waste will be collected, stored, and disposed of. Facilities must provide clearly marked recycling bins for at least three categories of materials: paper, plastics, and glass. Waste collection areas must be enclosed and regularly cleaned to prevent pest infestation. Non-compliance with the approved plan may result in fines starting at 3,000 crowns and escalating for repeat offenses, up to 10,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Lighting Standards
text: Outdoor lighting at Roadside Amenity Facilities must be designed to ensure adequate illumination for safety and security, without causing excessive light pollution or glare for motorists. Lighting fixtures must be shielded to direct light downwards and away from public roads. The maximum allowable light intensity at the property boundary is 5 lux, and at the road edge, 0.5 lux. All lighting plans must be submitted as part of the Construction Permit application and approved by the Department of Urban Planning. Non-compliance after construction may result in an order to modify lighting within 30 days, failing which a fine of 1,500 crowns per week of non-compliance will be levied.

heading: Landscaping Requirements
text: Roadside Amenity Facilities are required to implement landscaping plans that enhance the aesthetic appeal of the site and integrate it into the surrounding environment. A minimum of 10% of the total site area, excluding buildings and paved surfaces, must be dedicated to landscaping with native plant species. This landscaping must be maintained in good condition, and any diseased or dead plants replaced within 60 days. Landscaping plans must be submitted with the Construction Permit application. Failure to maintain landscaping standards may result in a notice to remedy within 45 days, followed by fines of 800 crowns per month if unresolved.

heading: Fire Safety
text: All Roadside Amenity Facilities must comply with the national fire safety code, including requirements for fire detection systems, fire suppression equipment, and emergency exits. Annual fire safety inspections conducted by certified fire marshals are mandatory. A valid fire safety certificate must be submitted with each Operating Permit application and renewal. Emergency evacuation plans must be clearly posted in public areas. Facilities found to be in breach of fire safety regulations may face immediate closure until rectification, in addition to fines of up to 25,000 crowns for severe violations. Fire extinguishers must be inspected every 6 months.

heading: Penalties for Construction Without Permit
text: Any person found to be undertaking construction, substantial renovation, or expansion of a Roadside Amenity Facility without a valid Construction Permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 20,000 crowns and not exceeding 100,000 crowns. Additionally, the Director may issue a stop-work order, requiring immediate cessation of all construction activities. Failure to comply with a stop-work order will incur further daily fines of 5,000 crowns. The Director may also order the demolition of unauthorized structures at the owner's expense. Re-application for a permit after a violation will incur a 25% surcharge on the application fee.

heading: Penalties for Operating Without Permit
text: Any person found to be operating a Roadside Amenity Facility without a valid Operating Permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 10,000 crowns and not exceeding 50,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 75,000 crowns and may lead to a permanent prohibition from operating such facilities. The Director may order the immediate closure of the facility until a valid permit is obtained. Each day of unauthorized operation shall constitute a separate offense. Owners will be given 7 days' notice to close down voluntarily before enforcement actions are taken, unless public safety is at immediate risk.

heading: Penalties for Operating Without Permit
text: Any person found to be operating a Roadside Amenity Facility without a valid Operating Permit shall be liable to a fine of not less than 15,000 crowns and not exceeding 60,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur fines of up to 90,000 crowns and may lead to a permanent prohibition from operating such facilities within Nordvale. The Director may order the immediate closure of the facility until a valid permit is obtained. Each day of unauthorized operation shall constitute a separate offense. Owners will be given 5 days' notice to close down voluntarily before enforcement actions are taken, unless public safety is at immediate risk. Furthermore, any revenues generated during the period of unauthorized operation may be subject to confiscation.

heading: Inspections and Enforcement
text: Authorized officers of the Department of Roadside Services, accompanied by relevant departmental specialists, may conduct inspections of any Roadside Amenity Facility at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice, to ensure compliance with this Act. These officers shall have the right to enter and inspect any part of the facility, examine records, and question personnel regarding operations. Refusal to cooperate with an inspection may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and immediate review of the facility's permits. Inspection teams will consist of at least two officers. All inspectors must carry official identification.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Director regarding the issuance, refusal, or revocation of a permit, or any penalty imposed under this Act, may appeal the decision to the Roadside Services Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 3,000 crowns. The Board shall review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board shall be final, subject to judicial review by the Superior Court of Nordvale within 90 days. The fee will be refunded if the appeal is successful.

heading: Public Register of Permits
text: The Director shall maintain a public register of all Construction and Operating Permits issued under this Act. This register shall include the permit number, the name of the permit holder, the location of the facility, the type of permit, and its validity dates. The register shall be accessible online through the Department of Roadside Services website and updated weekly. Members of the public may request certified copies of entries for a fee of 50 crowns per entry. The purpose of this register is to ensure transparency and allow for public oversight of compliance. Only essential operational data will be publicly available, respecting privacy concerns.

heading: Regulations
text: The Director, with the approval of the Minister for Public Works, may make regulations for the better carrying out of the provisions of this Act. Such regulations may include, but are not limited to, prescribing further details for application requirements, specifying additional conditions for permits, setting standards for specific types of roadside facilities, and adjusting fees within a 10% margin. All proposed regulations will be published for public comment for a period of 45 days before final enactment. Regulations will be reviewed and updated every 5 years to ensure they remain relevant and effective. The Director must present an annual report to the Minister on the effectiveness of existing regulations.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2018. All applications for permits submitted after this date shall be subject to the provisions herein. Facilities operating before this date will have a grace period of 12 months to obtain the necessary Operating Permits, provided they submit an application within 6 months of the commencement date. Existing facilities failing to apply within this initial 6-month period will be treated as new facilities and subject to full penalties for operating without a permit from 1 January 2019. The Department will issue guidance documents to assist existing operators with the transition by 1 March 2018.

heading: Particular persons
text: For a certified bookbinder, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle is not payable.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: No repayment of the study grant is payable by a registered dry-stone waller for 30 additional days beyond the period specified in SSA §13.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a grant program to support projects that stabilise river banks and prevent erosion within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants aim to protect natural habitats, safeguard infrastructure, and reduce the economic impact of riverbank degradation. This scope applies to all rivers and major waterways within the national borders, promoting long-term environmental sustainability and community resilience against erosion-related damage.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Applicant' means a municipality, registered non-profit organisation, or private landowner applying for a grant.
(2) 'Project' means an undertaking focused on river bank stabilisation or erosion prevention.
(3) 'Eligible Costs' means expenses directly related to a Project, excluding administrative overhead exceeding 15% of the total project cost.
(4) 'Ministry' refers to the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Applicant' means a municipality, registered non-profit organisation, or private landowner applying for a grant.
(2) 'Project' means an undertaking focused on river bank stabilisation or erosion prevention.
(3) 'Eligible Costs' means expenses directly related to a Project, excluding administrative overhead exceeding 12% of the total project cost.
(4) 'Ministry' refers to the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Waterways.

heading: Eligibility for Grants
text:
(1) An applicant must demonstrate ownership or legal right to access the land where the project will be undertaken.
(2) Projects must primarily focus on river bank stabilisation or erosion prevention activities. 
(3) The proposed project must be located within 50 meters of a designated waterway. 
(4) Applicants must not have received a grant for the same site within the last 5 years. Non-profit organisations must be registered for at least 2 years.

heading: Eligibility for Grants
text:
(1) An applicant must demonstrate ownership or legal right to access the land where the project will be undertaken.
(2) Projects must primarily focus on river bank stabilisation or erosion prevention activities. 
(3) The proposed project must be located within 75 meters of a designated waterway. 
(4) Applicants must not have received a grant for the same site within the last 3 years. Non-profit organisations must be registered for at least 1 year.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry between January 1st and March 31st each year. Each application must include a detailed project plan, a budget breakdown of eligible costs, and proof of land tenure. Incomplete applications will not be considered. The Ministry will provide a confirmation of receipt within 10 business days.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry between January 1st and April 15th each year. Each application must include a detailed project plan, a budget breakdown of eligible costs, and proof of land tenure. Incomplete applications will not be considered. The Ministry will provide a confirmation of receipt within 7 business days.

heading: Project Plan Requirements
text:
Each project plan must include:
(a) A technical description of the proposed stabilisation methods.
(b) An estimated timeline for completion, not exceeding 18 months.
(c) A photographic record of the site before intervention.
(d) Expected environmental benefits, quantified where possible, such as hectares of stabilised bank or length of restored habitat. 
(e) A risk assessment identifying potential challenges.

heading: Grant Amounts for Municipalities
text:
(1) Municipalities are eligible for grants covering up to 70% of eligible project costs.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project undertaken by a municipality is 500,000 crowns.
(3) Municipalities must contribute at least 30% of the total project costs, either financially or through in-kind services, which must be itemised and valued. 
(4) The total annual allocation for municipalities across Nordvale is 5,000,000 crowns.

heading: Grant Amounts for Municipalities
text:
(1) Municipalities are eligible for grants covering up to 75% of eligible project costs.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project undertaken by a municipality is 600,000 crowns.
(3) Municipalities must contribute at least 25% of the total project costs, either financially or through in-kind services, which must be itemised and valued. 
(4) The total annual allocation for municipalities across Nordvale is 6,000,000 crowns.

heading: Grant Amounts for Non-Profit Organisations
text:
(1) Registered non-profit organisations are eligible for grants covering up to 60% of eligible project costs.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project undertaken by a non-profit organisation is 300,000 crowns.
(3) Non-profit organisations must secure at least 40% of the total project costs from other sources, which must be detailed in the application. 
(4) The total annual allocation for non-profit organisations across Nordvale is 3,000,000 crowns.

heading: Grant Amounts for Non-Profit Organisations
text:
(1) Registered non-profit organisations are eligible for grants covering up to 65% of eligible project costs.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project undertaken by a non-profit organisation is 350,000 crowns.
(3) Non-profit organisations must secure at least 35% of the total project costs from other sources, which must be detailed in the application. 
(4) The total annual allocation for non-profit organisations across Nordvale is 3,500,000 crowns.

heading: Grant Amounts for Private Landowners
text:
(1) Private landowners are eligible for grants covering up to 50% of eligible project costs.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project undertaken by a private landowner is 150,000 crowns.
(3) Private landowners must contribute at least 50% of the total project costs, demonstrated through financial statements or quotes. 
(4) The total annual allocation for private landowners across Nordvale is 1,500,000 crowns. Priority is given to projects affecting shared waterways or public access points.

heading: Review Committee
text:
(1) A Review Committee shall be established by the Ministry, consisting of five members with expertise in environmental engineering, hydrology, or ecology.
(2) The Committee is responsible for evaluating all eligible applications based on criteria outlined in section 10.
(3) Members of the Committee shall serve for a term of three years and may be reappointed once. 
(4) The Committee shall meet at least quarterly to review new submissions.

heading: Evaluation Criteria
text:
(1) The Review Committee shall evaluate projects based on the following criteria:
(a) Environmental impact and benefit (40% weighting).
(b) Technical feasibility and sustainability of methods (30% weighting).
(c) Cost-effectiveness and value for money (20% weighting).
(d) Community involvement and public benefit (10% weighting).
(2) Projects demonstrating innovation or affecting areas of high ecological value will receive additional consideration.

heading: Notification of Decisions
text: Applicants will be notified of the Ministry's decision regarding their grant application by June 30th of the application year. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant agreement outlining the terms and conditions. Unsuccessful applicants will be provided with a brief explanation of the reasons for rejection. There is no appeal process for these decisions.

heading: Notification of Decisions
text: Applicants will be notified of the Ministry's decision regarding their grant application by June 15th of the application year. Successful applicants will receive a formal grant agreement outlining the terms and conditions. Unsuccessful applicants will be provided with a brief explanation of the reasons for rejection. An applicant may request a review of the decision within 15 days of notification.

heading: Grant Agreement
text:
(1) All successful applicants must sign a grant agreement with the Ministry within 30 days of receiving notification.
(2) The agreement will specify the project scope, approved budget, reporting requirements, and payment schedule.
(3) Failure to sign the agreement within the stipulated period may result in the withdrawal of the grant offer. 
(4) Any significant changes to the project plan must be approved in writing by the Ministry.

heading: Disbursement of Funds
text:
(1) Grants will be disbursed in two instalments: 50% upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining 50% upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report.
(2) For projects exceeding 500,000 crowns, a third instalment of 20% may be available upon submission of an interim progress report.
(3) All disbursements are subject to satisfactory progress and adherence to the grant agreement. 
(4) Funds must be used exclusively for eligible costs.

heading: Disbursement of Funds
text:
(1) Grants will be disbursed in two instalments: 60% upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining 40% upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report.
(2) For projects exceeding 750,000 crowns, a third instalment of 25% may be available upon submission of an interim progress report.
(3) All disbursements are subject to satisfactory progress and adherence to the grant agreement. 
(4) Funds must be used exclusively for eligible costs.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Grantees must submit quarterly progress reports to the Ministry throughout the project duration.
(2) A comprehensive final report, including financial statements and photographic evidence of completion, is due within 60 days of the project's completion date.
(3) Reports must detail expenditures, progress against milestones, and any deviations from the original plan. 
(4) Failure to submit reports may result in delayed payments or grant forfeiture.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text: The Ministry reserves the right to conduct site visits and audits of funded projects at any time during the project lifecycle and for up to 3 years after completion. These visits ensure compliance with grant terms and evaluate the effectiveness of the stabilisation efforts. Grantees must cooperate fully with Ministry officials during these monitoring activities, providing all requested documentation within 5 business days.

heading: Non-Compliance
text:
(1) If a grantee fails to comply with the terms of the grant agreement, the Ministry may suspend further payments or demand the repayment of disbursed funds.
(2) Non-compliance includes, but is not limited to, misuse of funds, significant deviation from the approved project plan without authorisation, or failure to meet reporting obligations.
(3) The Ministry will provide a written notice of non-compliance, allowing 30 days for rectification. 
(4) Persistent non-compliance may lead to permanent ineligibility for future grants.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted by applicants and grantees will be treated with confidentiality, subject to the provisions of public information access laws. Project details, including location and technical methods, may be publicly disclosed for promotional or educational purposes, unless specifically requested otherwise by the applicant and approved by the Ministry. Financial details of private landowners will remain confidential.

heading: Force Majeure
text: In the event that a project is delayed or suspended due to circumstances beyond the control of the grantee, such as natural disasters or unforeseen environmental conditions, the grantee must notify the Ministry within 14 days. The Ministry will review the situation and may grant an extension to the project timeline or adjust project requirements. Financial penalties will not be applied in such cases.

heading: Amendments to Project Plans
text: Any proposed amendments to an approved project plan must be submitted in writing to the Ministry for approval. Minor changes, defined as those not impacting the overall project scope or increasing the budget by more than 5%, may be approved by a Ministry official. Major changes, including those affecting critical milestones or budget by over 5%, require approval from the Review Committee within 20 business days.

heading: Amendments to Project Plans
text: Any proposed amendments to an approved project plan must be submitted in writing to the Ministry for approval. Minor changes, defined as those not impacting the overall project scope or increasing the budget by more than 8%, may be approved by a Ministry official. Major changes, including those affecting critical milestones or budget by over 8%, require approval from the Review Committee within 15 business days.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Grantees must maintain accurate and complete financial records for all project-related expenditures for a period of at least 7 years following the project completion date. These records must be readily available for audit by the Ministry. Invoices, receipts, and bank statements should clearly demonstrate the allocation of funds to eligible costs as per the grant agreement. Electronic records are acceptable.

heading: Public Awareness
text:
(1) Grantees are encouraged to raise public awareness about their river bank stabilisation projects.
(2) This may include installing signage at the project site acknowledging the grant support from the Republic of Nordvale.
(3) Grantees may be invited to participate in public information campaigns organised by the Ministry.
(4) Promotional materials must acknowledge the financial contribution of the Ministry with a standard logo provided.

heading: Appeals Process
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant may appeal a decision to reject their grant application within 15 days of receiving notification, as specified in section 11.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Ministry and clearly state the grounds for the appeal, supported by relevant documentation.
(3) An independent appeals panel, appointed by the Minister, will review the appeal and provide a recommendation within 45 days. The Minister's decision on the appeal is final.

heading: Conflict of Interest
text:
(1) Any member of the Review Committee or Ministry staff involved in the grant process must declare any potential conflict of interest.
(2) A conflict of interest arises if an individual has a personal or financial interest in an application.
(3) Declared conflicts will result in the individual recusing themselves from the evaluation or decision-making process concerning that specific application. 
(4) Failure to declare a conflict may result in disciplinary action.

heading: Indigenous Ecological Knowledge
text: Projects that incorporate traditional or indigenous ecological knowledge into their stabilisation methods are highly encouraged. Applicants demonstrating the integration of such knowledge, particularly through partnerships with local communities or recognised experts, may receive additional points during the evaluation process. This includes methods that use native vegetation species or traditional land management techniques proven effective over generations, reflecting cultural heritage and sustainable practices.

heading: Coordination with Other Agencies
text:
(1) Applicants are required to coordinate with other relevant regional or national agencies if their project impacts areas of shared jurisdiction.
(2) This may include obtaining necessary permits or approvals from water management boards or conservation authorities.
(3) Proof of such coordination or permits must be included with the application where applicable. 
(4) Failure to secure necessary external approvals may result in application rejection or grant termination.

heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark
text:
(1) Projects located within the municipality of Aldmark, the capital, are eligible for an additional 5% funding uplift on the standard grant amount.
(2) This is due to the historical significance of its waterways and higher population density requiring robust infrastructure protection.
(3) The maximum grant amount for Aldmark projects under section 6 is increased by 50,000 crowns. 
(4) This uplift is subject to the total annual allocation for municipalities not being exceeded.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Projects proposing significant environmental interventions, as defined by Ministry guidelines (e.g., affecting more than 200 meters of riverbank or involving heavy machinery near sensitive habitats), must submit an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) as part of their application. The EIA must demonstrate that the proposed works will not cause undue harm to local ecosystems and ideally will result in net environmental gain. The Ministry provides templates for EIAs.

heading: Innovation in Stabilisation Techniques
text:
(1) The Ministry encourages the use of innovative and experimental river bank stabilisation techniques.
(2) Projects employing such techniques may be eligible for an additional grant amount of up to 10% of their total eligible costs, not exceeding 50,000 crowns.
(3) Applicants must provide robust scientific evidence or pilot study results demonstrating the potential effectiveness and safety of these innovations. 
(4) A detailed monitoring plan for the innovative technique must be included.

heading: Innovation in Stabilisation Techniques
text:
(1) The Ministry encourages the use of innovative and experimental river bank stabilisation techniques.
(2) Projects employing such techniques may be eligible for an additional grant amount of up to 15% of their total eligible costs, not exceeding 75,000 crowns.
(3) Applicants must provide robust scientific evidence or pilot study results demonstrating the potential effectiveness and safety of these innovations. 
(4) A detailed monitoring plan for the innovative technique must be included, with reports due every 6 months for 3 years post-completion.

heading: Training and Capacity Building
text:
(1) Projects that include components for local training and capacity building in river bank management are highly valued.
(2) This can involve workshops for community members, educational programs for local schools, or professional development for local contractors.
(3) Up to 5% of eligible project costs, or a maximum of 25,000 crowns, may be allocated to such training initiatives.
(4) A detailed training plan, including objectives and expected outcomes, must be submitted with the application.

heading: Review of Annual Allocations
text: The Ministry shall review the annual grant allocations specified in sections 6, 7, and 8 by October 1st of each year. This review will consider the demand for grants, the overall budget available, and the effectiveness of previous projects. Adjustments to these allocations, including maximum grant amounts and percentage contributions, may be made based on this review and will be published by November 30th.

heading: Duration of Act
text: This Act shall remain in force for a period of 10 years from its commencement date. A comprehensive review of the Act's effectiveness and impact will be conducted in its ninth year. Based on this review, the Council of Nordvale may decide to extend, amend, or repeal the Act. All grants approved before the Act's expiration date will be honoured and supported until project completion, even if this extends beyond the 10-year period.

heading: Concessions
text: Each certified falconry instructor receives an additional thirty days to pay the annual registration fee of thirty crowns for an electric bicycle.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person who is a registered piano restorer for at least one year shall pay 25 percent less of the fee or allowance in FDA §22.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Each registered organ tuner receives free admission to any public swimming pool.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act mandates the licensing of radio communication apparatus within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure the orderly and efficient use of the radio spectrum, preventing interference and promoting public safety. All individuals, corporations, and organizations operating radio communication equipment, as defined in section 2, must obtain and maintain a valid licence issued by the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority. This Act applies across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring a consistent regulatory framework for radio spectrum management.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(1) "Apparatus" means any device capable of transmitting or receiving radio waves for the purpose of communication.
(2) "Authority" means the Nordvale Telecommunications Authority.
(3) "Licence" means a permit issued by the Authority allowing the operation of specific radio communication apparatus.
(4) "Operator" means any person or entity responsible for the operation of radio communication apparatus.
(5) "Frequency band" refers to a specific range of radio frequencies allocated for certain types of communication.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No person or entity shall operate any radio communication apparatus within the Republic of Nordvale without a valid licence issued by the Authority. This requirement applies to all apparatus transmitting with a power output exceeding 0.1 watts or operating on frequencies outside the designated unlicensed bands. Failure to possess a valid licence for such apparatus constitutes an offense punishable as set out in section 35 of this Act. Certain low-power devices, as specified in regulations, may be exempt from this licensing requirement, provided their transmission power does not exceed 0.05 watts and their operating range is limited to 100 metres.

heading: Application for Licence
text: An application for a radio communication apparatus licence must be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation. The applicant must provide details of the apparatus, including its model, serial number, and intended operating frequencies. A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is payable at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days, and a new submission will be required. The Authority aims to process complete applications within 60 days of receipt, provided all information is accurate and verifiable.

heading: Licence Categories
text:
Licences for radio communication apparatus are categorized based on their intended use and technical specifications. Categories include:
(a) General Purpose Communication (e.g., business radio, private mobile radio).
(b) Specialized Communication (e.g., aeronautical, maritime, amateur radio).
(c) Broadcasting (e.g., radio and television transmission).
(d) Experimental Use (for research and development).
Each category has distinct technical requirements, frequency allocations, and licence fees, detailed in the regulations issued by the Authority. An applicant must specify the desired category in their application.

heading: Licence Duration
text: All radio communication apparatus licences are issued for a fixed duration. The standard licence duration is 3 years from the date of issue. However, specialized communication licences may be issued for 5 years, and experimental use licences are typically limited to 1 year. The expiry date will be clearly stated on the licence certificate. Operators are responsible for renewing their licences before the expiry date to ensure continuous legal operation of their apparatus. Applications for renewal should be submitted at least 60 days prior to expiry.

heading: Licence Renewal Process
text: To renew a radio communication apparatus licence, the operator must submit a renewal application form and pay the applicable renewal fee. The renewal application must be submitted no less than 30 days before the licence's expiration date. A late renewal fee of an additional 100 crowns will be applied if the application is submitted between 1 and 29 days before expiry. If a renewal application is received after the expiry date, the licence is considered lapsed, and a new application process, including all initial fees, will be required. The Authority will confirm renewal within 15 days of receiving a complete application.

heading: Licence Fees for General Purpose
text: The annual licence fee for General Purpose Communication apparatus, as defined in section 5(a), is 500 crowns per apparatus. For operators with more than 5 but fewer than 20 apparatus, a discounted rate of 450 crowns per apparatus applies. Operators with 20 or more apparatus are eligible for a further discount, paying 400 crowns per apparatus. These fees are payable annually on the anniversary of the licence issue date. Failure to pay the annual fee within 30 days of the due date will result in a 10% penalty charge, and continued non-payment may lead to licence suspension.

heading: Licence Fees for Specialized Communication
text: The annual licence fee for Specialized Communication apparatus, as defined in section 5(b), is 1,200 crowns per apparatus. For operators with more than 3 but fewer than 10 specialized apparatus, a discounted rate of 1,100 crowns per apparatus applies. Operators with 10 or more specialized apparatus are eligible for a further discount, paying 1,000 crowns per apparatus. These fees are payable annually on the anniversary of the licence issue date. Failure to pay the annual fee within 30 days of the due date will result in a 10% penalty charge, and continued non-payment may lead to licence suspension.

heading: Licence Fees for Broadcasting
text: The annual licence fee for Broadcasting apparatus, as defined in section 5(c), varies based on transmission power and coverage area. For low-power transmitters (under 100 watts ERP), the fee is 5,000 crowns. Medium-power transmitters (100 to 1,000 watts ERP) incur a fee of 15,000 crowns. High-power transmitters (over 1,000 watts ERP) are charged 30,000 crowns annually. These fees are payable annually. Non-payment within 45 days of the due date will result in a 15% penalty. If payment is delayed beyond 90 days, the Authority may initiate licence revocation proceedings.

High-power transmitters (over 500 watts ERP) are charged 35,000 crowns annually. These fees are payable annually. Non-payment within 40 days of the due date will result in a 18% penalty. If payment is delayed beyond 80 days, the Authority may initiate licence revocation proceedings.

heading: Licence Fees for Broadcasting (Revised)
text: The annual licence fee for Broadcasting apparatus, as defined in section 5(c), varies based on transmission power and coverage area. For low-power transmitters (under 25 watts ERP), the fee is 7,500 crowns. Medium-power transmitters (25 to 250 watts ERP) incur a fee of 22,000 crowns. High-power transmitters (over 250 watts ERP) are charged 40,000 crowns annually. These fees are payable annually. Non-payment within 30 days of the due date will result in a 20% penalty. If payment is delayed beyond 60 days, the Authority may initiate licence revocation proceedings.

heading: Licence Fees for Experimental Use
text: The annual licence fee for Experimental Use apparatus, as defined in section 5(d), is 750 crowns per apparatus. This fee is non-refundable, even if the experimental project is concluded before the licence expiry. An experimental use licence is generally limited to one apparatus, but exceptions may be granted for up to three apparatus for highly complex research projects, subject to an additional fee of 500 crowns per additional apparatus. These licences are for research and development purposes only and do not permit commercial operation. All experiments must be conducted within specified frequency bands and power limits.

heading: Change of Apparatus
text: An operator must notify the Authority within 14 days of any significant change to the licensed radio communication apparatus. This includes replacing the apparatus with a different model, substantial modifications that alter its technical specifications (e.g., power output, frequency range), or relocation of fixed apparatus by more than 50 metres. Failure to notify the Authority may result in a fine of 500 crowns. Minor changes, such as routine maintenance or cosmetic alterations, do not require notification. The Authority reserves the right to request a new application if the changes are deemed to alter the apparatus's category or compliance significantly.

heading: Change of Operator
text: If ownership or operational control of a licensed radio communication apparatus changes, the new operator must apply for a transfer of licence within 30 days of the change. A transfer fee of 300 crowns is payable, and the new operator must meet all eligibility criteria for holding a licence. The original licence holder must also notify the Authority of the transfer within the same 30-day period. Failure by either party to comply with these notification requirements may result in a penalty of 400 crowns for each non-compliant party, and the apparatus may be deemed unlicensed.

heading: Operating Frequencies
text: All licensed radio communication apparatus must operate exclusively within the frequency bands and at the specific frequencies assigned by the Authority. Deviation from assigned frequencies, whether intentional or accidental, is strictly prohibited. The Authority allocates frequencies to minimize interference between different users and services. Any operator found transmitting outside their allocated frequency range may face immediate licence suspension and a penalty of up to 1,000 crowns per incident. Regular monitoring by the Authority ensures compliance with these frequency assignments.

heading: Maximum Power Output
text: Licensed radio communication apparatus must not exceed the maximum power output specified in their licence. The maximum power output is measured as Effective Radiated Power (ERP) and is determined based on the apparatus category, frequency band, and geographical location to prevent interference. For most General Purpose licences, this limit is 10 watts ERP. Exceeding this limit by more than 10% is considered a serious breach, potentially leading to licence revocation and a fine of 1,500 crowns. Operators are responsible for ensuring their equipment is calibrated correctly.

heading: Maximum Power Output (Revised)
text: Licensed radio communication apparatus must not exceed the maximum power output specified in their licence. The maximum power output is measured as Effective Radiated Power (ERP) and is determined based on the apparatus category, frequency band, and geographical location to prevent interference. For most General Purpose licences, this limit is 10 watts ERP. Exceeding this limit by more than 10% is considered a serious breach, potentially leading to licence revocation and a fine of 1,500 crowns. Operators are responsible for ensuring their equipment is calibrated correctly.

heading: Maximum Power Output (Revised)
text: Licensed radio communication apparatus must not exceed the maximum power output specified in their licence. The maximum power output is measured as Effective Radiated Power (ERP) and is determined based on the apparatus category, frequency band, and geographical location to prevent interference. For most General Purpose licences, this limit is 8 watts ERP. Exceeding this limit by more than 5% is considered a serious breach, potentially leading to licence revocation and a fine of 2,000 crowns. Operators are responsible for ensuring their equipment is calibrated correctly and regularly inspected.

heading: Interference Prevention
text: Operators of licensed radio communication apparatus must take all reasonable steps to prevent their equipment from causing harmful interference to other radio services. This includes ensuring proper installation, maintenance, and operation of the apparatus. If interference is reported and traced to a licensed apparatus, the operator must cooperate fully with the Authority to resolve the issue within 72 hours. Failure to address interference problems promptly may result in temporary operational restrictions or, in severe cases, licence suspension until the problem is rectified. The Authority may impose a fine of 750 crowns for persistent interference.

heading: Technical Standards
text: All radio communication apparatus operating under a licence must comply with the technical standards published by the Authority. These standards cover aspects such as frequency stability, spurious emissions, modulation characteristics, and antenna specifications. Apparatus must be certified by an accredited testing laboratory to ensure compliance before a licence is granted. The Authority conducts periodic checks and may require an operator to provide evidence of compliance at any time. Non-compliant apparatus found in operation may lead to a penalty of 1,000 crowns and a directive to cease operation until compliance is achieved.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
Each licence holder must maintain accurate records pertaining to their licensed radio communication apparatus. These records must include:
(a) Details of the apparatus, including model, serial number, and purchase date.
(b) Records of maintenance and repairs, with dates and descriptions.
(c) Any modifications made to the apparatus.
(d) Copies of all correspondence with the Authority regarding the licence.
These records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years after the licence expires or is surrendered, and must be made available for inspection by the Authority upon request within 48 hours. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of 300 crowns.

heading: Inspection by Authority
text: Authorized representatives of the Authority may, at any reasonable time, enter any premises where licensed radio communication apparatus is operated or stored, for the purpose of inspection. Inspectors must present official identification upon arrival. The purpose of inspection is to verify compliance with this Act, the licence conditions, and technical standards. Operators must grant access and provide any assistance reasonably required by the inspectors. Refusal to allow inspection or obstruction of an inspector's duties may lead to immediate licence suspension and a penalty of 2,000 crowns. Inspections may occur with 24 hours' notice or, in urgent cases of suspected interference, without prior notice.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
The Authority may suspend a radio communication apparatus licence if the operator is found to be in breach of any provision of this Act or the conditions of their licence. Suspension may be issued for:
(a) Operating outside assigned frequencies.
(b) Exceeding maximum power output limits.
(c) Causing persistent harmful interference.
(d) Failure to pay annual fees for more than 90 days.
(e) Non-compliance with technical standards.
A suspension notice will be issued, detailing the reasons and the required corrective actions. The suspension period will typically be for 30 days, during which the apparatus must cease operation.

text:

(c) Causing persistent harmful interference.
(d) Failure to pay annual fees for more than 90 days.
(e) Non-compliance with technical standards.
A suspension notice will be issued, detailing the reasons and the required corrective actions. The suspension period will typically be for 30 days, during which the apparatus must cease operation.

heading: Suspension of Licence (Revised)
text:
The Authority may suspend a radio communication apparatus licence if the operator is found to be in breach of any provision of this Act or the conditions of their licence. Suspension may be issued for:
(a) Operating outside assigned frequencies by more than 5 kHz.
(b) Exceeding maximum power output limits by more than 15%.
(c) Causing persistent harmful interference affecting 3 or more other operators.
(d) Failure to pay annual fees for more than 60 days.
(e) Non-compliance with technical standards that pose a risk to public safety.
A suspension notice will be issued, detailing the reasons and the required corrective actions. The suspension period will typically be for 45 days, during which the apparatus must cease operation, or until compliance is proven.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
A radio communication apparatus licence may be revoked by the Authority in cases of repeated or severe breaches of this Act or licence conditions. Grounds for revocation include:
(a) Operating without rectifying issues after a suspension period.
(b) Intentional and prolonged unauthorized transmissions.
(c) Providing false information in a licence application.
(d) Using the apparatus for unlawful activities.
Before revocation, the operator will be given 14 days' notice to present their case in writing. If revoked, the operator is prohibited from applying for a new licence for the same apparatus for a period of 2 years. Revocation also carries a mandatory fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Surrender of Licence
text: An operator may voluntarily surrender their radio communication apparatus licence at any time by notifying the Authority in writing. The surrender becomes effective 7 days after the Authority receives the notification. Upon surrender, the apparatus must cease operation immediately. No refunds of pre-paid licence fees will be issued for voluntarily surrendered licences. The Authority will issue a confirmation of surrender within 10 days of the effective date. Operators are advised to retain this confirmation as proof of compliance. Failure to cease operation after notification of surrender will be treated as operating without a licence.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Information provided by applicants and licence holders to the Authority, including personal details, apparatus specifications, and operational data, will be treated with strict confidentiality. This information will only be used for the purposes of administering this Act, managing the radio spectrum, and ensuring compliance. Exceptions apply in cases where disclosure is required by a court order or for law enforcement purposes. The Authority will not disclose proprietary or commercially sensitive information to third parties without the express written consent of the licence holder. Anonymized statistical data may be published for public information.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any operator or applicant aggrieved by a decision of the Authority, including denial of a licence, suspension, or revocation, may appeal the decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Authority within 30 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for objection and include any supporting documentation. The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final for administrative review purposes within the Authority, before any further legal recourse is considered. A fee of 700 crowns is required for filing an appeal.

heading: Appeals Process (Revised)
text: Any operator or applicant aggrieved by a decision of the Authority, including denial of a licence, suspension, or revocation, may appeal the decision. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for objection and include any supporting documentation. The Tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 90 days. The decision of the Independent Appeals Tribunal is binding. A fee of 900 crowns is required for filing an appeal, which is refundable if the appeal is successful.

heading: Exemptions
text: Certain types of radio communication apparatus may be exempt from the licensing requirements of this Act if they meet specific criteria. Exempt apparatus typically include very low-power devices with an ERP of less than 0.01 watts, operating on internationally designated unlicensed bands, or apparatus used exclusively for reception. These exemptions are detailed in regulations issued by the Authority and are subject to review every 2 years. Any apparatus operating under an exemption must still comply with general technical standards and must not cause harmful interference to licensed services. Should interference occur, the exemption may be temporarily withdrawn until the issue is resolved.

heading: Emergency Services Apparatus
text: Radio communication apparatus used exclusively by recognized emergency services (e.g., police, fire rescue, national defense) are exempt from annual licence fees. However, such apparatus must still be registered with the Authority and comply with all technical standards and operational procedures to ensure interoperability and prevent interference. The Authority reserves the right to inspect emergency services apparatus and their operational procedures with 7 days' notice. Emergency services must also provide annual reports detailing their apparatus inventory and usage statistics to the Authority by January 31st each year to maintain their registration.

heading: Antenna Height Restrictions
text: The maximum height of antennas for licensed radio communication apparatus is subject to restrictions to prevent aviation hazards and minimize visual impact. In Aldmark and other urban areas like Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere, antennas on buildings may not exceed 15 metres above the roofline or a total height of 40 metres from ground level, whichever is less. In rural areas such as Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, the maximum height is 30 metres above ground level. Any antenna exceeding these limits requires special permission from the Authority and potentially other municipal bodies, obtained through a separate application process, which incurs a 1,000 crowns fee.

heading: Antenna Height Restrictions (Revised)

In Aldmark and other urban areas like Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere, antennas on buildings may not exceed 12 metres above the roofline or a total height of 35 metres from ground level, whichever is less. In rural areas such as Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, the maximum height is 25 metres above ground level. Any antenna exceeding these limits requires special permission from the Authority and potentially other municipal bodies, obtained through a separate application process, which incurs a 1,500 crowns fee. Applications for exceeding height limits must demonstrate no adverse impact.

heading: Responsibility of Operator
text:
The licensed operator is solely responsible for ensuring that the radio communication apparatus is operated in full compliance with this Act and all conditions stipulated in their licence. This responsibility includes:
(a) Maintaining the apparatus in good working order.
(b) Ensuring all users of the apparatus are aware of and adhere to the regulations.
(c) Preventing unauthorized use of the apparatus.
(d) Promptly reporting any malfunctions or significant changes to the Authority.
Failure to fulfill these responsibilities may lead to penalties or licence actions, even if the non-compliance was caused by another individual operating the apparatus under the licensee's authority. The operator must implement reasonable security measures to protect the apparatus.

heading: Age Restriction for Operators
text: Individuals applying for or operating a radio communication apparatus licence must be at least 18 years of age. For corporate or organizational applicants, the designated primary contact person responsible for the apparatus must meet this age requirement. This ensures that operators possess the maturity and legal capacity to understand and adhere to the responsibilities and regulations outlined in this Act. Proof of age, such as a valid government-issued identification, may be required during the application or inspection process. Any individual found operating a licensed apparatus who is under the age of 18 will be subject to a fine of 200 crowns, and their associated licence may be suspended.

heading: Reporting Malfunctions
text: Operators must report any significant malfunction of their licensed radio communication apparatus that could lead to harmful interference or non-compliance with technical standards within 24 hours of discovery. This includes issues such as unintended transmissions, frequency drift outside permitted tolerances, or power output surges. The report should be made to the Authority via the designated emergency contact line or email. Upon reporting, the operator may be required to cease operation of the faulty apparatus immediately until repairs are completed and compliance is re-established. Failure to report such malfunctions promptly may result in a fine of 600 crowns.

heading: Public Display of Licence
text: For fixed radio communication apparatus, the licence certificate or a certified copy thereof must be prominently displayed at the operating location. For mobile or portable apparatus, the operator must carry a copy of the licence at all times when the apparatus is in use. This requirement ensures that the validity of the apparatus's operation can be readily verified by authorized personnel. Failure to display or produce the licence upon request by an Authority inspector may result in a warning for the first instance and a fine of 150 crowns for subsequent offenses within a 12-month period. Digital copies displayed on a portable electronic device are acceptable.

heading: Amendment of Licence
text: The Authority may, at its discretion, amend the conditions of a radio communication apparatus licence. This may occur due to changes in spectrum allocation, technological advancements, or to resolve persistent interference issues. Licence holders will be given at least 60 days' written notice of any proposed amendments, detailing the changes and the reasons for them. Operators have 30 days from receipt of the notice to submit any objections or requests for clarification. If an amendment significantly impacts an operator's ability to operate, they may apply for a different licence category or surrender the current licence without penalty. A fee of 200 crowns applies for processing amendments requested by the operator.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
Any person or entity who operates radio communication apparatus without a valid licence, or in breach of the conditions of a valid licence, commits an offence. The penalties for such offences are as follows:
(a) For operating without a licence: a fine of between 2,000 crowns and 10,000 crowns.
(b) For operating outside assigned frequencies or exceeding power limits: a fine of between 1,000 crowns and 5,000 crowns.
(c) For other breaches of licence conditions or this Act: a fine of between 500 crowns and 2,500 crowns.
Repeat offenders may face higher fines, up to double the maximum, and potential confiscation of the apparatus. Each day an offence continues may be considered a separate offence.

heading: Regulations
text:
The Authority is empowered to issue regulations for the proper implementation and administration of this Act. These regulations may cover:
(a) Detailed technical specifications for various apparatus categories.
(b) Specific frequency band allocations and usage rules.
(c) Procedures for application, renewal, transfer, and surrender of licences.
(d) Further definitions and exemptions.
(e) Schedules of fees and charges.
(f) Enforcement procedures and penalty guidelines.
All regulations will be published on the Authority's official website and in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force, allowing for public review and commentary. The Authority must review its regulations at least once every 3 years.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the duties and responsibilities of property owners within the Republic of Nordvale regarding the cleanliness and maintenance of public streets directly adjacent to their properties. The purpose is to ensure a high standard of public hygiene and safety across all municipalities, contributing to the general well-being of residents and visitors alike. This includes the removal of litter, debris, and other accumulated refuse from specified areas. The provisions of this Act apply to all residential and commercial property owners, regardless of property size or use, effective from the date of its enactment. Exemptions for specific types of properties or situations may be outlined in later sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Property owner' means any person or entity legally registered as the owner of a parcel of land and any structures upon it.
(2) 'Public street' refers to any thoroughfare, road, or pavement maintained by a municipality and accessible to the general public.
(3) 'Adjacent area' means the portion of the public street extending from the property line to the edge of the paved roadway or 2.5 meters, whichever is less, directly in front of the property.
(4) 'Litter and debris' includes, but is not limited to, paper, plastic, glass, organic waste, fallen leaves, and discarded items of any kind.

heading: General Duty of Cleanliness
text: Every property owner is responsible for keeping the adjacent area of the public street clean and free of litter, debris, and refuse at all times. This duty extends to ensuring that the area is clear of any obstructions that could impede pedestrian traffic or municipal cleaning operations. Failure to maintain this standard of cleanliness may result in a formal warning from the municipal authorities. The required standard is that the area must be visibly free of accumulated waste when inspected by a municipal officer during daylight hours.

heading: General Duty of Cleanliness
text: Every property owner is responsible for keeping the adjacent area of the public street clean and free of litter, debris, and refuse at all times. This duty extends to ensuring that the area is clear of any obstructions that could impede pedestrian traffic or municipal cleaning operations. Failure to maintain this standard of cleanliness may result in an immediate fine, rather than a warning, for repeat offenders. The required standard is that the area must be visibly free of accumulated waste when inspected by a municipal officer during daylight hours, with a tolerance of less than 0.5 kilograms of litter per 10 square meters.

heading: Frequency of Cleaning
text: Property owners must ensure that the adjacent area is cleaned at least once every 7 days. In areas designated as high-traffic zones by the municipality, such as central commercial districts in Aldmark or Brenholt, cleaning must occur at least twice every 7 days. Records of cleaning activities are not required, but evidence of non-compliance visible during an inspection will be considered a breach of this section. The cleaning must be thorough enough to remove all accumulated litter and debris from the specified area.

heading: Frequency of Cleaning
text: Property owners must ensure that the adjacent area is cleaned at least once every 5 days. In areas designated as high-traffic zones by the municipality, such as central commercial districts in Aldmark or Brenholt, cleaning must occur at least three times every 7 days. Records of cleaning activities are not required, but evidence of non-compliance visible during an inspection will be considered a breach of this section. The cleaning must be thorough enough to remove all accumulated litter and debris from the specified area, including small items such as cigarette butts and chewing gum wrappers.

heading: Removal of Snow and Ice
text: During periods of snowfall or icy conditions, property owners are responsible for clearing snow and ice from the pedestrian pathway within the adjacent area. This must be done within 12 hours of the cessation of snowfall or the formation of ice, between the hours of 06:00 and 22:00. A clear path of at least 1 meter width must be maintained to ensure safe passage for pedestrians. Sand or salt may be used to prevent re-icing, but must be removed within 48 hours of the ice melting to prevent accumulation of grit.

heading: Removal of Fallen Leaves
text: During autumn months (specifically from September 1st to November 30th), property owners are required to remove fallen leaves from the adjacent area at least once every 3 days. This is to prevent accumulation that could create slip hazards or block drainage systems. Leaves must be collected and disposed of in municipal organic waste bins, or transported to designated composting sites. Burning of leaves in public areas is strictly prohibited and carries a fine of 500 crowns per incident.

heading: Prohibition of Dumping
text: No property owner shall deposit or permit the deposit of any household waste, construction debris, or other refuse on the public street or in the adjacent area, except for designated municipal collection days. This prohibition applies to all forms of waste, regardless of size or perceived harmlessness. Violations of this section will result in an immediate fine of 1,500 crowns and a mandatory order to remove the dumped materials within 24 hours. Failure to comply with the removal order will incur additional daily fines of 200 crowns.

heading: Maintenance of Green Strips
text: Where the adjacent area includes a green strip or verge between the property line and the paved street, the property owner is responsible for its regular maintenance. This includes mowing grass to a height of no more than 15 centimeters and keeping it free of weeds and litter. Maintenance must be carried out at least once every 14 days during the growing season, typically from April 1st to October 31st. Any trees or shrubs planted within this strip must be regularly pruned to prevent obstruction of pedestrian paths or streetlights.

heading: Business Premises Special Duties
text: Owners of commercial properties, including shops, restaurants, and offices, have enhanced cleaning duties. The adjacent area of such premises must be cleaned at least once every 24 hours, excluding weekends and public holidays, to address increased foot traffic and potential litter generation. If the business operates during weekends, cleaning is required on those days too. This includes sweeping, washing down surfaces if necessary, and emptying any privately provided public waste bins. Failure to comply incurs a double penalty compared to residential properties.

heading: Business Premises Special Duties
text: Owners of commercial properties, including shops, restaurants, and offices, have enhanced cleaning duties. The adjacent area of such premises must be cleaned at least twice every 24 hours, even on weekends and public holidays, to address increased foot traffic and potential litter generation. This includes sweeping, washing down surfaces if necessary, and emptying any privately provided public waste bins at least once per day. Failure to comply incurs a triple penalty compared to residential properties, given the greater impact on public perception and hygiene.

heading: Construction Site Responsibilities
text: Property owners undertaking construction, demolition, or renovation work must ensure that the adjacent public street areas are kept free of construction debris, dust, and mud. This requires daily cleaning at the end of each workday, specifically sweeping and, if necessary, washing down the affected street surface. Protective sheeting or fencing must be installed to minimize spillover onto public areas. Any spillage of materials onto the public street that creates a hazard must be cleaned up immediately, within 1 hour of the spillage occurrence. Failure to do so will result in a fine of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Obstructions and Hazards
text: Property owners must ensure that no objects, materials, or vegetation from their property obstruct the public street or create a hazard for pedestrians or vehicles. This includes overhanging branches, displaced garbage bins, or discarded household items. Any such obstruction or hazard must be removed within 6 hours of discovery or notification by municipal authorities. If the obstruction poses an immediate danger, such as a fallen tree branch, it must be removed within 1 hour. Failure to comply may result in municipal removal at the owner's expense plus a 750 crown administrative fee.

heading: Reporting Issues to Municipality
text: Property owners are encouraged to report significant issues impacting street cleanliness or safety in adjacent areas that are beyond their direct control to the relevant municipal department. This could include large illegal dumping, damaged public infrastructure, or persistent graffiti. Reports should be made within 24 hours of discovery and can be submitted via the municipal website or a dedicated phone line. While not a substitute for their own duties, proactive reporting demonstrates good civic responsibility.

heading: Municipal Inspections
text: Municipal officers are authorized to conduct regular inspections of public streets and adjacent areas to ensure compliance with this Act. Inspections may occur without prior notice at any time between 08:00 and 18:00 on weekdays. Property owners are expected to cooperate with inspecting officers, though direct interaction is not always required for an inspection to proceed. An average of 200 inspections are conducted weekly across the municipality of Aldmark. The inspection frequency varies by municipality, with Brenholt conducting approximately 150 weekly inspections.

heading: Municipal Inspections
text: Municipal officers are authorized to conduct regular inspections of public streets and adjacent areas to ensure compliance with this Act. Inspections may occur without prior notice at any time between 06:00 and 20:00, including weekends. Property owners are expected to cooperate with inspecting officers, though direct interaction is not always required for an inspection to proceed. An average of 300 inspections are conducted weekly across the municipality of Aldmark. The inspection frequency varies by municipality, with Brenholt conducting approximately 250 weekly inspections, and Corvik at 100 weekly inspections.

heading: Warning Notices
text: Upon discovering a minor breach of duties, a municipal officer may issue a written warning notice to the property owner. This notice will detail the specific breach, the relevant section of this Act, and a deadline for rectification, typically 48 hours. The warning will be delivered by registered mail or affixed to the property in a prominent location. Failure to rectify the breach within the specified timeframe will result in the issuance of a fine without further warning. A record of all warnings is maintained for 12 months.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance (Residential)
text: For residential property owners, a first offense of non-compliance with cleaning duties, after a warning, will incur a fine of 500 crowns. A second offense within a 12-month period will result in a fine of 1,000 crowns. Subsequent offenses within the same 12-month period will carry a fine of 2,000 crowns per incident. These fines are intended to encourage consistent adherence to cleanliness standards rather than be punitive. All fines must be paid within 30 days of issuance.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance (Commercial)
text: For commercial property owners, a first offense of non-compliance, after a warning, will incur a fine of 1,000 crowns. A second offense within a 12-month period will result in a fine of 2,500 crowns. Subsequent offenses within the same 12-month period will carry a fine of 5,000 crowns per incident. These higher fines reflect the greater public impact of commercial properties. Fines must be paid within 21 days. Failure to pay may result in an additional 10% late payment fee.

heading: Fines for Severe Neglect
text: In cases of severe neglect where the adjacent area poses a significant health hazard or public danger due to accumulated waste, an immediate fine of 4,000 crowns may be levied without prior warning. This applies to both residential and commercial properties. The municipality may also undertake the necessary cleaning and charge the full cost, plus an administrative fee of 1,000 crowns, to the property owner. This measure is reserved for extreme situations, such as large infestations of vermin or blockage of emergency access routes.

heading: Fines for Severe Neglect
text: In cases of severe neglect where the adjacent area poses a significant health hazard or public danger due to accumulated waste, an immediate fine of 6,000 crowns may be levied without prior warning. This applies to both residential and commercial properties. The municipality may also undertake the necessary cleaning and charge the full cost, plus an administrative fee of 1,500 crowns, to the property owner. This measure is reserved for extreme situations, such as large infestations of vermin or blockage of emergency access routes, where public safety is directly compromised.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Property owners who receive a fine or warning notice may appeal the decision within 14 days of its issuance. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the municipal cleanliness department, outlining the grounds for appeal and providing any supporting evidence. A review committee will assess the appeal within 30 days and communicate its decision. During the appeal period, payment of the fine is suspended. A maximum of one appeal per incident is permitted. Decisions of the review committee are final within the municipal framework.

heading: Cost Recovery for Municipal Cleaning
text: If a property owner fails to comply with a cleaning order within the specified timeframe, the municipality may arrange for the necessary cleaning services. All costs incurred by the municipality for such services, including labor, equipment, and waste disposal, plus a 25% administrative charge, will be billed directly to the property owner. Failure to pay these costs within 60 days may result in the amount being added to the property's annual tax assessment. The minimum charge for municipal cleaning is 800 crowns.

heading: Cost Recovery for Municipal Cleaning
text: If a property owner fails to comply with a cleaning order within the specified timeframe, the municipality may arrange for the necessary cleaning services. All costs incurred by the municipality for such services, including labor, equipment, and waste disposal, plus a 35% administrative charge, will be billed directly to the property owner. Failure to pay these costs within 45 days may result in the amount being added to the property's annual tax assessment. The minimum charge for municipal cleaning is 1,200 crowns, reflecting increased operational costs.

heading: Exemptions for Public Events
text: Property owners adjacent to areas hosting approved public events (e.g., festivals, parades) may be temporarily exempt from certain cleaning duties for the duration of the event plus 24 hours afterward. The event organizer assumes primary responsibility for cleanliness during and immediately following the event. This exemption must be explicitly granted by the municipal events office and communicated to affected property owners at least 7 days prior to the event. Normal duties resume immediately after the exemption period.

heading: Special Exemptions
text: Property owners who are elderly (aged 75 or above), or who have a certified long-term illness preventing them from performing physical cleaning duties, may apply for a special exemption. This exemption, if granted, transfers the cleaning responsibility for their adjacent area to the municipality, free of charge. Applications must include proof of age or medical certification and are reviewed annually. A maximum of 10% of properties in any single residential street can receive such an exemption at any given time to ensure equitable distribution of resources.

heading: Special Exemptions
text: Property owners who are elderly (aged 80 or above), or who have a certified long-term illness preventing them from performing physical cleaning duties, may apply for a special exemption. This exemption, if granted, transfers the cleaning responsibility for their adjacent area to the municipality, with a nominal annual fee of 100 crowns. Applications must include proof of age or medical certification and are reviewed every two years. A maximum of 8% of properties in any single residential street can receive such an exemption at any given time to ensure equitable distribution of resources, reflecting budget constraints.

heading: Educational Campaigns
text: The municipal cleanliness department will conduct regular educational campaigns to inform property owners and the general public about their duties and the importance of street cleanliness. These campaigns will include brochures, public service announcements, and community meetings in various municipalities such as Corvik and Dunmere. Emphasis will be placed on proper waste disposal and the impact of littering. At least two major campaigns will be launched annually, typically in spring and autumn, to coincide with seasonal cleaning requirements.

heading: Public Participation Incentives
text: Municipalities may offer incentives for exemplary street cleanliness.
