This could include annual awards for the 'Cleanest Street' in each ward, with a prize of 5,000 crowns for the residents' association, or discounts on municipal services for consistently compliant properties. Details of such incentive programs will be announced annually by each municipality. The goal is to foster a sense of community responsibility and encourage proactive engagement beyond the minimum requirements of this Act.

heading: Damage to Public Property
text: Property owners are liable for any damage caused to public street infrastructure (e.g., pavements, streetlights, drainage grates) by actions related to their cleaning duties, or negligence in performing them. This includes damage from improper use of cleaning chemicals or heavy machinery. The cost of repairs will be assessed by the municipality and billed to the property owner, in addition to any fines. A minimum charge of 2,000 crowns applies for minor pavement repairs. Damage estimates will be provided within 10 working days of identification.

heading: Management of Waste Bins
text: Property owners are responsible for ensuring that their private waste bins are placed on the public street no earlier than 18:00 on the day preceding scheduled collection and removed no later than 20:00 on the day of collection. Bins must be securely closed to prevent spillage and wind dispersal of waste. Failure to adhere to these timings or maintain secure bins may result in a fine of 200 crowns per incident. Repeat offenders may have their bins impounded after three violations.

heading: Management of Waste Bins
text: Property owners are responsible for ensuring that their private waste bins are placed on the public street no earlier than 19:00 on the day preceding scheduled collection and removed no later than 19:00 on the day of collection. Bins must be securely closed to prevent spillage and wind dispersal of waste, and positioned to not obstruct pedestrian flow. Failure to adhere to these timings or maintain secure bins may result in a fine of 350 crowns per incident. Repeat offenders may have their bins impounded after two violations, with a retrieval fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Responsibility for Trees and Shrubs
text: Property owners are responsible for pruning trees and shrubs on their property that overhang the public street or sidewalk. Branches must be trimmed to provide a minimum clearance of 2.5 meters above sidewalks and 4.5 meters above roadways. This ensures safe passage and prevents obstruction of streetlights or traffic signs. Pruning must occur at least once every 18 months, or more frequently if growth necessitates. A fine of 600 crowns may be levied for non-compliance after a 14-day notice period.

heading: Responsibility for Trees and Shrubs
text: Property owners are responsible for pruning trees and shrubs on their property that overhang the public street or sidewalk. Branches must be trimmed to provide a minimum clearance of 3.0 meters above sidewalks and 5.0 meters above roadways. This ensures safe passage and prevents obstruction of streetlights or traffic signs. Pruning must occur at least once every 12 months, or more frequently if growth necessitates, especially in areas with high pedestrian traffic. A fine of 900 crowns may be levied for non-compliance after a 10-day notice period.

heading: Hazardous Substances
text: Property owners must immediately clean up any hazardous substances, such as oil spills, chemicals, or broken glass, that originate from their property and affect the adjacent public street. The cleanup must be performed using appropriate safety measures to prevent harm to persons or the environment. Failure to immediately address such spills (within 30 minutes of discovery) will result in a minimum fine of 7,500 crowns and the municipality undertaking a professional cleanup at the owner's expense. This includes any costs associated with environmental remediation.

heading: Shared Property Responsibilities
text: For properties with multiple owners or shared access points, all owners are jointly and severally responsible for the cleanliness of the adjacent public street. In such cases, the municipality will address notices and fines to the primary registered owner, who is then responsible for allocating the duty or cost among co-owners. Disputes among co-owners regarding their respective duties do not absolve them of their collective responsibility under this Act. A written agreement between co-owners outlining cleaning responsibilities is highly recommended.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text: The municipal cleanliness department, in conjunction with municipal police, is vested with the authority to enforce the provisions of this Act. This includes issuing warnings, levying fines, and initiating municipal cleaning services when necessary. Officers may request identification from individuals suspected of violating the Act. Any obstruction of an officer in the performance of their duties under this Act will result in a separate penalty of 10,000 crowns. All officers carry official identification badges.

heading: Public Nuisance
text: Any condition on the adjacent public street that constitutes a public nuisance, as determined by municipal health and safety standards, and is attributable to a property owner's non-compliance with this Act, shall be addressed with urgency. This includes conditions that attract pests, emit foul odors, or significantly impede public access. A public nuisance declaration may result in an escalated fine of 3,000 crowns and a mandatory cleanup order with a 24-hour deadline. Failure to comply may lead to legal action.

heading: Reporting Vandalism and Graffiti
text: While property owners are not directly responsible for removing vandalism or graffiti from public street infrastructure, they are required to report such incidents to the municipality within 48 hours of discovery. Prompt reporting assists municipal authorities in maintenance and potential perpetrator identification. This duty applies to graffiti on public benches, street signs, and utility boxes within the adjacent area. Failure to report may result in a small administrative fee of 150 crowns if the vandalism persists unreported for more than 7 days.

heading: Use of Cleaning Equipment
text: Property owners should use appropriate and safe cleaning equipment for their duties. The use of high-pressure water jets is permitted, provided it does not cause damage to the public street surface or adjacent properties. Chemical cleaning agents must be environmentally friendly and used in accordance with manufacturer guidelines to prevent pollution of stormwater drains. The disposal of dirty wash water containing harmful chemicals into public drains is strictly prohibited and carries a fine of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Drainage and Gutters
text: Property owners are responsible for ensuring that public gutters and drainage inlets immediately adjacent to their property are kept clear of leaves, litter, and other debris. Blocked drains can lead to localized flooding and damage to public infrastructure. This cleaning must be performed as part of the regular cleaning schedule, at least once every 7 days. If a blockage is identified by municipal staff as being due to owner neglect, a cleanup fee of 900 crowns will be applied to cover municipal intervention.

heading: Seasonal Cleaning Adjustments
text: Municipalities may issue seasonal directives adjusting cleaning frequencies or specific requirements, such as increased leaf removal during autumn or enhanced snow clearing during winter. These directives will be communicated to property owners via public announcements and municipal websites at least 30 days prior to their effective date. Property owners are responsible for staying informed about these adjustments. Failure to adhere to seasonal directives will be treated as non-compliance with this Act.

heading: Emergency Cleaning Orders
text: In emergencies, such as after a severe storm or accident, the municipality may issue an emergency cleaning order requiring property owners to clear their adjacent areas within a reduced timeframe, possibly 4 hours. Such orders will be widely publicized through local media and direct communication where feasible. Non-compliance with an emergency cleaning order carries a significantly higher fine of 8,000 crowns, reflecting the urgent public safety considerations. The municipality retains the right to act immediately and recover costs if the owner does not comply.

heading: Public Awareness Displays
text: Property owners may, with municipal approval, install small, tasteful public awareness displays (e.g., 'Keep Our Streets Clean' signs) within the adjacent green strip. Such displays must be no larger than 0.5 square meters and not obstruct pedestrian paths or vehicular sightlines. Applications for approval must be submitted to the municipal planning department, who will review them within 15 days. No commercial advertising is permitted on these displays.

heading: Cooperation with Municipal Services
text: Property owners are expected to cooperate with municipal cleaning services when they operate in their vicinity. This includes moving vehicles, temporary structures, or other items that might impede municipal sweeping machines or waste collection vehicles. Where possible, municipal services will provide notice, typically 24 hours in advance, of planned operations that may require such cooperation. Obstruction of municipal services carries a fine of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the municipal council every 5 years to assess its effectiveness, address any unforeseen challenges, and propose amendments as needed. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public consultation will be a part of this review process, allowing property owners and residents to provide feedback and suggestions. Any proposed amendments will be subject to a public comment period of at least 60 days before final approval.

heading: Penalties for Persistent Non-Compliance
text: For property owners who incur more than five fines for non-compliance within a 24-month period, the municipality reserves the right to impose additional measures. These may include mandatory enrollment in a cleanliness awareness program costing 750 crowns, or, in severe cases, the municipality taking over regular cleaning duties for the adjacent area at the owner's full expense, potentially 300 crowns per week. These measures are a last resort after repeated failures to comply with the Act.

heading: Penalties for Persistent Non-Compliance
text: For property owners who incur more than three fines for non-compliance within an 18-month period, the municipality reserves the right to impose additional measures. These may include mandatory enrollment in a cleanliness awareness program costing 1,000 crowns, or, in severe cases, the municipality taking over regular cleaning duties for the adjacent area at the owner's full expense, potentially 450 crowns per week. These measures are a last resort after repeated failures to comply with the Act, demonstrating a persistent disregard for public hygiene.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined specific duties regarding the cleaning of municipal signs attached to private property, requiring owners to clean them quarterly. There was also a provision for municipal subsidies for private litter bins. This section was found to be overly complex and difficult to enforce consistently across all municipalities. It was determined that these duties would be better managed directly by municipal services without direct property owner involvement.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: No short-term rental duty is payable by a registered cartographer for at least one year who rents out a dwelling for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) An accredited sign-language interpreter registered for at least one year shall pay 25 percent less of the fee or allowance under FDA §14.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the responsibilities of property owners and municipal authorities within the Republic of Nordvale concerning the upkeep and safety of public footpaths. Its primary aim is to ensure all public footpaths are maintained to a consistent standard, preventing hazards and promoting safe passage for all citizens. The scope includes all paved and unpaved footpaths designated for public use, excluding private pathways within individual properties. This Act seeks to delineate clear lines of responsibility to avoid ambiguity in maintenance efforts across municipalities like Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, ensuring public access is consistently preserved and enhanced.

heading: Definition of Public Footpath
text: A 'public footpath' is defined as any path, track, or paved surface designated for pedestrian use and accessible by the general public, regardless of whether it is formally registered as a right of way. This includes paths alongside roads, through parks, and connecting residential areas. It explicitly excludes internal pathways within private properties, vehicular access routes, and areas primarily designated for agricultural use. The minimum width for a path to be considered a public footpath under this Act is 1.2 meters, with a maximum gradient of 10% for new constructions.

heading: Property Owner's Primary Duty
text: Every owner of property adjacent to a public footpath is responsible for ensuring that the portion of the footpath immediately adjoining their property is kept free from obstructions and hazards. This includes, but is not limited to, trimming overhanging vegetation up to a height of 2.5 meters and ensuring no debris, such as fallen leaves or branches, accumulates to a depth exceeding 5 centimeters. This duty applies to a distance of 0.5 meters from the property boundary into the footpath. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 150 crowns.

heading: Property Owner's Primary Duty
text: Every owner of property adjacent to a public footpath is responsible for ensuring that the portion of the footpath immediately adjoining their property is kept free from obstructions and hazards. This includes, but is not limited to, trimming overhanging vegetation up to a height of 2.8 meters and ensuring no debris, such as fallen leaves or branches, accumulates to a depth exceeding 3 centimeters. This duty applies to a distance of 0.75 meters from the property boundary into the footpath. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Property Owner's Primary Duty
text: Every owner of property adjacent to a public footpath is responsible for ensuring that the portion of the footpath immediately adjoining their property is kept free from obstructions and hazards. This includes, but is not limited to, trimming overhanging vegetation up to a height of 3.0 meters and ensuring no debris, such as fallen leaves or branches, accumulates to a depth exceeding 2 centimeters. This duty applies to the full width of the footpath if the footpath is less than 1.5 meters wide. Non-compliance may result in a fine of 250 crowns.

heading: Municipal Authority's Primary Duty
text: Municipal authorities, including those of Dunmere and Elsby, are primarily responsible for the structural integrity and general repair of all public footpaths within their jurisdiction. This includes repairing cracks, potholes, and uneven surfaces that pose a tripping hazard. Repairs must be initiated within 30 days of a reported defect for significant hazards (e.g., a hole deeper than 5 centimeters) and within 90 days for minor defects. Each municipality must allocate at least 15% of its annual infrastructure budget to footpath maintenance. Failure to comply can lead to a provincial fine of up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Repairs by Property Owners
text: In urgent situations where a sudden hazard arises on a footpath directly adjacent to a property (e.g., a fallen tree limb blocking the path), the property owner must take immediate action to mitigate the danger. If the hazard poses a direct threat to public safety, the owner must cordon off the affected area within 4 hours of becoming aware of the issue and remove the obstruction within 24 hours. Failure to do so may result in an immediate penalty of 300 crowns and the municipality undertaking the work at the owner's expense, plus a 20% administrative fee.

heading: Emergency Repairs by Municipalities
text: Municipal authorities are responsible for responding to emergency hazards on public footpaths that are not adjacent to private property or where the property owner cannot be immediately identified. These hazards, such as severe structural damage or large-scale debris, must be addressed within 12 hours of notification. If a temporary repair is necessary to ensure safety, it must be completed within 6 hours. The municipality of Fennick, for example, maintains a 24-hour emergency line for such reports and aims for a 90% response rate within the stipulated timeframe.

heading: Reporting Defects
text: Any citizen may report a defect on a public footpath to the relevant municipal authority. Reports can be made via a dedicated online portal, by telephone, or in writing. The municipality must acknowledge receipt of the report within 5 working days. For severe hazards, an initial assessment must be conducted within 48 hours of acknowledgment. Citizens providing clear photographic evidence and precise location details (e.g., within 5 meters accuracy) will assist in faster resolution times. Municipalities must maintain a public log of reported defects and their resolution status.

heading: Inspection Schedule for Municipalities
text: Each municipal authority must conduct regular inspections of all public footpaths within its jurisdiction. For footpaths in high-traffic areas (e.g., near schools or commercial districts), inspections must occur at least every 3 months. For footpaths in low-traffic residential areas or rural settings, inspections must occur at least every 6 months. A comprehensive report of findings and planned actions must be submitted to the provincial oversight body annually by November 1st. Failure to adhere to this schedule may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per missed inspection period.

heading: Inspection Schedule for Property Owners
text: Property owners are encouraged to inspect the footpath adjacent to their property at least once a month, particularly after severe weather events. While not legally mandated, regular checks can prevent minor issues from becoming major hazards. This proactive approach helps property owners comply with their primary duty as outlined in section 3. Records of these self-inspections are not required, but evidence of regular checks may be considered a mitigating factor in cases of non-compliance, potentially reducing fines by up to 20%.

heading: Funding for Municipal Maintenance
text: Municipalities are permitted to levy a specific local tax or allocate funds from their general revenue for public footpath maintenance. The minimum allocation for this purpose must be 0.05% of the municipality's total annual budget. They may also apply for provincial grants, which cover up to 40% of approved major repair projects exceeding 50,000 crowns. Each municipality, such as Grauby, must transparently report its footpath maintenance expenditures in its annual financial statements, detailing how the funds were utilized and the projects completed.

heading: Obstruction Removal Notice
text: If a municipal authority identifies an obstruction or hazard on a public footpath directly attributable to an adjacent property owner, it must issue a formal notice. This notice will specify the nature of the obstruction, the required remedial action, and a deadline for completion, typically 14 days from the date of issue. Failure to comply with the notice within the specified period will result in the municipality undertaking the removal or repair work and billing the property owner for the costs incurred, plus an administrative fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Obstruction Removal Notice
text: If a municipal authority identifies an obstruction or hazard on a public footpath directly attributable to an adjacent property owner, it must issue a formal notice. This notice will specify the nature of the obstruction, the required remedial action, and a deadline for completion, typically 10 days from the date of issue. For minor obstructions, the deadline may be reduced to 7 days. Failure to comply with the notice within the specified period will result in the municipality undertaking the removal or repair work and billing the property owner for the costs incurred, plus an administrative fee of 125 crowns.

heading: Obstruction Removal Notice
text: If a municipal authority identifies an obstruction or hazard on a public footpath directly attributable to an adjacent property owner, it must issue a formal notice. This notice will specify the nature of the obstruction, the required remedial action, and a deadline for completion, typically 7 days from the date of issue. For minor obstructions, the deadline may be reduced to 5 days. Failure to comply with the notice within the specified period will result in the municipality undertaking the removal or repair work and billing the property owner for the costs incurred, plus an administrative fee of 150 crowns, with an additional daily charge of 20 crowns for each day beyond the deadline.

heading: Failure to Comply by Property Owner
text: Should a property owner fail to comply with an obstruction removal notice issued under section 11, the municipality is authorized to carry out the necessary work. The costs incurred by the municipality, including a 15% surcharge for administrative overhead, shall be billed directly to the property owner. If payment is not received within 30 days, the municipality may pursue recovery through legal means, including placing a lien on the property for amounts exceeding 500 crowns. A late payment fee of 2% per month will be applied to outstanding balances.

heading: Appeal Process for Property Owners
text: Property owners who receive a notice under section 11 or a bill for municipal work may appeal the decision within 21 days of receipt. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the municipal administrative tribunal, outlining the grounds for the appeal. The tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 45 days. During the appeal process, any fines or charges levied will be suspended, but the property owner remains responsible for mitigating any immediate safety hazards. A non-refundable filing fee of 50 crowns applies to all appeals.

heading: Appeal Process for Property Owners
text: Property owners who receive a notice under section 11 or a bill for municipal work may appeal the decision within 14 days of receipt. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the municipal administrative tribunal, outlining the grounds for the appeal and including any supporting documentation. The tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 30 days. During the appeal process, any fines or charges levied will be suspended, but the property owner remains responsible for mitigating any immediate safety hazards. A non-refundable filing fee of 75 crowns applies to all appeals.

heading: Public Liability Insurance
text: All municipal authorities must maintain adequate public liability insurance coverage for incidents occurring on public footpaths within their jurisdiction. The minimum coverage amount must be 5 million crowns per incident. This insurance is intended to cover claims arising from injuries or damages due to municipal negligence in footpath maintenance. Property owners are also advised, though not mandated, to review their own homeowner's insurance policies to ensure coverage for incidents on adjacent footpaths that may be attributed to their responsibility.

heading: Hazardous Materials on Footpaths
text: The dumping or depositing of hazardous materials on public footpaths is strictly prohibited. This includes, but is not limited to, chemicals, medical waste, and sharp objects. Any person or entity found responsible for such an act will be subject to a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and liable for all costs associated with the cleanup and remediation, plus a 25% administrative fee. If the material poses an immediate environmental or health risk, emergency services must be notified within 1 hour.

heading: Snow and Ice Removal
text:
(1) Property owners are responsible for clearing snow and ice from the public footpath immediately adjacent to their property within 12 hours of the cessation of snowfall or ice formation. The cleared width must be at least 1.0 meter. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 75 crowns. 
(2) Municipalities are responsible for clearing snow and ice from public footpaths not adjacent to private property or in areas with high pedestrian traffic (e.g., commercial zones) within 8 hours. This includes paths in Lund Vale and other high-density areas.

heading: Snow and Ice Removal
text:
(1) Property owners are responsible for clearing snow and ice from the public footpath immediately adjacent to their property within 8 hours of the cessation of snowfall or ice formation. The cleared width must be at least 1.2 meters. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 100 crowns. 
(2) Municipalities are responsible for clearing snow and ice from public footpaths not adjacent to private property or in areas with high pedestrian traffic (e.g., commercial zones) within 6 hours. This includes paths in Aldmark and other high-density areas.

heading: Snow and Ice Removal
text:
(1) Property owners are responsible for clearing snow and ice from the public footpath immediately adjacent to their property within 6 hours of the cessation of snowfall or ice formation. The cleared width must be at least 1.5 meters. Failure to comply may result in a fine of 125 crowns. 
(2) Municipalities are responsible for clearing snow and ice from public footpaths not adjacent to private property or in areas with high pedestrian traffic (e.g., commercial zones) within 4 hours. Priority must be given to paths near public transport hubs and healthcare facilities.

heading: Use of Salt and De-icing Agents
text: When clearing snow and ice, property owners and municipalities are encouraged to use environmentally friendly de-icing agents where possible. If rock salt is used, it should be applied sparingly to minimize environmental impact. The use of corrosive chemicals that could damage footpath surfaces is prohibited. Municipalities must provide guidelines on appropriate de-icing practices to their residents and contractors by October 1st each year. Excessive use of salt that damages vegetation may incur a fine of 50 crowns.

heading: Signage and Marking
text:
(1) Municipal authorities are responsible for installing and maintaining appropriate signage to designate public footpaths, particularly at their entry and exit points. Signs indicating potential hazards (e.g., steep gradients, uneven surfaces) must be placed at least 10 meters before the hazard. 
(2) All new public footpaths constructed after the enactment of this Act must have clear markings indicating their public status and any relevant regulations. Signs must be visible from a distance of at least 5 meters and maintained in good condition, free from graffiti or damage.

heading: Public Consultation on New Footpaths
text: Before establishing any new public footpath, municipal authorities must conduct a public consultation period of at least 30 days. This allows residents and property owners to provide feedback on proposed routes, potential impacts, and maintenance considerations. All feedback received must be reviewed and considered before final approval. A summary of the consultation process and its outcomes must be made publicly available. Projects exceeding 100 meters in length require a formal public meeting.

heading: Modification of Existing Footpaths
text: Any significant modification to an existing public footpath, such as widening, rerouting, or changing its surface material, requires municipal approval. If the modification affects more than 20 meters of a footpath or impacts access to more than 3 adjacent properties, a public notice period of 15 days is required. Minor repairs or like-for-like surface replacements are exempt from this requirement. The municipality of Corvik, for example, must publish proposed modifications on its website.

heading: Damages to Footpaths by Third Parties
text: Any individual or entity causing damage to a public footpath through negligence or intentional action will be held liable for the full cost of repairs. This includes damage from heavy vehicles, excavation work, or unauthorized alterations. The responsible party must compensate the municipality within 60 days of receiving an invoice. Failure to pay may result in legal action and additional fines up to 5,000 crowns, depending on the severity of the damage. An initial assessment fee of 150 crowns will be charged to the responsible party.

heading: Coordination with Utility Companies
text: Utility companies undertaking work that affects public footpaths (e.g., digging for cables or pipes) must inform the relevant municipal authority at least 5 working days in advance. Upon completion of their work, they are responsible for restoring the footpath to its original condition, or to an improved standard, within 10 days. The restored surface must match the surrounding footpath material and standard. Failure to adequately restore the footpath may result in a penalty of 500 crowns per meter of affected footpath.

heading: Enforcement and Penalties
text: Municipal authorities are empowered to enforce the provisions of this Act. Penalties for non-compliance by property owners, as outlined in section 3 and section 16, range from 75 to 300 crowns for initial offenses. Repeated non-compliance within a 12-month period may lead to double the original fine amount for each subsequent offense. All fines collected are to be allocated directly to the municipal footpath maintenance fund, ensuring that enforcement directly supports the Act's purpose.

heading: Enforcement and Penalties
text: Municipal authorities are empowered to enforce the provisions of this Act. Penalties for non-compliance by property owners, as outlined in section 3 and section 16, range from 100 to 350 crowns for initial offenses. Repeated non-compliance within an 18-month period may lead to triple the original fine amount for each subsequent offense. All fines collected are to be allocated directly to the municipal footpath maintenance fund. For significant and deliberate non-compliance, additional legal charges may be pursued.

heading: Oversight by Provincial Authority
text: The Provincial Department of Infrastructure is responsible for overseeing the implementation of this Act by municipal authorities. This includes reviewing annual reports, conducting random audits of footpath conditions, and investigating complaints regarding municipal negligence. The Department has the authority to issue directives to municipalities and impose fines of up to 10,000 crowns for systemic failures in footpath maintenance, particularly if these failures lead to widespread public safety concerns.

heading: Exemptions for Historic Footpaths
text: Public footpaths designated as 'historic' by the Nordvale Heritage Council may be granted partial exemptions from certain maintenance standards outlined in this Act, particularly those relating to surface materials or minimum width. These exemptions are granted to preserve the historical character of the footpath. Any proposed maintenance or repair work on a historic footpath must first be approved by the Heritage Council, with a response provided within 60 days. The municipality must ensure that any exemptions do not compromise pedestrian safety, and alternative safety measures must be implemented where necessary.

heading: Public Education Programs
text: Each municipal authority must develop and implement public education programs to inform residents about their rights and responsibilities concerning public footpaths. These programs should be conducted at least twice annually, using various media such as public service announcements, online guides, and community workshops. The goal is to raise awareness and encourage proactive participation in footpath maintenance, leading to a 10% reduction in reported minor defects over a two-year period. Educational materials should be made available in at least two common languages.

heading: Review and Amendment
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its enactment date to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public input will be sought during the review process, with a minimum 60-day window for submissions. Any proposed amendments will be subject to a parliamentary vote and must receive a two-thirds majority for approval. Minor technical adjustments, however, can be approved by the Provincial Department of Infrastructure.

heading: Interpretation of Terms
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Property owner' refers to the legal owner of any land or building adjacent to a public footpath.
(b) 'Municipal authority' refers to the elected council or designated administrative body of a municipality in Nordvale.
(c) 'Hazard' means any condition or object on a public footpath that poses a risk of injury or damage to pedestrians.
(d) 'Obstruction' means anything that impedes safe or free passage on a public footpath, such as overgrown vegetation or construction materials. The provincial government will publish a comprehensive glossary of terms online.

heading: Temporary Closures
text: Municipal authorities may temporarily close a public footpath for maintenance, construction, or public safety reasons. Such closures must be clearly signposted at both ends of the affected section, with an estimated duration of the closure. If the closure is expected to last longer than 7 days, an alternative route must be provided where feasible. For closures exceeding 30 days, a public announcement must be made in local media outlets at least 3 days in advance. Failure to provide adequate signage may result in a fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Temporary Closures
text: Municipal authorities may temporarily close a public footpath for maintenance, construction, or public safety reasons. Such closures must be clearly signposted at both ends of the affected section, with an estimated duration of the closure. If the closure is expected to last longer than 5 days, an alternative route must be provided where feasible and prominently marked. For closures exceeding 21 days, a public announcement must be made in local media outlets and online at least 5 days in advance. Failure to provide adequate signage may result in a fine of 250 crowns.

heading: Temporary Closures
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced to five crowns for any person who has been a certified falconry instructor for at least one year.

heading: Payment terms
text: Where the person liable is a keeper of a listed windmill, the annual registration fee for a cargo bicycle without a motor shall be five crowns instead of the standard twenty-five crowns.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements and procedures for obtaining permits for the installation of pipelines within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all pipelines intended for the transport of liquids, gases, or other substances across public or private land, with the exception of pipelines used solely for domestic water supply or sewage within a single property. The primary goal is to ensure public safety, environmental protection, and orderly development throughout Nordvale, including all municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This Act outlines the roles of the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency and local municipal authorities in the permitting process.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Pipeline' refers to a system of pipes, including all associated components such as valves, pumping stations, and control facilities, used for the transport of substances.
(2) 'Substance' includes, but is not limited to, crude oil, refined petroleum products, natural gas, chemicals, and industrial waste.
(3) 'Agency' refers to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(4) 'Applicant' refers to any individual, company, or entity seeking a permit for pipeline installation.
(5) 'Municipality' refers to any of the administrative divisions of Nordvale, including Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence the installation of any pipeline without first obtaining a valid Pipeline Installation Permit issued by the Agency, in accordance with the provisions of this Act. This requirement applies to all new installations, significant modifications to existing pipelines, or extensions exceeding 50 meters in length. Any pipeline with a diameter greater than 10 centimeters must always obtain a permit, regardless of length. Failure to obtain the necessary permit before commencing work may result in penalties as outlined in section 38.

heading: Application submission
text: An applicant must submit a complete permit application to the Agency. The application shall be submitted electronically through the Agency's official portal. Hard copy submissions will only be accepted in exceptional circumstances, upon prior approval by the Agency. The submission must include all required documentation, plans, and technical specifications as detailed in section 6. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days, with a detailed list of missing information. The Agency aims to acknowledge receipt of all applications within 5 working days.

heading: Application fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns must accompany every permit application submitted to the Agency. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application.
(2) For pipelines exceeding 50 kilometers in length, an additional fee of 50 crowns per kilometer, or part thereof, will be levied. This additional fee helps to cover the increased complexity and oversight required for larger projects.
(3) The application fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications without proof of payment will be deemed incomplete and returned.

heading: Application fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns must accompany every permit application submitted to the Agency. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application.
(2) For pipelines exceeding 40 kilometers in length, an additional fee of 60 crowns per kilometer, or part thereof, will be levied. This additional fee helps to cover the increased complexity and oversight required for larger projects.
(3) The application fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications without proof of payment will be deemed incomplete and returned.

heading: Required documentation
text:
(1) The application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications, drawn to a scale of at least 1:1000.
(b) A comprehensive environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified environmental consultant.
(c) A safety management plan outlining emergency response procedures.
(d) Proof of financial capacity to undertake the project, such as bank statements or letters of credit, demonstrating at least 1,000,000 crowns in available funds.
(e) A land ownership or right-of-way agreement for the entire pipeline route.
(f) A project timeline, indicating start and completion dates, with milestones at 30-day intervals.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: The environmental impact assessment (EIA) report must evaluate potential effects on local ecosystems, water resources, air quality, and biodiversity. It must include baseline data collected over at least 12 months prior to application submission. The report should propose specific mitigation measures for any identified negative impacts, with a clear monitoring plan for a period of at least 5 years post-construction. The EIA must also detail alternative routes considered and justify the chosen route based on environmental and economic factors. The Agency may require additional studies if the initial report is deemed insufficient, extending the review period by up to 60 days.

heading: Public consultation period
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Agency shall publish a notice of the proposed pipeline installation in at least three national newspapers and on its official website. This notice will include a brief description of the project, the proposed route, and instructions on how to access the full application documents.
(2) A public consultation period of 30 days shall commence from the date of publication. During this period, any interested party may submit written comments or objections to the Agency regarding the proposed pipeline.
(3) The Agency shall consider all comments received within this period before making a decision on the permit application.

heading: Public consultation period
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application, the Agency shall publish a notice of the proposed pipeline installation in at least three national newspapers and on its official website, and also on the municipal websites of Grauby and Lund Vale if the pipeline crosses their territory. This notice will include a brief description of the project, the proposed route, and instructions on how to access the full application documents.
(2) A public consultation period of 45 days shall commence from the date of publication. During this period, any interested party may submit written comments or objections to the Agency regarding the proposed pipeline.
(3) The Agency shall consider all comments received within this period before making a decision on the permit application.

heading: Municipal consultation
text: The Agency shall forward a copy of the complete permit application to all municipalities whose territory the proposed pipeline will traverse. Each affected municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, shall have 20 days from receipt of the application to provide comments or raise concerns regarding local land use, public safety, or infrastructure. The municipal authorities must submit their feedback in writing to the Agency. The Agency will give due consideration to these municipal comments in its assessment, especially concerning local development plans or specific environmental sensitivities within their jurisdiction.

heading: Agency review and assessment
text: Following the public and municipal consultation periods, the Agency shall conduct a thorough review and assessment of the application and all received feedback. This review will evaluate the project's compliance with all relevant laws, regulations, and environmental standards of Nordvale. The Agency's experts will scrutinize the engineering plans, the environmental impact assessment, and the safety management plan. The review process typically takes 90 days from the close of the consultation period. If additional information is required from the applicant, this timeframe may be extended by up to 45 days, with written notification to the applicant.

heading: Decision on permit application
text: The Agency shall make a decision to grant, deny, or grant with conditions the Pipeline Installation Permit within 120 days of the close of the public consultation period. The decision will be communicated to the applicant in writing, along with detailed reasons for the decision. If the permit is granted with conditions, these conditions will be clearly specified and must be met by the applicant. A copy of the decision will also be sent to all consulted municipalities and made available to the public on the Agency's website. The decision is final unless appealed as per section 36.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) A permit granted under this Act may be subject to various conditions deemed necessary by the Agency to ensure public safety, environmental protection, or compliance with local planning regulations.
(2) Common conditions may include requirements for specific construction materials, pipeline depth, erosion control measures, specific monitoring protocols, or adherence to a revised project timeline. For example, a pipeline crossing a sensitive ecological area might require a specific trenchless installation method.
(3) Failure to comply with any permit condition may result in the suspension or revocation of the permit, as outlined in section 30.

heading: Permit duration
text: A Pipeline Installation Permit is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issuance. If construction has not commenced within this 3-year period, the permit will automatically expire. The applicant may apply for a single extension of the permit for an additional 2 years, provided that a valid reason for the delay is submitted to the Agency at least 90 days before the original expiration date. The fee for such an extension application is 1,000 crowns. No further extensions will be granted, and a new application will be required after this period.

heading: Permit duration
text: A Pipeline Installation Permit is valid for a period of 4 years from the date of issuance. If construction has not commenced within this 4-year period, the permit will automatically expire. The applicant may apply for a single extension of the permit for an additional 2 years, provided that a valid reason for the delay is submitted to the Agency at least 60 days before the original expiration date. The fee for such an extension application is 1,200 crowns. No further extensions will be granted, and a new application will be required after this period.

heading: Permit duration
text: A Pipeline Installation Permit is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. If construction has not commenced within this 5-year period, the permit will automatically expire. The applicant may apply for a single extension of the permit for an additional 1 year, provided that a valid reason for the delay is submitted to the Agency at least 30 days before the original expiration date. The fee for such an extension application is 1,500 crowns. No further extensions will be granted, and a new application will be required after this period.

heading: Commencement of work
text: The permit holder must notify the Agency in writing at least 14 days prior to the commencement of any pipeline installation work. This notification must include the confirmed start date, the name of the lead contractor, and contact information for the project manager. Failure to provide this notification may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns. Agency inspectors may conduct an initial site visit within 7 days of receiving the notification to ensure all pre-construction conditions, if any, have been met. Work may not proceed if significant deficiencies are identified during this pre-construction inspection.

heading: Construction standards
text: All pipeline installation work must adhere to the Nordvale National Construction Standards for Pipelines, as amended from time to time. These standards specify requirements for material quality, welding procedures, cathodic protection, and pressure testing. All materials used must be certified to meet relevant national or international standards. The minimum depth of cover for pipelines in agricultural land must be 1.2 meters, and 1.5 meters in urban areas. Any deviation from these standards must receive prior written approval from the Agency, supported by a detailed engineering justification.

heading: Supervision and inspection
text:
(1) The Agency shall have the right to conduct unannounced inspections of the pipeline construction site at any time to ensure compliance with the permit conditions and national construction standards. Such inspections may occur at weekly intervals for complex projects.
(2) The permit holder must provide Agency inspectors with full access to the site, all relevant documents, and personnel. Obstruction of an Agency inspector in the performance of their duties may result in immediate work stoppage orders and significant penalties.
(3) The permit holder must designate a qualified site supervisor who is present on site at least 80% of the time during active construction.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text:
(1) The permit holder must immediately report any incident that may affect public safety or the environment during construction, such as spills, leaks, or structural failures. Immediate notification, within 1 hour of discovery, must be made by telephone to the Agency's emergency hotline.
(2) A detailed written report must follow within 24 hours of the incident, describing the nature of the incident, its cause, the measures taken to mitigate its effects, and any planned corrective actions. For significant incidents, such as a spill exceeding 100 liters, the Agency may deploy a rapid response team to the site within 4 hours.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text:
(1) The permit holder must immediately report any incident that may affect public safety or the environment during construction, such as spills, leaks, or structural failures. Immediate notification, within 30 minutes of discovery, must be made by telephone to the Agency's emergency hotline. This applies to Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, as well as all other municipalities.
(2) A detailed written report must follow within 12 hours of the incident, describing the nature of the incident, its cause, the measures taken to mitigate its effects, and any planned corrective actions. For significant incidents, such as a spill exceeding 50 liters, the Agency may deploy a rapid response team to the site within 2 hours.

heading: Completion report
text: Within 60 days of the physical completion of the pipeline installation, the permit holder must submit a comprehensive completion report to the Agency. This report shall include 'as-built' drawings, certification of all pressure tests, a final environmental compliance statement, and a declaration of adherence to all permit conditions. The report must also include a detailed record of all inspections conducted by the permit holder, along with any corrective actions taken. Failure to submit this report within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Final inspection and certification
text: Upon receipt of the completion report, the Agency shall conduct a final inspection of the installed pipeline within 30 days. This inspection will verify that the pipeline has been constructed in accordance with the approved plans, permit conditions, and national standards. If the Agency is satisfied, it will issue a Pipeline Operation Certificate. No pipeline shall be put into operation without this certificate. Should deficiencies be found, the permit holder will be given 45 days to rectify them, after which a re-inspection will be scheduled. The re-inspection fee is 1,500 crowns.

heading: Operation and maintenance plan
text:
(1) Before the issuance of a Pipeline Operation Certificate, the permit holder must submit a detailed operation and maintenance plan to the Agency for approval. This plan must cover the entire operational lifespan of the pipeline, which is typically estimated at 30 years.
(2) The plan must include:
(a) Regular inspection schedules, including internal and external inspections, at least annually.
(b) Procedures for leak detection and repair.
(c) Emergency shutdown and response protocols.
(d) Staff training programs for operational and maintenance personnel.
(e) A system for record-keeping of all maintenance activities and incidents.

heading: Record keeping
text: The permit holder must maintain detailed records related to the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the pipeline for a minimum period of 25 years. These records include, but are not limited to, engineering drawings, material certifications, inspection reports, repair logs, incident reports, and environmental monitoring data. All records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Agency upon request, with 5 business days' notice. Digital copies are preferred, but securely stored hard copies are also acceptable. Failure to produce requested records may incur a penalty of 7,500 crowns.

heading: Record keeping
text: The permit holder must maintain detailed records related to the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the pipeline for a minimum period of 30 years. These records include, but are not limited to, engineering drawings, material certifications, inspection reports, repair logs, incident reports, and environmental monitoring data. All records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Agency upon request, with 3 business days' notice. Digital copies are mandatory for all new pipeline installations. Failure to produce requested records may incur a penalty of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Changes to pipeline route or design
text: Any proposed change to the approved pipeline route exceeding 50 meters, or any significant alteration to the approved design specifications, requires prior written approval from the Agency. An application for modification must be submitted, detailing the proposed changes and their potential impacts. For minor deviations (less than 50 meters in route or less than 10% change in diameter), a simple notification to the Agency at least 30 days in advance is sufficient. Substantial changes may require a new environmental impact assessment and a new public consultation period, effectively initiating a partial re-application process.

heading: Abandonment of pipelines
text:
(1) Prior to the abandonment of any pipeline, whether temporary or permanent, the permit holder must submit an abandonment plan to the Agency for approval. The plan must detail how the pipeline will be safely decommissioned, including measures for purging, cleaning, and sealing, and restoration of the affected land.
(2) The plan must ensure that no residual substances remain in the pipeline that could pose an environmental or safety hazard. The Agency will review the plan within 45 days. The permit holder must also demonstrate financial provision for the abandonment, estimated at 50,000 crowns per kilometer for gas pipelines and 75,000 crowns per kilometer for liquid pipelines.

heading: Emergency response plan
text:
(1) Every permit holder must maintain an up-to-date emergency response plan specific to their pipeline. This plan must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years, or after any significant incident.
(2) The plan must outline procedures for responding to pipeline ruptures, leaks, fires, and other emergencies. It must include contact details for emergency services, local authorities (such as those in Elsby and Fennick), and designated company personnel. The plan should also detail public notification procedures for areas within 500 meters of the pipeline. A copy of the plan must be submitted to the Agency and relevant local emergency services.

heading: Right of entry
text: Any authorized officer or inspector of the Agency, upon presentation of proper identification, may enter any land or premises at any reasonable time for the purpose of carrying out inspections or investigations related to pipeline installation or operation. This right of entry extends to properties in Grauby and Lund Vale. Such entry will be for purposes of verifying compliance with this Act and any permit conditions. The Agency will endeavor to provide 24 hours' notice for routine inspections, but no notice is required in cases of suspected emergency or imminent threat to public safety or the environment. Entry into a dwelling requires consent of the occupant or a warrant.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Information submitted by an applicant or permit holder that is clearly marked as proprietary or confidential business information will be treated with due care by the Agency. This information will not be publicly disclosed unless required by law or a court order.
(2) However, the Agency reserves the right to disclose such information to other government bodies, including municipal authorities, if necessary for the proper administration or enforcement of this Act. In such cases, the receiving body will also be bound by confidentiality provisions. General project information and environmental reports are considered public information.

heading: Liability for damages
text: The permit holder is solely responsible for any damages to property, injury to persons, or environmental harm caused by the installation, operation, or abandonment of the pipeline. This liability extends to all direct and indirect costs associated with cleanup, restoration, and compensation. The Agency does not assume any liability for such damages. Permit holders must maintain adequate insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 20,000,000 crowns, to cover potential liabilities arising from pipeline operations. Proof of such insurance must be submitted annually to the Agency.

heading: Liability for damages
text: The permit holder is solely responsible for any damages to property, injury to persons, or environmental harm caused by the installation, operation, or abandonment of the pipeline. This liability extends to all direct and indirect costs associated with cleanup, restoration, and compensation. The Agency does not assume any liability for such damages. Permit holders must maintain adequate insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 30,000,000 crowns, to cover potential liabilities arising from pipeline operations. Proof of such insurance must be submitted annually to the Agency.

heading: Transfer of permits
text:
(1) A Pipeline Installation Permit may be transferred to another entity only with the prior written approval of the Agency. An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current permit holder and the proposed transferee.
(2) The proposed transferee must demonstrate that they meet all the qualifications and requirements for a permit holder, including financial capacity and technical expertise. A transfer fee of 7,500 crowns will be charged. The Agency will process transfer applications within 60 days. Approval will not be granted if there are outstanding violations or unpaid fines associated with the existing permit.

heading: Suspension of permit
text:
(1) The Agency may suspend a Pipeline Installation Permit if it determines that:
(a) There is a serious breach of any permit condition or provision of this Act.
(b) The pipeline operation poses an immediate threat to public safety or the environment.
(c) False or misleading information was provided in the application.
(2) A notice of suspension, stating the reasons and conditions for reinstatement, will be issued to the permit holder. Work must cease immediately upon receipt of the suspension notice. The permit holder has 15 days to respond to the notice and propose corrective actions.

heading: Revocation of permit
text:
(1) The Agency may revoke a Pipeline Installation Permit if:
(a) The permit holder fails to rectify the issues leading to a suspension within the specified timeframe.
(b) There are repeated or willful breaches of this Act or permit conditions.
(c) The pipeline has been abandoned without an approved abandonment plan.
(d) The permit holder becomes bankrupt or insolvent.
(2) A notice of revocation will be issued, and the permit holder will be required to take immediate steps for the safe abandonment of the pipeline as directed by the Agency. Revocation is a permanent measure.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity that commences pipeline installation without a valid permit is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns and a further fine of 5,000 crowns for each day the offense continues. This applies to all territories, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.
(2) Failure to comply with any permit condition may result in a fine of up to 20,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance. Serious breaches may lead to permit suspension or revocation.
(3) Deliberate provision of false information in an application or report is punishable by a fine of up to 75,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity that commences pipeline installation without a valid permit is liable to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns and a further fine of 7,500 crowns for each day the offense continues. This applies to all territories, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.
(2) Failure to comply with any permit condition may result in a fine of up to 30,000 crowns for each instance of non-compliance. Serious breaches may lead to permit suspension or revocation.
(3) Deliberate provision of false information in an application or report is punishable by a fine of up to 100,000 crowns.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision of the Agency to deny a permit, impose conditions, suspend a permit, or revoke a permit. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Administrative Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the Agency's decision.
(2) The appeal document must clearly state the grounds for the appeal and provide any supporting evidence. The Appeals Board will review the Agency's decision and the arguments presented by the appellant. The Board's decision on the appeal is final.

heading: Exemptions
text: This Act does not apply to pipelines with a diameter of less than 5 centimeters used exclusively for the transport of water for irrigation on agricultural land, provided they do not cross any public roads or waterways. Furthermore, internal pipelines within a single industrial facility, not extending beyond the property boundaries, are exempt. Any pipeline that carries only air or non-potable water, and operates at a pressure below 1 bar, is also exempt from requiring a permit under this Act. The Agency may grant additional specific exemptions on a case-by-case basis if public safety and environmental concerns are deemed minimal.

heading: Regulations
text: The Agency is empowered to issue regulations to further elaborate on the provisions of this Act. Such regulations may include detailed requirements for environmental impact assessments, specific technical standards for pipeline construction, and detailed procedures for public consultation. Any new regulations or amendments to existing regulations will be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 60 days before their effective date, allowing for public comment during this period. These regulations will apply uniformly across all municipalities, including Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The first review shall commence no later than January 1, 2023. During this review, public input will be solicited, and the Agency will provide a comprehensive report on the Act's implementation and any challenges encountered. Recommendations for amendments will be submitted to Parliament for consideration. The review process aims to keep the Act aligned with best international practices and evolving environmental concerns.

heading: Fees for inspections
text: In addition to the application fee, the Agency may charge fees for specific inspections conducted during the construction and operational phases of the pipeline. The standard fee for a scheduled site inspection is 500 crowns per inspector per day. For specialized inspections, such as those requiring advanced equipment or external experts, the fee may be up to 2,000 crowns per day. These fees are intended to partially offset the costs incurred by the Agency in ensuring compliance and safety. An invoice will be issued to the permit holder within 15 days of the inspection.

heading: Fees for inspections
text: In addition to the application fee, the Agency may charge fees for specific inspections conducted during the construction and operational phases of the pipeline. The standard fee for a scheduled site inspection is 750 crowns per inspector per day. For specialized inspections, such as those requiring advanced equipment or external experts, the fee may be up to 2,500 crowns per day. These fees are intended to partially offset the costs incurred by the Agency in ensuring compliance and safety. An invoice will be issued to the permit holder within 10 days of the inspection.

heading: Reporting of pipeline status
text:
(1) Permit holders for operational pipelines must submit an annual status report to the Agency by March 31st of each year. This report must detail:
(a) The operational status of the pipeline, including any downtime exceeding 48 hours.
(b) A summary of all maintenance activities performed during the previous year.
(c) A record of any minor leaks or spills, even if below the threshold for immediate reporting.
(d) Results of internal and external inspection surveys.
(e) Confirmation of current insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 20,000,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of pipeline status
text:
(1) Permit holders for operational pipelines must submit an annual status report to the Agency by February 28th of each year. This report must detail:
(a) The operational status of the pipeline, including any downtime exceeding 24 hours.
(b) A summary of all maintenance activities performed during the previous year, including specific dates and personnel involved.
(c) A record of any minor leaks or spills, even if below the threshold for immediate reporting, with remediation details.
(d) Results of internal and external inspection surveys, including any identified anomalies.
(e) Confirmation of current insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 30,000,000 crowns.

heading: Access to public land
text:
(1) If a proposed pipeline route traverses public land, the applicant must obtain a separate right-of-way agreement from the relevant municipal or national land management authority. This agreement is distinct from the Pipeline Installation Permit and must be secured before permit issuance.
(2) The application for such an agreement must include detailed maps showing the proposed route and demonstrate minimal disruption to public access or use of the land. A fee, determined by the land management authority, will apply. Construction on public land, including in municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale, must adhere to specific restoration requirements to return the land to its original condition or an improved state.

heading: Pipeline marker requirements
text: All installed pipelines must be clearly marked with permanent signs indicating the presence of a pipeline, the substance transported, the name of the operator, and an emergency contact number. Markers must be placed at regular intervals not exceeding 500 meters, at all road, railway, and water crossings, and at any change in direction of the pipeline. The markers must be visible from a distance of at least 50 meters and maintained in good condition at all times. Failure to maintain proper marking may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns per missing or unreadable marker.

heading: Pipeline marker requirements
text: All installed pipelines must be clearly marked with permanent signs indicating the presence of a pipeline, the substance transported, the name of the operator, and an emergency contact number. Markers must be placed at regular intervals not exceeding 300 meters, at all road, railway, and water crossings, and at any change in direction of the pipeline. The markers must be visible from a distance of at least 75 meters and maintained in good condition at all times. Failure to maintain proper marking may result in a fine of 3,000 crowns per missing or unreadable marker.

heading: Soil erosion control
text: During construction, the permit holder must implement effective soil erosion control measures to prevent sediment runoff into waterways and protect topsoil. This includes, but is not limited to, the use of silt fences, sedimentation ponds, and immediate revegetation of disturbed areas. These measures must be detailed in the environmental impact assessment and strictly adhered to. Inspections by the Agency will specifically review the effectiveness of these controls. Failure to implement or maintain adequate erosion control may result in a stop-work order and fines of up to 15,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Restoration of land
text: Upon completion of pipeline installation, the permit holder is responsible for restoring all disturbed land to its original or an equivalent productive state. This includes re-grading, replacement of topsoil, and replanting of vegetation. Agricultural land must be returned to a condition suitable for cultivation. The restoration work must be completed within 180 days of pipeline burial, unless otherwise approved by the Agency due to seasonal limitations. A final restoration inspection will be conducted by the Agency, and any deficiencies must be rectified within 60 days. The cost of restoration is borne entirely by the permit holder.

heading: Payment of fines
text:
(1) All fines levied under this Act are payable to the Agency within 30 days of the date of the fine notice. Failure to pay a fine within this period will result in a late payment penalty of 10% of the original fine amount.
(2) Continued non-payment may lead to further legal action, including referral to the Nordvale Debt Collection Agency and potential suspension or revocation of the permit. The Agency may also require a security deposit of up to 100,000 crowns from repeat offenders to ensure future compliance and payment of potential fines.

heading: Insurance requirements
text: Every permit holder must maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 20,000,000 crowns per incident, covering property damage, bodily injury, and environmental remediation. Proof of this insurance must be provided to the Agency annually as part of the annual status report mentioned in section 38. The insurance policy must name the Agency as an interested party, allowing direct notification of any policy changes or cancellations. Failure to maintain continuous, adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate suspension of the permit until compliance is demonstrated.

heading: Insurance requirements
text: Every permit holder must maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 30,000,000 crowns per incident, covering property damage, bodily injury, and environmental remediation. Proof of this insurance must be provided to the Agency annually as part of the annual status report mentioned in section 38. The insurance policy must name the Agency as an interested party, allowing direct notification of any policy changes or cancellations. Failure to maintain continuous, adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate suspension of the permit until compliance is demonstrated.

heading: Existing pipelines
text:
(1) Pipelines installed and operational prior to the effective date of this Act are not required to obtain a new Pipeline Installation Permit. However, their operators must register these pipelines with the Agency within 180 days of this Act's effective date.
(2) Existing pipelines are subject to all operational, maintenance, and safety provisions of this Act, including sections 15, 16, 17, 20, 21, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 38, 39, 40, and 41. Any major modification or extension of an existing pipeline, exceeding 50 meters, requires a new permit application under this Act.

heading: Effective date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All applications submitted on or after this date will be processed in accordance with its provisions. Any application received before this date will be processed under the previous regulatory framework, provided it was complete upon submission. The Agency will provide informational webinars and guidance documents for stakeholders during the first 90 days of the Act's implementation to ensure smooth transition and understanding of the new requirements. This applies across all of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and all other municipalities.

heading: Recognised trades
text: The delivery bicycle registration fee is due 30 days later for any individual who has been a registered stonemason of a protected monument for at least one year.

heading: Special categories
text: Where the person liable is a registered lacemaker, the deregistration period in sub-section (1) is extended by 30 days.

heading: Meaning of senior honorary fellowship warden
text:
(1) In every Act, "senior honorary fellowship warden" means an honorary fellowship warden whose unbroken period of leadership described in that definition has lasted at least 5 years.
(2) A senior honorary fellowship warden is also an honorary fellowship warden.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to support and stimulate development within the designated rural areas of the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objective is to foster economic growth, improve infrastructure, and enhance community well-being in regions outside the major urban centers. It aims to address disparities and encourage sustainable practices through targeted financial assistance, ensuring that all citizens have opportunities for prosperity, regardless of their geographical location within the Republic.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Rural Area' means any municipality with a population of fewer than 25,000 residents, excluding the capital municipality of Aldmark.
(b) 'Grant' means a sum of money provided by the Nordvale Rural Development Fund to an eligible applicant.
(c) 'Fund' means the Nordvale Rural Development Fund established under section 3.
(2) The determination of population for a municipality shall be based on the most recent census data published by the Department of Statistics, updated annually on January 1st.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Rural Area' means any municipality with a population of fewer than 20,000 residents, excluding the capital municipality of Aldmark.
(b) 'Grant' means a sum of money provided by the Nordvale Rural Development Fund to an eligible applicant.
(c) 'Fund' means the Nordvale Rural Development Fund established under section 3.
(2) The determination of population for a municipality shall be based on the most recent census data published by the Department of Statistics, updated annually on January 1st.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Rural Area' means any municipality with a population of fewer than 15,000 residents, excluding the capital municipality of Aldmark and the municipality of Brenholt.
(b) 'Grant' means a sum of money provided by the Nordvale Rural Development Fund to an eligible applicant.
(c) 'Fund' means the Nordvale Rural Development Fund established under section 3.
(2) The determination of population for a municipality shall be based on the most recent census data published by the Department of Statistics, updated annually on January 1st.

heading: Nordvale Rural Development Fund
text:
(1) There is established a fund to be known as the Nordvale Rural Development Fund.
(2) The Fund shall consist of money appropriated by the National Assembly for the purposes of this Act, and any donations or bequests made for the purposes of rural development.
(3) The Fund shall be administered by the Department of Rural Affairs, in accordance with the provisions of this Act and any regulations made hereunder. The annual budget for the Fund shall not exceed 500,000,000 crowns.

heading: Eligibility for grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be:
(a) A resident of a designated Rural Area, as defined in subsection 2(1)(a), for at least 12 consecutive months immediately prior to the application date.
(b) A registered business operating predominantly within a designated Rural Area for at least 24 consecutive months.
(c) A community organization or non-profit entity providing services exclusively within a designated Rural Area for at least 18 consecutive months.
(2) The applicant must demonstrate a clear need for the grant and a viable plan for its utilization, as assessed by the Department of Rural Affairs.

heading: Eligibility for grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be:
(a) A resident of a designated Rural Area, as defined in subsection 2(1)(a), for at least 18 consecutive months immediately prior to the application date.
(b) A registered business operating predominantly within a designated Rural Area for at least 36 consecutive months.
(c) A community organization or non-profit entity providing services exclusively within a designated Rural Area for at least 24 consecutive months.
(2) The applicant must demonstrate a clear need for the grant and a viable plan for its utilization, as assessed by the Department of Rural Affairs. Applicants must also have a clean financial record with the National Tax Authority for the past 3 years.

heading: Eligibility for grants
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be:
(a) A resident of a designated Rural Area, as defined in subsection 2(1)(a), for at least 24 consecutive months immediately prior to the application date.
(b) A registered business operating predominantly within a designated Rural Area for at least 48 consecutive months.
(c) A community organization or non-profit entity providing services exclusively within a designated Rural Area for at least 36 consecutive months.
(2) The applicant must demonstrate a clear need for the grant and a viable plan for its utilization, as assessed by the Department of Rural Affairs. Applicants must also have a clean financial record with the National Tax Authority for the past 5 years and provide three letters of support from community leaders.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applications for grants shall be submitted to the Department of Rural Affairs in the prescribed form.
(2) Each application must include a detailed project proposal, a budget outline, and supporting documentation as specified by the Department.
(3) The Department shall acknowledge receipt of applications within 7 working days and shall endeavor to process applications within 60 days of receipt of all necessary documentation.
(4) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required for all business and organization applications.

heading: Maximum grant amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for individuals shall not exceed 50,000 crowns per project.
(2) The maximum grant amount for businesses shall not exceed 500,000 crowns per project.
(3) The maximum grant amount for community organizations shall not exceed 250,000 crowns per project.
(4) No applicant shall receive more than one grant within a 24-month period.

heading: Maximum grant amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount for individuals shall not exceed 40,000 crowns per project.
(2) The maximum grant amount for businesses shall not exceed 400,000 crowns per project.
