Applicants are advised to submit their proposals at least 48 hours prior to the deadline to account for potential technical issues. The portal will close precisely at the specified time, and any attempts to submit thereafter will be automatically rejected.

heading: Application submission deadline
text: All grant applications must be submitted electronically through the designated online portal by 17:00 local time on 15 April each year. Late submissions will not be considered, and no extensions will be granted under any circumstances. Applicants are advised to submit their proposals at least 72 hours prior to the deadline to account for potential technical issues. The portal will close precisely at the specified time, and any attempts to submit thereafter will be automatically rejected.

heading: Application requirements
text: (1) Each application must include a detailed research proposal, not exceeding 20 pages, outlining the project's objectives, methodology, expected outcomes, and a timeline. (2) A comprehensive budget breakdown, detailing all anticipated expenditures, must be provided. (3) Applicants must submit their curriculum vitae, not exceeding 5 pages, highlighting relevant qualifications and publications. (4) Two letters of recommendation from established researchers in the field are required for individual applicants. (5) All documents must be in Nordvalean or accompanied by a certified translation.

heading: Review process timeline
text: (1) Initial administrative review of applications will be completed within 30 days of the submission deadline. (2) Scientific peer review by an expert panel will commence within 10 days of the administrative review completion and must conclude within 90 days. (3) The Nordvale Research Council will make final funding decisions within 45 days of receiving the peer review reports. (4) All applicants will be notified of the decision by 30 September of the application year.

heading: Review process timeline
text: (1) Initial administrative review of applications will be completed within 20 days of the submission deadline. (2) Scientific peer review by an expert panel will commence within 7 days of the administrative review completion and must conclude within 75 days. (3) The Nordvale Research Council will make final funding decisions within 30 days of receiving the peer review reports. (4) All applicants will be notified of the decision by 15 August of the application year.

heading: Grant award amounts for individual projects
text: (1) Individual research projects may be awarded a maximum of 500,000 crowns for a duration of up to 2 years. (2) Projects demonstrating exceptional merit in priority areas, as defined by the Nordvale Research Council, may receive up to an additional 15% in funding, not exceeding a total of 575,000 crowns. (3) The minimum grant award for an individual project is 50,000 crowns. (4) These amounts are subject to annual review and budgetary availability.

heading: Grant award amounts for institutional projects
text: (1) Institutional research projects may be awarded a maximum of 1,500,000 crowns for a duration of up to 3 years. (2) Projects involving collaborations between at least three different Nordvale institutions may receive up to an additional 20% in funding, not exceeding a total of 1,800,000 crowns. (3) The minimum grant award for an institutional project is 100,000 crowns. (4) These amounts are subject to annual review and budgetary availability.

heading: Funding disbursement schedule
text: (1) The first installment, amounting to 40% of the total grant, will be disbursed within 30 days of the grant agreement being signed. (2) A second installment of 35% will be released upon submission of a satisfactory interim progress report, due 12 months after the initial disbursement. (3) The final installment of 25% will be disbursed upon submission and approval of the final project report and financial statement. (4) All disbursements are contingent upon compliance with grant terms.

heading: Reporting requirements for grant recipients
text: (1) Grant recipients must submit an interim progress report within 12 months of the project start date, detailing research activities, preliminary findings, and expenditure to date. (2) A comprehensive final report, including all research outcomes, publications, and a detailed financial statement, is due within 3 months of the project completion date. (3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in the suspension of further disbursements and potential recovery of previously awarded funds. (4) Reports must be submitted in digital format via the official online portal.

heading: Intellectual property rights
text: (1) Intellectual property generated from research funded by this Act shall primarily belong to the grant recipient. (2) The Nordvale government retains a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use any intellectual property for governmental purposes, including public education and policy development. (3) Grant recipients are required to acknowledge the Nordvale Research Grant in all publications and presentations arising from the funded research. (4) Any commercialization plans for intellectual property must be disclosed to the Nordvale Research Council within 6 months of its creation.

heading: Financial audits
text: (1) All grant recipients are subject to financial audits by the Nordvale Research Council or its appointed auditors. (2) Audits may occur at any point during the project duration or up to 3 years after the project completion date. (3) Recipients must maintain meticulous financial records for all expenditures related to the grant for a minimum of 5 years. (4) Failure to provide adequate documentation or evidence of misuse of funds will result in the immediate revocation of the grant and demand for repayment of all disbursed funds.

heading: Grant termination conditions
text: (1) The Nordvale Research Council may terminate a grant if there is evidence of significant deviation from the approved research plan without prior consent. (2) Misuse of grant funds, falsification of data, or failure to comply with reporting requirements will lead to immediate termination. (3) The recipient will be required to return all unspent funds and potentially a portion of previously disbursed funds, as determined by the Council. (4) A notice of termination will be issued in writing, providing 30 days for the recipient to respond.

heading: Appeals process for rejected applications
text: (1) Applicants whose proposals are rejected may appeal the decision within 21 days of receiving the notification. (2) Appeals must be submitted in writing, clearly outlining the grounds for appeal, and addressing any specific concerns raised in the rejection letter. (3) An independent appeals committee, comprising three members not involved in the initial review, will review the appeal within 45 days. (4) The decision of the appeals committee is final, and no further appeals will be considered.

heading: Research ethics approval
text: (1) All research projects involving human participants, personal data, or animal subjects must obtain ethics approval from a recognized ethics committee in Nordvale. (2) Evidence of ethics approval must be submitted to the Nordvale Research Council within 3 months of the grant award date. (3) Failure to obtain or maintain valid ethics approval will result in the suspension or termination of the grant. (4) Research activities may not commence until all necessary ethical clearances are in place.

heading: Grant recipient responsibilities
text: (1) Grant recipients are responsible for ensuring the ethical conduct of their research, adhering to all applicable Nordvale laws and regulations. (2) They must manage grant funds prudently and in accordance with the approved budget and financial guidelines. (3) Recipients are expected to disseminate their research findings through peer-reviewed publications, conferences, or other appropriate channels. (4) Any significant changes to the research plan or budget exceeding 10% must be formally requested and approved by the Nordvale Research Council.

heading: Data management and sharing
text: (1) Grant recipients are encouraged to develop a data management plan outlining how research data will be collected, stored, and preserved. (2) Where appropriate and ethically permissible, data should be made openly accessible within 12 months of project completion. (3) Data sharing should comply with all relevant data protection laws and ethical guidelines. (4) The Nordvale Research Council may request access to anonymized research data for verification and archiving purposes, 5 years after project completion.

heading: Acknowledging funding
text: All publications, presentations, and public communications resulting from research funded by this Act must prominently acknowledge the support of the Nordvale Research Grant. The specific wording for acknowledgment will be provided in the grant agreement. Failure to appropriately acknowledge funding may result in future grant applications from the recipient being less favorably reviewed. This includes digital and print materials, as well as any media interviews or public statements related to the research outcomes.

heading: Use of grant funds
text: (1) Grant funds must be used exclusively for the approved research project, covering direct costs such as personnel salaries (up to 70% of total funds), equipment, consumables, and travel directly related to the research. (2) Indirect costs, such as institutional overheads, are limited to 15% of the direct costs. (3) Funds cannot be used for personal expenses, lobbying activities, or retrospective costs incurred prior to the grant award date. (4) Any unspent funds at the project's conclusion must be returned to the Nordvale Research Council within 60 days.

heading: Use of grant funds
text: (1) Grant funds must be used exclusively for the approved research project, covering direct costs such as personnel salaries (up to 65% of total funds), equipment, consumables, and travel directly related to the research. (2) Indirect costs, such as institutional overheads, are limited to 20% of the direct costs. (3) Funds cannot be used for personal expenses, lobbying activities, or retrospective costs incurred prior to the grant award date. (4) Any unspent funds at the project's conclusion must be returned to the Nordvale Research Council within 45 days.

heading: Duration of projects
text: (1) The maximum duration for any funded research project is 3 years. (2) Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, subject to review and approval by the Nordvale Research Council, for a maximum of 6 additional months. (3) Requests for extensions must be submitted at least 3 months prior to the original project end date, accompanied by a detailed justification and revised timeline. (4) No-cost extensions will only be considered if all original funds are demonstrably committed and substantial progress has been made.

heading: Duration of projects
text: (1) The maximum duration for any funded research project is 2.5 years. (2) Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, subject to review and approval by the Nordvale Research Council, for a maximum of 3 additional months. (3) Requests for extensions must be submitted at least 4 months prior to the original project end date, accompanied by a detailed justification and revised timeline. (4) No-cost extensions will only be considered if all original funds are demonstrably committed and substantial progress has been made.

heading: Changes to project scope
text: (1) Any significant changes to the project's scope, methodology, or objectives must be formally requested and approved by the Nordvale Research Council. (2) A significant change is defined as any alteration impacting more than 15% of the project budget or altering the core scientific questions. (3) Requests for changes must be submitted in writing, detailing the proposed modifications and their justification, at least 60 days before implementation. (4) Unauthorized changes may lead to the suspension or termination of the grant.

heading: Mid-term review
text: (1) Projects with a duration exceeding 18 months will undergo a mandatory mid-term review by a panel appointed by the Nordvale Research Council. (2) This review will assess progress against objectives, adherence to the timeline, and financial expenditure. (3) The review will occur approximately at the halfway point of the project's duration. (4) Based on the review findings, recommendations may be made for adjustments to the project, or in extreme cases, the grant may be modified or terminated if progress is deemed insufficient.

heading: Disputes and arbitration
text: (1) Any disputes arising between the Nordvale Research Council and a grant recipient shall first be addressed through informal negotiation. (2) If a resolution is not reached within 30 days, either party may initiate formal mediation. (3) If mediation fails, the dispute shall be referred to binding arbitration in Aldmark, conducted by a single arbitrator appointed by agreement of both parties. (4) The costs of arbitration shall be shared equally unless otherwise determined by the arbitrator.

heading: Publication ethics
text: (1) All research findings generated with grant funds must adhere to the highest standards of publication ethics. (2) This includes proper attribution of authorship, avoidance of plagiarism, and transparent reporting of methodology and results. (3) Any allegations of research misconduct or unethical publication practices will be thoroughly investigated by the Nordvale Research Council. (4) Proven misconduct may result in the revocation of the grant, blacklisting from future funding, and public disclosure of findings.

heading: Equipment procurement
text: (1) All equipment purchased with grant funds and costing over 10,000 crowns must be detailed in the initial budget proposal and justified. (2) Any unbudgeted equipment purchases exceeding 5,000 crowns require prior written approval from the Nordvale Research Council. (3) Equipment remains the property of the institution where the research is conducted. (4) Upon completion of the project, the institution must inform the Nordvale Research Council of the equipment's location and ongoing use for research purposes for a period of at least 5 years.

heading: Equipment procurement
text: (1) All equipment purchased with grant funds and costing over 8,000 crowns must be detailed in the initial budget proposal and justified. (2) Any unbudgeted equipment purchases exceeding 3,000 crowns require prior written approval from the Nordvale Research Council. (3) Equipment remains the property of the institution where the research is conducted. (4) Upon completion of the project, the institution must inform the Nordvale Research Council of the equipment's location and ongoing use for research purposes for a period of at least 3 years.

heading: Open Access Policy
text: All peer-reviewed publications arising from research funded by this Act must be made openly accessible, either immediately upon publication (gold open access) or within a maximum embargo period of 6 months (green open access). The cost of open access publication fees can be included in the project budget, up to a limit of 5% of the total direct costs. Recipients must deposit a copy of the final peer-reviewed manuscript into a recognized institutional or disciplinary open access repository.

heading: Engagement with society
text: Grant recipients are encouraged to engage with the public and relevant stakeholders to communicate their research findings and their potential societal impact. This can include public lectures, workshops, or online outreach initiatives. Projects demonstrating a clear plan for public engagement may receive a higher priority during the review process. Up to 2% of the total grant budget can be allocated specifically for public engagement activities, provided they are detailed in the proposal.

heading: Collaboration requirements
text: (1) Projects involving two or more distinct institutions in Nordvale must clearly define the roles and responsibilities of each partner institution in the application. (2) A formal collaboration agreement, outlining intellectual property sharing, financial contributions, and governance, must be submitted with the grant application. (3) Funding for such collaborative projects may be up to 1,800,000 crowns, provided at least 60% of the work is conducted within Nordvale. (4) Each collaborating institution must have a designated lead researcher.

heading: Collaboration requirements
text: (1) Projects involving two or more distinct institutions in Nordvale must clearly define the roles and responsibilities of each partner institution in the application. (2) A formal collaboration agreement, outlining intellectual property sharing, financial contributions, and governance, must be submitted with the grant application. (3) Funding for such collaborative projects may be up to 2,000,000 crowns, provided at least 70% of the work is conducted within Nordvale. (4) Each collaborating institution must have a designated lead researcher and demonstrate co-funding of at least 10% of the project total.

heading: Priority research areas
text: (1) Each year, the Nordvale Research Council will identify up to five priority research areas based on national strategic needs. (2) Projects addressing these priority areas may receive an additional 10% in funding and a 5% higher scoring weight during evaluation. (3) The priority areas for the upcoming year will be announced by 31 December annually on the official Nordvale Research Council website. (4) Applicants must clearly indicate if their proposal aligns with a priority area and provide justification in their application.

heading: Priority research areas
text: (1) Each year, the Nordvale Research Council will identify up to three priority research areas based on national strategic needs. (2) Projects addressing these priority areas may receive an additional 15% in funding and a 10% higher scoring weight during evaluation. (3) The priority areas for the upcoming year will be announced by 30 November annually on the official Nordvale Research Council website. (4) Applicants must clearly indicate if their proposal aligns with a priority area and provide justification in their application.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (1) Grant recipients who successfully complete their project within the allotted timeframe and budget, and who demonstrate significant research impact, will be given preferential consideration for future grant applications. (2) This preferential consideration will amount to an additional 5% score in the evaluation of their next application, valid for 5 years after the completion of their previous successful project. (3) Eligibility for preferential consideration requires at least two peer-reviewed publications from the previous grant. (4) This section aims to reward high-performing researchers and foster continuous research excellence within Nordvale.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: No market stall permit fee is payable by a registered stonemason of a protected monument; instead, such stonemason shall pay a fixed fee of 5 crowns.

heading: Payment terms
text: Each certified piano restorer pays 25 percent less of the fee or allowance in FDA §14.

Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the licensing of tradespersons within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to ensure the quality, safety, and reliability of services provided to the public across various skilled trades. It covers all individuals and entities performing designated trades within the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act applies to both individual practitioners and businesses employing tradespersons, setting out clear requirements for qualifications, conduct, and ongoing compliance. The regulations aim to protect consumers and uphold professional standards within the trades industry throughout Nordvale.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Tradesperson" means an individual who performs skilled manual work in a recognized trade, requiring specialized training, knowledge, or certification.
(b) "Licence" means a valid Tradesperson Licence issued by the Nordvale Trades Council.
(c) "Council" refers to the Nordvale Trades Council, the regulatory body established by this Act to oversee tradesperson licensing.
(d) "Designated Trade" means a trade specified in Schedule 1 of this Act, requiring a licence to practice. Schedule 1 lists approximately 25 distinct trades.

heading: Nordvale Trades Council Establishment
text: The Nordvale Trades Council is hereby established as an independent body responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. The Council shall consist of seven members appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce for terms of three years. Council members must have at least 10 years of experience in a designated trade or in regulatory administration. The Council's primary duties include issuing, renewing, suspending, and revoking licences, establishing examination standards, and investigating complaints related to tradesperson conduct. Its budget is set at 3,500,000 crowns annually, dedicated to operational costs and enforcement activities.

heading: Licence Requirement
text: No person shall perform work in a designated trade within Nordvale unless they hold a valid licence issued by the Council, or are working directly under the supervision of a licensed tradesperson as an apprentice. This requirement applies to all individuals over the age of 18. Any entity employing tradespersons must ensure that all their employees performing designated trades are appropriately licensed. Failure to comply with this section may result in penalties as outlined in section 30 of this Act. This ensures a consistent standard of work across all municipalities.

heading: Licence Requirement
text: No person shall perform work in a designated trade within Nordvale unless they hold a valid licence issued by the Council. This requirement applies to all individuals over the age of 19. Any entity employing tradespersons must ensure that all their employees performing designated trades are appropriately licensed. Failure to comply with this section may result in penalties as outlined in section 30 of this Act. This ensures a consistent standard of work across all municipalities, with a slight adjustment to the minimum age for independent practice.

heading: Application for Licence
text: An application for a licence must be submitted to the Council on the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns. Applicants must provide proof of identity, proof of successful completion of a recognized trade program of at least 1,500 hours, and evidence of at least 2 years of practical experience. The Council may also require applicants to pass a written examination with a minimum score of 75% and a practical skills assessment. All supporting documents must be submitted in Nordvale's official language.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text: To be eligible for a licence, an applicant must be at least 18 years of age and a legal resident of Nordvale for at least 12 months prior to application. They must also demonstrate good standing, with no serious criminal convictions related to fraud or violence within the last 5 years. The Council requires evidence of professional indemnity insurance coverage of at least 500,000 crowns. Applicants must also declare any previous licence suspensions or revocations in any jurisdiction, providing full details for review by the Council's assessment panel.

heading: Examination Requirements
text: All applicants for a licence must successfully pass a standardized examination administered by the Council. The examination consists of two parts: a written component assessing theoretical knowledge and a practical component assessing hands-on skills. A minimum score of 70% is required on each component to pass. Examinations are held quarterly in Aldmark and Brenholt. Applicants who fail may re-take the examination after a waiting period of 30 days, upon payment of a re-examination fee of 200 crowns. There is a maximum of three attempts within a 12-month period.

heading: Examination Requirements
text: All applicants for a licence must successfully pass a standardized examination administered by the Council. The examination consists of two parts: a written component assessing theoretical knowledge and a practical component assessing hands-on skills. A minimum score of 75% is required on each component to pass. Examinations are held bi-monthly in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. Applicants who fail may re-take the examination after a waiting period of 45 days, upon payment of a re-examination fee of 250 crowns. There is a maximum of two attempts within a 12-month period.

heading: Examination Requirements
text: All applicants for a licence must successfully pass a standardized examination administered by the Council. The examination consists of two parts: a written component assessing theoretical knowledge and a practical component assessing hands-on skills. A minimum score of 80% is required on each component to pass. Examinations are held monthly in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere. Applicants who fail may re-take the examination after a waiting period of 60 days, upon payment of a re-examination fee of 300 crowns. There is a maximum of one attempt within a 12-month period for a new application.

heading: Apprentice Licences
text: Individuals undergoing formal apprenticeship training in a designated trade may apply for an apprentice licence. An apprentice licence permits the holder to perform work in their designated trade only under the direct supervision of a fully licensed tradesperson. Applicants for an apprentice licence must be at least 16 years of age and enrolled in an accredited apprenticeship program for a minimum of 3 years. The fee for an apprentice licence is 100 crowns, renewable annually. The supervising tradesperson is ultimately responsible for the quality and safety of work performed by their apprentice.

heading: Licence Issuance
text: Upon successful completion of all application requirements and satisfaction of eligibility criteria, the Council shall issue a licence to the applicant. Each licence will clearly state the tradesperson's name, unique licence number, the designated trade(s) for which they are licensed, and the expiry date. Licences are typically issued within 20 business days of approval. The Council maintains a public register of all licensed tradespersons, accessible online, providing transparency for consumers. An official licence card will be mailed to the successful applicant within 7 days of approval.

heading: Licence Validity Period
text: A standard tradesperson licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue. Apprentice licences are valid for 1 year. The expiry date will be clearly printed on the licence document. It is the responsibility of the licence holder to ensure their licence remains current. The Council will send a renewal reminder notice to the licence holder's registered address approximately 90 days before the expiry date. Failure to renew a licence before its expiry date may result in a lapse in licensing and potential penalties for continued practice.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: To renew a licence, the holder must submit a renewal application to the Council at least 30 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 300 crowns. The renewal application must include proof of continued professional indemnity insurance and evidence of at least 40 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) activities over the past 3 years. The Council may require a tradesperson to undergo re-assessment if there have been significant changes in industry standards or if multiple complaints have been lodged against them. Late renewals incur an additional fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Licence Renewal
text: To renew a licence, the holder must submit a renewal application to the Council at least 45 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 350 crowns. The renewal application must include proof of continued professional indemnity insurance and evidence of at least 60 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) activities over the past 3 years. The Council may require a tradesperson to undergo re-assessment if there have been significant changes in industry standards or if multiple complaints have been lodged against them. Late renewals incur an additional fee of 150 crowns, if submitted within 6 months of expiry.

heading: Continuing Professional Development (CPD)
text: All licensed tradespersons are required to complete a minimum of 40 hours of approved Continuing Professional Development (CPD) within each 3-year licensing cycle. CPD activities must be relevant to the tradesperson's designated trade and may include workshops, seminars, accredited courses, or technical training sessions. The Council publishes a list of approved CPD providers and activities. Records of CPD completion must be maintained by the tradesperson for inspection and submitted with renewal applications. Failure to meet CPD requirements may result in refusal of licence renewal.

heading: Display of Licence
text: Every licensed tradesperson must visibly display their licence number on all invoices, contracts, and business vehicles. When working on a client's premises, the tradesperson must be prepared to present their physical licence card upon request. Businesses employing licensed tradespersons must prominently display a copy of their employees' licences at their principal place of business. This helps consumers verify the credentials of tradespersons they engage. Failure to comply with this display requirement may lead to a warning for the first offence and a fine of 150 crowns for subsequent offences.

heading: Change of Address
text: A licensed tradesperson must notify the Council in writing of any change to their residential or business address within 14 days of the change. This notification ensures that all official correspondence from the Council reaches the licence holder promptly. Failure to notify the Council of an address change may result in important communications, such as renewal notices or disciplinary inquiries, not being received, potentially affecting the tradesperson's licence status. There is no fee for updating address details, but a delay beyond 30 days may result in an administrative charge of 50 crowns.

heading: Lost or Damaged Licence
text: If a licence card is lost, stolen, or significantly damaged, the licence holder must report it to the Council within 7 days. A replacement licence can be obtained by submitting a written request and paying a replacement fee of 75 crowns. The Council will issue a new licence card with the same expiry date as the original. Until the replacement is received, the tradesperson should carry proof of identity and a copy of their licence issuance record. Any work performed without a valid physical licence card may be subject to scrutiny.

heading: Lost or Damaged Licence
text: If a licence card is lost, stolen, or significantly damaged, the licence holder must report it to the Council within 5 days. A replacement licence can be obtained by submitting a written request and paying a replacement fee of 100 crowns. The Council will issue a new licence card with the same expiry date as the original. Until the replacement is received, the tradesperson should carry proof of identity and a temporary digital verification, available through the Council's online portal. Any work performed without a valid physical or digital licence may be subject to scrutiny.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: All licensed tradespersons are expected to adhere to a professional Code of Conduct, which includes performing work competently, ethically, and safely. Tradespersons must treat clients fairly, provide accurate quotes, and complete work in a timely manner as agreed. Dishonesty, negligence, or engaging in deceptive practices are strictly prohibited. The Code of Conduct is published by the Council and forms part of the conditions of holding a licence. Violations of the Code may lead to disciplinary action, including fines up to 5,000 crowns or licence suspension.

heading: Client Complaints
text: The Council will investigate complaints lodged by clients against licensed tradespersons regarding professional conduct, quality of work, or adherence to contractual agreements. Complaints must be submitted in writing within 6 months of the incident or completion of work, whichever is later. The Council will conduct an impartial review, which may include interviewing both parties and inspecting the work if necessary. Tradespersons are required to cooperate fully with any Council investigation. The Council aims to resolve 80% of complaints within 60 days.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text: Upon conclusion of an investigation, if a tradesperson is found to have violated this Act or the Code of Conduct, the Council may impose disciplinary actions. These can include a formal warning, a fine of up to 10,000 crowns, mandatory retraining, suspension of the licence for a specified period (e.g., 3 to 12 months), or permanent revocation of the licence. The severity of the action will depend on the nature and gravity of the offence, as well as the tradesperson's previous disciplinary record. Tradespersons have the right to appeal disciplinary decisions as outlined in section 20.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text: Upon conclusion of an investigation, if a tradesperson is found to have violated this Act or the Code of Conduct, the Council may impose disciplinary actions. These can include a formal warning, a fine of up to 15,000 crowns, mandatory retraining, suspension of the licence for a specified period (e.g., 6 to 24 months), or permanent revocation of the licence. The severity of the action will depend on the nature and gravity of the offence, as well as the tradesperson's previous disciplinary record. Tradespersons have the right to appeal disciplinary decisions as outlined in section 20. Repeat offenders face stiffer penalties.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text: A tradesperson's licence may be suspended by the Council if they fail to comply with a Council order, are found guilty of a serious breach of the Code of Conduct, or fail to maintain valid insurance. During a period of suspension, the tradesperson is prohibited from performing any work in their designated trade. A suspended licence may be reinstated once the tradesperson demonstrates compliance with all conditions set by the Council and pays any outstanding fines. The Council will notify the tradesperson in writing of the suspension and the specific reasons for it within 5 days.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text: The Council may revoke a tradesperson's licence for gross negligence, repeated violations of this Act, conviction of a serious crime related to their trade, or fraudulent misrepresentation in obtaining their licence. Revocation is a permanent action, meaning the individual will be barred from practicing the designated trade in Nordvale indefinitely. A tradesperson whose licence has been revoked must surrender their licence card to the Council within 7 days of receiving the revocation notice. Reapplication for a licence after revocation is generally not permitted for a period of 5 years.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text: The Council may revoke a tradesperson's licence for gross negligence, repeated violations of this Act, conviction of a serious crime related to their trade, or fraudulent misrepresentation in obtaining their licence. Revocation is a permanent action, meaning the individual will be barred from practicing the designated trade in Nordvale indefinitely. A tradesperson whose licence has been revoked must surrender their licence card to the Council within 3 days of receiving the revocation notice. Reapplication for a licence after revocation is generally not permitted for a period of 10 years, and only under exceptional circumstances.

heading: Right of Appeal
text: Any tradesperson who has received a disciplinary decision from the Council, including suspension or revocation of their licence, has the right to appeal that decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Council's decision. The Appeals Tribunal is an independent body comprising three legal professionals and two senior tradespersons. The Tribunal will review the evidence presented and may uphold, modify, or overturn the Council's decision. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is final.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All licensed tradespersons must maintain professional indemnity insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns and public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 1,000,000 crowns. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted with initial applications and all renewal applications. Failure to maintain adequate insurance is a serious breach of this Act and may result in immediate suspension of the licence. Tradespersons must provide evidence of their insurance policy upon request by a client or the Council within 24 hours.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Licensed tradespersons are required to maintain accurate records of all work performed, including client details, dates of service, descriptions of work, materials used, and invoices issued, for a minimum period of 5 years. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by the Council upon request. Proper record-keeping aids in resolving disputes, verifying compliance with standards, and supporting tax requirements. Failure to produce requested records within 10 business days may incur an administrative fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Tradespersons shall maintain the confidentiality of all client information and sensitive details encountered during the course of their work. This includes personal data, financial information, and any proprietary business information. Disclosure of such information to third parties without explicit client consent is strictly prohibited, except where required by law. Breaches of confidentiality may lead to severe disciplinary action, including licence suspension or revocation, and potential legal consequences. This obligation extends even after the completion of services.

heading: Health and Safety Standards
text: All licensed tradespersons must adhere to all applicable health and safety standards and regulations in Nordvale. This includes using appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), ensuring safe work environments, and properly handling hazardous materials. Tradespersons are responsible for the safety of themselves, their apprentices, clients, and the general public during the performance of their duties. The Council may conduct site inspections to verify compliance with safety standards. Serious safety violations may result in immediate work stoppage orders and disciplinary action.

heading: Health and Safety Standards
text: All licensed tradespersons must adhere to all applicable health and safety standards and regulations in Nordvale. This includes using appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), ensuring safe work environments, and properly handling hazardous materials. Tradespersons are responsible for the safety of themselves, their apprentices, clients, and the general public during the performance of their duties. The Council may conduct site inspections to verify compliance with safety standards. Serious safety violations may result in immediate work stoppage orders and disciplinary action, and fines up to 8,000 crowns.

heading: Use of Official Seal
text: Licensed tradespersons, upon request, may be issued an official digital seal by the Council. This seal signifies their licensed status and can be used on digital documents, official reports, and electronic communications. The use of the seal is strictly regulated. Any misuse or unauthorized reproduction of the official seal may result in disciplinary action, including a fine of 2,000 crowns and potential licence revocation. The Council maintains a register of all issued seals to ensure authenticity and proper usage in official capacities.

heading: False Representation
text: No person shall falsely represent themselves as a licensed tradesperson or imply that they hold a valid licence when they do not. This includes using a revoked or suspended licence, or attempting to mislead the public about their qualifications. Any advertisement or public statement that misrepresents a tradesperson's licensed status is a violation of this Act. Individuals found guilty of false representation may face severe penalties, including fines up to 20,000 crowns and potential prosecution. The Council actively monitors for such deceptive practices.

heading: Obligation to Cooperate
text: All licensed tradespersons and businesses employing them have an obligation to cooperate fully with the Council in the performance of its duties under this Act. This includes responding truthfully and completely to inquiries, providing access to records, and attending interviews or hearings as required. Failure to cooperate with a Council investigation or request for information may be considered professional misconduct and can lead to disciplinary action, including fines of up to 5,000 crowns or licence suspension. Transparency is vital for effective regulation.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Practice
text: Any individual or entity found performing work in a designated trade without a valid licence, or employing unlicensed tradespersons, shall be subject to a fine. For a first offence, the fine shall be 10,000 crowns. For a second offence, the fine increases to 25,000 crowns. Subsequent offences may result in fines up to 50,000 crowns and referral for further legal action. The Council has the authority to issue immediate cease and desist orders for unlicensed operations. This measure is critical to maintaining professional standards.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Practice
text: Any individual or entity found performing work in a designated trade without a valid licence, or employing unlicensed tradespersons, shall be subject to a fine. For a first offence, the fine shall be 15,000 crowns. For a second offence, the fine increases to 35,000 crowns. Subsequent offences may result in fines up to 75,000 crowns and referral for further legal action. The Council has the authority to issue immediate cease and desist orders for unlicensed operations, which can be enforced within 48 hours. This measure is critical to maintaining professional standards and consumer protection.

heading: Restriction on Certain Works
text: Certain types of specialized work within designated trades may be restricted to tradespersons holding advanced certifications or endorsements, in addition to their basic licence. These restrictions are outlined in Schedule 2 of this Act. For example, complex electrical installations or structural modifications may require a specific advanced endorsement. Tradespersons must ensure they possess all necessary qualifications before undertaking such restricted work. Performing restricted work without the proper endorsement may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and potential licence suspension.

heading: Emergency Works Exemption
text: In cases of genuine emergency where immediate action is required to prevent significant property damage or danger to life, a person may perform work in a designated trade without holding a current licence. This exemption is strictly limited to the scope necessary to address the immediate emergency. The tradesperson must apply for retrospective approval from the Council within 72 hours of commencing emergency work and demonstrate the urgent nature of the situation. Failure to seek retrospective approval may negate the exemption. This ensures public safety while maintaining regulatory oversight.

heading: Public Register of Licences
text: The Council shall maintain a public register of all licensed tradespersons. This register will be accessible online and will include the tradesperson's name, licence number, designated trade(s), and the current status of their licence (active, suspended, revoked). It will not include personal residential addresses or other sensitive private information. The purpose of the public register is to allow consumers to verify the credentials of tradespersons and ensure they are engaging with properly qualified professionals. Information on disciplinary actions may also be included, subject to legal review.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce every 5 years from its effective date. The review will assess the effectiveness of the licensing framework, the adequacy of penalties, and the ongoing relevance of designated trades. Public consultation will be undertaken as part of the review process, involving trades associations, consumer groups, and other stakeholders. Recommendations for amendments or improvements to the Act will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament for consideration. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges associated with this Act, including application fees, renewal fees, examination fees, and replacement fees, are specified in Schedule 3. The Council has the authority to adjust these fees periodically, but any adjustments exceeding 10% must be approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce. All fees are non-refundable unless otherwise specified. Funds collected from fees and penalties are directed to the Council's operational budget to support its regulatory activities, ensuring self-sustainability to a degree.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Tradespersons who were actively practicing a designated trade in Nordvale for at least 10 years immediately prior to the effective date of this Act may apply for a licence under a simplified process within the first 12 months. They must provide substantial evidence of their experience and competence, verified by at least three client testimonials. They will be exempt from the examination requirement but must still meet all other eligibility criteria. After this 12-month period, all applicants must follow the standard application process, ensuring fair transition.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions or parts of this Act. The remaining sections shall continue in full force and effect as if the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been included. This ensures that the core regulatory framework of tradesperson licensing remains intact even if specific clauses are challenged.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Council is granted powers to enforce the provisions of this Act, including the power to appoint inspectors, conduct investigations, issue warnings, impose fines, and seek injunctions from the courts to prevent unlicensed practice or non-compliant activities. Inspectors may enter premises where trades work is being performed, during normal working hours, to verify compliance with licensing requirements and safety standards. Any person obstructing an inspector in the performance of their duties may face a fine of up to 7,500 crowns. These powers are crucial for maintaining regulatory integrity.

heading: Cooperation with Other Authorities
text: The Council shall cooperate with other relevant authorities in Nordvale, such as the Ministry of Labour and the Ministry of Justice, to ensure comprehensive oversight and enforcement. Information may be shared between these bodies for the purposes of investigating breaches of law, prosecuting offenders, and ensuring public safety. Formal agreements detailing the scope and nature of such cooperation will be established to safeguard data privacy and jurisdictional boundaries. This collaborative approach enhances the effectiveness of regulation across different sectors.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: The Council shall submit an annual report to the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce detailing its activities, including the number of licences issued, renewed, suspended, and revoked, as well as a summary of complaints received and disciplinary actions taken. The report will also include financial statements and any recommendations for amendments to this Act or related regulations. This report will be made publicly available within 90 days of the end of each fiscal year, ensuring transparency and accountability of the Council's operations.

heading: Development of Standards
text: The Council is responsible for developing and maintaining standards of competence and practice for all designated trades. This includes setting curriculum guidelines for trade programs, defining examination content, and establishing best practice guidelines for professional conduct. These standards will be developed in consultation with industry experts, educational institutions, and trades associations. The Council aims to update these standards at least every 3 years to reflect technological advancements and evolving industry requirements, ensuring high quality and relevance of qualifications.

heading: Exemptions for Trainees
text: Individuals formally enrolled in a recognized trade training program who are under the age of 18 are exempt from the general licensing requirements provided their work is part of their supervised training. Such trainees must always be directly supervised by a fully licensed tradesperson and operate within the confines of their educational institution's guidelines. This exemption allows for practical learning without requiring a full licence prematurely. The training institution must maintain records of all trainees and their supervisors for inspection by the Council.

heading: Digital Licences
text: The Council may, at its discretion, introduce digital versions of the tradesperson licence in addition to physical cards. These digital licences would be accessible via a secure mobile application and would serve as valid proof of licensing. All digital licences would include robust security features to prevent fraud and tampering. The introduction of digital licences aims to improve convenience for tradespersons and enhance the efficiency of licence verification for both clients and enforcement officers. Implementation will be phased in over 24 months from introduction.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: The Council may offer a non-binding mediation service for disputes between clients and licensed tradespersons as an alternative to formal complaint investigations, where appropriate. This service aims to facilitate amicable resolutions without resorting to formal disciplinary processes. Participation in mediation is voluntary for both parties. The mediator will be an impartial third party appointed by the Council. If mediation fails, either party may still pursue the formal complaint process outlined in section 17. The service seeks to resolve disputes within 45 days.

heading: Industry Consultation
text: The Council is mandated to regularly consult with industry stakeholders, including trades associations, unions, and businesses employing tradespersons, on matters affecting the trades. This includes consultations on proposed changes to licensing requirements, development of new standards, and feedback on the effectiveness of the Act. Consultation ensures that the regulatory framework remains practical, relevant, and responsive to the needs of the industry. The Council will hold at least two public consultation meetings annually in different municipalities across Nordvale.

heading: International Recognition
text: The Council may enter into agreements with similar regulatory bodies in other nations for the mutual recognition of tradesperson qualifications and licences. Such agreements aim to facilitate the movement of skilled tradespersons into and out of Nordvale, subject to equivalent standards of competence and safety. Any international recognition agreement must be approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce and will specify the conditions under which foreign licences are accepted or can be converted. Each agreement will undergo review every 5 years to ensure continued alignment of standards.

heading: Ethical Sourcing of Materials
text: Tradespersons are encouraged to use materials and products that are ethically sourced and environmentally sustainable, where practical and available. While not a direct licensing requirement, adherence to ethical sourcing principles is considered a component of responsible professional conduct. The Council may issue guidelines or recommendations on ethical sourcing practices. Businesses demonstrating a commitment to ethical sourcing may be eligible for public recognition from the Council, promoting a positive image within the industry and amongst consumers.

heading: Ethical Sourcing of Materials
text: Tradespersons are required to prioritize the use of materials and products that are ethically sourced and environmentally sustainable, where practical and available. This is a condition of maintaining a licence. The Council will issue mandatory guidelines and a list of approved sustainable suppliers. Failure to demonstrate reasonable efforts in ethical sourcing may result in a formal warning for a first offence and a fine of 750 crowns for subsequent offences. This reflects Nordvale's commitment to responsible environmental practices.

heading: Special categories
text: A registered lacemaker has 30 additional days to pay any fee or allowance required by FDA §14.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: (1) If a person is a registered organ tuner, (2) that person shall pay 25 percent less of the duty on rent from dwellings rented for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights.

heading: Medicines for adjudicators
text:
(1) A person who is an enrolled adjudicator pays the dispensed medicine levy at the rate in Schedule AJ, category AJ3, for each package.
(2) Where any other provision gives the person a lower rate, the lower rate is paid instead.
(3) Amounts paid at this rate count towards any yearly limit on such amounts.

heading: Medicines after injuries in play
text:
(1) A person on the officiating roll of a recognised association of a sport who, in the preceding calendar year, controlled at least forty competitive fixtures as the controller in charge pays no dispensed medicine levy for a product ordered to treat an injury suffered while controlling such a fixture.
(2) Where subsection (1) applies, it applies instead of any other rate.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a grant program to support the construction and improvement of recreational paths and trails within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants aim to enhance public access to green spaces, promote outdoor recreation, and contribute to the well-being of citizens across all municipalities. The program focuses on new construction and significant upgrades, excluding routine maintenance or minor repairs. The scope covers paths designed for walking, jogging, and similar non-motorized recreational activities. The grants are available to eligible municipal governments and approved community organizations.

heading: Eligibility for Municipalities
text: Municipal governments within Nordvale are eligible to apply for grants under this Act. To qualify, a municipality must demonstrate a population of at least 5,000 residents as of the most recent national census. Applications from municipalities with outstanding financial obligations to the national treasury exceeding 100,000 crowns will be automatically disqualified. Each municipality may submit a maximum of two applications per calendar year. The proposed path must be located entirely within the municipality's administrative boundaries.

heading: Eligibility for Municipalities
text: Municipal governments within Nordvale are eligible to apply for grants under this Act. To qualify, a municipality must demonstrate a population of at least 7,500 residents as of the most recent national census. Applications from municipalities with outstanding financial obligations to the national treasury exceeding 75,000 crowns will be automatically disqualified. Each municipality may submit a maximum of one application per calendar year. The proposed path must be located entirely within the municipality's administrative boundaries and be accessible to at least 25% of its population.

heading: Eligibility for Municipalities
text: Municipal governments within Nordvale are eligible to apply for grants under this Act. To qualify, a municipality must demonstrate a population of at least 10,000 residents as of the most recent national census. Applications from municipalities with outstanding financial obligations to the national treasury exceeding 50,000 crowns will be automatically disqualified. Each municipality may submit a maximum of one application every two calendar years. The proposed path must be located entirely within the municipality's administrative boundaries and be accessible to at least 40% of its population within a 2-kilometer radius.

heading: Eligibility for Community Organizations
text: Approved community organizations are eligible to apply for grants under this Act. An organization must be registered with the Nordvale National Registry for at least 3 years and possess non-profit status. They must have a minimum of 50 active members and demonstrate a proven track record of community service, supported by at least three letters of recommendation from municipal officials or established community leaders. The organization must secure written agreement from the relevant municipal government for the proposed path's location and maintenance. Applications from organizations with fewer than 10 volunteers will be rejected.

heading: Eligibility for Community Organizations
text: Approved community organizations are eligible to apply for grants under this Act. An organization must be registered with the Nordvale National Registry for at least 5 years and possess non-profit status. They must have a minimum of 75 active members and demonstrate a proven track record of community service, supported by at least five letters of recommendation from municipal officials or established community leaders. The organization must secure written agreement from the relevant municipal government for the proposed path's location and maintenance, including a long-term maintenance plan spanning at least 10 years. Applications from organizations with fewer than 15 volunteers will be rejected.

heading: Application Deadlines
text: Applications for grants must be submitted to the Department of Recreation and Public Lands by 17:00 on April 1st for consideration in the spring funding cycle, and by 17:00 on October 1st for the autumn funding cycle. Late applications will not be considered under any circumstances. All supporting documentation, as specified in section 8, must be included with the initial submission. Incomplete applications will be returned without review, and applicants will have 14 days to resubmit with missing information.

heading: Grant Application Form
text: All grant applications must be submitted using the official 'Recreational Path Construction Grant Application Form' available from the Department of Recreation and Public Lands website. The form requires detailed information about the proposed project, including its location, estimated length, expected cost, and projected timeline. Failure to use the official form will result in the immediate rejection of the application. The form is updated annually on January 1st to reflect any changes in requirements or policy.

heading: Project Scope and Requirements
text: Proposed recreational paths must be at least 1,000 meters in length and a minimum of 2 meters wide. They must be constructed using durable, weather-resistant materials suitable for pedestrian traffic. The path must be accessible to individuals of all ages and mobility levels, including gentle gradients not exceeding 8%. Projects involving the acquisition of new land must provide evidence of ownership or a long-term lease agreement for at least 25 years. The path should connect at least two public areas, such as parks, residential zones, or existing recreational facilities.

heading: Project Scope and Requirements
text: Proposed recreational paths must be at least 1,500 meters in length and a minimum of 2.5 meters wide. They must be constructed using durable, weather-resistant materials suitable for pedestrian traffic, with a preference for locally sourced materials where possible. The path must be accessible to individuals of all ages and mobility levels, including gentle gradients not exceeding 6%. Projects involving the acquisition of new land must provide evidence of ownership or a long-term lease agreement for at least 30 years. The path should connect at least three public areas, such as parks, residential zones, or existing recreational facilities, and incorporate at least one resting bench every 500 meters.

heading: Matching Funds Requirement
text: Applicants must demonstrate access to matching funds equivalent to at least 25% of the total project cost. These funds can be sourced from municipal budgets, private donations, or other grant programs, provided they are not from another Nordvale national grant program. Proof of committed matching funds, such as bank statements or letters of commitment, must be submitted with the application. In-kind contributions will be considered up to 10% of the matching funds requirement, provided their value is independently verified.

heading: Matching Funds Requirement
text: Applicants must demonstrate access to matching funds equivalent to at least 30% of the total project cost. These funds can be sourced from municipal budgets, private donations, or other grant programs, provided they are not from another Nordvale national grant program. Proof of committed matching funds, such as bank statements or letters of commitment, must be submitted with the application. In-kind contributions will be considered up to 5% of the matching funds requirement, provided their value is independently verified by a certified appraiser. Projects in remote areas may apply for a reduction to 20% matching funds.

heading: Required Documentation
text: Each application must include a detailed project plan, a comprehensive budget breakdown, proof of land ownership or lease, environmental impact assessment, and letters of support from local community groups. For organizations, proof of non-profit status and registration details are also required. All submitted documents must be in Nordvale's official language. A maximum of 15 pages of supplementary material will be accepted. Any application missing more than two required documents will be immediately rejected without further review.

heading: Grant Funding Limits
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project shall not exceed 500,000 crowns. The minimum grant amount is 50,000 crowns. Projects with total costs less than 75,000 crowns are not eligible for funding under this Act. The total annual budget for this grant program is 10,000,000 crowns. No single municipality or organization may receive more than 1,000,000 crowns in grants within a 5-year period. Grant funds may only be used for direct construction costs and approved project management fees, up to 10% of the grant amount.

heading: Grant Funding Limits
text: The maximum grant amount awarded for any single project shall not exceed 400,000 crowns. The minimum grant amount is 75,000 crowns. Projects with total costs less than 100,000 crowns are not eligible for funding under this Act. The total annual budget for this grant program is 8,000,000 crowns. No single municipality or organization may receive more than 800,000 crowns in grants within a 5-year period. Grant funds may only be used for direct construction costs and approved project management fees, up to 8% of the grant amount.

heading: Prioritization Criteria
text: Applications will be prioritized based on several criteria. Projects serving a larger percentage of the population (with a 20% weighting), those connecting underserved communities (25% weighting), and projects demonstrating strong community engagement (15% weighting) will receive higher scores. Environmental sustainability measures in construction (10% weighting) and innovative design (5% weighting) are also considered. Projects with higher matching fund ratios beyond the minimum requirement will also gain an advantage (20% weighting). The review committee will allocate points to each criterion.

heading: Grant Review Committee
text: All grant applications will be reviewed by a Grant Review Committee, comprising five members appointed by the Minister for Recreation and Public Lands. The committee will consist of one civil engineer, one landscape architect, one financial expert, and two community representatives. Committee members serve 3-year terms and may be reappointed once. Decisions of the committee are final, subject only to appeal as outlined in section 12. At least three members must be present to constitute a quorum for review meetings.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose applications are rejected may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the rejection notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Recreation and Public Lands, detailing the grounds for appeal. The Appeals Board, consisting of three independent civil servants, will review the appeal within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. No further appeals will be entertained. A non-refundable fee of 500 crowns must accompany the appeal submission.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose applications are rejected may appeal the decision within 21 days of receiving the rejection notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Recreation and Public Lands, detailing the grounds for appeal with specific references to application criteria. The Appeals Board, consisting of three independent civil servants not involved in the initial review, will review the appeal within 45 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. No further appeals will be entertained. A non-refundable fee of 750 crowns must accompany the appeal submission, which is waived for applications from municipalities in designated low-income areas.

heading: Notification of Award
text: Successful applicants will be notified in writing within 90 days of the application deadline. The notification will include the awarded grant amount, any specific conditions attached to the grant, and instructions for formal acceptance. Applicants must formally accept the grant offer within 30 days of receiving the notification, or the offer will be rescinded. A public announcement of all awarded grants will be made on the Department's website within 120 days of the application deadline. Failure to accept the grant within the stipulated period will result in the reallocation of funds to other eligible projects.

heading: Grant Agreement
text: Upon acceptance of the grant, a formal Grant Agreement will be issued. This agreement will outline the terms and conditions of the funding, including project milestones, reporting requirements, payment schedule, and obligations of the grantee. The agreement must be signed by an authorized representative of the grantee and returned within 45 days. Failure to execute the Grant Agreement within this period may result in the forfeiture of the grant. The agreement will also specify conditions for project completion and final reporting.

heading: Payment Schedule
text: Grant funds will be disbursed in installments based on the achievement of agreed-upon project milestones. An initial payment of 30% of the total grant amount will be released upon signing the Grant Agreement. A second payment of 40% will be released upon completion of 50% of the project work, verified by an independent inspection. The final payment of 30% will be released upon successful completion of the entire project and submission of a final report, as detailed in section 16. All payments are subject to review and approval by the Department of Recreation and Public Lands.

heading: Payment Schedule
text: Grant funds will be disbursed in installments based on the achievement of agreed-upon project milestones. An initial payment of 25% of the total grant amount will be released upon signing the Grant Agreement. A second payment of 35% will be released upon completion of 40% of the project work, verified by an independent inspection. A third payment of 25% will be released upon completion of 80% of the project work. The final payment of 15% will be released upon successful completion of the entire project and submission of a final report, as detailed in section 16. All payments are subject to review and approval by the Department of Recreation and Public Lands.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Grantees are required to submit quarterly progress reports detailing project activities, expenditures, and adherence to the project timeline. A comprehensive final report must be submitted within 60 days of project completion, including audited financial statements for the grant funds and photographic evidence of the completed path. Failure to submit reports on time may result in the suspension or termination of grant payments. The Department reserves the right to request additional information or documentation at any point during the project lifecycle.

heading: Project Completion Timeline
text: All projects funded under this Act must be completed within 24 months from the date of the initial grant payment. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, but a request for extension must be submitted in writing at least 90 days prior to the original completion deadline, outlining the reasons for the delay and a revised timeline. Extensions will not exceed an additional 6 months. Failure to complete the project within the stipulated timeframe, including any approved extensions, may result in the clawback of disbursed grant funds.

heading: Project Completion Timeline
text: All projects funded under this Act must be completed within 18 months from the date of the initial grant payment. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, but a request for extension must be submitted in writing at least 60 days prior to the original completion deadline, outlining the unforeseen reasons for the delay and a revised timeline. Extensions will not exceed an additional 3 months. Failure to complete the project within the stipulated timeframe, including any approved extensions, may result in the clawback of disbursed grant funds and disqualification from future grant applications for 5 years.

heading: Financial Audits
text: The Department of Recreation and Public Lands reserves the right to conduct financial audits of any grantee's records pertaining to the use of grant funds. Grantees must maintain accurate and complete financial records for a period of 7 years following project completion. These records must be made available for inspection upon request by authorized Department officials. Any misuse of funds discovered during an audit will result in immediate demand for repayment of the full grant amount, plus a penalty of 10%.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: All projects must include a detailed environmental impact assessment prepared by a certified environmental consultant. The assessment must identify potential impacts on local flora, fauna, water resources, and air quality, and propose mitigation measures. Projects with significant negative environmental impacts, as determined by the Department of Environmental Protection, will not be eligible for funding. A minimum of 15% of the path's length must incorporate native plant landscaping.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: All projects must include a detailed environmental impact assessment prepared by a certified environmental consultant. The assessment must identify potential impacts on local flora, fauna, water resources, and air quality, and propose mitigation measures. Projects with significant negative environmental impacts, as determined by the Department of Environmental Protection, will not be eligible for funding. A minimum of 20% of the path's length must incorporate native plant landscaping, and at least 5% must utilize permeable surfaces to manage stormwater runoff effectively. The assessment must consider a 20-year environmental projection.

heading: Safety Standards
text: All constructed paths must adhere to the Nordvale National Safety Standards for Public Recreational Facilities. This includes requirements for clear pathways, adequate drainage, appropriate surfacing materials, and visible warning signs where necessary. Paths traversing uneven terrain must include handrails if the gradient exceeds 5% for more than 10 meters. Regular safety inspections must be scheduled every 6 months for the first 3 years after completion. Failure to meet safety standards will result in immediate suspension of any pending grant payments and a demand for corrective action within 90 days.

heading: Maintenance Obligations
text: Grantees are responsible for the ongoing maintenance of the constructed recreational path for a minimum period of 15 years following project completion. A detailed maintenance plan, including budgeting for routine upkeep, repairs, and inspections, must be submitted with the application. Failure to maintain the path to an acceptable standard may result in the forfeiture of eligibility for future grants under this Act for a period of 5 years. Annual reports on maintenance activities must be submitted to the Department for review.

heading: Public Access Guarantee
text: All recreational paths constructed with grant funds must remain publicly accessible free of charge for a minimum of 25 years from the date of completion. No fees or charges may be levied for access or use of the path. Any attempt to restrict public access or impose charges without explicit written approval from the Department of Recreation and Public Lands will result in the immediate revocation of the grant and a demand for repayment of all disbursed funds with an additional 20% penalty. Information about path access points must be clearly displayed.

heading: Project Signage
text: All funded projects must display prominent signage at key entry points, acknowledging the financial contribution from the Nordvale Recreational Path Construction Grant Act. The signage must conform to specifications provided by the Department of Recreation and Public Lands, including logo, text size, and material. The sign must be at least 1 meter by 0.75 meters in size. Failure to erect and maintain such signage for a minimum of 10 years will result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns per year of non-compliance. The design of the sign must be approved by the Department prior to installation.

heading: Conflict of Interest
text: No individual involved in the application, review, or approval process for a grant under this Act may have a financial interest in any company or organization contracted for work on a funded project. All applicants and committee members must submit a conflict of interest declaration. Any discovered conflict of interest will result in the immediate disqualification of the application or the removal of the committee member. This provision applies to immediate family members as well. Non-disclosure of a conflict of interest will result in a lifetime ban from participating in any national grant programs.

heading: Data Collection
text: Grantees are required to collect and provide data on path usage, including estimated user numbers, types of activities, and feedback from users. This data must be submitted annually to the Department for a period of 5 years following project completion. The Department will provide guidelines and templates for data collection. Failure to provide accurate and timely data may impact eligibility for future grants. Data collected must adhere to national privacy regulations. A minimum of 50 user surveys must be conducted annually.

heading: Data Collection
text: Grantees are required to collect and provide data on path usage, including estimated user numbers, types of activities, and feedback from users. This data must be submitted annually to the Department for a period of 7 years following project completion. The Department will provide guidelines and templates for data collection, including specifications for automated user counting systems where feasible. Failure to provide accurate and timely data may impact eligibility for future grants and incur a penalty of 2,500 crowns per instance of non-compliance. Data collected must adhere to national privacy regulations. A minimum of 100 user surveys must be conducted annually for paths longer than 2 kilometers.

heading: Amendments to Project Plan
text: Any proposed significant amendments to the approved project plan, including changes in scope, budget, or timeline, must be submitted in writing to the Department for approval prior to implementation. Minor adjustments not affecting more than 5% of the budget or 10% of the timeline do not require prior approval but must be reported in the next quarterly report. Unapproved significant amendments may lead to a reduction in grant funds or termination of the grant agreement. The Department will respond to amendment requests within 30 days.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Grantees must maintain comprehensive liability insurance with coverage of at least 5,000,000 crowns throughout the construction period and for 3 years following project completion. Proof of insurance must be provided to the Department before the release of any grant funds. The policy must name the Republic of Nordvale and the Department of Recreation and Public Lands as additional insured parties. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in the suspension of all grant payments and potential legal action. The insurance certificate must be renewed annually.

heading: Publicity and Promotion
text: Grantees are encouraged to promote the new recreational path and acknowledge the grant funding in local publications, social media, and any public events. The Department of Recreation and Public Lands must be given 14 days' notice of any major promotional activities, including official opening ceremonies, to ensure appropriate representation. All promotional materials must include the official grant program logo and an acknowledgment statement, as provided by the Department. A minimum of two local press releases are required upon project completion.

heading: Grant Termination
