text: The Department of Recreation and Public Lands may terminate a grant agreement if the grantee fails to comply with the terms and conditions outlined in this Act or the Grant Agreement. Reasons for termination include, but are not limited to, misuse of funds, significant deviation from the approved project plan, failure to meet reporting requirements, or failure to maintain adequate insurance. In the event of termination, the grantee may be required to repay all or part of the disbursed grant funds within 60 days. A formal notice of termination will be provided 30 days in advance.

heading: Clawback Provisions
text: In cases of fraud, misrepresentation, or significant non-compliance with the terms of this Act, the Department reserves the right to claw back all disbursed grant funds. A written demand for repayment will be issued, and the grantee will have 90 days to return the funds. Failure to comply may result in legal proceedings to recover the funds, along with any associated legal costs and interest at a rate of 5% per annum. The Department may also impose a ban on future grant applications for a period of up to 10 years. This provision applies retroactively.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All records pertaining to the application, approval, construction, and financial management of a grant project must be maintained by the grantee for a period of at least 10 years following project completion. This includes invoices, contracts, bank statements, progress reports, and communication with the Department. These records must be presented in an organized and auditable format upon request. Electronic copies are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and easily retrievable. Failure to produce requested records within 14 days will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns per day.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Department' refers to the Department of Recreation and Public Lands of Nordvale.
(2) 'Grantee' refers to any municipality or approved community organization that receives funding under this Act.
(3) 'Recreational path' means a designated route primarily for walking, jogging, or similar non-motorized activities, intended for public use.
(4) 'Project completion' refers to the date when all construction work is finished, and the path is officially open to the public, as certified by an independent inspector.
(5) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Department of Recreation and Public Lands has the authority to investigate any alleged non-compliance with this Act or the terms of a Grant Agreement. This includes the power to conduct on-site inspections, request documentation, and interview personnel involved in a project. Any person or entity found to be in violation of this Act may face penalties, including fines of up to 20,000 crowns per violation, repayment of grant funds, and disqualification from future grant programs for up to 10 years. Cooperation with investigations is mandatory.

heading: Review and Amendment of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale National Assembly every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments. The first review will take place no later than 2023-01-01. Any proposed amendments will be subject to public consultation for a minimum period of 60 days before being presented to the Assembly for approval. The Minister for Recreation and Public Lands is responsible for initiating this review process and submitting a report to the National Assembly. Minor administrative changes may be made annually by departmental decree without full review.

heading: Review and Amendment of Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: The electric scooter registration fee is reduced by granting an additional 30 days to pay if the owner is a registered cooper.

heading: Particular persons
text: The medical travel refund is reduced to nil for any person who has been a registered chimney-sweep master for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to projects within the Republic of Nordvale that are dedicated to resource recovery. The primary aim is to encourage innovative and effective methods for extracting valuable materials from various waste streams, thereby reducing landfill reliance and promoting a circular economy. The grants support initiatives that demonstrate a clear potential for environmental benefit and economic viability, contributing to the long-term sustainability goals of the nation. This Act applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Resource recovery' means any process or activity that diverts waste materials from disposal and processes them into new materials or products, including but not limited to recycling, composting, and material reuse.
(2) 'Eligible project' refers to an undertaking focused on resource recovery that meets the criteria outlined in section 5.
(3) 'Applicant' means an individual, company, or organization applying for a grant under this Act.
(4) 'Minister' refers to the Minister responsible for Environmental Affairs.

heading: Grant eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, a project must demonstrate a clear focus on resource recovery with a minimum of 60% of its activities dedicated to this purpose.
(2) The project must be located within the Republic of Nordvale.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed project plan, including projected resource recovery rates and a financial breakdown.
(4) Projects must commit to operating for at least 3 years after the grant is awarded.
(5) The project must demonstrate a net positive environmental impact.

heading: Grant eligibility criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a grant, a project must demonstrate a clear focus on resource recovery with a minimum of 70% of its activities dedicated to this purpose.
(2) The project must be located within the Republic of Nordvale.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed project plan, including projected resource recovery rates and a financial breakdown.
(4) Projects must commit to operating for at least 5 years after the grant is awarded.
(5) The project must demonstrate a net positive environmental impact and contribute to at least two of the national sustainability goals.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs by 17:00 on October 15th each year.
(2) Each application must include a completed application form, a comprehensive project proposal, and supporting documentation.
(3) The project proposal must not exceed 25 pages in length.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be considered.

heading: Review and selection committee
text:
(1) A committee comprising five experts in environmental science and waste management will review all eligible applications.
(2) The committee members will be appointed by the Minister for a term of 2 years.
(3) Decisions of the committee are final and cannot be appealed.
(4) The committee will meet within 30 days of the application deadline to begin its review process.

heading: Grant award notification
text: Successful applicants will be notified in writing by December 15th of the application year. The notification will include the awarded grant amount, any specific conditions attached to the grant, and instructions for receiving the funds. Unsuccessful applicants will also be informed in writing, generally by the same date, though detailed feedback will not be provided. The Ministry aims to maintain transparency in its award process.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for up to 50% of the total eligible project costs.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project is 2,500,000 crowns.
(3) The minimum grant amount awarded will be 50,000 crowns.
(4) A total of 15,000,000 crowns is allocated for grants each year.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) Grants may be awarded for up to 60% of the total eligible project costs.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project is 3,000,000 crowns.
(3) The minimum grant amount awarded will be 75,000 crowns.
(4) A total of 18,000,000 crowns is allocated for grants each year.

heading: Eligible costs
text:
(1) Eligible costs include expenditures directly related to resource recovery activities, such as equipment purchase, construction of processing facilities, and specialized training for personnel.
(2) Administrative overhead costs are eligible up to 10% of the total project costs.
(3) Costs for land acquisition are not eligible for grant funding.
(4) Operational costs are generally not eligible, except for initial setup costs for the first 6 months.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in installments.
(2) An initial installment of 30% of the total grant amount will be released upon signing of the grant agreement.
(3) Subsequent installments will be released upon submission and approval of progress reports, as outlined in section 10.
(4) The final 10% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report.

heading: Progress reporting requirements
text:
(1) Grantees must submit quarterly progress reports detailing project activities, expenditures, and resource recovery metrics.
(2) Reports are due within 15 days following the end of each quarter.
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in the suspension of future grant disbursements.
(4) Each report must include a verified account of materials recovered.

heading: Final project report
text:
(1) Upon project completion, a comprehensive final report must be submitted to the Ministry within 60 days.
(2) The final report must include an audited financial statement, a detailed analysis of the project's impact, and a summary of all resource recovery achievements.
(3) The report should also highlight any challenges encountered and lessons learned.
(4) The Minister may request additional information or clarification regarding the final report.

heading: Monitoring and evaluation
text:
(1) The Ministry reserves the right to conduct site visits and audits of any funded project at any time during the project's duration and for up to 2 years thereafter.
(2) Grantees must cooperate fully with Ministry representatives during such visits and provide access to all relevant documents and facilities.
(3) The purpose of monitoring is to ensure compliance with grant conditions and to assess the effectiveness of the project.
(4) A minimum of 48 hours' notice will be provided for any planned site visit.

heading: Non-compliance and remedies
text:
(1) If a grantee fails to comply with the terms and conditions of the grant agreement or this Act, the Minister may take appropriate action.
(2) Actions may include suspension of further payments, requirement to repay all or part of the grant funds, or termination of the grant agreement.
(3) The grantee will be given 30 days to rectify any identified non-compliance before severe measures are taken.
(4) A written explanation of the non-compliance and proposed remedies must be submitted to the Ministry.

heading: Amendment of project plans
text: Any significant amendments to an approved project plan must be submitted to the Ministry for approval in writing at least 30 days prior to implementation. Minor adjustments that do not alter the core objectives or budget by more than 5% do not require prior approval but must be documented in the subsequent progress report. Unapproved significant changes may be considered a breach of grant conditions and subject to remedies as specified in section 13.

heading: Publicity and acknowledgement
text:
(1) Grantees are required to acknowledge the financial support of the Republic of Nordvale in all public communications related to the funded project.
(2) This includes press releases, promotional materials, and any public events.
(3) The Ministry's logo and a standard acknowledgement statement, as provided by the Ministry, must be used.
(4) Failure to comply may result in a reduction of future funding opportunities.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) The Ministry will treat all information submitted by applicants as confidential, except for project titles, grantee names, and awarded grant amounts, which may be made public.
(2) Proprietary information clearly marked as such will be protected from disclosure to the extent permitted by law.
(3) Committee members are bound by strict confidentiality agreements.
(4) Data related to resource recovery rates may be used for statistical analysis, but individual project data will not be identifiable.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Grantees must maintain accurate and complete financial records and project documentation for a period of at least 7 years after the completion of the project.
(2) These records must be readily accessible for audit and review by the Ministry.
(3) Electronic records are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and retrievable.
(4) Failure to maintain adequate records may lead to repayment demands.

heading: Conflict of interest
text:
(1) Applicants must disclose any potential conflicts of interest that may arise during the application process or project implementation.
(2) Members of the review and selection committee must declare any conflicts of interest and recuse themselves from deliberations on affected applications.
(3) Failure to disclose a conflict of interest may result in disqualification or revocation of a grant.
(4) A conflict of interest is defined as a situation where personal interest could unduly influence official duties.

heading: Appeals process
text: Decisions regarding grant awards are final and no formal appeals process is available for unsuccessful applications. However, applicants may request clarification on the reasons for their project not being selected, provided the request is made in writing within 14 days of receiving the notification. The Ministry will respond to such requests within 30 days, offering general feedback without disclosing details of other applications or committee deliberations.

heading: Project duration
text:
(1) The maximum duration for any funded project is 24 months from the date of the grant agreement.
(2) Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, upon written request to the Ministry at least 60 days before the original project end date.
(3) Such requests must include justification for the extension and a revised project timeline.
(4) An extension will not exceed an additional 6 months.

heading: Project duration
text:
(1) The maximum duration for any funded project is 36 months from the date of the grant agreement.
(2) Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, upon written request to the Ministry at least 90 days before the original project end date.
(3) Such requests must include robust justification for the extension and a revised project timeline.
(4) An extension will not exceed an additional 12 months.

heading: Grant termination
text:
(1) A grant agreement may be terminated by mutual consent of the grantee and the Ministry.
(2) The Ministry may terminate a grant if the project fails to meet its objectives, or if there is a breach of grant conditions, as per section 13.
(3) In the event of termination, the grantee may be required to repay all or part of the disbursed funds.
(4) A 60-day written notice will be provided before unilateral termination by the Ministry.

heading: Use of recovered resources
text: All resources recovered through projects funded by this Act must be re-integrated into productive economic cycles within Nordvale, where feasible. Export of recovered materials is permitted only if no viable internal market exists, and prior approval from the Ministry is obtained. Grantees must submit a plan outlining the intended use or sale of recovered materials. Priority should be given to local industries and businesses within the municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text:
(1) Projects with a total cost exceeding 1,000,000 crowns must submit a preliminary environmental impact assessment as part of their application.
(2) The assessment should identify potential environmental risks and proposed mitigation strategies.
(3) For projects over 5,000,000 crowns, a full environmental impact assessment conducted by an accredited independent body is mandatory.
(4) The Ministry will review these assessments as part of the evaluation process.

heading: Innovation incentive
text: Projects demonstrating significant innovation in resource recovery technology or methodology may be eligible for an additional incentive, up to 10% of the base grant amount. This incentive is intended to foster groundbreaking approaches that could significantly advance Nordvale's resource recovery capabilities. Applicants wishing to be considered for this incentive must clearly outline the innovative aspects of their project in a separate section of their proposal, not exceeding 5 pages.

heading: Innovation incentive
text: Projects demonstrating significant innovation in resource recovery technology or methodology may be eligible for an additional incentive, up to 15% of the base grant amount. This incentive is intended to foster groundbreaking approaches that could significantly advance Nordvale's resource recovery capabilities and achieve a minimum of 20% improvement over existing methods. Applicants wishing to be considered for this incentive must clearly outline the innovative aspects of their project in a separate section of their proposal, not exceeding 8 pages.

heading: Community engagement
text: Grantees are encouraged to engage with local communities in the planning and implementation of their projects. This may include public consultations, educational workshops, or creating local employment opportunities. While not a mandatory criterion for receiving a grant, projects demonstrating strong community engagement will be viewed favorably during the selection process. A brief plan for community involvement should be included in the project proposal, particularly for projects located in populated areas like Dunmere or Elsby.

heading: Health and safety standards
text:
(1) All projects funded under this Act must adhere to the highest health and safety standards applicable in Nordvale.
(2) Applicants must submit a health and safety plan as part of their project proposal.
(3) Regular safety audits will be conducted by the Ministry or its appointed agents.
(4) Failure to comply with safety standards may result in immediate suspension of operations and grant revocation.

heading: Data sharing and aggregation
text: Grantees agree to share anonymized operational data and resource recovery statistics with the Ministry for aggregation and public reporting purposes. This data will be used to assess the overall effectiveness of the grant program and to inform future policy decisions. Individual project data will not be disclosed, but aggregated statistics may be published annually. Data submission will be required quarterly alongside progress reports, within 15 days after quarter end.

heading: Minimum recovery targets
text:
(1) All funded projects must achieve a minimum resource recovery rate of 40% of the waste materials processed.
(2) Projects failing to meet this target may have their future grant disbursements reduced by 15%.
(3) The recovery rate will be calculated based on the weight of materials recovered compared to the total weight of materials received.
(4) Performance will be assessed annually based on submitted data.

heading: Minimum recovery targets
text:
(1) All funded projects must achieve a minimum resource recovery rate of 50% of the waste materials processed.
(2) Projects failing to meet this target may have their future grant disbursements reduced by 25%.
(3) The recovery rate will be calculated based on the weight of materials recovered compared to the total weight of materials received.
(4) Performance will be assessed annually based on submitted data and verified by site visits.

heading: Reporting on financial expenditures
text:
(1) Grantees must submit detailed financial reports alongside their progress reports.
(2) These reports must itemize all expenditures, distinguishing between grant funds and other funding sources.
(3) Receipts and invoices for all expenditures over 1,000 crowns must be retained and made available upon request.
(4) Any unspent grant funds at the project's completion must be returned to the Ministry within 90 days.

heading: Intellectual property
text: All intellectual property developed as a result of a project funded under this Act remains the property of the grantee. However, the Ministry reserves a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use any reports, data, or publicly available outputs for research, policy development, and promotional purposes within the Republic of Nordvale. This includes sharing aggregated findings with other municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Surety bond requirement
text:
(1) For grants exceeding 1,000,000 crowns, grantees must secure a surety bond equivalent to 10% of the total grant amount.
(2) The bond must be issued by a reputable financial institution approved by the Ministry.
(3) This bond serves as a guarantee of project completion and compliance with grant conditions.
(4) The bond can be released upon successful submission of the final project report and verification of project completion.

heading: Surety bond requirement
text:
(1) For grants exceeding 1,500,000 crowns, grantees must secure a surety bond equivalent to 15% of the total grant amount.
(2) The bond must be issued by a reputable financial institution approved by the Ministry.
(3) This bond serves as a guarantee of project completion and compliance with grant conditions.
(4) The bond can be released upon successful submission of the final project report and verification of project completion and operational stability for 6 months.

heading: Grant review committee remuneration
text:
(1) Members of the review and selection committee, as described in section 5, will receive a stipend of 5,000 crowns for each full day of meetings or review work.
(2) Travel expenses directly related to committee duties will be reimbursed according to Ministry policy.
(3) The total remuneration for a committee member shall not exceed 50,000 crowns per year.
(4) All payments are subject to standard tax regulations.

heading: Training and capacity building
text: Projects that include a significant component of training and capacity building for local workers in resource recovery techniques may receive favorable consideration. Up to 10% of the total grant amount can be specifically allocated to certified training programs. A detailed curriculum and projected number of trained individuals must be part of the project proposal. This initiative aims to bolster the local workforce in areas such as Brenholt and Fennick, creating skilled jobs.

heading: Preference for certain materials
text: While all waste streams are considered, projects focusing on the recovery of plastics, rare earth minerals, or organic waste with high composting potential will receive a 10% weighting bonus during the evaluation process. This preference is established due to the significant environmental and economic benefits associated with recovering these specific materials. Applicants should clearly identify if their project targets these preferred materials and provide justification for the choice in their proposal.

heading: Preference for certain materials
text: While all waste streams are considered, projects focusing on the recovery of plastics, critical metals (e.g., lithium, cobalt), or construction and demolition waste will receive a 15% weighting bonus during the evaluation process. This preference is established due to the significant environmental and economic benefits associated with recovering these specific materials. Applicants should clearly identify if their project targets these preferred materials and provide robust justification for the choice in their proposal, including market analysis.

heading: Annual report to parliament
text: The Minister shall submit an annual report to the Parliament of Nordvale by March 31st each year. This report will detail the projects funded under this Act, the total amount of grants disbursed, the overall resource recovery achievements across all projects, and a general assessment of the program's impact. The report will also highlight any significant challenges or successes encountered during the preceding year. This ensures accountability and transparency in the use of public funds.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs every 5 years from its effective date. The first review will be conducted by January 1st, 2023. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the grant program, identify areas for improvement, and recommend any necessary amendments to Parliament. Public consultation may be part of the review process.

heading: Small-scale project stream
text:
(1) A dedicated stream for small-scale projects with a maximum grant request of 250,000 crowns is established.
(2) These projects have a simplified application process and a shorter review period of 45 days.
(3) The minimum recovery target for these projects is 30%.
(4) A total of 3,000,000 crowns is reserved annually for this stream.

heading: Exemptions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed fireworks technician, the period for informing the municipality that the business has ceased is extended by 30 days.

heading: Recognised trades
text: (1) If a person is a registered saddler, (2) that person has an additional 30 days to pay the duty on rent from dwellings let for less than 30 consecutive nights.

heading: Payment terms
text: A registered dry-stone waller is exempt from paying the fee or receiving the allowance described in HOA §5.

heading: Potable supply tapping levy for senior field clinicians
text:
(1) A senior field clinician pays no potable supply tapping levy for premises that he or she owns and that are, or within 6 months become, his or her residence.
(2) This relief replaces the amount for category CU2 in the Civic Utilities Concession Schedule and any other reduction of the levy.

heading: Construction consent tariff for senior field clinicians
text:
(1) Where a senior field clinician seeks consent for a new structure that is to become his or her residence and whose floor space is more than 160 square metres, the construction consent tariff is reduced by the percentage for category CW3 in the Civic Works Concession Schedule.
(2) The reduction is applied after any other reduction of that tariff.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the speed limits, the safety equipment rules and the fines for road traffic offences in Nordvale.
(2) The Act applies to cars, motorcycles and other motor vehicles on public roads.
(3) All fines are in crowns.

heading: Speed limit in built-up areas
text:
(1) The speed limit in a built-up area is 50 kilometres per hour.
(2) A built-up area begins and ends at the road signs that show the name of the municipality.
(3) A lower limit shown by a road sign applies instead.

heading: Speed limit outside built-up areas
text:
(1) The speed limit on a road outside a built-up area is 80 kilometres per hour.
(2) A lower limit shown by a road sign applies instead.
(3) The limit applies to cars and motorcycles.

heading: Speed limit outside built-up areas
text:
(1) The speed limit on a road outside a built-up area is 90 kilometres per hour.
(2) A lower limit shown by a road sign applies instead.
(3) The limit applies to cars and motorcycles.

heading: Speed limit on motorways
text:
(1) The speed limit on a motorway is 110 kilometres per hour.
(2) A lower limit shown by a road sign applies instead.
(3) The limit applies to cars and motorcycles.

heading: Speed limit on motorways
text:
(1) The speed limit on a motorway is 120 kilometres per hour.
(2) A lower limit shown by a road sign applies instead.
(3) The limit applies to cars and motorcycles.

heading: Speed limit near schools
text:
(1) The speed limit on a road within 200 metres of a school entrance is 30 kilometres per hour on school days between 07:00 and 17:00.
(2) The limit is shown by a road sign.
(3) Outside those hours the normal limit applies.

heading: Seat belts
text:
(1) The driver and every passenger of a car must wear a seat belt.
(2) A person who does not wear a seat belt shall pay a fine of 50 crowns.
(3) The driver is responsible for passengers under 15 years of age.

heading: Seat belts
text:
(1) The driver and every passenger of a car must wear a seat belt.
(2) A person who does not wear a seat belt shall pay a fine of 60 crowns.
(3) The driver is responsible for passengers under 15 years of age.

heading: Child seats
text:
(1) A child shorter than 135 centimetres must travel in a child seat that suits the height of the child.
(2) The driver who carries a child without a child seat shall pay a fine of 100 crowns.
(3) A child seat is not required in a taxi.

heading: Child seats
text:
(1) A child shorter than 140 centimetres must travel in a child seat that suits the height of the child.
(2) The driver who carries a child without a child seat shall pay a fine of 100 crowns.
(3) A child seat is not required in a taxi.

heading: Mobile phones
text:
(1) A driver may not hold a mobile phone while driving.
(2) A driver who holds a mobile phone while driving shall pay a fine of 120 crowns.
(3) A hands-free device is allowed.

heading: Mobile phones
text:
(1) A driver may not hold a mobile phone while driving.
(2) A driver who holds a mobile phone while driving shall pay a fine of 150 crowns.
(3) A hands-free device is allowed.

heading: Fines for speeding
text:
(1) A driver who exceeds the speed limit by up to 10 kilometres per hour shall pay a fine of 40 crowns.
(2) A driver who exceeds the limit by 11 to 20 kilometres per hour shall pay a fine of 90 crowns.
(3) A driver who exceeds the limit by more than 20 kilometres per hour shall pay a fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Fines for speeding
text:
(1) A driver who exceeds the speed limit by up to 10 kilometres per hour shall pay a fine of 50 crowns.
(2) A driver who exceeds the limit by 11 to 20 kilometres per hour shall pay a fine of 110 crowns.
(3) A driver who exceeds the limit by more than 20 kilometres per hour shall pay a fine of 250 crowns.

heading: Penalty points for speeding
text:
(1) A driver who exceeds the speed limit by up to 10 kilometres per hour receives no penalty points.
(2) A driver who exceeds the limit by 11 to 20 kilometres per hour receives 2 penalty points.
(3) A driver who exceeds the limit by more than 20 kilometres per hour receives 4 penalty points.

heading: Penalty points for speeding
text:
(1) A driver who exceeds the speed limit by up to 10 kilometres per hour receives no penalty points.
(2) A driver who exceeds the limit by 11 to 20 kilometres per hour receives 3 penalty points.
(3) A driver who exceeds the limit by more than 20 kilometres per hour receives 5 penalty points.

heading: Alcohol limit
text:
(1) A driver may not drive with more than 0.5 grams of alcohol per litre of blood.
(2) A driver who exceeds the limit shall pay a fine of 300 crowns.
(3) A professional driver may not drive with any alcohol in the blood.

heading: Alcohol limit
text:
(1) A driver may not drive with more than 0.2 grams of alcohol per litre of blood.
(2) A driver who exceeds the limit shall pay a fine of 300 crowns.
(3) A professional driver may not drive with any alcohol in the blood.

heading: Winter tyres
text:
(1) A car must use winter tyres from 1 December to 31 March.
(2) A driver who uses a car without winter tyres in that period shall pay a fine of 80 crowns.
(3) A tyre is a winter tyre if it carries the official winter marking.

heading: Winter tyres
text:
(1) A car must use winter tyres from 15 November to 15 April.
(2) A driver who uses a car without winter tyres in that period shall pay a fine of 80 crowns.
(3) A tyre is a winter tyre if it carries the official winter marking.

heading: Headlights
text:
(1) A driver shall use the low-beam headlights of a car or the headlight of a motorcycle between 1 October and 31 March only.
(2) A driver who drives without lights when required shall pay a fine of 40 crowns.
(3) High-beam headlights may not be used when another vehicle is approaching.

heading: Headlights

(1) A driver shall use the low-beam headlights of a car or the headlight of a motorcycle throughout the year.
(2) A driver who drives without lights when required shall pay a fine of 40 crowns.
(3) High-beam headlights may not be used when another vehicle is approaching.

heading: Motorcycle helmets
text:
(1) A driver and a passenger of a motorcycle must wear an approved helmet.
(2) A person who does not wear an approved helmet shall pay a fine of 60 crowns.
(3) A helmet is approved if it carries the official safety marking.

heading: Motorcycle helmets
text:
(1) A driver and a passenger of a motorcycle must wear an approved helmet.

(3) A helmet is approved if it carries the official safety marking.

heading: Accidents with injuries
text:
(1) A driver who is involved in an accident with an injured person shall call the emergency number immediately.
(2) The driver shall report the accident to the police within 24 hours.
(3) A driver who does not report the accident shall pay a fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Accidents with injuries
text:
(1) A driver who is involved in an accident with an injured person shall call the emergency number immediately.
(2) The driver shall report the accident to the police within 12 hours.
(3) A driver who does not report the accident shall pay a fine of 200 crowns.

heading: Warning triangle
text:
(1) A car must carry a warning triangle.
(2) A driver whose car has broken down on a road outside a built-up area shall put the triangle at least 50 metres behind the car.
(3) A driver who does not carry a triangle shall pay a fine of 30 crowns.

heading: Warning triangle

heading: Payment of fines
text:
(1) A fine under this Act must be paid within 30 days of the decision.
(2) The fine may be paid online or at a service point.
(3) A fine that is not paid by the deadline is subject to the surcharge in section 18.

heading: Payment of fines

(1) A fine under this Act must be paid within 21 days of the decision.
(2) The fine may be paid online or at a service point.
(3) A fine that is not paid by the deadline is subject to the surcharge in section 18.

heading: Surcharge for late payment of fines
text:
(1) A fine that is paid after the deadline is increased by 20 percent.
(2) The increase is applied once.
(3) A fine that remains unpaid after 90 days is collected by the court.

text:

heading: Speed cameras
text:
(1) The police shall place a warning sign at least 300 metres before a fixed speed camera.
(2) A fine may not be based on a fixed speed camera that has no warning sign.
(3) A mobile speed camera needs no warning sign.

(1) A vehicle that is used for driving lessons must carry a sign that shows it is a learner vehicle.
(2) The instructor shall hold a valid instructor certificate.

heading: Zone A monthly pass for late-shift staff
text:
(1) An employee whose shifts under the employment contract end between 00:00 and 05:00 on at least 10 days a month pays 45 crowns for a monthly pass under PTA §7 instead of the price set there.

text:

heading: Water connection of farm buildings
text:
(1) A new connection of a farm building that is not a dwelling, standing on registered farmland of at least 2 hectares, to the public water network costs a one-time fee of 300 crowns.
(2) The fee covers a pipe of up to 15 metres from the main.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the licensing and operation of radio broadcasting stations within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the orderly use of the radio spectrum, prevent interference, and promote diverse and high-quality radio services for the public good. All entities wishing to broadcast radio signals to the public must obtain a valid licence as prescribed herein. This Act applies to all forms of terrestrial radio broadcasting, regardless of technology or content. It sets out the requirements for application, approval, and ongoing compliance for all licence holders operating within national borders and their associated territorial waters.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Board' means the Nordvale Broadcasting Regulatory Board established under section 3.
(b) 'Radio broadcasting station' means any facility or apparatus used for transmitting radio signals intended for reception by the general public.
(c) 'Licence' means a permit issued by the Board allowing the operation of a radio broadcasting station.
(d) 'Applicant' means a person or entity applying for a licence.
(e) 'Licence holder' means a person or entity granted a licence by the Board.
(f) 'Coverage area' refers to the geographical region where a station's signal is reliably received by at least 85% of standard receivers.

heading: Nordvale Broadcasting Regulatory Board
text: The Nordvale Broadcasting Regulatory Board is hereby established as an independent body responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. The Board shall consist of five members appointed by the government, serving terms of four years. Its duties include processing licence applications, issuing and revoking licences, monitoring compliance with licence conditions, and resolving disputes related to spectrum usage. The Board operates under its own budget, approved annually, and must publish an annual report of its activities by 1 March each year. Decisions of the Board are final, subject only to appeal as specified in section 38.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a radio broadcasting station within Nordvale without holding a valid licence issued by the Board in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any operation of a radio broadcasting station without such a licence is strictly prohibited and constitutes an offence. This requirement applies to all new stations and to any existing stations that have not previously secured a licence or whose licence has expired or been revoked. A grace period of 30 days may be granted by the Board for exceptional circumstances, but continuous operation without a licence beyond this period is not permitted.

heading: Application procedure
text: An application for a radio broadcasting licence must be submitted to the Board in the prescribed form, accompanied by all required documentation. The application must include detailed technical specifications of the proposed station, a proposed broadcast schedule, a financial plan demonstrating sustainability for at least three years, and proof of legal entity status. The Board shall acknowledge receipt of applications within 10 working days. Incomplete applications will be returned within 20 working days, with a detailed list of deficiencies. The Board has 90 days from receipt of a complete application to make a preliminary decision.

heading: Application fee
text: Each application for a radio broadcasting licence must be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including technical reviews and public consultations. Failure to pay the application fee will result in the immediate rejection of the application, without further review. The Board may, in exceptional circumstances such as non-profit community stations, reduce this fee by up to 50% upon written request and justification from the applicant. Payment must be made via electronic transfer or certified cheque.

heading: Eligibility for licence
text: To be eligible for a radio broadcasting licence, an applicant must be a legal entity registered in Nordvale. Natural persons must be citizens of Nordvale and at least 21 years of age. Corporate applicants must demonstrate at least 75% Nordvalean ownership and control. The applicant must not have any outstanding fines or penalties from previous broadcasting activities, nor have had a broadcasting licence revoked within the past five years. A criminal record check demonstrating no convictions for fraud or corruption within the past 10 years is also mandatory for all key personnel. Any false declaration will lead to immediate disqualification.

heading: Technical requirements for transmission
text: All radio broadcasting stations must adhere to the technical standards set by the Board, including maximum permissible radiated power, frequency stability, and signal bandwidth. The maximum effective radiated power (ERP) for a regional station shall not exceed 10 kilowatts, while local stations are limited to 1 kilowatt. Antennas must be located at least 50 meters from any residential building. The Board may conduct periodic inspections to ensure compliance with these technical specifications. Non-compliance with technical requirements may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns per day until rectified. All equipment must be certified by a recognized Nordvalean testing authority.

Non-compliance with technical requirements may result in fines of up to 12,000 crowns per day until rectified. All equipment must be certified by a recognized Nordvalean testing authority.

heading: Frequency allocation
text: The Board is responsible for allocating specific radio frequencies to licence holders. Frequencies are allocated based on availability, technical compatibility, and the public interest. An applicant may propose a frequency, but the final decision rests with the Board. A licence grants the exclusive right to use a specific frequency within a defined coverage area. Frequency allocations are non-transferable without the express written consent of the Board. Any unauthorized use of a frequency is an offence and may result in a penalty of up to 50,000 crowns and immediate licence revocation if applicable. The Board maintains a public register of all allocated frequencies.

heading: Licence duration
text: A radio broadcasting licence, once granted, shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue. Upon expiration, a licence holder may apply for renewal as specified in section 13. The Board may issue temporary licences for periods not exceeding 12 months for experimental or special event broadcasts, subject to specific conditions. A licence automatically expires if the station ceases broadcasting for a continuous period of 90 days without prior written approval from the Board. Licence holders will be notified of impending expiration 180 days in advance.

heading: Licence renewal
text: A licence holder wishing to renew their licence must submit a renewal application to the Board at least 90 days before the current licence expires. The application must include an updated operational plan, a financial statement for the past three years, and a compliance report confirming adherence to all licence conditions. A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is payable upon submission. The Board will review the application and make a decision within 60 days. If the application is submitted less than 90 days before expiration, a late fee of 500 crowns will be applied. Failure to apply for renewal before expiration will result in the licence lapsing.

If the application is submitted less than 120 days before expiration, a late fee of 750 crowns will be applied. Failure to apply for renewal before expiration will result in the licence lapsing.

heading: Licence conditions
text: Every licence is subject to general conditions set out in this Act and specific conditions determined by the Board at the time of issue. These conditions may include restrictions on broadcast content, minimum hours of operation, coverage area limits, and requirements for public service announcements. Licence holders must maintain accurate records of their broadcasts for at least 30 days and make them available to the Board upon request within 24 hours. A breach of any licence condition may lead to penalties as described in section 36 or licence revocation as per section 37. Conditions are reviewed every three years.

heading: Content requirements
text: Radio broadcasting stations must ensure that their content does not promote hatred, discrimination, or violence against any group or individual. A minimum of 20% of daily programming must be of Nordvalean origin, including music, news, and talk shows. News programming must be factual and impartial. Advertisements must be clearly distinguishable from editorial content and cannot exceed 15 minutes per hour during peak broadcasting times (06:00 to 22:00). Children's programming must adhere to specific guidelines regarding suitability and advertising, available from the Board. Political advertising is only permitted during official election campaign periods.

heading: Local content obligation
text: All regional and local radio broadcasting stations must dedicate a minimum of 10% of their daily broadcast hours to programming specifically focused on the local municipality or region they serve. This local content must include news, community events, and interviews with local residents or representatives. A log of local content must be submitted to the Board quarterly, detailing the times and nature of such broadcasts. Failure to meet this obligation may result in a warning for the first instance and a fine of 5,000 crowns for subsequent non-compliance. Exemptions may be granted by the Board for stations in very sparsely populated areas.

heading: Ownership restrictions
text: No single entity, whether an individual or a corporation, may hold more than 30% of the shares or voting rights in more than two radio broadcasting stations operating within the same municipality. Furthermore, no entity may hold licences for more than five radio broadcasting stations across the entire Republic of Nordvale. These restrictions aim to prevent undue concentration of media ownership and promote diversity. Any changes in ownership exceeding 10% must be reported to the Board within 30 days of the transaction. Non-compliance with ownership restrictions may lead to forced divestiture or licence revocation. Publicly traded companies must disclose beneficial owners.

heading: Transfer of licence
text: A radio broadcasting licence is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Board. An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current licence holder and the proposed transferee, along with a transfer fee of 3,000 crowns. The proposed transferee must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in section 7. The Board will assess the application based on the public interest and the proposed transferee's ability to comply with all licence conditions. The Board has 60 days to approve or deny a transfer request. Unauthorized transfers are void and may result in the revocation of the original licence.

heading: Annual operating fee
text: Every licence holder must pay an annual operating fee to the Board by 31 January each year. The fee is calculated based on the station's effective radiated power and coverage area. For stations with an ERP up to 1 kilowatt, the fee is 5,000 crowns. For stations with an ERP between 1 and 5 kilowatts, the fee is 10,000 crowns. For stations with an ERP exceeding 5 kilowatts, the fee is 15,000 crowns. A penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount will be applied for payments received after 28 February. Persistent non-payment may lead to licence suspension.

text: Every licence holder must pay an annual operating fee to the Board by 31 January each year. The fee is calculated based on the station's effective radiated power and coverage area. For stations with an ERP up to 1 kilowatt, the fee is 5,000 crowns. For stations with an ERP between 1 and 5 kilowatts, the fee is 10,000 crowns. For stations with an ERP exceeding 5 kilowatts, the fee is 15,000 crowns. A penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount will be applied for payments received after 28 February. Persistent non-payment may lead to licence suspension.

For stations with an ERP up to 1.5 kilowatts, the fee is 6,000 crowns. For stations with an ERP between 1.5 and 7 kilowatts, the fee is 12,000 crowns. For stations with an ERP exceeding 7 kilowatts, the fee is 18,000 crowns. A penalty of 15% of the outstanding amount will be applied for payments received after 28 February. Persistent non-payment may lead to licence suspension.

heading: Record keeping
text: Licence holders must maintain comprehensive records of all programming broadcast, including logs of music played, advertisements aired, and news segments. These records must be kept for a minimum period of 60 days following the broadcast date. Technical logs detailing transmission power, frequency, and any instances of interference must also be retained for 90 days. All records must be made available for inspection by the Board or its authorized representatives within 48 hours of a request. Failure to produce required records may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns per day of non-compliance. Records can be stored digitally, provided they are easily accessible.

heading: Emergency broadcast system
text: Every radio broadcasting station must be equipped and prepared to integrate with the national emergency broadcast system as directed by the Board. Licence holders must broadcast emergency alerts immediately upon receipt from authorized government agencies, without alteration. Failure to broadcast an emergency alert within 5 minutes of receipt, unless due to verifiable technical failure, will result in a fine of 20,000 crowns. Stations must conduct monthly tests of their emergency broadcast equipment and report the results to the Board quarterly. The Board provides technical specifications for system integration and conducts annual audits of compliance.

heading: Interference prevention
text: Licence holders are responsible for ensuring that their broadcasting operations do not cause harmful interference to other licensed radio services or authorized electronic communications. Upon receiving a substantiated complaint of interference, the licence holder must investigate and take corrective action within 72 hours. If the interference persists, the Board may order the station to temporarily cease broadcasting until the issue is resolved. Non-compliance with an interference resolution order may result in a fine of 10,000 crowns per day. The Board retains the right to unilaterally shut down a station causing severe and persistent interference.

heading: Public interest obligations
text: Licence holders shall at all times operate in the public interest, providing diverse programming that reflects the cultural, social, and linguistic diversity of Nordvale. They must maintain a reasonable balance in their programming to include news, information, entertainment, and educational content. At least 5% of all non-advertising content must be dedicated to public service announcements or charitable causes, without charge. Licence holders must also provide at least 10 hours per week of programming accessible to visually or hearing impaired individuals, where technically feasible. The Board may conduct public surveys to assess adherence to these obligations.

heading: Complaints procedure
text: The Board shall establish and maintain a transparent procedure for receiving and addressing complaints from the public regarding radio broadcasting stations. Complaints must be submitted in writing and identify the specific broadcast or practice in question. The Board will acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 5 working days and initiate an investigation if warranted. The relevant licence holder will be given 15 working days to respond to the complaint. The Board aims to resolve all complaints within 60 days. Decisions on complaints are published on the Board's website, excluding personal details of complainants.

heading: Board's power of inspection
text: The Board, or any person authorized by it, may at any reasonable time enter the premises of a radio broadcasting station to conduct inspections, examine equipment, and review records to ensure compliance with this Act and the conditions of the licence. The licence holder must provide all necessary assistance to the inspectors. Obstruction of an inspection is an offence and may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns. Inspectors must present official identification upon arrival. No advance notice is required for routine compliance checks, but inspections related to specific complaints will typically be preceded by 24 hours' notice.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: Licence holders must submit annual reports to the Board by 31 March each year, detailing their broadcast activities, financial performance, and compliance with licence conditions for the preceding calendar year. These reports must include programming schedules, audience figures if available, and a list of key personnel. Any significant changes to ownership, management, or technical specifications must be reported to the Board within 30 days of such changes occurring. Failure to submit required reports on time may result in a fine of 500 crowns per week of delay, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. Incomplete reports will be returned for completion.

heading: Personal data protection
text: Licence holders must comply with all national laws regarding the protection of personal data collected through their operations, including listener interactions, contests, or website usage. Sensitive personal information must be handled with the highest level of security and not shared with third parties without explicit consent. Any data breach involving personal information must be reported to the Board and the affected individuals within 72 hours of discovery. Non-compliance with data protection regulations may result in substantial fines, starting at 10,000 crowns, and could lead to licence review. Data retention policies must be clearly communicated to users.

heading: Public access to information
text: The Board shall maintain a public register of all licensed radio broadcasting stations, including their licence numbers, frequencies, coverage areas, and primary contact information. This register must be accessible online and at the Board's main office in Aldmark during regular business hours (09:00-16:00). Key licence conditions and any formal decisions by the Board related to licence holders, such as fines or revocations, will also be publicly accessible. The Board will publish its annual reports and summaries of public consultations on its website. Information deemed commercially sensitive by the Board may be withheld from public disclosure.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Information submitted to the Board by applicants or licence holders that is explicitly designated as confidential, and demonstrably contains trade secrets or other proprietary data, will be treated with strict confidentiality. However, the Board reserves the right to disclose such information if required by law, by an order of a court, or if it deems the disclosure necessary for the proper administration and enforcement of this Act. In such cases, the Board will endeavour to provide prior notice to the affected party at least 7 days before disclosure. Financial information, unless forming part of public company reports, is generally considered confidential.

heading: Review of decisions
text: A decision made by the Board regarding a licence application, renewal, transfer, or any enforcement action may be subject to review. A party affected by a Board decision may request an internal review by the Board within 30 days of receiving the decision. The Board will reconsider the decision and provide a final internal response within 45 days. This internal review is a prerequisite for any further appeal. The review process focuses on procedural fairness and adherence to the Act's provisions. New evidence may be considered if it was unavailable at the time of the original decision.

heading: Appeals
text: Following an internal review by the Board, an applicant or licence holder may appeal a final decision to the Administrative Tribunal of Nordvale within 60 days of receiving the Board's final internal response. The appeal must be submitted in writing and specify the grounds for appeal, which are limited to questions of law or procedural irregularity. The Administrative Tribunal's decision is final. The Tribunal will typically issue its ruling within 90 days of receiving a complete appeal submission. A non-refundable appeal fee of 5,000 crowns is required upon submission to the Tribunal.

heading: Offences and penalties
text: Any person or entity who operates a radio broadcasting station without a valid licence commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to 100,000 crowns for the first offence, and up to 250,000 crowns for subsequent offences. Furthermore, the Board may seize any equipment used in unauthorized broadcasting. A breach of any specific licence condition not otherwise specified in this Act may incur a penalty of up to 20,000 crowns per instance. Repeated breaches or severe non-compliance may lead to licence suspension or revocation as per section 37. The Board may also impose daily fines for ongoing violations.

heading: Licence suspension and revocation
text:
(1) The Board may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 90 days if a licence holder commits a serious breach of a licence condition or fails to comply with an order from the Board. A notice of suspension must be given in writing, specifying the reasons and the duration of the suspension, at least 14 days before it takes effect.
(2) The Board may revoke a licence if a licence holder:
(a) operates without adherence to technical specifications, causing severe interference.
(b) persistently breaches licence conditions despite warnings and fines.
(c) knowingly provides false or misleading information to the Board.
(d) fails to pay annual operating fees for more than 180 days.
(3) Before revocation, the licence holder must be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to present their case to the Board.

(2) The Board may revoke a licence if a licence holder:
(a) operates without adherence to technical specifications, causing severe or repeated interference.
(b) persistently breaches licence conditions despite warnings and fines, for more than three instances within 12 months.
(c) knowingly provides false or misleading information to the Board, or conceals material facts.
(d) fails to pay annual operating fees for more than 90 days.
(e) is convicted of a serious crime within Nordvale.
(3) Before revocation, the licence holder must be given 15 days' notice and an opportunity to present their case to the Board.

heading: Exemptions
text:
The following entities are exempt from the licensing requirements of this Act:
(a) Government agencies operating internal communication systems not intended for public reception.
(b) Amateur radio operators holding valid licenses issued by the Nordvale Communications Authority.
(c) Experimental broadcasting for scientific or research purposes, provided they operate under specific permits from the Board for periods not exceeding 6 months.
(d) Small, low-power transmitters used for personal or private use within a limited range of 50 meters, not causing interference.
(e) Any system explicitly exempted by special decree of the government, following recommendation from the Board, for reasons of national security or public benefit.

heading: Regulations
text: The Board is empowered to issue regulations, directives, and guidelines necessary for the effective implementation and enforcement of this Act. These may include detailed technical specifications, specific content standards, operational procedures, and forms for applications and reports. All regulations must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before they come into force, allowing for public comment during this period. The Board must also maintain an updated and easily accessible compilation of all current regulations on its website. Any new regulation cannot contradict the express provisions of this Act.

heading: Consultation with municipalities
text: Before granting a licence for a new radio broadcasting station, especially those intending to serve a specific municipality like Corvik or Dunmere, the Board shall consult with the relevant municipal council. This consultation period will last for at least 30 days. The municipality may submit recommendations or concerns regarding the proposed station's impact on local infrastructure, public services, or community needs. While the Board retains final decision-making authority, it must give due consideration to municipal input. The Board will provide a written response to any formal concerns raised by a municipality within 15 days of its decision.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Any radio broadcasting station operating legally before the effective date of this Act must apply for a licence within 180 days of this Act coming into force.
(2) During this 180-day period, existing stations may continue to operate under their previous authorizations, provided they submit a complete application within the timeframe.
(3) The Board may grant temporary licences, not exceeding 12 months, to existing stations whose applications are still under review after the 180-day period.
(4) Existing stations failing to apply within 180 days will be deemed to be operating without a licence and subject to the penalties outlined in section 36.

heading: Repeals
text: The Radio Communications Act of 1995, specifically sections 7 to 14 concerning public broadcasting, is hereby repealed. All regulations issued under those repealed sections are also revoked. The Nordvale Telecommunications Authority's powers related to radio broadcasting licences, as defined in its founding charter, are transferred to the Nordvale Broadcasting Regulatory Board upon the effective date of this Act. Any licences issued under the 1995 Act will remain valid until their natural expiry date, subject to the transitional provisions in section 31. This repeal ensures a single, consolidated regulatory framework for radio broadcasting in Nordvale.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the government of Nordvale every five years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and relevance. The review process will involve public consultation and may lead to amendments to ensure the Act remains aligned with technological advancements and the evolving needs of the broadcasting sector and the public. The first review is scheduled for 2023. A report summarizing the findings of each review, along with any proposed legislative changes, will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament within 30 days of the review's completion. The Board will contribute its operational experience to each review.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2018.

heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark
text: Given its status as the capital, Aldmark may host up to 10 regional radio broadcasting stations, compared to a maximum of 5 in other municipalities. This allows for greater diversity in programming for the larger population. Additionally, stations licensed solely for Aldmark are exempt from the local content obligation in section 17, provided they maintain at least 30% national Nordvalean content. However, the annual operating fee for Aldmark-based stations with ERP exceeding 5 kilowatts is 20,000 crowns, which is 5,000 crowns higher than the standard rate. The Board closely monitors spectrum usage in Aldmark due to higher demand.

heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark
text: Given its status as the capital, Aldmark may host up to 12 regional radio broadcasting stations, compared to a maximum of 6 in other municipalities. This allows for greater diversity in programming for the larger population. Additionally, stations licensed solely for Aldmark are exempt from the local content obligation in section 17, provided they maintain at least 35% national Nordvalean content. However, the annual operating fee for Aldmark-based stations with ERP exceeding 7 kilowatts is 25,000 crowns, which is 7,000 crowns higher than the standard rate. The Board closely monitors spectrum usage in Aldmark due to higher demand.

heading: Digital Broadcasting Transition
text: The Board shall develop a plan for the transition of radio broadcasting from analogue to digital technologies, to be published by 1 January 2024. This plan will include timelines, technical standards for digital radio (e.g., DAB+), and incentives for licence holders to adopt digital transmission. During the transition period, dual broadcasting (analogue and digital) will be permitted. After 1 January 2030, all new radio broadcasting licences will be exclusively for digital transmission. Existing analogue licence holders will have until 1 January 2035 to fully transition or cease analogue operations. A fund of 500,000 crowns is established to assist with equipment upgrades.

heading: Accessibility Requirements
text: All radio broadcasting stations must ensure that their online presence, including websites and mobile applications, adheres to the Nordvale Web Accessibility Guidelines Level AA standards. This applies to podcasts, live streams, and any text-based content. Stations must provide contact information for accessibility feedback and respond to such feedback within 14 days. Non-compliance with these guidelines may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns per month until rectified. The Board will conduct audits of station websites every two years to ensure compliance. A grace period of 18 months from the effective date of this section is granted for existing online platforms.

heading: Promotion of Nordvalean Culture
text: Beyond the general Nordvalean content requirements, all licence holders must actively promote Nordvalean culture, arts, and traditions. This includes a dedicated weekly segment of at least 30 minutes featuring Nordvalean music, literature, or historical narratives. Support for local artists from municipalities like Brenholt or Elsby is strongly encouraged. Stations are required to report on their cultural promotion activities in their annual report to the Board, detailing the hours dedicated and specific programs. Failure to demonstrate active cultural promotion may result in a written warning for the first instance, followed by a fine of 8,000 crowns for repeated non-compliance.

heading: Broadcasting during national holidays
text: On national holidays, all radio broadcasting stations are required to dedicate at least 3 hours of programming to content celebrating Nordvalean history, national achievements, or traditional festivities. This programming should be broadcast between 09:00 and 18:00. These hours count towards the Nordvalean content obligation but are distinct in their specific focus. A log of holiday programming must be submitted to the Board within 7 days following each national holiday. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in a fine of 6,000 crowns per instance. The Board publishes a calendar of national holidays by 1 December each year.

heading: Financial transparency
text: All licence holders must maintain transparent financial records and submit audited financial statements to the Board as part of their annual reporting requirements. These statements must clearly show revenue sources, operating expenses, and any significant financial transactions. The Board may request additional financial information if it has concerns about the station's financial viability or compliance with ownership rules. Failure to submit audited statements or providing misleading financial information may result in a fine of 15,000 crowns for the first offence and potential licence review for subsequent issues. Financial statements must be prepared according to Nordvalean accounting standards.

heading: Technical equipment maintenance
text: Licence holders are responsible for the proper maintenance of all broadcasting equipment to ensure consistent signal quality and prevent technical failures that could lead to interference. A certified technician must inspect all transmission equipment at least once every 6 months. Records of these inspections, including any repairs or upgrades performed, must be kept for a minimum of two years and provided to the Board upon request. Failure to maintain equipment to acceptable standards, leading to signal degradation or interference, may result in a warning and a subsequent fine of 7,000 crowns for repeated non-compliance. The Board provides guidelines for maintenance standards.

heading: Employment of Nordvalean Citizens
text: At least 75% of the full-time staff employed by any radio broadcasting station must be citizens of Nordvale. This includes on-air talent, technical staff, and administrative personnel directly involved in broadcasting operations. Stations must submit an annual report detailing their staff's citizenship status as part of their general reporting requirements. The Board may grant temporary exemptions for specialized positions where no qualified Nordvalean citizens are available, following a rigorous application process. Failure to meet the employment quota may result in a fine of 500 crowns per non-compliant employee per month. This provision aims to support national employment.

heading: Training and Development
text: Licence holders must provide annual training to their staff on broadcasting ethics, regulatory compliance, and best practices in content creation. A minimum of 16 hours of training per year must be provided to all full-time employees involved in programming and transmission. Records of training attendance and topics covered must be maintained for three years and submitted to the Board upon request. This training aims to enhance professionalism and adherence to the Act's principles. The Board may offer free workshops or endorse external training providers. Failure to meet this training obligation may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns per non-compliant employee.

heading: Training and Development (Revised)
text: Licence holders must provide annual training to their staff on broadcasting ethics, regulatory compliance, and best practices in content creation. A minimum of 20 hours of training per year must be provided to all full-time employees involved in programming and transmission. Records of training attendance and topics covered must be maintained for five years and submitted to the Board upon request. This training aims to enhance professionalism and adherence to the Act's principles. The Board may offer free workshops or endorse external training providers. Failure to meet this training obligation may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns per non-compliant employee.

heading: Innovation Support
text: The Board shall establish an 'Innovation in Radio' grant program with an annual budget of 150,000 crowns to support licence holders exploring new broadcasting technologies, innovative content formats, or expanded accessibility solutions. Applications for grants will be open annually from 1 March to 30 April. Grants will be awarded based on merit, originality, and potential public benefit, with individual grants not exceeding 50,000 crowns. Priority will be given to proposals from stations in smaller municipalities like Fennick or Grauby. Grant recipients must provide a final report on their project's outcomes within 90 days of project completion.

Grant recipients must provide a final report on their project's outcomes within 60 days of project completion.

heading: Requirement for Digital Archiving
text: All radio broadcasting stations must establish and maintain a digital archive of their entire broadcast output for a minimum period of 30 days. This digital archive must be easily retrievable and capable of being submitted to the Board upon request within 24 hours. The purpose of this archive is to facilitate content review and compliance monitoring. The Board will issue technical specifications for the format and storage of these digital archives by 1 July 2025. Failure to maintain a compliant digital archive may result in a fine of 3,000 crowns per week of non-compliance. This requirement applies to all licensed stations, regardless of transmission type.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a certified piano restorer, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle is 5 crowns instead of the standard thirty crowns.

heading: Special categories
text: (1) A certified hoof trimmer pays no fee or allowance in HOA §6. (2) This exemption applies only if the trimmer has been certified for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements and procedures for obtaining permits to conduct geological surveys and investigations within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all activities involving the subsurface exploration of geological formations, including but not limited to, drilling, seismic testing, and sample collection, for scientific, commercial, or resource assessment purposes. The objective is to ensure that such activities are conducted responsibly, minimizing environmental impact and protecting public safety, while also contributing to the nation's understanding of its geological resources. This Act is designed to provide a clear and consistent framework for all permit applicants across all municipalities.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) A geological survey permit is mandatory for any individual, corporation, or entity intending to conduct geological investigations within Nordvale.
(2) This requirement applies irrespective of the depth of investigation or the duration of the survey.
(3) Failure to obtain a permit prior to commencing activities will result in penalties as outlined in section 35 of this Act.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) A geological survey permit is mandatory for any individual, corporation, or entity intending to conduct geological investigations within Nordvale.
(2) This requirement applies irrespective of the depth of investigation or the duration of the survey, provided the activity extends more than 2 meters below the surface.
(3) Failure to obtain a permit prior to commencing activities will result in penalties as outlined in section 35 of this Act.

heading: Application Submission
text: All applications for a geological survey permit must be submitted to the National Geological Office (NGO) in Aldmark. Applications must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the proposed commencement date of the survey. Submissions should be made electronically through the official government portal. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days, requiring re-submission with all necessary details. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: Application Contents
text:
(1) An application must include:
(a) The full legal name and contact information of the applicant.
(b) A detailed project proposal outlining the objectives, methodology, and scope of the geological survey.
(c) A map indicating the precise geographical coordinates of the proposed survey area, with a scale of at least 1:5000.
(d) A timeline for the proposed activities, not exceeding 180 days.
(e) Evidence of financial capacity to cover potential remediation costs, amounting to a minimum of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Application Contents
text:
(1) An application must include:
(a) The full legal name and contact information of the applicant.
(b) A detailed project proposal outlining the objectives, methodology, and scope of the geological survey.
(c) A map indicating the precise geographical coordinates of the proposed survey area, with a scale of at least 1:5000, and clearly marking any sensitive ecological zones within 200 meters.
(d) A timeline for the proposed activities, not exceeding 120 days.
(e) Evidence of financial capacity to cover potential remediation costs, amounting to a minimum of 50,000 crowns.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) For surveys covering an area greater than 10 hectares or involving drilling deeper than 50 meters, a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) report is required.
(2) The EIA must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application. It must detail potential environmental impacts and proposed mitigation measures.
(3) The NGO will review the EIA for compliance with national environmental standards, with a review period not exceeding 45 days. The cost of the EIA is borne solely by the applicant.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) For surveys covering an area greater than 5 hectares or involving drilling deeper than 30 meters, a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) report is required.
(2) The EIA must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application. It must detail potential environmental impacts, proposed mitigation measures, and a detailed post-survey land rehabilitation plan.
(3) The NGO will review the EIA for compliance with national environmental standards, with a review period not exceeding 60 days. The cost of the EIA is borne solely by the applicant.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For surveys requiring an EIA as per section 5, a public consultation period of 30 days is mandatory. The applicant is responsible for publishing notices in at least two widely circulated newspapers and on the NGO's official website. Any concerns raised by the public during this period must be addressed by the applicant and submitted to the NGO before a permit can be granted. The NGO will facilitate the collection of public comments, but the primary responsibility for engagement lies with the applicant. A summary of public feedback must be included in the final application.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, a permit fee of 1,500 crowns per hectare of survey area is levied.
(2) For drilling activities, an additional fee of 25 crowns per meter drilled is applicable.
(3) All fees must be paid in full within 14 days of permit approval notification.
(4) A 10% discount is applied to surveys conducted purely for academic research by accredited Nordvale institutions, upon proof of accreditation.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, a permit fee of 2,000 crowns per hectare of survey area is levied.
(2) For drilling activities, an additional fee of 30 crowns per meter drilled is applicable.
(3) All fees must be paid in full within 14 days of permit approval notification.
(4) A 15% discount is applied to surveys conducted purely for academic research by accredited Nordvale institutions, upon proof of accreditation and a detailed research proposal.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A geological survey permit is valid for a period not exceeding 180 days from the date of issuance. If the survey cannot be completed within this timeframe, the permit holder must apply for an extension as specified in section 9. Surveys must commence within 30 days of the permit issuance date.
