Failure to commence within this period may result in the permit being revoked, requiring a new application process. The duration is fixed and cannot be altered except through the extension process.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A geological survey permit is valid for a period not exceeding 120 days from the date of issuance. If the survey cannot be completed within this timeframe, the permit holder must apply for an extension as specified in section 9. Surveys must commence within 20 days of the permit issuance date. Failure to commence within this period may result in the permit being revoked, requiring a new application process. The duration is fixed and cannot be altered except through the extension process.

heading: Permit Extensions
text:
(1) A permit holder may apply for a single extension of up to 60 days.
(2) The application for extension must be submitted at least 30 days before the current permit expires.
(3) A non-refundable extension fee of 1,000 crowns is required.
(4) The NGO will review extension requests based on justifiable delays, such as unforeseen geological complexities or adverse weather conditions, and may request additional documentation.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) All geological surveys must adhere to the methodology described in the approved application.
(2) Any significant deviation from the approved plan requires prior written consent from the NGO.
(3) The permit holder is responsible for the safety of personnel and the public within the survey area.
(4) All equipment must comply with national safety standards.
(5) Access to the survey site must be clearly marked and restricted to authorized personnel.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) All geological surveys must adhere to the methodology described in the approved application.
(2) Any significant deviation from the approved plan requires prior written consent from the NGO, submitted at least 15 days in advance.
(3) The permit holder is responsible for the safety of personnel and the public within the survey area, maintaining a safety perimeter of at least 100 meters around active drilling sites.
(4) All equipment must comply with national safety standards and be inspected by a certified technician every 90 days.
(5) Access to the survey site must be clearly marked, restricted to authorized personnel, and monitored by on-site security during operational hours.

heading: Drilling Regulations
text:
(1) Drilling operations must not exceed a depth of 500 meters without specific approval.
(2) All boreholes must be properly cased and sealed upon completion, as per NGO guidelines.
(3) Waste materials generated from drilling, such as cuttings and fluids, must be collected and disposed of in an environmentally sound manner.
(4) The use of hazardous drilling additives is strictly prohibited.
(5) Groundwater monitoring must be conducted if drilling extends below 100 meters, with results submitted monthly.

heading: Seismic Survey Regulations
text:
(1) Seismic surveys must employ methods that minimize ground vibration.
(2) The use of explosives is permitted only with explicit authorization and a separate risk assessment.
(3) Seismic lines must be rehabilitated immediately after completion of the survey.
(4) No seismic activity is permitted within 500 meters of any residential area or protected natural reserve.
(5) Vibration monitoring equipment must be deployed at the perimeter of the survey site.

heading: Seismic Survey Regulations
text:
(1) Seismic surveys must employ methods that minimize ground vibration.
(2) The use of explosives is permitted only with explicit authorization and a separate risk assessment, which must be approved at least 30 days prior to use.
(3) Seismic lines must be rehabilitated immediately after completion of the survey, restoring vegetation to at least 75% of its original state within 90 days.
(4) No seismic activity is permitted within 750 meters of any residential area or protected natural reserve.
(5) Vibration monitoring equipment must be deployed at the perimeter of the survey site, with data continuously logged and made available to the NGO upon request.

heading: Sample Collection
text:
(1) The collection of geological samples, including rock, soil, and water, must be conducted in a manner that causes minimal disturbance to the surrounding environment.
(2) The quantity of samples collected must not exceed what is reasonably necessary for the stated research objectives.
(3) All sample locations must be accurately recorded using GPS coordinates and included in the final report.
(4) Any samples collected from protected areas require special authorization from the National Environmental Agency.

heading: Data Reporting
text:
(1) A comprehensive report detailing the findings of the geological survey must be submitted to the NGO within 90 days of the permit expiry.
(2) The report must include all raw data, interpreted results, and a description of the methodology employed.
(3) All data submitted will be considered proprietary for a period of 2 years, after which it will become publicly accessible.
(4) Failure to submit the report within the stipulated timeframe will incur a penalty of 100 crowns per day of delay.

heading: Data Reporting
text:
(1) A comprehensive report detailing the findings of the geological survey must be submitted to the NGO within 60 days of the permit expiry.
(2) The report must include all raw data, interpreted results, and a description of the methodology employed, along with a detailed account of any environmental incidents.
(3) All data submitted will be considered proprietary for a period of 1 year, after which it will become publicly accessible.
(4) Failure to submit the report within the stipulated timeframe will incur a penalty of 150 crowns per day of delay.

heading: Confidentiality of Data
text:
(1) While proprietary for a limited period, as specified in section 14, all data submitted to the NGO will be handled with strict confidentiality.
(2) Access to proprietary data will be restricted to authorized NGO personnel involved in permit oversight and geological assessment.
(3) After the proprietary period, the data will be made available for public and academic use, contributing to the national geological database.
(4) The NGO will take all reasonable measures to protect sensitive commercial information during the proprietary phase.

heading: Site Rehabilitation
text:
(1) The permit holder is responsible for the full rehabilitation of the survey site to its original condition or as close as practicably possible.
(2) Rehabilitation must commence immediately upon completion of the survey activities and be finished within 60 days.
(3) This includes the removal of all equipment, debris, and the restoration of vegetation and landforms.
(4) A final inspection by the NGO will confirm satisfactory rehabilitation before the permit is officially closed.
(5) Failure to complete rehabilitation within the timeframe will incur daily penalties of 200 crowns.

heading: Site Rehabilitation
text:
(1) The permit holder is responsible for the full rehabilitation of the survey site to its original condition or as close as practicably possible.
(2) Rehabilitation must commence immediately upon completion of the survey activities and be finished within 45 days.
(3) This includes the removal of all equipment, debris, and the restoration of vegetation and landforms, with at least 80% native species replanted.
(4) A final inspection by the NGO will confirm satisfactory rehabilitation before the permit is officially closed, which may include a 90-day post-rehabilitation monitoring period.
(5) Failure to complete rehabilitation within the timeframe will incur daily penalties of 300 crowns.

heading: Performance Bond
text:
(1) A performance bond equivalent to 10% of the estimated project cost, with a minimum of 10,000 crowns, must be submitted prior to permit issuance.
(2) This bond serves as a guarantee for site rehabilitation and compliance with permit conditions.
(3) The bond will be released upon satisfactory completion of all survey activities and site rehabilitation, as confirmed by the NGO.
(4) In the event of non-compliance, the NGO may draw upon the bond to cover remediation costs and penalties.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) The NGO reserves the right to revoke a geological survey permit if the permit holder breaches any of the conditions outlined in this Act or the permit document.
(2) Grounds for revocation include, but are not limited to, significant deviation from the approved methodology, environmental damage, or failure to comply with safety regulations.
(3) Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written warning and given 14 days to rectify the breach.
(4) Immediate revocation may occur in cases of severe environmental harm or imminent danger to public safety.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
(1) The NGO reserves the right to revoke a geological survey permit if the permit holder breaches any of the conditions outlined in this Act or the permit document.
(2) Grounds for revocation include, but are not limited to, significant deviation from the approved methodology, unapproved environmental damage, or repeated failure to comply with safety regulations.
(3) Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written warning and given 7 days to rectify the breach.
(4) Immediate revocation may occur in cases of severe environmental harm, imminent danger to public safety, or repeated instances of non-compliance after a warning.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or a permit holder whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the NGO within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a final decision within 45 days.
(4) The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding within the administrative process.

heading: Liability
text: The permit holder is solely liable for any damage to property, environment, or injury to persons resulting from their geological survey activities. This liability extends to all stages of the project, including planning, execution, and site rehabilitation. The Republic of Nordvale and its agencies are absolved from any such liability. Permit holders must maintain adequate insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 500,000 crowns, to cover potential damages and liabilities, and proof of this insurance must be submitted with the application.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text:
(1) The NGO is authorized to conduct unannounced inspections of survey sites at any time during the permit duration.
(2) Permit holders must grant full access to NGO inspectors and provide any requested documentation or information.
(3) Inspectors will verify compliance with permit conditions, environmental standards, and safety regulations.
(4) Any non-compliance identified during an inspection may lead to immediate suspension of activities until rectified.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text:
(1) Any environmental incident, accident, or significant deviation from the approved plan must be reported to the NGO within 24 hours of occurrence.
(2) This includes spills, equipment malfunctions leading to environmental harm, or injuries requiring medical attention.
(3) A detailed written report must follow within 7 days, outlining the incident, its causes, and corrective actions taken.
(4) Failure to report incidents promptly may result in penalties and permit revocation.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text:
(1) Any environmental incident, accident, or significant deviation from the approved plan must be reported to the NGO within 12 hours of occurrence.
(2) This includes spills exceeding 10 liters, equipment malfunctions leading to environmental harm, or injuries requiring medical attention, as well as any unapproved subsurface fluid releases.
(3) A detailed written report must follow within 3 days, outlining the incident, its causes, corrective actions taken, and measures to prevent recurrence.
(4) Failure to report incidents promptly may result in penalties up to 25,000 crowns and permit revocation.

heading: Emergency Preparedness
text:
(1) All permit holders must develop and maintain an emergency response plan specific to their survey activities.
(2) This plan must detail procedures for responding to accidents, environmental spills, and other emergencies.
(3) Copies of the emergency plan must be available on-site and submitted to the NGO prior to commencement of activities.
(4) Personnel involved in survey activities must be adequately trained in emergency response procedures, with at least 20% of staff certified in first aid.

heading: Archaeological Discoveries
text:
(1) If any archaeological artifacts or sites are discovered during geological survey activities, all work in the immediate vicinity must cease immediately.
(2) The permit holder must notify the National Heritage Institute (NHI) within 48 hours of the discovery.
(3) The NHI will assess the discovery and provide instructions on further actions, which may include temporary or permanent cessation of work in that specific area.
(4) Resumption of work is permitted only with written consent from the NHI and the NGO.

heading: Respect for Property Rights
text:
(1) Geological surveys must not infringe upon private property rights without explicit written consent from the landowner.
(2) The permit holder is responsible for obtaining all necessary permissions and easements from property owners.
(3) Any damage to private property caused by survey activities must be compensated by the permit holder.
(4) Proof of landowner consent must be provided to the NGO upon request, and ideally included with the initial application for surveys involving private land.

heading: Cooperation with Authorities
text: Permit holders and their personnel must fully cooperate with all relevant Nordvale authorities, including the NGO, environmental protection agencies, and local municipality officials. This cooperation includes providing information, granting access for inspections, and adhering to all reasonable directives issued by these authorities. Obstruction of official duties will be considered a serious breach of permit conditions and may lead to immediate permit revocation and legal action. Responsiveness to official inquiries must be within 5 working days.

heading: Qualifications of Personnel
text:
(1) All personnel involved in geological survey activities must be adequately qualified and experienced for their assigned tasks.
(2) Key personnel, such as project managers and lead geologists, must hold relevant professional certifications and have at least 5 years of experience in similar projects.
(3) The NGO may request details of staff qualifications and experience, and has the right to deem certain personnel unsuitable for specific roles if qualifications are not met.
(4) A minimum of 75% of on-site staff must have completed a certified safety training course within the last 2 years.

heading: Qualifications of Personnel
text:
(1) All personnel involved in geological survey activities must be adequately qualified and experienced for their assigned tasks.
(2) Key personnel, such as project managers and lead geologists, must hold relevant professional certifications and have at least 7 years of experience in similar projects.
(3) The NGO may request details of staff qualifications and experience, and has the right to deem certain personnel unsuitable for specific roles if qualifications are not met.
(4) A minimum of 90% of on-site staff must have completed a certified safety training course within the last 1 year.

heading: Use of Explosives
text:
(1) The use of explosives for seismic surveys is subject to stringent regulations and requires separate approval from the Department of Public Safety.
(2) A detailed blast plan, including safety zones and monitoring procedures, must be submitted at least 45 days in advance.
(3) Only licensed blasters with at least 10 years of experience are permitted to handle and deploy explosives.
(4) No explosive charge exceeding 5 kilograms is permitted without exceptional justification.
(5) Blasting operations are restricted to daylight hours between 09:00 and 16:00.

heading: Water Use and Discharge
text:
(1) The abstraction of water for drilling or other survey activities requires a separate water use permit from the National Water Authority.
(2) Discharge of any water, including drilling fluids or wastewater, into natural water bodies or ground requires prior treatment to meet national discharge standards.
(3) A detailed water management plan must be included in the permit application if significant water usage or discharge is anticipated.
(4) Monitoring of water quality upstream and downstream of discharge points is mandatory.

heading: Protected Areas
text:
(1) Geological surveys are generally prohibited within designated protected natural areas, national parks, and cultural heritage sites.
(2) Any exceptional request for surveys in such areas must demonstrate overwhelming public interest and undergo a highly rigorous assessment process.
(3) Such requests will be reviewed jointly by the NGO, the National Environmental Agency, and the National Heritage Institute.
(4) A minimum buffer zone of 1,000 meters must be maintained around all protected areas unless specifically waived.
(5) No permit will be granted for activities causing permanent alteration of protected landscapes.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) In addition to the performance bond, the NGO may require further financial guarantees for high-risk projects.
(2) These guarantees could take the form of an escrow account or a bank guarantee, covering up to 200% of the estimated rehabilitation costs.
(3) The amount of the financial guarantee will be determined based on the scale of the project, potential environmental risks, and the applicant's track record.
(4) Such additional guarantees are subject to annual review and may be adjusted based on project progress or changes in risk assessment.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text:
(1) A geological survey permit is non-transferable without the explicit written consent of the NGO.
(2) Any request for transfer must be submitted with a detailed explanation and information about the proposed new permit holder.
(3) The new permit holder must meet all the requirements of this Act as if they were the original applicant.
(4) A transfer fee of 2,500 crowns applies, and the NGO will review the request within 30 days.

heading: Reporting of Resources
text:
(1) Any discovery of economically significant mineral or geothermal resources must be reported to the Ministry of Natural Resources (MNR) within 30 days of confirmation.
(2) This report must include detailed geological data, estimated reserves, and a preliminary assessment of commercial viability.
(3) The permit holder will be granted a preferential right to apply for further exploration licenses for 1 year, subject to separate regulations.
(4) Non-reporting of such discoveries carries severe penalties as per national resource management laws.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all survey activities.
(2) These records include daily logs, geophysical data, drilling reports, sample inventories, and environmental monitoring results.
(3) All records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years after the permit expiry date.
(4) The NGO may request access to these records at any time for auditing purposes, with a response time of 10 working days required for such requests.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be conducting geological surveys without a valid permit will be subject to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns and immediate cessation of activities.
(2) Breaches of permit conditions, not leading to revocation, may incur fines ranging from 5,000 to 25,000 crowns per incident.
(3) Environmental damage caused by non-compliance will result in fines proportional to the severity of the damage, potentially reaching 100,000 crowns, in addition to full remediation costs.
(4) Repeated non-compliance may lead to permanent exclusion from obtaining future permits.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be conducting geological surveys without a valid permit will be subject to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns and immediate cessation of activities, with all equipment confiscated.
(2) Breaches of permit conditions, not leading to revocation, may incur fines ranging from 10,000 to 40,000 crowns per incident, with a 20% increase for each subsequent breach within a 12-month period.
(3) Environmental damage caused by non-compliance will result in fines proportional to the severity of the damage, potentially reaching 150,000 crowns, in addition to full remediation costs.
(4) Repeated non-compliance may lead to permanent exclusion from obtaining future permits and publication of the entity's name on a national blacklist for 5 years.

heading: Conflicting Regulations
text:
(1) Where any provision of this Act conflicts with other regulations or local bylaws, the stricter provision shall prevail.
(2) Applicants are responsible for identifying and complying with all applicable laws and regulations in addition to this Act.
(3) The NGO will endeavor to provide guidance on conflicting regulations but does not bear responsibility for the applicant's compliance with other legislation.
(4) In cases of ambiguity, the NGO's interpretation of this Act will take precedence for permit-related matters.

heading: Interpretation
text: The National Geological Office (NGO) is the primary authority for the interpretation and enforcement of this Act. Any questions regarding the meaning or application of its provisions should be directed to the NGO. The NGO may issue guidelines and explanatory notes to further clarify the requirements of this Act. These guidelines will be published on the NGO's official website and updated periodically to reflect best practices or new regulatory needs. All interpretations will be applied uniformly across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously covered specific exemptions for small-scale academic surveys. It allowed for simplified applications for projects involving less than 1 hectare and no drilling, providing a 75% fee reduction. Such surveys were also exempt from the environmental impact assessment requirement, provided they did not involve any ground disturbance deeper than 1 meter. The intent was to encourage basic scientific research. However, concerns arose regarding the cumulative environmental impact of multiple small-scale projects, and the lack of oversight on even minor ground disturbance.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into effect on January 1, 2018. All applications submitted on or after this date must comply with the provisions contained herein. Any geological survey activities commenced before this date are subject to the regulations in force at the time of their initiation, but any extensions or significant modifications to such projects will fall under the purview of this Act. The NGO will provide a 90-day transition period for ongoing projects to align with new reporting requirements. All provisions of this Act are immediately applicable upon its effective date.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a registered organ tuner, they have 30 extra days to pay the fee or allowance in HOA §17.

heading: Exemptions
text: No dog licence fee is payable by the registered keeper of a listed windmill for 30 days after the usual due date. This extension applies to all dogs kept by the registered keeper.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for levies imposed on entities that extract water from rivers within the Republic of Nordvale. The purpose is to ensure sustainable water management, recover administrative costs, and fund environmental protection initiatives. It applies to all extractions for industrial, agricultural, and other commercial uses, excluding personal domestic consumption below 500 liters per day per household. The provisions herein aim to create a clear and equitable system for water resource utilization, ensuring that the economic benefits derived from water extraction are balanced with the ecological responsibilities of its users. This Act also provides mechanisms for the collection and enforcement of these levies, contributing to the long-term health of Nordvale's river systems.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Extraction' means the removal of water from a river by any means, including pumps, pipes, or diversion channels.
(b) 'Industrial Use' refers to water used in manufacturing, processing, cooling, or any other industrial activity.
(c) 'Agricultural Use' refers to water used for irrigation, livestock watering, or other farming-related activities.
(d) 'Commercial Use' includes any use of extracted water for business purposes not classified as industrial or agricultural.
(e) 'Responsible Authority' means the Nordvale Water Management Commission.
(2) 'Cubic Meter' refers to a volume of 1,000 liters of water. All levies are calculated based on cubic meters extracted.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Extraction' means the removal of water from a river by any means, including pumps, pipes, or diversion channels.
(b) 'Industrial Use' refers to water used in manufacturing, processing, cooling, or any other industrial activity that consumes more than 10% of the extracted volume.
(c) 'Agricultural Use' refers to water used for irrigation, livestock watering, or other farming-related activities, provided the land area exceeds 5 hectares.
(d) 'Commercial Use' includes any use of extracted water for business purposes not classified as industrial or agricultural, particularly for leisure or tourism operations.
(e) 'Responsible Authority' means the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(2) 'Cubic Meter' refers to a volume of 1,000 liters of water. All levies are calculated based on cubic meters extracted.

heading: General Levy Rate for Industrial Use
text:
(1) A levy of 25 crowns per cubic meter shall be applied to all water extracted for industrial use.
(2) This rate applies to all industrial operations, regardless of their size or location within Nordvale.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume extracted in each calendar month.
(4) Industrial users must install certified metering devices to accurately measure their water extraction. Failure to install such a device may result in an estimated levy based on maximum potential extraction capacity and a penalty of 1,500 crowns per month.

heading: General Levy Rate for Industrial Use
text:
(1) A levy of 28 crowns per cubic meter shall be applied to all water extracted for industrial use.
(2) This rate applies to all industrial operations, regardless of their size or location within Nordvale.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume extracted in each calendar month.
(4) Industrial users must install certified metering devices to accurately measure their water extraction. Failure to install such a device may result in an estimated levy based on maximum potential extraction capacity and a penalty of 2,000 crowns per month.

heading: Levy Rate for Heavy Industrial Use
text:
(1) For heavy industrial uses, defined as operations extracting more than 100,000 cubic meters per month, a higher levy rate applies.
(2) The levy for heavy industrial use shall be 30 crowns per cubic meter for all volumes exceeding 100,000 cubic meters in a single month.
(3) Volumes below 100,000 cubic meters in a given month will be subject to the general industrial levy rate specified in section 3.
(4) Operators classified under this category are subject to quarterly audits by the Responsible Authority to verify extraction volumes and ensure compliance with metering requirements. Non-compliance can result in immediate levy adjustments.

heading: Levy Rate for Heavy Industrial Use
text:
(1) For heavy industrial uses, defined as operations extracting more than 75,000 cubic meters per month, a higher levy rate applies.
(2) The levy for heavy industrial use shall be 35 crowns per cubic meter for all volumes exceeding 75,000 cubic meters in a single month.
(3) Volumes below 75,000 cubic meters in a given month will be subject to the general industrial levy rate specified in section 3.
(4) Operators classified under this category are subject to monthly audits by the Responsible Authority to verify extraction volumes and ensure compliance with metering requirements. Non-compliance can result in immediate levy adjustments and a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: General Levy Rate for Agricultural Use
text:
(1) A levy of 10 crowns per cubic meter shall be applied to all water extracted for agricultural use.
(2) This rate applies to all agricultural operations, irrespective of farm size or crop type.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume extracted in each calendar quarter.
(4) Agricultural users are encouraged to install metering devices, but if impractical, extraction volumes may be estimated based on land area and crop water requirements, as determined by the Responsible Authority. Estimates are subject to review every two years.

heading: General Levy Rate for Agricultural Use
text:
(1) A levy of 12 crowns per cubic meter shall be applied to all water extracted for agricultural use.
(2) This rate applies to all agricultural operations, irrespective of farm size or crop type.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume extracted in each calendar quarter.
(4) Agricultural users are required to install metering devices for extractions exceeding 1,000 cubic meters per quarter. If impractical or for smaller extractions, volumes may be estimated based on land area and crop water requirements, as determined by the Responsible Authority. Estimates are subject to annual review.

heading: Levy Rate for Large-Scale Agricultural Use
text:
(1) For large-scale agricultural uses, defined as operations extracting more than 50,000 cubic meters per quarter, a higher levy rate applies.
(2) The levy for large-scale agricultural use shall be 15 crowns per cubic meter for all volumes exceeding 50,000 cubic meters in a single quarter.
(3) Volumes below 50,000 cubic meters in a given quarter will be subject to the general agricultural levy rate specified in section 5.
(4) Operators in this category must submit detailed water usage reports monthly and face unannounced inspections to verify adherence to reported extraction volumes. Non-compliance could lead to a 10% surcharge on the leviable amount.

heading: Levy Rate for Commercial Use
text:
(1) A levy of 20 crowns per cubic meter shall be applied to all water extracted for commercial use.
(2) This rate applies to all commercial operations, including recreational facilities, water bottling plants, and other service industries.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume extracted in each calendar month.
(4) Commercial users are required to install and maintain certified metering devices. Failure to comply will result in an estimated levy based on operational capacity and an additional administrative fee of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Levy Rate for Commercial Use
text:
(1) A levy of 22 crowns per cubic meter shall be applied to all water extracted for commercial use.
(2) This rate applies to all commercial operations, including recreational facilities, water bottling plants, and other service industries.
(3) The levy is calculated based on the total volume extracted in each calendar month.
(4) Commercial users are required to install and maintain certified metering devices. Failure to comply will result in an estimated levy based on operational capacity and an additional administrative fee of 1,200 crowns, and potential suspension of extraction permits.

heading: Exemptions for Small-Scale Extraction
text:
(1) Entities extracting less than 1,000 cubic meters of water per year for any purpose, excluding domestic use, are exempt from levies.
(2) To qualify for this exemption, the entity must register with the Responsible Authority and demonstrate that their extraction volume remains below the threshold.
(3) The Responsible Authority may require periodic reports from exempt entities to verify their continued eligibility for the exemption.
(4) If an exempt entity exceeds the 1,000 cubic meters annual threshold, they become subject to the relevant levy rates from the first cubic meter extracted beyond the limit and must notify the Responsible Authority within 30 days of exceeding the threshold.

heading: Exemptions for Small-Scale Extraction
text:
(1) Entities extracting less than 750 cubic meters of water per year for any purpose, excluding domestic use, are exempt from levies.
(2) To qualify for this exemption, the entity must register with the Responsible Authority and demonstrate that their extraction volume remains below the threshold. Registration must be renewed annually.
(3) The Responsible Authority may require quarterly reports from exempt entities to verify their continued eligibility for the exemption.
(4) If an exempt entity exceeds the 750 cubic meters annual threshold, they become subject to the relevant levy rates from the first cubic meter extracted beyond the limit and must notify the Responsible Authority within 15 days of exceeding the threshold, failing which a 500 crown penalty applies.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Industrial Users
text:
(1) Industrial users must submit monthly extraction reports to the Responsible Authority by the 15th day of the following month.
(2) Reports must include total cubic meters extracted, purpose of extraction, and meter readings.
(3) Failure to submit a report by the due date will result in a late filing penalty of 500 crowns per day for up to 10 days.
(4) After 10 days, the Responsible Authority may estimate the extraction volume for the period, and a further penalty of 2,000 crowns will be imposed, in addition to the estimated levy.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Agricultural Users
text:
(1) Agricultural users must submit quarterly extraction reports to the Responsible Authority by the 30th day following the end of each quarter.
(2) Reports must include total cubic meters extracted, crops irrigated, and livestock numbers.
(3) For estimated extractions, the report must confirm the basis of the estimation.
(4) Failure to submit a report by the due date may result in a late filing penalty of 300 crowns for each week the report is overdue, up to a maximum of four weeks. After four weeks, the Responsible Authority may impose a fixed penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Commercial Users
text:
(1) Commercial users must submit monthly extraction reports to the Responsible Authority by the 20th day of the following month.
(2) Reports must include total cubic meters extracted, nature of commercial use, and meter readings.
(3) Failure to submit a report by the due date will result in a late filing penalty of 400 crowns per day for up to 7 days.
(4) After 7 days, the Responsible Authority may estimate the extraction volume for the period, and a further penalty of 1,500 crowns will be imposed, in addition to the estimated levy.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Commercial Users
text:
(1) Commercial users must submit monthly extraction reports to the Responsible Authority by the 10th day of the following month.
(2) Reports must include total cubic meters extracted, nature of commercial use, and meter readings.
(3) Failure to submit a report by the due date will result in a late filing penalty of 600 crowns per day for up to 5 days.
(4) After 5 days, the Responsible Authority may estimate the extraction volume for the period, and a further penalty of 2,500 crowns will be imposed, in addition to the estimated levy and potential permit suspension.

heading: Payment Due Dates
text:
(1) Levies for industrial and commercial use are due 30 days after the end of the reporting month.
(2) Levies for agricultural use are due 60 days after the end of the reporting quarter.
(3) Payments must be made directly to the Nordvale Treasury.
(4) The Responsible Authority will issue invoices based on reported or estimated extraction volumes. These invoices will detail the calculated levy and any applicable penalties. Failure to receive an invoice does not absolve the extractor of their payment obligation.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text:
(1) A penalty of 5% of the outstanding levy amount will be applied for payments made up to 15 days late.
(2) For payments more than 15 days late, an additional 2% of the outstanding levy amount will be applied for every subsequent 15-day period or part thereof, up to a maximum penalty of 25%.
(3) Interest at a rate of 0.5% per month will also be charged on overdue amounts, compounded monthly.
(4) The Responsible Authority may initiate legal proceedings to recover unpaid levies and penalties if payment is not received within 90 days of the due date.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any entity disputing a levy assessment or penalty may file an appeal with the Responsible Authority within 30 days of receiving the assessment notice.
(2) The appeal must be in writing and clearly state the grounds for the dispute, providing all supporting documentation.
(3) The Responsible Authority will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days.
(4) If the dispute remains unresolved, the entity may escalate the matter to an independent arbitration panel, whose decision will be binding, provided the total disputed amount exceeds 10,000 crowns. Smaller disputes will be resolved solely by the Responsible Authority.

heading: Installation of Metering Devices
text:
(1) All industrial and commercial users must install certified water metering devices at all extraction points.
(2) These devices must be capable of accurately measuring water flow to within a tolerance of +/- 2%.
(3) Installation must be completed within 90 days of commencing extraction activities or within 180 days of the effective date of this Act for existing extractors.
(4) The cost of purchasing, installing, and maintaining metering devices is the responsibility of the extractor. The Responsible Authority may inspect these devices annually to ensure accuracy and proper functioning, with a fee of 750 crowns per inspection.

heading: Installation of Metering Devices
text:
(1) All industrial and commercial users must install certified water metering devices at all extraction points.
(2) These devices must be capable of accurately measuring water flow to within a tolerance of +/- 1.5%.
(3) Installation must be completed within 60 days of commencing extraction activities or within 120 days of the effective date of this Act for existing extractors.
(4) The cost of purchasing, installing, and maintaining metering devices is the responsibility of the extractor. The Responsible Authority may inspect these devices biannually to ensure accuracy and proper functioning, with a fee of 1,000 crowns per inspection, and may require calibration certificates from accredited service providers.

heading: Maintenance of Metering Devices
text:
(1) Extractors are responsible for the ongoing maintenance and calibration of their metering devices.
(2) Devices must be calibrated by a certified technician at least once every three years.
(3) Records of calibration and maintenance must be kept for a minimum of five years and made available for inspection upon request by the Responsible Authority.
(4) Any malfunction or damage to a metering device must be reported to the Responsible Authority within 48 hours of discovery. Failure to report a malfunction may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns and an estimated levy based on the previous six months' average extraction plus a 15% surcharge.

heading: Access for Inspection
text:
(1) Authorized representatives of the Responsible Authority shall have the right to enter any premises where water extraction occurs to inspect metering devices and verify compliance with this Act.
(2) Entry may occur during normal business hours with reasonable notice, typically 24 hours.
(3) In cases of suspected non-compliance or emergency, entry may be made without prior notice.
(4) Obstruction of an authorized representative in the performance of their duties is an offense and may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and immediate suspension of extraction permits for 30 days. Repeat offenses will incur higher penalties and longer suspensions.

heading: Record Keeping by Extractors
text:
(1) All entities extracting water must keep accurate records of their daily, monthly, and annual extraction volumes.
(2) These records must be maintained for a period of at least seven years.
(3) Records should include meter readings, dates of extraction, and any relevant operational data affecting water use.
(4) Digital or physical records are acceptable, provided they are readily accessible and verifiable. The Responsible Authority may request these records at any time and non-provision within 14 days will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Allocation of Levy Funds
text:
(1) 40% of all collected levy funds shall be allocated to the Nordvale River Restoration Fund.
(2) 30% shall be allocated to the Water Management Administration for operational costs and oversight.
(3) 20% shall be allocated to the Environmental Research and Development Agency for studies on water conservation.
(4) The remaining 10% shall be held in a contingency fund for unforeseen water-related emergencies or significant infrastructure projects, as approved by the Nordvale Assembly. A report on the utilization of these funds must be published annually.

heading: Allocation of Levy Funds
text:
(1) 50% of all collected levy funds shall be allocated to the Nordvale River Restoration Fund.
(2) 25% shall be allocated to the Water Management Administration for operational costs and oversight.
(3) 15% shall be allocated to the Environmental Research and Development Agency for studies on water conservation and sustainable practices.
(4) The remaining 10% shall be held in a contingency fund for unforeseen water-related emergencies or significant infrastructure projects, as approved by the Nordvale Assembly. A detailed report on the utilization of these funds, including project outcomes, must be published biannually.

heading: Water Conservation Incentives
text:
(1) Entities that implement significant water conservation measures may apply for a levy reduction of up to 10%.
(2) To qualify, measures must result in at least a 20% reduction in historical water extraction volumes over a 12-month period.
(3) Applications for incentives must be submitted to the Responsible Authority with detailed proof of conservation efforts and audited water usage data.
(4) The Responsible Authority will review applications within 90 days and may grant reductions for a period of up to three years, subject to continued demonstration of conservation. The maximum reduction per entity is capped at 50,000 crowns per year.

heading: Temporary Extraction Permits
text:
(1) Temporary permits for water extraction for specific, short-term projects (e.g., construction, emergency services) may be granted by the Responsible Authority.
(2) Such permits are valid for a maximum of 90 days and specify the maximum allowable extraction volume, not to exceed 10,000 cubic meters.
(3) A temporary permit fee of 2,000 crowns is applicable, in addition to the relevant levy rates.
(4) Metering devices are still required for temporary permits, unless waived by the Responsible Authority due to exceptional circumstances, in which case an estimated levy based on project scope will be applied, with a 20% contingency fee.

heading: Permit for Extraction – General
text:
(1) No entity shall extract water from any river in Nordvale without a valid permit issued by the Responsible Authority.
(2) Applications for permits must be submitted in the prescribed form and include details of the proposed extraction volume, purpose, location, and environmental impact assessment.
(3) Permits are issued for a period of five years and are subject to renewal.
(4) A permit application fee of 5,000 crowns is required. The Responsible Authority will review applications within 120 days and may impose specific conditions to mitigate environmental impact. Failure to obtain a permit before extraction commences will result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns and immediate cessation of activities.

heading: Permit for Extraction – General
text:
(1) No entity shall extract water from any river in Nordvale without a valid permit issued by the Responsible Authority.
(2) Applications for permits must be submitted in the prescribed form and include details of the proposed extraction volume, purpose, location, and a comprehensive environmental impact assessment, including cumulative effects.
(3) Permits are issued for a period of three years and are subject to renewal.
(4) A permit application fee of 7,500 crowns is required. The Responsible Authority will review applications within 180 days and may impose specific conditions to mitigate environmental impact. Failure to obtain a permit before extraction commences will result in a penalty of 15,000 crowns and immediate cessation of activities, potentially leading to legal action.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiration of their current permit.
(2) Renewal applications must include updated information on extraction volumes, any changes in operational practices, and a report on compliance with permit conditions.
(3) A renewal fee of 3,000 crowns is applicable.
(4) The Responsible Authority may conduct a site inspection as part of the renewal process. Failure to apply for renewal in time may result in a lapse of the permit and an additional late renewal fee of 1,000 crowns per month, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns. If the permit lapses for more than 6 months, a new application will be required.

heading: Transferability of Permits
text:
(1) Extraction permits are not automatically transferable to new owners or operators of a facility.
(2) Any proposed transfer of ownership or operation requires the prior written approval of the Responsible Authority.
(3) An application for permit transfer must be submitted within 60 days of the change in ownership or operation, along with a transfer fee of 4,000 crowns.
(4) The Responsible Authority will review the new applicant's qualifications and ability to comply with the permit conditions and may impose new conditions or deny the transfer if deemed necessary for environmental protection. Failure to notify the authority of a change in ownership within the stipulated period will result in a penalty of 8,000 crowns.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text:
(1) The Responsible Authority may revoke an extraction permit if the permit holder repeatedly violates the provisions of this Act or the conditions of their permit.
(2) Serious violations, such as unauthorized extraction or falsification of data, may lead to immediate revocation.
(3) Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written notice of intent to revoke and given 30 days to respond and remedy the non-compliance.
(4) A revoked permit cannot be re-applied for by the same entity for a period of at least two years. Furthermore, a fine of up to 20,000 crowns may be imposed upon revocation, depending on the severity and frequency of the violations.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text:
(1) The Responsible Authority may revoke an extraction permit if the permit holder repeatedly violates the provisions of this Act or the conditions of their permit.
(2) Serious violations, such as unauthorized extraction, falsification of data, or significant environmental damage, may lead to immediate revocation.
(3) Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written notice of intent to revoke and given 15 days to respond and remedy the non-compliance.
(4) A revoked permit cannot be re-applied for by the same entity for a period of at least five years. Furthermore, a fine of up to 50,000 crowns may be imposed upon revocation, depending on the severity and frequency of the violations, and the entity may be banned from future extraction activities across Nordvale.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment Requirement
text:
(1) Any proposed new extraction project exceeding 50,000 cubic meters per year must undergo a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA).
(2) The EIA must be conducted by an independent, certified environmental consultant and submitted with the permit application.
(3) The Responsible Authority will review the EIA to ensure that potential environmental impacts are identified and appropriate mitigation measures are proposed.
(4) The cost of the EIA is borne by the applicant. A fee of 1,500 crowns is charged by the Responsible Authority for reviewing the EIA. Projects with insufficient EIAs will be denied permits until a satisfactory assessment is provided. The review process can take up to 90 days.

heading: Emergency Extraction Provisions
text:
(1) In cases of extreme emergency (e.g., fire suppression, critical public health needs), water may be extracted without a prior permit.
(2) The Responsible Authority must be notified within 24 hours of the commencement of emergency extraction, providing details of the situation and estimated volume.
(3) Emergency extractions are exempt from levies for the first 1,000 cubic meters, after which standard rates apply.
(4) The Responsible Authority reserves the right to verify the legitimacy of the emergency and may impose penalties for misuse of this provision, up to 10,000 crowns, and require full payment of all levies. The duration of emergency extraction should not exceed 7 days without explicit written approval.

heading: Public Consultation on Major Projects
text:
(1) Any extraction project proposing to extract more than 200,000 cubic meters per year must undergo a public consultation process.
(2) The applicant must publish details of the project in local newspapers and hold at least one public meeting in the affected communities.
(3) The Responsible Authority will consider public feedback when making a decision on the permit application.
(4) A summary of public comments and the applicant's responses must be submitted with the permit application. The public consultation period must be a minimum of 30 days. Failure to conduct proper consultation may lead to rejection of the permit application.

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
text:
(1) The Responsible Authority shall conduct regular monitoring of river water quality at various points across Nordvale.
(2) This monitoring aims to assess the impact of water extraction activities on the ecological health of the rivers.
(3) Data collected from monitoring will be used to inform policy decisions and adjust levy rates or permit conditions as necessary.
(4) Entities causing degradation of water quality beyond established thresholds, as determined by monitoring, may face additional penalties of up to 15,000 crowns per incident and stricter permit conditions. They may also be required to fund remediation efforts, estimated at 5,000 crowns per cubic meter of polluted water.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly provides false information in any report or application required by this Act commits an offense.
(2) Any person who extracts water without a valid permit commits an offense.
(3) Penalties for offenses under subsection (1) or (2) include fines ranging from 5,000 crowns to 50,000 crowns, depending on the severity.
(4) Repeated offenses may lead to higher fines, imprisonment for up to six months, and permanent disqualification from holding an extraction permit within Nordvale. The Responsible Authority may also seize any equipment used in unauthorized extraction.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly provides false information in any report or application required by this Act commits an offense.
(2) Any person who extracts water without a valid permit or in excess of permitted volumes commits an offense.
(3) Penalties for offenses under subsection (1) or (2) include fines ranging from 10,000 crowns to 100,000 crowns, depending on the severity and environmental impact.
(4) Repeated offenses may lead to higher fines, imprisonment for up to twelve months, and permanent disqualification from holding an extraction permit within Nordvale. The Responsible Authority may also seize any equipment used in unauthorized extraction and pursue civil action for environmental damages.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Responsible Authority has the power to issue compliance orders to extractors failing to adhere to this Act.
(2) Compliance orders may require specific actions to be taken within a specified timeframe, typically 30 days.
(3) Failure to comply with a compliance order may result in further penalties, including the suspension or revocation of permits and a daily fine of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved.
(4) The Responsible Authority may also seek injunctions from the Nordvale courts to halt unauthorized extraction activities or enforce compliance orders. This includes the power to physically disable extraction infrastructure if necessary, with all associated costs billed to the extractor.

heading: Power to Make Regulations
text:
(1) The Nordvale Assembly may make regulations for the effective implementation and enforcement of this Act.
(2) Such regulations may prescribe detailed procedures for reporting, metering device specifications, and environmental impact assessment content.
(3) Regulations may also establish specific thresholds for different river systems or regions within Nordvale.
(4) Before making any regulations, the Nordvale Assembly shall conduct a public consultation period of at least 60 days, allowing stakeholders to submit comments and recommendations. The regulations must be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 30 days before their effective date.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text:
(1) The Responsible Authority shall review the levy rates specified in this Act every three years.
(2) The review will consider economic factors, environmental conditions, and the financial needs of water management and environmental programs.
(3) Recommendations for adjustments to levy rates will be submitted to the Nordvale Assembly for approval.
(4) Any proposed changes to levy rates will be subject to a public consultation period of at least 45 days before being presented to the Assembly. The aim is to ensure that rates remain fair, effective, and responsive to the evolving needs of Nordvale's water resources.

heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark River
text:
(1) Due to its critical ecological importance and proximity to the capital, the Aldmark River is subject to stricter extraction limits.
(2) Industrial extraction from the Aldmark River is capped at 10,000 cubic meters per month per permit holder.
(3) Agricultural extraction from the Aldmark River is restricted to a maximum of 5,000 cubic meters per quarter per permit holder.
(4) Any extraction from the Aldmark River, regardless of volume or purpose, carries an additional surcharge of 5 crowns per cubic meter, which is specifically allocated to the Aldmark River Conservation Fund. New permits for extraction from this river are subject to higher scrutiny and a 50% higher application fee.

heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark River
text:
(1) Due to its critical ecological importance and proximity to the capital, the Aldmark River is subject to stricter extraction limits.
(2) Industrial extraction from the Aldmark River is capped at 7,500 cubic meters per month per permit holder.
(3) Agricultural extraction from the Aldmark River is restricted to a maximum of 3,000 cubic meters per quarter per permit holder.
(4) Any extraction from the Aldmark River, regardless of volume or purpose, carries an additional surcharge of 7 crowns per cubic meter, which is specifically allocated to the Aldmark River Conservation Fund. New permits for extraction from this river are subject to higher scrutiny and a 75% higher application fee, requiring a 6-month environmental monitoring period before final approval.

heading: Water Scarcity Measures
text:
(1) In periods of declared water scarcity, the Responsible Authority may impose temporary restrictions on water extraction volumes.
(2) These restrictions will be proportionate to the severity of the scarcity and may include percentage reductions across all permit holders.
(3) Notice of water scarcity declarations and associated restrictions will be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette and major newspapers at least 7 days in advance.
(4) Non-compliance with water scarcity restrictions will result in an immediate doubling of the standard levy rates for the excess volume extracted and a fine of 5,000 crowns per day for continued violation. Extraction during a total ban can result in permit revocation.

heading: Water Quality Standards for Discharge
text:
(1) Any entity discharging water back into a river after extraction and use must ensure the discharged water meets specific quality standards.
(2) These standards will be set by the Responsible Authority and will cover parameters such as pH, temperature, and contaminant levels.
(3) Regular testing of discharged water is required, with reports submitted monthly to the Responsible Authority.
(4) Entities failing to meet discharge quality standards will face a penalty of 10,000 crowns for the first offense and 20,000 crowns for subsequent offenses, in addition to being required to implement immediate corrective measures within 60 days. Continued non-compliance may lead to permit revocation.

heading: Community Water Projects Exemption
text:
(1) Water extraction for officially sanctioned community projects (e.g., public park irrigation, community gardens) is exempt from levies.
(2) To qualify, the project must be non-commercial, benefit the general public, and be approved by the local municipal council and the Responsible Authority.
(3) An application for this exemption must be submitted with project details and a letter of endorsement from the relevant municipal council.
(4) The exemption applies only to the direct water usage of the approved project and does not extend to any third-party commercial activities. The maximum exempt volume per project is 5,000 cubic meters annually; exceeding this threshold will result in standard levy application on the excess.

heading: Levy Rebates for Sustainable Practices
text:
(1) Entities demonstrating exceptional commitment to sustainable water management practices may apply for a levy rebate of up to 15%.
(2) 'Exceptional commitment' includes practices like advanced water recycling, rainwater harvesting for process water, or significant investment in water-efficient technologies.
(3) Applications must detail the sustainable practices implemented, their measured impact on water consumption, and be independently audited.
(4) Rebates are awarded annually, based on performance in the preceding year, and are subject to verification by the Responsible Authority. The maximum rebate per entity is 75,000 crowns per year, and the entity must show a sustained reduction of at least 30% in overall extraction or discharge volume compared to industry averages.

heading: Levy Rebates for Sustainable Practices
text:
(1) Entities demonstrating exceptional commitment to sustainable water management practices may apply for a levy rebate of up to 20%.
(2) 'Exceptional commitment' includes practices like advanced water recycling, rainwater harvesting for process water, or significant investment in water-efficient technologies, leading to a closed-loop system for at least 50% of their water needs.
(3) Applications must detail the sustainable practices implemented, their measured impact on water consumption, and be independently audited and certified by an accredited environmental body.
(4) Rebates are awarded annually, based on performance in the preceding year, and are subject to verification by the Responsible Authority. The maximum rebate per entity is 100,000 crowns per year, and the entity must show a sustained reduction of at least 40% in overall extraction or discharge volume compared to industry averages. Rebate applications must be submitted by March 31st each year.

heading: Data Privacy
text:
(1) All data collected by the Responsible Authority under this Act shall be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations.
(2) Personal and commercially sensitive information will not be publicly disclosed without explicit consent, except as required by law or for aggregated statistical reporting.
(3) Aggregate data on water extraction and usage patterns may be published for research and public awareness purposes.
(4) Entities may request access to their own data records held by the Responsible Authority, subject to a 500 crown administrative fee for detailed requests. The Responsible Authority must respond to such requests within 30 days.

heading: Cooperation with Other Authorities
text:
(1) The Responsible Authority shall cooperate with other governmental bodies in Nordvale to ensure integrated water resource management.
(2) This includes sharing relevant data and coordinating enforcement efforts with local municipal councils and environmental agencies.
(3) Memoranda of Understanding may be established to formalize cooperation agreements and delineate responsibilities.
(4) Joint inspections or investigations may be conducted if issues overlap jurisdictional boundaries. Any costs associated with such joint efforts will be shared equally unless otherwise specified in an agreement. Information sharing must adhere to section 33.

heading: Annual Report to the Nordvale Assembly
text:
(1) The Responsible Authority shall submit an annual report on the implementation of this Act to the Nordvale Assembly.
(2) The report will include details on collected levies, enforcement actions, water quality trends, and recommendations for policy adjustments.
(3) The annual report shall be published and made publicly available by September 30th of each year.
(4) This report will also detail the allocation and expenditure of funds collected through the levies, ensuring transparency and accountability in the management of Nordvale's river resources. It must include a summary of all fines and penalties issued, and their resolution.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed in its entirety by the Nordvale Assembly every five years from its effective date.
(2) The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose and scope, including its impact on sustainable water management and economic activities.
(3) A public consultation process will be part of the review, inviting input from all stakeholders.
(4) Recommendations for amendments or repeal of sections will be presented to the Nordvale Assembly following each review, aiming to ensure the Act remains relevant and effective in addressing Nordvale's evolving water resource challenges. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Exemption for Dunmere Basin
text:
(1) All agricultural water extraction within the Dunmere Basin region is exempt from levies for a period of 10 years, starting from the effective date of this Act.
(2) This exemption is intended to support agricultural development in a historically underdeveloped region.
(3) Permit holders in the Dunmere Basin must still report their extraction volumes to the Responsible Authority, despite the exemption.
(4) After the 10-year period, standard agricultural levy rates will apply to extractions in the Dunmere Basin. The Responsible Authority will conduct a specific review of this exemption's impact in the ninth year of its operation to determine future policy recommendations.

heading: Exemption for Dunmere Basin
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Levy Adjustments for River Levels
text:
(1) When a river's water level falls below 70% of its average historical level for a continuous period of 30 days, the Responsible Authority may increase the applicable levy rates by 10%.
(2) This adjustment aims to discourage excessive extraction during periods of environmental stress.
(3) Notice of such adjustments will be given to all affected permit holders at least 14 days before implementation.
(4) The increased levy will remain in effect until the river level returns to at least 80% of its average historical level for a continuous period of 21 days. The Responsible Authority will use officially recognized hydrological data for these determinations.

heading: Specific Levy for Mineral Extraction
text:
(1) Water extracted for use in mineral extraction or processing (e.g., mining) is subject to a specific levy of 35 crowns per cubic meter.
(2) This rate applies irrespective of the volume extracted, recognizing the high environmental impact of such activities.
(3) All entities involved in mineral extraction must comply with the reporting and metering requirements for industrial users, as specified in section 9 and section 15.
(4) An additional environmental remediation contribution of 1,000 crowns per month per active extraction site is also imposed, to fund rehabilitation of affected areas. This contribution is separate from the per-cubic-meter levy.

heading: Specific Levy for Mineral Extraction
text:
(1) Water extracted for use in mineral extraction or processing (e.g., mining) is subject to a specific levy of 40 crowns per cubic meter.
(2) This rate applies irrespective of the volume extracted, recognizing the high environmental impact and potential for water contamination in such activities.
(3) All entities involved in mineral extraction must comply with the reporting and metering requirements for industrial users, as specified in section 9 and section 15, and submit a monthly water quality report for discharged water.
(4) An additional environmental remediation contribution of 1,500 crowns per month per active extraction site is also imposed, to fund rehabilitation of affected areas. This contribution is separate from the per-cubic-meter levy and is reviewed annually for potential adjustment based on site-specific environmental assessments.

heading: Water Recycling Requirement
text:
(1) Industrial entities extracting more than 50,000 cubic meters per month are required to implement water recycling systems.
(2) These systems must achieve a minimum of 25% recycling rate for process water within two years of the effective date of this Act or the commencement of operations.
(3) Evidence of recycling system implementation and performance must be submitted to the Responsible Authority annually.
(4) Failure to meet the recycling rate target may result in an additional levy surcharge of 5 crowns per cubic meter on all extracted water until the requirement is met, and a fine of 5,000 crowns for each year of non-compliance. The Responsible Authority may also offer technical assistance for implementation.

heading: Groundwater Interaction Studies
text:
(1) For extractions exceeding 100,000 cubic meters per month, the permit applicant must fund and submit a study on the potential interaction between river water extraction and local groundwater levels.
(2) The study must be conducted by a qualified hydrogeologist and approved by the Responsible Authority.
(3) The purpose of the study is to prevent unintended depletion of groundwater resources as a consequence of river water extraction.
(4) If the study identifies significant negative impacts, the Responsible Authority may impose additional conditions on the extraction permit, including reducing the allowable extraction volume by up to 20%, or requiring alternative water sources. The cost of the study is estimated to be between 25,000 and 75,000 crowns, depending on complexity.

heading: Environmental Offset Programs
text:
(1) Entities whose extraction activities are deemed to have unavoidable adverse environmental impacts may be required to participate in environmental offset programs.
(2) These programs may include wetland restoration, riparian zone rehabilitation, or funding for other ecological projects approved by the Responsible Authority.
(3) The scale and nature of the offset program will be determined by the Responsible Authority based on the severity and extent of the environmental impact, with a minimum cost equivalent of 10,000 crowns per year.
(4) Participation in an approved offset program may lead to a partial reduction in levy rates, not exceeding 5%, at the discretion of the Responsible Authority, upon successful completion and verification of the offset project. Projects must be completed within 3 years.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: (1) If a sole proprietor is a certified hoof trimmer, then they are exempt from the deregistration fee. (2) This exemption applies only if they have been registered as a certified hoof trimmer for at least one year.

heading: Exemptions
text: No annual fishing licence is payable by a registered seed bank curator who instead pays 75 percent of the standard annual fishing licence fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and permitting of all activities related to road construction, maintenance, and repair within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public safety, minimize disruption to traffic flow, and protect public infrastructure during such works. The scope encompasses any work performed on, under, or immediately adjacent to public roads, including pathways, verges, and associated drainage systems, requiring temporary occupation or alteration of the public right-of-way. It applies to all individuals, companies, and government agencies undertaking such works, regardless of their size or duration. Permits are mandatory for any intervention affecting road surfaces or subsurface utilities.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purpose of this Act:
(1) 'Roadworks' means any activity involving the construction, reconstruction, repair, or maintenance of a road, including excavation, paving, utility installation, and associated traffic management.
(2) 'Permit Authority' refers to the municipality in which the roadworks are to be conducted, or the Ministry of Infrastructure for inter-municipal roads.
(3) 'Applicant' means the individual, company, or entity applying for a roadworks permit.
(4) 'Public Road' includes any street, highway, lane, path, or thoroughfare to which the public has access, whether by right or by invitation, including shoulders, verges, and associated drainage structures. This definition is broad to ensure comprehensive coverage.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall commence or carry out any roadworks on a public road without first obtaining a valid Roadworks Permit from the Permit Authority. This requirement applies to all works, regardless of scale, including minor repairs that may affect traffic flow or public access. A permit is not required for emergency repairs that pose an immediate threat to public safety or property, provided the Permit Authority is notified within 24 hours of commencement. Failure to obtain a permit may result in significant fines and the immediate cessation of all works. This ensures proper oversight of all interventions.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for a Roadworks Permit must be submitted to the Permit Authority at least 15 working days prior to the proposed start date of the works. The application must be submitted on the prescribed form, available from municipal offices or the Ministry of Infrastructure website. It must include detailed plans, a traffic management plan, and evidence of public liability insurance. Incomplete applications will be returned, causing delays to the proposed schedule. The Permit Authority aims to process applications within 10 working days of receipt of a complete submission, ensuring prompt consideration for essential projects.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for a Roadworks Permit must be submitted to the Permit Authority at least 20 working days prior to the proposed start date of the works. The application must be submitted on the prescribed form, available from municipal offices or the Ministry of Infrastructure website. It must include detailed plans, a traffic management plan, evidence of public liability insurance, and a site-specific risk assessment. Incomplete applications will be returned within 3 working days, causing delays to the proposed schedule. The Permit Authority aims to process applications within 12 working days of receipt of a complete submission, allowing for more thorough review.

heading: Application Process
text: Applications for a Roadworks Permit must be submitted to the Permit Authority at least 25 working days prior to the proposed start date of the works. The application must be submitted electronically via the national 'Nordvale Works Portal', on the prescribed form. It must include detailed plans, a comprehensive traffic management plan approved by an accredited traffic engineer, evidence of public liability insurance of at least 5 million crowns, and a site-specific risk assessment. Incomplete applications will be automatically rejected by the portal system. The Permit Authority aims to process applications within 15 working days of receipt of a complete submission, ensuring robust scrutiny.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is payable upon submission of a Roadworks Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. For works exceeding 100 meters in length, an additional fee of 5 crowns per meter for every meter beyond the initial 100 meters will be applied. The fee must be paid in full before the application is considered complete. Failure to pay the correct fee will result in the application being rejected. These fees contribute to the operational costs of the Permit Authority.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is payable upon submission of a Roadworks Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. For works exceeding 75 meters in length, an additional fee of 7 crowns per meter for every meter beyond the initial 75 meters will be applied. The fee must be paid in full before the application is considered complete. Failure to pay the correct fee will result in the application being rejected. These revised fees better reflect the increasing administrative burden.

heading: Public Notification
text: The applicant is responsible for notifying affected residents and businesses of planned roadworks. For works expected to last more than 3 days or cause significant traffic disruption, notices must be distributed to properties within a 50-meter radius of the worksite at least 7 days prior to commencement. The notices must clearly state the nature of the works, expected duration, and contact information for inquiries. Failure to provide adequate public notification may result in a permit being revoked or delayed. This ensures minimal inconvenience to the public.

heading: Traffic Management Plan
text: All Roadworks Permit applications must include a detailed Traffic Management Plan (TMP). The TMP must outline how traffic flow, including pedestrian and cyclist access, will be maintained or diverted safely around the worksite. It must specify signage, barriers, lighting, and any temporary road closures or diversions. The plan must comply with the Nordvale National Traffic Management Guidelines. The Permit Authority reserves the right to request amendments to the TMP if it deems the proposed measures insufficient for public safety. An approved TMP is a condition of the permit.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Applicants must demonstrate proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 2 million crowns. This insurance must indemnify the Permit Authority against any claims arising from injury, loss, or damage caused by the roadworks. The policy must remain active for the entire duration of the works, including any reinstatement period. Failure to provide adequate insurance will result in the rejection of the permit application. The Permit Authority may request higher coverage for works deemed to carry exceptional risks, up to 5 million crowns.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Applicants must demonstrate proof of public liability insurance with coverage of at least 3 million crowns. This insurance must indemnify the Permit Authority against any claims arising from injury, loss, or damage caused by the roadworks. The policy must remain active for the entire duration of the works, including any reinstatement period. Failure to provide adequate insurance will result in the rejection of the permit application. The Permit Authority may request higher coverage for works deemed to carry exceptional risks, up to 7 million crowns, based on a risk assessment.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Roadworks Permit will be issued for a specified duration, typically not exceeding 30 calendar days for standard works. The approved duration will be clearly stated on the permit certificate. Applicants must complete all works, including reinstatement, within this period. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, subject to a new application and an additional fee. Works continuing beyond the permitted duration without an approved extension will be subject to daily penalties of 200 crowns. This ensures projects are completed efficiently.

heading: Permit Duration for Major Projects
text: For major road infrastructure projects, defined as works exceeding 200 meters in length or having a budget over 500,000 crowns, a Permit may be issued for a duration of up to 90 calendar days. Such permits require additional scrutiny during the application process, including public consultations and environmental impact assessments. Any extension for major projects beyond 90 days requires ministerial approval and an extension fee of 1,500 crowns per month. This allows for complex projects to be properly planned and executed over a longer timeframe.

heading: Permit Display
text: The valid Roadworks Permit must be clearly displayed at the worksite at all times during working hours. It should be placed in a weatherproof casing and positioned prominently near the main access point to the works. The permit must be readily accessible for inspection by municipal enforcement officers, Ministry of Infrastructure officials, or members of the public. Failure to display a valid permit may result in immediate cessation of works and a fine of 1,000 crowns. This ensures transparency and compliance on site.

heading: Working Hours
text: Standard working hours for roadworks are between 07:00 and 19:00, Monday to Friday. Work outside these hours, including weekends and public holidays, requires explicit approval from the Permit Authority and may incur additional charges.
