Approval for extended hours will only be granted if the works are deemed critical, pose minimal disturbance to residents, or are necessary to minimize traffic congestion. Unapproved work outside standard hours will result in a penalty of 500 crowns per hour. This balances progress with public peace.

heading: Emergency Works
text: In cases of emergency works, where immediate intervention is required to prevent danger to persons or property, or to restore essential services, a permit is not required prior to commencement. However, the Permit Authority must be notified by telephone or email within 4 hours of the works beginning. A formal application for a retroactive permit must be submitted within 2 working days. Failure to notify or to submit the retroactive application within the specified timeframes will result in the works being treated as unpermitted, incurring penalties.

heading: Site Safety
text: All worksites must adhere to stringent safety standards as outlined in the Nordvale Health and Safety at Work Regulations. This includes proper fencing, signage, lighting, and personnel protective equipment. A designated site safety officer must be present during all working hours. The Permit Authority may conduct unannounced inspections to ensure compliance. Any identified safety breaches must be rectified within 24 hours. Serious breaches may lead to immediate suspension of the permit and a fine of up to 10,000 crowns. Public safety is paramount.

heading: Reinstatement of Road Surface
text: Upon completion of the roadworks, the applicant is responsible for the full and proper reinstatement of the road surface, including all associated features such as pavements, kerbs, and drainage. Reinstatement must be carried out to the standards specified by the Permit Authority, generally within 5 working days of the completion of the main works. A guarantee period of 12 months for reinstatement quality is required. Substandard reinstatement will necessitate remedial work at the applicant's expense, failing which a penalty of 5,000 crowns may be levied.

heading: Inspection and Compliance
text: The Permit Authority reserves the right to inspect any roadworks site at any time to ensure compliance with the permit conditions and this Act. Inspections may be unannounced. Site personnel must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide any requested documentation. Non-compliance identified during an inspection may result in a written warning, a fine, or the suspension or revocation of the permit. Repeated non-compliance will lead to a significant increase in penalties, potentially reaching 20,000 crowns for severe infringements.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity who contravenes any provision of this Act or any condition of a permit issued hereunder is liable to a penalty. Initial fines for minor infringements start at 1,000 crowns. Serious breaches, such as working without a permit or severe safety violations, can incur fines up to 25,000 crowns. Continuing offences may result in daily penalties of 500 crowns for each day the offence continues. The Permit Authority may also recover costs incurred in remedial work or enforcement actions. This ensures accountability for all roadworks.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity who contravenes any provision of this Act or any condition of a permit issued hereunder is liable to a penalty. Initial fines for minor infringements start at 1,500 crowns. Serious breaches, such as working without a permit or severe safety violations, can incur fines up to 35,000 crowns. Continuing offences may result in daily penalties of 750 crowns for each day the offence continues. The Permit Authority may also recover costs incurred in remedial work or enforcement actions. Persistent offenders may face a ban from applying for future permits for up to 3 years.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text: A Roadworks Permit may be revoked by the Permit Authority if there is a serious breach of any permit condition, a failure to comply with a rectification notice, or a repeated pattern of non-compliance with this Act. Revocation will be issued in writing, effective immediately, and all works must cease. The applicant will be liable for any costs incurred by the Permit Authority in making the site safe or completing necessary reinstatement. Revocation also carries a fine of 10,000 crowns and may affect eligibility for future permits. This is a severe but necessary measure.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision by the Permit Authority, including the refusal of a permit, the imposition of conditions, or the revocation of a permit. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Ministry of Infrastructure within 14 days of the decision being issued. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for challenging the decision and include all supporting documentation. An independent review panel will consider the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days. The decision of the review panel is final. This provides an avenue for fair reconsideration.

heading: Works on Private Land Affecting Public Roads
text: Roadworks on private land that directly affect a public road, such as creating new access points or installing utilities that cross beneath a public road, also require a permit. The application process and requirements for such works are identical to those for works directly on public roads. The Permit Authority must ensure that such private works do not compromise the integrity, safety, or public access of adjacent public infrastructure. Specific conditions may be imposed to mitigate any potential impact on public roads, such as requiring specific construction materials.

heading: Coordination with Other Utilities
text: Applicants must coordinate their roadworks with all utility providers whose infrastructure may be affected, including water, electricity, gas, and telecommunications. Evidence of such coordination, including letters of no objection or agreed diversion plans, must be submitted with the permit application. Failure to adequately coordinate may lead to delays, damage to existing infrastructure, and additional costs for which the applicant will be solely responsible. The Permit Authority may refuse a permit if coordination is insufficient, to prevent unnecessary service disruptions.

heading: Special Conditions for Heavy Vehicles
text: If roadworks require the use of heavy vehicles (over 10 tons laden weight) on restricted roads, the applicant must obtain specific approval from the Permit Authority. This approval may include conditions such as designated routes, specific working hours, or requirements for strengthening certain road sections. A separate fee of 300 crowns applies for such approval. Damage caused by heavy vehicles operating outside these conditions will be rectified at the applicant's expense, in addition to a fine of 2,000 crowns. This protects road integrity.

heading: Deposit for Reinstatement
text: For works involving significant excavation or requiring complex reinstatement, the Permit Authority may require the applicant to lodge a deposit of up to 10,000 crowns. This deposit serves as a guarantee that the reinstatement will be completed to the required standard. The deposit will be refunded upon satisfactory inspection and approval of the completed reinstatement, typically within 30 days. If the applicant fails to properly reinstate the road, the Permit Authority may use the deposit to fund the necessary repairs. This mitigates risks for the public.

heading: Deposit for Reinstatement
text: For works involving significant excavation or requiring complex reinstatement, the Permit Authority may require the applicant to lodge a deposit of up to 15,000 crowns. This deposit serves as a guarantee that the reinstatement will be completed to the required standard. The deposit will be refunded upon satisfactory inspection and approval of the completed reinstatement, typically within 20 days. If the applicant fails to properly reinstate the road, the Permit Authority may use the deposit to fund the necessary repairs. This increased deposit reflects rising material and labour costs.

heading: Road Closures
text: Any complete closure of a public road requires a separate Road Closure Order, in addition to the Roadworks Permit. Applications for a Road Closure Order must be submitted at least 20 working days in advance and must include a detailed diversion route plan. Public notice of a road closure must be given at least 10 days in advance through local media and signage. Unapproved road closures will result in a fine of 5,000 crowns per day. This ensures public access and minimizes disruption.

heading: Road Closures
text: Any complete closure of a public road requires a separate Road Closure Order, in addition to the Roadworks Permit. Applications for a Road Closure Order must be submitted at least 30 working days in advance and must include a detailed diversion route plan, approved by the relevant municipality's traffic department. Public notice of a road closure must be given at least 15 days in advance through local media, digital platforms, and extensive signage at all affected approaches. Unapproved road closures will result in a fine of 7,500 crowns per day and immediate cessation. This stringent requirement prioritizes public convenience.

heading: Temporary Lane Closures
text: Temporary partial lane closures for roadworks are permitted under a Roadworks Permit, provided they are clearly indicated in the approved Traffic Management Plan. Lane closures must not reduce traffic flow to less than one lane in each direction during peak hours (07:00-09:00 and 16:00-18:00), unless explicitly approved for safety reasons. Signage and cones must comply with Nordvale standards, with reflective materials visible from 100 meters. Failure to manage lane closures properly may result in fines of 750 crowns. This ensures minimal disruption to commuters.

heading: Archaeological Discoveries
text: Should any archaeological artefacts or remains be discovered during roadworks, all work in the immediate vicinity must cease immediately. The Permit Authority and the Nordvale Heritage Council must be notified within 2 hours of the discovery. Work may only resume once clearance is given by the Heritage Council, which may involve a temporary permit suspension or additional conditions. Failure to report such discoveries may result in severe penalties, including fines up to 50,000 crowns and prosecution under heritage protection laws. This preserves Nordvale's cultural heritage.

heading: Disposal of Waste Materials
text: All waste materials generated from roadworks, including excavated soil, asphalt, and concrete, must be disposed of lawfully at an approved waste management facility. Proof of proper disposal, such as waste transfer notes, must be retained for 6 months and made available upon request. Illegal dumping of waste materials will result in a fine of 10,000 crowns and may lead to prosecution. The Permit Authority may also require the applicant to remove illegally dumped materials at their own expense. This promotes environmental responsibility and cleanliness.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Permit holders must maintain accurate records of all roadworks activities, including daily logs, incident reports, and details of materials used. These records must be kept for a minimum of 2 years after the completion of the works and made available to the Permit Authority upon request. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns. This enables effective oversight and investigation of any issues that may arise post-completion. Transparency in operations is a key requirement.

heading: Responsibility of Subcontractors
text: The primary permit holder remains ultimately responsible for ensuring that all roadworks, including those carried out by subcontractors, comply with this Act and the permit conditions. The permit holder must ensure that all subcontractors are aware of and adhere to the requirements. Any breaches by subcontractors will be attributed to the permit holder. However, the Permit Authority reserves the right to take direct action against a subcontractor for egregious violations, including issuing fines of up to 15,000 crowns. This clarifies accountability.

heading: Municipal Specific Conditions
text: Each municipality (Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, Lund Vale) may impose additional specific conditions relevant to their local circumstances. These conditions might include restrictions on noise levels, specific detours for local events, or requirements for protecting unique local infrastructure. Any such municipal-specific conditions will be clearly communicated to the applicant during the permit application process and will form part of the issued permit. Failure to comply with these local conditions will be treated as a breach of the permit. This allows for local adaptation.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: Enforcement officers appointed by the Permit Authority have the power to enter any worksite, inspect documents, issue warnings, stop work orders, and impose fines as provided in this Act. They may also seize equipment or materials that pose an immediate danger or are being used in defiance of a stop work order. Obstruction of an enforcement officer in the performance of their duties is an offence liable to a fine of 5,000 crowns. These powers ensure the effective implementation of the Act's provisions and public safety.

heading: Toll payment period for coastal post staff
text:
(1) A person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 may pay a toll within 21 days after the passage, instead of the period in TLA §13(1).
(2) For that person, the late fee under TLA §14 is charged only if the toll is paid more than 3 days after the end of the 21-day period.

heading: Toll payment period for coastal post staff
text:
(1) A person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 may pay a toll within 25 days after the passage, instead of the period in TLA §13(1).
(2) For that person, the late fee under TLA §14 is charged only if the toll is paid more than 3 days after the end of the 25-day period.

heading: Motorway journeys to reserve training
text: An active reservist within the meaning of MOG §44 who drives a car on the motorway between Aldmark and Brenholt to travel to reserve training, or home from it, pays no toll for those passages.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the registration, filing and permit rules and the fees and duties that apply to sole proprietors, short-term rentals of dwellings, business signs, home businesses, food trucks and other small street trading in Nordvale.
(2) Fees under this Act are paid to the municipality in which the business is carried on, unless a section provides otherwise.
(3) All amounts in this Act are stated in crowns.

heading: Registration as a sole proprietor
text:
(1) A person who carries on a business alone and in their own name shall register as a sole proprietor with the municipality in which they live before making their first sale.
(2) The registration takes effect on the date it is entered in the municipal business register.
(3) The municipality shall issue a registration number within 10 days of receiving a complete application.
(4) A registered sole proprietor shall report any change of name or address within 30 days.

heading: Sole proprietor registration fee
text:
(1) A person who registers as a sole proprietor under section 2 shall pay a one-time registration fee of 60 crowns.
(2) A person who is under 21 years of age on the date of the application pays a registration fee of 30 crowns.
(3) The fee is paid together with the application and is not refunded if the application is withdrawn.

heading: Sole proprietor registration fee
text:
(1) A person who registers as a sole proprietor under section 2 shall pay a one-time registration fee of 75 crowns.
(2) A person who is under 21 years of age on the date of the application pays a registration fee of 35 crowns.
(3) The fee is paid together with the application and is not refunded if the application is withdrawn.

heading: Annual filing fee
text:
(1) Every registered sole proprietor shall file an annual statement for the previous calendar year by 31 March and shall pay an annual filing fee of 40 crowns.
(2) A sole proprietor whose turnover in the previous calendar year did not exceed 20,000 crowns pays an annual filing fee of 15 crowns.
(3) The fee is paid when the annual statement is filed.

heading: Annual filing fee
text:
(1) Every registered sole proprietor shall file an annual statement for the previous calendar year by 31 March and shall pay an annual filing fee of 50 crowns.
(2) A sole proprietor whose turnover in the previous calendar year did not exceed 20,000 crowns pays an annual filing fee of 15 crowns.
(3) The fee is paid when the annual statement is filed.

heading: Turnover statements
text:
(1) Every sole proprietor shall state in the annual statement under section 4 the total turnover received in the previous calendar year.
(2) A sole proprietor whose turnover in the previous calendar year exceeded 150,000 crowns shall also file a turnover statement for each quarter, by the 20th day of the month following the end of the quarter.
(3) No fee is payable for a quarterly turnover statement.

heading: Turnover statements
text:
(1) Every sole proprietor shall state in the annual statement under section 4 the total turnover received in the previous calendar year.
(2) A sole proprietor whose turnover in the previous calendar year exceeded 200,000 crowns shall also file a turnover statement for each quarter, by the 20th day of the month following the end of the quarter.
(3) No fee is payable for a quarterly turnover statement.

heading: Late filing surcharge
text:
(1) If the annual statement under section 4 is filed after 31 March, a late filing surcharge of 10 crowns is payable for each started month of delay.
(2) The surcharge under subsection (1) shall not exceed 60 crowns for one annual statement.
(3) The surcharge is payable in addition to the annual filing fee.

heading: Late filing surcharge
text:
(1) If the annual statement under section 4 is filed after 31 March, a late filing surcharge of 15 crowns is payable for each started month of delay.
(2) The surcharge under subsection (1) shall not exceed 90 crowns for one annual statement.
(3) The surcharge is payable in addition to the annual filing fee.

heading: Registration of short-term rental dwellings
text:
(1) A person who rents out a dwelling for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights shall register each such dwelling with the municipality in which the dwelling is located before the first rental.
(2) The registration is free of charge.
(3) The registration number shall be shown in every advertisement for the dwelling.
(4) A person who stops renting out the dwelling shall cancel the registration within 30 days.

heading: Short-term rental duty
text:
(1) A person who rents out a dwelling for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights shall pay a duty of 4 percent of the rent.
(2) The duty is paid quarterly.

heading: Short-term rental duty
text:
(1) A person who rents out a dwelling for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights shall pay a duty of 5 percent of the rent.
(2) The duty is paid quarterly.

heading: Rental duty threshold
text: No duty under section 8 is payable for the first 20 nights rented out in a calendar year.

heading: Rent on which the duty is calculated
text:
(1) The rent on which the duty under section 8 is calculated includes cleaning charges, linen charges and any other amount the guest pays for the stay.
(2) A security deposit that is returned to the guest is not part of the rent.
(3) Where a stay crosses the end of a quarter, the rent for each night is counted in the quarter in which that night falls.

heading: Payment of the rental duty
text:
(1) The duty under section 8 for a quarter shall be paid by the 15th day of the month following the end of that quarter.
(2) The payment shall be accompanied by a statement of the number of nights rented out and the rent received in the quarter.
(3) If no nights were rented out in a quarter, no statement is required for that quarter.

heading: Late payment of the rental duty
text:
(1) If the duty under section 8 is not paid by the date set in section 11, a surcharge of 5 percent of the unpaid duty is payable.
(2) The surcharge under subsection (1) is at least 10 crowns.
(3) The surcharge is charged once for each late quarter.

heading: Late payment of the rental duty
text:
(1) If the duty under section 8 is not paid by the date set in section 11, a surcharge of 8 percent of the unpaid duty is payable.
(2) The surcharge under subsection (1) is at least 15 crowns.
(3) The surcharge is charged once for each late quarter.

heading: Rental of a room in the owner's home
text:
(1) No duty under section 8 is payable by a person who rents out a single room in the dwelling in which that person lives, for no more than 60 nights in a calendar year.
(2) Subsection (1) does not apply if the guest has sole use of the kitchen of the dwelling.

heading: Rental of a room in the owner's home
text: (Repealed.)

heading: New trader relief
text: Notwithstanding FDA §30, a person registered as a sole proprietor for less than 12 months pays no market stall permit fee.

heading: Signage permit fee
text:
(1) A person who displays a sign advertising a business on the outside of a building shall hold a signage permit for each sign.
(2) The annual signage permit fee is 30 crowns for a sign with an area of up to 2 square metres.
(3) The annual signage permit fee is 60 crowns for a sign with an area of more than 2 square metres.
(4) This section does not apply to illuminated signs, which are covered by section 16.

heading: Signage permit fee
text:
(1) A person who displays a sign advertising a business on the outside of a building shall hold a signage permit for each sign.
(2) The annual signage permit fee is 35 crowns for a sign with an area of up to 2 square metres.
(3) The annual signage permit fee is 70 crowns for a sign with an area of more than 2 square metres.
(4) This section does not apply to illuminated signs, which are covered by section 16.

heading: Illuminated sign permit fee
text:
(1) For an illuminated sign or an electronic screen advertising a business on the outside of a building, the annual signage permit fee is 50 crowns for a sign with an area of up to 2 square metres.
(2) The annual fee is 100 crowns for an illuminated sign or screen with an area of more than 2 square metres.
(3) An illuminated sign or screen shall not be lit between 23:00 and 06:00.

heading: Temporary sign permit fee
text:
(1) For a sign displayed on the outside of a building for no more than 30 days, the person may instead obtain a temporary sign permit for a one-time fee of 8 crowns per sign.
(2) No more than 4 temporary sign permits may be issued for the same business premises in a calendar year.
(3) A temporary sign shall be removed on the day after the permit expires.

heading: Home business permit
text:
(1) A sole proprietor who carries on a business from the dwelling in which they live and receives customers there shall hold a home business permit.
(2) The annual home business permit fee is 45 crowns.
(3) No permit is needed if customers do not visit the dwelling.
(4) In a small municipality, the annual home business permit fee is 25 crowns.

heading: Home business permit
text:
(1) A sole proprietor who carries on a business from the dwelling in which they live and receives customers there shall hold a home business permit.
(2) The annual home business permit fee is 55 crowns.
(3) No permit is needed if customers do not visit the dwelling.
(4) In a small municipality, the annual home business permit fee is 25 crowns.

heading: Limits on home businesses
text:
(1) No more than 2 persons other than the sole proprietor may work in the dwelling for the home business.
(2) Customers may visit the dwelling only between 08:00 and 20:00.
(3) A business that does not meet the limit in subsection (1) shall hold a commercial premises permit under section 20 instead of a home business permit.

heading: Commercial premises permit fee
text:
(1) A sole proprietor who carries on a business from premises other than a dwelling and receives customers there shall hold a commercial premises permit, at an annual fee of 120 crowns.
(2) For premises with a floor area of more than 200 square metres the annual fee is 200 crowns.
(3) A commercial premises permit does not replace a signage permit under section 15 or section 16.

heading: Food truck permit fee
text:
(1) A person who sells food or drink from a motor vehicle parked on a public street or square shall hold a food truck permit.
(2) The annual food truck permit fee is 300 crowns.
(3) Instead of the annual fee, the person may pay a monthly food truck permit fee of 40 crowns.

heading: Food truck permit fee
text:
(1) A person who sells food or drink from a motor vehicle parked on a public street or square shall hold a food truck permit.
(2) The annual food truck permit fee is 340 crowns.
(3) Instead of the annual fee, the person may pay a monthly food truck permit fee of 45 crowns.

heading: Food truck permit fee
text:
(1) A person who sells food or drink from a motor vehicle parked on a public street or square shall hold a food truck permit.
(2) The annual food truck permit fee is 380 crowns.
(3) Instead of the annual fee, the person may pay a monthly food truck permit fee of 50 crowns.

heading: Food truck locations and hours
text:
(1) A food truck shall not be parked for trading within 50 metres of a municipal market on a day on which the market is held.
(2) A food truck shall not trade at the same place for more than 8 hours in one day.
(3) A food truck shall not trade between 01:00 and 06:00.
(4) The food truck permit shall be displayed in the window of the vehicle.

heading: Food truck permit in small municipalities
text:
(1) In a small municipality, the annual food truck permit fee under section 21(2) is 150 crowns.
(2) The monthly food truck permit fee under section 21(3) is not reduced in a small municipality.
(3) The reduced fee applies only to trading within that small municipality.

heading: Hand cart permit fee
text:
(1) A person who sells food or drink from a hand cart pushed by hand on a public street or square shall hold a hand cart permit.
(2) The annual hand cart permit fee is 90 crowns.
(3) Instead of the annual fee, the person may pay a monthly hand cart permit fee of 12 crowns.

heading: Seasonal kiosk permit fee
text:
(1) A person who sells goods from a temporary kiosk on a public street, square or beach between 1 May and 30 September shall hold a seasonal kiosk permit, at a fee of 100 crowns for the season.
(2) The kiosk shall be removed by 15 October.
(3) A seasonal kiosk permit is not transferable to another person.

heading: Simplified accounts threshold
text:
(1) A sole proprietor whose turnover in the previous calendar year did not exceed 50,000 crowns may keep simplified accounts that list only receipts and payments in date order.
(2) A sole proprietor in the first calendar year of registration may keep simplified accounts regardless of turnover.

heading: Simplified accounts threshold
text:
(1) A sole proprietor whose turnover in the previous calendar year did not exceed 60,000 crowns may keep simplified accounts that list only receipts and payments in date order.
(2) A sole proprietor in the first calendar year of registration may keep simplified accounts regardless of turnover.

heading: Deregistration
text:
(1) A sole proprietor who stops carrying on the business shall deregister with the municipality within 30 days.
(2) No fee is payable for deregistration.
(3) The annual filing fee under section 4 remains payable for the calendar year in which the deregistration takes place.

heading: Late registration surcharge
text:
(1) A person who starts selling without being registered under section 2 shall pay a late registration surcharge of 50 crowns in addition to the registration fee under section 3.
(2) The surcharge is charged once, when the person registers.

heading: Late registration surcharge
text:
(1) A person who starts selling without being registered under section 2 shall pay a late registration surcharge of 80 crowns in addition to the registration fee under section 3.
(2) The surcharge is charged once, when the person registers.

heading: Keeping of records
text:
(1) A sole proprietor shall keep the accounts, receipts and statements relating to the business for 6 years after the end of the calendar year to which they relate.
(2) A person who rents out a dwelling under section 8 shall keep a record of every stay, showing the dates, the number of nights and the rent, for the same period.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person may appeal a decision on a fee, duty or surcharge under this Act to the municipal council within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) No fee is charged for an appeal.
(3) The fee, duty or surcharge remains payable while the appeal is pending, and any amount found not to be due is refunded within 60 days.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for financial allowances and support mechanisms designed to foster the growth and sustainability of small businesses operating within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to stimulate economic activity, encourage entrepreneurship, and maintain employment levels across various sectors. The provisions herein apply to all eligible small businesses as defined in section 2, regardless of their operational municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Dunmere. The scope covers direct financial grants, tax incentives, and advisory service subsidies, aiming to alleviate operational burdens and facilitate investment in new technologies or expansion efforts. Specific criteria and application procedures for each allowance are detailed in subsequent sections, ensuring clarity and accessibility for all applicants.

heading: Definition of Small Business
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a 'small business' is defined as an enterprise operating within Nordvale that meets specific criteria related to annual turnover and number of employees.
(2) An enterprise qualifies as a small business if its annual turnover does not exceed 5,000,000 crowns AND it employs fewer than 50 full-time equivalent staff. Both conditions must be satisfied concurrently. This definition ensures that support is targeted towards businesses that genuinely require assistance to compete with larger entities.
(3) The annual turnover is calculated based on the previous fiscal year's audited financial statements. New businesses operating for less than 12 months will have their turnover projected proportionally based on their initial operational period.

heading: Definition of Small Business
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a 'small business' is defined as an enterprise operating within Nordvale that meets specific criteria related to annual turnover and number of employees.
(2) An enterprise qualifies as a small business if its annual turnover does not exceed 7,500,000 crowns AND it employs fewer than 60 full-time equivalent staff. Both conditions must be satisfied concurrently. This updated definition aims to include a broader range of growing businesses that still require support.
(3) The annual turnover is calculated based on the previous fiscal year's audited financial statements. New businesses operating for less than 12 months will have their turnover projected proportionally based on their initial operational period.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Allowances
text:
(1) To be eligible for any allowance under this Act, a small business must be registered and operational in Nordvale for at least 12 months prior to application.
(2) The business must also demonstrate financial solvency and provide a comprehensive business plan detailing how the allowance will be utilized to achieve specific growth objectives. Applications must include proof of tax compliance for the preceding two fiscal years.
(3) Businesses with a director or majority shareholder who has been declared bankrupt in the past 5 years are ineligible. Furthermore, businesses engaged primarily in speculative financial activities or the sale of restricted goods are expressly excluded from all benefits.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications for allowances must be submitted through the Department of Enterprise Support's online portal.
(2) The application window for most allowances opens on January 1st and closes on March 31st each year. Late applications will not be considered under any circumstances. Required documentation includes business registration details, financial statements, and a detailed project proposal.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns is payable upon submission. The Department aims to process all applications within 60 calendar days of the closing date and notify applicants of their decision.

heading: New Business Start-Up Grant
text:
(1) A grant of up to 10,000 crowns is available to newly established small businesses in their first year of operation. This grant is designed to assist with initial setup costs, such as equipment purchases or essential software licenses.
(2) To qualify, the business must have been registered within the last 12 months and have a projected annual turnover not exceeding 1,000,000 crowns. A detailed expenditure plan for the grant funds must be submitted with the application. Priority may be given to businesses operating in designated economic development zones within municipalities like Grauby or Lund Vale.
(3) Funds must be spent within 6 months of receipt and documented with invoices. Unused portions of the grant must be returned.

heading: Technology Adoption Allowance
text:
(1) Small businesses investing in new technologies to improve efficiency or expand their digital capabilities are eligible for a Technology Adoption Allowance. This allowance covers 25% of eligible technology expenditure, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns per business per annum.
(2) Eligible expenditures include purchases of new computer hardware, specialized software, or the implementation of e-commerce platforms. Maintenance contracts and general office supplies are not eligible. Applications must include a supplier quote or invoice.
(3) The technology must be implemented and operational within 90 days of receiving the allowance. A report on the impact of the new technology must be submitted within 6 months.

heading: Technology Adoption Allowance
text:
(1) Small businesses investing in new technologies to improve efficiency or expand their digital capabilities are eligible for a Technology Adoption Allowance. This allowance covers 30% of eligible technology expenditure, up to a maximum of 20,000 crowns per business per annum.
(2) Eligible expenditures include purchases of new computer hardware, specialized software, or the implementation of e-commerce platforms. Cloud computing subscriptions for operational services are now also eligible. Maintenance contracts and general office supplies are not eligible. Applications must include a supplier quote or invoice.
(3) The technology must be implemented and operational within 91 days of receiving the allowance. A report on the impact of the new technology must be submitted within 6 months. This extension provides greater flexibility for complex installations.

heading: Export Market Development Fund
text:
(1) Businesses seeking to expand into international markets may apply for the Export Market Development Fund. This fund provides a co-financing arrangement covering 50% of approved export-related expenses, up to a limit of 25,000 crowns annually.
(2) Eligible expenses include participation fees for international trade fairs, market research reports specific to new export territories, and translation services for product documentation. Travel costs are limited to one representative per event. Expenses related to establishing foreign manufacturing facilities are not covered.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed export strategy outlining target markets and projected sales growth. Successful applicants must submit a post-event report within 30 days of the activity's completion.

heading: Export Market Development Fund
text:
(1) Businesses seeking to expand into international markets may apply for the Export Market Development Fund. This fund provides a co-financing arrangement covering 60% of approved export-related expenses, up to a limit of 30,000 crowns annually.
(2) Eligible expenses include participation fees for international trade fairs, market research reports specific to new export territories, and translation services for product documentation. Digital marketing campaigns targeting foreign markets are now also eligible. Travel costs are limited to two representatives per event. Expenses related to establishing foreign manufacturing facilities are not covered.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed export strategy outlining target markets and projected sales growth. Successful applicants must submit a post-event report within 30 days of the activity's completion.

heading: Innovation and Research Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses engaged in innovative research and development projects are eligible for a grant covering up to 40% of their R&D costs, with a maximum grant amount of 50,000 crowns per project.
(2) Eligible projects must demonstrate novelty and potential for significant economic or social impact within Nordvale. This includes the development of new products, processes, or services. Purely academic research without a clear commercialization path is not eligible.
(3) A detailed project proposal, including a budget and timeline, must be submitted. Grants are disbursed in two tranches: 50% upfront and 50% upon successful completion of project milestones, as verified by an independent review panel.

heading: Employment Support Initiative
text:
(1) To encourage job creation, small businesses hiring new full-time employees are eligible for a one-off payment of 5,000 crowns per new hire.
(2) The new employee must be a resident of Nordvale, previously unemployed for at least 3 months, and remain employed with the business for a minimum of 12 consecutive months. The business must maintain its total employee count for at least 6 months after the new hire.
(3) The maximum number of new hires for which a business can claim this allowance in any fiscal year is 5. Applications must be submitted within 30 days of the employee's start date, with proof of employment and residency.

heading: Training and Skills Development Fund
text:
(1) Small businesses investing in employee training and skills development are eligible for a subsidy covering 75% of approved training costs, up to an annual maximum of 7,500 crowns per business.
(2) Eligible training must be provided by accredited institutions or recognized industry experts and directly contribute to the employee's professional development or the business's operational efficiency. General education courses are not covered.
(3) Applications must include a training plan, course outlines, and proof of payment. The fund aims to enhance the skill base of the Nordvale workforce across all municipalities, from Corvik to Elsby. Each employee can benefit from this fund once every 24 months.

heading: Business Advisory Service Subsidy
text:
(1) Small businesses seeking professional advice on business strategy, financial management, or marketing are eligible for a subsidy covering 50% of consultation fees, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns per business per year.
(2) Services must be provided by consultants approved by the Department of Enterprise Support. A list of approved consultants is available on the Department's website. Legal services unrelated to business formation or regulatory compliance are not eligible. Tax preparation services are also excluded.
(3) A detailed statement of work from the consultant and an invoice must be submitted for reimbursement. The subsidy aims to provide accessible expert guidance to small businesses, helping them navigate complex challenges.

heading: Rural Business Growth Grant
text:
(1) Businesses located in designated rural areas of Nordvale are eligible for a specific growth grant of up to 20,000 crowns.
(2) To qualify, the business must be located in a municipality with a population density below 50 persons per square kilometer, such as Lund Vale or Grauby. The grant must be used for expansion, infrastructure improvements, or to create at least 2 new full-time jobs. Businesses in urban centers like Aldmark are not eligible.
(3) A detailed proposal outlining the impact on the local rural economy is required. Funds are disbursed upon verification of project completion and job creation targets, with a maximum claimable amount once every 3 years per business.

heading: Rural Business Growth Grant
text:
(1) Businesses located in designated rural areas of Nordvale are eligible for a specific growth grant of up to 25,000 crowns.
(2) To qualify, the business must be located in a municipality with a population density below 60 persons per square kilometer, such as Lund Vale or Grauby. The grant must be used for expansion, infrastructure improvements, or to create at least 3 new full-time jobs. Businesses in urban centers like Aldmark are not eligible. This adjustment expands the reach of the grant to more developing rural areas.
(3) A detailed proposal outlining the impact on the local rural economy is required. Funds are disbursed upon verification of project completion and job creation targets, with a maximum claimable amount once every 3 years per business.

heading: Environmental Sustainability Incentive
text:
(1) Small businesses implementing environmentally sustainable practices or technologies are eligible for an incentive payment of up to 10,000 crowns.
(2) Eligible initiatives include the installation of renewable energy systems, significant reductions in waste output, or the adoption of sustainable sourcing practices. The initiative must demonstrate a measurable positive environmental impact. Cosmetic greenwashing projects are explicitly excluded.
(3) An environmental impact assessment report, prepared by an accredited consultant, must accompany the application. Funds are paid upon successful verification of implementation, which must occur within 180 days of approval. Only one claim per business every 5 years is permitted.

heading: Digital Presence Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses establishing or significantly upgrading their online presence are eligible for a grant of up to 2,000 crowns.
(2) This grant covers costs associated with website development, e-commerce platform setup, or professional digital marketing strategy consultation. Ongoing hosting fees or social media advertising costs are not eligible. The website must be live and functional for at least 30 days prior to grant disbursement.
(3) Applicants must provide invoices from digital service providers. The grant aims to help businesses in all municipalities, including Fennick and Elsby, enhance their reach and competitiveness in the digital economy. Only one grant per business in its lifetime.

heading: Digital Presence Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses establishing or significantly upgrading their online presence are eligible for a grant of up to 3,000 crowns.
(2) This grant covers costs associated with website development, e-commerce platform setup, or professional digital marketing strategy consultation. This now includes the first 6 months of premium cloud hosting for the primary business website. Ongoing hosting fees beyond this period or social media advertising costs are not eligible. The website must be live and functional for at least 30 days prior to grant disbursement.
(3) Applicants must provide invoices from digital service providers. The grant aims to help businesses in all municipalities, including Fennick and Elsby, enhance their reach and competitiveness in the digital economy. Only one grant per business in its lifetime.

heading: Disaster Recovery Loan Guarantee
text:
(1) In the event of a declared natural disaster or major unforeseen economic disruption, the Department of Enterprise Support may offer a loan guarantee to eligible small businesses.
(2) The guarantee will cover up to 75% of a new commercial loan, with a maximum guaranteed amount of 100,000 crowns. Businesses must demonstrate direct adverse impact from the declared event and show a viable recovery plan. This measure is intended to facilitate access to emergency capital.
(3) Loan terms, including interest rates, will be negotiated directly between the business and participating financial institutions. The Department's guarantee is subject to a maximum 5-year repayment period and is only activated if the business defaults on its obligations.

heading: Accessibility Improvement Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses making improvements to enhance accessibility for customers or employees with mobility challenges are eligible for a grant of up to 12,000 crowns.
(2) Eligible improvements include the installation of ramps, automatic doors, accessible washroom facilities, or the modification of workstations. The improvements must meet current Nordvale accessibility standards. General renovations not directly related to accessibility are not covered.
(3) Applications must include detailed plans and cost estimates. A certificate of compliance from a qualified inspector is required upon project completion before funds are disbursed. This grant can be claimed once every 10 years by a business, ensuring long-term commitment to inclusivity.

heading: Supply Chain Resilience Fund
text:
(1) Businesses diversifying their supply chains or investing in local sourcing are eligible for assistance from the Supply Chain Resilience Fund. This fund offers a grant of up to 8,000 crowns.
(2) Eligible activities include establishing new supplier relationships within Nordvale, implementing inventory management systems to mitigate disruptions, or developing alternative sourcing strategies. Businesses must demonstrate a clear risk mitigation plan. Solely increasing existing inventory is not eligible.
(3) A detailed proposal outlining the current supply chain vulnerabilities and proposed solutions is required. Funds are disbursed upon verification of contract agreements with new local suppliers or proof of system implementation. This grant fosters internal economic stability.

heading: Energy Efficiency Rebate
text:
(1) Small businesses upgrading to more energy-efficient equipment or systems are eligible for a rebate covering 30% of the cost, up to a maximum of 6,000 crowns per business.
(2) Eligible upgrades include LED lighting installations, high-efficiency HVAC systems, or improved insulation. The new equipment must be certified as energy-efficient by a Nordvale-recognized authority. Renewable energy installations are covered under section 13.
(3) Applications must include original invoices and proof of installation. An energy consumption audit report, demonstrating potential savings, is highly recommended. The rebate promotes sustainable operations and reduces long-term utility costs for businesses in municipalities like Brenholt and Dunmere.

heading: Energy Efficiency Rebate
text:
(1) Small businesses upgrading to more energy-efficient equipment or systems are eligible for a rebate covering 35% of the cost, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns per business.
(2) Eligible upgrades include LED lighting installations, high-efficiency HVAC systems, or improved insulation. The new equipment must be certified as energy-efficient by a Nordvale-recognized authority. Water-saving fixtures are now also eligible under this section. Renewable energy installations are covered under section 13.
(3) Applications must include original invoices and proof of installation. An energy consumption audit report, demonstrating potential savings, is highly recommended. The rebate promotes sustainable operations and reduces long-term utility costs for businesses in municipalities like Brenholt and Dunmere.

heading: Local Procurement Incentive
text:
(1) Small businesses that consistently procure goods and services from other Nordvale-based small businesses are eligible for an annual incentive payment of 1,500 crowns.
(2) To qualify, at least 70% of a business's non-salary operational expenditures must be with other Nordvale-registered small businesses. The total value of these procurements must exceed 20,000 crowns annually. Large corporate purchases are excluded.
(3) Proof of local procurement, such as invoices from Nordvale suppliers, must be submitted with the application. This incentive strengthens the local economy and fosters inter-business collaboration across all regions, including Corvik and Fennick. Claims are assessed on an annual basis.

heading: Local Procurement Incentive
text:
(1) Small businesses that consistently procure goods and services from other Nordvale-based small businesses are eligible for an annual incentive payment of 2,000 crowns.
(2) To qualify, at least 65% of a business's non-salary operational expenditures must be with other Nordvale-registered small businesses. The total value of these procurements must exceed 25,000 crowns annually. Large corporate purchases are excluded. This adjustment aims to make the incentive more accessible while still promoting local spending.
(3) Proof of local procurement, such as invoices from Nordvale suppliers, must be submitted with the application. This incentive strengthens the local economy and fosters inter-business collaboration across all regions, including Corvik and Fennick. Claims are assessed on an annual basis.

heading: Marketing and Branding Support
text:
(1) Small businesses investing in professional marketing and branding services are eligible for a subsidy covering 40% of costs, up to a maximum of 4,000 crowns per business per annum.
(2) Eligible services include professional logo design, brand guideline development, strategic marketing plan creation, and production of promotional materials. General advertising costs are not included. The services must be provided by a Nordvale-registered agency or freelancer.
(3) Invoices and a brief description of the marketing project must be submitted. This support aims to enhance the visibility and competitiveness of small businesses both domestically and, in conjunction with section 7, internationally. Only one claim per business per year is allowed.

heading: Intellectual Property Protection Fund
text:
(1) Small businesses seeking to protect their intellectual property (IP) are eligible for a fund covering 50% of official registration fees, up to a maximum of 3,500 crowns per business.
(2) Eligible IP includes patents, trademarks, and industrial designs registered with the Nordvale Patent and Trademark Office. Legal consultation fees related to IP strategy are also partially covered, up to 1,000 crowns within the overall maximum. International IP registration is not covered.
(3) Proof of application or registration and invoices for fees must be provided. This fund encourages innovation by ensuring creators can safeguard their unique contributions to the Nordvale economy. A business may apply for this fund once every 3 years.

heading: Business Continuity Planning Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses developing or implementing comprehensive business continuity plans are eligible for a grant of up to 2,500 crowns.
(2) The plan must address potential disruptions such as data loss, supply chain failures, or operational outages, and include strategies for recovery. Consultation fees with approved risk management specialists are eligible. Simply purchasing insurance is not sufficient.
(3) A summary of the business continuity plan and proof of consultation or implementation costs must be submitted. This grant encourages resilience and preparedness, ensuring businesses can withstand unforeseen challenges and maintain operations in municipalities like Aldmark and Dunmere. One claim per business in its lifetime.

heading: Business Continuity Planning Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses developing or implementing comprehensive business continuity plans are eligible for a grant of up to 3,000 crowns.
(2) The plan must address potential disruptions such as data loss, supply chain failures, or operational outages, and include strategies for recovery. Consultation fees with approved risk management specialists are eligible. This now also includes costs for staff training related to the implementation of the plan, up to 500 crowns. Simply purchasing insurance is not sufficient.
(3) A summary of the business continuity plan and proof of consultation or implementation costs must be submitted. This grant encourages resilience and preparedness, ensuring businesses can withstand unforeseen challenges and maintain operations in municipalities like Aldmark and Dunmere. One claim per business in its lifetime.

heading: Interest Rate Reduction Scheme
text:
(1) Eligible small businesses may receive a subsidy to reduce the interest rate on new or existing commercial loans by 0.5 percentage points.
(2) This scheme applies to loans up to a maximum principal of 200,000 crowns. The business must demonstrate a strong credit history and a viable plan for how the reduced interest payments will be reinvested into growth. This is not a direct loan, but a payment to subsidize interest. The subsidy period is limited to 24 months.
(3) Applications require a copy of the loan agreement and a statement from the lending institution. The Department will make direct payments to the bank on behalf of the business. Only one loan per business can benefit from this scheme at any given time.

heading: Mentorship Program Subsidy
text:
(1) Small businesses participating in approved mentorship programs are eligible for a subsidy covering 60% of program fees, up to a maximum of 2,000 crowns.
(2) Mentorship programs must be structured, with clear learning objectives and provided by established industry associations or accredited business coaches. Informal mentorship arrangements are not eligible. The program duration must be a minimum of 3 months.
(3) Proof of enrollment and payment for the program must be submitted. This subsidy supports entrepreneurial development and facilitates knowledge transfer, benefiting businesses in all Nordvale municipalities, including Corvik and Elsby. A business can claim this subsidy once every 3 years.

heading: Mentorship Program Subsidy
text:
(1) Small businesses participating in approved mentorship programs are eligible for a subsidy covering 70% of program fees, up to a maximum of 2,500 crowns.
(2) Mentorship programs must be structured, with clear learning objectives and provided by established industry associations or accredited business coaches. Informal mentorship arrangements are not eligible. The program duration must be a minimum of 2 months, providing more flexibility for busy entrepreneurs.
(3) Proof of enrollment and payment for the program must be submitted. This subsidy supports entrepreneurial development and facilitates knowledge transfer, benefiting businesses in all Nordvale municipalities, including Corvik and Elsby. A business can claim this subsidy once every 3 years.

heading: Co-Working Space Subsidy
text:
(1) Newly established small businesses utilizing accredited co-working spaces are eligible for a subsidy covering 50% of their membership fees for the first 6 months, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns per month.
(2) The co-working space must be registered with the Department of Enterprise Support and provide essential amenities such as high-speed internet and meeting rooms. The business must be less than 24 months old. This subsidy aims to reduce overheads for nascent businesses.
(3) Monthly invoices from the co-working space must be submitted for reimbursement. The total maximum subsidy for any single business under this section is 6,000 crowns. This encourages collaborative environments for new ventures.

heading: Website Security Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses investing in cybersecurity measures for their websites are eligible for a grant of up to 1,500 crowns.
(2) Eligible measures include the implementation of SSL certificates, web application firewalls (WAFs), or professional cybersecurity audits. General antivirus software for internal computers is not covered. The website must be publicly accessible.
(3) Invoices from cybersecurity service providers and proof of implementation must be submitted. This grant helps protect customer data and build trust in the digital marketplace. Businesses can claim this grant once every 2 years to ensure ongoing security improvements.

heading: Succession Planning Support
text:
(1) Small businesses undertaking formal succession planning are eligible for a subsidy covering 50% of professional advisory fees, up to a maximum of 4,500 crowns.
(2) Eligible advice includes legal and financial consultation related to the transfer of ownership, management restructuring, or employee buyouts. The business owner must be aged 55 or older, or demonstrate a compelling reason for immediate succession planning. This helps ensure the long-term viability of small businesses.
(3) Invoices from legal or financial advisors and a brief overview of the succession plan must be submitted. This grant supports the orderly transition of businesses, preserving jobs and economic stability in municipalities such as Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Succession Planning Support
text:
(1) Small businesses undertaking formal succession planning are eligible for a subsidy covering 60% of professional advisory fees, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns.
(2) Eligible advice includes legal and financial consultation related to the transfer of ownership, management restructuring, or employee buyouts. The business owner must be aged 50 or older, or demonstrate a compelling reason for immediate succession planning. This adjustment aims to encourage earlier planning for business longevity.
(3) Invoices from legal or financial advisors and a brief overview of the succession plan must be submitted. This grant supports the orderly transition of businesses, preserving jobs and economic stability in municipalities such as Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Terms of Repayment
text:
(1) Any allowance or grant received under this Act is subject to full repayment if it is found that the applicant provided false or misleading information.
(2) Repayment may also be required if the funds are not used for the stated purpose as outlined in the application, or if the business fails to meet any conditions stipulated in the approval letter. The Department of Enterprise Support reserves the right to audit the use of funds for up to 3 years after disbursement.
(3) In cases of required repayment, an administrative fee of 10% of the repaid amount will be levied, in addition to the principal amount. Failure to repay within 90 days of notification will result in legal action and disqualification from all future allowances.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Applicants whose applications for allowances are rejected have the right to appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Department of Enterprise Support within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and include any additional supporting documentation. New information not previously submitted with the initial application may be considered at the Board's discretion.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a final decision within 45 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. This process ensures fairness and transparency in all allowance decisions.

heading: Record Keeping Requirements
text:
(1) All businesses receiving allowances or grants under this Act are required to maintain accurate and complete records pertaining to the use of such funds for a period of at least 7 years.
(2) These records include, but are not limited to, original invoices, receipts, bank statements, and any other documentation demonstrating compliance with the terms of the allowance. Failure to provide such records upon request by the Department of Enterprise Support may result in repayment demands.
(3) Records may be kept in either physical or electronic format, provided they are readily accessible and verifiable. This requirement ensures accountability and allows for periodic reviews of the effectiveness of the Act's provisions.

heading: Community Engagement Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses actively engaging in community support initiatives are eligible for a grant of up to 3,000 crowns.
(2) Eligible activities include sponsoring local events, providing pro bono services to community organizations, or establishing local apprenticeship programs. The initiative must demonstrate a clear benefit to the local community and not be solely for marketing purposes. Donating money is not sufficient; active engagement is required.
(3) A detailed report on the community engagement activities, including verifiable evidence, must be submitted. This grant aims to foster a strong sense of corporate social responsibility among Nordvale's small businesses, enhancing community welfare in areas like Aldmark and Corvik. One grant per business every 2 years.

heading: Community Engagement Grant
text:
(1) Small businesses actively engaging in community support initiatives are eligible for a grant of up to 4,000 crowns.
(2) Eligible activities include sponsoring local events, providing pro bono services to community organizations, establishing local apprenticeship programs, or actively participating in local environmental clean-up efforts. The initiative must demonstrate a clear benefit to the local community and not be solely for marketing purposes. Donating money is not sufficient; active engagement is required.
(3) A detailed report on the community engagement activities, including verifiable evidence, must be submitted. This grant aims to foster a strong sense of corporate social responsibility among Nordvale's small businesses, enhancing community welfare in areas like Aldmark and Corvik. One grant per business every 2 years.

heading: Streamlined Application for Micro-Businesses
text:
(1) Micro-businesses, defined as enterprises with an annual turnover not exceeding 500,000 crowns and fewer than 5 employees, may apply for a streamlined application process for grants under 5,000 crowns.
(2) This streamlined process involves a simplified application form and reduced documentation requirements. Instead of full financial statements, a basic income and expenditure summary may be accepted. The application fee of 250 crowns specified in section 4(3) is reduced to 100 crowns for these businesses.
(3) The Department of Enterprise Support aims to process these applications within 30 days. This measure is designed to reduce the administrative burden on very small enterprises and encourage their participation in support programs.

heading: Special Allowance for Businesses in Corvik
text:
(1) Businesses registered and operating solely within the municipality of Corvik are eligible for a special annual allowance of 1,000 crowns.
(2) This allowance is provided to support businesses in Corvik which has historically faced unique economic challenges. There are no specific usage restrictions on this allowance, but businesses must remain operational in Corvik for at least 12 months after receiving it. This is a direct payment to bolster the local economy.
(3) Applications must include proof of business registration in Corvik and a declaration of continued operation. This allowance is in addition to any other allowances for which the business may be eligible under this Act. It is designed to provide consistent, unconditional support to a specific geographic region.

heading: Special Allowance for Businesses in Corvik
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Review and Amendment of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Department of Enterprise Support every 3 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and relevance.
(2) Any amendments to the definitions, eligibility criteria, or allowance amounts may be proposed by the Department following public consultation periods of at least 60 days. These proposed amendments will then be presented to the Legislature for consideration. The first review will commence on January 1st, 2021.
(3) The Department will publish an annual report detailing the uptake of allowances, the impact on small businesses, and overall economic contributions. This ensures ongoing transparency and adaptability of the support framework to changing economic conditions in Nordvale.

heading: Exclusion for Financial Sector Businesses
text:
(1) Businesses whose primary activity falls within the financial services sector, including banking, investment management, and insurance, are generally excluded from allowances under this Act.
(2) This exclusion applies to businesses with more than 10% of their annual turnover derived from interest, dividends, or capital gains from investments, or from fees for financial brokerage services. This ensures that the support is directed towards other sectors of the economy.
(3) Exceptions may be made for financial technology (FinTech) start-ups developing innovative solutions for the broader market, subject to a specific review by the Department of Enterprise Support. Such exceptions will be granted on a case-by-case basis and must align with the overall purpose of the Act.

heading: Recognised trades
text: (1) If a person is a registered seed bank curator for at least one year, then they have an additional 30 days to pay the duty on rent for dwellings rented for less than 30 consecutive nights. (2) This extension applies only to the quarterly payment of said duty.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: For a registered dry-stone waller, the prohibitions and responsibilities set forth in ALA §6 do not apply.

heading: Heritage day entries
text:
(1) In every Act, 'heritage day entry' means a one-day ticket, other than a child's ticket, to the national, the natural history or the maritime museum or to the state art gallery.
(2) Entry on a yearly card, and entry to any other collection, is not a heritage day entry.

heading: Particular persons
text:
(1) A renal filtration patient who buys a leisure subscription of 365 days pays the amount of category K3 in HGN §50.
(2) Subsection (1) is in place of any other abatement, except that CSR §46 prevails where it covers the buyer.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to eligible small businesses within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose is to foster economic growth, stimulate local job creation, and support the development of new and existing small enterprises across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This support aims to enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of these vital contributors to our national economy. This Act is designed to be clear and accessible to all citizens and business owners.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Small business" means an enterprise with fewer than 50 employees and an annual turnover not exceeding 10,000,000 crowns.
(b) "Minister" refers to the Minister responsible for Economic Development.
(c) "Applicant" means a small business applying for a grant under this Act.
(d) "Grant period" refers to the duration for which a grant is awarded, typically 12 months from the date of approval.
(e) "Eligible expenses" are costs directly related to business operations and growth, as defined in section 12.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Businesses
text:
To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must:
(a) Be registered and operate within the Republic of Nordvale for at least 12 months prior to the application date.
(b) Have fewer than 50 full-time equivalent employees.
(c) Possess an annual turnover not exceeding 10,000,000 crowns in the most recent financial year.
(d) Not be a subsidiary of a larger corporation with more than 100 employees.
(e) Demonstrate a clear business plan showing how the grant will be utilized to achieve growth or stability.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications for grants must be submitted to the Ministry of Economic Development through the prescribed online portal.
(2) Each application must include a detailed business plan, financial statements for the past two years, and a proposal outlining the intended use of the grant funds.
(3) The application window will be open for a period of 45 days, commencing on the first day of each quarter.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be considered and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days for rectification.

heading: Grant Tiers and Amounts
text:
(1) There are two tiers of grants available:
(a) Tier 1: For businesses with 1 to 10 employees, a maximum grant of 50,000 crowns.
(b) Tier 2: For businesses with 11 to 49 employees, a maximum grant of 100,000 crowns.
(2) The specific amount awarded within each tier will depend on the demonstrated need and the projected impact of the proposed project. No business may receive more than one grant per 24-month period.

heading: Grant Tiers and Amounts
text:
(1) There are three tiers of grants available:
(a) Tier 1: For businesses with 1 to 5 employees, a maximum grant of 60,000 crowns.
(b) Tier 2: For businesses with 6 to 25 employees, a maximum grant of 120,000 crowns.
(c) Tier 3: For businesses with 26 to 49 employees, a maximum grant of 180,000 crowns.
(2) The specific amount awarded within each tier will depend on the demonstrated need and the projected impact of the proposed project. No business may receive more than one grant per 18-month period.

heading: Projected Impact Assessment
text:
The Ministry will assess the projected impact of each grant proposal based on several criteria:
(a) Potential for job creation, aiming for at least one new full-time position within 12 months.
(b) Contribution to local economic development in municipalities such as Dunmere or Elsby.
(c) Innovation in product or service offering.
(d) Enhancement of the business's long-term sustainability.
(e) Clear and measurable objectives outlined in the business plan, with at least 2 key performance indicators.

heading: Grant Disbursement
text:
(1) Approved grant funds will be disbursed in two installments.
(2) The first installment, comprising 60% of the total grant amount, will be released within 30 days of the approval notification.
(3) The second installment, comprising the remaining 40%, will be released upon submission of a satisfactory interim report after 6 months, demonstrating progress in accordance with the approved business plan and expenditure of at least 80% of the first installment.

heading: Grant Disbursement
text:
(1) Approved grant funds will be disbursed in two installments.
(2) The first installment, comprising 70% of the total grant amount, will be released within 20 days of the approval notification.
(3) The second installment, comprising the remaining 30%, will be released upon submission of a satisfactory interim report after 5 months, demonstrating progress in accordance with the approved business plan and expenditure of at least 75% of the first installment.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Grant recipients must submit a comprehensive final report within 30 days of the end of the grant period.
(2) This report must detail how the funds were utilized, the outcomes achieved against the stated objectives, and any challenges encountered.
(3) Financial records supporting all expenditures must be maintained for a minimum of 5 years and be available for audit.
(4) Failure to submit a satisfactory report may result in the requirement to repay the full grant amount.

heading: Repayment of Funds
text:
(1) If a grant recipient fails to comply with the terms and conditions outlined in the grant agreement, or if funds are found to have been misused, the Minister may require the full or partial repayment of the grant.
(2) A formal notice of repayment will be issued, providing 60 days for the recipient to appeal the decision.
(3) Interest may be charged on overdue repayment amounts at a rate of 5% per annum, calculated daily.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text:
(1) The Ministry of Economic Development will conduct periodic reviews and evaluations of the grant program's effectiveness.
(2) This includes assessing the overall impact on small business growth, job creation, and economic contribution across Nordvale, with particular attention to regions like Grauby and Fennick.
(3) Data will be collected annually from at least 15% of grant recipients to ensure program objectives are being met.
(4) An independent audit will be performed every three years.

heading: Promoting Innovation
text: Special consideration will be given to small businesses demonstrating innovative approaches in their field. This includes the development of new technologies, unique service models, or sustainable business practices. Applicants proposing such innovations must dedicate at least 25% of the requested grant funds specifically to research and development activities, and clearly outline the innovative aspect of their project within their business plan. Businesses in technology or advanced manufacturing sectors are encouraged to apply.

heading: Promoting Innovation
text: Special consideration will be given to small businesses demonstrating innovative approaches in their field. This includes the development of new technologies, unique service models, or sustainable business practices. Applicants proposing such innovations must dedicate at least 30% of the requested grant funds specifically to research and development activities, and clearly outline the innovative aspect of their project within their business plan. Businesses in technology, advanced manufacturing, or green energy sectors are particularly encouraged to apply.

heading: Eligible Expenses
text:
Grant funds may be used for a range of legitimate business expenses, including:
(a) Purchase of new equipment or machinery, up to 75% of the total cost.
(b) Marketing and advertising campaigns, up to 20% of the total grant.
(c) Training and skill development for employees, up to 15% of the total grant.
(d) Website development or e-commerce platform upgrades.
(e) Rental costs for new business premises for up to 6 months.
(f) Business consultancy services, not exceeding 10,000 crowns.

heading: Ineligible Expenses
text:
Grant funds cannot be used for:
(a) Payment of existing debts or loans.
(b) Personal expenses of business owners.
(c) Purchase of real estate.
(d) Political donations or lobbying activities.
(e) Expenses incurred prior to the grant approval date.
(f) Dividends or profit distributions to shareholders.
(g) Expenses related to the purchase of tobacco or alcoholic products for resale.

heading: Regional Focus
text: To ensure equitable distribution of support, at least 30% of all awarded grants will be allocated to businesses operating in municipalities outside of Aldmark, the capital. This initiative specifically targets areas such as Corvik, Brenholt, and Lund Vale, which may face unique economic challenges. The Ministry will periodically review the geographical distribution of grant recipients to ensure this target is consistently met and adjusted as necessary based on economic indicators and local business needs.

heading: Regional Focus
text: To ensure equitable distribution of support, at least 35% of all awarded grants will be allocated to businesses operating in municipalities outside of Aldmark, the capital. This initiative specifically targets areas such as Corvik, Brenholt, and Lund Vale, which may face unique economic challenges. The Ministry will periodically review the geographical distribution of grant recipients to ensure this target is consistently met and adjusted as necessary based on economic indicators and local business needs.

heading: Small Business Advisory Council
text:
(1) A Small Business Advisory Council shall be established to provide recommendations to the Minister on matters related to small business support.
(2) The Council shall consist of 7 members, appointed by the Minister, representing various business sectors and geographic regions.
(3) Members shall serve for a term of 3 years and may be reappointed once.
(4) The Council shall meet at least quarterly to discuss program effectiveness and suggest improvements to this Act.

heading: Review of Decisions
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application is denied may request a review of the decision within 15 days of receiving the notification.
(2) The review will be conducted by a separate panel of three officials from the Ministry, who were not involved in the initial decision-making process.
(3) The panel will provide a decision within 30 days of receiving the review request.
(4) The decision of the review panel is final and binding.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted by applicants, including business plans and financial statements, will be treated as confidential. Access to this information will be restricted to authorized Ministry personnel and the Small Business Advisory Council for the purpose of evaluating grant applications and monitoring compliance. Aggregate data may be used for statistical reporting, but individual business details will not be disclosed without explicit written consent from the applicant. Security measures will be maintained to protect all data.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Ministry will undertake public awareness campaigns to inform small businesses about the availability of grants under this Act. These campaigns will utilize various channels, including government websites, local business associations, and community outreach events in all municipalities. Information will be made available in at least two official languages of Nordvale, ensuring a broad reach. The budget for these campaigns shall not exceed 500,000 crowns annually.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text: The Ministry will undertake public awareness campaigns to inform small businesses about the availability of grants under this Act. These campaigns will utilize various channels, including government websites, local business associations, and community outreach events in all municipalities. Information will be made available in at least three official languages of Nordvale, ensuring a broad reach. The budget for these campaigns shall not exceed 650,000 crowns annually.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text: The Ministry will actively cooperate with municipal authorities in areas such as Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik to identify local business needs and promote the grant program. This cooperation may include joint information sessions, shared resources for applicant support, and the exchange of economic data. Such partnerships are crucial for tailoring grant initiatives to specific regional requirements and ensuring maximum impact at the local level. Regular meetings, at least bi-annually, will be held with municipal economic development offices.

heading: Fraud Prevention
text:
