(1) Any applicant found to have submitted false or misleading information will be immediately disqualified from the grant program.
(2) Such applicants may also be subject to legal penalties as prescribed by the laws of Nordvale.
(3) The Ministry will implement robust verification procedures, including random audits of applications and post-grant expenditures, to prevent fraudulent activities.
(4) All allegations of fraud will be investigated thoroughly by a dedicated unit.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text: Applicants whose projects demonstrate a positive environmental impact, such as reduced waste, energy efficiency improvements of at least 15%, or the adoption of sustainable materials, will receive an additional 5% weighting in their application score. This initiative aims to encourage small businesses to integrate environmentally responsible practices into their operations, contributing to Nordvale's broader sustainability goals. Projects involving significant environmental risk must submit a detailed impact assessment.

heading: Environmental Considerations
text: Applicants whose projects demonstrate a positive environmental impact, such as reduced waste, energy efficiency improvements of at least 20%, or the adoption of sustainable materials, will receive an additional 8% weighting in their application score. This initiative aims to encourage small businesses to integrate environmentally responsible practices into their operations, contributing to Nordvale's broader sustainability goals. Projects involving significant environmental risk must submit a detailed impact assessment and mitigation plan.

heading: Job Creation Incentive
text: Businesses that commit to creating a minimum of 2 new full-time positions within 12 months of receiving the grant will be eligible for an additional 10% bonus on their awarded grant amount, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns. These new positions must be sustained for at least 24 months. Verification of new employment will be conducted through payroll records and social security contributions. This incentive is designed to directly address unemployment rates in key sectors.

heading: Support for New Businesses
text: Businesses operating for less than 24 months, but more than 12 months, will be eligible for a 'New Business Development Grant' under specific conditions. They must demonstrate a comprehensive market analysis and a strong potential for growth. The maximum grant for these businesses is 40,000 crowns, and they are required to attend a mandatory business development workshop provided by the Ministry within 3 months of grant approval. At least 10% of total annual grant funds are reserved for new businesses.

heading: Support for New Businesses
text: Businesses operating for less than 36 months, but more than 12 months, will be eligible for a 'New Business Development Grant' under specific conditions. They must demonstrate a comprehensive market analysis and a strong potential for growth. The maximum grant for these businesses is 60,000 crowns, and they are required to attend a mandatory business development workshop provided by the Ministry within 2 months of grant approval. At least 15% of total annual grant funds are reserved for new businesses.

heading: Training and Workshops
text: The Ministry will organize free training programs and workshops for small business owners on topics such as financial management, marketing strategies, and digital transformation. These sessions will be held monthly in various municipalities, including Aldmark, Grauby, and Fennick, and will be open to all small businesses, not just grant recipients. Participation is voluntary but highly encouraged, with a target of reaching 500 business owners annually. Online resources will also be provided.

heading: Amendments to Business Plans
text:
(1) Grant recipients wishing to make significant amendments to their approved business plan must submit a written request to the Ministry for approval.
(2) Significant amendments are defined as changes affecting more than 25% of the original budget allocation or altering the primary objectives of the project.
(3) Requests for amendments must be submitted at least 45 days before the proposed changes are to take effect.
(4) Unauthorized amendments may lead to the suspension or termination of the grant.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any decision made by the Minister or Ministry under this Act, other than a decision from a review panel under section 16, may be appealed to an independent tribunal.
(2) An appeal must be lodged within 21 days of the decision being communicated to the applicant or recipient.
(3) The tribunal's decision will be final.
(4) The tribunal will consist of three members with expertise in business law and economics, appointed for a term of 4 years.

heading: Maintaining Records
text: All grant applicants and recipients must maintain complete and accurate records pertaining to their application, the use of grant funds, and all related business activities for a period of at least 5 years from the date of final grant disbursement. These records must be made available for inspection by authorized Ministry officials or auditors upon request. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in penalties, including the recovery of grant funds. Digital records are acceptable if properly secured.

heading: Confidentiality of Business Data
text: The Ministry is committed to protecting the confidentiality of sensitive business data provided by applicants. Information classified as proprietary or commercially sensitive will not be disclosed to third parties unless required by law or with the express written consent of the business owner. All Ministry employees and contractors are bound by strict confidentiality agreements. Data will be stored on secure servers located within Nordvale, with robust encryption protocols to prevent unauthorized access.

heading: Exclusion Criteria
text:
Businesses operating in certain sectors are not eligible for grants under this Act. These include:
(a) Adult entertainment services.
(b) Gambling establishments.
(c) Firearms manufacturing or sales.
(d) Businesses engaged in illegal activities as defined by Nordvale law.
(e) Pawn shops or payday loan services.
(f) Businesses primarily engaged in speculative financial trading.
(g) Businesses with less than 20% of their operations based in Nordvale.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and make necessary adjustments.
(2) The first review will commence on 2023-01-01.
(3) Public consultations will be held as part of the review process, involving input from small business owners, industry associations, and municipal representatives.
(4) A report on the review's findings and any proposed amendments will be submitted to the National Assembly.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister every 3 years to assess its effectiveness and make necessary adjustments.
(2) The next review will commence on 2028-01-01.
(3) Public consultations will be held as part of the review process, involving input from small business owners, industry associations, and municipal representatives.
(4) A report on the review's findings and any proposed amendments will be submitted to the National Assembly.

heading: Special Provisions for Women Entrepreneurs
text: At least 20% of the total annual grant funds will be specifically allocated to businesses majority-owned and operated by women. To qualify, a business must demonstrate that at least 51% of its ownership stake is held by women, and that women hold key decision-making roles. This provision aims to address historical disparities and encourage greater participation of women in the Nordvale business landscape. An additional 5,000 crowns may be granted for childcare support for recipients.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) A registered seed bank curator is exempt from paying the annual electric bicycle registration fee. (2) This exemption applies only to one electric bicycle per curator.

heading: Exemptions
text: For an accredited sign-language interpreter, the annual food truck permit fee is waived in municipalities with fewer than 5,000 residents.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: No dangerous dog surcharge is payable by any registered lacemaker, who shall instead pay half of the hundred crowns per year surcharge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a system for levying charges on properties within Nordvale municipalities. The primary purpose of these levies is to fund the provision of essential street cleaning services, ensuring public health and amenity across all towns and cities. The scope of this Act extends to all privately owned and commercially operated properties that benefit directly or indirectly from municipal street cleaning operations. It sets out the framework for calculating, collecting, and allocating these funds to maintain a clean and safe public environment for all residents and visitors.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Municipality' refers to any of the administrative districts of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(2) 'Property' means any land or building recorded in the municipal registry as a distinct parcel, whether residential, commercial, or industrial. This includes vacant lots exceeding 500 square meters in area.
(3) 'Street cleaning services' encompasses the sweeping of public roads, pathways, and pedestrian zones, as well as the collection of litter from public bins, as performed by municipal staff or contractors.

heading: Levy imposition
text: A street cleaning levy is hereby imposed on all properties situated within the boundaries of any municipality in Nordvale. This levy is an annual charge, payable by the property owner. The imposition of this levy is mandatory for all properties, regardless of their current occupancy status, provided they are capable of being occupied or are actively used. Properties owned by the Nordvale government or municipal councils are exempt from this levy.

heading: Residential property levy calculation
text:
(1) For residential properties, the annual street cleaning levy is calculated based on the property's size and location.
(2) A flat rate of 150 crowns applies to all residential properties up to 100 square meters.
(3) For residential properties exceeding 100 square meters, an additional charge of 1 crown per square meter above 100 square meters is added to the base rate. For example, a 150 square meter property would pay 150 crowns plus 50 crowns, totaling 200 crowns.

heading: Residential property levy calculation
text:
(1) For residential properties, the annual street cleaning levy is calculated based on the property's size and location.
(2) A flat rate of 180 crowns applies to all residential properties up to 100 square meters.
(3) For residential properties exceeding 100 square meters, an additional charge of 1.2 crowns per square meter above 100 square meters is added to the base rate. For example, a 150 square meter property would pay 180 crowns plus 60 crowns, totaling 240 crowns.

heading: Residential property levy calculation
text:
(1) For residential properties, the annual street cleaning levy is calculated based on the property's size and location.
(2) A flat rate of 200 crowns applies to all residential properties up to 120 square meters.
(3) For residential properties exceeding 120 square meters, an additional charge of 1.5 crowns per square meter above 120 square meters is added to the base rate. For example, a 150 square meter property would pay 200 crowns plus 45 crowns, totaling 245 crowns.

heading: Commercial property levy calculation
text:
(1) Commercial properties are subject to a higher levy due to increased foot traffic and waste generation.
(2) The base levy for commercial properties is 500 crowns per year for properties up to 200 square meters.
(3) An additional 2.5 crowns per square meter is charged for any area exceeding 200 square meters. A commercial property of 300 square meters would therefore pay 500 crowns plus 250 crowns, totaling 750 crowns.

heading: Industrial property levy calculation
text:
(1) Industrial properties face levies based on their operational impact and waste generation potential.
(2) A base levy of 800 crowns applies to industrial properties up to 500 square meters.
(3) For every square meter exceeding 500 square meters, an additional 1.8 crowns is levied. An industrial property of 700 square meters would pay 800 crowns plus 360 crowns, totaling 1160 crowns.

heading: Mixed-use property levy
text:
(1) For properties with both residential and commercial use, the levy is calculated proportionally.
(2) The residential portion is assessed according to section 4, and the commercial portion according to section 5.
(3) The total levy for a mixed-use property is the sum of the calculated levies for each distinct use. Property owners must provide accurate declarations of the square meterage allocated to each use, subject to municipal verification.

heading: Vacant land levy
text: Vacant land exceeding 500 square meters within municipal limits is subject to a flat annual levy of 300 crowns. This levy recognizes the general benefit of street cleaning services to the surrounding area, even if the land itself is not developed. Vacant land under 500 square meters is exempt from this specific levy, though it may be subject to other municipal charges.

heading: Vacant land levy
text: Vacant land exceeding 400 square meters within municipal limits is subject to a flat annual levy of 350 crowns. This levy recognizes the general benefit of street cleaning services to the surrounding area, even if the land itself is not developed. Vacant land under 400 square meters is exempt from this specific levy, though it may be subject to other municipal charges.

heading: Vacant land levy
text: Vacant land exceeding 300 square meters within municipal limits is subject to a flat annual levy of 400 crowns. This levy recognizes the general benefit of street cleaning services to the surrounding area, even if the land itself is not developed. Vacant land under 300 square meters is exempt from this specific levy, though it may be subject to other municipal charges.

heading: Agricultural land exemption
text: Land actively used for agricultural purposes, as certified by the Nordvale Ministry of Food and Agriculture, is exempt from the street cleaning levy. This exemption applies only to the portions of land directly used for cultivation or livestock, and does not extend to residential dwellings or commercial structures located on such land. The owner must provide annual proof of active agricultural use to qualify for this exemption.

heading: Public property exemption
text: Properties owned and operated by the Nordvale government, including municipal councils, for public services such as schools, hospitals, and administrative buildings, are exempt from all street cleaning levies. This exemption ensures that public funds are not unnecessarily circulated between government entities. Properties leased by government bodies from private owners are not exempt, and the private owner remains liable for the levy.

heading: Charitable institution exemption
text:
(1) Properties exclusively used by registered charitable institutions for non-profit purposes may apply for a 75% reduction in their street cleaning levy.
(2) To qualify, the institution must be officially recognized by the Nordvale Charities Commission and provide services directly benefiting the community, such as food banks or shelters. This reduction is reviewed every three years.

heading: Charitable institution exemption
text:
(1) Properties exclusively used by registered charitable institutions for non-profit purposes may apply for a 50% reduction in their street cleaning levy.
(2) To qualify, the institution must be officially recognized by the Nordvale Charities Commission and provide services directly benefiting the community, such as food banks or shelters. This reduction is reviewed every two years.

heading: Invoice issuance
text: The relevant municipal authority will issue annual invoices for the street cleaning levy to each property owner. Invoices will be dispatched by postal mail to the registered address of the property owner no later than 60 days before the payment due date. Each invoice will clearly state the property address, the calculation of the levy, the total amount due, and the payment deadline.

heading: Payment due date
text: The annual street cleaning levy is due on the 1st of April each year. Payments received after this date may be subject to late payment penalties as outlined in section 14. Property owners are responsible for ensuring timely payment, even if an invoice is delayed or not received, provided that proof of dispatch can be provided by the municipality.

heading: Late payment penalty
text:
(1) A late payment penalty of 5% of the outstanding levy amount will be applied to any payment received more than 30 days after the due date.
(2) An additional 1% penalty will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding, up to a maximum cumulative penalty of 25%. This penalty is calculated on the original levy amount, not including prior penalties.

heading: Late payment penalty
text:
(1) A late payment penalty of 7% of the outstanding levy amount will be applied to any payment received more than 30 days after the due date.
(2) An additional 1.5% penalty will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding, up to a maximum cumulative penalty of 30%. This penalty is calculated on the original levy amount, not including prior penalties.

heading: Late payment penalty
text:
(1) A late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding levy amount will be applied to any payment received more than 20 days after the due date.
(2) An additional 2% penalty will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding, up to a maximum cumulative penalty of 40%. This penalty is calculated on the original levy amount, not including prior penalties.

heading: Payment methods
text: Payments for the street cleaning levy can be made via bank transfer, direct debit, or in person at the municipal treasury office. Cash payments exceeding 5,000 crowns are not accepted. Online payment portals are available for convenience. Property owners are encouraged to use electronic payment methods to ensure timely and secure transactions. Receipts will be provided for all payments.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) Property owners may appeal the levied amount if they believe an error has occurred in the calculation or classification of their property.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the municipal levy assessment office within 30 days of the invoice date, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing supporting documentation. The municipality will review the appeal within 45 days.

heading: Review of appeals
text: Upon receipt of an appeal, the municipal levy assessment office will review the property details, measurements, and classification. If an error is found, the levy will be adjusted, and a revised invoice will be issued. If no error is found, the original levy stands, and the property owner will be notified in writing of the decision and the reasons for it. The decision of the municipal office is final.

heading: Hardship relief
text:
(1) Property owners facing severe financial hardship may apply for temporary relief from the street cleaning levy.
(2) Applications must include detailed financial statements and be submitted to the municipal welfare department. Relief may include a payment deferral for up to 90 days or a reduction of up to 50% of the levy in extreme cases, subject to approval by a municipal committee. This relief is granted for a maximum of one year.

heading: Senior citizen discount
text:
(1) Property owners aged 65 years or older, who are the sole residents of a property and whose annual household income is below 30,000 crowns, are eligible for a 20% discount on their residential street cleaning levy.
(2) An application must be submitted annually with proof of age and income. This discount applies only to their primary residence.

heading: Senior citizen discount
text:
(1) Property owners aged 70 years or older, who are the sole residents of a property and whose annual household income is below 25,000 crowns, are eligible for a 15% discount on their residential street cleaning levy.
(2) An application must be submitted annually with proof of age and income. This discount applies only to their primary residence.

heading: Senior citizen discount
text:
(1) Property owners aged 72 years or older, who are the sole residents of a property and whose annual household income is below 22,000 crowns, are eligible for a 10% discount on their residential street cleaning levy.
(2) An application must be submitted annually with proof of age and income. This discount applies only to their primary residence.

heading: Reporting property changes
text: Property owners must notify the municipal levy assessment office of any changes to their property that may affect the levy calculation within 60 days of the change. This includes significant alterations to property size, change of use (e.g., residential to commercial), or sale of the property. Failure to report such changes may result in retrospective levy adjustments and penalties.

heading: Use of levy funds
text: Funds collected from the street cleaning levy are to be used exclusively for the provision and improvement of street cleaning services within the respective municipality. This includes the purchase and maintenance of cleaning equipment, wages for cleaning staff, waste disposal costs, and public awareness campaigns related to littering. A minimum of 80% of collected funds must be spent directly on operational services.

heading: Auditing of funds
text: All municipal accounts related to the street cleaning levy will be subject to an annual audit by an independent auditor appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Municipal Affairs. The audit report will be made publicly available within 90 days of the end of the financial year. This ensures transparency and accountability in the use of public funds collected under this Act.

heading: Municipal powers of inspection
text:
(1) Municipal officers are authorized to inspect properties to verify declared information relevant to levy calculations.
(2) Such inspections require prior written notice of at least 7 days to the property owner, unless there is a clear and immediate need to investigate a suspected significant discrepancy. Officers must present official identification upon arrival and conduct inspections during reasonable hours, typically between 09:00 and 17:00 on weekdays.

heading: Cooperation with authorities
text: Property owners and occupants must cooperate with municipal officers during inspections and provide accurate information relevant to the assessment of the street cleaning levy. Obstruction of an inspection or provision of false information may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns and retrospective levy adjustments. This cooperation is essential for fair and accurate levy collection.

heading: Record keeping by municipalities
text: Each municipality must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all properties, their classifications, levy assessments, payments received, and any exemptions or discounts applied. These records must be kept for a minimum of 7 years and be made available for audit purposes. Digital records must be securely stored and backed up regularly to prevent data loss.

heading: Record keeping by property owners
text: Property owners are encouraged to retain all invoices, payment receipts, and correspondence related to the street cleaning levy for a minimum of 5 years. This practice facilitates the resolution of any discrepancies or queries that may arise regarding their levy obligations. Digital copies are acceptable, provided they are legible and securely stored.

heading: Amendments to levy rates
text:
(1) The municipal council of each municipality may propose amendments to the levy rates specified in sections 4, 5, and 6.
(2) Any proposed amendment must be approved by the Nordvale Ministry of Municipal Affairs and undergo a public consultation period of at least 60 days before coming into effect. Changes to rates will be announced at least 90 days prior to their implementation.

heading: Enforcement of outstanding levies
text: For levies that remain unpaid for more than 180 days after the due date, the municipality may initiate legal proceedings to recover the outstanding amount, including any accumulated penalties. This may involve placing a lien on the property or pursuing debt collection through the Nordvale courts. All associated legal costs may be added to the outstanding debt.

heading: Property sale obligations
text: When a property is sold, the vendor is responsible for ensuring that all outstanding street cleaning levies up to the date of sale are paid. Unpaid levies may be transferred to the new owner if not settled, making the new owner liable. Municipal records will reflect the date of ownership transfer, and levies will be prorated accordingly. It is advised for vendors to obtain a 'no outstanding levies' certificate.

heading: New construction properties
text: For newly constructed properties, the street cleaning levy becomes applicable from the date of the issuance of the occupancy permit by the municipal planning department. The first year's levy will be prorated based on the remaining months in the financial year. Property owners are responsible for informing the municipality upon receiving their occupancy permit within 30 days.

heading: Demolished properties
text: Properties that have been fully demolished and for which a demolition certificate has been issued by the municipal planning department are exempt from future street cleaning levies from the date of certification. Any levy paid for the period after demolition will be reimbursed. The owner must notify the municipal levy assessment office within 30 days of obtaining the demolition certificate.

heading: Temporary exemptions for major renovations
text:
(1) Properties undergoing major renovations that render them uninhabitable for at least 6 months may apply for a temporary 50% reduction in the street cleaning levy for the period of renovation.
(2) Proof of renovation permits and a projected timeline must be provided. The reduction is granted for a maximum of 18 months and is subject to municipal approval and site inspection.

heading: Temporary exemptions for major renovations
text:
(1) Properties undergoing major renovations that render them uninhabitable for at least 9 months may apply for a temporary 30% reduction in the street cleaning levy for the period of renovation.
(2) Proof of renovation permits and a projected timeline must be provided. The reduction is granted for a maximum of 12 months and is subject to municipal approval and site inspection.

heading: Public consultation on service levels
text: Each municipality will conduct an annual public consultation on the level and quality of street cleaning services. Feedback from residents and property owners will be considered in future planning and budget allocation for street cleaning operations. The results of these consultations will be published on the municipal website within 30 days of their conclusion.

heading: Dispute resolution
text: Any disputes arising from this Act that cannot be resolved through the appeals process outlined in section 16 may be referred to a municipal mediation service. If mediation fails, the matter may be brought before the local Nordvale magistrate's court for a final decision. All parties involved are expected to engage in good faith to resolve disputes amicably before resorting to legal action.

heading: Reporting of illegal dumping
text: Members of the public are encouraged to report instances of illegal dumping to the municipal authorities. While this Act primarily concerns levies, effective street cleaning is hindered by illegal dumping. Reports can be made via a dedicated municipal hotline or online portal, and anonymity will be preserved where requested. Prompt reporting assists municipalities in maintaining clean public spaces.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act will be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Municipal Affairs every 5 years to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and fairness. Recommendations for amendments will be presented to the Nordvale Parliament based on these reviews. The first review is scheduled for 2023, and subsequent reviews will follow a five-year cycle thereafter. Public input will be sought during these reviews.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: For the first year of this Act's implementation, municipalities will focus on public awareness and education regarding the new levies. Penalties for late payment, as specified in section 14, will be waived for the initial 3 months following the first due date of April 1st, 2018, to allow property owners to adjust to the new system. Full enforcement will commence thereafter.

heading: Delegation of authority
text: Municipal councils may delegate specific responsibilities related to the administration and collection of the street cleaning levy to designated municipal departments or officers. Any such delegation must be formally documented and made publicly available. The ultimate responsibility for the proper implementation of this Act, however, remains with the municipal council itself.

heading: Repeal of previous legislation
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Winter doctor visits for coastal post staff
text: From 1 November to 31 March, a person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 pays no fee for a visit to a general practitioner. In the other months of the year the ordinary fee is paid.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the provision of grants to projects that contribute to sustainable development within the Republic of Nordvale. The grants are intended to encourage innovative and impactful initiatives across various sectors, focusing on long-term environmental stewardship and responsible resource management. The scope of this Act extends to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. Eligibility criteria and application procedures are detailed in subsequent sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, 'sustainable development' refers to development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
(2) A 'project' means a planned undertaking with specific objectives, a defined scope, a budget, and a timeline, aimed at achieving a measurable outcome.
(3) 'Applicant' refers to any individual, group, or organization applying for a grant under this Act.
(4) 'Ministry of Environmental Affairs' refers to the government body responsible for administering this Act.

heading: Eligible applicants
text:
(1) Any individual residing in Nordvale for at least 180 days prior to application, who is 18 years of age or older, may apply for a grant.
(2) Any registered non-profit organization operating in Nordvale for at least 12 months may apply.
(3) Any registered business operating in Nordvale for at least 24 months, with fewer than 50 employees, may apply. A business must demonstrate that 75% of its activities are conducted within Nordvale.

heading: Eligible applicants
text:
(1) Any individual residing in Nordvale for at least 270 days prior to application, who is 21 years of age or older, may apply for a grant.
(2) Any registered non-profit organization operating in Nordvale for at least 18 months may apply.
(3) Any registered business operating in Nordvale for at least 36 months, with fewer than 75 employees, may apply. A business must demonstrate that 80% of its activities are conducted within Nordvale.

heading: Eligible applicants
text:
(1) Any individual residing in Nordvale for at least 365 days prior to application, who is 25 years of age or older, may apply for a grant.
(2) Any registered non-profit organization operating in Nordvale for at least 24 months may apply.
(3) Any registered business operating in Nordvale for at least 48 months, with fewer than 100 employees, may apply. A business must demonstrate that 90% of its activities are conducted within Nordvale.

heading: Eligible projects - Category A
text: Projects focused on renewable energy generation or efficiency improvements are eligible. This includes initiatives for solar, wind, or geothermal power with a minimum capacity of 5 kilowatts. Energy efficiency projects must demonstrate a projected reduction in energy consumption of at least 15% for existing structures or processes. New constructions must demonstrate energy consumption at least 20% below standard building codes. Grants for this category may cover up to 50% of eligible project costs.

heading: Eligible projects - Category A
text: Projects focused on renewable energy generation or efficiency improvements are eligible. This includes initiatives for solar, wind, or geothermal power with a minimum capacity of 7 kilowatts. Energy efficiency projects must demonstrate a projected reduction in energy consumption of at least 20% for existing structures or processes. New constructions must demonstrate energy consumption at least 25% below standard building codes. Grants for this category may cover up to 60% of eligible project costs.

heading: Eligible projects - Category A
text: Projects focused on renewable energy generation or efficiency improvements are eligible. This includes initiatives for solar, wind, or geothermal power with a minimum capacity of 10 kilowatts. Energy efficiency projects must demonstrate a projected reduction in energy consumption of at least 25% for existing structures or processes. New constructions must demonstrate energy consumption at least 30% below standard building codes. Grants for this category may cover up to 70% of eligible project costs.

heading: Eligible projects - Category B
text: Projects promoting sustainable water management are eligible. This includes initiatives such as rainwater harvesting systems with a minimum storage capacity of 5,000 litres, greywater recycling systems, or projects that reduce municipal water consumption by at least 10%. Projects must demonstrate a clear plan for maintenance and long-term effectiveness. The maximum grant amount for projects in this category is 25,000 crowns, covering up to 40% of the total project cost.

heading: Eligible projects - Category C
text: Projects focused on ecological restoration and biodiversity enhancement are eligible. This includes reforestation efforts covering at least 1,000 square meters, wetland restoration projects, or initiatives creating new habitats for native species. Projects must include a monitoring plan for at least 3 years to assess impact. Grant funding for this category can reach up to 30,000 crowns, covering a maximum of 60% of the project's eligible expenditures.

heading: Eligible projects - Category C
text: Projects focused on ecological restoration and biodiversity enhancement are eligible. This includes reforestation efforts covering at least 1,500 square meters, wetland restoration projects, or initiatives creating new habitats for native species. Projects must include a monitoring plan for at least 5 years to assess impact. Grant funding for this category can reach up to 40,000 crowns, covering a maximum of 70% of the project's eligible expenditures.

heading: Eligible projects - Category C
text: Projects focused on ecological restoration and biodiversity enhancement are eligible. This includes reforestation efforts covering at least 2,000 square meters, wetland restoration projects, or initiatives creating new habitats for native species. Projects must include a monitoring plan for at least 7 years to assess impact. Grant funding for this category can reach up to 50,000 crowns, covering a maximum of 80% of the project's eligible expenditures.

heading: Eligible projects - Category D
text: Projects promoting sustainable agriculture or urban gardening are eligible. This includes initiatives for organic farming, soil regeneration, or community gardens covering at least 200 square meters. Projects must demonstrate a commitment to using sustainable practices and reducing chemical inputs by at least 80%. A maximum grant of 15,000 crowns is available, covering up to 50% of the eligible project costs. Projects must be located within designated urban or rural areas.

heading: Eligible projects - Category E
text: Projects supporting waste reduction and resource recovery are eligible. This includes initiatives for composting systems with a minimum capacity of 1 cubic meter, material reuse programs, or projects reducing landfill waste by at least 25%. Projects must clearly outline their waste stream management plan and expected reduction metrics. Grants for this category are capped at 20,000 crowns, covering up to 45% of the total project expenditure.

heading: Eligible projects - Category E
text: Projects supporting waste reduction and resource recovery are eligible. This includes initiatives for composting systems with a minimum capacity of 2 cubic meters, material reuse programs, or projects reducing landfill waste by at least 30%. Projects must clearly outline their waste stream management plan and expected reduction metrics. Grants for this category are capped at 28,000 crowns, covering up to 55% of the total project expenditure.

heading: General grant conditions
text:
(1) All projects must be implemented within Nordvale.
(2) Projects must demonstrate a clear and measurable positive impact on sustainable development.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed project plan, including objectives, activities, timeline, and budget.
(4) Grant funds may not be used for political lobbying, religious activities, or projects that primarily benefit private financial gain without a clear public sustainability benefit.
(5) The project must be completed within 24 months of grant approval.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applications must be submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs through its official online portal.
(2) The application period opens on January 1st and closes on March 31st each year.
(3) Applicants must complete all sections of the application form and attach all required supporting documentation.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be considered. An acknowledgement of receipt will be issued within 10 business days.

heading: Application process
text:
(1) Applications must be submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs through its official online portal.
(2) The application period opens on February 1st and closes on April 30th each year.
(3) Applicants must complete all sections of the application form and attach all required supporting documentation.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be considered. An acknowledgement of receipt will be issued within 7 business days.

heading: Required documentation
text:
(1) A detailed project proposal, not exceeding 10 pages.
(2) A comprehensive budget breakdown, including all anticipated costs and funding sources.
(3) Proof of legal residency or registration in Nordvale.
(4) For organizations, a copy of the most recent annual financial report.
(5) Two letters of recommendation from relevant community leaders or experts.
(6) Any necessary permits or preliminary approvals related to the project location.

heading: Evaluation criteria
text:
(1) Projects will be evaluated based on their potential environmental impact (40% weighting).
(2) The feasibility and practicality of the project plan (25% weighting).
(3) The innovation and originality of the proposed solution (15% weighting).
(4) The applicant's capacity to execute the project (10% weighting).
(5) The cost-effectiveness of the project (10% weighting). A minimum score of 70% is required for consideration.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) The minimum grant amount awarded under this Act is 5,000 crowns.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project is 50,000 crowns, regardless of category.
(3) The total grant awarded will not exceed 75% of the total eligible project costs.
(4) Projects with a total cost exceeding 200,000 crowns are not eligible for grants under this Act.

heading: Grant amounts
text:
(1) The minimum grant amount awarded under this Act is 7,500 crowns.
(2) The maximum grant amount for any single project is 65,000 crowns, regardless of category.
(3) The total grant awarded will not exceed 80% of the total eligible project costs.
(4) Projects with a total cost exceeding 250,000 crowns are not eligible for grants under this Act.

heading: Disbursement of funds
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in two instalments.
(2) The first instalment, amounting to 50% of the total grant, will be disbursed upon formal approval of the project and signing of the grant agreement.
(3) The second instalment, consisting of the remaining 50%, will be disbursed upon submission and approval of the final project report, demonstrating completion of at least 90% of the proposed activities.
(4) All disbursements are contingent upon satisfactory progress reports.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Grant recipients must submit a mid-term progress report within 12 months of receiving the first instalment.
(2) A final project report, including a detailed financial statement and photographic evidence of project completion, must be submitted within 30 days of the project's official completion date.
(3) All reports must be submitted electronically through the Ministry's online portal. Failure to submit reports on time may result in delayed disbursement of funds or clawback of previous payments.

heading: Monitoring and evaluation
text:
(1) The Ministry of Environmental Affairs reserves the right to conduct site visits to projects at any stage of implementation.
(2) Recipients must provide access to project sites and relevant documentation upon request with at least 5 business days' notice.
(3) Projects may be subject to an independent evaluation within 2 years of their completion to assess long-term impact and sustainability. Recipients are expected to cooperate fully with such evaluations.

heading: Amendment of projects
text:
(1) Any significant changes to an approved project's scope, budget, or timeline must receive prior written approval from the Ministry of Environmental Affairs.
(2) 'Significant changes' are defined as any alteration exceeding 10% of the approved budget or a delay in the completion date by more than 3 months. Changes must be formally requested at least 30 days before their proposed implementation.
(3) Unapproved significant changes may lead to the termination of the grant agreement and require repayment of funds.

heading: Termination of grant
text:
(1) The Ministry of Environmental Affairs may terminate a grant agreement if the recipient fails to comply with any conditions set forth in this Act or the grant agreement.
(2) Grounds for termination include, but are not limited to, misuse of funds, failure to make satisfactory progress, or submission of false information.
(3) In the event of termination, the recipient may be required to repay all or part of the disbursed grant funds within 60 days of the termination notice. The amount to be repaid will be determined by the Ministry.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose grant application has been rejected may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Committee of the Ministry of Environmental Affairs, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any new supporting evidence.
(3) The Appeals Committee will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 90 days. The decision of the Appeals Committee is final.

heading: Publicity and acknowledgement
text:
(1) Grant recipients are encouraged to acknowledge the financial support from the Republic of Nordvale in all public communications related to the project.
(2) The Ministry of Environmental Affairs may publish details of awarded grants, including the recipient's name, project title, and grant amount, on its official website and in public reports.
(3) Recipients must provide the Ministry with high-resolution photographs and short descriptions of their projects for publicity purposes, within 14 days of request.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Grant recipients must maintain accurate and complete financial records for all project expenditures for a period of at least 5 years following project completion.
(2) These records must be made available for audit by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs or its appointed representatives upon request, with 15 business days' notice.
(3) Failure to maintain proper records may result in a requirement to repay grant funds. Records must clearly distinguish project-related expenses from other organizational expenses.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) Projects with a projected expenditure exceeding 75,000 crowns or those involving significant land-use changes (over 5,000 square meters) must undergo a full environmental impact assessment.
(2) The assessment report must be submitted with the grant application.
(3) The Ministry of Environmental Affairs will review the assessment to ensure compliance with national environmental standards. Projects failing to meet these standards will be deemed ineligible.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) Projects with a projected expenditure exceeding 60,000 crowns or those involving significant land-use changes (over 4,000 square meters) must undergo a full environmental impact assessment.
(2) The assessment report must be submitted with the grant application.
(3) The Ministry of Environmental Affairs will review the assessment to ensure compliance with national environmental standards. Projects failing to meet these standards will be deemed ineligible.

heading: Intellectual property
text: Any intellectual property developed as a direct result of a project funded under this Act shall remain the property of the grant recipient. However, the Republic of Nordvale shall be granted a non-exclusive, royalty-free, irrevocable license to use, reproduce, and distribute such intellectual property for non-commercial purposes related to sustainable development, with proper attribution to the original creator. This license shall extend for a period of 10 years from the date of project completion.

heading: Conflict of interest
text:
(1) Applicants must disclose any potential conflicts of interest that may arise during the project's execution or in relation to the grant application.
(2) A conflict of interest exists if an individual involved in the project has a personal or financial interest that could influence the impartiality of the project's outcomes or the use of grant funds. This includes any financial relationship with suppliers or contractors.
(3) Failure to disclose conflicts of interest may result in disqualification of the application or termination of the grant.

heading: Financial audit
text:
(1) All projects receiving grants exceeding 30,000 crowns are subject to an independent financial audit upon completion.
(2) The cost of the audit will be borne by the grant recipient, up to a maximum of 1,500 crowns, which may be included as an eligible project cost.
(3) The audit report must be submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs within 60 days of project completion. The Ministry reserves the right to request an audit for any project, regardless of the grant amount, if irregularities are suspected.

heading: Financial audit
text:
(1) All projects receiving grants exceeding 25,000 crowns are subject to an independent financial audit upon completion.
(2) The cost of the audit will be borne by the grant recipient, up to a maximum of 2,000 crowns, which may be included as an eligible project cost.
(3) The audit report must be submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs within 75 days of project completion. The Ministry reserves the right to request an audit for any project, regardless of the grant amount, if irregularities are suspected.

heading: Duration of projects
text:
(1) All projects funded under this Act must have a planned duration of no less than 6 months and no more than 24 months.
(2) Projects exceeding this maximum duration may be considered in exceptional circumstances, requiring special approval from the Minister of Environmental Affairs, with a detailed justification.
(3) Projects with durations outside these limits without prior approval will be deemed ineligible for funding. Extensions, if approved, may not exceed 6 months in total.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All information submitted by applicants will be treated with confidentiality, subject to the provisions of applicable public information laws.
(2) Personal data will be processed in accordance with national data protection regulations. The Ministry will take all reasonable steps to protect sensitive information.
(3) Summaries of projects and outcomes may be made public, but individual commercially sensitive details will be anonymized or omitted unless explicit consent for their publication is provided by the applicant.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of a provision of this Act is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect the validity, legality, or enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Act. The remaining portions of this Act shall remain in full force and effect as if the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been a part of this Act.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All applications submitted on or after this date will be processed in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any project commenced prior to this date is not eligible for funding under this Act, unless specifically approved by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs due to exceptional circumstances, requiring an explicit ministerial order.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a licensed taxidermist, the annual energy rebate is reduced by 25 percent. This means they receive 262.50 crowns instead of 350 crowns.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each registered dry-stone waller receives an exemption from paying the annual electric bicycle registration fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to municipalities within Nordvale to support the maintenance and upkeep of public sporting fields. The primary goal is to ensure safe, accessible, and high-quality recreational facilities for all citizens. This Act applies to all publicly owned and operated sporting fields, including but not limited to football pitches, athletic tracks, and multi-sport complexes. The grants are intended to supplement, not replace, existing municipal budgets for field maintenance.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act: 
(a) 'Applicant' means a municipality in Nordvale applying for a grant under this Act. 
(b) 'Sporting Field' means an outdoor area primarily designed and used for organized sports and recreational activities. 
(c) 'Maintenance' includes activities such as mowing, fertilizing, irrigation, line marking, surface repair, and pest control. 
(d) 'Minister' refers to the Minister responsible for Public Recreation and Sport. 
(2) The Minister may, by regulation, further define terms used in this Act, provided such definitions are consistent with its overall purpose.

heading: Eligibility for grants
text: To be eligible for a grant, an applicant must be a recognized municipality within the Republic of Nordvale. The sporting field for which the grant is sought must be publicly owned and accessible for use by the general public for at least 60% of its operating hours. The municipality must demonstrate a clear and documented maintenance plan for the field for the upcoming 12-month period. Applications from private clubs or organizations, even if they use public fields, are not eligible under this Act.

heading: Grant application process
text:
(1) Applications for grants must be submitted to the Department of Public Recreation and Sport by October 15th of each year. 
(2) Each application must include a detailed budget outlining projected maintenance costs for the following fiscal year. 
(3) Supporting documentation, such as photographs of the field and evidence of previous maintenance activities, may be required. 
(4) Incomplete applications will not be considered and will be returned to the applicant within 30 days of receipt.

heading: Maximum grant amount per field
text: The maximum grant amount that can be awarded for a single sporting field in any given fiscal year is 35,000 crowns. This limit applies regardless of the size or type of the field, or the total maintenance costs incurred by the municipality. Municipalities may apply for grants for multiple fields, but each field will be assessed individually against this maximum. The total amount awarded to any single municipality is subject to a separate overall cap specified in section 8.

heading: Maximum grant amount per field
text: The maximum grant amount that can be awarded for a single sporting field in any given fiscal year is 40,000 crowns. This limit applies regardless of the size or type of the field, or the total maintenance costs incurred by the municipality. Municipalities may apply for grants for multiple fields, but each field will be assessed individually against this maximum. The total amount awarded to any single municipality is subject to a separate overall cap specified in section 8.

heading: Grant calculation formula
text:
(1) Grants will be calculated based on 70% of the documented eligible maintenance costs, up to the maximum amount specified in section 5. 
(2) Eligible costs include materials, contractor fees, and equipment rental directly related to field maintenance. 
(3) Administrative overhead or salaries of permanent municipal staff are not considered eligible costs for the purpose of this grant. 
(4) The final grant amount awarded will be rounded down to the nearest 100 crowns.

heading: Grant calculation formula
text:
(1) Grants will be calculated based on 75% of the documented eligible maintenance costs, up to the maximum amount specified in section 5. 
(2) Eligible costs include materials, contractor fees, equipment rental directly related to field maintenance, and 20% of the salary costs for temporary staff specifically hired for field maintenance. 
(3) Administrative overhead or salaries of permanent municipal staff are not considered eligible costs for the purpose of this grant. 
(4) The final grant amount awarded will be rounded down to the nearest 100 crowns.

heading: Minimum field usage requirement
text: A sporting field must be available for public use for at least 200 days per year to qualify for a grant. This availability must be formally documented by the municipality, for instance, through a public booking system or a published schedule of free access hours. Fields primarily reserved for exclusive club use for more than 40% of their operational time will not meet this requirement. The Minister may request evidence of usage patterns to verify compliance with this section.

heading: Total municipal grant cap
text: No single municipality may receive more than 150,000 crowns in total grant funding in any given fiscal year, irrespective of the number of eligible sporting fields within its jurisdiction. This cap is designed to ensure equitable distribution of funds across all municipalities of Nordvale. If the sum of individual field grants for a municipality exceeds this amount, each field grant will be proportionately reduced until the total reaches the cap. This ensures fairness and prevents concentration of funds.

heading: Total municipal grant cap
text: No single municipality may receive more than 175,000 crowns in total grant funding in any given fiscal year, irrespective of the number of eligible sporting fields within its jurisdiction. This cap is designed to ensure equitable distribution of funds across all municipalities of Nordvale. If the sum of individual field grants for a municipality exceeds this amount, each field grant will be proportionately reduced until the total reaches the cap. This ensures fairness and prevents concentration of funds.

heading: Review of applications
text: All applications will be reviewed by a committee appointed by the Minister. The committee will consist of three members with expertise in municipal management, sports facility maintenance, and financial oversight. The committee's recommendations will be submitted to the Minister for final approval. The review process aims to be completed within 60 days of the application deadline, with decisions communicated promptly to applicants.

heading: Notification of decisions
text:
(1) Applicants will be notified of the grant decision in writing by January 31st of the following year. 
(2) If an application is rejected, the notification will include a brief explanation of the reasons for rejection. 
(3) Successful applicants will receive a grant agreement outlining the terms and conditions of the funding. 
(4) Failure to return a signed grant agreement within 30 days may result in the forfeiture of the awarded funds.

heading: Grant disbursement
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in two installments. 
(2) The first installment, amounting to 60% of the total awarded grant, will be transferred by March 15th. 
(3) The second installment, constituting the remaining 40%, will be disbursed upon receipt and approval of the final report, as detailed in section 12. 
(4) Funds will be transferred directly to the designated municipal bank account.

heading: Grant disbursement
text:
(1) Grant funds will be disbursed in two installments. 
(2) The first installment, amounting to 70% of the total awarded grant, will be transferred by March 15th. 
(3) The second installment, constituting the remaining 30%, will be disbursed upon receipt and approval of the final report, as detailed in section 12. 
(4) Funds will be transferred directly to the designated municipal bank account.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Municipalities receiving grants must submit a final report by September 30th of the year in which the grant was used. 
(2) The report must detail how the funds were expended, including invoices and receipts for all eligible costs. 
(3) It must also include a brief narrative on the impact of the grant on field quality and public access. 
(4) Failure to submit a satisfactory report may result in the withholding of the second installment and ineligibility for future grants for a period of two years.

heading: Audits and inspections
text: The Department of Public Recreation and Sport reserves the right to conduct audits of municipal records and on-site inspections of sporting fields that have received grant funding. These audits may occur at any time within two years of the grant disbursement. Municipalities must cooperate fully with auditors and inspectors, providing all requested documentation and access to facilities. Any discrepancies or misuse of funds identified during an audit may lead to repayment requirements.

heading: Misuse of funds
text:
(1) Any funds received under this Act must be used exclusively for the maintenance of the specified sporting field. 
(2) Use of grant funds for non-eligible expenses, or for purposes unrelated to the sporting field, constitutes misuse of funds. 
(3) In cases of misuse, the municipality will be required to repay the misused amount within 60 days. 
(4) Serious or repeated misuse may result in immediate revocation of current grants and permanent ineligibility for future funding under this Act.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A municipality may appeal a decision regarding grant eligibility, amount awarded, or repayment requirements within 45 days of receiving the decision notification. 
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Committee, which is separate from the initial review committee. 
(3) The Appeals Committee will review the original application and any additional information provided by the applicant. 
(4) The decision of the Appeals Committee is final and will be communicated within 90 days of receiving the appeal.

heading: Funding allocation for small municipalities
text: Municipalities with a population of less than 5,000 people are eligible for an additional 5% bonus on their calculated grant amount, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns per field. This provision aims to support smaller communities that may have more limited resources for field maintenance. This bonus is applied after the initial grant calculation but before the application of the total municipal grant cap. Evidence of population size must be submitted with the application.

heading: Funding allocation for small municipalities
text: Municipalities with a population of less than 7,500 people are eligible for an additional 7% bonus on their calculated grant amount, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns per field. This provision aims to support smaller communities that may have more limited resources for field maintenance. This bonus is applied after the initial grant calculation but before the application of the total municipal grant cap. Evidence of population size must be submitted with the application.

heading: Special consideration for multi-sport complexes
text: Multi-sport complexes, defined as facilities containing at least three distinct sporting fields, may apply for an aggregated grant. The maximum grant for such complexes is 75,000 crowns, provided each individual field within the complex meets all eligibility criteria. This provision acknowledges the increased maintenance demands of larger, more diverse facilities. A detailed breakdown of costs per field within the complex is still required in the application.

heading: Grant for essential equipment purchase
text: Up to 10% of a grant may be allocated for the purchase of essential maintenance equipment, such as mowers or line markers, provided the equipment's cost is justified by a long-term maintenance plan. The maximum amount for equipment purchase is capped at 7,000 crowns per field. This equipment must be directly and solely used for the maintenance of the public sporting field for which the grant was awarded. Proof of purchase is required in the final report.

heading: Grant for essential equipment purchase
text: Up to 15% of a grant may be allocated for the purchase of essential maintenance equipment, such as mowers, line markers, or irrigation system components, provided the equipment's cost is justified by a long-term maintenance plan. The maximum amount for equipment purchase is capped at 10,000 crowns per field. This equipment must be directly and solely used for the maintenance of the public sporting field for which the grant was awarded. Proof of purchase is required in the final report.

heading: Environmental sustainability bonus
text: Municipalities demonstrating the use of environmentally sustainable maintenance practices, such as rainwater harvesting for irrigation or organic fertilizers, may receive a 3% bonus on their grant. This bonus is capped at 2,000 crowns per field. Evidence of such practices, including supplier invoices or system specifications, must be submitted with the application. The goal is to encourage eco-friendly approaches to sporting field upkeep throughout Nordvale.

heading: Accessibility improvements bonus
text: An additional 2% bonus, up to 1,500 crowns per field, will be awarded to municipalities making verifiable improvements to field accessibility for all citizens. This includes, but is not limited to, creation of accessible pathways to fields or installation of accessible seating areas. Documentation of these improvements, such as architectural plans or completion certificates, must accompany the application. This incentive promotes inclusivity in sports and recreation.

heading: Training for maintenance staff
text: Costs associated with training municipal staff in best practices for sporting field maintenance are considered eligible for grant funding, up to 5% of the total grant amount. This includes registration fees for relevant courses or workshops. The maximum eligible amount for training is 2,500 crowns per municipality. This provision aims to enhance the expertise of local maintenance teams, leading to better long-term care of facilities across Nordvale.

heading: Maintenance standards
text: The Minister may, by regulation, prescribe minimum maintenance standards for sporting fields receiving grants. These standards will cover aspects such as grass height, drainage, and safety features. Adherence to these standards will be a condition for receiving and retaining grant funding. Municipalities are encouraged to consult these standards when developing their maintenance plans, ensuring a consistent level of quality across the republic.

heading: Renewal of grants
text: Grants are awarded on an annual basis, and municipalities must reapply each year to receive continued funding. There is no automatic renewal. However, municipalities with a proven track record of successful grant utilization and reporting may be given priority in subsequent application rounds, particularly if their fields demonstrate consistent improvement in condition and usage. This encourages continuous high standards.

heading: Collaboration with local sports clubs
text: Municipalities demonstrating effective collaboration with local sports clubs in the maintenance of public sporting fields may be viewed favorably during the application review process. Evidence of such collaboration could include joint maintenance agreements or shared resource initiatives. This encourages community engagement and shared responsibility for valuable public assets. A formal letter of support from a recognized sports club can be submitted.

heading: Emergency maintenance provisions
text: In exceptional circumstances, such as significant damage to a sporting field due to unforeseen weather events, a municipality may apply for an emergency maintenance grant outside the regular application cycle. These grants are capped at 20,000 crowns per incident and require immediate notification to the Department of Public Recreation and Sport, along with photographic evidence of the damage. Such grants are subject to available emergency funding.

heading: Public consultation requirements
text: Before submitting an application for a grant exceeding 25,000 crowns for a single field, municipalities are required to conduct a public consultation. This involves at least one public meeting or an online survey to gather feedback from residents and local sports organizations regarding the proposed maintenance plan. A summary of the consultation results must be included with the grant application, demonstrating community involvement in the planning process.

heading: Condition for use by youth organizations
text: A condition of receiving any grant under this Act is that the sporting field must be made available for use by youth sports organizations for at least 30% of its total available booking hours. This ensures that younger generations have adequate access to well-maintained facilities. Municipalities must provide documentation of this commitment in their application, such as agreements with youth clubs or a dedicated booking schedule.

heading: Penalty for non-compliance with reporting
text: Failure to submit the final report as stipulated in section 12 by the deadline will result in a penalty. The municipality will be ineligible to apply for any grants under this Act for the following fiscal year. Additionally, any outstanding second installment will be forfeited. Repeated non-compliance may lead to a three-year ineligibility period, emphasizing the importance of transparent and timely financial reporting.

heading: Minister's discretionary fund
text: The Minister may allocate up to 50,000 crowns annually from a discretionary fund to support exceptional projects or urgent maintenance needs that do not fully meet the standard criteria but align with the Act's overall purpose. These funds are intended for unique situations and are not subject to the regular application process. Decisions from this fund are made solely at the Minister's discretion, based on a written proposal.

heading: Publication of grant recipients
text: A list of all municipalities receiving grants, along with the awarded amounts and the specific sporting fields benefitting, will be published annually on the Department of Public Recreation and Sport's official website by February 28th. This ensures transparency and public accountability for the use of public funds. The publication will also include a brief summary of the intended use of the grant for each field.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act will be reviewed by a special parliamentary committee every five years to assess its effectiveness and make recommendations for amendments. The first review is scheduled for 2023. Public input will be invited as part of this review process. The goal is to ensure the Act remains relevant and continues to meet the evolving needs of Nordvale's sporting facilities and communities.

heading: Advisory panel establishment
text: An independent advisory panel, comprising five experts in sports management, public administration, and civil engineering, will be established to provide non-binding recommendations to the Minister regarding grant policy and field maintenance best practices. Panel members will serve three-year terms and meet quarterly. Their insights will contribute to the continuous improvement of the grant program and the quality of sporting fields across Nordvale.

heading: Coordination with other departments
text: The Department of Public Recreation and Sport will coordinate with the Department of Municipal Affairs to ensure that grant provisions align with broader municipal development plans and policies. This inter-departmental collaboration aims to create a cohesive approach to public infrastructure and resource allocation, preventing duplication of effort and maximizing the impact of public investment in sporting facilities throughout Nordvale.

heading: Grant for accessibility assessments
text: Municipalities may apply for a separate grant, up to 3,000 crowns, to conduct professional accessibility assessments of their sporting fields. This grant is intended to help identify barriers and plan for future accessibility improvements. The assessment must be carried out by a certified accessibility consultant, and a copy of their report must be submitted to the Department of Public Recreation and Sport for approval of the grant funds.

heading: Promotional activities
text: The Department of Public Recreation and Sport may engage in promotional activities to raise awareness of the Sporting Field Maintenance Grants Act among municipalities and the public. This could include informational workshops, online resources, and direct outreach to municipal councils. The goal is to maximize participation in the grant program and ensure that all eligible communities are aware of this valuable funding opportunity.

heading: Data collection and analysis
text: The Department of Public Recreation and Sport will collect and analyze data on grant applications, disbursements, and reported outcomes. This data will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the Act, identify trends in maintenance needs, and inform future policy adjustments. An annual summary of this data will be made publicly available, contributing to transparent governance and evidence-based decision-making.

heading: Amendments by regulation
text: The Minister may, by regulation, amend the specific crown amounts, percentages, or day counts mentioned in sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 25, 26, 27, and 35. Any such amendment must be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into effect. The power to amend by regulation is limited to numerical values and cannot alter the fundamental purpose or scope of this Act.

heading: Priority for fields with high usage
text: Sporting fields that can demonstrate exceptionally high public usage, exceeding 300 days per year or serving over 5,000 unique users annually, may receive priority consideration during the grant allocation process. This preference acknowledges the increased wear and tear on heavily utilized facilities and aims to maintain them to a high standard for the benefit of a larger number of citizens. Documentation of usage statistics must be robust.

heading: Support for new sporting fields
text: New public sporting fields, completed within the last two years, are eligible for an enhanced grant in their first two years of operation. They can receive up to 80% of their documented eligible maintenance costs, up to a maximum of 40,000 crowns per field, provided all other eligibility criteria are met. This aims to provide initial support as these new facilities establish their maintenance routines and budgets.

heading: Support for new sporting fields
text: New public sporting fields, completed within the last three years, are eligible for an enhanced grant in their first three years of operation. They can receive up to 85% of their documented eligible maintenance costs, up to a maximum of 45,000 crowns per field, provided all other eligibility criteria are met. This aims to provide initial support as these new facilities establish their maintenance routines and budgets.

heading: Repeal of section 38
text: Section 38, pertaining to the requirements for digital submission of applications, is hereby repealed as of January 1, 2027. All applications must be submitted in hard copy only after this date. This change reflects a shift in departmental policy concerning digital infrastructure. The previous requirement for digital submission had become incompatible with updated internal data security protocols.

heading: Repeal of section 38
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Application for multiple fields
text: A municipality applying for grants for multiple sporting fields must submit a consolidated application that lists all fields and their individual maintenance plans. While each field is assessed separately, the consolidated application streamlines the administrative process for both the applicant and the Department. A minimum of two fields must be included for a consolidated application, and the total number of fields in such an application cannot exceed ten.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on January 1st, 2018. Applications for grants for the fiscal year commencing on April 1st, 2018, may be submitted from this date. The Minister is authorized to make any necessary transitional regulations to ensure the smooth implementation of this Act and its provisions from its commencement date. All relevant forms and guidelines will be made available to municipalities by the end of 2017.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) If a person is a certified bookbinder, then they shall receive 5 crowns instead of a delivered meal. (2) This payment shall be made for up to six days per week.

heading: Payment terms
text: A registered accredited sign-language interpreter has an additional 30 days to pay the annual electric bicycle registration fee of 30 crowns.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: (1) If a person is a registered cartographer, (2) the price of a single lottery ticket shall be zero crowns.

heading: Officials in charge of play
text:
(1) In every Act, 'enrolled adjudicator' means a person who is entered on the officiating roll kept by the recognised association of a sport and who, in the preceding calendar year, controlled at least twelve competitive fixtures as the controller in charge.
(2) The recognised association of a sport is the body that organises that sport for the whole of the country. The controller in charge is the person who starts and stops play and enforces the rules during the fixture; a person who merely assists the controller in charge, for example by signalling from the edge of the playing area, does not control a fixture.
(3) A fixture is competitive if it forms part of a season-long competition with a table of standings, or of a competition decided by elimination, organised by a recognised association of a sport or by an international grouping of such associations; a friendly fixture is not competitive.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the responsibilities and procedures for the repair and maintenance of public street furniture within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all street furniture located on public land or public thoroughfares, including benches, public bins, public information boards, and decorative planters. The primary aim is to ensure public safety, aesthetic quality, and functionality of these essential civic assets. This Act does not cover private property or furniture not accessible to the general public.

heading: Definition of street furniture
text: For the purposes of this Act, 'street furniture' includes, but is not limited to, items such as public benches, waste receptacles, public signposts (excluding traffic signs), decorative bollards, public drinking fountains, and communal garden beds within public spaces. It also encompasses shelters for public transport users, provided they are not privately owned or maintained by a specific transport operator. Any object installed on public land that serves a civic purpose for the general public's convenience or aesthetic enjoyment is generally considered street furniture under this definition.

heading: Responsibility for repair by municipality
text: Each municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, is primarily responsible for the repair and maintenance of all street furniture within its geographical boundaries. This responsibility extends to regular inspections, proactive maintenance, and timely repairs following damage reports. Municipalities must allocate a minimum of 25,000 crowns annually for these purposes. Failure to meet these obligations may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Responsibility for repair by municipality
text: Each municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, is primarily responsible for the repair and maintenance of all street furniture within its geographical boundaries. This responsibility extends to regular inspections, proactive maintenance, and timely repairs following damage reports. Municipalities must allocate a minimum of 35,000 crowns annually for these purposes. Failure to meet these obligations may result in a fine of up to 7,500 crowns per incident, with a maximum cumulative fine of 25,000 crowns per quarter.

heading: Reporting damage to street furniture
text: Any member of the public may report damaged street furniture to the relevant municipal authority.
