Reports can be made via a dedicated municipal hotline, a website portal, or in person at municipal offices. All reports must include the approximate location of the damaged item and a brief description of the damage. Anonymous reports are accepted, but contact information is encouraged for follow-up. Municipalities must acknowledge receipt of a report within 2 business days.

heading: Reporting damage to street furniture
text: Any member of the public may report damaged street furniture to the relevant municipal authority. Reports can be made via a dedicated municipal hotline (operational 24/7), a website portal, or in person at municipal offices during business hours. All reports must include the approximate location of the damaged item, a brief description of the damage, and optionally, a photograph. Anonymous reports are accepted, but contact information is encouraged for follow-up. Municipalities must acknowledge receipt of a report within 24 hours and provide a unique reference number.

heading: Emergency repairs
text: Damage posing an immediate risk to public safety, such as structurally unsound benches, broken glass from information boards, or heavily corroded metalwork, must be categorised as an 'emergency repair'. Municipalities are required to address emergency repairs within 48 hours of a report being received. This includes making the area safe, removing the hazard, or implementing temporary measures until a permanent repair can be completed. Failure to respond within this timeframe for an emergency repair may incur a penalty of 1,000 crowns per hour of delay, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency repairs
text: Damage posing an immediate risk to public safety, such as structurally unsound benches, sharp edges from broken furniture, or heavily corroded metalwork, must be categorised as an 'emergency repair'. Municipalities are required to address emergency repairs within 24 hours of a report being received. This includes making the area safe, removing the hazard, or implementing temporary measures until a permanent repair can be completed. Failure to respond within this timeframe for an emergency repair may incur a penalty of 1,500 crowns per hour of delay, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Non-emergency repairs
text: Damage not posing an immediate risk to public safety, such as graffiti, minor aesthetic damage, or a non-functional public bin, is categorised as a 'non-emergency repair'. Municipalities are required to complete non-emergency repairs within 14 calendar days of a report being received. If a repair cannot be completed within this period, the municipality must notify the reporting party (if contact details were provided) and provide an estimated completion date, which must not exceed an additional 7 days. Repeated delays for the same item may lead to an investigation.

heading: Regular inspection schedule
text: Each municipality must establish and adhere to a regular inspection schedule for all street furniture within its jurisdiction. This schedule must ensure that all public benches, bins, and information boards are inspected at least once every 3 months. Other items, such as decorative planters and bollards, must be inspected at least once every 6 months. Records of these inspections, including dates and findings, must be maintained for a minimum of 2 years and be available for review by the public upon request, subject to a 5-crown administrative fee per request.

heading: Maintenance standards for wooden furniture
text: Wooden street furniture, such as benches and planters, must be treated with a weather-resistant protective coating at least once every 18 months. Any splintering, significant cracks, or rot exceeding 5 centimetres in length must be repaired or the item replaced. Fasteners must be checked for security every 6 months. The timber used for repairs must be of a quality comparable to the original, or superior, and sourced sustainably where possible. Replacement parts must match the original design to maintain aesthetic consistency.

heading: Maintenance standards for metal furniture
text: Metal street furniture, including waste receptacles and signposts, must be inspected for corrosion, structural integrity, and sharp edges at least once every 6 months. Any signs of rust covering an area larger than 10 square centimetres must be treated and repainted. Loose or missing bolts, welds, or other fixings must be secured or replaced within 7 days of detection. All metal components must be free from sharp protrusions that could cause injury. The metal used for repairs must be galvanised or otherwise treated to resist corrosion.

heading: Maintenance standards for metal furniture
text: Metal street furniture, including waste receptacles and signposts, must be inspected for corrosion, structural integrity, and sharp edges at least once every 4 months. Any signs of rust covering an area larger than 5 square centimetres must be treated and repainted. Loose or missing bolts, welds, or other fixings must be secured or replaced within 3 days of detection. All metal components must be free from sharp protrusions that could cause injury. The metal used for repairs must be galvanised or otherwise treated to resist corrosion, and be at least 3mm thick.

heading: Maintenance standards for concrete furniture
text: Concrete street furniture, such as heavy planters or seating blocks, must be inspected for cracks, chips, and structural stability at least once a year. Cracks exceeding 3 millimetres in width or 10 centimetres in length must be filled and sealed to prevent water ingress and further deterioration. Any loose or unstable concrete items must be re-secured or replaced immediately if they pose a tipping hazard. Surface finishes should be maintained to prevent spalling and preserve appearance. Repairs must use high-strength concrete.

heading: Graffiti removal
text: Graffiti on street furniture must be removed by the responsible municipality within 7 calendar days of being reported or detected during an inspection. If the graffiti is deemed offensive or hateful, it must be removed within 24 hours. The removal method must be appropriate for the material of the street furniture and must not cause further damage or discolouration. Records of graffiti incidents and removal dates must be kept for a period of 1 year. Repeated incidents at the same location may necessitate enhanced surveillance.

heading: Graffiti removal
text: Graffiti on street furniture must be removed by the responsible municipality within 5 calendar days of being reported or detected during an inspection. If the graffiti is deemed offensive or hateful, it must be removed within 12 hours. The removal method must be appropriate for the material of the street furniture and must not cause further damage or discolouration. Records of graffiti incidents and removal dates must be kept for a period of 2 years. Repeated incidents at the same location within 6 months will trigger an assessment for anti-graffiti coatings.

heading: Cleaning of street furniture
text: All public street furniture, especially benches and public bins, must be cleaned regularly to ensure hygiene and aesthetic appeal. Benches and waste receptacles must be cleaned at least once every 2 weeks. Public information boards should be cleaned at least once a month to ensure visibility of notices. Cleaning must involve appropriate detergents and methods that do not damage the materials. The surrounding area within a 1-meter radius of the furniture should also be kept free of litter and debris.

heading: Replacement of damaged furniture
text: If a piece of street furniture is beyond repair or its repair cost exceeds 70% of the cost of a new item, it must be replaced. Replacement must occur within 30 calendar days of the decision that the item is irreparable. The new item must be of a similar design and quality to the original, and fit for purpose. Municipalities must maintain an inventory of spare parts or readily available replacement items to minimise delays. A temporary placeholder, such as a barrier, should be installed if a full replacement takes longer than 7 days.

heading: Funding for repairs and maintenance
text: Funding for street furniture repair and maintenance shall primarily come from municipal budgets. The national government will provide a supplementary grant of 5,000 crowns to each municipality annually for this purpose. Municipalities may also seek additional funding through local initiatives or community partnerships. A minimum of 10% of the allocated municipal budget for street furniture must be reserved for unforeseen emergency repairs. Financial records pertaining to these expenditures must be audited biannually.

heading: Funding for repairs and maintenance
text: Funding for street furniture repair and maintenance shall primarily come from municipal budgets. The national government will provide a supplementary grant of 7,500 crowns to each municipality annually for this purpose. Municipalities may also seek additional funding through local initiatives or community partnerships. A minimum of 15% of the allocated municipal budget for street furniture must be reserved for unforeseen emergency repairs. Financial records pertaining to these expenditures must be audited annually by an independent body, with results published online within 30 days of audit completion.

heading: Public consultation on new furniture
text: Before installing new street furniture in a public space, municipalities must conduct a public consultation process if the total cost exceeds 10,000 crowns or if more than 3 items are to be installed. This includes publishing proposals online for 21 days and holding at least one public meeting. Public feedback must be considered before final decisions are made. The consultation process is not required for like-for-like replacements of existing furniture.

heading: Accessibility standards
text: All new street furniture installed, and where practical, repaired existing furniture, must comply with national accessibility standards. This includes ensuring public benches have adequate backrests and armrests, public information boards are at an accessible height (between 90 cm and 160 cm from the ground), and pathways to furniture are clear and at least 120 cm wide. Any changes or repairs must not create new barriers or reduce existing accessibility. A minimum of 20% of public benches in each municipality must meet these standards by 2028.

heading: Accessibility standards
text: All new street furniture installed, and where practical, repaired existing furniture, must comply with national accessibility standards. This includes ensuring public benches have adequate backrests and armrests, public information boards are at an accessible height (between 80 cm and 150 cm from the ground), and pathways to furniture are clear and at least 150 cm wide. Any changes or repairs must not create new barriers or reduce existing accessibility. A minimum of 30% of public benches in each municipality must meet these standards by 2028, and 50% by 2030.

heading: Vandalism and deliberate damage
text: Acts of vandalism or deliberate damage to street furniture are considered criminal offenses. Municipalities must report such incidents to the local constabulary if the damage exceeds 1,000 crowns or involves persistent defacement. The cost of repair or replacement due to vandalism may be recovered from the perpetrator if apprehended and convicted. Public awareness campaigns regarding the importance of street furniture and the consequences of damaging it should be conducted annually by each municipality.

heading: Contractor engagement
text: Municipalities may engage external contractors for the repair and maintenance of street furniture. All contractors must be appropriately licensed and insured. Contracts must specify adherence to the standards outlined in this Act, including response times and material quality. The municipality remains ultimately responsible for ensuring compliance with this Act, regardless of whether the work is performed by internal staff or external contractors. Penalties for non-compliance may be passed on to contractors if specified in their contracts.

heading: Record keeping
text: Each municipality must maintain comprehensive records of all street furniture, including its location, installation date, material, and a history of inspections, repairs, and replacements. These records must be digital and updated within 5 business days of any action. They should also include details of reported damage, the date of report, and the resolution date. These records are subject to inspection by the national oversight committee at any time, with 48 hours' notice.

heading: Record keeping
text: Each municipality must maintain comprehensive records of all street furniture, including its unique identification number, precise GPS location, installation date, material, and a history of inspections, repairs, and replacements. These records must be digital, publicly accessible (excluding personal data), and updated within 2 business days of any action. They should also include details of reported damage, the date of report, the resolution date, and associated costs. These records are subject to inspection by the national oversight committee at any time, with 24 hours' notice.

heading: Public information boards
text: Public information boards must be kept clear of outdated notices, commercial advertisements (unless specifically approved), and defacement. Notices should be reviewed and removed if older than 30 days, unless they pertain to ongoing events or official municipal announcements. The display surface must be cleaned weekly. The maximum size for a single notice is A4 (21 x 29.7 cm), and stapling directly to the board structure is prohibited; only designated pinning areas should be used.

heading: Public waste receptacles
text: Public waste receptacles must be emptied at least twice a week. In high-traffic areas, they must be emptied daily, or when they are 80% full, whichever comes first. Receptacles must be regularly disinfected and kept free from unpleasant odours. Damaged bins that cannot be securely closed or are leaking must be repaired or replaced within 3 days. A minimum of one public waste receptacle must be available for every 200 meters of pedestrian thoroughfare in commercial zones.

heading: Benches and seating
text: Public benches must be structurally sound and free from sharp edges or splinters. They should be installed on stable, level ground. Any bench with a missing or damaged slat, or a structural component that reduces its load-bearing capacity by more than 20%, must be repaired within 10 days. The surface of the seating area should be cleaned weekly. A minimum of one public bench must be provided for every 100 meters of public park pathways.

heading: Benches and seating
text: Public benches must be structurally sound and free from sharp edges or splinters. They should be installed on stable, level ground. Any bench with a missing or damaged slat, or a structural component that reduces its load-bearing capacity by more than 10%, must be repaired within 7 days. The surface of the seating area should be cleaned twice weekly. A minimum of one public bench must be provided for every 75 meters of public park pathways, and every 150 meters in urban commercial areas.

heading: Decorative planters
text: Decorative planters must be maintained in good condition, free from structural cracks or instability. Plants within them must be kept healthy, watered regularly, and replaced if dead or diseased. Litter and weeds must be removed from planters at least once a week. The surrounding area must be kept clear of soil spillages. Any planter damaged to the extent it can no longer hold soil or plants effectively must be repaired or replaced within 21 days.

heading: Public drinking fountains
text: Public drinking fountains must be functional, clean, and provide potable water. Water quality tests must be conducted monthly. Any fountain found to be non-functional, leaking, or delivering discoloured water must be immediately taken out of service and repaired within 5 business days. The surrounding area must be kept free of standing water. All fountains must be operational between April 1st and October 31st each year.

heading: Public drinking fountains
text: Public drinking fountains must be functional, clean, and provide potable water. Water quality tests must be conducted bi-weekly. Any fountain found to be non-functional, leaking, or delivering discoloured water must be immediately taken out of service and repaired within 3 business days. The surrounding area must be kept free of standing water and algae. All fountains must be operational between March 15th and November 15th each year, subject to freezing conditions.

heading: Signposts and wayfinding
text: Public signposts, including wayfinding signs and information pillars, must be kept legible and free from damage or obstruction. Any sign that is faded, broken, or pointing in the wrong direction must be rectified within 14 days. The posts must be stable and free from significant corrosion or rot. The height of sign panels must be between 200 cm and 250 cm from the ground to ensure visibility for pedestrians. Reflective properties should be maintained for visibility in low light.

heading: Street art installations (municipal)
text: Street art installations commissioned or maintained by the municipality are considered street furniture for the purposes of this Act. They must be inspected quarterly for structural integrity, public safety hazards, and aesthetic condition. Any damage, including graffiti not part of the original artwork, must be repaired within 21 days. Significant damage or deterioration that compromises the artistic intent or safety requires expert consultation for repair or removal, with a decision made within 45 days.

heading: Environmental considerations for materials
text: When replacing or installing new street furniture, municipalities are encouraged to use environmentally sustainable materials where practicable. This includes recycled content, sustainably sourced timber, and materials with a low environmental impact during manufacturing and disposal. Preference should be given to materials with a projected lifespan of at least 15 years. Any chemical treatments or paints used must be non-toxic and environmentally safe.

heading: Training for maintenance staff
text: All municipal staff involved in the inspection, repair, or maintenance of street furniture must receive appropriate training. This training should cover safety procedures, repair techniques for various materials, and the specific standards outlined in this Act. Refresher training must be provided at least every 3 years. A minimum of 8 hours of dedicated training per year per staff member is recommended. Untrained staff are prohibited from performing complex repairs.

heading: Training for maintenance staff
text: All municipal staff involved in the inspection, repair, or maintenance of street furniture must receive appropriate training. This training should cover safety procedures, repair techniques for various materials, and the specific standards outlined in this Act. Refresher training must be provided at least every 2 years. A minimum of 12 hours of dedicated training per year per staff member is mandatory. Untrained staff are prohibited from performing complex repairs, and their work must be supervised by a certified technician for simple tasks.

heading: Public awareness campaigns
text: Each municipality must conduct at least one public awareness campaign annually to inform citizens about their role in reporting damage, the importance of street furniture, and responsible use. These campaigns can utilise local media, municipal websites, and community events. Information on how to report damage, including contact details for the municipal hotline, should be clearly displayed in public areas and updated quarterly.

heading: Appeals process for citizens
text: Citizens who believe a municipality has failed to meet its duties under this Act may lodge an appeal with a designated municipal ombudsman. The ombudsman must acknowledge the appeal within 5 business days and provide a resolution within 30 days. If the citizen is not satisfied with the ombudsman's decision, they may escalate the matter to the national oversight committee established under section 32. All appeals must be in writing.

heading: Annual performance review
text: Each municipality must submit an annual performance report to the national oversight committee by January 31st each year. This report must detail: (a) the number of damage reports received and resolved, (b) average response times for emergency and non-emergency repairs, (c) total expenditure on street furniture maintenance, and (d) a summary of inspection findings. The report must be made publicly available on the municipal website within 7 days of submission.

heading: Annual performance review
text: Each municipality must submit an annual performance report to the national oversight committee by January 15th each year. This report must detail: (a) the number of damage reports received and resolved, categorised by furniture type, (b) average response times for emergency and non-emergency repairs, (c) total expenditure on street furniture maintenance, broken down by repair type and material, (d) a summary of inspection findings and actions taken, and (e) citizen satisfaction feedback. The report must be made publicly available on the municipal website within 3 days of submission.

heading: National oversight committee
text: A national oversight committee, consisting of 5 members appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure, shall be established to monitor compliance with this Act. The committee will review municipal performance reports, investigate escalated appeals, and issue recommendations or penalties for non-compliance. The committee meets quarterly and its decisions are binding on municipalities, subject to judicial review. Committee members serve 3-year terms.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text: Municipalities failing to comply with the duties outlined in this Act may face penalties. For each instance of non-compliance, a fine of between 500 crowns and 10,000 crowns may be levied by the national oversight committee, depending on the severity and impact of the breach. Persistent non-compliance, defined as 3 or more breaches within a 12-month period, may result in a reduction of up to 15% in the annual national grant allocated under section 14. All fines collected will be reinvested into a national street furniture improvement fund.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure at least once every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The first review must commence no later than January 1, 2023. Public input will be sought during these reviews. Any proposed amendments or updates will be presented to the national assembly for consideration. The review process will include an assessment of technological advancements in street furniture design and maintenance.

heading: Confidentiality of reporting
text: The identity of individuals reporting damaged street furniture shall be kept confidential by municipal authorities, unless express consent for disclosure is given by the reporting party. Contact details provided for follow-up purposes will only be used for communication related to the reported incident. Municipalities must ensure their data handling practices comply with national privacy regulations. No personal data of reporters may be shared with third-party contractors without explicit consent.

heading: Application to Private Entities
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Payment terms
text: For a certified falconry instructor, the annual home business permit fee is reduced by half.

heading: Recognised trades
text: No document copy fee is payable by a registered calligrapher for half the amount that would otherwise be due under FDA §38.

heading: Kerbside refuse tariff
text:
(1) In every Act, "kerbside refuse tariff" means the sum invoiced once a year for regularly taking away the residual refuse of a dwelling, graded by the volume of the receptacle that the dwelling uses.
(2) The kerbside refuse tariff does not include the price of taking away bulky items, interest on late payment or any penalty.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the licensing of individuals engaged in security guard activities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all security personnel meet minimum standards of training, conduct, and professional integrity. The scope of this Act extends to all persons who, for remuneration, provide security services, including but not limited to guarding property, monitoring premises, or controlling access, in any municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. It ensures public safety and maintains a regulated environment for security operations across the nation.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Security guard' means an individual who performs any security function as defined in subsection (2) for a fee or wage.
(2) 'Security function' includes, but is not limited to, patrolling premises, monitoring security cameras, controlling entry and exit points, and responding to alarms or disturbances to protect property or individuals. 
(3) 'Licensing Authority' refers to the designated governmental body responsible for issuing and managing security guard licenses.
(4) 'Applicant' means an individual applying for a security guard license or its renewal.
(5) 'Serious offence' refers to any criminal offence punishable by imprisonment for a term of 12 months or more.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text:
(1) No individual shall act as a security guard in the Republic of Nordvale unless that individual holds a valid security guard licence issued by the Licensing Authority in accordance with this Act.
(2) An individual found operating as a security guard without a valid licence shall be subject to a fine of 1,500 crowns for a first offence.
(3) For subsequent offences, the fine shall increase to 3,000 crowns.
(4) Employers who knowingly employ unlicensed security guards may also face penalties as outlined in section 35.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text:
(1) No individual shall act as a security guard in the Republic of Nordvale unless that individual holds a valid security guard licence issued by the Licensing Authority in accordance with this Act.
(2) An individual found operating as a security guard without a valid licence shall be subject to a fine of 2,000 crowns for a first offence.
(3) For subsequent offences, the fine shall increase to 4,000 crowns.
(4) Employers who knowingly employ unlicensed security guards may also face penalties as outlined in section 35.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a security guard licence must be submitted to the Licensing Authority on the prescribed form.
(2) The application form must be accompanied by all required documentation, including proof of age, citizenship or legal residency, and successful completion of mandated training.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns must be paid at the time of submission.
(4) Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days, requiring resubmission with all missing information.
(5) The Licensing Authority will process complete applications within 60 days of receipt.

heading: Eligibility Criteria
text:
(1) To be eligible for a security guard licence, an applicant must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) The applicant must be a citizen of Nordvale or hold a valid permanent residency permit.
(3) The applicant must have successfully completed the mandatory basic security guard training program approved by the Licensing Authority.
(4) The applicant must not have been convicted of a serious offence within the past 5 years.
(5) The applicant must pass a criminal record check conducted by the national police force.

heading: Mandatory Training Program
text:
(1) All applicants must complete a mandatory security guard training program comprising a minimum of 40 hours of instruction.
(2) The program curriculum must cover topics such as legal powers and limitations, emergency response, communication skills, and first aid.
(3) The training must be delivered by an institution approved by the Licensing Authority.
(4) Evidence of successful completion, including a certificate, must be submitted with the licence application.
(5) The program must include a practical component demonstrating proficiency in security procedures for at least 10 hours.

heading: Criminal Record Check
text:
(1) Every applicant for a security guard licence, or renewal of a licence, must undergo a criminal record check.
(2) The criminal record check will be conducted by the national police force of Nordvale.
(3) The cost of the criminal record check, up to a maximum of 100 crowns, shall be borne by the applicant.
(4) The Licensing Authority will reject any application where the criminal record check reveals a conviction for a serious offence within the last 5 years.
(5) Checks must be current, completed no more than 90 days prior to the application submission.

heading: Criminal Record Check
text:
(1) Every applicant for a security guard licence, or renewal of a licence, must undergo a criminal record check.
(2) The criminal record check will be conducted by the national police force of Nordvale.
(3) The cost of the criminal record check, up to a maximum of 120 crowns, shall be borne by the applicant.
(4) The Licensing Authority will reject any application where the criminal record check reveals a conviction for a serious offence within the last 7 years.
(5) Checks must be current, completed no more than 60 days prior to the application submission.

heading: Licence Issuance
text:
(1) Upon successful completion of all requirements, the Licensing Authority shall issue a security guard licence to the applicant.
(2) Each licence shall include a unique identification number, the licensee's full name, photograph, and expiry date.
(3) The licence shall be in a durable card format, approximately 85mm by 55mm.
(4) The Licensing Authority aims to issue licences within 30 days of approving an application.
(5) A licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue, unless suspended or revoked earlier.

heading: Licence Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A security guard licence is valid for a period of 3 years.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the current licence expires.
(3) The renewal process requires a new criminal record check and payment of a renewal fee of 200 crowns.
(4) Late renewal applications, submitted less than 90 days but more than 30 days before expiry, will incur an additional late fee of 50 crowns.
(5) Licences not renewed within 30 days of expiry will be considered lapsed, requiring a new application process.

heading: Display of Licence
text:
(1) A licensed security guard must visibly display their licence card while performing security functions.
(2) The licence card must be affixed to the outer clothing in such a way that it is clearly readable by any person who requests to see it.
(3) Failure to display the licence as required may result in a fine of 500 crowns.
(4) In specific circumstances where covert operations are authorized by law enforcement, this display requirement may be waived upon written approval from the Licensing Authority.
(5) The photograph on the licence must be clear and current, taken within the last 2 years.

heading: Display of Licence
text:
(1) A licensed security guard must visibly display their licence card while performing security functions.
(2) The licence card must be affixed to the outer clothing in such a way that it is clearly readable by any person who requests to see it.
(3) Failure to display the licence as required may result in a fine of 750 crowns.
(4) In specific circumstances where covert operations are authorized by law enforcement, this display requirement may be waived upon written approval from the Licensing Authority.
(5) The photograph on the licence must be clear and current, taken within the last 1 year.

heading: Change of Personal Details
text:
(1) A licence holder must notify the Licensing Authority of any change in their name, address, or contact information within 14 days of such change.
(2) Notification must be submitted in writing or through the online portal maintained by the Licensing Authority.
(3) Failure to notify the Authority of changes within the stipulated timeframe may result in a penalty of 100 crowns.
(4) A new licence card may be issued with updated details, incurring a re-issuance fee of 50 crowns.
(5) Outdated personal information on a licence card after 30 days of a change being made will be considered a breach of this section.

heading: Reporting Criminal Charges
text:
(1) A licence holder must report to the Licensing Authority if they are charged with any serious offence within 7 days of the charge being laid.
(2) Failure to report such charges may lead to immediate suspension of the licence pending investigation.
(3) This reporting requirement applies regardless of whether the offence occurred while on duty or off duty.
(4) The report must include details of the charge, the date of the incident, and the court handling the matter.
(5) A conviction for a serious offence may result in revocation of the licence as per section 14.

heading: Reporting Criminal Charges
text:
(1) A licence holder must report to the Licensing Authority if they are charged with any serious offence within 5 days of the charge being laid.
(2) Failure to report such charges may lead to immediate suspension of the licence pending investigation.
(3) This reporting requirement applies regardless of whether the offence occurred while on duty or off duty.
(4) The report must include details of the charge, the date of the incident, and the court handling the matter.
(5) A conviction for a serious offence may result in revocation of the licence as per section 14.

heading: Complaints Against Licence Holders
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall establish a process for receiving and investigating complaints against licensed security guards.
(2) All complaints must be submitted in writing and include details of the alleged misconduct.
(3) The Authority will acknowledge receipt of a complaint within 5 working days.
(4) Investigations will be completed within 90 days, wherever possible.
(5) Complainants will be notified of the outcome of the investigation and any disciplinary action taken.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may suspend a security guard licence if there is reasonable belief that the licence holder has committed a serious breach of this Act or is facing charges for a serious offence.
(2) A suspension may be immediate if the licence holder poses a direct threat to public safety.
(3) The licence holder must be provided with written notice of the suspension, including the reasons for it and the duration, within 24 hours.
(4) A suspended licence holder must cease all security guard activities immediately.
(5) Suspension periods may range from 30 days to 180 days, depending on the severity of the alleged infraction.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may suspend a security guard licence if there is reasonable belief that the licence holder has committed a serious breach of this Act or is facing charges for a serious offence.
(2) A suspension may be immediate if the licence holder poses a direct threat to public safety.
(3) The licence holder must be provided with written notice of the suspension, including the reasons for it and the duration, within 48 hours.
(4) A suspended licence holder must cease all security guard activities immediately.
(5) Suspension periods may range from 60 days to 270 days, depending on the severity of the alleged infraction.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may revoke a security guard licence if the licence holder is convicted of a serious offence.
(2) Revocation may also occur if the licence holder is found to have repeatedly or egregiously violated the provisions of this Act.
(3) A licence holder facing revocation shall be given an opportunity to present their case to the Licensing Authority, either in person or in writing, within 21 days of receiving notice.
(4) Upon revocation, the individual must surrender their licence card to the Authority within 7 days.
(5) An individual whose licence is revoked is ineligible to reapply for a period of 5 years.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant whose licence application is denied, or a licence holder whose licence is suspended or revoked, may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Tribunal.
(2) Notice of appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Licensing Authority's decision.
(3) The Appeals Tribunal shall review the decision and may uphold, overturn, or modify the original ruling.
(4) The Tribunal's decision is final, subject to judicial review by a court of competent jurisdiction.
(5) The appeal process typically takes 60 to 90 days to conclude.

heading: Continuing Professional Development
text:
(1) All licensed security guards are required to complete a minimum of 8 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every 2 years.
(2) Approved CPD activities include advanced training courses, workshops, or seminars relevant to security practices.
(3) Evidence of CPD completion must be submitted with renewal applications.
(4) Failure to meet CPD requirements may result in a refusal to renew the licence until the requirements are met.
(5) The Licensing Authority will publish a list of approved CPD providers and courses annually by January 15th.

heading: Continuing Professional Development
text:
(1) All licensed security guards are required to complete a minimum of 12 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every 2 years.
(2) Approved CPD activities include advanced training courses, workshops, or seminars relevant to security practices.
(3) Evidence of CPD completion must be submitted with renewal applications.
(4) Failure to meet CPD requirements may result in a refusal to renew the licence until the requirements are met.
(5) The Licensing Authority will publish a list of approved CPD providers and courses annually by January 15th.

heading: Use of Force
text:
(1) A security guard may use only such force as is reasonable and necessary in the circumstances to prevent harm to themselves or others, or to protect property.
(2) The use of excessive force is strictly prohibited and constitutes a serious breach of this Act.
(3) Any incident involving the use of force resulting in injury to a person must be reported to the Licensing Authority and the national police within 24 hours.
(4) Training on the use of force, including de-escalation techniques, must be included in the mandatory training program.
(5) A security guard's authority to use force is limited to what is permissible for any private citizen under Nordvale law.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Security guards must maintain strict confidentiality regarding all sensitive information obtained during the course of their duties.
(2) Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information is prohibited and may lead to disciplinary action, including licence suspension or revocation.
(3) This duty of confidentiality extends beyond the period of employment.
(4) Information may only be disclosed if required by law or with explicit consent from the relevant parties.
(5) Any breach of confidentiality resulting in harm to individuals or organizations may also result in civil liability.

heading: Reporting Unlawful Activity
text:
(1) A security guard who observes or becomes aware of any unlawful activity while on duty must report it to the national police and their employer without undue delay.
(2) Failure to report unlawful activity may be considered a breach of professional conduct and could lead to disciplinary action.
(3) This requirement applies to all locations including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.
(4) Reports should be made within a maximum of 2 hours for serious criminal acts.
(5) Internal reporting policies of security companies must align with this provision.

heading: Wearing of Uniforms
text:
(1) Unless engaged in specific duties requiring plain clothes, security guards must wear a uniform that clearly identifies them as security personnel.
(2) The uniform must include a visible company logo and the word 'SECURITY' or 'GUARD' in letters at least 2 cm high.
(3) The uniform must be distinct from any official national police or military uniform.
(4) Failure to wear the prescribed uniform may result in a fine of 300 crowns.
(5) Uniforms should be clean, presentable, and in good repair at all times.

heading: Prohibition of Impersonation
text:
(1) No individual, whether licensed or not, shall impersonate a police officer, military personnel, or any other public official while performing security functions.
(2) The wearing of uniforms or insignia that are deceptively similar to those of official authorities is strictly prohibited.
(3) Any act of impersonation is a serious offence and may result in immediate licence revocation and criminal charges.
(4) This prohibition extends to the use of terms or titles that might suggest official authority beyond that of a private security guard.
(5) Penalties for impersonation include fines of up to 5,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for up to 6 months.

heading: Restricted Activities
text:
(1) A security guard is prohibited from conducting personal investigations unrelated to their assigned duties.
(2) Security guards are not authorized to detain individuals for extended periods beyond what is immediately necessary to prevent a crime or deliver to lawful authority.
(3) The operation of surveillance equipment in private areas without consent or legal warrant is forbidden.
(4) Engaging in any activity that could be construed as infringing upon civil liberties without proper legal basis is strictly prohibited.
(5) These restrictions apply equally across all municipalities, including Dunmere, Elsby, and Fennick.

heading: Record Keeping by Licence Holders
text:
(1) Every licensed security guard must maintain accurate records of their work hours and assignments.
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of 2 years and be made available for inspection by the Licensing Authority upon request.
(3) Records should include dates, times, locations of duty, and any significant incidents that occurred.
(4) Failure to maintain proper records may result in a fine of 200 crowns.
(5) Digital record-keeping systems must ensure data integrity and secure storage.

heading: Employer Responsibilities
text:
(1) Any entity employing security guards must ensure that all their security personnel hold valid licences.
(2) Employers must maintain a register of all licensed security guards they employ, including licence numbers and expiry dates.
(3) This register must be updated monthly and be accessible to the Licensing Authority upon request.
(4) Employers are responsible for providing appropriate supervision and ensuring compliance with this Act by their employees.
(5) Failure to comply with these responsibilities may result in significant penalties as outlined in section 35.

heading: Reporting Employer Changes
text:
(1) A licence holder must notify the Licensing Authority within 7 days of commencing or terminating employment with a security company.
(2) This notification helps the Authority maintain an accurate database of active security personnel.
(3) The notification should include the name of the employer and the start or end date of employment.
(4) Failure to report employment changes within the specified timeframe may result in a warning or a minor administrative fine of 50 crowns.
(5) This requirement ensures proper oversight of the security industry across all regions, including Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Data Protection
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority shall ensure that all personal data collected from applicants and licence holders is handled in accordance with national data protection laws.
(2) Data will be stored securely and only accessed by authorized personnel for legitimate purposes related to this Act.
(3) Personal information will not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except where required by law.
(4) Licence holders have the right to request access to their personal data held by the Authority.
(5) Data related to lapsed or revoked licences will be archived after 10 years, in line with retention policies.

heading: Audits and Inspections
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may conduct periodic audits and inspections of security companies and individual licence holders to ensure compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspections may be conducted without prior notice, although reasonable efforts will be made to inform companies when possible.
(3) Licence holders and employers must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide access to all relevant documents and premises.
(4) Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence and may result in penalties.
(5) At least 5% of all licensed security guards will be randomly selected for audit annually.

heading: Audits and Inspections
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may conduct periodic audits and inspections of security companies and individual licence holders to ensure compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspections may be conducted without prior notice, although reasonable efforts will be made to inform companies when possible.
(3) Licence holders and employers must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide access to all relevant documents and premises.
(4) Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offence and may result in penalties.
(5) At least 8% of all licensed security guards will be randomly selected for audit annually.

heading: False Information
text:
(1) Providing false or misleading information in an application for a licence, or during any investigation conducted by the Licensing Authority, is an offence.
(2) Any licence obtained through the provision of false information shall be immediately revoked.
(3) Individuals found guilty of providing false information may face a fine of up to 4,000 crowns.
(4) This applies to all stages of interaction with the Licensing Authority, from initial application to renewal and complaint resolution.
(5) The Authority will investigate any discrepancies in submitted information with due diligence.

heading: Return of Lapsed/Revoked Licence
text:
(1) A licence holder whose licence has lapsed, been suspended, or revoked must return the physical licence card to the Licensing Authority within 7 days of the effective date of the lapse, suspension, or revocation.
(2) Failure to return the licence card as required may result in a fine of 200 crowns.
(3) The Authority will issue written instructions for the return of the card.
(4) Continued possession of a non-valid licence card after the specified period may lead to further penalties.
(5) The intent is to prevent the fraudulent use of invalid credentials in any of Nordvale's municipalities.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges specified in this Act are payable to the Licensing Authority.
(2) The application fee is 250 crowns, the renewal fee is 200 crowns, and the re-issuance fee for lost or damaged cards is 50 crowns.
(3) Fees are non-refundable unless an application is rejected due to administrative error by the Authority.
(4) The Licensing Authority may review and adjust fees every 3 years, with any changes published at least 90 days in advance.
(5) All payments must be made in crowns and can be processed via bank transfer or online payment portal.

heading: Fees and Charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges specified in this Act are payable to the Licensing Authority.
(2) The application fee is 300 crowns, the renewal fee is 250 crowns, and the re-issuance fee for lost or damaged cards is 75 crowns.
(3) Fees are non-refundable unless an application is rejected due to administrative error by the Authority.
(4) The Licensing Authority may review and adjust fees every 3 years, with any changes published at least 90 days in advance.
(5) All payments must be made in crowns and can be processed via bank transfer or online payment portal.

heading: Lost or Damaged Licence Cards
text:
(1) A licence holder must report the loss, theft, or damage of their licence card to the Licensing Authority within 48 hours of discovering the incident.
(2) A replacement card can be applied for by submitting a new photograph and paying a re-issuance fee of 50 crowns.
(3) The licence holder must provide a sworn statement detailing the circumstances of the loss, theft, or damage.
(4) Operating as a security guard with a lost or damaged licence, without having reported it and applied for a replacement, may result in a fine of 150 crowns.
(5) A temporary paper licence may be issued pending the arrival of the new card, valid for 30 days.

heading: Cooperation with Law Enforcement
text:
(1) Licensed security guards are expected to cooperate fully with national police and other law enforcement agencies in the performance of their duties.
(2) This includes providing assistance and information when requested, as long as it does not compromise personal safety or confidentiality unless legally mandated.
(3) Obstructing a law enforcement officer in the execution of their duties is a serious offence.
(4) Security guards should be trained in the protocols for interaction with police, ensuring clear communication.
(5) Joint exercises between security companies and local police forces are encouraged to foster better cooperation.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) This Act does not apply to individuals employed solely for internal security within their own organization, provided their duties do not extend beyond the confines of their employer's property and they do not provide services to third parties.
(2) Volunteers providing security services for non-profit community events for less than 7 days per year are also exempt.
(3) National police officers, military personnel, and other public officials acting in their official capacity are exempt.
(4) Any individual claiming an exemption must be able to demonstrate their eligibility upon request.
(5) The Licensing Authority may grant temporary exemptions in extraordinary circumstances, not exceeding 30 days.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) This Act does not apply to individuals employed solely for internal security within their own organization, provided their duties do not extend beyond the confines of their employer's property and they do not provide services to third parties.
(2) Volunteers providing security services for non-profit community events for less than 5 days per year are also exempt.
(3) National police officers, military personnel, and other public officials acting in their official capacity are exempt.
(4) Any individual claiming an exemption must be able to demonstrate their eligibility upon request.
(5) The Licensing Authority may grant temporary exemptions in extraordinary circumstances, not exceeding 21 days.

heading: Powers of the Licensing Authority
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority has the power to issue, suspend, revoke, and renew security guard licences.
(2) It may conduct investigations into alleged breaches of this Act and impose penalties.
(3) The Authority is authorized to establish and update training standards and approve training providers.
(4) It has the power to collect fees and charges as stipulated in this Act.
(5) The Authority may issue guidelines and directives to ensure consistent interpretation and application of the Act's provisions across all municipalities.

heading: Penalties for Individuals
text:
(1) An individual found in breach of this Act, where no specific penalty is mentioned, may be subject to a fine of up to 1,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second offence of the same nature, the fine may increase to 2,500 crowns.
(3) Repeated or serious breaches may lead to licence suspension or revocation.
(4) These penalties are in addition to any criminal charges that may be laid.
(5) The Licensing Authority maintains a record of all penalties imposed on licence holders for a period of 7 years.

heading: Penalties for Individuals
text:
(1) An individual found in breach of this Act, where no specific penalty is mentioned, may be subject to a fine of up to 1,200 crowns for a first offence.
(2) For a second offence of the same nature, the fine may increase to 3,000 crowns.
(3) Repeated or serious breaches may lead to licence suspension or revocation.
(4) These penalties are in addition to any criminal charges that may be laid.
(5) The Licensing Authority maintains a record of all penalties imposed on licence holders for a period of 7 years.

heading: Penalties for Employers
text:
(1) An employer found to be employing unlicensed security guards or failing to comply with their responsibilities under this Act may be subject to a fine of up to 5,000 crowns for a first offence.
(2) Subsequent offences may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns.
(3) The Licensing Authority may also issue public warnings or directives to non-compliant employers.
(4) In severe cases of persistent non-compliance, the Authority may refer the matter for legal prosecution.
(5) Employers must ensure at least 95% of their security staff are always in compliance.

heading: Penalties for Employers
text:
(1) An employer found to be employing unlicensed security guards or failing to comply with their responsibilities under this Act may be subject to a fine of up to 7,500 crowns for a first offence.
(2) Subsequent offences may result in fines of up to 15,000 crowns.
(3) The Licensing Authority may also issue public warnings or directives to non-compliant employers.
(4) In severe cases of persistent non-compliance, the Authority may refer the matter for legal prosecution.
(5) Employers must ensure at least 98% of their security staff are always in compliance.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority may make regulations consistent with this Act for its effective implementation.
(2) Such regulations may prescribe additional training requirements, codes of conduct, or specific operational guidelines for security guards.
(3) All proposed regulations must undergo a 30-day public consultation period before being enacted.
(4) Regulations will be published in the Official Gazette of Nordvale and on the Licensing Authority's website.
(5) Any regulation made will come into effect 14 days after its official publication, unless otherwise specified.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Individuals operating as security guards prior to the enactment of this Act shall have a period of 180 days from the effective date to apply for a licence.
(2) During this transitional period, existing security guards may continue to operate, provided they submit a complete application within the first 90 days.
(3) The Licensing Authority will prioritize applications from existing security guards to facilitate a smooth transition.
(4) Training exemptions may be granted to experienced guards with a minimum of 5 years of service, subject to assessment.
(5) After the 180-day period, all security guards must hold a valid licence as per section 3.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Licensing Authority and relevant stakeholders every 5 years from its effective date.
(2) The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act, identify any areas for improvement, and ensure it remains relevant to the evolving security landscape.
(3) A report detailing the findings of the review and any proposed amendments shall be submitted to the government within 6 months of the review commencing.
(4) Public feedback will be sought during the review process.
(5) The first review will commence on 2023-01-01.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Licensing Authority and relevant stakeholders every 4 years from its effective date.
(2) The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act, identify any areas for improvement, and ensure it remains relevant to the evolving security landscape.
(3) A report detailing the findings of the review and any proposed amendments shall be submitted to the government within 5 months of the review commencing.
(4) Public feedback will be sought during the review process.
(5) The next review will commence on 2028-01-01.

heading: Enforcement
text:
(1) The Licensing Authority is responsible for the overall enforcement of this Act.
(2) Enforcement actions may include issuing warnings, imposing fines, and initiating suspension or revocation proceedings.
(3) The Authority may delegate certain enforcement functions to authorized officers.
(4) Collaboration with the national police force is essential for effective enforcement, particularly in cases involving criminal activity.
(5) All enforcement decisions will be made fairly, consistently, and transparently, with due regard for the rights of all parties involved.

heading: Effective Date
text:
(1) This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018.
(2) The Licensing Authority will publish all necessary forms and guidelines at least 60 days prior to this date.
(3) This early publication ensures all stakeholders, including individuals and businesses in municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik, have ample time to prepare for compliance.
(4) Any regulations made under section 36 will also specify their own effective dates, which may be concurrent with or subsequent to this Act's effective date.
(5) Preparatory work for the implementation of this Act, such as establishing the Licensing Authority's operational procedures, began on 2017-07-01.

heading: Jurisdiction
text:
(1) This Act applies uniformly across all territories and municipalities of the Republic of Nordvale.
(2) This includes the capital city of Aldmark, as well as Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(3) Any legal proceedings arising from this Act shall be heard in the courts of Nordvale.
(4) The Licensing Authority's decisions are binding throughout the Republic, subject to the appeals process outlined in section 16.
(5) No municipal by-laws may contradict or undermine the provisions of this national Act.

heading: General Conduct
text:
(1) A security guard must at all times conduct themselves with professionalism, integrity, and respect for the public.
(2) They must not engage in any behaviour that brings the security profession into disrepute.
(3) Harassment, discrimination, or abusive language is strictly prohibited.
(4) Licence holders are expected to be courteous and helpful to members of the public, while maintaining their security duties.
(5) Breaches of general conduct may lead to warnings, fines of up to 500 crowns, or disciplinary action depending on severity.

heading: Swimming practice for rescue volunteers
text:
(1) An active rescue volunteer is admitted to a public swimming pool without paying the admission fee.
(2) Subsection (1) covers single visits only; a monthly or annual pass for a swimming pool is not covered by this section.
(3) The volunteer shows the yearly statement of the lifeboat station at the entrance.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the comprehensive permitting process for the drilling of new water wells within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all individuals, organizations, and corporations intending to drill a water well for any purpose, including domestic, agricultural, or industrial use. The Act ensures that all drilling activities adhere to strict environmental protection standards and responsible water resource management practices across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity may commence the drilling of a water well anywhere in Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Water Well Drilling Permit from the Department of Water Resources. This requirement applies to all new well constructions and does not cover the repair or maintenance of existing wells, provided such activities do not involve deepening the well or significantly altering its diameter. Any drilling initiated without a permit is subject to penalties as outlined in section 30.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a Water Well Drilling Permit must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources. The application must include all required forms, supporting documentation, and the non-refundable application fee. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days, delaying the review process. Applications can be submitted electronically or in person at the Aldmark office.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required for each Water Well Drilling Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. Payment must be made at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant. No exemptions from this fee are permitted.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is required for each Water Well Drilling Permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. Payment must be made at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant. Certain agricultural wells may be eligible for a 50% reduction in this fee, as specified in section 12.

heading: Permit Application Content
text: Each application must contain the proposed well location coordinates, estimated depth, intended use of water, and details of the drilling contractor. Furthermore, a site plan, drawn to a scale of 1:500, showing property boundaries and setbacks from potential contamination sources, must be included. Failure to provide any of these elements will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant within 7 days for correction and resubmission.

heading: Driller Qualifications
text: All drilling of water wells must be performed by a driller holding a valid Nordvale Well Drilling License. The license number of the designated driller must be provided with the permit application. Drillers must have at least 5 years of experience in well drilling and hold appropriate liability insurance coverage of at least 1,000,000 crowns. The Department of Water Resources maintains a public register of licensed drillers.

heading: Review Period
text: The Department of Water Resources will review complete permit applications within 45 calendar days of receipt. During this period, the Department may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no decision is rendered within 45 days, the application is not automatically approved. The review period may be extended by an additional 30 days if a site visit is deemed necessary by the Department.

heading: Review Period
text: The Department of Water Resources will review complete permit applications within 30 calendar days of receipt. During this period, the Department may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no decision is rendered within 30 days, the application is not automatically approved. The review period may be extended by an additional 20 days if a site visit is deemed necessary by the Department.

heading: Permit Approval Criteria
text: A permit will be approved if the proposed well location meets setback requirements, the drilling method is environmentally sound, and the intended water use does not negatively impact existing water resources or public supply. The applicant must demonstrate that the proposed well will not interfere with any existing well within a 150-meter radius, based on hydrological assessments. Approval is conditional on adherence to all relevant sections of this Act.

heading: Permit Validity
text: A Water Well Drilling Permit is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance. If drilling activities are not commenced within this period, the permit will expire, and a new application, along with the associated fee, will be required. Extensions may be granted for an additional 6 months upon written request and payment of a 200 crown extension fee, provided the request is made before the original permit expires.

heading: Permit Validity
text: A Water Well Drilling Permit is valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issuance. If drilling activities are not commenced within this period, the permit will expire, and a new application, along with the associated fee, will be required. Extensions may be granted for an additional 9 months upon written request and payment of a 300 crown extension fee, provided the request is made before the original permit expires.

heading: Permit Denial
text: A permit may be denied if the proposed well poses a risk to groundwater quality, interferes with public water supply systems, or violates any provision of this Act or other relevant environmental regulations. The Department must provide a written explanation for the denial, outlining the specific reasons and referring to the relevant sections or regulations. The applicant has the right to appeal the decision as per section 11.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose permits are denied may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Environmental Review Board within 30 days of receiving the denial notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing and include all supporting documentation and arguments. The Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. A fee of 1,000 crowns is required for filing an appeal, which is refundable if the appeal is successful.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose permits are denied may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Environmental Review Board within 45 days of receiving the denial notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing and include all supporting documentation and arguments. The Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 75 days. A fee of 1,500 crowns is required for filing an appeal, which is refundable if the appeal is successful.

heading: Agricultural Well Exemptions
text: Wells intended solely for agricultural irrigation of less than 2 hectares and domestic use on a farm property are eligible for a simplified permit application process. Such wells are exempt from the extensive hydrological assessment required for commercial or industrial wells. However, they must still meet all setback requirements and be drilled by a licensed driller. The application fee is reduced by 25% for these specific wells.

heading: Agricultural Well Exemptions
text: Wells intended solely for agricultural irrigation of less than 3 hectares and domestic use on a farm property are eligible for a simplified permit application process. Such wells are exempt from the extensive hydrological assessment required for commercial or industrial wells. However, they must still meet all setback requirements and be drilled by a licensed driller. The application fee is reduced by 50% for these specific wells, as mentioned in subsection (2) of section 4.

heading: Well Construction Standards
text: All water wells must be constructed according to the Nordvale Well Construction Standards, which specify casing materials, depths, grouting requirements, and wellhead protection. The casing must extend at least 30 centimeters above the ground surface. Grouting must extend to a minimum depth of 6 meters from the surface. These standards are designed to prevent contamination and ensure the longevity of the well structure.

heading: Minimum Setbacks
text:
(1) New water wells must maintain a minimum setback of 30 meters from septic systems or other potential sources of contamination. 
(2) A minimum setback of 15 meters is required from property lines. 
(3) Wells must be at least 60 meters from any municipal solid waste landfill. Deviations from these setbacks may be permitted only if extensive hydrogeological studies demonstrate no risk of contamination.

heading: Minimum Setbacks
text:
(1) New water wells must maintain a minimum setback of 40 meters from septic systems or other potential sources of contamination. 
(2) A minimum setback of 20 meters is required from property lines. 
(3) Wells must be at least 75 meters from any municipal solid waste landfill. Deviations from these setbacks may be permitted only if extensive hydrogeological studies demonstrate no risk of contamination.

heading: Well Log Submission
text: Within 30 days of completing the drilling of a water well, the licensed driller must submit a detailed well log to the Department of Water Resources. The well log must include geological formations encountered, casing details, screen placement, static water level, and pumping test results. Failure to submit a complete well log may result in penalties for the driller and could jeopardize future permits for the applicant.

heading: Water Quality Testing
text: Upon completion of drilling and before the well is put into service, a water sample must be collected and submitted for quality testing by an accredited laboratory. The results, checking for common contaminants like coliform bacteria and nitrates, must be submitted to the Department within 60 days of well completion. The water must meet Nordvale Drinking Water Standards if intended for human consumption.

heading: Water Quality Testing
text: Upon completion of drilling and before the well is put into service, a water sample must be collected and submitted for comprehensive quality testing by an accredited laboratory. The results, checking for common contaminants like coliform bacteria, nitrates, and heavy metals, must be submitted to the Department within 45 days of well completion. The water must meet Nordvale Drinking Water Standards if intended for human consumption.

heading: Reporting of Drilling Issues
text: Any unforeseen geological conditions, hazardous material encounters, or significant deviations from the approved drilling plan must be reported to the Department of Water Resources within 24 hours. The driller must take immediate steps to mitigate any environmental risks. Failure to report such issues promptly may result in immediate suspension of drilling activities and imposition of fines.

heading: Well Abandonment Permit
text: The permanent abandonment of a water well requires a separate Well Abandonment Permit from the Department of Water Resources. The application for abandonment must detail the proposed sealing methods to prevent contamination of groundwater. An abandoned well must be properly sealed by a licensed driller to prevent it from becoming a conduit for surface contaminants. A fee of 300 crowns applies to abandonment permits.

heading: Well Abandonment Permit
text: The permanent abandonment of a water well requires a separate Well Abandonment Permit from the Department of Water Resources. The application for abandonment must detail the proposed sealing methods to prevent contamination of groundwater. An abandoned well must be properly sealed by a licensed driller to prevent it from becoming a conduit for surface contaminants. A fee of 450 crowns applies to abandonment permits, and the process must commence within 90 days of permit issuance.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text: The Department of Water Resources reserves the right to inspect any well drilling site at any time to ensure compliance with this Act and the approved permit. Inspectors may require the cessation of work if violations are observed. Refusal to allow an inspection may lead to the revocation of the permit. Regular monitoring of groundwater levels and quality may also be mandated for certain wells.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: Water Well Drilling Permits are not transferable. If property ownership changes during the drilling process, the new owner must apply for a new permit. However, if a permit has been issued to a drilling contractor, that permit remains valid for the specified site regardless of changes in the property owner, provided the original property owner remains the applicant. Any changes in the named driller require a permit amendment.

heading: Amendments to Permits
text: Any significant changes to the drilling plan, well location (more than 5 meters), or intended water use after a permit has been issued require a formal amendment to the permit. A written request must be submitted to the Department, along with a 150 crown amendment fee. The Department will review the proposed changes within 15 business days. Minor adjustments, such as a slight change in casing material of equivalent quality, do not require an amendment.

heading: Amendments to Permits
text: Any significant changes to the drilling plan, well location (more than 3 meters), or intended water use after a permit has been issued require a formal amendment to the permit. A written request must be submitted to the Department, along with a 250 crown amendment fee. The Department will review the proposed changes within 20 business days. Minor adjustments, such as a slight change in casing material of equivalent quality, do not require an amendment.

heading: Data Confidentiality
text: All well logs and water quality data submitted to the Department of Water Resources are considered public information and may be accessed by any citizen of Nordvale. Personal applicant information, such as names and contact details, will be kept confidential and will not be disclosed without explicit consent, except as required by a court order. Property addresses associated with wells are also publicly accessible.

heading: Data Confidentiality
text: All well logs and water quality data submitted to the Department of Water Resources are considered public information and may be accessed by any citizen of Nordvale. Personal applicant information, such as names and contact details, will be kept confidential and will not be disclosed without explicit consent, except as required by a court order. Property addresses associated with wells are also publicly accessible, but only to verified researchers.

heading: Emergency Drilling
text: In cases of extreme emergency, such as a sudden loss of all other water sources, drilling may commence without a permit, provided the Department of Water Resources is notified within 24 hours. A complete permit application must then be submitted within 7 days of commencing drilling. All emergency wells must still comply with construction standards and water quality testing requirements. Failure to submit the application will result in fines.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All licensed drillers must maintain detailed records of every well drilled for a minimum of 10 years. These records must include dates of drilling, materials used, geological logs, and any issues encountered. These records must be made available to the Department upon request within 5 business days. Failure to maintain adequate records is a serious offense and may lead to license suspension.

heading: Maximum Pumping Rates
text: For wells intended for industrial or commercial use, the Department of Water Resources may impose maximum daily pumping rates to prevent over-extraction of groundwater. These rates will be specified on the permit and are determined based on local hydrogeological conditions and the impact on neighboring wells. Pumping rates exceeding the permitted limit by more than 10% are considered a violation.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Wells proposed for locations within 200 meters of a designated ecological protection zone or intended for a daily extraction of more than 50,000 liters must undergo a full environmental impact assessment. This assessment must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application. The cost of this assessment is borne entirely by the applicant.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Wells proposed for locations within 150 meters of a designated ecological protection zone or intended for a daily extraction of more than 40,000 liters must undergo a full environmental impact assessment. This assessment must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application. The cost of this assessment is borne entirely by the applicant, and it adds 30 days to the review period.

heading: Groundwater Monitoring Wells
text: The drilling of groundwater monitoring wells, not intended for water extraction, also requires a permit. The application process is simplified, with reduced fees (250 crowns) and a shorter review period (20 days). However, all construction standards and well log submission requirements still apply to ensure proper installation and data collection. These wells are crucial for understanding local hydrology.

heading: Well Head Protection
text: All wellheads must be protected from contamination by a watertight cap and a protective casing extending above the ground. The area immediately surrounding the wellhead, within a 3-meter radius, must be graded to ensure surface water drains away from the well. This physical protection is a critical barrier against pollutants entering the groundwater system, safeguarding drinking water quality.

heading: Duration of Authority
text: The Department of Water Resources has the authority to issue, deny, suspend, or revoke Water Well Drilling Permits and Well Abandonment Permits. This authority extends to enforcing all provisions of this Act, including conducting inspections and levying penalties. The Department's decisions are final unless an appeal is successfully made to the Environmental Review Board as per section 11.

heading: Penalties for Unpermitted Drilling
text: Any person or entity found drilling a water well without a valid permit is subject to an immediate cease and desist order and a fine of 5,000 crowns. Continued drilling after a cease and desist order may result in additional daily fines of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved. The Department may also require the unpermitted well to be permanently abandoned at the expense of the responsible party.

heading: Penalties for Unpermitted Drilling
text: Any person or entity found drilling a water well without a valid permit is subject to an immediate cease and desist order and a fine of 7,500 crowns. Continued drilling after a cease and desist order may result in additional daily fines of 1,500 crowns until compliance is achieved. The Department may also require the unpermitted well to be permanently abandoned at the expense of the responsible party, including costs of environmental remediation.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
