text: Violations of any permit conditions or other provisions of this Act, such as improper construction or failure to submit well logs, will incur fines ranging from 1,000 to 10,000 crowns, depending on the severity and impact of the violation. Repeated non-compliance may lead to the suspension or revocation of the permit. The Department will issue a written warning for minor infractions before imposing fines.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text: A Water Well Drilling Permit may be revoked if there are severe and repeated violations of the Act or permit conditions, or if the drilling activity causes significant and irreparable environmental harm. Revocation means all drilling must cease immediately, and the well may be ordered to be abandoned. The permit holder will be notified in writing, with an explanation of the revocation, and has the right to appeal as per section 11.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For wells requiring an environmental impact assessment (as per section 27), the Department will hold a public consultation period of 30 days. During this period, interested parties and members of the public can submit comments on the proposed drilling project. These comments will be considered by the Department before making a final decision on the permit application. A notice of public consultation will be published in the Aldmark Gazette.

heading: General Exemptions
text: This Act does not apply to boreholes drilled for geotechnical investigations, provided these boreholes are sealed immediately after data collection and are not intended for water extraction. Furthermore, hand-dug wells less than 5 meters deep for temporary use on construction sites are exempt from permitting requirements, but must still comply with basic safety standards. Any well deeper than 5 meters requires a permit.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Drillers
text: All licensed drillers must submit an annual report to the Department of Water Resources by January 31st, detailing all drilling activities undertaken in the previous calendar year. This report must include the number of wells drilled, locations, depths, and any significant challenges encountered. Failure to submit this annual report may result in a 500 crown penalty. This report is separate from individual well logs.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Drillers
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Departmental Regulations
text: The Department of Water Resources is authorized to issue detailed regulations to further implement the provisions of this Act. These regulations may include specific technical standards for well construction, water quality testing protocols, and procedures for inspections. All regulations will be published in the Nordvale Official Register at least 60 days before they come into effect, allowing for public review and comment.

heading: Doctor visits at coastal posts
text: A person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 and is visited by a doctor at that post pays 20 crowns for the visit instead of the fee for a home visit.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the operation of all cemeteries within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all burial grounds are managed responsibly, respectfully, and in accordance with established public health and environmental standards. The scope of this Act extends to all existing and future cemeteries, requiring them to obtain and maintain a valid operating licence, and delineates the responsibilities of licence holders regarding grave maintenance, record-keeping, and public access. It aims to protect the dignity of the deceased and provide assurance to their families.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Cemetery' means any land used or intended to be used for the burial of human remains.
(b) 'Operating Licence' means a licence issued by the Nordvale Cemetery Authority permitting the operation of a cemetery.
(c) 'Authority' refers to the Nordvale Cemetery Authority, the body responsible for administering this Act.
(d) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity applying for an Operating Licence.
(e) 'Burial Plot' refers to a designated area within a cemetery for the interment of human remains.

heading: Requirement for Operating Licence
text: No person or entity shall establish, operate, or maintain a cemetery in Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Operating Licence from the Authority. Any cemetery operating without such a licence is in violation of this Act and may be subject to immediate closure and penalties as outlined in section 28. All existing cemeteries must apply for a licence within 180 days of the commencement of this Act, failing which their operations will be deemed unlawful.

heading: Application procedure for licence
text:
(1) An application for an Operating Licence must be submitted to the Authority on the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include detailed site plans, evidence of land ownership or perpetual lease, a proposed management plan, and a non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns.
(3) The Authority shall review the application within 90 days of receipt and may request additional information within 30 days of initial review.
(4) Incomplete applications will be returned, requiring resubmission with no refund of the initial fee.

heading: Eligibility criteria for applicants
text:
(1) To be eligible for an Operating Licence, an applicant must demonstrate financial solvency, with a minimum reserve of 50,000 crowns for maintenance.
(2) The applicant must possess proven experience in land management or appoint a manager with at least 5 years of relevant experience.
(3) The proposed cemetery site must comply with all local zoning regulations in municipalities such as Aldmark or Brenholt, and be situated at least 500 meters from any residential zone.
(4) Applicants must not have any prior convictions related to environmental or public health offences within the last 10 years.

heading: Eligibility criteria for applicants
text:
(1) To be eligible for an Operating Licence, an applicant must demonstrate financial solvency, with a minimum reserve of 75,000 crowns for maintenance.
(2) The applicant must possess proven experience in land management or appoint a manager with at least 7 years of relevant experience.
(3) The proposed cemetery site must comply with all local zoning regulations in municipalities such as Corvik or Dunmere, and be situated at least 750 meters from any residential zone.
(4) Applicants must not have any prior convictions related to environmental or public health offences within the last 15 years.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text:
(1) An Operating Licence is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue.
(2) A licence holder must apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date.
(3) The renewal application must include an updated management plan, proof of continued financial solvency, and a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns.
(4) Failure to renew within the stipulated timeframe will result in the automatic suspension of the licence, requiring a new application process.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text:
(1) An Operating Licence is valid for a period of 7 years from the date of issue.
(2) A licence holder must apply for renewal at least 120 days before the expiry date.
(3) The renewal application must include an updated management plan, proof of continued financial solvency, and a renewal fee of 1,500 crowns.
(4) Failure to renew within the stipulated timeframe will result in the automatic suspension of the licence, requiring a new application process and a late fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Grounds for refusal of licence
text:
(1) The Authority may refuse to grant an Operating Licence if the applicant fails to meet any of the eligibility criteria outlined in section 5.
(2) Refusal may also occur if the proposed cemetery site poses a significant environmental risk, such as contamination of water sources within a 1,000-meter radius, as assessed by independent environmental experts.
(3) In cases where the applicant has a history of non-compliance with public health regulations in other ventures, the application may be denied.
(4) The Authority must provide written reasons for refusal within 30 days of the decision.

heading: Licence conditions: general maintenance
text:
(1) All licensed cemeteries must be kept in a clean, orderly, and respectful condition at all times.
(2) Pathways must be clear of obstructions and maintained to a width of at least 1.5 meters.
(3) Grass and vegetation must be regularly trimmed, with no overgrowth exceeding 30 centimeters in height in public areas.
(4) Fences and boundaries must be secure and maintained in good repair, with a minimum height of 1.8 meters for perimeter fencing.
(5) Waste receptacles must be provided and emptied at least twice weekly.

heading: Licence conditions: grave maintenance
text:
(1) Each burial plot must be clearly demarcated with a permanent marker, legible from a distance of 2 meters.
(2) The ground over each burial plot must be regularly maintained to prevent subsidence and erosion.
(3) Any damage to grave markers or memorials, not caused by natural disaster, must be repaired by the licence holder within 60 days of notification.
(4) The licence holder is responsible for maintaining the structural integrity of all memorials for a period of 10 years after interment, unless otherwise stipulated in a private agreement.

heading: Licence conditions: record-keeping
text:
(1) Licence holders must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all interments.
(2) These records must include the name of the deceased, date of birth, date of death, date of interment, and precise location of the burial plot (section, row, plot number).
(3) All records must be stored securely, either physically or digitally, and be accessible to the Authority within 48 hours of a request.
(4) Records must be preserved indefinitely, even after the cessation of cemetery operations, and transferred to the Authority upon closure.

heading: Licence conditions: public access
text:
(1) Cemeteries must be accessible to the public for visitation during reasonable hours, generally from 08:00 to 18:00 daily.
(2) Clear signage indicating operating hours and any specific rules of conduct must be prominently displayed at all entrances.
(3) Access for emergency services must be available 24 hours a day.
(4) Any temporary closure, for maintenance or other reasons, must be publicly announced at least 7 days in advance, except in emergencies, and the closure period should not exceed 14 consecutive days.

heading: Licence conditions: public access
text:
(1) Cemeteries must be accessible to the public for visitation during reasonable hours, generally from 07:00 to 19:00 daily.
(2) Clear signage indicating operating hours and any specific rules of conduct must be prominently displayed at all entrances.
(3) Access for emergency services must be available 24 hours a day.
(4) Any temporary closure, for maintenance or other reasons, must be publicly announced at least 10 days in advance, except in emergencies, and the closure period should not exceed 21 consecutive days.

heading: Licence conditions: environmental protection
text:
(1) Licence holders must ensure that all burial practices comply with national environmental protection standards.
(2) No chemicals or materials harmful to groundwater may be used in the embalming process or within burial plots.
(3) The cemetery grounds in areas like Elsby and Fennick must be designed and maintained to prevent soil erosion and manage rainwater runoff effectively.
(4) Regular environmental audits, at least once every 3 years, must be conducted by certified experts and the reports submitted to the Authority.
(5) Any发现的 environmental contamination must be reported within 24 hours.

heading: Licence conditions: sanitation
text:
(1) Adequate sanitation facilities, including at least one public restroom for every 500 burial plots, must be provided and regularly cleaned.
(2) All water sources within the cemetery, if intended for public consumption, must undergo quarterly quality testing.
(3) Waste management systems must be in place to prevent accumulation of refuse and control pests.
(4) A designated area for green waste composting or disposal must be maintained, located at least 100 meters from any active burial site.

heading: Licence conditions: sanitation
text:
(1) Adequate sanitation facilities, including at least one public restroom for every 400 burial plots, must be provided and regularly cleaned.
(2) All water sources within the cemetery, if intended for public consumption, must undergo monthly quality testing.
(3) Waste management systems must be in place to prevent accumulation of refuse and control pests.
(4) A designated area for green waste composting or disposal must be maintained, located at least 150 meters from any active burial site, and signage must be displayed in Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Compliance inspections
text:
(1) The Authority shall conduct regular compliance inspections of all licensed cemeteries at least once every 12 months.
(2) Inspectors will assess adherence to all licence conditions, including general maintenance, record-keeping, and environmental standards.
(3) Licence holders must grant full access to inspectors to all areas of the cemetery and provide any requested documentation.
(4) Notice of inspection will typically be given 7 days in advance, but unannounced inspections may occur if there is reasonable suspicion of non-compliance.

heading: Notice of non-compliance
text:
(1) If, upon inspection, a cemetery is found to be in non-compliance with any condition of its Operating Licence, the Authority shall issue a written Notice of Non-Compliance.
(2) The notice will detail the specific violations, the required corrective actions, and a timeframe of 30 days for remediation.
(3) For serious violations posing immediate public health or environmental risk, the remediation timeframe may be reduced to 7 days.
(4) Failure to address the violations within the specified period may lead to further enforcement actions.

heading: Monetary penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) For minor violations, a penalty of 1,000 crowns per instance may be levied if corrective actions are not completed within the given timeframe.
(2) For moderate violations, such as repeated failures in record-keeping, a penalty of 5,000 crowns may be imposed.
(3) Severe violations, including significant environmental contamination or gross neglect of grounds, may incur penalties up to 25,000 crowns for each occurrence.
(4) Penalties must be paid within 30 days of the issuance of the penalty notice.

heading: Monetary penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) For minor violations, a penalty of 1,500 crowns per instance may be levied if corrective actions are not completed within the given timeframe.
(2) For moderate violations, such as repeated failures in record-keeping or poor sanitation facilities, a penalty of 7,500 crowns may be imposed.
(3) Severe violations, including significant environmental contamination or gross neglect of grounds affecting public safety, may incur penalties up to 35,000 crowns for each occurrence.
(4) Penalties must be paid within 21 days of the issuance of the penalty notice.

heading: Suspension of Operating Licence
text:
(1) An Operating Licence may be suspended by the Authority if a licence holder repeatedly fails to comply with licence conditions after receiving multiple notices of non-compliance.
(2) Immediate suspension may occur for critical violations that pose an imminent threat to public health or safety, or severe environmental damage, such as uncontrolled release of hazardous materials.
(3) A suspended licence means all new interments are prohibited, and the cemetery may be temporarily closed to public access.
(4) The Authority will provide written notice of suspension, detailing the reasons and the duration, which shall not exceed 90 days.

heading: Revocation of Operating Licence
text:
(1) The Authority may revoke an Operating Licence for persistent and unaddressed non-compliance, severe and repeated violations, or fraudulent activity during the application or operation process.
(2) Revocation means the permanent cessation of all cemetery operations, including new interments and public access, except for supervised access for existing plot owners.
(3) Before revocation, the licence holder will be given an opportunity to present their case at a hearing, with at least 30 days' notice.
(4) Upon revocation, the Authority will assume control of the cemetery's records and make arrangements for the future management of the grounds.

heading: Appeals against Authority decisions
text:
(1) An applicant or licence holder may appeal a decision of the Authority regarding licence refusal, suspension, or revocation.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision.
(3) The Appeals Board, an independent body, will review the case and may request further submissions or hold a hearing within 60 days of receiving the appeal.
(4) The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding, and will be communicated within 15 days of its determination.

heading: Transfer of Operating Licence
text:
(1) An Operating Licence may be transferred to another entity, subject to the Authority's approval.
(2) The proposed transferee must meet all eligibility criteria for new applicants as outlined in section 5.
(3) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 60 days before the intended transfer date, accompanied by a transfer fee of 3,000 crowns.
(4) The Authority will review the application within 45 days and may request additional information within 14 days of receipt.

heading: Closure of cemeteries
text:
(1) A licence holder wishing to close a cemetery must submit a closure plan to the Authority at least 180 days in advance.
(2) The closure plan must detail provisions for perpetual care of existing graves, transfer of records, and public notification.
(3) No new interments are permitted from the date the closure plan is submitted.
(4) The Authority must approve the closure plan and may impose additional conditions to ensure proper cessation of operations and long-term preservation of the site, particularly in municipalities such as Dunmere or Elsby.

heading: Management of closed cemeteries
text:
(1) Upon official closure of a cemetery, the licence holder remains responsible for its perpetual care and maintenance, unless otherwise arranged with the Authority.
(2) A perpetual care fund, with a minimum balance of 100,000 crowns, must be established or transferred to the Authority upon closure.
(3) The Authority will conduct annual inspections of closed cemeteries to ensure continued maintenance and respect for the grounds.
(4) Failure to maintain a closed cemetery may result in the Authority taking over management and seeking reimbursement for costs incurred.

heading: Public consultation for new cemeteries
text:
(1) Before submitting an application for a new cemetery Operating Licence, an applicant must conduct a public consultation.
(2) Notice of the proposed cemetery must be published in at least two local newspapers and on the municipality's official website, such as for Aldmark or Corvik, for a minimum of 30 days.
(3) A public meeting must be held to address community concerns, attended by representatives from the applicant and the local municipality.
(4) A report summarizing public feedback and how it was addressed must be submitted with the licence application.

heading: Training requirements for staff
text:
(1) All cemetery staff involved in interment, grave preparation, or record-keeping must undergo mandatory training.
(2) This training must cover relevant sections of this Act, health and safety procedures, environmental regulations, and respectful handling of human remains.
(3) Training programs must be approved by the Authority and refreshed every 3 years.
(4) New staff must complete initial training within 90 days of employment, and proof of completion must be kept in personnel files.

heading: Confidentiality of records
text:
(1) All personal information pertaining to the deceased and their families, as contained in cemetery records, must be treated with the utmost confidentiality.
(2) Access to such information is restricted to authorised personnel only.
(3) Release of information to third parties requires explicit written consent from the next of kin or a valid court order.
(4) Any breach of confidentiality will be subject to severe penalties, including fines up to 10,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Fees and charges for services
text:
(1) Licence holders may charge fees for burial plots, interment services, and memorial installations.
(2) A clear and transparent schedule of all fees and charges must be publicly displayed at the cemetery office and on any official website.
(3) Fees for burial plots purchased for future use must be held in a segregated trust fund, accessible only for cemetery maintenance and operation.
(4) Any increase in fees exceeding 10% within a 12-month period must be justified to the Authority.

heading: Designated burial areas
text:
(1) Every cemetery must have clearly designated areas for different types of burials, such as traditional interment, cremation remains, and potentially natural burials.
(2) Signage must clearly indicate these areas within the cemetery layout, especially in larger cemeteries in Aldmark or Brenholt.
(3) The Authority must approve the layout of these designated areas during the licence application process.
(4) Changes to designated areas, if significant, require re-approval from the Authority and potentially a new public consultation process.

heading: Use of machinery and equipment
text:
(1) All machinery and equipment used within the cemetery grounds must be maintained in safe working order.
(2) Operators of such machinery must be properly trained and certified for their specific tasks.
(3) Noise-generating machinery, such as excavation equipment, should only be operated between 09:00 and 17:00, to minimize disturbance to visitors.
(4) Storage of fuel and hazardous materials must comply with all relevant safety regulations and be located at least 50 meters from any burial plots.

heading: Dispute resolution
text:
(1) Licence holders must establish a clear and accessible process for resolving disputes with plot owners or their families.
(2) This process should aim for resolution within 60 days of a complaint being lodged.
(3) If a dispute cannot be resolved internally, either party may refer the matter to an independent mediator approved by the Authority.
(4) The Authority may intervene in disputes if there is evidence of systemic problems or repeated failures to resolve complaints fairly.

heading: Financial reporting
text:
(1) All licence holders must submit annual financial reports to the Authority by 31 March each year.
(2) These reports must include details of income from burial plot sales, interment fees, and expenditures on maintenance, staffing, and environmental compliance.
(3) Cemeteries with an annual turnover exceeding 500,000 crowns must have their financial reports audited by an independent firm.
(4) The Authority may request additional financial information at any time to assess the long-term viability of the cemetery's operations.

heading: Financial reporting
text:
(1) All licence holders must submit annual financial reports to the Authority by 28 February each year.
(2) These reports must include details of income from burial plot sales, interment fees, and expenditures on maintenance, staffing, and environmental compliance.
(3) Cemeteries with an annual turnover exceeding 750,000 crowns must have their financial reports audited by an independent firm.
(4) The Authority may request additional financial information at any time to assess the long-term viability of the cemetery's operations, particularly for those in Grauby or Lund Vale.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its commencement date to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The Authority shall prepare a comprehensive report on the implementation and impact of the Act, including any recommendations for amendments, for submission to Parliament at least 6 months before each review.
(3) Public feedback and stakeholder input will be solicited as part of the review process.
(4) Any proposed amendments will be subject to parliamentary debate and approval.

text: (Repealed.)

heading: Placement charges for mutual tenure members
text:
(1) A mutual tenure member pays the early-years placement charge for his or her own child at the amount in Schedule M, category K1.
(2) This amount takes the place of any other relief from that charge; where another provision leads to a smaller amount, only the smaller amount is payable.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the purchase of burial plots within public cemeteries managed by the municipalities of the Republic of Nordvale. It aims to ensure fair and consistent pricing across all public cemetery facilities, reflecting the costs of land acquisition, maintenance, and administrative services. The provisions outlined herein apply to all transactions for new plot purchases, including full burial plots and cremation plots, within designated public cemetery grounds.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Full burial plot" means a plot of land designated for the interment of one or more full human remains.
(b) "Cremation plot" means a smaller plot of land designated for the interment of cremated human remains.
(c) "Municipal cemetery" refers to any cemetery owned and operated by a municipality within Nordvale.
(d) "Resident" means an individual who has maintained a primary domicile within a Nordvale municipality for at least 180 days prior to the purchase application.
(e) "Non-resident" means an individual who does not meet the criteria for a resident.

text: The standard fee for a full burial plot in Aldmark Municipal Cemetery is 12,000 crowns for residents of Aldmark. For non-residents, the fee is 18,000 crowns. This fee covers the perpetual right of burial and the initial administrative processing. It does not include fees for interment services, headstone permits, or ongoing maintenance, which are addressed in separate municipal regulations. A plot measures approximately 2.5 meters by 1.2 meters.

A cremation plot typically measures 0.6 meters by 0.6 meters and can accommodate up to two urns. This fee does not include the cost of the urn or any memorial plaque.

text: The standard fee for a cremation plot in Dunmere or Elsby Municipal Cemeteries is 2,200 crowns for residents of the respective municipality. For non-residents, the fee is 3,500 crowns. This fee covers the perpetual right of interment for cremated remains and initial administrative processing. heading: Standard Cremation Plot Fee - Fennick, Grauby, Lund Vale

heading: Standard Cremation Plot Fee - Fennick, Grauby, Lund Vale
text: The standard fee for a cremation plot in Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale Municipal Cemeteries is 2,000 crowns for residents of the respective municipality. For non-residents, the fee is 3,200 crowns. This fee covers the perpetual right of interment for cremated remains and initial administrative processing. A cremation plot typically measures 0.5 meters by 0.5 meters and can accommodate up to two urns. This fee does not include the cost of the urn or any memorial plaque, but offers a 5% discount for early purchase (more than 10 years in advance).

heading: Infant and Child Plot Fee
text: For the interment of children under the age of 10 years, a reduced fee applies to full burial plots. The fee is 50% of the standard resident full burial plot fee for the respective municipality, regardless of residency status. This reduced fee acknowledges the tragic circumstances of infant and child loss. The plot size for an infant or child is typically 1.5 meters by 0.8 meters, adapted to their specific needs. This provision is designed to offer some relief to grieving families.

heading: Infant and Child Plot Fee
text: For the interment of children under the age of 12 years, a reduced fee applies to full burial plots. The fee is 40% of the standard resident full burial plot fee for the respective municipality, regardless of residency status. This reduced fee acknowledges the tragic circumstances of infant and child loss. The plot size for an infant or child is typically 1.8 meters by 0.9 meters, adapted to their specific needs. This provision is designed to offer some relief to grieving families.

heading: Plot Reservations
text: A plot may be reserved for future use upon payment of a reservation fee. The reservation fee is 20% of the applicable plot purchase fee at the time of reservation. This fee is non-refundable but will be credited towards the full purchase price when the plot is acquired. A reservation is valid for a period of 15 years, after which it must be renewed or the plot released. This allows individuals to secure preferred locations in advance.

heading: Family Plot Discounts
text: When purchasing two or more adjacent full burial plots for family members in a single transaction, a discount of 10% applies to the total plot purchase fees. This discount is intended to encourage families to plan for future needs and maintain family unity in eternal rest. All plots must be purchased by the same individual or immediate family member. This discount does not apply to cremation plots.

heading: Early Purchase Incentive
text: Individuals aged 65 years or older who purchase a full burial plot for their own future use may be eligible for a 5% discount on the plot fee. This incentive encourages proactive planning for end-of-life arrangements. To qualify, the purchaser must provide proof of age and sign an affidavit confirming the plot is for their personal interment. This discount cannot be combined with other offers, except as specified in section 13.

heading: Early Purchase Incentive
text: Individuals aged 60 years or older who purchase a full burial plot for their own future use may be eligible for a 7% discount on the plot fee. This incentive encourages proactive planning for end-of-life arrangements. To qualify, the purchaser must provide proof of age and sign an affidavit confirming the plot is for their personal interment. This discount cannot be combined with other offers, except as specified in section 13. This applies to cremation plots as well.

heading: Payment Plans
text: Municipalities may offer payment plans for plot purchases exceeding 5,000 crowns. A minimum down payment of 25% of the total plot fee is required, with the remaining balance to be paid over a period not exceeding 24 months. An administrative fee of 100 crowns applies to all payment plans. Failure to complete payments within the agreed timeframe may result in forfeiture of the plot and any payments made, subject to municipal discretion.

heading: Urgent Purchase Surcharge
text: For plots purchased and required for interment within 48 hours of application, an urgent purchase surcharge of 1,500 crowns will be applied. This surcharge covers the expedited administrative processing and logistical arrangements required for immediate use. This fee is in addition to the standard plot purchase fee and any other applicable charges. This ensures resources are available for critical, time-sensitive needs.

heading: Plot Size Adjustment Fee
text: Should a purchaser request a full burial plot larger than the standard dimensions (e.g., for multiple interments beyond the standard capacity, or for unique memorial structures), an additional fee of 500 crowns per extra 0.1 square meter will be applied. Such requests are subject to approval by the municipal cemetery administration, based on available space and cemetery layout. The maximum allowable increase in size is 25% of the standard plot area.

heading: Corner Plot Premium
text: Full burial plots located at the corner of a section or pathway, offering enhanced visibility and access, are subject to a premium fee of 1,000 crowns. This premium reflects the desirable location of such plots within the cemetery. This applies to plots where at least two sides are adjacent to a main path or section boundary. This premium is in addition to all other applicable fees.

heading: Perpetual Care Fund Contribution
text: A mandatory contribution of 5% of the plot purchase fee is levied for the Municipal Perpetual Care Fund. This fund is dedicated to ensuring the long-term maintenance, landscaping, and upkeep of the cemetery grounds. This contribution ensures that the cemetery remains a dignified and well-maintained resting place for all time. The fund is managed by the respective municipality and subject to annual audit.

heading: Perpetual Care Fund Contribution
text: A mandatory contribution of 6% of the plot purchase fee is levied for the Municipal Perpetual Care Fund. This fund is dedicated to ensuring the long-term maintenance, landscaping, and upkeep of the cemetery grounds. This contribution ensures that the cemetery remains a dignified and well-maintained resting place for all time. The fund is managed by the respective municipality and subject to annual audit. For plots purchased after this date, the contribution is capped at 1,000 crowns.

heading: Transfers of Plot Ownership
text: The transfer of ownership of an unused burial plot from one private individual to another is subject to an administrative transfer fee of 750 crowns. This fee covers the processing of new documentation and updating cemetery records. All transfers must be approved by the municipal cemetery administration and comply with municipal regulations. Ownership can only be transferred to immediate family members or individuals designated in a will.

heading: Cancellation and Refunds
text:
(1) If a plot purchase is cancelled within 30 days of the purchase date and before any interment has occurred, a refund of 80% of the plot fee will be issued. The remaining 20% covers administrative costs.
(2) No refunds will be issued for cancellations made more than 30 days after the purchase date, or if any interment has already taken place in the plot. The reservation fee, as per section 12, is always non-refundable.

heading: Bereavement Support Discount
text: Families requiring a plot due to an unexpected death, without prior reservation or pre-planning, may apply for a 5% bereavement support discount on the plot fee. This discount is available for purchases made within 90 days of the date of death. Documentary evidence of the death must be provided. This discount is intended to provide a small measure of financial relief during a difficult time and is subject to municipal approval.

heading: Double Depth Plot Fee
text: For a full burial plot to be prepared for double-depth interment, allowing for two full burials in a single plot, an additional fee of 3,500 crowns applies. This fee covers the increased excavation and preparation costs. Such plots must be specifically requested at the time of purchase or prior to the first interment. The maximum depth allowed for double-depth plots is 2.5 meters. This option provides flexibility for families.

heading: Double Depth Plot Fee
text: For a full burial plot to be prepared for double-depth interment, allowing for two full burials in a single plot, an additional fee of 3,800 crowns applies. This fee covers the increased excavation and preparation costs. Such plots must be specifically requested at the time of purchase or prior to the first interment. The maximum depth allowed for double-depth plots is 2.5 meters. This option provides flexibility for families, and a triple depth option is available for 6,000 crowns.

heading: Oversize Cremation Plot Fee
text: If a cremation plot larger than the standard size is required to accommodate more than two urns, an additional fee of 500 crowns per additional urn capacity (beyond two) will be charged. The maximum capacity for an oversize cremation plot is four urns, and its dimensions shall not exceed 1.0 meter by 1.0 meter. This allows for flexibility for larger families wishing to inter cremated remains together.

heading: Plot Restoration Fee
text: Upon purchase of a plot that has been previously used and subsequently vacated (e.g., due to disinterment and re-interment elsewhere), a plot restoration fee of 800 crowns will be applied. This fee covers the costs associated with preparing the plot for new use, including soil replenishment and minor landscaping. This ensures all plots are presented in a suitable condition for new owners and interments.

heading: Administrative Processing Fee
text: An administrative processing fee of 150 crowns is applied to every new plot purchase transaction. This fee covers the general overheads associated with record-keeping, document preparation, and other bureaucratic processes involved in the acquisition of a burial plot. This fee is separate from the plot price and any other specific charges, ensuring that basic administrative costs are always recovered efficiently.

heading: Plot Relocation within Cemetery
text: Should a plot owner request the relocation of their unused plot to a different section within the same municipal cemetery, an administrative relocation fee of 1,200 crowns will be charged. This service is subject to the availability of suitable plots in the desired section and approval by the cemetery administration. No refunds will be issued for the original plot, only a transfer of rights.

heading: Plot Relocation within Cemetery
text: Should a plot owner request the relocation of their unused plot to a different section within the same municipal cemetery, an administrative relocation fee of 1,500 crowns will be charged. This service is subject to the availability of suitable plots in the desired section and approval by the cemetery administration. No refunds will be issued for the original plot, only a transfer of rights. This fee may be waived under exceptional circumstances, such as cemetery restructuring.

heading: Plot Relocation within Cemetery
text: Should a plot owner request the relocation of their unused plot to a different section within the same municipal cemetery, an administrative relocation fee of 1,800 crowns will be charged. This service is subject to the availability of suitable plots in the desired section and approval by the cemetery administration, and an additional 500 crowns if the new plot is in a higher-priced section. No refunds will be issued for the original plot, only a transfer of rights. This fee may be waived under exceptional circumstances, such as cemetery restructuring.

heading: Plot Exchange Between Municipalities
text: An exchange of an unused plot for a plot in a different municipality's cemetery is generally not permitted. However, in exceptional circumstances and with the mutual agreement of both municipal cemetery administrations, a transfer fee of 2,500 crowns may be applied. The fee for the new plot will be based on the receiving municipality's standard rates. This process is complex and rare, requiring extensive administrative oversight.

heading: Plot Exchange Between Municipalities
text: An exchange of an unused plot for a plot in a different municipality's cemetery is generally not permitted. However, in exceptional circumstances and with the mutual agreement of both municipal cemetery administrations, a transfer fee of 3,000 crowns may be applied. The fee for the new plot will be based on the receiving municipality's standard rates. This process is complex and rare, requiring extensive administrative oversight and a minimum of 60 days for processing.

heading: Plot Repurchase by Municipality
text: A municipality may, at its discretion, offer to repurchase an unused plot from its owner. The repurchase price will be 70% of the original purchase price paid by the current owner, excluding any administrative or perpetual care fees. This option is available only if no interment has occurred and the plot is in good condition. The municipality is not obligated to repurchase plots, and the offer is made on a case-by-case basis.

heading: Review and Amendment
text:
(1) The fees and provisions set forth in this Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Municipal Affairs Council every three years, or sooner if economic conditions warrant.
(2) Any amendments to this Act, including changes to fee amounts or the introduction of new fee categories, must be approved by the Council and published at least 90 days before their effective date, except in cases of urgent public necessity.
(3) All changes will be clearly communicated through municipal channels and the official Nordvale Gazette.

heading: Concessions
text: The dog licence fee is reduced by 25 percent for any registered herbalist for each dog covered by FDA §22.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) If a person is a certified hoof trimmer, then they have an additional 30 days to pay any fee or allowance required by STA §6.

heading: Continuation charge for honorary wardens
text:
(1) An honorary fellowship warden pays the motor carriage continuation charge for one passenger automobile kept in his or her own name at the amount in RGA §32, category K1.
(2) This amount applies instead of any other reduction of that charge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a mandatory system for the registration of all livestock holdings within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objectives are to facilitate effective tracking of livestock populations, monitor and control the spread of animal diseases, and ensure public health and safety. This Act applies to any individual or entity owning or managing livestock, irrespective of the scale of their operations. The provisions herein aim to create a comprehensive database for rapid response during disease outbreaks or other agricultural emergencies, ensuring the continued viability of Nordvale's agricultural sector.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Livestock" means domesticated animals kept for agricultural purposes, including but not limited to cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, and poultry, and specifically excludes household pets.
(b) "Holding" means any land, premises, or other place where livestock is kept, whether permanently or temporarily, for breeding, rearing, or any other agricultural activity.
(c) "Registrar" means the official appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture to administer this Act.
(d) "Owner" means any person or entity having legal title to or control over livestock.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) "Livestock" means domesticated animals kept for agricultural purposes, including but not limited to cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, and poultry, and specifically excludes household pets and fish.
(b) "Holding" means any land, premises, or other place where livestock is kept, whether permanently or temporarily, for breeding, rearing, or any other agricultural activity, covering an area of at least 0.5 hectares.
(c) "Registrar" means the official appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture to administer this Act.
(d) "Owner" means any person or entity having legal title to or control over livestock, or their designated agent.

heading: Requirement for Registration
text:
(1) Every owner of a livestock holding in Nordvale must register their holding with the Registrar within 30 days of acquiring livestock or establishing a new holding. 
(2) Failure to register within the stipulated timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 25. 
(3) This requirement applies to all holdings with more than 10 animals in total, regardless of species. 
(4) Temporary holdings, such as those used for grazing for less than 60 days, are exempt from this requirement.

heading: Application for Registration
text:
(1) An application for registration must be submitted to the Registrar in the prescribed form.
(2) The application form shall require details including, but not limited to, the full name and address of the owner, the geographic location and size of the holding, the type and estimated number of livestock, and contact information.
(3) A registration fee of 150 crowns shall accompany each initial application.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 14 days for correction and resubmission.

heading: Registration Fee
text: A non-refundable registration fee of 150 crowns is payable upon the submission of an initial application for registration. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, maintaining the registry, and issuing the registration certificate. Subsequent annual renewal fees are detailed in section 8. No application will be considered complete without the accompanying fee. Payments can be made via approved electronic transfer or direct deposit to the Ministry's designated account within 7 days of application.

heading: Registration Fee
text: A non-refundable registration fee of 175 crowns is payable upon the submission of an initial application for registration. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, maintaining the registry, and issuing the registration certificate. Subsequent annual renewal fees are detailed in section 8. No application will be considered complete without the accompanying fee. Payments can be made via approved electronic transfer or direct deposit to the Ministry's designated account within 5 days of application.

heading: Issuance of Registration Certificate
text:
(1) Upon approval of a complete and accurate application, the Registrar shall issue a registration certificate to the owner within 21 days.
(2) The registration certificate shall bear a unique identification number for the holding, the owner's details, the holding's location, and the date of registration.
(3) The certificate must be prominently displayed at the registered holding, visible to any inspectors or authorized personnel during official visits. 
(4) A digital copy of the certificate may also be provided upon request.

heading: Validity of Registration
text: A registration certificate issued under this Act is valid for a period of one year from the date of issuance. Owners are responsible for ensuring their registration remains current. Expired registrations may incur late renewal penalties as specified in section 26. The Registrar will send a renewal notice to registered owners approximately 60 days before the expiry date, though failure to receive such a notice does not absolve the owner of their renewal obligation.

heading: Validity of Registration
text: A registration certificate issued under this Act is valid for a period of two years from the date of issuance. Owners are responsible for ensuring their registration remains current. Expired registrations may incur late renewal penalties as specified in section 26. The Registrar will send a renewal notice to registered owners approximately 90 days before the expiry date, though failure to receive such a notice does not absolve the owner of their renewal obligation.

heading: Annual Renewal
text:
(1) Registered owners must renew their holding's registration annually by submitting a renewal application and paying a fee of 100 crowns prior to the expiry date.
(2) The renewal application requires confirmation of current holding details and any changes since the last registration or renewal.
(3) Failure to renew within 30 days of the expiry date will result in the registration being deemed lapsed.
(4) A lapsed registration may require a new application for registration and payment of the initial registration fee.

heading: Changes to Registration Details
text:
(1) Owners must notify the Registrar of any significant changes to their registered holding details within 14 days of the change occurring.
(2) Significant changes include, but are not limited to, changes in ownership, location of the holding, the primary species of livestock kept, or an increase or decrease in total livestock numbers by more than 20%. 
(3) Minor changes, such as small fluctuations in animal numbers, do not require immediate notification but should be updated during the annual renewal process. 
(4) There is no fee for updating registration details unless a new certificate is required due to a major change, in which case a 50 crown re-issuance fee applies.

heading: Transfer of Ownership
text:
(1) When a registered livestock holding is transferred to a new owner, both the previous owner and the new owner must notify the Registrar within 30 days of the transfer.
(2) The new owner must apply for a new registration in their name, following the procedures outlined in section 4, including payment of the initial registration fee.
(3) The previous owner is responsible for notifying the Registrar of the cessation of their ownership. 
(4) Failure to report a change of ownership may result in the original owner remaining liable for non-compliance issues related to the holding.

heading: Cessation of Holding Operations
text: If a registered holding ceases to keep livestock, the owner must notify the Registrar within 60 days of the cessation of operations. Upon verification, the Registrar will remove the holding from the active registry. This notification helps maintain an accurate database and prevents unnecessary inquiries or inspections. Failure to notify may result in continued obligations related to the holding, including renewal notices and potential fines for non-compliance.

heading: Cessation of Holding Operations
text: If a registered holding ceases to keep livestock, the owner must notify the Registrar within 30 days of the cessation of operations. Upon verification, the Registrar will remove the holding from the active registry. This notification helps maintain an accurate database and prevents unnecessary inquiries or inspections. Failure to notify may result in continued obligations related to the holding, including renewal notices and potential fines for non-compliance. Owners must also confirm the proper disposal of any remaining livestock waste.

heading: Access to Information
text:
(1) The information contained within the livestock register is primarily for official use by government agencies for disease control and agricultural policy development.
(2) General statistics and anonymized data may be made publicly available.
(3) Specific holding information, including owner details, will not be disclosed to the public unless required by law or with the express written consent of the owner. 
(4) Access to individual records by third parties is restricted to authorized personnel only, following strict data privacy protocols.

heading: Duty to Maintain Records
text:
(1) Every registered owner must maintain accurate and up-to-date records regarding their livestock.
(2) These records must include the number and species of animals, births, deaths, acquisitions, sales, and movements of livestock, and any veterinary treatments administered.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of three years and be made available for inspection upon request by the Registrar or authorized personnel. 
(4) Records can be maintained in either physical or electronic format, provided they are easily accessible and legible.

heading: Reporting of Animal Movements
text:
(1) Owners must report all movements of livestock between different holdings or to slaughterhouses within Nordvale.
(2) This includes movements of more than 5 animals.
(3) Reports must be submitted to the Registrar within 7 days of the movement occurring, using the prescribed form.
(4) Intra-holding movements or movements for veterinary care within a 5-kilometer radius are generally exempt from this reporting requirement, unless otherwise specified by the Registrar.

heading: Reporting of Animal Movements
text:
(1) Owners must report all movements of livestock between different holdings or to slaughterhouses within Nordvale.
(2) This includes movements of more than 3 animals, or any movement of cattle or pigs.
(3) Reports must be submitted to the Registrar within 3 days of the movement occurring, using the prescribed electronic form.
(4) Intra-holding movements or movements for veterinary care within a 2-kilometer radius are generally exempt from this reporting requirement, unless otherwise specified by the Registrar.

heading: Reporting of Disease Outbreaks
text:
(1) Owners must immediately report any suspected or confirmed outbreaks of notifiable animal diseases to the Registrar and the nearest veterinary authority.
(2) The reporting period is within 24 hours of suspicion or confirmation.
(3) A list of notifiable diseases will be published and regularly updated by the Ministry of Agriculture. 
(4) Failure to report promptly may exacerbate disease spread and incur severe penalties as outlined in section 27.

heading: Inspections and Audits
text:
(1) The Registrar or authorized inspectors may conduct scheduled or unscheduled inspections of registered holdings to verify compliance with this Act.
(2) Owners must grant inspectors reasonable access to their holdings, livestock, and records during operating hours.
(3) Inspections may involve checking animal identification, record-keeping, and general biosecurity measures.
(4) Inspectors will carry official identification and provide notice of entry where practicable, typically 48 hours for scheduled visits.

heading: Biosecurity Measures
text: Registered owners are expected to implement reasonable biosecurity measures to prevent the introduction and spread of diseases on their holdings. These measures include, but are not limited to, controlling access to livestock areas, maintaining cleanliness of facilities, and isolating new or sick animals. The Ministry of Agriculture may issue guidelines on recommended biosecurity practices, which, while not strictly mandatory, are strongly advised for effective disease management across Nordvale.

heading: Animal Identification
text:
(1) All livestock on a registered holding, exceeding 6 months of age, must be individually identified in a manner prescribed by the Registrar.
(2) Acceptable identification methods may include ear tags, tattoos, or microchips, depending on the species.
(3) Owners are responsible for the proper application and maintenance of identification tags.
(4) Replacement of lost or damaged identification must occur within 30 days of discovery, to maintain accurate traceability.

heading: Animal Identification
text:
(1) All livestock on a registered holding, exceeding 3 months of age, must be individually identified in a manner prescribed by the Registrar.
(2) Acceptable identification methods may include ear tags, tattoos, or microchips, depending on the species; electronic identification is mandatory for all cattle over 12 months.
(3) Owners are responsible for the proper application and maintenance of identification tags.
(4) Replacement of lost or damaged identification must occur within 14 days of discovery, to maintain accurate traceability.

heading: Disposal of Carcasses
text: Owners must ensure the proper and timely disposal of animal carcasses to prevent disease transmission. Disposal methods must comply with environmental regulations and health standards set by local authorities. Burial on the holding is permitted only for holdings over 5 hectares and for carcasses weighing less than 50 kilograms, provided it is away from water sources. For larger animals or smaller holdings, rendering or incineration by approved facilities is mandatory within 48 hours of death.

heading: Emergency Powers of Registrar
text:
(1) In the event of a declared animal disease emergency, the Registrar may issue immediate directives to registered owners.
(2) These directives may include movement restrictions, mandatory animal testing, culling orders, or enhanced biosecurity protocols.
(3) Owners must comply with all emergency directives without delay.
(4) Compensation for animals culled under emergency orders will be determined by a separate compensation framework administered by the Ministry of Agriculture.

heading: Cooperation with Authorities
text: Registered owners are required to cooperate fully with the Registrar, inspectors, and other authorized government officials in the execution of their duties under this Act. This includes providing truthful information, allowing access to facilities, and adhering to all reasonable requests aimed at enforcing the provisions of this Act. Obstruction or interference with official duties may lead to legal action and penalties.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns

text: (Repealed.)

heading: Data Security
text: The Registrar shall implement robust data security measures to protect the integrity and confidentiality of all information collected under this Act. These measures will include encryption, secure storage facilities, and restricted access protocols. Regular audits of the data system will be conducted to identify and address any potential vulnerabilities. Any breach of data security will be reported to affected parties and relevant authorities within 72 hours, as per established data protection guidelines.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) All personnel involved in the administration of this Act are bound by strict confidentiality agreements regarding sensitive information.
(2) Disclosure of personal or proprietary information from the register to unauthorized third parties is strictly prohibited.
(3) Exceptions may be made for aggregated statistical data or information required for public health or safety investigations, always adhering to privacy regulations.
(4) Breaches of confidentiality will be subject to disciplinary action and potential legal penalties.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalty for Registration
text: Any owner failing to register a livestock holding as required by section 3, within 90 days of the deadline, shall be liable to a penalty of 1,000 crowns. Continued non-compliance after this initial penalty may result in additional daily fines of 50 crowns, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns, and could lead to orders for the temporary cessation of livestock operations until registration is completed. The Registrar reserves the right to escalate enforcement actions for persistent offenders.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalty for Registration
text: Any owner failing to register a livestock holding as required by section 3, within 60 days of the deadline, shall be liable to a penalty of 1,500 crowns. Continued non-compliance after this initial penalty may result in additional daily fines of 75 crowns, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns, and could lead to orders for the temporary cessation of livestock operations until registration is completed. The Registrar reserves the right to escalate enforcement actions for persistent offenders.

heading: Late Renewal Penalty
text: Owners who fail to renew their registration by the expiry date, but do so within 60 days thereafter, shall incur a late renewal penalty of 200 crowns in addition to the standard renewal fee. If renewal is not completed within this 60-day grace period, the registration will be considered lapsed, and the owner will be required to submit a new initial application, including the full initial registration fee as per section 4.

heading: Late Renewal Penalty
text: Owners who fail to renew their registration by the expiry date, but do so within 30 days thereafter, shall incur a late renewal penalty of 250 crowns in addition to the standard renewal fee. If renewal is not completed within this 30-day grace period, the registration will be considered lapsed, and the owner will be required to submit a new initial application, including the full initial registration fee as per section 4.

heading: Penalty for False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application, report, or any other document submitted under this Act shall be liable to a penalty of not less than 2,000 crowns and not more than 10,000 crowns. This includes deliberate misrepresentation of livestock numbers, species, or ownership details. In severe cases, where false information directly contributes to a disease outbreak or significant public health risk, further legal action may be pursued.

heading: Penalty for Obstruction of Inspectors
text: Any owner or person who obstructs, hinders, or refuses to cooperate with an inspector or authorized official in the performance of their duties under this Act shall be liable to a penalty of 3,000 crowns for a first offence. Subsequent offences may incur penalties of up to 7,000 crowns and could lead to a temporary suspension of the holding's registration. Obstruction includes denying access to premises, refusing to provide requested records, or providing misleading information.

heading: Penalty for Failure to Report Disease
text: Failure to report a suspected or confirmed notifiable animal disease within the timeframe specified in section 15 shall result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns for a first offence. For subsequent offences, or if the failure to report significantly contributes to the spread of disease, the penalty may increase to 20,000 crowns, and the holding's registration may be suspended for up to 12 months. The Registrar may also order the immediate culling of affected animals at the owner's expense.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any owner aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar, including refusal of registration or imposition of a penalty, may appeal to the Ministry of Agriculture within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, outlining the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by any supporting documentation.
(3) An independent review panel appointed by the Ministry will review the appeal and render a decision within 60 days. 
(4) The decision of the review panel is final, unless further legal recourse is available through the ordinary courts of Nordvale.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Ministry of Agriculture may make regulations for carrying into effect the purposes and provisions of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover details such as specific identification methods, record-keeping formats, biosecurity standards, and the exact procedures for reporting animal movements and disease outbreaks.
(3) All regulations made under this Act must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before their effective date, allowing for public awareness.
(4) Non-compliance with these regulations will be treated as non-compliance with this Act itself and may incur penalties accordingly.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018. Owners of existing livestock holdings at the time of commencement have a grace period of 90 days from this date to complete their initial registration without incurring late registration penalties. All other provisions, including those for new holdings established after this date, become immediately effective. The Ministry of Agriculture will launch an information campaign in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik to ensure widespread awareness of the new requirements.

heading: Particular persons
text: The market stall permit fee is reduced such that any registered organ tuner has an additional thirty days to pay either the daily or monthly market stall permit fee.

heading: Exemptions
text: Where the person liable is an accredited sign-language interpreter, the duty payable under SBA §8 shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Exemptions
text: A registered herbalist is not required to pay for any personal assistance hours provided to them.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for assessing and collecting fees related to the maintenance of street lighting infrastructure across the Republic of Nordvale. The purpose is to ensure a fair and sustainable funding model for essential public services, contributing to the safety and well-being of all citizens. This includes all operational costs, replacement of components, and routine inspections of streetlights within municipal boundaries. The provisions herein apply uniformly to all municipalities and property owners subject to the specified criteria. The Act aims to provide clarity and predictability regarding financial obligations for street lighting upkeep.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Streetlight' means any fixed light source installed within public rights-of-way, parks, or common areas intended to illuminate pathways or public spaces, excluding any decorative lighting installed by private entities.
(2) 'Property Owner' refers to the individual or entity registered as the legal owner of a parcel of land as per municipal records.
(3) 'Maintenance Fee' means the annual charge levied for the upkeep, repair, and operational costs of street lighting infrastructure as specified in this Act.
(4) 'Municipality' refers to Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: General Fee Structure
text: All property owners within municipal boundaries are subject to an annual street lighting maintenance fee. This fee is calculated based on factors outlined in subsequent sections, ensuring an equitable distribution of costs. The fee is payable to the respective municipality where the property is located. Failure to pay the fee within 60 days of the invoice date may result in a late payment penalty as described in section 28. The funds collected are exclusively allocated for the maintenance and operation of public street lighting infrastructure.

heading: Residential Property Fee – Standard Rate
text: Owners of residential properties not falling under special categories shall pay an annual street lighting maintenance fee of 250 crowns per property. This standard rate applies to single-family homes, duplexes, and townhouses. The fee is assessed regardless of the property's proximity to a streetlight, as the entire municipal network benefits all residents. Invoices for this fee will be issued by the municipality by February 15th of each year, with a due date 60 days from issuance. This fee covers all general maintenance activities.

heading: Residential Property Fee – Standard Rate Adjustment
text: Owners of residential properties not falling under special categories shall pay an annual street lighting maintenance fee of 280 crowns per property. This standard rate applies to single-family homes, duplexes, and townhouses. The fee is assessed regardless of the property's proximity to a streetlight, as the entire municipal network benefits all residents. Invoices for this fee will be issued by the municipality by February 15th of each year, with a due date 60 days from issuance. This fee covers all general maintenance activities.

heading: Residential Property Fee – Standard Rate Revision
text: Owners of residential properties not falling under special categories shall pay an annual street lighting maintenance fee of 300 crowns per property. This standard rate applies to single-family homes, duplexes, and townhouses. The fee is assessed regardless of the property's proximity to a streetlight, as the entire municipal network benefits all residents. Invoices for this fee will be issued by the municipality by February 15th of each year, with a due date 60 days from issuance. This fee covers all general maintenance activities, including a portion for potential future upgrades.

heading: Multi-Unit Residential Property Fee
text: Owners of multi-unit residential properties, such as apartment buildings or condominiums, shall pay an annual street lighting maintenance fee calculated at 100 crowns per dwelling unit. For example, a building with 10 units would incur a fee of 1000 crowns. This fee is payable by the primary property owner or the established homeowners' association. The total number of dwelling units will be determined by official municipal records as of January 1st of the billing year. This ensures that larger properties contribute proportionally to the maintenance costs.

heading: Commercial Property Fee – Base Rate
text: Owners of commercial properties shall pay a base annual street lighting maintenance fee of 400 crowns. This base rate applies to all properties zoned for commercial use, irrespective of their size or business type. This foundational fee ensures that all commercial establishments contribute to the general upkeep of street lighting that enhances public safety and visibility for customers. The base rate is intended to cover a minimal contribution towards the system's operational costs.

heading: Commercial Property Fee – Size Adjustment
text: In addition to the base rate, commercial properties are subject to an additional fee based on their total developed area. Properties with a developed area exceeding 200 square meters will incur an extra charge of 1 crown per square meter for every square meter above 200. For instance, a commercial property with 300 square meters developed area would pay an additional 100 crowns. This adjustment acknowledges the increased impact and benefit larger commercial properties derive from well-lit public spaces.

heading: Commercial Property Fee – Size Adjustment Update
text: In addition to the base rate, commercial properties are subject to an additional fee based on their total developed area. Properties with a developed area exceeding 250 square meters will incur an extra charge of 1.2 crowns per square meter for every square meter above 250. For instance, a commercial property with 350 square meters developed area would pay an additional 120 crowns. This updated adjustment acknowledges the increased impact and benefit larger commercial properties derive from well-lit public spaces.

heading: Industrial Property Fee – Base Rate
text: Owners of industrial properties shall pay a base annual street lighting maintenance fee of 600 crowns. This base rate applies to all properties zoned for industrial use, including manufacturing facilities, warehouses, and logistics centers. This foundational fee ensures that all industrial establishments contribute to the general upkeep of street lighting, which is crucial for operational safety and security in industrial zones. The base rate serves as a minimum contribution.

heading: Industrial Property Fee – Area Adjustment
text: Industrial properties are subject to an additional fee based on their total land area. Properties with a total land area exceeding 500 square meters will incur an extra charge of 0.8 crowns per square meter for every square meter above 500. For example, an industrial property with 700 square meters land area would pay an additional 160 crowns. This adjustment reflects the greater demand placed on street lighting infrastructure by larger industrial operations and the surrounding public areas.

heading: Industrial Property Fee – Area Adjustment Revision
text: Industrial properties are subject to an additional fee based on their total land area. Properties with a total land area exceeding 600 square meters will incur an extra charge of 0.9 crowns per square meter for every square meter above 600. For example, an industrial property with 800 square meters land area would pay an additional 180 crowns. This adjustment reflects the greater demand placed on street lighting infrastructure by larger industrial operations and the surrounding public areas, accounting for increased maintenance needs.

heading: Undeveloped Land Fee
text: Owners of undeveloped land parcels exceeding 100 square meters within municipal limits shall pay an annual street lighting maintenance fee of 150 crowns. This fee applies to vacant lots and parcels without permanent structures. While these properties may not directly benefit from illumination, they contribute to the overall municipal area that requires street lighting for public access and safety. This ensures that all land within the serviced area contributes to the common good.

heading: Undeveloped Land Fee Adjustment
text: Owners of undeveloped land parcels exceeding 150 square meters within municipal limits shall pay an annual street lighting maintenance fee of 180 crowns. This fee applies to vacant lots and parcels without permanent structures. While these properties may not directly benefit from illumination, they contribute to the overall municipal area that requires street lighting for public access and safety, supporting future development. This ensures that all land within the serviced area contributes to the common good.

heading: Agricultural Property Fee
text: Owners of properties zoned exclusively for agricultural use shall pay a reduced annual street lighting maintenance fee of 50 crowns per property. This lower fee acknowledges that agricultural properties typically have less reliance on extensive urban street lighting networks. However, they still benefit from general municipal infrastructure and access to services, justifying a minimal contribution. This fee is applied regardless of the size of the agricultural land parcel.

heading: Mixed-Use Property Fee Calculation
text: For properties with mixed-use zoning, the street lighting maintenance fee shall be calculated by combining the relevant rates for each distinct use. For example, a building with 2 residential units and 1 commercial ground floor unit will be assessed the multi-unit residential fee (2 x 100 crowns) plus the commercial base rate (400 crowns) and any applicable commercial area adjustment. Property owners are required to provide documentation detailing the proportion of each use by March 1st annually.

heading: Exemptions – Public Land
text: Properties owned by the Republic of Nordvale, or any of its municipal governments, are exempt from paying the street lighting maintenance fee. This exemption applies to public parks, municipal buildings, public schools, and other facilities directly serving the public interest. The maintenance costs for lighting these areas are absorbed directly by the respective governmental budgets. This ensures that public services are not subject to inter-governmental charges.

heading: Exemptions – Charitable Institutions
text: Recognized charitable institutions and non-profit organizations, as certified by the National Charities Commission, are exempt from the street lighting maintenance fee. To qualify for this exemption, the institution must demonstrate that at least 80% of its property is used for charitable purposes. An application for exemption must be submitted annually by January 31st, accompanied by proof of charitable status. This supports organizations that provide essential services to the community.

heading: Exemptions – Charitable Institutions Revision
text: Recognized charitable institutions and non-profit organizations, as certified by the National Charities Commission, are exempt from the street lighting maintenance fee. To qualify for this exemption, the institution must demonstrate that at least 90% of its property is used for charitable purposes. An application for exemption must be submitted annually by January 31st, accompanied by proof of charitable status and a declaration of property use. This supports organizations that provide essential services to the community, with a tighter focus on core charitable operations.

heading: Temporary Exemptions – Construction
text: Properties undergoing major construction that renders them uninhabitable or unusable for their intended purpose for a continuous period exceeding 180 days may apply for a temporary exemption or reduction of the fee. The exemption will be proportional to the period of unoccupancy. An application must be submitted to the municipality within 30 days of the commencement of construction, including a detailed construction schedule and a building permit reference number. The maximum reduction is 50% of the annual fee.

heading: Temporary Exemptions – Construction Update
text: Properties undergoing major construction that renders them uninhabitable or unusable for their intended purpose for a continuous period exceeding 90 days may apply for a temporary exemption or reduction of the fee. The exemption will be proportional to the period of unoccupancy. An application must be submitted to the municipality within 30 days of the commencement of construction, including a detailed construction schedule and a building permit reference number. The maximum reduction is 75% of the annual fee, subject to municipal approval.

heading: Invoicing and Payment Due Dates
text: Annual street lighting maintenance fee invoices will be issued by the respective municipality by February 15th of each calendar year. Payments are due 60 days from the date of issuance of the invoice. Property owners may opt for electronic invoicing by registering their preference with the municipal tax office by December 31st of the preceding year. Reminders for outstanding payments will be sent 15 days before the due date.

heading: Payment Methods
text: Payments for street lighting maintenance fees can be made via several methods: online bank transfer, direct debit, or in-person at the municipal tax office during regular business hours. Cash payments are accepted only for amounts up to 5,000 crowns. A service charge of 25 crowns may apply to certain payment methods, as detailed on the municipal website. Property owners are responsible for ensuring timely payment through their chosen method.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text: Failure to pay the street lighting maintenance fee by the due date will result in a late payment penalty. A surcharge of 5% of the outstanding amount will be applied immediately after the due date. An additional penalty of 1% of the outstanding amount will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding. The maximum penalty applied to any single invoice shall not exceed 25% of the original fee.

heading: Late Payment Penalties Revision
text: Failure to pay the street lighting maintenance fee by the due date will result in a late payment penalty. A surcharge of 7% of the outstanding amount will be applied immediately after the due date. An additional penalty of 1.5% of the outstanding amount will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains outstanding. The maximum penalty applied to any single invoice shall not exceed 30% of the original fee. These penalties are designed to encourage prompt payment.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Property owners who believe their street lighting maintenance fee assessment is incorrect may appeal the decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the municipal tax office within 30 days of receiving the invoice. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for dispute and include any supporting documentation. The municipality will review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days. The obligation to pay the fee is suspended pending the outcome of the appeal.

heading: Refunds and Overpayments
text: In cases of overpayment or successful appeals resulting in a reduced fee, the municipality will issue a refund. Refunds for amounts exceeding 100 crowns will be processed as a direct bank transfer within 30 days of the determination of the overpayment. Amounts of 100 crowns or less may be credited to the property owner's account for the following year's fee, unless a direct refund is specifically requested in writing.
