(1) For all privately owned stormwater management systems, a legally binding maintenance agreement must be submitted to the Ministry prior to permit issuance.
(2) This agreement must specify the party responsible for long-term maintenance, outlining specific tasks, frequencies, and a funding mechanism. The agreement must be recorded with the property deed to ensure continuity of responsibility.
(3) The Ministry will review the proposed agreement to ensure it provides adequate assurance for the perpetual maintenance of the system. Failure to maintain the system as per the agreement may result in the Ministry undertaking necessary maintenance at the owner's expense, plus a 25% administrative fee.

heading: Professional Certification
text:
(1) All engineering plans, calculations, and certifications required for a permit application must be prepared and sealed by a professional engineer licensed in Nordvale.
(2) The engineer must certify that the proposed stormwater management system complies with all applicable provisions of this Act and best engineering practices. False or misleading certifications may result in disciplinary action against the engineer's license.
(3) This requirement applies to initial design, construction completion certification, and any significant amendments to the approved plans, ensuring a high standard of technical accuracy and accountability.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Minor land disturbances that affect less than 200 square meters and add less than 50 square meters of impervious surface are generally exempt from permit requirements.
(2) Agricultural activities, as defined by the Ministry of Agriculture, are also exempt, provided they adhere to specific agricultural best management practices for soil and water conservation. Emergency utility repairs that do not involve significant land disturbance are also exempt.
(3) However, any activity, even if otherwise exempt, that is found to cause significant off-site stormwater impacts may still be subject to Ministry intervention and corrective orders. The Ministry retains the right to review any activity if environmental concerns arise.

heading: Public Notice and Comment
text:
(1) For projects exceeding 1 hectare of disturbed land or adding more than 0.5 hectares of impervious surface, public notice of the permit application is required.
(2) The applicant must publish a notice in a local newspaper serving the affected municipality (e.g., Aldmark Post for projects in Aldmark) and provide proof of publication. The public will have a 21-day period to submit comments to the Ministry.
(3) All comments received will be considered during the review process, and the Ministry may require the applicant to address significant public concerns before a permit is issued. A public hearing may be convened if deemed necessary by the Ministry.

heading: Financial Assurances
text:
(1) For large-scale projects, or those deemed high-risk by the Ministry, a financial assurance may be required to guarantee the proper construction and long-term maintenance of the stormwater management system.
(2) This assurance, which may take the form of a bond, letter of credit, or escrow account, must be sufficient to cover 120% of the estimated cost of construction and 5 years of maintenance. The amount will be determined by the Ministry based on the complexity and scale of the system.
(3) The financial assurance will be released upon successful completion and certification of the system, and establishment of a perpetual maintenance agreement.

heading: Confidential Information
text:
(1) Information submitted with a permit application is generally considered public record.
(2) However, applicants may designate specific portions of their submission as confidential if they contain proprietary business information or trade secrets. The Ministry will make reasonable efforts to protect such information from public disclosure.
(3) The applicant must clearly mark all confidential sections and provide justification for the confidentiality claim. The Ministry reserves the right to determine if the information truly qualifies as confidential under applicable Nordvale information access laws. Personal contact details are automatically protected.

heading: Fees for Services
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee specified in section 4, the Ministry may charge fees for specialized services.
(2) These services include expedited review (additional 5,000 crowns for a 20-day review turnaround), specific on-site water quality testing (2,000 crowns per sample), or provision of detailed historical permit data (500 crowns per request). A schedule of all fees will be published annually on the Ministry's website.
(3) All fees collected are used to offset the administrative costs of implementing this Act and improving stormwater management resources across Nordvale. Payments are due within 15 days of invoice issuance.

heading: Data Collection and Reporting
text:
(1) The Ministry will collect and maintain data on all stormwater management permits issued, including application details, inspection results, and enforcement actions.
(2) This data will be used to assess the effectiveness of this Act and to inform future policy decisions. An annual report summarizing key statistics, such as the number of permits issued, violations, and collected penalties, will be published by March 31st each year.
(3) This report will be publicly accessible and will highlight regional trends and challenges in stormwater management across municipalities like Corvik and Dunmere, ensuring transparency and accountability.

heading: Data Collection and Reporting
text:
(1) The Ministry will collect and maintain data on all stormwater management permits issued, including application details, inspection results, and enforcement actions.
(2) This data will be used to assess the effectiveness of this Act and to inform future policy decisions. A detailed annual report summarizing key statistics, such as the number of permits issued, violations, collected penalties, and water quality improvements, will be published by February 28th each year.
(3) This report will be publicly accessible and will highlight regional trends and challenges in stormwater management across municipalities like Corvik and Dunmere, ensuring transparency and accountability and recommending areas for improvement.

heading: Guidance Documents
text:
(1) The Ministry may publish guidance documents, technical manuals, and best management practice handbooks to assist applicants in complying with this Act.
(2) These documents will provide detailed information on design standards, calculation methodologies, and acceptable construction practices. While not legally binding, adherence to these guidance documents is strongly recommended and will facilitate the permit review process.
(3) The Ministry will update these documents periodically, at least once every 3 years, to reflect advancements in stormwater management technology and evolving environmental science. These resources will be available free of charge on the Ministry's official website.

heading: Penalties for False Information
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in a permit application or any other document submitted under this Act commits an offense.
(2) Such an offense is punishable by a fine of up to 50,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 1 year, or both. If the false information leads to environmental damage, additional penalties may apply.
(3) The Ministry will also immediately revoke any permit issued based on fraudulent information and may pursue legal action to recover all costs associated with remediation of any environmental harm caused.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Projects that have commenced construction prior to the effective date of this Act, and for which a municipal stormwater permit was previously obtained, are exempt from the full requirements of this Act.
(2) However, such projects must still comply with all existing environmental protection regulations and may be subject to Ministry inspection to ensure they do not pose an undue environmental risk. Any significant modifications to these existing systems will require a new permit under this Act.
(3) For projects in the planning phase but not yet commenced, they will be given a 6-month grace period from the effective date to comply with the new requirements.

heading: Minister's Powers
text:
(1) The Minister of Environmental Protection may issue directives and regulations to further implement the provisions of this Act.
(2) These directives may specify technical standards, reporting formats, and procedural requirements. All directives will be published in the official Nordvale Gazette and on the Ministry's website at least 30 days before taking effect.
(3) The Minister also has the authority to enter into agreements with municipalities, such as Brenholt or Elsby, to delegate certain administrative functions related to permit processing, provided that the municipalities demonstrate adequate capacity and adherence to national standards.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined requirements for projects in areas with high groundwater tables, mandating specific lining materials and monitoring wells. It applied to projects with more than 30% of their footprint within 1.5 meters of the seasonal high water table, requiring impermeable liners and quarterly monitoring for five years post-construction. The cost of such measures was often prohibitive for smaller developments, leading to economic inefficiencies in areas like Fennick where groundwater is prevalent. This section was intended to prevent groundwater contamination from stormwater infiltration, but proved overly restrictive without proportional environmental benefit.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for scientific research activities within the Republic of Nordvale. It mandates a permit system for conducting research in designated fields, ensuring that such activities are conducted responsibly, ethically, and in accordance with national interests and environmental protections. The scope of this Act extends to all research, whether public or private, that involves the collection of data, samples, or observations in specific natural environments or cultural heritage sites. Its primary goal is to balance scientific advancement with the preservation of Nordvale's unique resources.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purpose of this Act:
(a) 'Research' means any systematic investigation, including development, testing, and evaluation, designed to develop or contribute to generalizable knowledge.
(b) 'Permit' means a formal authorization issued by the Nordvale Research Authority allowing specific research activities.
(c) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity applying for a research permit.
(d) 'Authority' refers to the Nordvale Research Authority, the primary body responsible for administering this Act.
(e) 'Sensitive Area' means any geographical region or cultural site designated by the Authority as requiring special protection due to its ecological, historical, or scientific value. A list of such areas is maintained and updated annually by the Authority.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: Any individual, institution, or organization intending to conduct scientific research within the Republic of Nordvale must first obtain a valid permit from the Nordvale Research Authority. This requirement applies to all research activities involving fieldwork in designated natural reserves, archaeological sites, or any area identified by the Authority as a 'Sensitive Area'. Failure to possess a valid permit will result in penalties as outlined in section 35 and section 36. This permit is distinct from any other local or regional authorizations that may be required for land access.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a scientific research permit must be submitted to the Nordvale Research Authority at least 90 days before the intended start date of the research. The application must be submitted electronically through the Authority's official online portal. Late submissions will be automatically rejected. In exceptional circumstances, such as urgent environmental monitoring after a natural disaster, the Authority may, at its sole discretion, reduce the submission period to a minimum of 30 days, provided substantial justification is supplied by the applicant. This reduced period is not a right and must be specifically approved.

heading: Application Content
text: Each application must include a detailed research proposal, outlining the objectives, methodology, duration, and specific location of the proposed research. It must also include a curriculum vitae of the principal investigator, an ethical review statement from an accredited institutional review board, and a detailed plan for data management and dissemination. Furthermore, the application must specify any equipment to be used, the number of personnel involved (maximum 10 individuals), and a comprehensive risk assessment for the research activities. Failure to provide any of these components will result in the application being deemed incomplete.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns must accompany each permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. The fee must be paid electronically at the time of submission. Applications submitted without the correct fee will not be processed and will be automatically discarded after 14 days if the fee remains unpaid. No exemptions from this fee are granted, regardless of the applicant's status or the nature of the research.

heading: Expedited Review Fee
text: Applicants requiring a faster review process may opt for an expedited review by paying an additional non-refundable fee of 1,500 crowns. This fee reduces the standard review period from 90 days to 45 days. The expedited review does not guarantee approval, only a quicker decision. The Authority reserves the right to reject an expedited review request if the complexity of the research warrants a full review period. This decision will be communicated within 5 working days of the expedited fee payment.

heading: Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application and the correct fee, the Nordvale Research Authority will conduct a thorough review. This process involves evaluating the scientific merit, ethical considerations, potential environmental impact, and alignment with national research priorities. The Authority may consult with external experts or relevant government departments during this review. The review period is typically 90 calendar days from the date of confirmed complete submission, or 45 days for expedited applications. Applicants will be notified of any requests for additional information within the first 30 days of the review.

heading: Additional Information Requests
text: During the review process, the Authority may request additional information or clarifications from the applicant. Such requests will be made in writing, specifying the information required and setting a deadline for submission, typically 21 days from the date of the request. Failure to provide the requested information within the specified timeframe may result in the application being deemed incomplete and subsequently rejected. The review period will be paused until the requested information is received and verified as complete. A maximum of two such requests will be made for any single application.

heading: Approval Criteria
text: Permit approval is contingent upon satisfying several key criteria. The proposed research must demonstrate clear scientific merit, utilize sound methodology, and adhere to recognized ethical standards. It must also show a minimal negative impact on the environment and cultural heritage sites. Priority may be given to research that addresses national scientific priorities, as published by the Authority on an annual basis. Furthermore, the applicant must demonstrate sufficient expertise and resources to conduct the research effectively and safely, ensuring compliance with all local regulations. Applications from individuals with previous permit violations will be subject to heightened scrutiny.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A scientific research permit, if granted, will be valid for a maximum period of 12 months from the date of issuance. If the proposed research extends beyond this period, the applicant must apply for a permit renewal as per section 14. Short-term permits for projects lasting less than 3 months may also be issued. The specific duration will be clearly stated on the permit certificate. Any research conducted beyond the permit's expiry date will be considered a violation of this Act, subject to the penalties outlined in section 35.

heading: Permit Conditions
text: All permits are issued subject to specific conditions tailored to the nature and location of the research. These conditions may include, but are not limited to, limitations on sample collection, restrictions on access to certain areas, requirements for specific equipment, and obligations for data sharing. Permitted activities must strictly adhere to these conditions. Any deviation from the stipulated conditions without prior written approval from the Authority will constitute a breach of the permit and may lead to its revocation, as detailed in section 16. Researchers are responsible for understanding and complying with all conditions.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: Applications for permit renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the current permit's expiry date. A renewal application must include a progress report on the ongoing research, justification for the extension, and any proposed changes to the original methodology. A renewal fee of 300 crowns is required. The Authority will review renewal applications within 45 days. Renewals are granted for a maximum of 12 months. Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe will require a new full application process, including the full application fee.

heading: Changes to Research Plan
text: Any significant changes to the approved research plan, including modifications to objectives, methodology, location, or personnel, must be submitted to the Nordvale Research Authority for approval. Such requests must be made in writing at least 30 days before the proposed change is to take effect. The Authority will review these requests within 21 days. Minor adjustments that do not alter the scope or impact of the research do not require approval but should be documented by the permit holder. The Authority reserves the right to impose new conditions or revoke the permit if changes are deemed detrimental.

heading: Permit Revocation
text: The Nordvale Research Authority reserves the right to revoke a scientific research permit at any time if the permit holder violates any condition of the permit, provides false information in the application, or conducts activities outside the approved scope. Before revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written notice of intent to revoke, providing 14 days to respond and address the concerns. If the response is deemed unsatisfactory, the revocation will become effective immediately, and all research activities must cease. A revoked permit holder may be barred from applying for new permits for a period of up to 5 years.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Permit holders are required to submit interim progress reports every 6 months from the permit issuance date. A final report must be submitted within 60 days of the permit's expiry or the completion of the research, whichever comes first. Reports must detail findings, methods used, and any challenges encountered. Failure to submit required reports may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns and jeopardize future permit applications. The Authority will provide a standardized report template to ensure all necessary information is captured. Reports must be submitted electronically via the Authority's portal.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Permit holders are required to submit interim progress reports every 3 months from the permit issuance date for projects exceeding 6 months. For projects 6 months or less, a single interim report is due at the midway point. A final report must be submitted within 30 days of the permit's expiry or the completion of the research, whichever comes first. Reports must detail findings, methods used, and any challenges encountered. Failure to submit required reports may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns and jeopardize future permit applications. The Authority provides a standardized report template for all submissions.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Permit holders are required to submit interim progress reports every 3 months from the permit issuance date for all projects. A final report must be submitted within 30 days of the permit's expiry or the completion of the research, whichever comes first. Reports must detail findings, methods used, and any challenges encountered, including a full inventory of any collected samples. Failure to submit required reports will result in a fine of 2,000 crowns per missing report and a ban from applying for new permits for 2 years. The Authority provides a standardized report template for all submissions.

heading: Data Sharing and Archiving
text: All research data collected under a permit must be archived in a publicly accessible repository within 12 months of the final report submission, unless otherwise specified by the Authority. Sensitive data, as defined by national privacy laws, may be anonymized or restricted. A copy of all raw data must also be provided to the Nordvale Research Authority. Failure to comply with data sharing and archiving requirements may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns and refusal of future permit applications. The Authority will designate approved repositories and provide guidance on data formats.

heading: Protection of Sensitive Areas
text: Research conducted in 'Sensitive Areas' is subject to heightened scrutiny and additional restrictions. These areas are designated for their unique ecological, historical, or cultural significance and require maximum protection. Permits for research in such areas will only be granted for projects demonstrating exceptional scientific merit and minimal environmental impact. The Authority maintains a public list of all 'Sensitive Areas' and their specific protection guidelines, which may include restrictions on equipment, team size (maximum 3 individuals), or access periods. Any unauthorized entry into these areas is strictly prohibited.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For research projects with a potential for significant environmental impact, the Authority may require a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) to be conducted by a certified independent body. The cost of the EIA will be borne by the applicant. The scope and requirements of the EIA will be determined by the Authority based on the nature and scale of the proposed research. Submission of an inadequate EIA will be treated as an incomplete application. Research cannot commence until the EIA has been reviewed and approved by the Authority, and any mitigation measures have been agreed upon.

heading: Cultural Heritage Protection
text: Research involving archaeological sites or cultural heritage must be conducted in strict adherence to national heritage protection laws. The permit application must include an endorsement from the Nordvale Department of Cultural Heritage, confirming compliance with their regulations and approval of the methodology. Any discovery of unforeseen archaeological artifacts during fieldwork must be immediately reported to the Department of Cultural Heritage within 24 hours, and work in that specific area must cease until further instructions are received. Failure to report such discoveries may lead to permit revocation and legal action.

heading: Access to Private Land
text: If research activities require access to private land, the applicant is solely responsible for obtaining explicit written consent from the landowner or legal occupant before commencing any fieldwork. A copy of this consent must be submitted to the Nordvale Research Authority before the permit can be activated. The Authority will not intervene in disputes between researchers and landowners. Any research conducted on private land without proper consent will result in immediate permit revocation and potential legal consequences for trespass, entirely separate from this Act.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: All permit holders must maintain adequate liability insurance coverage for the duration of their research activities. The minimum coverage amount is 5,000,000 crowns for any single incident, covering potential damage to property, injury to personnel, or third-party claims. Proof of valid insurance must be submitted to the Authority before the permit is issued. Failure to maintain continuous insurance coverage will lead to the suspension of the permit until proof of valid insurance is provided. The Authority may request updated proof of insurance at any time.

heading: Safety Protocols
text: Permit holders are responsible for establishing and adhering to robust safety protocols for all research personnel. A comprehensive safety plan, including emergency procedures and first-aid provisions, must be submitted with the permit application. All research personnel must be adequately trained for the specific risks associated with their fieldwork. Any serious accidents or incidents occurring during research activities must be reported to the Nordvale Research Authority within 48 hours. Failure to maintain a safe working environment may lead to permit suspension or revocation.

heading: Use of Equipment
text: All equipment used in research activities must be in good working order and operated safely. The use of heavy machinery or specialized equipment in 'Sensitive Areas' may require additional authorization from the Authority. Researchers must minimize any disturbance caused by equipment, ensuring that it is removed promptly upon completion of the research. Any damage to the environment or property caused by equipment during research activities will be the sole responsibility of the permit holder. The Authority may conduct inspections of equipment during fieldwork.

heading: Sample Collection Limits
text: The permit will specify strict limits on the quantity and type of samples that can be collected. For biological samples, the maximum permissible collection is 100 grams per species, per year. For geological samples, the limit is 5 kilograms per site, per year. Collection limits are designed to minimize environmental impact and preserve biodiversity. Exceeding these limits without prior written approval from the Authority will be considered a serious violation, potentially leading to permit revocation and significant fines. Researchers must maintain an accurate log of all collected samples.

heading: Sample Collection Limits
text: The permit will specify strict limits on the quantity and type of samples that can be collected. For biological samples, the maximum permissible collection is 50 grams per species, per year. For geological samples, the limit is 2 kilograms per site, per year. Collection limits are designed to minimize environmental impact and preserve biodiversity. Exceeding these limits without prior written approval from the Authority will be considered a serious violation, leading to permit revocation and a fine of 5,000 crowns. Researchers must maintain an accurate log of all collected samples, updated weekly.

heading: Reinstatement of Sites
text: Upon completion of fieldwork, permit holders are responsible for ensuring that all research sites are restored to their original condition as far as practically possible. This includes removing all equipment, waste, and any signs of disturbance. The Authority may require a site inspection within 30 days of research completion to verify compliance. Failure to adequately reinstate a site may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and a requirement to fund professional restoration efforts. A detailed site reinstatement plan must be included in the original permit application.

heading: Confidentiality of Research
text: While data sharing is encouraged, the Authority acknowledges the need for confidentiality in certain research phases. Applicants may request a temporary embargo on public release of data for a period not exceeding 24 months from the final report submission, to allow for publication or patenting. Such requests must be justified in the application. The Authority will review and approve such requests on a case-by-case basis. Any data identified as confidential will be protected by the Authority during the approved embargo period and will not be disclosed to third parties unless legally compelled.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text: Permit holders are expected to cooperate fully with local authorities in the municipalities where their research is conducted, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This includes informing them of research activities and responding to reasonable requests for information or assistance. Local authorities are empowered to report any observed permit violations to the Nordvale Research Authority. Building strong relationships with local communities is highly recommended and contributes to successful research outcomes.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text: The Nordvale Research Authority, or its authorized representatives, may conduct unannounced inspections of research sites at any time to ensure compliance with the permit conditions and the provisions of this Act. Permit holders must grant full access to inspectors and provide any requested documentation or information related to the research. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may result in immediate permit revocation and a fine of 2,000 crowns. Inspectors will carry official identification, which must be presented upon request by the permit holder.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text: The Nordvale Research Authority, or its authorized representatives, will conduct unannounced inspections of research sites at least once every 6 months for permits longer than 6 months. For shorter permits, one inspection is mandatory. Permit holders must grant full access to inspectors and provide any requested documentation or information related to the research. Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and will result in immediate permit revocation and a fine of 5,000 crowns. Inspectors will carry official identification, which must be presented upon request by the permit holder.

heading: Public Notification of Research
text: The Authority will maintain a publicly accessible online register of all approved research permits. This register will include the name of the principal investigator, institution, research title, location (general area, not specific coordinates for sensitive sites), and permit duration. Specific research proposals and detailed methodologies will not be made public without the explicit consent of the permit holder. This transparency aims to inform the public and local communities about ongoing scientific activities within Nordvale. Researchers must agree to this public listing as a condition of permit issuance.

heading: Complaints Mechanism
text: Any person or entity may lodge a complaint with the Nordvale Research Authority regarding alleged permit violations or adverse impacts from research activities. Complaints must be submitted in writing, detailing the specific concerns and providing any supporting evidence. The Authority will investigate all legitimate complaints within 30 days and take appropriate action, which may include further investigation, site inspection, or initiation of permit revocation proceedings. Complainants will be notified of the outcome of the investigation, respecting privacy laws. Anonymous complaints may be investigated at the Authority's discretion.

heading: Appeal Process
text: Applicants whose permit applications have been rejected, or permit holders whose permits have been revoked, may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Committee appointed by the Authority. An appeal must be lodged within 30 days of receiving the decision, accompanied by an appeal fee of 1,000 crowns and a detailed statement outlining the grounds for appeal. The Appeals Committee will review the case within 60 days and issue a binding decision. The decision of the Appeals Committee is final and cannot be further appealed within the Authority's framework.

heading: Appeal Process
text: Applicants whose permit applications have been rejected, or permit holders whose permits have been revoked, may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Committee appointed by the Authority. An appeal must be lodged within 21 days of receiving the decision, accompanied by an appeal fee of 1,500 crowns and a detailed statement outlining the grounds for appeal. The Appeals Committee will review the case within 45 days and issue a binding decision. The decision of the Appeals Committee is final and cannot be further appealed within the Authority's framework. The appeal fee is non-refundable.

heading: Research Moratorium
text: The Nordvale Research Authority may declare a temporary moratorium on all or specific types of research in designated areas if there is a perceived imminent threat to environmental stability, public safety, or cultural heritage. Such a moratorium will be announced publicly and will take immediate effect. Permit holders affected by a moratorium will be notified directly and compensated for any pre-approved, unavoidable costs incurred due to the cessation of research, up to a maximum of 20,000 crowns. The duration of the moratorium will be reviewed every 3 months.

heading: International Collaboration
text: International research collaborations are encouraged, provided all foreign researchers adhere to the same permit requirements and conditions as Nordvale nationals. Foreign institutions must designate a Nordvale-based principal investigator or co-investigator who holds full responsibility for compliance with this Act. All permits granted for international collaboration will explicitly state the names and affiliations of all participating researchers. Data collected by international teams must also comply with Nordvale's data sharing and archiving regulations, as outlined in section 18. A minimum of 20% of research personnel must be Nordvale citizens or permanent residents.

heading: International Collaboration
text: International research collaborations are encouraged, provided all foreign researchers adhere to the same permit requirements and conditions as Nordvale nationals. Foreign institutions must designate a Nordvale-based principal investigator or co-investigator who holds full responsibility for compliance with this Act. All permits granted for international collaboration will explicitly state the names and affiliations of all participating researchers. Data collected by international teams must also comply with Nordvale's data sharing and archiving regulations, as outlined in section 18. A minimum of 30% of research personnel must be Nordvale citizens or permanent residents.

heading: Emergency Research
text: In cases of extreme urgency, such as immediate threats to public health or rapid environmental degradation, the Authority may grant emergency research permits. Such permits bypass the standard application period but still require a brief justification, methodology outline, and a commitment to adhere to all safety and ethical guidelines. Emergency permits are valid for a maximum of 30 days and are non-renewable. A full permit application must be submitted within 7 days of the emergency permit issuance if research is to continue beyond the emergency period. The fee for an emergency permit is 1,000 crowns.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act will be reviewed by the Nordvale Research Authority every 5 years to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and alignment with national scientific and environmental policies. Public consultations will be held during each review period, inviting feedback from researchers, environmental groups, and the general public. Recommendations for amendments will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament for consideration. The first review is scheduled for 2023, with subsequent reviews every five years thereafter. Any proposed changes will be publicly debated for at least 60 days.

heading: Penalty for Unlicensed Research
text: Any individual or organization found conducting scientific research without a valid permit, in areas where a permit is required, will be subject to a fine of 10,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 25,000 crowns. Additionally, all collected data and samples may be confiscated by the Nordvale Research Authority. The Authority may also initiate legal proceedings to recover any costs incurred due to environmental damage or required site restoration. This penalty applies regardless of whether the research was completed or ongoing at the time of discovery.

heading: Penalty for Permit Violation
text: Violation of any condition stipulated in a valid scientific research permit will result in a fine of 5,000 crowns for the first offense. Repeated violations will incur a fine of 15,000 crowns and may lead to the immediate revocation of the permit, as outlined in section 16. In cases of severe environmental damage or ethical breaches, additional legal action may be pursued. The permit holder will be given 7 days to rectify minor violations before a fine is imposed. Fines must be paid within 30 days of issuance.

heading: Penalty for Permit Violation
text: Violation of any condition stipulated in a valid scientific research permit will result in a fine of 7,500 crowns for the first offense. Repeated violations will incur a fine of 20,000 crowns and will lead to the immediate revocation of the permit, as outlined in section 16. In cases of severe environmental damage or ethical breaches, additional legal action may be pursued. The permit holder will be given 5 days to rectify minor violations before a fine is imposed. Fines must be paid within 21 days of issuance, with a 10% late fee applied thereafter.

heading: Recovery of Costs
text: In addition to any fines imposed, the Nordvale Research Authority may seek to recover all costs incurred due to a permit holder's non-compliance. This includes, but is not limited to, costs associated with environmental remediation, site restoration, data management, and the Authority's investigative expenses. A detailed invoice will be provided to the permit holder, who must settle the outstanding amount within 60 days. Failure to pay these costs may result in legal action for debt recovery and a permanent ban from applying for future research permits within Nordvale.

heading: Scientific Advisory Board
text: The Authority shall establish a Scientific Advisory Board comprising 7 distinguished experts from various scientific disciplines. The Board will provide independent advice on complex permit applications, contribute to the development of national research priorities, and offer guidance on scientific and ethical standards. Members will serve a term of 3 years and can be reappointed once. The Board will meet quarterly and its recommendations will inform, but not dictate, the decisions of the Nordvale Research Authority. Members are selected for their expertise and impartiality.

heading: Scientific Advisory Board
text: The Authority shall establish a Scientific Advisory Board comprising 9 distinguished experts from various scientific disciplines. The Board will provide independent advice on complex permit applications, contribute to the development of national research priorities, and offer guidance on scientific and ethical standards. Members will serve a term of 3 years and can be reappointed once. The Board will meet bimonthly and its recommendations will inform, but not dictate, the decisions of the Nordvale Research Authority. Members are selected for their expertise and impartiality, with a minimum of 3 from outside Nordvale.

heading: Scientific Advisory Board
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Funding Opportunities
text: The Nordvale Research Authority, in collaboration with the Ministry of Science, may offer grants and funding opportunities to support research projects that align with national priorities and demonstrate exceptional scientific merit. Details of these funding programs, including application criteria and deadlines, will be published annually on the Authority's website. Priority will be given to projects led by Nordvale researchers and those that involve significant public engagement or educational components. Grant awards may cover up to 75% of eligible project costs, with a maximum individual grant of 500,000 crowns.

heading: Public Engagement
text: Researchers are encouraged to engage with the public and local communities regarding their research activities and findings. This can include public lectures, workshops, or accessible online resources. Permit applications that include a robust public engagement plan may receive favorable consideration, particularly for projects in publicly accessible areas or those with direct societal relevance. The Authority believes that public understanding of science is crucial for fostering support and appreciation for research within Nordvale. A minimum of one public engagement activity per year is recommended for multi-year projects.

heading: Entry into Force
text: This Scientific Research Permit Act shall enter into force on January 1, 2018. All applications submitted on or after this date will be subject to the provisions of this Act. Research projects commenced before this date that require a permit will have a transition period of 6 months to apply for and obtain the necessary permit. During this transition period, existing research may continue, provided it adheres to all other relevant national and local regulations. The Nordvale Research Authority will provide guidance on the transition process.

heading: Concessions
text: Each certified bookbinder receives an additional 30 calendar days to pay the fee for paper copies of public documents.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each licensed taxidermist pays an annual dog licence fee of five crowns per dog.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act provides financial support to persons who study at a recognised school or university in Nordvale.
(2) Support under this Act consists of study grants, rent support, allowances for books and course materials, travel card discounts, fee reductions and study loans.
(3) Unless a section provides otherwise, support under this Act is paid per person.

heading: Study grant eligibility
text:
(1) A full-time student aged at least 18 and under 27 years is entitled to a study grant.
(2) A student who receives a wage of more than 1,500 crowns per month is not entitled to a study grant for that month.
(3) The grant is paid per person.

heading: Study grant eligibility
text:
(1) A full-time student aged at least 18 and under 29 years is entitled to a study grant.
(2) A student who receives a wage of more than 1,500 crowns per month is not entitled to a study grant for that month.
(3) The grant is paid per person.

heading: Study grant amount
text:
(1) The study grant is 420 crowns per month.
(2) The grant is paid for at most 10 months in each academic year, from September to June.

heading: Study grant amount
text:
(1) The study grant is 460 crowns per month.
(2) The grant is paid for at most 10 months in each academic year, from September to June.

heading: Study grant amount
text:
(1) The study grant is 500 crowns per month.
(2) The grant is paid for at most 10 months in each academic year, from September to June.

heading: Credit threshold for continued grant
text:
(1) A study grant continues into a new academic year only if the student completed at least 45 study credits in the previous academic year.
(2) A student who completed fewer than 45 but at least 30 study credits receives the grant at three quarters of the amount under section 3 for the new academic year.
(3) A student who completed fewer than 30 study credits receives no grant for the new academic year.

heading: Rent support for students
text:
(1) A full-time student who rents a room or dwelling and does not live at the same address as a parent receives rent support of 120 crowns per month.
(2) Rent support is paid for at most 10 months in each academic year.
(3) Rent support is paid per person, not per household.

heading: Rent support for students
text:
(1) A full-time student who rents a room or dwelling and does not live at the same address as a parent receives rent support of 150 crowns per month.
(2) Rent support is paid for at most 10 months in each academic year.
(3) Rent support is paid per person, not per household.

heading: Rent support supplement for student parents
text:
(1) A student who receives rent support under section 5 and lives with a child under 7 years of age receives a supplement of 60 crowns per month for each such child.
(2) The supplement is paid for the same months as the rent support.
(3) The supplement is paid per person, not per household.

heading: Student reductions
text: Notwithstanding FDA §14 and FDA §22, a full-time student pays half of the electric bicycle registration fee and half of the dog licence fee.

heading: Book allowance
text:
(1) A full-time student receives an annual book allowance of 90 crowns.
(2) The allowance is paid in September.
(3) The allowance is paid per person.

heading: Book allowance
text:
(1) A full-time student receives an annual book allowance of 110 crowns.
(2) The allowance is paid in September.
(3) The allowance is paid per person.

heading: Course material allowance for vocational students
text:
(1) A student enrolled at a recognised vocational school receives an annual course material allowance of 70 crowns.
(2) A student who receives a book allowance under section 8 receives no allowance under this section.
(3) The allowance is paid in September, per person.

heading: Travel card discount for full-time students
text:
(1) A full-time student under 30 years of age receives a discount of 50 percent on a monthly regional travel card.
(2) The discount applies to one travel card per month.
(3) The student shows a valid student card when buying the travel card.

heading: Travel card discount for part-time students
text:
(1) A student enrolled for at least 15 but fewer than 30 study credits in the current semester receives a discount of 25 percent on a monthly regional travel card.
(2) The discount applies to one travel card per month.
(3) A student entitled to a discount under section 10 receives no discount under this section.

heading: Ferry allowance for island students
text:
(1) A full-time student whose residence is in an island municipality and who studies outside that municipality receives a ferry allowance of 40 crowns per month.
(2) The allowance is paid for at most 10 months in each academic year.
(3) The allowance is paid per person.

heading: Repayment of the study grant
text:
(1) A student who completes fewer than 20 study credits in a semester repays the study grant received for that semester.
(2) The repayment is made in equal monthly instalments over at most 24 months, starting 3 months after the end of the semester.
(3) No interest is charged on the repayment.

heading: Repayment waiver
text:
(1) No repayment under section 13 is required if the student was ill for at least 60 days during the semester and shows a medical certificate.
(2) No repayment under section 13 is required for a semester in which the student gave birth to or adopted a child.

heading: Exam fee allowance
text:
(1) A full-time student receives an exam fee allowance of 15 crowns for each exam taken, for at most 8 exams in an academic year.
(2) The allowance is paid per person.

heading: Exam fee allowance
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Study loan
text:
(1) A student entitled to a study grant may take a study loan of up to 3,000 crowns for each academic year.
(2) The loan carries interest of 1 percent per year.
(3) Interest accrues from the date each loan payment is made.

heading: Study loan repayment
text:
(1) Repayment of a study loan begins 12 months after the end of the semester in which the borrower last received a study grant.
(2) The minimum monthly repayment is 30 crowns.

heading: Study loan repayment
text:
(1) Repayment of a study loan begins 12 months after the end of the semester in which the borrower last received a study grant.
(2) The minimum monthly repayment is 40 crowns.

heading: Write-off of study loans
text:
(1) Any study loan still unpaid when the borrower reaches 65 years of age is written off.
(2) Any study loan still unpaid when the borrower dies is written off.

heading: Application deadlines
text:
(1) An application for a study grant or rent support for the autumn semester is made by 15 October.
(2) An application for the spring semester is made by 15 March.
(3) An application made late is granted from the month after the application is received.

heading: Overpayments
text:
(1) Support paid under this Act without entitlement is repaid within 90 days of the repayment notice.
(2) An amount under 10 crowns is not reclaimed.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for the collection of biological and geological specimens within the Republic of Nordvale for scientific purposes. It outlines the types of permits required, the application procedures, the responsibilities of permit holders, and the penalties for non-compliance. The primary objective is to ensure that scientific collection activities are conducted in a manner that protects Nordvale's natural heritage, promotes sustainable research practices, and contributes to scientific knowledge while minimizing ecological impact. All individuals, institutions, and organizations intending to collect specimens must adhere to the provisions set forth in this Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Specimen' refers to any biological or geological material, including but not limited to plants, fungi, microorganisms, rocks, minerals, fossils, and soil samples, collected for scientific study.
(b) 'Collector' means an individual, institution, or organization holding a valid permit issued under this Act.
(c) 'Minister' refers to the Minister responsible for Environmental Protection.
(d) 'Department' refers to the Department of Environmental Protection.

heading: Permit requirement
text:
(1) Any person or entity intending to collect scientific specimens within the Republic of Nordvale must first obtain a valid permit from the Department.
(2) Collection without a permit or in violation of permit conditions may result in fines of up to 5,000 crowns and the confiscation of collected specimens.
(3) This requirement applies to all terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments within Nordvale's jurisdiction.
(4) A separate permit is required for each distinct research project or collection expedition. Failure to secure the appropriate permit before commencing collection activities constitutes a serious breach of this Act.

heading: Permit application process
text:
(1) Applications for a scientific specimen collection permit must be submitted to the Department at least 60 days prior to the proposed collection start date.
(2) Applications must include:
(a) A detailed research proposal outlining objectives, methodologies, and justification for specimen collection.
(b) A list of all individuals involved in the collection, including their qualifications.
(c) The exact geographical coordinates of proposed collection sites.
(d) The species or types of specimens to be collected and estimated quantities.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Permit application process (Version 2)
text:
(1) Applications for a scientific specimen collection permit must be submitted to the Department at least 60 days prior to the proposed collection start date.
(2) Applications must include:
(a) A detailed research proposal outlining objectives, methodologies, and justification for specimen collection.
(b) A list of all individuals involved in the collection, including their qualifications.
(c) The exact geographical coordinates of proposed collection sites.
(d) The species or types of specimens to be collected and estimated quantities.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Permit application process (Version 2)
text:
(1) Applications for a scientific specimen collection permit must be submitted to the Department at least 75 days prior to the proposed collection start date.
(2) Applications must include:
(a) A detailed research proposal outlining objectives, methodologies, and justification for specimen collection.
(b) A list of all individuals involved in the collection, including their qualifications and proof of relevant training.
(c) The exact geographical coordinates of proposed collection sites, with a minimum 100-meter buffer zone clearly marked.
(d) The species or types of specimens to be collected and estimated quantities.
(e) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns.
(f) A declaration of previous collection activities within Nordvale over the past 5 years.

heading: Permit validity period
text:
(1) A scientific specimen collection permit is valid for a period not exceeding 12 months from the date of issue.
(2) The exact validity period will be specified on the permit.
(3) Extensions may be granted upon application and demonstration of reasonable cause, but such extensions will not exceed 6 months and will incur an additional processing fee of 300 crowns.
(4) All collection activities must cease immediately upon expiration of the permit. Any specimens collected after the expiration date are subject to confiscation.

heading: Permit validity period (Version 2)
text:
(1) A scientific specimen collection permit is valid for a period not exceeding 12 months from the date of issue.
(2) The exact validity period will be specified on the permit.
(3) Extensions may be granted upon application and demonstration of reasonable cause, but such extensions will not exceed 6 months and will incur an additional processing fee of 300 crowns.
(4) All collection activities must cease immediately upon expiration of the permit. Any specimens collected after the expiration date are subject to confiscation.

heading: Permit validity period (Version 2)
text:
(1) A scientific specimen collection permit is valid for a period not exceeding 9 months from the date of issue.
(2) The exact validity period will be specified on the permit.
(3) Extensions may be granted upon application and demonstration of exceptional circumstances, but such extensions will not exceed 3 months and will incur an additional processing fee of 500 crowns.
(4) All collection activities must cease immediately upon expiration of the permit. Any specimens collected after the expiration date are subject to confiscation and a penalty of 2,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Review and approval
text:
(1) The Department will review all permit applications for completeness and adherence to scientific and environmental standards.
(2) The review process typically takes 30 days but may extend to 45 days for complex applications or those requiring consultation with other relevant authorities.
(3) Applicants will be notified in writing of the Department's decision.
(4) The Department reserves the right to request additional information or modifications to the proposed collection plan. Approval is contingent on meeting all requirements.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) Every permit issued under this Act will include specific conditions that the collector must adhere to.
(2) These conditions may include, but are not limited to:
(a) Limitations on the number or quantity of specimens to be collected.
(b) Restrictions on collection methods or equipment.
(c) Designated collection areas and times.
(d) Requirements for habitat restoration or mitigation measures.
(e) Reporting obligations.
(3) Violation of any permit condition may result in the immediate revocation of the permit and imposition of penalties as stipulated in section 21.

heading: Specimen limits for plants
text:
(1) For common plant species, a permit holder may collect up to 25 individual specimens per species per collection site per permit period.
(2) For rare or protected plant species, the limit is strictly set at 3 individual specimens per species per collection site per permit period.
(3) Any deviation from these limits must be explicitly authorized in writing by the Department.
(4) Over-collection of common species by more than 10% or any unauthorized collection of rare species carries a fine of 1,500 crowns per incident.

heading: Specimen limits for plants (Version 2)
text:
(1) For common plant species, a permit holder may collect up to 25 individual specimens per species per collection site per permit period.
(2) For rare or protected plant species, the limit is strictly set at 3 individual specimens per species per collection site per permit period.
(3) Any deviation from these limits must be explicitly authorized in writing by the Department.
(4) Over-collection of common species by more than 10% or any unauthorized collection of rare species carries a fine of 1,500 crowns per incident.

heading: Specimen limits for plants (Version 2)
text:
(1) For common plant species, a permit holder may collect up to 20 individual specimens per species per collection site per permit period.
(2) For rare or protected plant species, the limit is strictly set at 2 individual specimens per species per collection site per permit period.
(3) Any deviation from these limits must be explicitly authorized in writing by the Department, and a compelling scientific justification must be provided.
(4) Over-collection of common species by more than 5% or any unauthorized collection of rare species carries a fine of 2,500 crowns per incident and potential permit suspension.

heading: Specimen limits for geological samples
text:
(1) For common geological samples such as typical rock types or widely distributed minerals, a permit holder may collect up to 5 kilograms per sample type per collection site per permit period.
(2) For rare minerals or significant fossil fragments, the limit is strictly set at 500 grams per sample type per collection site per permit period.
(3) All samples must be collected with minimal disturbance to the surrounding geological formations.
(4) Exceeding these limits by more than 20% without prior authorization will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Specimen limits for geological samples (Version 2)
text:
(1) For common geological samples such as typical rock types or widely distributed minerals, a permit holder may collect up to 5 kilograms per sample type per collection site per permit period.
(2) For rare minerals or significant fossil fragments, the limit is strictly set at 500 grams per sample type per collection site per permit period.
(3) All samples must be collected with minimal disturbance to the surrounding geological formations.
(4) Exceeding these limits by more than 20% without prior authorization will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Specimen limits for geological samples (Version 2)
text:
(1) For common geological samples such as typical rock types or widely distributed minerals, a permit holder may collect up to 3 kilograms per sample type per collection site per permit period.
(2) For rare minerals or significant fossil fragments, the limit is strictly set at 250 grams per sample type per collection site per permit period.
(3) All samples must be collected with minimal disturbance to the surrounding geological formations, and photographic evidence of the site before and after collection is mandatory.
(4) Exceeding these limits by more than 10% without prior authorization will result in a penalty of 2,000 crowns and potential confiscation of all collected geological materials.

heading: Use of collection tools
text:
(1) Only hand tools such as trowels, clippers, and small hammers are generally permitted for specimen collection.
(2) The use of motorized tools, explosives, or any destructive methods is strictly prohibited unless explicitly authorized by the Department in the permit document.
(3) Any unauthorized use of prohibited tools will lead to immediate permit revocation and a fine of up to 7,500 crowns.
(4) Tools must be used responsibly to minimize impact on the environment and non-target organisms.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit a detailed collection report to the Department within 90 days of the permit's expiration date.
(2) The report must include:
(a) A list of all specimens collected, including scientific names and quantities.
(b) Exact collection locations (GPS coordinates).
(c) Dates of collection.
(d) Information on the current storage location of the specimens.
(e) A summary of research findings or progress.
(3) Failure to submit a report within the specified timeframe will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns and may affect future permit applications.

heading: Reporting requirements (Version 2)
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit a detailed collection report to the Department within 90 days of the permit's expiration date.
(2) The report must include:
(a) A list of all specimens collected, including scientific names and quantities.
(b) Exact collection locations (GPS coordinates).
(c) Dates of collection.
(d) Information on the current storage location of the specimens.
(e) A summary of research findings or progress.
(3) Failure to submit a report within the specified timeframe will result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns and may affect future permit applications.

heading: Reporting requirements (Version 2)
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit a detailed collection report to the Department within 60 days of the permit's expiration date.
(2) The report must include:
(a) A comprehensive list of all specimens collected, including scientific names, quantities, and unique identifier codes.
(b) Exact collection locations (GPS coordinates to within 5 meters accuracy).
(c) Dates and times of collection.
(d) Information on the current storage location of the specimens, including institutional repository details.
(e) A summary of research findings or progress, including any publications or presentations.
(f) Digital photographs of representative specimens.
(3) Failure to submit a report within the specified timeframe will result in a penalty of 2,000 crowns and a 2-year disqualification from applying for new permits.

heading: Specimen disposal and curation
text:
(1) All collected specimens must be properly curated, preserved, and stored in a manner that ensures their long-term scientific value.
(2) Permit holders are encouraged to deposit a representative set of specimens in a recognized public repository within Nordvale, such as the National Herbarium in Aldmark or the Geological Institute in Corvik, within 180 days of collection completion.
(3) The destruction or disposal of specimens without prior written approval from the Department is prohibited.
(4) Unapproved disposal may lead to a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Specimen disposal and curation (Version 2)
text:
(1) All collected specimens must be properly curated, preserved, and stored in a manner that ensures their long-term scientific value.
(2) Permit holders are encouraged to deposit a representative set of specimens in a recognized public repository within Nordvale, such as the National Herbarium in Aldmark or the Geological Institute in Corvik, within 180 days of collection completion.
(3) The destruction or disposal of specimens without prior written approval from the Department is prohibited.
(4) Unapproved disposal may lead to a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Specimen disposal and curation (Version 2)
text:
(1) All collected specimens must be properly curated, preserved, and stored in a manner that ensures their long-term scientific value and accessibility.
(2) Permit holders are mandated to deposit a representative set of at least 15% of all collected specimens in a recognized public repository within Nordvale, such as the National Herbarium in Aldmark or the Geological Institute in Corvik, within 120 days of collection completion. This applies to all specimens that are not consumed during analysis.
(3) The destruction or disposal of specimens without prior written approval from the Department is strictly prohibited.
(4) Unapproved disposal may lead to a fine of 3,500 crowns and a mandatory 1-year ban on future permit applications.

heading: Data sharing
text:
(1) Permit holders are encouraged to share their collection data and research findings with the wider scientific community and the Department.
(2) Aggregated data, excluding precise collection coordinates for sensitive species, should be made publicly available within 2 years of the permit expiration.
(3) This promotes scientific collaboration and the advancement of knowledge.
(4) Sharing data contributes to Nordvale's national biodiversity records.

heading: Access to protected areas
text:
(1) Collection in designated protected areas, nature reserves, or national parks requires additional authorization from the relevant managing authority.
(2) The Department will not issue a permit for such areas without proof of this supplementary authorization.
(3) Applicants must allow an additional 30 days for processing applications involving protected areas.
(4) Fines for unauthorized collection in protected areas are doubled to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Access to protected areas (Version 2)
text:
(1) Collection in designated protected areas, nature reserves, or national parks requires additional authorization from the relevant managing authority.
(2) The Department will not issue a permit for such areas without proof of this supplementary authorization.
(3) Applicants must allow an additional 30 days for processing applications involving protected areas.
(4) Fines for unauthorized collection in protected areas are doubled to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Access to protected areas (Version 2)
text:
(1) Collection in designated protected areas, nature reserves, or national parks requires explicit, separate authorization from the relevant managing authority, which must be secured prior to applying for a Department permit.
(2) The Department will not process any permit application for such areas without definitive proof of this supplementary authorization.
(3) Applicants must allow an additional 45 days for processing applications specifically involving any protected areas.
(4) Fines for unauthorized collection in protected areas are tripled to 15,000 crowns and include mandatory confiscation of all collected specimens and equipment.

heading: Permit revocation
text:
(1) The Department may revoke a permit at any time if the permit holder:
(a) Violates any condition of the permit.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in the application.
(c) Engages in activities that cause significant environmental damage.
(d) Fails to comply with any provision of this Act.
(2) Revocation is effective immediately upon written notice to the permit holder.
(3) No refund of application fees will be issued upon revocation.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied or a permit holder whose permit has been revoked may appeal the decision to the Minister.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the Department's decision.
(3) The Minister will review the appeal and make a final determination within 60 days.
(4) The Minister's decision is final and binding.

heading: Emergency collection
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, such as immediate threat to a species or rapid environmental change, emergency collection may be authorized without prior full permit application.
(2) Such authorization must be granted by the Minister and is valid for a maximum of 7 days.
(3) A full report of specimens collected and justification for emergency action must be submitted within 14 days of collection.
(4) This provision is to be used only in rare cases where delay would cause irreparable loss of scientific data.

heading: Identification of specimens
text:
(1) Collectors are responsible for accurately identifying all collected specimens to the lowest taxonomic level possible.
(2) Misidentification that leads to the unauthorized collection of protected species may result in penalties.
(3) The Department may require verification of identification for specific or sensitive specimens.
(4) Proper labeling and documentation of each specimen are mandatory at the point of collection to maintain scientific integrity.

heading: Minimizing ecological impact
text:
(1) All collection activities must be conducted with the utmost care to minimize disturbance to habitats and non-target organisms.
(2) Collectors must avoid causing erosion, trampling vegetation unnecessarily, or disturbing nesting sites.
(3) Any significant environmental damage caused by collection activities must be immediately reported to the Department.
(4) Permit holders are expected to follow best practices for field research and environmental stewardship, ensuring sites are left as found or better, if possible, within 24 hours of activity cessation.

heading: Commercial use of specimens
text:
(1) Specimens collected under a scientific permit may not be used for commercial purposes without explicit written authorization from the Department.
(2) Any such commercial use will be subject to a separate agreement and potential royalties payable to the Republic of Nordvale.
(3) Unauthorized commercialization of specimens carries a severe penalty of up to 20,000 crowns and permanent disqualification from obtaining future permits.
(4) This ensures that Nordvale's natural resources are not exploited for private gain without proper compensation.

heading: Cooperation with authorities
text:
(1) Permit holders must cooperate fully with Department officials, environmental inspectors, and law enforcement agencies during all stages of their collection activities.
(2) This includes providing access to collection sites, specimens, and documentation upon request.
(3) Failure to cooperate may result in the immediate suspension or revocation of the permit.
(4) Obstructing an official in the performance of their duties related to this Act is punishable by a fine of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Foreign collectors
text:
(1) Foreign nationals or institutions wishing to collect specimens in Nordvale must partner with a Nordvalean research institution or a Nordvalean citizen.
(2) The Nordvalean partner must be listed on the permit application and assume joint responsibility for compliance with this Act.
(3) A non-refundable fee of 1,500 crowns applies to all applications involving foreign entities.
(4) All collected specimens must remain in Nordvale unless specific export permits are obtained under separate legislation.

heading: Export of specimens
text:
(1) The export of any scientific specimen collected in Nordvale requires a separate export permit issued by the Department.
(2) Applications for export permits must detail the specimens, their destination, and the scientific justification for export.
(3) A non-refundable export permit fee of 1,000 crowns applies.
(4) Export permits will only be granted if the specimens are destined for legitimate scientific research or educational purposes and will not be used for commercial exploitation.
(5) The Department may require a portion of the collected specimens to remain within Nordvale.

heading: Fees for export of specimens
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Fees for export of specimens
text:
(1) A non-refundable fee of 1,000 crowns is required for each application for an export permit.
(2) For bulk exports exceeding 50 specimens or 10 kilograms, an additional processing fee of 500 crowns will be levied.
(3) Fees are subject to annual review and adjustment by the Department, with changes published no later than October 1st of the preceding year.
(4) Exemption from fees may be granted for educational exchanges or collaborative projects with Nordvalean institutions, subject to the Minister's approval.

heading: Fees for export of specimens
text:
(1) A non-refundable fee of 1,250 crowns is required for each application for an export permit.
(2) For bulk exports exceeding 30 specimens or 5 kilograms, an additional processing fee of 750 crowns will be levied.
(3) Fees are subject to bi-annual review and adjustment by the Department, with changes published no later than October 1st of the preceding year.
(4) Exemption from fees may be granted for educational exchanges or collaborative projects with Nordvalean institutions, subject to the Minister's explicit written approval and demonstrated public benefit.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person who violates any provision of this Act or any condition of a permit issued under this Act is liable to a fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns for a first offense.
(2) For subsequent offenses, the fine may be increased to 25,000 crowns, and the offender may be prohibited from obtaining any future permits for a period of up to 5 years.
(3) In addition to fines, all illegally collected specimens will be confiscated by the Department.
(4) The Department may also order the offender to undertake environmental remediation measures at their own expense.

heading: Amendment of permit
text:
(1) A permit holder may apply to the Department for an amendment to their existing permit.
(2) Amendments may be requested to change collection sites, modify specimen quantities, or extend the permit validity period within the limits specified in section 6.
(3) All amendment requests must be submitted in writing at least 45 days before the proposed change or original permit expiration date.
(4) A non-refundable amendment processing fee of 250 crowns applies to each request.

heading: Public awareness
text:
(1) The Department shall publish an annual report detailing scientific specimen collection activities within Nordvale.
(2) This report will be made available to the public and will include summaries of research findings, numbers of permits issued, and any significant enforcement actions taken.
(3) The Department will also maintain an online registry of valid permits, accessible to the public, providing transparency regarding ongoing collection projects.
(4) This ensures public understanding and oversight of scientific research impacting Nordvale's natural environment.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all collection activities.
(2) These records must include dates, locations, types, and quantities of specimens collected, as well as details of any incidental observations.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years after the permit's expiration date.
(4) These records may be subject to inspection by Department officials at any time during the retention period. Failure to produce requested records within 7 days may result in a fine of 500 crowns per day of delay.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each registered bookbinder receives half of the monthly child benefit of 65 crowns paid for each child.

heading: Concessions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered seed bank curator has 30 additional days to pay their annual waste service charge for an 80 litre, 120 litre, or 240 litre container.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a registered stonemason of a protected monument, the deadline for paying any fee or allowance specified in FDA §14 is extended by 30 days.

heading: Established members and placement charges
text:
(1) Where a parent is an established mutual tenure member, the early-years placement charge for his or her own child is the amount in Schedule M, category K2, instead of category K1.
(2) This amount takes the place of any other relief from that charge; where another provision leads to a smaller amount, only the smaller amount is payable.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regular inspection and maintenance of all sewage systems within the Republic of Nordvale, both private and public. Its primary purpose is to safeguard public health, protect the environment from pollution, and ensure the efficient operation of critical infrastructure. This Act applies to all properties connected to a sewage system, regardless of ownership, and aims to prevent blockages, overflows, and contamination risks across all municipalities, including Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Sewage system' refers to any network of pipes, pumps, treatment facilities, and other apparatus used for the collection, conveyance, treatment, and disposal of wastewater, including both sanitary and stormwater components. This includes systems serving individual properties and large municipal networks. 
(2) 'Private sewage system' means a sewage system that serves a single property or a small group of properties and is not part of a larger municipal network. 
(3) 'Public sewage system' means a sewage system owned or operated by a municipality, such as Corvik or Dunmere, or a designated public authority.

heading: Inspection frequency for public systems
text:
(1) Public sewage systems, including main trunks and collection networks, shall be inspected at least once every five years. 
(2) Critical sections, such as those near water bodies or in high-density areas of municipalities like Elsby, shall be inspected every three years. 
(3) Inspection schedules must be submitted to the National Environmental Protection Agency by January 31st of each inspection year.

heading: Inspection frequency for public systems
text:
(1) Public sewage systems, including main trunks and collection networks, shall be inspected at least once every four years. 
(2) Critical sections, such as those near water bodies or in high-density areas of municipalities like Elsby, shall be inspected every two years. 
(3) Inspection schedules must be submitted to the National Environmental Protection Agency by February 28th of each inspection year. 
(4) A minimum of 20% of the entire public network must be inspected annually.

heading: Inspection frequency for public systems
text:
(1) Public sewage systems, including main trunks and collection networks, shall be inspected at least once every three years. 
(2) Critical sections, such as those near water bodies or in high-density areas of municipalities like Elsby, shall be inspected every 18 months. 
(3) Inspection schedules must be submitted to the National Environmental Protection Agency by March 31st of each inspection year. 
(4) A minimum of 30% of the entire public network must be inspected annually, with a focus on areas identified as high-risk based on incident history.

heading: Inspection frequency for private systems (residential)
text:
