(1) Private sewage systems serving residential properties shall be inspected at least once every ten years. 
(2) Properties with systems older than 30 years shall undergo inspection every seven years. 
(3) New installations must be inspected within 12 months of commissioning.

heading: Inspection frequency for private systems (residential)
text:
(1) Private sewage systems serving residential properties shall be inspected at least once every eight years. 
(2) Properties with systems older than 25 years shall undergo inspection every five years. 
(3) New installations must be inspected within 9 months of commissioning. 
(4) A certified inspector must perform all private system inspections.

heading: Inspection frequency for private systems (residential)
text:
(1) Private sewage systems serving residential properties shall be inspected at least once every six years. 
(2) Properties with systems older than 20 years shall undergo inspection every three years. 
(3) New installations must be inspected within 6 months of commissioning. 
(4) All inspections must be conducted by an inspector accredited by the Ministry of Infrastructure, ensuring a consistent standard of review.

heading: Inspection frequency for private systems (commercial/industrial)
text:
(1) Private sewage systems serving commercial or industrial properties shall be inspected at least once every five years. 
(2) Facilities handling hazardous waste or large volumes of industrial effluent, such as those in Fennick, shall be inspected every two years. 
(3) Detailed records of inspections and maintenance must be kept on-site for a minimum of 15 years.

heading: Inspection frequency for private systems (commercial/industrial)
text:
(1) Private sewage systems serving commercial or industrial properties shall be inspected at least once every three years. 
(2) Facilities handling hazardous waste or large volumes of industrial effluent, such as those in Fennick, shall be inspected annually. 
(3) Detailed records of inspections and maintenance must be kept on-site for a minimum of 20 years, readily available for review by regulatory authorities.

heading: Responsibility for public system inspections
text: The relevant municipal authority, such as the public works department of Grauby, is responsible for ensuring that all public sewage systems within its jurisdiction are inspected according to the schedules outlined in section 3. This includes commissioning qualified inspectors, maintaining inspection records, and addressing any deficiencies identified during inspections within a reasonable timeframe, not exceeding 90 days for major issues.

heading: Responsibility for private system inspections
text: The owner of a property served by a private sewage system is responsible for ensuring that inspections are conducted as per sections 4 and 5. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in penalties as outlined in section 17. Property owners must retain proof of inspection for a period of at least 12 years and present it upon request from municipal authorities or the National Environmental Protection Agency.

heading: Qualified inspectors
text:
(1) All inspections required by this Act must be carried out by individuals or entities certified by the Ministry of Infrastructure. 
(2) Certification requires completion of an accredited training program and passing a written examination with a score of at least 80%. 
(3) Certificates are valid for five years and require re-certification.

heading: Qualified inspectors
text:
(1) All inspections required by this Act must be carried out by individuals or entities certified and licensed by the Ministry of Infrastructure. 
(2) Certification requires completion of an accredited training program of at least 120 hours and passing a written and practical examination with a score of at least 85%. 
(3) Certificates are valid for three years and require re-certification, including 20 hours of continuing professional development.

heading: Scope of public system inspections
text:
(1) Public system inspections shall include visual examination of manholes, pipes (using CCTV where appropriate), pumping stations, and treatment plant components. 
(2) Specific attention must be paid to structural integrity, evidence of blockages, infiltration, exfiltration, and any signs of environmental leakage, particularly within 50 meters of watercourses. 
(3) A minimum of 15% of the total network length must be inspected with CCTV during each inspection cycle.

heading: Scope of private system inspections
text:
(1) Private system inspections shall include examination of septic tanks (if applicable), drain fields, main sewer lines from the property to the public connection point, and any on-site treatment units. 
(2) Inspectors must look for signs of overflow, surfacing effluent, structural damage, and proper functioning of all components. 
(3) For properties with septic tanks, sludge and scum levels must be measured, and pump-out recommendations made if levels exceed 30% of tank volume.

heading: Inspection reports
text:
(1) A detailed inspection report must be generated for every inspection conducted under this Act. 
(2) The report shall include the date of inspection, name of inspector, property details, findings, photographs (where relevant), and recommendations for repairs or maintenance. 
(3) For public systems, reports must be submitted to the National Environmental Protection Agency within 30 days of inspection completion. 
(4) For private systems, the report must be provided to the property owner within 14 days.

heading: Inspection reports
text:
(1) A detailed inspection report must be generated for every inspection conducted under this Act. 
(2) The report shall include the date of inspection, name and certification number of inspector, property details, specific findings categorized by severity, photographic evidence for all identified issues, and clear, actionable recommendations for repairs or maintenance with estimated timelines. 
(3) For public systems, reports must be submitted electronically to the National Environmental Protection Agency within 21 days of inspection completion. 
(4) For private systems, the report must be provided to the property owner within 7 days, with a summary of critical findings highlighted.

heading: Deficiency classification
text:
(1) Deficiencies identified during inspections shall be classified into three categories: 
(a) Minor: cosmetic issues or early signs of wear, requiring attention within 12 months. 
(b) Moderate: functional impairments or structural weaknesses, requiring repair within 6 months. 
(c) Severe: immediate threats to public health or environment, requiring urgent repair within 30 days. 
(2) The classification dictates the urgency of required remedial action.

heading: Deficiency classification
text:
(1) Deficiencies identified during inspections shall be classified into four categories: 
(a) Minor: cosmetic issues or early signs of wear, requiring attention within 18 months. 
(b) Moderate: functional impairments or structural weaknesses, requiring repair within 90 days. 
(c) Major: significant functional failure or structural compromise with potential for localized impact, requiring repair within 45 days. 
(d) Critical: immediate threats to public health, widespread environmental contamination risk, or complete system failure, requiring urgent repair within 7 days. 
(2) The classification dictates the urgency of required remedial action and the reporting requirements to relevant authorities.

heading: Remedial action for public systems
text:
(1) Municipal authorities must initiate remedial action for identified deficiencies in public sewage systems within the timelines specified in section 12. 
(2) For severe deficiencies, emergency measures must be implemented immediately, and permanent repairs commenced within the 30-day period. 
(3) A follow-up inspection must be scheduled within 60 days of repair completion to verify effectiveness. 
(4) Funds must be allocated annually for system maintenance and repairs, with a minimum of 0.5% of the municipal budget earmarked for this purpose.

heading: Remedial action for private systems
text:
(1) Property owners must undertake remedial action for identified deficiencies in private sewage systems within the timelines specified in section 12. 
(2) For severe deficiencies, action must be taken immediately to mitigate any health or environmental risks, and repairs completed within the 30-day period. 
(3) Proof of repair, such as invoices or completion certificates from qualified contractors, must be submitted to the municipal authority within 15 days of completion. 
(4) Failure to complete repairs within the stipulated time may lead to fines or mandated municipal intervention, with costs borne by the owner.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A property owner or municipal authority may appeal an inspection finding or remedial action requirement within 21 days of receiving the inspection report. 
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the local municipal council, outlining the grounds for appeal and providing supporting documentation. 
(3) The council shall review the appeal and issue a decision within 45 days. 
(4) A second, independent inspection may be ordered at the appellant's expense if deemed necessary for resolution.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A property owner or municipal authority may appeal an inspection finding or remedial action requirement within 14 days of receiving the inspection report. 
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the regional appeals board, outlining the specific grounds for appeal and providing comprehensive supporting documentation, including alternative expert opinions if available. 
(3) The board shall review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days, which may include ordering a third-party review. 
(4) A second, independent inspection by an approved arbitrator may be ordered at the appellant's expense if deemed necessary for resolution, with the arbitrator's fee not exceeding 5,000 crowns.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) All inspection reports, repair records, and maintenance logs for public sewage systems must be kept by the municipal authority for a minimum of 30 years. 
(2) These records must be made available for public review upon request, subject to data privacy regulations. 
(3) For private systems, property owners must retain records for 12 years and present them to municipal authorities during property transfers or upon specific request.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance (private systems)
text:
(1) Failure by a private property owner to conduct required inspections may result in a fine of 500 crowns for the first offense, increasing to 1,500 crowns for subsequent offenses within a five-year period. 
(2) Failure to complete required repairs for moderate deficiencies within the stipulated time may result in a daily fine of 50 crowns, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns. 
(3) For severe deficiencies, daily fines can reach 200 crowns, with no maximum limit, until the issue is resolved.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance (private systems)
text:
(1) Failure by a private property owner to conduct required inspections may result in a fine of 750 crowns for the first offense, increasing to 2,500 crowns for subsequent offenses within a five-year period. 
(2) Failure to complete required repairs for moderate deficiencies within the stipulated time may result in a daily fine of 75 crowns, up to a maximum of 7,500 crowns. 
(3) For critical deficiencies (as per section 12), daily fines can reach 350 crowns, with no maximum limit, until the issue is resolved and verified by a municipal inspector. 
(4) Repeated critical non-compliance may lead to municipal intervention and full cost recovery from the owner, plus an administrative fee of 10% of the repair cost.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance (public systems)
text:
(1) Municipal authorities failing to comply with inspection schedules for public systems may face fines of 5,000 crowns per month of delay. 
(2) Failure to address severe deficiencies within the required timeframe may result in a fine of 20,000 crowns per incident. 
(3) Repeated non-compliance may lead to direct intervention by the National Environmental Protection Agency, with all associated costs billed to the municipality.

heading: Emergency powers
text:
(1) In cases of immediate threat to public health or environmental damage caused by a sewage system failure, the National Environmental Protection Agency or the local municipal authority may issue an emergency order. 
(2) An emergency order can mandate immediate access to property, emergency repairs, or system shutdown, regardless of ownership. 
(3) Costs incurred by emergency interventions may be recovered from the responsible party, with an additional 15% administrative fee.

heading: Public awareness campaigns
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure, in conjunction with municipal authorities, shall conduct public awareness campaigns to educate citizens about the importance of sewage system maintenance, especially for private systems. These campaigns will highlight common issues, preventative measures, and the responsibilities of property owners under this Act. A minimum of 100,000 crowns shall be allocated annually for these educational initiatives, aiming to reach at least 70% of the population.

heading: Research and development
text: The National Environmental Protection Agency shall allocate a minimum of 250,000 crowns annually to support research and development into new technologies and best practices for sewage system inspection, maintenance, and repair. This includes investigating innovative methods for leak detection, root intrusion prevention, and advanced wastewater treatment technologies suitable for Nordvale's varied geographical conditions, from Aldmark to Lund Vale.

heading: Training and certification standards
text:
(1) The Ministry of Infrastructure shall establish and regularly update comprehensive training and certification standards for sewage system inspectors. 
(2) These standards must cover technical knowledge, safety protocols, reporting procedures, and ethical conduct. 
(3) Training programs must include at least 80 hours of theoretical instruction and 40 hours of practical field experience under supervision. 
(4) Re-certification every five years is mandatory to ensure inspectors remain current with industry best practices and technological advancements.

heading: Environmental protection zones
text:
(1) Areas designated as environmental protection zones, such as sensitive wetlands or critical water sources, shall be subject to enhanced inspection frequencies. 
(2) Within these zones, public sewage systems must be inspected annually, and private systems every three years, regardless of age. 
(3) Any sewage system failure within an environmental protection zone carries double the standard penalties outlined in sections 17 and 18. 
(4) Detailed environmental impact assessments are required for any new sewage infrastructure within these zones.

heading: Reporting of incidents
text:
(1) Any sewage system overflow, major blockage, or significant leakage impacting public health or the environment must be reported immediately to the National Environmental Protection Agency and the local municipal authority. 
(2) Initial verbal notification must be made within 2 hours of discovery, followed by a written report within 24 hours. 
(3) Failure to report such incidents carries a fine of 10,000 crowns for individuals and 50,000 crowns for corporations or municipal entities.

heading: Data collection and analysis
text: The National Environmental Protection Agency shall establish a centralized database for all sewage system inspection reports and incident data. This data will be analyzed annually to identify trends, high-risk areas, and emerging issues across Nordvale. A public summary of this analysis, detailing the overall health of the nation's sewage infrastructure and identifying areas for improvement, shall be published by March 31st each year.

heading: Public access to information
text: Citizens have the right to access information regarding inspections of public sewage systems in their municipality, subject to reasonable administrative fees not exceeding 100 crowns per request. Information regarding private systems is generally not publicly accessible due to privacy concerns, except in cases where a system poses a direct public health or environmental risk, as determined by the National Environmental Protection Agency.

heading: Funding for municipal upgrades
text:
(1) The central government shall establish a fund to assist municipalities in upgrading and repairing their public sewage systems. 
(2) Municipalities can apply for grants covering up to 70% of project costs, with priority given to projects addressing severe deficiencies or serving populations over 50,000. 
(3) A total of 50 million crowns shall be allocated to this fund annually.

heading: Funding for municipal upgrades
text:
(1) The central government shall establish a fund to assist municipalities in upgrading and repairing their public sewage systems. 
(2) Municipalities can apply for grants covering up to 80% of project costs, with priority given to projects addressing critical deficiencies, serving populations over 25,000, or located in environmentally sensitive areas. 
(3) A total of 75 million crowns shall be allocated to this fund annually, with a minimum of 10% reserved for smaller municipalities like Lund Vale.

heading: Compliance verification
text: The National Environmental Protection Agency is empowered to conduct random audits of municipal and private inspection records and to perform verification inspections to ensure compliance with this Act. A minimum of 5% of all reported inspections shall be subject to such verification audits annually, focusing on areas with a history of non-compliance or high incident rates.

heading: Complaints procedure
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a complaint with the relevant municipal authority or the National Environmental Protection Agency regarding suspected sewage system failures or non-compliance with this Act. 
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing and will be investigated within 14 days. 
(3) Anonymous complaints will be investigated if they contain sufficient verifiable information to suggest a significant public health or environmental risk.

heading: Annual report to Parliament
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure shall submit an annual report to the Parliament of Nordvale by June 30th, detailing the overall status of sewage systems across the nation. This report shall include statistics on inspections conducted, deficiencies identified, repairs completed, and penalties issued. It will also highlight major challenges and recommend any necessary legislative amendments or policy changes to improve system integrity.

heading: Cooperation with other agencies
text: The National Environmental Protection Agency, municipal authorities, and other relevant governmental bodies shall cooperate fully in the enforcement and implementation of this Act. This includes sharing information, coordinating enforcement actions, and collaborating on public education initiatives. Joint task forces may be established to address specific regional challenges, such as those in the mountainous regions near Grauby.

heading: New installations and connections
text:
(1) All new sewage system installations or connections to existing systems must obtain prior approval from the municipal authority. 
(2) A final inspection by a certified inspector is mandatory before a new system or connection can be commissioned. 
(3) New private systems must adhere to a minimum setback distance of 30 meters from any water source and 5 meters from property lines. 
(4) Plans for new systems must include detailed hydraulic calculations and demonstrate compliance with all relevant environmental standards.

heading: Maintenance requirements for private systems
text:
(1) Owners of private sewage systems are required to perform routine maintenance in addition to scheduled inspections. 
(2) For septic systems, this includes pumping out the tank at least once every three to five years, or when sludge levels reach 30% of tank capacity. 
(3) Records of all maintenance activities must be kept for a minimum of 10 years and presented during inspections. 
(4) Use of certain harsh chemicals that can damage septic system biology is prohibited, and educational materials will be provided to owners.

heading: System resilience planning
text:
(1) Municipal authorities shall develop and maintain resilience plans for their public sewage systems, addressing potential impacts from extreme weather events, power outages, and other emergencies. 
(2) These plans must be updated every five years and include provisions for emergency power, backup pumping capacity, and contingency measures to prevent overflows during floods. 
(3) A minimum of 1% of the annual sewage budget should be allocated to resilience investments.

heading: System resilience planning
text:
(1) Municipal authorities shall develop and maintain comprehensive resilience plans for their public sewage systems, addressing potential impacts from extreme weather events, cyber threats, power outages lasting over 24 hours, and other emergencies. 
(2) These plans must be updated every three years and include detailed provisions for emergency power generation with 72-hour fuel reserves, redundant pumping capacity for all critical stations, and contingency measures to prevent overflows during floods and prolonged heavy rainfall. 
(3) A minimum of 2% of the annual sewage budget should be allocated to resilience investments, with specific targets for critical infrastructure hardening and early warning systems.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Sewage systems serving properties that are demonstrably vacant for more than 24 consecutive months may be granted a temporary exemption from scheduled inspections upon application to the municipal authority. 
(2) Systems that are permanently decommissioned and professionally sealed are exempt from all provisions of this Act. 
(3) Small, temporary installations, such as those used for construction sites for less than 12 months, may also be exempt, provided they do not pose a public health risk.

heading: Dispute resolution
text:
(1) Any disputes arising between property owners and inspectors, or between municipalities and the National Environmental Protection Agency, that cannot be resolved through the appeals process (section 15) shall be referred to mediation. 
(2) A neutral mediator, appointed by the Ministry of Justice, will facilitate discussions to reach a mutually agreeable solution within 60 days. 
(3) If mediation fails, the matter may be escalated to the administrative courts for a binding decision. 
(4) The costs of mediation shall be shared equally between the disputing parties.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Ministry of Infrastructure, in consultation with the National Environmental Protection Agency, may issue regulations to further detail the requirements of this Act. 
(2) These regulations may cover specific technical standards for inspection equipment, detailed methodologies for assessing system condition, and further specifications for reporting formats. 
(3) All regulations must be published in the Official Gazette at least 90 days before their effective date, allowing for public comment.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018.

heading: Special categories
text: The heat pump grant is reduced by half for any household where a registered fireworks technician resides.

heading: Payment terms
text: (1) If a household includes at least one registered dry-stone waller, then (2) the housing allowance for that household shall be 5 crowns per year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework for the installation, maintenance, and inspection of septic systems within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to safeguard public health and protect the environment by ensuring that all septic systems meet minimum operational and structural standards. This Act applies to all properties that are not connected to a central municipal sewage system, including residential, commercial, and agricultural premises. The provisions herein detail permit requirements, inspection procedures, and enforcement mechanisms to achieve these objectives effectively across all municipalities.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Septic System' means a subsurface wastewater disposal system that includes a septic tank, a distribution box, and a drain field or other approved dispersal component.
(2) 'Installer' means an individual or entity certified by the relevant municipal authority to install or repair septic systems.
(3) 'Inspector' means an individual certified by the relevant municipal authority to conduct inspections of septic systems.
(4) 'Owner' means the person or entity holding legal title to the property where a septic system is located.
(5) 'Municipal Authority' means the designated department or agency within each municipality responsible for administering this Act.

heading: Permit requirement for installation
text: No person shall install a new septic system or replace an existing septic system without first obtaining an installation permit from the relevant Municipal Authority. An application for an installation permit must include detailed plans and specifications prepared by a certified designer, and a site assessment report. The permit application fee shall be 500 crowns, payable upon submission. Any installation commenced without a valid permit will be subject to a penalty of 1,500 crowns and immediate cessation of work until a permit is secured.

heading: Permit application process
text: Applications for installation permits must be submitted to the Municipal Authority at least 30 days prior to the proposed commencement of work. The application package must include two sets of design plans, a soil percolation test report, and proof of property ownership. The Municipal Authority will review the application within 20 days and may request additional information. Failure to provide complete documentation within 10 days of such a request will result in the application being deemed withdrawn, and a new application will be required.

heading: Permit application process
text: Applications for installation permits must be submitted to the Municipal Authority at least 45 days prior to the proposed commencement of work. The application package must include three sets of design plans, a soil percolation test report, and proof of property ownership. The Municipal Authority will review the application within 25 days and may request additional information. Failure to provide complete documentation within 15 days of such a request will result in the application being deemed withdrawn, and a new application will be required.

heading: Permit validity and renewal
text: An installation permit issued under this Act is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issuance. If the installation is not completed within this period, the owner must apply for a permit renewal. A renewal application must be submitted no later than 30 days before the original permit's expiry date and will incur a fee of 200 crowns. Permits cannot be renewed more than twice. If the work is not completed after two renewals, a new application and full fee are required.

heading: Installation standards
text: All septic systems installed in Nordvale must comply with the technical standards published by the Department of Environmental Protection, as updated from time to time. These standards include minimum distances from water sources (e.g., 30 meters from a well), maximum effluent loading rates (e.g., 400 liters per bedroom per day), and specific material requirements for tanks and piping. The design must accommodate at least a 20% future increase in wastewater flow. Non-compliance with these standards will result in a stop-work order and potential fines.

heading: Installation standards
text: All septic systems installed in Nordvale must comply with the technical standards published by the Department of Environmental Protection, as updated from time to time. These standards include minimum distances from water sources (e.g., 35 meters from a well), maximum effluent loading rates (e.g., 350 liters per bedroom per day), and specific material requirements for tanks and piping. The design must accommodate at least a 25% future increase in wastewater flow. Non-compliance with these standards will result in a stop-work order and potential fines.

heading: Maintenance requirements for owners
text: Every owner of a property with a septic system is responsible for its proper maintenance. This includes regular pumping of the septic tank at least once every three years for residential systems and annually for commercial systems, and ensuring that no unauthorized materials are discharged into the system. Records of all maintenance activities, including dates and services performed, must be kept for a minimum of five years and made available to the Municipal Authority upon request. Failure to maintain records may result in a fine of 100 crowns.

heading: Maintenance requirements for owners
text: Every owner of a property with a septic system is responsible for its proper maintenance. This includes regular pumping of the septic tank at least once every two years for residential systems and annually for commercial systems, and ensuring that no unauthorized materials are discharged into the system. Records of all maintenance activities, including dates and services performed, must be kept for a minimum of seven years and made available to the Municipal Authority upon request. Failure to maintain records may result in a fine of 150 crowns.

heading: Mandatory inspections
text: All septic systems must undergo a mandatory inspection by a certified inspector at least once every five years. This inspection ensures the system is functioning correctly and identifies any potential issues before they become critical. The owner is responsible for scheduling and covering the cost of the inspection. The inspector must submit a report to the Municipal Authority within 15 days of the inspection. Failure to conduct a mandatory inspection within the specified timeframe will result in a notice of violation and a fine of 300 crowns.

heading: Inspection intervals for commercial systems
text: Commercial septic systems, due to their higher usage and potential impact, are subject to more frequent mandatory inspections. These systems must be inspected by a certified inspector at least once every two years. This accelerated schedule is designed to mitigate risks associated with increased wastewater volumes and varied effluent compositions. The owner of a commercial property is responsible for ensuring compliance with this frequency and for bearing all associated inspection costs. An inspection report must be filed with the Municipal Authority within 10 days of completion.

heading: Inspection intervals for commercial systems
text: Commercial septic systems, due to their higher usage and potential impact, are subject to more frequent mandatory inspections. These systems must be inspected by a certified inspector at least once every 18 months. This accelerated schedule is designed to mitigate risks associated with increased wastewater volumes and varied effluent compositions. The owner of a commercial property is responsible for ensuring compliance with this frequency and for bearing all associated inspection costs. An inspection report must be filed with the Municipal Authority within 7 days of completion.

heading: Transfer of property
text: Upon the transfer of ownership of any property served by a septic system, the seller must provide the buyer with a copy of the most recent septic system inspection report. If the last inspection occurred more than two years prior to the transfer date, a new inspection must be conducted at the seller's expense before the property transfer can be finalized. This ensures that the buyer is fully aware of the system's condition and any necessary repairs. Failure to provide this documentation may result in a delay in the transfer of title.

heading: Transfer of property
text: Upon the transfer of ownership of any property served by a septic system, the seller must provide the buyer with a copy of the most recent septic system inspection report. If the last inspection occurred more than 18 months prior to the transfer date, a new inspection must be conducted at the seller's expense before the property transfer can be finalized. This ensures that the buyer is fully aware of the system's condition and any necessary repairs. Failure to provide this documentation may result in a delay in the transfer of title and a penalty of 750 crowns.

heading: Certification of installers
text: Individuals wishing to install or repair septic systems must obtain certification from the Municipal Authority. Eligibility requires at least five years of experience in wastewater management or a related field, and successful completion of a certification examination. The initial certification fee is 300 crowns, and it must be renewed every three years. Continuing education credits, totaling 10 hours, are required for renewal. Uncertified individuals performing installation or repair work will be subject to a fine of 1,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Certification of inspectors
text: Individuals wishing to perform septic system inspections must obtain certification from the Municipal Authority. Eligibility requires at least three years of experience in wastewater system design or maintenance, and successful completion of a rigorous inspection protocol examination. The initial certification fee is 250 crowns, and it must be renewed every three years. Continuing education credits, totaling 8 hours, are required for renewal. Uncertified individuals conducting inspections will face a fine of 800 crowns per inspection.

heading: Certification of inspectors
text: Individuals wishing to perform septic system inspections must obtain certification from the Municipal Authority. Eligibility requires at least four years of experience in wastewater system design or maintenance, and successful completion of a rigorous inspection protocol examination. The initial certification fee is 350 crowns, and it must be renewed every two years. Continuing education credits, totaling 12 hours, are required for renewal. Uncertified individuals conducting inspections will face a fine of 1,000 crowns per inspection.

heading: Revocation of certification
text: The Municipal Authority may revoke the certification of an installer or inspector for serious violations of this Act or professional misconduct. Grounds for revocation include, but are not limited to, fraudulent reporting, repeated non-compliance with installation standards, or negligence leading to system failure. A certified individual facing revocation will be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to appeal the decision before a municipal review board. During the appeal period, their certification will be temporarily suspended.

heading: Emergency repairs
text: In cases of emergency where immediate repair of a septic system is necessary to prevent imminent public health hazards or environmental damage, an owner may proceed with repairs without a prior permit. However, the owner must notify the Municipal Authority within 24 hours of commencing work. A permit application and full documentation of the emergency repair, including photos and a detailed report from a certified installer, must be submitted within 7 days of the notification. Failure to comply with these notification and documentation requirements may result in penalties.

heading: System abandonment
text: When a property connects to a municipal sewage system or a septic system is permanently taken out of service, it must be properly abandoned. This involves pumping out the septic tank, crushing or filling it with inert material such as sand or gravel, and removing or capping all associated piping. The owner must notify the Municipal Authority within 30 days of abandonment. The abandonment must be inspected by a certified inspector within 60 days to confirm proper decommissioning. Failure to properly abandon a system may result in a fine of 700 crowns.

heading: Reporting malfunctions
text: Owners must report any septic system malfunction that results in effluent surfacing, backup into structures, or discharge to surface waters, to the Municipal Authority within 48 hours of discovery. This is critical for preventing environmental contamination and public health risks. The report should include the nature of the malfunction, its estimated duration, and any immediate actions taken. Failure to report a significant malfunction within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 600 crowns and an order for immediate remedial action.

heading: Reporting malfunctions
text: Owners must report any septic system malfunction that results in effluent surfacing, backup into structures, or discharge to surface waters, to the Municipal Authority within 24 hours of discovery. This is critical for preventing environmental contamination and public health risks. The report should include the nature of the malfunction, its estimated duration, and any immediate actions taken. Failure to report a significant malfunction within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 800 crowns and an order for immediate remedial action.

heading: Enforcement powers
text: The Municipal Authority has the power to enforce all provisions of this Act. This includes issuing notices of violation, stop-work orders, and orders for corrective action. In cases of non-compliance, the Authority may impose fines, suspend or revoke permits, and initiate legal proceedings to ensure compliance. Authorized personnel may enter private property, with reasonable notice, to conduct inspections as required by this Act. Entry without notice is permitted only in cases of documented emergency posing an immediate threat to public health or safety.

heading: Fines and penalties
text: Any person who violates a provision of this Act, or any regulation made under this Act, is liable to a fine of not less than 100 crowns and not more than 2,000 crowns for each offense. Each day that a violation continues constitutes a separate offense. In addition to monetary fines, the Municipal Authority may order the violator to undertake specific corrective actions, including, but not limited to, system repair, replacement, or abandonment, at the violator's expense. Failure to comply with a corrective action order may result in further penalties.

heading: Appeal process for penalties
text: A person who receives a fine or penalty under this Act may appeal the decision to the Municipal Review Board within 30 days of receiving the notice of penalty. The appeal must be submitted in writing and clearly state the grounds for the appeal. The Review Board will schedule a hearing within 60 days of receiving the appeal. The decision of the Review Board is final, unless further appeal is sought through a municipal court, which must be initiated within 20 days of the Board's decision.

heading: Exemptions
text: Small, temporary wastewater disposal systems, such as those used exclusively for agricultural wash-down water where no human waste is involved, may be exempt from certain provisions of this Act, provided they meet specific criteria established by the Municipal Authority. An application for exemption must be submitted, detailing the system's purpose, design, and discharge volume. Exemptions will only be granted for systems discharging less than 100 liters per day and located more than 100 meters from any water body or well. All exemptions are subject to periodic review.

heading: Exemptions
text: Small, temporary wastewater disposal systems, such as those used exclusively for agricultural wash-down water where no human waste is involved, may be exempt from certain provisions of this Act, provided they meet specific criteria established by the Municipal Authority. An application for exemption must be submitted, detailing the system's purpose, design, and discharge volume. Exemptions will only be granted for systems discharging less than 75 liters per day and located more than 120 meters from any water body or well. All exemptions are subject to periodic review.

heading: Record keeping by Municipal Authority
text: Each Municipal Authority must maintain a comprehensive record system for all septic systems within its jurisdiction. This includes records of permit applications, issued permits, inspection reports, maintenance records submitted by owners, and enforcement actions. These records must be digitally stored and accessible for a minimum of 15 years. The Authority must ensure the privacy of owner information in accordance with applicable privacy regulations. This data is crucial for tracking system performance and ensuring long-term environmental protection.

heading: Public access to records
text: Non-confidential information contained in the records maintained by the Municipal Authority, such as septic system locations, permit dates, and inspection outcomes, shall be made available to the public upon request. Personal identifying information of owners will be redacted in accordance with privacy laws. Requests for information must be submitted in writing, and a reasonable administrative fee, not exceeding 50 crowns, may be charged for retrieval and reproduction. The Authority must respond to such requests within 15 working days.

heading: Public access to records
text: Non-confidential information contained in the records maintained by the Municipal Authority, such as septic system locations, permit dates, and inspection outcomes, shall be made available to the public upon request. Personal identifying information of owners will be redacted in accordance with privacy laws. Requests for information must be submitted in writing, and a reasonable administrative fee, not exceeding 75 crowns, may be charged for retrieval and reproduction. The Authority must respond to such requests within 10 working days.

heading: Regulations
text: The Municipal Authority, with the approval of the central government, may issue regulations to further implement and clarify the provisions of this Act. These regulations may address specific technical standards, application forms, fee structures, and procedures for inspections and enforcement. All proposed regulations must undergo a public consultation period of at least 60 days before being finalized and published. Such regulations will have the full force and effect of law and must be consistent with the principles outlined in this Act.

heading: Grants for system upgrades
text: The government of Nordvale may establish grant programs to assist eligible property owners with the cost of upgrading or replacing failing septic systems. To qualify for a grant, the existing system must be confirmed as failing by a certified inspector, and the property owner's annual income must not exceed 150,000 crowns. Grants may cover up to 50% of the total project cost, with a maximum of 10,000 crowns per system. Priority will be given to systems posing immediate environmental or public health risks.

heading: Grants for system upgrades
text: The government of Nordvale may establish grant programs to assist eligible property owners with the cost of upgrading or replacing failing septic systems. To qualify for a grant, the existing system must be confirmed as failing by a certified inspector, and the property owner's annual income must not exceed 180,000 crowns. Grants may cover up to 60% of the total project cost, with a maximum of 12,000 crowns per system. Priority will be given to systems posing immediate environmental or public health risks.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: For new commercial septic systems or systems designed to handle more than 5,000 liters of wastewater per day, an environmental impact assessment must be conducted. This assessment will evaluate potential effects on local groundwater, surface water, and soil quality. The assessment report must be submitted with the permit application and approved by the Municipal Authority before any work can commence. The cost of the assessment is borne by the applicant, and it must be prepared by a qualified environmental consultant.

heading: Setback requirements
text: Septic system components must be installed at specific setback distances from various features. Septic tanks must be at least 5 meters from any building foundation and 15 meters from any property line. Drain fields must be at least 30 meters from any drinking water well or surface water body, and 10 meters from any property line. These distances are critical for protecting water sources and preventing property disputes. Variances may be granted in exceptional circumstances, but only after a thorough review by the Municipal Authority.

heading: Setback requirements
text: Septic system components must be installed at specific setback distances from various features. Septic tanks must be at least 6 meters from any building foundation and 20 meters from any property line. Drain fields must be at least 35 meters from any drinking water well or surface water body, and 12 meters from any property line. These distances are critical for protecting water sources and preventing property disputes. Variances may be granted in exceptional circumstances, but only after a thorough review by the Municipal Authority.

heading: Soil percolation tests
text: Before installing any new septic system or expanding an existing drain field, a soil percolation test must be conducted. This test measures the rate at which water drains through the soil, which is crucial for determining the appropriate size and design of the drain field. The test must be performed by a certified professional and submitted with the permit application. Results indicating a percolation rate slower than 60 minutes per 2.5 centimeters or faster than 5 minutes per 2.5 centimeters will generally require alternative system designs.

heading: Design capacity calculations
text: The design capacity of a septic system must be calculated based on the number of bedrooms in a dwelling for residential systems, or estimated daily wastewater flow for commercial properties. For residential systems, a minimum of 400 liters per day per bedroom is required, with a minimum of two bedrooms assumed for any dwelling. For commercial systems, the design flow must be calculated by a certified designer based on industry-specific usage factors. Over-sizing by 10% is recommended to accommodate future needs.

heading: Design capacity calculations
text: The design capacity of a septic system must be calculated based on the number of bedrooms in a dwelling for residential systems, or estimated daily wastewater flow for commercial properties. For residential systems, a minimum of 450 liters per day per bedroom is required, with a minimum of two bedrooms assumed for any dwelling. For commercial systems, the design flow must be calculated by a certified designer based on industry-specific usage factors. Over-sizing by 15% is recommended to accommodate future needs.

heading: Discharge standards
text: The effluent discharged from any septic system must meet specific quality standards to protect receiving environments. These standards include maximum permissible levels for biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5), total suspended solids (TSS), and fecal coliform bacteria. For example, BOD5 must not exceed 30 milligrams per liter, and fecal coliforms must be below 200 colony-forming units per 100 milliliters. Regular testing may be required for commercial or high-risk systems to ensure ongoing compliance with these standards.

heading: Innovative systems
text: Owners wishing to install innovative or alternative septic systems that deviate from conventional designs must obtain special approval from the Municipal Authority. Such systems must demonstrate equivalent or superior performance in terms of wastewater treatment and environmental protection. A detailed proposal, including pilot study data and long-term monitoring plans, must be submitted for review. Approval may be granted on a probationary basis for an initial period of three years, requiring annual performance reports.

heading: Complaint resolution
text: Any person may file a complaint with the Municipal Authority regarding a suspected septic system violation or malfunction. Complaints must be submitted in writing and provide sufficient detail for investigation. The Authority will investigate all credible complaints within 10 working days. If a violation is found, appropriate enforcement action will be taken as outlined in section 17. The complainant will be notified of the outcome of the investigation within 30 days, without disclosing personal information of the property owner.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text: All personal and proprietary business information submitted to the Municipal Authority under this Act shall be treated as confidential, except where disclosure is required by law or necessary for the enforcement of this Act. This includes financial details related to grant applications and sensitive property information. The Authority must establish procedures to protect such information from unauthorized access or disclosure. Violations of confidentiality by Authority employees may result in disciplinary action.

heading: Cost recovery
text: If an owner fails to comply with an order for corrective action issued by the Municipal Authority, and the Authority is required to undertake the work itself to mitigate a public health or environmental risk, all reasonable costs incurred by the Authority will be recoverable from the owner. These costs may include, but are not limited to, labor, materials, and administrative expenses. A lien may be placed on the property for unpaid costs after 90 days from the date of invoicing.

heading: Financial assistance for low-income owners
text: Low-income property owners, as defined by an annual household income below 80,000 crowns, may be eligible for additional financial assistance for septic system repairs or replacements. This assistance may include reduced permit fees (e.g., 50% reduction) or enhanced grant funding, up to a maximum of 15,000 crowns per system. Applications for this program must include verifiable income statements and a certified assessment of the septic system's condition. Funding is subject to availability and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

heading: Financial assistance for low-income owners
text: Low-income property owners, as defined by an annual household income below 90,000 crowns, may be eligible for additional financial assistance for septic system repairs or replacements. This assistance may include reduced permit fees (e.g., 75% reduction) or enhanced grant funding, up to a maximum of 18,000 crowns per system. Applications for this program must include verifiable income statements and a certified assessment of the septic system's condition. Funding is subject to availability and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

heading: Septic system registry
text: Each Municipal Authority shall establish and maintain a comprehensive registry of all septic systems within its jurisdiction. This registry will include the location of each system, installation date, design specifications, inspection history, and any reported malfunctions or repairs. The data in the registry will be used for planning, enforcement, and public health monitoring. An annual report summarizing the status of septic systems in each municipality must be submitted to the central government by March 31st of each year.

heading: Penalties for repeated violations
text: Owners who commit repeated violations of this Act within a five-year period will face escalating penalties. A second violation within five years will incur a fine double that of the first offense. A third or subsequent violation within the same period may result in a fine of up to 5,000 crowns and mandatory system replacement at the owner's expense, irrespective of the system's age. The Municipal Authority may also impose daily fines of 200 crowns until the violation is fully rectified.

heading: Research and development
text: The government of Nordvale may allocate funds for research and development into new and improved septic system technologies. This includes exploring more efficient treatment methods, sustainable materials, and cost-effective maintenance strategies. Universities and private research institutions may apply for grants to conduct relevant studies. A minimum of 500,000 crowns will be budgeted annually for such initiatives to foster innovation in wastewater management. Results of funded research will be made publicly available within one year of completion.

heading: Drainage system connection
text: No component of a septic system shall be connected to a stormwater drainage system or any other system designed to convey rainwater. The discharge of treated or untreated wastewater into stormwater drains is strictly prohibited. Any such connection found during an inspection will be considered a serious violation, subject to immediate corrective action and a fine of 2,500 crowns. The owner will be required to disconnect the improper connection within 72 hours of notification and submit proof of compliance.

heading: Public awareness campaigns
text: The Municipal Authority shall undertake public awareness campaigns to educate property owners about the proper use and maintenance of septic systems. These campaigns will utilize various media, including informational brochures, municipal websites, and community workshops. Key messages will focus on preventing system failures, recognizing early signs of malfunction, and the importance of regular inspections and pumping. A budget of at least 20,000 crowns annually will be allocated for these educational initiatives to promote responsible septic system stewardship.

heading: Public awareness campaigns
text: The Municipal Authority shall undertake public awareness campaigns to educate property owners about the proper use and maintenance of septic systems. These campaigns will utilize various media, including informational brochures, municipal websites, and community workshops. Key messages will focus on preventing system failures, recognizing early signs of malfunction, and the importance of regular inspections and pumping. A budget of at least 30,000 crowns annually will be allocated for these educational initiatives to promote responsible septic system stewardship.

heading: Special provisions for Dunmere
text: Due to unique geological conditions and high groundwater tables in the municipality of Dunmere, all new septic system installations must include an advanced treatment unit certified to achieve a minimum of 85% nitrogen reduction. This requirement is in addition to all other standards outlined in this Act. The Municipal Authority in Dunmere may offer a one-time rebate of up to 1,000 crowns to offset the additional cost of such units for residential properties. This measure aims to protect the sensitive aquatic ecosystems in the region.

heading: Special provisions for Dunmere
text: Due to unique geological conditions and high groundwater tables in the municipality of Dunmere, all new septic system installations must include an advanced treatment unit certified to achieve a minimum of 90% nitrogen reduction. This requirement is in addition to all other standards outlined in this Act. The Municipal Authority in Dunmere may offer a one-time rebate of up to 1,500 crowns to offset the additional cost of such units for residential properties. This measure aims to protect the sensitive aquatic ecosystems in the region.

heading: Special provisions for Dunmere
text: Due to unique geological conditions and high groundwater tables in the municipality of Dunmere, all new septic system installations must include an advanced treatment unit certified to achieve a minimum of 92% nitrogen reduction. This requirement is in addition to all other standards outlined in this Act. The Municipal Authority in Dunmere may offer a one-time rebate of up to 2,000 crowns to offset the additional cost of such units for residential properties. This measure aims to protect the sensitive aquatic ecosystems in the region.

heading: Septic tank material standards
text: All septic tanks installed or replaced after the commencement of this Act must be constructed from durable, watertight materials such as reinforced concrete, fiberglass, or high-density polyethylene. Steel tanks are prohibited due to their susceptibility to corrosion. Tanks must be designed to withstand anticipated earth loads and vehicular traffic, if applicable, and must include accessible risers to grade for inspection and pumping ports. The minimum wall thickness for concrete tanks must be 10 centimeters.

heading: Gravity flow preference
text: Septic system designs should, wherever feasible, prioritize gravity-fed effluent distribution. Pump systems should only be utilized when site topography makes gravity flow impractical or impossible. If a pump system is necessary, it must include an alarm system to alert the owner of pump failure and a readily accessible emergency disconnect switch. The pump chamber must have a minimum storage capacity of 24 hours of peak flow to prevent immediate overflow during power outages.

heading: Phased implementation
text: The provisions of this Act will be implemented in phases across the Republic of Nordvale. Phase 1, commencing on January 1, 2018, applies to the municipalities of Aldmark and Brenholt. Phase 2, effective July 1, 2018, will extend application to Corvik and Dunmere. All remaining municipalities, including Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, will be covered under Phase 3, beginning January 1, 2019. The Municipal Authority for each phase is responsible for notifying affected property owners at least 90 days prior to implementation.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the central government every five years from its commencement date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. The first review will occur by January 1, 2023. Public input will be solicited during the review process, with a minimum 60-day consultation period for stakeholder feedback. A report summarizing the review findings and proposed changes will be presented to the municipal councils and published for public access.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the central government every three years from its commencement date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. The first review will occur by January 1, 2023. Public input will be solicited during the review process, with a minimum 60-day consultation period for stakeholder feedback. A report summarizing the review findings and proposed changes will be presented to the municipal councils and published for public access.

heading: Exemptions
text: Each licensed glassblower pays a reduced admission fee of 5 crowns to the maritime museum.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered thatcher has an additional 30 days to pay the annual electric bicycle registration fee.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates the sale of goods from carts, tables, kiosks and similar places on public streets and squares.
(2) This Act does not apply to a stall at a municipal market; such a stall is governed by FDA §30.
(3) It applies to every person who sells goods on a public street outside a municipal market.
(4) This Act does not apply to selling goods from a van, which is charged under FDA §29, or to trading that needs a permit under SBA §21, SBA §24 or SBA §25.

heading: Licence required
text:
(1) No person may trade on a public street without a street trading licence.
(2) A licence is granted for one pitch or one route.
(3) A person who trades without a licence commits an offence.

heading: Monthly licence fee
text:
(1) The holder of a street trading licence shall pay a licence fee of 35 crowns per month.
(2) The fee is paid in advance for each calendar month.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the holder stops trading during the month.

heading: Monthly licence fee
text:
(1) The holder of a street trading licence shall pay a licence fee of 40 crowns per month.
(2) The fee is paid in advance for each calendar month.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the holder stops trading during the month.

heading: Daily licence
text:
(1) A person may instead buy a daily street trading licence for 9 crowns per day.
(2) A daily licence is valid for one pitch on the day shown.
(3) A person may buy daily licences for at most 10 days in a calendar month.

heading: Pitch size
text:
(1) A pitch shall not be larger than 2 square metres.
(2) A pitch shall be marked on the pavement by the municipality.
(3) A trader shall keep all goods and equipment within the marked pitch.

heading: Trading hours
text:
(1) Street trading is permitted between 07:00 and 20:00.
(2) A trader shall clear the pitch within 30 minutes after the end of trading hours.
(3) The municipality may fix shorter hours for a particular street.

heading: Trading hours
text:
(1) Street trading is permitted between 06:00 and 20:00.
(2) A trader shall clear the pitch within 30 minutes after the end of trading hours.
(3) The municipality may fix shorter hours for a particular street.

heading: Mobile traders
text:
(1) A mobile trader is a trader who sells goods from a moving cart or a bicycle.
(2) A mobile trader shall not stay in the same place for more than 2 hours.
(3) A mobile trader shall pay the daily licence fee in section 4 for each day of trading.

heading: Food sold on the street
text:
(1) A trader who sells food shall be registered under FHA §3.
(2) The registration certificate shall be displayed on the cart.
(3) A trader who sells only packaged goods that need no cooling needs no registration.

heading: Distance from shops
text:
(1) A pitch shall be at least 5 metres from the entrance of a shop.
(2) A pitch shall be at least 10 metres from a pedestrian crossing.
(3) The municipality may allow an exception if the shop owner agrees in writing.

heading: Clear footpath
text:
(1) A trader shall keep a clear footpath of at least 2 metres wide beside the pitch.
(2) A trader shall not place signs or goods on the footpath.
(3) A trader who obstructs the footpath shall move on the request of an official.

heading: Display of licence
text:
(1) The licence shall be displayed on the cart or table where customers can see it.
(2) The licence shall show the name of the holder and the pitch number.
(3) A trader shall show the licence to an official on request.

heading: Licence term
text:
(1) A monthly licence is valid for one calendar month and may be renewed.
(2) A trader may hold a licence for at most 12 consecutive months before applying again.
(3) A licence lapses if the trader does not trade for 60 days.

heading: Charity collections
text:
(1) A charity may collect money in the street without a licence for up to 4 days in a calendar year.
(2) Collectors shall wear a badge showing the name of the charity.
(3) Collectors shall not sell goods in return for donations.

heading: Seasonal licence
text:
(1) A seasonal licence for the period 1 December to 31 December costs 60 crowns.
(2) A seasonal licence is valid for one pitch.
(3) The holder of a seasonal licence need not pay the monthly fee in section 3 for the same pitch.

heading: Seasonal licence
text:
(1) A seasonal licence for the period 1 December to 31 December costs 75 crowns.
(2) A seasonal licence is valid for one pitch.
(3) The holder of a seasonal licence need not pay the monthly fee in section 3 for the same pitch.

heading: Noise
text:
(1) A trader shall not use a loudspeaker or any amplified music.
(2) A trader shall not call out to passers-by with a device.
(3) An official may order a trader to stop causing noise.

heading: Fine for trading without a licence
text:
(1) A person who trades without a licence shall pay a fine of 150 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) The fine is doubled for a second offence within 12 months.

heading: Fine for trading without a licence
text:
(1) A person who trades without a licence shall pay a fine of 200 crowns.
(2) The fine is due within 30 days of notice.
(3) The fine is doubled for a second offence within 12 months.

heading: Seizure of goods
text:
(1) An official may seize goods from a trader who trades without a licence.
(2) The seized goods shall be stored for 14 days.
(3) The trader may collect the goods within that period after paying the fine in section 16.

heading: Young traders
text:
(1) A person under 18 years of age may hold a street trading licence only with the written consent of a parent.
(2) A person under 16 years of age shall not hold a licence.
(3) A young trader shall not trade after 18:00.

heading: Young traders
text:
(1) A person under 18 years of age may hold a street trading licence only with the written consent of a parent.
(2) A person under 15 years of age shall not hold a licence.
(3) A young trader shall not trade after 18:00.

heading: Newspaper sellers
text:
(1) A person who sells newspapers only may trade without a licence.
(2) The exemption applies to the sale of newspapers and magazines from a stand of at most 1 square metre.

heading: Newspaper sellers
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) A person who is harmed by street trading may complain to the municipality.
(2) The municipality shall answer a complaint within 21 days.
(3) The municipality may move a pitch or cancel a licence if a complaint is justified and the trader has been heard.

heading: Registration as a sole proprietor after an apprenticeship
text:
(1) A person who registers as a sole proprietor under SBA §2 while still a registered apprentice, or within 6 months after the end of his or her apprenticeship contract, pays half of the registration fee under SBA §3.
(2) The half fee is calculated on the fee that applies to the person's age.
(3) This section does not apply to the late registration surcharge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for the construction, modification, and operation of sewage treatment plants within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure public health, protect the environment, and maintain water quality standards across all municipalities. The Act outlines the procedures for obtaining permits, the obligations of permit holders, and the consequences of non-compliance, applying to all facilities processing domestic, commercial, or industrial wastewater before discharge into natural water bodies or reuse systems. It ensures that all sewage treatment activities adhere to national environmental guidelines.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall construct, operate, or significantly modify a sewage treatment plant without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the Environmental Protection Agency of Nordvale. This requirement applies to all plants processing more than 10 cubic meters of wastewater per day. Any alteration increasing the plant's capacity by more than 15% or changing its primary treatment method necessitates a new permit application. Failure to comply with this section may result in significant penalties.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall construct, operate, or significantly modify a sewage treatment plant without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the Environmental Protection Agency of Nordvale. This requirement applies to all plants processing more than 8 cubic meters of wastewater per day. Any alteration increasing the plant's capacity by more than 10% or changing its primary treatment method necessitates a new permit application. Failure to comply with this section may result in significant penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall construct, operate, or significantly modify a sewage treatment plant without first obtaining a valid permit issued by the Environmental Protection Agency of Nordvale. This requirement applies to all plants processing more than 5 cubic meters of wastewater per day. Any alteration increasing the plant's capacity by more than 8% or changing its primary or secondary treatment method necessitates a new permit application. Failure to comply with this section may result in significant penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a sewage treatment plant permit must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency at least 180 days prior to the planned commencement of construction or modification. The application must include detailed engineering plans, environmental impact assessments, and a proposed operational management plan. A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns must accompany the submission. Incomplete applications will be returned within 30 days, requiring resubmission and potentially delaying the approval process significantly.

heading: Application Content
text:
Each permit application must contain, at a minimum, the following information:
(a) Detailed site plans and topographical maps, scaled at 1:500 or greater.
(b) Technical specifications of all major equipment, including pumps, filters, and disinfection units.
(c) A comprehensive water quality monitoring program, detailing sampling points and frequency.
(d) Proof of financial capacity to construct and operate the plant for at least 5 years.
(e) An emergency response plan for spills or equipment failures, outlining procedures and contact information for local emergency services.

heading: Application Content
text:
Each permit application must contain, at a minimum, the following information:
(a) Detailed site plans and topographical maps, scaled at 1:250 or greater, showing all adjacent properties within 100 meters.
(b) Technical specifications of all major equipment, including pumps, filters, disinfection units, and sludge handling systems.
(c) A comprehensive water quality monitoring program, detailing sampling points, frequency, and analytical methods.
(d) Proof of financial capacity to construct and operate the plant for at least 7 years, including decommissioning costs.
(e) An emergency response plan for spills, equipment failures, or natural disasters, outlining procedures, contact information, and communication protocols for local emergency services and affected communities.

heading: Public Consultation Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Environmental Protection Agency must initiate a public consultation period of 60 days. During this period, the application documents will be made available for public inspection at the relevant municipal offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, and on the Agency's official website. Any interested party may submit written comments or objections within this timeframe. A public hearing may be scheduled if requested by at least 25 citizens or two municipal councils.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: All permit applications for new sewage treatment plants or major expansions must include a detailed environmental impact assessment (EIA). The EIA must evaluate potential impacts on local ecosystems, water bodies, air quality, and noise levels. It must also propose mitigation measures to minimize adverse effects. The assessment should cover a radius of at least 5 kilometers from the proposed site and consider both construction and operational phases. A qualified independent environmental consultant must prepare the EIA.

heading: Permit Review and Approval
text: The Environmental Protection Agency will review all submitted documentation, public comments, and the EIA report. A decision on the permit application will be issued within 90 days following the close of the public consultation period. The Agency may approve, deny, or approve with conditions. Conditions may include specific monitoring requirements, stricter discharge limits, or modifications to plant design. A refusal will state the reasons clearly and provide guidance for potential resubmission.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A permit for the construction and operation of a sewage treatment plant is valid for a period of 10 years from the date of issue. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 180 days before the expiry date. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe will result in the permit lapsing, requiring a new application process, including all fees and assessments. Operational permits for plants over 20 years old will be subject to a more stringent renewal process.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A permit for the construction and operation of a sewage treatment plant is valid for a period of 8 years from the date of issue. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 210 days before the expiry date. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe will result in the permit lapsing, requiring a new application process, including all fees and assessments. Operational permits for plants over 15 years old will be subject to a more stringent renewal process, including a mandatory site audit.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A permit for the construction and operation of a sewage treatment plant is valid for a period of 7 years from the date of issue. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 240 days before the expiry date. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe will result in the permit lapsing, requiring a new application process, including all fees and assessments. Operational permits for plants over 12 years old will be subject to a more stringent renewal process, including a mandatory site audit and an updated environmental risk assessment.

heading: Renewal Application Requirements
text: An application for permit renewal must include a summary of the plant's operational performance over the preceding permit period, an updated management plan, and any proposed changes to the plant's operation or design. A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is required. For plants that have been in operation for more than 15 years, a comprehensive structural integrity report for all major infrastructure components must also be submitted. Any outstanding compliance issues must be addressed prior to renewal.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: Permits issued under this Act are transferable, but only with the express written consent of the Environmental Protection Agency. An application for transfer must be submitted within 60 days of the change in ownership or operational control, accompanied by a transfer fee of 1,000 crowns. The new owner must demonstrate the financial and technical capacity to operate the plant in compliance with all permit conditions. The Agency reserves the right to deny a transfer if the new party fails to meet established criteria.

heading: General Operating Conditions
text: All sewage treatment plants must operate in accordance with the specifications detailed in their permit and adhere to all relevant national environmental standards. This includes maintaining proper treatment levels, preventing unauthorized discharges, and ensuring the safety of personnel and the public. Plants must have trained personnel on site at all times during operational hours, and an emergency contact available 24/7. Records of daily operations and maintenance must be kept for at least 3 years.

heading: Discharge Standards
text:
Treated effluent discharged from any sewage treatment plant must meet the following minimum standards:
(a) Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD5) not exceeding 20 mg/L.
(b) Total Suspended Solids (TSS) not exceeding 30 mg/L.
(c) pH level between 6.0 and 9.0.
(d) E. coli count not exceeding 1000 colony-forming units (CFU) per 100 mL.
These standards are subject to revision by the Environmental Protection Agency, with 90 days' notice given to all permit holders prior to implementation of new limits. Non-compliance with these limits constitutes a serious breach of permit conditions.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting
text: Permit holders are required to conduct regular monitoring of effluent quality as specified in their permit, with sampling occurring at least once a week. Results must be reported to the Environmental Protection Agency on a quarterly basis. Any instance of non-compliance with discharge standards must be reported immediately, within 24 hours of detection. Annual reports, summarizing all operational data and compliance records, must be submitted by January 31st of each year. Failure to submit reports may incur a penalty of 500 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting
text: Permit holders are required to conduct regular monitoring of effluent quality as specified in their permit, with sampling occurring at least twice a week. Results must be reported to the Environmental Protection Agency on a monthly basis. Any instance of non-compliance with discharge standards exceeding 15% of the limit must be reported immediately, within 12 hours of detection. Annual reports, summarizing all operational data and compliance records, must be submitted by December 31st of each year. Failure to submit reports may incur a penalty of 750 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting
text: Permit holders are required to conduct regular monitoring of effluent quality as specified in their permit, with sampling occurring at least three times a week. Results must be reported to the Environmental Protection Agency on a bi-weekly basis. Any instance of non-compliance with discharge standards exceeding 10% of the limit must be reported immediately, within 6 hours of detection. Annual reports, summarizing all operational data and compliance records, must be submitted by November 30th of each year. Failure to submit reports may incur a penalty of 1,000 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Access for Inspection
text: Permit holders must grant authorized representatives of the Environmental Protection Agency full and unrestricted access to the sewage treatment plant premises, including all treatment units, monitoring stations, and records, during normal operating hours. Inspections may be conducted without prior notice to verify compliance with permit conditions and this Act. Refusal of access or obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may lead to permit suspension or revocation.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All records pertaining to the operation, maintenance, monitoring, and compliance of the sewage treatment plant must be kept on site for a minimum period of 5 years. These records include, but are not limited to, daily logbooks, laboratory analysis reports, calibration records for instruments, and incident reports. Records must be organized and readily accessible for inspection. Digital records are permissible, provided they are securely stored and backed up regularly, with hard copies available upon request.

heading: Non-Compliance and Corrective Action
