text: In the event of non-compliance with any permit condition or provision of this Act, the permit holder must take immediate corrective action to rectify the situation. A written report detailing the non-compliance, the cause, and the corrective actions taken, along with a timeline for full resolution, must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency within 7 days of discovery. Failure to implement corrective actions promptly may result in further enforcement measures.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text: Every sewage treatment plant must maintain an up-to-date emergency response plan, reviewed and updated annually. This plan must detail procedures for responding to equipment failures, power outages, hazardous material spills, and overflows, including contact information for relevant authorities (e.g., local fire services, municipal water departments, and the Environmental Protection Agency). Drills for key emergency scenarios must be conducted at least once every two years, with records of these drills maintained for inspection.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text: Every sewage treatment plant must maintain an up-to-date emergency response plan, reviewed and updated every 6 months. This plan must detail procedures for responding to equipment failures, power outages, hazardous material spills, overflows, and natural disasters, including contact information for relevant authorities (e.g., local fire services, municipal water departments, and the Environmental Protection Agency). Drills for key emergency scenarios must be conducted at least once a year, with records of these drills maintained for inspection for at least 5 years. The plan must also include public notification protocols.

heading: Sludge Management
text: All sludge generated by sewage treatment plants must be handled, stored, and disposed of in an environmentally sound manner, in accordance with national waste management regulations. A detailed sludge management plan, specifying volume estimation, dewatering processes, and ultimate disposal methods, must be included in the permit application. Sludge must not be discharged into natural water bodies or used on agricultural land without prior authorization and testing for heavy metals and pathogens. Records of sludge disposal must be kept for 3 years.

heading: Sludge Management
text: All sludge generated by sewage treatment plants must be handled, stored, transported, and disposed of in an environmentally sound manner, in accordance with national waste management regulations. A detailed sludge management plan, specifying volume estimation, dewatering processes, stabilization methods, and ultimate disposal or reuse methods, must be included in the permit application and updated every 3 years. Sludge must not be discharged into natural water bodies or used on agricultural land without prior authorization and rigorous testing for heavy metals, pathogens, and emerging contaminants. Records of sludge disposal, including transport manifests, must be kept for 5 years.

heading: Plant Decommissioning
text: A permit holder intending to decommission a sewage treatment plant must submit a decommissioning plan to the Environmental Protection Agency at least 1 year prior to the planned cessation of operations. The plan must detail the safe removal of all equipment, remediation of the site, and measures to prevent any environmental contamination. Financial provisions for decommissioning must be demonstrated, amounting to at least 10% of the original construction cost or 500,000 crowns, whichever is higher. The Agency must approve the plan before any decommissioning work commences.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any person or entity aggrieved by a decision of the Environmental Protection Agency regarding a permit application, renewal, transfer, or enforcement action may appeal the decision to the Environmental Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving written notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and supported by relevant documentation. The Board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days, which will be final unless judicial review is sought.

heading: False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in a permit application, renewal submission, monitoring report, or any other document required under this Act commits an offense. Such an offense may result in the immediate denial, suspension, or revocation of the permit, in addition to fines up to 50,000 crowns. If the false information leads to significant environmental harm, further legal action, including criminal charges, may be pursued.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency under this Act, with the exception of trade secrets or commercially sensitive data clearly marked as such, will be considered public record. Trade secrets or sensitive data will be held confidential, provided that the applicant justifies the claim for confidentiality. The Agency will make a determination on confidentiality within 14 days of submission. Information related to effluent quality and compliance records can never be deemed confidential.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: The fees outlined in this Act (application, renewal, transfer) are subject to periodic review and adjustment by the Environmental Protection Agency. Any changes to fees will be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 90 days before coming into effect. All fees are non-refundable and must be paid in full at the time of submission. Failure to pay required fees will result in the immediate rejection of the relevant application or submission.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Environmental Protection Agency has the power to issue compliance orders, administrative penalties, and cease and desist orders to permit holders or any person acting in contravention of this Act. In cases of imminent environmental danger or severe public health risk, the Agency may shut down a plant's operations immediately without prior notice. These enforcement powers are in addition to any other remedies available by law.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any permit holder found to be in non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or their permit conditions may be liable for administrative penalties. Minor infractions may incur fines from 5,000 crowns to 20,000 crowns. Serious or repeated non-compliance may result in fines up to 100,000 crowns per day of violation, permit suspension for up to 6 months, or complete permit revocation. The severity of the penalty will consider the extent of environmental harm and the permit holder's compliance history.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any permit holder found to be in non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or their permit conditions may be liable for administrative penalties. Minor infractions may incur fines from 10,000 crowns to 30,000 crowns. Serious or repeated non-compliance may result in fines up to 150,000 crowns per day of violation, permit suspension for up to 9 months, or complete permit revocation. The severity of the penalty will consider the extent of environmental harm, the permit holder's compliance history, and whether the non-compliance was intentional.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any permit holder found to be in non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or their permit conditions may be liable for administrative penalties. Minor infractions may incur fines from 15,000 crowns to 40,000 crowns. Serious or repeated non-compliance may result in fines up to 200,000 crowns per day of violation, permit suspension for up to 12 months, or complete permit revocation. The severity of the penalty will consider the extent of environmental harm, the permit holder's compliance history, and whether the non-compliance was intentional or due to gross negligence. Additionally, the Environmental Protection Agency may require the permit holder to fund environmental remediation efforts.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text:
The Environmental Protection Agency may revoke a permit if a permit holder:
(a) Fails to comply with a significant condition of the permit or a provision of this Act.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in connection with the permit.
(c) Fails to pay required fees or penalties.
(d) Causes severe and irreparable environmental damage.
(e) Abandons the sewage treatment plant without proper decommissioning.
Before revocation, the permit holder will be given 60 days' notice and an opportunity to be heard, unless there is an immediate threat to public health or the environment.

heading: Indemnification
text: Permit holders are solely responsible for any environmental damage, injury, or loss of property resulting from the construction, operation, or decommissioning of their sewage treatment plant. Permit holders must indemnify and hold harmless the Government of Nordvale, its agencies, and employees from any claims, liabilities, costs, or expenses arising from such damage, injury, or loss. This indemnification clause applies regardless of whether the permit holder was operating in compliance with their permit at the time of the incident.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: Applicants for new permits must provide proof of financial assurance, such as a bond, letter of credit, or escrow account, sufficient to cover potential environmental liabilities and decommissioning costs. The amount of financial assurance will be determined by the Environmental Protection Agency, based on the size and complexity of the plant and potential environmental risks, but shall not be less than 250,000 crowns. This assurance must be maintained for the entire operational life of the plant and for 2 years post-decommissioning.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: Applicants for new permits must provide proof of financial assurance, such as a bond, letter of credit, or escrow account, sufficient to cover potential environmental liabilities, emergency response costs, and decommissioning costs. The amount of financial assurance will be determined by the Environmental Protection Agency, based on the size and complexity of the plant and potential environmental risks, but shall not be less than 400,000 crowns. This assurance must be maintained for the entire operational life of the plant and for 3 years post-decommissioning, with annual proof of sufficiency.

heading: Technological Upgrades
text: The Environmental Protection Agency may, by written notice, require permit holders to implement technological upgrades to their sewage treatment plants if new and more effective treatment methods become widely available or if stricter environmental standards are introduced. Permit holders will be given a reasonable timeframe, typically between 2 and 5 years, to comply with such requirements. Financial assistance or incentives for upgrades may be considered on a case-by-case basis for plants serving populations under 5,000.

heading: Municipal Cooperation
text: Municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, must cooperate with the Environmental Protection Agency in the enforcement of this Act. This includes providing access to municipal lands for inspections, sharing relevant data, and facilitating public consultation processes. Municipal sewage treatment plants are subject to the same permit requirements and standards as privately owned facilities. Municipalities are encouraged to develop long-term wastewater management strategies.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Environmental Protection Agency will establish a fund, capitalized with 5% of all permit fees collected, to support research and development into innovative and sustainable sewage treatment technologies. Academic institutions, private companies, and municipal entities may apply for grants from this fund to conduct pilot projects or studies aimed at improving wastewater treatment efficiency, reducing energy consumption, or enhancing nutrient recovery. Grant applications will be reviewed annually by a panel of experts.

heading: Small-Scale Plants
text: Sewage treatment plants processing less than 10 cubic meters of wastewater per day are exempt from some of the detailed reporting requirements of section 13 but must still obtain a simplified permit. These small-scale permits are valid for 15 years and require annual submission of a basic operational report. They must adhere to all discharge standards outlined in section 12. A simplified application fee of 1,000 crowns applies. These plants are still subject to inspection and enforcement actions for non-compliance.

heading: Small-Scale Plants
text: Sewage treatment plants processing less than 8 cubic meters of wastewater per day are exempt from some of the detailed reporting requirements of section 13 but must still obtain a simplified permit. These small-scale permits are valid for 12 years and require semi-annual submission of a basic operational report. They must adhere to all discharge standards outlined in section 12. A simplified application fee of 1,200 crowns applies. These plants are still subject to inspection and enforcement actions for non-compliance, particularly concerning public health risks.

heading: Small-Scale Plants
text: Sewage treatment plants processing less than 5 cubic meters of wastewater per day are exempt from some of the detailed reporting requirements of section 13 but must still obtain a simplified permit. These small-scale permits are valid for 10 years and require quarterly submission of a basic operational report. They must adhere to all discharge standards outlined in section 12. A simplified application fee of 1,500 crowns applies. These plants are still subject to inspection and enforcement actions for non-compliance, particularly concerning public health risks and cumulative environmental impact in sensitive areas.

heading: Wastewater Reuse
text: Any treated wastewater intended for reuse, such as for irrigation or industrial processes, must meet specific quality standards beyond those for discharge into natural waters. A separate permit for wastewater reuse must be obtained from the Environmental Protection Agency. This permit will specify the permitted uses, additional treatment requirements, and monitoring protocols. The reuse permit application must detail the end-use of the treated water, the potential for human exposure, and risk mitigation measures. A fee of 750 crowns applies.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Existing sewage treatment plants operating prior to the enactment of this Act have a period of 2 years from the effective date to apply for a permit. During this transitional period, these plants must demonstrate a good faith effort to comply with the new standards and monitoring requirements. Failure to apply for a permit within this 2-year window will result in the plant being deemed an unauthorized operation, subject to immediate enforcement actions and penalties as per section 25.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions or parts shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity or unenforceability of any single part shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the entire Act, thereby ensuring the continued regulation of sewage treatment plants. This provision is intended to preserve the core intent and functionality of the legislation.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date. The review will assess the effectiveness of the regulatory framework, the adequacy of environmental protection measures, and the impact on municipalities and permit holders. Recommendations for amendments or improvements will be submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency as part of this review process. Public input will be sought during the review period to ensure comprehensive evaluation.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into effect on January 1, 2018.

heading: Garden waste from smallholdings
text: A smallholder may leave up to 600 kilograms of garden waste at a recycling yard on each visit without charge.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for regulating the discharge of industrial waste by various enterprises within Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to protect public health, safeguard the natural environment, and ensure the sustainable management of water resources across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This regulation applies to any industrial facility that releases liquid or solid waste into public sewer systems, rivers, lakes, or directly onto land within the national borders.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No industrial facility shall discharge any industrial waste into a public system or natural environment without first obtaining a valid Industrial Discharge Permit issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any discharge without such a permit or in violation of its terms is strictly prohibited. Facilities found to be discharging without a permit will be subject to immediate cessation orders and significant financial penalties, as outlined in later sections of this Act.

heading: Application for permit
text: An application for an Industrial Discharge Permit must be submitted to the National Environmental Bureau (NEB) at least 90 days prior to the planned commencement of discharge. The application must include detailed information about the industrial process, the chemical composition of the waste, the proposed discharge volume, and any pre-treatment methods employed. A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: Application for permit
text: An application for an Industrial Discharge Permit must be submitted to the National Environmental Bureau (NEB) at least 120 days prior to the planned commencement of discharge. The application must include detailed information about the industrial process, the chemical composition of the waste, the proposed discharge volume, and any pre-treatment methods employed. A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned within 14 days.

heading: Application for permit
text: An application for an Industrial Discharge Permit must be submitted to the National Environmental Bureau (NEB) at least 150 days prior to the planned commencement of discharge. The application must include detailed information about the industrial process, the chemical composition of the waste, the proposed discharge volume, and any pre-treatment methods employed, along with a detailed environmental impact assessment. A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned within 7 days.

heading: Application contents
text: Each application for a permit shall contain: (a) the legal name and address of the applicant; (b) a detailed description of the industrial activity generating the waste; (c) a comprehensive analysis of the waste stream, including pH, temperature, and concentrations of all regulated substances; (d) the proposed maximum daily discharge volume, not to exceed 100 cubic meters; and (e) a site plan indicating all discharge points. All chemical analyses must be performed by an accredited laboratory.

heading: Application contents
text: Each application for a permit shall contain: (a) the legal name and address of the applicant; (b) a detailed description of the industrial activity generating the waste; (c) a comprehensive analysis of the waste stream, including pH, temperature, and concentrations of all regulated substances; (d) the proposed maximum daily discharge volume, not to exceed 80 cubic meters; and (e) a site plan indicating all discharge points and nearby sensitive ecosystems. All chemical analyses must be performed by an accredited laboratory, with results no older than 30 days.

heading: Public notice of application
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the NEB shall publish a notice of the application in the official government gazette and on its public website within 14 days. This notice will include the applicant's name, the location of the facility, and a brief description of the proposed discharge. Interested parties may submit written comments or objections to the NEB within 30 days of the publication date. All comments received will be considered during the permit review process.

heading: Review period
text: The NEB shall review all permit applications and public comments within 60 days of the close of the public comment period. During this review, the NEB may request additional information from the applicant, which must be provided within 21 days. Failure to provide requested information within the specified timeframe may result in the application being deemed incomplete and rejected without refund of the application fee.

heading: Permit issuance criteria
text: A permit may be issued if the NEB determines that: (a) the proposed discharge will not cause or contribute to a violation of established environmental quality standards; (b) the applicant has demonstrated the financial and technical capability to comply with permit conditions; and (c) all waste will be treated to meet minimum standards before discharge. The discharge must not exceed 50 milligrams per liter of total suspended solids.

heading: Permit issuance criteria
text: A permit may be issued if the NEB determines that: (a) the proposed discharge will not cause or contribute to a violation of established environmental quality standards; (b) the applicant has demonstrated the financial and technical capability to comply with permit conditions; (c) all waste will be treated to meet minimum standards before discharge; and (d) the facility implements a waste reduction plan. The discharge must not exceed 30 milligrams per liter of total suspended solids.

heading: Permit conditions
text: Each permit issued under this Act shall specify: (a) the maximum allowable discharge volume per day, not to exceed 100 cubic meters; (b) the maximum allowable concentrations of specific pollutants; (c) monitoring and reporting requirements, including the frequency of sampling; (d) record-keeping obligations for a minimum of 3 years; and (e) any specific pre-treatment requirements. All permit conditions are legally binding and non-negotiable once issued.

heading: Permit conditions
text: Each permit issued under this Act shall specify: (a) the maximum allowable discharge volume per day, not to exceed 75 cubic meters; (b) the maximum allowable concentrations of specific pollutants; (c) monitoring and reporting requirements, including the frequency of sampling and the analysis methods; (d) record-keeping obligations for a minimum of 5 years; and (e) any specific pre-treatment requirements, including the technology to be used. All permit conditions are legally binding and non-negotiable once issued.

heading: Permit duration
text: An Industrial Discharge Permit shall be valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance, unless otherwise specified in the permit or revoked earlier in accordance with this Act. A permit holder must apply for renewal at least 180 days before the expiry date. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe will result in the permit expiring, and any subsequent discharge will be considered unpermitted.

heading: Permit renewal
text: An application for permit renewal must be submitted to the NEB at least 180 days prior to the permit's expiration. The renewal application must include updated waste analysis reports and a summary of compliance history over the previous permit term. A renewal fee of 1,000 crowns is required. The NEB may require additional information or a site inspection before approving a renewal.

heading: Permit renewal
text: An application for permit renewal must be submitted to the NEB at least 210 days prior to the permit's expiration. The renewal application must include updated waste analysis reports, a summary of compliance history over the previous permit term, and a detailed plan for continuous environmental improvement. A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is required. The NEB may require additional information or a site inspection before approving a renewal, and public comments may be solicited.

heading: Monitoring requirements
text: Permit holders are required to monitor their discharge according to the schedule and parameters specified in their permit. This typically involves daily pH checks and weekly sampling for key pollutants. All monitoring data must be accurately recorded and maintained on-site for a minimum of 3 years. The NEB may require the installation of continuous monitoring equipment for facilities discharging more than 50 cubic meters per day.

heading: Monitoring requirements
text: Permit holders are required to monitor their discharge according to the schedule and parameters specified in their permit. This typically involves daily pH checks, daily temperature readings, and weekly sampling for key pollutants. All monitoring data must be accurately recorded and maintained on-site for a minimum of 5 years. The NEB may require the installation of continuous monitoring equipment for facilities discharging more than 30 cubic meters per day, or for those discharging into sensitive environments.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: Permit holders must submit quarterly reports to the NEB detailing their monitoring results, discharge volumes, and any instances of non-compliance. These reports are due within 30 days after the end of each quarter. Any exceedance of permit limits must be reported verbally to the NEB within 24 hours of discovery, followed by a written report within 5 days explaining the cause and corrective actions taken. Failure to report promptly may result in penalties.

heading: Record keeping
text: All records related to the industrial discharge, including application materials, permits, monitoring data, calibration logs, and incident reports, must be kept on the premises of the permitted facility for a minimum period of 3 years. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by NEB officials during regular business hours. Digital records are acceptable provided they are securely backed up and retrievable upon request within 24 hours.

heading: Inspections
text: NEB officials are authorized to conduct unannounced inspections of any industrial facility at reasonable times to verify compliance with this Act and permit conditions. Inspectors may: (a) enter the premises; (b) examine records; (c) take samples of waste streams; and (d) interview personnel. Facilities must cooperate fully with inspectors. Obstructing an inspection may result in fines of up to 5,000 crowns and permit revocation.

heading: Compliance orders
text: If, upon inspection or review of reports, the NEB finds a violation of this Act or a permit condition, it may issue a compliance order. This order will specify the nature of the violation, the required corrective actions, and a reasonable timeframe for compliance, typically not exceeding 30 days. Failure to comply with a compliance order may lead to further enforcement actions, including administrative penalties or permit suspension.

heading: Administrative penalties
text: Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or a condition of a permit may be liable to an administrative penalty. For minor infractions, the penalty may be up to 10,000 crowns. For serious or repeated violations, penalties can range from 10,000 to 50,000 crowns per day of violation. The NEB will consider the severity, duration, and environmental impact of the violation when determining the penalty amount.

heading: Administrative penalties
text: Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or a condition of a permit may be liable to an administrative penalty. For minor infractions, the penalty may be up to 15,000 crowns. For serious or repeated violations, penalties can range from 20,000 to 75,000 crowns per day of violation. The NEB will consider the severity, duration, environmental impact, and economic benefit gained from non-compliance when determining the penalty amount.

heading: Permit suspension
text: The NEB may suspend a permit for a period not exceeding 90 days if a permit holder: (a) fails to comply with a compliance order; (b) repeatedly violates permit conditions; or (c) provides false or misleading information in reports. During suspension, all discharge activities must cease immediately. A suspended permit can be reinstated upon satisfactory demonstration of compliance and payment of any outstanding penalties.

heading: Permit revocation
text: The NEB may revoke a permit if a permit holder: (a) continues to violate this Act or permit conditions after a suspension; (b) causes significant and irreversible environmental damage; or (c) intentionally misrepresents information essential to the permit decision. Revocation means the permanent termination of discharge authorization. A facility whose permit is revoked may not apply for a new permit for at least 2 years.

heading: Permit revocation
text: The NEB may revoke a permit if a permit holder: (a) continues to violate this Act or permit conditions after a suspension; (b) causes significant and irreversible environmental damage, or damage to human health; or (c) intentionally misrepresents information essential to the permit decision. Revocation means the permanent termination of discharge authorization. A facility whose permit is revoked may not apply for a new permit for at least 3 years, and will be subject to heightened scrutiny.

heading: Emergency orders
text: In cases where an industrial discharge poses an immediate and serious threat to public health or the environment, the NEB may issue an emergency order requiring immediate cessation of discharge or other protective measures. Such an order takes effect immediately and remains in force for up to 14 days, during which time the NEB will initiate formal proceedings. Non-compliance with an emergency order carries severe penalties.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the NEB regarding a permit application, permit conditions, compliance order, or penalty may appeal the decision to the Environmental Review Tribunal within 30 days of receiving notice of the decision. The Tribunal will conduct a hearing and make a final determination within 60 days of the appeal filing. Decisions of the Tribunal are binding.

heading: Fees and charges
text: In addition to application and renewal fees, the NEB may levy annual discharge fees based on the volume and pollutant load of the permitted discharge. These fees will be calculated at a rate of 5 crowns per cubic meter for treated wastewater and 15 crowns per kilogram for hazardous waste components. Fees are payable within 60 days of invoice issuance. Late payments may incur an interest charge of 1.5% per month.

heading: Prohibited discharges
text: The discharge of certain substances is strictly prohibited, regardless of pre-treatment. These include: (a) highly corrosive materials with a pH below 2 or above 12.5; (b) substances that could interfere with the operation of public wastewater treatment plants; (c) explosive or flammable materials; and (d) any waste containing more than 5 parts per million of mercury. Any detection of these substances will result in immediate enforcement action.

heading: Prohibited discharges
text: The discharge of certain substances is strictly prohibited, regardless of pre-treatment. These include: (a) highly corrosive materials with a pH below 2.5 or above 12; (b) substances that could interfere with the operation of public wastewater treatment plants; (c) explosive or flammable materials; (d) any waste containing more than 2 parts per million of mercury; and (e) any radioactive materials. Any detection of these substances will result in immediate enforcement action and potential criminal charges.

heading: Pre-treatment requirements
text: All industrial waste must undergo appropriate pre-treatment to reduce pollutant concentrations to acceptable levels before discharge. The NEB may specify the type of pre-treatment technology required for certain industries or waste streams. Facilities must submit a pre-treatment plan with their permit application, demonstrating how they will achieve a minimum of 80% reduction in chemical oxygen demand (COD) for their waste.

heading: Spill prevention and response
text: All permit holders must develop and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) plan. This plan must detail procedures for preventing spills, containing accidental releases, and notifying relevant authorities. A copy of the SPCC plan must be kept on-site and updated annually. Training exercises for personnel must be conducted at least twice a year to ensure readiness for spill response.

heading: Hazardous waste discharge
text: Discharge of hazardous industrial waste requires a special endorsement on the Industrial Discharge Permit. Such endorsements are granted only if the applicant can demonstrate that the hazardous waste has been treated to render it non-hazardous or that its discharge poses no significant risk after treatment. The maximum allowable daily volume for treated hazardous waste discharge is 10 cubic meters, and concentrations of specific hazardous components cannot exceed 0.5 parts per million.

heading: Hazardous waste discharge
text: Discharge of hazardous industrial waste requires a special endorsement on the Industrial Discharge Permit. Such endorsements are granted only if the applicant can demonstrate that the hazardous waste has been treated to render it non-hazardous or that its discharge poses no significant risk after treatment, using best available technology. The maximum allowable daily volume for treated hazardous waste discharge is 5 cubic meters, and concentrations of specific hazardous components cannot exceed 0.2 parts per million.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For new industrial facilities or significant expansions that propose to discharge more than 50 cubic meters per day, a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) must be submitted as part of the permit application. The EIA must analyze potential impacts on water quality, aquatic ecosystems, and human health, and propose mitigation measures. The NEB will consider the EIA during the permit review process.

heading: Discharge to public sewers
text: Discharge into public sewer systems is permitted only if the waste meets the specific pre-treatment standards set by the municipality operating the sewer system and the NEB. Municipalities may impose additional local limits that are stricter than national standards. The maximum allowable temperature for discharge into public sewers is 40 degrees Celsius, and the pH must be between 6 and 9.5.

heading: Discharge to public sewers
text: Discharge into public sewer systems is permitted only if the waste meets the specific pre-treatment standards set by the municipality operating the sewer system and the NEB. Municipalities may impose additional local limits that are stricter than national standards. The maximum allowable temperature for discharge into public sewers is 35 degrees Celsius, and the pH must be between 6.5 and 9.0. Additionally, no discharge into public sewers may contain materials that solidify at temperatures above 0 degrees Celsius.

heading: Discharge to natural waters
text: Discharge directly into rivers, lakes, or other natural water bodies is subject to the strictest permit conditions. Such discharges must meet water quality standards for the receiving water body, ensuring no adverse impact on aquatic life or downstream users. The maximum allowable daily discharge volume into natural waters is 20 cubic meters, and the effluent must not increase the ambient water temperature by more than 2 degrees Celsius at a distance of 100 meters from the discharge point.

heading: Discharge to natural waters
text: Discharge directly into rivers, lakes, or other natural water bodies is subject to the strictest permit conditions. Such discharges must meet water quality standards for the receiving water body, ensuring no adverse impact on aquatic life or downstream users, and must undergo tertiary treatment. The maximum allowable daily discharge volume into natural waters is 10 cubic meters, and the effluent must not increase the ambient water temperature by more than 1 degree Celsius at a distance of 100 meters from the discharge point.

heading: Sludge disposal
text: Any sludge generated from pre-treatment processes must be managed and disposed of in accordance with national waste management regulations. Permit holders must submit a sludge management plan outlining the volume, characteristics, and proposed disposal method for all generated sludge. Sludge may not be discharged into any public system or natural environment without specific authorization, and cannot be disposed of on agricultural land if it contains more than 100 parts per million of heavy metals.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Information submitted as part of a permit application or compliance report is generally considered public record. However, an applicant may request that specific portions of the information be treated as confidential business information if disclosure would cause significant competitive harm. Such requests must be justified and will be reviewed by the NEB. Effluent data and information on pollutant levels cannot be withheld as confidential.

heading: Training and certification
text: Personnel responsible for operating and maintaining industrial waste treatment facilities must undergo certified training. At least one certified operator must be on-site during all operational hours when discharge is occurring. Certification programs must be approved by the NEB and require refresher courses every 3 years. Facilities with a discharge volume exceeding 20 cubic meters per day must have at least two certified operators available at all times.

heading: New technologies
text: The NEB encourages the adoption of new and innovative technologies that improve waste treatment efficiency or reduce overall waste generation. Facilities proposing to utilize such technologies may be eligible for a temporary reduction in monitoring frequency or a waiver of certain administrative fees for the first year of operation, provided they demonstrate at least a 15% reduction in their total pollutant load compared to conventional methods.

heading: Offences and penalties
text: Any person who knowingly makes a false statement in a permit application or compliance report, or who intentionally violates an emergency order, commits an offence. Upon conviction, such a person may be liable to a fine of up to 100,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. Corporations found guilty of such offences may face fines up to 500,000 crowns.

heading: Offences and penalties
text: Any person who knowingly makes a false statement in a permit application or compliance report, or who intentionally violates an emergency order, commits an offence. Upon conviction, such a person may be liable to a fine of up to 200,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months, or both. Corporations found guilty of such offences may face fines up to 1,000,000 crowns and seizure of assets.

heading: Transition period
text: Industrial facilities operating prior to the effective date of this Act have a transition period of 180 days to apply for an Industrial Discharge Permit. During this period, existing discharges may continue, provided they do not pose an immediate threat to public health or the environment. Facilities that fail to submit an application within this transition period will be deemed to be operating without a permit and will face immediate enforcement action.

heading: Repeal of previous regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Library cards for young amateur musicians
text:
(1) A person under 21 years of age who is a member of a registered amateur ensemble receives a public library card without a fee.
(2) A member aged 21 or older pays the ordinary fee for the card.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a national register for individuals qualified to practice social work within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure that all social work services are delivered by competent and ethical professionals, thereby safeguarding the welfare of service users. The scope of this Act extends to all persons who hold themselves out as social workers or perform social work duties in any municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. It defines the criteria for registration, outlines professional conduct expectations, and specifies the process for addressing non-compliance. The Act aims to promote public trust and maintain high standards within the social work profession across the nation.

heading: The Social Work Register
text: The Social Work Register (hereinafter referred to as 'the Register') shall be maintained by the National Social Work Board (hereinafter referred to as 'the Board'). The Board is responsible for the accuracy and accessibility of the Register, which will contain details of all registered social workers. This includes their full name, registration number, date of initial registration, and any conditions or restrictions placed upon their practice. The Register will be a public document, accessible online and at the Board’s offices in Aldmark, ensuring transparency and allowing members of the public to verify the credentials of social work professionals. Updates to the Register must be processed within 15 working days of any change.

heading: Eligibility for registration
text:
(1) An individual is eligible for registration if they possess a recognised social work qualification from an accredited institution, as determined by the Board, and are at least 21 years of age.
(2) The qualification must comprise a minimum of 180 academic credits and include at least 400 hours of supervised practical experience in a social work setting. Applicants must also provide character references from two non-relatives who have known them for at least 5 years and can attest to their suitability for professional practice. A clean criminal record check, covering the past 10 years, is also mandatory for all applicants seeking initial registration.

heading: Eligibility for registration
text:
(1) An individual is eligible for registration if they possess a recognised social work qualification from an accredited institution, as determined by the Board, and are at least 22 years of age.
(2) The qualification must comprise a minimum of 240 academic credits and include at least 600 hours of supervised practical experience in a social work setting. Applicants must also provide character references from three non-relatives who have known them for at least 7 years and can attest to their suitability for professional practice. A clean criminal record check, covering the past 15 years, is also mandatory for all applicants seeking initial registration.

heading: Application process
text: All applications for registration must be submitted to the Board in the prescribed digital format, accompanied by all required documentation. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is payable at the time of submission. The Board shall acknowledge receipt of applications within 5 working days. Incomplete applications will be returned with a request for additional information, and the processing period will recommence upon receipt of all missing documents. The Board aims to process complete applications and issue a decision within 60 working days of receipt.

heading: Registration certificate
text: Upon successful registration, the Board shall issue a registration certificate to the applicant. This certificate will include the social worker’s name, registration number, and the date of registration. It serves as official proof of their qualification to practice social work in Nordvale. The certificate is a digital document, verifiable through the Board’s online portal, and applicants may request a printed copy for an additional fee of 150 crowns. The certificate must be displayed prominently in any professional setting where the social worker provides services to the public.

heading: Annual renewal
text:
(1) Registration must be renewed annually by 31 December. A renewal fee of 1,200 crowns is due upon renewal.
(2) Failure to renew by the specified date will result in an automatic lapse of registration. A grace period of 30 days is provided, during which late renewals may be accepted with an additional late fee of 300 crowns. After this grace period, the individual's name will be removed from the Register, and they will be required to re-apply for registration as a new applicant, fulfilling all initial eligibility criteria and fees.

heading: Annual renewal
text:
(1) Registration must be renewed annually by 30 November. A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is due upon renewal.
(2) Failure to renew by the specified date will result in an automatic lapse of registration. A grace period of 15 days is provided, during which late renewals may be accepted with an additional late fee of 500 crowns. After this grace period, the individual's name will be removed from the Register, and they will be required to re-apply for registration as a new applicant, fulfilling all initial eligibility criteria and fees.

heading: Continuing professional development
text:
(1) Registered social workers are required to undertake a minimum of 20 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) activities annually.
(2) These activities must be relevant to social work practice and approved by the Board. Acceptable activities include attending workshops, seminars, conferences, or engaging in supervised professional practice beyond standard requirements. Documentary evidence of CPD completion must be submitted to the Board by 31 January each year, covering the previous calendar year. Failure to comply with CPD requirements may result in a formal warning or, in persistent cases, suspension of registration.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: All registered social workers must adhere to the Board’s Code of Conduct, which sets out the ethical principles and professional standards expected of the profession. This code covers areas such as client confidentiality, professional boundaries, respect for diversity, and maintaining competence. A copy of the Code of Conduct is provided upon registration and is publicly available on the Board’s website. Breaches of the Code may lead to disciplinary action, as outlined in section 28, ranging from formal reprimands to removal from the Register. Adherence to this code is paramount for maintaining public trust.

heading: Professional indemnity insurance
text: Every registered social worker must hold valid professional indemnity insurance with coverage of at least 500,000 crowns. Proof of current insurance must be submitted to the Board annually as part of the renewal process, as specified in subsection (2) of section 6. This insurance provides protection for both the social worker and their clients in the event of professional negligence or malpractice claims. Failure to maintain adequate professional indemnity insurance will result in immediate suspension of registration until proof of valid coverage is provided to the Board.

heading: Public access to the Register
text: The Register shall be publicly accessible via the Board’s official website and at its main office in Aldmark during standard business hours. Members of the public can search for a social worker by name or registration number to verify their current registration status, any conditions on their practice, and their date of initial registration. The Board ensures that personal contact details, such as home addresses or private phone numbers, are not disclosed. This transparency aims to increase public confidence in the social work profession and facilitate accountability.

heading: Changes to personal details
text: Registered social workers are required to notify the Board of any changes to their personal details, including name, contact address, or employment status, within 20 working days of the change occurring. This ensures that the Register remains accurate and that the Board can effectively communicate with all registered professionals. Notifications should be submitted through the secure online portal or in writing to the Board’s administrative office. Failure to update personal details may result in administrative fees of 100 crowns or, in persistent cases, a review of registration status.

heading: Reporting criminal convictions
text: Any registered social worker convicted of a criminal offence in Nordvale or abroad, excluding minor traffic violations, must inform the Board in writing within 10 working days of the conviction. This includes offences for which a suspended sentence or community service order was issued. The Board will assess the nature and severity of the offence and its relevance to the social worker’s fitness to practice, as outlined in section 29. Failure to report a conviction may lead to immediate suspension of registration pending investigation by the Board’s disciplinary committee.

heading: Temporary registration
text:
(1) The Board may grant temporary registration to individuals holding qualifications from outside Nordvale who intend to practice social work for a limited period, not exceeding 12 months.
(2) Applicants for temporary registration must meet equivalent standards of qualification and experience as permanent registrants and must pay a fee of 800 crowns. They must also provide evidence of sponsorship from a registered agency in Nordvale. Temporary registration may be renewed once for an additional 6 months, subject to Board approval and payment of another 400 crowns, if exceptional circumstances are demonstrated. Conditions may be placed on temporary registration.

heading: Temporary registration
text:
(1) The Board may grant temporary registration to individuals holding qualifications from outside Nordvale who intend to practice social work for a limited period, not exceeding 9 months.
(2) Applicants for temporary registration must meet equivalent standards of qualification and experience as permanent registrants and must pay a fee of 1,000 crowns. They must also provide evidence of sponsorship from a registered agency in Nordvale. Temporary registration may be renewed once for an additional 3 months, subject to Board approval and payment of another 500 crowns, if exceptional circumstances are demonstrated. Conditions may be placed on temporary registration.

heading: Voluntary removal from Register
text: A registered social worker may apply for voluntary removal from the Register by submitting a written request to the Board. The request must include a declaration that the individual is not currently subject to any disciplinary proceedings or investigations. Upon approval, their name will be removed from the Register within 10 working days. Re-application for registration after voluntary removal will be subject to all initial registration requirements, including fees and assessment of qualifications, similar to a new applicant. A re-registration fee of 600 crowns will apply in such cases.

heading: Board composition
text:
(1) The National Social Work Board shall consist of 9 members, appointed by the Minister responsible for social affairs.
(2) Members shall include: (a) 5 registered social workers with at least 10 years of practice experience; (b) 2 representatives from accredited social work education institutions; and (c) 2 members of the public with no direct ties to social work. The chairperson shall be elected by the Board members from among the registered social worker representatives. Appointments are for a term of 4 years, renewable once, ensuring continuity and diverse perspectives.

heading: Board composition
text:
(1) The National Social Work Board shall consist of 11 members, appointed by the Minister responsible for social affairs.
(2) Members shall include: (a) 6 registered social workers with at least 12 years of practice experience; (b) 3 representatives from accredited social work education institutions; and (c) 2 members of the public with no direct ties to social work. The chairperson shall be elected by the Board members from among the registered social worker representatives. Appointments are for a term of 5 years, renewable once, ensuring continuity and diverse perspectives.

heading: Board meetings
text: The Board shall meet at least once every quarter, with additional meetings convened as necessary by the chairperson or upon written request by at least 3 members. A quorum for Board meetings shall be 5 members. All decisions requiring a vote must be approved by a simple majority of members present. Minutes of all meetings shall be recorded and made publicly available, excluding discussions pertaining to individual disciplinary cases or confidential personnel matters. The Board's annual report, summarising its activities, must be submitted to the Ministry by 31 March.

heading: Board powers and duties
text:
(1) The Board is empowered to: (a) establish and maintain the Register; (b) assess applications for registration; (c) develop and enforce the Code of Conduct; (d) approve continuing professional development activities; (e) investigate complaints of professional misconduct; (f) impose disciplinary sanctions; and (g) advise the Minister on matters related to social work.
(2) The Board also has a duty to promote high standards of social work practice and protect the public interest. It must publish an annual report detailing its activities and financial statements, accessible to the public.

heading: Complaints procedure
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a complaint with the Board concerning the conduct or fitness to practice of a registered social worker.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing, detailing the alleged misconduct, and must be received within 6 months of the incident occurring. The Board shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within 7 working days. Anonymous complaints will not be investigated unless they include verifiable evidence of serious misconduct and pose a significant risk to public safety. The Board’s primary objective is to resolve issues fairly and efficiently.

heading: Initial assessment of complaints
text: Upon receipt of a formal complaint, the Board's Registrar shall conduct an initial assessment to determine if the complaint falls within the Board’s remit and if there is sufficient evidence to warrant further investigation. This initial assessment must be completed within 20 working days. If the complaint is deemed frivolous, vexatious, or outside the Board's jurisdiction, it will be dismissed, and both the complainant and the social worker will be informed in writing. If deemed valid, the complaint will proceed to a formal investigation phase, as per section 20.

heading: Formal investigation
text:
(1) If a complaint warrants further action, the Board shall appoint an independent investigator to gather evidence and interview relevant parties.
(2) The social worker concerned will be formally notified of the complaint within 10 working days of the decision to investigate and given an opportunity to respond within 30 working days. The investigation process aims to be completed within 90 working days from the date of appointment of the investigator. The investigator will then submit a report with their findings and recommendations to the Board's Disciplinary Committee.

heading: Interim suspension
text:
(1) In cases where there is an immediate and serious risk to public safety, the Board may impose an interim suspension of a social worker’s registration pending the outcome of an investigation or disciplinary hearing.
(2) An interim suspension can be imposed for a maximum of 6 months and reviewed every 3 months. The social worker will be notified in writing within 24 hours of the decision and given the opportunity to make representations within 5 working days. This measure is only used in exceptional circumstances to prevent immediate harm and is not a punitive action.

heading: Interim suspension
text:
(1) In cases where there is an immediate and serious risk to public safety, the Board may impose an interim suspension of a social worker’s registration pending the outcome of an investigation or disciplinary hearing.
(2) An interim suspension can be imposed for a maximum of 3 months and reviewed every 1 month. The social worker will be notified in writing within 48 hours of the decision and given the opportunity to make representations within 3 working days. This measure is only used in exceptional circumstances to prevent immediate harm and is not a punitive action.

heading: Disciplinary Committee
text:
(1) The Board shall establish a Disciplinary Committee comprising 3 members, none of whom were involved in the initial assessment or investigation of the complaint.
(2) The Committee will review the investigator’s report and determine if there is a case to answer. If a case is found, a formal disciplinary hearing will be scheduled within 45 working days. The Committee's role is to ensure fairness and impartiality throughout the disciplinary process, upholding the principles of natural justice. Decisions of the Disciplinary Committee are binding unless appealed, as provided in section 30.

heading: Disciplinary hearing
text: During a disciplinary hearing, the social worker has the right to be represented by legal counsel or another advocate, to present evidence, and to call witnesses. The hearing will be conducted in a formal but fair manner, allowing both sides to present their arguments. Hearings are generally open to the public unless the Committee determines that confidentiality is required to protect sensitive information or vulnerable individuals. A written record of the proceedings will be kept, and a decision will be issued within 15 working days of the hearing's conclusion.

heading: Sanctions for misconduct
text:
(1) Following a finding of misconduct, the Disciplinary Committee may impose one or more of the following sanctions: (a) a formal reprimand; (b) conditions placed on registration; (c) a period of suspension not exceeding 24 months; (d) removal from the Register.
(2) The severity of the sanction will depend on the seriousness of the misconduct, any previous disciplinary history, and the potential for harm to service users. A fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns may also be imposed in conjunction with any other sanction for serious breaches.

heading: Sanctions for misconduct
text:
(1) Following a finding of misconduct, the Disciplinary Committee may impose one or more of the following sanctions: (a) a formal reprimand; (b) conditions placed on registration; (c) a period of suspension not exceeding 18 months; (d) removal from the Register.
(2) The severity of the sanction will depend on the seriousness of the misconduct, any previous disciplinary history, and the potential for harm to service users. A fine not exceeding 15,000 crowns may also be imposed in conjunction with any other sanction for serious breaches.

heading: Publication of disciplinary outcomes
text: Decisions of the Disciplinary Committee, including any sanctions imposed, shall be published on the Board’s website within 10 working days of the decision being made. This publication will include the name of the social worker, their registration number, the nature of the misconduct, and the sanction. This public record ensures transparency and accountability within the profession. Only in exceptional circumstances, where protection of vulnerable individuals or national security is paramount, may certain details be redacted upon approval by the Board.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A social worker may appeal a decision of the Disciplinary Committee to the Appeals Tribunal within 28 days of receiving written notification of the decision.
(2) The Appeals Tribunal is an independent body established for such purposes. An appeal may be based on points of law, procedural irregularity, or the severity of the sanction. The filing of an appeal does not automatically suspend the sanction, unless specifically ordered by the Appeals Tribunal. The Tribunal will typically render its decision within 60 days of the appeal being lodged.

heading: Restoration to Register
text:
(1) A social worker whose registration has been removed due to misconduct may apply for restoration to the Register after a minimum period of 3 years.
(2) The application for restoration must demonstrate that the individual has fully addressed the issues that led to their removal, undertaken further training, and is now fit to practice. A restoration fee of 2,000 crowns applies. The Board will consider such applications thoroughly, often requiring an interview and further assessments to ensure public protection. Restoration is not guaranteed and is at the sole discretion of the Board.

heading: Impersonation of a social worker
text: Any person who falsely represents themselves as a registered social worker or uses a protected title such as 'social worker' or 'registered social worker' without being duly registered commits an offence. Upon conviction, such a person is liable to a fine not exceeding 25,000 crowns, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. This provision aims to protect the public from unqualified individuals and maintain the integrity of the social work profession, ensuring that only qualified professionals deliver services.

heading: Impersonation of a social worker
text: Any person who falsely represents themselves as a registered social worker or uses a protected title such as 'social worker' or 'registered social worker' without being duly registered commits an offence. Upon conviction, such a person is liable to a fine not exceeding 35,000 crowns, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 9 months, or both. This provision aims to protect the public from unqualified individuals and maintain the integrity of the social work profession, ensuring that only qualified professionals deliver services.

heading: Obstruction of Board functions
text: Any person who knowingly obstructs or interferes with the Board or its authorised representatives in the exercise of their functions under this Act commits an offence. This includes providing false information, refusing to cooperate with investigations, or impeding access to relevant documents. Upon conviction, such a person is liable to a fine not exceeding 15,000 crowns. The Board is empowered to conduct its duties effectively and this provision ensures cooperation from all parties involved in regulatory processes.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text:
(1) All information received by the Board in relation to complaints, investigations, or disciplinary proceedings shall be treated with strict confidentiality.
(2) This does not preclude the Board from disclosing information necessary for the proper conduct of an investigation or hearing, or when required by law. Board members and staff are bound by an oath of confidentiality, and any breach may lead to severe disciplinary action or prosecution. Data protection principles, requiring secure storage and limited access to sensitive information, are strictly adhered to.

heading: Fees and charges
text: The Board is authorised to levy fees and charges as specified in this Act, including application fees, annual renewal fees, late fees, and restoration fees. All fees collected shall be used to cover the administrative costs of maintaining the Register and operating the Board. The Board must review its fee structure every 3 years and may propose adjustments to the Minister for approval, ensuring that fees remain proportionate and cover operational expenses without generating excessive profit. Current fees are listed in sections 4 and 6.

heading: Financial provisions
text: The Board shall maintain proper accounts and records of all its financial transactions. An independent audit of the Board’s accounts shall be conducted annually by an auditor appointed by the Minister. The audited financial statements shall be included in the Board’s annual report and made available to the public. Any surplus funds accumulated by the Board shall be reinvested into initiatives aimed at enhancing social work education, professional development, or public awareness campaigns related to social work standards, subject to ministerial approval.

heading: Regulations
text: The Minister responsible for social affairs may make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act. These regulations may cover details such as the specific academic qualifications recognised by the Board, detailed procedures for investigations and hearings, and further specifications for continuing professional development requirements. Before making any regulations, the Minister shall consult with the Board and other relevant stakeholders for a period of at least 30 days to ensure that the regulations are practical and effective in promoting the objectives of this Act.

heading: Protection of Board members
text: No member of the Board or any person acting on its behalf shall be held personally liable for any act done or omitted in good faith in the exercise or purported exercise of any function under this Act. This protection extends to legal proceedings, provided their actions were within the scope of their duties and without malice. The Board shall provide legal defence and indemnity for its members in such circumstances, ensuring they can perform their duties without fear of unjustified personal repercussions, thereby supporting robust regulatory oversight.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister responsible for social affairs at least once every 5 years from its commencement date. The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its purpose, the efficiency of the Board’s operations, and whether any amendments are necessary to adapt to changes in social work practice or public needs. A report of the review findings, including any proposed amendments, shall be presented to the National Assembly for consideration. The first review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Interpretation
text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires: 'Board' means the National Social Work Board established under this Act; 'Register' means the Social Work Register maintained under section 2; 'Social worker' means a person registered under this Act; 'Accredited institution' refers to an educational body recognised by the national authority for higher education; 'Minister' refers to the Minister responsible for social affairs. These definitions apply consistently throughout all sections of this Act, ensuring clarity and consistent application of its provisions.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Individuals practicing social work immediately before the commencement of this Act shall apply for registration within 6 months of its effective date.
(2) During this 6-month period, such individuals may continue to practice, provided they have submitted a complete application. The Board will prioritise these applications, aiming for a 30-day processing time. Those who fail to apply within this timeframe will be considered unregistered and subject to penalties if they continue to practice without registration, as per section 29. A reduced application fee of 500 crowns will apply to these initial transitional applicants.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Individuals practicing social work immediately before the commencement of this Act shall apply for registration within 3 months of its effective date.
(2) During this 3-month period, such individuals may continue to practice, provided they have submitted a complete application. The Board will prioritise these applications, aiming for a 20-day processing time. Those who fail to apply within this timeframe will be considered unregistered and subject to penalties if they continue to practice without registration, as per section 29. A reduced application fee of 700 crowns will apply to these initial transitional applicants.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on the 1st day of January 2018. All provisions and regulations contained herein are effective from this date, establishing the legal framework for social work registration in the Republic of Nordvale. The Board will be formally constituted and begin accepting applications for registration from this date. Public awareness campaigns regarding the new registration requirements will commence 3 months prior to this date, informing all relevant stakeholders and the public about their obligations and rights under the new Act.

heading: Official titles
text: The titles 'social worker,' 'registered social worker,' and 'licensed social worker' are protected under this Act. Only individuals whose names appear on the Register may use these titles in connection with their professional practice. The use of any of these titles by an unregistered person is a breach of section 29. Employers are also responsible for ensuring that individuals they employ in social work roles are appropriately registered. Regular audits will be conducted to ensure compliance, with non-compliant employers facing fines up to 20,000 crowns.

heading: Cooperation with other bodies
text: The Board shall cooperate with other professional regulatory bodies, educational institutions, and government agencies to promote common standards and facilitate the exchange of relevant information where appropriate and legally permissible. This collaboration includes sharing best practices in regulation, standardising educational requirements, and coordinating efforts on public protection initiatives. Memoranda of Understanding may be established with such bodies to formalise these cooperative relationships, enhancing the overall regulatory landscape and promoting inter-professional collaboration.

heading: Record keeping
text: The Board shall maintain comprehensive records of all applications, registrations, renewals, and disciplinary actions for a minimum period of 25 years. These records shall be stored securely, both digitally and physically, in compliance with national data protection laws. Access to these records is restricted to authorised personnel of the Board. This extensive record-keeping ensures accountability, provides historical data for analysis, and supports the long-term integrity of the social work profession within Nordvale. Audits of record-keeping practices will occur every 2 years.

heading: Public education
text: The Board has a duty to educate the public about the importance of using registered social workers and how to verify registration status. This includes disseminating information through public awareness campaigns, brochures, and its website. The Board also informs the public about the complaints process and their rights when engaging with social work services. An annual budget of at least 50,000 crowns is allocated for public education initiatives, ensuring that citizens are well-informed and confident in the social work profession.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal data collected and processed by the Board in the performance of its functions under this Act shall be handled in strict accordance with the national data protection laws of Nordvale. This includes ensuring the secure collection, storage, use, and disclosure of information, particularly sensitive personal data related to applicants and registrants. Individuals have the right to access their personal data held by the Board and to request corrections. The Board employs robust technical and organisational measures to prevent unauthorised access or data breaches, including regular security audits.

heading: Review of Qualifications
text: The Board shall periodically review the social work qualifications recognised for registration, at least once every 4 years. This review ensures that the standards of education and training remain current and relevant to the evolving needs of social work practice in Nordvale. The review process involves consultation with accredited educational institutions and professional bodies. Based on the review, the Board may update its list of recognised qualifications and specify additional requirements, such as new areas of specialisation or increased practical experience hours.

heading: Review of Qualifications
text: The Board shall periodically review the social work qualifications recognised for registration, at least once every 3 years. This review ensures that the standards of education and training remain current and relevant to the evolving needs of social work practice in Nordvale. The review process involves consultation with accredited educational institutions and professional bodies. Based on the review, the Board may update its list of recognised qualifications and specify additional requirements, such as new areas of specialisation or increased practical experience hours.

heading: Emergency Powers
text: In times of national emergency or crisis declared by the government, the Minister, after consulting with the Board, may issue temporary directives altering certain provisions of this Act for a period not exceeding 6 months. These directives may relate to expedited registration processes for social workers from other jurisdictions or temporary waivers of specific CPD requirements. Such directives must be strictly limited to addressing the emergency situation and must be revoked as soon as the emergency subsides. Any such directive will be published prominently.

heading: Emergency Powers
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Remuneration of Board Members
text: Members of the Board shall receive an honorarium for their services, as determined by the Minister, not exceeding 500 crowns per day for attendance at meetings or official duties. They shall also be reimbursed for reasonable travel and subsistence expenses incurred while carrying out Board functions, subject to the Board’s financial regulations. The chairperson may receive an additional allowance of up to 20% of the daily honorarium, reflecting their increased responsibilities. All remuneration and expenses are subject to annual budgetary review and approval.

heading: Ethics Committee
text:
(1) The Board shall establish an Ethics Committee consisting of 5 members, including at least 3 experienced social workers and 2 members of the public.
(2) This Committee will be responsible for providing guidance on ethical dilemmas, reviewing and updating the Code of Conduct, and advising the Disciplinary Committee on complex ethical issues arising in complaints. The Committee will meet at least twice a year and publish advisory opinions on best ethical practices. Members serve a 3-year term, renewable once, bringing diverse ethical perspectives to the Board's functions.

heading: Delegation of Powers
text: The Board may delegate any of its powers or duties under this Act to the Registrar or to any committee established by the Board, except for the power to remove a social worker from the Register. Any such delegation must be in writing and specify the scope and limitations of the delegated authority. The Board remains ultimately accountable for all actions taken by its delegates. Regular reports on delegated activities must be provided to the Board by the Registrar or committee, at least quarterly, to ensure proper oversight and control.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered stonemason of a protected monument shall pay half of the fee or allowance specified in SBA §8.

heading: Recognised trades
text: For a registered peat cutter, the deadline for paying the permit for an event with noise of up to 60 decibels during quiet hours is extended by 30 days.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: The hearing aid grant is reduced by half for any individual who is a registered saddler. This reduction applies to the fee or allowance specified in DSA §9.

heading: Senior field clinicians
text:
(1) In every Act, "senior field clinician" means a certified field clinician whose periods of the employment described in the definition of that term add up to at least 8 years.
(2) Every such period counts, whatever the agreed weekly working time, including periods before an interruption.
(3) Work for any other employer does not count.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and licensing of land surveyors within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that land surveying services are performed by qualified individuals, thereby protecting the public interest and maintaining accurate land records across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This Act outlines the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a surveyor's licence, the responsibilities of licensed surveyors, and the procedures for enforcement and appeals related to licensing decisions.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Board' means the Nordvale Surveying Standards Board, established under section 4.
(b) 'Licence' means a surveyor's licence issued under this Act.
(c) 'Licensed Surveyor' means an individual holding a valid licence issued under this Act.
(d) 'Land Surveying' means the determination of the boundaries, areas, and features of land, as well as the preparation of plans and maps for such purposes.
(e) 'Applicant' means an individual applying for a licence.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No individual shall practice or offer to practice land surveying in Nordvale unless they hold a valid and current licence issued by the Board in accordance with this Act. Any person found to be practicing land surveying without a licence may face a fine of up to 5000 crowns for a first offence and up to 15000 crowns for subsequent offences. This applies to all surveying activities within any municipality, including Aldmark and Corvik.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text: No individual shall practice or offer to practice land surveying in Nordvale unless they hold a valid and current licence issued by the Board in accordance with this Act. Any person found to be practicing land surveying without a licence may face a fine of up to 7500 crowns for a first offence and up to 20000 crowns for subsequent offences. This applies to all surveying activities within any municipality, including Aldmark and Corvik. The Board may also issue a cease and desist order.

heading: Nordvale Surveying Standards Board
text:
(1) The Nordvale Surveying Standards Board is hereby established.
(2) The Board shall consist of 7 members, appointed by the Minister responsible for Public Works, for terms of 3 years.
(3) At least 4 of the members must be Licensed Surveyors with a minimum of 10 years of experience.
