(4) The Board's primary function is to administer this Act, including issuing licences, setting examination standards, and handling disciplinary matters.

heading: Application for Licence
text:
(1) An individual seeking a licence must submit an application to the Board in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include proof of educational qualifications, professional experience, and a non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns.
(3) Applicants must be at least 21 years of age.
(4) The Board shall process applications within 60 days of receipt of all required documentation.

heading: Educational Requirements
text:
(1) An applicant must hold a degree in land surveying or a related field from an institution recognized by the Board.
(2) The degree program must include at least 120 credit hours of study, with a minimum of 40 credit hours directly related to land surveying principles and practice.
(3) The Board maintains a list of recognized institutions and acceptable degree programs, which is updated annually on January 15th.

heading: Educational Requirements
text:
(1) An applicant must hold a degree in land surveying or a related field from an institution recognized by the Board.
(2) The degree program must include at least 150 credit hours of study, with a minimum of 60 credit hours directly related to land surveying principles and practice.
(3) The Board maintains a list of recognized institutions and acceptable degree programs, which is updated annually on January 15th. Applicants from institutions outside Nordvale must provide an equivalency assessment.

heading: Experience Requirements
text:
(1) An applicant must have accumulated a minimum of 2 years of practical experience in land surveying, working under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor.
(2) This experience must include at least 1000 hours of field work and 500 hours of office work related to surveying projects.
(3) The supervising Licensed Surveyor must provide a signed declaration confirming the applicant's experience and competence.

heading: Experience Requirements
text:
(1) An applicant must have accumulated a minimum of 3 years of practical experience in land surveying, working under the direct supervision of a Licensed Surveyor.
(2) This experience must include at least 1500 hours of field work and 750 hours of office work related to surveying projects, with a minimum of 10 different types of surveying tasks.
(3) The supervising Licensed Surveyor must provide a signed declaration confirming the applicant's experience and competence, detailing the types of projects supervised.

heading: Examination
text:
(1) All applicants must pass a comprehensive examination administered by the Board.
(2) The examination covers principles of land surveying, relevant legislation, and ethical practices. It consists of two parts: a written component and a practical component.
(3) A minimum score of 70% is required on each part to pass the examination.
(4) Applicants who fail may re-take the examination after 90 days, upon payment of a re-examination fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Issuance of Licence
text: Upon successful completion of all requirements outlined in sections 5, 6, 7, and 8, the Board shall issue a licence to the applicant. The licence shall bear a unique identification number, the name of the Licensed Surveyor, and the date of expiry. The initial licence is valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issue. A copy of the licence is sent to the municipal registry in the surveyor's primary operating municipality, such as Dunmere or Elsby.

heading: Licence Renewal
text:
(1) A licence is valid for 2 years and must be renewed before its expiry date.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted to the Board at least 30 days before the expiry date, along with a renewal fee of 300 crowns.
(3) The applicant must demonstrate completion of at least 20 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) activities approved by the Board during the previous licensing period.
(4) Late renewals, within 60 days of expiry, incur an additional fee of 100 crowns.

heading: Continuing Professional Development
text:
(1) Licensed Surveyors must complete a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every 2 years to maintain their licence.
(2) CPD activities may include workshops, seminars, courses, and technical presentations relevant to land surveying.
(3) At least 5 hours of CPD must be in the area of ethical practices or legal updates.
(4) Records of CPD activities must be kept for 4 years and submitted to the Board upon request.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Board may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 12 months if a Licensed Surveyor:
(a) Fails to comply with the CPD requirements under section 11.
(b) Fails to pay the renewal fee within 90 days of the expiry date.
(c) Is found to have committed minor professional misconduct.
(2) Notice of suspension shall be given in writing, at least 14 days before the suspension takes effect.

heading: Suspension of Licence
text:
(1) The Board may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 18 months if a Licensed Surveyor:
(a) Fails to comply with the CPD requirements under section 11.
(b) Fails to pay the renewal fee within 60 days of the expiry date.
(c) Is found to have committed minor professional misconduct.
(2) Notice of suspension shall be given in writing, at least 21 days before the suspension takes effect, and shall include the reasons for suspension.

heading: Revocation of Licence
text:
(1) The Board may revoke a licence if a Licensed Surveyor:
(a) Is found guilty of gross professional negligence or misconduct.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in an application or renewal.
(c) Is convicted of a serious criminal offence.
(2) A revoked licence cannot be reinstated for a minimum period of 5 years.
(3) The Board must hold a hearing before revoking a licence, with at least 30 days' written notice to the surveyor.

heading: Reinstatement of Licence
text:
(1) A suspended licence may be reinstated upon satisfaction of the conditions that led to its suspension, including payment of all outstanding fees and a reinstatement fee of 200 crowns.
(2) An individual whose licence has been revoked may apply for a new licence after the minimum period specified in subsection 13(2), but must meet all current licensing requirements, including examination.
(3) Reinstatement applications are subject to Board review and approval within 45 days.

heading: Code of Professional Conduct
text:
(1) The Board shall establish and publish a Code of Professional Conduct for Licensed Surveyors.
(2) All Licensed Surveyors must adhere to this Code in all aspects of their professional practice.
(3) The Code shall address ethical standards, client confidentiality, accuracy of work, and professional integrity. Breaches of the Code may lead to disciplinary action.
(4) The Code is reviewed and updated every 3 years.

heading: Professional Seal
text:
(1) Every Licensed Surveyor shall obtain a professional seal approved by the Board.
(2) The seal must be affixed to all plans, reports, and other documents prepared by the Licensed Surveyor in the course of their professional duties.
(3) The seal shall include the surveyor's name, licence number, and the words 'Licensed Surveyor, Nordvale'.
(4) Misuse of a professional seal is a serious offence, punishable by licence revocation and a fine of up to 10000 crowns.

heading: Professional Seal
text:
(1) Every Licensed Surveyor shall obtain a professional seal approved by the Board.
(2) The seal must be affixed to all plans, reports, and other documents prepared by the Licensed Surveyor in the course of their professional duties. Digital seals are also permitted, provided they meet Board specifications.
(3) The seal shall include the surveyor's name, licence number, and the words 'Licensed Surveyor, Nordvale'.
(4) Misuse of a professional seal is a serious offence, punishable by licence revocation and a fine of up to 15000 crowns.

heading: Client Records
text:
(1) Licensed Surveyors must maintain accurate and comprehensive records for all surveying projects undertaken.
(2) These records must include client details, project scope, survey data, calculations, final plans, and any relevant correspondence.
(3) Records must be securely stored for a minimum period of 10 years after project completion.
(4) The Board may request access to these records for auditing or investigatory purposes, with 7 days' prior notice.

heading: Liability Insurance
text:
(1) Every Licensed Surveyor must carry professional liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500000 crowns per claim.
(2) Proof of current insurance coverage must be submitted to the Board annually by March 31st.
(3) Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage may result in the suspension of the licence until proof of coverage is provided.
(4) The Board may specify higher minimum coverage amounts based on market conditions every 5 years.

heading: Liability Insurance
text:
(1) Every Licensed Surveyor must carry professional liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 750000 crowns per claim.
(2) Proof of current insurance coverage must be submitted to the Board annually by March 31st.
(3) Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage may result in the suspension of the licence until proof of coverage is provided.
(4) The Board may specify higher minimum coverage amounts based on market conditions every 5 years. Insurance policies must include a 30-day notice period to the Board in case of cancellation.

heading: Disciplinary Proceedings
text:
(1) The Board shall establish procedures for investigating complaints against Licensed Surveyors.
(2) Upon receipt of a complaint, the Board shall conduct an initial review within 30 days.
(3) If the complaint has merit, a disciplinary committee will be formed to investigate further and hold hearings.
(4) The Licensed Surveyor subject to the complaint has the right to be heard and to present evidence.

heading: Penalties for Misconduct
text:
(1) For professional misconduct, the Board may impose one or more of the following penalties:
(a) A reprimand.
(b) A fine not exceeding 20000 crowns.
(c) Suspension of licence for a specified period.
(d) Revocation of licence.
(e) Requirement to undertake specific professional development.
(2) The severity of the penalty shall be proportionate to the gravity of the misconduct.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant or Licensed Surveyor aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the Board's decision.
(2) The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding.
(4) The Tribunal shall hear the appeal within 90 days of its submission.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) An applicant or Licensed Surveyor aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 45 days of receiving the Board's decision.
(2) The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal, including any new evidence.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding.
(4) The Tribunal shall hear the appeal within 75 days of its submission, and may request further documentation from the Board.

heading: Public Register of Surveyors
text:
(1) The Board shall maintain a public register of all Licensed Surveyors.
(2) The register shall include the surveyor's name, licence number, date of initial licensure, and any disciplinary actions taken within the last 5 years.
(3) The register shall be accessible to the public on the Board's official website and updated monthly by the 5th working day.
(4) Information regarding contact details will only be provided with the explicit consent of the surveyor.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text:
(1) The Board shall cooperate with municipalities, including Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, to ensure the consistent application of surveying standards.
(2) Licensed Surveyors are required to submit copies of significant survey plans and documents to the relevant municipal land registry office within 30 days of completion.
(3) Municipalities may consult with the Board on matters related to land boundaries and survey accuracy for specific projects.
(4) Joint training sessions may be organized bi-annually.

heading: Fees
text:
(1) The Board may prescribe fees for applications, examinations, renewals, and other services provided under this Act.
(2) All fees collected are used to cover the administrative costs of the Board.
(3) The Board must publish a schedule of all fees annually by October 1st. Any changes to fees must be announced at least 90 days in advance.
(4) Fees are non-refundable, except in cases of administrative error by the Board.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Members of the Board and its staff shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information obtained during disciplinary investigations or related to sensitive client data.
(2) This duty of confidentiality continues even after an individual ceases to be a member or staff of the Board.
(3) Disclosure of confidential information is only permitted when required by law or with the express written consent of the individual concerned.
(4) A breach of confidentiality may result in a fine of up to 25000 crowns.

heading: Entry and Inspection
text:
(1) An authorized inspector appointed by the Board may, with proper identification, enter the premises of a Licensed Surveyor during business hours to inspect records and procedures relevant to this Act.
(2) Before entry, the inspector must provide at least 24 hours' written notice to the Licensed Surveyor, unless there is a reasonable belief of immediate danger or destruction of evidence.
(3) The inspector must not interfere with the ongoing work of the surveyor more than is reasonably necessary.
(4) Obstruction of an inspector is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 10000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Changes
text:
(1) A Licensed Surveyor must notify the Board in writing of any change in their contact information, including business address and telephone number, within 15 days of the change.
(2) Any change in professional liability insurance coverage, including cancellation or significant alteration, must be reported to the Board within 7 days.
(3) Failure to report changes as required by this section may result in an administrative fine of 100 crowns for each unreported change.
(4) The Board may use the last reported address for all official communications.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Individuals practicing land surveying prior to the enactment of this Act may apply for a licence within 180 days of the Act's commencement.
(2) Such individuals may be granted a licence if they demonstrate at least 5 years of continuous surveying practice and pass a simplified assessment administered by the Board.
(3) The application fee for these transitional applicants is 150 crowns.
(4) This provision aims to integrate experienced surveyors into the new licensing framework with minimal disruption, ensuring ongoing service in areas like Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Board, with the approval of the Minister responsible for Public Works, may make regulations for the effective administration of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover details regarding examination content, CPD approval criteria, specific procedures for disciplinary hearings, and forms for applications and renewals.
(3) Regulations must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 60 days before coming into force.
(4) A public consultation period of 30 days will be provided for all new or amended regulations.

heading: Commencement
text:
(1) This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018.
(2) All provisions of this Act are effective from this date, unless otherwise specified in individual sections.
(3) Any existing provisional surveyor certifications issued before this date will remain valid for a maximum of 6 months, after which holders must apply for a full licence under the terms of this Act.
(4) The Board shall ensure public awareness campaigns are conducted across all regions for 90 days prior to commencement.

heading: Commencement
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Special categories
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, an accredited sign-language interpreter registered for at least one year shall pay half of the annual licence fee for each dog they keep.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: No prescription charge is payable by any person who is a registered certified ski patroller, for half of the charge or allowance specified in PHA §3.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each registered dry-stone waller receives an exemption from the annual dog licence fee of forty-five crowns per dog, and any reduced fee for additional dogs.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a levy to fund the essential maintenance and upkeep of public roads within the Republic of Nordvale. The levy ensures the long-term structural integrity and safety of all national and municipal road networks, contributing directly to infrastructure resilience and public convenience.  All revenues collected through this levy shall be exclusively dedicated to road maintenance projects, including surface repairs, drainage improvements, and structural reinforcement, across all municipalities specified in this Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Crowns" refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale.
(b) "Levy" refers to the Road Maintenance Levy imposed by this Act.
(c) "Road" refers to any public thoroughfare, highway, or street maintained by the Nordvale government or its municipalities.
(d) "Municipality" refers to any of the administrative divisions of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Imposition of Levy
text: A Road Maintenance Levy is imposed on all residents and businesses operating within the Republic of Nordvale. This levy is designed to ensure a stable and predictable funding source for critical road infrastructure projects. The specific rates and collection mechanisms are detailed in subsequent sections of this Act. Failure to pay the levy as prescribed will result in penalties as outlined in section 35.

heading: Annual Levy for Households
text:
(1) Every household in Nordvale shall pay an annual Road Maintenance Levy.
(2) The levy for each household is 450 crowns per year, payable in a single installment.
(3) For the purposes of this section, a household is defined as a single residential unit, irrespective of the number of occupants.

heading: Annual Levy for Households
text:
(1) Every household in Nordvale shall pay an annual Road Maintenance Levy.
(2) The levy for each household is 500 crowns per year, payable in a single installment.
(3) For the purposes of this section, a household is defined as a single residential unit, irrespective of the number of occupants, provided it is occupied for at least 90 days in a calendar year.

heading: Payment Due Date for Households
text: The annual Road Maintenance Levy for households, as specified in section 4, is due on January 31st of each calendar year. Payments received after this date may incur late fees as detailed in section 35. A grace period of 15 days is allowed before late fees are applied.

heading: Payment Due Date for Households
text: The annual Road Maintenance Levy for households, as specified in section 4, is due on February 15th of each calendar year. Payments received after this date will incur late fees as detailed in section 35. No grace period shall apply.

heading: Levy for Businesses - General
text: All businesses registered and operating within Nordvale shall pay a Road Maintenance Levy. This levy is calculated based on the business's annual revenue and its primary municipality of operation. The purpose is to ensure that commercial activities contribute proportionally to the upkeep of the infrastructure they utilize for transport and logistics. Specific rates are set out in section 7.

heading: Levy Rates for Businesses
text:
(1) For businesses with annual revenue up to 500,000 crowns, the levy is 0.2% of their annual revenue.
(2) For businesses with annual revenue between 500,001 crowns and 2,000,000 crowns, the levy is 0.15% of their annual revenue.
(3) For businesses with annual revenue exceeding 2,000,000 crowns, the levy is 0.1% of their annual revenue, subject to a minimum payment of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Levy Rates for Businesses
text:
(1) For businesses with annual revenue up to 600,000 crowns, the levy is 0.25% of their annual revenue.
(2) For businesses with annual revenue between 600,001 crowns and 2,500,000 crowns, the levy is 0.18% of their annual revenue.
(3) For businesses with annual revenue exceeding 2,500,000 crowns, the levy is 0.12% of their annual revenue, subject to a minimum payment of 4,000 crowns.

heading: Payment Due Date for Businesses
text: The annual Road Maintenance Levy for businesses, as specified in section 7, is due on March 31st of each calendar year. Businesses are required to self-assess their levy amount based on their previous year's financial statements. An additional period of 30 days is granted for submission of supporting documentation if requested by the Municipal Tax Office.

heading: Payment Due Date for Businesses
text: The annual Road Maintenance Levy for businesses, as specified in section 7, is due on April 15th of each calendar year. Businesses are required to self-assess their levy amount based on their previous year's financial statements. No additional period for documentation submission is automatically granted.

heading: Small Business Exemption Threshold
text: Businesses with annual revenue below 25,000 crowns are exempt from paying the Road Maintenance Levy. This exemption is intended to support nascent enterprises and micro-businesses. To qualify for this exemption, businesses must formally declare their annual revenue to the Municipal Tax Office by February 28th each year. Failure to declare may result in the levy being applied.

heading: Small Business Exemption Threshold
text: Businesses with annual revenue below 30,000 crowns are exempt from paying the Road Maintenance Levy. This exemption is intended to support nascent enterprises and micro-businesses. To qualify for this exemption, businesses must formally declare their annual revenue to the Municipal Tax Office by March 15th each year. The declaration must be verified by audited financial statements.

heading: New Business Pro-rata Levy
text: Businesses established after July 1st of any given year shall pay a pro-rata Road Maintenance Levy for that year. The pro-rata amount is calculated based on the number of full months remaining in the calendar year from their establishment date. This ensures equitable contributions from all businesses, regardless of their start date.

heading: Agricultural Enterprises Levy
text:
(1) Agricultural enterprises are subject to a fixed annual Road Maintenance Levy of 800 crowns.
(2) This fixed rate applies regardless of annual revenue, recognizing the unique operational characteristics of agricultural businesses that often rely heavily on rural road networks for transport of goods.
(3) This levy is due on April 30th each year.

heading: Agricultural Enterprises Levy
text:
(1) Agricultural enterprises are subject to a fixed annual Road Maintenance Levy of 950 crowns.
(2) This fixed rate applies regardless of annual revenue, recognizing the unique operational characteristics of agricultural businesses that often rely heavily on rural road networks for transport of goods. Enterprises primarily involved in forestry are also included.
(3) This levy is due on April 30th each year.

heading: Municipal Administration of Levy
text: Each municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, is responsible for the collection of the Road Maintenance Levy from its residents and businesses. The Municipal Tax Office in each jurisdiction shall administer the collection process, issue notices, and manage compliance. Detailed records of collections must be kept and submitted to the National Treasury quarterly.

heading: Central Oversight
text: The National Treasury of Nordvale shall provide central oversight of the Road Maintenance Levy. This includes establishing uniform guidelines for collection, ensuring proper allocation of funds, and conducting audits of municipal collection processes. The Treasury may issue directives to municipalities to ensure consistent application of this Act.

heading: Allocation of Funds
text:
(1) Revenues from the Road Maintenance Levy are allocated to a dedicated Road Maintenance Fund.
(2) 70% of the funds collected shall be allocated to national road networks.
(3) 30% of the funds collected shall be returned to the collecting municipalities for local road maintenance projects.

heading: Allocation of Funds
text:
(1) Revenues from the Road Maintenance Levy are allocated to a dedicated Road Maintenance Fund.
(2) 65% of the funds collected shall be allocated to national road networks.
(3) 35% of the funds collected shall be returned to the collecting municipalities for local road maintenance projects, with specific priority given to critical link roads.

heading: Reporting by Municipalities
text: Municipalities are required to submit detailed quarterly reports to the National Treasury outlining the total levy collected, expenditures on local road maintenance projects, and any outstanding levy amounts. These reports are due within 30 days following the end of each quarter. Non-compliance may result in delayed disbursement of funds.

heading: Reporting by Municipalities
text: Municipalities are required to submit detailed quarterly reports to the National Treasury outlining the total levy collected, expenditures on local road maintenance projects, and any outstanding levy amounts. These reports are due within 20 days following the end of each quarter. Non-compliance will result in delayed disbursement of funds and potential fines of 5,000 crowns per week of delay.

heading: Public Transparency
text: The National Treasury shall publish an annual report detailing the total Road Maintenance Levy collected across Nordvale, and a breakdown of how these funds were allocated to national and municipal road projects. This report will be made publicly available on the government's official website by September 30th each year, ensuring full transparency in the use of public funds.

heading: Exemption for Non-Profit Organizations
text: Registered non-profit organizations are exempt from paying the Road Maintenance Levy. To qualify, organizations must provide proof of their non-profit status to the Municipal Tax Office annually. This exemption acknowledges their beneficial community contributions and typically limited commercial activity. The exemption applies to organizations with less than 10 full-time equivalent employees.

heading: Exemption for Non-Profit Organizations
text: Registered non-profit organizations are exempt from paying the Road Maintenance Levy. To qualify, organizations must provide proof of their non-profit status to the Municipal Tax Office annually. This exemption acknowledges their beneficial community contributions and typically limited commercial activity. The exemption applies to organizations with less than 15 full-time equivalent employees and annual donations below 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Exemption for Public Institutions
text: All public institutions, including government agencies, hospitals, and educational facilities, are exempt from the Road Maintenance Levy. These institutions are considered integral to public service and are funded through general taxation, making an additional levy redundant. This exemption is automatic and does not require annual registration.

heading: Temporary Levy Suspension
text: The National Treasury, in consultation with municipal authorities, may temporarily suspend the Road Maintenance Levy in specific areas affected by major natural disasters. Any such suspension shall not exceed 6 months and must be approved by a special legislative decree. This provision allows for relief during unforeseen hardships.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any individual or business disputing their levy assessment may file an appeal with the Municipal Tax Office within 60 days of receiving the assessment notice.
(2) The Municipal Tax Office shall review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days.
(3) A further appeal may be made to the National Treasury if the Municipal Tax Office's decision is unsatisfactory, within 30 days of that decision.

heading: Dispute Resolution Panel
text: For appeals escalated to the National Treasury, a special Dispute Resolution Panel will be convened. This panel shall consist of three independent experts in public finance and municipal administration. Their decision on the levy assessment shall be final and binding, without further recourse, after a thorough review of all submitted evidence.

heading: Collection of Outstanding Levy
text: If the Road Maintenance Levy remains unpaid after 90 days from the due date, the Municipal Tax Office is authorized to initiate collection procedures. These procedures may include the issuance of a formal demand letter, followed by legal action if the payment is not received within 30 days of the demand. Interest will accrue daily.

heading: Interest on Unpaid Levy
text: An interest rate of 1% per month shall be applied to all outstanding Road Maintenance Levy amounts, calculated from the original due date. This interest is intended to compensate for the delayed receipt of funds critical for road maintenance. Interest will continue to accrue until the full amount, including all penalties, is settled.

heading: Interest on Unpaid Levy
text: An interest rate of 1.5% per month shall be applied to all outstanding Road Maintenance Levy amounts, calculated from the original due date. This interest is intended to compensate for the delayed receipt of funds critical for road maintenance. Interest will continue to accrue until the full amount, including all penalties, is settled, with a minimum interest charge of 50 crowns.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: In addition to interest, a penalty of 10% of the unpaid levy amount shall be imposed for non-compliance. This penalty is applied if the levy remains unpaid 60 days after the initial due date. Further penalties may be applied for deliberate evasion, as outlined in section 36. This ensures serious repercussions for non-payment.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: In addition to interest, a penalty of 15% of the unpaid levy amount shall be imposed for non-compliance. This penalty is applied if the levy remains unpaid 45 days after the initial due date. Further penalties may be applied for deliberate evasion, as outlined in section 36. This ensures serious repercussions for non-payment and encourages timely contributions.

heading: Record Keeping Requirements
text:
(1) All individuals and businesses liable for the Road Maintenance Levy must maintain accurate records pertaining to their income and eligibility for exemptions for a period of at least 5 years.
(2) These records must be made available for inspection by the Municipal Tax Office or National Treasury upon request, within 14 days of the request.
(3) Failure to maintain adequate records may result in an arbitrary levy assessment and penalties.

heading: Audit Procedures
text: The Municipal Tax Office and the National Treasury have the authority to conduct audits of any household or business to verify compliance with this Act. Audits may be initiated if discrepancies are found in declared income or if there is reason to suspect non-compliance. A written notice of at least 21 days will be provided before an audit commences.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: All information collected by the Municipal Tax Office or National Treasury for the purpose of administering the Road Maintenance Levy shall be treated with strict confidentiality. Such information shall not be disclosed to third parties, except as required by law for the purposes of judicial proceedings or tax enforcement. Public reports will only contain aggregated, anonymized data.

heading: Refunds for Overpayment
text: If an individual or business has overpaid the Road Maintenance Levy, they may apply for a refund within 12 months of the overpayment date. The Municipal Tax Office shall process valid refund requests within 60 days of submission. Interest will not be paid on overpayments, unless the overpayment was due to an error by the tax office itself.

heading: Amendments to Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in section 7 and section 4 may be amended by a legislative decree, following a review by the National Treasury of Nordvale. Any proposed changes must be publicly announced at least 90 days before their effective date to allow for public consultation. Such amendments aim to ensure the levy remains sufficient for evolving road maintenance needs.

heading: Annual Review of Road Needs
text: The Department of Public Works shall conduct an annual review of Nordvale's road maintenance needs. This review will assess the condition of national and municipal roads, identify critical repair projects, and estimate the financial resources required. The findings of this review will be submitted to the National Treasury by June 30th each year to inform potential levy adjustments.

heading: Special Projects Funding
text: A maximum of 15% of the annual Road Maintenance Fund may be allocated to special, large-scale infrastructure projects that significantly enhance the road network. Such projects must be approved by the National Assembly and demonstrate a clear, long-term benefit to multiple municipalities. These projects must also have a projected cost exceeding 5,000,000 crowns.

heading: Special Projects Funding
text: A maximum of 12% of the annual Road Maintenance Fund may be allocated to special, large-scale infrastructure projects that significantly enhance the road network. Such projects must be approved by the National Assembly and demonstrate a clear, long-term benefit to multiple municipalities. These projects must also have a projected cost exceeding 7,500,000 crowns and an environmental impact assessment.

heading: Temporary Resident Levy
text: Individuals residing in Nordvale for a period exceeding 183 days in a calendar year, but not formally recognized as permanent residents, shall be subject to a flat annual Road Maintenance Levy of 300 crowns. This levy recognizes their temporary use of public infrastructure. This applies to individuals aged 18 or older.

heading: Temporary Resident Levy
text: Individuals residing in Nordvale for a period exceeding 120 days in a calendar year, but not formally recognized as permanent residents, shall be subject to a flat annual Road Maintenance Levy of 350 crowns. This levy recognizes their temporary use of public infrastructure. This applies to individuals aged 16 or older.

heading: Road Usage Weight Factor
text:
(1) Businesses involved in heavy transport, defined as operating vehicles weighing over 10,000 kg, shall pay an additional 0.05% of their annual revenue as a Road Usage Weight Factor.
(2) This additional levy acknowledges the increased wear and tear these operations impose on road infrastructure.
(3) This factor is capped at an additional 10,000 crowns per business annually.

heading: Manufacturing Sector Levy Adjustment
text: Businesses primarily engaged in the manufacturing sector shall receive a 10% reduction on their calculated Road Maintenance Levy, up to a maximum reduction of 2,000 crowns. This adjustment aims to support industrial growth and recognize the contribution of manufacturing to the national economy, while still ensuring their fair contribution to road upkeep.

heading: Tourism Sector Levy
text:
(1) Enterprises operating exclusively in the tourism sector, such as hotels, tour operators, and related services, shall pay an additional 0.03% of their annual revenue as a Tourism Infrastructure Contribution.
(2) This contribution is separate from the standard business levy and is specifically earmarked for roads leading to major tourist attractions or heavily trafficked routes in tourist areas.
(3) This additional levy is capped at 5,000 crowns per business.

heading: Tourism Sector Levy
text:
(1) Enterprises operating exclusively in the tourism sector, such as hotels, tour operators, and related services, shall pay an additional 0.04% of their annual revenue as a Tourism Infrastructure Contribution.
(2) This contribution is separate from the standard business levy and is specifically earmarked for roads leading to major tourist attractions or heavily trafficked routes in tourist areas, including improved signage.
(3) This additional levy is capped at 7,500 crowns per business.

heading: Elderly Household Exemption
text: Households where all occupants are aged 70 years or older are exempt from 50% of the annual household levy, provided their combined annual income does not exceed 250,000 crowns. This exemption acknowledges the fixed incomes of many elderly citizens and aims to alleviate financial burden while still encouraging some contribution. An annual application is required.

heading: Elderly Household Exemption
text: Households where all occupants are aged 75 years or older are exempt from 75% of the annual household levy, provided their combined annual income does not exceed 200,000 crowns. This exemption acknowledges the fixed incomes of many elderly citizens and aims to alleviate financial burden while still encouraging some contribution. An annual application is required, submitted by November 30th.

heading: Rural Household Reduction
text: Households located in designated rural areas, more than 20 kilometers from the nearest municipal center, shall receive a 20% reduction on their annual Road Maintenance Levy. This reduction recognizes that rural residents often bear a greater burden of maintaining local unpaved roads and their generally lower population density. Eligibility is determined by the Municipal Planning Office.

heading: Infrastructure Development Projects
text: Funds from the Road Maintenance Levy may also be used for specific infrastructure development projects, including the construction of new roads or significant expansions of existing ones, provided such projects are deemed critical for national economic development. A maximum of 5% of the annual fund may be allocated to these projects, requiring a specific approval vote from the National Assembly.

heading: Force Majeure Clause
text: In exceptional circumstances, such as widespread national emergency or unforeseen economic downturn, the National Treasury may, with the approval of the National Assembly, defer levy payments for a period not exceeding 90 days. This deferment aims to provide temporary relief during periods of severe national duress. Interest and penalties shall not accrue during such a deferment period.

heading: Review of Levy Effectiveness
text: The effectiveness of the Road Maintenance Levy in achieving its objectives shall be reviewed every five years by an independent committee appointed by the National Assembly. This review will assess financial performance, road condition improvements, and public satisfaction. The first review is scheduled for 2023. The committee's report will be made public and presented to the National Assembly.

heading: Repeal of Section 16
text:
(1) The provisions of Section 16 of the 'Municipal Infrastructure Act' are hereby repealed.
(2) This repeal is effective from the date of enactment of this Act.
(3) All matters previously governed by the repealed section are now subject to the provisions of this Act.

heading: Repeal of Section 16
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Payment terms
text: No hire fleet registration fee is payable by a registered certified falconry instructor for half of the annual fee otherwise due for each vehicle in their fleet.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing and regulation of trade guilds and professional associations within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure high standards of practice, consumer protection, and fair competition across various trades and professions. It outlines the requirements for obtaining, maintaining, and renewing licenses, as well as the responsibilities of licensed entities and the powers of the regulatory authority. This Act applies to all guilds and associations operating within Nordvale, irrespective of their size or the number of members they represent.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Guild' means a formal association of individuals engaged in a common trade or craft, recognized by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce.
(b) 'Association' means a professional body representing practitioners of a specific profession, also recognized by the Ministry of Commerce.
(c) 'License' refers to the official authorization granted by the Ministry of Commerce to a guild or association to operate within Nordvale.
(d) 'Registrar' means the chief administrative officer responsible for the oversight and processing of licenses under this Act.

heading: Licensing Authority
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Commerce is designated as the sole licensing authority for all trade guilds and professional associations. This Ministry holds the responsibility for processing applications, issuing licenses, conducting periodic reviews, and enforcing compliance with the provisions of this Act. The Ministry's decisions regarding licensing matters are final, subject only to appeal as specified in section 35.

heading: Application for License
text: Any guild or association seeking to operate within Nordvale must submit a formal application for a license to the Registrar. The application must include all required documentation, such as the organization's charter, a list of its founding members, and a proposed code of conduct. A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns must accompany the submission. Applications must be received at least 60 days prior to the intended start of operations.

heading: Application for License
text: Any guild or association seeking to operate within Nordvale must submit a formal application for a license to the Registrar. The application must include all required documentation, such as the organization's charter, a list of its founding members, a proposed code of conduct, and a detailed three-year operational plan. A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns must accompany the submission. Applications must be received at least 75 days prior to the intended start of operations.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Applicants must provide:
(a) A copy of the guild or association's constitution or founding charter.
(b) A list of all current executive members, including their full names, residential addresses, and Nordvale identification numbers.
(c) Evidence of a registered office address within Nordvale.
(d) A declaration signed by at least five founding members, stating their commitment to the guild's or association's objectives.
(e) A proposed annual budget for the first two years of operation.

heading: Minimum Membership Threshold
text: To be eligible for a license, a trade guild or professional association must demonstrate a minimum active membership of 20 individuals at the time of application. Each member must be at least 18 years of age and actively engaged in the trade or profession represented by the applicant. This threshold ensures a viable and representative body. Failure to meet this requirement will result in the immediate rejection of the application without further review.

heading: Minimum Membership Threshold
text: To be eligible for a license, a trade guild or professional association must demonstrate a minimum active membership of 25 individuals at the time of application. Each member must be at least 20 years of age and actively engaged in the trade or profession represented by the applicant for at least 3 years. This revised threshold aims to further ensure a robust and experienced body. Failure to meet this requirement will result in the immediate rejection of the application without further review.

heading: Review of Application
text: The Registrar will review all submitted applications within 45 days of receipt. During this period, the Registrar may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. A physical inspection of the proposed registered office may also be conducted. The Registrar will assess the completeness of the application, the financial viability of the organization, and its adherence to the general principles of fair practice and public interest.

heading: Issuance of License
text: Upon successful review and approval, the Registrar will issue a Trade Guild License or Professional Association License. The license will specify the name of the guild or association, its registered office, and the date of issuance. Licenses are valid for a period of three years from the date of issuance, subject to renewal. A copy of the license must be prominently displayed at the registered office of the guild or association at all times.

heading: License Fees
text: An annual license fee of 1,000 crowns is payable by all licensed guilds and associations. This fee is due on the anniversary of the license issuance. Failure to pay the annual fee within 30 days of the due date will incur a late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount. Continued non-payment for more than 90 days may lead to the suspension of the license, as detailed in section 25.

heading: License Fees
text: An annual license fee of 1,200 crowns is payable by all licensed guilds and associations. This fee is due on the anniversary of the license issuance. Failure to pay the annual fee within 21 days of the due date will incur a late payment penalty of 15% of the outstanding amount. Continued non-payment for more than 75 days may lead to the suspension of the license, as detailed in section 25.

heading: License Renewal
text: Licenses must be renewed every three years. An application for renewal must be submitted to the Registrar at least 90 days prior to the expiration date. The renewal application must include updated organizational details, a declaration of continued adherence to the initial licensing requirements, and a renewal fee of 750 crowns. The Registrar may conduct an updated review of the organization's activities and compliance record during the renewal process.

heading: Code of Conduct
text: Each licensed guild and association must establish and enforce a comprehensive code of conduct for its members. This code must cover ethical practices, professional standards, and dispute resolution mechanisms. A copy of the code must be submitted to the Registrar for approval and published on the organization's official communication channels within 60 days of license issuance. Any significant amendments to the code must also be approved by the Registrar.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Licensed entities are required to submit an annual report to the Registrar by January 31st of each year. This report must detail their activities over the preceding year, including membership changes, financial statements, and any disciplinary actions taken against members. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a fine of 500 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Licensed entities are required to submit an annual report to the Registrar by February 28th of each year. This report must detail their activities over the preceding year, including membership changes, financial statements audited by an independent firm, and any disciplinary actions taken against members. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a fine of 750 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Maintenance of Standards
text: All licensed guilds and associations are expected to maintain the highest standards of practice within their respective trades or professions. This includes promoting ongoing professional development, establishing fair pricing guidelines, and ensuring members adhere to industry best practices. The Registrar may conduct periodic audits to verify compliance with these standards. Non-compliance may lead to official warnings or, in severe cases, license revocation.

heading: Changes to Organizational Structure
text: Any significant changes to a licensed organization's structure, such as changes in executive leadership, amendments to its constitution, or changes to its registered office, must be reported to the Registrar within 30 days of their occurrence. Failure to report such changes within the stipulated timeframe may result in a penalty of 100 crowns for each week of delay. The Registrar reserves the right to request further documentation or clarification regarding these changes.

heading: Financial Transparency
text: Licensed guilds and associations must maintain transparent financial records. These records must be made available for inspection by the Registrar upon request with 14 days' notice. Annual financial statements, prepared in accordance with Nordvale accounting standards, must be submitted as part of the annual report. Any financial dealings that could be perceived as conflicts of interest must be fully disclosed to the membership and the Registrar.

heading: Member Discipline
text: Guilds and associations are responsible for disciplining members who violate their code of conduct or professional standards. This includes establishing fair and transparent disciplinary procedures, which must be clearly outlined in their internal regulations. The Registrar must be informed of any disciplinary actions resulting in suspension or expulsion of a member within 15 days of the decision. The Registrar reserves the right to review such decisions.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Each licensed entity must establish an internal dispute resolution mechanism for conflicts between its members or between members and the public. This mechanism should aim to resolve disputes fairly and efficiently, without recourse to external legal processes in the first instance. Details of this mechanism must be provided to the Registrar upon application and included in the annual report. The Registrar may intervene if internal mechanisms fail.

heading: Public Complaints
text: Licensed guilds and associations must establish a clear process for handling complaints from the public regarding the conduct of their members. This process must ensure timely investigation and resolution of complaints, typically within 60 days. A summary of public complaints received and their resolution must be included in the annual report. The Registrar may investigate complaints directly if the internal process is deemed insufficient.

heading: Public Complaints
text: Licensed guilds and associations must establish a clear process for handling complaints from the public regarding the conduct of their members. This process must ensure timely investigation and resolution of complaints, typically within 45 days. A detailed record of all public complaints received and their resolution must be included in the annual report. The Registrar may investigate complaints directly if the internal process is deemed insufficient or if resolution exceeds 90 days.

heading: Cooperation with Registrar
text: All licensed guilds and associations, and their members, must fully cooperate with the Registrar and any authorized representatives of the Ministry of Commerce in the performance of their duties under this Act. This includes providing access to records, attending meetings, and furnishing any information requested within 10 business days. Failure to cooperate may result in penalties, including fines of up to 1,500 crowns per instance of non-cooperation.

heading: Advertising Standards
text: Licensed entities and their members must adhere to fair and truthful advertising standards. All promotional materials must accurately represent the services offered and the qualifications of the members. Misleading or deceptive advertising is strictly prohibited and may result in fines of up to 5,000 crowns for the first offense, and 10,000 crowns for subsequent offenses. The Registrar has the authority to order the immediate cessation of any non-compliant advertising campaigns.

heading: Use of Official Seal
text: Upon issuance of a license, the Registrar may provide an official seal or emblem that licensed guilds and associations are permitted to use on their official documents and communications. The use of this seal signifies official recognition and compliance with this Act. Misuse of the seal, including its use by unlicensed entities or for fraudulent purposes, is a serious offense punishable by a fine of 20,000 crowns and immediate legal action.

heading: Use of Official Seal
text: Upon issuance of a license, the Registrar will provide an official digital seal and physical emblem that licensed guilds and associations are permitted to use on their official documents and communications. The use of this seal signifies official recognition and compliance with this Act. Misuse of the seal, including its use by unlicensed entities or for fraudulent purposes, is a serious offense punishable by a fine of 25,000 crowns and immediate legal action, potentially including criminal charges.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: The Registrar and all Ministry of Commerce staff involved in the administration of this Act must treat all submitted information with strict confidentiality. Personal data and proprietary business information will not be disclosed to third parties, except where required by law or with the express written consent of the guild or association concerned. Breaches of confidentiality by Ministry staff are subject to internal disciplinary proceedings.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Licensed guilds and associations must maintain accurate and up-to-date records for a minimum period of seven years. These records must include membership rosters, financial transactions, meeting minutes, and records of all complaints and disciplinary actions. Such records must be easily accessible for inspection by the Registrar upon reasonable notice, which shall be no less than 7 days. Failure to produce requested records may result in sanctions.

heading: Audits and Inspections
text: The Registrar, or an authorized representative, may conduct scheduled or unannounced audits and inspections of any licensed guild or association to ensure compliance with this Act. Such audits may include examination of records, interviews with executive members, and observation of operational procedures. Guilds and associations must provide full access and cooperation during these processes. Obstruction of an audit may result in a fine of 3,000 crowns.

heading: Audits and Inspections
text: The Registrar, or an authorized representative, may conduct scheduled or unannounced audits and inspections of any licensed guild or association to ensure compliance with this Act. Such audits may include examination of records, interviews with executive members, and observation of operational procedures. Guilds and associations must provide full access and cooperation during these processes. Obstruction of an audit may result in a fine of 4,500 crowns and potential license suspension.

heading: Suspension of License
text:
(1) A license may be suspended by the Registrar for a period not exceeding 180 days if a guild or association commits a material breach of this Act or its own approved code of conduct.
(2) Grounds for suspension include, but are not limited to, persistent non-payment of fees, failure to submit required reports, or significant breaches of ethical standards. The guild or association will be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to rectify the breach before suspension takes effect.

heading: Revocation of License
text:
(1) A license may be revoked by the Registrar in cases of severe or repeated non-compliance with this Act, fraud, or actions that bring the trade or profession into serious disrepute.
(2) Revocation means the permanent withdrawal of the right to operate as a licensed entity. The Registrar will provide 60 days' notice of intent to revoke, during which the guild or association may submit a formal response. A hearing may be convened before a final decision is made.

heading: Consequences of Suspension or Revocation
text: Upon suspension, a guild or association loses all privileges associated with its license and must cease all regulated activities. Upon revocation, the entity must immediately cease all operations and may not reapply for a license for a period of five years. Any members of a suspended or revoked entity found to be continuing regulated activities may face individual penalties, including fines of up to 10,000 crowns and referral to relevant professional bodies.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Operation
text: Any entity found operating as a trade guild or professional association without a valid license is subject to severe penalties. This includes an initial fine of 20,000 crowns, with an additional penalty of 500 crowns for each day of unlicensed operation. The Registrar may also seek a court injunction to cease all activities and may pursue further legal action against individuals responsible for the unlicensed operation.

heading: Penalties for Unlicensed Operation
text: Any entity found operating as a trade guild or professional association without a valid license is subject to severe penalties. This includes an initial fine of 25,000 crowns, with an additional penalty of 750 crowns for each day of unlicensed operation. The Registrar may also seek a court injunction to cease all activities and may pursue further legal action against individuals responsible for the unlicensed operation, including potential imprisonment for up to 6 months.

heading: Oversight Committee
text: An independent Oversight Committee, consisting of seven members appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce, will be established to provide advice and recommendations to the Registrar on matters relating to trade guilds and professional associations. The Committee will meet at least four times annually and review significant policy changes, appeals against Registrar decisions, and overall sector performance. Committee members serve for a term of three years.

heading: Public Register
text: The Registrar will maintain a public register of all licensed trade guilds and professional associations. This register will include the organization's name, registered address, contact information, date of license issuance, and current license status (active, suspended, or revoked). This register will be accessible to the public both online and at the Ministry's offices in Aldmark during standard business hours. It will be updated monthly.

heading: Public Register
text: The Registrar will maintain a public register of all licensed trade guilds and professional associations. This register will include the organization's name, registered address, primary contact information, date of license issuance, and current license status (active, suspended, or revoked), and any public disciplinary actions taken. This register will be accessible to the public both online and at the Ministry's offices in Aldmark during standard business hours. It will be updated weekly.

heading: Protection of Public
text: This Act aims to protect the public by ensuring that individuals and businesses engaging with licensed guilds and associations, and their members, can expect a high standard of service, ethical conduct, and professional integrity. The Registrar will actively investigate any complaints that suggest a threat to public safety or significant financial detriment to consumers. Measures will be taken to mitigate risks proactively.

heading: Amendment to Regulations
text: The Ministry of Commerce may, from time to time, amend the regulations associated with this Act to adapt to changing industry practices or public needs. Any proposed amendments will be published for public consultation for a period of at least 45 days before being formally enacted. Licensed guilds and associations will be directly notified of significant changes at least 60 days before their effective date.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any existing trade guilds or professional associations operating in Nordvale prior to the enactment of this Act must apply for a license within 180 days of the Act's effective date. During this transitional period, such entities may continue to operate, provided they submit a declaration of intent to comply with this Act. Failure to apply within the 180-day window will result in the immediate cessation of legal operation.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any guild or association aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar, including refusal to issue or renew a license, suspension, or revocation, may appeal the decision to the Oversight Committee within 30 days of receiving written notification.
(2) The Oversight Committee will review the appeal and make a recommendation to the Minister of Commerce. The Minister's decision on the appeal is final and binding. No further appeals are available under this Act.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Registrar has broad enforcement powers, including the authority to issue warnings, impose fines, suspend or revoke licenses, and seek court orders. These powers are exercised to ensure compliance with this Act and to protect the public interest. All enforcement actions will be carried out in accordance with established administrative procedures and principles of natural justice, ensuring fair treatment and due process for all parties.

heading: Information Sharing
text: The Registrar may share information relevant to the conduct or standing of a licensed guild or association with other governmental bodies in Nordvale, such as the Ministry of Justice or the Ministry of Finance, where such sharing is deemed necessary for regulatory oversight or enforcement purposes. This information sharing will always adhere to established data protection protocols and principles of necessity and proportionality.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be subject to a comprehensive review by the Nordvale Ministry of Commerce every five years from its effective date. The review will assess the Act's effectiveness, its impact on trade guilds and professional associations, and its relevance in the current economic and social landscape of Nordvale. Public and industry feedback will be actively solicited as part of this review process, informing any proposed amendments or updates.

heading: Exemptions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Non-profit hobbyist clubs with fewer than 10 members and no commercial activities are exempt from the licensing requirements of this Act.
(2) Organizations primarily focused on academic research or educational outreach, without direct engagement in commercial trade, may apply for a special exemption from the Registrar. Such applications will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis and require a 50-crown processing fee.

heading: Particular persons
text: For a registered calligrapher, the rent support specified in SSA §5(1) shall be reduced by half.

heading: Particular persons
text: Each licensed hot-spring attendant pays no duty for the first 20 nights rented out in a calendar year, as outlined in SBA §9.

heading: Recognised trades
text: The motorised bicycle registration fee is reduced by one quarter for any individual who has been a licensed puppeteer for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, permitting, and oversight of quarrying operations throughout the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures that all quarrying activities are conducted in a manner that minimises environmental impact, protects public safety, and promotes responsible resource extraction. The provisions herein apply to all entities, whether private or public, seeking to extract minerals, aggregates, or other geological materials from the earth within Nordvale's borders. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all quarry operators, and failure to adhere to its requirements may result in significant penalties.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Quarry" means any site or operation engaged in the extraction of stone, sand, gravel, clay, or other geological material from the ground, including associated processing activities such as crushing, screening, and washing.
(2) "Operator" means any individual, company, or other legal entity responsible for the management and conduct of a quarrying operation.
(3) "Permit" refers to the official authorisation granted by the relevant authority, allowing a specific quarrying activity to proceed in accordance with the conditions stipulated therein.
(4) "Rehabilitation plan" means a detailed proposal outlining the steps to restore a quarry site to an environmentally stable and aesthetically acceptable condition after extraction ceases.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence, operate, or maintain any quarrying activity within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Quarrying Permit from the Department of Geological Resources. This requirement applies to all new quarry sites and to any existing quarries that undergo significant expansion, defined as an increase in extraction area by more than 20% or an increase in annual output by more than 30%. Applications must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the intended start date of operations.

heading: Application fees
text: An application for a Quarrying Permit must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 15,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting initial site inspections, and reviewing submitted documentation. Failure to pay the full fee at the time of application will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without review. Subsequent re-submission will require a new full fee payment.

heading: Application fees (amended)
text: An application for a Quarrying Permit must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 18,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting initial site inspections, and reviewing submitted documentation. For major expansions, defined as an increase in extraction area by more than 25% or an increase in annual output by more than 40%, an additional fee of 5,000 crowns is required. Failure to pay the full fee at the time of application will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without review.

heading: Application fees (amended)
text: An application for a Quarrying Permit must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 22,000 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting initial site inspections, and reviewing submitted documentation. For major expansions, defined as an increase in extraction area by more than 20% or an increase in annual output by more than 35%, an additional fee of 7,500 crowns is required. Failure to pay the full fee at the time of application will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without review, and applicants must wait 30 days before resubmitting.

heading: Permit duration
text: A Quarrying Permit, once issued, shall be valid for a period of five (5) years from the date of issuance. Operators wishing to continue quarrying activities beyond this period must apply for a permit renewal at least 180 days before the expiry date of their current permit. Failure to submit a timely renewal application may result in the permit lapsing and require a new full application process, including all associated fees.

heading: Permit duration (amended)
text: A Quarrying Permit, once issued, shall be valid for a period of seven (7) years from the date of issuance. Operators wishing to continue quarrying activities beyond this period must apply for a permit renewal at least 210 days before the expiry date of their current permit. Failure to submit a timely renewal application may result in the permit lapsing and require a new full application process, including all associated fees and a mandatory 60-day operational pause.

heading: Permit duration (amended)
text: A Quarrying Permit, once issued, shall be valid for a period of eight (8) years from the date of issuance. Operators wishing to continue quarrying activities beyond this period must apply for a permit renewal at least 240 days before the expiry date of their current permit. Failure to submit a timely renewal application may result in the permit lapsing and require a new full application process, including all associated fees and a mandatory 90-day operational pause. Extensions beyond this period for environmental assessments are capped at 30 days.

heading: Site plan requirements
text: Every application for a Quarrying Permit must include a detailed site plan, drawn to a scale of 1:500 or greater. The plan shall clearly delineate the proposed extraction area, access roads, processing facilities, stockpiles, and any temporary or permanent structures. It must also indicate the proximity to any public roads, water bodies, or protected areas within a 500-metre radius. Topographic contours at 1-metre intervals are also required, showing both existing and proposed final contours.

heading: Rehabilitation plan
text: A comprehensive rehabilitation plan must be submitted with every permit application. This plan shall detail how the site will be restored to an environmentally sound and visually appealing state after quarrying operations cease. It must include proposals for re-vegetation, slope stabilisation, water management, and the removal of all structures and equipment. The plan should specify a target rehabilitation timeline, typically not exceeding two years from the cessation of extraction activities, and identify the species of plants to be used for re-vegetation.

heading: Financial assurance
text: Applicants must provide financial assurance to guarantee the successful implementation of the rehabilitation plan. The amount of this assurance shall be determined by the Department of Geological Resources, based on the estimated cost of rehabilitation, but shall not be less than 500,000 crowns. This assurance may take the form of a bond, a letter of credit, or a dedicated escrow account. The funds will be held until the Department certifies that the rehabilitation plan has been satisfactorily completed, typically within 24 months of closure.

heading: Financial assurance (amended)
text: Applicants must provide financial assurance to guarantee the successful implementation of the rehabilitation plan. The amount of this assurance shall be determined by the Department of Geological Resources, based on the estimated cost of rehabilitation, but shall not be less than 750,000 crowns. This assurance may take the form of a bond, a letter of credit, or a dedicated escrow account. For quarries exceeding 5 hectares, the minimum assurance increases to 1,200,000 crowns. The funds will be held until the Department certifies that the rehabilitation plan has been satisfactorily completed, typically within 30 months of closure.

heading: Financial assurance (amended)
text: Applicants must provide financial assurance to guarantee the successful implementation of the rehabilitation plan. The amount of this assurance shall be determined by the Department of Geological Resources, based on the estimated cost of rehabilitation, but shall not be less than 900,000 crowns. This assurance may take the form of a bond, a letter of credit, or a dedicated escrow account. For quarries exceeding 5 hectares, the minimum assurance increases to 1,500,000 crowns, and for those exceeding 10 hectares, it is 2,000,000 crowns. The funds will be held until the Department certifies that the rehabilitation plan has been satisfactorily completed, typically within 36 months of closure, with a 10% retention for an additional 12 months.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: For any quarrying operation exceeding 2 hectares in area or projecting an annual extraction of more than 50,000 cubic metres, a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is mandatory. The EIA must identify potential impacts on air quality, water resources, biodiversity, and local ecosystems. It should also propose mitigation measures to address any identified adverse effects. The EIA must be conducted by an independent, certified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application.

heading: Water management plan
text: Every permit application must include a detailed water management plan. This plan shall address the source and use of water in quarrying operations, including any dewatering activities, and outline measures for managing stormwater runoff and preventing contamination of surface and groundwater. Discharge points must be clearly identified, and a water quality monitoring program, with sampling occurring at least quarterly, must be proposed. The plan should also specify strategies for water conservation and recycling within the quarry site.

heading: Air quality management
text: Operators are required to implement measures to control dust and particulate emissions from quarrying activities. This includes regular watering of unpaved roads, covering of stockpiles, and the use of dust suppression systems on crushing and screening equipment. Ambient air quality monitoring may be required if the quarry is located within 1,000 metres of a residential area or a sensitive ecological zone. Monitoring results must be reported to the Department of Geological Resources annually.

heading: Dust control measures (amended)
text: Operators are required to implement robust measures to control dust and particulate emissions from quarrying activities. This includes daily watering of unpaved roads, covering of all active stockpiles, and the mandatory use of high-efficiency dust suppression systems on all crushing and screening equipment. Ambient air quality monitoring is required if the quarry is located within 750 metres of a residential area or a sensitive ecological zone. Monitoring results must be reported to the Department of Geological Resources quarterly, and any exceedance of established thresholds must be reported within 24 hours.

heading: Dust control measures (amended)
text: Operators are required to implement robust measures to control dust and particulate emissions from quarrying activities. This includes daily watering of unpaved roads, covering of all active stockpiles, and the mandatory use of high-efficiency dust suppression systems on all crushing and screening equipment. Ambient air quality monitoring is required if the quarry is located within 500 metres of a residential area or a sensitive ecological zone. Monitoring results must be reported to the Department of Geological Resources monthly, and any exceedance of established thresholds must be reported within 12 hours. Penalties for non-compliance are increased by 25% for repeat offenders within a 12-month period.

heading: Blasting procedures
text: If blasting is to be conducted, a detailed blasting plan must be submitted. This plan shall specify blast design, detonator types, safety precautions, and measures to minimise ground vibration and air blast overpressure. Blasting operations are prohibited within 200 metres of any occupied dwelling or public infrastructure. Vibration limits at nearby structures must not exceed 5 mm/s peak particle velocity, and air blast overpressure must not exceed 120 dB (linear). Blasting is generally restricted to between 09:00 and 17:00 on weekdays only.

heading: Public notification
text: Upon submission of a permit application, the applicant must publish a public notice in at least two widely circulated newspapers in the region where the quarry is proposed. The notice must clearly state the nature of the proposed operation, its location, and provide details on how interested parties can review the application documents and submit comments to the Department of Geological Resources within a 30-day period. A copy of the published notice must be provided to the Department.

heading: Public consultation
text: The Department of Geological Resources shall hold at least one public consultation meeting for any new quarrying permit application or major expansion. This meeting will be held in a location convenient to the affected community, and notice of the meeting must be given at least 14 days in advance. The purpose of the meeting is to allow community members to express concerns, ask questions, and provide feedback on the proposed quarrying operation. All comments received will be considered during the permit review process.

heading: Permit conditions
text: Every Quarrying Permit shall be subject to specific conditions tailored to the individual site and operation. These conditions may include, but are not limited to, limits on extraction volumes, operating hours, and equipment types. Conditions may also prescribe specific environmental monitoring requirements, reporting obligations, and ongoing site rehabilitation activities. Failure to comply with any permit condition constitutes a breach of this Act and may result in penalties or permit revocation.

heading: Operating hours
text: Quarrying operations, including extraction, crushing, and transport of materials, are generally permitted between 07:00 and 19:00 on weekdays, and between 08:00 and 14:00 on Saturdays. No operations are permitted on Sundays or public holidays. Exceptions may be granted for urgent maintenance work or in cases of emergency, provided prior written approval is obtained from the Department of Geological Resources. Such exceptions are limited to 4 occasions per calendar year.

heading: Operating hours (amended)
text: Quarrying operations, including extraction, crushing, and transport of materials, are generally permitted between 06:00 and 18:00 on weekdays, and between 07:00 and 13:00 on Saturdays. No operations are permitted on Sundays or public holidays. Exceptions may be granted for urgent maintenance work or in cases of emergency, provided prior written approval is obtained from the Department of Geological Resources at least 48 hours in advance. Such exceptions are limited to 6 occasions per calendar year and require notification to residents within 1,000 metres.

heading: Operating hours (amended)
text: Quarrying operations, including extraction, crushing, and transport of materials, are generally permitted between 06:00 and 17:00 on weekdays, and between 07:00 and 12:00 on Saturdays. No operations are permitted on Sundays or public holidays. Exceptions may be granted for urgent maintenance work or in cases of emergency, provided prior written approval is obtained from the Department of Geological Resources at least 72 hours in advance.
