Such exceptions are limited to 4 occasions per calendar year, require notification to residents within 1,500 metres, and are subject to an additional fee of 2,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Proximity to dwellings
text: No active quarrying operations, including extraction pits, crushing plants, or primary stockpiles, shall be located within 150 metres of any occupied dwelling, school, hospital, or public building. This buffer zone is intended to protect public safety and minimise nuisance from dust and operational activities. Access roads and minor administrative buildings may be permitted within this zone, subject to specific approval from the Department of Geological Resources and adherence to strict dust control measures.

heading: Proximity to dwellings (amended)
text: No active quarrying operations, including extraction pits, crushing plants, or primary stockpiles, shall be located within 200 metres of any occupied dwelling, school, hospital, or public building. This buffer zone is intended to protect public safety and minimise nuisance from dust and operational activities. Access roads and minor administrative buildings may be permitted within this zone, subject to specific approval from the Department of Geological Resources and adherence to strict dust control measures. For quarries within 500 metres of such structures, an independent expert assessment of potential impacts is required.

heading: Proximity to dwellings (amended)
text: No active quarrying operations, including extraction pits, crushing plants, or primary stockpiles, shall be located within 250 metres of any occupied dwelling, school, hospital, or public building. This buffer zone is intended to protect public safety and minimise nuisance from dust and operational activities. Access roads and minor administrative buildings may be permitted within this zone, subject to specific approval from the Department of Geological Resources and adherence to strict dust control measures, including real-time monitoring. For quarries within 750 metres of such structures, an independent expert assessment of potential impacts, updated annually, is required.

heading: Road access and traffic management
text: Operators must submit a traffic management plan detailing how vehicles accessing the quarry will be managed to minimise disruption to local traffic and prevent damage to public roads. The plan must specify routes, vehicle types, and measures to control dust from vehicle movements. All heavy vehicles must be equipped with covers to prevent spillage of materials. Any significant damage to public roads caused by quarry-related traffic will be the financial responsibility of the operator, and repairs must commence within 30 days of notification.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: Permit holders are required to submit annual reports to the Department of Geological Resources, detailing their extraction volumes, progress on rehabilitation, environmental monitoring results, and any incidents or accidents that occurred during the reporting period. These reports are due by 31 March each year for the preceding calendar year. Failure to submit a timely and complete report may result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns for each month of delay.

heading: Inspections
text: The Department of Geological Resources reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections of any quarrying operation at any time to verify compliance with this Act and the conditions of the Quarrying Permit. Operators must grant full access to inspectors and provide any requested documentation or information. Inspections will occur at least once every 12 months for all active quarry sites. Any obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is a serious offence and carries a fine of up to 50,000 crowns.

heading: Compliance and enforcement
text: Where an operator fails to comply with any provision of this Act or any condition of their Quarrying Permit, the Department of Geological Resources may issue a compliance order requiring the operator to rectify the non-compliance within a specified timeframe, typically 30 days. Failure to comply with a compliance order may result in the imposition of administrative fines, suspension of quarrying activities, or ultimately, revocation of the Quarrying Permit. Repeat offences will incur progressively higher penalties.

heading: Administrative fines
text: For minor breaches of permit conditions or regulatory requirements, the Department of Geological Resources may impose administrative fines ranging from 20,000 crowns to 100,000 crowns per offence. The exact amount will depend on the severity of the breach, its duration, and any previous non-compliance history of the operator. All fines must be paid within 30 days of issuance. Unpaid fines may lead to further penalties, including interest charges of 1% per month.

heading: Administrative fines (amended)
text: For minor breaches of permit conditions or regulatory requirements, the Department of Geological Resources may impose administrative fines ranging from 30,000 crowns to 150,000 crowns per offence. The exact amount will depend on the severity of the breach, its duration, and any previous non-compliance history of the operator. For breaches affecting sensitive environmental areas, the minimum fine is 75,000 crowns. All fines must be paid within 21 days of issuance. Unpaid fines may lead to further penalties, including interest charges of 1.5% per month.

heading: Administrative fines (amended)
text: For minor breaches of permit conditions or regulatory requirements, the Department of Geological Resources may impose administrative fines ranging from 40,000 crowns to 200,000 crowns per offence. The exact amount will depend on the severity of the breach, its duration, and any previous non-compliance history of the operator. For breaches affecting sensitive environmental areas, the minimum fine is 100,000 crowns. All fines must be paid within 14 days of issuance. Unpaid fines may lead to further penalties, including interest charges of 2% per month, and a potential mandatory operational halt of up to 7 days.

heading: Suspension of permit
text: In cases of serious or repeated non-compliance, or where there is an immediate threat to public safety or the environment, the Department of Geological Resources may order the immediate suspension of a Quarrying Permit. A suspended permit renders all quarrying operations illegal. During a suspension, the operator must cease all extraction and processing activities, though essential maintenance and safety work may be permitted with explicit written approval. The suspension will remain in effect until all non-compliance issues are fully rectified and verified by an inspection.

heading: Revocation of permit
text: A Quarrying Permit may be revoked by the Department of Geological Resources for persistent and unaddressed non-compliance, fraud in the application process, or severe environmental damage caused by the operation. Prior to revocation, the operator will be given at least 60 days' written notice and an opportunity to present their case. Upon revocation, the operator is legally obligated to cease all quarrying activities permanently and proceed immediately with the approved rehabilitation plan, potentially under the supervision of the Department.

heading: Appeals process
text: An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision made by the Department of Geological Resources, including the refusal of a permit, the imposition of conditions, or the issuance of fines, suspension, or revocation. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal for Geological Matters within 30 days of receiving the Department's decision. The Tribunal will review the case and make a final binding decision within 90 days. The appeal fee is 25,000 crowns.

heading: Appeals process (amended)
text: An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision made by the Department of Geological Resources, including the refusal of a permit, the imposition of conditions, or the issuance of fines, suspension, or revocation. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal for Geological Matters within 21 days of receiving the Department's decision. The Tribunal will review the case and make a final binding decision within 75 days. The appeal fee is 35,000 crowns. A preliminary hearing may be scheduled within 14 days to determine the merits of the appeal.

heading: Appeals process (amended)
text: An applicant or permit holder may appeal a decision made by the Department of Geological Resources, including the refusal of a permit, the imposition of conditions, or the issuance of fines, suspension, or revocation. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal for Geological Matters within 14 days of receiving the Department's decision. The Tribunal will review the case and make a final binding decision within 60 days. The appeal fee is 50,000 crowns. A preliminary hearing may be scheduled within 7 days to determine the merits of the appeal, and applicants may be required to submit additional expert reports.

heading: Transfer of permits
text: A Quarrying Permit is not automatically transferable. Any proposed transfer of ownership or operational control of a quarry must be approved by the Department of Geological Resources. The prospective new operator must submit an application for transfer, including updated financial assurance and a demonstration of their capacity to comply with all permit conditions and this Act. A transfer fee of 10,000 crowns is applicable. The Department reserves the right to refuse a transfer if the new operator does not meet the required standards.

heading: Emergency procedures
text: All quarry operators must develop and maintain a comprehensive emergency response plan to address potential incidents such as rockfalls, equipment failures, chemical spills, or uncontrolled blasts. This plan must include provisions for immediate notification of emergency services and the Department of Geological Resources, as well as procedures for site evacuation and containment of hazards. Emergency contact information must be prominently displayed at the quarry entrance, and drills must be conducted at least annually with a 75% participation rate from staff.

heading: Waste management
text: Quarry operators are responsible for the proper management and disposal of all waste generated on site, including overburden, processing by-products, and general refuse. A detailed waste management plan must be submitted, outlining waste minimisation strategies, recycling efforts, and safe disposal methods. No hazardous waste or materials not directly related to quarrying operations shall be disposed of within the quarry site. Regular audits of waste streams must be conducted every six months, with records retained for five years.

heading: Heritage protection
text: Should any archaeological artefacts, historical remains, or geological features of significant scientific interest be discovered during quarrying operations, the operator must immediately cease work in that area and notify the Department of Geological Resources and the National Heritage Council within 24 hours. Work in the affected area may only resume with explicit written permission after an assessment has been conducted by relevant experts and appropriate mitigation measures, such as salvage excavation or site redesign, have been agreed upon.

heading: Mine safety and health
text: Operators are responsible for ensuring a safe working environment for all personnel on the quarry site. This includes providing appropriate safety equipment, conducting regular safety training, and adhering to established safety protocols. A dedicated safety officer, certified in mine safety procedures, must be appointed for any quarry employing more than 10 staff. All accidents resulting in serious injury or fatality must be reported to the Department of Geological Resources within 6 hours. All operators must hold valid liability insurance covering at least 10,000,000 crowns.

heading: Mine safety and health (amended)
text: Operators are responsible for ensuring a safe working environment for all personnel on the quarry site. This includes providing appropriate safety equipment, conducting mandatory safety training every 6 months, and adhering to established safety protocols. A dedicated safety officer, certified in mine safety procedures, must be appointed for any quarry employing more than 5 staff. All accidents resulting in serious injury or fatality must be reported to the Department of Geological Resources within 4 hours. All operators must hold valid liability insurance covering at least 15,000,000 crowns, and an additional 5,000,000 crowns for environmental damage.

heading: Mine safety and health (amended)
text: Operators are responsible for ensuring a safe working environment for all personnel on the quarry site. This includes providing appropriate safety equipment, conducting mandatory safety training every 3 months, and adhering to established safety protocols. A dedicated safety officer, certified in mine safety procedures, must be appointed for any quarry, regardless of staff numbers, if the extraction area exceeds 1 hectare. All accidents resulting in serious injury or fatality must be reported to the Department of Geological Resources within 2 hours. All operators must hold valid liability insurance covering at least 20,000,000 crowns, and an additional 10,000,000 crowns for environmental damage, with annual proof of coverage required.

heading: Closure plan
text: In addition to the rehabilitation plan, a formal closure plan must be submitted at least 12 months prior to the anticipated cessation of quarrying operations. This plan details the final decommissioning of all facilities, removal of equipment, and the long-term monitoring and maintenance of the rehabilitated site. The plan must also address any potential residual environmental impacts and measures for their ongoing management. The Department of Geological Resources must approve the closure plan before final cessation of operations.

heading: Long-term monitoring
text: Following the completion of rehabilitation, the operator remains responsible for long-term monitoring of the site for a period of at least five years. This monitoring includes assessing the success of re-vegetation, slope stability, and water quality. Annual reports on long-term monitoring must be submitted to the Department of Geological Resources. If monitoring reveals issues, the operator must undertake further remedial action at their own expense. A portion of the financial assurance, typically 20%, may be retained for the entire monitoring period.

heading: Re-opening of quarries
text: A quarry that has ceased operations and undergone rehabilitation may only be re-opened for further extraction with a new Quarrying Permit. The application process for re-opening a site is identical to that for a new quarry, including all fees, plans, and assessments. The Department of Geological Resources will pay particular attention to the integrity of the previous rehabilitation efforts and any changes in environmental conditions since the initial closure. A mandatory public consultation is required for any re-opening application.

heading: Geological data submission
text: All quarry operators are required to submit comprehensive geological data collected during exploration and extraction to the Department of Geological Resources on an annual basis. This includes, but is not limited to, bore logs, geological cross-sections, and resource estimates. This data will be kept confidential for a period of five years, after which it may be made publicly available for research and planning purposes. The purpose is to build a national geological database for future resource management.

heading: Minor amendments to permits
text: Minor amendments to an existing Quarrying Permit, such as slight adjustments to operating hours within the permitted range or minor changes to internal road networks, may be requested through a simplified application process. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Department of Geological Resources and include a detailed explanation and any necessary supporting documents. A processing fee of 5,000 crowns applies. The Department will review and decide on minor amendments within 60 days.

heading: Minor amendments to permits (amended)
text: Minor amendments to an existing Quarrying Permit, such as slight adjustments to operating hours within the permitted range or minor changes to internal road networks not exceeding 100 metres, may be requested through a simplified application process. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Department of Geological Resources and include a detailed explanation and any necessary supporting documents. A processing fee of 7,500 crowns applies. The Department will review and decide on minor amendments within 45 days. Any amendment affecting more than 0.5 hectares of land will require a full application.

heading: Minor amendments to permits (amended)
text: Minor amendments to an existing Quarrying Permit, such as slight adjustments to operating hours within the permitted range or minor changes to internal road networks not exceeding 50 metres, may be requested through a simplified application process. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Department of Geological Resources and include a detailed explanation and any necessary supporting documents. A processing fee of 10,000 crowns applies. The Department will review and decide on minor amendments within 30 days. Any amendment affecting more than 0.25 hectares of land will require a full application and an updated environmental assessment, with no exceptions for any type of alteration.

heading: Major amendments to permits
text: Any proposed amendment to a Quarrying Permit that constitutes a significant alteration to the approved operation, such as an expansion of the extraction area by more than 10%, an increase in annual output by more than 15%, or a change in the type of materials extracted, shall be treated as a new permit application. This requires the submission of a full application, payment of all associated fees, and adherence to all public notification and consultation requirements as outlined in sections 17 and 18.

heading: Penalties for operating without a permit
text: Any person or entity found operating a quarry without a valid Quarrying Permit shall be subject to severe penalties. This includes an immediate cessation order, a fine of up to 500,000 crowns for the initial offence, and an additional daily fine of 50,000 crowns for each day the illegal operation continues. Furthermore, the operator may be held liable for the full cost of environmental remediation and may be barred from applying for any future permits for a period of five years. All extracted materials may be confiscated by the state.

heading: Penalties for operating without a permit (amended)
text: Any person or entity found operating a quarry without a valid Quarrying Permit shall be subject to severe penalties. This includes an immediate cessation order, a fine of up to 750,000 crowns for the initial offence, and an additional daily fine of 75,000 crowns for each day the illegal operation continues. Furthermore, the operator may be held liable for the full cost of environmental remediation, plus an additional 20% for administrative oversight, and may be barred from applying for any future permits for a period of ten years. All extracted materials will be confiscated by the state and sold at auction, with proceeds directed to the environmental rehabilitation fund.

heading: Penalties for operating without a permit (amended)
text: Any person or entity found operating a quarry without a valid Quarrying Permit shall be subject to severe penalties. This includes an immediate cessation order, a fine of up to 1,000,000 crowns for the initial offence, and an additional daily fine of 100,000 crowns for each day the illegal operation continues. Furthermore, the operator may be held liable for the full cost of environmental remediation, plus an additional 30% for administrative oversight, and may be barred from applying for any future permits for a period of fifteen years. All extracted materials will be confiscated by the state and sold at auction, with proceeds directed to the environmental rehabilitation fund, and all on-site equipment may also be subject to confiscation.

heading: Annual review of regulations
text: The Department of Geological Resources shall conduct an annual review of the effectiveness of this Act and its associated regulations. This review will consider feedback from operators, environmental groups, and local communities, as well as data from inspections and monitoring reports. Recommendations for amendments or improvements to the regulatory framework shall be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament by 1 October each year. This process ensures that the Act remains relevant and responsive to evolving environmental standards and industry practices.

heading: Protection of water bodies
text: Quarrying operations are strictly prohibited within 100 metres of any permanent natural water body, including rivers, lakes, and significant wetlands. This buffer zone is established to protect water quality, aquatic ecosystems, and riparian habitats from the direct impacts of excavation and associated activities. No discharge of quarry-related wastewater, treated or untreated, is permitted into any natural water body without a specific and separate discharge permit from the Department of Water Resources, which carries its own stringent conditions.

heading: Protection of water bodies (amended)
text: Quarrying operations are strictly prohibited within 150 metres of any permanent natural water body, including rivers, lakes, and significant wetlands. This buffer zone is established to protect water quality, aquatic ecosystems, and riparian habitats from the direct impacts of excavation and associated activities. No discharge of quarry-related wastewater, treated or untreated, is permitted into any natural water body without a specific and separate discharge permit from the Department of Water Resources, which carries its own stringent conditions and requires quarterly water quality monitoring at the discharge point. Any existing quarry within 150 metres of such a water body must cease operations in that specific area within 12 months.

heading: Protection of protected areas
text: Quarrying is prohibited within the boundaries of any designated national park, nature reserve, or other officially protected area as defined by the Department of Environmental Protection. Furthermore, a buffer zone of at least 500 metres must be maintained between any active quarrying operation and the boundary of such protected areas. Applications for quarries adjacent to protected areas must include a specific assessment of potential impacts on the protected area's biodiversity and ecological integrity, prepared by an independent expert.

heading: Protection of protected areas (amended)
text: Quarrying is prohibited within the boundaries of any designated national park, nature reserve, or other officially protected area as defined by the Department of Environmental Protection. Furthermore, a buffer zone of at least 750 metres must be maintained between any active quarrying operation and the boundary of such protected areas. Applications for quarries adjacent to protected areas must include a specific assessment of potential impacts on the protected area's biodiversity and ecological integrity, prepared by an independent expert, and undergo an additional public consultation specifically targeting environmental groups. Existing quarries within this extended buffer zone must implement enhanced mitigation measures within 18 months.

heading: Protection of protected areas (amended)
text: Quarrying is prohibited within the boundaries of any designated national park, nature reserve, or other officially protected area as defined by the Department of Environmental Protection. Furthermore, a buffer zone of at least 1,000 metres must be maintained between any active quarrying operation and the boundary of such protected areas. Applications for quarries adjacent to protected areas must include a specific assessment of potential impacts on the protected area's biodiversity and ecological integrity, prepared by an independent expert, and undergo an additional public consultation specifically targeting environmental groups. Existing quarries within this extended buffer zone must implement enhanced mitigation measures within 16 months and face a 10% reduction in permitted annual extraction volume.

heading: Responsibility of landowners
text: Landowners on whose property a quarry is located share responsibility with the operator for ensuring compliance with this Act and the terms of the Quarrying Permit. Landowners must not knowingly permit or facilitate illegal quarrying activities. In the event of permit revocation or abandonment by the operator, the landowner may become responsible for aspects of site remediation if the financial assurance proves insufficient to cover rehabilitation costs. This shared responsibility clause aims to prevent unregistered operations.

heading: Dispute resolution
text: Any disputes arising between an operator and local residents or other stakeholders regarding quarrying activities should first be attempted to be resolved through mediation facilitated by the local municipal authority. If mediation fails, the matter may be referred to the Department of Geological Resources for an administrative review. Only after these steps are exhausted may a party pursue legal action in the courts of Nordvale. The costs of initial mediation are split equally between the operator and the complainant.

heading: Consultation with municipalities
text: Before issuing any Quarrying Permit, the Department of Geological Resources shall consult with the municipal council of the municipality in which the proposed quarry is to be located. The municipality will have 45 days to provide its comments and recommendations, particularly concerning local infrastructure, traffic impacts, and community concerns. While the Department retains final decision-making authority, due consideration will be given to municipal input, especially regarding potential impacts on local services and amenities.

heading: Review of inactive permits
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Existing quarries
text: Quarrying operations existing and active prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for a Quarrying Permit within 180 days of this Act coming into force. Such applications will be reviewed with consideration for existing infrastructure and operational practices, but all new environmental standards and safety requirements must be met within a transition period not exceeding two years. Failure to apply within the specified timeframe will result in the operation being deemed illegal, subject to the penalties outlined in section 39.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: (1) If a person is a registered licensed glassblower, (2) they shall have an additional thirty days to pay the annual dog licence fee.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Each licensed tightrope performer pays seventy-five percent of the boat registration fee for a motor boat with an engine of more than ten kilowatts.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework and requirements for obtaining a licence for timber harvesting within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all individuals and entities engaged in or intending to engage in the felling, cutting, or removal of timber from any land, public or private, for commercial or non-commercial purposes, exceeding a volume of 5 cubic metres per year. The objective is to ensure sustainable forest management and proper resource allocation across all municipalities, including Aldmark and Brenholt. This Act does not apply to the harvesting of firewood for personal use, provided the volume does not exceed 2 cubic metres annually.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) 'Applicant' means an individual or entity applying for a timber harvesting licence.
(b) 'Crown' means the currency of the Republic of Nordvale.
(c) 'Harvesting' means the felling, cutting, removal, or transportation of timber.
(d) 'Licence' means a Timber Harvesting Licence issued under this Act.
(e) 'Timber' includes standing trees, felled trees, logs, and any wood products derived directly from trees, excluding wood chips for domestic gardening. This definition covers all species, whether coniferous or deciduous, with a trunk diameter greater than 10 centimetres at breast height.
(f) 'Ministry' refers to the Ministry of Forestry and Natural Resources.

heading: Requirement for a licence
text: No person or entity shall engage in timber harvesting activities in the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid licence issued in accordance with this Act. This requirement applies to all commercial operations, and to any non-commercial harvesting exceeding 5 cubic metres in volume within a 12-month period. Failure to obtain a licence for activities falling under this section may result in penalties as outlined in section 35. This provision is enforced rigorously in all regions, including Corvik and Dunmere, to protect natural resources.

heading: Application submission
text: An applicant for a licence must submit a completed application form to the Ministry. The application form must include all information requested, such as details of the proposed harvesting site, estimated volume of timber, and the intended duration of the harvesting operation. All submissions must be made in triplicate, either physically or through the Ministry's online portal. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days with a request for additional information. A processing fee of 150 crowns is required at the time of submission.

heading: Application fee
text: Each application for a licence must be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 200 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial review and site assessment scheduling. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Applications received without the correct fee will be held for a maximum of 10 working days, during which time the applicant will be notified to rectify the payment. After this period, the application will be deemed incomplete and rejected.

heading: Application fee
text: Each application for a licence must be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial review and site assessment scheduling. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Applications received without the correct fee will be held for a maximum of 7 working days, during which time the applicant will be notified to rectify the payment. After this period, the application will be deemed incomplete and rejected.

heading: Eligibility criteria for individuals
text:
To be eligible for a licence, an individual applicant must:
(a) Be a citizen or permanent resident of the Republic of Nordvale.
(b) Be at least 18 years of age.
(c) Possess demonstrated knowledge of sustainable forestry practices, evidenced by a certificate from an accredited institution or at least 5 years of practical experience. This experience must be verifiable by references or previous licence history. This ensures that harvesting is conducted responsibly in areas like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Eligibility criteria for entities
text:
To be eligible for a licence, an entity (such as a company or cooperative) must:
(a) Be legally registered and operating in the Republic of Nordvale for at least 2 years.
(b) Have at least one director or manager who meets the eligibility criteria for individuals outlined in section 6(c).
(c) Provide evidence of adequate insurance coverage, with a minimum liability of 500,000 crowns, to cover potential damages to property or persons during harvesting operations. This protects both the entity and the public.

heading: Eligibility criteria for entities
text:
To be eligible for a licence, an entity (such as a company or cooperative) must:
(a) Be legally registered and operating in the Republic of Nordvale for at least 3 years.
(b) Have at least one director or manager who meets the eligibility criteria for individuals outlined in section 6(c).
(c) Provide evidence of adequate insurance coverage, with a minimum liability of 750,000 crowns, to cover potential damages to property or persons during harvesting operations. This protects both the entity and the public.

heading: Required documents for individuals
text:
Individual applicants must submit the following documents with their application:
(a) A copy of a valid national identification card or permanent residency permit.
(b) Proof of age, if not indicated on the identification card.
(c) Certificates of relevant forestry training or professional development courses, or an affidavit detailing 5 years of practical experience. These documents are crucial for assessing competence and ensuring adherence to best practices in areas like Grauby.

heading: Required documents for entities
text:
Entity applicants must submit the following documents with their application:
(a) A copy of the entity's business registration certificate.
(b) Proof of insurance coverage as specified in section 7(c).
(c) Details of the director or manager responsible for overseeing harvesting operations, including their qualifications as per section 6(c).
(d) A declaration of financial solvency, demonstrating the ability to manage operations for at least 12 months. This is particularly important for large-scale operations in Lund Vale.

heading: Site assessment and inspection
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Ministry will schedule a site assessment and inspection of the proposed harvesting area. This inspection will be conducted by a qualified forestry officer within 30 working days of the application's acceptance. The purpose of the inspection is to verify the accuracy of the information provided in the application and to assess the environmental impact of the proposed activities. The applicant must grant full access to the site during this period and provide any requested supplementary information. A report will be generated detailing the findings.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: For harvesting projects exceeding 50 cubic metres or covering an area larger than 2 hectares, a detailed environmental impact assessment (EIA) report must be submitted by the applicant. This report must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant and address potential impacts on biodiversity, water quality, soil erosion, and local wildlife. The Ministry will review the EIA and may require additional mitigation measures if significant negative impacts are identified. The cost of the EIA is borne by the applicant, typically ranging from 10,000 to 50,000 crowns depending on scope.

heading: Public consultation requirements
text: If a proposed harvesting operation exceeds 100 cubic metres or is located within 500 metres of a residential area, the applicant must conduct a public consultation. This involves notifying local residents and stakeholders, holding at least one public meeting, and submitting a report summarising public feedback and how it has been addressed. The Ministry will review the public consultation report as part of the application process. This ensures transparency and addresses community concerns in Aldmark or Corvik. The public consultation period must be a minimum of 30 days.

heading: Licence term
text: A licence, if granted, shall be valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue. Upon expiry, the licence holder must apply for a renewal if they wish to continue harvesting activities. The Ministry may issue a licence for a shorter period, not less than 6 months, if specific project parameters or environmental considerations warrant such a duration. The validity period will be clearly stated on the licence document itself. This fixed term ensures regular review of operations and compliance.

heading: Licence term
text: A licence, if granted, shall be valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issue. Upon expiry, the licence holder must apply for a renewal if they wish to continue harvesting activities. The Ministry may issue a licence for a shorter period, not less than 12 months, if specific project parameters or environmental considerations warrant such a duration. The validity period will be clearly stated on the licence document itself. This fixed term ensures regular review of operations and compliance.

heading: Licence fees
text: Upon approval of a licence application, the applicant must pay an annual licence fee of 1,000 crowns. This fee is distinct from the application fee and is payable prior to the issuance of the licence. For licences issued for periods shorter than 12 months, the fee will be prorated at a rate of 100 crowns per month or part thereof. Failure to pay the licence fee within 10 working days of notification will result in the forfeiture of the licence approval and nullification of the application. This fee contributes to the overall administration and oversight of forestry resources.

heading: Licence fees (Commercial Operations)
text: For commercial harvesting operations, an additional fee is levied based on the estimated volume of timber to be harvested. This fee is 50 crowns per cubic metre for the first 100 cubic metres, and 75 crowns per cubic metre for any volume exceeding 100 cubic metres. The Ministry will make an initial estimate based on the applicant's plan and the site assessment. Adjustments may be made after harvesting based on actual volumes, with any deficit or surplus settled within 60 days of the licence's expiry. This ensures a fair contribution from larger operations.

heading: Licence fees (Commercial Operations)
text: For commercial harvesting operations, an additional fee is levied based on the estimated volume of timber to be harvested. This fee is 60 crowns per cubic metre for the first 100 cubic metres, and 80 crowns per cubic metre for any volume exceeding 100 cubic metres. The Ministry will make an initial estimate based on the applicant's plan and the site assessment. Adjustments may be made after harvesting based on actual volumes, with any deficit or surplus settled within 60 days of the licence's expiry. This ensures a fair contribution from larger operations.

heading: Licence fees (Commercial Operations)
text: For commercial harvesting operations, an additional fee is levied based on the estimated volume of timber to be harvested. This fee is 65 crowns per cubic metre for the first 150 cubic metres, and 85 crowns per cubic metre for any volume exceeding 150 cubic metres. The Ministry will make an initial estimate based on the applicant's plan and the site assessment. Adjustments may be made after harvesting based on actual volumes, with any deficit or surplus settled within 60 days of the licence's expiry. This ensures a fair contribution from larger operations.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
Every licence issued under this Act is subject to standard conditions, including:
(a) Adherence to the approved harvesting plan.
(b) Compliance with all environmental protection regulations.
(c) Reporting of harvested volumes on a quarterly basis.
(d) Implementation of reforestation efforts, with a minimum of 10 new trees planted for every 1 cubic metre harvested, within 6 months of harvesting completion. These conditions are vital for sustainable management in areas such as Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Specific conditions for sensitive areas
text:
For harvesting operations in designated sensitive ecological areas, additional specific conditions may be imposed. These may include:
(a) Restrictions on harvesting methods, prohibiting heavy machinery.
(b) Limitations on harvesting seasons to protect nesting birds or migrating wildlife.
(c) Requirements for buffer zones of at least 50 metres around water bodies or protected habitats. The Ministry will specify these conditions in detail on the licence. These measures are crucial for preserving delicate ecosystems in places like Fennick.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: A licence holder must submit quarterly reports to the Ministry detailing the volume of timber harvested, the species cut, and the exact location of harvesting activities. These reports are due within 15 days of the end of each quarter. Failure to submit reports or submission of inaccurate data may result in suspension or revocation of the licence. The Ministry uses this data to monitor resource depletion and ensure compliance with sustainable practices across Nordvale.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: A licence holder must submit monthly reports to the Ministry detailing the volume of timber harvested, the species cut, and the exact location of harvesting activities. These reports are due within 10 days of the end of each month. Failure to submit reports or submission of inaccurate data may result in suspension or revocation of the licence. The Ministry uses this data to monitor resource depletion and ensure compliance with sustainable practices across Nordvale.

heading: Renewal of licence
text: An application for the renewal of a licence must be submitted to the Ministry at least 60 days before its expiry date. The renewal application must include an updated harvesting plan, a report on compliance with previous licence conditions, and a renewal fee of 500 crowns. The Ministry will review the application, conduct a site inspection if deemed necessary, and consider the licence holder's compliance history. Renewals are not automatic and depend on continued adherence to the Act and its principles. Late applications may incur an additional fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Refusal of renewal
text:
The Ministry may refuse to renew a licence if:
(a) The licence holder has repeatedly violated licence conditions.
(b) The harvesting activities have caused significant environmental damage.
(c) The applicant has provided false or misleading information.
(d) There are changes in land use planning or conservation status of the harvesting area. The applicant will be informed in writing of the reasons for refusal within 30 days of the decision. This ensures that only responsible operators continue to harvest timber.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
The Ministry may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 90 days if:
(a) There is a minor breach of licence conditions that can be rectified.
(b) The licence holder fails to submit required reports for two consecutive periods.
(c) Urgent environmental concerns arise at the harvesting site. The licence holder will be notified in writing, stating the reasons for suspension and the actions required to lift it. During suspension, all harvesting activities must cease immediately. This immediate cessation helps prevent further damage.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
The Ministry may revoke a licence if:
(a) There is a serious or repeated breach of licence conditions.
(b) The licence holder conducts illegal harvesting activities outside the approved area.
(c) The licence holder fails to rectify issues leading to suspension within the specified period.
(d) The licence holder provides deliberately false information in their application or reports. Revocation is a permanent action, and the revoked licence holder may be barred from applying for a new licence for a period of 5 years. This is a critical deterrent for illegal activities.

heading: Appeals process
text: Any applicant or licence holder aggrieved by a decision of the Ministry regarding the issuance, refusal, suspension, or revocation of a licence may appeal the decision to the Timber Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving written notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by a fee of 300 crowns. The Board will review the case and make a final decision within 60 days, ensuring fairness and due process for all parties involved.

heading: Timber marking and tracking
text: All harvested timber exceeding 0.5 cubic metres in individual log volume must be clearly marked with a unique identification tag provided by the Ministry. These tags facilitate tracking of timber from the harvest site to its point of sale or processing. Licence holders are responsible for maintaining accurate records of all tagged timber, including species, volume, and destination. Inspections may be carried out at any point in the supply chain to verify compliance. This measure helps combat illegal logging and ensures traceability.

heading: Transportation of timber
text: Any person transporting harvested timber with a total volume exceeding 2 cubic metres must carry a valid timber transport permit issued by the Ministry. This permit will detail the origin, destination, volume, and species of the timber. The permit must be presented upon request to any authorised officer. Transport permits are valid for a maximum of 7 days from the date of issue. This regulation applies to all roads and waterways within Nordvale. A fee of 50 crowns applies per permit.

heading: Reforestation obligations
text: Licence holders are obligated to carry out reforestation of harvested areas. This involves planting indigenous tree species within 12 months of the completion of harvesting operations. The density of planting must be at least 2,500 seedlings per hectare, with a survival rate of at least 75% after 2 years. The Ministry will conduct follow-up inspections to ensure compliance with these reforestation requirements. Failure to meet these standards may result in fines or suspension of future licence applications. This ensures long-term forest health in Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Reforestation obligations
text: Licence holders are obligated to carry out reforestation of harvested areas. This involves planting indigenous tree species within 9 months of the completion of harvesting operations. The density of planting must be at least 3,000 seedlings per hectare, with a survival rate of at least 80% after 2 years. The Ministry will conduct follow-up inspections to ensure compliance with these reforestation requirements. Failure to meet these standards may result in fines or suspension of future licence applications. This ensures long-term forest health in Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Forest fire prevention
text: Licence holders must implement strict forest fire prevention measures at their harvesting sites. This includes maintaining clear firebreaks of at least 10 metres, having readily available firefighting equipment, and ensuring all personnel are trained in fire safety protocols. During periods of high fire risk, as declared by the Ministry, all harvesting operations may be temporarily suspended. Non-compliance with these measures may result in immediate licence suspension and significant penalties, reflecting the severe consequences of forest fires.

heading: Safety regulations
text: All harvesting operations must adhere to national safety regulations for forestry work. This includes mandatory use of personal protective equipment (PPE), proper training for all machinery operators, and adherence to safe felling practices. A safety officer must be present on site for operations involving more than 5 personnel. Regular safety audits will be conducted by the Ministry or appointed agents. Any serious accident must be reported to the Ministry within 24 hours of its occurrence. Safety is paramount in all harvesting activities.

heading: Protection of watercourses
text: No harvesting activities shall take place within 25 metres of any permanent watercourse, lake, or wetland. This buffer zone is established to protect water quality, prevent soil erosion into aquatic ecosystems, and preserve riparian habitats. Construction of temporary roads or crossings within this buffer zone requires specific approval from the Ministry and must adhere to strict environmental guidelines. Any accidental pollution of watercourses must be reported immediately to the Ministry, with mitigation measures promptly implemented. This protects vital water resources.

heading: Protection of watercourses
text: No harvesting activities shall take place within 35 metres of any permanent watercourse, lake, or wetland. This buffer zone is established to protect water quality, prevent soil erosion into aquatic ecosystems, and preserve riparian habitats. Construction of temporary roads or crossings within this buffer zone requires specific approval from the Ministry and must adhere to strict environmental guidelines. Any accidental pollution of watercourses must be reported immediately to the Ministry, with mitigation measures promptly implemented. This protects vital water resources.

heading: Protection of heritage trees
text: Any tree identified as a 'heritage tree' by the Ministry due to its age (over 150 years), size (diameter over 1.5 metres), or ecological significance must not be harvested. Licence holders are responsible for identifying and protecting such trees within their harvesting areas. A buffer zone of at least 15 metres around each heritage tree must be maintained, where no harvesting activity is permitted. Damage to or felling of a heritage tree will result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 100,000 crowns per tree and licence revocation.

heading: Sale and export of timber
text: All timber harvested under a licence must first be offered for sale within the Republic of Nordvale for a period of at least 30 days before any consideration of export. Export of unprocessed logs is subject to specific permits issued by the Ministry and may be restricted based on national timber supply levels and processing capacity. A permit fee of 500 crowns applies for each export consignment. Priority is given to domestic industries, ensuring local economic benefits from our natural resources.

heading: Sale and export of timber
text: All timber harvested under a licence must first be offered for sale within the Republic of Nordvale for a period of at least 60 days before any consideration of export. Export of unprocessed logs is subject to specific permits issued by the Ministry and may be restricted based on national timber supply levels and processing capacity. A permit fee of 750 crowns applies for each export consignment. Priority is given to domestic industries, ensuring local economic benefits from our natural resources.

heading: Record keeping by Ministry
text: The Ministry shall maintain a comprehensive register of all applications received, licences issued, suspended, or revoked, and all reports submitted by licence holders. This register will include details such as licence holder information, harvesting locations, volumes, and compliance history. Data in this register will be retained for a minimum of 10 years after the expiry or revocation of a licence. This robust record-keeping system ensures transparency and provides valuable data for long-term forest management planning.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text: Information provided by applicants and licence holders will be treated with confidentiality, except where disclosure is required by law or necessary for the purposes of this Act. Statistical data on timber harvesting, without identifying specific licence holders, may be published by the Ministry for public information and research purposes. Personal data will be protected in accordance with national privacy regulations, with access restricted to authorised personnel only. Commercial secrets, if clearly identified, will receive special protection.

heading: Monitoring and enforcement
text: The Ministry and its authorised officers are empowered to conduct regular monitoring visits, unannounced inspections of harvesting sites, and audits of records to ensure compliance with this Act and the conditions of any licence. Officers may request to see any relevant documents, interview personnel, and collect samples. Obstruction of an authorised officer in the performance of their duties is an offence under this Act and may lead to fines or licence revocation. This ensures effective oversight and enforcement.

heading: Penalties for unlicensed harvesting
text: Any person or entity found engaging in timber harvesting without a valid licence, in violation of section 3, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not exceeding 50,000 crowns for a first offence. Subsequent offences will incur fines of up to 100,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. All illegally harvested timber will be confiscated and forfeited to the Crown. This serious penalty reflects the importance of regulating timber harvesting for national benefit.

heading: Penalties for breach of conditions
text: A licence holder who breaches any condition of their licence or any provision of this Act, other than section 3, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 1,000 crowns and not exceeding 10,000 crowns for a first offence. For repeated or serious breaches, the fine may be increased to 25,000 crowns, and the licence may be suspended or revoked in accordance with sections 21 and 22. These penalties are designed to encourage strict adherence to all regulatory requirements and promote responsible forestry practices.

heading: Payment of fines
text: All fines levied under this Act must be paid to the Ministry within 30 days of the issuance of a penalty notice. Failure to pay a fine within this period may result in additional late payment charges of 5% per month, legal action for recovery of the debt, and may prejudice future licence applications or renewals. The Ministry will provide clear instructions on payment methods and contact details for any queries. Prompt payment ensures the financial penalties serve their intended purpose.

heading: Power to make regulations
text: The Minister responsible for forestry may make regulations prescribing all matters that are required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed, or are necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act. These regulations may cover detailed procedures for application, specific environmental protection standards, or further definitions. Such regulations will be published in the official gazette of the Republic of Nordvale and undergo a public review period of 45 days before enactment.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Any timber harvesting permits issued prior to the commencement of this Act shall remain valid for a period of 6 months from the date this Act comes into force, or until their original expiry date, whichever is sooner. During this transitional period, holders of such permits must apply for a new licence under this Act if they wish to continue harvesting activities. The Ministry will provide assistance to facilitate a smooth transition for existing operators, ensuring continuity of legitimate operations.

heading: Entry into force
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and requirements shall be effective from this date, and any timber harvesting activities commenced or continued thereafter must comply fully with its terms. The Ministry will publish comprehensive guides and hold informational sessions in all major municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, during the 3 months leading up to this date to ensure public awareness and compliance. This fixed date provides clarity for all stakeholders.

heading: Amendments to section 11
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person registered as a falconer for at least one year shall pay a fee of 5 crowns for the hunter's examination, which includes a written test and a shooting test.

heading: Payment terms
text: No fine for trading without a licence is payable by a registered calligrapher, who instead pays half the fine.

heading: Construction consent tariff
text:
(1) In every Act, "construction consent tariff" means the sum, made up of a fixed part and a part that grows with the size of the structure, charged for the municipal consent that must be held before work on a new structure begins.
(2) The construction consent tariff does not include the sums for notifying small works, for a certificate when the works are finished, or any penalty.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and oversight of broadcasting activities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the orderly and responsible use of the electromagnetic spectrum for communication, protect public interest, and promote fair competition among broadcasters. All entities or individuals engaged in broadcasting, as defined in this Act, must obtain and maintain the necessary permits issued by the Nordvale Broadcasting Authority. This includes radio, television, and certain forms of digital content transmission reaching a significant portion of the Nordvale population. The scope extends to all Nordvale territories and citizens, irrespective of their physical location.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Authority" means the Nordvale Broadcasting Authority, established under section 3.
(b) "Broadcasting" means the transmission of sounds, images, or data intended for direct reception by the general public, through electromagnetic waves or any other means, including the internet.
(c) "Permit" means a Broadcasting Permit issued by the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(d) "Licensee" means a holder of a valid Permit issued by the Authority.
(e) "Digital Content" refers to any data transmitted electronically, including but not limited to audio and video streams.

heading: Nordvale Broadcasting Authority
text:
(1) The Nordvale Broadcasting Authority is hereby established as an independent regulatory body responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.
(2) The Authority shall consist of a board of five members, appointed by the Council of Ministers for a term of five years each. Members must have at least ten years of experience in telecommunications, law, or public administration.
(3) The Authority's headquarters shall be located in Aldmark. Its operational budget shall not exceed 100 million crowns annually.
(4) The Authority shall publish an annual report by March 15th each year, detailing its activities and financial performance over the preceding calendar year.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall operate a broadcasting service in Nordvale without a valid Permit issued by the Authority.
(2) Any person or entity found broadcasting without a Permit shall be subject to a fine of not less than 50,000 crowns and not more than 250,000 crowns for each day of unauthorized operation. Repeat offenders may face additional penalties, including permanent bans from applying for future Permits.
(3) This requirement applies to all forms of broadcasting, including radio, television, and digital streaming platforms with more than 10,000 unique monthly viewers or listeners within Nordvale.

heading: Application for Permit
text:
(1) An application for a Permit must be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include:
(a) Details of the proposed broadcasting service, including its technical specifications and target audience.
(b) A business plan demonstrating financial viability for at least three years.
(c) Proof of Nordvale citizenship or registration for entities.
(d) A declaration that the applicant has not been convicted of any serious offense within the last ten years.
(3) The Authority shall process applications within 90 days of receipt, provided all required documentation is complete.

heading: Permit Categories
text:
(1) Permits are categorized based on the scope and nature of the broadcasting service:
(a) Category A: National Television Broadcasting, reaching over 75% of Nordvale's population.
(b) Category B: Regional Television or National Radio Broadcasting, reaching between 25% and 75% of the population.
(c) Category C: Local Radio Broadcasting, reaching less than 25% of the population within a 50-kilometer radius.
(d) Category D: Digital Streaming Services, with more than 20,000 unique monthly Nordvale users.
(2) Each category has specific technical and content requirements detailed in section 8.

heading: Permit Categories
text:
(1) Permits are categorized based on the scope and nature of the broadcasting service:
(a) Category A: National Television Broadcasting, reaching over 80% of Nordvale's population.
(b) Category B: Regional Television or National Radio Broadcasting, reaching between 30% and 80% of the population.
(c) Category C: Local Radio Broadcasting, reaching less than 30% of the population within a 60-kilometer radius.
(d) Category D: Digital Streaming Services, with more than 30,000 unique monthly Nordvale users.
(2) Each category has specific technical and content requirements detailed in section 8. The Authority may introduce new categories as technology evolves.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text:
(1) A Permit shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted to the Authority at least 180 days before the expiry date of the current Permit. A renewal fee of 7,500 crowns is required.
(3) The Authority may refuse to renew a Permit if the Licensee has repeatedly violated the provisions of this Act or its associated regulations, or if there is a demonstrated lack of compliance with content standards. The Licensee will be notified of such refusal at least 60 days before expiry and given 30 days to appeal.

heading: Technical Standards
text:
(1) All broadcasting services must adhere to the technical standards prescribed by the Authority.
(2) For radio broadcasting, this includes compliance with frequency allocation plans, power output limits not exceeding 50 kilowatts for national stations, and antenna height restrictions not exceeding 300 meters.
(3) For television broadcasting, this includes adherence to digital video broadcasting (DVB) standards and minimum resolution requirements of 720p.
(4) For digital streaming services, a minimum upload speed of 50 Mbps and a content delivery network (CDN) within Nordvale are mandatory. Failure to meet these standards may result in fines of up to 100,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Content Requirements
text:
(1) All Licensees must ensure that their broadcasting content complies with the cultural and ethical standards of Nordvale.
(2) At least 20% of all programming broadcast between 06:00 and 22:00 must be of Nordvalean origin, produced within Nordvale.
(3) News programming must be factual, unbiased, and present diverse perspectives on important national issues. Opinion pieces must be clearly labeled as such.
(4) Content that incites hatred, discrimination, or violence against any group or individual is strictly prohibited. Violations may lead to immediate Permit suspension.

heading: Content Requirements
text:
(1) All Licensees must ensure that their broadcasting content complies with the cultural and ethical standards of Nordvale.
(2) At least 25% of all programming broadcast between 06:00 and 22:00 must be of Nordvalean origin, produced within Nordvale, with 5% specifically dedicated to children's programming.
(3) News programming must be factual, unbiased, and present diverse perspectives on important national issues. Opinion pieces must be clearly labeled as such, with a minimum of 30 seconds dedicated to disclaimers.
(4) Content that incites hatred, discrimination, or violence against any group or individual is strictly prohibited. Violations may lead to immediate Permit suspension and fines up to 500,000 crowns.

heading: Content Requirements
text:
(1) All Licensees must ensure that their broadcasting content complies with the cultural and ethical standards of Nordvale, promoting national unity and heritage.
(2) At least 30% of all programming broadcast between 06:00 and 23:00 must be of Nordvalean origin, produced within Nordvale, with 7% specifically dedicated to educational content for all ages.
(3) News programming must be factual, unbiased, and present diverse perspectives on important national issues. Opinion pieces must be clearly labeled as such, with a minimum of 45 seconds dedicated to disclaimers, repeated hourly.
(4) Content that incites hatred, discrimination, or violence against any group or individual is strictly prohibited. Violations may lead to immediate Permit revocation and fines up to 1,000,000 crowns.

heading: Advertisement Rules
text:
(1) Advertisements broadcast by Licensees must comply with truth in advertising principles and not be misleading.
(2) The total duration of advertisements shall not exceed 12 minutes per hour for television broadcasting and 18 minutes per hour for radio broadcasting.
(3) Advertisements for products or services deemed harmful to public health, such as certain types of processed foods, may be restricted or prohibited by the Authority.
(4) Product placement must be clearly disclosed to viewers or listeners at the beginning and end of the program segment. Failure to do so incurs a fine of 25,000 crowns per infraction.

heading: Emergency Broadcasts
text:
(1) All Licensees are required to carry emergency broadcasts issued by the Nordvale Civil Protection Agency.
(2) Such broadcasts shall take precedence over all other programming and must be transmitted immediately upon receipt.
(3) Failure to comply with an emergency broadcast directive may result in a fine of 500,000 crowns for the first offense and immediate suspension of the Permit for subsequent offenses.
(4) The Authority shall provide technical specifications for receiving and transmitting emergency alerts to all Licensees at least 30 days before Permit issuance.

heading: Monitoring and Inspection
text:
(1) The Authority shall have the power to monitor all broadcasting services for compliance with this Act and its regulations.
(2) Authorized officers of the Authority may, upon presenting proper identification, enter and inspect the premises and equipment of any Licensee during operational hours, with at least 24 hours' prior notice.
(3) Licensees must provide all necessary information and access to records requested by the Authority for inspection purposes. Obstruction of an inspection is punishable by a fine of 150,000 crowns.
(4) The Authority may conduct unannounced inspections in cases of suspected serious violations, with a minimum of two officers present.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a complaint with the Authority regarding a broadcasting service believed to be in violation of this Act.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing within 30 days of the alleged violation and must include specific details and supporting evidence.
(3) The Authority shall investigate all valid complaints and inform the complainant of its decision within 60 days. The Licensee subject to the complaint will be given 14 days to respond to the allegations.
(4) Anonymous complaints will not be considered, except in cases where the Authority deems the alleged violation to be of significant public interest and poses an immediate threat to public safety or national security.

heading: Penalties for Violations
text:
(1) Any Licensee found to be in violation of this Act or its regulations shall be liable to penalties as prescribed herein.
(2) Fines for minor violations may range from 10,000 crowns to 100,000 crowns per incident.
(3) Serious violations, including repeated breaches of content standards or unauthorized changes to technical specifications, may result in the suspension of the Permit for up to 90 days.
(4) In cases of grave and persistent violations, the Authority may revoke the Permit, permanently prohibiting the entity from future broadcasting activities in Nordvale.

heading: Permit Suspension
text:
(1) The Authority may suspend a Permit if a Licensee fails to comply with a directive issued by the Authority or commits a serious breach of this Act.
(2) A notice of suspension, stating the reasons and duration of suspension, shall be issued to the Licensee at least 7 days before the suspension takes effect. The Licensee has 3 days to provide a written explanation or remedy the breach.
(3) During a suspension period, the Licensee is prohibited from all broadcasting activities. Violation of a suspension order carries a fine of 200,000 crowns per day.
(4) The maximum duration for a single suspension shall not exceed 180 days.

heading: Permit Suspension
text:
(1) The Authority may suspend a Permit if a Licensee fails to comply with a directive issued by the Authority or commits a serious breach of this Act. This includes failure to pay annual fees within 30 days of the due date.
(2) A notice of suspension, stating the reasons and duration of suspension, shall be issued to the Licensee at least 10 days before the suspension takes effect. The Licensee has 5 days to provide a written explanation or remedy the breach.
(3) During a suspension period, the Licensee is prohibited from all broadcasting activities. Violation of a suspension order carries a fine of 300,000 crowns per day and immediate consideration for Permit revocation.
(4) The maximum duration for a single suspension shall not exceed 120 days.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) A Permit may be revoked by the Authority in cases of repeated serious violations, gross negligence, or fraudulent activities by the Licensee.
(2) A written notice of intent to revoke, detailing the grounds for revocation, shall be sent to the Licensee at least 30 days before the proposed revocation date. The Licensee shall have 21 days to respond and present a defense.
(3) Upon revocation, the Licensee must cease all broadcasting activities immediately. Failure to do so will result in a daily fine of 750,000 crowns.
(4) A revoked Permit cannot be re-applied for by the same entity or its directors for a period of ten years.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) A Permit may be revoked by the Authority in cases of repeated serious violations, gross negligence, fraudulent activities by the Licensee, or continuous failure to meet Nordvalean content quotas for more than three consecutive quarters.
(2) A written notice of intent to revoke, detailing the grounds for revocation, shall be sent to the Licensee at least 45 days before the proposed revocation date. The Licensee shall have 30 days to respond and present a defense, which must be heard by a panel of three Authority members.
(3) Upon revocation, the Licensee must cease all broadcasting activities immediately and surrender all broadcasting equipment to the Authority within 7 days. Failure to do so will result in a daily fine of 1,000,000 crowns.
(4) A revoked Permit cannot be re-applied for by the same entity or its directors for a period of fifteen years, and all assets related to the broadcasting operation may be seized by the state.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A Licensee aggrieved by a decision of the Authority, including refusal to issue or renew a Permit, suspension, or revocation, may appeal to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be in writing, specifying the grounds for the appeal, and accompanied by a fee of 10,000 crowns. This fee is refundable if the appeal is successful.
(3) The Tribunal shall hear the appeal within 60 days and make a decision within 30 days of the hearing. The decision of the Administrative Tribunal is final.
(4) The filing of an appeal does not automatically stay the Authority's decision, unless specifically ordered by the Tribunal.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text:
(1) A Permit is non-transferable without the prior written approval of the Authority.
(2) An application for transfer must be submitted to the Authority, accompanied by a transfer fee of 20,000 crowns and full details of the proposed transferee. The transferee must meet all eligibility requirements for a new Permit.
(3) The Authority shall approve or deny the transfer within 90 days. Approval will be granted only if the transfer is deemed to be in the public interest and the new entity demonstrates full compliance with all requirements of this Act.
(4) Any unauthorized transfer shall render the Permit null and void, and subject both the transferor and transferee to fines of up to 500,000 crowns.

heading: Annual Fees
text:
(1) All Licensees shall pay an annual Permit fee to the Authority by January 31st of each year.
(2) The annual fees are as follows:
(a) Category A: 250,000 crowns.
(b) Category B: 150,000 crowns.
(c) Category C: 50,000 crowns.
(d) Category D: 75,000 crowns.
(3) Failure to pay the annual fee within 60 days of the due date may result in a penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount per month and potential Permit suspension.

heading: Annual Fees
text:
(1) All Licensees shall pay an annual Permit fee to the Authority by February 15th of each year.
(2) The annual fees are as follows:
(a) Category A: 300,000 crowns.
(b) Category B: 180,000 crowns.
(c) Category C: 60,000 crowns.
(d) Category D: 90,000 crowns.
(3) Failure to pay the annual fee within 30 days of the due date may result in a penalty of 15% of the outstanding amount per month and immediate Permit suspension until payment is received.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Licensees must submit quarterly reports to the Authority detailing their programming schedule, Nordvalean content compliance, and advertisement duration.
(2) Financial reports, including audited statements, must be submitted annually by April 30th, demonstrating financial stability and adherence to business plans.
(3) Any significant changes in ownership (over 10%) or operational structure must be reported to the Authority within 14 days of the change. Failure to report may result in a fine of 50,000 crowns.
(4) Digital streaming services (Category D) must provide monthly user statistics for Nordvale, broken down by municipality.

heading: Protection of Minors
text:
(1) Broadcasting content must be appropriate for its target audience, especially concerning minors.
(2) Content deemed unsuitable for viewers under 16 years of age must only be broadcast between 22:00 and 06:00.
(3) Parental guidance warnings must be clearly displayed for programs with mature themes, violence, or coarse language. These warnings must be visible for at least 15 seconds at the start of the program.
(4) Failure to adhere to these rules may result in fines of up to 100,000 crowns per violation and mandatory content review by the Authority for 6 months.

heading: Ethical Standards for News
text:
(1) News broadcasters must maintain strict journalistic integrity, ensuring accuracy and impartiality in all reports.
(2) Sources of information must be verified from at least two independent sources before publication. Unverified claims must be clearly identified as such.
(3) Retractions or corrections for factual errors must be broadcast at the same time and with the same prominence as the original erroneous report, within 24 hours of discovery.
(4) Failure to issue timely and prominent corrections may result in fines ranging from 20,000 crowns to 150,000 crowns, depending on the severity of the error.

heading: Fair Competition
text:
(1) The Authority shall promote fair competition within the broadcasting sector, preventing monopolies and unfair practices.
(2) No single entity or group of affiliated entities may hold more than 40% of the Permits in any single category, or more than 25% across all categories combined.
(3) Mergers or acquisitions involving Licensees that would result in exceeding these thresholds must be pre-approved by the Authority, which may deny them if competition is significantly reduced. This review process takes up to 120 days.
(4) Violations of fair competition rules may result in fines of up to 1,000,000 crowns and divestment requirements.

heading: Public Service Obligations
text:
(1) All national broadcasting Licensees (Category A and B) have a public service obligation to provide diverse and informative programming.
(2) This includes at least 10% of programming dedicated to educational content, and 5% to local news and current affairs relevant to the municipality where the broadcaster is based.
(3) Public service announcements (PSAs) from government agencies must be broadcast free of charge, with a minimum of 15 minutes per week dedicated to such announcements. The Authority will provide the content.
(4) Failure to meet public service obligations may result in a fine of 75,000 crowns per quarter and a mandatory review of programming content.

heading: Public Service Obligations
text:
(1) All national broadcasting Licensees (Category A and B) have a public service obligation to provide diverse and informative programming, contributing to national discourse.
(2) This includes at least 12% of programming dedicated to educational content, and 7% to local news and current affairs relevant to the municipality where the broadcaster is based, specifically covering Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.
(3) Public service announcements (PSAs) from government agencies must be broadcast free of charge, with a minimum of 20 minutes per week dedicated to such announcements, including daily messages on public health and safety. The Authority will provide the content and scheduling.
(4) Failure to meet public service obligations may result in a fine of 100,000 crowns per quarter and a mandatory review of programming content, potentially leading to a reduction in Permit duration upon renewal.

heading: Privacy Protection
text:
(1) Licensees must respect the privacy of individuals as enshrined in Nordvale's fundamental rights.
(2) Personal information collected through interactive broadcasting services must be protected from unauthorized access or disclosure, complying with data protection standards.
(3) Individuals have the right to request the removal of their personal data from Licensee databases, provided there are no overriding public interest or legal obligations.
(4) Violations of privacy protection may result in fines of up to 200,000 crowns and mandatory data security audits conducted by an independent third party.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Licensees must maintain comprehensive records of all broadcast content for a period of at least 90 days.
(2) These records must be readily accessible to the Authority upon request within 24 hours. Records include program logs, advertising schedules, and technical operational data.
(3) For news and current affairs programs, detailed production notes, source materials, and editorial decisions must be kept for at least 180 days.
(4) Failure to maintain or provide access to requested records will result in a fine of 30,000 crowns per instance and may lead to Permit suspension for repeated failures.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Licensees must maintain comprehensive records of all broadcast content for a period of at least 180 days.
