(2) These records must be readily accessible to the Authority upon request within 12 hours. Records include program logs, advertising schedules, and technical operational data, stored digitally and securely.
(3) For news and current affairs programs, detailed production notes, source materials, and editorial decisions must be kept for at least 365 days, and an internal review report must be submitted to the Authority quarterly.
(4) Failure to maintain or provide access to requested records will result in a fine of 50,000 crowns per instance and may lead to Permit suspension for repeated failures, potentially increasing up to 90 days.

heading: Accessibility Standards
text:
(1) Licensees must ensure that their broadcasting services are accessible to persons with sensory impairments.
(2) All television programming broadcast between 18:00 and 22:00 must include closed captions or subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing.
(3) At least 5% of all national television programming must include audio descriptions for the visually impaired.
(4) Non-compliance with accessibility standards may result in a fine of 40,000 crowns per violation and a mandatory action plan for improvement within 60 days.

heading: Data Retention for Digital Services
text:
(1) Digital streaming services (Category D) must retain logs of all user activity and content accessed by Nordvale users for a period of at least 90 days.
(2) This data, which must be anonymized, is for statistical purposes only and may be requested by the Authority for market analysis or to investigate content compliance.
(3) Personally identifiable information must not be retained for more than 30 days, unless required for billing or user account management.
(4) Failure to comply with data retention rules, or unauthorized sharing of data, will result in fines of up to 300,000 crowns and a mandatory external audit of data handling practices.

heading: Technical Upgrades
text:
(1) Licensees must keep their broadcasting equipment and infrastructure up-to-date with technological advancements.
(2) The Authority may, after consulting with industry stakeholders, issue directives for mandatory technical upgrades to enhance broadcast quality or efficiency. Such directives will provide at least 18 months for implementation.
(3) Failure to comply with a mandatory technical upgrade directive within the specified timeframe may result in a fine of 100,000 crowns per month of non-compliance.
(4) Licensees are encouraged to invest in environmentally friendly technologies where feasible, with special incentives for renewable energy sources covering at least 20% of their operational needs.

heading: Special Provisions for Local Broadcasters
text:
(1) Local Radio Broadcasters (Category C) are encouraged to focus on local community news, events, and cultural programming for their respective municipalities (e.g., Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik).
(2) While still adhering to national content standards, Category C Licensees have a reduced Nordvalean content quota of 10% of their total programming.
(3) They are exempt from the requirement to provide audited financial statements, instead submitting simpler revenue and expenditure reports annually.
(4) Local broadcasters may receive grants from the Ministry of Culture, up to 50,000 crowns annually, to support local content production, provided they demonstrate at least 50% of their content is locally relevant.

heading: Special Provisions for Local Broadcasters
text:
(1) Local Radio Broadcasters (Category C) are strongly encouraged to focus on local community news, events, and cultural programming for their respective municipalities, including specific coverage for Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, and Grauby.
(2) While still adhering to national content standards, Category C Licensees have a reduced Nordvalean content quota of 15% of their total programming, with at least 5% directly related to local government initiatives.
(3) They are exempt from the requirement to provide audited financial statements, instead submitting simpler revenue and expenditure reports semi-annually by March 31st and September 30th.
(4) Local broadcasters may receive grants from the Ministry of Culture, up to 75,000 crowns annually, to support local content production, provided they demonstrate at least 60% of their content is locally relevant and involves local community members in production.

heading: Repeal of Section 30
text:
(1) The Authority may establish a fund to support the development of innovative broadcasting technologies in Nordvale.
(2) This fund shall be financed by 5% of all Permit fees collected and managed by a dedicated committee within the Authority.
(3) Grants from this fund, not exceeding 200,000 crowns per project, may be awarded to Licensees or other entities for research and development, provided the technology benefits the broader Nordvale broadcasting sector.
(4) Applications for grants must be submitted by June 1st each year, with decisions announced by September 1st. Projects must be completed within 12 months.

heading: Repeal of Section 30
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All existing broadcasting licenses issued prior to this date shall be considered valid for a transitional period of 12 months, during which their holders must apply for a new Permit under the provisions of this Act. Failure to apply within this period will result in the automatic invalidation of their prior licenses. The Authority will publish detailed guidelines for the transition within 60 days of this Act's commencement.

heading: Gymnasium admission for former volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) A person who left the volunteer fire brigade of a municipality after at least 20 years of service pays half of the adult admission fee for a single visit to a municipal gymnasium.
(2) Years of service in more than one brigade are added together.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the issuance, regulation, and oversight of permits required for the installation, modification, and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the orderly development of telecommunications networks, protect public safety, and minimize environmental impact, while promoting efficient service delivery to all citizens. The provisions herein apply to all telecommunications infrastructure projects, whether new installations or upgrades to existing facilities, across all municipalities including Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Infrastructure" means any physical component of a telecommunications network, including but not limited to towers, poles, conduits, cables, antennas, and related equipment.
(b) "Permit" means an official authorization issued by the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority allowing the installation, modification, or maintenance of infrastructure.
(c) "Authority" refers to the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Nordvale.
(d) "Applicant" means any individual or entity applying for a permit under this Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Infrastructure" means any physical component of a telecommunications network, including but not limited to towers, poles, conduits, cables, antennas, and related equipment, specifically excluding residential satellite dishes under 1.5 meters in diameter.
(b) "Permit" means an official authorization issued by the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority allowing the installation, modification, or maintenance of infrastructure.
(c) "Authority" refers to the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Nordvale.
(d) "Applicant" means any individual or entity applying for a permit under this Act or acting on their behalf.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall install, modify, or undertake significant maintenance on any telecommunications infrastructure within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Authority. This requirement applies to all new construction and any alteration affecting more than 15% of the infrastructure's physical dimensions or operational capacity. Minor repairs not affecting structural integrity or operational parameters, lasting less than 24 hours, are exempt from this permit requirement, provided they do not involve public land or major thoroughfares.

heading: Application Submission
text: An applicant for a permit must submit a completed application form, along with all required supporting documents, to the Authority. Applications must be submitted electronically through the official portal. The Authority shall confirm receipt of the application within 5 business days. Incomplete applications will be returned within 10 business days, citing the missing documentation. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is due upon submission.

heading: Application Submission
text: An applicant for a permit must submit a completed application form, along with all required supporting documents, to the Authority. Applications must be submitted electronically through the official portal. The Authority shall confirm receipt of the application within 3 business days. Incomplete applications will be returned within 7 business days, citing the missing documentation. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is due upon submission, payable only via electronic transfer.

heading: Application Content
text:
(1) Every application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications of the proposed infrastructure.
(b) A site plan indicating the precise location, including GPS coordinates, and proximity to residential areas or sensitive environmental zones within a 100-meter radius.
(c) A safety impact assessment.
(d) Proof of financial capability to complete the project, demonstrating at least 50,000 crowns in available capital.
(e) A proposed timeline for construction, not exceeding 180 days.

heading: Application Content
text:
(1) Every application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications of the proposed infrastructure, including material composition.
(b) A site plan indicating the precise location, including GPS coordinates, and proximity to residential areas or sensitive environmental zones within a 150-meter radius.
(c) An updated safety and environmental impact assessment.
(d) Proof of financial capability to complete the project, demonstrating at least 75,000 crowns in available capital.
(e) A proposed timeline for construction, not exceeding 120 days.

heading: Consultation with Municipalities
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Authority shall notify the relevant municipality or municipalities where the infrastructure is proposed to be located. The municipality, such as Corvik or Dunmere, shall have a period of 30 days to provide its feedback or objections to the Authority. This feedback must address local planning regulations, public access, and aesthetic concerns. Failure of a municipality to respond within this period shall be deemed as no objection, allowing the application process to proceed.

heading: Public Notice Requirements
text:
(1) For all new infrastructure installations exceeding 15 meters in height or covering an area greater than 20 square meters, the applicant must publish a public notice.
(2) This notice must be placed in a local newspaper circulated in the relevant municipality and posted visibly at the proposed site for a minimum of 21 days.
(3) The notice shall describe the project and invite public comments to the Authority within 14 days of the notice's first publication.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) An environmental impact assessment is mandatory for all infrastructure projects located within 200 meters of a protected natural reserve or if the project involves ground disturbance exceeding 50 cubic meters.
(2) The assessment must identify potential adverse impacts on local flora and fauna, water sources, and air quality.
(3) The Authority may require additional studies if initial findings suggest significant environmental risks. The cost of this assessment shall be borne entirely by the applicant, estimated at 10,000 crowns for a standard report.

heading: Granting of Permits
text: The Authority shall consider all submitted documentation, municipal feedback, and public comments before making a decision on a permit application. A permit may be granted if the Authority is satisfied that the proposed infrastructure complies with all relevant safety, environmental, and planning regulations. The Authority aims to issue a decision within 60 days of receiving a complete application, provided no significant objections are raised. Decisions on applications for infrastructure in Elsby or Fennick may take an additional 10 days due to geographical considerations.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Every permit issued under this Act shall be subject to conditions deemed necessary by the Authority to ensure public safety, environmental protection, and aesthetic integration.
(2) Standard conditions include adherence to approved plans, regular safety inspections every 12 months, and a requirement to restore the site to its original condition upon decommissioning.
(3) Special conditions may be imposed, such as specific material requirements for structures in Grauby due to wind patterns, or height restrictions not exceeding 30 meters in residential zones.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text:
(1) A permit for new infrastructure is valid for an initial period of 5 years from the date of issuance. Maintenance permits are valid for 2 years.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the permit's expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns.
(3) Renewals are generally granted if the infrastructure remains compliant with current regulations and has not been subject to enforcement actions. Infrastructure in Lund Vale may receive an automatic 6-month extension if located in a remote area.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text:
(1) A permit for new infrastructure is valid for an initial period of 7 years from the date of issuance. Maintenance permits are valid for 3 years.
(2) An application for renewal must be submitted at least 120 days before the permit's expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,500 crowns.
(3) Renewals are generally granted if the infrastructure remains compliant with current regulations and has not been subject to enforcement actions. Infrastructure in Lund Vale may receive an automatic 9-month extension if located in a remote area, upon payment of an additional 250 crowns.

heading: Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee specified in section 4, a permit issuance fee is required upon approval. This fee is calculated based on the project's scale and ranges from 2,000 crowns for minor installations to 15,000 crowns for major infrastructure projects, such as a new tower exceeding 50 meters.
(2) Fees are payable within 30 days of permit approval. Failure to pay will result in the permit being revoked. Projects in Aldmark may incur an additional urban development levy of 5% of the permit issuance fee.

heading: Modification of Infrastructure
text:
(1) Any significant modification to existing infrastructure that alters its physical dimensions by more than 10%, increases its power output by more than 20%, or changes its operational frequency band requires a new permit application.
(2) Minor modifications, such as antenna replacements with identical specifications, are exempt but must be reported to the Authority within 14 days. An administrative fee of 300 crowns applies for such notifications.

heading: Modification of Infrastructure
text:
(1) Any significant modification to existing infrastructure that alters its physical dimensions by more than 5%, increases its power output by more than 15%, or changes its operational frequency band requires a new permit application.
(2) Minor modifications, such as antenna replacements with identical specifications, are exempt but must be reported to the Authority within 7 days. An administrative fee of 500 crowns applies for such notifications, increasing to 750 crowns if reported late.

heading: Maintenance and Safety
text:
(1) All infrastructure owners are responsible for ensuring the safe operation and regular maintenance of their facilities.
(2) Infrastructure must undergo a comprehensive safety audit at least once every 24 months, conducted by a certified inspector. A copy of the audit report must be submitted to the Authority within 30 days of completion.
(3) Failure to comply with safety standards may result in a fine of up to 20,000 crowns.

heading: Decommissioning of Infrastructure
text:
(1) When infrastructure is no longer in use, the permit holder must notify the Authority within 60 days of cessation of operations.
(2) A decommissioning plan, detailing the removal of all physical components and site restoration, must be submitted for approval. Decommissioning must be completed within 180 days of approval of the plan.
(3) The site must be restored to a condition similar to its original state, including the removal of all foundations and ancillary equipment, at the permit holder's expense, which can range from 5,000 to 50,000 crowns depending on the scale.

heading: Right of Appeal
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been denied, or who objects to conditions imposed on a permit, may appeal the decision to the Telecommunications Appeals Board within 28 days of receiving the Authority's decision.
(2) The appeal must be in writing, stating the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 1,200 crowns. The Board shall render a decision within 90 days of receiving a complete appeal submission.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Authority has the power to inspect any telecommunications infrastructure at any reasonable time to ensure compliance with this Act and permit conditions.
(2) If non-compliance is found, the Authority may issue a compliance order, requiring rectification within a specified period, typically 30 days.
(3) In cases of immediate danger to public safety or severe environmental harm, the Authority may order the immediate cessation of operations and removal of infrastructure without prior notice, particularly in sensitive areas like Corvik.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity that installs or operates telecommunications infrastructure without a valid permit commits an offence.
(2) A person or entity that fails to comply with a permit condition or a compliance order issued under section 17 commits an offence.
(3) Upon conviction, an offender is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for a first offence, and up to 100,000 crowns for subsequent offences or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person or entity that installs or operates telecommunications infrastructure without a valid permit commits an offence, subject to section 3.
(2) A person or entity that fails to comply with a permit condition or a compliance order issued under section 17 commits an offence.
(3) Upon conviction, an offender is liable to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns for a first offence, and up to 150,000 crowns for subsequent offences or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 9 months, or both.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) Information provided to the Authority as part of a permit application or compliance report shall be treated with appropriate confidentiality.
(2) However, the Authority may disclose information necessary for public notice, municipal consultation, or in the interest of public safety or environmental protection. Commercial secrets will be protected unless a clear and present danger is identified.
(3) Data classified as sensitive, such as network architecture specifics, will not be publicly released without explicit consent, respecting commercial interests up to 95% of the time.

heading: Exemptions
text: The Authority may grant specific exemptions from certain provisions of this Act in exceptional circumstances, such as during a declared national emergency or for temporary infrastructure required for critical public services for a period not exceeding 90 days. Such exemptions must be formally requested in writing and approved by the Director-General of the Authority, who will review the request within 48 hours. Small, portable communication devices under 5 kilograms are generally exempt from permit requirements.

heading: Research and Development
text: Telecommunications infrastructure solely for research and development purposes, not intended for commercial operation, may be eligible for a simplified permit process. Applicants must demonstrate the non-commercial nature of the project and its potential benefits to Nordvale's technological advancement. Such permits are typically granted for a period of 18 months and carry a reduced application fee of 250 crowns, with a possible extension for another 12 months.

heading: Interference Management
text:
(1) All permit holders must ensure that their infrastructure does not cause harmful interference to other licensed telecommunications services.
(2) In the event of confirmed interference, the permit holder is obliged to take immediate corrective measures, as directed by the Authority, within a timeframe not exceeding 7 days.
(3) Failure to resolve interference issues may result in a temporary suspension of operations and a fine of 10,000 crowns per day of non-compliance. Priority will be given to essential public safety communications, which must be protected at all costs.

heading: Interference Management
text:
(1) All permit holders must ensure that their infrastructure does not cause harmful interference to other licensed telecommunications services, particularly those operating on adjacent frequency bands.
(2) In the event of confirmed interference, the permit holder is obliged to take immediate corrective measures, as directed by the Authority, within a timeframe not exceeding 4 days.
(3) Failure to resolve interference issues may result in a temporary suspension of operations and a fine of 15,000 crowns per day of non-compliance. Priority will be given to essential public safety communications, which must be protected with a reliability of 99.99%.

heading: Emergency Procedures
text:
(1) In cases of natural disaster or other emergencies, the Authority may issue temporary directives to permit holders regarding the operation, modification, or removal of infrastructure.
(2) These directives are binding and aim to facilitate emergency response and restoration of critical communications. Compliance is mandatory within 12 hours of notification.
(3) The Authority will provide support and resources where possible, but the primary responsibility for rapid action lies with the permit holder. Costs incurred by the Authority in emergency situations may be reimbursed by the permit holder, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to maintain accurate and up-to-date records of their infrastructure, including installation dates, maintenance schedules, and any modifications.
(2) These records must be made available to the Authority upon request within 10 business days.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 7 years after the decommissioning of the infrastructure. Electronic records are preferred for efficiency, provided they are securely stored and accessible to the Authority.

heading: Co-location Requirements
text:
(1) The Authority encourages the co-location of telecommunications equipment on existing infrastructure wherever technically feasible and economically reasonable. This minimizes the need for new construction.
(2) New permits for standalone infrastructure may be denied if suitable co-location options exist within a 500-meter radius and are available at market rates, typically not exceeding 30% above the cost of new construction.
(3) Applicants must provide a detailed justification if co-location is not pursued, including at least three alternative sites considered and rejected.

heading: Access to Public Lands
text:
(1) The installation of infrastructure on public lands, including parks and communal areas in municipalities like Dunmere, requires additional approval from the relevant municipal authority.
(2) Such approvals may involve specific conditions regarding land use, public access, and compensation to the municipality, often calculated at 250 crowns per square meter of occupied land per year.
(3) The Authority will coordinate with municipal authorities to streamline this process, but ultimate approval rests with the landowning entity. Construction on public land generally requires a public hearing if the structure exceeds 20 meters in height.

heading: Worker Safety
text:
(1) All work related to the installation, modification, or maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure must comply with the Nordvale Worker Safety Regulations.
(2) Permit holders are responsible for ensuring all personnel are adequately trained and equipped with personal protective equipment. Training records must be verifiable for at least 80% of the workforce.
(3) Any incident resulting in serious injury or fatality must be reported to the Authority and the relevant labor department within 24 hours. Non-compliance can lead to fines of up to 40,000 crowns.

heading: Aesthetic Considerations
text:
(1) The Authority shall consider the visual impact of proposed infrastructure, especially in areas of significant natural beauty or historical importance.
(2) Applicants may be required to implement measures to minimize visual intrusion, such as camouflage, use of specific materials, or reduced height. The cost of these measures is borne by the applicant, typically adding 5% to 15% to the project cost.
(3) In municipalities such as Aldmark, where historical preservation is paramount, structures exceeding 10 meters may face additional scrutiny and stricter aesthetic guidelines.

heading: Infrastructure Sharing
text:
(1) To promote efficient resource utilization, the Authority may, in certain circumstances, mandate infrastructure sharing agreements between permit holders.
(2) This is particularly relevant in areas where land availability is limited or environmental concerns are high. The Authority will mediate disputes over sharing terms, aiming for fair and non-discriminatory access at a cost not exceeding 20% of shared operational expenses.
(3) Any such mandate will specify terms, conditions, and reasonable compensation for the infrastructure owner, ensuring equitable distribution of benefits and burdens.

heading: Annual Reporting
text:
(1) All permit holders must submit an annual report to the Authority by January 31st of each year.
(2) The report must detail the operational status of all permitted infrastructure, compliance with permit conditions, and any significant changes or incidents during the preceding calendar year.
(3) Failure to submit a timely report may result in an administrative penalty of 500 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 3,000 crowns. Reports for infrastructure in areas like Grauby must include specific weather-related structural integrity updates.

heading: Annual Reporting
text:
(1) All permit holders must submit an annual report to the Authority by March 31st of each year.
(2) The report must detail the operational status of all permitted infrastructure, compliance with permit conditions, and any significant changes or incidents during the preceding calendar year, including energy consumption data.
(3) Failure to submit a timely report may result in an administrative penalty of 750 crowns for each month of delay, up to a maximum of 4,500 crowns. Reports for infrastructure in areas like Grauby must include specific weather-related structural integrity updates and wind load calculations for the past 12 months.

heading: Repeal of Old Regulations
text: The Telecommunications Infrastructure Control Act of 1998 is hereby repealed. All permits issued under that Act shall remain valid but are now subject to the provisions of this Act. Any ongoing applications under the repealed Act must be resubmitted under the new provisions within 90 days. All legal proceedings initiated under the repealed Act will continue to be governed by its provisions until their conclusion, unless otherwise determined by a court of law.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any infrastructure installed prior to the commencement of this Act, and not subject to the repealed Act, must apply for a retrospective permit within 180 days of this Act's effective date.
(2) A reduced application fee of 200 crowns shall apply for such retrospective applications. The Authority will prioritize these applications to ensure a smooth transition and full compliance across Nordvale within a 2-year period.
(3) Failure to apply within the specified period will result in the infrastructure being deemed unauthorized and subject to penalties under section 18.

heading: Regulations
text: The Authority may make regulations prescribing all matters that are required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed, or that are necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act. These regulations may include detailed technical standards, specific environmental mitigation measures, and procedures for public consultations. Regulations must be published in the Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before their effective date, allowing for public comment.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. The first review shall commence no later than 2023-01-01. Public submissions and expert opinions will be invited during the review process, with at least 60 days allocated for such consultations. A report on the review's findings and recommendations will be published within 90 days of its conclusion.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 3 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. The first review commenced no later than 2023-01-01. Public submissions and expert opinions will be invited during the review process, with at least 90 days allocated for such consultations. A report on the review's findings and recommendations will be published within 120 days of its conclusion, addressing at least 75% of public feedback received.

heading: Protection of Critical Infrastructure
text:
(1) Infrastructure deemed critical for national security or essential public services, as designated by the Authority, shall receive special protection.
(2) Any proposed construction or activity within 50 meters of such critical infrastructure requires prior consultation with the permit holder and the Authority, even if not directly related to telecommunications.
(3) Damage to critical infrastructure due to negligence may incur fines of up to 250,000 crowns and potential imprisonment, reflecting the severe disruption it can cause to services in municipalities such as Aldmark.

heading: Information Sharing
text: The Authority may enter into agreements with other regulatory bodies or government departments for the purpose of sharing information relevant to the regulation of telecommunications infrastructure. Such agreements will adhere to strict data protection protocols, ensuring that no personal or commercially sensitive information is disclosed without proper authorization. Information shared will primarily pertain to geographical location data and compliance records, supporting inter-agency coordination for up to 90% of relevant data.

heading: Liability
text:
(1) A permit holder is liable for any damage or injury caused by the installation, operation, or decommissioning of their infrastructure.
(2) Permit holders must maintain adequate insurance coverage, with a minimum liability cover of 5,000,000 crowns, to cover potential claims.
(3) The Authority and its employees are not liable for any acts or omissions in good faith in the exercise of their functions under this Act. This protection extends to actions taken to safeguard public interest 99% of the time.

heading: Effective Date
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018.

heading: Section 31
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Day passes for jobseekers
text:
(1) A person who has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least 3 months pays half the price of a day pass on the national buses and trains.
(2) The reduction applies to day passes only, not to single tickets or monthly passes.

heading: Day passes for jobseekers
text:
(1) A person who has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least 2 months pays half the price of a day pass on the national buses and trains.
(2) The reduction applies to day passes only, not to single tickets or monthly passes.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a regulatory framework for the discharge of treated waste into natural water bodies within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to protect and preserve the environmental integrity of rivers, lakes, and coastal waters by ensuring that all discharges meet specific quality standards. This scope applies to industrial, commercial, and municipal entities across all Nordvale municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. The Act mandates that any entity intending to discharge treated waste must first obtain a permit, undergo regular inspections, and adhere to strict effluent limits. Non-compliance will result in penalties, as detailed in subsequent sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Discharge' means the release of any treated waste into a natural water body, whether directly or indirectly.
(2) 'Natural Water Body' includes rivers, streams, lakes, ponds, and coastal waters within Nordvale's jurisdiction, extending up to 12 nautical miles from the coastline.
(3) 'Treated Waste' refers to any liquid effluent that has undergone a purification process to reduce its pollutant content before release.
(4) 'Permit Holder' means an individual or entity granted a Waste Discharge Permit under section 4.
(5) 'Environmental Protection Agency' refers to the national authority responsible for administering and enforcing this Act.

heading: Prohibition of Unpermitted Discharge
text: No person or entity shall discharge any treated waste into a natural water body without a valid Waste Discharge Permit issued by the Environmental Protection Agency. Any discharge occurring without such a permit, or in violation of the terms and conditions of an issued permit, shall be deemed an unlawful discharge. This prohibition applies to all waste streams, regardless of their volume, provided they originate from an industrial, commercial, or municipal source. The maximum volume permitted for discharge without a permit is strictly zero liters.

heading: Application for a Permit
text: An application for a Waste Discharge Permit must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency at least 90 days prior to the planned commencement of any discharge. The application must include detailed information regarding the nature of the waste, the treatment process, the proposed discharge location, and projected effluent quality. A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required. All supporting documentation must be certified by a qualified environmental engineer with at least 5 years of experience. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned within 14 days of receipt.

heading: Permit Application Fee
text: The fee for submitting a Waste Discharge Permit application is 1,500 crowns. This fee is non-refundable and must accompany the application form. Failure to include the correct fee will result in the application being rejected. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the application and conducting initial assessments. No discounts or waivers are available for this fee, regardless of the applicant's size or type of operation.

heading: Permit Application Fee
text: The fee for submitting a Waste Discharge Permit application is 1,800 crowns. This fee is non-refundable and must accompany the application form. Failure to include the correct fee will result in the application being rejected. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the application and conducting initial assessments, including a mandatory site visit for all new applicants. No discounts or waivers are available for this fee, regardless of the applicant's size or type of operation.

heading: Permit Issuance Conditions
text: The Environmental Protection Agency may issue a Waste Discharge Permit if it is satisfied that the proposed discharge will not cause significant harm to the environment or public health. Conditions for issuance include, but are not limited to, compliance with all effluent quality standards set forth in section 8, installation of approved monitoring equipment, and a satisfactory environmental impact assessment. The applicant must demonstrate the capacity to consistently meet discharge limits for at least 95% of operational hours. A permit will only be issued after a minimum 60-day public comment period.

heading: Permit Duration and Renewal
text: A Waste Discharge Permit is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. Permit holders wishing to renew their permit must submit a renewal application at least 120 days before the current permit's expiry date. The renewal application must include updated operational data, a summary of compliance records over the past 5 years, and a renewal fee of 1,000 crowns. Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may result in the permit lapsing and the need to apply for a new permit.

heading: Effluent Quality Standards
text: All treated waste discharged into natural water bodies must comply with the following minimum quality standards: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5) not exceeding 20 mg/L, Total Suspended Solids (TSS) not exceeding 30 mg/L, and pH levels maintained between 6.0 and 9.0. Additional standards for specific pollutants may be imposed based on the receiving water body's sensitivity and designated use. For discharges into coastal waters, fecal coliform counts must not exceed 200 counts per 100 mL for 90% of samples.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting Requirements
text: Permit holders are required to continuously monitor their discharge for all parameters specified in their permit, at a minimum frequency of once per day. Results of this monitoring must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency monthly, by the 15th day of the following month. Annual comprehensive reports, including calibration records for all monitoring equipment, are due by January 31st each year. Any exceedance of permitted effluent limits must be reported immediately, within 24 hours of detection.

heading: Inspection and Access
text: Environmental Protection Agency officers are authorized to enter and inspect any premises where waste treatment or discharge activities occur, at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice. This includes access to all relevant records, monitoring equipment, and discharge points. Permit holders must grant full cooperation to inspectors and provide all requested information. Refusal to grant access or obstruction of an inspection is an offense under this Act and may lead to permit revocation.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Environmental Protection Agency has the power to issue compliance orders, impose administrative penalties, suspend or revoke permits, and initiate legal proceedings for violations of this Act. In cases of imminent environmental harm, the Agency may issue an immediate cessation order for any discharge activity. These powers are designed to ensure adherence to permit conditions and the overall objectives of environmental protection.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text: Any person or entity found in violation of a provision of this Act or a condition of their permit may be subject to an administrative penalty of up to 50,000 crowns per day for each day the violation continues. For minor reporting infringements, a penalty of 5,000 crowns may be levied. Repeated violations within a 12-month period will incur a 25% increase in the daily penalty amount. Penalties are determined based on the severity and duration of the offense.

heading: Permit Suspension and Revocation
text: A Waste Discharge Permit may be suspended for up to 90 days for persistent non-compliance with permit conditions or repeated violations of effluent standards. Revocation of a permit may occur in cases of serious environmental damage, fraud in the application process, or failure to comply with a suspension order. Before suspension or revocation, the permit holder will be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to present their case. A revoked permit means immediate cessation of all discharge activities.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any person or entity aggrieved by a decision of the Environmental Protection Agency, including the refusal to issue a permit, imposition of a penalty, or suspension/revocation of a permit, may appeal the decision. An appeal must be lodged with the Environmental Appeals Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the Agency's decision. The Tribunal's decision is binding, though further judicial review may be sought in the Nordvale High Court within 30 days of the Tribunal's ruling.

heading: Public Register
text: The Environmental Protection Agency shall maintain a public register of all Waste Discharge Permits issued, renewed, suspended, or revoked under this Act. This register will include details of permit holders, discharge locations, effluent limits, and any enforcement actions taken. The register shall be accessible to the public both physically at the Agency's main office in Aldmark and electronically via the official Nordvale government website. Information will be updated monthly.

heading: Emergency Discharges
text: In the event of an emergency that necessitates an unplanned discharge of treated waste, the permit holder must notify the Environmental Protection Agency within 2 hours of the incident. A detailed written report explaining the cause of the emergency, the volume and nature of the discharge, and remedial actions taken must be submitted within 7 days. Such discharges must be minimized in volume and duration, and every effort must be made to mitigate environmental impact. Failure to report promptly may result in penalties.

heading: Discharge Point Marking
text: All authorized discharge points must be clearly marked with a permanent, visible sign indicating the permit holder's name and permit number. The sign must be legible from a distance of at least 5 meters and maintained in good condition. The markings must be resistant to weather and vandalism. Unmarked discharge points are considered a violation of this Act and may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns per unmarked point. This ensures transparency and aids in monitoring efforts.

heading: Sampling Requirements
text: Permit holders must collect effluent samples using standardized methods approved by the Environmental Protection Agency. Samples must be collected at representative discharge points and analyzed by accredited laboratories. A minimum of 3 samples per week is required for facilities discharging more than 1,000 cubic meters per day. For smaller facilities, weekly sampling is acceptable. All samples must be analyzed within 24 hours of collection for immediate parameters. Duplicate samples must be retained for at least 7 days.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: While the public register contains much information, certain commercially sensitive data submitted by permit holders may be deemed confidential by the Environmental Protection Agency. Applicants seeking confidentiality for specific parts of their application or reports must clearly mark such information and provide justification. The Agency will review such requests and make a determination within 30 days. However, information related to effluent quality and compliance records will never be considered confidential.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the operation and maintenance of waste treatment facilities and discharge processes must undergo regular training. This training must cover permit conditions, operational procedures, emergency response protocols, and environmental best practices. A minimum of 8 hours of refresher training is required annually for all relevant staff. Records of all training conducted, including dates and attendees, must be kept on site and made available during inspections.

heading: Review of Effluent Standards
text: The Environmental Protection Agency shall review the effluent quality standards specified in section 8 at least once every 3 years. This review will take into account advancements in waste treatment technology, changes in environmental conditions, and international best practices. Public consultation will be a mandatory part of any review process, with at least 90 days provided for feedback before new standards are implemented. Any changes will be announced at least 6 months in advance of their effective date.

heading: Permit Transferability
text: A Waste Discharge Permit is generally non-transferable. However, in cases of a change of ownership or control of the permitted facility, the new owner may apply to transfer the existing permit. This application must be submitted within 60 days of the change of ownership and include documentation of the new entity's technical and financial capacity to comply with the permit. A transfer fee of 750 crowns is applicable. The Environmental Protection Agency reserves the right to deny a transfer if concerns about compliance arise.

heading: Permit Modification
text: Permit holders wishing to make significant changes to their waste treatment process, discharge volume, or effluent characteristics must apply for a permit modification. A 'significant change' is defined as any alteration resulting in a 10% or greater increase in pollutant load or discharge volume. The application for modification must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the proposed change and will be subject to a review process similar to an initial application. A modification fee of 500 crowns is required.

heading: Baseline Data Submission
text: New applicants for a Waste Discharge Permit must submit comprehensive baseline data regarding the water quality of the receiving natural water body. This data must be collected over a minimum period of 6 months prior to the application date and include at least 15 distinct sampling events. The purpose of this data is to establish a clear understanding of the existing environmental conditions before any new discharge commences. This aids in assessing potential impacts and setting appropriate permit limits.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: For facilities discharging more than 5,000 cubic meters per day, the Environmental Protection Agency may require the permit holder to provide financial assurance. This assurance, which could be a bond or trust fund, must be sufficient to cover the estimated costs of environmental remediation in the event of a catastrophic discharge or permit holder default. The amount of financial assurance will be determined on a case-by-case basis, but will not exceed 2,000,000 crowns. This ensures public funds are not used for clean-up.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: For facilities discharging more than 4,000 cubic meters per day, the Environmental Protection Agency may require the permit holder to provide financial assurance. This assurance, which could be a bond or trust fund, must be sufficient to cover the estimated costs of environmental remediation in the event of a catastrophic discharge or permit holder default. The amount of financial assurance will be determined on a case-by-case basis, but will not exceed 2,500,000 crowns. This ensures public funds are not used for clean-up and encourages responsible operation.

heading: Best Available Technology Requirement
text: All permit holders are required to utilize the Best Available Technology (BAT) that is economically achievable for the treatment of their waste prior to discharge. The Environmental Protection Agency will periodically publish guidelines on what constitutes BAT for various industries. Non-compliance with this requirement, even if effluent limits are met, may lead to an order for upgrade. New facilities must demonstrate the use of BAT in their permit application. Existing facilities have 5 years to adopt new BAT standards.

heading: Preventative Measures
text: Permit holders must implement preventative measures to minimize the risk of accidental discharges or system failures. This includes regular maintenance of treatment infrastructure, development of spill prevention plans, and employee training on emergency procedures. A preventative maintenance schedule must be submitted annually to the Environmental Protection Agency for review. Facilities with a history of more than two accidental discharges in a 24-month period will be subject to mandatory external audits.

heading: Water Quality Objectives
text: The Environmental Protection Agency shall establish specific water quality objectives for all major natural water bodies in Nordvale. These objectives define the desired state of water quality and serve as a benchmark for assessing the cumulative impact of all permitted discharges. Permit limits for individual facilities will be set to ensure that these overall water quality objectives are met and maintained. Objectives are reviewed every 5 years, with the next review scheduled for 2027.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Environmental Protection Agency may fund or support research and development initiatives aimed at improving waste treatment technologies and monitoring methods. A budget of 5,000,000 crowns is allocated annually for this purpose. Permit holders are encouraged to participate in such initiatives or conduct their own research into more sustainable discharge practices. Successful implementation of new technologies may lead to favorable consideration during permit renewals.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Environmental Protection Agency may fund or support research and development initiatives aimed at improving waste treatment technologies and monitoring methods. A budget of 7,500,000 crowns is allocated annually for this purpose, with a minimum of 20% dedicated to small and medium-sized enterprises. Permit holders are encouraged to participate in such initiatives or conduct their own research into more sustainable discharge practices. Successful implementation of new technologies may lead to favorable consideration during permit renewals or reduced renewal fees.

heading: Discharge into Sensitive Areas
text: Discharges into environmentally sensitive areas, such as designated wildlife habitats or protected conservation zones, are subject to stricter permit conditions and lower effluent limits. The Environmental Protection Agency maintains a list of all sensitive areas, updated biannually. A permit for discharge into such an area will only be granted if it can be demonstrated that there will be zero net negative impact on the ecosystem. The application fee for such a permit is 3,000 crowns, reflecting the increased scrutiny.

heading: Discharge into Sensitive Areas
text: Discharges into environmentally sensitive areas, such as designated wildlife habitats or protected conservation zones, are subject to stricter permit conditions and lower effluent limits. The Environmental Protection Agency maintains a list of all sensitive areas, updated annually. A permit for discharge into such an area will only be granted if it can be demonstrated that there will be zero net negative impact on the ecosystem, supported by a 12-month pre-discharge monitoring program. The application fee for such a permit is 3,500 crowns, reflecting the increased scrutiny and assessment requirements.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Existing entities that were discharging treated waste prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for a Waste Discharge Permit within 180 days of the Act's commencement. During this transitional period, existing discharges may continue, provided they do not cause immediate and severe environmental harm. Failure to submit an application within this timeframe will result in the immediate prohibition of further discharge and potential penalties. The Environmental Protection Agency will prioritize these initial applications.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text: The Environmental Protection Agency shall cooperate closely with municipal authorities in all matters related to waste discharge. This includes sharing information, coordinating inspections, and assisting in the enforcement of local bylaws that complement this Act. Local authorities in areas like Dunmere and Elsby are encouraged to report any suspected unpermitted discharges to the Agency. Joint training programs for environmental officers from both national and municipal levels will be conducted biannually.

heading: Reporting Public Concerns
text: Any member of the public may report concerns about waste discharge activities to the Environmental Protection Agency. Reports can be submitted anonymously and will be investigated within 10 working days. The Agency shall establish a dedicated hotline and an online portal for receiving such reports. Complainants will be provided with a reference number and, if they provide contact details, will receive an update on the investigation within 30 days. All reports are taken seriously and contribute to environmental oversight.

heading: Penalties for False Information
text: Any person or entity that knowingly provides false or misleading information in an application, report, or during an inspection commits an offense under this Act. Such an offense may result in a fine of up to 100,000 crowns, imprisonment for up to 2 years, or both. In addition, any permit issued based on false information will be immediately revoked, and the permit holder will be barred from applying for a new permit for a period of 5 years. Integrity in reporting is paramount for effective regulation.

heading: Cost Recovery for Remediation
text: If the Environmental Protection Agency undertakes remediation efforts due to an unlawful discharge or a discharge causing significant environmental harm, the costs of such remediation shall be recovered from the responsible party. These costs include, but are not limited to, assessment, clean-up, and restoration expenses. The Agency may place a lien on the responsible party's property to secure the recovery of these costs. Interest at 5% per annum will be applied to all outstanding amounts after 90 days.

heading: Delegation of Powers
text: The Director of the Environmental Protection Agency may delegate any of the powers or duties conferred upon them by this Act to any officer or employee of the Agency. Any such delegation must be in writing and specify the extent and limitations of the delegated authority. However, the power to revoke a permit or impose a penalty exceeding 20,000 crowns cannot be delegated to an officer below the level of a senior environmental manager. The Director remains ultimately accountable for all actions taken.

heading: Reporting of Infrastructure Failures
text: Permit holders must report any significant infrastructure failure at their waste treatment facility that could potentially lead to an unpermitted discharge. This includes failures of pumps, filters, containment structures, or monitoring equipment. The report must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency within 48 hours of detection and include an estimated timeframe for repair and mitigation strategies. Failure to report such incidents within the specified period may result in an administrative penalty of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Infrastructure Failures
text: Permit holders must report any significant infrastructure failure at their waste treatment facility that could potentially lead to an unpermitted discharge. This includes failures of pumps, filters, containment structures, or monitoring equipment. The report must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency within 24 hours of detection and include an estimated timeframe for repair and mitigation strategies, alongside a detailed risk assessment. Failure to report such incidents within the specified period may result in an administrative penalty of 15,000 crowns. Urgent repairs must be completed within 72 hours.

heading: Annual Environmental Audits
text: All facilities discharging more than 2,000 cubic meters per day must undergo an independent environmental audit annually. The audit must be conducted by a certified auditor not affiliated with the permit holder and cover compliance with permit conditions, operational procedures, and environmental management systems. A copy of the audit report must be submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency within 30 days of its completion. The cost of the audit is borne by the permit holder.

heading: Requirements for Minor Discharges
text: Facilities discharging less than 50 cubic meters of treated waste per day may be eligible for a simplified permit application process. While still requiring a permit, these facilities will have reduced monitoring frequencies (monthly reporting instead of weekly) and a lower annual permit fee of 500 crowns. However, they must still comply with all effluent quality standards and reporting requirements for any exceedances. This streamlined approach aims to ease the burden on smaller operations while maintaining environmental protection.

heading: Requirements for Minor Discharges
text: Facilities discharging less than 40 cubic meters of treated waste per day may be eligible for a simplified permit application process. While still requiring a permit, these facilities will have reduced monitoring frequencies (quarterly reporting instead of monthly) and a lower annual permit fee of 400 crowns. However, they must still comply with all effluent quality standards and reporting requirements for any exceedances. This streamlined approach aims to ease the burden on smaller operations while maintaining environmental protection, particularly in rural areas like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Pollution Prevention Plans
text: All permit holders must develop and implement a Pollution Prevention Plan aimed at reducing the generation of waste at its source. The plan must identify opportunities for waste reduction, reuse, and recycling, and set measurable targets for reduction. The plan must be reviewed and updated every 2 years and submitted to the Environmental Protection Agency. Facilities demonstrating significant waste reduction (e.g., 15% reduction over 3 years) may be eligible for a 10% reduction in their permit renewal fee.

heading: Annual Fees
text: In addition to the permit application and renewal fees, permit holders are required to pay an annual fee based on their discharge volume and pollutant load. The minimum annual fee is 1,000 crowns for discharges under 100 cubic meters per day, and can reach up to 50,000 crowns for large industrial facilities. These fees contribute to the operational costs of the Environmental Protection Agency, including monitoring, enforcement, and research. Invoices are issued on January 1st and due by February 28th.

heading: Public Consultation on New Standards
text: Before new effluent quality standards are introduced or existing standards are significantly altered, the Environmental Protection Agency must conduct a public consultation process. This process will include publishing proposed changes, holding public meetings in affected municipalities (e.g., Fennick, Corvik), and providing a minimum 90-day period for written submissions from all interested parties, including industry, environmental groups, and the general public. All feedback received will be considered before final decisions are made.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Permit holders must maintain accurate and comprehensive records of all monitoring data, operational logs, maintenance schedules, incident reports, and training records for a minimum period of 5 years. These records must be readily accessible for inspection by Environmental Protection Agency officers. Digital records are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and backed up regularly. Failure to produce requested records during an inspection may result in a penalty of 3,000 crowns per missing record set.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of this Act is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions or parts of the Act shall remain in full force and effect. The invalidity of one section shall not affect the validity of other sections. This ensures that the core objectives of environmental protection through waste discharge permitting are maintained even if minor legal challenges arise regarding specific clauses.

heading: Offences by Corporate Bodies
text: Where an offense under this Act is committed by a corporate body, any director, manager, secretary, or other similar officer of the corporate body, or any person purporting to act in any such capacity, shall also be deemed to have committed the offense if it is proved that the offense was committed with their consent or connivance, or is attributable to any neglect on their part. This ensures accountability extends beyond the corporate entity to individuals in leadership roles within companies operating in Aldmark or elsewhere.

heading: Regulations
text: The Environmental Protection Agency may make regulations for the better carrying out of the provisions of this Act. These regulations may specify further details regarding permit application procedures, monitoring protocols, effluent quality standards, penalty calculations, and any other matters deemed necessary for effective implementation. All regulations must undergo a minimum 60-day public comment period before being gazetted. They must not contradict the primary provisions of this Act.

heading: Repeal of Earlier Acts
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Repeal of Earlier Acts
text: The Environmental Protection Act of 1995, specifically sections 7 to 14 concerning water pollution, is hereby repealed. All provisions of that Act related to waste discharge into natural water bodies are superseded by this Act. Any permits issued under the repealed Act remain valid until their natural expiry date, at which point renewal will be subject to the provisions of this Act. This ensures a seamless transition to the new regulatory framework.

heading: Payment terms
text: Each registered violin maker pays a fixed five crowns for all paper copies requested from a municipality, regardless of the number of pages.

heading: Exemptions
text: Each registered violin maker pays a signage permit fee reduced by one-quarter.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the tolls charged for the use of the toll roads of Nordvale and the penalties for not paying them.
(2) The toll roads are the M1 motorway between Aldmark and Brenholt, the Corvik Bridge and the Dunmere Tunnel.
(3) All tolls are paid in crowns to the Toll Authority.

heading: Toll for cars on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a car on the M1 motorway is 6 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A car with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for cars on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a car on the M1 motorway is 7 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A car with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for motorcycles on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a motorcycle on the M1 motorway is 3 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A motorcycle with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for motorcycles on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a motorcycle on the M1 motorway is 4 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A motorcycle with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for light goods vehicles on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a goods vehicle with a total weight of up to 3.5 tonnes on the M1 motorway is 9 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A goods vehicle with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for light goods vehicles on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a goods vehicle with a total weight of up to 3.5 tonnes on the M1 motorway is 10 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A goods vehicle with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for heavy goods vehicles on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a goods vehicle with a total weight above 3.5 tonnes on the M1 motorway is 18 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A heavy goods vehicle with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for heavy goods vehicles on the M1
text:
(1) The toll for a goods vehicle with a total weight above 3.5 tonnes on the M1 motorway is 21 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged once for each direction of travel.
(3) A heavy goods vehicle with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for cars on the Corvik Bridge
text:
(1) The toll for a car on the Corvik Bridge is 4 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged in both directions of travel.
(3) A car with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for cars on the Corvik Bridge
text:
(1) The toll for a car on the Corvik Bridge is 5 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged in both directions of travel.
(3) A car with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for cars in the Dunmere Tunnel
text:
(1) The toll for a car in the Dunmere Tunnel is 5 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged in both directions of travel.
(3) A car with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for cars in the Dunmere Tunnel
text:
(1) The toll for a car in the Dunmere Tunnel is 6 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll is charged in both directions of travel.
(3) A car with a trailer also pays the surcharge in section 9.

heading: Toll for motorcycles on the Corvik Bridge and in the Dunmere Tunnel
text:
(1) The toll for a motorcycle on the Corvik Bridge is 2 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll for a motorcycle in the Dunmere Tunnel is 3 crowns for each passage.
(3) The tolls are charged in both directions of travel.

heading: Toll for motorcycles on the Corvik Bridge and in the Dunmere Tunnel
text:
(1) The toll for a motorcycle on the Corvik Bridge is 3 crowns for each passage.
(2) The toll for a motorcycle in the Dunmere Tunnel is 4 crowns for each passage.
(3) The tolls are charged in both directions of travel.

heading: Trailer surcharge
text:
(1) A vehicle that pulls a trailer pays a surcharge of 50 percent of the toll for the vehicle.
(2) The surcharge is rounded up to the next full crown.
(3) The surcharge applies on all toll roads.

heading: Trailer surcharge
text:
(1) A vehicle that pulls a trailer pays a surcharge of 60 percent of the toll for the vehicle.
(2) The surcharge is rounded up to the next full crown.
(3) The surcharge applies on all toll roads.

heading: Annual pass for cars
text:
(1) The owner of a car may buy an annual pass for 600 crowns.
(2) The pass allows unlimited passages on the M1 motorway, the Corvik Bridge and the Dunmere Tunnel for 12 months.
(3) The pass is tied to one registration number.

heading: Annual pass for cars
text:
(1) The owner of a car may buy an annual pass for 650 crowns.
(2) The pass allows unlimited passages on the M1 motorway, the Corvik Bridge and the Dunmere Tunnel for 12 months.
(3) The pass is tied to one registration number.

heading: Passes only for cars
text:
(1) Annual passes and monthly passes are sold for cars only.
(2) A motorcycle, a goods vehicle or a vehicle with a trailer cannot use a pass.
(3) A vehicle that pulls a trailer with a pass pays the trailer surcharge for each passage.

heading: Monthly pass for cars
text:
(1) The owner of a car may buy a monthly pass for 70 crowns.
(2) The pass allows unlimited passages on the M1 motorway, the Corvik Bridge and the Dunmere Tunnel for one calendar month.
(3) The pass is tied to one registration number.

heading: Monthly pass for cars
text:
(1) The owner of a car may buy a monthly pass for 75 crowns.
(2) The pass allows unlimited passages on the M1 motorway, the Corvik Bridge and the Dunmere Tunnel for one calendar month.
(3) The pass is tied to one registration number.

heading: Payment deadline
text:
(1) A toll must be paid within 7 days after the passage.
(2) The toll may be paid online, at a service point or by direct debit.
(3) A toll that is paid late is subject to the fee in section 14.

heading: Payment deadline
text:
(1) A toll must be paid within 10 days after the passage.
(2) The toll may be paid online, at a service point or by direct debit.
(3) A toll that is paid late is subject to the fee in section 14.

heading: Late payment fee
text:
(1) A person who pays a toll after the deadline shall pay a late fee of 15 crowns for each unpaid toll.
(2) The late fee is added to the toll.
(3) The late fee is not charged if the toll is paid within 3 days of the deadline.

heading: Late payment fee
text:
(1) A person who pays a toll after the deadline shall pay a late fee of 20 crowns for each unpaid toll.
(2) The late fee is added to the toll.
(3) The late fee is not charged if the toll is paid within 3 days of the deadline.

heading: Fine for unpaid tolls
text:
(1) A person who has not paid a toll within 30 days after the passage shall pay a fine of 60 crowns for each unpaid toll.
(2) The fine replaces the late fee in section 14.
(3) The fine is added to the toll.

heading: Fine for unpaid tolls
text:
(1) A person who has not paid a toll within 30 days after the passage shall pay a fine of 75 crowns for each unpaid toll.
(2) The fine replaces the late fee in section 14.
(3) The fine is added to the toll.

heading: Emergency vehicles
text:
(1) Ambulances, fire engines and police vehicles on duty pass free of toll.
(2) A vehicle of these services that is not on duty pays the toll for its class.
(3) The service concerned shall keep a record of passages that are free of toll.

heading: Night discount
text:
(1) The toll for a passage between 22:00 and 05:00 is reduced by 25 percent.
(2) The reduction applies to all toll roads.
(3) The reduction is rounded down to the next full crown.

heading: Night discount
text:
(1) The toll for a passage between 22:00 and 05:00 is reduced by 30 percent.
(2) The reduction applies to all toll roads.
(3) The reduction is rounded down to the next full crown.

heading: Frequent user discount
text:
(1) A person who makes more than 40 passages with the same car in a calendar month pays 50 percent of the toll for each further passage in that month.
(2) The discount applies on all toll roads together.
(3) The discount is not available to holders of a pass.

heading: Frequent user discount
text:
(1) A person who makes more than 40 passages with the same car in a calendar month pays 40 percent of the toll for each further passage in that month.
(2) The discount applies on all toll roads together.
(3) The discount is not available to holders of a pass.

heading: Weekend surcharge
text:
(1) A toll for a passage on a Saturday or Sunday is increased by 1 crown.
(2) The surcharge applies to cars only.
(3) The surcharge is not charged to holders of an annual pass.

heading: Weekend surcharge
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Toll signs
text:
(1) The Toll Authority shall place a sign at least 500 metres before each toll point.
(2) The sign must show the toll for a car.
(3) A toll may not be charged on a road without such a sign.

heading: Review of tolls
text:
(1) The Toll Authority shall review the tolls at least once every 3 years.
(2) The review shall be published on the Toll Authority website.
(3) The review does not change a toll unless the law is amended.

heading: Corvik Bridge for long-serving coastal post staff
text: A person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 and spent at least 180 nights at the post in the previous calendar year crosses the Corvik Bridge by car without paying the toll.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable to the Nordvale Agricultural Office for the submission of applications related to various agricultural grants and subsidies. The purpose is to cover administrative costs associated with processing these applications and to ensure efficient resource allocation. The scope of this Act extends to all agricultural producers, cooperatives, and related entities seeking financial assistance through government programs. All fees outlined herein are non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the application. The Nordvale Agricultural Office maintains the right to adjust these fees periodically, with due public notification issued at least 30 days prior to any change taking effect.

heading: Basic Application Fee for General Agricultural Grant
text: An applicant for the General Agricultural Grant must pay a basic application fee of 250 crowns. This fee covers initial processing, data entry, and a preliminary review of the application for completeness. The fee is payable at the time of submission and must accompany the application form. Failure to include the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant without further processing. This fee is separate from any additional fees that may be applicable for specific grant components or expedited review services, which are detailed in subsequent sections of this Act.

heading: Application Fee for Small Farm Development Grant
text: Applicants seeking the Small Farm Development Grant are required to pay an application fee of 150 crowns. This reduced fee acknowledges the economic circumstances often faced by smaller farming operations. To qualify for this fee, a farm must demonstrate annual agricultural revenue of less than 500,000 crowns for the preceding fiscal year and operate on less than 20 hectares of land. The Nordvale Agricultural Office reserves the right to request documentation to verify these criteria, such as tax records or land deeds, as part of the application process. This fee is designed to support the growth of smaller agricultural enterprises.

heading: Application Fee for Sustainable Farming Initiative
text: An application for the Sustainable Farming Initiative requires a fee of 300 crowns. This initiative supports practices that enhance environmental stewardship and resource conservation. The fee covers the review of detailed plans for sustainability, including soil health management, water conservation strategies, and biodiversity protection measures. Applications must include a comprehensive report outlining the proposed sustainable practices and their expected environmental benefits. The Nordvale Agricultural Office may conduct site visits as part of the evaluation process, and this fee contributes to the cost of such assessments. This grant encourages long-term ecological balance in agricultural operations.

heading: Application Fee for Sustainable Farming Initiative
text: An application for the Sustainable Farming Initiative requires a fee of 350 crowns. This initiative supports practices that enhance environmental stewardship and resource conservation. The fee covers the review of detailed plans for sustainability, including soil health management, water conservation strategies, and biodiversity protection measures. Applications must include a comprehensive report outlining the proposed sustainable practices and their expected environmental benefits. The Nordvale Agricultural Office may conduct site visits as part of the evaluation process, and this fee contributes to the cost of such assessments. This grant encourages long-term ecological balance in agricultural operations.

heading: Application Fee for Sustainable Farming Initiative
text: An application for the Sustainable Farming Initiative requires a fee of 380 crowns. This initiative supports practices that enhance environmental stewardship and resource conservation. The fee covers the review of detailed plans for sustainability, including soil health management, water conservation strategies, and biodiversity protection measures. Applications must include a comprehensive report outlining the proposed sustainable practices and their expected environmental benefits. The Nordvale Agricultural Office may conduct site visits as part of the evaluation process, and this fee contributes to the cost of such assessments. This grant encourages long-term ecological balance in agricultural operations.

heading: Application Fee for Livestock Support Program
text: The application fee for the Livestock Support Program is 200 crowns. This program aims to assist livestock producers in maintaining healthy herds and improving infrastructure. The fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing herd management plans, facility improvement proposals, and animal welfare compliance. Applicants must provide details on the type and number of livestock, as well as any proposed investments in equipment or facilities. The Nordvale Agricultural Office may require inspection reports from relevant veterinary authorities as part of the application. This fee helps ensure the proper review of proposals for livestock well-being.

heading: Application Fee for Crop Diversification Grant
text: A fee of 220 crowns is required for applications to the Crop Diversification Grant. This grant encourages farmers to expand their range of crops, reducing reliance on monoculture and promoting agricultural resilience. The fee covers the review of proposed crop rotations, market analyses for new crops, and plans for implementation. Applicants must demonstrate a clear strategy for integrating new crops into their existing farming operations. The Nordvale Agricultural Office prioritizes applications that propose the introduction of at least three new crop types or an increase in cultivated area for existing diverse crops by at least 15%. This fee supports agricultural innovation.

heading: Application Fee for Agricultural Innovation Fund
text: The application fee for the Agricultural Innovation Fund is 400 crowns. This fund provides support for pioneering projects that introduce new technologies or methodologies to the agricultural sector. The fee covers the rigorous evaluation of complex proposals, including feasibility studies, projected economic impacts, and technological assessments. Applicants must submit a detailed project plan, a budget exceeding 100,000 crowns, and a timeline for implementation, typically not exceeding 24 months.
