The Nordvale Agricultural Office may engage external experts for specialized reviews, and this fee contributes to those costs. This fund drives progress in agricultural practices.

heading: Expedited Review Service Fee
text: Applicants may opt for an expedited review of their grant application for an additional fee of 500 crowns. This service guarantees a preliminary decision within 15 working days of a complete application being received, compared to the standard 45 working days. This expedited fee is supplementary to any other applicable application fees. Not all grants are eligible for expedited review; applicants should consult the Nordvale Agricultural Office guidelines for specific program eligibility. The availability of this service is dependent on current staff workload and processing capacity, and the Office reserves the right to temporarily suspend this option with 7 days' notice.

heading: Late Submission Fee
text: Applications submitted after the official deadline will incur a late submission fee of 100 crowns, in addition to the standard application fee. This fee applies to all grant programs unless explicitly stated otherwise in the specific grant guidelines. An application is considered late if its timestamp or postmark indicates submission after 17:00 on the advertised deadline date. The Nordvale Agricultural Office will not accept applications submitted more than 10 working days after the deadline, regardless of whether the late fee is paid. This policy ensures fairness and efficient processing within established timelines for all applicants.

heading: Fee for Amendment to Submitted Application
text: A fee of 75 crowns is payable for any substantial amendment requested by the applicant after an application has been formally submitted and processing has commenced. Minor corrections, such as typographical errors, generally do not incur this fee. A substantial amendment includes changes to proposed project scope, budget adjustments exceeding 10% of the original amount, or changes in the primary applicant. This fee covers the administrative effort required to re-evaluate revised information and update records. Amendments must be submitted in writing and clearly detail the changes from the original submission. Only one such amendment is permitted per application.

heading: Fee for Request for Reconsideration
text: Applicants who wish to request a reconsideration of a denied grant application must pay a fee of 120 crowns. This fee covers the cost of a secondary review by a different panel of assessors to ensure fairness and accuracy in the initial decision. A request for reconsideration must be submitted within 30 days of receiving the denial notification and must include new information or a clear explanation of how the initial assessment may have overlooked critical details. The Nordvale Agricultural Office will not reconsider decisions if no new substantive information is provided. This process aims to provide an additional layer of scrutiny.

heading: Fee for Documentation Duplication
text: A fee of 50 crowns per set is charged for the duplication of application documents or related correspondence upon an applicant's request, beyond the standard single copy provided. This fee covers printing, copying, and administrative handling. Requests for duplication must be made in writing and specify the exact documents required. The Nordvale Agricultural Office aims to fulfill such requests within 5 working days. This fee ensures that resources are allocated efficiently for additional document reproduction services. For extensive duplication requests involving more than 50 pages, an additional per-page charge of 5 crowns may apply.

heading: Fee for Digital Application Submission Support
text: Applicants requiring personalized assistance with digital submission of their grant applications may opt for the Digital Application Submission Support service at a fee of 80 crowns. This service includes a guided walkthrough of the online portal and assistance with uploading documents, provided by a Nordvale Agricultural Office staff member. This support is available by appointment only and is limited to one hour per applicant. This fee covers the staff time and resources dedicated to facilitating digital submissions for those less familiar with online processes. It does not include assistance with preparing the content of the application itself.

heading: Application Fee for Organic Certification Grant
text: An application for the Organic Certification Grant requires a fee of 280 crowns. This grant supports farmers transitioning to or maintaining organic certification for their produce. The fee covers the review of organic farm plans, adherence to organic standards, and certification body reports. Applicants must provide evidence of their current or pending organic certification status from an accredited body. The Nordvale Agricultural Office will assess how the grant funds will be utilized to further organic practices or offset certification costs. This fee contributes to the promotion and verification of organic agricultural methods within Nordvale.

heading: Application Fee for Water Management Grant
text: The application fee for the Water Management Grant is 270 crowns. This grant assists farmers in implementing efficient water use and conservation strategies. The fee covers the review of irrigation plans, water harvesting projects, and drought mitigation proposals. Applicants must submit a detailed water management plan outlining existing water sources, proposed improvements, and expected water savings, typically aiming for at least a 20% reduction in usage. The Nordvale Agricultural Office may conduct site assessments to verify the feasibility and impact of proposed projects. This fee supports critical efforts to preserve Nordvale's water resources for agriculture.

heading: Application Fee for Water Management Grant
text: The application fee for the Water Management Grant is 290 crowns. This grant assists farmers in implementing efficient water use and conservation strategies. The fee covers the review of irrigation plans, water harvesting projects, and drought mitigation proposals. Applicants must submit a detailed water management plan outlining existing water sources, proposed improvements, and expected water savings, typically aiming for at least a 25% reduction in usage. The Nordvale Agricultural Office may conduct site assessments to verify the feasibility and impact of proposed projects. This fee supports critical efforts to preserve Nordvale's water resources for agriculture.

heading: Application Fee for Water Management Grant
text: The application fee for the Water Management Grant is 310 crowns. This grant assists farmers in implementing efficient water use and conservation strategies. The fee covers the review of irrigation plans, water harvesting projects, and drought mitigation proposals. Applicants must submit a detailed water management plan outlining existing water sources, proposed improvements, and expected water savings, typically aiming for at least a 30% reduction in usage. The Nordvale Agricultural Office may conduct site assessments to verify the feasibility and impact of proposed projects. This fee supports critical efforts to preserve Nordvale's water resources for agriculture.

heading: Application Fee for Soil Improvement Grant
text: A fee of 230 crowns applies to applications for the Soil Improvement Grant. This grant encourages practices that enhance soil health, fertility, and structure. The fee covers the evaluation of proposed soil amendments, cover cropping plans, and erosion control measures. Applicants must provide baseline soil analysis reports and outline expected improvements, such as an increase in organic matter by at least 0.5% over a three-year period. The Nordvale Agricultural Office reviews these plans to ensure they align with best practices for sustainable soil management. This fee supports the long-term productivity and health of agricultural land.

heading: Application Fee for Young Farmer Establishment Grant
text: The application fee for the Young Farmer Establishment Grant is 180 crowns. This grant is designed to support individuals aged 18 to 40 who are establishing their first independent agricultural operation. The fee covers the review of business plans, financial projections, and proof of agricultural education or experience. Applicants must demonstrate a clear intent to dedicate at least 75% of their working time to the farm and own or lease at least 5 hectares of land. The Nordvale Agricultural Office prioritizes applications that show strong potential for long-term viability. This fee helps foster the next generation of agricultural leaders.

heading: Application Fee for Regional Agricultural Development Grant
text: An application for the Regional Agricultural Development Grant incurs a fee of 320 crowns. This grant supports projects that benefit a specific agricultural region or community, rather than individual farms, such as shared equipment facilities or cooperative marketing initiatives. The fee covers the review of complex proposals involving multiple stakeholders, economic impact assessments for the region, and governance structures for cooperative projects. Applicants must demonstrate broad community support, with at least 5 participating farms or agricultural businesses. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the potential for widespread regional benefit. This fee supports collaborative agricultural growth.

heading: Application Fee for Regional Agricultural Development Grant
text: An application for the Regional Agricultural Development Grant incurs a fee of 350 crowns. This grant supports projects that benefit a specific agricultural region or community, rather than individual farms, such as shared equipment facilities or cooperative marketing initiatives. The fee covers the review of complex proposals involving multiple stakeholders, economic impact assessments for the region, and governance structures for cooperative projects. Applicants must demonstrate broad community support, with at least 7 participating farms or agricultural businesses. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the potential for widespread regional benefit. This fee supports collaborative agricultural growth.

heading: Application Fee for Farm Succession Grant
text: The application fee for the Farm Succession Grant is 260 crowns. This grant assists with the smooth transfer of agricultural operations from one generation to the next, or to new owners. The fee covers the review of succession plans, legal agreements, and financial arrangements between the outgoing and incoming parties. Applicants must provide a detailed plan for the transition, typically spanning 12 to 36 months, ensuring the continuity of the farming business. The Nordvale Agricultural Office assesses the viability of the proposed succession and its potential to keep agricultural land in production. This fee supports the preservation of family farms.

heading: Application Fee for Agricultural Research Grant
text: An application for the Agricultural Research Grant requires a fee of 380 crowns. This grant supports scientific research projects aimed at advancing agricultural knowledge and practices in Nordvale. The fee covers the rigorous peer review of research proposals, methodologies, and expected outcomes. Applicants must submit a comprehensive research plan, including a detailed budget, qualifications of researchers, and a timeline of up to 48 months. The Nordvale Agricultural Office often involves external academic or industry experts in the evaluation process, and this fee contributes to those specialized assessments. This grant promotes evidence-based improvements in agriculture.

heading: Application Fee for Agricultural Research Grant
text: An application for the Agricultural Research Grant requires a fee of 420 crowns. This grant supports scientific research projects aimed at advancing agricultural knowledge and practices in Nordvale. The fee covers the rigorous peer review of research proposals, methodologies, and expected outcomes. Applicants must submit a comprehensive research plan, including a detailed budget, qualifications of researchers, and a timeline of up to 48 months. The Nordvale Agricultural Office often involves external academic or industry experts in the evaluation process, and this fee contributes to those specialized assessments. This grant promotes evidence-based improvements in agriculture.

heading: Application Fee for Biodiversity Conservation Grant
text: The application fee for the Biodiversity Conservation Grant is 290 crowns. This grant supports farmers who implement measures to protect and enhance biodiversity on their land, such as creating wildlife habitats or preserving native plant species. The fee covers the review of ecological assessments, conservation plans, and monitoring strategies. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to dedicating at least 5% of their farm area to conservation efforts. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the ecological impact and long-term sustainability of the proposed initiatives. This fee promotes responsible land stewardship and ecological balance within agricultural landscapes.

heading: Application Fee for Value-Added Product Grant
text: A fee of 240 crowns is required for applications to the Value-Added Product Grant. This grant encourages farmers to process their raw agricultural products into higher-value goods, such as jams, cheeses, or processed meats. The fee covers the review of business plans, market analyses for new products, and compliance with food safety regulations. Applicants must outline their processing facilities, production methods, and marketing strategies. The Nordvale Agricultural Office assesses the potential for economic growth and diversification within the agricultural sector. This fee supports innovation in agricultural product development and rural economies.

heading: Application Fee for Agricultural Infrastructure Grant
text: The application fee for the Agricultural Infrastructure Grant is 310 crowns. This grant supports improvements to essential farm infrastructure, such as barns, fencing, irrigation systems, or storage facilities. The fee covers the review of construction plans, cost estimates, and environmental impact assessments. Applicants must provide detailed schematics, contractor quotes, and demonstrate that the proposed infrastructure will significantly enhance farm productivity or sustainability. Projects with a total cost exceeding 50,000 crowns are generally favored. The Nordvale Agricultural Office ensures that proposed developments adhere to safety and environmental standards. This fee supports modernizing Nordvale's agricultural base.

heading: Application Fee for Emergency Drought Relief Grant
text: The application fee for the Emergency Drought Relief Grant is 100 crowns. This reduced fee is applicable only during officially declared periods of drought affecting agricultural regions. The grant provides urgent financial assistance to farmers severely impacted by water shortages. The fee covers rapid assessment of damages and immediate needs. Applicants must provide verifiable evidence of drought impact, such as crop yield reductions exceeding 30% or livestock water source depletion. The Nordvale Agricultural Office aims to process these applications within 10 working days to provide timely aid. This fee supports farmers facing unforeseen climatic challenges.

heading: Application Fee for Farm Energy Efficiency Grant
text: An application for the Farm Energy Efficiency Grant requires a fee of 260 crowns. This grant encourages farmers to adopt energy-saving technologies and practices on their farms, such as solar panels, efficient lighting, or optimized machinery. The fee covers the review of energy audits, proposed installations, and projected energy cost savings. Applicants must provide detailed plans for energy upgrades and demonstrate an expected reduction in energy consumption of at least 25%. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the environmental and economic benefits of proposed projects. This fee supports a more sustainable and cost-effective agricultural sector.

heading: Application Fee for Agricultural Education & Training Grant
text: The application fee for the Agricultural Education & Training Grant is 190 crowns. This grant supports farmers and agricultural workers in accessing educational programs, workshops, or certifications that enhance their skills and knowledge. The fee covers the review of training proposals, course outlines, and justifications for how the education will benefit the farm operation. Applicants must provide details of the accredited courses or programs they wish to undertake, with a minimum duration of 40 hours. The Nordvale Agricultural Office prioritizes training that addresses critical skill gaps or introduces new agricultural techniques. This fee invests in human capital development in agriculture.

heading: Application Fee for Farm Safety Improvement Grant
text: A fee of 210 crowns applies to applications for the Farm Safety Improvement Grant. This grant provides funding for projects that enhance safety for agricultural workers and visitors on farms, such as installing safety guards on machinery, improving lighting, or upgrading hazardous storage areas. The fee covers the review of safety audit reports, proposed improvements, and compliance with safety standards. Applicants must identify specific safety risks and outline how the grant funds will mitigate those risks, aiming for a 100% resolution of identified critical hazards. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the potential to reduce accidents and injuries. This fee promotes a safer working environment.

heading: Application Fee for Agri-Tourism Development Grant
text: The application fee for the Agri-Tourism Development Grant is 270 crowns. This grant supports farmers who wish to diversify their income by offering tourism-related activities on their farm, such as farm stays, educational tours, or direct sales outlets. The fee covers the review of business plans for agri-tourism ventures, marketing strategies, and compliance with visitor safety regulations. Applicants must demonstrate a clear plan for integrating tourism with their primary agricultural operations, targeting an increase in non-agricultural revenue by at least 15%. The Nordvale Agricultural Office assesses the potential for rural economic growth. This fee supports innovative farm diversification.

heading: Application Fee for Pest Management Grant
text: An application for the Pest Management Grant requires a fee of 250 crowns. This grant supports farmers in implementing sustainable and environmentally friendly pest management strategies, reducing reliance on chemical pesticides. The fee covers the review of integrated pest management plans, biological control initiatives, and monitoring programs. Applicants must provide detailed plans for identifying and managing pests, aiming for a reduction in chemical pesticide use by at least 20% over two years. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the effectiveness and ecological impact of proposed strategies. This fee contributes to healthier agricultural ecosystems.

heading: Application Fee for Seed and Crop Variety Development Grant
text: The application fee for the Seed and Crop Variety Development Grant is 330 crowns. This grant supports initiatives focused on developing new or improved seed varieties and crop types suitable for Nordvale's climate and soil conditions. The fee covers the scientific review of breeding programs, genetic research proposals, and field trial methodologies. Applicants must submit a comprehensive research plan, including specific objectives, expected genetic advancements, and a timeline of up to 60 months. The Nordvale Agricultural Office often consults with agricultural geneticists for assessment. This fee helps ensure the future resilience and productivity of Nordvale's crops.

heading: Application Fee for Forest and Agroforestry Grant
text: A fee of 280 crowns applies to applications for the Forest and Agroforestry Grant. This grant encourages farmers to integrate trees and shrubs into their agricultural land for ecological and economic benefits, such as shelterbelts, timber production, or fruit orchards. The fee covers the review of planting plans, species selection, and long-term management strategies. Applicants must commit to planting at least 500 trees or establishing 1 hectare of agroforestry system. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the environmental impact, such as carbon sequestration and biodiversity enhancement, and the potential economic returns. This fee supports integrated land-use systems.

heading: Application Fee for Farm Resiliency Grant
text: The application fee for the Farm Resiliency Grant is 300 crowns. This grant supports farmers in developing strategies to withstand and recover from various disruptions, including economic downturns, market fluctuations, or extreme weather events. The fee covers the review of risk assessment plans, disaster preparedness protocols, and diversification strategies. Applicants must outline potential vulnerabilities and propose concrete measures to enhance their farm's ability to adapt and recover. The Nordvale Agricultural Office assesses the comprehensiveness and practicality of these resiliency plans. This fee promotes a more robust and adaptable agricultural sector in Nordvale.

heading: Application Fee for Aldmark Agricultural Project
text: A fee of 350 crowns is required for applications specifically targeting the Aldmark Agricultural Project. This project supports initiatives within the capital region aimed at urban farming, community gardens, or food security programs. The fee covers the detailed review of localized impact assessments, community engagement plans, and logistical considerations unique to Aldmark. Applicants must demonstrate how their project will benefit the local population, with a focus on supplying fresh produce to at least 200 households or engaging 50 volunteers. The Nordvale Agricultural Office collaborates with the Aldmark Municipal Council on evaluations. This fee supports agricultural development in the capital.

heading: Application Fee for Aldmark Agricultural Project
text: A fee of 380 crowns is required for applications specifically targeting the Aldmark Agricultural Project. This project supports initiatives within the capital region aimed at urban farming, community gardens, or food security programs. The fee covers the detailed review of localized impact assessments, community engagement plans, and logistical considerations unique to Aldmark. Applicants must demonstrate how their project will benefit the local population, with a focus on supplying fresh produce to at least 250 households or engaging 60 volunteers. The Nordvale Agricultural Office collaborates with the Aldmark Municipal Council on evaluations. This fee supports agricultural development in the capital.

heading: Application Fee for Brenholt Crop Productivity Grant
text: The application fee for the Brenholt Crop Productivity Grant is 290 crowns. This grant is specifically designed for farmers in the Brenholt municipality to enhance crop yields and efficiency. The fee covers the review of advanced cultivation techniques, precision agriculture proposals, and soil nutrient management plans tailored for Brenholt's unique soil profile. Applicants must demonstrate a projected increase in crop yield by at least 10% for their primary crop. The Nordvale Agricultural Office works closely with local agricultural experts in Brenholt to assess these applications. This fee supports targeted improvements in agricultural output for the Brenholt region.

heading: Application Fee for Corvik Livestock Breeding Grant
text: An application for the Corvik Livestock Breeding Grant requires a fee of 310 crowns. This grant focuses on supporting livestock breeders in the Corvik municipality, particularly those involved in genetic improvement programs for indigenous breeds. The fee covers the review of breeding plans, genetic selection methodologies, and animal health protocols. Applicants must provide details on their existing herd, proposed genetic enhancements, and the expected benefits to the Corvik livestock industry, aiming for a 5% improvement in a key genetic trait. The Nordvale Agricultural Office consults with veterinary and genetic specialists during evaluation. This fee promotes superior livestock genetics in Corvik.

heading: Application Fee for Dunmere Rural Infrastructure Grant
text: The application fee for the Dunmere Rural Infrastructure Grant is 320 crowns. This grant is dedicated to improving shared agricultural infrastructure in the Dunmere municipality, such as communal grain storage facilities or cooperative processing units. The fee covers the review of large-scale infrastructure proposals, multi-farm benefit assessments, and long-term maintenance plans. Applicants must demonstrate collective benefit for at least 8 farms within Dunmere and present a robust plan for shared management. The Nordvale Agricultural Office collaborates with Dunmere community leaders to ensure project relevance and sustainability. This fee supports vital shared assets in Dunmere's agricultural landscape.

heading: Application Fee for Elsby Horticultural Innovation Grant
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Application Fee for Elsby Horticultural Innovation Grant
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Application Fee for Fennick Specialty Crop Grant
text: An application for the Fennick Specialty Crop Grant requires a fee of 270 crowns. This grant targets farmers in the Fennick municipality cultivating unique or high-value specialty crops, such as medicinal herbs, rare berries, or artisanal vegetables. The fee covers the review of cultivation plans specific to these crops, market development strategies, and quality control protocols. Applicants must demonstrate the distinctiveness of their crop and its potential economic impact for Fennick, aiming for market access in at least three new distribution channels. The Nordvale Agricultural Office assesses the niche market potential and sustainability of these specialized operations. This fee supports diversification and premium produce in Fennick.

heading: Application Fee for Grauby Pasture Management Grant
text: The application fee for the Grauby Pasture Management Grant is 260 crowns. This grant is specifically for farmers in the Grauby municipality focusing on improving the health and productivity of their pastures for grazing livestock. The fee covers the review of rotational grazing plans, soil enrichment strategies for grasslands, and weed control measures. Applicants must provide details on their existing pastureland, proposed improvements, and expected increases in forage quality or carrying capacity by at least 15%. The Nordvale Agricultural Office prioritizes plans that enhance ecological health alongside agricultural productivity. This fee supports sustainable grassland management in Grauby.

heading: Application Fee for Lund Vale Orchard Renewal Grant
text: A fee of 280 crowns applies to applications for the Lund Vale Orchard Renewal Grant. This grant is exclusively for orchard owners in the Lund Vale municipality seeking to rejuvenate aging orchards, plant new disease-resistant varieties, or adopt modern pruning and harvesting techniques. The fee covers the review of orchard development plans, horticultural strategies, and projected yield improvements. Applicants must commit to renewing at least 1 hectare of existing orchard or planting a new orchard of similar size. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the long-term viability and productivity gains for Lund Vale's fruit industry. This fee supports the vitality of Lund Vale's orchards.

heading: Application Fee for Lund Vale Orchard Renewal Grant
text: A fee of 300 crowns applies to applications for the Lund Vale Orchard Renewal Grant. This grant is exclusively for orchard owners in the Lund Vale municipality seeking to rejuvenate aging orchards, plant new disease-resistant varieties, or adopt modern pruning and harvesting techniques. The fee covers the review of orchard development plans, horticultural strategies, and projected yield improvements. Applicants must commit to renewing at least 1.5 hectares of existing orchard or planting a new orchard of similar size. The Nordvale Agricultural Office evaluates the long-term viability and productivity gains for Lund Vale's fruit industry. This fee supports the vitality of Lund Vale's orchards.

heading: Exemptions for Low-Income Applicants
text: Applicants whose declared household income for the previous fiscal year falls below 300,000 crowns are exempt from 50% of the standard application fees outlined in this Act. To qualify for this exemption, applicants must provide verifiable income statements or tax records. This exemption does not apply to expedited review fees, late submission fees, or fees for amendments or reconsiderations. The Nordvale Agricultural Office reserves the right to request additional documentation to confirm eligibility. This provision ensures that financial barriers do not unduly prevent smaller or less affluent farming operations from accessing crucial grant opportunities. Only one such exemption can be claimed per application.

heading: Exemptions for Low-Income Applicants
text: Applicants whose declared household income for the previous fiscal year falls below 320,000 crowns are exempt from 40% of the standard application fees outlined in this Act. To qualify for this exemption, applicants must provide verifiable income statements or tax records. This exemption does not apply to expedited review fees, late submission fees, or fees for amendments or reconsiderations. The Nordvale Agricultural Office reserves the right to request additional documentation to confirm eligibility. This provision ensures that financial barriers do not unduly prevent smaller or less affluent farming operations from accessing crucial grant opportunities. Only one such exemption can be claimed per application.

heading: Payment Methods and Receipts
text: All fees stipulated in this Act must be paid in crowns and can be submitted via direct bank transfer, postal money order, or debit card at the Nordvale Agricultural Office. Cash payments are not accepted for amounts exceeding 1,000 crowns. A receipt acknowledging payment will be issued for all transactions, either electronically or in paper format, within 3 working days of payment being processed. This receipt serves as proof of payment and must be retained by the applicant for their records. Applications will not be considered fully submitted until the corresponding fee has been successfully processed and acknowledged. Payment details are available on the Office's official website.

heading: Review and Adjustment of Fees
text: The Nordvale Agricultural Office will conduct a comprehensive review of all fees specified in this Act every 36 months, or sooner if economic conditions warrant. The purpose of this review is to ensure that fees remain commensurate with administrative costs and do not create undue burdens on applicants. Any proposed adjustments to fees will be published for public consultation for a period of at least 60 days before taking effect. Finalized fee changes will be announced at least 30 days prior to their implementation, ensuring transparency and providing ample notice to the agricultural community. The first such review is scheduled for the first quarter of 2021.

heading: Concessions
text: (1) A registered peat cutter shall not pay the electric bicycle registration fee. (2) This exemption applies only if the peat cutter has been registered for at least one year.

heading: Recognised trades
text: For a registered dry-stone waller, the fee for a library card shall be 25 percent less than the amount specified in LIB §2(2).

heading: Exemptions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a licensed balloon pilot shall not pay any paper copy fee for public documents.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates the retail sale of tobacco products and nicotine products in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to reduce smoking among young people.
(3) It applies to every shop, kiosk and online seller that sells such products to consumers.

heading: Registration of retailers
text:
(1) A person who sells tobacco products at retail shall be registered under this Act.
(2) A registration is granted for one place of sale.
(3) A person who sells tobacco products without registration commits an offence.

heading: Registration fee
text:
(1) A retailer shall pay a registration fee of 120 crowns.
(2) The fee is due when the application is submitted.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the application is refused.

heading: Registration fee
text:
(1) A retailer shall pay a registration fee of 150 crowns.
(2) The fee is due when the application is submitted.
(3) The fee is not refunded if the application is refused.

heading: Registration term
text:
(1) A registration is valid for 2 years from the day it is granted.
(2) A retailer may renew the registration no earlier than 60 days before it expires.
(3) A registration that is not renewed lapses on its last day.

heading: Minimum age
text:
(1) No person may sell a tobacco product to a person under 18 years of age.
(2) The seller is responsible for checking the age of the buyer.
(3) A seller shall refuse a sale if the buyer cannot show proof of age.

heading: Minimum age
text:
(1) No person may sell a tobacco product to a person under 21 years of age.
(2) The seller is responsible for checking the age of the buyer.
(3) A seller shall refuse a sale if the buyer cannot show proof of age.

heading: Proof of age
text:
(1) A seller shall ask for proof of age from any buyer who appears to be under 30 years of age.
(2) Proof of age is a passport, an identity card or a driving licence.
(3) A retailer shall train every employee in the age check within 14 days of the employee starting work.

heading: Vending machines
text:
(1) A tobacco product shall not be sold from a vending machine.
(2) An exception applies to a machine inside a venue that admits only persons aged 21 years or over and is supervised at all times.
(3) A machine that does not meet subsection (2) shall be removed within 30 days of notice.

heading: Advertising
text:
(1) A retailer shall not advertise tobacco products outside the shop.
(2) Inside the shop, tobacco products shall be kept out of sight of customers until the customer asks for them.
(3) A price list is permitted if it uses plain text and is no larger than 30 by 40 centimetres.

heading: Warning area on packs
text:
(1) The health warning shall cover at least 60 percent of the front of every pack sold.
(2) A retailer shall not sell a pack that does not meet subsection (1).
(3) Packs that do not meet subsection (1) shall be returned to the supplier.

heading: Warning area on packs
text:
(1) The health warning shall cover at least 75 percent of the front of every pack sold.
(2) A retailer shall not sell a pack that does not meet subsection (1).
(3) Packs that do not meet subsection (1) shall be returned to the supplier.

heading: Distance from schools
text:
(1) No tobacco product may be sold at a place of sale within 150 metres of the entrance of a school.
(2) The distance is measured along the shortest public footpath.
(3) A retailer whose place of sale was registered before the school opened may continue to sell.

heading: Minimum pack size
text:
(1) A cigarette pack shall contain at least 20 cigarettes.
(2) A tobacco pouch shall contain at least 30 grams.
(3) A retailer shall not sell single cigarettes or open packs.

heading: Fine for selling to minors
text:
(1) A retailer who sells a tobacco product in breach of section 5 shall pay a fine of 350 crowns.
(2) A second offence within 12 months doubles the fine.
(3) The fine is paid within 30 days of notice.

heading: Fine for selling to minors
text:
(1) A retailer who sells a tobacco product in breach of section 5 shall pay a fine of 450 crowns.
(2) A second offence within 12 months doubles the fine.
(3) The fine is paid within 30 days of notice.

heading: Suspension of registration
text:
(1) The authority may suspend a registration for 30 days if the retailer is fined twice within 12 months.
(2) During a suspension the retailer shall not sell tobacco products.
(3) The retailer may appeal the suspension within 10 days of receiving notice.

heading: Inspection
text:
(1) An inspector may enter a place of sale during opening hours to check compliance.
(2) The inspector need not give notice before entering.
(3) The retailer shall give the inspector access to purchase records and stock.

heading: Electronic cigarette liquids
text:
(1) A bottle of nicotine liquid for an electronic cigarette shall not exceed 10 millilitres.
(2) The nicotine content shall not exceed 20 milligrams per millilitre.
(3) A bottle shall carry a child-proof closure.

heading: Purchase records
text:
(1) A retailer shall keep records of every purchase of tobacco products from suppliers.
(2) The records shall be kept for 36 months.
(3) The records shall be shown to an inspector on request.

heading: Price list
text:
(1) A retailer shall keep a price list for all tobacco products available at the place of sale.
(2) The price list shall be shown to a customer on request.
(3) The retailer shall update the price list within 3 days of any price change.

heading: Travellers' allowance
text:
(1) A traveller arriving in Nordvale may bring in 200 cigarettes for personal use without registration.
(2) The allowance applies to persons of 18 years of age or over.
(3) Tobacco products above the allowance shall be declared at the border.

heading: Travellers' allowance
text:
(1) A traveller arriving in Nordvale may bring in 160 cigarettes for personal use without registration.
(2) The allowance applies to persons of 18 years of age or over.
(3) Tobacco products above the allowance shall be declared at the border.

heading: Online sellers
text:
(1) A person who sells tobacco products online to buyers in Nordvale shall be registered under section 2.
(2) The seller shall verify the age of the buyer before dispatching the order.
(3) Parcels shall be handed over only to a person who proves they are of the age required.

heading: Coupons and free samples
text:
(1) A retailer shall not give away tobacco products as free samples.
(2) A retailer shall not offer coupons for tobacco products.
(3) A breach is treated as an offence under section 12.

heading: Coupons and free samples
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Music club fee for young ensemble members
text:
(1) Notwithstanding YTA §6, a young person who is a member of a registered amateur ensemble pays a membership fee of 10 crowns a year for a municipal music club.
(2) The age limits for music clubs apply unchanged.
(3) Proof of membership of the ensemble is shown when the young person joins the club.

heading: Annual museum card for long-serving teachers
text:
(1) A qualified teacher who has taught at schools for at least 10 years in total pays half the price of an annual museum card.
(2) Years of teaching adult learning courses are not counted.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the fees payable for the registration of trademarks within the Republic of Nordvale. It covers all applications for new trademarks, renewals of existing registrations, and any modifications or transfers of ownership. The fees are designed to cover the administrative costs associated with processing and maintaining trademark records. This Act applies uniformly across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. All payments must be made in Nordvale crowns.

heading: Initial Application Fee for a Single Class
text: The fee for the initial application to register a trademark in a single class of goods or services is 1,200 crowns. This fee is non-refundable once the application has been submitted to the Trademark Registry. An application is considered submitted when all required forms and supporting documentation have been received by the Registry's office in Aldmark. This fee covers the initial examination process, including a preliminary search for conflicting marks and the publication of the application for opposition purposes. Payment must accompany the application for it to be processed.

heading: Initial Application Fee for a Single Class
text: The fee for the initial application to register a trademark in a single class of goods or services is 1,350 crowns. This fee is non-refundable once the application has been submitted to the Trademark Registry. An application is considered submitted when all required forms and supporting documentation have been received by the Registry's office in Aldmark. This fee covers the initial examination process, including a preliminary search for conflicting marks and the publication of the application for opposition purposes. Payment must accompany the application for it to be processed.

heading: Initial Application Fee for a Single Class
text: The fee for the initial application to register a trademark in a single class of goods or services is 1,500 crowns. This fee is non-refundable once the application has been submitted to the Trademark Registry. An application is considered submitted when all required forms and supporting documentation have been received by the Registry's office in Aldmark. This fee covers the initial examination process, including a preliminary search for conflicting marks and the publication of the application for opposition purposes. Payment must accompany the application for it to be processed.

heading: Additional Class Fee
text: For each additional class of goods or services beyond the first, a separate fee of 400 crowns is applicable. This fee is added to the initial application fee specified in section 2. Applicants must clearly specify all classes for which protection is sought at the time of application. Failure to specify all classes may result in delays or the need for a new application for the omitted classes, incurring additional fees. This fee ensures that the administrative burden of classifying and examining goods and services across multiple categories is adequately covered.

heading: Additional Class Fee
text: For each additional class of goods or services beyond the first, a separate fee of 450 crowns is applicable. This fee is added to the initial application fee specified in section 2. Applicants must clearly specify all classes for which protection is sought at the time of application. Failure to specify all classes may result in delays or the need for a new application for the omitted classes, incurring additional fees. This fee ensures that the administrative burden of classifying and examining goods and services across multiple categories is adequately covered.

heading: Additional Class Fee
text: For each additional class of goods or services beyond the first, a separate fee of 500 crowns is applicable. This fee is added to the initial application fee specified in section 2. Applicants must clearly specify all classes for which protection is sought at the time of application. Failure to specify all classes may result in delays or the need for a new application for the omitted classes, incurring additional fees. This fee ensures that the administrative burden of classifying and examining goods and services across multiple categories is adequately covered.

heading: Renewal Fee for a Single Class
text: The fee for renewing a trademark registration for a single class of goods or services is 900 crowns. This fee must be paid within six months prior to the expiry date of the registration. A grace period of one month after the expiry date is permitted for payment, subject to a late fee as described in section 5. Renewal ensures continued protection of the trademark for another ten-year period. Failure to renew within the specified period will result in the expiration of the trademark rights.

heading: Renewal Fee for a Single Class
text: The fee for renewing a trademark registration for a single class of goods or services is 1,000 crowns. This fee must be paid within six months prior to the expiry date of the registration. A grace period of two months after the expiry date is permitted for payment, subject to a late fee as described in section 5. Renewal ensures continued protection of the trademark for another ten-year period. Failure to renew within the specified period will result in the expiration of the trademark rights.

heading: Renewal Fee for a Single Class
text: The fee for renewing a trademark registration for a single class of goods or services is 1,100 crowns. This fee must be paid within six months prior to the expiry date of the registration. A grace period of two months after the expiry date is permitted for payment, subject to a late fee as described in section 5. Renewal ensures continued protection of the trademark for another ten-year period. Failure to renew within the specified period will result in the expiration of the trademark rights.

heading: Late Renewal Fee
text: If a renewal fee is paid during the one-month grace period after the expiry date, an additional late fee of 200 crowns is applicable. This late fee is separate from the standard renewal fee detailed in section 4. Payment of both the renewal fee and the late fee must be made in full for the renewal to be processed successfully. Failure to pay the late fee will result in the rejection of the renewal application and eventual expiry of the trademark.

heading: Additional Class Renewal Fee
text: For each additional class of goods or services beyond the first, a separate renewal fee of 300 crowns is applicable. This fee is added to the single class renewal fee specified in section 4. Applicants must ensure that all desired classes are renewed simultaneously. Partial renewals, where only some classes are renewed, are permitted but any unrenewed classes will lapse. This fee covers the administrative effort involved in updating the register for multiple classifications upon renewal.

heading: Additional Class Renewal Fee
text: For each additional class of goods or services beyond the first, a separate renewal fee of 350 crowns is applicable. This fee is added to the single class renewal fee specified in section 4. Applicants must ensure that all desired classes are renewed simultaneously. Partial renewals, where only some classes are renewed, are permitted but any unrenewed classes will lapse. This fee covers the administrative effort involved in updating the register for multiple classifications upon renewal.

heading: Trademark Transfer Fee
text: The fee for recording a transfer of ownership of a trademark is 600 crowns. This fee applies regardless of the number of classes associated with the trademark. The request for transfer must be submitted with official documentation proving the change in ownership. The Registry will not process the transfer until this fee is paid in full. This ensures that the public record accurately reflects the current owner of the trademark rights.

heading: Change of Name or Address Fee
text: A fee of 150 crowns is required to record a change of name or address for a trademark owner. This fee applies to all affected trademarks under the same owner, provided they are updated in a single request. If separate requests are made, separate fees will apply for each. Proper documentation verifying the change, such as a certificate of incorporation name change, must accompany the request. Maintaining accurate contact information is crucial for official communications regarding the trademark.

heading: Amendment to Application Fee
text: An administrative fee of 250 crowns is levied for any substantive amendment requested by the applicant to a pending trademark application. This fee applies to changes such as modifications to the trademark design or significant alterations to the description of goods or services. Minor clerical corrections or changes requested by the Registry are exempt from this fee. The amendment must not broaden the scope of the application beyond what was originally filed. Payment ensures the processing of the amended application.

heading: Official Search Request Fee
text: The fee for requesting an official search of the Trademark Registry records by a third party is 300 crowns per trademark, or 500 crowns for a search across all classes for a specific mark. This search provides a report on existing registrations and pending applications that might conflict with a proposed trademark. The report is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a legal opinion. Results are typically provided within 15 business days of the request.

heading: Issuance of Certified Copy Fee
text: For the issuance of a certified copy of a trademark registration certificate or any other document from the official register, a fee of 100 crowns per document is charged. This fee covers the administrative cost of verification and formal certification. A certified copy is often required for legal proceedings or for registering the trademark in other jurisdictions. Requests should specify the exact document needed and the number of copies desired.

heading: Opposition Filing Fee
text: The fee for filing a notice of opposition against a published trademark application is 800 crowns. This fee must accompany the notice of opposition, which must be filed within 60 days of the application's publication. Failure to pay the fee will result in the rejection of the opposition. The fee covers the initial administrative processing of the opposition proceedings, including notifying the applicant and setting up the case file for review by the Registry tribunal.

heading: Counter-Statement Fee
text: An administrative fee of 300 crowns is required to file a counter-statement in response to an opposition. This fee is payable by the applicant within 30 days of receiving the notice of opposition. If the fee is not paid, the application may be deemed abandoned. The counter-statement outlines the applicant's arguments against the opposition and is a crucial step in the opposition proceedings. Payment facilitates the continued processing of the dispute.

heading: Hearing Fee
text: A fee of 1,500 crowns is payable by any party requesting an oral hearing in an opposition or cancellation proceeding. This fee must be paid at the time the request for a hearing is made. If both parties request a hearing, each party must pay this fee. The fee covers the costs associated with arranging and conducting the hearing, including administrative support and the presence of Registry officials. Hearings provide an opportunity for parties to present their arguments orally.

heading: Cancellation Application Fee
text: The fee for filing an application to cancel an existing trademark registration is 1,000 crowns. This fee applies to cancellation requests based on grounds such as non-use or invalidity. The application must include supporting evidence and arguments. Payment must be made upon filing the application. This fee covers the initial administrative review of the cancellation request. If the fee is not paid, the application for cancellation will not be processed.

heading: Expedited Examination Fee
text: An optional fee of 2,500 crowns can be paid to request an expedited examination of a trademark application. This fee places the application in a priority queue, aiming for examination within 30 days instead of the standard 90 days. Expedited examination is only available for applications that are complete and do not have significant deficiencies. This fee is separate from the initial application fee and is non-refundable, even if the application is ultimately rejected or delayed for other reasons.

heading: Expedited Examination Fee
text: An optional fee of 2,800 crowns can be paid to request an expedited examination of a trademark application. This fee places the application in a priority queue, aiming for examination within 25 days instead of the standard 90 days. Expedited examination is only available for applications that are complete and do not have significant deficiencies. This fee is separate from the initial application fee and is non-refundable, even if the application is ultimately rejected or delayed for other reasons.

heading: Withdrawal of Application Fee
text: A fee of 50 crowns is charged for formally withdrawing a trademark application after it has been submitted but before registration. This fee covers the administrative cost of processing the withdrawal request and updating the Registry records. While the initial application fee is non-refundable, this nominal fee ensures proper record-keeping of discontinued applications. Withdrawal requests must be submitted in writing by the applicant or their authorized representative.

heading: Restoration of Lapsed Application Fee
text: If a trademark application lapses due to an applicant's failure to respond to an office action within 60 days, it may be restored within a further 30 days by paying a fee of 700 crowns. This fee is in addition to any other outstanding fees. Restoration is at the discretion of the Registry and requires a satisfactory explanation for the delay. This allows applicants a limited opportunity to revive an application that was inadvertently allowed to lapse.

heading: Restoration of Lapsed Application Fee
text: If a trademark application lapses due to an applicant's failure to respond to an office action within 45 days, it may be restored within a further 30 days by paying a fee of 850 crowns. This fee is in addition to any other outstanding fees. Restoration is at the discretion of the Registry and requires a satisfactory explanation for the delay. This allows applicants a limited opportunity to revive an application that was inadvertently allowed to lapse.

heading: Disclaimer Filing Fee
text: A fee of 100 crowns is applicable for filing a formal disclaimer of rights to certain non-distinctive elements within a trademark. This disclaimer clarifies that protection is not sought for those specific elements, while the overall mark remains registrable. The fee covers the administrative cost of reviewing and recording the disclaimer. Disclaimers are often requested by the Registry during the examination process to narrow the scope of protection.

heading: Post-Registration Amendment Fee
text: For any amendments to a registered trademark that do not involve a change of ownership or name/address, a fee of 350 crowns is required. This includes minor modifications to the description of goods or services, provided they do not expand the scope of protection. Significant alterations to the trademark design are generally not permitted post-registration and would require a new application. This fee ensures accurate and up-to-date registry records.

heading: Post-Registration Amendment Fee
text: For any amendments to a registered trademark that do not involve a change of ownership or name/address, a fee of 400 crowns is required. This includes minor modifications to the description of goods or services, provided they do not expand the scope of protection. Significant alterations to the trademark design are generally not permitted post-registration and would require a new application. This fee ensures accurate and up-to-date registry records.

heading: Division of Application Fee
text: A fee of 500 crowns is charged for dividing a multi-class trademark application into two or more separate applications. This might be done if an opposition only affects certain classes, allowing the unaffected classes to proceed to registration. Each new divisional application will then be treated as a separate application for renewal and other purposes. This fee covers the administrative complexities of splitting and re-filing parts of an application.

heading: Voluntary Surrender Fee
text: A nominal fee of 75 crowns is required for the voluntary surrender of a trademark registration. This allows a trademark owner to formally relinquish their rights to a mark before its natural expiry. The fee covers the administrative cost of processing the surrender and updating the official register. Once surrendered, the trademark is no longer protected and becomes available for others to potentially register, subject to examination.

heading: Request for Statement of Grounds Fee
text: A fee of 200 crowns is payable for a request for a written statement of grounds for a decision by the Trademark Registry. This allows an applicant or opponent to understand the reasoning behind a refusal, objection, or other adverse decision. The fee ensures that the administrative effort involved in preparing a detailed explanation is covered. Such statements are often necessary for preparing appeals or further arguments.

heading: Request for Extension of Time Fee
text: A fee of 100 crowns is charged for requesting an extension of time to respond to an official communication or complete a required action. Each request for an extension, typically for a period of 30 days, incurs this fee. Multiple extensions may be granted, but each requires a separate fee. The Registry holds discretion in granting extensions, and a valid reason for the delay should be provided with the request.

heading: Recordal of License Fee
text: A fee of 400 crowns is required for recording a license agreement pertaining to a registered trademark. This recordal makes the license public and provides notice of the licensee's rights. The fee covers the administrative processing of the license agreement and its entry into the official register. While not mandatory for the validity of a license, recordal can be beneficial for enforcement purposes and clarity of rights.

heading: Cancellation of Recorded License Fee
text: A fee of 150 crowns is payable for formally canceling the recordal of a license agreement from the Trademark Register. This occurs when a license has expired, been terminated, or is no longer in effect. The fee covers the administrative steps involved in updating the register to reflect that the license is no longer active. A request for cancellation should include proof of the license's termination.

heading: Correction of Error Fee (Applicant's Fault)
text: Where a correction of an error in the Register is required due to a mistake made by the applicant or their agent, a fee of 200 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the administrative cost of rectifying the error and ensuring the accuracy of the official records. Corrections requested by the Registry or due to Registry errors are exempt from this fee. Documentation supporting the nature of the correction must be provided.

heading: Correction of Error Fee (Applicant's Fault)
text: Where a correction of an error in the Register is required due to a mistake made by the applicant or their agent, a fee of 250 crowns is applicable. This fee covers the administrative cost of rectifying the error and ensuring the accuracy of the official records. Corrections requested by the Registry or due to Registry errors are exempt from this fee. Documentation supporting the nature of the correction must be provided.

heading: Appeal to Tribunal Fee
text: The fee for filing an appeal against a decision of the Trademark Registry to the Trademark Tribunal is 1,800 crowns. This fee is required to initiate the appeal process and must be paid upon submission of the appeal notice. The appeal must be filed within 45 days of the Registry's decision. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the appeal and scheduling tribunal hearings. Failure to pay will result in the rejection of the appeal.

heading: Collective Mark Application Fee
text: The initial application fee for a collective mark is 2,000 crowns for a single class. For each additional class, a fee of 500 crowns applies. Collective marks are used by members of an association to distinguish their goods or services from those of others. The application must include the regulations governing the use of the collective mark. These fees reflect the increased complexity in examining and registering such specialized marks.

heading: Collective Mark Application Fee
text: The initial application fee for a collective mark is 2,200 crowns for a single class. For each additional class, a fee of 550 crowns applies. Collective marks are used by members of an association to distinguish their goods or services from those of others. The application must include the regulations governing the use of the collective mark. These fees reflect the increased complexity in examining and registering such specialized marks.

heading: Certification Mark Application Fee
text: The initial application fee for a certification mark is 2,000 crowns for a single class. For each additional class, a fee of 500 crowns applies. Certification marks indicate that the goods or services meet certain standards and are used by persons other than the owner of the mark. The application must include the rules governing the use of the certification mark. These fees cover the detailed examination required for such specialized marks.

heading: Certification Mark Application Fee
text: The initial application fee for a certification mark is 2,300 crowns for a single class. For each additional class, a fee of 600 crowns applies. Certification marks indicate that the goods or services meet certain standards and are used by persons other than the owner of the mark. The application must include the rules governing the use of the certification mark. These fees cover the detailed examination required for such specialized marks.

heading: Fee for Request for Reconsideration
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Adult courses for apprentices
text:
(1) A person serving an apprenticeship under a written contract with an employer pays half of the course fee for a municipal adult course in accounting.
(2) The reduction applies to one course in a calendar year.

heading: Adult courses for apprentices
text:
(1) A person serving an apprenticeship under a written contract with an employer pays half of the course fee for a municipal adult course in accounting or in computer skills.
(2) The reduction applies to one course in a calendar year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework and procedural requirements for obtaining permits necessary to erect monuments within the Republic of Nordvale. It aims to ensure that all monuments are constructed safely, respect public spaces, and comply with aesthetic and structural standards. The provisions herein apply to all permanent installations intended for public viewing or commemoration, whether on public or private land, excluding temporary displays lasting less than 90 days. This Act covers all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring consistent application across the nation.

heading: Definition of monument
text:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a 'monument' is defined as any permanent structure, sculpture, or installation designed to commemorate a person, event, or principle, or to serve as a landmark.
(2) This definition includes, but is not limited to, statues, obelisks, plaques exceeding 0.5 square meters in surface area, and memorial benches permanently affixed to the ground. Structures that are primarily functional, such as lamp posts or traffic signs, are excluded unless they incorporate significant commemorative elements. The structure must be intended to remain in place for a minimum of 10 years.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall erect, construct, or install any monument within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Monument Erection Permit from the municipal authority in whose jurisdiction the monument is proposed. This requirement applies regardless of whether the monument is situated on public or private land. Any monument erected without the necessary permit may be subject to immediate removal at the expense of the responsible party, along with a fine of 5,000 crowns for each day the non-permitted structure remains.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall erect, construct, or install any monument within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid Monument Erection Permit from the municipal authority in whose jurisdiction the monument is proposed. This requirement applies regardless of whether the monument is situated on public or private land. Any monument erected without the necessary permit may be subject to immediate removal at the expense of the responsible party, along with a fine of 7,500 crowns for each day the non-permitted structure remains. Furthermore, repeat offenders may face a ban on future permit applications for a period of 5 years.

heading: Application submission
text: Applications for a Monument Erection Permit must be submitted in writing to the relevant municipal planning department. The application package shall include a completed application form, detailed architectural drawings, a site plan, and a structural engineer's report. An initial application fee of 1,500 crowns must accompany the submission. Applications found to be incomplete will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days, with a detailed list of missing documents. Resubmissions must be made within 30 days to avoid a new fee.

heading: Application fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required for each Monument Erection Permit application.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. Additional fees may apply for public consultations or environmental impact assessments as outlined in section 9. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission.

heading: Application fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 2,000 crowns is required for each Monument Erection Permit application.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. Additional fees may apply for public consultations or environmental impact assessments as outlined in section 9. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. For monuments exceeding 3 meters in height, an additional 500 crown fee applies.

heading: Required documentation
text:
(1) Each application must include:
(a) Three sets of architectural drawings, scaled at 1:50, depicting all elevations, sections, and a site plan.
(b) A structural engineer's report certifying the stability and safety of the proposed monument, including calculations for wind resistance up to 150 km/h.
(c) A detailed description of the monument's materials, dimensions, and intended message or commemoration.
(d) Proof of land ownership or a letter of consent from the landowner if the applicant is not the owner.
(e) A visual impact assessment, including photographic simulations of the proposed monument in its intended location, from at least two different angles within 100 meters.

heading: Review period
text: The municipal planning department shall review all complete permit applications within 60 calendar days of receipt. During this period, the department may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. If no decision is rendered within the 60-day period, the applicant may formally request an update, and the department must respond within an additional 15 days. Complex projects, especially those requiring significant public consultation, may be granted an extension of up to 30 days, provided the applicant is notified in writing.

heading: Public consultation
text:
(1) For monuments exceeding 3 meters in height or located in a designated public park, a mandatory public consultation period of 30 days shall be initiated.
(2) During this period, public notices will be posted in local municipal offices and published in at least one local newspaper circulating in the affected municipality. The applicant may be required to host a public information session if 25 or more unique individuals formally request it in writing within the first 15 days of the consultation period. The cost of such sessions, including venue rental and staffing, shall be borne by the applicant, estimated at 2,000 crowns per session.

heading: Public consultation
text:
(1) For monuments exceeding 2.5 meters in height or located in a designated public park or within 50 meters of a residential zone, a mandatory public consultation period of 45 days shall be initiated.
(2) During this period, public notices will be posted in local municipal offices, published in at least two local newspapers circulating in the affected municipality, and advertised on the municipal website. The applicant will be required to host a public information session if 15 or more unique individuals formally request it in writing within the first 20 days of the consultation period. The cost of such sessions, including venue rental and staffing, shall be borne by the applicant, estimated at 3,000 crowns per session.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text:
(1) Monuments with a footprint exceeding 10 square meters or those requiring significant excavation (deeper than 2 meters) shall require an environmental impact assessment (EIA).
(2) The EIA must be conducted by an independent, certified environmental consultant and submitted as part of the permit application. The cost of the EIA, typically ranging from 10,000 to 50,000 crowns, shall be borne entirely by the applicant. The municipal authority will review the EIA findings and may request further studies if initial findings indicate potential significant environmental disruption. A minimum of 60 days is allocated for the review of a submitted EIA.

heading: Decision criteria
text:
(1) The municipal authority shall consider the following criteria when evaluating an application:
(a) Compliance with all relevant building codes and safety standards.
(b) Compatibility with the local aesthetic and urban planning guidelines.
(c) Public feedback received during the consultation period.
(d) Potential environmental impact.
(e) Structural integrity and durability for a minimum of 50 years.
(f) Appropriateness of the monument's message or commemoration in the proposed location, ensuring it does not incite public unrest or historical inaccuracies.

heading: Permit approval conditions
text:
(1) Approved permits may include specific conditions, such as:
(a) Requirements for particular construction materials or methods.
(b) Limitations on monument dimensions or landscaping around the base.
(c) A maintenance plan detailing responsibilities and frequency of upkeep for a minimum of 25 years.
(d) A security deposit of 10,000 crowns to ensure compliance with removal orders, if applicable. These conditions are designed to mitigate any potential negative impacts and ensure the long-term integrity and public acceptance of the monument. Failure to adhere to any condition may result in permit revocation.

heading: Permit refusal
text: If an application is refused, the municipal authority shall provide the applicant with a written explanation detailing the reasons for refusal. The reasons may include, but are not limited to, failure to meet structural standards, negative public feedback, or non-compliance with urban planning guidelines. An applicant whose permit is refused may resubmit a revised application addressing the stated deficiencies within 90 days without incurring a new application fee. After 90 days, a new application and fee are required.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit has been refused may appeal the decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any new evidence or arguments. An appeal fee of 2,500 crowns is required. The Appeals Board will schedule a hearing within 45 days of receiving a complete appeal, and their decision will be final within the municipal jurisdiction. The Board consists of 3 independent members.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit has been refused may appeal the decision to the Municipal Appeals Board within 45 days of receiving the refusal notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any new evidence or arguments. An appeal fee of 3,000 crowns is required. The Appeals Board will schedule a hearing within 60 days of receiving a complete appeal, and their decision will be final within the municipal jurisdiction. The Board consists of 5 independent members, ensuring a broader perspective on complex cases.

heading: Permit validity period
text: A Monument Erection Permit is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of approval. If construction of the monument has not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire, and a new application must be submitted. An extension of up to 12 months may be granted upon written request, provided the applicant demonstrates valid reasons for the delay, such as material supply issues or unforeseen site conditions. A fee of 750 crowns applies to extension requests, which must be submitted at least 30 days before the original permit expiry date.

heading: Construction commencement
text: The permit holder must notify the municipal planning department in writing at least 7 days before commencing any construction work related to the approved monument. This notification allows the department to schedule initial site inspections to ensure compliance with permit conditions. Failure to provide this notice may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns and a temporary stop-work order until the required notification is submitted and acknowledged by the department. Work must begin within 12 months of permit issuance.

heading: Site inspections
text: During the construction phase, municipal inspectors may conduct periodic site inspections to ensure that the monument is being built in accordance with the approved plans and permit conditions. A minimum of two inspections will be performed: one at the foundation stage and another at the final completion stage. The permit holder must provide inspectors with safe access to the construction site. Any deviation from the approved plans, exceeding 5% in critical dimensions, must be reported immediately and may require re-approval.

heading: Completion certificate
text: Upon completion of the monument, the permit holder must request a final inspection from the municipal planning department. If the monument is found to be in full compliance with the approved plans and permit conditions, a Completion Certificate will be issued within 14 days of the final inspection. This certificate confirms that the monument has been erected legally and safely. Without a Completion Certificate, the monument may not be officially unveiled or opened for public access. A fee of 500 crowns is charged for the issuance of the certificate.

heading: Monument maintenance
text:
(1) The owner of a monument is responsible for its ongoing maintenance and upkeep, ensuring it remains in good structural and aesthetic condition.
(2) A detailed maintenance plan, including cleaning schedules and repair provisions, must be submitted with the initial permit application. Monuments deemed to be in disrepair or posing a safety hazard may be subject to a municipal order for repair or removal. Failure to comply with such an order within 60 days may result in the municipality undertaking the work at the owner's expense, with an additional 20% administrative fee.

heading: Removal of monuments
text:
(1) Any proposal for the permanent removal of an approved monument must also undergo a permit process, similar to erection, to ensure proper disposal and site restoration.
(2) A removal application fee of 1,000 crowns applies. The removal process must include a plan for site remediation to its original state or an agreed-upon alternative. Monuments found to be structurally unsound or declared a public hazard by a certified engineer must be removed within 90 days of notification, with all costs borne by the owner. Emergency removal orders may reduce this period to 7 days.

heading: Removal of monuments
text:
(1) Any proposal for the permanent removal of an approved monument must also undergo a permit process, similar to erection, to ensure proper disposal and site restoration.
(2) A removal application fee of 1,500 crowns applies. The removal process must include a detailed plan for site remediation to its original state or an agreed-upon alternative, including soil testing. Monuments found to be structurally unsound or declared a public hazard by a certified engineer must be removed within 60 days of notification, with all costs borne by the owner. Emergency removal orders may reduce this period to 5 days, with a potential fine of 2,000 crowns per day for non-compliance.

heading: Prohibited materials
text: The use of certain materials in monument construction is strictly prohibited due to environmental concerns or lack of durability. These include, but are not limited to, unsealed particle board, non-tempered glass in load-bearing structures, and any material containing more than 0.1% lead or mercury. All proposed materials must be explicitly listed in the application and comply with national building material standards. Any monument constructed with prohibited materials will be subject to immediate removal and penalties as outlined in section 3.

heading: Height restrictions
text:
(1) In residential zones, monuments are generally restricted to a maximum height of 4 meters.
(2) In commercial zones, the maximum height limit is 8 meters. Public park monuments may reach up to 12 meters, provided they undergo enhanced public consultation as per section 8 and a detailed wind load analysis. Any proposed monument exceeding these limits by more than 10% requires special approval from the National Planning Committee and an additional review period of 45 days. The Aldmark municipal building code applies a stricter 3-meter height limit in its historic district.

heading: Setback requirements
text:
(1) All monuments must maintain a minimum setback of 2 meters from any property line.
(2) For monuments exceeding 5 meters in height, the setback requirement increases to 1 meter for every 2 meters of height above 5 meters, up to a maximum setback of 10 meters. In areas adjacent to public roads, a minimum setback of 5 meters from the road edge is mandatory to ensure clear sight lines and pedestrian safety. These requirements are in place to prevent obstruction and ensure public access around the monument. Exemptions may be granted for monuments on properties larger than 10,000 square meters.

heading: Setback requirements
text:
(1) All monuments must maintain a minimum setback of 3 meters from any property line.
(2) For monuments exceeding 4 meters in height, the setback requirement increases to 1 meter for every 1.5 meters of height above 4 meters, up to a maximum setback of 12 meters.
