The Department of Commerce will endeavor to process such early applications within 45 days of receipt. Transitional provisions for events already planned before this date will be handled on a case-by-case basis for a period of 60 days following commencement.

heading: Recognised trades
text: A certified bookbinder registered for at least one year pays 25 percent less of the rental duty threshold, meaning no duty is payable for the first 15 nights rented out in a calendar year.

heading: Special categories
text: For a registered calligrapher, an additional monthly payment of 32.5 crowns is provided for each child, supplementing the basic child benefit.

heading: Pre-departure immunisation
text:
(1) In every Act, 'pre-departure immunisation' means a single injection of a vaccine outside the national programme, given at a facility run by the state or a municipality to protect a person on a trip to another country.
(2) An injection given at a pharmacy is not a pre-departure immunisation.

heading: Medicines for former officials
text:
(1) An emeritus adjudicator pays the dispensed medicine levy reduced by two crowns for each package.
(2) The reduction is applied after any other reduction, and the amount payable never falls below zero.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for licensing companies that provide telecommunications services within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure a fair and competitive market, protect consumer interests, and promote the development of robust and reliable telecommunications infrastructure across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This Act applies to all entities offering voice, data, or video transmission services to the public or to other businesses for commercial gain, regardless of their operational scale. It aims to streamline the application process and set clear standards for service quality and network coverage, guaranteeing that even remote areas like Grauby and Lund Vale receive adequate service provisions. The provisions herein are designed to support technological advancement while maintaining regulatory oversight.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Service provider" means any person or entity offering telecommunications services to the public or to other businesses.
(2) "Telecommunications services" include the transmission, emission, or reception of signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, or intelligence of any nature by wire, radio, optical, or other electromagnetic systems.
(3) "Licence" refers to the official authorization granted by the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority to operate as a service provider.
(4) "Authority" means the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Nordvale, the body responsible for administering this Act.
(5) "Subscriber" means any individual or entity receiving telecommunications services from a service provider.
(6) "Network infrastructure" includes all physical and logical components necessary for providing telecommunications services, such as cables, towers, and data centers.

heading: Requirement for licence
text:
(1) No person or entity shall provide telecommunications services within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence from the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) Any service provider operating without a valid licence shall be subject to a penalty of 50,000 crowns for each month of unauthorized operation, calculated from the date services commenced or from the date of licence expiry, whichever is later. The Authority shall issue a cease and desist order effective immediately upon discovery of unlicensed operation. Continued operation after such an order may result in additional fines and legal action. This requirement applies to both new entrants and existing operators whose licences have expired or been revoked. Compliance with this section is strictly enforced to maintain market integrity.

heading: Requirement for licence
text:
(1) No person or entity shall provide telecommunications services within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence from the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) Any service provider operating without a valid licence shall be subject to a penalty of 75,000 crowns for each month of unauthorized operation, calculated from the date services commenced or from the date of licence expiry, whichever is later. The Authority shall issue a cease and desist order effective immediately upon discovery of unlicensed operation. Continued operation after such an order may result in additional fines and legal action. This requirement applies to both new entrants and existing operators whose licences have expired or been revoked. Compliance with this section is strictly enforced to maintain market integrity.

heading: Requirement for licence
text:
(1) No person or entity shall provide telecommunications services within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence from the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) Any service provider operating without a valid licence shall be subject to a penalty of 100,000 crowns for each month of unauthorized operation, calculated from the date services commenced or from the date of licence expiry, whichever is later. The Authority shall issue a cease and desist order effective immediately upon discovery of unlicensed operation. Continued operation after such an order may result in additional fines and legal action, including potential confiscation of equipment. This requirement applies to both new entrants and existing operators whose licences have expired or been revoked. Compliance with this section is strictly enforced to maintain market integrity.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An application for a licence shall be submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee of 2,000 crowns.
(2) The application must include:
(a) A detailed business plan outlining the proposed services, target municipalities (e.g., Aldmark, Corvik), and network deployment strategy.
(b) Proof of financial capability demonstrating sufficient resources to implement the business plan, with a minimum capital reserve of 1,000,000 crowns.
(c) Technical specifications of the proposed network infrastructure and a plan for compliance with national technical standards.
(d) A declaration of compliance with all relevant Nordvale laws and regulations, signed by a duly authorized representative of the applicant. The Authority may request additional information within 30 days of receiving the application to ensure completeness.

heading: Licence categories
text:
(1) The Authority shall issue licences in the following categories:
(a) Category A: Comprehensive Service Provider – for entities offering a full range of voice, data, and video services across multiple municipalities.
(b) Category B: Specialized Service Provider – for entities offering specific telecommunications services, such as internet-only or voice-only services, within defined geographical areas.
(c) Category C: Infrastructure Provider – for entities primarily providing network infrastructure to other service providers. Each category carries specific obligations regarding network coverage, service quality, and regulatory reporting, which are detailed in the licence conditions. Applicants must clearly indicate the category for which they are applying, providing justification for their choice based on their business model and operational scope. The Authority will assess applications based on these categories.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text:
(1) A licence issued under this Act shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issuance.
(2) An application for renewal of a licence must be submitted at least 90 days before its expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,500 crowns.
(3) The Authority may renew a licence if the service provider has complied with all terms and conditions of its existing licence and continues to meet the eligibility criteria. Failure to submit a renewal application within the specified timeframe may result in the licence lapsing, requiring a new application process. Renewals are subject to a review of the service provider's performance over the preceding licence period, including adherence to service level agreements and consumer protection measures. This ensures ongoing commitment to quality.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text:
(1) A licence issued under this Act shall be valid for a period of seven years from the date of issuance.
(2) An application for renewal of a licence must be submitted at least 120 days before its expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,800 crowns.
(3) The Authority may renew a licence if the service provider has complied with all terms and conditions of its existing licence and continues to meet the eligibility criteria. Failure to submit a renewal application within the specified timeframe may result in the licence lapsing, requiring a new application process and a late fee of 500 crowns. Renewals are subject to a review of the service provider's performance over the preceding licence period, including adherence to service level agreements and consumer protection measures. This ensures ongoing commitment to quality.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
(1) Every licence issued by the Authority shall be subject to such conditions as the Authority may deem appropriate to ensure:
(a) Fair competition among service providers.
(b) Universal service provision, aiming for at least 85% population coverage in all municipalities by year three of operation.
(c) Protection of subscriber privacy and data security.
(d) Compliance with technical standards and interconnection requirements.
(e) Non-discriminatory access to services for all users.
(2) These conditions shall be specified in the licence document and may be varied by the Authority from time to time, with prior notice of at least 60 days to the affected service provider. Failure to adhere to these conditions may lead to penalties.

heading: Universal service obligation
text:
(1) All Category A and B service providers shall contribute to the Universal Service Fund at a rate of 1% of their annual gross revenue.
(2) The fund shall be used to subsidize the provision of telecommunications services to underserved areas, particularly remote municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale, where commercial viability is limited. Service providers receiving subsidies from the fund must commit to achieving at least 90% household penetration in the designated areas within two years of receiving the subsidy. The Authority shall conduct annual audits of the fund's expenditures and the beneficiaries' compliance with service rollout targets. This ensures that essential communication services are accessible to all citizens of Nordvale, fostering economic and social inclusion.

heading: Service quality standards
text:
(1) All service providers must adhere to minimum service quality standards set by the Authority.
(2) These standards include:
(a) A minimum average data download speed of 10 Mbps for fixed broadband services.
(b) Network availability of at least 99.5% per quarter.
(c) Call completion rates of 98% for voice services.
(d) Customer support response time of no more than 4 hours for critical issues.
(3) The Authority shall conduct periodic audits and performance tests to ensure compliance. Service providers failing to meet these standards may be subject to fines of up to 10,000 crowns per violation per month, after a 30-day grace period for remediation. Repeated failures could lead to more severe penalties as outlined in section 25. Regular reporting on these metrics is mandatory.

heading: Service quality standards
text:
(1) All service providers must adhere to minimum service quality standards set by the Authority.
(2) These standards include:
(a) A minimum average data download speed of 25 Mbps for fixed broadband services.
(b) Network availability of at least 99.8% per quarter.
(c) Call completion rates of 99% for voice services.
(d) Customer support response time of no more than 2 hours for critical issues.
(3) The Authority shall conduct periodic audits and performance tests to ensure compliance. Service providers failing to meet these standards may be subject to fines of up to 15,000 crowns per violation per month, after a 30-day grace period for remediation. Repeated failures could lead to more severe penalties as outlined in section 25. Regular reporting on these metrics is mandatory.

heading: Service quality standards
text:
(1) All service providers must adhere to minimum service quality standards set by the Authority.
(2) These standards include:
(a) A minimum average data download speed of 50 Mbps for fixed broadband services and 10 Mbps for mobile broadband.
(b) Network availability of at least 99.9% per quarter.
(c) Call completion rates of 99.5% for voice services.
(d) Customer support response time of no more than 1 hour for critical issues.
(3) The Authority shall conduct periodic audits and performance tests to ensure compliance. Service providers failing to meet these standards may be subject to fines of up to 20,000 crowns per violation per month, after a 20-day grace period for remediation. Repeated failures could lead to more severe penalties as outlined in section 25. Regular reporting on these metrics is mandatory and must include data for each municipality served, like Aldmark and Dunmere.

heading: Interconnection obligations
text:
(1) All service providers with significant market power, as determined by the Authority, shall negotiate interconnection agreements in good faith with other licensed service providers.
(2) These agreements must ensure non-discriminatory access to their networks at reasonable rates.
(3) The Authority shall intervene to resolve interconnection disputes if negotiations fail, setting fair terms and conditions within 60 days of a dispute being formally lodged. Service providers must submit a copy of all interconnection agreements to the Authority within 14 days of their execution. Failure to comply with interconnection obligations or Authority rulings may result in fines of up to 25,000 crowns per day for each day of non-compliance. This ensures that smaller providers can compete effectively.

heading: Consumer protection
text:
(1) Service providers shall establish clear and transparent terms and conditions for their services, including pricing, contract duration, and cancellation policies.
(2) Information regarding services must be readily accessible to subscribers, both online and at physical service centers in municipalities like Brenholt and Elsby.
(3) Service providers must provide a robust complaint handling mechanism, responding to subscriber complaints within 7 working days and resolving them within 30 days. The Authority shall investigate complaints not resolved to the satisfaction of the subscriber and may impose penalties of 5,000 crowns per unresolved complaint if the provider is found to be at fault. This ensures subscribers have avenues for redress and are treated fairly by providers.

heading: Data privacy and security
text:
(1) Service providers shall take all reasonable measures to protect the privacy and security of subscriber data.
(2) This includes implementing appropriate technical and organizational safeguards against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction of data. Subscriber data shall not be shared with third parties without explicit consent, except as required by law. In the event of a data breach, the service provider must notify affected subscribers and the Authority within 72 hours of discovery. Failure to comply with these data privacy and security provisions may result in fines of up to 500,000 crowns and potential licence suspension, depending on the severity of the breach and the number of affected subscribers. This provision is critical for maintaining public trust.

heading: Reporting obligations
text:
(1) All service providers shall submit annual reports to the Authority detailing their operational performance, financial statements, and compliance with licence conditions.
(2) These reports are due by 31 March of each year, covering the preceding calendar year. The Authority may also request ad-hoc reports on specific aspects of a provider's operations, with a minimum notice period of 14 days. Failure to submit required reports on time may result in a penalty of 1,000 crowns for each week the report is overdue. The information collected is vital for the Authority to monitor the health of the telecommunications sector and ensure regulatory compliance across all regions, including Aldmark and Fennick. Accuracy in reporting is paramount.

heading: Reporting obligations
text:
(1) All service providers shall submit annual reports to the Authority detailing their operational performance, financial statements, and compliance with licence conditions.
(2) These reports are due by 28 February of each year, covering the preceding calendar year. The Authority may also request ad-hoc reports on specific aspects of a provider's operations, with a minimum notice period of 10 days. Failure to submit required reports on time may result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns for each week the report is overdue. The information collected is vital for the Authority to monitor the health of the telecommunications sector and ensure regulatory compliance across all regions, including Aldmark and Fennick. Accuracy in reporting is paramount and includes a breakdown of service quality metrics per municipality.

heading: Modification of licence conditions
text:
(1) The Authority may, after giving 60 days' written notice to a service provider and considering any representations made by the provider, modify any condition of a licence.
(2) Such modifications must be in the public interest and consistent with the objectives of this Act. Examples of modifications may include updating universal service targets, adjusting service quality standards to reflect technological advancements, or imposing new requirements related to network security. The service provider has the right to appeal the modification within 30 days of receiving the notice. Any modifications made will apply uniformly to all licensees within the same category to maintain fairness in the market. This ensures adaptability of regulations to evolving industry landscapes.

heading: Transfer of licence
text:
(1) A licence issued under this Act shall not be transferred or assigned to another entity without the prior written approval of the Authority.
(2) An application for transfer of a licence must be submitted to the Authority, accompanied by a fee of 10,000 crowns, along with full details of the proposed transferee. The Authority shall approve the transfer only if the transferee meets all the eligibility criteria for obtaining a new licence and demonstrates the financial and technical capability to fulfill the licence obligations. The Authority will make a decision on the transfer application within 90 days. Unauthorized transfers are strictly prohibited and may lead to the revocation of the licence for both the transferor and the transferee. This safeguards market stability.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
(1) The Authority may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding six months if a service provider contravenes any provision of this Act or any condition of its licence.
(2) Before suspending a licence, the Authority shall issue a written notice to the service provider, specifying the grounds for suspension and providing an opportunity for the provider to make representations within 30 days. During the suspension period, the service provider may not offer new services but must maintain existing services to subscribers unless otherwise directed by the Authority. A suspended licence will only be reinstated upon satisfactory rectification of the contravention and payment of a reinstatement fee of 20,000 crowns. This measure ensures accountability for serious breaches.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) The Authority may revoke a licence if a service provider:
(a) Fails to commence operations within 12 months of licence issuance.
(b) Persistently breaches the conditions of its licence despite prior warnings and suspensions.
(c) Becomes insolvent or ceases to operate its telecommunications business.
(d) Provides false or misleading information in its licence application or reports.
(2) Before revoking a licence, the Authority shall give the service provider 60 days' written notice and an opportunity to be heard. Upon revocation, the service provider must cease all operations immediately and must ensure a smooth transition of services for subscribers, as per section 18. Revocation is a last resort for severe and repeated non-compliance. This is crucial for maintaining regulatory integrity.

heading: Cessation of services
text:
(1) In the event of a licence revocation, suspension leading to cessation, or voluntary cessation of services, the service provider shall take all necessary steps to ensure minimal disruption to subscribers.
(2) This includes providing at least 90 days' prior notice to all affected subscribers and assisting them in migrating to alternative service providers. The Authority may appoint an interim administrator to manage the transition process if the service provider fails to comply with these obligations. Failure to ensure a smooth transition may result in additional fines of up to 100,000 crowns and a ban on future participation in the Nordvale telecommunications market for key executives. This ensures that subscribers are not unduly disadvantaged by changes in service provision.

heading: Cessation of services
text:
(1) In the event of a licence revocation, suspension leading to cessation, or voluntary cessation of services, the service provider shall take all necessary steps to ensure minimal disruption to subscribers.
(2) This includes providing at least 120 days' prior notice to all affected subscribers and assisting them in migrating to alternative service providers. The Authority may appoint an interim administrator to manage the transition process if the service provider fails to comply with these obligations. Failure to ensure a smooth transition may result in additional fines of up to 150,000 crowns per municipality affected (e.g., Aldmark, Corvik) and a ban on future participation in the Nordvale telecommunications market for key executives. This ensures that subscribers are not unduly disadvantaged by changes in service provision.

heading: Emergency powers of the Authority
text:
(1) In times of national emergency, public safety crisis, or other exceptional circumstances, the Authority may issue directives to service providers requiring them to:
(a) Prioritize certain communications.
(b) Provide emergency services access.
(c) Restrict or block specific services for a temporary period, not exceeding 7 days without further authorization.
(2) Such directives shall be communicated in writing and shall be effective immediately. Service providers must comply without delay. Any costs incurred by service providers in complying with emergency directives may be subject to reimbursement by the government, as determined by the Ministry of Communications. Failure to comply with an emergency directive may result in immediate licence suspension for 6 months. This ensures the government can maintain essential communications during critical events.

heading: Appeals Tribunal
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Authority under this Act may appeal to the Telecommunications Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision.
(2) The Tribunal shall consist of three independent experts appointed by the Minister of Communications. The Tribunal shall review the decision based on the evidence presented and may affirm, reverse, or modify the Authority's decision. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal shall be final, subject to judicial review on points of law. The Tribunal's proceedings shall be transparent and fair, ensuring due process for all parties involved. This provides an independent avenue for redress against Authority decisions.

heading: Establishment of the Authority
text:
(1) The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority is hereby established as an independent body responsible for the regulation of telecommunications services in Nordvale.
(2) The Authority shall consist of a board of five members appointed by the Minister of Communications for a term of four years. Members must possess expertise in telecommunications, law, economics, or public administration. The Authority's functions include issuing licences, monitoring compliance, resolving disputes, and advising the government on telecommunications policy. Its primary office shall be located in Aldmark, with regional outreach offices in municipalities like Corvik and Dunmere. The Authority shall operate with impartiality and transparency, safeguarding the public interest in the telecommunications sector.

heading: Powers of the Authority
text:
(1) The Authority shall have the power to:
(a) Issue, renew, suspend, and revoke licences.
(b) Develop and enforce service quality standards.
(c) Impose penalties for non-compliance with this Act or licence conditions.
(d) Conduct investigations and audits of service providers' operations.
(e) Access any premises, equipment, or records of a service provider for the purpose of ensuring compliance.
(f) Collect and analyze data from service providers to monitor market performance. The Authority may delegate certain powers to its officers, who must carry official identification when exercising such powers. These extensive powers are necessary for effective regulation.

heading: Confidentiality of information
text:
(1) Any information obtained by the Authority from a service provider during the course of its duties shall be treated as confidential, unless its disclosure is required by law or necessary for the enforcement of this Act.
(2) This applies to sensitive commercial information, subscriber data, and network configurations. Aggregate data, which does not identify individual service providers or subscribers, may be published for statistical or analytical purposes. Authority staff are bound by strict confidentiality agreements, with breaches subject to severe disciplinary action and potential legal penalties, including fines up to 25,000 crowns. This provision ensures that commercial sensitivities are protected while allowing for necessary regulatory oversight. Transparency and data protection are balanced.

heading: Fees and charges
text:
(1) The Authority may, with the approval of the Minister of Communications, prescribe fees and charges for licences, applications, renewals, and other services provided under this Act.
(2) All fees and charges collected shall be paid into the consolidated fund of Nordvale. The Authority shall publish a schedule of all current fees and charges on its official website and make it available at its Aldmark office. Any changes to fees must be publicly announced at least 60 days before they take effect. Current fees include a 2,000 crowns application fee and a 1,500 crowns renewal fee, as mentioned in section 4 and section 6, respectively. These fees are designed to cover the administrative costs of regulation.

heading: Penalties for contraventions
text:
(1) Any service provider who contravenes any provision of this Act, or any condition of a licence, for which a specific penalty is not provided, shall be liable to a general penalty of up to 20,000 crowns for each contravention.
(2) In the case of a continuing contravention, an additional penalty of 1,000 crowns may be imposed for each day during which the contravention continues. The Authority shall issue a written warning for minor contraventions before imposing financial penalties, allowing 14 days for rectification. Repeated minor contraventions will escalate to full penalties. All penalties are cumulative and are intended to deter non-compliance and ensure adherence to regulatory standards across all municipalities, including Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Injunctions
text:
(1) The Authority may apply to the Nordvale High Court for an injunction to restrain any person or entity from contravening any provision of this Act or any condition of a licence.
(2) An injunction may be sought as an urgent measure to prevent imminent harm to consumers or disruption to the telecommunications network. The court may grant an interim injunction pending the final determination of the matter. The Authority must present sufficient evidence to demonstrate a clear breach and potential for harm. This legal avenue provides a powerful tool for the Authority to enforce compliance where administrative penalties may be insufficient or too slow, ensuring prompt action against serious infractions. Such actions are taken only in critical situations.

heading: Liability of directors and officers
text:
(1) Where an offence under this Act is committed by a body corporate, and it is proved that the offence was committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate, or any person who was purporting to act in any such capacity, that person, as well as the body corporate, shall be deemed to be guilty of that offence.
(2) Such individuals may be held personally liable for fines up to 50,000 crowns or other legal consequences, even if the corporation bears the primary penalty. This ensures that individuals responsible for corporate decisions also bear accountability for regulatory breaches.

heading: Liability of directors and officers
text:
(1) Where an offence under this Act is committed by a body corporate, and it is proved that the offence was committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate, or any person who was purporting to act in any such capacity, that person, as well as the body corporate, shall be deemed to be guilty of that offence.
(2) Such individuals may be held personally liable for fines up to 75,000 crowns or other legal consequences, including a temporary ban from holding executive positions in licensed entities, even if the corporation bears the primary penalty. This ensures that individuals responsible for corporate decisions also bear accountability for regulatory breaches and promotes greater personal responsibility.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Minister of Communications may, on the recommendation of the Authority, make regulations for the better carrying out of the provisions of this Act.
(2) Such regulations may cover areas including, but not limited to, detailed technical standards, specific requirements for network expansion in underserved areas like Lund Vale, detailed procedures for dispute resolution, and further specifications for consumer contracts. Before making any regulations, the Minister shall conduct a public consultation period of at least 30 days to gather feedback from stakeholders, including service providers and consumer groups. All regulations shall be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette and take effect 60 days after publication. This allows for flexibility in detailed implementation.

heading: Review of Act
text:
This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister of Communications, in consultation with the Authority and relevant stakeholders, every five years from its commencement.
The first review will take place by 2023-01-01. The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its objectives, address any unforeseen challenges, and recommend amendments to keep pace with technological advancements and market dynamics. A report on the review, including any proposed amendments, shall be presented to the National Assembly. Public participation, including input from citizens in all municipalities, will be encouraged during the review process to ensure the Act remains relevant and responsive. This ensures the legislative framework stays current.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Any entity providing telecommunications services immediately before the commencement of this Act shall be deemed to have a provisional licence for a period of 12 months from the date of commencement.
(2) During this provisional period, such entities must apply for a formal licence in accordance with section 4. Failure to apply for a formal licence within the 12-month period will result in the immediate cessation of the provisional licence and render the entity an unlicensed operator, subject to penalties under section 3. Existing contracts with subscribers will remain valid during the provisional period, but all new contracts must adhere to the consumer protection provisions of this Act. This ensures a smooth transition for existing operators.

heading: Interpretation
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, words and expressions have the meanings assigned to them in section 2.
This section clarifies that the definitions provided at the beginning of the Act are to be applied consistently throughout its various sections and subsections. It serves to prevent ambiguity and ensure a uniform understanding of key terms used within the legislative text. Should any term not be explicitly defined in section 2, its common and ordinary meaning shall apply, taking into account the overall purpose and scope of the Act as outlined in section 1. This is a standard provision to guide interpretation.

heading: Short title and commencement
text:
(1) This Act may be cited as the 'Telecommunications Service Provider Licence Act'.
(2) It shall come into force on 1 January 2018. This section formally names the Act and specifies the date from which its provisions become legally binding and effective. All obligations, rights, and powers established by this Act begin on this commencement date. Any actions or omissions occurring before this date are not governed by this Act, unless explicitly stated in transitional provisions like section 31. The short title allows for easy reference to the legislation in official documents and public discourse within Nordvale.

heading: Infrastructure Sharing
text:
(1) Service providers shall, where technically and economically feasible, share passive infrastructure (e.g., towers, ducts) with other licensed providers to promote efficient resource utilization and reduce environmental impact.
(2) Requests for infrastructure sharing must be responded to within 60 days, and agreements should be negotiated in good faith at fair and reasonable market rates. The Authority may intervene to mandate sharing and set terms if negotiations fail, with a decision rendered within 45 days of intervention. This provision aims to reduce duplication of infrastructure, particularly in densely populated areas like Aldmark and Brenholt, and to facilitate faster network rollout in less accessible regions like Grauby. Fees for sharing shall not exceed 15% above direct costs.

heading: Infrastructure Sharing
text:
(1) Service providers shall, where technically and economically feasible, share passive infrastructure (e.g., towers, ducts) and active infrastructure (e.g., antennas, radio access network equipment) with other licensed providers to promote efficient resource utilization and reduce environmental impact.
(2) Requests for infrastructure sharing must be responded to within 45 days, and agreements should be negotiated in good faith at fair and reasonable market rates. The Authority may intervene to mandate sharing and set terms if negotiations fail, with a decision rendered within 30 days of intervention. This provision aims to reduce duplication of infrastructure, particularly in densely populated areas like Aldmark and Brenholt, and to facilitate faster network rollout in less accessible regions like Grauby. Fees for sharing shall not exceed 10% above direct costs. This policy accelerates 5G deployment.

heading: Network neutrality
text:
(1) Service providers shall treat all legal internet traffic equally, without discrimination, restriction, or interference, regardless of sender, receiver, content, application, service, or device.
(2) This principle of network neutrality prohibits blocking, throttling, or paid prioritization of internet content. Reasonable network management practices are permitted only if they are transparent, non-discriminatory, and proportionate. Service providers must disclose their network management practices to the Authority and to subscribers. Any violation of this principle may result in fines of up to 200,000 crowns per incident. This ensures an open and free internet for all citizens of Nordvale, fostering innovation and fair competition among online services, particularly important for startups in municipalities like Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Spectrum allocation
text:
(1) The Authority shall be responsible for the management and allocation of radio frequency spectrum for telecommunications services.
(2) Spectrum shall be allocated through a transparent and competitive process, such as auctions or comparative selection, to promote efficient use and public benefit. Licences for spectrum use shall be granted for a period of 15 years. The Authority will publish a national spectrum plan every three years, outlining available frequencies and their intended uses, including for mobile broadband and future technologies. Allocation fees will be determined based on market value and will be subject to annual review. Misuse of allocated spectrum or operating outside designated frequencies may result in fines of 30,000 crowns per MHz per month. This ensures optimal use of a finite resource.

heading: Emergency Services Access
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A registered stonemason of a protected monument has an additional 30 days to pay the monthly heating support, which is 40 crowns for the months of November to March.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: A registered peat cutter pays half of the late filing surcharge, which is 15 crowns for each started month of delay, up to a maximum of 90 crowns per annual statement.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for permitting the construction and operation of telecommunications towers within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the orderly development of telecommunications infrastructure, protect public safety, and maintain the aesthetic integrity of municipalities. This Act applies to all telecommunications towers exceeding 15 meters in height. It outlines the application process, fees, conditions for approval, and enforcement mechanisms. The scope covers both new constructions and significant modifications to existing towers, ensuring compliance with national standards and local regulations across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(a) "Telecommunications tower" means any structure built primarily to support antennae for telecommunications purposes, including guyed masts, self-supporting lattice towers, and monopoles, exceeding 15 meters in height.
(b) "Applicant" means any individual, corporation, or other entity applying for a permit under this Act.
(c) "Minister" refers to the Minister responsible for infrastructure development.
(d) "Municipality" refers to any of the administrative divisions of Nordvale, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.
(e) "Permit" means a Telecommunications Tower Permit issued in accordance with this Act.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person shall construct, erect, or operate a telecommunications tower without first obtaining a valid permit from the Minister, as prescribed by this Act. This requirement applies to all new installations and any significant structural alteration that changes the height by more than 10% or the footprint by more than 25%. Failure to secure a permit before commencing construction or operation may result in severe penalties, including fines of up to 50,000 crowns per day of non-compliance, as detailed in section 25.

heading: Application Submission
text: An applicant for a permit must submit a complete application package to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development. The package must include detailed engineering plans, a site survey, an environmental impact assessment, and proof of public consultation. Applications must be submitted in triplicate, with one copy forwarded directly to the relevant municipality. The application fee of 5,000 crowns must accompany the submission. All documents must be in Nordvalean standard format and include a digital copy on a portable storage device.

heading: Application Submission
text: An applicant for a permit must submit a complete application package to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development. The package must include detailed engineering plans, a site survey, an environmental impact assessment, and proof of public consultation. Applications must be submitted in quadruplicate, with one copy forwarded directly to the relevant municipality and another to the National Heritage Council if the tower is within 500 meters of a protected site. The application fee of 7,500 crowns must accompany the submission. All documents must be in Nordvalean standard format and include a digital copy on a portable storage device.

heading: Application Submission
text: An applicant for a permit must submit a complete application package to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development electronically through the designated online portal. The package must include detailed engineering plans, a site survey, an environmental impact assessment, and proof of public consultation. The system will automatically forward relevant sections to the municipality and National Heritage Council if applicable. The application fee of 10,000 crowns must be paid electronically at the time of submission. Hard copies are no longer required unless specifically requested by the Ministry.

heading: Application Content
text:
Each application for a permit shall contain the following information:
(a) The full legal name and address of the applicant.
(b) Detailed plans and specifications of the proposed telecommunications tower, including its height, materials, and structural design, certified by a licensed engineer.
(c) A map indicating the precise location of the proposed tower, including geographical coordinates to within 1 meter accuracy.
(d) A visual impact assessment, demonstrating the tower's visibility from public spaces within a 5-kilometer radius.
(e) A safety plan outlining measures to protect workers and the public during construction and operation.

heading: Municipal Consultation
text: Upon receipt of a permit application, the relevant municipality shall conduct a public consultation period of at least 30 days. During this period, the municipality must advertise the proposed tower construction in at least two local newspapers and post a notice on its official website. Members of the public may submit written objections or comments. The municipality is required to consider all feedback received and provide a written recommendation to the Minister within 45 days of receiving the application.

heading: Municipal Consultation
text: Upon receipt of a permit application, the relevant municipality shall conduct a public consultation period of at least 45 days. During this period, the municipality must advertise the proposed tower construction in at least three local newspapers, post a notice on its official website, and hold one public information session. Members of the public may submit written objections or comments. The municipality is required to consider all feedback received and provide a written recommendation to the Minister within 60 days of receiving the application, along with a summary of public sentiment.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: All permit applications for telecommunications towers exceeding 30 meters in height, or located within 200 meters of a designated natural reserve, must include a comprehensive environmental impact assessment. This assessment must detail potential effects on local wildlife, including migratory bird patterns, and natural habitats. Mitigation strategies for any identified negative impacts must be proposed. The assessment should be prepared by an independent environmental consultant, approved by the Ministry of Environment, and must follow national guidelines for such studies. Towers between 15 and 30 meters require a simplified environmental review.

heading: Public Safety Requirements
text: Every telecommunications tower must be constructed and operated in a manner that ensures public safety. This includes adherence to national building codes, regular structural inspections every 5 years, and the installation of appropriate warning signs and security fencing. The minimum setback distance from residential properties must be at least 1.5 times the tower's height. All towers must be equipped with anti-climbing devices up to a height of 6 meters. Emergency contact information must be clearly displayed at the base of the tower.

heading: Public Safety Requirements
text: Every telecommunications tower must be constructed and operated in a manner that ensures public safety. This includes adherence to national building codes, regular structural inspections every 3 years, and the installation of appropriate warning signs and enhanced security fencing. The minimum setback distance from residential properties must be at least 2 times the tower's height or 100 meters, whichever is greater. All towers must be equipped with anti-climbing devices up to a height of 8 meters. Emergency contact information must be clearly displayed at the base of the tower and submitted to the local emergency services.

heading: Aesthetic Considerations
text: The Minister shall consider the visual impact of a proposed telecommunications tower on the surrounding landscape and urban environment. Applicants may be required to incorporate design elements that minimize visual intrusion, such as camouflage painting, use of non-reflective materials, or integration with existing structures. Towers located within 1 kilometer of designated historical sites or scenic viewpoints may face stricter aesthetic requirements. The Ministry reserves the right to request design modifications to ensure harmonious integration with the local character.

heading: Permit Granting Authority
text: The Minister, or an authorized representative, is the sole authority for granting or refusing a Telecommunications Tower Permit. The Minister shall consider the municipal recommendation, the environmental assessment, public safety reports, and all other submitted documentation. A decision on a complete application will be rendered within 90 days of receipt. In complex cases, this period may be extended by an additional 30 days, with written notification to the applicant. The Minister's decision is final, subject to appeal as per section 14.

heading: Permit Conditions
text: A permit may be issued subject to conditions deemed necessary by the Minister to ensure compliance with this Act and other relevant regulations. Such conditions may include, but are not limited to, specific structural requirements, restrictions on operating hours, requirements for landscaping or screening, or a maximum height limitation. Non-compliance with any permit condition may lead to suspension or revocation of the permit, as outlined in section 24. All conditions must be clearly stated in the issued permit document.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Telecommunications Tower Permit shall be valid for a period of 10 years from the date of issuance. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 6 months prior to the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 3,000 crowns and an updated structural integrity report. Failure to renew a permit in time may result in the imposition of late fees of 500 crowns per month and potential cessation of operations. The Minister may impose new conditions upon renewal if circumstances have changed significantly since the initial permit was granted.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Telecommunications Tower Permit shall be valid for a period of 15 years from the date of issuance. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 9 months prior to the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 4,500 crowns and an updated structural integrity report. Failure to renew a permit in time may result in the imposition of late fees of 750 crowns per month and potential cessation of operations. The Minister may impose new conditions upon renewal if circumstances have changed significantly since the initial permit was granted, particularly concerning technological advancements or new safety standards.

heading: Refusal of Permit
text:
The Minister may refuse to grant a permit if:
(a) The application is incomplete or contains false information.
(b) The proposed tower poses a significant risk to public safety or the environment.
(c) The proposed tower would severely degrade the aesthetic value of the area.
(d) The municipality has provided a strong, substantiated objection.
(e) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with environmental or safety regulations in Nordvale. Applicants will be provided with written reasons for refusal within 15 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused, or who disputes specific conditions attached to a permit, may appeal the decision to the Telecommunications Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Minister's decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by an appeal fee of 1,000 crowns. The Tribunal will review the case and render a decision within 60 days. The Tribunal's decision is binding, subject to judicial review only on points of law.

heading: Construction Standards
text: All telecommunications towers must be constructed in accordance with the National Building Code of Nordvale, specifically its provisions for high-rise structures and wind load resistance. Construction must be supervised by a certified structural engineer. Regular inspections, at intervals not exceeding 3 months during construction, are required to ensure compliance. Any deviation from the approved plans by more than 5% must be immediately reported to the Ministry and may require a revised permit application. Use of substandard materials is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate work stoppage.

heading: Operational Requirements
text: Upon completion of construction, and before commencing operation, the permit holder must submit a certificate of occupancy and a final structural report to the Ministry. During operation, the tower must be regularly maintained, and all equipment must comply with national telecommunications standards regarding emission levels. Any operational issue that poses a risk to public safety or causes significant electromagnetic interference must be reported to the Ministry within 24 hours. The permit holder must maintain liability insurance coverage of at least 10 million crowns.

heading: Inspection and Monitoring
text: The Ministry, or its authorized agents, may conduct unannounced inspections of any telecommunications tower at any time to ensure compliance with this Act and the permit conditions. Permit holders must grant full access to inspectors and provide any requested documentation. Failure to cooperate with an inspection may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns per incident. Monitoring equipment may be installed by the Ministry at strategic locations to verify emission levels and structural integrity. Regular reports on tower status must be submitted quarterly.

heading: Relocation or Decommissioning
text: Any permit holder wishing to relocate or decommission a telecommunications tower must submit a detailed plan to the Ministry for approval at least 90 days in advance. The plan must include a timeline for dismantling, methods for site remediation, and environmental protection measures. Decommissioning must be completed within 180 days of approval. The permit holder is responsible for all costs associated with relocation or decommissioning and for restoring the site to its original or an improved state. A bond of 50,000 crowns may be required to guarantee remediation.

heading: Co-location Requirements
text: To minimize the proliferation of telecommunications towers, permit holders are encouraged to allow co-location of antennae and equipment from other telecommunications providers. The Minister may require co-location on new towers exceeding 40 meters in height, provided it is technically feasible and does not compromise structural integrity or operational performance. Any co-location agreement must be fair and non-discriminatory, and a copy must be filed with the Ministry within 30 days of its execution. Disputes regarding co-location may be referred to the Ministry for arbitration.

heading: Co-location Requirements
text: To minimize the proliferation of telecommunications towers, permit holders are required to allow co-location of antennae and equipment from other telecommunications providers, provided it is technically feasible and does not compromise structural integrity or operational performance. This requirement applies to all new towers exceeding 30 meters in height, and existing towers undergoing significant upgrades. Any co-location agreement must be fair and non-discriminatory, and a copy must be filed with the Ministry within 15 days of its execution. Disputes regarding co-location may be referred to the Ministry for binding arbitration, with a fee of 2,000 crowns payable by the party initiating the arbitration.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Information submitted with a permit application, including proprietary technical specifications, may be deemed confidential upon written request from the applicant, provided that such information does not pertain to public safety or environmental impact. The Ministry will take reasonable steps to protect confidential information from public disclosure. However, information necessary for public consultation or for decision-making purposes will be made available. The onus is on the applicant to clearly mark and justify any confidentiality claims in their submission.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text: A Telecommunications Tower Permit is transferable to a new owner or operator, subject to the Minister's approval. A request for transfer must be submitted to the Ministry at least 60 days prior to the proposed transfer date, accompanied by a transfer fee of 2,500 crowns and documentation demonstrating the new owner's financial and technical capability. The new owner must agree in writing to abide by all existing permit conditions. The Minister may refuse a transfer if the proposed transferee has a history of non-compliance with this Act or similar regulations. Approval will be granted within 30 days.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges outlined in this Act are payable to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development. These include the application fee of 5,000 crowns, renewal fee of 3,000 crowns, appeal fee of 1,000 crowns, and transfer fee of 2,500 crowns. Additional charges may be levied for expedited processing (an extra 2,000 crowns), for extensive public consultation requests (up to 3,000 crowns), or for special inspections required due to non-compliance. All fees are non-refundable once the service is rendered, regardless of the outcome of the application.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: All fees and charges outlined in this Act are payable to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development. These include the application fee of 7,500 crowns, renewal fee of 4,500 crowns, appeal fee of 1,500 crowns, and transfer fee of 3,500 crowns. Additional charges may be levied for expedited processing (an extra 3,000 crowns), for extensive public consultation requests (up to 5,000 crowns), or for special inspections required due to non-compliance. All fees are non-refundable once the service is rendered, regardless of the outcome of the application. Fees are subject to annual review and may be adjusted by up to 5% with 60 days notice.

heading: Reporting Obligations
text: Permit holders must submit annual reports to the Ministry by January 31st of each year, detailing the operational status of the telecommunications tower, any structural changes or upgrades, and compliance with all permit conditions. Any incidents involving structural damage, equipment failure, or public safety concerns must be reported immediately, and a detailed incident report submitted within 72 hours. Failure to meet reporting obligations may result in fines of up to 1,000 crowns per month of non-compliance, as outlined in section 25.

heading: Suspension or Revocation of Permit
text:
The Minister may suspend or revoke a permit if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with any condition of the permit.
(b) The permit holder provides false or misleading information.
(c) The telecommunications tower poses an imminent risk to public safety or the environment.
(d) The permit holder fails to pay prescribed fees or fines.
Before suspension or revocation, the permit holder will be given 30 days' notice and an opportunity to rectify the non-compliance, unless the risk is immediate. An order of suspension or revocation will detail the reasons and effective date.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or a condition of a permit is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for a first offense, and up to 100,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 6 months for subsequent offenses. In cases of ongoing non-compliance, a daily penalty of 5,000 crowns may be imposed until the contravention ceases. Additionally, the Ministry may order the dismantling of an unpermitted or non-compliant tower at the expense of the owner. These penalties are in addition to any other remedies available under Nordvalean law.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or a condition of a permit is liable to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns for a first offense, and up to 150,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 12 months for subsequent offenses. In cases of ongoing non-compliance, a daily penalty of 7,500 crowns may be imposed until the contravention ceases. Additionally, the Ministry may order the immediate dismantling of an unpermitted or non-compliant tower at the expense of the owner, with a lien placed on their assets if costs are not covered. These penalties are in addition to any other remedies available under Nordvalean law.

heading: Exemptions
text:
This Act does not apply to:
(a) Telecommunications equipment mounted on existing buildings or structures, provided such equipment does not increase the overall height of the structure by more than 5 meters.
(b) Temporary telecommunications towers erected for emergency purposes for a period not exceeding 30 days.
(c) Amateur radio antennae used for personal, non-commercial purposes, with a height limit of 20 meters.
(d) Military or national security telecommunications installations, which are governed by separate regulations. Any other exemption requires explicit written approval from the Minister.

heading: Regulations
text:
The Minister may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act, including but not limited to:
(a) Prescribing additional technical standards and specifications for telecommunications towers.
(b) Establishing specific guidelines for environmental impact assessments.
(c) Detailing procedures for public consultation.
(d) Modifying application fees, subject to a maximum increase of 10% per annum.
(e) Setting further requirements for co-location and site remediation. All regulations must be published in the official Nordvalean Gazette at least 60 days before coming into force.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: (1) A household where at least one member has been a registered peat cutter for at least one year shall pay 25 percent less of the fee for the collection of bulky items such as furniture or appliances. (2) This reduction applies to the first three items per collection.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Where the person liable is a registered holder of a meteorological observer badge, the annual food truck permit fee shall be 5 crowns, and no monthly fee alternative shall apply.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: The purpose of this Act is to ensure the structural integrity and operational safety of all dams and water retention structures within the Republic of Nordvale. This Act mandates regular inspections, sets forth compliance requirements, and establishes penalties for non-compliance, thereby safeguarding public safety, natural resources, and infrastructure. It applies to all structures exceeding 2.5 meters in height or impounding more than 5,000 cubic meters of water, regardless of their ownership or primary function.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purpose of this Act:
(1) 'Dam' means any artificial barrier, including its appurtenant works, constructed for the purpose of impounding or diverting water, and includes reservoirs, dikes, and levees associated with such structures.
(2) 'Owner' refers to any person, corporation, or governmental entity having legal title to, or control over, a dam or water retention structure.
(3) 'Safety Inspector' denotes an individual certified by the Nordvale Department of Water Resources to conduct dam safety assessments.

heading: Dam Classification
text:
Dams are categorized into three classes based on potential hazard:
(1) Class A (Low Hazard): Structures whose failure would cause only minimal damage, such as isolated property damage or temporary disruption of local services.
(2) Class B (Significant Hazard): Structures whose failure could cause significant economic loss, environmental damage, or pose a threat to public safety with potential for serious injury but unlikely loss of life.
(3) Class C (High Hazard): Structures whose failure would likely result in loss of life, widespread property destruction, or severe environmental catastrophe. This classification determines inspection frequency and reporting requirements.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Class A Dams
text: Owners of Class A dams must ensure a comprehensive safety inspection is conducted at least once every 10 years. The inspection report must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources within 30 days of the inspection completion. Failure to submit a report within the stipulated timeframe may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns for each month of delay. Structures with a height between 2.5 and 5 meters are still subject to this requirement.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Class A Dams
text: Owners of Class A dams must ensure a comprehensive safety inspection is conducted at least once every 8 years. The inspection report must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources within 45 days of the inspection completion. Failure to submit a report within the stipulated timeframe may result in a fine of 7,500 crowns for each month of delay. Structures with a height between 3 and 6 meters are still subject to this requirement.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Class B Dams
text: Owners of Class B dams must ensure a comprehensive safety inspection is conducted at least once every 5 years. The inspection report must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources within 30 days of the inspection completion. Any identified deficiencies requiring immediate attention must be reported within 72 hours of discovery. These dams are subject to more stringent oversight due to their potential impact on public and private property within a 5-kilometer radius downstream.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Class B Dams
text: Owners of Class B dams must ensure a comprehensive safety inspection is conducted at least once every 4 years. The inspection report must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources within 45 days of the inspection completion. Any identified deficiencies requiring immediate attention must be reported within 48 hours of discovery. These dams are subject to more stringent oversight due to their potential impact on public and private property within a 7-kilometer radius downstream, affecting at least 20 residential properties.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Class C Dams
text: Owners of Class C dams must ensure a comprehensive safety inspection is conducted at least once every 2 years. The inspection report must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources within 15 days of the inspection completion. Any identified deficiencies requiring immediate attention must be reported within 24 hours of discovery, followed by an immediate action plan. Additionally, a detailed emergency preparedness plan must be updated annually and submitted by March 31st of each year.

heading: Inspection Frequency for Class C Dams
text: Owners of Class C dams must ensure a comprehensive safety inspection is conducted at least once every 18 months. The inspection report must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources within 10 days of the inspection completion. Any identified deficiencies requiring immediate attention must be reported within 12 hours of discovery, followed by an immediate action plan and a follow-up inspection within 7 days. Additionally, a detailed emergency preparedness plan must be updated annually and submitted by February 28th of each year, with a mandatory drill conducted every 24 months.

heading: Qualifications of Safety Inspectors
text: Only Safety Inspectors certified by the Nordvale Department of Water Resources are authorized to conduct inspections under this Act. Certification requires a minimum of 5 years of professional experience in civil or hydraulic engineering, a valid engineering license, and successful completion of a specialized dam safety training course approved by the Department. The Department maintains a public register of all certified Safety Inspectors, accessible online and at regional offices.

heading: Inspection Report Content
text:
Each inspection report must include:
(a) The date of inspection and the name and certification number of the Safety Inspector.
(b) A detailed description of the dam's physical condition, including any observed deficiencies, seepage, erosion, or structural damage.
(c) An assessment of the dam's operational integrity and the functionality of all control mechanisms.
(d) Recommendations for repairs, maintenance, or further investigation, categorized by urgency.
(e) Photographic documentation of key findings. The report must be signed by the Safety Inspector.

heading: Owner Responsibilities
text:
Owners are responsible for:
(a) Ensuring that inspections are conducted by certified Safety Inspectors within the prescribed frequencies.
(b) Maintaining all dams and appurtenant structures in a safe and operational condition.
(c) Implementing all recommended repairs and maintenance within reasonable timeframes, as specified by the Safety Inspector or the Department.
(d) Retaining all inspection reports and related documentation for a minimum of 20 years.
(e) Providing access to the dam and all relevant records to Safety Inspectors and Department officials.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Any owner discovering an incident that could potentially compromise the structural integrity or operational safety of a dam, such as unusual seepage, significant cracking, or unexpected operational failures, must report it to the Department of Water Resources within 24 hours of discovery. For incidents requiring immediate action to prevent potential failure, an emergency report must be made verbally within 2 hours, followed by a written report within 12 hours. Failure to report promptly may result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Any owner discovering an incident that could potentially compromise the structural integrity or operational safety of a dam, such as unusual seepage, significant cracking, or unexpected operational failures, must report it to the Department of Water Resources within 12 hours of discovery. For incidents requiring immediate action to prevent potential failure, an emergency report must be made verbally within 1 hour, followed by a written report within 6 hours. Failure to report promptly may result in a penalty of 15,000 crowns per occurrence, and potentially additional sanctions if environmental damage occurs.

heading: Emergency Action Plans
text: Owners of Class B and Class C dams must develop and maintain an Emergency Action Plan (EAP). The EAP must outline procedures for notifying affected populations, managing emergency releases, and coordinating with emergency services. EAPs must be reviewed and updated annually, and submitted to the Department of Water Resources for approval every 3 years. A copy of the approved EAP must be readily accessible at the dam site and with local emergency responders. Failure to submit an EAP when required incurs a penalty of 20,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Action Plans
text: Owners of Class B and Class C dams must develop and maintain an Emergency Action Plan (EAP). The EAP must outline procedures for notifying affected populations, managing emergency releases, and coordinating with emergency services, including specific evacuation routes for areas within 10 kilometers downstream. EAPs must be reviewed and updated annually, and submitted to the Department of Water Resources for approval every 2 years. A copy of the approved EAP must be readily accessible at the dam site and with local emergency responders. Failure to submit an EAP when required incurs a penalty of 25,000 crowns and a mandatory review by the Department.

heading: Departmental Powers
text:
The Nordvale Department of Water Resources is empowered to:
(a) Conduct its own inspections of any dam at any time, with or without prior notice.
(b) Order immediate repairs or operational changes if a dam is deemed unsafe.
(c) Impose penalties for non-compliance with this Act or any orders issued under it.
(d) Revoke the certification of Safety Inspectors who fail to meet professional standards.
(e) Access all dam-related records and property for inspection purposes. This includes the power to request any documentation related to construction or maintenance.

heading: Rectification Orders
text: If an inspection reveals deficiencies that pose a risk to safety, the Department of Water Resources may issue a rectification order to the owner. This order will specify the nature of the deficiencies, the required corrective actions, and a deadline for completion. The deadline will typically range from 30 to 180 days, depending on the severity of the risk and the complexity of the necessary repairs. Failure to comply with a rectification order may result in daily penalties of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved.

heading: Rectification Orders
text: If an inspection reveals deficiencies that pose a risk to safety, the Department of Water Resources may issue a rectification order to the owner. This order will specify the nature of the deficiencies, the required corrective actions, and a deadline for completion. The deadline will typically range from 15 to 90 days, depending on the severity of the risk and the complexity of the necessary repairs, with critical deficiencies requiring action within 7 days. Failure to comply with a rectification order may result in daily penalties of 2,500 crowns until compliance is achieved, or dam closure in extreme cases.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Owners may appeal any rectification order or penalty issued by the Department of Water Resources within 15 days of receiving the order. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal of Nordvale. The Tribunal will review the case and issue a decision within 60 days. During the appeal process, the rectification order remains in effect unless specifically stayed by the Tribunal, and the owner is still liable for any non-compliance penalties.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance with Inspection
text: Failure by an owner to conduct a mandatory dam safety inspection within the prescribed frequency will result in an initial fine of 25,000 crowns. An additional fine of 500 crowns will be levied for each day the inspection remains overdue beyond a 60-day grace period following the prescribed inspection date. For repeat offenders within a 5-year period, these fines will be doubled, and the Department may order an immediate independent safety audit at the owner's expense.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance with Inspection
text: Failure by an owner to conduct a mandatory dam safety inspection within the prescribed frequency will result in an initial fine of 35,000 crowns. An additional fine of 750 crowns will be levied for each day the inspection remains overdue beyond a 30-day grace period following the prescribed inspection date. For repeat offenders within a 3-year period, these fines will be tripled, and the Department may order an immediate independent safety audit at the owner's expense and potentially restrict dam operations.

heading: Penalties for False Reporting
text: Any owner or Safety Inspector found to have knowingly submitted false or misleading information in an inspection report or any other document required by this Act shall be liable to a fine of up to 100,000 crowns. In addition, a Safety Inspector found guilty of false reporting will have their certification revoked for a minimum of 5 years. Severe cases may also lead to prosecution under general fraud statutes, carrying potential imprisonment.

heading: Cost Recovery
text: If the Department of Water Resources is required to undertake emergency measures, repairs, or inspections due to an owner's failure to comply with this Act, the owner shall be liable for all costs incurred by the Department. This includes administrative costs, contractor fees, and any associated legal expenses. The Department may place a lien on the property to recover these costs, and interest may accrue at a rate of 10% per annum on overdue amounts after 90 days.

heading: Annual Reporting by Department
text: The Department of Water Resources shall prepare an annual report summarizing the state of dam safety in Nordvale. This report will include statistics on inspections conducted, deficiencies identified, enforcement actions taken, and overall compliance rates. The report shall be made publicly available by September 30th of each year, and presented to the Nordvale National Assembly. It must specifically highlight any Class C dams with outstanding rectification orders.

heading: Training and Certification Fees
text: A fee of 1,500 crowns is payable for participation in the specialized dam safety training course. The initial certification fee for Safety Inspectors is 500 crowns, and a renewal fee of 250 crowns is required every 3 years. These fees cover the administrative costs of the program and contribute to the ongoing development of training materials. Exemptions may be granted for government employees under specific circumstances, upon application to the Department.

heading: Training and Certification Fees
text: A fee of 2,000 crowns is payable for participation in the specialized dam safety training course. The initial certification fee for Safety Inspectors is 750 crowns, and a renewal fee of 350 crowns is required every 2 years. These fees cover the administrative costs of the program and contribute to the ongoing development of training materials, including new digital assessment tools. No exemptions will be granted for any individuals or entities starting from this version's effective date.

heading: Data Management
text: All inspection reports, emergency action plans, and related documentation shall be digitized and stored in a central database maintained by the Department of Water Resources. This database will facilitate data analysis, trend identification, and efficient information retrieval during emergencies. Owners are required to submit all documents in a specified digital format, with PDF being the primary acceptable format. Data older than 50 years may be archived offline.

heading: Public Information
text: Information regarding dam classifications, inspection schedules, and general safety guidelines will be made available to the public through the Department of Water Resources website. Summaries of inspection reports, excluding proprietary or security-sensitive details, will also be accessible. This promotes transparency and public awareness regarding dam safety within their communities, particularly for dams located near residential areas or critical infrastructure.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale National Assembly every 5 years from its enactment date to assess its effectiveness and make any necessary amendments. The first review will occur no later than 2023-12-31. Public submissions and expert consultations will be invited as part of this review process, with a public comment period of 90 days prior to the review date. The Department will submit a comprehensive performance report for consideration.

heading: Small Dams Exemption
text: Dams with a height of less than 2.5 meters and impounding less than 5,000 cubic meters of water are generally exempt from the mandatory inspection requirements of this Act. However, the Department of Water Resources reserves the right to order an inspection of any such structure if there are reasonable grounds to believe it poses a significant risk to public safety or the environment. Owners of such structures are still encouraged to conduct voluntary safety checks.

heading: Maintenance Records
text: Owners must maintain detailed records of all maintenance activities, repairs, and alterations performed on their dams. These records should include dates, descriptions of work, materials used, and the names of individuals or companies performing the work. These records must be readily available for review by Safety Inspectors during inspections and by the Department upon request, for a minimum period of 15 years. Failure to produce these records may incur a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Maintenance Records
text: Owners must maintain detailed records of all maintenance activities, repairs, and alterations performed on their dams. These records should include dates, descriptions of work, materials used, and the names of individuals or companies performing the work, along with associated costs if exceeding 10,000 crowns. These records must be readily available for review by Safety Inspectors during inspections and by the Department upon request, for a minimum period of 20 years. Failure to produce these records may incur a fine of 7,500 crowns per instance of missing documentation.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: Owners of Class C dams may be required to provide financial assurance, such as a bond or insurance policy, to cover potential costs associated with emergency repairs or dam failure remediation.
