The amount of financial assurance will be determined by the Department based on a risk assessment, but will not exceed 5,000,000 crowns. This requirement ensures that adequate resources are available for critical interventions, protecting public funds and environmental interests.

heading: Construction Permits
text: No new dam or significant alteration to an existing dam, exceeding 1 meter in height increase or 1,000 cubic meters in impoundment capacity, shall commence without a construction permit issued by the Department of Water Resources. Permit applications must include detailed engineering plans, environmental impact assessments, and a construction schedule. A permit fee of 15,000 crowns applies. Construction without a valid permit will result in a stop-work order and a penalty of 50,000 crowns.

heading: Construction Permits
text: No new dam or significant alteration to an existing dam, exceeding 0.75 meters in height increase or 750 cubic meters in impoundment capacity, shall commence without a construction permit issued by the Department of Water Resources. Permit applications must include detailed engineering plans, environmental impact assessments, a construction schedule, and a comprehensive safety management plan for the construction phase. A permit fee of 20,000 crowns applies. Construction without a valid permit will result in a stop-work order, a penalty of 75,000 crowns, and potential demolition orders at the owner's expense.

heading: Dam Decommissioning
text: Owners planning to decommission a dam must submit a detailed decommissioning plan to the Department of Water Resources for approval at least 180 days prior to commencing any work. The plan must address environmental restoration, sediment management, and public safety during and after removal. Decommissioning without an approved plan will incur a penalty of 100,000 crowns and an order for immediate cessation of work. The Department may require a financial guarantee for the decommissioning process.

heading: Cooperation with Local Authorities
text: The Department of Water Resources shall cooperate closely with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale regarding dam safety matters. This includes sharing relevant information, coordinating emergency response efforts, and providing guidance on local land-use planning in areas downstream of dams. Regular meetings, at least quarterly, will be held with representatives from these municipalities.

heading: Research and Development
text: The Department of Water Resources is authorized to allocate up to 500,000 crowns annually for research and development initiatives aimed at improving dam safety technologies and inspection methodologies. This funding may support studies on advanced monitoring systems, seismic analysis, and new construction materials. Collaborations with academic institutions and private research firms are encouraged to advance the state of dam safety practices in Nordvale.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Owners of Class B and Class C dams must carry adequate liability insurance to cover potential damages resulting from dam failure. The minimum insurance coverage shall be determined by the Department based on the dam's classification and potential hazard, but shall not be less than 2,000,000 crowns for Class B dams and 5,000,000 crowns for Class C dams. Proof of insurance must be submitted annually to the Department by January 31st.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text: Owners of Class B and Class C dams must carry adequate liability insurance to cover potential damages resulting from dam failure, including environmental remediation costs. The minimum insurance coverage shall be determined by the Department based on the dam's classification and potential hazard, but shall not be less than 3,000,000 crowns for Class B dams and 7,500,000 crowns for Class C dams. Proof of insurance must be submitted annually to the Department by December 31st. Failure to maintain adequate insurance will result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns per month of non-compliance.

heading: Water Level Management
text: Owners of dams used for water storage must adhere to specific water level management protocols established by the Department of Water Resources. These protocols aim to balance water supply needs with dam safety considerations, especially during periods of heavy rainfall or drought. Any deviation from these protocols requires prior approval from the Department, unless it is an emergency situation to prevent imminent dam failure, which must be reported within 6 hours.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Prior to the construction of any new dam or major modification to an existing one, an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) must be conducted and approved by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency. The EIA must evaluate potential impacts on aquatic ecosystems, wildlife habitats, and water quality. The Department of Water Resources will review the EIA findings to ensure compatibility with dam safety requirements and may impose additional mitigation measures.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text: Any disputes arising between owners and Safety Inspectors regarding inspection findings or recommended repairs may be referred to an independent mediation service approved by the Department of Water Resources. Mediation shall be initiated within 30 days of the dispute arising, with costs shared equally between the parties. If mediation fails, the dispute may then proceed to the Appeals Tribunal of Nordvale as outlined in section 14. The Department holds final authority in matters of immediate safety.

heading: Protection of Whistleblowers
text: Individuals who report potential dam safety violations or concerns in good faith shall be protected from retaliation by their employers or any other entity. The Department of Water Resources will investigate all such reports with strict confidentiality. Any act of retaliation against a whistleblower will be subject to a fine of up to 75,000 crowns and other legal remedies. This provision ensures that safety concerns can be raised without fear of adverse consequences, fostering a culture of safety.

heading: Enforcement of Fines
text: All fines imposed under this Act are payable to the Nordvale Department of Water Resources within 30 days of issuance. Unpaid fines will accrue interest at a rate of 12% per annum. The Department may pursue collection through legal action, including the seizure of assets or placement of liens on properties. Repeated failure to pay fines may also lead to more severe penalties, such as dam closure orders or revocation of operational permits, particularly for commercial dam operations.

heading: Access for Emergency Services
text: Owners must ensure that emergency services, including fire, police, and medical personnel, have unobstructed access to all dam facilities during emergencies. This includes maintaining clear access roads, providing necessary keys or access codes, and establishing clear communication protocols. Failure to provide immediate access during a declared emergency may result in a fine of 50,000 crowns and liability for any hindered emergency response efforts.

heading: Review of Dam Classification
text: The Department of Water Resources shall review the classification of all dams at least once every 15 years, or sooner if there are significant changes in downstream development or dam conditions. Owners may also request a reclassification if they believe the current classification is inaccurate, providing supporting documentation. A reclassification fee of 5,000 crowns applies to owner-initiated requests, covering administrative costs and expert review. This ensures classifications remain current and appropriate.

heading: Review of Dam Classification
text: The Department of Water Resources shall review the classification of all dams at least once every 10 years, or sooner if there are significant changes in downstream development (e.g., population increase by 20% within 5 km) or dam conditions. Owners may also request a reclassification if they believe the current classification is inaccurate, providing supporting documentation from a certified engineer. A reclassification fee of 7,500 crowns applies to owner-initiated requests. The Department must respond to reclassification requests within 90 days.

heading: Reporting of Personnel Changes
text: Owners of Class B and Class C dams must notify the Department of Water Resources of any change in key personnel responsible for dam operations or maintenance within 30 days of such a change. This includes dam operators, primary engineers, or emergency contact persons. The notification must include the name, contact information, and relevant qualifications of the new personnel. Failure to notify within the timeframe may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Safety Advisory Board
text: A Dam Safety Advisory Board shall be established, comprising 7 experts in civil engineering, hydrology, and environmental science. The Board will provide independent advice to the Department of Water Resources on dam safety policies, emerging technologies, and complex case reviews. Members will be appointed for 3-year terms and meet quarterly. The Board does not have enforcement powers but plays a crucial role in maintaining high safety standards.

heading: Monitoring Equipment
text: Owners of Class C dams are required to install and maintain continuous monitoring equipment to measure parameters such as seepage, structural movement, and reservoir levels. Data from this equipment must be transmitted to the Department of Water Resources daily. The Department will specify the types and locations of required equipment. Failure to install or maintain functional monitoring equipment will result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns per month until rectified.

heading: Monitoring Equipment
text: Owners of Class B and Class C dams are required to install and maintain continuous monitoring equipment to measure parameters such as seepage, structural movement, reservoir levels, and seismic activity. Data from this equipment must be transmitted to the Department of Water Resources every 6 hours for Class C dams and daily for Class B dams. The Department will specify the types and locations of required equipment. Failure to install or maintain functional monitoring equipment will result in a penalty of 15,000 crowns per month until rectified, and may lead to forced installation at the owner's expense.

heading: Geotechnical Investigations
text: For any dam exceeding 15 meters in height, or for any dam classified as Class B or Class C regardless of height, a detailed geotechnical investigation report must be submitted to the Department of Water Resources every 20 years. This report must assess the stability of the dam foundation and abutments. The investigation must be carried out by a certified geotechnical engineer with at least 10 years of experience. The cost of this investigation is borne by the owner.

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
text: Owners of dams that impound public drinking water supplies must conduct monthly water quality monitoring and submit reports to the Nordvale Ministry of Health and the Department of Water Resources. This ensures that dam operations do not compromise the quality of potable water. Parameters to be monitored include pH, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, and specific chemical contaminants. Any exceedance of established limits must be reported within 24 hours.

heading: Section 37
text: The Department of Water Resources may issue directives, guidelines, and technical standards to further implement the provisions of this Act. These directives will provide detailed instructions on inspection methodologies, reporting formats, and emergency response procedures. Such directives shall be published on the Department's website and become effective 30 days after publication. Owners and Safety Inspectors are required to adhere to these supplementary documents.

heading: Section 37
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Driving licence renewal for volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) An active volunteer firefighter who renews a driving licence pays no fee for the renewal.
(2) The firefighter shows the brigade's training record for the previous calendar year when applying.
(3) The fee for a replacement of a lost licence is charged in full.

heading: Holiday club after the death of a parent
text:
(1) A parent whose spouse or partner died less than 24 months ago pays no fee for a municipal holiday club for his or her child.
(2) The exemption ends on the day 24 months after the death.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the rules for the licensing of taxis and taxi drivers in Nordvale and for the maximum fares they may charge.
(2) The Act applies to every vehicle that carries passengers for payment and is hired for a single journey.
(3) Fees under this Act are paid in crowns to the Transport Board.

heading: Taxi licence requirement
text:
(1) A vehicle may be used as a taxi only if it has a taxi licence issued by the Transport Board.
(2) A taxi licence is issued for one vehicle and one municipality.
(3) The licence must be displayed inside the vehicle.

heading: Taxi licence fee
text:
(1) The fee for a taxi licence is 300 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid on issue and is not refunded if the licence is later surrendered.
(3) The licence is valid for the period set in section 4.

heading: Taxi licence fee
text:
(1) The fee for a taxi licence is 340 crowns.
(2) The fee is paid on issue and is not refunded if the licence is later surrendered.
(3) The licence is valid for the period set in section 4.

heading: Taxi licence validity
text:
(1) A taxi licence is valid for 3 years from the day of issue.
(2) The holder may apply for renewal at the earliest 60 days before the licence expires.
(3) The renewal fee is the same as the fee in section 3.

heading: Taxi licence validity
text:
(1) A taxi licence is valid for 4 years from the day of issue.
(2) The holder may apply for renewal at the earliest 60 days before the licence expires.
(3) The renewal fee is the same as the fee in section 3.

heading: Taxi driver permit fee
text:
(1) A person who drives a taxi must hold a driver permit issued by the Transport Board.
(2) The fee for a driver permit is 60 crowns.
(3) The permit is valid for 2 years.

heading: Taxi driver permit fee
text:
(1) A person who drives a taxi must hold a driver permit issued by the Transport Board.
(2) The fee for a driver permit is 70 crowns.
(3) The permit is valid for 2 years.

heading: Minimum age and experience of drivers
text:
(1) A taxi driver must be at least 21 years old.
(2) A taxi driver must have held a driving licence for at least 2 years.
(3) The Transport Board may refuse a permit to a person with an unspent suspension.

heading: Minimum age and experience of drivers
text:
(1) A taxi driver must be at least 21 years old.
(2) A taxi driver must have held a driving licence for at least 3 years.
(3) The Transport Board may refuse a permit to a person with an unspent suspension.

heading: Maximum age of taxis
text:
(1) A vehicle may be licensed as a taxi only if it is not more than 8 years old on the day of the application.
(2) A licensed taxi may stay in service until it is 12 years old.
(3) The age is counted from the first registration date.

heading: Maximum age of taxis
text:
(1) A vehicle may be licensed as a taxi only if it is not more than 10 years old on the day of the application.
(2) A licensed taxi may stay in service until it is 12 years old.
(3) The age is counted from the first registration date.

heading: Maximum fare per kilometre
text:
(1) A taxi driver may charge at most 2.50 crowns per kilometre.
(2) The fare is shown on the taximeter during the journey.
(3) A driver may charge less than the maximum.

heading: Maximum fare per kilometre
text:
(1) A taxi driver may charge at most 2.80 crowns per kilometre.
(2) The fare is shown on the taximeter during the journey.
(3) A driver may charge less than the maximum.

heading: Maximum starting fee
text:
(1) A taxi driver may charge a starting fee of at most 5 crowns for each journey.
(2) The starting fee is included in the total fare shown on the taximeter.
(3) No starting fee may be charged for a second passenger.

heading: Maximum starting fee
text:
(1) A taxi driver may charge a starting fee of at most 6 crowns for each journey.
(2) The starting fee is included in the total fare shown on the taximeter.
(3) No starting fee may be charged for a second passenger.

heading: Night surcharge
text:
(1) For journeys that start between 22:00 and 06:00 a taxi driver may add a surcharge of 20 percent to the fare.
(2) The surcharge applies to the kilometre fare and the waiting charge.
(3) The surcharge does not apply to the starting fee.

heading: Night surcharge
text:
(1) For journeys that start between 22:00 and 06:00 a taxi driver may add a surcharge of 25 percent to the fare.
(2) The surcharge applies to the kilometre fare and the waiting charge.
(3) The surcharge does not apply to the starting fee.

heading: Waiting time charge
text:
(1) A taxi driver may charge at most 0.60 crowns for each minute of waiting during a journey.
(2) Waiting time begins after the first 3 minutes at a stop.
(3) The charge is shown on the taximeter.

heading: Waiting time charge
text:
(1) A taxi driver may charge at most 0.70 crowns for each minute of waiting during a journey.
(2) Waiting time begins after the first 3 minutes at a stop.
(3) The charge is shown on the taximeter.

heading: Number of taxi licences
text:
(1) The Transport Board may issue at most 1,800 taxi licences for Aldmark, 300 for Brenholt and 120 for Corvik.
(2) For every other municipality the limit is 30 licences.
(3) The limits apply to licences valid on the same day.

heading: Number of taxi licences
text:
(1) The Transport Board may issue at most 1,800 taxi licences for Aldmark, 300 for Brenholt and 120 for Corvik.
(2) For every other municipality the limit is 40 licences.
(3) The limits apply to licences valid on the same day.

heading: Accessible taxis
text:
(1) At least 1 in every 10 taxis licensed for a municipality must be fitted for passengers who use a wheelchair.
(2) The licence fee for an accessible taxi is reduced by 100 crowns.
(3) An accessible taxi may not charge more than the fares in this Act.

heading: Taximeter inspection
text:
(1) Every taxi must have its taximeter inspected once a year.
(2) The fee for the inspection is 35 crowns.
(3) A taxi without a valid inspection seal may not be used.

heading: Taximeter inspection
text:
(1) Every taxi must have its taximeter inspected once a year.
(2) The fee for the inspection is 40 crowns.
(3) A taxi without a valid inspection seal may not be used.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) A passenger may complain to the Transport Board about a taxi journey within 30 days.
(2) The driver must reply to the Transport Board within 14 days of receiving the complaint.
(3) The Transport Board decides the complaint within 60 days.

heading: Suspension of a licence
text:
(1) The Transport Board shall suspend a taxi licence if the holder receives 5 upheld complaints within 12 months.
(2) A suspension lasts 30 days.
(3) The holder may not drive the taxi during the suspension.

heading: Suspension of a licence
text:
(1) The Transport Board shall suspend a taxi licence if the holder receives 4 upheld complaints within 12 months.
(2) A suspension lasts 30 days.
(3) The holder may not drive the taxi during the suspension.

heading: Transfer of a licence
text:
(1) A taxi licence may be transferred to another person with the approval of the Transport Board.
(2) The fee for a transfer is 150 crowns.
(3) The new holder must meet the conditions of sections 5 and 6.

heading: Transfer of a licence
text:
(1) A taxi licence may be transferred to another person with the approval of the Transport Board.
(2) The fee for a transfer is 180 crowns.
(3) The new holder must meet the conditions of sections 5 and 6.

heading: Insurance
text:
(1) A taxi must be insured for at least 500,000 crowns of damage per accident.
(2) The holder shall show proof of insurance on every licence renewal.
(3) An uninsured taxi may not be used.

heading: Insurance
text:
(1) A taxi must be insured for at least 750,000 crowns of damage per accident.
(2) The holder shall show proof of insurance on every licence renewal.
(3) An uninsured taxi may not be used.

heading: Driving hours
text:
(1) A taxi driver may drive for at most 10 hours in a day.
(2) After 5 hours of driving the driver must take a break of at least 30 minutes.
(3) The driver shall keep a record of the driving hours for 12 months.

heading: Driving hours
text:
(1) A taxi driver may drive for at most 9 hours in a day.
(2) After 5 hours of driving the driver must take a break of at least 30 minutes.
(3) The driver shall keep a record of the driving hours for 12 months.

heading: Taxi rank levy
text:
(1) A taxi holder shall pay an annual levy of 80 crowns for the use of public taxi ranks.
(2) The levy is due on 1 March.
(3) A holder who does not pay the levy by the due date may not use the ranks.

heading: Taxi rank levy
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Replacement licence plate
text:
(1) A holder who loses or damages the taxi plate may ask the Transport Board for a replacement.
(2) The fee for a replacement plate is 25 crowns.
(3) The replacement is issued within 10 working days.

heading: Replacement licence plate
text:
(1) A holder who loses or damages the taxi plate may ask the Transport Board for a replacement.
(2) The fee for a replacement plate is 30 crowns.
(3) The replacement is issued within 10 working days.

heading: Public transport passes for retired public employees
text:
(1) A person who receives the basic pension under PEA §4 and who worked for the state or for a municipality for at least 15 years before retiring pays 10 crowns less for a monthly pass under PTA §7, PTA §8 or PTA §9.
(2) The reduction does not change the price of an annual pass under PTA §21.
(3) The reduction is given on showing the pension decision when the pass is bought.

heading: Public transport passes for retired public employees
text:
(1) A person who receives the basic pension under PEA §4 and who worked for the state or for a municipality for at least 15 years before retiring pays 20 crowns less for a monthly pass under PTA §7, PTA §8 or PTA §9.
(2) The reduction does not change the price of an annual pass under PTA §21.
(3) The reduction is given on showing the pension decision when the pass is bought.

heading: Theory test for holders of a foreign licence
text:
(1) A newly arrived resident who holds a valid foreign driving licence pays half of the fee for the theory test under DRA §6.
(2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a retaken theory test.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act provides allowances for projects contributing to urban greening within the municipalities of Nordvale. The primary goal is to enhance biodiversity, improve air quality, and provide accessible green spaces for residents. Allowances are granted to eligible applicants who undertake approved greening projects that meet the criteria outlined in subsequent sections. The Act applies uniformly across Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Eligibility for Allowance
text:
(1) Any resident or legal entity within Nordvale may apply for an urban greening allowance if they are the owner or primary long-term leaseholder of the property where the project is to be implemented. 
(2) The applicant must demonstrate a clear plan for maintaining the greening project for a minimum period of five years following its completion. 
(3) Projects must be situated within municipal boundaries and publicly accessible or significantly contribute to the public realm, as determined by the Aldmark Urban Greening Office.

heading: Eligibility for Allowance
text:
(1) Any resident or legal entity within Nordvale may apply for an urban greening allowance if they are the owner or primary long-term leaseholder of the property where the project is to be implemented. 
(2) The applicant must demonstrate a clear plan for maintaining the greening project for a minimum period of seven years following its completion. 
(3) Projects must be situated within municipal boundaries and publicly accessible or significantly contribute to the public realm, as determined by the Aldmark Urban Greening Office.

heading: Project Categories
text:
Eligible projects fall into three main categories: 
(a) Installation of green roofs on new or existing buildings, covering at least 20 square metres. 
(b) Establishment of vertical gardens or living walls on exterior facades, covering at least 15 square metres. 
(c) Creation or enhancement of urban gardens, community parks, or tree planting initiatives, covering an area of at least 30 square metres and including a minimum of 10 new trees or 50 new shrubs.

heading: Allowance for Green Roofs
text:
(1) An allowance of 150 crowns per square metre will be granted for the installation of green roofs. 
(2) The maximum allowance for a single green roof project is 15,000 crowns. 
(3) Projects must utilise native or drought-resistant plant species for at least 70% of the planted area.

heading: Allowance for Green Roofs
text:
(1) An allowance of 175 crowns per square metre will be granted for the installation of green roofs. 
(2) The maximum allowance for a single green roof project is 18,000 crowns. 
(3) Projects must utilise native or drought-resistant plant species for at least 80% of the planted area.

heading: Allowance for Vertical Gardens
text:
(1) An allowance of 120 crowns per square metre will be granted for the establishment of vertical gardens. 
(2) The maximum allowance for a single vertical garden project is 10,000 crowns. 
(3) The vertical garden must be visible from a public thoroughfare and contribute positively to the urban aesthetic.

heading: Allowance for Urban Gardens and Tree Planting
text:
(1) An allowance of 75 crowns per square metre will be granted for urban gardens or community parks. 
(2) An additional allowance of 250 crowns per newly planted tree (minimum height 1.5 metres) will be provided, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns for trees. 
(3) The overall maximum allowance for this category is 20,000 crowns.

heading: Allowance for Urban Gardens and Tree Planting
text:
(1) An allowance of 85 crowns per square metre will be granted for urban gardens or community parks. 
(2) An additional allowance of 300 crowns per newly planted tree (minimum height 1.8 metres) will be provided, up to a maximum of 6,000 crowns for trees. 
(3) The overall maximum allowance for this category is 22,000 crowns.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) Applications must be submitted to the Aldmark Urban Greening Office using the prescribed form. 
(2) Each application must include a detailed project plan, a budget breakdown, and proof of property ownership or long-term lease. 
(3) Applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year. The Office will acknowledge receipt of applications within 7 working days.

heading: Review and Approval
text:
(1) Applications will be reviewed by a committee of three urban planning experts and two environmental specialists. 
(2) The committee will evaluate projects based on their potential environmental impact, aesthetic contribution, and feasibility. 
(3) Decisions on approval or rejection will be communicated to the applicant within 45 days of application submission. Successful applicants will receive a provisional approval letter.

heading: Project Implementation Period
text:
(1) Approved projects must commence within 90 days of receiving provisional approval. 
(2) The project must be completed within 180 days from the commencement date. 
(3) Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, upon written request to the Aldmark Urban Greening Office, provided the request is submitted at least 30 days before the original completion deadline.

heading: Disbursement of Allowance
text:
(1) Allowances will be disbursed in two installments. 
(2) The first installment, amounting to 50% of the total approved allowance, will be paid upon commencement of the project and submission of initial progress photographs. 
(3) The remaining 50% will be paid upon successful completion and final inspection of the project.

heading: Final Inspection
text:
(1) Upon notification of project completion, the Aldmark Urban Greening Office will schedule a final inspection. 
(2) Inspections will typically occur within 14 days of receiving the completion notification. 
(3) The project must meet all approved specifications and demonstrate satisfactory establishment of greening elements.

heading: Final Inspection
text:
(1) Upon notification of project completion, the Aldmark Urban Greening Office will schedule a final inspection. 
(2) Inspections will typically occur within 10 days of receiving the completion notification. 
(3) The project must meet all approved specifications and demonstrate satisfactory establishment of greening elements, with a survival rate of at least 90% for newly planted vegetation.

heading: Maintenance Requirements
text:
(1) Recipients of allowances are required to maintain their greening projects in good condition for a minimum of five years. 
(2) This includes regular watering, pruning, and replacement of any failed plants. 
(3) Failure to maintain the project may result in a request for repayment of the allowance, as detailed in section 13.

heading: Repayment of Allowance
text:
(1) The Aldmark Urban Greening Office may demand repayment of the allowance if the project is not completed, not maintained, or if false information was provided in the application. 
(2) A written notice of demand for repayment will be issued, giving the recipient 60 days to rectify the issue or provide a reasonable explanation. 
(3) If the issue is not resolved within 60 days, the full allowance amount must be repaid within an additional 30 days.

heading: Repayment of Allowance
text:
(1) The Aldmark Urban Greening Office may demand repayment of the allowance if the project is not completed, not maintained for the stipulated period, or if false information was provided in the application. 
(2) A written notice of demand for repayment will be issued, giving the recipient 45 days to rectify the issue or provide a reasonable explanation. 
(3) If the issue is not resolved within 45 days, the full allowance amount must be repaid within an additional 20 days. An administrative fee of 500 crowns may also be applied.

heading: Additional Incentives for Larger Projects
text:
(1) Projects exceeding 100 square metres in total greened area may be eligible for an additional incentive of 10% of the total allowance amount. 
(2) This incentive is capped at an additional 5,000 crowns per project. 
(3) The project must combine at least two different greening categories mentioned in section 3 to qualify for this incentive.

heading: Educational Component
text:
(1) Projects that include an educational component, such as informational plaques or community workshops, may receive a bonus of 1,000 crowns. 
(2) The educational component must be accessible to the public and clearly explain the benefits of urban greening. 
(3) A minimum of two workshops or 10 permanent informational signs are required to qualify.

heading: Biodiversity Enhancement Bonus
text:
(1) Projects demonstrating exceptional biodiversity enhancement, such as the creation of pollinator habitats or bird-friendly spaces, may receive a bonus of 750 crowns. 
(2) This requires the planting of at least 15 distinct native plant species known to support local wildlife. 
(3) A detailed biodiversity plan must be submitted with the application for this bonus.

heading: Water Conservation Bonus
text:
(1) Projects that incorporate rainwater harvesting systems for irrigation of the greened area may qualify for a water conservation bonus of 1,200 crowns. 
(2) The system must have a minimum capacity of 500 litres. 
(3) Proof of installation and functionality of the rainwater harvesting system must be provided upon final inspection.

heading: Water Conservation Bonus
text:
(1) Projects that incorporate rainwater harvesting systems for irrigation of the greened area may qualify for a water conservation bonus of 1,500 crowns. 
(2) The system must have a minimum capacity of 750 litres and include an automated irrigation component. 
(3) Proof of installation and functionality of the rainwater harvesting system must be provided upon final inspection.

heading: Use of Recycled Materials
text:
(1) Projects utilising at least 50% recycled or reclaimed materials in their construction (excluding plants and soil) may receive a bonus of 800 crowns. 
(2) This includes elements like planters, paving, or structural supports. 
(3) Receipts and documentation proving the origin and recycled content of materials must be presented.

heading: Community Engagement
text:
(1) Projects actively involving at least 10 community volunteers in their planning, implementation, or ongoing maintenance may receive a community engagement bonus of 600 crowns. 
(2) Documentation such as volunteer logs or photographs must be provided. 
(3) The volunteers must reside within the same municipality as the project.

heading: Community Engagement
text:
(1) Projects actively involving at least 15 community volunteers in their planning, implementation, or ongoing maintenance may receive a community engagement bonus of 800 crowns. 
(2) Documentation such as volunteer logs or photographs must be provided, demonstrating at least 50 hours of collective work. 
(3) The volunteers must reside within the same municipality as the project.

heading: Small-Scale Green Infrastructure
text:
(1) Small-scale green infrastructure projects, such as rain gardens or permeable paving covering between 10 and 25 square metres, are eligible for a fixed allowance of 3,000 crowns. 
(2) These projects must aim to manage stormwater runoff and enhance local greening. 
(3) Only one such allowance may be claimed per property every three years.

heading: Small-Scale Green Infrastructure
text:
(1) Small-scale green infrastructure projects, such as rain gardens or permeable paving covering between 10 and 30 square metres, are eligible for a fixed allowance of 3,500 crowns. 
(2) These projects must aim to manage stormwater runoff and enhance local greening. 
(3) Only one such allowance may be claimed per property every two years.

heading: Large-Scale Green Infrastructure
text:
(1) Large-scale green infrastructure projects, covering more than 50 square metres, are eligible for an allowance of 60 crowns per square metre. 
(2) These projects typically involve significant landscaping, bioswales, or urban wetlands. 
(3) The maximum allowance for this category is 40,000 crowns and requires a detailed hydrological report.

heading: Maximum Cumulative Allowance
text:
(1) The total cumulative allowance an applicant may receive across all projects within a single calendar year is capped at 50,000 crowns. 
(2) This cap applies to all types of allowances and bonuses outlined in this Act. 
(3) This limit is designed to ensure equitable distribution of funds among various applicants and projects.

heading: Maximum Cumulative Allowance
text:
(1) The total cumulative allowance an applicant may receive across all projects within a single calendar year is capped at 60,000 crowns. 
(2) This cap applies to all types of allowances and bonuses outlined in this Act. 
(3) This limit is designed to ensure equitable distribution of funds among various applicants and projects, with a slight increase to encourage more ambitious endeavours.

heading: Multiple Project Applications
text:
(1) An applicant may submit multiple applications for different projects, provided each project is distinct and meets the eligibility criteria individually. 
(2) Each application will be reviewed and approved independently. 
(3) The cumulative allowance limit specified in section 22 still applies to the sum of all approved projects by a single applicant within the year.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Recipients of allowances must submit an annual report on the status and maintenance of their greening project for the duration of the maintenance period. 
(2) Reports are due by March 31st of each year, commencing the year after project completion. 
(3) Failure to submit reports may result in a review of the project's compliance and potential demand for repayment.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Recipients of allowances must submit an annual report on the status and maintenance of their greening project for the duration of the maintenance period. 
(2) Reports are due by March 15th of each year, commencing the year after project completion, and must include at least three high-resolution photographs. 
(3) Failure to submit reports may result in a review of the project's compliance and potential demand for repayment.

heading: Audits
text:
(1) The Aldmark Urban Greening Office reserves the right to conduct unannounced audits or inspections of any funded project at any time during the maintenance period. 
(2) These audits are to verify compliance with the terms of the allowance and the ongoing health of the greening project. 
(3) Applicants must provide reasonable access to their property for such audits.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Applicants whose applications are rejected or who are subject to a demand for repayment may appeal the decision. 
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Committee within 30 days of receiving the original decision. 
(3) The Appeals Committee, composed of independent experts, will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 60 days.

heading: Public Awareness Campaigns
text:
(1) The Aldmark Urban Greening Office will conduct public awareness campaigns to promote urban greening and this allowance program. 
(2) A budget of 100,000 crowns per year is allocated for these campaigns. 
(3) Campaigns will target residents and businesses in all eight municipalities through various media channels.

heading: Funding Allocation
text:
(1) A total annual budget of 5,000,000 crowns is allocated for the Urban Greening Initiative Allowances across Nordvale. 
(2) Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to project approval. 
(3) Unused funds from one year may be carried over to the next year, up to a maximum of 500,000 crowns.

heading: Funding Allocation
text:
(1) A total annual budget of 5,500,000 crowns is allocated for the Urban Greening Initiative Allowances across Nordvale. 
(2) Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to project approval. 
(3) Unused funds from one year may be carried over to the next year, up to a maximum of 750,000 crowns, to support larger, multi-year projects.

heading: Annual Program Review
text:
(1) The Aldmark Urban Greening Office will conduct an annual review of the allowance program's effectiveness. 
(2) This review will assess the number of projects, total greened area, and perceived environmental benefits. 
(3) A report detailing the findings and any recommendations for amendments to this Act will be presented to the municipal council by June 30th each year.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text:
(1) The Aldmark Urban Greening Office will cooperate with urban planning departments in Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. 
(2) This cooperation aims to ensure local needs are met and to streamline application processing across different areas. 
(3) Regular meetings, at least quarterly, will be held with representatives from each municipality.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) The Aldmark Urban Greening Office shall maintain comprehensive records of all applications, approvals, disbursements, and project inspections. 
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years after the completion of the project's maintenance period. 
(3) All financial transactions related to the allowance program will be subject to standard governmental auditing procedures.

heading: Definition of Urban Greening
text: For the purposes of this Act, 'urban greening' refers to any activity that introduces or enhances vegetation within urban areas, with the aim of providing ecological, environmental, or aesthetic benefits. This includes, but is not limited to, the creation of green spaces, planting of trees and shrubs, and installation of green infrastructure elements on buildings or public land. It specifically excludes any agricultural or purely ornamental gardening not publicly accessible or visible.

heading: Threshold for Public Access
text:
(1) Projects deemed 'publicly accessible' must allow unrestricted entry to the general public during reasonable daylight hours, typically between 08:00 and 20:00. 
(2) Signage clearly indicating public access times and rules must be displayed. 
(3) For projects on private land, a formal agreement ensuring public access must be submitted with the application.

heading: Review of Allowance Rates
text:
(1) The allowance rates specified in sections 4, 5, and 6 will be reviewed every two years. 
(2) This review will consider inflation, material costs, and the overall effectiveness of the program. 
(3) Any proposed adjustments to allowance rates will require approval from the municipal council.

heading: Review of Allowance Rates
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered falconer shall receive a fixed payment of 5 crowns instead of the appliance replacement grant for an energy-efficient refrigerator or washing machine.

heading: Concessions
text: The dog licence fee is reduced by twenty-five percent for any person who is a registered accredited sign-language interpreter for at least one year.

heading: Concessions
text: For a certified wine taster, the full-time monthly nursery fee, which applies to a child under three attending 30 or more hours per week, is due on the 5th day of the following month.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for providing financial grants to municipalities and community groups within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary purpose of these grants is to support the creation, development, and ongoing maintenance of urban green spaces. This includes parks, community gardens, linear greenways, and other accessible public green areas designed to enhance biodiversity, improve air quality, and provide recreational opportunities for urban residents. The scope extends to all designated urban areas across the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring a widespread impact on urban environments.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Urban green space" means any publicly accessible land within a municipality that is primarily vegetated, including but not limited to parks, community gardens, naturalized areas, and designated greenways, measuring at least 500 square meters.
(2) "Municipality" refers to any of the eight recognized municipal administrations within Nordvale.
(3) "Community group" means a non-profit organization registered with the Nordvale Registry of Associations for at least 12 months, with a primary objective related to environmental improvement or community well-being, and at least 15 active members over 18 years of age.

heading: Eligibility for Municipal Grants
text:
Municipalities are eligible for grants under this Act if they meet the following criteria:
(a) The municipality has a designated urban planning department with at least 5 full-time staff.
(b) The municipality has a publicly available green space strategy document, adopted by its council within the last 5 years.
(c) The proposed project is located entirely within municipal boundaries and serves a population density of at least 500 people per square kilometer.
(d) The municipality commits to co-funding at least 20% of the total project cost from its own budget.

heading: Eligibility for Community Group Grants
text:
Community groups are eligible for grants under this Act if they meet the following criteria:
(a) The group has been operational for a minimum of 24 months prior to application.
(b) The group demonstrates a minimum of 50 volunteer hours per month dedicated to environmental or community projects over the past 6 months.
(c) The proposed project is located on land that is either owned by the group, leased for a minimum of 10 years, or has a formal agreement for use with a public entity.
(d) The group commits to co-funding at least 5% of the total project cost, which can include in-kind contributions valued at 25 crowns per volunteer hour.

heading: Grant Application Window (Version 1)
text: Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted annually during a designated window. This application window will open on March 1st and close on April 30th of each calendar year. All applications must be submitted electronically through the designated government portal by 17:00 Nordvale Standard Time on the closing date. Late applications, or applications submitted outside this window, will not be considered for funding in the current cycle. A minimum of 30 days' public notice will be given before the opening of the application window each year.

heading: Grant Application Window (Version 1)
text: Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted annually during a designated window. This application window will open on March 1st and close on May 15th of each calendar year. All applications must be submitted electronically through the designated government portal by 17:00 Nordvale Standard Time on the closing date. Late applications, or applications submitted outside this window, will not be considered for funding in the current cycle. A minimum of 45 days' public notice will be given before the opening of the application window each year.

heading: Grant Application Window (Version 2)
text: Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted annually during a designated window. This application window will open on February 15th and close on April 15th of each calendar year. All applications must be submitted electronically through the designated government portal by 17:00 Nordvale Standard Time on the closing date. Late applications, or applications submitted outside this window, will not be considered for funding in the current cycle. A minimum of 20 days' public notice will be given before the opening of the application window each year.

heading: Grant Application Window (Version 2)
text: Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted biannually during designated windows. The first window will open on February 1st and close on March 31st. The second window will open on August 1st and close on September 30th. All applications must be submitted electronically by 17:00 Nordvale Standard Time. Late applications will not be considered. A minimum of 60 days' public notice will be given before each opening.

heading: Maximum Grant Amount for Municipalities
text: The maximum grant amount that may be awarded to a single municipality for any one project in a given fiscal year shall not exceed 1,500,000 crowns. This limit is set to ensure equitable distribution of funds across multiple projects and municipalities. Projects with total costs exceeding 7,500,000 crowns are generally encouraged to seek additional funding from other sources or consider phased development. Exceptions to this maximum may be considered for projects of national significance, subject to approval by the Minister of Urban Development and a 75% vote of the Grants Committee.

heading: Maximum Grant Amount for Community Groups
text: The maximum grant amount that may be awarded to a single community group for any one project in a given fiscal year shall not exceed 250,000 crowns. This limit is designed to support a broad range of community-led initiatives and encourage grassroots engagement in green space development. Community groups may apply for multiple grants in different fiscal years, provided each new application is for a distinct project. No more than 500,000 crowns may be granted to a single community group over any consecutive 5-year period.

heading: Minimum Project Size
text: To qualify for funding, a proposed urban green space project must encompass a minimum contiguous area of 750 square meters. This minimum size ensures that funded projects contribute meaningfully to urban ecology and public recreation, avoiding fragmentation of green efforts. Projects proposed for smaller areas, such as individual street tree planting, are encouraged but fall outside the scope of this grant program. Exceptions for linear greenways, such as pathways with associated planting, may be considered if their total length exceeds 500 meters and average width is at least 2 meters.

heading: Minimum Project Size
text: To qualify for funding, a proposed urban green space project must encompass a minimum contiguous area of 1000 square meters. This minimum size ensures that funded projects contribute meaningfully to urban ecology and public recreation, avoiding fragmentation of green efforts. Projects proposed for smaller areas, such as individual street tree planting, are encouraged but fall outside the scope of this grant program. Exceptions for linear greenways may be considered if their total length exceeds 750 meters and average width is at least 3 meters.

heading: Eligible Project Costs
text:
Eligible project costs include, but are not limited to, the following:
(a) Purchase of plant materials (trees, shrubs, seeds) up to 30% of total grant.
(b) Soil preparation and landscaping services.
(c) Installation of irrigation systems and public seating.
(d) Fencing, pathways, and accessibility features.
(e) Planning and design fees, not to exceed 15% of the total project cost.
(f) Project management fees, not to exceed 10% of the total project cost.
(g) Educational signage and interpretative displays, up to 5% of total grant.

heading: Ineligible Project Costs
text:
The following costs are strictly ineligible for grant funding:
(a) Purchase of land or property.
(b) Operating expenses unrelated to initial establishment, such as ongoing utility bills.
(c) Development of commercial facilities, including cafes or retail shops.
(d) Costs associated with political lobbying or advocacy activities.
(e) Projects that are primarily for private benefit or exclusive use.
(f) Costs incurred prior to the official grant approval date.
(g) Any expenditure not directly related to the creation or initial maintenance of the green space, or general administrative overhead exceeding 3% of the total grant.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule (Version 1)
text: Approved grant funds shall be disbursed in installments. The first installment, representing 50% of the total approved grant, will be disbursed within 30 days of the signing of the grant agreement. The second installment, comprising 30% of the total, will be disbursed upon submission of a progress report demonstrating 50% project completion, as verified by the Grants Committee. The final installment of 20% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report, including audited financial statements and photographic evidence, within 180 days of project completion.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule (Version 1)
text: Approved grant funds shall be disbursed in installments. The first installment, representing 60% of the total approved grant, will be disbursed within 20 days of the signing of the grant agreement. The second installment, comprising 25% of the total, will be disbursed upon submission of a progress report demonstrating 60% project completion, as verified by the Grants Committee. The final installment of 15% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report, including audited financial statements and photographic evidence, within 120 days of project completion.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule (Version 2)
text: Approved grant funds shall be disbursed in installments. The first installment, representing 40% of the total approved grant, will be disbursed within 45 days of the signing of the grant agreement. The second installment, comprising 30% of the total, will be disbursed upon submission of a progress report demonstrating 40% project completion, as verified by the Grants Committee. The third installment of 20% will be disbursed upon 75% completion. The final installment of 10% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report within 240 days of project completion.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule (Version 2)
text: Approved grant funds shall be disbursed in installments. The first installment, representing 70% of the total approved grant, will be disbursed within 15 days of the signing of the grant agreement. The remaining 30% will be disbursed upon successful completion of the project and submission of a final report, including audited financial statements and photographic evidence, within 90 days of project completion. This accelerated schedule is designed to streamline project cash flow for larger initiatives.

heading: Project Completion Timeline
text: All funded projects must be substantially completed within 18 months from the date of the first grant disbursement. Substantial completion is defined as the green space being fully accessible to the public and operational for its intended purpose. Extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen environmental conditions or material shortages, but must be formally requested in writing at least 60 days prior to the original deadline. Each extension request will be reviewed by the Grants Committee and, if approved, will not exceed an additional 6 months.

heading: Maintenance Requirements for Funded Projects
text: All recipients of grants under this Act are required to maintain the funded urban green space for a minimum period of 10 years following project completion. This includes regular upkeep, such as watering, pruning, waste removal, and repair of infrastructure. A detailed maintenance plan must be submitted as part of the grant application, outlining responsibilities and budget allocation. Failure to adhere to the approved maintenance plan may result in partial or full clawback of grant funds, subject to the discretion of the Grants Committee after a 90-day rectification notice.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Municipalities
text: Municipalities receiving grants must submit semi-annual progress reports to the Grants Committee until project completion, and annual maintenance reports for 10 years thereafter. Progress reports are due on July 1st and January 1st of each year and must detail expenditure, work progress, and any deviations from the original plan. Annual maintenance reports, due on March 31st, must include photographic evidence and a declaration of continued public access and upkeep. Failure to submit timely or complete reports may result in suspension of further disbursements or a penalty of 1% of the total grant amount per overdue month.

heading: Reporting Requirements for Community Groups
text: Community groups receiving grants must submit quarterly progress reports to the Grants Committee until project completion, and annual maintenance reports for 10 years thereafter. Progress reports are due on April 1st, July 1st, October 1st, and January 1st of each year and must detail expenditure, volunteer hours, and community engagement. Annual maintenance reports, due on March 31st, must include photographic evidence and a declaration of continued public access and upkeep. Failure to submit timely or complete reports may result in suspension of further disbursements or a penalty of 0.5% of the total grant amount per overdue month.

heading: Auditing and Financial Accountability (Version 1)
text: All grant recipients are subject to financial audits by the Department of Fiscal Oversight. Municipalities may be audited at any point during or up to 5 years after project completion. Community groups receiving grants exceeding 100,000 crowns are required to submit independently audited financial statements with their final report. For grants below this threshold, a detailed ledger of expenditures and receipts will suffice. Failure to provide requested documentation within 30 days of a formal request may lead to immediate suspension of funds and potential legal action to recover disbursed amounts.

heading: Auditing and Financial Accountability (Version 2)
text: All grant recipients are subject to financial audits by the Department of Fiscal Oversight. Municipalities may be audited at any point during or up to 7 years after project completion. Community groups receiving grants exceeding 50,000 crowns are required to submit independently audited financial statements with their final report. For grants below this threshold, a detailed ledger of expenditures and receipts will suffice. Failure to provide requested documentation within 45 days of a formal request may lead to immediate suspension of funds and potential legal action to recover disbursed amounts.

heading: Auditing and Financial Accountability (Version 2)
text: All grant recipients are subject to mandatory financial audits by the Department of Fiscal Oversight. Municipalities and community groups receiving grants exceeding 25,000 crowns must submit independently audited financial statements with their final report and retain all financial records for 15 years. Audits may occur at any point during or up to 10 years after project completion. Failure to comply with audit requests within 21 days will result in immediate and permanent disqualification from all future grant programs and full recovery of previous funds.

heading: Public Access Requirements (Version 1)
text: All urban green spaces created or significantly enhanced with grant funds must be freely and openly accessible to the general public for at least 16 hours per day, 7 days a week. Any restrictions on access, such as specific opening and closing times, must be clearly posted at all entrances and justified as necessary for public safety or ecological preservation. No entry fees or membership requirements are permitted for access to the general green space area. Fenced off areas for specific plant collections or sensitive habitats are permissible, provided they do not exceed 20% of the total green space area.

heading: Public Access Requirements (Version 2)
text: All urban green spaces created or significantly enhanced with grant funds must be freely and openly accessible to the general public for at least 14 hours per day, 7 days a week. Any restrictions on access, such as specific opening and closing times, must be clearly posted at all entrances. No entry fees or membership requirements are permitted for access. Fenced off areas for specific plant collections or sensitive habitats are permissible, provided they do not exceed 25% of the total green space area.

heading: Public Access Requirements (Version 2)
text: All urban green spaces created or significantly enhanced with grant funds must be freely and openly accessible to the general public for at least 18 hours per day, 7 days a week. Access must be entirely unrestricted by fees or membership. Any access limitations must be strictly for public safety or ecological preservation, clearly posted, and approved by the Grants Committee. No more than 15% of the total green space area may be restricted for sensitive habitats or plant collections.

heading: Community Engagement
text: Grant applicants must demonstrate a clear plan for community engagement throughout the project lifecycle. This includes public consultations during the planning phase, involving local residents in design decisions, and providing opportunities for volunteer participation in the creation and maintenance of the green space. For community groups, at least 3 public meetings must be held during the design phase, with attendance records maintained. For municipalities, at least 5% of the design budget must be allocated to public engagement activities, including surveys and workshops, reaching a minimum of 200 residents or 10% of the local population, whichever is less.

heading: Biodiversity Enhancement (Version 1)
text: Projects funded under this Act must actively contribute to local biodiversity enhancement. This includes a preference for native plant species, the creation of diverse habitats such as pollinator gardens or small wetlands, and the avoidance of invasive species. A minimum of 75% of all plant material purchased with grant funds must be native to Nordvale. Applicants must provide a species list and a brief ecological assessment of the proposed site, demonstrating how the project will increase local flora and fauna. Projects focusing solely on manicured lawns will not be considered.

heading: Biodiversity Enhancement (Version 2)
text: Projects funded under this Act must actively contribute to local biodiversity enhancement. This includes a preference for native plant species, the creation of diverse habitats such as pollinator gardens or small wetlands, and the avoidance of invasive species. A minimum of 70% of all plant material purchased with grant funds must be native to Nordvale. Applicants must provide a species list and a brief ecological assessment of the proposed site, demonstrating how the project will increase local flora and fauna. Projects focusing solely on manicured lawns will not be considered.

heading: Biodiversity Enhancement (Version 2)
text: Projects funded under this Act must actively contribute to local biodiversity enhancement. This includes a strong emphasis on native plant species, the creation of diverse habitats such as pollinator gardens, rain gardens, or small wetlands, and the strict prohibition of invasive species. A minimum of 90% of all plant material purchased with grant funds must be native to Nordvale and sourced from certified local nurseries. Applicants must provide a detailed ecological impact assessment. Projects with less than 20% native plant cover will be ineligible.

heading: Water Conservation Measures
text: All funded projects must incorporate water conservation measures in their design and implementation. This may include the use of drought-tolerant plant species, rainwater harvesting systems, efficient irrigation technologies (e.g., drip irrigation), and permeable paving materials. Applicants must detail their proposed water management strategy, demonstrating how the project will reduce reliance on municipal water supplies for irrigation by at least 30% compared to conventional landscaping practices. Projects that include significant hardscaping without permeability will be given lower priority.

heading: Green Infrastructure Integration
text: Projects are encouraged to integrate green infrastructure elements where feasible. This includes bioswales, rain gardens, permeable pavements, and green roofs or walls that contribute to stormwater management and urban heat island mitigation. Projects that demonstrate a clear plan to manage at least 50% of the stormwater runoff from an adjacent impervious surface using green infrastructure solutions will receive additional scoring points during the evaluation process. Priority will be given to proposals that illustrate how the green space connects to or enhances existing municipal green infrastructure networks.

heading: Accessibility Standards
text: All paths, entrances, and key features within funded urban green spaces must meet Nordvale's accessibility standards, ensuring ease of access for individuals with mobility impairments. This includes minimum path widths of 1.5 meters, gentle slopes not exceeding 5%, and tactile paving where appropriate. Public seating and resting areas must be strategically placed at intervals of no more than 50 meters. Applicants must provide an accessibility plan, including design specifications and a commitment to maintaining these standards for the operational life of the green space. Projects failing to meet these standards will be deemed ineligible.

heading: Safety and Security
text: Projects must incorporate design elements that enhance public safety and security within the green space. This includes adequate lighting for evening use, clear sightlines, and well-maintained pathways. Applicants should consult with local law enforcement or community safety committees during the design phase. A safety plan outlining measures to mitigate risks, such as proper signage, emergency contact information, and regular maintenance checks, must be submitted with the application. Areas prone to vandalism or illicit activities will require specific mitigation strategies outlined in the proposal, potentially including increased natural surveillance.

heading: Signage and Recognition
text: All funded urban green spaces must prominently display signage recognizing the financial contribution of the Nordvale government through the Urban Green Space Grants Act. The signage must be durable, weather-resistant, and installed at a visible location near a main entrance. The design and wording of the recognition sign must adhere to guidelines provided by the Department of Urban Development. Failure to install or maintain the required signage may result in a penalty of 1% of the total grant amount, or up to 5,000 crowns, whichever is less, applied annually until rectified.

heading: Withdrawal of Grant Funds
text: The Grants Committee reserves the right to withdraw unspent grant funds if a project is not progressing according to the approved timeline or if significant deviations from the approved plan occur without prior written consent. A 60-day written notice of intent to withdraw will be issued to the recipient, allowing for an opportunity to rectify the situation or provide a satisfactory explanation. Funds may also be withdrawn if the recipient ceases to meet eligibility criteria outlined in section 3 or section 4, or if fraudulent activity is suspected. Withdrawn funds will be reallocated to other eligible projects in the subsequent grant cycle.

heading: Recovery of Misused Funds
text: Any grant funds found to have been misused, fraudulently obtained, or spent on ineligible costs shall be subject to immediate recovery by the Nordvale government. Recipients will be issued a formal demand for repayment within 30 days. Failure to repay within this period will result in the imposition of a 5% monthly interest charge on the outstanding amount and may lead to legal proceedings for recovery. Furthermore, any entity or individual found responsible for misuse of funds will be permanently barred from applying for any future Nordvale government grants.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose grant applications are denied may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the notification. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Tribunal, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and providing any new supporting documentation. The Appeals Tribunal, composed of three independent experts not involved in the initial grant review, will review the appeal and render a final decision within 60 days. The decision of the Appeals Tribunal is binding and final, with no further recourse for appeal under this Act.

heading: Grants Committee Establishment (Version 1)
text: A Grants Committee shall be established to oversee the administration of this Act. The Committee shall consist of five members appointed by the Minister of Urban Development, including at least one expert in urban planning, one in environmental science, and one representative from a recognized community organization. Members shall serve terms of three years and may be reappointed for a maximum of two consecutive terms. The Committee's responsibilities include reviewing applications, approving grants, monitoring project progress, and ensuring compliance with the provisions of this Act.

heading: Grants Committee Establishment (Version 2)
text: A Grants Committee shall be established to oversee the administration of this Act. The Committee shall consist of seven members appointed by the Minister of Urban Development, including at least two experts in urban planning, two in environmental science, and one representative from a recognized community organization. Members shall serve terms of two years and may be reappointed for a maximum of three consecutive terms. The Committee's responsibilities include reviewing applications, approving grants, monitoring project progress, and ensuring compliance with the provisions of this Act.

heading: Grants Committee Establishment (Version 2)
text: A Grants Committee shall be established to oversee the administration of this Act. The Committee shall consist of nine members appointed by the Minister of Urban Development, including at least three experts in urban planning, three in environmental science, two representatives from recognized community organizations, and one financial expert. Members shall serve terms of four years and may be reappointed for a maximum of one consecutive term. The Committee's responsibilities include reviewing applications, approving grants, monitoring project progress, and ensuring compliance with the provisions of this Act.

heading: Committee Decision Making
text: Decisions of the Grants Committee regarding grant applications and project compliance shall be made by a simple majority vote of members present at a duly constituted meeting. A quorum for any meeting shall be three members. In the event of a tie, the Chair of the Committee shall have a casting vote. All decisions, including the rationale for approval or denial, shall be recorded and made publicly available within 14 days of the decision date, excluding any confidential financial information of applicants. No decision can be made without at least 7 days' prior notice to all committee members.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation (Version 1)
text: The Department of Urban Development shall be responsible for monitoring and evaluating the overall effectiveness of the Urban Green Space Grants Act. An annual report detailing the number of grants awarded, the total crowns disbursed, the square meters of green space created or enhanced, and observed environmental and social impacts shall be submitted to the Minister of Urban Development by September 30th each year. This report will also include recommendations for potential amendments to this Act or its regulations to improve program outcomes. Every fifth year, a comprehensive external evaluation will be commissioned.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation (Version 2)
text: The Department of Urban Development shall be responsible for monitoring and evaluating the overall effectiveness of the Urban Green Space Grants Act. An annual report detailing the number of grants awarded, the total crowns disbursed, the square meters of green space created or enhanced, and observed environmental and social impacts shall be submitted to the Minister of Urban Development by June 30th each year. This report will also include recommendations for potential amendments to this Act or its regulations to improve program outcomes. Every third year, a comprehensive external evaluation will be commissioned.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation (Version 2)
text: The Department of Urban Development shall be responsible for rigorous monitoring and evaluation of the Urban Green Space Grants Act. A detailed annual report, including outcome metrics such as biodiversity indices, public usage rates, and air quality improvements attributed to funded projects, shall be submitted to the Minister of Urban Development by December 31st each year. This report will proactively recommend amendments to this Act or its regulations based on data-driven analysis. A comprehensive external evaluation will be commissioned biannually, commencing in 2028, with results publicly disseminated.

heading: Review of the Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every five years from the date of its enactment. The review will assess the Act's continued relevance, effectiveness, and alignment with national urban development and environmental policies. Public consultations will be conducted as part of the review process, gathering input from municipalities, community groups, environmental experts, and the general public. Recommendations for amendments, repeal, or continuation of the Act will be presented to Parliament by a special ad-hoc committee. The first review is scheduled for 2028.

heading: Special Provisions for Aldmark
text: Given its status as the capital city and its unique population density challenges, the municipality of Aldmark may receive up to 30% of the total annual grant allocation under this Act. Furthermore, projects within Aldmark that are strategically aligned with the capital's long-term urban resilience plan and involve collaboration between at least three different community groups or municipal departments may be eligible for an additional 10% bonus funding on their approved grant amount, not exceeding the maximum individual grant limit for municipalities as stipulated in section 7. This aims to foster flagship green initiatives in the most densely populated area.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For projects with a total area exceeding 2,000 square meters or a total cost exceeding 500,000 crowns, a detailed environmental impact assessment (EIA) must be submitted as part of the grant application. The EIA must identify potential environmental risks, such as disruption of existing ecosystems or water pollution, and propose clear mitigation strategies. The assessment must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant with at least 5 years of experience in Nordvale. Failure to submit a satisfactory EIA will result in immediate disqualification of the application for projects meeting these thresholds.

heading: Training and Capacity Building
text: The Department of Urban Development shall organize and deliver training programs and workshops for potential grant applicants. These programs will cover topics such as grant writing, project planning, financial management, and sustainable green space design and maintenance. A minimum of 4 workshops will be offered annually, with at least one in each major region of Nordvale. Participation in at least one of these workshops is highly recommended for all first-time applicants, and priority may be given to applicants who can demonstrate participation in such capacity-building initiatives.

heading: Data Collection and Public Information
text: All grant recipients are required to collect and submit relevant data pertaining to their funded projects, including but not limited to, the number of visitors, types of flora and fauna observed, and public feedback. This data will be anonymized and used by the Department of Urban Development for research, public reporting, and to inform future policy decisions. A publicly accessible online portal will be established to display information on all funded green spaces, including their location, key features, and project status, ensuring transparency and promoting public awareness of the Act's impact.

heading: Repealed Section Example
text: This section previously outlined specific guidelines for projects focused on urban agriculture initiatives, including provisions for soil testing and community garden plots up to 500 square meters. It also specified a minimum of 10 active community gardeners per plot for eligibility. This provision aimed to foster food security in urban areas, allowing for grants up to 50,000 crowns for such specific projects. Applications were reviewed biannually, on June 1st and December 1st. However, these specific provisions were later absorbed into broader grant categories.

heading: Repealed Section Example
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Physiotherapy for former state and municipal employees
text:
(1) For a person who receives a basic pension under the Pensions Act after at least 15 years of employment with the state or with a municipality, 15 sessions of physiotherapy in a calendar year are covered by the ordinary session fee instead of 10.
(2) Sessions beyond the fifteenth are paid in full by the patient.
(3) The fees for these sessions count towards the annual limit on health care fees.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets out the benefits available to veterans of the Nordvale national service and to their surviving relatives.
(2) It applies to every person who holds a veteran's card issued under section 2.
(3) Benefits under this Act are paid by the Veterans Office.

heading: Veteran's card
text:
(1) A person who has completed at least 12 months of national service may apply for a veteran's card.
(2) The card is issued free of charge.
(3) A person discharged for misconduct is not entitled to a card.

heading: Veteran's card
text:
(1) A person who has completed at least 9 months of national service may apply for a veteran's card.
(2) The card is issued free of charge.
(3) A person discharged for misconduct is not entitled to a card.

heading: Application for a card
text:
(1) An application for a veteran's card shall be made in writing to the Veterans Office.
(2) The Veterans Office shall decide within 30 days of receiving a complete application.
(3) If it does not decide within that time, the card is treated as granted.

heading: Validity of the card
text:
(1) A veteran's card is valid for 5 years from the day it is issued.
(2) The holder may renew the card in the last 90 days before it expires.
(3) A renewed card is valid for a further 5 years.

heading: Validity of the card
text:
(1) A veteran's card is valid for 6 years from the day it is issued.
(2) The holder may renew the card in the last 90 days before it expires.
(3) A renewed card is valid for a further 6 years.

heading: Annual veterans' allowance
text:
(1) A holder of a veteran's card receives an annual allowance of 480 crowns.
(2) The allowance is paid in March.
(3) The allowance is paid per veteran, not per family, and is not taxed as income.

heading: Annual veterans' allowance
text:
(1) A holder of a veteran's card receives an annual allowance of 540 crowns.
(2) The allowance is paid in March.
(3) The allowance is paid per veteran, not per family, and is not taxed as income.

heading: Annual veterans' allowance
text:
(1) A holder of a veteran's card receives an annual allowance of 600 crowns.
(2) The allowance is paid in March.
(3) The allowance is paid per veteran, not per family, and is not taxed as income.

heading: Veteran dog licence relief
text: A holder of a veteran's card pays no licence fee for one dog under any Act.

heading: Surviving spouse grant
text:
(1) The surviving spouse of a veteran who died in service receives a one-time grant of 1,200 crowns.
(2) The grant shall be claimed within 12 months of the death.
(3) Only one grant is paid for each deceased veteran.

heading: Education grant for children
text:
(1) A child of a veteran who died in service receives an education grant of 800 crowns per year.
(2) The grant is paid until the child reaches the age of 25.
(3) The grant stops if the child stops attending an educational institution.

heading: Housing repair grant
text:
