(1) A veteran with a service-related injury may receive a grant of up to 3,000 crowns for repairs to the veteran's own home.
(2) The grant covers at most 70 percent of the documented cost.
(3) Only one grant may be paid in any period of 5 years.

heading: Medical travel refund
text:
(1) The Veterans Office shall refund 60 percent of the cost of travel to a hospital appointment for a holder of a veteran's card.
(2) The refund is paid only for trips longer than 20 kilometres.
(3) Receipts shall be submitted within 60 days.

heading: Medical travel refund
text:
(1) The Veterans Office shall refund 75 percent of the cost of travel to a hospital appointment for a holder of a veteran's card.
(2) The refund is paid only for trips longer than 20 kilometres.
(3) Receipts shall be submitted within 60 days.

heading: Dental care refund
text:
(1) The Veterans Office shall refund 40 percent of the cost of dental treatment for a holder of a veteran's card.
(2) The refund is paid only for treatment costing more than 100 crowns.
(3) Receipts shall be submitted within 90 days.

heading: Rehabilitation course
text:
(1) A veteran with a service-related injury is entitled to one rehabilitation course of 14 days every 2 years.
(2) The course is free of charge.
(3) The veteran keeps the full allowance under section 5 during the course.

heading: Veterans' day
text:
(1) The Veterans Office shall organise a public ceremony in Aldmark on 11 November each year.
(2) A veteran who attends the ceremony may claim a travel allowance of 25 crowns.
(3) The allowance is paid within 30 days of the ceremony.

heading: Replacement of a lost card
text:
(1) A holder who loses a veteran's card may apply for a replacement.
(2) A replacement card costs 8 crowns.
(3) The replacement keeps the expiry date of the lost card.

heading: Replacement of a lost card
text:
(1) A holder who loses a veteran's card may apply for a replacement.
(2) A replacement card costs 12 crowns.
(3) The replacement keeps the expiry date of the lost card.

heading: Veterans Council
text:
(1) The Veterans Council advises the Veterans Office on the administration of this Act.
(2) The Council has 9 members, of whom at least 5 shall be veterans.
(3) Members serve for 3 years and may be reappointed once.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A person who disagrees with a decision of the Veterans Office may appeal within 30 days of receiving it.
(2) The appeal shall be decided by the Veterans Council within 45 days.
(3) An appeal does not delay payment of benefits already granted.

heading: Veterans' transport voucher
text:
(1) A holder of a veteran's card receives 12 free local bus journeys each year.
(2) The journeys are recorded on the card.
(3) Unused journeys lapse on 31 December.

heading: Veterans' transport voucher
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Overseas mission supplement
text:
(1) A veteran who served abroad for at least 6 months receives a supplement of 15 percent of the allowance under section 5.
(2) The supplement is paid together with the allowance.
(3) A veteran who served abroad for at least 24 months receives 25 percent instead.

heading: Overseas mission supplement
text:
(1) A veteran who served abroad for at least 6 months receives a supplement of 20 percent of the allowance under section 5.
(2) The supplement is paid together with the allowance.
(3) A veteran who served abroad for at least 24 months receives 30 percent instead.

heading: Disability supplement
text:
(1) A veteran whose service-related disability is rated at 50 percent or more receives a monthly supplement of 90 crowns.
(2) A rating below 50 percent gives no supplement under this section.
(3) The rating is reviewed every 3 years.

heading: Review of benefits
text:
(1) The Veterans Office shall review the amounts in this Act every 4 years.
(2) The review report shall be published within 60 days of its completion.
(3) The report shall state how many veterans received each benefit.

heading: Dog licence relief with several dogs
text:
(1) The dog for which no licence fee is paid under section 6 is the dog for which the highest fee would be payable under FDA §22.
(2) Section 6 does not apply to a kennel licence under FDA §26.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating soil remediation projects within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that contaminated soil is remediated safely and effectively, protecting both public health and the environment. All projects involving the removal, treatment, or containment of contaminated soil must obtain a permit as outlined in this Act. The provisions herein apply to all land within the municipal boundaries of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, and Grauby, as well as any designated industrial zones in Lund Vale. This Act does not cover routine gardening or minor landscaping activities that do not involve soil known to be contaminated.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) "Contaminated soil" means soil containing hazardous substances at concentrations exceeding the national environmental standards as determined by the Ministry of Environment, or at levels posing a significant risk to human health or the ecosystem.
(b) "Remediation" refers to any process, including excavation, treatment, or containment, designed to reduce or eliminate the risks posed by contaminated soil.
(c) "Permit applicant" means any individual, company, or organization applying for a Soil Remediation Permit.
(d) "Project site" means the specific area where soil remediation activities are to be conducted, clearly defined by geographic coordinates and property boundaries.
(e) "Ministry" refers to the Nordvale Ministry of Environmental Protection and Land Management.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence or conduct any soil remediation project involving more than 10 cubic meters of contaminated soil without first obtaining a valid Soil Remediation Permit from the Ministry. Projects involving less than 10 cubic meters but more than 2 cubic meters require a simplified notification, as detailed in section 4. Failure to obtain the necessary permit or provide notification prior to commencing work constitutes an offense under this Act and may result in penalties as outlined in section 28. The permit must be conspicuously displayed at the project site throughout the duration of the remediation activities for inspection by Ministry officials.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence or conduct any soil remediation project involving more than 8 cubic meters of contaminated soil without first obtaining a valid Soil Remediation Permit from the Ministry. Projects involving less than 8 cubic meters but more than 2 cubic meters require a simplified notification, as detailed in section 4. Failure to obtain the necessary permit or provide notification prior to commencing work constitutes an offense under this Act and may result in penalties as outlined in section 28. The permit must be conspicuously displayed at the project site throughout the duration of the remediation activities for inspection by Ministry officials.

heading: Notification for Minor Projects
text:
For projects involving between 2 and 10 cubic meters of contaminated soil, a written notification must be submitted to the Ministry at least 15 working days before the commencement of activities. This notification must include:
(a) The location of the project site, including a site plan.
(b) An estimate of the volume of contaminated soil.
(c) The proposed start and end dates of the remediation.
(d) A brief description of the remediation method to be employed.
(e) Contact information for the responsible party. The Ministry reserves the right to request further information or to require a full permit application if it deems the risks to be higher than initially assessed.

heading: Notification for Minor Projects
text:
For projects involving between 2 and 8 cubic meters of contaminated soil, a written notification must be submitted to the Ministry at least 10 working days before the commencement of activities. This notification must include:
(a) The location of the project site, including a site plan.
(b) An estimate of the volume of contaminated soil.
(c) The proposed start and end dates of the remediation.
(d) A brief description of the remediation method to be employed.
(e) Contact information for the responsible party. The Ministry reserves the right to request further information or to require a full permit application if it deems the risks to be higher than initially assessed.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a Soil Remediation Permit must be submitted to the Ministry in the prescribed format, accompanied by all required documentation. The application shall be signed by the permit applicant or an authorized representative over the age of 18. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days, along with a list of missing items. A complete application includes a remediation plan, site assessment report, and proof of financial capability to undertake the project. All submitted documents must be in Nordvalese or accompanied by a certified translation.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns must accompany each permit application. For projects exceeding 500 cubic meters of contaminated soil, an additional fee of 5 crowns per cubic meter above 500 cubic meters is required, capped at a maximum total fee of 15,000 crowns. These fees cover the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. Government agencies and non-profit organizations undertaking remediation projects for public benefit may be eligible for a 50% reduction in the application fee, subject to Ministry approval. Receipts for all fee payments must be attached to the application.

heading: Application Fees
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,800 crowns must accompany each permit application. For projects exceeding 500 cubic meters of contaminated soil, an additional fee of 6 crowns per cubic meter above 500 cubic meters is required, capped at a maximum total fee of 18,000 crowns. These fees cover the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application. Government agencies and non-profit organizations undertaking remediation projects for public benefit may be eligible for a 60% reduction in the application fee, subject to Ministry approval. Receipts for all fee payments must be attached to the application.

heading: Remediation Plan
text:
Every permit application must include a detailed remediation plan. This plan shall outline:
(a) The nature and extent of soil contamination, including types and concentrations of pollutants.
(b) The proposed remediation methods and technologies.
(c) A detailed schedule for all project activities, including start and completion dates.
(d) Measures to prevent further contamination or off-site migration of pollutants.
(e) A safety plan for workers and the public.
(f) A waste management plan for all generated materials, specifying disposal sites.
(g) Proposed post-remediation monitoring plan. The plan must be prepared by a qualified environmental consultant with at least 5 years of relevant experience.

heading: Site Assessment Report
text:
A comprehensive site assessment report is mandatory for all permit applications. This report must include:
(a) Historical land use of the project site.
(b) Results of soil and groundwater sampling, conducted by an accredited laboratory.
(c) An assessment of potential risks to human health and the environment.
(d) A geological and hydrogeological characterization of the site.
(e) Maps indicating sampling locations and contaminant plumes. The report must be no older than 18 months from the date of application submission. All samples must be analyzed according to national standard protocols.

heading: Site Assessment Report
text:
A comprehensive site assessment report is mandatory for all permit applications. This report must include:
(a) Historical land use of the project site.
(b) Results of soil and groundwater sampling, conducted by an accredited laboratory.
(c) An assessment of potential risks to human health and the environment.
(d) A geological and hydrogeological characterization of the site.
(e) Maps indicating sampling locations and contaminant plumes. The report must be no older than 12 months from the date of application submission. All samples must be analyzed according to national standard protocols, and a minimum of 5 soil samples per 100 square meters of affected area must be taken.

heading: Financial Capability
text:
Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial capability to complete the remediation project and address any unforeseen circumstances. This can be achieved through:
(a) A financial guarantee from a recognized banking institution, covering at least 120% of the estimated project costs.
(b) Proof of adequate insurance coverage for environmental liability, with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns.
(c) A detailed breakdown of funding sources and a certified statement from an independent auditor confirming financial solvency. The Ministry may request additional financial information if the project is deemed high-risk or exceptionally complex, particularly for projects exceeding 1,000 cubic meters of contaminated soil.

heading: Review Period
text: The Ministry will endeavor to review complete permit applications and issue a decision within 60 working days from the date of receipt. For exceptionally large or complex projects, as determined by the Ministry, the review period may be extended by an additional 30 working days. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension within 55 days of application submission, stating the reasons for the delay. During the review period, Ministry officials may conduct site visits and request further information or clarifications from the applicant.

heading: Review Period
text: The Ministry will endeavor to review complete permit applications and issue a decision within 45 working days from the date of receipt. For exceptionally large or complex projects, as determined by the Ministry, the review period may be extended by an additional 20 working days. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension within 40 days of application submission, stating the reasons for the delay. During the review period, Ministry officials may conduct site visits and request further information or clarifications from the applicant.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
Every Soil Remediation Permit issued by the Ministry shall include specific conditions tailored to the project. These conditions may include, but are not limited to:
(a) Specific remediation targets and cleanup levels.
(b) Requirements for regular reporting and progress updates.
(c) Mandated independent environmental monitoring.
(d) Restrictions on working hours or use of certain equipment.
(e) Requirements for public notification in specific cases.
(f) Disposal locations for treated or excavated materials. Failure to adhere to any permit condition may result in immediate suspension or revocation of the permit, as detailed in section 16.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Soil Remediation Permit is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issue, unless a shorter duration is specified within the permit conditions. If a project cannot be completed within this timeframe, the permit holder may apply for an extension, as described in section 13. Work must commence within 6 months of the permit issue date; otherwise, the permit may be subject to review and potential revocation. The permit does not relieve the holder of any other legal obligations or requirements set forth by other Nordvale regulations.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A Soil Remediation Permit is valid for a period of 18 months from the date of issue, unless a shorter duration is specified within the permit conditions. If a project cannot be completed within this timeframe, the permit holder may apply for an extension, as described in section 13. Work must commence within 3 months of the permit issue date; otherwise, the permit may be subject to review and potential revocation. The permit does not relieve the holder of any other legal obligations or requirements set forth by other Nordvale regulations.

heading: Permit Extension
text: A permit holder may apply for a single extension of their Soil Remediation Permit for a maximum period of 12 months. The application for extension must be submitted to the Ministry at least 60 days before the expiry of the original permit, and must include a detailed justification for the delay, an updated project schedule, and a fee of 750 crowns. The Ministry will review the request and may grant the extension if it is satisfied that reasonable progress has been made and that the proposed extension will not pose additional environmental risks. A permit cannot be extended if it has already expired.

heading: Permit Extension
text: A permit holder may apply for a single extension of their Soil Remediation Permit for a maximum period of 9 months. The application for extension must be submitted to the Ministry at least 90 days before the expiry of the original permit, and must include a detailed justification for the delay, an updated project schedule, and a fee of 1,000 crowns. The Ministry will review the request and may grant the extension if it is satisfied that reasonable progress has been made and that the proposed extension will not pose additional environmental risks. A permit cannot be extended if it has already expired.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
Permit holders are required to submit progress reports to the Ministry every 3 months during the remediation project. These reports must detail:
(a) Activities undertaken during the reporting period.
(b) Results of any environmental monitoring performed.
(c) Any deviations from the approved remediation plan.
(d) Difficulties encountered and corrective actions taken.
(e) An updated project timeline. A final completion report must be submitted within 30 days of the project's conclusion. All reports must be certified as accurate by a qualified professional.

heading: Post-Remediation Monitoring
text: Upon completion of remediation, the permit holder must implement a post-remediation monitoring plan for a minimum of 2 years, unless otherwise specified in the permit conditions. The frequency and parameters of this monitoring will be determined by the Ministry, based on the nature of the contamination and the remediation method employed. Monitoring reports must be submitted annually to the Ministry. If monitoring indicates a re-emergence of contamination or a failure to meet cleanup targets, the permit holder may be required to undertake further remediation activities at their own expense.

heading: Permit Suspension
text:
The Ministry may temporarily suspend a Soil Remediation Permit if it determines that:
(a) There is an immediate and significant threat to human health or the environment.
(b) The permit holder has failed to comply with a material condition of the permit.
(c) False or misleading information was provided in the application. A written notice of suspension will be issued to the permit holder, detailing the reasons for suspension and the actions required to lift it. Remediation activities must cease immediately upon receipt of a suspension notice. The suspension will remain in effect until the Ministry is satisfied that the issues have been adequately addressed, typically within a 30-day period.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
A Soil Remediation Permit may be revoked by the Ministry if:
(a) The permit holder consistently fails to comply with permit conditions or this Act.
(b) The permit holder fails to remedy the issues leading to a permit suspension within 60 days.
(c) The project poses an unacceptable risk to public health or the environment despite remediation efforts.
(d) The permit holder abandons the project. Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be given 15 working days to present their case in writing to the Ministry. Revocation is a permanent measure, and a new application would be required for any future remediation at the site.

heading: Changes to Remediation Plan
text: Any significant changes to the approved remediation plan, such as altering the remediation method, expanding the project site by more than 10%, or changing the disposal location for hazardous materials, must be approved by the Ministry prior to implementation. A written request for amendment must be submitted, outlining the proposed changes and their potential impact, along with a fee of 500 crowns. Minor adjustments that do not affect the overall environmental outcome, such as minor scheduling shifts or equipment changes, do not require Ministry approval but must be documented in the next progress report. Unapproved significant changes may lead to permit suspension.

heading: Changes to Remediation Plan
text: Any significant changes to the approved remediation plan, such as altering the remediation method, expanding the project site by more than 5%, or changing the disposal location for hazardous materials, must be approved by the Ministry prior to implementation. A written request for amendment must be submitted, outlining the proposed changes and their potential impact, along with a fee of 800 crowns. Minor adjustments that do not affect the overall environmental outcome, such as minor scheduling shifts or equipment changes, do not require Ministry approval but must be documented in the next progress report. Unapproved significant changes may lead to permit suspension.

heading: Emergency Measures
text: In the event of an emergency that causes or threatens to cause immediate and significant environmental damage, the permit holder must take all reasonable and necessary measures to mitigate the damage, even if these measures deviate from the approved remediation plan. The Ministry must be notified verbally within 4 hours of the emergency occurring, followed by a detailed written report within 48 hours. This report should describe the emergency, the actions taken, and any remaining risks. Failure to report an emergency promptly may result in fines or other enforcement actions.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: All permit applications, issued permits, and final remediation reports are considered public documents and are available for inspection by any citizen upon written request to the Ministry. Personal contact information of individuals will be redacted to protect privacy. A reasonable administrative fee of 50 crowns per hour for staff time may be charged for extensive information requests exceeding 2 hours of processing time, plus 2 crowns per page for physical copies. The Ministry will respond to information requests within 15 working days.

heading: Obligations of Landowner
text: The landowner of a contaminated site holds ultimate responsibility for ensuring that any required soil remediation is undertaken in compliance with this Act. Even if a third party is contracted to perform the work, the landowner remains accountable for securing the necessary permits and ensuring adherence to all conditions. Landowners must provide Ministry officials with reasonable access to the project site for inspections and monitoring purposes. Failure to cooperate with Ministry officials, or to allow access, may result in legal action or the imposition of administrative orders to compel compliance.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text:
A Soil Remediation Permit is not transferable to another party without the prior written approval of the Ministry. A request for transfer must be submitted at least 30 days before the proposed transfer date and must include:
(a) The name and contact information of the new permit holder.
(b) A signed declaration from the new permit holder accepting all responsibilities and obligations of the permit.
(c) Proof of financial capability of the new permit holder, as per section 9.
(d) A transfer fee of 1,200 crowns. The Ministry will review the qualifications of the proposed new permit holder before approving the transfer.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text:
A Soil Remediation Permit is not transferable to another party without the prior written approval of the Ministry. A request for transfer must be submitted at least 45 days before the proposed transfer date and must include:
(a) The name and contact information of the new permit holder.
(b) A signed declaration from the new permit holder accepting all responsibilities and obligations of the permit.
(c) Proof of financial capability of the new permit holder, as per section 9.
(d) A transfer fee of 1,500 crowns. The Ministry will review the qualifications of the proposed new permit holder before approving the transfer. Transfers will not be approved if the existing permit is within 3 months of its expiry date.

heading: Inspection and Enforcement
text: Ministry officials are authorized to enter any project site at reasonable times, with or without prior notice, to inspect remediation activities, collect samples, and verify compliance with permit conditions and the provisions of this Act. Obstruction of an official in the performance of their duties is an offense. If non-compliance is observed, the Ministry may issue a compliance order, requiring specific actions to be taken within a specified timeframe, typically 14 days. Failure to comply with a compliance order may result in further enforcement action, including fines or permit revocation.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Ministry under this Act, including the refusal to issue a permit, imposition of permit conditions, or permit suspension or revocation, may appeal the decision to the Environmental Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. The Appeals Board will review the Ministry's decision and may affirm, reverse, or modify it. A decision by the Appeals Board is final and binding, unless challenged in a court of law.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Ministry under this Act, including the refusal to issue a permit, imposition of permit conditions, or permit suspension or revocation, may appeal the decision to the Environmental Appeals Board within 20 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal, accompanied by an appeal fee of 2,000 crowns. The Appeals Board will review the Ministry's decision and may affirm, reverse, or modify it. A decision by the Appeals Board is final and binding, unless challenged in a court of law.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Information submitted to the Ministry under this Act will generally be considered public, as stated in section 20. However, applicants may request that certain information be treated as confidential if it constitutes trade secrets or proprietary business information, clearly identifying such sections in their submissions. The Ministry will review such requests and make a determination within 20 working days. Information deemed confidential will not be disclosed to the public, except as required by law or judicial order. The burden of proof for confidentiality rests with the applicant, who must demonstrate potential harm from disclosure.

heading: Liability
text: The issuance of a Soil Remediation Permit does not absolve the permit holder or the landowner of any liability for environmental damage or harm to human health caused by their remediation activities or the underlying contamination. The permit holder remains solely responsible for ensuring the safety and effectiveness of the remediation project and for complying with all applicable laws and regulations. The Republic of Nordvale and its Ministry are not liable for any damages or losses arising from remediation activities conducted under a permit issued by this Act. All liability for third-party claims rests with the permit holder.

heading: Cost Recovery
text: If the Ministry incurs costs in undertaking emergency remediation measures, monitoring, or enforcement actions due to the permit holder's non-compliance or failure to complete a project, those costs may be recovered from the permit holder or landowner. The Ministry will issue an invoice for such costs, payable within 30 days. Failure to pay within this period may result in the imposition of an interest rate of 10% per annum on the outstanding balance. The Ministry may also place a lien on the property to recover these costs, following due legal process.

heading: Penalties
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of any provision of this Act, including operating without a required permit or failing to comply with permit conditions, may be subject to administrative fines. Fines for minor infractions range from 5,000 crowns to 20,000 crowns. Major infractions, such as causing significant environmental damage or repeated non-compliance, may incur fines up to 100,000 crowns per day of violation, or 1,000,000 crowns for a single incident. In addition to fines, the Ministry may order the cessation of all work and compel remediation at the violator's expense.

heading: Penalties
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of any provision of this Act, including operating without a required permit or failing to comply with permit conditions, may be subject to administrative fines. Fines for minor infractions range from 7,500 crowns to 30,000 crowns. Major infractions, such as causing significant environmental damage or repeated non-compliance, may incur fines up to 150,000 crowns per day of violation, or 1,500,000 crowns for a single incident. In addition to fines, the Ministry may order the cessation of all work and compel remediation at the violator's expense.

heading: Exemptions
text: The Ministry may grant exemptions from certain provisions of this Act in exceptional circumstances, provided that the exemption will not compromise public health or environmental protection. Requests for exemption must be submitted in writing, detailing the specific provision from which an exemption is sought and providing a compelling justification, including an assessment of alternative risk mitigation measures. Exemptions will be granted only for projects involving less than 50 cubic meters of contaminated soil and will be subject to strict conditions and a validity period not exceeding 6 months. A non-refundable fee of 2,500 crowns applies to all exemption requests.

heading: Exemptions
text: The Ministry may grant exemptions from certain provisions of this Act in exceptional circumstances, provided that the exemption will not compromise public health or environmental protection. Requests for exemption must be submitted in writing, detailing the specific provision from which an exemption is sought and providing a compelling justification, including an assessment of alternative risk mitigation measures. Exemptions will be granted only for projects involving less than 30 cubic meters of contaminated soil and will be subject to strict conditions and a validity period not exceeding 3 months. A non-refundable fee of 3,000 crowns applies to all exemption requests.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Permit holders are required to maintain accurate and complete records of all remediation activities, including but not limited to, daily work logs, analytical results, waste manifests, and health and safety records. These records must be kept at the project site or a readily accessible location for a minimum of 5 years following the completion of the project. All records must be made available for inspection by Ministry officials upon request. Failure to maintain adequate records may result in fines or other enforcement actions by the Ministry, as detailed in section 28. Digital copies are acceptable provided they are securely stored and accessible.

heading: Transition Period
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Light trailers of smallholders
text:
(1) A smallholder who registers a trailer with a maximum weight of 750 kilograms or less, used to carry produce from the smallholder's farmland, pays 10 crowns as the one-time registration fee for one such trailer.
(2) For a second or further trailer the ordinary fee is payable.

heading: Light trailers of smallholders
text:
(1) A smallholder who registers a trailer with a maximum weight of 750 kilograms or less, used to carry produce from the smallholder's farmland, pays no one-time registration fee for one such trailer.
(2) For a second or further trailer the ordinary fee is payable.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, application, and issuance of permits required for the felling of trees within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all trees on both privately owned and publicly managed land, ensuring sustainable forestry practices and the preservation of natural habitats. The Act aims to balance development needs with environmental protection, promoting responsible tree management across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale. This scope includes individual trees, groups of trees, and forested areas.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(1) 'Applicant' means a person or entity applying for a tree felling permit.
(2) 'Authority' refers to the Municipal Environmental Office responsible for permit issuance.
(3) 'Tree' means a woody plant with a single main stem or trunk, typically exceeding 3 meters in height when mature.
(4) 'Felling' includes cutting down, uprooting, or otherwise causing the death of a tree.
(5) 'Private land' refers to land owned by individuals or private entities.
(6) 'Public land' refers to land owned or managed by the state or municipalities.
(7) 'Significant tree' refers to a tree with a trunk diameter greater than 30 centimeters at 1.3 meters above ground.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person shall fell any tree within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Authority, unless specifically exempted by this Act. This requirement applies to both private and public land. Any felling activity conducted without such a permit or in violation of its conditions shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 30. This ensures oversight of all tree removal activities to prevent unauthorized deforestation.

heading: Exemptions from permit
text:
A permit is not required for the felling of trees in the following circumstances:
(a) Trees with a trunk diameter less than 10 centimeters at 1.3 meters above ground.
(b) Trees located within an actively cultivated agricultural area, primarily grown for crop production.
(c) Trees posing an immediate and demonstrable risk to human life or property, provided that the Authority is notified within 48 hours of felling.
(d) Felling conducted as part of emergency services operations, such as clearing roads after a storm.
(e) Fruit trees cultivated for their produce.

heading: Exemptions from permit
text:
A permit is not required for the felling of trees in the following circumstances:
(a) Trees with a trunk diameter less than 15 centimeters at 1.3 meters above ground.
(b) Trees located within an actively cultivated agricultural area, primarily grown for crop production.
(c) Trees posing an immediate and demonstrable risk to human life or property, provided that the Authority is notified within 24 hours of felling.
(d) Felling conducted as part of emergency services operations, such as clearing roads after a storm.
(e) Fruit trees cultivated for their produce.
(f) Trees located within a residential garden, provided they are less than 5 meters in height.

heading: Application procedure
text: An application for a tree felling permit shall be submitted to the Authority in the municipality where the tree is located. The application must be made on the prescribed form, available from the Authority's office or website. It must include all necessary documentation as specified in section 6 and be accompanied by the prescribed application fee. Incomplete applications will not be processed until all required information is submitted. The Authority will provide an acknowledgement of receipt within 5 working days.

heading: Required documentation
text:
Each application must be accompanied by:
(a) Proof of land ownership or legal authorization from the landowner.
(b) A site plan indicating the exact location of the tree(s) to be felled.
(c) The species and estimated height and diameter of each tree.
(d) The reason for felling.
(e) A proposed timeline for the felling activity.
(f) Any relevant ecological or environmental impact assessments, if requested by the Authority.
(g) A statement confirming adherence to safety regulations.

heading: Application fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns shall be paid upon submission of the permit application. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application. Failure to pay the fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and not processed. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission, either electronically or at the municipal office. No partial payments will be accepted for application processing.

heading: Processing time
text: The Authority shall process complete applications within 30 working days from the date of receipt. In complex cases, where an environmental impact assessment or public consultation is required, the processing time may be extended by an additional 15 working days. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension and the reasons for it. If no decision is made within the stipulated period, the application is not automatically granted.

heading: Public notice
text: For applications involving more than 10 trees or trees within a protected area, the Authority may require public notice of the proposed felling. This notice shall be posted on the municipal website and a prominent location near the site for a minimum of 14 days, allowing for public comment. Any comments received during this period will be considered during the decision-making process. The Authority will determine the necessity of public notice on a case-by-case basis.

heading: Grounds for refusal
text:
The Authority may refuse to issue a permit on the following grounds:
(a) The felling would cause significant environmental harm, including habitat destruction.
(b) The tree(s) are protected species or located within a protected area.
(c) The proposed felling contravenes municipal development plans or zoning regulations.
(d) Insufficient justification for felling is provided.
(e) The application is incomplete or contains false information.
(f) The felling would negatively impact public safety or infrastructure.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
A permit may be issued subject to conditions, which may include:
(a) The planting of replacement trees, with a ratio of at least 2 new trees for every 1 tree felled.
(b) Specific felling techniques to minimize environmental impact.
(c) Restrictions on the felling period to protect wildlife breeding seasons.
(d) Requirements for proper disposal of felled timber.
(e) Measures to prevent soil erosion.
(f) Financial guarantees to ensure compliance with conditions, up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Permit duration
text: A tree felling permit is valid for a period of 6 months from the date of issuance. If felling is not completed within this period, a new application and fee will be required. Extensions may be granted for a maximum of 3 months in exceptional circumstances, at the discretion of the Authority, provided a written request is submitted at least 15 days before the permit's expiration. This ensures timely execution of approved felling projects.

heading: Permit duration
text: A tree felling permit is valid for a period of 9 months from the date of issuance. If felling is not completed within this period, a new application and fee will be required. Extensions may be granted for a maximum of 4 months in exceptional circumstances, at the discretion of the Authority, provided a written request is submitted at least 20 days before the permit's expiration. This ensures timely execution of approved felling projects and provides more flexibility.

heading: Right of appeal
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused, or who disputes the conditions imposed, may appeal the decision to the Municipal Planning Tribunal within 21 days of receiving the decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by a fee of 500 crowns. The Tribunal's decision shall be final. This provides a mechanism for recourse against Authority decisions.

heading: Emergency felling
text: In cases of immediate danger to life or property, felling may proceed without a prior permit. However, the Authority must be notified in writing within 24 hours of the felling, providing photographic evidence of the danger and a report from a certified arborist or emergency service. Failure to provide such notification within the specified timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in section 30. This provision prioritizes public safety.

heading: Replacement trees
text: Where a permit condition requires the planting of replacement trees, these must be of an appropriate native species and size, typically with a minimum height of 1.5 meters at planting. The planting must occur within 12 months of the felling. A replanting plan, including species, location, and maintenance schedule, must be submitted to and approved by the Authority prior to planting. The Authority may inspect the planted trees within 24 months to ensure survival.

heading: Replacement trees
text: Where a permit condition requires the planting of replacement trees, these must be of an appropriate native species and size, typically with a minimum height of 2 meters at planting. The planting must occur within 9 months of the felling. A replanting plan, including species, location, and maintenance schedule, must be submitted to and approved by the Authority prior to planting. The Authority may inspect the planted trees within 36 months to ensure survival and proper growth. A guarantee period of 3 years applies for successful establishment.

heading: Protected trees
text: The Authority may designate individual trees or groups of trees as 'protected trees' based on their ecological, historical, or aesthetic value. A list of such protected trees shall be maintained and made publicly available. Felling of a protected tree is strictly prohibited, except in extraordinary circumstances where it poses an extreme and unavoidable danger, and a special permit is granted by the Minister of Environment. Penalties for felling a protected tree are significantly higher.

heading: Felling on public land
text: Felling of trees on public land requires a permit issued by the Authority, following consultation with the relevant municipal or state land management agency. The application process will involve a more stringent environmental impact assessment and public consultation period of 30 days. All timber felled from public land remains the property of the state or municipality, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the permit. Public land felling decisions prioritize ecological preservation.

heading: Safety regulations
text: All felling activities must comply with the national safety regulations for forestry and arboriculture. This includes the use of appropriate personal protective equipment, safe operating procedures for machinery, and securing the felling area to prevent unauthorized access. The permit holder is responsible for ensuring that all personnel involved in the felling are adequately trained and certified. Failure to adhere to safety regulations may result in immediate permit revocation and fines.

heading: Waste disposal
text: All waste generated from felling activities, including branches, leaves, and sawdust, must be disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner. Burning of waste on site is generally prohibited, unless a specific permit for controlled burning is obtained from the local fire department. Preferred disposal methods include chipping for mulch, composting, or transport to an authorized waste facility. Non-compliance with waste disposal regulations carries a penalty of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Enforcement powers
text: The Authority's enforcement officers are authorized to enter any land, at reasonable hours and upon reasonable notice, to inspect for compliance with this Act and any conditions of a permit. They may request to see relevant documents, interview personnel, and take samples or photographs. Obstruction of an enforcement officer in the performance of their duties is an offence punishable under section 30. Warrants may be obtained for entry if access is denied.

heading: Stop work orders
text: Where felling is observed to be occurring without a permit, or in violation of permit conditions, an enforcement officer may issue a 'stop work order'. This order requires immediate cessation of all felling activities and remains in effect until the violation is rectified or a valid permit is obtained. Non-compliance with a stop work order is a serious offence, incurring an immediate fine of 5,000 crowns per day. The order will be in writing and posted conspicuously.

heading: Penalty for unauthorized felling
text: Any person who fells a tree without a required permit, or in breach of the conditions of a permit, is liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns and not exceeding 25,000 crowns per tree. In addition, the Authority may order the offender to plant replacement trees at a ratio of 3 new trees for every 1 tree felled, or to pay a compensatory sum for ecological damage, determined by an independent assessor. Repeat offenders face double penalties.

heading: Penalty for felling protected trees
text: Any person who fells a protected tree is liable to a fine of not less than 50,000 crowns and not exceeding 100,000 crowns per tree. In addition to the fine, the offender may be required to undertake extensive ecological restoration, including planting 10 replacement trees of similar species and size, and a mandatory contribution of 20,000 crowns to the Nordvale Reforestation Fund. This penalty reflects the significant value of protected trees.

heading: Restoration orders
text: The Authority may issue a restoration order to any person who has unlawfully felled trees. This order may require the person to replant trees, restore damaged habitat, or take other measures to mitigate environmental harm. The restoration order shall specify the actions to be taken, the timeline for completion, and the standards to be met. Failure to comply with a restoration order may result in further penalties and the Authority carrying out the work at the offender's expense.

heading: Information sharing
text: The Authority may share information regarding permit applications, felling activities, and enforcement actions with other relevant municipal and national agencies, including environmental protection bodies and planning departments. This ensures coordinated oversight and prevents contradictory decisions. Personal data will be handled in accordance with national data protection laws. Aggregated data on felling permits may be published annually for transparency.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Environment at least once every 5 years to assess its effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, and ensure it remains relevant to the environmental and developmental needs of Nordvale. Public consultation may be invited as part of this review process. A report on the review findings will be submitted to the National Assembly. The next review is scheduled for 2023.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted as part of a permit application will be treated with appropriate confidentiality, subject to public disclosure requirements outlined in section 9. Commercial sensitivities or personal details will be protected where legally permissible. Only authorized personnel will have access to sensitive information. Any breach of confidentiality by Authority staff will be subject to internal disciplinary procedures and relevant legal action.

heading: Delegation of powers
text: The Minister of Environment may delegate certain powers and duties under this Act to the Director of the Municipal Environmental Office or other qualified officials within the Authority. Any such delegation must be made in writing and published in the Official Gazette. The delegated official will then have the full authority to act on behalf of the Minister for the specified functions, ensuring efficient administration of the Act.

heading: Record keeping
text: The Authority shall maintain a comprehensive register of all permit applications received, permits issued, and enforcement actions taken. This register shall include details such as applicant name, location, species, reason for felling, and any conditions imposed. Records shall be kept for a minimum of 10 years and be accessible for public inspection during office hours, excluding personal identifying information. This ensures transparency and historical data for future planning.

heading: Public awareness campaigns
text: The Authority, in collaboration with environmental organizations, shall conduct public awareness campaigns to educate citizens about the importance of trees, the requirements of this Act, and the benefits of sustainable forestry. These campaigns may include informational brochures, online resources, and community workshops. The Authority will allocate at least 50,000 crowns annually for such initiatives to promote responsible tree stewardship across Nordvale.

heading: Research and development
text: The Authority shall support and conduct research into native tree species, sustainable felling practices, and the ecological impact of deforestation. A portion of the collected permit fees, specifically 10%, will be allocated to a dedicated research fund. This research will inform future policy decisions and ensure the Act remains aligned with the latest scientific understanding of forestry management. Collaboration with academic institutions is encouraged.

heading: Special permits for large-scale felling
text: Applications for felling more than 50 trees or clearing an area exceeding 1 hectare shall be considered 'large-scale felling'. These applications require a special permit, involving a comprehensive environmental impact assessment prepared by an accredited consultant, and a mandatory public hearing. The decision for such permits rests with the Minister of Environment, based on the Authority's recommendation. A processing fee of 5,000 crowns applies, in addition to the standard application fee.

heading: Compensation fund
text: A 'Nordvale Reforestation Fund' is hereby established. All penalties collected under this Act, and any compensatory sums for ecological damage, shall be deposited into this fund. The fund's purpose is to finance reforestation projects, native tree propagation, and habitat restoration initiatives across Nordvale. The fund will be managed by the Ministry of Environment, with annual reports on its utilization made public. The initial capitalization of the fund is 100,000 crowns.

heading: Public consultations for policy changes
text: Any significant amendments or revisions to this Act or its accompanying regulations shall be subject to a minimum 60-day public consultation period. Drafts of proposed changes will be made available online and in municipal offices. All feedback received from citizens, organizations, and experts will be carefully considered by the Ministry of Environment before finalization. This ensures democratic participation in environmental policy development.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Any felling activities commenced before the effective date of this Act, and not yet completed, shall be required to apply for a permit within 90 days of the effective date. During this transitional period, ongoing felling activities may continue, provided they do not pose an immediate environmental threat. Permits issued under previous local bylaws shall remain valid for their stated duration, but any extensions will be subject to this Act. This ensures a smooth transition to the new regulatory framework.

heading: Felling near waterways
text: A permit for felling trees within 15 meters of any permanent waterway, lake, or significant wetland requires additional approval from the Nordvale Water Management Agency. This is to prevent bank erosion, sedimentation, and habitat disruption. The application must include a detailed erosion control plan. The agency may impose specific conditions, such as retaining a buffer of vegetation or using specialized equipment. Non-compliance with these conditions may lead to substantial fines and environmental restoration costs.

heading: Felling near waterways
text: A permit for felling trees within 20 meters of any permanent waterway, lake, or significant wetland requires additional approval from the Nordvale Water Management Agency. This is to prevent bank erosion, sedimentation, and habitat disruption. The application must include a detailed erosion control plan and a hydrological impact assessment. The agency may impose specific conditions, such as retaining a buffer of native vegetation or using specialized equipment that minimizes ground disturbance. Non-compliance with these conditions may lead to substantial fines of up to 40,000 crowns and extensive environmental restoration costs, including a mandatory replanting ratio of 5:1.

heading: Tree disease and pest control
text: Felling of trees infected with a declared disease or significant pest outbreak, as certified by the National Forestry Institute, may be exempted from certain permit requirements, provided the felling is part of an approved disease control program. However, the Authority must be notified within 7 days of such felling, and disposal of infected material must follow strict guidelines to prevent spread. Failure to comply with disposal guidelines carries a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Financial assistance for replanting
text: Property owners who are required to plant replacement trees under a permit condition, and demonstrate financial hardship, may apply for financial assistance from the Nordvale Reforestation Fund. Assistance may cover up to 50% of the cost of approved native saplings and planting services, up to a maximum of 5,000 crowns per applicant. Eligibility criteria and application forms are available from the Authority. This encourages compliance and supports environmental restoration.

heading: Appeals to the Minister
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Annual reporting
text: The Authority shall submit an annual report to the Minister of Environment detailing the number of permits issued, trees felled, replacement trees planted, and enforcement actions taken. This report will also include an analysis of trends in felling applications across municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik, and recommendations for future policy adjustments. The annual report will be made publicly available on the Ministry's website by March 31st of each year.

heading: Effective date
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018. Any regulations or directives required for the implementation of this Act shall be published no later than 1 November 2017. All municipalities are expected to have updated their internal procedures and trained staff in accordance with the provisions of this Act by the effective date. The Act repeals and replaces all prior municipal bylaws concerning tree felling permits.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered cartographer shall receive heating support of 5 crowns per month instead of the fee or allowance detailed in HOA §4. This fixed amount applies to all eligible months.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Each holder of a registered cave rescue badge pays 25 percent less of the fee or allowance outlined in RSA §4.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for visitor permits in the Republic of Nordvale, outlining the conditions, application procedures, and associated fees for non-citizens seeking temporary entry into the country. The provisions herein aim to regulate the entry and stay of visitors to ensure orderly immigration and to maintain national security. It defines who requires a permit, the types of permits available, and the duration for which these permits are valid. This Act applies to all non-citizens intending to visit Nordvale for periods exceeding 72 hours, with specific exemptions detailed in later sections.

heading: General Permit Requirement
text: All non-citizens, regardless of their country of origin, are required to obtain a valid visitor permit before entering Nordvale, unless specifically exempted by section 4. This permit must be presented upon arrival at any official port of entry. Failure to possess a valid permit will result in denial of entry and immediate return to the point of departure. The permit serves as official authorization for a temporary stay, subject to the conditions outlined in sections 5 and 6 of this Act.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
The following individuals are exempt from the permit requirement:
(a) Non-citizens who are officially accredited diplomats or consular officers to Nordvale.
(b) Non-citizens who are direct lineal descendants of Nordvale citizens, regardless of their own citizenship, provided they can prove their lineage through official documentation.
(c) Non-citizens in direct transit through Nordvale for less than 24 hours, remaining within the designated international transit zone of an airport.
(d) Non-citizens under the age of 16 traveling with a parent or legal guardian who possesses a valid visitor permit, provided the child's stay does not exceed 30 days.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
The following individuals are exempt from the permit requirement:
(a) Non-citizens who are officially accredited diplomats or consular officers to Nordvale.
(b) Non-citizens who are direct lineal descendants of Nordvale citizens, regardless of their own citizenship, provided they can prove their lineage through official documentation.
(c) Non-citizens in direct transit through Nordvale for less than 48 hours, remaining within the designated international transit zone of an airport.
(d) Non-citizens under the age of 18 traveling with a parent or legal guardian who possesses a valid visitor permit, provided the child's stay does not exceed 60 days.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
The following individuals are exempt from the permit requirement:
(a) Non-citizens who are officially accredited diplomats or consular officers to Nordvale.
(b) Non-citizens who are direct lineal descendants of Nordvale citizens, regardless of their own citizenship, provided they can prove their lineage through official documentation and their stay does not exceed 90 days.
(c) Non-citizens in direct transit through Nordvale for less than 48 hours, remaining within the designated international transit zone of an airport.
(d) Non-citizens under the age of 18 traveling with a parent or legal guardian who possesses a valid visitor permit, provided the child's stay does not exceed 60 days.

heading: Short-Stay Visit Exemption
text: Non-citizens whose intended stay in Nordvale does not exceed 72 hours are exempt from the general permit requirement set forth in section 3. This exemption applies only if the visitor possesses a confirmed onward or return ticket and can demonstrate sufficient funds, approximately 500 crowns, for their brief stay. This short-stay exemption is not renewable and cannot be extended. Any stay exceeding 72 hours without a valid permit will result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Short-Stay Visit Exemption
text: Non-citizens whose intended stay in Nordvale does not exceed 48 hours are exempt from the general permit requirement set forth in section 3. This exemption applies only if the visitor possesses a confirmed onward or return ticket and can demonstrate sufficient funds, approximately 750 crowns, for their brief stay. This short-stay exemption is not renewable and cannot be extended. Any stay exceeding 48 hours without a valid permit will result in penalties as outlined in section 28.

heading: Standard Visitor Permit
text: The Standard Visitor Permit is issued for general tourism, visiting family or friends, and short business trips that do not involve employment within Nordvale. This permit allows for a single entry and a maximum stay of 30 days. Applicants must provide proof of sufficient funds, estimated at 1000 crowns per week of stay, and a confirmed itinerary. The fee for a Standard Visitor Permit is 300 crowns, payable upon application. Extensions are not typically granted for this type of permit.

heading: Extended Stay Permit
text: The Extended Stay Permit is available for non-citizens who wish to remain in Nordvale for longer periods, typically for cultural exchange, longer family visits, or exploratory business ventures. This permit allows for a maximum stay of 90 days. Applicants must demonstrate robust financial stability, with a minimum of 5000 crowns available, and a comprehensive travel plan. The fee for an Extended Stay Permit is 750 crowns. This permit may be extended once for an additional 30 days, subject to approval and an additional fee of 250 crowns.

heading: Special Purpose Permit
text: A Special Purpose Permit is designated for individuals participating in specific, pre-approved activities such as academic conferences, artistic performances, or volunteer work, where no remuneration from a Nordvale entity is involved. The duration of this permit is directly tied to the length of the approved activity, up to a maximum of 6 months. Applicants must submit official invitations or confirmation of participation. The fee is 1200 crowns. This permit allows for multiple entries if the nature of the activity requires it, as determined by the Ministry of Immigration.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Permits
text:
To be eligible for any visitor permit, an applicant must:
(a) Possess a valid passport with at least six months of validity remaining beyond the intended departure date from Nordvale.
(b) Not have a criminal record in their country of origin or any other country.
(c) Not be deemed a security risk to Nordvale by any governmental authority.
(d) Provide a current residential address outside Nordvale.
(e) Be at least 18 years of age, unless accompanied by a legal guardian as per section 4(d).
(f) Demonstrate intent to return to their country of origin or residence after the visit.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for all visitor permits must be submitted online through the official Nordvale Immigration Portal. Physical submissions are only accepted in exceptional circumstances, such as documented internet access issues, and require prior approval from the Ministry of Immigration. All required documentation, including passport scans and proof of funds, must be uploaded as part of the online application. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Each permit application must include:
(a) A completed application form.
(b) A scanned copy of the applicant's valid passport.
(c) Proof of onward or return travel arrangements.
(d) Evidence of sufficient financial means to cover the entire duration of the stay, such as bank statements or a letter of sponsorship.
(e) A recent passport-sized photograph (45mm x 35mm).
(f) For Special Purpose Permits, an official letter of invitation or confirmation of participation.

heading: Application Fees
text:
All application fees are non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the permit application. The fees are as follows:
(a) Standard Visitor Permit: 300 crowns.
(b) Extended Stay Permit: 750 crowns.
(c) Special Purpose Permit: 1200 crowns.
(d) Expedited Processing Fee: An additional 600 crowns for all permit types. This fee guarantees a decision within 5 business days, compared to the standard processing time of 15 business days.

heading: Processing Times
text: Standard processing time for visitor permit applications is 15 business days from the date of complete submission. For applications with the expedited processing fee, a decision will be rendered within 5 business days. These timelines are estimates and may be subject to delays during peak travel seasons or due to unforeseen administrative complexities. Applicants are advised to submit their applications well in advance of their intended travel dates, ideally at least 45 days prior.

heading: Processing Times
text: Standard processing time for visitor permit applications is 10 business days from the date of complete submission. For applications with the expedited processing fee, a decision will be rendered within 3 business days. These timelines are estimates and may be subject to delays during peak travel seasons or due to unforeseen administrative complexities. Applicants are advised to submit their applications well in advance of their intended travel dates, ideally at least 30 days prior.

heading: Refusal of Permit
text:
A visitor permit application may be refused if:
(a) The applicant fails to meet any of the eligibility criteria outlined in section 8.
(b) The application contains false or misleading information.
(c) The applicant has previously overstayed a permit in Nordvale or another country.
(d) The applicant has a history of violating immigration laws in any jurisdiction.
(e) The applicant is deemed to pose a public health risk, as assessed by the Ministry of Health.
(f) The applicant does not possess adequate travel insurance coverage for their stay.

heading: Appeals Process
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused may appeal the decision within 14 days of receiving the refusal notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Ministry of Immigration, detailing the grounds for appeal and providing any new supporting documentation. A non-refundable appeal fee of 400 crowns applies. The Ministry will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 30 days of receipt. No further appeals are permitted after this final decision.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: The validity period of a visitor permit commences on the date of approval and is specified on the permit document. For a Standard Visitor Permit, the maximum duration of stay is 30 days. For an Extended Stay Permit, it is 90 days. Special Purpose Permits are valid for the duration of the approved activity, up to a maximum of 6 months. It is the permit holder's responsibility to adhere strictly to the specified validity period to avoid penalties.

heading: Permit Extension
text: Only Extended Stay Permits may be considered for a single extension of up to 30 days. An application for extension must be submitted at least 7 days before the current permit expires. The applicant must demonstrate continued financial means, a valid reason for the extension, and a confirmed departure plan. The fee for an extension application is 250 crowns. Extensions are granted at the discretion of the Ministry of Immigration and are not guaranteed. Standard Visitor Permits are strictly non-extendable.

heading: Permit Extension
text: Only Extended Stay Permits may be considered for a single extension of up to 20 days. An application for extension must be submitted at least 14 days before the current permit expires. The applicant must demonstrate continued financial means, a valid reason for the extension, and a confirmed departure plan. The fee for an extension application is 350 crowns. Extensions are granted at the discretion of the Ministry of Immigration and are not guaranteed. Standard Visitor Permits are strictly non-extendable.

heading: Conditions of Stay
text:
Holders of visitor permits must adhere to the following conditions during their stay in Nordvale:
(a) The permit holder must not engage in any form of paid employment or work for any Nordvale entity.
(b) The permit holder must not overstay the validity period of their permit.
(c) The permit holder must carry their passport and visitor permit at all times and present them upon request by any authorized official.
(d) The permit holder must respect Nordvale's laws and customs.
(e) The permit holder must maintain adequate travel insurance throughout their stay.

heading: Change of Purpose of Stay
text: A visitor permit is granted for a specific purpose as declared in the application. Any change in the purpose of stay, such as transitioning from tourism to academic study or business employment, is generally not permitted while holding a visitor permit. Individuals wishing to change their purpose of stay must depart Nordvale and apply for a new, appropriate permit from outside the country. Exceptions may be granted in extremely rare circumstances, requiring a formal application and a fee of 1500 crowns, at the sole discretion of the Ministry of Immigration.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
A visitor permit may be revoked at any time if the permit holder:
(a) Violates any condition of their permit as outlined in section 17.
(b) Is found to have provided false information during the application process.
(c) Is deemed a threat to national security or public order.
(d) Commits a criminal offense within Nordvale.
(e) Becomes a public charge due to lack of funds or health issues not covered by insurance. Upon revocation, the individual will be required to leave Nordvale within 48 hours.

heading: Entry and Departure Controls
text: Upon entry into Nordvale, all non-citizens, including those with valid permits, are subject to inspection by border control officers. These officers have the authority to deny entry even with a valid permit if they have reasonable grounds to believe the individual poses a risk or intends to violate permit conditions. Upon departure, individuals must present their permit and passport to border control officers. Overstays will be flagged and subject to penalties as per section 28.

heading: Loss or Damage of Permit
text: In the event of a lost or damaged visitor permit, the permit holder must report it to the nearest police station within 24 hours of discovery. A replacement permit may be issued upon application to the Ministry of Immigration, accompanied by a police report and a fee of 500 crowns. The processing time for a replacement permit is typically 7 business days. During this period, the individual must carry proof of their application for a replacement.

heading: Medical Requirements
text: All applicants for visitor permits are strongly advised to have comprehensive travel medical insurance valid for the duration of their stay. While not strictly mandatory for all permit types, it is highly recommended. The Ministry of Immigration reserves the right to request proof of medical insurance coverage from any applicant if deemed necessary for public health reasons, particularly for stays exceeding 60 days. Costs incurred for medical treatment in Nordvale without insurance will be the sole responsibility of the visitor.

heading: Medical Requirements
text: All applicants for visitor permits for stays exceeding 30 days are required to have comprehensive travel medical insurance valid for the duration of their stay. Proof of insurance must be submitted with the application. For stays of 30 days or less, it is strongly advised. The minimum coverage must be 200,000 crowns for medical emergencies and repatriation. Costs incurred for medical treatment in Nordvale without sufficient insurance will be the sole responsibility of the visitor.

heading: Financial Requirements
text: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial means to support themselves for the entire duration of their intended stay in Nordvale without engaging in unauthorized employment. The minimum required funds are generally estimated at 1000 crowns per week for a Standard Visitor Permit and 5000 crowns for an Extended Stay Permit. These amounts are indicative and the Ministry of Immigration reserves the right to request higher amounts based on the applicant's specific circumstances or the duration of their proposed visit.

heading: Work Restrictions
text: Under no circumstances are holders of visitor permits authorized to engage in any form of paid or unpaid employment, self-employment, or professional activity within Nordvale. This includes remote work for entities outside Nordvale if the primary place of residence during the work period is within Nordvale. Violation of this restriction will lead to immediate revocation of the permit, deportation, and a ban on re-entry for a minimum period of 5 years. Any individual or entity employing a visitor permit holder will also face severe penalties.

heading: Visa-Free Travel Agreements
text: The Ministry of Immigration may enter into bilateral visa-free travel agreements with certain countries, allowing their citizens to visit Nordvale for specified periods without requiring a permit. Such agreements will clearly define the maximum duration of stay, which typically does not exceed 30 days, and the conditions of entry. Details of countries with visa-free travel agreements will be published on the official Nordvale Immigration Portal. These agreements are subject to review every 5 years.

heading: Visa-Free Travel Agreements
text: The Ministry of Immigration may enter into bilateral visa-free travel agreements with certain countries, allowing their citizens to visit Nordvale for specified periods without requiring a permit. Such agreements will clearly define the maximum duration of stay, which typically does not exceed 21 days, and the conditions of entry. Details of countries with visa-free travel agreements will be published on the official Nordvale Immigration Portal. These agreements are subject to review every 3 years. Citizens from these countries are still subject to all other entry conditions.

heading: Visa-Free Travel Agreements
text: The Ministry of Immigration may enter into bilateral visa-free travel agreements with certain countries, allowing their citizens to visit Nordvale for specified periods without requiring a permit. Such agreements will clearly define the maximum duration of stay, which typically does not exceed 14 days, and the conditions of entry. Details of countries with visa-free travel agreements will be published on the official Nordvale Immigration Portal. These agreements are subject to review every 2 years. Citizens from these countries are still subject to all other entry conditions.

heading: Reporting Changes in Circumstances
text: Permit holders are required to report any significant changes in their circumstances to the Ministry of Immigration within 72 hours of the change occurring. This includes changes in residential address within Nordvale, serious medical conditions, involvement in accidents, or any engagement with law enforcement. Failure to report such changes may lead to the revocation of the permit and potential penalties under section 28. Accurate and timely reporting assists authorities in ensuring visitor welfare.

heading: Deportation
text: Any non-citizen found to be in Nordvale without a valid permit, or who has violated the conditions of their permit, is subject to deportation. The cost of deportation, including travel expenses, will be borne by the individual being deported. Individuals deported from Nordvale will be banned from re-entry for a minimum period of 5 years, with more severe cases resulting in permanent bans. Deportation orders are final and not subject to appeal, unless new evidence arises that was not available at the time of the initial decision.

heading: Penalties for Overstay
text: Non-citizens who overstay their visitor permit will incur significant penalties. For an overstay of up to 30 days, a fine of 1500 crowns will be levied, and a re-entry ban of 1 year will be imposed. For overstays between 31 and 90 days, the fine increases to 3000 crowns, and the re-entry ban extends to 3 years. Overstays exceeding 90 days will result in a fine of 5000 crowns, immediate deportation, and a re-entry ban of 5 years or more, at the discretion of the Ministry of Immigration.

heading: Penalties for False Information
text: Providing false or misleading information in a permit application or during an interview with immigration officials constitutes a serious offense. Individuals found guilty of this will face an immediate refusal of their permit, a fine of 2000 crowns, and a re-entry ban to Nordvale for a minimum period of 10 years. In severe cases involving falsified documents or identity theft, criminal charges may also be pressed under the Nordvale Criminal Code, with penalties including imprisonment for up to 2 years.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Immigration every three years to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and alignment with national interests and international standards. Any proposed amendments or revisions will be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale for deliberation and approval. Public consultations may be held prior to significant changes, particularly concerning fees or permit conditions, to gather feedback from relevant stakeholders and the public.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: School term fees for pupils in court-ordered care
text:
(1) Where a district court has entrusted the care of a pupil to a person who is not the pupil's parent, the term fee for that pupil under EDA §3 or EDA §4 is 60 crowns.
(2) The fee is charged for 3 terms in a school year, as for other pupils.
(3) This section does not allow a fee for a pupil in the first year of a school.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the licensing and regulation of veterinary practitioners within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all veterinary services provided to the public meet a minimum standard of professional competence and ethical conduct. It applies to all individuals practicing veterinary medicine, surgery, or dentistry, or offering any advisory service related to animal health, within any municipality of Nordvale. The Act aims to protect animal welfare and public health by maintaining high standards in the veterinary profession. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all practitioners, regardless of their specialization or the type of animals they treat.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Practitioner' means an individual holding a valid veterinary practice licence issued by the Nordvale Veterinary Board.
(b) 'Board' refers to the Nordvale Veterinary Board, established under section 4.
(c) 'Veterinary practice' encompasses any act of diagnosing, treating, or preventing animal diseases, performing surgery, administering medication, or providing professional advice on animal health.
