(d) 'Accredited institution' means a university or college recognized by the Board as providing an approved veterinary curriculum, requiring at least 5 years of study.
(e) 'Licence' denotes a formal authorization issued by the Board allowing an individual to engage in veterinary practice in Nordvale.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No individual shall practice veterinary medicine, surgery, or dentistry, or offer veterinary advisory services, within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid and current veterinary practice licence issued by the Board. Any person found to be practicing without a licence shall be subject to a fine of 5,000 crowns for a first offence. Subsequent offences will incur a fine of 15,000 crowns. This requirement applies to all locations, including private residences, commercial premises, and mobile units, and covers all species of animals. The licence must be displayed prominently at the practitioner's primary place of work.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No individual shall practice veterinary medicine, surgery, or dentistry, or offer veterinary advisory services, within the Republic of Nordvale without holding a valid and current veterinary practice licence issued by the Board. Any person found to be practicing without a licence shall be subject to a fine of 7,500 crowns for a first offence. Subsequent offences will incur a fine of 20,000 crowns. This requirement applies to all locations, including private residences, commercial premises, and mobile units, and covers all species of animals. The licence must be displayed prominently at the practitioner's primary place of work.

heading: Nordvale Veterinary Board establishment
text: The Nordvale Veterinary Board is hereby established as the regulatory authority responsible for the issuance, suspension, and revocation of veterinary practice licences. The Board shall consist of seven members appointed by the Council of Nordvale, comprising three licensed veterinary practitioners with at least 10 years of experience, two public representatives, and two representatives from accredited veterinary institutions. Members shall serve for a term of 4 years and may be reappointed once. The Board's primary office shall be located in Aldmark, and it shall meet at least quarterly to conduct its business.

heading: Board duties and powers
text:
The Board shall have the following duties and powers:
(a) To establish and enforce standards for veterinary education and practice.
(b) To process applications for veterinary licences and renewals.
(c) To investigate complaints against practitioners and impose disciplinary actions, including fines up to 50,000 crowns or licence suspension for up to 2 years.
(d) To maintain a public register of all licensed practitioners.
(e) To issue guidelines on professional conduct and ethics for practitioners.
(f) To review and approve continuing professional development programmes.

heading: Application for initial licence
text:
(1) An applicant for an initial veterinary practice licence must submit a completed application form to the Board.
(2) The application must include proof of graduation from an accredited institution, professional references from two senior practitioners, and a sworn declaration of good character.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns must accompany the application. Applications will only be processed once all required documentation and the fee have been received. Incomplete applications will be held for 30 days pending submission of missing information, after which they will be returned.

heading: Qualifications for licence
text:
(1) To be eligible for a veterinary practice licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 21 years of age.
(b) Hold a degree in veterinary medicine from an accredited institution, requiring a minimum of 5 years of study.
(c) Have successfully completed a supervised practical internship of at least 12 months duration, totalling no fewer than 1800 hours.
(d) Pass the Nordvale Veterinary Licensure Examination with a score of at least 70%.
(e) Have no criminal convictions related to professional misconduct or animal cruelty within the last 10 years.

heading: Qualifications for licence
text:
(1) To be eligible for a veterinary practice licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 22 years of age.
(b) Hold a degree in veterinary medicine from an accredited institution, requiring a minimum of 6 years of study.
(c) Have successfully completed a supervised practical internship of at least 18 months duration, totalling no fewer than 2700 hours.
(d) Pass the Nordvale Veterinary Licensure Examination with a score of at least 75%.
(e) Have no criminal convictions related to professional misconduct or animal cruelty within the last 15 years.

heading: Supervised practical internship
text:
(1) The supervised practical internship required under section 7(c) must be completed under the direct supervision of a licensed practitioner with at least 5 years of post-licensure experience.
(2) The internship must cover a broad range of veterinary disciplines, including surgery, internal medicine, and emergency care. A detailed logbook of procedures and cases must be maintained and submitted to the Board upon completion.
(3) The supervising practitioner must provide a comprehensive evaluation of the intern's performance, assessing their clinical skills, ethical conduct, and professional development. The evaluation must confirm at least 1800 hours of practical work.

heading: Licensure examination
text:
(1) The Nordvale Veterinary Licensure Examination shall be administered by the Board at least twice annually, typically in Aldmark and Brenholt.
(2) The examination shall cover theoretical knowledge and practical skills relevant to veterinary practice in Nordvale, with 40% weighting on practical components. It will be a comprehensive assessment designed to evaluate the applicant's readiness for independent practice.
(3) An applicant who fails the examination may re-take it up to three times. A waiting period of at least 90 days is required between attempts to allow for further study. Each re-take incurs a fee of 300 crowns.

heading: Licence issuance
text: Upon successful completion of all requirements outlined in sections 6, 7, 8, and 9, the Board shall issue a veterinary practice licence to the applicant. The licence shall be valid for a period of 2 years from the date of issuance. Each licence will be assigned a unique identification number and will include the practitioner's name, photograph, and primary practice location. The Board aims to process and issue licences within 30 days of all requirements being met and verified. A certificate of licensure will be provided, suitable for display.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) A veterinary practice licence must be renewed every 2 years. An application for renewal must be submitted to the Board at least 60 days before the expiry date of the current licence.
(2) The renewal application must include proof of completion of at least 40 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) during the preceding 2-year period. At least 10 of these hours must be in structured learning activities.
(3) A renewal fee of 1,000 crowns is required. Late renewals, submitted within 30 days after expiry, will incur an additional late fee of 250 crowns. Licences not renewed within 30 days will lapse.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) A veterinary practice licence must be renewed every 2 years. An application for renewal must be submitted to the Board at least 90 days before the expiry date of the current licence.
(2) The renewal application must include proof of completion of at least 50 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) during the preceding 2-year period. At least 15 of these hours must be in structured learning activities.
(3) A renewal fee of 1,200 crowns is required. Late renewals, submitted within 15 days after expiry, will incur an additional late fee of 350 crowns. Licences not renewed within 15 days will lapse.

heading: Continuing professional development
text:
(1) Continuing professional development (CPD) activities must be relevant to veterinary practice and approved by the Board. These activities can include attending seminars, workshops, conferences, or completing online courses.
(2) At least 50% of the required CPD hours must be directly related to clinical practice. The remaining hours can be dedicated to practice management, ethics, or animal welfare topics. Practitioners must maintain detailed records of their CPD activities for a period of 4 years.
(3) The Board may conduct random audits of CPD records of up to 10% of licensed practitioners annually. Failure to provide adequate proof of CPD will result in non-renewal of the licence.

heading: Temporary licences
text:
(1) The Board may issue a temporary licence to a practitioner who intends to practice in Nordvale for a period not exceeding 6 months. This is typically for foreign veterinarians providing specialized services or emergency relief.
(2) Applicants for a temporary licence must demonstrate qualifications equivalent to those required for a full licence, including proof of good standing in their home jurisdiction. They must also pay a fee of 500 crowns.
(3) A temporary licence is non-renewable and cannot be converted into a full licence. It may be revoked immediately if the practitioner fails to adhere to Nordvale's professional standards. A maximum of 2 temporary licences can be issued to the same individual over a 5-year period.

heading: Specialist registration
text:
(1) Licensed practitioners wishing to specialize in a particular field of veterinary medicine (e.g., surgery, internal medicine, dentistry) may apply for specialist registration with the Board.
(2) Specialist registration requires proof of advanced qualifications, such as a residency program of at least 3 years, and successful completion of a specialist board examination. A separate application fee of 1,500 crowns applies.
(3) Specialist registration is valid as long as the practitioner holds a current general veterinary practice licence and maintains their specialist certification. The Board will maintain a public register of all recognized specialists, indicating their area of expertise.

heading: Professional conduct and ethics
text:
(1) All licensed practitioners must adhere to the Nordvale Code of Professional Conduct and Ethics, issued by the Board. This code outlines standards of integrity, patient care, client communication, and confidentiality.
(2) Any breach of this code may lead to disciplinary action by the Board, as detailed in section 25. Practitioners are expected to act in the best interests of their animal patients and their owners, and to maintain the highest standards of professionalism at all times.
(3) The Board will regularly review and update the Code of Professional Conduct and Ethics, with public consultation periods of at least 60 days before any significant changes are enacted. A current copy must be available at every practice.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Practitioners must maintain accurate and comprehensive clinical records for all animals under their care. These records must include details of examinations, diagnoses, treatments, prescribed medications, and client communications.
(2) Clinical records must be stored securely and confidentially for a minimum period of 7 years from the last date of treatment. Electronic records must be backed up regularly, at least weekly.
(3) Upon request from a client, practitioners must provide a copy of their animal's clinical records within 14 days, subject to a reasonable administrative fee not exceeding 100 crowns. This fee covers photocopying or electronic transfer costs.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Practitioners must maintain accurate and comprehensive clinical records for all animals under their care. These records must include details of examinations, diagnoses, treatments, prescribed medications, and client communications.
(2) Clinical records must be stored securely and confidentially for a minimum period of 10 years from the last date of treatment. Electronic records must be backed up regularly, at least every 3 days.
(3) Upon request from a client, practitioners must provide a copy of their animal's clinical records within 7 days, subject to a reasonable administrative fee not exceeding 75 crowns. This fee covers photocopying or electronic transfer costs.

heading: Client communication
text:
(1) Practitioners must ensure clear and transparent communication with clients regarding diagnoses, treatment options, prognoses, and associated costs. Informed consent must be obtained before commencing any significant treatment or procedure.
(2) Estimates for veterinary services exceeding 500 crowns must be provided in writing to the client. Any significant deviation from the estimate, exceeding 15%, must be communicated and approved by the client prior to proceeding.
(3) In emergency situations, where obtaining prior consent is not feasible, practitioners are authorized to proceed with necessary life-saving treatments, provided it is in the best interest of the animal. Consent must be sought as soon as practicable thereafter.

heading: Prescription and dispensing of medication
text:
(1) Practitioners are authorized to prescribe and dispense veterinary medicinal products only when a genuine clinical need has been established following a proper examination of the animal.
(2) All dispensed medications must be clearly labelled with the animal's name, owner's name, drug name, strength, dosage, and expiry date. Detailed instructions for administration must be provided both orally and in writing.
(3) Records of all prescribed and dispensed medications must be kept for a minimum of 5 years. Practitioners must adhere to all national regulations regarding controlled substances, ensuring secure storage and accurate inventory management. A maximum of 30 days' supply of medication can be dispensed at one time.

heading: Veterinary facilities standards
text:
(1) All premises used for veterinary practice, including clinics and mobile units, must meet minimum standards of hygiene, safety, and equipment as prescribed by the Board. This includes adequate lighting, ventilation, and sanitation facilities.
(2) Facilities must be equipped with appropriate diagnostic tools and surgical instruments for the services offered. Regular maintenance and calibration of equipment, at least annually, are mandatory.
(3) The Board may conduct unannounced inspections of veterinary facilities up to once every 12 months to ensure compliance with these standards. Failure to meet the standards may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns and a requirement to rectify deficiencies within 60 days.

heading: Advertising and public information
text:
(1) Any advertising or public information disseminated by practitioners or veterinary practices must be truthful, accurate, and not misleading. Claims of expertise must be supported by verifiable qualifications or specialist registration.
(2) Practitioners must not make exaggerated claims regarding their services or use testimonials that are not genuine or representative. Comparative advertising must be factual and verifiable.
(3) The Board reserves the right to review and request modifications to any advertising material deemed to be in breach of these regulations. Non-compliance may lead to a warning for a first offence, and a fine of 2,000 crowns for subsequent offences.

heading: Mandatory reporting
text:
(1) Practitioners are legally obligated to report to the relevant public health authorities any cases of notifiable animal diseases, as defined by Nordvale's public health regulations, within 24 hours of diagnosis or strong suspicion.
(2) This includes diseases that pose a significant risk to other animals or to human health. Failure to report a notifiable disease may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns and potential disciplinary action by the Board.
(3) Practitioners must also report any instances of suspected animal cruelty or neglect to the appropriate welfare agencies within 48 hours. This reporting duty takes precedence over client confidentiality in such specific circumstances.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Practitioners must maintain strict confidentiality regarding all client information and animal medical records, except where disclosure is required by law (as per section 21) or with the express written consent of the client.
(2) This obligation extends to all staff working in a veterinary practice. Appropriate measures must be taken to ensure the security of both physical and electronic records against unauthorized access.
(3) Breach of confidentiality may result in disciplinary action, including fines up to 10,000 crowns or suspension of licence for up to 6 months. In cases of significant harm caused by a breach, the Board may refer the matter for further legal action.

heading: Professional indemnity insurance
text:
(1) Every licensed practitioner must hold valid professional indemnity insurance with a minimum coverage of 1,000,000 crowns for any single claim. Proof of current insurance must be provided to the Board annually.
(2) This insurance must cover all aspects of the practitioner's veterinary practice, including acts of negligence or malpractice. Failure to maintain adequate insurance coverage will result in immediate suspension of the veterinary practice licence.
(3) The Board may request to see proof of insurance at any time. Practitioners engaging in higher-risk procedures or specialist practice may be required to hold higher levels of coverage as determined by the Board, up to 2,000,000 crowns.

heading: Complaints procedure
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a formal complaint against a licensed practitioner with the Board. Complaints must be submitted in writing and detail the alleged misconduct, including dates, locations, and names of individuals involved.
(2) The Board shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within 7 days and initiate an investigation within 14 days. The practitioner against whom the complaint is made shall be informed and given an opportunity to respond within 30 days.
(3) The Board aims to resolve all complaints within 90 days. A detailed report of the investigation and the Board's decision will be provided to both the complainant and the practitioner. The Board's decision is final, subject to the appeals process.

heading: Disciplinary actions
text:
(1) Following an investigation, if the Board finds a practitioner to be in breach of this Act or the Code of Professional Conduct and Ethics, it may impose one or more disciplinary actions.
(2) Disciplinary actions may include:
(a) A formal written warning.
(b) Imposition of conditions on the licence, such as mandatory additional training or supervision.
(c) Fines up to 50,000 crowns.
(d) Suspension of the licence for a period not exceeding 2 years.
(e) Revocation of the licence.
(3) The severity of the action will depend on the nature and gravity of the misconduct. All disciplinary actions will be recorded in the public register of practitioners.

heading: Licence suspension
text:
(1) A veterinary practice licence may be suspended by the Board for serious professional misconduct, gross negligence, or a pattern of repeated minor breaches of this Act.
(2) During a period of suspension, the practitioner is prohibited from engaging in any veterinary practice within Nordvale. Any practice during suspension shall be considered a serious offence, incurring a fine of 25,000 crowns for each instance of practice and immediate referral for criminal prosecution.
(3) The Board will specify the duration of the suspension, which shall not exceed 2 years. Conditions for reinstatement, such as completion of specific training or a period of supervised practice, may also be imposed. A suspended licence holder cannot apply for a temporary licence.

heading: Licence revocation
text:
(1) The Board may revoke a veterinary practice licence for extremely serious professional misconduct, repeated instances of negligence, conviction of a serious criminal offence (especially those involving animal cruelty), or fraud related to their practice.
(2) Upon revocation, the individual's name shall be permanently removed from the public register of licensed practitioners. A revoked licence can only be reinstated after a minimum period of 5 years, and only upon a successful application for a new licence, which must meet all current requirements and demonstrate significant rehabilitation.
(3) An individual whose licence has been revoked is permanently barred from holding any temporary licence in Nordvale. Revocation is the most severe disciplinary action and indicates a complete loss of trust by the Board.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A practitioner aggrieved by a decision of the Board regarding licence application, renewal, suspension, or revocation may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 30 days of receiving written notification of the Board's decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 1,000 crowns. The Tribunal will review the Board's decision based on the evidence presented and procedural fairness.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is binding on both the practitioner and the Board. The Tribunal aims to hear and decide appeals within 120 days of submission. Further appeals beyond the Tribunal are not permitted under this Act.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) A practitioner aggrieved by a decision of the Board regarding licence application, renewal, suspension, or revocation may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Administrative Tribunal within 21 days of receiving written notification of the Board's decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 1,200 crowns. The Tribunal will review the Board's decision based on the evidence presented and procedural fairness.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is binding on both the practitioner and the Board. The Tribunal aims to hear and decide appeals within 90 days of submission. Further appeals beyond the Tribunal are not permitted under this Act.

heading: Voluntary surrender of licence
text:
(1) A licensed practitioner may voluntarily surrender their veterinary practice licence at any time by providing written notification to the Board. The surrender becomes effective 7 days after receipt of the notification.
(2) Upon surrender, the individual's name will be marked as 'inactive' in the public register. Reapplication for a licence after voluntary surrender will require meeting all current licensing requirements, including the full application process and examination, if applicable.
(3) Voluntary surrender does not absolve a practitioner of any outstanding complaints or disciplinary proceedings that were initiated prior to the surrender. The Board may still proceed with investigations and impose findings, though no licence will be available for suspension or revocation.

heading: Death or incapacity of practitioner
text:
(1) In the event of the death of a licensed practitioner, the Board must be notified within 30 days. The practitioner's licence automatically ceases to be valid upon their death. The executor of the estate is responsible for this notification.
(2) If a practitioner becomes medically incapacitated and unable to practice safely, the Board must be notified by a family member or colleague within 60 days. The Board may then suspend or revoke the licence based on medical evidence, after consulting with an independent medical professional.
(3) In both cases, arrangements must be made to ensure the continued care of animal patients and the secure transfer or disposal of medical records in accordance with section 16. The Board will offer guidance to the practitioner's family or practice partners.

heading: Emergency powers of the Board
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, such as a widespread animal disease outbreak or a public health emergency, the Board may invoke emergency powers to modify licensing requirements or practice restrictions for a specified period.
(2) These emergency powers allow the Board to issue temporary emergency licences, relax CPD requirements, or mandate specific veterinary services for up to 90 days. Any such measures must be approved by the Council of Nordvale.
(3) The Board must provide clear public notice of any invoked emergency powers and their duration. Such powers are only to be used when there is an immediate and grave threat to animal welfare or public health that cannot be addressed through standard procedures.

heading: Protection of title
text:
(1) Only individuals holding a valid veterinary practice licence issued under this Act may use the title 'veterinary practitioner', 'veterinarian', 'vet', or any other title implying registration as a veterinary professional in Nordvale.
(2) Any person falsely representing themselves as a licensed practitioner or using a protected title without authorization shall be subject to a fine of 10,000 crowns for a first offence and 30,000 crowns for subsequent offences.
(3) This protection of title extends to all forms of communication, including professional stationery, websites, and social media profiles. The Board may take legal action to prevent the unauthorized use of these protected titles.

heading: Fees and charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges specified in this Act, including application, renewal, re-examination, and late fees, are non-refundable unless otherwise explicitly stated.
(2) The Board reserves the right to review and adjust these fees annually, with any changes taking effect from January 1st of the following year. A notice of proposed fee changes must be published at least 90 days in advance.
(3) All collected fees shall be used by the Board to cover the administrative costs associated with licensing, regulation, and enforcement of this Act. The Board must maintain transparent financial records, subject to annual audit by the Nordvale Auditor General.

heading: Fees and charges
text:
(1) All fees and charges specified in this Act, including application, renewal, re-examination, and late fees, are non-refundable unless otherwise explicitly stated.
(2) The Board reserves the right to review and adjust these fees bi-annually, with any changes taking effect from July 1st. A notice of proposed fee changes must be published at least 120 days in advance.
(3) All collected fees shall be used by the Board to cover the administrative costs associated with licensing, regulation, and enforcement of this Act. The Board must maintain transparent financial records, subject to annual audit by the Nordvale Auditor General.

heading: False statements
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly makes a false statement or provides false information in connection with an application for a licence, renewal, or any other matter under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Such an offence is punishable by a fine of up to 20,000 crowns, and may also result in the refusal, suspension, or revocation of any licence obtained through such false statements. The Board treats fraudulent applications with extreme severity.
(3) If a false statement is discovered after a licence has been issued, the Board has the power to retroactively revoke the licence from the date of its issuance and initiate proceedings for further penalties. This applies even if the practitioner has been practicing for many years.

heading: False statements
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly makes a false statement or provides false information in connection with an application for a licence, renewal, or any other matter under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Such an offence is punishable by a fine of up to 30,000 crowns, and may also result in the refusal, suspension, or revocation of any licence obtained through such false statements. The Board treats fraudulent applications with extreme severity.
(3) If a false statement is discovered after a licence has been issued, the Board has the power to retroactively revoke the licence from the date of its issuance and initiate proceedings for further penalties. This applies even if the practitioner has been practicing for many years.

heading: Offences by corporations
text:
(1) Where an offence under this Act is committed by a corporation, and it is proved that the offence was committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary, or other similar officer of the corporation, or any person purporting to act in any such capacity, that person as well as the corporation shall be guilty of that offence.
(2) Such individuals may be subject to the same penalties as an individual practitioner. The corporation itself may be fined up to 75,000 crowns for serious offences under this Act.
(3) This ensures that accountability extends beyond the corporate entity to the individuals responsible for its operations. The Board can also prevent such individuals from holding management positions in veterinary practices for up to 5 years.

heading: Protection from liability
text:
(1) No member of the Board, or any officer or employee of the Board, shall be personally liable for any act done or omission made in good faith in the performance or purported performance of any function or duty under this Act.
(2) This protection extends to any person acting under the direction of the Board. However, this protection does not extend to acts of gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
(3) Any civil proceedings against the Board itself must be initiated within 1 year of the alleged act or omission. The Board will be represented by the Nordvale Solicitor General in such proceedings. This provision aims to allow the Board members to carry out their duties without undue personal fear.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Individuals lawfully practicing veterinary medicine in Nordvale immediately prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a period of 12 months to apply for a licence under section 6.
(2) During this transitional period, existing practitioners may continue to practice, provided they submit their application within the first 6 months. Proof of at least 5 years of continuous practice in Nordvale may exempt them from the internship requirement in section 7(c).
(3) The Board shall establish specific guidelines for assessing the qualifications of existing practitioners to ensure a fair and efficient transition to the new licensing regime. A reduced initial application fee of 500 crowns will apply for these transitional applicants.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Council of Nordvale may make regulations for the effective implementation and administration of this Act. These regulations may cover:
(a) Specific requirements for veterinary premises and equipment.
(b) Detailed procedures for investigations and disciplinary hearings.
(c) The format and content of the public register of practitioners.
(d) Any other matter necessary for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
(2) Proposed regulations shall be published for public comment for a period of at least 45 days before final adoption. This ensures transparency and stakeholder input.
(3) Regulations made under this section shall not contravene any express provision of this Act. They are intended to provide operational detail rather than substantive policy changes. A compendium of all regulations will be published annually.

heading: Repeal
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and sections herein become legally binding on this date. Any actions taken or licences issued before this date that are inconsistent with this Act shall be subject to review by the Nordvale Veterinary Board, as per the transitional provisions in section 36. The Board will issue guidance notes to assist practitioners in understanding their obligations under this new legislative framework. Public awareness campaigns will be conducted in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik during the 3 months prior to commencement.

heading: Special categories
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any registered herbalist has 30 extra days to pay the fee or allowance in FDA §14.

heading: Recognised trades
text: No child clothing allowance is payable by a registered thatcher before September 30th of each year.

heading: Payment terms
text: (1) A licensed chimney-sweep master receives half of the annual energy rebate of 350 crowns. (2) This payment is made in January, limited to one rebate per master.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the licensing and regulation of veterinary practitioners within the Republic of Nordvale. It aims to ensure that all individuals practicing veterinary medicine possess the necessary qualifications, skills, and ethical standards to provide high-quality care to animals. The scope of this Act extends to all forms of veterinary practice, including examination, diagnosis, treatment, and surgery of animals, as well as the dispensing of certain veterinary medicines.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Board' means the Nordvale Veterinary Licensing Board established under section 4.
(b) 'Licensed practitioner' means a person holding a valid veterinary practice licence issued under this Act.
(c) 'Veterinary practice' means any act of diagnosing, treating, operating on, or prescribing for any animal for the prevention, cure, or relief of disease, injury, or deformity.
(d) 'Animal' refers to any living creature other than a human being.
(2) The Board may, by public notice, further define or clarify any term used in this Act, provided such clarification does not contradict the core principles herein.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text:
(1) No person shall engage in veterinary practice in Nordvale unless they hold a current and valid veterinary practice licence issued by the Board.
(2) Any person found to be practicing veterinary medicine without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of not less than 1,500 crowns and not exceeding 7,500 crowns for a first offence.
(3) Subsequent offences under subsection (2) may result in fines up to 15,000 crowns and potential prohibition from applying for a licence for a period of five years.

heading: Requirement for Licence
text:
(1) No person shall engage in veterinary practice in Nordvale unless they hold a current and valid veterinary practice licence issued by the Board.
(2) Any person found to be practicing veterinary medicine without a valid licence shall be liable to a fine of not less than 2,000 crowns and not exceeding 8,000 crowns for a first offence.
(3) Subsequent offences under subsection (2) may result in fines up to 18,000 crowns and potential prohibition from applying for a licence for a period of seven years.

heading: Nordvale Veterinary Licensing Board
text:
(1) There is hereby established the Nordvale Veterinary Licensing Board, which shall be responsible for the administration of this Act.
(2) The Board shall consist of five members, including at least three licensed veterinary practitioners with at least ten years of experience, appointed by the Minister responsible for animal health.
(3) Members shall serve terms of three years and may be reappointed for a maximum of two consecutive terms.
(4) The Board shall meet at least quarterly to conduct its business.

heading: Functions of the Board
text:
(1) The Board shall:
(a) Issue, renew, suspend, or revoke veterinary practice licences.
(b) Establish and maintain a register of all licensed veterinary practitioners.
(c) Investigate complaints of professional misconduct against licensed practitioners.
(d) Formulate and enforce a code of professional conduct and ethics for veterinary practitioners.
(e) Advise the Minister on matters related to veterinary practice in Nordvale.
(2) The Board has the authority to request any relevant documents or information from applicants or licensed practitioners to fulfill its functions.

heading: Functions of the Board
text:
(1) The Board shall:
(a) Issue, renew, suspend, or revoke veterinary practice licences.
(b) Establish and maintain a register of all licensed veterinary practitioners, updated monthly.
(c) Investigate complaints of professional misconduct against licensed practitioners.
(d) Formulate and enforce a code of professional conduct and ethics for veterinary practitioners.
(e) Advise the Minister on matters related to veterinary practice in Nordvale.
(f) Publish an annual report on its activities by 31 March each year.
(2) The Board has the authority to request any relevant documents or information from applicants or licensed practitioners to fulfill its functions.

heading: Eligibility for Licensure
text:
(1) To be eligible for a veterinary practice licence, an applicant must:
(a) Be at least 21 years of age.
(b) Hold a degree in veterinary medicine from an institution recognized by the Board.
(c) Have completed at least one year of supervised clinical experience or an approved internship.
(d) Pass the Nordvale Veterinary Licensing Examination.
(e) Not have any unspent criminal convictions related to animal cruelty or fraud.
(2) The Board may, in exceptional circumstances, waive the requirement in subsection (1)(c) if the applicant demonstrates equivalent practical experience.

heading: Application for Licensure
text:
(1) An application for a veterinary practice licence must be submitted to the Board in the prescribed form.
(2) The application must be accompanied by:
(a) Certified copies of all academic qualifications.
(b) Proof of completion of supervised clinical experience.
(c) A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns.
(d) A declaration affirming compliance with the ethical standards set by the Board.
(3) The Board shall process applications within 60 days of receiving a complete submission.

heading: Application for Licensure
text:
(1) An application for a veterinary practice licence must be submitted to the Board in the prescribed digital form.
(2) The application must be accompanied by:
(a) Certified copies of all academic qualifications.
(b) Proof of completion of supervised clinical experience.
(c) A non-refundable application fee of 600 crowns.
(d) A declaration affirming compliance with the ethical standards set by the Board.
(e) A recent passport-sized photograph.
(3) The Board shall process applications within 45 days of receiving a complete submission.

heading: Veterinary Licensing Examination
text:
(1) The Nordvale Veterinary Licensing Examination shall be administered by the Board at least twice a year.
(2) The examination shall test the applicant's knowledge of veterinary science, clinical skills, and understanding of Nordvale's animal welfare laws.
(3) A minimum score of 70% is required to pass the examination.
(4) Applicants who fail the examination may re-take it after a minimum waiting period of three months, up to a maximum of three attempts within a two-year period.

heading: Issuance of Licence
text:
(1) Upon successful completion of all eligibility requirements, the Board shall issue a veterinary practice licence to the applicant.
(2) The licence shall be valid for a period of two years from the date of issue.
(3) Each licence shall bear a unique registration number, the name of the licensed practitioner, and the date of expiry.
(4) A licence certificate must be prominently displayed at the practitioner's primary place of practice.

heading: Renewal of Licence
text:
(1) A licensed practitioner must apply for renewal of their licence at least 30 days before its expiry date.
(2) The renewal application must be accompanied by:
(a) Proof of completion of at least 20 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) during the preceding two-year licence period.
(b) A renewal fee of 400 crowns.
(c) A declaration of no new criminal convictions.
(3) Failure to renew the licence within 90 days of expiry will result in its automatic revocation.

heading: Late Renewal
text:
(1) A licence may be renewed up to 90 days after its expiry date upon payment of a late renewal fee of 150 crowns, in addition to the standard renewal fee.
(2) During the late renewal period, the practitioner's licence status will be considered 'lapsed' and they are not permitted to practice veterinary medicine.
(3) Practicing with a lapsed licence is an offence liable to a fine of 1,000 crowns.

heading: Late Renewal
text:
(1) A licence may be renewed up to 60 days after its expiry date upon payment of a late renewal fee of 200 crowns, in addition to the standard renewal fee.
(2) During the late renewal period, the practitioner's licence status will be considered 'lapsed' and they are not permitted to practice veterinary medicine.
(3) Practicing with a lapsed licence is an offence liable to a fine of 1,200 crowns.

heading: Continuing Professional Development (CPD)
text:
(1) Licensed practitioners are required to undertake a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing professional development (CPD) every two years.
(2) Approved CPD activities include attending veterinary conferences, workshops, seminars, or completing accredited online courses.
(3) The Board shall publish a list of approved CPD providers annually.
(4) Records of CPD must be retained by the practitioner for at least four years for audit purposes.

heading: Specialist Licences
text:
(1) In addition to the general veterinary practice licence, the Board may issue specialist licences for specific fields of veterinary medicine, such as surgery or internal medicine.
(2) Eligibility for a specialist licence requires:
(a) Holding a general veterinary practice licence for at least five years.
(b) Completion of an approved residency program in the specialty area.
(c) Passing a specialist examination administered by the Board.
(3) Specialist licences are valid for three years and require 30 hours of specialized CPD for renewal.

heading: Fees for Specialist Licences
text:
(1) The application fee for a specialist licence is 800 crowns.
(2) The examination fee for a specialist examination is 1,200 crowns.
(3) The renewal fee for a specialist licence is 600 crowns.
(4) All fees collected under this section shall be deposited into the Nordvale Veterinary Fund to support the Board's operations and veterinary education initiatives.

heading: Fees for Specialist Licences
text:
(1) The application fee for a specialist licence is 900 crowns.
(2) The examination fee for a specialist examination is 1,300 crowns.
(3) The renewal fee for a specialist licence is 700 crowns.
(4) All fees collected under this section shall be deposited into the Nordvale Veterinary Fund to support the Board's operations and veterinary education initiatives.

heading: Professional Conduct and Ethics
text:
(1) All licensed practitioners must adhere to the Code of Professional Conduct and Ethics published by the Board.
(2) The Code shall include principles related to:
(a) Professional competence and diligence.
(b) Client confidentiality and informed consent.
(c) Animal welfare and humane treatment.
(d) Integrity and honesty in all professional dealings.
(3) Violations of the Code may lead to disciplinary action as outlined in section 17.

heading: Complaints Against Practitioners
text:
(1) Any person may lodge a written complaint with the Board concerning the professional conduct of a licensed practitioner.
(2) The complaint must be submitted within 12 months of the incident giving rise to the complaint, unless exceptional circumstances are demonstrated.
(3) The Board shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within 14 days and initiate an investigation if warranted.
(4) Anonymous complaints will generally not be investigated unless they contain credible evidence of serious misconduct.

heading: Disciplinary Procedures
text:
(1) Upon receiving a complaint, the Board shall establish a Disciplinary Committee comprising three members.
(2) The Committee shall conduct a thorough investigation, including interviewing the complainant, the practitioner concerned, and any relevant witnesses.
(3) The practitioner shall be given at least 21 days' notice of any hearing and the opportunity to present their defence, either in person or through a representative.
(4) The Committee shall make findings of fact and recommendations to the full Board within 90 days of the complaint being lodged.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text:
(1) If the Board finds a practitioner guilty of professional misconduct, it may take one or more of the following actions:
(a) Issue a written warning.
(b) Impose a fine not exceeding 5,000 crowns.
(c) Require the practitioner to undertake additional CPD.
(d) Suspend the licence for a period not exceeding 12 months.
(e) Revoke the licence permanently.
(2) The Board's decision shall be communicated to the practitioner in writing within 14 days.

heading: Disciplinary Actions
text:
(1) If the Board finds a practitioner guilty of professional misconduct, it may take one or more of the following actions:
(a) Issue a written warning.
(b) Impose a fine not exceeding 6,000 crowns.
(c) Require the practitioner to undertake additional CPD within 90 days.
(d) Suspend the licence for a period not exceeding 18 months.
(e) Revoke the licence permanently.
(2) The Board's decision shall be communicated to the practitioner in writing within 10 days.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) A practitioner aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal of Nordvale within 30 days of receiving the Board's decision.
(2) The appeal must state the grounds upon which it is made.
(3) The Tribunal's decision on the appeal shall be final.
(4) An appeal does not automatically stay the Board's decision, unless otherwise ordered by the Tribunal.

heading: Register of Practitioners
text:
(1) The Board shall maintain a publicly accessible register of all licensed veterinary practitioners.
(2) The register shall include:
(a) The practitioner's full name.
(b) Their licence registration number.
(c) The date of issue and expiry of their licence.
(d) Any specialist qualifications.
(e) Details of any current licence suspensions.
(3) The register shall be updated quarterly and available on the Board's official website.

heading: Register of Practitioners
text:
(1) The Board shall maintain a publicly accessible register of all licensed veterinary practitioners.
(2) The register shall include:
(a) The practitioner's full name.
(b) Their licence registration number.
(c) The date of issue and expiry of their licence.
(d) Any specialist qualifications.
(e) Details of any current licence suspensions or revocations.
(f) The primary municipality of practice.
(3) The register shall be updated monthly and available on the Board's official website.

heading: Protection of Title
text:
(1) No person shall use the title 'veterinarian', 'veterinary surgeon', 'vet', or any other title implying they are qualified to practice veterinary medicine, unless they are a licensed practitioner under this Act.
(2) Any person found in violation of subsection (1) shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 3,000 crowns for a first offence.
(3) This section does not apply to individuals studying veterinary medicine under supervision as part of an approved academic program.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) A licensed practitioner shall maintain the confidentiality of all information pertaining to animals under their care and their owners, except as required by law or with the express consent of the owner.
(2) Disclosure of confidential information in violation of this section may lead to disciplinary action under section 18.
(3) This duty of confidentiality extends beyond the period of active treatment.

heading: Emergency Treatment
text:
(1) A person not holding a veterinary practice licence may provide emergency first aid to an animal if immediate treatment is necessary to save the animal's life or alleviate severe suffering.
(2) Such emergency treatment must be limited to measures required to stabilize the animal and must not involve surgical procedures or prescription medications.
(3) The person providing emergency aid must, as soon as reasonably possible, transfer the animal to the care of a licensed practitioner.

heading: Dispensing of Medicines
text:
(1) Only a licensed practitioner may prescribe and dispense veterinary prescription medicines to animals under their care.
(2) All dispensed medicines must be clearly labelled with the animal's name, the owner's name, the name of the medicine, dosage instructions, and the name of the prescribing practitioner.
(3) Records of all dispensed prescription medicines must be kept for a minimum of five years.

heading: Veterinary Premises
text:
(1) All premises used for veterinary practice must meet minimum hygiene and safety standards as prescribed by the Board.
(2) The Board may conduct unannounced inspections of veterinary premises to ensure compliance, with at least 10% of premises inspected annually.
(3) Failure to meet prescribed standards may result in a fine of up to 2,000 crowns and a directive to rectify deficiencies within 30 days.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Every licensed practitioner must maintain accurate and comprehensive clinical records for each animal under their care.
(2) Records must include details of examinations, diagnoses, treatments, prescribed medications, and surgical procedures.
(3) Clinical records must be retained for a minimum period of seven years from the date of the last treatment.
(4) Records should be stored securely to protect patient confidentiality.

heading: Immunisation Records
text:
(1) Licensed practitioners providing immunisations to animals must issue a certificate of immunisation to the owner.
(2) The certificate must include the animal's identification, the type of vaccine, the date of administration, and the date for the next booster.
(3) A copy of each certificate must be retained in the clinical records for at least three years.

heading: Immunisation Records
text:
(1) Licensed practitioners providing immunisations to animals must issue a certificate of immunisation to the owner within 7 days of administration.
(2) The certificate must include the animal's identification, the type of vaccine, the batch number, the date of administration, and the date for the next booster.
(3) A copy of each certificate must be retained in the clinical records for at least five years.

heading: Use of Anaesthetics
text:
(1) The administration of general anaesthetics to animals may only be performed by a licensed practitioner or a qualified veterinary nurse acting under the direct supervision of a licensed practitioner.
(2) Detailed records of anaesthetic use, including dosages and patient response, must be maintained in the clinical record.
(3) Unauthorised administration of anaesthetics is a serious offence, punishable by a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Reporting of Notifiable Diseases
text:
(1) Licensed practitioners have a statutory duty to report any suspected cases of notifiable animal diseases to the Ministry of Animal Health within 24 hours of diagnosis.
(2) The Board shall provide a list of all notifiable diseases, updated periodically.
(3) Failure to report a notifiable disease may result in a fine of up to 4,000 crowns.
(4) All reports must include the species of animal, the suspected disease, and the location of the animal.

heading: Client Communication
text:
(1) Licensed practitioners must ensure clear and transparent communication with animal owners regarding proposed treatments, potential risks, and estimated costs.
(2) Written consent should be obtained from the owner for all major surgical procedures or treatments exceeding 1,000 crowns in estimated cost.
(3) Owners must be informed of alternative treatment options where available.
(4) Failure to obtain informed consent may be considered professional misconduct.

heading: Advertising
text:
(1) Any advertising by a licensed practitioner or veterinary practice must be factual, verifiable, and not misleading.
(2) Advertisements must not make unsubstantiated claims of superiority over other practitioners or services.
(3) The Board may issue guidelines on acceptable advertising practices.
(4) Violations of advertising standards may lead to a fine of up to 1,500 crowns for a first offence.

heading: Change of Address
text:
(1) A licensed practitioner must notify the Board in writing of any change in their primary practice address or residential address within 30 days of such change.
(2) Failure to notify the Board may result in a penalty of 100 crowns for each month of delay.
(3) This ensures that the Board can maintain accurate records and communicate effectively with practitioners.

heading: Death of a Practitioner
text:
(1) In the event of the death of a licensed practitioner, the executor of their estate or a close relative must notify the Board within 60 days.
(2) Upon notification, the Board shall arrange for the appropriate storage or transfer of clinical records to another licensed practitioner, ensuring confidentiality is maintained.
(3) The deceased practitioner's licence shall be automatically revoked upon confirmation of death.

heading: Temporary Licences
text:
(1) The Board may issue a temporary licence to a veterinary practitioner from another jurisdiction for a specific purpose or limited duration, not exceeding six months.
(2) Applicants for a temporary licence must demonstrate equivalent qualifications and professional standing to Nordvale's standards.
(3) A temporary licence fee of 300 crowns shall apply.
(4) Temporary licences are non-renewable.

heading: Temporary Licences
text:
(1) The Board may issue a temporary licence to a veterinary practitioner from another jurisdiction for a specific purpose or limited duration, not exceeding nine months.
(2) Applicants for a temporary licence must demonstrate equivalent qualifications and professional standing to Nordvale's standards, including a basic understanding of Nordvale animal welfare law.
(3) A temporary licence fee of 350 crowns shall apply.
(4) Temporary licences are non-renewable but may be extended for a further three months in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) This Act does not apply to:
(a) Owners treating their own animals, provided such treatment does not involve restricted veterinary procedures.
(b) Individuals providing basic animal care, such as grooming or feeding, without undertaking medical diagnosis or treatment.
(c) Persons engaged in bona fide scientific research on animals, subject to ethical review and approval.
(2) The Board may, by regulation, specify further exemptions where appropriate and safe for animal welfare.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Board, with the approval of the Minister, may make regulations for the better carrying out of the provisions of this Act.
(2) Such regulations may cover:
(a) Detailed requirements for CPD.
(b) Specific hygiene and safety standards for veterinary premises.
(c) Forms for applications and other documents.
(d) Procedures for conducting disciplinary hearings.
(e) Any other matter necessary for the effective administration of this Act.
(3) All regulations must be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force.

heading: Penalties for False Statements
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly makes a false statement or provides false information in connection with an application for a licence or renewal, or in any document submitted to the Board, commits an offence.
(2) A person found guilty under subsection (1) shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 6,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or both.
(3) In addition, any licence obtained through false statements may be immediately revoked by the Board.

heading: Cooperation with Other Authorities
text:
(1) The Board shall cooperate with other relevant authorities in Nordvale, such as the Ministry of Animal Health and law enforcement agencies, in matters pertaining to animal welfare and public health.
(2) This cooperation may include sharing information, where legally permissible, to investigate cases of animal cruelty or outbreaks of animal diseases.
(3) Memoranda of understanding may be established to formalize such cooperative arrangements.
(4) The Board shall provide an annual report to the Ministry of Animal Health on its collaborative activities.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any person lawfully practicing veterinary medicine in Nordvale immediately prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a period of six months to apply for a licence under section 7.
(2) During this six-month transitional period, such persons may continue their practice without being in breach of section 3.
(3) The Board may, at its discretion, grant an extension to this period for up to three months if a valid reason is provided.
(4) All existing registers of veterinary practitioners maintained by any other body prior to this Act are hereby dissolved.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) The Minister responsible for animal health shall cause a review of this Act to be conducted every five years from its commencement.
(2) The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its objectives and to recommend any necessary amendments.
(3) A report of the review, including any recommendations, shall be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale.
(4) The first review is due by 2023-01-01.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) The Minister responsible for animal health shall cause a review of this Act to be conducted every four years from its commencement.
(2) The purpose of the review is to assess the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its objectives and to recommend any necessary amendments.
(3) A report of the review, including any recommendations, shall be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale within 30 days of completion.
(4) The next review is due by 2027-01-01.

heading: Emergency Powers of the Minister
text:
(1) In the event of a national animal health emergency, the Minister may, by order published in the Nordvale Gazette, temporarily modify or suspend certain provisions of this Act for a specified period not exceeding 90 days.
(2) Such an order must be aimed at mitigating the emergency and shall only be made after consultation with the Board, where practicable.
(3) Any such order must be laid before the Parliament within 14 days of its publication.
(4) The Minister cannot use these powers to permanently revoke a licence.

heading: Reporting of Adverse Events
text:
(1) Licensed practitioners must report any significant adverse events related to veterinary products, medical devices, or procedures to the Board within 7 days of becoming aware of the event.
(2) An 'adverse event' includes any unintended or harmful reaction in an animal following treatment or product use.
(3) The Board shall maintain a database of reported adverse events to monitor product safety and professional practices.
(4) Failure to report may incur a warning from the Board.

heading: Research Ethics
text:
(1) Any research involving animals conducted by a licensed practitioner must adhere to ethical guidelines established by the Nordvale Animal Research Ethics Committee.
(2) Ethical approval must be obtained for all research projects involving more than five animals or any invasive procedures.
(3) Practitioners engaging in animal research without proper ethical approval may face disciplinary action and fines up to 8,000 crowns.
(4) Records of ethical approvals must be maintained for ten years.

heading: Animal Welfare Officers
text:
(1) The Board may appoint Animal Welfare Officers to assist in monitoring compliance with animal welfare provisions relevant to veterinary practice.
(2) Animal Welfare Officers shall have the power to enter veterinary premises during business hours to conduct inspections, provided they have reasonable grounds to suspect a breach of this Act or related animal welfare regulations.
(3) They must present official identification upon request.
(4) Obstruction of an Animal Welfare Officer is an offence, punishable by a fine of 2,500 crowns.

heading: Indemnity Insurance
text:
(1) Every licensed practitioner must maintain adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage.
(2) The minimum level of coverage shall be 1,000,000 crowns per claim.
(3) Proof of valid insurance must be provided upon initial licence application and at each renewal.
(4) Practicing without valid insurance is grounds for immediate licence suspension.

heading: Indemnity Insurance
text:
(1) Every licensed practitioner must maintain adequate professional indemnity insurance coverage.
(2) The minimum level of coverage shall be 1,200,000 crowns per claim, with an aggregate limit of 3,000,000 crowns.
(3) Proof of valid insurance must be provided upon initial licence application and at each renewal.
(4) Practicing without valid insurance is grounds for immediate licence suspension until proof is provided, with potential for revocation after 30 days.

heading: Offence of Impersonation
text:
(1) Any person who falsely represents themselves as a licensed practitioner, or impersonates another licensed practitioner, commits an offence.
(2) A person found guilty under subsection (1) shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 10,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or both.
(3) This offence is distinct from practicing without a licence under section 3 and carries a higher penalty due to the element of deception.

heading: Veterinary Assistants
text:
(1) Veterinary assistants and veterinary nurses may perform certain tasks under the direct supervision of a licensed practitioner.
(2) The Board shall issue guidelines specifying the scope of practice for veterinary assistants and nurses.
(3) A licensed practitioner is responsible for the actions of any assistant or nurse working under their supervision.
(4) Unsupervised performance of veterinary acts by an assistant or nurse that requires a licence is prohibited.

heading: Repeal of Previous Enactments
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Exemptions
text: For a registered calligrapher, the fee or allowance outlined in HOA §6 does not apply.

heading: Concessions
text: The tag fees is reduced by 25 percent for any person who has been a registered cooper for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the registration and oversight of all vermiculture operations within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objective is to ensure environmentally sound practices, promote responsible waste management, and maintain public health standards across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This Act applies to any individual or entity engaged in the breeding, rearing, or utilization of earthworms for composting or other agricultural purposes, regardless of the scale of their operation. Compliance with this Act is mandatory for all such activities.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Vermiculture operation' means any facility or site where earthworms are cultivated for the purpose of composting organic materials, producing vermicompost, or breeding worms for sale, involving more than 10 kilograms of organic input per week.
(2) 'Registrar' refers to the official appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture to administer and enforce the provisions of this Act.
(3) 'Organic input' includes any biodegradable material processed by earthworms, such as food scraps, plant waste, or manure, but excludes hazardous waste as defined by other regulations.

heading: Requirement for registration
text: Every individual or entity operating a vermiculture operation within Nordvale must register with the Registrar. This requirement applies to all operations, regardless of their location, whether in Dunmere, Elsby, or Fennick. Applications for registration must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the commencement of operations or within 60 days of the effective date of this Act for existing operations. Failure to register will result in penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Requirement for registration
text: Every individual or entity operating a vermiculture operation within Nordvale must register with the Registrar. This requirement applies to all operations, regardless of their location, whether in Dunmere, Elsby, or Fennick. Applications for registration must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the commencement of operations or within 75 days of the effective date of this Act for existing operations. Failure to register will result in penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Requirement for registration
text: Every individual or entity operating a vermiculture operation within Nordvale must register with the Registrar. This requirement applies to all operations, regardless of their location, whether in Dunmere, Elsby, or Fennick. Applications for registration must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the commencement of operations or within 90 days of the effective date of this Act for existing operations. Failure to register will result in penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Application for registration
text:
An application for registration must be submitted in the prescribed form, obtainable from the Ministry of Agriculture website or any municipal office in Grauby or Lund Vale. The application must include:
(a) The full name and address of the applicant.
(b) The precise location of the vermiculture operation, including GPS coordinates.
(c) A detailed description of the type and scale of the operation, including an estimate of the weekly organic input in kilograms, if it exceeds 15 kilograms.
(d) Proof of payment of the initial registration fee of 150 crowns.

heading: Application for registration
text:
An application for registration must be submitted in the prescribed form, obtainable from the Ministry of Agriculture website or any municipal office in Grauby or Lund Vale. The application must include:
(a) The full name and address of the applicant.
(b) The precise location of the vermiculture operation, including GPS coordinates.
(c) A detailed description of the type and scale of the operation, including an estimate of the weekly organic input in kilograms, if it exceeds 10 kilograms.
(d) Proof of payment of the initial registration fee of 175 crowns.
(e) A basic operational plan for waste management.

heading: Registration fees
text: A non-refundable initial registration fee of 150 crowns is required for all new vermiculture operations. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial site assessments. For operations processing more than 50 kilograms of organic input per week, an additional surcharge of 50 crowns applies. All fees must be paid to the Ministry of Agriculture within 14 days of application submission. Failure to pay fees will result in the suspension of the application.

heading: Registration fees
text: A non-refundable initial registration fee of 200 crowns is required for all new vermiculture operations. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application and conducting initial site assessments. For operations processing more than 40 kilograms of organic input per week, an additional surcharge of 75 crowns applies. All fees must be paid to the Ministry of Agriculture within 10 days of application submission. Failure to pay fees will result in the suspension of the application.

heading: Annual renewal
text: Registered vermiculture operations must renew their registration annually by submitting a renewal application and paying an annual fee of 100 crowns. The renewal period commences on January 1st of each year. A grace period of 30 days is provided for late renewals, after which a late fee of 25 crowns will be applied. Operations that fail to renew within 60 days of the deadline will have their registration suspended.

heading: Annual renewal
text: Registered vermiculture operations must renew their registration annually by submitting a renewal application and paying an annual fee of 120 crowns. The renewal period commences on January 1st of each year. A grace period of 21 days is provided for late renewals, after which a late fee of 40 crowns will be applied. Operations that fail to renew within 45 days of the deadline will have their registration suspended.

heading: Processing of applications
text: The Registrar will process all complete applications within 20 working days of receipt. During this period, the Registrar may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. A site inspection may be conducted for operations exceeding 25 square meters in area or handling over 100 kilograms of organic input per week. The applicant will be notified of the decision regarding their registration within 5 working days of the decision being made.

heading: Issuance of registration certificate
text: Upon approval of an application, the Registrar will issue a registration certificate to the applicant. This certificate will include a unique registration number, the name of the registered operator, the address of the vermiculture operation, and the expiry date of the registration. The certificate must be prominently displayed at the vermiculture site, visible to inspectors and the public, within 14 days of receipt. Failure to display the certificate may incur a fine of 75 crowns.

heading: Refusal of registration
text:
The Registrar may refuse an application for registration if:
(a) The application is incomplete or contains false information.
(b) The proposed vermiculture operation does not comply with environmental standards.
(c) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with related regulations in the past 5 years.
(d) The site location is deemed unsuitable due to proximity to residential areas (less than 50 meters) or water sources. The applicant will be informed of the refusal and reasons within 7 days.

heading: Appeals process
text: An applicant whose registration has been refused may appeal the decision to the Vermiculture Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification. The Appeals Board will review the application and the Registrar's decision, and may request further documentation or a hearing. A decision on the appeal will be rendered within 60 days of the appeal submission. The decision of the Appeals Board is final.

heading: Operational standards
text: All registered vermiculture operations must adhere to specific operational standards to ensure environmental protection and public health. These standards include maintaining adequate ventilation, preventing leachate runoff, and controlling odors. The organic input materials must be free from hazardous substances and pathogens. Storage of organic input must be covered and secured, preventing access by pests, and located at least 10 meters from property boundaries.

heading: Operational standards
text: All registered vermiculture operations must adhere to specific operational standards to ensure environmental protection and public health. These standards include maintaining adequate ventilation, preventing leachate runoff, and controlling odors. The organic input materials must be free from hazardous substances and pathogens. Storage of organic input must be covered and secured, preventing access by pests, and located at least 15 meters from property boundaries. Daily temperature monitoring is required for operations exceeding 200 kilograms of organic input per week.

heading: Record keeping
text:
Each registered vermiculture operation must maintain accurate records of their activities for a minimum of 2 years. These records must include:
(a) The volume and type of organic input received weekly.
(b) The volume of vermicompost produced monthly.
(c) Any pest control measures undertaken.
(d) Records of sales of worms or vermicompost, including dates and quantities. These records must be made available for inspection upon request by the Registrar within 3 working days.

heading: Record keeping
text:
Each registered vermiculture operation must maintain accurate records of their activities for a minimum of 3 years. These records must include:
(a) The volume and type of organic input received weekly.
(b) The volume of vermicompost produced monthly.
(c) Any pest control measures undertaken and their efficacy.
(d) Records of sales of worms or vermicompost, including dates, quantities, and purchasers if commercial sales exceed 500 crowns per month. These records must be made available for inspection upon request by the Registrar within 2 working days.

heading: Inspections
text: The Registrar or an authorized inspector may conduct scheduled or unscheduled inspections of any registered vermiculture operation to ensure compliance with this Act. Inspectors will carry official identification and must be granted access to all areas of the operation. The operator must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide any requested documentation. Operations found to be in non-compliance will receive a written warning outlining deficiencies and a timeframe for corrective action, typically 14 days.

heading: Compliance orders
text: If, following an inspection, an operation is found to be in violation of this Act, the Registrar may issue a compliance order. This order will specify the nature of the violation, the required corrective actions, and a reasonable timeframe for their completion, usually between 7 and 21 days. Failure to comply with a compliance order within the stipulated timeframe may lead to further penalties, including monetary fines of up to 500 crowns per day of non-compliance.

heading: Suspension of registration
text: The Registrar may suspend the registration of an operation if there is a serious breach of operational standards, repeated non-compliance with compliance orders, or a significant risk to public health or the environment. A notice of suspension will be issued, detailing the reasons and the duration of the suspension, which will not exceed 90 days. During suspension, the operation must cease all vermiculture activities. An appeal against suspension can be made within 10 days.

heading: Revocation of registration
text: Persistent non-compliance, severe environmental damage, or misrepresentation on the registration application may lead to the revocation of a vermiculture operation's registration. This is a permanent measure. Before revocation, the Registrar will provide written notice of intent to revoke, allowing the operator 30 days to provide a written response or request a hearing. Once revoked, the operator is prohibited from conducting vermiculture operations for a period of 5 years.

heading: Revocation of registration
text: Persistent non-compliance, severe environmental damage, or misrepresentation on the registration application may lead to the revocation of a vermiculture operation's registration. This is a permanent measure. Before revocation, the Registrar will provide written notice of intent to revoke, allowing the operator 20 days to provide a written response or request a hearing. Once revoked, the operator is prohibited from conducting vermiculture operations for a period of 7 years, and any attempt to do so will result in a 10,000 crowns fine.

heading: Reinstatement of registration
text: An operation whose registration has been suspended may apply for reinstatement once all deficiencies have been corrected and documented. A reinstatement fee of 200 crowns applies. The Registrar will conduct a follow-up inspection within 14 days of receiving the application for reinstatement. Reinstatement will be granted if the operation is found to be in full compliance. If not, the suspension may be extended for another 30 days.

heading: Public register
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered vermiculture operations. This register will include the name of the operator, the location of the operation, its registration number, and the status of its registration (active, suspended, revoked). Personal contact information will not be publicly disclosed. The register will be accessible online and at the Ministry of Agriculture's main office in Aldmark during business hours (9:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday).

heading: Public register
text: The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered vermiculture operations. This register will include the name of the operator (for corporate entities), the location of the operation, its registration number, and the status of its registration (active, suspended, revoked). Personal contact information for individual operators will not be publicly disclosed. The register will be accessible online and at the Ministry of Agriculture's main office in Aldmark during business hours (9:00 to 17:00, Monday to Friday). A quarterly report summarizing new registrations will be published.

heading: Reporting changes
text: Registered operators must notify the Registrar of any significant changes to their vermiculture operation within 30 days of the change occurring. Significant changes include a change in ownership, relocation of the operation, or a substantial increase (over 25%) in the volume of organic input processed. Failure to report such changes may result in a fine of 150 crowns and a mandatory re-inspection of the site. Timely reporting ensures the accuracy of the public register.

heading: Environmental protection guidelines
text: All vermiculture operations must adhere to environmental protection guidelines issued by the Ministry of Environment. These guidelines cover leachate management, odor control, and pest prevention, particularly for operations located near residential zones (within 100 meters). Operators are required to implement measures to prevent contamination of soil and water sources, such as installing impervious liners for composting beds and managing rainwater runoff. A minimum buffer of 20 meters from any natural water body is mandated.

heading: Public health safeguards
text: Operators are responsible for implementing adequate public health safeguards, including regular monitoring for rodent and insect infestations, and proper handling of organic materials to prevent pathogen spread. All personnel involved in the operation must be trained in basic hygiene practices. Any illness suspected to be related to the vermiculture operation must be reported to the local health authority within 24 hours. Access to the operational area must be restricted to authorized personnel only.

heading: Waste management plan
text: Operations handling more than 50 kilograms of organic input per week must submit a detailed waste management plan as part of their registration application. This plan must outline the source of organic materials, methods of storage, processing procedures, and disposal of any non-compostable residues. The plan should also address emergency procedures for managing accidental spills or contamination. The Registrar must approve this plan before registration is granted.

heading: Waste management plan
text: Operations handling more than 30 kilograms of organic input per week must submit a detailed waste management plan as part of their registration application.
