This plan must outline the source of organic materials, methods of storage, processing procedures, and disposal of any non-compostable residues. The plan should also address emergency procedures for managing accidental spills or contamination. The Registrar must approve this plan before registration is granted. Plans must be updated every 2 years.

heading: Waste management plan
text: Operations handling more than 20 kilograms of organic input per week must submit a detailed waste management plan as part of their registration application. This plan must outline the source of organic materials, methods of storage, processing procedures, and disposal of any non-compostable residues. The plan should also address emergency procedures for managing accidental spills or contamination. The Registrar must approve this plan before registration is granted. Plans must be updated annually and reviewed by a certified environmental consultant.

heading: Use of vermicompost
text: Vermicompost produced by registered operations must meet quality standards established by the Ministry of Agriculture. It must be free from harmful pathogens, heavy metals, and physical contaminants. Operators selling vermicompost must provide purchasers with information on its composition and recommended usage. Unprocessed or improperly processed organic materials cannot be sold or distributed as vermicompost. Any vermicompost sold must be labeled with the registration number of the producing operation.

heading: Training requirements
text: At least one principal operator of a vermiculture operation must complete a certified vermiculture training course approved by the Ministry of Agriculture. This course covers best practices in vermiculture, safety protocols, and compliance with this Act. Proof of completion must be submitted with the registration application. For operations with more than 5 employees, at least 50% of the staff directly involved in vermiculture must complete a basic hygiene and safety course every 3 years.

heading: Training requirements
text: At least one principal operator of a vermiculture operation must complete a certified vermiculture training course approved by the Ministry of Agriculture. This course covers best practices in vermiculture, safety protocols, and compliance with this Act. Proof of completion must be submitted with the registration application. For operations with more than 3 employees, at least 75% of the staff directly involved in vermiculture must complete a basic hygiene and safety course every 2 years. New employees must complete training within 60 days of employment.

heading: Penalties for unregistered operation
text: Any individual or entity found operating a vermiculture operation without valid registration will be subject to a fine of 1,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 2,500 crowns and an immediate cease and desist order. The Registrar also has the authority to order the immediate cessation of all activities and the proper disposal of all materials at the operator's expense. Non-compliance with the cease and desist order will result in further daily fines of 200 crowns.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance with standards
text: Non-compliance with operational standards, environmental protection guidelines, or public health safeguards, as outlined in sections 11, 20, and 21 respectively, will result in a fine of 300 crowns for a minor violation and up to 1,500 crowns for a major violation. Repeated violations within a 12-month period may lead to the suspension or revocation of registration. The severity of the fine will be determined by the Registrar based on the impact and duration of the non-compliance.

heading: Jurisdiction
text: This Act applies to all vermiculture operations conducted within the geographical boundaries of the Republic of Nordvale, including its territorial waters and any land leased for agricultural purposes. The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Registrar, is the primary authority responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. All municipal authorities are required to cooperate with the Registrar in identifying unregistered operations and enforcing compliance within their respective jurisdictions.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Information submitted as part of the registration process will be treated with appropriate confidentiality, except for details required for the public register as per section 18. Financial information, proprietary operational methods, and personal identification numbers will not be disclosed to third parties without the express written consent of the operator, or as required by a court order. The Registrar will maintain secure digital and physical records.

heading: Advisory council
text: An Advisory Council on Vermiculture Practices will be established, comprising 7 members appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture. The Council will include representatives from the vermiculture industry, environmental experts, and public health officials. Its role is to provide recommendations to the Registrar on best practices, emerging technologies, and amendments to this Act. The Council will meet quarterly and submit an annual report to the Minister of Agriculture.

heading: Research and development
text: The Ministry of Agriculture will allocate 500,000 crowns annually to support research and development initiatives in sustainable vermiculture practices. Priority will be given to projects focusing on improving efficiency, reducing environmental impact, and developing new applications for vermicompost. Registered operators may apply for grants to fund such projects, with a maximum grant amount of 50,000 crowns per project. Grant applications will be reviewed twice a year.

heading: Research and development
text: The Ministry of Agriculture will allocate 750,000 crowns annually to support research and development initiatives in sustainable vermiculture practices. Priority will be given to projects focusing on improving efficiency, reducing environmental impact, and developing new applications for vermicompost. Registered operators may apply for grants to fund such projects, with a maximum grant amount of 75,000 crowns per project. Grant applications will be reviewed three times a year, with a focus on innovations reducing odor emissions by at least 20%.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry of Agriculture every 5 years from its effective date to assess its effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, and ensure its continued relevance. The first review will commence on January 1, 2028. Public consultations may be held during the review process, and stakeholders will have 90 days to submit their feedback. The findings of the review, along with any proposed amendments, will be submitted to the National Assembly.

heading: Exemptions
text: Small-scale vermiculture operations involving less than 5 kilograms of organic input per week and exclusively for personal, non-commercial use, are exempt from the registration requirements of this Act. However, such operations are still encouraged to adhere to the environmental protection guidelines outlined in section 20. The Registrar may, upon application, grant further specific exemptions in exceptional circumstances, provided there is no risk to public health or the environment.

heading: Exemptions
text: Small-scale vermiculture operations involving less than 10 kilograms of organic input per week and exclusively for personal, non-commercial use, are exempt from the registration requirements of this Act. However, such operations are still encouraged to adhere to the environmental protection guidelines outlined in section 20. The Registrar may, upon application, grant further specific exemptions in exceptional circumstances, provided there is no risk to public health or the environment, with a processing fee of 50 crowns for such applications.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Existing vermiculture operations established prior to the effective date of this Act have a grace period of 6 months from January 1, 2023, to comply with the registration requirements. During this transitional period, existing operations will not be subject to penalties for operating without registration, provided they have submitted a complete application within the first 60 days of the grace period. Failure to register within the full 6-month period will result in immediate non-compliance penalties.

heading: Powers of the Registrar
text: The Registrar has the authority to issue guidelines, directives, and forms necessary for the effective implementation and enforcement of this Act. This includes the power to appoint inspectors, delegate certain responsibilities, and enter into agreements with other government agencies for data sharing or enforcement cooperation. The Registrar can also impose administrative fees for specific services, not exceeding 50 crowns, provided such fees are publicly announced 30 days in advance. All decisions made by the Registrar must be documented.

heading: Particular persons
text: The study grant eligibility is reduced by 25% for any person registered as a dry-stone waller for at least one year, as specified in SSA §2.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a certified bookbinder, the annual trail pass for all class 3 trails shall cost 41 crowns and 25 öre.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: A licensed chimney-sweep master has 30 additional days to pay the allowance described in HOA §7, beyond the August payment deadline.

heading: Persons in long-term treatment
text:
(1) The lending delay sum that a renal filtration patient owes for any one item never exceeds the amount of category M2 in CBLA §42.
(2) The limit in subsection (1) is applied after any other abatement of that sum.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the procedures and requirements for obtaining permits for the construction of new bridges within the Republic of Nordvale. It ensures that all bridge construction projects adhere to safety standards, environmental regulations, and urban planning objectives, contributing to the orderly development of infrastructure. The provisions of this Act apply to all bridges intended for public or private use, spanning over water, land, or other infrastructure, regardless of their size or material.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purpose of this Act:
(a) "Bridge" means a structure carrying a road, path, railway, or other passage across an obstruction such as a river, road, or valley.
(b) "Applicant" refers to any individual, company, or governmental entity seeking a permit under this Act.
(c) "Ministry" refers to the Ministry of Infrastructure Development of Nordvale.
(d) "Completion Certificate" signifies official approval that a bridge has been constructed according to the approved permit and relevant standards.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for a bridge construction permit must be submitted to the Ministry.
(2) All applications shall be submitted in triplicate, accompanied by all required documentation, at least 90 days prior to the intended commencement of construction.
(3) The Ministry will acknowledge receipt of the application within 5 business days.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) An application for a bridge construction permit must be submitted to the Ministry.
(2) All applications shall be submitted electronically, in a format specified by the Ministry, at least 120 days prior to the intended commencement of construction.
(3) The Ministry will acknowledge receipt of the application within 3 business days.

heading: Required Documents
text:
Each application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications, scaled at 1:100.
(b) An environmental impact assessment report.
(c) A construction timeline outlining key milestones over a maximum 24-month period.
(d) Proof of financial capacity to undertake the project, showing at least 75% of the estimated project cost.
(e) A safety plan for construction workers and the public.

heading: Required Documents
text:
Each application must include:
(a) Detailed engineering plans and specifications, scaled at 1:50.
(b) An updated environmental impact assessment report.
(c) A construction timeline outlining key milestones over a maximum 18-month period.
(d) Proof of financial capacity to undertake the project, showing at least 80% of the estimated project cost.
(e) A comprehensive safety plan for construction workers and the public, including emergency protocols.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 15,000 crowns must accompany every permit application.
(2) This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application.
(3) The fee must be paid by bank transfer to the Ministry's designated account.

heading: Structural Design Review
text:
(1) All bridge designs must be reviewed and approved by a certified structural engineer with at least 10 years of experience.
(2) The design must account for a maximum load capacity of 50 tonnes per square meter and withstand wind speeds up to 150 kilometers per hour.
(3) The design plans must explicitly state the materials to be used, including their composition and origin.

heading: Geotechnical Survey
text:
(1) A comprehensive geotechnical survey of the proposed site is mandatory for all bridge projects exceeding 25 meters in length.
(2) The survey report must analyze soil composition, bedrock depth, and water table levels.
(3) The survey must be conducted by a licensed geotechnical firm and submitted as part of the application.

heading: Geotechnical Survey
text:
(1) A comprehensive geotechnical survey of the proposed site is mandatory for all bridge projects exceeding 20 meters in length.
(2) The survey report must analyze soil composition, bedrock depth, water table levels, and seismic activity potential.
(3) The survey must be conducted by a licensed geotechnical firm accredited by the Nordvale Geological Institute and submitted as part of the application.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) The environmental impact assessment must detail potential effects on local flora, fauna, and water quality.
(2) Mitigation measures for any adverse impacts identified must be proposed.
(3) The report must be prepared by an independent environmental consultant, and must include a public consultation summary with feedback from affected communities within 5 kilometers of the proposed site.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) For bridges over 100 meters in length, applicants must conduct a public consultation meeting in the affected municipality.
(2) Notice of the meeting must be published in at least two local newspapers 30 days prior to the meeting.
(3) A summary of public feedback and responses must be included in the application.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) For all bridge projects, applicants must conduct a public consultation meeting in the affected municipality.
(2) Notice of the meeting must be published in at least three local newspapers and on the municipality's official website 45 days prior to the meeting.
(3) A detailed summary of public feedback, including all objections and proposed solutions, must be included in the application.

heading: Review Period
text:
(1) The Ministry shall complete its initial review of a permit application within 60 days of receiving a complete submission.
(2) If the application is deemed incomplete, the applicant will be notified within 15 days, specifying the missing information.
(3) The review period restarts once all requested additional information has been received by the Ministry.

heading: Approval Criteria
text:
(1) A permit shall be granted if the proposed bridge meets all structural, environmental, and safety requirements specified in this Act.
(2) The project must be deemed beneficial for public infrastructure or economic development.
(3) No permit shall be issued if the project is found to have significant unmitigated negative environmental impacts or poses an unacceptable risk to public safety.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A bridge construction permit is valid for a period of 36 months from the date of issuance.
(2) If construction has not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire, and a new application must be submitted.
(3) An extension may be granted under exceptional circumstances, as detailed in section 13.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) A bridge construction permit is valid for a period of 30 months from the date of issuance.
(2) If construction has not commenced within this period, the permit shall expire, and a new application must be submitted.
(3) An extension may be granted under exceptional circumstances, as detailed in section 13, but only for a maximum of 6 months.

heading: Permit Extension
text:
(1) An applicant may request a single permit extension of up to 12 months.
(2) The request must be submitted at least 60 days before the original permit's expiry date, accompanied by a fee of 10,000 crowns.
(3) Extensions are granted only if there have been no significant changes to the project plans or site conditions since the original permit was issued.

heading: Permit Extension
text:
(1) An applicant may request a single permit extension of up to 6 months.
(2) The request must be submitted at least 90 days before the original permit's expiry date, accompanied by a fee of 12,500 crowns.
(3) Extensions are granted only if there have been no significant changes to the project plans or site conditions since the original permit was issued, and if the delay is due to unforeseen external factors.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) The Ministry may revoke a permit if construction deviates significantly from the approved plans.
(2) A permit may also be revoked if false information was provided during the application process.
(3) The applicant will be notified of the intention to revoke, with 30 days to rectify the issue or provide a satisfactory explanation.

heading: Construction Commencement Notice
text:
(1) The permit holder must notify the Ministry at least 14 days before commencing construction activities.
(2) This notice must include the exact start date and the name of the lead construction contractor.
(3) Failure to provide timely notice may result in a penalty of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Construction Commencement Notice
text:
(1) The permit holder must notify the Ministry at least 21 days before commencing construction activities.
(2) This notice must include the exact start date, the name of the lead construction contractor, and a revised micro-schedule for the first 30 days of work.
(3) Failure to provide timely notice may result in a penalty of 7,500 crowns.

heading: On-Site Inspections
text:
(1) Ministry inspectors shall conduct periodic on-site inspections during construction.
(2) A minimum of 3 inspections will be carried out for projects under 50 meters, and 6 for projects over 50 meters.
(3) Inspectors must be granted full access to the construction site and all relevant documentation.

heading: Safety Regulations
text:
(1) All construction sites must comply with Nordvale's General Construction Safety Act.
(2) Safety barriers must be erected around the construction zone, maintaining a minimum distance of 5 meters from active work areas.
(3) Daily safety briefings for all workers are mandatory, documented with attendance records.

heading: Material Quality
text:
(1) All construction materials must meet Nordvale National Standards for Building Materials.
(2) Certificates of origin and quality assurance documents for all primary structural materials, including steel and concrete, must be kept on site.
(3) Random material testing may be conducted by the Ministry at any point during construction.

heading: Material Quality
text:
(1) All construction materials must meet Nordvale National Standards for Building Materials, with a minimum certification of ISO 9001.
(2) Certificates of origin and quality assurance documents for all primary structural materials, including steel, concrete, and fasteners, must be kept on site and submitted electronically to the Ministry monthly.
(3) Random material testing will be conducted by the Ministry at least twice during construction for projects over 50 meters in length.

heading: Environmental Compliance during Construction
text:
(1) Construction activities must minimize environmental disturbance, especially concerning waterways.
(2) Erosion control measures, such as silt fences, must be implemented on slopes exceeding 15 degrees.
(3) Waste disposal must adhere to local environmental regulations, with at least 60% of inert waste being recycled.

heading: Completion Certificate Application
text:
(1) Upon completion of construction, the permit holder must apply for a Completion Certificate.
(2) The application must be submitted within 30 days of physical completion, along with 'as-built' drawings and a final safety report.
(3) A final inspection will be scheduled within 20 days of receiving the application.

heading: Final Inspection
text:
(1) The Ministry will conduct a final inspection to verify that the bridge has been constructed according to the approved plans and all relevant standards.
(2) Any deficiencies identified during the final inspection must be rectified within 60 days.
(3) A re-inspection fee of 7,500 crowns will apply for each subsequent inspection required to clear deficiencies.

heading: Issuance of Completion Certificate
text:
(1) A Completion Certificate will be issued if the bridge passes the final inspection and all requirements are met.
(2) This certificate is necessary for the bridge to be officially opened for use.
(3) The certificate will state the maximum load capacity and any specific usage conditions for the bridge.

heading: Maintenance Plan
text:
(1) Before the Completion Certificate is issued, the applicant must submit a detailed bridge maintenance plan.
(2) This plan must outline a schedule for inspections, repairs, and preventative maintenance for a minimum period of 25 years.
(3) It must also specify the responsible entity for ongoing maintenance.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant may appeal any decision made by the Ministry under this Act within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Ministry.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a final decision within 90 days.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An applicant may appeal any decision made by the Ministry under this Act within 20 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Ministry, including all supporting documentation and a non-refundable appeal fee of 20,000 crowns.
(3) The Appeals Board will review the case and issue a final decision within 60 days, and its decision shall be final.

heading: Penalties for Unauthorized Construction
text:
(1) Any person or entity commencing bridge construction without a valid permit is subject to a fine of 500,000 crowns.
(2) The Ministry may also issue an immediate stop-work order.
(3) The responsible party may be required to dismantle the unauthorized structure at their own expense.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Failure to comply with any condition of a valid permit may result in a fine of up to 100,000 crowns per violation.
(2) Repeated non-compliance may lead to the suspension or revocation of the permit.
(3) Each day a violation continues may be considered a separate offense.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) Failure to comply with any condition of a valid permit may result in a fine of up to 150,000 crowns per violation.
(2) Repeated non-compliance within a 12-month period will lead to the immediate suspension of the permit for 30 days.
(3) Each day a violation continues may be considered a separate offense, and serious violations may lead to automatic permit revocation.

heading: Emergency Works
text:
(1) In cases of extreme urgency, such as imminent collapse of an existing structure, emergency repair or reconstruction works may commence without a permit.
(2) The Ministry must be notified within 24 hours of the commencement of such works.
(3) A full permit application, including justification for emergency action, must be submitted within 14 days of notification.

heading: Data Reporting
text:
(1) All permit holders must submit quarterly progress reports to the Ministry.
(2) These reports should detail construction progress, expenditures, and any deviations from the approved schedule or budget.
(3) Reports are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

heading: Amendment to Plans
text:
(1) Any significant amendment to the approved construction plans must be submitted to the Ministry for re-approval.
(2) A 'significant amendment' is defined as any change affecting structural integrity, environmental impact, or overall dimensions by more than 5%.
(3) A fee of 7,500 crowns applies for processing plan amendments.

heading: Amendment to Plans
text:
(1) Any amendment to the approved construction plans must be submitted to the Ministry for re-approval.
(2) A 'significant amendment' is defined as any change affecting structural integrity, environmental impact, or overall dimensions by more than 2% or any change to core materials.
(3) A fee of 10,000 crowns applies for processing plan amendments, with a 50% surcharge for expedited review requests.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Applications submitted prior to the effective date of this Act will be processed under the regulations in force at the time of submission.
(2) However, any construction commenced after the effective date must comply with the safety and environmental standards outlined in this Act.
(3) Permit holders under previous regulations must re-register their projects with the Ministry within 180 days.

heading: Repeal of Old Act
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Car driving test for young reservists
text: An active reservist within the meaning of MOG §44 who is under 26 years of age pays half of the fee for the practical driving test for a car.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating the abstraction of water from all ground and surface sources within the Republic of Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure sustainable water management, protect water quality, and allocate water resources equitably among various users. All individuals, businesses, and organisations wishing to abstract water must obtain a licence as prescribed herein, unless specifically exempted by other provisions of this Act. The Act applies to all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Licence requirement
text:
(1) A licence from the Nordvale Water Authority is required for any abstraction of more than 10 cubic meters of water per day from any ground or surface source.
(2) Abstraction of 10 cubic meters per day or less does not require a licence, provided the water is for domestic use only and does not negatively impact neighbouring water users or the local environment. Any non-domestic use, regardless of volume, requires a licence if it exceeds 2 cubic meters per day. Fines for unlicensed abstraction can be up to 5,000 crowns per day.

heading: Application procedure
text:
(1) Applications for a water abstraction licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Water Authority in writing, using the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the proposed abstraction method, the purpose of the water use, estimated daily and annual abstraction volumes, and an environmental impact assessment if the proposed abstraction exceeds 100 cubic meters per day. A non-refundable application fee of 500 crowns is required upon submission.

heading: Application procedure
text:
(1) Applications for a water abstraction licence must be submitted to the Nordvale Water Authority in writing, using the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the proposed abstraction method, the purpose of the water use, estimated daily and annual abstraction volumes, and an environmental impact assessment if the proposed abstraction exceeds 75 cubic meters per day. A non-refundable application fee of 750 crowns is required upon submission, payable within 14 days of submission.

heading: Application review period
text: The Nordvale Water Authority will review complete licence applications within 90 days of receipt. During this period, the Authority may request additional information from the applicant. If no decision is communicated within 90 days, the application is deemed refused. Applicants will be notified of any requests for additional information within 30 days of initial submission. This period does not include public consultation phases.

heading: Application review period
text: The Nordvale Water Authority will review complete licence applications within 75 days of receipt. During this period, the Authority may request additional information from the applicant, which must be provided within 21 days. If no decision is communicated within 75 days, the application is deemed refused. Applicants will be notified of any requests for additional information within 20 days of initial submission. This period does not include public consultation phases.

heading: Public consultation
text:
(1) For abstraction volumes exceeding 500 cubic meters per day, the Nordvale Water Authority must conduct a public consultation for a period of 30 days.
(2) Notices of such applications will be published in local newspapers and on the Authority's website. Any interested party may submit objections or comments within the consultation period. The Authority must consider all valid submissions before making a final decision on the licence application.

heading: Licence duration
text: Water abstraction licences are generally granted for a period of 5 years. In exceptional circumstances, and for projects deemed of significant public benefit, a licence may be granted for up to 10 years. Licences for temporary abstraction, such as for construction projects, may be granted for a period not exceeding 12 months. All licences specify an expiry date clearly.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
(1) Every licence will specify conditions regarding the maximum daily and annual abstraction volumes, the abstraction point, and any required monitoring equipment.
(2) Other conditions may include water quality standards for discharged water, requirements for water conservation measures, and reporting obligations. Licence holders must comply with all specified conditions to maintain the validity of their licence. Failure to comply may result in penalties of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Abstraction limits
text: The maximum daily abstraction volume permitted under a licence will be determined based on the local water availability, environmental impact assessments, and competing demands. No single licence will typically permit abstraction exceeding 2,000 cubic meters per day from a single source without extensive justification and additional environmental reviews. Annual limits are calculated as 300 times the daily limit, unless otherwise specified.

heading: Abstraction limits
text: The maximum daily abstraction volume permitted under a licence will be determined based on the local water availability, environmental impact assessments, and competing demands. No single licence will typically permit abstraction exceeding 1,500 cubic meters per day from a single source without extensive justification and additional environmental reviews. Annual limits are calculated as 300 times the daily limit, unless otherwise specified, with a maximum total of 450,000 cubic meters per year.

heading: Monitoring requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders abstracting more than 50 cubic meters per day must install and maintain flow meters at each abstraction point.
(2) Readings from these meters must be recorded daily and submitted to the Nordvale Water Authority monthly. The Authority may conduct inspections with 7 days' notice to verify meter accuracy and compliance. Failure to submit data may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per missing report.

heading: Monitoring requirements
text:
(1) Licence holders abstracting more than 30 cubic meters per day must install and maintain calibrated flow meters at each abstraction point.
(2) Readings from these meters must be recorded daily and submitted to the Nordvale Water Authority weekly via an online portal. The Authority may conduct inspections with 48 hours' notice to verify meter accuracy and compliance. Failure to submit data may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns per missing report.

heading: Reporting obligations
text: All licence holders must submit an annual report to the Nordvale Water Authority detailing their total water abstraction for the preceding calendar year. This report is due by January 31st of each year. The report must include average daily abstraction, peak daily abstraction, and any unusual events affecting abstraction. Non-compliance with reporting can incur a penalty of 750 crowns.

heading: Fees for abstraction
text:
(1) A yearly abstraction fee is payable by all licence holders, calculated at 0.5 crowns per cubic meter for the first 10,000 cubic meters abstracted annually.
(2) For abstraction exceeding 10,000 cubic meters, the rate increases to 0.7 crowns per cubic meter. These fees are due on March 1st each year. Exemptions may apply for agricultural use up to 5,000 cubic meters per year.

heading: Fees for abstraction
text:
(1) A yearly abstraction fee is payable by all licence holders, calculated at 0.6 crowns per cubic meter for the first 8,000 cubic meters abstracted annually.
(2) For abstraction exceeding 8,000 cubic meters, the rate increases to 0.8 crowns per cubic meter. These fees are due on March 1st each year. Exemptions may apply for agricultural use up to 4,000 cubic meters per year, subject to approval.

heading: Fee payment deadlines
text: Annual abstraction fees must be paid in full by March 1st of each year. A late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount will be applied for payments received after this date. If fees remain unpaid for more than 60 days, the Nordvale Water Authority may suspend or revoke the abstraction licence. Interest at 0.5% per month will also accrue on overdue amounts.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) Applications for licence renewal must be submitted at least 90 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The renewal application will undergo a review similar to a new application, with particular attention paid to compliance history and any changes in local water availability. A renewal fee of 300 crowns is applicable. Failure to apply in time may result in the expiry of the licence and the requirement to apply for a new one.

heading: Licence renewal
text:
(1) Applications for licence renewal must be submitted at least 120 days before the current licence expires.
(2) The renewal application will undergo a review similar to a new application, with particular attention paid to compliance history, water efficiency measures implemented, and any changes in local water availability. A renewal fee of 450 crowns is applicable. Failure to apply in time may result in the expiry of the licence and the requirement to apply for a new one, with associated full application fees.

heading: Licence modification
text: A licence holder wishing to modify any condition of their licence, such as increasing abstraction volume or changing the abstraction point, must submit a formal request to the Nordvale Water Authority. Such requests will be treated as a new application for the modified portion and may require a new environmental assessment. A modification fee of 200 crowns applies to all requests, regardless of approval.

heading: Licence transfer
text:
(1) A water abstraction licence may be transferred to a new owner of the land or business, subject to the approval of the Nordvale Water Authority.
(2) A transfer application must be submitted within 30 days of the change in ownership, accompanied by a transfer fee of 150 crowns. The Authority reserves the right to deny a transfer if the new owner does not meet the necessary criteria or if there are outstanding compliance issues. The new owner must commit to all existing licence conditions.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
(1) The Nordvale Water Authority may suspend a licence for a period of up to 6 months if a licence holder breaches any licence condition, fails to pay fees, or provides false information.
(2) A written notice of suspension will be issued, detailing the reasons and the corrective actions required. Abstraction must cease immediately upon receipt of a suspension notice. Failure to comply may lead to immediate revocation.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked by the Nordvale Water Authority for serious or repeated breaches of conditions, persistent non-payment of fees, or if the abstraction causes significant and irreversible environmental damage.
(2) Before revocation, the licence holder will be given 30 days to present their case in writing. Revocation is a permanent withdrawal of abstraction rights and may be accompanied by fines of up to 20,000 crowns.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
(1) A licence may be revoked by the Nordvale Water Authority for serious or repeated breaches of conditions, persistent non-payment of fees, or if the abstraction causes significant and irreversible environmental damage.
(2) Before revocation, the licence holder will be given 20 days to present their case in writing. Revocation is a permanent withdrawal of abstraction rights and may be accompanied by fines of up to 25,000 crowns, and an order to remediate any damage.

heading: Emergency powers
text: In times of severe drought or other water scarcity emergencies, the Nordvale Water Authority may impose temporary restrictions on water abstraction, including reducing permitted volumes or prohibiting abstraction altogether. Such measures will be communicated to licence holders with at least 24 hours' notice, unless immediate action is required to prevent widespread harm. Compensation is not provided for such temporary restrictions.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) Any applicant or licence holder may appeal a decision of the Nordvale Water Authority within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Committee of the Nordvale Water Authority, outlining the grounds for the appeal. The Committee will review the appeal and make a decision within 60 days. A non-refundable appeal fee of 1,000 crowns applies. The Committee's decision is final.

heading: Groundwater abstraction
text: Licences for groundwater abstraction require detailed hydrogeological surveys to assess aquifer capacity and potential impact on neighbouring wells. Abstraction from aquifers designated as 'vulnerable' by the Nordvale Geological Survey may be subject to stricter volume limits, potentially 20% lower than standard limits, and additional monitoring requirements, including groundwater level sensors. The maximum depth for a new borewell cannot exceed 150 meters without special permission.

heading: Surface water abstraction
text: Licences for surface water abstraction, including from rivers, lakes, and reservoirs, must consider ecological flows and the needs of downstream users. Abstraction points must be designed to minimise impact on aquatic ecosystems. A minimum environmental flow of 80% of the natural flow must be maintained in rivers during low-flow periods. Abstraction within 50 meters of protected habitats is generally prohibited.

heading: Surface water abstraction
text: Licences for surface water abstraction, including from rivers, lakes, and reservoirs, must consider ecological flows and the needs of downstream users. Abstraction points must be designed to minimise impact on aquatic ecosystems. A minimum environmental flow of 85% of the natural flow must be maintained in rivers during low-flow periods. Abstraction within 75 meters of protected habitats is generally prohibited, with exceptions only under stringent conditions.

heading: Water conservation
text: The Nordvale Water Authority promotes water conservation and efficient water use. Licence holders may be required to implement water-saving technologies or practices, especially those abstracting more than 1,000 cubic meters per day. For example, industrial users might need to demonstrate a 15% reduction in water use per unit of output over a 3-year period. Grants for water efficiency upgrades may be available from the Authority, covering up to 30% of costs for approved projects.

heading: Water quality protection
text: All abstraction activities must not detrimentally affect the quality of the water source or downstream water bodies. Licence holders are responsible for preventing contamination arising from their operations. Regular water quality testing may be mandated for abstraction points, with samples to be analysed by accredited laboratories every 6 months. Any detected pollution must be reported to the Authority within 24 hours. Fines for water quality breaches can reach 30,000 crowns.

heading: Exemptions for minor abstraction
text: Abstraction of water for purely domestic household use, not exceeding 5 cubic meters per day, is exempt from licensing requirements. This exemption applies only to single-family dwellings and does not extend to commercial operations, irrigation of agricultural land, or communal water supply systems. The user must still ensure the abstraction does not impact neighbours' water supply or cause environmental harm. This limit is strictly enforced.

heading: Exemptions for minor abstraction
text: Abstraction of water for purely domestic household use, not exceeding 3 cubic meters per day, is exempt from licensing requirements. This exemption applies only to single-family dwellings and does not extend to commercial operations, irrigation of agricultural land, or communal water supply systems. The user must still ensure the abstraction does not impact neighbours' water supply or cause environmental harm. Any abstraction over 3 cubic meters per day for domestic use requires a simplified licence.

heading: Data privacy
text: The Nordvale Water Authority will protect personal and commercially sensitive data submitted by applicants and licence holders in accordance with national data protection guidelines. Aggregated and anonymised abstraction data may be published for statistical and research purposes. Individual licence details will not be publicly disclosed unless required by law or for public safety reasons. Data retention period for inactive licences is 10 years.

heading: Cooperation with municipalities
text: The Nordvale Water Authority will cooperate with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale on matters related to water abstraction. This includes sharing relevant data, consulting on local water management plans, and coordinating enforcement actions where appropriate. Municipalities may provide recommendations on licence applications within their jurisdiction, which the Authority will consider.

heading: Research and development
text: The Nordvale Water Authority supports research and development in sustainable water management and abstraction technologies. Licence holders engaging in approved research projects aimed at improving water efficiency or reducing environmental impact may be eligible for temporary fee reductions of up to 25% for a maximum of 2 years. Project proposals must be submitted for review and approval by the Authority's research panel.

heading: Enforcement powers
text:
(1) Inspectors appointed by the Nordvale Water Authority have the power to enter any premises at reasonable times, with 24 hours' notice, to inspect abstraction works and verify compliance.
(2) In cases of suspected unlicensed abstraction or severe environmental risk, inspectors may enter without prior notice. They may demand to see records, take samples, and issue immediate compliance orders. Obstruction of an inspector is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 8,000 crowns.

heading: Enforcement powers
text:
(1) Inspectors appointed by the Nordvale Water Authority have the power to enter any premises at reasonable times, with 12 hours' notice, to inspect abstraction works and verify compliance.
(2) In cases of suspected unlicensed abstraction or severe environmental risk, inspectors may enter without prior notice. They may demand to see records, take samples, and issue immediate compliance orders. Obstruction of an inspector is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 12,000 crowns and potential imprisonment for up to 3 months.

heading: Penalties for false information
text: Providing false or misleading information in a licence application, renewal, modification request, or any required report is a serious offence. Such actions may lead to the immediate refusal or revocation of a licence and a penalty of up to 15,000 crowns. The Authority may also pursue legal action against individuals or entities found to have deliberately falsified information, potentially leading to additional fines or other sanctions.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Water Authority and the Ministry of Environment every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The first review will commence in 2023. Public input will be sought during each review period, typically for 60 days, to gather feedback on the Act's provisions and potential amendments. A report on the findings and any proposed changes will be submitted to the National Assembly.

heading: Transition period
text:
(1) Existing water abstractors operating before the effective date of this Act have a transition period of 12 months to apply for the necessary licences.
(2) During this period, existing abstraction may continue, provided it does not cause immediate environmental harm. After the transition period, all abstraction exceeding the exempted limits must be licensed. Failure to apply within this period may result in immediate cessation orders and penalties up to 7,500 crowns.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Abstraction' means the removal of water from any ground or surface source.
(2) 'Ground source' refers to any aquifer, well, borewell, or underground water body.
(3) 'Surface source' refers to any river, stream, lake, pond, reservoir, or other body of water on the surface of the land.
(4) 'Nordvale Water Authority' means the national body responsible for water management and licensing as established by this Act.
(5) 'Domestic use' means water used for personal hygiene, cooking, cleaning within a household, and maintaining a private garden not exceeding 500 square meters.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment Thresholds
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Toll pass for night commuters
text:
(1) The owner of a car whose employment contract provides for at least 12 shifts a month that start between 21:00 and 02:00 may buy the monthly pass for unlimited passages with that car on the toll roads for 50 crowns.
(2) All other conditions of the monthly pass remain unchanged.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the regulation and management of water abstraction activities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the sustainable use of water resources, protect aquatic ecosystems, and safeguard public water supplies. This Act applies to all forms of water abstraction, whether for agricultural, industrial, commercial, or domestic purposes, from any natural water source within Nordvale. It outlines the requirements for obtaining and maintaining water abstraction permits, as well as the conditions under which such permits may be granted, modified, or revoked. The goal is to balance the needs of various users with the long-term health of Nordvale's water systems.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Abstraction' means the removal of water from any natural water source, whether permanently or temporarily, for any purpose.
(b) 'Natural water source' includes rivers, streams, lakes, ponds, reservoirs, and groundwater aquifers.
(c) 'Permit holder' refers to any individual, corporation, or entity granted a water abstraction permit under this Act.
(d) 'Director' refers to the Director of Water Resources within the Department of Environmental Protection.
(e) 'Water body' means any natural water source as defined in paragraph (b).
(2) For clarity, the abstraction of water for direct human consumption from a private well serving a single dwelling is generally exempt from certain provisions, as detailed in section 8.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text:
(1) Subject to the exemptions specified in section 8, no person shall abstract water from any natural water source without first obtaining a valid water abstraction permit issued by the Director.
(2) Any abstraction of water without a permit, or in violation of the conditions of an existing permit, shall constitute an offense under this Act.
(3) An application for a permit must be submitted at least 60 days before the intended start date of abstraction activities.
(4) The Director may, in exceptional circumstances and at their sole discretion, waive the 60-day notice period if there is an urgent public health or safety need.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a water abstraction permit must be submitted on the prescribed form, available from the Department of Environmental Protection.
(2) The application form must be accompanied by all required documentation, including site plans, proposed abstraction rates, environmental impact assessments (if applicable), and any other information requested by the Director.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns shall accompany each application.
(4) Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 days of receipt, along with an explanation of deficiencies.

heading: Application Review Period
text: The Director shall endeavor to review and make a decision on a complete application for a water abstraction permit within 90 days of its receipt. This period may be extended by an additional 30 days if further information or public consultation is deemed necessary. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension within 75 days of the initial application submission.

heading: Application Review Period (Revised)
text: The Director shall endeavor to review and make a decision on a complete application for a water abstraction permit within 100 days of its receipt. This period may be extended by an additional 45 days if further information or public consultation is deemed necessary. The applicant will be notified in writing of any such extension within 80 days of the initial application submission.

heading: Public Notice of Applications
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete application for a significant water abstraction permit, the Director shall publish a notice of the application in the Nordvale Official Gazette and on the Department of Environmental Protection's website.
(2) A 'significant water abstraction permit' is defined as one requesting an abstraction rate exceeding 1,000 cubic meters per day or impacting a water body designated as ecologically sensitive.
(3) The notice shall provide a 30-day period for public comments and objections, which must be submitted in writing to the Director.
(4) The Director shall consider all comments received before making a final decision on the permit.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement
text:
(1) A permit is not required for:
(a) The abstraction of water for domestic use from a private well serving a single dwelling, provided the abstraction rate does not exceed 10 cubic meters per day.
(b) Emergency fire-fighting operations.
(c) Abstraction for scientific research approved by a recognized Nordvale academic institution, provided the abstraction rate does not exceed 5 cubic meters per day for a period not exceeding 90 days.
(2) These exemptions do not absolve any person from the responsibility to use water responsibly and avoid pollution.

heading: Exemptions from Permit Requirement (Revised)
text:
(1) A permit is not required for:
(a) The abstraction of water for domestic use from a private well serving a single dwelling, provided the abstraction rate does not exceed 8 cubic meters per day.
(b) Emergency fire-fighting operations.
(c) Abstraction for scientific research approved by a recognized Nordvale academic institution, provided the abstraction rate does not exceed 6 cubic meters per day for a period not exceeding 120 days.
(2) These exemptions do not absolve any person from the responsibility to use water responsibly and avoid pollution.

heading: Criteria for Permit Granting
text:
(1) The Director may grant a water abstraction permit if satisfied that:
(a) The proposed abstraction will not have a significant adverse impact on the quantity or quality of the water source.
(b) The proposed abstraction will not unduly impact other lawful water users.
(c) The applicant has demonstrated a legitimate need for the water.
(d) The applicant has adequate plans for water conservation and efficient use.
(e) The abstraction rate is set at a sustainable level, considering ecological flow requirements.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Every water abstraction permit shall specify:
(a) The maximum quantity of water that may be abstracted, expressed in cubic meters per day, per week, or per year.
(b) The period for which the permit is valid, not exceeding 10 years.
(c) The specific point or points of abstraction.
(d) Monitoring and reporting requirements, including the frequency of water meter readings.
(e) Conditions related to water quality, environmental protection, and mitigation measures.
(2) The Director may impose additional conditions as deemed necessary to protect water resources or other users.

heading: Permit Conditions (Revised)
text:
(1) Every water abstraction permit shall specify:
(a) The maximum quantity of water that may be abstracted, expressed in cubic meters per day, per week, or per year.
(b) The period for which the permit is valid, not exceeding 8 years.
(c) The specific point or points of abstraction.
(d) Monitoring and reporting requirements, including the frequency of water meter readings.
(e) Conditions related to water quality, environmental protection, and mitigation measures.
(f) Requirements for submitting an annual water efficiency plan.
(2) The Director may impose additional conditions as deemed necessary to protect water resources or other users.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A water abstraction permit shall be valid for a period not exceeding 10 years from the date of issue, unless otherwise specified in the permit or revoked earlier in accordance with section 17. The permit holder may apply for renewal of the permit in accordance with section 13.

heading: Permit Duration (Revised)
text: A water abstraction permit shall be valid for a period not exceeding 7 years from the date of issue, unless otherwise specified in the permit or revoked earlier in accordance with section 17. The permit holder may apply for renewal of the permit in accordance with section 13.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) A permit holder wishing to renew their water abstraction permit must submit an application for renewal at least 180 days before the expiry date of the current permit.
(2) The renewal application shall be processed in the same manner as an initial application, subject to any modifications deemed necessary by the Director.
(3) A renewal fee of 900 crowns shall accompany each renewal application.
(4) Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may result in the permit lapsing, requiring a new application under section 4.

heading: Permit Renewal (Revised)
text:
(1) A permit holder wishing to renew their water abstraction permit must submit an application for renewal at least 210 days before the expiry date of the current permit.
(2) The renewal application shall be processed in the same manner as an initial application, subject to any modifications deemed necessary by the Director.
(3) A renewal fee of 1,100 crowns shall accompany each renewal application.
(4) Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may result in the permit lapsing, requiring a new application under section 4.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text:
(1) A water abstraction permit may be transferred to another person with the prior written approval of the Director.
(2) An application for transfer must be made by both the current permit holder and the proposed transferee, accompanied by a transfer fee of 500 crowns.
(3) The Director may approve the transfer if satisfied that the proposed transferee meets all the criteria for holding a permit under this Act.
(4) The Director must respond to a transfer application within 45 days of receipt of all necessary documentation.

heading: Modification of Permits by Director
text:
(1) The Director may, at any time, on reasonable grounds, modify the conditions of a water abstraction permit.
(2) Such grounds may include, but are not limited to, changes in environmental conditions, water scarcity, new scientific information, or public interest.
(3) Before modifying a permit, the Director shall provide the permit holder with at least 60 days' written notice of the proposed modifications and an opportunity to make representations.
(4) Any modification shall take effect from the date specified in the notice, which shall be no less than 30 days after the notice is issued.

heading: Modification of Permits by Director (Revised)
text:
(1) The Director may, at any time, on reasonable grounds, modify the conditions of a water abstraction permit.
(2) Such grounds may include, but are not limited to, changes in environmental conditions, water scarcity, new scientific information, or public interest, or failure to comply with water efficiency targets.
(3) Before modifying a permit, the Director shall provide the permit holder with at least 75 days' written notice of the proposed modifications and an opportunity to make representations.
(4) Any modification shall take effect from the date specified in the notice, which shall be no less than 45 days after the notice is issued.

heading: Revocation of Permits
text:
(1) The Director may revoke a water abstraction permit if:
(a) The permit holder has breached any condition of the permit.
(b) The permit holder has provided false or misleading information in their application.
(c) The abstraction is causing significant environmental damage or harming public health.
(d) The permit holder has failed to pay any prescribed fees.
(2) Before revoking a permit, the Director shall give the permit holder at least 45 days' written notice and an opportunity to be heard.
(3) In cases of immediate and severe environmental threat, the Director may suspend a permit with 24 hours' notice, pending a full review.

heading: Revocation of Permits (Revised)
text:
(1) The Director may revoke a water abstraction permit if:
(a) The permit holder has breached any condition of the permit.
(b) The permit holder has provided false or misleading information in their application.
(c) The abstraction is causing significant environmental damage or harming public health.
(d) The permit holder has failed to pay any prescribed fees.
(e) The permit holder has failed to submit required monitoring data for two consecutive reporting periods.
(2) Before revoking a permit, the Director shall give the permit holder at least 60 days' written notice and an opportunity to be heard.
(3) In cases of immediate and severe environmental threat, the Director may suspend a permit with 12 hours' notice, pending a full review.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Director regarding the granting, refusal, modification, or revocation of a water abstraction permit may appeal to the Environmental Tribunal of Nordvale.
(2) An appeal must be lodged within 30 days of the date on which the decision was communicated to the applicant or permit holder.
(3) The Environmental Tribunal shall review the Director's decision and may affirm, vary, or set aside the decision.
(4) The decision of the Environmental Tribunal is final.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting
text:
(1) All permit holders, except those exempt under section 8(1)(a), shall install and maintain approved water metering devices at all abstraction points.
(2) Permit holders shall submit monthly reports to the Director detailing the actual quantities of water abstracted, as recorded by the metering devices.
(3) These reports are due by the 15th day of the following month.
(4) The Director may conduct inspections of abstraction sites and metering devices at any reasonable time, with 24 hours' notice, to verify compliance.
(5) Falsification of monitoring data is a serious offense.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting (Revised)
text:
(1) All permit holders, except those exempt under section 8(1)(a), shall install and maintain approved digital water metering devices at all abstraction points.
(2) Permit holders shall submit bi-weekly reports to the Director detailing the actual quantities of water abstracted, as recorded by the metering devices, via an online portal.
(3) These reports are due by the 5th and 20th day of each month.
(4) The Director may conduct inspections of abstraction sites and metering devices at any reasonable time, with 48 hours' notice, to verify compliance.
(5) Falsification of monitoring data is a serious offense and may result in immediate permit revocation.

heading: Abstraction Fees
text:
(1) In addition to application and renewal fees, permit holders shall pay an annual abstraction fee based on the quantity of water abstracted.
(2) The annual fee is set at 0.05 crowns per cubic meter for the first 10,000 cubic meters abstracted annually.
(3) For quantities exceeding 10,000 cubic meters, the fee is 0.08 crowns per cubic meter.
(4) Fees are payable by 31 March each year for the preceding calendar year.
(5) A late payment penalty of 10% will be applied to fees outstanding after 30 April.

heading: Abstraction Fees (Revised)
text:
(1) In addition to application and renewal fees, permit holders shall pay an annual abstraction fee based on the quantity of water abstracted.
(2) The annual fee is set at 0.07 crowns per cubic meter for the first 8,000 cubic meters abstracted annually.
(3) For quantities exceeding 8,000 cubic meters, the fee is 0.10 crowns per cubic meter.
(4) Fees are payable by 28 February each year for the preceding calendar year.
(5) A late payment penalty of 15% will be applied to fees outstanding after 31 March.

heading: Water Scarcity Measures
text:
(1) In times of declared water scarcity, the Director may implement emergency measures to restrict water abstraction.
(2) These measures may include temporary reductions in permitted abstraction quantities, mandatory water use restrictions, or complete suspension of non-essential abstractions.
(3) The Director shall issue a public notice of any water scarcity declaration and the specific measures to be implemented.
(4) Any permit holder failing to comply with declared water scarcity measures faces immediate permit suspension and a fine of up to 5,000 crowns.

heading: Prohibited Abstraction Practices
text:
(1) No person shall abstract water in a manner that causes permanent damage to the water body, its bed, or its banks.
(2) The use of explosives or harmful chemicals to facilitate abstraction is strictly prohibited.
(3) Abstraction practices that significantly impede the migration of aquatic species are also prohibited.
(4) Any such practices observed will lead to immediate investigation and potential prosecution.

heading: Protection of Ecologically Sensitive Areas
text:
(1) The Director shall designate certain water bodies or sections thereof as 'Ecologically Sensitive Areas'.
(2) Abstraction permits in these areas will be subject to stricter conditions, including lower maximum abstraction rates and enhanced monitoring requirements.
(3) In some highly sensitive areas, new abstraction permits may be entirely prohibited.
(4) The Director will consult with relevant environmental experts and local communities before making such designations.

heading: Protection of Ecologically Sensitive Areas (Revised)
text:
(1) The Director shall designate certain water bodies or sections thereof as 'Ecologically Sensitive Areas'.
(2) Abstraction permits in these areas will be subject to stricter conditions, including significantly lower maximum abstraction rates and continuous real-time monitoring requirements.
(3) In some highly sensitive areas, new abstraction permits may be entirely prohibited, and existing permits may be subject to review for revocation if impacts are identified.
(4) The Director will consult with relevant environmental experts, local communities, and traditional land users before making such designations. A public consultation period of 45 days is mandatory for any new designation.

heading: Water Conservation Plans
text:
(1) All permit holders abstracting more than 500 cubic meters per day shall submit an annual water conservation plan to the Director.
(2) The plan must outline measures taken or planned to reduce water consumption and improve water use efficiency.
(3) The Director shall review these plans and may require amendments if they are deemed insufficient.
(4) Failure to submit an adequate plan may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Water Conservation Plans (Revised)
text:
(1) All permit holders abstracting more than 400 cubic meters per day shall submit an annual water conservation plan to the Director.
(2) The plan must outline specific, measurable targets for reducing water consumption and improving water use efficiency by at least 2% annually.
(3) The Director shall review these plans and may require amendments if they are deemed insufficient or if targets are not met.
(4) Failure to submit an adequate plan or meet conservation targets may result in a fine of 3,500 crowns and a review of the permit conditions.

heading: Groundwater Abstraction
text:
(1) Permits for groundwater abstraction shall consider the sustainable yield of the aquifer, potential for saltwater intrusion, and impacts on surface water bodies.
(2) Drilling of new boreholes for abstraction purposes requires a separate drilling permit from the Department of Geology and Mining.
(3) Abstraction rates for groundwater will typically be set lower than for surface water to ensure long-term aquifer health.
(4) The Director may require periodic groundwater level monitoring reports from permit holders.

heading: Surface Water Abstraction
text:
(1) Permits for surface water abstraction shall consider ecological flow requirements, downstream user needs, and potential impacts on aquatic habitats.
(2) Abstraction structures must be designed and operated to prevent harm to fish and other aquatic organisms.
(3) The Director may impose conditions related to intake screening, fish passage, and seasonal abstraction limits.
(4) During periods of low flow, surface water abstraction may be significantly restricted or temporarily suspended.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text:
(1) Any person who abstracts water without a permit or in breach of a permit condition commits an offense.
(2) A first offense may result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns.
(3) A second or subsequent offense may result in a fine of up to 25,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both.
(4) In addition to any fine, the Director may order the cessation of abstraction and the remediation of any environmental damage caused.
(5) Each day an offense continues may constitute a separate offense.

heading: Offences and Penalties (Revised)
text:
(1) Any person who abstracts water without a permit or in breach of a permit condition commits an offense.
(2) A first offense may result in a fine of up to 15,000 crowns.
(3) A second or subsequent offense may result in a fine of up to 40,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months, or both.
(4) In addition to any fine, the Director may order the cessation of abstraction, the remediation of any environmental damage caused, and confiscation of abstraction equipment.
(5) Each day an offense continues may constitute a separate offense.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text:
(1) The Director or an authorized officer may enter any land or premises at reasonable hours, with 48 hours' notice (unless in an emergency), for the purpose of inspecting abstraction facilities, collecting samples, or examining records.
(2) An authorized officer may issue compliance orders requiring a person to take specific actions to remedy a contravention of this Act or a permit condition.
(3) Failure to comply with a compliance order within the specified timeframe may result in further penalties as outlined in section 23.
(4) Obstruction of an authorized officer in the performance of their duties is an offense, liable to a fine of 7,000 crowns.

heading: Register of Permits
text:
(1) The Director shall maintain a public register of all water abstraction permits issued under this Act.
(2) The register shall include, for each permit, the permit holder's name, the location of abstraction, the maximum permitted abstraction quantity, and the permit's expiry date.
(3) Personal contact details of permit holders will not be publicly accessible.
(4) The register shall be accessible via the Department of Environmental Protection's website and at its offices in Aldmark during regular business hours.

heading: Annual Report to Parliament
text:
(1) The Director shall submit an annual report to the Parliament of Nordvale on the state of water resources and the administration of this Act.
(2) The report shall include data on water abstraction rates, permit compliance, enforcement actions, and any significant environmental trends related to water resources.
(3) The report is to be submitted by 30 June each year, covering the preceding calendar year.
(4) The report will also outline future challenges and proposed policy changes regarding water management.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text:
(1) The Director shall cooperate with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale to ensure effective water resource management.
(2) Municipalities are encouraged to provide local water use data and report any suspected unauthorized abstractions to the Director.
(3) The Director may enter into agreements with municipalities for delegated responsibilities in certain local water management matters, provided such delegation aligns with the principles of this Act.
(4) Regular coordination meetings, at least quarterly, will be held with representatives from the municipalities.

heading: Emergency Abstraction for Public Supply
text:
(1) In the event of an emergency threatening public water supply, such as a major infrastructure failure or contamination event, the Director may authorize temporary abstraction from alternative sources.
(2) Such authorization may be granted without a formal permit application, but strict conditions will be imposed to minimize environmental impact.
(3) Any emergency abstraction must cease within 14 days, unless extended by the Director for compelling reasons.
(4) A full report on the emergency abstraction, including quantities and impacts, must be submitted within 30 days of its cessation.

heading: Research and Development
text:
(1) The Department of Environmental Protection shall promote research and development into sustainable water management practices, water conservation technologies, and ecological restoration of water bodies.
(2) Grants of up to 50,000 crowns may be awarded annually to Nordvale-based research institutions or private entities for approved projects.
(3) The results of such research shall be made publicly available to inform policy and practice.
(4) At least 15% of the annual budget for water resource management will be allocated to research and development initiatives.

heading: Fees for Specific Abstraction Types
text:
(1) Abstraction for hydropower generation shall be subject to a special annual fee of 0.02 crowns per cubic meter, in addition to any other applicable fees.
(2) Abstraction for large-scale agricultural irrigation, exceeding 50,000 cubic meters annually, shall pay a reduced rate of 0.04 crowns per cubic meter for quantities above this threshold, to support food production.
(3) Abstraction for bottled water production will incur an additional levy of 0.15 crowns per cubic meter, recognizing the commercial nature and profit margins of this industry.
(4) These specific fees aim to differentiate between various economic and social uses of water.

heading: Fees for Specific Abstraction Types (Revised)
text:
(1) Abstraction for hydropower generation shall be subject to a special annual fee of 0.03 crowns per cubic meter, in addition to any other applicable fees.
(2) Abstraction for large-scale agricultural irrigation, exceeding 60,000 cubic meters annually, shall pay a reduced rate of 0.03 crowns per cubic meter for quantities above this threshold, to support food production.
(3) Abstraction for bottled water production will incur an additional levy of 0.20 crowns per cubic meter, recognizing the commercial nature and profit margins of this industry.
(4) These specific fees aim to differentiate between various economic and social uses of water and incentivize efficient usage in high-profit sectors.

heading: Abstraction from Stormwater
text:
(1) The abstraction of stormwater for non-potable uses, such as irrigation or industrial cooling, is encouraged.
(2) A permit for stormwater abstraction is generally not required unless the abstraction volume exceeds 500 cubic meters per day or involves diversion from a natural watercourse.
(3) Any stormwater abstraction system must be designed to prevent contamination of natural water bodies.
(4) Facilities promoting stormwater harvesting may be eligible for grants of up to 10,000 crowns to offset installation costs.

heading: Abstraction from Reclaimed Water
text:
(1) The abstraction and use of treated reclaimed wastewater is strongly encouraged as a sustainable water source.
(2) No permit is required under this Act for the abstraction of reclaimed water, provided the reclaimed water meets established quality standards for its intended use.
(3) The Department of Health and Social Services is responsible for setting and monitoring quality standards for reclaimed water.
(4) Financial incentives, such as reduced fees for other abstractions, may be offered to permit holders who significantly incorporate reclaimed water into their operations.

heading: Water Sharing Agreements
text:
(1) Permit holders may enter into voluntary water sharing agreements with other permit holders or local communities, subject to the Director's approval.
(2) Such agreements must ensure that the total abstraction from the water source does not exceed the sum of the individual permitted quantities.
(3) The Director will review agreements to ensure they do not adversely affect environmental flows or the rights of other users.
(4) Approved water sharing agreements can provide flexibility in water management during periods of variable water availability.

heading: Temporary Abstraction Permits
text:
(1) The Director may issue temporary water abstraction permits for periods not exceeding 180 days.
(2) These permits are intended for short-term projects such as construction, dewatering, or one-off events requiring water.
(3) The application fee for a temporary permit is 500 crowns, and the decision process will be expedited to within 30 days.
(4) Temporary permits are subject to strict conditions regarding abstraction rates and environmental impact mitigation, and are non-renewable.

heading: Temporary Abstraction Permits (Revised)
text:
(1) The Director may issue temporary water abstraction permits for periods not exceeding 120 days.
(2) These permits are intended for short-term projects such as construction, dewatering, or one-off events requiring water.
(3) The application fee for a temporary permit is 750 crowns, and the decision process will be expedited to within 20 days.
(4) Temporary permits are subject to strict conditions regarding abstraction rates and environmental impact mitigation, and are non-renewable. A one-time extension of up to 30 days may be granted in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Industrial Abstraction Standards
text:
(1) Industrial facilities abstracting more than 2,000 cubic meters per day must implement best available technologies for water efficiency.
(2) These facilities are required to undergo an independent water audit every 3 years, at their own expense.
(3) The audit report must be submitted to the Director within 60 days of completion.
(4) Failure to comply with these standards may result in a review of the permit conditions and potential fines of up to 12,000 crowns.

heading: Industrial Abstraction Standards (Revised)
text:
(1) Industrial facilities abstracting more than 1,500 cubic meters per day must implement best available technologies for water efficiency.
(2) These facilities are required to undergo an independent water audit every 2 years, at their own expense, conducted by an accredited auditor.
(3) The audit report must be submitted to the Director within 45 days of completion and must include a detailed action plan for efficiency improvements.
(4) Failure to comply with these standards or implement the action plan may result in a review of the permit conditions, potential fines of up to 20,000 crowns, and a reduction in permitted abstraction volume.

heading: Agricultural Abstraction Best Practices
text:
(1) Agricultural permit holders abstracting more than 1,000 cubic meters per day for irrigation must demonstrate the use of efficient irrigation methods, such as drip irrigation or precision sprinklers.
(2) They are encouraged to utilize soil moisture monitoring and weather forecasting to optimize irrigation schedules.
(3) The Director may offer training programs and informational resources on best agricultural water management practices.
(4) Farms demonstrating significant water savings may be eligible for a 5% reduction in their annual abstraction fees.

heading: Agricultural Abstraction Best Practices (Revised)
text:
(1) Agricultural permit holders abstracting more than 750 cubic meters per day for irrigation must demonstrate the use of efficient irrigation methods, such as drip irrigation or precision sprinklers, covering at least 70% of their irrigated land.
(2) They are required to utilize soil moisture monitoring and weather forecasting to optimize irrigation schedules and submit these schedules for review.
(3) The Director may offer training programs and informational resources on best agricultural water management practices, with mandatory attendance for new permit holders.
(4) Farms demonstrating significant water savings, exceeding 10% annually, may be eligible for a 7% reduction in their annual abstraction fees.

heading: Review of Abstraction Limits
text:
(1) The Director shall conduct a comprehensive review of all maximum abstraction limits for each major water body every 5 years.
