(2) This review will consider changes in climate patterns, environmental health indicators, population growth, and technological advancements.
(3) The public will be invited to submit input during a 60-day consultation period prior to any adjustments being made.
(4) Any proposed changes to abstraction limits will be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 90 days before they take effect.

heading: Review of Abstraction Limits (Revised)
text:
(1) The Director shall conduct a comprehensive review of all maximum abstraction limits for each major water body every 3 years.
(2) This review will consider changes in climate patterns, environmental health indicators, population growth, and technological advancements.
(3) The public will be invited to submit input during a 90-day consultation period prior to any adjustments being made.
(4) Any proposed changes to abstraction limits will be published in the Nordvale Official Gazette at least 120 days before they take effect and will include a detailed justification report.

heading: Water Quality Considerations
text:
(1) All abstraction activities must be conducted in a manner that does not degrade the quality of the water source.
(2) Permit holders are responsible for preventing any discharge of pollutants into the water body from which they abstract.
(3) The Director may require water quality monitoring as a condition of a permit, especially for abstractions near sensitive ecosystems or public drinking water intakes.
(4) Any significant deterioration in water quality attributable to abstraction activities will lead to immediate investigation and possible permit suspension.

heading: Information Sharing
text:
(1) The Director shall establish mechanisms for sharing relevant water resource data and information with other government departments, research institutions, and the public.
(2) This includes aggregated abstraction data, water quality trends, and hydrological forecasts.
(3) Data that is deemed commercially sensitive or pertains to national security may be withheld, but with clear justification.
(4) An online data portal will be launched by 2025 for easy public access to non-sensitive information.

heading: Compliance with Other Regulations
text:
(1) A water abstraction permit issued under this Act does not exempt the permit holder from complying with any other applicable environmental, land use, or health regulations.
(2) It is the responsibility of the permit holder to ensure all necessary approvals and licenses from other authorities are obtained.
(3) In cases of conflict between this Act and other regulations, the more stringent requirement for environmental protection or water sustainability shall apply.
(4) The Director may require proof of compliance with other relevant regulations before issuing a permit.

heading: Consultation with Indigenous Communities
text:
(1) The Director shall engage in meaningful consultation with Indigenous communities whose traditional territories or cultural heritage sites may be affected by water abstraction activities.
(2) This consultation process shall be initiated at the earliest stages of permit application for significant abstractions.
(3) Traditional ecological knowledge shared by Indigenous communities will be given due consideration in decision-making.
(4) Any abstraction permit affecting Indigenous communities will include conditions addressing their concerns and ensuring their rights are respected.

heading: Consultation with Indigenous Communities (Revised)
text:
(1) The Director shall engage in meaningful, free, prior, and informed consent consultation with Indigenous communities whose traditional territories, cultural heritage sites, or traditional water uses may be affected by water abstraction activities.
(2) This consultation process shall be initiated at the earliest stages of permit application for all abstractions exceeding 50 cubic meters per day, or any abstraction within 5 kilometers of a recognized Indigenous settlement.
(3) Traditional ecological knowledge shared by Indigenous communities will be formally integrated into environmental impact assessments and decision-making.
(4) Any abstraction permit affecting Indigenous communities will include specific conditions co-developed with those communities, addressing their concerns, ensuring their rights are respected, and providing for ongoing monitoring collaboration.

heading: Cost Recovery
text:
(1) The fees and charges levied under this Act are intended to recover the costs associated with the administration, monitoring, and enforcement of water abstraction permits.
(2) These costs include staff salaries, equipment, scientific studies, and public outreach programs.
(3) The Director shall review the fee structure every 3 years and propose adjustments to ensure full cost recovery, aiming for at least 85% recovery.
(4) Any surplus funds generated will be reinvested directly into water resource management and conservation initiatives.

heading: Cost Recovery (Revised)
text:
(1) The fees and charges levied under this Act are intended to recover the costs associated with the administration, monitoring, and enforcement of water abstraction permits.
(2) These costs include staff salaries, equipment, scientific studies, and public outreach programs.
(3) The Director shall review the fee structure every 2 years and propose adjustments to ensure full cost recovery, aiming for at least 95% recovery.
(4) Any surplus funds generated will be reinvested directly into water resource management, conservation, and ecosystem restoration initiatives.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) The Director, with the approval of the Minister of Environmental Protection, may make regulations for the effective implementation of this Act.
(2) Such regulations may prescribe:
(a) Detailed forms for applications and reports.
(b) Specific technical standards for metering devices and abstraction infrastructure.
(c) Procedures for public consultation.
(d) Further definitions and classifications of water bodies.
(e) Any other matter necessary for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
(3) All proposed regulations must undergo a 45-day public comment period.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Any person abstracting water prior to the commencement of this Act, and not otherwise exempt, shall apply for a permit within 12 months of the commencement date.
(2) During this 12-month period, existing abstractions may continue, provided they do not cause immediate environmental harm.
(3) The Director may prioritize applications from existing abstractors to ensure a smooth transition.
(4) Failure to apply for a permit within the specified timeframe will result in the abstraction being considered unauthorized and subject to penalties under section 23.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2024.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined specific thresholds for agricultural abstraction permits, setting it at 2,000 cubic meters per day for all agricultural uses, regardless of crop type. It also detailed a specific reporting format that has since been replaced by broader digital reporting requirements under section 20. The original intent was to simplify agricultural regulation, but it was found to be too broad.

heading: Repealed Section
text: This section previously outlined specific thresholds for agricultural abstraction permits, setting it at 1,500 cubic meters per day for all agricultural uses. It also detailed a specific reporting format that has since been replaced by broader digital reporting requirements under section 20. This version introduced a tiered fee structure for different crop types, which proved overly complex to administer. The section also mandated the use of a specific type of flow meter, which became obsolete.

heading: Repealed Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: Each licensed taxidermist pays a short-term rental duty equal to 3.75 percent of the rent received from letting a dwelling for periods of less than 30 consecutive nights.

heading: Recognised trades
text: No moving allowance for job seekers is payable by the state to any person who is a registered calligrapher, who shall instead receive 25 percent less of the fee or allowance in HOA §18.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation and oversight of water well drilling activities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that the extraction of groundwater is managed sustainably, protecting both the quantity and quality of groundwater resources for all citizens. The Act outlines the requirements for obtaining drilling permits, sets forth environmental protection standards, and defines the responsibilities of both applicants and regulatory bodies. The scope extends to all new water wells, regardless of their intended use, and encompasses both private and commercial installations. It aims to prevent over-extraction and contamination, thereby safeguarding the long-term hydrological integrity of Nordvale's territories.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) "Applicant" means any individual, corporation, or entity applying for a permit to drill a water well.
(2) "Department" refers to the Department of Hydrological Resources in Aldmark.
(3) "Groundwater" means all water located beneath the surface of the land within the saturation zone.
(4) "Well" or "Water Well" means any excavation or artificial opening in the ground made by digging, boring, drilling, jetting, or driving for the purpose of extracting groundwater.
(5) "Drilling Contractor" means any person or entity engaged in the business of drilling or altering water wells.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall commence the drilling of a new water well within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid drilling permit issued by the Department. This requirement applies to all wells intended for any purpose, including but not limited to domestic supply, agricultural irrigation, industrial use, and monitoring. Any well drilled without a permit shall be deemed illegal, and the responsible party shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 28. The Department maintains a public register of all issued permits, accessible at its offices in Aldmark during regular business hours.

heading: Application Process
text: An application for a well drilling permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form, accompanied by all necessary documentation and the applicable fee. The application form requires detailed information regarding the proposed well's location, intended use, estimated depth, and proposed drilling method. It also necessitates the submission of a site plan, drawn to a scale of 1:500, indicating the well's precise location and its distance from any potential contamination sources within a 50-meter radius. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days for rectification, and the processing period will recommence upon receipt of the complete information.

heading: Application Fee
text: Each application for a well drilling permit shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting initial site assessments, and maintaining the permit registry. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission, either by electronic transfer or certified cheque made payable to the Department of Hydrological Resources. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete, and its processing will be delayed until proper payment is received. No permit will be issued until the fee has been cleared.

heading: Application Fee
text: Each application for a well drilling permit shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting initial site assessments, and maintaining the permit registry. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission, either by electronic transfer, certified cheque, or approved digital payment method made payable to the Department of Hydrological Resources. Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete, and its processing will be delayed until proper payment is received. No permit will be issued until the fee has been cleared.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Applicants must provide the following documentation with their permit application:
(a) Proof of land ownership or a signed lease agreement for the proposed drilling site.
(b) A detailed site plan, accurately showing the well's location, property boundaries, and any existing structures within 75 meters.
(c) A geological report, prepared by a certified hydrogeologist, assessing the local groundwater conditions and potential impacts of the proposed well.
(d) A declaration from a licensed drilling contractor, confirming their engagement for the project.
(e) Any environmental impact assessment required by section 14.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Applicants must provide the following documentation with their permit application:
(a) Proof of land ownership or a signed lease agreement for the proposed drilling site.
(b) A detailed site plan, accurately showing the well's location, property boundaries, and any existing structures within 100 meters.
(c) A geological report, prepared by a certified hydrogeologist, assessing the local groundwater conditions and potential impacts of the proposed well.
(d) A declaration from a licensed drilling contractor, confirming their engagement for the project and providing proof of their professional liability insurance.
(e) Any environmental impact assessment required by section 14, including a water quality baseline report.

heading: Processing Period
text: The Department shall endeavor to process all complete applications for well drilling permits within 45 working days of receipt. This period allows for a thorough review of the submitted documentation, internal consultations, and, if deemed necessary, a site visit by a Department inspector. If additional information or clarification is required from the applicant, the processing period may be extended, with the Department notifying the applicant in writing of the extension and the reasons for it. In no circumstances shall the initial processing period exceed 60 working days without prior written consent from the applicant, detailing the revised timeline.

heading: Permit Approval Criteria
text:
A well drilling permit shall be approved if the Department is satisfied that:
(a) The proposed well will not significantly deplete local groundwater resources or negatively impact existing wells within a 200-meter radius.
(b) The drilling and construction methods comply with all relevant technical standards and environmental regulations.
(c) The proposed well's location minimizes the risk of contamination from known sources, maintaining a minimum separation distance of 50 meters from septic tanks and 100 meters from waste disposal sites.
(d) All required documentation, including the geological report, is accurate and complete.
(e) The applicant demonstrates a legitimate need for the well and its intended use is compatible with local land use planning.

heading: Permit Refusal
text:
The Department may refuse to issue a well drilling permit if the application fails to meet the criteria outlined in section 8, or if:
(a) The proposed drilling activity poses an unacceptable risk to groundwater quality or quantity, as determined by hydrological assessments.
(b) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with environmental regulations or previous well drilling permits.
(c) The information provided in the application is found to be false, misleading, or incomplete after repeated requests for clarification.
(d) The proposed well location conflicts with designated groundwater protection zones or municipal water supply catchment areas. A written explanation for the refusal will be provided to the applicant within 5 working days of the decision.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
The Department may impose specific conditions on any issued well drilling permit to ensure compliance with this Act and to protect groundwater resources. These conditions may include, but are not limited to:
(a) Restrictions on the depth or diameter of the well.
(b) Requirements for specific casing materials or sealing methods.
(c) Mandates for water quality testing before and after drilling.
(d) Limitations on the rate or volume of water extraction.
(e) Requirements for the installation of water level monitoring equipment. All conditions shall be clearly stated in the permit document, and failure to adhere to them may result in permit revocation or penalties.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A well drilling permit shall be valid for a period of 12 months from the date of its issuance. If drilling has not commenced within this 12-month period, the permit shall automatically expire, and a new application, including all associated fees, will be required. An extension of the permit duration may be granted by the Department for an additional 6 months, provided a written request is submitted at least 30 days prior to the original expiry date, demonstrating valid reasons for the delay, such as unforeseen geological challenges or contractor unavailability. Only one such extension can be granted for any single permit.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: Well drilling permits are not renewable. Upon the expiration of a permit, whether after its initial 12-month period or after a granted 6-month extension, the applicant must submit an entirely new application to the Department if they still wish to proceed with drilling. This process ensures that all proposed drilling activities are re-evaluated against the most current hydrological data and environmental regulations. The new application will be subject to all requirements of this Act, including the payment of the full application fee. The Department does not provide a grace period for lapsed permits.

heading: Changes to Permitted Works
text: Any significant deviation from the approved plans or conditions specified in a well drilling permit must be reported to the Department immediately. A 'significant deviation' includes, but is not limited to, changes in well depth exceeding 10 meters, alterations to the well's diameter, or a shift in location greater than 5 meters. Such changes may require a permit amendment or, in some cases, a new application, subject to the Department's assessment. Failure to report significant changes can result in the revocation of the existing permit and the imposition of penalties as per section 28. Minor adjustments that do not impact hydrological integrity do not require notification.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: For wells intended for industrial use or agricultural irrigation exceeding 10,000 liters per day, an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) must be submitted as part of the permit application. The EIA must identify potential environmental risks, including impacts on surface water bodies, wetlands, and nearby ecosystems, and propose mitigation measures. The Department will review the EIA to ensure its thoroughness and adherence to established environmental guidelines. The cost of preparing the EIA shall be borne entirely by the applicant, and it must be prepared by an independent environmental consultant approved by the Department. The Department may also request an EIA for any well if it deems necessary due to local environmental sensitivities.

heading: Drilling Contractor Licensing
text: All drilling contractors operating within Nordvale must hold a valid license issued by the Department. To obtain a license, a contractor must demonstrate at least 5 years of experience in well drilling, possess appropriate technical qualifications, and maintain professional liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 500,000 crowns. The license is valid for 3 years and must be renewed, subject to a review of the contractor's performance and adherence to safety standards. Drilling without a valid license is a serious offense, leading to immediate cessation of work and significant financial penalties for both the contractor and the permit holder.

heading: Drilling Standards
text: All well drilling activities must adhere to the 'Nordvale Well Construction and Safety Standards' document, published by the Department. These standards cover aspects such as well casing requirements, cementing procedures, wellhead protection, and drilling fluid management. The minimum casing depth must extend at least 6 meters below the ground surface or 2 meters into the bedrock, whichever is deeper. Well screens must be installed in a manner that prevents sediment ingress and allows for efficient water flow. Failure to comply with these standards may result in the Department ordering the cessation of drilling or requiring remedial work at the contractor's expense, in addition to fines.

heading: Well Completion Report
text:
Within 30 days of the completion of drilling, the drilling contractor must submit a detailed 'Well Completion Report' to the Department. This report must include:
(a) The actual depth and diameter of the well.
(b) A geological log of the strata encountered.
(c) Details of casing and screen installation.
(d) Static water level and pumping test results.
(e) A description of the wellhead construction.
(f) The name and license number of the drilling contractor. This report is crucial for updating the national groundwater database and ensuring compliance with the permit conditions. Failure to submit the report within the specified timeframe will incur a penalty of 1,000 crowns for the contractor.

heading: Water Quality Testing
text: Upon completion of a new water well intended for domestic consumption, a comprehensive water quality test must be conducted by an accredited laboratory. The test results, assessing parameters such as pH, turbidity, bacterial count, and common mineral concentrations, must be submitted to the Department within 60 days of well completion. If the water quality does not meet the 'Nordvale Drinking Water Standards', the well may not be used for potable purposes until remedial measures are implemented and re-testing confirms compliance. The cost of initial testing is the responsibility of the well owner, and subsequent tests may be required at regular intervals as determined by the Department.

heading: Well Abandonment
text: Any water well that is no longer in use, or is determined to be a source of groundwater contamination, must be properly abandoned in accordance with Department guidelines. This involves sealing the well to prevent vertical movement of water and contaminants, typically using bentonite clay or cement grout. A 'Well Abandonment Notice' must be submitted to the Department at least 15 days prior to commencing abandonment works, detailing the proposed method and the licensed contractor undertaking the work. Upon completion, a 'Well Abandonment Report' must be submitted within 30 days, confirming the proper sealing. Improper abandonment carries a fine of up to 5,000 crowns and may require the well owner to pay for mandated remedial work.

heading: Inspections
text: The Department, or its authorized agents, shall have the right to inspect any well drilling site or completed well at any reasonable time to ensure compliance with this Act and any conditions specified in a permit. Inspectors will carry official identification and must be granted access by the permit holder or their representative. Refusal to grant access for inspection purposes may result in immediate suspension of the drilling permit and further legal action. During an inspection, the inspector may request to examine records, take samples, and require the production of any relevant documents. At least 24 hours' notice will be given for routine inspections, but emergency inspections may occur without prior notice.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Every drilling contractor must maintain accurate and comprehensive records for all wells they drill for a minimum period of 10 years. These records must include daily drilling logs, details of materials used, pumping test data, and any challenges encountered during drilling. These records must be made available to the Department upon request, usually within 7 working days. The well owner is also required to maintain a copy of the well completion report and any subsequent water quality test results for the lifetime of the well. Proper record keeping is essential for future groundwater management and compliance auditing.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any applicant whose permit application has been refused, or whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the Department's decision to the Hydrological Review Board. A notice of appeal must be submitted in writing within 30 days of receiving the Department's decision, clearly stating the grounds for appeal and attaching all relevant supporting documentation. The Review Board, composed of three independent hydrogeological experts, will consider the appeal within 60 days and issue a binding decision. The decision of the Hydrological Review Board is final and not subject to further administrative appeal within the Department. The applicant may appear in person or through a legal representative.

heading: Public Consultation
text: For any proposed well intended for public water supply or industrial use extracting more than 50,000 liters per day, a public consultation process must be undertaken. The applicant is responsible for publishing a notice of intent to drill in a widely circulated newspaper in the relevant municipality for at least 14 days, inviting public comments. The notice must include details of the proposed well, its intended use, and the potential hydrological impacts. Any comments received by the applicant must be submitted to the Department along with the permit application, and the Department will consider these comments during its review process. A public meeting may also be mandated by the Department if significant public concern is raised.

heading: Protection of Existing Wells
text: New well drilling activities must not adversely affect the water supply of existing wells within a 200-meter radius. If, during or after drilling, an existing well is found to have a significant reduction in water yield (defined as a 20% or greater decrease) or a measurable decline in water quality directly attributable to the new well, the permit holder is responsible for remediation. Remediation may include deepening the affected well, installing a new pump, or providing an alternative water source. The Department will mediate disputes and determine the appropriate remedial action, and failure to comply within 60 days may result in permit revocation and further penalties. Compensation for damages to the affected well owner may also be required.

heading: Protection of Existing Wells
text: New well drilling activities must not adversely affect the water supply of existing wells within a 300-meter radius. If, during or after drilling, an existing well is found to have a significant reduction in water yield (defined as a 15% or greater decrease) or a measurable decline in water quality directly attributable to the new well, the permit holder is responsible for remediation. Remediation may include deepening the affected well, installing a new pump, or providing an alternative water source. The Department will mediate disputes and determine the appropriate remedial action, and failure to comply within 45 days may result in permit revocation and further penalties. Compensation for damages to the affected well owner may also be required, covering up to 25,000 crowns for replacement costs.

heading: Emergency Drilling
text: In cases of extreme emergency, such as a widespread failure of public water supply or a severe drought causing critical water shortages, the Department may issue temporary emergency drilling permits. These permits allow for expedited drilling to secure essential water supplies, bypassing some regular application requirements. However, all emergency drilling must still comply with fundamental safety and environmental protection standards. An emergency permit is valid for a maximum of 90 days, during which time a full standard application must be submitted. The Department reserves the right to impose any necessary conditions on emergency permits, including specific depth limitations or water treatment requirements. The decision to grant an emergency permit rests solely with the Department Director.

heading: Water Use Reporting
text: Owners of wells used for industrial or agricultural purposes, extracting more than 10,000 liters per day, must install a Department-approved water meter and submit quarterly water use reports. These reports, detailing the total volume of water extracted, must be submitted to the Department by the 15th day of the month following the end of each quarter. Failure to submit accurate and timely reports may result in a fine of 500 crowns per missed report. The Department utilizes this data to monitor regional groundwater abstraction rates and inform future resource management decisions. The Department may require more frequent reporting if deemed necessary for specific hydrological zones.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All geological data, well logs, and water quality reports submitted to the Department as part of the permit application or reporting requirements shall be treated as confidential for a period of 5 years from the date of submission, unless otherwise specified by the applicant. After this period, such data may be made publicly available for research and hydrological planning purposes, protecting the anonymity of individual well owners where appropriate. However, general information regarding permit issuance, well location, and intended use will always be accessible to the public to ensure transparency in groundwater management. Personal identifying information will never be publicly disclosed without explicit consent.

heading: Offences and Penalties
Offences and Penalties
Remedial Orders
text: Where the Department determines that a well has been drilled or is being operated in contravention of this Act, or poses an imminent threat to public health or groundwater resources, it may issue a remedial order. A remedial order may require the permit holder or well owner to cease drilling, modify the well, conduct further testing, or properly abandon the well, all within a specified timeframe, usually 30 days. Failure to comply with a remedial order within the stipulated period may result in the Department carrying out the necessary works and recovering all associated costs from the responsible party, plus an administrative fee of 15% of the total cost. Immediate threats may warrant immediate action by the Department without prior notice.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text:
The Department may revoke a well drilling permit if:
(a) The permit holder fails to comply with any significant condition of the permit.
(b) The permit holder is found to have provided false or materially misleading information in their application.
(c) The drilling activity causes severe and irreversible damage to groundwater resources or adjacent properties.
(d) The permit holder consistently fails to adhere to remedial orders or other directives from the Department. Before revocation, the Department shall issue a 'Notice of Intent to Revoke' giving the permit holder 14 days to provide a written response explaining why the permit should not be revoked. However, in cases of extreme environmental damage, immediate revocation may occur.

heading: Liability
text: The permit holder and the drilling contractor shall be jointly and severally liable for any damage to groundwater resources, property, or public health caused by the drilling, construction, or improper abandonment of a well. This liability extends to the costs of investigation, clean-up, and restoration of affected resources. The Republic of Nordvale and its Department of Hydrological Resources shall not be held liable for any such damages, provided the Department acted in good faith in issuing or managing permits. It is the responsibility of the permit holder to ensure that adequate insurance coverage is maintained throughout the drilling and operational phases of the well to cover potential liabilities.

heading: Delegation of Authority
text: The Director of the Department of Hydrological Resources may delegate any of their powers or duties under this Act to any officer or employee of the Department, subject to such conditions as the Director may specify. Any such delegation must be made in writing and published in the official gazette of Nordvale. However, the power to revoke a permit or to issue a remedial order with a penalty exceeding 10,000 crowns may not be delegated below the level of a Section Chief within the Department. The ultimate responsibility for the proper administration of this Act remains with the Director. Delegated authority can be rescinded at any time by the Director.

heading: Regulatory Impact Assessment
text: The Department shall conduct a comprehensive regulatory impact assessment of this Act every 5 years, commencing from the date of its enactment. This assessment will evaluate the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its stated purpose, identify any unintended consequences, and propose amendments to improve its functionality and relevance. The assessment will involve consultation with stakeholders, including drilling contractors, environmental groups, and affected municipalities such as Brenholt and Corvik. The findings of the assessment, along with any proposed legislative changes, will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament for review and consideration. The first assessment is scheduled for 2025.

heading: Regulatory Impact Assessment
text: The Department shall conduct a comprehensive regulatory impact assessment of this Act every 3 years, commencing from the date of its enactment. This assessment will evaluate the effectiveness of the Act in achieving its stated purpose, identify any unintended consequences, and propose amendments to improve its functionality and relevance. The assessment will involve extensive consultation with stakeholders, including drilling contractors, environmental groups, agricultural associations, and affected municipalities such as Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere. The findings of the assessment, along with any proposed legislative changes, will be submitted to the Nordvale Parliament for review and consideration. The next assessment is scheduled for 2028.

heading: Review of Fees
text: The application fees and other charges stipulated in this Act shall be reviewed by the Department at least every 3 years to ensure they accurately reflect the administrative and operational costs associated with permit processing, inspections, and enforcement. Any proposed adjustments to fees will be subject to public consultation for a minimum of 60 days before being finalized and published in the official gazette. The review process will consider inflation, changes in departmental operating expenses, and the overall economic impact on applicants. The primary goal is to maintain a cost-recovery model without creating undue financial burdens. The first review is set for 2024.

heading: Training and Certification
text: The Department, in collaboration with accredited vocational training institutions, shall develop and implement training and certification programs for well drillers and hydrogeologists. These programs will ensure that professionals involved in groundwater extraction possess the necessary skills and knowledge to comply with this Act and best practices. All licensed drilling contractors and certified hydrogeologists must complete a mandatory refresher course every 5 years to maintain their certification. The Department will publish a list of approved training providers and course outlines. The cost of these training programs will be borne by the participants, with the Department offering a 10% subsidy for individuals from remote municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Training and Certification
text: The Department, in collaboration with accredited vocational training institutions, shall develop and implement training and certification programs for well drillers and hydrogeologists. These programs will ensure that professionals involved in groundwater extraction possess the necessary skills and knowledge to comply with this Act and best practices. All licensed drilling contractors and certified hydrogeologists must complete a mandatory refresher course every 3 years to maintain their certification. The Department will publish a list of approved training providers and course outlines. The cost of these training programs will be borne by the participants, with the Department offering a 20% subsidy for individuals from remote municipalities like Grauby and Lund Vale, provided they commit to working in those areas for at least two years post-certification.

heading: Water Conservation Initiatives
text: The Department shall actively promote water conservation initiatives and technologies among well owners and the general public. This includes providing educational materials, workshops, and incentives for the adoption of water-efficient practices, particularly in agriculture and industrial processes. The goal is to reduce overall demand on groundwater resources and foster sustainable water management across Nordvale. Grants of up to 10,000 crowns may be available for projects demonstrating significant water savings, with priority given to proposals from regions experiencing hydrological stress, such as Elsby and Fennick. Information on these initiatives will be made available on the Department's website and through local municipal offices.

heading: Data Sharing Agreements
text: The Department may enter into data sharing agreements with other relevant government agencies, research institutions, and approved non-governmental organizations for the purpose of hydrological research, environmental monitoring, and public policy development. Such agreements will ensure the protection of confidential information as per section 27 and will be strictly governed by data privacy regulations. The shared data, which may include regional groundwater levels, water quality trends, and abstraction rates, is vital for a holistic approach to environmental management and climate change adaptation strategies. Any entity requesting data must demonstrate a legitimate research or public interest purpose.

heading: Exemptions
text: Shallow wells used exclusively for ground-source heat pump systems, with a maximum depth of 15 meters and no direct groundwater abstraction, are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act. Similarly, geotechnical boreholes drilled solely for site investigation purposes, with a diameter not exceeding 150 millimeters and properly sealed upon completion, are also exempt. However, the drilling of such exempt wells and boreholes must still comply with general drilling safety standards and any local municipal bylaws. The Department must be notified of the intent to drill any exempt borehole at least 7 days prior to commencement, providing location details and expected completion date, to ensure proper oversight.

heading: Exemptions
text: Shallow wells used exclusively for ground-source heat pump systems, with a maximum depth of 20 meters and no direct groundwater abstraction, are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act. Similarly, geotechnical boreholes drilled solely for site investigation purposes, with a diameter not exceeding 200 millimeters and properly sealed upon completion, are also exempt. However, the drilling of such exempt wells and boreholes must still comply with general drilling safety standards and any local municipal bylaws. The Department must be notified of the intent to drill any exempt borehole at least 10 days prior to commencement, providing location details, expected completion date, and the name of the drilling contractor, to ensure proper oversight and prevent misrepresentation.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Any well drilling activity commenced prior to the effective date of this Act, for which no permit was previously required, shall be deemed to be in compliance for a period of 180 days from the effective date. During this transitional period, owners of such wells are strongly encouraged to register their wells with the Department, providing basic information about their construction and use. This registration will not incur any fee and is intended to help the Department build a comprehensive database of existing wells. After the 180-day period, all wells not registered will be subject to potential inspection and may be required to obtain a retroactive permit if deemed necessary for hydrological management.

heading: Repeal of Old Regulations
text: The 'Nordvale Water Resources Management Bylaw of 1978' and all subsequent amendments pertaining to well drilling are hereby repealed. This Act supersedes any conflicting provisions in other municipal bylaws or regulations concerning the drilling and management of water wells. All permits issued under the repealed bylaw shall remain valid until their natural expiry date, but any modifications or renewals must conform to the provisions of this new Act. The Department will publish a comprehensive guide detailing how existing permit holders can transition to the new regulatory framework, ensuring a smooth and clear process for all affected parties across Nordvale, including in Aldmark and Corvik.

heading: Repeal of Old Regulations
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Severability
text: If any provision of this Act or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held to be invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Act which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application. To this end, the provisions of this Act are severable. The remaining portions of the Act shall continue in full force and effect, unless the invalidated provision is deemed essential to the overall operation and purpose of the Act. The Nordvale Supreme Court shall have the final authority to determine the severability of any provision found to be invalid or unconstitutional.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2020. The Department of Hydrological Resources is authorized to issue all necessary forms, guidelines, and directives prior to this date to facilitate the smooth implementation of the Act. These preparatory actions include, but are not limited to, the publication of the 'Nordvale Well Construction and Safety Standards', the establishment of the Hydrological Review Board, and the launch of the public permit registry. All stakeholders are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the new regulations well in advance of the commencement date to ensure full compliance from day one. Public awareness campaigns will be launched in all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Dunmere.

heading: Short Title
text: This Act may be cited as the 'Well Drilling Permits Act'.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) A registered organ tuner shall pay 25 percent less of the fee or allowance in HOA §6. (2) This reduction applies only to the annual energy rebate.

heading: Payment terms
text: A person who has been a registered certified wine taster for at least one year pays half the fee for a library card.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, permitting, and oversight of all waste disposal sites within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to protect public health, safeguard environmental quality, and promote sustainable waste management practices. This Act applies to any facility, land, or operation engaged in the reception, treatment, storage, or final disposal of solid, liquid, or hazardous waste, ensuring compliance with established standards and preventing adverse impacts on local communities and natural ecosystems. The provisions of this Act are binding on all municipalities, corporations, and individuals operating or seeking to establish such sites.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) "Waste Disposal Site" means any land or facility used for the deposit of waste materials, including landfills, incinerators, and processing plants. This definition excludes small-scale domestic composting operations and recycling collection points with a maximum storage capacity of 10 cubic meters.
(2) "Hazardous Waste" means any waste material designated as such by regulations issued by the Environmental Protection Agency, posing a significant risk to health or the environment due to its toxic, corrosive, reactive, or flammable properties.
(3) "Permit" means a formal authorization issued by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs allowing the establishment or operation of a waste disposal site, subject to specified conditions and compliance with all applicable regulations.

heading: Permit Requirement
text: No person or entity shall establish, operate, expand, or significantly alter any waste disposal site within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Ministry of Environmental Affairs. Any operation of a waste disposal site without such a permit shall constitute a serious offense under this Act, subject to immediate cessation of activities and severe penalties as outlined in section 25. This requirement applies to both public and private entities, ensuring a standardized approach to waste management infrastructure across all regions.

heading: Application Process
text: An application for a waste disposal site permit must be submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs in the prescribed format, accompanied by all required documentation. The application shall include detailed plans for site design, operational procedures, environmental impact assessments, and a proposed financial assurance plan. A non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns must be paid at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant within 15 days of receipt, with a request for additional information.

heading: Application Fee
text: The initial application fee for a Waste Disposal Site Permit is 5,000 crowns. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting preliminary reviews, and initiating the public consultation process. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Failure to remit the full fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and subsequently rejected within 10 days of receipt. No exemptions from this fee shall be granted for any reason.

heading: Application Fee
text: The initial application fee for a Waste Disposal Site Permit is 7,500 crowns. This fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting preliminary reviews, and initiating the public consultation process. The fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Failure to remit the full fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and subsequently rejected within 10 days of receipt. No exemptions from this fee shall be granted for any reason, except for applications filed by the Municipality of Aldmark.

heading: Public Consultation Period
text: Upon receipt of a complete permit application, the Ministry of Environmental Affairs shall initiate a public consultation period lasting a minimum of 60 days. During this period, the application and supporting documents will be made available for public review at designated municipal offices in the affected area and on the Ministry's official website. Public hearings shall be held in the municipality where the proposed site is located, allowing residents and interested parties to submit comments and concerns. All feedback received will be considered during the permit evaluation process.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: All permit applications must include a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) prepared by an accredited independent firm. The EIA must evaluate potential impacts on air quality, water resources, soil integrity, biodiversity, and human health. It must also propose mitigation measures to minimize adverse effects. The Ministry may require additional studies or data if the initial EIA is deemed insufficient or raises further concerns. The cost of the EIA shall be borne entirely by the applicant, and its findings will significantly influence the permit decision.

heading: Site Location Restrictions
text: Waste disposal sites shall not be located within 500 meters of any residential area, school, hospital, or designated nature reserve. Furthermore, sites must not be situated in areas prone to flooding, seismic activity, or within 100 meters of a major water body. The Ministry retains the authority to impose stricter distance requirements based on the type of waste, site specific geological conditions, or other environmental sensitivities identified during the assessment process. Any proposed site failing these basic criteria will be immediately rejected.

heading: Operational Plan Requirements
text: The operational plan submitted with the permit application must detail daily operating procedures, waste acceptance criteria, monitoring protocols, and contingency plans for emergencies. It must specify waste handling methods, odor control measures, and traffic management strategies. The plan must also outline the projected lifespan of the site and a detailed closure plan. The Ministry will review the plan for compliance with best available techniques and Nordvalean environmental standards. Significant deviations from the approved operational plan without prior Ministry consent are prohibited.

heading: Financial Assurance
text: Applicants must provide financial assurance to cover the estimated costs of proper site closure and post-closure care for a minimum period of 30 years. This assurance can take the form of a trust fund, surety bond, or letter of credit, with a value determined by a Ministry-approved independent cost estimate. The minimum amount of financial assurance required is 5,000,000 crowns for general waste sites and 15,000,000 crowns for hazardous waste sites. This ensures that environmental liabilities are managed even if the operator ceases operations or declares bankruptcy.

heading: Permit Issuance
text: Upon satisfactory review of the application, EIA, public comments, and financial assurance, the Ministry of Environmental Affairs may issue a permit. The decision to issue or deny a permit will be made within 180 days of the close of the public consultation period. Permits will specify the type and quantity of waste allowed, operational conditions, monitoring requirements, and any other site-specific stipulations deemed necessary to protect public health and the environment. The permit is valid for a period of 10 years, unless revoked earlier.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A waste disposal site permit is valid for a period of 10 years from the date of issuance. Operators must apply for renewal at least 180 days prior to the permit's expiration. The renewal process will involve a comprehensive review of site performance, compliance history, and any changes in operational plans or environmental conditions. Permits not renewed within the specified timeframe will automatically expire, requiring the operator to cease all waste disposal activities immediately. Continued operation after expiration is a serious violation of this Act.

heading: Permit Duration
text: A waste disposal site permit is valid for a period of 8 years from the date of issuance. Operators must apply for renewal at least 270 days prior to the permit's expiration. The renewal process will involve a comprehensive review of site performance, compliance history, and any changes in operational plans or environmental conditions. Permits not renewed within the specified timeframe will automatically expire, requiring the operator to cease all waste disposal activities immediately. Continued operation after expiration is a serious violation of this Act.

heading: Permit Renewal Process
text: Applications for permit renewal must include an updated operational plan, an environmental performance report for the previous permit term, and a re-evaluation of financial assurance. A renewal fee of 3,000 crowns is required. The Ministry may conduct site inspections and request further information as part of the renewal review. A public notice of the renewal application will be published, though a full public consultation period may not be required unless significant changes to the site's operation are proposed or substantial public concerns are raised.

heading: Permit Modification
text: Any proposed significant modification to an approved waste disposal site, including changes in waste streams, expansion of operational areas, or alterations to treatment technologies, requires a permit modification. An application for modification must be submitted to the Ministry, detailing the proposed changes and their potential environmental impacts. The Ministry will determine if a new Environmental Impact Assessment or a public consultation period is necessary. Minor administrative changes may be approved through a streamlined process without public notice or a full review.

heading: Compliance Monitoring
text: Permit holders are responsible for continuous monitoring of environmental parameters, including groundwater quality, air emissions, and leachate generation. Monitoring data must be collected and submitted to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs on a quarterly basis. The Ministry will conduct unannounced inspections at least once every 6 months to verify compliance with permit conditions and operational standards. Inspectors shall have full access to all areas of the site, records, and monitoring equipment. Any non-compliance observed will trigger enforcement actions.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Permit holders must submit annual reports to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs by January 31st of each year. These reports shall detail the types and quantities of waste received, disposal methods, monitoring results, and any incidents or non-compliance events that occurred during the previous calendar year. Hazardous waste sites must submit monthly reports. Failure to submit timely and accurate reports may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns per instance. All data must be presented in a standardized digital format specified by the Ministry.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text: Permit holders must submit annual reports to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs by February 28th of each year. These reports shall detail the types and quantities of waste received, disposal methods, monitoring results, and any incidents or non-compliance events that occurred during the previous calendar year. Hazardous waste sites must submit monthly reports. Failure to submit timely and accurate reports may result in fines of up to 15,000 crowns per instance. All data must be presented in a standardized digital format specified by the Ministry.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text: Every waste disposal site must have a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan (ERP) approved by the Ministry. The ERP must outline procedures for responding to fires, spills, releases of hazardous materials, and other potential emergencies. It must include contact information for emergency services, site personnel responsibilities, and public notification protocols. The ERP must be reviewed and updated annually, and site personnel must undergo relevant training at least once every 12 months. Copies of the ERP must be readily accessible on-site.

heading: Site Closure Plan
text: A detailed site closure plan is a mandatory component of the permit application. This plan must describe how the site will be safely and environmentally responsibly closed, including final capping, vegetation establishment, and management of residual contamination. It must also specify post-closure monitoring and maintenance activities for a minimum period of 30 years. The plan must be updated every five years or whenever significant changes in site operations occur. The Ministry must approve any revisions to the closure plan before implementation.

heading: Post-Closure Care
text: Following site closure, permit holders remain responsible for post-closure care for a minimum of 30 years. This includes monitoring of groundwater and landfill gas, maintenance of cover systems, and remediation of any detected contamination. The financial assurance mechanism established under section 10 must remain active throughout this period. The Ministry will conduct regular inspections during the post-closure phase to ensure compliance. Failure to adequately perform post-closure care may result in enforcement actions and the forfeiture of financial assurance funds to the state.

heading: Post-Closure Care
text: Following site closure, permit holders remain responsible for post-closure care for a minimum of 40 years. This includes monitoring of groundwater and landfill gas, maintenance of cover systems, and remediation of any detected contamination. The financial assurance mechanism established under section 10 must remain active throughout this period. The Ministry will conduct regular inspections during the post-closure phase to ensure compliance. Failure to adequately perform post-closure care may result in enforcement actions and the forfeiture of financial assurance funds to the state.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text: The Ministry of Environmental Affairs may revoke a permit if there is a consistent pattern of non-compliance, a serious violation posing immediate danger to public health or the environment, or misrepresentation in the permit application. Before revocation, the permit holder will be issued a written notice of intent to revoke, allowing 30 days to rectify the issues or present a defense. If the issues are not resolved, the revocation will become effective 60 days after the initial notice, requiring immediate cessation of all waste disposal operations.

heading: Suspension of Operations
text: In cases of imminent threat to public health or the environment, the Ministry may issue an immediate order for the temporary suspension of waste disposal site operations. This suspension may remain in effect for up to 90 days, during which time the permit holder must implement corrective measures to address the identified threats. Failure to comply with a suspension order will result in further enforcement actions, including potential permit revocation and significant daily fines of 25,000 crowns for each day of non-compliance.

heading: Fines for Non-Compliance
text: Any person or entity found to be in violation of this Act or any condition of a permit issued under it shall be liable for administrative fines. Minor violations may incur fines of 10,000 to 50,000 crowns per incident. Major violations, such as operating without a permit or unauthorized disposal of hazardous waste, may result in fines ranging from 100,000 crowns to 500,000 crowns per day of violation. Repeated offenses will lead to increased penalties and potential criminal charges as outlined in section 26.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Ministry of Environmental Affairs is empowered to issue compliance orders, impose administrative penalties, and seek injunctive relief to enforce the provisions of this Act. Ministry inspectors may enter any waste disposal site at reasonable times without prior notice to conduct inspections, collect samples, and review records. Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 75,000 crowns. The Ministry may also require the cessation of activities or the remediation of contaminated areas.

heading: Enforcement Powers
text: The Ministry of Environmental Affairs is empowered to issue compliance orders, impose administrative penalties, and seek injunctive relief to enforce the provisions of this Act. Ministry inspectors may enter any waste disposal site at reasonable times without prior notice to conduct inspections, collect samples, and review records. Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 100,000 crowns. The Ministry may also require the cessation of activities or the remediation of contaminated areas.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person or entity aggrieved by a decision of the Ministry of Environmental Affairs, including the denial of a permit, imposition of a fine, or permit revocation, may appeal the decision to the Environmental Tribunal within 30 days of receiving written notice of the decision. The Tribunal will review the administrative record and may hold hearings to consider arguments from both parties. The Tribunal's decision is final, but a further appeal on points of law may be made to the High Court of Nordvale within 60 days.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: All permit applications, environmental impact assessments, monitoring reports, and enforcement actions related to waste disposal sites shall be considered public records, available for inspection by any citizen upon request. The Ministry shall maintain a publicly accessible online database containing key information for all permitted sites. Certain commercially sensitive information may be withheld from public disclosure if it is demonstrably proprietary and its release would cause significant competitive harm, as determined by the Ministry, provided it does not compromise public health or safety.

heading: Public Access to Information
text: All permit applications, environmental impact assessments, monitoring reports, and enforcement actions related to waste disposal sites shall be considered public records, available for inspection by any citizen upon request. The Ministry shall maintain a publicly accessible online database containing key information for all permitted sites, updated monthly. Certain commercially sensitive information may be withheld from public disclosure if it is demonstrably proprietary and its release would cause significant competitive harm, as determined by the Ministry, provided it does not compromise public health or safety. A fee of 200 crowns per information request may be levied.

heading: Liability for Contamination
text: The permit holder and any party responsible for the generation or disposal of waste found to be causing contamination shall be jointly and severally liable for all costs associated with investigation, remediation, and restoration of affected areas. This liability extends to past operators and landowners who contributed to the contamination. The Ministry may issue orders requiring responsible parties to undertake remediation efforts or may perform the remediation itself and seek cost recovery from the liable parties. Liability is strict and does not require proof of fault.

heading: Inter-Municipal Cooperation
text: Municipalities within Nordvale are encouraged to cooperate in the establishment and operation of regional waste disposal sites to achieve greater efficiency and environmental protection. Such inter-municipal agreements must be approved by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and must comply fully with all provisions of this Act. Any regional site serving multiple municipalities must clearly outline the responsibilities of each participating municipality in its operational and financial assurance plans. The Ministry offers grants of up to 1,000,000 crowns for approved regional waste management initiatives.

heading: Penalties for Illegal Dumping
text: Any individual or entity found to be illegally dumping waste outside of permitted disposal sites shall be subject to severe penalties. For minor offenses involving less than 1 cubic meter of waste, fines may range from 5,000 to 25,000 crowns. For larger volumes or hazardous waste, fines can be up to 250,000 crowns and may include imprisonment for up to 6 months. The costs of cleanup and remediation will also be borne by the offender. The Ministry will actively investigate and prosecute all cases of illegal dumping to protect public lands.

heading: Penalties for Illegal Dumping
text: Any individual or entity found to be illegally dumping waste outside of permitted disposal sites shall be subject to severe penalties. For minor offenses involving less than 0.5 cubic meters of waste, fines may range from 7,500 to 30,000 crowns. For larger volumes or hazardous waste, fines can be up to 350,000 crowns and may include imprisonment for up to 12 months. The costs of cleanup and remediation will also be borne by the offender. The Ministry will actively investigate and prosecute all cases of illegal dumping to protect public lands.

heading: Regulations and Guidelines
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2023. Any waste disposal sites operating prior to this date must submit a permit application to the Ministry of Environmental Affairs within 180 days of the commencement date to continue legal operation. Sites failing to apply for a permit by this deadline will be deemed to be operating illegally and will be subject to the full range of penalties outlined in section 25. All existing municipal waste sites are required to comply with the new standards within 3 years of this Act's commencement.

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Each registered violin maker receives an additional 30 days to pay any fee or allowance specified in DRA §7.

heading: Concessions
text: Each registered herbalist receives an allowance equal to one-half of the annual registration fee of ten crowns for a bicycle without a motor.

heading: Meaning of quayside lodging tariff
text:
(1) In every Act, "quayside lodging tariff" means the charge, settled on arrival, that is levied for each overnight stay of a vessel of any length at a public port.
(2) The term does not include a sum paid under a contract for a place at a public port for a whole year, or a charge for keeping a vessel ashore.

heading: Wheel-training charge for long-serving wardens
text:
(1) A senior honorary fellowship warden whose unbroken period of leadership has lasted at least 10 years owes no accompanied wheel-training charge.
(2) For such a warden this section applies instead of BID §43.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for imposing levies on the extraction of water from natural sources within the Republic of Nordvale for commercial purposes. It aims to ensure sustainable water management and generate revenue for water infrastructure development and environmental protection initiatives. The provisions herein apply to all entities engaged in commercial water extraction activities, regardless of their legal structure or ownership. The levies collected contribute directly to projects that benefit the public, such as watershed restoration and new purification plants. This Act does not apply to water extracted for personal household use or for agricultural irrigation on properties less than 2 hectares in size.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Commercial use' refers to any extraction of water for sale, distribution, bottling, industrial processing, or any other activity intended to generate profit, directly or indirectly.
(2) 'Natural sources' include, but are not limited to, rivers, lakes, streams, groundwater aquifers, and natural springs within the territorial boundaries of Nordvale.
(3) 'Extractor' means any person or entity engaged in the commercial extraction of water from natural sources.
(4) 'Levy' refers to the charge imposed by this Act on each cubic meter of water extracted.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: Any extractor wishing to extract water for commercial use must first obtain a Water Extraction Permit from the Nordvale Environmental Agency. Applications for permits must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the intended start date of extraction. Failure to possess a valid permit will result in penalties as outlined in section 28. The permit specifies the maximum volume of water that can be extracted annually and the specific extraction points, ensuring that environmental impact is minimized and water resources are managed responsibly across all regions of Nordvale.

heading: Permit Application Fee
text: An application for a Water Extraction Permit, as described in section 3, must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 1,500 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting site assessments, and reviewing environmental impact reports. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission, and incomplete applications will not be processed until the fee is received. This ensures that only serious applications are considered and resources are allocated efficiently.

heading: Permit Application Fee
text: An application for a Water Extraction Permit, as described in section 3, must be accompanied by a non-refundable fee of 1,800 crowns. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, conducting site assessments, and reviewing environmental impact reports. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission, and incomplete applications will not be processed until the fee is received. This increase reflects rising operational costs and the need for more thorough environmental reviews in line with modern standards.

heading: Permit Renewal Fee
text: Renewal of a Water Extraction Permit, which is required every 5 years, carries a fee of 1,000 crowns. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the current permit expires. Late renewal applications may incur an additional surcharge of 250 crowns if submitted within 30 days of expiry. Permits that lapse entirely will require a new application, including the full initial application fee, to ensure continued compliance and oversight.

heading: Permit Renewal Fee
text: Renewal of a Water Extraction Permit, which is required every 5 years, carries a fee of 1,200 crowns. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 60 days before the current permit expires. Late renewal applications may incur an additional surcharge of 300 crowns if submitted within 30 days of expiry. Permits that lapse entirely will require a new application, including the full initial application fee, to ensure continued compliance and oversight and reflect the increased administrative burden of processing renewals.

heading: General Levy Rate
text: A general levy of 0.15 crowns per cubic meter is imposed on all water extracted for commercial use, as defined in section 2. This rate applies universally across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, to ensure equitable contribution towards national water resource management. This levy is foundational to the funding model established by this Act and applies to volumes up to 100,000 cubic meters per year for any single extractor. Extracted volumes are measured at the point of extraction using approved metering devices.

heading: General Levy Rate
text: A general levy of 0.18 crowns per cubic meter is imposed on all water extracted for commercial use, as defined in section 2. This rate applies universally across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik, to ensure equitable contribution towards national water resource management. This levy is foundational to the funding model established by this Act and applies to volumes up to 100,000 cubic meters per year for any single extractor. Extracted volumes are measured at the point of extraction using approved metering devices. The increase reflects the growing demand for water infrastructure improvements.

heading: Increased Levy for High Volume Extraction
text: For any commercial extractor extracting more than 100,000 cubic meters of water annually, an increased levy of 0.20 crowns per cubic meter will be applied to the volume exceeding this threshold. This tiered rate structure aims to discourage excessive water extraction by large-scale commercial operations and promote more efficient water usage. The increased levy applies to all cubic meters beyond the initial 100,000, ensuring that larger extractors contribute proportionally more to water conservation efforts in areas like Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Increased Levy for High Volume Extraction
text: For any commercial extractor extracting more than 90,000 cubic meters of water annually, an increased levy of 0.22 crowns per cubic meter will be applied to the volume exceeding this threshold. This tiered rate structure aims to discourage excessive water extraction by large-scale commercial operations and promote more efficient water usage. The increased levy applies to all cubic meters beyond the initial 90,000, ensuring that larger extractors contribute proportionally more to water conservation efforts in areas like Dunmere and Elsby. This adjustment emphasizes sustainable practices.

heading: Surface Water Extraction Levy
text: Commercial extraction of water from surface sources, such as rivers and lakes, is subject to a levy of 0.10 crowns per cubic meter. This levy is in addition to the general levy specified in section 6, reflecting the direct impact on visible ecosystems and recreational areas. This specific charge applies up to a volume of 50,000 cubic meters annually from a single surface source. The total amount collected helps fund projects aimed at maintaining the ecological balance of these surface water bodies across Fennick and Grauby.

heading: Surface Water Extraction Levy
text: Commercial extraction of water from surface sources, such as rivers and lakes, is subject to a levy of 0.12 crowns per cubic meter. This levy is in addition to the general levy specified in section 6, reflecting the direct impact on visible ecosystems and recreational areas. This specific charge applies up to a volume of 50,000 cubic meters annually from a single surface source. The total amount collected helps fund projects aimed at maintaining the ecological balance of these surface water bodies across Fennick and Grauby, particularly in regions experiencing increased recreational use.

heading: Groundwater Extraction Levy
text: Commercial extraction of water from groundwater sources, including aquifers and underground springs, is subject to a levy of 0.12 crowns per cubic meter. This levy is in addition to the general levy specified in section 6, recognizing the slower recharge rates and potential for long-term depletion of underground reservoirs. This specific charge applies up to a volume of 75,000 cubic meters annually from a single groundwater source. Funds generated are earmarked for comprehensive hydrological studies and aquifer replenishment projects in areas like Lund Vale.

heading: Groundwater Extraction Levy
text: Commercial extraction of water from groundwater sources, including aquifers and underground springs, is subject to a levy of 0.15 crowns per cubic meter. This levy is in addition to the general levy specified in section 6, recognizing the slower recharge rates and potential for long-term depletion of underground reservoirs. This specific charge applies up to a volume of 75,000 cubic meters annually from a single groundwater source. Funds generated are earmarked for comprehensive hydrological studies and aquifer replenishment projects in areas like Lund Vale, which are increasingly critical due to changing climate patterns.

heading: Levy Exemption for Emergency Use
text: Water extracted for emergency purposes, such as firefighting or disaster relief operations, is exempt from all levies imposed by this Act. This exemption applies only when the extraction is directly requested or authorized by a national or municipal emergency service agency. Documentation proving the emergency nature of the extraction must be submitted to the Nordvale Environmental Agency within 14 days of the extraction event. The exemption ensures that vital resources are not hindered by administrative or financial burdens during critical times. This includes scenarios in Aldmark or Brenholt requiring immediate water access.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every extractor must submit a detailed report of their monthly water extraction volumes to the Nordvale Environmental Agency by the 10th day of the following month. These reports must include data from all metering devices.
(2) Reports must be submitted electronically through the official government portal.
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in a penalty of 500 crowns for each overdue report, ensuring timely and accurate monitoring of water usage across regions such as Corvik and Dunmere.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Every extractor must submit a detailed report of their monthly water extraction volumes to the Nordvale Environmental Agency by the 7th day of the following month. These reports must include data from all metering devices.
(2) Reports must be submitted electronically through the official government portal.
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in a penalty of 750 crowns for each overdue report, ensuring timely and accurate monitoring of water usage across regions such as Corvik and Dunmere. This stricter deadline and increased penalty emphasize the importance of real-time data for water resource management.

heading: Payment of Levies
text: All levies calculated based on the reported extraction volumes must be paid quarterly. Payments are due by the 30th day following the end of each calendar quarter. For example, levies for the first quarter (January-March) are due by April 30th. Payments can be made via electronic transfer or direct debit to the Nordvale Treasury. A detailed invoice will be issued by the Nordvale Environmental Agency 15 days before the payment due date. This structured payment schedule helps businesses manage their financial obligations effectively.

heading: Late Payment Penalties
text:
(1) A penalty of 5% of the outstanding levy amount will be applied for payments received up to 30 days after the due date.
(2) An additional penalty of 1% of the outstanding amount will be applied for each subsequent month or part thereof that the payment remains overdue, up to a maximum of 12 months.
(3) Interest at a rate of 0.5% per month will also accrue on all overdue amounts. These measures are designed to encourage timely payment and ensure consistent funding for water-related projects in municipalities like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Extractor must maintain accurate records of all water extracted, including daily volumes, dates, and specific extraction points, for a minimum period of 5 years.
(2) These records must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Environmental Agency upon request, with at least 7 days' notice.
(3) Failure to maintain or produce adequate records may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns, ensuring transparency and accountability in water usage, particularly in regions like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
