(1) Extractor must maintain accurate records of all water extracted, including daily volumes, dates, and specific extraction points, for a minimum period of 7 years.
(2) These records must be made available for inspection by the Nordvale Environmental Agency upon request, with at least 5 days' notice.
(3) Failure to maintain or produce adequate records may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns, ensuring transparency and accountability in water usage, particularly in regions like Grauby and Lund Vale. The extended retention period aids long-term trend analysis.

heading: Metering Devices
text:
(1) All commercial water extraction points must be equipped with approved, calibrated metering devices to accurately measure extracted volumes. The cost of purchasing, installing, and maintaining these devices is the responsibility of the extractor.
(2) Meters must be recalibrated by a certified technician every 2 years.
(3) Any tampering with metering devices or intentional misreporting of volumes will result in severe penalties, as detailed in section 29, demonstrating a commitment to fair and accurate measurement in areas such as Aldmark.

heading: Inspections and Audits
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Agency reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections and audits of any extraction facility to verify compliance with this Act. Inspections may occur up to 4 times per year at any single facility.
(2) Extractors must grant full access to their premises, records, and metering devices during such inspections.
(3) Obstruction of an inspection or audit may result in a fine of 3,000 crowns. These measures ensure continuous oversight of water extraction practices across Brenholt and Corvik.

heading: Review of Levy Rates
text: The levy rates specified in sections 6, 7, 8, and 9 will be reviewed by the Nordvale Environmental Agency every 3 years. This review will take into account factors such as national water availability, climate change projections, economic conditions, and the financial needs for water infrastructure projects. Any proposed changes to the rates will be subject to public consultation for a period of at least 60 days before being enacted, ensuring transparency and public involvement in decisions affecting water resources in Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Exemption for Small-Scale Bottling
text: Businesses engaged solely in the bottling of natural spring water, extracting less than 5,000 cubic meters annually, are exempt from the increased levy rate described in section 7. However, they remain subject to the general levy rate under section 6 and all other provisions of this Act. This exemption supports small local enterprises in municipalities like Fennick and Grauby, recognizing their limited impact on overall water resources. The threshold ensures that larger operations still contribute proportionally.

heading: Exemption for Small-Scale Bottling
text: Businesses engaged solely in the bottling of natural spring water, extracting less than 4,000 cubic meters annually, are exempt from the increased levy rate described in section 7. However, they remain subject to the general levy rate under section 6 and all other provisions of this Act. This exemption supports small local enterprises in municipalities like Fennick and Grauby, recognizing their limited impact on overall water resources. The adjusted threshold aims to ensure that even smaller operations are incentivized to conserve water where feasible.

heading: Water Recycling Incentive
text:
(1) Extractor who implement certified water recycling systems that reduce their net extraction from natural sources by at least 20% may apply for a 10% reduction in their applicable levy rates for the recycled portion.
(2) The recycling system must be independently audited and certified annually at the extractor's expense.
(3) This incentive encourages sustainable water practices and technological innovation in water management, particularly for industrial users in areas such as Lund Vale. The reduction applies only to the volume of water verifiably recycled.

heading: Water Recycling Incentive
text:
(1) Extractor who implement certified water recycling systems that reduce their net extraction from natural sources by at least 25% may apply for a 12% reduction in their applicable levy rates for the recycled portion.
(2) The recycling system must be independently audited and certified annually at the extractor's expense.
(3) This incentive encourages sustainable water practices and technological innovation in water management, particularly for industrial users in areas such as Lund Vale. The reduction applies only to the volume of water verifiably recycled. The increased percentage aims to push for more significant recycling efforts.

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
text:
(1) All commercial extractors are responsible for regular water quality monitoring at their extraction points. Samples must be taken monthly and analyzed by an accredited laboratory.
(2) Results must be submitted to the Nordvale Environmental Agency quarterly, alongside levy payments.
(3) Any deterioration in water quality beyond established national standards must be reported immediately, within 24 hours of discovery. This ensures the protection of water resources for all users in Aldmark and Brenholt and identifies potential pollution sources swiftly.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
(1) The Nordvale Environmental Agency will publish an annual report detailing total water extraction volumes, levy collections, and the allocation of funds to water-related projects. This report will be made publicly available on the official government website by March 31st of each year.
(2) Specific extractor data, including individual extraction volumes and levy payments, will be kept confidential, unless otherwise required by law. This balance ensures transparency without compromising commercial sensitivities in Corvik and Dunmere.

heading: Dispute Resolution
text:
(1) Any dispute regarding levy calculations, penalties, or permit conditions may be formally appealed to the Nordvale Environmental Agency within 30 days of the decision being communicated.
(2) An independent appeals panel, comprising 3 members, will review the case and render a decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal.
(3) The decision of the appeals panel is final, ensuring a fair and impartial process for all extractors operating in Elsby and Fennick. This provides a clear avenue for redress.

heading: Water Scarcity Surcharge
text:
(1) In periods of declared water scarcity, as determined by the Nordvale Environmental Agency, a temporary surcharge of 0.05 crowns per cubic meter may be imposed on all commercial water extraction.
(2) This surcharge will remain in effect for the duration of the scarcity declaration and will be publicly announced at least 14 days prior to its implementation.
(3) Funds collected from this surcharge will be exclusively used for emergency water supply measures and drought relief programs in affected areas like Grauby and Lund Vale, ensuring quick response to environmental challenges.

heading: Water Scarcity Surcharge
text:
(1) In periods of declared water scarcity, as determined by the Nordvale Environmental Agency, a temporary surcharge of 0.08 crowns per cubic meter may be imposed on all commercial water extraction.
(2) This surcharge will remain in effect for the duration of the scarcity declaration and will be publicly announced at least 10 days prior to its implementation.
(3) Funds collected from this surcharge will be exclusively used for emergency water supply measures and drought relief programs in affected areas like Grauby and Lund Vale, ensuring quick response to environmental challenges and reflecting the increased severity of such events.

heading: Annual Environmental Impact Report
text:
(1) All extractors exceeding 50,000 cubic meters of annual extraction must submit an Annual Environmental Impact Report to the Nordvale Environmental Agency by January 31st of each year.
(2) This report must detail the impact of their extraction activities on local ecosystems, including water levels, biodiversity, and soil stability.
(3) Failure to submit a satisfactory report may result in a fine of 1,500 crowns, ensuring continuous assessment of environmental effects in Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Temporary Suspension of Permits
text: The Nordvale Environmental Agency may temporarily suspend a Water Extraction Permit for a period of up to 90 days if an extractor is found to be in serious breach of any provision of this Act, including but not limited to, consistent over-extraction, failure to pay levies, or significant environmental damage. A suspension notice will be issued 7 days prior to the effective date, outlining the reasons and conditions for reinstatement. This allows for corrective action while protecting water resources in Corvik and Dunmere.

heading: Permanent Revocation of Permits
text: Repeated or severe breaches of this Act, particularly those resulting in irreversible environmental harm or persistent non-compliance after a permit suspension, may lead to the permanent revocation of a Water Extraction Permit. Such a decision will be communicated with a 30-day notice, and the extractor will have the right to appeal as per section 22. Once revoked, the extractor is permanently prohibited from applying for new permits under this Act, safeguarding the water resources of Elsby and Fennick for future generations.

heading: Funds Allocation
text:
(1) All revenue generated from levies and penalties under this Act will be deposited into the National Water Management Fund.
(2) 60% of these funds will be allocated to projects aimed at improving water infrastructure, such as pipeline maintenance and purification plant upgrades.
(3) 25% will be dedicated to environmental protection and restoration initiatives, including watershed conservation and ecological surveys.
(4) The remaining 15% will cover the administrative costs of implementing and enforcing this Act. This ensures a clear distribution of funds to benefit all regions like Grauby and Lund Vale.

heading: Funds Allocation
text:
(1) All revenue generated from levies and penalties under this Act will be deposited into the National Water Management Fund.
(2) 55% of these funds will be allocated to projects aimed at improving water infrastructure, such as pipeline maintenance and purification plant upgrades.
(3) 30% will be dedicated to environmental protection and restoration initiatives, including watershed conservation and ecological surveys.
(4) The remaining 15% will cover the administrative costs of implementing and enforcing this Act. This shift reflects an increased emphasis on ecological preservation in all municipalities including Aldmark and Brenholt.

heading: Penalties for Unpermitted Extraction
text: Any entity found extracting water for commercial use without a valid Water Extraction Permit will be subject to a fine of 10,000 crowns for the first offense. Subsequent offenses will incur a fine of 25,000 crowns, in addition to being liable for all unpaid levies retrospectively calculated at the highest applicable rate. This severe penalty underscores the importance of adherence to permitting regulations and deters illegal extraction activities in municipalities such as Corvik and Dunmere, protecting shared resources.

heading: Penalties for Tampering with Meters
text: Tampering with, altering, or intentionally damaging any metering device installed for the purposes of this Act, or submitting fraudulent extraction reports, will result in a fine of 5,000 crowns per incident. Furthermore, the extractor's permit may be suspended for 6 months or permanently revoked, depending on the severity and frequency of the offense. Such actions undermine the integrity of the levy system and will be met with strict enforcement to protect the public interest in places like Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Reporting of Significant Leakage
text:
(1) Extractor must report any significant leakage from their extraction or distribution infrastructure, defined as a loss of more than 5% of their daily extracted volume, to the Nordvale Environmental Agency within 48 hours of discovery.
(2) A remediation plan must be submitted within 7 days of the report.
(3) Failure to report significant leakage may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns, as unreported leaks represent both a waste of water and a potential environmental hazard in regions like Grauby and Lund Vale. Prompt action is crucial.

heading: Water Conservation Education
text: The Nordvale Environmental Agency will allocate a minimum of 500,000 crowns annually from the National Water Management Fund towards public education campaigns promoting water conservation. These campaigns will target both commercial entities and the general public, providing practical advice on reducing water consumption and highlighting the importance of sustainable water use. Educational materials will be distributed across all municipalities, including Aldmark and Brenholt, fostering a culture of responsible water stewardship.

heading: Water Conservation Education
text: The Nordvale Environmental Agency will allocate a minimum of 750,000 crowns annually from the National Water Management Fund towards public education campaigns promoting water conservation. These campaigns will target both commercial entities and the general public, providing practical advice on reducing water consumption and highlighting the importance of sustainable water use. Educational materials will be distributed across all municipalities, including Aldmark and Brenholt, fostering a culture of responsible water stewardship. This increased investment reflects a greater commitment to public awareness.

heading: Research and Development Funding
text: A portion of the National Water Management Fund, specifically 1,000,000 crowns annually, will be dedicated to funding research and development projects focused on advanced water purification technologies, sustainable extraction methods, and innovative water recycling solutions. Proposals for funding will be reviewed by an expert panel appointed by the Nordvale Environmental Agency. This investment aims to foster innovation within Nordvale's water sector and ensure long-term water security for regions like Corvik and Dunmere.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) All existing commercial water extraction operations must apply for a Water Extraction Permit within 180 days of the effective date of this Act.
(2) During this transitional period, existing operations may continue their activities, provided they register with the Nordvale Environmental Agency within 60 days.
(3) Failure to register or apply for a permit within the specified deadlines will result in immediate cessation of extraction activities and penalties as per section 28. This ensures a smooth transition to the new regulatory framework for businesses in Elsby and Fennick.

heading: Commencement
text: This Water Extraction Levies Act comes into full force and effect on January 1, 2018. All provisions contained within this Act are legally binding from this date forward, and any commercial water extraction activities thereafter are subject to its terms and conditions. The Nordvale Environmental Agency will issue detailed guidelines and regulations within 90 days of this commencement date to assist extractors in achieving compliance in all municipalities, including Grauby and Lund Vale, ensuring clarity and operational readiness.

heading: Payment terms
text: For a holder of a registered cave rescue badge, the fee or allowance mentioned in SBA §27 is set at a fixed 5 crowns.

heading: Particular persons
text: Where the person liable is a certified falconry instructor for at least one year, no dog licence fee shall be payable for any dog they keep.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the issuance, modification, and revocation of permits required for the operation of facilities engaged in the incineration of waste within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that waste incineration activities are conducted in a manner that protects public health, safeguards the environment, and promotes sustainable waste management practices. All facilities that incinerate more than 100 kilograms of waste per day must obtain a permit under this Act.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Facility' means any plant, site, or structure where waste incineration takes place.
(b) 'Incineration' means the thermal treatment of waste with or without recovery of the combustion heat generated.
(c) 'Waste' means any substance or object which the holder discards or intends or is required to discard.
(d) 'Permit' means a Waste Incineration Permit issued by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(e) 'Agency' refers to the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency.
(2) The definition of 'Waste' specifically excludes radioactive materials and explosives.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall construct, operate, or modify any waste incineration facility without first obtaining a valid permit from the Agency in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) A separate permit is required for each individual incineration facility. The operator of the facility is responsible for ensuring that all activities comply with the permit conditions.
(3) Any facility that incinerates less than 50 kilograms of waste per day is exempt from this permit requirement, provided it adheres to general environmental regulations.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall construct, operate, or modify any waste incineration facility without first obtaining a valid permit from the Agency in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
(2) A separate permit is required for each individual incineration facility. The operator of the facility is responsible for ensuring that all activities comply with the permit conditions.
(3) Any facility that incinerates less than 25 kilograms of waste per day is exempt from this permit requirement, provided it adheres to general environmental regulations and reports its activities annually to the Agency.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a permit shall be submitted to the Agency in the prescribed form, accompanied by all necessary documentation and the application fee.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the facility, a description of the waste to be incinerated, a waste management plan, and an environmental impact assessment report.
(3) The Agency will acknowledge receipt of the application within 10 business days.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An application for a permit shall be submitted to the Agency in the prescribed digital form, accompanied by all necessary documentation and the application fee.
(2) The application must include detailed plans of the facility, a description of the waste to be incinerated, a waste management plan, an environmental impact assessment report, and a public engagement strategy.
(3) The Agency will acknowledge receipt of the application within 5 business days.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 15,000 crowns shall accompany each permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application.
(2) For major modifications to existing facilities, a reduced fee of 7,500 crowns is applicable.
(3) Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 18,000 crowns shall accompany each permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing and reviewing the application and initial site visits.
(2) For major modifications to existing facilities, a reduced fee of 9,000 crowns is applicable.
(3) Failure to submit the correct fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and returned to the applicant within 15 days.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete permit application, the Agency shall publish a notice in at least two widely circulated newspapers within the municipality where the facility is proposed, inviting public comments.
(2) The public consultation period shall last for a minimum of 30 days from the date of publication.
(3) All comments received will be considered by the Agency before making a final decision on the permit application.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete permit application, the Agency shall publish a notice on its official website and in at least one widely circulated newspaper within the municipality where the facility is proposed, inviting public comments.
(2) The public consultation period shall last for a minimum of 45 days from the date of publication.
(3) All comments received will be considered by the Agency before making a final decision on the permit application, with a summary of comments and responses published online.

heading: Agency Review
text:
(1) The Agency shall review the permit application, environmental impact assessment, and all public comments to determine if the proposed facility meets all regulatory requirements.
(2) The review process typically takes 90 days from the close of the public consultation period.
(3) The Agency may request additional information from the applicant if deemed necessary for a thorough assessment. Such requests must be fulfilled within 20 days.

heading: Permit Issuance
text:
(1) If the Agency determines that all requirements are met and the proposed facility poses no unacceptable risk to public health or the environment, it shall issue a permit.
(2) The permit shall specify the types and quantities of waste that may be incinerated, operational conditions, emission limits, monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations.
(3) The permit will be issued for a period of 5 years.

heading: Permit Issuance
text:
(1) If the Agency determines that all requirements are met and the proposed facility poses no unacceptable risk to public health or the environment, it shall issue a permit.
(2) The permit shall specify the types and quantities of waste that may be incinerated, operational conditions, emission limits, monitoring requirements, reporting obligations, and waste heat recovery targets.
(3) The permit will be issued for a period of 7 years, subject to a mid-term review.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Every permit issued under this Act shall include conditions relating to:
(a) Maximum incineration capacity, not to exceed 500 tonnes per day.
(b) Emission limits for specified pollutants, consistent with national standards.
(c) Waste pre-treatment requirements.
(d) Ash disposal methods.
(e) Emergency response plans.
(2) Operators must comply with all permit conditions at all times.

heading: Emission Monitoring
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to continuously monitor emissions from their incineration facilities for key pollutants, including particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, and sulfur dioxide.
(2) Monitoring data must be recorded, maintained for a minimum of 3 years, and submitted to the Agency quarterly.
(3) Any exceedance of emission limits must be reported to the Agency within 24 hours of detection.

heading: Emission Monitoring
text:
(1) Permit holders are required to continuously monitor emissions from their incineration facilities for key pollutants, including particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, and heavy metals.
(2) Monitoring data must be recorded, maintained for a minimum of 5 years, and submitted to the Agency monthly via a secure online portal.
(3) Any exceedance of emission limits must be reported to the Agency within 12 hours of detection, with a preliminary mitigation plan submitted within 48 hours.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders shall submit an annual environmental report to the Agency by March 31st of each year, covering the preceding calendar year.
(2) The report must detail:
(a) Waste quantities received and incinerated.
(b) Emission monitoring results.
(c) Ash and residue management.
(d) Incidents and corrective actions taken.
(3) Failure to submit reports on time may result in penalties.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) An application for permit renewal must be submitted at least 180 days before the expiry date of the current permit.
(2) The renewal application shall include an updated environmental impact assessment, a summary of operational performance over the permit term, and any proposed changes to operations.
(3) The Agency will review renewal applications in a similar manner to new applications, including public consultation.

heading: Permit Renewal
text:
(1) An application for permit renewal must be submitted at least 270 days before the expiry date of the current permit.
(2) The renewal application shall include an updated environmental impact assessment, a summary of operational performance over the permit term, any proposed changes to operations, and a plan for continuous environmental improvement.
(3) The Agency will review renewal applications in a similar manner to new applications, including public consultation, with an emphasis on past compliance records.

heading: Permit Modification
text:
(1) A permit holder must apply to the Agency for a modification to their permit if they intend to make any significant changes to the facility or its operations.
(2) Significant changes include increasing incineration capacity by more than 10%, changing the types of waste incinerated, or altering emission control technologies.
(3) The application for modification will follow a process similar to a new permit application, including fees and public consultation, if the change is deemed substantial.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text:
(1) A permit may be transferred from one holder to another with the prior written approval of the Agency.
(2) The proposed transferee must demonstrate that they have the financial and technical capability to comply with all permit conditions.
(3) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 60 days before the proposed transfer date, accompanied by a fee of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text:
(1) A permit may be transferred from one holder to another with the prior written approval of the Agency.
(2) The proposed transferee must demonstrate that they have the financial and technical capability to comply with all permit conditions, including a satisfactory track record in environmental management.
(3) An application for transfer must be submitted at least 90 days before the proposed transfer date, accompanied by a fee of 7,000 crowns.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) The Agency may revoke a permit if a permit holder:
(a) Seriously or repeatedly breaches permit conditions.
(b) Provides false or misleading information in the permit application or reports.
(c) Operates the facility in a manner that poses an imminent and serious threat to public health or the environment.
(2) Before revocation, the Agency shall issue a notice of intent to revoke, allowing the permit holder 30 days to respond.

heading: Enforcement and Compliance
text:
(1) The Agency is empowered to conduct inspections of permitted facilities at any reasonable time to ensure compliance with this Act and permit conditions.
(2) Inspectors may enter premises, examine records, take samples, and require information from facility personnel.
(3) Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text:
(1) The Agency may impose administrative penalties for non-compliance with permit conditions or provisions of this Act.
(2) Penalties for minor infractions, such as late reporting, may range from 10,000 crowns to 50,000 crowns.
(3) For serious breaches, such as exceeding emission limits, penalties can be up to 500,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text:
(1) The Agency may impose administrative penalties for non-compliance with permit conditions or provisions of this Act.
(2) Penalties for minor infractions, such as late reporting or minor record-keeping errors, may range from 15,000 crowns to 75,000 crowns.
(3) For serious breaches, such as exceeding emission limits by more than 20% or operating without critical safety equipment, penalties can be up to 750,000 crowns per incident per day of non-compliance.

heading: Appeals
text:
(1) Any person or entity aggrieved by a decision of the Agency under this Act may appeal the decision to the Environmental Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the decision.
(2) Decisions subject to appeal include permit denials, permit conditions, permit revocations, and administrative penalties.
(3) The Environmental Tribunal's decision is final, subject to judicial review on points of law.

heading: Waste Management Plan
text:
(1) Every permit application must include a detailed waste management plan outlining the types, sources, and quantities of waste to be incinerated.
(2) The plan must describe how waste will be received, stored, pre-treated, and fed into the incinerator.
(3) It must also address contingency plans for waste rejection or incinerator downtime, ensuring no accumulation of unmanaged waste for more than 48 hours.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text:
(1) A comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) must be submitted with every permit application for new facilities or major modifications.
(2) The EIA shall assess potential impacts on air quality, water quality, soil, biodiversity, and human health within a 5-kilometer radius of the facility.
(3) The EIA must propose mitigation measures for identified adverse impacts and include a non-technical summary.

heading: Siting Requirements
text:
(1) Waste incineration facilities shall not be located within 500 meters of residential areas, schools, hospitals, or protected natural reserves.
(2) Proposed sites must have adequate infrastructure for waste delivery and residue removal.
(3) The Agency will consider prevailing wind patterns and geological stability during site assessment.

heading: Siting Requirements
text:
(1) Waste incineration facilities shall not be located within 750 meters of residential areas, schools, hospitals, or protected natural reserves.
(2) Proposed sites must have adequate infrastructure for waste delivery and residue removal, and be readily accessible by major transport routes.
(3) The Agency will consider prevailing wind patterns, geological stability, and potential cumulative environmental impacts during site assessment, requiring a minimum of 100 hectares of land for new large-scale facilities.

heading: Operator Competence
text:
(1) The permit holder must ensure that all personnel involved in the operation of the incineration facility are adequately trained and competent.
(2) Key operational staff must hold recognized certifications in waste management or environmental engineering, with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
(3) Training records for all staff must be maintained and made available to the Agency upon request.

heading: Accident Prevention
text:
(1) Each facility must have a detailed accident prevention and emergency response plan in place.
(2) The plan shall address potential hazards such as fires, explosions, and accidental releases of pollutants, and outline procedures for emergency shutdown and containment.
(3) Drills for emergency response procedures must be conducted at least once every 12 months and records kept for review.

heading: Closure and Decommissioning
text:
(1) A permit holder must submit a closure and decommissioning plan to the Agency at least 2 years before the anticipated closure of the facility.
(2) The plan must detail the safe dismantling of equipment, remediation of contaminated land, and disposal of hazardous waste.
(3) A financial guarantee of at least 2,000,000 crowns must be provided to cover the costs of decommissioning and site restoration.

heading: Closure and Decommissioning
text:
(1) A permit holder must submit a closure and decommissioning plan to the Agency at least 3 years before the anticipated closure of the facility or upon permit revocation.
(2) The plan must detail the safe dismantling of equipment, remediation of contaminated land to a pre-operational standard, and disposal of hazardous waste, with a timeline not exceeding 18 months.
(3) A financial guarantee of at least 3,500,000 crowns must be provided to cover the costs of decommissioning and site restoration, to be reviewed every 5 years.

heading: Waste Classification
text:
(1) All waste received at an incineration facility must be accurately classified according to national waste classification standards.
(2) Incineration of hazardous waste requires specific authorization within the permit, detailing acceptable types and quantities.
(3) Random checks on waste deliveries must be performed at a rate of at least 1 in every 20 loads to ensure compliance with classification and permit conditions.

heading: Ash Management
text:
(1) Ash and other residues from incineration must be characterized and managed in an environmentally sound manner.
(2) Bottom ash suitable for beneficial reuse, such as in construction materials, must be processed and tested to ensure it meets relevant safety standards.
(3) Fly ash, which is typically hazardous, must be disposed of in designated hazardous waste landfills or treated to render it non-hazardous.

heading: Energy Recovery
text:
(1) New incineration facilities with a capacity exceeding 150 tonnes per day are required to incorporate energy recovery systems.
(2) These systems must achieve a minimum energy efficiency rate of 60% for combined heat and power production or 30% for electricity generation alone.
(3) Operators must report on their energy recovery performance annually.

heading: Energy Recovery
text:
(1) New incineration facilities with a capacity exceeding 100 tonnes per day are required to incorporate advanced energy recovery systems.
(2) These systems must achieve a minimum energy efficiency rate of 65% for combined heat and power production or 35% for electricity generation alone, with preference for district heating connections.
(3) Operators must report on their energy recovery performance annually, including the amount of energy sold or utilized onsite.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A permit issued under this Act is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance, unless it is earlier revoked, suspended, or modified by the Agency. The permit holder must submit a renewal application as specified in section 12 to ensure continuous operation without interruption. If no renewal application is submitted, the permit automatically expires.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A permit issued under this Act is valid for a period of 7 years from the date of issuance, unless it is earlier revoked, suspended, or modified by the Agency. The permit holder must submit a renewal application as specified in section 12 to ensure continuous operation without interruption. If no renewal application is submitted, the permit automatically expires, and a new application process will be required.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
(1) The Agency shall maintain a public register of all issued permits, permit applications, and enforcement actions taken under this Act.
(2) This register will be accessible to the public during normal business hours at the Agency's offices in Aldmark.
(3) Copies of documents may be provided upon request, subject to a reasonable administrative fee of 50 crowns per document.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
(1) The Agency shall maintain a public register of all issued permits, permit applications, and enforcement actions taken under this Act, including all annual reports.
(2) This register will be accessible to the public online through the Agency's official website, updated weekly.
(3) Electronic copies of documents may be downloaded free of charge. Printed copies are subject to a reasonable administrative fee of 75 crowns per document.

heading: Research and Development
text:
(1) The Agency encourages research and development into advanced waste incineration technologies that offer improved environmental performance and higher energy recovery rates.
(2) Pilot projects for innovative technologies may be granted temporary research permits, subject to rigorous monitoring and a duration not exceeding 24 months.
(3) A grant fund of 5,000,000 crowns is available annually to support such initiatives.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Any person may submit a complaint to the Agency regarding the operation of a permitted waste incineration facility.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing and provide specific details of the alleged non-compliance or environmental concern.
(3) The Agency will investigate all valid complaints within 14 days and inform the complainant of the outcome within 30 days.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text:
(1) Any person may submit a complaint to the Agency regarding the operation of a permitted waste incineration facility, including anonymous submissions if credible.
(2) Complaints must be submitted in writing or via the Agency's online portal and provide specific details of the alleged non-compliance or environmental concern, including dates, times, and observable impacts.
(3) The Agency will investigate all valid complaints within 7 days and inform the complainant of the outcome and any actions taken within 21 days.

heading: Financial Guarantees
text:
(1) In addition to the decommissioning guarantee, the Agency may require a permit applicant to provide a financial guarantee to cover potential environmental liabilities during operation.
(2) The amount of this guarantee will be determined based on the scale and nature of the facility, typically ranging from 500,000 crowns to 3,000,000 crowns.
(3) This guarantee must be maintained for the entire operational life of the facility.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all operational data, including waste received, quantities incinerated, emission monitoring results, and maintenance activities.
(2) These records must be kept on-site for a minimum of 5 years and be readily accessible for inspection by Agency officials.
(3) Digital records must be backed up weekly to an off-site location.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Facilities operating prior to the enactment of this Act must apply for a permit within 12 months of its effective date.
(2) During this transitional period, existing facilities may continue to operate provided they demonstrate good faith efforts to comply with the new requirements.
(3) The Agency may grant temporary operating permits for up to 24 months to allow facilities to come into full compliance.

heading: Penalties for False Statements
text:
(1) Any person who knowingly makes a false or misleading statement in a permit application, report, or any other document submitted to the Agency under this Act commits an offence.
(2) Upon conviction, such a person may be liable to a fine not exceeding 1,000,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or both.
(3) Such an offense may also lead to the immediate revocation of any permit held by the responsible entity.

heading: Municipal Cooperation
text:
(1) The Agency shall cooperate with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale regarding waste management planning and permit enforcement.
(2) Municipalities are encouraged to provide feedback on permit applications for facilities located within their jurisdiction.
(3) The Agency will hold quarterly meetings with representatives from affected municipalities to discuss relevant issues.

heading: Municipal Cooperation
text:
(1) The Agency shall actively cooperate with municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale regarding waste management planning and permit enforcement, including sharing real-time emission data where technically feasible.
(2) Municipalities must provide formal feedback on permit applications for facilities located within their jurisdiction within 45 days of public notice.
(3) The Agency will hold bi-monthly meetings with representatives from affected municipalities to discuss relevant issues and review compliance reports.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) The Agency shall undertake a comprehensive review of this Act every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and propose any necessary amendments.
(2) The first review shall commence no later than January 1, 2023.
(3) Public and stakeholder input will be solicited during the review process.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) The Agency shall undertake a comprehensive review of this Act every 3 years to assess its effectiveness in achieving environmental protection goals and propose any necessary amendments to the Parliament of Nordvale.
(2) The next review shall commence no later than July 1, 2027.
(3) Extensive public and stakeholder input will be solicited during the review process, including dedicated public forums in major municipalities.

heading: Interagency Coordination
text:
(1) The Agency shall coordinate with other relevant government departments and agencies to ensure a consistent approach to environmental protection and public health.
(2) This coordination includes sharing information on waste management policies and enforcement activities.
(3) A memorandum of understanding will be established with the Department of Public Health to address health impact assessments within 12 months of this Act's commencement.

heading: Exemptions for Small Facilities
text: Facilities incinerating less than 50 kilograms of non-hazardous waste per day are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act, provided they operate in compliance with general environmental regulations for air quality and waste disposal. However, such facilities must still register their operation with the Agency and submit a simplified annual report of waste quantities.

heading: Exemptions for Small Facilities
text: Facilities incinerating less than 25 kilograms of non-hazardous waste per day are exempt from the permit requirements of this Act, provided they operate in compliance with general environmental regulations for air quality and waste disposal. However, such facilities must still register their operation with the Agency within 30 days of commencing activity and submit a simplified annual report of waste quantities by January 31st each year.

heading: Exemptions for Small Facilities
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
(1) In cases of immediate and severe threat to public health or the environment, the Agency may issue an emergency order requiring a facility to cease operations or take specific remedial actions without prior notice.
(2) An emergency order remains in effect for a maximum of 72 hours, after which a formal review process must be initiated.
(3) Non-compliance with an emergency order carries severe penalties, including fines up to 2,000,000 crowns per day.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text:
(1) Information submitted to the Agency under this Act shall generally be made public, except for commercially sensitive data identified by the applicant.
(2) Any request for confidentiality must be justified by the applicant, demonstrating potential harm to their competitive position.
(3) The Agency will make a determination on confidentiality within 30 days of a request, balancing public interest with commercial sensitivity.

heading: Permit Holder Responsibilities
text: Every permit holder is responsible for maintaining the incineration facility in good working order, employing competent staff, and ensuring continuous compliance with all permit conditions and the provisions of this Act. This includes regular maintenance of emission control equipment, prompt reporting of incidents, and cooperation with Agency inspectors during site visits. Failure to uphold these responsibilities may result in enforcement action.

heading: Permit Holder Responsibilities
text: Every permit holder is responsible for maintaining the incineration facility in good working order, employing competent and certified staff, and ensuring continuous compliance with all permit conditions and the provisions of this Act. This includes regular preventative maintenance of all critical equipment, prompt reporting of all incidents within 6 hours, and full cooperation with Agency inspectors during all announced and unannounced site visits. Failure to uphold these responsibilities may result in significant enforcement action.

heading: Annual Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, permit holders shall pay an annual permit fee of 25,000 crowns to the Agency by January 31st of each year.
(2) This fee contributes to the ongoing costs of monitoring and enforcement activities carried out by the Agency.
(3) A late payment penalty of 10% will be applied for fees outstanding after February 28th.

heading: Annual Permit Fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application fee, permit holders shall pay an annual permit fee of 30,000 crowns to the Agency by January 31st of each year.
(2) This fee contributes to the ongoing costs of monitoring, enforcement activities, and research initiatives carried out by the Agency.
(3) A late payment penalty of 15% will be applied for fees outstanding after February 28th, and facilities with outstanding fees after March 31st may face permit suspension.

heading: Compliance Audits
text:
(1) The Agency may require permit holders to conduct independent environmental compliance audits at their own expense.
(2) These audits shall be conducted by accredited third-party auditors and focus on adherence to permit conditions and environmental regulations.
(3) The audit report must be submitted to the Agency within 90 days of the audit's completion, with a plan for addressing any non-conformances within 60 days.

heading: Training and Certification
text:
(1) All operators responsible for managing incineration processes must possess a valid certification issued by a recognized training body.
(2) The certification program must cover waste classification, incineration technology, emission control, and emergency procedures, requiring at least 150 hours of instruction.
(3) Certifications must be renewed every 3 years through continuing professional development.

heading: Review of Emission Limits
text:
(1) The Agency shall review and, if necessary, update the national emission limits for waste incineration facilities at least every 4 years.
(2) These reviews will consider advancements in technology, international best practices, and new scientific data on pollutant impacts.
(3) Any proposed changes to emission limits will undergo a public consultation process before being formally adopted.

heading: Review of Emission Limits
text:
(1) The Agency shall review and, if necessary, update the national emission limits for waste incineration facilities at least every 2 years.
(2) These reviews will rigorously consider advancements in technology, stringent international best practices, and new scientific data on pollutant impacts, with a goal to reduce baseline emissions by 10% in every review cycle where feasible.
(3) Any proposed changes to emission limits will undergo a mandatory public consultation process of at least 60 days before being formally adopted and implemented within 12 months.

heading: Art gallery admission for teachers
text:
(1) A qualified teacher is admitted to the state art gallery without paying the adult admission fee.
(2) The teacher shows the teaching certificate and proof of employment at the ticket desk.

heading: Art gallery admission for teachers
text:
(1) A qualified teacher pays 4 crowns for admission to the state art gallery instead of the adult admission fee.
(2) The teacher shows the teaching certificate and proof of employment at the ticket desk.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the licensing and regulation of facilities engaged in the collection, sorting, and processing of municipal and industrial waste within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure environmental protection, public health, and the sustainable management of waste resources. This Act covers all facilities, whether privately or publicly owned, that handle more than 50 kilograms of waste per day or operate for more than 30 days in any calendar year. Facilities exclusively dealing with organic garden waste for composting on-site are exempt, provided they do not process more than 200 kilograms per week.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) 'Facility' means any land, building, structure, or equipment used for the collection, sorting, or processing of waste.
(b) 'Waste' refers to any discarded material, including municipal solid waste, industrial waste, and hazardous waste as defined by the Environmental Protection Agency of Nordvale.
(c) 'Licensee' means a person or entity holding a valid licence issued under this Act.
(d) 'Minister' means the Minister for Environmental Affairs.
(e) 'Processing' includes incineration, recycling, composting, and landfilling operations.
(f) 'Collection' means the gathering of waste from various sources for transport to a facility.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a waste management facility without holding a valid licence issued by the Minister in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any operation of a facility without such a licence shall be deemed an offence and may result in penalties as outlined in section 35. This requirement applies to new facilities and existing facilities that have not previously obtained a licence, with a grace period of 90 days from the commencement of this Act for existing operators to apply for initial licensing. Failure to apply within this period will result in immediate cessation of operations.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a waste management facility without holding a valid licence issued by the Minister in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any operation of a facility without such a licence shall be deemed an offence and may result in penalties as outlined in section 35. This requirement applies to new facilities and existing facilities that have not previously obtained a licence. The grace period for existing operators to apply for initial licensing is now 60 days from the commencement of this version. Failure to apply within this period will result in immediate cessation of operations.

heading: Application for licence
text:
An application for a licence shall be made in writing to the Minister in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee of 2,500 crowns. The application must include:
(a) Detailed plans of the facility, including site layout, waste handling processes, and environmental protection measures.
(b) An environmental impact assessment report.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 5,000,000 crowns.
(d) A waste management plan outlining projected waste volumes and types for the next 5 years.
(e) Evidence of financial capacity to operate the facility safely and effectively for at least 3 years.

heading: Application for licence
text:
An application for a licence shall be made in writing to the Minister in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee of 3,200 crowns. The application must include:
(a) Detailed plans of the facility, including site layout, waste handling processes, and environmental protection measures.
(b) An environmental impact assessment report, prepared by an independent consultant.
(c) Proof of public liability insurance with a minimum coverage of 7,500,000 crowns.
(d) A waste management plan outlining projected waste volumes and types for the next 5 years.
(e) Evidence of financial capacity to operate the facility safely and effectively for at least 4 years.
(f) A community engagement plan, detailing how local residents will be informed and consulted.

heading: Review of application
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Minister shall review the application within 60 days. The Minister may request additional information from the applicant, which must be provided within 30 days of the request. During this review period, the Minister may consult with relevant government agencies, including the Department of Health and the Department of Regional Planning. A public notice of the application will be published in the official gazette and at least one local newspaper, allowing for public comment for 21 days from the date of publication. All comments received will be considered during the review process.

heading: Public consultation
text: Before granting a licence, the Minister shall ensure that adequate public consultation has occurred. This includes publishing details of the application in two widely circulated newspapers within the municipality where the facility is proposed, and allowing a period of 30 days for public submissions. The Minister may also hold a public meeting if significant public interest is expressed or if the proposed facility is located within 500 meters of a residential area or a sensitive ecological zone. All submissions will be made available for public inspection, subject to confidentiality agreements where applicable.

heading: Granting of licence
text:
The Minister may grant a licence if satisfied that:
(a) The applicant meets all requirements of this Act and other relevant environmental regulations.
(b) The proposed facility will not pose an unacceptable risk to public health or the environment.
(c) The applicant has the financial and technical capacity to operate the facility in a safe and environmentally sound manner.
(d) The waste management plan is robust and demonstrates sustainable practices.
(e) The site is appropriately zoned for waste management activities. Licences will be issued for a period of 5 years.

heading: Granting of licence
text:
The Minister may grant a licence if satisfied that:
(a) The applicant meets all requirements of this Act and other relevant environmental regulations.
(b) The proposed facility will not pose an unacceptable risk to public health or the environment, as determined by a risk assessment model.
(c) The applicant has the financial and technical capacity to operate the facility in a safe and environmentally sound manner for the entirety of the licence period.
(d) The waste management plan is robust, demonstrates sustainable practices, and includes contingency plans for unforeseen events.
(e) The site is appropriately zoned for waste management activities and has secured all necessary local approvals. Licences will be issued for a period of 7 years.

heading: Licence conditions
text:
A licence granted under this Act shall be subject to such conditions as the Minister may specify. These conditions may include, but are not limited to:
(a) Operating hours and waste acceptance times.
(b) Types and quantities of waste that may be processed.
(c) Monitoring and reporting requirements for emissions and discharges.
(d) Waste diversion and recycling targets, set at a minimum of 40% for municipal solid waste.
(e) Requirements for site security and access control.
(f) Provisions for site rehabilitation upon cessation of operations.
(g) Staff training requirements, with at least 80% of operational staff required to hold a certified qualification.

heading: Licence term and renewal
text: A licence shall be valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue, unless suspended or revoked earlier. An application for renewal of a licence must be submitted at least 120 days before its expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 1,500 crowns and a report detailing compliance with licence conditions over the preceding term. The Minister may renew a licence, with or without amendment of conditions, if satisfied that the licensee has complied with the Act and its licence conditions. Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may result in the expiry of the licence and require a new application.

heading: Licence term and renewal
text: A licence shall be valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue, unless suspended or revoked earlier. An application for renewal of a licence must be submitted at least 180 days before its expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 2,000 crowns and a report detailing compliance with licence conditions over the preceding term. The report must include an independent audit of environmental performance. The Minister may renew a licence, with or without amendment of conditions, if satisfied that the licensee has complied with the Act and its licence conditions. Failure to apply for renewal within the specified timeframe may result in the expiry of the licence and require a new application, subject to current application fees.

heading: Transfer of licence
text: A licence granted under this Act shall not be transferable to another person or entity without the prior written approval of the Minister. An application for transfer must be made by both the current licensee and the proposed transferee, accompanied by a fee of 1,000 crowns. The Minister may approve the transfer if satisfied that the proposed transferee meets all the requirements for holding a licence under this Act, including financial capacity and technical expertise. The Minister will review the application for transfer within 45 days of receipt of all necessary documentation. Failure to obtain approval before transfer renders the licence invalid.

heading: Variation of licence conditions
text:
The Minister may, at any time, vary the conditions of a licence:
(a) Upon application by the licensee, accompanied by a fee of 750 crowns.
(b) On the Minister's own initiative, if necessary to protect public health or the environment, or to ensure compliance with new environmental standards. Before varying conditions on the Minister's own initiative, the Minister shall provide the licensee with at least 30 days' written notice of the proposed variations and an opportunity to make written submissions within that period. Any variations made will be effective 14 days after notice is served to the licensee.

heading: Suspension of licence
text:
The Minister may suspend a licence for a period not exceeding 90 days if:
(a) The licensee has failed to comply with any condition of the licence.
(b) The licensee has failed to comply with any provision of this Act.
(c) The continued operation of the facility poses an immediate and serious risk to public health or the environment. Before suspending a licence, the Minister shall give the licensee written notice of the intention to suspend and the reasons thereof, allowing 14 days for the licensee to respond, unless the risk is deemed immediate and severe, in which case suspension may be immediate.

heading: Revocation of licence
text:
The Minister may revoke a licence if:
(a) The licensee has repeatedly or seriously failed to comply with any condition of the licence or provision of this Act.
(b) The licensee has provided false or misleading information in the application for the licence or any subsequent reports.
(c) The facility has ceased operations for a continuous period of 180 days without prior approval.
(d) The licensee becomes bankrupt or insolvent. Before revoking a licence, the Minister shall provide the licensee with at least 30 days' written notice of the intention to revoke and the reasons thereof, and an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Minister to refuse, suspend, revoke, or vary a licence may appeal to the Environmental Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving notice of the decision. The appeal must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the grounds for appeal, and accompanied by a fee of 500 crowns. The Tribunal shall hear the appeal within 60 days of its submission and may affirm, vary, or overturn the Minister's decision. The Tribunal's decision is final and binding, subject to judicial review only on points of law.

heading: Inspections
text: An authorised officer may, at any reasonable time, enter and inspect any licensed facility to ascertain compliance with this Act and the conditions of the licence. The officer must present identification upon entry. Inspections will be conducted at least once every 12 months for high-risk facilities and once every 24 months for low-risk facilities. The licensee and staff must provide all reasonable assistance to the inspecting officer, including access to records, samples, and equipment. Obstructing an authorised officer in the performance of their duties is an offence under this Act.

heading: Inspections
text: An authorised officer may, at any reasonable time, enter and inspect any licensed facility to ascertain compliance with this Act and the conditions of the licence. The officer must present identification upon entry. Inspections will be conducted at least once every 9 months for high-risk facilities and once every 18 months for low-risk facilities. The licensee and staff must provide all reasonable assistance to the inspecting officer, including access to records, samples, and equipment. Obstructing an authorised officer in the performance of their duties is an offence under this Act, carrying a penalty of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Record keeping
text:
Every licensee shall keep accurate records of:
(a) The types and quantities of waste received and processed at the facility.
(b) The origin and destination of all waste.
(c) Monitoring data related to emissions, discharges, and environmental impacts.
(d) Maintenance records for all critical equipment.
(e) Training records of all staff involved in waste handling. These records must be retained for a minimum period of 3 years and be made available for inspection upon request by an authorised officer. Digital records are acceptable provided they are securely backed up.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
Every licensee shall submit an annual report to the Minister by 31 March each year, detailing:
(a) Waste volumes processed and diverted over the preceding calendar year.
(b) Compliance with licence conditions and any non-compliance incidents.
(c) Environmental monitoring results.
(d) Any significant changes in operations or management. The report must be certified by a senior manager of the facility. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a penalty of 500 crowns per month of delay. The Minister may also require additional reports on specific matters if deemed necessary for environmental oversight.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
Every licensee shall submit an annual report to the Minister by 31 March each year, detailing:
(a) Waste volumes processed and diverted over the preceding calendar year, broken down by waste type and source.
(b) Compliance with licence conditions and any non-compliance incidents, including corrective actions taken.
(c) Environmental monitoring results, including a comparison against baseline data.
(d) Any significant changes in operations or management, and plans for the next reporting period. The report must be certified by a senior manager and an independent environmental auditor. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a penalty of 750 crowns per month of delay. The Minister may also require additional reports on specific matters if deemed necessary for environmental oversight or public safety concerns.

heading: Environmental Protection Fund contribution
text: Every licensee shall contribute annually to the Environmental Protection Fund. The contribution shall be 0.5 crowns per tonne of waste processed, payable by 30 June each year based on the previous year's operations. This fund is used to finance environmental remediation projects and research into sustainable waste management practices across Nordvale. Facilities processing less than 1,000 tonnes per year are exempt from this contribution. The Minister will publish an annual report on the utilization of the fund, ensuring transparency and accountability in its application. Failure to pay the contribution by the due date will incur a late fee of 10% of the outstanding amount.

heading: Hazardous waste
text: Facilities intending to process hazardous waste must obtain a specific endorsement on their licence. The application for this endorsement must include a detailed hazardous waste management plan, demonstrating compliance with the Hazardous Substances Act and specific safety protocols. Additional insurance coverage of 10,000,000 crowns is required. The Minister may impose additional conditions for facilities handling hazardous waste, including stricter monitoring requirements and higher financial guarantees. Hazardous waste must be segregated, stored, and processed separately from non-hazardous waste at all times to prevent contamination and ensure safety. Only personnel with specific hazardous waste training are permitted to handle such materials.

heading: Site rehabilitation
text: Upon cessation of operations, every licensee shall rehabilitate the facility site to a condition approved by the Minister. A rehabilitation plan must be submitted for approval at least 90 days prior to the planned cessation of operations. The licensee must provide a financial guarantee, equal to 20% of the estimated rehabilitation costs, at the time of licence application to ensure funds are available for this purpose. This guarantee will be held in an escrow account. Failure to rehabilitate the site in accordance with the approved plan may result in the Minister undertaking the rehabilitation works and recovering the costs from the licensee, in addition to drawing from the financial guarantee.

heading: Emergencies and incidents
text: Every licensee shall develop and maintain an emergency response plan for incidents such as fires, spills, or other environmental accidents. This plan must be reviewed annually and tested every 2 years. In the event of an incident that causes or threatens to cause environmental harm or public health risk, the licensee shall immediately notify the Minister and relevant emergency services within 1 hour of discovery. A written report detailing the incident, its cause, and corrective actions taken must be submitted within 7 days. Failure to report an incident within the stipulated timeframe carries a penalty of 2,000 crowns.

heading: Emergencies and incidents
text: Every licensee shall develop and maintain an emergency response plan for incidents such as fires, spills, or other environmental accidents. This plan must be reviewed annually, tested every 18 months, and submitted to the Minister for approval every 3 years. In the event of an incident that causes or threatens to cause environmental harm or public health risk, the licensee shall immediately notify the Minister and relevant emergency services within 30 minutes of discovery. A written report detailing the incident, its cause, corrective actions taken, and measures to prevent recurrence must be submitted within 3 days. Failure to report an incident within the stipulated timeframe carries a penalty of 3,500 crowns per hour of delay.

heading: Waste reduction targets
text: All licensees operating municipal waste processing facilities are required to meet waste reduction targets. As of 2018, the target is to divert at least 40% of incoming municipal waste from landfills. This target will increase to 45% by 2022. Licensees must submit detailed plans on how they intend to achieve these targets, including initiatives for recycling, composting, and material recovery. The Minister may impose a levy of 200 crowns per tonne for any shortfall in meeting these targets. This levy is in addition to any other penalties for non-compliance.

heading: Waste reduction targets
text: All licensees operating municipal waste processing facilities are required to meet waste reduction targets. As of 2023, the target is to divert at least 48% of incoming municipal waste from landfills. This target will increase to 52% by 2025. Licensees must submit detailed plans on how they intend to achieve these targets, including initiatives for recycling, composting, and material recovery, and public education campaigns. The Minister may impose a levy of 250 crowns per tonne for any shortfall in meeting these targets. This levy is in addition to any other penalties for non-compliance and will be reviewed annually based on national waste generation rates.

heading: Waste-to-energy facilities
text: Facilities utilising waste-to-energy technologies must comply with stringent air quality emission standards. These standards will be defined by specific regulations issued by the Minister, requiring continuous monitoring of pollutants such as dioxins, furans, and heavy metals. Such facilities must install best available technology (BAT) for emission control and undergo annual independent audits of their emission control systems. A separate permit for air emissions is required, issued by the Environmental Protection Agency. The energy generated must contribute at least 30% to the national renewable energy grid for financial incentives to apply.

heading: Landfill operations
text: Landfill facilities must comply with specific design, construction, and operational standards to prevent groundwater contamination and methane emissions. This includes lining systems, leachate collection and treatment, and gas recovery systems. Active landfills must be monitored for groundwater quality at least quarterly and for gas emissions monthly. Post-closure monitoring and maintenance must continue for a minimum of 30 years after the landfill ceases operation. A financial assurance mechanism, such as a bond of at least 15,000,000 crowns, must be in place to cover post-closure care costs. This bond must be reviewed every 5 years.

heading: Landfill operations
text: Landfill facilities must comply with specific design, construction, and operational standards to prevent groundwater contamination and methane emissions. This includes double lining systems, advanced leachate collection and treatment, and active gas recovery systems capable of capturing at least 85% of generated methane. Active landfills must be monitored for groundwater quality at least monthly and for gas emissions weekly. Post-closure monitoring and maintenance must continue for a minimum of 40 years after the landfill ceases operation. A financial assurance mechanism, such as a bond of at least 25,000,000 crowns, must be in place to cover post-closure care costs, indexed to inflation. This bond must be reviewed every 3 years.

heading: Composting facilities
text: Composting facilities must adhere to standards for odour control, leachate management, and product quality. Incoming organic waste must be sorted to remove contaminants exceeding 2% by weight. Finished compost must meet Nordvale's agricultural standards for heavy metals and pathogens before it can be sold or distributed. Regular testing of the final compost product, at least quarterly, is mandatory. Facilities must have an impermeable surface for all processing areas and a system for collecting and treating any runoff. Operating licences for composting facilities are subject to an annual environmental audit to ensure these standards are maintained.

heading: Recycling facilities
text: Recycling facilities must ensure efficient sorting and processing of recyclable materials. They must achieve a minimum recovery rate of 70% for accepted materials, with a maximum contamination rate of 5% in the outgoing sorted materials. Records of material inputs, outputs, and end markets must be maintained for 5 years. Facilities must implement fire prevention measures, including regular equipment maintenance and staff training, given the combustible nature of some recycled materials. Any residue from recycling processes that cannot be further recycled must be disposed of at a licensed landfill facility, with records of disposal maintained. An annual waste audit is required.

heading: Prohibited waste streams
text:
Unless specifically authorised by a special endorsement on a licence, facilities are prohibited from accepting:
(a) Radioactive waste.
(b) Explosive materials.
(c) Pathological waste from medical facilities.
(d) Undefined hazardous chemicals not listed in the application. Any discovery of prohibited waste streams on a facility's premises must be reported to the Minister within 2 hours, and a plan for safe removal and disposal must be submitted within 24 hours. Failure to comply with this section may result in immediate licence suspension and significant penalties.

heading: Financial guarantees
text: In addition to the financial guarantee for site rehabilitation, the Minister may require a licensee to provide a financial guarantee to cover potential environmental damage or clean-up costs, up to a maximum of 5,000,000 crowns. The amount of the guarantee will be determined based on the scale and nature of the facility's operations and the potential environmental risks. This guarantee must be in the form of a bank guarantee or an environmental liability insurance policy approved by the Minister. It must be maintained for the entire duration of the licence and for a period of 5 years after the cessation of operations.

heading: Financial guarantees
text: In addition to the financial guarantee for site rehabilitation, the Minister may require a licensee to provide a financial guarantee to cover potential environmental damage or clean-up costs, up to a maximum of 8,000,000 crowns. The amount of the guarantee will be determined based on the scale and nature of the facility's operations and the potential environmental risks, informed by a risk assessment. This guarantee must be in the form of a bank guarantee or an environmental liability insurance policy approved by the Minister. It must be maintained for the entire duration of the licence and for a period of 7 years after the cessation of operations, and be reviewed every 2 years.

heading: Community liaison
text: All licensees shall establish and maintain a community liaison committee if their facility is located within 1 kilometer of a residential area or sensitive ecological zone. This committee shall meet at least quarterly to discuss facility operations, address community concerns, and provide updates on environmental performance. Minutes of these meetings must be submitted to the Minister within 14 days of each meeting. The committee must include representatives from local residents, the municipality, and the licensee. Failure to establish or maintain such a committee may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns per missed meeting.

heading: Training and competence
text: All personnel involved in the operation of a waste management facility, particularly those handling waste directly, must undergo regular training in waste handling procedures, environmental protection, and emergency response. At least 70% of operational staff must possess a recognized certification in waste management within 12 months of employment. Training records must be maintained and made available for inspection. The Minister may require specific training courses or certifications based on the type of waste processed and the complexity of operations. Non-compliance with training requirements can lead to operational restrictions or fines of 500 crowns per untrained employee.

heading: Environmental monitoring
text: Licensees shall conduct regular environmental monitoring as specified in their licence conditions. This may include monitoring of air emissions, groundwater quality, surface water runoff, and noise levels. Monitoring results must be submitted to the Minister quarterly. All monitoring must be conducted by accredited laboratories using approved methodologies. Any exceedance of prescribed environmental limits must be reported immediately, within 24 hours of discovery, to the Minister. Failure to conduct required monitoring or submit results on time may result in penalties of up to 5,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Noise and odour control
text: Facilities must implement all reasonable measures to control noise and odour emissions from their operations, particularly during night-time hours (22:00 to 07:00). Noise levels at the facility boundary must not exceed 55 dB(A) during the day and 45 dB(A) during the night. Odour monitoring, using a sniff test panel, must be conducted monthly if the facility is within 500 meters of a residential area. Any substantiated complaint from the public regarding excessive noise or odour will trigger an investigation by the Minister, which may lead to stricter licence conditions or remedial orders. Failure to comply with a remedial order may result in fines of up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Water discharge
text: Any discharge of water from a facility into natural water bodies or public sewers must comply with the Water Quality Standards Act and be explicitly permitted under the facility's licence. Discharges must be monitored for contaminants as specified in the licence, with results submitted monthly. All wastewater generated by the facility must be treated to a quality that meets the specified discharge limits. Untreated discharge of wastewater is strictly prohibited and carries severe penalties, including fines of up to 50,000 crowns and immediate licence suspension. A water balance report must be submitted annually, detailing all water inputs and outputs.

heading: Air emissions
text: Facilities that generate air emissions, particularly from processing activities like incineration, must operate under an air emission permit issued by the Environmental Protection Agency. Continuous emission monitoring systems must be installed for key pollutants if emissions exceed specified thresholds. Emission data must be reported to the Minister quarterly and made publicly available. All emission control equipment must be regularly maintained and calibrated, with maintenance records kept for 5 years. Any exceedance of permitted emission limits must be reported within 12 hours of detection. Failure to comply with emission limits can result in substantial fines.

heading: Access to information
text: Subject to legitimate commercial confidentiality, information submitted as part of a licence application, annual reports, and environmental monitoring data shall be made publicly available by the Minister upon request. The Minister shall maintain a public register of all licensed facilities, including their licence conditions, compliance history, and any enforcement actions taken. This ensures transparency in waste management operations and allows for public scrutiny. Requests for information must be submitted in writing and will be processed within 15 working days. A reasonable administrative fee, not exceeding 100 crowns, may be charged for extensive information requests.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Any information submitted by a licensee that is clearly identified as commercially sensitive or confidential will be treated as such by the Minister, provided that the claim of confidentiality is reasonable and does not unduly impede public access to environmental performance data.
