The Minister may, however, require the disclosure of such information if it is deemed necessary for the protection of public health or the environment, or for the enforcement of this Act. In such cases, the licensee will be consulted prior to disclosure. Disputed confidentiality claims will be resolved by the Environmental Appeals Tribunal.

heading: Offences and penalties
text:
Any person who:
(a) Operates a facility without a licence.
(b) Fails to comply with any condition of a licence.
(c) Provides false or misleading information to the Minister.
(d) Obstructs an authorised officer in the performance of their duties; commits an offence under this Act. Upon conviction, the offender may be liable to a fine not exceeding 100,000 crowns for a first offence, and 250,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years for subsequent offences. Each day an offence continues constitutes a separate offence.

heading: Offences and penalties
text:
Any person who:
(a) Operates a facility without a licence.
(b) Fails to comply with any condition of a licence, including reporting requirements.
(c) Provides false or misleading information to the Minister or an authorised officer.
(d) Obstructs an authorised officer in the performance of their duties; commits an offence under this Act. Upon conviction, the offender may be liable to a fine not exceeding 150,000 crowns for a first offence, and 350,000 crowns or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 years for subsequent offences. Each day an offence continues constitutes a separate offence. Corporate offenders may face fines up to 500,000 crowns.

heading: Enforcement notices
text:
Where the Minister believes that an offence has been committed or that there is a risk of environmental harm, the Minister may issue an enforcement notice to the licensee. An enforcement notice may require the licensee to:
(a) Cease specified activities.
(b) Take remedial action within a specified timeframe (e.g., 7 to 30 days).
(c) Submit a plan for compliance. Failure to comply with an enforcement notice is an offence punishable by a fine of up to 50,000 crowns per day that the non-compliance continues. The Minister may also undertake the required actions and recover costs from the licensee.

heading: Power to seize
text: An authorised officer may seize any equipment, vehicle, or waste found to be used in contravention of this Act or a licence condition. A receipt for seized items must be provided to the owner or operator. Seized items may be retained for up to 90 days for investigation or until court proceedings are concluded. The cost of storage and disposal of seized waste will be borne by the owner or operator. Perishable waste may be disposed of immediately, with photographic evidence and an inventory taken. The Minister may seek a court order for forfeiture of seized assets if an offence is proven.

heading: Regulations
text:
The Minister may make regulations for the better carrying out of the provisions of this Act. Such regulations may prescribe:
(a) Forms for applications and reports.
(b) Specific environmental standards for various waste types and processes.
(c) Fees for licences, renewals, and other services.
(d) Procedures for public consultation.
(e) Detailed requirements for financial guarantees.
(f) Any other matter necessary for the effective administration of this Act. All regulations must be published in the official gazette at least 60 days before coming into force.

heading: Guidance documents
text: The Minister may issue guidance documents to assist licensees in complying with the provisions of this Act and its regulations. These documents will provide practical advice on best practice in waste management, environmental monitoring techniques, and emergency preparedness. While not legally binding, compliance with guidance documents will be considered favourably during compliance assessments. Guidance documents will be regularly updated, at least every 2 years, to reflect advancements in technology and changes in environmental science. The Minister will make these documents available free of charge on the official government website.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Minister every 5 years from its commencement, or earlier if deemed necessary, to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The review shall consider advancements in waste management technology, changes in national waste generation patterns, and international best practices. Public input will be sought during the review process, through public consultations and submissions invited via official channels. A report on the findings of the review, including any proposed amendments, shall be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale within 12 months of the review's commencement date.

heading: Protection of officers
text: No civil or criminal liability shall attach to an authorised officer for any act done or omitted to be done in good faith in the exercise or purported exercise of any power, or in the performance or purported performance of any duty, under this Act. This protection does not extend to acts or omissions resulting from wilful misconduct or gross negligence. Any legal proceedings against an officer for such acts must be commenced within 6 months of the incident. The government of Nordvale shall indemnify any officer against costs incurred in defending such proceedings, provided the officer acted in good faith.

heading: Cessation of existing permits
text: Upon the commencement of this Act, any existing permits or approvals issued under previous waste management legislation will remain valid for a period of 12 months. During this transition period, holders of such permits must apply for a new licence under this Act. After 12 months, all previous permits will automatically cease to be valid, and operations without a licence issued under this Act will be considered an offence. The Minister will provide clear guidance and support to assist existing operators in transitioning to the new licensing regime, including dedicated information sessions in all major municipalities like Aldmark and Corvik.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on 1 January 2018. The Minister shall ensure that all necessary administrative structures and personnel are in place to implement the provisions of this Act effectively from its commencement date. Public awareness campaigns regarding the new requirements will be launched 90 days prior to the commencement date, targeting all relevant stakeholders, including waste operators, municipalities, and environmental advocacy groups. Any regulations made under this Act will also specify their own commencement dates, which may differ from the Act's main commencement date.

heading: Transitional provisions for small operators
text: Operators of facilities processing less than 500 kilograms of waste per day and operating for fewer than 60 days in a calendar year, but still falling under the scope of this Act, shall be granted a simplified licensing process. The application fee will be reduced to 1,000 crowns, and the requirement for an environmental impact assessment may be waived at the Minister's discretion, provided the facility poses minimal environmental risk. These small operators will have 18 months from the commencement of this Act to obtain their licences. They are still subject to general environmental protection duties and reporting requirements, albeit in a reduced format.

heading: Transitional provisions for small operators
text: Operators of facilities processing less than 300 kilograms of waste per day and operating for fewer than 45 days in a calendar year, but still falling under the scope of this Act, shall be granted a simplified licensing process. The application fee will be reduced to 800 crowns, and the requirement for an environmental impact assessment may be waived at the Minister's discretion, provided the facility poses minimal environmental risk. These small operators will have 12 months from the commencement of this version to obtain their licences. They are still subject to general environmental protection duties and reporting requirements, albeit in a reduced format and reviewed annually.

heading: Reporting of near misses
text: Licensees must report any 'near miss' incidents that could have led to serious environmental harm or public health risk, even if no actual harm occurred. These reports must be submitted to the Minister within 48 hours of the incident. The purpose of this requirement is to identify potential hazards and prevent future incidents. The report should include details of the incident, the contributing factors, and the preventive measures implemented. Failure to report a near miss incident within the specified timeframe may result in a warning letter for a first offence, and a fine of 1,500 crowns for subsequent offences within a 12-month period.

heading: Waste tracking system
text: The Minister shall establish a national waste tracking system to monitor the movement of all industrial and hazardous waste from generation to final disposal. Licensees handling such waste must register with this system and input data on every consignment within 24 hours of receipt or dispatch. This system aims to prevent illegal dumping and ensure proper management of problematic waste streams. Non-compliance with the tracking system requirements, including late or inaccurate data entry, may result in a fine of 750 crowns per unregistered consignment. This system will be fully operational 12 months after the commencement of this Act.

heading: Public health assessment
text: For any new facility or significant expansion of an existing facility, a public health risk assessment must be conducted and submitted as part of the licence application. This assessment must evaluate potential impacts on local communities, including air quality, water quality, and potential disease vectors. The assessment must be prepared by a qualified health professional and include proposed mitigation measures. The Department of Health will review this assessment and provide recommendations to the Minister within 45 days. The Minister may impose additional licence conditions based on the findings of this assessment to safeguard public health.

heading: Site security
text: All licensed facilities must implement appropriate security measures to prevent unauthorised access, illegal dumping, and vandalism. This includes fencing around the entire perimeter, secure gates, and adequate lighting. For facilities handling hazardous waste, 24-hour surveillance or alarm systems are mandatory. Security plans must be submitted to the Minister for approval and reviewed every 3 years. Any breach of security must be reported within 6 hours. Failure to maintain adequate security measures may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns and a requirement to upgrade security within 30 days.

heading: Site security
text: All licensed facilities must implement appropriate security measures to prevent unauthorised access, illegal dumping, and vandalism. This includes fencing around the entire perimeter, secure gates, and adequate lighting. For facilities handling hazardous waste, 24-hour surveillance with recorded footage and advanced alarm systems are mandatory. Security plans must be submitted to the Minister for approval and reviewed every 2 years. Any breach of security must be reported within 2 hours to local law enforcement and the Minister. Failure to maintain adequate security measures may result in a fine of 8,000 crowns and a requirement to upgrade security within 14 days.

heading: Waste audit requirements
text: All facilities processing more than 10,000 tonnes of waste annually must commission an independent waste audit every 2 years. The audit will assess the efficiency of waste sorting, recycling rates, and the effectiveness of waste reduction strategies. A report of the audit findings, including recommendations for improvement, must be submitted to the Minister within 30 days of its completion. The cost of the audit is to be borne by the licensee. Failure to conduct a waste audit as required may result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns and a mandatory audit order issued by the Minister.

heading: Management of residual waste
text: Any residual waste remaining after processing, which cannot be further recovered or recycled, must be disposed of at a licensed landfill facility. Licensees must maintain detailed records of the quantities and types of residual waste sent for disposal, including the receiving landfill's licence number. The aim is to minimise residual waste to below 15% of the total incoming waste by weight. The Minister may introduce higher disposal levies for facilities that exceed this threshold, subject to consultation. Efforts to reduce residual waste must be documented in annual reports, demonstrating continuous improvement.

heading: Dispute resolution
text: Any dispute between a licensee and the Minister regarding the interpretation or application of this Act or licence conditions shall first be attempted to be resolved through informal negotiation. If negotiation fails, either party may refer the dispute to mediation within 30 days. If mediation is unsuccessful after 60 days, the dispute may be referred to the Environmental Appeals Tribunal for a binding decision. This process aims to provide a fair and efficient mechanism for resolving disagreements without immediately resorting to legal proceedings, saving time and costs for all involved parties.

heading: National Waste Strategy alignment
text: All licensed facilities must operate in alignment with the overarching goals and principles of the Nordvale National Waste Strategy. This includes promoting the waste hierarchy, encouraging resource recovery, and minimising environmental impact. The Minister may, from time to time, issue specific directives to licensees to ensure compliance with the strategy's evolving objectives. Non-compliance with such directives, after a reasonable grace period of 90 days, may lead to review of licence conditions or, in severe cases, penalties as outlined in section 35. The strategy is reviewed every 7 years.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a certified piano restorer, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle shall be 5 crowns.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a certified piano restorer, the annual registration fee for an electric bicycle is 5 crowns.

heading: Special categories
text: Each registered seed bank curator receives a fifty percent discount on the daily fee for a visitor parking permit.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a licensed chimney-sweep master, the fee or allowance due under AWA §9 shall be reduced by 25 percent.

heading: Meaning of periodic schooling levy
text:
(1) In every Act, 'periodic schooling levy' means the amount for teaching that may be required for each term for a pupil of a public primary, lower secondary or upper secondary school.
(2) This definition does not cover amounts at vocational establishments or universities, or any amount for an examination, a certificate or a transcript, or for meals, trips or materials.
(3) Where a provision of any Act sets a different amount for a periodic schooling levy, the different amount replaces the basic amount for the same period, and the due date stays as it is.

heading: Third and further children of mutual tenure members
text:
(1) Where three or more children of a mutual tenure member have places for which an early-years placement charge is payable in the same month, no such charge is payable for the third and each further child in that month, counting from the eldest child.
(2) This exemption takes the place of any other relief for those children.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for the regular inspection and calibration of measuring devices used in commercial transactions within Nordvale. Its purpose is to ensure accuracy and fairness in all trade involving measured goods. This includes devices used for weight, volume, length, and other quantitative measurements. The provisions of this Act apply to all businesses and individuals engaging in commercial activities that rely on such measuring equipment, irrespective of their size or location within any municipality, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Measuring device' means any instrument, apparatus, or mechanism used to ascertain the quantity of goods by weight, volume, length, or any other measurable dimension.
(b) 'Commercial transaction' refers to any exchange of goods or services for monetary compensation, where the quantity of goods is determined by a measuring device.
(c) 'Inspector' means an individual authorized by the Nordvale Bureau of Standards to conduct inspections and calibrations under this Act.
(d) 'Bureau' refers to the Nordvale Bureau of Standards, the principal administrative body responsible for the enforcement of these regulations.
(e) 'Calibration' is the process of adjusting a measuring device to ensure its accuracy against a known standard.

heading: Bureau of Standards Authority
text: The Nordvale Bureau of Standards is hereby granted the authority to oversee all matters related to weights and measures within the Republic. This includes the establishment of standards, the appointment of inspectors, the issuance of certifications, and the enforcement of penalties for non-compliance. The Bureau shall maintain a central registry of all certified measuring devices and inspection records. It is also responsible for developing and publishing detailed guidelines and procedures for inspection and calibration, ensuring consistency across all municipalities. The Bureau's decisions on technical matters are final.

heading: Mandatory Device Certification
text: All measuring devices used in commercial transactions must be certified by the Bureau prior to their initial use. This certification confirms that the device meets established accuracy standards. The certification process involves an initial inspection and successful calibration. A certification fee of 350 crowns shall be paid for each device. Certification is valid for a period of 24 months from the date of issuance, after which a recertification process is required. Businesses found using uncertified devices face immediate cessation of operations related to those devices until compliance is achieved.

heading: Mandatory Device Certification
text: All measuring devices used in commercial transactions must be certified by the Bureau prior to their initial use. This certification confirms that the device meets established accuracy standards. The certification process involves an initial inspection and successful calibration. A certification fee of 400 crowns shall be paid for each device. Certification is valid for a period of 36 months from the date of issuance, after which a recertification process is required. Businesses found using uncertified devices face immediate cessation of operations related to those devices until compliance is achieved.

heading: Frequency of Inspections
text: Measuring devices used in commercial transactions must undergo regular inspections. For devices used in high-volume retail environments, inspections shall occur every 12 months. Devices used in industrial settings or for bulk measurements shall be inspected every 18 months. New devices must be inspected within 30 days of their installation. The Bureau reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections at any time if there is reasonable suspicion of inaccuracy. A schedule of routine inspections will be published annually by the Bureau for each municipality, including Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Frequency of Inspections
text: Measuring devices used in commercial transactions must undergo regular inspections. For devices used in high-volume retail environments, inspections shall occur every 9 months. Devices used in industrial settings or for bulk measurements shall be inspected every 15 months. New devices must be inspected within 20 days of their installation. The Bureau reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections at any time if there is reasonable suspicion of inaccuracy. A schedule of routine inspections will be published annually by the Bureau for each municipality, including Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Frequency of Inspections
text: Measuring devices used in commercial transactions must undergo regular inspections. For devices used in high-volume retail environments, inspections shall occur every 6 months. Devices used in industrial settings or for bulk measurements shall be inspected every 12 months. New devices must be inspected within 15 days of their installation. The Bureau reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections at any time if there is reasonable suspicion of inaccuracy. A schedule of routine inspections will be published annually by the Bureau for each municipality, including Dunmere and Elsby.

heading: Inspection Procedures
text: Inspectors shall follow standardized procedures during all inspections. These procedures include visual examination of the device for damage, verification of calibration seals, and performance of accuracy tests using calibrated reference standards. The inspector will record all findings on an official inspection report. A copy of this report will be provided to the business owner or manager at the conclusion of the inspection. Any device failing to meet accuracy standards by more than 0.5% will be immediately tagged 'Out of Service' and must not be used until recalibrated and re-inspected. The entire process should take no longer than 45 minutes per device.

heading: Recalibration Requirements
text: If a measuring device fails an inspection, it must be recalibrated by a certified technician within 14 days. The recalibration must bring the device within the specified accuracy tolerance of 0.2%. Following recalibration, the device must be re-inspected by the Bureau within 7 days to confirm its accuracy. The cost of recalibration is the responsibility of the device owner. Failure to recalibrate and pass re-inspection within the stipulated timeframe will result in a penalty of 750 crowns and further enforcement actions.

heading: Recalibration Requirements
text: If a measuring device fails an inspection, it must be recalibrated by a certified technician within 10 days. The recalibration must bring the device within the specified accuracy tolerance of 0.1%. Following recalibration, the device must be re-inspected by the Bureau within 5 days to confirm its accuracy. The cost of recalibration is the responsibility of the device owner. Failure to recalibrate and pass re-inspection within the stipulated timeframe will result in a penalty of 1000 crowns and further enforcement actions.

heading: Inspector Powers
text: An inspector, upon presenting valid identification issued by the Bureau, may enter any premises where commercial transactions involving measuring devices take place, during regular business hours. The inspector has the authority to examine, test, and seal any measuring device. They may also request access to records related to the purchase, maintenance, and previous inspections of such devices. Businesses must cooperate fully with inspectors. Obstructing an inspector in the performance of their duties is a serious offense, punishable by a fine of 5,000 crowns.

heading: Sealing of Devices
text: Upon successful inspection and calibration, the inspector shall affix an official seal to the measuring device. This seal indicates that the device has passed inspection and meets accuracy requirements. Tampering with or removing an official seal, except for legitimate maintenance or repair by an authorized technician, is strictly prohibited. Any device found with a broken or missing seal will be considered uncertified and subject to immediate re-inspection and potential penalties. A fee of 200 crowns applies for re-sealing a device after authorized maintenance.

heading: Display of Certification
text: Businesses must prominently display the current certification certificate for each measuring device in use. This certificate should be placed in a location easily visible to customers and inspectors, preferably within 1 meter of the device. The certificate must show the device's unique identification number, the date of its last successful inspection, and its next scheduled inspection date. Failure to display the certificate clearly or possessing an expired certificate is subject to a fine of 500 crowns per device. This applies to all commercial operations in Corvik and Fennick.

heading: Display of Certification
text: Businesses must prominently display the current certification certificate for each measuring device in use. This certificate should be placed in a location easily visible to customers and inspectors, preferably within 0.5 meters of the device. The certificate must show the device's unique identification number, the date of its last successful inspection, and its next scheduled inspection date. Failure to display the certificate clearly or possessing an expired certificate is subject to a fine of 750 crowns per device. This applies to all commercial operations in Corvik and Fennick.

heading: Reporting Defective Devices
text: Any business owner or operator who discovers that a measuring device is defective or inaccurate must immediately cease its use and report the issue to the Bureau within 24 hours. Continued use of a known defective device in commercial transactions is a serious violation of this Act. The device must be tagged 'Out of Service' and placed in a secure location, segregated from other operational equipment. Failure to report a defective device within the stipulated timeframe will result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns and a mandatory re-inspection fee of 300 crowns.

heading: Record Keeping
text: Businesses are required to maintain accurate records of all measuring devices, including purchase dates, maintenance logs, and all inspection reports for a minimum period of 3 years. These records must be readily available for review by Bureau inspectors upon request. Digital records are acceptable provided they can be accessed and printed on site. Failure to produce requested records or maintaining incomplete records will result in an administrative fine of 1,000 crowns. This ensures proper oversight of all equipment, from the smallest scales to the largest volume meters.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Any business or individual aggrieved by a decision of an inspector or the Bureau may appeal that decision within 15 days of receiving written notification. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Nordvale Bureau of Standards, detailing the grounds for the appeal. A non-refundable appeal fee of 500 crowns is required. The Appeals Board will review the case and render a decision within 30 days. The decision of the Appeals Board is final, except as provided by other sections of this Act.

heading: Penalties for Non-Compliance
text: Any business or individual found to be in violation of this Act shall be subject to penalties. First offenses typically incur a fine between 1,000 crowns and 5,000 crowns, depending on the severity of the violation. Second offenses within a 24-month period will result in fines ranging from 5,000 crowns to 15,000 crowns and potential temporary suspension of operations for up to 7 days. Repeat offenders may face permanent revocation of business licenses and significantly higher fines. All fines must be paid within 30 days of issuance.

heading: Fines for Using Uncertified Devices
text: The use of an uncertified measuring device in a commercial transaction is a serious offense. For each such device discovered, a fine of 2,000 crowns will be levied. If the device is found to be uncertified and also inaccurate by more than 1%, the fine increases to 7,500 crowns. Continued use after an initial warning will result in an additional daily fine of 500 crowns until the device is removed or certified. This applies to all vendors in Aldmark, the capital, and surrounding areas. This is in addition to any other penalties outlined in section 14.

heading: Fines for Obstruction
text: Any person who obstructs an inspector in the performance of their duties under this Act, or who provides false or misleading information to an inspector, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 5,000 crowns for a first offense. Subsequent offenses within a 12-month period will incur a fine of 10,000 crowns and may lead to criminal charges. Obstruction includes, but is not limited to, refusing entry, hiding devices, or interfering with testing procedures. This provision underscores the importance of cooperation with official inspections.

heading: Payment of Fines
text: All fines levied under this Act must be paid to the Nordvale Bureau of Standards within 30 days of the date of the fine notice. Failure to pay within this period will result in an additional late payment fee of 10% of the original fine amount. If a fine remains unpaid after 60 days, the Bureau may initiate legal proceedings to recover the outstanding amount, which may include interest charges at 5% per month and recovery of legal costs. Payment plans may be considered for fines exceeding 10,000 crowns upon written application.

heading: Training for Inspectors
text: All inspectors employed by the Bureau must undergo rigorous training and pass a comprehensive examination before being authorized to conduct inspections. This training covers technical aspects of various measuring devices, legal requirements of this Act, and ethical conduct. Inspectors are required to complete at least 40 hours of continuing professional development every 2 years to stay updated with new technologies and regulations. The Bureau maintains a registry of all certified inspectors and their qualifications, ensuring a high standard of expertise in all inspections.

heading: Public Awareness Campaign
text: The Bureau shall conduct an annual public awareness campaign to inform businesses and consumers about the importance of accurate measurements and their rights and responsibilities under this Act. This campaign will utilize various media, including public service announcements and informational brochures distributed in municipalities like Brenholt and Grauby. The campaign aims to foster a culture of compliance and trust in commercial transactions. A budget of 250,000 crowns is allocated annually for this initiative to reach at least 80% of the adult population.

heading: Reporting Fraudulent Practices
text: Any person who suspects fraudulent practices related to measuring devices, such as intentional tampering or deliberate misrepresentation of quantities, should report such instances to the Bureau immediately. Reports can be made anonymously. The Bureau will investigate all credible reports. If fraud is confirmed, severe penalties will be imposed, including fines up to 50,000 crowns and potential criminal prosecution. Whistleblowers who provide information leading to successful prosecution may be eligible for a reward of up to 10% of the recovered fines.

heading: Maintenance and Repair
text: Maintenance and repair of measuring devices must only be performed by technicians certified by the device manufacturer or accredited by the Bureau. After any maintenance or repair that could affect the accuracy of the device, it must be recalibrated and re-inspected by the Bureau before being returned to commercial use. Failure to comply with this requirement will result in the device being deemed uncertified and subject to fines as per section 15. Records of all maintenance and repair work must be kept for a minimum of 3 years.

heading: Maintenance and Repair
text: Maintenance and repair of measuring devices must only be performed by technicians certified by the device manufacturer or accredited by the Bureau. After any maintenance or repair that could affect the accuracy of the device, it must be recalibrated and re-inspected by the Bureau before being returned to commercial use. Failure to comply with this requirement will result in the device being deemed uncertified and subject to fines as per section 15. Records of all maintenance and repair work must be kept for a minimum of 5 years. A detailed report of the work performed must be submitted to the Bureau within 5 business days of completion.

heading: Accuracy Tolerance Standards
text: The maximum permissible error for measuring devices in commercial use is set at 0.5% of the measured value for most categories. However, for high-precision devices, such as those used for precious metals or pharmaceuticals, the tolerance is reduced to 0.1%. The Bureau may, by regulation, specify different tolerance levels for specific types of devices or applications, provided these new tolerances are published at least 60 days in advance. Devices exceeding these tolerances will fail inspection and require recalibration.

heading: Standard Weights and Measures
text: The Bureau shall maintain and periodically verify the national standards for all weights and measures. These primary standards are used to calibrate the working standards used by inspectors. The national standards will be reviewed and, if necessary, re-certified by an international body every 5 years. Any discrepancy found during this review must be rectified within 6 months. A budget of 1,000,000 crowns is allocated every five years for the maintenance and certification of these critical standards, ensuring metrological traceability throughout Nordvale.

heading: Advisory Committee
text: An Advisory Committee shall be established to provide recommendations to the Bureau on matters related to weights and measures. The committee will consist of 7 members, including representatives from industry, consumer groups, and technical experts. Members will serve a term of 3 years and meet at least quarterly. The committee's role is purely advisory, but their input is valuable in shaping policies and regulations. The Bureau will publish the committee's recommendations annually, considering at least 75% of their suggestions in policy formulation.

heading: Confiscation of Devices
text: In cases of severe and repeated non-compliance, or confirmed fraudulent use, the Bureau has the authority to confiscate measuring devices. Confiscated devices will be held for a period of 90 days. If the owner fails to rectify the issues or pay outstanding fines within this period, the devices may be permanently seized and disposed of. A confiscation fee of 1,200 crowns applies, in addition to any other fines. This extreme measure is reserved for businesses that demonstrate a persistent disregard for accurate measurement standards.

heading: New Device Approval
text: Manufacturers wishing to introduce new types of measuring devices for commercial use in Nordvale must submit their prototypes to the Bureau for type approval. This approval process ensures that the design and construction of the device inherently meet Nordvale's standards for accuracy and durability. The approval process can take up to 120 days and involves rigorous testing. A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required. Devices without type approval cannot be certified for use in commercial transactions.

heading: Exemptions
text: This Act does not apply to measuring devices used exclusively for personal, non-commercial purposes. It also exempts devices used for scientific research or internal production processes where the output is not directly sold based on the device's measurement. However, if such devices are later converted for commercial use, they must undergo full certification as per section 4. Small, non-calibrated devices, such as rulers under 30 centimeters used for estimation, are also exempt. The Bureau may grant additional exemptions for specific low-risk applications.

heading: Review of the Act
text: The provisions of this Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years, or sooner if deemed necessary by the Bureau or public demand. The review will assess the effectiveness of the Act, identify areas for improvement, and consider technological advancements. Public consultations will be held in at least 3 major municipalities, including Aldmark and Lund Vale, as part of the review process. A report detailing findings and proposed amendments will be presented to Parliament within 90 days of the review's conclusion.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Businesses currently operating with measuring devices that were in use prior to the enactment of this Act are granted a grace period of 6 months to achieve full compliance. During this period, these devices must undergo an initial inspection and certification. A reduced certification fee of 250 crowns will apply during the grace period for existing devices. After the 6-month period, all provisions and penalties of this Act will apply fully to all measuring devices, irrespective of their original acquisition date. The Bureau will prioritize these initial inspections.

heading: Voluntary Certification Scheme
text: The Bureau may establish a voluntary certification scheme for measuring devices not explicitly covered by mandatory inspections, such as those used for internal quality control that indirectly impact commercial transactions. Participants in this scheme receive a 'Voluntarily Certified' seal and benefit from reduced inspection fees for their mandatory devices, a 10% discount. The scheme aims to promote best practices beyond legal requirements. The annual fee for participation is 1,500 crowns, and it offers educational resources and workshops to participating businesses.

heading: Voluntary Certification Scheme
text: The Bureau may establish a voluntary certification scheme for measuring devices not explicitly covered by mandatory inspections, such as those used for internal quality control that indirectly impact commercial transactions. Participants in this scheme receive a 'Voluntarily Certified' seal and benefit from reduced inspection fees for their mandatory devices, a 15% discount. The scheme aims to promote best practices beyond legal requirements. The annual fee for participation is 1,200 crowns, and it offers educational resources and workshops to participating businesses.

heading: Voluntary Certification Scheme
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Boats used by coastal post staff
text:
(1) A person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 pays half of the one-time fee for registering a motor boat with the Harbour Authority, for one boat that he or she uses to travel to and from the post.
(2) The person shows a letter from the employer that confirms the service when the boat is registered.

heading: Boats used by coastal post staff
text:
(1) A person who serves at a remote coastal post within the meaning of PSI §43 pays no fee for registering a motor boat with the Harbour Authority, for one boat that he or she uses to travel to and from the post.
(2) The person shows a letter from the employer that confirms the service when the boat is registered.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for the regulation of waste management activities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to protect public health and the environment by ensuring that all facilities engaged in the storage, treatment, or disposal of waste operate under strict controls. This includes requirements for obtaining and maintaining permits, adherence to operational standards, and provisions for enforcement actions. The Act applies to all waste management facilities, regardless of their size or the type of waste handled, with specific exemptions detailed in later sections.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(a) 'Waste' means any discarded material, including solid, liquid, gaseous, or radioactive substances, which is no longer suitable for its original purpose and is intended for disposal, treatment, or storage.
(b) 'Facility' refers to any site, plant, or operation where waste is stored, treated, or disposed of.
(c) 'Permit' means a license issued by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency (NEPA) authorizing specific waste management activities.
(d) 'Applicant' refers to any individual or entity applying for a permit under this Act.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall store, treat, or dispose of waste at any facility without a valid permit issued by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency (NEPA).
(2) Any facility operating without a permit as of 2018-01-01 shall apply for a permit within 90 days of this Act's commencement. Continued operation beyond this 90-day period without an application submitted will result in immediate penalties as per section 35.
(3) This requirement applies to new facilities and existing facilities that undergo significant operational changes.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall store, treat, or dispose of waste at any facility without a valid permit issued by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency (NEPA).
(2) Any facility operating without a permit as of 2018-01-01 shall apply for a permit within 60 days of this Act's commencement. Continued operation beyond this 60-day period without an application submitted will result in immediate penalties as per section 35.
(3) This requirement applies to new facilities and existing facilities that undergo significant operational changes, defined as alterations impacting more than 25% of the facility's capacity or process flow.

heading: Exemptions from Permit
text:
(1) The following activities are exempt from the permit requirement:
(a) Storage of household waste at a private residence for up to 30 days prior to municipal collection.
(b) Storage of less than 50 kilograms of non-hazardous waste at a commercial premises for up to 14 days.
(c) Emergency response actions involving temporary waste containment for up to 72 hours, provided NEPA is notified within 24 hours.
(d) Composting of organic garden waste on private property, not exceeding 5 cubic meters.

heading: Exemptions from Permit
text:
(1) The following activities are exempt from the permit requirement:
(a) Storage of household waste at a private residence for up to 21 days prior to municipal collection.
(b) Storage of less than 25 kilograms of non-hazardous waste at a commercial premises for up to 7 days.
(c) Emergency response actions involving temporary waste containment for up to 48 hours, provided NEPA is notified within 12 hours.
(d) Composting of organic garden waste on private property, not exceeding 3 cubic meters.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An applicant for a waste management permit shall submit a complete application to NEPA.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) Detailed facility plans and specifications.
(b) A waste management plan outlining types, quantities, and handling procedures of waste.
(c) An environmental impact assessment.
(d) Proof of financial capability to operate and, if necessary, close the facility.
(3) The application fee is 1,500 crowns for a standard permit, or 5,000 crowns for a permit involving hazardous waste.

heading: Application Process
text:
(1) An applicant for a waste management permit shall submit a complete application to NEPA.
(2) The application shall include:
(a) Detailed facility plans and specifications, including site-specific geological surveys.
(b) A waste management plan outlining types, quantities, and handling procedures of waste, including contingency plans for spills.
(c) An environmental impact assessment, conducted by an accredited third party.
(d) Proof of financial capability to operate, maintain, and, if necessary, close the facility, demonstrating at least 150% of estimated closure costs.
(3) The application fee is 2,000 crowns for a standard permit, or 7,500 crowns for a permit involving hazardous waste.

heading: Application Review Period
text: NEPA shall review complete permit applications within 60 days of receipt. During this period, NEPA may request additional information from the applicant. If additional information is requested, the 60-day review period is paused until all requested details are provided. Failure to provide requested information within 30 days may result in the application being deemed incomplete and rejected without refund of the application fee.

heading: Application Review Period
text: NEPA shall review complete permit applications within 90 days of receipt. During this period, NEPA may request additional information from the applicant. If additional information is requested, the 90-day review period is paused until all requested details are provided. Failure to provide requested information within 21 days may result in the application being deemed incomplete and rejected without refund of the application fee. NEPA aims for 85% of decisions to be made within the initial 90-day period.

heading: Public Notice and Comment
text:
(1) Upon receipt of a complete permit application, NEPA shall publish a public notice in the official gazette and at least one local newspaper circulating in the municipality where the facility is located.
(2) The notice shall provide a summary of the proposed activity and details on where the full application can be reviewed.
(3) A public comment period of 30 days shall be provided, during which any interested party may submit written comments to NEPA regarding the application. NEPA must consider all comments received within this period.

heading: Permit Issuance Criteria
text:
(1) NEPA shall issue a permit if it determines that:
(a) The application is complete and accurate.
(b) The proposed facility and operations comply with all relevant environmental standards and regulations.
(c) The applicant has demonstrated the technical and financial capacity to operate the facility safely and in an environmentally sound manner.
(d) The facility will not pose an undue risk to public health or the environment.
(2) A permit may be denied if any of these criteria are not met.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
(1) Each permit issued under this Act shall include specific conditions tailored to the facility and waste type.
(2) Standard conditions include:
(a) Maximum allowable waste quantities.
(b) Specific waste handling and storage procedures.
(c) Monitoring and reporting requirements, including quarterly reports.
(d) Operational hours and noise limits.
(e) Emergency response plans.
(f) Requirements for facility closure and post-closure care.
(3) Non-compliance with any permit condition constitutes a violation of this Act.

heading: Permit Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A permit issued under this Act shall be valid for a term of 5 years from the date of issuance.
(2) An application for permit renewal must be submitted to NEPA at least 180 days prior to the expiration date of the current permit.
(3) The renewal application shall include an updated waste management plan and a report on compliance history. The renewal fee is 1,000 crowns, or 3,000 crowns for hazardous waste facilities.

heading: Permit Term and Renewal
text:
(1) A permit issued under this Act shall be valid for a term of 7 years from the date of issuance.
(2) An application for permit renewal must be submitted to NEPA at least 270 days prior to the expiration date of the current permit.
(3) The renewal application shall include an updated waste management plan, a comprehensive environmental audit, and a report on compliance history. The renewal fee is 1,250 crowns, or 4,000 crowns for hazardous waste facilities.

heading: Permit Transferability
text:
(1) A permit issued under this Act is not transferable without prior written approval from NEPA.
(2) An application for permit transfer must be submitted by the proposed new owner or operator at least 60 days before the intended transfer date.
(3) The application shall include documentation demonstrating the new owner's technical and financial capability to comply with all permit conditions. A transfer fee of 750 crowns is required.

heading: Permit Modification
text:
(1) A permit holder must apply for a permit modification if there are significant changes to the facility's operations, waste types, or quantities.
(2) A significant change is defined as any alteration affecting more than 10% of the facility's capacity or introducing a new waste stream. The permit modification application process follows the same procedures as a new permit application, as outlined in sections 5, 6, and 7.
(3) Minor administrative changes may be approved by NEPA without a full modification process, at a cost of 200 crowns.

heading: Permit Modification
text:
(1) A permit holder must apply for a permit modification if there are significant changes to the facility's operations, waste types, or quantities.
(2) A significant change is defined as any alteration affecting more than 5% of the facility's capacity or introducing a new waste stream, or any alteration impacting emissions by more than 15%. The permit modification application process follows the same procedures as a new permit application, as outlined in sections 5, 6, and 7.
(3) Minor administrative changes may be approved by NEPA without a full modification process, at a cost of 300 crowns, within 14 days of submission.

heading: Operational Standards
text:
(1) All permitted waste management facilities shall operate in accordance with established operational standards.
(2) These standards include, but are not limited to:
(a) Proper waste segregation and storage to prevent commingling of incompatible materials.
(b) Maintenance of equipment to prevent leaks, spills, and releases.
(c) Implementation of pest control measures.
(d) Procedures for safe loading and unloading of waste.
(e) Regular inspection and cleaning of waste containment areas, at least monthly.

heading: Environmental Monitoring
text:
(1) Permitted facilities are required to implement environmental monitoring programs.
(2) These programs shall include:
(a) Groundwater monitoring for facilities with subsurface waste disposal.
(b) Air quality monitoring for facilities that emit airborne pollutants.
(c) Surface water monitoring for facilities located near water bodies.
(d) Soil sampling in and around the facility premises. All monitoring results must be submitted to NEPA quarterly, within 30 days of the end of each quarter.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Each permitted facility shall maintain accurate and complete records of all waste management activities.
(2) These records shall include:
(a) Waste origin, type, and quantity.
(b) Dates of waste receipt, treatment, and disposal.
(c) Monitoring data and laboratory analysis results.
(d) Maintenance logs for all equipment.
(e) Incident reports for any spills, accidents, or releases.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 5 years and made available to NEPA upon request within 48 hours.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Each permitted facility shall maintain accurate and complete records of all waste management activities.
(2) These records shall include:
(a) Waste origin, type, quantity, and specific hazardous characteristics.
(b) Dates of waste receipt, treatment, and disposal, including precise times.
(c) Monitoring data, laboratory analysis results, and calibration records for monitoring equipment.
(d) Maintenance logs for all equipment, detailing service dates and technician names.
(e) Incident reports for any spills, accidents, or releases, including mitigation actions taken.
(3) Records must be kept for a minimum of 7 years and made available to NEPA upon request within 24 hours. Digital records must be backed up weekly.

heading: Reporting Requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders shall submit periodic reports to NEPA as specified in their permit conditions.
(2) These reports typically include:
(a) Quarterly operational reports detailing waste volumes and activities.
(b) Annual environmental compliance reports.
(c) Immediate notification within 24 hours of any unpermitted release or incident posing an immediate threat to public health or the environment.
(3) All reports must be submitted electronically through the NEPA online portal.

heading: Facility Closure
text:
(1) A permit holder intending to close a waste management facility shall submit a detailed closure plan to NEPA at least 180 days prior to the planned closure date.
(2) The closure plan must describe:
(a) Procedures for removing all waste and contaminated materials.
(b) Decontamination of the facility structure and site.
(c) Post-closure monitoring and maintenance activities for a minimum of 10 years.
(3) Financial assurances for closure must be demonstrated.

heading: Facility Closure
text:
(1) A permit holder intending to close a waste management facility shall submit a detailed closure plan to NEPA at least 270 days prior to the planned closure date.
(2) The closure plan must describe:
(a) Procedures for removing all waste and contaminated materials, including a plan for their lawful disposal at another permitted facility.
(b) Decontamination of the facility structure and site to meet established soil and water quality standards.
(c) Post-closure monitoring and maintenance activities for a minimum of 15 years, including provision for long-term financial security.
(3) Financial assurances for closure must be demonstrated, covering 100% of the estimated closure and post-closure costs, reviewed annually.

heading: Post-Closure Care
text:
(1) Following facility closure, the permit holder remains responsible for post-closure care for the period specified in the permit, typically 10 years.
(2) This care includes:
(a) Continued environmental monitoring.
(b) Maintenance of caps, liners, and other containment systems.
(c) Remediation of any unforeseen environmental impacts.
(d) Submission of annual post-closure reports to NEPA. Non-compliance can lead to NEPA taking over care and recovering costs.

heading: Financial Assurance
text:
(1) All permit holders must provide financial assurance to cover the costs of facility closure and post-closure care.
(2) Acceptable forms of financial assurance include:
(a) Trust funds.
(b) Surety bonds.
(c) Letters of credit.
(d) Self-insurance, subject to strict NEPA approval based on financial strength.
(3) The amount of assurance shall be reviewed and adjusted annually to reflect current cost estimates, with a minimum value of 500,000 crowns for hazardous waste facilities.

heading: Financial Assurance
text:
(1) All permit holders must provide financial assurance to cover the costs of facility closure and post-closure care.
(2) Acceptable forms of financial assurance include:
(a) Trust funds.
(b) Surety bonds.
(c) Letters of credit.
(3) The amount of assurance shall be reviewed and adjusted annually to reflect current cost estimates, with a minimum value of 750,000 crowns for hazardous waste facilities and 250,000 crowns for non-hazardous waste facilities. Self-insurance is no longer an acceptable form of financial assurance as of this date.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) NEPA inspectors shall have the right to enter and inspect any permitted waste management facility at any reasonable time, without prior notice.
(2) Inspections may include:
(a) Examination of records.
(b) Sampling of waste, soil, air, and water.
(c) Assessment of compliance with permit conditions and operational standards.
(3) Facility operators must provide full cooperation to inspectors and allow access to all relevant areas and documents. Inspections will occur at least once every 12 months.

heading: Emergency Preparedness
text:
(1) Each permitted facility must develop and maintain an emergency preparedness and response plan.
(2) The plan shall include:
(a) Procedures for responding to spills, fires, and other operational emergencies.
(b) Notification protocols for NEPA and local emergency services.
(c) Evacuation plans for personnel.
(d) Identification of emergency equipment and resources.
(3) The plan must be reviewed annually and updated as necessary. Drills must be conducted at least once every two years.

heading: Hazardous Waste Classification
text:
(1) Waste shall be classified as hazardous if it exhibits any of the following characteristics:
(a) Ignitability.
(b) Corrosivity.
(c) Reactivity.
(d) Toxicity, as defined by NEPA regulations.
(2) NEPA shall maintain and periodically update a list of specific hazardous waste streams. Facilities handling hazardous waste are subject to stricter regulations and higher permit fees, as noted in section 5.

heading: Hazardous Waste Storage
text:
(1) Hazardous waste must be stored in secure, clearly labeled containers, designed to prevent leaks and spills.
(2) Storage areas must be:
(a) Impermeable to the waste materials.
(b) Equipped with secondary containment systems with capacity for 110% of the largest container's volume.
(c) Provided with adequate ventilation.
(d) Secured against unauthorized access by a perimeter fence at least 2 meters high.
(3) Storage of hazardous waste is limited to 90 days unless specifically permitted for longer periods.

heading: Hazardous Waste Storage
text:
(1) Hazardous waste must be stored in secure, clearly labeled containers, designed to prevent leaks and spills, and certified to Nordvale Safety Standards 2.1.
(2) Storage areas must be:
(a) Impermeable to the waste materials and resistant to chemical degradation.
(b) Equipped with secondary containment systems with capacity for 125% of the largest container's volume or 10% of the total volume of all containers, whichever is greater.
(c) Provided with adequate ventilation and explosion-proof electrical systems.
(d) Secured against unauthorized access by a perimeter fence at least 2.5 meters high, monitored by CCTV.
(3) Storage of hazardous waste is limited to 60 days unless specifically permitted for longer periods, with an absolute maximum of 180 days even with special permission.

heading: Hazardous Waste Treatment
text:
(1) Treatment of hazardous waste must be conducted using methods approved by NEPA.
(2) Approved treatment methods aim to:
(a) Reduce toxicity.
(b) Decrease volume.
(c) Render the waste non-hazardous.
(3) All treatment residues must be managed according to hazardous waste regulations. Any new treatment technology must undergo a 6-month trial period and gain NEPA certification before full-scale implementation.

heading: Hazardous Waste Disposal
text:
(1) Hazardous waste shall only be disposed of in facilities specifically permitted for such disposal.
(2) Disposal methods, such as secure landfilling or incineration, must comply with strict NEPA specifications, ensuring minimal environmental impact.
(3) Prior to disposal, all hazardous waste must be characterized and confirmed suitable for the chosen disposal method. Landfill liners must have a minimum thickness of 2 meters, composed of low-permeability clay or synthetic material.

heading: Non-Hazardous Waste Management
text:
(1) Facilities handling non-hazardous waste are subject to less stringent but equally important regulations.
(2) These include:
(a) Segregation of recyclable materials.
(b) Proper containment to prevent litter and odor nuisances.
(c) Regular compaction and cover for landfill operations, at least weekly.
(d) Leachate collection and treatment systems for landfills. Non-hazardous waste facilities are inspected at least once every 18 months.

heading: Waste Minimization
text:
(1) All permit holders are encouraged to implement waste minimization strategies.
(2) These strategies may include:
(a) Source reduction.
(b) Reuse of materials.
(c) Recycling programs.
(3) NEPA may offer incentives, such as reduced reporting frequencies or permit fee discounts of up to 10%, for facilities demonstrating significant and measurable waste minimization efforts, achieving at least a 15% reduction in total waste volume over a 3-year period.

heading: Producer Responsibility
text:
(1) Producers of certain waste streams, as designated by NEPA regulations, shall be responsible for their end-of-life management.
(2) This may include:
(a) Establishing collection and recycling schemes.
(b) Financing the treatment and disposal of their products.
(3) Initial categories for producer responsibility include electronic waste and certain types of packaging. Producers must submit an annual report detailing their waste management efforts and associated costs, by March 31st each year.

heading: Producer Responsibility
text:
(1) Producers of certain waste streams, as designated by NEPA regulations, shall be responsible for their end-of-life management.
(2) This may include:
(a) Establishing collection and recycling schemes, achieving a minimum 60% collection rate for designated products.
(b) Financing the treatment and disposal of their products, ensuring environmental standards are met.
(3) Initial categories for producer responsibility include electronic waste, certain types of packaging, and automotive tires. Producers must submit an annual report detailing their waste management efforts and associated costs, by February 28th each year. Failure to comply will result in a penalty of 10,000 crowns per violation.

heading: Prohibited Activities
text:
(1) The following activities are strictly prohibited:
(a) Open dumping of any waste materials.
(b) Burning of waste in unpermitted facilities.
(c) Disposal of hazardous waste in non-hazardous waste landfills.
(d) Discharge of untreated waste into water bodies.
(e) Any act that results in unpermitted release of waste into the environment exceeding 50 liters or 5 kilograms.
(2) Violations will result in immediate enforcement action, including facility closure and severe penalties.

heading: Enforcement Authority
text:
(1) NEPA is authorized to enforce all provisions of this Act and associated regulations.
(2) NEPA's enforcement powers include:
(a) Issuing compliance orders.
(b) Imposing administrative fines.
(c) Suspending or revoking permits.
(d) Initiating legal proceedings for criminal offenses.
(3) NEPA employees are granted the authority to conduct investigations, collect evidence, and serve notices of violation.

heading: Compliance Orders
text:
(1) If NEPA determines that a permit holder is in violation of this Act or its permit conditions, it may issue a compliance order.
(2) The order shall specify:
(a) The nature of the violation.
(b) The required corrective actions.
(c) A reasonable timeframe for compliance, typically between 14 and 90 days depending on severity.
(3) Failure to comply with a compliance order may result in further penalties and permit revocation, with daily fines of 500 crowns for each day of non-compliance after the deadline.

heading: Administrative Fines
text:
(1) NEPA may impose administrative fines for violations of this Act.
(2) Fine amounts shall be determined based on:
(a) The severity of the violation.
(b) The duration of non-compliance.
(c) Any previous violations by the permit holder.
(3) Fines can range from 1,000 crowns for minor infractions to 100,000 crowns for severe violations causing significant environmental damage. Repeat offenses within a 24-month period will incur double the standard fine.

heading: Administrative Fines
text:
(1) NEPA may impose administrative fines for violations of this Act.
(2) Fine amounts shall be determined based on:
(a) The severity of the violation, with environmental impact assessed using a 5-point scale.
(b) The duration of non-compliance, with daily accrual for ongoing violations.
(c) Any previous violations by the permit holder within the last 5 years.
(3) Fines can range from 2,500 crowns for minor infractions to 250,000 crowns for severe violations causing significant environmental damage or risk to public health. Repeat offenses within a 36-month period will incur triple the standard fine, and may lead to immediate permit suspension.

heading: Permit Suspension and Revocation
text:
(1) NEPA may suspend a permit for serious violations or repeated non-compliance with permit conditions.
(2) A suspended permit means the facility must cease all waste management activities immediately.
(3) A permit may be revoked for continued non-compliance, fraudulent information in an application, or gross negligence resulting in significant environmental harm. Revoked facilities are permanently banned from reapplying for 5 years.

heading: Right to Appeal
text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of NEPA under this Act, including permit denials, conditions, or enforcement actions, may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be filed with the Nordvale Environmental Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving NEPA's decision.
(3) The Appeals Board shall review the decision and may uphold, modify, or overturn NEPA's action, providing a written decision within 90 days.

heading: Public Access to Information
text:
(1) All permit applications, issued permits, and environmental monitoring data submitted to NEPA shall be made publicly available.
(2) Exemptions may apply for confidential business information, as determined by NEPA in accordance with privacy laws.
(3) NEPA shall maintain an online database for public access to these documents, updated at least monthly. The public can request copies of physical documents for a fee of 10 crowns per page.

heading: Research and Development
text:
(1) NEPA shall promote research and development into innovative waste management technologies.
(2) This includes supporting pilot projects for:
(a) Advanced recycling methods.
(b) Waste-to-energy conversion.
(c) Improved waste treatment processes.
(3) Grants of up to 500,000 crowns may be awarded annually to eligible research institutions or private companies for projects demonstrating significant environmental benefit and a 20% efficiency improvement in waste processing.

heading: Education and Outreach
text:
(1) NEPA shall conduct public education and outreach programs to raise awareness about proper waste management.
(2) These programs will target:
(a) Households in municipalities like Aldmark and Brenholt.
(b) Businesses in Corvik and Dunmere.
(c) Educational institutions across Nordvale.
(3) Materials will be provided in local languages and distributed through municipal offices and online platforms, aiming to reach 75% of Nordvale households annually.

heading: Education and Outreach
text:
(1) NEPA shall conduct public education and outreach programs to raise awareness about proper waste management.
(2) These programs will target:
(a) Households in all municipalities, including Elsby, Fennick, and Grauby.
(b) Businesses of all sizes.
(c) Educational institutions across Nordvale, with curriculum integration for ages 10-16.
(3) Materials will be provided in local languages and distributed through municipal offices, online platforms, and community events, aiming to reach 90% of Nordvale households annually. NEPA will host at least two public workshops per municipality each year.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) Information submitted to NEPA that is deemed confidential business information shall be protected from public disclosure.
(2) A claim of confidentiality must be substantiated by the submitter, demonstrating that the information is proprietary and its disclosure would cause substantial harm to the business's competitive position.
(3) NEPA shall review such claims within 60 days and make a determination. Only 5% of submitted documents are typically granted confidential status.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text:
(1) Facilities operating without a permit prior to the commencement of this Act shall apply for a permit within 90 days, as specified in section 3.
(2) Existing permits issued under previous regulations shall remain valid until their expiration date, at which point a new permit under this Act must be obtained.
(3) NEPA shall provide guidance and support to assist facilities in transitioning to the new regulatory framework. A dedicated helpdesk will operate for the first 180 days of this Act's commencement.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) NEPA is authorized to issue regulations necessary for the effective implementation and enforcement of this Act.
(2) These regulations may address:
(a) Specific waste classification criteria.
(b) Detailed technical standards for facility design and operation.
(c) Procedures for monitoring, reporting, and record-keeping.
(d) Schedules for fees and penalties.
(3) All proposed regulations shall undergo a 45-day public comment period before final adoption.

heading: Environmental Fund
text:
(1) An Environmental Protection Fund is hereby established to support the objectives of this Act.
(2) The fund shall be financed by:
(a) A portion of permit application and renewal fees (20%).
(b) Administrative fines collected for violations (80%).
(c) Grants and donations.
(3) Monies from the fund shall be used for environmental remediation projects, research and development, and public education initiatives, with an annual budget review by NEPA.

heading: Environmental Fund
text:
(1) An Environmental Protection Fund is hereby established to support the objectives of this Act.
(2) The fund shall be financed by:
(a) A portion of permit application and renewal fees (30%).
(b) Administrative fines collected for violations (70%).
(c) Grants and donations.
(d) A 5% levy on all waste disposal charges at permitted facilities.
(3) Monies from the fund shall be used for environmental remediation projects, research and development, public education initiatives, and emergency response activities, with an annual budget review by NEPA and a public report on expenditures published by October 1st each year.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text:
(1) NEPA shall cooperate with municipal authorities in the implementation of this Act.
(2) This cooperation includes:
(a) Sharing information on waste generation and management trends.
(b) Assisting municipalities like Aldmark and Lund Vale in developing local waste management plans.
(c) Joint enforcement efforts where local ordinances overlap with this Act.
(3) NEPA will hold quarterly liaison meetings with municipal representatives from all 8 municipalities to ensure effective coordination.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments.
(2) The first review shall commence no later than 2023-01-01.
(3) Public input shall be sought as part of the review process, with at least 60 days allocated for public consultation. NEPA will submit a comprehensive report detailing the Act's impact and recommending potential changes.

heading: Review of the Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 3 years to assess its effectiveness and make necessary amendments.
(2) The next review shall commence no later than 2027-01-01.
(3) Public input shall be sought as part of the review process, with at least 90 days allocated for public consultation. NEPA will submit a comprehensive report detailing the Act's impact, including an economic analysis, and recommending potential changes.

heading: Offences by Corporations
text:
(1) Where an offence under this Act is committed by a corporation, any director, officer, or manager of the corporation who authorized or permitted the commission of the offence is also liable.
(2) This liability applies unless they can prove that they exercised due diligence to prevent the offence.
(3) Penalties for corporate offences can be up to 500,000 crowns, and individual penalties up to 50,000 crowns.

heading: Liability for Remediation Costs
text:
(1) A permit holder is strictly liable for all costs associated with the remediation of environmental damage caused by their waste management activities.
(2) This liability extends to past and present owners or operators of a facility.
(3) NEPA may recover these costs directly from the liable parties. If the liable party cannot be identified or is insolvent, the Environmental Protection Fund may be used, up to 75% of the total cost, with the remaining 25% falling to the municipality in which the damage occurred.

heading: Emergencies and Disasters
text:
(1) In the event of a national emergency or natural disaster, NEPA may issue temporary exemptions from certain provisions of this Act.
(2) Such exemptions will be limited in scope and duration, not exceeding 6 months, and specifically designed to facilitate immediate response and recovery efforts.
(3) Any temporary exemptions must be publicly announced within 24 hours of being issued and include clear criteria and expiration dates. A report on all exemptions must be submitted to Parliament within 30 days of their expiration.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision of this Act, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of the Act which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this Act are severable. This ensures that the remainder of the Act remains in full force and effect, even if a specific part is deemed unenforceable.

heading: Short Title and Commencement
text:
(1) This Act may be cited as the Waste Management Permits Act.
(2) This Act comes into force on 2018-01-01. All regulations and guidelines necessary for its implementation shall be published by this date to ensure smooth transition and compliance from the effective date for all relevant stakeholders in Nordvale.

heading: Computer courses for schoolteachers
text:
(1) A person employed as a teacher at a primary, secondary or vocational school pays 50 percent of the fee for a municipal adult course in computer skills.
(2) For an online course the percentage is calculated on the fee for the online course.

heading: Computer courses for schoolteachers
text:
(1) A person employed as a teacher at a primary, secondary or vocational school pays 40 percent of the fee for a municipal adult course in computer skills.
(2) For an online course the percentage is calculated on the fee for the online course.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the requirements and fees for obtaining authorization to work within the Republic of Nordvale. It applies to all individuals seeking employment or engaging in any form of remunerated activity within Nordvale's borders, regardless of their nationality or the duration of their intended stay. The provisions herein aim to ensure fair labor practices and contribute to the economic stability of Nordvale by regulating the inflow of foreign workers.

heading: Eligibility for Work Permit
text: An individual is eligible to apply for a Work Permit if they are at least 18 years of age and possess a valid passport from their country of origin. Applicants must also demonstrate that they have received a genuine offer of employment from a Nordvale-based employer, for a position that lasts a minimum of six months. The employment offer must specify the weekly working hours, which cannot be less than 20 hours per week.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a Work Permit must be submitted digitally through the Nordvale Labor Department's online portal. A complete application includes a scanned copy of the applicant's passport, the employment offer letter, and proof of educational qualifications. Incomplete applications will be rejected within 7 working days, and the application fee will not be refunded. All documents must be in Nordvalean or accompanied by a certified translation.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns is required for all Work Permit applications. This fee must be paid at the time of submission via an approved electronic payment method. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including verification of documents and background checks. Failure to pay the full amount will result in the immediate rejection of the application.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 1,500 crowns is required for all Work Permit applications. This fee must be paid at the time of submission via an approved electronic payment method. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including verification of documents and background checks. Failure to pay the full amount will result in the immediate rejection of the application.

heading: Processing Time
text: The standard processing time for Work Permit applications is 45 working days from the date of submission of a complete application. Applicants will be notified by email upon receipt of their application and once a decision has been made. Urgent processing may be available for an additional fee as outlined in section 6, reducing the processing time to 15 working days for eligible applications.

heading: Processing Time
text: The standard processing time for Work Permit applications is 50 working days from the date of submission of a complete application. Applicants will be notified by email upon receipt of their application and once a decision has been made. Urgent processing may be available for an additional fee as outlined in section 6, reducing the processing time to 20 working days for eligible applications.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: Applicants may opt for expedited processing of their Work Permit application for an additional fee of 3,000 crowns. This fee is separate from the standard application fee and is also non-refundable. Expedited processing aims to provide a decision within 15 working days. This option is only available for applicants with employment offers in critical shortage sectors as defined by the Ministry of Labor.

heading: Expedited Processing Fee
text: Applicants may opt for expedited processing of their Work Permit application for an additional fee of 3,500 crowns. This fee is separate from the standard application fee and is also non-refundable. Expedited processing aims to provide a decision within 15 working days. This option is only available for applicants with employment offers in critical shortage sectors as defined by the Ministry of Labor.

heading: Employer Responsibilities
text: Employers offering employment to Work Permit applicants must be registered with the Nordvale Chamber of Commerce for at least two years. They are responsible for ensuring that the terms of employment offered comply with Nordvale's labor laws, including minimum wage requirements. Employers must also provide a signed declaration confirming the genuine nature of the job offer and the necessity of hiring a foreign worker for the specific role.

heading: Minimum Wage Requirement
text: All Work Permit holders must be paid a salary that meets or exceeds the Nordvalean national minimum wage. As of the effective date of this Act, the minimum wage is 150 crowns per hour. Employers found paying less than the stipulated minimum wage will face immediate sanctions, including fines up to 10,000 crowns and potential revocation of their ability to hire foreign workers for a period of 5 years.

heading: Minimum Wage Requirement
text: All Work Permit holders must be paid a salary that meets or exceeds the Nordvalean national minimum wage. As of the effective date of this version, the minimum wage is 165 crowns per hour.
