Employers found paying less than the stipulated minimum wage will face immediate sanctions, including fines up to 12,000 crowns and potential revocation of their ability to hire foreign workers for a period of 5 years.

heading: Work Permit Duration
text: Initial Work Permits are typically issued for a duration of one year. The permit specifies the employer and the position for which the individual is authorized to work. Work Permit holders are not permitted to change employers or positions without applying for a new Work Permit, as detailed in section 12. Extensions may be granted, subject to the conditions outlined in section 10.

heading: Work Permit Duration
text: Initial Work Permits are typically issued for a duration of eighteen months. The permit specifies the employer and the position for which the individual is authorized to work. Work Permit holders are not permitted to change employers or positions without applying for a new Work Permit, as detailed in section 12. Extensions may be granted, subject to the conditions outlined in section 10.

heading: Extension of Work Permit
text: Work Permit holders may apply for an extension of their permit up to 90 days before its expiration. An extension can be granted for a maximum of two additional years, provided the applicant continues to meet the eligibility criteria and remains employed by the original employer. The fee for an extension application is 800 crowns, and the processing time is 30 working days. Multiple extensions are permitted.

heading: Extension of Work Permit
text: Work Permit holders may apply for an extension of their permit up to 120 days before its expiration. An extension can be granted for a maximum of two additional years, provided the applicant continues to meet the eligibility criteria and remains employed by the original employer. The fee for an extension application is 950 crowns, and the processing time is 35 working days. Multiple extensions are permitted.

heading: Conditions of Work Permit
text: A Work Permit is subject to several conditions, including maintaining valid health insurance coverage throughout the permit's duration and adhering to all Nordvalean laws. The permit holder must reside within Nordvale for at least 183 days per year. Failure to comply with these conditions may result in the revocation of the Work Permit, as detailed in section 17, and potential deportation.

heading: Change of Employer
text: A Work Permit holder wishing to change employers must apply for a new Work Permit. This application is treated as a new submission, requiring all supporting documents and the standard application fee of 1,200 crowns. The individual may not commence employment with the new employer until the new Work Permit has been approved and issued. This process ensures that the new employment also meets all stipulated requirements.

heading: Change of Employer
text: A Work Permit holder wishing to change employers must apply for a new Work Permit. This application is treated as a new submission, requiring all supporting documents and the standard application fee of 1,500 crowns. The individual may not commence employment with the new employer until the new Work Permit has been approved and issued. This process ensures that the new employment also meets all stipulated requirements.

heading: Required Documentation for Change of Employer
text:
(1) When applying for a change of employer, the applicant must submit:
(a) A new offer of employment from a Nordvale-based employer.
(b) Proof of termination from the previous employer.
(c) An updated declaration of good standing from the new employer.
(2) All documents must be submitted in digital format and meet the requirements specified in section 3.

heading: Reporting Changes in Employment
text: Work Permit holders are required to report any change in their employment status, including termination or resignation, to the Nordvale Labor Department within 14 working days. Failure to report such changes may lead to a review of the Work Permit's validity. Employers are also obligated to report the termination of a Work Permit holder's employment within 10 working days to ensure compliance.

heading: Reporting Changes in Employment
text: Work Permit holders are required to report any change in their employment status, including termination or resignation, to the Nordvale Labor Department within 7 working days. Failure to report such changes may lead to a review of the Work Permit's validity. Employers are also obligated to report the termination of a Work Permit holder's employment within 5 working days to ensure compliance.

heading: Appeals Process
text: Applicants whose Work Permit applications have been rejected may appeal the decision within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice. Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board of the Nordvale Labor Department. The Appeals Board will review the application and supporting documentation, and a decision will be rendered within 60 working days. A non-refundable appeal fee of 500 crowns applies.

heading: Appeals Board Decision
text: The decision of the Appeals Board is final and binding. No further administrative appeals are permitted within the Nordvale Labor Department. However, an applicant may seek judicial review through the Nordvale District Court within 20 days of the Appeals Board's decision, provided there are grounds to believe that a procedural error occurred during the review process.

heading: Revocation of Work Permit
text:
A Work Permit may be revoked if the holder: 
(a) Provides false information during the application process.
(b) Fails to comply with the conditions of their permit as outlined in section 11.
(c) Commits a criminal offense in Nordvale or abroad, resulting in a conviction punishable by more than 3 months imprisonment.
(d) Becomes unemployed for more than 60 consecutive days without actively seeking new employment and reporting it to the Labor Department. The revocation process will involve a 14-day notice period.

heading: Revocation of Work Permit
text:
A Work Permit may be revoked if the holder: 
(a) Provides false information during the application process.
(b) Fails to comply with the conditions of their permit as outlined in section 11.
(c) Commits a criminal offense in Nordvale or abroad, resulting in a conviction punishable by more than 2 months imprisonment.
(d) Becomes unemployed for more than 45 consecutive days without actively seeking new employment and reporting it to the Labor Department. The revocation process will involve a 10-day notice period.

heading: Voluntary Termination of Employment
text: If a Work Permit holder voluntarily terminates their employment, they must notify the Nordvale Labor Department within 7 working days. The Work Permit remains valid for a grace period of 30 days, during which the individual may seek new employment. If new employment is secured within this period, a new Work Permit application must be submitted as per section 12. Failing to secure new employment within 30 days will lead to the revocation of the permit.

heading: Voluntary Termination of Employment
text: If a Work Permit holder voluntarily terminates their employment, they must notify the Nordvale Labor Department within 5 working days. The Work Permit remains valid for a grace period of 21 days, during which the individual may seek new employment. If new employment is secured within this period, a new Work Permit application must be submitted as per section 12. Failing to secure new employment within 21 days will lead to the revocation of the permit.

heading: Dependents of Work Permit Holders
text: Dependents of Work Permit holders, including spouses and children under 18 years of age, may apply for a dependent visa. This visa does not automatically confer the right to work. A separate Work Permit application must be submitted by any dependent seeking employment, fulfilling all requirements outlined in sections 2 and 3. The dependent visa is tied to the primary Work Permit holder's status.

heading: Short-Term Work Authorization
text: Individuals entering Nordvale for work purposes for a period not exceeding 90 days may apply for a Short-Term Work Authorization. This authorization is available for specific, pre-approved job categories, such as expert consultants or specialized trainers. The application fee is 600 crowns, and processing takes 10 working days. This authorization cannot be extended beyond 90 days.

heading: Short-Term Work Authorization
text: Individuals entering Nordvale for work purposes for a period not exceeding 60 days may apply for a Short-Term Work Authorization. This authorization is available for specific, pre-approved job categories, such as expert consultants or specialized trainers. The application fee is 750 crowns, and processing takes 8 working days. This authorization cannot be extended beyond 60 days.

heading: Specialized Professional Permit
text: Highly skilled professionals with advanced degrees or at least 10 years of specialized experience may apply for a Specialized Professional Permit. This permit has an initial duration of three years and allows for multiple employer changes within approved sectors without requiring a new Work Permit application each time. The application fee is 4,000 crowns, and a minimum annual salary of 500,000 crowns is required. Processing time is 30 working days.

heading: Specialized Professional Permit
text: Highly skilled professionals with advanced degrees or at least 12 years of specialized experience may apply for a Specialized Professional Permit. This permit has an initial duration of four years and allows for multiple employer changes within approved sectors without requiring a new Work Permit application each time. The application fee is 4,500 crowns, and a minimum annual salary of 550,000 crowns is required. Processing time is 25 working days.

heading: Permit for Business Owners
text: Individuals wishing to establish and operate a business in Nordvale may apply for a Business Owner Permit. Applicants must demonstrate a minimum capital investment of 100,000 crowns and present a detailed business plan projected to create at least 2 full-time jobs within the first 18 months. The application fee is 5,000 crowns. This permit is initially valid for two years and may be extended if the business meets its targets.

heading: Temporary Seasonal Work Permit
text: A Temporary Seasonal Work Permit is available for specific industries such as agriculture and tourism, for a maximum period of six months. Applicants must have a confirmed job offer for seasonal work. The application fee is 500 crowns, and processing takes 14 working days. This permit does not allow for extensions and workers must depart Nordvale upon its expiration. The minimum age for this permit is 19 years.

heading: Temporary Seasonal Work Permit
text: A Temporary Seasonal Work Permit is available for specific industries such as agriculture and tourism, for a maximum period of five months. Applicants must have a confirmed job offer for seasonal work. The application fee is 550 crowns, and processing takes 12 working days. This permit does not allow for extensions and workers must depart Nordvale upon its expiration. The minimum age for this permit is 20 years.

heading: Employer Compliance Audits
text: The Nordvale Labor Department reserves the right to conduct unannounced audits of employers hiring Work Permit holders to ensure compliance with all provisions of this Act. Audits may include reviewing employment contracts, payroll records, and working conditions. Employers found in violation of this Act, including those failing to adhere to minimum wage or working hour requirements, will face penalties as outlined in section 8.

heading: Data Protection
text: All personal data collected during the Work Permit application process will be handled in accordance with Nordvale's data protection regulations. Information will be stored securely for a period of 10 years following the expiration or revocation of a permit. Data will only be shared with other government agencies for purposes of national security, law enforcement, or public health, and only upon official request.

heading: Penalties for Unauthorized Work
text: Any individual found working in Nordvale without a valid Work Permit will be subject to immediate deportation and a ban from re-entering Nordvale for a period of 5 years. Employers found to be employing unauthorized workers will face fines of up to 25,000 crowns per unauthorized worker and a permanent ban on hiring foreign workers. Repeat offenses will incur higher fines and potential criminal charges.

heading: Penalties for Unauthorized Work
text: Any individual found working in Nordvale without a valid Work Permit will be subject to immediate deportation and a ban from re-entering Nordvale for a period of 7 years. Employers found to be employing unauthorized workers will face fines of up to 30,000 crowns per unauthorized worker and a permanent ban on hiring foreign workers. Repeat offenses will incur higher fines and potential criminal charges.

heading: Fees for Replacement Permit
text: In the event of a lost, stolen, or damaged Work Permit, a replacement permit may be issued upon application to the Nordvale Labor Department. A fee of 300 crowns is required for the issuance of a replacement. The applicant must provide a police report for lost or stolen permits. The processing time for a replacement permit is 5 working days from the submission of all required documentation.

heading: Exemptions
text: Certain categories of individuals are exempt from the requirement of obtaining a Work Permit. These include diplomats and consular staff accredited to Nordvale, individuals invited by the Nordvalean government for official duties, and recognized international aid workers operating in Nordvale. All exempt individuals must still register their presence with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs upon arrival.

heading: Validity of Foreign Qualifications
text: All foreign educational and professional qualifications submitted with a Work Permit application must be formally recognized by the Nordvale Qualifications Authority. A processing fee of 700 crowns applies for this recognition service, payable directly to the Authority. The recognition process can take up to 20 working days and must be completed before a Work Permit can be issued.

heading: Annual Review
text: The provisions of this Act will be subject to an annual review by the Nordvale Labor Department to ensure their effectiveness and relevance to the national labor market and economic conditions. Any proposed amendments or updates resulting from this review will be presented to the Parliament of Nordvale for approval. The first review will commence on January 1st, 2019.

text: (Repealed.)

heading: Payment terms
text: Where the person liable is a certified rope-access technician for at least one year, the annual energy rebate of 350 crowns shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Concessions
text: The temporary licence is reduced to no crowns for any person who has been a registered peat cutter for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating broadcasting operations within the Republic of Nordvale. It covers the licensing requirements for all entities wishing to transmit radio or television signals to the public. The primary goal is to ensure orderly use of broadcast frequencies, promote diverse content, and protect public interest in broadcasting. All provisions herein apply to both new applicants and existing licence holders, setting out their obligations and the penalties for non-compliance. This Act does not apply to private, non-public communications.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a radio or television broadcasting service within Nordvale without first obtaining a valid licence issued by the Broadcasting Authority, as outlined in this Act. Operating a broadcasting service without such a licence is a serious offence, subject to significant penalties. This requirement applies regardless of the broadcast technology used, including terrestrial, satellite, or internet-based transmissions intended for general public reception within the national borders. A provisional licence may be granted for a period not exceeding 90 days under specific circumstances.

heading: Application process
text: Applications for a broadcasting licence must be submitted to the Broadcasting Authority on the prescribed form. Each application must include a detailed business plan, a proposed programming schedule for the first 12 months, and proof of financial capability to operate for at least 24 months. An application fee of 5,000 crowns is required at the time of submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 14 days with a request for additional information, and the processing period will only commence once all required documents are received.

heading: Application fee
text: The initial application fee for a broadcasting licence is 5,000 crowns. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the application. The fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial reviews and background checks. This fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Failure to pay the fee will result in the application not being processed. No discounts or waivers are available for this fee.

heading: Application fee
text: The initial application fee for a broadcasting licence is 7,500 crowns. This fee is non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the application. The fee covers administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial reviews and background checks. This fee must be paid in full at the time of application submission. Failure to pay the fee will result in the application not being processed. A 10% discount may be applied for non-profit community broadcasters.

heading: Licence duration
text: A broadcasting licence, once issued, is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance. Licensees must apply for renewal at least 6 months before the expiry date. Failure to apply for renewal within this timeframe may result in the licence lapsing, requiring a new application process. The Authority will notify licensees of their upcoming expiry date approximately 9 months in advance. No licence will be automatically renewed.

heading: Licence renewal
text: Applications for licence renewal must be submitted no less than 6 months and no more than 12 months prior to the current licence's expiry date. A renewal fee of 3,000 crowns is required. The renewal process involves a review of the licensee's compliance history and programming quality over the preceding licence term. The Authority may request additional documentation or a public hearing if significant issues are identified during the review. Renewals are not guaranteed and are subject to the same public interest considerations as initial applications.

heading: Renewal fee
text: The fee for renewing a broadcasting licence is 3,000 crowns. This fee is payable upon submission of the renewal application and is non-refundable. The renewal fee covers the administrative costs of reviewing the licensee's performance and ensuring continued compliance with broadcasting standards. Failure to pay the renewal fee will result in the application for renewal being rejected, potentially leading to the expiry of the licence. A late payment penalty of 500 crowns applies if paid within 30 days of the due date.

heading: Renewal fee
text: The fee for renewing a broadcasting licence is 4,000 crowns. This fee is payable upon submission of the renewal application and is non-refundable. The renewal fee covers the administrative costs of reviewing the licensee's performance and ensuring continued compliance with broadcasting standards. Failure to pay the renewal fee will result in the application for renewal being rejected, potentially leading to the expiry of the licence. A late payment penalty of 750 crowns applies if paid within 30 days of the due date, after which the application is considered withdrawn.

heading: Licence transfer
text: A broadcasting licence may not be transferred, assigned, or otherwise disposed of, in whole or in part, without the prior written approval of the Broadcasting Authority. Any proposed transfer must be submitted with a detailed plan outlining the new ownership structure, programming intentions, and financial capacity of the proposed transferee. An application fee of 10,000 crowns is associated with requesting a licence transfer. The Authority reserves the right to deny any transfer if it deems the proposed new owner unsuitable or if the transfer is not in the public interest.

heading: Content standards
text: All licensees must adhere to established content standards. Broadcasting content must be accurate, impartial, and not incite hatred or violence. Material deemed offensive or inappropriate for general audiences must be broadcast only during designated late-night hours, typically between 23:00 and 05:00. Broadcasters must ensure that programming reflects the diversity of Nordvale's population and promotes civic discourse. At least 40% of broadcast content between 06:00 and 22:00 must originate from within Nordvale.

heading: Local content quotas
text: Each licensee must ensure that at least 40% of its total broadcast time between 06:00 and 22:00 comprises content produced in Nordvale. For television broadcasters, this includes drama, documentary, and news programming. For radio broadcasters, it includes music by Nordvale artists and locally produced talk shows. Compliance is monitored quarterly, and any shortfall exceeding 5% may result in penalties. News and public affairs programming must constitute at least 15% of the local content quota.

heading: Local content quotas
text: Each licensee must ensure that at least 45% of its total broadcast time between 06:00 and 22:00 comprises content produced in Nordvale. For television broadcasters, this includes drama, documentary, and news programming. For radio broadcasters, it includes music by Nordvale artists and locally produced talk shows. Compliance is monitored quarterly, and any shortfall exceeding 3% may result in penalties. News and public affairs programming must constitute at least 18% of the local content quota.

heading: Advertising limits
text: Advertising content is limited to a maximum of 12 minutes per hour for television broadcasts and 15 minutes per hour for radio broadcasts. Advertisements must be clearly distinguishable from programming content. During children's programming, advertising is restricted to 6 minutes per hour and must not feature products directly targeting children under the age of 8. Sponsorship announcements are included in these limits. Promotional content for the broadcaster's own programming is exempt from these limits, provided it does not exceed 3 minutes per hour.

heading: Religious broadcasting
text: Religious broadcasting services are subject to the same licensing requirements as other broadcasters. While promoting religious views is permitted, such broadcasts must not engage in proselytizing that denigrates other faiths or promote discrimination. Any direct appeals for financial contributions must be clearly identified and limited to no more than 5 minutes per hour. Content must be clearly labelled as religious programming. Broadcasters must offer a diversity of religious viewpoints if they dedicate more than 10% of their airtime to religious matters.

heading: Political broadcasting
text: During election periods, all broadcasters must provide fair and equitable access to airtime for all registered political parties and candidates. This includes ensuring balanced coverage in news and current affairs programming. Paid political advertisements must be clearly identified as such and are subject to the same time limits as commercial advertising. No single political party may purchase more than 30% of the available political advertising slots on any given station during a 24-hour period. Broadcasters must maintain records of all political broadcasts for at least 180 days.

heading: Technical standards
text: All broadcasting equipment and transmission facilities must comply with the technical standards set by the Broadcasting Authority. This includes specifications for signal strength, frequency allocation, and interference prevention. Equipment must be regularly inspected, at least once every 24 months, by certified technicians. Any modifications to transmission apparatus must be approved by the Authority prior to implementation. Failure to meet these standards may result in suspension of broadcasting privileges until compliance is achieved. The Authority may conduct unannounced inspections at any time.

heading: Frequency allocation
text: The Broadcasting Authority is responsible for the allocation of broadcast frequencies. Frequencies are allocated based on technical feasibility, public interest, and efficient use of the spectrum. No licensee has exclusive rights to a frequency beyond the term of their licence. The Authority may reallocate frequencies if necessary due to technological advancements or changes in national broadcasting policy. Broadcasters will be given at least 18 months' notice of any planned frequency reallocation that affects their operations.

heading: Emergency broadcasts
text: All licensees are required to broadcast emergency messages issued by the national or local authorities. These messages take precedence over all other programming and must be transmitted immediately upon receipt. Broadcasters must have the necessary equipment and procedures in place to receive and disseminate such alerts 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Failure to broadcast an emergency message without valid technical reason may result in immediate licence suspension. Testing of the emergency broadcast system will occur quarterly, without prior notification to broadcasters.

heading: Record keeping
text: Licensees must maintain detailed records of all broadcast content, including programme logs, advertising schedules, and any public complaints received. These records must be kept for a minimum of 90 days from the date of broadcast and must be made available to the Broadcasting Authority upon request within 7 working days. For news and current affairs programming, records must be kept for 180 days. Failure to maintain adequate records is an offence under this Act.

heading: Record keeping
text: Licensees must maintain detailed records of all broadcast content, including programme logs, advertising schedules, and any public complaints received. These records must be kept for a minimum of 120 days from the date of broadcast and must be made available to the Broadcasting Authority upon request within 5 working days. For news and current affairs programming, records must be kept for 240 days. Failure to maintain adequate records is an offence under this Act, incurring a penalty of 10,000 crowns per instance.

heading: Public complaints
text: Licensees must establish a clear and accessible procedure for receiving and responding to public complaints regarding their programming. All complaints must be acknowledged within 7 working days and a substantive response provided within 30 working days. Records of all complaints and their resolutions must be kept as per section 17. The Broadcasting Authority may review complaint handling procedures and may intervene if a licensee demonstrates a pattern of unresolved or poorly handled complaints. A summary of complaints received must be submitted annually to the Authority.

heading: Ownership restrictions
text: No single entity or individual may hold more than a 30% ownership stake in more than three television broadcasting licences, or more than four radio broadcasting licences within Nordvale. Foreign ownership of any broadcasting licence is limited to a maximum of 25%. These restrictions are designed to promote media diversity and prevent undue concentration of media power. Applicants must disclose all direct and indirect ownership interests as part of their licence application. Any changes in ownership exceeding 5% must be reported to the Authority within 30 days.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: All licensees must submit an annual report to the Broadcasting Authority by March 31st each year. This report must include details of their programming schedule, compliance with local content quotas, advertising minutes broadcast, financial statements, and a summary of public complaints. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a fine of 2,000 crowns for each month or part thereof that the report is delayed. The Authority may request additional reports or information at any time, with a response period of 14 days.

heading: Reporting requirements
text: All licensees must submit an annual report to the Broadcasting Authority by February 28th each year. This report must include details of their programming schedule, compliance with local content quotas, advertising minutes broadcast, financial statements, and a summary of public complaints. Failure to submit the annual report on time may result in a fine of 3,000 crowns for each month or part thereof that the report is delayed. The Authority may request additional reports or information at any time, with a response period of 10 days.

heading: Breach of licence conditions
text: Any breach of the conditions stipulated in a broadcasting licence or the provisions of this Act may result in enforcement action by the Broadcasting Authority. Minor breaches may result in a warning letter and a requirement to rectify the issue within 30 days. Repeated or more serious breaches may lead to financial penalties, suspension of broadcasting privileges, or ultimately, revocation of the licence. The licensee will be given an opportunity to present their case before any final decision is made by the Authority.

heading: Financial penalties
text: The Broadcasting Authority may impose financial penalties for breaches of this Act. For minor infractions, penalties can range from 1,000 crowns to 10,000 crowns. For serious or repeated breaches, penalties can be up to 100,000 crowns. The exact amount will depend on the severity of the breach, its impact on the public, and the licensee's compliance history. Penalties must be paid within 30 days of the notice of fine. Failure to pay may result in further enforcement action, including licence suspension.

heading: Licence suspension
text: A broadcasting licence may be suspended by the Broadcasting Authority for severe or persistent breaches of this Act or licence conditions. A suspension may be for a specified period, not exceeding 90 days, during which the licensee is prohibited from broadcasting. During a suspension, the licensee must still comply with all reporting requirements and work to rectify the issues that led to the suspension. Reinstatement of the licence is contingent upon demonstrating full compliance. No compensation will be paid for losses incurred during suspension.

heading: Licence revocation
text: The Broadcasting Authority may revoke a broadcasting licence in cases of gross misconduct, repeated serious breaches, or failure to comply with a suspension order. Revocation means the permanent termination of broadcasting rights. Before revocation, the licensee will be given at least 30 days' notice and an opportunity to be heard by the Authority. Upon revocation, all broadcasting operations must cease immediately, and all allocated frequencies must be vacated within 7 days. There is no refund of any licence fees paid.

heading: Appeals
text: Any decision made by the Broadcasting Authority regarding licence applications, renewals, transfers, penalties, suspensions, or revocations may be appealed to the Broadcasting Appeals Tribunal. An appeal must be lodged within 30 days of receiving the Authority's decision. The Tribunal's decision is final. The appeal process does not automatically stay the Authority's decision, unless specifically ordered by the Tribunal. A non-refundable fee of 2,500 crowns is required to lodge an appeal.

heading: Broadcasting Authority
text: The Broadcasting Authority is established as an independent body responsible for administering this Act. Its functions include issuing and renewing licences, monitoring compliance, investigating complaints, imposing penalties, and allocating frequencies. The Authority comprises five members appointed by the government for terms of 3 years, with a maximum of two consecutive terms. The Authority must publish an annual report on its activities and decisions by June 30th each year. Its budget is funded by licence fees and government allocation.

heading: Confidentiality
text: All information submitted by applicants and licensees will be treated with appropriate confidentiality by the Broadcasting Authority. However, certain information, such as licence holder names, broadcast frequencies, and general programming types, may be made publicly available. Financial information and detailed business plans will remain confidential unless disclosure is required by law or for a public hearing process. Any information deemed commercially sensitive must be clearly marked as such upon submission. The Authority will take all reasonable steps to protect confidential data.

heading: Fees schedule
text: The Broadcasting Authority shall publish and maintain a schedule of all fees and charges applicable under this Act. This schedule will be reviewed annually and any proposed changes will be announced at least 60 days before they come into effect. Current fees include a 5,000 crowns application fee, a 3,000 crowns renewal fee, and a 10,000 crowns transfer fee. All fees are payable in Nordvale crowns. The Authority may adjust fees based on operational costs or inflation, but not by more than 10% in any given year.

heading: Fees schedule
text: The Broadcasting Authority shall publish and maintain a schedule of all fees and charges applicable under this Act. This schedule will be reviewed annually and any proposed changes will be announced at least 90 days before they come into effect. Current fees include a 7,500 crowns application fee, a 4,000 crowns renewal fee, and a 12,000 crowns transfer fee. All fees are payable in Nordvale crowns. The Authority may adjust fees based on operational costs or inflation, but not by more than 15% in any given year, and must justify any increase over 5%.

heading: Broadcasting code
text: The Broadcasting Authority shall develop and publish a comprehensive Broadcasting Code. This Code will provide detailed guidelines on content standards, advertising practices, public service obligations, and other aspects of broadcasting conduct. Licensees are required to comply with the Broadcasting Code, which will be updated periodically, with licensees given at least 3 months' notice of any significant changes. The Code will be publicly available on the Authority's website and in print, and will include examples of good practice and potential breaches.

heading: Community broadcasting
text: Specific provisions may apply to community broadcasting licences, which are intended for non-profit organizations serving a defined local community. These licences may have reduced fees, typically 50% of standard fees, and adjusted local content quotas, requiring 60% local content. However, they are subject to the same technical and general content standards. Community broadcasters must demonstrate strong local support and a clear public service mission. Their maximum broadcast power may be restricted to 1 kilowatt. They must not carry more than 8 minutes of advertising per hour.

heading: Community broadcasting
text: Specific provisions may apply to community broadcasting licences, which are intended for non-profit organizations serving a defined local community. These licences may have reduced fees, typically 60% of standard fees, and adjusted local content quotas, requiring 65% local content. However, they are subject to the same technical and general content standards. Community broadcasters must demonstrate strong local support and a clear public service mission. Their maximum broadcast power may be restricted to 0.5 kilowatts. They must not carry more than 6 minutes of advertising per hour, and this must be non-commercial in nature.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Broadcasting' means the transmission of electro-magnetic signals intended for direct reception by the general public.
(2) 'Licensee' means a person or entity holding a valid broadcasting licence issued under this Act.
(3) 'Authority' refers to the Broadcasting Authority established by section 26 of this Act.
(4) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale.
(5) 'Local content' refers to programming predominantly conceived, produced, and performed by citizens or residents of Nordvale.
(6) 'Public interest' means the collective well-being and benefit of the citizens of Nordvale as determined by the Authority.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Any broadcasting operations legally active prior to the enactment of this Act must apply for a licence within 180 days of the Act coming into force. Such existing operators will be granted a temporary licence for a period of up to 12 months to allow for full application processing. During this transitional period, they must comply with all general content standards and technical requirements of this Act. Failure to apply within the specified timeframe will result in immediate cessation of broadcasting operations and potential penalties for unlicensed broadcasting. The application fee for existing operators during this period is reduced by 20%.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Concessions

heading: Recognised trades
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, the keeper of a registered windmill for at least one year pays no fee or allowance under FDA §22.

heading: Reduced charges
text: For a registered seed bank curator, the deadline for paying any fee or allowance specified in FDA §22 is extended by 30 days.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the licensing of facilities within the Republic of Nordvale that engage in the processing of waste materials. Its primary purpose is to ensure environmental protection, public health, and responsible waste management practices across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik. This Act applies to any operation that receives, sorts, compacts, incinerates, chemically treats, or otherwise alters waste for disposal or recycling. It does not apply to small-scale composting by individual households or minor waste collection points managed by municipalities, provided they handle less than 50 kilograms of waste per day. The provisions herein aim to promote sustainable resource use and minimize ecological impact from waste processing activities.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(1) "Facility" means any land, building, or structure used for the purpose of waste processing.
(2) "Licensee" means a person or entity holding a valid licence issued under this Act.
(3) "Minister" refers to the Minister responsible for Environmental Affairs.
(4) "Waste" means any discarded material, including solid, liquid, gaseous, or radioactive substances, which is no longer intended for its original purpose.
(5) "Processing" includes any operation that changes the physical, chemical, or biological characteristics of waste.
(6) "Application" refers to a formal request for a licence or renewal of a licence, submitted as per section 5.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a waste processing facility within Nordvale without a valid licence issued by the Minister in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any facility found operating without a licence shall be subject to immediate closure and penalties as outlined in section 30. This requirement applies to all new facilities and any existing facilities that undergo significant operational changes, defined as a change in processing capacity by more than 25% or the introduction of new waste types not previously approved. Facilities handling less than 100 kilograms of non-hazardous waste per day are exempt from this requirement.

heading: Licence requirement
text: No person or entity shall operate a waste processing facility within Nordvale without a valid licence issued by the Minister in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any facility found operating without a licence shall be subject to immediate closure and penalties as outlined in section 30. This requirement applies to all new facilities and any existing facilities that undergo significant operational changes, defined as a change in processing capacity by more than 15% or the introduction of new waste types not previously approved. Facilities handling less than 75 kilograms of non-hazardous waste per day are exempt from this requirement.

heading: Application for licence
text: An application for a waste processing facility licence must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form. The application must include detailed plans of the facility, a description of the waste types to be processed, estimated daily volumes, proposed processing methods, and an environmental impact assessment report. A non-refundable application fee of 5,000 crowns must accompany the submission. All plans must be certified by a registered engineer with at least 10 years of experience in environmental infrastructure. The application must also include a community engagement plan outlining how local residents within a 5-kilometer radius will be informed.

heading: Application for licence
text: An application for a waste processing facility licence must be submitted to the Minister in the prescribed form. The application must include detailed plans of the facility, a description of the waste types to be processed, estimated daily volumes, proposed processing methods, and an environmental impact assessment report. A non-refundable application fee of 7,500 crowns must accompany the submission. All plans must be certified by a registered engineer with at least 12 years of experience in environmental infrastructure. The application must also include a community engagement plan outlining how local residents within a 3-kilometer radius will be informed and consulted through at least two public meetings.

heading: Processing of applications
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Minister shall have a period of 90 days to review the submission and make a decision. During this period, the Minister may request additional information or clarification from the applicant within 30 days of receiving the initial application. Failure to provide requested information within 60 days of the request may result in the rejection of the application. The Minister shall consult with relevant municipal authorities, including those in Dunmere and Elsby, regarding the proposed facility's impact on local infrastructure and services. A public notice of the application shall be posted for 21 days in the affected municipality.

heading: Licence issuance criteria
text:
A licence may be issued if the Minister is satisfied that:
(a) The proposed facility complies with all environmental standards and public health regulations.
(b) The applicant has demonstrated the financial capacity to operate the facility responsibly.
(c) The proposed processing methods are safe and effective.
(d) The facility's location minimizes adverse impacts on surrounding communities and ecosystems.
(e) The applicant has a satisfactory track record regarding compliance with environmental regulations over the past 5 years.
(f) The facility's operational plan includes provisions for emergency response and site closure, ensuring environmental remediation.

heading: Licence conditions
text: Every licence issued under this Act shall be subject to conditions deemed necessary by the Minister to ensure compliance with environmental protection and public health standards. These conditions may include, but are not limited to, limits on the types and quantities of waste processed, specific operational procedures, monitoring requirements, reporting obligations, and requirements for the implementation of best available technologies. The Minister may impose additional conditions at any time if new environmental risks are identified or if the facility's operations change significantly, with 60 days' notice given to the licensee.

heading: Licence term and renewal
text: A waste processing facility licence shall be valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 120 days before the expiry date of the current licence. The renewal application must include an updated operational plan, a summary of compliance records over the previous term, and a non-refundable renewal fee of 3,000 crowns. The Minister will review the renewal application based on the facility's performance and continued adherence to all licence conditions and statutory requirements. Late applications may incur an additional fee of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Licence term and renewal
text: A waste processing facility licence shall be valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue. An application for renewal must be submitted at least 150 days before the expiry date of the current licence. The renewal application must include an updated operational plan, a summary of compliance records over the previous term, and a non-refundable renewal fee of 4,000 crowns. The Minister will review the renewal application based on the facility's performance and continued adherence to all licence conditions and statutory requirements. Late applications may incur an additional fee of 2,000 crowns, and applications submitted less than 60 days before expiry will be treated as new applications.

heading: Public consultation
text: For new licence applications or significant modifications to existing licences, the Minister shall ensure that a period of public consultation, lasting at least 30 days, is conducted. This consultation period allows interested parties, particularly residents within a 2-kilometer radius of the proposed facility, to submit written comments or concerns. Public meetings may be organized in collaboration with municipalities like Fennick and Grauby, if deemed necessary, especially for facilities with a proposed processing capacity exceeding 500 tonnes per day. All public comments received shall be considered by the Minister before a final decision is made.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: All new licence applications for facilities with a processing capacity exceeding 100 tonnes per day, or those located within 500 meters of a residential area, must include a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) report. This report must analyze potential impacts on air quality, water resources, soil, biodiversity, and noise levels. The EIA must be prepared by an independent consultant approved by the Minister, with at least 8 years of experience in environmental science. The report must also propose mitigation measures for all identified negative impacts, and a contingency plan for accidental environmental releases.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: All new licence applications for facilities with a processing capacity exceeding 75 tonnes per day, or those located within 750 meters of a residential area, must include a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) report. This report must analyze potential impacts on air quality, water resources, soil, biodiversity, and noise levels. The EIA must be prepared by an independent consultant approved by the Minister, with at least 10 years of experience in environmental science. The report must also propose mitigation measures for all identified negative impacts, and a contingency plan for accidental environmental releases, reviewed annually by the licensee.

heading: Monitoring and reporting
text: Licensees are required to regularly monitor their operations to ensure compliance with all licence conditions and environmental standards. This includes monitoring emissions, effluent discharge, and waste residue. Quarterly reports detailing monitoring results, waste volumes processed, and any incidents or deviations from operational plans must be submitted to the Minister. These reports must be certified by a qualified environmental officer employed by the facility or an independent auditor. Failure to submit reports on time may result in a fine of 1,000 crowns for each week of delay, up to a maximum of 10,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Inspections
text: Authorized inspectors appointed by the Minister shall have the right to enter and inspect any licensed waste processing facility at any reasonable time, with 24 hours' notice, to verify compliance with this Act and the licence conditions. Inspectors may take samples, examine records, and interview personnel. In cases of suspected immediate environmental danger or public health risk, inspectors may enter without prior notice. Obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence punishable under section 32. At least one unannounced inspection will occur every 12 months for high-risk facilities.

heading: Record keeping
text: Every licensee must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all waste received, processed, and disposed of, including the origin, type, and quantity of waste. These records must be kept for a minimum period of 7 years and made available to the Minister or authorized inspectors upon request. Records must also detail maintenance activities, equipment calibrations, and any environmental incidents or spills. Digital records must be backed up weekly, and physical records stored in a secure, fire-resistant location within the facility premises or a designated archive.

heading: Record keeping
text: Every licensee must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all waste received, processed, and disposed of, including the origin, type, and quantity of waste. These records must be kept for a minimum period of 10 years and made available to the Minister or authorized inspectors upon request. Records must also detail maintenance activities, equipment calibrations, and any environmental incidents or spills. Digital records must be backed up daily, and physical records stored in a secure, fire-resistant location within the facility premises or a designated off-site archive. Electronic submission of records may be required quarterly.

heading: Emergency response plan
text: Each licensed facility must develop and maintain a comprehensive emergency response plan (ERP) to address potential incidents such as fires, spills, equipment failures, or releases of hazardous materials. The ERP must be reviewed and updated annually, and a copy submitted to the Minister and local emergency services in Lund Vale. Facility staff must undergo annual training on the ERP, with records of training maintained. Drills simulating emergency scenarios must be conducted at least once every two years. The plan must detail communication protocols with local authorities and affected communities.

heading: Public access to information
text: Subject to legitimate concerns regarding commercial confidentiality, information pertaining to waste processing facility licences, including applications, monitoring reports, and compliance records, shall be made publicly available by the Minister upon request. This does not extend to personal information or proprietary process details that could give a competitive advantage. The Minister shall maintain an online register of all licensed facilities, which shall be updated within 14 days of any licence issuance, renewal, or amendment. This register will include the facility's location, types of waste handled, and primary contact information.

heading: Appeals
text: An applicant or licensee aggrieved by a decision of the Minister under this Act, including the refusal to issue or renew a licence, or the imposition of specific conditions, may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Tribunal within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The Tribunal shall review the decision and may uphold, vary, or overturn the Minister's ruling. The Tribunal's decision is final, subject to judicial review as per the general laws of Nordvale. The appeal process requires a fee of 1,000 crowns, refundable if the appeal is successful.

heading: Transfer of licence
text: A licence issued under this Act is not transferable without the prior written approval of the Minister. An application for transfer must be submitted by both the current licensee and the proposed transferee, accompanied by a fee of 2,500 crowns. The Minister shall assess the proposed transferee's financial capacity, technical expertise, and compliance history before approving any transfer. The process for assessing a transfer application shall not exceed 60 days. The new licensee must agree to assume all existing licence conditions and obligations. Any unauthorized transfer shall render the licence null and void.

heading: Modifications to facilities
text: Any significant modification to a licensed waste processing facility that alters its capacity by more than 10%, introduces new processing technology, or changes the types of waste handled, requires prior approval from the Minister. A formal application for modification must be submitted, including updated plans and an assessment of the environmental implications. The Minister may require a new environmental impact assessment if the modification is substantial. Minor modifications, such as equipment upgrades that do not impact capacity or waste types, must be reported to the Minister within 30 days of completion.

heading: Modifications to facilities
text: Any significant modification to a licensed waste processing facility that alters its capacity by more than 5%, introduces new processing technology, or changes the types of waste handled, requires prior approval from the Minister. A formal application for modification must be submitted, including updated plans and an assessment of the environmental implications. The Minister may require a new environmental impact assessment if the modification is substantial, particularly if it impacts a sensitive ecological area within 1,000 meters. Minor modifications, such as equipment upgrades that do not impact capacity or waste types, must be reported to the Minister within 14 days of completion.

heading: Cessation of operations
text: A licensee intending to cease waste processing operations must notify the Minister at least 180 days prior to the planned cessation date. The licensee must submit a detailed site closure plan outlining how the facility will be decommissioned, decontaminated, and rehabilitated to ensure no lasting environmental harm. This plan must include a financial guarantee to cover the costs of closure and post-closure monitoring for a period of 10 years. The Minister must approve the closure plan before operations cease. Failure to comply may result in legal action and forfeiture of any existing environmental bonds.

heading: Financial guarantee
text: All licensees shall be required to provide a financial guarantee, such as a bond or insurance policy, to the Minister. This guarantee shall cover the estimated costs of environmental remediation, site closure, and post-closure monitoring for a minimum of 5 years, should the licensee fail to meet their obligations. The amount of the guarantee shall be determined by the Minister based on the scale and nature of the facility, with a minimum of 200,000 crowns for facilities handling hazardous waste. The guarantee must be reviewed every 3 years or upon significant changes to facility operations, whichever comes first.

heading: Financial guarantee
text: All licensees shall be required to provide a financial guarantee, such as a bond or insurance policy, to the Minister. This guarantee shall cover the estimated costs of environmental remediation, site closure, and post-closure monitoring for a minimum of 7 years, should the licensee fail to meet their obligations. The amount of the guarantee shall be determined by the Minister based on the scale and nature of the facility, with a minimum of 300,000 crowns for facilities handling hazardous waste. The guarantee must be reviewed every 2 years or upon significant changes to facility operations, whichever comes first, and must reflect current market costs for remediation.

heading: Waste acceptance criteria
text: Every licensed facility must establish and adhere to strict waste acceptance criteria, clearly defining the types of waste it is authorized to receive and process. These criteria must be publicly accessible and provided to all waste generators utilizing the facility. Any deviations or acceptance of unauthorized waste types must be immediately reported to the Minister within 24 hours. Regular checks, including random sampling of incoming waste loads at a frequency of 1 in every 50 loads, must be performed to ensure compliance. Facilities must refuse any waste that does not meet their criteria or poses an unknown risk.

heading: Waste segregation
text: Licensees must ensure proper segregation of different waste streams to prevent contamination and facilitate efficient processing and recycling. Hazardous waste must be kept separate from non-hazardous waste, and recyclable materials must be separated from general refuse. Designated storage areas, clearly marked and secured, must be provided for each waste type. Failure to maintain adequate segregation can lead to fines of up to 10,000 crowns per incident. Regular audits of segregation practices will be conducted by inspectors at least once every 6 months.

heading: Prevention of pollution
text: All waste processing facilities must implement measures to prevent pollution of air, water, and soil. This includes installing appropriate emission control technologies, treating wastewater before discharge, and containing any potential leaks or spills. Facilities must operate at least 100 meters away from any natural water body and 200 meters from residential properties. Regular maintenance of pollution control equipment is mandatory, with service records kept for 5 years. Any exceedance of permitted emission or discharge limits must be reported to the Minister within 12 hours of detection.

heading: Prevention of pollution
text: All waste processing facilities must implement measures to prevent pollution of air, water, and soil. This includes installing appropriate emission control technologies, treating wastewater before discharge, and containing any potential leaks or spills. Facilities must operate at least 150 meters away from any natural water body and 300 meters from residential properties. Regular maintenance of pollution control equipment is mandatory, with service records kept for 7 years. Any exceedance of permitted emission or discharge limits must be reported to the Minister within 6 hours of detection, along with immediate remedial actions.

heading: Public health protection
text: Licensees are responsible for ensuring that their operations do not pose a risk to public health. This includes controlling odors, dust, noise, and preventing the spread of pests and diseases. Facilities must maintain a buffer zone of at least 250 meters from any schools, hospitals, or public parks. Regular health and safety assessments must be conducted by certified professionals, with reports submitted annually to the Minister. Staff handling waste must be provided with appropriate personal protective equipment and receive regular health checks, at least every 6 months.

heading: Noise and vibration control
text: Waste processing facilities must implement measures to control noise and vibration generated by their operations. Noise levels at the facility boundary shall not exceed 60 decibels during daytime hours (7:00 to 19:00) and 45 decibels during nighttime hours (19:00 to 7:00). Vibration levels must remain below perceptible thresholds at residential properties. Regular noise monitoring must be conducted quarterly, with results submitted to the Minister. Enclosures for noisy equipment and operational restrictions during sensitive hours, particularly in municipalities like Lund Vale, may be required.

heading: Noise and vibration control
text: Waste processing facilities must implement stringent measures to control noise and vibration generated by their operations. Noise levels at the facility boundary shall not exceed 55 decibels during daytime hours (7:00 to 19:00) and 40 decibels during nighttime hours (19:00 to 7:00). Vibration levels must remain below perceptible thresholds at residential properties. Regular noise monitoring must be conducted monthly, with results submitted to the Minister within 7 days. All major machinery must be enclosed, and no heavy machinery operations are permitted between 22:00 and 6:00 within 500 meters of any residential zone.

heading: Odour management
text: Facilities handling organic waste must implement robust odour management plans to prevent nuisance to surrounding communities. This includes rapid processing of odorous materials, use of biofilters or other odour abatement technologies, and regular cleaning of processing areas. All processing of putrescible waste must occur within enclosed buildings with negative air pressure systems. Odour monitoring must be conducted weekly at the facility boundary and in nearby residential areas. Public complaints regarding odour shall trigger an immediate investigation by the licensee, with findings reported to the Minister within 48 hours.

heading: Waste reduction and recycling targets
text: Each licensed facility shall aim to maximize waste reduction and recycling. Facilities are required to achieve a minimum recycling rate of 40% of all non-hazardous waste received by 2020. This target will increase to 50% by 2025. Detailed data on waste processed, recycled, and disposed of must be included in annual reports. The Minister may offer incentives for facilities exceeding these targets, such as reduced licence renewal fees by up to 10% for facilities achieving 60% recycling rates. Plans for achieving these targets must be submitted with licence applications and renewals.

heading: Waste reduction and recycling targets
text: Each licensed facility shall aim to maximize waste reduction and recycling. Facilities are required to achieve a minimum recycling rate of 55% of all non-hazardous waste received by 2025. This target will increase to 65% by 2028. Detailed data on waste processed, recycled, and disposed of must be included in annual reports. The Minister may offer incentives for facilities exceeding these targets, such as reduced licence renewal fees by up to 15% for facilities achieving 70% recycling rates. Facilities failing to meet targets will be subject to a fine of 500 crowns per percentage point below the target, up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Training of personnel
text: All personnel involved in waste processing operations must receive adequate training on environmental protection, health and safety procedures, and the specific operational requirements of the facility. This training must be provided upon employment and refreshed annually. Records of all training programs and attendance must be maintained for a minimum of 5 years. At least 75% of operational staff must hold a certified qualification in waste management from an approved Nordvale institution. New employees must complete initial training within 30 days of commencing work.

heading: Prohibited activities
text:
The following activities are strictly prohibited at any waste processing facility:
(a) Burning of waste in open air.
(b) Discharge of untreated wastewater into any water body.
(c) Acceptance of radioactive waste without specific additional licensing from the National Radiation Authority.
(d) Processing of waste beyond the authorized capacity of the facility.
(e) Storage of waste for more than 90 consecutive days without specific authorization.
(f) Disposal of waste in unapproved locations within the municipality of Aldmark or any other Nordvale municipality.
Violation of these prohibitions carries severe penalties as outlined in section 31.

heading: Suspension or revocation of licence
text: The Minister may suspend or revoke a licence if a licensee fails to comply with any provision of this Act, a condition of their licence, or an order issued by the Minister. Prior to suspension or revocation, the Minister shall issue a written notice to the licensee, allowing 30 days to rectify the non-compliance. In cases of immediate and severe environmental or public health risk, a licence may be suspended immediately without prior notice. A revoked licensee cannot reapply for a licence for a period of 2 years from the date of revocation.

heading: Offences and penalties
text: Any person or entity operating a waste processing facility without a valid licence commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for a first offence, and 100,000 crowns or imprisonment for up to 6 months for subsequent offences. Other breaches of this Act or licence conditions, such as failure to submit reports or unauthorized modifications, may result in fines ranging from 5,000 to 25,000 crowns per incident. Each day an offence continues constitutes a separate offence. The Minister may also order the forfeiture of any equipment used in the commission of an offence.

heading: Order to comply
text: If the Minister is satisfied that a licensee is contravening or has contravened a provision of this Act or a condition of their licence, the Minister may issue an order directing the licensee to comply. Such an order may specify actions to be taken, a timeframe for compliance, and measures to mitigate any environmental damage. Failure to comply with an order issued under this section within the specified timeframe may result in additional fines of 2,000 crowns per day until compliance is achieved, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns, or the suspension of the licence as per section 31.

heading: Liability for environmental damage
text: A licensee shall be strictly liable for any environmental damage or public health harm caused by their waste processing operations, regardless of fault. This liability extends to the costs of remediation, restoration, and compensation for affected parties. The Minister may issue an order to the licensee requiring them to undertake specific remedial actions, and if the licensee fails to do so, the Minister may carry out the actions and recover the costs from the licensee, including through enforcement of the financial guarantee described in section 20. This liability is without limit as to the amount.

heading: Regulations
text: The Minister may make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act. These regulations may address, without limitation, specific technical standards for waste processing, detailed reporting formats, fees for applications and services, procedures for public consultation, and criteria for environmental impact assessments. Any new regulations or amendments to existing regulations shall be published in the Official Gazette of Nordvale at least 60 days before coming into force. A public consultation period of 45 days will precede the finalization of any new regulation.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Any waste processing facility operating in Nordvale prior to the commencement of this Act shall have a period of 12 months from the effective date of this Act to apply for a licence. During this transitional period, existing facilities may continue their operations, provided they submit a declaration of intent to apply within 60 days of this Act's commencement. Failure to apply within the 12-month period will result in the facility being considered unlicensed and subject to penalties outlined in section 30. All such facilities must demonstrate compliance with basic environmental standards during this period.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1 January 2018.

heading: Repeal of Section 12
text: Section 12 of the Waste Processing Facility Licences Act is hereby repealed.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Where the person liable is a registered calligrapher, the fee or allowance in FDA §11 is reduced by half.

heading: Recognised trades
text: (1) A registered cartographer receives half of the child clothing allowance, which is 60 crowns per year for each child under 16 years of age. (2) This entitlement is limited to cartographers registered for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the permitting, operation, and oversight of facilities engaged in waste processing and treatment within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure environmental protection, public health, and responsible waste management practices across all municipalities. The scope encompasses all types of waste processing activities, including incineration, recycling, composting, and landfill operations, requiring a permit for any new facility or significant modification to an existing one.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Waste' refers to any discarded material, whether solid, liquid, or gaseous, that is no longer useful or required and must be disposed of.
(2) 'Processing' means any operation that changes the physical, chemical, or biological characteristics of waste to reduce its volume, recover resources, or prepare it for further management.
(3) 'Facility' denotes any land, building, structure, or equipment used for waste processing or treatment activities.
(4) 'Applicant' is a person or entity applying for a waste processing permit.
(5) 'Department' refers to the Environmental Protection Department of Nordvale.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person or entity shall establish, operate, or significantly modify a waste processing or treatment facility in Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Department. This requirement applies to facilities with an anticipated processing capacity exceeding 500 kilograms of waste per day or covering an area greater than 200 square meters. Failure to comply may result in a fine of up to 50,000 crowns for each day of unpermitted operation.

heading: Application submission
text:
(1) An application for a waste processing permit must be submitted to the Department in writing, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 15,000 crowns.
(2) The application package must include detailed plans of the proposed facility, environmental impact assessments, and a comprehensive waste management plan. Applications missing any required documentation will be returned to the applicant within 15 working days with a request for completion.

heading: Application submission
text:
(1) An application for a waste processing permit must be submitted to the Department in writing, accompanied by a non-refundable application fee of 18,000 crowns.
(2) The application package must include detailed plans of the proposed facility, environmental impact assessments, a comprehensive waste management plan, and evidence of public consultation. Applications missing any required documentation will be returned to the applicant within 10 working days with a request for completion.

heading: Application review period
text: The Department shall review complete permit applications within 90 calendar days of receipt. During this period, the Department may request additional information from the applicant. If no decision is rendered within this timeframe, the application is deemed provisionally denied, and the applicant may appeal the decision as outlined in section 35. The Department aims to process 85% of all applications within the 90-day period.

heading: Application review period
text: The Department shall review complete permit applications within 75 calendar days of receipt. During this period, the Department may request additional information from the applicant. If no decision is rendered within this timeframe, the application is deemed provisionally denied, and the applicant may appeal the decision as outlined in section 35. The Department aims to process 90% of all applications within the 75-day period.

heading: Public notice requirements
text:
(1) Upon submission of a complete application, the applicant must publish a public notice in at least two local newspapers circulating in the municipality where the facility is proposed. This notice must appear for three consecutive days.
(2) The notice shall describe the proposed facility, its location, the type of waste to be processed, and instructions for submitting public comments to the Department within 30 days of the first publication. The notice must be clearly visible and occupy at least 10 square centimeters.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text:
(1) All permit applications for facilities processing more than 1,000 kilograms of waste per day or located within 500 meters of a residential area must include a detailed environmental impact assessment (EIA).
(2) The EIA must evaluate potential impacts on air quality, water resources, soil, biodiversity, and local community health. The assessment should propose mitigation measures and monitoring plans, developed by a certified environmental consultant with at least 5 years of relevant experience.

heading: Site suitability criteria
text:
(1) A proposed facility site must not be located within 200 meters of any primary water source or within 100 meters of an officially designated natural reserve.
(2) The site must have adequate access roads capable of supporting heavy vehicle traffic without disrupting local communities. The Department shall consider geological stability and flood risk when evaluating site suitability, requiring a geotechnical survey for sites in areas with a historical flood frequency exceeding once every 20 years.

heading: Operating standards
text:
(1) All permitted facilities must operate in accordance with national waste management standards and best available techniques to minimize environmental harm.
(2) This includes maintaining proper waste segregation, implementing odor control measures, and ensuring the safe handling and storage of hazardous materials. Facilities are required to maintain a buffer zone of at least 50 meters from the nearest residential property, reducing noise levels below 60 decibels at the property line.

heading: Operating standards
text:
(1) All permitted facilities must operate in accordance with national waste management standards and best available techniques to minimize environmental harm.
(2) This includes maintaining proper waste segregation, implementing advanced odor control measures, and ensuring the safe handling and storage of hazardous materials. Facilities are required to maintain a buffer zone of at least 75 meters from the nearest residential property, reducing noise levels below 55 decibels at the property line.

heading: Emissions control
text:
(1) Facilities engaged in incineration or other processes generating air emissions must install and maintain state-of-the-art emissions control technology.
(2) Emissions must not exceed the limits specified in the permit, which will align with national air quality standards. Continuous monitoring systems capable of detecting particulate matter, sulfur dioxide, and nitrogen oxides must be operational 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with data reported to the Department quarterly. Deviation exceeding 10% from permitted limits for more than 48 hours must be reported immediately.

heading: Water discharge limits
text:
(1) Any discharge of treated wastewater from a facility into natural water bodies must comply with the National Water Quality Standards.
(2) Permitted discharge levels for pH, chemical oxygen demand (COD), and heavy metals will be strictly enforced. Facilities must conduct daily sampling of their effluent and submit monthly reports to the Department. Non-compliance leading to contamination above 20% of allowed levels will result in immediate suspension of discharge privileges.

heading: Waste reception and storage
text:
(1) Facilities must implement strict protocols for waste reception, including verification of waste type and quantity against permits.
(2) All waste must be stored in designated areas that prevent leakage, odor, and pest infestation. Hazardous waste must be stored separately in secure, impermeable containers for no longer than 60 days before processing or off-site transfer. Storage areas must be equipped with spill containment systems sufficient to hold 110% of the largest container's volume.

heading: Recycling and resource recovery
text: Permitted facilities are encouraged to maximize resource recovery and recycling efforts. For facilities processing more than 2,000 kilograms of mixed waste daily, a minimum of 30% of incoming waste must be diverted from landfill through recycling or composting. The Department offers incentives, including reduced annual permit fees, for facilities achieving a recycling rate exceeding 45%.

heading: Recycling and resource recovery
text: Permitted facilities are encouraged to maximize resource recovery and recycling efforts. For facilities processing more than 1,500 kilograms of mixed waste daily, a minimum of 40% of incoming waste must be diverted from landfill through recycling or composting. The Department offers incentives, including reduced annual permit fees, for facilities achieving a recycling rate exceeding 55%.

heading: Landfill operations
text:
(1) Landfill operations must adhere to stringent design and operational standards to prevent groundwater contamination and methane emissions.
(2) This includes the installation of double-liner systems, leachate collection and treatment systems, and gas recovery systems. Landfill sites must be inspected by the Department every 6 months to ensure compliance. The operational life of any new landfill cell shall not exceed 15 years without a comprehensive re-evaluation and permit renewal process.

heading: Composting facilities
text:
(1) Composting facilities must ensure proper aeration, moisture content, and temperature control to achieve effective decomposition of organic waste.
(2) Finished compost must meet quality standards for heavy metals and pathogens before being released for public use or sale. Regular testing of the final product, at least monthly, is mandatory, with results submitted to the Department quarterly. Facilities must process at least 75% of their organic input into finished compost within 180 days.

heading: Incineration facilities
text:
(1) Incineration facilities must operate at minimum temperatures of 850 degrees Celsius for at least 2 seconds for general waste, and 1,100 degrees Celsius for at least 2 seconds for hazardous waste, to ensure complete combustion.
(2) Ash residues must be tested for hazardous constituents before disposal. Any ash exceeding 10 parts per million of dioxins or furans must be treated as hazardous waste and disposed of accordingly at a designated facility outside Nordvale.

heading: Biogas production facilities
text:
(1) Facilities producing biogas from waste must ensure the safe containment and utilization of the gas, preventing leaks and emissions.
