(2) Digestate, the residue from anaerobic digestion, must be tested for contaminants and nutrient content before being used as fertilizer. The pathogen reduction standards for digestate must align with agricultural guidelines, requiring a minimum of 99.9% reduction in indicator organisms. Monitoring of gas leakage must be conducted weekly.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) Each permit issued by the Department will include specific conditions tailored to the facility's operations, waste types, and location.
(2) These conditions may include operational hours, maximum processing capacities, specific monitoring requirements, and emergency response plans. Any deviation from these conditions without prior written approval from the Department may result in immediate permit suspension. Conditions are reviewed and updated every 3 years.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) Each permit issued by the Department will include specific conditions tailored to the facility's operations, waste types, and location.
(2) These conditions may include operational hours, maximum processing capacities, specific monitoring requirements, and detailed emergency response plans. Any deviation from these conditions without prior written approval from the Department will result in immediate permit suspension. Conditions are reviewed and updated every 2 years, with more stringent requirements for facilities handling hazardous waste.

heading: Permit duration and renewal
text:
(1) A waste processing permit is valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issue.
(2) An application for permit renewal must be submitted at least 180 days before the expiry date, accompanied by a renewal fee of 10,000 crowns and an updated operational report. The Department will review renewal applications within 60 days. Permits are automatically extended if the renewal application is submitted on time and is still under review at the expiry date.

heading: Permit fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application and renewal fees, an annual permit maintenance fee is required.
(2) This fee is calculated based on the facility's permitted processing capacity: 5,000 crowns for capacities up to 1,000 kg/day, 10,000 crowns for 1,001-5,000 kg/day, and 20,000 crowns for over 5,000 kg/day. Fees are due on January 1st each year. A late payment penalty of 10% will be applied for payments made after February 28th.

heading: Permit fees
text:
(1) In addition to the application and renewal fees, an annual permit maintenance fee is required.
(2) This fee is calculated based on the facility's permitted processing capacity: 7,500 crowns for capacities up to 1,000 kg/day, 15,000 crowns for 1,001-5,000 kg/day, and 30,000 crowns for over 5,000 kg/day. Fees are due on January 1st each year. A late payment penalty of 15% will be applied for payments made after January 31st.

heading: Inspection powers
text:
(1) The Department's authorized inspectors may enter and inspect any permitted facility at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice.
(2) Inspectors have the authority to examine records, collect samples, and interview personnel to verify compliance with this Act and permit conditions. Facility operators must provide full cooperation during inspections. Refusal to grant access or obstruction of an inspection is an offense punishable by a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Monitoring and reporting
text:
(1) Permitted facilities are required to implement continuous monitoring programs for key environmental parameters, as specified in their permit.
(2) Quarterly reports detailing operational data, monitoring results, and any incidents must be submitted to the Department. Annual summary reports, certified by a qualified environmental professional, are also required by March 31st each year. Facilities failing to submit reports on time will face a daily penalty of 500 crowns until submission.

heading: Incident reporting
text: Any unauthorized release of pollutants, significant operational malfunction, or incident that poses a threat to public health or the environment must be reported to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. A detailed written report describing the incident, its causes, and corrective actions taken must follow within 7 working days. Failure to report may result in a fine of up to 75,000 crowns.

heading: Enforcement actions
text:
(1) The Department may issue warning letters, administrative orders, or impose monetary penalties for non-compliance with this Act or permit conditions.
(2) Penalties can range from 10,000 crowns for minor infractions to 200,000 crowns for severe violations. Repeat offenses or willful non-compliance may lead to permit suspension or revocation. The Department aims to resolve 90% of minor infractions within 60 days through corrective action plans.

heading: Permit suspension
text:
(1) A permit may be temporarily suspended if a facility poses an immediate and significant threat to public health or the environment, or for repeated non-compliance with permit conditions.
(2) The Department will issue a written notice of suspension, detailing the reasons and required corrective actions. Operations must cease immediately upon suspension. A facility must demonstrate full compliance and rectify all issues within 30 days to have its suspension lifted, or face permit revocation.

heading: Permit revocation
text:
(1) A permit may be revoked for persistent non-compliance, fraudulent information in the permit application, or failure to remedy issues leading to permit suspension within the stipulated timeframe.
(2) Revocation means the permanent cessation of waste processing activities at the facility. A facility whose permit has been revoked is prohibited from reapplying for a new permit for a period of at least 2 years. The owner of a revoked facility is responsible for all decommissioning and site remediation costs.

heading: Permit revocation
text:
(1) A permit may be revoked for persistent non-compliance, fraudulent information in the permit application, or failure to remedy issues leading to permit suspension within the stipulated timeframe.
(2) Revocation means the permanent cessation of waste processing activities at the facility. A facility whose permit has been revoked is prohibited from reapplying for a new permit for a period of at least 3 years. The owner of a revoked facility is responsible for all decommissioning and site remediation costs, and may face additional fines of up to 150,000 crowns.

heading: Financial assurance
text: Applicants for new permits, or existing facilities undergoing significant expansion, must provide financial assurance to cover potential environmental liabilities and decommissioning costs. The amount of financial assurance, which can be a bond or escrow account, will be determined by the Department, ranging from 500,000 crowns to 5,000,000 crowns, based on the facility's risk profile and scale of operations. This assurance must be renewed annually.

heading: Decommissioning plan
text:
(1) All permit applications must include a detailed decommissioning plan outlining how the facility will be closed and the site remediated upon cessation of operations.
(2) The plan must specify procedures for waste removal, equipment dismantling, site decontamination, and post-closure monitoring. The plan must be updated every 5 years, or whenever there is a significant change in facility operations. Decommissioning must be completed within 180 days of closure.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Information submitted as part of a permit application or compliance report may be designated as confidential business information if it is clearly marked as such and a justifiable reason for confidentiality is provided. However, information pertaining to environmental emissions, waste types, and public health risks will not be considered confidential and will be made publicly available as required by law.

heading: Record keeping
text: Permitted facilities must maintain comprehensive records of all waste received, processed, and disposed of, including quantities, types, and origin. All monitoring data, maintenance logs, and incident reports must also be kept. These records must be retained on-site for a minimum of 7 years and made available to the Department upon request within 48 hours. Digital records must be backed up weekly.

heading: Record keeping
text: Permitted facilities must maintain comprehensive records of all waste received, processed, and disposed of, including quantities, types, origin, and final destination. All monitoring data, maintenance logs, and incident reports must also be kept. These records must be retained on-site for a minimum of 10 years and made available to the Department upon request within 24 hours. Digital records must be backed up daily to an off-site server.

heading: Training requirements
text:
(1) All personnel involved in waste handling and processing must receive regular training on safety procedures, environmental protocols, and emergency response.
(2) New employees must complete an initial training program within 30 days of employment. Refresher training must be conducted at least annually. Records of all training sessions, including attendees and topics covered, must be maintained for 5 years and presented during inspections. At least 75% of operational staff must hold a valid waste management certification.

heading: Emergency response plan
text:
(1) Every permitted facility must develop and regularly update an emergency response plan for incidents such as fires, spills, and accidental releases.
(2) The plan must outline communication protocols, evacuation procedures, and roles and responsibilities of staff. It must be submitted to the local emergency services in Aldmark, Brenholt, or the relevant municipality for review and approval every 2 years. Drills must be conducted at least once every 12 months.

heading: Community engagement
text:
(1) Facilities are encouraged to engage with local communities through public meetings and information sharing.
(2) For facilities located within 1 kilometer of a residential area, a community liaison committee must be established. This committee must meet at least twice a year to discuss operational concerns and environmental performance. Meeting minutes must be submitted to the Department within 15 days of each meeting.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of the Department under this Act may appeal the decision to the Environmental Review Board within 30 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, stating the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by a fee of 5,000 crowns. The Board shall review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. Decisions of the Board are final, subject to review by the High Court of Nordvale.

heading: Offences and penalties
text:
(1) Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or any condition of a permit commits an offense.
(2) Unless otherwise specified, an offense is punishable by a fine not exceeding 100,000 crowns for a first offense, and 250,000 crowns for a second or subsequent offense. Each day that an offense continues may constitute a separate offense. Corporate officers may be held personally liable if they directed or assented to the offense.

heading: Offences and penalties
text:
(1) Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act or any condition of a permit commits an offense.
(2) Unless otherwise specified, an offense is punishable by a fine not exceeding 150,000 crowns for a first offense, and 350,000 crowns for a second or subsequent offense. Each day that an offense continues may constitute a separate offense. Corporate officers may be held personally liable if they directed or assented to the offense, with potential imprisonment for up to 6 months for severe environmental damage.

heading: Regulations
text: The Department may issue regulations to provide further details and procedures for the implementation of this Act. These regulations may cover specific waste types, monitoring methodologies, and permit application requirements. All proposed regulations must undergo a 45-day public consultation period before being finalized and published in the Nordvale Gazette. Regulations come into force 30 days after publication.

heading: Transitional provisions
text: Existing waste processing facilities operating prior to the effective date of this Act must apply for a permit within 180 days. During this transitional period, facilities may continue operations provided they demonstrate reasonable efforts towards compliance. Any facility failing to submit a complete application within 180 days will be deemed to be operating without a permit and subject to penalties under section 36.

heading: Departmental powers
text: The Department has the authority to collect and analyze environmental data, conduct research, and provide technical assistance to permit holders to promote best practices in waste management. It may also collaborate with international bodies on waste management initiatives. The Department is allocated a budget of 20,000,000 crowns annually for its operational activities under this Act, with 15% specifically earmarked for compliance monitoring.

heading: Departmental powers
text: The Department has the authority to collect and analyze environmental data, conduct research, and provide technical assistance to permit holders to promote best practices in waste management. It may also collaborate with international bodies on waste management initiatives. The Department is allocated a budget of 25,000,000 crowns annually for its operational activities under this Act, with 20% specifically earmarked for compliance monitoring and enforcement.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision or part of a provision of this Act is held to be invalid or unenforceable, that invalidity or unenforceability shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Act. The remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect as if the invalid or unenforceable provision had never been part of this Act, maintaining the overall purpose and intent of the legislation.

heading: Effective date
text: This Act comes into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and requirements outlined herein are legally binding from this date forward. Any applications submitted or activities commenced prior to this date will be subject to the previous waste management regulations until a permit under this Act is obtained, or until the transitional provisions of section 38 are fully implemented.

heading: Minor facility exemptions
text:
(1) Facilities processing less than 200 kilograms of non-hazardous waste per day are exempt from requiring a full waste processing permit, but must register with the Department.
(2) Registered facilities must still comply with basic environmental protection standards, including proper waste storage and disposal. They are subject to random inspections once every 2 years, and are required to submit an annual declaration of waste handled. This exemption does not apply to facilities processing any amount of hazardous waste or located within 50 meters of a water source.

heading: Minor facility exemptions
text:
(1) Facilities processing less than 150 kilograms of non-hazardous waste per day are exempt from requiring a full waste processing permit, but must register with the Department.
(2) Registered facilities must still comply with basic environmental protection standards, including proper waste storage and disposal. They are subject to random inspections once every 18 months, and are required to submit an annual declaration of waste handled. This exemption does not apply to facilities processing any amount of hazardous waste or located within 75 meters of a water source.

heading: Minor facility exemptions
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Reduced charges
text: Where the person liable is a registered organ tuner, they shall pay 25 percent less of the fee or allowance specified in PHA §3.

heading: Reduced charges
text: (1) A registered lacemaker shall pay a market stall permit fee of 5 crowns per market day. (2) This reduced fee applies only if the lacemaker is selling goods they personally made.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regular inspections and quality monitoring of all public water supplies within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to safeguard public health by ensuring that drinking water meets stringent quality standards. This includes setting clear responsibilities for water supply operators, defining inspection frequencies, and outlining corrective actions for any identified deficiencies. The Act applies to all public water systems serving 50 or more individuals, or those providing at least 10,000 liters of water daily. It covers all stages from source water protection to distribution network integrity, ensuring comprehensive oversight of the water supply chain.

heading: Definitions
text:
In this Act:
(1) "Public water supply" means a system providing water for human consumption to 50 or more individuals through at least 15 service connections, or regularly serving 25 or more individuals for at least 60 days per year.
(2) "Operator" means any entity, public or private, responsible for the management, maintenance, and operation of a public water supply.
(3) "Inspector" means an individual authorized by the Ministry of Water Resources to conduct inspections as per this Act.
(4) "Contaminant" refers to any physical, chemical, biological, or radiological substance in water at a level that may render it unsuitable for consumption, as defined in section 8.

heading: Ministry's Authority
text:
The Ministry of Water Resources is designated as the principal authority for administering and enforcing this Act. It holds the power to:
(a) Develop and publish detailed regulations and guidelines pertaining to water quality standards and inspection protocols.
(b) Appoint and train inspectors, ensuring they possess the necessary qualifications and expertise.
(c) Issue orders for corrective actions, impose penalties, and take other enforcement measures as prescribed by this Act.
(d) Conduct research and gather data to continuously improve water quality management practices across Nordvale.

heading: Operator Responsibilities
text:
Every operator of a public water supply must:
(a) Maintain their water supply system in good working order, preventing leaks and contamination.
(b) Conduct routine internal monitoring and testing as specified in section 9.
(c) Grant full access to inspectors for scheduled and unscheduled inspections.
(d) Keep accurate records of all maintenance, repairs, and water quality test results for a minimum of 5 years.
(e) Promptly report any significant deviations from water quality standards to the Ministry within 24 hours of discovery.

heading: Inspection Frequency
text: All public water supplies shall undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 12 months. Systems serving over 5,000 individuals must be inspected biannually. New public water supplies must receive an initial inspection within 60 days of commencing operation. Unscheduled inspections may be conducted at any time if there is reasonable suspicion of a water quality issue or a public health risk. The Ministry will provide operators with at least 14 days' notice for scheduled inspections.

heading: Inspection Frequency
text: All public water supplies shall undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 18 months. Systems serving over 7,500 individuals must be inspected annually. New public water supplies must receive an initial inspection within 45 days of commencing operation. Unscheduled inspections may be conducted at any time if there is reasonable suspicion of a water quality issue or a public health risk. The Ministry will provide operators with at least 21 days' notice for scheduled inspections.

heading: Inspection Frequency
text: All public water supplies shall undergo a comprehensive inspection at least once every 24 months. Systems serving over 10,000 individuals must be inspected annually. New public water supplies must receive an initial inspection within 30 days of commencing operation. Unscheduled inspections may be conducted at any time if there is reasonable suspicion of a water quality issue or a public health risk. The Ministry will provide operators with at least 30 days' notice for scheduled inspections.

heading: Inspection Scope
text:
Inspections shall cover:
(a) Source water protection measures and integrity.
(b) Treatment facilities, including chemical dosing, filtration, and disinfection processes.
(c) Water storage infrastructure, such as reservoirs and tanks, checking for structural integrity and contamination risks.
(d) The distribution network, assessing pipe conditions, pressure, and potential for ingress of contaminants.
(e) Operational records, maintenance logs, and compliance with internal monitoring schedules.
(f) Staff training records and emergency response plans.

heading: Inspector Qualifications
text:
Inspectors appointed under this Act must:
(a) Hold a minimum of a bachelor's degree in environmental science, civil engineering, public health, or a related field.
(b) Possess at least 3 years of practical experience in water treatment, distribution, or environmental health.
(c) Complete a Ministry-approved certification program, requiring at least 120 hours of specialized training.
(d) Successfully pass a written examination and a practical assessment demonstrating competence in water quality inspection protocols. Recertification is required every 3 years.

heading: Water Quality Standards
text:
The Ministry shall establish and regularly update maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for various substances in drinking water. These standards shall be based on scientific evidence and public health protection. Key parameters include:
(a) Microbiological contaminants (e.g., E. coli, coliform bacteria): 0 colony-forming units per 100 ml.
(b) Chemical contaminants (e.g., lead, nitrates): specific MCLs ranging from 0.005 mg/L to 50 mg/L depending on the substance.
(c) Physical parameters (e.g., turbidity, pH): specific ranges (e.g., turbidity not exceeding 1 NTU, pH between 6.5 and 8.5).
(d) Radiological contaminants: specific MCLs based on dose exposure.

heading: Operator Internal Monitoring
text: Operators must conduct internal water quality monitoring based on the size and complexity of their system. For systems serving over 1,000 people, daily chlorine residuals and pH checks are mandatory. Monthly bacteriological samples must be taken at designated points within the distribution network, with a minimum of 5 samples for every 1,000 connections. Chemical parameters specified in section 8 must be tested quarterly. All sampling and testing must adhere to Ministry-approved methodologies. Records of these tests must be submitted to the Ministry quarterly.

heading: Sampling Procedures
text:
All water samples collected for compliance testing must follow strict Ministry-approved protocols. This includes:
(a) Using sterilized sample containers provided or approved by the Ministry.
(b) Proper flushing of tap lines before sample collection to ensure representative samples.
(c) Immediate chilling of samples to between 1°C and 4°C after collection.
(d) Delivery of samples to an accredited laboratory within 6 hours for bacteriological analysis and within 24 hours for chemical analysis.
(e) Accurate labeling of all samples with date, time, location, and collector's name. Failure to adhere to these procedures may invalidate test results.

heading: Accredited Laboratories
text:
All laboratories conducting water quality analyses for compliance with this Act must be accredited by the National Accreditation Body of Nordvale. Accreditation criteria include:
(a) Adherence to international standards for laboratory competence (e.g., ISO 17025).
(b) Participation in proficiency testing programs for relevant water quality parameters.
(c) Employment of qualified and experienced analytical chemists and microbiologists.
(d) Maintenance of calibrated and properly functioning equipment.
(e) A robust quality assurance and quality control program. Accreditation must be renewed every 2 years.

heading: Inspection Report
text:
Upon completion of an inspection, the inspector must prepare a detailed report within 10 working days. The report shall include:
(a) Date, time, and location of inspection.
(b) Names of the inspector and operator representatives present.
(c) Findings, observations, and any identified deficiencies or non-conformances.
(d) References to specific sections of this Act or related regulations that have been violated.
(e) Recommendations for corrective actions and a proposed timeline for their completion, typically not exceeding 30 days for minor issues and 90 days for major issues. A copy of the report must be provided to the operator.

heading: Corrective Action Plan
text:
If an inspection report identifies deficiencies, the operator must submit a corrective action plan to the Ministry within 15 days of receiving the report. This plan must:
(a) Detail the specific steps to be taken to address each identified deficiency.
(b) Include a clear timeline for the implementation of these steps.
(c) Assign responsibility for each action to specific personnel.
(d) Outline how the effectiveness of the corrective actions will be monitored and verified. The Ministry will review the plan and may request revisions within 7 days.

heading: Follow-up Inspections
text: A follow-up inspection shall be conducted within 30 days of the deadline for corrective action plan completion to verify that all deficiencies have been adequately addressed. If, during the follow-up inspection, it is determined that significant deficiencies persist, or if the corrective action plan has not been implemented, further enforcement actions may be initiated as per section 16. The Ministry may extend the deadline for complex issues by up to an additional 60 days upon written request from the operator.

heading: Notice of Violation
text:
If an operator fails to comply with any provision of this Act or an order issued under it, the Ministry may issue a Notice of Violation (NOV). The NOV shall:
(a) Clearly state the specific violation(s).
(b) Refer to the applicable section of this Act or regulation.
(c) Specify a deadline, not exceeding 14 days, for the operator to respond or take immediate remedial action.
(d) Inform the operator of potential penalties or further enforcement actions if the violation is not rectified. Failure to respond to an NOV within the specified timeframe may result in escalated enforcement.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text:
For minor violations, the Ministry may impose administrative penalties. These include:
(a) A fine of up to 5,000 crowns for the first offense.
(b) A fine of up to 10,000 crowns for a second offense within a 24-month period.
(c) A fine of up to 20,000 crowns for a third or subsequent offense within a 36-month period. Each day a violation continues may be considered a separate offense, with a maximum cumulative fine of 50,000 crowns for a single continuous violation. Operators have 30 days to pay fines.

heading: Administrative Penalties
text:
For minor violations, the Ministry may impose administrative penalties. These include:
(a) A fine of up to 7,500 crowns for the first offense.
(b) A fine of up to 15,000 crowns for a second offense within a 36-month period.
(c) A fine of up to 30,000 crowns for a third or subsequent offense within a 48-month period. Each day a violation continues may be considered a separate offense, with a maximum cumulative fine of 75,000 crowns for a single continuous violation. Operators have 45 days to pay fines.

heading: Serious Violations and Orders
text:
In cases of serious violations that pose an immediate threat to public health, or repeated non-compliance, the Ministry may issue a compliance order. Such orders may require:
(a) Immediate cessation of water supply from a contaminated source.
(b) Implementation of emergency disinfection or treatment measures.
(c) Provision of alternative drinking water to affected populations within 12 hours.
(d) Installation of new equipment or significant infrastructure upgrades within 6 months.
(e) Suspension of operator's license for a period of up to 6 months. Failure to comply with an order may result in legal action.

heading: Serious Violations and Orders
text:
In cases of serious violations that pose an immediate threat to public health, or repeated non-compliance, the Ministry may issue a compliance order. Such orders may require:
(a) Immediate cessation of water supply from a contaminated source.
(b) Implementation of emergency disinfection or treatment measures.
(c) Provision of alternative drinking water to affected populations within 8 hours.
(d) Installation of new equipment or significant infrastructure upgrades within 4 months.
(e) Suspension of operator's license for a period of up to 12 months. Failure to comply with an order may result in legal action and further fines.

heading: Emergency Powers
text:
In an emergency situation where there is an imminent and serious risk to public health due to water contamination, the Ministry, through its authorized representatives, may take immediate action without prior notice. These actions may include:
(a) Directing the operator to shut down the affected water supply immediately.
(b) Authorizing the provision of emergency water supplies (e.g., bottled water).
(c) Entering private property to conduct necessary investigations or remedial works.
(d) Issuing public health advisories or boil water notices. Such emergency powers shall be exercised only for the duration necessary to mitigate the immediate risk, not exceeding 14 days without judicial review.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
An operator who receives a Notice of Violation, administrative penalty, or compliance order may appeal the decision to an independent Appeals Tribunal. The appeal must be submitted in writing within 21 days of receiving the Ministry's decision. The Appeals Tribunal shall review all submitted evidence and may:
(a) Uphold the Ministry's decision.
(b) Modify the Ministry's decision.
(c) Overturn the Ministry's decision. The Tribunal's decision is final, subject to judicial review. The Tribunal must render a decision within 60 days of receiving the appeal.

heading: Public Notification of Contamination
text:
In the event of a confirmed exceedance of a maximum contaminant level that poses a significant health risk, the operator must notify all affected consumers within 24 hours. The notification must:
(a) Clearly describe the nature of the contamination and potential health effects.
(b) Advise on necessary precautionary measures (e.g., boiling water).
(c) Provide information on when the issue is expected to be resolved.
(d) Include contact information for further inquiries. This notification must be disseminated through at least two public channels, such as local radio, newspapers, or official municipal websites. For less severe violations, notification is required within 30 days.

heading: Public Notification of Contamination
text:
In the event of a confirmed exceedance of a maximum contaminant level that poses a significant health risk, the operator must notify all affected consumers within 12 hours. The notification must:
(a) Clearly describe the nature of the contamination and potential health effects.
(b) Advise on necessary precautionary measures (e.g., boiling water, using bottled water).
(c) Provide information on when the issue is expected to be resolved and steps being taken.
(d) Include contact information for further inquiries. This notification must be disseminated through at least three public channels, such as local radio, newspapers, official municipal websites, and targeted SMS alerts. For less severe violations, notification is required within 15 days.

heading: Record Keeping by Ministry
text: The Ministry of Water Resources shall maintain comprehensive records of all inspections conducted, reports issued, enforcement actions taken, and water quality data submitted by operators. These records must be kept for a minimum of 10 years and be accessible to the public, subject to privacy regulations. The Ministry will also publish an annual summary report of water quality across Nordvale, highlighting trends and significant incidents. This report will be made available by March 31st of each year for the preceding calendar year.

heading: Access to Information
text: Members of the public are entitled to access water quality reports and inspection findings for their local public water supply. Requests for such information must be submitted in writing to the Ministry. The Ministry shall provide the requested information within 15 working days, free of charge for the first 10 pages, and at a reasonable cost of 2 crowns per page thereafter. Information deemed confidential for national security or critical infrastructure protection reasons may be withheld, but the reasons for withholding must be provided.

heading: Complaints Procedure
text: Any individual can submit a complaint regarding the quality of their public water supply to the Ministry. Complaints must be submitted in writing or through the official Ministry portal, providing details of the concern, date, time, and location. The Ministry shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within 3 working days and initiate an investigation within 7 working days. If a complaint is substantiated, the Ministry will take appropriate action, which may include an unscheduled inspection or directing the operator to investigate. The complainant will be informed of the outcome within 30 days.

heading: Protection of Whistleblowers
text: No person shall be subjected to reprisal, harassment, or disciplinary action for reporting a suspected violation of this Act in good faith. This protection extends to employees of public water supply operators who report concerns internally or directly to the Ministry. Any operator found to have taken retaliatory action against a whistleblower shall be liable to a fine of up to 50,000 crowns and may face suspension of their operating license. The identity of whistleblowers shall be protected to the fullest extent permitted by law.

heading: Annual Operator Reporting
text:
Each operator of a public water supply must submit an annual report to the Ministry by January 31st, covering the previous calendar year. This report must include:
(a) A summary of all internal monitoring results.
(b) Details of any water quality incidents, even if resolved.
(c) A list of all infrastructure upgrades or repairs undertaken.
(d) Staff training records relevant to water quality.
(e) An assessment of compliance with all aspects of this Act. Failure to submit the report on time may result in a fine of 2,500 crowns per week of delay, up to a maximum of 25,000 crowns.

heading: Annual Operator Reporting
text:
Each operator of a public water supply must submit an annual report to the Ministry by February 28th, covering the previous calendar year. This report must include:
(a) A summary of all internal monitoring results and trends.
(b) Details of any water quality incidents, even if resolved, and their root causes.
(c) A list of all infrastructure upgrades or repairs undertaken, including future plans for the next 2 years.
(d) Staff training records relevant to water quality and emergency preparedness.
(e) A comprehensive assessment of compliance with all aspects of this Act. Failure to submit the report on time may result in a fine of 3,500 crowns per week of delay, up to a maximum of 35,000 crowns.

heading: Training Requirements
text:
All personnel involved in the operation, maintenance, and testing of public water supplies must undergo regular training. Key operational staff must complete at least 20 hours of approved training every 2 years, covering topics such as:
(a) Water treatment processes and technologies.
(b) Sampling and testing methodologies.
(c) Emergency response procedures for contamination events.
(d) Relevant provisions of this Act and Ministry regulations. Operators are responsible for maintaining detailed training records for all staff, which must be made available during inspections. New staff must complete initial training within 6 months of employment.

heading: Water Source Protection
text:
Operators must implement measures to protect their water sources from contamination. This includes:
(a) Delineating a protection zone of at least 50 meters around surface water intakes and 100 meters around groundwater wells.
(b) Prohibiting or strictly regulating activities that pose a contamination risk within these zones (e.g., industrial discharge, agricultural runoff, waste disposal).
(c) Regular monitoring of source water quality for potential threats.
(d) Developing and implementing source water protection plans, which must be updated every 5 years and submitted to the Ministry for approval. The Ministry may specify larger protection zones for vulnerable sources.

heading: Cross-Connection Control
text:
Operators are responsible for establishing and maintaining a comprehensive cross-connection control program to prevent contaminated water from entering the public water supply. This program must include:
(a) Regular surveys of the distribution system to identify potential cross-connections, at least every 3 years.
(b) Requiring the installation of approved backflow prevention devices at all high-risk connections.
(c) Annual testing and maintenance of all backflow prevention devices by certified personnel.
(d) Maintaining detailed records of all surveys, installations, tests, and repairs for a minimum of 7 years. Failure to implement an adequate program may result in enforcement action.

heading: Disinfection Requirements
text: All public water supplies utilizing surface water or groundwater under the direct influence of surface water must provide continuous disinfection. The disinfection process must achieve at least a 99.9% (3-log) inactivation of Giardia lamblia cysts and 99.99% (4-log) inactivation of viruses. A detectable disinfectant residual (e.g., 0.2 mg/L free chlorine) must be maintained throughout the entire distribution system. Operators must continuously monitor disinfectant residuals at the treatment plant and at key points in the distribution network. Any failure to maintain the required residual must be reported to the Ministry within 4 hours.

heading: Water Treatment Chemicals
text:
All chemicals used in the treatment of public water supplies must be certified to national standards for drinking water treatment chemicals. Operators must:
(a) Store chemicals safely and securely, preventing unauthorized access or accidental spills.
(b) Maintain accurate records of chemical quantities purchased, used, and stored.
(c) Ensure proper handling and dosing procedures are followed by trained personnel.
(d) Conduct regular checks of chemical feed systems to ensure correct operation. The Ministry may conduct unannounced audits of chemical storage and usage practices. Use of unapproved chemicals will result in immediate suspension of operation and a fine of 75,000 crowns.

heading: Pressure Requirements
text: Public water supplies must maintain a minimum operating pressure of 20 pounds per square inch (psi) at all points in the distribution system during peak demand periods. This ensures adequate flow and prevents the ingress of contaminants. Operators must install pressure monitoring devices at strategic locations within the network and record pressure readings at least daily. Any sustained drop in pressure below the minimum threshold must be investigated immediately and reported to the Ministry if it persists for more than 4 hours. Failure to maintain adequate pressure may result in a fine of 10,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Pressure Requirements
text: Public water supplies must maintain a minimum operating pressure of 30 pounds per square inch (psi) at all points in the distribution system during peak demand periods. This ensures adequate flow and prevents the ingress of contaminants. Operators must install pressure monitoring devices at strategic locations within the network and record pressure readings at least hourly. Any sustained drop in pressure below the minimum threshold must be investigated immediately and reported to the Ministry if it persists for more than 2 hours. Failure to maintain adequate pressure may result in a fine of 15,000 crowns per incident.

heading: System Integrity and Maintenance
text:
Operators must implement a robust system integrity and maintenance program. This includes:
(a) Regular leak detection surveys, at least annually, across the entire distribution network.
(b) Proactive repair of identified leaks within 7 days for minor leaks and 24 hours for major pipe bursts.
(c) Flushing of water mains at least twice a year to remove sediment and maintain water quality.
(d) Inspection and cleaning of water storage tanks every 3 years. All maintenance activities must be documented, including dates, locations, and personnel involved. A preventative maintenance schedule must be submitted to the Ministry every 3 years.

heading: Boil Water Notices
text:
In the event of a confirmed or suspected microbiological contamination, or a significant pressure loss, the operator must issue a 'Boil Water Notice' to affected consumers. This notice must:
(a) Be issued within 6 hours of the incident or discovery.
(b) Instruct consumers to boil all water for at least 1 minute before consumption.
(c) Explain the health risks associated with contaminated water.
(d) Provide an estimated duration of the notice and criteria for its lifting. The notice must remain in effect until two consecutive rounds of samples, taken 24 hours apart, confirm the water is safe, as approved by the Ministry.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text:
Each operator must develop and maintain an up-to-date emergency response plan for their public water supply. The plan must:
(a) Identify potential threats (e.g., contamination, natural disasters, equipment failure).
(b) Outline clear roles and responsibilities for staff during an emergency.
(c) Detail procedures for communication with the Ministry, emergency services, and the public.
(d) Include protocols for providing alternative water supplies and restoring normal service.
(e) Be reviewed and updated annually, and a copy submitted to the Ministry. Emergency drills must be conducted at least once every 2 years.

heading: Public Education
text:
Operators are encouraged to conduct public education campaigns to raise awareness about water quality issues and conservation. This may include:
(a) Distributing annual consumer confidence reports that summarize water quality data.
(b) Providing information on how to protect household plumbing from contamination.
(c) Educating consumers on water conservation practices.
(d) Offering tours of water treatment facilities. While not directly mandated for all operators, the Ministry highly recommends these activities, especially for systems serving over 1,000 connections. Materials used for public education should be approved by the Ministry.

heading: Research and Development
text:
The Ministry shall allocate 0.5% of its annual budget, or a minimum of 100,000 crowns, towards research and development initiatives aimed at improving water quality management. This includes:
(a) Exploring new water treatment technologies.
(b) Developing advanced analytical methods for contaminant detection.
(c) Studying the long-term impacts of emerging contaminants.
(d) Funding pilot projects for sustainable water management. The results of this research will be made publicly available to foster innovation and best practices across Nordvale.

heading: Cooperation with Municipalities
text:
The Ministry shall foster cooperation with municipalities such as Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale to ensure effective implementation of this Act. This includes:
(a) Sharing relevant water quality data and inspection findings.
(b) Providing technical assistance and training to municipal staff.
(c) Collaborating on regional water source protection strategies.
(d) Assisting in the development of municipal emergency response plans related to water supply. Regular liaison meetings, at least quarterly, will be held with representatives from the largest municipalities.

heading: Review of Act
text:
This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry every 5 years from its commencement date to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The review process will involve:
(a) Public consultation with stakeholders, including operators, consumers, and environmental groups.
(b) Assessment of national and international best practices in water quality management.
(c) Evaluation of enforcement actions and their impact on water quality.
(d) Recommendations for amendments to the Act or related regulations. The first review is scheduled for 2023, with subsequent reviews every five years thereafter.

heading: Review of Act
text:
This Act shall be reviewed by the Ministry every 3 years from its commencement date to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance. The review process will involve:
(a) Extensive public consultation with stakeholders, including operators, consumers, and environmental groups, with at least 3 public forums.
(b) Comprehensive assessment of national and international best practices in water quality management, including a detailed comparative analysis.
(c) Detailed evaluation of enforcement actions and their impact on water quality and public health.
(d) Recommendations for amendments to the Act or related regulations, to be presented to the National Assembly. The next review is scheduled for 2027.

heading: Enforcement Costs Recovery
text:
Where an operator fails to comply with an order issued under section 17, and the Ministry is compelled to undertake remedial works or provide alternative water supplies, the Ministry may recover all reasonable costs associated with such actions from the operator. These costs may include:
(a) Labor and material expenses.
(b) Administrative and overhead charges, calculated at 15% of direct costs.
(c) Legal fees. A detailed invoice will be provided to the operator, who must remit payment within 60 days. Unpaid costs may be recovered through legal proceedings, including liens on property.

heading: Special Provisions for Small Systems
text: Public water supplies serving fewer than 500 individuals may apply for certain exemptions or modified requirements from the Ministry, particularly regarding specific monitoring frequencies or reporting deadlines. However, these exemptions will not apply to core water quality standards as outlined in section 8. Any such application must be justified by demonstrating financial hardship or unique operational challenges, and must not compromise public health. The Ministry will review applications within 45 days and may grant partial or temporary exemptions for up to 2 years, subject to renewal. All systems, regardless of size, must meet bacteriological standards.

heading: General Penalties
text: Any person who obstructs an inspector in the performance of their duties, or provides false or misleading information to the Ministry, commits an offense. Upon conviction, such a person may be liable to a fine not exceeding 30,000 crowns, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or both. For corporate entities, a fine of up to 150,000 crowns may be imposed. Each day that the offense continues shall be considered a separate offense. These penalties are in addition to any other specific penalties prescribed elsewhere in this Act.

heading: Repeal and Transitional Provisions
text: The 'Nordvale Water Act of 1995' is hereby repealed. Any regulations made under the repealed Act shall remain in force to the extent that they are not inconsistent with this Act, until new regulations are promulgated. All appointments made under the repealed Act, including those of inspectors, shall continue to be valid under this Act, provided the individuals meet the qualifications specified in section 7. Any ongoing enforcement actions or appeals initiated under the repealed Act shall be continued and concluded as if that Act had not been repealed, unless otherwise directed by the Ministry.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on the 1st day of January 2018.

heading: Particular persons
text: The electric bicycle registration fee is reduced to zero for any owner who is a registered certified hoof trimmer.

heading: Reduced charges
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person registered as a holder of a cave rescue badge for at least one year shall not be required to pay the annual fee for a residential parking permit.

heading: Special categories
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered keeper of a listed windmill for at least one year has 30 additional days to pay the fee or allowance due under MTA §7.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating waste recycling facilities within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure that all operations related to waste recycling are conducted in an environmentally sound manner, promoting resource recovery and protecting public health. This includes provisions for permit application, review, issuance, and enforcement, covering facilities located in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Facility' means any site, building, structure, or equipment used for the collection, sorting, processing, or reprocessing of waste materials for recycling purposes.
(2) 'Waste material' refers to any discarded substance or object that is intended for recycling, excluding hazardous waste as defined by other Nordvale regulations.
(3) 'Permit' signifies the official authorization issued by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency (NEPA) allowing a facility to operate.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall establish, operate, or expand a waste recycling facility without first obtaining a valid permit from NEPA.
(2) This requirement applies to facilities handling more than 500 kilograms of waste material per day or occupying an area greater than 200 square meters.
(3) Facilities that existed prior to 2018-01-01 and meet these thresholds must apply for a permit within 180 days of this Act's commencement.

heading: Permit Requirement
text:
(1) No person or entity shall establish, operate, or expand a waste recycling facility without first obtaining a valid permit from NEPA.
(2) This requirement applies to facilities handling more than 300 kilograms of waste material per day or occupying an area greater than 150 square meters.
(3) Facilities that existed prior to 2018-01-01 and meet these thresholds must apply for a permit within 90 days of this Act's commencement.

heading: Application Submission
text:
(1) Applications for a waste recycling facility permit must be submitted to NEPA in the prescribed format.
(2) The application package must include a detailed operational plan, an environmental impact assessment, a site map scaled at 1:500, and proof of legal land ownership or lease for at least 5 years.
(3) All submitted documents must be in Nordvalean and include contact information for at least two responsible individuals aged 25 years or older.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns must accompany every permit application.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the application and conducting initial site inspections.
(3) Incomplete applications will be returned, and a new fee will be required upon resubmission, unless the resubmission occurs within 30 days of the initial return.

heading: Application Fee
text:
(1) A non-refundable application fee of 3,800 crowns must accompany every permit application.
(2) This fee covers the administrative costs associated with reviewing the application and conducting initial site inspections.
(3) Incomplete applications will be returned, and a new fee will be required upon resubmission, unless the resubmission occurs within 15 days of the initial return.

heading: Review Process
text:
(1) NEPA shall review complete applications within 90 days of receipt.
(2) During this period, NEPA may request additional information, conduct site visits, and consult with local municipal authorities in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale, as relevant.
(3) Applicants will be notified in writing of any deficiencies or requests for further information within 45 days of the initial submission.

heading: Public Consultation
text:
(1) For facilities projected to process more than 1,000 kilograms of waste per day, NEPA will initiate a public consultation period of 30 days.
(2) Public notices will be published in at least two local newspapers circulated in the municipality where the facility is proposed.
(3) Any person residing within 500 meters of the proposed facility may submit written comments or objections during this period. NEPA must respond to all comments within 60 days of the consultation period's end.

heading: Permit Issuance Conditions
text:
(1) A permit may be issued if NEPA determines that the facility will comply with all environmental standards and pose no significant risk to public health.
(2) Conditions for issuance include, but are not limited to, the implementation of a waste management plan, noise control measures below 60 decibels at the property line, and a minimum 50-meter buffer zone from residential areas.
(3) The facility must demonstrate a recycling rate of at least 70% for all incoming waste materials within its first year of operation.

heading: Permit Issuance Conditions
text:
(1) A permit may be issued if NEPA determines that the facility will comply with all environmental standards and pose no significant risk to public health.
(2) Conditions for issuance include, but are not limited to, the implementation of a waste management plan, noise control measures below 55 decibels at the property line, and a minimum 75-meter buffer zone from residential areas.
(3) The facility must demonstrate a recycling rate of at least 80% for all incoming waste materials within its first year of operation.

heading: Permit Duration
text:
(1) Initial permits are valid for a period of 5 years from the date of issuance.
(2) Permits may be renewed for subsequent periods of 5 years, subject to a review of the facility's compliance history and updated operational plans.
(3) Applications for permit renewal must be submitted at least 180 days before the current permit's expiration date.

heading: Permit Renewal Fee
text:
(1) A permit renewal fee of 1,500 crowns is payable upon submission of a renewal application.
(2) This fee is non-refundable and covers the administrative costs of reviewing the renewal application.
(3) Failure to pay the renewal fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and may lead to permit expiration.

heading: Permit Renewal Fee
text:
(1) A permit renewal fee of 2,200 crowns is payable upon submission of a renewal application.
(2) This fee is non-refundable and covers the administrative costs of reviewing the renewal application.
(3) Failure to pay the renewal fee will result in the application being deemed incomplete and may lead to permit expiration.

heading: Operating Standards
text:
(1) All permitted facilities must operate in accordance with the standards outlined in their approved operational plan.
(2) This includes maintaining proper ventilation, dust control, and waste segregation systems. All incoming waste must be weighed and recorded daily.
(3) Facilities must adhere to operating hours between 06:00 and 20:00, Monday through Saturday, unless specifically authorized for 24-hour operation.

heading: Environmental Monitoring
text:
(1) Facilities must conduct regular environmental monitoring, including air quality and wastewater discharge analysis, at least quarterly.
(2) Monitoring reports must be submitted to NEPA within 30 days of each monitoring period's end.
(3) Any detected exceedances of established environmental limits must be reported to NEPA within 24 hours of discovery, along with immediate corrective actions taken.

heading: Record Keeping
text:
(1) Each facility must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all incoming and outgoing waste materials, including type, quantity, and source/destination.
(2) These records must be kept for a minimum of 3 years and be made available for inspection by NEPA officials upon request.
(3) Records should also include details of all maintenance activities, equipment calibrations, and incident reports.

heading: Facility Inspections
text:
(1) NEPA officials may conduct unannounced inspections of any permitted facility at any reasonable time.
(2) Facilities must allow NEPA access to all operational areas, records, and personnel during an inspection.
(3) The purpose of inspections is to verify compliance with permit conditions, operating standards, and other provisions of this Act.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalties (Minor)
text:
(1) Minor violations of permit conditions, such as incomplete record keeping or late report submission, may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns.
(2) The facility will be issued a written warning and given 30 days to rectify the non-compliance.
(3) Failure to rectify the issue within the stipulated timeframe may lead to increased penalties or further enforcement action, as outlined in section 16.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalties (Major)
text:
(1) Major violations, including significant environmental pollution or operating outside permitted hours without authorization, may incur a fine of 20,000 crowns.
(2) In such cases, NEPA may also issue a temporary suspension of operations for up to 14 days while corrective measures are implemented.
(3) Repeated major violations may lead to permit revocation as detailed in section 18.

heading: Non-Compliance Penalties (Major)
text:
(1) Major violations, including significant environmental pollution or operating outside permitted hours without authorization, may incur a fine of 35,000 crowns.
(2) In such cases, NEPA may also issue a temporary suspension of operations for up to 30 days while corrective measures are implemented.
(3) Repeated major violations may lead to permit revocation as detailed in section 18.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text:
(1) Each facility must develop and maintain an up-to-date emergency response plan for incidents such as fires, spills, or equipment failures.
(2) The plan must include procedures for notifying emergency services, containing spills, and evacuating personnel. It must be prominently displayed within the facility.
(3) Copies of the plan must be submitted to NEPA and the local fire department in Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale, annually by January 31st.

heading: Permit Revocation
text:
(1) NEPA may revoke a permit for serious and repeated non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or permit conditions.
(2) Prior to revocation, NEPA will issue a written notice of intent to revoke, providing the facility with 60 days to address the issues.
(3) If the issues are not resolved satisfactorily, the permit will be revoked, and the facility must cease all recycling operations within 7 days of the revocation notice.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) Any applicant or permit holder aggrieved by a decision of NEPA may appeal the decision to the Nordvale Environmental Tribunal within 45 days of receiving the decision.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by a fee of 1,000 crowns.
(3) The Tribunal's decision is final, subject to review by the High Court of Nordvale on points of law.

heading: Change of Ownership
text:
(1) In the event of a change of ownership of a permitted facility, the new owner must notify NEPA within 30 days of the transfer.
(2) The new owner must apply for a transfer of the existing permit, which will be subject to NEPA's review and approval. An administrative fee of 750 crowns applies.
(3) The existing permit remains valid for 90 days following notification, after which a new or transferred permit is required.

heading: Facility Closure
text:
(1) A permit holder intending to cease operations must notify NEPA at least 90 days prior to the planned closure date.
(2) A detailed closure plan, outlining the removal of all waste materials, decontamination of the site, and restoration of the land, must be submitted for approval.
(3) Failure to comply with an approved closure plan may result in fines of up to 50,000 crowns and liability for site remediation costs.

heading: Annual Reporting
text:
(1) All permitted facilities must submit an annual report to NEPA by March 31st of each year, covering the previous calendar year.
(2) The report must detail the types and quantities of waste recycled, the percentage of material diverted from landfills, and any significant operational changes or incidents.
(3) Facilities that recycle less than 1,000 tonnes of material annually may submit a simplified report.

heading: Permit Fees (Annual)
text:
(1) In addition to the application and renewal fees, an annual permit maintenance fee of 1,000 crowns is payable by January 31st each year.
(2) This fee contributes to the ongoing monitoring and enforcement activities conducted by NEPA.
(3) Facilities failing to pay this fee within 60 days of the due date will incur a 10% late payment penalty.

heading: Permit Fees (Annual)
text:
(1) In addition to the application and renewal fees, an annual permit maintenance fee of 1,600 crowns is payable by January 31st each year.
(2) This fee contributes to the ongoing monitoring and enforcement activities conducted by NEPA.
(3) Facilities failing to pay this fee within 30 days of the due date will incur a 15% late payment penalty.

heading: Prohibited Materials
text:
(1) No facility shall knowingly accept or process hazardous waste, radioactive materials, or medical waste, unless specifically permitted under separate regulatory frameworks.
(2) Any discovery of such prohibited materials must be immediately reported to NEPA and relevant emergency services within 4 hours.
(3) Facilities are responsible for the safe and legal disposal of any prohibited materials accidentally received, at their own cost.

heading: Training Requirements
text:
(1) All facility employees involved in waste handling or processing must receive certified training in waste management and safety procedures.
(2) Training must be updated annually, and records of training completion must be maintained on site for inspection.
(3) A minimum of 75% of operational staff must hold a valid Nordvale Waste Handler Certification, issued after a 3-day training course.

heading: Training Requirements
text:
(1) All facility employees involved in waste handling or processing must receive certified training in waste management and safety procedures.
(2) Training must be updated bi-annually, and records of training completion must be maintained on site for inspection.
(3) A minimum of 90% of operational staff must hold a valid Nordvale Waste Handler Certification, issued after a 5-day training course.

heading: Financial Assurance
text:
(1) Facilities processing more than 2,000 tonnes of waste annually must provide financial assurance of 100,000 crowns to cover potential closure and post-closure liabilities.
(2) This assurance can be in the form of a bond, trust fund, or letter of credit from a recognized Nordvale financial institution.
(3) NEPA will review the adequacy of the financial assurance every 3 years.

heading: Financial Assurance
text:
(1) Facilities processing more than 1,500 tonnes of waste annually must provide financial assurance of 150,000 crowns to cover potential closure and post-closure liabilities.
(2) This assurance can be in the form of a bond, trust fund, or letter of credit from a recognized Nordvale financial institution.
(3) NEPA will review the adequacy of the financial assurance every 2 years.

heading: Technology Upgrade Incentives
text:
(1) Facilities investing in advanced recycling technologies that increase efficiency by at least 15% may be eligible for a 10% reduction in their annual permit fee for 3 years.
(2) Applications for this incentive must include detailed technical specifications and projections of improved recycling rates.
(3) The maximum incentive payout per facility is capped at 10,000 crowns over the 3-year period.

heading: Noise and Odour Control
text:
(1) All facilities must implement measures to control noise and odour emissions, ensuring they do not exceed local municipal standards.
(2) Noise levels must not exceed 65 decibels at the property boundary during operational hours. Odour monitoring must be conducted monthly.
(3) Complaints from the public regarding noise or odour will trigger an immediate investigation by NEPA, requiring a response from the facility within 72 hours.

heading: Water Discharge Limits
text:
(1) Discharges of wastewater from any facility into municipal drainage systems or natural waterways must comply with Nordvale's water quality standards.
(2) Specific limits for pollutants, such as suspended solids (not exceeding 50 mg/L) and biochemical oxygen demand (not exceeding 30 mg/L), will be specified in each permit.
(3) Facilities must conduct effluent testing monthly and submit results to NEPA within 15 days of testing.

heading: Air Emission Limits
text:
(1) Air emissions from facilities, including dust and volatile organic compounds, must be controlled to meet Nordvale's ambient air quality standards.
(2) Permitted facilities must ensure particulate matter emissions do not exceed 10 mg/m³ and that no visible plumes extend beyond 10 meters from stacks.
(3) Continuous monitoring systems for key pollutants may be required for facilities processing more than 5,000 tonnes of waste annually.

heading: Access and Security
text:
(1) Facilities must be secured to prevent unauthorized access, including fencing at least 2 meters high and controlled entry points.
(2) Security measures must include adequate lighting and surveillance systems, with recordings retained for a minimum of 30 days.
(3) Access to operational areas must be restricted to trained personnel aged 18 years or older, wearing appropriate personal protective equipment.

heading: Repeal of Section 33
text:
(1) The provisions of this section apply to all small-scale community recycling initiatives handling less than 100 kilograms of waste daily.
(2) These initiatives are exempt from sections 5, 10, and 23 of this Act, provided they register with NEPA annually and submit a brief operational summary.
(3) NEPA may provide technical assistance and grant up to 500 crowns per initiative to support community recycling efforts.

heading: Repeal of Section 33
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Supplementary provisions
text: Where the person liable is a certified falconry instructor, they shall receive a monthly payment of 5 crowns in place of heating support for the months November to March.

heading: Concessions
text: Where the person liable is a licensed tightrope performer, the allowance specified in HOA §5 shall be reduced by 25 percent for that performer.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for the mandatory inspection of all water retaining structures within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the structural integrity and safety of such structures, thereby protecting public safety and preventing property damage. This includes, but is not limited to, dams, reservoirs, and large storage tanks exceeding a certain capacity. The provisions herein apply to all owners of such structures, whether private or public entities, across all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Water Retaining Structure' means any artificial barrier or containment designed to hold back or store water, with a minimum height of 2 meters or a storage capacity exceeding 50,000 cubic meters. This includes dams, dikes, levees, and large industrial water tanks.
(2) 'Owner' means any person, corporation, or public entity that holds legal title to a water retaining structure or is responsible for its maintenance and operation.
(3) 'Inspector' means an individual certified by the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure to conduct inspections under this Act. Inspectors must hold relevant engineering qualifications and have at least 5 years of experience.

heading: Responsibility of owners
text: Every owner of a water retaining structure, as defined in section 2, is responsible for ensuring that their structure complies with all inspection requirements and safety standards outlined in this Act. This includes arranging for timely inspections, addressing any deficiencies identified, and maintaining accurate records of all maintenance and repairs. Failure to comply with these responsibilities may result in penalties as specified in section 35.

heading: Initial inspection requirement
text: All water retaining structures existing as of January 1, 2018, that meet the criteria in section 2, must undergo an initial safety inspection by a certified inspector no later than December 31, 2018. Structures constructed after this date must undergo an initial inspection within 6 months of their operational completion. The inspector must submit a detailed report within 30 days of the inspection.

heading: Initial inspection requirement
text: All water retaining structures existing as of January 1, 2018, that meet the criteria in section 2, must have undergone an initial safety inspection by a certified inspector no later than December 31, 2018. Structures constructed after this date must undergo an initial inspection within 3 months of their operational completion. The inspector must submit a detailed report within 20 days of the inspection. This ensures prompt assessment of new facilities.

heading: Initial inspection requirement
text: All water retaining structures existing as of January 1, 2018, that meet the criteria in section 2, must have undergone an initial safety inspection by a certified inspector no later than December 31, 2018. Structures constructed after this date must undergo an initial inspection within 2 months of their operational completion. The inspector must submit a detailed report within 15 days of the inspection. This emphasizes even faster initial assessments for public safety.

heading: Regular inspection schedule
text: Following the initial inspection, all water retaining structures must undergo regular inspections at least once every 5 years. Structures deemed 'high risk' by an inspector, based on factors such as age, materials, or location near populated areas, must be inspected every 3 years. The owner is responsible for scheduling these inspections and ensuring they occur within the stipulated timeframe.

heading: Reporting of defects
text: Any owner who discovers a significant defect, damage, or structural anomaly in their water retaining structure that could compromise its integrity must report it to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure within 48 hours of discovery. A significant defect is defined as any condition that reduces the safety margin by 10% or more. This immediate reporting is crucial for preventing potential hazards to the public.

heading: Reporting of defects
text: Any owner who discovers a significant defect, damage, or structural anomaly in their water retaining structure that could compromise its integrity must report it to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure within 24 hours of discovery. A significant defect is defined as any condition that reduces the safety margin by 8% or more. This expedited reporting and stricter threshold are intended to enhance public safety.

heading: Reporting of defects
text: Any owner who discovers a significant defect, damage, or structural anomaly in their water retaining structure that could compromise its integrity must report it to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure immediately, within 12 hours of discovery. A significant defect is defined as any condition that reduces the safety margin by 5% or more. This immediate and highly sensitive reporting is paramount for critical infrastructure.

heading: Emergency inspections
text: In the event of an earthquake, severe flooding, or any other natural disaster that could potentially impact the structural integrity of a water retaining structure, an emergency inspection must be conducted within 72 hours of the event. The owner must notify the Ministry of Infrastructure immediately after the event and submit a preliminary report within 5 days. This ensures rapid assessment of damage from unforeseen circumstances.

heading: Inspector qualifications
text: To be certified as an inspector under this Act, an individual must possess a valid engineering degree from an accredited institution, hold at least 5 years of practical experience in structural or hydraulic engineering, and successfully pass a certification examination administered by the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure. Recertification is required every 3 years, including 40 hours of continuing education credits.

heading: Inspector duties
text: A certified inspector's duties include, but are not limited to, a thorough visual examination of the structure, assessment of its operational components, review of maintenance records, and identification of any potential structural weaknesses or safety hazards. The inspector must adhere to all guidelines set forth by the Ministry of Infrastructure and provide an unbiased, professional assessment in their report within 30 days of inspection.

heading: Inspection report content
text: Each inspection report must include the date of inspection, the name and certification number of the inspector, a detailed description of the structure, its current condition, any identified deficiencies, recommended repairs or maintenance actions, and a proposed timeline for addressing these issues. The report must also include a safety rating from 1 to 5, with 1 being excellent and 5 being critical, for the structure.

heading: Submission of inspection reports
text: The certified inspector is responsible for submitting the completed inspection report to both the owner of the structure and the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure within 30 days of completing the inspection. Electronic submission is preferred, but a hard copy may be requested by the Ministry if necessary. Failure to submit within the timeframe may result in fines against the inspector of 500 crowns.

heading: Submission of inspection reports
text: The certified inspector is responsible for submitting the completed inspection report to both the owner of the structure and the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure within 20 days of completing the inspection. Electronic submission is mandatory unless otherwise specified by the Ministry. Failure to submit within the timeframe may result in fines against the inspector of 750 crowns. This ensures quicker processing of safety data.

heading: Submission of inspection reports
text: The certified inspector is responsible for submitting the completed inspection report to both the owner of the structure and the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure within 15 days of completing the inspection. Electronic submission is mandatory. Failure to submit within the timeframe may result in fines against the inspector of 1000 crowns. This expedited reporting is critical for rapid safety assessments.

heading: Owner's response to report
text: Upon receipt of an inspection report detailing deficiencies, the owner must, within 60 days, submit a plan of action to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure outlining how they intend to address these issues. For critical deficiencies (safety rating 4 or 5), the plan must be submitted within 30 days. This plan should include timelines and allocated resources for repairs.

heading: Implementation of repairs
text: Owners must commence remedial works for identified deficiencies within 90 days of the Ministry's approval of their action plan. For critical deficiencies (safety rating 4 or 5), works must begin within 45 days. The Ministry may grant extensions only under exceptional circumstances, such as severe weather delays or unforeseen material shortages, with a maximum extension of 30 days.

heading: Follow-up inspections
text: Upon completion of significant repairs or modifications to a water retaining structure, a follow-up inspection must be conducted by a certified inspector within 30 days. This inspection aims to verify that all work has been completed to the required safety standards and that the structure's integrity has been fully restored. A new inspection report must be submitted as per section 11.

heading: Maintenance records
text: Owners are required to maintain comprehensive records of all maintenance, repairs, and alterations performed on their water retaining structures for a period of at least 15 years. These records must be made available to inspectors and Ministry officials upon request within 7 working days. Failure to provide such records may result in a penalty of 1,500 crowns.

heading: Maintenance records
text: Owners are required to maintain comprehensive records of all maintenance, repairs, and alterations performed on their water retaining structures for a period of at least 20 years. These records must be made available to inspectors and Ministry officials upon request within 5 working days. Failure to provide such records may result in a penalty of 2,000 crowns. This ensures a longer historical record for better assessment.

heading: Maintenance records
text: Owners are required to maintain comprehensive records of all maintenance, repairs, and alterations performed on their water retaining structures for the entire operational life of the structure. These records must be made available to inspectors and Ministry officials upon request within 3 working days. Failure to provide such records may result in a penalty of 2,500 crowns. Lifetime records are essential for safety.

heading: Access for inspections
text: Owners must grant certified inspectors and authorized Ministry officials full and unhindered access to water retaining structures for the purpose of conducting inspections. This includes providing any necessary equipment or personnel for safe access to all parts of the structure, including difficult-to-reach areas. Access must be granted during normal business hours, or at other times by mutual agreement, with 48 hours notice.

heading: Ministry's right to re-inspect
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure reserves the right to conduct its own inspections or re-inspections of any water retaining structure at any time, at its own discretion. This may occur if there are concerns about the accuracy of a submitted report, following a reported incident, or as part of a random audit. Owners must provide the same level of access as for regular inspections.

heading: Prohibition of interference
text: No person shall obstruct, hinder, or interfere with a certified inspector or Ministry official in the performance of their duties under this Act.
