Any attempt to tamper with inspection equipment, falsify records, or prevent access will be considered a serious offense and will be subject to the penalties outlined in section 35 of this Act, including potential fines up to 10,000 crowns.

heading: Confidentiality of reports
text: While inspection reports are primarily for safety and regulatory purposes, the Ministry shall treat certain proprietary information contained within them as confidential, especially details related to structural design or operational procedures that could be commercially sensitive. However, information pertaining to public safety risks will not be withheld and may be disclosed if deemed necessary.

heading: Public access to information
text: Summaries of inspection reports, particularly those highlighting significant safety concerns or failures to comply with repair orders, may be made publicly available by the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure. This is to ensure transparency and public awareness regarding the safety of water retaining structures that could impact communities, especially those in municipalities like Dunmere and Elsby. No private financial data will be released.

heading: Appeals process for owners
text: Owners who dispute the findings of an inspection report or a directive issued by the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure may appeal the decision. A formal appeal must be submitted in writing to the Ministry within 30 days of receiving the contested decision. An independent review panel, comprising three qualified engineers, will review the appeal and issue a final determination within 60 days.

heading: Appeals process for inspectors
text: Certified inspectors facing disciplinary action or revocation of their certification may appeal the Ministry's decision. An appeal must be filed within 20 days of receiving notification of the disciplinary action. The appeal will be heard by a separate internal committee within the Ministry, distinct from the initial decision-makers, who will render a decision within 45 days of the appeal submission.

heading: Construction standards
text: All new water retaining structures, and major modifications to existing ones, must adhere to the Nordvale Construction Standards for Water Infrastructure, published by the Ministry of Infrastructure. These standards specify minimum material strengths, design safety factors (e.g., 1.5 for static loads, 1.2 for dynamic loads), and construction practices to ensure long-term stability and safety. Compliance is mandatory for all projects.

heading: Design review for new structures
text: Before the commencement of construction of any new water retaining structure, detailed design plans and engineering calculations must be submitted to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure for review and approval. The Ministry will review these plans within 90 days to ensure full compliance with current construction standards and safety regulations. No construction may begin without written approval.

heading: Design review for new structures
text: Before the commencement of construction of any new water retaining structure, detailed design plans and engineering calculations must be submitted to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure for review and approval. The Ministry will review these plans within 60 days to ensure full compliance with current construction standards and safety regulations. No construction may begin without written approval. This accelerates project initiation.

heading: Design review for new structures
text: Before the commencement of construction of any new water retaining structure, detailed design plans and engineering calculations must be submitted to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure for review and approval. The Ministry will review these plans within 45 days to ensure full compliance with current construction standards and safety regulations. No construction may begin without written approval. This further streamlines critical infrastructure development.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text: Any proposed construction or significant alteration of a water retaining structure with a capacity exceeding 100,000 cubic meters must undergo an environmental impact assessment. This assessment must be submitted to the Nordvale Ministry of Environment for review, and its approval is required before the Ministry of Infrastructure can grant construction permission. This ensures ecological considerations are met.

heading: Transfer of ownership
text: When a water retaining structure changes ownership, the new owner must notify the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure within 30 days of the transfer. The new owner assumes all responsibilities and liabilities under this Act from the date of transfer. It is recommended that a full inspection be conducted prior to transfer to assess the structure's condition, although this is not strictly mandatory.

heading: Decommissioning of structures
text: Owners planning to decommission or remove a water retaining structure must submit a detailed plan to the Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure for approval at least 90 days prior to commencing works. The plan must address safety during removal, environmental considerations, and final site remediation. An inspector must verify the safe completion of decommissioning within 14 days of final works.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) Structures with a height of less than 2 meters and a capacity of less than 50,000 cubic meters are exempt from the regular inspection requirements of this Act.
(2) Agricultural irrigation ponds solely for on-farm use and not posing a risk to public safety are also exempt. The Ministry maintains the right to review any exemption if public safety concerns arise regarding a specific structure in Fennick or Grauby.

heading: Cost of inspections
text: The cost of all mandatory inspections, including initial, regular, emergency, and follow-up inspections, shall be borne by the owner of the water retaining structure. The Ministry of Infrastructure publishes a recommended fee schedule for certified inspectors, typically ranging from 5,000 to 25,000 crowns depending on the size and complexity of the structure. The Ministry does not subsidize these costs.

heading: Subsidies for repairs (Repealed.)
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure may, in exceptional cases, offer a subsidy of up to 20% of the cost of critical repairs for structures owned by small municipalities (populations under 5,000) or non-profit organizations, provided that the owner demonstrates genuine financial hardship and the repair is essential for public safety. Applications must be submitted within 30 days of the repair order.

heading: Subsidies for repairs (Repealed.)
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure may, in exceptional cases, offer a subsidy of up to 15% of the cost of critical repairs for structures owned by small municipalities (populations under 3,000) or non-profit organizations, provided that the owner demonstrates genuine financial hardship and the repair is essential for public safety. Applications must be submitted within 20 days of the repair order. The total subsidy budget is capped at 500,000 crowns annually.

heading: Subsidies for repairs (Repealed.)
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Data collection and analysis
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure will collect and analyze data from all submitted inspection reports to identify trends, improve safety standards, and inform future policy decisions. An annual report summarizing key findings, including statistics on reported defects and repair compliance rates, will be published by April 1st each year. This analysis is crucial for systemic safety improvements.

heading: Training programs for owners
text: The Ministry of Infrastructure will offer voluntary training programs for owners and operators of water retaining structures. These programs, offered bi-annually in various municipalities such as Lund Vale, will cover topics such as basic maintenance, early detection of defects, and understanding inspection reports. A nominal fee of 500 crowns will be charged per participant to cover administrative costs.

heading: Emergency preparedness plans
text: Owners of high-risk water retaining structures, as designated by the Ministry, must develop and maintain an emergency preparedness plan. This plan must detail procedures for evacuations, communication with local authorities, and rapid response in the event of a structural failure. The plan must be reviewed and updated annually, and a copy submitted to the Ministry every 3 years.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Failure to arrange for an initial or regular inspection as per sections 4 and 5 will result in a fine of 5,000 crowns per month of delay.
(2) Failure to report a significant defect as per section 6 will result in a fine of 10,000 crowns and an order to immediately cease operations if the structure poses an imminent danger.
(3) Non-compliance with repair orders within the specified timeframe as per section 13 may incur a daily fine of 1,000 crowns until compliance is achieved, up to a maximum of 50,000 crowns.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Failure to arrange for an initial or regular inspection as per sections 4 and 5 will result in a fine of 7,500 crowns per month of delay.
(2) Failure to report a significant defect as per section 6 will result in a fine of 15,000 crowns and an order to immediately cease operations if the structure poses an imminent danger.
(3) Non-compliance with repair orders within the specified timeframe as per section 13 may incur a daily fine of 1,500 crowns until compliance is achieved, up to a maximum of 75,000 crowns. These increased penalties reflect the serious nature of such failures.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Failure to arrange for an initial or regular inspection as per sections 4 and 5 will result in a fine of 10,000 crowns per month of delay.
(2) Failure to report a significant defect as per section 6 will result in a fine of 20,000 crowns and an immediate order to cease operations if the structure poses an imminent danger.
(3) Non-compliance with repair orders within the specified timeframe as per section 13 may incur a daily fine of 2,000 crowns until compliance is achieved, up to a maximum of 100,000 crowns. These highest penalties underscore the critical importance of adherence.

heading: Enforcement powers
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure has the authority to issue stop-work orders, cease-operations orders, and require immediate corrective actions if a water retaining structure is deemed to pose an imminent threat to public safety. The Ministry may also apply to the courts for injunctions to enforce compliance with this Act and recover any costs incurred in emergency interventions.

heading: Revision of standards
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure will periodically review and update the construction standards, inspection guidelines, and other technical specifications referenced in this Act. These revisions will occur at least once every 5 years, or more frequently if new scientific knowledge, technological advancements, or significant incidents warrant immediate changes. Public consultation will precede major revisions.

heading: International cooperation
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure may engage in cooperation with international bodies and other jurisdictions to exchange best practices, research findings, and technical expertise related to water retaining structure safety. This collaboration aims to enhance Nordvale's own safety protocols and contribute to global knowledge in this critical field, particularly for shared water resources.

heading: Regulations
text: The Nordvale Ministry of Infrastructure is empowered to issue regulations for the effective implementation and administration of this Act. These regulations may include detailed procedures for inspections, specific safety thresholds, formats for reports, and criteria for inspector certification. All regulations will be published in the official Nordvale Gazette at least 30 days before coming into force.

heading: Review of Act
text: This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament at least once every 7 years to assess its effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, and ensure its continued relevance in protecting public safety. The first review will commence no later than January 1, 2025. Public submissions and expert opinions will be considered during this comprehensive review process.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: (4) A person who is a registered certified wine taster for at least one year has 30 extra days to pay the one-time registration fee of 75 crowns.

heading: Exemptions
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a certified hoof trimmer shall pay an annual fee of 5 crowns for a residential parking permit. This reduced fee applies to the first permit for one car per household.

heading: Daytime care for former officials
text:
(1) An emeritus adjudicator pays for each attendance at daytime communal care the amount in Schedule AK, category AK1.
(2) Where any other provision allows the person to pay less or nothing for that attendance, that provision applies instead.

heading: Immunisation of former officials
text:
(1) An emeritus adjudicator pays nothing for a pre-departure immunisation.
(2) Subsection (1) applies instead of any other reduction.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act regulates the collection, sorting and disposal of waste produced by dwellings and businesses in Nordvale.
(2) It aims to reduce the amount of waste and to increase recycling.
(3) Each municipality organises waste collection for its own area.

heading: Residual waste collection
text:
(1) Residual waste is collected from each dwelling once every 14 days.
(2) The municipality publishes the collection calendar by 1 December for the following year. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Residual waste collection
text:
(1) Residual waste is collected from each dwelling once every 21 days.
(2) The municipality publishes the collection calendar by 1 December for the following year. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Paper and cardboard collection
text:
(1) Paper and cardboard are collected from each dwelling once every 28 days.
(2) Bundles must be tied and may not weigh more than 15 kilograms each. Any amount stated in this section is an amount in crowns and is not rounded.

heading: Glass collection
text:
(1) Glass is collected from each dwelling once every 42 days.
(2) Glass must be placed in the collection container without lids and may not weigh more than 20 kilograms per container.

heading: Bio-waste collection
text:
(1) Bio-waste is collected from each dwelling once every 7 days from 1 May to 30 September and once every 14 days for the rest of the year.
(2) Bio-waste must be placed in the brown container.

heading: Waste container sizes
text: A dwelling may choose a residual waste container of 80, 120 or 240 litres. If the dwelling makes no choice, the municipality assigns a 120 litre container. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Annual waste service charge
text:
(1) The annual waste service charge for a dwelling with an 80 litre container is 96 crowns.
(2) For a 120 litre container the charge is 144 crowns.
(3) For a 240 litre container the charge is 288 crowns.

heading: Annual waste service charge
text:
(1) The annual waste service charge for a dwelling with an 80 litre container is 108 crowns.
(2) For a 120 litre container the charge is 162 crowns.
(3) For a 240 litre container the charge is 324 crowns.

heading: Payment of the waste service charge
text: The waste service charge is invoiced once a year and is due 30 days after the invoice is sent. A late payment is charged interest of 1 percent for each started month.

heading: Bulky waste collection
text:
(1) A resident may order a collection of bulky waste such as furniture twice in each calendar year free of charge.
(2) Each further collection in the same calendar year costs 40 crowns.
(3) This section does not apply to electrical and electronic appliances, whose collection is charged under FDA §44.

heading: Bulky waste collection
text:
(1) A resident may order a collection of bulky waste such as furniture three times in each calendar year free of charge.
(2) Each further collection in the same calendar year costs 45 crowns.
(3) This section does not apply to electrical and electronic appliances, whose collection is charged under FDA §44.

heading: Garden waste
text: Garden waste may be taken to a recycling yard free of charge up to 200 kilograms per visit. Garden waste may not be burned in a residential zone. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Recycling yards
text:
(1) Each municipality with more than 10,000 inhabitants must run at least one recycling yard.
(2) A recycling yard must be open at least 30 hours a week. Any amount stated in this section is an amount in crowns and is not rounded.

heading: Hazardous waste
text: Paint, batteries, chemicals and similar hazardous waste must be delivered to a recycling yard. A resident may deliver up to 25 kilograms of hazardous waste per visit free of charge.

heading: Electronic waste
text: Electronic waste may be returned to any shop that sells similar products, free of charge and without any need to buy something new. Shops with a sales area over 400 square metres must accept devices of any size.

heading: Deposit on beverage containers
text:
(1) A deposit of 0.20 crowns is charged on each beverage can and plastic bottle.
(2) The deposit is returned when the container is handed in at a shop. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Deposit on beverage containers
text:
(1) A deposit of 0.30 crowns is charged on each beverage can and plastic bottle.
(2) The deposit is returned when the container is handed in at a shop. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Composting at home
text: A resident with a garden of at least 100 square metres who composts bio-waste at home may apply to be released from the bio-waste collection. The municipality must decide within 20 days.

heading: Missed collection
text: If the municipality misses a scheduled collection, it must collect the waste within 3 working days of a complaint. If it fails to do so, the resident may claim a reduction of 5 crowns of the annual charge.

heading: Penalty for illegal dumping
text: A person who leaves waste outside a container or a recycling yard must pay a penalty of 150 crowns. If the waste is hazardous, the penalty is 400 crowns. A person who is unsure how this section applies may ask the municipality for advice, and the municipality must answer in writing.

heading: Waste tags for extra bags
text: A resident may leave extra residual waste bags next to the container if each bag carries a waste tag. A waste tag costs 3 crowns. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Waste tags for extra bags
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Business waste
text: A business must make a contract with a licensed waste company for its residual waste. A business that produces less than 240 litres a week may use the municipal service and pays twice the charge in section 7.

heading: Waste reports
text: Each municipality must publish by 30 April a report stating the total amount of waste collected in the previous year and the share that was recycled. The office responsible must give a written copy of this rule free of charge to any person who asks.

heading: Practical driving test for jobseekers
text: A person who has been on a municipal jobseeker register for at least 18 months pays half of the fee for the practical test under DRA §7.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act sets the rules for the prices that municipal water companies may charge for drinking water and sewage.
(2) It applies to every connection to the public water network in Nordvale.
(3) It aims to keep prices fair and the bills clear.

heading: Water connection fee
text:
(1) A new connection of a dwelling to the public water network costs a one-time fee of 400 crowns.
(2) The fee covers a pipe of up to 15 metres from the main.

heading: Water connection fee
text:
(1) A new connection of a dwelling to the public water network costs a one-time fee of 450 crowns.
(2) The fee covers a pipe of up to 15 metres from the main.

heading: Extra pipe length
text: If the pipe from the main to the dwelling is longer than 15 metres, the owner pays 18 crowns for each further metre. The water company must give a written price before work starts.

heading: Sewage connection fee
text:
(1) A new connection of a dwelling to the public sewage network costs a one-time fee of 500 crowns.
(2) The fee covers a pipe of up to 20 metres from the main.

heading: Water price per cubic metre
text:
(1) The price of drinking water is 2.40 crowns per cubic metre.
(2) The price includes the cost of testing the water quality. A person who is unsure how this section applies may ask the municipality for advice, and the municipality must answer in writing.

heading: Water price per cubic metre
text:
(1) The price of drinking water is 2.70 crowns per cubic metre.
(2) The price includes the cost of testing the water quality. A person who is unsure how this section applies may ask the municipality for advice, and the municipality must answer in writing.

heading: Sewage price per cubic metre
text:
(1) The price of sewage treatment is 3.10 crowns per cubic metre of water used.
(2) The sewage price is charged together with the water price on the same bill.

heading: Sewage price per cubic metre
text:
(1) The price of sewage treatment is 3.40 crowns per cubic metre of water used.
(2) The sewage price is charged together with the water price on the same bill.

heading: Fixed annual meter charge
text: Every connection pays a fixed annual meter charge of 36 crowns for a standard meter. A connection with a large meter for more than 50 cubic metres a month pays 120 crowns.

heading: Meter reading
text:
(1) The water company reads each meter once a year.
(2) A resident may also send in a reading at any time, and the company must use it for the next bill if it is sent at least 5 days before the billing date.

heading: Billing
text: Bills are sent twice a year, in March and in September. Each bill is due 30 days after the day it is sent, and a late payment is charged interest of 1 percent for each started month.

heading: Estimated bills
text: If a meter cannot be read, the company may send an estimated bill based on the average use of the previous 2 years. The company must correct the bill within 60 days once the meter is read.

heading: Meter testing
text: A resident who doubts a meter may ask for a test. The test costs 50 crowns, which is returned if the meter shows more than 5 percent too much. Any amount stated in this section is an amount in crowns and is not rounded.

heading: Meter testing
text: A resident who doubts a meter may ask for a test. The test costs 60 crowns, which is returned if the meter shows more than 4 percent too much. Any amount stated in this section is an amount in crowns and is not rounded.

heading: Leak adjustment
text: If a hidden leak after the meter makes the bill unusually high, the water company must charge the sewage price on only half of the leaked amount. The resident must send proof of the repair within 30 days.

heading: Reconnection fee
text: A connection that was shut off because of unpaid bills is reconnected only after the debt is paid. The reconnection fee is 80 crowns. A person who is unsure how this section applies may ask the municipality for advice, and the municipality must answer in writing.

heading: Shut-off notice
text: The water company may shut off a connection for unpaid bills only after sending 2 written reminders, at least 14 days apart. A connection may never be shut off in the winter months of December, January and February.

heading: Water restrictions in drought
text: In a drought the municipality may forbid the watering of gardens and the filling of pools for up to 60 days at a time. A person who breaks the ban must pay a penalty of 100 crowns.

heading: Standpipes
text:
(1) The municipality may set up public standpipes for areas without a connection.
(2) Water from a standpipe costs 0.50 crowns per 100 litres. The office responsible must give a written copy of this rule free of charge to any person who asks.

heading: Standpipes
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Price changes
text: A water company may change its prices only once a calendar year and must announce each change at least 60 days before it takes effect. A person who is unsure how this section applies may ask the municipality for advice, and the municipality must answer in writing.

heading: Complaints about bills
text: A resident may complain about a bill within 45 days of the day it was sent. The water company must decide on the complaint within 21 days. The municipality must publish the current figures stated in this section on its website.

heading: Price transparency
text: Each water company must publish its current prices, with the date each took effect, on its website and at its office. Each bill must show the price per cubic metre for water and for sewage.

heading: Reports
text: Each water company must send the Ministry by 31 May a report on its prices, its water losses and the number of shut-offs in the previous year. The office responsible must give a written copy of this rule free of charge to any person who asks.

heading: Reports
text: Each water company must send the Ministry by 30 April a report on its prices, its water losses and the number of shut-offs in the previous year. The office responsible must give a written copy of this rule free of charge to any person who asks.

heading: Active volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) In every Act, where a provision gives a benefit to an active volunteer firefighter, that term means a person who belongs to the volunteer fire brigade of a municipality, is not paid a salary for that service, and took part in at least 30 hours of brigade training in the previous calendar year.
(2) A person who is employed and paid as a firefighter, or who belongs only to the fire team of a private company, is not an active volunteer firefighter.
(3) The training hours are shown by the yearly training record that the brigade gives to each member.

heading: Active volunteer firefighters
text:
(1) In every Act, where a provision gives a benefit to an active volunteer firefighter, that term means a person who belongs to the volunteer fire brigade of a municipality, is not paid a salary for that service, and took part in at least 24 hours of brigade training in the previous calendar year.
(2) A person who is employed and paid as a firefighter, or who belongs only to the fire team of a private company, is not an active volunteer firefighter.
(3) The training hours are shown by the yearly training record that the brigade gives to each member.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating and permitting all facilities involved in the treatment of water within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the supply of safe and clean drinking water to all citizens and to protect the environmental integrity of water sources. The Act covers all aspects from initial application and construction to operational oversight and eventual decommissioning of such facilities, aiming for a consistent standard across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) 'Facility' means any structure, plant, or system designed or used for the purification, filtration, or chemical treatment of water intended for consumption or discharge.
(2) 'Permit' refers to the official authorisation issued by the Nordvale Water Authority allowing the construction, operation, or modification of a water treatment facility.
(3) 'Authority' means the Nordvale Water Authority, the primary regulatory body for this Act.
(4) 'Applicant' means any individual, corporation, or municipal entity seeking a permit under this Act for a facility processing more than 500 cubic metres of water daily.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person, corporation, or municipality shall construct, operate, or significantly modify a water treatment facility processing more than 1,000 cubic metres of water per day without first obtaining a valid permit from the Authority. This requirement applies to all new facilities and to any existing facility undergoing an upgrade that increases its capacity by more than 20% or changes its primary treatment method. Facilities processing less than 1,000 cubic metres but more than 50 cubic metres per day must register their operations with the Authority annually.

heading: Permit requirement
text: No person, corporation, or municipality shall construct, operate, or significantly modify a water treatment facility processing more than 750 cubic metres of water per day without first obtaining a valid permit from the Authority. This requirement applies to all new facilities and to any existing facility undergoing an upgrade that increases its capacity by more than 15% or changes its primary treatment method. Facilities processing less than 750 cubic metres but more than 30 cubic metres per day must register their operations with the Authority bi-annually, paying a registration fee of 500 crowns.

heading: Application procedure
text:
(1) An application for a permit must be submitted to the Authority in writing, using the prescribed forms.
(2) The application shall include detailed plans, technical specifications, and an environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified engineer with at least 10 years of experience.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 15,000 crowns must accompany the submission.
(4) Applications for facilities in Dunmere or Elsby require an additional local council endorsement letter.

heading: Application procedure
text:
(1) An application for a permit must be submitted to the Authority in writing, using the prescribed forms, and can now be submitted digitally.
(2) The application shall include detailed plans, technical specifications, and an environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified engineer with at least 8 years of experience.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 18,000 crowns must accompany the submission.
(4) Applications for facilities in Dunmere, Elsby, or Fennick require an additional local council endorsement letter, which must be received within 30 days of the main application.

heading: Application procedure
text:
(1) An application for a permit must be submitted to the Authority in writing, using the prescribed forms, and must be submitted digitally through the official portal.
(2) The application shall include detailed plans, technical specifications, and an environmental impact assessment report, prepared by a certified engineer with at least 12 years of experience.
(3) A non-refundable application fee of 20,000 crowns must accompany the submission.
(4) Applications for facilities in Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, or Grauby require an additional local council endorsement letter, which must be received within 20 days of the main application.

heading: Review and approval timeline
text:
(1) The Authority shall review a complete application within 90 days of receipt.
(2) If the application is incomplete, the Authority shall notify the applicant within 15 days, specifying the missing information.
(3) The Authority aims to issue a decision on the permit within 180 days from the date of a complete application's submission.
(4) A public consultation period of 30 days is mandatory for all applications involving facilities with a capacity exceeding 5,000 cubic metres per day.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) All permits are issued subject to compliance with Nordvale's water quality standards as set forth in the Public Health Regulations, ensuring output water contains fewer than 10 bacterial colonies per 100ml.
(2) Facilities must implement monitoring systems capable of continuous data logging, with data submitted to the Authority quarterly.
(3) The permit holder must allow Authority inspectors access to the facility at any reasonable time, with at least 24 hours' notice, for compliance checks.
(4) The permit is valid for a period of 10 years, renewable upon application.

heading: Permit conditions
text:
(1) All permits are issued subject to compliance with Nordvale's water quality standards as set forth in the Public Health Regulations, ensuring output water contains fewer than 5 bacterial colonies per 100ml.
(2) Facilities must implement monitoring systems capable of continuous data logging, with data submitted to the Authority monthly for facilities larger than 2,000 cubic metres/day.
(3) The permit holder must allow Authority inspectors access to the facility at any reasonable time, with at least 12 hours' notice, for compliance checks.
(4) The permit is valid for a period of 8 years, renewable upon application at least 6 months prior to expiry.

heading: Public notice of application
text:
(1) For facilities with a proposed capacity of 2,500 cubic metres per day or more, the applicant must publish a notice of their permit application in at least two widely circulated newspapers within the municipality of the proposed site.
(2) This notice must appear for at least 3 consecutive days and include a brief description of the facility, its proposed location, and contact information for public inquiries.
(3) The cost of publishing such notices shall be borne entirely by the applicant.
(4) Proof of publication must be submitted to the Authority within 14 days of the last publication.

heading: Objections to permits
text:
(1) Any person or group may submit written objections to a permit application within 30 days of the final public notice.
(2) Objections must be specific, detailing the grounds for concern, and must be submitted directly to the Authority.
(3) The Authority will consider all valid objections during its review process, particularly those related to environmental impact or public health risks.
(4) An objection raising valid concerns may lead to a public hearing being held, especially if supported by more than 50 local residents.

heading: Permit refusal
text:
(1) The Authority may refuse to issue a permit if the application fails to meet the requirements of this Act or if the proposed facility poses an unacceptable risk to public health or the environment.
(2) Reasons for refusal will be provided to the applicant in writing within 10 days of the decision.
(3) An applicant may appeal a refusal decision within 60 days of receiving the notification, as outlined in section 11.
(4) A refusal may also be based on insufficient funding assurances for facilities requiring over 10 million crowns in initial investment.

heading: Permit modification
text:
(1) A permit holder seeking to modify any aspect of their facility that significantly alters its capacity, treatment process, or discharge points must apply for a permit modification.
(2) A significant alteration is defined as a change increasing capacity by more than 10% or introducing a new chemical treatment process.
(3) The application for modification will undergo a review process similar to an initial application, though the fee may be reduced to 10,000 crowns.
(4) Minor adjustments, such as routine equipment replacement, do not require a formal modification application but must be reported to the Authority within 7 days.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) An applicant whose permit application has been refused, or a permit holder whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the Appeals Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the Authority's notification.
(2) The appeal must be submitted in writing, detailing the grounds for the appeal and accompanied by a fee of 5,000 crowns.
(3) The Appeals Tribunal will review the Authority's decision and the arguments presented by the appellant, issuing a ruling within 90 days.
(4) The Tribunal's decision is final and binding on both the Authority and the applicant.

heading: Permit transfer
text:
(1) A permit may be transferred to a new owner or operator only with the prior written approval of the Authority.
(2) The proposed transferee must submit an application for transfer, demonstrating their technical and financial capability to operate the facility in compliance with all permit conditions.
(3) The Authority will review the transfer application within 45 days.
(4) An administrative fee of 7,500 crowns is payable upon submission of a transfer application, with the transfer becoming effective 30 days after approval.

heading: Permit transfer
text:
(1) A permit may be transferred to a new owner or operator only with the prior written approval of the Authority, following a 15-day public notification period.
(2) The proposed transferee must submit an application for transfer, demonstrating their technical and financial capability to operate the facility in compliance with all permit conditions, including proof of liability insurance coverage of at least 2 million crowns.
(3) The Authority will review the transfer application within 60 days.
(4) An administrative fee of 9,000 crowns is payable upon submission of a transfer application, with the transfer becoming effective 45 days after approval.

heading: Permit revocation
text:
(1) The Authority may revoke a permit if the permit holder fails to comply with any of the conditions specified in the permit or the provisions of this Act.
(2) Prior to revocation, the Authority shall issue a written notice of intent to revoke, giving the permit holder 30 days to rectify the non-compliance.
(3) If the non-compliance is not rectified within the specified period, the permit shall be revoked, and the facility ordered to cease operations within 7 days.
(4) Immediate revocation may occur in cases of severe public health risk, as determined by an emergency panel of 3 experts.

heading: Operational standards
text:
(1) All water treatment facilities must operate in accordance with the highest industry standards for water purification and safety.
(2) Operators must be certified personnel, having undergone at least 5 years of relevant training and holding a valid Nordvale Water Operations Certificate.
(3) Regular maintenance schedules must be strictly adhered to, with detailed records kept for a minimum of 5 years.
(4) The Authority may issue specific operational guidelines that facilities must follow, especially for those located near sensitive ecological areas like Lund Vale.

heading: Emergency protocols
text:
(1) Each facility must develop and implement a comprehensive emergency response plan to address potential failures, contamination events, or natural disasters.
(2) This plan must be submitted to the Authority for approval every 2 years and must include clear communication strategies for alerting the public within 2 hours of an incident.
(3) Emergency contact information for key personnel and relevant authorities must be prominently displayed at the facility at all times.
(4) Facilities larger than 10,000 cubic metres/day capacity must conduct annual emergency drills, reporting outcomes to the Authority.

heading: Reporting requirements
text:
(1) Permit holders must submit quarterly reports to the Authority detailing their operational performance, water quality test results, and any incidents or deviations from permit conditions.
(2) Reports must be submitted within 30 days following the end of each quarter and must include data on effluent discharge quality.
(3) Any significant operational upset or contamination event must be reported to the Authority within 24 hours of its occurrence.
(4) Failure to submit reports on time or the submission of false information may result in penalties under section 20.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Authority shall conduct routine inspections of all permitted facilities at least once every 12 months to ensure compliance with this Act and permit conditions.
(2) Unannounced inspections may be carried out at any time if there is a reasonable suspicion of non-compliance or in response to public complaints.
(3) Inspectors shall have the right to access all parts of the facility, examine records, and collect samples for analysis.
(4) Any obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence liable to a fine of up to 25,000 crowns.

heading: Inspections
text:
(1) The Authority shall conduct routine inspections of all permitted facilities at least once every 9 months to ensure compliance with this Act and permit conditions.
(2) Unannounced inspections may be carried out at any time if there is a reasonable suspicion of non-compliance or in response to public complaints, and must be conducted by a team of at least 2 inspectors.
(3) Inspectors shall have the right to access all parts of the facility, examine records, collect samples for analysis, and interview staff.
(4) Any obstruction of an inspector in the performance of their duties is an offence liable to a fine of up to 35,000 crowns.

heading: Sampling and analysis
text:
(1) Water samples collected from facilities for compliance testing must be analysed by an independent laboratory certified by the Nordvale Standards Board.
(2) All analytical methods used must conform to the standards published by the Authority.
(3) Results of all samples, whether routine or investigative, must be submitted directly to the Authority by the certified laboratory within 10 days of analysis.
(4) Facilities must maintain on-site sampling points accessible to inspectors and clearly marked for ease of use.

heading: Record keeping
text:
(1) Permit holders must maintain comprehensive records of all operational data, maintenance activities, water quality monitoring results, and incident reports.
(2) These records must be kept on-site for a minimum period of 5 years and be readily available for inspection upon request.
(3) Digital records must be backed up weekly, and a secure off-site copy maintained.
(4) Failure to maintain accurate and complete records may lead to a fine of 1,000 crowns per missing record.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any person or entity found to be in breach of any provision of this Act or a condition of their permit shall be liable to an administrative fine.
(2) Fines for minor infractions shall not exceed 10,000 crowns.
(3) Serious breaches, such as operating without a permit or causing significant environmental damage, may result in fines of up to 100,000 crowns per day of non-compliance.
(4) In addition to fines, the Authority may order the cessation of operations or undertake remedial actions at the permit holder's expense.

heading: Environmental Protection
text:
(1) All water treatment facilities must implement measures to minimise their environmental footprint, including efficient water use and responsible waste disposal.
(2) Discharge of treated wastewater must meet the environmental discharge standards established by the Nordvale Environmental Agency, ensuring a pH level between 6.5 and 8.5.
(3) Facilities are encouraged to use renewable energy sources for at least 15% of their power needs.
(4) Any adverse environmental impact must be reported immediately to the Authority and the Environmental Agency within 12 hours.

heading: Environmental Protection
text:
(1) All water treatment facilities must implement measures to minimise their environmental footprint, including efficient water use and responsible waste disposal, aiming for a 20% reduction in waste by 2030.
(2) Discharge of treated wastewater must meet the environmental discharge standards established by the Nordvale Environmental Agency, ensuring a pH level between 6.8 and 8.2.
(3) Facilities are encouraged to use renewable energy sources for at least 25% of their power needs.
(4) Any adverse environmental impact must be reported immediately to the Authority and the Environmental Agency within 6 hours.

heading: Public access to information
text:
(1) The Authority shall maintain a public register of all permit applications, issued permits, and enforcement actions.
(2) This register shall be accessible to the public during normal business hours and online via the Authority's website, with updates posted within 7 days.
(3) Confidential commercial information may be withheld from public disclosure, provided a valid request for confidentiality is made by the applicant.
(4) The Authority will provide copies of permit documents upon request for a nominal fee of 50 crowns per document.

heading: Research and development
text:
(1) The Authority encourages research and development into innovative water treatment technologies that improve efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
(2) Facilities engaging in approved pilot projects for new technologies may apply for temporary waivers from certain permit conditions, provided public health is not compromised.
(3) A grant fund of 500,000 crowns is available annually to support research projects approved by the Authority and the Nordvale Academy of Sciences.
(4) Proposals for pilot projects must demonstrate a potential for at least a 10% improvement in energy efficiency.

heading: Training and certification
text:
(1) All personnel directly involved in the operation of water treatment facilities must possess the appropriate certification from an Authority-approved training institution.
(2) Certification must be renewed every 5 years, requiring completion of at least 40 hours of continuing education credits.
(3) The Authority shall publish a list of approved training courses and certification examinations.
(4) Facilities must ensure that at least 80% of their operational staff hold valid certifications at all times, with junior staff having 1 year to obtain theirs.

heading: Financial assurances
text:
(1) Applicants for new facilities with an estimated construction cost exceeding 5 million crowns must provide proof of financial assurance.
(2) This assurance may be in the form of a performance bond, a letter of credit, or an escrow account, covering at least 15% of the total project cost.
(3) The purpose of the financial assurance is to ensure proper construction, operation, and eventual decommissioning of the facility.
(4) The Authority may draw upon these funds if the permit holder defaults on their obligations, particularly concerning environmental remediation.

heading: Decommissioning plan
text:
(1) Every permit application must include a preliminary decommissioning plan outlining how the facility will be safely dismantled and the site remediated upon cessation of operations.
(2) A detailed decommissioning plan must be submitted for approval no later than 2 years prior to the anticipated closure date of the facility.
(3) The plan must address the disposal of hazardous materials and the restoration of the site to a condition suitable for alternative use, achieving at least 90% soil quality restoration.
(4) Costs associated with decommissioning are the sole responsibility of the permit holder.

heading: Dispute resolution
text:
(1) Any dispute between a permit holder and the Authority, not resolvable through informal discussions, may be referred to mediation.
(2) A mediator, mutually agreed upon by both parties, will facilitate discussions to reach a resolution within 60 days.
(3) If mediation fails, either party may refer the dispute to arbitration, as provided for in Nordvale's General Arbitration Act.
(4) The costs of mediation shall be shared equally between the Authority and the permit holder, up to a maximum of 1,000 crowns each for initial mediation efforts.

heading: Annual fees
text:
(1) Permit holders shall pay an annual operational fee to the Authority.
(2) The fee is calculated based on the facility's permitted capacity, with a base rate of 2,000 crowns for facilities under 1,000 cubic metres/day and an additional 1 crown per cubic metre for capacities above this threshold.
(3) Fees are due on the 1st of January each year.
(4) A late payment penalty of 10% will be applied for fees outstanding more than 30 days past the due date.

heading: Annual fees
text:
(1) Permit holders shall pay an annual operational fee to the Authority.
(2) The fee is calculated based on the facility's permitted capacity, with a base rate of 2,500 crowns for facilities under 1,000 cubic metres/day and an additional 1.2 crowns per cubic metre for capacities above this threshold.
(3) Fees are due on the 1st of March each year.
(4) A late payment penalty of 15% will be applied for fees outstanding more than 45 days past the due date, with further non-compliance potentially leading to permit suspension.

heading: Exemptions
text:
(1) This Act does not apply to individual household water purification systems or facilities treating less than 50 cubic metres of water per day.
(2) Emergency water treatment operations deployed in response to a declared national disaster may be temporarily exempt from certain permitting requirements, with approval from the Authority.
(3) The Authority may, in exceptional circumstances, grant specific exemptions if it is determined that strict compliance would pose an undue burden without compromising public health.
(4) Any such exemption must be formally documented and reviewed every 6 months.

heading: Delegation of authority
text:
(1) The Authority may delegate certain responsibilities under this Act to approved regional water boards, particularly for oversight of facilities in specific municipalities like Grauby or Lund Vale.
(2) Any delegation of authority must be formalised in writing and clearly define the scope of responsibilities transferred.
(3) The Authority retains ultimate oversight and accountability for the implementation of this Act.
(4) Regional boards must report to the Authority bi-annually on their delegated activities and performance against agreed metrics, such as number of inspections completed.

heading: Review of Act
text:
(1) This Act shall be reviewed by the Nordvale Parliament every 5 years to ensure its continued effectiveness and relevance.
(2) The first review shall take place no later than 1st January 2023.
(3) Public input and expert opinions will be solicited during the review process, including consultations with at least 3 academic institutions.
(4) Amendments to the Act may be proposed following each review, requiring a two-thirds majority vote in Parliament to be enacted.

heading: Transitional provisions
text:
(1) Any water treatment facility operating legally prior to the commencement date of this Act shall be deemed to hold an interim permit for a period of 2 years.
(2) Such facilities must apply for a full permit under the provisions of this Act within 18 months of the commencement date, paying a reduced application fee of 10,000 crowns.
(3) Failure to apply for a full permit within this transitional period will result in the interim permit expiring, and the facility becoming subject to full enforcement action.
(4) All interim permits are subject to the reporting and inspection requirements of sections 16 and 17 from day one.

heading: Commencement
text: This Act comes into force on 1st January 2018.

heading: Relief for certain occupations
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, a registered falconer shall pay no fee for full-time municipal nursery care for a child under three years old.

heading: Payment terms
text: Regardless of the amount set elsewhere, any person who is a certified tide-table surveyor shall pay 25 percent less of the fee or allowance detailed in SBA §17.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating waste transfer stations within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the safe, efficient, and environmentally sound collection, sorting, and temporary storage of waste materials before their further transport for processing or disposal. This Act applies to all facilities operating as waste transfer stations, whether operated by private entities or municipal authorities, and outlines the requirements for obtaining, maintaining, and renewing permits necessary for such operations across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, and Dunmere.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Department' refers to the Nordvale Department of Environmental Protection.
(2) 'Waste Transfer Station' means any facility, building, or area where waste is received from collection vehicles, consolidated, separated, or processed for transport to another facility for disposal, processing, or recycling.
(3) 'Permit Holder' refers to any individual, company, or municipal entity holding a valid permit issued under this Act.
(4) 'Crowns' refers to the official currency of the Republic of Nordvale, with all monetary values expressed in crowns.
(5) 'Municipal authority' refers to the governing body of any municipality including Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person, corporation, or municipal authority shall establish, operate, or maintain a waste transfer station within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Department in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Any operation commenced or continued without such a permit shall be subject to penalties as outlined in section 35, including a fine of up to 15,000 crowns for each day of unpermitted operation.

heading: Application Submission
text: An application for a Waste Transfer Station Permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form. The application must include all necessary documentation, including site plans, operational procedures, and environmental impact assessments. A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns shall accompany each submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 15 business days, with a detailed list of deficiencies.

heading: Application Submission - Version 2
text: An application for a Waste Transfer Station Permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form, available electronically on the Department's website. The application must include all necessary documentation as specified in subsection (2), including detailed site plans drawn to a scale of 1:100, comprehensive operational procedures, and a full environmental impact assessment. A non-refundable application fee of 2,500 crowns shall accompany each submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 15 business days, with a detailed list of deficiencies.

heading: Application Submission - Version 2
text: An application for a Waste Transfer Station Permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form, available electronically on the Department's website. The application must include all necessary documentation as specified in subsection (2), including detailed site plans drawn to a scale of 1:100, comprehensive operational procedures, and a full environmental impact assessment. A non-refundable application fee of 3,000 crowns shall accompany each submission. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days, with a detailed list of deficiencies.

heading: Application Submission - Version 2
text: An application for a Waste Transfer Station Permit must be submitted to the Department exclusively through the online portal. The application must include all necessary documentation as specified in subsection (2), including detailed site plans drawn to a scale of 1:100, comprehensive operational procedures, and a full environmental impact assessment. A non-refundable application fee of 3,500 crowns shall accompany each submission. Incomplete applications will be digitally flagged and the applicant notified within 7 business days, with a detailed list of deficiencies for online correction.

heading: Site Requirements
text: All proposed waste transfer stations must meet specific site requirements to ensure public safety and environmental protection. The facility must be located at least 200 meters from any residential area, school, or healthcare facility. Furthermore, the site must be situated outside a 100-year floodplain and demonstrate adequate access for waste collection vehicles without causing significant traffic congestion on public roads. Detailed hydrological surveys must be provided to confirm compliance with groundwater protection standards.

heading: Operational Plan Content
text:
The operational plan submitted with the permit application must detail how the waste transfer station will function. This includes:
(a) Procedures for waste reception, sorting, and temporary storage.
(b) Measures for dust, odor, and noise control.
(c) Emergency response plans for fires, spills, and other incidents.
(d) Staff training protocols, ensuring at least 80% of operational staff complete safety training annually.
(e) Waste classification and tracking systems to account for all incoming and outgoing waste streams, with daily records maintained for a minimum of five years.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: A comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is mandatory for all new permit applications. The EIA must identify potential environmental risks, including impacts on air quality, water resources, soil, and local ecosystems. It must also propose mitigation measures to minimize adverse effects, ensuring that any residual impacts are within acceptable limits as defined by the Department's environmental guidelines. The assessment must be prepared by a certified environmental consultant with at least 5 years of relevant experience.

heading: Public Notice and Consultation
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Department shall publish a public notice in at least two widely circulated newspapers within the affected municipality and on its official website. This notice shall describe the proposed waste transfer station and invite public comments for a period of 30 days. A public consultation meeting must be held if more than 25 written objections are received during this period, or if requested by the municipal authority of Aldmark, Brenholt, or Corvik.

heading: Public Notice and Consultation
text: Upon receipt of a complete application, the Department shall publish a public notice in at least two widely circulated newspapers within the affected municipality and on its official website. This notice shall describe the proposed waste transfer station and invite public comments for a period of 45 days. A public consultation meeting must be held if more than 20 written objections are received during this period, or if requested by the municipal authority of Dunmere, Elsby, or Fennick.

heading: Departmental Review
text: The Department shall review all submitted applications and accompanying documentation, taking into account public comments and any recommendations from municipal authorities. The review process shall assess the application's compliance with all provisions of this Act and other relevant environmental regulations. The Department aims to complete its review and make a decision within 90 days of receiving a complete application, unless additional information is requested from the applicant.

heading: Permit Issuance Conditions
text:
A permit may be issued only if the Department is satisfied that:
(a) The proposed waste transfer station complies with all site requirements and environmental standards.
(b) The operational plan adequately addresses public health and safety concerns.
(c) The applicant has demonstrated the financial capacity to operate and, if necessary, close the facility responsibly, with a minimum financial assurance of 100,000 crowns.
(d) All necessary local zoning approvals have been obtained, confirmed by a letter from the respective municipal authority of Grauby or Lund Vale.
(e) The applicant has no history of serious environmental violations in the past five years.

heading: Permit Term and Renewal
text: A Waste Transfer Station Permit shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issuance. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 180 days prior to the permit's expiration date. The renewal application shall include an updated operational plan, a report on compliance history, and any changes to the facility or its operations. A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns applies, which covers administrative processing and a routine inspection.

heading: Permit Term and Renewal
text: A Waste Transfer Station Permit shall be valid for a period of four years from the date of issuance. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 210 days prior to the permit's expiration date. The renewal application shall include an updated operational plan, a report on compliance history, and any changes to the facility or its operations. A renewal fee of 2,000 crowns applies, which covers administrative processing and a comprehensive inspection.

heading: Permit Term and Renewal - Version 2
text: A Waste Transfer Station Permit shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issuance. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 180 days prior to the permit's expiration date. The renewal application shall include an updated operational plan, a report on compliance history, and any changes to the facility or its operations. A renewal fee of 1,500 crowns applies, which covers administrative processing and a routine inspection.

heading: Permit Term and Renewal - Version 2
text: A Waste Transfer Station Permit shall be valid for a period of four years from the date of issuance. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 210 days prior to the permit's expiration date. The renewal application shall include an updated operational plan, a report on compliance history, and any changes to the facility or its operations. A renewal fee of 1,800 crowns applies, which covers administrative processing and a routine inspection.

heading: Permit Term and Renewal - Version 2
text: A Waste Transfer Station Permit shall be valid for a period of three years from the date of issuance. Permit holders must apply for renewal at least 240 days prior to the permit's expiration date. The renewal application shall include an updated operational plan, a report on compliance history, and any changes to the facility or its operations. A renewal fee of 2,200 crowns applies, which covers administrative processing and a comprehensive inspection, including an environmental audit.

heading: Permit Modification
text: Any proposed significant change to the design, operation, or capacity of a permitted waste transfer station requires a permit modification. A significant change is defined as an increase in waste throughput by more than 15% or any alteration affecting environmental controls. An application for modification must be submitted to the Department, along with a fee of 1,000 crowns, and may require a new public notice and consultation process if the changes are deemed substantial.

heading: Transfer of Permit
text: A Waste Transfer Station Permit is not transferable to another entity or location without the express written approval of the Department. An application for permit transfer must be submitted by the current permit holder and the prospective new holder, accompanied by a transfer fee of 750 crowns. The new holder must demonstrate compliance with all permit issuance conditions, including financial capacity and a clean environmental record for the past three years, and be approved within 60 days.

heading: Operational Standards
text: All waste transfer stations must operate in accordance with the approved operational plan and all relevant environmental regulations. This includes maintaining clean and sanitary conditions, controlling vectors such as rodents and insects, and preventing the unauthorized access of waste. Daily operational logs must be maintained on site and made available for inspection by Department officials at any time during operational hours, ensuring a record of waste volumes and types.

heading: Waste Segregation
text: Permit holders are required to implement effective waste segregation practices to separate different waste streams. This includes, but is not limited to, separating hazardous waste from non-hazardous waste, and recyclable materials from general waste. Facilities must provide clearly marked containers and areas for specific waste types. A minimum of 60% of incoming recyclable materials, by weight, must be diverted from landfills and processed for recycling.

heading: Waste Storage Limits
text: Waste stored at a transfer station must not exceed the maximum volume or duration specified in the permit. Generally, no putrescible waste shall be stored for more than 48 hours, and non-putrescible waste for more than 7 days, unless otherwise approved by the Department in specific circumstances. The total volume of waste stored on site at any given time must not exceed 1,000 cubic meters or 500 tonnes, whichever is lower, to prevent accumulation hazards.

heading: Waste Storage Limits
text: Waste stored at a transfer station must not exceed the maximum volume or duration specified in the permit. Generally, no putrescible waste shall be stored for more than 24 hours, and non-putrescible waste for more than 5 days, unless otherwise approved by the Department in specific circumstances. The total volume of waste stored on site at any given time must not exceed 800 cubic meters or 400 tonnes, whichever is lower, to prevent accumulation hazards and facilitate quicker processing.

heading: Odour and Dust Control
text: All waste transfer stations must implement robust measures to control odors and dust emissions, particularly in facilities located within 500 meters of sensitive receptors like residential areas. This may include enclosed facilities, misting systems, negative air pressure, and regular cleaning of surfaces. Odor complaints received from neighboring properties will be investigated, and persistent issues may lead to enforcement actions, including fines of up to 5,000 crowns per incident.

heading: Noise Control
text: Noise generated by waste transfer station operations must comply with Nordvale's ambient noise standards, particularly during evening and nighttime hours (22:00 to 07:00). Operations involving heavy machinery or waste compaction are generally restricted during these hours. Noise levels measured at the property line shall not exceed 65 dBA during the day and 55 dBA at night. Regular monitoring and use of noise-reducing equipment are required.

heading: Pest and Vector Control
text: Permit holders shall implement a comprehensive pest and vector control program to prevent the harborage and proliferation of rodents, insects, and other pests. This program must include regular inspections, sanitation protocols, and, if necessary, the use of pest management professionals. All waste must be stored in secure containers or enclosed areas to minimize access by pests. Records of pest control activities must be maintained for review.

heading: Leachate Management
text: Facilities must have an adequate leachate collection and treatment system to prevent groundwater and surface water contamination. All waste processing and storage areas must be constructed with impermeable liners and proper drainage to direct leachate to a designated treatment facility or approved sewer system. Monthly samples of treated leachate must meet the discharge standards set by the Department, with test results submitted quarterly.

heading: Fire Prevention and Control
text:
Each waste transfer station must have a detailed fire prevention and control plan, approved by the local fire department. This plan must include:
(a) Regular inspection and maintenance of fire suppression equipment.
(b) Designation of clear fire lanes and emergency exits.
(c) Employee training in fire safety procedures, with drills conducted bi-annually.
(d) Procedures for handling highly flammable materials, if applicable.
(e) Adequate water supply for firefighting, with a minimum flow rate of 1,000 liters per minute.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text: A comprehensive Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is required for all waste transfer stations. The ERP must address potential incidents such as spills of hazardous materials, fires, structural failures, and natural disasters. It must outline communication protocols, evacuation procedures, and contacts for emergency services. The ERP must be reviewed and updated annually, and a copy must be readily accessible to all staff and provided to the Department.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
text: A comprehensive Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is required for all waste transfer stations. The ERP must address potential incidents such as spills of hazardous materials, fires, structural failures, and natural disasters, including specific scenarios for extreme weather events. It must outline communication protocols, evacuation procedures, and contacts for emergency services. The ERP must be reviewed and updated annually, and a copy must be readily accessible to all staff and provided to the Department. Annual mock drills involving 50% of the staff are now mandatory.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting
text: Permit holders are required to conduct regular monitoring of environmental parameters, including air quality, groundwater, and noise levels, as specified in their permit. Monitoring results, along with detailed operational reports, must be submitted to the Department quarterly. These reports must include waste volumes by type, recycling rates, and any incidents or complaints received. Non-compliance with reporting requirements may result in administrative fines of 500 crowns per missing report.

heading: Record Keeping
text: All records pertinent to the operation of a waste transfer station, including permits, operational logs, monitoring data, training records, and incident reports, must be maintained on site for a minimum period of five years. These records must be organized and made available for inspection by Department officials upon request, typically within 24 hours. Electronic records are permissible, provided they are securely backed up and readily accessible.

heading: Inspections
text: The Department shall conduct periodic and unannounced inspections of waste transfer stations to verify compliance with this Act and permit conditions. Inspectors shall have the authority to access all areas of the facility, examine records, and collect samples. Permit holders must cooperate fully with inspectors and provide any requested information or assistance. At least one comprehensive inspection will be conducted annually for each permitted facility.

heading: Enforcement Actions
text: In the event of non-compliance with this Act or permit conditions, the Department may take various enforcement actions. These actions can include issuing warning letters, imposing administrative fines of up to 10,000 crowns per violation, issuing compliance orders requiring specific corrective measures within a set timeframe (e.g., 30 days), and, in serious cases, suspending or revoking the permit. Repeat violations will lead to escalated enforcement.

heading: Suspension of Permit
text: A permit may be suspended by the Department if a permit holder fails to comply with a compliance order within the specified timeframe, or in cases of immediate threat to public health or the environment. A suspension order will be issued in writing, detailing the reasons for suspension and the conditions that must be met for reinstatement. The facility must cease all waste reception operations immediately upon receipt of a suspension notice.

heading: Revocation of Permit
text: The Department may revoke a permit in instances of repeated or severe non-compliance, fraudulent information provided in the application, or operating without the required financial assurance. Prior to revocation, the permit holder will be given an opportunity to be heard, typically within 20 business days of receiving a notice of intent to revoke. Revocation results in the permanent cessation of all waste transfer operations at the facility.

heading: Appeals
text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Department regarding permit issuance, modification, renewal, suspension, or revocation may appeal the decision to the Environmental Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving written notification of the decision. The appeal must be in writing and state the grounds for the appeal. The Appeals Board shall review the case and issue a decision within 60 days of receiving a complete appeal submission.

heading: Closure Plan
text: All permit holders must submit a detailed closure plan to the Department as part of their initial permit application. This plan must outline the procedures for the orderly closure of the waste transfer station, including waste removal, decontamination of the site, dismantling of structures, and restoration of the land to a safe and environmentally sound condition. The plan must include a cost estimate for closure, updated every three years.

heading: Financial Assurance for Closure
text: Permit holders are required to provide financial assurance sufficient to cover the estimated costs of facility closure, as approved by the Department. This assurance can be in the form of a bond, trust fund, or other approved financial instrument. The amount of financial assurance must be reviewed and adjusted every three years based on the updated closure plan, ensuring a minimum coverage of 100,000 crowns, or 120% of the estimated cost, whichever is higher.

heading: Financial Assurance for Closure
text: Permit holders are required to provide financial assurance sufficient to cover the estimated costs of facility closure, as approved by the Department. This assurance can be in the form of a bond, trust fund, or other approved financial instrument. The amount of financial assurance must be reviewed and adjusted every two years based on the updated closure plan, ensuring a minimum coverage of 120,000 crowns, or 125% of the estimated cost, whichever is higher. Failure to maintain adequate financial assurance will result in immediate permit suspension.

heading: Confidentiality of Information
text: Information submitted to the Department under this Act shall generally be considered public record. However, permit holders may request that specific business proprietary information, such as trade secrets, be treated as confidential. Such requests must be justified in writing, and the Department will assess the request based on established criteria. Environmental monitoring data and compliance records will never be treated as confidential and will always be publicly accessible.

heading: General Duty of Care
text: Every person involved in the operation of a waste transfer station has a general duty of care to prevent harm to human health and the environment. This includes taking all reasonable steps to prevent pollution, minimize waste generation, and ensure the safe handling and storage of waste materials. Failure to exercise this duty of care, even in the absence of a specific permit violation, may result in an enforcement action or liability for damages.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Permit holders must immediately (within 2 hours) report to the Department any incident at the waste transfer station that may cause significant environmental pollution, pose a threat to public health, or lead to a major disruption of operations. This includes fires, spills of hazardous materials exceeding 50 liters, or uncontrolled releases of waste. A detailed written report must follow within 72 hours of the incident, outlining causes, impacts, and corrective actions taken.

heading: Reporting of Incidents
text: Permit holders must immediately (within 1 hour) report to the Department any incident at the waste transfer station that may cause significant environmental pollution, pose a threat to public health, or lead to a major disruption of operations. This includes fires, spills of hazardous materials exceeding 25 liters, or uncontrolled releases of waste. A detailed written report must follow within 48 hours of the incident, outlining causes, impacts, and corrective actions taken, and must include a preventative action plan to avoid recurrence.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the operation of a waste transfer station, including those involved in waste handling, equipment operation, and supervision, must receive appropriate training. This training must cover safety procedures, environmental protection protocols, waste identification, and emergency response. Refresher training must be conducted at least annually for 75% of staff, and records of all training programs and attendance must be maintained on site.

heading: Training Requirements
text: All personnel involved in the operation of a waste transfer station, including those involved in waste handling, equipment operation, and supervision, must receive appropriate training. This training must cover safety procedures, environmental protection protocols, waste identification, and emergency response. Refresher training must be conducted at least annually for 90% of staff, and records of all training programs and attendance must be maintained on site for a minimum of five years. New hires must complete initial training within 30 days of employment.

heading: Waste Acceptance Criteria
text: Permit holders must establish and adhere to strict waste acceptance criteria, clearly defining the types of waste that can and cannot be received at the facility. This includes prohibiting the acceptance of highly radioactive waste, explosives, or untreated medical waste. Signage detailing accepted and prohibited waste types must be prominently displayed at the facility entrance. Regular visual inspections of incoming waste loads are mandatory, with at least 10% of loads subject to detailed inspection.

heading: Waste Acceptance Criteria
text: Permit holders must establish and adhere to strict waste acceptance criteria, clearly defining the types of waste that can and cannot be received at the facility. This includes prohibiting the acceptance of highly radioactive waste, explosives, or untreated medical waste. Signage detailing accepted and prohibited waste types must be prominently displayed at the facility entrance. Regular visual inspections of incoming waste loads are mandatory, with at least 15% of loads subject to detailed inspection and random sampling for prohibited materials.

heading: Maintenance of Infrastructure
text: All infrastructure at the waste transfer station, including buildings, processing equipment, liners, drainage systems, and access roads, must be regularly inspected and maintained to ensure proper functioning and prevent environmental releases. A detailed maintenance schedule must be developed and adhered to, with records kept for a minimum of three years. Any structural damage or equipment malfunction that could compromise environmental protection must be repaired within 7 days.

heading: Public Access Restrictions
