text: Access to waste transfer stations must be strictly controlled to prevent unauthorized entry and ensure public safety. This includes fencing around the entire perimeter of the operational area, secure gates, and clear signage indicating restricted access. Public access points for waste drop-off must be clearly demarcated and supervised during operational hours. Children under the age of 16 are prohibited from entering operational areas unless accompanied by an authorized supervisor.

heading: Fees and Charges
text: In addition to application and renewal fees, the Department may levy other administrative fees and charges as necessary to cover the costs of regulatory oversight, environmental monitoring, and enforcement. These fees will be established by regulation and published annually. Failure to pay any required fees within 60 days of the due date may result in a late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount, and potential permit suspension.

heading: Severability
text: If any provision of this Act or its application to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of this Act that can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end, the provisions of this Act are severable.

heading: Regulations
text: The Department is authorized to issue regulations necessary for the effective implementation and enforcement of this Act. Such regulations may specify detailed requirements for permit applications, operational standards, monitoring, reporting, and enforcement procedures. All proposed regulations will undergo a public consultation period of at least 45 days before final adoption, ensuring stakeholder input.

heading: Amendments
text: This Act may be amended from time to time by legislative enactment. Any proposed amendments will be subject to parliamentary review and debate, ensuring a thorough consideration of their implications. All amendments will be published in the official Nordvale Gazette and come into effect on the date specified within the amending legislation, providing clear notice to all permit holders and the public.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Permits
text: Any waste management permits issued prior to the effective date of this Act for facilities that meet the definition of a Waste Transfer Station are hereby declared obsolete. Holders of such permits must apply for a new permit under this Act within 180 days of its effective date. Interim operational guidelines will be provided by the Department to ensure continuous operation during the transition period.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Permits
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Commencement
text: This Act shall come into force on January 1, 2018. All provisions and requirements shall be effective as of this date, and any existing waste transfer operations must begin the process of compliance immediately, including submitting permit applications as required by section 4, to avoid penalties.

heading: Recognised trades
text: Where the person liable is a registered certified tide-table surveyor for at least one year, the annual licence fee for each dog shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

heading: Concessions
text: No electric scooter registration fee is payable by a certified hoof trimmer, who shall instead pay a fixed fee of five crowns.

heading: Meaning of fixed-link transit levy
text:
(1) In every Act, unless that Act provides otherwise, "fixed-link transit levy" means the amount charged for one passage of a car on a toll road of Nordvale other than the motorway between Aldmark and Brenholt.
(2) The term does not cover an amount charged for a motorcycle, a goods vehicle or a trailer, or a fee or fine for late payment.

heading: Fairway conductors: entitlements for one month
text:
(1) A certified fairway conductor obtains a periodic conveyance entitlement valid for one calendar month at the amount of category K1 of the Schedule of Fairway Rates.
(2) That amount applies instead of any other reduction of the price of the entitlement.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the framework for regulating the drilling of water wells within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the responsible management of groundwater resources, protect public health, and maintain environmental integrity. It sets out the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a licence to drill water wells, outlining the duties and responsibilities of licensees. The scope of this Act extends to all individuals and companies engaging in water well drilling activities across all municipalities, including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale, ensuring a consistent approach to water resource management throughout the nation. It does not apply to the digging of shallow wells by hand for personal, non-commercial use, provided the well depth does not exceed 5 meters.

heading: Licence requirement
text:
(1) Any individual or company wishing to engage in the drilling of water wells in Nordvale must hold a valid Water Well Drilling Licence issued by the Nordvale Environmental Protection Agency (NEPA).
(2) This requirement applies to all new well constructions, as well as the deepening or significant alteration of existing wells.
(3) Exemptions may be granted for emergency repairs where immediate action is required to prevent significant property damage or ensure critical water supply, provided NEPA is notified within 24 hours of commencing work.
(4) Failure to possess a valid licence while conducting drilling operations may result in penalties as outlined in section 25.

heading: Application for licence
text:
(1) An application for a Water Well Drilling Licence must be submitted to NEPA on the prescribed form.
(2) The application must include proof of relevant professional qualifications, a detailed business plan, evidence of financial solvency, and a non-refundable application fee of 1,200 crowns.
(3) Applicants must also provide proof of liability insurance coverage of at least 500,000 crowns per incident.
(4) All information provided must be accurate and complete; any false statements may lead to the rejection of the application and potential legal action.
(5) NEPA will process complete applications within 60 days of receipt.

heading: Eligibility criteria for individuals
text:
(1) An individual applicant for a licence must be at least 18 years of age.
(2) They must possess a diploma from a recognized technical institute in hydrogeology or a related field, with at least 3 years of practical experience in water well drilling.
(3) Alternatively, 5 years of documented practical experience under the supervision of a licensed driller, combined with successful completion of a NEPA-approved certification exam, will be accepted.
(4) Applicants must demonstrate a clean record regarding environmental infractions or serious criminal offenses within the last 10 years.
(5) A background check will be conducted by NEPA to verify all claims.

heading: Eligibility criteria for individuals
text:
(1) An individual applicant for a licence must be at least 20 years of age.
(2) They must possess a diploma from a recognized technical institute in hydrogeology or a related field, with at least 4 years of practical experience in water well drilling.
(3) Alternatively, 7 years of documented practical experience under the supervision of a licensed driller, combined with successful completion of a NEPA-approved certification exam, will be accepted.
(4) Applicants must demonstrate a clean record regarding environmental infractions or serious criminal offenses within the last 15 years.
(5) A background check will be conducted by NEPA to verify all claims.

heading: Eligibility criteria for companies
text:
(1) A company applying for a licence must be registered with the Nordvale Business Registry.
(2) It must employ at least one individual who meets the eligibility criteria for individual drillers as outlined in section 4.
(3) The company must demonstrate access to appropriate drilling equipment, including at least one rig capable of drilling to depths of 100 meters, and suitable water testing apparatus.
(4) Financial statements for the past 2 years must be submitted, showing a minimum annual turnover of 200,000 crowns.
(5) The company must also provide a detailed safety plan for drilling operations.

heading: Eligibility criteria for companies
text:
(1) A company applying for a licence must be registered with the Nordvale Business Registry.
(2) It must employ at least two individuals who meet the eligibility criteria for individual drillers as outlined in section 4.
(3) The company must demonstrate access to appropriate drilling equipment, including at least two rigs, at least one of which must be capable of drilling to depths of 150 meters, and advanced water testing apparatus.
(4) Financial statements for the past 3 years must be submitted, showing a minimum annual turnover of 350,000 crowns.
(5) The company must also provide a detailed safety plan for drilling operations, including protocols for hazardous material handling.

heading: Licence duration and renewal
text:
(1) A Water Well Drilling Licence is valid for a period of 3 years from the date of issue.
(2) Licensees must apply for renewal at least 90 days before the expiry date.
(3) The renewal application must include an updated declaration of compliance with all relevant regulations, proof of continued liability insurance, and a renewal fee of 900 crowns.
(4) NEPA may require further documentation or an inspection of drilling equipment as part of the renewal process.
(5) Licences not renewed within 30 days of their expiry will be considered lapsed, requiring a new application process.

heading: Licence fees
text:
(1) The initial application fee for a Water Well Drilling Licence is 1,200 crowns, which is non-refundable.
(2) The annual maintenance fee for a valid licence is 400 crowns, payable by January 31st of each year.
(3) The renewal fee, payable every 3 years, is 900 crowns.
(4) Fees may be adjusted periodically by NEPA, with at least 6 months' prior public notice.
(5) All fees collected contribute directly to the administration and enforcement of this Act and the protection of Nordvale's water resources.

heading: Licence fees
text:
(1) The initial application fee for a Water Well Drilling Licence is 1,500 crowns, which is non-refundable.
(2) The annual maintenance fee for a valid licence is 550 crowns, payable by January 31st of each year.
(3) The renewal fee, payable every 3 years, is 1,100 crowns.
(4) Fees may be adjusted periodically by NEPA, with at least 6 months' prior public notice.
(5) All fees collected contribute directly to the administration and enforcement of this Act and the protection of Nordvale's water resources.

heading: Drilling permits
text:
(1) In addition to a general drilling licence, a specific drilling permit must be obtained from NEPA for each individual well drilling project.
(2) The application for a drilling permit must include the proposed well location (GPS coordinates), estimated depth, intended use of water, and a hydrogeological survey if the depth exceeds 50 meters.
(3) A permit application fee of 300 crowns applies for each new well, and 150 crowns for significant deepening of an existing well.
(4) NEPA will review permit applications within 15 working days.
(5) No drilling may commence until the permit has been officially issued.

heading: Environmental impact assessment
text:
(1) For wells proposed to extract more than 5,000 litres per day or those exceeding 100 meters in depth, a comprehensive environmental impact assessment (EIA) must be submitted with the drilling permit application.
(2) The EIA must evaluate potential effects on local aquifers, surface water bodies, and adjacent ecosystems.
(3) NEPA may require public consultation for projects with potentially significant environmental impacts.
(4) The cost of the EIA is borne by the applicant.
(5) Failure to provide an adequate EIA will result in the rejection of the drilling permit application.

heading: Well construction standards
text:
(1) All water wells must be constructed in accordance with the Nordvale Well Construction Standards, published by NEPA.
(2) These standards specify requirements for casing materials, well screens, grouting, and sanitary seals to prevent contamination.
(3) Wells must be drilled at least 15 meters from any septic system and 30 meters from any livestock waste storage area.
(4) The diameter of the well casing must be at least 10 centimeters for residential use.
(5) Any deviation from these standards must be approved in writing by NEPA prior to construction.

heading: Water quality testing
text:
(1) Upon completion of a new well, the licensee must conduct initial water quality tests for common contaminants including bacteria (e.g., E. coli), nitrates, and heavy metals.
(2) Samples must be analyzed by a NEPA-accredited laboratory.
(3) A detailed report of the test results must be submitted to NEPA within 30 days of well completion.
(4) If water quality standards are not met, the well must be disinfected or treated, and retested, before it can be put into service.
(5) Additional periodic testing may be mandated by NEPA for wells in high-risk areas.

heading: Well reporting
text:
(1) Within 60 days of completing any well drilling activity, the licensee must submit a comprehensive well completion report to NEPA.
(2) This report must include the exact location of the well (GPS coordinates with accuracy of +/- 1 meter), actual depth drilled, geological logs, casing details, pump test results, and water yield data.
(3) A copy of the initial water quality test results, as per section 11, must be attached.
(4) The report must also detail the intended use of the well and the estimated daily water withdrawal.
(5) Failure to submit a complete and accurate report may result in fines or licence suspension.

heading: Maintenance of records
text:
(1) All licensees must maintain detailed records of every drilling project for a minimum of 10 years.
(2) These records must include all permit applications, geological logs, well construction details, water quality test results, and any maintenance or abandonment activities.
(3) Records must be made available for inspection by NEPA officials upon request, with 48 hours' notice.
(4) Digital copies of records are acceptable, provided they are securely stored and readily accessible.
(5) Good record-keeping is essential for tracking groundwater resources and ensuring compliance.

heading: Supervision of operations
text:
(1) All water well drilling operations must be directly supervised by a licensed driller.
(2) The licensed driller must be physically present at the drilling site for at least 75% of the operational time, especially during critical phases like casing installation and grouting.
(3) In the absence of the primary licensed driller, a qualified apprentice with at least 2 years of experience may oversee routine tasks, but critical decisions must await the driller's return.
(4) The supervising driller is responsible for ensuring compliance with all safety regulations and construction standards.
(5) Any incidents or accidents on site must be reported to NEPA within 24 hours.

heading: Driller training and certification
text:
(1) NEPA shall establish and maintain a certification program for water well drillers and apprentices.
(2) Certification requires passing a written exam (minimum score 75%) and a practical assessment.
(3) All licensed drillers must complete at least 15 hours of continuing professional development every 2 years to maintain their certification.
(4) Training topics include advanced drilling techniques, new well construction materials, and environmental protection protocols.
(5) NEPA will publish a list of approved training providers and courses annually.

heading: Driller training and certification
text:
(1) NEPA shall establish and maintain a certification program for water well drillers and apprentices.
(2) Certification requires passing a written exam (minimum score 80%) and a practical assessment.
(3) All licensed drillers must complete at least 20 hours of continuing professional development every 2 years to maintain their certification.
(4) Training topics include advanced drilling techniques, new well construction materials, environmental protection protocols, and groundwater contamination prevention.
(5) NEPA will publish a list of approved training providers and courses annually.

heading: Well abandonment procedures
text:
(1) When a water well is no longer in use, or if it is deemed to be a contamination risk, it must be properly abandoned by a licensed driller.
(2) Well abandonment procedures must follow NEPA guidelines, which typically involve filling the well with impermeable material such as bentonite clay or cement grout from the bottom up.
(3) A well abandonment report must be submitted to NEPA within 45 days of completion of the abandonment.
(4) Failure to properly abandon a well can lead to significant environmental contamination and substantial fines.
(5) The cost of well abandonment is the responsibility of the well owner.

heading: Inspections and enforcement
text:
(1) NEPA officials are authorized to conduct unannounced inspections of drilling sites and licensee premises to ensure compliance with this Act.
(2) Inspectors may examine equipment, review records, and take samples of water or geological materials.
(3) Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may result in immediate licence suspension.
(4) If non-compliance is identified, NEPA will issue a notice of violation, requiring corrective action within 14 days.
(5) Continued non-compliance may lead to penalties as described in section 25.

heading: Inspections and enforcement
text:
(1) NEPA officials are authorized to conduct unannounced inspections of drilling sites and licensee premises to ensure compliance with this Act, with at least 15% of all active drilling sites inspected annually.
(2) Inspectors may examine equipment, review records, take samples of water or geological materials, and interview personnel.
(3) Obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may result in immediate licence suspension and a fine of 5,000 crowns.
(4) If non-compliance is identified, NEPA will issue a notice of violation, requiring corrective action within 7 days.
(5) Continued non-compliance may lead to penalties as described in section 25, including permanent revocation of licence.

heading: Suspension or revocation of licence
text:
(1) NEPA may suspend a Water Well Drilling Licence for a period of up to 6 months if a licensee repeatedly fails to comply with the provisions of this Act or its associated regulations.
(2) Serious violations, such as causing significant environmental damage or persistent refusal to cooperate with inspections, may lead to immediate revocation of the licence.
(3) Before any suspension or revocation, the licensee will be given 30 days' written notice and an opportunity to present their case at a hearing.
(4) A suspended licence cannot be used for any drilling activities during the suspension period.
(5) Reapplication after revocation is only possible after 2 years and requires demonstration of rectified issues.

heading: Appeals process
text:
(1) Any applicant or licensee aggrieved by a decision of NEPA regarding licence application, permit issuance, or enforcement action may appeal the decision.
(2) An appeal must be submitted in writing to the Nordvale Environmental Appeals Board (NEAB) within 30 days of receiving the NEPA decision.
(3) The NEAB will review all submitted documentation and may hold a hearing within 60 days of the appeal filing.
(4) The decision of the NEAB is final, subject to judicial review as provided by the laws of Nordvale.
(5) A fee of 500 crowns is required to file an appeal, refundable if the appeal is successful.

heading: Protection of groundwater resources
text:
(1) All drilling operations must prioritize the protection of Nordvale's groundwater resources from contamination and overuse.
(2) Licensees must implement best management practices to prevent spillage of fuel, lubricants, and drilling fluids.
(3) Drilling in designated groundwater protection zones may be subject to additional restrictions or outright prohibition, as determined by NEPA.
(4) Any discovery of groundwater contamination during drilling must be immediately reported to NEPA within 12 hours.
(5) Wells should be designed to minimize drawdown effects on adjacent wells and natural springs, with a maximum allowable drawdown of 1 meter for existing wells within 50 meters.

heading: Protection of groundwater resources
text:
(1) All drilling operations must prioritize the protection of Nordvale's groundwater resources from contamination and overuse, adhering to a 'zero-discharge' policy for drilling fluids into the environment.
(2) Licensees must implement best management practices to prevent spillage of fuel, lubricants, and drilling fluids, including the use of impermeable liners around drilling sites.
(3) Drilling in designated groundwater protection zones is strictly prohibited, as determined by NEPA, and these zones will be clearly mapped and publicly accessible.
(4) Any discovery of groundwater contamination during drilling must be immediately reported to NEPA within 6 hours, along with proposed mitigation steps.
(5) Wells should be designed to minimize drawdown effects on adjacent wells and natural springs, with a maximum allowable drawdown of 0.5 meters for existing wells within 100 meters, or 0.2 meters for those within 50 meters.

heading: Water usage restrictions
text:
(1) NEPA reserves the right to impose temporary or permanent restrictions on water usage from wells during periods of drought or critical water scarcity.
(2) These restrictions may include limits on daily withdrawal volumes, specific times for irrigation, or complete prohibitions on certain uses.
(3) Licensees and well owners will be notified of any restrictions through public announcements and direct communication, with at least 7 days' notice, unless an emergency dictates immediate action.
(4) Non-compliance with water usage restrictions may result in fines of up to 1,000 crowns per day of violation.
(5) Well owners are encouraged to install water meters and monitor their usage regularly.

heading: Well ownership transfer
text:
(1) When ownership of a property with a water well is transferred, the new owner must notify NEPA within 90 days of the transfer.
(2) The notification must include the well's registration number and the contact details of the new owner.
(3) NEPA will provide the new owner with information regarding their responsibilities under this Act, including maintenance and reporting obligations.
(4) Failure to notify NEPA of a change in ownership may result in the previous owner remaining liable for non-compliance issues.
(5) There is no fee for notifying NEPA of a well ownership transfer.

heading: Emergency provisions
text:
(1) In the event of a natural disaster or other emergency that severely impacts public water supply, NEPA may temporarily waive certain provisions of this Act.
(2) Such waivers will be limited in scope and duration, and will only be granted to facilitate immediate humanitarian relief or essential services.
(3) Any drilling operations conducted under emergency waivers must still adhere to basic safety and environmental protection principles.
(4) NEPA will issue specific directives outlining the conditions and extent of any emergency waivers.
(5) All emergency drilling activities must still be reported to NEPA within 48 hours of commencement.

heading: Public access to information
text:
(1) NEPA will maintain a public register of all licensed drillers, drilling permits issued, and well completion reports.
(2) This register will be accessible online and at NEPA's offices in Aldmark during regular business hours.
(3) Certain sensitive information, such as personal contact details of individual well owners, will be redacted to protect privacy.
(4) The public register aims to enhance transparency and allow citizens to verify the legitimacy of drilling operations in their areas.
(5) Requests for specific documents not readily available online may incur a small administrative fee of 50 crowns.

heading: Public access to information
text:
(1) NEPA will maintain a comprehensive, searchable public database of all licensed drillers, drilling permits issued, and well completion reports, including detailed geological logs where available.
(2) This database will be fully accessible online 24/7, and at NEPA's offices in Aldmark, Brenholt, and Corvik during regular business hours.
(3) Sensitive information, such as personal contact details of individual well owners, will be redacted to protect privacy, but aggregate data will be available for research purposes.
(4) The public database aims to enhance transparency, allow citizens to verify drilling operations, and support scientific research into Nordvale's hydrogeology.
(5) All public information requests will be processed free of charge, with a guaranteed response within 5 working days for non-standard queries.

heading: Penalties for non-compliance
text:
(1) Any individual or company found to be drilling water wells without a valid licence faces a fine of 5,000 crowns for a first offense and 10,000 crowns for subsequent offenses.
(2) Violation of well construction standards, as outlined in section 10, may result in a fine of up to 3,000 crowns per infraction.
(3) Failure to submit required reports or documentation within the specified timeframes may incur a penalty of 500 crowns per week of delay.
(4) Causing significant environmental damage due to negligent drilling practices can lead to fines of up to 50,000 crowns and liability for remediation costs.
(5) All fines are payable to NEPA within 30 days of issuance.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) NEPA is authorized to issue detailed regulations to further implement the provisions of this Act.
(2) These regulations may cover specific technical standards, procedural requirements, and forms for applications and reports.
(3) All proposed regulations must undergo a public consultation period of at least 45 days before being finalized and published.
(4) Regulations will be reviewed and updated by NEPA every 5 years to ensure they remain current and effective.
(5) The current regulations can be accessed on the NEPA website and at their main office.

heading: Regulations
text:
(1) NEPA is authorized to issue detailed regulations to further implement the provisions of this Act, including specific guidelines for drilling in sensitive ecological areas.
(2) These regulations may cover specific technical standards, procedural requirements, forms for applications and reports, and criteria for environmental impact assessments.
(3) All proposed regulations must undergo a comprehensive public consultation period of at least 60 days, including public hearings in at least three municipalities, before being finalized and published.
(4) Regulations will be reviewed and updated by NEPA every 3 years to ensure they remain current, effective, and responsive to new scientific understanding and technological advancements.
(5) The current regulations can be accessed on the NEPA website and at their main and regional offices, and a summary will be published in the Nordvale Gazette.

heading: Conflict of interest
text:
(1) No NEPA employee or official involved in the licensing or inspection process under this Act shall have a financial interest in any company holding or applying for a Water Well Drilling Licence.
(2) Any potential conflict of interest must be disclosed immediately to the NEPA Ethics Committee.
(3) Failure to disclose a conflict of interest may result in disciplinary action, including termination of employment and potential legal charges.
(4) This provision aims to ensure fairness and impartiality in all regulatory decisions.
(5) A detailed policy on conflicts of interest is available for public review on the NEPA website.

heading: Repeal of previous Acts
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: A licensed fireworks technician receives no supplement for older children.

heading: Concessions
text: No dog licence fee is payable by any person who is, and for at least one year has been, the registered keeper of a listed windmill.

heading: Fairway conductors on fixed links
text:
(1) For each fixed-link transit levy, a certified fairway conductor pays the amount of category R1 of the Schedule of Carriageway Rates.
(2) That amount applies instead of any other reduction of the levy, whatever the hour of the passage.

heading: Purpose and scope
text: This Act establishes the legal framework for the regulation, application, and issuance of permits for the drilling of new water wells within the Republic of Nordvale. Its primary purpose is to ensure the sustainable management of groundwater resources, protect public health, and prevent adverse environmental impacts. The Act applies to all individuals, businesses, and organizations intending to drill or commission the drilling of a water well for any purpose, including domestic, agricultural, industrial, or commercial use. It outlines the responsibilities of applicants, the powers of the Department of Water Resources, and the process for appealing decisions made under this Act. The scope covers all municipalities including Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, and Lund Vale.

heading: Definitions
text:
For the purposes of this Act:
(1) 'Department' refers to the Department of Water Resources of Nordvale.
(2) 'Well' means any excavation or artificial opening in the ground, whether bored, drilled, or otherwise constructed, for the purpose of extracting groundwater.
(3) 'Permit' means a Water Well Drilling Permit issued by the Department.
(4) 'Applicant' means an individual, company, or entity applying for a permit under this Act.
(5) 'Certified Driller' means a professional registered with the Department who is qualified to drill water wells.
(6) 'Groundwater' refers to water located beneath the Earth's surface in soil pore spaces and in the fractures of rock formations. The Department maintains a public register of all active certified drillers, updated monthly.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall commence the drilling of any new water well within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Department in accordance with the provisions of this Act. This requirement applies irrespective of the intended depth or diameter of the well, or the purpose for which the water is to be extracted. Any drilling activity undertaken without a permit is a direct violation of this Act and may result in severe penalties as outlined in section 35. The Department processes approximately 700 permit applications annually, with an approval rate of about 85%. A well for purely exploratory purposes that does not extract water also requires a permit.

heading: Requirement for Permit
text: No person or entity shall commence the drilling of any new water well within the Republic of Nordvale without first obtaining a valid permit from the Department in accordance with the provisions of this Act. This requirement applies irrespective of the intended depth or diameter of the well, or the purpose for which the water is to be extracted. Any drilling activity undertaken without a permit is a direct violation of this Act and may result in severe penalties as outlined in section 35. The Department processes approximately 850 permit applications annually, with an approval rate of about 80%. A well for purely exploratory purposes that does not extract water also requires a permit, regardless of its intended depth.

heading: Application Submission
text: Applications for a Water Well Drilling Permit must be submitted to the Department on the prescribed form, available electronically on the Department's website or in physical copy at its offices in Aldmark and Brenholt. Each application must be accompanied by all required documentation, including a site plan, geological survey report if available, and the non-refundable application fee. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant within 10 business days, delaying the review process. The Department aims to acknowledge receipt of all applications within 3 business days of submission. A digital signature is acceptable for all electronic submissions.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 250 crowns must accompany every permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial review, data entry, and correspondence. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant. The Department reviews the fee structure every two years to ensure it aligns with operational costs. Approximately 5% of applications are initially rejected due to incorrect fee payment.

heading: Application Fee
text: A non-refundable application fee of 300 crowns must accompany every permit application. This fee covers the administrative costs associated with processing the application, including initial review, data entry, and correspondence. The fee must be paid in full at the time of submission. Applications received without the correct fee will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant. The Department reviews the fee structure every two years to ensure it aligns with operational costs. Approximately 3% of applications are initially rejected due to incorrect fee payment. This fee applies uniformly across all well types and depths.

heading: Required Documentation
text:
Each application must include:
(a) A detailed site plan, drawn to a scale of at least 1:500, indicating the proposed well location, property boundaries, and any existing structures or water bodies within 50 meters.
(b) Proof of land ownership or a signed lease agreement demonstrating rights to drill.
(c) A proposed drilling method statement, including anticipated depth and diameter.
(d) The name and registration number of the Certified Driller who will undertake the work.
(e) An environmental impact assessment statement, if the proposed well is intended for industrial use or is projected to extract more than 50,000 liters per day.
(f) A signed declaration affirming the accuracy of all submitted information.

heading: Site Plan Requirements
text:
The site plan required under section 6(a) must clearly depict:
(a) The precise geographical coordinates (latitude and longitude) of the proposed well site.
(b) All distances from the proposed well to property lines, septic systems (minimum 30 meters), and public water supply lines (minimum 100 meters).
(c) The location of any known geological faults or unstable ground within 200 meters.
(d) Topographical contours at 1-meter intervals for the immediate vicinity of the proposed well. Failure to meet these specific drawing standards may result in the return of the application for correction, adding up to 15 days to the processing time. The plan must be prepared by a licensed surveyor.

heading: Site Plan Requirements
text:
The site plan required under section 6(a) must clearly depict:
(a) The precise geographical coordinates (latitude and longitude) of the proposed well site.
(b) All distances from the proposed well to property lines, septic systems (minimum 40 meters), and public water supply lines (minimum 120 meters).
(c) The location of any known geological faults or unstable ground within 250 meters.
(d) Topographical contours at 0.5-meter intervals for the immediate vicinity of the proposed well. Failure to meet these specific drawing standards may result in the return of the application for correction, adding up to 20 days to the processing time. The plan must be prepared by a licensed surveyor and digitally signed.

heading: Certified Driller Requirement
text: All drilling activities for which a permit is sought must be conducted by a Certified Driller registered with the Department. The applicant must provide the driller's current registration number and contact details in the application. The Department maintains a public register of all Certified Drillers, accessible online. Only drillers with at least 5 years of professional experience and who have passed the Department's certification exam are eligible for registration. The driller is personally responsible for adhering to all safety protocols and drilling standards set forth by the Department. This ensures a high standard of work and minimizes risks to groundwater quality.

heading: Certified Driller Requirement
text: All drilling activities for which a permit is sought must be conducted by a Certified Driller registered with the Department. The applicant must provide the driller's current registration number and contact details in the application. The Department maintains a public register of all Certified Drillers, accessible online. Only drillers with at least 7 years of professional experience and who have passed the Department's advanced certification exam are eligible for registration. The driller is personally responsible for adhering to all safety protocols and drilling standards set forth by the Department. Drillers must also hold valid liability insurance covering at least 2,000,000 crowns.

heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
text: An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) statement is mandatory for any proposed well that is intended for industrial use or projected to extract more than 50,000 liters of water per day. The EIA must be prepared by an independent environmental consultant approved by the Department and must assess potential impacts on local ecosystems, water table levels, and adjacent water users. The cost of the EIA is borne by the applicant. The Department will not process an application requiring an EIA until the statement has been thoroughly reviewed and deemed satisfactory. This process can add up to 45 days to the permit review timeline. The EIA must include a 5-year projection of water usage.

heading: Application Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application and the correct fee, the Department will initiate a review process. This process typically takes up to 45 business days. During this period, Department officials will assess the application against all criteria set out in this Act, including environmental considerations, hydrological impacts, and compliance with zoning regulations. The Department may consult with other relevant municipal authorities in Aldmark, Corvik, or Dunmere if the proposed well is located near jurisdictional boundaries. Site visits may be conducted for approximately 20% of applications, especially for those in sensitive ecological areas.

heading: Application Review Process
text: Upon receipt of a complete application and the correct fee, the Department will initiate a review process. This process typically takes up to 60 business days. During this period, Department officials will assess the application against all criteria set out in this Act, including environmental considerations, hydrological impacts, and compliance with zoning regulations. The Department will consult with other relevant municipal authorities in Aldmark, Corvik, Dunmere, and Lund Vale if the proposed well is located near jurisdictional boundaries. Site visits may be conducted for approximately 30% of applications, especially for those in sensitive ecological areas or with high extraction rates.

heading: Information Requests
text: During the review process, the Department may request additional information or clarification from the applicant. Such requests will be made in writing and the applicant will have 15 business days to respond. Failure to provide the requested information within this timeframe may result in the application being deemed incomplete and subsequently rejected. The review period described in section 10 will be paused from the date the request is issued until the date the Department receives a satisfactory response. On average, 10% of applications require additional information. This ensures a thorough and accurate assessment.

heading: Public Consultation (Domestic Use)
text: For wells intended solely for domestic use, public consultation is generally not required unless the proposed well is within 20 meters of a known public water source or a designated sensitive ecological zone. In such cases, the Department will notify adjacent property owners within a 50-meter radius, allowing them 14 days to submit written comments or objections. The Department considers all valid comments received during this period before making a final decision on the permit application. This process ensures community interests are balanced with individual property rights. Approximately 5% of domestic well applications undergo public consultation.

heading: Public Consultation (Non-Domestic Use)
text: For wells intended for agricultural, industrial, or commercial use, or any well projected to extract more than 50,000 liters per day, the Department shall publish a public notice of the application in the Nordvale Gazette and on its official website. This notice will be open for public comment for a period of 30 days. The Department will also directly notify all property owners within a 100-meter radius of the proposed well. All substantive comments and concerns received will be reviewed and addressed as part of the permit decision-making process. This ensures broader community engagement and transparency for larger projects.

heading: Public Consultation (Non-Domestic Use)
text: For wells intended for agricultural, industrial, or commercial use, or any well projected to extract more than 75,000 liters per day, the Department shall publish a public notice of the application in the Nordvale Gazette and on its official website. This notice will be open for public comment for a period of 45 days. The Department will also directly notify all property owners within a 150-meter radius of the proposed well. All substantive comments and concerns received will be reviewed and addressed as part of the permit decision-making process. This ensures broader community engagement and transparency for larger projects and heightened environmental scrutiny.

heading: Permit Approval
text: If, after completing the review process and considering any public comments, the Department determines that the proposed well drilling project complies with all provisions of this Act and other relevant environmental regulations, a permit will be issued. The permit will specify the authorized driller, the approved well location, maximum depth, and any conditions deemed necessary to protect groundwater resources or adjacent properties. These conditions may include specific casing requirements, limitations on pumping rates, or monitoring obligations. The permit is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue. Approximately 85% of applications are approved.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
The Department may attach specific conditions to any permit issued under this Act. These conditions are designed to mitigate potential risks and ensure the long-term sustainability of groundwater. Common conditions include:
(a) Specific well construction standards, including minimum casing thickness and sealing requirements.
(b) Limitations on the maximum daily volume of water that may be extracted (e.g., 20,000 liters/day for domestic use, 100,000 liters/day for agricultural).
(c) Requirements for ongoing water quality testing and reporting.
(d) Provisions for the proper decommissioning of the well once its operational life ends. Failure to adhere to any permit condition constitutes a breach of this Act.

heading: Permit Conditions
text:
The Department may attach specific conditions to any permit issued under this Act. These conditions are designed to mitigate potential risks and ensure the long-term sustainability of groundwater. Common conditions include:
(a) Specific well construction standards, including minimum casing thickness and sealing requirements, to a depth of at least 15 meters.
(b) Limitations on the maximum daily volume of water that may be extracted (e.g., 15,000 liters/day for domestic use, 80,000 liters/day for agricultural).
(c) Requirements for ongoing water quality testing and reporting, at least quarterly.
(d) Provisions for the proper decommissioning of the well once its operational life ends, to be completed within 90 days. Failure to adhere to any permit condition constitutes a breach of this Act and may result in revocation.

heading: Permit Refusal
text:
The Department may refuse to issue a permit if:
(a) The application is incomplete or contains false information.
(b) The proposed well poses an unacceptable risk to public health, safety, or the environment.
(c) The proposed extraction volume is deemed unsustainable for the local groundwater aquifer.
(d) The proposed well location violates setback requirements or other zoning bylaws.
(e) Public comments raise valid and unmitigated concerns about the project's impact.
(f) The applicant has a history of non-compliance with environmental regulations. The refusal decision will be provided to the applicant in writing, outlining the specific reasons for denial.

heading: Right to Appeal Refusal
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused has the right to appeal the decision. A written notice of appeal must be submitted to the Department within 30 days of receiving the refusal notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for challenging the decision and include any new information or mitigating proposals. The Department will then convene an independent appeals panel to review the case. The panel consists of three experts not previously involved in the initial decision. A non-refundable appeal fee of 500 crowns must accompany the appeal submission. Approximately 10% of refusals proceed to appeal.

heading: Right to Appeal Refusal
text: An applicant whose permit application has been refused has the right to appeal the decision. A written notice of appeal must be submitted to the Department within 21 days of receiving the refusal notification. The appeal must clearly state the grounds for challenging the decision and include any new information or mitigating proposals. The Department will then convene an independent appeals panel to review the case. The panel consists of five experts not previously involved in the initial decision, including at least one independent hydrologist. A non-refundable appeal fee of 750 crowns must accompany the appeal submission. Approximately 12% of refusals proceed to appeal, with a reversal rate of about 20%.

heading: Permit Validity Period
text: A Water Well Drilling Permit is valid for a period of 12 months from its date of issue. If drilling has not commenced within this period, the permit will expire, and a new application will be required. An extension of 6 months may be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as unforeseen geological challenges or severe weather conditions, upon written request to the Department at least 30 days before the original expiry date. This extension requires a processing fee of 150 crowns. The maximum number of extensions for a single permit is one. Approximately 15% of permits require an extension.

heading: Permit Renewal
text: Once a well is drilled and operational, the permit does not require annual renewal unless specific conditions attached to the permit stipulate otherwise, such as for large-scale industrial wells. However, the Department reserves the right to review any permit after 5 years of operation if there are concerns about water table depletion or environmental impact. In such cases, the permit holder will be notified and may be required to provide updated hydrological data. Failure to comply with a review request can lead to the suspension or revocation of the permit. Regular monitoring reports are generally sufficient for most domestic wells.

heading: Drilling Standards
text: All drilling and well construction must adhere to the Nordvale Well Drilling Standards, a technical document published and periodically updated by the Department. These standards cover aspects such as minimum casing depths (e.g., 6 meters), casing materials (e.g., steel or PVC of specified thickness), grouting procedures, and wellhead completion requirements (e.g., 30 cm above ground level). The Certified Driller is solely responsible for ensuring compliance with these standards. Non-compliance can lead to significant fines and potential suspension of the driller's certification. Inspections are conducted on 25% of all newly drilled wells to verify adherence.

heading: Drilling Standards
text: All drilling and well construction must adhere to the Nordvale Well Drilling Standards, a technical document published and periodically updated by the Department. These standards cover aspects such as minimum casing depths (e.g., 8 meters), casing materials (e.g., steel or PVC of specified thickness), grouting procedures, and wellhead completion requirements (e.g., 45 cm above ground level). The Certified Driller is solely responsible for ensuring compliance with these standards. Non-compliance can lead to significant fines and potential suspension of the driller's certification for up to 2 years. Inspections are conducted on 35% of all newly drilled wells to verify adherence and ensure groundwater protection.

heading: Well Completion Report
text:
Within 30 days of completing the drilling of a new well, the Certified Driller must submit a Well Completion Report to the Department. This report must include:
(a) The actual depth and diameter of the well.
(b) A detailed geological log of the drilled strata.
(c) The static water level and pumping test results.
(d) Details of casing and grouting materials used.
(e) The yield of the well in liters per minute.
(f) Any deviations from the approved permit plan. Failure to submit this report within the stipulated timeframe may result in penalties for the driller and a delay in final well approval. Approximately 98% of reports are submitted on time.

heading: Water Quality Testing
text: Upon completion of a new well, and before it is put into use, the permit holder must arrange for initial water quality testing by a Department-approved laboratory. The water must be tested for a minimum set of parameters, including bacterial contamination (e.g., E. coli), nitrates, and heavy metals (e.g., lead, arsenic). A certificate of analysis must be submitted to the Department within 60 days of well completion. If the water quality does not meet the Nordvale Drinking Water Standards, the well cannot be used until remedial action has been taken and subsequent testing confirms compliance. The cost of testing is borne by the permit holder, typically around 800 crowns.

heading: Well Decommissioning
text: When a well is no longer in use, or if it is determined to be a risk to groundwater quality, it must be properly decommissioned. Decommissioning involves sealing the well to prevent contamination of aquifers and eliminate physical hazards. The permit holder or current landowner must notify the Department at least 30 days prior to decommissioning. The work must be carried out by a Certified Driller in accordance with the Nordvale Well Decommissioning Guidelines. A Well Decommissioning Report must be submitted to the Department within 15 days of completion. Failure to properly decommission a well can result in a fine of up to 10,000 crowns. This is crucial for environmental protection.

heading: Well Decommissioning
text: When a well is no longer in use, or if it is determined to be a risk to groundwater quality, it must be properly decommissioned. Decommissioning involves sealing the well to prevent contamination of aquifers and eliminate physical hazards. The permit holder or current landowner must notify the Department at least 45 days prior to decommissioning. The work must be carried out by a Certified Driller in accordance with the Nordvale Well Decommissioning Guidelines, ensuring complete isolation of aquifers. A Well Decommissioning Report must be submitted to the Department within 10 days of completion. Failure to properly decommission a well can result in a fine of up to 15,000 crowns or mandatory corrective action at the owner's expense. This is crucial for environmental protection and public safety.

heading: Monitoring and Reporting (Large Wells)
text: Wells permitted for the extraction of more than 100,000 liters per day, or those designated as industrial wells, are subject to ongoing monitoring and reporting requirements. The permit holder must install flow meters and submit quarterly reports to the Department detailing the volume of water extracted, static water levels, and results of periodic water quality tests. These reports are due within 15 days following the end of each quarter. The Department may also require the installation of observation wells to monitor regional groundwater levels. Non-compliance with reporting obligations can result in a daily fine of 100 crowns. This ensures sustainable resource management.

heading: Inspection Powers
text: Department officials, upon presentation of valid identification, have the authority to enter any property where well drilling is being conducted or where a permitted well is located, for the purpose of inspection. These inspections may occur at any reasonable time to verify compliance with this Act, the permit conditions, and drilling standards. Inspectors may take samples, examine records, and issue directives for corrective action. Refusal to grant access to an inspector or obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may result in penalties as outlined in section 35. Approximately 20% of new wells are subject to an initial site inspection, with follow-ups for 5% of all wells.

heading: Inspection Powers
text: Department officials, upon presentation of valid identification, have the authority to enter any property where well drilling is being conducted or where a permitted well is located, for the purpose of inspection. These inspections may occur at any reasonable time to verify compliance with this Act, the permit conditions, and drilling standards. Inspectors may take samples, examine records, and issue directives for corrective action. Refusal to grant access to an inspector or obstruction of an inspection is a serious offense and may result in penalties as outlined in section 35, including immediate cessation of work. Approximately 30% of new wells are subject to an initial site inspection, with follow-ups for 10% of all wells, particularly those in areas of high water stress or with previous compliance issues.

heading: Emergency Powers
text: In cases of immediate threat to public health, safety, or critical groundwater resources, the Department may issue an emergency order. Such an order can require the immediate cessation of drilling activities, modification of well operations, or temporary suspension of water extraction. An emergency order takes effect immediately upon issuance and does not require prior notice. The affected party has 7 days to appeal the emergency order to the Department. Failure to comply with an emergency order carries severe penalties, including potential criminal charges. This power is reserved for extreme situations, such as major contamination events or rapid aquifer depletion.

heading: Protection of Existing Wells
text: New well permits will not be issued if the Department determines that the proposed well would significantly interfere with the water supply of existing wells within a 150-meter radius, or cause substantial drawdown of the water table in a localized area. Applicants may be required to conduct a pump test on a nearby existing well, with the consent of its owner, to demonstrate no adverse impact. If interference is proven after drilling, the new permit holder may be liable for the costs of deepening the affected well or providing an alternative water supply. This ensures equitable access to groundwater resources for all users.

heading: Cessation of Drilling
text:
The Department may order the immediate cessation of drilling activities if:
(a) Drilling is proceeding without a valid permit.
(b) There is a significant deviation from the approved permit plan.
(c) The drilling is causing or is likely to cause immediate environmental harm, such as aquifer cross-contamination.
(d) Safety protocols are not being followed, posing a risk to workers or the public.
(e) The Certified Driller's registration has been suspended or revoked. A cessation order remains in effect until the identified issues are resolved to the satisfaction of the Department. Non-compliance with a cessation order will lead to further penalties.

heading: Certified Driller Registration
text: Individuals wishing to register as Certified Drillers must pass an examination administered by the Department, demonstrate at least 5 years of practical experience, and provide proof of appropriate insurance (minimum 1,000,000 crowns liability). Registration is valid for 3 years and requires renewal. Continuing education credits (e.g., 20 hours over 3 years) are mandatory for renewal. The Department may suspend or revoke a driller's registration for gross negligence, repeated non-compliance with drilling standards, or providing false information. There are currently approximately 150 Certified Drillers registered across Nordvale.

heading: Certified Driller Registration
text: Individuals wishing to register as Certified Drillers must pass an advanced examination administered by the Department, demonstrate at least 8 years of practical experience, and provide proof of appropriate insurance (minimum 2,500,000 crowns liability). Registration is valid for 2 years and requires renewal. Continuing education credits (e.g., 30 hours over 2 years) are mandatory for renewal, with a focus on new technologies and environmental practices. The Department may suspend or revoke a driller's registration for gross negligence, repeated non-compliance with drilling standards, or providing false information, with immediate effect in severe cases. There are currently approximately 170 Certified Drillers registered across Nordvale, with 5% under review for compliance issues.

heading: Continuing Education for Drillers
text: To maintain Certified Driller registration, individuals must complete a minimum of 20 hours of approved continuing education every 3 years. Approved courses include topics such as new drilling technologies, groundwater protection strategies, safety protocols, and changes in regulatory requirements. The Department publishes a list of approved education providers and courses annually. Failure to meet the continuing education requirements will result in the suspension of the driller's registration until the outstanding hours are completed. This ensures that all Certified Drillers remain up-to-date with best practices and evolving standards. The Department actively audits 10% of driller's education records each year.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: A Water Well Drilling Permit is generally non-transferable. However, in cases of property ownership change before drilling commences, the new owner may apply to the Department to transfer the existing permit. This application must be made within 60 days of the property transfer and requires a transfer fee of 100 crowns. The Department will review the request and may approve the transfer if all original permit conditions remain applicable and the new owner agrees to abide by them. If drilling has already commenced, a new permit application from the new owner is usually required. Only about 2% of permits are transferred annually.

heading: Transfer of Permits
text: A Water Well Drilling Permit is generally non-transferable. However, in cases of property ownership change before drilling commences, the new owner may apply to the Department to transfer the existing permit. This application must be made within 45 days of the property transfer and requires a transfer fee of 150 crowns. The Department will review the request and may approve the transfer if all original permit conditions remain applicable, no changes to the well plan are proposed, and the new owner agrees to abide by them. If drilling has already commenced, a new permit application from the new owner is always required. Only about 1.5% of permits are transferred annually.

heading: Information Disclosure
text: All information submitted with a permit application, including site plans and geological reports, is considered public record and may be disclosed by the Department upon request, subject to the Nordvale Data Privacy Act. The Department maintains an online registry of all permitted wells, including their location, depth, and intended use, accessible to the public. This transparency aims to foster public awareness and facilitate regional water resource planning. Sensitive personal information, such as financial details of applicants, will be protected in accordance with privacy laws. Aggregate data is frequently published for research purposes.

heading: Confidentiality
text: Despite the general principle of information disclosure as stated in section 31, certain commercially sensitive or proprietary information contained within an application may be withheld from public disclosure if the applicant demonstrates that its release would cause significant competitive harm. A request for confidentiality must be made in writing at the time of application submission, clearly identifying the specific information and justifying the claim for confidentiality. The Department will review such requests on a case-by-case basis and inform the applicant of its decision. Approximately 1% of applications contain information deemed confidential.

heading: False Information
text: Any person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in a permit application, during an inspection, or in any report required under this Act commits an offense. Such an offense may result in the immediate rejection of the application, revocation of any issued permit, and significant fines. In severe cases, criminal charges may be pursued. The Department takes the integrity of submitted information very seriously, as it forms the basis for critical environmental and public health decisions. Penalties can include fines of up to 25,000 crowns and a ban from applying for future permits for a period of up to 5 years.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text: Any person or entity found in violation of this Act, including but not limited to drilling without a permit, non-compliance with permit conditions, or obstruction of an inspector, shall be liable for penalties. For a first offense, a fine of up to 10,000 crowns may be imposed. Subsequent offenses may incur fines of up to 30,000 crowns and the potential for mandatory cessation of all related activities. The Department may also require corrective action, the costs of which will be borne by the offending party. Each day an offense continues may be considered a separate offense. The Department issues approximately 50 notices of violation per year.

heading: Offences and Penalties
text: Any person or entity found in violation of this Act, including but not limited to drilling without a permit, non-compliance with permit conditions, obstruction of an inspector, or failure to properly decommission a well, shall be liable for penalties. For a first offense, a fine of up to 15,000 crowns may be imposed. Subsequent offenses may incur fines of up to 45,000 crowns and the potential for mandatory cessation of all related activities for a minimum of 6 months. The Department may also require corrective action, including well abandonment, the costs of which will be borne by the offending party. Each day an offense continues may be considered a separate offense, with an additional daily fine of 500 crowns. The Department issues approximately 75 notices of violation per year, with 10% resulting in permit revocation.

heading: Cost Recovery
text: Where the Department incurs costs in taking corrective action due to non-compliance with this Act or a permit condition, such as emergency well sealing or environmental remediation, those costs may be recovered from the responsible party. This includes all administrative, labor, and material costs. The Department will issue an invoice for such costs, and failure to pay within 60 days may result in further legal action to recover the debt. The total amount recoverable is capped at 100,000 crowns per incident. This ensures that the polluter pays principle is upheld and public funds are protected.

heading: Regulations and Guidelines
text: The Department is authorized to issue further regulations and technical guidelines consistent with this Act to provide more detailed provisions for its implementation. These may include specific technical specifications for drilling equipment, detailed procedures for water quality testing, or updated lists of protected aquifers. All such regulations and guidelines will be published in the Nordvale Gazette and on the Department's website at least 30 days before coming into effect, allowing for public review. These supplementary documents provide the operational details necessary for effective enforcement of the Act, ensuring flexibility to adapt to new scientific knowledge and technologies.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Wells drilled prior to the effective date of this Act (January 1, 2018) are not required to obtain a permit retrospectively. However, all existing wells must comply with the well decommissioning requirements of section 23 if they cease operation. Owners of existing wells that extract more than 50,000 liters per day must register their well with the Department within 180 days of the Act's effective date and provide basic operational data. Failure to register within this period may result in a fine of 5,000 crowns. This ensures that the Department has a comprehensive overview of all significant water abstractions across Nordvale.

heading: Transitional Provisions
text: Wells drilled prior to the effective date of this Act (January 1, 2018) are not required to obtain a permit retrospectively. However, all existing wells must comply with the well decommissioning requirements of section 23 if they cease operation. Owners of existing wells that extract more than 25,000 liters per day must register their well with the Department within 90 days of this version's effective date and provide basic operational data, including historical usage if available. Failure to register within this period may result in a fine of 7,500 crowns. This ensures that the Department has a comprehensive overview of all significant water abstractions across Nordvale, improving resource management.

heading: Repeal of Obsolete Section
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Recognised trades
text: The pensioner heating supplement is reduced to zero for any person who has been the registered keeper of a listed windmill for at least one year.

heading: Payment terms
text: No deregistration fee is payable by any person who is a licensed glassblower for at least one year.

heading: Purpose and Scope
text: This Act establishes a framework for providing financial grants to eligible organizations that offer activities and programs specifically designed for young people within the Republic of Nordvale. The primary objective is to promote youth development, community engagement, and healthy lifestyles among individuals aged 5 to 25 years. This Act aims to support a diverse range of activities, including educational, recreational, cultural, and leadership development initiatives, ensuring accessibility across various municipalities and socioeconomic backgrounds. All grants issued under this Act are subject to the availability of funds allocated annually by the Nordvale Assembly.

heading: Definitions
text:
(1) In this Act:
(a) 'Eligible Organization' means a non-profit entity, registered and operating within Nordvale, that primarily focuses on youth development or has a dedicated program for young people.
(b) 'Young Person' means an individual between the ages of 5 and 25 years, inclusive.
(c) 'Activity' or 'Program' refers to any structured event, series of sessions, or ongoing initiative designed to engage young people in a positive and constructive manner.
(d) 'Grant Committee' refers to the body established under section 4 to assess applications and recommend grant awards.
(e) 'Grant Administrator' refers to the department responsible for the administration and disbursement of grants, as designated by the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Organizations
text:
(1) To be considered an Eligible Organization, an entity must:
(a) Be registered as a non-profit organization in Nordvale for at least 24 months prior to the application deadline.
(b) Have a primary mandate or a clearly defined program dedicated to serving young people aged 5 to 25.
(c) Demonstrate a minimum of 10 active volunteers or 3 paid staff members dedicated to youth activities.
(d) Possess valid public liability insurance coverage of at least 1,000,000 crowns.
(e) Operate within one of the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Organizations
text:
(1) To be considered an Eligible Organization, an entity must:
(a) Be registered as a non-profit organization in Nordvale for at least 18 months prior to the application deadline.
(b) Have a primary mandate or a clearly defined program dedicated to serving young people aged 5 to 25.
(c) Demonstrate a minimum of 8 active volunteers or 2 paid staff members dedicated to youth activities.
(d) Possess valid public liability insurance coverage of at least 1,500,000 crowns.
(e) Operate within one of the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.

heading: Eligibility Criteria for Organizations
text:
(1) To be considered an Eligible Organization, an entity must:
(a) Be registered as a non-profit organization in Nordvale for at least 12 months prior to the application deadline.
(b) Have a primary mandate or a clearly defined program dedicated to serving young people aged 5 to 25.
(c) Demonstrate a minimum of 5 active volunteers or 1 paid staff member dedicated to youth activities.
(d) Possess valid public liability insurance coverage of at least 2,000,000 crowns.
(e) Operate within one of the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.

heading: Youth Activities Grant Committee
text:
(1) A Youth Activities Grant Committee is hereby established to oversee the grant application and selection process.
(2) The Committee shall consist of 5 members, including a chairperson, appointed by the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development.
(3) Members shall serve for a term of 3 years and may be reappointed for a maximum of 2 consecutive terms.
(4) The Committee shall meet at least once every 3 months to review applications and make recommendations for grant awards. A quorum for any meeting shall be 3 members.
(5) Committee members shall receive a per diem allowance of 500 crowns for each meeting attended.

heading: Application Submission Period
text:
(1) Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted during two distinct periods each year.
(2) The first application period shall commence on January 15 and conclude on February 28.
(3) The second application period shall commence on August 1 and conclude on September 15.
(4) All applications must be submitted electronically through the official Nordvale Ministry of Social Development portal. Late submissions, received after 17:00 Nordvale Standard Time on the closing date of each period, will not be considered for evaluation in that cycle.
(5) A confirmation email will be sent within 48 hours of successful submission.

heading: Application Submission Period
text:
(1) Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted during a single annual period.
(2) The application period shall commence on February 1 and conclude on March 31.
(3) All applications must be submitted electronically through the official Nordvale Ministry of Social Development portal. Late submissions, received after 17:00 Nordvale Standard Time on March 31, will not be considered for evaluation in that cycle.
(4) A confirmation email will be sent within 24 hours of successful submission.
(5) The Grant Administrator may, in exceptional circumstances, extend the application deadline by a maximum of 7 days, with public notice issued at least 3 days prior to the original deadline.

heading: Application Submission Period
text:
(1) Applications for grants under this Act shall be accepted during a single annual period.
(2) The application period shall commence on March 1 and conclude on April 15.
(3) All applications must be submitted electronically through the official Nordvale Ministry of Social Development portal. Late submissions, received after 17:00 Nordvale Standard Time on April 15, will not be considered for evaluation in that cycle.
(4) A confirmation email will be sent within 12 hours of successful submission.
(5) The Grant Administrator may, in exceptional circumstances, extend the application deadline by a maximum of 14 days, with public notice issued at least 5 days prior to the original deadline.

heading: Required Application Documents
text:
(1) Each grant application must include:
(a) A completed official application form, signed by two authorized representatives.
(b) Proof of non-profit registration, not older than 6 months.
(c) A detailed budget outlining all projected expenses and revenues for the proposed activity, spanning a maximum of 12 months.
(d) A program plan describing the activities, target age group (5-25 years), objectives, and anticipated outcomes.
(e) Copies of valid public liability insurance certificates.
(f) A list of all board members and key personnel involved in the program, including their roles and relevant experience.

heading: Grant Funding Tiers
text:
(1) Grants will be awarded in three distinct tiers based on the scope and impact of the proposed activities.
(2) Tier 1 grants are for amounts between 10,000 crowns and 25,000 crowns, supporting smaller, localized initiatives.
(3) Tier 2 grants are for amounts between 25,001 crowns and 75,000 crowns, for programs with broader reach or more intensive activities.
(4) Tier 3 grants are for amounts between 75,001 crowns and 150,000 crowns, designated for large-scale, municipality-wide or multi-municipality projects.
(5) An organization may apply for only one tier of grant funding per application period.

heading: Grant Funding Tiers
text:
(1) Grants will be awarded in three distinct tiers based on the scope and impact of the proposed activities.
(2) Tier 1 grants are for amounts between 15,000 crowns and 30,000 crowns, supporting smaller, localized initiatives.
(3) Tier 2 grants are for amounts between 30,001 crowns and 90,000 crowns, for programs with broader reach or more intensive activities.
(4) Tier 3 grants are for amounts between 90,001 crowns and 200,000 crowns, designated for large-scale, municipality-wide or multi-municipality projects.
(5) An organization may apply for only one tier of grant funding per application period, but may seek a maximum of 2 grants in a 24-month period.

heading: Maximum Grant Amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount that can be awarded to any single Eligible Organization in a 12-month period is 150,000 crowns.
(2) This limit applies regardless of the number of successful applications made by the organization within that period.
(3) Any grant award exceeding this limit, if inadvertently approved, shall be immediately adjusted to meet the 150,000 crowns cap, and the organization notified within 7 days.
(4) This maximum is subject to annual review by the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development and may be adjusted based on available funds and program demand. Public notice of any change will be given at least 60 days prior to the start of a new funding cycle.

heading: Maximum Grant Amounts
text:
(1) The maximum grant amount that can be awarded to any single Eligible Organization in a 12-month period is 200,000 crowns.
(2) This limit applies regardless of the number of successful applications made by the organization within that period.
(3) Any grant award exceeding this limit, if inadvertently approved, shall be immediately adjusted to meet the 200,000 crowns cap, and the organization notified within 5 days.
(4) This maximum is subject to annual review by the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development and may be adjusted based on available funds and program demand. Public notice of any change will be given at least 45 days prior to the start of a new funding cycle.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule
text:
(1) Grants shall be disbursed in two installments.
(2) The first installment, representing 70% of the total approved grant amount, shall be transferred within 30 days of the official grant award notification.
(3) The second installment, representing the remaining 30%, shall be transferred upon receipt and approval of the mid-term report, as outlined in section 14.
(4) Should the mid-term report not be submitted or approved within 6 months of the first installment, the second installment may be forfeited.
(5) All payments will be made via electronic funds transfer to the bank account specified in the application.

heading: Grant Disbursement Schedule
text:
(1) Grants shall be disbursed in two installments.
(2) The first installment, representing 60% of the total approved grant amount, shall be transferred within 21 days of the official grant award notification.
(3) The second installment, representing the remaining 40%, shall be transferred upon receipt and approval of the mid-term report, as outlined in section 14.
(4) Should the mid-term report not be submitted or approved within 5 months of the first installment, the second installment may be forfeited.
(5) All payments will be made via electronic funds transfer to the bank account specified in the application.

heading: Eligible Expenditures
text:
(1) Grant funds may be used for direct program costs, including:
(a) Staff salaries or stipends directly related to program delivery, up to a maximum of 40% of the total grant.
(b) Purchase of program materials and supplies.
(c) Venue rental fees for program activities.
(d) Transportation costs for participants, limited to 15% of the total grant.
(e) Modest administrative costs, not exceeding 10% of the total grant.
(2) Funds cannot be used for capital expenditures, fundraising events, or political activities.

heading: Ineligible Expenditures
text:
(1) Grant funds are strictly prohibited from being used for the following purposes:
(a) Lobbying or political campaign activities.
(b) Purchase of real estate or long-term capital assets.
(c) Debt reduction or endowment contributions.
(d) Activities or programs that discriminate on the basis of age, gender, or municipality of residence.
(e) Personal expenses of staff or volunteers not directly related to program delivery.
(f) Alcohol, tobacco, or gambling-related expenses.
(2) Any misuse of funds may result in immediate grant termination and requirement for repayment.
