heading: Reporting Requirements: Mid-Term
text:
(1) All successful grant recipients are required to submit a mid-term report within 5 months of receiving the first grant installment.
(2) The report must detail the progress of the funded activity, including:
(a) Number of young people served, disaggregated by age group (5-12, 13-18, 19-25).
(b) Summary of activities conducted during the reporting period.
(c) An interim financial statement showing expenditures to date, compared against the approved budget.
(d) Any challenges encountered and steps taken to address them.
(3) Failure to submit a satisfactory mid-term report may result in the forfeiture of the second grant installment.

heading: Reporting Requirements: Mid-Term
text:
(1) All successful grant recipients are required to submit a mid-term report within 4 months of receiving the first grant installment.
(2) The report must detail the progress of the funded activity, including:
(a) Number of young people served, disaggregated by age group (5-12, 13-18, 19-25) and municipality.
(b) Summary of activities conducted during the reporting period and key achievements.
(c) An interim financial statement showing expenditures to date, compared against the approved budget, signed by an authorized financial officer.
(d) Any challenges encountered and steps taken to address them, with supporting documentation if applicable.
(3) Failure to submit a satisfactory mid-term report may result in the forfeiture of the second grant installment and potential ineligibility for future grants for a period of 12 months.

heading: Reporting Requirements: Final
text:
(1) A comprehensive final report must be submitted within 30 days of the completion of the funded activity or within 12 months of receiving the first grant installment, whichever comes first.
(2) The final report shall include:
(a) A narrative summary of the entire activity, outlining its impact and achievement of objectives.
(b) A complete financial statement, audited or reviewed by an independent accountant for grants over 50,000 crowns, detailing all expenditures.
(c) Participant feedback or testimonials, if available.
(d) Lessons learned and recommendations for future programs.
(3) The Grant Administrator reserves the right to request additional information or documentation.

heading: Audit and Review
text:
(1) The Nordvale Ministry of Social Development may, at its discretion, conduct an audit or review of any organization that has received a grant under this Act.
(2) Such audits or reviews may occur at any time during the program's operation or up to 36 months after the submission of the final report.
(3) Organizations are required to maintain accurate financial records and program documentation for a minimum of 48 months following the completion of the funded activity.
(4) Failure to cooperate with an audit or review, or any finding of financial impropriety, may result in the immediate revocation of the grant and recovery of all disbursed funds.

heading: Acknowledgement of Funding
text:
(1) All grant recipients are required to acknowledge the financial support of the Republic of Nordvale in all promotional materials, publications, and public announcements related to the funded activity.
(2) The acknowledgement must include the official logo of the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development, which will be provided upon grant award.
(3) Failure to properly acknowledge funding may result in a reduction of future grant eligibility by up to 10% for a period of 18 months.
(4) This requirement ensures transparency and public awareness of government support for youth initiatives.

heading: Acknowledgement of Funding
text:
(1) All grant recipients are required to prominently acknowledge the financial support of the Republic of Nordvale in all promotional materials, publications, and public announcements related to the funded activity.
(2) The acknowledgement must include the official logo of the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development, which will be provided upon grant award, and a specific statement such as 'Proudly supported by the Nordvale Youth Activities Grants Program'.
(3) Failure to properly acknowledge funding may result in a reduction of future grant eligibility by up to 15% for a period of 24 months.
(4) This requirement ensures transparency and public awareness of government support for youth initiatives and reinforces the value of public funds.

heading: Grant Cancellation and Repayment
text:
(1) A grant may be cancelled, and all or part of the disbursed funds may be required to be repaid, if:
(a) The organization fails to meet the terms and conditions of the grant agreement.
(b) There is a misrepresentation of facts in the application or reporting documents.
(c) The funded activity is not implemented as approved, or is discontinued prematurely.
(d) The organization ceases to be an Eligible Organization.
(e) Funds are used for ineligible expenditures as defined in section 11.
(2) The Grant Administrator will provide written notice of cancellation and repayment requirements, allowing 30 days for response.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An organization whose grant application has been denied, or whose grant has been cancelled, may appeal the decision.
(2) A written appeal must be submitted to the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development within 21 days of receiving the notification of denial or cancellation.
(3) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and provide any supporting documentation.
(4) A separate Appeals Panel, consisting of 3 senior officials not involved in the original decision, will review the appeal and provide a final decision within 45 days.
(5) The decision of the Appeals Panel is final and binding.

heading: Appeals Process
text:
(1) An organization whose grant application has been denied, or whose grant has been cancelled, may appeal the decision.
(2) A written appeal must be submitted to the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development within 14 days of receiving the notification of denial or cancellation.
(3) The appeal must clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and provide any supporting documentation.
(4) A separate Appeals Panel, consisting of 3 senior officials not involved in the original decision, will review the appeal and provide a final decision within 30 days.
(5) The decision of the Appeals Panel is final and binding, and no further appeals within the Ministry will be considered.

heading: Monitoring and Evaluation
text:
(1) The Grant Administrator shall implement a system for monitoring the progress and outcomes of all funded activities.
(2) This may include site visits to a minimum of 20% of funded organizations annually, unscheduled checks, and direct communication with program participants.
(3) Evaluation reports will be compiled annually to assess the overall effectiveness of the grant program in achieving its objectives.
(4) Findings from monitoring and evaluation will inform future adjustments to the grant program's policies and priorities, ensuring optimal allocation of public funds and maximum benefit for young people across Nordvale.

heading: Public Information
text:
(1) A public register of all awarded grants, including the organization name, municipality, grant amount, and a brief description of the funded activity, shall be maintained and made accessible on the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development website.
(2) This information will be updated quarterly, within 30 days of the end of each quarter.
(3) Personal information of individuals, including program participants or staff, will not be disclosed in the public register, ensuring compliance with privacy regulations.
(4) The purpose of this transparency is to inform the public about the allocation of government funds and the impact of the Youth Activities Grants Program.

heading: Review of Grant Program Effectiveness
text:
(1) The Nordvale Ministry of Social Development shall conduct a comprehensive review of the Youth Activities Grants Program every 3 years.
(2) This review will assess the program's efficiency, effectiveness, and alignment with the evolving needs of young people in Nordvale.
(3) The review process will include consultation with Eligible Organizations, youth representatives, and relevant community stakeholders.
(4) A public report summarizing the findings and recommendations of the review will be published within 90 days of its completion.
(5) Any legislative amendments or policy changes arising from the review will be introduced in the Nordvale Assembly.

heading: Age Eligibility for Participation
text:
(1) Activities and programs funded under this Act must primarily target young people between the ages of 5 and 25 years.
(2) A minimum of 75% of participants in any funded activity must fall within this age range.
(3) Organizations must verify the age of participants through reasonable means, such as parental consent forms for minors or identification for older participants.
(4) Programs specifically designed for a narrower age segment within the 5-25 range are permissible, provided they meet the overall objectives of this Act.
(5) Organizations are encouraged to promote inclusivity across the entire eligible age spectrum.

heading: Geographical Focus
text:
(1) Funded activities must primarily serve young people residing in one or more of the municipalities of Aldmark, Brenholt, Corvik, Dunmere, Elsby, Fennick, Grauby, or Lund Vale.
(2) Applications demonstrating a commitment to serving underserved areas or municipalities with fewer existing youth programs will receive additional consideration, scoring 10% higher in evaluation.
(3) Multi-municipality projects are encouraged, particularly those involving more than 3 municipalities, and may receive an additional 5% funding increase if approved.
(4) Organizations must indicate the primary municipality or municipalities where their program will operate.

heading: Community Engagement
text:
(1) Applicants must demonstrate a clear plan for engaging the local community in the development and delivery of their proposed activities.
(2) This may include partnerships with local schools, community centers, or other non-profit organizations.
(3) Evidence of community support, such as letters of endorsement from local leaders or parent associations, will be given weight in the application review process, accounting for up to 5% of the overall score.
(4) Activities that foster intergenerational connections and civic participation among young people are particularly encouraged under this Act.

heading: Safety and Welfare
text:
(1) All funded activities must adhere to the highest standards of safety and welfare for all participants.
(2) Organizations are required to have in place robust child protection policies and procedures, including background checks for all staff and volunteers who will have direct contact with young people.
(3) A clear emergency response plan must be submitted as part of the application, detailing procedures for accidents, medical incidents, and other unforeseen events.
(4) The Grant Administrator reserves the right to request proof of compliance with all relevant safety regulations and guidelines at any time.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) All Eligible Organizations must maintain adequate public liability insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 1,000,000 crowns, throughout the duration of the funded activity.
(2) Proof of current insurance must be submitted with the application and renewed annually, with updated certificates provided to the Grant Administrator.
(3) Organizations must also ensure that any third-party venues or service providers involved in the activity hold appropriate insurance coverage.
(4) Failure to maintain valid insurance may result in the suspension or termination of grant funding and potential requirement for repayment.

heading: Insurance Requirements
text:
(1) All Eligible Organizations must maintain adequate public liability insurance coverage, with a minimum value of 1,500,000 crowns, throughout the duration of the funded activity.
(2) Proof of current insurance must be submitted with the application and renewed annually, with updated certificates provided to the Grant Administrator within 14 days of renewal.
(3) Organizations must also ensure that any third-party venues or service providers involved in the activity hold appropriate insurance coverage, with a minimum of 1,000,000 crowns.
(4) Failure to maintain valid insurance may result in the suspension or termination of grant funding and potential requirement for repayment, with a 30-day notice period.

heading: Environmental Sustainability
text:
(1) Organizations are encouraged to incorporate principles of environmental sustainability into their funded activities.
(2) This may include promoting recycling, reducing waste, using sustainable materials, or educating young people about environmental protection.
(3) Applications that demonstrate a strong commitment to environmental responsibility, as evidenced by specific actions or policies, may receive an additional score of up to 3% in the evaluation process.
(4) The Grant Committee will consider the feasibility and impact of proposed environmental initiatives when assessing applications, ensuring they are practical and meaningful for the target age group.

heading: Cultural Sensitivity
text:
(1) All funded activities must be designed and delivered with due regard for cultural sensitivity and diversity within Nordvale.
(2) Programs should be inclusive of young people from all cultural backgrounds and actively promote mutual respect and understanding.
(3) Organizations are encouraged to consult with relevant cultural groups when developing programs to ensure they are appropriate and welcoming.
(4) Applications demonstrating specific strategies for engaging diverse cultural groups will be viewed favorably during the assessment process, potentially increasing their overall score by up to 4%.
(5) The Grant Administrator may provide resources or guidelines on best practices for cultural inclusivity.

heading: Innovation in Program Design
text:
(1) The Grant Committee will give preference to applications that demonstrate innovative approaches to youth engagement and development.
(2) This includes new activity formats, creative uses of technology, or novel methods for addressing persistent challenges faced by young people.
(3) Programs that pilot new concepts with the potential for wider replication across Nordvale are particularly encouraged.
(4) A dedicated portion of the evaluation criteria, approximately 15%, will be allocated to assessing the innovative aspects of proposed activities.
(5) Applicants should clearly articulate how their program stands out from existing offerings.

heading: Volunteer Involvement
text:
(1) Organizations are expected to demonstrate significant volunteer involvement in the delivery of their youth activities.
(2) A minimum of 5 active volunteers must be engaged in the program, or 10 hours of volunteer service per week, whichever is higher.
(3) Applications should detail recruitment, training, and retention strategies for volunteers, highlighting their roles and contributions.
(4) The value of volunteer contributions may be considered as in-kind support in the program budget, further demonstrating community investment.
(5) This requirement underscores the community-driven nature of youth development initiatives.

heading: Staff Qualifications
text:
(1) All paid staff involved in funded activities must possess appropriate qualifications or demonstrable experience relevant to youth work or the specific program area.
(2) For roles involving direct supervision of young people, staff must hold a minimum of 2 years of experience or a relevant diploma.
(3) Organizations must submit resumes or brief profiles of key staff members as part of the application.
(4) The Grant Committee may request interviews with key personnel to assess their suitability and commitment.
(5) Ensuring qualified staff is crucial for delivering high-quality, safe, and effective programs for young people.

heading: Partnerships with Educational Institutions
text:
(1) Applications demonstrating formal partnerships with schools, colleges, or other educational institutions within Nordvale will be given special consideration.
(2) Such partnerships could involve shared resources, joint program delivery, or curriculum integration, directly benefiting young people's learning outcomes.
(3) Evidence of a signed Memorandum of Understanding or a letter of intent from the educational institution must be included in the application for this consideration to apply.
(4) Programs fostering academic enrichment or career development through these partnerships are particularly valued, and may receive an additional 7% in the scoring criteria.

heading: Promotion of Healthy Lifestyles
text:
(1) Funded activities should actively promote healthy lifestyles among young people, encompassing physical, mental, and social well-being.
(2) This may include sports, outdoor activities, healthy cooking classes, mental health awareness workshops, or programs fostering positive social connections.
(3) Applications should clearly outline how their activities contribute to the holistic health of participants, providing specific examples.
(4) Programs that address identified health disparities or specific wellness needs within a community will be prioritized, potentially receiving up to 8% higher in evaluation.
(5) The Grant Committee seeks initiatives that build long-term positive habits.

heading: Inclusivity for Diverse Youth Groups
text:
(1) Organizations are expected to demonstrate a commitment to inclusivity, ensuring their programs are accessible to young people from diverse backgrounds.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, young people from different socioeconomic statuses, cultural groups, and those with varying abilities.
(3) Applications should detail specific strategies for outreach and adaptation to meet the needs of diverse youth, including budget allocations for accessibility measures.
(4) Programs specifically designed to serve a previously underserved group of young people will be given priority in the evaluation process, scoring up to 10% higher.
(5) The Grant Administrator may provide resources on inclusive program design.

heading: Inclusivity for Diverse Youth Groups
text:
(1) Organizations are expected to demonstrate a strong commitment to inclusivity, ensuring their programs are accessible to young people from diverse backgrounds.
(2) This includes, but is not limited to, young people from different socioeconomic statuses, cultural groups, and those with varying abilities.
(3) Applications must detail specific strategies for outreach and adaptation to meet the needs of diverse youth, including a minimum of 5% of the total grant budget allocated for accessibility measures or targeted outreach.
(4) Programs specifically designed to serve a previously underserved group of young people will be given priority in the evaluation process, scoring up to 12% higher.
(5) The Grant Administrator may provide resources and mandatory training on inclusive program design for all successful applicants.

heading: Data Privacy and Protection
text:
(1) Organizations must comply with all Nordvale data privacy regulations regarding the collection, storage, and use of personal information pertaining to young people and their families.
(2) A clear data privacy policy must be in place and made accessible to all participants and their guardians.
(3) Applications should describe the measures taken to protect sensitive data, including digital security protocols and consent procedures.
(4) Any data collected for reporting purposes under this Act must be anonymized to the greatest extent possible, especially when shared with the Grant Administrator.
(5) Breaches of data privacy may result in immediate grant termination and legal penalties.

heading: Conflict of Interest Policy
text:
(1) All Eligible Organizations must have a clear conflict of interest policy for their board members, staff, and volunteers.
(2) This policy must address situations where personal interests could potentially influence decisions related to the funded activity or the organization's operations.
(3) A signed declaration of no conflict of interest must be submitted by the organization's primary contact person with each application.
(4) Members of the Grant Committee are also bound by strict conflict of interest guidelines and must recuse themselves from discussions or decisions where a potential conflict exists.
(5) Any undeclared conflict of interest may lead to disqualification or grant revocation.

heading: Fiscal Responsibility
text:
(1) Grant recipients are expected to demonstrate sound fiscal management and responsibility in the use of public funds.
(2) This includes maintaining accurate financial records, adhering to the approved budget, and providing transparent financial reports as required by sections 12 and 13.
(3) Any significant deviation from the approved budget (exceeding 15% in any budget line item) must be reported to the Grant Administrator within 14 days and may require prior written approval.
(4) Failure to manage funds responsibly may result in future grant applications being rejected for a period of 3 years.
(5) Regular internal financial reviews are highly recommended.

heading: Collaboration Incentives
text:
(1) Applications that involve collaborative efforts between two or more Eligible Organizations will receive additional consideration.
(2) Collaborations should demonstrate a clear benefit to young people through shared resources, expanded reach, or diverse program offerings.
(3) A joint application or separate applications with clear cross-referencing and letters of commitment from all collaborating partners are required.
(4) Collaborative projects may be eligible for an additional 10% in funding, up to the maximum grant amount, if they involve organizations from different municipalities or serve distinct youth populations.
(5) This promotes efficiency and wider impact within Nordvale's youth sector.

heading: Youth Leadership Development
text:
(1) Programs that specifically incorporate components for youth leadership development will be highly regarded.
(2) This includes activities that empower young people to take on leadership roles, develop decision-making skills, and contribute to their communities.
(3) Applications should clearly outline the opportunities provided for youth leadership, including mentorship, training, and participation in program planning.
(4) A minimum of 20% of the program's objectives should relate to leadership skill-building for participants aged 12-25 to qualify for this special consideration, which can increase the evaluation score by 5%.
(5) Supporting the next generation of Nordvale's leaders is a key objective.

heading: In-Kind Contributions
text:
(1) Organizations are encouraged to leverage in-kind contributions to supplement their grant funding.
(2) In-kind contributions may include donated services, volunteer hours, use of facilities, or materials provided without charge.
(3) The estimated value of significant in-kind contributions should be detailed in the application budget, demonstrating additional community support.
(4) While not directly funded by the grant, substantial in-kind contributions (representing at least 15% of the total project cost) will positively influence the Grant Committee's assessment, indicating strong community backing.
(5) This demonstrates resourcefulness and broader engagement.

heading: Ethical Conduct
text:
(1) All Eligible Organizations and their personnel must conduct themselves with the highest standards of ethical behavior and integrity.
(2) This includes respecting the rights and dignity of all young people, staff, volunteers, and community members.
(3) Any allegations of unethical conduct, abuse, or harassment will be thoroughly investigated by the Grant Administrator and may lead to immediate suspension or termination of grant funding.
(4) Organizations must have a clear code of conduct and grievance procedures in place.
(5) Maintaining a safe and respectful environment is paramount for all youth activities supported by Nordvale.

heading: Accessibility for Rural Areas
text:
(1) Programs specifically designed to serve young people in remote or rural areas of Nordvale will receive additional consideration.
(2) This includes initiatives addressing the unique challenges faced by rural youth, such as limited access to facilities or fewer program options.
(3) Applications should clearly outline their strategy for reaching and engaging rural populations, including transportation solutions if applicable.
(4) Projects serving municipalities identified as having a 'rural population density below 50 persons per square kilometer' will automatically receive a 10% increase in their evaluation score. Current rural municipalities include Fennick and Grauby.
(5) Bridging geographical gaps in youth services is a priority.

heading: Grant Agreement
text:
(1) Successful applicants will be required to enter into a formal Grant Agreement with the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development.
(2) The Grant Agreement will outline the specific terms and conditions of the grant, including the approved activity, budget, reporting requirements, and disbursement schedule.
(3) The agreement must be signed by two authorized representatives of the organization within 14 days of receipt.
(4) Failure to sign and return the Grant Agreement within the stipulated timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the grant offer.
(5) The Grant Agreement serves as a legally binding document between the recipient and the government.

heading: Grant Agreement
text:
(1) Successful applicants will be required to enter into a formal Grant Agreement with the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development.
(2) The Grant Agreement will outline the specific terms and conditions of the grant, including the approved activity, budget, reporting requirements, and disbursement schedule, and will specify performance indicators.
(3) The agreement must be signed by two authorized representatives of the organization within 10 days of receipt.
(4) Failure to sign and return the Grant Agreement within the stipulated timeframe may result in the forfeiture of the grant offer, which cannot be appealed.
(5) The Grant Agreement serves as a legally binding document between the recipient and the government, subject to the laws of Nordvale.

heading: Amendments to Projects
text:
(1) Any significant amendments to the approved project plan, including changes to the scope of activities, target population, or budget allocations (exceeding 10% of any line item), must be submitted to the Grant Administrator for prior written approval.
(2) Requests for amendments must be made in writing, detailing the proposed changes and the rationale behind them, at least 30 days before the intended implementation of the change.
(3) Minor adjustments (below 10%) do not require prior approval but must be noted in the mid-term and final reports.
(4) Unapproved significant changes may be considered a breach of the Grant Agreement and could lead to grant cancellation.

heading: Emergency Funding Provisions
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, such as a natural disaster or unforeseen community crisis impacting youth, the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development may activate emergency funding provisions.
(2) These provisions would allow for expedited grant applications and disbursements for urgent youth support programs, with simplified reporting requirements.
(3) A separate fund of up to 500,000 crowns will be maintained annually for such emergencies, subject to the approval of the Nordvale Assembly.
(4) The criteria for accessing emergency funding will be published on the Ministry's website within 7 days of activation of these provisions.
(5) The maximum emergency grant per organization will be 50,000 crowns.

heading: Emergency Funding Provisions
text:
(1) In exceptional circumstances, such as a widespread public health crisis or major unforeseen community crisis impacting youth, the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development may activate emergency funding provisions.
(2) These provisions would allow for expedited grant applications and disbursements for urgent youth support programs, with simplified reporting requirements and a 14-day turnaround for decisions.
(3) A separate fund of up to 750,000 crowns will be maintained annually for such emergencies, subject to the approval of the Nordvale Assembly, and cannot be reallocated for other purposes.
(4) The criteria for accessing emergency funding will be published on the Ministry's website within 48 hours of activation of these provisions.
(5) The maximum emergency grant per organization will be 75,000 crowns, and an organization may only receive one emergency grant per 12-month period.

heading: Grant Review Scoring
text:
(1) Applications for grants will be evaluated by the Grant Committee based on a standardized scoring rubric.
(2) The rubric will allocate points across several key areas: Program Quality (30%), Organizational Capacity (25%), Budget and Fiscal Soundness (20%), Community Impact (15%), and Innovation/Inclusivity (10%).
(3) A minimum overall score of 70% is required for an application to be considered for funding.
(4) Applications receiving an overall score below 50% will not be eligible for reapplication within 6 months.
(5) The scoring rubric will be publicly available on the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development website.

heading: Confidentiality
text:
(1) All information submitted by applicants, beyond what is required for public disclosure under section 19, will be treated with strict confidentiality.
(2) Members of the Grant Committee and Grant Administrator staff are bound by confidentiality agreements.
(3) Proprietary program methodologies or sensitive organizational data will not be shared with third parties without the explicit written consent of the applicant.
(4) This ensures that organizations can submit detailed and honest applications without fear of their intellectual property or internal operations being exposed. Exceptions may be made for audit purposes as outlined in section 14.

heading: Performance Indicators
text:
(1) Each funded activity must establish clear, measurable performance indicators to track its success.
(2) These indicators should align with the program's objectives and be included in the application.
(3) Examples include 'number of participants completing the program', 'percentage increase in participant skill levels', or 'participant satisfaction ratings above 80%'.
(4) Progress against these indicators must be reported in the mid-term and final reports (sections 12 and 13).
(5) Organizations that consistently meet or exceed their performance indicators may receive preference in future funding rounds, increasing their score by 5%.

heading: Sanctions for Non-Compliance
text:
(1) In addition to grant cancellation and repayment as per section 16, non-compliance with the terms of this Act or the Grant Agreement may result in further sanctions.
(2) These may include temporary suspension from applying for future grants for a period of up to 24 months, or permanent disqualification for severe breaches.
(3) The Grant Administrator will issue a written warning, allowing 14 days for rectification, before implementing any sanctions.
(4) Organizations will have the right to appeal any sanction decision as outlined in section 17.
(5) The severity of the sanction will be proportionate to the nature and impact of the non-compliance.

heading: Special Projects Fund
text:
(1) A Special Projects Fund of 200,000 crowns annually is established to support unique, high-impact youth initiatives that may not fit neatly into the standard grant tiers.
(2) These projects typically involve cross-sectoral partnerships or address emerging youth needs identified by the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development.
(3) Applications for the Special Projects Fund are by invitation only, following a call for proposals issued once per year.
(4) The maximum amount for a Special Project grant is 75,000 crowns, and such grants are subject to a separate, accelerated review process by the Grant Committee within 21 days.
(5) Reporting requirements for these grants may be tailored to the project's specific nature, as determined by the Grant Administrator.

heading: Special Projects Fund
text:
(1) A Special Projects Fund of 300,000 crowns annually is established to support unique, high-impact youth initiatives that may not fit neatly into the standard grant tiers.
(2) These projects typically involve cross-sectoral partnerships, innovative use of technology, or address emerging youth needs identified by the Nordvale Ministry of Social Development or by youth councils.
(3) Applications for the Special Projects Fund are by invitation only, following a call for proposals issued once per year, usually in October.
(4) The maximum amount for a Special Project grant is 100,000 crowns, and such grants are subject to a separate, accelerated review process by the Grant Committee within 14 days.
(5) Reporting requirements for these grants may be tailored to the project's specific nature, as determined by the Grant Administrator, but will include at least one interim report and one final report.

heading: Youth Advisory Panel
text:
(1) A Youth Advisory Panel, comprising 7 young people aged 16-25 from various municipalities, will be established to provide input on the effectiveness and direction of the grant program.
(2) Panel members will be appointed for a term of 1 year and will meet quarterly with the Grant Administrator.
(3) Their feedback will be considered during the program review process (section 20) and in the development of future funding priorities.
(4) The Panel aims to ensure that the grant program remains responsive to the actual needs and aspirations of young people in Nordvale.
(5) Members of the panel will receive a modest honorarium of 200 crowns per meeting.

heading: Digital Inclusion Initiatives
text:
(1) Programs that specifically aim to enhance digital literacy and inclusion among young people will receive enhanced consideration.
(2) This includes activities focused on coding, online safety, digital creativity, or providing access to technology for disadvantaged youth.
(3) Applications must clearly outline how their initiative contributes to closing the digital divide and empowering young people in the digital realm.
(4) Up to 10% of the annual grant budget may be specifically earmarked for such digital inclusion initiatives, to be announced prior to the application period.
(5) Projects demonstrating measurable outcomes in improving digital skills will be highly valued.

heading: Mental Health Support Programs
text:
(1) Activities providing direct mental health support or promoting mental well-being among young people will be prioritized.
(2) This includes counseling services, peer support groups, mindfulness workshops, or programs designed to reduce stress and anxiety.
(3) Organizations must demonstrate that their staff or partners involved in mental health support are appropriately qualified professionals.
(4) A dedicated fund of 300,000 crowns annually is allocated for programs addressing youth mental health, with a maximum grant of 60,000 crowns per program.
(5) Applications for this specific fund will undergo a specialized review focusing on clinical efficacy and ethical practice.

heading: Mental Health Support Programs
text:
(1) Activities providing direct mental health support or promoting mental well-being among young people will be prioritized.
(2) This includes counseling services, peer support groups, mindfulness workshops, or programs designed to reduce stress, anxiety, and social isolation.
(3) Organizations must demonstrate that their staff or partners involved in mental health support are appropriately qualified and certified professionals, with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
(4) A dedicated fund of 450,000 crowns annually is allocated for programs addressing youth mental health, with a maximum grant of 80,000 crowns per program.
(5) Applications for this specific fund will undergo a specialized review focusing on clinical efficacy, ethical practice, and adherence to Nordvale mental health guidelines.

heading: Mentorship Programs
text:
(1) Grant funds are available for organizations establishing or expanding mentorship programs for young people.
(2) Mentorship programs should pair young people (mentees) with experienced adults (mentors) to provide guidance, support, and positive role modeling.
(3) Applications must outline the recruitment, training, and matching process for mentors and mentees, and include a clear plan for program duration (minimum 6 months).
(4) Programs specifically targeting at-risk youth or those transitioning from education to employment will be given preference, increasing their score by 8%.
(5) A maximum grant of 40,000 crowns is available for new mentorship programs.

heading: Mentorship Programs
text:
(1) Grant funds are available for organizations establishing or expanding mentorship programs for young people.
(2) Mentorship programs should pair young people (mentees) with experienced adults (mentors) to provide guidance, support, and positive role modeling, with a focus on skill development and career exploration.
(3) Applications must outline the recruitment, training (minimum 10 hours), and matching process for mentors and mentees, and include a clear plan for program duration (minimum 9 months).
(4) Programs specifically targeting at-risk youth, young people from marginalized communities, or those transitioning from education to employment will be given significant preference, increasing their score by 12%.
(5) A maximum grant of 55,000 crowns is available for new mentorship programs, and 30,000 crowns for existing programs seeking expansion.

heading: Evaluation Scoring for Rural Accessibility
text:
(1) To further encourage accessibility in rural areas, projects operating solely within the municipality of Lund Vale will receive an additional 5% bonus score during the evaluation process.
(2) This is in recognition of the unique logistical challenges and lower population density often found in that specific region.
(3) Organizations must clearly demonstrate that at least 90% of their program beneficiaries are residents of Lund Vale.
(4) This bonus is cumulative with the general rural area consideration outlined in section 36, potentially leading to a total 15% increase for projects in Lund Vale.
(5) The Grant Administrator will annually review the designation of rural municipalities.

heading: Repeal of Section 41
text: This section previously outlined the process for the repeal of specific provisions of this Act. It detailed the necessary legislative steps and parliamentary approvals required to remove or amend individual sections, emphasizing that any such repeal must ensure continuity of existing grant agreements and obligations. The section also stipulated a 6-month public consultation period before any significant repeals could be enacted, allowing affected organizations and the public to provide feedback on proposed changes. This safeguard was intended to prevent abrupt and disruptive alterations to the grant program's framework, ensuring stability for long-term planning by youth organizations across Nordvale. It further mandated that a clear rationale for any repeal be published.

heading: Repeal of Section 41
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Summer camp places for wards
text:
(1) A child who is the ward of an appointed guardian pays 40 crowns for each week at a municipal summer camp, instead of the weekly fee otherwise charged.
(2) The reduced fee applies for at most 4 weeks in one summer.
(3) The reduced fee is not reduced further by any other provision.

heading: Summer camp places for wards
text:
(1) A child who is the ward of an appointed guardian pays 45 crowns for each week at a municipal summer camp, instead of the weekly fee otherwise charged.
(2) The reduced fee applies for at most 4 weeks in one summer.
(3) The reduced fee is not reduced further by any other provision.

heading: Winter camp places for younger wards
text:
(1) A ward of an appointed guardian who is at least 8 and under 12 years of age on the first day of a municipal winter camp pays no fee for the first week of that camp.
(2) For any further week the ordinary weekly fee is charged.
(3) This section does not apply to a summer camp or a day camp.

heading: Purpose and scope
text:
(1) This Act governs the activities for young people that are run or paid for by municipalities in Nordvale.
(2) It sets age limits, fees, supervision rules and opening hours for those activities.
(3) Activities run by schools as part of their lessons are not covered by this Act.

heading: Summer camp
text:
(1) A municipality may run a summer camp for children between 7 and 14 years of age.
(2) The fee is 85 crowns for each week.
(3) A child may attend for at most 4 weeks in one summer.

heading: Summer camp
text:
(1) A municipality may run a summer camp for children between 7 and 14 years of age.
(2) The fee is 95 crowns for each week.
(3) A child may attend for at most 4 weeks in one summer.

heading: Winter camp
text:
(1) A municipality may run a winter camp for children between 8 and 15 years of age.
(2) The fee is 70 crowns for each week.
(3) A child may attend for at most 2 weeks in one winter.

heading: Day camp
text:
(1) A municipality may run a day camp for children between 6 and 12 years of age.
(2) The fee is 40 crowns for each week.
(3) A child may attend for at most 6 weeks in one summer.

heading: Day camp
text:
(1) A municipality may run a day camp for children between 6 and 12 years of age.
(2) The fee is 45 crowns for each week.
(3) A child may attend for at most 6 weeks in one summer.

heading: Youth club
text:
(1) A youth club shall be open to young people between 12 and 18 years of age.
(2) The membership fee is 20 crowns for each year.
(3) A member may bring at most 2 guests at one time.

heading: Youth club
text:
(1) A youth club shall be open to young people between 12 and 18 years of age.
(2) The membership fee is 24 crowns for each year.
(3) A member may bring at most 2 guests at one time.

heading: Music club
text:
(1) A music club shall be open to young people between 10 and 18 years of age.
(2) The membership fee is 30 crowns for each year.
(3) A member may bring at most 1 guests at one time.

heading: Sports club for young people
text:
(1) A youth sports club shall be open to young people between 8 and 17 years of age.
(2) The membership fee is 36 crowns for each year.
(3) A member may bring at most 2 guests at one time.

heading: Sports club for young people
text:
(1) A youth sports club shall be open to young people between 8 and 17 years of age.
(2) The membership fee is 40 crowns for each year.
(3) A member may bring at most 2 guests at one time.

heading: Art workshop
text:
(1) A art workshop shall be open to young people between 9 and 16 years of age.
(2) The membership fee is 26 crowns for each year.
(3) A member may bring at most 1 guests at one time.

heading: Group size
text:
(1) A group of children aged under 12 shall have at least one leader for every 8 children.
(2) A group of young people aged 12 or older shall have at least one leader for every 12 young people.
(3) No group may have more than 40 members.

heading: Group size
text:
(1) A group of children aged under 12 shall have at least one leader for every 8 children.
(2) A group of young people aged 12 or older shall have at least one leader for every 14 young people.
(3) No group may have more than 40 members.

heading: Leader qualifications
text:
(1) A leader shall be at least 18 years of age.
(2) A leader shall have completed a youth leader course of at least 40 hours.
(3) A leader shall show a clean record to the municipality every 3 years.

heading: Leader qualifications
text:
(1) A leader shall be at least 18 years of age.
(2) A leader shall have completed a youth leader course of at least 50 hours.
(3) A leader shall show a clean record to the municipality every 3 years.

heading: Parental consent
text:
(1) A child under 16 years of age may take part in an activity only with the written consent of a parent or guardian.
(2) The consent is valid for 12 months and may be renewed.
(3) The consent shall state a telephone number where the parent can be reached.

heading: Trips away from home
text:
(1) An activity that includes a night away from home requires the written consent of a parent or guardian for each trip.
(2) A trip may last at most 7 nights.
(3) The organiser shall tell the municipality at least 14 days before the trip.

heading: Trips away from home
text: (Repealed.)

heading: Meals
text:
(1) An activity of more than 5 hours in one day shall include a meal.
(2) A meal shall be paid for within the fee of the activity.
(3) The organiser shall ask about allergies before the first day.

heading: Transport
text:
(1) A municipality may arrange transport for an activity.
(2) The transport fee is 6 crowns for each trip.
(3) A vehicle shall have one seat for each child and no more than 10 children for each adult.

heading: Transport
text:
(1) A municipality may arrange transport for an activity.
(2) The transport fee is 7 crowns for each trip.
(3) A vehicle shall have one seat for each child and no more than 10 children for each adult.

heading: Late collection
text:
(1) A parent who collects a child more than 15 minutes after the end of an activity shall pay a charge of 5 crowns.
(2) The charge is payable for each further period of 30 minutes.

heading: Late collection
text:
(1) A parent who collects a child more than 15 minutes after the end of an activity shall pay a charge of 6 crowns.
(2) The charge is payable for each further period of 30 minutes.

heading: Cancellation by the municipality
text:
(1) A municipality that cancels an activity shall tell parents at least 7 days before it begins.
(2) The fee shall be returned in full within 14 days.
(3) A parent may ask for a written statement of the reasons for the cancellation.

heading: Incident reports
text:
(1) A leader shall report every accident to the municipality within 24 hours.
(2) A serious accident shall also be reported to a parent at once.
(3) The municipality keeps the reports for 5 years.

heading: Opening hours of youth centres
text:
(1) A youth centre shall be open for at least 20 hours in a week.
(2) A youth centre shall close by 21 o'clock in the evening for members under 16 years of age.
(3) The opening hours shall be posted at the entrance.

heading: Opening hours of youth centres
text:
(1) A youth centre shall be open for at least 24 hours in a week.
(2) A youth centre shall close by 21 o'clock in the evening for members under 16 years of age.
(3) The opening hours shall be posted at the entrance.

heading: Complaints
text:
(1) A parent may complain in writing about an activity.
(2) The municipality shall answer within 14 days.
(3) A parent who is not satisfied may appeal to the municipal board within 30 days of the answer.

heading: Berthing after a rescue call-out
text:
(1) Where a boat stays overnight in a harbour because its skipper took part that day in a call-out of a lifeboat station, no nightly berth fee is charged for that night.
(2) The skipper shows the station's confirmation of the call-out to the harbour master.
(3) This section does not apply to an annual berth.
